short_definition: Alpha — Α, α, ἄλφα (which see), τό, indecl., — ah! — ἔα,
deep_entry:
Abbott-Smith / STEPBible (TBESG)
Α, α, ἄλφα (which see), τό, indecl.,
alpha, the first letter of the Greek alphabet. As a numeral, ά = 1, α = 1000. As a prefix, it appears to have at least two and perhaps three distinct senses:
__1. ἀ- (before a vowel, ἀν-) negative, as in ἄ-γνωστος, ἄ-δικος.
__2. ἀ-, ἁ- copulative, indicating community and fellowship, as in ἁ-πλοῦς, ἀ-κολουθέω, ἀ-δελφός.
__3. An intensive force (LS, s. α), as in ἀ-τενίζω is sometimes assumed (but see Boisacq, see word).
(AS)

---

interj.,

deep_entry:
Abbott-Smith / STEPBible (TBESG)
ἀγαθός, -ή, -όν,
[in LXX chiefly for טוֹב ;]
in general, good, in physical and in moral sense, used of persons, things, acts, conditions, etc., applied to that which is regarded as "perfect in its kind, so as to produce pleasure and satisfaction, . . . that which, in itself good, is also at once for the good and the advantage of him who comes in contact with it" (Cremer, 3): γῆ, Luk.8:8; δένδρον, Mat.7:18; καρδία, Luk.8:15; δόσις, Jas.1:17; μέρις, Luk.10:42; ἔργον (frequently in Pl.), Php.1:6; ἐλπίς, 2Th.2:16; θησαυρός, Mat.12:35; μνεία, 1Th.3:6 (cf. 2Ma.7:20); as subst., τὸ ἀ, that which is morally good, beneficial, acceptable to God, Rom.12:2; ἐργάζεσθαι τὸ ἀ, Rom.2:10, Eph.4:28; πράσσειν, Rom.9:11, 2Co.5:10; διώκειν, 1Th.5:15; μιμεῖσθαι, III Jo 11; κολλᾶσθαι τῷ ἀ, Rom.12:9; ερωτᾶν περὶ τοῦ ἀ., Mat.19:17; διάκονος εἰς τὸ ἀ., Rom.13:4; τὸ ἀ. σου, thy favour, benefit, Phm 14; pl., τὰ ἀ., of goods, possessions, Luk.12:18; of spiritual benefits, Rom.10:15, Heb.9:11, 10:1. ἀ is opposite to πονηρός, Mat.5:45, 20:5; κακός, Rom.7:19; φαῦλος, Rom.9:11, 2Co.5:10 (cf. MM, VGT, see word).
SYN.: καλός, δίκαιος. κ. properly refers to goodliness as manifested in form: ἀ. to inner excellence (cf. the cl. καλὸς κἀγαθός and ἐν καρδία κ. καὶ ἀ., Luk.8:15). In Rom.5:7, where it is contrasted with δ., ἀ. implies a kindliness and attractiveness not necessarily possessed by the δίκαιος, who merely measures up to a high standard of rectitude (cf. ἀγαθωσύνη). (AS)

---

LSJ / STEPBible (TFLSJ)
ἀγᾰθός [ᾰγ], ή, όν,
Laconian dialect ἀγασός [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Lysistrata” 1301, 5th c.AD: Cypria ἀζαθός “GDI” 57]]:— good:

__I
of persons,

__I.1
well-born, gentle, opposed to κακός, δειλός, οἷά τε τοῖς ἀγαθοῖσι παραδρώωσι χέρηες[Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 15.324, compare 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 1.275; ἀφνειός τ᾽ ἀ. τε 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 13.664, compare 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 18.276; πατρὸς δ᾽ εἴμ᾽ ἀγαθοῖο, θεὰ δέ με γείνατο μήτηρ 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 21.109, compare 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 4.611; κακὸς ἐξ ἀ. 6th c.BC: Theognis Elegiacus 190, compare 57f; πραῢς ἀστοῖς, οὐ φθονέων ἀγαθοῖς 5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “P.” 3.71, compare 2.96, 4.285; τίς ἂν εὔπατρις ὧδε βλάστο; οὐδεὶς τῶν ἀ. κτλ. 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Electra” 1082; οἵ τ᾽ ἀ. πρὸς τῶν ἀγενῶν κατανικῶνται [prev. author] “fragment” 84]]; τοὺς εὐγενεῖς γὰρ κἀγαθοὺς.. φιλεῖ Ἄρης ἐναίρειν[Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. work] 649, compare 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Alcestis” 600, +others: ἀγαθοὶ καὶ ἐξ ἀγαθῶν 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Phaedrus” 274a]]:—in political sense, aristocrats, especially in the phrase καλοὶ κἀγαθοί (see. entry καλοκἀγαθός).

__I.2

deep_entry:
Abbott-Smith / STEPBible (TBESG)
ἀγαπάω, -ῶ,
[in LXX chiefly for אהב ;]
to love, to feel and exhibit esteem and goodwill to a person, to prize and delight in a thing.
__1. Of human affection, to men: τ. πλησίον, Mat.5:43; τ. ἐχθρούς, ib. 44; to Christ, Jhn.8:42; to God, Mat.22:37; with accusative of thing(s), Luk.11:43, Jhn.12:43, Eph.5:25, II Tim 4:8, 10, Heb.1:9, 1Pe.2:17, 3:10, 2Pe.2:15, 1Jn.2:15, Rev.12:11.
__2. Of divine love;
__(a) God's love: to men, Rom.8:37; to Christ, Jhn.3:35;
__(b) Christ's love: to men, Mrk.10:21; to God, Jhn.14:31; with cogn. accusative, Jhn.17:26, Eph.2:4.
SYN.: φιλέω. From its supposed etymology (Thayer, LS; but see also Boisacq) ἀ. is commonly understood properly to denote love based on esteem (diligo), as distinct from that expressed by φιλέω (amo), spontaneous natural affection, emotional and unreasoning. If this distinction holds, ἀ. is fitly used in NT of Christian love to God and man, the spiritual affection which follows the direction of the will, and which, therefore, unlike that feeling which is instinctive and unreasoned, can be commanded as a duty. (Cf. ἀγάπη, and v. Tr., Syn. §xii; Cremer, 9, 592; and esp. MM, VGT, see word) (AS)

---

deep_entry:
Abbott-Smith / STEPBible (TBESG)
ἀγάπη, -ης, ἡ
[in LXX for אַהֲבָה, which is also rendered by ἀγάπησις and φιλία ;]
love, goodwill, esteem. Outside of bibl. and eccl. books, there is no clear instance (with Deiss., LAE, 18:4, 70:2, cf. the same writer in Constr. Quar., ii, 4; and with MM, VGT, see word, cf. Dr. Moulton in Exp. Times, xxvi, 3, 139). In NT, like ἀγαπάω, -ῶ,
__1. Of men's love:
__(a) to one another, Jhn.13:35;
__(b) to God, 1Jn.2:5.
__2. Of divine love;
__(a) God's love: to men, Rom.5:8; to Christ, Jhn.17:26;
__(b) Christ's love to men: Rom.8:35.
__3. In pl., love feasts: Ju 12 (DB, iii, 157).
SYN.: φιλία. ἀ., signifying properly (see: ἀγαπάω) love which chooses its object, is taken over from LXX, where its connotation is more general, into NT, and there used exclusively to express that spiritual bond of love between God and man and between man and man, in Christ, which is characteristic of Christianity. It is thusdistinct from φιλία, friendship (Jas.4:4 only), στοργή, natural affection (in NT only in compounds, see: ἄστοργος) and ἔρως, sexual love, which is not used in NT, its place being taken by ἐπιθυμία. (Cf. ἀγαπάω; and see Abbott, Essays, 70f.; DB, vol. i., 555; Cremer, 13, 593; MM, VGT, see word). (AS)

deep_entry:

ἁγιάζω, Hellenistic form of ἁγίζω
(ἅγιος),
to make holy, consecrate, sanctify; [in LXX chiefly for קדשׁ pi., hi. ;]
__1. to dedicate, separate,  set apart for God; of things: Mat.23:17,19, 2Ti.2:21; of persons: Christ, Jhn.10:36, 17:19.
__2. to purify, make conformable in character to such dedication: forensically, to free from guilt, 1Co.6:11, Eph.5:26, Heb.2:11, 10:10, 14, 29, 13:12; internally, by actual sanctification of life, Jhn.17:17, 19, Act.20:32, 26:18, Rom.15:16, 1Co.1:2, 7:14, 1Th.5:23, Rev.22:11; of a nonbeliever influenced by marriage with a Christian, 1Co.7:14.
__3. In the intermediate sense of ceremonial or levitical purification:
__(a) of things, 2Ti.2:21;
__(b) of persons, Heb.9:13.
__4. to treat as holy: Mat.6:9, Luk.11:2, 1Pe.3:16 (Cremer, 53, 602; MM, VGT, see word).

deep_entry:
Abbott-Smith / STEPBible (TBESG)
ἅγιος, -α, ον
(τό ἅγός, religious awe; ἅζω, to venerate), [in LXX chiefly for קֹ֫דֶשׁ ;]
primarily, dedicated to the gods, sacred (Hdt.; rare in Att., never in Hom., Hes. and Trag., who use ἁγνός), hence, holy, characteristic of God, separated to God, worthy of veneration.
__1.  Its highest application is to God himself, in his purity, majesty, and glory: Luk.1:49, Jhn.17:11, Rev.4:8. Hence
__(a) of things and places which have a claim to reverence as sacred to God, e.g. the Temple: Mat.24:15, Heb.9:1;
__(b) of persons employed by him, as angels: 1Th.3:13; prophets, Luk.1:70; apostles, Eph.3:5.
__2. Applied to persons as separated to God's service:
__(a) of Christ, Mrk.1:24, Jhn.6:69, Act.4:30;
__(b) of Christians, Act.9:13, Rom.1:7, Heb.6:10, Rev.5:8.
__3. In the moral sense of sharing God's purity: Mrk.6:20, Jhn.17:11, Act.3:14, Rev.3:7.
__4. Of pure, clean sacrifices and offerings: 1Co.7:14, Eph.1:4.
SYN.: ἁγνός, pure, both in ceremonial and spiritual sense; ἱερός (sacer), sacred, that which is inviolable because of its (external) relation to God; ὅσιος (sanctus as opposite to nefas), that which is based on everlasting ordinances of right. (Cf. Tr., Syn., §lxxxviii; DB, ii, 399 f.; Cremer, 34, 594-601; MM, VGT, see word) (AS)

---

[in LXX for עִזָּבוֹן, שׁוּק ;]

__2. a place of assembly, a public place or forum, a market-place (Hom., Thuc, al.; LXX): Mat.11:16 20:2 23:7, Mrk.6:56 (cf . MM, VGT, see word, ἀγυιά) 7:4 (Bl., §46, 7) 12:38, Luk.7:32 (Bl., l.with) 11:43 20:46, Act.16:19 17:7 (Cremer, 59; MM, VGT, see word).

LSJ / STEPBible (TFLSJ)
ἀγορά [ᾰγ], ᾶς,
Ionic dialect ἀγορή, ῆς, ἡ, (ἀγείρω):— assembly, especially of the People, opposed to the Council of Chiefs, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 2.93, 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 2.69, etc.]]; τοῖσιν δ᾽ οὔτ᾽ ἀγοραὶ βουληφόροι (i.e. Κυκλώπεσσι) [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 9.112; ὀρθῶν ἑσταότων ἀ γένετ᾽ οὐδέ τις ἔτλη ἕζεσθαι 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 18.246]]; ἀ. Πυλάτιδες, of the Amphictyonic Council at Pylae, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Trachiniae” 638, cf. Ion Eleg. 1.3; μακάρων ἀ. 5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “I.” 8(7).29, compare “Anecdota Graeca - Bekker” 210]]; ἀγορήνδε καλέσσασθαι, κηρύσσειν, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 1.54, 2.51]]; ἀγορὴν ποιήσασθαι, θέσθαι, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 8.489, 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 9.171]]; εἰς ἀ. ἰέναι, ἀγέρεσθαι,[Refs 8th c.BC+ [8.12, 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 18.245; ἀγορήνδε καθέζεσθαι 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 1.372.]]—Not common in Prose, ἀγορὰν συνάγειν, συλλέγειν[Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 5.7.3; ποιῆσαι 4th c.BC: Aeschines Orator 3.27; ἀγορὰς ποιεῖσθαι 4th c.BC: Hyperides Orator “Fragmenta” 150]]: of the assembly in Attic demes, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 44.36, “IG” 2.585, +others; ἀ. συνέδριον φυλετῶν καὶ δημοτῶν “Anecdota Graeca - Bekker” 327: in late Prose, ἀ. δικῶν προθεῖναι, καταστήσασθαι]], = Latin conventus agere, [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd c.AD: Lucianus Sophista]]“Bis Acc.” 4,12: meeting for games, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “N.” 3.14: _metaphorically_, μυρμήκων ἀ. 2nd c.AD: Lucianus Sophista “Icar.” 19: proverbial, θεῶν ἀ. 'Babel', 10th c.AD: Suidas Legal icographus, etc.]]

__II
place of assembly, τοὺς δ᾽ εὗρ᾽ εἰν ἀγορῇ[Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 7.382; ἵνα σφ᾽ ἀ. τε θέμις τε 11.807, compare 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 6.266; _plural_, 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 8.16; οὔτε.. εἰς ἀ. ἔρχεται οὔτε δίκας 6th c.BC: Theognis Elegiacus 268.]]

__II.2
market-place, perhaps not earlier than [Refs [“Hom.epigram” 14.5 πολλὰ μὲν εἰν ἀγορῇ πωλεύμενα, πολλὰ δ᾽ ἀγυιαῖς]]; frequently in later authors, πρυμνοῖς ἀγορᾶς ἔπι[Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “P.” 5.93; θεοὶ.. ἀγορᾶς ἐπίσκοποι 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Septem contra Thebas” 272; μέση Τραχινίων ἀ. 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Trachiniae” 424; ἀγορᾷ οὐδὲ ἄστει δέχεσθαι 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 6.44; ὀλιγάκις.. ἀγορᾶς χραίνων κύκλον 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Orestes” 919]]; οἱ ἐκ τῆς ἀ. market people, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 1.2.18; ἐξ ἀγορᾶς εἶ 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Equites” 181, etc.]]; εἰς ἀ. ἐμβάλλειν to go into the forum, i. e. be a citizen, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Lycurgus Orator 5]]; ἐν τῇ ἀ. ἐργάζεσθαι to trade in the market, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 57.31]]; εἰς τὴν ἀ. χειροτονεῖν (opposed to ἐπὶ τὸν πόλεμον) 'for the market', [Refs 1st c.BC+ [[prev. author] 4.26; the Roman “Forum”, 1st c.BC: Dionysius Halicarnassensis 5.48.]]

__III
business of the ἀγορά:

__III.1
public speaking, gift of speaking, mostly in plural, ἔσχ᾽ ἀγοράων withheld him from speaking, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 2.275]]; οἱ δ᾽ ἀγορὰς ἀγόρευον[Refs 8th c.BC+ [[prev. work] 788, compare 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 4.818; ᾠδὴν ἀντ᾽ ἀγορῆς θέμενος 6th c.BC: Solon Lyricus 1.]]

__III.2
market, ἀγορὰν παρασκευάζειν[Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 7.40, 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Historia Graeca (Hellenica)” 3.4.11; ἀ. παρέχειν 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 6.44, etc.; ἄγειν 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 5.7.33, etc.]]; opposed to ἀγορᾷ χρῆσθαι to have supplies,[Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. work] 7.6.24; τῆς ἀ. εἴργεσθαι 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 1.67, 1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus “Pericles” 29]]; ἀ. ἐλευθέρα, i. e. καθαρὰ τῶν ὠνίων πάντων, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Politica” 1331a31, compare 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 1.2.3; opposed to ἀ. ἀναγκαία 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Politica” 1331b11]]; generally, provisions, supplies, [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [PPetr. 3p.131 (3rd c.BC), “PS” 14.354 (3rd c.BC), +others]]; in plural, Nic.Dam.p.6.17 [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator]]; ἀγορὰς περικόπτειν cut off supplies, [Refs 1st c.BC+ [1st c.BC: Dionysius Halicarnassensis 10.43.]]

__III.2.b
market, sale, ἀ. τῶν βιβλίων, τῶν παρθένων, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [2nd c.AD: Lucianus Sophista “Ind.” 19, 2nd-3rd c.AD: Aelianus “Varia Historia” 4.1, compare 4th c.BC: Nicochares Comicus 7.]]

__IV
as a mark of time, ἀ. πλήθουσα the forenoon, when the market-place was full, ἀγορῆς πληθυούσης[Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 4.181; πληθούσης ἀγορᾶς 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Memorabilia” 1.1.10, compare “SIG” 695.38 (5th c.BC: Magnes Comicus Mae.)]]; περὶ or ἀμφὶ ἀ. πλήθουσαν[Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 2.1.7, 1.8.1; ἐν ἀ. πληθούσῃ 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Gorgias” 469d, compare 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 8.92; also ἀγορῆς πληθώρη 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 2.173, 7.223; poetry, ἐν ἀ. πλήθοντος ὄχλου 5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “P.” 4.85; πρὶν ἀ. πεπληθέναι 5th c.BC: Pherecrates Comicus 29: ἀγορῆς διάλυσις]] the time just after mid-day, when they went home from market, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 3.104, compare 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Oeconomicus” 12.1.]]

__V
marketday, = Latin nundinae, [Refs 1st c.BC+ [1st c.BC: Dionysius Halicarnassensis 7.58.]]

deep_entry:
Abbott-Smith / STEPBible (TBESG)
ἀγρυπνέω, -ῶ (ἄγρυπνος, seeking sleep ; ἀγρεύω, ὕπνος),
[in LXX chiefly for שׁקד ;]
to be sleepless, wakeful (Theogn., Xen., al.); metaphorically (LXX) = cl. ἐγρήγορα, to be watchful, vigilant: Mrk.13:33, Luk.21:36, Eph.6:18, Heb.13:17.†
SYN.: γρηγορέω, which see; νήφω, associated with γ. in 1Pe.5:8, expressing a wariness which results from self-control, a condition of moral, not merely mental alertness (see M, Th., I, 5:6). (AS)

---

LSJ / STEPBible (TFLSJ)
ἀγρυπν-έω,
perfect ἠγρύπνηκα[Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Hippocrates Medicus “προγνωστικόν” 2]]:—lie awake, pass sleepless nights, [Refs 6th c.BC+ [6th c.BC: Theognis Elegiacus 471, Hp.[same place], 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Leges” 695a, etc.]]; opposed to καθεύδω, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 8.3.42]]; ἀγρυπνεῖν τὴν νύκτα to pass a sleepless night, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [[prev. author] “HG” 7.2.19, 4th-3rd c.BC: Menander Comicus 113]]; οἱ -οῦντες sufferers from insomnia, [Refs 1st c.AD+ [1st c.AD: Dioscorides (Dioscurides) Medicus 4.64.]]

__2
metaphorically, to be watchful, [LXX+NT [LXX.Wis.6.15, NT.Mark.13.33, NT.Eph.6.18; ὑπὲρ τῶν ψυχῶν NT.Heb.13.17; ἐπὶ τὰ κακά LXX.Dan.9.14]]: with infinitive, μηθέν σε ἐνοχλήσειν[Refs [“PGrenf.” 2.14a3.]]

__3
with accusative, lie awake and think of, τινά[Refs [“PMag.Par.” 1.2966.]]

ἄγω [ᾰ],
imperfect ἦγον, Epic dialect and Ionic dialect ἄγεσκον[Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.148, 3rd c.BC: Apollonius Rhodius Epicus 1.849]]: future ἄξω[Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 1.139, etc.]]: thematic aorist imperative ἄξετε[Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 3.105,]]infinitive ἀξέμεναι, -έμεν, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 23.50, 111]]: aorist 2 ἤγαγον[Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 6.291, etc., _optative_ ἀγαγοίην 7th-6th c.BC: Sappho Lyrica 159:]]aorist 1 ἦξα rare, ἦζε[Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Timotheus Lyricus “Persae” 165]], participle ἄξας[Refs [Batrachomyomachia 119]], infinitive ἄξαι[Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Antipho Orator 5.46]]: perfect ἦχα[Refs 7th c.BC+ [“SIG” 1 (Abu Simbel, 7th-6th c.BC), 2nd c.BC: Polybius Historicus 3.111.3]], (προ-) [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 19.18]], (συν-) [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Memorabilia” 4.2.8; ἀγήγοχα “OGI” 219.15 (Sigeum, 3rd c.BC)]], etc., Doric dialect συν-αγάγοχα[LXX+1st c.AD+ [“Test.Epict.” 3.12; ἀγήοχα LXX.Tob.12.3, 1st c.AD: Josephus Historicus “Bellum Judaicum” 1.30.1, 2nd c.AD: Alexander Rhetor “De Figuris” 1.11, etc.]] (also in compounds, (εἰσ-) Ps.-Philipp. cited in [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 18.39]], (κατ-) Canon Laws texts[Refs [[prev. work]73)]]; ἀγείοχα[Refs 2nd c.BC+ [“PTeb.” 5.193 (2nd c.BC), etc.]]; ἀγέωχα (δι-) [Refs 2nd c.BC+ [“CIG” “Corpus Inscriptionum Graecarum” “Corpus Inscriptionum Graecarum” 4897d (Philae, 1st c.BC), “PTeb.” 5.198 (2nd c.BC)]], etc.: pluperfect ἀγηόχει[Refs 2nd c.BC+ [2nd c.BC: Polybius Historicus 30.4.17]]:—middle, future ἄξομαι[Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Homerus Epicus, 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus]], Trag.: them. aorist 1 ἄξοντο[Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 8.545, _imperative_ ἄζεσθε [prev. work] 505: also ἀξάμην]] (ἐσ-) [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 5.34]], (προεσ-) [Refs [1.190, 8.20:]]aorist 2 ἠγαγόμην[Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Homerus Epicus, etc.]], 2nd pers.singular ἀγάγαο[Refs [“GDI” 5088.8 (Cretan dialect)]]:—passive, future ἀχθήσομαι[Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Hp.Ma.” 292a]], (προσ-) [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 4.87, etc.]]; ἄξομαι in passive sense, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Agamemnon” 1632, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 458d]], (προσ-) [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 4.115, etc.]]: aorist 1 ἤχθην[Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 6.3.10]], Ionic dialect ἄχθην[Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 6.30]], participle ἀχθείς[Refs 6th c.BC+ [6th c.BC: Hipponax Iambographus 9:]]perfect ἦγμαι[Refs 4th c.BC+ [Hdt 2.158, 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 13.15]]; also in middle sense, see below [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Bacchylides Lyricus 2.]]

__I
lead, carry, fetch, bring, of living creatures, φέρω being used of things, δῶκε δ᾽ ἄγειν ἑτάροισι.. γυναῖκα, καὶ τρίποδα.. φέρειν[Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 23.512]]; βοῦν δ᾽ ἀγέτην κεράων by the horns, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 3.439]]; ἄ. εἰς or πρὸς τόπον, poetry also with accusative loci, νόστοι δ᾽ ἐκ πολέμων ἀπόνους (i.e. ἄνδρας).. ἆγον οἴκους[Refs 8th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Persae” 863 (Lyric poetry); Ἅιδας.. ἄγει τὰν Ἀχέροντος ἀκτάν 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Antigone” 811 (Lyric poetry); ἄ. τινά τινι 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 14.386; ἵππους ὑφ᾽ ἅρματ᾽ ἄ. 3.476, compare 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Prometheus Vinctus” 465.]]

__I.b
participle ἄγων taking, στῆσε δ᾽ ἄγων[Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 2.558, compare 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 1.130, 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Coloneus” 1342, etc.]]

__I.2
take with one, ἑταίρους[Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 10.405, compare 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Coloneus” 832, etc.]]; τι [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 15.531, 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.70]]; of a wife, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Prometheus Vinctus” 559 (Lyric poetry) (more usually _middle_, which see).]]

__I.3
carry off as captives or booty, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 1.367, 9.594, 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Septem contra Thebas” 340, etc.; ἄχθη ἀγόμενος παρὰ βασιλέα 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 6.30]]; ἀγόμενος, i.e. δοῦλος, [Refs 7th c.BC+ [7th c.BC: Archilochus Lyricus 155, compare 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Troades” 140, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Leges” 914e]]; Δίκην ἄγειν to lead Justice forcibly away, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th-7th c.BC: Hesiodus Epicus “Opera et Dies” 220; ἡ ἐπιθυμία ἄγει 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Ethica Nicomachea” 1147a34]]; of a fowler, φῦλον ὀρνίθων ἀμφιβαλὼν ἄγει[Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Antigone” 343: especially in phrase ἄ. καὶ φέρειν]] harry, ravage a country, first in [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 5.484 οἷόν κ᾽ ἠὲ φέροιεν Ἀχαιοὶ ἤ κεν ἄγοιεν, compare 23.512f]]; frequently in [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus]] and Attic dialect Prose:—in passive, ἀγόμεθα, φερόμεθα[Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Troades” 1310, compare 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Nubes” 241]]: more rarely reversed, φέρουσί τε καὶ ἄγουσι[Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.88; ἔφερε καὶ ἦγε πάντας [prev. author] 3.39: with _accusative_ loci, φέρων καὶ ἄγων τὴν Βιθυνίδα 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Historia Graeca (Hellenica)” 3.2.2; ἦγον καὶ ἔκαον τὴν 5th c.BC: Bacchylides Lyricus [prev. work]5]]; ἄ. alone, ravage, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [Inscriptiones Graecae 9(1).333 (_Locrian dialect_, 5th c.BC):]] —but φέρειν καὶ ἄγειν sometimes means simply bear and carry, bring together, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Phaedrus” 279c]]; τὴν ποίησιν φέρειν τε καὶ ἄγειν, i.e. bring it into the state, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. author] “Lg.” 817a, compare 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 3.3.2.]]

__I.4
ἄ. εἰς δίκην or δικαστήριον, ἐπὶ τοὺς δικαστάς to carry one before a court of justice, frequently in Attic dialect, πρὸς τὴν δίκην ἄ.[Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Fragmenta” 1049; ὑπ᾽ ἐπίγνωσιν ἀχθῆναι “PTeb.” 28.11 (2nd c.BC)]]; simply ἄγειν[Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Gorgias” 527a, etc.; ἐπὶ θανάτῳ ἄ. 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 1.6.10, etc.]]:—passive, ἐπὶ βασιλεῖς ἀχθήσεσθε[NT+2nd c.AD+ [NT.Matt.10.18, compare “PTeb.” 331.16 (2nd c.AD)]]; φόνου ἄγεσθαι[Refs 1st c.AD+ [1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus 2.309e.]]

__I.4.b
passive, to be confiscated, τὰ κτήνη ἀχθήσεται πρὸς τὰ ἐκφόρια (to meet the rent) [Refs 2nd c.BC+ [“PTeb.” 27.75 (2nd c.BC).]]

__I.5
of ships, carry as cargo, import, [οἶνον] νῆες ἄγουσι[Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 9.72, etc.]]; ἵνα οἱ σὺν φόρτον ἄγοιμι (i.e. σύν οἱ) [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 14.296.]]

__I.6
draw on, bring on, πῆμα τόδ᾽ ἤγαγον Οὐρανίωνες[Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 24.547; Ἰλίω φθοράν 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Agamemnon” 406 (Lyric poetry); τερμίαν ἁμέραν 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Antigone” 1330 (Lyric poetry); ὕπνον [prev. author] “Ph.” 638; χαράν 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Fragmenta” 174; δάκρυ [prev. author] Alcaeus1081.]]

__I.7
bear up, φελλοὶ δ᾽ ὥς. ἄγουσι δίκτυον[Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Choephori” 506.]]

__I.8
carry far and wide, spread abroad, κλέος[Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 5.311.]]

__I.9
in Medicine texts, remove, φλέγμα[Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Hippocrates Medicus “περὶ φύσιος ἀνθρώπου” 6, compare “Aph.” 4.2; ἕλμινθα 1st c.AD: Dioscorides (Dioscurides) Medicus 1.16.]]

__II
lead towards a point, lead on, τὸν δ᾽ ἄγε μοῖρα κακὴ θανάτοιο τέλοσδε[Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 13.602; κῆρες ἄγον θανάτοιο 2.834; οἷ μ᾽ ἀτιμίας ἄγεις 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Electra” 1035: also with]]infinitive, ἄγει θανεῖν leads to death, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Hecuba” 43: with _accusative_ _cognate_, ἄγομαι τάνδ᾽ ἑτοίμαν ὁδόν 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Antigone” 877 (Lyric poetry)]]; ὁδὸς ἄγει the road leads, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [1st c.AD(?): Heraclitus 71, 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Tyrannus” 734, “Tab.Heracl.” 1.16, etc.]]: metaphorically, tend, ἐπὶ τὸ ἄκρον[Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Leges” 701e.]]

__II.2
lead, guide, especially in war, λαόν[Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 10.79]]; ἄ. στρατιάν, ναῦς, etc., [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 7.12, 8.59, etc., compare 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 4.8.12]]; hence absolutely, march, θᾶσσον ὁ Νικίας ἦγε[Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 7.81, compare 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Historia Graeca (Hellenica)” 4.2.19, etc.]]: simply, go, ἄγωμεν[NT.Mark.1.38]; of the gods, etc., guide, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus, 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus, etc.; ἐπ᾽ ἀρετήν 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Fragmenta” 672; διὰ πόνων ἄγειν τινά [prev. author] “IT” 988.]]

__II.3
manage, νόῳ πλοῦτον[Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “P.” 6.47; πολιτείαν 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 1.127]]; τὴν σοφίαν conduct philosophical inquiry, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Theaetetus” 172b]]; of reasoning, ἀγαγεῖν τοὺς λόγους[Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Analytica Priora” 47a21; εἰς τὸ ἀδύνατον ἄ. [prev. work] 27a15 (variant{ἀπάγοντας})]]:—passive, to be led, guided, λογισμῷ[Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 431c; ἡγούμενος τῶν ἡδονῶν ἀλλ᾽ οὐκ ἀγόμενος ὑπ᾽ αὐτῶν 5th-6th c.BC: Isocrates Orator 9.45.]]

__II.4
refer, attribute, τι εἰς ἐθελοκάκησιν[Refs 2nd c.BC+ [2nd c.BC: Polybius Historicus 27.15.13; τι ἐς Διόνυσον 2nd c.AD: Lucianus Sophista “Syr.D.” 33.]]

__II.5
bring up, train, educate, ἀγόμενοις ὀρθῶς[Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Leges” 782d; ἤχθη τὴν λεγομένην ἀγωγήν 1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus “Agesilaus” 1]]; of animals, train, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Memorabilia” 4.1.3.]]

__II.6
reduce, ἐς βραχὺ τὴν ἀρχήν[Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Hippocrates Medicus “περὶ ἀρχαίης ἰητρικῇς” 1; ἐς τὸ ἥμισυ [prev. author] “Mul.” 1.78]]; of propositions, εἰς ῥᾳδιξστέραν κατασκευήν[Refs 3rd c.AD+ [3rd c.AD(?): Pappus Mathematicus 1076.6.]]

__III
draw out in length, τεῖχος ἄ. to draw a line of wall, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 6.99; μέλαθρον εἰς ὀρόφους “Anthologia Graeca” 9.649 (1st c.AD(?): Macedonius Epigrammaticus); ὄγμον ἄ. 3rd c.BC: Theocritus Poeta Bucolicus 10.2]]; ἄ. γραμμάς to draw lines, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Topica” 101a16]]; ἤχθωσαν κάθετοι let perpendiculars be drawn, Mete.[Refs [373a11]]; ἄ. ἐπίπεδον describe a plane, [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [3rd c.BC: Archimedes Geometra “περὶ σφαίρας καὶ κυλίνδρου” 1.7, etc.]]:—passive, ἦκται ἡ διῶρυξ[Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 2.158, compare 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 6.100]]; κόλπου ἀγομένου τῆς γῆς, i.e. when the land forms a bight, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 4.99.]]

__IV
hold, celebrate, Ἀπατούρια, ὁρτήν, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.147, 183 (more usually ἀνάγειν)]]; frequently in Attic dialect, ἄ. ἀγῶνα[LXX+5th c.BC+ [“IG” 1.53.33; θυσίαν, θεωρίαν 5th-6th c.BC: Isocrates Orator 19.10; κρεουργὸν ἦμαρ εὐθύμως ἄγειν 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Agamemnon” 1592; γάμους 4th-3rd c.BC: Menander Comicus “Σαμία” 336, cf. LXX.Tob.11.19 (_passive_)]]; ἐκκλησίαν[Refs 1st c.AD+ [1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus “Aemilius Paulus” 30]]:—passive, ἀγοραῖοι ἄγονται[NT.Act.19.38.]

__IV.2
keep, observe a date, ἄ. τὴν ἡμέραν ταύτην πάντα τὸν χρόνον[Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 5.54, compare 4th-3rd c.BC: Menander Comicus 521; κατὰ σελήνην τὰς ἡμέρας 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Nubes” 626]]; reckon, τοὺς ἐνιαυτοὺς καθ᾽ ἥλιον[Refs 1st c.BC+ [1st c.BC: Geminus Astronomicus 8.6.]]

__IV.3
keep, observe, ὀρθὰν ἄγεις ἐφημοσύναν[Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “P.” 6.20; σπονδὰς ἄ. πρός τινας 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 6.7; εἰρήνην 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 465b, etc.: with _accusative_, as periphrastic for a _neuter_ Verb, σχολὴν ἄγειν, ={σχολάζειν}, 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Medea” 1238, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 376d]]; ἡσυχίαν ἄ., ={ἡσυχάξειν}, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 3.1.14; ἄ. ἀπαστίαν 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Nubes” 621]]; κρύψιν ἄ., of stars between setting and rising, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Autolycus Astronomus 2.9]]; keep up, sustain, maintain, νεῖκος[Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “P.” 9.31]]; γέλωτ᾽ ἄγειν to keep laughing, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Ajax” 382; ἄ. κτύπον 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Orestes” 182 (Lyric poetry)]]; with predicate, maintain, ἐλευθέραν ἦγε τὴν Ἑλλάδα[Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 9.36.]]

__IV.4
of Time, pass, ἀπήμαντον ἄγων βίοτον[Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “O.” 8.87]]; ποίας ἡμέρας δοκεῖς μ᾽ ἄγει; [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Electra” 266; ὁ βίος οὑμὸς ἑσπέραν ἄγει 2nd c.AD: Alexander Rhetor 228, compare ὥραν ἄγειν]] to be ripe, τῆς γαστρὸς ὥραν ἀγούσης[Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd-3rd c.AD: Philostratus Sophista “Vita Apollonii” 2.14]]; ὥραν ἦγε θανάτου[Refs 5th c.BC+ [Chor. p.38B.; τῆς ἡλικίας ἄγον τὸ ἄνθος [prev. author] p.53 5th c.BC: Bacchylides Lyricus; τέταρτον ἔτος ἄγων καὶ τριακοστόν 2nd c.AD: Galenus Medicus “Lib. Propr.” 1.]]

__IV.5
of beliefs, hold, αἵρεσιν[Refs 2nd c.BC+ [2nd c.BC: Polybius Historicus 27.15.14.]]

__V
hold account, treat, ἄ. ἀρετὰν οὐκ αἴσχιον φυᾶς[Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “I.” 7(6).22]]; ἐν τιμῇ ἄγειν or ἄγεσθαι, ἐν οὐδεμιῇ μοίρῃ ἄ., περὶ πλείστου ἄ., [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.134, 2.172, 9.7, etc.]]; θεοὺς ἄ. to believe in, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Supplices” 924]]; διὰ τιμῆς ἄ. τινά, etc., [Refs 5th c.BC+ [2nd c.AD: Lucianus Sophista “Prom.Es” 4, etc.; τὸ πρᾶγμ᾽ ἄ... ὡς παρ᾽ οὐδέν 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Antigone” 34; τὴν Ἀφροδίτην πρόσθ᾽ ἄ. τοῦ Βακχίου 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Bacchae” 225; τιμιώτερον ἄ. τινά 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 8.81; εὐεργεσίας εἰς ἀχαριστίαν καὶ προπηλακισμὸν ἄ. 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 18.316:—with Adverbs, δυσφόρως τοὔνειδος ἦγον 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Tyrannus” 784; ἐντίμως ἄ. 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 528c, etc.]]:—passive, ἠγόμην δ᾽ ἀνὴρ ἀστῶν μέγιστος[Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Tyrannus” 775.]]

__VI
draw down in the scale, hence, weigh, ἄ. μνᾶν, τριακοσίους δαρεικούς, etc., weigh a mina, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [300 darics, etc., 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 22.76, 24.129, compare 4th-3rd c.BC: Philippides Comicus 9.4, etc.; ἄ. πλέον 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Problemata” 931b15; ἄ. σταθμόν 1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus 2.96b.]]

__VII
on ἄγε, ἄγετε, see.s. voccative

__B
middle ἄγομαι, carry away for oneself, χρυσόν τε καὶ ἄργυρον οἴκαδ᾽ ἄγεσθαι[Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 10.35]]; take with one,[Refs 5th c.BC+ [6.58, 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Heraclidae” 808, etc.]]; of a ship's cargo, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 35.20]]; take to oneself, δῶρον[Refs 3rd c.BC+ [3rd c.BC: Theocritus Poeta Bucolicus 1.9, compare 11]]; take upon oneself, ἄγεσθαι ἐς χεῖρας[Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.126, 4.79.]]

__B.2
ἄγεσθαι γυναῖκα take to oneself a wife, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 14.211; γυναῖκα ἄ. ἐς τὰ οἰκία 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.59, etc.; ἄγεσθαί τινα ἐς δῶμα 8th-7th c.BC: Hesiodus Epicus “Theogonia” 410]]; simply ἄ. marry, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 2.47, etc.:]]perfect passive ἦγμαι is used in this middle sense, [Refs 1st c.AD+ [1st c.AD: Josephus Historicus “Antiquitates Judaicae” 14.12.1]]; of the father, bring home a wife for his son, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 4.10, 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.34]]; of a brother, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 15.238]]; of friends of the bridegroom and bride, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 6.28, 8th-7th c.BC: Hesiodus Epicus “Scutum Herculis” 274]]: later in passive of the wife, [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [“PGnom.” 138 (2nd c.AD).]]

__B.3
like active, bring; διὰ στόμα ἄγεσθαι μῦθον bring through the mouth, i.e. utter, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 14.91.]]

ἀγωγή, -ῆς, ἡ
(ἄγω), [in LXX: Est.2:20 10:3, 2Ma.4:16 6:8 11:24, 3Ma.4:10 * ;]
__1. a carrying away.
__2. a leading, guiding; metaphorically, training; hence, from the expression ἀ. τοῦ βίου, absol., conduct, way of life: 2Ti.3:10 (Cremer, 61; MM, VGT, see word).
† (AS)

---

LSJ / STEPBible (TFLSJ)
ἀγωγή, ἡ,
(ἄγω) carrying away, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 6.85, etc.]]; freight, carriage, πρὸς τὰς ἀγωγὰς.. χρῆσθαι ὑποζυγίοις[Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 370e, compare 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Respublica Lacedaemoniorum” 7.5, “PLond.” 3.948.2 (3rd c.AD).]]

__b
intransitive, τὴν ἀ. διὰ τάχους ἐποιεῖτο pursued his voyage, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 4.29 (variant)]]; movement, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 604b]]; ἀ. ἐπί τι tendency towards.., [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Hippocrates Medicus “ἐπιδημίαι” 1.1.]]

__2
bringing to or in, ὑμῶν ἡ ἐς τοὺς ὀλίγους ἀ. your bringing us before the council, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 5.85.]]

__3
forcible seizure, carrying off, abduction, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Agamemnon” 1263, 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Coloneus” 662; ἀγωγὴν ποιήσασθαι “PTeb.” 39.22 (2nd c.BC), compare 48.22.]]

__4
ὕδατος ἀγωγαί aqueducts, [Refs 1st c.BC+ [Inscriptiones Graecae 12(5).872 (from Tenos), compare 1st c.BC: Dionysius Halicarnassensis 3.67.]]

__5
load, [Refs [Ostr. 1168]]; weight, [Refs [AB 333.]]

__6
winding up of engine, [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [3rd-2nd c.BC: Philo Mechanicus “(Belopoeica) Excerpte aus Philons Mechanik - Ath. Berl. Akad.” 57.13 (_plural_).]]

__7
drawing of lines, [Refs 5th c.AD+ [5th c.AD: Proclus Philosophus “in primum Euclidis librum commentarius” pp.284,376F.]]

__8
evoking, πνευμάτων[Refs 4th c.AD+ [4th c.AD: Iamblichus Philosophus “de Mysteriis” 3.6 (_plural_).]]

__8.b
spell for bringing a person, usually love-charm, [Refs [PMag.Par. 1.1390.]]

__II
leading, guidance, ἵππου[Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “de Equitandi ratione” 6.4; ἡ τοῦ νόμου, τοῦ λογισμοῦ ἀ. 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Leges” 645a, compare “Plt.” 274b.]]

__II.2
leading of an army, [Refs [[prev. author] “Lg.” 746e (_plural_)]]; ἀ. στραταρχίας conduct of an expedition, [Refs 2nd c.BC+ [2nd c.AD: Vettius Valens Astrologus 339.29; ἡ ἀ. τῶν πραγμάτων 2nd c.BC: Polybius Historicus 3.8.5.]]

__II.3
direction, training, παιδεία μέν ἐσθ᾽ ἡ παίδων ὁλκή τε καὶ ἀ. πρὸς τὸν ὑπὸ τοῦ νόμου λόγον ὀρθὸν εἰρημένον[Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Leges” 659d, compare 819a; ἀ. ὀρθῆς τυχεῖν πρὸς ἀρετήν 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Ethica Nicomachea” 1179b31; διὰ τὸ ἦθος καὶ τὴν ἀ. [prev. author] “Pol.” 1292b14, compare 4th-3rd c.BC: Cleanthes Stoicus 1.107]]: in plural, systems of education, [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [3rd c.BC: Chrysippus Stoicus 3.173]]; especially of the public education of the Spartan youth, Λακωνικὴ ἀ.[Refs 2nd c.BC+ [2nd c.BC: Polybius Historicus 1.32.1; Ἀγησίλαος ἤχθη τὴν λεγομένην ἀγωγὴν ἐν Δακεδαίμονι 1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus “Agesilaus” 1]]; ἀ. στοιχειώδης elementary course, [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [3rd-2nd c.BC: Apollonius Pergaeus Geometra “Conica” 1]] Praef.:—also of plants, culture, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-3rd c.BC: Theophrastus Philosophus “Historia Plantarum” 1.3.2]]; of diseases, treatment, [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd c.AD: Galenus Medicus 12.414, 15.436.]]

__II.4
way of life, conduct, Archyt cited in [NT+3rd c.BC+ [5th c.AD: Stobaeus, Joannes 2.31.120 (_plural_), “PTeb.” 24.57 (2nd c.BC), “OGI” 223.15 (Erythrae, 3rd c.BC), LXX.2Mac.6.8, NT.2Tim.3.10, 2nd c.AD: Marcus Antoninus Imperator 1.6.]]

__II.5
keeping, observance, ἡμερῶν[Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aristoxenus Musicus “Rhythmica” 2.37; μηνῶν 1st c.BC: Geminus Astronomicus 8.48.]]

__II.6
generally, method, construction (of a law), [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Rhetorica” 1375b12]]; style, [Refs 1st c.BC+ [1st c.BC: Dionysius Halicarnassensis “de Isocrate” 20, +others; ἡ ἀ. τῶν διαλέκτων 1st c.BC-1st c.AD: Strabo Geographus 14.1.41.]]

__II.7
method of proof, especially of syllogistic reasoning, λόγοι τὰς ἀγωγὰς ὑγιεῖς ἔχοντες[Refs 3rd c.BC+ [3rd c.BC: Chrysippus Stoicus 2.84, compare 6th c.AD: Simplicius Philosophus “in Aristotelis Physica commentaria - Comm. in Arist. Graeca” 759.14]]; line of argument, [Refs 1st c.AD+ [1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus 2.106b.]]

__II.8
school of philosophers, [Refs 1st c.BC+ [1st c.BC: Philodemus Gadarensis Epigrammaticus “Sto.Herc.” 339.12, “Acad.Ind.” p.68 M., 2nd c.AD: Sextus Empiricus Philosophus “Πυρρώνειοι ὑποτυπώσεις” 1.145, etc.]]

__II.9
Milit., manoeuvre, movement, [Refs 1st c.BC+ [1st c.BC: Asclepiodotus Tacticus “Tact.” 12.7 and 10]]; order of march, [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [[prev. work]11.8,compare 2nd-3rd c.AD: Aelianus “Tactica - Griechische Kriegsschriftsteller” 39.1.]]

__II.10
in Law, = Latin actio, [Refs 4th c.AD+ [4th-6th c.AD: Codex Justinianus 4.24.1, +others]]

__III
tempo, in music, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 400c (_plural_), 4th c.BC: Aristoxenus Musicus “Harmonica” p.34 M., 3rd c.AD(?): Aristides Quintilianus Musicus 1.19]]; sequence, of a melody, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aristoxenus Musicus “Harmonica” p.29 M.]]; musical style, [Refs 1st c.BC+ [1st c.BC-1st c.AD: Strabo Geographus 14.1.41, 1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus 2.1141c.]]

Abbott-Smith / STEPBible (TBESG)
ἀγών, -ῶνος, ὁ
(ἄγω), [in LXX: Isa.7:13 (לאה), Est.4:17, Wis.4:2 10:12, II Mac.6, 4Mac .5 * ;]
__1. a gathering, esp. for games.
__2. a place of assembly.
__3. a contest, struggle, trial; metaphorically (MM, VGT, see word),
__(a) of the Christian life as a contest and struggle: Php.1:30, 1Th.2:2, 1Ti.6:12, 2Ti.4:7 Heb.12:1;
__(b) solicitude, anxiety: Col.2:1.
† (AS)

---

LSJ / STEPBible (TFLSJ)
ἀγών [ᾰ], ῶνος, ὁ,
Aeolic dialect ἄγωνος, ου, ὁ, [Refs 7th c.BC+ [7th-6th c.BC: Alcaeus Lyricus 121 (also E.cited in Scholia Il. “Oxy.” 1087.60)]]; Elean dative plural ἀγώνοιρ[Refs [“GDI” 1172.26]]: (ἄγω):—gathering, assembly, ἵζανεν εὐρὺν ἀ.[Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 23.258; λῦτο δ᾽ ἀ. 24.1, compare 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 8.200; νεῶν ἐν ἀγῶνι 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 15.428, compare 12th c.AD: Eustathius Episcopus Thessalonicensis 1335.57]]: especially assembly met to see games, frequently in [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 23]]; Ὑπερβορέων ἀ. Pi [Refs 4th c.BC+ [“P.” 10.30; κοινοὺς ἀ. θέντες 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Agamemnon” 845.]]

__2
place of contest, lists, course, βήτην ἐς μέσσον ἀ.[Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 23.685, compare 531, 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 8.260, 8th-7th c.BC: Hesiodus Epicus “Scutum Herculis” 312, 5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “P.” 9.114, and especially 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 5.50: proverbial, ἔξω ἀγῶνος]] out of the lists or course, i.e. beside the mark, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “P.” 1.44, 2nd c.AD: Lucianus Sophista “Anach.” 21: _plural_, κατ᾽ ἀγῶνας 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 8.259.]]

__II
assembly of the Greeks at the national games, ὁ ἐν Ὀλυμπίῃ ἀ.[Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 6.127; ὁ Ὀλυμπικὸς ἀ. 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Plutus” 583; Ἑλλάδος πρόσχημ᾽ ἀ. 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Electra” 682, compare 699]]:— hence, contest for a prize at the games, ἀ. γυμνικός, ἱππικός, μουσικός, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 2.91, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Leges” 658a, 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Plutus” 1163, compare 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 3.104; οἱ τῶν λαμπάδων ἀ. 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Ἀθηναίων Πολιτεία” 57.1]]; ἀ. τῶν ἀνδρῶν contest in which the chorus was composed of men, opposed to to παίδων or ἀγενείων (which see), [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 21.18, etc.]]; ἀ. στεφανηφόρος or στεφανίτης contest where the prize is a crown, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 5.102, 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Rhetorica” 1357a19]]; ἀ. χάλκεος, where it is a shield of brass, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “N.” 10.22; ἀ. θεματικός “IG” 14.739 (from Naples)]]; ἀργυρίτης δωρίτης[Refs 1st c.AD+ [1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus 2.820d:]] —hence many phrases, ἀγῶνα καταστῆσαι establish a contest, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Isocrates Orator 4.1; τιθέναι 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 5.8; ποιεῖν 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 3.104; οὐ λόγων τοὺς ἀ. προθήσοντες [prev. author] 3.67; προηγόρευέ τε ἀγῶνας καὶ ἆθλα προυτίθει 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 8.2.26; προκαλούμενος ἑαυτὸν εἰς ἀ. [prev. work] 1240]]; ψυχῆς ἀ. τὸν προκείμενον πέρι struggle for life and death, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Orestes” 847, compare “Ph.” 1330; πολλοὺς ἀ. δραμέονται περὶ σφέων αὐτῶν 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 8.102; λόγων γὰρ οὐ.. ἁγών, ἀλλὰ σῆς ψυχῆς πέρι 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Electra” 1492, compareinfr. 5.]]

future -ῐοῦμαι[Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Heraclidae” 992]], etc. (in passive sense, see infr. B); -ίσομαι only in late writers, as [Refs 3rd c.AD+ [3rd c.AD: Porphyrius Tyrius Philosophus “de Abstinentia - Porphyrii Opuscula” 1.31;]] -ισθήσομαι [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd c.AD: Aristides Rhetor 1.504J.]]: aorist ἠγωνισάμην[Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Supplices” 427]], etc.: perfect ἠγώνισμαι (in active sense) Id [Refs 5th c.BC+ [“Ion” 939, 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Vespae” 993, 5th-6th c.BC: Isocrates Orator 18.31]] (passive, see infr. B): aorist ἠγωνίσθην in passive sense, infr. B: active form ἀγωνίσας[Refs [“IG” 4.429 (from Sicyon):]] —

contend for the prize on the stage, of the rhapsode, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 5.67]]; of the playwright, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Acharnenses” 140, 419]]; of the actor, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 19.246, compare 250, 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Poetica” 1451a8]]; of the choragus, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 21.66: with _accusative_, δράματα “IG” 12(7).226 (from Amorgos)]]: generally, contend for victory, καλῶς.. ἠγώνισαι[Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Symposium” 194a, compare “Mx.” 235d]]; argue, ὅλῳ τῷ πράγματι about the question as a whole, [Refs [“Hp.Mi.” 369c]]; especially argue sophistically, opposed to διαλέγομαι, [Refs [“Tht.” 167e.]]

generally, struggle, exert oneself, with infinitive, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 4.87; εὖ ἀ. 5th c.BC: Lysias Orator 20.22, compare 1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus “Phocion” 37.]]

Κυρίου (Mat.12:46-49 13:55 28:10, Mrk.3:31-34, Luk.8:19-21, Jhn.2:12 7:3, 5 10 20:17, Act.1:14, 1Co.9:5) may have been sons of Joseph and Mary (Mayor, Ja., Intr. viff.; DB, i, 320ff.) or of Joseph by a former marriage (Lft., Gal., 252ff.; DCG, i, 232ff.), but the view of Jerome, which makes ἀ. equivalent to ἀνεψιός, is inconsistent with Greek usage. regard for others, respect, reverence, αἰδοῦς οὐδεμιῆς ἔτυχον[Refs 6th c.BC+ [6th c.BC: Theognis Elegiacus 1266, compare 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Heraclidae” 460]]; αἰ. τοκέων respect for them, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “P.” 4.218]]; τὴν ἐμὴν αἰδῶ respect for me, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Persae” 699]]; regard for friends, αἰδοῦς ἀχαλκεύτοισιν ἔζευκται πέδαις[Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Fragmenta” 595]]; especially regard for the helpless, compassion, αἰδοῦς κῦρσαι[Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Coloneus” 247]]; forgiveness, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Antipho Orator 1.26, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Leges” 867e (compare αἰδέομαι 11.2).]]

__II
usually praise, approve, opposed to νεικέω, ψέγω, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 10.249, 6th c.BC: Theognis Elegiacus 612, etc.; ἀνδρὸς ὃν οὐδ᾽ αἰνεῖν τοῖσι κακοῖσι θέμις 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Fragmenta” 673]]:— passive, ὑπὸ Σιμωνίδεω αἰνεθείς[Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 5.102; ἐπ᾽ ἔργμασιν ἐσθλοῖς 3rd c.BC: Theocritus Poeta Bucolicus 16.15.]]

__II.2
approve, advise, recommend [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 16.380, 403]]: with infinitive, recommend to do a thing, euphemistic for κελεύω, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Choephori” 555, 715: with]]participle, αἰνεῖν ἰόντα to commend one's going, [Refs [[prev. author] “Pers.” 643:]] —ὦ δεινὸν αἶνον αἰνέσας giver of dire counsel, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Philoctetes” 1380]]:— with accusative of things, to be content with, acquiesce in, γάμον[Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “P.” 3.13, compare “N.” 1.72, 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Eumenides” 469, “Supp.” 902, 1070 (Lyric poetry), 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Medea” 1157; θῆσσαν τράπεζαν αἰνέσαι [prev. author] Alcaeus2.]]

__II.3

absolutely, approve, ὁ δᾶμος αἰνεῖ[Refs [“IG” 9(1).119 (_Locrian dialect_).]]

to promise or vow, τινί τι or τινὶ ποιεῖν τι, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Philoctetes” 1398, 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Alcestis” 12.]]

__1. = μῦθος, a tale (Horn., al.).
__2. = Att. ἔπαινος, praise (Horn., al.): Mat.21:16 (LXX), Luk.18:43.
__3. In π., a decree (MM, VGT, see word).
† (AS)

αἶνος, ὁ,
(αἰνέω) poetry and Ionic dialect word, tale, story, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 23.652, 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 14.508, 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Supplices” 534 (Lyric poetry)]]; αἰνεῖν αἶνον to tell a tale, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. author] “Ag.” 1483 (Lyric poetry), 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Philoctetes” 1380]]: especially story with moral, fable, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th-7th c.BC: Hesiodus Epicus “Opera et Dies” 202, 7th c.BC: Archilochus Lyricus 86, 89; ἄκουε δὴ τὸν αἶνον 3rd c.BC: Callimachus Epicus “Iambi” 1.211]]: generally, saying, proverb, παλαιὸς αἶ.[Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Fragmenta” 508, compare 3rd c.BC: Theocritus Poeta Bucolicus 14.43]]; riddle, [Refs [Carm.Pop. 34.]]

__II
= Attic dialect ἔπαινος, praise, [NT+8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 23.795, 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 21.110, 5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “N.” 1.6; ἐπιτύμβιος αἶ. 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Agamemnon” 1547, compare 780, 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Coloneus” 707 (all Lyric poetry); ἄξιος αἴνου μεγάλου 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 7.107 (variant{ἐπαίνου}),cf. LXX.Psa.8.2, +others, NT.Luke.18.43.]]

__III
decree, resolution, τῶν Ἀχαιῶν[Refs [“IG” 4.926 (Epid.)]]; κατ᾽ αἶνον, opposed to κατὰ ψήφισμα, [Refs [“SIG” 672.15 (Delph.), compare “Etymologicum Magnum” 36.16.]]

Abbott-Smith / STEPBible (TBESG)
αἱρέω,
[in LXX for אמר hi., בּחר, etc. ;]
to take; Mid., -ομαι (M, Pr., 158 f.; MM, VGT, see word), to choose: Php.1:22, 2Th.2:13, Heb.11:25. (Cf. ἀν-, ἀφ-, δι-, ἐξ-, καθ-, περι-, προ-αιρέω.) †
(AS)

---

LSJ / STEPBible (TFLSJ)
αἱρέω,
imperfect ᾕρεον[Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 24.579]], Ionic dialect αἵρεον[Refs 8th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 6.31, but _contraction_ ᾕρει even in 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 17.463, ᾕρευν 8th-7th c.BC: Hesiodus Epicus “Scutum Herculis” 302]]: future αἱρήσω[Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 9.28, etc.:]]aorist 1 ᾕρησα late (ἀν-) [Refs 4th c.AD+ [4th c.AD(?): Quintus Smyrnaeus Epicus 4.40, etc.]]: perfect ᾕρηκα[Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Agamemnon” 267, 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 1.61, etc., _Ionic dialect_ ἀραίρηκα or αἵρηκα]] (ἀν-) [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 5.102]]: pluperfect ἀραιρήκεε[Refs [3.39]]:—middle, future αἱρήσομαι[Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 10.235, etc.]]: aorist 1 ᾑρησάμην[Refs 2nd c.BC+ [2nd c.BC: Polybius Historicus 38.13.7 assuming variant, 2nd c.AD: Galenus Medicus 19.53, etc.]]: perfect in middle sense ᾕρημαι[Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Aves” 1577, 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 5.6.12, 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 2.15, etc.]]: 3rd.pers.plural pluperfect ᾕρηντο[Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 1.62]]:—passive, future αἱρεθήσομαι[Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 2.13, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Menexenus” 234b; rarely ᾑρήσομαι [prev. author] “Prt.” 338c:]]aorist ᾑρέθην and perfect ᾕρημαι[Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 20.146, +others]]; perfect participle ἀραιρημένος[Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 4.66: plqf. ᾕρηντο 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 3.2.1, ἀραίρητο 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.191, etc.]] —From [root]ἑλ-: future ἑλῶ only late (δι-) [Refs [“Test.Epict.” 6.18]], (ἀν-) [Refs 1st c.BC+ [1st c.BC: Dionysius Halicarnassensis 11.18]], (καθ-) [Refs 1st c.AD+ [“APl.” 4.334 (1st c.AD: Antiphilus Epigrammaticus):]]aorist 1 εἷλα (ἀν-) [NT.Act.2.23], (ἀν-) [Refs [“epigram Gr.” 314.24 (from Smyrna)]]: elsewhereaorist 2 εἷλον[Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 10.561, etc.]], Epic dialect ἕλον[Refs [17.321]], Ionic dialect ἕλεσκε[Refs [24.752]]:— middle, future ἑλοῦμαι[Refs 1st c.BC+ [1st c.BC: Dionysius Halicarnassensis 4.75]], (ἀφ-) [Refs 2nd c.BC+ [2nd c.BC: Timostratus Comicus 5]], (δι-) [Refs 1st c.BC+ [1st c.BC: Dionysius Halicarnassensis 4.60]], (ἐξ-) [Refs 4th c.AD+ [4th c.AD: Alciphro Epistolographus 1.9]]: aorist 1 εἱλάμην[Refs [“epigram Gr.” 314.5 (from Smyrna)]], (ἀφ-) variant in [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd c.AD: Athenaeus Epigrammaticus 12.546a]], (δι-) [Refs 1st c.AD+ [“Anthologia Graeca” 9.56 (1st c.AD: Philippus Epigrammaticus)]]: elsewhere aorist 2 εἱλόμην[Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 16.139, etc.]], 2nd pers.singular ἤλεο[Refs 7th c.BC+ [7th-6th c.BC: Sappho Lyrica “Papyrus fragments” in 1787.6.3:—Cretan dialect forms αἰλεθῇ “Leg.Gort.” 2.21, ἀν-αιλῆθαι [prev. work]7.10, +others:] —the etymology is doubtful, and ἀγρέω (which see) probably has a different root.]

__A
active, take with the hand, grasp, seize, αἱ. τι ἐν χερσίν[Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 4.66]]; αἱ. τινὰ χειρός to take one by the hand, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 1.323]]; κόμης τινά[Refs 8th c.BC+ [[prev. work] 197; μ᾽ ἑλὼν ἐπὶ μάστακα χερσίν 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 23.76:]]participle ἑλών adverbially, κατακτεῖναί μ᾽ ἑλών[Refs 8th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Antigone” 497; ἄξω ἑλών 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 1.139, compare 5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “O.” 7.1]]; but ἔνθεν ἑλών having taken up [the song], [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 8.500.]]

__A.2
take away, ἀπ᾽ ἀπήνης ᾕρεον ἄποινα[Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 24.579.]]

__A.II
take, get into one's power, νῆας [Refs [[prev. work] 13.42]]; especially take a city,[Refs 5th c.BC+ [2.37, 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Philoctetes” 347, etc.]]; overpower, kill, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 4.457, etc.; ἕλοιμί κεν ἤ κε ἁλοίην 22.253]]:—frequently of passions, etc., come upon, seize, χόλος[Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 18.322; ἵμερος 3.446; ὕπνος 10.193; λήθη 2.34, etc.: with double _accusative_, τὸν δ᾽ ἄτη φρένας εἷλε 16.805]]; of disease, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Theaetetus” 142b.]]

__A.II.2
catch, take, ζωὸν ἑλεῖν[Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 21.102]]; take in hunting, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th-7th c.BC: Hesiodus Epicus “Scutum Herculis” 302, 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.36, etc.]]; overtake, in a race, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 23.345]]; get into one's power, entrap, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Coloneus” 764, etc.]]; in good sense, win over, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Memorabilia” 2.3.16, compare 3.11.11, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Lysis” 205e, etc.]]

__A.II.2.b
with participle, catch, detect one doing a thing, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Antigone” 385, 655; ἐπ᾽ αὐτοφώρῳ ἑλεῖν 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Ion” 1214; φῶρα ἐπὶ κλοπῇ ἑλεῖν 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Leges” 874b.]]

__A.II.3
generally, win, gain, κῦδος[Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 17.321; στεφάνους 5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “P.” 3.74, etc.; especially in games, Ἴσθμι᾽ ἑλὼν πύξ 4th-5th c.BC: Simonides Lyricus 158]]; with double sense, overcome and win, ἑλέτην δίφρον τε καὶ ἀνέρε[Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 11.328; ἕλεν Οἰνομάου βίαν παρθένον τε σύνευνον 5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “O.” 1.88, compare 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Trachiniae” 353:]] — passive, ἁγὼν ᾑρέθη the fight was won, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Coloneus” 1148.]]

__A.II.3.b
generally, get, obtain, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 359a, “Ti.” 64b, etc.]]

__A.II.4
as law-term, convict, τινά τινος[Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Nubes” 591, 4th c.BC: Isaeus Orator 9.36, 4th c.BC: Aeschines Orator 3.156; εἷλέ σ᾽ ἡ Δίκη 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Heracl.” 941, compare “Supp.” 608: with]]participle, αἱ. τινὰ κλέπτοντα to convict of theft, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Equites” 829, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Leges” 941d]]; ᾑρῆσθαι κλοπεύς (i.e. ὤν) [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Antigone” 493, compare 406.]]

__A.II.4.b
αἱ. δίκην, γραφήν get a verdict for conviction, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Antipho Orator 2.1.5, etc.]]; also ἑλεῖν τινα obtain a conviction against one, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Isaeus Orator 7.13]]; ἑλεῖν τὰ διαμαρτυρηθ έντα convict the evidence of falsehood, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Isocrates Orator 18.15.]]

__A.II.4.c
absolutely, get a conviction, οἱ ἑλόντες, opposed to οἱ ἑαλωκότες, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 21.11]]; δολίοις ἕλε Κύπρις λόγοις Aphrodite won her cause.., [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Andromache” 289, compare 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Leges” 762b, etc.]]

__A.II.4.d
of a thing or circumstances which convict, τοῦτ᾽ ἔστιν ὃ ἐμὲ αἱρεῖ[Refs [[prev. author] “Ap.” 28a.]]

__A.II.5
ὁ λόγος αἱρέει reason or the reason of the thing proves, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 2.33]]: with accusative person, reason persuades one, i.e. it seems good to one, [Refs [[prev. author] 1.132, 7.41]]; ὡς ἐμὴ γνώμη αἱ. [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 2.43; ὅπῃ ὁ λόγος αἱ. βέλτιστ᾽ ἂν ἔχειν 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 604c, compare “Lg.” 663d]]: with infinitive, [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [“R.” 440b; ὁ αἱρῶν λόγος 3rd c.BC: Chrysippus Stoicus 3.92]]; αἱρεῖ alone, proves, [Refs 1st c.AD+ [1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus 2.651b.]]

__A.II.5.b
τὸ αἱροῦν the sum due, [Refs 1st c.AD+ [PRyl. 167.25 (1st c.AD)]]; τὰ αἱροῦντα [τάλαντα][Refs 2nd c.BC+ [“PGrenf.” 2.23.14 (2nd c.BC), “PRyl.” 88.19 (2nd c.AD).]]

__A.III
grasp with the mind, understand, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Philebus” 17e, 20d, “Plt.” 282d.]]

__B
middle, with perfect ᾕρημαι (see. above), take for oneself, ἔγχος ἑλέσθαι take one's spear, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 16.140, etc.; ἐκ γαίας λίθον 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Fragmenta - American Journal of Philology” 199]]; δόρπον, δεῖπνον take one's supper, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 7.370, 2.399]]; πιέειν δ᾽ οὐκ εἶχεν ἑλέσθαι [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 11.584]]; Τρωσὶν.. ὅρκον ἑλ. obtain it from.., [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 22.119]]; and so in most senses of the active, with the reflexive force added.

__B.II
take to oneself, choose, ἕταρον[Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 10.235, compare 9.139, 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 16.149, etc.]]; prefer, τι πρό τινος[Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.87; τι ἀντί τινος 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 1.7.3, 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 2.15; τί τινος 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Philoctetes” 1101, compare 3rd c.BC: Theocritus Poeta Bucolicus 11.49.]]

__B.II.b
with infinitive, prefer to do, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.11, etc.; ἑλέσθαι μᾶλλον τεθνάναι 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Memorabilia” 1.2.16, compare 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Apologia” 38e; μᾶλλον ἂν ἕλοιτό μ᾽ ἢ τοὺς πάντας Ἀργείους λαβεῖν 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Philoctetes” 47: without μᾶλλον, 5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “N.” 10.59, 5th c.BC: Lysias Orator 2.62.]]

__B.II.c
αἱ. εἰ.. to be content if., [Refs 1st c.BC+ [“Anthologia Graeca” 12.68 (1st c.BC: Meleager Epigrammaticus).]]

__B.II.2
αἱ. τά τινων take another's part, join their party, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 3.63, etc.]]; αἱ. γνώμην to adopt an opinion, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 4.137.]]

__B.II.3
choose by vote, elect to an office, αἱ. τινὰ δικαστήν, στρατηγόν, etc., [Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. author] 1.96, 5th c.BC: Eupolis Comicus 117, etc.]]; τινὰς ἀριστίνδην Legal cited in [Refs 8th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 43.57; αἱ. τινὰ ἐπ᾽ ἀρχήν 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Meno” 90b; αἱ. τινὰ ἄρχειν [prev. author] “Ap.” 28e, compare 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 2.127.]]

__C
passive, to be taken, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.185, 191, 9.102]]; more commonly ἁλίσκομαι.

__C.2
see above [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus 11.3.]]

__C.II
passive to middle sense, to be chosen, in perfect ᾕρημαι[Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Agamemnon” 1209, etc.]]; Ionic dialect ἀραίρημαι[Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 7.118, 172, 173, +others; στρατηγεῖν ᾑρημένος 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Memorabilia” 3.2.1]]; ἐπ᾽ ἀρχῆς ᾑρῆσθαι[Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. work] 3.3.2; ἐπὶ τὴν τῶν παίδων ἀρχήν 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Leges” 809a]]; τοῦ ἔτους.. ᾑρημένοι elected for the year.., [Refs [“IGRom.” 3.1422 (Bithyn.):]] —aorist ᾑρέθην is always so used, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Septem contra Thebas” 505, 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Aves” 799, 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 7.31, etc.]]; present rarely, αἱροῦνται πρεσβευταί are chosen, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Politica” 1299a19, compare 5th-6th c.BC: Andocides Orator 4.16.]]

deep_entry:
Abbott-Smith / STEPBible (TBESG)
αἵρεσις, -εως, ἡ
(αἱρέω, -ομαι), [in LXX for נְדָבָה,]
__1. capture.
__2. choosing, choice (see MM, VGT, see word).
__3. that which is chosen, hence, opinion; esp. a peculiar opinion, heresy: 1Co.11:19, Gal.5:20, 2Pe.2:1 R, txt.
__4. In late writers (MM, VGT), of a set of persons professing particular principles or opinions, a school, sect, party, faction: Act.5:17 15:5 24:5,14 26:5 28:22, I Co, Ga, II Pe, l.with, R, mg. (Cremer, 614).
† (AS)

---

LSJ / STEPBible (TFLSJ)
αἵρεσις, εως, ἡ,
taking, especially of a town, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 4.1, etc.]]; ἡ βασιλέος αἵ. the taking by the king, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. author] 9.3; ἐλπίζων ταχίστην -σιν ἔσεσθαι 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 2.75]]; αἵ. δυνάμεως acquisition of power, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Gorgias” 513a]]:—generally, taking, receiving, ἐπιγενημάτων[Refs 2nd c.BC+ [“PTeb.” 27.66 (2nd c.BC).]]

__B
(αἱρέομαι) choice, αἵρεσίν τ᾽ ἐμοὶ δίδου[Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Prometheus Vinctus” 779; τῶνδε.. αἵρεσιν παρδίδωμι 5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “N.” 10.82]]; followed by relative, αἵ. διδόναι ὁκοτέρην.., εἰ.., etc., [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.11, compare 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 22.19]]; αἵ. προτιθέναι, προβάλλειν, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Theaetetus” 196c, “Sph.” 245b; εἰ νέμοι τις αἵρεσιν 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Ajax” 265; αἵρεσιν λαβεῖν 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 36.11; ποιεῖσθαι 5th-6th c.BC: Isocrates Orator 7.19; αἵ. γίγνεταί τινι 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 2.61]]; οὐκ ἔχει αἵρεσιν it admits no choice, [Refs 1st c.AD+ [1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus 2.708b.]]

__B.2
choice, election of magistrates, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 8.89, compare 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Politica” 1266a26, +others; αἱρέσει, opposed to κλήρῳ, 1300a19, etc.]]

__B.3
inclination, choice, πρός τινα Philipp. cited in [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 18.166, 2nd c.BC: Polybius Historicus 2.61.9, etc., compare “IG” 2.591b]]; opposed to φυγή, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-3rd c.BC: Epicurus Philosophus “Epistulae” 3p.62U.]]; περὶ αἱρέσεων καὶ φυγῶν, title of treatise by Epicurus.

__B.II
purpose, course of action or thought, like{προαίρεσις}, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Phaedrus” 256c; ἡ αἵ. τῆς πρεσβείας 4th c.BC: Aeschines Orator 2.11]]; αἵ. Ἐλληνική the study of Greek literature, [Refs 2nd c.BC+ [2nd c.BC: Polybius Historicus 39.1.3]]:—conduct, [Refs 2nd c.BC+ [PTeb. 28.10 (2nd c.BC).]]

__B.II.2
system of philosophic principles, or those who profess such principles, sect, school, [Refs 2nd c.BC+ [2nd c.BC: Polybius Historicus 5.93.8, 1st c.BC: Diodorus Siculus Historicus 2.29, Polystr. p.20 W., 1st c.BC: Dionysius Halicarnassensis “Amm.” 1.7, “Comp.” 2, +others, compare 1st c.BC: Cicero, M. but usually to be accused, τινός of a crime, φόνου[Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 5.70]]: with infinitive, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Vespae” 506]]; followed by ὡς.., [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Apologia” 38c]]; by ὡς with participle, [Refs [[prev. author] “Phdr.” 249d]]; ὑπό τινος by some one, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Eumenides” 99, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 565b: reversely, αἰτία ἔχει τινά 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 5.70, 71; αἰ. φεύγειν τινός 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Philoctetes” 1404]]; ἐν αἰτίᾳ εἶναι or γίγνεσθαι, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Hippocrates Medicus “περὶ ἄρθρων ἐμβολῆς” 67, 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Memorabilia” 2.8.6]]; αἰτίαν ὑπέχειν lie under a charge, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Apologia” 33b, 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 6.3.16; ὑπομεῖναι 4th c.BC: Aeschines Orator 3.139; φέρεσθαι 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 2.60]]; λαβεῖν ἀπό τινος[Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. work] 18; αἰτίαις ἐνέχεσθαι 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Crito” 52a; αἰτίαις περιπίπτειν 5th c.BC: Lysias Orator 7.1; εἰς αἰτίαν ἐμπίπτειν 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Theaetetus” 150a; αἰτίας τυγχάνειν 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator “Epistulae” 2.2; ἐκτὸς αἰτίας κυρεῖν 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Prometheus Vinctus” 332]]; ἐν αἰτίῃ ἔχειν hold one guilty, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 5.106; δι᾽ αἰτίας ἔχειν 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 2.60, etc.; ἐν αἰτίᾳ βάλλειν 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Tyrannus” 656]]; τὴν αἰτίαν ἐπιφέρειν τινί impute the fault to one, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.26; αἰτίαν νέμειν τινί 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Ajax” 28; ἐπάγειν 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 18.283; προσβάλλειν τινί 5th c.BC: Antipho Orator 3.2.4]]; ἀνατιθέναι, προστιθέναι, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Hippocrates Medicus “περὶ ἀρχαίης ἰητρικῇς” 21, 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Pax” 640, etc.]]; ἀπολύειν τινὰ τῆς αἰτίης to acquit of guilt, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 9.88, etc.]]

__2
in forensic oratory, invective without proof (opposed to ἔλεγχος), [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 22.23, compare 18.15.]]

__3
in good sense, εἰ.. εὖ πράξαιμεν, αἰτία θεοῦ the credit is his, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Septem contra Thebas” 4]]; δι᾽ ὅντινα αἰτίαν ἔχουσιν Ἀθηναῖοι βελτίους γεγονέναι are reputed to have become better, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Gorgias” 503b, cf. Alcaeus1.119a, 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Metaphysica” 984b19]]; ὧν.. πέρι αἰτίαν ἔχεις διαφέρειν in which you are reputed to excel, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Theaetetus” 169a]]; οἳ.. ἔχουσι ταύτην τὴν αἰ. who have this reputation, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. author] “R.” 435e, compare 5th-6th c.BC: Andocides Orator 2.12; αἰτίαν λαμβάνειν 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Leges” 624a.]]

__4
expostulation, μὴ ἐπ᾽ ἔχθρᾳ τὸ πλέον ἢ αἰτίᾳ[Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 1.69.]]

__II
cause, δι᾽ ἣν αἰτίην ἐπολέμησαν[Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus “Prooem.”, compare 3rd c.AD: Democritus Epigrammaticus 83, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Timaeus” 68e, “Phd.” 97a]] {αἰτιάζομαι}, etc.; on the four causes of [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus see “Ph.” 194b16, “Metaphorical” 983a26:—αἰ. τοῦ γενέσθαι or γεγονέναι 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Phaedo” 97a; τοῦ μεγίστου ἀγαθοῦ τῇ πόλει αἰτία ἡ κοινωνία [prev. author] “R.” 464b:]] — _dative_ αἰτίᾳ for the sake of, κοινοῦ τινος ἀγαθοῦ[Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 4.87, compare 1st c.BC: Dionysius Halicarnassensis 8.29:—αἴτιον compare (αἴτιος 11.2) is used like{αἰτία}]] in the sense of cause, not in that of accusation.

__III
occasion, motive, αἰτίαν ῥοαῖσι Μοισᾶν ἐνέβαλε gave them a the me for song, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “N.” 7.11; αἰτίαν παρέχειν 2nd c.AD: Lucianus Sophista “Tyr.” 13.]]

__IV
head, category under which a thing comes, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 23.75.]]

case in dispute, ἡ αἰ. τοῦ ἀνθρώπου μετὰ τῆς γυναικός[NT.Matt.10.10.]

__2
substantive, αἴτιος, ὁ, the accused, the culprit, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Choephori” 70, etc.]]; οἱ αἴ. τοῦ πατρός they who have sinned against my father, [Refs [[prev. work] 273]]:—with genitive of things, οἱ αἴ. τοῦ φόνου[Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. work] 117, compare 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Philoctetes” 590, 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 4.200.]]

__II
responsible for, with genitive of things, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.1, etc.]]; αἴτιός τινός τινι being the cause of a thing to a person, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Lysias Orator 13.57, compare 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 23.54, 5th-6th c.BC: Isocrates Orator 8.100]]: with infinitive, αἴ. τὸν ἠέρα ξηρὸν εἶναι[Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 2.26; τοῦ μὴ φαλακροῦσθαι [prev. author] 3.12, etc.; αἴ. θανεῖν 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Antigone” 1173; αἰ. πεμφθῆναι ἄγγελον 5th c.BC: Antipho Orator 5.23, compare 5th c.BC: Lysias Orator 13.82; αἴτιος τὸ σὲ ἀποκρίνασθαι 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Laches” 190e]]: comparative, τοῦ.. ἐλευθέραν εἶναι.. αἰτιώτερον[Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 24.5, compare 51.21: _superlative_ αἰτιώτατος, ἐν τῷ στενῷ ναυμαχῆσαι]] mainly instrumental in causing the sea-fight, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 1.74; αἰ. τοῦ μὴ ἀποθανεῖν 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 20.42; -ώτατόν τι καὶ τελέως δραστικόν 1st c.BC: Philodemus Gadarensis Epigrammaticus “D.” 1.23.]]

__II.2
αἴτιον, τό, cause, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Hippocrates Medicus “περὶ ἀρχαίης ἰητρικῇς” 6 (_plural_), 21, 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 7.125, 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Iphigenia Aulidensis” 939, 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 4.26, etc.]]; τί ποτ᾽ οὖν ἐστι τὸ αἴτιον τό.. μηδένα εἰπεῖ; [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 8.56; frequently in Philos., τὸ δ᾽ αἴ. τούτου εἶναι ὅτι.. 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Phaedo” 11oe, etc.]]

αἰών, -ῶνος, ὁ,
[in LXX chiefly for עַד ,עוֹלָם ;]
__1. in cl., like Lat. aevum (LS, MM, VGT, see word), a space of time, as, a lifetime, generation, period of history, an indefinitely long period; in NT of an indefinitely long period, an age, eternity, usually with prep. (MM, VGT);
__(a) of the past: ἀπ᾽ αἰ. (cf. Heb. מֵעוֹלָם), Luk.1:70;
__(b) of the future: εἰς τ. αἰ. (cf. לְעוֹלָם), forever, Mat.21:19; id., with neg., never, Jhn.4:14; more strongly, εἰς τὸν αἰ. τοῦ αἰ., Heb.1:8 (LXX); εἰς τοὺς αἰ., Mat.6:13; εἰς τοὺς αἰ. τῶν αἰ. (cf. Isa.45:17, עַד־עוֹלְמֵי עַד), Rom.16:27, LT; cf. also Eph.3:21, 2Pe.3:18, Ju 25, Rev.14:11.
__2. οἱ αἰ., the worlds, the universe, "the sum of the periods of time, including all that is manifested in them": He :12 11:3 (cf. 1Ti.1:17, where τῶν αἰ. are prob. "the ages or world-periods which when summed up make eternity".
__3. the present age (Heb. הָעוֹלָם הַזֶּה): ὁ αἰ., Mat.13:22; ὁ αἰ. οὗτος, Mat.12:32; ὁ νῦν αἰ., 1Ti.6:17; ὁ ἐνεστὼς αἰ., Gal.1:4; similarly, of the time after Christ's second coming (הָעוֹלָם הַבָּא), ὁ αἰ. ἐκεῖνος, Luk.20:35; ὁ αἰ. μέλλων, Mat.12:32; ὁ αἰ. ὁ ἐρχόμενος, Mrk.10:30.
SYN.: κόσμος, the ordered universe, the scheme of material things; οἰκουμένη, the inhabited earth; in contrast with both of which αἰ. is the world under aspects of time (cf. Westc. on Heb.1:2; Tr., Syn., §lix; Thayer, see word, αἰ.; Cremer, 74, 620; MM, VGT). (AS)

---

Αἰακιδᾶν, periphrastic for the Aeacidae, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Ajax” 645 assuming variant; ἀπέπνευσεν αἰῶνα 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Fragmenta” 801; ἐμὸν κατ᾽ αἰῶνα 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Septem contra Thebas” 219.]]

__I.2
age, generation, αἰ. ἐς τρίτον [Refs [[prev. work] 744]]; ὁ μέλλων αἰών posterity, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 18.199, compare 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Axiochus” 370c.]]

__II.2
space of time clearly defined and marked out, epoch, age, ὁ αἰὼν οὗτος this present world, opposed to ὁ μέλλων, [NT.Matt.13.22, cf. NT.Rom.12.2; ὁ νῦν αἰ. NT.1Tim.6.17, NT.2Tim.4.10]:—hence in plural, the ages, i.e. eternity, [LXX+1st c.BC+ [1st c.BC: Philodemus Gadarensis Epigrammaticus “D.” 3 “fragment” 84; εἰς πάντας τοὺς αἰ. LXX.Tob.13.4]]; εἰς τοὺς αἰ[LXX+NT [[prev. work]. __II.3
Αἰών, ὁ, personified, Αἰὼν Χρόνου παῖς[Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Heraclidae” 900 (Lyric poetry), compare “Corpus Hermeticum” 11, etc.]]; as title of various divine beings, [Refs 5th c.AD+ [5th-6th c.AD: Damascius Philosophus “de Principiis” 151, +others; especially=Persian Zervan, 10th c.AD: Suidas Legal icographus see at {Ἡρασκος}.]]

[Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Pythagoras Philosophus, = 10, “Theologumena Arithmeticae” 59.]]

of persons, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 2.134, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Protagoras” 335e]]; ἀ. σώματι, ῥώμῃ, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Memorabilia” 4.4.23, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Politicus” 310d, etc.]]; of cities and states, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 3.57, 5.28; ἀ. τὸ σῶμα ἀπὸ τῶν λ ἐτῶν μέχρι τῶν έ καὶ λ 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Rhetorica” 1390b9]]; ={τὰ τῶν νέων πράττειν} [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Hyperides Orator “Fragmenta” 122.]]

__I.2
flourish, abound in a thing, πλούτῳ[Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.29; παρασκευῇ πάσῃ 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 1.1; νεότητι [prev. author] 2.20; ναυσὶκαὶ χρήμασι 4th c.BC: Aeschines Orator 3.163.]]

__I.3
with infinitive, to be strong enough to do, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 3.1.25.]]

__II
of things, ἀ. ὁ πυρετός, ἡ νόσος is at its height, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Hippocrates Medicus “ἀφορισμοί” 2.29, “Epid.” 1.25, 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 2.49; τοῦ πάθους ἀκμάζοντος 1st c.BC: Philodemus Philosophus “περὶ παρρησίας” p.31 O.; ἀ. ὁ πόλεμος 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 3.3]]; of corn, to be ripe, [Refs [[prev. author] 2.19.]]

__II.2
ἡνίκα.. ἀκμάζοι [ὁ θυμός] when passion is at its height, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Timaeus” 70d; ἀκμάζουσα ῥώμη 5th c.BC: Antipho Orator 4.3.3]]; ἀκμάζει πάντα ἐπιμελείας δεόμενα require the utmost care, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 4.2.40.]]

__II.3
impersonal, with infinitive, ἀκμάζει βρετέων ἔχεσθαι 'tis time to.., [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Septem contra Thebas” 97 (Lyric poetry)]]; νῦν γὰρ ἀ. Πειθὼ.. ξυγκαταβῆναι now 'tis time for her to.., [Refs [[prev. author] “Ch.” 726.]]

Abbott-Smith / STEPBible (TBESG)
ἀκοή, -ῆς, ἡ
(ἀκούω), [in LXX: Exo.15:26, al. for שׁמע, its parts and derivatives, exc. Deu.11:22 (שׁמר) ;]
__1. hearing, the sense of hearing: 1Co.12:17, 2Pe.2:8; "Hebraic dative," ἀκοῇ ακούειν (frequently in LXX; V. M, Pr., 14, 75), Mat.13:14, Act.28:26.
__2. organ of hearing, the ear (Arist., al.; MM, VGT, see word): 2Ti.4:3-4; pl., Mrk.7:35, Luk.7:1, Act.17:20, Heb.5:11.
__3. a thing heard, i.e.,
__(a) a message, teaching: Jhn.12:38 and Rom.16:16,17" (LXX), Gal.3:2,5 R, mg.; λόγος ἀκοῆς, 1Th.2:13, Heb.4:2;
__(b) a report, rumour: with genitive, of person(s), Mat.4:24, 14:1, 24:6; Mrk.1:28 13:7 (Cremer, 82, 623; MM, VGT, see word).†
(AS)

---

LSJ / STEPBible (TFLSJ)
ἀκοή, ἡ,
Epic dialect ἀκουή· (ἀκοϝ, compare ἀκούω):— hearing, sound heard, ἕκαθεν δέ τε γίγνετ᾽ ἀ.[Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 16.634.]]

__2
thing heard, tidings, μετὰ πατρὸς ἀκουὴν ἱκέσθαι, βῆναι, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 2.308, 4.701]]; κατὰ τὴν Σόλωνος ἀκοήν according to Solon's story, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Timaeus” 21a]]; report, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “P.” 1.84, 90]]; ἀ. σοφοῖς thing for wise men to listen to, [Refs [[prev. work] 9.78]]; ἀκοῇ ἱστορεῖν, παραλαβεῖν τι by hearsay, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 2.29, 148; ἐπίστασθαι 5th c.BC: Antipho Orator 5.67, 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 4.126; ἐξ ἀκοῆς λέγειν 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Phaedo” 61d]]; τὰς ἀ. τῶν προγεγενημένων traditions, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 1.20; ἀκοαὶ.. λόγων [prev. author] 1.73]]; ἀκοὴν μαρτυρεῖν, προσάγειν, give, bring hearsay evidence, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 57.4; βαρὺν.. ἀκοῆς ψόφον “Anthologia Graeca” 6.220 (3rd c.BC: Dioscorides Epigrammaticus)]]; ἐκ γὰρ ἀκουῆς οἰκτίρω σε[Refs 6th c.AD+ [[prev. work] 7.220 (6th c.AD: Agathias Historicus et Epigrammaticus).]]

__II
sense of hearing, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.38, etc.]]; joined with ὄψις, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Phaedo” 65b, etc.; οἷς ὦτα μέν ἐστιν, ἀκοαὶδὲ οὐκ ἔνεισιν 1st c.AD: Philo Judaeus 1.474.]]

__II.2
act of hearing, ἐς ἀκοὰν ἐμήν to my hearing, my ear, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Prometheus Vinctus” 689; γᾶρυν ἀραρεῖν ἀκοαῖσι 4th-5th c.BC: Simonides Lyricus 41; ὀξεῖαν ἀ... λόγοις διδούς 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Electra” 30; ἀκοῇ κλύειν [prev. author] “Ph.” 1412]]; ἀκοαῖς δέχεσθαι, εἰς ἀκοὰς.. ἥκειν, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Iphigenia Taurica” 1496, “Ph.” 1480; δι᾽ ἀκοῆς αἰσθάνεσθαι 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Leges” 900a]]; ἀκοὴν ὑπειπών demanding a hearing, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Hercules Furens” 962; τοῖς ἀκροάμασι τὰς ἀ. ἀνατεθεικώς 2nd c.BC: Polybius Historicus 24.5.9.]]

__II.3
ear, ὀππάτεσσι δ᾽ οὖδεν ὄρημ᾽, ἐπιρρόμβεισι δ᾽ ἄκουαι[Refs 7th c.BC+ [7th-6th c.BC: Sappho Lyrica 2.12, compare 3rd c.BC: Apollonius Rhodius Epicus 4.17; ἀπεσθίει μου τὴν ἀ. 5th c.BC: Hermippus Comicus 52, compare 5th c.BC: Pherecrates Comicus 199]]; δυσὶν ἀκοαῖς κρίνειν with two ears, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Politica” 1287b27, compare “Pr.” 960a30, 3rd c.BC: Callimachus Epicus “Fragmenta” 106.5.]]

__III
hearing, listening to, ἀκοῆς ἄξιος[Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Theaetetus” 142d]]; εἰς ἀκοὴν φωνῆς within hearing of.., [Refs 1st c.BC+ [1st c.BC: Diodorus Siculus Historicus 19.41.]]

__IV
obedience, ἀ. ὑπὲρ θυσίαν ἀγαθή[LXX.1Ki.15.22.]

__V
in plural, place where supernatural voices are heard, [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [Inscriptiones Graecae 4.955.10 (Epid.), 5th-6th c.AD: Marinus Biographus “Procl.” 32; αἱ ἀ. τοῦ θεοῦ 2nd c.AD: Aristides Rhetor “Orationes” 47(23).13.]]

deep_entry:
Abbott-Smith / STEPBible (TBESG)
ἀκολουθέω, -ῶ
(ἀκόλουθος, following; ἀ- cop., κέλευθος, poët., away), [in LXX chiefly for הָלַךְ ;]
to accompany, follow: Mat.4:25, al. Metaphorical, of discipleship: Mat.9:9, Mrk.9:38, Jhn.12:26, al. Absol.: Mat.18:10; more freq., with dative (cl.), Mat.8:1, al.; before μετά, with genitive, (cl.; Eutherford, N.Phr., 458 f.), Luk.9:49; ὀπίσω, with genitive (Heb. הָלַךְ אָהֲרֵי), Mat.10:38 (cf. ἐξ-, ἐπ-, κατ-, παρ-, συν-ἀκολουθέω).
SYN.: (cl.) ἕπομαι, not in NT (see Cremer, 80; MM, VGT, see word). (AS)

---

LSJ / STEPBible (TFLSJ)
ἀκολουθ-έω,
follow one, go after or with him, frequently of soldiers and slaves:—mostly with dative person, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Plutus” 19, etc.; ἀ. τῷ ἡγουμένῳ 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 474c; with Preps., ἀ. μετά τινος 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 7.57, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Laches” 187e, 5th c.BC: Lysias Orator 2.27, etc.; τοῖς σώμασι μετ᾽ ἐκείνων ἠκολούθουν, ταῖς δ᾽ εὐνοίαις μεθ᾽ ὑμῶν ἦσαν 5th-6th c.BC: Isocrates Orator 14.15; ἀ. σύν τινι 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 7.5.3; κατόπιν τινός 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Plutus” 13: rarely with _accusative_, 4th-3rd c.BC: Menander Comicus 558: _absolutely_, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Politicus” 277e, 4th-3rd c.BC: Theophrastus Philosophus “Characteres” 18.8, etc.]]; ἀ. ἐφ᾽ ἁρπαγήν, of soldiers, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 2.98]]; ἀκολουθῶν, ὁ, as substantive, ={ἀκόλουθος}[Refs 4th c.BC+ [1, 4th-3rd c.BC: Menander Comicus “Adul.fragment” 1.]]

__2
of stars, follow in the diurnal rotation, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Autolycus Astronomus 2.2.]]

__II
metaphorically, follow, be guided by, τῇ γνώμῃ τινός[Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 3.38]]; τοῖς πράγμασιν, τοῖς τοῦ πολέμου καιροῖς, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 4.39, 24.95]]; obey, τοῖς νόμοις[Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Andocides Orator 4.19: with _accusative_ _neuter_, ἀ. ἅπαντα “PLille” 1.26.]]

__II.2
follow the thread of a discourse, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Phaedo” 107b, etc.]]

__II.3
of things, follow upon, to be consequent upon, consistent with, εὐλογία.. εὐηθείᾳ ἀ.[Refs [[prev. author] “R.” 400e, compare 398d]]; follow analogy of, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Historia Animalium” 499a10, +others]]

__II.3.b
absolutely, to be consequent, ὡς γένους ὄντος τοῦ ἀεὶ ἀκολουθοῦντος[Refs [“Top.” 128b4]]; as species to individual, [Refs [“GA” 768b13.]]

__II.4
absolutely, ἀκολουθεῖ it follows, [Refs 6th c.BC+ [[prev. author] “Cat.” 14a31.—Not in Trag.: first in 6th c.BC: Hipponax Iambographus 55, with ᾱ (assuming variant)]], elsewhere ; takes place of ἕπομαι in later Greek.
