deep_entry:
Abbott-Smith / STEPBible (TBESG)
ἀκούω,
[in LXX chiefly for שׁמע ]
to hear, listen, attend, perceive by hearing, comprehend by hearing.
__1. Intrans.: Mrk.4:3 7:37, Jas.2:5, Rev.2:7, al.; τ. ὠσίν, Mat.13:15 (LXX); with cogn. dative, ακοῇ ἀ. (see: ἀκοή), Mat.13:14, Act.28:26" (LXX) ; ὁ ἔχων ὦτα (οὖς) ἀκούειν, ἀκουσάτω, Mat.11:15, Mrk.4:23, Rev.2:7, al.
__2. Trans., prop. with accusative of thing(s), of thing heard, genitive of person(s), from whom heard (LS, see word): Act.1:4; with accusative of thing(s), Mat.12:19, Jhn.3:8 (Abbott, JG, 76), Act.22:9, al.; with dupl. accusative, Jhn.12:18, 1Co.11:18; with genitive of thing(s), Jhn.7:40 (Abbott, JV, 116); τ. φωνῆς (cf. Heb. שָׁמַע בְּקוֹל, Exo.18:19), Jhn.5:25, 28 Act.9:7 (on the distinction bet. this and ἀ. φωνήν, ib. 4, see M, Pr., 66; Field, Notes, 117; Abbott, Essays, 93f.); of God answering  prayer, Jhn.9:31, 1Jn.5:14, 15; with accusative of thing(s), before παρά, Jhn.8:26, 40 Act.10:22, 2Ti.2:2; id. before ἀπό, 1Jn.1:5; with genitive pars. before ptcp., Mrk.14:58, Luk.18:36, al. (On NT usage generally, see Bl., §36, 5; Cremer, 82.)
(AS)

ἀκούω:
Epic dialect imperfect ᾰκουον[Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 12.442:]]future ἀκούσομαι (active ἀκούσω first in [NT+4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Hyperides Orator “Epitaphius” 34 assuming variant, then in 3rd c.BC: Lycophron Tragicus 378, 686, 1st c.BC: Dionysius Halicarnassensis 5.57, NT.Matt.12.19, etc.:]]aorist ἤκουσα, Epic dialect ᾰκουσα[Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 24.223:]]perfect ἀκήκοα, Laconian dialect ἄκουκα[Refs 1st c.AD+ [1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus “Lycurgus” 20, “Ages.” 21]]; ἤκουκα is a late form, [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [“POxy.” 237 vii 23 (2nd c.AD)]]; later Ionic dialect ἀκήκουκα[Refs 3rd c.BC+ [3rd c.BC: Herodas Mimographus 5.49]]: pluperfect ἀκηκόειν[Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 2.52, 7.208; ἠκηκόειν 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Oeconomicus” 15.7]]; old Attic dialect ἠκηκόη[Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Vespae” 800, “Pax” 616, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Cratylus” 384b:]] —rare in middle, present (see. below [Refs [11.2)]]: Epic dialect imperfect ἀκούετο[Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 4.331]]: aorist ἠκουσάμην[Refs 2nd c.BC+ [2nd c.BC: Moschus Bucolicus 3.119]]:—passive, future ἀκουσθήσομαι[Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 507d]]: aorist ἠκούσθην[Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 3.38, 2nd c.AD: Lucianus Sophista “Somn.” 5]]: perfect ἤκουσμαι[Refs 1st c.BC+ [1st c.BC: Dionysius Halicarnassensis “Ars Rhetorica” 11.10, Ps.- 2nd c.AD: Lucianus Sophista “Philopatr.” 4]]; ἀκήκουσμαι is uncertain in [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd c.AD: Lucianus Sophista “Hist. Conscr.” 49]]: pluperfect ἤκουστο[Refs 4th c.BC+ [Anonymus cited in 4th c.BC: Demetrius Phalereus Rhetor “Demetrius on Style” 217]], (παρ-) [Refs 1st c.AD+ [1st c.AD: Josephus Historicus “Antiquitates Judaicae” 17.10.10. (ἀ-κοϝ-, compare κοέω)]]:—hear, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Homerus Epicus, etc.]]: properly with accusative of thing heard, genitive of person from whom it is heard, ταῦτα Καλυψοῦς ἤκουσα[Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 12.389, compare 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Tyrannus” 43, etc.; _genitive_ _person_ frequently omitted, πάντ᾽ ἀκήκοας λόγον [prev. author] “Aj.” 480, etc.]]; or the accusative of things, ἄκουε τοῦ θανόντος[Refs [[prev. author] “El.” 792, compare 793]]:—also with genitive _of things_, φθογγῆς, κτύπου, hear it, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 12.198 (as see l.), 21.237; λόγων 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Coloneus” 1187; once in 8th c.BC: Homerus Epicus]] in middle, ἀκούετο λαὸς ἀϋτῆς[Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 4.331.]]

__b
with genitive objecti, hear of, hear tell of, ἀ. πατρός[Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 4.114: frequently with]]participle, τεθνηῶτος (i.e. πατρός) ἀκούσῃς[Refs [1.289, etc.]]; but εἰ.. πατρὸς νόστον ἀ.[Refs 8th c.BC+ [[prev. work] 287; ἀ. περί τινος 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 19.270, compare 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Iphigenia Taurica” 964, 5th-6th c.BC: Isocrates Orator 5.72, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 358d, 358e; τι περί τινος 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 7.7.30.]]

__c
in Prose the person from whom thing is heard frequently takes preposition, ἀ. τι ἀπό, ἐκ, παρά, πρός τινος, first in [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 6.524, compare 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 3.62, 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Tyrannus” 7, 95, 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 1.125.]]

__d
less frequently with double genitive person et of things, hear of a thing from a person, as [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 17.115, 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 18.9.]]

__e
with participle or infinitive added, as εἰ πτώσσοντας ὑφ᾽ Ἕκτορι πάντας ἀκούσαι should he hear that all are now crouching under Hector, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 7.129, compare 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 7.10.θ, 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 2.4.12, 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 3.9]]; ἀ. αὐτὸν ὄλβιον εἶναι to hear [generally] that he is happy, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 24.543, compare 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 2.5.13, etc.:—also ἀ. τινὰ ὅτι or ὡς, Ἀτρεΐδην ἀκοετε ὡς.. 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 3.193]]; τὸν Δαίδαλον οὐκ ἀκήκοας, ὁτι..; [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Memorabilia” 4.2.33; ἀ. οὕνεκα 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Coloneus” 33.]]

__f
with genitive et participle, to express what one actually hears from a person, ταῦτ᾽.. ἤκουον σαφῶς Ὀδυσσέως λέγοντος[Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Philoctetes” 595]]; ἀ. τινὸς λέγοντος, διαλεγομένου, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Protagoras” 320b, 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Memorabilia” 2.4.1]]: rarely with accusative et participle, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Philoctetes” 614.]]

__2
know by hearsay, ἔξοιδ᾽ ἀκούων[Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Tyrannus” 105]]: present is used like a perfect, νῆσός τις Συρίη κικλήσκεται, εἴ που ἀκούεις[Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 15.403, compare 3.193]]; in Prose, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Gorgias” 503c, 2nd c.AD: Lucianus Sophista “Gall.” 13.]]

__3
absolutely, hearken, give ear, especially in proclamations, ἀκούετε λεῴ oyez! oyez! Susar.[Refs 5th c.BC+ [1, etc.: for 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Tyrannus” 1386 see at {πηγή} 2.]]

__4

of oracles, true, unerring, ἀλαθέα μαντίων θῶκον[Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “P.” 11.6, compare 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Philoctetes” 993, 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Ion” 1537]]; of dreams, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Septem contra Thebas” 710.]]

__II
of qualities or events, true, real, φίλος[Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Orestes” 424; ἀ. τὸ πραχθέν 5th c.BC: Antipho Orator 1.6]]; genuine, ἀ. εἶναι δεῖ τὸ σεμνόν, οὐ κενόν[Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-3rd c.BC: Menander Comicus 596.]]

__II.2
realizing itself, coming to fulfilment, ἀρά[Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Septem contra Thebas” 944.]]

__III
adverb ἀληθῶς, Ionic dialect -θέως, truly, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Simonides Lyricus 5.1, 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.11, +others, 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Supplices” 315, etc.]]

__III.b
actually, in reality, γένος τόδε Ζηνός ἐστιν ἀ.[Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. work] 585; ἀ. οὐδὲν ἐξῃκασμένα [prev. author] “Ag.” 1244, compare 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 1.22, etc.]]; τὴν ἀ. μουσικήν (i.e. οὖσαν) [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Antiphanes Comicus 209.6:]] —ὡς ἀ. in the true way, really, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Orestes” 739, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Phaedo” 63a, etc.; ἡ μὲν γὰρ ὡς ἀ. μήτηρ 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 21.149]]: comparative -εστέρως[Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 347e,]] -έστερον [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Antipho Orator 3.3.4]]: superlative -έστατα[Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Memorabilia” 4.8.1.]]

__III.2
neuter as adverb, proparoxytone ἄληθε; indeed? really? ironically, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Tyrannus” 350, “Ant.” 758, 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Cyclops” 241, 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Ranae” 840, “Av.” 174.]]

__III.3
τὸ ἀληθές truly, Ionic dialect τὠληθές[Refs 3rd c.BC+ [3rd c.BC: Herodas Mimographus 7.70.]]

__B
not forgetting, careful, γυνὴ χερνῆτις ἀ.[Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 12.433, compare 4th-5th c.AD(?): Nonnus Epicus “Dionysiaca” 24.233]]:—the sense honest is post- [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Homerus Epicus]] ἀληθ-ίζω, dye with genuine purple, [Refs [PHolm. 18.6.]]

__B.II
middle -ίζομαι, ={ἀληθεύω}, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.136, 3.72, 1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus 2.230b, 4th c.AD: Alciphro Epistolographus 3.39, 59.]]

short_definition: but — ἀλλά (ἀλλ᾽ usually bef. α and υ, often bef. ε and η, rarely bef. ο and ω, never bef. ι; Tdf., Pr., 93 f.; WH, App., 146),
deep_entry:
Abbott-Smith / STEPBible (TBESG)
ἀλλά (ἀλλ᾽ usually bef. α and υ, often bef. ε and η, rarely bef. ο and ω, never bef. ι; Tdf., Pr., 93 f.; WH, App., 146),
adversative particle,
stronger than δέ; prop. neuter pl. of ἄλλος, used adverbially, with changed accent; hence prop. otherwise, on the other hand (cf. Rom.3:31);
__1. opposing a previous negation, but: οὐ (μὴ) . . . ἀ., Mat.5:15, 17 Mrk.5:39, Jhn.7:16, al.; rhetorically subordinating but not entirely negativing what precedes, οὐ . . . ἀ., not so much . . . as, Mrk.9:37, Mat.10:20, Jhn.12:44, al.; with ellipse of the negation, Mat.11:7-9, Act.19:2, 1Co.3:6 6:11 7:7, 2Co.7:1, Gal.2:3, al.; in opposition to a foregoing pos. sentence, ἀ. οὐ, Mat.24:6, 1Co.10:23; οὐ μόνον . . . ἀ. καί, Jhn.5:18, Rom.1:32, al.; elliptically, after a negation, ἀ. ἵνα, Mrk.14:49, Jhn.1:8 9:3, al.; = εἰ μή (Bl., §77, 13; M, Pr., 241; but cf. WM, §iii, 10), Mat.20:23, Mrk.4:22.
__2. Without previous negation, to express opposition, interruption, transition, etc., but: Jhn.16:20 12:27, Gal.2:14; before commands or requests, Act.10:20 26:16, Mat.9:18, Mrk.9:22, al.; to introduce an accessory idea, 2Co.7:11; in the apodosis after a condition or concession with εἰ, ἐάν, εἴπερ, yet, still, at least, Mrk.14:29, 1Co.9:2, 2Co.4:16, Col.2:5, al.; after μέν, Act.4:17, Rom.14:20, 1Co.14:17; giving emphasis to the following clause, ἀλλ᾽ ἔρχεται ὥρα, yea, etc., Jhn.16:2; so with neg., ἀλλ᾽ οὐδέ, nay, nor yet, Luk.23:15.
__3. Joined with other particles (a practice which increases in late writers; Simcox, LNT, 166), ἀ. γε, yet at least, Luk.24:21, 1Co.9:2; ἄ ἤ., save only, except, Luk.12:51, 2Co.1:13; ἀ. μὲν οὖν, Php.3:8 (on this usage, see MM, VGT, see word).
(AS)

---

LSJ / STEPBible (TFLSJ)
ἀλλά,
conjunction, originally neuter plural of ἄλλος, otheruise: used adversatively to limit or oppose words, sentences, or clauses, stronger than δέ:

__I
in simple oppositions, but,

__I.1
after negative clauses, οὐ κακός, ἀλλ᾽ ἀγαθός[Refs 8th c.BC+ [6th c.BC: Theognis Elegiacus 212; οὐδὲ μὲν Ἕκτωρ μίμνεν, ἀλλ᾽.. ἐφορμᾶται 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 15.690, etc.]]

__I.1.b
after a simple negative, ἦ παραφρονεῖ; οὔκ, ἀλλ᾽ ὕπνος μ᾽ ἔχει[Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Vespae” 9, etc.]]

__I.1.c
frequently after οὐ μόνον, μὴ μόνον, with or without καί, οὐ μόνον ἅπαξ, ἀ. πολλάκις[Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Phaedrus” 228a, compare 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 3.59, 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Memorabilia” 1.4.13, etc.; without μόνον, οὐχ ἑσπέρας, ἀλλὰ καὶ μεσημβρίας 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Fragmenta” 1006: also after οὐχ (or μὴ (ὅτι, οὐχ (or μὴ) ὅπως]], either, not only.. but.., μὴ ὅτι ἰδιώτην τινά, ἀλλὰ τὸν μέγαν βασιλέα[Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Apologia” 40d; μὴ ὅτι κατὰ τὸ σῶμα, ἀλλὰ καὶ κατὰ τὴν ψυχήν [prev. author] “Smp.” 207e]]; or, not only not.. but.., οὐχ ὅπως κωλυταὶ.. γενήσεσθε, ἀλλὰ καὶ.. περιόψεσθε[Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 1.35; οὐχ ὅτι ὠργίζοντο, ἀλλ᾽ ἐζήλουν 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 19.265]]; the negative form is ἀλλ᾽ οὐδέ, μὴ ὅτι ὑπὲρ ἄλλου, ἀλλ᾽ οὐδὲ ὑπὲρ ἐμαυτοῦ δίκην εἴρηκα[Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Isaeus Orator 10.1, etc.]]

__I.2
in the apodosis of hypothetical sentences, still, at least, εἴπερ γάρ τε.. ἀλλά τε[Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 1.82, etc.: in Prose, especially ἀλλ᾽ οὖν.. γε or ἀλλά.. γε, εἰ καὶ σμικρά, ἀ. οὖν ἴση γε ἡ χάρις 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 3.140]]; εἰ μή (i.e. ὁρῶ), ἀλλ᾽ ἀκούω γε, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Gorgias” 470d, compare 5th-6th c.BC: Isocrates Orator 3.15, +others; εἰ μηδέν ἐστι τελευτήσαντι, ἀλλ᾽ οὖν τοῦτόν γε τὸν χρόνον ἧττον ἀηδὴς ἔσομαι 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Phaedo” 91b (in later Gk. ἀλλά γε]] may be in juxtaposition, εἰ ἄλλοις οὐκ εἰμὶ ἀπόστολος, ἀλλά γε ὑμῖν εἰμί[NT+8th c.BC+ [NT.1Cor.9.2, and ἀ. γε δή is found with vv. 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” in 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Phaedrus” 262a)]]; εἰ καὶ μετέχουσι.. ἀλλ᾽ οὐ.. [Refs 8th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Politica” 1282a11:—less frequently after Conjunctions of Time, as ἐπεὶ δή 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 14.151; ἐπεί 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Coloneus” 241.]]

__I.2.b
after [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Homerus Epicus, ἀ. is used elliptically, especially with _adverbs_ of Time, ὦ θεοὶ πατρῷοι, συγγένεσθέ γ᾽ ἀ. νῦν (i.e. εἰ μὴ πρότερον, ἀ. νῦν γε) 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Electra” 411, compare “Ant.” 552, 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Heraclidae” 565; ἀ. τῷ χρόνῳ [prev. author] “Med.” 912]]; ἐὰν οὖν ἀ. νῦν γ᾽ ἔτι, i.e.ἐὰν οὖν [μὴἄλλοτε], ἀ. νῦν γε.. if then now at least ye still.., [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 3.33, compare 5th c.BC: Lysias Orator 10.15]]:—without an adverb of Time, at least, ἡ δ᾽ ἀ. πρός σε μικρὸν εἰπάτω μόνον[Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Pax” 660, compare 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Coloneus” 1276, 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Hercules Furens” 331.]]

__I.3
sometimes = ἀλλ᾽ ἤ (which see), except, but, οὔτι μοι αἴτιος ἄλλος, ἀ... τοκῆε no one else, but.., [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 8.312; οὐδέ τις ἄλλη φαίνετο γαιάων, ἀ. οὐρανὸς ἠδὲ θάλασσα 12.404; ἔπαισεν οὔτις ἀ. ἐγώ 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Tyrannus” 1331; ἡδέα.. οὐκ ἔστιν ἀ. τούτοις 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Ethica Nicomachea” 1176a22, compare 1152b30]]: compare reverse process in our word but=be out, except:—sometimes with force of ἤ after comparatives, τάφον, οὐκ ἐν ᾧ κεῖνται μᾶλλον, ἀ.ἐν ᾧ ἡ δόξα κτλ. not that in which they are lying, but far more.., [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 2.43; οὐχ ὅπλων τὸ πλέον, ἀ. δαπάνης [prev. author] 1.83.]]

__I.4
with negative after an affirmative word or clause, to be rendered simply by not, ἀγαθῶν, ἀ. οὐχὶ κακῶν αἴτιον[Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Lysias Orator 14.16; τῶν σπουδαίων, ἀ. μὴ τῶν φαύλων 5th-6th c.BC: Isocrates Orator 1.2; ἐκεῖθεν, ἀ. οὐκ ἐνθένδε ἡρπάσθη 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Phaedrus” 229d:—after a question, τί δεῖ ἐμβαλεῖν λόγον περὶ τούτου, ἀ. οὐχὶ προειπεῖ; 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 2.2.19, compare 5th-6th c.BC: Isocrates Orator 15.229, etc.]]

__I.4.b
without negative, μικρὸς μὲν ἔην δέμας, ἀ. μαχητής[Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 5.801.]]

__II
to oppose whole sentences,but, yet:

__II.1
frequently in transitions, as [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 1.135, 140, etc.; ἀ. καὶ ὥς.. 1.116]]; ἀ. οὐδ᾽ ὥς.. [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 1.6:—after 8th c.BC: Homerus Epicus]] in answers and objections, nay but.., well but.., frequently with negatives, especially in making and answering objections, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Acharnenses” 402, 407]]; also in affirmative answers, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Protagoras” 330b, “Grg.” 449a, etc.]]:—repeated in a succession of questions or objections, πότερον ᾔτουν σέ τι..; ἀ. ἀπῄτου; ἀ. περὶ παιδικῶν μαχόμενο; ἀ. μεθύων ἐπαρῴνησ; [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 5.8.4, compare 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Theages” 123e, 5th-6th c.BC: Isocrates Orator 17.47]]; ἀ. μήν.., answered by ἀ.., [Refs 8th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Politica” 1287a23:—in vehement answers 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus often uses νὴ τοὺς θεοὺς ἀ..., μὰ Δἴ ἀ.., “Grg.” 481c, “Phlb.” 36a, cf. Alcaeus1.110b, c:—at beginning of speech, to introduce a general objection, 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 4.472, compare 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Symposium” 1, 4th-3rd c.BC: Menander Comicus “Γεωργός” 22.]]

__II.2
with imperative or subjunctive, to remonstrate, encourage, persuade, etc., frequently in [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Homerus Epicus, ἀ. ἄγε, ἴθι, 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 1.210, 11.611; ἀ. ἴομεν 6.526; ἀ. πίθεσθε 1.259; after _vocative_, ὦ Φίντις, ἀ. ζεῦξον 5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “O.” 6.22, compare 7th c.BC: Tyrtaeus Elegiacus 10.15, etc.]]; answered by a second ἀ., ἀ. περιμένετε. ἀ. περιμενοῦμεν[Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 327b; ἀλλ᾽ ἕρπεθ᾽ ὡς τάχιστα 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Coloneus” 1643, compare “Ant.” 1029, etc.]]

__II.3
to break off a subject abruptly, ἀ. τά γε Ζεὺς οἶδεν[Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 15.523]]; ἀ. ταῦτα μὲν τί δεῖλέγει; [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Philoctetes” 11, compare “Tr.” 467, etc.]]

__II.4
in resuming an address after parenthesis, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “O.” 2.12, 4.7.]]

__II.5
in elliptical phrases, οὐ μὴν ἀ., οὐ μέντοι ἀ... it is not [so], but.., ὁ ἵππος πίπτει καὶ μικροῦ αὐτὸν ἐξετραχήλισεν· οὐ μὴν [ἐξετραχήλισεν] ἀ. ἐπέμεινεν ὁ Κῦρος it did not however [throw him], but.., [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 1.4.8; οὐ μέντοι ἀ. 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Symposium” 173b; οὐ γὰρ ἀ. 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Ranae” 58, 498:—after δέ, ὑμεῖς δέ μ᾽ ἀ. παιδὶ συμφονεύσατε 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Hecuba” 391.]]

__III
when joined with other Particles, each retains proper force, as,

__III.1
ἀλλ᾽ ἄρα, used by [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Homerus Epicus in transitions, 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 6.418, 12.320, etc.]]; later, to introduce an objection, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Apologia” 25a]]; in questions,ἀλλ᾽ ἆρα..; [Refs [[prev. author] “R.” 381b.]]

__III.2
ἀλλ᾽ οὖν, concessive, at all events, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Ranae” 1298; τοὺς πρώτους χρόνους ἀ. οὖνπροσεποιοῦνθ᾽ ὑμῖν εἶναι φίλοι 4th c.BC: Aeschines Orator 3.86]]; well then, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Protagoras” 310a]]; but then, however, with γε following, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 3.140, 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Antigone” 84, 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Cyclops” 652, 5th-6th c.BC: Isocrates Orator 3.18, etc.; ἀλλ᾽ οὖν γε in apodosi, see above 1.2.]]

__III.3
ἀλλὰ γάρ, frequently with words between, but really, certainly, as ἀλλὰ γὰρ Κρέοντα λεύσσω.., παύσω γόους, but this is irregular for ἀλλά, Κρέοντα γὰρ λεύσσω, παύσω γόους, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Phoenissae” 1308, compare 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Antigone” 148]]; for the regular order[Refs 8th c.BC+ [compare 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Philoctetes” 81, 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Heraclidae” 480, “Med.” 1067; frequently elliptical, the Verb being understood, 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 8.8, 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Prometheus Vinctus” 941, 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Antigone” 155: in 8th c.BC: Homerus Epicus]] only with negatives, ἀλλ᾽ οὐ γάρ[Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 7.242, 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 14.355, +others, compare 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Tyrannus” 1409]]; ἀ. γὰρ δή, ἀ. γάρ τοι, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Ajax” 167, “Ph.” 81.]]

__III.4
ἀ. εἰ.. quid si.. ?  [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 16.559.]]

__III.5
ἀ. ἦ in questions, chiefly of surprise or remonstrance, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Choephori” 220, 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Electra” 879, 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Acharnenses” 1111]]; ἀλλ᾽ ἦ, τὸ λεγόμενον, κατόπιν ἑορτῆς ἥκομε; [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Gorgias” 447a, compare “Prt.” 309c.]]

__III.6
ἀ. followed by strengthening Particle, ἀλλ᾽ ἤτοι μὲν ταῦτα θεῶν ἐν γούνασι κεῖται[Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 17.514; especially with _imperative_, 1.211, +others]]; ἀλλά τοι[Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 15.518, 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Persae” 795, etc.]]; ἀ. μέντοι, with or without γε, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Symposium” 214e, “Hp.Ma.” 287d, +others]]; ἀ. μήν, see at {μή; ἀ. δή}, mostly with words between, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Ajax” 1271, “OC” 586, 5th-6th c.BC: Isocrates Orator 4.109, etc.]]; without intervening words, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Apologia” 37c, +others; ἀ. δῆτα [prev. author] “Hp.Ma.” 285c; ἀ. μὲν δὴ καὶ αὐτός [prev. author] “Tht.” 143b, compare 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Electra” 103.]]

__IV
= et quidem, [Refs 6th c.AD+ [6th c.AD: Olympiodorus Philosophus “in Aristotelis Meteora commentaria - pars” 1.13, +others]]

__II
ἀ. τί τινος give in exchange, barter one thing for another, τῆς σῆς λατρείας τὴν ἐμὴν δυσπραξίαν.. οὐκ ἂν ἀλλάξαιμ᾽ ἐγώ[Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Prometheus Vinctus” 967; τι ἀντί τινος 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Alcestis” 661]]:— middle, τὴν παραντίκα ἐλπίδα.. οὐδενὸς ἂν ἠλλάξαντο[Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 8.82.]]

__II.2

__II.4
middle, ἔξω τρίβου ἀλλάσσεσθαι ἴχνος move one's position, [Refs [[prev. author] “El.” 103.]]

__III
take one thing in exchange for another, κάκιον τοὐσθλοῦ παρεόντος[Refs 6th c.BC+ [6th c.BC: Theognis Elegiacus 21]]; πόνῳ πόνον ἀ. to exchange one suffering with another (nisi to be read πόνου), [Refs [“Tragica Adespota” 7.3]]; ἠλλαττόμεσθ᾽ ἂν δάκρυα δόντες χρυσίον should take in exchange, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-3rd c.BC: Philemo Comicus 73: ἀ. θνητὸν εἶδος]] assume it, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Bacchae” 53, compare 1331:]] —more frequently in middle, τί τινος one thing for another, εὐδαιμονίας κακοδαιμονίαν[Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Antipho Orator 5.79, compare 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Leges” 733b]]; τὰ οἰκήϊα κακὰ ἀλλάξασθαι τοῖσι πλησίοισι exchange them with them, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 7.152]]: hence, buy, τι ἀντ᾽ ἀργυρίου[Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 371c; διά τινος ὠνῆς ἢ καὶ πράσεως ἀλλάττεσθαί τί τινι [prev. author] “Lg.” 915d, 915e]]; τοῦ παντὸς ἀ. prize above all things, [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [3rd-2nd c.BC: Philo Mechanicus “(Belopoeica) Excerpte aus Philons Mechanik - Ath. Berl. Akad.” 56.30.]]

__III.2
take a new position, i.e. go to a place, ἀ.Ἅιδα θαλάμους[Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Hecuba” 483; πόλιν ἐκ πόλεως 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Politicus” 289e.]]

__IV
absolutely, have dealings, as buyer or seller, in middle, πρός τινα[Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Leges” 915e.]]

__IV.2
alternate, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Empedocles Poeta Philosophus 17.6]]; σκῆπτρ᾽ ἔειν ἐνιαυτὸν ἀλλάσσοντε to enjoy power in turn, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Phoenissae” 74, compare 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Timaeus” 42c:]] —passive, ἀρεταὶ.. ἀλλασσόμεναι in turns, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “N.” 11.38, compare 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Problemata” 940a15]]. ϝ. passive, to be reconciled, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Fragmenta” 997.]]

other, another: absol., Mat.20:3, al.; ἄ. δέ, 1Co.3:10 12:8; pl., Mrk.6:15; attached to a noun, Mat.2:12 4:21, al.; with art., ὁ ἄ., the other, Mat.5:39, Jhn.19:32 (Bl., §47, 8); οἱ ἄ., the others, the rest, Jhn.20:25, 1Co.14:29; ἄ. πρὸς ἄλλον = πρὸς ἀλλήλους (BL, §48, 10), Act.2:12; ἄλλ᾽ (i.e. ἄλλο) ἤ (Bl., §77, 13), Luk.12:51; before πλήν, Mrk.12:32; εἰ μή, Jhn.6:22; παρά with accusative, 1Co.3:11.
SYN.: ἕτερος, which see ἄ. denotes numerical, ἕ. qualitative difference (Cremer, 89). ἄ. generally "denotes simply distinction of individuals, ἕ. involves the secondary idea of difference in kind" (see Lft., Meyer, Ramsay, on Gal.1:6, 7; Tr., Syn., §xcv; BL, §51, 6; M, Pr., 79f., 246; MM, VGT, s.vv.). As to whether the distinction can be maintained in 1Co.12:8, 10 see ICC, in l., and on Heb.11:35f., see Westc, in l. (AS)

ἄλλος, η, ο,
[Refs 5th c.AD+ [5th c.AD: Cypria αἶλος “Inscription Cyprian dialect” 135 H. (from Idalion): (from ἀλ]] yος, cf. Latin alius):—another, i. e. one besides what has been mentioned, either adjective or pronoun: when adjective, its substantive is either in the same case, or in genitive, Ζεῦ ἄλλοι τε θεοί[Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 6.476; θεῶν ἄ. 16.446:]] —ἄ. μέν.. ἄ. δέ.. one.. another.., more rarely the one.. the other..  (of two persons, etc.), [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 22.493, etc.]]; τὰ μέν.. ἄλλα δέ.. [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 6.147]], and Attic dialect; ἕτερον μέν.. ἄλλον δέ.. [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 9.313]]; ἄλλο μέν.. ἑτέρου δέ.. [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.32; θάτερον.. τὸ δ᾽ ἄλλο 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Iphigenia Taurica” 962.]]

__II
with τις, any other, οὐδέ τις ἄ. ἔγνω ἀλλ᾽ ἄρα Κασσάνδρη[Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 24.697; ἄ. τις 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 3.85]]; οὐδεὶς ἄ. no other, [Refs [[prev. passage]]]; ἄλλα πολλά[Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 9.639; πολλὰ καὶ ἄλλα 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 3.56; for εἴ τις ἄλλος [prev. author] 6.32, etc., and εἴ τις καὶ ἄ. 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 1.4.15, etc., see at {εἰ}.]]

__II.2
frequently with another of its own cases or derived Adverbs, ἄ. ἄλλα λέγει one man says one thing, one another, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 2.1.15; ἄ. ἄλλω᾽ ἔλεγεν 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Symposium” 220c; ἄ. ἄλλῃ ἐτράπετο 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 4.8.19]]; see at {ἄλλοθεν, ἄλλοσε, ἄλλοτε}; also with Verb in plural, παραλαμβάνων ἄ. ἄλλον ἐπ᾽ ἄλλου, τὸν δ᾽ ἐπ᾽ ἄλλου χρείᾳ.. ἐθέμεθα πόλιν ὄνομα[Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 369c, compare 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 2.1.4, etc.: _plural_, ἄλλοι]] when the several parties are plural, λείπουσι τὸν λόφον.. ἄλλοι ἄλλοθεν[Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 1.10.13.]]

__II.3
ἄ. καὶ ἄ., one and then another, one or two, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 1.5.12]]; ἄλλο καὶ ἄλλο one thing after another, [Refs [[prev. author] “Cyr.” 4.1.15]]; πρὸς ἄλλὡ καὶ ἄλλὡ σημείὡ to different points, [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [3rd c.BC: Euclides Geometra 1.7.]]

__II.4
repeated for emphasis, ἄ. ἄ. τρόπος quite another sort, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Phoenissae” 132.]]

__II.5
οὐδ᾽ ἄ. for οὐδέτερος, [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [3rd c.BC: Theocritus Poeta Bucolicus 6.45.]]

__II.6
with Article, ὁ ἄλλος, the rest, all besides; in plural, οἱ ἄλλοι (Ionic dialect contraction ὧλλοι) all the others, the rest, frequently from [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Homerus Epicus downwards (ἄλλοι in same signification, 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 2.1)]]; τὰ ἄλλα, contraction τἆλλα, all else, τἆλλα πλὴν ὁ χρυσός[Refs [“Scol.” 1 (Pytherm.)]]; in Attic dialect frequently as adverb, for the rest, especially in amendments to decrees, τὰ μὲν ἄλλα καθάπερ ὁ δεῖνα κτλ. [Refs 5th c.BC+ [“IG” 1.27a70, etc.: of Time, ={τὸν ἄλλον χρόνον}, 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Historia Graeca (Hellenica)” 3.2.2]]; ὁ ἄ. χρόνος, ={ὁ λοιπὸς χρόνος}, of the future, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Lysias Orator 14.4]] (but also of the past, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 20.16)]]; τῇ ἄλλῃ ἡμέρᾳ, τῷ ἄλλῳ ἔτει, next day, next year, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Historia Graeca (Hellenica)” 1.1.13, 1.2.1]]; οἵτε ἄλλοι καί.. all others and especially.., γυναῖκας ἄλλας τε πολλὰς καὶ δὴκαὶ βασιλέος θυγατέρα[Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.1, etc.]]; ἄλλα τε δὴ εἶπε, καί.. [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Theaetetus” 142c; (see. ἄλλως 1):]] —τὸ ἄλλο is much less frequently than τὰ ἄλλα.

__II.7
with Numerals, yet, still, further, τρίτον ἄ. γένος[Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th-7th c.BC: Hesiodus Epicus “Opera et Dies” 143]]; πέμπτος ποταμὸς ἄ. yet a fifth river, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 4.54, compare 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Septem contra Thebas” 486, 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Antigone” 1295, etc.]]

__II.8
in enumerations, as well, besides, ἅμα τῇγε καὶ ἀμφίπολοι κίον ἄλλαι with her their mistress came attendants also, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 6.84; μήτηρ ἠδὲ πατὴρ ἠδ᾽ ἄλλοι πάντες ἑταῖροι 9.367]]; οὐ γὰρ ἦν χόρτος οὐδὲ ἄ. δένδρον οὐδέν there was no grass nor any tree at all, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 1.5.5; πολιτῶν καὶ τῶν ἄλλων ξένων 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Gorgias” 473d]]; προσοφλὼν οὐ τὴν ἐπωβελίαν μόνον ἀλλὰ καὶ ἄλλην ὕβριν besides, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aeschines Orator 1.163:—pleonastic, παρ᾽ ἀγγέλων ἄλλων ἀκούειν 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Tyrannus” 7, compare 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 1.6.2; ἰδὼν ἐς πλησίον ἄλλον 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 4.81; γυναικῶν τῶν ἄλλων μία 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Medea” 945; μόνη τῶν ἄλλων ἐπιστημῶν 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Charmides” 166e]]; with comparative, frequently in [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Homerus Epicus, οὔτις σεῖο νεώτερος ἄ. Ἀχαιῶν 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 15.569, compare 22.106, +others]]; with superlative, ὀϊζυρώτατος ἄλλων[Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 5.105.]]

__III
less frequently, ={ἀλλοῖος}, of other sort, different, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 13.64, 21.22; ἄ. γέγονεν 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Phaedrus” 241a.]]

__III.2
in this sense, with genitive, ἄλλα τῶν δικαίων other than just, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Memorabilia” 4.4.25:]] —followed by ἤ.., with preceding _negative_, οὐδὲ ἄλλο.., οὐδὲν ἄλλο (or ἄλλο οὐδέν).., ἤ.. nothing else than.., [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.49, 7.168, 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 4.14; οὐδὲν ἄλλο γ᾽ ἤπτήξας 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Persae” 209]]; ἃ μηδὲν ἄλλο ἢ διανεῖταί τις which one only thinks, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Theaetetus” 195e:—more frequently in questions, τίς ἄλλος ἢ 'γώ..; 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Prometheus Vinctus” 440]]; τί δ᾽ ἄλλογ᾽ ἢπόνοι..; [Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. author] “Th.” 852: elliptically, τί ἄλλο (i.e. πάσχω) ἢ ἱπποκένταυρος γίγνομα; 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 4.3.20]]; τί ἄλλο (i.e. ἐποίησαν) ἢ ἐπεβούλευσα; [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 3.39:—followed by πλήν, 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Ajax” 125, 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Acharnenses” 39]]; by Preps., πρό..[Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 3.85]]; ἀντί.. [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Prometheus Vinctus” 467]]; παρά.. [Refs 8th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Phaedo” 80b, etc.: with _negative_, sometimes followed by ἀλλά, 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 18.403, 21.275:]] —see also ἄλλο τι.

__III.3
other than what is, untrue, unreal, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 4.348.]]

__III.4
other than right, wrong, bad, ἄλλου τινος ἡττῆσθαι yield to some unworthy motive, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 21.218, compare 1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus 2.187d, etc.]]; compare ἄλλως.

ἀλλότριος,
Aeolic dialect ἀλλότερρος [Refs [“Etymologicum Magnum” 529.24]], α, ον, (ἄλλος) of or belonging to another, βίοτος, νηῦς, ἄχεα, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 1.160, 9.535, 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 20.298]]; γυνή another man's wife, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Agamemnon” 448 (Lyric poetry)]]; ἀλλοτρίων χαρίσασθαι to be bountiful of what is another's, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 17.452]]; γναθμοῖσι γελοίων ἀλλοτρίοισιν with faces unlike their own, of a forced, unnatural laugh, [Refs [[prev. work] 20.347]]; ἀ. ὄμμασιν εἷρπον by the help of another's eyes, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Coloneus” 146(Lyric poetry)]]; οὐκ ἀ. ἄτην not inflicted by other hands, [Refs [[prev. author] “Ant.” 1259]]; but ἀ. φόνος murder of a stranger[Refs 5th c.BC+ [(compare 11.1), 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Euthyphro” 4b: proverbial, ἀ. ἀμᾶν θέρος]] reap where one has not sown, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Equites” 392, compare 8th-7th c.BC: Hesiodus Epicus “Theogonia” 599]]; ἀλλοτριωτάτοις τοῖς σώμασιν χρῆσθαι deal with one's body as if it belonged to another, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 1.70]]; τὰ ἀλλότρια, contraction τἀλλότρια, what belongs to others, not one's own, τἀ. ἀποστερεῖν, δειπνεῖν, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Agesilaus” 4.1, Theopomp. Comedy texts 34.]]

__II
opposed to οἰκεῖος, foreign, strange,

__II.1
of persons, ἀ. φώς stranger, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 18.219, compare 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Ranae” 481]]; almost = enemy, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 5.214, 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 16.102]]; οὐδέ τις ἀλλοτρίων no stranger, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 3.155; εἴτε ἀ. εἴτε οἰκεῖος ὁ τεθνεώς 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Euthyphro” 4b; ἀ. τῆς πόλεως 5th c.BC: Lysias Orator 28.6; οὐδείς ἐστί μοι ἀ., ἂν ᾖ χρηστός 4th-3rd c.BC: Menander Comicus 602]]; ἀλλοτριώτερος τῶνπαίδων less near than thy children, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 3.119]]; ἀλλοτριώτερος, opposed to οἰκειότερος, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Ethica Nicomachea” 1162a3: with _dative_, ἀλλότριοι ὑμῖν ὄντες 5th-6th c.BC: Isocrates Orator 14.51.]]

__II.1.b
hostile, unfavourably disposed, with genitive, ἀ. Ῥωμαίων[Refs 2nd c.BC+ [2nd c.BC: Polybius Historicus 28.4.4; -ώτατος μοναρχίας 1st c.BC: Diodorus Siculus Historicus 16.65; ἀλλότρια φρονῶν τοῦ βασιλέως 2nd c.BC: Polybius Historicus 36.15.7, compare “OGI” 90.19 (from Rosetta).]]

__II.1.c
disinclined, πρὸς τὰς κακοπαθείας[Refs 2nd c.BC+ [2nd c.BC: Polybius Historicus 36.15.2.]]

__II.2
of things, alien, strange, τροφή[Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 491d (_comparative_), etc.]]; εἴ τι πρότερον γέγονεν ἀ. estrangement, Canon Laws texts cited in [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 18.185; ἡ ἀ.]]alien country, enemy's country, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Lysias Orator 2.6, 5th-6th c.BC: Isocrates Orator 10.50, compare 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 8.73]]: with genitive, alien from, ἐπιτηδεύματα δημοκρατίας ἀ.[Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Lysias Orator 31.34]]; οὐδὲν ἀ. ποιῶν τοῦ τρόπου Canon Laws texts cited in [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 18.182.]]

__II.2.b
in Medicine texts, abnormal, [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd c.AD: Soranus Medicus 2.5, 2nd c.AD: Galenus Medicus 14.780]]; ἀ. σάρκες superfluous fat, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 556d.]]

__II.2.c
foreign to the purpose, λόγοι[Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Ethica Eudemia” 1218b23]]: comparative, [Refs [[prev. author] “EN” 1159b24]]: superlative, [Refs [[prev. author] “Cat.” 15b29, cf. Polystr. p.17 W.]]

__II.2.d
Astrology texts, ={ἀπόστροφος}, [Refs [“POxy.” 464.16.]]

__III
adverb ἀλλοτρίως, διακεῖσθαι πρὸς ἀλλήλας to be unfavourably disposed towards.., [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Lysias Orator 33.1, compare 5th-6th c.BC: Isocrates Orator 12.159]]; ἄ. ἔχειν πρός.. [Refs [[prev. author] 5.80]]: comparative -ιώτερον less favourably, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 18.9.]]

__III.2
strangely, marvellously, [Refs [epigram Gr. 989.2.]]

__III.3
in a manner foreign to, with genitive, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [3rd c.BC: Persaeus Citieus Stoicus 1.1co. [-ο ¯ τρ- only in 4th-3rd c.BC: Menander Comicus 557 assuming variant]]]

[Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 4.60]]; followed by τε.. δέ.., [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “P.” 4.79: also _neuter_ _plural_, ἀμφότερα μένειν πέμπειν τε 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Eumenides” 480; φιλοχρήματος καὶ φιλότιμος, ἤτοι τὰ ἕτερα τούτων ἢ ἀ. 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Phaedo” 68c; ἀ. ἄριστος καὶ στρατηγὸς καὶ ῥαψῳδός “Ion” 541b]]; by τε.. καί.., [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “O.” 1.104.]]

__3
dual in [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Homerus Epicus, as ἀ. Αἴαντε 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 12.265, +others]], less frequently in later writers, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 1.1.1, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Parmenides” 143c, 5th-6th c.BC: Isocrates Orator 4.134, etc.]]; but plural is much more frequently, and is found with a dual Noun, χεῖρε πετάσσας ἀμφοτέρας[Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 21.115.]] —Phrases: κατ᾽ ἀμφότερα on both sides, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 7.10.β, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Parmenides” 159a; ἐπ᾽ ἀμφότερα]]towards both sides, both ways, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 3.87, +others, 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 1.83, +others]]; ἀμφότερα, absolutely, on both sides, [Refs [[prev. work] 13, +others]]; ἀπ᾽ ἀμφοτέρων from or on both sides, Ξέρξεω ἀπ᾽ ἀ. ἀδελφεός[Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 7.97; παρ᾽ ἀμφοτέρων 1st c.BC: Diodorus Siculus Historicus 16.7, +others]]; μετ᾽ ἀμφοτέροισι one with another (assuming variant), [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [3rd c.BC: Theocritus Poeta Bucolicus 12.12]]; ἀμφοτέροις βλέπειν (i.e. ὄμμασι) [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [3rd c.BC: Callimachus Epicus “Epigrammata” 32.6]]; ἀμφοτέραις, Epic dialect -ῃσι (i.e. χερσί) [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 10.264]]; ἐπ᾽ ἀμφοτέροις βεβακώς (i.e. ποσί) [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [3rd c.BC: Theocritus Poeta Bucolicus 14.66.]]

__II
later, of more than two, all together, [NT+2nd c.AD+ [NT.Acts.19.16, “PLond.” 2.336.13 (2nd c.AD).]]

deep_entry:
Abbott-Smith / STEPBible (TBESG)
ἄν,
conditional particle,
which cannot usually be separately translated in English, its force depending on the constructions which contain it (see further, LS, see word; WM, §xlii; M, Pr., 165 ff.; MM, VGT, see word).
__1. In apodosis,
__(i) with indic, imperfect or aor., expressing what would be or would have been if (εἰ with impf., aor. or plpf.) some condition were or had been fulfilled: Luk.7:39  17:6, Jhn.5:46, Gal.1:10, Mat.12:7  24:43, 1Co.2:8, Act.18:14, 1Jn.2:19, al. The protasis is sometimes understood (as also in cl.): Mat.25:27, Luk.19:23. In hypothetical sentences, expressing unreality, ἄν (as often in late writers, more rarely in cl.) is omitted: Jhn.8:39  15:24 19:11, Rom.7:7, Gal.4:15;
__(ii) with opt., inf., ptcp. (cl.; see LS, see word; M, Int., §275; M, Pr., 167:4).
__2. In combination with conditional, relative, temporal, and final words;
__(i) as in cl., with subj.,
__(a) in protasis with εἰ, in Attic contr. ἐάν, which see;
__(b) in conditional, relative, and temporal clauses (coalescing with ὅτε, ἐπεί, etc.; see: ὅταν, ἐπάν, etc.), ever, soever;
__(α) with pres., ἡνίκα, 2Co.3:15; ὃς ἄν, Rom.9:15 (LXX) 16:2, al.; ὅσοι ἄν, Luk.9:5; ὡς ἄν, Rom.15:24 (M, Pr., 167);
__(β) with aor., ὃς ἄν, Mat.5:21, 22, 31; ἕως ἄν, until, Mat.2:13, Mrk.6:10, al.; ὡς ἄν, as soon as (M, Pr., 167), 1Co.11:34, Php.2:23. On the frequently use of ἐάν for ἄν with the foregoing words, see: ἐάν;
__(ii) in late Gk., when some actual fact is spoken of, with indic.: ὅταν (which see); ὅπου ἄν, Mrk.6:56 (M, Pr., 168); καθότι ἄν, Act.2:45 4:35; ὡς ἄν, 1Co.12:2.
__3. in iterative construction, with imperfect and aor. indic. (M, Pr., 167): Act.2:45 4:35, 1Co.12:2.
__4. with optative, giving a potential sense to a question or wish: Act.8:31 26:29.
__5. Elliptical constructions: εἰ μή τι ἄν (M, Pr., 169), 1Co.7:5; ὡς ἄν, with inf., as it were (op. cit. 167), 2Co.10:9.
(AS)

---

LSJ / STEPBible (TFLSJ)
ἄν, [ᾰ],
Epic dialect, Lyric poetry, Ionic dialect, [Refs 4th c.AD+ [4th c.AD(?): Arcadius Grammaticus]], Attic dialect; also κεν) Epic dialect, Aeolic dialect, Thess., κᾱ Doric dialect, Boeotian dialect, El.; the two combined in Epic dialect (below [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 11.2) and 4th c.AD(?): Arcadius Grammaticus]], εἰκ ἄν[Refs 4th c.BC+ [“IG” 5(2).6.2, 15 (4th c.BC)]]:—modal Particle used with Verbs to indicate that the action is limited by circumstances or defined by conditions. In [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Homerus Epicus]] κε is four times as common as ἄν, in Lyric poetry about equally common. No clear distinction can be traced, but κε as an enclitic is somewhat less emphatic; ἄν is preferred by [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Homerus Epicus]] in negative clauses, κε (ν) with the relative.

__A
In Simple Sentences, and in the Apodosis of Compound Sentences; here ἄν belongs to the Verb, and denotes that the assertion made by the Verb is dependent on a condition, expressed or implied: thus ἦλθεν he came, ἦλθεν ἄν he would have come (under conditions, which may or may not be defined), and so he might have come; ἔλθοι may he come, ἔλθοι ἄν he would come (under certain conditions), and so he might come.

__A.I
WITH INDICATIVE:

__A.I.1
with historical tenses, generally imperfect and aorist, less frequently pluperfect, never perfect, see below,

__A.I.1.a
most frequently in apodosis of conditional sentences, with protasis implying nonfulfilment of a past or present condition, and apodosis expressing what would be or would have been the case if the condition were or had been fulfilled. The imperfect with ἄν refers to continued action, in [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Homerus Epicus]] always in past time, except perhaps καί κε θάμ᾽ ἐνθάδ᾽ ἐόντες ἐμισγόμεθ᾽[Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 4. 178]]; later also in present time, first in [Refs 6th c.BC+ [6th c.BC: Theognis Elegiacus 905]]; πολὺ ἂν θαυμαστότερον ἦν, εἰ ἐτιμῶντο it would be far more strange if they were honoured, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 489a]]; οὐκ ἂν νήσων ἐκράτει, εἰ μή τι καὶ ναυτικὸν εἶχεν he would not have been master of islands if he had not had also some naval power, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 1.9]]. The aorist strictly refers only to past time, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “N.” 11.24, etc.]]; εἰ τότε ταύτην ἔσχε τὴν γνώμην, οὐδὲν ἂν ὧν νυνὶ πεποίηκεν ἔπραξεν if he had then come to this opinion, he would have accomplished nothing of what he has now done, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 4.5, +others]], but is used idiomatically with Verbs of saying, answering, etc., as we say I should have said, εἰ μὴ πατὴρ ἦσθ᾽, εἶπον ἄν σ᾽ οὐκ εὖ φρονεῖν[Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Antigone” 755, compare 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Symposium” 199d, “Euthphr.” 12d, etc.: the]]pluperfect refers to completed actions, as ὃ εἰ ἀπεκρίνω, ἱκανῶς ἂν ἤδη παρὰ σοῦ τὴν ὁσιότητα ἐμεμαθήκη I should have already learnt..,[Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. work] 14c; εἰ ὁ ἀνὴρ ἀπέθανεν, δικαίως ἂν ἐτεθνήκει 5th c.BC: Antipho Orator 4.2.3.]]

__A.I.1.b
the protasis is frequently understood: ὑπό κεν ταλασίφρονά περ δέος εἷλεν fear would have seized even the stout-hearted (had he heard the sound), [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 4.421]]; τὸ γὰρ ἔρυμα τῷ στρατοπέδῳ οὐκ ἂν ἐτειχίσαντο they would not have built the wall (if they had not won a battle), [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 1.11]]; πολλοῦ γὰρ ἂν ἦν ἄξια for (if that were so) they would be worth much, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 374d]]; οὐ γὰρ ἦν ὅ τι ἂν ἐποιεῖτε for there was nothing which you could have done, i. e. would have done (if you had tried), [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 18.43.]]

__A.I.1.c
with no definite protasis understood, to express what would have been likely to happen, or might have happened in past time: ἢ γάρ μιν ζωόν γε κιχήσεαι, ἤ κεν Ὀρέστης κτεῖνεν ὑποφθάμενος for either you will find him alive, or else Orestes may already have killed him before you, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 4.546]]; ὃ θεασάμενος πᾶς ἄν τις ἀνὴρ ἠράσθη δάϊος εἶναι every man who saw this (the 'Seven against Thebes') would have longed to be a warrior, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Ranae” 1022]]; especially with τάχα, which see, ἀλλ᾽ ἦλθε μὲν δὴ τοῦτο τοὔνειδος τάχ᾽ ἂν ὀργῇ βιασθὲν μᾶλλον ἢ γνώμῃ φρενῶν, i. e. it might perhaps have come, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Tyrannus” 523]]; τάχα ἂν δὲ καὶ ἄλλως πως ἐσπλεύσαντες (i.e. διέβησαν) and they might also perhaps have crossed by sea (to Sicily) in some other way, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 6.2, compare 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Phaedrus” 265b.]]

__A.I.1.d
ἄν is frequently omitted in apodosi with Verbs expressing obligation, propriety, or possibility, as ἔδει, ἐχρῆν, εἰκὸς ἦν, etc., and sometimes for rhetorical effect, εἰ μὴ.. ᾖσμεν, φόβον παρέσχεν it had caused (for it would have caused) fear, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Hecuba” 1113. This use becomes more common in later Gk.]]

__A.I.2
with future indicative:

__A.I.2.a
frequently in Epic dialect, usually with κεν, rarely ἄν, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 9.167, 22.66, indicating a limitation or condition, ὁ δέ κεν κεχολώσεται ὅν κεν ἵκωμαι]] and he will likely be angry to whom-soever I shall come, [Refs [[prev. work] 1.139]]; καί κέ τις ὧδ᾽ ἐρέει and in that case men will say,[Refs 8th c.BC+ [4.176; ἐγὼ δέ κέ τοι καταλέξω 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 3.80]]; so in Lyric poetry, μαθὼν δέ τις ἂν ἐρεῖ[Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “N.” 7.68, compare “I.” 6(5).59.]]

__A.I.2.b
rarely in codices of Attic dialect Prose writers, σαφὲς ἂν καταστήσετε[Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 1.140; οὐχ ἥκει, οὐδ᾽ ἂν ἥξει δεῦρο 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 615d, compare “Ap.” 29c, 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 2.5.13; uncertain in 5th c.BC: Hippocrates Medicus “γυναικεῖα” 2.174: in later Prose, 2nd-3rd c.AD: Philostratus Sophista “V A” 2.21, S 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “M.” 9.225: also in Poetry, 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Electra” 484, 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Aves” 1313; οὐκ ἂν προδώσω 3rd c.BC: Herodas Mimographus 6.36 (correlated -δοίην):— for ἄν with]]future infinitive and participle see below

__A.II
WITH SUBJUNCTIVE, only in Epic dialect, the meaning being the same as with the future indicative [Refs [(1.2a), frequently with _1st pers._, as εἰ δέ κε μὴ δώῃσιν, ἐγὼ δέ κεν αὐτὸς ἕλωμαι in that case]]I will take her myself, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 1.324]]; πείθευ, ἐγὼ δέ κέ τοι εἰδέω χάριν obey and if so I will be grateful, [Refs [14.235 (the _subjunctive_ is always introduced by δέ in this usage)]]; also with other persons, giving emphasis to the future, οὐκ ἄν τοι χραίσμῃ κίθαρις[Refs [3.54, +others]]

__A.III
WITH OPTATIVE (never future, rarely perfect πῶς ἂν λελήθοι [με]; [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Symposium” 3.6):]]

__A.III.a
in apodosis of conditional sentences, after protasis in optative with εἰ or some other conditional or relative word, expressing a future condition: ἀλλ᾽ εἴ μοί τι πίθοιο, τό κεν πολὺ κέρδιον εἴη[Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 7.28; οὐ πολλὴ ἂν ἀλογία εἴη, εἰ φοβοῖτο τὸν θάνατο; 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Phaedo” 68b:—in 8th c.BC: Homerus Epicus]] present and aorist optative with κε or ἄν are sometimes used like imperfect and aorist indicative with ἄν in Attic, with either regular indicative or another optative in the protasis: καί νύ κεν ἔνθ᾽ ἀπόλοιτο.. εἰ μὴ.. νόησε κτλ., i. e. he would have perished, had she not perceived, etc., [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 5.311, compare 5.388, 17.70]]; εἰ νῦν ἐπὶ ἄλλῳ ἀεθλεύοιμεν, ἦ τ᾽ ἂν ἐγὼ.. κλισίηνδε φεροίμην if we were now contending in another's honour, I should now carry.., [Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. work] 23.274: so rarely in Trag., οὐδ᾽ ἂν σὺ φαίης, εἴ σε μὴ κνίζοι λέχος (for εἰ μὴ ἔκνιζε) 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Medea” 568.]]

__A.III.b
with protasis in present or future, the optative with ἄν in apodosi takes a simply future sense: φρούριον δ᾽ εἰ ποιήσονται, τῆς μὲν γῆς βλάπτοιεν ἄν τι μέρος they might perhaps damage, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 1.142, compare 2.60, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Apologia” 25b, “R.” 333e; ἢν οὖν μάθῃς.. οὐκ ἂν ἀποδοίην 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Nubes” 116, compare 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 1.26, +others]]

__A.III.c
with protasis understood: φεύγωμεν· ἔτι γάρ κεν ἀλύξαιμεν κακὸν ἦμαρ[Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 10.269]]; οὔτε ἐσθίουσι πλείω ἢ δύνανται φέρειν· διαρραγεῖεν γὰρ ἄν for (if they should do so) they would burst, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 8.2.21]]; τὸν δ᾽ οὔ κε δύ᾽ ἀνέρε.. ἀπ᾽ οὔδεος ὀχλίσσειαν two men could not heave the stone from the ground, i. e. would not, if they should try, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 12.447; οὐδ᾽ ἂν δικαίως ἐς κακὸν πέσοιμί τι 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Antigone” 240, compare 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 2.8: in 8th c.BC: Homerus Epicus]] sometimes with reference to past time, Τυδεΐδην οὐκ ἂν γνοίης ποτέροισι μετείη[Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 5.85.]]

__A.III.d
with no definite protasis implied, in potential sense: ἡδέως δ᾽ ἂν ἐροίμην Λεπτίνην but I would gladly ask Leptines, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 20.129]]; βουλοίμην ἄν I should like, Latin velim (but ἐβουλόμην ἄν I should wish, if it were of any avail, vellem); ποῖ οὖν τραποίμεθ᾽ ἄ; which way then can we turn? [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Euthydemus” 290a]]; οὐκ ἂν μεθείμην τοῦ θρόνου I will not give up the throne, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Ranae” 830]]; idiomatically, referring to the past, αὗται δὲ οὐκ ἂν πολλαὶ εἶεν but these would not (on investigation) prove to be many, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 1.9]]; εἴησαν δ᾽ ἂν οὗτοι Κρῆτες these would be (i. e. would have been) Cretans, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.2: used in order to soften assertions by giving them a less positive form, as οὐκ ἂν οὖν πάνυ γέ τι σπουδαῖον εἴη ἡ δικαιοσύνη,]] i.e. it would not prove to be, etc. (for, it is not, etc.), [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “R.” 333e.]]

__A.III.e
in questions, expressing a wish: τίς ἂν θεῶν.. δοί;[Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Coloneus” 1100, compare 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Agamemnon” 1448; πῶς ἂν θάνοιμ; 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Ajax” 389: hence (with no question)]] as a mild command, exhortation, or entreaty, τλαίης κεν Μενελάῳ ἐπιπροέμεν ταχὺν ἰόν[Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 4.94]]; σὺ μὲν κομίζοις ἂν σεαυτὸν ᾗ θέλεις you may take yourself off (milder than κόμιζε σεαυτόν), [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Antigone” 444]]; χωροῖς ἂν εἴσω you may go in, [Refs [“El.” 1491; κλύοις ἂν ἤδη, Φοῖβε hear me now, Phoebus, [prev. work] 637]]; φράζοις ἄν, λέγοις ἄν, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Philebus” 23c, 48b.]]

__A.III.f
in a protasis which is also an apodosis: εἴπερ ἄλλῳ τῳ ἀνθρώπων πειθοίμην ἄν, καὶ σοὶ πείθομαι if I would trust any (other) man (if he gave me his word), I trust you, [Refs [[prev. author] “Prt.” 329b]]; εἰ μὴ ποιήσαιτ᾽ ἂν τοῦτο if you would not do this (if you could), [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 4.18, compare 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Memorabilia” 1.5.3, 3rd c.AD: Plotinus Philosophus 6.4.16.]]

__A.III.g
rarely omitted with optative in apodosis: ῥεῖα θεός γ᾽ ἐθέλων καὶ τηλόθεν ἄνδρα σαώσαι[Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 3.231, compare 14.123, 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 5.303]]; also in Trag., θᾶσσον ἢ λέγοι τις[Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Hippolytus” 1186; τεὰν δύνασιν τίς.. κατάσχο; 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Antigone” 605.]]

__A.III.h
ἄν with future optative is probably always corrupt (compare [Refs 5th c.BC+ [1.2b), as τὸν αὐτὸν ἂν ἐπαινέσοι (ἐπαινέσαι Bekk.) 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Leges” 719e]]; εἰδὼς ὅτι οὐδέν᾽ ἂν καταλήψοιτο (οὐδένα Bekk.) [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Lysias Orator 1.22.]]

__A.IV
WITH infinitive and participle (sometimes adjective equivalent to participle, τῶν δυνατῶν ἂν κρῖναι[Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 577b) representing _indicative_ or _optative_:]]

__A.IV.1
present infinitive or participle:

__A.IV.1.a
representing imperfect indicative, οἴεσθε τὸν πατέρα.. οὐκ ἂν φυλάττει; do you think he would not have kept them safe? (οὐκ ἂν ἐφύλαττεν), [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 49.35]]; ἀδυνάτων ἂν ὄντων [ὑμῶν] ἐπιβοηθεῖν when you would have been unable, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 1.73, compare 4.40.]]

__A.IV.1.b
representing present optative, πόλλ᾽ ἂν ἔχων (representing ἔχοιμ᾽ ἄν) ἕτερ᾽ εἰπεῖν παραλείπω[Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 18.258, compare 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 2.3.18: with _Article_, τὸ ἐθέλειν ἂν ἰέναι ἄκλητος ἐπὶ δεῖπνον 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Symposium” 174b.]]

__A.IV.2
aorist infinitive or participle:

__A.IV.2.a
representing aorist indicative, οὐκ ἂν ἡγεῖσθ᾽ αὐτὸν κἂν ἐπιδραμεῖ; do you not think he would even have run thither? (καὶ ἐπέδραμεν ἄν), [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 27.56]]; ἴσμεν ὑμᾶς ἀναγκασθέντας ἄν we know you would have been compelled, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 1.76, compare 3.89]]; ῥᾳδίως ἂν ἀφεθείς when he might easily have been acquitted, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Memorabilia” 4.4.4.]]

__A.IV.2.b
representing aorist optative, οὐδ᾽ ἂν κρατῆσαι αὐτοὺς τῆς γῆς ἡγοῦμαι I think they would not even be masters of the land (οὐδ᾽ ἂν κρατήσειαν), [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 6.37, compare 2.20]]; ὁρῶν ῥᾳδίως ἂν αὐτὸ ληφθέν (ληφθείη ἄν) [Refs [[prev. author] 7.42]]; οὔτε ὄντα οὔτε ἂν γενόμενα, i.e. things which are not and never could happen (ἃ οὔτε ἂν γένοιτο), [Refs [[prev. author] 6.38.]]

__A.IV.3
perfect infinitive or participle representing:

__A.IV.3.a
pluperfect indicative, πάντα ταῦθ᾽ ὑπὸ τῶν βαρβάρων ἂν ἑαλωκέναι (φήσειεν ἄν) he would say that all these would have been destroyed by the barbarians (ἑαλώκη ἄν), [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 19.312.]]

__A.IV.3.b
perfect optative, οὐκ ἂν ἡγοῦμαι αὐτοὺς δίκην ἀξίαν δεδωκέναι, εἰ.. καταψηφίσαισθε I do not believe they would (then) have suffered (δεδωκότες ἂν εἶεν) punishment enough, etc., [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Lysias Orator 27.9.]]

__A.IV.4
future infinitive or participle, never in Epic dialect, and probably always corrupt in Attic dialect, νομίζων μέγιστον ἂν σφᾶς ὠφελήσειν (to be read -ῆσαι) [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 5.82, compare 6.66, 8.25, 71]]; participle is still more exceptional, ὡς ἐμοῦ οὐκ ἂν ποιήσοντος ἄλλα[Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Apologia” 30c (codices), compare 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 19.342 (variant)]]; both are found in later Gk., νομίσαντες ἂν οἰκήσειν οὕτως ἄριστα[Refs 2nd c.BC+ [2nd c.BC: Polybius Historicus 8.30.8, compare 1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus “Marcellus” 15, 2nd c.AD: Arrianus Historicus “Anabasis” 2.2.3]]; with participle, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-3rd c.BC: Epicurus Philosophus “De rerum natura - Wien. Stud.” 14.1, 2nd c.AD: Lucianus Sophista “Asin.” 26, 4th c.AD: Libanius Sophista “Orationes” 62.21, uncertain reading in 2nd c.AD: Arrianus Historicus “Anabasis” 6.6.5.]]

__B
IN DEPENDENT CLAUSE[Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus]]

__B.I
In the protasis of conditional sentences with εἰ, regularly with the subjunctive. In Attic εἰ ἄν is contracted into ἐάν, ἤν, or ἄν (ᾱ) (which see): [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Homerus Epicus has generally εἴ κε (or αἴ κε), sometimes ἤν, once εἰ δ᾽ ἄν 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 3.288, twice εἴπερ ἄν 5.224, 232. The protasis expresses either future condition (with apodosis of _future_ time) or general condition (with apodosis of repeated action): εἰ δέ κεν ὣς ἔρξῃς καί τοι πείθωνται Ἀχαιοί, γνώσῃ ἔπειθ᾽ ὅς.. if thus thou shalt do.., [prev. work] 2.364]]; ἢν ἐγγὺς ἔλθῃ θάνατος, οὐδεὶς βούλεται θνῄσκειν if death (ever) come near.., [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Alcestis” 671.]]

__B.I.2
in relative or temporal clauses with a conditional force; here ἄν coalesces with ὅτε, ὁπότε, ἐπεί, ἐπειδή, compare ὅταν, ὁπόταν, ἐπήν or ἐπάν (Ionic dialect ἐπεάν), ἐπειδάν: [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Homerus Epicus has ὅτε κε (sometimes ὅτ᾽ ἄν), ὁππότε κε (sometimes ὁπότ᾽ ἄν or ὁππότ᾽ ἄν), ἐπεί κε (ἐπεὶ ἄν 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 6.412)]], ἐπήν, εὖτ᾽ ἄ; see also εἰσόκε (εἰς ὅ κε):—τάων ἥν κ᾽ ἐθέλωμι φίλην ποιήσομ᾽ ἄκοιτιν whomsoever of these I may wish.., [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 9.397]]; ὅταν δὴ μὴ σθένω, πεπαύσομαι when I shall have no strength.., [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Antigone” 91]]; ἐχθρὸς γάρ μοι κεῖνος.. ὅς χ᾽ ἕτερον μὲν κεύθῃ ἐνὶ φρεσίν, ἄλλο δὲ εἴπῃ whoever conceals one thing in his mind and speaks another, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 9.312, compare 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 4.6, 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 1.21. — 8th c.BC: Homerus Epicus uses]]subjunctive in both the above constructions [Refs [(1 and 2)]] without ἄ; also Trag. and Comedy texts, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Ajax” 496, 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Equites” 805]]; μέχρι and πρίν occasionally take subjunctive without ἄν in prose, e.g. [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 1.137, 4.16]] (μέχρι οὗ), [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Phaedo” 62c, 4th c.BC: Aeschines Orator 3.60.]]

__B.I.3
in final clauses introduced by relative adverbs, as ὡς, ὅπως (of Manner), ἵνα (of Place), ὄφρα, ἕως, etc. (of Time), frequently in Epic dialect, σαώτερος ὥς κε νέηαι[Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 1.32; ὄφρα κεν εὕδῃ 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 3.359; ὅπως ἂν εἰδῇ.. φράσω 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Prometheus Vinctus” 824; ὅπως ἂν φαίνηται κάλλιστος 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Symposium” 198e; μηχανητέον ὅπως ἂν διαφύγῃ “Grg.” 481a (where ὅπως with _future_ _indicative_ is the regular _construction_)]]; also after ὡς in [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus, Trag., 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 2.5.16, +others, once in 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 6.91 (but _future_]] indicative is regular in _Attic dialect_); ἵνα final does not take ἄν or κε except ἵνα εἰδότες ἤ κε θάνωμεν ἤ κεν.. φύγοιμεν[Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 12.156 (ἵνα]] = where in [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Coloneus” 405). μή,]] = lest, takes ἄν only with optative in apodosis, as [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Trachiniae” 631, 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 2.93.]]

__B.II
in Epic dialect sometimes with OPTATIVE as with subjunctive (always κε (ν), except εἴ περ ἂν αὐταὶ Μοῦσαι ἀείδοιεν[Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 2.597), εἴ κεν Ἄρης οἴχοιτο 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 8.353]]; ὥς κε.. δοίη ᾧ κ᾽ ἐθέλοι that he might give her to whomsoever he might please,[Refs 8th c.BC+ [[prev. work] 2.54: so in 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus in final clauses, 1.75, 99:—in 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 23.135 ὥς κέν τις φαίη, κέν]] belongs to Verb in apodosis, as in ὡς δ᾽ ἂν ἥδιστα ταῦτα φαίνοιτο[Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 7.5.81.]]

__B.II.2
rarely in oratio obliqua, where a relative or temporary word retains an ἄν which it would have with subjunctive in direct form, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Trachiniae” 687, 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Memorabilia” 1.2.6, 5th-6th c.BC: Isocrates Orator 17.15; ἐπειδὰν δοκιμασθείην 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 30.6]]:—similarly after a preceding optative, οὐκ ἀποκρίναιο ἕως ἂν.. σκέψαιο[Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Phaedo” 101d.]]

__B.III
rarely with εἰ and INDICATIVE in protasis, only in Epic dialect:

__B.III.1
with future indicative as with subjunctive: αἴ κεν Ἰλίου πεφιδήσεται[Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 15.213:—so with _relative_, οἵ κέ με τιμήσουσι 1.175.]]

__B.III.2
with εἰ and a past tense of indicative, once in [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Homerus Epicus, εἰ δέ κ᾽ ἔτι προτέρω γένετο δρόμος 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 23.526]]; so Ζεὺς γάρ κ᾽ ἔθηκε νῆσον εἴ κ᾽ ἐβούλετο Oracle texts cited in [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.174, compare 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Lysistrata” 1099 (codex R), 3rd c.BC: Apollonius Rhodius Epicus 1.197.]]

__B.IV
in later Greek, ἄν with relative words is used with INDICATIVE in all tenses, as ὅπου ἂν εἰσεπορεύετο[NT+4th c.AD+ [NT.Mark.6.56; ὅσ᾽ ἂν πάσχετε “PFay.” 136 (4th c.AD)]]; ἔνθ᾽ ἂν πέφυκεν ἡ ὁλότης εἶναι[Refs 6th c.AD+ [6th c.AD: Philoponus, Joannes Philosophus “in Aristotelis Physica commentaria - Comm. in Arist. Graeca” 436.19]]; compare ἐάν, ὅταν.

__C
with imperfect and more rarely aorist indicative in ITERATIVE construction, to express elliptically a condilion fulfilled whenever an opportumty offered; frequently in [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus (not in 5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus or 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus), κλαίεσκε ἂν καὶ ὀδυρέσκετο]] she would (i. e. used to) weep and lament, 3.119; εἶτα πῦρ ἂν οὐ παρῆν[Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Philoctetes” 295]]; εἴ τινες ἴδοιεν.., ἀνεθάρσησαν ἄν whenever they saw it, on each occasion, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 7.71; διηρώτων ἂν αὐτοὺς τί λέγοιεν 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Apologia” 22b:]]infinitive representing imperfect of this construction, ἀκούω Λακεδαιμονίους τότε ἐμβαλόντας ἂν.. ἀναχωρεῖν, i. e. I hear they used to retire (ἀνεχώρουν ἄν), [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 9.48.]]

__D
GENERAL REMARKS:

__D.I
POSITION OF ἄν.

__D.I.1
in A, when ἄν does not coalesce with the relative word (as in ἐάν, ὅταν), it follows directly or is separated only by other particles, as μέν, δέ, τε, γάρ, καί, νυ, περ,, etc.; as εἰ μέν κεν.. εἰ δέ κε[Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 3.281- 4]]; rarely by τις, as ὅποι τις ἄν, οἶμαι, προσθῇ[Refs 8th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 2.14:—in 8th c.BC: Homerus Epicus and 8th-7th c.BC: Hesiodus Epicus]] two such Particles may precede κε, as εἴ περ γάρ κεν[Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 8.355, compare 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 2.123]]; εἰ γάρ τίς κε, ὃς μὲν γάρ κε, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th-7th c.BC: Hesiodus Epicus “Opera et Dies” 280, 357]]; rarely in Prose, ὅποι μὲν γὰρ ἄν[Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 4.45; ὁπότερος οὖν ἄν 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Ranae” 1420: also ὁπόσῳ πλέον ἄν 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Leges” 647e, compare 850a; ὅπου τὸ πάλαι λεγόμενον ἂν γίγνηται 739c.]]

__D.I.2
in apodosis, ἄν may stand either next to its Verb (before or after it), or after some other emphatic word, especially an interrogative, a negative (e. g. οὐδ᾽ ἂν εἷς, οὐκ ἂν ἔτι, etc.), or an important Adjective or Adverb; also after a participle which represents the protasis, λέγοντος ἄν τινος πιστεῦσαι οἴεσθ; do you think they would have believed it if any one had told them? (εἴ τις ἔλεγεν, ἐπίστευσαν ἄν), [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 6.20.]]

__D.I.3
ἄν is frequently separated from its infinitive by such Verbs as οἴομαι, δοκέω, φημί, οἶδα, etc., οὐκ ἂν οἴει..; frequently in [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus, “Grg.” 486d, +others]]; καὶ νῦν ἡδέως ἄν μοι δοκῶ κοινωνῆσαι I think that I should, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 8.7.25; οὕτω γὰρ ἄν μοι δοκεῖ ἥ τε πόλις ἄριστα διοικεῖσθαι 4th c.BC: Aeschines Orator 3.2]]; ἃ μήτε προῄδει μηδεὶς μήτ᾽ ἂν ᾠήθη τήμερον ῥηθῆναι (where ἄν belongs to ῥηθῆναι) [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 18.225:—in the phrase οὐκ οἶδ᾽ ἂν εἰ, or οὐκ ἂν οἶδ᾽ εἰ, ἄν belongs not to οἶδα, but to the Verb which follows, οὐκ οἶδ᾽ ἂν εἰ πείσαιμι, for οὐκ οἶδα εἰ πείσαιμι ἄν, 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Medea” 941, cf. Alcaeus48; οὐκ ἂν οἶδ᾽ εἰ δυναίμην 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Timaeus” 26b; οὐκ οἶδ᾽ ἂν εἰ ἐκτησάμην 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 5.4.12.]]

__D.I.4
ἄν never begins a sentence, or even a clause after a comma, but may stand first after a parenthetic clause, ἀλλ᾽, ὦ μέλ᾽, ἄν μοι σιτίων διπλῶν ἔδει[Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Pax” 137.]]

__D.II
REPETITION OF ἄν:—in apodosis ἄν may be used twice or even three times with the same Verb, either to make the condition felt throughout a long sentence, or to emphasize certain words, ὥστ᾽ ἄν, εἰ σθένος λάβοιμι, δηλώσαιμ᾽ ἄν[Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Electra” 333, compare “Ant.” 69, 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Agamemnon” 340, 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 1.76 (near the end), 2.41, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Apologia” 31a, 5th c.BC: Lysias Orator 20.15; ἀφανεῖς ἂν ὄντες οὐκ ἂν ὑμνήθημεν ἄν 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Troades” 1244, compare 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Fragmenta” 739]]; attached to a parenthetical phrase, ἔδρασ᾽ ἄν, εὖ τοῦτ᾽ ἴσθ᾽ ἄν, εἰ.. [Refs [[prev. author] “OT” 1438.]]

__D.II.2
ἄν is coupled with κε (ν) a few times in [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Homerus Epicus, as 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 11.187, 202, 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 5.361, +others; compare ἤν περ γάρ κ᾽ ἐθέλωσιν variant [prev. work] 18.318.]]

__D.III
ELLIPSIS OF VERB:—sometimes the Verb to which ἄν belongs must be supplied, in [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Homerus Epicus only εἰμί, as τάτ᾽ ἔλδεται ὅς κ᾽ ἐπιδευής (i.e. ᾖ) 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 5.481]]; ἀλλ᾽ οὐκ ἂν πρὸ τοῦ (i.e. ἔρρεγκον) [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Nubes” 5]]; τί δ᾽ ἂν δοκεῖ σοι Πρίαμος (i.e. πρᾶξαι), εἰ τάδ᾽ ἤνυσε;[Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Agamemnon” 935:]] —so in phrases like{πῶς γὰρ ἄν}; and πῶς οὐκ ἄν (i.e. εἴη); also in ὥσπερ ἂν εἰ (or ὡσπερανεί), as φοβούμενος ὥσπερ ἂν εἰ παῖς (i. e. ὥσπερ ἂν ἐφοβήθη εἰ παῖς ἦν) [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Gorgias” 479a]]; so τοσοῦτον ἐφρόνησαν, ὅσον περ ἂν (i.e. ἐφρόνησαν) εἰ..[Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Isocrates Orator 10.48:—so also when κἂν εἰ (={καὶ ἂν εἰ}) has either no Verb in the apodosis or one to which ἄν cannot belong, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 477a, “Men.” 72c]]; compare κἄν:—so the Verb of a protasis containing ἄν may be understood, ὅποι τις ἂν προσθῇ, κἂν μικρὰν δύναμιν (i. e. καὶ ἐὰν προσθῇ) [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 2.14]]; ὡς ἐμοῦ οὖν ἰόντος ὅπῃ ἂν καὶ ὑμεῖς (i.e. ἴητε) [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 1.3.6.]]

__D.IV
ELLIPSIS OF ἄν:—when an apodosis consists of several co-ordinate clauses, ἄν is generally used only in the first and understood in the others: πείθοι᾽ ἂν εἰ πείθοι᾽· ἀπειθοίης δ᾽ ἴσως[Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Agamemnon” 1049]]: even when the construction is continued in a new sentence, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 352e, compare 439b codices: but ἄν]] is repeated for the sake of clearness or emphasis,[Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. work] 398a, compare 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 19.156 (where an _optative_ is implied with the third ὡς): rarely expressed with the second of two co-ordinate Verbs and understood with the first, τοῦτον ἂν.. θαρσοίην ἐγὼ καλῶς μὲν ἄρχειν, εὖ δ᾽ ἂν ἄρχεσθαι θέλειν (i. e. καλῶς μὲν ἂν ἄρχοι, εὖ δ᾽ ἂν θέλοι ἄρχεσθαι) 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Antigone” 669.]]

__B
ἄν, [ᾱ], Attic dialect, ={ἐάν},{ἤν}, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 4.46 codices, +others; frequently in 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus, ἂν σωφρονῇ “Phd.” 61b]]; ἂν θεὸς θέλῃ[Refs 4th c.BC+ [[prev. work] 80d, compare 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 4.50; ἄν τ᾽.. ἄν τε 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Ἀθηναίων Πολιτεία” 48.4]]: not common in earlier Attic dialect Inscrr., [NT+4th c.BC+ [“IG” 1.2a5, 2.179b49, +others: but frequently later, “SIG” 1044.27 (4th-3rd c.BC), “PPetr.” 2p.47 (3rd c.BC), “PPar.” 32.19 (2nd c.BC), “PTeb.” 110.8 (1st c.BC), NT.John.20.23, etc.]]

__C
ἄν or ἀν, Epic form of ἀνά, (which see)

__D
ἄν, shortened from ἄνα, see entry ἀνά G.

Abbott-Smith / STEPBible (TBESG)
ἀνά
prep. (the rarest in NT; M, Pr., 98; MM, VGT, see word), prop.,
upwards, up, always with accusative
__1. In phrases: ἀ. μέσον, among, between, with genitive, Mat.13:1-58 25:1-46, Mrk.7:31, 1Co.6:5 (M, Pr., 99), Rev.7:17 [so in LXX for בְּתוׄך׃]; ἀ. μέρος, in turn, 1Co.14:27 (both found in Polyb.; cf. MGr. ἀνάμεσα).
__2. Distrib., apiece, by: Mat.20:9-10, Luk.9:3 (WH om.), Luk.9:14 Luk.10:1, Jhn.2:6, Rev.4:8.
__3. Adverbially ("a vulgarism," B1., § 51, 5; cf. Deiss., BS, 139 f.), ἀ. εἷς ἕκαστος, Rev.21:21.
As prefix, ἀ. signifies
__(a) up: ἀναβαίνειν;
__(b) to: ἀναγγέλλειν;
__(with) anew: ἀναγεννᾶν;
__(d) back: ἀνακάμπτειν.†
(AS)

LSJ / STEPBible (TFLSJ)
ἀνά [ᾰνᾰ],
Aeolic dialect, Thess., [Refs 4th c.AD+ [4th c.AD(?): Arcadius Grammaticus, 5th c.AD: Cypria]] ὀν, preposition governing genitive, dative, and accusative By apocope ἀνά becomes ἄν before dentals, as ἂν τὸν ὀδελό; ἄγ before gutturals, as ἂγ γύαλ; ἄμ before labials, as ἂμ βωμοῖσι, ἂμ πέτραις, etc.; ἀμπεπλεγμένας[Refs 4th c.AD+ [“IG” 5(2).514.10 (4th c.AD(?): Arcadius Grammaticus).]]

__A
WITH GEN., three times in [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey”, in phrase ἀνὰ νηὸς βαίνειν]] go on board ship, [Refs [2.416, 9.177, 15.284]]; ἂν τοῦ τοίχου, τᾶς ὁδοῦ, τοῦ ῥοειδίου, [Refs [“IG” 14.352i40, ii 15,83 (from Halaesa).]]

__B
WITH DAT., on, upon, without any notion of motion, Epic dialect, Lyric poetry, and Trag. (only Lyric poetry), ἀνὰ σκήπτρῳ upon the sceptre, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 1.15, 5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “P.” 1.6; ἂμ βωμοῖσι 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 8.441; ἀνὰ σκολόπεσσι 18.177; ἀνὰ Γαργάρῳ ἄκρῳ 15.152]]; ἀνὰ ὤμῳ upon the shoulder, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 11.128]]; ἀν ἵπποις, i. e. in a chariot, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “O.” 1.41; ἂμ πέτραις 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Supplices” 351 (Lyric poetry); ἀνά τε ναυσὶν καὶ σὺν ὅπλοις 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Iphigenia Aulidensis” 754; ἂγ Κόσσῳ “GDI” 1365 (from Epirus).]]

__C
WITH ACCU[Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus]], the common usage, implying motion upwards:

__C.I
of Place, up, from bottom to top, up along, κίον᾽ ἀν᾽ ὑψηλὴν ἐρύσαι[Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 22.176]]; ἀνὰ μέλαθρον up to,[Refs 8th c.BC+ [[prev. work] 239; [φλὲψ] ἀνὰ νῶτα θέουσα διαμπερὲς αὐχέν᾽ ἱκάνει 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 13.547; ἀνὰ τὸν ποταμόν 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 2.96]]; ἂν ῥόον up-stream, [Refs [“GDI” 5016.11 (from Gortyn)]]; κρῆς ἂν τὸν ὀδελὸν ἐμπεπαρμένον[Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Acharnenses” 796 (from Megarian)]]; simply, along, ἂν τὼς ὄρως[Refs [“Tab.Heracl.” 2.32.]]

__C.I.2
up and down, throughout, ἀνὰ δῶμα[Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 1.570]]; ἀνὰ στρατόν, ἄστυ, ὅμιλον,[Refs 8th c.BC+ [[prev. work] 384, 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 8.173, etc.; ἂγ γύαλα 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Supplices” 550 (Lyric poetry)]]; ἀνὰ πᾶσαν τὴν Μηδικήν, ἀνὰ τὴν Ἑλλάδα, [Refs 7th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.96, 2.135, etc.; ὀν τὸ μέσσον 7th-6th c.BC: Alcaeus Lyricus 18.3]]; ἀνὰ τὸ σκοτεινόν in the darkness, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 3.22.]]

__C.I.3
metaphorically, ἀνὰ θυμὸν φρονέειν, ἀνὰ στόμα ἔχειν, to have continually in the mind, in the mouth, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 2.36, 250]]; ἀν᾽ Αἰγυπτίους ἄνδρας among them, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 14.286]]; ἀνὰ πρώτους εἶναι to be among the first, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 9.86.]]

__C.II
of Time, throughout, ἀνὰ νύκτα all night through, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 14.80; ἀνὰ τὰς προτέρας ἡμέρας 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 7.223; ἀνὰ τὸν πόλεμον 8.123]]; ἀνὰ χρόνον in course of time, [Refs [1.173, 2.151, 5.27]]; ἀνὰ μέσσαν ἀκτῖνα (i. e. in the south) [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Coloneus” 1247.]]

__C.II.2
distributively, ἀνὰ πᾶσαν ἡμέραν day by day, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 2.37, 130, etc.; ἀνὰ πᾶν ἔτος 1.136, etc.; ἀνὰ πάντα ἔτεα 8.65: also ἀνὰ πρεσβύτᾱτα]] in order of age, [Refs [“Test.Epict.” 4.28.]]

__C.III
distributively with Numerals, κρέα εἴκοσιν ἀν᾽ ἡμιωβολιαῖα 20 pieces of meat at half an obol each, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Ranae” 554; τῶν ἀν᾽ ὀκτὼ τὠβολοῦ that sell 8]] for the obol, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Timocles Comicus 18]]; ἀνὰ πέντε παρασάγγας τῆς ἡμέρας [they marched] at the rate of [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5 parasangs a day, 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 4.6.4]]; ἔστησαν ἀνὰ ἑκατόν μάλιστα ὥσπερ χοροί they stood in bodies of about [Refs [100 men]]each. [Refs [[prev. work] 5.4.12]]; κλισίας ἀνὰ πεντήκοντα companies at the rate of [Refs [50]]in each, [NT.Luke.9.14]; ἔλαβον ἀνὰ δηνάριον a denarius apiece, [NT.Matt.20.10]; in doctor's prescriptions, ἀνὰ ὀβολὼ β[Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd c.AD: Soranus Medicus 1.63, etc.: also ἀνὰ δύο ἥμισυ ζῳδίων]]amounting to [Refs 4th c.BC+ [2 1/ 2 signs, 4th c.BC: Autolycus Astronomus 1.10]]; multiplied by, [Refs [PPetr. 3p.198.]]

__C.IV
Phrases: ἀνὰ κράτος up to the full strength, i. e. vigorously, ἀνὰ κράτος φεύγειν, ἀπομάχεσθαι, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 4.2.30, 5.3.12]]; ἀνὰ τὸν αὐτὸν λόγον and ἀνὰ λόγον proportionately, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Phaedo” 110d; especially in math. sense, [prev. author] “Ti.” 37a, 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Analytica Posteriora” 85a38, etc.]]; ἀνὰ μέσον in the midst, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Antiphanes Comicus 13, 4th-3rd c.BC: Menander Comicus 531.19; ἀνὰ μέρος]]by turns, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Politica” 1287n17.]]

__D
WITH NOM. of Numerals, etc., distributively, [NT+2nd c.AD+ [NT.Rev.21.21, see reading in 2nd c.AD: Soranus Medicus 1.11, 12, compare 4th c.AD: Oribasius Medicus “fragment” 50,54.]]

__E
WITHOUT CASE as adverb, thereupon, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Homerus Epicus]] and other Poets:— and with the notion of spreading all over a space, throughout, all over, μέλανες δ᾽ ἀνὰ βότρυες ἦσαν all over there were clusters, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 18.562, compare 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 24.343:]] —but ἀνά often looks like an adverb in [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Homerus Epicus]], where really it is only parted from its Verb by tmesis, ἀνὰ δ᾽ ἔσχετ; ἀνὰ δ᾽ ὦρτο (for ἀνῶρτο δέ); ἀνὰ τεύχε᾽ ἀείρας (for τεύχεα ἀναείρας), etc.

__F
IN COMPOSITION (joined with other words),

__F.1
as in C. 1, up to, upwards, up, opposed to κατά, as ἀνα-βαίνω, -βλέπω, ἀν-αιρέω, -ίστημι: poetry sometimes doubled, ἀν᾽ ὀρσοθύρην ἀναβαίνειν[Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 22.132.]]

__F.2
hence flows the sense of increase or strengthening, as in ἀνακρίν; though it cannot always be translated, as in Homer's ἀνείρομαι:—in this case opposed to ὑπό.

__F.3
from the notion throughout (E), comes that of repetition and improvement, as in ἀνα-βλαστάνω, -βιόω, -γεννάω.

__F.4
the notion of back, backwards, in ἀναχωρέω, ἀνανεύω, etc., seems to come from such phrases as ἀνὰ ῥόον up, i. e. against, the stream.

__G
ἄνα, written with anastrophe as adverb, up! arise! ἀλλ᾽ ἄνα[Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 6.331, 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 18.13]]:—in this sense the ultima  is never elided;[Refs 8th c.BC+ [compare ἀλλ᾽ ἄνα, εἰ μέμονάς γε 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 9.247; ἀλλ᾽ ἄνα ἐξ ἑδράνων 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Ajax” 194.]]

__G.2
apocopation ἄν after ὤρνυτο, ὦρτο, and up stood.. arose, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 3.268, 23.837, etc.]]

__G.3
when used as preposition ἀνά never suffers anastrophe.

deep_entry:
Abbott-Smith / STEPBible (TBESG)
ἀναβαίνω
[in LXX chiefly for עָלָה ;]
to go up, ascend,
__(a) of persons: ἐπί συκομωρέαν, Luk.19:4; εἰς τ. πλοῖον, Mrk.6:51; εἰς Ἱεροσόλυμα, Mat.20:17; εἰς τ. ἱερόν, with inf. (M, Pr., 205), Luk.18:10; with mention of place of departure, Mat.3:16 (ἀπό), Act.8:39 (ἐκ);
__(b) of things, to rise, spring up, come up: a fish, Mat.17:27; smoke, Rev.8:4; plants growing, Mat.13:7; metaphorically, of things coming up in one's mind (as Heb. לֵב אֵל עָלָה; 4Ki.12:4, al.), Luk.24:38, 1Co.2:9; of prayers, Act.10:4; messages, Act.21:31 (for late exx., see MM, VGT, see word)
(AS)
