LSJ / STEPBible (TFLSJ)
ἀναβαίνω,
imperfect ἀνέβαινον: future -βήσομαι: (for aorist 1 see infr. B): aorist 2 ἀνέβην, imperative ἀνάβηθι, -βῶ, -βῆναι, -βάς: perfect -βέβηκα:— middle, aorist 1 -εβησάμην, Epic dialect 3rd.pers.singular -εβήσετο, see infr. B:—passive, see below 11.2:— go up, mount, with accusative loci, οὐρανόν, ὑπερώϊα ἀ. go up to heaven, to the upper rooms, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 1.497, 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 18.302]]; φάτις ἀνθρώπους ἀναβαίνει goes up among, [Refs [[prev. work] 6.29]]; more frequently with preposition, ἀ. εἰς ἐλάτην, ἐς δίφρον, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 14.287, 16.657]]; rarely with ἀνά repeated, ἀν᾽ ὀρσοθύρην ἀ.[Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 22.132; after 8th c.BC: Homerus Epicus, most. frequently with ἐπί, ἀ. ἐπὶ τὰ ὑψηλότατα τῶν ὀρέων 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.131: with _dative_, νεκροῖς ἀ.]] to trample on the dead, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 10.493: _metaphorically_, ἐπειδὴ ἐνταῦθα ἀναβεβήκαμεν τοῦ λόγου 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 445c.]]

__II
Special usages:

__II.1
mount a ship, go on board, in [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Homerus Epicus]] mostly absolutely; ἐς Τροίην ἀ. embark for Troy, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 1.210; ἀπὸ Κρήτης ἀ. 14.252; ἐπὶ τὰς ναῦς 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 4.44, etc.: _metaphorically_, ἀναβάσομαι στόλον]] I will mount a prow, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “P.” 2.62.]]

__II.2
mount on horse-back (compare ἀναβάτης), ἀ. ἐφ᾽ ἵππον[Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 4.1.7, compare 7.1.3: _absolutely_, ἀναβεβηκώς]] mounted; ἀναβάντες (absolutely) ἐφ᾽ ἵππων ἐλάσαι[Refs [3.3.27]]; ἀ. ἐπὶ τροχόν mount on the wheel of torture, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Antipho Orator 5.40.]]

__II.2.b
with accusative, ἀ. ἵππον mount a horse, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Theopompus Historicus 2:]] —passive, [ἵππος] ὁ μήπω ἀναβαινόμενος that has not yet been mounted, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “de Equitandi ratione” 1.1]]; ἀναβαθείς when mounted,[Refs [[prev. work] 3.4; ἐν ἵππῳ ἀναβεβαμένῳ [prev. author] “Eq.Mag.” 3.4, compare 1.4.]]

__II.3
of land-journeys, go up from the coast into Central Asia, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 5.100, 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 1.1.2; ἀ. παρὰ βασιλέα 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus Alcaeus1.123b.]]

__II.3.b
go up to a temple, [“PPar.” 47.19, NT.Luke.18.10]; to a town, [NT+3rd c.AD+ [NT.Matt.20.18, +others, compare “PLond.” 3.1170b. 46 (3rd c.AD), etc.]]; in curses, ἀ. παρὰ Δάματρα πεπρημένος[Refs [“GDI” 3536.19 (from Cnidus), compare “SIG” 1180.9 ([prev. passage]).]]

__II.3.c
ascend to heaven, [Refs [“Ascens.Is.” 2.16.]]

__II.4
of rivers in flood, rise, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 2.13]]; ἀ. ἐς τὰς ἀρούρας overflow the fields, [Refs [[prev. author] 1.193.]]

__II.5
of plants, shoot up, ἐπὶ δένδρα[Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Oeconomicus” 19.18]]; climb on sticks, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-3rd c.BC: Theophrastus Philosophus “Historia Plantarum” 8.3.2]]; generally, shoot, spring up, [NT.Matt.13.7]; of hair, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Symposium” 4.23.]]

__II.6
in Attic dialect, ἀ. ἐπὶ τὸ βῆμα, or ἀ. alone, mount the tribune, rise to speak, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 18.66, 21.205, “Prooem.” 56]]; ἀ. εἰς τὸ πλῆθος, εἰς or ἐπὶ τὸ δικαστήριον come before the people, before the court, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Apologia” 31c, 40b, “Grg.” 486b]]; ἀ. ἐπὶ τὸν ὀκρίβαντα mount the stage, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. author] “Smp.” 194b: _absolutely_, ἀνάβαινε 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Equites” 149; ἀνάβηθι [prev. author] “V.” 963]]; of witnesses in court, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Lysias Orator 1.29.]]

__II.7
of the male, mount, cover, ἀ. τὰς θηλέας[Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.192, compare 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Fragmenta” 329; ἀ. ἐπί 1st c.AD: Philo Judaeus 1.651, compare 2nd c.AD: Moeris Grammaticus 3]]:—passive, [Refs 6th c.BC+ [“Milet.” 3.31 (a).6 (6th c.BC).]]

of things, abrogate, annul, ὅρους ἀνεῖλον πολλαχῇ πεπηγότας[Refs 6th c.BC+ [6th c.BC: Solon Lyricus 36.4; νόμον 4th c.BC: Aeschines Orator 3.39; διαθήκας 4th c.BC: Isaeus Orator 1.14; στήλας 5th-6th c.BC: Andocides Orator 1.103; ἀταξίαν 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 3.35, etc.; ἐκ μέσου ἀ. βλασφημίας [prev. author] 10.36; τηλικαύτην ἀνελόντας μαρτυρίαν [prev. author] 28.5]]; abolish, τὰς τῶν παρανόμων γραφάς[Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Ἀθηναίων Πολιτεία” 29.4]]:— passive, ἀνῄρηνται ὀλιγαρχίαι[Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 1.1.1.]]

take up in one's arms, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 16.8]]: hence, take up new-born children, own them, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus “Antonius” 36, compare 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Nubes” 531]]; take up an exposed child, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-3rd c.BC: Menander Comicus “Σαμία” 159, compare “BGU” 1110, etc.]]

mode of life, behaviour, [NT+2nd c.BC+ [2nd c.BC: Polybius Historicus 4.82.1, 3rd c.AD(?): Diogenes Laertius 0.64; -φὴν ποιεῖσθαι “IG” 2.477b12, compare “SIG” 491.5, LXX.Tob.4.14, NT.Gal.1.13, NT.Eph.4.22, +others; ἀ. πολιτική “PGiss.” 40ii29 (3rd c.AD)]]; ἐξημερωμένης -φῆς civilized life, [Refs 1st c.BC+ [1st c.BC: Philodemus Gadarensis Epigrammaticus “Sto.Herc.” 339.19.]]

relaxation, recreation, opposed to σπουδή, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Leges” 724a, 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Rhetorica” 1371b34, compare 4th-3rd c.BC: Cleanthes Stoicus 1.122; ἄ. καὶ σχολή 2nd c.BC: Polybius Historicus 1.66.10; ψυχῆς 3rd c.BC: Mnesitheus Atheniensis Medicus cited in 2nd c.AD: Athenaeus Epigrammaticus 11.484a.]]

__4
solution, [Refs 1st c.AD+ [1st c.AD: Dioscorides (Dioscurides) Medicus 5.96.]]

__5
={τὸ τελευταῖον τῆς παρακμῆς} [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd c.AD: Archigenes Medicus cited in 2nd c.AD: Galenus Medicus 7.424.]]

__II
indulgence, licence, ἡδονῶν[Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 561a; ἡ τῶν γυναικῶν παρ᾽ ὑμῖν ἄ. [prev. author] “Lg.” 637c, compare 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Politica” 1270a1; δούλων [prev. work] 1313b35]]; relaxation of custody, [NT.Acts.24.23.]

__III
of musical pitch, [Refs 3rd c.AD+ [3rd c.AD(?): Aristides Quintilianus Musicus 1.5]]; of an unaccented syllable, [Refs 1st c.BC+ [1st c.BC: Philodemus Philosophus “περὶ ποιημάτων” 2.18.]]

LSJ / STEPBible (TFLSJ)
ἄνευ,
Megarian and Hellenistic ἄνις (which see); ἄνευν[Refs 6th c.AD+ [“IG” 4.1484.58 (Epid.); ἄνευς “GDI” 1157 (6th c.AD: Olympiodorus Philosophus):]] —_preposition_ (never used in _composition_) with genitive (with accusative only [Refs [“GDI” [same place])]], without, opposed to σύν, ἄνευ ἕθεν οὐδὲ σὺν αὐτῷ 11.17.407; ἄ. κέντροιο without the goad, 23.387; μόνος ἄ. τινός[Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Lysistrata” 143, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Symposium” 217a]]; in pregnant sense, ἄ. θεῶν, mostly with negative, οὔτι ἄ. θεοῦ ἥδε γε βουλή[Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 2.372; οὔ τοι ἄ. θεοῦ ἔπτατο.. ὄρνις 15.531; οὐκ ἄ. θεῶν τινος 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Persae” 164; μηδὲ θύεσθαι μέν τιν᾽ ἰδίᾳ ἄ. τοῦ ἄρχοντος 4th c.BC: Aeneas Tacticus 10.4]]; also without negative, ἄ. ἐμέθεν without my knowledge and will, [Refs [11.15.213]]; ἄ. πολιτᾶν without their consent, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Choephori” 431; ἄ. τοῦ κραίνοντος 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Coloneus” 926]]; ἄ. τοῦ ὑγιεινοῦ without reference to health, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Gorgias” 518d, compare 519a; οὐκ ἐνδέχεται ζῆν ἄ. κακοῦ τινος 4th-3rd c.BC: Diphilus Comicus 32.12,etc.]]

__II
away from, far from, ἄ. δηΐων[Refs 5th c.BC+ [11.13.556; ἄ. ὄψου ποιεῖν τινας ἑστιωμένους 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 372c, compare “Hp.Ma.” 290e.]]

__III
in Prose, except, besides, πάντα ἄ. χρυσοῦ[Refs [[prev. author] “Criti.” 112c; ἄ. τοῦ καλὴν δόξαν ἐνεγκεῖν]]praeterquam quod attulerit.., [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 18.89]]; καὶ ἄ. τοῦ λαμβάνειν even without it, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 5.4.28.]]—In early writers it rarely follows its case, ὑφηγητοῦ δ᾽ ἄ.[Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Coloneus” 502; ὧν ἄ. 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 6.1.14]]; frequently in later Prose, as always in [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus, “Metaphorical” 1071a2, +others, compare 1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus 2.47c, etc.]] (Cf. Gothic inu, OHG. ᾱνο 'without'; perhaps akin to negative pref. ἀ-.)

ἀνευρ-ίσκω,
future -ευρήσω: aorist -εῦρον, later -ευράμην[Refs 3rd c.BC+ [3rd c.BC: Apollonius Rhodius Epicus 4.1133:]] —passive, aorist -ευρέθην:—find out, discover, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.67, 2.54, etc.; ἀγαθὰ ἀ. λογιζόμενος [prev. author] 7.8. ; ἀ. φόνον 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Agamemnon” 1094]]; σὸν χρέος ἀνευρίσκειν πότερον.. [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Iphigenia Taurica” 883; ἀ. τὴν αἰτίαν 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Phaedo” 100b; τὴν τοῦ θεοῦ φύσιν “Phdr.” 252e, etc.]]:—middle, win, gain, ἱερὸν χῶρον ἀνευρομένην[Refs [“epigram Gr.” 259]]:—passive, to be found out or discovered, ὡς ὕστερον ἀνευρέθη[Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 1.128]]: with participle, ἀνεύρηται ὁμοῖα παρεχομένη[Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 4.44.]]

deep_entry:
Abbott-Smith / STEPBible (TBESG)
ἀν-έχω
[in LXX chiefly for אָפַק hithp. ;]
to hold up; in NT always mid., to bear with, endure: in cl. most frequently with accusative, but in NT with genitive of person(s), Mat.17:17, Mrk.9:19, Luk.9:41, 2Co.11:1 11:19, Eph.4:2, Col.3:13; before μικρόν τι, with genitive of person(s) and with genitive of thing(s), 2Co.11:1; with dative of thing(s), 2Th.1:4 (v M, Th., in l); before εἴ τις, 2Co.11:20; absol., 1Co.4:12, 2Co.11:4; to bear with = to listen to, with genitive of person(s), Act.18:14; with genitive of thing(s), 2Ti.4:3, Heb.13:22 (cf. προσανέχω and MM, VGT, see word).†
(AS)

---

LSJ / STEPBible (TFLSJ)
ἀνέχω,
imperfect ἀνεῖχον: also ἀνίσχω, imperfect ἀνῖσχον: future ἀνέξω[Refs 7th c.BC+ [7th c.BC: Archilochus Lyricus 82, 2nd c.AD: Lucianus Sophista “Hist.Conscr.” 4(s. see l.), also ἀνασχήσω 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 5.106, 7.14, 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Iphigenia Aulidensis” 732]]: aorist ἀνέσχον[Refs [11.17.310, etc.]]; poetry ἀνέσχεθον[Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. work] 10.461, 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Medea” 1027]], Epic dialect infinitive ἀνσχεθέειν[Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 5.320]]: perfect ἀνέσχηκα[Refs 3rd c.BC+ [2nd c.AD: Sextus Empiricus Philosophus “adversus Mathematicos” 7.190, 3rd-2nd c.BC: Phalaris Epistolographus “Epistulae - Epistolographi” 105]]:—middle ἀνέχομαι: imperfect ἠνειχόμην (with double augment) [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Agamemnon” 905, 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Philoctetes” 411, 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 1.77, etc.]]: future ἀνέξομαι[Refs 5th c.BC+ [11.5.895, 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Electra” 1028, 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 18.160, etc.; also ἀνασχήσομαι 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Septem contra Thebas” 252, 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Acharnenses” 299]], Epic dialect infinitive ἀνσχήσεσθαι[Refs [11.5.104]]: aorist ἀνεσχόμην[Refs 5th c.BC+ [18.430, 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Choephori” 747 codices, 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Hippolytus” 687 (where ἠνέσχου is contra metrically)]]; more frequently with double augment ἠνεσχόμην[Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 5.48, 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Agamemnon” 1274]]; and Attic dialect, as [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Nubes” 1363, 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 3.28, 5th c.BC: Lysias Orator 3.3, etc.; syncopated. ἠνσχόμην 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Antigone” 467; _2nd pers.__sing._ _imperative_ ἄνσχεο (see. below with 11)]]:—passive, [LXX+1st c.BC+ [1st c.BC: Dionysius Halicarnassensis 3.55, LXX.4Mac.1.35.]]

__A
transitive, hold up, lift up, χεῖρας ἀνέσχον held up their hands in fight [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 18.89]] (later of pugilists, hold up the hands in token of defeat, [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [3rd c.BC: Theocritus Poeta Bucolicus 22.129)]]:—frequently lift up the hands in prayer, θεοῖσι δὲ χεῖρας ἀνέσχον[Refs 7th c.BC+ [11.3.318, compare 1.450, 7th c.BC: Archilochus Lyricus 82, etc.]]; so ἄνακτι εὐχὰς ἀ. offer prayers, perhaps with uplifted hands, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Electra” 636; ἄνεχε χέρας, ἄνεχε λόγον 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Electra” 592]]; also ἀ. τὴν χεῖρα offer the hand (to shake), [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Theopompus Comicus 82 (uncertain).]]

__A.2
lift up as an offering, τάγ᾽ Ἀθηναίῃ ληΐτιδι.. ὑψόσ᾽ ἀνέσχεθε χειρί[Refs [11.10.461]]; as a testimony, σκῆπτρον ἀ. πᾶσι θεοῖσι[Refs [7.412]]; μαζὸν ἀ., of Hecuba entreating her son Hector,[Refs 4th c.BC+ [22.80; κενεὰς.. ἀνέσχε γλήνας 3rd c.BC: Apollonius Rhodius Epicus 2.254; ἄκουε δ᾽ ἀν᾽ οὖς ἔχων 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Fragmenta - American Journal of Philology” 126.]]

__A.3
ἀ. φλόγα hold up a torch, especially at weddings, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Iphigenia Aulidensis” 732: hence the phrase ἄνεχε, πάρεχε i.e. τὸ φῶς)]] hold up, pass on the light in procession, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. author] “Tr.” 308, “Cyc.” 203, compare 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Vespae” 1326; also ἀ. φάος σωτήριον 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Medea” 482; τὸ σημεῖον τοῦ πυρός 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 4.111.]]

__A.4
lift up, exalt, τὰ κείνων[Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “P.” 2.89.]]

__A.5
hold up, prop, sustain, οὐρανὸν καὶ γῆν, of Atlas, [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd c.AD: Pausanias Periegeta 5.11.5; κίων ἀ. τὴν στέγην 2nd c.AD: Oenomaus Philosophus cited in 4th c.AD: Eusebius Caesariensis Scriptor Ecclesiasticus “Praeparatio Evangelica” 5.34]]:—passive, γέφυρα σκάφαις ἀνεχομένη[Refs 1st c.BC+ [1st c.BC: Dionysius Halicarnassensis 3.55:]] —but more frequently,

__A.5.b
metaphorically, uphold, maintain, εὐδικίας[Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 19.111; πολέμους 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 1.141]]; ὄργια ἀ. keep up the revels, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Thesmophoriazusae” 948; Βάκχης ἀνέχων λέκτρ᾽ Ἀγαμέμνων]]remaining constant to, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Hecuba” 121 (see. below 5th c.BC: Bacchylides Lyricus 3)]]; οἰνῶπ᾽ ἀνέχουσα κισσόν keeping constant to, haunting the ivy, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Coloneus” 674 (assuming variant)]]; βαρὺν ἀνὰ θυμὸν ἔχοισα keeping up his anger, [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [3rd c.BC: Theocritus Poeta Bucolicus 1.96.]]

__A.6
put forth, δάφνα ἀ. πτόρθους[Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Hecuba” 459 (Lyric poetry).]]

__A.II
hold back, check, ἄνεχ᾽ ἵππους[Refs 1st c.BC+ [11.23.426; ἀ. τὰ ὅπλα διὰ τῶν ἀνακλητικῶν 1st c.BC: Dionysius Halicarnassensis 9.21]]; ἀ. Σικελίαν μὴ ὑπ᾽ αὐτοὺς εἶναι keep it from being.., [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 6.86; ἑαυτὸν ἀπό τινος 1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus 2.514a]]:—passive, ἀνέχεται τὰ πάθη ὑπὸ τοῦ λογισμοῦ[LXX.4Mac.1.35.]

__B
intransitive, rise up, emerge, ἀνσχεθέειν.. ὑπὸ κύματος ὁρμῆς[Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 5.320]]; of a diver, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 8.8; σκόπελοι ἐν τῷ Νείλῳ ὀξέες ἀ. [prev. author] 2.29; ἀ. ἐς ἀέρα 3rd c.BC: Apollonius Rhodius Epicus 3.1383.]]

__B.b
especially in form ἀνίσχω, of the sun, πρὸς ἥλιον ἀνίσχοντα[Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 3.98, etc.; so λαμπὰς ἀνίσχει 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Agamemnon” 93 (Lyric poetry); ἅμ᾽ ἡλίῳ ἀνίσχοντι 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Cynegeticus” 6.13, compare 4th c.BC: Eubulus Comicus 119.9.]]

__B.c
of events, arise, happen, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 5.106, 7.14.]]

__B.d
appear, show oncself, ἄελπτον ὄμμα.. φήμης ἀνασχόν[Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Trachiniae” 204]]; turn out, prove to be, μελοποιὸς ἢ τραγῳδὸς ἄριστος[Refs 4th c.AD+ [4th-5th c.AD: Eunapius Historicus “Fragmenta Historica - HGM” p.209D.]]

__B.e
stand up, κίονες περὶ τοίχοις[Refs 3rd c.BC+ [3rd c.BC: Apollonius Rhodius Epicus 3.217.]]

__B.2
come forth, αἰχμὴ παρὰ.. ὦμον ἀνέσχεν[Refs 1st c.AD+ [11.17.310, compare 1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus “Caesar” 44]]; of a headland, jut out into the sea, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 7.123, 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 1.46, etc.; ἀ. πρὸς τὸ Σικελικὸν πέλαγος [prev. author] 4.53, compare 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 23.166]]; ἐς τὸν πόντον [τὴν ἄκρην] ἀνέχοντα jutting out with its headland into the sea, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 4.99 (uncertain reading); reversely, κοιλάδες ἐς μεσόγαιαν ἐκ θαλάσσης ἀ. 1st c.BC-1st c.AD: Strabo Geographus 3.2.4.]]

__B.3
hold on, keep doing, with participle, ἀ. διασκοπῶν[Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 7.48]]; σε.. στέρξας ἀνέχει is constant in his love for thee, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Ajax” 212 (Lyric poetry, compare above 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus 1.5b): with _dative_, τελεταῖς]]practise regularly, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.AD: Eunapius Historicus “Fragmenta Historica - HGM” p.249 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator]]: absolutely, wait, ταύτῃ ἀνέχειν[Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 8.94, compare 2.18.]]

__B.4
hold up, cease, Ζεὺς οὔθ᾽ ὕων πάντεσσ᾽ ἁνδάνει οὔτ᾽ ἀνέχων[Refs 6th c.BC+ [6th c.BC: Theognis Elegiacus 26, compare 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Historia Graeca (Hellenica)” 1.6.28; uncertain reading in 5th c.BC: Hippocrates Medicus “ἐπιδημίαι” 5.20.]]

__B.5
with genitive, cease from, οὐδὲ.. καμάτων ἀνέχουσι γυναῖκες[Refs 8th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Tyrannus” 174; τοῦ πολέμου 2nd c.AD: Appianus Historicus “Αιβυκή” 75; τοῦ φονεύειν 1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus “Alexander” 33.— 8th c.BC: Homerus Epicus uses no tense _intransitive_ except]]aorist

__C
middle, hold up what is one's own, ὁ δ᾽ ἀνέσχετο μείλινον ἔγχος[Refs 8th c.BC+ [11.5.655; δούρατ᾽ ἀνασχόμενοι 11.594, etc.: hence ἀνασχόμενος is often used _absolutely_ (i.e. ἔγχος, ξίφος, etc.), πλῆξεν ἀ. 3.362; κόψε δ᾽ ἀ. 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 14.425; πὺξ μάλ᾽ ἀνασχομένω πεπληγέμεν 11.23.660; also ἄντα δ᾽ ἀνασχομένω χερσί [prev. work] 686.]]

__C.II
hold oneself up, bear up, οὐδέ σ᾽ ὀΐω δηρὸν ἔτ᾽ ἀνσχήσεσθαι[Refs 8th c.BC+ [[prev. work] 5.285, compare 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 11.375:]]aorist imperative ἀνάσχεο, ={τέτλαθι}, be of good courage,[Refs [11.1.586; ἄνσχεο]]be patient, [Refs [23.587]]; ἀνὰ δ᾽ ἔχευ is probable reading for ἀνὰ δ᾽ εὖ in [Refs 7th c.BC+ [7th c.BC: Archilochus Lyricus 6.2: in]]present participle, ἀνεχόμενοι φέρουσι τὸν χειμῶνα they bear with patience, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 4.28; Stoic motto ἀνέχου καὶ ἀπέχου 2nd c.AD: Gellius, Aulus Grammaticus Latinus 17.19.]]

__C.II.2
with accusative, τοσσάδ᾽ ἐνὶ φρεσὶν ᾗσιν ἀνέσχετο κήδεα 11.18.430; ἦ δὴ πολλὰ κάκ᾽ ἄνσχεο σὸν κατὰ θυμόν 24.518; τὴν δουλοσύνην οὐκ ἀ.[Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.169; τὰ πρὶν κακὰ ἠνειχόμεσθα 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Agamemnon” 905, etc.; χαλκὸν ἀνασχέσθαι 11.4.511, etc.: with _accusative_ _person_, οὐ γὰρ ξείνους.. ἀνέχονται]] they do not suffer or bear with strangers, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 7.32, compare 17.13; τῶν ἵππων οὔτι ἀνεχομένων τὰς καμήλους 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 7.87; τούτους ἀνάσχου δεσπότας 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Alcestis” 304, compare 5th c.BC: Eupolis Comicus 6 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator]]: with accusative of things et genitive person, οὐδεὶς ἂν αὐτοῦ ἀγελαστὶ ἠνέσχετο ταῦτα τὰ ἔπη[Refs 5th c.BC+ [2nd c.AD: Athenaeus Epigrammaticus 5.188c, compare 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Lysistrata” 507.]]

__C.II.3
with genitive, uncertain in [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Homerus Epicus, δουλοσύνης ἀνέχεσθαι variant in 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 22.423; so ἅπαντος ἀνδρὸς ἀ. 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Protagoras” 323a, compare 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 19.16]]; to be content with, τοῦ ἐν σώματι κάλλους[Refs 3rd c.AD+ [3rd c.AD: Plotinus Philosophus 5.9.2.]]

__C.II.4
the dependent clause is mostly (always in [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Homerus Epicus) in]]participle, οὐ μάν σε.. ἀνέξομαι ἄλγε᾽ ἔχοντα I will not suffer thee to have.., [Refs [11.5.895]]; οὐ γὰρ ἀεργὸν [ὄντα] ἀνέξομαι I will not suffer one [to be].., [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 19.27; εἰ τὸν.. θανόντ᾽ ἄθαπτον ἠνσχόμην νέκυν 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Antigone” 467; οὐκ ἀνέξεται τίκτοντας ἄλλους 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Andromache” 712]]; καὶ γάρ κ᾽.. ἀνεχοιμην ἥμενος for I would be content to sit.., [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 4.595; σοῦ κλύων ἀνέξεται 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Persae” 838, compare 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Electra” 1028, “Ph.” 411; ἀνάσχεσθε σιγῶσαι [prev. author] “fragment” 679; also οὐ σῖγ᾽ ἀνέξε; [prev. author] “Aj.” 75: frequently in Prose, 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.80, 206, 5.19, +others, 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 2.74, etc.; ἄποτος ἀ. 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Historia Animalium” 596a2; also ἀ. τοῦ ἄλλα λέγοντος 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 564d; ἀ. τῶν οἰκείων ἀμελουμένων [prev. author] “Ap.” 31b; οὐδ᾽ ἂν ἠνέσχεσθε εἴ τις.. 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 21.170]]:—also in active, ἀνέσχηκα[Refs 3rd c.BC+ [3rd-2nd c.BC: Phalaris Epistolographus “Epistulae - Epistolographi” 105.]]

__C.II.5
rarely with infinitive, suffer, οὐκ ἀνέξομαι τὸ μὴ οὐ..[Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Eumenides” 914; κοκκύζειν τὸν ἀλεκτρυόν᾽ οὐκ ἀνέχονται 5th c.BC: Cratinus Comicus 311; ἀνακεκλίσθαι οὐκ ἀ. 2nd c.AD: Aretaeus Medicus “περὶ αἰτιῶν καὶ σημείων ὀξέων παθῶν” 1.9; ἀ. πάντα ὑπομένειν 4th c.AD: Alciphro Epistolographus 3.34; σὺν ἄλλοις βιοῦν οὐκ ἀ. 2nd-3rd c.AD: Aelianus “De Natura Animalium - Ar.Byzantine Epit.” 6.30.]]

__C.II.5.b
dare to do, ἀνέσχοντο τὸν ἐπιόντα δέξασθαι[Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 7.139.]]

__C.II.5.c
οὐκ ἀ., with infinitive, refuse to do.., [Refs [“POxy.” 903.36, +others]]

__C.III
rarely, hold on by one another, hang together, ἀνά τ᾽ ἀλλήλησιν ἔχονται[Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 24.8.]]

Abbott-Smith / STEPBible (TBESG)
ἀνήρ, ἀνδρός, ὁ,
[in LXX chiefly for אִישׁ, frequently אֱנוֹשׁ, also אָדָם, etc. ;]
a man, Lat. vir.
__1. As opposite to a woman, Act.8:12, 1Ti.2:12; as a husband, Mat.1:16, Jhn.4:16, Rom.7:2, Tit.1:6.
__2. As opposite to a boy or infant, 1Co.13:11, Eph.4:13, Jas.3:2.
__3. In appos. with a noun or adj., as ἀ. ἁμαρτωλός, Luk.5:8; ἀ. προφήτης, 24:19; frequently in terms of address, as ἀ. ἀδελφοί, Act.1:16; and esp. with gentilic names, as ἀ. Ἰουδαῖος, Act.22:3; ἀ. Ἐφέσιοι, 19:35.
__4. In general, a man, a male person: = τις, Luk.8:41, Act.6:11.
SYN.: ἄνθρωπος, which see (cf. MM, VGT, see word). (AS)

---

LSJ / STEPBible (TFLSJ)
ἀνήρ, ὁ, ἀνδρός, ἀνδρί, ἄνδρα,
vocative ἄνερ: plural ἄνδρες, -δρῶν, -δράσι [ᾰ], -dras: Aeolic dialect dative plural ἄνδρεσι[Refs 7th c.BC+ [7th-6th c.BC: Alcaeus Lyricus “Supp.” 14.8: late _nominative_ _sing._ ἄνδρας “Catalogus Codicum Astrologorum” 7.109.7: in _Attic dialect_ the _Article_ often forms a crasis with the Noun, ἁνήρ for ὁ ἀνήρ, τἀνδρός, τἀνδρί for τοῦ ἀνδρός, etc., ἅνδρες]] for οἱ ἄνδρε; the Ionic dialect crasis is ὡνήρ, ὧνδρες, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 4.161, 134: _Epic dialect_ also ἀνέρα, ἀνέρος, ἀνέρι, _dual_ ἀνέρε, _plural_ ἀνέρες, ἀνέρας, ἄνδρεσσι.]] [Epic dialect Poets mostly use ᾱ in arsi, ᾰ in thesi; but in trisyllable forms with stem ἀνέρ- always ; so also Trag. in Lyric poetry, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Trachiniae” 1011, “OT” 869. But in Trag. senarians ᾰ always.] (ἀ-]] in nominative by analogy; cf. Sanskrit nar- from I.-[Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus]] ner-, nṛ- from nṛ-, Gk. ἀνδρ- from ṇr-):—man, opposed to woman (ἄνθρωπος being man as opposed to to beast), [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 17.435, 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 21.323]]; τῶν ἀνδρῶν ἄπαις without male children, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Leges” 877e; in 8th c.BC: Homerus Epicus]] mostly of princes, leaders, etc., but also of free men; ἀ δήμου one of the people, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 2.198, compare 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 17.352]]; with a qualifying word to indicate rank, ἀ. βουληφόρος[Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 2.61; ἀ. βασιλεύς 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 24.253; ἡγήτορες ἄ. 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 11.687.]]

__II
man, opposed to god, πατὴρ ἀνδρῶν τε θεῶν τε [Refs [[prev. work] 1.544, +others]]; Διὸς ἄγγελοι ἠδὲ καὶ ἀνδρῶν [Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. work] 334, compare 403, 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 5.63, etc.]]: most common in plural, yet sometimes in singular, e.g. [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 18.432:—frequently with a Noun added, βροτοί, θνητοὶ ἄ., 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 5.197, 10.306; ἄ. ἡμίθεοι 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 12.23; ἄ. ἥρωες [prev. work] 5.746]]:—also of men, opposed to monsters, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 21.303]]:—of men in societies and cities, οὔτε παρ᾽ ἀνδράσιν οὔτ᾽ ἐν ναυσὶ κοίλαις[Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “O.” 6.10]]; and so probably, ἄλλοτε μέν τ᾽ ἐπὶ Κύνθου ἐβήσαο.., ἄλλοτε δ᾽ ἂν νήσους τε καὶ ἀνέρας..[Refs [“hymnus ad Apollinem” 142.]]

__III
man, opposed to youth, unless the context determines the meaning, as in οὔ πως ἔστι νεωτέρῳ ἀνδρὶ μάχεσθαι ἄνδρα γέροντα[Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 18.53]]; but ἀ. alone always means a man in the prime of life, especially warrior, ἀ. ἕλεν ἄνδρα[Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 15.328; so ἀ. ἀντ᾽ ἀνδρὸς ἐλύθησαν 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 2.103]]; the several ages are given as παῖς, μειράκιον, ἀ., πρεσβύτης[Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Symposium” 4.17]]; εἰς ἄνδρας ἐγγράφεσθαι, συντελεῖν, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 19.230, 5th-6th c.BC: Isocrates Orator 12.212; εἰς ἄνδρας ἀναβῆναι “BMus.Inscription” 898]]; in Inscrr. relating to contests, opposed to παῖδες, [Refs [“IG” 22.1138.10, etc.]]

__IV
man emphatically, man indeed, ἀνέρες ἄστε, φίλοι[Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 5.529; frequently in 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus, πολλοὶ μὲν ἄνθρωποι, ὀλίγοι δὲ ἄνδρες 7.210; πρόσθεν οὐκ ἀ. ὅδ᾽ ἦ; 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Ajax” 77; ἄνδρα γίγνεσθαί σε χρή 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Electra” 693; ἀ. γεγένησαι δι᾽ ἐμέ 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Equites” 1255; ὃ μαθὼν ἀ. ἔσει [prev. author] “Nu.” 823; ἄνδρας ἡγοῦνται μόνους τοὺς πλεῖστα δυναμένους καταφαγεῖν [prev. author] “Ach.” 77; εἰ ἄνδρες εἶεν οἱ στρατηγοί 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 4.27; οὐκέτι ἀ. ἀλλὰ σκευοφόρος 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 4.2.25; τὸν Αυκομήδην.. μόνον ἄνδρα ἡγοῦντο [prev. author] “HG” 7.1.24]]; οὐκ ἐν ἀνδράσι not like a man, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Alcestis” 723, compare 732]]; ἀνδρὸς τὰ προσπίπτοντα γενναίως φέρειν 'tis the part of a man.., [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-3rd c.BC: Menander Comicus 771, etc.]]

__V
husband, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 19.291, 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 24.196, 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.146, etc.; εἰς ἀνδρὸς ὥραν ἡκούσης τῆς κόρης 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Critias” 113d; so ἐξοικιεῖν εἰς ἀνδρὸς [οἶκον] θυγατέρα 2nd c.AD: Lucianus Sophista “Legal.” 11]]:—also of a paramour, opposed to πόσις, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Trachiniae” 551, compare 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Hippolytus” 491, 3rd c.BC: Theocritus Poeta Bucolicus 15.131; ἀ. ἁπασῶν τῶν γυναικῶν ἐστι νῦν 5th c.BC: Pherecrates Comicus 155; αἰγῶν ἄνερ 3rd c.BC: Theocritus Poeta Bucolicus 8.49.]]

__VI
Special usages:

__VI.1

__1. generically, a human being, male or female (Lat. homo): Jhn.16:21; with art., Mat.4:4 12:35, Mrk.2:27, Jhn.2:25, Rom.7:1, al; disting. from God, Mat.19:6, Jhn.10:33, Col.3:23, al.; from animals, etc., Mat.4:19, Luk.5:10, Rev.9:4, al.; implying human frailty and imperfection, 1Co.3:4; σοφία ἀνθρώπων, 1Co.2:5; ἀνθρώπων ἐπιθυμίαι, 1Pe.4:2; κατὰ ἄνθρωπον περιπατεῖν, 1Co.3:3; κατὰ ἄ. λέγειν (λαλεῖν), Rom.3:5, 1Co.9:8; κατὰ ἄ- λέγειν, Gal.3:15 (cf. 1Co.15:32, Gal.1:11); by meton., of man's nature or condition, ὁ ἔσω (ἔξω) ἄ., Rom.7:22, Eph.3:16, 2Co.4:16 (cf. 1Pe.3:4); ὁ παλαιὸς, καινὸς, νέος ἄ., Rom.6:6, Eph.2:15 4:22, 24 Col.3:9, 10; joined with another subst., ἄ. ἔμπορος, a merchant, Mat.13:45 (WH, txt. om. ἄ.); οἰκοδεσπότης, Mat.13:52; βασιλεύς, 18:23; φάγος, 11:19; with name of nation, Κυρηναῖος, Mat.27:32; Ἰουδαῖος, Act.21:39; Ῥωμαῖος, Act.16:37; pl. οἱ ἄ., men, people: Mat.5:13, 16 Mrk.8:24, Jhn.4:28; οὐδεὶς ἀνθρώπων, Mrk.11:2, 1Ti.6:16.
__2. Indef., ἄ. = τις, some one, a man: Mat.17:14, Mrk.12:1, al.; τις ἄ., Mat.18:12, Jhn.5:5, al.; indef. one (Fr. on), Rom.3:28, Gal.2:16, al.; opposite to women, servants, etc., Mat.10:36 19:10, Jhn.7:22, 23.
__3. Definitely, with art., of some particular person; Mat.12:13, Mrk.3:5, al.; οὗτος ὁ ἄ., Luk.14:30; ὁ ἄ οὗτος, ἐκεῖνος, Mrk.14:71, Mat.12:45; ὁ ἄ. τ. ἀνομίας, 2Th.2:3; ἄ τ. θεοῦ (of Heb. אִישׁ אֱלֹהִים), 1Ti.6:11, 2Ti.3:17, 2Pe.1:21; ὁ υἰὸς τοῦ ἀ., see: υἱός.
SYN.: ἀνήρ, which see (and cf. MM, VGT, 44; Cremer, 103, 635). (AS)

ἄνθρωπος, ἡ,
Attic dialect crasis ἅνθρωπος, Ionic dialect ὥνθρωπος, for ὁ ἄνθρ-:— man, both as a generic term and of individuals, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Homerus Epicus etc.]], opposed to gods, ἀθανάτων τε θεῶν χαμαὶ ἐρχομένων τ᾽ ἀνθρώπων[Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 5.442, etc.]]; πρὸς ἠοίων ἢ ἑσπερίων ἀνθρώπων the men of the east or of the west, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 8.29]]; even of the dead in the Isles of the Blest,[Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. work] 4.565; κόμπος οὐ κατ᾽ ἄνθρωπον 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Septem contra Thebas” 425, compare 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Ajax” 761.]]

__2
[Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus]] uses it both with and without the Article to denote man generically, ὁ ἄ. θείας μετέσχε μοίρας[Refs [“Prt.” 322a; οὕτω.. εὐδαιμονέστατος γίγνεται ἄ. “R.” 619b, +others]]; ὁ ἄ. the ideal man, humanity, ἀπώλεσας τὸν ἄ., οὐκ ἐπλήρωσας τὴν ἐπαγγελίαν[Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd c.AD: Arrianus Historicus “Epicteti Dissertationes” 2.9.3.]]

__3
in plural, mankind, ἀνθρώπων.. ἀνδρῶν ἠδὲ γυναικῶν[Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 9.134; ἐν τῷ μακρῷ.. ἀνθρώπων χρόνῳ 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Philoctetes” 306]]; ἐξἀνθρώπων γίγνεσθαι depart this life, [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd c.AD: Pausanias Periegeta 4.26.5, compare 2nd-3rd c.AD: Philostratus Sophista “Vita Apollonii” 8.31.]]

__3.b
joined with a superlative to increase its force, δεινότατον τῶν ἐν ἀνθρώποις ἁπάντων[Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 53.2]]; ὁ ἄριστος ἐν ἀνθρώποις ὄρτυξ the best quail in the world, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Lysis” 211e]]; frequently without a preposition, μάλιστα, ἥκιστα ἀνθρώπων, most or least of all, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.60, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Leges” 629a, “Prt.” 361e]]; ἄριστά γ᾽ ἀ., ὀρθότατα ἀ., [Refs [[prev. author] “Tht.” 148b, 195b, etc.]]

__3.c
τὰ ἐξ ἀνθρώπων πράγματα 'all the trouble in the world',[Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. work] 170e; γραφὰς τὰς ἐξ ἀνθρώπων ἐγράφετο 5th c.BC: Lysias Orator 13.73; αἱ ἐξ ἀνθρώπων πληγαί 4th c.BC: Aeschines Orator 1.59; πάντα τὰ ἐξ ἀνθρώπων κακὰ ἔλεγε 2nd-3rd c.AD: Dio Cassius Historicus 57.23.]]

__4
joined with another substantive, like{ἀνήρ}, ἄ. ὁδίτης [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 16.263; πολίτας ἀ. 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 22.54]]; with names of nations, πόλις Μερόπων ἀνθρώπων[Refs [“hymnus ad Apollinem” 42]]; in Attic dialect frequently in a contemptuous sense, ἄ. ὑπογραμματεύς, ἄ. γόης, ἄ. συκοφάντης, [NT+5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Lysias Orator 30.28, 4th c.BC: Aeschines Orator 2.153,183; ἄ. ἀλαζών 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Memorabilia” 1.7.2; ἄ. ὑφάντης 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Phaedo” 87b; Μενίππου, Καρός τινος ἀνθρώπου 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 21.175; ἄ. βασιλεύς NT.Matt.22.2.]]

__5
ἅνθρωπος or ὁ ἄνθρωπος alone, the man, the fellow, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Protagoras” 314e, “Phd.” 117e; ὡς ἀστεῖος ὁ ἄ., with slight irony, [prev. work] 116d, +others]]; with a sense of pity, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 21.91.]]

__6
in the vocative frequently in a contemptuous sense, as when addressed to slaves, etc., ἄνθρωπε or ὤνθρωπε sirrah! you sir! [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 3.63, 8.125, and frequently in 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus, but in Trag. only 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Ajax” 791, 1154]]; simply, brother, [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [POxy. 215.1, 2nd c.AD: Diogenes Oenoandensis Epicureus 2.]]

__7
slave, ἂν ἄ. ᾖ[Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-3rd c.BC: Philemo Comicus 22; ἄ. ἐμός 2nd c.AD: Galenus Medicus 14.649]]; ὁ ἄ. τῆς ἁμαρτίας or ἀνομίας[NT.2Thes.2.3; ἄ. τοῦ Θεοῦ NT.1Tim.6.11]; but τιθέναι τινὰ ἐν ἀνθρώποις make a man of, of a freed slave, [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [3rd c.BC: Herodas Mimographus 5.15.]]

__8
ἄ. ἄ. any one, Hebraism in [LXX.Lev.17.3 (compare ἀνήρ VI. 8)]; ἄ. like [Refs 1st c.BC+ [\{1st c.BC-1st c.AD\}: Germanicus Caesar Epigrammaticus]] man 'one', [NT.1Cor.4.1, +others]

__9
in Medicine texts, name of a plaster, ἡ διὰ σάνδυκος ἄ. καλουμένη[Refs 6th c.AD+ [6th c.AD: Aëtius Medicus 15.43.]]

__II
as feminine, woman, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “P.” 4.98, 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.60, 5th-6th c.BC: Isocrates Orator 18.52, 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Ethica Nicomachea” 1148b20]]; contemptuously, of female slaves, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Antipho Orator 1.17, 4th c.BC: Isaeus Orator 6.20, etc.]]; with a sense of pity, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 19.197.]] —Prop. opposed to θηρίον, compare ἀνή; but opposed to γυνή, [LXX+4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aeschines Orator 3.137; ἀπὺ ἀνθρώπου ἕως γυναικός LXX.1Esd.9.40, etc.]]

ἀν-ίημι
(ἀνά, ἵημι), [in LXX for רָפָה, נָשָׂא, etc. ;]
__1. to send up, produce, to send back.
__2. to let go, leave without support: Heb.13:5 (cf. Deu.31:6; Hom., Iliad., ii, 71).
__3. to relax, loosen (see Field, Notes, 124 f.): Act.16:26 27:40; hence, metaphorically, to give up, desist from: Eph.6:9.†
(AS)

---

LSJ / STEPBible (TFLSJ)
ἀνίημι, ης
(ἀνιεῖς, as if from ἀνιέω, uncertain in [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 5.880)]], ησι: imperfect ἀνίην, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Homerus Epicus and _Attic dialect_ 2]] and 3rd.pers.singular εις, ει, Ionic dialect 3rd.pers.singular ἀνίη[Refs 8th c.BC+ [“SIG” 1 (Abu Simbel, 6th c.BC, Iterat. ἀνίεσκε 8th-7th c.BC: Hesiodus Epicus “Theogonia” 157; also ἠνίει 5th c.BC: Hippocrates Medicus “ἐπιδημίαι” 7.46]]; 1st pers.singular ἀνίειν[Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd c.AD: Lucianus Sophista “Cat.” 4:]]future ἀνήσω: perfect ἀνεῖκα: aorist 1 ἀνῆκ; Ionic dialect ἀνέηκα.:—the Homeric forms ἀνέσει[Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 18.265]], aorist optative ἀνέσαιμι[Refs [14.209]], participle ἀνέσαντες[Refs 8th c.BC+ [13.657 should be referred to ἀνέζω, but ἄνεσαν 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 21.537 is from ἀνίημι]]: aorist 2, 3rd.pers.plural ἀνεῖσαν[Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 5.32, _imperative_ ἄνες 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Choephori” 489, 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Antigone” 1101, 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Helena” 442]], subjunctive ἀνῇς[Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Eumenides” 183]], Epic dialect 3rd.pers.singular subjunctive ἀνήη[Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 2.34, _optative_ ἀνείη,]]infinitive ἀνεῖναι, participle ἀνείς:—passive, ἀνίεμαι: perfect ἀνεῖμαι[Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 2.65, 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Septem contra Thebas” 413]], 3rd.pers.plural perfect ἀνέωνται[Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 2.165 (variant{ἀνέονται}),]]infinitive ἀνἑῶσθαι (sic) [Refs [“Tab.Heracl.” 1.153]]: aorist participle ἀνεθείς[Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 41c e]]: future ἀνεθήσομαι[Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 8.63. [ἀνῐ- _Epic dialect_, ἀνῑ-]] Attic dialect: but even [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Homerus Epicus has ἀνῑει, ἀνῑέμενος, and we find ἀνῐησιν in 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Comicus 153 (_anapaest meter_)]].]: —send up or forth, Ζεφύροιο.. ἀήτας Ὠκεανὸς ἀνίησιν[Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 4.568]]; of Charybdis, τρὶς μὲν γάρ τ᾽ ἀνίησιν.. τρὶς δ᾽ ἀναροιβδεῖ[Refs [12.105; ἀφρὸν ἀ.]]spew up, vomit, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Eumenides” 183; σταγόνας [αἵματος] ἀ. 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Tyrannus” 1277]]; of the earth, καρπὸν ἀ. make corn or fruit spring up, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [Hymnus in Cererem 333; κνώδαλα 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Supplices” 266]]; also of the gods, ἀ. ἄροτον γῆς[Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Tyrannus” 270, etc.]]; so of females, produce, [Refs [[prev. work] 1405]]:—in passive, σπαρτῶν ἀπ᾽ ἀνδρῶν ῥίζωμ᾽ ἀνεῖται[Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Septem contra Thebas” 413]]: then in various relations, συὸς χρῆμα ἀ.[Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Fragmenta” 401; κρήνην 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Bacchae” 766]]; of a forest, πῦρ καὶ φλόγα[Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 2.77; πνεῦμ᾽ ἀνεὶς ἐκ πνευμόνων 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Orestes” 277]]:—send up from the grave or nether world, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Persae” 650, 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Ranae” 1462, 5th c.BC: Phrynichus Comicus 1 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Cratylus” 403e, etc.:]] — passive, ἐκ γῆς κάτωθεν ἀνίεται ὁ πλοῦτος[Refs [[prev. passage]]]; of fruit, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-3rd c.BC: Theophrastus Philosophus “de Causis Plantarum” 5.1.5.]]

__2
let come up, give access to, τινά[Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Historia Graeca (Hellenica)” 2.4.11; εἰς τὸ πεδίον [prev. work] 7.2.12.]]

__II
let go, from [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Homerus Epicus downwards a very common sense, ἐμὲ δὲ γλυκὺς ὕπνος ἀνῆκεν,]] i.e. left me, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 2.71, etc., compare 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Protagoras” 310d]]: —passive, ἀνίεσθαι wake up, [Refs 1st c.BC+ [1st c.BC: Diodorus Siculus Historicus 17.56]]; set free, ἐκ στέγης ἀ.[Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Antigone” 1101]]; let go unpunished, ἄνδρα τὴν ὀλιγαρχίαν λυμαινόμενον[Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Historia Graeca (Hellenica)” 2.3.51, compare 5th c.BC: Lysias Orator 13.93]]; ἄνετέ μ᾽ ἄνετε leave me alone, forbear, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Electra” 229 (Lyric poetry)]]; of a state of mind, ἐμὲ δ᾽ οὐδ᾽ ὣς θυμὸν ἀνίει.. ὀδύνη[Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 15.24; ὅταν μ᾽ ἀνῇ νόσος μανίας 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Orestes” 227; ὥς μιν ὁ οἶνος ἀνῆκε 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.213, etc.]]; ἀ. ἵππον to let him go (by slackening the rein), [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Electra” 721; ἵππους εἰς τάχος ἀ. 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “de Equitum magistro” 3.2; τῷ δήμῳ τὰς ἡνίας ἀ. 1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus “Pericles” 11.]]

__II.b
loosen, unfasten, δεσμόν[Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 8.359 (variant{δεσμῶν}); δεσμά τ᾽ ἀνεῖσαι 3rd c.BC: Callimachus Epicus “Hecale” 1.2.13]]: hence, open, πύλας ἄνεσαν[Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 21.537; ἀ. θύρετρα 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Bacchae” 448]]; ἀ. σήμαντρα break the seal, [Refs [[prev. author] “IA” 325]]:—passive, πύλαι ἀνειμέναι[Refs 1st c.BC+ [1st c.BC: Dionysius Halicarnassensis 10.14.]]

__II.2
ἀ. τινί let loose at one, slip at, ἀ. τὰς κύνας[Refs 8th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Cynegeticus” 7.7: hence ἄφρονα τοῦτον ἀνέντες 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 5.761, compare 880: with _accusative_ et]]infinitive, Διομήδεα μαργαίνειν ἀνέηκεν[Refs [[prev. work] 882]]: generally, set on or urge to do a thing, with infinitive, Μοῦσ᾽ ἄρ᾽ ἀοιδὸν ἀνῆκεν ἀειδέμεναι[Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 8.73, compare 17.425, 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 2.276, 5.422]]: frequently with accusative person only, let loose, excite, as οὐδέ κε Τηλέμαχον.. ῷδ᾽ ἀνιείης[Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 2.185; μέγας δέ σε θυμὸς ἀνῆκεν 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 7.25]]; τοῖσιν μὲν Θρασυμήδεα δῖον ἀνῆκεν urged Thrasymedes to their aid, [Refs [17.705]]:—so in passive, ἅπας κίνδυνος ἀνεῖται σοφίας[Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Nubes” 955.]]

__II.3
ἀ. τινὰ πρός τι to let go for any purpose, τὸν λεὼν.. ἀνεῖναι πρὸς ἔργα τε καὶ θυσίας[Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 2.129]]; ἐς παιγνίην ἑωυτὸν ἀ.[Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. work] 173; τὰ μικρὰ εἰς τύχην ἀνείς 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Fragmenta” 974 (variant{ἀφείς}); τὰ σώματα ἐπὶ ῥᾳδιουργίαν 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 7.5.75]]; ἐὰν δ᾽ ἀνῇς, ὕβριστον χρῆμα κἀκόλαστον [γυνή] if you leave her free, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Comicus 98.]]

__II.4
let, allow, with accusative et infinitive, ἀνεῖναι αὐτοὺς ὅ τι βούλονται ποιεῖν[Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Laches” 179a; ἀ. τρίχας αὔξεσθαι 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 2.36, compare 4.175]]: with infinitive omitted, ἀνεῖσα πένθει κόμαν[Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Phoenissae” 323]]; ἀ. στολίδος κροκόεσσαν τρυφάν[Refs 1st c.AD+ [[prev. work] 1491; κόμας 1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus “Lysander” 1: with _dative_ _person_ et]]infinitive, ἀνεὶς αὐτῷ θηρᾶν having given him leave to hunt, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 4.6.3.]]

__II.5
middle, loosen, undo, with accusative, κόλπον ἀνιεμένη baring her breast, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 22.80]]; αἶγας ἀνιέμενοι stripping or flaying goats, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 2.300; so ἀνεῖτο λαγόνας 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Electra” 826]]; so in active, ἀνιέναι· δέρειν, [Refs 5th c.AD+ [5th c.AD(?): Hesychius Legal icographus]]

__II.6
let go free, leave untilled, of ground dedicated to a god, τέμενος ἀνῆκεν ἅπαν[Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 4.116; ἀργὸν παντάπασι τὸ χωρίον ἀνιέντες τῷ θεῷ 1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus “Publicola” 8; generally, τὴν χώραν ἀ. μηλόβοτον 5th-6th c.BC: Isocrates Orator 14.31; ἀρούρας ἀσπόρους ἀ. 4th-3rd c.BC: Theophrastus Philosophus “Historia Plantarum” 8.11.9; στέλεχος ἀνειμένον]]allowed to run wild, [LXX.Gen.49.21]:—but this sense mostly in passive, devote oneself, give oneself up, ἐς τὸ ἐλεύθερον[Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 7.103]]; especially of animals dedicated to a god, which are let range at large (compare ἄνετος), ἀνεῖται τὰ θηρία[Refs [[prev. author] 2.65]]; of a person devoted to the gods, νῦν δ᾽ οὗτος ἀνεῖται στυγερῷ δαίμονι[Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Ajax” 1214]]; of places, etc., θεοῖσιν ἀ. δένδρεα[Refs 3rd c.BC+ [3rd c.BC: Callimachus Epicus “Hymnus in Cererem” 47]]; ἄλσος ἀνειμένον a consecrated grove, conjecture in [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Leges” 761c]]; of land, ἀ. εἰς νομάς[Refs 2nd c.BC+ [“PTeb.” 60.8, 72.36 (2nd c.BC): hence _metaphorically_, ἀνειμένος εἴς τι]] devoted to a thing, wholly engaged in it, e.g. ἐς τὸν πόλεμον[Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 2.167]]; ἀνέωνται ἐς τὸ μάχιμον they are given up to military service, [Refs [[prev. work] 165]]; ἐς τὸ κέρδος λῆμ᾽ ἀνειμένον given up to.., [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Heraclidae” 3: hence]]perfect participle passive ἀνειμένος as adjective, going free, left to one's own will and pleasure, at large, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Antigone” 579, “El.” 516; ἀ. τι χρῆμα πρεσβυτῶν γένος καὶ δυσφύλακτον 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Andromache” 727]]; πέπλοι ἀνειμένοι let hang loose, [Refs [[prev. work] 598]]; τὸ εἰς ἀδικίαν καὶ πλεονεξίαν -μένον unrestrained propensity to.., [Refs 1st c.AD+ [1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus “Numa” 16; σώματα πρὸς πᾶσαν ἐπιθυμίαν ἀνειμένα [prev. author] “Lyc.” 10.]]

__II.7
slacken, relax, opposed to ἐπιτείνω or ἐντείνω, of a bow or stringed instrument, unstring, as [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 3.22, compare 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 442a, “Ly.” 209b, 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Memorabilia” 3.10.7, etc.]]; especially of musical scales, ἁρμονίαι ἀνειμέναι, opposed to σύντονοι, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Politica” 1342b22, +others; ἀνειμένα Ἰαστὶ μοῦσα Pratin.Lyric poetry 5]]: metaphorically, ὀργῆς ὀλίγον τὸν κόλλοπ᾽ ἀ.[Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Vespae” 574, compare 5th c.BC: Pherecrates Comicus 145.4, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 410e; πολιτεῖαι ἀνειμέναι καὶ μαλακαί 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Politica” 1290a28; τοῖς γηράσκουσι ἀνίεται ἡ συντονία “GA” 787b13]]; ἀνειμένη τάσις the grave accent,[Refs [Scholia 2nd c.BC: Dionysius Thrax Grammaticus p.130H.; οἱ πάγοι τὰς φλόγας ἀ.]]temper, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “de Mundo” 397b2: hence,]]

__II.7.b
remit, neglect, give up, στέρνων ἀραγμούς[Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Coloneus” 1608; φυλακὰς ἀνῆκα 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Supplices” 1042]]; φυλακήν, ἄσκησιν, etc., [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 4.27, 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 7.5.70, etc.]]; ἀ. θάνατόν τινι to remit sentence of death to one, let one live, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Andromache” 531; ἔχθρας, κολάσεις τισί 1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus 2.536a]]; ἀ. τὰ χρέα, τὰς καταδίκας, [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [[prev. author] “Sol.” 15, 2nd-3rd c.AD: Dio Cassius Historicus 64.8, compare 72.2]]; ἄνες λόγον speak more mildly, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Helena” 442; so ἀ. τινὸς ἔχθραν 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 3.10]]; ἀ. ἀρχήν, πόλεμον, etc., [Refs [[prev. author] 1.76, 7.18, etc.]]:—passive, to be treated remissly, ἀνεθήσεται τὰ πράγματα[Refs [[prev. author] 8.63; ὁ νόμος ἀνεῖται]]has become effete, powerless, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Orestes” 941: frequently in]]perfect participle ἀνειμένος as an adjective, ἐν τῷ ἀνειμένῳ τῆς γνώμης when their minds are not strung up for action, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 5.9]]; ἀνειμένῃ τῇ διαίτῃ relaxed, unconstrained, of the Athenians, [Refs [[prev. author] 1.6]]; δίαιτα λίαν ἀ., of the Ephors, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Politica” 1270b32; ἀ. ἡδοναί]]dissolute, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 573a]]; ἄνανδρος καὶ λίαν ἀ.[Refs [[prev. work] 549d; ἀ. χείλεα]]parched, [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [3rd c.BC: Theocritus Poeta Bucolicus 22.63]]; of climate, ἀ. καὶ μαλακός[Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-3rd c.BC: Theophrastus Philosophus “de Causis Plantarum” 5.4.4; ὀσμὴ μαλακὴ καὶ ἀ. 5.7.1]]: comparative ἀνειμενώτερος[Refs 4th c.AD+ [4th c.AD: Iamblichus Philosophus “de vita Pythagorica” 15.67:]] —but,

__II.8
the sense of relaxation occurs also as an intransitive usage of the active, slacken, abate, of the wind, ἐπειδὰν πνεῦμ᾽ ἀνῇ[Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Philoctetes” 639, compare 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 2.113, 4.152; ἕως ἀνῇ τὸ πῆμα 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Philoctetes” 764, compare 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.94]]; ἐμφῦσα οὐκ ἀνίει, of a viper, having fastened on him she does not let go, [Refs [[prev. author] 3.109: especially in phrase οὐδὲν ἀνιέναι]] not to give way at all, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Historia Graeca (Hellenica)” 2.3.46, compare “Cyr.” 1.4.22]]; τὰς τιμὰς ἀνεικέναι ἤκουον that prices had fallen, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 56.25, compare 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Rhetorica” 1390a15]]; σιδήρια ἀ. ἐν τοῖς μαλακοῖς lose their edge, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-3rd c.BC: Theophrastus Philosophus “Historia Plantarum” 5.5.1.]]

__II.8.b
with participle, give up or cease doing, ὕων οὐκ ἀνίει [ὁ θεός] [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 4.28, compare 125, 2.121.β, 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Iphigenia Taurica” 318, etc.]]

__II.8.c
with genitive, cease from a thing, μωρίας[Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. author] “Med.” 457; τῆς ὀργῆς 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Ranae” 700, 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 21.186; φιλονικίας 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 5.32]]; ἀνῆκε τοῦ ἐξελθεῖν forbore to come forth, [LXX.1Ki.23.13.]

__II.9
dilute, dissolve, διά τινος or τινί, [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd c.AD: Galenus Medicus 13.520, +others, “Geoponica” 4.7.3, compare 2nd c.AD: Arrianus Historicus “Anabasis” 7.20.5 (2nd c.AD: Phrynichus Atticista 19 says that διΐημι is more correct in this sense)]]; διυγραινομένων καὶ ἀνιεμένων[Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-3rd c.BC: Theophrastus Philosophus “de Ventis” 58.]]

deep_entry:
Abbott-Smith / STEPBible (TBESG)
ἀνίστημι (ἀνά, ἵστημι),
[in LXX chiefly for קוּם ;]
__1. causal, in fut. and 1 aor. act., with accusative, to raise up: Act.9:41; from death, Jhn.6:39, Act.2:32; to raise up, cause to be born or appear: Mat.22:24, Act.3:22, 26.
__2. Intrans., in mid. and 2 aor act.;
__(a) to rise: from lying, Mrk.1:35; from sitting, Luk.4:16; to leave a place, Mat.9:9; pleonastically, as Heb. קוּם, before verbs of going, Mrk.10:1, al. (see Dalman, Words, 23; M, Pr., 14); of the dead, Mat.17:23, Mrk.8:31; before ἐκ νεκρῶν, Mat.17:9, Mrk.9:9;
__(b) to arise, appear: Act.5:36, Rom.15:12 (cf. ἐπ-, ἐξ- ἀνίστημι, and see Cremer, 306, 738; MM, VGT, see word).
SYN.: ἐγείρω.
(AS)

---

LSJ / STEPBible (TFLSJ)
ἀνίστημι,
causal in present ἀνίστημι (later ἀνιστάω [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd c.AD: Sextus Empiricus Philosophus “adversus Mathematicos” 9.61):]]imperfect ἀνίστην: future ἀναστήσω, poetry ἀνστήσω: aorist 1 ἀνέστησα, Epic dialect ἄνστησα, Aeolic dialect 3rd.pers.plural ὄστασαν[Refs 5th c.AD+ [5th c.AD(?): Hesychius Legal icographus]]: perfect ἀνέστακα[LXX+2nd c.AD+ [LXX.1Ki.15.12, 2nd c.AD: Arrianus Historicus “Epicteti Dissertationes” 1.4.30: also in]]aorist 1 middle ἀνεστησάμην (see. below [Refs [1.5, 111.6).]]

__I
make to stand up, raise up, γέροντα δὲ χειρὸς ἀνίστη he raised the old man up by his hand, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 24.515, compare 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 14.319; τί μ᾽ αὖ.. ἐξ ἑδρας ἀνίστατ; 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Ajax” 788; ἀ. τινὰ ἐκ τῆς κλίνης 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Protagoras” 317e; ὀρθὸν ἀ. τινά 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Memorabilia” 1.4.11; ἀπὸ τοῦ καθαρμοῦ τινα 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 18.259.]]

__I.2
raisefrom sleep, wake up, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 10.32, etc.; εἰς ἐκκλησίαν ἀ. τινά 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Ecclesiazusae” 740; ἀ. τινὰ ὠμόϋπνον 5th c.BC: Eupolis Comicus 305: _metaphorically_, ἀ. νόσον 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Trachiniae” 979.]]

__I.3
raise from the dead, οὐδέ μιν ἀνστήσεις[Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 24.551, compare 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Agamemnon” 1361, 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Electra” 139]]; from misery or misfortune, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [[prev. author] “Ph.” 666, 4th c.BC: Aeschines Orator 1.67.]]

__I.4
produce a witness, etc. (compare 111.6), προφήτην ὑμῖν ἀ. ὁ Θεός[NT.Act.3.22, +others]

__I.5
after [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Homerus Epicus,]] also of things, set up, build, στήλας variant in [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 2.102; πύργους 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 7.5.12, etc.; τρόπαια Διί 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Phoenissae” 572]]; ἀνδριάντα ἐς Δελφούς Philipp. cited in [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 12.21]]; so ἀ. τινὰ χρυσοῦν, χαλκοῦν (in pure Attic ἱστάναι), set up a golden, brazen statue of him, [Refs 1st c.AD+ [1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus 2.170e, “Brut.” 1 (_passive_, see infr. B):]] —so in aorist 1 middle, ἀναστήσασθαι πόλιν build oneself a city, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.165]]; ἀνεστήσαντο δὲ βωμούς they set them up altars, [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [3rd c.BC: Callimachus Epicus “Hymnus in Dianam” 199.]]

__I.5.b
build up again, restore, τείχη[Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 20.68: _metaphorically_, θεῶν τιμάς 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Hercules Furens” 852.]]

__I.6
put up for sale, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.196.]]

__II
rouse to action, stir up, ἀλλ᾽ ἴθι νῦν Αἴαντα.. ἄνστησον[Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 10.176, compare 179, 15.64]], etc.: with dative person, raise up against another, τούτῳ δὲ πρόμον ἄλλον ἀναστήσουσιν [Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. work] 7.116 (see. below 5th c.BC: Bacchylides Lyricus 1.5)]]: rouse to arms, raise troops, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 2.68, 96; ἀ. πόλεμον ἐπί τινα 1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus “Coriolanus” 21]]; ἀναστήσας ἦγε στρατόν he called up his troops and marched them, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 4.93, compare 112, etc.]]

__III
make people rise, break up an assembly by force, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 1.191]]; but ἐκκλησίαν ἀναστῆσαι adjourn it, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Historia Graeca (Hellenica)” 2.4.42.]]

__III.2
make people emigrate, transplant (compare below [Refs 8th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Bacchylides Lyricus 11.2), ἔνθεν ἀναστήσας ἄγε 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 6.7; ἀνίστασαν τοὺς δήμους 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 9.73; Αἰγινήτας ἐξ Αἰγίνης 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 2.27; even γαῖαν ἀναστήσειν 3rd c.BC: Apollonius Rhodius Epicus 1.1349; οἴκους 1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus “Publicola” 21; also ἀ. τινὰ ἐκ τῆς ἐργασίας 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 18.129.]]

__III.3
make suppliants rise and leave sanctuary, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 5.71, 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 1.137, 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Coloneus” 276, etc.: also ἀ. στρατόπεδον ἐκ χώρας]] make an army decamp, [Refs 2nd c.BC+ [2nd c.BC: Polybius Historicus 29.27.10; τὰ πράγματα ἀνίστησί τινα 1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus “Alcibiades” 31.]]

__III.4
ἀ. ἐπὶ τὸ βῆμα make to ascend the tribune, [Refs [[prev. author] 2.784c, compare “Cam.” 32.]]

__III.5
of sportsmen, put up game, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 1.5.3, compare “Cyr.” 2.4.20 (_passive_), “Cyn.” 6.23, 1st-2nd c.AD: Dio Chrysostomus Sophista 2.2.]]

__III.6
μάρτυρα ἀναστής ασθαί τινα call him as one's witness, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Leges” 937a.]]

__B
intransitive in present and imperfect ἀνίσταμαι, -μην, in future ἀναστήσομαι, in aorist 2 ἀνέστην (but ἀναστῶ, for ἀναστήσω, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Crates Comicus 4D.), _imperative_ ἄστηθι (for ἄν-στηθι) 3rd c.BC: Herodas Mimographus 8.1]], participle ἀστάς[Refs [“IG” 4.951.112 (Epid.):]]perfect ἀνέστηκα, Attic dialect pluperfect ἀνεστήκ; also perfect ἀνεστέασι[Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 3.62:]]aorist passive ἀνεστάθην, Aeolic dialect participle ὀσταθείς[Refs 5th c.AD+ [5th c.AD(?): Hesychius Legal icographus]]:—stand up, rise, especially to speak, τοῖσι δ᾽ ἀνέστη[Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 1.68, 101, etc.; ἐν μέσσοισι 19.77: in _Attic dialect_ with]]future participle, ἀ. λέξων, κατηγορήσων, etc.: so with infinitive, ἀνέστη μαντεύεσθαι[Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 20.380]]: in participle, ἀναστὰς εἶπε[Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Orestes” 885; παραινέσεις ἐποιοῦντο ἐν σφίσιν αὐτοῖς ἀνιστάμενοι 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 8.76]]; also, rise from one's seat as a mark of respect, θεοὶ δ᾽ ἅμα πάντες ἀνέσταν[Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 1.533]]; ἀπὸ βωμοῦ [Refs 4th c.BC+ [compare (4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus 111.3) 4th c.BC: Aeschines Orator 1.84.]]

__B.2
rise from bed or sleep, ἐξ εὐνῆς ἀνστᾶσα[Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 14.336, compare 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Eumenides” 124; εὐνῆθεν 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 20.124; ὄρθρου ἀ. 8th-7th c.BC: Hesiodus Epicus “Opera et Dies” 577; ὀψέ 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Vespae” 217]]; οὐδ᾽ ἀνιστάμην ἐκ κλίνης, of a sick person, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Andocides Orator 1.64]]: absolutely, rise from sleep, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.31.]]

__B.3
rise from the dead, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 21.56, compare 15.287, 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 3.62, 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Agamemnon” 569; παρὰ τῶν πλειόνων 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Ecclesiazusae” 1073.]]

__B.4
rise from an illness, recover, ἐκ τῆς νούσου[Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.22, compare 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Laches” 195c: _absolutely_, 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 2.49.]]

__B.5
rise as a champion, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 23.709]]; θανάτων χώρᾳ πύργος ἀνέστα [Oedipus] [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Tyrannus” 1201]]: hence with dative, stand up [to fight against..], Ἀγκαῖον.., ὅς μοι ἀνέστη[Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 23.635; μή τίς τοι.. ἄλλος ἀναστῇ 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 18.334; Τυφῶνα θοῦρον πᾶσιν ὃς ἀνέστη θεοῖς 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Prometheus Vinctus” 354 codices]]; see above [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus 11.]]

__B.6
rise up, rear itself, πύργοι[Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Phoenissae” 824 (Lyric poetry), compare 2nd c.BC: Polybius Historicus 16.1.5]]; of statues, etc., to be set up, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus 2.91a, 198f: _metaphorically_, μή τι ἐξ αὐτῶν ἀναστήῃ κακόν 5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “P.” 4.155; πόλεμος 1st c.BC: Dionysius Halicarnassensis 3.23; θορύβου ἀναστάντος 2nd c.AD: Appianus Historicus “Bella Civilia” 1.56.]]

__B.7
to be set up, βασιλεύς as king, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 3.66 codices]]

__B.8
of a river, rise, ἐξ ὀρέων[Refs 1st c.AD+ [1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus “Pompeius” 34.]]

ἀντί
(the ι is elided only in ἀνθ᾽ ὧν), prep. with genitive (cf. MM, VGT, see word);
__1. prop, in local sense, over against, opposite, hence
__2. instead of, in place of, for (Hom., etc.): Mat.5:38 17:27, Luk.11:11, 1Co.11:15, Heb.12:2; with artic. inf. (cl.), Jas.4:15; of succession, Mat.2:22; χάριν ἀ. χάριτος, Jhn.1:16 (M, Pr., 100); of price in exchange, Heb.12:16; λύτρον ἀ. πολλῶν, Mat.20:28, Mrk.10:45 (M, Pr., 105); of requital, Rom.12:17, 1Th.5:16,  1Pe.3:9 (cf. Wis.11:15); ἀνθ᾽ ὧν, because, Luk.1:20 19:44, Act.12:23, 2Th.2:10 (cl., LXX for אֲשֶׁר תַּחַת); id. therefore (cl., LXX), Luk.12:3; ἀ. τούτου (LXX for כֵּן נַעֲרָה)Eph.5:31. As a prefix, ἀντι- (before vowels ἀντ-, ἀνθ᾽-), denotes
__(a) over against, ἀντιπέραν;
__(b) co-operation, ἀντιβάλλειν;
__(with) requital, ἀντιμισθία;
__(d) opposition, ἀντίχριστος;
__(e) substitution, ἀνθύπατος.
Compounds of ἀ. usually govern dative (B1., § 37, 7).†
(AS)

ἀντί,
preposition governing genitive:—originally sense, over against. (Cf. Sanskrit  ánti 'opposite', 'facing', Latin ante, etc.)

__A
USAGE:

__A.I
of Place, opposite, over against, formerly quoted from several places of [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Homerus Epicus, as 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 21.481 ἀντὶ ἐμεῖο (where now ἀντί᾽ ἐμεῖο, i.e. ἀντία) Τρώων ἄνθ᾽ ἑκατόν (i.e. ἄντα) 8.233]]; so ἄντ᾽ Αἴαντος (i.e. ἄντα)[Refs 8th c.BC+ [15.415, compare 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 4.115, 8th-7th c.BC: Hesiodus Epicus “Opera et Dies” 727]]; but ἀντί is so used in [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 4.7.6, “IG” 2.835]]c-l68; αἱ ὀπαὶ αἱ γιγνόμεναι ἀ. τόρμων mortises facing tenons, [Refs 2nd c.BC+ [2nd-1st c.BC(?): Hero Mechanicus “Belopoeica” 97.5]]; ἀντὶ μαιτύρων in the presence of witnesses, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [“Leg.Gort.” 1.40; ἀντὶ τῆς ὄψεως ἡμῶν 4th c.BC: Eudoxus Astronomus “Ars astronomica” 18.]]

__A.II
of Time, ἀντὶ νυκτός the same night, [Refs [“SIG” 1025.43 (from Cos)]]; ἀντὶ ϝέτεος[Refs 1st c.BC+ [“GDI” 2561 A 45 (Delph.); ἀντ᾽ ἐνιαυτοῦ “IG” 5(2).266.8 (Mantinea, 1st c.BC)]]; ἀνθ᾽ ἡμέρας· δι᾽ ὅλης τῆς ἡμέρας, [Refs 5th c.AD+ [5th c.AD(?): Hesychius Legal icographus]]; compare ἀντετοῦς.

__A.III
instead, in the place of, Ἕκτορος ἀντὶ πεφάσθαι[Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 24.254; ἀντὶ γάμοιο τάφον 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 20.307; so later πολέμιος ἀντὶ φίλου καταστῆναι 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.87; ἀντὶ ἡμέρης νὺξ ἐγένετο [prev. author] 7.37; ἀντὶ φωτῶν σποδός 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Agamemnon” 434; τὸν πόλεμον ἀντ᾽ εἰρήνης μεταλαμβάνειν 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 1.120, compare 4.20, 7.75; βασιλεύειν ἀντί τινος 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 1.1.4; also ἀντὶ ἄρχεσθαι ὑπ᾽ ἄλλων ἄρχειν ἁπάντων 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.210, compare 6.32, 7.170 (where the usual _construction_ would be ἀντὶ τοῦ ἄρχεσθαι,compare 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 7.28, 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 6.2.19, etc.); ὀργίλοι ἀντὶ θυμοειδοῦς γεγένηνται 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 411c]]: sometimes used elliptically, ἦ 'τολμήσατ᾽ ἀντ᾽ ἐμοῦ δοῦναί τιν; i.e. ἀντὶ τοῦ ἐμοὶ δοῦναι, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Philoctetes” 369, compare “OC” 448, 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Aves” 58.]]

__A.III.2
in [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Homerus Epicus often to denote equivalence, ἀντί νυ πολλῶν λαῶν ἐστιν ἀνήρ]] he is as good as many men, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 9.116]]; ἀντὶ κασιγνήτου ξεῖνος.. τέτυκται a guest is as much as a brother, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 8.546]]; ἀντί τοί εἰμ᾽ ἱκέταο I am as a suppliant, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 21.75, compare 8.163]]; so later τοῦτό σφι ἀντὶ λουτροῦ ἐστί serves as a bath, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 4.75]]; ὑπάρχειν ἀντὶ τῶν ἔνδον to be as hostages for.., [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 2.5]]; δουλεύειν ἀντὶ ἀργυρωνήτων just like bought slaves, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 17.3; ἀντὶ [πλεύμονος] βράγχια 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “de Partibus Animalium” 669a4.]]

__A.III.3
to denote exchange, at the price of, in return for, σοὶ δὲ θεοὶ τῶνδ᾽ ἀντὶ χάριν.. δοῖεν[Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 23.650]]; νῆσον ἀντὶ χρημάτων παρέλαβον for money paid, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 3.59; ἀντ᾽ ἀργυρίου ἀλλάξασθαι 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 371d; ἀμείβειν τι ἀντί τινος 5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “P.” 4.17, compare 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Orestes” 646, 651; ἀντὶ ποίας εὐεργεσία; 5th c.BC: Lysias Orator 6.40, etc.; τί δ᾽ ἐστὶν ἀνθ᾽ οὗ..; 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Antigone” 237; ὄνειδος ἀνθ᾽ ὅτου [prev. author] “OC” 967]]; δοίην ἀντ᾽ ἀνιῶν ἀνίας grief for grief, [Refs 6th c.BC+ [6th c.BC: Theognis Elegiacus 344; ἀντ᾽ ἀγαθῶν ἀγαθοῖσι βρύοις 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Supplices” 966]]:—hence ἀνθ᾽ ὧν wherefore, [NT+5th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Prometheus Vinctus” 31, 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Tyrannus” 264, 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 6.83, NT.Luke.12.3]]; ἀντὶ τούτου therefore, [NT.Eph.5.31]; but ἀνθ᾽ ὧν also for ἀντὶ τούτων ὄτι.., because, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Antigone” 1068, 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Plutus” 434]]; ἀντὶ το; wherefore? why? [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Tyrannus” 1021]]; also ἀνθ᾽ ὧν ὅτι ἦτε.. instead of being as you were.., [LXX.Deu.28.62.]

__A.III.4
for the sake of, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Menexenus” 237a, 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Ethica Nicomachea” 1110a21]]; with Verbs of entreaty, like{πρός} with genitive, ἀντὶ παίδων ἱκετεύομέν σε[Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Coloneus” 1326.]]

__A.III.5
to mark comparison, ἓν ἀνθ᾽ ἑνός one set against the other, compared with it, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 331b, “Lg.” 705b]]; χάριν ἀντὶ χάριτος, i.e. ever-increasing grace, [NT.John.1.16]; in preference to, ἀφνεὸν βούλεται ἀντ᾽ ἀγαθοῦ[Refs 6th c.BC+ [6th c.BC: Theognis Elegiacus 188; ἀντὶ αὐλοῦ καὶ ἀντὶ κιθάρας ὁ ἦχος ἀκούεται 4th c.BC: Demetrius Phalereus Rhetor “Demetrius on Style” 71; αἱρεῖσθαί τι ἀντί τινος 5th-6th c.BC: Isocrates Orator 9.3, 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 1.1, compare 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Respublica Lacedaemoniorum” 9.1]]: even after Comparatives, πλέον ἀντὶ σοῦ[Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Trachiniae” 577; μείζον᾽ ὅστις ἀντὶ τῆς αὑτοῦ πάτρας φίλον νομίζει [prev. author] “Ant.” 182]]; so (especially after a negative) ἄλλος ἀντ᾽ ἐμοῦ[Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Prometheus Vinctus” 467, 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Ajax” 444, 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Nubes” 653; δόξαν ἀντὶ τοῦ ζῆν ἠγαπηκώς 1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus “Alexander” 42.]]

__B
POSITION: ἀντί rarely follows its case, as in [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 23.650, 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Agamemnon” 1277, “Ig” 5(1).1119 (Geronthrae, 4th c.BC), “Anthologia Graeca” 7.715 (1st c.AD: Leonidas Alexandrinus Epigrammaticus)]]; but the Grammars  hold that it never suffers anastrophe.

__C
IN COMPOSITION (joined with other words), it signified,

__C.1
over against, opposite, as ἀντιβαίνω, ἀντίπορος.

__C.2
against, in opposition to, as ἀντιλέγω, ἀντίβιος.

__C.3
one against another, mutually, as ἀντιδεξιόομαι.

__C.4
in return, as ἀντιβοηθέω.

__C.5
instead of, as ἀντιβασιλεύς, ἀνθύπατος.

__C.6
equal to, like, as ἀντίθεος, ἀντίπαις, ἀντίδουλος.

__C.7
corresponding, counter, as ἀντίφορτος, ἀντίτυπος.

of persons, οἱ ἑωυτοῦ ἄξιοι those of one's own rank, his peers, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.107.]]

sufficient for, with genitive, ἄ. τοῦ πολέμου τὰ χρήματα[Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 14.27.]]

__7
αἰδοῦς ἀξίαν.. τὴν προθυμίαν μᾶλλον ἢ θράσους more like modesty than rashness, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “de Caelo” 291b25.]]

__II
after [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Homerus Epicus]], in moral relation, worthy, estimable, of persons and things, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 7.224, etc.]]; οὐδὲν ἀξία nothing worth, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Choephori” 445; ἀξίαν κἀπ᾽ ἀξίων [prev. author] “Eu.” 435; ἀξίων γεννητόρων ἤθη φυλάσσεις 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Ion” 735.]]

__II.2
worthy of, deserving, mostly with genitive of things, ἄξιον φυγῆς, ἄξια στεναγμάτων, γέλωτος, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. author] “Med.” 1124, “Or.” 1326, “Heracl.” 507; ἐγκωμίων τί ἀξιώτερον ἤ..; 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Agesilaus” 10.3: with _genitive_ _person_, ποιεῖν ἄξια οὔτε ὑμῶν οὔτε πατέρων 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 2.71; ἄξιον τοῦ πατρός 5th-6th c.BC: Isocrates Orator 9.80; ἄξια τοῦ Μαραθῶνος διανοεῖσθαι 1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus “Cimon” 5.]]

__II.2.b
with genitive of things et dative person, ἡμῖν δ᾽ Ἀχιλλεὺς ἄξιος τιμῆς is worthy of honour at our hands, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Hecuba” 309; πολλῶν ἀγαθῶν ἄ. ὑμῖν 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Acharnenses” 633; ἄ. πλείστου Λακεδαιμονίοις 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 4.81; θανάτου τῇ πόλει 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Memorabilia” 1.1.1, compare 1.2.62; εἰμὶ δ᾽ οὐ τούτων ὑμῖν ἄ. 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 21.217; χάριτος ἄ. τῇ πόλει 5th c.BC: Antipho Orator 6.10; later τιμῆς ἄ. παρὰ πάντων 2nd c.AD: Lucianus Sophista “Tox.” 3.]]

__II.3
with infinitive, Προθοήνορος ἀντὶ πεφάσθαι ἄ. worthy to be killed instead of him, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 14.472, compare 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 1.76; τίεσθαι δ᾽ ἀξιώτατος 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Agamemnon” 531; ἄ. θρήνων τυχεῖν 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Ajax” 924]]; ἄξιοι δουλεύειν only fit to be slaves, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Politica” 1254b36; also ἄ. σέβειν 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Heraclidae” 315 (Elmsl.).]]

__II.3.b
ἄξιός εἰμι, like{δίκαιός εἰμι}, I deserve to.., ἄξιός εἰμι πληγὰς λαβεῖν[Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Ecclesiazusae” 324; ἄξιός εἰμι ἀπολαῦσαι 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 5.4.19]]: absolutely, the infinitive being supplied, authorized to act, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Andocides Orator 1.132]]; ἄ. γάρ, emphatically, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Theaetetus” 143e.]]

__II.3.c
later ἄ. ἵνα[NT.John.1.27.]

__II.4
ἄξιόν [ἐστι] 'tis meet, fit, due, ἄξιον εἶναι τρεῖς ἑνὸς ἀντὶ πεφάσθαι[Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 13.446; ἄ. μνήμην ἔχειν 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.14]]: later with future infinitive, ἄ. διαπορήσειν[Refs 1st c.BC+ [1st c.BC: Didymus Grammaticus]]in D.[Refs [9.15.]]

__II.4.b
with dative person et infinitive, τῇ πόλει γὰρ ἄξιον ξυλλαβεῖν τὸν νο̄ρα 'tis meet for the city, is worth her while.., [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Acharnenses” 205; τί σοι ζῆν ἄξιο; [prev. author] “Nu.” 1074, compare “Av.” 548; ἄξιόν γε πᾶσιν ἐπολολύξαι [prev. author] “Eq.” 616; frequently in 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus as ὡς οὐκ ἄξιον εἴη βασιλεῖ ἀφεῖναι κτλ.]] that it was not meet for him.., [Refs [“An.” 2.3.25.]]

__II.4.c
the infinitive is sometimes omitted, ἄξιον γὰρ Ἑλλάδι 'tis meet in the eyes of Hellas [so to do], [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Acharnenses” 8]]; and sometimes the dative, ἄξιόν ἐστι operae pretium est, it is worth while, ἐνθυμηθῆναι[Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 1.21; γαμεῖν οὐκ ἄξιον 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Alcestis” 628.]]

__III
adverb ἀξίως, with genitive, ἐμάχοντο ἀξίως λόγου[Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 6.112; οὔτε ἑωυτοῦ ἀ. [prev. author] 3.125; οὐκ ἀ. ἀπηγήσιος [prev. passage]; τῆς ἀσικίας 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 3.39]]; ἀ. τοῦ θεοῦ, τῆς θεᾶς, [NT+5th c.BC+ [“OGI” 331.9 (Pergam.), “Inscription Magn.” 33.30, cf. NT.1Thes.2.12: _absolutely_, 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Tyrannus” 133, etc.]]; κολάσετε ἀξίως as they deserve, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 3.40.]]

deep_entry:
Abbott-Smith / STEPBible (TBESG)
ἀξιόω, -ῶ
(ἄξιος), [in LXX chiefly for בְּעָא, בָּקַשׁ; frequently in Wis.1:1-16, 2 Mac ;]
__(a) to deem worthy: with accusative and inf. (see MM, VGT, see word, and cf. κατ-αξιόω), Luk.7:7; id. and genitive of thing(s), 2Th.1:11; pass. with genitive of thing(s), 1Ti.5:17, Heb.3:3 10:29
__(b) to think fit: with inf. (see M, Pr., 205), Act.15:38 28:22.†

LSJ / STEPBible (TFLSJ)
ἀξιόω,
perfect ἠξίωκα[Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Isocrates Orator 18.24]]:—middle, see below 111.2:—passive, future ἀξιωθήσομαι[Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. author] 9.6, but also ἀξιώσεται 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Antigone” 637:]]aorist ἠξιώθην: perfect ἠξίωμαι: (ἄξιος):—think, deem worthy,

__I
with accusative et genitive, whether in good sense, think worthy of a reward, ἡμᾶς ἀξιοῖλόγου[Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Medea” 962; ἑαυτὸν τῶν καλλίστων 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 3.2.7]]; or in bad, of a punishment, γοργύρης[Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 3.145]]; ἀ. τινὰ ἀτιμίας Philipp. cited in [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 18.166; κακοῦ 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Apologia” 38a]]:—passive, ἀξιεύμενος θυγατρὸς τῆς σῆς[Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 9.111]]; λέχη.. τυράννων ἠξιωμένα deemed worthy of kings, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Hecuba” 366; ἀξιοῦσθαι κακῶν 5th c.BC: Antipho Orator 3.2.10; τοῦ αὑτοῦ ὀνόματος 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Phaedo” 103e, +others]]

__I.2
with accusative only, esteem, honour, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Ajax” 1114, 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Heraclidae” 918]]; ἀ. τινὰ προσφθέγμασιν honour one with words, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Agamemnon” 903]]; of things, value, οὐκ ἐξἴσου πάσας ἀξιοῦμεν ὑπολήψεις[Refs 1st c.BC+ [1st c.BC: Philodemus Gadarensis Epigrammaticus “Herc.” 1251.12]]:—passive, καλοῖς ὑμεναίοις ἀξιοῦσθαι[Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Orestes” 1210: _absolutely_, τύμβον ἀξιούμενον ὁρᾶσθαι [prev. author] “Hec.” 319, compare 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 5.16.]]

__I.3
value at a certain price, ὁπόσης ἂν τιμῆς ἀξιώσῃ τὸ πωλούμενον[Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Leges” 917d.]]

__II
c.accusative person et infinitive, think one worthy to do or be, σέ τοι ἠξίωσε ναίειν[Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Alcestis” 572]]; οὐκ ἀξιῶ ’γὼ ’μαυτὸν ἰσχύειν μέγα [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Equites” 182; τί σαυτὸν ἀποτίνειν ἀξιοῖ; 5th c.BC: Pherecrates Comicus 93]]:—passive, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “N.” 10.39, 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Prometheus Vinctus” 242]]; διδάσκαλος ἀξιοῦσθαι to be esteemed as a teacher, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Theaetetus” 161d.]]

__II.2
think fit, expect, require that.., ἀ. τινὰ ἰέναι[Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 2.162; ἀ. τινὰ ἀληθῆ λέγειν 5th c.BC: Antipho Orator 2.3.4]]; οὐκ ἀ. [ὑμᾶς] τὰ μὴ δεινὰ ἐν ὀρρωδίᾳ ἔχειν we expect that you do not.., [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 2.89, compare 3.44; ἀ. σωτηρίαν ἐμοὶ γενέσθαι 5th-6th c.BC: Andocides Orator 1.143]]; ἀ. καὶ παρακαλεῖν τινα with infinitive, Canon Laws texts cited in [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 18.165; ἀ. ἵνα.. “Inscription Prien.” 53.58, +others]]; simply, ask, request, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Elephantine Papyri 19.18, 3rd-2nd c.BC: Apollonius Pergaeus Geometra 1 “Praef.” (_passive_)]]; especially pray, τὸν θεὸν ὅπως.. Aristeas 245,[cf. LXX.Jer.7.16, “SIG” 1181.1 Aristeas 18]; also, ask, inquire of an oracle, [Refs 3rd c.AD+ [3rd c.AD: Pseudo-Callisthenes Historicus 1.3.]]

__III
with infinitive only, ἀ. κομίζεσθαι, τυγχάνειν think one has a right to receive, expect to receive, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 1.43, 7.15; προῖκα θεωρεῖν ἀ. 4th-3rd c.BC: Theophrastus Philosophus “Characteres” 6.4; ἄλλο τι ἀξιοῖς ἢ ἀποθανεῖ; 5th c.BC: Lysias Orator 22.5: with a _negative_, οὐκ ἀξιῶ ὑποπτεύεσθαι]] I think I do not deserve to be suspected, have a right not to be.., [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 4.86:]] —passive, ὥστε ἀξιοῦσθαι λῃτουργεῖν so as to be required to.., [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 27.64; υἱῷ προθύμως τἀξιούμενον ποιῶν]]one's duty, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-3rd c.BC: Menander Comicus 663.]]

__III.2
think fit, expect, consent, resolve, etc., and so in various senses, ἀξιῶ θανεῖν I consent to die, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Tyrannus” 944, etc.]]; dare, ἀξιῶσαι μάχην συνάψαι[Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Persae” 335]]; deign to do, εἴ τις ἀξιοῖ μαθεῖν[Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. author] “Ag.” 1661, compare 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Tyrannus” 1413]]; ἀξιῶ χρήματα λαμβάνειν I do not hesitate to receive, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Hp.Mi.” 364d, etc.]]; οἶμαι πάντας.. φέρειν ἀξιοῦν ἔρανον I think that all should be glad to bring, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 21.101:]] —frequently with _negative_, οὐδ᾽ ἀξιῶ μνησθῆναι I do not think them worth mentioning, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 2.20; οὐκ ἠξίωσαν οὐδὲ προσβλέψαι 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Prometheus Vinctus” 217; οὐκ ἀξιώσαντες.. τοῦτο παθεῖν 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 1.102 (but ἀξιοῦτε μὴ ἀντιδοῦναι δίκην 3.66); πείθεσθαι οὐκ ἀξιοῦντες]]refusing, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Oeconomicus” 21.4:]] —also in middle (not in Attic dialect Prose), ἀξιοῦσθαι μέλειν deign to care for, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Agamemnon” 370]]; φονεὺς γὰρ εἶναι ἠξιώσατο thought fit to be, [Refs [[prev. author] “Eu.” 425]]; οὐκ ἀξιεύμεναι ἀναμίσγεσθαι τῇσι ἄλλῃσι not condescending to.., [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.199]]; οὐκ ἀξιεύμενος ἐς τὸν.. θρόνον ἵζεσθαι not deeming oneself worthy to.., [Refs [[prev. author] 7.16.]]

__III.3
think, deem, ἀξιοῦντες ἀδικέεσθαι[Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. author] 6.87, compare 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Coloneus” 579, 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Hercules Furens” 1343]]; ἑκάτεροι νικᾶν ἠξίουν claimed the victory, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 1.55.]]

__IV
make a claim, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [[prev. author] 4.58; πάντες καθ᾽ ὑπεροχὴν -οῠσιν 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Politica” 1288a23; ἀξίωσιν ἀ. 2nd c.BC: Polybius Historicus 38.7.7]]; ἀξιοῦν τινά τι make a claim on a person, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Memorabilia” 3.11.12.]]

__IV.2
ἐγὼ μὲν οὑτωσὶ περὶ τῆς τύχης ἀξιῶ hold this opinion.., [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 18.255]]; ἐγὼ μὲν οὐκ ἀξιῶ I think not, [Refs [[prev. author] 20.12]]: in philosophic language, lay down, maintain [Refs 4th c.BC+ [compare (ἀξίωμα 11.2), 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Analytica Priora” 37a10, compare 41b10, Polystr. p.24 W.]]; ἐν τῷ τοιῷδε ἀξιοῦντι in such a state of opinion, variant in [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 3.43.]]

ἀξίως,
adv. [in LXX: Wis.7:15 16:1, Sir.14:11 * ;]
worthily: Rom.16:2, Eph.4:1, Php.1:27; with genitive (frequently in Inscr.; Deiss., BS, 248; MM, VGT, 51), ἀ. τ. Κυρίου, Col.1:10; τ. θεοῦ 1Th.2:12, 3Jn.6.†
