LSJ / STEPBible (TFLSJ)
Included with:  ἄξιος, ία, ιον
(ος, ον [Refs 4th c.AD+ [4th-5th c.AD(?): Nonnus Epicus “Dionysiaca” 8.314), for Αγ-τιος,]] counterbalancing,[Refs [compare ἄγω v1]]: hence properly weighing as much, of like value, worth as much as, with genitive, βοὸς ἄ.[Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 23.885]]; νῦν δ᾽ οὐδ᾽ ἑνὸς ἄξιοί εἰμεν Ἕκτορος we are not—all together—worth one Hector,[Refs 8th c.BC+ [8.234, compare 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.32, 7.21; πάντων Ζεὺς ἄξιον ἦμαρ ἔδωκεν 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 15.719]]; so πολλοῦ ἄ. worth much, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 4.1.28, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Symposium” 185b, etc.; πλείονος ἄ. [prev. author] “Phdr.” 235b, etc.; πλείστου ἄ. 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 2.65, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Gorgias” 464d, etc.]]; παντός, τοῦ παντὸς ἄ., [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Fragmenta” 275, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Sophista” 216c]]; παντὸς ἄ., with infinitive, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Aves” 797]]; λόγου ἄ., ={ἀξιόλογος}, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.133, 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 1.73, etc.]]; σπουδῆς, μνήμης ἄ., [Refs 6th c.BC+ [1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus 2.35a,172e:—opposed to to these are οὐδενὸς ἄ. 6th c.BC: Theognis Elegiacus 456; ἢ παντὸς ἢ τὸ παράπαν οὐδενός 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Philebus” 64d; ὀλίγου [prev. author] “Grg.” 497b, etc.; σμικροῦ [prev. author] “R.” 504d, etc.; βραχέος [prev. author] “Lg.” 692c]]; μείονος, ἐλάττονος ἄ., [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “de Vectigalibus” 4.50, “Cyr.” 2.2.14; πολλαπλασίου τιμήματος ἄ. κτήσεις 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Politica” 1306b12]]; also εἰς ὀγδοήκοντα μνᾶς ἄ. worth up to a sum of.., [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 27.10.]]

__2
with dative person, σοὶ δ᾽ ἄξιόν ἐστιν ἀμοιβῆς 'tis worth a return to thee, i.e. will bring thee a return, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 1.318; πολέος δέ οἱ ἄξιος ἔσται 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 23.562; βασιλεῖ ἂν πολλοῦ ἄξιοι γένοιντο 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 2.1.14.]]

__3
absolutely, worthy, goodly, ἄξια δῶρα[Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 9.261]]; ἄ. ὦνος a goodly price, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 15.429]]; ὅθεν κέ τοι ἄξιον ἄλφοι it would bring thee a good price,[Refs 5th c.BC+ [20.383; φέροντες ὅ τι ἕκαστος ἄξιον εἶχε 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 3.3.2.]]

__3.b
in Attic dialect in an exactly opposite sense, 'good value for the money', i.e. cheap, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Equites” 672, 895]]: comparative,[Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. work] 645; ὡς ἀξιώτατον πρίασθαι 5th c.BC: Lysias Orator 22.18; ὡς ἄ. γεγόνασιν οἱ πυροὶ ἐν τῇ ἀγορᾷ 4th-3rd c.BC: Theophrastus Philosophus “Characteres” 3.3, compare 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “de Vectigalibus” 4.6.]]

__4
deserved, meet, due, δίκη[Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Electra” 298, 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Oeconomicus” 12.19; χάρις [prev. author] “HG” 1.6.11]]; ἄξια δράσας ἄξια πάσχων fit suffering for fit deeds, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Agamemnon” 1527, compare 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Ion” 735.]]

__5
of persons, οἱ ἑωυτοῦ ἄξιοι those of one's own rank, his peers, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.107.]]

__6
sufficient for, with genitive, ἄ. τοῦ πολέμου τὰ χρήματα[Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 14.27.]]

__7
αἰδοῦς ἀξίαν.. τὴν προθυμίαν μᾶλλον ἢ θράσους more like modesty than rashness, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “de Caelo” 291b25.]]

__II
after [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Homerus Epicus]], in moral relation, worthy, estimable, of persons and things, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 7.224, etc.]]; οὐδὲν ἀξία nothing worth, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Choephori” 445; ἀξίαν κἀπ᾽ ἀξίων [prev. author] “Eu.” 435; ἀξίων γεννητόρων ἤθη φυλάσσεις 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Ion” 735.]]

__II.2
worthy of, deserving, mostly with genitive of things, ἄξιον φυγῆς, ἄξια στεναγμάτων, γέλωτος, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. author] “Med.” 1124, “Or.” 1326, “Heracl.” 507; ἐγκωμίων τί ἀξιώτερον ἤ..; 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Agesilaus” 10.3: with _genitive_ _person_, ποιεῖν ἄξια οὔτε ὑμῶν οὔτε πατέρων 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 2.71; ἄξιον τοῦ πατρός 5th-6th c.BC: Isocrates Orator 9.80; ἄξια τοῦ Μαραθῶνος διανοεῖσθαι 1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus “Cimon” 5.]]

__II.2.b

__II.3
with infinitive, Προθοήνορος ἀντὶ πεφάσθαι ἄ. worthy to be killed instead of him, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 14.472, compare 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 1.76; τίεσθαι δ᾽ ἀξιώτατος 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Agamemnon” 531; ἄ. θρήνων τυχεῖν 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Ajax” 924]]; ἄξιοι δουλεύειν only fit to be slaves, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Politica” 1254b36; also ἄ. σέβειν 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Heraclidae” 315 (Elmsl.).]]

__II.3.b
ἄξιός εἰμι, like{δίκαιός εἰμι}, I deserve to.., ἄξιός εἰμι πληγὰς λαβεῖν[Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Ecclesiazusae” 324; ἄξιός εἰμι ἀπολαῦσαι 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 5.4.19]]: absolutely, the infinitive being supplied, authorized to act, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Andocides Orator 1.132]]; ἄ. γάρ, emphatically, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Theaetetus” 143e.]]

__II.3.c
later ἄ. ἵνα[NT.John.1.27.]

__II.4
ἄξιόν [ἐστι] 'tis meet, fit, due, ἄξιον εἶναι τρεῖς ἑνὸς ἀντὶ πεφάσθαι[Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 13.446; ἄ. μνήμην ἔχειν 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.14]]: later with future infinitive, ἄ. διαπορήσειν[Refs 1st c.BC+ [1st c.BC: Didymus Grammaticus]]in D.[Refs [9.15.]]

__II.4.b
with dative person et infinitive, τῇ πόλει γὰρ ἄξιον ξυλλαβεῖν τὸν νο̄ρα 'tis meet for the city, is worth her while.., [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Acharnenses” 205; τί σοι ζῆν ἄξιο; [prev. author] “Nu.” 1074, compare “Av.” 548; ἄξιόν γε πᾶσιν ἐπολολύξαι [prev. author] “Eq.” 616; frequently in 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus as ὡς οὐκ ἄξιον εἴη βασιλεῖ ἀφεῖναι κτλ.]] that it was not meet for him.., [Refs [“An.” 2.3.25.]]

__II.4.c
the infinitive is sometimes omitted, ἄξιον γὰρ Ἑλλάδι 'tis meet in the eyes of Hellas [so to do], [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Acharnenses” 8]]; and sometimes the dative, ἄξιόν ἐστι operae pretium est, it is worth while, ἐνθυμηθῆναι[Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 1.21; γαμεῖν οὐκ ἄξιον 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Alcestis” 628.]]

NT.1Thes.2.12: _absolutely_, 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Tyrannus” 133, etc.]]; κολάσετε ἀξίως as they deserve, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 3.40.]]

[Refs 4th c.AD+ [4th c.AD: Julianus Imperator “Orationes” 7.225a]]:—middle, take away for or with oneself, παρθένον[Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.196, compare 4.80, 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Nubes” 1105, etc.]]; or that which is one's own, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 3.1.37, etc.]]:—passive, ἐς ὀξὺ ἀπηγμένας brought to a point, tapering off, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 7.64, compare 2.28, 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “de Partibus Animalium” 658b30.]]

__IV.2

[prev. author] “Ph.” 880.]]

__3

deep_entry:
Abbott-Smith / STEPBible (TBESG)
ἀπειλέω, -ῶ (ἀπειλή)
[in LXX: Nam.1:4 (גָּעַר), Isa.66:14 (זָעַם), Sir.19:17, al. ;]
to threaten: 1Pe.2:23; mid., Act.4:17 (see MM, VGT, see word, and cf. προσαπειλέω).†

LSJ / STEPBible (TFLSJ)
ἀπειλέω,

__B
3rd.pers.dual imperfect active ἀπειλήτην, Epic dialect for ἠπειλείτην, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 11.313]]: later Epic dialect present ἀπειλείω [Refs 4th c.AD+ [5th-6th c.AD: Musaeus Epicus 122, 4th-5th c.AD(?): Nonnus Epicus “Dionysiaca” 20.204]]:— hold out either in the way of promise or threat, and therefore:

__B.I
sometimes in good sense, promise, οὐδ᾽ ἠπείλησεν ἄνακτι.. ῥέξειν κλειτὴν ἑκατόμβην[Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 23.863, compare 872]]; also, boast or brag, ὥς ποτ᾽ ἀπειλήσει.1; ἦ μὲν ἀπείλησας βητάρμονας εἶναι ἀρίστους[Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 8.383, compare 4th c.AD: Julianus Imperator “Orationes” 2.57a.]]

__B.II
commonly in bad sense, threaten, in [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Homerus Epicus either _absolutely_, as 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 2.665, 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 21.368: or (more frequently) with _dative_ _person_, [prev. work] 20.272, etc.: c._accusative_ _cognate_, αἶψα δ᾽ ἀναστὰς ἠπείλησεν μῦθον]] spake a threatening speech, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 1.388]]; ἀπειλὰς ἀ., see at {ἀπειλ; δείν᾽ ἀπειλήσων ἔπη} [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Supplices” 542]]: frequently with neuter pronoun or adjective, ἀ. τόγε θυμῷ[Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 15.212]]; ταῦτα, πολλὰ ἀ., [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 7.18, 1.111, 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 8.33, etc.; πύργοις ἀ. δεινά 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Septem contra Thebas” 426; τοῦτ᾽ ἀπειλήσας ἔχεις 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Coloneus” 817.]]

__B.II.2
with accusative of the thing threatened, θάνατον ἀ. ὃς ἂν..[Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 4.81; ξίφος 1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus “Pompeius” 47; ζημίας ἀ. κατά τινος [prev. author] “Cam.” 39]]; ἠπείλησαν τοὺς ἄρχοντας threatened them with the prefects, [Refs 4th c.AD+ [4th c.AD: Libanius Sophista “Orationes” 47.7.]]

__B.II.3
dependent clauses were added in future infinitive, γέρας.. ἀφαιρήσεσθαι ἀπειλεῖς[Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 1.161, compare 15.179, 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 11.313; σφέας.. ἀπείλεε ἐκτρίψειν 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 6.37; ἀ. δράσειν τι 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Medea” 287; ἀ. ἀποκτενεῖν 5th c.BC: Lysias Orator 3.28]]: rarely in present infinitive, ἠπ... ἑλκέμεν[Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 9.682: after 8th c.BC: Homerus Epicus]] in aorist infinitive, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Memorabilia” 3.5.4, “HG” 5.4.7, 3rd c.BC: Theocritus Poeta Bucolicus 24.16.]]

__B.II.4
ἀ. ὅτι.., ὡς.., [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Plutus” 88, 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 5.5.22, etc.]]; ἀ. τινί, εἰ μή.. [Refs [[prev. author] “Cyr.” 4.5.12.]]

__B.III
passive, ἀπειλοῦμαι, of persons, to be terrified by threats, [Refs [[prev. author] “Smp.” 4.31.]]

__B.III.2
of things, τὰ ἀπειληθέντα, ={ἀπειλαί}, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Leges” 823c.]]

__B.IV
later in middle, with aorist 1 -ησάμην[Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd c.AD: Appianus Historicus “Bella Civilia” 3.29, 2nd c.AD: Polyaenus Historicus 7.35.2]]: with infinitive, forbid with threats, ἀπειλησώμεθα αὐτοῖς μηκέτι λαλεῖν[NT.Act.4.17.]

infinitive ἀπειπεῖν, Epic dialect ἀπο?~Xειπεῖν, ἀπο?~Xειπέμεν, and participle ἀποειπών, i.e. ἀποϝειπών, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 19.35, etc.]]: less frequently aorist I ἀπεῖπα[Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 3.153, 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Antigone” 405:]]future in use is ἀπερῶ, perfect ἀπείρηκα, mostly in signification [Refs [IV.  3]]:—middle, aorist I ἀπειπάμην[Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.59, 5.56, 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Ethica Nicomachea” 1163b19]], but never in correct Attic dialect:—passive, future ἀπορρηθήσομαι[Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Lysias Orator 22.14]]: aorist ἀπερρήθην[Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Leges” 929a, 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 33.21:]] —present and imperfect are supplied by ἀπαυδάω, ἀπόφημι, and in Attic dialect Prose by ἀπαγορεύω:—speak out, tell out, declare, μῦθον[Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 9.309, compare 431; ἀγγελίην 7.416; ἀληθείην 23.361; ἐφημοσύνην 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 16.340]]; μνηστήρεσσιν ἀπειπέμεν (probably μνηστῆρσ᾽ ἀποειπέμεν) to give them full notice,[Refs 8th c.BC+ [[prev. work] 1.91; ἀπηλεγέως ἀποειπεῖν 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 9.309, compare 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 1.373]]; ῥῆσιν ἀπερέοντα to deliver a verbal message, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.152]]: in aorist middle, ἀπείπασθαι θανάτῳ ζημιοῦν τοὺς πλευσομένους[Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Mirabilia” 837a2.]]

__II

__III
forbid [Refs [compare (ἀπαγορεύω 1), frequently in Prose, ἀ. τινι μὴ ποιεῖν]] forbid one to do, tell him not to do, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.155, 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Coloneus” 1760, 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Aves” 556]]; also without μή, [Refs 2nd c.BC+ [2nd c.BC: Polybius Historicus 2.52.8]]: with infinitive omitted, ἀπειπὼν εἴργει μελάθρων[Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Agamemnon” 1333, compare 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Antigone” 405]]; ἀ. τινί τι forbid him the use of it, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Politica” 1264a21]]:—passive, ἀπειρῆσθαι γάρ οἱ.. μηδενὶ ἐπιδεικνύναι[Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 6.61]]; τὸ ἀπειρημένον a forbidden thing, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. author] 3.52, 5th c.BC: Antipho Orator 3.2.7; ἀπείρηται δὲ τοῦτο τῷ νόμῳ 4th c.BC: Xenarchus Comicus 7.7]]; ἀπειρημένον, absolutely, contrary to orders, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Rhetorica” 1373b10.]]

__IV

__IV.2

__IV.3

ἀπέραντος, -ον
(περαίνω, to complete, finish) [in LXX: Job.36:26 (חֵקֶר אַיִן) 3Mac.20 * ;]
endless, interminable: 1Ti.1:4.†
(AS)

---

LSJ / STEPBible (TFLSJ)
ἀπέραντος, ον,
(περαίνω) boundless, infinite, of space, πεδίον[Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “N.” 8.38 (who also has ἀπείραντος ἀλκά “P.” 9.35); πόντου κλῇδ᾽ ἀ. 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Medea” 213 (Lyric poetry); τὸν ἀέρα τόνδ᾽ ὄντ᾽ ἀ. 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Nubes” 393; ὁδός 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Theaetetus” 147c]]; of time, endless, τὸ χρῆμα τῶν νυκτῶν ὅσον· ἀπέραντον[Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Nubes” 3; χρόνος 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Politicus” 302a]]; of number, countless, infinite, ἀ. ἀριθμὸς ἀνθρώπων[Refs 1st c.AD+ [[prev. author] “Criti.” 119a; ἀ. κακά [prev. author] “R.” 591d, +others; λῦπαι 1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus “Solon” 7; πένθη “Fab.” 17]]; unlimited, τιμωρίαι[Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 23.39]]; generally, of events, business, etc., ἀπέραντον ἦν there was no end to it, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 4.36; μακρὸν καὶ ἀ. φαίνεται 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Ethica Nicomachea” 1101a26]]; ἀπέραντα περαίνειν represent as concluded what is not concluded, [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd c.AD: Lucianus Sophista “Philops.” 9]] (with allusion to signification [Refs 2nd c.BC+ [111); μηδὲν ἀβασάνιστον μηδ᾽ ἀ. 2nd c.BC: Polybius Historicus 4.75.3.]]adverb, τὸ ἀπεράντως διεστηκός of unlimited dimensions, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Physica” 204b21, “Metaphorical” 1066b33.]]

__II
allowing no escape, whence none can pass, Τάρταρος, δίκτυον, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Prometheus Vinctus” 153, 1087 (both Lyric poetry).]]

__III
in Logic, inconclusive, λόγος[Refs 1st c.BC+ [1st c.BC: Philodemus Gadarensis Epigrammaticus “Ir.” p.97 W., compare “Stoicorum Veterum Fragmenta” 2.77.]]

__IV
incomplete, imperfect, of persons, ἀτελὴς καὶ ἀ.[Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd c.AD: Artemidorus Daldianus Onirocriticus 1.12.]]

deep_entry:
Abbott-Smith / STEPBible (TBESG)
ἀπέρχομαι,
[in LXX chiefly for הלךְ ;]
__1. to go away, depart (also, in late writers, with "perfective" force, to arrive at a destination, the  thought being carried on to the goal; M, Pr., 111f., 247; MM, see word);
__(a) absol.: Mat.13:25, al.; ptcp., ἀπελθών, used pleonastically with other verbs as in Heb. (Dalman, Words, 21), Mat.13:28, al.;
__(b) with mention of place or person: εἰς, Mat.14:15; ἐπί, Luk.24:24; πρός, Rev.10:9; ἀπό, Luk.1:38; ἐξω, Act.4:15; ἐκεῖ, Mat.2:22.
__2. As in LXX, before ὀπίσω, with genitive (Heb. הָלַךְ אַחֲרֵי), to go after, follow: Mrk.1:20, Jhn.12:19; metaphorically, Mrk.1:42, Rev.21:1.
(AS)

---

LSJ / STEPBible (TFLSJ)
ἀπέρχομαι,
future -ελεύσομαι (Attic dialect future ἄπειμι): perfect -ελήλυθα: aorist -ῆλθον:— go away, depart from, with genitive, πάτρης[Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 24.766; οἴκου 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 2.136, compare 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Coloneus” 1165, etc.; λόγου 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Iphigenia Taurica” 546; ἀ. ἀπὸ τοῦ βουλευτηρίου 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 8.92; ἐκ τῆς χώρας [prev. author] 1.89, etc.: _metaphorically_, ἀ. ἐκ δακρύων]] cease from tears. [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Orestes” 205.]]

__2
with εἰς, implying departure from one place and arrival at another, ἀ. ἐς τὰς Σάρδις[Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.22; ἀ. εἰς Θουρίους οἰκήσοντες 5th-6th c.BC: Andocides Orator 4.12; παρά τινα 2nd c.AD: Lucianus Sophista “Tim.” 11]]; ἀ. ἐπ᾽ οἴκου depart homewards, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 1.92; ἀθῷος οἴκαδε 5th-6th c.BC: Archippus Comicus 40]]; ἀπῆλθεν ὅθεν.. went back to the place whence he came, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th-3rd c.BC: Menander Comicus 481.3: _metaphorically_, ἀ. εἰς τὴν ἀρχαίαν φύσιν 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Symposium” 193c.]]

__3
absolutely, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.199, etc.]]; ταχεῖ᾽ ἀπέρχεται (i.e. ἡ νόσος) [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Philoctetes” 808]]; κᾷτ᾽ ὀφλὼν ἀ. [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Acharnenses” 689]]; ἄπελθε τουτονὶ λαβών take him and be off! [Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. author] “Av.” 948; ἀπελθόντος ἐνιαυτοῦ 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Leges” 954d; νυκτὸς -ομένης 4th-3rd c.BC: Aratus Epicus 315.]]

__4
with participle, ἀ. νικῶν come off conqueror, [Refs 1st c.AD+ [2nd c.AD: Aristides Rhetor 2.2 1st c.AD: Josephus Historicus, compare 1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus “Agesilaus” 7,etc.]]

__5
spread abroad, ἀπῆλθεν ἡ ἀκοὴ αὐτοῦ εἰς Συρίαν[NT.Matt.4.24.]

__II
depart from life, ἀ. κάτω[Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Alcestis” 379, compare 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Antigone” 818(Lyric poetry): _absolutely_, 3rd c.AD(?): Diogenes Laertius 3.6, “Anthologia Graeca” 11.335, compare 1st c.AD: Philo Judaeus 1.513, 3rd c.AD: Plotinus Philosophus 4.7.15; εἰς τοὺς θεούς “PPetr.” 2p.45 (3rd c.BC).]]

deep_entry:

to receive (in full); to be distant; (middle) to abstain, avoid
trans. to have in full what is due or is sought, Mt. 6:2, 5, 16; Lk. 6:24; Phil. 4:18; to have altogether, Phlm. 15; hence, it is enough, Mk. 14:41; intransitive to be distant, Lk. 7:6; to be estranged, Mt. 15:8; Mk. 7:6, middle to abstain from, Acts 14:20

---

LSJ / STEPBible (TFLSJ)
Included with:  ἀπέχω,
future ἀφέξω, and [Refs 8th c.BC+ [(8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 19.572) ἀποσχήσω:]]aorist ἀπέσχον:— keep off or away from, αἴ κεν τυδέος υἱὸν ἀπόσχη Ἰλίου ἱρῆς[Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 6.96, 277; ἑκὰς νήσων ἀπέχων εὐεργέα νῆα 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 15.33]]; κληῖδες ἀπ᾽ ὤμων αὐχέν᾽ ἔχουσιν the collar-bone parts the neck from the shoulders, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 22.324]]; Εὐβοίης ἀπέχειν.. αἶγας Oracle texts cited in [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 8.20, compare 22; ἄπεχε τῆς βοὸς τὸν ταῦρον 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Agamemnon” 1125 (Lyric poetry), compare “Pr.” 687 (Lyric poetry).]]

__2
with dative person, τοι.. χεῖρας ἀφέξω[Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 20.263.]]

__3
with a preposition, ἀ. φρένα περισσῶν παρὰ φωτῶν[Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Bacchae” 427 (Lyric poetry); ῥῖνα ἀπὸ κάκκης 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Pax” 162.]]

__4
c.accusative only, keep off or away, σκοτεινὸν ἀ. ψόγον[Refs 5th c.BC+ [Pi.N. 7.61; ἀ. φάσγανον 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Orestes” 1519.]]

__5
οὐδὲν ἀπέχει with infinitive, nothing hinders, debars one from doing, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus Cra.407b, 1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus 2.433a.]]

__II
middle, κακῶν ἄπο χεῖρας ἔχεσθαι hold one's hands off or away from.., [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 22.316; κυάμων ἄπο χεῖρας ἔχεσθε 5th c.BC: Empedocles Poeta Philosophus 141; ἀθανάτων ἀ. χεῖρας 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Eumenides” 350 (Lyric poetry), compare “Supp.” 756, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Symposium” 213d, 214d:]] —but mostly,

__II.2
ἀπέχεσθαί τινος hold oneself off a thing, abstain or desist from it, πολέμου[Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 8.35, +others; βοῶν 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 12.321]]; οὐδὲ.. σευ ἀφέξομαι will not keep my hands off thee,[Refs [[prev. work] 19.489; Δεκελέης]]abstain from ravaging [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator, 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 0.73, compare 1.66, 4.118, +others, 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 1.20, etc.]]; keep away from, πόλεως[Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Historia Graeca (Hellenica)” 7.3.10]]: in perfect passive, μηδὲ τῶν μικρῶν ἀπεσχημένον[Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 27.47; ἀγορᾶς ἀπεσχ. 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Politica” 1278a25.]]

__II.3
with infinitive, ἀπέχεσθαι μὴ στρατεῦσαι abstain from marching, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 5.25; λαμβάνειν ἀπέσχετο 4th-3rd c.BC: Philemo Comicus 94.3; ἀπέχεσθαι τοῦ ποιεῖν 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Memorabilia” 4.2.3; οὐκ ἀ. τὸ μὴ οὐ ποιεῖν [prev. author] “Cyr.” 1.6.32, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 354b]]: also with participle, [Refs 4th c.AD+ [4th c.AD: Julianus Imperator “Orationes” 1.43d.]]

__II.4
absolutely, refrain oneself, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 21.61.]]

__III
intransitive in active, to be away or far from, with genitive loci, τῶν Ἐπιπολῶν ἓξ ἢ ἑπτὰ σταδίους[Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 6.97]]; ἀ.ἀπὸ Βαβυλῶνος, etc., [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.179,compare 3.26, +others; ἀπὸ θαλάττης.. δώδεκα δδὸν ἡμερῶν ἀ. 3rd c.BC: Euphro Comicus 11.3; ἀ. παμπόλλων ἡμερῶν ὁδόν 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 1.1.3; τὸ μέσον ἴσον τῶν ἐσχάτων ἀ. 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Parmenides” 145b; πλεῖστον ἀ. κατὰ τόπον 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Meteorologica” 363a31; a). τὴν ἡμίσειαν διάμετρον [prev. author] Cael. 293b30, etc.]]

__III.b
project, extend, [Refs [[prev. author] “GA” 781a11; τὰἀπέχοντα]]prominent parts, PA [Refs [655a32.]]

__III.c
ἀποσχὼν τεσσαράκοντα μάλιστα σταδίους μὴ φθάσαι ἐλθώνfailing to arrinein time by.., [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 5.3.]]

__III.2
of actions, to be far from, ἀπεῖχον τῆς ἐξευρέσιος οὐδὲν ἔλασσον were just as farfrom the discovery, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.67; τοσοῦτον ἀπέχω τοῦ ποιεῖν τι ὥστε.. 5th-6th c.BC: Isocrates Orator 6.70; τοσούτῳ πλέον ἡμῶν ἀπέχεις τοῦ πιστὰ λέγειν ὅσον.. [prev. work] 11.32]]; ἀπέχει τοῦ μὴ μετ᾽ ὀργῆς [πράττειν] [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 21.41]]; πλεῖστον ἀ. τινός to be as far as possible from doing, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Memorabilia” 1.2.62]]; but τοσοῦτ᾽ ἀπέχει τῶν χορηγῶν so far is it from the thoughts of.., [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 21.59.]]

__III.3
generally, to be far remoued from, πολιτείας, μοναρχίας, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Politica” 1289b2, 1293a17; τοῦ μέσου [prev. author] “EN” 1109a10.]]

__III.4
differ from, οὐδέν τι ἀπεῖχε γαμετῆς γυναικός[Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd c.AD: Herodianus Grammaticus 1.16.4.]]

__III.5
διαφύσιες.. ᾗσιν οὐδὲν ἀπέχει ἀγγεῖα εἶναι nothing is wanting, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Hippocrates Medicus “περὶ τέχνης” 10.]]

__IV
have or receive in full, τὴν ἀπόκρισιν[Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aeschines Orator 2.50]]; τὸ χρέος ἀ. receive payment in full, [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [3rd c.BC: Callimachus Epicus “Epigrammata” 55; χάριτας [prev. work] 51]]; ἀπέχω in receipts, [Refs 1st c.AD+ [“BGU” 612.2 (1st c.AD), etc.]]; ἀ. τὸν μισθόν[NT+1st c.AD+ [1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus “Solon” 22, NT.Matt.6.2, +others; καρπὸν ἀ. τῶν πονηθέντων 1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus “Themistocles” 17; ἀ. τὸ μέτεριον [prev. author] 2.124e.]]

__IV.2
impersonal, ἀπέχει it sufficeth, it is enough, [NT.Mark.14.41, compare “Anacreontea” 15.33.]

__I.2
with dative person, κρατέουσιν[Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Empedocles Poeta Philosophus 5.1, compare 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 8.83, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Protagoras” 319b, etc.: so with _dative_ _of things_, τῷ χρησμῷ 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.158; πῶς ἀπιστήσω λόγοι; 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Philoctetes” 1350, compare 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 6.86; ἀ.τῇ ἐξ αὑτῶν ξυνέσει [prev. author] 3.37; τοῖς ἰάμασιν “IG” 4.951.24 (Epid.); ἡμῖν αὐτοῖς 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Ethica Nicomachea” 1112b10]]; ἀ.τινί τι disbelieve one in a thing, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 3.122; περί τινος [prev. author] 4.96]]; οἷς ἠπίστησαν ἔχειν.. whom they suspected of having, [Refs 2nd c.BC+ [2nd c.BC: Polybius Historicus 4.18.8.]]

νεκρὸς τὸν θάνατον ἀπιστούμενος belying death, [Refs 1st c.AD+ [1st-2nd c.AD: Polemo Sophista “Callimachus” 55.]]

deep_entry:
Abbott-Smith / STEPBible (TBESG)
ἀπό (on the frequently neglect of elision bef. vowels, see Tdf., Pr., 94, WH, App., 146),
prep. with genitive (WM, 462ff.; on its relation to ἐκ, παρά, ὑπό, ib. 456f.), [in LXX for לְ ,בְּ ,מִן ;]
from (i.e. from the exterior).
__1. Of separation and cessation;
__(1) of motion from a place: Mat.5:29, 30 7:23, Luk.5:2  22:41, al.;
__(2) in partitive sense (M, Pr., 72, 102, 245; MM, see word; Bl., §40, 2), Mat.9:16  27:21, Jhn.21:10, Act.5:2, al.; also after verbs of eating, etc.;
__(3) of alienation (cl. genitive of separation), after such verbs as λούω (Deiss., BS, 227), λύω, σώζω, παύω, etc.; ἀνάθεμα ἀ., Rom.9:3; ἀποθνήσκειν ἀ., Col.2:20; σαλευθῆναι, 2Th.2:2, καθαρός, -ίζειν, ἀ. (Deiss., BS, 196, 216), Act.20:26, 2Co.7:1, Heb.9:14;
__(4) of position, Mat.23:34 24:31, al.; after μακράν, Mat.8:30; transposed before measures of distance, Jhn.10:18 21:8, Rev.14:20 (Abbott, JG, 227);
__(5) of time, ἀπὸ τ. ὥρας, ἡμέρας, etc., Mat.9:22, Jhn.19:27, Act.20:18, Php.1:5, al.; ἀπ᾽ αἰῶνος, Luk.1:70, al.; ἀπ᾽ ἀρχῆς, etc., Mat.19:4, Rom.1:20; ἀπὸ βρέφους, 2Ti.3:15; ἀφ᾽ ἧς, since, Luk.7:45, al.; ἀπὸ τ. νῦν, Luk.1:48, al.; ἀπὸ τότε, Mat.4:17, al.; ἀπὸ πέρυσι, a year ago, 2Co.8:10 9:2; ἀπὸ πρωΐ, Act.28:23;
__(6) of order or rank, ἀπὸ διετοῦς, Mat.2:16; ἀπὸ Ἀβραάμ, Mat.1:17; ἐβδομος ἀπὸ Ἀδάμ, Ju 14; ἀπὸ μικροῦ ἕως μεγάλου, Act.8:10, Heb.8:11; ἄρχεσθαι ἀπό, Mat.20:8, Jhn.8:9, Act.8:35, al.
__2. Of origin;
__(1) of birth, extraction, and hence, in late writers,
__(a) of local extraction (cl. ἐξ; Abbott, JG, 227ff.), Mat.21:11, Mrk.15:43, Jhn.1:45, Act.10:38, al.; οἱ ἀπὸ Ἰταλίας (WM, §66, 6; M, Pr., 237; Westc, Rendall, in l.), Heb.13:24;
__(b) of membership in a community or society (BL, §40, 2), Act.12:1, al.;
__(with) of material (= cl. genitive; Bl. l.with; M, Pr., 102), Mat.3:4 27:21;
__(d) after verbs of asking, seeking, etc., Luk.11:50, 51 1Th.2:6 (Milligan, in l.);
__(2) of the cause, instrument, means or occasion (frequently = ὑπό, παρά, and after verbs of learning, hearing, knowing, etc.; Bl., §40, 3), Mat.7:16 11:29, Luk.22:45, Act.2:22 4:36 9:13 12:14, 1Co.11:23, Gal.3:2, al.; ἀπὸ τ. ὄχλου, Luk.19:3 (cf. Jhn.21:6, Act.22:11); ἀπὸ τ. φόβου, Mat.14:26, al. (cf. Mat.10:26 13:44).
__3. Noteworthy Hellenistic phrases: φοβεῖσθαι ἀπό (M, Pr., 102, 107); προσέχειν ἀπό (M, Pr., 11. with; Milligan, NTD, 50); ἀπὸ νότου (Heb. מִגֶּנֶב), Rev.21:13; ἀπὸ προσώπου (מִפְּנֵי), 2Th.1:9 (Bl., §40, 9); ἀπὸ τ. καρδιῶν (בְּלֵב), Mat.18:35; ἀπὸ ὁ ὤν (WM, §10, 2; M, Pr., 9), Rev.1:4.

of the source from which life, power, etc., are sustained, ζῆν ἀπ᾽ ὕλης ἀγρίης[Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.203]]; ἀ. κτήνεων καὶ ἰχθύων[Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. work] 216; ἀ. πολέμου [prev. author] 5.6; ἀπ᾽ ἐλαχίστων χρημάτων 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Memorabilia” 1.2.14; ἀ. τῆς ἀγορᾶς [prev. author] “An.” 6.1.1; τρέφειν τὸ ναυτικὸν ἀ. τῶν νήσων [prev. author] “HG” 4.8.9, compare 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 1.99; ἀ. τῶν κοινῶν πλουτεῖν 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Plutus” 569, compare 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 24.124; ἀ. μικρῶν εὔνους.. γεγένησαι 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Equites” 788, compare 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 18.102; ἀφ᾽ ὥρας ἐργάζεσθαι]]quaestum corpore facere, [Refs 1st c.AD+ [1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus “Timoleon” 14.]]

__A.III.6
of the cause, means, or occasion from, by, or because of which a thing is done, ἀ. τούτου κριοπρόσωπον τὤγαλμα τοῦ Διὸς ποιεῦσι[Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 2.42]]; ἀ. τινος ἐπαινεῖσθαι, θαυμάζεσθαι, ὠφελεῖσθαι, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 2.25, 6.12, 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 1.1.2; ἀ. τῶν ξυμφορῶν διαβάλλεσθαι 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 5.17; τὴν ἐπωνυμίαν ἔχειν ἀ. τινος [prev. author] 1.46; ἀ. λῃστείας τὸν βίον ἔχειν 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 7.7.9; ἀπ᾽ αὐτῶν τῶν ἔργων κρίνειν 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 2.27]]; ἀ. τοῦ πάθους in consequence of.., [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 4.30; βλάπτειν τινὰ ἀ. τινος [prev. author] 7.29; κατασκευάσαντα τὸ πλοῖον ἀφ᾽ ὧν ὑπελάμβανε σωθήσεσθαι 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 18.194]]; τρόπαιον ἀ. τινος εἱστήκει on occasion of his defeat, [Refs [[prev. author] 19.320]]; τλήμων οὖσ᾽ ἀπ᾽ εὐτόλμου φρενός[Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Agamemnon” 1302, compare 1643]]; ἀ. δικαιοσύνης by reason of it (variant for{ὑπό}), [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 7.164]]; ἀ. τῶν αὐτῶν λημμάτων on the same scale of profits, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 3.34, etc.]]; for ὅσον ἀ. βοῆς ἕνεκα, see at {ἕνεκα}: hence in half adverbial usages, ἀ. σπουδῆς in earnest, eagerly, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 7.359]]; ἀ. τοῦἴσου, ἀ. τῆς ἴσης, or ἀπ᾽ ἴσης, equally, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 1.99, 15, 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 14.6, etc.; ἀπ᾽ ὀρθῆς καὶ δικαίας τῆς ψυχῆς [prev. author] 18.298; ἀ. ἀντιπάλου παρασκευῆς 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 1.91; ἀ. τοῦ προφανοῦς openly, [prev. work] 35]]; ἀ. τοῦ εὐθέος straightforwardly, [Refs [[prev. author] 3.43]]; ἀ. τοῦ αὐτομάτου of free-will, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Protagoras” 323c]]; ἀ. γλώσσης by word of mouth, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.123]] (but also, from hearsay, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Agamemnon” 813); ἀ. στόματος 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Theaetetus” 142d]]; ἀπ᾽ ὄψεως at sight, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Lysias Orator 16.19]]; ἀ. χειρὸς λογίζεσθαι on your fingers, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Vespae” 656; πεύθομαι δ᾽ ἀπ᾽ ὀμμάτων νόστον 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Agamemnon” 988]]; ὀμμάτων ἄπο in the public gaze, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Medea” 216; ἀ. τοῦ κυάμου ἄρχοντας καθίστασθαι 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Memorabilia” 1.2.9; ἡ βουλὴ ἡ ἀ. τοῦ κυάμου 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 8.66, compare “IG” 1.9; τοὺς ἀ. τοῦ κυάμου δισχιλίους ἄνδρας 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Ἀθηναίων Πολιτεία” 24.3]]; τριηράρχους αἱρεῖσθαι ἀ. τῆς οὐσίας Canon Laws texts cited in [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 18.106]]; ἀφ᾽ ἑαυτοῦ from oneself, on one's own account, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 8.6, etc.; ἀφ᾽ ἑαυτοῦ γνώμης [prev. author] 4.68]]; ἀ. συνθήματος, ἀ. παραγγέλματος, by agreement, by word of command, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 5.74, 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 8.99]]; ἀ. σάλπιγγος by sound of trumpet, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “de Equitum magistro” 3.12 (assuming variant)]]; ἐπίτροπος ἀ. τῶν λόγων, = Latin procurator a rationibus, Ann.epigram.[Refs 2nd c.AD+ [1913.143a (Ephesus, 2nd c.AD).]]

__A.III.7
of the object spoken of, τὰ ἀ. τῆς νήσου οἰκότα ἐστί the things told from or of the island.., [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 4.195, compare 54, 7.195; νόμος κείμενος ἀ. τῶν τεχνῶν 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Ranae” 762.]]

__B
in [Refs 4th c.AD+ [4th c.AD(?): Arcadius Grammaticus, 5th c.AD: Cypria, ἀπύ takes _dative_, ἀπὺ τᾷ [ἁμέρᾳ] “IG” 5(2).6 (from Tegea)]]; ἀπὺ τᾷ ζᾷ[Refs [“Inscription Cyprian dialect” 135.8 H. (from Idalion).]]

__B.2
in later Greek ἀπό is found with accusative, [Refs 4th c.AD+ [“PLond.” 1.124.30 (4th-5th c.AD).]]

__C
in [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Homerus Epicus]] frequent with Verbs in tmesi, as [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 5.214, etc., and sometimes in Prose, as 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 8.89.]]

__D
IN COMPOSITION (joined with other words),

__D.1
asunder, as ἀποκόπτω, ἀπολύω, ἀποτέμνω: and hence, away, off, as ἀποβάλλω, ἀποβαίν; denoting, remoual of an accusation, as ἀπολογέομαι, ἀποψηφίζομαι.

__D.2
finishing off, completing, ἀπεργάζομαι, ἀπανδρόω, ἀπανθρωπίζω, ἀπογλαυκόω.

__D.3
ceasing from, leaving off, as ἀπαλγέω, ἀποκηδεύω, ἀπολοφύρομαι, ἀποζέω, ἀπανθίζω, ἀφυβρίζω.

__D.4
back again, as ἀποδίδωμι, ἀπολαμβάνω, ἀπόπλους: also, in full, or what is one's own, as ἀπέχω, ἀπολαμβάνω: frequently it only strengthens the sense of the simple.

__D.5
by way of abuse, as in ἀποκαλέω.

__D.6
almost ={ἀ-} privative; sometimes with Verbs, as ἀπαυδάω, ἀπαγορεύ; more frequently with Adjectives, as ἀποχρήματος, ἀπότιμος, ἀπόσιτος, ἀπόφονος.

__E
ἄπο, by anastrophe for ἀπό, when it follows its Noun, as ὀμμάτων ἄπο[Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Electra” 1231, etc.]]; never in Prose.

__E.2
ἄπο for ἄπεστι, [Refs 7th c.BC+ [7th-6th c.BC(?): Semonides Iambographus 1.20, 5th c.BC: Timocreon Lyricus 9.]]

ἀπο-βαίνω
[in LXX for הָיָה, etc. ;]
to step off, disembark: Luk.5:2, Jhn.21:9; metaphorically, of events, to issue, turn out (Field, Notes, 74): Luk.21:13, Php.1:19 (MM, see word).†
(AS)

LSJ / STEPBible (TFLSJ)
ἀποβαίνω,
future -βήσομαι, with Epic dialect aorist 1 -εβήσετο[Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 2.35:]]aorist 2 ἀπέβην: perfect ἀποβέβηκα—in these tenses intransitive (present not in [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Homerus Epicus)]]:— step off from a place, νηὸς ἀ. alight, disembark from a ship, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 13.281]]; ἀπὸ τῶν νεῶν, ἀπὸ τῶν πλοίων, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 5.86, 4.110; ἐκ τῶν νεῶν 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Historia Graeca (Hellenica)” 5.1.12]]:absolutely, disembark, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 2.29, 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 1.111, etc.; ἀ. ἐς χώρην 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 7.8.β,compare 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Fragmenta” 705, 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 4.9, 5th c.BC: Lysias Orator 2.21; ἐς τὴν γῆν 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 1.100]]; ἐξ ἵππων ἀ. ἐπὶ χθόνα dismount from a chariot, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 3.265, compare 11.619; ἵππων 17.480; but in 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 61.23 τὸ ἀποβαίνειν]] seems to be the art of leaping from horse to horse (compare ἀποβάτης) τῇ συνωρίδι τοῦ ἀποβάντος[Refs [“IG” 9(2).527.10 (from Larissa): generally, ἀβάτων ἀποβάς]] having stepped off ground on which none should step, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Coloneus” 167.]]

__2
go away, depart, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 1.428, 5.133, etc.; ἀπέβη πρὸς μακρὸν Ολυμπον 24.468]]; πρὸς δώματα, κατὰ δῶμα, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 4.657, 715; μετ᾽ ἀθανάτους 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 21.298: with _genitive_, ἀ. πεδίων 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Hecuba” 140; ἀπὸ τῆς φάτνης 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “de Equitum magistro” 1.16]]; of death, ἀπὸ δὲ φθίμενοι βεβᾶσι[Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Andromache” 1022]]; of hopes, vanish, come to nought, [Refs [[prev. author] “Ba.” 909 (Lyric poetry).]]

__II
of events, issue, result from, τὰ ἔμελλε ἀποβήσεσθαι ἀπὸ τῆς μάχης[Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 9.66; τἀναντία ἀπέβη]]resulted, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Philebus” 39a, compare “Lg.” 782e; ὅ τι ἀποβήσεται [prev. author] “Prt.” 318a, etc.]]; τὸ ἀποβαῖνον, contraction τὠποβαῖνον, the issue, event, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 2.82, etc.]]; τὰ ἀποβαίνοντα, τὸ ἀποβάν, the results, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 1.83, 2.87; τὰ ἀποβησόμενα]]the probable results, [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [[prev. author] 3.38, compare 2nd c.AD: Sextus Empiricus Philosophus “adversus Mathematicos” 5.103.]]

__II.2
frequently with an adverb or other qualifying phrase, σκοπέειν.. τὴν τελευτὴν κῇ ἀποβήσεται how it will turn out, issue, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.32; ἀ. τῇ περ εἶπε [prev. work] 86; ἀ. κατὰ τὸ ἐόν [prev. work] 97]]; ἀ. παρὰ δόξαν, ἀ. τοιοῦτον, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. author] 8.4, 7.23; τοιόνδ᾽ ἀπέβη τόδε πρᾶγμα 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Medea” 1419, compare 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 1.5.13; πολέμου τοιοῦτον ἀπέβη τὸ τέλος 2nd c.BC: Polybius Historicus 26.6.15; οὐδὲν αὐτῷ.. ὡς προσεδέχετο ἀπέβαινεν 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 4.104, compare 3.26; παρὰ γνώμην ἀ. 5.14; opposed to κατὰ γνώμαν ἀ. 3rd c.BC: Theocritus Poeta Bucolicus 15.38; πῶς ἡ φήμη δοκεῖ ὑμῖν ἀποβῆνα; 5th-6th c.BC: Andocides Orator 1.131.]]

__II.3
absolutely, turn out well, succeed, ἡ ὑπόσχεσις ἀπέβη[Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 4.39, compare 5.14]]; of dreams, turn out true, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Div. Somn.” 463b10.]]

__II.4
of persons, with an adjective, turn out, prove to be so and so, ἀ. οὐ κοινοί prove partial, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 3.53; ἀ. χείρους 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Leges” 952b; φρενιτικοὶ ἀ. 5th c.BC: Hippocrates Medicus “Κωακαὶ προγνώσιες” 405; τύραννος ἐκ βασιλέως ἀ. 2nd c.BC: Polybius Historicus 7.13.7]]; also of a wound, ἰάσιμον ἀ.[Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Leges” 878c.]]

__II.4.b
with εἰς.., ἀ. εἰς τὰ πολιτικὰ οἱ τοιοῦτοι prove fit for public affairs, [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [[prev. author] “Smp.” 192a; ἐς ἀλαθινὸν ἄνδρ᾽ ἀ. 3rd c.BC: Theocritus Poeta Bucolicus 13.15.]]

__II.4.c
of conditions, etc., ἀπέβη ἐς μουναρχίην things ended in a monarchy, [NT+5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 3.82; εἰς ἓν τέλεον καὶ νεανικόν 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 425c; ἀποβήσεται εἰς μαρτυρίαν NT.Luke.21.13.]]

__II.5
of space, μέγεθος μὲν ἦν πρὸς τὸν Ἠριδανὸν ἀποβεβηκῦα reaching, extending to.., [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Critias” 112a.]]

__II.6
τῷ ἀποβεβηκότι ποδί with the hind foot, opposed to τῷ προβεβηκότι, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “de Incessu Animalium” 706a9.]]

__B
causal, in aorist 1 ἀπέβησα, cause to dismount, disembark, land (in which sense ἀποβιβάζω serves as present), ἀ. στρατιήν[Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 5.63, 6.107; ἐς τὴν Ψυττάλειαν [prev. author] 8.95.]]

__B.II
hence, in passive, τὸ ἀποβαινόμενον σκέλος a leg put out so as not to bear the weight of the body, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Hippocrates Medicus “περὶ ἄρθρων ἐμβολῆς” 52]]:—active, [Refs [[prev. author] “Mochl.” 20.]]

Dion.Brut.” 3.]]

throw away, sell too cheap, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Oeconomicus” 20.28.]]

lose, τὴν τυραννίδα[Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.60]]; τὰ πατρώια, τὸν στρατόν, τὴν κεφαλήν, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. author] 3.53, 8.65, +others; βιοτάν 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Fragmenta” 593; τὴν οὐσίαν 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Ecclesiazusae” 811, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Crito” 44e, etc.; ἱκανὸν μέρος τῶν ὄντων 5th c.BC: Antipho Orator 2.1.6, etc.]]; opposed to κτᾶσθαι, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Isocrates Orator 6.57, 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Politica” 1291b41]]; ἀ.δόξαν, τέχνην, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. author] “de An.” 428b5, “Metaphorical” 1047a1, +others; ἀ. τι ὑπό τινος 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Symposium” 4.32; ἀ. πολλοὺς τῶν στρατιωτῶν 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 4.7; τὸν εὐεργέταν 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Hercules Furens” 878]]:—in middle, ἀγαθὸν πολίτην[Refs [“SIG” 730.20 (from Olbia).]]

to give up or back, restore, return: Mat.27:58, Luk.4:20 9:42 19:8; esp. of wages, debts, oaths, etc. (MM, see word), to render what is due, to pay (Deiss., LAE, 334 f.): absol., Mat.18:25, 28, Luk.7:42. with accusative, Mat.5:26 18:29-30, 34 20:8 21:41 22:21, Mrk.12:17, Luk.10:35 12:59 20:25, Rom.13:7, Heb.12:11, Rev.22:2; ὅρκους, Mat.5:33 (cf. Num.30:3, Deu.23:21 al.); of conjugal duty, τ. ὀφειλήν, 1Co.7:3; ἀμοιβάς, 1Ti.5:4; μαρτύριον, to give (as in duty bound) testimony, Act.4:33; λόγον, to render account, Mat.12:36, Luk.16:2, Act.19:40, Heb.13:17, 1Pe.4:5; hence of requital, recompense, both in good and bad sense, Mat.6:4, 6 6:18 16:27, Rom.2:6, 2Ti.4:8 4:14 Rev.18:6 22:12; κακὸν ἀντὶ κακοῦ, Rom.12:17, 1Th.5:15, 1Pe.3:9. ἀποκρίνω, ἀποκρίνομαι,
[in LXX chiefly for ענה ;]
in cl.,
__1. to separate, distinguish.
__2. to choose.
Mid., to answer: Mat.27:12, Mrk.14:61, Luk.3:16 23:9, Jhn.5:17, 19 Act.3:12. In late Gk. the pass, also is used in this sense, and pass. forms are the more frequently in NT (M, Pr., 39, 161; MM, see word);
__(a) in general sense: absol., Mrk.12:34; with accusative of thing(s), Mat.22:46; with dative of person(s), Mat.12:38; before πρός, Act.25:16;
__(b) Hebraistically
__(i) like ענה, to begin to speak, take up the conversation (Kennedy, Sources, 124f.): Mat.11:25, al.,
__(ii) redundant, as in the Heb. phrase וַיַּעַן וַיּאֹמֶר (Dalman, Words, 24f., 38; M, Pr., 14; Bl., §58, 4; 74, 2; Cremer, 374): ἀποκριθεὶς εἶπε, Mat.4:4; ἔφη, 8:8; λέγει, Mrk.3:33; in Jo most frequently (ἀπεκ. κ. εἶπε, 1:49. )
(AS)

middle, ἀποκρίνομαι, future -κρῐνοῦμαι, etc.: [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus]] uses perfect and pluperfect passive in middle sense, [Refs [“Prt.” 358a, “Grg.” 463c]], etc., but also in passive sense (see. below):—give answer to, reply to question,[Refs 5th c.BC+ [uncertain 1. in 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 5.49, 8.101 (elsewhere ὑποκρ-),compare 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Bacchae” 1271, “IA” 1354; ἀ. τινί 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Nubes” 1245, etc.: _metaphorically_, ἀ. τοῖς πράγμασιν ὡς ἐπὶ τῶν ἐρωτημάτων 2nd c.AD: Arrianus Historicus “Epicteti Dissertationes” 2.16.2]]; ἀ. πρός τινα, πρὸς τὸ ἐρωτώμενον, to a questioner or question, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 5.42, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Protagoras” 338d; ἀ. εἰ.. 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Vespae” 964; ἀ. ὅτι.. 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 1.90: with _accusative_, ἀποκρίνεσθαι τὸ ἐρωτηθέν]] to answer the question, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. author] 3.61, compare 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Crito” 49a, “Hp.Ma.” 287b, 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Metaphysica” 1007a9: with _accusative_ _cognate_, ἀ. οὐδὲ γρῦ 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Plutus” 17; οὐδὲν ξυμβατικόν 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 8.71; ἀ. ἀπόκρισιν 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Leges” 658c:]] —passive, τοῦτό μοι ἀποκεκρίσθω let this be my answer, [Refs [[prev. author] “Tht.” 187b]]; καλῶς ἄν σοι ἀπεκέκριτο your answer would have been sufficient, [Refs [[prev. author] “Grg.” 453d, compare “Men.” 75c, “Euthd.” 299d.]]

__IV.2
answer charges, defend oneself, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Acharnenses” 632; ὁ ἀποκρινόμενος]]the defendant, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Antipho Orator 6.18, compare 2.4.3]]; ἀπεκρινάμην frequently in legal documents, [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [“PHib.” 1.31.24 (3rd c.BC), etc.]]

__IV.3
aorist passive ἀπεκρίθη, ={ἀπεκρίνατο}, he answered, condemned by [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd c.AD: Phrynichus Atticista 86]], is unknown in earlier Attic dialect, except in [LXX+5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Pherecrates Comicus 51, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus Alcaeus2.149b; but occurs in Machoap. 2nd c.AD: Athenaeus Epigrammaticus 8.349d, “UPZ” 6.30 (2nd c.BC), “SIG” 674.61 (Narthacium, 2nd c.BC), “IG” 4.679 (Hermione, 2nd c.BC), 2nd c.BC: Polybius Historicus 4.30.7, etc.; once in 1st c.AD: Josephus Historicus, “AJ” 9.3.1, twice in 2nd c.AD: Lucianus Sophista, “Sol.” 5, “Demon.” 26; regular in LXX (but sometimes ἀπεκρινάμην]] in solemn language, as [Refs [“3 Ki.” 2.1)]] and prevails in “NT” especially in the phrase ἀποκριθεὶς εἶπεν[NT+5th c.BC+ [NT.Matt.3.15; ἀ. λέγει NT.Mark.8.20, +others, compare 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 2.1.22 codices:]]future ἀποκριθήσομαι in same sense, [LXX+NT+2nd c.AD+ [LXX.Isa.14.32, +others, NT.Matt.25.45, 2nd c.AD: Hermogenes Rhetor “περὶ εὑρέσεως” 4.6.]]

[in LXX for H2308 יָתַר, etc. ;]
__1. to leave, leave behind (in π. a term. techn. in wills; see MM, see word): 2Ti.4:13 4:20, Tit.1:5; pass., to be reserved, remain: Heb.4:6, 9 10:26.

LSJ / STEPBible (TFLSJ)
ἀπο-λείπω,
aorist ἀπέλῐπον (ἀπέλειψα late, [Refs 1st c.AD+ [4th c.AD: Themistius Sophista “Orationes” 25.310d, 1st c.AD(?): Pseudo-Phocylidea 77)]]:—

__A
leave over or behind, οὐδ᾽ ἀπέλειπεν ἔγκατα[Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 9.292, compare 1st c.AD(?): Heraclitus 56, etc.; κλέος καὶ φήμην 5th c.BC: Critias Philosophus, Tragicus, Elegiacus 44 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator]]; bequeath, Test. Epict.[Refs 2nd c.BC+ [2.3, compare 2nd c.BC: Moschus Bucolicus 3.97]]; ἀ. κληρονόμον leave as one's heir, [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [“POxy.” 105.3 (2nd c.AD)]]; bequeath to posterity, of writings, [Refs 3rd c.AD+ [3rd c.AD(?): Diogenes Laertius 8.58, compare 7.54.]]

__A.2
leave hold of, lose, ψυχάν[Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “P.” 3.101 (tmesis); βίον 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Ph.” (Lyric poetry, tmesis); νέαν ἁμέραν ἀπολιπὼν θάνοι 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Ion” 720 (Lyric poetry): conversely, ἐμὲ μὲν ἀπολέλοιπεν ἤδη βίοτος 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Electra” 185 (Lyric poetry). 3]]. leave behind in the race, distance: generally, surpass, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 8.3.25, 5th c.BC: Lysias Orator 2.4; τινὰ περί τι 5th-6th c.BC: Isocrates Orator 4.50]]:—more frequently in middle and passive, see below 4. leave undisputed: hence, admit, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [3rd c.BC: Chrysippus Stoicus 3.173, 1st c.BC: Philodemus Philosophus “de Pietate - Herkulanische Studien” 17, 2nd c.AD: Sextus Empiricus Philosophus “adversus Mathematicos” 7.55, 3rd c.AD(?): Diogenes Laertius 7.54; αἰτίαν νόσων ἀ. τὸ αἷμα 4th c.BC: Meno Medicus “Iatrika” 11.43; [ὁ Διοκλῆς] τὴν φρόνησιν περὶ τὴν καρδίαν ἀ. 3rd c.BC: Herodas Mimographus]] middle in [Refs [“Rh.Mus.” 49.540.5]]. leave, allow, ὑπερβολὴν οὐδὲ ταῖς ἑταίραις[Refs 4th c.AD+ [4th c.AD: Julianus Imperator “Orationes” 7.210d.]]

__A.II
desert, abandon, one's post, etc., οὐδ᾽ ἀπολείπουσιν κοῖλον δόμον, of bees, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 12.169, compare 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 8.41, +others]]; ἀ. (i.e. τὴν πολιορκίην) [Refs [[prev. author] 7.170]]; τὴν ξυμμαχίαν, τὴν ξυνωμοσίαν, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 3.9, 64]]; of persons, καί σ᾽ ἀπολείψω σου λειπόμενος[Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Electra” 1310]]; ξεῖνον πατρώϊον ἀ. leave him in the lurch, [Refs 6th c.BC+ [6th c.BC: Theognis Elegiacus 521; ἀπολιπὼν οἴχεται 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 3.48, compare 5.103, 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Ranae” 83]]; of a wife, desert her husband, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Andocides Orator 4.14, 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 30.4]] (not of the husband, [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd c.AD: Lucianus Sophista “Sol.” 9)]]; of sailors, desert, τὴν ναῦν[Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 50.14.2. with]]infinitive, ἀ. τούτους κακῶς γηράσκειν leave them to grow old, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Oeconomicus” 1.22.3]]. leave undone or unsaid, ὅσα ἀπέλιπε κτείνων τε καὶ διώκων.. σφέα ἀπετέλεσε[Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 5.92. ; ὕβρεως οὐδ᾽ ὁτιοῦν ἀ. 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 54.4, compare 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 420a]]; omit, συχνὰ ἀπολείπω [Refs [[prev. work] 509c.]]

__A.III
leave open, leave a space, ἀ. μεταίχμιον οὐ μέγα[Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 6.77; ἀ. ὡς πλέθρον 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 6.5.11]]; μικρὸν ἀ. leaving a small interval, [Refs 2nd c.BC+ [2nd-1st c.BC(?): Hero Mechanicus “Automatopoetica” 27.1.]]

__A.IV
intransitive, cease, fail, τάων οὔποτε καρπὸς ἀπόλλυται οὐδ᾽ ἀπολείπει[Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 7.117]]; opposed to γίνεται, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Diogenes Apolloniates Philosophus 7]]; of rivers, fall, sink, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 2.14, 93; ἀ. τὸ ῥέεθρον [prev. author] 2.19; τῆς θαλάττης τὰ μὲν ἀπολειπούσης, τὰ δ᾽ ἐπιούσης 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Meteorologica” 353a22]]; of swallows, δι᾽ ἔτεος ἐόντες οὐκ ἀπολείπουσι[Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 2.22]]; of youth, begin to decay, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Symposium” 8.14]]; fail, flag, lose heart, [Refs [[prev. author] “Cyr.” 4.2.3]]; of the moon, wane, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Analytica Posteriora” 0.98a33.]]

__A.IV.2
with genitive, to be wanting of or in a thing, προθυμίας οὐδὲν ἀ.[Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 8.22, compare 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 533a: frequently of numbers, μηδὲν ἀ. τῶν πέντε κτλ. [prev. author] “Lg.” 828b; τῶν εἴκοσιν ὀλίγον ἀ. 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Historia Animalium” 573b16, etc.]]; ἀπὸ τεσσέρων πηχέων ἀ. τρεῖς δακτύλους wanting three fingers of four cubits, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.60, compare 7.117; μήτ᾽ ἄρ᾽ ὑπερβάλλων βοὸς ὁπλὴν μήτ᾽ ἀπολείπων 8th-7th c.BC: Hesiodus Epicus “Opera et Dies” 489: with]]infinitive, ὀλίγον ἀπέλιπον ἐς Ἀθήνας ἀπικέσθαι wanted but little of coming, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 7.9. ; βραχὺ ἀ. διακόσιαι γενέσθαι 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 7.70; οὐδὲν δ᾽ ἀπολείπετε οὕτω πολεμεῖν 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 4.40; ἡ πόλις μικρὸν ἀπέλιπεν ἔρημος εἶναι 1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus “Tim.” I.]]

__A.IV.3
with participle, leave off doing, ἀ. λέγων[Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Oeconomicus” 6.1: _absolutely_, ὅθεν ἀπέλιπες]] from the point at which.., [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Gorgias” 497c, compare “Phd.” 78b, 4th c.BC: Isaeus Orator 5.12.]]

__A.IV.4
depart from, ἐκ τῶν Συρακουσῶν[Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 5.4; ἐκ τοῦ Μηδικοῦ πολέμου [prev. author] 3.10, compare 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Phaedo” 112c.]]

__B
middle (aorist ἀπελιπόμην in [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [3rd c.BC: Apollonius Rhodius Epicus 1.399 (tmesis)), like]]active [Refs [1.1]], bequeath to posterity, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 2.134 codices]]; compare ἀπολείψεται· ἐάσεται, [Refs 5th c.AD+ [5th c.AD(?): Hesychius Legal icographus]]

__C
passive, to be left behind, stay behind, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 7.75 (variant for{ὑπο-}) 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 1.4.20; μόνος ἀπολελειμμένος 5th c.BC: Antipho Orator 1.3]]; to be unable to follow an argument, be at a loss, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Theaetetus” 192d.]]

__C.2
to be distanced by, inferior to, ἀ. [ἀπὸ] τῶν ἄλλων θηρίων[Refs [Diocl.fragment 145]]; to be inferior, ἔν τισι[Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Isocrates Orator 12.61.]]

__C.II
to be absent or distant from, with genitive, πολὺ τῆς ἀληθηΐης ἀπολελειμμένοι[Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 2.106, compare 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 475d; ἥβας 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Hercules Furens” 440 (Lyric poetry): with _genitive_ _person_, 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Memorabilia” 4.2.40, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Symposium” 192d: _absolutely_, 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Orestes” 80, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Phaedrus” 240c]]; to be deprived of, τοῦ σοῦ.. μὴ ἀπολείπεσθαι τάφου[Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Electra” 1169; πατρῴας μὴ ἀ. χθονός 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Medea” 35; τῶν πρὶν ἀπολειφθεὶς φρενῶν [prev. author] “Or.” 216.]]

__C.II.2
to be wanting in, fall short of, ὅτι τοῦ σκώπτειν ἀπελείφθη[Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Equites” 525]]; τοῖς ἀπολειφθεῖσι (i.e. τῆς παιδείας[Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 18.128, compare 5th-6th c.BC: Isocrates Orator 12.209]]; ἀπολειφθεὶς ἠμῶν without our cognizance, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 19.36; ἀπολειφθῆναι τῶν πραγμάτων]]to be left in ignorance of.., [Refs [[prev. author] 27.2]]; καιροῦ ἀ. miss the opportunity, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. author] 34.38, compare 5th-6th c.BC: Isocrates Orator 3.19]]; θεάματος, ἑορτῆς ἀ., [Refs 5th c.BC+ [2nd c.AD: Lucianus Sophista “DMar.” 15.1, “Sacr.” 1; εἰσβολῆς 5th-6th c.BC: Isocrates Orator 14.31.]]

__C.II.3
remain to be done, [Refs 2nd c.BC+ [2nd c.BC: Polybius Historicus 3.39.12: _impersonal_, ἀπολείπεται λέγειν, διδάσκειν, 3rd c.AD(?): Diogenes Laertius 7.85, 2nd c.AD: Sextus Empiricus Philosophus “adversus Mathematicos” 7.1.]]

Abbott-Smith / STEPBible (TBESG)
ἀπ-όλλυμι and ἀπολλύω
[in LXX for אָבַד, etc. (38 words in all)].
__1. Act.,
__1 to destroy utterly, destroy, kill: Mk 124, 922, al.; τ. ψνχήν, Mat.10:28, al.;
__2 to lose utterly: Mat.10:42, al.; metaphorically, of failing to save, Jhn.6:39 18:9.
__2. Mid.,
__1 to perish;
__(a) of things: Mat.5:29, Jhn.6:12, Heb.1:11 (LXX, al.;
__(b) of persons: Mat.8:26, al. Metaphorical, of loss of eternal life, Jhn.3:15-16 10:28 17:12, Rom.2:12, 1Co.8:11 15:18, 2Pe.3:9. In οἱ ἀπολλὺμενοι, the perishing, contrasted in 1Co.1:18, al., with οἱ σωζόμενοι, the "perfective" force of the verb, WH. " implies the completion of the process of destruction," is illustrated (see M, Pr., 114 f.; M, Th., ii, 2:10);
__2 to be lost: Luk.15:4 21:18. Metaphorical, on the basis of the relation between shepherd and flock, of spiritual destitution and alienation from God: Mat.10:6 15:24, Luk.19:10 (MM, see word; DCG, i, 191 f., ii, 76, 554; Cremer, 451)
(AS)

Included with:  ἀπόλλῡμι
or ἀπολλύω [Refs 5th c.BC+ [(5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 4.25, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 608e, 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Politica” 1297a12, but _falsa lectio_ in 4th-3rd c.BC: Menander Comicus 580]]; the form is rejected by [Refs 5th c.BC+ [2nd c.AD: Phrynichus Atticista “Praeparatio Sophistica” p.10 5th c.BC: Bacchylides Lyricus, 2nd c.AD: Moeris Grammaticus 12)]], imperfect ἀπώλλυν[Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Persae” 652(Lyric poetry), 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Electra” 1360, ἀπώλλυον 5th-6th c.BC: Andocides Orator 1.58:]]future ἀπολέσω, Epic dialect ἀπολέσσω, Attic dialect ἀπολῶ, Ionic dialect ἀπολέω[Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.34, +others:]]aorist ἀπώλεσα, Epic dialect ἀπόλεσσα: perfect ἀπολώλεκα:—frequently in tmesi in Epic dialect; preposition postponed in [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 9.534:]] —stronger form of ὄλλυμι, destroy utterly, kill, in [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Homerus Epicus]] mostly of death in battle, ἀπώλεσε λαὸν Ἀχαιῶν[Refs [11.5.758, +others; ἐκπάγλως ἀπόλεσσαν [prev. work] 1.268]]; also of things, demolish, lay waste, ἀπώλεσεν Ἴλιον ἱρήν [Refs [[prev. work] 5.648]], etc.; generally, βίοτον δ᾽ ἀπὸ πάμπαν ὀλέσσει will waste my substance, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 2.49]]; οἵ μ᾽ ἀπωλλύτην sought to destroy me (imperfect sense), [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Tyrannus” 1454]]; in pregnant sense, ἐπεί με γᾶς ἐκ πατρίας ἀπώλεσε drove me ruined from.., [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Hecuba” 946]]; τῆς παρ᾽ ἡμέραν χάριτος τὰ μέγιστα τῆς πόλεως ἀ. for the sake of.., [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 8.70.]]

__2
λόγοις or λέγων ἀ. τινά talk or bore one to death, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Electra” 1360, 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Nubes” 892 (Lyric poetry)]]: hence, alone, in future ἀπολεῖς με[Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. author] “Ach.” 470; οἴμ᾽ ὡς ἀπολεῖς με 5th c.BC: Pherecrates Comicus 108.20]]; ἀπολεῖ μ᾽ οὑτοσί by his questions, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Antiphanes Comicus 222.8, etc.]]

__3
ruin a woman, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Lysias Orator 1.8.]]

__II
lose, πατέρ᾽ ἐσθλὸν ἀπώλεσα[Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 2.46, compare 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 18.82, 3rd c.AD: Democritus Epigrammaticus 272; ἀπώλεσε νόστιμον ἦμαρ 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 1.354]]; ἀπὸ θυμὸν ὀλέσσαι lose one's life,[Refs 8th c.BC+ [11.16.861, 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 12.350]]; θυμὸν οὐκ ἀπώλεσεν loses not his spirit, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Electra” 26; ἔλεον ἀπώλεσεν 11.24.44]]; frequently of things, ἡ τοῦ πλέονος ἐπιθυμίη τὸ παρεὸν ἀπόλλυσι[Refs 5th c.BC+ [3rd c.AD: Democritus Epigrammaticus 224; ἵππους ἑβδομήκοντα ἀπολλύασι 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 7.51; ἀπώλεσαν τὴν ἀρχὴν ὑπὸ Περσῶν 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 3.4.11, compare 7.2.22; μηδὲν ἀπολλὺς τοῦ ὄγκου 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Theaetetus” 155c]]; ἀ. οὐσίαν, ={ἀπόλλυσθαι}, [Refs [[prev. author] “Prm.” 163d.]]

__B
middle, ἀπόλλῠμαι: future -ολοῦμαι, Ionic dialect -ολέομαι[Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 7.218:]]aorist 2 -ωλόμην: perfect -όλωλα, whence the barbarous imperfect ἀπόλωλο[Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Thesmophoriazusae” 1212:]]pluperfect in Attic dialect Prose sometimes written ἀπωλώλειν in codices, as [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 4.133, 7.27]]:—perish, die, [Refs [11.1.117]], etc.; cease to exist, opposed to γίγνεσθαι, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Melissus Philosophus 8, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Parmenides” 156b, etc.: sometimes with _accusative_ _cognate_, ἀπόλωλε κακὸν μόρον 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 1.166; ἀπωλόμεθ᾽ αἰπὺν ὄλεθρον [prev. work] 9.303: with _dative_ modi, ἀπώλετο λυγρῷ ὀλέθρῳ (variant{λυγρὸν ὄλεθρον}) [prev. work] 3.87; ἀ. ὑπό τινος 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 5.126]]; simply, to be undone, αὐτῶν.. ἀπωλόμεθ᾽ ἀφραδίῃσιν[Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 10.27; ἀπωλώλει τῷ φόβῳ μή.. 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 6.1.2: frequently in _Attic dialect_, especially in]]perfect, ἀπόλωλας you are lost, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Nubes” 1077; ἀπωλόμεθ᾽ ἂν εἰ μὴ ἀπολώλειμεν 1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus 2.185f; ἱκανὸν χρόνον ἀπολλύμεθα καὶ κατατετρίμμεθα 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Pax” 355; βλέπειν ἀπολωλός 3rd c.AD: Philostratus Junior Sophista “Imagines” 2:—as an imprecation, κάκιστ᾽ ἀπολοίμην εἰ.. 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Acharnenses” 151, +others; κακὸς κακῶς ἀπόλοιθ᾽ ὅστις.. 4th c.BC: Eubulus Comicus 116; ἐξώλης ἀπόλοιθ᾽ ὅστις.. 4th-3rd c.BC: Menander Comicus 154]]; ἀπολλύμενος, opposed to σῳζόμενος, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Isocrates Orator 6.36, compare 1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus 2.469d: frequently in]]participle future, κάκιστ᾽ ἀπολούμενε o destined to a miserable end! i.e. o thou villain, scoundrel, knave! [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Plutus” 713, compare 456, “Ach.” 865, “Pax” 2; ὁ κάκιστ᾽ ἀνέμων ἀ. 2nd c.AD: Lucianus Sophista “DDeor.” 14.2.]]

__B.2
in NT, perish, in theol. sense, [NT.John.3.16, +others]; οἱ ἀπολλύμενοι, opposed to οἱ σῳζόμενοι, [NT.1Cor.1.18.]

__B.II
to be lost, ὕδωρ ἀπολέσκετ᾽ (of the water eluding Tantalus) [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 11.586]]; οὔποτε καρπὸς ἀπόλλυται never falls untimely,[LXX+8th c.BC+ [[prev. work] 7.117; ἀπό τέ σφισιν ὕπνος ὄλωλεν 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 10.186; γέλως ἐξ ἀνθρώπων ἀπόλωλεν 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Symposium” 1.15; ἀπολόμενον ἀργύριον 5th c.BC: Antipho Sophista 54; ἀπώλοντο οἱ ὄνοι LXX.1Ki.9.3.]]

LSJ / STEPBible (TFLSJ)
ἀπολύω
[see. λύω], future -λύσω, etc.: future passive

__A
ἀπολελύσομαι[Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 6.2.37]]:—loose from, ἱμάντα θοῶς ἀπέλυσε κορώνης[Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 21.46]]; ὄφρ᾽ ἀπὸ τοίχους λῦσε κλύδων τρόπιος the sides of the ship from the keel, [Refs [[prev. work] 12.420]]; undo, ἀπὸ κρήδεμνον ἔλυσεν[Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. work] 3.392; ἐπιδέσματα 5th c.BC: Hippocrates Medicus “περὶ ἀγμῶν” 25.]]

__A.2
set free, release, relieve from, ἀ. τινὰ τῆς φρουρῆς[Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 2.30; τῆς ἐπιμελείας 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 8.3.47; τῶν ἐκεῖ κακῶν 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 365a; τὴν ψυχὴν ἀπὸ τῆς τοῦ σώματος κοινωνίας [prev. author] “Phd.” 65a, compare 67a]]; ἀ. τῆς μετρήσεως save them from the trouble of measuring, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Politica” 1257a40]]:— passive, to be set free, τῶν δεινῶν, φόβου, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 1.70, 7.56, etc.]]

__A.2.b
frequently in legal sense, ἀ. τῆς αἰτίης acquit of the charge, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 9.88, 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 6.6.15]]; opposed to καταψηφίζω, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [3rd c.AD: Democritus Epigrammaticus 262; τῆς εὐθύνης 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Vespae” 571: with]]infinitive, ἀ. τινὰ μὴ φῶρα εἶναι acquit of being a thief, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 2.174; so ἀπολύεται μὴ ἀδικεῖν 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 1.95, compare 128]]: absolutely, acquit, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Vespae” 988, 1000, 5th c.BC: Lysias Orator 20.20, etc.]]

__A.II
in [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” always, ={ἀπολυτρόω}]], release on receipt of ransom, οὐδ᾽ ἀπέλυσε θύγατρα καὶ οὐκ ἀπεδέξατ᾽ ἄποινα[Refs [1.95; Ἕκτορ᾽ ἔχει.. οὐδ᾽ ἀπέλυσεν 24.115, +others]]:—middle, set free by payment of ransom, ransom, redeem, χαλκοῦ τε χρυσοῦ τ᾽ ἀπολυσόμεθ᾽ at a price of.., [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 22.50]] (but active in Prose, ἀπολύειν πολλῶν χρημάτων[Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Historia Graeca (Hellenica)” 4.8.21).]]

__A.II.2
let go, let alone, leave one, of an illness, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Hippocrates Medicus “Κωακαὶ προγνώσιες” 564.]]

__A.III
discharge, disband an army, ἀ. οἴκαδε[Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Historia Graeca (Hellenica)” 6.5.21]]; generally, dismiss, discharge, ἐμὲ.. ἀπέλυσ᾽ ἄδειπνον[Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Acharnenses” 1155, compare 2nd c.BC: Bion Bucolicus 1.96.]]

__A.III.2
divorce a wife, [NT+1st c.BC+ [NT.Matt.1.19, etc.; τὸν ἄνδρα 1st c.BC: Diodorus Siculus Historicus 12.18.]]

__A.III.3
do away with, remove, αἰσχύνην[Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 20.47]]:—passive, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Antipho Orator 2.1.5.]]

__A.III.4
discharge or pay a debt, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Cratylus” 417b]]; pay, ἀ. τὸν χαλκόν[Refs 1st c.BC+ [“PTeb.” 490 (1st c.BC)]]; pay off a mortgage, [Refs [“POxy.” 509.15.]]

__A.III.5
dismiss a charge, εἰσαγγελία ὑπὸ τοῦ κατηγόρου ἀπολελυμένη[Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Hyperides Orator “pro Euxenippo” 38.]]

__A.IV
ἀ. ἀνδράποδα Θρᾳξίν sell, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Antipho Orator 5.20]]; ἀ. οἰκίαν τινί sell a mortgaged house outright, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Isaeus Orator 6.33.]]

__A.V
deliver, τί τινι[Refs 3rd c.AD+ [“PFlor.” 123.2 (3rd c.AD):]] —passive [Refs 3rd c.AD+ [, [prev. work] 228.6 (3rd c.AD).]]

__A.VI
begin to count, [μοίρας] ἀπό.. Vett. Val. [Refs 4th c.AD+ [135: _absolutely_, [prev. author] 19.19, 4th c.AD: Paulus Alexandrinus Astrologus “Q.” 2.]]

__A.VII
intransitive, depart (cf. B.IV, C. 2), [Refs 2nd c.BC+ [2nd c.BC: Polybius Historicus 3.69.14, +others]]

__B
middle with aorist 2 ἀπελύμην (in passive sense), [Refs 3rd c.AD+ [3rd c.AD: Oppianus Apamensis Epicus “Cynegetica” 3.128]]:— redeem, see above [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus 11.]]

__B.II
ἀπολύεσθαι διαβολάς do away with, refute calumnies against one, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 8.87, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Apologia” 37b, +others: _absolutely_, 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Rhetorica” 1416b9.]]

__B.II.2
τὴν αἰτίαν, τὰς βλασφημίας, τὰ κατηγορημένα, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 5.75, 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 15.2, 18.4: with _genitive_, τῶν εἰς Ἀριστόβουλον -σασθαι 1st c.AD: Josephus Historicus “Antiquitates Judaicae” 15.3.5.]]

__B.II.2.b
refute, τοὺς ἐναντίους λόγους[Refs 5th c.AD+ [5th-6th c.AD: Damascius Philosophus “de Principiis” 126 ter: _absolutely_, ὁ δὲ ἀπολυόμενος ἔφη]]in defence, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 8.59.]]

__B.III
like active, acquit, τοῦ μὴ κακῶς ἔχειν ἀλλ᾽ ὀρθῶς[Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Leges” 637c.]]

__B.III.2
release from, τοὺς Ἕλληνας ἀ. δουλείας[Refs [[prev. author] “Mx.” 245a.]]

__B.IV
like passive (with [Refs [11),]]depart, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Antigone” 1314]]; also, put off, πνεῦμα ἀ.[Refs 1st c.BC+ [“Anthologia Graeca” 9.276 (1st c.BC-1st c.AD: Crinagoras Epigrammaticus); but πνεῦμα μελῶν ἀπέλυε “IG” 14.607e (from Carales).]]

__C
passive, to be released, ἐλπίζων τοὺς υἱέας τῆς στρατηΐης ἀπολελύσθαι from military service, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 4.84, compare 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 6.2.37]]; τῆς ἀρχῆς ἀπολυθῆναι βουλόμενοι to be freed from their rule, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 2.8; τῶν δεινῶν μηδέποτε οἴεσθαι ἀπολυθήσεσθαι [prev. author] 1.70; τῆς ὑποψίας 5th c.BC: Antipho Orator 2.4.3; τῆς μιαρίας [prev. work] 3.11]]: absolutely, to be acquitted, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 6.29]]; to be absolved from, τῶν ἀδικημάτων[Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Phaedo” 113d.]]

__C.II
of combatants, to be separated, part, οὐ ῥᾳδίως ἀπελύοντο[Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 1.49]]; generally, to be separated or detached, ἀλλήλων or ἀπ᾽ ἀλλήλων, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Metaphysica” 1031b3, “Ph.” 185a28; ἀ. τὰ ᾠὰ τῆς ὑστέρας [prev. author] “GA” 754b18, +others]]; ἀπολελυμένος, absolutely, detached, αἰδοῖον, γλῶττα, ὄρχεις, [Refs [[prev. author] “HA” 500b2, 533a27, 535b2]]; τὴν γλῶτταν ἀ. having its tongue detached, [Refs [[prev. author] “fragment” 319, +others]]; also, distinct, differentiated, [Refs [[prev. author] “HA” 497b22.]]

__C.II.2
depart, ἔθανες, ἀπελύθης, [LXX+5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Antigone” 1268 (Lyric poetry), compare 2nd c.BC: Polybius Historicus 6.58.4, +others, LXX.Num.20.29, +others; compare above 5th c.BC: Bacchylides Lyricus IV.]]

__C.III
of a child, to be brought forth, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Hippocrates Medicus “περὶ ἐπικυήσιος” 11, compare 24, 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “de Generatione Animalium” 745b11]]; of the mother, to be delivered, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Hippocrates Medicus “ἐπιδημίαι” 2.2.17.]]

__C.IV
to be annulled, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Ethica Nicomachea” 1156a22.]]

__C.V
ἀπολελυμένος, η, ον, absolute, especially in Grammars, [Refs 2nd c.BC+ [2nd c.BC: Dionysius Thrax Grammaticus 636.15, 2nd c.AD: Apollonius Dyscolus Grammaticus “de Syntaxi;” 97.20, +others]]: also, general, of meaning, [Refs 4th c.AD+ [4th c.AD(?): Olympiodorus Alchemista p.72B.]]

__C.VI
of metres, irregular, without strophic responsion, [Refs 7th c.AD+ [7th c.AD: Hephaestio Grammaticus “Poëm.” 5.]]

ἀπομάσσω,

prop., to fasten to; hence, of fire, to kindle, light: Luk.8:16 11:33 15:8, Act.28:2. Mid., with genitive, to fasten oneself to, cling to, lay hold of (so in π.; MM, see word): Mat.8:3, 15, Jhn.20:17, al.; of carnal intercourse, 1Co.7:1; with reference to levitical and ceremonial prohibitions, 2Co.6:17, Col.2:21; of hostile action, 1Jn.5:18 (cf. ἀν-, καθ-, περι- άπτω)
SYN.: θιγγάνω, ψηλαφάω. ἅ. is the stronger, θ., to touch, the lighter term. ψ. is to feel, as in search of something (Tr., Syn., § xvii; Lft., Col., 201 f.)  (AS)

with genitive, εἴ κέ μιν οὐδοῦ ἀπώσομεν[Refs 5th c.BC+ [22.76, compare 2.130; γῆς ἀπῶσαί [με] πατρίδος 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Tyrannus” 641]]:—middle, thrust from oneself, drive away, μνηστῆρας ἀπώσεαι ἐκ μεγάροιο[Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 1.270]]:—passive, to be expelled, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.173; ἀπωθοῦμαι δόμων 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Acharnenses” 450; γῆς 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Tyrannus” 670.]]

__4
thrust aside, spurn, [Refs [[prev. author] “Aj.” 446, +others]]:—passive, τὸν δῆμον πρότερον ἀπωσμένον pushed aside, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 5.69.]]

__5
repel, drive back, in middle, Τρῶας ἀπώσασθαι[Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 8.206; νεῖκος ἀπωσαμένους 12.276; ἀπώσασθαι κακὰ νηῶν 15.503; νηῶν μὲν ἀπωσάμενοι δήϊον πῦρ 16.301; πένθος 7th c.BC: Archilochus Lyricus 9.10; νοῦσον “Anthologia Graeca” 6.190 (1st c.AD: Gaetulicus, Cn. Lentulus Epigrammaticus)]]:— also in Prose, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Antipho Orator 4.4.6, etc.: with double _accusative_, τὴν ναυμαχίαν ἀπεωσάμεθα Κορινθίους 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 1.32.]]

__6
in middle, reject, τὸ ἀργύριον[Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.199; τὸν αὐλόν 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Trachiniae” 216(Lyric poetry); φιλότητα [prev. author] “Ph.” 1122(Lyric poetry); τὰς σπονδάς 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 5.22; τὰ ἐξ ἀδικίας κέρδη 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 366a]]; ἀ. πόνους decline them, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Fragmenta” 789]]; τὴν δουλοσύνην shake off slavery, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.95]]; ὕπνον shake off sleep, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 571c]]: absolutely, refuse, ποιήσω κοὐκ ἀπώσομαι[Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Trachiniae” 1249.]]

ἀρά, -ᾶς, ἡ
[in LXX chiefly for אָלָה ];

LSJ / STEPBible (TFLSJ)
ἀρά,
Ionic dialect ἀρή, ἡ, prayer, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 15.378, 598, 23.199, 8th-7th c.BC: Hesiodus Epicus “Opera et Dies” 726, 5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “I.” 6(5).43]]; ἀρὴν ἐποιήσαντο παῖδα γενέσθαι Ἀρίστωνι offered prayers that a child should be born, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 6.63.]]

__2
vow, [Refs [Inscription Cyprian dialect 83, 147H.]]

__3
curse, imprecation, ἐξ ἀρέων μητρὸς.. ἥ ῥα θεοῖσι πόλλ᾽ ἀχέουσ᾽ ἠρᾶτο[Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 9.566]]; frequently in Trag., mostly in plural, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Prometheus Vinctus” 910, 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Tyrannus” 295]]; ἀρὰς ἀρᾶσθαι,προστιθέναι, ἐξανιέναι, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Phoenissae” 67, 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Coloneus” 952, 154(Lyric poetry), 1375; ἐπεύχεσθαι 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Critias” 119e; θέσθαι ἐπί τινας 1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus “Camillus” 13]]: also in singular, πατρὸς δ᾽ ἀ. κρανθήσεται[Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Prometheus Vinctus” 910, compare “Ag.” 457 (Lyric poetry), etc.; ἡ τοῦ νόμου ἀ. 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Leges” 871b; ἀρᾷ.. ἔνοχος ἔστω [prev. work] 742b]], etc.: in plural, imprecations, frequently in Inscrr. on those who shall mutilate or remove them, [Refs 2nd c.BC+ [“Inscription Magn.” 105.53 (2nd c.BC), “IG” 3.1417ff]]

__II
Ἀρά personified as the goddess of destruction and revenge, ὦ πότνι᾽ Ἀρὰ σεμναί τε θεῶν παῖδες Ἐρινύες[Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “El.” III; δεινόπους Ἀρά [prev. author] “OT” 418; but in 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Eumenides” 417 the Erinyes say that Ἀραί]] is their own name γῆς ὑπα; Ἀρά τ᾽ Ἐρινὺς πατρὸς ἡ μεγασθενής[Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. author] “Th.” 70; Ἀρᾶς ἱερόν 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Fragmenta” 575. (Hence the Verb ἀράομαι.)]] [Epic dialect always ᾱρ, Attic dialect always ᾰρ.] (From ἀρϝᾱ, compare κάταρ ϝος.)
