deep_entry:
Abbott-Smith / STEPBible (TBESG)
ἄρα,
illative particle, expressing a more subjective or informal inference than οὖν,
then: prop. (as in cl.), the second word in the sentence, Rom.7:21 8:1, Gal.3:7; ἐπεὶ ἄρα, 1Co.7:14 (with another word between) 5:10; as the first word, Luk.11:48, Act.11:18, Rom.10:17, 1Co.15:18, 2Co.5:15 7:12, Heb.4:9; so prop. in apodosis after protasis with εἰ, Mat.12:28, Luk.11:20, Gal.2:21 3:29 5:11, Heb.12:8 (κενὸν ἄρα), 1Co.15:14; often in interrogations, direct and indirect, τίς (τί) ἄρα, Mat.18:1 19:25, 27 24:45, Mrk.4:41, Luk.1:66 8:25 12:42 22:23, Act.12:18; εἰ ἄρα, Mrk.11:13, Act.8:22; εἴπερ ἄρα, 1Co.15:15; οὐκ ἄρα, Act.21:38; μήτι ἄρα, 2Co.1:17; in strengthened forms, ἄρα γε, ἄραγε, Mat.7:20 17:26, Act.17:27, and more frequently ἄρα οὖν (Epp. Paul.), so then, Rom.5:18 7:3, 25 8:12 9:16, 18 14:19, Gal.6:10, Eph.2:19, 1Th.5:6, 2Th.2:15 (Bl., §77, 2; 78, 5; MM, see word).†
(AS)

---

LSJ / STEPBible (TFLSJ)
ἄρᾰ,
Epic dialect ῥά (which is enclitic and used after monosyllables, ἦ, ὅς, γάρ, etc., or words ending in a vowel or diphthong, e.g. ἐπεί), before a consonant ἄρ (perhaps cf. Lithuanian i[rtilde] 'and'): expressing consequence, then, or mere succession, there and then, and in many derived uses.

__A
EARLIER USAGE: to denote,

__A.I
immediate transition, there and then, straightway, ὣς φάτο βῆ δ᾽ ἄρ᾽ Ὄνειρος[Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 2.16]]: after a participle, ὣς εἰπὼν κατ᾽ ἄρ᾽ ἕζετο[Refs 5th c.BC+ [1.68, +others; πυθόμενος.. εἶπε ἄ. 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 4.134, compare 9.9; ἐρωτώσης τῆς μητρὸς ἀπεκρίνατο ἄρα 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 1.3.2; with other Particles, δέ, ἦ, ὡς, etc., compare ὁ δὲ Ἀστυάγης ἄ. εἶπεν [prev. work] 4.10: also after _adverbs_ of Time, τότε δή ῥα, τῆμος ἄρα, etc.]]; οὕτως ἄρα[Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Phaedrus” 259b]]; often in apodosi, as αὐτὰρ ἐπεὶ δὴ θηήσατο.. αὐτίκ᾽ ἄρ᾽ ἤλυθεν[Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 5.77; repeated τὼ μὲν ἄρ᾽.. κεῖντο ἡ δ᾽ ἄρ᾽.. ἀγόρευε 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 21.426]]: in enumerations, e. g. in Homer's catalogue, then, next, οἱ δ᾽ ἄρ᾽ Ἀθήνας εἶχον[Refs [2.546]]; so in genealogies, Σίσυφος.. ὁ δ᾽ ἄ. Γλαῦκον τέκεθ᾽ υἱόν[Refs [6.154.]]

__A.I.2
to draw attention, mark you! τὸν τρεῖς μὲν ἐπιρρήσσεσκον.. τῶν ἄλλων Ἀχιλεὺς δ᾽ ἄρ᾽ ἐπιρρήσσεσκε καὶ οἶος[Refs [24.456; with _imperative_, ἀλλ᾽ ἄγε δὴ κατ᾽ ἄρ᾽ ἕζευ 24.522]]: to point a moral or general statement, φευγόντων δ᾽ οὔτ᾽ ἂρ κλέος ὄρνυται οὔτε τις ἀλκή[Refs [5.532.]]

__A.II
connexion, such as,

__A.II.1
that of antecedent and consequent, οἰνοχόει.. ἄσβεστος δ᾽ ἄρ᾽ ἐνῶρτο γέλως[Refs [1.599, compare 24.507; τοὔνεκ᾽ ἄρ᾽ ἄλγε᾽ ἔδωκε 1.96; frequently with οὕνεκα in protasi, 7.140, +others]]: also in questions, τίς τ᾽ ἄρ τῶν ὄχ᾽ ἄριστος ἔη; who then (say you) was.. ? [Refs [2.761: with _demonstrative_ Pronoun in recapitulation, ἀλλ᾽ υἱὸν Πριάμοιο.. τόν ῥ᾽ Ὀδυσεὺς βάλε]]he it was, whom.., [Refs [4.501: frequently in such phrases as ὣς ἄρα φωνήσας 2.35, +others; ὣς ἄρ᾽ ἔφη 1.584, +others; ἦ ῥα 3.355, +others]], thus, then he spoke.—This usage is universal in Greek.

__A.II.2
explanation of that which precedes, χωόμενον κατὰ θυμὸν ἐϋζώνοιο γυναικὸς τήν ῥα.. ἀπηύρων whom (and for this cause he was angry) they had taken away, [Refs [1.429]]; εἰ μὴ ὑπερφίαλον ἔπος ἔκβαλε.. φῆ ῥ᾽ ἀέκητι θεῶν φυγέειν for he said, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 4.504: frequently with οὕνεκα]]; so with relatives, ἐκ δ᾽ ἔθορε κλῆρος ὃν ἄρ᾽ ἤθελον αὐτοί the very one which.., [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 7.182.]]

__B
LATER USAGE, always with inferential force: 1. in drawing conclusions (more subjective than οὖν), ἄριστον ἄ. ἡ εὐδαιμονία[Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Ethica Nicomachea” 1099a24; δῆλον ἄ. [prev. author] “Pol.” 1295b33; in pseudo-syllogistic conclusions, [prev. author] “SE” 174b11, “Rh.” 1401a3, +others]]: especially by way of informal inference, as it seems, οὐκ ἄ. σοί γε πατὴρ ἦν Πηλεύς[Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 16.33; οὐδ᾽ ἄ. πως ἦν ἐν πάντεσσ᾽ ἔργοισι δαήμονα φῶτα γενέσθαι 23.670; μάτην ἄρ᾽, ὡς ἔοικεν, ἥκομεν 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Electra” 772]]; οὕτω κοινόν τι ἄ. χαρᾷ καὶ λύπῃ δάκρυά ἐστιν so true is it that.., [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Historia Graeca (Hellenica)” 7.1.32; πολὺ γὰρ ἀμείνων ἄ. ὁ τοῦ ἀδίκου ἢ ὁ τοῦ δικαίου βίος 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 358c; ἦν ἄ. πυρός γ᾽ ἕτερα.. θερμότερα 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Equites” 382; ὦ τλῆμον ἀρετή, λόγος ἄρ᾽ ἦσθα “Tragica Adespota” 374]]; so in announcing the discovery or correction of an error, as οὐκ ἐννενοήκαμεν ὅτι εἰσὶν ἄ... [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 375d; φαίνεται πρὸ ποδῶν ἡμῖν κυλινδεῖσθαι καὶ οὐχ ἑωρῶμεν ἄρ᾽ αὐτό [prev. work] 432d]]; εἰκότως ἄ. οὐκ ἐγίγνετο· ὡς γὰρ ἐγὼ νῦν πυνθάνομαι.. [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 2.2.3.]]

__B.2
in questions, expressing the anxiety of the questioner, τίς ἄ. ῥύσετα; who is there to save ? [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Septem contra Thebas” 92]]; so in exclamations to heighten the expression of emotion, οἵαν ἄρ᾽ ἥβην.. ἀπώλεσεν what a band of youth was that.. ! [Refs [[prev. author] “Pers.” 733]]; so ὡς ἄρα[Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. work] 472, 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Fragmenta” 577; τί μ᾽ ἄ. τί μ᾽ ὀλέκει; [prev. author] “Ant.” 1285; τί οὖν.. ἄ. 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Oeconomicus” 6.2]]; πῶς ἄ.; οὕτως ἄ., etc.; ἄ. alone, ἔζης ἄ.[Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Fragmenta” 686]]: especially in ironical comments, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Aves” 476, 1371, etc.]]

__B.3
epexegetic, namely, ἐρῶ, ὡς ἄ... [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Theaetetus” 152d, compare 156e.]]

__B.4
for τοι ἄρα, τἄρα, see entry τοι [Refs [11.2.]]

__B.5
εἰ (or ἐάν) μὴ ἄ. unless perhaps, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Apologia” 38b, 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 58.4]]; separated from εἰ μή, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. author] 9.20; with irony, εἰ μὴ ἄ. ἡ τῆς ἀρετῆς ἐπιμέλεια διαφθορά ἐστιν 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Memorabilia” 1.2.8.]]

__B.6
in hypothetical clauses, to indicate the improbability of the supposition, ἢν ἄ. ποτὲ κατὰ γῆν βιασθῶσιν[Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 1.93, etc.]]; or simply, perhaps (sometimes separated from εἰ), εἴ τις οὖν ὑμῶν ἄ... ὑπελάμβανεν[Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 21.8; εἴ τις ἰδίᾳ τινὰ δεδιὼς ἄ. ἀπρόθυμός ἐστιν 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 4.86.]]

__C
IN CRASIS, frequently τἄρα, μεντἄρα, οὐτἄρα: also δήξομἄρα for δήξομαι ἄ., [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Acharnenses” 325]]; οἰμώξετἄρα, κλαύσἄρα, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. author] “Th.” 248, “Pax” 532: also in Trag., 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Hyps.fragment” 34.86.]]

__D
ἄρα never stands first in the sentence in Classical Greek [Refs 4th c.BC+ [(4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Mechanica” 851a22 is corrupt)]], but is found at the beginning of an apodosis in [NT.Matt.12.28, NT.Rom.10.17], and first in a sentence, [NT+2nd c.AD+ [NT.Luke.11.48, 2nd c.AD: Vettius Valens Astrologus 305.20]]; in conclusion of syllogism, [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd-3rd c.AD: Hermes Trismegistus cited in 5th c.AD: Stobaeus, Joannes 3.11.31.]]

Abbott-Smith / STEPBible (TBESG)
ἆρα,
interrog. particle,
implying anxiety or impatience, "quite rare and only in Luke and Paul, therefore a literary word" (Bl., §77, 2).
__1. (num igitur) expecting a neg. reply, Luk.18:8; ἆρά γε, Act.8:30.
__2. (ergone) in apodosis, expecting an affirm. reply, Gal.2:17 (Bl., l.with; Lft., Ga., in l.; MM, see word).
† (AS)

---

LSJ / STEPBible (TFLSJ)
ἆρᾰ,
interrogative Particle, implying anxiety or impatience, = Epic dialect and Lyric poetry ἦ ῥα:

__1
alone, it simply marks the question, the nature of which is determined by the context: e.g. in [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 35.44]] a negative answer is implied in the question ἆρ᾽ ἂν οἴεσθε..; but an affirmative in [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 4.6.4]] ἆ. βέβληκα δὶς ἐφεξῆ; compare ἆρ᾽ εὐτυχεῖς.. ἢ δυστυχεῖ; [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Phoenissae” 424.—To make it plainly _negative_, we have ἆ. μή..; 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Septem contra Thebas” 208, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Phaedo” 64c]]; and to make it plainly affirmative, ἆρ᾽ ο; ἆρ᾽ οὐχ; [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Coloneus” 791, “OT” 540]]; ἆρ᾽ οὐχ οὕτω; [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Philebus” 11d.]]

__2
ἆ. οὖ; is used to draw an affirmative inference, [Refs [[prev. author] “Grg.” 477a, “La.” 190b]]; also when a negative answer is expected, [Refs [[prev. author] “Chrm.” 159b]]; with a negative, ἆρ᾽ οὖν οὐ..; [Refs [[prev. author] “Phdr.” 263a, etc.]]

__3
in ἆρά γε, each Particle retains its force, γε serving to make the question more definite, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Plutus” 546, 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Memorabilia” 1.5.4, etc.]]

__4
less frequently with τίς interrogative, τίνος ποτ᾽ ἆρ᾽ ἔπραξε χειρί[Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Ajax” 905]]; τίδ᾽ ἆρ᾽ ἐγὼ σ; [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Iphigenia Aulidensis” 1228; τίς ἆρ᾽ ὁ φεύγω; 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Vespae” 893]]; with ἤν, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Rhesus” 118.]]

__5
in indirect questions, σκεψώμεθα τοῦτο ἆ... [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Phaedo” 70e, compare “R.” 526c, +others, 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Physica” 204b3, etc.]]

__II
in Poets sometimes like{ἄρα}, [Refs 7th c.BC+ [7th c.BC: Archilochus Lyricus 86, 89, 5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “P.” 4.78, 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Vespae” 3; τοιοῖσδε χρησμοῖς ἆ. χρὴ πεποιθένα; 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Choephori” 297, compare 435; τῷ δὲ ξιφήρης ἆρ᾽ ὑφειστήκει λόχος 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Andromache” 1114: in exclamations, βραδεῖαν ἡμᾶς ἆρ᾽ ὁ τήνδε τὴν ὁδὸν πέμπων ἔπεμψεν 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Ajax” 738; ὀδυνηρὸς ἆρ᾽ ὁ πλοῦτος 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Phoenissae” 566, compare “El.” 1229, “Hipp.” 1086; ἦ δεινὸν ἆρ᾽ ἦν [prev. author] “fragment” 931; ἔμελλόν σ᾽ ἆ. κινήσειν 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Nubes” 1301, compare “Ach.” 347.]]

__B
In Prose, ἆ. almost always stands first in the sentence, but[Refs 5th c.BC+ [compare 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Gorgias” 467e]]; καὶ ὑπὲρ τούτων ἆ... [Refs 4th c.AD+ [4th c.AD: Julianus Imperator “Orationes” 2.61c: in Poetry greater licence is taken, see above 1.4, 11.]]

ἀργέω,

ἀργός, -όν
(in late Gk., incl. NT, -ή, -όν; ἀ- neg., ἔργον) [in LXX: 3Ki.6:7 (מַסָּע), Wis.14:5 15:15, Sir.37:11 38:28 * ;]

LSJ / STEPBible (TFLSJ)
ἀργός, όν,

__B
later ή, όν [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Ethica Nicomachea” 1167a11, “Mete.” 352a13, 4th-3rd c.BC: Theophrastus Philosophus “de Lapidibus” 27, 2nd c.BC: Athenaeus Mechanicus 12.11, etc.: (_contraction_ from ἀεργός)]]:—properly not working the ground, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 5.6]]; idle, lazy, opposed to ἐργάτις, [Refs 6th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Philoctetes” 97, compare 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Nubes” 53, etc.; γαστέρες ἀ. 6th c.BC: Epimenides Philosophus 1; ἀ. ἐπιθυμίαι 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 572e]]; ἀ. τὴν διάνοιαν[Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. work] 458a; τὸ πρὸς ἅπαν ξυνετὸν ἐπὶ πᾶν ἀ. 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 3.82]]; ἂν ἀ. ᾖ if he have no trade, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Antiphanes Comicus 123.3; πότερον ἀνθρώπου οὐδέν ἐστιν [ἔργον] ἀλλ᾽ ἀργὸν πέφυκε; 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Ethica Nicomachea” 1097b30]]: with genitive of things, idle at a thing, free from it, τῶν οἴκοθεν from domestic toils, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Iphigenia Aulidensis” 1000; πόνων σφοδρῶν 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Leges” 835d; γυναῖκας ἀργοὺς ταλασίας [prev. work] 806a]]; ἀ. αἰσχρῶν slow to evil, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Septem contra Thebas” 411; ἀργότεραι ἐς τὸ δρᾶν τι 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 7.67; ἀ. περί τι 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Leges” 966d.]]

__B.2
of things, δόρυ[Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Phoenissae” 1387]]; of money, lying idle, yielding no return, opposed to ἐνεργός, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 27.7]] and 20; of land, lying fallow, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Isocrates Orator 4.132, 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 3.2.19, 4th-3rd c.BC: Theophrastus Philosophus “Historia Plantarum” 9.12.2]]; opposed to πεφυτευμένος, [Refs 3rd c.AD+ [“IG” 7.2226 B (Thisbe, 3rd c.AD)]]; διατριβὴ ἀ. in which nothing is done, fruitless, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Ranae” 1498 (Lyric poetry), 5th-6th c.BC: Isocrates Orator 4.44; χρόνον ἀργὸν διάγειν 1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus “Coriolanus” 31]]. adverb ἀργῶς, ἐπιμέλεσθαι[Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Memorabilia” 2.4.7; ἔχειν 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 6.3: _comparative_ and _superlative_ ἀργότερον, -ότατα, 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Oeconomicus” 15.6 and 1.]]

__B.2.b
ἀ. λόγος, name of a sophism, [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [3rd c.BC: Chrysippus Stoicus 2.277, compare 1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus 2.574e.]]

__B.II
passive,unwrought, ἁρμός, κυμάτιον, [Refs [“IG” 1.322b23,59; πυροὶ ἀ.]]unprepared for eating, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Hippocrates Medicus “περὶ ἀρχαίης ἰητρικῇς” 13; ἄργυρος 2nd c.AD: Pausanias Periegeta 3.12.3]]; βύρσαι undressed hides, [Refs 2nd c.BC+ [2nd c.BC: Athenaeus Mechanicus [same place]]]; unpolished, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-3rd c.BC: Theophrastus Philosophus “de Lapidibus” 27.]]

__B.II.2
not done, left undone, κοὐκ ἦν ἔτ᾽ οὐδὲν ἀ.[Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Coloneus” 1605; ἓν δ᾽ ἐστὶν ἡμῖν ἀ. 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Phoenissae” 766]]; οὐκ ἐν ἀργοῖς not among things neglected, [Refs 6th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Tyrannus” 287; τὰ μὲν προβέβηκεν ἀμήχανόν ἐστι γενέσθαι ἀργά 6th c.BC: Theognis Elegiacus 584.]]

__B.II.3
unattempted, μάχη[Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Euthydemus” 272a.]]

__B.II.4
Astrology texts, τόπος ἀ., name of the [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [8th of the 12 'houses', 2nd c.AD: Ptolemaeus Mathematicus “Tetrabiblos” 128, 4th c.AD: Paulus Alexandrinus Astrologus “M.” 4; πλανήτης 3rd c.AD: Plotinus Philosophus 2.3.3; ζῴδιον 2nd c.AD: Sextus Empiricus Philosophus “adversus Mathematicos” 5.15.]]

also α, ον [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Hercules Furens” 413 (Lyric poetry)]]; Ionic dialect Ἀρήϊος, η, ο; Aeolic dialect Ἀρεύϊος [Refs 7th c.BC+ [7th-6th c.BC: Alcaeus Lyricus “Supp.” 1a.10]]: (Ἄρης):— devoted to Ares, warlike, martial; in [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Homerus Epicus]], mostly of warriors, Μενέλαος Ἀρήιος[Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 3.339, +others; Ἀρήϊοι υἷες Ἀχαιῶν 11.800, +others]]; of arms, Ἀρήϊα τεύχεα δύω[Refs [6.340, compare 10.407]]; the Attic dialect form only in the phrase τεῖχος Ἄρειον[Refs 5th c.BC+ [4.407, +others; also in 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus, ἀρήιοι ἀγῶνες]] conflicts in real war, opposed to γυμνικοί,[Refs [9.33; ὅπλον ἀ. 4.23]]; of a man, as substantive, warrior,[Refs 6th c.BC+ [6.98; Ἀθηνᾶ Ἀρεία “OGI” 229.70 (from Smyrna), compare “IG” 12(5).913 (from Tenos): _comparative_ ἀρειότερος (which see) 6th c.BC: Theognis Elegiacus 548 is probably to be read instead of med from ἀρείων, as χερειότερος from χερείων.]]

__3

__4
Ἄρειον, τό, ={ξιφίον}, Ps.-[Refs 1st c.AD+ [1st c.AD: Dioscorides (Dioscurides) Medicus 4.20]]; ={ἰσάτις}, [Refs [[prev. author] 2.184.]]

LSJ / STEPBible (TFLSJ)
ἀρέσκω [ᾰ],
imperfect ἤρεσκον[Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 5.37, etc.]]: future ἀρέσω[Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 39.33, _Epic dialect_ ἀρέσσω]] (συν-) [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [3rd c.BC: Apollonius Rhodius Epicus 3.901]]: aorist ἤρεσα[Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 8.19, “Comica Adespota” 19.4 D]]., etc., Epic dialect ἄρεσσα[Refs 3rd c.BC+ [3rd c.BC: Apollonius Rhodius Epicus 3.301]], infinitive ἀρέσαι[Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad”, 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus]]: perfect ἀρήρεκα[Refs 1st c.AD+ [1st c.AD: Cornutus Philosophus “de Natura Deorum” 24, 2nd c.AD: Sextus Empiricus Philosophus “adversus Mathematicos” 1.238]]:—middle, future ἀρέσομαι[Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Supplices” 655 (Lyric poetry)]], Epic dialect ἀρέσσομαι[Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 4.362:]]aorist ἠρεσάμην, Epic dialect ἀρ-[Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th-7th c.BC: Hesiodus Epicus “Scutum Herculis” 255]], Epic dialect participle ἀρεσσάμενος[Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 9.112, 6th c.BC: Theognis Elegiacus 762]]: aorist passive in middle sense, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Antigone” 500]]:—passive, aorist ἠρέσθην[Refs 1st c.AD+ [2nd c.AD: Pausanias Periegeta 2.13.8, 1st c.AD: Josephus Historicus “Antiquitates Judaicae” 12.9.6.]]

__I
of person only, make good, make amends, ἂψ ἐθέλω ἀρέσαι[Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 9.120]]:—middle, ταῦτα δ᾽ ὄπισθεν ἀρεσσόμεθ᾽ εἴ τι κακὸν νῦν εἴρηται[Refs 8th c.BC+ [4.362, compare 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 22.55, 4th c.AD(?): Quintus Smyrnaeus Epicus 4.377, 9.510]]; σπονδὰς θεοῖς ἀρέσασθαι make full drink-offerings to the gods, [Refs 6th c.BC+ [6th c.BC: Theognis Elegiacus [prev. cited]]]

__I.2
in [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Homerus Epicus]] also frequently in middle, with accusative person et dative modi, appease, conciliate, αὐτὸν ἀρεσσάσθω ἐπέεσσι καὶ δώρῳ[Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 8.396]]; τὸν ξεῖνον ἀρέσσομαι ὡς σὺ κελεύεις[Refs 8th c.BC+ [[prev. work] 402; ὥς κέν μιν ἀρεσσάμενοι πεπίθωμεν δώροισι 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 9.112, compare 19.179; καθαροῖσι βωμοῖς θεοὺς ἀρέσονται 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Supplices” 655; καί σε φίλως θυέεσσιν ἀρέσσατο 3rd c.BC: Maiistas Epicus 11]]: with genitive _of things_, ἀρέσαντο φρένας αἵματος they sated their heart with blood, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th-7th c.BC: Hesiodus Epicus “Scutum Herculis” 255.]]

__I.3
after [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Homerus Epicus]], with dative person, please, satisfy, οὔτε γάρ μοι Πολυκράτης ἤρεσκε δεσπόζων.. [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 3.142; δεῖ μ᾽ ἀρέσκειν τοῖς κάτω 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Antigone” 75, compare 89]]; ἀεὶ δ᾽ ἀρέσκειν τοῖς κρατοῦσιν to be obsequious to them, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Fragmenta” 93, compare 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Memorabilia” 2.2.11]]; ἀ. τρόποις τινός conform to his ways, [NT+4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 61.19; τὸ κολακεύειν νῦν ἀρέσκειν ὄνομ᾽ ἔχει 4th c.BC: Anaxandrides Comicus 42; πᾶσιν ἀρέσκω NT.1Cor.10.33; ἑαυτοῖς NT.Rom.15.1]]:—middle, μάλιστα ἠρέσκοντό [οἱ] οἱ ἀπ᾽ Ἀθηνέων pleased him most, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 6.128.]]

__II
of things, with dative person, please, εἴ τοι ἀρέσκει τὰ ἐγὼ λέγω[Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.89; κάρτα οἱ ἤρεσε ἡ ὑποθήκη [prev. author] 8.58, compare 3.40, 6.22; τῷ τοῦτ᾽ ἤρεσε; 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Electra” 409; σοὶ ταῦτ᾽ ἀρέσκει [prev. author] “Ant.” 211, etc.]]; τοῖς.. πρέσβεσιν ἤρεσκεν [the proposal] pleased them, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 5.37, compare 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Theaetetus” 157d, +others: also in]]aorist passive, μηδ᾽ ἀρεσθείη ποτέ (i.e. μηδὲν τῶν σῶν λόγων) [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Antigone” 500.]]

__III
with accusative person, οὐ γάρ μ᾽ ἀρέσκει γλῶσσά σου τεθηγμένη[Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. author] “Aj.” 584; οὐδέ σ᾽ ἀρέσκει τὸ παρόν 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Hippolytus” 185 (Lyric poetry), compare “Or.” 210; τουτὶ.. μ᾽ οὐκ ἀ. 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Plutus” 353, compare “Ach.” 189, “Ra.” 103, 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 1.128; πότερός σε ὁ τρόπος ἀ.; 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Cratylus” 433e, compare 391c, “R.” 557b, “Tht.” 172d]]: hence in passive, to be pleased, satisfied, οὐκ ἠρέσκετο λειπομένου Μαρδονίου ὑπὸ βασιλέος[Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 9.66]]; τῇ κρίσι with the decision, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. author] 3.34; διαίτῃ Σκυθικῇ [prev. author] 4.78; τοῖς λόγοις 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 1.129, compare 2.68; τῇ σῇ συνουσίᾳ 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Theages” 127b]]; later in aorist, ἠρέσθη τῇ γνώμῃ[Refs 1st c.AD+ [1st c.AD: Josephus Historicus [same place], +others; ἀρεσθεὶς τῷ πώματι 2nd c.AD: Pausanias Periegeta [prev. cited]]]

__IV
ἀρέσκει is used impersonal to express the opinion or resolution of a public body, ταῦτα ἤρεσέ σφι ποιέειν[Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 8.19; ἢν δ᾽ ἀρέσκῃ ταῦτ᾽ Ἀθηναίοις 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Equites” 1311]]; ἀρέσκει.. εἶναι Δελφῶν it is resolved that.., [Refs [“SIG” 827 D 10]]; also of prevailing opinions, ἀρέσκει περὶ τρίψεως παραγγέλλοντας.. writers on massage lay down the rule that.., [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd c.AD: Galenus Medicus 6.96]]; τὰ ἀρέσκοντα the dogmas of philosophers, [Refs 1st c.AD+ [1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus 2.448a, 1006d, etc.]]:—middle, ἐξεῖναι παρ᾽ ὁποτέρους ἂν ἀρέσκηται ἐλθεῖν[Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 1.35.]]

__V
participle ἀρέσκων, ουσα, ον, grateful, acceptable, ὅσοις τάδ᾽ ἔστ᾽ ἀρέσκονθ᾽[Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Tyrannus” 274; μηδὲν ἀρέσκον λέγειν 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 3.34; ἀρέσκοντας ὑμῖν λόγους 5th-6th c.BC: Isocrates Orator 8.5.]]

__V.2
of persons, acceptable, τὸν ἀρέσκοντα αὑτῷ προσλαμβάνειν[Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Leges” 951e; τῇ πόλει ἀ. 5th c.BC: Lysias Orator 19.13. (Cognate with ἀραρίσκω.)]]

ἀρετή, -ῆς, ἡ
[in LXX, in sing.: Hab.3:3, Zec.6:13 (הוֹד), in pl.: Isa.42:8, 12 43:21 63:7 (תְּהִלָּה), Wis.4:1 5:13 8:7 2:1-24; 4Mac.2.2 * ;]
prop., whatever procures pre-eminent estimation for a person or thing, in Hom. any kind of conspicuous advantage. Later confined by philos. writers to intrinsic eminence-moral goodness, virtue;
__(a) of God: 2Pe.1:3;
__(b) of men: Php.4:8, 2Pe.1:5; pl. (Isa, Es, ll. with), excellencies: 1Pe.2:9 (the usage appears to be a survival of an early comprehensive sense in which the original idea is blended with the impression which it makes on others, i.e. praise, renown; see Hort, 1 Pe., 129. Deiss., BS, 95 f., thinks it means manifestations of divine power, as in current Gk. speech; cf. also MM, see word)†
(AS)

---

ἀρετή [ᾰ], ἡ,
goodness, excellence, of any kind, in [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Homerus Epicus]] especially of manly qualities, ποδῶν ἀρετὴν ἀναφαίνων[Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 20.411; ἀμείνων παντοίας ἀρετὰς ἠμὲν πόδας ἠδὲ μάχεσθαι καὶ νόον 15.642]]; so of the gods, τῶν περ καὶ μείζων ἀ. τιμή τε βίη τε[Refs [9.498]]; also of women, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 2.206]]; ἀ. εἵνεκα for valour, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 8.92: _plural_, ἀ. ἀπεδείκνυντο]] displayed brave deeds, [Refs [[prev. author] 1.176, 9.40.]]

__b
later, of the gods, chiefly in plural, glorious deeds, wonders, miracles, [NT+1st c.BC+ [“SIG” 1172, 1st c.BC-1st c.AD: Strabo Geographus 17.1.17; ζῶσαι ἀ. “IG” 14.966, cf. NT.1Pet.2.9]]: also in singular, ὄψιν ἰδοῦσα ἀρετὴν τῆς θεοῦ[Refs 3rd c.BC+ [“IG” 2.1426 b, compare 3rd c.BC: Isyllus Lyricus 62, “BSA” 21.169,180.]]

__2
generally, excellence, ἡ ἀ. τελείωσίς τις[Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Metaphysica” 1021b20, compare “EN” 1106a15, etc.]]; of persons, ἄνδρα πὺξ ἀρετὰν εὑρόντα[Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “O.” 7.89, compare “P.” 4.187, 5th c.BC: Bacchylides Lyricus 9.13, etc.; τὸ φρονεῖν ἀ. μεγίστη 1st c.AD(?): Heraclitus 112]]: in plural, forms of excellence, μυρίαι ἀνδρῶν ἀ.[Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Bacchylides Lyricus 13.8, compare 5th c.BC: Gorgias Rhetor et Sophista “fragment” 8, etc.; δικαστοῦ αὕτη ἀ. 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Apologia” 18a]]; especially moral virtue, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [3rd c.AD: Democritus Epigrammaticus 179, 263, +others, 5th c.BC: Gorgias Rhetor et Sophista “fragment” 6]]; opposed to κακία, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Memorabilia” 2.1.21, compare 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 500d, “Lg.” 963a, 963cf, 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 60.17, 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Ethica Nicomachea” 1102a6, “Pol.” 1295a37, etc.]]; good nature, kindness, etc., [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Fragmenta” 163.]]

__2.b
of animals, things, as land, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 4.198, 7.5, 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 1.2]]; ἡ ἐν ἀρετῇ κειμένη γῆ productive land, [Refs 2nd c.BC+ [“PTeb.” 5.165 (2nd c.BC)]]; ἵππου[Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 3.88]]; κυνῶν, ἵππων, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 335b; σκεύους [prev. work] 601d]]; [ἀστακοῦ] [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Archestratus Epicus “fragment” 24; ἀ. βίου 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 618c; πολιτείας “Lg.” 886b, etc.]]

__3
prosperity, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 13.45.]]

__II
ἀ. εἴς τινα active merit, good service done him, ἐς τοὺς Ἕλληνας[Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 3.58, compare 2.40; ἀ. περί τινα 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 1.4.8; ἀνταποδοῦναι ἀ. 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 4.19; ἀρετὰς παρασχέσθαι ὑπέρ τινος 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 19.312]]; ἀρετῆς ἕνεκα, frequently in honorary Inscrr., [Refs [“IG” 22.107.14, etc.]]

__III
reward of excellence, distinction, fame, πλούτῳ δ᾽ ἀρετὴ καὶ κῦδος ὀπηδεῖ[Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th-7th c.BC: Hesiodus Epicus “Opera et Dies” 313, compare 7th-6th c.BC: Sappho Lyrica 80, 5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “N.” 5.53, +others; ἀθάνατος ἀ. 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Philoctetes” 1420, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Symposium” 208d; ἃ ἆθλα τοῦ πολέμου τοῖς ἀνδράσιν ἐστίν, ἐλευθερία καὶ ἀ. 4th c.BC: Lycurgus Orator 49]]; of God, δόξα καὶ ἀ.[NT.2Pet.1.3]: in plural, glories, [LXX+6th c.BC+ [6th c.BC: Theognis Elegiacus 30, 5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “N.” 10.2, +others; πλοῦτος ἀρεταῖς δεδαιδαλμένος [prev. author] “O.” 2.53; γενναίων ἀ. πόνων 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Hercules Furens” 357 (Lyric poetry), compare 5th c.BC: Lysias Orator 2.26; προγόνων ἀ. 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 618b; in LXX]] frequently of the praises of God, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Isaeus Orator 42.8, +others]]

__IV
Ἀρετή personified, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Prodicus Philosophus 1, 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Fragmenta” 675, 3rd c.BC(?): Callixinus Historicus 2, “CIG” “Corpus Inscriptionum Graecarum” “Corpus Inscriptionum Graecarum” 2786, “SIG” 985.10, etc.]]

__V
ἡ ἀ. σου as a title, Your worship, [Refs [PLips. 13 ii 20, etc.]]

__VI
an engine of war, [Refs 2nd c.BC+ [2nd c.BC: Athenaeus Mechanicus 38.11.]]

__VII
a plaster, [Refs 1st c.AD+ [1st c.AD: Andromachus Poeta Medicus cited in 2nd c.AD: Galenus Medicus 13.531.]]

ἀρήν

ἀριθμ-έω [ᾰ],
imperfect ἠρίθμεον as trisyllable, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 10.204]], 3rd.pers.singular ἠρίθμει[Refs [13.218]]:—middle, aorist ἠριθμησάμην[Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Phaedrus” 270d]]:—passive, future middle in passive sense ἀριθμήσομαι[Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Bacchae” 1318]]; future ἀριθμηθήσομαι[LXX+2nd c.AD+ [LXX.3Ki.3.8, 2nd c.AD: Galenus Medicus 10.68: _Epic dialect_]]aorist infinitive ἀριθμηθήμεναι (for -ῆναι) [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 2.124]]:—number, count, reckon up, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 4.411, 5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “N.” 10.46, etc.]]; αὐτὰρ ἐγὼ δίχα πάντας.. ἑταίρους ἠρίθμεον counted them so as to halve them, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 10.204]]; ἀριθμήσαντες after numbering the army, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 7.60]]; οὐδεὶς πώποτ᾽.. ἠρίθμησε stopped to count the enemy, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Equites” 570: poetry, ἀριθμήσεις γαῖαν ἀπειρεσίην, ={μετρήσεις}, “Anthologia Graeca” 11.349 (6th c.AD: Palladas Epigrammaticus)]]:—passive, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 6.111, 9.32:]] —middle, ἠριθμοῦντο counted each for himself, πλίνθους[Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 3.20.]]

__2
count out, pay, χρυσίον, ἀργύριον, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Symposium” 4.44, 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 49.30, “IG” 5(1).1390.51 (from Andania), “Mon.Anc.Gr.” 7.22.]]

__3
reckon, account, ἐν εὐεργεσίας μέρει[Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 21.166; ἀ. τινὰ κλυτόπαιδα “Anthologia Graeca” 9.262 (1st c.AD: Philippus Epigrammaticus); κέρδος τι ἀ. 1st-2nd c.AD: Dio Chrysostomus Sophista 31.158]]:—passive, to be reckoned, ἐν τοῖσι γενναίοισιν[Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Helena” 729; ἐν γράμμασι 2nd c.AD: Lucianus Sophista “Jud.Voc.” 2; εἴς τινας 2nd c.AD: Herodianus Grammaticus 1.1.1]]; ἀριθμεῖσθαι τῶν φιλτάτων as one of.., [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Bacchae” 1318; μακάρων 3rd c.BC: Theocritus Poeta Bucolicus 13.72. [-ῐθμ- 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Vespae” 333, “Comica Adespota” 21.28 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator]]]

LSJ / STEPBible (TFLSJ)
ἀριθμός [ᾰ],
(ἁρ-[Refs [“IG” 1.164)]], ὁ, number, first in [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey”, λέκτο δ᾽ ἀριθμόν 4.451; ἀριθμῷ παῦρα 7th-6th c.BC(?): Semonides Iambographus 3; ἓν ἀριθμῷ 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 3.6; ἀριθμὸν ἕξ [prev. author] 1.14, compare 50; ἐς τὸν ἀ. τρισχίλια [prev. author] 7.97]]; πλῆθος ἐς ἀ. the amount in point of number,[Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. work] 60; τὸν ἀ. δώδεκα 3rd c.BC: Euphro Comicus 11.11; δύο τινὲς ἢ τρεῖς.. εἰς τὸν ἀ. 4th-3rd c.BC: Menander Comicus 165; ἔλαττον μήτε ὄγκῳ μήτε ἀριθμῷ 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Theaetetus” 155a; οὔτ᾽ ἀριθμοῖς οὔτε μεγέθεσιν ἐλάττους [prev. author] “Lg.” 861e; σταθμῷ καὶ ἀ. 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Symposium” 4.45; δι᾽ ἀ. καὶ μέτρου 1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus “Pericles” 16, compare 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Troades” 620: proverbial, λέγειν ποντιᾶν ψάφων ἀριθμόν]] 'count the pebbles on the shore', [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “O.” 13.46, compare 2.98]]; οὐ γιγνώσκων ψήφων ἀριθμούς, of a blockhead, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Ephippus Comicus 19; οὔτ᾽ ἀριθμὸν οὔτ᾽ ἔλεγχον.. ἔχων 4th c.BC: Dionysius Comicus 3.13.]]

__2
amount, sum, πολὺς ἀ. χρόνου[Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aeschines Orator 1.78; ἀ. τῆς ὁδοῦ 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 2.2.6]]; ἀ. [χρυσίου] a sum of money, [Refs [[prev. author] “Cyr.” 8.2.16.]]

__3
ἀριθμῷ, absolutely, in certain numbers, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 6.58; but δένδρα ἀριθμῷ ὑμέτερα]]by tale, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 2.72; ἀ. διδόναι 4th c.BC: Dionysius Comicus 3.6.]]

__4
item or term in a series, ὁ δεύτερος ἀ.[Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Ion” 1014; τρίτον ὠδίνων ἀ. “epigram Gr.” 574; ναῦς πολλοὺς ἀ. ἄγνυται ναυαγίων 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Helena” 410, compare 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Poetica” 1461b24]]; τοὺς ἀ. τοῦ σώματος points of the body, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Leges” 668d; τοὺς ἀ. ἑκάστου τῶν νοσημάτων 5th c.BC: Hippocrates Medicus “περὶ διαίτης ὀξέων” 3; τὸ καλὸν ἐκ πολλῶν ἀ. ἐπιτελεῖσθαι 1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus 2.45c]]: hence as a mark of completeness, πάντας τοὺς ἀ. περιλαβών[Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Isocrates Orator 11.16]]; τοῦ καθήκοντος τοὺς ἀριθμούς the sum total of duty, [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd c.AD: Marcus Antoninus Imperator 3.1.]]

__5
number, account, as a mark of station, worth, rank, μετ᾽ ἀνδρῶν ἵζει ἀριθμῷ takes his place among men, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 11.449; εἰς ἀνδρῶν μὲν οὐ τελοῦσιν ἀ. 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Fragmenta” 492; εἰς ἀ. τῶν κακῶν πεφύκαμεν [prev. author] “Hec.” 1186]]; ξενίας ἀριθμῷ πρῶτ᾽ ἔχειν ἐμῶν φίλων in regard of friendship, [Refs [[prev. work] 794]]; δειλοὶ γὰρ ἄνδρες οὐκ ἔχουσιν ἐν μάχῃ ἀριθμόν have no account made of them, [Refs [[prev. author] “fragment” 519]]; οὐδ᾽ εἰς ἀ. ἥκει λόγων she comes not into my account, [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [[prev. author] “El.” 1054; ἀ. οὐδεὶς οὐδὲ λόγος ἐστί τινος 1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus 2.682f, compare 3rd c.BC: Callimachus Epicus “Epigrammata” 27.6, Oracle texts cited in Scholia 3rd c.BC: Theocritus Poeta Bucolicus 14.48.]]

__6
mere number, quantity, opposed to quality, ταῦτ᾽ οὐκ ἀ. ἐστιν, ὦ πάτερ, λόγων a mere set of words, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Coloneus” 382]]; of men, οὐκ ἀ. ἄλλως not a mere lot, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Troades” 476; ἀριθμός, πρόβατ᾽ ἄλλως 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Nubes” 1203]]; sometimes even of a single man, οὐκ ἀριθμὸν ἀλλ᾽ ἐτητύμως ἄνδρ᾽ ὄντα not a mere unit, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Heraclidae” 997]]; also ἀριθμὸν πληροῦν to be a mere cipher, [Refs 6th c.AD+ [6th c.AD: Choricius Rhetor “Milt.” 66.]]

__II
numbering, counting, μάσσων ἀριθμοῦ past counting, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “N.” 2.23]]; especially in phrases, ἀ. ποιεῖσθαι τῶν νεῶν to hold a muster of.., [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 8.7; ποιεῖν 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 7.1.7, etc.; παρεῖναι εἰς τὸν ἀ. [prev. work]II; εἴ τι δυνατὸν ἐς ἀ. ἐλθεῖν]] can be stated in numbers, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 2.72.]]

__III
the science of numbers, arithmetic, ἀριθμόν, ἔξοχον σοφισμάτων[Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Prometheus Vinctus” 459; ἀριθμῶν καὶ μέτρων εὑρήματα 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Fragmenta” 432; ἀ. καὶ λογισμὸν εὑρεῖν 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Phaedrus” 274c, compare “R.” 522c: proverbial, εἴπερ γὰρ ἀριθμὸν οἶδα 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Fragmenta” 360.19.]]

__IV
in Philos., abstract number, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Categoriae” 4b23, “Metaphorical” 990a19, +others; ἀ. μαθηματικός [prev. work] 1090b35]]; ἀ. οὐσιώδης, opposed to τοῦ ποσοῦ, [Refs 3rd c.AD+ [3rd c.AD: Plotinus Philosophus 5.5.4]]; ἀ. ἑνιαῖος, οὐσιώδης, ἑτεροῖος, [Refs 5th c.AD+ [5th-6th c.AD: Damascius Philosophus “de Principiis” 228.]]

__V
Grammars, number, [Refs 2nd c.BC+ [Stoic. 3.214, 2nd c.BC: Dionysius Thrax Grammaticus 634.16, 2nd c.AD: Apollonius Dyscolus Grammaticus “de Syntaxi;” 32.2, +others]]; compare ἑνικός, δυικός, πληθυντικός.

__VI
numeral, [Refs [[prev. work] 36.6]], etc.; ὁ τέσσαρα ἀ.[Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd c.AD: Sextus Empiricus Philosophus “adversus Mathematicos” 7.96]]; παιδὸς ἀ., ={δεκάτη}, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Electra” 1132.]]

__VII
unknown quantity (x), defined as πλῆθος μονάδων ἀορίστων, [Refs 3rd c.AD+ [3rd c.AD: Diophantus Mathematicus “Def.” 2.]]

__VIII
Rhet., rhythm in Prose, in plural, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [1st c.BC: Dionysius Halicarnassensis “de Compositione Verborum” 23, “Dem.” 52, compare 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Rhetorica” 1408b29; but also ἀριθμοὶ τῶν ἀρχαίων ποιητᾶν “SIG” 703.7 (Delph.).]]

__IX
line of a book, [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd c.AD: Apollonius Biographus Cit. 2.]]

__X
sum of numerical values of letters in a name, [NT.Rev.13.17, +others]; φιλῶ ἧς ἀριθμὸς φμέ Pompeian Inscription in [Refs [“Rend.Linc.” 10(1901).257.]]

__XI
unit of troops, = Latin numerus, [Refs 6th c.AD+ [“CIG” “Corpus Inscriptionum Graecarum” “Corpus Inscriptionum Graecarum” 5187 (6th c.AD), “BGU” 673 (6th c.AD), etc.]]; = legio, [Refs 4th c.AD+ [4th c.AD: Julianus Imperator]]ad Ath.280d, [Refs 1st c.BC+ [1st c.BC: Zosimus Epigrammaticus 5.26, “PLond.” 5.1711.69 (6th c.AD).]]

__XII
Astrology texts, mostly in plural, degrees traversed in a given time, [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd c.AD: Ptolemaeus Mathematicus “Tetrabiblos” 112, 2nd c.AD: Dorotheus Astrologus in “Catalogus Codicum Astrologorum” 6.107.30]]; τοῖς ἰδίοις ἀ. at her normal speed, of the moon, [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd c.AD: Galenus Medicus 19.531]]; also of degrees of latitude, [Refs 4th c.AD+ [4th c.AD: Hephaestio Astrologus 2.8, 3.1.]]

__XIII
in Medicine texts, in plural, precise conditions, παρόντων τῶν πρὸς τὴν φλεβοτομίαν ἀριθμῶν Herod.middle in [Refs 5th c.BC+ [“Rh.Mus.” 58.71, compare 2nd c.AD: Aretaeus Medicus “ὀξέων νούσων θεραπευτικόν” 2.3, probably in 1st c.AD: Herodotus Medicus cited in 6th c.AD: Aëtius Medicus 9.2; compare above 1.4. [ῐ 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Electra” 1132, 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Nubes” 1203.] (ἀρῐ-θμός from root ἀρι-, compare ἐπάριτος (which see), νήριτος.)]]

chariot and horses, yoked chariot, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 2.384, etc.; ἅ. τέθριππον 5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “I.” 1.14]]; ἅ. τετράορον, τέτρωρον, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. author] “P.” 10.65, 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Alcestis” 483: _metaphorically_, τρίπωλον ἅ. δαιμόνων]] of three goddesses, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Andromache” 277 (Lyric poetry).]]

__3
team, chariot-horses, ἅρμασιν ἐνδίδωσι κέντρον[Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. author] “HF” 881 (Lyric poetry); ἅρματα.. φυσῶντα καὶ πνέοντα 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Pax” 902]]; ἅρματα τρέφειν keep chariot-horses for racing, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Hiero” 11.5]]; ἅρματος τροφεύς [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Leges” 834b.]]

__4
metaphorically, ἅ. θαλάσσης a ship, [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [4th-5th c.AD(?): Nonnus Epicus “Dionysiaca” 4.230, +others, 2nd-3rd c.AD: Oppianus Anazarbensis Epicus “Halieutica - Poetae Bucolici et Didactici” 1.190.]]

__II
a mountain district in Attica, where omens from lightning were watched for: hence proverbial, ὁπόταν δἰ Ἅρματος ἀστράψη, i.e. seldom or never, [Refs 1st c.BC+ [1st c.BC-1st c.AD: Strabo Geographus 9.2.11]]; δι᾽ Ἅρματος alone, [Refs 1st c.AD+ [1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus 2.679c.]]

__III
[Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Pythagoras Philosophus]] name for unity, [Refs [Theol.Ar. 6.]]

Abbott-Smith / STEPBible (TBESG)
ἁρμόζω
(ἁρμός), [in LXX for אמן, etc. ;]
__1. to fit, join.
__2. of marriage, to betroth. Mid.,
__(a) to join to oneself, marry, take to wife; (b) to give in marriage: 2Co.11:2 (for this there is no direct parallel. But see M, Pr., 160; MM, see word).†
(AS)

---

LSJ / STEPBible (TFLSJ)
ἁρμόζω,
Attic dialect ἁρμόττω, Doric dialect ἁρμόσδω [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [3rd c.BC: Theocritus Poeta Bucolicus 1.53]] (ἐφ-); participle ἁρμόσσον[Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Hippocrates Medicus “περὶ ἄρθρων ἐμβολῆς” 37:]]imperfect ἥρμοζον, Doric dialect ἅρμ-[Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “N.” 8.11]]: future ἁρμόσω[Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Antigone” 1318 (Lyric poetry), 5th c.BC: Hippocrates Medicus “περὶ ἀγμῶν” 31, 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Thesmophoriazusae” 263]]: aorist ἥρμοσα[Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 3.333, etc.]], Doric dialect ἅρμοξα[Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “N.” 10.12]] (συν-): perfect ἥρμοκα[Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Poetica” 1459b32]]:— middle, Epic dialect imperative ἁρμόζεο[Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 5.162,]] -όζου [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-3rd c.BC: Philemo Comicus 187]]: future -όσομαι[Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd c.AD: Galenus Medicus 10.971]]: aorist ἡρμοσάμην[Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 5.32, etc.]], Doric dialect ἁρμοξάμην[Refs 7th c.BC+ [7th c.BC: Alcman Lyricus 71]]: —passive, perfect ἥρμοσμαι[Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Phoenissae” 116 (Lyric poetry), 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Laches” 193d]], Ionic dialect ἅρμοσμαι[Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 2.124]]; Doric dialect infinitive ἁρμόχθαι[Refs 1st c.BC+ [1st c.BC(?): Ocellus Lucanus Philosophus cited in 5th c.AD: Stobaeus, Joannes 1.13.2]]; Doric dialect 3rd.pers.singular ἅρμοκται[Refs 5th c.AD+ [Ecphantus Pythagoreus cited in 5th c.AD: Stobaeus, Joannes 4.7.64]]: aorist ἡρμόσθην[Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Phaedo” 93a]], Doric dialect ἁρμόχθην[Refs 3rd c.AD+ [3rd c.AD(?): Diogenes Laertius 8.85]]: future ἁρμοσθήσομαι[Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Coloneus” 908]]:—fit together, join, especially of joiner's work, ἥρμοσεν ἀλλήλοισιν (i.e. τὰ δοῦρα) [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 5.247]] (also in middle, put together, ἁρμόζεο χαλκῷ εὐρεῖαν σχεδίην[Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. work] 162; ναυπηγίαν ἁρμόζων 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Cyclops” 460; ἁρμόζειν χαίταν στεφάνοισι 5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “I.” 7 6). 39; ἀρβύλαισιν ἁ. πόδα 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Hippolytus” 1189]]; ἁ. πόδα ἐπὶ γαίας plant foot on ground, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [[prev. author] “Or.” 233; ἁ. ποδὸς ἴχνια 4th-5th c.BC: Simonides Lyricus 182]]; ἐν ἁσυχαία βάσει βάσιν ἅρμοσαι (aorist imperative middle) [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Coloneus” 198; στόμ᾽ ἅρμοσον]]kiss, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Troades” 763]]; ἁ. ψαλίοις ἵππους furnish them with..,  [Refs [[prev. author] “Rh.” 27 (Lyric poetry).]]

__b
generally, adapt, accommodate, ἁ. δίκην εἰς ἕκαστον award each his just due, [Refs 6th c.BC+ [6th c.BC: Solon Lyricus 36.17]]; σφισὶν βίοτον ἁ. accord them life, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “N.” 7.98]]; apply a remedy, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Trachiniae” 687]]; make ready, τοὐπτάνιον[Refs [Hegesippus Epigrammaticus Comedy texts 1.19]]:—middle, accommodate, suit oneself, πρὸς τὴν παροῦσαν πάντοθ᾽ ἁρμόζου τύχην Philem.[same place]; πρός τινα[Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd c.AD: Lucianus Sophista “Merc.Cond.” 30]]; ἁ. σύνεσιν acquire it, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Hippocrates Medicus “νόμος” 2.]]

__2
of marriage, betroth, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 9.108; ἁ. κόρᾳ ἄνδρα 5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “P.” 9.117]]; ἁ. γάμον, γάμους,[Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. work] 13, 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Phoenissae” 411]]:—middle, betroth to oneself, take to wife, τὴν θυγατέρα τινός[Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 5.32, 47]] (but middle = active, [NT+2nd c.AD+ [NT.2Cor.11.2); ἁ. ὡς ἐὰν αἱρῆται γάμῳ “POxy.” 906.7 (2nd-3rd c.AD):—]]passive, ἁρμόσθαι θυγατέρα τινὸς γυναῖκα have her betrothed or married to one, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 3.137]]; ὡς ἐκείνῳ τῇδέ τ᾽ ἦν ἡρμοσμένα as troth was plighted between him and her, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Antigone” 570.]]

__3
bind fast, ἁ. τινὰ ἐν ἄρκυσι[Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Bacchae” 231.]]

__4
set in order, regulate, govern, στρατόν[Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “N.” 8.11]]:—passive, [νόμοις] οὐκ ἄλλοισιν ἁρμοσθήσεται[Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Coloneus” 908]]; κονδύλοις ἡρμοττόμην I was ruled or drilled with cuffs, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Equites” 1236.]]

__4.b
in the Spartan Constitution, act as harmost, ἐν ταῖς πόλεσιν[Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Respublica Lacedaemoniorum” 14.2, etc.: with _accusative_, ἁρμοστὴν ὃς ἥρμοζε τὴν Ἀσίαν 2nd c.AD: Lucianus Sophista “Tox.” 17.]]

__5
in Music, tune instruments, τὸ σύμφωνον[Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Philebus” 56a, etc.]]:—middle, ἁρμόττεσθαι ἁρμονίαν[Refs [[prev. author] “R.” 591d]]; ἁ. λύραν tune one's lyre,[Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. work] 349e; Δωριστὶ ἁ. λύραν 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Equites” 989; αὐλόν 2nd c.AD: Lucianus Sophista “Harm.” 1 (but μέλη ἔς τι ἁ.]] adapt them to a subject, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Simonides Lyricus 184)]]:—passive, of the lyre, ἡρμόσθαι to be tuned,[Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Theaetetus” 144e, compare “Phd.” 85e; ἁρμονίαν καλλίστην ἡρμ. [prev. author] “La.” 188d]]; ὁμονοητικὴ καὶ ἡρμοσμένη ψυχή at harmony with itself, [Refs [[prev. author] “R.” 554e.]]

__6
compose, ᾆσμα[Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd-3rd c.AD: Philostratus Sophista “Heroicus” 19.17.]]

__II
intransitive, fit well, of clothes or armour, ἥρμοσε δ᾽ αὐτῷ [θώρηξ] [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 3.333; Ἕκτορι δ᾽ ἥρμοσε τεύχε᾽ ἐπὶ χροΐ 17.210; ἐσθὰς ἁρμόζοισα γυίοις 5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “P.” 4.80]]; ἆρ᾽ ἁρμόσει μοι (i.e. τὰ ὑποδήματα); [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Thesmophoriazusae” 263]]; τοῖς τρόποις ἁ. ὥσπερ περὶ πόδα fit like a shoe, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus Comedy texts 129; θώραξ περὶ τὰ στέρνα ἁρμόζων 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 2.1.16.]]

__II.b
in Mathematics texts, coincide with, with dative, [Refs 3rd c.AD+ [3rd c.AD(?): Pappus Mathematicus 612.14]]; correspond, [Refs 2nd c.BC+ [2nd-1st c.BC(?): Hero Mechanicus “Automatopoetica” 1.4.]]

__II.2
suit, be adapted for, τινί[Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Tyrannus” 902 (Lyric poetry), “El.” 1293, 5th-6th c.BC: Andocides Orator 4.6]]; τόδ᾽ οὐκ ἐπ᾽ ἄλλον ἁρμόσει shall not be adapted to another, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Antigone” 1318; κἂν ἐπὶ τῶν θηρίων ἁρμόσειε λόγος 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Politica” 1281b19]]; εἴς τι, πρός τι, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Politicus” 289b, 286d; πρὸς τὰς συνουσίας 5th-6th c.BC: Isocrates Orator 2.34, compare 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 61.24]]; of medicines, [Refs 1st c.AD+ [1st c.AD: Dioscorides (Dioscurides) Medicus 1.2, +others]]; of an argument, apply, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Physica” 209a9, +others; τὸ τοῦ Ξενοφάνους ἁρμόττει]]is applicable, [Refs [[prev. author] “Rh.” 1377a19.]]

__II.3
impersonal, ἁρμόζει it is fitting, with accusative et infinitive, σιγᾶν ἂν ἁρμόζοι σε[Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Trachiniae” 731]]: c.infinitive only, λόγους οὓς ἁρμόσει λέγειν[Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 18.42; πάντα τὰ τοιαῦτα ἁρμόττει καλεῖν [prev. author] 21.166; οὔτε ἁ. μοι οἰκεῖν μετὰ τοιούτων [prev. author] 40.57; τὰ τοιαῦτα ῥηθῆναι μάλιστ᾽ ἂν ἁρμόσειεν 5th-6th c.BC: Isocrates Orator 9.72.]]

__II.4
participle ἁρμόζων, ουσα, ον, fitting, suitable, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “P.” 4.129]]; ἡ ἁρμόζουσα ἀπόφασις the appropriate verdict, [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [3rd c.BC: Archimedes Geometra “περὶ σφαίρας καὶ κυλίνδρου” 1]] Praef.; ἀλλήλοις[Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Laches” 188d, +others: with _genitive_, 2nd c.BC: Polybius Historicus 1.44.1; πρός τι 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Memorabilia” 4.3.5, etc.]]

__II.5
to be in tune, λύραν ἐπίτειν᾽ ἕως ἂν ἁρμόσῃ[Refs 3rd c.BC+ [3rd c.BC: Macho Comicus 2.9.]]

[in LXX: Gen.18:15 (כָּחַשׁ pi.), Wis.12:27 16:16 17:10, 4Ma.8:7 4Mac 10:15 * ;]

(AS)

LSJ / STEPBible (TFLSJ)
ἀρνέομαι,
future -ήσομαι[Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Prometheus Vinctus” 268, 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Ecclesiazusae” 365; also ἀρνηθήσομαι 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Philoctetes” 527]] (ἀπ-), [NT.Luke.12.9:]aorist passive ἠρνήθην frequently in Attic dialect, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 6.60, etc.]]: also aorist middle ἠρνησάμην[Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Homerus Epicus (see. below), 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 3.1]]; rare in Trag. and Attic dialect, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Ion” 1026, 4th c.BC: Aeschines Orator 2.69, 3.324]]: perfect ἤρνημαι[Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 28.24]]:—deny, disown, τεὸν ἔπος ἀρνήσασθαι[Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 14.212, 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 8.358, etc.; ἀ. ἀμφὶ βόεσσιν “hymnus ad Mercurium” 390; ἀ. ἃ εἶπον 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Hecuba” 303: _absolutely_, 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 2.174]]; ἀρνούμενοι ἔπαινοι negative praises, [Refs 1st c.AD+ [1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus 2.58a.]]

__2
refuse, τόξον.. δόμεναί τε καὶ ἀρνήσασθαι[Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 21.345, compare 8th-7th c.BC: Hesiodus Epicus “Opera et Dies” 408, 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 3.1; ἀ. γάμον 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 1.249]]; ἀ. χρείαν decline, renounce a duty or office, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 18.282; διαθήκην [prev. author] 36.34; κληρονομίαν “PFlor.” 61.49 (1st c.AD)]]; ζωὰν ἀ., of a suicide, [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [“Anthologia Graeca” 7.473 (3rd-2nd c.BC: Aristodicus Epigrammaticus); δυνάμει τὸν βίον ἀ. 2nd c.AD: Sextus Empiricus Philosophus “adversus Mathematicos” 11.163]]; ἀ. ἀνθρώπους cast aside humanity, [Refs 4th c.AD+ [4th c.AD: Himerius Sophista “Orationes” 2.10.]]

__3
absolutely, say No, decline, ὁ δ᾽ ἠρνεῖτο στεναχίζων[Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 19.304; αὐτὰρ ὅ γ᾽ ἠρνεῖτο στερεῶς 23.42, etc.]]

__4
in expressing denial, with infinitive, either without μή, deny that.., [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Eumenides” 611, 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Iphigenia Aulidensis” 966]]; or with μή, say that.. not.., [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Equites” 572, 5th c.BC: Antipho Orator 3.3.7, etc.]]; οὐδ᾽ αὐτὸς ἀρνεῖται μὴ οὐ.. [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd-3rd c.AD: Dio Cassius Historicus 50.22]]; also οὐκ ἂν ἀρνοίμην τὸ δρᾶν [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Philoctetes” 118]]; ἀ. ὅτι οὐ.., ὡς οὐ.., [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Respublica Atheniensium” 2.17, 5th c.BC: Lysias Orator 4.1, 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 9.54.]]

__5
in expressing refusal, with infinitive, ἀ. εἶναι χρηστούς[Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 6.13]]: poetry also with participle, οὐ γὰρ εὐτυχῶν ἀρνήσομαι[Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Alcestis” 1158, compare “Or.” 1582.]]

deep_entry:
Abbott-Smith / STEPBible (TBESG)
ἁρπαγμός, οῦ, ὁ
(ἁρπάζω);
__1. prop., accusative, to the rule of its formation (Bl., § 27, 2), actively, the act of seizing, robbery (Plut., Deu Puer. Educ., p. 12A), Php.2:6, AV (Waterland, Works, II, 108; Cremer, 649 f.; Meyer, in l; cf. also JThS, July, 1909, April, 1911; MM, see word).
__2. Passively = ἅρπαγμα (Eze.22:25, of a lion's prey, ), a thing seized, hence, a prize: Phi, l.with, RV (Lft., Ellic., ICC, in l; Donaldson, NCrat., 450 ff.; and esp. Gifford, The Incarnation, 59-71, and reff. in DB, ii, 835 B). The lexical data favour the active meaning, but as they also admit the possibility of the alternative, most modern expositors have accepted the latter as seeming to suit the logic of the passage better. The lexical difficulty, however, remains (MM, see word, esp. the last ref.). As to the usage of St. Paul, he seems inclined to adopt the -μα form where it is appropriate (e.g. Rom.11:9, where cf. LXX; 1Co.13:9, 2 Co 19), and there is certainly a presumption in favour of the active meaning here from the fact that he does not use the LXX ἅρπαγμα. Suggestions looking to a fresh exegesis are given in JThS, ll with†
(AS)

ἀρχαῖος, -αία, -αῖον
(ἀρχή), [in LXX chiefly for קֶדֶם ;]
original, ancient: Mat.5:21, 33, Luk.9:8, 19, Act.15:7, 21 21:16, 2Co.5:17, 2Pe.2:5, Rev.12:9 20:2.†
SYN.: παλαιός, old, without the reference to beginning and origin contained in ἀ. The distinction is observed in π. (MM, see word). ἀ. is the antithesis to καινός: παλ. to vέος (see Westc., He., 223; Cremer, 116)  (AS)

---

LSJ / STEPBible (TFLSJ)
ἀρχαῖος, α, ον,
(ἀρχή I) from the beginning or origin:

__I
mostly of things, ancient, σκότος[Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Coloneus” 106; ἐσθής 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 5.88; δόμοις ἐπασσάλευσαν ἀρχαῖον γάνος 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Agamemnon” 579 codices; Ζηνὸς ἀρχαίοις νόμοις 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Coloneus” 1382]]; χερὸς σῆς πίστιν ἀρχαίαν faith firm for ever, [Refs [[prev. work] 1632 codices]]

__I.2
old-fashioned, antiquated, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Prometheus Vinctus” 317 (Lyric poetry), 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Nubes” 984, 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 22.14]]; of literary style, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demetrius Phalereus Rhetor “Demetrius on Style” 244.]]

__I.2.b
simple, silly, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Nubes” 915, +others, 5th c.BC: Pherecrates Comicus 205; -ότερος εἶ τοῦ δέοντος 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Euthydemus” 295c, etc.]]

__I.3
ancient, former, τὸ ἀ. ῥέεθον[Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.75; τοῦ ἀ. λόγου [prev. author] 7.160; οὐ γὰρ δὴ τό γ᾽ ἀ. δέμας 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Coloneus” 110]]; οἱ ἀ., opposed to οἱ ὕστερον, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 2.16; ἀ. φύσις 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Choephori” 281, 5th c.BC: Hippocrates Medicus “περὶ ἄρθρων ἐμβολῆς” 53, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Symposium” 193c, etc.; φύσις καὶ κατάστασις ἀ. 3rd c.AD: Democritus Epigrammaticus 278; coupled with παλαιός, παλαιὸν δῶρον ἀρχαίου θηρός 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Trachiniae” 555, compare 5th c.BC: Lysias Orator 6.51, D. [prev. cited]]]

__I.4
old, worn out, ὑποδήματα[Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 4.5.14; πινάκια “BGU” 781i1 (1st c.AD).]]

__II
of persons, Θέμιν.. ἀρχαίαν ἄλοχον Διός[Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “Fragmenta.” 6.5]]; ἀ. θεαί, of the Erinyes, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Eumenides” 728; Πέλοψ 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Ajax” 1292]]; οἱ ἀ. the Ancients, name given by [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus]] to the pre-Socratics, [Refs [“Metaphorical” 1069a25, “GC” 314a6]]; in Lit. Crit., ancient, classical writers, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demetrius Phalereus Rhetor “Demetrius on Style” 15, 67; in 3rd c.AD: Plotinus Philosophus]], the philosophers down to Aristotle, [Refs [5.1.9]]; in NT, the Fathers, [NT.Matt.5.21, +others]

__II.2
ancient, old, βαλὴν ἀ., of Darius, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Persae” 657 (Lyric poetry); λάτρις 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Hecuba” 609; ἑταῖρος 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Memorabilia” 2.8.1]]; οἱ ἀ. κύριοι the original owners, [Refs 2nd c.BC+ [“BGU” 992 ii 6 (2nd c.BC)]]; τὰς ἀ. πόλεις (banished from) their original cities, [Refs [Polystr. p.22]] W.; ἀ. μαθητής an original disciple, [NT.Act.21.16; ἀ. μύστης “Inscription Magn.” 215 b;] παιδαγωγὸς ἀ., i.e of old, formerly, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Electra” 287, compare 853.]]

__III
neuter as adverb, τὸ ἀρχαῖον, Ionic dialect contraction τὠρχαῖον, anciently, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.56, 173, +others]], Attic dialect τἀρχαῖον[Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Supplices” 326; ἀπὸ τοῦ ἀ. 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 4.117; ἐξ ἀρχαίων 1st c.BC: Diodorus Siculus Historicus 1.14.]]

__III.2
regular adverb ἀρχαίως in olden style, καινὰ ἀ. λέγειν[Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Phaedrus” 267b, compare 5th-6th c.BC: Isocrates Orator 4.8, 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 9.48; ἀ. καὶ σεμνῶς 4th c.BC: Aeschines Orator 1.183.]]

__IV
irregular comparative ἀρχαιέστερος[Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “Fragmenta.” 45 (on ἀρχέστατος see entry .)]]; usual comparative -ότερος[Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Aves” 469]]: superlative -ότατος[Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.105, etc.]]

__V
as substantive, τὸ ἀρχαῖον, of money, prime cost, πλέον τοῦ ἀ.[Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “de Vectigalibus” 3.2]]; principal, mostly in plural, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Nubes” 1156, etc.; τἀρχαῖα ἀποδιδόναι 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 34.26, etc.]]; τῶν ἀρχαίων ἀπέστησαν lost their capital, [Refs [[prev. author] 1.15: opposed to ἔργον, [prev. author] 27.10]]; opposed to πρόσοδοι, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Isaeus Orator 6.38.]]

__V.2
ἀρχαίη, ἡ, ={ἀρχή}, [Refs [12th c.AD: Eustathius Episcopus Thessalonicensis 475.1, etc.]]

[in LXX for קֶדֶם, רֹאשׁ, רֹאשׁ, etc. ;]
__1. beginning, origin;
__(a) absol., of the beginning of all things: of God as the Eternal, the First Cause, Rev.21:6 (cf. 18); similarly, of Christ, Rev.22:13; of Christ as the uncreated principle, the active cause of creation, Rev.3:14; in his relation to the Church, Col.1:18; ἐν ἀ., Jhn.1:1-2; ἀπ᾽ ἀ. (and ἀπ᾽ ἀ. κτισεως), Mat.19:4, 8 24:21, Mrk.10:6 13:19, Jhn.8:44, 2Th.2:13, 2Pe.3:4, 1Jn.1:1 Jn 2:13-14 Jn 2:24; κατ ἀρχἀς, Heb.1:10;
__(b) relatively: Heb.7:3; ἀ. ὠδίνων, Mat.24:8, Mrk.13:9; τ. σημείων, Jhn.2:11; τ. ὑποστάσεως, Heb.3:14; τ. λογίων, Heb.5:12; ὁ τ. ἀρχῆς τ. Χριστοῦ λόγος, the account of the beginning, the elementary view of Christ, Heb.6:1; ἀρχὴν λαμβάνειν, to begin, Heb.2:3; ἐξ ἀ., Jhn.6:64 16:4; ἀπ᾽ ἀ., Luk.1:2, Jhn.15:27, 1Jn.2:7 Jn 2:24 Jn 3:11, 2Jn.5-6; ἐν ἀ., Act.11:15 26:4, Php.4:15; τὴν ἀρχήν, adverbially, at all (Hdt., al.; v MM, see word): Jhn.8:25.
__2. an extremity, a corner: Act.10:11 11:5.
__3. sovereignty, principality, rule (cf. DB, i, 616 f.): Luk.12:11 20:20, Rom.8:38, 1Co.15:24, Eph.1:21 3:10 6:12, Col.1:16 2:10, 15 Tit.3:1, Ju 6 (Cremer, 113).†
(AS)

LSJ / STEPBible (TFLSJ)
ἀρχή, ἡ,
(see. ἄρχω) beginning, origin, νείκεος ἀ.[Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 22.116; πήματος 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 8.81; φόνου 21.4, etc.]]; opposed to τέλος, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 7.51, etc.]]; opposed to τελευτή, [Refs 6th c.BC+ [6th c.BC: Theognis Elegiacus 607, compare 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Leges” 715e, 5th c.BC: Hippocrates Medicus “περὶ νούσων” 1.1; ἀ. γενέσθαι κακῶν 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 5.97; ἀ. ποιήσασθαί τινος 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 1.128, 5th-6th c.BC: Andocides Orator 2.37, 5th-6th c.BC: Isocrates Orator 12.120, etc.; ἀ. λαβεῖν τινός 4th c.BC: Aeschines Orator 1.11; τὰς ἀρχὰς εἰληφέναι 2nd c.BC: Polybius Historicus 4.28.3]]; ἀρχὴν ὑποθέσθαι lay a foundation, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 3.2, etc.; βαλέσθαι 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Epistulae” 326e]] (and passive, ἀρχαὶ βέβληνται[Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “N.” 1.8); ἀρχὴν ἄρχεσθαί τινος 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Timaeus” 36e]]; source of action, [ὁ ἄνθρωπος] ἔχει ἀρχὴν ἐλευθέραν[Refs 3rd c.AD+ [3rd c.AD: Plotinus Philosophus 3.3.4.]]

__b
with Preps. in adverbial usages, ἐξ ἀρχῆς from the beginning, from the first, from of old, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 1.188, 6th c.BC: Xenophanes Poeta Philosophus 10, etc.; οὑξ ἀ. φίλος 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Tyrannus” 385; ἡ ἐξ ἀ. ἔχθρα 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 54.3; τὸ ἐξ ἀ. 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Cynegeticus” 12.6; but πλουτεῖν ἐξ ἀ. πάλιν]]anew, afresh, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Plutus” 221; λόγον πάλιν ὥσπερ ἐξ ἀ. κινεῖν 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 450a]]; ὁ ἐξ ἀ. λόγος the original argument, [Refs [[prev. author] “Tht.” 177c, etc.]]; τὰ ἐξ ἀ. the principal sum, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Politica” 1280a30:—also ἀπ᾽ ἀ. 8th-7th c.BC: Hesiodus Epicus “Theogonia” 425, 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 2.104, 5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “P.” 8.25, 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Supplices” 344, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Theaetetus” 206d]]; κατ᾽ ἀρχάς in the beginning, at first, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 3.153, 7.5; αὐτίκα κατ᾽ ἀ. [prev. author] 8.94; τὸ κατ᾽ ἀ. 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Leges” 798a, +others]]

__c
accusative ἀρχήν, absolutely, to begin with, at first, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.9, 2.28, 8.132; τὴν ἀρχήν 5th-6th c.BC: Andocides Orator 3.20: _plural_, τὰς ἀρχάς 2nd c.BC: Polybius Historicus 16.22.8]]: frequently followed by a negative, not at all, ἀρχὴν μηδὲ λαβών[Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 3.39, compare 1.193, +others; ἀ. δὲ θηρᾶν οὐ πρέπει τἀμήχανα 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Antigone” 92; ἀ. κλύειν ἂν οὐκ.. ἐβουλόμην [prev. author] “Ph.” 1239, compare “El.” 439, 5th-6th c.BC: Philolaus Philosophus 3, 5th c.BC: Antipho Orator 5.73, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Gorgias” 478c; sometimes with _Article_, τοῦτο οὐκ ἐνδέκομαι τὴν ἀ. 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 4.25; τὴν ἀ. γὰρ ἐξῆν αὐτῷ μὴ γράφειν 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 23.93.]]

__2
first principle, element, first so used by Anaximander, accusative to [Refs 4th c.BC+ [6th c.AD: Simplicius Philosophus “in Aristotelis Physica commentaria - Comm. in Arist. Graeca” 150.23, compare 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Metaphysica” 983b11, etc.; Ἡράκλειτος τὴν ἀ. εἶναί φησι ψυχήν [prev. author] “de An.” 405a25]]; of ὕλη and θεός, opposed to στοιχεῖα, [Refs [“Placita Philosophorum” 1.3.25]]; practical principle of conduct, τῶν πράξεων τὰς ἀρχὰς καὶ τὰς ὑποθέσεις[Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 2.10]]; principles of knowledge, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Metaphysica” 995b8, +others]]

__3

branch of a river, [LXX.Gen.2.10 (_plural_).]

sum, total,[LXX.Num.1.2.]

vital organs of the body, [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd c.AD: Galenus Medicus 1.318, +others]]

__II
first place or power, sovereignty (not in [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Homerus Epicus), Διὸς ἀρχά 5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “O.” 2.64, compare 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.6, etc.; γενέσθαι ἐπ᾽ ἀρχῆς 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Politica” 1284b2: _metaphorically_, μεγάλην μεντἂν ἀ. εἴης εὑρηκώς,]] of a stroke of fortune, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 21.196: _plural_, ἀρχαὶ πολισσονόμοι 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Choephori” 864 (Lyric poetry); τὰς ἐμὰς ἀρχὰς σέβων 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Antigone” 744, etc.: with _genitive_ _of things_, τῆσδ᾽ ἔχων ἀρχὴν χθονός 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Tyrannus” 737]]; ἀ. τῶν νεῶν, τῆς θαλάσσης, power over them, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 3.90, 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Respublica Atheniensium” 2.7, etc.: proverbial, ἀ. ἄνδρα δείξει Biasap. 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Ethica Nicomachea” 1130a1, compare 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator “Prooemia” 48]]; method of government, οὐδὲ τὴν ἄλλην ἀ. ἐπαχθής[Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 6.54.]]

empire, realm, Κύρου, Περδίκκου ἀ., [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.91, 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 4.128, etc.]]

[prev. author] 6.54]]; ἀ. χειροτονητή, κληρωτή, Legal cited in [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aeschines Orator 1.21; withsg. Noun, Κυθηροδίκης ἀ. ἐκ τῆς Σπάρτης διέβαινεν αὐτόσε 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 4.53]]; term of office, ἀρχῆς λοιποὶ αὐτῷ δύο μῆνες[Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Antipho Orator 6.42; ἀρχαὶ καὶ λειτουργίαι “POxy.” 119.16 (3rd c.AD).]]

ἄρχων, οντος, ὁ,
(participle of ἄρχω) ruler, commander, νεός[Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 5.33: _absolutely_, 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Septem contra Thebas” 674, 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Ajax” 668, etc.]]; chief, king, Ἀσίας[Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Persae” 73]]; ἄ. τοῦ κόσμου τούτου, of Satan, [NT.John.16.11, +others]

__II
as official title, chief magistrate, especially at Athens, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 1.126, etc.; οἱ ἐννέα ἄρχοντες “IG” 2.163]]; οἱ ἄ., at Sparta, the authorities, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 6.106: _sing._, ὁ ἄρχων]] the eponymous magistrate of the year, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [Inscriptiones Graecae 1.52, +others, 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Ἀθηναίων Πολιτεία” 3.3, etc.]]; so in Boeotia, at Delphi, Delos, and elsewhere, [Refs [“IG” 7.2407, “SIG” 295.18, “IG” 2.814, etc.]]; = Latin consul, [Refs 2nd c.BC+ [2nd c.BC: Polybius Historicus 1.39.1.]]

__II.2
governor of a dependency or province, e.g. in the Athenian Empire, [Refs [“IG” 1.62b19, etc.]]; of a Roman governor, [Refs [“OGI” 441.59]]; = praefectus, [Refs 2nd c.BC+ [2nd c.BC: Polybius Historicus 6.26.5.]]

__II.3
generally, magistrate, official, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aeschines Orator 3.29, etc.]]; opposed to ἰδιώτης, [Refs [“SIG” 672.16 (Delph.)]]; ruler of a synagogue, [NT.Matt.9.18]; president of a club, [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [“PLond.” 3.1178.6 (2nd c.AD).]]

of oneself, of one's own accord, ἀλλά τις αὐ. ἴτω[Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 17.254; σπεύδοντα καὶ αὐτὸν ὀτρύνεις 8.293; καταπαύσομεν· οἱ δὲ καὶ αὐτοὶ παυέσθων 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 2.168; ἥξει γὰρ αὐτά 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Tyrannus” 341]]; also, in person, τῶν πραγμάτων ὑμῖν.. αὐτοῖς ἀντιληπτέον[Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 1.2.]]

__I.3
by oneself or itself, alone, αὐτός περ ἐών although alone, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 8.99]]; αὐτὸς ἐγείναο παῖδ᾽, i.e. without a mother,[Refs 8th c.BC+ [5.880, compare 8th-7th c.BC: Hesiodus Epicus “Theogonia” 924; ἀνακομισθῆναι αὐτὸν ἐς Φάληρον]]by himself, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 5.85]]; αὐτοὶ γάρ ἐσμεν we are by ourselves, i.e. among friends, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Acharnenses” 504, compare “Th.” 472, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Parmenides” 137b, 3rd c.BC: Herodas Mimographus 6.70, 1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus 2.755c, 2nd c.AD: Lucianus Sophista “DDeor.” 10.2; αὐτοῖς τοῖς ἀνδράσι.. ἢ καὶ τοῖς ἄλλοις 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 2.3.7; ἄνευ τοῦ σίτου τὸ ὄψον αὐτὸ ἐσθίειν [prev. author] “Mem.” 3.14.3; τὸν τρίβωνα ὃν αὐτὸν φορεῖ 4th-3rd c.BC: Theophrastus Philosophus “Characteres” 22.13 (probably)]]; αὐτὰ γὰρ ἔστιν ταῦτα these and no others, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Empedocles Poeta Philosophus 21.13, +others: strengthened, αὐτὸς κτήσατο οἶος]] himself alone, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 14.450]]; αὐτὸς μόνος, see at {μόνος} II; αὐτὸς καθ᾽ αὑτόν, see at {ἑαυτοῦ}.

__I.4
in Philosophy, by or in itself, of an abstract concept or idea, δίκαιον αὐτό[Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Phaedo” 65d; αὐτὸ τὸ ἕν [prev. author] “Prm.” 143a, +others, compare 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Metaphysica” 997b8: _neuter_, αὐτό]] is frequently in this sense, attached to Nouns of all genders, οὐκ αὐτὸ δικαιοσύνην ἐπαινοῦντες ἀλλὰ τὰς ἀπ᾽ αὐτῆς εὐδοκιμήσεις[Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 363a; less frequently with _Article_, τί ποτ᾽ ἐστὶν αὐτὸ ἡ ἀρετή [prev. author] “Prt.” 360e]]; more fully, εἰ αὐτὸ τοῦτο πατέρα ἠρώτων, ἆρα ὁ πατήρ ἐστι πατήρ τινος, ἢ ο; [Refs [[prev. author] “Smp.” 199d]]; ἀδελφός, αὐτὸ τοῦτο ὅπερ ἔστιν the ideal, abstract brother, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [[prev. passage]e: later, in _composition_, αὐτοαγαθόν, αὐτοάνθρωπος, etc. (which see),compare 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Metaphysica” 1040b33]]; less frequently agreeing with the substantive, ἵνα αὐτὴ δικαιοσύνη πρὸς ἀδικίαν αὐτὴν κριθείη[Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 612c, etc.; doubled, ἐκ τῆς εἰκόνος μανθάνειν αὐτήν τε αὐτήν, εἰ καλῶς εἴκασται]]its very self, [Refs [[prev. author] “Cra.” 439a.]]

__I.5
in dative with substantive, in one, together, ἀνόρουσεν αὐτῇ σὺν φόρμιγγι he sprang up lyre in hand, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 9.194]]; αὐτῇ σὺν πήληκι κάρη helmet and all,[Refs 8th c.BC+ [14.498, compare 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 13.118; αὐτῷ σὺν ἄγγει 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Ion” 32, compare “Hipp.” 1213; also without σύν, αὐτῇ κεν γαίῃ ἐρύσαι 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 8.24: so frequently in Prose and Poetry, αὐτοῖς ἀνδράσι]] men and all, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 6.93]]; αὐτοῖσι συμμάχοισι allies and all, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Prometheus Vinctus” 223 (Lyric poetry); αὐτοῖς μελάθροις διακναιομένους 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Medea” 164: with _Article_, αὐτοῖσι τοῖσι ἱματίοισι ἀπ᾽ ὦν ἔβαψε ἑωυτόν 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 2.47; αὐτοῖσι τοῖς πόρπαξι 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Equites” 849, etc.; αὐτοῖς τοῖς ἵπποις κατακρημνισθῆναι 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 1.4.7.]]

__I.6
added to ordinal Numbers, e.g. πέμπτος αὐτός himself the fifth, i. e. himself with four others, [NT+5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 1.46, compare 8.35, 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Historia Graeca (Hellenica)” 2.2.17, NT.Rev.17.11, etc.:—αὐτός always being the chief person.]]

__I.7
frequently coupled with οὗτος, τοῦτ᾽ αὐτό ἐστι τὸ ζητηθέν[Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Politicus” 267c, etc.; αὐτὸ τοῦτο μόνον [prev. author] “Grg.” 500b; also λεγόντων ἄλλο μὲν οὐδέν.. αὐτὰ δὲ τάδε 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 1.139; πόλεις ἄλλας τε καὶ αὐτὸ τοῦτο τὸ Βυζάντιον 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 7.1.27]]; ταῦτα ἥκω αὐτὰ ἵνα.. [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Protagoras” 310e.]]

__I.8
καὶ αὐτός himself too, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 7.73, 14.45, 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 5.5.9, etc.]]

__I.9
repeated in apodosi for emphasis, αὐτὸς ἐπαγγειλάμενος σώσειν.. αὐτὸς ἀπώλεσεν[Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Lysias Orator 12.68, compare 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Fragmenta - American Journal of Philology” 350, 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 3.2.4.]]

__I.10
in connexion with the person. pronoun, ἐγὼν αὐτός[Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 2.194; σέθεν αὐτοῦ 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 23.312; νωΐτερον αὐτῶν 15.39 (always divisim in 8th c.BC: Homerus Epicus)]]; followed by an enclitic pronoun, αὐτόν μιν[Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 4.244; so αὐτὸν γάρ σε δεῖ Προμηθέως 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Prometheus Vinctus” 86; also αὐτὸς ἔγωγε 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Phaedo” 59b, etc.:— after 8th c.BC: Homerus Epicus in the oblique cases αὐτός coalesces with the _pronoun_, ἐμαυτοῦ, σεαυτοῦ (these not in 7th-6th c.BC: Alcaeus Lyricus or 7th-6th c.BC: Sappho Lyrica, 2nd c.AD: Apollonius Dyscolus Grammaticus “de Pronominibus;” 80.10 ff.), ἑαυτοῦ, etc. (which see).]]

__I.10.b
with person. pronoun omitted, αὐτός.. ἧσθαι λιλαίομαι, for ἐγὼ αὐτός, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 13.252]]; αὐτὸν ἐλέησον, for ἐμὲ αὐτόν,[Refs 8th c.BC+ [24.503; αὐτῶν γὰρ ἀπωλόμεθ᾽ ἀφραδίῃσιν 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 10.27; in 2.33 οἱ αὐτῷ]] is simply a strengthened form of ο; and so in Attic dialect, when σὲ αὐτόν, ἐμοὶ αὐτῷ, etc., are read divisim, they are emphatic, not reflexive; in this case αὐτός generally precedes the person. pronoun,[Refs 5th c.BC+ [compare 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 6.2.25 with 6.1.14.]]

__I.10.c
with the reflexive ἑαυτοῦ, αὑτοῦ, etc., to add force and definiteness, αὐτὸς καθ᾽ αὑτοῦ[Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Septem contra Thebas” 406]]; αὐτοὶ ὑφ᾽ αὑτῶν[Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. work] 194; αὐτοὶ καθ᾽ αὑτούς 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Memorabilia” 3.5.4; αὐτὸ καθ᾽ αὑτό 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Theaetetus” 201e]]; sometimes between the Article and reflexive pronoun, τοῖς αὐτὸς αὑτοῦ πήμασιν βαρύνεται[Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Agamemnon” 836, compare “Pr.” 762; τούς γ᾽ αὐτὸς αὑτοῦ πολεμίους 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Ajax” 1132: also κατ᾽ αὐτὺ (_Boeotian dialect_ for αὐτοὶ) αὐτῶν “IG” 7.3172.121 (Orchom. _Boeotian dialect_).]]

__I.10.d
αὐτοῦ, αὐτῶν with possessive pronoun, πατρὸς κλέος ἠδ᾽ ἐμὸν αὐτοῦ[Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 6.446; θρῆνον.. ἐμὸν τὸν αὐτῆς 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Agamemnon” 1323; ἐχθρὸς ὢν τοῖς σοῖσιν αὐτοῦ 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Tyrannus” 416]]; τοῖς οἷσιν αὐτοῦ[Refs 8th c.BC+ [[prev. work] 1248; αὐτῶν σφετέρῃσιν ἀτασθαλίῃσιν 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 1.7; τοῖς ἡμετέροις αὐτῶν φίλοις 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 7.1.29.]]

__I.10.e
αὐτὸς ἑαυτοῦ with comparative and superlative adjective, αὐτὸς ἑωυτοῦ ῥέει πολλῷ ὑποδεέστερος[Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 2.25; τῇ εὐρυτάτη ἐστὶ αὐτὴ ἑωυτῆς [prev. author] 1.203.]]

__I.11
αὐτός for ὁ αὐτός, the same, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 12.225, 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 8.107, 16.138, 5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “N.” 5.1 (never in Trag.)]], and in later Prose, αὐταῖς ταῖς ἡμέραις[NT+2nd c.AD+ [“IG” 14.966 (2nd c.AD),cf. NT.Luke.23.12.]]

__I.12
comparative αὐτότερος[Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Epicharmus Comicus 5]]: superlative αὐτότατος his very self, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Plutus” 83: _neuter_ _plural_ αὐτότατα uncertain in 1st c.BC: Philodemus Philosophus “de Pietate - Herkulanische Studien” 80]]. adverb, comparative αὐτοτέρως[Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd c.AD: Galenus Medicus 18(2).431.]]

__II
he, she, it, for the simple pronoun of 3 person, only in oblique cases (except in later Gk., [NT.Luke.4.15, etc.)], and rarely first in a sentence, [NT+5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Laches” 194e, and later, NT.Eph.2.10, etc.]]: rare in Epic dialect, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 12.204 (where 2nd c.AD: Herodianus Grammaticus treated it as enclitic)]], and mostly emphatic,[Refs 8th c.BC+ [[prev. work] 14.457, 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 16.388]]; so in Trag., [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Helena” 421]]: in Prose, to recall a Noun used earlier in the sentence, ἐγὼ μὲν οὖν βασιλέα.. οὐκ οἶδα ὅ τι δεῖ αὐτὸν ὀμόσαι[Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 2.4.7; πειράσομαι τῷ πάππῳ.. συμμαχεῖν αὐτῷ [prev. author] “Cyr.” 1.3.15; ἄνδρα δὴ.. εἰ ἀφίκοιτο εἰς τὴν πόλιν, προσκυνοῖμεν ἂν αὐτόν 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 398a]]; after a Relative, ὅς κε θεοῖς ἐπιπείθηται.. ἔκλυον αὐτοῦ[Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 1.218; οὓς μὴ εὕρισκον, κενοτάφιον αὐτοῖς ἐποίησαν 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 6. 4.9, compare 1.9.29]]; especially where a second Verb requires a change of case in the pronoun, οἳ ἂν ἐξελεγχθῶσι.. ὡς προδότας αὐτοὺς ὄντας τιμωρηθῆναι[Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. author] “An.” 2.5.27; ἐκεῖνοι οἷς οὐκ ἐχαρίζονθ᾽ οἱ λέγοντες οὐδ᾽ ἐφίλουν αὐτούς 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 3.24; in subdivisions, ὅσοι.. οἱ μὲν αὐτῶν.. 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 1.1.1, compare 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Charmides” 168e]]; later, pleonastically after a Relative, ὧν ὁ μὲν αὐτῶν[NT+5th c.BC+ [3rd c.BC: Callimachus Epicus “Epigrammata” 43, cf. NT.Luke.3.16, NT.Rev.7.2, etc.: in 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Philoctetes” 316 αὐτοῖς is emphatic 'in their own persons'.]]

__III
with Article ὁ αὐτός, ἡ αὐτή, τὸ αὐτό, and Attic dialect contraction αὑτός, αὑτή, ταὐτό and ταὐτόν (as required by the metre,[Refs 5th c.BC+ [compare 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Tyrannus” 734 with 325, and in Prose to avoid hiatus): _genitive_ ταὐτοῦ, _dative_ ταὐτῷ,]] plural neuter ταὐτ; Ionic dialect ὡυτός, τὠυτό:—the very one, the same, rare in [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Homerus Epicus, 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 6.391, 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 7.55, 326; ὁ αὐ. εἰμι τῇ γνώμῃ 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 3.38, compare 5.75; ἐπὶ τὸ αὐ. αἱ γνῶμαι ἔφερον [prev. author] 1.79]]: with dative, to denote sameness or agreement, especially in Prose, τὠυτὸ ἂν ὑμῖν ἐπρήσσομεν[Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 4.119; τὸν αὐτὸν χῶρον ἐκλιπὼν ἐμοί 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Choephori” 543]]; ὁ αὐτὸς τῷ λίθῳ the same as the stone, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Euthydemus” 298a]]; ἐν ταὐτῷ εἶναί τινι to be in the place with.., [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 3.1.27]]; προσίεσθαί τινα ἐς ταὐτὸ ἑαυτῷ to have a person meet one,[Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. work] 30, compare 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Choephori” 210; κατὰ ταὐτὰ τῷ Νείλῳ 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 2.20; τῇ αὐτῇ.. καί [prev. author] 4.109; τὴν αὐτὴν διάνοιαν καὶ κατ᾽ ἐκείνην ἡλικίαν 5th-6th c.BC: Isocrates Orator 5.83; ὁ αὐτός.. ὥσπερ 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Phaedo” 86a; ἐς ταὐτὸν ἀλλήλοις]]face to face, [Refs 4th c.AD+ [4th c.AD: Julianus Imperator “Orationes” 2.5a0.]]

__III.2
in later Greek, the said, the above-named, Ἡρώδης ὁ αὐ.[Refs 3rd c.BC+ [“PLille” 23.8 (3rd c.BC), etc.]]

__IV
Adverbial phrases:

__IV.1
αὐτὸ μόνον simply, merely, [Refs 1st c.AD+ [1st c.AD: Philo Judaeus 2.252, etc.; αὐ. μόνον ἐργάτης 2nd c.AD: Lucianus Sophista “Somn.” 9; αὐ. μόνον τὸ ὄνομα τῆς φωνῆς 2nd c.AD: Apollonius Dyscolus Grammaticus “de Syntaxi;” 22.20.]]

__IV.2
αὐτό as adverb, ={ἄρτι}, [Refs [“epigram Gr.” 540.1 (from Thrace).]]

__IV.3
αὐτὸ τοῦτο as adverb, [NT+2nd c.BC+ [“PGrenf.” 1.114 (2nd c.BC), NT.2Pet.1.5; τῆς αὐτὸ τοῦτο κινουμένης σφαίρας 4th c.AD: Iamblichus Philosophus “de communi mathematica scientia” 17.]]

__IV.4
with Preps., ἐπὶ τὸ αὐτό added together, making a total, [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [PLond. 2.196.37 (2nd c.AD)]]; κατὰ τὸ αὐτό together, at the same time,[NT.Acts.14.1], etc.; but κατ᾽ αὐτό just then, [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd c.AD: Herodianus Grammaticus 1.12.3.]]

__V
In Compos.:

__V.1
of or by oneself, self-.., as in αὐτοδίδακτος, αὐτογνώμων, αὐτόματος: and so, independently, as in αὐτοκράτωρ, αὐτόνομος.

__V.2
hence, as a second self, very.., bodily, as with proper names, Αὐτοθαΐς.

__V.3
in the abstract, the ideal, see above[Refs [1.4.]]

__V.4
precisely, as in αὐτόδεκα.

__V.5
rarely with reflexive sense of ἀλλήλων, as in αὐτοκτονέω.

__V.6
in one piece with, together with, as in αὐτόκωπος, αὐτοχείλης, αὐτόπρεμνος, αὐτόρριζος.

__V.7
by itself: hence, only, as in αὐτόξυλος, αὐτόποκος.—For αὐτοῦ, αὐτῶς, etc., see the respective Arts.

Doric dialect αὐτῶ and αὐτεῖ, adverb, properly genitive of αὐτός:— just there or just here, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Homerus Epicus, etc.]]; ἐπίσχες αὐτοῦ stop there! [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Cratinus Comicus 66:]] —frequently with the place added, αὐτοῦ ἐνὶ Τροίῃ, μέν᾽ αὐτοῦ τῷδ᾽ ἐνὶ χώρῳ, here in Troy, etc., [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 2.237, 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 10.271; αὐτοῦ ἔνθα 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 8.207]]; που αὐτοῦ ἀγρῶν somewhere there on the farm, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 4.639; αὐτοῦ ὑπὲρ κεφαλῆς 8.68; αὐτοῦ περὶ τεῖχος 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Agamemnon” 452 (Lyric poetry)]]; αὐτοῦ ταύτῃ in this very place, exactly here, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.214, 3.77, 4.135; αὐτοῦ τῇ περ ἔπεσε [prev. author] 1.30:]] — so that αὐτοῦ usually precedes; but κεῖθι αὐτοῦ[Refs 6th c.BC+ [“hymnus ad Apollinem” 374; κατ᾽ οἴκους αὐτοῦ 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Pax” 89; ἐνθάδ᾽ αὐτοῦ 6th c.BC: Solon Lyricus 36.11, 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Plutus” 1187; τοῖς ἐνθάδ᾽ αὐτοῦ μὴ κατ᾽ ἄστυ δημόταις 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Coloneus” 78.]]
