LSJ / STEPBible (TFLSJ)
ἑαυτοῦ, ῆς, οῦ, ἑαυτῷ, ῇ, ῷ, ἑαυτόν, ήν, ό,
plural ἑαυτῶν, ἑαυτοῖς, ἑαυτούς άς, ά: Ionic dialect ἑωυτοῦ [Refs 5th c.BC+ [“SIG” 57.44 (Milet., 5th c.BC), etc.]]; also ωὑτῆς [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [3rd c.BC: Herodas Mimographus 6.84, ωὑτέου 2nd c.AD: Aretaeus Medicus “περὶ αἰτιῶν καὶ σημείων ὀξέων παθῶν” 1.7 (_Ionic dialect_ ἑωυ- by contraction of ἕο αὐ-, from which also _Attic dialect_ ἑᾱυ-, frequently written ἑατοῦ]] in Papyrus and Inscrr., as [Refs 1st c.BC+ [“SIG” 774.2 (Delph., 1st c.BC)]]: Attic dialect contraction αὑτοῦ, etc., which is the usual form in Trag., though ἑαυτοῦ, etc., are used (though rarely) when the metre requires, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Prometheus Vinctus” 188 (_anapaest meter_), +others; in _Attic dialect_ Inscrr. αὑτοῦ prevails after BC 300 4th c.BC]]; Cretan dialect ϝιαυτοῦ Kohler-Ziebarth Stadtrecht von Gortyn [Refs [p.34]]; Doric dialect αὐταυτοῦ, αὐσαυτοῦ (which see); Thess. εὑτοῦ (dative), [Refs [“IG” 9(2).517.16]]: genitive plural ηὑτῶν [Refs [“Schwyzer” 251 A 44 (from Cos)]]:—reflexive pronoun of 3rd pers., of himself, herself, itself, etc.; first in [Refs 7th c.BC+ [7th-6th c.BC: Alcaeus Lyricus 78, 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus]], and Attic dialect [Refs 8th c.BC+ [(8th c.BC: Homerus Epicus has ἕο αὐτοῦ, οἷ αὐτῷ, ἑ αὐτόν): αὐτὸ ἐφ᾽ ἑαυτό (variant -τοῦ)]] itself by itself, absolutely, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Theaetetus” 152b]]; αὐτὸ ἐφ᾽ αὑτοῦ[Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. work] 160b; ὅταν τὸ ἐφ᾽ ἑαυτὸν ἕκαστος σπεύδῃ 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 1.141; αὐτὸ καθ᾽ αὑτό 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Theaetetus” 157a; αὐτὰ πρὸς αὑτά [prev. work] 154e]]; ἀφ᾽ ἑαυτῶν, ἑαυτοῦ, of themselves, himself, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 5.60, 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Memorabilia” 2.10.3]]; ἐφ᾽ ἑαυτοῦ, see at {ἐπ; ἐν ἑαυτῷ γίγνεσθαι}, ἐντὸς ἑαυτοῦ γ., see at {ἐν}, ἐντό; παρ᾽ ἑαυτῷ at his own house, [Refs [[prev. work] 3.13.3, etc.: especially with _comparative_ and _superlative_, ἐγένοντο ἀμείνονες αὐτοὶ ἑωυτῶν they surpassed]]themselves, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 8.86]]; πλουσιώτεροι ἑαυτῶν continually richer, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 1.8; θαρραλεώτεροι αὐτοὶ ἑαυτῶν 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Protagoras” 350a]], compare d; τῇ αὐτὸ ἑωυτοῦ ἐστι μακρότατον at its very greatest length, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 2.8, compare 149, 4.85, 198.]]

__II
in Attic dialect, Trag., and later, αὑτοῦ, etc., is used for the 1st pers. or 2nd pers., as for ἐμαυτοῦ, αὐτὸς καθ᾽ αὑτοῦ τἄρα μηχανορραφῶ [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Choephori” 221, compare 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Tyrannus” 138, etc.; for σεαυτοῦ, μόρον τὸν αὑτῆς οἶσθα 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Agamemnon” 1297, compare 1141, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Phaedo” 101c (variant), 3rd-2nd c.BC: Philo Mechanicus “(Belopoeica) Excerpte aus Philons Mechanik - Ath. Berl. Akad.” 59.16, etc.: so in _plural_, τὰ αὑτῶν (={ἡμῶν αὐτῶν}) ἐκποριζώμεθα 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 1.82; δώσομεν ἑαυτούς 4th-3rd c.BC: Epicurus Philosophus “Gnomologium Vaticanum - Kleine Schriften” 47]]; ἐφ᾽ ἑαυτοῖς by ourselves, [LXX+2nd c.BC+ [LXX.1Ki.14.9, compare “PPar.” 47.26 (2nd c.BC), NT.2Cor.7.1, etc.]]; ἑαυτῶν, ={ὑμῶν αὐτῶν}, [Refs 2nd c.BC+ [“PPar.” 63.128 (2nd c.BC).]]

__III
plural, ἑαυτῶν, ἑαυτοῖς, etc., is sometimes used for ἀλλήλων, ἀλλήλοις, one another, διάφοροι ἑωυτοῖσι [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 3.49; παρακελευόμενοι ἐν ἑαυτοῖς 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 4.25, etc.]]; καθ᾽ αὑτοῖν one against the other, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Antigone” 144 (_anapaest meter_); πρὸς αὑτούς 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 18.19; περιιόντες αὑτῶν πυνθάνονται [prev. author] 4.10, compare 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Lysis” 215b.]]

LSJ / STEPBible (TFLSJ)
αὐτό-χειρ, χειρος, ὁ, ἡ,
with one's own hand, creative, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Supplices” 592 (Lyric poetry)]]; αὐ. λούειν, παίειν, κτείνειν, [NT+5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Antigone” 900, 1315, “Aj.” 57; τίνες ᾠκοδόμησα;—ὄρνιθες αὐτόχειρες 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Aves” 1132 {αὐτοχειρί}, compare “Lys.” 269, 5th c.BC: Theopompus Comicus 86, NT.Act.27.19, etc.]]: with genitive, very doer, per-petrator of a thing, αὐ. τοῦδε τοῦ τάφου[Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Antigone” 306]]; τῆς ἀσελγείας ταύτης[Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 21.60]]; αὐ. οὔτε τῶν ἀγαθῶν οὔτε τῶν κακῶν men who accomplish neither.., [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Isocrates Orator 5.150.]]

__II
absolutely, one who kills himself, suicide, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Antigone” 1175; αὐ. ἑαυτῶν 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Fragmenta” 502]]; simply, murderer, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Tyrannus” 231, 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 21.116]]; αὐτὸν.. νομίζω αὐτόχειρά μου γεγενῆσθαι τούτοις τοῖς ἔργοις [Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. work]106: with _genitive_, αὐ. καὶ φονεῖς τῶν πολιτῶν 5th-6th c.BC: Isocrates Orator 4.111, compare 4th-3rd c.BC: Menander Comicus “Σαμία” 216; in full, τὸν αὐ. τοῦ φόνου 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Tyrannus” 266, compare “El.” 955, 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 18.287.]]

__III
as adjective, murderous, especially of murder committed by one's own hand or by kinsmen, αὐ. θάνατος, σφαγή, μοῖρα, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Phoenissae” 880, “Or.” 947, “Med.” 1281 (Lyric poetry)]]; πληγέντες αὐτόχειρι σὺν μιάσματι, of brothers smitten by mutual slaughter, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Antigone” 172; φόνος 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 615c.]]

__III.2
αὐτόχειρα γράμματα written with one's own hand, autograph, [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd-3rd c.AD: Dio Cassius Historicus 59.4.]]

__II

ἀφ-ίημι,
[in LXX for נשׂא, נוח hi., נתן, סלח ni., עזב, etc. ;]
__1. to send forth, send away, let go: of divorce (DB, iii, 274a), τ. γυναῖκα (Hdt.), 1Co.7:11-13; of death, τ. πνεῦμα (Gen.35:18, Hdt., al.), Mat.27:50; (φωνήν, to utter a cry, Mrk.15:37; of debts, to remit, forgive (cl.), τ. δανεῖον, Mat.18:27; τ. ὀφειλήν, Mat.18:32; esp. of sins (Cremer 296f.), τ. ἁμαρτίας, ἁμαρτήματα, ἀνομίας, Mat.9:2, Rom.4:7" (LXX), 1Jn.1:9, al.; punctiliar and iterative present (M, Pr., 119), Mrk.2:5, Luk.11:4; Ion. pf., ἀφέωνται (M, Pr., 38), Luk.5:23.
__2. to leave alone, leave, neglect: Mat.4:11 5:24 15:14, Mrk.1:20, 31 Jhn.4:3, 28 al.; τ. ἐντολὴν τ. θεοῦ, Mrk.7:8; τον̀ τ. ἀρχῆς τ. Χριστοῦ λόγον, Heb.6:1; τ. ἀγάπην τ. πρώτην, Rev.2:4; ptcp., ἀφείς, pleonastic (as in Aram.; M, Pr., 14; Dalman, Words, 21f.), Mat.13:36 22:22, Mrk.8:13, al.
__3. to let, suffer, permit: Mat.3:15; with accusative, Mat.3:15, 19:14, al.; with accusative of thing(s) and dative of person(s), Mat.5:40; with inf. pres., Mat.23:14, al.; aor., Mrk.5:37, al.; in late Gk. (M, Pr., 175f.), before ἵνα, Mrk.11:16, Jhn.12:7; with subjunct. (M, Pr., l.with; Bl., §64, 2), Mat.7:4 27:49, Mrk.15:36, Luk.6:42 (see further MM, see word).

leave alone, pass by, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 3.95, etc.]]; neglect, τὰ θεῖα [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Coloneus” 1537; τὸν καιρόν 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 1.8; λέκτρων εὐνάς 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Persae” 544: followed by a predicate, ἀφύλακτον ἀ. τὴν ἑωυτῶν]] leave unguarded, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 8.70]]; ἄτιμον, ἔρημον ἀ. τινά, [NT+5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Coloneus” 1279, “Ant.” 887; ἀ. τινὰς ὀρφανούς NT.John.14.18; ἀ. τι ἀόριστον 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Politica” 1265a39]]; leave, περὶ κινήσεως, ὅθεν ὑπάρχει, τοῖς ἄλλοις ἀφεῖσαν[Refs [[prev. author] “Metaphorical” 985b20, compare 987b14]]:—passive, especially in perfect imperative, ἀφείσθω ἐπὶ τοῦ παρόντος missum fiat, [Refs [[prev. author] “EN” 1166a34, compare “Pol.” 1286a5, 1289b12.]]

__III.2
with accusative et infinitive, ἀ. τὸ πλοῖον φέρεσθαι let the boat be carried away, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.194; μὴ ἀφεῖναί με ἐπὶ ξένης ἀδιαφορηθῆναι “PLond.” 2.144.14(1st c.AD).]]

__IV

[Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd c.AD: Arrianus Historicus “Epicteti Dissertationes” 4.13.19]]; οὐκ ἤφιεν ἵνα.. [NT.Mark.11.16]:—passive, ἀφείθη σχολάζειν[Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Metaphysica” 981b24.]]

__V
seemingly intransitive (i.e. στρατόν, ναῦς, etc.), break up, march, sail, etc., [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 7.193; ἀ. ἐς τὸ πέλαγος 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 7.19; compare 11.2b.]]

__V.2
with infinitive, give up doing, ἀφεὶς σκοπεῖν τὰ δίκαια[Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-3rd c.BC: Diphilus Comicus 94.]]

__B
middle, send forth from oneself, much like active; θορήν[Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 3.101.]]

__B.2

[Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Tyrannus” 1521; τοῦ κοινοῦ τῆς σωτηρίας ἀ. 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 2.60; λόγων 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Gorgias” 458c, 4th c.BC: Aeschines Orator 1.178; μὴ ἀφίεσο τοῦ Θεαιτήτου, ἀλλ᾽ ἐρώτα 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Theaetetus” 146b, etc.; ἀφεῖσθαι τοῦ δικαίου τούτου 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 37.1; ἀφέμενος τῆς ἰαμβικῆς ἰδέας 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Poetica” 1449b8.]]

[Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 8.202]]; frequently also with Preps., ἀ. ἐς.. [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 24.431, 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 4.255, etc.]]; less frequently ἐπί.. [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 10.281, 22.208]]; still more rarely κατά.., ποτί..,[Refs 8th c.BC+ [13.329, 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 6.297; ἀ. πρὸς τέλος γόων 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Coloneus” 1622; ἐπὶ τῶν νήσων 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Historia Graeca (Hellenica)” 5.1.2; ἄχρι τοῦ μὴ πεινῆν ἀ. [prev. author] “Smp.” 4.37; θανάτου τοῦτ᾽ ἐγγυτάτω τοὔπος ἀφῖκται 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Antigone” 934; παρά τινος ἀ. [prev. author] “OT” 935, etc.]]: absolutely, arrive, ὁπποίης ἐπὶ νηὸς ἀφίκεο[Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 1.171; ὅταν ἀ. ὥρη 6th c.BC: Theognis Elegiacus 723; σῖτος ἀφικνούμενος 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 20.31; ὁ ἀφικνούμενος]]the stranger, newcomer, [Refs [Inscriptiones Graecae 12.118.11:]] —Phrases:

__1
ἀ. ἐπὶ or εἰς πάντα, to try every means, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Tyrannus” 265, 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Hippolytus” 284; ἀ. ἐς πᾶσαν βάσανον 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 8.110; ἐς διάπειράν τινος ἀ. come into a certain condition, ἀ. ἐς πᾶν κακοῦ[Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 7.118; ἐς ἀπορίην πολλήν [prev. author] 1.79]]; ἐς τοσοῦτο τύχης, ἐς τοῦτο δυστυχίας, come into such a..,[Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. work] 124, 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 7.86]]; ἐς ὀλίγον ἀ. νικηθῆναι come within little of being conquered, [Refs [Id  4.129]]; εἰς τὸ ἴσον ἀ. τινί attain equality with.., [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 1.4.5; εἰς ὀργήν 4th-3rd c.BC: Menander Comicus “Περικειρομένη” 44]]; elliptically, ἐς ἄνδρ᾽ ἀφίκου reachedst man's estate, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Ion” 322.]]

of intercourse with others, ἀ. τινὶ ἐς λόγους hold converse with one, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 2.28]]; ἐς ἔχθεα, ἐς ἔριν ἀ. τινί, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. author] 3.82, 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Iphigenia Aulidensis” 319]]; διὰ μάχης, δι᾽ ἔχθρας ἀ. τινί, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.169, 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Hippolytus” 1164; διὰ λόγων ἐμαυτῇ [prev. author] “Med.” 872.]]

__4
εἰς τόξευμα ἀ. come within shot, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 1.4.23, etc.]]

__5
of things, ἐς ὀξὺ ἀ. uncertain reading for ἀπηγμένα, -μένας in [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 2.28, 7.64; ὁ λόγος εἰς ταὐτὸν ἀ. 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Ethica Nicomachea” 1097a24, compare 1167a12, +others]]

the sense of return is sometimes implied in the context, but is not inherent in the word, as [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 10.420, 5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “P.” 8.54, 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Electra” 6, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Charmides” 153a.]]

ἀφ-ίστημι
[in LXX for סוּר, מָעַל, etc. (41 words in all) ;]
__1. trans. in pres., impf., fut., 1 aor., to put away, lead away; metaphorically, to move to revolt: Act.5:37.
__2. Intrans. in pf., plpf., 2 aor., to stand off, depart from, withdraw from: with genitive, Luk.2:37; before ἀπό, Luk.4:13 13:27, Act.5:38 12:10 15:38 19:9 22:29, 2Co.12:8; metaphorically, ἀπὸ ἀδικίας, 2Ti.2:19; ἀπὸ θεοῦ, (fall away, apostatize), Heb.3:12 Mid. (exc. 1 aor., WH. is trans.), to withdraw oneself from, absent oneself from: Luk.2:37; metaphorically, fall away, apostatize: absol., Luk.8:13; with genitive, 1Ti.4:1 (MM, see word; Cremer, 308).†
(AS)

---

LSJ / STEPBible (TFLSJ)
ἀφίστημι:
causal in present and imperfect, in future ἀποστήσω, and aorist I ἀπέστησα, as also in aorist I middle (see. below):—put away, remove, keep out of the way, τὸ ἀσθενέστατον τοῦ στρατεύματος[Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Historia Graeca (Hellenica)” 7.5.23; ἄχος 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Choephori” 416 (Lyric poetry)]]; of diseases, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [1st c.AD: Dioscorides (Dioscurides) Medicus 2.96, 2nd c.AD: Galenus Medicus 13.846; τὰ συγκείμενα ἀ. ἀπ᾽ ἀλλήλων 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Politicus” 282b; ἀ. τῆς ἐλάας τὸν φλοιόν 4th-3rd c.BC: Theophrastus Philosophus “de Causis Plantarum” 3.3.2; ἀ. τινὰ λόγου]]hinder from.., [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Iphigenia Taurica” 912]]; ἀ. τὰς τῶν πολεμίων ἐπιβουλάς frustrate them, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 1.93]]; ἀ. τὸν ἄρχοντα depose him, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Historia Graeca (Hellenica)” 7.1.45:]] —aorist middle, Ἀργείων δόρυ πυλῶν ἀπεστήσασθε remoued it from your own gates, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus ph.1087:—in 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 9.23 ἀποστήσαντες, ={ἀποστάντες}]], having retired.

__2
cause to revolt, of allies, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. author] 8.19, 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Equites” 238, 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 1.81; τινὰ ἀπό τινος 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.76, 154, etc.; τινά τινος 5th-6th c.BC: Andocides Orator 3.22.]]

__3
in geometrical constructions, cut off, [Refs 5th c.AD+ [5th c.AD: Proclus Philosophus “Hypotyposis astronomicarum positionum” 6.7.]]

__II
weigh out, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Symposium” 2.20; ἀποστησάτωσαν τὰ χρυσία “IG” 7.303.19 (from Oropus)]]; pay, δραχμὰς ή ἀργυρίου[Refs 2nd c.BC+ [“UPZ” 93.2 (2nd c.BC): also in]]aorist I middle, μὴ.. ἀποστήσωνται Ἀχαιοὶ χρεῖος lest they weigh out (i. e. pay in full) the debt, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 13.745, compare “IG” 12.91.20, +others:]] —in strict sense of middle, ἀποστήσασθαι τὸν χαλκόν to have the brass weighed out to one, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 49.52.— 8th c.BC: Homerus Epicus has it _transitive_ only in [prev. cited]]]

__III
middle, give a final decision (or break up, dismiss the assembly), ῥήτρα cited in [Refs 1st c.AD+ [1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus “Lycurgus” 6.]]

__B
intransitive, in passive, as also in aorist 2 ἀπέστην, imperative ἀπόστηθι[Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Thesmophoriazusae” 627, ἀπόστα 4th-3rd c.BC: Menander Comicus 375:]]perfect ἀφέστηκα in present sense, syncopated. in plural ἀφέστᾰμεν, -στᾰτε, -στᾶσι, as in infinitive ἀφεστάναι, participle ἀφεστώς, -ῶσα, -ός or -ώς: pluperfect ἀφεστήκειν, Attic dialect -κη[Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Theaetetus” 208e]]: future middle ἀποστήσομαι[Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Hecuba” 1054, 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 5.64, etc. (while]]aorist I middle is causal (see. above)): for future ἀφεστήξω see entry .:—stand away or aloof from, keep far from, ὅσσον δὲ τροχοῦ ἵππος ἀφίσταται[Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 23.517; οὐ μέν κ᾽ ἄλλη γ᾽ ὧδε γυνὴ.. ἀνδρὸς ἀφεσταίη 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 23.101; ἀποστᾶσ᾽ ἐκποδών 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Helena” 1023; ἐς ἄλλο σχῆμ᾽ ἀ. βίου [prev. author] “Med.” 1039; ἀποσταθῶμεν πράγματος τελουμένου 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Choephori” 872]]; ὡς γραφεὺς (or βραβεὺς) ἀποσταθείς[Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Hecuba” 807; μακρὰν τόποις καὶ χρόνοις ἀ. 1st c.BC: Diodorus Siculus Historicus 13.22: hence in various relations, ἀφεστάναι φρενῶν]] lose one's wits, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Philoctetes” 865; φύσεος 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Vespae” 1457 (Lyric poetry)]]; οὐδενὸς ἀποστήσονται ὅσα ἂν δίκαια λέγητε depart from, object to right proposals, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 4.118; ἀ. τῶν πραγμάτων, τῆς πολιτείας, etc., withdraw from business, politics, have done with it, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 10.1, 18.308, etc.]]; ἔργων ἢ πόνων ἢ κινδύνων shun them, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Isocrates Orator 4.83, compare 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Historia Graeca (Hellenica)” 7.5.19, etc.]]; __1. adv., utterly (Hom.).
__2. Prep. with genitive, until, unto, as far as;
__(a) of time Act.3:21 22:22, Rom.1:13 5:13, 1Co.4:11, 2Co.3:14, Gal.4:2, Php.1:6; ἄ. καιροῦ, Luk.4:13, Act.13:11; ἄ. ἧς ἡμέρας, Mat.24:38, Luk.1:20 17:27, Act.1:2 (τῆς ἡ. ἧς), Act.1:22; ἄ. ταύτης τ. ἡμέρας (τ. ἡ. ταύτης), Act.2:29 23:1 26:22; ἄ. ἡμερων πέντε, Act.20:6; ἄ. αὐγῆς, Act.20:11; ἄ. τοῦ νῦν, Rom.8:22, Php.1:5; ἄ. τέλους, Heb.6:11, Rev.2:26;
__(b) of space: Act.11:5 13:6 20:4 (R, txt., WH, mg.) Act.28:15, 2Co.10:13-14, Heb.4:12, Rev.14:20 18:5;
__(with) of measure or degree: ἄ. θανάτου, Act.22:4, Rev.2:10 12:11.

__(a) ἄχρι alone: with subj. aor., Gal.3:19 (ἄ. οὗ T, WH, mg.); id. without ἄν (Bl., § 65, 10), Rev.7:3 15:8 20:3, 5; with indic. fut., Rev.17:17;
__(b) ἄ. οὗ (i.e. ἄ.. τούτου ᾧ): with indic. aor., Act.7:18; impf., Act.27:33; with subj. aor. (Bl., ut supr.), Luk.21:24, Rom.11:25, 1Co.11:26 15:25, Gal.3:19, T, WH, mg.; id. with ἄν, Rev.2:25; with indic. pres., while, Heb.3:13 (cf. μέχρι).†

__II
preposition with genitive, even to, as far as,

of Time, until, ἄχρι μάλα κνέφαος until deep in the night, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 18.370; ἄχρι τῆς τήμερον ἡμέρας 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 9.28; ἀπὸ τῆς ἀρχῆς ἄχρι τῆς τελευτῆς [prev. author] 18.179; ἄχρι γήρως 4th-3rd c.BC: Apollodorus Comicus 2]]; ἄχρι δὲ τούτου until then, [NT+6th c.BC+ [6th c.BC: Solon Lyricus 13.35; ἄχρι τοῦ νῦν 2nd c.BC: Timostratus Comicus 1, NT.Rom.8.22; ἄχρι νῦν 2nd c.AD: Lucianus Sophista “Tim.” 39, LXX.Gen.44.28; ἄχρι παντός]]continually, [Refs 1st c.AD+ [1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus “Cicero” 6.]]

of Space, as far as, even to, ἄχρι τῆς ἐσόδου τοῦ ἱροῦ[Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 2.138 (who elsewhere has μέχρι); ἄ. τῆς ὁδοῦ “IG” 12.893; ἄ. τῆς πυλίδος “SIG” 2587.25; ἄ. τοῦ Πειραιῶς 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 18.301; ἔδακνεν ἄχρι τῆς καρδίας “Comica Adespota” 475; ἄχρις ἥπατος 5th-4th c.BC: Timaeus Locrus Philosophus 101a, compare 100e; ἄχρι τῆς πόλεως 1st c.BC: Dionysius Halicarnassensis 2.43; ἄ. τοῦ δεῦρο 2nd c.AD: Galenus Medicus 10.676]]: after its case, ἰνίου ἄχρις[Refs 3rd c.BC+ [3rd c.BC: Euphorio Epicus 41.]]

__III.1
of Time, until, so long as, ἄχρι οὗ ὅδε ὁ λόγος ἐγράφετο[Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Historia Graeca (Hellenica)” 6.4.37; ἄχρις ὅτου “epigram Gr.” 314.24 (from Smyrna)]]; ἄχρι οὗ ἄν or ἄχρι ἄν with Subj., ἄχρι ἂν σχολάσῃ till he should be at leisure, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 2.3.2; ἄχρις οὗ ἂν δοκέῃ 5th c.BC: Hippocrates Medicus “περὶ συρίγγων” 3; ἄχρις ἂν αἱ ἡμέραι παρέλθωσιν [prev. author] “Int.” 40]]; ἄχρι ἂν ἔχῃ τὸ ἴδιον ἐντελές [ἡ ἱστορία] [Refs 2nd c.BC+ [2nd c.AD: Lucianus Sophista “Hist.Conscr.” 9: without ἄν, ἄχρις ῥεύσῃ 2nd c.BC: Bion Bucolicus 1.47]]; ἄχρι οὗ τελευτήσῃ (variant{-σει}) [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.117; ἄχρι οὗ ἐπιλάμψῃ 1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus “Aemilius Paulus” 17]]; ἄχρι ἄν, c.infinitive, Epist.[Refs 1st c.BC+ [1st c.BC: Mithradates Epistolographus in “SIG” 741.37]]: with infinitive only, ἄχρις ἱκέσθαι ὀστέον[Refs 4th c.AD+ [4th c.AD(?): Quintus Smyrnaeus Epicus 4.361.]]

__III.2
of Space, so far as, διώξας, ἄχρι οὗ ἀσφαλὲς ᾤετο εἶναι[Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 5.4.16]]: with subjunctive, αὐξάνεται εἰς μῆκος, ἄχρι οὗ δὴ ἐφίκηται τοῦ ἡλίου[Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-3rd c.BC: Theophrastus Philosophus “Historia Plantarum” 5.1.8]]; compare μέχρι throughout. —Epic dialect poets use ἄχρι or ἄχρις, as the metre requires: in Ionic dialect μέχρι is preferred (see. above): but ἄχρι, -ις are more common in [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Homerus Epicus than μέχρι: the only _Attic dialect_ forms are ἄχρι, μέχρι,]] before both consonants and vowels,[Refs 2nd c.AD+ [compare 2nd c.AD: Phrynichus Atticista 6, 2nd c.AD: Moeris Grammaticus 34]]; and so in Attic dialect Inscrr. (where it is somewhat less frequently than μέχρι): ἄχρι ἄν with hiatus in [Refs 4th c.BC+ [“IG” 2.2729, 3rd c.BC: Hegesippus Comicus 1.26; but ἄχρις 4th-3rd c.BC: Menander Comicus “Σαμία” 179.]] —Never in Trag. (ἄχρι, ={ṃṃ-χρι}, compare μέχρι.)

βαθμ-ός
or βασμός, ὁ, (βαίνω) step, threshold, [LXX+5th c.BC+ [LXX.1Ki.5.5, [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus] “fragment” 1127]]; degree on the dial, [LXX.2Ki.20.9f]; fifteen degrees of the zodiac, [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd c.AD: Vettius Valens Astrologus 31.2]]; interval in a musical scale, [Refs 4th c.AD+ [4th c.AD: Iamblichus Philosophus “de vita Pythagorica” 26.120.]]

__2
rung of a ladder, [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd c.AD: Lucianus Sophista “Trag.” 221.]]

base or plinth of a tower, [Refs [“GDI” 5524.10 (from Cyzicus).]]

__II
metaphorically, step, degree in rank (οἱ β. κλίμακος προκοπὴν σημαίνουσι [NT+2nd c.AD+ [2nd c.AD: Artemidorus Daldianus Onirocriticus 2.42), NT.1Tim.3.13, 6th c.AD: Procopius Caesariensis Historicus “Historia Arcana” 24, 6th c.AD: Lydus, Joannes Laurentius Historicus “Mag.” 2.8, +others; οἱ τᾶς ἀξίας βάσμοι “IG” 12(2).243.16 (Mytil.)]]; simply, degree, τολμημάτων βαθμοί [Refs 1st c.AD+ [1st c.AD: Josephus Historicus “Bellum Judaicum” 4.3.10; ὥσπερ ἡδονῆς κλίμακα συμπηξάμενος ἔρως πρῶτον ἔχει β. ὄψεως 2nd c.AD: Lucianus Sophista “Am.” 53]]; step in an argument, [Refs 6th c.AD+ [6th c.AD: Simplicius Philosophus “in Aristotelis de Caelo commentaria - Comm. in Arist. Graeca” 718.35]]; of a genealogy, ἀπωτέρω δυοῖν β. two steps farther back, i.e. farther back than one's grandfather, [Refs 1st c.AD+ [1st-2nd c.AD: Dio Chrysostomus Sophista 41.6.]]

[prev. author] “Metaphorical” 1020a12]]: with Preps., ἐκ βάθεος in depth, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.186]]; ἐκ βάθους through and through, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [3rd c.AD: Plotinus Philosophus 5.8.10; εἰς βάθος 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Meteorologica” 386a23, +others; ἐν βάθει [prev. author] “Sens.” 440a14, etc.; κατὰ βάθους [prev. author] “Mete.” 339b12]]; κατὰ βάθος in a descending scale, metaphorically of causation, [Refs 5th c.AD+ [5th-6th c.AD: Damascius Philosophus “de Principiis” 95]]: frequently in military sense, depth of a line of battle, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Historia Graeca (Hellenica)” 3.4.13, etc.; ἐπὶ βάθος τάσσεσθαι]]in depth of line, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 5.68; ἐς β. ἐκτάξαι 2nd c.AD: Arrianus Historicus “Anabasis” 1.2.4]]; β. τριχῶν, of long thick hair, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 5.9; ἄτομα πώγωνος βάθη 4th c.BC: Ephippus Comicus 14.7]]; interior of a country, [Refs 1st c.BC+ [1st c.BC-1st c.AD: Strabo Geographus 3.3.7, +others]]; depth, of perspective in a picture, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.AD: Procopius Gazaeus Rhetor “ἔκφρασις ὡρολογίου” p.157 5th c.BC: Bacchylides Lyricus: _plural_, βάθη]]depths, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Timaeus” 44d, etc.]]; deep water, opposed to shallows near shore, [LXX+NT+4th c.BC+ [LXX.Psa.68(69).2, +others, NT.Luke.5.4; ἐν τοῖς βάθεσιν 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Historia Animalium” 599b9.]]

NT.Rom.11.33; β. ἡγεμονίας 1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus “Pompeius” 53]]; depth of mind, β. τι ἔχειν γενναῖον, of Parmenides, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Theaetetus” 184a]]; ἐν βάθει πόσιος deep in drink, [LXX+3rd c.BC+ [3rd c.BC: Theocritus Poeta Bucolicus 14.29; β. καρδίας ἀνθρώπου LXX.Jdt.8.14]]; τὰ β. τοῦ θεοῦ, τοῦ Σατανᾶ, [NT.1Cor.2.10, NT.Rev.2.24.]

deep_entry:

LSJ / STEPBible (TFLSJ)
βᾰθύς, βαθεῖα
Ionic dialect βαθέᾰ, βαθύ; feminine βαθύς [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [3rd c.BC: Callimachus Epicus “Hymnus in Delum” 37, 3rd c.BC: Eratosthenes Epicus 8]]; genitive βαθέος, βαθείας Ionic dialect βαθέης: dative βαθέϊ, βαθείῃ Ionic dialect βαθέῃ: comparative βαθύτερος, poetry βαθίων [ῑ Attic dialect, ῐ [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [3rd c.BC: Theocritus Poeta Bucolicus 5.43], _Doric dialect_ βάσσων (which see): _superlative_ βαθύτατος, poetry βάθιστος]]:—deep or high, accusative to one's position, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Homerus Epicus, etc.]]; βαθέης ἐξάλλεται αὐλῆς a court within a high fence, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 5.142, compare 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 9.239]]; ἠϊόνος προπάροιθε βαθείης the deep, i.e. wide, shore, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 2.92; τάφρος 7.341, +others; κρατήρ 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Fragmenta” 563]]; κύλικες [Refs [[prev. author] “Aj.” 1200 (Lyric poetry)]]; βαθὺ πτῶμα a fall from a high rock, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Supplices” 796]]; πλευρὰ βαθυτάτη (vulgar form βαρυτάτη), of an athlete, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Vespae” 1193]]; of a line of battle, βαθύτεραι φάλαγγες [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Respublica Lacedaemoniorum” 11.6, compare “HG” 2.4.34]]; β. τομή, πληγή, a deep cut, [Refs 1st c.AD+ [1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus 2.131a, 2nd c.AD: Lucianus Sophista “Nigr.” 35.]]

__2
deep or thick in substance, of a mist, ἠέρα βαθεῖαν [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 21.7, compare 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 9.144]]; of sand, ἀμάθοιο βαθείης [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 5.587; ἐπὶ θῖνα βαθύν 3rd c.BC: Theocritus Poeta Bucolicus 22.32]]; of ploughed land, νειοῖο βαθείης [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 10.353]]; β. γῆ, opposed to to stony ground, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Andromache” 637, 4th-3rd c.BC: Theophrastus Philosophus “de Causis Plantarum” 1.18.1]]; of luxuriant growth, deep, thick, of woods, etc., βαθείης τάρφεσιν ὕλης [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 5.555; βαθείης ἐκ ξυλόχοιο 11.415; βαθὺ λήϊον 2.147, 6th c.BC: Theognis Elegiacus 107; τοῦ ληΐου τὸ.. βαθύτατον 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 5.92. ; λειμών 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Prometheus Vinctus” 652; σῖτος 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Historia Graeca (Hellenica)” 3.2.17; χλόα 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Hippolytus” 1139 (Lyric poetry)]]; χαίτη, τρίχες, πώγων, [Refs 7th c.BC+ [7th-6th c.BC(?): Semonides Iambographus 7.66, 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Cynegeticus” 4.8, 2nd c.AD: Lucianus Sophista “Pisc.” 41.]]

__2.b
deep, of colour, [Refs [“PHolm.” 21.9]]: comparative, [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd-3rd c.AD: Aelianus “Varia Historia” 6.6, 6th c.AD: Lydus, Joannes Laurentius Historicus “Mag.” 2.13, πορφύριον -ύτερον “PLond.” 3.899.4 (2nd c.AD).]]

__3
of quality, strong, violent, βαθείῃ λαίλαπι [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 11.306.]]

__3.b
generally, copious, abundant, β. κλᾶρος [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “O.” 13.62]]; β. ἀνήρ a rich man, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Oeconomicus” 11.10; β. οἶκος 3rd c.BC: Callimachus Epicus “Hymnus in Cererem” 113; β. πλοῦτος 2nd-3rd c.AD: Aelianus “Varia Historia” 3.18, 4th c.AD: Julianus Imperator “Orationes” 2.82b]]; β. χρέος deep debt, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “O.” 10(11).8; στεφάνων β. τέρψις 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Ajax” 1200 (Lyric poetry); β. κλέος 5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “O.” 7.53; κίνδυνος [prev. author] “P.” 4.207]]; β. ὕπνος deep sleep, [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [3rd c.BC: Theocritus Poeta Bucolicus 8.65, “Anthologia Graeca” 7.170, compare 2nd c.AD: Lucianus Sophista “DMar.” 2.3; εἰρήνη [prev. author] “Tox.” 36; σιωπή 2nd c.AD: Appianus Historicus “Μιθριδάτειος” 99, “BC” 4.109 (_superlative_).]]

__4
of the mind, ἄχος ὀξὺ κατὰ φρένα τύψε β. in the depths of his soul, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 19.125]]; but also, profound, φρήν [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “N.” 4.8; φροντίς 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Supplices” 407; μέριμνα 5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “O.” 2.60; βαθεῖαν ἄλοκα διὰ φρενὸς καρπούμενος 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Septem contra Thebas” 593; μουσικὴ πρᾶγμ᾽ ἐστὶ β. 5th c.BC: Eupolis Comicus 336]]; βαθύτερα ἤθη more sedate natures, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Leges” 930a]] (but, more recondite, i.e. civilized, manners, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 4.95)]]: of persons, deep, wise, β. τῇ φύσει στρατηγός [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [3rd c.BC: Posidippus Comicus 27.4; ταῖς ψυχαῖς 2nd c.BC: Polybius Historicus 6.24.9]]; also, deep, crafty, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-3rd c.BC: Menander Comicus 1001; ἦθος 1st c.AD: Philo Judaeus 2.468.]]

__5
of time, β. ὄρθρος dim twilight, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Vespae” 216, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Crito” 43a, etc.]]; β. νύξ a late hour in the night, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [2nd c.AD: Lucianus Sophista “Asin.” 34; περὶ ἑσπέραν β. 1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus 2.179e, compare 2nd c.AD: Pausanias Periegeta 4.18.3; βαθὺ τῆς ἡλικίας 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Nubes” 514]]; β. γῆρας conjecture in [Refs 5th c.BC+ [“Anthologia Graeca” 7.163 (1st c.AD: Leonidas Alexandrinus Epigrammaticus), compare 4th-5th c.AD: Eunapius Historicus “Vitae Sophistarum” p.457 5th c.BC: Bacchylides Lyricus, +others; β. ὥρα ἔτους 2nd c.AD(?): Charito Scriptor Eroticus 1.7.]]

__II
adverb -έως[Refs 3rd c.BC+ [3rd c.BC: Theocritus Poeta Bucolicus 8.66]]; profoundly, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.AD: Proclus Philosophus “in Platonis Parmenidem commentarii” p.475 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus]]: superlative βαθύτατα, γηρῶν [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd-3rd c.AD: Aelianus “Varia Historia” 2.36. (bṇqu/s, compare βένθος.)]]

__II
javelin (as if from βάλλω), a pun in [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [Dionysius Epigrammaticus cited in 2nd c.AD: Athenaeus Epigrammaticus 3.98d]]. (The spelling βαλλ-is better attested than that with βαλ-,[Refs 5th c.BC+ [compare 1st c.BC: Philodemus Gadarensis Epigrammaticus “Rh.” 1.354 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus, etc.]]; compare βαλλαντιοτομέω, -τόμος.)
source_notes: STEPBible TBESG (CC BY), STEPBible TFLSJ (CC BY)

short_definition: to throw: throw — βάλλω, — to throw: put — βάλλω, — to throw: sow — βάλλω, — to throw: pour — βάλλω, — to throw: hit — βάλλω,
deep_entry:
Abbott-Smith / STEPBible (TBESG)
βάλλω,
[in LXX for נפל, שׂום, ידד, etc. ;]
prop., of a weapon or missile; then generally, of things and persons, lit. and metaphorically, to throw, cast, put, place: with accusative, before εἰς, Mat.4:18, and frequently ἐπί, Mat.10:34; κάτω, Mat.4:6; ἔξω, Mat.5:13; ἀπό, Mat.5:29; ἐκ, Mrk.12:44; δρέπανον, Rev.14:19; μάχαιραν, Mat.10:34; κλῆρον, Mat.27:35; of fluids, to pour: Mat.9:17, Jhn.13:5; pass., to be laid, to lie ill: Mat.9:2; ἐβλήθη (timeless aor., M, Pr., 134), Jhn.15:6; intrans., to rush (Bl., §53, 1): Act.27:14. Metaphorical, β. εἰς τ. καρδίαν, Jhn.13:2 (cf. usage in π., without idea of violence; also of liquids; MM, Exp., x; see also Cremer, 120, 657; cf. ἀμφι-, ἀνα-, ἀντι-, ἀπο-, δια-, ἐκ-, ἐμ-, παρ-εμ-, ἐπι-, κατα-, μετα-, παρα-, περι-, προ-, συμ-, ὑπερ-, ὑπο-βάλλω).
(AS)

---

LSJ / STEPBible (TFLSJ)
βάλλω,
future βᾰλῶ (in Attic dialect Prose only in compounds), Ionic dialect βαλέω [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 8.403, βαλλήσω 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Vespae” 222, 1491:]]aorist 2 ἔβᾰλον, Ionic dialect προ-βάλεσκε [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 5.331]]; later aorist 1 ἔβαλα [LXX.3Ki.6.1 (5.18)]; Epic dialect and Ionic dialect infinitive βαλέειν [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 2.414, +others, 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 2.111, +others, but βαλεῖν 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 13.387, 14.424]]; optative βλείης in [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Epicharmus Comicus 219]], participle βλείς [Refs [[prev. author] 176, as if from ἔβλην (see. συμβάλλω):]]perfect βέβληκα: pluperfect ἐβεβλήκειν, Epic dialect βεβλήκειν [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 5.661]]:—middle, Ionic dialect imperfect βαλλέσκετο [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 9.74:]]future βᾰλοῦμαι (προ-) [Refs 8th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Ranae” 201, (ἐπι-) 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 6.40, etc., _Epic dialect_ βαλεῦμαι (ἀμφι-) 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 22.103:]]aorist 2 ἐβᾰλόμην, Ionic dialect imperative βαλεῦ [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 8.68.γ,]] used mostly in compounds:—passive, future βληθήσομαι [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Historia Graeca (Hellenica)” 7.5.11, (δια-) 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Hecuba” 863; also βεβλήσομαι [prev. author] “Or.” 271, 3rd c.AD: Heliodorus Scriptor Eroticus 2.13, (δια-) 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 16.2]]; participle δια-βεβλησόμενος [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd-3rd c.AD: Philostratus Sophista “Vita Apollonii” 6.13 (_Epic dialect_ _future_ ξυμ-βλήσομαι, see at {συμβάλλω})]]: aorist ἐβλήθην [Refs 8th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.34, 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 8.84, etc.: 8th c.BC: Homerus Epicus]] also has an Epic dialect aorist passive, ἔβλητο [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 11.675, ξύμβλητο 14.39]]; subjunctive βλήεται [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 17.472]]; optative βλῇο or βλεῖο [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 13.288]]; infinitive βλῆσθαι [Refs [4.115]]; participle βλήμενος [Refs [15.495:]]perfect βέβλημαι, Ionic dialect 3rd.pers. plural βεβλήαται [Refs [11.657]] (but 3rd.pers. singular [Refs 5th c.BC+ [“hymnus ad Apollinem” 20), _optative_ δια-βεβλῇσθε 5th-6th c.BC: Andocides Orator 2.24:]]pluperfect ἐβεβλήμην (περι-) [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Historia Graeca (Hellenica)” 7.4.22, (ἐξ-) 5th-6th c.BC: Isocrates Orator 18.17]]; Ionic dialect 3rd.pers. plural περι-εβεβλέατο [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 6.25.]] — _Epic dialect_ perfect βεβόλημαι in special sense, see at {βολέω}.

__A
active, throw:

__I
with accusative of person or thing aimed at, throw so as to hit, hit with a missile, frequently opposed to striking with a weapon in the hand, βλήμενος ἠὲ τυπείς [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 15.495; τὸν βάλεν, οὐδ᾽ ἀφάμαρτε 11.350, compare 4.473, +others]]; so even in ἐγγύθεν ἐλβὼν βεβλήκει.. δουρί [Refs [5.73; and δουρὶ ὤμων μεσσηγὺς σχεδόθεν βάλε 16.807]]; but later opposed to τοξεύειν, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 9.17, 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 4.2.12; ἐκ χειρὸς β. [prev. work] 3.3.15: with _dative_ instrumenti, β. τινὰ δουρί, πέτρῳ, κεραυνῷ, etc., 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 13.518, 20.288, 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 5.128, etc.: βλήμενος ἢ ἰῷ ἢ ἔγχεϊ 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 8.514: with double _accusative_ _person_ et partis, μιν βάλε μηρὸν ὀϊστῷ 11.583: with _accusative_ partis only, 5.19, 657]]; so τὸν δ᾽ Ὀδυσεὺς κατὰ λαιμὸν.. βάλεν ἰῷ [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 22.15; δουρὶ βαλὼν πρὸς στῆθος 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 11.144: with _accusative_ _cognate_, ἕλκος.., τό μιν βάλε Πάνδαρος ἰῷ 5.795]]; also βάλε Τυδεΐδαο κατ᾽ ἀσπίδα smote upon it, [Refs [[prev. work] 281.]]

__I.2
less frequently of things, ἡνίοχον κονίης ῥαθάμιγγες ἔβαλλον [Refs [23.502]]; of drops of blood,[Refs 5th c.BC+ [11.536, compare 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Agamemnon” 1390: _metaphorically_, κηλὶς ἔβαλέ νιν μητροκτόνος 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Iphigenia Taurica” 1200, compare “HF” 1219]]; of the sun, ἀκτῖσιν ἔβαλλεν [θάμνους] [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 5.479; ἔβαλλε.. οὐρανὸν Ἠώς 3rd c.BC: Apollonius Rhodius Epicus 4.885]] (so passive, σελήνη.. δι᾽ εὐτρήτων βαλλομένη θυρίδων [Refs 1st c.BC+ [“Anthologia Graeca” 5.122 (1st c.BC: Philodemus Gadarensis Epigrammaticus))]]; strike the senses, of sound, ἵππων ὠκυπόδων ἀμφὶ κτύπος οὔατα βάλλει [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 10.535, compare 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Antigone” 1188, “Ph.” 205 (Lyric poetry)]]; of smell, ὀσμὴ β. τινά [Refs [[prev. author] “Ant.” 412; τάχ᾽ ἂν πέμφιξ σε βροντῆς καὶ δυσοσμίας β. [prev. author] “fragment” 538.]]

__I.3
metaphorically, β. τινὰ κακοῖς, φθόνῳ, ψόγῳ, smite with reproaches, etc., [Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. author] “Aj.” 1244, 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Electra” 902, 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Thesmophoriazusae” 895; στεφάνοις β. τινά 5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “P.” 8.57]] (hence metaphorically, praise, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [[prev. author] “O.” 2.98); φθόνος βάλλει 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Agamemnon” 947; φίλημα βάλλει τὴν καρδίαν 3rd c.AD(?): Achilles Tatius Astronomus 2.37.]]

__II
with accusative of the weapon thrown, cast, hurl, of missiles, rare in [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Homerus Epicus, βαλὼν βέλος 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 9.495; χαλκὸν ἐνὶ στήθεσσι βαλών 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 5. 346, compare 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 20.62; ἐν νηυσὶν.. πῦρ β. 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 13.629]]: with dative, of the weapon, throw or shoot with a thing, οἱ δ᾽ ἄρα χερμαδίοισι.. βάλλον [Refs 8th c.BC+ [12.155; βέλεσι 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 16.277: in Prose _absolutely_, β. ἐπί τινα]] throw at one, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 8.75; ἐπὶ σκοπόν 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 1.6.29; ἐπίσκοπα 2nd c.AD: Lucianus Sophista “Am.” 16; alone, οἱ ψιλοὶ βάλλοντες εἶργον 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 4.33: with _genitive_, βάλλοντα τοῦ σκοποῦ]] hitting the mark, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Sisyphus” 391a.]]

__II.2
generally of anything thrown, εἰς ἅλα λύματ᾽ ἔβαλλον [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 1.314; τὰ μὲν ἐν πυρὶ βάλλε 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 14.429; [νῆα] β. ποτὶ πέτρας 12.71]]; εὐνὰς β. throw out the anchor-stones, [Refs [9.137]]; β. σπόρον cast the seed, [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [3rd c.BC: Theocritus Poeta Bucolicus 25.26; β. κόπρον “POxy.” 934.9 (3rd c.AD): hence β. ἀρούρας]]manure, [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [PFay. 118.21 (2nd c.AD)]]: metaphorically, ὕπνον.. ἐπὶ βλεφάροις β. [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 1.364; β. σκότον ὄμμασι 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Phoenissae” 1535 (Lyric poetry); β. λύπην τινί 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Philoctetes” 67.]]

__II.2.b
of persons, β. τινὰ ἐν κονίῃσιν, ἐν δαπέδῳ, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 8.156, 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 22.188; γῆς ἔξω β. 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Tyrannus” 622; β. τινὰ ἄθαπτον [prev. author] “Aj.” 1333; ἄτιμον [prev. author] “Ph.” 1028]]:—passive, ὑπὸ χλαίνῃ βεβλημένος [Refs 1st c.BC+ [“Anthologia Graeca” 5.164 (1st c.BC: Meleager Epigrammaticus); βεβλημένος]]on a sick-bed, [NT+8th c.BC+ [NT.Matt.8.14: then _metaphorically_, ἐς κακὸν β. τινά 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 12.221; ὅς με μετ᾽.. ἔριδας καὶ νείκεα β. 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 2.376]]; β. τινὰ ἐς ἔχθραν, ἐς φόβον, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Prometheus Vinctus” 390, 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Troades” 1058]]; also ἐν αἰτίᾳ or αἰτίᾳ β. τινά, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Tyrannus” 657, “Tr.” 940 (but in 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Troades” 305 β. αἰτίαν ἔς τινα); κινδύνῳ β. τινά 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Septem contra Thebas” 1053.]]

__II.3
let fall, ἑτέρωσε κάρη βάλεν [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 8.306, compare 23.697; β. ἀπὸ δάκρυ παρειῶν 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 4.198, compare 114; κατὰ βλεφάρων β. δάκρυα 6th c.BC: Theognis Elegiacus 1206; κατ᾽ ὄσσων 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Hippolytus” 1396; αἵματος πέμφιγα πρὸς πέδῳ β. 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Fragmenta - American Journal of Philology” 183]]; β. τοὺς ὀδόντας cast, shed them, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Historia Animalium” 501b2, etc.]]; so βάλλειν alone,[Refs [[prev. work] 576a4; βοῦς βεβληκώς “SIG” 958.7 (from Ceos).]]

__II.4
of the eyes, ἑτέρωσε βάλ᾽ ὄμματα cast them, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 16.179; ὄμματα πρὸς γῆν 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Ion” 582; πρόσωπον εἰς γῆν [prev. author] “Or.” 958: _intransitive_, ὀφθαλμὸς πρὸς τὸ φῶς βαλών]] aiming at.., [Refs 3rd c.AD+ [3rd c.AD: Plotinus Philosophus 2.4.5]]; βαλὼν πρὸς αὐτό directing one's gaze at.., [Refs [[prev. author] 3.8.10.]]

__II.5
of animals, push forward or in front, τοὺς σοὺς [ἵππους] πρόσθε βαλών [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 23.572]]; πλήθει πρόσθε βαλόντες (i.e. ἵππους)[Refs 3rd c.BC+ [[prev. work] 639; βάλλε κάτωθε τὰ μοσχία 3rd c.BC: Theocritus Poeta Bucolicus 4.44: _metaphorically_, β. ψυχὰν ποτὶ κέρδεα 2nd c.BC: Bion Bucolicus “fragment” 5.12.]]

__II.6
in a looser sense, put, place, with or without a notion of haste, τὼ μὲν.. βαλέτην ἐν χερσὶν ἑταίρων [NT+8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 5.574, compare 17.40, 21.104; μῆλα.. ἐν νηΐ β. 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 9.470; ἐπὶ γᾶν ἴχνος ποδὸς β. 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Rhesus” 721 (Lyric poetry); φάσγανον ἐπ᾽ αὐχένος β. [prev. author] “Or.” 51; τοὺς δακτύλους εἰς τὰ ὦτα NT.Mark.7.33]]; β. πλίνθους lay bricks, [Refs [“Edict.Diocl.” 7.15]]; pour, οἶνον εἰς ἀσκούς [NT+1st c.AD+ [NT.Matt.9.17; εἰς πίθον 2nd c.AD: Arrianus Historicus “Epicteti Dissertationes” 4.13.12, compare 1st c.AD: Dioscorides (Dioscurides) Medicus 1.71.5 (variant for{ἐμβ}.)]]: metaphorically, ἐν στήθεσσι μένος βάλε ποιμένι λαῶν [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 5.513]]; ὅπως.. φιλότητα μετ᾽ ἀμφοτέροισι βάλωμεν may put friendship between them,[Refs 8th c.BC+ [4.16; μαντεύσομαι ὡς ἐνὶ θυμῷ ἀθάνατοι βάλλουσι 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 1.201; ἐν καρδίᾳ β. 5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “O.” 13.16]]; but also θυμῷ, ἐς θυμὸν β., lay to heart, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Prometheus Vinctus” 706, 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Tyrannus” 975.]]

__II.6.b
especially of putting round, ἀμφ᾽ ὀχέεσσι θοῶς βάλε καμπύλα κύκλα [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 5.722]]; of clothes or arms, ἀμφὶ δ᾽ Ἀθήνη ὤμοις.. βάλ᾽ αἰγίδα [Refs [18.204]]; put on, φαιὰ ἱμάτια [Refs 2nd c.BC+ [2nd c.BC: Polybius Historicus 30.4.5.]]

__II.6.c
place money on deposit, ἀργύριον τοῖς τραπεζίταις [NT.Matt.25.27.]

__II.6.d
pay, [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [PLond. 3.1177 (2nd c.AD), “POxy.” 1448.5 (4th c.AD).]]

__II.7
of dice, throw, τρὶς ἓξ βαλεῖν [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Agamemnon” 33, compare 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Leges” 968e; ἄλλα βλήματ᾽ ἐν κύβοις βαλεῖν 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Supplices” 330: so probably ψῆφος βαλοῦσα,]] absolutely, by its throw, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Eumenides” 751]]: metaphorically, εὖ or καλῶς βάλλειν to be lucky, successful, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [1st c.BC: Philodemus Gadarensis Epigrammaticus lr. p.51 W., “Rh.” 1.10 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus]]

__III
intransitive, fall, ποταμὸς Μινυήϊος εἰς ἅλα βάλλων [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 11.722, compare 3rd c.BC: Apollonius Rhodius Epicus 2.744, etc.]]; ἄνεμος κατ᾽ αὐτῆς (i.e. νεώς) ἔβαλε [NT.Act.27.14]; [ἵππους] περὶ τέρμα βαλούσας having run round the post, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 23.462]]; ἐγὼ δὲ.. τάχ᾽ ἐν πέδῳ βαλῶ (i.e. ἐμαυτήν) [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Agamemnon” 1172 (Lyric poetry)]]; λίμνηθεν ὅτ᾽ εἰς ἁλὸς οἶδμα βάλητε arrive at.., [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [3rd c.BC: Apollonius Rhodius Epicus 4.1579]]; εἴσω β. enter a river's mouth, Oracle texts cited in [Refs 1st c.BC+ [1st c.BC: Diodorus Siculus Historicus 8.23]]; βαλὼν κάθευδε lie down and sleep, [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd c.AD: Arrianus Historicus “Epicteti Dissertationes” 2.20.10]]; τί οὖν, οὐ ῥέγκω βαλών[Refs 4th c.BC+ [; [prev. work] 4.10.29; βαλὼν ἐπὶ τῆς στιβάδος ἐπεχείρει καθεύδειν Anonymus cited in “POxy.” 1368.51; compare 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus 11.4.]]

__III.2
in familiar language, βάλλ᾽ ἐς κόρακας away with you! be hanged! [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Vespae” 835, etc.; βάλλ᾽ ἐς μακαρίαν 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Hp.Ma.” 293a, compare 4th-3rd c.BC: Menander Comicus “Ἐπιτρέποντες” 389.]]

__B
middle, put for oneself, ὡς ἐνὶ θυμῷ βάλλεαι that thou may'st lay it to heart, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 20.196, compare 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 12.218; σὺ δ᾽ ἐνὶ φρεσὶ βάλλεο σῇσιν 8th-7th c.BC: Hesiodus Epicus “Opera et Dies” 107; εἰ μὲν δὴ νόστον γε μετὰ φρεσὶ.. βάλλεαι 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 9.435; ἐς θυμὸν βαλέσθαι τι 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.84, etc.]]; εἰς or ἐπὶ νοῦν, εἰς μνήμην, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus “Theseus” 24, 4th c.AD: Julianus Imperator “Orationes” 2.58a, etc. (see. above 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus 11.6)]]; ἐπ᾽ ἑωυτῶν βαλόμενοι on their own responsibility, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 4.160, compare 3.71, +others]]; ἑτέρως ἐβάλοντο θεοί, see l. for ἐβόλοντο in [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 1.234; θεοὶ δ᾽ ἑτέρωσε βάλοντο 4th c.AD(?): Quintus Smyrnaeus Epicus 1.610.]]

__B.2
τόξα or ξίφος ἀμφ᾽ ὤμοισιν βάλλεσθαι throw about one's shoulder, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 10.333, 19.372, etc.; ἐπὶ κάρα στέφη β. 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Iphigenia Aulidensis” 1513 (Lyric poetry).]]

__B.3
ἐς γαστέρα βάλλεσθαι γόνον conceive, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 3.28.]]

__B.4

βάπτω,
future βάψω (ἐμ-) [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Pax” 959]]: aorist ἔβαψα [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Ajax” 95, etc.]]:— middle, future βάψομαι [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Lysistrata” 51]]: aorist ἐβαψάμην [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-3rd c.BC: Aratus Epicus 951, “Anthologia Graeca” 9.326 (1st c.AD: Leonidas Alexandrinus Epigrammaticus)]]:—passive, future βᾰφήσομαι [LXX+2nd c.AD+ [LXX.Lev.11.32, 2nd c.AD: Marcus Antoninus Imperator 8.51]]: aorist ἐβάφθην [Refs 5th c.BC+ [“Anthologia Graeca” 6.254 (Myrinus Epigrammaticus), (ἀπ-) 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Fragmenta” 416]]; in Attic dialect generally ἐβάφην [ᾰ] [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 429e, etc.]]: perfect βέβαμμαι [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 7.67, 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Pax” 1176.]]

__I
transitive, dip, ὡς δ᾽ ὅτ᾽ ἀνὴρ χαλκεὺς πέλεκυν.. εἰν ὕδατι ψυχρῷ βάπτῃ (so as to temper the red-hot steel) [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 9.392; β. εἰς ὕδωρ 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Timaeus” 73e, compare 5th c.BC: Empedocles Poeta Philosophus 100.11; τἄρια θερμῷ 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Ecclesiazusae” 216]]; εἰς μέλι, εἰς κηρόν, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Historia Animalium” 605a29, “de An.” 435a2:]] —passive, βαπτόμενος σίδηρος iron in process of being tempered, [Refs 1st c.AD+ [1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus 2.136a]]; and of coral, become hard, [Refs 1st c.AD+ [1st c.AD: Dioscorides (Dioscurides) Medicus 5.121 (assuming variant).]]

__I.b
of slaughter in Trag, ἐν σφαγαῖσι βάψασα ξίφος [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Prometheus Vinctus” 863; ἔβαψας ἔγχος εὖ πρὸς Ἀργείων στρατ; 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Ajax” 95; φάσγανον εἴσω σαρκὸς ἔβαψεν 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Phoenissae” 1578 (Lyric poetry)]]; in later Prose, εἰς τὰ πλευρὰ β. τὴν αἰχμήν [LXX+1st c.BC+ [1st c.BC: Dionysius Halicarnassensis 5.15; β. τὸν δάκτυλον ἀπὸ τοῦ αἵματος LXX.Lev.4.17.]]

__I.c
also, dip in poison, ἔβαψεν ἰούς [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Trachiniae” 574; χιτῶνα τόνδ᾽ ἔβαψα [prev. work] 580.]]

__I.2
dye, ἔβαψεν.. ξίφος the sword dyed [the robe] red, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Choephori” 1011]]; β. τὰ κάλλη dye the beautiful cloths, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Eupolis Comicus 333; β. ἔρια ὥστ᾽ εἶναι ἁλουργά 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 429d; εἵματα βεβαμμένα 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 7.67; τρίχας βάπτειν “Anthologia Graeca” 11.68 (1st c.AD: Lucillius Epigrammaticus)]]: absolutely in middle, dye the hair, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-3rd c.BC: Menander Comicus 363.4, 4th c.BC(?): Nicolaus Comicus 1.33]]; glaze earthen vessels, [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd c.AD: Athenaeus Epigrammaticus 11.480e]]; of gilding and silvering, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [2nd c.AD: Pseudo-Democritus Alchemista Alch. p.46 5th c.BC: Bacchylides Lyricus: Comedy texts, βάπτειν τινὰ βάμμα Σαρδιανικόν]] dye one in the [red] dye of Sardes, i. e. give him a bloody coxcomb, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Acharnenses” 112]]; but βέβαπται β. Κυζικηνικόν he has been dyed in the dye of Cyzicus, i. e. is an arrant coward, [Refs [[prev. author] “Pax” 1176 (see. Scholia).]]

__I.3
draw water by dipping a vessel, ἀνθ᾽ ὕδατος τᾷ κάλπιδι κηρία βάψαι [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [3rd c.BC: Theocritus Poeta Bucolicus 5.127]]; ἀρύταιναν.. ἐκ μέσου βάψασα τοῦ λέβητος ζέοντος ὕδατος draw water by dipping the bucket, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Antiphanes Comicus 25, compare 4th-3rd c.BC: Theophrastus Philosophus “Characteres” 9.8]]; βάψασα ποντίας ἁλός (i.e. τὸ τεῦχος) having dipped it so as to draw water from the sea, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Hecuba” 610.]]

__I.4
baptize, [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd c.AD: Arrianus Historicus “Epicteti Dissertationes” 2.9.20 (_passive_).]]

__II
intransitive, ναῦς ἔβαψεν the ship dipped, sank, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Orestes” 707]]; β. εἰς ψυχρὸν [αἱ ἐγχέλυς] [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Historia Animalium” 592a18]]; εἰ δ᾽ ὁ μὲν (i.e. ἠέλιος) ἀνέφελος βάπτοι ῥόου ἑσπερίοιο [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-3rd c.BC: Aratus Epicus 858 (ῥόον Scholia): with _accusative_, νῆα.. βάπτουσαν ἤδη κῦμα κυρτόν]] dipping into.., [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd c.AD: Babrius Fabularum Scriptor 71.2]]:—also middle, ποταμοῖο ἐβάψατο [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-3rd c.BC: Aratus Epicus 951.]]

__II.2
βάψας (i.e. τὴν κώπην) [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Fragmenta” 225]]. (Cf. O Norse kuefia 'dip'.)

βάρβᾰρος, ον,
barbarous, i.e. non-Greek, foreign, not in [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Homerus Epicus (but compare βαρβαρόφωνος); β. ψυχαί 1st c.AD(?): Heraclitus 107]]; especially as substantive βάρβαροι, οἱ, originally all non-Greek-speaking peoples, then specially of the Medes and Persians, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Persae” 255, 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.58, etc.: generally, opposed to Ἕλληνες, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Politicus” 262d, compare 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 1.3, 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Politica” 1252b5, 1st c.BC-1st c.AD: Strabo Geographus 14.2.28; βαρβάρων Ἕλληνας ἄρχειν εἰκός 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Iphigenia Aulidensis” 1400; β. καὶ δοῦλον ταὐτὸ φύσει 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Politica” 1252b9; οἱ β. δουλικώτεροι τὰ ἤθη φύσει τῶν Ἑλλήνων [prev. work] 1285a20]]; β. πόλεμον war with the barbarians, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 2.36 codices]]; ἡ βάρβαρος (i.e. γῆ), opposed to αἱ Ἑλληνίδες πόλεις, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 2.97, compare 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Persae” 187, 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 5.5.16.]] adverb -ρως, opposed to Ἑλληνικῶς,[Refs 3rd c.AD+ [3rd c.AD: Porphyrius Tyrius Philosophus “de Abstinentia - Porphyrii Opuscula” 3.3.]]

LSJ / STEPBible (TFLSJ)
βᾰρύς, εῖα, ύ,
poetry genitive plural feminine βαρεῶν uncertain in [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Eumenides” 932 (_anapaest meter_): _comparative_ βαρύτερος, _superlative_ βαρύτατος]]:— heavy in weight, β. ἀείρεσθαι, opposed to κοῦφος, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 4.150, compare 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Theaetetus” 152d, 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “de Caelo” 310b25, etc.: in 8th c.BC: Homerus Epicus]] mostly with collateral notion of strength and force, χεῖρα βαρεῖαν [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 1.219, compare 89; ἀκμᾷ βαρύς 5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “I.” 4(3).51; β. τὸ σῶμα 2nd c.AD: Appianus Historicus “Μακεδονική” 14]]; of athletes, [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd-3rd c.AD: Philostratus Sophista “de gymnastica” 31]]; ὀφρύς bushy, [Refs [[prev. work] 48]]; but also, heavy with age, infirmity or suffering, νόσῳ [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Trachiniae” 235; σὺν γήρᾳ [prev. author] “OT” 17; ἐν γήρᾳ [prev. author] “Aj.” 1017; ὑπὸ γήρως 2nd-3rd c.AD: Aelianus “Varia Historia” 9.1; ὑπὸ τῆς μέθης 1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus 2.596a]]; pregnant, [Refs 4th c.AD+ [PGoodsp.Cair. 15.15 (4th c.AD)]]; β. βάσις heavy, slow, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Trachiniae” 966; τυπάδι βαρείᾳ [prev. author] “fragment” 844]]. adverb κοῦφον βαρέως [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Theaetetus” 189d.]]

__2
heavy to bear, grievous, ἄτη, ἔρις, κακότης, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 2.111, 20.55, 10.72; Κλῶθες 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 7.197; κῆρες 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 21.548; β. κὴρ τὸ μὴ πιθέσθαι 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Agamemnon” 206 (Lyric poetry)]]; βαρὺ or βαρέα στενάχειν sob heavily, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 8.95, 534, 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 8.334, etc.]]: in Trag. and Prose, burdensome, grievous, oppressive, β. ξυμφορά, τύχαι, καταλλαγαί, etc., [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Persae” 1044 (Lyric poetry), “Th.” 332 (Lyric poetry), 767 (Lyric poetry), etc.; ἡδονή 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Coloneus” 1204; ἀγγελία β. ἢν ἐν τοῖς βαρύτατ᾽ ἂν ἐνέγκαιμι 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Crito” 43c; πόλεμος 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 18.241; βαρὺ κοὐχὶ δίκαιον [prev. author] 21.66; νόσος]]causing disgust, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Philoctetes” 1330; αὐδά, ἠχώ, [prev. work] 208 (Lyric poetry), 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Hippolytus” 791]]; unwholesome, χωρίον [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Memorabilia” 3.6.12; πλησμονή [prev. author] “Cyn.” 7.4]]; indigestible, [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd c.AD: Athenaeus Epigrammaticus 3.115e; β. νότος 2nd c.AD: Pausanias Periegeta 10.17.11.]] adverb -έως, φέρειν τι take a thing ill, suffer it impatiently, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 5.19; β. φέρειν ἐπί τινι 2nd c.BC: Polybius Historicus 15.1.1 (but β. φέρειν]] bear with dignity, [Refs 1st c.BC+ [1st c.BC: Diodorus Siculus Historicus 26.3)]]; β. ἔχειν, with part, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Rhetorica ad Alexandrum” 1424b5; πρός τι [prev. author] “Pol.” 1311b9]]; τοῖς λογίοις [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Arg. Euripides Tragicus “Heracl.”]]: comparative βαρυτέρως τινὶ ἐναντιωθῆναι [LXX.3Mac.3.1]; βαρέως ἀκούειν hear with disgust, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 2.1.9.]]

__3
violent, ὀργή [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Philoctetes” 368; μῆνις [prev. author] “OC” 1328; ἀπέχθειαι 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Apologia” 23a (_superlative_)]]; θυμός [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [3rd c.BC: Theocritus Poeta Bucolicus 1.96.]]

__4
weighty, grave, ἐπιστολαί [NT.2Cor.10.10; αἰτιώματα NT.Act.25.7; τὰ βαρύτερα τοῦ νόμου NT.Matt.23.23]; ample, βαρυτάτην εὐδαιμονίαν τοῖς ἀρχομένοις παρέξειν [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd c.AD: Herodianus Grammaticus 2.14.3.]]

__II
of persons, severe, stern, β. ἐπιτιμητής [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Prometheus Vinctus” 77; εὔθυνος [prev. author] “Pers.” 828, compare 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Tyrannus” 546; Κύπρι βαρεῖα 3rd c.BC: Theocritus Poeta Bucolicus 1.100]]; wearisome, troublesome, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Supplices” 894, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Theaetetus” 210c, etc.; ξύνοικος 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Supplices” 415, 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Fragmenta” 753; γείτονες 2nd c.BC: Polybius Historicus 1.10.6.]]

__II.2
overbearing, σεμνότεροι ἢ βαρύτεροι [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Rhetorica” 1391a27 (but σεμνὸς καὶ β. 1st c.BC-1st c.AD: Strabo Geographus 14.1.42); ὑπερήφανοι καὶ β. 1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus 2.279c]]; important, powerful, πόλις [Refs 2nd c.BC+ [2nd c.BC: Polybius Historicus 1.17.5, etc.]]

__II.3
of soldiers, heavy-armed, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 5.3.37 (assuming variant)]]; of the ὁπλίτης [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Leges” 833b (_comparative_)]]; τὰ β. τῶν ὅπλων [Refs 2nd c.BC+ [2nd c.BC: Polybius Historicus 1.76.3.]]

__II.4
difficult, ὅρκος γὰρ οὐδεὶς ἀνδρὶ φηλήτῃ β. [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Fragmenta” 933.]]

__III
of impressions on the senses,

__III.1
of sound, strong, deep, bass, opposed to to ὀξύς, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 9.257, 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Philoctetes” 208, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Protagoras” 332c, 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Ethica Nicomachea” 1125a14, etc.; βαρὺ ἀμβόασον 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Persae” 572 (Lyric poetry); φθέγγονται βαρύτατον ἀνθρώπων 5th c.BC: Hippocrates Medicus “Aër.” 15; βαρύτατα ὑπακούειν, of diseases, [prev. author] “Prorrh.” 2.39; πενθεῖν 2nd-3rd c.AD: Aelianus “Varia Historia” 12.1]]; especially of musical pitch, low, opposed to ὀξύς, βαρυτάτη χορδή [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Phaedrus” 268e]]; ἆχος, φωνά, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Archytas Tarentinus Philosophus I, compare 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Ethica Eudemia” 1235a28, 4th c.BC: Aristoxenus Musicus “Harmonica” p.3]] M.; of accent, grave, ἀντὶ ὀξείας τῆς μέσης συλλαβῆς βαρεῖαν ἐφθεγξάμεθα [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Cratylus” 399b; ὀξείᾳ καὶ βαρείᾳ καὶ μέσῃ φωνῇ 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Rhetorica” 1403b30, etc.: hence ἡ βαρεῖα (i.e. προσῳδία)]] accentus gravis, [Refs 2nd c.BC+ [2nd c.BC: Dionysius Thrax Grammaticus 630.1, etc.; β. τάσις 1st c.BC: Dionysius Halicarnassensis “de Compositione Verborum” 11, 2nd c.AD: Apollonius Dyscolus Grammaticus “de Syntaxi;” 307.13; β. τόνος 2nd c.BC: Dionysius Thrax Grammaticus 674.13, compare 2nd c.AD: Apollonius Dyscolus Grammaticus “de Pronominibus;” 36.5; β. συλλαβή]]unaccented, [Refs [[prev. author] “Synt.” 100.8, +others]] adverb βαρέως with the accent thrown back, [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [[prev. author] “Pron.” 51.1, 2nd c.AD: Athenaeus Epigrammaticus 2.53b: _comparative_ -ύτερον, opposed to ὀξύτερον]] (ου) opposed to οὗ), [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Sophistici Elenchi” 178a3]] (but, on a lower note, αὐλεῖν [Refs [[prev. author] “GA” 788a22).]]

of smell, strong, offensive, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 6.119.]]

Abbott-Smith / STEPBible (TBESG)
βασανίζω
(βάσανος), [in LXX: 1Ki.5:3, Sir.4:17, and frequently in Wi, II, 4Mac ;]
__1. prop., to rub on the touchstone, put to the test.
__2. to examine by torture, hence, generally, to torture, torment, distress: Mat.8:6, 29 14:24, Mrk.5:7 6:48, Luk.8:28, 2Pe.2:8, Rev.9:5 11:10 12:2 14:10 20:10.

βᾰσᾰν-ίζω,
Attic dialect future -ῐῶ[Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Ranae” 802, 1121, “Ec.” 748:]]aorist ἐβασάνισα, subjunctive βασανίσω variant in [Refs [[prev. author] “Ra.” 618 codex R:]] —passive, aorist ἐβασανίσθην: perfect βεβασάνισμαι:—rub upon the touch-stone (βάσανος), χρυσόν [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Gorgias” 486d]]: hence, put to the test, prove, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “de Generatione Animalium” 747a3 (_passive_), etc.]]; investigate scientifically, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Hippocrates Medicus “Aër.” 3;]] of the instances used in inductive inference, ἀπὸ τῶν πανταχόθεν βεβασανισμένων [μεταβαίνομεν] [Refs 1st c.BC+ [1st c.BC: Philodemus Philosophus “περὶ σημείων καὶ σημειώσεων” 29.]]

__II
of persons, examine closely, cross-question, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.116, 2.151, 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Acharnenses” 110, “Ra.” 802, etc.]]; βεβασανισμένος εἰς δικαιοσύνην having his love of justice put to the test, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 361c, compare 413e, “Smp.” 184a]]; ὑπὸ δακρύων βασανίζεσθαι, i.e. to be convicted of being painted by tears (washing off the cosmetic), [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Oeconomicus” 10.8.]]

__II.2
question by applying torture, torture, rack (see. βάσανοςIII), [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Ranae” 616, 618; [δούλους] πάντας παραδίδωμι βασανίσαι 5th c.BC: Antipho Orator 2.4.8, compare 5.36]]:—passive, to be put to the torture, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 7.86, 5th c.BC: Lysias Orator 4.14, 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Rhetorica ad Alexandrum” 1443b31; αἰωνίοις ἀμοιβαῖς βασανισθησόμενοι πρὸς τῶν θεῶν 1st c.BC: Philodemus Gadarensis Epigrammaticus “D.” 1.19]]; to be tortured by disease (censured by [NT+2nd c.AD+ [2nd c.AD: Lucianus Sophista “Sol.” 6), NT.Matt.8.6; ὑπὸ τῶν κυμάτων [prev. work] 14.24]]; of animals, [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd-3rd c.AD: Philostratus Sophista “Vita Apollonii” 1.38]]: metaphorically of the earth,[Refs [[prev. work] 6.10.]]

__II.3
metaphorically of style, strain, [Refs 3rd c.AD+ [3rd c.AD: Longinus Rhetor 10.6; βεβασανισμένος]]forced, unnatural, [Refs 1st c.BC+ [1st c.BC: Dionysius Halicarnassensis “de Thucydide” 55.]]

βασιλεία, -ας, ἡ
(βασιλεύω), [in LXX chiefly for מַמְלָכָה ,מַלְכוּת ;]
__1. prop. abstract, sovereignty, royal power, dominion: Luk.1:33 22:29, Jhn.18:36, Act.1:6, Heb.1:8, 1Co.15:24; λαβεῖν β., Luk.19:12, 15 Rev.17:12; δοῦναι τὴν, ib. 17; ἔχειν β., ib. 18; ἔρχεσθαι ἐν τ. (εἰς τὴν) β., Mat.16:28, Luk.23:42; β. τ. θεοῦ, Rev.12:10.
__2. By meton., concrete (MM, Exp., x),
__(a) a kingdom, the territory or people over whom the king rules (Est.5:3, al.): Mat.4:8 12:25, 26 24:7, Mrk.3:24 6:23, Luk.4:5, Heb.11:33, al.;
__(b) the royal majesty (cf. our phrase His Majesty), the king himself (τ. σπέρμα τῆς β., 4Ki.11:1).
__3. In LXX (Wis.6:5, Tob.13:1, al.), Targ. and NT, of the Messianic rule and kingdom, ἡ β. τ. θεοῦ, τ. οὐρανῶν (Heb. מַלְכוּת שָׁמַיִם, Aram. מַלְכוּתָא דִשׁמַיָּא; see Dalman, Words, 91-147; Cremer, 132, 658), the kingdom of God (on the equivalence of the two phrases, see Dalman, op. cit., 93, 218f.); τ. θεοῦ, Mat.6:33 12:28, al.; τ. οὐρανῶν, Mat.3:2 4:17, al.; τ. Χριστοῦ (מַלִכוּת דִמְשִׁיחא, Targ. Jon. on Isa.53:10), Eph.5:5; τ. κυρίου, 2Pe.1:11, Rev.11:15; τ. Δαυείδ, Mrk.11:10; absol., ἡ β., Mat.4:23, Jas.2:5, al. The kingdom is regarded as present: Mat.11:12, Luk.17:21, Rom.14:17, al.; as that which is to be consummated in the future, Mat.6:10, Mrk.9:1, Jhn.3:5, 2Pe.1:11, al. Noteworthy phrases are: ζητεῖν τὴν β., Mat.6:33; δέχεσθαι, Mrk.10:15; κλρονομεῖν, Mat.25:34; διδόναι, Lk 12:32; παραλαμβάνειν, Heb.12:28; αὐτῶν (τοιούτων) εστὶν ἡ β., Mat.5:3, 10 19:14, Mrk.10:14, Luk.18:16; διὰ τὴν β., Mat.19:12; ἕνεκεν τῆς β., Luk.18:29; εὐαγγελίζεσθαι, κηρύσσειν, διαγγέλλειν τὴν β., Luk.4:43 9:2, 60; ἤγγικεν ἡ β., Mat.3:2, Mrk.1:15; κλεῖς τῆς β., Mat.16:10; κλείειν τὴν β., Mat.23:14; υἱοὶ τῆς β., Mat.8:12 13:38 (cf. Cremer, 132, 658).
(AS)

[prev. author] “Ch.” 893]]; θήρειος β., ={Κένταυροι}, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Trachiniae” 1059.]]

βῐάζω,
constrain, active once in [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Homerus Epicus, ἦ μάλα δή με βιάζετε 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 12.297; ἐβίασε τὴν γυναῖκά μου 5th-6th c.BC: Alcaeus Comicus 29: _absolutely_, εἰ πάνυ ἐβίαζον]] if they used force, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Hippocrates Medicus “ἐπιδημίαι” 2.24; compare below 1.2]]:—passive, future βιασθήσομαι [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd c.AD: Pausanias Periegeta 6.5.9:]]aorist ἐβιάσθην, perfect βεβίασμαι (see. below):—to be hard pressed or overpowered, βελέεσσι βιάζεται [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 11.589]]; βιάζετο γὰρ βελ[Refs 5th c.BC+ [. 15.727; βιασθέντες λύᾳ 5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “N.” 9.14; νόσῳ 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Fragmenta” 20 (= “Tragica Adespota” 70)]]; to be forced or constrained to do, with infinitive, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. author] “Th.” 890: with _accusative_ _cognate_, βιάζομαι τάδε 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Antigone” 66, compare 1073; βιασθείς [prev. author] “El.” 575; ἐπεὶ ἐβιάσθη 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 4.44; ὑπό τινος [prev. author] 1.2]]; opposed to ἀδικεῖσθαι,[Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. work] 77; βιασθεὶς ἄκων ἔπραξεν 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 6.16; ἵνα ἢ συγχωρήσωσιν.. ἢ βιασθῶσιν [prev. author] 18.175; βιαζόμενος ὑπό τινος ἐξήμαρτεν 5th c.BC: Antipho Orator 4.4.5]]; βεβιασμένοι forcibly made slaves, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Hiero” 2.12]]; πόλεις βεβ. [Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. author] “HG” 5.2.23: βιαζόμενος ὑπὸ τῆς παρούσης ἀπορίας 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 7.67]]; τὸ βιασθέν those who are forced, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Politica” 1255a11]]; of things, τοὔνειδος ὀργῇ βιασθέν forced from one by anger, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Tyrannus” 524]]; τὸ βεβιασμένον forced to fit a hypothesis, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Metaphysica” 1082b2]]; βεβ. σχήματα forced figures of speech, [Refs 1st c.BC+ [1st c.BC: Dionysius Halicarnassensis “de Thucydide” 33, compare 3rd c.AD: Porphyrius Tyrius Philosophus “de Antro Nympharum - Porphyrii Opuscula” 36.]]

__2
active, make good, suffice to discharge a debt, [Refs [“PFlor.” 56.13.]]

__II
more frequently βιάζομαι, aorist middle ἐβιασάμην, perfect βεβίασμαι [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 19.206, 4th-3rd c.BC: Menander Comicus “Σαμία” 63, 2nd-3rd c.AD: Dio Cassius Historicus 46.45]]:—overpower by force, press hard, ἦ μάλα δή σε βιάζεται ὠκὺς Ἀχιλλεύς [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 22.229, etc.]]; β. τοὺς πολεμίους dislodge them, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 1.4.5]]; β. νόμους to do them violence, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 8.53]]; βιασάμενος ταῦτα πάντα having broken through all these restraints, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Lysias Orator 6.52]]; β. γυναῖκα force her, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Plutus” 1092]]; opposed to πείθειν, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Lysias Orator 1.32]]; β. αὑτόν lay violent hands on oneself, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Phaedo” 61c, 61d]]; β. τινά, with infinitive, force one to do, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 1.3.1]]; τί με βιάζεσθε λέγει; [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Fragmenta” 44: with]]infinitive omitted, β. τὰ σφάγια force the victims [to be favourable], [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 9.41; β. ἄστρα 3rd c.BC: Theocritus Poeta Bucolicus 22.9: with double _accusative_, αὐδῶ πόλιν σε μὴ β. τόδε 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Septem contra Thebas” 1047.]]

__II.2
with accusative of things, carry by force, βιάσασθαι τὸν ἔκπλουν force an exit, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 7.72; τὴν ἀπόβασιν [prev. author] 4.11: with _accusative_ _neuter_, 5th-6th c.BC: Andocides Orator 4.17, 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Historia Graeca (Hellenica)” 5.3.12.]]

__II.3
absolutely, act with violence, use force, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Prometheus Vinctus” 1010, “Ag.” 1509 (Lyric poetry), 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Ajax” 1160, etc.; πρὸς τὸ λαμπρὸν ὁ φθόνος βιάζεται “Tragica Adespota” 547.12]]; opposed to δικάζομαι, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 1.77]]; β. διὰ φυλάκων force one's way, [Refs [[prev. author] 7.83]]; β. ἐς τὸ ἔξω, β. εἴσω,[Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. work] 69, 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 3.3.69; δρόμῳ β. 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 1.63]]: with infinitive, β. πρὸς τὸν λόφον ἐλθεῖν [Refs [[prev. author] 7.79]]; βιαζόμενοι βλάπτειν using every effort to hurt me, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Lysias Orator 9.16]]; but βιαζόμενοιμὴ ἀποδιδόναι refusing with violence to repay, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Historia Graeca (Hellenica)” 5.3.12: especially in]]participle, ἵνα βιασάμενοι ἐκπλεύσωσι may sail out by forcing their way, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 7.67; συνεξέρχονται βιασάμενοι 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 7.8.11]]; ἐπὶ μᾶλλον ἔτι β. (of a famine) grow worse and worse, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.94.]]

contend or argue vehemently, with infinitive, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Sophista” 246b; β. τὸ μὴ ὂν ὡς ἔστι κατά τι [prev. work] 241d]]: absolutely, persist in assertion, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 21.205.]]

deep_entry:
Abbott-Smith / STEPBible (TBESG)
βίος, -ου, ὁ,
[in LXX chiefly for יָמִים ;]
__1. period or course of life, life: Luk.8:14, 1Ti.2:2, 2Ti.2:4, 1Jn.2:16.
__2. living, livelihood, means (in Pro.31:14 for לֶחֶם; see DCG, ii, 39a): Mrk.12:44, Luk.8:43 15:12, 30 21:4, 1Jn.3:17.†
SYN.: ζωή, is life intensive, "vita quâ, vivimus," the vital principle; βίος, life extensive, "vita quam vivimus," (1) the period of life, (2) the means by which it is sustained. Hence, in cl., ζ., being confined to the physical life common to men and animals, is the  inferior word (cf. zoology, biography). In NT, ζωή is elevated into the ethical and spiritual sphere (cf. Tr., Syn., §xxvii). (AS)

__1. of bodily sight;
__(a) to see, have sight (opposite to τυφλὸς): Mat.12:22, Jhn.9:7, Act.9:9, Rom.11:8, Rev.3:18, al.;
__(b) to perceive, look (at), see: absol.,  Act.1:9; with accusative, Mat.7:3, Mrk.5:31, Luk.6:41, Jhn.1:29, al.; ὅραμα, Act.12:9; γυναῖκα, Mat.5:28; βιβλίον, Rev.5:3, 4; τ. βλεπόμενα, 2Co.4:18.

__(b) to consider, look to, take heed: absol., Mrk.13:23, 33; with accusative, 1Co.1:26, al.; before πῶς, with indic., Luk.8:18, 1Co.3:10, Eph.5:15; before τί, with indic., Mrk.4:24; before εἰς πρόσωπον, of partiality, Mat.22:16, Mrk.12:14. Colloq. (for ex. from π., V. Deiss., LAE, 122; M, Pr., 107; MM, Exp., x; Milligan, NTD, 50), β. ἑαυτόν: Mrk.13:9; before ἵνα μή, II Jo 8; β. ἀπό, Mrk.8:15 12:38; before μή (cl. ὁρᾶν), with fut. indic., Col.2:8, Heb.3:12; id. with aor. subj., Mat.24:4, Mrk.13:5.
__3. Of situation and direction (Lat. specto), to look, face (towards), places, etc. (before πρός, Xen, Hell., vii, 1, 17; Eze.40:23, 24): before κατά, with accusative, Act.27:12 (cf. ἀνα-, ἀπο-, δια-, ἐμ-, ἐπι-, περ-, προ-βλέπω), see DCG, i, 446; ii, 596.
