(Epic dialect also βόλομαι, which see), Doric dialect βώλ- (which see), Aeolic dialect βόλλ- (see. βόλομαι), Thess. βέλλ- [Refs [“IG” 9(2).517.20]], Boeotian dialect βείλ- [Refs [[prev. work]7.3080,]]βήλ- [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [“SIG” 1185.18 (Tanagra, 3rd c.BC)]], Locrian dialectand Delph. δείλ- [Refs [“IG” 9(1).334.3, “GDI” 2034.10]], Coan, etc. δήλ- (which see), Ionic dialect 2nd pers. singular βούλεαι [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 18.364, 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.11]]: imperfect ἐβουλόμην [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 11.79, etc.; ἠβουλόμην 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Helena” 752, 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 1.15, etc.]]; Ionic dialect 3rd.pers. plural ἐβουλέατο codices in [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.4, 3.143]]: future βουλήσομαι [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Prometheus Vinctus” 867, 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Tyrannus” 1077, etc.]]; later future βουληθήσομαι variant in [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd c.AD: Aristides Rhetor “Orationes” 48(24).8, 2nd c.AD: Galenus Medicus]] 13.636: aorist ἐβουλήθην, also ἠβ- (see. below), βουληθείς [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Coloneus” 732, “IG” 22.1236, etc]]., but Epic dialect aorist subjunctive 3rd.pers. singular βούλεται (from *βόλσ-ε-ται) [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 1.67]]: perfect βεβούλημαι [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 18.2]]; also βέβουλα (προ-) [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 1.113 (ἐβέβουλε]] uncertain in epigram in [Refs [“Berl.Sitzb.” 1894.907):]] — forms with augment ἠ- are found in Attic dialect Inscrr. from [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th c.BC onwards, as “IG” 22.657, +others, and occur frequently in Mss. as ἠβούλοντο variant in 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 2.2, 6.79, ἠβούλου 4th c.BC: Hyperides Orator “pro Lycophrone” 11]]; said to be Ionic in [Refs [“Anecdota Graeca - MSS. Bibl. Oxon.” 2.374.]] — An active βούλητε (={βούλησθε}) Mitteis [Refs 4th c.AD+ [“Chr.” 361.10 (4th c.AD)]]:—will, wish, be willing, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Homerus Epicus, etc.: usually implying choice or preference (cf. IV) opposed to ἐθέλω]] 'consent', εἰ βούλει, ἐγὼ ἐθέλω [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Gorgias” 522e, compare “R.” 347b, 437b; ἐὰν βούλῃ σὺ.. ἐὰν θεὸς ἐθέλῃ [prev. author] Alcaeus1.135d; ἂν οἵ τε θεοὶ 'θέλωσι καὶ ὑμεῖς βούλησθε 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 2.20; οὔτ᾽ ἀκούειν ἠθέλετ᾽ οὔτε πιστεύειν ἐβούλεσθε [prev. author] 19.23]]; but ἐθέλω is also used = 'wish', λέξαι θέλω σοι, πρὶν θανεῖν, ἃ βούλομαι, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Alcestis” 281 (so ἐθέλω εἰπεῖν 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Protagoras” 309b, but φράσαι τι βούλομαι 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Plutus” 1090): 8th c.BC: Homerus Epicus uses βούλομαι for ἐθέλω]] in the case of the gods, for with them wish is will: ἐθέλω is more general, and is sometimes used where βούλομαι might have stood, e.g. [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 7.182.]]—Construct.: mostly with infinitive, Τρώεσσιν ἐβούλετο κῦδος ὀρέξαι [Refs [11.79, etc.]]; sometimes with infinitive future, [Refs 6th c.BC+ [6th c.BC: Theognis Elegiacus 184]]; with accusative et infinitive, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 4.353, and frequently in Prose: when βούλομαι is followed by _accusative_ only, an]]infinitive may generally be supplied, as καί κε τὸ βουλοίμην (i.e. γενέσθαι) [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 20.316]]; ἔτυχεν ὧν ἐβούλετο (i.e. τυχεῖν) [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Antiphanes Comicus 18.6]]; πλακοῦντα β. (i.e. σε λέγειν) [Refs [[prev. author] 52.11]]; καὶ εἰ μάλα βούλεται ἄλλῃ [Ποσειδάων] (i.e. τοῦτο γενέσθαι) [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 15.51]]; so εἰς τὸ βαλανεῖον βούλομαι (i.e. ἰέναι) [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Ranae” 1279]]; βουλοίμην ἄν (i.e. τόδε γενέσθαι) [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Euthyphro” 3a.]]

__2
in [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Homerus Epicus of gods, with _accusative_ _of things_ et _dative_ _person_, Τρώεσσιν.. ἐβούλετο νίκην]] he willed victory to the Trojans, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 7.21, compare 23.682: later with _accusative_, τὸ βουλόμενον τὴν πολιτείαν πλῆθος]] that supports the constitution, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Politica” 1309b17.]]

__II
Attic dialect usages:

__II.1
βούλει or βούλεσθε followed by Verb in subjunctive, βούλει λάβωμα; would you have me take hold? [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Philoctetes” 761]]; βούλει φράσ; [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Equites” 36, compare 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Phaedo” 79a, “R.” 596a]]; ποῦ δὴ βούλει ἀναγνῶμε; [Refs [[prev. author] “Phdr.” 228e.]]

__II.2
εἰ βούλει if you please, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Antigone” 1168, 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 3.4.41]]; also εἰ δὲ βούλει, ἐὰν δὲ βούλῃ, to express a concession, or if you like, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Symposium” 201a, etc.; εἰ μὲν β., φρονήσει, εἰ δὲ β., ἰσχύι [prev. author] “R.” 432a.]]

__II.3
ὁ βουλόμενος any one who likes, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.54, 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 1.26, etc.; ἔδωκεν ἅπαντι τῷ βουλομένῳ 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 21.45]]; ὁ β. the 'common in former', [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Plutus” 918 (whence, in jest, βούλομαι [prev. work] 908)]]; ὅστις βούλει who or which ever you like, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Gorgias” 517b, “Cra.” 432a.]]

__II.4
βουλομένῳ μοί ἐστι, with infinitive, it is according to my wish that.., [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 2.3; εἰ σοὶ β. ἐστὶν ἀποκρίνεσθαι 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Gorgias” 448d; also τὰ θεῶν οὕτω βουλόμεν᾽ ἔσται 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Iphigenia Aulidensis” 33]]; τὸ κεἰνου βουλόμενον his wish, [Refs [[prev. work] 1270]]; but with passive sense, τὸ β. the object of desire, [Refs 1st c.AD+ [2nd c.AD: Lucianus Sophista “Am.” 37, 1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus “Artoxerxes” 28.]]

__II.5
τί βουλόμενο; with what purpose? [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Phaedo” 63a, 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 18.172; τί βουληθεὶς πάρε; 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Electra” 1100.]]

__III
mean, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 362e, 590e, etc.]]; τί ἡμῖν βούλεται οὗτος ὁ μῦθος; (followed by β. λέγειν ὡς..) [Refs 1st c.BC+ [[prev. author] “Tht.” 156c; τί β. σημαίνειν τὸ τέρας 1st c.BC: Dionysius Halicarnassensis 4.59]]; βούλεται εἶναι professes or pretends to be, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 595c; β. τὸ ὄνομα ἐπικεῖσθαι [prev. author] “Cra.” 412c; frequently in 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus, τὸ ἀκούσιον βούλεται λέγεσθαι οὐκ εἰ.. “EN” 1110b30; β. ἄσωτος εἶναι ὁ ἕν τι κακὸν ἔχων [prev. work] 1119b34; β. ὁ πρᾶος ἀτάραχος εἶναι [prev. work] 1125b33]]; tend to be, ἡ τοῦ ὕδατος φύσις β. εἶναι ἄχυμος [Refs [[prev. author] “Sens.” 441a3]]; β. ἤδη τότε εἶναι πόλις ὅταν.. [Refs [[prev. author] “Pol.” 1261b12, compare 1293b40]]; ἡ φύσις β. μὲν τοῦτο ποιεῖν πολλάκις, οὐ μέντοι δύναται[Refs [[prev. work] 1255b3, compare “GA” 778a4, +others]]

__III.2
to be wont, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 6.3.18.]]

__IV
followed by ἤ.., prefer, for βούλομαι μᾶλλον (which is more usually in Prose), βούλομ᾽ ἐγὼ λαὸν σόον ἔμμεναι ἢ ἀπολέσθαι I had rather.., [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 1.117, compare 23.594, 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 3.232, 11.489, 12.350; β. τὸ μέν τι εὐτυχέειν.. ἢ εὐτυχέειν τὰ πάντα 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 3.40]]; β. παρθενεύεσθαι πλέω χρόνον ἢ πατρὸς ἐστερῆσθαι (for πολὺν χρόνον, μᾶλλον ἤ[Refs 5th c.BC+ [..) [prev. work] 124, compare 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Andromache” 351]]; less frequently without ἤ.., πολὺ βούλομαι αὐτὴν οἴκοι ἔχειν I much prefer.., [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 1.112, compare 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 15.88]]. [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Medea” 606]]; ἐγημάμην, of a man marrying a rich wife, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Antiphanes Comicus 46]]; γαμεῖται ἕκαστος (obscene meaning) [Refs 1st c.BC+ [2nd c.AD: Lucianus Sophista “VH” 1.22; ὁ γαμηθεὶς ὡς παρθένος κἄπειτα γενόμενος ἀνήρ 1st c.BC: Philodemus Philosophus “περὶ σημείων καὶ σημειώσεων” 2]]; incorrectly, in later writers, γημάμενος [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd c.AD: Apollodorus Damascenus Mechanicus 3.12.6, compare 4th c.AD(?): Quintus Smyrnaeus Epicus 1.728.]]

__II.2
of parents, get their children married, betroth them, get a wife for the son, Πηλεύς θήν μοι ἔπειτα γυναῖκα γαμέσσεται αὐτός (where [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [3rd-2nd c.BC: Aristarchus Grammaticus γε μάσσεται]] will seek or make suit for) [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 9.394:]] —active aorist 1 ἐγάμησα[Refs 4th c.BC+ [in this sense, 4th-3rd c.BC: Menander Comicus 885.]]

__III
passive, to be taken to wife: hence, marry a husband, [prev. cited] ad [near the start], [Refs 4th c.AD+ [“PGrenf.” 2.76.11 (4th c.AD)]], etc.; rarely in correct authors, [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd c.AD(?): Pollianus Epigrammaticus 3.45.]]

LSJ / STEPBible (TFLSJ)
γάμος [ᾰ], ὁ,
wedding, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 5.4.29, +others; γάμοι εἰλαπίναι τε 18.491]]; γάμον τεύχειν furnish forth a wedding, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 1.277; γ. δαινύναι 4.3]]; ἀρτύειν[Refs 4th c.BC+ [[prev. work] 770; γάμον ποιεῖν 3rd c.BC: Herodas Mimographus 7.86, “Test.Epict.” 2.19: _plural_, γάμους διττοὺς ἑστιᾶν 4th c.BC: Isaeus Orator 8.9]]; of a single wedding, οἰκοσίτους τοὺς γ. ποιεῖσθαι [NT+4th c.BC+ [4th-3rd c.BC: Menander Comicus 450; γάμους ποιεῖν 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 30.21, NT.Matt.22.2; ἐπιτελεῖν γ. τῆς θυγατρός 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Fragmenta” 549, compare 1st c.BC: Diodorus Siculus Historicus 13.84; οἱ κεκλημένοι εἰς τοὺς γ. 4th-3rd c.BC: Diphilus Comicus 17.2; ἐν τοῖς γ. ἄκλητος εἰσδεδυκέναι 4th-3rd c.BC: Apollodorus Carystius Comicus 24.]]

__II
marriage, wedlock, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 13.382, etc.; ἄγειν [γυναῖκα] ἐπὶ γάμῳ 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 2.4.8; ἀγαγέσθαι τινὰ πρὸς γάμον 1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus “Cat.Ma.” 24]]; τὸν Οἰνέως γ. the marriage granted by O., [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Trachiniae” 792; γ. θεῶν τινος 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Troades” 979, compare “IT” 25; εἰς γ. τινὸς ἐλθεῖν [prev. author] “IA” 1044 (Lyric poetry); more frequently in _plural_, 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Prometheus Vinctus” 558 (Lyric poetry), 739 (Lyric poetry), “Ag.” 1156 (Lyric poetry), etc.; compare γαμέω 1: also τοῖς μεθημερινοῖς γάμοις]], i.e. prostitution, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 18.129]]; Πανὸς ἀναβοᾷ γάμους, i.e. rape, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Helena” 190 (Lyric poetry)]]; of unlawful wedlock, as of Paris and Helen, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. author] “Tr.” 932; γάμοι ἄρρενες 2nd c.AD: Lucianus Sophista “VH” 1.22; γ. ἀνδρεῖοι 6th c.AD: Procopius Caesariensis Historicus “Historia Arcana” 16.23:— 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Andromache” 103, 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 8.4.19]], do not establish the sense of a wife; for [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Troades” 357, see at {γαμέω} I.1.]]

__III
ἱερὸς γ. ritual marriage, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-3rd c.BC: Menander Comicus 320, 5th c.AD(?): Hesychius Legal icographus, “Etymologicum Magnum” 468.56; as a nickname, 4th c.BC: Anaxandrides Comicus 34.2]]; name of play by Ale.Comedy texts

__IV
[Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Pythagoras Philosophus]] name for three, [Refs [Theol.Ar. 16]]; for five, [Refs 1st c.AD+ [1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus 2.388c; for six, Theo Sm.p.102H., “Theologumena Arithmeticae” 33.]]

__V
Γάμος personified, [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [3rd c.BC: Philoxenus Epigrammaticus 13, 4th c.AD: Libanius Sophista “Orationes” 5.27.]]

__VI
name of month at Epidaurus, [Refs [“IG” 4.1485,1492]]. (Perh. akin to Sanskrit jāmís 'brother or sister', Latin geminus.)

Abbott-Smith / STEPBible (TBESG)
γάρ,
co-ordinating particle, contr. of γε ἄρα,
verily then, hence, in truth, indeed, yea, then, why, and when giving a reason or explanation, for, the usage in NT being in general accord with that of cl.;
__1. explicative and epexegetic: Mat.4:18 19:12, Mrk.1:16 5:42 16:4, Luk.11:3o, Rom.7:1, 1Co.16:5, al.
__2. Conclusive, in questions, answers and exclamations: Mat.9:5 27:23, Luk.9:25 22:27, Jhn.9:30, Act.8:31 16:37 19:35, Rom.15:26, 1Co.9:10, Php.1:18 (Ellic., in l.), 1Th.2:20, al.
__3. Causal: Mat.1:21 2:2, 5, 6, 3:23, Mrk.1:22, 9:6, Luk.1:15, 18, Jhn.2:25, Act.2:25, Rom.1:9, 11, 1Co.11:5, Rev.1:3, al.; giving the reason for a command or prohibition, Mat.2:20 3:9, Rom.13:11, Col.3:3, 1Th.4:3, al.; where the cause is contained in an interrog. statement, Luk.22:27, Rom.3:3 4:3, 1Co.10:29; καὶ γάρ, for also, Mrk.10:45, Luk.6:32, 1Co.5:7, al. id. as in cl. = etenim, where the καί loses its connective force (Bl., §78, 6; Kühner 3, ii, 854f.), Mrk.14:70, Luk.1:66 22:37, 2Co.13:4. The proper place of γάρ is after the first word in a clause, but in poets it often comes third or fourth, and so in late prose: 2Co.1:19. Yet "not the number but the nature of the word after which it stands is the point to be noticed" (see Thayer, see word).
(AS)

LSJ / STEPBible (TFLSJ)
γάρ
(γε, ἄρα), causal conjunction, used alone or with other Particles.

__I
introducing the reason or cause of what precedes, for, τῷ γὰρ ἐπὶ φρεσὶ θῆκε θεὰ λευκώλενος Ἥρη· κήδετο γ. Δαναῶν [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 1.56, etc.]]; but frequently in explanation of that which is implied in the preceding clause, πολλάων πολίων κατέλυσε κάρηνα.. τοῦ γὰρ κράτος ἐστὶ μέγιστον [Refs [2.118, etc.: hence,]]

__I.b
in simple explanations, especially after a Pronoun or demonstrative adjective, ἀλλὰ τόδ᾽ αἰνὸν ἄχος κραδίην καὶ θυμὸν ἱκάνει· Ἕκτωρ γ. ποτε φήσει [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8.148, compare 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 2.163]]; ὃ δὲ δεινότατον.. ὁ Ζεὺς γ... [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Aves” 514; ὃ δὲ πάντων ἀδικώτατον ἔδοξε· τῶν γὰρ προγε γραμμένων ἠτίμωσε καὶ υἱούς 1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus “Sulla” 31]]; frequently in introducing proofs or examples, μαρτύριον δέ· Δήλου γ. καθαιρομένης.. [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 1.8]]; τεκμήριον δέ· οὔτε γ. Λακεδαιμόνιοι.. [Refs 4th c.BC+ [[prev. author] 2.39, compare 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 20.10, etc.]]; in full, τεκμήριον δὲ τούτου τόδε· αἱ μὲν γ... [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 2.58]]; παράδειγμα τόδε τοῦ λόγου· ἐκ γ... [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 1.2; δηλοῖ δέ μοι τόδε· πρὸ γ... [prev. work] 3.]]

__I.c
to introduce a detailed description or narration already alluded to, ὅμως δὲ λεκτέα ἃ γιγνώσκω· ἔχει γ. [ἡ χώρα] πεδία κάλλιστα.. [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 5.6.6, etc.]]

__I.d
in answers to questions or statements challenging assent or denial, yes,.., no,.. , οὔκουν.. ἀνάγκη ἐστ;—ἀνάγκη γ. οὖν, ἔφη, ay doubtless it is necessary, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 2.1.7, compare § 4 and 13; indicating assent, ἔχει γ. 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Phaedrus” 268a]]; ἱκανὸς γ., ἔφη, συμβαίνει γ., ἔφη, [Refs [[prev. author] “R.” 502b, 502c,compare “Ap.” 41a, etc.]]; οὔκουν δὴ τό γ᾽ εἰκός.—οὐ γ.: [Refs [[prev. author] “Phdr.” 276c.]]

__I.2
by inversion, preceding the fact explained, since, as, Ἀτρεΐδη, πολλοὶ γ. τεθνᾶσιν Ἀχαιοί.. τῷ σε χρὴ πόλεμον παῦσαι [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 7.328]]; χρόνου δὲ οὐ πολλοῦ διελθόντος (χρῆν γ. Κανδαύλῃ γενέσθαι κακῶς) ἔλεγε πρὸς τὸν Γύγην τοιάδε, Γύγη, οὐ γ. σε δοκέω πείθεσθαι.. (ὦτα γ. τυγχάνει κτλ.), ποίει ὅκως.. [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.8. compare 6.102, +others]]; εἶεν, σὺ γ. τούτων ἐπιστήμων, τί χρὴ ποιεῖ; [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Phaedo” 117a]]; the principal proposition is sometimes

__I.2.b
blended with the causal one, τῇ δὲ κακῶς γ. ἔδεε γενέσθαι εἶπε, i.e. ἡ δέ (κακῶς γ. οἱ ἔδεε γενέσθαι) εἶπε [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 9.109, compare 1.24, 4.149, 200, 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 1.72, 8.30.]]

__I.2.c
attached to the hypothet. Particle instead of being joined to the apodosis, οὐδ᾽ εἰ γ. ἦν τὸ πρᾶγμα μὴ θεήλατον, ἀκάθαρτον ὑμᾶς εἰκὸς ἦν οὕτως ἐᾶν, i.e. οὐδὲ γ. εἰ ἦν.., [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Tyrannus” 255.]]

__I.2.d
repeated, οὐ γ. οὖν σιγήσομαι· ἔτικτε γ... [Refs [[prev. author] “OC” 980, compare “Ant.” 659f, 1255.]]

__I.3
in elliptical phrases, where that of which γάρ gives the reason is omitted, and must be supplied,

__I.3.a
frequently in Trag. dialogue and [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus]], when yes or no may be supplied from the context, καὶ δῆτ᾽ ἐτόλμας τούσδ᾽ ὑπερβαίνειν νόμου;—οὐ γ. τί μοι Ζεὺς ἦν ὁ κηρύξας τάδε [yes], for it was not Zeus, etc., [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Antigone” 450, compare “OT” 102, etc.; καλῶς γὰρ αὐτὸς ἠγάνισαι 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Symposium” 194a]]; frequently in phrase ἔστι γ. οὕτω [yes], for so it is, i. e. yes certainly: λέγεταί τι καινό; γένοιτο γ. ἄν τι καινότερον ἢ..; [why,] could there be.. ? [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 4.10; with negatives, 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Ranae” 262 τούτῳ γ. οὐ νικήσετε]] [do so], yet shall ye never prevail by this means: for ἀλλὰ γ., see below[Refs [11.1.]]

__I.3.b
to confirm or strengthen something said, οἵδ᾽ οὐκέτ᾽ εἰσί· τοῦτο γάρ σε δήξεται [I say this], for it will sting thee, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Medea” 1370]]: after an Exclamation, ὦ πόποι· ἀνάριθμα γ. φέρω πήματα [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Tyrannus” 168 (Lyric poetry), compare 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Helena” 857.]]

__I.3.c
in conditional propositions, where the condition is omitted, else, οὐ γ. ἄν με ἔπεμπον πάλιν (i.e. εἰ μὴ ἐπίστευον) [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 7.6.33]]; γίνεται γ. ἡ κοινωνία συμμαχία for in that case, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Politica” 1280b8.]]

__I.4
in abrupt questions, why, what, τίς γ. σε θεῶν ἐμοὶ ἄγγελον ἧκε; why who hath sent thee? [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 18.182; πῶς γ. νῦν.. εὕδουσ; 10.424]]; πατροκτονοῦσα γ. ξυνοικήσεις ἐμο; what, wilt thou.. ? [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Choephori” 909: generally, after _interrogative_ Particles, ἦ γ.]]..; what, was it.. ? [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Tyrannus” 1000, 1039, etc.]]; τί γ.; quid enim? i. e. it must be so, [Refs [[prev. author] “OC” 539, 542, 547, etc.]]; τί γ. δή ποτ; [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 21.44]]; also πῶς γ.; πῶς γ. ο;, see at {πῶς}.

__I.5
to strengthen a wish, with optative, κακῶς γ. ἐξόλοιο O that you might perish ! [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Cyclops” 261]]; compare αἴ, εἰ, εἴθε, πῶς.

__II
joined with other Particles:

__II.1
ἀλλὰ γ. where γάρ gives the reason of a clause to be supplied between ἀλλά and itself, as ἀλλ᾽ ἐν γὰρ Τρώων πεδίῳ.. but [far otherwise], for.., [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 15.739]]; ἀλλὰ γὰρ ἥκουσ᾽ αἵδ᾽ ἐπὶ πρᾶγος πικρόν but [hush], for.., [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Septem contra Thebas” 861]]; ἀλλ᾽ οὐ γ. σ᾽ ἐθέλω.. but [look out] for.., [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 7.242; in full, ἀλλ᾽ οὐ γάρ σφιν ἐφαίνετο κέρδιον εἶναι μαίεσθαι προτέρω, τοὶ μὲν πάλιν αὖτις ἔβαινον 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 14.355; ἀλλ᾽, οὐ γ. ἔπειθε, διδοῖ τὸ φᾶρος 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 9.109.]]

__II.2
γ. ἄρα for indeed, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Protagoras” 315d, “Smp.” 205b.]]

__II.3
γ. δή for of course, for you know, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 2.301, 23.607, 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.34, 114, etc.]]; φάμεν γ. δή yes certainly we say so, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Theaetetus” 187e, compare 164d; οὐ γ. δή 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Antigone” 46, etc.]]

__II.4
γ. νυ [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 14.359.]]

__II.5
γ. οὖν for indeed, to confirm or explain, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 15.232, 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 5.34, 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Antigone” 489, 771, etc.]]; φησὶ γ. οὖν yes of course he says so, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Theaetetus” 170a; γ. οὖν δή [prev. author] “Prm.” 148c, etc.; οὐ γ. οὖν [prev. work] 134b]]; compare τοιγαροῦν.

__II.6
γ. που for I suppose, especially with negatives, [Refs [[prev. author] “R.” 381c, “Phd.” 62d, etc.; οὐ γ. δήπου [prev. author] “Prt.” 309c.]]

__II.7
γ. ῥα, ={γὰρ ἄρα}, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 1.113, +others]]

__II.8
γ. τε, [Refs [23.156]]; also τε γ. [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 19.159, 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Politica” 1333a2, +others]]

__II.9
γ. τοι for surely.., [Refs 8th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Helena” 93, “Supp.” 564, etc.; οὐ γ. τοι 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 21.172, etc.]]; compare τοιγάρτοι.

__B
POSITION: γάρ properly stands after the first word in a clause, but in Pocts it frequently stands third or fourth, when the preceding words are closely connected, as ὁ μὲν γὰρ.. [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Ajax” 764]]; χἠ ναῦς γὰρ.. [Refs [[prev. author] “Ph.” 527]]; τό τ᾽ εἰκαθεῖν γὰρ.. [Refs [[prev. author] “Ant.” 1096]]; τὸ μὴ θέμις γὰρ.. [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Choephori” 641, compare 753: also in Prose, τὸ κατ᾽ ἀξίαν γὰρ.. 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Ethica Nicomachea” 1163b11]]: sometimes for metrical reasons, where there is no such connexion, as third [Refs 5th c.BC+ [(4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Agamemnon” 222.729, 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Philoctetes” 219 (all Lyric poetry)), fourth (5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Aves” 1545)]]; in later Comedy texts fifth [Refs 4th c.BC+ [(4th-3rd c.BC: Menander Comicus 462.2); sixth (4th c.BC: Antiphanes Comicus 26.22); seventh (4th-3rd c.BC: Menander Comicus “Ἐπιτρέποντες” 531, “Pk.” 170, 3rd c.BC: Athenio Comicus 1.5)]]; once sixth in [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus, καιρὸς καὶ πλοῦς ὅδ᾽ ἐπείγει γὰρ κατὰ πρύμναν “Ph.” 1451.]]

__B.2
inserted before the demonstrative -ί, as νυνγαρί for νυνὶ γά; compare νυνί.

__C
QUANTITY: γάρ is sometimes long in [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Homerus Epicus for the sake of meter, θήσειν γὰρ ἔτ᾽ ἔμελλεν 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 2.39; φωνῆς γὰρ ἤκουσα “hymnus ad Cererem” 57]].—In Attic dialect always short: [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Equites” 366, “V.” 217, “Lys.” 20 are corrupt.]]

Abbott-Smith / STEPBible (TBESG)
γαστήρͅ, -τρός, ἡ,
[in LXX for בֶּטֶן, ἐν γ. ἔχειν for הרה, ἐν γ. λαμβάνειν for חרה ;]
__1. the belly: metaphorically, a glutton, Tit.1:12.
__2. the womb: ἐν γ. ἔχειν, to be with child, Mat.1:18, 23" (LXX) 24:19, Mrk.13:17, Luk.21:23, 1Th.5:3, Rev.12:2; εν γ. συλλαμβ., to conceive, Luk.1:31.

LSJ / STEPBible (TFLSJ)
γαστήρ, ἡ,
genitive έρος, γαστρός: dative -έρι, γαστρί (the longer forms in Epic dialect, Lyric poetry, and once in Trag., [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Cyclops” 220)]]: dative plural γαστῆρσι [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Hippocrates Medicus “περὶ νούσων” 4.54, γαστράσι 2nd-3rd c.AD: Dio Cassius Historicus 54.22]]:—paunch, belly, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 13.372, etc.]]; γ. ἀσπίδος the hollow of a shield, [Refs 7th c.BC+ [7th c.BC: Tyrtaeus Elegiacus 11.24]]; belly or wide part of a bottle, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Cratinus Comicus 190.]]

__2
the belly, as craving food, κέλεται δέ ἑ γ. [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 6.133; βόσκειν ἣν γαστέρ᾽ 17.228]]; γαστέρι δ᾽ οὔ πως ἔστι νέκυν πενθῆσαι, i. e. by fasting, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 19.225; ἐν γαστρὸς ἀνάγκαις 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Agamemnon” 726 (Lyric poetry)]]; to express gluttony, γαστέρες οἶον [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th-7th c.BC: Hesiodus Epicus “Theogonia” 26; γ. ἀργαί 6th c.BC: Epimenides Philosophus 1; ἐγκράτεια γαστρὸς καὶ ποτοῦ 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 1.2.8, compare “Oec.” 9.11]]; γαστρὸς ἐγκρατής master of his belly, [Refs [[prev. author] “Mem.” 1.2.1; opposed to γαστρὸς ἥττων, [prev. work] 1.5.1]]; γαστρὶ δουλεύειν, χαρίζεσθαι, to be the slave of his belly, [Refs [[prev. work] 1.6.8, 2.1.2]]; γ. δελεάζεσθαι[Refs 4th c.BC+ [[prev. work] 2.1.4; τῇ γ. μετρεῖν τὴν εὐδαιμονίαν 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 18.296]]; τᾶς γαστρὸς φείδεσθαι, com. of one who has nothing to eat, [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [3rd c.BC: Theocritus Poeta Bucolicus 21.41.]]

__3
paunch stuffed with mincemeat, sausage, haggis, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 18.44, 118, 20.25, 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Nubes” 409.]]

__II
womb, ὅντινα γαστέρι μήτηρ.. φέροι [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 6.58]]; ἐκ γαττρός from the womb, from infancy, [Refs 6th c.BC+ [6th c.BC: Theognis Elegiacus 305]]; ἐν γαστρὶ ἔχουσα big with child, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 3.32; ὗν ἔχουσαν ἐν γ. “PFlor.” 130.3 (3rd c.AD)]]; ἐν γ. φέρουσα [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Leges” 792e]]; ἐν γ. λαβεῖν conceive, [LXX+4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Historia Animalium” 632a28, “Anthologia Graeca” 11.18 (1st c.AD: Nicarchus Epigrammaticus), LXX.Gen.30.41, +others]]; συλλαμβάνειν variant [LXX+NT+5th c.BC+ [LXX.Gen.25.21, cf. NT.Luke.1.31; ἐς γ. βάλλεσθαι 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 3.28]]; κατὰ γαστρὸς ἔχειν Vett.[Refs 2nd c.AD+ [Val. 193.33; φέρειν “Geoponica” 16.1.3; also γυνὴ ἑπτὰ ἤδη γαστέρας δυστοκοῦσα 2nd-3rd c.AD: Philostratus Sophista “Vita Apollonii” 3.39. (Perh.for γραστήρ, compare γράω.)]]

short_definition: indeed — γε, enclitic postpositive particle, rarer in κοινή than in cl., giving special prominence to the word to which it is attached, distinguishing it as the least or the most important
root_and_cognates: LSJ-hänvisningar: ὅ γε, ὥς γε, καί το; ἀλλά γε, γοῦν, γέα
deep_entry:
Abbott-Smith / STEPBible (TBESG)
γε, enclitic postpositive particle, rarer in κοινή than in cl., giving special prominence to the word to which it is attached, distinguishing it as the least or the most important (Thayer, see word),
indeed, at least, even (but not always translatable into English);
__1. used alone: Luk.11:8 18:5 Rom.8:32.
__2. More frequently with other particles: αλλά γε, Luk.24:21, 1Co.9:2; ἄρα γε, Mat.7:20 17:26, Act.17:27; ἆρά γε, Act.8:30; εἴ γε (Rec. εἴγε), 2Co.5:3, Gal.3:4, Eph.3:2 4:21, Col.1:23 (see Meyer, Ellic., on Ga, Eph, ll. with; Lft., on Ga, Col, ll. with); εἰ δὲ μήγε, following an affirmation, Mat.6:1, Luk.10:6 13:9; a negation, Mat.9:17, Luk.5:36, 37 14:32, 2Co.11:16; καί γε (Rec. καίγε, cl. καὶ . . . γε), Luk.19:42 (WH om.), Act.2:18 17:27; καίτοιγε (L καίτοι γε, Tr. καί τοι γε), Jhn.4:2; μενοῦνγε (see see word); μήτι γε, see: μήτι; ὄφελόν, 1Co.4:8.
† (AS)

---

LSJ / STEPBible (TFLSJ)
γε,
Doric dialect and Boeotian dialect γα, enclitic Particle, giving emphasis to the word or words which it follows.

__I
with single words, at least, at any rate, but often only to be rendered by italics in writing, or emphasis in pronunciation: τὸ γὰρ.. σιδήρου γε κράτος ἐστίν such is the power of iron, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 9.393]]; εἴ που πτωχῶν γε θεοὶ.. εἰσίν if the poor have any gods to care for them,[Refs [17.475; μάλιστά γε 4.366]]; ὅ γ᾽ ἐνθάδε λεώς at any rate the people here, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Coloneus” 42, etc.: with negatives, οὐ δύο γε]] not even two, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 5.303, 20.286]]; οὔκουν φθόγγος γε not the least sound, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Iphigenia Aulidensis” 9.]]

__I.2
with Pronouns: with pronoun of 1st pers. [Refs 8th c.BC+ [4th c.AD: Perses Epigrammaticus so closely joined, that the accent is changed, in ἔγωγε, ἔμοιγε (also ἔγωγα _Laconian dialect_, but ἐγώνγα, ἰώνγα _Boeotian dialect_): in 8th c.BC: Homerus Epicus frequently with _Article_ used as _pronoun_, see at {ὅ γε}: with _demonstrative_ Pronouns, κεῖνός γε, τοῦτό γε, etc.: in Comedy texts coalescing with -ί final, αὑτηγί 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Acharnenses” 784]]; τουτογί, ταυταγί, etc., [Refs 8th c.BC+ [[prev. author] “V.” 781, “Pax” 1057, etc. (but ἐνγεταυθί “Th.” 646): after possess. Pronouns, ἐμόν γε θυμόν 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 20.425, etc.: frequently after _relative_ Pronouns, ὅς γε, οἵ γε, etc., οἵ γέ σου καθύβρισαν 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Philoctetes” 1364; ὅς γ᾽ ἐξέλυσας δασμόν [prev. author] “OT” 35, etc.]]; ὅσον γε χρῄζεις even as much as..,[Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. work] 365; οἷόν γέ μοι φαίνεται 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 329a]]: rarely with interrogative Pronouns, τίνα γε.. εἶπας ;[Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Troades” 241]]; ποίου γε τούτου πλήν γ᾽ Ὀδυσσέως ἐρεῖς ; [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Philoctetes” 441.]]

__I.3
after Conjunctions, to emphasize the modification or condition introduced by the subjoined clause, πρίν γε, before at least, sometimes repeated, οὐ μὲν.. ὀΐω πρίν γ᾽ ἀποπαύσεσθαι, πρίν γε.. αἵματος ἆσαι Ἀρῆα [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 5.288, compare 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 2.127]]; πρὶν ἄν γε or πρίν γ᾽ ἄν, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Equites” 961, “Ra.” 78, etc.; ὅτε γε 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Phaedo” 84e; ὁπότε γε 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Coloneus” 1699; ἐπεί γε 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 1.3.9; ἐπειδή γε 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 6.18; ὅπου γε 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 2.3.11]]; εἴ γε, ἐάν γε, if that is to say, if really, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 6.18, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Phaedrus” 252c]]; also simply to lay stress on the condition, κἄν γε μὴ λέγω and if I do not.., [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Acharnenses” 317]]; εἴπερ γε if at any rate, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 7.16.γ, 143]], etc.; ὥστε γε (variant{ὥς γε}), with infinitive, so far at least as to.., [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Phaedrus” 230b; ὥς γ᾽ ἐμοὶ χρῆσθαι κριτῇ 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Alcestis” 801]]; ὥς γε or ὥσπερ γε as at least, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Antigone” 570, “OT” 715, etc.]]:—γε may follow τε, when τε is closely attached to the preceding word, ὡς οἷόν τέ γε μάλιστα [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Memorabilia” 4.5.2, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 412b; ἐάντε γε [prev. author] “Plt.” 293d; οἵ τέ γε [prev. author] “Grg.” 454e:—for its use in opposed or disjunctive clauses, see below 11.3.]]

__I.4
after other Particles, καὶ μὴν.. γε, οὐ μὴν.. γε, with words intervening, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Memorabilia” 1.4.12, 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Alcestis” 518, etc.]]; after ἄν in apodosi, when preceded by οὐ or καί, [Refs [[prev. author] “Ph.” 1215, “Or.” 784]]; ἄταρ.. γε but yet, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Acharnenses” 448]]; καίτοι γε, see at {καί το; ἀλλά γε} (without intervening words) is falsa lectio in [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Hp.Ma.” 287b (to be read ἀλλ᾽ ἄγε), “R.” 331b (ἀλλά γε ἕν codices, ἀλλὰ ἕν γε 5th c.AD: Stobaeus, Joannes)]]; ἀλλά γε δή uncertain in [Refs 1st c.AD+ [[prev. author] “Phdr.” 262a; later, 1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus 2.394c, 2nd-3rd c.AD: Aelianus “De Natura Animalium - Ar.Byzantine Epit.” 10.49 codices: but,]]

__I.5
when preceding other Particles, γε commonly refers to the preceding word, while the Particle retains its own force: but sometimes modifies the sense of the following Particle, γε μήν nevertheless, πάντως γε μήν [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Equites” 232, compare 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Electra” 754, 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus, etc.]]; Epic dialect and Ionic dialect γε μέν [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 2.703, 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 4.195, 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 7.152; γε μὲν δή 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Agamemnon” 661, 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Trachiniae” 484; γε μέντοι 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Theaetetus” 164a, 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 2.3.9, etc.: γε δή]] frequently strengthens an assertion, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Prometheus Vinctus” 42, 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 2.62, etc.; οἰόμεθά γε δή 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Euthydemus” 275a (compare also 11.1)]]; γέ τοι, implying that the assertion is the least that one can say, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Vespae” 934, “Pl.” 424, 1041, etc.; γέ τοι 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Gorgias” 447b; γέ τοι δή 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Tyrannus” 1171, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Phaedrus” 264b; γέ τοί που [prev. author] “Lg.” 888e; γε δήπου [prev. author] “Phd.” 94a, etc.]]; γέ που at all events, any how, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Acharnenses” 896, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 607d, 478a, etc.]]; for γε οὖν, see at {γοῦν}.

__II
exercising an influence over the whole clause:

__II.1
epexegetic, namely, that is, Διός γε διδόντος that is if God grant it, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 1.390]]; κλῦθι, Ποσείδαον.., εἰ ἐτεόν γε σός εἰμι if indeed I am really thine, [Refs [9.529: hence to limit, strengthen or amplify a general assertion, ἀνὴρ.. ὅστις πινυτός γε]] any man—at least any wise man, [Refs [1.229]]; frequently preceded by καί, usually with words intervening, ἦ μὴν κελεύσω κἀπιθωΰξω γε πρός ay and besides that.., [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Prometheus Vinctus” 73]]; παρῆσάν τινες καὶ πολλοί γε some, ay and a great many, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Phaedo” 58d; καὶ γελοίως γε [prev. author] “R.” 531a]]; frequently with the last term in an enumeration, ταύτῃ ἄρα.. πρακτέον καὶ γυμναστέον καὶ ἐδεστέον γε καὶ ποτέον [[prev. author] “Cri.” 47b; ὄψεις τε καὶ ἀκοαὶ καὶ.. καὶ ἡδοναί γε δή [prev. author] “Tht.” 156b; repeated, συνήγαγόν μοι καί γε ἀργύριον καί γε χρυσίον LXX.Eccl.2.8]; rarely without intervening words, καί γε ὁ θάνατος διὰ τὴν μοίρην ἔλαχεν [NT+5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Hippocrates Medicus “περὶ ἑπταμήνου” 9, compare 5th c.BC: Lysias Orator 11.7 codices; καί γε.. ἐκχεῶ NT.Act.2.18: hence,]]

__II.2
in dialogue, in answers where something is added to the statement of the previous speaker, as ἔπεμψέ τίς σοι.. κρέα; Answ. καλῶς γε ποιῶν yes and quite right too, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Acharnenses” 1049]]; κενὸν τόδ᾽ ἄγγος, ἢ στέγει τι; Answ. σά γ᾽ ἔνδυτα.. yes indeed, your clothes, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Ion” 1412]]; οὕτω γὰρ ἂν μάλιστα δηχθείη πόσις. Answ. σὺ δ᾽ ἂν γένοιο γ᾽ ἀθλιωτάτη γυνή yes truly, and you.., [Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. author] “Med.” 817, compare 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Tyrannus” 680, etc.]]; πάνυ γε yes certainly, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Euthyphro” 8e, etc.]]; οὕτω γέ πως yes somehowso, [Refs [[prev. author] “Tht.” 165c]]; sometimes preceded by καί, καὶ οὐδέν γ᾽ ἄτοπον yes and no wonder, [Refs [[prev. work] 142b, compare d, 147e]]; sometimes ironically, εὖ γε κηδεύεις πόλιν [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Iphigenia Taurica” 1212.]]

__II.3
to heighten a contrast or opposition,

__II.3.a
after conditional clauses, εἰ μὲν δὴ σύ γ᾽.., τῷ κε Ποσειδάων γε.. if you do so, then at all events Poseidon will.., [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 15.49]] {γέα}; ἐπεὶ πρὸς τοῦτο σιωπᾶν ἥδιόν σοι.. τόδε γε εἰπέ at any rate tell me this, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 5.5.20; εἰ μὴ τὸ ὅλον, μέρος γ᾽ ἐπιβάλλει 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 18.272:—sometimes in the protasis, εἰ γὰρ μὴ ἑκόντες γε.. ἀλλ᾽ ἀέκοντας.. 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 4.120.]]

__II.3.b
in disjunctive sentences to emphasize an alternative, ἤτοι κεῖνόν γε.. δεῖ ἀπόλλυσθαι ἢ σέ.. [Refs 8th c.BC+ [[prev. author] 1.11; ἤτοι κρίνομέν γε ἢ ἐνθυμούμεθα ὀρθῶς τὰ πράγματα 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 2.40; πατὴρ δ᾽ ἐμός.. ζώει ὅ γ᾽ ἢ τέθνηκε 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 2.131, compare 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 10.504]]: also in the second clause, εἰπέ μοι, ἠὲ ἑκὼν ὑποδάμνασαι ἤ σέ γε λαοὶ ἐχθαίρουσι [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 3.214, compare 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 7.10.θ, 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Tyrannus” 1098f]]

__II.4
in exclamations, etc., ὥς γε μή ποτ᾽ ὤφελον λαβεῖν uncertain in [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Iphigenia Aulidensis” 70, compare 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Coloneus” 977, “Ph.” 1003, 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Acharnenses” 93, 836, etc.]]; in oaths, οὔτοι μὰ τὴν Δήμητρά γ᾽ variant in [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Equites” 698; μὰ τὸν Ποσειδῶ γ᾽ οὐδέποτ᾽ [prev. author] “Ec.” 748; καὶ ναὶ μὰ Δία γε 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Apologia Socratis” 20; καὶ νὴ Δία γε 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Equites” 1350, 1st-2nd c.AD: Dio Chrysostomus Sophista 17.4, 2nd c.AD: Lucianus Sophista “Merc.Cond.” 28, 4th c.AD: Libanius Sophista “Orationes” 11.59, etc.: with words intervening, καὶ νὴ Δί᾽, ὦ ἄνδρες Ἀθηναῖοι, ἕτεροί γε.. 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 13.16; νὴ Δία, ὦ Ἀθηναῖοι, ὥρα γε ὑμῖν 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Historia Graeca (Hellenica)” 7.1.37]]; merely in strong assertions, τίς ἂν φιλέοντι μάχοιτ; ἄφρων δὴ κεῖνός γέ.. [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 8.209, etc.]]

__II.5
implying concession, εἶμί γε well then I will go (in apodosi), [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Hercules Furens” 861; δρᾶ γ᾽ εἴ τι δράσεις [prev. author] “IA” 817, compare “Andr.” 239.]]

__III
γε frequently repeated in protasis and apodosis, as πρίν γε.., πρίν γε, see[Refs 5th c.BC+ [above 1.3; εἰ μή γε.. τινὶ μείζονι, τῇ γε παρούσῃ ἀτιμίᾳ 5th c.BC: Lysias Orator 31.29]]; even in the same clause, οὐδέν γ᾽ ἄλλο πλήν γε καρκίνους [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Vespae” 1507, compare 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.187, 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Phoenissae” 554, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 335b, “Grg.” 502a.]]

__IV
POSITION: γε normally follows the word which it limits; but is frequently placed immediately after the Article, as ὅ γε πόλεμος [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 1.66, etc.]]; or the preposition, κατά γε τὸν σὸν λόγον [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 3.1.15; ἔν γε ταῖς Θήβαις 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Tyrannus” 1380; or δέ, νῦν δέ γε 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Theaetetus” 144e]]; τὸ δέ γε[Refs [[prev. work] 164b; δοῖμεν δέ γέ που ἄν [prev. author] “R.” 607d, compare “Phd.” 94a, etc.]]; frequently in retorts, ἁμές ποκ᾽ ἦμες ἄλκιμοι νεανίαι. Answ. ἁμὲς δέ γ᾽ εἰμές [Refs [“Carmina Popularia” 18]]; οὐκ οἶδ᾽ ὅτι λέγεις. Answ. ἡ γραῦς δέ γε οἶδ᾽, ὡς ἐγῷμαι [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-3rd c.BC: Menander Comicus “Ἐπιτρέποντες” 577, compare 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Septem contra Thebas” 1031, etc.]]

deep_entry:

γέεννα (γέενα, Mrk.9:45, Rec.), -ης, ἡ (perh. through Aram. גֵּיהִנָּם, from Heb. גֵּי הִנֹּם, Neh.11:30; גֵּי בֶּן־הִנֹּם, Jhn.18:16; גֵּי בּנֵי־הִנֹּם, 4Ki.23:10; valley of (the son, sons of) lamentation);
[in LXX the nearest approach to γ. is γαίεννα, Jos.18:16 (Γαὶ Ὀννόμ, A), elsewhere φάραγξ Ὀνόμ (Jos.15:8, al.), V. Swete on Mrk.9:43 ;]
Gehenna, a valley W. and S. of Jerusalem, which as the site of fire-worship from the time of Ahaz, was desecrated by Josiah and became a dumping-place for the offal of the city. Later, the name was used as a symbol of the place of future punishment, as in NT: Mat.5:29, ; 10:28, Mrk.9:43, 45 47, Luk.12:5, Jas.3:6; γ. τ. πυρός, Mat.5:22 18:19, prob. with ref. to fires of Moloch (DB, ii, 119b); υἱὸς γεέννης, Mat.23:15; κρίσις γεέννης, 23:33.†
(AS)

with accusative, deride, τινά [Refs 5th c.BC+ [3rd c.BC: Theocritus Poeta Bucolicus 20.1; ἢ τόδε γελᾶτε, εἰ..; 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Symposium” 2.19]]; τί δὲ τοῦτ᾽ ἐγέλασας ἐτεόν; what is this you are laughing at? in Logic, opposed to εἶδος (species), [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Parmenides” 129c, +others, 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Topica” 102a31, 102b12, +others; τὰ γ. εἰς εἴδη πλείω καὶ διαφέροντα διαιρεῖται [prev. author] “Metaphorical” 1059b36.]]

short_definition: to be — γίνομαι, Ion. and κοινή for Att. γίγν- (M. Pr., 47; Bl., §6, 8 Mayser, 166 f.),
deep_entry:
Abbott-Smith / STEPBible (TBESG)
γίνομαι, Ion. and κοινή for Att. γίγν- (M. Pr., 47; Bl., §6, 8 Mayser, 166 f.),
[in LXX chiefly for היה ;]
__1. of persons, things occurrences, to come into being, be born, arise, come on: Jhn.1:15 8:58, 1Co.15:37; a first appearance in public, Mrk.1:4, Jhn.1:6, al.; before ἐκ (of birth), Rom.1:3, Gal.4:4; διά, Jhn.1:3; βροντή, Jhn.12:29; σεισμός, Rev.6:12; γογγυσμός, Act.6:1; χαρά, Act.8:8, many other similar exx.; ἡμέρα, Luk.22:66, al.; ὀψέ, Mrk.11:19; πρωΐα, Mat.27:1; νύξ, Act.27:27.
__2. Of events, to come to pass, take place, happen: Mat.5:18, Mrk.5:14, Luk.1:20 2:15, Act.4:21, 2Ti.2:18, al.; μὴ γένοιτο [LXX for חָלִילָה, Jhn.22:29, al.], far be it, God forbid: Rom.3:4 (ICC, in l.), 1Co.6:15 and frequently in Pl.; καὶ ἐγένετο, ἐγένετο δέ ([in LXX for וַיְהִי ;] see Burton, 142 f.; M, Pr., 16f.; Dalman, Words, 32 f.; Robertson, Gr., 1042 f.), with indic, Mat.7:28, Luk.1:8, al.; before καί and indic., Luk.8:1, Act.5:7, al.; with accusative and inf., Mrk.2:23, Luk.3:21, al.; ὡς δὲ ἐγένετο, before τοῦ with inf., Act.10:25; with dative of person(s), to befall one: with inf., Act.20:16; with accusative and inf., Act.22:6; with adv., εὖ, Eph.6:3; τ́ ἐγένετο αὐτῷ (Field, Notes, 115), Act.7:40 (LXX); before εἰς, Act.28:6.
__3. to be made, done, performed, observed, enacted, ordained, etc.: Mat.6:10 19:8, Mrk.2:27 11:23, Act.19:26, al.; before διά with genitive, Mrk.6:2, Act.2:43; ὑπό, Luk.13:17; ἐκ, Luk.4:23; ἐν, 1Co.9:15; ἀπογραφή, Luk.2:2; ἀνάκρισις Act.25:26; ἄφεσις, Heb.9:22; ὁ νόμος, Gal.3:17; τὸ πάσχα, Mat.26:2.
__4. to become, be made, come to be: with pred., Mat.4:3, Luk.4:3, Jhn.2:9, 1Co.13:11, al.; before ὡς, ὡσεί, Mat.10:25, Mrk.9:26; εἰς (M, Pr., 71f.), Mrk.12:1o, al.; with genitive Rev.11:15; id., of age, Luk.2:42; with dative, γ. ἀνδρί ([LXX for הָיָה לְאִישׁ, Rut.1:12, al. ;] see Field, Notes, 156), Rom.7:3, 4; before ἐν, Act.22:17, Rev.1:10, al.; ἐπάνω, Luk.19:19; μετά, with genitive, Mrk.16:[10], Act.9:19; before εἰς, ἐπί (Field, Notes, 135), κατά (ib., 62), with accusative of place, Act.20:16 21:35 27:7, al.; before ἐκ, Mrk.9:7, Luk.3:22, 2Th.2:7, al. Aoristic pf. γέγονα (M, Pr., 52, 145f.; Field, Notes, 1f.), Mat.25:6, Luk.10:36, al. Aor. ἐγενήθη (for ἐγένετο, M, Pr., 139f.; Mayser, 379), Mat.11:23, al. (Cf. απο-, δια-, επι-, παρα-, συμ-, παρα-, προ-.)
(AS)

γίγνομαι,
Ionic dialect and after [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus]] γίνομαι [ῑ], (Attic dialect Inscrr. have γιγν- in fifth and fourth cententury,[Refs [compare “IG” 2.11.9, 1055.25, etc.)]]; Thess. γίνυμαι [Refs [“IG” 9(2).517.22]]; Boeotian dialect γίνιουμαι [Refs [[prev. work]7.3303:]]future γενήσομαι: aorist ἐγενόμην (ἐγενάμην [LXX.Jer.14.1, +others] (προ-) Decrees Byzantine cited in [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 18.90)]], Ionic dialect 2nd pers. singular γένευ [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 5.897]], 3rd.pers. singular γενέσκετο [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 11.208, ἔγεντο 8th-7th c.BC: Hesiodus Epicus “Theogonia” 705, 7th-6th c.BC: Sappho Lyrica 16, 5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “P.” 3.87, 4th-5th c.BC: Parmenides Poeta Philosophus 8.20, “IG” 4.492 (from Mycenae), probably in “Scol.” 19]]; Epic dialect γέντο [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th-7th c.BC: Hesiodus Epicus “Theogonia” 199, 5th c.BC: Empedocles Poeta Philosophus 98.5, 3rd c.BC: Callimachus Epicus “Hymnus in Jovem” 1.50, 3rd c.BC: Theocritus Poeta Bucolicus 14.27, etc.]] (gṇ-το): perfect γέγονα [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 19.122, etc.]]: 3rd.pers. plural γέγοναν [NT.Rev.21.6]: pluperfect ἐγεγόνει [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Lysias Orator 31.17, etc.]]; Ionic dialect ἐγεγόνεε [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 2.2]]; Epic dialect forms (as if from perfect γέγᾰα), 2nd pers. plural γεγάᾱτε [Refs 8th c.BC+ [Batrachomyomachia 143; γεγάᾱσι 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 4.325, frequently in 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey”: _3rd.pers._ _plural_ γεγᾱκᾰσιν conjecture in 5th c.BC: Empedocles Poeta Philosophus 23.10: _3rd.pers._ _dual_]]pluperfect ἐκ-γεγάτην [ᾰ] [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 10.138]]; infinitive γεγάμεν [ᾰ] [Refs 8th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “O.” 9.110, (ἐκ) 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 5.248, etc.]]; participle γεγᾰώς -ᾰυῖα, plural -ᾰῶτες, -ᾰυῖαι [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Homerus Epicus, etc.]], contraction γεγώς, -ῶσα [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Ajax” 472, 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Medea” 406]]; infinitive γεγᾱκειν [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “O.” 6.49]]: middle forms ἐκγεγάασθε epigram [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Homerus Epicus 16, ἐκ-γεγάονται (in _future_ sense) “hymnus ad Venerem” 197 (assuming variant)]]:—passive forms, future γενηθήσομαι (only in [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Parmenides” 141e, οὔτε γενήσεται, οὔτε γενηθήσεται,compare 5th c.AD: Proclus Philosophus “in Platonis Parmenidem commentarii” p.963 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus)]]: aorist ἐγενήθην [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Epicharmus Comicus 209, 4th c.BC: Archytas Tarentinus Philosophus 1, 5th c.BC: Hippocrates Medicus “ἐπιδημίαι” 6.8.32, 7.3]], later Attic dialect, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-3rd c.BC: Philemo Comicus 95.2 and 167, “IG” 2.630b10 (1st c.BC)]] and Hellenistic Gk., [Refs 2nd c.BC+ [2nd c.BC: Polybius Historicus 2.67.8, 1st c.BC: Diodorus Siculus Historicus 13.51]]: perfect γεγένημαι [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Simonides Lyricus 69]], frequently in Attic dialect Poets and Prose, in Attic dialect inscription first in 4th C, [Refs [“IG” 2.555]]: 3rd.pers. plural γεγενέανται [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-3rd c.BC: Philetas cited in 12th c.AD: Eustathius Episcopus Thessalonicensis 1885.51]]: pluperfect ἐγεγένητο [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 7.18, +others]]; compare γείνομαι:—come into a new state of being: hence,

__I
absolutely, come into being opposed to εἶναι, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Empedocles Poeta Philosophus 17.11, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Phaedo” 102e, compare “Ti.” 29a]]; and so,

__I.1
of persons, to be born, νέον γεγαώς new born, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 19.400]]; ὑπὸ Τμώλῳ γεγαῶτας born (and so living) under Tmolus, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 2.866; ἢ πρόσθε θανεῖν ἢ ἔπειτα γ. 8th-7th c.BC: Hesiodus Epicus “Opera et Dies” 175]]; γιγνομέναισι λάχη τάδ᾽.. ἐκράνθη at our birth, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Eumenides” 347; γ. ἔκ τινος 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 5.548, 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 7.11; πατρὸς ἐκ ταὐτοῦ 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Iphigenia Aulidensis” 406, compare 5th-6th c.BC: Isocrates Orator 5.136; σέθεν.. ἐξ αἵματος 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Septem contra Thebas” 142; less frequently ἀπό τινος 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 8.22, etc.; ἐσθλῶν 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Hecuba” 380, etc.]]; γεγονέναι κακῶς, καλῶς, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Equites” 218, 5th-6th c.BC: Isocrates Orator 7.37, etc.]]; κάλλιον, εὖ, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.146, 3.69]]; τὸ μὴ γενέσθαι not to have been born, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Fragmenta - American Journal of Philology” 401: frequently with Numerals, ἔτεα τρία καὶ δέκα γεγονώς 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.119; ἀμφὶ τὰ πέντε ἢ ἑκκαίδεκα ἔτη γενόμενος 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 1.4.16; γεγονὼς ἔτη περὶ πεντήκοντα 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 21.154]]; οἱ ὑπὲρ τὰ στρατεύσιμα ἔτη γεγονότες those of an age beyond.., [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 1.2.4: with _genitive_, γεγονὼς πλειόνων ἐτῶν ἢ πεντήκοντα 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Leges” 951c, etc.]]: rarely with ordinals, ὀγδοηκοστὸν ἔτος γεγονώς [Refs 1st c.AD+ [2nd c.AD: Lucianus Sophista “Macr.” 22, compare 1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus “Philopoemen” 18.]]

__I.2
of things, to be produced, ὅσα φύλλα καὶ ἄνθεα γίγνεται ὥρῃ [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 9.51]]; opposed to ὄλλυσθαι, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Parmenides Poeta Philosophus 8.13, 40]]; opposed to ἀπόλλυσθαι, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Anaxagoras Philosophus 17, compare 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 527b, etc.]]; opposed to ἀπολείπειν, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Diogenes Cynicus Philosophus]] Apoll.7; opposed to ἀπολήγειν, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Empedocles Poeta Philosophus 17.30; τὰ γιγνόμενα καὶ ἐξ ὧν γίγνεται 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Philebus” 27a; ἁπλῇ διηγήσει ἢ διὰ μιμήσεως γ. [prev. author] “R.” 392d; ὁ ἐκ τῆς χώρας γιγνόμενος σῖτος 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Memorabilia” 3.6.13; τὰ ἐν ἀγρῷ γιγνόμενα [prev. work] 2.9.4]]; of profits, καρποὶ οἱ ἐξ ἀγελῶν γ. [Refs [[prev. author] “Cyr.” 1.1.2, etc.]]; τὰ ἆθλα ἀπὸ τεττάρων ταλάντων ἐγένοντο were the produce of, i.e. were worth, [Refs [4 talents, [prev. author] “HG” 4.2.7]]; τὸ ἀπὸ τῶν αἰχμαλώτων γενόμενον ἀργύριον produced by [the ransom of].., [Refs [[prev. author] “An.” 5.3.4]]; of sums, ὁ γεγονὼς ἀριθμὸς τῶν ψήφων the total of the votes, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Apologia” 36a; ἕκατον εἴκοσι στατήρων γίγνονται τρισχίλιαι τριακόσιαι ἑξήκοντα [δραχμαί] 120]] staters amount to [Refs 4th c.BC+ [3, 360 drachmae, 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 34.24]]; so in in Mathematics texts, of products, ὁ ἐξ αὐτῶν γενόμενος ἀριθμός [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [3rd c.BC: Euclides Geometra 7.24]]; ἀριθμὸς γενόμενος ἑκατοντάκις multiplied[Refs 3rd c.AD+ [by 100, 3rd c.AD(?): Pappus Mathematicus 10.13]]; of times of day, ὡς ἡ ἡμέρα ἐγένετο [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 7.81, etc.; ἕως ἂν φῶς γένηται 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Protagoras” 311a; ἅμα ἕῳ γιγνομένῃ 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 4.32]]; of Time in general, elapse, διέτης χρόνος ἐγεγόνεε ταῦτα πρήσσουσι [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 2.2; χρόνου γενομένου 1st c.BC: Diodorus Siculus Historicus 20.109.]]

__I.2.b
falldue, οἱ γιγνόμενοι δασμοί [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 1.1.8; τοὺς τόκους τοὺς γ. 5th-6th c.BC: Isocrates Orator 17.37]]; τὸ τίμημα τὸ γ., τὸ γ. ἀργύριον, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 24.82, Syngr. cited in [same work] 35.11; τὸ γ. μέρος 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Historia Graeca (Hellenica)” 7.4.33; τὸ γ. τοῖ πλήθι τᾶς ζαμίαυ “IG” 5(2).6 A 20 (Tegea, 4th c.BC)]]: with dative, τὸ γ. τινὶ ἔλαιον [Refs 2nd c.BC+ [“UPZ” 19.32 (2nd c.BC)]]; τοῖς γείτοσι τὸ γ. [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-3rd c.BC: Theophrastus Philosophus “Fragmenta” 97; τὰ γ.]]dues, [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [PHib. 1.92 and 111 (3rd c.BC): hence γιγνόμενος]] regular, normal, τίμημα, χάρις, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 38.25]]; ἐν ταῖς γ. ἡμέραις in the usual number of days, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 5.4.51]]; frequently in later Gk., as [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd c.AD: Lucianus Sophista “Tox.” 18, etc.]]

__I.3
of events, take place, come to pass, and in past tenses to be, καί σφιν ἄχος κατὰ θυμὸν ἐγίγνετο [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 13.86, etc.; μάχη ἐγεγόνει 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Charmides” 153b, etc.; ἐκεχειρία γίγνεταί τισι πρὸς ἀλλήλους 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 4.58; ἡ νόσος ἤρξατο γίγνεσθαι [prev. author] 2.47; πνεῦμα εἰώθει γ. [prev. work] 84]]; τὰ Ὀλύμπια γίγνεται, τραγῳδοὶ γίγνονται, are held, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Historia Graeca (Hellenica)” 7.4.28, 4th c.BC: Aeschines Orator 3.41, etc.]]; ψήφισμα γ. is passed, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 2.2.21]]; πιστὰ γ., ὅρκοι γ., pledges are given, oaths taken,[Refs 4th c.BC+ [[prev. work] 7.4.3, 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 19.158]]; γίγνεταί τι ὑπό τινος (masculine), [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 7.1.30, (_neuter_) 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Theaetetus” 200e; τὰ γιγνόμενα ὑπὸ τῶν Ἀθηναίων 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 6.88; τὰ γενόμενα ἐξ ἀνθρώπων 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus “Praef.”; ὕβρισμα ἐκ τῶν Σαμίων γενόμενον [prev. author] 3.48; ἀπό τινος γ. 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 5.6.30; παρά τινος 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 614a]]; ὃ μὴ γένοιτο which God forbid, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 10.27, 28.21]]; but γένοιτο, = [“Amen”, LXX.Isa.25.1]; γένοιτο γένοιτο[LXX.Psa.71(72).19: in Mathematics texts, γεγονέτω] suppose it done, [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [3rd c.BC: Euclides Geometra 6.23, etc.; short_definition: to know — γινώσκω (= γιγν-: see previous word. So also vulgar Attic, in Inscr., see Thumb, MGV, 207),
root_and_cognates: LSJ-hänvisningar: ἀναγιγνώσκω, τὴν γνώμην λ, εἰδέναι χάριν
deep_entry:
Abbott-Smith / STEPBible (TBESG)
γινώσκω (= γιγν-: see previous word. So also vulgar Attic, in Inscr., see Thumb, MGV, 207),
[in LXX chiefly for ידע ;]
to be taking in knowledge, come to know, recognize, perceive, understand; in past tenses to know, realize; pass., to become known: with accusative, Mat.22:18, Mrk.5:43, Col.4:8, 1Th.3:5, al. Pass., Mat.10:26, Php.4:5, al.; before ὅτι, Mat.21:45, Jhn.4:1, al.; τί, Mat.6:3; ἀπό, Mrk.15:45; ὅ, Rom.7:15; τ. λεγόμενα, Luk.18:34; τ. θέλημα, Luk.12:47; τ. καρδίας, Luk.16:15; with accusative of person(s), of recognition by God, 1Co.8:3, Gal.4:9; by Christ, neg., Mat.7:23; frequently of the knowledge of divine things, of God and Christ; τ. θεόν, Rom.1:21 Gal.4:9; τ. πατέρα, Jhn.8:55; τ. κύριον, Heb.8:1 (LXX); νοῦν κυρίου, Rom.11:34; Χριστόν, Jhn.17:3, 1Jn.3:6; τὰ τοῦ πνεύματος, 1Co.2:14; τ. πνεύμα, 1Jn.4:6; τ. ἀλήθειαν, Jhn.8:32; of Christ's knowledge of the Father (ἐπιγ.), Mat.11:27 (Dalman, Words, 282ff.). In Hellenistic writers [LXX for Heb. ידע, Gal.4:1, al.], of sexual intercourse, to know carnally: Mat.1:25, Luk.1:34 (Cremer, 153).
SYN.: γ., to know by observation and experience is thus prop. disting. from οἶδα, to know by reflection (a mental process, based on  intuition or information); cf. also ἐφίστημι, συνίημι. (Cf. ἀνα-, δια-, ἐπι-, κατα-, προ-γινώσκω.) (AS)

γνώμη, -ης, ἡ
(γιγνώσκω), [in LXX: Da TH 2:15 (דָּת), Ps 82(83):3 (סוֹד), elsewhere, chiefly II Es, for טְעֵם ;]
__1. a means of knowing, a token (Theogn.).
__2. In Attic writers, the mind, its operations and results (see Edwards, Lex., App., A);
__(a) mind, understanding;
__(b) purpose, intention: Act.20:3;
__(with) judgment, opinion: 1Co.1:10, Rev.17:13;
__(d) counsel, advice: 1Co.7:25, 40 2Co.8:10, Phm 14;
__(e) royal purpose, decree (as in Da, I and II Es): Rev.17:17 (Cremer, 671).
† (AS)

---

LSJ / STEPBible (TFLSJ)
γνώμ-η, ἡ,
means of knowing: hence, mark, token, [Refs 6th c.BC+ [6th c.BC: Theognis Elegiacus 60 (_plural_)]]; of the teeth [Refs 4th c.BC+ [compare (γνώμων 111), 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Historia Animalium” 576b15.]]

__II
organ by which one perceives or knows, intelligence,

__II.1
thought, judgement (τῆς ψυχῆς ἡ γ. [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Leges” 672b), ἐκμαθεῖν ψυχήν τε καὶ φρόνημα καὶ γ. 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Antigone” 176: _accusative_ _absolutely_, γνώμην ἱκανός]] intelligent, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 3.4]]; γ. ἀγαθός, κακός, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Tyrannus” 687, “Ph.” 910; τοιάδε τὴν γ. [prev. author] “El.” 1021; κατὰ γ. ἴδρις [prev. author] “OT” 1087 (Lyric poetry); γνώμᾳ διπλόαν θέτο βουλάν 5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “N.” 10.89; γνώμῃ μαθεῖν τι 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Coloneus” 403; γνώμῃ κυρήσας [prev. author] “OT” 398]]; γνώμῃ φρενῶν, opposed to ὀργῇ,[Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. work] 524; γνώμης ξύνεσις 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 1.75; γνώμης μᾶλλον ἐφόδῳ ἢ ἰσχύος [prev. author] 3.11; ταῖς γ. καὶ τοῖς σώμασι σφάλλεσθαι 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 1.3.10, compare 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 1.70]]; γνώμῃ, opposed to τύχῃ, σωφρονοῦντες [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Isocrates Orator 3.47]]; γνώμης ἅπτεσθαι affect the head, of wine or fever, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Hippocrates Medicus “περὶ διαίτης ὀξέων” 63, “Fract.” 11]]; γνώμην ἔχειν understand, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Electra” 214 (Lyric poetry), 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Acharnenses” 396; πάντων γ. ἴσχειν 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Philoctetes” 837 (Lyric poetry)]]; προσέχειν γνώμην give heed, attend, δεῦρο τὴν γ. προσίσχετε [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Eupolis Comicus 37; πρὸς ἕτερον γνώμην ἔχειν 4th c.BC: Aeschines Orator 3.192]]; to be on one's guard, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 1.95]]; δηλοῦν τὴν γ. ἔν τινι to show one's wit in.., [Refs 4th c.BC+ [[prev. author] 3.37; ἐν γνώμῃ τι παραστῆσαι 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 4.17]]; ἀπὸ γνώμης φέρειν ψῆφον δικαίαν with a good conscience, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Eumenides” 674]]; but οὐκ ἀπὸ γ. λέγεις not without judgement, with good sense, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Trachiniae” 389; ἄτερ γνώμης 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Prometheus Vinctus” 456; ἄνευ γ. 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Coloneus” 594]]; γνώμῃ κολάζειν with good reason, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 2.6.10]]; γνώμῃ τῇ ἀρίστῃ (i.e. κρίνειν or δικάζειν) to the best of one's judgement, in the dicasts' oath, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Rhetorica” 1375a29; ἡ καλουμένη γ. τοῦ ἐπιεικοῦς κρίσις ὀρθή [prev. author] “EN” 1143a19; so περὶ ὧν ἂν νόμοι μὴ ὦσι, γνώμῃ τῇ δικαιοτάτῃ κρινεῖν 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 20.118; γ. τῇ δ. δικάσειν ὀμωμόκασιν [prev. author] 23.96, compare 39.40; τῇ δ. γ. 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Politica” 1287a26]]; ὅστις γνώμῃ μὴ καθαρεύει has not a clear conscience, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Ranae” 355.]]

__II.2
will, disposition, inclination, εὐσεβεῖ γνώμᾳ [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “O.” 3.41; γ. Διός 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Prometheus Vinctus” 1003]]; ἐν γνώμῃ γεγονέναι τινί to stand high in his favour, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 6.37]]; πάσῃ τῇ γ. with all one's zeal, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 6.45; τίνα αὐτοὺς οἴεσθε γ. ἕξειν περὶ σφῶν αὐτῶν 5th-6th c.BC: Andocides Orator 1.104; γ. ἔ. περί τινα 5th c.BC: Lysias Orator 10.21]]; πρὸς τοὺς Ἀθηναίους τὴν γ. ἔχειν to be inclined towards.., [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 5.44]]; ἐμπιμπλάναι τὴν γ. τινός satisfy his wishes, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 1.7.8, compare “HG” 6.1.15 (_plural_)]]; ἀφ᾽ ἑαυτοῦ γνώμης on his own initiative, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 4.68]]; ἐκ μιᾶς γ. of one accord, with one consent, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 10.59; μιᾷ γνώμῃ 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 1.122, 6.17; διὰ μιᾶς γ. γίγνεσθαι 5th-6th c.BC: Isocrates Orator 4.139]]; κατὰ γνώμην according to one's mind or wishes, ὅταν τἀκεῖ θῶ κατὰ γνώμην ἐμήν [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Andromache” 737; ἄν τι μὴ κατὰ γ. ἐκβῇ 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 1.16: in _plural_, φίλιαι γνῶμαι]] friendly sentiments, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 9.4.]]

__III
judgement, opinion, βροτῶν γ. [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Parmenides Poeta Philosophus 8.61]]; ταύτῃ.. τῇ γνώμῃ πλεῖστός εἰμι I in cline mostly to this view, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 7.220 (assuming variant); also ταύτῃ πλεῖστος τὴν γνώμην εἰμί [prev. author] 1.120; ἡ πλείστη γ. ἐστί τινι [prev. author] 5.126; τλέον φέρει ἡ γ. τινί [prev. author] 8.100; τὸ πλεῖστον τῆς γ. εἶχεν.. προσμεῖξαι 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 3.31; γνώμην τίθεσθαι 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 3.80]]; οὕτως τὴν γ. ἔχειν to be of this opinion, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 7.15, compare 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 6.2.8, 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Nubes” 157; εἴ τινι γ. τοιαύτη παρειστήκει περὶ ἐμοῦ 5th-6th c.BC: Andocides Orator 1.54; τὴν αὐτὴν γ. ἔχειν 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 2.55]]; τῆς αὐτῆς γ. εἶναι, ἔχεσθαι, [Refs [[prev. author] 1.113, 140; ὁ αὐτὸς εἰμὶ τῇ γ. [prev. author] 3.38]]; κατὰ γ. τὴν ἐμήν in my judgement or opinion, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 2.26, 5.3; elliptically, κατά γε τὴν ἐμήν 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Ecclesiazusae” 153, compare 2nd c.BC: Polybius Historicus 18.1.18, 1st c.BC: Dionysius Halicarnassensis “de Isocrate” 3: _absolutely_, γνώμην ἐμήν 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Vespae” 983, “Pax” 232]]; παρὰ γνώμην τοῖς Ἕλλησιν ἐγένετο contrary to general opinion, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 4.40]]; but παρὰ γ. κινδυνευταί reckless venturers, [Refs [[prev. author] 1.70, compare 4.19]]; εἰπὲ μὴ παρὰ γ. ἐμοί either contrary to my wish, or contrary to your true opinion, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Agamemnon” 931, compare “Supp.” 454]]: frequently of opinions delivered publicly, ἑστάναι πρὸς τὴν γ. τινός [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 4.56]]; Θεμιστοκλέους γνώμῃ by the advice of [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus, [prev. author] 1.90, 93]]; γνώμην ἀποφαίνειν deliver an opinion, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.40]]; ἀποδείκνυσθαι[Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. work] 207; ἐκφαίνειν [prev. author] 5.36; τίθεσθαι 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Philoctetes” 1448 (_anapaest meter_), 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Ecclesiazusae” 658; ἀποφαίνεσθαι 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Supplices” 336; ποιεῖσθαι περί τινων 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 3.36]]; γνώμας κατέθεντο have made up their minds, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Parmenides Poeta Philosophus 8.53.]]

__III.b
verdict, ἡ τοῦ δικαστοῦ γ. [Refs 2nd c.BC+ [“IG” 4.364 (Corinth, 4th c.AD), compare 685.32 (_plural_, Cretan dialect, 2nd c.BC).]]

__III.2
proposition, motion, γνώμην εἰσφέρειν [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 3.80, 81; εἰπεῖν 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 8.68, etc.]]; (but γνώμας προτιθέναι hold a debate, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 3.36); γνῶμαι τρεῖς προεκέατο 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 3.83]]: frequently in Inscrr., resolution, [Refs [Inscriptiones Graecae 12.118.28, etc.; γ. στρατηγῶν [prev. work]22.27; Κλεισόφου καὶ συμπρυτάνεων [prev. work]1; ἡ ἐκφερομένη γ. [prev. work]1051c26; γνώμην νικᾶν]] carry a motion, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Vespae” 594, “Nu.” 432; κρατεῖν τῇ γ. 1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus “Coriolanus” 17.]]

__III.3
γνῶμαι, αἱ, practical maxims, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [1st c.AD(?): Heraclitus 78, 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Ajax” 1091, 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Memorabilia” 4.2.9, 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Rhetorica” 1395a11 (_sing._, 1394a22).]]

__III.4
in plural, fancies, illusions, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Ajax” 52.]]

__III.5

γράμμα, -τος, τό
(γράφω), [in LXX for סֵפֶר, etc. ;]
__1. that which is traced or drawn, a picture.
__2. that which is written;
__(1) a character, letter: Gal.6:11;
__(2) a writing, a written document;
__(a) a bill or account: Luk.16:6, 7;
__(b) a letter: Act.28:21;
__(with) τὰ ἱερὰ γ., the sacred writings, i.e. the OT: 2Ti.3:15 (so in Philo, Vit. Mos., iii, 39) ;
__(d) τὸ γ., the letter, the written word as an external authority in contrast with the direct influence of the Spirit as manifested in the new Covenant: Rom.2:27, 29 7:6, 2Co.3:6, 7;
__(3) τὰ γ., letters, i.e. learning: Jhn.7:15, Act.26:24. (In π. an illiterate person is very frequently referred to as γράμματα μ᾽̀ εἰδότης, and this "never means anything else than inability to write": MM, Exp., x; but see also Cremer, 166; DCG, i, 202; ii, 584.)
† (AS)

deep_entry:
Abbott-Smith / STEPBible (TBESG)
γράφω, [in LXX chiefly for כּתב ];
__1. to scrape, graze (Hom.), and later (Hdt.) to sketch, draw.
__2. to write;
__(a) of forming or tracing letters on writing material: Jhn.8:[6], Gal.6:11, 2Th.3:17;
__(b) to express in writing, commit to writing, record: Luk.1:63, Jhn.19:21, 22 Rev.1:11, 19 al.; of scripture as a standing authority (Deiss., BS, 112ff.), γέγραπται, it  stands written (Luther), Mat.4:4, Mrk.7:6, Luk.4:8, Rom.1:17, 1Co.1:31, al.; id. before ἐν, Mrk.1:2, Act.1:20, al.; with accusative, to write of: Jhn.1:46, Rom.10:5; before περί, Mat.26:24, Mrk.14:21, Jhn.5:46; al.; with dative (WM, §31, 4), Luk.18:31; id. before ἵνα (M, Pr., 207f.), Mrk.12:19, Luk.20:28; κατὰ τ. γεγραμμένον, 2Co.4:13; γεγραμμένον ἐστί, Jhn.2:17; ἐγράφη, Rom.4:24; ἐπ᾽ αὐτῷ γεγραμμένα, Jhn.12:16;
__(with) of writing directions or information, with dative of person(s): Rom.15:15, 2Co.7:12, al.;
__(d) of that which contains the record or message: βιβλίον, Mrk.10:4, Jhn.21:25, Rev.5:1; τίτλον, Jhn.19:19; ἐπιστολήν, Act.23:25; ἐντολήν, Mrk.10:5 (cf. ἀπο-, ἐγ-, ἐπι-, κατα-, προ-).
(AS)

consume, use up, ἡ φύσις δ. τὸν θορόν [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “de Generatione Animalium” 757a25; χρόνον εἴς τι 1st c.AD: Onosander (Onasander) Tacticus 1.5]]:—passive, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “de Generatione Animalium” 745a13]]; of time, [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd c.AD: Appianus Historicus “Αιβυκή” 130]]; destroy, consume, φλὸξ δ. πάντα [Refs 1st c.AD+ [1st c.AD: Philo Judaeus 2.208; ἄνεμος [πόλιν] ἐδαπάνησεν 2nd c.AD: Appianus Historicus “Bella Civilia” 1.94]]; of persons, to be destroyed, ὑπὸ θηρίων [Refs 1st c.AD+ [1st c.AD: Philo Judaeus 2.43]]; καθάπερ ὑπὸ πυρός[Refs 1st c.BC+ [[prev. work] 433; πρὸς θηρίων 2nd c.AD: Appianus Historicus “Bella Civilia” 5.79; ἐν ταρτάροις καὶ βαράθροις δαπανωμένους 1st c.BC: Dionysius Halicarnassensis 4.81]]; ὑπὸ νόσου or νόσῳ δαπανᾶσθαι [Refs 1st c.AD+ [1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus “Galba” 17, 4th c.AD: Libanius Sophista “Orationes” 55.27:]] —middle, πυρὶ καὶ φόνῳ καὶ σιδήρῳ πάντα δαπανήσασθαι Eun.[prev. cited]

deep_entry:
Abbott-Smith / STEPBible (TBESG)
δέ (before vowels δ᾽; on the general neglect of the elision in NT, see WH, App., 146; Tdf., Pr., 96),
post-positive conjunctive particle;
__1. copulative, but, in the next place, and, now (Abbott, JG, 104): Mat.1:2ff., 2Co.6:15, 16, 2Pe.1:5-7; in repetition for emphasis, Rom.3:21, 22, 9:30, 1Co.2:6, Gal.2:2, Php.2:8; in transition to something new, Mat.1:18, 2:19, Luk.13:1, Jhn.7:14, Act.6:1, Rom.8:28, 1Co.7:1 8:1, al.; in explanatory parenthesis or addition, Jhn.3:19, Rom.5:8, 1Co.1:12, Eph.2:4, 5:32, al.; ὡς δέ, Jhn.2:9; καὶ . . . δέ, but also, Mat.10:18, Luk.1:76, Jhn.6:51, Rom.11:23, al.; καὶ ἐὰν δέ, yea even if, Jhn.8:16.
__2. Adversative, but, on the other hand, prop., answering to a foregoing μέν (which see), and distinguishing a word or clause from one preceding (in NT most frequently without μέν; Bl., §77, 12): ἐὰν δέ, Mat.6:14, 23, al.; ἐγὼ (σὺ, etc.) δέ, Mat.5:22, 6:6, Mrk.8:29, al.; ὁ δέ, αὐτὸς δέ, Mrk.1:45, Luk.4:40, al.; after a negation, Mat.6:19, 20, Rom.3:4, 1Th.5:21, al.
(AS)

---

LSJ / STEPBible (TFLSJ)
δέ,
but: adversative and copulative Particle,

__I
answering to μέν (which see), τὴν νῦν μὲν Βοιωτίαν, πρότερον δὲ Καδμηίδα γῆν καλουμένην [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 1.12, etc.]]

__II
without preceding μέν,

__II.1
adversative, expressing distinct opposition, αἰεί τοι τὰ κάκ᾽ ἐστὶ φίλα.. μαντεύεσθαι, ἐσθλὸν δ᾽ οὔτε τί πω εἶπας[Refs 5th c.BC+ [lines 1.108; ὀρθῶς ἔλεξας, οὐ φίλως δέ μοι λέγεις 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Orestes” 100, compare 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Antigone” 85, etc.; τέθνηκεν ἀνδρὸς οὐδενός, θεοῦ δ᾽ ὕπο [prev. author] “Ph.” 334]]; so in Prose, οὐκ ἐπὶ κακῷ, ἐλευθερώσει δέ.. [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 4.86; οἱ αἰχμάλωτοι.. ᾤχοντο εἰς Δεκέλειαν, οἱ δ᾽ εἰς Μέγαρα 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Historia Graeca (Hellenica)” 1.2.14, compare “Cyr.” 4.5.46; ἡ δ᾽ ἑτέρα “IG” 2.652 A 45.]]

__II.2
copulative,

__II.2.a
in explanatory clauses, ξυνέβησαν.. τὰ μακρὰ τείχη ἑλεῖν (ἦν δὲ σταδίων μάλιστα ὀκτώ) [Refs 8th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 4.66, compare 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 7.48]]: when a substantive is followed by words in apposition, Ἀρισταγόρῃ τῷ Μιλησίῳ, δούλῳ δὲ ἡμετέρῳ [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 7.8. β; μήτηρ βασιλέως βασίλεια δ᾽ ἐμή 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Persae” 152]]; so in answers, διπλᾶ λέγειν. —Answ. διπλᾶδ᾽ ὁρᾶν [Refs [[prev. author] “Th.” 974.]]

__II.2.b
in enumerations or transitions, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 1.43 - 49, 345 - 351, 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 1.2.1, etc.]]; with repetition of a word in different relations, ὣς Ἀχιλεὺς θάμβησεν.., θάμβησαν δὲ καὶ ἄλλοι [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 24.483; σάκος εἷλε.., εἵλετο δ᾽ ἔγχος 14.9 {δε}; Ζεύς ἐστιν αἰθήρ, Ζεὺς δὲ γῆ, Ζεὺς δ᾽ οὐρανός 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Fragmenta - American Journal of Philology” 70; κινεῖκραδίαν, κινεῖδὲ χόλον 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Medea” 99; ὄζει ἴων, ὄζει δὲ ῥόδων, ὄζει δ᾽ ὑακίνθου 5th c.BC: Hermippus Comicus 82.8]]; in rhetorical outbursts, οὐκ ἂν εὐθέως εἴποιεν· τὸν δὲ βάσκανον, τὸν δὲ ὄλεθρον, τοῦτον δὲ ὑβρίζειν,—ἀναπνεῖν δέ. [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 21.209]]; in a climax, πᾶν γύναιον καὶ παιδίον καὶ θηρίον δέ nay even beast, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Theaetetus” 171e, compare 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Historia Graeca (Hellenica)” 5.2.37]]; in the combination καὶ δέ [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 23.80, +others, καὶ.. δέ 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Prometheus Vinctus” 973, 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Electra” 1117, etc., each particle retains its force.]]

__II.2.c
answering to τε (which see), ἃ τῶν τε ἀποβαινόντων ἕνεκα ἄξια κεκτῆσθαι, πολὺ δὲ μᾶλλον αὐτὰ αὑτῶν [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 367c.]]

__II.3
implying causal connexion, less direct than γάρ, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 6.160, 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 1.433.]]

__II.4
in questions, with implied opposition, ἑόρακας δ᾽, ἔφη, τὴν γυναῖκ; [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 5.1.4; καὶ ὁ Σωκράτης, εἰπέ μοι, ἔφη, κύνας δὲ τρέφει; [prev. author] “Mem.” 2.9.2, compare 2.1.26, 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Antigone” 1172: in Trag. (not in Comedy texts or Oratt.), when the speaker turns from one person to another, the _vocative_ stands first, then the _person_ _pronoun_ followed by δέ, as Μενέλαε, σοὶ δὲ τάδε λέγω.. 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Orestes” 622, etc.; also in 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus, ὦ δέσποτα, ἐγὼ δὲ ταῦτα ἐποίησα 1.115.]]

__II.4.b
τί δ; what then? to mark a transition in dialogue; see at {τίς}.

__II
in apodosi:

__II.1
after hypothetical clauses, εἰ δέ κε μὴ δώωσιν, ἐγὼ δέ κεν αὐτὸς ἕλωμαι if they will not give it, then I.., [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 1.137, compare 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 12.54; εἰ μηδὲ τοῦτο βούλει ἀποκρίνασθαι, σὺ δὲ τοὐντεῦθεν λέγε 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 5.5.21, compare 5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “O.” 3.43 (variant), 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Agamemnon” 1060, 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 5.1, etc.]]

__II.1.b
after temporal or relative clauses, with ἐπεί, ἕως, etc., [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 24.255, 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 9.70, etc.; μέχρι.. εἶχον τὰ βέλη, οἱ δὲ ἀντεῖχον 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 3.98]]; with demonstrative Pronouns or adverbs answering to a preceding relative, οἵηπερ φύλλων γενεή, τοίη δὲ καὶ ἀνδρῶν [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 6.146, etc.; ἆθλα οἷς κεῖται ἀρετῆς μέγιστα, τοῖς δὲ καὶ ἄνδρες ἄριστοι πολιτεύουσιν 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 2.46; τοὺς δ᾽ ἔλαβε τυράννους.. τούτους δὲ.. ἐξεδίδου 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 5.37, compare 5th-6th c.BC: Isocrates Orator 4.98, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Laches” 194d; οἷα μὲν ἕκαστα ἐμοὶ φαίνεται τοιαῦτα μὲν ἔστιν ἐμοί, οἷα δὲ σοί, τοιαῦτα δὲ αὖ σοί [prev. author] “Tht.” 152a]]: sometimes after a participle, οἰόμενοι.. τιμῆς τεύξεσθαι, ἀντὶ δὲ τούτων οὐδ᾽ ὅμοιοι.. ἐσόμεθα [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 6.6.16, compare 5th-6th c.BC: Isocrates Orator 15.71 (variant).]]

__II.2
to resume after an interruption or parenthesis, χρόνου δὲ ἐπιγινομένου καὶ κατεστραμμένων σχεδὸν πάντων..,—κατεστραμμένων δὲ τούτων.. [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.28, 29; νῦν δ᾽ αὖ πάλιν ὑπό τε πλούτου διαθρυπτόμενος.. καὶ ὑπ᾽ ἀνθρώπων.. ὑπὸ τοιούτων δέ.. 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 7.2.23]]; with an anacoluthon, ἡ δὲ ψυχὴ ἄρα,—οἷ ἂν θεὸς θέλῃ.. τῇ ἐμῇ ψυχῇ ἰτέον, αὕτη δὲ δή.. [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Phaedo” 80d: for δ᾽ οὖν, see at {οὖν}.]]

__II.3
to begin a story, ἦμος δ᾽ ἠέλιος.. well, when the sun.., [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 4.400.]]

__II.4
to introduce a proof, τεκμήριον δέ, σημεῖον δέ, (see entry).

__B
POSITION of δέ. It usually stands second: hence frequently between Article and substantive or preposition and case; but also after substantive, or words forming a connected notion, hence it may stand third, γυναῖκα πιστὴν δ᾽ ἐν δόμοις εὕροι [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Agamemnon” 606, compare “Th.” 411, “Eu.” 531, 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Philoctetes” 959, etc.; fourth, [prev. author] “OT” 485, 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Helena” 688, 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Prometheus Vinctus” 323, 383, etc.; fifth, [prev. work] 401 codices; even sixth, Epigen. 7 (codices 2nd c.AD(?): Pollianus Epigrammaticus)]]; so in Prose after a negative, οὐχ ὑπ᾽ ἐραστοῦ δέ, to avoid confusion between οὐ δέ and οὐδέ, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Phaedrus” 227c.]]

deep_entry:
Abbott-Smith / STEPBible (TBESG)
δέησις, -εως, ἡ
(δέομαι), [in LXX for תְּחִנָּה, רִנָּה, תְּפִלָּה, etc. ;]
__1. a wanting, need (so Ps 21(22):25).
__2. an asking, entreaty, supplica­tion; in NT always addressed to God: Luk.1:13, 2Co.1:11, Php.1:19, 2Ti.1:3, Jas.5:16, 1Pe.3:12" (LXX) ; with νηστεῖαι, Luk.2:37; προσυνχή, -αί, Eph.6:18, Php.4:6, 1Ti.2:1 5:5; ἱκετηρίαι, Heb.5:7; προσκαρτέρησις, Eph.6:18; ἐντεύξεις, 1Ti.2:1; δ. ποιεῖσθαι (Deiss., BS, 250), Luk.5:33, Php.1:4 (pl.), 1Ti.2:1; before ὑπέρ, 2Co.9:14, Php.1:4; περί, Eph.6:18; πρός, Rom.10:1.†
SYN.: προσευχή, used of prayer in general, while δ. gives prominence to the sense of need; on the other hand, δ. is used as well of requests from man to man, while π. is limited to prayer to God. ἔντευξις, in the π., is the regular word for petition to a superior (Deiss., BS, 250; cf. the Pauline ἐντυγχάνειν, to entreat). Cf. also εὐχή. (Jas.5:15), αἴτημα, ἱκετηρία (Tr., Syn., § li; Cremer, 73, 174, 684). (AS)

---

entreaty, [NT+5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Lysias Orator 2.15 (_plural_), 5th-6th c.BC: Isocrates Orator 8.138 (_plural_), 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Epistulae” 329d (_plural_), etc.; δέομαι δ᾽ ὑμῶν.. δικαίαν δέησιν 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 29.4; δεήσεις ποιεῖσθαι NT.Luke.5.33, cf. Wilcken “Chr.” 41 ii 12 (3rd c.AD).]]

written petition, [Refs 1st c.AD+ [CPHerm. 6.10, 1st c.AD: Josephus Historicus “Bellum Judaicum” 7.5.2, 1st c.AD: Philo Judaeus 2.586, “PGen.” 16.10 (3rd c.AD).]]

__II
want, need, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Antipho Sophista 11; ἐν ἐπιθυμίαις τε καὶ δεήσεσιν 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Eryxias” 405e]]; κατὰ τὰς δεήσεις according to their needs, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Politica” 1257a23; δεήσεις εἰσὶν αἱ ὀρέξεις [prev. author] “Rh.” 1385a22.]]
