deep_entry:
Abbott-Smith / STEPBible (TBESG)
δεῖ  impersonal (δέω),
[in LXX chiefly for infin. with לְ ;]
one must, it is necessary: with inf., Mat.26:54, Mrk.13:7, Act.5:29, al.; with accusative and inf., Mat.16:21, Mrk.8:31, Jhn.3:7, Act.25:10, al.; with ellipse of accusative, Mat.23:23; of accusative, and inf., Mrk.13:14, Rom.1:27 8:26; οὐ (μὴ) δεῖ (non licet), ought not, must not: Act.25:24, 2Ti.2:24; impf., ἔδει, of necessity or obligation in past time regarding a past event (Bl., § 63, 4), Mat.18:33, Luk.15:32, Jhn.4:4, Act.27:21, al.; periphr., δέον ἐστίν (as in Attic, χρεών ἐστι = χρή, see: δέον), Act.19:36; id., with ellipse of ἐστίν, 1Pe.1:6 τὰ μὴ δέοντα (= ἃ οὐ δεῖ 1Ti.5:13.
SYN.: ὀφείλει, expressing moral obligation, as distinct from δεῖ, denoting logical necessity and χρή, a need which results from the fitness of things (see Tr., Syn., § cvii, 10; Westc. on Heb.2:1, 1Jn.2:6; Hort on Jas.3:10). (AS)

---

LSJ / STEPBible (TFLSJ)
δεῖ:
subjunctive δέη, sometimes contraction δῆ (in codices of Comedy texts, as [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Ranae” 265)]]; ὁπόσου κα δῆ [Refs 5th c.BC+ [“IG” 4.1484.65 (Epid.), compare “SIG” 245 G 47 (Delph.); _optative_ δέοι 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 4.4]]; infinitive δεῖ; participle δέον (see. infr. IV): imperfect ἔδει, Ionic dialect ἔδεε: future δεήσει [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Hippolytus” 941, etc.]]: aorist I ἐδέησε [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 2.77, etc.]] —Impers. from δέω (A), there is need (the sense of moral obligation, properly belonging to χρή, is later, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Philoctetes” 583, etc.):]]

__I
c.accusative person et infinitive, it is needful for one to do, one must, once in [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Homerus Epicus, τί δὲ δεῖ πολεμιζέμεναι.. Ἀργείους]] why need the Argives fight? [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 9.337; δ. [μ᾽] ἐλθεῖν 5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “O.” 6.28, etc.]]: with nominative of the pronoun, ἡγούμην.. δεῖν.. μεγαλοψυχότερος φαίνεσθαι [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 19.235: rarely δεῖ σ᾽ ὅπως δείξεις, ={δεῖ σε δεῖξαι}, 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Ajax” 556, compare “Ph.” 54; δεῖ σ᾽ ὅπως μηδὲν διοίσεις 5th c.BC: Cratinus Comicus 108; (the full _construction_ in 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Philoctetes” 77 τοῦτο δεῖ σοφισθῆναι.. ὅπως γενήσῃ)]]: rarely with dative person, there is need of.. for.., θεοῖσι προσβαλεῖν χθονὶ ἄλλην δεήσει γαῖαν [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Hippolytus” 941, compare 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 3.4.35, “Oec.” 7.20: the _accusative_ _person_ is often omitted, ἐκ τῶν μανθάνειν δεῖ (i.e. ἡμᾶς) 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.8, compare 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Agamemnon” 567, “Eu.” 826, etc.]]

__I.2
with accusative of things et infinitive, δεῖ τι γενέσθαι [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 5.26; παραδείγματα, καθ᾽ ἃ δέοι ἀποκρίνεσθαι 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Meno” 79a, etc.]]; also ἐπεὶ δέ οἱ ἔδεε κακῶς γενέσθαι since it was fated for him.., since he was doomed.., [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 2.161, compare 8.53, 9.109, 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Tyrannus” 825]]; for οἴομαι δεῖν, see at {οἴομαι}.

__I.3
absolutely with infinitive understood, μὴ πεῖθ᾽ ἃ μὴ δεῖ (i.e. πείθειν) [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Coloneus” 1442, compare “OT” 1273]]; εἴ τι δέοι, ἤν τι δέῃ (i.e. γενέσθαι), [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Memorabilia” 1.2.59, 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 1.44]]; κἂν δέῃ (i.e. τροχάζειν), τροχάζῶ [Refs 6th c.BC+ [{5-6th c.BC}: Philetaerus Comicus 3.]]

__II
with genitive of things, there is need of, frequently with negative, οὐδὲν ἂν δέοι πολλοῦ ἀργυρίου [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Crito” 45a, etc.; τί δεῖ τῆς ἀρετῆ; 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Politica” 1309b10]]; sometimes with infinitive added, μακροῦ λόγου δεῖ ταῦτ᾽ ἐπεξελθεῖν [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Prometheus Vinctus” 870, compare 875, “Supp.” 407.]]

__II.b
frequently in phrases, πολλοῦ δεῖ there wants much, far from it, ὀλίγου δεῖ there wants little, all but; in full with infinitive, πολλοῦ δεῖ οὕτως ἔχειν [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Apologia” 35d; τοὺς Πλαταιέας ἐλαχίστου ἐδέησε διαφθεῖραι [τὸ πῦρ] 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 2.77; πολλοῦ γε δεῖ, πολλοῦ γε καὶ δεῖ 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Acharnenses” 543, 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 18.300, 21.71]]; τοῦ πλεῦνος αἰεὶ ἔδεε there was always further to travel, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 4.43; τοῦ παντὸς δεῖ 2nd c.AD: Lucianus Sophista “Merc.Cond.” 13: also ὀλίγου δεῖν]] absolutely, in same sense, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Apologia” 22a, etc.; μικροῦ δεῖν 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 27.29.]]

__II.2
with dative person added, δεῖ μοί τινος [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Agamemnon” 848, 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Medea” 565, 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 1.71, etc.]]

__II.3
with accusative person added, αὐτὸν γάρ σε δεῖ προμηθέως [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Prometheus Vinctus” 86, compare 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Rhesus” 837, “Hipp.” 23.]]

__II.4
rarely with Subj. in nominative, δεῖ μοί τι something is needful to me, ἓν δεῖ μόνον μοι [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Supplices” 594; εἴ τι δέοι τῷ χορῷ 5th c.BC: Antipho Orator 6.12; πρῶτον μὲν τοῦτο δεῖ, ὑπειληφέναι.. 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 10.15.]]

__III
middle, δεῖται there is need, with genitive, δεῖταί σοι τῆς αὐτῆς ἐρωτήσεως [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Meno” 79c; ὅσων δέοιτο 4th c.BC: Aeneas Tacticus 13.1; ἑτέρου δεῖσθαι στρατηγοῦ νομίζων 1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus “Pelopidas” 26]]: with infinitive, ὥστε βραχἔ ἐμοὶ δεῖσθαι φράσαι [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Coloneus” 570 (codices); δεήσεται.. ἀναγράφεσθαι 4th c.BC: Aeneas Tacticus 31.9; τήν μευ γλῶσσαν ἐκτεμεῖν δεῖται 3rd c.BC: Herodas Mimographus 6.41.]]

__IV
neuter participle δέον (δεῖν is uncertain in [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Fragmenta” 220, 5th c.BC: Lysias Orator 14.7, compare 2nd c.AD: Apollonius Dyscolus Grammaticus “de Adverbiis;” 132.30, Hdn.Gr. 2.328, +others, 5th c.AD(?): Hesychius Legal icographus)]]: absolutely, it being needful or fitting, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Protagoras” 355d, etc.]]; οὐκ ἀπήντα, δέον, he did not appear in court, though he ought to have done so, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 21.90]]: with infinitive, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Nubes” 988]]; οὐδὲν δέον there being no need, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 3.65, etc.]]: future ὡς αὐτίκα δεῆσον διώκειν [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 3.2.8]]: aorist δεῆσαν [Refs 2nd c.BC+ [1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus “Fabius Maximus” 9, etc.: also δέον ἂν εἴη, ={δέοι ἄν}, 2nd c.BC: Polybius Historicus 2.37.5, etc.: less frequently _genitive_ _absolutely_ δέοντος,]] with accusative infinitive, [Refs 1st c.AD+ [1st c.AD: Cornutus Philosophus “de Natura Deorum” 17.]]

__IV.2
substantive δέον, τό (see entry vocative).

3rd.pers. singular δείκνυεν [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “P.” 4.220]]: future δείξω [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 12.25, etc.]], Ionic dialect δέξω [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 4.179, +others:]]aorist 1 ἔδειξα, Epic dialect δεῖξα [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 3.174, etc.]], Ionic dialect ἔδεξα [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 2.30, +others]]: perfect δέδειχα [Refs 4th c.BC+ [2nd c.AD: Alexander Rhetor 268, (ἐπι-) 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 26.16, (ἀνα-) 2nd c.BC: Polybius Historicus 4.48.3:]] —middle, with perfect passive, for Epic dialect forms δεικνύμενος, δείδεκτο, δειδέχαται, δειδέχατο, see at {δειδίσκομαι}:—passive, future δειχθήσομαι [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Isocrates Orator 5.1, 12.4; show, prove, with participle, ποῦ γὰρ ὢν δείξω φίλο; [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Orestes” 802; ἔδειξαν ἕτοιμοι ὄντες 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 4.73, compare 5.72; δεικνύω ἐσπουδακώς 4th-3rd c.BC: Menander Comicus 562; δείξω αὐτὸν πολλῶν θανάτων ὄντ᾽ ἄξιον 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 21.21; εἰ.. δειχθήσεται τοῦτο πεποιηκώς [prev. work]160; ἱκανώτατα δέδεικται ψυχὴ τῶν πάντων πρεσβυτάτη 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Leges” 896b: followed by a _relative_ clause with ὡς.., ὅτι.., εἰ..,etc., 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Septem contra Thebas” 176, 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 1.76, 143, etc.; πᾶσα ἀπόδειξίς τι κατά τινος δείκνυσι 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Anthologia Graeca” 0.90b34: ὅπερ ἔδει δεῖξαι, = Q.E. 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator, 3rd c.BC: Euclides Geometra 1.4, +others: _absolutely_, δέδεικται]] it is clear or proven, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Phaedo” 66d, etc.; δεδείξεται 2nd c.AD: Apollonius Dyscolus Grammaticus [prev. cited]]]

of accusers, inform against, τινά [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Equites” 278 (Dobree ex Scholia ἐγὼ ἐνδείκνυμι).]]

display, exhibit, ἀγλαΐαν [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “P.” 6.46]]; ἀρετήν, προθυμίαν, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 1.37, 6.11.]]

fortunate, especially of the flight of birds and other omens, δ. ὄρνις [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 13.821, compare 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 2.154, 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Prometheus Vinctus” 489, “Michel” 727 (from Ephesus); ἀοιδὰν.. δεξιωτάταν ὀπαδόν 5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “N.” 3.8; βροντή 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 7.1.3]]. adverb -ῶς[Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd c.AD: Herodianus Grammaticus 3.9.12.]]

(mid. of δέω, II, which see, as depon.) [in LXX for חנן, etc. ;]
to want for oneself;
__1. to want, need:
__(a) absol.;
__(b) with genitive
__2. to beg, request, beseech, pray;
__(i) in general: absol., Act.26:3, WH; with genitive of person(s), Luk.5:12; 8:28; 38 (ἐδεῖτο; T, ἐδέετο, cf. Veitch, see word δέω) 9:38, Act.8:34; 21:39, 2Co.5:20, Gal.4:12; before ἵνα, Luk.9:40; before τό, with inf., 2Co.10:2; with genitive of person(s) and of thing(s), 2Co.8:4;

SYN.: αἰτέω, and cf. δέησις. (AS)

LSJ / STEPBible (TFLSJ)
δέω,

__B
[Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Prometheus Vinctus” 1006, etc.]]: future δεήσω [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 395e]]: aorist ἐδέησα [Refs 8th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Lysias Orator 30.8, _Epic dialect_ δῆσα only 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 18.100]]: perfect δεδέηκα [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Politicus” 277d]]:—middle, future δεήσομαι [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 1.32, etc.]], Doric dialect δεοῦμαι [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Epicharmus Comicus 120]]; later -ηθήσομαι [LXX+1st c.AD+ [LXX.Job.5.8, 1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus 2.213c, etc.]]: aorist ἐδεήθην [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 4.84, 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Plutus” 986, etc.]]: perfect δεδέημαι [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 7.7.14, 4th c.BC: Isaeus Orator 8.22 (the forms δεήσω, etc., compared with the _Epic dialect_ ἐδεύησα, δεύομαι, point to root δεϝ)]]:—lack, miss, stand in need of, with genitive, ἐμεῖο δὲ δῆσε.. ἀλκτῆρα γενέσθαι [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” [prev. cited] (elsewhere 8th c.BC: Homerus Epicus uses δεύω, which see)]]; παραδείγματος τὸ παράδειγμα αὐτὸ δεδέηκεν [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Politicus” 277d, compare 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Memorabilia” 4.2.10.]]

__B.2
frequently in Attic dialect, πολλοῦ δέω I want much, i.e. am far from, mostly with infinitive present, πολλοῦ δ. ἀπολογεῖσθαι I am far from defending myself, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Apologia” 30d; πολλοῦ δεῖς εἰπεῖν [prev. author] “Men.” 79b; π. δ. ἀγνοεῖν [prev. author] “Ly.” 204e; π. γε δέουσι μαίνεσθαι [prev. author] “Men.” 92a; also μικροῦ ἔδεον ἐν χερσὶν εἶναι 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Historia Graeca (Hellenica)” 4.6.11, compare 4th-3rd c.BC: Menander Comicus “Γεωργός” 25; τοσούτου δέω ἱκανὸς εἶναι λέγειν ὥστε.. 5th c.BC: Lysias Orator 17.1; τοσούτου δέουσι μιμεῖσθαι 5th-6th c.BC: Isocrates Orator 14.17 (also τοσοῦτον δέω εἰδέναι 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Meno” 71a)]]; παρὰ μικρὸν ἐδέησα ἀποθανεῖν variant in [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Isocrates Orator 17.42; simply ἐδέησα κινδύνῳ περιπεσεῖν 4th c.AD: Alciphro Epistolographus 3.5: _absolutely_, πολλοῦ γε δέω]] I am far from it, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Phaedrus” 228a; τοῦ παντὸς δέω 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Prometheus Vinctus” 1006; παντὸς δεῖ τοιοῦτος εἶναι 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Sophista” 221d (_impersonal_ πολλοῦ δεῖ, etc., see at {δεῖ} II.1. b)]]: in participle, παλαστῆς δεόντων τεττάρων ποδῶν [Refs 4th c.BC+ [“IG” 12.373.8; μικροῦ δέοντα τέτταρα τάλαντα 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 27.35]]; the participle is frequently used to express numerals compounded with 8 or 9, ἀνδράσιν ἑνὸς δέουσι τριάκοντα [Refs [“IG” 12.374.413]]; δυοῖν δέοντα τεσσεράκοντα forty lacking two, thirty-eight, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.14; πεντήκοντα δυοῖν δέοντα ἔτη 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 2.2]]; ἑνὸς δέον εἰκοστὸν ἔτος the [Refs [20th year]]save one,[Refs 5th c.BC+ [the 19th, [prev. author] 8.6; δυοῖν δεούσαις εἴκοσι ναυσίν 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Historia Graeca (Hellenica)” 1.1.5: later, the]]infinitive stands absolutely, περὶ τὰ ἑνὸς δεῖν πεντήκοντα fifty save one, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Rhetorica” 1390b11]]: participle in genitive, τροφαλίδες μιᾶς δεούσης εἴκοσιν [Refs 1st c.AD+ [[prev. author] “HA” 522a31; πόλεων δυοῖν δεούσαιν ἑξήκοντα 3rd c.AD(?): Diogenes Laertius 5.27; ἑξήκοντα ἑνὸς δέοντος ἔτη 1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus “Pompeius” 79.]]

__B.3
participle δέων, δέουσα, as adjective, fit, proper, ὁ καιρὸς οὐκ ἔστι χρόνος δέων [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Analytica Priora” 48b36; τοῖς δέουσι χρόνοις “IG” 12(3).247.11 (from Anaphe)]]; ἡ δέουσα ἑκάστων χρῆσις Hierocl.p.61 [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus, etc.: especiallyfrequently in _neuter_, see at {δέον}.]]

__B.4
δεῖ impersonal, see entry

__B.II
deponent verb δέομαι: contraction δῆσθε [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophron Comicus 46]], participle δεύμενος [Refs [[prev. author] 36]]: future δεήσομαι [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Philebus” 53b:]]aorist ἐδεήθην: always personal, and used by [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Homerus Epicus only in form δεύομαι (see. δεύω B):]]

__B.II.1
absolutely, to be in want or need, require, mostly in participle, κάρτα δεόμενος [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 8.59]]; οἱ δεόμενοι the needy, opposed to οἱ κεκτημένοι τὰς οὐσίας, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Isocrates Orator 6.67.]]

__B.II.1.b
stand in need of, want, with genitive, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.36, etc.; τὰ σὰ δεῖται κολαστοῦ.. ἔπη 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Tyrannus” 1148; ῥώμης τινὸς δ. [prev. work] 1293]]; οὐδὲν δεῖσθαι τροφῆς have no need of.., [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 8.43]]; ἤν τι δέωνται βασιλέως if they have any need of him, [Refs [[prev. work] 37: with]]infinitive, τοῦτο ἔτι δέομαι μαθεῖν [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 392d, compare “Euthd.” 275d, etc.]]; τὰ πράττεσθαι δεόμενα things needing to be done, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 2.3.3; τὰ δεόμενα]]necessaries, [Refs [Inscriptiones Graecae 2.573.4]]; ἐπισκευάσαι τὰ δεόμενα parts needing repair, [Refs [[prev. work]22.1176.15]]; τὸ δεόμενον the point threatened, [Refs 2nd c.BC+ [2nd c.BC: Polybius Historicus 15.15.7]]; δεῖται impersonal, see at {δεῖ}.

__B.II.2
beg a thing from a person, with double genitive of things et person, τῶν ἐδέετο σφέων [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 3.157, compare 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 1.32, etc.; μή μου δεηθῇς. ΘΗ. πράγματος ποίο; 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Coloneus” 1170: frequently with _neuter_ _pronoun_ in _accusative_, τοῦτο ὑμῶν δέομαι 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Apologia” 17c, compare “Smp.” 173e, etc.: with _accusative_ _cognate_, δέημα, or oftener δέησιν, δεῖσθαί τινος, 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Acharnenses” 1059, 4th c.BC: Aeschines Orator 2.43, etc.: also with _accusative_ _of things_ only, ξύμφορα δ. 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 1.32; δυνατά τινος 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Protagoras” 335e; δίκαια καὶ μέτρια ὑμῶν 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 38.2; διαπράξωμαι ἃ δέομαι 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 2.3.29: with _genitive_ _person_ only, δεηθεὶς ὑμῶν]] having begged a favour of you, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 21.108]]: c.genitive person et infinitive, ἐδέετο τοῦ δήμου φυλακῆς πρὸς αὐτοῦ κυρῆσαι [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.59, compare 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Protagoras” 336a, etc.; δ. τινὸς ὥστε.. 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 1.119; ὅπως.. 1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus “Antonius” 84: rarely with _accusative_ _person_, ἐδέοντο Βοιωτοὺς ὅπως παραδώσουσι 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 5.36: parenthetic, δέομαι]]I pray, [LXX.Gen.44.18.]

second, (perhaps from δύο with comparative termination):

__I
next in Order (with a notion of Time), in [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” (not in 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey”)]] of one who comes in second in a race,[Refs [23.265; δ. ἐλθεῖν 22.207; δ. αὖτ᾽.. προΐει.. ἔγχος]]next, [Refs [20.273, etc.]]; οὔ μ᾽ ἔτι δ. ὧδε ἵξετ᾽ ἄχος no second grief, i.e. none hereafter like this, [Refs [23.46]]; as comparative, with genitive, ἐμεῖο δεύτεροι after my time, [Refs [[prev. work] 248]]; σοὶ δ᾽ οὐκέτι δ. ἔσται no second choice will be allowed thee, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th-7th c.BC: Hesiodus Epicus “Opera et Dies” 34]]; in Attic dialect and Trag. with Article, ὁ δ. [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Coloneus” 1315, etc.]]; αἱ δ. πως φροντίδες σοφώτεραι second thoughts are wisest, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Hippolytus” 436: proverbial, δ. πλοῦς]] the next best way, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Phaedo” 99d, etc.; ὁ δ. πλοῦς ἐστι δήπου λεγόμενος, ἂν ἀποτύχῃ τις οὐρίου, κώπαισι πλεῖν 4th-3rd c.BC: Menander Comicus 241.]]

__I.2
of Time, next, later, δ. χρόνῳ in after time, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “O.” 1.43]]; δ. ἡμέρῃ on the next day, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.82]]; δ. ἔτεϊ τούτων in the year after this, [Refs [[prev. author] 6.46: _neuter_ as]] adverb, δεύτερον αὖ, αὖτε, αὖτις, a second time, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 3.332, 191, 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 9.354; ἐν τᾷ δ. ἐκκλησίᾳ “SIG” 644.20]]: with the Article, τὸ δ. [Refs 7th c.BC+ [7th-6th c.BC: Sappho Lyrica “Papyrus fragments” in E. Diehl, 4.11, 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.79, 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Agamemnon” 1082, 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 2.2.1: also _plural_, 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 3.53, 9.3]]; τὰ δ. κινδυνεύσοντας about to run the next dangers, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 6.78]]; later, ἐκ δευτέρου for the second time, [NT+2nd c.BC+ [NT.Mark.14.72, 1st c.AD: Dioscorides (Dioscurides) Medicus 5.87.10; ἐκ δευτέρης 2nd c.AD: Babrius Fabularum Scriptor 114.5, compare “PStrassb.” 100.22 (2nd c.BC)]]: regular adverb δευτέρως [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Leges” 955e, 4th c.AD: Sallustius Philosophus 18, etc.]]

__I.2.b
ὁ δ. the younger, [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [“BGU” 592.10 (2nd c.AD).]]

__II
in Order or Rank (without any notion of Time), second, δ.μετ᾽ ἐκεῖνον [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.31, compare 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Philoctetes” 1442, etc.; πολὺ δ. [prev. author] “OC” 1228 (Lyric poetry)]]; πολὺ δ. μετά τι very much behind, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 2.97; μετὰ τὸ πλουτεῖν δ. 4th c.BC: Antiphanes Comicus 144.9: with _genitive_, δ. οὐδενός]] second to none, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.23, 2nd c.BC: Polybius Historicus 31.27.16; δ. παιδὸς σῆς 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Troades” 618; πάντα τἄλλα δεύτερ᾽ ἦν τῶν προσδοκιῶν 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 19.24; πρὸς τὰ χρήματα θνητοῖσι τἄλλα δεύτερ᾽ 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Fragmenta” 354.5; τὰ ἄλλα πάντα δ. τε καὶ ὕστερα λεκτέον 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Philebus” 59c]]; logically or metaphysically posterior, πᾶν πλῆθος δ. ἐστι τοῦ ἑνός [Refs 5th c.AD+ [5th c.AD: Proclus Philosophus “Inst.” 5, compare 36, 5th-6th c.AD: Damascius Philosophus “de Principiis” 126, +others]]; δεύτερ᾽ ἡγεῖσθαι think quite secondary, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Coloneus” 351]]; δεύτερον ἄγειν, δεύτερα ποιεῖσθαι, [Refs 1st c.AD+ [2nd c.AD: Lucianus Sophista “Symp.” 9, 1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus 2.162e; ἐν δευτέρῳ τίθεσθαι [prev. author] “Fab.” 24, compare 4th c.AD: Julianus Imperator “Orationes” 8.242b]]; ἱερὸν δ. of the second class, [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [“OGI” 56.59 (3rd c.BC), etc.]]

__II.2
the second of two, δ. αὐτή herself with another, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 4.113, compare “Anecdota Graeca - Bekker” 89]]; ἑπτὰ δ. σοφοί a second seven sages, [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [3rd c.BC: Euphro Comicus 1.12]]; εἷς καὶ δ. unus et alter,[Refs 1st c.AD+ [Hdn.Gr. 2.934; εἷς ἢ δ. 4th c.AD: Julianus Imperator “Orationes” 6.190d; ἕν τι.. ἢ δεύτερον 1st-2nd c.AD: Dio Chrysostomus Sophista 33.7]]; δ. καὶ τρίτος two or three, [Refs 2nd c.BC+ [2nd c.BC: Polybius Historicus 26.1.1.]]; neuter as adverb, ἅπαξ καὶ δεύτερον once or twice, [Refs 4th c.AD+ [4th c.AD: Julianus Imperator]] ad Ath.278c.

take upon oneself, τὴν δαπάνην [Refs 2nd c.BC+ [2nd c.BC: Polybius Historicus 31.28.5]]: with infinitive, undertake, [Refs [“SIG” 245.34.]]

__II
of persons as the object, welcome, κόλπῳ [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 6.483; ἀγαθῷ νόῳ 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.60]]; ἐν μεγάροισι, ἐν δόμοισιν, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 18.331, 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 17.110; δόμοις δ. τινά 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Tyrannus” 818]]; στέγαις, πυρὶ δ. τινά, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Orestes” 47; δ. χώρᾳ [prev. author] “Med.” 713]]; τῇ τόλει δ. to admit into the city, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 4.103]]; ἀγορᾷ, ἄστει δ., [Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. author] 6.44; ἔσω [prev. passage]; εἰς τὸ τεῖχος 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 5.5.6]]; δ. τινὰ ξύμμαχον accept or admit as an ally, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 1.43, etc.]]; accept as security, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [PGrenf. 1.33.4, etc.: _metaphorically_ of places, τόποι τοὺς κατοικιζομένους ἵλεῳ δεχόμενοι 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Leges” 747e]]; entertain, δείπνοις [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Anaxandrides Comicus 41.2 (_anapaest meter_); δωρήμασιν 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Coloneus” 4.]]

__II.2
receive as an enemy, await the attack of, ἐπιόντα δ. δουρί [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 5.238, compare 15.745]]; of a hunter waiting for game, [Refs [4.107]]; of a wild boar waiting for the hunters, [Refs [12.147]]; of troops, εἰς χεῖρας δ. [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 4.3.31; τοὺς Λακεδαιμονίους δ. 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 3.54, compare 8.28, 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 4.43; ἐπιόντας δ. [prev. author] 7.77; δ. τὴν πρώτην ἔφοδον [prev. author] 4.126; ἐδέξατο πόλις πόνον 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Supplices” 393.]]

__II.3
expect, wait, with accusative et future infinitive, ἀλλ᾽ αἰεί τινα φῶτα.. ἐδέγμην ἐνθάδ᾽ ἐλεύσεσθαι [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 9.513, compare 12.230; also δέγμενος Αἰακίδην, ὁπότε λήξειεν 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 9.191; δεδεγμένος εἰσόκεν ἔλθῃς 10.62.]]—In these two last senses, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Homerus Epicus always uses]]future δεδέξομαι, perfect δέδεγμαι, and δεδεγμένος,[Refs 3rd c.BC+ [compare δεδεγμένος ὁππόθ᾽ ἵκοιτο 3rd c.BC: Theocritus Poeta Bucolicus 25.228; δέγμενος is used in sense 3 only, except in “hymnus ad Cererem” 29, “Merc.” 477:]]infinitive δειδέχθαι as imperative, expect, with genitive, βορέω [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-3rd c.BC: Aratus Epicus 795, compare 907, 928.]]

__III
rarely with a thing as the subject, occupy, engage one, τίς ἀρχὰ δέξατο ναυτιλίας [αὐτούς]; [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “P.” 4.70.]]

__III.2
receive, hold, τὴν τροφήν [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Historia Animalium” 531a23, +others; οἰκίαι ἱκαναὶ δέξασθαι ὑμᾶς “SIG” 344.10.]]

__III.3
admit of, ψεῦδος οὐδὲν δ. ἁ τῶ ἀριθμῶ φύσις [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Philolaus Philosophus 11; τὸ μᾶλλον 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Topica” 146a3, compare 1st c.BC: Dionysius Halicarnassensis “de Isocrate” 2.]]

__III.4
Geometry texts, contain, circum-scribe, γωνίας ἴσας [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [3rd c.BC: Euclides Geometra 3 “Def.” 11; πεντάγωνον 3rd c.AD(?): Pappus Mathematicus 422.34.]]

__IV
intransitive, succeed, come next, ὥς μοι δέχεται κακὸν ἐκ κακοῦ αἰεί [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 19.290; ἄλλος γ᾽ ἐξ ἄλλου δέχεται χαλεπώτερος ἆθλος 8th-7th c.BC: Hesiodus Epicus “Theogonia” 800; ἄλλος ἐξ ἄλλου δ. 5th c.BC: Empedocles Poeta Philosophus 115.12]]; of places, ἐκ τοῦ στεινοῦ τὸ Ἀρτεμίσιον δέκεται [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 7.176. (δέκομαι]] is probably the original form, cf. Slavonic desiti, dositi 'find'.)

Abbott-Smith / STEPBible (TBESG)
δέω (I),
[in LXX chiefly for אסר ;]
to tie, bind, fasten;
__(1) with accusative of thing(s), before εἰς δεσμάς, Mat.13:30; of an ass, Mat.21:2, Mrk.11:2, 4 Luk.19:30.
__(2) with accusative of person(s), of swathing a dead body, ὀθονίοις, Jhn.19:40; δεδομένος τ. πόδας . . . κειρίαις (Bl., §34, 6; Kühner 3, iii, 125), Jhn.11:44; of binding with chains, ἀγγέλους, Rev.9:14; a demoniac, πέδαις κ. ἁλύσεσι, Mrk.5:3, 4; captives, Mat.12:29 14:3 22:13 27:2, Mrk.3:27 6:17 15:1, 7, Jhn.18:12, 24, Act.9:2, 14, 21, 21:11, 13 22:5, 29 24:27, Col.4:3, Rev.20:2; ἁλύσεσι, Act.12:6 21:33. Metaphorical, ὁ λόγος τ. Θεοῦ, 2Ti.2:9; of Satan binding by disease (MM, see word), Luk.13:16; of constraint or obligation, Act.20:22; of the marriage bond,  1Co.7:39; id. with dative of person(s), ἀνδρί, Rom.7:2; γυναικί, 1Co.7:27; in Rabbinic lang. (Dalman, Words, 213f.), to forbid, declare forbidden, Mat.16:19 18:18 (cf. κατα-, περι-, συν-, ὐπο-δέω; Cremer, 82).
† (AS)

LSJ / STEPBible (TFLSJ)
δέω,

__B
[Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Prometheus Vinctus” 1006, etc.]]: future δεήσω [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 395e]]: aorist ἐδέησα [Refs 8th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Lysias Orator 30.8, _Epic dialect_ δῆσα only 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 18.100]]: perfect δεδέηκα [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Politicus” 277d]]:—middle, future δεήσομαι [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 1.32, etc.]], Doric dialect δεοῦμαι [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Epicharmus Comicus 120]]; later -ηθήσομαι [LXX+1st c.AD+ [LXX.Job.5.8, 1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus 2.213c, etc.]]: aorist ἐδεήθην [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 4.84, 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Plutus” 986, etc.]]: perfect δεδέημαι [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 7.7.14, 4th c.BC: Isaeus Orator 8.22 (the forms δεήσω, etc., compared with the _Epic dialect_ ἐδεύησα, δεύομαι, point to root δεϝ)]]:—lack, miss, stand in need of, with genitive, ἐμεῖο δὲ δῆσε.. ἀλκτῆρα γενέσθαι [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” [prev. cited] (elsewhere 8th c.BC: Homerus Epicus uses δεύω, which see)]]; παραδείγματος τὸ παράδειγμα αὐτὸ δεδέηκεν [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Politicus” 277d, compare 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Memorabilia” 4.2.10.]]

__B.2
frequently in Attic dialect, πολλοῦ δέω I want much, i.e. am far from, mostly with infinitive present, πολλοῦ δ. ἀπολογεῖσθαι I am far from defending myself, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Apologia” 30d; πολλοῦ δεῖς εἰπεῖν [prev. author] “Men.” 79b; π. δ. ἀγνοεῖν [prev. author] “Ly.” 204e; π. γε δέουσι μαίνεσθαι [prev. author] “Men.” 92a; also μικροῦ ἔδεον ἐν χερσὶν εἶναι 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Historia Graeca (Hellenica)” 4.6.11, compare 4th-3rd c.BC: Menander Comicus “Γεωργός” 25; τοσούτου δέω ἱκανὸς εἶναι λέγειν ὥστε.. 5th c.BC: Lysias Orator 17.1; τοσούτου δέουσι μιμεῖσθαι 5th-6th c.BC: Isocrates Orator 14.17 (also τοσοῦτον δέω εἰδέναι 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Meno” 71a)]]; παρὰ μικρὸν ἐδέησα ἀποθανεῖν variant in [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Isocrates Orator 17.42; simply ἐδέησα κινδύνῳ περιπεσεῖν 4th c.AD: Alciphro Epistolographus 3.5: _absolutely_, πολλοῦ γε δέω]] I am far from it, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Phaedrus” 228a; τοῦ παντὸς δέω 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Prometheus Vinctus” 1006; παντὸς δεῖ τοιοῦτος εἶναι 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Sophista” 221d (_impersonal_ πολλοῦ δεῖ, etc., see at {δεῖ} II.1. b)]]: in participle, παλαστῆς δεόντων τεττάρων ποδῶν [Refs 4th c.BC+ [“IG” 12.373.8; μικροῦ δέοντα τέτταρα τάλαντα 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 27.35]]; the participle is frequently used to express numerals compounded with 8 or 9, ἀνδράσιν ἑνὸς δέουσι τριάκοντα [Refs [“IG” 12.374.413]]; δυοῖν δέοντα τεσσεράκοντα forty lacking two, thirty-eight, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.14; πεντήκοντα δυοῖν δέοντα ἔτη 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 2.2]]; ἑνὸς δέον εἰκοστὸν ἔτος the [Refs [20th year]]save one,[Refs 5th c.BC+ [the 19th, [prev. author] 8.6; δυοῖν δεούσαις εἴκοσι ναυσίν 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Historia Graeca (Hellenica)” 1.1.5: later, the]]infinitive stands absolutely, περὶ τὰ ἑνὸς δεῖν πεντήκοντα fifty save one, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Rhetorica” 1390b11]]: participle in genitive, τροφαλίδες μιᾶς δεούσης εἴκοσιν [Refs 1st c.AD+ [[prev. author] “HA” 522a31; πόλεων δυοῖν δεούσαιν ἑξήκοντα 3rd c.AD(?): Diogenes Laertius 5.27; ἑξήκοντα ἑνὸς δέοντος ἔτη 1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus “Pompeius” 79.]]

__B.3
participle δέων, δέουσα, as adjective, fit, proper, ὁ καιρὸς οὐκ ἔστι χρόνος δέων [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Analytica Priora” 48b36; τοῖς δέουσι χρόνοις “IG” 12(3).247.11 (from Anaphe)]]; ἡ δέουσα ἑκάστων χρῆσις Hierocl.p.61 [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus, etc.: especiallyfrequently in _neuter_, see at {δέον}.]]

__B.4
δεῖ impersonal, see entry

__B.II
deponent verb δέομαι: contraction δῆσθε [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophron Comicus 46]], participle δεύμενος [Refs [[prev. author] 36]]: future δεήσομαι [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Philebus” 53b:]]aorist ἐδεήθην: always personal, and used by [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Homerus Epicus only in form δεύομαι (see. δεύω B):]]

__B.II.1
absolutely, to be in want or need, require, mostly in participle, κάρτα δεόμενος [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 8.59]]; οἱ δεόμενοι the needy, opposed to οἱ κεκτημένοι τὰς οὐσίας, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Isocrates Orator 6.67.]]

__B.II.1.b
stand in need of, want, with genitive, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.36, etc.; τὰ σὰ δεῖται κολαστοῦ.. ἔπη 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Tyrannus” 1148; ῥώμης τινὸς δ. [prev. work] 1293]]; οὐδὲν δεῖσθαι τροφῆς have no need of.., [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 8.43]]; ἤν τι δέωνται βασιλέως if they have any need of him, [Refs [[prev. work] 37: with]]infinitive, τοῦτο ἔτι δέομαι μαθεῖν [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 392d, compare “Euthd.” 275d, etc.]]; τὰ πράττεσθαι δεόμενα things needing to be done, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 2.3.3; τὰ δεόμενα]]necessaries, [Refs [Inscriptiones Graecae 2.573.4]]; ἐπισκευάσαι τὰ δεόμενα parts needing repair, [Refs [[prev. work]22.1176.15]]; τὸ δεόμενον the point threatened, [Refs 2nd c.BC+ [2nd c.BC: Polybius Historicus 15.15.7]]; δεῖται impersonal, see at {δεῖ}.

__B.II.2
beg a thing from a person, with double genitive of things et person, τῶν ἐδέετο σφέων [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 3.157, compare 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 1.32, etc.; μή μου δεηθῇς. ΘΗ. πράγματος ποίο; 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Coloneus” 1170: frequently with _neuter_ _pronoun_ in _accusative_, τοῦτο ὑμῶν δέομαι 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Apologia” 17c, compare “Smp.” 173e, etc.: with _accusative_ _cognate_, δέημα, or oftener δέησιν, δεῖσθαί τινος, 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Acharnenses” 1059, 4th c.BC: Aeschines Orator 2.43, etc.: also with _accusative_ _of things_ only, ξύμφορα δ. 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 1.32; δυνατά τινος 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Protagoras” 335e; δίκαια καὶ μέτρια ὑμῶν 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 38.2; διαπράξωμαι ἃ δέομαι 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 2.3.29: with _genitive_ _person_ only, δεηθεὶς ὑμῶν]] having begged a favour of you, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 21.108]]: c.genitive person et infinitive, ἐδέετο τοῦ δήμου φυλακῆς πρὸς αὐτοῦ κυρῆσαι [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.59, compare 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Protagoras” 336a, etc.; δ. τινὸς ὥστε.. 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 1.119; ὅπως.. 1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus “Antonius” 84: rarely with _accusative_ _person_, ἐδέοντο Βοιωτοὺς ὅπως παραδώσουσι 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 5.36: parenthetic, δέομαι]]I pray, [LXX.Gen.44.18.]

deep_entry:
Abbott-Smith / STEPBible (TBESG)
δή
consecutive co-ordinating particle with no exact equiv. in Eng., giving greater exactness and emphasis to the word or words to which it is attached; sometimes translatable as now therefore, then, verily, certainly.
__1. With verbs: imperat., Act.6:3 (WH, mg.) 13:2, 1Co.6:20; hort. subjc., Luk.2:15, Act.15:36; indic., δή που (Τ, δήπου, which see), Heb.2:16.
__2. With pronouns: ὃ δή, now this is he who, Mat.13:23.†
(AS)

---

LSJ / STEPBible (TFLSJ)
δή,
properly a temporal Particle (compare ἤδη), at this or that point: hence, now, then, already, or at length:

__I
in Epic dialect (rarely Lyric poetry) sometimes at the beginning of a sentence or clause, Τεῦκρε πέπον, δὴ νῶϊν ἀπέκτατο πιστὸς ἑταῖρος [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 15.437; δὴ πάμπαν ἀποίχεαι ἀνδρὸς ἑῆος 19.342; δὴ γὰρ μέγα νεῖκος ὄρωρεν 13.122; δὴ τότε, δή ῥα τότε, 1.476, 13.719, +others,compare 5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “O.” 3.25, 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Septem contra Thebas” 214 (Lyric poetry): but usually second (or nearly so)]], frequently with Numerals and temporal Particles, ὀκτὼ δὴ προέηκα.. ὀϊστούς [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 8.297]]; ἐννέα δὴ βεβάασι.. ἐνιαυτοί full nine years, [Refs [2.134]]; ἕκτον δὲ δὴ τόδ᾽ ἦμαρ this is just the sixth day, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Orestes” 39, compare 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 24.107, etc.: also after _adverbs_ of Time, πολλάκι δή]] many a time and oft, often ere now,[Refs 5th c.BC+ [19.85; ὀψὲ δὲ δή 7.94; τρὶς δή 5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “P.” 9.91]]; πάλαι δή, Latin jamdudum, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Philoctetes” 806]]; νῦν δή just now, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Aves” 923 (frequently written νυνδή, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Theaetetus” 145b, etc.); νῦν τε καὶ ἄλλοτε δή [prev. work] 187d]]; now at length, [Refs [[prev. author] “R.” 353a, etc.]]; τότε δή at that very time, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 1.49, etc.]]; αὐτίκα δὴ μάλα this very instant, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 338b, etc.]]; ὕστερον δή yet later, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 2.17: frequently with temporal Conjunctions, ἐπεὶ δή (written ἐπειδή, which see), etc.]]

__II
without temporal significance, as a Particle of emphasis, in fact, of course, certainly, ναὶ δή, ἦ δή, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 1.286, 518, etc.]]; οὐ δή surely not, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Philoctetes” 246, compare 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Orestes” 1069, etc.]]; δῆλα δή, see at {δῆλος}; with Verbs, δὴ γὰρ ἴδον ὀφθαλμοῖσι [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 15.488; νῦν δὲ ὁρᾶτε δή 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 3.2.12; καὶ ἴστε δὴ οἷος.. 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Apologia” 21a: less frequently with Substantives, σοφιστὴν δή τοι ὀνομάζουσι τὸν ἄνδρα εἶναι]] they call the man a sophist as you know, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [[prev. author] “Prt.” 311e: with Conjunctions, ἵνα δή, ὡς δή, 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 23.207, 5.24, etc.; ὅπως δή 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 5.85]]; γὰρ δή for manifestly, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Choephori” 874, 891, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Theaetetus” 156c; οὐ γὰρ δή 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Coloneus” 265: hence with a]]participle representing Conjunction and Verb, ἅτε δὴ ἐόντες since they evidently are, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 8.90]]; but ὡς φόνον νίζουσα δή as though she were.., [Refs 8th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Iphigenia Taurica” 1338, compare 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.66, 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 5.4.4, etc.; and so, ironically, ὡς δή 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 1.110, 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Vespae” 1315, “Eq.” 693, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Protagoras” 342c, +others; frequently with σύ, ὡς δὴ σύ μοι τύραννος Ἀργείων ἔσῃ 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Agamemnon” 1633, compare 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Coloneus” 809, 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Andromache” 235, etc.]]; also ἵνα δή.. [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 420e, “Men.” 86d; ὅτι δή.. [prev. author] “Phdr.” 268d]]; also εἰσήγαγε τὰς ἑταιρίδας δή the pretended courtesans, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Historia Graeca (Hellenica)” 5.4.6, compare 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Ion” 1181, 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 4.67, 6.80.]]

__II.2
frequently placed immediately after Pronouns, ἐμὲ δή me of all persons, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 3.155]]; σὺ δή you of all persons, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. author] 1.115, 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Ajax” 1226]]; οὗτος δή this and no other, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.43; ὑμεῖς δὲ κεῖνοι δὴ οἵ.. 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Trachiniae” 1091]]; οὗτος δὴ ὁ Σωκράτης, ironically, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Theaetetus” 166a]]; τὸ λεγόμενον δὴ τοῦτο as the well-known saying goes, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. author] “Grg.” 514e, compare 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Hippolytus” 962]]; δή τις some one you know of, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Phaedo” 108c, +others: with possess. Pronouns, τὸ σὸν δὴ τοῦτο 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Symposium” 221b, compare “Grg.” 5c8 d, etc.: with relatives, ὃς δὴ νῦν κρατέει 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 21.315; τὰ δὴ καὶ ἐγένετο 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.22]]; οἷος δὴ σύ just such as thou, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 24.376, compare 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 1.32, 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Ajax” 995, etc.; ὅσα δή 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Acharnenses” 1, etc.: with _adjectives_, οἴη δή, μοῦνος δή, 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 12.69, 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.25; ἐν πολλῇ δὴ ἀπορίᾳ ἦσαν 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 3.1.2: frequently with Superlatives, μάχη ἐγένετο πλείστου δὴ χρόνου μεγίστη δὴ τῶν Ἑλληνικῶν 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 5.74; ἁπάντων δὴ ἄλγιστον 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Ajax” 992, etc.]]

__III
to mark a transition, with or without inference, so, then, νίκη μὲν δὴ φαίνετ᾽.. [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 3.457; τὴν μὲν δὴ τυραννίδα οὕτω ἔσχον 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.14; τοῦτο δὴ τὸ ἄγος οἱ Λακεδαιμόνιοι ἐκέλευον ἐλαύνειν 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 1.127.]]

__IV
with Indef. Particles, see at {δήποθεν, δήποτε, δήπω, δήπουθεν}: with interrogatives, τοῦ δὴ ἕνεκ; [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Gorgias” 457e; τί δὲ δή..; [prev. author] “Phd.” 58c]] (simply τί δ; what then? R.[Refs [357d)]]; πότερα δ; [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Philoctetes” 1235 (and with _adverbs_, ποῖ δὴ καὶ πόθε; 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Phdr.”]][near the start]; ποῦ δ; πῇ δ;[Refs 8th c.BC+ [[prev. work] 228e, 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 2.339, etc.): with Indef. Pronouns, δή strengthens the _indefinite_ notion, ἄλλοισιν δὴ ταῦτ᾽ ἐπιτέλλεο]] others be they who they may, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 1.295]]; μηδεὶς δή no one at all, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Theaetetus” 170e]]; δή τις some one or other, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. author] “R.” 498a (_plural_), etc. (rarely τις δή 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Iphigenia Taurica” 946)]]; the neuter δή τι is common, ἦ ἄρα δή τι ἐΐσκομεν ἄξιον εἶνα; in any way, whatever it be, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 13.446; τὸ ἱππικόν, τῷ δή τι καὶ ἐπεῖχε ἐλλάμψεσθαι 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.80; οὕτω δή τι [prev. author] 3.108, etc.; θεῶν ὅτεῳ δή]]whosoever it be, [Refs [[prev. author] 1.86]]; ἐπὶ μισθῷ ὅσῳ δή, Latin quantocumque, [Refs [[prev. work] 160]], etc.; οἵα δή γε.. [Refs 8th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Heraclidae” 632, compare “Supp.” 162; but θαυμαστὰ δὴ ὅσα 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Symposium” 220b; ὡς δή 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 5.24, etc.]]; so almost, ={ἤδη, ἀναπέτομαι δὴ πρὸς Ὄλυμπον} [Refs 6th c.BC+ [6th c.BC: Anacreon Lyricus 24; καὶ δὴ φίλον τις ἔκταν᾽ ἀγνοίας ὕπο 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Supplices” 499; ἤκουσα δή 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Antigone” 823; πάθη μὲν οὖν δὴ πόλλ᾽ ἔγωγ᾽ ἐκλαυσάμην [prev. author] “Tr.” 153; οἶσθα μὲν δή [prev. work] 627]]; so καὶ δή already, in fact, frequently not at the beginning of the sentence, κεῖται καὶ δὴ πάνθ᾽ ἅπερ εἶπας [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Ecclesiazusae” 514, compare “Nu.” 906, 3rd c.BC: Theocritus Poeta Bucolicus 5.83; but καὶ δή σφε λείπω 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Supplices” 507.]]

__IV.2
to continue a narrative, frequently after μέν, then, so, τότε μὲν δὴ.. ἡσυχίην εἶχε [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.11; Σόλων μὲν δὴ ἔνεμε [prev. work] 32; τὸν μὲν δὴ πέμπει [prev. work] 116; alone, εἷς δὴ τούτων.. ?? one of these.., [prev. work] 114, etc.: frequently in summing up, τοιαῦτα μὲν δὴ ταῦτα,]] Latin haec hactenus, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Prometheus Vinctus” 500, compare 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.14, 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 2.4; τούτων δὴ ἕνεκα 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 3.2.28, etc.]]; in summing up numbers, γίγνονται δὴ οὗτοι χίλιοι these then amount to [Refs [1, 000, [prev. work] 1.5.5]]; in resuming after a parenthesis, Ἀνδρομάχη, θυγάτηρ μεγαλήτορος Ἠετίωνος.., τοῦ περ δὴ θυγάτηρ [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 6.395; οὗτος δὴ.., ὁ μὲν δή 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.43.]]

__IV.2.b
with imperative and subjunctive, μὴ δὴ.. ἐπιέλπεο [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 1.545, compare 5.684, etc.; χωρῶμεν δὴ πάντες 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Philoctetes” 1469]]; ἐννοεῖτε γὰρ δή for do but consider, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 4.3.5]]; ἄγε δή, φέρε δή, ἴθι δή, σκόπει δή, λέγε δή, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Sophista” 235a, “Phd.” 63b, “Sph.” 224c, “Phd.” 80a, “Prt.” 312c.]]

__IV.3
to express what follows a fortiori, καὶ μετὰ ὅπλων γε δή above all with arms, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 4.78]]; μή τί γε δή not to mention, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 2.23; εἰ δὲ δὴ πόλεμος ἥξει [prev. author] 1.27.]]

__IV.4
καὶ δή and what is more, adding an emphatic statement, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 1.161, 15.251, 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 5.67, 5th c.BC: Lysias Orator 13.4; in Prose, frequently καὶ δὴ καί.., ἐς Αἴγυπτον ἀπίκετο.., καὶ δὴ καὶ ἐς Σάρδις 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.30, etc.]]; καὶ δὴ καὶ νῦν τί φῄ; and now what do you say? [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Theaetetus” 187c]]; καὶ δὴ μὲν οὖν παρόντα yes, and actually here present, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Coloneus” 31]]; especially in a series, ὑγίεια καὶ ἰσχὺς καὶ κάλλος καὶ πλοῦτος δή and of course riches, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Meno” 87e, compare “Tht.” 159c, “R.” 367d; εἴτ᾽.. εἴτ᾽.. εἴτεδή [prev. work] 493d.]]

__IV.4.b
καὶ δή is also used in answers, ἦ καὶ παρέστη κἀπὶ τέρμ᾽ ἀφίκετ; Answ. καὶ δὴ 'πὶ δισσαῖς ἦν.. πύλαις yes, he was even so far as.., [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Ajax” 49]]; βλέψον κάτω. Answ. καὶ δὴ βλέπω well, I am looking, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Aves” 175, compare “Pax” 327, “Pl.” 227f, 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Electra” 317f, 1436, etc.]]; πρόσθιγέ νύν μου. Answ. ψαύω καὶ δή [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Coloneus” 173]]; without καί, ἀποκρίνου περὶ ὧν ἂν ἐρωτῶ. Answ. ἐρώτα δή [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Theaetetus” 157d]]; ἐρώτα. Answ. ἐρωτῶ δή [Refs [[prev. author] “Grg.” 448b.]]

__IV.4.c
in assumptions or suppositions, καὶ δὴ δέδεγμαι and now suppose I have accepted, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Eumenides” 894, compare “Ch.” 565, 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Medea” 386, “Hel.” 1059, not found in 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus, once in 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Vespae” 1224.]]

__IV.5
δή in apodosi, after εἰ or ἐάν, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 5.898, 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.108, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 524e, etc.]]; after ὅτε, ἡνίκα, even then, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Antigone” 170f, “El.” 954]]; after ἐπεί, ἐπειδάν, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 1.6.14, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Cratylus” 435e, etc.]]; after ὡς, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 7.2.4; ἐν ᾧ δὲ ταῦτα ἐβουλεύοντο, καὶ δὴ ὁ βασιλεύς..]]already, [Refs [[prev. author] “An.” 1.10.10.]]

deep_entry:
Abbott-Smith / STEPBible (TBESG)
δῆλος, -η, -ον
[in LXX for אוּר, etc. ;]
__1. visible.
__2. clear to the mind, evident: Mat.26:73; δ. (sc. ἐστίν), before ὅτι, 1Co.15:27, Gal.3:11.†
SYN.: φανερός, with ref. to outward appearance, manifest as opposite to concealed; δ. with ref. to inner perception, evident, known, under­stood. (AS)

---

LSJ / STEPBible (TFLSJ)
δῆλος
(also Doric dialect, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Archytas Tarentinus Philosophus 1, 3rd c.BC: Theocritus Poeta Bucolicus 11.79, etc., and _Aeolic dialect_, compare πρόδηλος)]], η, ον, also ος, ον [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Medea” 1197]]: Epic dialect δέελος:

__I
properly visible, conspicuous, δέελον δ᾽ ἐπὶ σῆμά τ᾽ ἔθηκε [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 10.466, but:]]

__II
commonly, clear to the mind, manifest, νῦν δ᾽ ἤδη τόδε δ. [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 20.333, etc.]]

__II.2
δ. εἰμι is frequently used with participle, δ. ἐστιν ἀλγεινῶς φέρων i.e. it is clear that he takes it ill, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Philoctetes” 1011, compare “OT” 673, 1008, etc.]]; οἳ ἂν δ. ὦσι μὴ ἐπιτρέψοντες who are clearly not going to permit, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 1.71; with ὡς, δ. ἐστιν ὥς τι δρασείων κακόν 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Ajax” 326; δ. ἔσεσθε ὡς ὀργιζόμενοι 5th c.BC: Lysias Orator 12.90, compare 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 1.5.9]]; δ. ὁρᾶσθαι.. ὤν being as was plainly to be seen, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Orestes” 350: with ὅτι]] and a Verb, δ. ἐστιν ὅτι.. ἀκήκοεν [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Plutus” 333; δ. ἡ οἰκοδομία ὅτι κατὰ σπουδὴν ἐγένετο 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 1.9; δ. ἔσται ὅτι.. 5th c.BC: Lysias Orator 12.50: sometimes the]]participle or relative clause must be supplied, καταγελᾷς μου, δ. εἶ (i.e. καταγελῶν) [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Aves” 1407, compare [prev. author] “Lys.” 919]]; δῆλοι δέ (i.e. οὐ μένοντες) [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 5.10.]]

__II.3
δῆλον ποιεῖν show plainly, τινὶ ὅτι.. [Refs [[prev. author] 6.34, etc.]]: with participle, δῆλον ἐποιήσατε.. μηδίσαντες [Refs [[prev. author] 3.64.]]

__II.4
δῆλον (i.e. ἐστί) it is manifest, αὐτὸς πρὸς αὑτοῦ· δῆλον [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Ajax” 906; ἀλγεινά, Πρόκνη, δῆλον [prev. author] “fragment” 585; ἐκ πίθω ἀντλεῖς, δῆλον 3rd c.BC: Theocritus Poeta Bucolicus 10.13]]; δῆλον δέ, to introduce a proof, followed by γάρ, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 1.11, 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “de Coloribus” 799a5, etc.; δῆλον γάρ 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Fragmenta” 63; δῆλον ὅτι 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 3.38, etc.; τὰ Κύρου δῆλον ὅτι οὕτως ἔχει 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 1.3.9, compare “Cyr.” 2.4.24, etc.]], see at {δηλονότι}: in plural, δῆλα δή, δ. δ. καὶ ταῦτα [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Crito” 48b; ἢ δ. δ. ὅτι..; [prev. author] “Prt.” 309a, etc.: hence as]] adverb, usually written δηλαδή (which see).

__II.5
adverb δήλως is rejected by Attic dialect, [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd c.AD(?): Pollianus Epigrammaticus 6.207.]]

__III
δῆλοι, οἱ, Urim, [LXX.1Ki.28.6, +others (Cf. δέατο.)]

Abbott-Smith / STEPBible (TBESG)
δηλόω, -ῶ
[in LXX chiefly for ידע ;]
to make plain, declare: with accusative, 1Co.3:13, Col.1:8, Heb.9:8 12:27; with dative of person(s), 2Pe.1:14; with dative of person(s), before περί (pass.), 1Co.1:11; before εἰς, 1Pe.1:11.†
SYN.: ἐμφανίζω, to make manifest, render visible to the sight; δ. to render evident to the mind. (AS)

---

LSJ / STEPBible (TFLSJ)
δηλ-όω:—
passive, future δηλωθήσομαι [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 1.144]]; δηλώσομαι in passive sense, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Coloneus” 581; δεδηλώσομαι 5th c.BC: Hippocrates Medicus “περὶ ἄρθρων ἐμβολῆς” 45, 5th c.BC: Diogenes Apolloniates Philosophus 4]]:—make visible or manifest, show, exhibit, τὸν ἄνδρ᾽ Ἀχαιοῖς δ. [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Philoctetes” 616; ποῖον ὄμμα πατρὶ δηλώσ; [prev. author] “Aj.” 462]]: with infinitive added, ὡς γένος ἄτλητον ἀνθρώποισι δηλώσοιμ᾽ ὁρᾶν [Refs [[prev. author] “OT” 792, etc.]]:—passive, to be or become manifest, [Refs [[prev. author] “OC” 581, etc.]]

__2
make known, disclose, reveal, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Persae” 519, 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Tyrannus” 77, etc.]]; prove, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. author] “OC” 146, 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 1.3; δηλοῖ ὁ λόγος ὅτι.. 3rd c.AD: Democritus Epigrammaticus 7; αὐτὸ δηλώσει 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 19.157]]; explain, set forth, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 2.62]]; signify, ἐδήλουν οὐδὲν ὅτι ἴσασιν gave no sign of knowing, [Refs [[prev. author] 4.68]]: indicate, τὰς μεγίστας καὶ ἐλαχίστας [Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. author] 1.10, etc. Construct.: mostly δ. τινί τι 5th c.BC: Antipho Orator 1.30]]; δ. τι πρός or εἴς τινα, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Trachiniae” 369, 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 1.90; δ. περί τινος 5th c.BC: Lysias Orator 10.7; τινὶ περί τι 5th-6th c.BC: Isocrates Orator 11.9]]: with accusative et infinitive, [Refs 3rd c.AD+ [“SIG” 888.52 (Scaptopara, 3rd c.AD)]]: followed by a relative clause, δ. ὅτι [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Electra” 1106, 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 2.149, compare 1.57, etc.; οἷα φρονῶ 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Electra” 334; δ. περί τινος, ὡς.. 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 1.72, 73]]: with accusative et participle, σκευή τε γάρ σε καὶ τὸ δύστηνον κάρα δηλοῦτον.. ὄνθ᾽ ὃς εἶ [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Coloneus” 555]]; ὥς σε δηλώσω κακόν [ὄντα[Refs [] [prev. work] 783, compare “Ant.” 471: with]]participle nominative, referring to the subject, δηλώσω πατρὶ μὴ ἄσπλαγχνος γεγώς I will show my father that I am no dastard, [Refs [[prev. author] “Aj.” 472]]; δηλοῖς.. τι καλχαίνουσ᾽ ἔπος thou showest that thou art pondering.., [Refs [[prev. author] “Ant.” 20; δηλοῖς ὥς τι σημανῶν [prev. work] 242]]; δηλώσω οὐ παραγενόμενος I will show that I was not present, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Antipho Orator 2.4.8; δηλώσει μείζων γεγενημένος 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 1.21; also Λιβύη δηλοῖ ἑωυτὴν ἐοῦσα περίρρυτος 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 4.42; ἑαυτὸν ἐδήλωσεν ὅστις ἦν 1st c.BC: Dionysius Halicarnassensis 3.48.]]

__II
intransitive, to be clear or plain, δηλοῖ ὅτι οὐκ Ὁμήρου τὰ Κύπρια ἔπεά ἐστι [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 2.117; δηλοῖ δὲ ταῦτα.. ὅτι οὕτως ἔχει 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Gorgias” 483d; δηλώσει ἡ ἔχθρα ὅταν πρῶτον.. 5th-6th c.BC: Andocides Orator 4.12]]; to be significant, possess a meaning, with dative, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Cratylus” 434c.]]

__II.2
impersonal δηλοῖ, ={δῆλόν ἐστι}, δηλοῖ μοι ὅτι.., [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 9.68, compare 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Politica” 1296a20; δηλώσει 5th c.BC: Lysias Orator 10.20, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 497c; ἐδήλωσε 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Memorabilia” 1.2.32, compare “Cyr.” 7.1.30.]]

δημιουργ-ός,

Αιδης δ. ἄγριος 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Ajax” 1035]]; of medical practitioners, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Hippocrates Medicus “περὶ ἀρχαίης ἰητρικῇς” 1, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Symposium” 186d]]; but opposed to scientific physicians (ἀρχιτεκτονικοί), [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Politica” 1282a3]]; of sculptors, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 529e]]; of confectioners and cooks, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 7.31, 4th-3rd c.BC: Menander Comicus 518.12 (_feminine_), 4th c.BC: Antiphanes Comicus 225, Alexandr.Comedy texts 3]]; μέλιτος δ., of the bee, [Refs 4th c.AD+ [4th c.AD: Julianus Imperator “Orationes” 8.241a]]; οἱ δ. the artisan class at Athens, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Ἀθηναίων Πολιτεία” 13.2, 1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus “Theseus” 25]]; opposed to πολιτικοί, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Apologia” 23e]]; δαμιουργοί, ={πόρναι}, [Refs 5th c.AD+ [5th c.AD(?): Hesychius Legal icographus]]

metaphorically, maker, ἡ μαντικὴ φιλίας θεῶν καὶ ἀνθρώπων δ. [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Symposium” 188d]]; νόμων, πολιτείας, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Politica” 1273b32; λόγων 4th c.BC: Aeschines Orator 3.215]]; δ. κακῶν author of ill, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Fragmenta” 1059.7; πειθοῦς δ. ἡ ῥητορική 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Gorgias” 453a; ἀρετῆς [prev. author] “R.” 500d, 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Politica” 1329a21; ἐναργείας 4th c.BC: Demetrius Phalereus Rhetor “Demetrius on Style” 215]]; ὄρθρος δημιοεργός morn that calls man to work, [Refs [hymnus ad Mercurium 98.]]

creator, producer, νυκτός τε καὶ ἡμέρας [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Timaeus” 40c; οὐρανοῦ [prev. author] “R.” 530a]]; especially in later philosophy, the Creator of the visible world, Demiurge, [[Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Philolaus Philosophus] 21, 5th c.BC: Hippocrates Medicus “ἐπιστολαί” 23, 1st c.AD: Philo Judaeus 1.632, etc.; ὁ νοῦς ἀπεκύησε ἕτερον νοῦν δ. “Corpus Hermeticum” 1.9]]; also name for μονάς, [Refs [“Theologumena Arithmeticae” 5.24: as]] adjective, δ. λόγος creative reason, [Refs 5th c.AD+ [5th c.AD: Syrianus Philosophus et Rhetor “in Metaphysica commentaria - Comm. in” 7.27.]]

δῆμος, -ου, ὁ
[in LXX chiefly for מִשְׁפָּחָה ;]
__1. a district, country.
__2. the common people, the people generally; esp. the people assembled: Act.12:22 17:5 19:30 33.
† SYN.: λαός, the people at large: δ., the people as a body politic; opposite to δ. is ὄχλος, the unorganized multitude. ἔθνος, in sing., means in NT as in Gk. writers generally, a nation, but in pl. denotes the rest of mankind apart from the Jews: Gentiles. λ. also, rare in cl. (Att... λεώς), is frequently in LXX and NT, and usually limited to the chosen people, Israel (cf. Cl. Rev., i, 42 f.; Cremer, 689). (AS)

---

LSJ / STEPBible (TFLSJ)
δῆμος,
Doric dialect δᾶμος (compare infr. IV), ὁ, district, country, land, Βοιωτοὶ μάλα πίονα δ. ἔχοντες [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 5.710; Λυκίης ἐν πίονι δ. 16.437, compare 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 13.322, etc.; 'Ιθάκης ἐνὶ δ. 1.103; δήμῳ ἔνι Τρώων 13.266; λαοὶ ἀνὰ δῆμον 16.95: _metaphorically_, δῆμος ὀνείρων]] the land of dreams, [Refs [24.12.]]

__2
the people, inhabitants of such a district, πόληΐ τε παντί τε δήμῳ [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 3.50, compare “hymnus ad Cererem” 271; Βακτρίων ἔρρει πανώλης δ. 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Persae” 732.]]

__II
hence (since the common people lived in the country, the chiefs in the city), the commons, common people, δήμου ἀνήρ, opposed to βασιλεύς, ἔξοχος ἀνήρ, etc., [NT+8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 2.198, 188, compare 11.328, 8th-7th c.BC: Hesiodus Epicus “Opera et Dies” 261, 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 5.66, NT.Act.12.22, etc. (rarely of a single person, δῆμον ἐόντα]] being a commoner, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 12.213)]]; opposed to οἱ εὐδαίμονες, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.196]]; opposed to οἱ παχέες, [Refs [[prev. author] 5.30]]; opposed to οἱ δυνατοί, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 5.4; οἱ.. ἐπαναστάντες τοῖς δυνατοῖς καὶ ὄντες δῆμος [prev. author] 8.73]]; = Latin plebs, [Refs 1st c.BC+ [1st c.BC: Dionysius Halicarnassensis 6.88, etc.; τοῦ πολλοῦ δ. εἷς]]unus de plebe, [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd c.AD: Lucianus Sophista “Sat.” 2; τοῦ δ. ὤν [prev. author] “Gall.” 22]]; in an army, rank and file, opposed to officers, ὁ δ. τῶν στρατιωτῶν [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 6.1.14.]]

__II.2
metaphorically, δ. ἰχθύων [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Antiphanes Comicus 206.7; τυράννων 2nd-3rd c.AD: Philostratus Sophista “Vitae Sophistarum” 1.15.1; πιθήκων [prev. author] “VA” 3.4]]; ὀρνέων [Refs 4th c.AD+ [4th c.AD: Alciphro Epistolographus 3.30.]]

__III
in a political sense, the sovereign people, the free citizens, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Septem contra Thebas” 199, 1011, etc.; ὁ δ. ὁ Ἀθηναίων “IG” 12.10.37, etc.; προστάτης τοῦ δήμου 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 6.35, etc.; personified, 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Equites” 42, +others; ἱερεὺς τοῦ Δ. καὶ τῶν Χαρίτων “IG” 22.1028.]]

__III.2
popular government, democracy, opposed to ὀλιγαρχίη, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 3.82]]; opposed to οἱ τύραννοι, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Andocides Orator 1.106; πολίτεομα εἶναι ἐν Χίῳ δ. “SIG” 283.4 (4th c.BC)]]; δήμου κατάλυσις [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Historia Graeca (Hellenica)” 2.3.28, 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Ἀθηναίων Πολιτεία” 8.4; ταῦτα καταλύει δῆμον, οὐ κωμῳδία 4th-3rd c.BC: Philippides Comicus 25.7]]; δ. καταστῆσαι, καταπαύειν, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Historia Graeca (Hellenica)” 7.3.3, 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 1.107]]: in plural, democracies, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [[prev. author] 3.82, 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 20.15; δ. ὁ ἔσχατος 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Politica” 1277b3.]]

__III.3
the popular assembly, λέγειν ἐν τῷ δ. [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 565b]]; ἡ βουλὴ καὶ ὁ δ., formula in Inscrr., as [Refs [“IG” 12.39, etc.]]; of the assembly of Oxyrhynchus, [Refs 3rd c.AD+ [“POxy.” 41.19 (3rd-4th c.AD), 1407.19 (3rd c.AD).]]

__IV
township, commune (= Doric dialect κώμη accusative to [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Poetica” 1448a37; but διελόμενοι τὴν μὲν πόλιν κατὰ κώμας, τὴν δὲ χώραν κατὰ δήμους 5th-6th c.BC: Isocrates Orator 7.46, compare 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Leges” 746d, and see below), in Attica, 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 5.69, 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Ἀθηναίων Πολιτεία” 21.5, 1st c.BC-1st c.AD: Strabo Geographus 9.1.16, “IG” 12.76.9, +others; elsewhere, [prev. work]12(5).594 (from Ceos), “Phib.” 1.28.13 (3rd c.AD), “OGI” 49.14 (from Ptolemais)]], etc.:—Doric dialect δᾶμος, [Refs [“Michel” 418.34 (from Calymna), “IG” 12(1).58.23 (from Lindos)]]: in indications of origin, Σωφάνης ἐκ δ. Δεκελεῆθεν [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 9.73; δήμου Ἁλαιεύς 4th c.BC: Antiphanes Comicus 211; τῶν δήμων Πιτθεύς 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Euthyphro” 2b; τῶν δ. Θορίκιος 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 39.30, compare 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Ἀθηναίων Πολιτεία” 21.4; ἐπιγράψαι τοὺς βουλευτὰς πατρόθεν καὶ τοῦ δ. “IG” 22.223 B 4: _metaphorically_, οἱ τῆς θαλάσσης δ. 2nd-3rd c.AD: Philostratus Sophista “de gymnastica” 44.]]

__V
name for a prostitute, [Refs 7th c.BC+ [7th c.BC: Archilochus Lyricus 184.]]

={κατανάγκη}, Ps.-[Refs 1st c.AD+ [1st c.AD: Dioscorides (Dioscurides) Medicus 4.131]]. (Perh. cognate with Sanskrit dā´ti 'reap', δαίομαι, δατέομαι.)

δημόσιος, -α, -ον
(δῆμος), [in LXX: 2Ma.6:10, 3Ma.2:27 4:7 * ;]
belonging to the people, public: Act.5:18; dative fem. used adverbially (cl.);

LSJ / STEPBible (TFLSJ)
δημόσιος,
Doric dialect δᾱμ-, α, ον (ος, ον [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Hippocrates Medicus (see. below))]], belonging to the people or state, κτέανα [Refs 6th c.BC+ [6th c.BC: Xenophanes Poeta Philosophus 2.8; τὰδ. 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 5.29, 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Vespae” 554; δ. χρήματα 5th c.BC: Cratinus Comicus 171; πλοῦτος 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 1.80]]; χώρα, opposed to ἱερά, ἰδία, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Politica” 1267b34; ἡ δ. τράπεζα “IG” 22.1013]]; τὰ ἱερὰ τὰ δ., opposed to ἰδιωτικά, [Refs [“SIG” 1015.9 (Halic.)]]; ἀγῶνες, δίκαι, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aeschines Orator 1.2, 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Politica” 1320a12]]; δ. λόγος, = Latin fiscus, [Refs [“BGU” 193.27, “OGI” 1669.21]]; δημόσιον εἶναι, γίγνεσθαι, to be, become state-property, be confiscated, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 2.13, “IG” 22.1100.40 (2nd c.AD: Hadrianus Imperator Epigrammaticus), 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Leges” 742b, etc.; γῆν δ. ποιεῖν 5th c.BC: Lysias Orator 18.14.]]

__b
used by the public, βαλανεῖα, λουτρόν, [Refs 2nd c.BC+ [2nd c.BC: Polybius Historicus 26.1.12, 2nd c.AD: Herodianus Grammaticus 1.12.4.]]

__2
common, δημοσιώτατος τρόπος, τόπος, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Topica” 162a35, “SE” 165a5; δημόσιος κακίη]]epidemic, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Hippocrates Medicus “ἐπιστολαί” 19 (“Hermes” 53.67).]]

__II
as substantive:

__II.a
δημόσιος (i.e. δοῦλος), ὁ, any public slave or servant, as, the public crier, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 6.121]]; policeman, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Lysistrata” 436]]; public notary, ={γραμματεύς}, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 19.129, etc.]]; public executioner, [Refs 1st c.BC+ [1st c.BC: Diodorus Siculus Historicus 13.102]]: generally, public official, τὸν ἀρχέφοδον καὶ τοὺς ἄλλους δημοσίους [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [“POxy.” 69.13 (2nd c.AD).]]

__II.b
public victim, ={φάρμακος}, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Equites” 1136, cf. Scholia (at [prev. work])]]

__II.c
harlot, prostitute, [Refs 7th c.BC+ [6th c.AD: Procopius Caesariensis Historicus “Historia Arcana” 9 (compare 7th-6th c.BC: Sappho Lyrica 148).]]

__III
neuter, δημόσιον, τό, the state, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.14, 4th c.BC: Aeschines Orator 3.58; οἱ ἐκ δ.]]public officials, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Respublica Lacedaemoniorum” 3.3.]]

__III.b
public building, hall, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 6.52.]]

__III.c
treasury, ={τὸ κοινόν, ἀργύριον ὀφείλοντες τῷ δ}. [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Andocides Orator 1.73, compare 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 21.182, 4th-3rd c.BC: Dinarchus Orator 2.2; ὁ ἐκ δ. μισθός 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 6.31; ἡ ἐκ τοῦ δ. τροφή 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 465d; τελεῖν εἰς τὸ δ. “BGU” 1188.12 (Aug.), 1158.18 (1st c.BC).]]

__III.d
the public prison, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 5.18.]]

__III.2
τὰ δ. public archives, [Refs [“OGI” 229.108 (from Smyrna).]]

__III.2.b
public dues, taxes, in plural, [Refs 3rd c.AD+ [“PLond.” 3.938.11 (3rd c.AD), “BGU” 1018.21 (3rd c.AD).]]

__IV
feminine, δαμοσία (i.e. σκηνή), ἡ, tent of the Spartan kings: hence οἱ περὶ δαμοσίαν the king's council, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Historia Graeca (Hellenica)” 4.5.8, “Lac.” 13.7.]]

__V
as adverb:

__V.1
dative δημοσία, Ionic dialect -ίῃ, at the public expense, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.30, 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Aves” 396, etc.]]; by public consent, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 21.50]]; on public service, δ. ἀποδημεῖν [Refs [[prev. author] 45.3]]; δ. κρίνειν try in the public courts, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Andocides Orator 1.105]]; δ. τεθνάναι to die by the hands of the public executioner, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 45.81.]]

__V.2
as a community, opposed to ἰδίᾳ, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Apologia” 30b.]]

__V.3
commonly, popularly, τὰ δ. νομιζόμενα ἀγαθά [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd c.AD: Lucianus Sophista “Nigr.” 4.]]

__V.4
regular adverb -ίως[Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd c.AD: Apollonius Dyscolus Grammaticus “de Adverbiis;” 151.12]]; on public business, καταπλεῦσαι [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [“SIG” 520.7 (Naxos, 3rd c.BC).]]

εἰ δή ποτε if ever, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 1.40.]]

__3
with interrogative, τί δή ποτ; what in the world? what or why now? καίτοι τί δή ποτ; [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 4.35]]; πόσοι δή ποτ᾽ εἰσὶν οἱ..; how many do you suppose? [Refs [[prev. author] 20.21.]]

__4
especially frequently with relatives, ὅτι δή κοτε πράξαντα [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 6.134; ὅστις δ. ὤν 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Phaedrus” 273c]]; ὅτι δή ποτε whatever it may be, 'so-and-so', [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 21.32; ὁπόθεν δ. [prev. author] 35.6: strengthened by οὖν, ὅντινα δή ποτ᾽ οὖν τρόπον [prev. author] 40.8]]; οἷος δή ποτ᾽ οὖν variant in [Refs 1st c.AD+ [1st c.AD: Dioscorides (Dioscurides) Medicus 5.10]]; also δή ποτ᾽ οὖν without relative, κατὰ πρεσβείαν ἢ κατ᾽ ἄλλην δ. χρείαν [Refs [“Arch.Papyrus” 6.9 (from Delos).]]

LSJ / STEPBible (TFLSJ)
δήπου,
indefinite adverb (better written δή που) perhaps, it may be, ᾧ δή που ἀδελφεὸν ἔκτανε [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 24.736]]: in Trag. and Attic dialect usually doubtless, I presume, οὐ δήπου τλητόν [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Prometheus Vinctus” 1064; τῶν Ααΐου δ. τις ὠνομάζετο 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Tyrannus” 1042, compare 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Plutus” 491, 582, 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 1.121, etc.]]; ἴστε γὰρ δή που, μέμνησθε γὰρ δή που, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 2.25, 19.113, compare 18.249; σχεδὸν ἴσμεν ἅπαντες δή που [prev. author] 3.9; οὐδεὶς ἀγνοεῖ δή που [prev. author] 21.156.]]

__II
as interrogative implying an affirmative answer, τὴν αἰχμάλωτον κάτοισθα δή πο; i.e. I presume you know, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Trachiniae” 418; ἀνόμοιον δή που 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Theaetetus” 159b]]; οὐ δή πο; surely it is not so? implying a negative answer, as [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Ranae” 526, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Meno” 73c.]]

deep_entry:
Abbott-Smith / STEPBible (TBESG)
διά (before a vowel δ᾽, exc. Rom.8:10, 2Co.5:7, and in (Proper name)s; Tdf., Pr., 94),
prep. with genitive, accusative, as in cl.;
__1. with genitive, through;
__(i) of Place, after verbs of motion or action: Mat.2:12  12:43, Mrk.2:23, Luk.4:30, Jhn.4:4, 2Co.11:33, al.; σώζεσθαι (διας-) δ. πυρός, ὕδατος, 1Co.3:15, 1Pe.3:20; βλέπειν δ. ἐσόπτρου, 1Co.13:12; metaphorically, of a state or condition: Rom.14:20, 2Co.2:4  5:7, 10; δ. γράμματος, ἀκροβυστίας (Lft., Notes, 263, 279), Rom.2:27  4:11; δι ̓ὑπομενῆς, Rom.8:25.
__(ii) Of Time;
__(a) during which: Mat.26:61, Mrk.14:58, Luk.5:5; δ. παντὸς τοῦ ζῆν, Heb.2:15; δ. παντός (διαπαντός in Mrk.5:5, Luk.24:53), always, continually, Mat.18:10, Act.2:25" (LXX)  10:2 24:16, Rom.11:10" (LXX), 2Th.3:16, Heb.9:6  13:15.
__(b) within which: Act.1:3; δ. νυκτός, Act.5:19  16:9 17:10 23:31;
__(with) after which (Field, Notes, 20; Abbott, JG, 255f.): Mrk.2:1, Act.24:17, Gal.2:1.
__(iii) Of the Means or Instrument;
__(1) of the efficient cause (regarded also as the instrument): of God, Rom.11:36, 1Co.1:9, Gal.4:7, Heb.2:10  7:21; of Christ, Rom.1:8  5:1,  17, 1Co.15:21, 1Pe.4:11, al.; δ. τ. ὑμῶν δεήσεως, Rom.1:12, 2Co.1:4, Gal.4:23, al.;
__(2) of the agent, instrument or means;
__(a) with genitive of person(s), Mat.11:2, Luk.1:70, Jhn.1:17, Act.1:16, Rom.2:16, 1Co.1:21, Eph.1:5, Heb.2:14, Rev.1:1, al.; ὑπὸ τ. κυρίου δ. τ. προφήτου (δ. τ. κυρίου, 1Th.4:2 (M, Th., in l.); Lft., Rev., 121f.), Mat.1:22  2:15, Rom.1:2; δ. ἐπιστολῆς ὡς δ. ἡμῶν (Field, Notes, 202), 2Th.2:2; δ. Σ. (NTD, 22), 1Pe.5:12;
__(b)  with genitive of thing(s) (where often the simple dative is used in cl.; Jannaris, Gr., 375), Jhn.11:4, Act.5:12; δ. τ. πίστεως, Rom.3:30; δ. λόγου θεοῦ, 1Pe.1:23; δ. παραβολῆς, Luk.8:4; δουλεύειν δ. τ. ἀγάπης, Gal.5:13; δ. ἐπαγγελίας, Gal.3:18,
__2. C. accusative;
__(i) rarely, as with genitive, through (Hom), δ. μέσον Σαμαρίας (ICC, in l.; Bl., §42, 1; Robertson, Gr., 581), Luk.17:11.
__(ii) by reason of, because of, for the sake of;
__(a) with accusative of person(s) (M, Pr., 105), Mrk.2:27, Jhn.6:57 11:42, Rom.8:20;
__(b) with accusative of thing(s), δ. φθόνον, Mat.27:18, Mrk.15:10; δ. φόβον, Jhn.7:13 20:19; δ. ἀγάπην, Eph.2:4; δ. τοῦτο, freq., for this cause, therefore, Mat.6:25, Mrk.6:14, Luk.11:49, Jhn.6:65, al.; id. before ὅτι, Jhn.5:16 10:17, al.; δ. τί, why, Mat.9:11, 14 Mrk.2:18, Jhn.7:45, al.; δ. τό, with inf., Mrk.5:4, Luk.9:7, Jas.4:2.
__3. In composition,
__(1) through, as in διαβαίνω;
__(2) of separation, asunder, as in διασπάω;
__(3) of distribution, abroad, as in διαγγέλλω;
__(4) of transition, as διαλλάσσω;
__(5) of "perfective" action (M, Pr., 112f., 115f.), as διαφύγω, διακαθαρίζω.
(AS)
