LSJ / STEPBible (TFLSJ)
διά,
poetry διαί (Aeolic dialect ζά, which see), preposition governing genitive and accusative — Rad. sense, through; never anastrophic [Prop. δῐᾰ: but [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Homerus Epicus]] uses ῑ at the beginning of a line, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 3.357, 4.135, +others]]: also ᾱ, for the sake of meter, frequently in [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Homerus Epicus, for which 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus]] uses διαί in Lyric poetry, [Refs [“Ag.” 448, +others]]]

__A
WITH GEN.

__A.I
of Place or Space:

__A.I.1
of motion in a line, from one end to the other, right through, in [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Homerus Epicus]] frequently of the effect of weapons, διὰ μὲν ἀσπίδος ἦλθε.. ἔγχος καὶ διὰ θώρηκος.. [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 3.357; δουρὶ βάλεν Δάμασον κυνέης διά 12.183; δι᾽ ὤμου.. ἔγχος ἦλθεν 4.481; in Prose, τιτρώσκειν διὰ τοῦ θώρακος 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 1.8.26; διὰ τοῦ ὀρόφου ἐφαίνετο πῦρ [prev. work] 7.4.16: also of persons, διὰ Σκαιῶν πεδίονδ᾽ ἔχον ὠκέας ἵππους]] out through the Scaean gate, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 3.263]]; δι᾽ ἠέρος αἰθέρ᾽ ἵκανεν quite through the lower air even to the ether, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 14.288, compare 2.458]]; διὰ Τρώων πέτετο straight through them,[Refs 5th c.BC+ [13.755; δι᾽ ὄμματος.. λείβων δάκρυον 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Coloneus” 1250, etc.]]: also in Compos. with πρό and ἐκ, see at {διαπρό},{διέκ}: in adverbial phrases, διὰ πασῶν (i.e. χορδῶν), see at {διαπασῶν}:from beginning to end,_ [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Prometheus Vinctus” 275, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 519c, etc.: with _adjectives_ alone, δ. παντός]]continually, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Choephori” 862 (Lyric poetry), etc.]]; δι᾽ ὀλίγου for a short time, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 1.77; δ. μακροῦ 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Hecuba” 320; ὁ δ. μέσου χρόνος 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 8.27.]]

__A.I.2
of the interval which has passed between two points of Time, δ. χρόνου πολλοῦ or δ. πολλοῦ χρ. after a long time, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. author] 3.27, 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Plutus” 1045; δ. μακρῶν χρόνων 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Timaeus” 22d: without an]] adjective, δ. χρόνου after a time, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Philoctetes” 758, 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 1.4.28, etc.]]; δι᾽ ἡμερῶν after several days, [NT.Mark.2.1]; and with adjectives alone, δι᾽ ὀλίγου [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 5.14; οὐ δ. μακροῦ [prev. author] 6.15, 91; δ. πολλοῦ 2nd c.AD: Lucianus Sophista “Nigr.” 2, etc.: with Numerals, δι᾽ ἐτέων εἴκοσι 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 6.118, compare “OGI” 56.38 (3rd c.BC), etc.: but δ. τῆς ἑβδόμης]] till the seventh day, [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd c.AD: Lucianus Sophista “Hist.Conscr.” 21: also distributively, χρόνος δ. χρόνου προὔβαινε]] time after time, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Philoctetes” 285; ἄλλος δι᾽ ἄλλου 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Andromache” 1248.]]

__A.I.3
of successive Intervals, δ. τρίτης ἡμέρης every other day, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 2.37; δ. τρίτου ἔτεος [prev. work] 4, etc.]]; δ. πεντετηρίδος every four years (with inclusive reckoning), [Refs [[prev. author] 3.97]]; δι᾽ ἔτους πέμπτου, of the Olympic games, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Plutus” 584 (but δι᾽ ἑνδεκάτου ἔτεος]] in the course of the eleventh year, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.62).]]

__A.III
causal, through, by,

__A.III.a
of the Agent, δι᾽ ἀλλέλων or -ου ἐπικηρυκεύεσθαι, ποιεῖσθαι, by the mouth of.., [NT+5th c.BC+ [[prev. author] 1.69, 6.4, compare 1.113; δι᾽ ἑρμηνέως λέγειν 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 2.3.17, etc.; τὸ ῥηθὲν ὑπὸ Κυρίου δ. τοῦ προφήτου NT.Matt.1.22; δι᾽ ἑκόντων ἀλλ᾽ οὐ δ. βίας ποιεῖσθαι 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Philebus” 58b]]; πεσόντ᾽ ἀλλοτρίας διαὶ γυναικός by her doing, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Agamemnon” 448 (Lyric poetry); ἐκ θεῶν γεγονὼς δ. βασιλέων πεφυκώς 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 7.2.24]]; δι᾽ ἑαυτοῦ ποιεῖν τι of oneself, not by another's agency, [Refs [[prev. work] 1.1.4]], etc.; but also, by oneself alone, unassisted, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 15.14, compare 22.38.]]

__A.III.b
of the Instrument or Means, δ. χειρῶν by hand (properly by holding between the hands), δι᾽ ὁσίων χ. θιγών [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Coloneus” 470]]; also δ. χερῶν λαβεῖν, δ. χειρὸς ἔχειν in the hand, [Refs [[prev. author] “Ant.” 916, 1258 (but τὰ τῶν ξυμμάχων δ. χειρὸς ἔχειν]] to keep a firm hand on, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 2.13); δ. στέρνων ἔχειν 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Antigone” 639; ἡ ἀκούουσα πηγὴ δι᾽ ὤτων [prev. author] “OT” 1387; δ. στόματος ἔχειν 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 1.4.25; δ. μνήμης ἔχειν 2nd c.AD: Lucianus Sophista “Cat.” 9; αἱ δ. τοῦ σώματος ἡδοναί 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Memorabilia” 1.5.6]]; δ. λόγων συγγίγνεσθαι to hold intercourse by word, [NT+5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Politicus” 272b; δ. λόγου ἀπαγγέλλειν NT.Act.15.27; δι᾽ ἐπιστολῶν NT.2Cor.10.9, “POxy.” 1070.15 (3rd c.AD).]]

__A.III.c
of Manner (where διά with its Noun frequently serves as an adverb), δ. μέθης ποιήσασθαι τὴν συνουσίαν [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Symposium” 176e]]; παίω δι᾽ ὀργῆς through passion, in passion, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Tyrannus” 807]]; δ. τάχους, ={ταχέως}, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. author] “Aj.” 822, 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 1.63 (but δ. ταχέων [prev. work] 80, +others)]]; δ. σπουδῆς in haste, hastily, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Bacchae” 212]]; δι᾽ αἰδοῦς with reverence, respectfully, [Refs [[prev. work] 441]]; δ. ψευδῶν ἔπη lying words, [Refs [[prev. author] “Hel.” 309]]; αἱ δ. καρτερίας ἐπιμέλειαι long-continued exertions, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Memorabilia” 2.1.20]]; δι᾽ ἀκριβείας, δ. πάσης ἀκρ., [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Timaeus” 23d, “Lg.” 876c; δ. σιγῆς [prev. author] “Grg.” 450c; δ. ξυμφορῶν ἡ ξύμβασις ἐγένετο 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 6.10; οὐ δι᾽ αἰνιγμάτων, ἀλλ᾽ ἐναργῶς γέγραπται 4th c.BC: Aeschines Orator 3.121; δι᾽ αἵματος, οὐ δ. μέλανος τοὺς νόμους ὁ Δράκων ἔγραψεν 1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus “Solon” 17: also with _adjectives_, δ. βραχέων, δ. μακρῶν τοὺς λόγους ποιεῖσθαι, 5th-6th c.BC: Isocrates Orator 14.3, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Gorgias” 449b; ἀποκρίνεσθαι δ. βραχυτάτων [prev. passage] d; compare infr. IV.]]

__A.III.2
in later Prose, of Material out of which a thing is made, κατασκευάζειν εἴδωλα δι᾽ ἐλέφαντος καὶ χρυσοῦ [Refs 1st c.BC+ [1st c.BC: Diodorus Siculus Historicus 17.115; θυσίαι δι᾽ ἀλφίτου καὶ σπονδῆς πεποιημέναι 1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus “Numa” 8; βρώματα δ. μέλιτος καὶ γάλακτος γιγνόμενα 2nd c.AD: Athenaeus Epigrammaticus 14.646e; οἶνος δ. βουνίου 1st c.AD: Dioscorides (Dioscurides) Medicus 5.46.]]

__A.IV
διά τινος ἔχειν, εἶναι, γίγνεσθαι, to express conditions or states, ἀγὼν διὰ πάσης ἀγωνίης ἔχων extending through every kind of contest, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 2.91; δι᾽ ἡσυχίης εἶναι [prev. author] 1.206]]; δι᾽ ὄχλου εἶναι to be troublesome, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Ecclesiazusae” 888; δ. φόβου εἶναι 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 6.59; δι᾽ ἀπεχθείας γίγνεσθαι 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Hiero” 9.2; ἡ ἐπιμέλεια δ. χάριτος γίγνεται [prev. passage]; δ. μιᾶς γνώμης γίγνεσθαι 5th-6th c.BC: Isocrates Orator 4.138.]]

__A.IV.b
with Verbs of motion, δ. μάχης ἐλεύσονται will engage in battle, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 6.9; ἐλθεῖν 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 4.92]]; δ. παντὸς πολέμου, δ. φιλίας ἰέναι τινί, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 3.2.8]]; δ. δίκης ἰέναι τινί go to law with.., [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Antigone” 742, compare 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 6.60; δ. τύχης ἰέναι 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Tyrannus” 773; δι᾽ ὀργῆς ἥκειν [prev. author] “OC” 905]]; ἐμαυτῷ δ. λόγων ἀφικόμην I held converse with myself, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Medea” 872]]; δ. λόγων, δ. γλώσσης ἰέναι come to open speech, [Refs [[prev. author] “Tr.” 916, “Supp.” 112]]; δ. φιλημάτων ἰέναι come to kissing, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. author] “Andr.” 416; δ. δικαιοσύνης ἰέναι καὶ σωφροσύνης 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Protagoras” 323a, etc.]]; δ. πυρὸς ἰέναι (see. πῦρ): in passive sense, δι᾽ ἀπεχθείας ἐλθεῖν τινι to be hated by.., [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Prometheus Vinctus” 121 (_anapaest meter_).]]

__A.IV.c
with transitive Verbs, δι᾽ αἰτίας ἔχειν or ἄγειν τινά hold in fault, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 2.60, 2nd-3rd c.AD: Aelianus “Varia Historia” 9.32; δι᾽ ὀργῆς ἔχειν τινά 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 2.37, etc.; δ. φυλακῆς ἔχειν τι [prev. author] 7.8]]; δι᾽ οἴκτου ἔχειν τινά, δι᾽ αἰσχύνης ἔχειν τι, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Hecuba” 851, “IT” 683; δ. πένθους τὸ γῆρας διάγειν 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 4.6.6; δι᾽ οὐδενὸς ποιεῖσθαί τι 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Coloneus” 584.]]

__B
WITH Acc.

__B.I
of Place, only poetical, in same sense as διά with genitive:

__B.I.1
through, ἓξ δὲ δ. πτύχας ἦλθε.. χαλκός [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 7.247; ἤϊξε δ. δρυμὰ.. καὶ ὕλην 11.118, compare 23.122, etc.]]; δ. τάφρον ἐλαύνειν across it,[Refs 5th c.BC+ [12.62; δ. δώματα ποιπνύοντα 1.600; ἐπὶ χθόνα καὶ δ. πόντον βέβακεν 5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “I.” 4(3).41; φεύγειν δ. κῦμ᾽ ἅλιον 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Supplices” 14 (_anapaest meter_).]]

__B.I.2
through, among, in, οἴκεον δι᾽ ἄκριας [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 9.400; ἄραβος δὲ δ. στόμα γίγνετ᾽ ὀδόντων 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 10.375 (but μῦθον, ὃν.. δ. στόμα.. ἄγοιτο]] through his mouth,[Refs 8th c.BC+ [14.91; so δ. στόμα ὄσσαν ἱεῖσαι 8th-7th c.BC: Hesiodus Epicus “Theogonia” 65; ἀεὶ γὰρ ἡ γυνή σ᾽ ἔχει δ. στόμα 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Lysistrata” 855); δ. κρατερὰς ὑσμίνας 8th-7th c.BC: Hesiodus Epicus “Theogonia” 631; νόμοι δι᾽ αἰθέρα τεκνωθέντες 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Tyrannus” 867 (Lyric poetry).]]

__B.II
of Time, also poetical, δ. νύκτα [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 2.57, etc.]]; δ. γλυκὺν ὕπνον during sweet sleep, [Refs 2nd c.BC+ [2nd c.BC: Moschus Bucolicus 4.91.]]

__B.III
causal:

__B.III.1
of persons, thanks to, by aid of, νικῆσαι δ... __B.III.2
of things, to express the Cause, Occasion, or Purpose, δι᾽ ἐμὴν ἰότητα because of my will, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 15.41; Διὸς μεγάλου δ. βουλάς 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 8.82]]; δι᾽ ἀφραδίας for, through want of thought,[Refs [19.523; δι᾽ ἀτασθαλίας 23.67]]; δι᾽ ἔνδειαν by reason of poverty, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 7.8.6]]; δ. καῦμα, δ. χειμῶνα,[Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. work] 1.7.6; δι᾽ ἄγνοιαν καὶ ἀμαθίαν 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Protagoras” 360b, etc.]]: frequently also with neuter adjectives, δ. τ; wherefore?; δ. τοῦτο, δ. ταῦτα on this account; δι᾽ ὅ, δι᾽ ἅ on which account; δ. πολλά for many reasons, etc.

__B.III.3
={ἕνεκα}, to express Purpose, δἰ ἀχθηδόνα for the sake of vexing, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 4.40, compare 5.53]]; δ. τὴν τούτου σαφήνειαν with a view to clearing this up, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 524c, compare 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Ethica Nicomachea” 1172b21]]; αὐτή δι᾽ αὑτήν for its own sake, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 367b, etc.]]

WITHOUT CASE as adverb throughout, δ. πρό (see. supr. A.I.I); δ. δ᾽ ἀμπερές [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 11.377.]]

__D
IN COMPOSITION (joined with other words),

__D.I
through, right through, of Space, διαβαίνω, διέχω, διιππεύω.

__D.II
in different directions, as in διαπέμπω, διαφορέ; of separation, asunder, διαιρέω, διαλύ; of difference or disagreement, at variance, διαφωνέω, διαφέρ; or simply mutual relation, one with another, διαγωνίζομαι, διάδω, διαθέω, διαπίνω, διαφιλοτιμέομαι.

__D.III
pre-eminence, διαπρέπω, διαφέρω.

__D.IV
completion, to the end, utterly, διεργάζομαι, διαμάχομαι, διαπράττω, διαφθείρω: of Time, διαβιόω.

__D.V
to add strength, thoroughly, out and out, διαγαληνίζω, etc.; compare ζά.

__D.VI
of mixture, between, partly, especially in adjective, as διάλευκος, διάχρυσος, διάχλωρος, etc.

__D.VII
of leaving an interval or breach, διαλείπω, διαναπαύω. (Cogn. with δύο, δίς.)

__B
as deponent verb, διαλέγομαι: future διαλέξομαι [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Isocrates Orator 12.5 and 112;]] also -λεχθήσομαι [Refs 4th c.BC+ [[prev. author] 9.34, 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 18.252]]; -λεγήσομαι [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [“Inscription Perg.” 5 (3rd c.BC)]]: aorist διελεξάμην [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Homerus Epicus, 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Fragmenta” 343]]; Aeolic dialect imperative ζάλεξαι [Refs 7th c.BC+ [7th-6th c.BC: Sappho Lyrica “Papyrus fragments” in E. Diehl, 16.3; also διελέχθην 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 3.51]], and always in Attic dialect Inscrr., [Refs [“IG” 22.657, etc.]]: less frequently aorist 2 διελέγην [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Topica” 154a34, 159a5, 2nd c.BC: Scymnus Geographus 7, “IG” 5(1).5.5 (_Laconian dialect_), “GDI” 5163a2 (from Crete), “PPetr.” 3p.130 (3rd c.BC), “IG” 22.1236]]; 3rd.pers. plural διέλεγεν [Refs [“CIG” “Corpus Inscriptionum Graecarum” “Corpus Inscriptionum Graecarum” 3656.7 (Cyzic.)]]: perfect διείλεγμαι [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Theaetetus” 158c, 5th-6th c.BC: Isocrates Orator 5.81]]: pluperfect διείλεκτο [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 21.119]], but in passive sense, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Lysias Orator 9.5]]:—hold converse with, with dative person, μοι ταῦτα φίλος διελέξατο θυμός [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 11.407, compare 7th c.BC: Archilochus Lyricus 80, 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 3.50, 51, 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Nubes” 425, etc.; πρὸς ἀλλήλους 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Politicus” 272c, etc.]]; δ. τί τινι or πρός τινα, discuss a question with another, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Memorabilia” 2.10.1, 1.6.1]]; δ. ὅρους talk in definitions, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Analytica Posteriora” 92b32; δ. περί τινος 5th-6th c.BC: Isocrates Orator 3.8, 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 18.252; ἀνὴρ ἀνδρὶ δ. 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 8.93]]; δ. τινὶ μὴ ποιεῖν argue with one against doing, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [[prev. author] 5.59; εἰ τουτὶ τὸ ῥῆμα, ἀλλὰ μὴ τουτὶ διελέχθην ἐγώ 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 18.232]]; οἱ νόμοι οὐδὲν τούτῳ δ. have nothing to say to him, concern him not, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [[prev. author] 43.59; ὁ νομοθέτης οὔπω τινὶ δ. 4th c.BC: Aeschines Orator 1.17; δ. πρός τι]]to argue on.., [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Topica” 159a7]]; or against.., [Refs [[prev. author] “Ph.” 185a6]]: absolutely, to discourse, reason, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Memorabilia” 4.5.12; __2
intermit, τὴν ὀχείαν [Refs [[prev. author] “GA” 757b4: especially of Time, διαλιπὼν ἡμέρας τὰς συγκειμένας, ἐνιαυτόν,]] having left an interval of.., [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 3.157, 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 20.8]]; ἀκαρῆ διαλιπών having waited an instant, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Nubes” 496; χρόνον ὀλίγον 5th-6th c.BC: Isocrates Orator 5.8; πολὺν χρόνον 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Politica” 1299a37]]; later in genitive, μιᾶς ἡμέρας δ. with participle, mostly with negative, οὐ πώποτε διέλειπον ζητῶν [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Apologia Socratis” 16, etc.]]; οὐδένα διαλέλοιπα χρόνον διαβαλλόμενος I have never ceased to be slandered, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Isocrates Orator 12.5; οὐ διέλιπον.. παραινῶν πείθεσθαι.. “BGU” 747i 7 (2nd c.AD),compare “POxy.” 281.16 (1st c.AD)]]: without a negative, [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd c.AD: Lucianus Sophista “Vit.Auct.” 13, “DMeretr.” 11.1.]]

__II.3
of Time, διαλιπόντων ἐτῶν τριῶν, διαλιπούσης ἡμέρας, after an interval of.., [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 1.112, 3.74; τὸ διαλεῖπον]]the interval of time, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Physica” 228b4.]]

διαλλ-άσσω,

__II.1

__2

__3

Stud.” 908.2]]; to be tossed about, uncertain in [NT+1st c.BC+ [1st c.BC-1st c.AD: Strabo Geographus 3.2.5; δ. ἐν τῷ Ἀδρίᾳ NT.Act.27.27, compare 1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus “Galba” 26.]]

__II.2

[Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd c.AD: Lucianus Sophista “Alex.” 15: with _Article_, τρεῖς μόναι ψῆφοι διήνεγκαν τὸ μὴ θανάτου τιμῆσαι]] three votes made the difference (i.e. majority) against capital punishment, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 23.167]]; also διαφέρει τὸ ἥμισυ τοῦ ἔργου makes a difference equal to half the effort expended, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Oeconomicus” 20.17.]]

__III.2
impersonal, διαφέρει it makes a difference, πλεῖστον δ. [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Hippocrates Medicus “ἀφορισμοί” 5.22; βραχὺ δ. τοῖς θανοῦσιν εἰ.. 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Troades” 1248, etc.]]; οὐδὲν δ. it makes no odds, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Phaedo” 89c, compare 4th-3rd c.BC: Menander Comicus “Ἐπιτρέποντες” 193; σμικρὸν οἴει διαφέρει; 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 467c: with _dative_ _person_, δ. μοι]] it makes a difference to me, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Antipho Orator 5.13, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Protagoras” 316b, etc.]]; ἰδίᾳ τι αὐτῷ δ. he has some private interest at stake, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 3.42]]; εἰ ὑμῖν μή τι δ. if you see no objection, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Laches” 187d; τί δέ σοι τοῦτο δ. εἴτε.. εἴτε μ; [prev. author] “R.” 349a, compare “Grg.” 497b, etc.]]: with infinitive, οὐδέ τί οἱ διέφερεν ἀποθανεῖν [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.85]]: with personal construction, πράγματά τινι διαφέροντα [Refs 1st c.AD+ [1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus “Caesar” 65]]; to be of importance, πρός or εἴς τι, [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd c.AD: Galenus Medicus 15.420,428; τῷ ζῴῳ [prev. author] “UP” 9.5.]]

Prose phrases, δ. ὅρκον, opposed to λαμβάνειν, tender an oath, δοκεῖ κἂν ὀμόσαι εἴ τις αὐτῷ ὅρκον διδοίη [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Isaeus Orator 9.24, compare 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 39.3, 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Rhetorica” 1377a8]]; δ. ψῆφον, γνώμην, put a proposal to the vote, propose a resolution, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 21.87, 24.13: δ. χάριν, ={χαρίζεσθαι}, 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Ajax” 1354, 5th c.BC: Cratinus Comicus 317]]; ὀργῇ χάριν δούς having indulged.., [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Coloneus” 855]]; λόγον τινὶ δ. give one leave to speak, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Historia Graeca (Hellenica)” 5.2.20; δ. λόγον σφίσι]]deliberate, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.97; οὐκ, εἰ διδοίης.. σαυτῷ λόγον 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Tyrannus” 583]]; δοῦναι, λαβεῖν λόγον, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Sophistici Elenchi” 165a27 (but δ. λόγον, εὐθύνας,]] render accounts, [Refs [“IG” 12.91, +others): δ. δίκην or δίκας, see at {δίκη}: ἀκοὴν δ. λόγοις]] lend an ear to.., [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Electra” 30, etc.]]; δ. ἐργασίαν give diligence, = Latin dare operam, [Refs 1st c.BC+ [“OGI” 441.109 (Lagina, 1st c.BC), “POxy.” 742.11]]: with infinitive, [NT.Luke.12.58: _absolutely_, i.e. πληγήν, λίθῳ δ. τινί “PLips.” 13 iii 3]; ἐμβολὰς διδόναι, ram, of ships, [Refs 1st c.BC+ [1st c.BC: Diodorus Siculus Historicus 13.10.]]

__II
with accusative person, hand over, deliver up, ἀχέεσσί με δώσεις [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 19.167; μιν.. ὀδύνῃσιν ἔδωκεν 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 5.397; Ἕκτορα κυσίν 23.21; πυρί τινα 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 24.65; πληγαῖς τινά 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 574c; ἔδωκε θῆρας φόβῳ 5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “P.” 5.60.]]

__II.2
of parents, give their daughter to wife, θυγατέρα ἀνδρί [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 6.192, 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 4.7]]; also of Telemachus, ἀνέρι μητέρα δώσω [Refs [2.223]]; τὴν.. Σάμηνδε ἔδοσαν gave her in marriage to go to Samé, [Refs [15.367, compare 17.442]]; with infinitive added, δώσω σοι Χαρίτων μίαν ὀπυιέμεναι [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 14.268: in Prose and Trag., θυγατέρα δ. τινὶ γυναῖκα 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.107, compare 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 6.59, 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Historia Graeca (Hellenica)” 4.1.4, etc.: _absolutely_, ἐδίδοσαν καὶ ἤγοντο ἐξ ἀλλήλων 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 5.92.β,compare 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Medea” 288; also δ. κόρᾳ ἄνδρα 5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “P.” 9.117.]]

__II.3
διδόναι τινά τινι grant another to one's entreaties, pardon him at one's request, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 6.6.31]]; διδόναι τινί τι forgive one a thing, condone it, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Cyclops” 296 (assuming variant).]]

__II.4
δ. ἑαυτόν τινι give oneself up, δ. σφέας αὐτοὺς τοῖσι Ἀθηναίοισι [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 6.108, compare 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Philoctetes” 84, 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 2.68; τινὶ εἰς χεῖρας 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Electra” 1348; δ. ἑαυτὸν τοῖς δεινοῖς 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 18.97; εἰς τοὺς κινδύνους 2nd c.BC: Polybius Historicus 3.17.8; εἰς ἔντευξιν [prev. author] 3.15.4]]; εἰς τρυφήν, εἰς λῃστείας, [Refs 1st c.BC+ [1st c.BC: Diodorus Siculus Historicus 17.108, 18.47]]: with infinitive, δίδωσ᾽ ἑκὼν κτείνειν ἑαυτόν [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Philoctetes” 1341.]]

__II.5
appoint, establish, of a priest, [LXX.Exo.31.6]; δῶμεν ἀρχηγόν[LXX.Num.14.4]; δ. τινὰ εἰς ἔθνος μέγα[LXX.Gen.17.20]; place, τινὰ ὑπεράνω πάντα τὰ ἔθνη[LXX.Deu.28.1:—]passive, οἱ δεδομένοι, = Nethinim, ministers of the Temple,[LXX.Neh.5.3]; ἐδόθη αὐτοῖς ἵνα.. orders were given them that.., [NT.Rev.9.5.]

__III
in vows and prayers, with accusative person et infinitive, grant, allow, bring about that.., especially in prayers, δὸς ἀποφθίμενον δῦναι δόμον Ἄϊδος εἴσω grant that he may go.., [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 3.322; τὸν κασίγνητον δότε τυίδ᾽ ἴκεσθαι 7th-6th c.BC: Sappho Lyrica “Papyrus fragments” in E. Diehl, 1.2]]; δός με τείσασθαι give me to.., [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Choephori” 18, compare “Eu.” 31; also with _dative_ _person_, τούτῳ.. εὐτυχεῖν δοῖεν θεοί [prev. author] “Th.” 422; θεοὶ δοῖέν ποτ᾽ αὐτοῖς.. παθεῖν 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Philoctetes” 316, compare “OC” 1101, 1287, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Leges” 737b.]]

__III.2
grant, concede in argument, δ. καὶ συγχωρεῖν [Refs 4th c.BC+ [[prev. author] “Phd.” 100b, compare 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Metaphysica” 990a12, +others]]: with infinitive, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [[prev. author] “Ph.” 239b29; δ. εἶναι θεούς 4th c.AD: Iamblichus Philosophus “de Mysteriis” 1.3; ἑνὸς ἀτόπου δοθέντος τἆλλα συμβαίνει 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Physica” 186a9]]; δεδομένα, τά, data, title of work by Euclid; ἡ δοθεῖσα γραμμή, γωνία, etc., [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Meno” 87a, 3rd c.BC: Euclides Geometra 1.9, etc.; δεδόσθω κύκλος 3rd c.BC: Archimedes Geometra “περὶ σφαίρας καὶ κυλίνδρου” 1.6, +others]]; also in Alchemy, δός take certain substances, [Refs [“Pleid.X.” 69.]]

__IV
Grammars, describe, record, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [Scholia 5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “P.” 5.93, Scholia 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 16.207.]]

__V
seemingly intransitive, give oneself up, devote oneself, with dative, especially ἡδονῇ [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Phoenissae” 21, 1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus “Publicola” 13; ἡδοναῖς 2nd-3rd c.AD: Philostratus Sophista “Vitae Sophistarum” 1.12; ἐλπίδι 1st c.AD: Josephus Historicus “Antiquitates Judaicae” 17.12.2; εἰς δημοκοπίαν 1st c.BC: Diodorus Siculus Historicus 25.8; δρόμῳ δοὺς φέρεσθαι]]at full speed, [Refs 4th c.AD+ [4th c.AD: Alciphro Epistolographus 3.47.]]

Eph.4:24; ἀγαθωσύνῃ καὶ δ., Eph.5:9; δ. κ. εἰρήνη κ. χαρά, Rom.14:17; δ. κ. ἁγιασμός, 1Co.1:30; opposite to ἁμαρτία, Rom.8:10; ἀνομία, 2Co.6:14; άδικία, Rom.3:5; ποιεῖν τὴν δ., 1Jn.2:29 Jn 3:7; id. as an inclusive term for the active duties of the religious life (ICC, in l; Abbott, Essays, 73 ff), Mat.6:1; ἐργάζεσθαι δ., Act.10:35; διώκειν δ., 1Ti.6:11; πληροῦν πᾶσαν δ., Mat.3:15; ζῆν τῇ δ., 1Pe.2:24; δ. θεοῦ, a righteousness divine in its character and origin, Mat.6:33, Jas.1:20, (where it also includes the idea of God's personal r.; see ICC, on Rom.1:17) Rom.1:17 3:5, 21-26 10:3, 2Co.5:21, Php.3:9; ἡ δ. τ. πίσιεως, Rom.4:11; ἡ ἐκ π. δ., Rom.9:30; ἡ κατὰ π. δ., Heb.11:7; opposite to this is ἡ ἐκ νόμου δ., Rom.10:5; ἡ δ. ἐν ν., Php.3:6; ἡ ἰδία δ., Rom.10:3, cf. [Refs 8th c.BC+ [9.175, compare 8.575; [Γαλακτοφάγοι] δικαιότατοι 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 13.6; [Χείρων] δικαιότατος Κενταύρων 11.832, compare 6th c.BC: Theognis Elegiacus 314, 794]]; δ. πολίτης a good citizen, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 3.21, etc.]]: metaphorically of the sea, [Refs 6th c.BC+ [6th c.BC: Solon Lyricus 12.2 (_superlative_)]]; δικαίη ζόη a civilized way of living, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 2.177.]] adverb δικαίως, μνᾶσθαι woo in due form, decently, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 14.90; ὑπὸ ζυγῷ λόφον δ. εἶχον]]loyally, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Antigone” 292.]]

__A.2
observant of duty to gods and men, righteous, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 13.209, etc.; δ. πρὸς πᾶσαν ὁμιλίην 5th c.BC: Hippocrates Medicus “περὶ ἰητροῦ” 2; ἰθὺς καὶ δ. 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.96]]; opposed to δυσσεβής, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Septem contra Thebas” 598, compare 610; δ. καὶ ὅσιος 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Gorgias” 507b; δικαίων ἀδίκους φρένας παρασπᾷς 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Antigone” 791 (Lyric poetry)]]; also of actions, etc., righteous, ἐπὶ ῥηθέντι δικαίῳ a thing rightly said, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 18.414, etc.]]

__A.3
ὁ δίκαιος, euphemistic of a sacred snake, [Refs [“GDI” 5056 (from Crete).]]

__B
later:

__B.I
equal, even, well-balanced, ἅρμα δίκαιον evengoing chariot, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 2.2.26: so _metaphorically_, νωμᾷ δικαίῳ πηδαλίῳ στρατόν 5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “P.” 1.86; δικαιόταται ἀντιρροπαί 5th c.BC: Hippocrates Medicus “περὶ ἄρθρων ἐμβολῆς” 7]]; δικαιότατα μοχλεύειν [Refs [[prev. passage]: hence,]]fair, impartial, βάσανος [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Antipho Orator 1.8; συγγραφεύς 2nd c.AD: Lucianus Sophista “Hist.Conscr.” 39.]]

__B.I.b
legally exact, precise, τῷ δικαιοτάτῳ τῶν λόγων to speak quite exactly, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 7.108, compare 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 3.44]]; of Numbers, αἱ ἑκατὸν ὀργυιαὶ δίκαιαι [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 2.149]]. adverb -αίως, πάντα δ. ὑμῖν τετήρηται [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 21.3; δ. ἐξετάζειν [prev. work]154.]]

__B.I.2
lawful, just, especially τὸ δ. right, opposed to τὸ ἄδικον, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.96, 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Prometheus Vinctus” 189 (Lyric poetry), etc.; τὸ δ. τὸ νόμιμον καὶ τὸ ἴσον 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Ethica Nicomachea” 1129a34; δ. διορθωτικόν, διανεμητικόν, [prev. work] 1131b25, 27]]; τὸ πολιτικὸν δ.[Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. work] 1134b18; ἔστι ἐπιεικὲς τὸ παρὰ τὸν γεγραμμένον νόμον δ. [prev. author] “Rh.” 1374a27, compare “EN” 1137b12; καὶ δίκαια κἄδικα 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Nubes” 99; τὰ ἴσα καὶ τὰ δ. 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 21.67]]; τοὐμὸν δ. my own right, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Iphigenia Aulidensis” 810]]; ἐλθεῖν ἐπὶ τοῦτο τὸ δ. bring the case to this issue, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Antipho Orator 6.24]]; οὐδὲν τῶν δ. ποιεῖν τινί not to do what is just and right by a man, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Historia Graeca (Hellenica)” 5.3.10]]; τὰ δ. ἔχειν, λαμβάνειν, receive one's due, [Refs [[prev. author] “An.” 7.7.14, 17]]; τὰ δ. πράττεσθαι πόλιν give a city its deserts, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Agamemnon” 812]]; ἐκ τοῦ δικαίου, ={δικαίως}, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Aves” 1435, compare 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 2.89]]; so ἀπὸ τοῦ δικαίου, τῶν δικαίων, [Refs 2nd c.BC+ [“Inscription Prien.” 50.8 (2nd c.BC), 123.8 (1st c.BC)]]; μετὰ τοῦ δ. [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Lysias Orator 2.12, 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 21.177]]; τὸ δίκαιον lawful claim, ἃ ἔχομεν δίκαια πρός.. [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 3.54, compare 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 21.179, 1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus “Lucullus” 3, etc.]]; τὰ πρὸς ἀλλήλους δ. mutual obligations or contracts, [Refs 2nd c.BC+ [2nd c.BC: Polybius Historicus 3.21.10]]; ἐπὶ συγκειμένοις τισὶ δικαίοις on certain agreed terms, [Refs 1st c.BC+ [1st c.BC: Dionysius Halicarnassensis 3.51]]. adverb -αίως rightly, justly, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 6.137; μεῖζον ἢ δ. 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Agamemnon” 376 (Lyric poetry); καὶ δ. καὶ ἀδίκως 5th-6th c.BC: Andocides Orator 1.135.]]

__B.II
of persons and things, meet and right, fitting, δ. τοῦδε τοῦ φόνου ῥαφεύς [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Agamemnon” 1604; κόσμος οὐ φέρειν δ. [prev. author] “Eu.” 55]]; ἵππον δ. ποιεῖσθαί τινι make a horse fit for another's use, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Memorabilia” 4.4.5, compare “Cyn.” 7.4 (ἵππος δ. τὴν σιαγόνα]] having a good mouth, [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd c.AD(?): Pollianus Epigrammaticus 1.196).]]

__B.II.b
normal, σχήματα [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Hippocrates Medicus “περὶ ἄρθρων ἐμβολῆς” 69; φύσις [prev. author] “Fract.” 1 (_superlative_).]]

__B.II.2
real, genuine, γόνος [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Fragmenta” [1119]; ποιῶν τὰ ἐν τῇ τέχνῃ δ. “Supp.epigram” 2.184.7 (Tanagra, 2nd c.BC).]] adverb, εἴπερ δικαίως ἐστ᾽ ἐμός really and truly mine, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Ajax” 547, compare 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Cratylus” 418e.]]

__B.II.3
ὁ δ. λόγος the plea of equity, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 1.76]]. adverb -αίως with reason, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. author] 6.34, compare 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Tyrannus” 675]]: comparative -ότερον[Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Vespae” 1149, etc.;]] also -οτέρως [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Isocrates Orator 15.170]]: superlative -ότατα[Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Aves” 1222]]; Aeolic dialect δικαίτατα [Refs [“IG” 12(2).526c17 (from Eresus).]]

__B.III
ψυχὴ ἐς τὸ δ. ἔβη 'the land of the leal', [Refs [“IG” 7.2543.3 (from Thebes).]]

__C
in Prose, δίκαιός εἰμι, with infinitive, δίκαιοί ἐστε ἰέναι you are bound to come, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 9.60, compare 8.137; δ. εἰμεν ἔχειν [prev. author] 9.27]]; δ. εἰμι κολάζειν I have a right to punish, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Nubes” 1434, compare 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Antigone” 400; δ. ἐστι περιπεσεῖν κακοῖς 5th c.BC: Antipho Orator 3.3.7]]; δ. εἰσι ἀπιστότατοι εἶναι they have most reason to distrust, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 4.17; δ. βλάπτεσθαι 5th c.BC: Lysias Orator 20.12; δ. ἐστιν ἀπολωλέναι]]dignus est qui pereat, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 6.37]]; ὁ σπουδαῖος ἄρχειν δ. has a right to.., [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Politica” 1287b12]]; with a non-personal subject, ἔλεος δ. ἀντιδίδοσθαι [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 3.40]]: less frequently in comparative and superlative, δικαιότεροι χαρίσασθαι [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Lysias Orator 20.34; δικαιότατος εἶ ἀπαγγέλλειν 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Symposium” 172b]]; but δίκαιόν ἐστι is also found, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.39, 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Prometheus Vinctus” 611, etc.: _plural_, δίκαια γὰρ τόνδ᾽ εὐτυχεῖν 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Ajax” 1126, compare “Tr.” 495, 1116]]; δικαίως ἄν, with optative, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Phaedrus” 276a. [δικαίων]] with penultimate short in [Refs 5th c.AD+ [5th-6th c.AD: Orphica “Fragmenta” 247.2]]; compare οὐ δίκαον· οὐ δίκαιον, [Refs 5th c.AD+ [5th c.AD(?): Hesychius Legal icographus]]]

setting right, doing justice to: hence,

(δικάζω), [in LXX for שָׁפַט ;]

SYN.: κριτής, WH. "gives prominence to the mental process" (Thayer). δ. is the forensic term. In Attic law, the δικασταί were jurors, with a κριτής as presiding officer (LS, see word; Enc. Brit. 11, xii, 504 f.)  (AS)

deep_entry:
Abbott-Smith / STEPBible (TBESG)
δίκη, -ης, ἡ
[in LXX for נָקָם, רִיב, etc. ;]
__1. custom.
__2. right.
__3. a judicial hearing; hence its result, the execution of a sentence, punishment: δ. τίνειν, 2Th.1:9; δ. υπεχειν, Ju 7.
__4. Personified (cf. Lat. Justitia), justice, vengeance: Act.28:4.†
(AS)

---

LSJ / STEPBible (TFLSJ)
δίκη [ῐ], ἡ,
custom, usage, αὕτη δ. ἐστὶ βροτῶν this is the way of mortals, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 11.218; ἡ γὰρ δ. ἐστὶ γερόντων 24.255, etc.; ἥ τ᾽ ἐστὶ δ. θείων βασιλήων 4.691; ἡ γὰρ δμώων δ. ἐστίν 14.59, etc.]]; ἡ γὰρ δ., ὁππότε.. this is always the way, when.., [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [19.168 (so in late Prose, ἥπερ ἱππομαχίας δ. 2nd c.AD: Arrianus Historicus “Anabasis” 3.15.2)]]; δίκαν ἐφέπειν τινός to imitate him, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “P.” 1.50]]; δ. ἐπέχειν τινός to be like.., [Refs 1st c.AD+ [1st c.AD: Anonymus Londinensis 6.18]]; normal course of nature, ἐκ τουτέων ὁ θάνατος οὐ γίνεται κατά γε δίκην, οὐδ᾽ ἢν γένηται [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Hippocrates Medicus “περὶ τῶν ἐν κεφαλη—ͅ τρωμάτων” 3: hence,]]

__2
adverbial in accusative δίκην, in the way of, after the manner of, with genitive, λύκοιο [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “P.” 2.84; πώλου 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Fragmenta” 659; τοξότου 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Leges” 705e]]; in later Prose, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “de Mundo” 395b22, 2nd c.AD: Lucianus Sophista “Dem.Enc.” 31, 4th c.AD: Alciphro Epistolographus 1.6, etc.: mostly of living creatures or persons, but also of things, as δίκην ὕδατος, ἀγγείου, 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Septem contra Thebas” 85 (Lyric poetry), 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Phaedrus” 235d.]]

__II
order, right, μή τι δίκης ἐπιδευές nothing short of what is fit, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 19.180; opposed to βία, might, 16.388]]; opposed to σχέτλια ἔργα, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 14.84; personified, 8th-7th c.BC: Hesiodus Epicus “Theogonia” 902, 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Septem contra Thebas” 662, etc.; Δίκης βωμός [prev. author] “Ag.” 383 (Lyric poetry), “Eu.” 539 (Lyric poetry)]]; Truth, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “P.” 8.71.]]

__II.2
δίκη ἐστί, ={δίκαιόν ἐστι}, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Agamemnon” 259, compare 811, “Eu.” 277.]]

__II.3
Adverb. usages, δίκῃ duly, rightly, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 23.542, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Critias” 112e; ἐν δίκᾳ 5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “O.” 6.12, compare 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Trachiniae” 1069, etc.; σὺν δίκῃ 6th c.BC: Theognis Elegiacus 197, 5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “P.” 9.96, 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Septem contra Thebas” 444, etc.; κατὰ δίκην 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 7.35, 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Troades” 888, etc.; μετὰ δίκης 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Leges” 643e; πρὸς δίκης 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Tyrannus” 1014, “El.” 1211 (but πρὸς δίκας]] on the score of justice, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. author] “OC” 546 (Lyric poetry)); διαὶ δίκας 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Choephori” 641; ἐκ δίκης 3rd c.BC: Herodas Mimographus 4.77: opposed to παρὰ δίκαν 5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “O.” 2.18, etc.; ἄνευ δίκης 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Eumenides” 554; πέρα δίκης [prev. author] “Pr.” 30; βίᾳ δίκης [prev. author] “Supp.” 430 (Lyric poetry)]]; δίχα δίκης without trial, [Refs 1st c.AD+ [1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus “Agesilaus” 32]]; πρὸ δίκης in preference to legal proceedings, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 1.141.]]

__III
judgement, δίκην ἰθύντατα εἰπεῖν give judgement most righteously (compare ἰθύς), [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 18.508: especially in _plural_, Λυκίην εἴρυτο δίκῃσί τε καὶ σθένεϊ ᾧ 16.542; περὶ οἶδε δίκας 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 3.244, etc.; δίκαι σκολιαί 8th-7th c.BC: Hesiodus Epicus “Opera et Dies” 219, 250; κρῖνε εὐθεῖαν δίκην 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Eumenides” 433.]]

__IV
after [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Homerus Epicus]], of proceedings instituted to determine legal rights, hence,

__IV.1
lawsuit, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Euthyphro” 2a, 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 18.210, etc.]]; properly private suit or action, opposed to γραφή (which see), [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Lysias Orator 1.44, etc.; ἐκαλοῦντο αἱ γραφαὶ δίκαι, οὐ μέντοι αἱ δίκαι καὶ γραφαί 2nd c.AD(?): Pollianus Epigrammaticus 8.41]]; οἱ δίκην ἔχοντες the parties to a suit, [Refs 1st c.AD+ [Inscriptiones Graecae 7.21.8 (from Megara), compare 1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus “Cicero” 17.]]

__IV.2
trial of the case, πρὸ δίκης [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Isaeus Orator 5.10, etc.; μέχρι τοῦ δίκην γενέσθαι 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 2.53]]; court by which it was tried, ἐν ὑμῖν ἐστι καὶ τῇ δίκῃ [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Antipho Orator 6.6.]]

__IV.2.b
δίκην εἰπεῖν to plead a cause, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Memorabilia” 4.8.1; δ. μακρὰν λέγειν 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Vespae” 776, compare 4th-3rd c.BC: Menander Comicus “Ἐπιτρέποντες” 12.]]

__IV.3
the object or consequence of the action, atonement, satisfaction, penalty, δίκην ἐκτίνειν, τίνειν, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 9.94, 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Ajax” 113]]: adverbially in accusative, τοῦ δίκην πάσχεις τάδ; [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Prometheus Vinctus” 614]]; frequently δίκην or δίκας διδόναι suffer punishment, i. e. make amends (but δίκας δ., in [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Supplices” 703 (Lyric poetry)]], to grant arbitration); δίκας διδόναι τινί τινος [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.2, compare 5.106; ἔμελλε τῶνδέ μοι δώσειν δίκην 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Electra” 538, etc.]]; also ἀντί or ὑπέρ τινος, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Plutus” 433, 5th c.BC: Lysias Orator 3.42]]; also δίκην διδόναι ὑπὸ θεῶν to be punished by.., [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Gorgias” 525b]]; but δίκας ἤθελον δοῦναι they consented to submit to trial, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 1.28]]; δίκας λαμβάνειν sometimes ={δ. διδόναι}, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.115; δίκην ἀξίαν ἐλάμβανες 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Bacchae” 1312, “Heracl.” 852]]; more frequently its correlative, inflict punishment, take vengeance, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Lysias Orator 1.29, etc.; λαβεῖν δίκην παρά τινος 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 21.92, compare 9.2, etc.]]; so δίκην ἔχειν to have one's punishment, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Antipho Orator 3.4.9, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 529c (but ἔχω τὴν δ.]] have satisfaction, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. author] “Ep.” 319e; δοκέω, -ῶ
(δόκος, opinion, δέκομαι, Ion, form of δέχ-), [in LXX for טוֹב, נָדַב, etc. ;]
__1. to be of opinion, suppose: Mat.24:44, Luk.12:40, Heb.10:29; with inf., Mat.3:9, Luk.8:18 24:37, Jhn.5:39 16:2, Act.12:9 27:13, 1Co.3:18 7:40 8:2 10:12 14:37, Gal.6:3, Php.3:4, Jas.1:26; with accusative and inf., 1Co.12:23, 2Co.11:16; before ὅτι, Mat.6:7 26:53, Mrk.6:49, Luk.12:51 13:2, 4 19:11, Jhn.5:45 11:13, 31 13:29 20:15, 1Co.4:9, 2Co.12:19, Jas.4:5.
__2. to seem, be reputed: Act.25:27; with inf., Mrk.10:42, Luk.10:36 22:24, Act.17:13 26:9, 1Co.11:16 12:22, 2Co.10:9, Gal.2:6, 9, Heb.4:1 12:11; οἱ δοκοῦντες, those of repute, Gal.2:2. Impers., it seems, with dative of person(s);
__(a) to think: Mat.17:25 18:12 21:28 22:17, 42 26:66, Jhn.11:56, Heb.12:10;
__(b) to please, seem good to: with inf., Luk.1:3, Act.15:22, 25 15:23, 34.†
SYN. (δοκέω 1): ἡγέομαι 2, νομίζω2, οἴομαι; ἡ. and ν. properly express belief resting on external proof, ἡ. denoting the more careful judgment; δ. and οἴ. imply a subjective judgment which in the case of οἴ. is based on feeling, in δ. on thought (see Schmidt, with 17) (δοκέω2): φαίνομαι; φ., from the standpoint of the object, "expresses how a matter phenomenally shows and presents itself"; δ., from the standpoint of the observer, expresses one's subjective judgment about a matter (see Tr., Syn., LXXx; Cremer, 204). (AS)

seem, pretend, with infinitive (with or without negative), ὁρέων μὲν οὐδέν, δοκέων δὲ [ὁρᾶν] uncertain reading in [Refs 7th c.BC+ [7th c.BC: Alcman Lyricus 87; οὔτε ἔδοξε μαθέειν 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.10; οὐδὲ γιγνώσκειν δοκῶν 5th c.BC: Pherecrates Comicus 163; τὰ μὲν ποιεῖν, τὰ δὲ δοκεῖν 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Politica” 1314a39; ἤκουσά του λέγοντος, οὐ δοκῶν κλύειν 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Medea” 67; πόσους δοκεῖς.. ὁρῶντας.. μὴ δοκεῖν ὁρᾶ; [prev. author] “Hipp.” 462, compare 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Equites” 1146, 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Historia Graeca (Hellenica)” 4.5.6.]]

__I.5
passive, to be considered, δοκεῖσθαι οὕτω [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 612d]]; τὰ νῦν δοκούμενα περί τινος the current opinions, [Refs [[prev. work] 490a.]]

__I.6
middle, [Refs 3rd c.AD+ [3rd c.AD: Oppianus Apamensis Epicus “Cynegetica” 4.296; δοκεύμενος.. ἀλύξειν [prev. work] 109.]]

__II
of an Object, seem, with dative person et infinitive present, δοκέεις δέ μοι οὐκ ἀπινύσσειν [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 5.342]]; δόκησε δ᾽ ἄρα σφίσι θυμὸς ὣς ἔμεν ὡς εἰ.. their heart seemed just as if.., felt as though.., [Refs [10.415: with]]infinitive future, seem likely, δοκέει δέ μοι ὧδε λώϊον ἔσσεσθαι [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 6.338]]: with infinitive aorist (never in [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Homerus Epicus), τί δ᾽ ἂν δοκεῖ σοι Πρίαμος (i.e. ποιῆσαι); 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Agamemnon” 935]]; seem or be thought to have done, especially of suspected persons, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 2.21]]; to be convicted, ἂν ἁλῷ καὶ δοκῇ τοὔργον εἰργάσθαι [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 23.71.]]

__II.2
absolutely, seem, as opposed to to reality, τὸ δοκεῖν καὶ τὰν ἀλάθειαν βιᾶται [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Simonides Lyricus 76; οὐ δοκεῖν ἄριστος ἀλλ᾽ εἶναι θέλει 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Septem contra Thebas” 592, compare 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Gorgias” 527b; in full, τὸ δοκεῖν εἶναι 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Agamemnon” 788 (_anapaest meter_).]]

__II.3
seem good, be resolved on, εἰ δοκεῖ σοι ταῦτα[Refs [[prev. work] 944; τοιαῦτ᾽ ἔδοξε τῷδε Καδμείων τέλει [prev. author] “Th.” 1030.]]

__II.4
frequently impersonal, δοκεῖ μοι it seems to me, methinks, ὥς μοι δοκεῖ εἶναι ἄριστα [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 12.215]]; ὡς ἐμοὶ δοκεῖ as I think, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Septem contra Thebas” 369, etc.]]; τὸ σοὶ δοκοῦν your opinion, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 487d: frequently in]]infinitive in parenthesis clause, ὡς ἐμοὶ δοκέειν to my thinking, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 9.113; δοκέειν ἐμοί [prev. author] 1.172; ἀλλ᾽, ἐμοὶ δοκεῖν, τάχ᾽ εἴσει 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Persae” 246, etc.]]; without μοι, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 4.5.1.]]

it seems good to me, it is my pleasure, δοκεῖ ἡμῖν χρῆσθαι [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 4.118, compare 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Agamemnon” 1350]]: frequently of a public resolution, τοῖσι Ἕλλησι δόξαι.. ἀπαιτέειν [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.3, etc.; ἔδοξεν Ἀργείοισιν 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Supplices” 605, compare “Th.” 1010]]; especially in decrees and the like, ἔδοξε τῇ βουλῇ, τῷ δήμῳ, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Thesmophoriazusae” 372, 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 4.118, compare “IG” 1.32, etc.; τὰ δόξαντα 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Electra” 29, 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 3.14; παρὰ τὸ δοκοῦν ἡμῖν 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 1.84, etc.]]:—passive, δέδοκται [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 4.68; οὕτω δέδοκτα; 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Philoctetes” 1277, etc.; εἰ ἐπαινῆσαι δεδόκηται 5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “N.” 5.19; δεδόχθω τὸ ἄτοπον τοῦτο 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Leges” 799e, etc.; τοῦτ᾽ ἐστ᾽ ἐμοὶ δεδογμένον 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Heraclidae” 1; δεδογμέν᾽ [ἐστί].. τήνδε κατθανεῖν 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Antigone” 576, compare “OC” 1431; τὰ δεδογμένα 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 3.76; δεδόχθαι τῇ βουλῇ καὶ τῷ δήμῳ “IG” 22.1.12, etc. with _accusative_ _absolutely_, δόξαν]] when it was decreed or resolved, δόξαν αὐτοῖς ὥστε διαναυμαχεῖν [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 8.79]]; δόξαν δέ σφι (i.e. λιπέσθαι) [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 2.148; δόξαν ἡμῖν ταῦτα 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Protagoras” 314c, compare 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 4.1.13]]; ἰδίᾳ δοκῆσάν σοι τόδ᾽..; [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Supplices” 129; also δεδογμένον αὐτοῖς 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 1.125, etc.; but also δόξαντος τούτου 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Historia Graeca (Hellenica)” 1.1.36; δόξαντα ταῦτα καὶ περανθέντα [prev. work] 3.2.19.]]

__II.5
to be reputed, with infinitive, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “O.” 13.56, “P.” 6.40; ἄξιοι ὑμῖν δοκοῦντες 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 1.76]]; δοκοῦντες εἶναί τι men who are held to be something, men of repute, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Gorgias” 472a; τὸ δοκεῖν τινὲς εἶναι.. προσειληφότες 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 21.213; τὸ φρονεῖν ἐδόκει τις εἶναι περιττός 1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus “Aristides” 1; οἱ δοκοῦντες 1st c.AD(?): Heraclitus 28 (uncertain), 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Hecuba” 295]]; τὰ δοκοῦντα, opposed to τὰ μηδὲν ὄντα, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. author] “Tr.” 613; μετ᾽ ἀρετῆς δοκούσης ἐς ἀλλήλους γίγνεσθαι 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 3.10]]; to be an established, current opinion, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Analytica Posteriora” 76b24, +others; τὰ δοκοῦντα [prev. author] “Metaphorical” 1088a16, +others:]] — passive, οἱ δεδογμένοι ἀνδροφόνοι those who have been found guilty of homicide, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 23.28; also αἱ δοκούμεναι Πέρσαις τέχναι 1st-2nd c.AD: Polemo Sophista “Callimachus” 60. (The two senses of δοκέω are sometimes contrasted, τὰ ἀεὶ δοκοῦντα.. τῷ δοκοῦντι εἶναι ἀληθῆ]] that which seems true is true to him who thinks it, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Theaetetus” 158e; τὸ δοκοῦν ἑκάστῳ τοῦτο καὶ εἶναι τῷ δοκοῦντι [prev. work] 162c.)]]

__2
of persons, δ. αὐτούς put them to the test, make trial of them, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Isocrates Orator 2.50; δ. τοὺς μηνυτάς 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 6.53; φίλους 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Memorabilia” 2.6.1, compare “PEleph.” 1.8 (4th c.BC), etc.]]; also of Apis-bulls, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 2.38.]]

__II
approve, sanction, μετὰ δεδοκιμασμένου [λόγου] μὴ ξυνέπεσθαι [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 3.38; ἐψηφίσασθε δοκιμάσαντες τοὺς νόμους, εἶτ᾽ ἀναγράψαι τούτους οἳ ἂν δοκιμασθῶσι 5th-6th c.BC: Andocides Orator 1.82; ἄρρενας ἔρωτας 1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus 2.11e; ὅπῃ ταύτῃ ἀρετὴ δοκιμάζεται 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 407c: with]]infinitive, ἐκπονεῖν ἐδοκίμαζε he approved of their working, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Memorabilia” 1.2.4; ἐπειδή.. ἐδοκιμάσθη ταῦτα καλῶς ἔχειν 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 2.35.]]

__II.2
as a political term,

__II.2.a
approve after scrutiny as fit for an office, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Lysias Orator 16.3, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Leges” 759d, 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Ἀθηναίων Πολιτεία” 45.3]]:—passive, to be approved as fit, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Lysias Orator 15.6, etc.; δοκιμασθεὶς ἀρχέτω 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Leges” 765b]]; μου δοκιμαζομένου when I was undergoing a scrutiny, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 21.111]]; δεδοκιμασμένος [ἰατρός] [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [“PFay.” 106.24 (2nd c.AD),compare “PGnom.” 201 (2nd c.AD)]]: metaphorically, ὃν ὁ Ἥφαιστος ἐδοκίμασεν [Refs 2nd c.BC+ [“OGI” 90.3 (2nd c.BC)]]; ὑπὲρ τοῦ στεφανωθῆναι δοκιμάζομαι [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 18.266.]]

__II.2.b
pass as fit to serve, ἱππεύειν δεδοκιμασμένος [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Lysias Orator 14.22, compare 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 3.3.20, “IG” 22.1126.15, 1369.]]

__II.2.c
examine and admit boys to the class of ἔφηβοι or ἔφηβοι to the rights of manhood, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Vespae” 578 (_passive_), 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Ἀθηναίων Πολιτεία” 42.2, etc.; ἕως ἐγὼ ἀνὴρ εἶναι δοκιμασθείην 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 27.5; εἰς ἄνδρας δεδοκιμασμένοι 5th-6th c.BC: Isocrates Orator 12.28.]]

__II.2.d
test an orator's right to speak [Refs [compare (δοκιμασία 4), “Anecdota Graeca - Bekker” 310.]]

__II.3
with infinitive, think fit to do, [Refs 1st c.AD+ [2nd c.AD: Lucianus Sophista “Bis Acc.” 31, 1st c.AD: Josephus Historicus “Antiquitates Judaicae” 2.7.4, etc.]]: with negative, refuse to do, [NT+1st c.AD+ [NT.Rom.1.28: _absolutely_, “BGU” 248.19 (1st c.AD), etc.]]

__3. Later also (not cl.) as in LXX (= הוֹד, Job.39:20, 1Ch.29:25; כָּבוֹד, Job.19:9, Est.5:11, al.), visible brightness, splendour, glory: of light, Act.22:11; of heavenly bodies, 1Co.15:40ff.; esp. that wh. radiates from God's presence, as manifested in the pillar of cloud and in the Holy of Holies (= כָּבוֹד, Exo.16:10 25:22 40:34, al.; and new Heb. שְׁכִינָה, 2Ma.2:8; see DB, iv, 489b), Rom.9:4, Jas.2:1 (see Hort, Mayor, in l.); hence of the manifested glory of God, Rom.1:23, Col.1:11 Eph.1:6, 12 17 3:16; of the same as communicated to man through Christ, 2Co.3:18 4:6; and of the glorious condition into which Christians shall enter hereafter, Rom.8:18, 21 9:23, 2Ti.2:10, al.

Diehl, 3.3, “GDI” 4952 A 42 (from Crete)]]: imperfect 2nd pers. singular ἐδύνω [Refs 5th c.BC+ [“hymnus ad Mercurium” 405, 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 1.6.7; later ἐδύνασο 5th c.BC: Hippocrates Medicus “ἐπιστολαί” 16 (variant{ἠδ}.), 2nd c.AD: Lucianus Sophista “DMort.” 9.1]]; Ionic dialect 3rd.pers. plural ἐδυνέατο [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 4.110, +others (ἠδ- codices)]]: future δυνήσομαι [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 16.238, etc.]]; Doric dialect δυνᾱσοῦμαι [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Archytas Tarentinus Philosophus 3; later δυνηθήσομαι 2nd-3rd c.AD: Dio Cassius Historicus 52.37]]: aorist ἐδυνησάμην [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 14.33]], Epic dialect δυν- [Refs [5.621]]; subjunctive δυνήσωνται [Refs 7th c.BC+ [7th-6th c.BC(?): Semonides Iambographus 1.17]], never in good Attic dialect, falsa lectio in [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 19.323:]]passive forms, Epic dialect, Ionic dialect, Lyric poetry, ἐδυνάσθην or δυνάσθην [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 23.465, +others, 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 2.19, +others, 5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “O.” 1.56, 5th c.BC: Hippocrates Medicus “περὶ ἄρθρων ἐμβολῆς” 48 (variant{δυνηθείη}), also in 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Memorabilia” 1.2.24, “An.” 7.6.20]]; Trag. and Attic dialect Prose ἐδυνήθην [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Ajax” 1067, “OT” 1212 (Lyric poetry), 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Ion” 867 (_anapaest meter_), 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 21.80,186]]: perfect δεδύνημαι [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 4.30, 4th-3rd c.BC: Dinarchus Orator 2.14, 1st c.BC: Philodemus Gadarensis Epigrammaticus “Rh.” 1.261S.]] —The double augment ἠδυνάμην is Attic dialect accusative to [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd c.AD: Moeris Grammaticus 175]], but Ionic dialect accusative to [Refs 5th c.BC+ [“Anecdota Graeca - MSS. Bibl. Oxon.” 2.374, and is found in codices of 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 4.110, +others, 5th c.BC: Hippocrates Medicus “ἐπιδημίαι” 1.26.β᾽, +others]]; ἠδύνω is required by metre in [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-3rd c.BC: Philippides Comicus 16; but is not found in _Attic dialect_ Inscrr. before 4th c.BC, “IG” 22.678.12, +others, compare ἠδύνασθε [prev. work]7.2711 (Acraeph., 1st c.AD)]]; both forms occur in later writers: ἠδυνήθην occurs in [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Prometheus Vinctus” 208, and codices of 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 4.33, 5th c.BC: Lysias Orator 3.42, etc.: δύνομαι]] is a late form frequently in Papyrus as [Refs 2nd c.BC+ [“UPZ” 9 (2nd c.BC), +others]] [ῠ, except in δῡναμένοιο [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 1.276, 11.414, 8th c.BC: Homerus Epicus “Epigrammata” 15.1, and _proper name_ Δῡναμένη, for the sake of meter]]]

__I
to be able, strong enough to do, with infinitive present et aorist, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 19.163, 1.562]], etc.: future infinitive is falsa lectio (πείσειν for πείθειν) in [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Philoctetes” 1394, (κωλύσειν for κωλῦσαι) 2nd c.BC: Polybius Historicus 21.11.13]], etc.: frequently absolutely, with infinitive supplied from the context, εἰ δύνασαί γε if at least thou canst (i.e. περισχέσθαι), [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 1.393]]: also with accusative pronoun or adjective, ὅσσον δύναμαι χερσίν τε ποσίν τε [Refs 8th c.BC+ [20.360; [Ζεὺς] δύναται ἅπαντα 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 4.237]]; μέγα δυνάμενος very powerful, mighty, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [1.276, compare 11.414; δ. μέγιστον ξείνων 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 9.9, etc.]]; μέγα δύναται, multum valet, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Eumenides” 950 (Lyric poetry); δ. Διὸς ἄγχιστα [prev. author] “Supp.” 1035]]; οἱ δυνάμενοι men of power, rank, and influence, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Orestes” 889, 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 6.39, etc.]]; οἱ δυνάμενοι, opposed to οἱ μὴ ἔχοντες, [Refs 3rd c.AD+ [3rd c.AD: Democritus Epigrammaticus 255]]; opposed to οἱ πένητες, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Archytas Tarentinus Philosophus 3]]; δυνάμενος παρά τινι having influence with him, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 7.5, 5th-6th c.BC: Andocides Orator 4.26, etc.; δύνασθαι ἐν τοῖς πρώτοις 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 4.105]]; δ. τοῖς χρήμασι, τῷ σώματι, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Lysias Orator 6.48, 24.4]]; ὁ δυνάμενος one that can maintain himself, [Refs [[prev. author] 24.12]]; of things, [διαφέρει] οἷς δύνανται differ in their potentialities, [Refs 3rd c.AD+ [3rd c.AD: Plotinus Philosophus 6.3.17.]]

__I.2
of moral possibility, to be able, dare, bear to do a thing, mostly with negative, οὔτε τελευτὴν ποιῆσαι δύναται [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 1.250; σε.. οὐ δύναμαι προλιπεῖν 13.331, compare 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Antigone” 455; οὐκέτι ἐδύνατο ἐν τῷ καθεστῶτι τρόπῳ βιοτεύειν 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 1.130; οὐδὲ σθένειν τοσοῦτον ᾠόμην τὰ σὰ κηρύγμαθ᾽ ὥστε.. θεῶν νόμιμα δύνασθαι.. ὑπερδραμεῖν 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Antigone” 455.]]

__I.2.b
enjoy a legal right, δ. τῆς γεωργίας ἀπηλλάχθαι [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [“POxy.” 899.31 (2nd-3rd c.AD), etc.]]

__I.3
with ὡς and superlative, ὡς ἐδύναντο ἀδηλότατα as secretly as they could, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 7.50]]; ὡς δύναμαι μάλιστα κατατείνας as forcibly as I possibly can, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 367b; ὡς δύναιτο κάλλιστον [prev. author] “Smp.” 214c; ὡς ἂν δύνωμαι διὰ βραχυτάτων 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 27.3, etc.]]; simply ὡς ἐδύνατο in the best way he could, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 2.6.2: with _relative_, ὅσους ἐδύνατο πλείστους ἀθροίσας [prev. author] “HG” 2.2.9; λαβεῖν.. οὓς ἂν σοφωτάτους δύνωμαι 2nd c.AD: Alexander Rhetor 213.]]

__II
to be equivalent to, λόγοι ἔργα δυνάμενοι words that are as good as deeds, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 6.40: hence,]]

__II.1
of money, to be worth, with accusative, ὁ σίγλος δύναται ἑπτὰ ὀβολούς [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 1.5.6, compare 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 34.23]]: absolutely, pass, be current, [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd c.AD: Lucianus Sophista “Luct.” 10.]]

__II.2
of Number, etc., to be equal or equivalent to, τριηκόσιαι γενεαὶ δυνέαται μύρια ἔτεα [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 2.142]]; δυνήσεται τὴν ὑποτείνουσαν will be equivalent to the hypotenuse, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “de Incessu Animalium” 709a19.]]

__II.3
of words, signify, mean, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 4.110, +others; τὸ πειρηθῆναι καὶ τὸ ποιεῖν ἴσον δύναται [prev. author] 6.86. ; δύναται ἴσον τῷ δρᾶν τὸ νοεῖν 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Fragmenta” 691; δύναται τὸ νεοδαμῶδες ἤδη ἐλεύθερον εἶναι 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 7.58: in later Greek, δύναται τὸ μνασθέντι ἀντὶ τοῦ μνασθέντος]]is equivalent to.., [Refs 5th c.BC+ [Scholia 5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “O.” 7.110.]]

__II.3.b
avail to produce, οὐδένα καιρὸν δύναται brings no advantage, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Medea” 128 (_anapaest meter_), compare 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Philebus” 23d.]]

__II.3.c
of things, mean, 'spell', τὸ τριβώνιον τί δύνατα; [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Plutus” 842]]; αἱ ἀγγελίαι τοῦτο δύνανται they mean this much, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 6.36; τὴν αὐτὴν δ. δούλωσιν [prev. author] 1.141, compare 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Politica” 1313b25.]]

__II.4
in Mathematics texts, δύνασθαί τι to be equivalent when squared to a number or area, τοῖς ἐπιπέδοις ἃ δύνανται in the areas of which they [the lines] are the roots, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Theaetetus” 148b]]; ἡ ΒΓ τῆς Α μεῖζον δύναται τῇ ΔΖ the square on ΒΓ is greater than the square on A by the square on ΔΖ, [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [3rd c.BC: Euclides Geometra 10.17]]; αἱ δυνάμεναι αὐτά [τὰ μεγέθη] the lines representing their square roots,[Refs [[prev. work] “Def.” 4, compare “Prop.” 22]]; αὐξήσεις δυνάμεναί τε καὶ δυναστευόμεναι increments both in the roots and powers of numbers, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 546b; τὴν ὑποτείνουσαν ταῖς περὶ τὴν ὀρθὴν ἴσον δυναμένην 1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus 2.720a, compare 4th c.AD: Iamblichus Philosophus “de communi mathematica scientia” 17]]; ἡ δυναμένη, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Pythagoras Philosophus]] name for the hypotenuse of a right-angled triangle, [Refs 3rd c.AD+ [3rd c.AD: Alexander Aphrodisiensis Philosophus “in Aristotelis Metaphysica commentaria - Comm. in Arist. Graeca” 75.31.]]

__II.4.b
of numbers multiplied together, come to, [Refs 3rd c.AD+ [3rd c.AD(?): Pappus Mathematicus 1.24, 27.]]

__III
impersonal, οὐ δύναται, with aorist infinitive, it cannot be, is not to be, τοῖσι Σπαρτιήτῃσι καλλιερῆσαι οὐκ ἐδύνατο [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 7.134, compare 9.45]]; δύναται it is possible, [Refs 1st c.AD+ [1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus 2.440e (assuming variant).]]

δύναμις, -εως, ἡ
(δύναμαι), [in LXX for עֹז ,גּבוּרָה ,צָבָה ,(חֵיל) חַיִל, etc.; 35 words in all ;]
power, might, strength; relatively, ability, power to perform: Mat.25:15, Act.3:12, Heb.11:11; κατὰ δ., 2Co.8:3; παρὰ δ., ib.; ὑπὲρ δ., 2Co.1:8; of pecuniary ability, 2Co.8:3, Rev.18:3; absol., power, might: Luk.24:49, Act.1:8; opposite to ἀσθένεια, 1Co.15:43; ἡ δ. τ. ἁμαρτίας, 1Co.15:56; of power in action, Rom.1:16, 20 1Co.1:18, Php.3:10, al.; ἡ δ. τ. θεοῦ, Mat.22:29, Mrk.12:24, Rom.1:20, al.; opposite to μόρφωσις, 2Ti.3:5; in doxologies, Rev.4:11 7:12, al.; ἐν δ., Mrk.9:1, Luk.4:36, Rom.1:4, al.; of the power of performing miracles, Act.6:8, 2Th.2:9; pl., Mat.13:54, Mrk.6:14, Gal.3:5, al.; of the force or meaning of a word (Plat., al.), 1Co.14:11. By meton., of persons or things;
__(a) of God, Mat.26:64, Mrk.14:62 (Dalman, Words, 200ff.);
__(b) of angels, Rom.8:38, Eph.1:21, 1Pe.3:22;
__(with) of armies, pl. [LXX for צְבָאוֹת ], metaphorically, of the stars, Mat.24:29, Mrk.13:25, Luk.21:26;
__(d) of that wh. manifests God's power: Christ, 1Co.1:24; τ. εὐαγγέλλιον, Rom.1:16; ἡ δ. τ. κυρίου, 1Co.5:4;
__(e) of mighty works (Tr., Syn., §xci), δ. ποιεῖν, Mrk.6:5 9:39; pl., Mat.7:22, Mrk.6:2, Luk.10:13, al.; σημεῖακ. δ., Act.8:13; δ. κ. τέρατα κ. σημεῖα, Act.2:22, 2Co.12:12.
SYN.: βία, ἐνέργεια, ἐξουσία, ἰσχύς, κράτος (see Tr., l.with; Cremer, 218, 236; DB, i, 616; iv, 29; DCG, i, 607; ii, 188). (AS)

δύνᾰμις [ῠ], ἡ,
genitive εως, Ionic dialect ιος, Ionic dialect dative δυνάμι: (δύναμαι):— power, might, in [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Homerus Epicus]], especially of bodily strength, εἴ μοι δ. γε παρείη [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 2.62, compare 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 8.294; οἵη ἐμὴ δ. καὶ χεῖρες 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 20.237; ἡ δ. τῶν νέων 5th c.BC: Antipho Orator 4.3.2, etc.]]: generally, strength, power, ability to do anything, πὰρ δύναμιν beyond one's strength, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 13.787; in Prose, παρὰ δ. τολμηταί 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 1.70, etc.; ὑπὲρ δ. 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 18.193]]; opposed to κατὰ δ. as far as lies in one, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 3.142, etc. (κὰδ δ. 8th-7th c.BC: Hesiodus Epicus “Opera et Dies” 336); εἰς δύναμιν 5th c.BC: Cratinus Comicus 172, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 458e, etc.; πρὸς τὴν δ. [prev. author] “Phdr.” 231a.]]

__2
outward power, influence, authority, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Persae” 174 (_anapaest meter_), “Ag.” 779 (Lyric poetry); καταπαύσαντα τὴν Κύρου δ. 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.90; δυνάμει προὔχοντες 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 7.21, etc.]]; ἐν δ. εἶναι, γενέσθαι, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Historia Graeca (Hellenica)” 4.4.5, 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 13.29.]]

__3
force for war, forces, δ. ἀνδρῶν [LXX+5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 5.100, compare 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Menexenus” 240d, 2nd c.BC: Polybius Historicus 1.41.2, LXX.Gen.21.22, “OGI” 139.8 (2nd c.BC)]]; μετὰ δυνάμεων ἱκανῶν Wilcken [Refs 2nd c.BC+ [“Chr.” 10 (2nd c.BC), etc.]]; δ. καὶ πεζὴ καὶ ἱππικὴ καὶ ναυτική [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 1.3.12]]; πέντε δυνάμεσι πεφρουρημένον, of the five projecting rows of sarissae in the phalanx, [Refs 1st c.BC+ [1st c.BC: Asclepiodotus Tacticus “Tact.” 5.2, +others]]

__4
a power, quantity, χρημάτων δ. [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 7.9.ά]].

__5
means, κατὰ δύναμιν [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Ethica Eudemia” 1243b12]]; opposed to παρὰ δ., [NT.2Cor.8.3; κατὰ δ. τῶν ὑπαρχόντων “BGU” 1051.17 (Aug.).]

__II
power, faculty, capacity, αἱ ἀμφὶ τὸ σῶμα δ. [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Hippocrates Medicus “περὶ ἀρχαίης ἰητρικῇς” 14; αἱ τοῦ σώματος δυνάμεις 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Theaetetus” 185e; ἡ τῆς ὄψεως δ. [prev. author] “R.” 532a; ἡ τῶν λεγόντων δ. 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 22.11]]: with genitive of things, capacity for, τῶν ἔργων [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Politica” 1309a35; τοῦ λέγειν [prev. author] “Rh.” 1362b22]]; τοῦ λόγου, τῶν λόγων, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-3rd c.BC: Menander Comicus 578, 2nd c.AD: Alexander Rhetor 94; δ. στρατηγική 2nd c.BC: Polybius Historicus 1.84.6; δ. ἐν πραγματείᾳ [prev. author] 2.56.5; δ. συνθετική 1st c.BC: Dionysius Halicarnassensis “de Compositione Verborum” 2]]: absolutely, any natural capacity or faculty, that may be improved and may be used for good or ill, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Topica” 126a37, compare “MM” 1183b28.]]

__II.2
elementary force, such as heat, cold, etc., [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Hippocrates Medicus “περὶ ἀρχαίης ἰητρικῇς” 16, 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “de Partibus Animalium” 646a14]]; ἡ τοῦ θερμοῦ δ.[Refs 4th c.BC+ [[prev. work] 650a5; θερμαντικὴ δ. 4th-3rd c.BC: Epicurus Philosophus “Fragmenta” 60, cf. Polystr. p.23 W.]]

__II.2.b
property, quality, ἰδίην δύναμιν καὶ φύσιν ἔχειν [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Hippocrates Medicus “περὶ ἀρχαίης ἰητρικῇς” 13, compare “Nat.Hom.” 5, “Vict.” 1.10]]; especially of the natural properties of plants, etc., αἱ δ. τῶν φυομένων, τῶν σπερμάτων, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 8.8.14, 4th-3rd c.BC: Theophrastus Philosophus “Historia Plantarum” 8.11.1]]; productive power, τῆς γῆς [Refs [[prev. author] “Oec.” 16.4; μετάλλων [prev. author] “Vect.” 4.1]]: generally, function, faculty, δύναμις φυσική, ζωική, ψυχική, [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd c.AD: Galenus Medicus 10.635]]; περὶ φυσικῶν δ., title of work by Galen.

__II.2.c
in plural, agencies, ὑπάρχειν ἐν τῇ φύσει τὰς τοιαύτας δυνάμεις (i.e. the gods) Polystr.p.10 W.

__II.2.d
function, meaning, of part in whole, [Refs [[prev. author] p.17 W.]]

__II.2.e
in Music, function, value, of a note in the scale, δ. ἐστι τάξις φθόγγου ἐν συστήματι [Refs 4th c.BC+ [2nd c.AD: Cleonides Musicus “Introductio Harmonica - Musici Scriptores Graeci” 14, compare 4th c.BC: Aristoxenus Musicus “Harmonica” p.69M.]]; μέση κατὰ δύναμιν, opposed to κατὰ θέσιν, [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd c.AD: Ptolemaeus Mathematicus “Harmonica - Opera Mathematica” 2.5.]]

__II.3
faculty, art, or craft, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 532d, 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Metaphysica” 1018a30, “EN” 1094a10, 2nd c.AD: Arrianus Historicus “Epicteti Dissertationes” 1.1.1]]; δ. σκεπτική the doctrine of the Sceptics, [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd c.AD: Sextus Empiricus Philosophus “adversus Mathematicos” 7.1.]]

__II.4

product of two numbers, ἡ ἀμφοῖν (i.e. τριάδος καὶ δυάδος) δ. ἑξάς [Refs 1st c.AD+ [1st c.AD: Philo Judaeus 1.3, compare 4th c.AD: Iamblichus Philosophus “in Nicomachi arithmeticam introductionem” p.108 P.]]; δυνάμει in product, [Refs 2nd c.BC+ [2nd-1st c.BC(?): Hero Mechanicus “Metrica” 1.15, “Theologumena Arithmeticae” 33.]]

deep_entry:
Abbott-Smith / STEPBible (TBESG)
δυσ-
inseparable prefix, opposite to εὖ, like un-, mis- (in unrest, mischance), giving the idea of difficulty, opposition, injuriousness, etc.
(AS)

---

LSJ / STEPBible (TFLSJ)
δῠσ-,
insepar. Prefix, opposed to εὖ, un-, mis-, with notion of hard, bad, unlucky, etc., as δυσήλιος, δύσαγνος; destroying the good sense of a word, or increasing its bad sense: hence, joined even to words expressing negation, as δυσάμμορος, δυσανάσχετο; poetry in strong contrasts, as Πάρις Δύσπαρις, γάμος δύσγαμος. Before στ, σθ, σπ, σφ, σχ, the final ς was omitted, see δυστ-. (Cf. Sanskrit du[snull]-, dur-, e.g. durmanās, ={δυσμενής}; ONorse tor-, e.g. torsóttligr (δύσμαχος); OIr. du-, do-, e.g. dochruth 'misshapen'.)

short_definition: if — ἐάν, contr. fr. εἰ ἄν,
deep_entry:
Abbott-Smith / STEPBible (TBESG)
ἐάν, contr. fr. εἰ ἄν,
conditional particle,
representing something as "under certain circumstances actual or liable to happen," but not so definitely expected as in the case of εἰ with ind. (Bl., §65, 4; cf. Jhn.13:17, 1Co.7:36), if haply, if;
__1. with subjc. (cl.);
__(a) pres.: Mat.6:22, Luk.10:6, Jhn.7:17, Rom.2:25, 26 al.;
{ __(b) aor. (= Lat. fut. pf.): Mat.4:9 16:26 (cf. ptcp. in Luk.9:25; M, Pr., 230), Mrk.3:24, Luk.14:34, Jhn.5:43, Rom.7:2, al.; = cl. εἰ, with opt., Jhn.9:22 11:57, Act.9:2; as Heb. אִם = ὅταν, Jhn.12:32 14:3, I Jhn.2:28 3:2, Heb.3:7" (LXX) .
__2. C. indic, (as in late writers, fr. Arist. on; see WH, App., 171; VD, MGr. 2, App., §77; Deiss., BS, 201f., LAE, 155, 254; M, Pr., 168, 187; Bl., §65, 4);
__(a) fut.: Mat.18:19 T, Luk.19:40,  Act.7:7;
__(b) pres.: 1Th.3:8 (see Milligan, in l.).
__3. With other particles: ἐ. καί (Bl., §65, 6), Gal.6:1; ἐ. μή (M, Pr., 185, 187; Bl., l.with), with subjc. pres., Mat.10:13, 1Co.8:8, Jas.2:17, 1Jn.3:21; aor., Mat.6:15, Mrk.3:27, Jhn.3:3, Rom.10:15, Gal.1:8 2:16 (see Lft., Ellic., in ll.); ἐ. τε . . . ἐ. τε, [in LXX for אִם . . . אִם, Est.19:13, al.,] Rom.14:8.
__4. = cl. ἄν (which see) after relat. pronouns and adverbs (Tdf., Pr., 96; WH, App., 173; M, Pr., 42f.; Bl., §26, 4; Mayser, 152f.; Deiss., BS, 202ff.): ὃς ἐ., Mat.5:19, Mrk.6:22, 23 Luk.17:32, 1Co.6:18, al.; ὅπου ἐ., Mat.8:19; ὁσάκις ἐ., Rev.11:6; οὗ ἐ., 1Co.16:6; καθὸ ἐ., 2Co.8:12; ὅστις ἐ., Gal.5:10.
(AS)

ἐάν
(so early Attic Inscrr., as [Refs 4th c.BC+ [“IG” 12.3.20, εἰάν sometimes after BC 400 4th c.BC, [prev. work]22.28.17,compare “PEleph.” 1.8, 10 (4th c.BC))]], also contraction ἤν and ἄν, see at {ἤν},{ἄν} (B) [ᾱ], which by crasis with καί become κἄν:—if haply, if, regularly followed by subjunctive: for its use and for examples, see at {εἰ} [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Bacchylides Lyricus 11, and ἄν (A) 5th c.BC: Bacchylides Lyricus 1.1.]]

in Hellenistic and late Greek, ={ἄν} after relative Pronouns and Conjunctions, as ὃς ἐάν whosoever, [LXX+5th c.BC+ [LXX.Gen.15.14, “PTeb.” 107.8 (2nd c.BC), NT.Matt.5.19, +others; ὅσος ἐάν “PPetr.” 3p.120 (3rd c.BC), NT.Matt.18.18; ὅστις ἐάν 1st c.AD: Philo Judaeus 1.220, 2nd c.AD: Marcus Antoninus Imperator 9.23; ὅπου ἐάν NT.Matt.8.19, etc.; ὅθεν ἐάν “Geoponica” 1.3.3: followed by _indicative_, LXX.1Ki.2.14. root_and_cognates: LSJ-hänvisningar: ἐπ; ἐν ἑαυτῷ γίγνεσθαι, ἐν, ἡμῶν αὐτῶν, ὑμῶν αὐτῶν
deep_entry:
Abbott-Smith / STEPBible (TBESG)
ἑαυτοῦ, -ῆς, -οῦ, dative -ῷ, etc., accusative -όν, etc., pi. -ῶν, etc. (Att. contr. αὑτοῦ, etc);
reflex pron.;
__1. prop, of 3rd person (Lat. sui, sibi, se), of himself, herself, itself, etc.: Mat.27:42, Mrk.15:31, Luk.23:35, al.; added to a middle verb, διεμερίσαντο ἑαυτοῖς, Jhn.19:24; to an active verb, Act.14:14 (M, Pr., 157); ἀφ᾽ ἑαυτοῦ, Luk.12:57 21:30, Jhn.5:19, al. (see: ἀπό); δι᾽ ἑαυτοῦ, Rom.14:14; ἐν ἑ., Mat.3:9, Mrk.5:30, al.; εἰς ἑ., Luk.15:17; καθ᾽ ἑαυτόν, Act.28:16, Jas.2:17; παρ᾽ ἑαυτῷ, at his own house, 1Co.16:2; πρὸς ἑ., with, to himself, Luk.18:11; as poss. pron. (with emphasis weakened; see M, Pr., 87f.), τ. ἑαυτῶν νεκρούς, Luk.9:60.
__2. As reflexive 1st and 2nd of person(s) (so also frequently in cl., chiefly poetry), Mat.23:31, Mrk.9:50, Rom.8:23, 1Th.2:8, al.
__3. In pl., for reciprocal pron., ἀλλήλων, -οις, -ους, of one another, etc.: Mat.21:38, Mrk.16:3, Eph.5:19, al.
(AS)

---

LSJ / STEPBible (TFLSJ)
ἑαυτοῦ, ῆς, οῦ, ἑαυτῷ, ῇ, ῷ, ἑαυτόν, ήν, ό,
plural ἑαυτῶν, ἑαυτοῖς, ἑαυτούς άς, ά: Ionic dialect ἑωυτοῦ [Refs 5th c.BC+ [“SIG” 57.44 (Milet., 5th c.BC), etc.]]; also ωὑτῆς [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [3rd c.BC: Herodas Mimographus 6.84, ωὑτέου 2nd c.AD: Aretaeus Medicus “περὶ αἰτιῶν καὶ σημείων ὀξέων παθῶν” 1.7 (_Ionic dialect_ ἑωυ- by contraction of ἕο αὐ-, from which also _Attic dialect_ ἑᾱυ-, frequently written ἑατοῦ]] in Papyrus and Inscrr., as [Refs 1st c.BC+ [“SIG” 774.2 (Delph., 1st c.BC)]]: Attic dialect contraction αὑτοῦ, etc., which is the usual form in Trag., though ἑαυτοῦ, etc., are used (though rarely) when the metre requires, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Prometheus Vinctus” 188 (_anapaest meter_), +others; in _Attic dialect_ Inscrr. αὑτοῦ prevails after BC 300 4th c.BC]]; Cretan dialect ϝιαυτοῦ Kohler-Ziebarth Stadtrecht von Gortyn [Refs [p.34]]; Doric dialect αὐταυτοῦ, αὐσαυτοῦ (which see); Thess. εὑτοῦ (dative), [Refs [“IG” 9(2).517.16]]: genitive plural ηὑτῶν [Refs [“Schwyzer” 251 A 44 (from Cos)]]:—reflexive pronoun of 3rd pers., of himself, herself, itself, etc.; first in [Refs 7th c.BC+ [7th-6th c.BC: Alcaeus Lyricus 78, 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus]], and Attic dialect [Refs 8th c.BC+ [(8th c.BC: Homerus Epicus has ἕο αὐτοῦ, οἷ αὐτῷ, ἑ αὐτόν): αὐτὸ ἐφ᾽ ἑαυτό (variant -τοῦ)]] itself by itself, absolutely, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Theaetetus” 152b]]; αὐτὸ ἐφ᾽ αὑτοῦ[Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. work] 160b; ὅταν τὸ ἐφ᾽ ἑαυτὸν ἕκαστος σπεύδῃ 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 1.141; αὐτὸ καθ᾽ αὑτό 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Theaetetus” 157a; αὐτὰ πρὸς αὑτά [prev. work] 154e]]; ἀφ᾽ ἑαυτῶν, ἑαυτοῦ, of themselves, himself, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 5.60, 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Memorabilia” 2.10.3]]; ἐφ᾽ ἑαυτοῦ, see at {ἐπ; ἐν ἑαυτῷ γίγνεσθαι}, ἐντὸς ἑαυτοῦ γ., see at {ἐν}, ἐντό; παρ᾽ ἑαυτῷ at his own house, [Refs [[prev. work] 3.13.3, etc.: especially with _comparative_ and _superlative_, ἐγένοντο ἀμείνονες αὐτοὶ ἑωυτῶν they surpassed]]themselves, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 8.86]]; πλουσιώτεροι ἑαυτῶν continually richer, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 1.8; θαρραλεώτεροι αὐτοὶ ἑαυτῶν 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Protagoras” 350a]], compare d; τῇ αὐτὸ ἑωυτοῦ ἐστι μακρότατον at its very greatest length, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 2.8, compare 149, 4.85, 198.]]

__II
in Attic dialect, Trag., and later, αὑτοῦ, etc., is used for the 1st pers. or 2nd pers., as for ἐμαυτοῦ, αὐτὸς καθ᾽ αὑτοῦ τἄρα μηχανορραφῶ [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Choephori” 221, compare 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Tyrannus” 138, etc.; for σεαυτοῦ, μόρον τὸν αὑτῆς οἶσθα 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Agamemnon” 1297, compare 1141, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Phaedo” 101c (variant), 3rd-2nd c.BC: Philo Mechanicus “(Belopoeica) Excerpte aus Philons Mechanik - Ath. Berl. Akad.” 59.16, etc.: so in _plural_, τὰ αὑτῶν (={ἡμῶν αὐτῶν}) ἐκποριζώμεθα 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 1.82; δώσομεν ἑαυτούς 4th-3rd c.BC: Epicurus Philosophus “Gnomologium Vaticanum - Kleine Schriften” 47]]; ἐφ᾽ ἑαυτοῖς by ourselves, [LXX+2nd c.BC+ [LXX.1Ki.14.9, compare “PPar.” 47.26 (2nd c.BC), NT.2Cor.7.1, etc.]]; ἑαυτῶν, ={ὑμῶν αὐτῶν}, [Refs 2nd c.BC+ [“PPar.” 63.128 (2nd c.BC).]]

__III
plural, ἑαυτῶν, ἑαυτοῖς, etc., is sometimes used for ἀλλήλων, ἀλλήλοις, one another, διάφοροι ἑωυτοῖσι [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 3.49; παρακελευόμενοι ἐν ἑαυτοῖς 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 4.25, etc.]]; καθ᾽ αὑτοῖν one against the other, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Antigone” 144 (_anapaest meter_); πρὸς αὑτούς 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 18.19; περιιόντες αὑτῶν πυνθάνονται [prev. author] 4.10, compare 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Lysis” 215b.]]
