deep_entry:
Abbott-Smith / STEPBible (TBESG)
ἐάω, -ῶ,
[in LXX for רפה hi., etc. ;]
__1. to let, permit: with accusative, with inf., with accusative and inf. (M, Pr., 205): Mat.24:43, Luk.4:41 22:51, Act.14.16; 16.7, 19:30 23.32 27:32 28:4 , 1Co.10:13.
__2. to let alone, leave: ἀγκύρας, Act.27:40 (cf. προσ-εάω).
† (AS)

---

LSJ / STEPBible (TFLSJ)
ἐάω,
contraction ἐῶ [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 8.428, etc.]]; Epic dialect εἰῶ [Refs 8th c.BC+ [4.55; _Epic dialect_ 2 and _3rd.pers._ _sing._ ἐάᾳς, ἐάᾳ, 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 12.137, 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 8.414]]; infinitive ἐάαν [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 8.509:]]imperfect εἴων,-ας, -α, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 18.448, 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 19.25, 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 1.28, etc.]]; Ionic dialect and Epic dialect ἔων [Refs 8th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 9.2, ἔα 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 5.517, 16.731; also ἔασκον or εἴασκον, 2.832, 5.802]], etc.: future ἐάσω [ᾱ] [Refs [18.296]], etc.: aorist εἴᾱσα (εἴᾰσεν is variant for{εἴᾱς}' in [Refs [10.299) 24.684, etc.]]; Epic dialect ἔᾱσα [Refs [11.437]]: perfect εἴᾱκα [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 8.37, 43.78, 3rd c.BC: Cercidas Iambographus 17.35:]] —passive, future ἐάσομαι in passive sense, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Iphigenia Aulidensis” 331, 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 1.142]]: aorist εἰάθην [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Isocrates Orator 4.97]]: perfect passive εἴᾱμαι [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 45.22.— 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus]] never uses the augment in this Verb. [ᾰ in present and imperfect, ᾱ in future and aorist even in Ionic dialect (so probably in [Refs 6th c.BC+ [6th c.BC: Anacreon Lyricus 56, 57]]; forms with -ασς- occur as variants in [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Homerus Epicus and 4th-5th c.BC: Parmenides Poeta Philosophus 8.7)]]. Synizesis occurs in 3rd.pers. singular ἐᾷ [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 5.256, in 1]] subjunctive ἐῶμεν [Refs 8th c.BC+ [10.344, and probably in ἐάσουσιν 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 21.233]]; also in Trag., in imperative ἔα [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Tyrannus” 1451, “Ant.” 95, 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Nubes” 932; _indicative_ ἐῶ [prev. author] “Lys.” 734: 5th c.AD(?): Hesychius Legal icographus has the form ἦσεν· εἴασεν, compare ἦσαι· παῦσαι]]]:—suffer, permit, with accusative person et infinitive, τούσδε δ᾽ ἔα φθινύθειν leave them alone to perish, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 2.346; αἴ κεν ἐᾷ με.. ζώειν 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 13.359, etc.; ἐᾶν οἰκεῖν 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 3.48, compare “IG” 12.1; ἐ. τοὺς Ἕλληνας αὐτονόμους [prev. work]2.17.9; ἐᾶν ἄκλαυτον, ἄταφον 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Antigone” 29, compare “Tr.” 1083; ἐᾶν τί τινι 1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus 2.233d:]] —so in passive, Κρέοντί γε θρόνους ἐᾶσθαι should be given up, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Coloneus” 368.]]

__b
concede, allow in argument, with accusative et infinitive, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Parmenides” 135b.]]

__2
with negative, οὐκ ἐᾶν not to suffer: hence, forbid, prevent, τρεῖν μ᾽ οὐκ ἐᾷ Παλλὰς Ἀθήνη [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 5.256; εἴπερ γὰρ φθονέω τε καὶ οὐκ εἰῶ διαπέρσαι 4.55]]; especially of the law, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aeschines Orator 3.21; δμωὰς δ᾽ οὐκ εἴας προβλωσκέμεν 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 19.25, etc.: used elliptically with ἀλλά]] following, οὐκ ἐῶν φεύγειν, ἀλλὰ [κελεύων] μένοντας ἐπικρατέειν [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 7.104, compare 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 2.21]]; also, persuade or advise not to do.., [Refs [[prev. author] 1.133: an]]infinitive may frequently be supplied, οὐκ ἐάσει σε τοῦτο will not allow thee [to do] this, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Antigone” 538]]; κἂν μηδεὶς ἐᾷ even if all men forbid, [Refs [[prev. author] “Aj.” 1184, compare “Ph.” 444:]] —so in passive, οὐκ ἐᾶσθαι, with infinitive, to be hindered, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Iphigenia Taurica” 1344, 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 1.142, 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 2.16.]]

__II
let alone, let be, with accusative, ἔα χόλον [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 9.260]]; μνηστήρων μὲν ἔα βουλήν heed not the suitors' plan, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 2.281]]; ἐπεί με πρῶτον ἐάσας as soon as thou hast dismissed me, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 24.557, compare 569, 684]]; ἤ κέν μιν ἐρύσσεαι, ἦ κεν ἐάσῃς or wilt leave him alone,[Refs 5th c.BC+ [20.311, compare 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 6.108, etc.; ἐάσωμεν ἕκηλον αὐτόν 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Philoctetes” 825; [πρᾶγμα] ἀκάθαρτον ἐᾶν [prev. author] “OT” 256; τὰ παθήματα.. παρεῖσ᾽ ἐάσω [prev. author] “OC” 363, compare 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 2.36; ἐᾶν φιλοσοφίαν 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Gorgias” 484c: with]]infinitive, ἐπὶ Σκύθας ἰέναι.. ἔασον let it alone, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 3.134]]; κλέψαι μὲν ἐάσομεν Ἕκτορα we will have done with stealing Hector, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 24.71; ἐᾶν περί τινος 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Protagoras” 347c, etc.; ἐῶ γὰρ εἰ φίλον 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 21.122: _absolutely_, ἀλλ᾽ ἄγε δὴ καὶ ἔασον]] have done, let be, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 21.221, compare 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Prometheus Vinctus” 334; οὐ χρὴ μάχεσθαι πρὸς τὸ θεῖον, ἀλλ᾽ ἐᾶν 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Fragmenta” 491.5]]; θεὸς τὸ μὲν δώσει, τὸ δ᾽ ἐάσει he will give one thing, the other he will let alone, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 14.444]]:—passive, ἡ δ᾽ οὖν ἐάσθω [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Trachiniae” 329, etc.]]

__II.2
for ἐᾶν χαίρειν, see at {χαίρω} entry near the end (ἐϝάω, compare ἔβασον· ἔασον, and εὔα· ἔα, [Refs 5th c.AD+ [5th c.AD(?): Hesychius Legal icographus who also has ἔησον· ἔασον.)]]

short_definition: Hebrew — Ἑβραῖος (WH, Ἐβ-), -α, -ον (Aram, עִבְרַי), as subst., ὁ Ἑ.,
deep_entry:
Abbott-Smith / STEPBible (TBESG)
Ἑβραῖος (WH, Ἐβ-), -α, -ον (Aram, עִבְרַי), as subst., ὁ Ἑ.,
[in LXX for עֵבֶר, עִבְרִי ;]
a Hebrew.
__1. In OT, of Israelites in contrast with those of another race (Gen.14:13, Exo.1:15, Deu.15:12, al.).
__2. In NT as the correlative of Ἑλληνιστής, a Jew who had adopted, in greater or less degree, Greek culture and Greek language. The distinction was not merely linguistic (DB, ii, 325); as far as it was so, Συριστής would be a more correct Greek term for the Jew of Semitic speech (see: Ἑβραΐς, and cf. Dalman, Words, 7): Act.6:1, 2Co.11:22, Php.3:5.
† (AS)

short_definition: to arise — ἐγείρω, [in LXX for קוּם, etc. ;] trans. (imperat. ἔγειρε used intransitively, Mat.9:5, Mrk.2:11, al.);
deep_entry:
Abbott-Smith / STEPBible (TBESG)
ἐγείρω, [in LXX for קוּם, etc. ;] trans. (imperat. ἔγειρε used intransitively, Mat.9:5, Mrk.2:11, al.);
__1. to awaken, arouse from sleep: Mrk.4:38, Act.12:7; metaphorically, of spiritual awakening, Rom.13:11 (pass.), Eph.5:14; pass., to be aroused, wake up: Mat.25:7, Mrk.4:27; ἀπὸ τ. ὕπνου, Mat.1:24.
__2. Freq. in NT, to raise from the dead: νεκρούς, Jhn.5:21, Act.26:8, 2Co.1:9; ἐκ νεκρῶν, Jhn.12:1, Act.3:15, Rom.8:11, al.; pass., rise from death: Mat.11:5, Luk.7:22, Jhn.2:22, Rom.6:9, al.; ἀπὸ τ. νεκρῶν, Mat.14:2, al.
__3. In late Gk.,
__(a) to raise, from sitting, lying, sickness; mid. and pass., to rise: Mat.9:5, 7 Mrk.1:31 9:27 10:49, al.; redundant, like Heb. קוּם, Mat.2:15 9:19, Rev.11:1 (see Dalman, 23f.);
__(b) to raise up, cause to appear: Act.13:22 (cf. Jdg.2:18); τέκνα, Mat.3:9; pass., to appear: Mat.11:11, Mrk.13:22, al.
__4. to rouse, stir up; pass., to rise against: Mat.24:7, Mrk.13:8.
__5. Of buildings, to raise: τ. ναόν, Jhn.2:19, 20 (cf . Deu.16:22, Sir.49:13); (cf. δι-, ἐξ-, συν-εγείρω, and V. Cremer, 224).
(AS)

---

__I

__I.2
rouse, stir up, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 5.208; ἐπεί μιν ἔγειρε Διὸς νόος 15.242]]; ἐγείρειν Ἄρηα stir the fight, [Refs [2.440, etc.; ἐ. μάχην, φύλοπιν, etc., 13.778, 5.496]], etc.; Τρωσὶν θυμὸν ἐ. (variant{ἀγεῖραι})[Refs 8th c.BC+ [[prev. work] 510; ἐ. τινὰ ἐπὶ ἔργον 8th-7th c.BC: Hesiodus Epicus “Opera et Dies” 20; ἔγειρε νῆα “hymnus ad Apollinem” 408]]; ἐκδοχὴν πομποῦ πυρὸς ἐ. wake up the bale-fire, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Agamemnon” 299]]; λαμπάδας ἐ. [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Ranae” 340: frequently _metaphorically_, ἐ. ἀοιδάν, λύραν, μέλος, θρῆνον, 5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “P.” 9.104, “N.” 10.21, 5th c.BC: Cratinus Comicus 222, 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Coloneus” 1778 (_anapaest meter_); μῦθον 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Politicus” 272d]]; τὸ οὖς ἐ. 'prick up' the ears, [Refs 3rd c.AD+ [3rd c.AD: Plotinus Philosophus 5.1.12.]]

__I.3

__I.4

__II

[Refs [7.371, 18.299 (whereas ἔγρεο is]]wake up! [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 15.46)]]; ἐγρήγορας ἢ καθεύδει; [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Protagoras” 310b; πόλις ζῶσα καὶ ἐγρηγορυῖα [prev. author] “Lg.” 809d; καὶ ἐφρόνει καὶ ἐγρηγόρει 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 1.4.20, etc.]]; of things, ἐγειρομένου χειμῶνος arising, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 7.49: so _metaphorically_, τὰ ἐκ τοῦ βαρβάρου ἐγειρόμενα [prev. work] 148; ἐγρηγορὸς φρούρημα 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Eumenides” 706; ἐ. τὸ πῆμα [prev. author] “Ag.” 346, etc.]]

__II.2

short_definition: I/we — ἐγώ, genitive, etc., ἐμοῦ, ἐμοί, ἐμέ (enclitic μου, μοι, με), pl. ἡμεῖς, -ῶν, -ῖν, -ᾶς,
deep_entry:
Abbott-Smith / STEPBible (TBESG)
ἐγώ, genitive, etc., ἐμοῦ, ἐμοί, ἐμέ (enclitic μου, μοι, με), pl. ἡμεῖς, -ῶν, -ῖν, -ᾶς,
of person(s) pron.
I.
__(a) The nom. is usually emphatic, when expressed as subjc, as in Mat.3:11, Mrk.1:8, Luk.3:16, al. But often there is no apparent emphasis, as Mat.10:16, Jhn.10:17; ἰδοὺ ἐ. (= Heb. הִנֵּנִי, cf. 1Ki.3:8), Act.9:10; ἐ. (like Heb. אֲנִי), I am, Jhn.1:23 (LXX), Act.7:32 (LXX).
__(b) The enclitic forms (see supr.) are used with nouns, adjectives, verbs, adverbs, where there is no emphasis: ἐν τ. πατρί μου, Jhn.14:20; μου τ. λόγους, Mat.7:24; ὀπίσω μου, Mat.3:11; ἰσχυρότερός μου, ib.; λέγει μοι, Rev.5:5; also with the prep. πρός, as Mrk.9:19, al. The full forms (ἐμοῦ, etc.) are used with the other prepositions, as δι᾽ ἐμοῦ, ἐν ἐμοί, εἰς ἐμέ, etc., also for emphasis, as Luk.10:16, Jhn.7:23, Mrk.14:7, al.
__(with) The genitive μου and ἡμῶν are often used for the poss. pronouns ἐμός, ἡμέτερος: τ. λαόν μου, Mat.2:6; μου τῂ ἀπιστιᾳ, Mrk.9:24.
__(d) τί ἐμοὶ καὶ σοί ( = Heb. מַה־לִי וָלָךְ, Jdg.11:12, al.), i.e. what have we in common: Mat.8:29, Mrk.1:24, 5:7, Luk.8:28, Jhn.2:4; τί γάρ μοι, 1Co.5:2.
__(e) The interchange of ἐγώ and ἡμεῖς, common in π., appears in Pauline Epp. (see M, Pr., 86f., M, Th., 131f.).
__(f) κἀγώ (= καὶ ἐγώ), and I, even I, I also: Mat.2:8, Luk.2:48, Jhn.6:56, Rom.3:7, 1Co.7:40, al.; κἀγώ . . . καί, both . . . and, Jhn.7:28.
(AS)

---

deep_entry:
Abbott-Smith / STEPBible (TBESG)
εἰ,
conjunctive particle, used in conditions and in indirect   questions.
__I. Conditional, if;
__1. with indic, expressing a general assumption;
__(a) pres.: before indic, pres., Mat.11:14, Rom.8:25, al.; before imperat., Mrk.4:23  9:22, Jhn.15:18, 1Co.7:9, al.; before fut. indic., Luk.16:31, Rom.8:11, al.; before pf. or aor., with negation in apodosis, Mat.12:26, Rom.4:14, al.; similarly, before impf., Luk.17:6, Jhn.8:39; before quæst., Mat.6:23, Jhn.5:47  7:23 8:46, 1Pe.2:20;
__(b) fut.: Mat.26:33, 1Pe.2:20;
__(with) pf.: Jhn.11:12, Rom.6:5, al.;
__(d) aor.: Luk.16:11  19:8, Jhn.13:32, 18:23, Rev.20:15, al.
__2. Where the assumption is certain = ἐπεί: Mat.12:28, Jhn.7:4, Rom.5:17, al.
__3. Of an unfulfilled condition, with indic, impf., aor. or plpf., before ἄν, with imp. or aor. (see: ἄν, I, i).
__4. C. indic., after verbs denoting wonder, etc., sometimes, but not always, coupled with an element of doubt: Mrk.15:44, 1Jn.3:13, al.
__5. C. indic., as in LXX (Num.14:3o, 1Ki.14:45, al. = Heb. אִם), in oaths, with the formula of imprecation understood in a suppressed apodosis (WM, 627; Burton, §272): Mrk.8:12, Heb.3:11" (LXX)  4:3 (LXX).
__6. Rarely (cl.) with optative, to express a merely possible condition: Act.24:19 27:39, 1Co.14:10 15:37, I Pe3:14, 17.
__II. Interrogative, if, whether.
__1. As in cl., in indir. questions after verbs of seeing, asking, knowing, saying, etc.: with indic. pres., Mat.26:63, Mrk.15:36, Act.19:2, 2Co.13:5, al.; fut., Mrk.3:2, Act.8:22, al.; aor., Mrk.15:44, 1Co.1:16, al.; with subjc. aor. (M, Pr., 194), Php.3:12.
__2. As in LXX (= Heb. אִם and interrog. הֲ, Gen.17:17, al.; see WM, 639f.; Viteau, i, 22), in direct questions: Mrk.8:23 (Tr., WH, txt.), Luk.13:23, 22:49, Act.19:2, al.
__III. With other particles.
__1. εἰ ἄρα, εἴγε, εἰ δὲ μήγε, see: ἄρα, γε.
__2. εἰ δὲ καί, but if also: Luk.11:18; but even if, 1Co.4:7, 2Co.4:3 11:16.
__3. εἰ δὲ μή, but if not, but if otherwise: Mrk.2:21, 22 Jhn.14:2, Rev.2:5, al.
__4. εἰ καί, if even, if also, although: Mrk.14:29, Luk.11:8, 1Co.7:21, 2Co.4:16, Php.2:17, al.
__5. καὶ εἰ, even if, see: καί
__6. εἰ μή, if not, unless, except, but only: Mat.24:22, Mrk.2:26 6:5, Jhn.9:33, 1Co.7:17 (only), Gal.1:19 (cf. ἐὰν μή, 2:16; see Hort., Ja., xvi); ἐκτὸς εἰ μή, pleonastic (Bl., §65, 6), 1Co.14:5 15:2, 1Ti.5:19.
__7. εἰ μήν = cl. ἦ μήν (M, Pr., 46), in oaths, surely (Eze.33:27, al.): Heb.6:14.
__8. εἴ πως, if haply: Act.27:12, Rom.1:10.
__9. εἴτε . . . εἴτε, whether . . . or; Rom.12:6-8, 1Co.3:22 13:8, al.
(AS)

INTERJECTIONALLY, in [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Homerus Epicus]], come now! with imperative, εἰ δὲ.. ἄκουσον [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 9.262; εἰ δὲ καὶ αὐτοὶ φευγόντων [prev. work] 46; most frequently with ἄγε (which see), 1.302, +others]]

in wishes, with optative, ἀλλ᾽ εἴ τις.. καλέσειεν [Refs [10.111, compare 24.74]]; so later, εἴ μοι ξυνείη μοῖρα [Refs 8th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Tyrannus” 863 (Lyric poetry); εἴ μοι γένοιτο φθόγγος ἐν βραχίοσιν 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Hecuba” 836: more frequently followed by γάρ, αἲ γὰρ δὴ οὕτως εἴη 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 4.189, +others; εἰ γὰρ γενοίμην ἀντὶ σοῦ νεκρός 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Hippolytus” 1410; εἰ γὰρ γένοιτο 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 6.1.38; εἰ γὰρ ἐν τούτῳ εἴη 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Protagoras” 310d]]; of unattained wishes, in [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Homerus Epicus only with _optative_, εἰ γὰρ ἐγὼν.. Διὸς πάϊς αἰγιόχοιο εἴην 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 13.825; Ζεῦ πάτερ, αἰ γὰρ ἐμὸς πόσις εἴη 7th c.BC: Alcman Lyricus 29]]; later with past tenses of indicative, εἰ γάρ μ᾽ ὑπὸ γῆν.. ἧκεν [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Prometheus Vinctus” 152 (_anapaest meter_)]]; εἰ γὰρ τοσαύτην δύναμιν εἶχον ὥστε.. [Refs 8th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Alcestis” 1072: twice in 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” with]]infinitive (compare the use of infinitive in commands), αἰ γὰρ τοῖος ἐὼν.. ἐμὸς γαμβρὸς καλέεσθαι [Refs [7.311, compare 24.376.]]

__A.2.b
εἴθε, Epic dialect αἴθε, is frequently used in wishes in the above constructions, εἴθε οἱ αὐτῷ Ζεὺς ἀγαθὸν τελέσειεν [Refs 8th c.BC+ [2.33; εἴθ᾽ ὣς ἡβώοιμι 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 7.157; ἰὼ γᾶ, εἴθ᾽ ἔμ᾽ ἐδέξω 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Agamemnon” 1537 (Lyric poetry); εἴθε σοι, ὦ Περίκλεις, τότε συνεγενόμην 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Memorabilia” 1.2.46]]: later with infinitive, γαίης χθαμαλωτέρη εἴθε.. κεῖσθαι [Refs 1st c.BC+ [“Anthologia Graeca” 9.284 (1st c.BC-1st c.AD: Crinagoras Epigrammaticus).]]

__A.2.c
εἰ γάρ, εἴθε are also used with ὤφελον (Epic dialect ὤφελλον), of past unattained wishes, αἴθ᾽ ὤφελλες στρατοῦ ἄλλου σημαίνειν [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 14.84]]; εἰ γὰρ ὤφελον [κατιδεῖν] [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 432c.]]

__A.2.d
followed by a clause expressing a consequence of the fulfilment of the wish, αἰ γὰρ τοῦτο.. ἔπος τετελεσμένον εἴη· τῷ κε τάχα γνοίης.. [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 15.536, compare 17.496, +others]]; sometimes hard to distinguish from εἰ in conditions (which may be derived from this use), εἴ μοί τι πίθοιο, τό κεν πολὺ κέρδιον εἴη [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 7.28.]]

__B
IN CONDITIONS, if:

__B.I
with INDIC.,

__B.I.1
with all tenses (for future, see below [Refs [2), to state a condition, with nothing implied as to its fulfilment, εἰ δ᾽ οὕτω τοῦτ᾽ ἐστίν, ἐμοὶ μέλλει φίλον εἶναι but]]if this is so, it will be.., [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 1.564]]: any form of the Verb may stand in apodosi, εἰ θεοί τι δρῶσιν αἰσχρόν, οὐκ εἰσὶν θεοί [Refs 8th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Fragmenta” 292.7; εἰ δοκεῖ, πλέωμεν 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Philoctetes” 526; εἰ Φαῖδρον ἀγνοῶ, καὶ ἐμαυτοῦ ἐπιλέλησμαι 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Phaedrus” 228a; κάκιστ᾽ ἀπολοίμην, Ξανθίαν εἰ μὴ φιλῶ 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Ranae” 579, compare 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 17.475; εἰ θεοῦ ἦν, οὐκ ἦν αἰσχροκερδής· εἰ δ᾽ αἰσχροκερδής, οὐκ ἦν θεοῦ 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 408c; εἰ ταῦτα λέγων διαφθείρω τοὺς νέους, ταῦτ᾽ ἂν εἴη βλαβερά [prev. author] “Ap.” 30b, compare 25b]]; εἰ οὗτοι ὀρθῶς ἀπέστησαν, ὑμεῖς ἂν οὐ χρεὼν ἄρχοιτε if these were right in their revolt, (it would follow that) you rule when you have no right, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 3.40.]]

__B.I.1.b
to express a general condition, if ever, whenever, sometimes with present, εἴ τις δύο ἢ καὶ πλείους τις ἡμέρας λογίζεται, μάταιός ἐστιν [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Trachiniae” 943]]: with imperfect, εἴ τίς τι ἠρώτα ἀπεκρίνοντο [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 7.10]]: rarely with aorist, [Refs 1st c.BC+ [1st c.BC: Diodorus Siculus Historicus 31.26.1, 2nd c.AD: Sextus Empiricus Philosophus “Πυρρώνειοι ὑποτυπώσεις” 1.84; compare 111.2.]]

__B.I.2
with future (much less frequently than ἐάν with subjunctive), either to express a future supposition emphatically, εἰ φθάσομεν τοὺς πολεμίους κατακαίνοντες οὐδεὶς ἡμῶν ἀποθανεῖται [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 7.1.19; εἰ μὴ βοηθήσετε οὐ περιέσται τἀκεῖ 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 6.91; εἰ αὕτη ἡ πόλις ληφθήσεται, ἔχεται ἡ πᾶσα Σικελία [prev. passage];]] in threats or warnings, εἰ μὴ καθέξεις γλῶσσαν ἔσται σοι κακά [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Fragmenta” 5; εἰ τιμωρήσεις Πατρόκλῳ, αὐτὸς ἀποθανῇ 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Apologia” 28c, compare 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 28.21: or,]]

__B.I.2.b
to express a present intention or expectation, αἶρε πλῆκτρον εἰ μαχεῖ if you mean to fight, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Aves” 759; ἐγὼ μὲν οὐκ ἀνήρ.. εἰ ταῦτ᾽ ἀνατεὶ τῇδε κείσεται κράτη 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Antigone” 485, compare 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 1.61, 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Hecuba” 863.]]

__B.I.3
with historical tenses, implying that the condition is or was unfulfilled.

__B.I.3.a
with imperfect, referring to present time or to continued or repeated action in past time (in [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Homerus Epicus always the latter, 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 24.715, +others): ταῦτα οὐκ ἂν ἐδύναντο ποιεῖν, εἰ μὴ διαίτῃ μετρίᾳ ἐχρῶντο they would not be able to do this (as they do)]], if they did not live an abstemious life, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 1.2.16, compare 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 489b; οὐκ ἂν νήσων ἐκράτει, εἰ μή τι καὶ ναυτικὸν εἶχεν he (from Agamemnon)]] would not have been master of islands, if he had not had also some naval force, [Refs 7th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 1.9; αἰ δ᾽ ἦχες ἔσλων ἴμερον ἢ κάλων.. αἴδως κεν.. ἦχεν 7th-6th c.BC: Sappho Lyrica 28]]; εἰ ἦσαν ἄνδρες ἀγαθοὶ.. οὐκ ἄν ποτε ταῦτα ἔπασχον if they had been good men, they would never have suffered as they did, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Gorgias” 516e, compare 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Memorabilia” 1.1.5]]; εἰ γὰρ ἐγὼ τάδε ᾔδἐ.. οὐκ ἂν ὑπεξέφυγε if I had known this.., [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 8.366.]]

__B.I.3.b
with aorist referring to past time, εἰ μὴ ἔφυσε θεὸς μέλι.. ἔφασκον γλύσσονα σῦκα πέλεσθαι [Refs 6th c.BC+ [6th c.BC: Xenophanes Poeta Philosophus 38]]; εἰ μὴ ὑμεῖς ἤλθετε, ἐπορευόμεθα ἂν ἐπὶ βασιλέα had you not come, we should be on our way.., [Refs 8th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 2.1.4; καὶ ἴσως ἂν ἀπέθανον, εἰ μὴ ἡ ἀρχὴ διὰ ταχέων κατελύθη 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Apologia” 32d, compare 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 5.680, 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 4.364, 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 4.5, 27.63]]: with pluperfect in apodosi, εἰ τριάκοντα μόναι μετέπεσον τῶν ψήφων, ἀπεπεφεύγη ἄν [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Apologia” 36a.]]

__B.I.3.c
rarely with pluperfect referring to action finished in past or present time, λοιπὸν δ᾽ ἂν ἦν ἡμῖν ἔτι περὶ τῆς πόλεως διαλεχθῆναι, εἰ μὴ προτέρα τῶν ἄλλων τὴν εἰρήνην ἐπεποίητο if she had not (as she has done) made peace before the rest, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Isocrates Orator 5.56, compare 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Timaeus” 21c.]]

__B.II
with SUB[Refs 1st c.AD+ [1st c.AD: Josephus Historicus, εἰ is regularly joined with ἄν]] (Epic dialect κε, κεν), compare ἐάν: [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.AD(?): Arcadius Grammaticus εἰκαν in Tegean Inscrr. of 4th c.BC (“IG” 5(2).3.16, 31, 6.2, “SIG” 306.34) should be understood as εἰκ ἄν (εἰ: εἰκ ={οὐ}: οὐκ), since εἰ δ᾽ ἄν is also found in “IG” 5(2).3.2, 6.45, and εἰκ alone, [prev. work]3.21]]; but ἄν (κε, κεν) are frequently absent in [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Homerus Epicus as 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 5.221, 14.373 (and compare below 2), and Lyric poetry, 5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus (who never uses εἰ with ἄν or κε (ν)) “P.” 4.266, +others; in dialects, αἰ δείλητ᾽ ἀγχωρεῖν “IG” 9(1).334.6 (_Locrian dialect_, 5th c.BC)]], cf. Foed.Doric dialect cited in [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 5.79; rarely in 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus, εἰ μὴ ἀναβῇ 2.13]]; occasionally in Trag., [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Eumenides” 234, 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Tyrannus” 198 (Lyric poetry), etc.]]; very rarely in Attic dialect Prose, εἰ ξυστῶσιν αἱ πόλεις [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 6.21; εἴ τι που ἄλσος ἢ τέμενος ἀφειμένον ᾖ 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Leges” 761c]]: in later Prose, εἴ τις θελήσῃ [NT+3rd c.AD+ [NT.Rev.11.5; εἰ φονεύῃ 3rd c.AD: Plotinus Philosophus 2.9.9, compare 5th c.AD: Proclus Philosophus “Inst.” 26.]]

__B.II.1
when the apodosis is future, to express a future condition more distinctly and vividly than εἰ with optative, but less so than εἰ with future indicative (above [Refs [1.2a)]]; εἰ δέ κεν ὣς ἕρξῃς καί τοι πείθωνται Ἀχαιοί, γνώσῃ ἔπειθ᾽.. if thou do thus.., thou shalt know, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 2.364, compare 1.128, 3.281, 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 17.549; ἂν δέ τις ἀνθιστῆται, σὺν ὑμῖν πειρασόμεθα χειροῦσθαι 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 7.3.11]]; ἂν μὴ νῦν ἐθέλωμεν ἐκεῖ πολεμεῖν αὐτῷ, ἐνθάδ᾽ ἴσως ἀναγκασθησόμεθα τοῦτο ποιεῖν if we be not now willing, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 4.50, compare 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 5.3.27: followed by _imperative_, ἢν εἰρήνης δοκῆτε δεῖσθαι, ἄνευ ὅπλων ἥκετε [prev. work] 3.2.13, compare 5.4.30.]]

__B.II.2
when the apodosis is present, denoting customary or repeated action, to express a general condition, if ever, ἤν ποτε δασμὸς ἵκηται, σοὶ τὸ γέρας πολὺ μεῖζον (i.e. ἐστί) whenever a division comes, your prize is (always) greater, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 1.166]]; ἢν ἐγγὺς ἔλθῃ θάνατος, οὐδεὶς βούλεται θνῄσκειν if death come near, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Alcestis” 671]]; with ἄν omitted, εἴ περ γάρ τε χόλον.. καταπέψῃ ἀλλά.. ἔχει κότον [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 1.81.]]

__B.II.2.b
with Rhet. present in apodosis, ἐὰν μὴ οἱ φιλόσοφοι βασιλεύσωσιν, οὐκ ἔστι κακῶν παῦλα there is (i.e. can be, will be) no rest.., [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 473d.]]

__B.III
with OPTATIVE (never with ἄν in early Gr., later ἐάν with optative, [Refs 5th c.AD+ [5th-6th c.AD: Damascius Philosophus “de Principiis” 114, +others),]]

__B.III.1
to express a future condition less definitely than ἐάν with subjunctive, usually with optative with ἄν in apodosis, ἦ κεν γηθήσαι Πρίαμος Πριάμοιό τε παῖδες.. εἰ σφῶιν τάδε πάντα πυθοίατο μαρναμένοιιν surely they would exult, if they should hear.., [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 1.255, compare 7.28, 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 3.223; εἴης φορητὸς οὐκ ἄν, εἰ πράσσοις καλῶς 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Prometheus Vinctus” 979; οὐδὲ γὰρ ἄν με ἐπαινοίη, εἰ ἐξελαύνοιμι τοὺς εὐεργέτας 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 7.7.11; οἶκος δ᾽ αὐτός, εἰ φθογγὴν λάβοι, σαφέστατ᾽ ἂν λέξειεν 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Agamemnon” 37, etc.]]: future optative is falsa lectio in [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Theaetetus” 164a]]: with present indicative in apodosis, [Refs 6th c.BC+ [6th c.BC: Xenophanes Poeta Philosophus 34.3, 3rd c.AD: Democritus Epigrammaticus 253]]: with future indicative, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Melissus Philosophus 5.]]

__B.III.1.b
in Hom.sometimes with present optative, to express an unfulfilled present condition, εἰ μὲν νῦν ἐπὶ ἄλλῳ ἀεθλεύοιμεν, ἦ τ᾽ ἂν ἐγὼ τὰ πρῶτα φεροίμην if we were now contending, etc., [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 23.274: rarely in Trag., εἰ μὴ κνίζοι (={εἰ μὴ ἔκνιζε}) 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Medea” 568; also εἰ ἀναγκαῖον εἴη ἀδικεῖν ἢ ἀδικεῖσθαι, ἑλοίμην ἂν μᾶλλον ἀδικεῖσθαι 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Gorgias” 469c.]]

__B.III.2
when the apodosis is past, denoting customary or repeated action, to express a general condition in past time (corresponding to use of subjunctive in present time, above [Refs [11.2)]]; once in [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Homerus Epicus, εἴ τίς με.. ἐνίπτοι, ἀλλὰ σὺ τόν γ᾽.. κατέρυκες 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 24.768]]; εἰ δέ τινας θορυβουμένους αἴσθοιτο.., κατασβεννύναι τὴν ταραχὴν ἐπειρᾶτο if he should see (whenever he saw) any troops in confusion, he (always) tried, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 5.3.55, compare “An.” 4.5.13, “Mem.” 4.2.40]]; εἴ τις ἀντείποι, εὐθὺς ἐτεθνήκει if any one made objection, he was a dead man at once, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 8.66; ἀλλ᾽ εἴ τι μὴ φέροιμεν, ὤτρυνεν φέρειν 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Alcestis” 755. For εἰ with _indicative_ in this sense see above 1.1]]: indicative and optative are found in same sentence, ἐμίσει, οὐκ εἴ τις κακῶς πάσχων ἠμύνετο, ἀλλ᾽ εἴ τις εὐεργετούμενος ἀχάριστος φαίνοιτο [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Agesilaus” 11.3.]]

__B.III.3
in oratio obliqua after past tenses, representing ἐάν with subjunctive or εἰ with a primary (never an historical) tense of the indicative in oratio recta, ἐλογίζοντο ὡς, εἰ μὴ μάχοιντο, ἀποστήσοιντο αἱ πόλεις (representing ἐὰν μὴ μαχώμεθα, ἀποστήσονται) [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Historia Graeca (Hellenica)” 6.4.6, compare 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 21.104, 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Historia Graeca (Hellenica)” 5.2.2]]; ἔλεγεν ὅτι, εἰ βλαβερὰ πεπραχὼς εἴη, δίκαιος εἴη ζημιοῦσθαι (representing εἰ βλαβερὰ πέπραχε, δίκαιός ἐστι)[Refs [[prev. work] 32, compare “An.” 6.6.25]]; εἰ δέ τινα φεύγοντα λήψοιτο, προηγόρευεν ὅτι ὡς πολεμίῳ χρήσοιτο (representing εἴ τινα λήψομαι, χρήσομαι) [Refs [[prev. author] “Cyr.” 3.1.3]]; also, where oratio obliqua is implied in the leading clause, οὐκ ἦν τοῦ πολέμου πέρας Φιλίππῳ, εἰ μὴ Θηβαίους.. ἐχθροὺς ποιήσειε τῇ πόλει, i.e. Philip thought there would be no end to the war, unless he should make.. (his thought having been ἐὰν μὴ ποιήσω), [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 18.145; ἐβούλοντο γὰρ σφίσιν, εἴ τινα λάβοιεν, ὑπάρχειν ἀντὶ τῶν ἔνδον, ἢν ἄρα τύχωσί τινες ἐζωγρημένοι 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 2.5.]]

__B.III.4
with optative with ἄν, only when the clause serves as apodosis as well as protasis,[Refs 5th c.BC+ [compare 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Protagoras” 329b, 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 4.18, 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Memorabilia” 1.5.3 (see. ἄν 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus 111. d).]]

__B.IV
with infinitive, in oratio obliqua, only in [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus, εἰ γὰρ δὴ δεῖν πάντως περιθεῖναι ἄλλῳ τέῳ τὴν βασιληΐην, [ἔφη] δικαιότερον εἶναι κτλ. 1.129; εἰ εἶναι τοῦτο μὴ φίλον 2.64, compare 172, 3.105, 108.]]

__B.V
after Verbs denoting wonder, delight, indignation, disappointment, contentment, and similar emotions, εἰ with indicative is used instead of ὅτι, to express the object of the feeling in a hypothetical form, θαυμάζω εἰ μηδεὶς ὑμῶν μήτ᾽ ἐνθυμεῖται μήτ᾽ ὀργίζεται, ὁρῶν.. I wonder that no one of you is either concerned or angry when he sees.., [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 4.43; οὐκ ἀγαπᾷ εἰ μὴ δίκην δέδωκεν, ἀλλ᾽ εἰ μὴ καὶ χρυσῷ στεφάνῳ στεφανωθήσεται ἀγανακτεῖ 4th c.BC: Aeschines Orator 3.147]]: after past tenses, ἐθαύμασε δ᾽ εἰ μὴ φανερόν ἐστιν [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Memorabilia” 1.1.13; δεινὸν εἰσῄει, εἰ μὴ.. δόξει 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 19.33; ἐθαύμαζον εἴ τι ἕξει τις χρήσασθαι τῷ λόγῳ 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Phaedo” 95a; οὐδὲ ᾐσχύνθη εἰ.. ἐπάγει 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 21.105: in oratio obliqua (expressed or implied) with _optative_, ἐπεῖπεν ὡς δεινὸν (i.e. εἴη) εἰ.. μεγαλόψυχος γένοιτο 4th c.BC: Aeschines Orator 2.157; ᾤκτιρον εἰ ἁλώσοιντο 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 1.4.7]]; ἐθαύμαζε δ᾽ εἴ τις ἀρετὴν ἐπαγγελλόμενος ἀργύριον πράττοιτο he wondered that any one should demand money, [Refs [[prev. author] “Mem.” 1.2.7]]; ἔχαιρον ἀγαπῶν εἴ τις ἐάσοι I rejoiced, being content if any one should let it pass, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 450a:]] —in this use the _negative_ οὐ is also found, ἀγανακτῶ εἰ ὁ Φίλιππος ἁρπάζων οὐ λυπεῖ [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 8.55; δεινὸν ἂν εἴη εἰ οἱ ἐκείνων ξύμμαχοι οὐκ ἀπεροῦσιν 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 1.121; τέρας λέγεις, εἰ οὐκ ἂν δύναιντο λαθεῖν 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Meno” 91d, etc.]]

__B.VI
in citing a fact as a ground of argument or appeal, as surely as, since, εἴ ποτ᾽ ἔην γε if there was [as there was], i.e. as sure as there was such an one, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 3.180, +others; εἰ τότε κοῦρος ἔα, νῦν αὖτέ με γῆρας ὀπάζει 4.321]]; πολλοὺς γὰρ οἶκε εἶναι εὐπετέστερον διαβάλλειν ἢ ἕνα, εἰ Κλεομένεα μὲν μοῦνον οὐκ οἷός τε ἐγένετο διαβαλεῖν, τρεῖς δὲ μυριάδας Ἀθηναίων ἐποίησε τοῦτο it seems easier to deceive many than one, if (as was the fact, i.e. since) he was not able.., [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 5.97, compare 1.60, +others]]

__B.VII
ELLIPTICAL CONSTRUCTIONS:

__B.VII.1
with apodosis implied in the context, εἰ having the force of in case, supposing that, πρὸς τὴν πόλιν, εἰ ἐπιβοηθοῖεν, ἐχώρουν they marched towards the city [so as to meet the citizens], in case they should rush out, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 6.100]]; ἱκέται πρὸς σὲ δεῦρ᾽ ἀφίγμεθα, εἴ τινα πόλιν φράσειας ἡμῖν εὔερον we have come hither to you, in case you should tell us of some fleecy city (i.e. that we might hear of it), [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Aves” 120]]; παρέζεο καὶ λαβὲ γούνων, αἴ κέν πως ἐθέλῃσιν ἐπὶ Τρώεσσιν ἀρῆξαι sit by him and grasp his knees [so as to persuade him], in case he be willing to help the Trojans, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 1.408, compare 66, 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 1.94, 3.92]]; ἄκουσον καὶ ἐμοῦ, ἐάν σοι ἔτι ταὐτὰ δοκῇ hear me also [that you may assent], in case the same opinion please you, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 358b]]; ἰδὲ δή, ἐάν σοι ὅπερ ἐμοὶ συνδοκῇ look now, in case you approve what I do, [Refs [[prev. work] 434a.]]

__B.VII.2
with apodosis suppressed for rhetorical reasons, εἴ περ γάρ κ᾽ ἐθέλῃσιν Ὀλύμπιος.. στυφελίξαι if he wish to thrust him away, [he will do so], [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 1.580]]; εἰ μὲν δώσουσι γέρας—· εἰ δέ κε μὴ δώωσιν, ἐγὼ δέ κεν αὐτὸς ἕλωμαι if they shall give me a prize, [well and good]; but if they give not, then I will take one for myself, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [1.135, compare 6.150, 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Plutus” 468]]; καὶ ἢν μὲν ξυμβῇ ἡ πεῖρα—· εἰ δὲ μή.. and if the attempt succeed, [well]; otherwise.., [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 3.3, compare 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Protagoras” 325d.]]

__B.VII.3
with the Verb of the protasis omitted, chiefly in the following expressions:

__B.VII.3.a
εἰ μή except, οὐδὲν ἄλλο σιτέονται, εἰ μὴ ἰχθῦς μοῦνον [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.200]]; μὰ τὼ θεώ, εἰ μὴ Κρίτυλλά γ᾽ [εἰμί]—nay, if I'm not Critylla! i.e. I am, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Thesmophoriazusae” 898]]; εἰ μὴ ὅσον except only, ἐγὼ μέν μιν οὐκ εἶδον, εἰ μὴ ὅσον γραφῇ [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 2.73, compare 1.45, 2.20; εἰ μὴ εἰ 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 1.17, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Gorgias” 480b, etc.]]; εἰ μή τι οὖν, ἀλλὰ σμικρόν γέ μοι τῆς ἀρχῆς χάλασον if nothing else, yet.., [Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. author] “Men.” 86e; ironical, εἰ μὴ ἄρα ἡ τῆς ἀρετῆς ἐπιμέλεια διαφθορά ἐστιν 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Memorabilia” 1.2.8; εἰ μή πέρ γε τὸν ὑοσκύαμον χρήματα εἶναι φήσομεν [prev. author] “Oec.” 1.13.]]

__B.VII.3.b
εἰ δὲ μή but if not, i.e. otherwise, προηγόρευε τοῖς Λαμψακηνοῖσι μετιέναι Μιλτιάδεα, εἰ δὲ μή, σφέας πίτυος τρόπον ἀπείλεε ἐκτρίψειν [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 6.37, compare 56]]; after μάλιστα μέν, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 1.32, 35, etc.:]] —after a preceding _negative_, μὴ τύπτ᾽· εἰ δὲ μή, σαυτόν ποτ᾽ αἰτιάσει don't beat me; otherwise, you will have yourself to blame, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Nubes” 1433; ὦ Κῦρε, μὴ οὕτω λέγε· εἰ δὲ μή, οὐ θαρροῦντά με ἕξεις 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 3.1.35; οὔτ᾽ ἐν τῷ ὕδατι τὰ ὅπλα ἦν ἔχειν· εἰ δὲ μή [prev. author] “An.” 4.3.6, compare 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 1.28, 131, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Phaedo” 91c.]]

__B.VII.3.c
εἰ δέ sometimes stands for εἰ δὲ μή, εἰ μὲν βούλεται, ἑψέτω· εἰ δ᾽, ὅτι βούλεται, τοῦτο ποιείτω [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Euthydemus” 285c, compare “Smp.” 212c; εἰ δ᾽ οὖν 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Antigone” 722; εἰ δ᾽ οὕτως 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Ethica Nicomachea” 1094a24]]; εἰ δὲ τοῦτο and if so, [Refs 1st c.BC+ [1st c.BC-1st c.AD: Strabo Geographus 2.1.29.]]

__B.VII.3.d
εἰ γάρ for if so, [Refs [[prev. author] 7.3.6.]]

__B.VII.3.e
εἴ τις if any, i. e. as much as or more than any, τῶν γε νῦν αἴ τις ἐπιχθονίων, ὀρθῶς [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Bacchylides Lyricus 5.5; ὄτλον ἄλγιστον ἔσχον, εἴ τις Αἰτωλὶς γυνή 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Trachiniae” 8, compare “OC” 734]]; εἴ τις ἄλλος, siquis alius, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Andromache” 6, etc.; εἴ τινες καὶ ἄλλοι 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 3.2, etc.; εἴπερ τις ἄλλος 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 501d]]; also κατ᾽ εἰ δέ τινα τρόπον in any way, [Refs [“IG” 5(2).6.27 (from Tegea).]]

__B.VII.3.f
εἴ ποτε or εἴπερ ποτέ now if ever, ἡμῖν δὲ καλῶς, εἴπερ ποτέ, ἔχει.. ἡ ξυναλλαγή [Refs 7th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 4.20, compare 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Equites” 594; αἴ ποτα κἄλλοτα 7th-6th c.BC: Alcaeus Lyricus “Supp.” 7.11, compare 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 6.4.12, etc.]]; but in prayers, εἴ ποτέ τοι ἐπὶ νηὸν ἔρεψα.. τόδε μοι κρήηνον ἐέλδωρ [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 1.39.]]

__B.VII.3.g
εἴ ποθεν (i.e. δυνατόν ἐστι) if from any quarter, i.e. from some quarter or other, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Philoctetes” 1204 (Lyric poetry)]]; so εἴ ποθι somewhere, anywhere, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [[prev. author] “Aj.” 885 (Lyric poetry); εἴ που 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 4.193.]]

__B.VII.3.h
εἴ πως[Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. work] 388, 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 2.3.11]]: in an elliptical sentence (cf. VII. [Refs 5th c.BC+ [1), πρέσβεις πέμψαντες, εἴ πως πείσειαν 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 1.58.]]

__B.VIII
with other PARTICLES:

__B.VIII.1
for the distinction between καὶ εἰ (or καὶ ἐάν, or κἄν) even if, and εἰ καί (or ἐὰν καί) even though, see at {καί}:—the opposite of καὶ εἰ is οὐδ᾽ εἰ, not even if; that of εἰ καί is εἰ μηδέ, if (although) not even.

__B.VIII.2
for ὡς εἰ, ὡς εἴ τε, ὥσπερ εἰ, etc., see at {ὡς} and ὥσπερ.

__B.VIII.3
for εἰ ἄρα, see at {ἄρα}; for εἰ δή, εἴπερ, see at {εἰ δή, εἴπερ}; for εἴ γε, see at {γέ}.

__B.IX
in negative oaths, = Hebrew im, [LXX+NT [LXX.Psa.94(95).11, NT.Mark.8.12, +others]]

__C
IN INDIRECT QUESTIONS, whether, followed by the indicative, subjunctive, or optative, according to the principles of oratio obliqua:

__C.1
with IN[Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator after primary tenses, representing the same tense in the direct question, σάφα δ᾽ οὐκ οἶδ᾽ εἰ θεός ἐστιν]] whether he is a god, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 5.183; εἰ ξυμπονήσεις.. σκόπει 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Antigone” 41.]]

__C.2
with SUB[Refs 1st c.AD+ [1st c.AD: Josephus Historicus after primary tenses, representing a dubitative]]subjunctive in the direct question, τὰ ἐκπώματα οὐκ οἶδ᾽ εἰ Χρυσάντᾳ τουτῳῒ δῶ whether I should give them, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 8.4.16: sometimes elliptical, ἐς τὰ χρηστήρια ἔπεμπε, εἰ στρατεύηται ἐπὶ τοὺς Πέρσας 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.75.]]

__C.3
OPT. after past tenses, representing either of the two previous constructions in the direct question, ἤρετο εἴ τις ἐμοῦ εἴη σοφώτερος he asked whether any one was wiser than I (direct ἔστι τις σοφώτερο;), [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Apologia” 21a; ἐπεκηρυκεύετο Πεισιστράτῳ, εἰ βούλοιτό οἱ τὴν θυγατέρα ἔχειν γυναῖκα 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.60: rarely]]aorist optative for the aorist indicative, ἠρώτων αὐτὸν εἰ ἀναπλεύσειεν I asked him whether he had set sail (direct ἀνέπλευσα;), [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 50.55: but]]aorist optative usually represents aorist subjunctive, τὸν θεὸν ἐπήροντο εἰ παραδοῖεν Κορινθίοις τὴν πόλιν.. καὶ τιμωρίαν τινὰ πειρῷντ᾽ ἀπ᾽ αὐτῶν ποιεῖσθαι they asked whether they should deliver their city to the Corinthians, and should try.., [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 1.25:]] —in both constructions the _indicative_ or subjunctive may be retained, ψῆφον ἐβούλοντο ἐπαγαγεῖν εἰ χρὴ πολεμεῖν[Refs [[prev. work] 119]]; ἐβουλεύοντο εἴτε κατακαύσωσιν.. εἴτε τι ἄλλο χρήσωνται whether they should burn them or should dispose of them in some other way, [Refs [[prev. author] 2.4]]; ἀνακοινοῦσθαι αὐτὸν αὑτῷ εἰ δῷ ἐπιψηφίσαι τοῖς προέδροις [he said that] he consulted him whether he should give.., [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aeschines Orator 2.68.]]

__C.4
with OPT. and ἄν when this was the form of the direct question, ἠρώτων εἰ δοῖεν ἂν τούτων τὰ πιστά they asked whether they would give (direct δοιήτε ἄ;), [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 4.8.7.]]

__C.5
the NEG. used with εἰ in indirect questions is οὐ, when οὐ would be used in the direct question, ἐνετέλλετο.. εἰρωτᾶν εἰ οὔ τι ἐπαισχύνεται whether he is not ashamed, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.90, etc.]]; but if μή would be required in the direct form, it is retained in the indirect, οὐ τοῦτο ἐρωτῶ, ἀλλ᾽ εἰ τοῦ μὲν δικαίου μὴ ἀξιοῖ πλέον ἔχειν μηδὲ βούλεται ὁ δίκαιος, τοῦ δὲ ἀδίκου (the direct question would be μὴ ἀξιοῖ μηδὲ βούλετα; he does not see fit nor wish, does he?) [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 349b]]:—in double indirect questions, εἴτε.. εἴτε..; εἰ.. εἴτε..; εἴτε.. ἢ.., either οὐ or μή can be used in the second clause, ὅπως ἴδῃς εἴτ᾽ ἔνδον εἴτ᾽ οὐκ ἔνδον [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Ajax” 7; σκοπῶμεν εἰ ἡμῖν πρέπει ἢ οὔ 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 451d]]; εἰ ἀληθὲς ἢ μή, πειράσομαι μαθεῖν[Refs 4th c.BC+ [[prev. work] 339a; πολλὰ ἂν περιεσκέψω, εἴτε ἐπιτρεπτέον εἴτε οὔ·.. οὐδένα λόγον οὐδὲ συμβουλὴν ποιῇ, εἴτε χρὴ ἐπιτρέπειν σαυτὸν αὐτῷ εἴτε μή [prev. author] “Prt.” 313a, 313b; ἀνάγκη τὴν ἐμὴν μητέρα, εἴτε θυγάτηρ ἦν Κίρωνος εἴτε μή, καὶ εἰ παρ᾽ ἐκείνῳ διῃτᾶτο ἢ οὔ, καὶ γάμους εἰ διττοὺς ὑπὲρ ταύτης εἱστίασεν ἢ μὴ.. πάντα ταῦτα εἰδέναι τοὺς οἰκέτας 4th c.BC: Isaeus Orator 8.9]]; τοὺς νόμους καταμανθάνειν εἰ καλῶς κεῖνται ἢ μή.. τοὺς λόγους εἰ ὀρθῶς ὑμᾶς διδάσκουσιν ἢ οὔ [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Antipho Orator 5.14.]]

deep_entry:
Abbott-Smith / STEPBible (TBESG)
εἰμί,
with various uses and significations, like the English verb to be.
__I. As substantive verb.
__1. Of persons and things, to be, exist: Act.17:28, Jhn.1:1, 8:58, 17:5, al; ὁ ὢν καὶ ὁ ἦν (for past ptcp.), Rev.1:4, 8, 4:8, 11:17, 16:5 (see Swete, Ap., 5; M, Pr., 228); τὰ (μὴ) ὄντα, Rom.4:17, 1Co.1:28.
__2. Of times, events, etc., to be, happen, take place: Mat.24:3, Mrk.14:2, 15:42, Luk.21:23, Jhn.4:6, 23, 5:10, al.
__3. to be present, be in a place, have come: Mat.2:13, 15, Mrk.1:45, 5:21, 15:40, Luk.1:80, 5:29, Jhn.7:30, al.; before εἰς, Mrk.2:1; before  ἐκ, (ἐξ), Mat.1:20, 21:25, Mrk.11:30, Jhn.3:31, al.
__4. Impers.,  ἔστι, ἦν, etc.;
__(a) there is (Fr. il y a), was, etc.: Mat.16:28, Luk.16:19, Jhn.3:1, 5:2, Rom.3:10, al.; with dative (of the possessor; Bl., §37, 3), Mat.16:22, Luk.1:7, Jhn.18.10, Rom.9:2, al.;  ἔστιν ὅς, ὅστις (chiefly in pl), Mat.16:28, 19:2, Mrk.9:1, al.;
__(b) with inf., = ἔξεστιν (which see), it is possible: Heb.9:5, 1Co.11:20, RV (but see ICC, in l.).
__II. As copula uniting subject and predicate.
__1. Expressing simply identity or equivalence: Mat.5:13, 14:15, Luk.1:18, 19, Jhn.1:1, 4:19, Rev.3:9, al. mult.
__2. Explicative, as in parable, figure, type, etc.: Mat.13:19, 1Co.9:2, 10:4, 11:25, Gal.4:24, Rev.17:15, al.; ταῦτ᾽ ἔστιν, Mat.27:46, Mrk.7:2, Rom.7:18 al.; ὅ ἐστιν, Mrk.3:17, Col.1:24, Heb.7:2, al.; akin to this is the sacramental usage: Mat.26:26-28, Mrk.14:22, 24, Luk.22:19, 1Co.11:24 (see ICC on Mk, I Co, ll. with; DB, iii, 148 f.).
__3. C. genitive: qual., etc., Mrk.5:42, Luk.3:23, 1Co.14:33, Heb.12:11, al.; part., 1Ti.1:20, 2Ti.1:15; poss., Mat.5:3, 10, Mrk.12:7, Luk.4:7; of service or partisanship, Rom.8:9, 1Co.1:12, 2Co.10:7, 2Ti.2:19.
__4. C. dative (BL, §37, 3): Act.1:8, 9:15, Rom.4:12, 1Co.1:18, 2:14, Rev.21:7, al.
__5. C. ptcp., as a periphrasis for the simple verb (Bl., §62, 1, 2; M, Pr., 225 ff.);
__(a) with ptcp. pf. (cl.): Mat.10:30, Luk.9:32, Jhn.3:24, Act.21:35, 1Co.15:19, al;
__(b) with ptcp. pr. (esp. in impf., as in Heb. and Aram.; Dalman, Words, 35 f.), Mat.7:29, Mrk.1:22, Luk.4:31, 14:1, Act.1:10, al. mult., id. for imper. (M, Pr., 180f., 182f.), with ellipsis of εἰμί, Rom.12:9, 10, Heb.13:5, al.;
__(with) with ptcp. aor. (cl), Luk.23:9.
__6. Seq. εἰς (cf. Heb. הָיָה לְ), a vernac. usage (M, Pr., 71): Mat.19:5, Mrk.10:8, Heb.8:10, al.
__7. C. adv.: Mat.19:20, Mrk.4:26, Luk.18:11, al.
__8. Ellipses;
__(a) of the copula (Bl., §30, 3): Mat.8:29, 24:32, Jhn.21:22, 23, Heb.6:4, al.;
__(b) of the predicate: ἐγώ εἰμί, Mat.14:27, Mrk.6:50, al.; absol. (cf. Deu.32:39; אֲנִי הוּא), Mrk.13:6, Jhn.4:26, al. (cf. ἄπ-, ἔν-, πάρ-, συμ-πάρ-, σύν-ειμι).
(AS)

εἰμί
(sum), Aeolic dialect ἔμμι [Refs 7th c.BC+ [7th-6th c.BC: Sappho Lyrica 2.15, 3rd c.BC: Theocritus Poeta Bucolicus 20.32]]; Cretan dialect ἠμί [Refs [“GDI” 4959a]]; 2nd pers. singular εἶ, Epic dialect and Ionic dialect εἰς [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 17.388, +others, _Aeolic dialect_ ἔσσι]], Epic dialect and Doric dialect ἐσσί [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 1.176, 5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “O.” 6.90, 5th c.BC: Sophron Comicus 134; ἐ. ὅπῃ, ἔσθ᾽ ὅπου, somehow, somewhere, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Protagoras” 331d, 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Eumenides” 517, 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Tyrannus” 448, etc.]]; in questions expecting a negative answer, ἐ. ὁπόθεν, ὅπω; [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Philebus” 35a, “R.” 493e, etc.; οὐ γάρ ἐσθ᾽ ὅπως 5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “Fragmenta.” 61, compare 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 7.102, 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Agamemnon” 620]]; οὐκ ἔ. ὅπως οὐ in any case, necessarily, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Pax” 188; οὐκ ἔ. ὡς 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Meno” 76e, etc.]]; ἐ. ὅτε, ἔσθ᾽ ὅτε, sometimes, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “Fragmenta.” 180.2, 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Ajax” 56, 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 7.21, etc.]]

__A.V
ἦν is sometimes used with plural masculine and feminine, usually at the beginning of a sentence, there was, τῆς δ᾽ ἦν τρεῖς κεφαλαί [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th-7th c.BC: Hesiodus Epicus “Theogonia” 321; (but in ἦν δ᾽ ἐρῳδιοί τε πολλοί 5th c.BC: Epicharmus Comicus 46, compare 59, +others, it may be taken as _Doric dialect_ _3rd.pers._ _plural_)]]; ἦν δ᾽ ἀμφίπλεκτοι κλίμακες [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Trachiniae” 520 (Lyric poetry)]]; ἦν ἄρα κἀκεῖνοι ταλακάρδιοι epigram cited in [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aeschines Orator 3.184; less frequently ἔστι, ἔστι δὲ μεταξὺ.. ἑπτὰ στάδιοι 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.26, compare 7.34; ἔστι.. ἄρχοντές τε καὶ δῆμος 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 463a]]; before dual Nouns, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Vespae” 58, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Gorgias” 500d.]]

__A.VI
ἔστι impersonal, with infinitive, it is possible, ἔστι γὰρ ἀμφοτέροισιν ὀνείδεα μυθήσασθαι [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 20.246; ἔστι μὲν εὕδειν, ἔστι δὲ τερπομένοισιν ἀκούειν 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 15.392]]; εἴ τί πού ἐστι (i.e. πιθέσθαι)[Refs 5th c.BC+ [4.193; τοιάδε.. ἐστὶν ἀκοῦσαι 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Prometheus Vinctus” 1055 (_anapaest meter_); ἔστι τεκμήρια ὁρᾶν 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 3.2.13, compare 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Ranae” 1163, 4th c.BC: Aeschines Orator 3.105, 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 18.272, 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Ἀθηναίων Πολιτεία” 53.6, etc.]]; so in imperative, optative, and subjunctive, ἔστω ἀποφέρεσθαι τῷ βουλομένῳ [Refs 8th c.BC+ [“IG” 12.10.7; μυρία ἂν εἴη λέγειν 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Politicus” 271e; ὅπως ἂν ᾖ δρᾶν “IG” 2.1054.91: more frequently in _negative_ clauses, 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 6.267, etc.]]; followed by ὥστε with infinitive, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Philoctetes” 656]]: with accusative et infinitive, ἁδόντα δ᾽ εἴη με τοῖς ἀγαθοῖς ὁμιλεῖν [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “P.” 2.96; ἔστιν ἐκπεσεῖν ἀρχῆς Δία 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Prometheus Vinctus” 757]]: sometimes not impersonal in this sense, θάλασσα δ᾽ οὐκέτ᾽ ἦν ἰδεῖν [Refs [[prev. author] “Pers.” 419.]]

__A.VI.b
ἔστω in argument, let it be granted, ἔστω τοῦτο ἀληθὲς εἶναι [Refs 4th c.BC+ [1st c.BC: Dionysius Halicarnassensis “de Compositione Verborum” 25; ἔστω σοι τοῦθ᾽ οὕτως 1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus 2.987b; ἔστω εἶναί τινα τοιοῦτον 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator Chr.74.24.]]

__B
most frequently, to be, the Copula connecting the predicate with the Subject, both being in the same case: hence, signify, import, τὸ γὰρ εἴρειν λέγειν ἐστίν [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Cratylus” 398d]]; especially in the phrase τοῦτ᾽ ἔστι, hoc est; Σκαιόλαν, ὅπερ ἐστὶ Λαϊόν [Refs 1st c.AD+ [1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus “Publicola” 17: with numerals, τὰ δὶς πέντε δέκα ἐστίν]] twice five are ten, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Memorabilia” 4.4.7]]; εἶναί τις or τι, to be somebody, something, be of some consequence, see at {τι; οὐδὲν εἶναι} [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 562d, etc.]]

__B.2
periphrastic with the Participle to represent the finite Verb: with perfect participle once in [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Homerus Epicus, τετληότες εἰμέν, for τετλήκαμεν, 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 5.873]]; so in Trag. and Attic dialect, ἦν τεθνηκώς, for ἐτεθνήκει, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Agamemnon” 869]]; ἔσται δεδορκώς[Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. work] 1179; εἰμὶ γεγώς 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Ajax” 1299; πεφυκός ἐστι 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Aves” 1473; δεδρακότες εἰσίν 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 3.68; κατακεκονότες ἔσεσθε 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 7.6.36]]: with aorist participle, once in [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Homerus Epicus, βλήμενος ἦν 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 4.211]]; so προδείσας εἰμί, οὐ σιωπήσας ἔσε; [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Tyrannus” 90, 1146, compare 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Supplices” 460]]: with present participle, ἦν προκείμενον [Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. author] “Pers.” 371; φεύγων Ὀρέστης ἐστίν [prev. author] “Ch.” 136; εἴην οὐκ ἂν εὖ φρονῶν 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Ajax” 1330]]; τί δ᾽ ἐστί.. φέρο; [Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. author] “OT” 991, compare 274, 708; λέγων ἐστίν τις 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Hecuba” 1179; ἦν τίς σ᾽ ὑβρίζων [prev. author] “HF” 313; πόρρω ἤδη εἶ πορευόμενος 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Lysis” 204b; βαδίζων εἰμί 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Ranae” 36; frequently in 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus, ἦσαν ἱέντες 1.57, +others; even εἰσὶ διάφοροι ἐόντες 3.49 (assuming variant):]] — if the _Article_ is joined with the Part., the noun is made emphatic, Κᾶρές εἰσι οἱ καταδέξαντες the persons who showed her were Carians, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. author] 1.171; αὐτὸς ἦν ὁ μαρτυρῶν 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Eumenides” 798; δόλος ἦν ὁ φράσας 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Electra” 197 (_anapaest meter_).]]

__C
εἶναι is frequently modified in sense by the addition of adverbs, or the cases of Nouns without or with Preps.:

__C.I
εἶναι with adverbs, where the adverb often merely represents a Noun and stands as the predicate, ἅλις δέ οἱ ἦσαν ἄρουραι [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 14.122, etc.]]; ἀκέων, ἀκήν εἶναι, to be silent,[Refs 8th c.BC+ [4.22, 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 2.82; σῖγα πᾶς ἔστω λεώς 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Hecuba” 532; διαγνῶναι χαλεπῶς ἦν ἄνδρα ἕκαστον 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 7.424]]; ἀσφαλέως ἡ κομιδὴ ἔσται will go on safely, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 4.134]]; ἐγγύς, πόρρω εἶναι, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 6.88, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Protagoras” 356e: frequently _impersonal_ with words implying good or ill fortune, Κουρήτεσσι κακῶς ἦν]] it fared ill with them, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 9.551; εὖ γὰρ ἔσται 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Medea” 89, compare 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Plutus” 1188, etc.; ἡδέως ἂν αὐτοῖς εἴη 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 59.30.]]

__C.II
with genitive, to express descent or extraction, πατρὸς δ᾽ εἴμ᾽ ἀγαθοῖο [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 21.109; αἵματός εἰς ἀγαθοῖο 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 4.611, compare 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 3.71, 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 2.71, etc.; πόλεως μεγίστης εἶ 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 7.3.19.]]

__C.II.b
to express the material of which a thing is made, ἡ κρηπίς ἐστι λίθων μεγάλων consists of.., [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.93; τῆς πόλιος ἐούσης δύο φαρσέων [prev. work] 186]]; τοιούτων ἔργων ἐστὶ ἡ τυραννίς is made up of.., [Refs [[prev. author] 5.92]].ή, etc.

__C.II.c
to express the class to which a person or thing belongs, εἶ γὰρ τῶν φίλων you are one of them, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Plutus” 345; ἐτύγχανε βουλῆς ὤν 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 3.70; ὅσοι ἦσαν τῶν προτέρων στρατιωτῶν [prev. author] 7.44; Κριτίας τῶν τριάκοντα ὤν 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Memorabilia” 1.2.31]]; ἔστι τῶν αἰσχρῶν it is in the class of disgraceful things, i. e. it is disgraceful, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 2.2.]]

__C.II.d
to express that a thing belongs to another, Τροίαν Ἀχαιῶν οὖσαν [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Agamemnon” 269; τὸ πεδίον ἦν μέν κοτε Χορασμίων 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 3.117, etc.]]: hence, to be of the party of, ἦσαν.. τινὲς μὲν φιλίππου, τινὲς δὲ τοῦ βελτίστου [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 9.56, compare 37.53]]; to be de pendent upon, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Antigone” 737, etc.]]; to be at the mercy of, ἔστι τοῦ λέγοντος, ἢν φόβους λέγῃ [Refs [[prev. author] “OT” 917.]]

__C.II.e
to express one's duty, business, custom, nature, and the like, οὔτοι γυναικός ἐστι 'tis not a woman's part, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Agamemnon” 940; τὸ ἐπιτιμᾶν παντὸς εἶναι 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 1.16]]; τὸ δὲ ναυτικὸν τέχνης ἐστίν is matter of art, requires art, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 1.142, compare 83.]]

__C.II.f
in LXX, to be occupied about, ἦσαν τοῦ θύειν [LXX.2Ch.30.17]; ἔσεσθαι, with genitive, to be about to, ἐσόμεθα τοῦ σῶσαί σε [LXX.2Ki.10.11.]

__C.III
with the dative, ἐστί μοι I have, frequently in [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Homerus Epicus, etc.]]

__C.III.2
with two datives., σφίσι τε καὶ Ἀθηναίοισι εἶναι οὐδὲν πρῆγμα that they and the Athenians have nothing to do one with another, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 5.84; μηδὲν εἶναι σοὶ καὶ φιλίππῳ πρᾶγμα 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 18.283]]; more shortly, σοί τε καὶ τούτοισι πρήγμασι τί ἐστ; [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 5.33]]; τί τῷ νόμῳ καὶ τῇ βασάν; [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 29.36]]; τί ἐμοὶ καὶ σο; Latin quid tecum est mihi? [NT.Mark.5.7, etc.]; also ἐμοὶ οὐδὲν πρὸς τοὺς τοιούτους (i.e. ἐστίν) [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Isocrates Orator 4.12; ἐν οἷς πρὸς τοὺς ἐναντίους ἐστὶ τῷ δήμῳ 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 18.278]]; ἔσται αὐτῳ πρὸς τὸν θεόν, in tomb inscriptions, [Refs [“JHS” 18.113, etc.]]

__C.III.3
with ἄσμενος, βουλόμενος, etc., added, ἐμοὶ δέ κεν ἀσμένῳ εἴη 'twould be to my delight, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 14.108; οὐκ ἂν σφίσι βουλομένοις εἶναι 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 7.35; προσδεχομένῳ [prev. author] 6.46; θέλοντι 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Tyrannus” 1356 (Lyric poetry); ἡδομένοις 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Laches” 187c.]]

__C.IV
with Preps., εἶναι ἀπό τινος, ={εἶναί τινος}[Refs 5th c.BC+ [(above 11.a), 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Memorabilia” 1.6.9; εἰσὶν ἀπ᾽ ἐναντίων αὗται πραγμάτων 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Philebus” 12d]]; but εἶναι ἀπ᾽ οἴκου to be away from.., [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 1.99.]]

__C.IV.2
εἶναι ἔκ τινος to be sprung from, εἴμ᾽ ἐκ Παιονίης, Μυρμιδόνων ἔξ εἰμι, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 21.154, 24.397, etc.]]; ἔστιν ἐξ ἀνάγκης it is of necessity, i. e. necessary, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Sophista” 256d.]]

__C.IV.3
εἶναι ἐν.. to be in a certain state, ἐν εὐπαθείῃσι [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.22]]; ἐν ἀθυμία, etc., [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 6.46, etc.; ἐν ταραχαῖς 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 18.218]]; εἶναι ἐν ἀξιώματι to be in esteem, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 1.130]]; οἱ ἐν τέλεϊ ἐόντες those in office, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 3.18, etc.]]; but εἶναι ἐν τέχνῃ, ἐν φιλοσοφία to be engaged in.., [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Tyrannus” 562, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Phaedo” 59a.]]

__C.IV.3.b
ἐν σοί ἐστι it depends on thee, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 6.109, 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Philoctetes” 963; ἐν σοὶ γάρ ἐσμεν [prev. author] “OT” 314; so also ἐπί τινι [prev. author] “Ph.” 1003, 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 1.6.2, etc.]]

__C.IV.4
εἶναι διά.., much like{εἶναι ἐν}.., εἶναι διὰ φόβου, ={φοβεῖσθαι}, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 6.34]]; εἶναι δι᾽ ὄχλου, ={ὀχληρὸν εἶναι}, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. author] 1.73; εἶναι διὰ μόχθων 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 1.6.25]]; εἶναι δι᾽ αἰτίας, ={αἰτιᾶσθαι}, [Refs 1st c.BC+ [1st c.BC: Dionysius Halicarnassensis 1.70]]; Geometry texts, pass through, διὰ τᾶς ἑτέρας διαμέτρου ἐόντος τοῦ ἐπιπέδου [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [3rd c.BC: Archimedes Geometra “περὶ κωνοειδέων καὶ σφαιροειδέων” 20.]]

__C.IV.5
εἶναι ἐφ᾽ ἑαυτῆς to be by oneself, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 25.23]]; εἶναι ἐπὶ ὀνόματος to bear a name, [Refs [[prev. author] 39.21]]; εἶναι ἐπὶ τοῖς πράγμασιν to be engaged in.., [Refs [[prev. author] 2.12]]; εἶναι ἐπί τινα to be against him, [Refs [[prev. author] 6.33]]; εἶναι ἐφ᾽ ἑξήκοντα στάδια to reach sixty stadia, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 4.6.11]]; εἶναι ἐπὶ τὰς ἁφάς pass through the points of contact, [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd c.AD: Apollonius Biographus Perg. “Con.” 4.1]]; εἶναι ἐπί τινι, see above 3 b.

__C.IV.6
εἶναι πρός τινος to be in one's favour, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 4.10, 29, etc.]]; to suit, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 1.2.11, etc.]]; εἶναι πρός τινι engaged in, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Phaedo” 84c, 2nd-3rd c.AD: Philostratus Sophista “Vita Apollonii” 5.31]]; πρὸς τοῖς ἰδίοις mind one's own affairs, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Politica” 1309a6, “Ath.” 16.3; εἶναι πρὸς τὸ κωλύειν 2nd c.BC: Polybius Historicus 1.26.3]]; πρὸς τὸ πονεῖν[Refs 5th c.BC+ [Teles p.46 H.; εἶναι περί τι 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 3.5.7, etc.]]

__C.IV.7
εἶναι παρά τινι or τινα, = παρειναι, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. author] “Cyr.” 6.2.15, 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 8.140.ά]] (assuming variant).

__C.IV.8
εἶναι ὑπό τινα or τινι to be subject to.., [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Historia Graeca (Hellenica)” 5.2.17 (assuming variant), 6.2.4.]]

__C.IV.9
περὶ τούτων ἐστίν that is the question, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-3rd c.BC: Menander Comicus “Ἐπιτρέποντες” 30.]]

__C.IV.10
εἶναι ἀπό.., in Geometry texts, to be constructed upon, [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [3rd c.BC: Archimedes Geometra “περὶ σφαίρας καὶ κυλίνδρου” 2.9, “Con.Sph.” 7.]]

__D
ἐστί is very frequently omitted, mostly in the present indicative before certain predicates, as ἀνάγκη, ἄξιον, δυνατόν, εἰκός, ἕτοιμον, οἷόν τε, ῥᾴδιον, χρεών, etc., and after the neuter of Verbals in -τέος, and such forms as θαυμαστὸν ὅσον: less frequently with other persons and moods, εἰμί omitted, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Tyrannus” 92, “Aj.” 813]]; εἶ, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 4.206]]; ἐσμέν, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Antigone” 634]]; ἐστέ, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 10.463]]; εἰσί, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Tyrannus” 499 (Lyric poetry), “IG” 2.778 B]]; subjunctive ᾖ, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 14.376, 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Hippolytus” 659, 5th c.BC: Antipho Orator 5.32]]; optative εἴη, [Refs [“IG” 22.1183.12]]; imperfect ἦν, [Refs [[prev. work]2.778 B]]; future ἔσονται, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 14.394.]]

__E
the Inf. frequently seems redundant,

__E.1
in phrases implying power or will to do a thing, ἑκὼν εἶναι (see. ἑκών) κατὰ δύναμιν εἶναι [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Isaeus Orator 2.32; εἰς δύναμιν εἶναι 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Politicus” 300c]]; τὸ ἐπ᾽ ἐκείνοις εἶναι, quantum in illis esset, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 8.48, 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Historia Graeca (Hellenica)” 3.5.9, compare 5th c.BC: Lysias Orator 13.58; τὸ ἐπὶ σφᾶς εἶναι 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 4.28; τὸ κατὰ τοῦτον εἶναι 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 1.6.9; κατὰ τοῦτο εἶναι 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Protagoras” 317a]]; τὸ τήμερον, τὸ νῦν εἶναι, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [[prev. author] “Cra.” 396e, “La.” 201c, Theopomp. Comedy texts 98, Decrees cited in 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Ἀθηναίων Πολιτεία” 31.2, etc.]]

__E.2
after Verbs of naming or choosing, σοφιστὴν ὀνομάζουσι τὸν ἄνδρα εἶναι [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Protagoras” 311e; σύμμαχόν μιν εἵλοντο εἶναι 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 8.134]]; of giving, δῶκε ξεινήϊον εἶναι [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 11.20.]]

__F
imperfect ἦνissts. used where other languages take the present,

__F.1
after ἄρα, to express a fact which is and has always been the same, δέρμα δὲ ἀνθρώπου.. ἦν ἄρα σχεδὸν δερμάτων πάντων λαμπρότατον human skin then it appears is.., [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 4.64; Κύπρις οὐκ ἄρ᾽ ἦν θεός 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Hippolytus” 359]]; ὡς ἄρ᾽ ἦσθ᾽ ἐμὸς πατὴρ ὀρθῶς[Refs 3rd c.BC+ [[prev. work] 1169; ἦ πολύμοχθον ἄρ᾽ ἦν γένος.. ἁμερίων [prev. author] “IA” 1330; ἦ στωμύλος ἦσθα 3rd c.BC: Theocritus Poeta Bucolicus 5.79]]; so also when there is reference to a past thought, τουτὶ τί ἦ; what is this? [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Acharnenses” 157, compare 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Cratylus” 387c: so in the Aristotelian formula τὸ τί ἦν εἶναι (“APo.” 82b38, +others)]], used to express the essential nature of a thing, where τί ἦν (for ἐστί) takes the place of the dative in such phrases as τὸ ἀγαθῷ εἶναι, τὸ μεγέθει εἶναι, [Refs [“APr.” 67b12, “de An.” 429b10.]]

__G
ἐγώ εἰμι, in [LXX, pleonastic for ἐγώ, ἐγώ εἰμι οὐχ ἥμαρτον LXX.Judg.11.27, compare 6.18; also ἔσται πᾶς ἀποκτενεῖ με LXX.Gen.4.14.]

deep_entry:
Abbott-Smith / STEPBible (TBESG)
εἰ,
conjunctive particle, used in conditions and in indirect   questions.
__I. Conditional, if;
__1. with indic, expressing a general assumption;
__(a) pres.: before indic, pres., Mat.11:14, Rom.8:25, al.; before imperat., Mrk.4:23  9:22, Jhn.15:18, 1Co.7:9, al.; before fut. indic., Luk.16:31, Rom.8:11, al.; before pf. or aor., with negation in apodosis, Mat.12:26, Rom.4:14, al.; similarly, before impf., Luk.17:6, Jhn.8:39; before quæst., Mat.6:23, Jhn.5:47  7:23 8:46, 1Pe.2:20;
__(b) fut.: Mat.26:33, 1Pe.2:20;
__(with) pf.: Jhn.11:12, Rom.6:5, al.;
__(d) aor.: Luk.16:11  19:8, Jhn.13:32, 18:23, Rev.20:15, al.
__2. Where the assumption is certain = ἐπεί: Mat.12:28, Jhn.7:4, Rom.5:17, al.
__3. Of an unfulfilled condition, with indic, impf., aor. or plpf., before ἄν, with imp. or aor. (see: ἄν, I, i).
__4. C. indic., after verbs denoting wonder, etc., sometimes, but not always, coupled with an element of doubt: Mrk.15:44, 1Jn.3:13, al.
__5. C. indic., as in LXX (Num.14:3o, 1Ki.14:45, al. = Heb. אִם), in oaths, with the formula of imprecation understood in a suppressed apodosis (WM, 627; Burton, §272): Mrk.8:12, Heb.3:11" (LXX)  4:3 (LXX).
__6. Rarely (cl.) with optative, to express a merely possible condition: Act.24:19 27:39, 1Co.14:10 15:37, I Pe3:14, 17.
__II. Interrogative, if, whether.
__1. As in cl., in indir. questions after verbs of seeing, asking, knowing, saying, etc.: with indic. pres., Mat.26:63, Mrk.15:36, Act.19:2, 2Co.13:5, al.; fut., Mrk.3:2, Act.8:22, al.; aor., Mrk.15:44, 1Co.1:16, al.; with subjc. aor. (M, Pr., 194), Php.3:12.
__2. As in LXX (= Heb. אִם and interrog. הֲ, Gen.17:17, al.; see WM, 639f.; Viteau, i, 22), in direct questions: Mrk.8:23 (Tr., WH, txt.), Luk.13:23, 22:49, Act.19:2, al.
__III. With other particles.
__1. εἰ ἄρα, εἴγε, εἰ δὲ μήγε, see: ἄρα, γε.
__2. εἰ δὲ καί, but if also: Luk.11:18; but even if, 1Co.4:7, 2Co.4:3 11:16.
__3. εἰ δὲ μή, but if not, but if otherwise: Mrk.2:21, 22 Jhn.14:2, Rev.2:5, al.
__4. εἰ καί, if even, if also, although: Mrk.14:29, Luk.11:8, 1Co.7:21, 2Co.4:16, Php.2:17, al.
__5. καὶ εἰ, even if, see: καί
__6. εἰ μή, if not, unless, except, but only: Mat.24:22, Mrk.2:26 6:5, Jhn.9:33, 1Co.7:17 (only), Gal.1:19 (cf. ἐὰν μή, 2:16; see Hort., Ja., xvi); ἐκτὸς εἰ μή, pleonastic (Bl., §65, 6), 1Co.14:5 15:2, 1Ti.5:19.
__7. εἰ μήν = cl. ἦ μήν (M, Pr., 46), in oaths, surely (Eze.33:27, al.): Heb.6:14.
__8. εἴ πως, if haply: Act.27:12, Rom.1:10.
__9. εἴτε . . . εἴτε, whether . . . or; Rom.12:6-8, 1Co.3:22 13:8, al.
(AS)

LSJ / STEPBible (TFLSJ)
Included with:  γε,
Doric dialect and Boeotian dialect γα, enclitic Particle, giving emphasis to the word or words which it follows.

__I
with single words, at least, at any rate, but often only to be rendered by italics in writing, or emphasis in pronunciation: τὸ γὰρ.. σιδήρου γε κράτος ἐστίν such is the power of iron, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 9.393]]; εἴ που πτωχῶν γε θεοὶ.. εἰσίν if the poor have any gods to care for them,[Refs [17.475; μάλιστά γε 4.366]]; ὅ γ᾽ ἐνθάδε λεώς at any rate the people here, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Coloneus” 42, etc.: with negatives, οὐ δύο γε]] not even two, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 5.303, 20.286]]; οὔκουν φθόγγος γε not the least sound, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Iphigenia Aulidensis” 9.]]

__I.2
with Pronouns: with pronoun of 1st pers. [Refs 8th c.BC+ [4th c.AD: Perses Epigrammaticus so closely joined, that the accent is changed, in ἔγωγε, ἔμοιγε (also ἔγωγα _Laconian dialect_, but ἐγώνγα, ἰώνγα _Boeotian dialect_): in 8th c.BC: Homerus Epicus frequently with _Article_ used as _pronoun_, see at {ὅ γε}: with _demonstrative_ Pronouns, κεῖνός γε, τοῦτό γε, etc.: in Comedy texts coalescing with -ί final, αὑτηγί 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Acharnenses” 784]]; τουτογί, ταυταγί, etc., [Refs 8th c.BC+ [[prev. author] “V.” 781, “Pax” 1057, etc. (but ἐνγεταυθί “Th.” 646): after possess. Pronouns, ἐμόν γε θυμόν 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 20.425, etc.: frequently after _relative_ Pronouns, ὅς γε, οἵ γε, etc., οἵ γέ σου καθύβρισαν 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Philoctetes” 1364; ὅς γ᾽ ἐξέλυσας δασμόν [prev. author] “OT” 35, etc.]]; ὅσον γε χρῄζεις even as much as..,[Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. work] 365; οἷόν γέ μοι φαίνεται 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 329a]]: rarely with interrogative Pronouns, τίνα γε.. εἶπας ;[Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Troades” 241]]; ποίου γε τούτου πλήν γ᾽ Ὀδυσσέως ἐρεῖς ; [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Philoctetes” 441.]]

__I.3
after Conjunctions, to emphasize the modification or condition introduced by the subjoined clause, πρίν γε, before at least, sometimes repeated, οὐ μὲν.. ὀΐω πρίν γ᾽ ἀποπαύσεσθαι, πρίν γε.. αἵματος ἆσαι Ἀρῆα [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 5.288, compare 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 2.127]]; πρὶν ἄν γε or πρίν γ᾽ ἄν, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Equites” 961, “Ra.” 78, etc.; ὅτε γε 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Phaedo” 84e; ὁπότε γε 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Coloneus” 1699; ἐπεί γε 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 1.3.9; ἐπειδή γε 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 6.18; ὅπου γε 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 2.3.11]]; εἴ γε, ἐάν γε, if that is to say, if really, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 6.18, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Phaedrus” 252c]]; also simply to lay stress on the condition, κἄν γε μὴ λέγω and if I do not.., [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Acharnenses” 317]]; εἴπερ γε if at any rate, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 7.16.γ, 143]], etc.; ὥστε γε (variant{ὥς γε}), with infinitive, so far at least as to.., [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Phaedrus” 230b; ὥς γ᾽ ἐμοὶ χρῆσθαι κριτῇ 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Alcestis” 801]]; ὥς γε or ὥσπερ γε as at least, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Antigone” 570, “OT” 715, etc.]]:—γε may follow τε, when τε is closely attached to the preceding word, ὡς οἷόν τέ γε μάλιστα [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Memorabilia” 4.5.2, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 412b; ἐάντε γε [prev. author] “Plt.” 293d; οἵ τέ γε [prev. author] “Grg.” 454e:—for its use in opposed or disjunctive clauses, see below 11.3.]]

__I.4
after other Particles, καὶ μὴν.. γε, οὐ μὴν.. γε, with words intervening, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Memorabilia” 1.4.12, 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Alcestis” 518, etc.]]; after ἄν in apodosi, when preceded by οὐ or καί, [Refs [[prev. author] “Ph.” 1215, “Or.” 784]]; ἄταρ.. γε but yet, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Acharnenses” 448]]; καίτοι γε, see at {καί το; ἀλλά γε} (without intervening words) is falsa lectio in [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Hp.Ma.” 287b (to be read ἀλλ᾽ ἄγε), “R.” 331b (ἀλλά γε ἕν codices, ἀλλὰ ἕν γε 5th c.AD: Stobaeus, Joannes)]]; ἀλλά γε δή uncertain in [Refs 1st c.AD+ [[prev. author] “Phdr.” 262a; later, 1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus 2.394c, 2nd-3rd c.AD: Aelianus “De Natura Animalium - Ar.Byzantine Epit.” 10.49 codices: but,]]

__I.5
when preceding other Particles, γε commonly refers to the preceding word, while the Particle retains its own force: but sometimes modifies the sense of the following Particle, γε μήν nevertheless, πάντως γε μήν [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Equites” 232, compare 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Electra” 754, 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus, etc.]]; Epic dialect and Ionic dialect γε μέν [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 2.703, 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 4.195, 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 7.152; γε μὲν δή 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Agamemnon” 661, 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Trachiniae” 484; γε μέντοι 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Theaetetus” 164a, 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 2.3.9, etc.: γε δή]] frequently strengthens an assertion, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Prometheus Vinctus” 42, 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 2.62, etc.; οἰόμεθά γε δή 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Euthydemus” 275a (compare also 11.1)]]; γέ τοι, implying that the assertion is the least that one can say, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Vespae” 934, “Pl.” 424, 1041, etc.; γέ τοι 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Gorgias” 447b; γέ τοι δή 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Tyrannus” 1171, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Phaedrus” 264b; γέ τοί που [prev. author] “Lg.” 888e; γε δήπου [prev. author] “Phd.” 94a, etc.]]; γέ που at all events, any how, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Acharnenses” 896, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 607d, 478a, etc.]]; for γε οὖν, see at {γοῦν}.

__II
exercising an influence over the whole clause:

__II.1
epexegetic, namely, that is, Διός γε διδόντος that is if God grant it, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 1.390]]; κλῦθι, Ποσείδαον.., εἰ ἐτεόν γε σός εἰμι if indeed I am really thine, [Refs [9.529: hence to limit, strengthen or amplify a general assertion, ἀνὴρ.. ὅστις πινυτός γε]] any man—at least any wise man, [Refs [1.229]]; frequently preceded by καί, usually with words intervening, ἦ μὴν κελεύσω κἀπιθωΰξω γε πρός ay and besides that.., [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Prometheus Vinctus” 73]]; παρῆσάν τινες καὶ πολλοί γε some, ay and a great many, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Phaedo” 58d; καὶ γελοίως γε [prev. author] “R.” 531a]]; frequently with the last term in an enumeration, ταύτῃ ἄρα.. πρακτέον καὶ γυμναστέον καὶ ἐδεστέον γε καὶ ποτέον [[prev. author] “Cri.” 47b; ὄψεις τε καὶ ἀκοαὶ καὶ.. καὶ ἡδοναί γε δή [prev. author] “Tht.” 156b; repeated, συνήγαγόν μοι καί γε ἀργύριον καί γε χρυσίον LXX.Eccl.2.8]; rarely without intervening words, καί γε ὁ θάνατος διὰ τὴν μοίρην ἔλαχεν [NT+5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Hippocrates Medicus “περὶ ἑπταμήνου” 9, compare 5th c.BC: Lysias Orator 11.7 codices; καί γε.. ἐκχεῶ NT.Act.2.18: hence,]]

__II.2
in dialogue, in answers where something is added to the statement of the previous speaker, as ἔπεμψέ τίς σοι.. κρέα; Answ. καλῶς γε ποιῶν yes and quite right too, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Acharnenses” 1049]]; κενὸν τόδ᾽ ἄγγος, ἢ στέγει τι; Answ. σά γ᾽ ἔνδυτα.. yes indeed, your clothes, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Ion” 1412]]; οὕτω γὰρ ἂν μάλιστα δηχθείη πόσις. Answ. σὺ δ᾽ ἂν γένοιο γ᾽ ἀθλιωτάτη γυνή yes truly, and you.., [Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. author] “Med.” 817, compare 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Tyrannus” 680, etc.]]; πάνυ γε yes certainly, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Euthyphro” 8e, etc.]]; οὕτω γέ πως yes somehowso, [Refs [[prev. author] “Tht.” 165c]]; sometimes preceded by καί, καὶ οὐδέν γ᾽ ἄτοπον yes and no wonder, [Refs [[prev. work] 142b, compare d, 147e]]; sometimes ironically, εὖ γε κηδεύεις πόλιν [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Iphigenia Taurica” 1212.]]

__II.3
to heighten a contrast or opposition,

__II.3.a
after conditional clauses, εἰ μὲν δὴ σύ γ᾽.., τῷ κε Ποσειδάων γε.. if you do so, then at all events Poseidon will.., [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 15.49]] {γέα}; ἐπεὶ πρὸς τοῦτο σιωπᾶν ἥδιόν σοι.. τόδε γε εἰπέ at any rate tell me this, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 5.5.20; εἰ μὴ τὸ ὅλον, μέρος γ᾽ ἐπιβάλλει 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 18.272:—sometimes in the protasis, εἰ γὰρ μὴ ἑκόντες γε.. ἀλλ᾽ ἀέκοντας.. 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 4.120.]]

__II.3.b
in disjunctive sentences to emphasize an alternative, ἤτοι κεῖνόν γε.. δεῖ ἀπόλλυσθαι ἢ σέ.. [Refs 8th c.BC+ [[prev. author] 1.11; ἤτοι κρίνομέν γε ἢ ἐνθυμούμεθα ὀρθῶς τὰ πράγματα 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 2.40; πατὴρ δ᾽ ἐμός.. ζώει ὅ γ᾽ ἢ τέθνηκε 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 2.131, compare 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 10.504]]: also in the second clause, εἰπέ μοι, ἠὲ ἑκὼν ὑποδάμνασαι ἤ σέ γε λαοὶ ἐχθαίρουσι [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 3.214, compare 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 7.10.θ, 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Tyrannus” 1098f]]

__II.4
in exclamations, etc., ὥς γε μή ποτ᾽ ὤφελον λαβεῖν uncertain in [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Iphigenia Aulidensis” 70, compare 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Coloneus” 977, “Ph.” 1003, 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Acharnenses” 93, 836, etc.]]; in oaths, οὔτοι μὰ τὴν Δήμητρά γ᾽ variant in [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Equites” 698; μὰ τὸν Ποσειδῶ γ᾽ οὐδέποτ᾽ [prev. author] “Ec.” 748; καὶ ναὶ μὰ Δία γε 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Apologia Socratis” 20; καὶ νὴ Δία γε 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Equites” 1350, 1st-2nd c.AD: Dio Chrysostomus Sophista 17.4, 2nd c.AD: Lucianus Sophista “Merc.Cond.” 28, 4th c.AD: Libanius Sophista “Orationes” 11.59, etc.: with words intervening, καὶ νὴ Δί᾽, ὦ ἄνδρες Ἀθηναῖοι, ἕτεροί γε.. 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 13.16; νὴ Δία, ὦ Ἀθηναῖοι, ὥρα γε ὑμῖν 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Historia Graeca (Hellenica)” 7.1.37]]; merely in strong assertions, τίς ἂν φιλέοντι μάχοιτ; ἄφρων δὴ κεῖνός γέ.. [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 8.209, etc.]]

__II.5
implying concession, εἶμί γε well then I will go (in apodosi), [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Hercules Furens” 861; δρᾶ γ᾽ εἴ τι δράσεις [prev. author] “IA” 817, compare “Andr.” 239.]]

__III
γε frequently repeated in protasis and apodosis, as πρίν γε.., πρίν γε, see[Refs 5th c.BC+ [above 1.3; εἰ μή γε.. τινὶ μείζονι, τῇ γε παρούσῃ ἀτιμίᾳ 5th c.BC: Lysias Orator 31.29]]; even in the same clause, οὐδέν γ᾽ ἄλλο πλήν γε καρκίνους [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Vespae” 1507, compare 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.187, 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Phoenissae” 554, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 335b, “Grg.” 502a.]]

__IV
POSITION: γε normally follows the word which it limits; but is frequently placed immediately after the Article, as ὅ γε πόλεμος [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 1.66, etc.]]; or the preposition, κατά γε τὸν σὸν λόγον [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 3.1.15; ἔν γε ταῖς Θήβαις 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Tyrannus” 1380; or δέ, νῦν δέ γε 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Theaetetus” 144e]]; τὸ δέ γε[Refs [[prev. work] 164b; δοῖμεν δέ γέ που ἄν [prev. author] “R.” 607d, compare “Phd.” 94a, etc.]]; frequently in retorts, ἁμές ποκ᾽ ἦμες ἄλκιμοι νεανίαι. Answ. ἁμὲς δέ γ᾽ εἰμές [Refs [“Carmina Popularia” 18]]; οὐκ οἶδ᾽ ὅτι λέγεις. Answ. ἡ γραῦς δέ γε οἶδ᾽, ὡς ἐγῷμαι [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-3rd c.BC: Menander Comicus “Ἐπιτρέποντες” 577, compare 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Septem contra Thebas” 1031, etc.]]

short_definition: but if not — μήγε, see: γε.
root_and_cognates: LSJ-hänvisningar: οὐ, εἰ μὴ ἔκνιζε, καί, ὡς, ἄρα, εἰ δή, εἴπερ, γέ
deep_entry:
Abbott-Smith / STEPBible (TBESG)
μήγε, see: γε.
γε, enclitic postpositive particle, rarer in κοινή than in cl., giving special prominence to the word to which it is attached, distinguishing it as the least or the most important (Thayer, see word),
indeed, at least, even (but not always translatable into English);
__1. used alone: Luk.11:8 18:5 Rom.8:32.
__2. More frequently with other particles: αλλά γε, Luk.24:21, 1Co.9:2; ἄρα γε, Mat.7:20 17:26, Act.17:27; ἆρά γε, Act.8:30; εἴ γε (Rec. εἴγε), 2Co.5:3, Gal.3:4, Eph.3:2 4:21, Col.1:23 (see Meyer, Ellic., on Ga, Eph, ll. with; Lft., on Ga, Col, ll. with); εἰ δὲ μήγε, following an affirmation, Mat.6:1, Luk.10:6 13:9; a negation, Mat.9:17, Luk.5:36, 37 14:32, 2Co.11:16; καί γε (Rec. καίγε, cl. καὶ . . . γε), Luk.19:42 (WH om.), Act.2:18 17:27; καίτοιγε (L καίτοι γε, Tr. καί τοι γε), Jhn.4:2; μενοῦνγε (see see word); μήτι γε, see: μήτι; ὄφελόν, 1Co.4:8.
† (AS)
