Included with:  εἰ,
Attic dialect-Ionic dialect and [Refs 4th c.AD+ [4th c.AD(?): Arcadius Grammaticus (for εἰκ, see below 11 ad [near the start]), = _Doric dialect_ and _Aeolic dialect_ αἰ, αἰκ (which see), 5th c.AD: Cypria]] ἤ [Refs [“Inscription Cyprian dialect” 135.10 H., both εἰ and αἰ]] in Epic dialect:— Particle used interjectionally with imperative and to express a wish, but usually either in conditions, if, or in indirect questions, whether. In the former use its regular negative is μ; in the latter, οὐ.

__A
INTERJECTIONALLY, in [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Homerus Epicus]], come now! with imperative, εἰ δὲ.. ἄκουσον [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 9.262; εἰ δὲ καὶ αὐτοὶ φευγόντων [prev. work] 46; most frequently with ἄγε (which see), 1.302, +others]]

__A.2
in wishes, with optative, ἀλλ᾽ εἴ τις.. καλέσειεν [Refs [10.111, compare 24.74]]; so later, εἴ μοι ξυνείη μοῖρα [Refs 8th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Tyrannus” 863 (Lyric poetry); εἴ μοι γένοιτο φθόγγος ἐν βραχίοσιν 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Hecuba” 836: more frequently followed by γάρ, αἲ γὰρ δὴ οὕτως εἴη 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 4.189, +others; εἰ γὰρ γενοίμην ἀντὶ σοῦ νεκρός 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Hippolytus” 1410; εἰ γὰρ γένοιτο 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 6.1.38; εἰ γὰρ ἐν τούτῳ εἴη 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Protagoras” 310d]]; of unattained wishes, in [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Homerus Epicus only with _optative_, εἰ γὰρ ἐγὼν.. Διὸς πάϊς αἰγιόχοιο εἴην 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 13.825; Ζεῦ πάτερ, αἰ γὰρ ἐμὸς πόσις εἴη 7th c.BC: Alcman Lyricus 29]]; later with past tenses of indicative, εἰ γάρ μ᾽ ὑπὸ γῆν.. ἧκεν [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Prometheus Vinctus” 152 (_anapaest meter_)]]; εἰ γὰρ τοσαύτην δύναμιν εἶχον ὥστε.. [Refs 8th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Alcestis” 1072: twice in 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” with]]infinitive (compare the use of infinitive in commands), αἰ γὰρ τοῖος ἐὼν.. ἐμὸς γαμβρὸς καλέεσθαι [Refs [7.311, compare 24.376.]]

__A.2.b
εἴθε, Epic dialect αἴθε, is frequently used in wishes in the above constructions, εἴθε οἱ αὐτῷ Ζεὺς ἀγαθὸν τελέσειεν [Refs 8th c.BC+ [2.33; εἴθ᾽ ὣς ἡβώοιμι 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 7.157; ἰὼ γᾶ, εἴθ᾽ ἔμ᾽ ἐδέξω 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Agamemnon” 1537 (Lyric poetry); εἴθε σοι, ὦ Περίκλεις, τότε συνεγενόμην 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Memorabilia” 1.2.46]]: later with infinitive, γαίης χθαμαλωτέρη εἴθε.. κεῖσθαι [Refs 1st c.BC+ [“Anthologia Graeca” 9.284 (1st c.BC-1st c.AD: Crinagoras Epigrammaticus).]]

__A.2.c
εἰ γάρ, εἴθε are also used with ὤφελον (Epic dialect ὤφελλον), of past unattained wishes, αἴθ᾽ ὤφελλες στρατοῦ ἄλλου σημαίνειν [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 14.84]]; εἰ γὰρ ὤφελον [κατιδεῖν] [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 432c.]]

__A.2.d
followed by a clause expressing a consequence of the fulfilment of the wish, αἰ γὰρ τοῦτο.. ἔπος τετελεσμένον εἴη· τῷ κε τάχα γνοίης.. [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 15.536, compare 17.496, +others]]; sometimes hard to distinguish from εἰ in conditions (which may be derived from this use), εἴ μοί τι πίθοιο, τό κεν πολὺ κέρδιον εἴη [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 7.28.]]

__B
IN CONDITIONS, if:

__B.I
with INDIC.,

__B.I.1
with all tenses (for future, see below [Refs [2), to state a condition, with nothing implied as to its fulfilment, εἰ δ᾽ οὕτω τοῦτ᾽ ἐστίν, ἐμοὶ μέλλει φίλον εἶναι but]]if this is so, it will be.., [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 1.564]]: any form of the Verb may stand in apodosi, εἰ θεοί τι δρῶσιν αἰσχρόν, οὐκ εἰσὶν θεοί [Refs 8th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Fragmenta” 292.7; εἰ δοκεῖ, πλέωμεν 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Philoctetes” 526; εἰ Φαῖδρον ἀγνοῶ, καὶ ἐμαυτοῦ ἐπιλέλησμαι 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Phaedrus” 228a; κάκιστ᾽ ἀπολοίμην, Ξανθίαν εἰ μὴ φιλῶ 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Ranae” 579, compare 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 17.475; εἰ θεοῦ ἦν, οὐκ ἦν αἰσχροκερδής· εἰ δ᾽ αἰσχροκερδής, οὐκ ἦν θεοῦ 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 408c; εἰ ταῦτα λέγων διαφθείρω τοὺς νέους, ταῦτ᾽ ἂν εἴη βλαβερά [prev. author] “Ap.” 30b, compare 25b]]; εἰ οὗτοι ὀρθῶς ἀπέστησαν, ὑμεῖς ἂν οὐ χρεὼν ἄρχοιτε if these were right in their revolt, (it would follow that) you rule when you have no right, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 3.40.]]

__B.I.1.b
to express a general condition, if ever, whenever, sometimes with present, εἴ τις δύο ἢ καὶ πλείους τις ἡμέρας λογίζεται, μάταιός ἐστιν [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Trachiniae” 943]]: with imperfect, εἴ τίς τι ἠρώτα ἀπεκρίνοντο [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 7.10]]: rarely with aorist, [Refs 1st c.BC+ [1st c.BC: Diodorus Siculus Historicus 31.26.1, 2nd c.AD: Sextus Empiricus Philosophus “Πυρρώνειοι ὑποτυπώσεις” 1.84; compare 111.2.]]

__B.I.2
with future (much less frequently than ἐάν with subjunctive), either to express a future supposition emphatically, εἰ φθάσομεν τοὺς πολεμίους κατακαίνοντες οὐδεὶς ἡμῶν ἀποθανεῖται [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 7.1.19; εἰ μὴ βοηθήσετε οὐ περιέσται τἀκεῖ 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 6.91; εἰ αὕτη ἡ πόλις ληφθήσεται, ἔχεται ἡ πᾶσα Σικελία [prev. passage];]] in threats or warnings, εἰ μὴ καθέξεις γλῶσσαν ἔσται σοι κακά [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Fragmenta” 5; εἰ τιμωρήσεις Πατρόκλῳ, αὐτὸς ἀποθανῇ 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Apologia” 28c, compare 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 28.21: or,]]

__B.I.2.b
to express a present intention or expectation, αἶρε πλῆκτρον εἰ μαχεῖ if you mean to fight, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Aves” 759; ἐγὼ μὲν οὐκ ἀνήρ.. εἰ ταῦτ᾽ ἀνατεὶ τῇδε κείσεται κράτη 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Antigone” 485, compare 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 1.61, 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Hecuba” 863.]]

__B.I.3
with historical tenses, implying that the condition is or was unfulfilled.

__B.I.3.a
with imperfect, referring to present time or to continued or repeated action in past time (in [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Homerus Epicus always the latter, 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 24.715, +others): ταῦτα οὐκ ἂν ἐδύναντο ποιεῖν, εἰ μὴ διαίτῃ μετρίᾳ ἐχρῶντο they would not be able to do this (as they do)]], if they did not live an abstemious life, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 1.2.16, compare 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 489b; οὐκ ἂν νήσων ἐκράτει, εἰ μή τι καὶ ναυτικὸν εἶχεν he (from Agamemnon)]] would not have been master of islands, if he had not had also some naval force, [Refs 7th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 1.9; αἰ δ᾽ ἦχες ἔσλων ἴμερον ἢ κάλων.. αἴδως κεν.. ἦχεν 7th-6th c.BC: Sappho Lyrica 28]]; εἰ ἦσαν ἄνδρες ἀγαθοὶ.. οὐκ ἄν ποτε ταῦτα ἔπασχον if they had been good men, they would never have suffered as they did, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Gorgias” 516e, compare 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Memorabilia” 1.1.5]]; εἰ γὰρ ἐγὼ τάδε ᾔδἐ.. οὐκ ἂν ὑπεξέφυγε if I had known this.., [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 8.366.]]

__B.I.3.b
with aorist referring to past time, εἰ μὴ ἔφυσε θεὸς μέλι.. ἔφασκον γλύσσονα σῦκα πέλεσθαι [Refs 6th c.BC+ [6th c.BC: Xenophanes Poeta Philosophus 38]]; εἰ μὴ ὑμεῖς ἤλθετε, ἐπορευόμεθα ἂν ἐπὶ βασιλέα had you not come, we should be on our way.., [Refs 8th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 2.1.4; καὶ ἴσως ἂν ἀπέθανον, εἰ μὴ ἡ ἀρχὴ διὰ ταχέων κατελύθη 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Apologia” 32d, compare 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 5.680, 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 4.364, 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 4.5, 27.63]]: with pluperfect in apodosi, εἰ τριάκοντα μόναι μετέπεσον τῶν ψήφων, ἀπεπεφεύγη ἄν [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Apologia” 36a.]]

__B.I.3.c
rarely with pluperfect referring to action finished in past or present time, λοιπὸν δ᾽ ἂν ἦν ἡμῖν ἔτι περὶ τῆς πόλεως διαλεχθῆναι, εἰ μὴ προτέρα τῶν ἄλλων τὴν εἰρήνην ἐπεποίητο if she had not (as she has done) made peace before the rest, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Isocrates Orator 5.56, compare 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Timaeus” 21c.]]

__B.II
with SUB[Refs 1st c.AD+ [1st c.AD: Josephus Historicus, εἰ is regularly joined with ἄν]] (Epic dialect κε, κεν), compare ἐάν: [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.AD(?): Arcadius Grammaticus εἰκαν in Tegean Inscrr. of 4th c.BC (“IG” 5(2).3.16, 31, 6.2, “SIG” 306.34) should be understood as εἰκ ἄν (εἰ: εἰκ ={οὐ}: οὐκ), since εἰ δ᾽ ἄν is also found in “IG” 5(2).3.2, 6.45, and εἰκ alone, [prev. work]3.21]]; but ἄν (κε, κεν) are frequently absent in [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Homerus Epicus as 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 5.221, 14.373 (and compare below 2), and Lyric poetry, 5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus (who never uses εἰ with ἄν or κε (ν)) “P.” 4.266, +others; in dialects, αἰ δείλητ᾽ ἀγχωρεῖν “IG” 9(1).334.6 (_Locrian dialect_, 5th c.BC)]], cf. Foed.Doric dialect cited in [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 5.79; rarely in 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus, εἰ μὴ ἀναβῇ 2.13]]; occasionally in Trag., [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Eumenides” 234, 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Tyrannus” 198 (Lyric poetry), etc.]]; very rarely in Attic dialect Prose, εἰ ξυστῶσιν αἱ πόλεις [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 6.21; εἴ τι που ἄλσος ἢ τέμενος ἀφειμένον ᾖ 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Leges” 761c]]: in later Prose, εἴ τις θελήσῃ [NT+3rd c.AD+ [NT.Rev.11.5; εἰ φονεύῃ 3rd c.AD: Plotinus Philosophus 2.9.9, compare 5th c.AD: Proclus Philosophus “Inst.” 26.]]

__B.II.1
when the apodosis is future, to express a future condition more distinctly and vividly than εἰ with optative, but less so than εἰ with future indicative (above [Refs [1.2a)]]; εἰ δέ κεν ὣς ἕρξῃς καί τοι πείθωνται Ἀχαιοί, γνώσῃ ἔπειθ᾽.. if thou do thus.., thou shalt know, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 2.364, compare 1.128, 3.281, 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 17.549; ἂν δέ τις ἀνθιστῆται, σὺν ὑμῖν πειρασόμεθα χειροῦσθαι 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 7.3.11]]; ἂν μὴ νῦν ἐθέλωμεν ἐκεῖ πολεμεῖν αὐτῷ, ἐνθάδ᾽ ἴσως ἀναγκασθησόμεθα τοῦτο ποιεῖν if we be not now willing, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 4.50, compare 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 5.3.27: followed by _imperative_, ἢν εἰρήνης δοκῆτε δεῖσθαι, ἄνευ ὅπλων ἥκετε [prev. work] 3.2.13, compare 5.4.30.]]

__B.II.2
when the apodosis is present, denoting customary or repeated action, to express a general condition, if ever, ἤν ποτε δασμὸς ἵκηται, σοὶ τὸ γέρας πολὺ μεῖζον (i.e. ἐστί) whenever a division comes, your prize is (always) greater, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 1.166]]; ἢν ἐγγὺς ἔλθῃ θάνατος, οὐδεὶς βούλεται θνῄσκειν if death come near, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Alcestis” 671]]; with ἄν omitted, εἴ περ γάρ τε χόλον.. καταπέψῃ ἀλλά.. ἔχει κότον [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 1.81.]]

__B.II.2.b
with Rhet. present in apodosis, ἐὰν μὴ οἱ φιλόσοφοι βασιλεύσωσιν, οὐκ ἔστι κακῶν παῦλα there is (i.e. can be, will be) no rest.., [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 473d.]]

__B.III
with OPTATIVE (never with ἄν in early Gr., later ἐάν with optative, [Refs 5th c.AD+ [5th-6th c.AD: Damascius Philosophus “de Principiis” 114, +others),]]

__B.III.1
to express a future condition less definitely than ἐάν with subjunctive, usually with optative with ἄν in apodosis, ἦ κεν γηθήσαι Πρίαμος Πριάμοιό τε παῖδες.. εἰ σφῶιν τάδε πάντα πυθοίατο μαρναμένοιιν surely they would exult, if they should hear.., [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 1.255, compare 7.28, 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 3.223; εἴης φορητὸς οὐκ ἄν, εἰ πράσσοις καλῶς 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Prometheus Vinctus” 979; οὐδὲ γὰρ ἄν με ἐπαινοίη, εἰ ἐξελαύνοιμι τοὺς εὐεργέτας 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 7.7.11; οἶκος δ᾽ αὐτός, εἰ φθογγὴν λάβοι, σαφέστατ᾽ ἂν λέξειεν 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Agamemnon” 37, etc.]]: future optative is falsa lectio in [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Theaetetus” 164a]]: with present indicative in apodosis, [Refs 6th c.BC+ [6th c.BC: Xenophanes Poeta Philosophus 34.3, 3rd c.AD: Democritus Epigrammaticus 253]]: with future indicative, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Melissus Philosophus 5.]]

__B.III.1.b
in Hom.sometimes with present optative, to express an unfulfilled present condition, εἰ μὲν νῦν ἐπὶ ἄλλῳ ἀεθλεύοιμεν, ἦ τ᾽ ἂν ἐγὼ τὰ πρῶτα φεροίμην if we were now contending, etc., [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 23.274: rarely in Trag., εἰ μὴ κνίζοι (={εἰ μὴ ἔκνιζε}) 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Medea” 568; also εἰ ἀναγκαῖον εἴη ἀδικεῖν ἢ ἀδικεῖσθαι, ἑλοίμην ἂν μᾶλλον ἀδικεῖσθαι 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Gorgias” 469c.]]

__B.III.2
when the apodosis is past, denoting customary or repeated action, to express a general condition in past time (corresponding to use of subjunctive in present time, above [Refs [11.2)]]; once in [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Homerus Epicus, εἴ τίς με.. ἐνίπτοι, ἀλλὰ σὺ τόν γ᾽.. κατέρυκες 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 24.768]]; εἰ δέ τινας θορυβουμένους αἴσθοιτο.., κατασβεννύναι τὴν ταραχὴν ἐπειρᾶτο if he should see (whenever he saw) any troops in confusion, he (always) tried, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 5.3.55, compare “An.” 4.5.13, “Mem.” 4.2.40]]; εἴ τις ἀντείποι, εὐθὺς ἐτεθνήκει if any one made objection, he was a dead man at once, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 8.66; ἀλλ᾽ εἴ τι μὴ φέροιμεν, ὤτρυνεν φέρειν 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Alcestis” 755. For εἰ with _indicative_ in this sense see above 1.1]]: indicative and optative are found in same sentence, ἐμίσει, οὐκ εἴ τις κακῶς πάσχων ἠμύνετο, ἀλλ᾽ εἴ τις εὐεργετούμενος ἀχάριστος φαίνοιτο [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Agesilaus” 11.3.]]

__B.III.3
in oratio obliqua after past tenses, representing ἐάν with subjunctive or εἰ with a primary (never an historical) tense of the indicative in oratio recta, ἐλογίζοντο ὡς, εἰ μὴ μάχοιντο, ἀποστήσοιντο αἱ πόλεις (representing ἐὰν μὴ μαχώμεθα, ἀποστήσονται) [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Historia Graeca (Hellenica)” 6.4.6, compare 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 21.104, 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Historia Graeca (Hellenica)” 5.2.2]]; ἔλεγεν ὅτι, εἰ βλαβερὰ πεπραχὼς εἴη, δίκαιος εἴη ζημιοῦσθαι (representing εἰ βλαβερὰ πέπραχε, δίκαιός ἐστι)[Refs [[prev. work] 32, compare “An.” 6.6.25]]; εἰ δέ τινα φεύγοντα λήψοιτο, προηγόρευεν ὅτι ὡς πολεμίῳ χρήσοιτο (representing εἴ τινα λήψομαι, χρήσομαι) [Refs [[prev. author] “Cyr.” 3.1.3]]; also, where oratio obliqua is implied in the leading clause, οὐκ ἦν τοῦ πολέμου πέρας Φιλίππῳ, εἰ μὴ Θηβαίους.. ἐχθροὺς ποιήσειε τῇ πόλει, i.e. Philip thought there would be no end to the war, unless he should make.. (his thought having been ἐὰν μὴ ποιήσω), [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 18.145; ἐβούλοντο γὰρ σφίσιν, εἴ τινα λάβοιεν, ὑπάρχειν ἀντὶ τῶν ἔνδον, ἢν ἄρα τύχωσί τινες ἐζωγρημένοι 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 2.5.]]

__B.III.4
with optative with ἄν, only when the clause serves as apodosis as well as protasis,[Refs 5th c.BC+ [compare 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Protagoras” 329b, 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 4.18, 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Memorabilia” 1.5.3 (see. ἄν 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus 111. d).]]

__B.IV
with infinitive, in oratio obliqua, only in [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus, εἰ γὰρ δὴ δεῖν πάντως περιθεῖναι ἄλλῳ τέῳ τὴν βασιληΐην, [ἔφη] δικαιότερον εἶναι κτλ. 1.129; εἰ εἶναι τοῦτο μὴ φίλον 2.64, compare 172, 3.105, 108.]]

__B.V
after Verbs denoting wonder, delight, indignation, disappointment, contentment, and similar emotions, εἰ with indicative is used instead of ὅτι, to express the object of the feeling in a hypothetical form, θαυμάζω εἰ μηδεὶς ὑμῶν μήτ᾽ ἐνθυμεῖται μήτ᾽ ὀργίζεται, ὁρῶν.. I wonder that no one of you is either concerned or angry when he sees.., [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 4.43; οὐκ ἀγαπᾷ εἰ μὴ δίκην δέδωκεν, ἀλλ᾽ εἰ μὴ καὶ χρυσῷ στεφάνῳ στεφανωθήσεται ἀγανακτεῖ 4th c.BC: Aeschines Orator 3.147]]: after past tenses, ἐθαύμασε δ᾽ εἰ μὴ φανερόν ἐστιν [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Memorabilia” 1.1.13; δεινὸν εἰσῄει, εἰ μὴ.. δόξει 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 19.33; ἐθαύμαζον εἴ τι ἕξει τις χρήσασθαι τῷ λόγῳ 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Phaedo” 95a; οὐδὲ ᾐσχύνθη εἰ.. ἐπάγει 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 21.105: in oratio obliqua (expressed or implied) with _optative_, ἐπεῖπεν ὡς δεινὸν (i.e. εἴη) εἰ.. μεγαλόψυχος γένοιτο 4th c.BC: Aeschines Orator 2.157; ᾤκτιρον εἰ ἁλώσοιντο 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 1.4.7]]; ἐθαύμαζε δ᾽ εἴ τις ἀρετὴν ἐπαγγελλόμενος ἀργύριον πράττοιτο he wondered that any one should demand money, [Refs [[prev. author] “Mem.” 1.2.7]]; ἔχαιρον ἀγαπῶν εἴ τις ἐάσοι I rejoiced, being content if any one should let it pass, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 450a:]] —in this use the _negative_ οὐ is also found, ἀγανακτῶ εἰ ὁ Φίλιππος ἁρπάζων οὐ λυπεῖ [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 8.55; δεινὸν ἂν εἴη εἰ οἱ ἐκείνων ξύμμαχοι οὐκ ἀπεροῦσιν 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 1.121; τέρας λέγεις, εἰ οὐκ ἂν δύναιντο λαθεῖν 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Meno” 91d, etc.]]

__B.VI
in citing a fact as a ground of argument or appeal, as surely as, since, εἴ ποτ᾽ ἔην γε if there was [as there was], i.e. as sure as there was such an one, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 3.180, +others; εἰ τότε κοῦρος ἔα, νῦν αὖτέ με γῆρας ὀπάζει 4.321]]; πολλοὺς γὰρ οἶκε εἶναι εὐπετέστερον διαβάλλειν ἢ ἕνα, εἰ Κλεομένεα μὲν μοῦνον οὐκ οἷός τε ἐγένετο διαβαλεῖν, τρεῖς δὲ μυριάδας Ἀθηναίων ἐποίησε τοῦτο it seems easier to deceive many than one, if (as was the fact, i.e. since) he was not able.., [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 5.97, compare 1.60, +others]]

__B.VII
ELLIPTICAL CONSTRUCTIONS:

__B.VII.1
with apodosis implied in the context, εἰ having the force of in case, supposing that, πρὸς τὴν πόλιν, εἰ ἐπιβοηθοῖεν, ἐχώρουν they marched towards the city [so as to meet the citizens], in case they should rush out, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 6.100]]; ἱκέται πρὸς σὲ δεῦρ᾽ ἀφίγμεθα, εἴ τινα πόλιν φράσειας ἡμῖν εὔερον we have come hither to you, in case you should tell us of some fleecy city (i.e. that we might hear of it), [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Aves” 120]]; παρέζεο καὶ λαβὲ γούνων, αἴ κέν πως ἐθέλῃσιν ἐπὶ Τρώεσσιν ἀρῆξαι sit by him and grasp his knees [so as to persuade him], in case he be willing to help the Trojans, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 1.408, compare 66, 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 1.94, 3.92]]; ἄκουσον καὶ ἐμοῦ, ἐάν σοι ἔτι ταὐτὰ δοκῇ hear me also [that you may assent], in case the same opinion please you, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 358b]]; ἰδὲ δή, ἐάν σοι ὅπερ ἐμοὶ συνδοκῇ look now, in case you approve what I do, [Refs [[prev. work] 434a.]]

__B.VII.2
with apodosis suppressed for rhetorical reasons, εἴ περ γάρ κ᾽ ἐθέλῃσιν Ὀλύμπιος.. στυφελίξαι if he wish to thrust him away, [he will do so], [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 1.580]]; εἰ μὲν δώσουσι γέρας—· εἰ δέ κε μὴ δώωσιν, ἐγὼ δέ κεν αὐτὸς ἕλωμαι if they shall give me a prize, [well and good]; but if they give not, then I will take one for myself, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [1.135, compare 6.150, 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Plutus” 468]]; καὶ ἢν μὲν ξυμβῇ ἡ πεῖρα—· εἰ δὲ μή.. and if the attempt succeed, [well]; otherwise.., [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 3.3, compare 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Protagoras” 325d.]]

__B.VII.3
with the Verb of the protasis omitted, chiefly in the following expressions:

__B.VII.3.a
εἰ μή except, οὐδὲν ἄλλο σιτέονται, εἰ μὴ ἰχθῦς μοῦνον [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.200]]; μὰ τὼ θεώ, εἰ μὴ Κρίτυλλά γ᾽ [εἰμί]—nay, if I'm not Critylla! i.e. I am, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Thesmophoriazusae” 898]]; εἰ μὴ ὅσον except only, ἐγὼ μέν μιν οὐκ εἶδον, εἰ μὴ ὅσον γραφῇ [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 2.73, compare 1.45, 2.20; εἰ μὴ εἰ 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 1.17, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Gorgias” 480b, etc.]]; εἰ μή τι οὖν, ἀλλὰ σμικρόν γέ μοι τῆς ἀρχῆς χάλασον if nothing else, yet.., [Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. author] “Men.” 86e; ironical, εἰ μὴ ἄρα ἡ τῆς ἀρετῆς ἐπιμέλεια διαφθορά ἐστιν 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Memorabilia” 1.2.8; εἰ μή πέρ γε τὸν ὑοσκύαμον χρήματα εἶναι φήσομεν [prev. author] “Oec.” 1.13.]]

__B.VII.3.b
εἰ δὲ μή but if not, i.e. otherwise, προηγόρευε τοῖς Λαμψακηνοῖσι μετιέναι Μιλτιάδεα, εἰ δὲ μή, σφέας πίτυος τρόπον ἀπείλεε ἐκτρίψειν [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 6.37, compare 56]]; after μάλιστα μέν, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 1.32, 35, etc.:]] —after a preceding _negative_, μὴ τύπτ᾽· εἰ δὲ μή, σαυτόν ποτ᾽ αἰτιάσει don't beat me; otherwise, you will have yourself to blame, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Nubes” 1433; ὦ Κῦρε, μὴ οὕτω λέγε· εἰ δὲ μή, οὐ θαρροῦντά με ἕξεις 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 3.1.35; οὔτ᾽ ἐν τῷ ὕδατι τὰ ὅπλα ἦν ἔχειν· εἰ δὲ μή [prev. author] “An.” 4.3.6, compare 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 1.28, 131, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Phaedo” 91c.]]

__B.VII.3.c
εἰ δέ sometimes stands for εἰ δὲ μή, εἰ μὲν βούλεται, ἑψέτω· εἰ δ᾽, ὅτι βούλεται, τοῦτο ποιείτω [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Euthydemus” 285c, compare “Smp.” 212c; εἰ δ᾽ οὖν 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Antigone” 722; εἰ δ᾽ οὕτως 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Ethica Nicomachea” 1094a24]]; εἰ δὲ τοῦτο and if so, [Refs 1st c.BC+ [1st c.BC-1st c.AD: Strabo Geographus 2.1.29.]]

__B.VII.3.d
εἰ γάρ for if so, [Refs [[prev. author] 7.3.6.]]

__B.VII.3.e
εἴ τις if any, i. e. as much as or more than any, τῶν γε νῦν αἴ τις ἐπιχθονίων, ὀρθῶς [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Bacchylides Lyricus 5.5; ὄτλον ἄλγιστον ἔσχον, εἴ τις Αἰτωλὶς γυνή 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Trachiniae” 8, compare “OC” 734]]; εἴ τις ἄλλος, siquis alius, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Andromache” 6, etc.; εἴ τινες καὶ ἄλλοι 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 3.2, etc.; εἴπερ τις ἄλλος 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 501d]]; also κατ᾽ εἰ δέ τινα τρόπον in any way, [Refs [“IG” 5(2).6.27 (from Tegea).]]

__B.VII.3.f
εἴ ποτε or εἴπερ ποτέ now if ever, ἡμῖν δὲ καλῶς, εἴπερ ποτέ, ἔχει.. ἡ ξυναλλαγή [Refs 7th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 4.20, compare 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Equites” 594; αἴ ποτα κἄλλοτα 7th-6th c.BC: Alcaeus Lyricus “Supp.” 7.11, compare 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 6.4.12, etc.]]; but in prayers, εἴ ποτέ τοι ἐπὶ νηὸν ἔρεψα.. τόδε μοι κρήηνον ἐέλδωρ [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 1.39.]]

__B.VII.3.g
εἴ ποθεν (i.e. δυνατόν ἐστι) if from any quarter, i.e. from some quarter or other, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Philoctetes” 1204 (Lyric poetry)]]; so εἴ ποθι somewhere, anywhere, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [[prev. author] “Aj.” 885 (Lyric poetry); εἴ που 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 4.193.]]

__B.VII.3.h
εἴ πως[Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. work] 388, 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 2.3.11]]: in an elliptical sentence (cf. VII. [Refs 5th c.BC+ [1), πρέσβεις πέμψαντες, εἴ πως πείσειαν 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 1.58.]]

__B.VIII
with other PARTICLES:

__B.VIII.1
for the distinction between καὶ εἰ (or καὶ ἐάν, or κἄν) even if, and εἰ καί (or ἐὰν καί) even though, see at {καί}:—the opposite of καὶ εἰ is οὐδ᾽ εἰ, not even if; that of εἰ καί is εἰ μηδέ, if (although) not even.

__B.VIII.2
for ὡς εἰ, ὡς εἴ τε, ὥσπερ εἰ, etc., see at {ὡς} and ὥσπερ.

__B.VIII.3
for εἰ ἄρα, see at {ἄρα}; for εἰ δή, εἴπερ, see at {εἰ δή, εἴπερ}; for εἴ γε, see at {γέ}.

__B.IX
in negative oaths, = Hebrew im, [LXX+NT [LXX.Psa.94(95).11, NT.Mark.8.12, +others]]

__C
IN INDIRECT QUESTIONS, whether, followed by the indicative, subjunctive, or optative, according to the principles of oratio obliqua:

__C.1
with IN[Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator after primary tenses, representing the same tense in the direct question, σάφα δ᾽ οὐκ οἶδ᾽ εἰ θεός ἐστιν]] whether he is a god, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 5.183; εἰ ξυμπονήσεις.. σκόπει 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Antigone” 41.]]

__C.2
with SUB[Refs 1st c.AD+ [1st c.AD: Josephus Historicus after primary tenses, representing a dubitative]]subjunctive in the direct question, τὰ ἐκπώματα οὐκ οἶδ᾽ εἰ Χρυσάντᾳ τουτῳῒ δῶ whether I should give them, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 8.4.16: sometimes elliptical, ἐς τὰ χρηστήρια ἔπεμπε, εἰ στρατεύηται ἐπὶ τοὺς Πέρσας 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.75.]]

__C.3
OPT. after past tenses, representing either of the two previous constructions in the direct question, ἤρετο εἴ τις ἐμοῦ εἴη σοφώτερος he asked whether any one was wiser than I (direct ἔστι τις σοφώτερο;), [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Apologia” 21a; ἐπεκηρυκεύετο Πεισιστράτῳ, εἰ βούλοιτό οἱ τὴν θυγατέρα ἔχειν γυναῖκα 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.60: rarely]]aorist optative for the aorist indicative, ἠρώτων αὐτὸν εἰ ἀναπλεύσειεν I asked him whether he had set sail (direct ἀνέπλευσα;), [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 50.55: but]]aorist optative usually represents aorist subjunctive, τὸν θεὸν ἐπήροντο εἰ παραδοῖεν Κορινθίοις τὴν πόλιν.. καὶ τιμωρίαν τινὰ πειρῷντ᾽ ἀπ᾽ αὐτῶν ποιεῖσθαι they asked whether they should deliver their city to the Corinthians, and should try.., [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 1.25:]] —in both constructions the _indicative_ or subjunctive may be retained, ψῆφον ἐβούλοντο ἐπαγαγεῖν εἰ χρὴ πολεμεῖν[Refs [[prev. work] 119]]; ἐβουλεύοντο εἴτε κατακαύσωσιν.. εἴτε τι ἄλλο χρήσωνται whether they should burn them or should dispose of them in some other way, [Refs [[prev. author] 2.4]]; ἀνακοινοῦσθαι αὐτὸν αὑτῷ εἰ δῷ ἐπιψηφίσαι τοῖς προέδροις [he said that] he consulted him whether he should give.., [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aeschines Orator 2.68.]]

__C.4
with OPT. and ἄν when this was the form of the direct question, ἠρώτων εἰ δοῖεν ἂν τούτων τὰ πιστά they asked whether they would give (direct δοιήτε ἄ;), [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 4.8.7.]]

__C.5
the NEG. used with εἰ in indirect questions is οὐ, when οὐ would be used in the direct question, ἐνετέλλετο.. εἰρωτᾶν εἰ οὔ τι ἐπαισχύνεται whether he is not ashamed, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.90, etc.]]; but if μή would be required in the direct form, it is retained in the indirect, οὐ τοῦτο ἐρωτῶ, ἀλλ᾽ εἰ τοῦ μὲν δικαίου μὴ ἀξιοῖ πλέον ἔχειν μηδὲ βούλεται ὁ δίκαιος, τοῦ δὲ ἀδίκου (the direct question would be μὴ ἀξιοῖ μηδὲ βούλετα; he does not see fit nor wish, does he?) [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 349b]]:—in double indirect questions, εἴτε.. εἴτε..; εἰ.. εἴτε..; εἴτε.. ἢ.., either οὐ or μή can be used in the second clause, ὅπως ἴδῃς εἴτ᾽ ἔνδον εἴτ᾽ οὐκ ἔνδον [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Ajax” 7; σκοπῶμεν εἰ ἡμῖν πρέπει ἢ οὔ 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 451d]]; εἰ ἀληθὲς ἢ μή, πειράσομαι μαθεῖν[Refs 4th c.BC+ [[prev. work] 339a; πολλὰ ἂν περιεσκέψω, εἴτε ἐπιτρεπτέον εἴτε οὔ·.. οὐδένα λόγον οὐδὲ συμβουλὴν ποιῇ, εἴτε χρὴ ἐπιτρέπειν σαυτὸν αὐτῷ εἴτε μή [prev. author] “Prt.” 313a, 313b; ἀνάγκη τὴν ἐμὴν μητέρα, εἴτε θυγάτηρ ἦν Κίρωνος εἴτε μή, καὶ εἰ παρ᾽ ἐκείνῳ διῃτᾶτο ἢ οὔ, καὶ γάμους εἰ διττοὺς ὑπὲρ ταύτης εἱστίασεν ἢ μὴ.. πάντα ταῦτα εἰδέναι τοὺς οἰκέτας 4th c.BC: Isaeus Orator 8.9]]; τοὺς νόμους καταμανθάνειν εἰ καλῶς κεῖνται ἢ μή.. τοὺς λόγους εἰ ὀρθῶς ὑμᾶς διδάσκουσιν ἢ οὔ [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Antipho Orator 5.14.]]

Abbott-Smith / STEPBible (TBESG)
εἰρήνη, -ης, ἡ,
[in LXX chiefly for שָׁלוֹם ;]
peace;
__1. of public peace, freedom from war: Luk.14:32, Act.12:20 24:2; of the church, Ac 9:31.
__2. Of peace between persons, concord, agreement : Mat.10:34, Luk.12:51, Rom.14:17, 1Co.7:15, Gal.5:22, Jas.3:18; ζητεῖν εἰ., 1Pe.3:11; διώκειν, 2Ti.2:22; ib. before μετὰ πάντων, Heb.12:14; by meton., of him who brings peace, Eph.2:14.
__3. As in LXX (= Heb. שָׁלוֹם, Aram. שְׁלָם), of a state of security and safety: Jhn.16:33, Rom.2:10, 1Th.5:3,́ whence the formulae, ὕπαγε (πορεύου) εἰς εἰ, Mrk.5:34, Luk.7:50 (cf. 1Ki.1:17, al.; לְכִי לְשָׁלוֹם); εἰ. ὑμῖν (שָׁלוֹם לָכֶם), Jhn.20:19, 21, 26; ἀπολύειν ἐν εἰ., Luk.2:29, cf. 1Co.16:11; ἡ εἰ. ὑμῶν, Mat.10:13, Luk.10:6; υἱὸς εἰρήνης, ib.
__4. Of spiritual peace, the peace of Christ's kingdom (DCG, ii, 330f.): Luk.1:79 2:14 Jhn.16:33, Rom.2:10 5:1 8:6, al.; ὁ κύριος τῆς εἰ., 2Th.3:16; ὁ θεὸς τῆς εἰ., Rom.15:33 16:20, 2Co.13:11, al.; in epistolary salutations, Rom.1:7, 1Co.1:3, Gal.1:3, 1Th.1:1, 1Pe.1:2, 2Jo.3, Rev.1:4, al. (see Cremer, 244).
(AS)

LSJ / STEPBible (TFLSJ)
εἰρήν-η
(see. below), ἡ, peace, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 24.486, etc.]]; ἐπ᾽ εἰρήνης in time of peace, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 2.797; ἔθηκε πᾶσιν εἰ. φίλοις 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Persae” 769]]; εἰ. τἀκεῖθεν τέκνοις on that side they have peace, have naught to fear, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Medea” 1004]]; εἰ. γίγνεται peace is made, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.74]]: hence later, a peace, treaty of peace, ἡ βασιλέως εἰ. deep_entry:
Abbott-Smith / STEPBible (TBESG)
εἰς,
prep. with accusative,
expressing entrance, direction, limit, into, unto, to, upon, towards, for, among (Lat. in, with accusative).
__I. Of place.
__1. After verbs of motion;
__(a) of entrance into: Mat.8:23, 9:7, Mrk.1:45, Luk.2:15, 8:31, al.;
__(b) of approach, to or towards: Mrk.11:1, Luk.6:8, 19:28, Jhn.11:31, 21:6, al.;
__(with) before pl. and collective nouns, among: Mrk.4:7, 8:19, 20, Luk.11:49, Jhn.21:23, al.;
__(d) Of a limit reached, unto, on, upon: Mat.8:18, 21:1, Mrk.11:1, 13:16, Luk.14:10, Jhn.6:3, 11:32, al.; with accusative of person(s) (as in Ep. and Ion.), Act.23:15, Rom.5:12, 16:19, 2Co.10:14;
__(e) elliptical: ἐπιστολαὶ εἰς Δαμασκόν, Act.9:2; ἡ διακονία μου ἡ εἰς Ἱ., Rom.15:31; metaphorically, of entrance into a certain state or condition, or of approach or direction towards some end (Thayer, B, i, 1; ii, 1), εἰς τ. ὄνομα, M, Pr., 200.
__2. Of direction;
__(a) after verbs of seeing: Mat.6:26, Mrk.6:41, Luk.9:16, 62, Jhn.13:22, al.; metaphorically, of the mind, Heb.11:26, 12:2, al.;
__(b) after verbs of speaking: Mat.13:10, 14:9, 1Th.2:9, al.
__3. After verbs of rest;
__(a) in "pregnant" construction, implying previous motion (cl.; see WM, 516; Bl., §39, 3; M, Pr., 234f.): Mat.2:23, 4:13, 2Th.2:4, 2Ti.1:11, Heb.11:9, al.;
__(b) by an assimilation general in late Gk (see Bl., M, Pr., ll. with) = ἐν: Luk.1:44, 4:23, Act.20:16, 21:17, Jhn.1:18 (but see Westc, in l.), al.
__II. Of time, for, unto;
__1. accentuating the duration expressed by the accusative: εἰς τ. αἰῶνα, Mat.21:19; εἰς γενεὰς καὶ γ., Luk.1:50; εἰς τ. διηνεκές, Heb.7:3, al.
__2. Of a point or limit of time, unto, up to, until: Mat.6:34, Act.4:3, 25:21, Php.1:10, 2:16, 1Th.4:15, 2Ti.1:12; of entrance into a future period, σεις τὸ μέλλον (see: μέλλω), next (year), Luk.13:9 (but with ICC, in l.); εἰς τ. μεταξὺ σάββατον, on the next Sabbath, Act.13:42; εἰς τὸ πάλιν (see: πάλιν, 2Co.13:2.
__III. Of result, after verbs of changing, joining, dividing, etc.: στρέφειν εἰς, Rev.11:6; μετας-, Act.2:20, Jas.4:9; μεταλλάσσειν, Rom.1:26; σχίζειν εἰς δύο, Mat.27:51, al.; predicatively with εἴναι, Act.8:23.
__IV. Of relation, to, towards, for, in regard to (so in cl., but more frequently in late Gk., εἰς encroaching on the simple dative, which it has wholly displaced in MGr.; Jannaris, Gr., §1541; Robertson, Gr., 594; Deiss., BS, 117f.): Luk.7:30, Rom.4:20, 15:2, 26, 1Co.16:1, Eph.3:16, al.; ἀγάπη εἰς, Rom.5:8, al.; χρηστός, Eph.4:32; φρονεῖν εἰς, Rom.12:16; θαρρεῖν, 2Co.10:1.
__V. Of the end or object: εὔθετος εἰς, Luk.14:34; σόφος, Rom.16:19; ἰσχύειν, Mat.5:13; εἰς τοῦτο, Mrk.1:38, al.; ἀφορίζειν εἰς, Rom.1:1; indicating purpose, εἰς φόβον, Rom.8:15; εἰς ἔνδειξιν, Rom.3:25; εἰς τό, with inf. (= ἵνα or ὥστε; Bl., §71, 5; M, Pr., 218ff.): Mat.20:19, Rom.1:11, 1Co.9:18, al.
__VI. Adverbial phrases: εἰς τέλος, εἰς τὸ πάλιν, etc (see: τέλος, πάλιν, etc.).
(AS)

LSJ / STEPBible (TFLSJ)
ἐν εἰς
or ἐς, PREP. WITH ACC. ONLY:—both forms are found in [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Homerus Epicus]], Ionic dialect poets, and early metrical Inscrr.; ἐς is best attested in [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus and 5th c.BC: Hippocrates Medicus]], and is found in nearly all early Ionic dialect Inscrr. (except [Refs 5th c.BC+ [“IG” 12(8).262.16 (Thasos, 5th c.BC), [prev. work]7.235.1 (Oropus, 4th c.BC)); εἰς in _Attic dialect_ Inscrr. from 4th c.BC, “IG” 2.115, etc.]]; and usually in Attic dialect Prose (except [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus) and Comedy texts (except in parody): Trag. apparently prefer εἰς, but ἐς]] is used before vowels for the sake of meter; ἐς was retained in the phrases ἐς κόρακας (whence the Verb σκορακίζω), ἐς μακαρίαν. Aeolic dialect poets have εἰς before vowels, ἐς before consonants, and this is given as the rule in [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Homerus Epicus by “Anecdota Graeca - MSS. Bibl. Oxon.” 1.172, compare 2nd c.AD(?): Helladius Epigrammaticus cited in 9th c.AD: Photius Legal icographus, etc. “Bibliotheca - Patrologia Graeca” p.533B. (Orig. ἐνς, as in “IG” 4.554.7 (from Argos), “GDI” 4986.11 (from Crete)]]; compare ἐν, ἰν. The diphthong is genuine in Aeolic dialect εἰς, but spurious in Attic dialect-Ionic dialect) Radical sense into, and then more loosely, to:

__I
OF PLACE, the oldest and commonest usage, εἰς ἅλα into or to the sea, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 1.141, +others; εἰς ἅλαδε 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 10.351; ἔς ῥ᾽ ἀσαμίνθους 4.48; ἐς οἶνον βάλε φάρμακον [prev. work] 220]]; frequently of places, to, εἰς Εὔβοιαν [Refs [3.174]]; ἐς Αἴγυπτον, etc., [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.5, etc.]]; ἐς Μίλητον into the territory of Miletus,[Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. work] 14; εἰς Ἑλλήσποντον εἰσέπλει 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Historia Graeca (Hellenica)” 1.1.2; ἀφίκετο εἰς Μήδους πρὸς Κυαξάρην [prev. author] “Cyr.” 2.1.2]]; εἰς ἅρματα βαίνειν to step into.., [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 8.115; εἰς ἐλάτην ἀναβῆναι 14.287]]; opposed to ἐκ, in such phrases as ἐς σφυρὸν ἐκ πτέρνης, ἐς πόδας ἐκ κεφαλῆς, from heel to ankle-joint, from head to foot, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [22.397, 23.169; ἐκ πάτου ἐς σκοπιήν 20.137; ἐς μυχὸν ἐξ οὐδοῦ 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 7.87]]; κἠς ἔτος ἐξ ἔτεος from year to year, [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [3rd c.BC: Theocritus Poeta Bucolicus 18.15]]: with Verbs implying motion or direction, as of looking, ἰδεῖν εἰς οὐρανόν [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 3.364]]; εἰς ὦπα ἰδέσθαι to look in the face, [Refs [9.373]], etc.; εἰς ὦπα ἔοικεν he is like in face (i.e. ἰδόντι), [Refs [3.158]], etc.; ἐς ὀφθαλμούς τινος ἐλθεῖν to come before another's eyes,[Refs 5th c.BC+ [24.204; ἐς ὄψιν ἀπικνέεσθαί τινος 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.136; καλέσαι τινὰ ἐς ὄψιν [prev. author] 5.106, etc.]]; ἐς ταὐτὸν ἥκειν come to the same point, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Hippolytus” 273]]: less frequently after a substantive, ὁδὸς ἐς λαύρην [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 22.128]]; τὸ ἐς Παλλήνην τεῖχος facing Pallene, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 1.56; ξύνοδος ἐς τὴν Δῆλον [prev. author] 3.104, compare 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Theaetetus” 173d.]]

__I.b
Epic dialect and Ionic dialect, also with accusative person (Attic dialect ὡς, πρός, παρά), [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 7.312, 15.402, 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 14.127, 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 4.147]]; also in Attic dialect with collective Nouns, ἐς τὸν δῆμον παρελθόντες [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 5.45, or plurals, εἰς ὑμᾶς εἰσῆλθον 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 18.103]]; especially of consulting an oracle, ἐς θεὸν ἐλθεῖν [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “O.” 7.31; εἰς Ἄμμων᾽ ἐλθόντες 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Aves” 619.]]

__I.2
with Verbs expressing restin a place, when a previous motion into or to it is implied, ἐς μέγαρον κατέθηκεν ἐπὶ θρόνου he put it in the house (i.e. he brought it into the house, and put it there), [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 20.96]]; ἐς θρόνους ἕζοντο they sat them down upon the seats, [Refs [4.51, compare 1.130]]; ἐφάνη λὶς εἰς ὁδόν the lion appeared in the path, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 15.276; ἀπόστολος ἐς τὴν Μίλητον ἦν 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.21 (assuming variant); αὐτὸς ἐς Αακεδαίμονα ἀπόστολος ἐγίνετο [prev. author] 5.38; ἐς κώμην παραγίνονται [prev. author] 1.185; παρῆν ἐς Σάρδις [prev. author] 6.1; ἐς δόμους μένειν 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Ajax” 80 (codex Laur.); ἐς τὴν νῆσον κατέκλῃσε 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 1.109, compare 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 3.13]]; ἀπόβασιν ποιήσασθαι ἐς.. [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 2.33, etc.]]; later used like{ἐν}, τὴν γῆν εἰς ἣν ὑμεῖς κατοικεῖτε [LXX+1st c.BC+ [LXX.Num.35.34; τὸ χρυσίον ὃ εἰλήφεσαν εἰς Ῥώμην 1st c.BC: Diodorus Siculus Historicus 14.117; οἰκεῖν εἰς τὰ Ὕπατα 2nd c.AD: Lucianus Sophista “Asin.” 1; εἰς Ἐκβάτανα ἀποθανεῖν 2nd-3rd c.AD: Aelianus “Varia Historia” 7.8; εἰς ἅπασαν τὴν γῆν 10th c.AD: Suidas Legal icographus see {Καλλίμαχος}]]: generally, τοὔνομα εἰς τὴν Ἑλλάδα, φασίν, Ἱππομιγὴς δύναται [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd-3rd c.AD: Aelianus “Varia Historia” 9.16.]]

__I.3
with Verbs of saying or speaking, εἰς relates to the persons to or before whom one speaks, εἰπεῖν ἐς πάντας, ἐς πάντας αὔδα, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 8.26, 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Tyrannus” 93; λέγειν εἰς τὸ μέσον τῶν ταξιάρχων 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 3.3.7; αἱ ἐς τὸ φανερὸν λεγόμεναι αἰτίαι 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 1.23]]: with other Verbs, εἰς τοὺς Ἕλληνας σαυτὸν σοφιστὴν παρέχων [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Protagoras” 312a; καλὸν ἐς τοὺς Ἕλληνας τὸ ἀγώνισμα φανεῖσθαι 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 7.56]]; ἐπαχθὴς ἦν ἐς τοὺς πολλούς [Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. author] 6.54; στρατιὰν ἐπαγγέλλων ἐς τοὺς ξυμμάχους [prev. author] 7.17; διαβεβλῆσθαι εἴς τινα 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 539c.]]

__I.4
elliptical usages,

__I.4.a
after Verbs which have no sense of motion to or into a place, τὴν πόλιν ἐξέλιπον εἰς χωρίον ὀχυρόν they quitted the city for a strong position, i.e. to seek a strong position, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 1.2.24]]; γράμματα ἑάλωσαν εἰς Ἀθήνας letters were captured [and sent] to Athens, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. author] “HG” 1.1.23, compare 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 468a; ἀνίστασθαι ἐς Ἄργος 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Heraclidae” 59, compare 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Phaedo” 116a.]]

__I.4.b
participles signifying motion are frequently omitted with εἰς, τοῖς στρατηγοῖς τοῖς εἰς Σικελίαν (i.e. ἀποδειχθεῖσιν) [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Andocides Orator 1.11, etc.]]

__I.4.c
with genitive, mostly of proper names, as εἰς Ἀΐδαο, Attic dialect εἰς Ἅιδου [δόμους], [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 21.48]]; ἐς Ἀθηναίης [ἱερόν] to the temple of Athena, [Refs [6.379; ἐς Πριάμοιο [οἶκον] 24.160, compare 309]]; εἰς Αἰγύπτοιο [ῥόον] [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 4.581; ἐς τοῦ Κλεομένεος 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 5.51; εἰς Ἀσκληπιοῦ 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Plutus” 411; ἐπὶ δεῖπνον [ἰέναι] εἰς Ἀγάθωνος 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Symposium” 174a: with Appellatives, ἀνδρὸς ἐς ἀφνειοῦ]] to a rich man's house, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 24.482; ἐς πατρός 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 2.195]]; πέμπειν εἰς διδασκάλων send to school, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Respublica Lacedaemoniorum” 2.1; εἰς δ. φοιτᾶν 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Protagoras” 326c]]; ἐς σεωυτοῦ, ἑωυτοῦ, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.108, 9.108, etc.]]

__II
OF TIME,

__II.1
to denote a certain point or limit of time, up to, until, ἐς ἠῶ [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 11.375]]; ἐς ἠέλιον καταδύντα till sunset, [Refs [9.161 (but also,]]towards or near sunset,[Refs 8th c.BC+ [3.138); ἐκ νεότητος ἐς γῆρας 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 14.86; ἐκ παιδὸς ἐς γῆρας 4th c.BC: Aeschines Orator 1.180]]; ἐς ἐμέ up to my time, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.92, +others: with _adverbs_, εἰς ὅτε (compare ἔς τε)]] against the time when.., [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 2.99]]; εἰς πότ; until when ? how long ? [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Ajax” 1185 (Lyric poetry, compare εἰσόκ; εἰς ὁπότε 4th c.BC: Aeschines Orator 3.99]]; ἐς τ; ={εἰς πότε}; [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 5.465]]; ἐς ὅ until, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.93, etc.; ἐς οὗ [prev. author] 1.67, 3.31, etc.; ἐς τόδε [prev. author] 7.29, etc.]]

__II.2
to determine a period, εἰς ἐνιαυτόν for a year, i.e. a whole year, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 19.32, 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 4.526]]; within the year,[Refs 8th c.BC+ [[prev. work] 86 (compare ἐς ἐνίαυτον 7th-6th c.BC: Alcaeus Lyricus “Supp.” 8.12); εἰς ὥρας 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 9.135]]; ἐς θέρος ἢ ἐς ὀπώρην for the summer, i.e. throughout it, [Refs [14.384]]; ἡ εἰς ἐνιαυτὸν κειμένη δαπάνη εἰς τὸν μῆνα δαπανᾶται the expenditure for a year is expended in the month, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Oeconomicus” 7.36; μισθοδοτεῖν τινὰς εἰς ἓξ μῆνας 1st c.BC: Diodorus Siculus Historicus 19.15; χοίνικα κριθῶν εἰς τέσσαρας ἡμέρας διεμέτρει 2nd-1st c.BC: Posidonius Historicus 36J.]]; εἰς ἑσπέραν ἥκειν to come at even, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Plutus” 998]]; εἰς τρίτην ἡμέραν or εἰς τρίτην alone, on the third day, in two days, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Hp.Ma.” 286b, 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 5.3.27; ἥκειν ἐς τὴν ὑστεραίαν [prev. author] “An.” 2.3.25; ἥκειν εἰς τὸ ἔαρ “Hellenica Oxyrhynchia” 17.4]]; ἐς τέλος at last, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 3.40]]; ἐς καιρόν in season, [Refs [[prev. author] 4.139]]; οὐκ ἐς ἀναβολάς, ἀμβολάς, with no delay, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. author] 8.21, 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Heraclidae” 270, etc.]]; ἐς τότε at this time, variant in [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 7.317 (but εἰς τότε]] at that time (in the future), [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 14.24, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Leges” 830b)]]; ἐς ὕστερον or τὸ ὕστερον, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 12.126, 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 2.20: with _adverbs_, ἐς αὔριον 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 8.538, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Leges” 858b; ἔς περ ὀπίσσω 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 20.199; ἐς αὖθις 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 4.63 (see. εἰσαῦθις]] (; ἐς αὐτίκα μάλ᾽ [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Pax” 367]]; εἰς ἔπειτα (see. εἰσέπειτα (; ἐς τὸ ἔ., [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 2.64; ἐς ὀψέ [prev. author] 8.23]]; εἰς ἅπαξ, see at {εἰσάπα; εἰς ἔτι}, see at {εἰσέτι}.

__III
to express MEASURE OR LIMIT, without reference to Time, ἐς δίσκουρα λέλειπτο was left behind as far as a quoit's throw, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 23.523]]; ἐς δραχμὴν διέδωκε paid them as much as a drachma, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 8.29; ἱματισμὸν ζητῆσαι εἰς δύο τάλαντα 4th-3rd c.BC: Theophrastus Philosophus “Characteres” 23.8]]; so ἐς τὰ μάλιστα to the greatest degree, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.20, etc.; ἐς τοσοῦτο τύχης ἀπίκευ [prev. author] 1.124; εἰς τοσοῦτο ἥκειν 5th c.BC: Lysias Orator 27.10; εἰς τοῦτο θράσους καὶ ἀναιδείας ἀφίκετο 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 21.194]]; ἐς ὅ ἐμέμνηντο so far as they remembered, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 5.66; ἐς τὸ ἔσχατον 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 7.229, etc.; εἰς ἅλις 3rd c.BC: Theocritus Poeta Bucolicus 25.17.]]

__III.2
frequently with Numerals, ἐς τριακάδας δέκα ναῶν [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Persae” 339]]; ναῦς ἐς τὰς τετρακοσίας, διακοσίας, to the number of [Refs 5th c.BC+ [400, etc., 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 1.74, 100, etc.]]; εἰς ἕνα, εἰς δύο, εἰς τέσσαρας, one, two, four deep, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 2.3.21]]; but εἰς τέσσαρας four abreast, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aeneas Tacticus 40.6: with _adverbs_, ἐς τρίς or ἐστρίς]] thrice, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “O.” 2.68, 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.86]]; of round numbers, about, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 1.1.10.]]

__III.3
distributive, εἰς φυλάς by tribes, [LXX.1Ki.10.21, cf. LXX.2Ki.18.]

__III.4

__IV
to express RELATION, towards, in regard to, ἐξαμαρτεῖν εἰς θεούς [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Prometheus Vinctus” 945, etc.]]; ἁμάρτημα εἴς τινα, αἰτίαι ἐς ἀλλήλους, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Isocrates Orator 8.96, 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 1.66; ὄνειδος ὀνειδίζειν εἴς τινα 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Philoctetes” 522; ἔχθρη ἔστινα 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 6.65; φιλία ἐς ἀμφοτέρους 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 2.9]]; λέγειν ἐς.. [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.86; γνώμη ἀποδεχθεῖσα ἐς τὴν γέφυραν [prev. author] 4.98; ἡ ἐς γῆν καὶ θάλασσαν ἀρχή 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 8.46.]]

__IV.b
of the subject of a work, especially in titles, e.g. τὰ ἐς Ἀπολλώνιον [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd-3rd c.AD: Philostratus Sophista “VA”]]; of the object of a dedication, as in titles of hymns, ἐπινίκια, etc.

__IV.2
in regard to, πρῶτος εἰς εὐψυχίαν [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Persae” 326; σκώπτειν ἐς τὰ ῥάκια 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Pax” 740, compare “Eq.” 90; διαβάλλειν τινὰ ἔς τι 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 8.88; αἰτία ἐπιφερομένη ἐς μαλακίαν [prev. author] 5.75; μέμφεσθαι εἰς φιλίαν 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 2.6.30; εἰς τὰ πολεμικὰ καταφρονεῖσθαι [prev. author] “HG” 7.4.30; πόλεως εὐδοκιμωτάτης εἰς σοφίαν 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Apologia” 29d]]; in respect of, εὐτυχεῖν ἐς τέκνα [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Orestes” 542, compare 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Apologia” 35b, etc.; εἰς χρήματα ζημιοῦσθαι [prev. author] “Lg.” 774b, compare 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 22.55]]; ἐς τὰ ἄλλα Th.I.I; εἰς ἄπαντα [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Trachiniae” 489; ἐς τὰ πάνθ᾽ ὁμῶς 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Prometheus Vinctus” 736; εἰς μὲν ταῦτα 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Lysis” 210a]]; τό γ᾽ εἰς ἑαυτόν, τὸ εἰς ἐμέ, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Tyrannus” 706, 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Iphigenia Taurica” 691, compare 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Ichn.” 346; ἐς ὀλίγους μᾶλλον τὰς ἀρχὰς ποιεῖν 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 8.53; ἐς πλείονας οἰκεῖν [prev. author] 2.37]]; for τελεῖν ἐς Ἕλληνας, Βοιωτούς, ἄνδρας, etc., see at {τελέω}.

__IV.3
of Manner, ἐς τὸν νῦν τρόπον [Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. author] 1.6; τίθεμεν τἆλλα εἰς τὸν αὐτὸν λόγο; 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 353d; ἐς ἓν μέλος 3rd c.BC: Theocritus Poeta Bucolicus 18.7: frequently periphrastic for _adverbs_, ἐς κοινὸν φράζειν, λέγειν, 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Prometheus Vinctus” 844, “Eu.” 408]]; ἐς τὸ πᾶν, ={πάντως}, [Refs [[prev. author] “Ag.” 682 (Lyric poetry)]]; ἐς τάχος, ={ταχέως}, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Acharnenses” 686]]; ἐς εὐτέλειαν, ={εὐτελῶς}, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. author] “Av.” 805; ἐς τἀρχαῖον [prev. author] “Nu.” 593; εἰς καλόν 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Tyrannus” 78, compare 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Phaedo” 76e; ἐς δέον γεγονέναι 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.119, compare 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Tyrannus” 1416, and see at {δέον}.]]

__V
ofan end or limit, ἔρχεσθαι, τελευτᾶν, λήγειν ἐς.., to end in.., [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.120, 3.125, 4.39, etc.; ἐς ἑβδομήκοντα ἔτεα ου,ρον ἀνθρώπῳ προτίθημι [prev. author] 1.32]]; καταξαίνειν ἐς φοινικίδα to cut into red rags, [NT+5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Acharnenses” 320 (troch.); στρέφειν τι εἰς αἷμα NT.Rev.11.6]]; εἰς ἄνδρας ἐκ μειρακίων τελευτᾶν, εἰς ἄνδρα γενειᾶν, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Theaetetus” 173b, 3rd c.BC: Theocritus Poeta Bucolicus 14.28; ἐκτρέφειν τὸ σπέρμα εἰς καρπόν 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Oeconomicus” 17.10: so with εἶναι or γίγνομαι]] to form a predicate, ἔσται εἰς ἔθνη [LXX.Gen.17.16; ἐγενήθη εἰς γυναῖκα [prev. work] 20.12]; πιστὸς (i.e. ἦν) εἰς προφήτην [LXX+NT [LXX.1Ki.3.20; ἐγένετο εἰς δένδρον NT.Luke.13.19, +others]]

__V.2
of Purpose or Object, εἰπεῖν εἰς ἀγαθόν, πείσεται εἰς ἀγαθόν, for good, for his good, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 9.102, 11.789; εἰς ἀγαθὰ μυθεῖσθαι 23.305; ἐς πόλεμον θωρήξομαι 8.376, compare 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 7.29, etc.]]; ἐς φόβον to cause fear, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 15.310; ἐς ὑποδήματα δεδόσθαι 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 2.98; κόσμος ὁ εἰς ἑορτάς 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Oeconomicus” 9.6; ἐπιτηδεότατος, εὐπρεπής, ἔς τι 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.115, 2.116]]; εἰς κάλλος ζῆν to live for show, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 8.1.33, compare “Ages.” 9.1; ἐς δαίτην ἐκάλεσσε 3rd c.BC: Callimachus Epicus “Aetia” 1.1.5; εἰς κέρδος τι δρᾶν 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Ph.” III; πάσας φωνὰς ἱέντων εἰς ἀπόφυξιν 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Vespae” 562; εἰς γράμματα παιδὶ δεκετεῖ ἐνιαυτοὶ τρεῖς 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Leges” 809e]]; εἰς τὸ πρᾶγμα εἶναι to be pertinent, to the purpose, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 36.54]]; frequently of expenditure on an object, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [“IG” 22.102.11, 116.41, +others; ἐς τὸ δέον 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Nubes” 859, etc.; ἐς δᾷδα [prev. work] 612.]]

__B
POSITION: εἰς is sometimes parted from its accusative by several words, εἰς ἀμφοτέρω Διομήδεος ἅρματα βήτην [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 8.115; εἰς δὲ μονάρχου δῆμος ἀϊδρίῃ δουλοσύνην ἔπεσεν 6th c.BC: Solon Lyricus 9: seldom (only in Poets)]] put after its case, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 15.59, 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 3.137, 15.541, 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Coloneus” 126 (Lyric poetry)]]: after an adverb, αὔριον ἔς· τῆμος δὲ.. [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 7.318.]]

Abbott-Smith / STEPBible (TBESG)
εἷς
ιά, ἕν, genitive ἑνός, μιᾶς, ἑνός,
cardinal numeral, one;
__1. one, as opposite to many: Mat.25:15, Rom.5:12, 1Co.10:8, al.; as subst., Rom.5:15, Eph.2:14; id. with genitive partit., Mat.5:19, al.; before ἐκ (ἐξ), Mrk.14:18, Jhn.6:8, al.; metaphorically, of union and concord, Jhn.10:30 17:11, Rom.12:4-5, Php.1:27; ἀπὸ μιᾶς (B1., § 44, 1), Luk.14:18; with neg., εἷς. . . οὐ (μή), more emphatic than οὐδείς, no one, none (cl.), Mat.5:18 10:29, Luk.11:46 12:6.
__2. Emphatically, to the exclusion of others;
__(a) a single (one): Mat.21:24, Mrk.8:14; absol., 1Co.9:24, al.; οὐδὲ εἷς, Mat.27:14, Jhn.1:3, Rom.3:10, al.;
__(b) one, alone: Mrk.2:7 10:18, Luk.18:19;
__(with) one and the same: Rom.3:30, 1Co.3:8 11:5 12:11, 1Jn.5:8.
__3. In late Gk., with weakened force, = τις or indef. art. (of. Heb. אֶחָד, Gen.22:13, al.; see B1., § 45, 2; M, Pr., 96 f.): Mat.8:19 19:6, Rev.8:13, al.; εἷς τις (Bl., l.with), Luk.22:50, Jhn.11:49
__4. Distributively: εἷς καστος (cl.), Luk.4:40, Act.2:6, al.; εἷς . . . καὶ εἷς (cl., εἷς μὲν . . . εἷς δέ), Mat.17:4, Mrk.9:5, Jhn.20:12, al. (cf. LXX and use of Heb. אֶחָד, Exo.17:12, al); ὁ εἷς . . . ὁ ἕτερος (ἄλλος) = cl. ὁ μὲν (ἕτερος) . . . ὁ δέ (ἕτερος), Mat.6:24, Luk.7:41, Rev.17:10; καθ᾽ εἷς, εἷς κ. είς (in which καθ᾽ is adverbial, or the expression formed from the analogy of ἕν καθ᾽ ἔν; M, Pr., 105), one by one, severally: Mrk.14:19, Rom.12:5, al.; εἷς τὸν ἕνα = ἀλλήλους (B1., 45, 2; M, Pr., 246), 1Th.5:11.
__5. As ordinal = πρῶτος (like Heb. אֶחָד; Bl., § 45, 1; M, Pr., 95 f.), first: Mat.28:1, Mrk.16:2, al

LSJ / STEPBible (TFLSJ)
εἷς, μίᾰ, ἕν
(μίη only in late Ionic dialect Prose): genitive ἑνός, μιᾶς, ἑνός:—Epic dialect ἕεις [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th-7th c.BC: Hesiodus Epicus “Theogonia” 145, “Anthologia Graeca” 7.341 (5th c.AD: Proclus Philosophus), conjecture in 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 5.603]]:—Doric dialect ἧς [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [3rd c.BC: Rhinthon Comicus 12, “Tab.Heracl.” 1.136]]:—Epic dialect, Aeolic dialect, and Ionic dialect feminine ἴᾰ [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 13.354, probably in 5th c.BC: Hippocrates Medicus “περὶ νούσων” 4.37; _accusative_ ἴαν 7th-6th c.BC: Alcaeus Lyricus 33.6 (probably), 7th-6th c.BC: Sappho Lyrica 69.1 (compare μηδεΐα), 6th c.BC: Corinna Lyrica “Supp.” 2.56, “IG” 9(2).517.22(Thess.); _genitive_ ἰῆς 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 16.173, 24.496; _dative_ ἰῇ 9.319, 11.174, etc.]]: neuter dative (ἰῷ κίον ἤματι) [Refs 5th c.BC+ [6.422. (In Comedy texts οὐδὲ (μηδὲ) εἷς, οὐδὲ (μηδὲ) ἕν, occur, mostly at the end of an iambic trimeter, without elision, 5th c.BC: Cratinus Comicus 302, 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Ranae” 927, “Pl.” 37, 138, +others)]] (Orig. ἕνς, assim. ἔν (δ) probably in [Refs [“Leg.Gort.” 9.50, from *εμς,]] Indo-European sem-(compare ὁμός); μία from sm-ί; ἴα is not related to μία, but probably to pronominal stem i-(Latin is), compareἰός.)

__1
as a Numeral, εἷς κοίρανος ἔστω [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 2.204, etc.]]; strengthened, εἷς οἶος, μία οἴη, a single

__A
one, one alone,[Refs 8th c.BC+ [4.397, 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 7.65; μία μούνη 23.227; εἷς μοῦνος 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.119, 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Plutus” 1053, etc.; εἷς καὶ μόνος 1st c.BC: Dionysius Halicarnassensis 1.74; εἷς ὤν 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Tyrannus” 247, 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Phoenissae” 894, etc.; opposed to πολύς, μία τὰς πολλὰς ψυχὰς ὀλέσασα 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Agamemnon” 1456, compare 1465, “Ch.” 299, etc.]]

__b
emphatically with a superlative, εἷς οἰωνὸς ἄριστος [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 12.243, etc.: frequently in Trag., εἷς ἀνὴρ πλεῖστον..πόνον παρασχών 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Persae” 327; πλείστας ἀνὴρ εἷς.. ἔγημε 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Trachiniae” 460; κάλλιστ᾽ ἀνὴρ εἷς [prev. author] “OT” 1380; ἕνακριθέντ᾽ ἄριστον [prev. author] “Ph.” 1344]]; also in Prose, ἐπὶ πλεῖστον δὴ χλιδῆς εἷς ἀνὴρ ἀπίκετο [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 6.127, compare 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 8.68; Μυτιληναίους μάλιστα δὴ μίαν πόλιν [prev. author] 3.39; πάντων εἷς ἀνὴρ μεγίστων αἴτιος κακῶν 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 18.143]]: without a superlative, Ἐτεοκλέης ἂν εἷς πολὺς κατὰ πτόλιν ὑμνοῖθ᾽ [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Septem contra Thebas” 6.]]

__c
in oppos., made emphatic by the Article, ὁ εἷς, ἡ μία, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 20.272, 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 20.110, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Crito” 48a; τοῦ ἑνὸς οἱ δύο ἀγαθοὶ βελτίους 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Politica” 1287b13, compare 3rd c.BC: Theocritus Poeta Bucolicus 6.22.]]

__d
with a negative, εἷς οὐδείς no single man, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.32; ἓν οὐδὲ ἓν ἴαμα 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 2.51]]; οὐκ ἐν ἄλλῳ ἑνί γε χωρίῳ in no other single country, [Refs [[prev. author] 1.80]]; οὐχ εἷς, i.e. more than one, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Septem contra Thebas” 103, 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Andromache” 96]]; εἷς οὐ.., εἷς μή.., emphatic for οὐδείς, μηδείς, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Thesmophoriazusae” 549, 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 5.6.12]]; more emphatic, οὐδὲ εἷς, μηδὲ εἷς, see at {οὐδείς},{μηδείς}.

__e
εἷς ἕκαστος each one, each by himself, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.123, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Protagoras” 332c, etc.]]; αἴσθησις μία ἑνός (i.e. γένους) one of each, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Metaphysica” 1003b19: _plural_, ἑκάτεροι ἕνες “POxy.” 276.8 (1st c.AD).]]

__f
with κατά, καθ᾽ ἓν ἕκαστον each singly, piece by piece, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.9, etc.]]; καθ᾽ ἕν one by one, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Sophista” 217a, etc.]]; καθ᾽ ἕν, τό, list, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Elephantine Papyri 20.7 (3rd c.BC), etc.]]; καθ᾽ ἕν᾽ ἡμῶν ἕκαστον ἀποστερεῖν to deprive each of us singly, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 21.142, compare 4th-3rd c.BC: Menander Comicus “Ἐπιτρέποντες” 164, 186]]; εἷς κατὰ εἷς one by one, [NT.Mark.14.19]; but καθ᾽ ἓν γίγνεσθαι, εἶναι, to be united, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 8.46, 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Historia Graeca (Hellenica)” 5.2.16.]]

__g
with other Preps., ἓν ἀνθ᾽ ἑνός above all,[Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 331b, “Phlb.” 63c]]; but μίαν ἀντὶ μιᾶς alternately, [Refs [PStrassb. 25.13]], etc.; ἐπὶ μίαν ἑκάστην ῥάβδον τιθέντες θεσπίζουσι one by one, separately, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 4.67; ἐπὶ ἑνός 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Theaetetus” 157a; ἓν ἐφ᾽ ἑνί [prev. author] “Sph.” 229b, “Lg.” 758b: ἓν πρὸς ἕν, with or without συμβάλλειν, in comparisons, 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 4.50, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Leges” 647b; πρὸς ἕν᾽ εἷς 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 21.131: παρ᾽ ἕνα]]alternately, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [2nd c.AD: Lucianus Sophista “Salt.” 12; εἰς ἓν συναγαγεῖν 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Orestes” 1640; ἰσχὺς τοσαύτη εἰς ἓν ξυστᾶσα 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 6.85; εἰς ἓν μοίρας συνέκυρσας 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Andromache” 1172; ἐς μίαν βουλεύειν 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 2.379; in full, ἐς μίαν βουλήν 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 5.111; εἰς μίαν νοεῖν 2nd-3rd c.AD: Aelianus “De Natura Animalium - Ar.Byzantine Epit.” 5.9; ἓν ἐξ ἑνὸς ἐπισεσώρευκεν 2nd c.AD: Arrianus Historicus “Epicteti Dissertationes” 1.10.5, compare 2nd c.AD: Lucianus Sophista “Asin.” 54]]; ἀπὸ μιᾶς with one accord, [NT.Luke.14.18; ὑφ᾽ ἕν]at once, [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd c.AD: Sextus Empiricus Philosophus “adversus Mathematicos” 10.124; also ὑφ᾽ ἓν θέσθαι τὸ ὂν τῷ μὴ ὄντι 3rd c.AD: Plotinus Philosophus 6.2.1]]; compare ὑφέν.

__h
in compound numerals, as an ordinal, τῷ ἑνὶ καὶ τριηκοστῷ [ἔτει] [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 5.89, compare 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 8.109, etc.]]; so in Attic dialect Inscrr., [Refs [“IG” 2.660.30, +others,: later εἷς]] alone,=first, [LXX.Gen.1.5; μιᾷ τοῦ μηνός [prev. work] 8.13.]

__i
μίαν μίαν, ={κατὰ μίαν}, [LXX+5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Fragmenta” 201; εἷς εἷς LXX.1Ch.24.6.]]

__i.2
one, i.e. the same, τώ μοι μία γείνατο μήτηρ [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 3.238, etc.]]; εἷς καὶ ὁ αὐτός one and the same, ἓν καὶ ταὐτὸν ἀριθμῷ [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Metaphysica” 1039a28, etc.; ὑπὸ μίαν καὶ τὰν αὐτὰν ἀρχάν Perictione Philosophus cited in 5th c.AD: Stobaeus, Joannes 3.1.121; ταὐτὸν καὶ ἕν 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Physica” 201b3; so ἓν καὶ ὅμοιον 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Phaedrus” 271a; εἷς καὶ κοινός 1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus 2.699f: with _dative_, ἐμοὶ μιᾶς ἐγένετ᾽ ἐκ ματρός 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Phoenissae” 156; ἐκ μιᾶς οἰνοχόης Ἐπικούρῳ πεπωκότες 1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus 2.1089a.]]

__i.2.b
possessing unity, ἧττον μία ἡ μίμησις ἡ τῶν ἐποποιῶν [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Poetica” 1462b3; λίαν ἓν ποιεῖν τὴν πόλιν [prev. author] “Pol.” 1263b7; τὰ κυρίως ἕνα 5th-6th c.AD: Damascius Philosophus “de Principiis” 437.]]

__i.3
one, opposed to another, ἓν μὲν..ἓν δὲ.. [Refs 8th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Ethica Nicomachea” 1139a6, “Pol.” 1285b38, etc.; ὁ μὲν..εἷς δὲ..εἷς δ᾽ αὖ.. 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 3.421 {εἷσα}, compare 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 369d; εἷς μὲν..ἕτερος δὲ.. 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Historia Graeca (Hellenica)” 1.7.23.]]

__i.4
indefinitely, εἷς τις some one, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Tyrannus” 118, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Gorgias” 471e, etc.; ἐξ ἑνός γέ του τρόπου 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 6.34; rarely τις εἷς 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Antigone” 269, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Parmenides” 145d]]; εἷς γάρ τις ἦν ἕκαστος οὑξειργασμένος each single one was suspected, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Antigone” 262; εἷς ὁστισοῦν 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Politica” 1325b28]]; εἷς ὁ πρῶτος, [Refs 1st c.BC+ [\{1st c.BC-1st c.AD\}: Germanicus Caesar Epigrammaticus]] der erste beste, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Isaeus Orator 8.33, 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 1.9, compare 2nd c.AD: Lucianus Sophista “Herm.” 61]]: alone, like our indefinite Article, a, an, Κάδμου θυγατέρων μιᾷ [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Bacchae” 917]]; εἷς κάπηλος, στρατηγός, [NT+5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Aves” 1292, 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 4.50; εἷς Ἀθηναίων 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 21.87, cf. LXX.Gen.21.15, NT.Matt.21.19, etc.]]; εἷς ἀπό.. [LXX.Lev.6.3(22).]

__i.5
οὐχ εἷς many, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Septem contra Thebas” 103, 3rd c.BC: Callimachus Epicus “Hymnus in Dianam” 33]]; οὐχ εἷς οὐδὲ δύο not one or two only, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 29.12]]; οὐ μίαν οὐδὲ δύο not once nor twice, [LXX+2nd c.BC+ [LXX.4Ki.6.10; ἓν ἢ καὶ δύο ληφθὲν μαρτύριον 2nd c.BC: Polybius Historicus 2.38.10; εἷς ἢ δεύτερος 4th c.AD: Julianus Imperator “Orationes” 6.190d: proverbial, εἷς ἀνὴρ οὐδεὶς ἀνήρ]] one man's no man, [Refs 1st c.AD+ [1st-2nd c.AD: Dio Chrysostomus Sophista 48.10.]]

__i.6
in Mathematics texts, τὸ ἕν unity, opposed to πλῆθος, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Pythagoras Philosophus “fragment” 5, etc.: _plural_, ἕνα]]units, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Metaphysica” 1056b21; ὁ ἀριθμός ἐστιν ἕνα πλείω [prev. author] “Ph.” 207b7; τῶν προτέρων ἑνῶν 5th-6th c.AD: Damascius Philosophus “de Principiis” 460.]]

__i.7
Philos., ἕν, τό, unity, the One, ἐκ πάντων ἓν καὶ ἐξ ἑνὸς πάντα [Refs 5th c.BC+ [1st c.AD(?): Heraclitus 10, compare 5th c.BC: Empedocles Poeta Philosophus 17.1, etc.]]: later indeclinable, ἓν εἶναι τοῦ ἓν παρουσίᾳ [Refs 3rd c.AD+ [3rd c.AD: Plotinus Philosophus 6.6.14, compare 5.5.5.]]

Abbott-Smith / STEPBible (TBESG)
εἰσ-άγω
[in LXX chiefly for בּוֹא, hi. ;]
to bring in: with accusative, Luk.2:27, Jhn.18:16, Act.7:45; before εἰς, Luk.22:54, Act.9:8 21:28-29, 37 22:24, Heb.1:6; ὧδε, Luk.14:21.†
(AS)

---

LSJ / STEPBible (TFLSJ)
εἰσάγω [ᾰ],
Ionic dialect imperfect ἐσάγεσκον [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.196]]: perfect -αγήοχα Epist. Philipp. cited in [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 18.39]]: perfect passive ἐσῆγμαι [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 2.49]]:—lead in or into, especially into one's dwelling, introduce, with doubleaccusative, αὐτοὺς εἰσῆγον θεῖον δόμον [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 4.43]]; Κρήτην εἰσήγαγ᾽ ἑταίρους he led his comrades to Crete,[Refs 5th c.BC+ [3.191; ἐς. τινὰ ἐς.. 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.196, etc.: with _dative_, τινὰ δόμοις 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Alcestis” 1112 codices; εἰ. ψυχᾷ χάριν [prev. author] “Hipp.” 526 (Lyric poetry)]]; ὅταν σε καιρὸς εἰσάγῃ, ={ὅταν καιρὸς ᾖ σὲ εἰσιέναι}, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Electra” 39; νὺξ εἰ. πόνον [prev. author] “Tr.” 29]]:—middle, admit forces into a city, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 8.16, 108]]; take in with one, introduce into a league or conspiracy, Ὀτάνης ἐσάγεται Ἰνταφρένεα [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 3.70]]:— passive, τὴν θερμότητα εἰσάγεσθαι εἰς τοὺς πόρους [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-3rd c.BC: Theophrastus Philosophus “de Igne” 38.]]

__2
ἐσαγαγεῖν or ἐσαγαγέσθαι γυναῖκα to lead a wife into one's house, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 5.40, 6.63.]]

__3
bring in, σῖτον [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 4.26]]; import, οἶνον Ἀθήναζε κατ᾽ ἐμπορίαν [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 35.35]]:—middle, εἰσάγεσθαι καὶ ἐξάγεσθαι [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Respublica Atheniensium” 2.3, compare 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 18.145; εἰ. ὧν ἐνδεεῖς 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Politica” 1257a32:]] —passive, εἰσαγόμενα καὶ ἐξαγ. imports and exports, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. author] “Rh.” 1359b22, compare 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 3.6, “SIG” 37 (Teos, 5th c.BC).]]

__4
εἰ. εἰς τοὺς φράτερας introduce a child to the members of one's φρατρία, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Lysias Orator 30.2 (_passive_), 4th c.BC: Isaeus Orator 3.75, compare 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 57.54; εἰς Κήρυκας 5th-6th c.BC: Andocides Orator 1.127; εἰ. τινὰς εἰς τὴν πολιτείαν 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Politica” 1308a8]]; τινὰς ἐς σπονδάς secure their adhesion, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 5.35]]; ἰατρὸν εἰσάγειν τινί call in a physician for another, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Memorabilia” 2.4.3, compare 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 47.67]]:—middle, of the physician himself when ill, εἰσάγεσθαι ἄλλους ἰατρούς [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Politica” 1287a41.]]

__5
introduce new customs, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 2.49 (_passive_)]]; τελετὰς πονηράς [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Bacchae” 260; σόφισμα [prev. author] “Ph.” 1408; δεινότατον ἔθος εἰς τὴν πολιτείαν 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 19.2]]; εἰ. τὰ εἴδη the doctrineofideas, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Ethica Nicomachea” 1096a13; αὐλὸν καὶ ῥυθμὸν εἰς τὸν πόλεμον ἀντὶ σάλπιγγος 2nd c.BC: Polybius Historicus 4.20.6.]]

__6
δούλιον εἰσᾶγον αἶσαν, for δ. ἆγον εἰς αἶσαν, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Choephori” 77 (Lyric poetry).]]

__II
bring in, bring forward, especially on the stage, χορόν [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Ach.” II; Ἥραν ἠλλοιωμένην 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 381d; δράματα [prev. author] “Ap.” 35b, compare 2nd c.AD: Lucianus Sophista “Hist.Conscr.” 58]]; of an orator, εἰ. σεαυτὸν ποιόν τινα [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Rhetorica” 1417b7]]; represent in art, [Refs 1st c.AD+ [1st c.AD: Cornutus Philosophus “de Natura Deorum” 28, +others (_passive_).]]

__II.2
εἰ. τινὰ εἰς τὴν βουλήν bring a culprit before the Council, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Historia Graeca (Hellenica)” 7.3.5, etc.]]

__II.3
aslaw-term, εἰ. δίκην or γραφήν to bring a cause into court, of the prosecutor, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Eumenides” 580, 582, compare 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 24.10, “PHal.” 1.125, etc.; ὑπόθεσιν “OG” 1669.41 (Egypt, 1st c.AD)]]; also of the εἰσαγωγεύς II, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Antipho Orator 6.42, “IG” 12(7).3.40 (from Arcesine), etc.]]; οἱ δὲ θεσμοθέται εἰσαγόντων εἰς τὴν Ἡλιαίαν Legal cited in [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 21.47.]]

__II.3.b
εἰ. τινά bring forward the case of an officer at the εὔθυναι (which see), [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 18.117]]: generally, bring a person into court, prosecute, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Apologia” 25c, +others]]; in full, εἰ. εἰς δικαστήριον[Refs [[prev. work] 29a, “Grg.” 521c (_passive_),compare “Lg.” 910e, +others]]

__II.4
pay in, τὴν τιμὴν ἐπὶ τὴν δημοσίαν τράπεζαν [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [“IG” 22.1013.28; ἀργύριον “PHib.” 46.18 (3rd c.BC), etc.]]

__II.5
enter, register, [Refs [POxy. 1535.8 (_passive_), etc.]]

__III
introduce to a subject, instruct:—passive, εἰσαγόμενοι, οἱ, beginners, [Refs 1st c.AD+ [1st c.AD: Philo Judaeus 1.175, 2nd c.AD: Galenus Medicus “Libr.Propr.Prooem.”, etc.]]

__IV
intransitive, enter, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [Scholia T. 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 6.252.]]

είσ-ακούω
[in LXX chiefly for שָׁמַע, also for עָנָה, etc. ;]
to listen to, in two senses;
__(a) to obey: 1Co.14:21 (cf. Deu.1:43, Sir.3:6)
__(b) to listen, assent to; pass., to be heard: of persons praying, Mat.6:7, Heb.5:7; of the prayer offered, Luk.1:13, Act.10:31 (cf. Psa.4:2, Sir.34:26); see Cremer, 624).†
(AS)

LSJ / STEPBible (TFLSJ)
εἰσᾰκούω,
hearken or give ear to one, ὡς ἔφατ᾽· οὐδ᾽ ἐσάκουσε.. Ὀδυσσεύς [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 8.97, compare 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 4.133, +others: with _accusative_, φωνὴν ἐσάκουσαν “hymnus ad Cererem” 284, compare 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Hecuba” 559, etc.: with _genitive_ _person_, 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Ajax” 789; τῶν ἐμῶν λόγων 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Iphigenia Aulidensis” 1368: with _dative_ _person_, 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.214, etc.; τινί τι [prev. author] 9.60]]; give way, yield to a request, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 1.126, 3.4]]; of God, τινός or τῆς προσευχῆς [LXX.Psa.4.2, etc.]:—so in passive, of the prayer, [NT.Luke.1.13]; of the person, [NT.Matt.6.7.]

__2
in Poets, simply, hear, τούτου λέγοντος εἰσήκουσ᾽ ἐγώ, ὡς.. [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Trachiniae” 351]]; τίνος βροτῶν λόγον τόνδ᾽ εἰ.; [Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. author] “El.” 884, compare “Aj.” 318, 4th-3rd c.BC: Axiopistus Poeta Ethicus 1.12; ζῶντ᾽ εἰσακούσας παῖδα 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Electra” 416.]]

__3
perceive, feel effect of, τοῦ ἐγκεφάλου ἐσακούσαντος τοῦ τρώματος [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Hippocrates Medicus “προρρητικόν” 2.14.]]

__II
passive in strict sense, ἔξωθεν εἰς τὰς οἰκίας εἰσακούεται μᾶλλον ἢ ἔσωθεν ἔξω [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Problemata” 903b13 (variant{εἴσω ἀκ}.).]]

εἰσ-δέχομαι
[in LXX for קָבַץ ;]
to admit, receive: 2Co.6:17 (LXX) (Cremer, 687).†
(AS)

---

LSJ / STEPBible (TFLSJ)
εἰσδέχομαι,
Ionic dialect ἐσδέκ-, take into, admit, ἐς τὸ ἱρόν [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.144, compare 206: with _accusative_ _person_, 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Tyrannus” 238; εἰ. φρουράν “IG” 22.43.22: with _accusative_ _locative_, οὐκ εἰσεδέξατ᾽ οἶκον 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Supplices” 876: with _dative_, ἄντροις εἰ. τινά]] receive him in the cave, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. author] “Cyc.” 35: rarely with _genitive_, τόνδ᾽ εἰσεδέξω τειχέων,=τειχέων εἴσω ἐδέξω (cf. Scholia (at [prev. work])), 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Phoenissae” 451: with _accusative_ double, ἐσδέξασθαί τινα συνοικιστῆρα]] admit him as a fellow-colonist, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “Fragmenta.” 186; εἰ. τινά ὑπόστεγον 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Trachiniae” 376:]]aorist I εἰσδεχθῆναι in passive sense, [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd c.AD: Lucianus Sophista “Tox.” 30, “Merc.Cond.” 10.]]

εἴσειμι,
infinitive -ιέναι, serving as future to εἰσέρχομαι: imperfect εἰσῄειν:— enter, go into, οὐδ᾽ Ἀχιλῆος ὀφθαλμοὺς εἴσειμι I will not come before Achilles' eyes, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 24.463: more frequently with Preps., οὐκ εἴσειμι μετ᾽ ἀνέρας 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 18.184; παρὰ βασιλέα 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.99; mostly with εἰς, ἐς τὸ μέγαρον [prev. work] 65, etc.]]; πρός τινα [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Philoctetes” 953, 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 2.4.5]]; ἐσιέναι ἐς σπονδάς enter into a treaty, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 5.30: _absolutely_, τὸν εἰσιόντα μῆνα]] the ensuing month, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Andocides Orator 1.42; τὸν εἰσιόντα ἐνιαυτόν 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Ἀθηναίων Πολιτεία” 31.2, compare “POxy.” 1278.17 (3rd c.AD), etc.]]

of the Chorus or actors, come upon the stage, enter, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Leges” 664c]]; τὸ τοὺς τυράννους..εἰσιέναι take the part of king, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 19.247, compare 4th c.AD: Libanius Sophista “Orationes” 30.28.]]

of public speakers, come into the assembly, εἰς ἀγοράν [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 24.60; καθ᾽ ὅτι ἂν ἐσίῃ ἡ πρεσβεία 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 4.118]]; of judges, come into court, εἰ. κρινοῦντες [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 18.210.]]

future -ειεύσομαι: aorist -ήλῠθον, -ῆλθον: in Attic dialect, future is supplied by εἴσειμι, and imperfect by εἰσῄειν:— go in or into, enter, in [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Homerus Epicus and Poets mostly with _accusative_, Φρυγίην εἰσήλυθον 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 3.184; ἀλλ᾽ εἰσέρχεο τεῖχος 22.56; αὐιάν 5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “N.” 10.16]]; ἄλσος, δόμους, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Trachiniae” 1167, 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Alcestis” 563; οἴκαδε 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Historia Graeca (Hellenica)” 5.4.28; οἴκαδε εἰς ἐμαυτοῦ 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Hp.Ma.” 304d]]; εἰσῆλθ᾽ ἑκατόμβας invaded the hecatombs, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 2.321]]: but in Prose mostly with Preps., ἐς οἴκημα [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 1.134, etc.]]; ἐς. ἐς τὰς σπονδάς come into the treaty, [Refs [[prev. author] 5.36]]; εἰς τὸν πόλεμον variant in [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 7.1.27]]; εἰ. εἰς τοὺς ἐφήβους enter the ranks of the Ephebi, [Refs [[prev. author] “Cyr.” 1.5.1]]; also εἰ. πρός τινα enter his house, visit him, [Refs [[prev. work] 3.3.13]]; of a doctor, pay a visit, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [2nd c.AD: Galenus Medicus 18(2).36; εἰ. ἐπὶ τὸ δεῖπνον 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 7.3.21]]: absolutely, of money, etc., come in, προσόδους εἰσελθούσας [Refs [[prev. author] “Vect.” 5.12.]]

__II
of the Chorus, actors, etc., come upon the stage, enter, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 580b, 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 6.1.9, etc.]]; enter the lists, in a contest, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Electra” 700]]; πρός τινα in competition with.., [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 18.319.]]

as law-term, of the accuser, come into court, εἰς ὑμᾶς (i.e. τοὺς δικαστάς) [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 59.1; but also τοὺς ὑπὲρ τῶν κοινῶν -εληλυθότας δικαστάς [prev. author] 18.278.]]

__III.2
of the parties, with accusative, εἰ. τὴν γραφήν enter the charge, [Refs [[prev. author] 18.105; εἰ. δίκας [prev. author] 28.17 (so also εἰ. [τὴν καταχειροτονίαν] [prev. author] 21.6]]; εἰ. λόγον κατά τινος argument Isoc.II).

__III.3
of the accused, come before the court, δεῦρο [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Apologia” 29c; εἰς δικαστήριον [prev. author] “Grg.” 522b; εἰς ὑμᾶς 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 18.103, compare 21.176]]; εἰσελθόντες δ᾽ ὡς ὑμᾶς is probably in [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Rhetorica” 1410a18.]]

__III.4
of the cause, to be brought in, ποῖ οὖν δεῖ ταύτην εἰσελθεῖν τὴν δίκη; [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 35.49.]]

__IV
enter on an office, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Antipho Orator 6.44; ἐς. ἐς τὴν ὑπατείαν 2nd-3rd c.AD: Dio Cassius Historicus 41.39; ἐπὶ τὴν ἀρχήν [prev. author] 64.7.]]

Abbott-Smith / STEPBible (TBESG)
εἰμί,
with various uses and significations, like the English verb to be.
__I. As substantive verb.
__1. Of persons and things, to be, exist: Act.17:28, Jhn.1:1, 8:58, 17:5, al; ὁ ὢν καὶ ὁ ἦν (for past ptcp.), Rev.1:4, 8, 4:8, 11:17, 16:5 (see Swete, Ap., 5; M, Pr., 228); τὰ (μὴ) ὄντα, Rom.4:17, 1Co.1:28.
__2. Of times, events, etc., to be, happen, take place: Mat.24:3, Mrk.14:2, 15:42, Luk.21:23, Jhn.4:6, 23, 5:10, al.
__3. to be present, be in a place, have come: Mat.2:13, 15, Mrk.1:45, 5:21, 15:40, Luk.1:80, 5:29, Jhn.7:30, al.; before εἰς, Mrk.2:1; before  ἐκ, (ἐξ), Mat.1:20, 21:25, Mrk.11:30, Jhn.3:31, al.
__4. Impers.,  ἔστι, ἦν, etc.;
__(a) there is (Fr. il y a), was, etc.: Mat.16:28, Luk.16:19, Jhn.3:1, 5:2, Rom.3:10, al.; with dative (of the possessor; Bl., §37, 3), Mat.16:22, Luk.1:7, Jhn.18.10, Rom.9:2, al.;  ἔστιν ὅς, ὅστις (chiefly in pl), Mat.16:28, 19:2, Mrk.9:1, al.;
__(b) with inf., = ἔξεστιν (which see), it is possible: Heb.9:5, 1Co.11:20, RV (but see ICC, in l.).
__II. As copula uniting subject and predicate.
__1. Expressing simply identity or equivalence: Mat.5:13, 14:15, Luk.1:18, 19, Jhn.1:1, 4:19, Rev.3:9, al. mult.
__2. Explicative, as in parable, figure, type, etc.: Mat.13:19, 1Co.9:2, 10:4, 11:25, Gal.4:24, Rev.17:15, al.; ταῦτ᾽ ἔστιν, Mat.27:46, Mrk.7:2, Rom.7:18 al.; ὅ ἐστιν, Mrk.3:17, Col.1:24, Heb.7:2, al.; akin to this is the sacramental usage: Mat.26:26-28, Mrk.14:22, 24, Luk.22:19, 1Co.11:24 (see ICC on Mk, I Co, ll. with; DB, iii, 148 f.).
__3. C. genitive: qual., etc., Mrk.5:42, Luk.3:23, 1Co.14:33, Heb.12:11, al.; part., 1Ti.1:20, 2Ti.1:15; poss., Mat.5:3, 10, Mrk.12:7, Luk.4:7; of service or partisanship, Rom.8:9, 1Co.1:12, 2Co.10:7, 2Ti.2:19.
__4. C. dative (BL, §37, 3): Act.1:8, 9:15, Rom.4:12, 1Co.1:18, 2:14, Rev.21:7, al.
__5. C. ptcp., as a periphrasis for the simple verb (Bl., §62, 1, 2; M, Pr., 225 ff.);
__(a) with ptcp. pf. (cl.): Mat.10:30, Luk.9:32, Jhn.3:24, Act.21:35, 1Co.15:19, al;
__(b) with ptcp. pr. (esp. in impf., as in Heb. and Aram.; Dalman, Words, 35 f.), Mat.7:29, Mrk.1:22, Luk.4:31, 14:1, Act.1:10, al. mult., id. for imper. (M, Pr., 180f., 182f.), with ellipsis of εἰμί, Rom.12:9, 10, Heb.13:5, al.;
__(with) with ptcp. aor. (cl), Luk.23:9.
__6. Seq. εἰς (cf. Heb. הָיָה לְ), a vernac. usage (M, Pr., 71): Mat.19:5, Mrk.10:8, Heb.8:10, al.
__7. C. adv.: Mat.19:20, Mrk.4:26, Luk.18:11, al.
__8. Ellipses;
__(a) of the copula (Bl., §30, 3): Mat.8:29, 24:32, Jhn.21:22, 23, Heb.6:4, al.;
__(b) of the predicate: ἐγώ εἰμί, Mat.14:27, Mrk.6:50, al.; absol. (cf. Deu.32:39; אֲנִי הוּא), Mrk.13:6, Jhn.4:26, al. (cf. ἄπ-, ἔν-, πάρ-, συμ-πάρ-, σύν-ειμι).
(AS)
