LSJ / STEPBible (TFLSJ)
δόξᾰ, ἡ,
(δοκέω, δέκομαι) expectation, οὐδ᾽ ἀπὸ δόξης not otherwise than one expects, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 10.324, 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 11.344; in Prose, παρὰ δόξαν ἢ ὡς κατεδόκεε 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.79, etc.]]; ἐν δόξᾳ θέμενος εὖχος hoping for.., [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “O.” 10(11).63]]; δόξαν παρέχειν τινὶ μὴ ποιήσεσθαι.. to make one expect that.., [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Historia Graeca (Hellenica)” 7.5.21]]; δόξαν παρέχεσθαί τινι ὡς.., with participle, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Sophista” 216d]]; ἀπὸ τῆς δ. πεσέειν, = Latin spe excidere, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 7.203.]]

__II
after [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Homerus Epicus]], notion, opinion, judgement, whether well grounded or not, βροτῶν δόξαι [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Parmenides Poeta Philosophus 1.30, compare 8.51; ψυχῆς εὐτλήμονι δόξῃ 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Persae” 28 (_anapaest meter_); ἃ δόξῃ τοπάζω 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Fragmenta” 235; δόξῃ γοῦν ἐμῇ [prev. author] “Tr.” 718]]; κατά γε τὴν ἐμήν, with or without δόξαν, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Gorgias” 472e, “Phlb.” 41b: opposed to ἐπιστήμη, [prev. author] “Tht.” 187bf, “R.” 506c, 5th c.BC: Hippocrates Medicus “νόμος” 4, 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Metaphysica” 1074b36; φάσεις καὶ δ. [prev. author] “EN” 1143b13]]; opposed to νόησις, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 534a]]; ἀληθεῖ δόξῃ δοξασταί capable of being subjects of true opinion, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [[prev. author] “Tht.” 202b; δ. ἀληθεῖς ἢ ψευδεῖς [prev. author] “Phlb.” 36c; δόξης ὀρθότης ἀλήθεια 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Ethica Nicomachea” 1142b11; δ. ἐμποιεῖν περί τινος [prev. author] “Pol.” 1314b22]]; κύριαι δ. philosophical maxims, title of work by Epicurus, [Refs 1st c.BC+ [1st c.BC: Philodemus Gadarensis Epigrammaticus “Ir.” p.86 W., etc.; αἱ κοιναὶ δ.]]axioms, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Metaphysica” 996b28.]]

__II.2
mere opinion, conjecture, δόξῃ ἐπίστασθαι, ἡγεῖσθαι, imagine, suppose (wrongly), [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 8.132, 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 5.105; δόξης ἁμαρτία [prev. author] 1.32]]; δόξαι joined with φαντασίαι, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Theaetetus” 161e, compare 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Physica” 254a29 (but distinguished from φαντασίαι, [prev. author] “de An.” 428a20)]]; κατὰ δόξαν, opposed to κατ᾽ οὐσίαν, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 534c]]; ὡς δόξῃ χρώμενοι speaking by guess, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Isocrates Orator 8.8, compare 13.8.]]

__II.3
fancy, vision, δ. ἀκόνας λιγυρᾶς [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “O.” 6.82; δ. βριζούσης φρενός 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Agamemnon” 275; οὐκ εἰσὶ δόξαι τῶνδε πημάτων [prev. author] “Ch.” 1053, compare 1051]]; of a dream, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Rhesus” 780; δ. ἐνυπνίου 2nd-3rd c.AD: Philostratus Sophista “Vita Apollonii” 1.23]]: plural, hallucinations, [Refs 6th c.AD+ [6th c.AD: Alexander Trallianus Medicus 1.17.]]

__III
the opinion which others have of one, estimation, repute, first in [Refs 6th c.BC+ [6th c.BC: Solon Lyricus 13.4 ἀνθρώπων δόξαν ἔχειν ἀγαθήν, compare 34; δ. ἐπ᾽ ἀμφότερα φέρεσθαι 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 2.11.]]

__III.2
mostly, good repute, honour, glory, [Refs 7th c.BC+ [7th-6th c.BC: Alcaeus Lyricus “Supp.” 25.11, 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Eumenides” 373 (Lyric poetry, _plural_), 5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “O.” 8.64, etc.; δόξαν φύσας 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 5.91]]; δόξαν σχεῖν τινός for a thing, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Hercules Furens” 157; ἐπὶ σοφίᾳ δ. εἰληφώς 5th-6th c.BC: Isocrates Orator 13.2; ἐπὶ καλοκἀγαθίᾳ καὶ σωφροσύνῃ δ. ὁμολογουμένην πεποιημένος 2nd c.BC: Polybius Historicus 35.4.8; δόξαν ἀντὶ τοῦ ζῆν ᾑρημένος 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 2.15; δόξαν εἶχον ἄμαχοι εἶναι 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Menexenus” 241b]]; δ. ἔχειν ὥς εἰσι.. [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 2.17; δ. καταλιπεῖν [prev. author] 3.24: in _plural_, οἱ ἐν ταῖς μεγίσταις δόξαις ὄντες 5th-6th c.BC: Isocrates Orator 4.51.]]

__III.3

(ἐκεῖ), [in LXX chiefly for הַהוּא ,הוּא, and cogn. forms ;]
demonstr. pron.,
that person or thing (ille), implying remoteness as compared with οὗτος (hic);
__1. absol., emphatic he, she, it: opposite to οὗτος, Luk.18:14, Jas.4:15; ἡμεῖς, Heb.12:25; ὑμεῖς, Mrk.4:11; ἄλλοι, Jhn.9:9; ἐγώ, Jhn.3:30; to persons named, Mk 16:[10, 13, 20], Jhn.2:21; of one (absent) who is not named, contemptuously (Abbott, JG, §§2385,  2732), Jhn.7:11 9:28; with respect, of Christ, 1Jo.2:6 3:3, al.; referring to a preceding noun, Mrk.16:[10], Jhn.7:45; resumption of a participial subject, Jhn.1:33 9:37 10:1, Rom.14:14, al. (on its reference in Jhn.19:35, see Westc, in l.; Moffatt, Intr., 568; Sanday, Fourth Gospel, 77ff.).
__2. As adj., joined, like οὗτος, to a noun with the article: Mat.7:25, Mrk.3:24, Jhn.18:15, al.; esp. of time, past or future: ἐν τ. ἡμέραις ἐ., Mat.3:1, Mrk.1:9, Act.2:18" (LXX), al.; ἐν ἐ. τ. ἡμέρᾳ, esp of the Parousia, Mat.7:22, Luk.6:23, 2Th.1:10, 2Ti.1:12; adverbially, ἐκεινής (sc. ὁδοῦ) = cl. ἐκεινῇ (Bl., §36, 13), that way, Luk.19:4.

publish, deliver, χρηστήριον [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 5.79; ἐ. λόγον 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Trachiniae” 741, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Menexenus” 236c, compare 1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus “Themistocles” 23; εἰς τοὺς Ἕλληνας τὰ τῆς πόλεως ἁμαρτήματα 5th-6th c.BC: Isocrates Orator 8.14]]; of public measures, refer, ἐξενεῖκαι ἐς τὸν δῆμον [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 9.5; ἐς πολύφημον ἐξενείκαντας [prev. author] 5.79]]; ἐ. προβούλευμα εἰς τὸν δῆμον bring a project of law before the people, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 59.4]] (so in middle, ἐκφέρεσθαι προβούλευμα εἰς τὴν ἐκκλησίαν [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aeschines Orator 3.125)]]: absolutely, frequently in Attic dialect Inscrr., ἡ δὲ βουλὴ ἐς τὸν δῆμον ἐξενεγκέτω ἐπάναγκες [Refs [“IG” 12.76.61, compare 22.360.47]]; of authors, publish a work, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Isocrates Orator 9.74, 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Poetica” 1447b17, 1st c.BC: Dionysius Halicarnassensis “de Compositione Verborum” 1, 1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus 2.10c, etc.:]] —middle, ἐκφέρεσθαι γνώμην declare one's opinion, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Isocrates Orator 5.36]]:—passive, εἰς Ἕλληνας ἐξοισθήσεται [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Supplices” 561.]]

__II.4
produce, exhibit, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Lysias Orator 19.30]]; display, δείγματα εἰς φῶς [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Leges” 788c, compare 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 19.12; φανερῶς τὸ μῖσος εἴς τινας 2nd c.BC: Polybius Historicus 15.27.3; ἐ. τὴν ἰατρικὴν ἐπιστήμην 1st c.BC: Diodorus Siculus Historicus 5.74.]]

__II.5
disclose, τι πρὸς τὸν μάγον [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 3.71]]; τὴν ἀπάτην[Refs [[prev. work] 74; τὴν ἐπιχείρησιν [prev. author] 8.132.]]

__II.6
put forth, exert, δύνασιν [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Ion” 1012]]:—and in middle, μέγα τι σθένος ἁ Κύπρις ἐκφέρεται νίκας [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Trachiniae” 497 (Lyric poetry).]]

__II.7
ἐ. πόλεμον begin war, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 1.21; ἐπί τινα 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 6.56; πρός τινα 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Historia Graeca (Hellenica)” 3.5.1; τινί 2nd c.BC: Polybius Historicus 2.36.4, etc.]]

__II.8
show the marks of, betray, reproduce, ἐκφέρουσι γὰρ μητρῷ᾽ ὀνείδη [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Andromache” 621.]]

__II.9
ὅρον ἐ. produce a definition, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Metaphysica” 1040b2]]; express, διάνοιαν [Refs 1st c.BC+ [1st c.BC: Philodemus Philosophus “περὶ ποιημάτων” 5.26, +others]]; 'word' a sentence, [Refs 1st c.BC+ [1st c.BC: Dionysius Halicarnassensis “de Compositione Verborum” 3 (_passive_), 7]]; utter, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demetrius Phalereus Rhetor “Demetrius on Style” 94]]; cite, adduce, [Refs [[prev. work] 142]]; πρὸς ἑαυτὸν ἐ. soliloquize, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [Scholia 5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “O.” 1.5.]]

__II.9.b
pronounce, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [2nd c.AD: Athenaeus Epigrammaticus 3.94f; ὅταν μακρῶς ἐκφέρηται 1st c.BC: Dionysius Halicarnassensis “de Compositione Verborum” 15, compare 4th c.BC: Archytas Tarentinus Philosophus 1, 1st c.BC-1st c.AD: Strabo Geographus 9.5.17.]]

__II.10
pay as indemnity, δισχίλια τάλαντα [Refs 2nd c.BC+ [2nd c.BC: Polybius Historicus 3.27.5, etc.]]

__II.10.b
passive, of words, to be formed, κατὰ μίμησιν [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demetrius Phalereus Rhetor “Demetrius on Style” 220; ἐπιρρηματικῶς 2nd c.AD: Apollonius Dyscolus Grammaticus “de Adverbiis;” 175.28; διὰ τοῦ ε ¯ ἐ. [prev. work] 193.5.]]

__II.11
exact, ἀργύριον [LXX.2Ki.15.20.]

__III
passive, to be carried beyond bounds, ἔξω ὅρων ἐξενεχθὲν ἀκόντιον [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Antipho Orator 3.2.4]]: mostly metaphorically, to be carried away by passion, ἀπαιδευσίᾳ ὀργῆς [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 3.84, compare 3rd c.BC: Chrysippus Stoicus 3.127]]; πρὸς ὀργὴν ἐκφέρει givest way to passion, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Electra” 628]]; ἐ. πρὸς αἰδῶ is inclined to feel respect, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Alcestis” 601 (Lyric poetry); λέγων ἐξηνέχθην 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Cratylus” 425a; ἐξενεχθεὶς ὥστε κωμῳδοποιὸς γενέσθαι [prev. author] “R.” 606c; πρὸς τὸ ἄγριοι πολῖται γενέσθαι 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 1.6.34]]; πάθος defined as ὁρμὴ ἐκφερομένη καὶ ἀπειθὴς λόγῳ [Refs [“Stoicorum Veterum Fragmenta” 3.92]]:—later in active, [θυμὸς] ἐ. τινὰ τοῦ λογισμοῦ [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd-3rd c.AD: Philostratus Sophista “Philostrati majoris imagines” 2.21.]]

__IV
bring to one's end, bring on to the trail, εὖ δέ σ᾽ ἐκφέρει.. βάσις [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Ajax” 7]]; κινδυνεύει ὥσπερ ἀτραπός [τις] ἐκφέρειν ἡμᾶς [ἐν τῇ σκέψει] [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Phaedo” 66b, compare “IG” 12.94.37:]] —passive, ἐξηνέχθην εἰς ἅπερ Πρωταγόρας λέγει [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Cratylus” 386a.]]

__V
intransitive (i.e. ἑαυτόν) shoot forth (before the rest), ὦκα δ᾽ ἔπειτα αἱ Φηρητιάδαο.. ἔκφερον ἵπποι· τὰς δὲ μέτ᾽ ἐξέφερον Διομήδεος.. ἵπποι [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 23.376, compare 759]]; also, to run away, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “de Equitandi ratione” 3.4.]]

__V.2
come to fulfilment, ὁρᾷς τὰ τοῦδε.. ὡς ἐς ὀρθὸν ἐκφέρει μαντεύμᾰτα [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Coloneus” 1424]]; come to an end, [Refs [[prev. author] “Tr.” 824 (Lyric poetry).]]

ἐκ-φεύγω
[in LXX for נוּס, etc. ;]
to flee away, escape: absol., Act.16:27, 1Th.5:3, Heb.2:3; before ἐκ, Act.19:10; with accusative of person(s), Heb.12:25; with accusative of thing(s), Luk.21:36, Rom.2:3; τ. χεῖρας αὐτοῦ, 2Co.11:33.†

---

LSJ / STEPBible (TFLSJ)
ἐκ-φεύγω,
future -ξομαι[Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Vespae” 157, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Symposium” 189b]], and -ξοῦμαι [Refs [[prev. author] “R.” 432d]]:—flee out or away, escape: absolutely, ἐκφυγέειν μεμαώς [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 19.231, compare 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Persae” 510, etc.; φεύγων ἐκφεύγειν 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 5.95.]]

__b
of persons accused, to be acquitted, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Vespae” 157.]]

__2
with genitive, escape out of, ἐξέφυγον πολιῆς ἁλὸς ἤπειρόνδε [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 23.236; νούσου “epigram Gr.” 1041.9]]; of things, βέλος ἔκφυγε χειρός [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 5.18: with _preposition_, ματρὸς ἐκ κόλπων “APl.” 4.182 (1st c.AD: Leonidas Alexandrinus Epigrammaticus).]]

__3
with accusative, escape, ἐξ αὖ νῦν ἔφυγες θάνατον [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 11.362; κῆρας 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 4.512; κακότητα 5.414; θανάτοιο τέλος 7th c.BC: Archilochus Lyricus 6; νοῦσον 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.25; Σκύθας [prev. author] 6.40; τὴν πεπρωμένην 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Prometheus Vinctus” 518; τὰν θεῶν νέμεσιν 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Philoctetes” 518 (Lyric poetry), etc.]]

__3.b
simply, to have escaped, to be beyond, οὐ πολλὰ ἐκφεύγεις παιδιὰς ἔτη [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Politicus” 268e.]]

__3.c
of things, ἐκπεφεύγασιν γάμοι με [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Helena” 1622; ἐκφύγοι τὰ πράγματ᾽ αὐτόν 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 18.33, compare 19.123]]; ἐ. τὰς αἰσθήσεις escape one's sense, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Fragmenta” 208]]; also, escape one's lips, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Lysis” 213d: _absolutely_, ἐκφεύγει τἀμελούμενον 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Tyrannus” 111, compare 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Metaphysica” 1090b21.]]

__3.d
ἐκφεύγοντες τὴν χιόνα τόποι places free from snow, [Refs 2nd c.BC+ [2nd c.BC: Polybius Historicus 3.55.7.]]

__3.e
Astron., of stars, emerge from the Sun's rays, become visible, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Autolycus Astronomus 1.9, 1st c.BC: Geminus Astronomicus 13.9, etc.]]

__3.f
pass over, omit, [Refs 1st c.BC+ [1st c.BC: Apollonius Citiensis Medicus 1.]]

__4
with infinitive (with or without Article), [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Sophista” 235b]]; οὐκ ἐκφεύγει μὴ οὐκ εἶναι.. [Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. author] “Phdr.” 277e; τὸ μὴ ἕτερα εἶναι [prev. author] “Prm.” 147a; ἐ. τὸ ἀποθανεῖν [prev. author] “Ap.” 39a; μικρὸν ἐξέφυγε μὴ καταπετρωθῆναι 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 1.3.2]]; ἐκφεύξεται τὰ δύο will not admit of duality, [Refs 3rd c.AD+ [3rd c.AD: Plotinus Philosophus 3.8.9.]]

LSJ / STEPBible (TFLSJ)
ἐκφύω,
generate: mostly of the male, beget, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Tyrannus” 437, 827, etc.]]; ὃς ἐξέφυσεν Ἀερόπης λέκτρων ἄπο Ἀγαμέμνον᾽ [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Helena” 391.]]

__2
rarely of the female, bear, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Coloneus” 984.]]

__3
generally, produce, ἡ γῆ κατὰ καιρὸν ἐκφύουσα πάντα [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “de Mundo” 397a26; ἐ. κέρατα [prev. author] “HA” 611b13]]: absolutely, of seed, germinate, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 24.154.]]

__II
passive, with perfect and aorist 2 active, to be engendered, born from, κεφαλαὶ τρεῖς ἑνὸς αὐχένος ἐκπεφυυῖαι (Epic dialect perfect participle) [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 11.40]]; πατρός, μητρὸς ἐκφῦναι, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Ajax” 487, 1295, 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Ion” 542]]; λάληα ἐκπεφυκός a born tattler, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Antigone” 320.]]

__II.2
grow, of hair, μέχρις ἂν [αἱ τρίχες] ἐκφυῶσι [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd c.AD: Archigenes Medicus cited in 2nd c.AD: Galenus Medicus 12.407]]; spring, take rise, of muscles, [Refs [[prev. work]18(2).981.]]

__III
intransitive in present active, ἕλκεα ἐκφύουσιν [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Hippocrates Medicus “ἐπιδημίαι” 6.5.15, compare 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Problemata” 883b26.]]

to pour out: φιάλην, Rev.16:1-4, 8 16:10, 12 16:17; κέρματα, Jhn.2:15; αἷμα, Mat.23:35 (cf. MM, Exp., xii), Luk.11:50, Act.22:20, Rom.3:15" (LXX) Rev.16:6. Sir.36:8, ὀργήν); pass., of persons (like Lat. effundor), to give oneself up to (RV, ran riotously in): Ju 11.†

ἐκχέω
(laterἐκφων-χύνω [NT.Matt.23.35 (_passive_)], etc., condemned by [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd c.AD: Lucianus Sophista “Pseudol.” 29),]]future -χέω (see. χέω): aorist 1 ἐξέχεα (also imperative ἔκχυσον [Refs 5th c.AD+ [5th c.AD(?): Hesychius Legal icographus)]]; Epic dialect aorist middle ἐκχευάμην [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 24.178]]: perfect ἐκκέχῠκα [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-3rd c.BC: Menander Comicus 915]]:—pour out, properly of liquids, οἶνον [NT+8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 3.296; αἷμ᾽ ἐκχέας πέδοι 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Eumenides” 653, cf. NT.Matt.23.35 (_passive_)]]; ἀναίτιον αἷμα [Refs 2nd c.BC+ [“SIG” 1181.5 (Jewish, 2nd c.BC)]]; πηγάς [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Hercules Furens” 941; δάκρυα 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Symposium” 215e (_passive_), 1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus “Alcibiades” 6; ὁ οἶνος ἐκχεῖται]]is spilt,  [NT.Matt.9.17: _metaphorically_, (in _middle_) ταχέας δ᾽ ἐκχεύατ᾽ ὀϊστούς] he poured forth his arrows, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 22.3, 24.178; σοὶ.. δαίμονες.. ἐλπίδας ἐξέχεαν 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Epigrammata - PLG” 7.4.]]

__b
pour away: hence, spill, a vessel, ποδάνιπτρον [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Fragmenta” 306]]; τὸν χόα Men.[same place]:—passive, to be drained, εἰς [διώρυχα] [Refs 1st c.AD+ [“PRyl.” 154.18 (1st c.AD).]]

__2
of words, pour forth, utter, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Thesmophoriazusae” 554; μολπάς 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Supplices” 773; πολλὴν γλῶσσαν ἐκχέας μάτην 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Fragmenta” 929, compare 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Agamemnon” 1029 (Lyric poetry).]]

__3
pour out like water, squander, waste, ὄλβον [Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. author] “Pers.” 826; τὰ πάντα [prev. author] “Ch.” 520, compare 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Electra” 1291; πλοῦτον ἐξέχεεν εἰς δαπάνας “Anthologia Graeca” 9.367 (2nd c.AD: Lucianus Sophista); ἐ. τά τε αὑτοῦ καὶ ἑαυτόν 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 553b]]; spoil, τὸ πᾶν σόφισμα [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Philoctetes” 13.]]

__4
spread out, λίνα, ὀθόνας, [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [3rd c.BC: Apollonius Rhodius Epicus 2.902 (tmesis), 2nd c.AD: Lucianus Sophista “Am.” 6.]]

__5
throw down, τινὰ κατὰ τοῦ κρηνοῦ [Refs 1st c.BC+ [1st c.BC: Dionysius Halicarnassensis 13.8, compare 4.7, 14.10.]]

__6
ὕπνον ἐ. shed, i.e. shake off sleep, [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [3rd c.BC: Herodas Mimographus 7.7.]]

__7

__2

LSJ / STEPBible (TFLSJ)
ἐλασσ-όω,
Attic dialect ἐλαττόω: aorist ἠλάττωσα [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Lysias Orator 13.9, 2nd c.BC: Polybius Historicus 16.21.5]]: perfect ἠλλάττωκα [Refs 1st c.BC+ [1st c.BC: Dionysius Halicarnassensis “de Compositione Verborum” 6, etc.]]:—passive, future -ωθήσομαι[Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 5.34, 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 21.66]]: future middle in same sense, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 6.11, 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 5.104:]]aorist ἠλασσώθην, -ττώθην, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [[prev. author] 1.77, 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 10.33]]: perfect ἠλάττωμαι [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-3rd c.BC: Apollodorus Comicus 7.3, 2nd c.BC: Polybius Historicus 18.4.3]]:—make less or smaller, diminish, reduce in amount, [Refs 2nd c.BC+ [PTeb. 19.11 (2nd c.BC), “PLips.” 105.28 (1st c.AD)]]:—passive, [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [“POxy.” 918xi3 (2nd c.AD).]]

__2
in early writers, lower, degrade, τὴν πόλιν [LXX+5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Lysias Orator 13.9, 5th-6th c.BC: Isocrates Orator 8.17; ἠλάττωσας αὐτὸν βραχύ τι παρ᾽ ἀγγέλους LXX.Psa.8.6]]; cut down, shorten, συναλοιφαῖς τὰ ῥήματα [Refs 1st c.BC+ [1st c.BC: Dionysius Halicarnassensis “de Compositione Verborum” 6]]: with genitive, detract from, μὴ προστιθέναι τιμήν, ἀλλὰ μὴ ἐλασσοῦν τῆς ὑπαρχούσης [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 3.42]]:—middle, reduce the power of, τινάς [Refs 2nd c.BC+ [2nd c.BC: Polybius Historicus 22.15.1.]]

__II
passive,

__II.1
absolutely, to be lessened, suffer loss, be depreciated, of things, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 2.62]]; of persons, [NT+4th c.BC+ [[prev. author] 4.59, +others, “OGI” 139.10(2nd c.BC), “PTeb.” 382.13 (1st c.BC), 1st c.BC: Philodemus Philosophus “περὶ παρρησίας” p.32 O., +others, NT.John.3.30, etc.; μέγα τοῦθ᾽ οἱ πατέρες ἠλαττώμεθα 4th-3rd c.BC: Apollodorus Comicus 7.3]]; also, take less than one's due, waive one's rights or privileges, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 1.77, 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 56.14]]; but, fall short of one's professions, act dishonestly, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Isocrates Orator 1.49.]]

__II.2
with dative of things, have the worst of it, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 6.11, 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 5.104, etc.; τῷ πολέμῳ [prev. author] 1.115]]; to be inferior, τῇ ἐμπειρίᾳ [Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. author] 5.72; πολλαῖς ναυσί 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Historia Graeca (Hellenica)” 1.5.15; πᾶσι τούτοις [prev. work] 6.2.28]]; ἠλαττωμένος τοῖς ὄμμασι, of a one-eyed man, [Refs 2nd c.BC+ [2nd c.BC: Polybius Historicus 18.4.3; πρός τινα “POxy.” 215ii18]]: with genitive, fall short of, τῶν ἀρχετύπων [Refs 1st c.AD+ [1st c.AD: Philo Judaeus 1.606.]]

__II.3
with genitive person, to be at a disadvantage with a person, πολλὰ μὲν οὖν ἔγωγ᾽ ἐλαττοῦμαι κατὰ τουτονὶ τὸν ἀγῶν᾽ Αἰσχίνου [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 18.3; ἐλαττοῦσθαί τινός τινι 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus Alcaeus1.121b; μηδὲν τῶν δημιουργῶν [prev. author] “Grg.” 459c.]]

__II.4
with genitive of things, suffer loss in respect of, κεφαλαίου, τόκων, [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [“BGU” 155.10 (2nd c.AD)]]; to be in want of, [LXX.1Ki.21.15(16): also with _dative_, LXX.2Ki.3.29.]

ἐς τὴν ἀγορὴν τὸ ζεῦγος 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.59]]; ἐ. ἵππον ride it, [Refs [[prev. author] 4.64, +others]]; κέλητας καὶ ἅρματα ἐ. ride and drive, [Refs [[prev. author] 7.86]]; ἐ. νῆα row it, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 12.109, etc.]]; στρατὸν ἐ. [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “O.” 10(11).66, 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.176, 4.91, etc.]]

__b
with accusative omitted, intransitive, go in a chariot, drive, μάστιξεν δ᾽ ἐλάαν (i.e. ἵππους) he whipped them on, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 5.366, +others, compare 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Electra” 734, 739]]; βῆ δ᾽ ἐλάαν ἐπὶ κύματα he drove on over the waves, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 13.27]]; διὰ νύκτα ἐλάαν travel the night through, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 15.50]]; ἐς τὸ ἄστυ ἐ. drive into the city, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.60; ἐπὶ ζευγέων ἐ. [prev. work] 199]]; ride, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. author] 7.88, 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “de Equitum magistro” 3.9, etc.]]; ἐλῶν ἐς Θρηΐκην marching.., [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 9.89, etc.]]; row, μάλα σφοδρῶς ἐλάαν [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 12.124]]; ἐλαύνοντες rowers, [Refs [13.22, etc.]]

__c
in this intransitive sense, it sometimes took an accusative loci, γαλήνην ἐλαύνειν to sail the calm sea, i.e. over it, [Refs [7.319]]; so τὰ ἕσπερα νῶτ᾽ ἐ. [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Electra” 731 (Lyric poetry)]]; also ἐλαύνειν δρόμον run a course, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Nubes” 28; ὁδόν 2nd c.AD: Dionysius Periegeta 586.]]

__d
passive, [νηῦς] ἐλαυνομένη a ship under way, [NT+8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 13.155 (but πλοῖα ὑπὸ σκληρῶν ἀνέμων ἐλαυνόμενα NT.Jam.3.4)]]; τὰ κατάντη ἐλαύνεσθαι, of horses, to be ridden on steep ground, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “de Equitum magistro” 8.3.]]

__2
drive away, carry off, in [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Homerus Epicus]] of stolen cattle or horses, βοῶν ἀρίστας [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 12.353; ἵππους 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 5.236; ἐ. ὅ τι δύναιντο 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Historia Graeca (Hellenica)” 4.8.18]]:—middle, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 4.637, 20.51; ῥύσι᾽ ἐλαυνόμενος 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 11.674, etc.]]

__3
drive away, expel, ἐ. [τινὰ] ἐκ δήμου [Refs 5th c.BC+ [6.158; ἄνδρας ἀπ᾽ Οἰνώνας 5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “N.” 5.16: frequently in Trag., ἐ. τινὰ γῆς 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Medea” 70]]; μύσος, μίασμα ἐ., [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Choephori” 967 codices, “Eu.” 283 (_passive_),compare 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Tyrannus” 98]]; ἄγος ἐ.,= ἀγηλατέω, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 1.126; ἐ. λῃστάς 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Acharnenses” 1188, etc.]]:—passive, γῆν πρὸ γῆς ἐλαύνομαι [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Prometheus Vinctus” 682.]]

__4
drive (to extremities), persecute, plague, οἵ μιν ἄδην ἐλόωσι.. πολέμοιο who will harass him till he has had enough of war, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 13.315]]; ἔτι μέν μίν φημι ἄδην λάαν κακότητος I think I shall persecute him till he has had enough, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 5.290; θεὸς ἐλαύνει πόλιν 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Tyrannus” 28; Ἰωνίαν ἤλασεν βίᾳ 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Persae” 771; μή τι δαιμόνιον τὰ πράγματα ἐλαύνῃ 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 9.54; σὺ δ᾽ ἀπειλεῖς πᾶσιν, ἐλαύνεις πάντας [prev. author] 21.135, compare 173]]:—passive, ἐλαυνομένων καὶ ὑβριζομένων [Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. author] 18.48; λύπῃ πᾶς ἐλήλαται κακῇ 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Ajax” 275; κακοῖς πρός τινος 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Andromache” 31; ὑπ᾽ ἀνάγκης καὶ οἴστρου 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Phaedrus” 240d; τὴν ψυχὴν ἐρωτικῇ μανίᾳ 2nd-3rd c.AD: Aelianus “De Natura Animalium - Ar.Byzantine Epit.” 14.18]]; ἐλαύνεσθαι τὴν γνώμην to be out of one's mind, [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd-3rd c.AD: Philostratus Sophista “Vitae Sophistarum” 2.27.5.]]

__5
={βινέω}, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Ecclesiazusae” 39, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus Comedy texts 3.4.]]

__6
intransitive in expressions like{ἐς τοσοῦτον ἤλασαν} they drove it so far (where πρᾶγμα must be supplied), [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 5.50; ἐς πᾶσαν κακότητα [prev. author] 2.124]]; εἰς κόρον ἐλαύνειν push matters till disgust ensued, [Refs 7th c.BC+ [7th c.BC: Tyrtaeus Elegiacus 11.10]]; εἰς ἴσον (i.e. τισί) [Refs 1st c.AD+ [1st c.AD: Onosander (Onasander) Tacticus “Praef.” 4]]: hence, push on, go on, ἐγγὺς μανιῶν [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Heraclidae” 904 (Lyric poetry)]]; ἔξω τοῦ φρονεῖν [Refs [[prev. author]]]*ba.[Refs [853]]; πόρρω ἐ. σοφίας go far in.., [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Euthyphro” 4b, compare “Grg.” 486a, 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 1.6.39.]]

__II
strike, ἐλάτῃσιν πόντον ἐλαύνοντες [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 7.6; κιθάραν πλήκτρῳ 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Hercules Furens” 351 (Lyric poetry).]]

__II.2
strike with a weapon, but never with a missile, τὸν σκήπτρῳ ἐλάσασκεν [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 2.199; ξίφει ἤλασε κόρσην 5.584; κόρυθος φάλον ἤλασεν 13.614]]; ὀδόντας ἐ. knock out, [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [3rd c.BC: Apollonius Rhodius Epicus 2.785: with double _accusative_, τὸν μὲν.. μεταδρομάδην ἔλασ᾽ ὦμον]] him he struck on.., [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 5.80]]; χθόνα δ᾽ ἤλασε παντὶ μετώπῳ struck earth with his forehead, of a falling man, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 22.94]]: with accusative cognate, inflict a wound, οὐλὴν τήν ποτέ με σῦς ἤλασε [Refs [21.219]]:—passive, with accusative νῶτον ὄπισθ᾽ αἰχμῇ δουρὸς ἐληλαμένος [Refs 7th c.BC+ [7th c.BC: Tyrtaeus Elegiacus 11.20; ἐλαύνεται εἰς τὸν μηρόν 2nd c.AD: Lucianus Sophista “Tox.” 61.]]

__II.3

__B
argument of disproof or refutation, πολύδηρις ἔ. [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Parmenides Poeta Philosophus 1.36, compare 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Phaedrus” 276a; ὁ ἔ. συναγωγὴ τῶν ἀντικειμένων ἐστίν 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Rhetorica” 1410a22, compare 1396b26; ἔ. δὲ συλλογισμὸς μετ᾽ ἀντιφάσεως τοῦ συμπεράσματος [prev. author] “SE” 165a2, compare “APr.” 66b11]]; ἐλέγχου ἄγνοια, ignoratio elenchi, [Refs 1st c.BC+ [[prev. author] “SE” 168a18; ὅταν ὑπὸ τῶν ἐ. πιέζωνται 1st c.BC: Philodemus Gadarensis Epigrammaticus “D.” 3.8.]]

__B.II
generally, cross-examining, testing, scrutiny, especially for purposes of refutation, οὐκ ἔχει ἔλεγχον does not admit of disproof, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 2.23]]; τῶνδ᾽ ἔλεγχον, absolutely, as a test of this, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Tyrannus” 603; τὰ ψευδῆ ἔλεγχον ἔχει 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 3.53]]; ἔ. παραδοῦναί τινι to give him an opportunity of refuting, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Phaedrus” 273c]]; δόμεν τι βασάνῳ ἐς ἔ. to submit it to scrutiny, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “N.” 8.21]]; χρυσὸς νόθου ἀρετῆς ἔ. [Refs [“Comica Adespota” 195]]; ἀρετῆς ἔ. δοῦναι a proof or test of it, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Andocides Orator 1.150]]; ἔ. διδόναι τοῦ βίου to give an account of one's life, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Apologia” 39c; οἱ ἔ. περὶ ὀρφανῶν 4th c.BC: Isaeus Orator 4.22; τὸ πρᾶγμα τὸν ἔ. δώσει 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 4.15]]; ἔ. ποιεῖν τινός to test it, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Ranae” 786; ἔ. ποιήσασθαι τῶν πεπραγμένων 5th c.BC: Antipho Orator 1.7]]; ἔ. λαβεῖν τινός make trial of it, [Refs [[prev. work]12]]; ἐλέγχους ἀποδέχεσθαι to admit tests, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Lysias Orator 19.6]]; ἐλέγχους προσφέρειν to allege them, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Lysistrata” 484]]; διάπειρα βροτῶν ἔ. [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “O.” 4.20; οὐδὲ ἔ. παρασχὼν οὐδὲ βάσανον 5th c.BC: Antipho Orator 2.4.7; ἔ. διδόναι 5th-6th c.BC: Andocides Orator 2.4]]; εἰς ἔ. πεσεῖν to be convicted, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Hippolytus” 1310, compare “HF” 73]]; δεικνυμένων ἐ. or ἐλίσσω (the latter more frequently in codices of [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Homerus Epicus)]], Attic dialect ἑλίττω, Epic dialect infinitive -έμεν[Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 23.309]]; Ionic dialect εἰλίσσω or εἱλίσσω (εἱ. is found in codices of [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus (see. below), but κατ-ελίσσειν 5th c.BC: Hippocrates Medicus “Acut.(Sp.”) 37, κατειλίξαι [prev. author] “Morb.” 2.18, +others)]]: future ἑλίξω [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Phoenissae” 711]]: aorist εἴλιξα [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Timaeus” 73a (εἵλ-]] codices, but κατ-ειλίξας [Refs [“IG” 22.204.32)]]; participle ἑλίξας [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 23.466]], Ionic dialect εἰλίξας [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 4.34]]:—middle, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 23.320]]: future ἑλίξομαι [Refs [17.728]]: aorist ἑλιξάμην [Refs [12.467, 17.283]]:—passive,future ἑλιγήσομαι [LXX.Isa.34.4]: aorist 1 εἱλίχθην [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Orestes” 358]]; participle ἑλιχθείς [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 12.74]]: perfect εἵλιγμαι [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th-7th c.BC: Hesiodus Epicus “Theogonia” 791, ἐλήλιγμαι 2nd c.AD: Pausanias Periegeta 10.17.12]]: pluperfect εἵλικτο [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Hercules Furens” 927]]; Ionic dialect 3rd.pers. plural εἱλίχατο [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 7.90.]] —The _Ionic dialect_ form is found in Trag. (see. below, codices usually εἱλ-; but τ᾽ εἰ.[Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Prometheus Vinctus” 138 (Lyric poetry, codex _middle_),compare 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Ranae” 1314, 1348 (codex Rav.)), in “IG” [same place], and codices of 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus (as “Ti.” [same place], ἀν-ειλίττων “Phlb.” 15e)]]; ἐπειλίξας is falsa lectio in [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 23.161. (ϝελ-, ἐϝελ-, compare εἴλω, ἐλελίζω ad near the end)]]:—turn round or about: active in [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Homerus Epicus]] always of turning a chariot round the doublingpost, οἶσθα γὰρ εὖ περὶ τέρματ᾽ ἐλισσέμεν [ἵππους] [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 23.309,compare 466.]]

__3

to draw: with accusative of thing(s), Jhn.18:10 21:6; with accusative of person(s), before ἔξω, Act.21:30; εἰς, Act.16:19, Jas.2:6. Metaphorical, to draw, lead, impel: Jhn.6:44 12:32. (For discussion of ἕ. in Oxyrh. Log., see Deiss., LAE, 437 ff.)†

LSJ / STEPBible (TFLSJ)
ἕλκω
(ἑλκύω late, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [12th c.AD: Tzetzes, Joannes Grammaticus “Historiarum variarum chiliades” 6.621), 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 24.52, etc.]], imperfect

__A
εἷλκον [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Fragmenta - American Journal of Philology” 39, etc.]], Epic dialect ἕλκον [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 4.213, +others (never εἵλκυον)]]: future ἕλξω [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Supplices” 909, etc., rarely ἑλκύσω [ῠ] 5th c.BC: Hippocrates Medicus “περὶ ἀγμῶν” 2, 4th-3rd c.BC: Philemo Comicus 174]]: aorist εἵλκῠσα [Refs 5th c.BC+ [Batrachomyomachia 232, 5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “N.” 7.103]], Trag. and Attic dialect, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Phoenissae” 987, 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Nubes” 540, “SIG” 2587.23, +others, etc.; ἥλκυσα “IG” 11(2).287 B 61 (Delos, 2nd c.BC), “CIG” “Corpus Inscriptionum Graecarum” “Corpus Inscriptionum Graecarum” 4993,5006 (Egypt, 3rd c.AD)]]; later εἷλξα, poetry ἕλξα [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [“Anthologia Graeca” 9.370 (Tiberius Rhetor Ill.), 5th-6th c.AD: Orphica “Argonautica” 258, 2nd c.AD: Galenus Medicus “περὶ φυσικῶν δυνάμεων - Scripta Minora” 1.12]]: perfect εἵλκῠκα [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 22.59]]; perfect participle ἑολκώς probably in [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Epicharmus Comicus 177:]] —middle, future -ύσομαι (ἐφ-) [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd c.AD: Antyllus Medicus cited in 4th c.AD: Oribasius Medicus 6.10.9:]]aorist εἱλκυσάμην (ἀφ-) variant in [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Hippocrates Medicus “περὶ ἄρθρων ἐμβολῆς” 11]], subjunctive ἀφελκύσωμαι [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Acharnenses” 1120; rarely εἱλξάμην 2nd c.AD: Galenus Medicus 4.534]]:—passive, future ἑλκυσθήσομαι [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Septem contra Thebas” 614 (ξυγκαθ-), 3rd c.BC: Lycophron Tragicus 358, ἑλχθήσομαι 2nd c.AD: Galenus Medicus “de Usu Partium” 7.7]]: aorist εἱλκύσθην [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Hippocrates Medicus “ἐπιδημίαι” 4.14, (ἐξ-) 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Ecclesiazusae” 688, ἑλκ- 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.140, ἡλκ- “IG” 12(7).115.11 (from Amorgos)]]; later εἵλχθην [Refs 1st c.AD+ [1st c.AD: Philo Judaeus 2.11, 2nd-3rd c.AD: Philostratus Sophista “Vita Apollonii” 8.15, 3rd c.AD(?): Diogenes Laertius 6.91]]: perfect εἵλκυσμαι [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Hippocrates Medicus “περὶ ἐπικυήσιος” 16, 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Rhesus” 576, 1st c.AD: Philo Judaeus 1.316, (καθ-) 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 6.50, ἕλκυσμαι (ἀν-) 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 9.98, ἥλκυσμαι “BGU” 1256.11 (2nd c.BC)]]: pluperfect εἵλκυστο [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Hippocrates Medicus “ἐπιδημίαι” 4.36.]] —In _Attic dialect_, ἕλκω, ἕλξω were alone used in present and future, while the other tenses were formed from ἑλκυ-; compare ἑλκέω (which see), ἑλκυστάζω. In [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Homerus Epicus, 3rd-2nd c.BC: Aristarchus Grammaticus]] rejected the augment (Cf. Latin sulcus, Lithuanian velkù 'drag'):— draw, drag, with collateralnotion of force or exertion, ὣς εἰπὼν ποδὸς ἕλκε began to drag [the dead body] by the foot, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 13.383; ἤν περ.. ποδῶν ἕλκωσι θύραζε 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 16.276; τινὰ τῆς ῥινός 2nd c.AD: Lucianus Sophista “Herm.” 73; Ἕκτορα.. περὶ σῆμ᾽ ἑτάροιο ἕλκει 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 24.52]]; drag away a prisoner, [Refs [22.65 (_passive_)]]; draw ships down to the sea, [Refs [2.152]], etc.; draw along a felled tree, [Refs [17.743]]; of mules, draw a chariot, [Refs [24.324]]; ἑλκέμεναι νειοῖο.. πηκτὸν ἄροτρον draw the plough through the field, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [10.353, compare 23.518; ἕ. τινὰ ἐπὶ κνάφου 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.92]]; περιβαλόντας σχοινία ἕ. haul at them, [Refs [[prev. author] 5.85.]]

__A.2
draw after one, ἐν δ᾽ ἔπεσ᾽ Ὠκεανῷ.. φάος ἠελίοιο, ἕλκον νύκτα μέλαιναν [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 8.486]]; πέδας ἕ. trail fetters after one, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 3.129]]; ἕ. χλανίδα let one's cloak trail behind, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Ephippus Comicus 19 (_anapaest meter_); θοἰμάτιον 5th-6th c.BC: Archippus Comicus 45.]]

__A.3
tear in pieces (used by [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Homerus Epicus only in the form ἑλκέω), ὀνύχεσσι παρειάν 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Troades” 280]]; worry, τὰς κύνας ὥλαφος ἕλκοι [Refs 5th c.BC+ [3rd c.BC: Theocritus Poeta Bucolicus 1.135; ἑλκυσθῆναι ὑπὸ κυνός 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.140.]]

__A.3.b
metaphorically, carp at, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “N.” 7.103.]]

__A.4
draw a bow, ἕλκε.. γλυφίδας τε λαβὼν καὶ νεῦρα βόεια [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 4.122, compare 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 21.419, 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 3.21, 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 4.2.28, etc.]]

__A.5
draw a sword, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Antigone” 1233, 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Rhesus” 576 (_passive_)]]:—middle, ἕλκετο δ᾽ ἐκ κολεοῖο.. ξίφος [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 1.194.]]

__A.6
ἕ. ἱστία hoist sails, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 2.426]]:—also in middle,[Refs [“hymnus ad Bacchum” 32.]]

__A.7
lift up scales, so as to poise them, ἕλκε δὲ μέσσα λαβών [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 8.72, 22.212.]]

__A.II
after [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Homerus Epicus,]]

__A.II.1
pull a barge-pole, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.194.]]

__A.II.2
tow a ship, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 2.90, etc.]]

__A.II.3
drag into court, ἕλκω σε κλητεύσοντα [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Nubes” 1218, compare 1004 (_passive_)]]; εἰς ἀγοράν [NT.Act.16.19]; drag about, especially with lewd violence, ἕλκει καὶ βιάζεται [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 21.150; μηδένα ἕλξειν μηδ᾽ ὑβριεῖν [prev. work] 221; ἕλκειν γυναῖκα 5th c.BC: Lysias Orator 1.12: _metaphorically_, ἄνω κάτω τοὺς λόγους ἕ. 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Theaetetus” 195c, compare 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Sophistici Elenchi” 167a35; ἡμέας ὁ καιρὸς ἕλκει 3rd c.BC: Herodas Mimographus 2.10]]; also ἥλκυσμαι λαμπαδάρχης I have been compelled to serve as λ., [Refs [“BGU” [prev. cited]]]

__A.II.4
draw or suck up, [ἥλιος] ἕλκει τὸ ὕδωρ ἐπ᾽ ἑωυτόν [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 2.25]]; ἕ. τὸν ἀέρα draw it in, breathe it, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Hippocrates Medicus “Aër.” 19, 5th-4th c.BC: Timaeus Locrus Philosophus 101d (_passive_),compare 5th c.BC: Philyllius Comicus 20: ζωὴν φύσιν Archel. cited in 3rd c.BC: Antigonus Carystius Paradoxographus “Mirabilia” 89]]; especially of persons drinking, drink in long draughts, quaff, μέθυ [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Ion” 1200; ἄμυστιν [prev. author] “Cyc.” 417]]; τὴν.. τοῦ Πραμνίου [σπονδήν] [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Equites” 107]]; οἶνον ἐκ.. λεπαστῆς Telecl[Refs 4th c.BC+ [[prev. author] 24 (Lyric poetry); ἀπνευστί 4th c.BC: Antiphanes Comicus 74.14, etc.]]: with accusative of the cup, δέπας μεστὸν.. ἕλκουσι γνάθοις ἀπαύστοις [Refs 4th c.BC+ [[prev. author] 237, compare 4th c.BC: Eubulus Comicus 56.7, +others]]; so ἕ. μαστόν suck it, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Phoenissae” 987]]; inhale, ὀσμήν [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [3rd c.BC: Antigonus Carystius Paradoxographus “Mirabilia” 89]]; of roots, draw up nourishment, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-3rd c.BC: Theophrastus Philosophus “Historia Plantarum” 1.6.10: _metaphorically_, χανδὸν καὶ ἀμυστὶ τῶν μαθηυάτων ἕ. 4th-5th c.AD: Eunapius Historicus “Vitae Sophistarum” p.474D.]]

__A.II.5
draw from a receptacle, ἐξ ἑκάστου κιβωτίου πινάκιον ἕν [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Ἀθηναίων Πολιτεία” 64.1.]]

__A.II.6
ἕ. βίοτον, ζόαν, drag out a weary life, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Orestes” 207 (Lyric poetry), “Ph.” 1535 (Lyric poetry)]]; προφάσιας ἕ. keep making excuses, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 6.86; πάσας τε προφάσεις.. ἕλκουσι 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Lysistrata” 727]]; ἕ. χρόνους make long, in prosody, [Refs 3rd c.AD+ [3rd c.AD: Longinus Rhetor “Proll. Heph.” p.83C.: hence _intransitive_, ἐπὶ τοσοῦτο λέγεται ἑλκύσαι τὴν σύστασιν..]] that the conflict dragged on, lasted, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 7.167, compare “PHib.” 1.83.9 (3rd c.BC)]]:—passive, τῶν ἐγκλημάτων εἱκλυσμένων πλείονα χρόνον [Refs 2nd c.BC+ [“Supp.epigram” 2.281 (Delph., 2nd c.BC)]]; also of a person, ἑλκόμενος καὶ μόγις [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 350d.]]

__A.II.7
ἕ. κόρδακα dance in long, measured steps, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Nubes” 540]]; ἓν τουτὶ (σχῆμα) [Refs [[prev. author] “Pax” 328.]]

__A.II.8
draw to oneself, attract, of the magnet, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Fragmenta” 567; by spells, τινὰ ποτὶ δῶμα 3rd c.BC: Theocritus Poeta Bucolicus 2.17, compare 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Memorabilia” 3.11.18, 3rd c.AD: Plotinus Philosophus 4.4.40, etc.]]; πείθειν καὶ ἑ. [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 458d; ἐχθροὺς ἐφ᾽ ἑαυτόν 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 22.59]]; draw on, ἐπὶ ἡδονάς [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Phaedrus” 238a; εἰς τυραννίδας ἕ. τὰς πολιτείας [prev. author] “R.” 568c]]:—passive, to be drawn on as by a spell, ἴυγγι δ᾽ ἕλκομαι ἦτορ [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “N.” 4.35; πρὸς φιλοσοφίαν 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 494e.]]

__A.II.9
of things weighed, ἕ. σταθμὸν τάλαντα δέκα draw down the balance, i.e. weigh ten talents, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.50, compare 5th c.BC: Eupolis Comicus 116: _absolutely_, τὸ δ᾽ ἂν ἑλκύσῃ]] whatever it weigh, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 2.65]]; πλεῖον ἕ. [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Minos” 316a.]]

__A.II.9.b
ἕ. τὰς ψήφους cast up the account, [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [“PPetr.” 2p.37 (3rd c.BC), “PHib.” 1.17.25 (3rd c.BC).]]

__A.II.10
draw or derive from a source, ἐντεῦθεν εἵλκυσεν ἐπὶ τὴν.. τέχνην τὸ πρός φορον αὐτῇ [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Phaedrus” 270a, compare 4th c.AD: Julianus Imperator “Orationes” 7.207a; τὸ γένος ἀπό τινος 1st c.BC-1st c.AD: Strabo Geographus 11.9.3]]; assume, μείζω φαντασίαν [Refs 2nd c.BC+ [2nd c.BC: Polybius Historicus 32.10.5; ὁ ἄρτος ἕλκει χρῶμα κάλλιστον 2nd c.AD: Athenaeus Epigrammaticus 3.113c.]]

__A.II.11
ἑλκύσαι πλίνθους make bricks, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.179, compare “PPetr.” 3p.137]]; ἕ. λάγανον Chrysipp. Tyan. cited in [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd c.AD: Athenaeus Epigrammaticus 14.647e.]]

__A.II.12
αἱ θυρίδες ἕλκουσι the win dows draw in air, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-3rd c.BC: Theophrastus Philosophus “de Ventis” 29.]]

__A.II.13
ἕ. ἑαυτόν, expressing some kind of athletic exercise, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Parmenides” 135d.]]

__B
middle, ἕ. χαίτας ἐκ κεφαλῆς tear one's hair, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 10.15]]; ἀσσοτέρω πυρὸς ἕλκετο δίφρον drew his chair nearer to the fire, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 19.506, compare 7th-6th c.BC(?): Semonides Iambographus 7.26.]]

__B.2
draw to oneself, scrape up, amass, τιμάς, ἄφενος ἕλκεσθαι, [Refs 6th c.BC+ [6th c.BC: Theognis Elegiacus 30.]]

__B.3
ἕλκεσθαι στάθμας περισσᾶς in [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “P.” 2.90]], means literal, to drag at too great a line, i.e.grasp more than one's due-- but whence the metaphor is taken remains unexplained.

__C
passive, to be drawn or wrenched, νῶτα.. ἑλκόμενα στερεῶς, of wrestlers, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 23.715]]; of the nails, to be curved, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Hippocrates Medicus “περὶ νούσων” 2.48]]; to close in when the core is removed, of the timber of certain trees, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-3rd c.BC: Theophrastus Philosophus “Historia Plantarum” 5.5.2.]]

__C.2
to be drawn or to flow at a place, of streams, [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [3rd c.BC: Lycophron Tragicus 702; πρὸς ἀντολίην ἕ. αἶα 2nd c.AD: Dionysius Periegeta 1086.]]

__C.3
to be drawn or contracted, εἱλκύσθη ἐπὶ τὰ δεξιὰ τράχηλος [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Hippocrates Medicus “ἐπιδημίαι” 4.14.]]

Diehl, 15.11, compare 2nd c.AD: Apollonius Dyscolus Grammaticus “de Pronominibus;” 80.10]]; ἐμαυτόν is uncertain in [Refs 6th c.BC+ [6th c.BC: Xenophanes Poeta Philosophus (“PLG” 2p.116B.) and 6th c.BC: Anacreon Lyricus 64]]; Ionic dialect ἐμεωυτοῦ [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 4.97 (but ἐμωυτοῦ 2nd c.AD: Apollonius Dyscolus Grammaticus “de Pronominibus;” 74.4), ἐμεωυτῷ 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 3.142, ἐμεωυτόν 1st c.AD(?): Heraclitus 101]]; ἐμᾱτοῦ, ἐμᾱτόν, [Refs 1st c.BC+ [“Lyrica Alexandrina Adespota” 4.23, “SIG” 741.12 (1st c.BC): in _plural_ always separated, ἡμῶν αὐτῶν, etc.]]; ἐν ἐμαυτῷ συννοεῖσθαι in or with oneself, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Orestes” 634; πρὸς ἐμαυτόν 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Ranae” 53, etc.; strengthened, ἴσχυόν τ᾽ αὐτὸς ἐμαυτοῦ [prev. author] “V.” 357, compare “Lys.” 1125]]; but ἐν ἐμαυτοῦ (i.e. οἴκῳ) εἶναι, metaphorically, to be master of oneself, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Charmides” 155d: _nominative_ ἐμαυτός, com. formation in 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Comicus 78.]]

ἐμ-βαίνω
[in LXX for עָלָה, etc. ;]
to step into: Jhn.5:4 (WH, RV omit); εἰς πλοῖον, to embark: Mat.8:23 9:1 13:2 14:22 15:39, Mrk.4:1 5:18 6:45 8:10, 13, Luk.5:3 8:22, 37, Jhn.6:17, 24 21:3, Act.21:6.†
(AS)

---

LSJ / STEPBible (TFLSJ)
ἐμβαίνω,
future -βήσομαι: perfect -βέβηκα; Epic dialect participle ἐμβεβᾰώς, -υῖα, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 5.199, 8th-7th c.BC: Hesiodus Epicus “Theogonia” 12, etc.:]]aorist 2 ἐνέβη; Epic dialect 3rd.pers. singular ἔμβη [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 4.656; dual _imperative_ ἔμβητον 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 23.403]]:—step in, μή τις.. ἐμβήῃ let none step in (so as to interfere), [Refs 5th c.BC+ [16.94: with _dative_, ποταμῷ οὐκ ἔστιν δὶς τῷ αὐτῷ ἐμβῆναι 1st c.AD(?): Heraclitus 91; εἰς πηλόν [prev. author] 5; ἐμβέβακεν ἴχνεσιν πατρός 5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “P.” 10.12.]]

__2
go on, go quickly, ἔμβητον, says Antilochus to his horses, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 23.403; ἔμβα]]advance! [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Electra” 113 (Lyric poetry).]]

__3
embark on a ship, ἐρέται δ᾽ ἐν ἑκάστη πεντήκοντα ἐμβέβασαν [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 2.720; τότε δ᾽ ἔμβη νηΐ Πύλονδε 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 4.656, compare 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 1.311]]; ἐς ἕτερον πλοῖον ἐ. (variant for{ἐσβ-}) [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 2.29, compare 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 1.18 (variant), 5th c.BC: Lysias Orator 2.40, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Menexenus” 243c: with _accusative_, λέμβον ἐ. 2nd c.BC: Polybius Historicus 30.9.11]]: absolutely, embark, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Troades” 455 (troch.), 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Ranae” 188, etc.]]: generally, step into, mount, εἰς τὸ φορεῖον [Refs 1st c.AD+ [1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus “Galba” 26]]: perfect, to be mounted on, ἵπποισι καὶ ἅρμασιν ἐμβεβαῶτα [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 5.199; ἐπ᾽ ἀπήνης ἐμβεβώς 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Tyrannus” 803: also with _accusative_, Τροίαν Ἰλιάδ᾽ ἐμβεβαῶτα 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Hecuba” 922 (Lyric poetry); στέγην τήνδ᾽ ἐμβεβῶτες [prev. author] “Cyc.” 92.]]

__4
step upon, τῷ δ᾽ ἐγὼ ἐμβαίνων [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 10.164; πεδίλοις ἐμβεβαυῖα 8th-7th c.BC: Hesiodus Epicus “Theogonia” 12; τοῖσδ᾽ ἁλουργέσιν 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Agamemnon” 946]]; δαίμων ἐνέβη Περσῶν γενεᾷ trampled upon it, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [[prev. author] “Pers.” 911 (_anapaest meter_); μὴ᾽ μβαινε τῷ δυστυχοῦντι 4th-3rd c.BC: Menander Comicus “Μονόστιχοι - Fragmenta Comicorum Graecorum” 356]]: absolutely, tread on one's toes, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-3rd c.BC: Theophrastus Philosophus “Characteres” 15.6]]; compare βοῦς viii.

__5
enter upon, ἐς τόνδε χρησμόν uncertain in [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Agamemnon” 1567; εἰς κίνδυνον 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 2.1.15: with _accusative_, ἐ. κέλευθον 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Supplices” 989 (Lyric poetry).]]

__5.b
metaphorically, enter upon, embark in, μεγαλανορίαις [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “N.” 11.44; τῷ ἐπιτηδεύατι 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Phaedrus” 252e]]; ἐν αὐτοῖς τοῖς δεινοῖς ἐμβεβηκώς embarked, engaged in.., [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 18.248]]; light upon, εἰς ἀρχήν τε καὶ τύπον τῆς δικαιοσύνης [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 443c]]: absolutely, enter upon office, [Refs [Inscriptiones Graecae 5(1).1390.31 (from Andania).]]

__6
rarely with genitive, step upon, νᾶος [Refs 7th c.BC+ [7th-6th c.BC: Alcaeus Lyricus 19; γῆς ὅρων 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Coloneus” 400.]]

__7
Poets, with accusative of the instrument of motion, ὄχοις.. ἐμβεβὼς πόδα [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Fragmenta” 672]]; ἐς ἄντλον ἐμβήσει (2nd pers. singular) πόδα [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Heraclidae” 168.]]

__8
to be fixed or fastened, κατά τι [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 24.81]]; to be fixed in, εἰς ἐμπυελίδας [Refs 2nd c.BC+ [2nd-1st c.BC(?): Hero Mechanicus “Automatopoetica” 2.3.]]

__9
={ἐμβατεύω}[Refs 3rd c.BC+ [11, “SIG” 364.75 (Ephesus, 3rd c.BC).]]

__II
causal in aorist 1 ἐνέβησα, make to step in, put in, ἐν δὲ τὰ μῆλα.. ἐβήσαμεν [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 11.4; δίφρον ἐμβῆσαί τινα 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Heraclidae” 845, compare “Cyc.” 467; ἐ. τὰν ἀρχάν “Schwyzer” 485.9 (Thespiae, 3rd c.BC): _metaphorically_, ἐμβῆσαί τινα ἐς φροντίδα]] plunge him into anxiety, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.46.]]

__III
intransitive, step, march or dance, ὀρθῶς [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus Alcaeus1.108c; πρὸς ῥυθμόν 2nd c.AD: Lucianus Sophista “Salt.” 10.]]

ἐμ-βάλλω

LSJ / STEPBible (TFLSJ)
ἐμβάλλω,
future -βᾰλῶ: perfect -βέβληκα: aorist 2 ἐνέβᾰλον (passive is mostly supplied by ἐμπίπτω):— throw in, τινὰ πόντῳ [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 14.258]]; μιν.. χερσὶν᾽ Ἀχιλλῆος θεὸς ἔμβαλεν let him fall into Achilles' hands,[Refs 5th c.BC+ [21.47; ἐ. νιν βροτοῦ ἀνέρος εὐνῇ 18.85; ἐ. τινὰ εἰς τὸ βάραθρον 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Ranae” 574, “Nu.” 1450; εἰς τὸ δεσμωτήριον 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 53.14; ἐ. τινὰ εἰς συμφοράς 5th c.BC: Antipho Orator 3.4.10; εἰς ἀτυχίας 4th c.BC: Aeschines Orator 3.79; εἰς αἰσχύνην καὶ ἀδικίαν 4th-3rd c.BC: Dinarchus Orator 3.7; εἰς ὑποψίαν 1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus “Themistocles” 23; ἐς γραφάς 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Acharnenses” 679, compare 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 4.72, etc.; εἰς ἀπορίαν 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Philebus” 20a; εἰς ἔχθραν 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 18.70.]]

__2
of things, ἵπποις χαλινοὺς ἐ. [Refs 8th c.BC+ [6th c.BC: Theognis Elegiacus 551, 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “de Equitandi ratione” 6.7 (_passive_), 9.9, compare 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 19.394; πώλοις ἡνίας 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Iphigenia Taurica” 1424; ἐ. ψήφους εἰς τὸν καδίσκον 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 57.13, compare 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 2.2.21]]; ἐ. μοχλόν (i.e. εἰς τὴν θύραν) [Refs [[prev. author] “An.” 7.1.12]]; ἐ. σῖτον (i.e. εἰς τὴν φάτνην) [Refs [[prev. author] “Cyr.” 8.1.38]]; τοῖς ὑποζυγίοις ἐ. throw food to.., [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-3rd c.BC: Theophrastus Philosophus “Characteres” 4.8]]; simply, lay or put in, [ἱμάντα] οἱ ἔμβαλε χερσίν put it into his hands, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 14.218]]; ἐνέβαλον τῶν χρημάτων [εἰς τὸ κανοῦν] [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Politica” 1304a3, compare 2nd-3rd c.AD: Aelianus “Varia Historia” 11.5]]; hand in, submit a petition, [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [“PPetr.” 3P. 39 (3rd c.BC), etc.]]; ἐ. τὴν χεῖρά τινι slide one's hand into another's, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Vespae” 554]]; ἔμβαλλε χεῖρα δεξιάν as a pledge of good faith, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Trachiniae” 1181, compare 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Ranae” 754]]; ἔμβαλλε χειρὸς πίστιν, to which Neoptolemus answers—ἐμβάλλω μενεῖν I give my pledge to remain, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Philoctetes” 813 (troch.).]]

__3
frequently of the mind, ἐνὶ φρεσὶν ἐ. [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 19.10 (compare below 111.2); εἰς νοῦν τινί 1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus “Timoleon” 3]]; ἐ. ἵμερον, μένος τινί, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 3.139, 16.529]]; ἐ. νεῖκός τισι to throw in strife between them, [Refs [4.444]]; τισὶ λύσσαν ἐρισμοῦ[Refs 5th c.BC+ [Timo 28.3; ἐ. λόγον 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 344d; βουλὴν ἐ. περί τινος 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 2.2.18 (and _absolutely_, ἐ. τινὶ περί τινος]] to give one advice on a thing, [Refs [[prev. work] 5.5.43]] (nisi addendum [βουλήν])); ἐ. πρᾶγμα εἰς γέλωτα καὶ λοιδορίαν [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 10.75.]]

__4
throw upon or against, νηῒ κεραυνόν [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 12.415; δαλὸν νήεσσι 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 13.320; πέτρον στέρνῳ 5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “N.” 10.68; [Ἀχαιοὺς] πέτραις 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Helena” 1129 (Lyric poetry); πῆχυν στέρνοις [prev. author] “Or.” 1466 (Lyric poetry); λίθον τινὶ εἰς κεφαλήν 5th c.BC: Antipho Orator 5.26; πληγάς τινι 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 1.5.11, compare 1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus “Caesar” 66]]; so ἐμβαλέτω ἰσχυρότατα (i.e. πληγάς) let him lay on.., [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “de Equitandi ratione” 8.4]]; ἐ. ἕλκεα to inflict them, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “Fragmenta.” 111]]; ἐ. πῦρ set fire to.., [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 7.53]]; ἐ. ῥήγεα lay on blankets, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 4.298: _metaphorically_, ἐ. φόβον τινί]] strike fear into him, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 7.10. ; ἄταν 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Septem contra Thebas” 316 (Lyric poetry)]]; φροντίδας variant in [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Antipho Orator 2.2.2]]; impose, ἔργα εἰς τὴν γῆν [Refs 1st c.BC+ [“PTeb.” 37.7 (_passive_, 1st c.BC)]]; of a fine, [Refs [“BCH” 8.307 (from Delos).]]

__5
ἐ. ὦμον put one's shoulder to the work, in archery, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Hippocrates Medicus “περὶ ἀγμῶν” 2.]]

__6
put into its place, to set a broken or dislocated limb, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [[prev. work] 24 (_passive_), “Art.” 1, +others, 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “de Partibus Animalium” 685b6.]]

__7
in Medicine texts, put in, ἀμυχάς, διαίρεσιν, [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [3rd c.AD: Philumenus Medicus “de Venenatis Animalibus” 7.4, 2nd c.AD: Antyllus Medicus cited in 4th c.AD: Oribasius Medicus 45.24.4.]]

__8
graft a tree, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 53.15 (_passive_)]]; but simply, plant, τὰ φυτά [Refs [“IG” 12(7).62.29.]]

__9
ἐ. τινί (i.e. μάρμαρον) to throw at another, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 12.383.]]

__10
insert a word or a letter, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Protagoras” 343d, “Cra.” 414c, +others; εἰς κωμῳδίαν στίχον 1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus 2.334f.]]

__11
ἐ. οἰκίαν τινί bring it down upon him, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Acharnenses” 511, compare “Nu.” 1489.]]

__12
τάφρον ἐ. make a trench, [Refs 1st c.AD+ [1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus “Pyrrhus” 27, “Mar.” 15.]]

__13
pay, contribute, ἀργύριον [Refs [“IG” 7.235.13 (from Oropus)]]; τροφάν [Refs [“GDI” 1884.12 (Delph.).]]

__14
denounce an offender, ἐς τὰν βωλάν [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [“SIG” 527.103 (Dreros, 3rd c.BC).]]

__15
intercalate a month, [Refs [“IG” 12.76.53.]]

__II
intransitive (i.e. στρατόν), make an inroad or invasion, variant for{ἐσβ}. in [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 4.125, 5.15, 9.13, compare 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Agesilaus” 1.29; in full, ἐ. στράτευμα 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Septem contra Thebas” 583, 1024]]: metaphorically, attack, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Theaetetus” 165d.]]

__II.b
generally, burst, rush in, ἐμβάλλειν εἰς τὴν ἀγοράν [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aeschines Orator 2.164, 4th c.BC: Lycurgus Orator 5, etc.]]; embark upon, ἐμβάλωμεν εἰς ἄλλον λόγον [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Electra” 962: with _dative_, εἰκασίαις Hierocl. p.37 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus; βίβλοις μακραῖς καὶ δυσελίκτοις 4th c.AD: Julianus Imperator “Orationes” 7.227b.]]

__II.2
strike a ship with the ram (ἔμβολος [Refs [1.3)]], charge or ram it, νηΐ [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 8.84, +others, compare 7.10]].; ἐ. ταῖς λοιπαῖς (i.e. ναυσί) [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 4.14]]; ξυνετύγχανε.. διὰ τὴν στενοχωρίαν τὰ μὲν ἄλλοις ἐμβεβληκέναι τὰ δὲ αὐτοὺς ἐμβεβλῆσθαι on one side had charged others, on the other had been charged themselves, [Refs [[prev. author] 7.70.]]

__II.2.b
of water, ἐ. τοῖς ὄρεσι to dash against them, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 2.28: _absolutely_, τὸ ὕδωρ ἐμβαλὸν τὰ χωρία ἐλυμήνατο 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 55.11.]]

__II.3
κώπῃς ἐ. (i.e. χεῖρας) lay oneself to the oars, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 10.129, compare 5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “P.” 4.201]]; ἐ. alone, pull hard, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Equites” 602, “Ra.” 206, 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Historia Graeca (Hellenica)” 5.1.13.]]

__II.4
of a river, empty itself, εἰς.. [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Phaedo” 113c.]]

__III
middle, throw in what is one's own, ὅρκον εἰς τὸν ἐχῖνον [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 49.65, compare 27.51]]: absolutely, draw lots, [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [“SIG” 1006.3 (Cos, 3rd c.BC).]]

__III.2
metaphorically, μή μοι φύξιν ἐμβάλλεο θυμῷ [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 10.447]]; μῆτιν ἐ. θ[Refs 4th c.BC+ [. 23.313; εἰς τὸν νοῦν ἐμβάλλεσθαί τι 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 18.68]] (later in active, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [“PTaur.” 4.9); τὸ καρτερὸν ἐμβαλόμενοι 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 4.2.21 (compare above 1.3).]]

__III.3
with genitive, ἐμβάλλεσθε τῶν λαγῴων fall upon the hare's flesh, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Pax” 1312.]]

__III.4
put on board ship, [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [PHib. 1.152 (3rd c.BC), “POxy.” 1292.3 (1st c.AD), 2nd c.AD: Lucianus Sophista “VH” 1.5, etc.]]

__III.5
set to work upon, τῇ γεωργίᾳ [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [“PStrassb.” 111.3 (3rd c.BC).]]

__IV
passive, to be dashed against: of ships, charge (see.[Refs 5th c.BC+ [above 11.2), 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 7.34, 70.]]

ἐμβατεύω

deep_entry:
Abbott-Smith / STEPBible (TBESG)
ἐγώ, genitive, etc., ἐμοῦ, ἐμοί, ἐμέ (enclitic μου, μοι, με), pl. ἡμεῖς, -ῶν, -ῖν, -ᾶς,
of person(s) pron.
I.
__(a) The nom. is usually emphatic, when expressed as subjc, as in Mat.3:11, Mrk.1:8, Luk.3:16, al. But often there is no apparent emphasis, as Mat.10:16, Jhn.10:17; ἰδοὺ ἐ. (= Heb. הִנֵּנִי, cf. 1Ki.3:8), Act.9:10; ἐ. (like Heb. אֲנִי), I am, Jhn.1:23 (LXX), Act.7:32 (LXX).
__(b) The enclitic forms (see supr.) are used with nouns, adjectives, verbs, adverbs, where there is no emphasis: ἐν τ. πατρί μου, Jhn.14:20; μου τ. λόγους, Mat.7:24; ὀπίσω μου, Mat.3:11; ἰσχυρότερός μου, ib.; λέγει μοι, Rev.5:5; also with the prep. πρός, as Mrk.9:19, al. The full forms (ἐμοῦ, etc.) are used with the other prepositions, as δι᾽ ἐμοῦ, ἐν ἐμοί, εἰς ἐμέ, etc., also for emphasis, as Luk.10:16, Jhn.7:23, Mrk.14:7, al.
__(with) The genitive μου and ἡμῶν are often used for the poss. pronouns ἐμός, ἡμέτερος: τ. λαόν μου, Mat.2:6; μου τῂ ἀπιστιᾳ, Mrk.9:24.
__(d) τί ἐμοὶ καὶ σοί ( = Heb. מַה־לִי וָלָךְ, Jdg.11:12, al.), i.e. what have we in common: Mat.8:29, Mrk.1:24, 5:7, Luk.8:28, Jhn.2:4; τί γάρ μοι, 1Co.5:2.
__(e) The interchange of ἐγώ and ἡμεῖς, common in π., appears in Pauline Epp. (see M, Pr., 86f., M, Th., 131f.).
__(f) κἀγώ (= καὶ ἐγώ), and I, even I, I also: Mat.2:8, Luk.2:48, Jhn.6:56, Rom.3:7, 1Co.7:40, al.; κἀγώ . . . καί, both . . . and, Jhn.7:28.
(AS)

---

I: pronoun of the first person:—Epic dialect mostly ἐγών before vowels (so in Doric dialect, before consonants, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Epicharmus Comicus 85, 5th c.BC: Sophron Comicus 81, 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Acharnenses” 748, 754), rarely in Trag., 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Persae” 932 (Lyric poetry)]]; Boeotian dialect ἱών [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd c.AD: Apollonius Dyscolus Grammaticus “de Pronominibus;” 51.4]]:— strengthened ἔγωγε, I at least, for my part, indeed, for myself (more frequently in Attic dialect than in [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Homerus Epicus)]]: Doric dialect ἐγώνγα [Refs 7th c.BC+ [7th c.BC: Alcman Lyricus 51, 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Acharnenses” 736, “Lys.” 986, _dative_ ἐμίνγα “IG” 22.1126.7 (Amphict. Delph.)]]: Boeotian dialect ἱώνγα [Refs 6th c.BC+ [6th c.BC: Corinna Lyrica 21]]; ἱώνει [Refs [Ead. 10]]; ἰώγα [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Acharnenses” 898]]: Laconian dialect and Tarentum dialect ἐγώνη, [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [5th c.AD(?): Hesychius Legal icographus, 2nd c.AD: Apollonius Dyscolus Grammaticus “de Conjunctionibus;” 255.29.]]

__II
oblique cases from a different root, genitive ἐμοῦ, enclitic μο; Ionic dialect and Epic dialect ἐμέο, ἐμεῦ, μευ, also ἐμέθεν [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 1.525, 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Helena” 177 (Lyric poetry)]]; Aeolic dialect ἔμεθεν [Refs 7th c.BC+ [7th-6th c.BC: Sappho Lyrica “Papyrus fragments” in E. Diehl, 23.7; ἐμεῖο “IG” 3.1337; μεθέν 5th c.BC: Sophron Comicus 20]]; Doric dialect ἐμέος, ἐμεῦς, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Epicharmus Comicus 144]]; Boeotian dialect ἐμοῦς [Refs 6th c.BC+ [6th c.BC: Corinna Lyrica 37; also ἐμῶς, ἐμίο, ἐμίω, ἐμίως 2nd c.AD: Apollonius Dyscolus Grammaticus “de Pronominibus;” 74.17:]] — _dative_ ἐμοί, enclitic μοι (which may be compared with Sanskrit genitive me in κλῦθί μοι [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 5.115, +others); ὅ μοι πόσις “Schwyzer” 683 (5th c.AD: Cypria)]]; Doric dialect ἐμίν [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Epicharmus Comicus 99, “AJA” 29.461 (Rhodian, 5th c.BC), 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Acharnenses” 733, 3rd c.BC: Theocritus Poeta Bucolicus 4.30]]; Tarentum dialect ἐμίνη [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [3rd c.BC: Rhinthon Comicus 13: _accusative_ ἐμέ]], enclitic μ; [Refs 5th c.AD+ [5th c.AD: Cypria μι “Inscription Cyprian dialect” 59,60 H.]]

__III

__IV
plural, nominative ἡμεῖς (ἡμέες falsa lectio in [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 2.6, +others, rejected by 2nd c.AD: Apollonius Dyscolus Grammaticus “de Pronominibus;” 93.1)]]; Aeolic dialect ἄμμες [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 9.303, 7th-6th c.BC: Alcaeus Lyricus 18.3, 5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “P.” 4.144]]; ἄμμων [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [[prev. work]74, 2nd c.AD: Apollonius Dyscolus Grammaticus “de Pronominibus;” 95.3]]; Doric dialect ἁμέων [Refs 7th c.BC+ [7th c.BC: Alcman Lyricus 66]]; ἁμῶν [[Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Epicharmus Comicus] 266, 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Lysistrata” 168, 3rd c.BC: Theocritus Poeta Bucolicus 2.158]]; ἄμμεσιν 7th-6th c.BC: Alcaeus Lyricus 100]]; Doric dialect also ἁμίν or ἇμιν, [Refs 7th c.BC+ [7th c.BC: Alcman Lyricus 77, 78, 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Eumenides” 347 (Lyric poetry), 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Lysistrata” 1081]]; Hdn.Gr. 2.140)]]; Aeolic dialect ἄμμε [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 1.59, 7th-6th c.BC: Sappho Lyrica 115]], Theocr.8.25; Doric dialect ἁμέ [Refs 6th c.BC+ [“SIG” 1 (Abu Simbel, 6th c.BC), 5th c.BC: Epicharmus Comicus 173, 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Acharnenses” 759 codices, “Lys.” 95.]]—On these dialectic varieties, [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [see 2nd c.AD: Apollonius Dyscolus Grammaticus “de Pronominibus;” 50]] ff. deep_entry:
Abbott-Smith / STEPBible (TBESG)
ἐγώ, genitive, etc., ἐμοῦ, ἐμοί, ἐμέ (enclitic μου, μοι, με), pl. ἡμεῖς, -ῶν, -ῖν, -ᾶς,
of person(s) pron.
I.
__(a) The nom. is usually emphatic, when expressed as subjc, as in Mat.3:11, Mrk.1:8, Luk.3:16, al. But often there is no apparent emphasis, as Mat.10:16, Jhn.10:17; ἰδοὺ ἐ. (= Heb. הִנֵּנִי, cf. 1Ki.3:8), Act.9:10; ἐ. (like Heb. אֲנִי), I am, Jhn.1:23 (LXX), Act.7:32 (LXX).
__(b) The enclitic forms (see supr.) are used with nouns, adjectives, verbs, adverbs, where there is no emphasis: ἐν τ. πατρί μου, Jhn.14:20; μου τ. λόγους, Mat.7:24; ὀπίσω μου, Mat.3:11; ἰσχυρότερός μου, ib.; λέγει μοι, Rev.5:5; also with the prep. πρός, as Mrk.9:19, al. The full forms (ἐμοῦ, etc.) are used with the other prepositions, as δι᾽ ἐμοῦ, ἐν ἐμοί, εἰς ἐμέ, etc., also for emphasis, as Luk.10:16, Jhn.7:23, Mrk.14:7, al.
__(with) The genitive μου and ἡμῶν are often used for the poss. pronouns ἐμός, ἡμέτερος: τ. λαόν μου, Mat.2:6; μου τῂ ἀπιστιᾳ, Mrk.9:24.
__(d) τί ἐμοὶ καὶ σοί ( = Heb. מַה־לִי וָלָךְ, Jdg.11:12, al.), i.e. what have we in common: Mat.8:29, Mrk.1:24, 5:7, Luk.8:28, Jhn.2:4; τί γάρ μοι, 1Co.5:2.
__(e) The interchange of ἐγώ and ἡμεῖς, common in π., appears in Pauline Epp. (see M, Pr., 86f., M, Th., 131f.).
__(f) κἀγώ (= καὶ ἐγώ), and I, even I, I also: Mat.2:8, Luk.2:48, Jhn.6:56, Rom.3:7, 1Co.7:40, al.; κἀγώ . . . καί, both . . . and, Jhn.7:28.
(AS)

possessive pronoun of 1st pers.: (ἐγώ, ἐμοῦ):— mine; contraction with the Article, οὑμός, τοὐμόν, τοὐμοῦ, τὠμῷ, τἀμά, Trag. (not Comedy texts, τἀμὰ γὰρ διοίχεται is paratragoedia in [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Ecclesiazusae” 393)]], rarely in Prose, οὑμός [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Epistulae” 354c; τἀμά [prev. author] “Plt.” 258b]]; οὑμός even in [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 8.360]]; and (accusative to some Grammars ) τὠμῷ [Refs 8th c.BC+ [11.608, 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 4.71; τἠμῇ 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 9.654]]:—poetry ἀμός (which see):

__I
with a substantive:

__I.1
subjectively, mine, of me, ἐμὰ δάκρυα [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 1.42]]; χεῖρες ἐμαί[Refs 8th c.BC+ [[prev. work] 166; ἐμός τε πατὴρ καὶ σός 8th-7th c.BC: Hesiodus Epicus “Opera et Dies” 633]]: with the Article, τὸν ἐμὸν χόλον [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 4.42, etc.]]: in Poets sometimes joined with genitive, to strengthen the possessive notion, ἐμὸν αὐτοῦ mine own,[Refs 8th c.BC+ [6.446, 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 2.45; δαὴρ.. ἐμὸς ἔσκε κυνώπιδος 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 3.180; θρῆνον ἐμὸν τὸν αὐτῆς 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Agamemnon” 1323; τἀμὰ δυστήνου κακά 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Coloneus” 344, compare “El.” 252; τὸν ἐμὸν αὐτοῦ.. βίον 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Plutus” 33.]]

__I.1.b
mine, i.e. favourable to me, τεκμήρια ἐμά, οὐ τούτων [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Antipho Orator 2.4.10.]]

__I.2
objectively, relating to me, against me, ἐμὴ ἀγγελίη [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 19.336; τὸν ἐμὸν γάμον 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 2.97]]; τὴν ἐμὴν αἰδῶ respect for me, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Persae” 699 (troch.)]]; τἀμὰ νουθετήματα warnings to me, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Electra” 343]]; τὠμῷ πόθῳ by love for me, [Refs [[prev. author] “OT” 969]]; αἱ ἐμαὶ διαβολαί slanders against me, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 6.90]]; δωρεὰ ἐμή a gift to me, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 8.3.32]]; sometimes with another genitive added, τὰς ἐμὰς Λαΐου διαφθοράς murder of L. by me, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Tyrannus” 572]]; τοὐμὸν αἷμα πατρός his blood shed by me, [Refs [[prev. work] 1400]]; τὰ ἐμὰ δῶρα Κύπριδος (Dind. for Κύπρις) her gifts to me, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Helena” 364 (_anapaest meter_).]]

__II
without a substantive, mine, οὐ γὰρ ἐμὸν παλινάγρετον my word, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 1.526]]; τὸ μὲν ἐμόν [ἐστι] 'tis my counsel, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “I.” 8(7).42]]: in Trag. and Prose, it is my duty, my business, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Ion” 1020, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Leges” 664b.]]

__II.2
ἐμοί my friends, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 20.205; οἱ ἐμοί 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 3.2.28, etc.]]; ὁ ἐμὸς Ἡράκλειτος my dear Heraclitus, [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd c.AD: Arrianus Historicus “Epicteti Dissertationes” 2.2.17.]]

__II.3
τὰ ἐμά my property, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Protagoras” 310e, etc.]]; of children, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Electra” 538, “OC” 922; τὸ τύπτειν καὶ ἐμὲ καὶ τὰ ἐμὰ ἀδίκως 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Gorgias” 508e]]; of servants. [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [“PEdgar” 4.6 (3rd c.BC), etc.]]; but also τὰ ἐμά or τὸ ἐμόν, my part, my affairs, my interest, οὕτω τὸ ἐμὸν ἔχει things stand thus with me, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 4.127; τὰ τούτου μᾶλλον ἢ τοὐμόν 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Ajax” 124; ἔρρει τἀμὰ παντελῶς 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 6.1.3; τὸ ἐμὸν εὖ πράττει 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 463e, etc.; in full, τοὐμὸν μέρος 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Trachiniae” 1215]]: hence in Trag. and Attic dialect, my conduct (almost periphrastic for ἐγώ), [Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. author] “El.” 1302, “Tr.” 1068, 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Thesmophoriazusae” 105; τὸ μὲν οὖν ἐμὸν οὐκ ἐμποδὼν ὑμῖν ἔσται 5th c.BC: Lysias Orator 8.19, compare 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Gorgias” 452c, etc.: _absolutely_, τό γε ἐμόν]] for my part, as far as concerns me, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.108, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Protagoras” 338c, “Sph.” 237b.]]

__II.4
ἡ ἐ. (i.e. γῆ) my country, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 6.78]]; also (i.e. γνώμη) my opinion, ἐὰν ἡ ἐ. νικᾷ [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 397d]]; κατά γε τὴν ἐ. [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Ecclesiazusae” 153, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Politicus” 277a.]]
