deep_entry:
Abbott-Smith / STEPBible (TBESG)
ἐγώ, genitive, etc., ἐμοῦ, ἐμοί, ἐμέ (enclitic μου, μοι, με), pl. ἡμεῖς, -ῶν, -ῖν, -ᾶς,
of person(s) pron.
I.
__(a) The nom. is usually emphatic, when expressed as subjc, as in Mat.3:11, Mrk.1:8, Luk.3:16, al. But often there is no apparent emphasis, as Mat.10:16, Jhn.10:17; ἰδοὺ ἐ. (= Heb. הִנֵּנִי, cf. 1Ki.3:8), Act.9:10; ἐ. (like Heb. אֲנִי), I am, Jhn.1:23 (LXX), Act.7:32 (LXX).
__(b) The enclitic forms (see supr.) are used with nouns, adjectives, verbs, adverbs, where there is no emphasis: ἐν τ. πατρί μου, Jhn.14:20; μου τ. λόγους, Mat.7:24; ὀπίσω μου, Mat.3:11; ἰσχυρότερός μου, ib.; λέγει μοι, Rev.5:5; also with the prep. πρός, as Mrk.9:19, al. The full forms (ἐμοῦ, etc.) are used with the other prepositions, as δι᾽ ἐμοῦ, ἐν ἐμοί, εἰς ἐμέ, etc., also for emphasis, as Luk.10:16, Jhn.7:23, Mrk.14:7, al.
__(with) The genitive μου and ἡμῶν are often used for the poss. pronouns ἐμός, ἡμέτερος: τ. λαόν μου, Mat.2:6; μου τῂ ἀπιστιᾳ, Mrk.9:24.
__(d) τί ἐμοὶ καὶ σοί ( = Heb. מַה־לִי וָלָךְ, Jdg.11:12, al.), i.e. what have we in common: Mat.8:29, Mrk.1:24, 5:7, Luk.8:28, Jhn.2:4; τί γάρ μοι, 1Co.5:2.
__(e) The interchange of ἐγώ and ἡμεῖς, common in π., appears in Pauline Epp. (see M, Pr., 86f., M, Th., 131f.).
__(f) κἀγώ (= καὶ ἐγώ), and I, even I, I also: Mat.2:8, Luk.2:48, Jhn.6:56, Rom.3:7, 1Co.7:40, al.; κἀγώ . . . καί, both . . . and, Jhn.7:28.
(AS)

---

LSJ / STEPBible (TFLSJ)
ἐγώ,
I: pronoun of the first person:—Epic dialect mostly ἐγών before vowels (so in Doric dialect, before consonants, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Epicharmus Comicus 85, 5th c.BC: Sophron Comicus 81, 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Acharnenses” 748, 754), rarely in Trag., 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Persae” 932 (Lyric poetry)]]; Boeotian dialect ἱών [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd c.AD: Apollonius Dyscolus Grammaticus “de Pronominibus;” 51.4]]:— strengthened ἔγωγε, I at least, for my part, indeed, for myself (more frequently in Attic dialect than in [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Homerus Epicus)]]: Doric dialect ἐγώνγα [Refs 7th c.BC+ [7th c.BC: Alcman Lyricus 51, 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Acharnenses” 736, “Lys.” 986, _dative_ ἐμίνγα “IG” 22.1126.7 (Amphict. Delph.)]]: Boeotian dialect ἱώνγα [Refs 6th c.BC+ [6th c.BC: Corinna Lyrica 21]]; ἱώνει [Refs [Ead. 10]]; ἰώγα [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Acharnenses” 898]]: Laconian dialect and Tarentum dialect ἐγώνη, [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [5th c.AD(?): Hesychius Legal icographus, 2nd c.AD: Apollonius Dyscolus Grammaticus “de Conjunctionibus;” 255.29.]]

__II
oblique cases from a different root, genitive ἐμοῦ, enclitic μο; Ionic dialect and Epic dialect ἐμέο, ἐμεῦ, μευ, also ἐμέθεν [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 1.525, 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Helena” 177 (Lyric poetry)]]; Aeolic dialect ἔμεθεν [Refs 7th c.BC+ [7th-6th c.BC: Sappho Lyrica “Papyrus fragments” in E. Diehl, 23.7; ἐμεῖο “IG” 3.1337; μεθέν 5th c.BC: Sophron Comicus 20]]; Doric dialect ἐμέος, ἐμεῦς, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Epicharmus Comicus 144]]; Boeotian dialect ἐμοῦς [Refs 6th c.BC+ [6th c.BC: Corinna Lyrica 37; also ἐμῶς, ἐμίο, ἐμίω, ἐμίως 2nd c.AD: Apollonius Dyscolus Grammaticus “de Pronominibus;” 74.17:]] — _dative_ ἐμοί, enclitic μοι (which may be compared with Sanskrit genitive me in κλῦθί μοι [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 5.115, +others); ὅ μοι πόσις “Schwyzer” 683 (5th c.AD: Cypria)]]; Doric dialect ἐμίν [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Epicharmus Comicus 99, “AJA” 29.461 (Rhodian, 5th c.BC), 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Acharnenses” 733, 3rd c.BC: Theocritus Poeta Bucolicus 4.30]]; Tarentum dialect ἐμίνη [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [3rd c.BC: Rhinthon Comicus 13: _accusative_ ἐμέ]], enclitic μ; [Refs 5th c.AD+ [5th c.AD: Cypria μι “Inscription Cyprian dialect” 59,60 H.]]

__III
dual, nominative and accusative, νῶι, we two, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 5.34, etc.]]; accusative νῶιν Zenod.ad [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 8.377]]; Attic dialect νώ [Refs 8th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Phaedrus” 278b (also 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 5.219, 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 15.475); νῶε 5th-6th c.BC: Antimachus Colophonius Elegiacus et Epicus 39, 6th c.BC: Corinna Lyrica 5: _genitive_, _dative_ νῶι; νῷν 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Antigone” 3]]; νῶι dative, [Refs 5th c.AD+ [5th-6th c.AD: Orphica “Lithica” 773]]; νῶιν, ={ἡμῖν}, [Refs 4th c.AD+ [4th c.AD(?): Quintus Smyrnaeus Epicus 1.213, etc.]]

__IV
plural, nominative ἡμεῖς (ἡμέες falsa lectio in [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 2.6, +others, rejected by 2nd c.AD: Apollonius Dyscolus Grammaticus “de Pronominibus;” 93.1)]]; Aeolic dialect ἄμμες [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 9.303, 7th-6th c.BC: Alcaeus Lyricus 18.3, 5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “P.” 4.144]]; Doric dialect ἁμές [Refs 7th c.BC+ [7th c.BC: Alcman Lyricus 65, 5th c.BC: Epicharmus Comicus 42, 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Lysistrata” 168:— _genitive_ ἡμῶν (also ἥμων 2nd c.AD: Apollonius Dyscolus Grammaticus “de Syntaxi;” 130.23)]]; Ionic dialect ἡμέων [Refs 8th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.112, etc.; ἡμείων 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 24.170, 3rd c.BC: Herodas Mimographus 1.46]]; Aeolic dialect ἀμμέων [Refs 7th c.BC+ [7th-6th c.BC: Alcaeus Lyricus 88, “Milet.” 3 No.152.29]]; ἄμμων [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [[prev. work]74, 2nd c.AD: Apollonius Dyscolus Grammaticus “de Pronominibus;” 95.3]]; Doric dialect ἁμέων [Refs 7th c.BC+ [7th c.BC: Alcman Lyricus 66]]; ἁμῶν [[Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Epicharmus Comicus] 266, 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Lysistrata” 168, 3rd c.BC: Theocritus Poeta Bucolicus 2.158]]; Cretan dialect, Boeotian dialect ἁμίων [Refs 5th c.BC+ [“SIG” 528.5, 2nd c.AD: Apollonius Dyscolus Grammaticus “de Pronominibus;” 95.21:— _dative_ ἡμῖν, in 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus also ἡμίν]] (ῐ) (or ἧμιν Aristarch.ad [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 1.214, 2nd c.AD: Apollonius Dyscolus Grammaticus “de Pronominibus;” 95.3)]]; also rarely in Comedy texts, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Phrynichus Comicus 37, 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Aves” 386 (uncertain)]]; Aeolic dialect ἄμμῐν, ἄμμῐ, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 1.384, 7th-6th c.BC: Alcaeus Lyricus 80, +others, 5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “P.” 4.155, 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Septem contra Thebas” 156 (Lyric poetry), “Milet.” 3 No.152; ἄμμεσιν 7th-6th c.BC: Alcaeus Lyricus 100]]; Doric dialect also ἁμίν or ἇμιν, [Refs 7th c.BC+ [7th c.BC: Alcman Lyricus 77, 78, 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Eumenides” 347 (Lyric poetry), 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Lysistrata” 1081]]; with ῑ, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [[prev. author] “Ach.” 821, 3rd c.BC: Theocritus Poeta Bucolicus 7.145:— _accusative_ ἡμᾶς (also ἧμᾰς 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 16.372)]]; Ionic dialect ἡμέας [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 8.211, “SIG” 273.25 (Milet., 4th c.BC)]]; ἥμεας [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 4.294 (cf. Hdn.Gr. 2.140)]]; Aeolic dialect ἄμμε [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 1.59, 7th-6th c.BC: Sappho Lyrica 115]], Theocr.8.25; Doric dialect ἁμέ [Refs 6th c.BC+ [“SIG” 1 (Abu Simbel, 6th c.BC), 5th c.BC: Epicharmus Comicus 173, 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Acharnenses” 759 codices, “Lys.” 95.]]—On these dialectic varieties, [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [see 2nd c.AD: Apollonius Dyscolus Grammaticus “de Pronominibus;” 50]] ff. (Cf. Sanskrit ahám (ἐγών), accusative plural asmā´n; for νώ cf. Sanskrit nau):—frequently in answers, as an affirmative, especially in form ἔγωγε, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Trachiniae” 1248, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Theaetetus” 149b, etc.]]; οὗτος ἐ. here am [Refs 5th c.BC+ [I, 5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “O.” 4.26; ὅδ᾽ ἐκεῖνος ἐ. 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Coloneus” 138 (Lyric poetry)]]; rarely with Article, τὸν ἐμέ myself, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Theaetetus” 166a, “Sph.” 239b (but ὁ ἐ.]] the Self, the Ego, [Refs 5th c.AD+ [5th-6th c.AD: Damascius Philosophus “de Principiis” 444)]]; τίς ὢν οὗτος ὁ ἐγὼ τυγχάν; [Refs 4th c.BC+ [1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus 2.1119a; τί ἐστι φίλο; ἄλλος ἐ. 4th-5th c.BC: Pythagoras Philosophus cited in 5th c.AD: Hermias Alexandrinus Philosophus “in Platonis Phaedrum scholia” p.166 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus]]; τί τοῦτ᾽ ἐμο; ἡμῖν τί τοῦτ᾽ ἔστ; Latin quid mea hoc refert ? [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Thesmophoriazusae” 498, etc.]]; ἐγ; in a question, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Equites” 1336, +others]]; ἡμεῖς the self, ἔνθα δὴ ἡμεῖς μάλιστα [Refs 3rd c.AD+ [3rd c.AD: Plotinus Philosophus 1.1.7.]]

__III.2
with dative, ἀμπελίνῳ καρπῷ ἐ. to be filled with.., [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.212; ἐμπιπλάμενοι πυριάτῃ 5th c.BC: Cratinus Comicus 142; ἐμπίπλαται.. αἵματι ὁ βωμός 2nd c.AD: Pausanias Periegeta 3.16.10.]]

__III.3
with participle, μισῶν οὔποτ᾽ ἐμπλησθήσομαι γυναῖκας [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Hippolytus” 664, compare “Ion” 925; βάλλων.. οὐκ ἂν ἐμπλῄμην 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Acharnenses” 236; οὐκ ἐνεπίμπλασο ὑπισχνούμενος 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 7.7.46]]; ἔμπλησο λέγων speak thy fill, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Vespae” 603.]] —The two last constructions are post-Homeric. deep_entry:
Abbott-Smith / STEPBible (TBESG)
ἐν,
prep, (the most frequently of all in NT), with dative (= Heb. בְּ, Lat. in, with abl.).
__I. Of place, with dative of thing(s), of person(s), in, within, on, at, by, among: ἐν τ. πόλει, Luk.7:37; τ. οφθαλμῷ, Mat.7:3; τ. κοιλίᾳ, Mat.12:40; τ. ὄρει, 2Pe.1:18; τ. θρόνῳ, Rev.3:21; τ. δεξιᾷ τ. θεοῦ, Rom.8:34; ἐν ἡμῖν Abbott-Smith has ὑμῖν., Luk.1:1; of books, ἐν τ. βιβλίῳ, Gal.3:10; τ. νόμῳ, Mat.12:5, al.; ἐν τοῖς τ. Πατρός, in my Father's house (RV; cf. M, Pr., 103), Luk.2:49; trop., of the region of thought or feeling, ἐν τ. καρδίᾳ (-αις), Mat.5:28, 2Co.4:6, al.; τ. συνειδήσεσιν, 2Co.5:11; after verbs of motion, instead of εἰς (constructio praegnans, a usage extended in late Gk. beyond the limits observed in cl.; cf. Bl., §41, 1; M, Th., 12), ἀποστέλλω . . . ἐν, Mat.10:16. δέδωκεν ἐν τ. χειρί (cf. τιθέναι ἐν χερσί, Hom., Il., i, 441, al.), Jhn.3:35; id. after verbs of coming and going (not in cl.), εἰσῆλθε, Luk.9:46; ἐξῆλθεν, Luk.7:17.
__II. Of state, condition, form, occupation, etc.: ἐν ζωῇ, Rom.5:10; ἐν τ. θανάτῳ, 1Jn.3:14; ἐν πειρασμοῖς, 1Pe.1:6; ἐν εἰρήνῃ, Mrk.5:25; ἐν δόξῃ, Php.4:19; ἐν πραΰτητι, Jas.3:13; ἐν μυστηρίῳ, 1Co.2:7; ἐν τ. διδαχῇ, Mrk.4:2; of a part as contained in a whole, ἐν τ. ἀμπέλῳ, Jhn.15:4; ἐν ἑνὶ σώματι, Rom.12:4; of accompanying objects or persons (simple dative in cl.), with, ἐν αἵματι, Heb.9:25; ἐν δέκα χιλιάσιν, Luk.14:31 (cf. Ju 14, Act.7:14); similarly (cl.), of clothing, armour, arms, ἐν στολαῖς, Mrk.12:38; ἐν ἐσθῆτι λαμπρᾷ, Jas.2:2; ἐν μαξαίρῃ, Luk.22:49; ἐν ῥάβδῳ, 1Co.4:21 (cf. ἐν τόξοις, Xen., Mem., 3, 9, 2); of manner (cl.), ἐν τάχει (= ταχέως), Luk.18:8 (cf. Bl., §41, 1); of spiritual influence, ἐν πνεύματι, Rom.8:9; ἐν π. ἀκαθάρτῳ, Mrk.1:23; of the mystical relation of the Christian life and the believer himself, to God and Christ (cf. ICC, Ro., 160f.;  Mayor on Ju 1; M, Pr., 103): ἐν Χριστῷ, Rom.3:24, 6:11, 1Co.3:1, 4:10, 2Co.12:2, Gal.2:17, Eph.6:21, Col.4:7, 1Th.4:16, al.
__III. Of the agent, instrument or means (an extension of cl. ἐν of instr.—see LS, see word Ill—corresponding to similar use of Heb. בְּ), by, with: ἐν ὑμῖν κρίνεται ὁ κόσμος (= cl. παρά, C. dative), 1Co.6:2; ἐν τ. ἄρχοντι τ. δαιμονίων, Mat.9:34; ἐν αἵματι, Heb.9:22; ἐν ὕδατι, Mat.3:11, al.; ἐν μαχαίρᾳ ἀποκτενεῖ (cf. the absol. ἐν μ., ἐν ῥάβδῳ, supr., II, which some would classify here), Rev.13:10 (cf. 6:8). Allied to this usage and distinctly Semitic are the following: ἠγόρασας . . . ἐν τ. αἵματι σου (cf. BDB, see word בְּ, III, 3), Rev.5:9; ὁμολογεῖν ἐν (= Aram. אודי בּ; cf. McNeile on Mt, I.with; M, Pr., 104), Mat.10:32, Luk.12:8; ὀμνύναι ἐν (= cl. accusative, so Jas.5:12), Mat.5:34, al.; also at the rate of, amounting to, Mrk.4:8 (WH; vv. ll., εἰς, ἒν), Act.7:14 (LXX).
__IV. Of time,
__(a) in or during a period: ἐν τ. ἡμέρᾳ (νυκτί), Jhn.11:9, al.; ἐν σαββάτῳ, Mat.12:2, al.; ἐν τῷ μεταξύ, meanwhile, Jhn.4:31;
__(b) at the time of an event: ἐν τ. παρουσίᾳ, 1Co.15:23; ἐν τ. ἀναστάσει, Mat.22:28;
__(with) with art. inf.,
__(α) present (so sometimes in cl., but not as in NT = ἕως; V. M, Pr., 215), while: Mat.13:4, Mrk.6:48, Gal.4:18, al.;
__(β) aor., when, after: Luk.9:36, al.;
__(d) within (cl.): Mat.27:40,
__V. In composition: (1) meaning: (a) with adjectives, it signifies usually the possession of a quality, as ἐνάλιος, ἐν́δοξος; (b) with verbs, continuance in (before ἐν) or motion into (before εἰς), as ἐμμένω, ἐμβαίνω. (ii) Assimilation: ἐν becomes ἐμ- before β, μ, π, φ, ψ; ἐγ- before γ, κ, ξ, χ; ἐλ- before λ. But in the older MSS of NT, followed by modern editions, assimilation is sometimes neglected, as in ἐνγράφω, ἐγκαινίζω, etc.

OF TIME, ὥρῃ ἐν εἰαρινῇ [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 16.643; ἐν νυκτί 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 6.69, 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Symposium” 1.9; ἐν χρόνῳ μακρῷ 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Philoctetes” 235, “OC” 88]]; ἐν τούτῳ (i.e. τῷ χρόνῶ) in this space of time, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.126, etc.]]; ἐν ᾧ (i.e. χρόνῳ) during the time that, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Trachiniae” 929, etc. (also ἐν οἷς 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “de Mundo” 391a2); ἐν ὅσῳ 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 3.28]]; ἐν ταῖς σπονδαῖς in the time of the truce, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 3.1.1; ἐν τῇ ἑορτῇ 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 7.73 (but in some phrases the ἐν is omitted, as μυστηρίοις]] in the course of the mysteries, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Plutus” 1013]]; τραγῳδοῖς at the performance of.., [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aeschines Orator 3.36).]]

__A.IV.b
ἐν ἄρχοντι Μητροδώρῳ during the archonship of M., [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [“IG” 7.1773 (Thebes, 2nd c.AD); ἐν ἄρχοντι Σύλλᾳ [prev. work]3.113.]]

__A.IV.2
in, within, ἐν ἡμέρῃ [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.126; ἐν ἔτεσι πεντήκοντα 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 1.118; ἐν τρισὶ μησί 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Historia Graeca (Hellenica)” 1.1.37, etc.]]; μυρίαις ἐν ἁμέραις in, i.e. after, countless days, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Phoenissae” 305 (Lyric poetry); ἐν ἡμέραις πολλαῖς νοσῆσαι 6th c.AD: Procopius Caesariensis Historicus “Historia Arcana” 9.35.]]

__A.V
OF NUMBERS generally, ἐν δυσὶ σταδίοις within two stadia, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [1st c.BC: Diodorus Siculus Historicus 20.74, compare 19.39, uncertain in 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 6.1.]]

__A.V.2
with genitive of price, ἐν δύο ταλάντων [LXX.1Ki.16.24.]

__A.V.3
amounting to, προῖκα ἐν δραχμαῖς ἐννακοσίαις [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [“BGU” 970.14 (2nd c.AD), etc.]]

__B
WITH Acc., into, on, for, [Refs 4th c.AD+ [4th c.AD(?): Arcadius Grammaticus ἰν, νόμος ἰν ἄματα πάντα “IG” 5 (2).5; γράψαι ἐν χάλκωμα [prev. work]511; ἐν πελτοφόρας ἀπεγράψατο [prev. work]7.210 (from Aegosthenae), etc.]]; also poetry, ἐν πάντα νόμον [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “P.” 2.86.]]

__C
WITHOUT CASE, AS adverb, in the phrase ἐν δέ..,

__C.1
and therein, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 9.361; ἐν μέν.. ἐν δέ 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 13.244.]]

__C.2
and among them, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 2.588, etc.; in 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus, mostly ἐν δὲ δή.. 3.39, 5.95; or ἐν δὲ καί.. 2.43, 172, 176.]]

__C.3
and besides, moreover (not in Attic dialect Prose), [Refs 8th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Ajax” 675, “OT” 181 (Lyric poetry), +others; ἐν δ᾽ ὑπέρας τε κάλους τε πόδας τ᾽ ἐνέδησεν ἐν αὐτῇ 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 5.260.]]

__C.4
ἔνι, ={ἔνεστι, ἔνεισι}, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 20.248, etc.]]

__D
POSITION: ἐν frequently stands between its substantive and the adjective agreeing therewith, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 22.61, 5th c.BC: Bacchylides Lyricus 5.41, etc.]]: without an adjective, τῷ δ᾽ ἐν ἐρινεός ἐστι μέγας [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 12.103: most frequently in 8th c.BC: Homerus Epicus in the form ἐνί, which is then written by anastrophe ἔνι, 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 7.221, 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 5.57; in 5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus]] between substantive and genitive, χόρτοις ἐν λέοντος [Refs [“O.” 13.44, +others]]--One or more independent words sometimes come between the preposition and its dative, as in [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 11.115]]; also in Prose, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 6.69.]]

__E
IN COMPOSITION (joined with other words),

__E.I
with Verbs, the preposition mostly retains its sense of being in or at a place, etc., with dative, or followed by εἰς.., or ἐν..: in such forms as ἐνορᾶν τινί τι, in translating, we resolve the compound, to remark a thing in one.

__E.I.b
also, at a person, ἐγγελᾶν, ἐνυβρίζειν τινί.

__E.I.2
with adjectives, it expresses

__E.I.2.a
a modified degree, as in ἔμπηλος, ἔμπικρος, ἔνσιμος, rather...

__E.I.2.b
the possession of a quality, as in ἔναιμος with blood in it, ἐνάκανθος thorny: ἔμφωνος with a voice: ἔννομος in accordance with law, etc.

__E.II
ἐν becomes ἐμ- before the labials β μ π φ ; ἐγ- before the gutturals γ κ ξ ; ἐλ- before ; ἐρ- before ; rarely ἐσ- before ; but Inscrr. and Papyri often preserve ἐν- in all these cases.

ἐν-αντίος, -α, -ον
(ἀντίος, set against), [in LXX: ἐξ ἐναντίας, for נֶגֶד, etc.; ἐναντίον, for פָּנִים etc. ;]
over against, opposite, contrary: ἄνεμος, Mat.14:24, Mrk.6:48, Act.27:4; ἐξ ἐναντίας (ellipse obscure, see Bl., § 44,1; Mozley, Psa.42:1-11), with genitive, Mrk.15:39. Metaphorical, opposed, hostile: 1Th.2:15, Act.26:9 28:17; ὁ ἐξ ἐ., Tit.2:8. LSJ / STEPBible (TFLSJ)
ἐναντίος, α, ον,
opposite, ={ἀντίος} (which is rare in Prose):

__1
of Place, on the opposite side, opposite, c.dative, ἀκταὶ ἐναντίαι ἀλλήλῃσιν [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 10.89; Πάτροκλος δέ οἱ.. ἐ. ἧστο 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 9.190, compare 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 23.89]]: hence, fronting, face to face, αὐτῳ οὔ πω φαίνετ᾽ ἐναντίη [Refs 7th c.BC+ [6.329; ὄττις ἐ. τοι ἰσδάνει 7th-6th c.BC: Sappho Lyrica 2.2]]; δεῖξον.. τὸ σὸν πρόσωπον δεῦρ᾽ ἐ. πατρί before him, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Hippolytus” 947]]; τὰναντία τινί things open to one's sight, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 3.3.345: _absolutely_, ἐ. στάνθ᾽ 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Hippolytus” 1078 (but ἐ. κεῖσθαι]] look opposite ways, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Symposium” 190a).]]

__1.b
with Verbs of motion, in the opposite direction, ἔνθα οἱ.. ἐναντίη ἤλυθε μήτηρ came to meet him, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 6.251; ἐναντίοι ἀλλήλοισιν ὄγμον ἐλαύνωσιν 11.67; δύο ἅμαξαι ἐ. ἀλλήλαις 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 1.93; ἄνεμος ἐ. ἔπνει 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 4.5.3.]]

__1.c
Astrology texts, in diametrical aspect, [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd c.AD: Vettius Valens Astrologus 70.16, 4th c.AD(?): Manetho Astrologus 3.360.]]

__2
in hostile sense, opposing, facing in fight, with genitive, ἐναντίοι ἔσταν Ἀχαιῶν [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 5.497, compare 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Ajax” 1284, 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 4.3.28, etc.: with _dative_, 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 5.12, 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Supplices” 856, “IT” 1415]]; οἱ ἐ. one's adversaries, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Septem contra Thebas” 375, 5th c.BC: Gorgias Rhetor et Sophista “fragment” 12 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator, etc.]]; the enemy, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 7.225, 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 4.64, etc.]]

__2.b
generally, opposed to, τινί [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 3.2.10]]; τὸ ἐ. the opposite party, [Refs [[prev. author] “Ath.” 1.4]]; presenting obstacles, hindering, τινί [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Philoctetes” 642.]]

__2.c
ὁ δι ἐναντίας the opponent in a alawsuit, [Refs 3rd c.AD+ [“PFlor.” 1.58.15 (3rd c.AD), etc.]]

__3
of qualities, acts, etc., opposite, contrary, reverse, τἀναντί᾽ εἰπεῖν [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Agamemnon” 1373; δίκαια καὶ τἀναντία 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Antigone” 667: mostly with _genitive_, τὰ ἐ. τούτων]] the very reverse of these things, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.82, compare 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 7.75, etc.]]; δείξας.. ἄστρων τὴν ἐ. ὁδόν, i.e. τὴν τοῦ ἡλίου ὁδὸν ἐ. οὖσαν τοῖς ἄστροις [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Fragmenta” 861: also with _dative_, Ὀρφεῖ δὲ γλῶσσαν τὴν ἐναντίαν ἔχεις 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Agamemnon” 1629]]; τἀναντία πρήσσειν [τῇ ὑγιείῃ] [Refs 5th c.BC+ [3rd c.AD: Democritus Epigrammaticus 234; δύο τὰ -ώτατα εὐβουλίᾳ 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 3.42; ἀγαθῷ κακὸν -ώτερον ἢ τῷ μὴ ἀγαθῷ 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 491d; ἐναντία λέγει αὐτὸς αὑτῷ [prev. author] “Prt.” 339b, compare 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Acharnenses” 493; τἀναντία τούτοις 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Prt” 323d]]; ἐναντία γνῶναι ταῖς πλείσταις [πόλεσιν] [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Respublica Lacedaemoniorum” 1.2; τὴν ἐ. τινὶ ψῆφον θέσθαι 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 19.65; simply τὴν ἐ. θέσθαι τινί 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Laches” 184d: followed by ἤ, τοὺς ἐ. λόγους ἢ ὡς αὐτὸς κατεδόκεε 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.22; τοὐ. δρῶν ἢ προσῆκ᾽ αὐτῷ ποιεῖν 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Plutus” 14; τοὐ. ἔπαθεν ἢ τὸ προσδοκώμενον 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Leges” 966e, compare “R.” 567c, etc.: frequently strengthened, πᾶν τοὐ., πάντα τἀ]]., quite the contrary, Lg.[Refs 5th c.BC+ [967a, 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Memorabilia” 3.12.4]]; πολὺ τοὐ. [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Strattis Comicus 57; τὸ δὲ πολὺ ἐναντίον ἀποβήσεται 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Apologia” 39c.]]

__3.b
τὰ ἐ. opposites in Philos., [Refs 6th c.BC+ [6th c.BC: Pherecydes Syrius Philosophus 3, 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Metaphysica” 986b3, etc.]]

__4
in the Philos. of [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus, τἀναντία (distinct from other ἀντικείμενα, “Metaphorical” 1018a25)]] are contraries, especially the two attributes within the same genus which differ most widely from each other (as hot and cold), [Refs [“Cat.” 6a18, +others]]

__4.b
ἐ. ἀποφάνσεις, προτάσεις, contrary propositions (All [Refs [B is A, No B is A)]], opposed to contradictory (see. ἀντιφατικῶς), [Refs [[prev. author] “Int.” 17b4, “APr.” 63b28.]]

__II
frequently in adverb usages:

__II.1
from [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Homerus Epicus downwards, _neuter_ ἐναντίον]] as adverb, opposite, facing, ἐ. ὧδε κάλεσσον here to my face, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 17.544]]; εἰς ὦπα ἰδέσθαι ἐ. to look one in the face,[Refs 5th c.BC+ [23.107; ἐ. προσβλέπειν τινά 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Hecuba” 968, etc.; γυναῖκας ἀνδρῶν μὴ βλέπειν ἐ. [prev. work] 975: _absolutely_, 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 4.40, etc.]]: hence, like a preposition with genitive, in the presence of, τῆς βουλῆς [Refs [“IG” 12.91]]; τῶνδ᾽ ἐ. [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Coloneus” 1002]]; μαρτύρων ἐ. [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Ecclesiazusae” 448; ἐ. τοῦ παιδίου [prev. author] “Lys.” 907; ἐ. ἁπάντων λέγειν 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 6.25; ἐ. Διός 2nd c.BC: Polybius Historicus 7.9.2; also _neuter_ _plural_, “IG” 7.1779 (from Thespiae).]]

__II.1.b
in hostile sense, against, with genitive, ἀνέσταν.. σφοῦ πατρὸς ἐ. [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 1.534; ἐ. ἰέναι τινός 21.574; ἐ. μάχεσθαί τινος 20.97; ἐ. ἵστασ᾽ ἐμεῖο 13.448: _absolutely_, ἐ. μίμνειν]] stand one's ground against, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. work] 106: with _dative_, νεικεῖν ἀλλήλοισιν ἐ. 20.252; ἐ. θεοῖς 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Orestes” 624; ἐ. τῷ ὅρκῳ πράττειν “IG” 22.1258.2.]]

__II.1.c
contrariwise, in Attic dialect also with the Article, τοὐναντίον on the other hand, τοὐ. δέ.. [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Antiphanes Comicus 80.4]]; ἢ πάλιν τοὐ. [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-3rd c.BC: Menander Comicus 460.5]]; conversely, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Meno” 89e.]]

__II.1.d
neuter plural ἐναντία as adverb, with dative, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 6.32, 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 1.29, etc.]]

__II.2
with Preps., ἐκ τοῦ ἐ. over against, opposite, opposed to ἐκ πλαγίου, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Historia Graeca (Hellenica)” 4.5.15, etc.]]; ἐξ ἐναντίας, Ionic dialect -ίης, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 7.225, 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 4.33 (οἱ ἐξ ἐ]]. the opposing parties, probably in [Refs 4th c.AD+ [“PGrenf.” 2.78.26 (4th c.AD))]]; ἐκ τῶν ἐ. on the contrary, [Refs 2nd c.BC+ [2nd c.BC: Polybius Historicus 5.9.9; ἀπ᾽ ἐναντίας 1st c.BC: Asclepiodotus Tacticus “Tact.” 1.2; ἀπ᾽ ἐ. Χωρεῖν 6th c.AD: Procopius Caesariensis Historicus “Historia Arcana” 4]]; κατὰ τὰ ἐ. [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Timaeus” 39a: Geometry texts, αἱ κατ᾽ ἐναντίον τοῦ παραλληλογράμμου πλευραί]] the opposite sides of the parallelogram, [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [3rd c.BC: Archimedes Geometra “περὶ ἰσορροπιῶν” 1.9]]; αἱ κατ᾽ ἐ. τομαί opposite sections (i. e. branches) of the hyperbola, [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [3rd-2nd c.BC: Apollonius Pergaeus Geometra “Conica” 3.23.]]

__II.3
regular adverb -ίως contrariwise, with dative, τούτοις οὐκ ἐ. λέγεις [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Eumenides” 642; ἐ. διακεῖσθαί τινι 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 361c; ἐ. ἀντικεῖσθαι 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “de Interpretatione” 17b20]]; πικρῶς καὶ ἐ. like an enemy, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 19.339; ἐ. ἢ ὡς ἀνδραπόδοις τραφεῖσι 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Theaetetus” 175d]]; ἐ. ἔχειν to be exactly opposed, [Refs [[prev. author] “Euthd.” 278a]]; πρός τι to be contrary in respect of.., [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 1.4]]; in the Logic of [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus, “Metaphorical” 1057b11, +others, compare 5th c.AD: Proclus Philosophus “in Platonis Alcibiadem” p.268C.]]

ἔνειμι
(εἰμί, sum), 3rd.pers. singular and plural ἔνι frequently for ἔνεστι, ἔνεισι (see. below): infinitive ἐνεῖμεν [Refs [“IG” 22.1126.24 (Amphict.Delph.): _3rd.pers._ _sing._ ἔνι frequently for]]future ἐνέσομαι:—to be in, ἄργυρος ἀσκῷ ἔνεστι [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 10.45]]; ἔνι (for ἔνεστι) κήδεα θυμῷ [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 18.53; ἔνι τοι φρένες οὐδ᾽ ἠβαιαί 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 21.288; εἰ.. χάλκεον.. μοι ἦτορ ἐνείη 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 2.490]]; εἴ τι ἐνέοι (i.e. τοῖς χρησμοῖσι) [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 7.6; νοῦς ἔνεστιν ὑμῖν ἐγγενής 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Electra” 1328]]; τοῖς λόγοις ἔ. κέρδος[Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. work] 370; πόλλ᾽ ἔ. τῷ γήρᾳ κακά 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Vespae” 441; πλήθη, ἐν οἷς τὸ ἓν οὐκ ἔνι 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Parmenides” 158c; στάσιν ἐνέσεσθαι τῇ γνώμῃ 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 2.20; εἴσοι πυκνότης ἔνεστ᾽ ἐν τῷ τρόπῳ 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Equites” 1132; ἐνῆν ἄρ᾽.. κἀν οἴνῳ λόγος 4th c.BC: Amphis Comicus 41; ἀγαθὸς βαφεὺς ἔνεστιν ἐν τῷ παιδιῳ 4th-3rd c.BC: Diphilus Comicus 72: ἔνι τις καὶ ἐν ἡμῖν παῖς 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Phaedo” 77e; also ἐν τοῖσιν οὔρεσι δένδρεα ἔνι ἄγρια 4th-5th c.BC: Hecataeus Milesius Historicus 292 1st c.AD: Josephus Historicus; ἐν [ὄρει] ἔνι μέταλλα 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 7.112; ἐν τῷ προθυμεῖσθαι ἐνοῦσαν ζημίαν 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Prometheus Vinctus” 383, etc.]]

__b
with dative plural, to be among, [NT+6th c.BC+ [6th c.BC: Theognis Elegiacus 1135, 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 3.81, +others; οὐκ ἔνι ἐν ὑμῖν οὐδεὶς σοφός NT.1Cor.6.5.]]

__c
with adverb loci, οἴκοι ἔνεστι γόος [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 24.240]]; ἔνεστιν αὐτόθι is in this very place, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Equites” 119; ἐνταῦθα [prev. author] “Nu.” 211, etc.]]

__2
absolutely, to be present in a place, οἶνος ἐνέην [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 9.164]]; οὐδ᾽ ἄνδρες νηῶν ἔνι τέκτονες[Refs 4th c.BC+ [[prev. work] 126; οὐδ᾽ ἔνι στάσις 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Persae” 738 (troch.); Ἄρης οὐκ ἔνι χώρᾳ [prev. author] “Ag.” 78 (_anapaest meter_)]]; σίτου οὐκ ἐνόντος as there was no corn there, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 4.8]]; τὰ ἐνόντα ἀγαθά the good that is therein, [Refs [[prev. work] 20]]; ἱερῶν τῶν ἐνόντων the temples that were in the place,[Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. work] 97; ἀμέλειά τις ἐνῆν καὶ διατριβή [prev. author] 5.38; πόλεμος οὐκ ἐνῆν 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Politicus” 271e; μηδὲ μύλαν ἐνεῖμεν μηδὲ ὅλμον “IG” 22.[same place]]]; also, to be mentioned in a treaty, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 8.43, compare 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Aves” 974]]; χρόνος ἐνέσται time will be necessary, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 1.80]]; ἡ βὴξ ἔνι the cough is persistent, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Hippocrates Medicus “ἐπιδημίαι” 7.12.]]

__II
to be possible, ἄρνησις οὐκ ἔ. ὧν ἀνιστορεῖς [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Tyrannus” 578; τῶνδ᾽ ἄρνησις οὐκ ἔ. μοι [prev. author] “El.” 527]]; τίς δ᾽ ἔνεστί μοι λόγο; what plea is possible for me [to make]? [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Iphigenia Taurica” 998; οὐκ ἐνῆν πρόφασις 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 2.1.25; οὐκ ἐνέσται αὐτῷ λόγος οὐδὲ εἷς 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 21.41; εἴ τι ἄλλο ἐνῆν [prev. author] 18.190; ἐνούσης οὐδεμιᾶς ἔτ᾽ ἀποστροφῆς [prev. author] 24.9.]]

__II.2
impersonal, with dative person et infinitive, it is in one's power, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Trachiniae” 296, “Ant.” 213, etc.]]: with infinitive only, οὔκουν ἔ. καὶ μεταγνῶνα; [Refs 4th c.BC+ [[prev. author] “Ph.” 1270; οὐ γὰρ δὴ τοῦτό γ᾽ ἔνεστιν εἰπεῖν 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 29.14; πῶς ἔ. ἢ πῶς δυνατό; [prev. author] 57.24, etc.]]; οὐκ ἔνεστι it is not possible, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Anaxilas Comicus 22.7]]; ὃ μὴ νεώς γε τῆς ἐμῆς ἔνι which it is not possible [to get] from my ship, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Philoctetes” 648 (sed to be read ἔπι): ἔνι is frequently in this sense, ἃ δὲ ἔνι [λέγειν] 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 2.4; δι᾽ ὀργήν γ᾽ ἔνι φῆσαι πεποιηκέναι [prev. author] 21.41]]; ὡς ἔνι ἥδιστα in the pleasantest way possible, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Memorabilia” 4.5.9, compare 3.8.4; ὡς ἔνι μάλιστα 2nd c.BC: Polybius Historicus 21.4.14, 1st c.AD: Philo Judaeus 1.465, 2nd c.AD: Lucianus Sophista “Prom.” 6, 4th c.AD: Julianus Imperator “Orationes” 7.218c]]: imperfect, ὡς ἐνῆν ἄριστα [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd c.AD: Lucianus Sophista “Tyr.” 17.]]

__II.2.b
ἔνεστιν ὑμᾶς εἰδέναι it is relevant, pertinent, [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [“BGU” 486.12 (2nd c.AD).]]

__II.3
participle ἐνόν, absolutely, ἐνὸν αὐτοῖς σώζεσθαι since it was in them, was possible for them, [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd c.AD: Herodianus Grammaticus 8.3.2, compare 2nd c.AD: Lucianus Sophista “Anach.” 9.]]

__II.4
τὰ ἐνόντα all things possible: τὸ πλῆθος τῶν ἐ. εἰπεῖν the possible materials for a speech, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Isocrates Orator 5.110, compare 11.44; τῶν ἐ... ἐν τῷ πράγματι 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Phaedrus” 235b; τῶν φαινομένων καὶ ἐ. τὰ κράτιστα ἑλέσθαι 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 18.190]]; ἐκ τῶν ἐ. as well as one can under the circumstances, [Refs [[prev. work]256]]; τὰ ἐ. καὶ τὰ ἁρμόττοντα [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Poetica” 1450b5: in _sing._, πᾶν τὸ ἐνὸν ἐκλέγων 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 4.59.]]

__II.4.b
τὰ ἐνόντα cargo or stores in a ship, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 488c]]; contents of a basket, [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [“PTeb.” 414.20 (2nd c.AD).]]

[Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 1.110, etc.]], or ἕνεκεν (twice in [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Homerus Epicus, 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 17.288, 310, rare in Trag., as 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Medea” 999 (Lyric poetry), and early Prose, 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 6.2, 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Historia Graeca (Hellenica)” 2.1.14, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Symposium” 210e; in Comedy texts, 4th-3rd c.BC: Menander Comicus “Ἐπιτρέποντες” 330]]; twice in 4th C Attic dialect Inscrr., [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [“IG” 2.987A2, 611b13, but prevalent in later Inscrr., compare “SIG” 577.7 (Milet., 3rd-2nd c.BC)]]; εἵνεκεν [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Bacchylides Lyricus 12.136, 5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “I.” 8(7).35 codices]]; εἵνεκε [Refs 5th c.BC+ [2nd c.AD: Aretaeus Medicus “ὀξέων νούσων θεραπευτικόν” 1.2, _falsa lectio_ in 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 7.133)]]: ἕνεκε [Refs 4th c.BC+ [“SIG” 333.14 (Samos, 4th c.BC), “Supp.epigram” 1.351.10 ([prev. passage]), “CIG” “Corpus Inscriptionum Graecarum” “Corpus Inscriptionum Graecarum” 3655.18 (Cyzicus, 3rd-2nd c.BC)]]: Aeolic dialect ἔννεκα [Refs 7th c.BC+ [7th-6th c.BC: Alcaeus Lyricus “Supp.” 9.1, “IG” 12(2).258.8 (Lesbos, 1st c.AD)]], but ἔνεκα [Refs [[prev. work] 11(4).1064b32 (from Delos), 12(1).645a38 (from Nesus): late]]ἕνεκον [Refs [“JHS” 37.108 (from Lydia)]], etc.:—preposition with genitive, usually after its case; also before, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 1.94, 5th c.BC: Bacchylides Lyricus 12.136, 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 3.122, etc.]] When it follows its case, it is sometimes separated from it by several words, as in [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.30, 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 20.88, etc.]]

__1
on account of, Τρώων πόλιν.. ἧς εἵνεκ᾽ ὀϊζύομεν κακὰ πολλά [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 14.89, etc.; ὕβριος εἵνεκα τῆσδε 1.214]]; τοῦδ᾽ ἕνεκα for this,[Refs [[prev. work] 110; ὧν ἕ.]]wherefore, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [20.21; τίνος ἕ. βλάβη; 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Fragmenta - American Journal of Philology” 181; παῖσαι ἄνδρας ἕνεκεν ἀταξίας 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 5.8.13; στεφανοῦσθαι ἀρετῆς ἕνεκα 4th c.BC: Aeschines Orator 3.10]]; for the sake of, τοῦ ἕ.; [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Protagoras” 31c b]]; τῶν δὲ εἵνεκα, ὅκως.., or ἵνα.., [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 8.35, 40; κολακεύειν ἕ. μισθοῦ 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Historia Graeca (Hellenica)” 5.1.17]]; διὰ νόσον ἕ. ὑγιείας by reason of sickness for the sake of health, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Lysis” 218e, compare “Smp.” 185b]]; τὸ οὗ ἕ. the final cause, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Physica” 194a27, “Metaphorical” 983a31; τὸ οὗ ἕνεκεν [prev. author] “Ph.” 243a3, “Metaphorical” 1059a35.]]

__2
as far as regards, ἐμοῦ γ᾽ ἕνεκα as far as depends on me, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Acharnenses” 386, 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 20.14; τοῦ φυλάσσοντος εἵνεκεν 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.42]]; εἵνεκεν χρημάτων as for money, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. author] 3.122, etc.; ἕνεκά γε φιλονικίας 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 548d, compare 329b]]; ἐμπειρίας μὲν ἄρα ἕ.[Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. work] 582d; ὁμοῖοι τοῖς τυφλοῖς ἂν ἦμεν ἕνεκά γε τῶν ἡμετέρων ὀφθαλμῶν 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Memorabilia” 4.3.3.]]

__3
in consequence of, εἵνεκα τέχνας by force of art, [Refs [“Anthologia Graeca” 9.729.]]

__4
pleonastic, ἀμφὶσοὔνεκα [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Philoctetes” 554 codices]]; ὅσον ἀπὸ βοῆς ἕ. as far as shouting went, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 8.92, 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Historia Graeca (Hellenica)” 2.4.31; τίνος χάριν ἕ.; 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Leges” 701d, compare “Plt.” 302b.]]

conjunction, for οὕνεκα (which see), because, [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [hymnus ad Venerem 199, 3rd c.BC: Callimachus Epicus “Aetia” 3.1.6, “fragment” 287.]]

consideration, reflection, [NT+5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 1.132, NT.Matt.9.4 (_plural_), 2nd-3rd c.AD: Symmachus LXX.Job.21.27, Vett. Val.301.8, etc.]]

__II.2
idea, conception, εἰς ἐ. ἐσθήτων ἦλθον [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Diogenes Cynicus Philosophus Oen.10; τὰς ἐ. ὀξύς 2nd c.AD: Lucianus Sophista “Salt.” 81.]]

__III
anxiety, worry, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Hippocrates Medicus “παραγγελίαι” 4.]]

__IV
resolution, [Refs 4th c.AD+ [“BGU” 1024 iv 12 (4th c.AD).]]

deep_entry:
Abbott-Smith / STEPBible (TBESG)
ἔνι  Ionic form of ἐν (ἐνί), with strengthened accent;
[in LXX: Sir.37:2, 4Ma.4:22 * ;]
= ἔνεστι,
is in, has place, can be: 1Co.6:5, Gal.3:28 (tris) Col.3:11, Jas.1:17 (cf. Lft., Ga.; Hort and Mayor, Ja., ll. with).†
(AS)

---

LSJ / STEPBible (TFLSJ)
ἔνειμι
(εἰμί, sum), 3rd.pers. singular and plural ἔνι frequently for ἔνεστι, ἔνεισι (see. below): infinitive ἐνεῖμεν [Refs [“IG” 22.1126.24 (Amphict.Delph.): _3rd.pers._ _sing._ ἔνι frequently for]]future ἐνέσομαι:—to be in, ἄργυρος ἀσκῷ ἔνεστι [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 10.45]]; ἔνι (for ἔνεστι) κήδεα θυμῷ [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 18.53; ἔνι τοι φρένες οὐδ᾽ ἠβαιαί 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 21.288; εἰ.. χάλκεον.. μοι ἦτορ ἐνείη 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 2.490]]; εἴ τι ἐνέοι (i.e. τοῖς χρησμοῖσι) [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 7.6; νοῦς ἔνεστιν ὑμῖν ἐγγενής 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Electra” 1328]]; τοῖς λόγοις ἔ. κέρδος[Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. work] 370; πόλλ᾽ ἔ. τῷ γήρᾳ κακά 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Vespae” 441; πλήθη, ἐν οἷς τὸ ἓν οὐκ ἔνι 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Parmenides” 158c; στάσιν ἐνέσεσθαι τῇ γνώμῃ 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 2.20; εἴσοι πυκνότης ἔνεστ᾽ ἐν τῷ τρόπῳ 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Equites” 1132; ἐνῆν ἄρ᾽.. κἀν οἴνῳ λόγος 4th c.BC: Amphis Comicus 41; ἀγαθὸς βαφεὺς ἔνεστιν ἐν τῷ παιδιῳ 4th-3rd c.BC: Diphilus Comicus 72: ἔνι τις καὶ ἐν ἡμῖν παῖς 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Phaedo” 77e; also ἐν τοῖσιν οὔρεσι δένδρεα ἔνι ἄγρια 4th-5th c.BC: Hecataeus Milesius Historicus 292 1st c.AD: Josephus Historicus; ἐν [ὄρει] ἔνι μέταλλα 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 7.112; ἐν τῷ προθυμεῖσθαι ἐνοῦσαν ζημίαν 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Prometheus Vinctus” 383, etc.]]

__b
with dative plural, to be among, [NT+6th c.BC+ [6th c.BC: Theognis Elegiacus 1135, 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 3.81, +others; οὐκ ἔνι ἐν ὑμῖν οὐδεὶς σοφός NT.1Cor.6.5.]]

__c
with adverb loci, οἴκοι ἔνεστι γόος [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 24.240]]; ἔνεστιν αὐτόθι is in this very place, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Equites” 119; ἐνταῦθα [prev. author] “Nu.” 211, etc.]]

__2
absolutely, to be present in a place, οἶνος ἐνέην [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 9.164]]; οὐδ᾽ ἄνδρες νηῶν ἔνι τέκτονες[Refs 4th c.BC+ [[prev. work] 126; οὐδ᾽ ἔνι στάσις 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Persae” 738 (troch.); Ἄρης οὐκ ἔνι χώρᾳ [prev. author] “Ag.” 78 (_anapaest meter_)]]; σίτου οὐκ ἐνόντος as there was no corn there, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 4.8]]; τὰ ἐνόντα ἀγαθά the good that is therein, [Refs [[prev. work] 20]]; ἱερῶν τῶν ἐνόντων the temples that were in the place,[Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. work] 97; ἀμέλειά τις ἐνῆν καὶ διατριβή [prev. author] 5.38; πόλεμος οὐκ ἐνῆν 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Politicus” 271e; μηδὲ μύλαν ἐνεῖμεν μηδὲ ὅλμον “IG” 22.[same place]]]; also, to be mentioned in a treaty, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 8.43, compare 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Aves” 974]]; χρόνος ἐνέσται time will be necessary, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 1.80]]; ἡ βὴξ ἔνι the cough is persistent, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Hippocrates Medicus “ἐπιδημίαι” 7.12.]]

__II
to be possible, ἄρνησις οὐκ ἔ. ὧν ἀνιστορεῖς [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Tyrannus” 578; τῶνδ᾽ ἄρνησις οὐκ ἔ. μοι [prev. author] “El.” 527]]; τίς δ᾽ ἔνεστί μοι λόγο; what plea is possible for me [to make]? [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Iphigenia Taurica” 998; οὐκ ἐνῆν πρόφασις 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 2.1.25; οὐκ ἐνέσται αὐτῷ λόγος οὐδὲ εἷς 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 21.41; εἴ τι ἄλλο ἐνῆν [prev. author] 18.190; ἐνούσης οὐδεμιᾶς ἔτ᾽ ἀποστροφῆς [prev. author] 24.9.]]

__II.2
impersonal, with dative person et infinitive, it is in one's power, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Trachiniae” 296, “Ant.” 213, etc.]]: with infinitive only, οὔκουν ἔ. καὶ μεταγνῶνα; [Refs 4th c.BC+ [[prev. author] “Ph.” 1270; οὐ γὰρ δὴ τοῦτό γ᾽ ἔνεστιν εἰπεῖν 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 29.14; πῶς ἔ. ἢ πῶς δυνατό; [prev. author] 57.24, etc.]]; οὐκ ἔνεστι it is not possible, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Anaxilas Comicus 22.7]]; ὃ μὴ νεώς γε τῆς ἐμῆς ἔνι which it is not possible [to get] from my ship, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Philoctetes” 648 (sed to be read ἔπι): ἔνι is frequently in this sense, ἃ δὲ ἔνι [λέγειν] 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 2.4; δι᾽ ὀργήν γ᾽ ἔνι φῆσαι πεποιηκέναι [prev. author] 21.41]]; ὡς ἔνι ἥδιστα in the pleasantest way possible, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Memorabilia” 4.5.9, compare 3.8.4; ὡς ἔνι μάλιστα 2nd c.BC: Polybius Historicus 21.4.14, 1st c.AD: Philo Judaeus 1.465, 2nd c.AD: Lucianus Sophista “Prom.” 6, 4th c.AD: Julianus Imperator “Orationes” 7.218c]]: imperfect, ὡς ἐνῆν ἄριστα [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd c.AD: Lucianus Sophista “Tyr.” 17.]]

__II.2.b
ἔνεστιν ὑμᾶς εἰδέναι it is relevant, pertinent, [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [“BGU” 486.12 (2nd c.AD).]]

__II.3
participle ἐνόν, absolutely, ἐνὸν αὐτοῖς σώζεσθαι since it was in them, was possible for them, [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd c.AD: Herodianus Grammaticus 8.3.2, compare 2nd c.AD: Lucianus Sophista “Anach.” 9.]]

__II.4
τὰ ἐνόντα all things possible: τὸ πλῆθος τῶν ἐ. εἰπεῖν the possible materials for a speech, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Isocrates Orator 5.110, compare 11.44; τῶν ἐ... ἐν τῷ πράγματι 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Phaedrus” 235b; τῶν φαινομένων καὶ ἐ. τὰ κράτιστα ἑλέσθαι 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 18.190]]; ἐκ τῶν ἐ. as well as one can under the circumstances, [Refs [[prev. work]256]]; τὰ ἐ. καὶ τὰ ἁρμόττοντα [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Poetica” 1450b5: in _sing._, πᾶν τὸ ἐνὸν ἐκλέγων 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 4.59.]]

__II.4.b
τὰ ἐνόντα cargo or stores in a ship, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 488c]]; contents of a basket, [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [“PTeb.” 414.20 (2nd c.AD).]]

deep_entry:
Abbott-Smith / STEPBible (TBESG)
ἐνιαυτός, -oῦ, ὁ
[in LXX for שָׁנֶה ;]
__1. prop., a cycle of time.
__2. = ἔτος, a year: Jhn.11:49, 51 18:13, Act.11:26 18:11, Jas.5:17, Rev.9:15; pl., of sabbatical years, Gal.4:10; ποιεῖν ἐ., to spend a year, Jas.4:13;ἅπαξ τοῦ ἐ., Heb.9:7; κατ᾽ ἐ., Heb.9:25 10:1, 3; ἐ. δεκτόν, Luk.4:19 (LXX).†
(AS)

---

LSJ / STEPBible (TFLSJ)
ἐνῐ-αυτός, ὁ,
(ἐνί, αὐτός) properly anniversary, μηδὲ τᾷ ὑστεραίᾳ μηδ᾽ ἐν ταῖς δεκάταις μηδ᾽ ἐν τοῖς ἐνιαυτοῖς [Refs [“Michel” 995 C 49 (_plural_, Delph.): hence πρὸ τῶ ἐ.]] before the lapse of a year, [Refs [Leges Gortynensium 9.29]]; ἐνιαυτῷ on the expiry of a year, [Refs [[prev. work]1.35]]; and so, any long period of time, cycle, period, ἔτος ἦλθε περιπλομένων ἐνιαυτῶν as times rolled on the year came, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 1.16; ἐπιπλομένων ἐ. 8th-7th c.BC: Hesiodus Epicus “Theogonia” 493, “Sc.” 87; χρονίους ἐτῶν παλαιῶν ἐνιαυτούς 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Ranae” 347; πόλιν ἐνιαυτόν τινα ἔδοσαν ἐνοικεῖν 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 3.68]]; ὁ μέγας ἐ., of a Pythagorean cycle, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Eudemus Philosophus cited in 2nd c.AD: Theon Smyrnaeus Philosophus p.198 H]].; also of the Metonic Cycle of nineteen years, [Refs 1st c.BC+ [1st c.BC: Diodorus Siculus Historicus 12.36]]; of a period of [Refs 1st c.AD+ [600 years, 1st c.AD: Josephus Historicus “Antiquitates Judaicae” 1.3.9:— ἀΐδιος ἐ. 2nd c.AD: Apollodorus Damascenus Mechanicus 3.4.2.]]

__2
={ἔτος}, a year, εἴνατός ἐστι περιτροπέων ἐ. [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 2.295; δεκάτους περιτελλομένους ἐ. 8.404; Διὸς ἐνιαυτοί 2.134]]; μῆνές τε καὶ ἐνιαυτῶν περίοδοι [LXX+5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Timaeus” 47a; ἐ. ἡμερῶν LXX.Lev.25.29; ἐνιαυτόν]]during a year, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 1.288]]; αἱ σπονδαὶ ἐνιαυτὸν ἔσονται Indut. cited in [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 4.118; ἐπεί κε ὠνίαυτος ἐξέλθῃ “IG” 12(2).1.12 (Mytil., 4th c.BC)]]; τὸν πρῶτον ἐ. [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Lysias Orator 32.8]]; ὁπηνίκα.. τοὐνιαυτοῦ at what time in the year, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Fragmenta” 569.7]]; δὶς τοῦ ἐ. twice a year, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Critias” 118e; τοῦ ἐ.]]every year, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “de Vectigalibus” 4.23; ἑκάστου ἐ. [prev. author] “Ath.” 3.4; but ἕκαστον τὸν ἐ. “IG” 2.1055.4: with Preps., δι᾽ ἐνιαυτοῦ 5th c.BC: Antipho Orator “fragment” 28]]; δι᾽ ἐ. πέμπτου every five years, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Critias” 119d]]; θητεύσαμεν εἰς ἐ. for a year, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 21.444; τελεσφόρον εἰς ἐ. 19.32]]; κατ᾽ ἐνιαυτὸν ἄρξαι for a year, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 1.93]]; or, every year, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Isocrates Orator 3.17, 4th-3rd c.BC: Diphilus Comicus 38.5; καθ᾽ ἕκαστον ἐ. [prev. author] 89]]; ἐπ᾽ ἐ. for a year, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Leges” 945b, etc.]]; μετὰ τὸν ἐ. at the end of the year, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 1.138]]; παρ᾽ ἐνιαυτὸν ἄρχειν in alternate years, [Refs 1st c.BC+ [1st c.BC: Diodorus Siculus Historicus 4.65]]; πρὸ ἐνιαυτοῦ a year before, [Refs 1st c.AD+ [1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus 2.147e]]; ἐς τὸν σᾶτες ἐ. for the current year, [Refs [Inscriptiones Graecae 14.256 (from Phintias)]]; ἐν τῷ καθ᾽ ἕτος ἐ. in the current year, [Refs [“CIG” “Corpus Inscriptionum Graecarum” “Corpus Inscriptionum Graecarum” 3641b5 (from Lampsacus).]]

__3
Ἐνιαυτός, personified, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [2nd-3rd c.AD: Aelianus “Fragmenta” 19, 5th-6th c.AD: Orphica “Fragmenta” 127.3 (assuming variant), 5th c.AD: Proclus Philosophus “in Platonis Timaeum commentarii” 3.41 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator]]

__II
name for a Cornucopiae, [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [3rd c.BC(?): Callixinus Historicus 2, compare 2nd c.AD: Athenaeus Epigrammaticus 11.783c.]]

deep_entry:
Abbott-Smith / STEPBible (TBESG)
ἐν-ίστημι
[in LXX: 4Ki.13:6 A (עֶמְדָּה), 3Ki.12:24, 1Es.5:47 Est.9:6, Est.3:13, 1; 4Ma.9.1-32 * ;]
to place in; in pf., plpf., 2 aor. and in mid., intrans.;
__(a) to be at hand, impend, threaten: 2Ti.3:1;
__(b) to be present: 2Th.2:2 (but see Thayer, see word); pf. ptcp., present: 1Co.7:26, Gal.1:4, Heb.9:9; pl., Rom.8:38, 1Co.3:22 (Cremer, 3O9).†
(AS)

---

LSJ / STEPBible (TFLSJ)
ἐνίστημι,
causal in present, future and aorist 1 active, and aorist 1 middle:— put, place in, ἵππον ἐν λίθοις ἐνιστάναι [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “de Equitum magistro” 1.16; στήλας ἐνίστη ἐς τὰς χώρας 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 2.102]]; εἰς αὐτὴν (i.e. τὴν πόλιν) ἡνίοχον ἐνστῆσαι [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Politicus” 266e]]; τοὺς ἱπποκόμους εἰς (i.e. amongst) τοὺς ἱππέας ἐ. [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “de Equitum magistro” 5.6: with _dative_, ἱστὸν ἐνεστήσαντο μεσόδμῃ 3rd c.BC: Apollonius Rhodius Epicus 1.563.]]

__2
in Law, institute an heir, ἐ. κληρονόμους τοὺς υἱούς [Refs 6th c.AD+ [“PMasp.” 151.75 (6th c.AD).]]

__3
aorist 1 middle, also, begin, ὅσαι τὸ πρᾶγμα τοῦτ᾽ ἐνεστήσαντο [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Lysistrata” 268; οὐδὲν πώποτε τῶν πραγμάτων ἐνεστήσασθ᾽ ὀρθῶς 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 10.21]]; ὁ τοιοῦτον ἀγῶν᾽ ἐνστησάμενος [Refs [[prev. author] 18.4]]; ἐ. τὸ πρᾶγμα, Latin rem instituere, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Problemata” 951a28; ἀρχὰς τῆς γενέσεως 4th-3rd c.BC: Theophrastus Philosophus “Historia Plantarum” 7.10.4]]; ὀργὴν καὶ μῖσος πρός τινα ἐνστήσασθαι to begin to show.., [Refs 2nd c.BC+ [2nd c.BC: Polybius Historicus 1.82.9; πρᾶξιν 1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus “Aratus” 16]]: with infinitive, [Refs 1st c.BC+ [1st c.BC: Diodorus Siculus Historicus 14.53.]]

__4
ἐνστήσασθαι τὸ μέγεθος determine the size, [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [3rd-2nd c.BC: Philo Mechanicus “(Belopoeica) Excerpte aus Philons Mechanik - Ath. Berl. Akad.” 50.29.]]

__B
passive, with aorist 2, perfect, and pluperfect active:—to be set in, stand in, λὁχοις [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Supplices” 896; ἐν τῷ νηῷ 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 2.91: _absolutely_, πύλαι ἐνεστᾶσι ἑκατόν [prev. author] 1.179, compare 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Timaeus” 50d, etc.]]

__B.2
enter upon, take possession of, ὁ νικάσας ἐν τὰν οὐσίαν ἐνίσταται τὰν τοῦ ἁλόντος [Refs [“Foed. Delph.Pell.” 2 B 14.]]

__B.II
to be appointed, σοῦ ἐνεστεῶτος βασιλέος [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.120, compare 6.59; ἐς ἀρχήν [prev. author] 3.68; ἐς τυραννίδας [prev. author] 2.147.]]

__B.III
to be upon, threaten, with dative person, τοιούτων τοῖσι Σπαρτιήτῃσι ἐνεστεώτων πρηγμάτων [Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. author] 1.83; τὸν πόλεμον τὸν ἐνστάντα σοὶ καὶ τῇ πόλει 5th-6th c.BC: Isocrates Orator 5.2]]; in war, press hard, τινί [Refs 2nd c.BC+ [2nd c.BC: Polybius Historicus 3.97.1]]: absolutely, begin, [τοῦ θέρους] ἐνισταμένου [LXX+4th c.BC+ [4th-3rd c.BC: Theophrastus Philosophus “Historia Plantarum” 9.8.2; ἐνισταμένου τοῦ ἐνιαυτοῦ LXX.1Ki.12.24]]; to be at hand, arise, ὁ τότ᾽ ἐνστὰς πόλεμος [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 18.89, compare 139, 2nd c.BC: Polybius Historicus 1.71.4; τοῦ πολέμου πρὸς Φίλιππον ὑμῖν ἐνεστηκότος 4th c.BC: Aeschines Orator 2.58]]: especially in perfect participle, pending, present, μιᾶς ἐνεστώσης δίκης [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Nubes” 779, compare 4th c.BC: Isaeus Orator 11.45, 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 33.14; ὁ νῦν ἐνεστηκὼς ἀγών 4th c.BC: Lycurgus Orator 7; so οὐδενὸς ἡμῖν ἐνεστῶτος πρὸς αὐτούς “PStrassb.” 91.21 (1st c.BC)]]; of Time, instant, present, τοῦ ἐνεστῶτος μηνός Philipp. cited in [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 18.157]]; ἡ ἐνεστῶσα κακία, ἀνάγκη, [NT+4th c.BC+ [“PPetr.” 2p.60, NT.1Cor.7.26; κατὰ τὸν ἐ. καιρόν 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Rhetorica” 1366b23; ἀγαθὸν ἐνεστὼς ἢ μέλλον “Stoicorum Veterum Fragmenta” 3.94; compare ἐνεστάναι τὸν πάντα χρόνον ὡς τὸν ἐνιαυτὸν ἐνεστηκέναι λέγομεν 2nd c.BC: Apollodorus Seleuciensis Stoicus 3.260.]]

__B.III.2
esp. Grammars, ὁ ἐνεστὼς (i.e. χρόνος) the present tense, [Refs 2nd c.BC+ [Stoic. 2.48, 2nd c.BC: Dionysius Thrax Grammaticus 638.22, 2nd c.AD: Apollonius Dyscolus Grammaticus “de Pronominibus;” 58.7, +others; also ἐνεστῶσα συντέλεια]]the state of completion expressed by the perfect tense, [Refs [[prev. author] “Synt.” 205.15: also in]]aorist, τοῦ ποτὲ ἐνστάντος when the moment has arrived, [Refs 3rd c.AD+ [3rd c.AD: Plotinus Philosophus 4.3.13]]; τὰ ἐνεστηκότα πράγματα present circumstances, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Historia Graeca (Hellenica)” 2.1.6; so τὰ ἐνεστῶτα 2nd c.BC: Polybius Historicus 2.26.3.]]

__B.IV

draw out from, release from, ἀχέων τινά [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “P.” 3.51]]; ἐ. τινὰ ἐκ τοῦ ζῆν, i.e. put him to death, [Refs 2nd c.BC+ [2nd c.BC: Polybius Historicus 23.16.13]]; ἑαυτὸν ἐκ τοῦ ζῆν commit suicide, [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [[prev. author] 38.16.5; τοῦ ζῆν 1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus 2.1076b; τοῦ σώματος [prev. author] “Comp. of merchandise, etc., carry out, export, ῥῶπον χθονός [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Fragmenta - American Journal of Philology” 263, compare 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Equites” 278, 282, etc.]]; εἴ τις ἐξαγαγὼν παῖδα ληφθείη exporting him as a slave, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Lysias Orator 10.10, compare 13.67]]:—passive, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Andocides Orator 2.11, 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 6.31, 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “de Vectigalibus” 3.2, etc.; τὰ -όμενα]]exports, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Rhetorica” 1359b22; οὔτε γὰρ ἐξήγετο.. οὐδὲν οὔτ᾽ εἰσήγετο 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 18.145]]:—middle, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Respublica Atheniensium” 2.3.]]

__II.3
of building, draw or carry farther out, αἱμασιάν [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 55.22]]:—passive, ὁ περίβολος πανταχῇ ἐξήχθη τῆς πόλεως [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 1.93.]]

__II.4
of expenses, ἐπὶ πλεῖστον ἐξάγεσθαι [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd-3rd c.AD: Dio Cassius Historicus 43.25.]]

__III
bring forth, produce, οὐκ ἐξάγουσι καρπὸν οἱ ψευδεῖς λόγοι [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Fragmenta” 834; ᾠά]]hatch, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Historia Animalium” 564b8]]; call forth, excite, δάκρυ τινί [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Supplices” 770]]:—middle, γέλωτα ἐξαγαγέσθαι [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 2.2.15; μικρὰ ἆθλα πολλοὺς πόνους ἐξάγεται]]elicit, induce, [Refs [[prev. author] “Hier.” 9.11.]]

lead on, carry away, excite, τινά [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Alcestis” 1080, “Supp.” 79; τινὰ ἐπ᾽ οἶκτον [prev. author] “Ion” 361, compare “HF” 1212 (_anapaest meter_); ἐς τοὺς κινδύνους 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 3.45]]; in bad sense, lead on, tempt, οὐδέ με οἶνος ἐ. ὥστε εἰπεῖν [Refs 6th c.BC+ [6th c.BC: Theognis Elegiacus 414; ἐ. ἐπὶ τὰ πονηρότερα τὸν ὄχλον 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 6.89]]:—middle, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Hercules Furens” 775 (Lyric poetry); εἰς τὸ διδόναι λόγον 1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus 2.922f]]:—passive, to be led on to do a thing, c.infinitive, ἐξήχθην ὀλοφύρασθαι [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Lysias Orator 2.61; ταῦτα.. ἐξήχθημεν εἰπεῖν 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 572b, compare 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 1.8.21; ἃ μὲν ἄν τις ἐξαχθῇ πρᾶξαι 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 21.41, compare 74; εἰς ἅμιλλαν 1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus “Solon” 29]]: absolutely, to be carried away by passion, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-3rd c.BC: Dinarchus Orator 1.15; ὑπὸ τοῦ θυμοῦ 2nd c.AD: Pausanias Periegeta 5.17.8, etc.]]; ἐξάγουσα ὀδύνη distracting pain, [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [3rd c.BC: Herodas Mimographus]] middle cited in [Refs 4th c.AD+ [4th c.AD: Oribasius Medicus 7.8.1.]]

__IV.2
lead away, [λόγον] εἰς ἄλλας ὑποθέσεις [Refs 1st c.AD+ [1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus 2.42e; προβλήματα ἐ. εἰς ὀργανικὰς κατασκευάς]]reduce, [Refs [[prev. author] “Marc.” 14 (also εἰς ἔργον πρόβλημα [prev. passage])]]; ἐ. εἰς τὸ ἀνώτερον, Latin altius repetere, [Refs [[prev. author] 2.639e]]; πρὸς τὴν Ἑλληνικὴν διάλεκτον ἐξάγειν τοὔνομα express in Greek, [Refs [[prev. author] “Num.” 13.]]

intransitive, pass one's life, [Refs 1st c.BC+ [1st c.BC: Diodorus Siculus Historicus 3.43.]]

Pericl. cited in 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Rhetorica” 1365a33.]]

__2

__I

__I.1

__I.2
with implied reference to some later time, ἐ. or ἐπειδή, ={ἐξ οὗ}, from the time when, since, mostly with aorist, πολλὰ πλάγχθη, ἐ. ἔπερσε [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 1.2]]; ἐπείτε παρέλαβον τὸν θρόνον, τοῦτο ἐφρόντιζον ever since I came to the throne, I had this in mind, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 7.8. ; ἐπειδήπερ ὑπέστη 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 8.68; δέκατον μὲν ἔτος τόδ᾽ ἐ... ἦραν 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Agamemnon” 40: sometimes with]]present (used in perfect sense) and perfect, ἐ. δὲ φροῦδός ἐστι στρατός since the army is gone, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Antigone” 15]]; ἐπείτε ὑπὸ τῷ Πέρσῃ εἰσί, πεπόνθασι τοιόνδε ever since they have been, now that they are.., [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 3.117.]]

with Subj., ἄν being always added in Attic dialect Prose, and ἄν or κε generally in Poetry: ἐπεί with ἄν becomes ἐπήν (so in Comedy texts, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Lysistrata” 1175, “Av.” 983), later ἐπάν (which see)]], Ionic dialect ἐπεάν [Refs 8th c.BC+ [“Schwyzer” 800 (6th c.BC), 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 3.153, +others, ἐπήν 5th c.BC: Hippocrates Medicus “περὶ ἀγμῶν” 6, +others, and ἐπειδή with ἄν ἐπειδάν (which see); 8th c.BC: Homerus Epicus has ἐπεί κε, ἐπήν (once ἐπεὶ ἄν 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 6.412):]]

__II.1
referring to future time with future apodosis, τέκνα ἄξομεν.. ἐπὴν πτολίεθρον ἕλωμεν when we shall have taken the city, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 4.238; ἐ. κ᾽ ἀπὸ λαὸς ὄληται 11.764. compare 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 17.23; ἐπεάν περ ἡμίονοι τέκωσι, τότε τὸ τεῖχος ἁλώσεσθαι 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 3.153]]; ταῦτ᾽, ἐπειδὰν περὶ τοῦ γένους εἴπω, τότ᾽ ἐρῶ I will speak of this, when I have spoken.., [Refs 8th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 57.16, compare 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 2.3.29; ἐ. ἂν σύ γε πότμον ἐπίσπῃς 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 6.412]]; χρὴ δέ, ὅταν μὲν τιθῆσθε τοὺς νόμους,.. σκοπεῖν, ἐπειδὰν δὲ θῆσθε, φυλάττειν whenever you are enacting your laws,.. and after you have enacted them.., [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 21.34.]]

__II.2
of repeated action, with a present apodosis, whenever, when once, δαμνᾷ, ἐ. κε λίπῃ ὀστέα θυμός [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 11.221, compare 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 9.409]]; ἐπειδὰν ἡ ἐκφορὰ ᾖ.. ἄγουσι whenever the burial takes place they bring, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 2.34]]; ἐπειδὰν κρύψωσι γῇ.. λέγει when they have covered them with earth, [Refs [[prev. passage]: sometimes without ἄν or]] κε in Poets, ἐ. ἂρ βλέφαρ᾽ ἀμφικαλύψῃ [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 20.86; ἐ. δὴ τόν γε δαμάσσεται.. ὀϊστός 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 11.478, compare 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Coloneus” 1225 (Lyric poetry), “Ant.” 1025.]]

__II.3
like [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus 1.2, δέκα ἡμερῶν ἐπειδὰν δόξῃ]] within ten days from the passing of the resolution, [Refs [“IG” 12.88.7.]]

__III
with Opt. (without ἄν):

__III.1
referring to future time, ἐπειδὴ πρὸς τὸ φῶς ἔλθοι, ὁρᾶν οὐδ᾽ ἂν ἓν δύνασθαι (i.e. οὐκ οἴει); after he had come into the light.., [Refs 8th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 516a: 8th c.BC: Homerus Epicus sometimes uses ἐπήν with _optative_ in same sense as ἐπεί, 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 24.227, 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 2.105 (codices), etc.]]

__III.2
more frequently of repeated action, with a past apodosis, ἐ. ζεύξειεν.., δησάσκετο [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 24.14; ἐπειδὴ δέ τι ἐμφάγοιεν, ἀνίσταντο 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 4.5.9; ἐ. πύθοιτο, ἐπῄνει [prev. author] “Cyr.” 5.3.55, compare 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 8.38, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Phaedo” 59d, “Prt.” 315b.]]

__III.3
in indirect speech after past tenses, representing a subjunctive in direct speech, αὐτὸς δὲ ἐπεὶ διαβαίης, ἀπιέναι ἔφησθα (the direct form being ἐπὴν διαβῶ) [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 7.2.27, compare 3.5.18, “Cyr.” 1.4.21]]; after optative in a final clause, ἐπορεύοντο, ὅπως ἐπειδὴ γένοιντο ἐπὶ τῷ ποταμῷ.. ἴοιεν [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 7.80.]]

__III.4
by assimilation to optative in principal clause, ἦ τ᾽ ἂν.. νῦν μὲν ἀνώγοιμι πτολεμίζειν.. ἐπὴν τεισαίμεθα λώβην [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 19.208; ὃς τὸ καταβρόξειεν ἐπεὶ κρητῆρι μιγείη 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 4.222.]]

__III.5
ἐπειδάν with optative is falsa lectio in some passages of early authors, as [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 1.3.11, 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 30.6 (with _indicative_, 2nd c.BC: Polybius Historicus 13.7.8)]]: found in later Gr., [Refs 1st c.BC+ [6th c.AD: Agathias Historicus et Epigrammaticus 2.5, +others, 1st c.BC: Zosimus Epigrammaticus 5.18.10.]]

__IV
with Inf., only in indirect speech, ἐπειδὴ δὲ κατὰ σχολὴν σκέψασθαι, κόπτεσθαι (i.e. ἔφη) [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 619c, compare “Smp.” 174d, 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 4.10, 7.150.]]

__V
with other words:

__V.1
ἐ. τάχιστα as soon as, frequently separated by a word, ἐ. ἦλθε τάχιστα,.. ἀπέδοτο [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 7.2.6; ἐ. δὲ τάχιστα διέβη [prev. author] “Cyr.” 3.3.22; ἐ. θᾶττον 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Politica” 1284a40; ἐ. εὐθέως 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Historia Graeca (Hellenica)” 3.2.4; ἐ... αὐτίκα 5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “N.” 1.35; ἐπειδὴ τάχιστα 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Protagoras” 310c, 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 27.16; ἐπειδὰν τάχιστα 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 8.144, 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 3.1.9; rarely ἐπειδὴ θᾶττον 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 37.41; ἐπειδὰν θᾶττον 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Protagoras” 325c.]]

__V.1.b
ἐ. τὰ πρῶτα [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 12.420; ἐ. τὸ πρῶτον 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Agamemnon” 1287.]]

__V.2
with emphatic Particles, ἐπεὶ ἄρα when then, in continuing a narrative, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 6.426]]; ἐπεὶ οὖν when then, in resuming a narrative, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [1.57, 3.4; ἐπεὶ ὦν 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 3.9; ἐπεὶ γὰρ δή [prev. author] 9.90, etc.]]

__B
CAUSAL (ἐπεί more frequently in this sense in early Prose: ἐπειδή whereas is used in preambles of decrees, [Refs [“IG” 22.103, etc.; ἐπειδήπερ]]inasmuch as,  NT.Luke.1.1), since, seeing that, frequently from [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Homerus Epicus downwards:]]

__B.1
with Ind. (after both present and past tenses), ἐ. οὐδὲ ἔοικε [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 1.119, compare 153, 278, 5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “O.” 4.16, 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Memorabilia” 2.3.4; ἐπειδή 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 8.80; ἐπειδὴ οὐκ ἐθέλεις 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Protagoras” 335c; νίκη δ᾽ ἐπείπερ ἕσπετ᾽, ἐμπέδως μένοι 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Agamemnon” 854]]; frequently with past tenses with ἄν, ἐπεὶ οὔποτ᾽ ἂν στόλον ἐπλεύσατ᾽ ἄν [Refs 8th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Philoctetes” 1037; ἐπεὶ οὔ κεν ἀνιδρωτί γ᾽ ἐτελέσθη 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 15.228, compare 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 18.49]]; οὐ γὰρ ἂν σθένοντά γε εἷλέν μ᾽· ἐπεὶ οὐδ᾽ ἂν ὧδ᾽ ἔχοντ᾽ (i.e. εἷλεν) [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Philoctetes” 948]]: especially in the sense, for otherwise.., [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “O.” 9.29, 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Tyrannus” 433, 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Memorabilia” 2.7.14, 3rd c.BC: Herodas Mimographus 2.72, etc.: so with]]future, ἐξέστω δὲ μηδενὶ.. τεθῆναι.., ἐ. ἀποδώσει.. otherwise he shall pay.., [Refs [“Rev.Et.Anc.” 4.261 (near Smyrna): with _imperative_, ἐ. δίδαξον]] for teach me, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Electra” 352, “OC” 969, compare “OT” 390, 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Vespae” 73, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Gorgias” 473e]]: with an interrogative, ἐ. πῶς ἂν καλέσεια; for how would you call him? [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Nubes” 688, compare 5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “P.” 7.5, 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Choephori” 214, 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Trachiniae” 139 (Lyric poetry); ὦ Ἀλκιβιάδη, ἐπειδὴ περὶ τίνος Ἀθηναῖοι διανοοῦνται βουλεύεσθαι, ἀνίστασαι συμβουλεύσω; 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus Alcaeus1.106c.]]

__B.2
with Opt., ἐ. ἂν μάλα τοι σχεδὸν ἔλθοι [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 9.304, compare 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Ajax” 916]]; so after past tenses on the principle of indirect speech, ἐπείπερ ἡγήσαιντο since (as they said) they believed, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Memorabilia” 1.4.19.]]

__B.3
with Inf. in indirect speech, ἐ. γιγνώσκειν γε αὐτά [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Protagoras” 353a, compare 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 8.111, 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 2.93.]]

__B.4
in elliptical expressions, ἀδύνατός [εἰμι], ἐ. ἐβουλόμην ἂν οἷός τ᾽ εἶναι I am unable (and yet I am sorry), for I should like to have the power, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Protagoras” 335c]]; so εἶμι· ἐ. καὶ ταῦτ᾽ ἂν ἴσως οὐκ ἀηδῶς σου ἤκουον [Refs [[prev. passage] (here the sense may be given by]]and yet, although, compare [Refs 4th c.BC+ [[prev. work] 333c, 317a, “Ap.” 19e, “Smp.” 187a, 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Ethica Nicomachea” 1121a19)]]; ἐ. ὅ γε ἀποθανὼν πελάτης τις ἦν ἐμός and yet (moreover) the murdered man was my own hired man, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Euthyphro” 4c.]]

__B.4.b
sometimes after a vocative, where 'listen' may be supplied, Ἕκτορ, ἐ. με κατ᾽ αἶσαν ἐνείκεσας [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 3.59, compare 13.68, 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 3.103, 211.]]

__B.5
with other Particles, ἐ. ἄρα, ἐ. ἂρ δή since then, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 17.185]]; ἐ. γε (ἐπεί.. γε [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 1.352, 8th-7th c.BC: Hesiodus Epicus “Theogonia” 171), more emphatic than ἐ.,]] since indeed, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Cyclops” 181, “Hipp.” 955]]; ἐπειδή γε[Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. work] 946, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Phaedo” 77d, 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 54.29; sometimes separated, ἐπειδή.. γε 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Electra” 631, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Phaedo” 87c; ἐ. γε δή 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 3.9, 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Antigone” 923, ἐπειδή γε καί 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 6.18]]; ἐ. ἦ since in truth, ἐ. ἦ πολὺ φέρτερόν ἐστι [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 1.169, compare 156, 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 9.276]]; ἐπείπερ (ἐ... περ [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 13.447, 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 20.181) in Trag. and Prose, 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Agamemnon” 822, 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Coloneus” 75, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Phaedo” 114d]]; ἐπειδήπερ in Comedy texts and Prose, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Acharnenses” 437, 495, “Nu.” 1412, 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 6.18, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 350e]]; ἐ. τοι since surely, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Coloneus” 433; ἐ. νύ τοι 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 1.416; ἐ. τοι καί 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Medea” 677, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 567e. [ἐ.]] sometimes begins a verse in [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Homerus Epicus, 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 22.379, 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 4.13, 8.452, 21.25]]; sometimes coalesces by synizesis with οὐ, οὐδέ, etc., [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Philoctetes” 446, 948, etc.]]]

ἐπει-δή
conj.;
__1. of time, when now, after that: Luk.7:1 (WH, txt.).
__2. Of cause, seeing that, forasmuch as: Luk.11:6, Act.13:46 (WH, txt., RV) Act.14:12 15:24, 1Co.1:21-22 14:16 15:21, Php.2:26.†
