ἐπεί,
conjunction, both temporal and causal; also ἐπειδή, ἐπείτε. OF TIME (ἐπειδή is more frequently in this sense in Prose), after that, since, when, from [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Homerus Epicus downwards:]]

__I
with Ind.,

__I.1
of a definite occurrence in past time, mostly with aorist, ἐπεί π᾽ εὔξαντο after they had prayed, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 1.458; ἐπειδὴ ἐτελεύτησε Δαρεῖος καὶ κατέστη Ἀρταξέρξης]]after [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator had died and 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus had succeeded, 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 1.1.3]]: rarely with imperfect, ἐπειδὴ εἱστιώμεθ᾽ [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Nubes” 1354; ἐ. πόντον εἰσεβάλλομεν 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Iphigenia Taurica” 260; ἐ. ἠσθένει Δαρεῖος 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 1.1.1: with]]pluperfect, ἐπειδὴ ἐξηπάτησθε.. after you had been deceived.., [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 18.42]]; but generally the aorist is found, the pluperfect being used only for special emphasis: with imperfect to express an action not yet complete, ἐπεὶ ὑπηντίαζεν ἡ φάλαγξ καὶ ἡ σάλπιγξ ἐφθέγξατο after the phalanx began to advance and the trumpet had sounded, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 6.5.27.]]

__I.2
with implied reference to some later time, ἐ. or ἐπειδή, ={ἐξ οὗ}, from the time when, since, mostly with aorist, πολλὰ πλάγχθη, ἐ. ἔπερσε [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 1.2]]; ἐπείτε παρέλαβον τὸν θρόνον, τοῦτο ἐφρόντιζον ever since I came to the throne, I had this in mind, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 7.8. ; ἐπειδήπερ ὑπέστη 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 8.68; δέκατον μὲν ἔτος τόδ᾽ ἐ... ἦραν 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Agamemnon” 40: sometimes with]]present (used in perfect sense) and perfect, ἐ. δὲ φροῦδός ἐστι στρατός since the army is gone, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Antigone” 15]]; ἐπείτε ὑπὸ τῷ Πέρσῃ εἰσί, πεπόνθασι τοιόνδε ever since they have been, now that they are.., [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 3.117.]]

__II
with Subj., ἄν being always added in Attic dialect Prose, and ἄν or κε generally in Poetry: ἐπεί with ἄν becomes ἐπήν (so in Comedy texts, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Lysistrata” 1175, “Av.” 983), later ἐπάν (which see)]], Ionic dialect ἐπεάν [Refs 8th c.BC+ [“Schwyzer” 800 (6th c.BC), 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 3.153, +others, ἐπήν 5th c.BC: Hippocrates Medicus “περὶ ἀγμῶν” 6, +others, and ἐπειδή with ἄν ἐπειδάν (which see); 8th c.BC: Homerus Epicus has ἐπεί κε, ἐπήν (once ἐπεὶ ἄν 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 6.412):]]

__II.1
referring to future time with future apodosis, τέκνα ἄξομεν.. ἐπὴν πτολίεθρον ἕλωμεν when we shall have taken the city, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 4.238; ἐ. κ᾽ ἀπὸ λαὸς ὄληται 11.764. compare 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 17.23; ἐπεάν περ ἡμίονοι τέκωσι, τότε τὸ τεῖχος ἁλώσεσθαι 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 3.153]]; ταῦτ᾽, ἐπειδὰν περὶ τοῦ γένους εἴπω, τότ᾽ ἐρῶ I will speak of this, when I have spoken.., [Refs 8th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 57.16, compare 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 2.3.29; ἐ. ἂν σύ γε πότμον ἐπίσπῃς 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 6.412]]; χρὴ δέ, ὅταν μὲν τιθῆσθε τοὺς νόμους,.. σκοπεῖν, ἐπειδὰν δὲ θῆσθε, φυλάττειν whenever you are enacting your laws,.. and after you have enacted them.., [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 21.34.]]

__II.2
of repeated action, with a present apodosis, whenever, when once, δαμνᾷ, ἐ. κε λίπῃ ὀστέα θυμός [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 11.221, compare 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 9.409]]; ἐπειδὰν ἡ ἐκφορὰ ᾖ.. ἄγουσι whenever the burial takes place they bring, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 2.34]]; ἐπειδὰν κρύψωσι γῇ.. λέγει when they have covered them with earth, [Refs [[prev. passage]: sometimes without ἄν or]]κε in Poets, ἐ. ἂρ βλέφαρ᾽ ἀμφικαλύψῃ [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 20.86; ἐ. δὴ τόν γε δαμάσσεται.. ὀϊστός 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 11.478, compare 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Coloneus” 1225 (Lyric poetry), “Ant.” 1025.]]

__II.3
like [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus 1.2, δέκα ἡμερῶν ἐπειδὰν δόξῃ]] within ten days from the passing of the resolution, [Refs [“IG” 12.88.7.]]

__III
with Opt. (without ἄν):

__III.1
referring to future time, ἐπειδὴ πρὸς τὸ φῶς ἔλθοι, ὁρᾶν οὐδ᾽ ἂν ἓν δύνασθαι (i.e. οὐκ οἴει); after he had come into the light.., [Refs 8th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 516a: 8th c.BC: Homerus Epicus sometimes uses ἐπήν with _optative_ in same sense as ἐπεί, 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 24.227, 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 2.105 (codices), etc.]]

__III.2
more frequently of repeated action, with a past apodosis, ἐ. ζεύξειεν.., δησάσκετο [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 24.14; ἐπειδὴ δέ τι ἐμφάγοιεν, ἀνίσταντο 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 4.5.9; ἐ. πύθοιτο, ἐπῄνει [prev. author] “Cyr.” 5.3.55, compare 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 8.38, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Phaedo” 59d, “Prt.” 315b.]]

__III.3
in indirect speech after past tenses, representing a subjunctive in direct speech, αὐτὸς δὲ ἐπεὶ διαβαίης, ἀπιέναι ἔφησθα (the direct form being ἐπὴν διαβῶ) [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 7.2.27, compare 3.5.18, “Cyr.” 1.4.21]]; after optative in a final clause, ἐπορεύοντο, ὅπως ἐπειδὴ γένοιντο ἐπὶ τῷ ποταμῷ.. ἴοιεν [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 7.80.]]

__III.4
by assimilation to optative in principal clause, ἦ τ᾽ ἂν.. νῦν μὲν ἀνώγοιμι πτολεμίζειν.. ἐπὴν τεισαίμεθα λώβην [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 19.208; ὃς τὸ καταβρόξειεν ἐπεὶ κρητῆρι μιγείη 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 4.222.]]

__III.5
ἐπειδάν with optative is falsa lectio in some passages of early authors, as [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 1.3.11, 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 30.6 (with _indicative_, 2nd c.BC: Polybius Historicus 13.7.8)]]: found in later Gr., [Refs 1st c.BC+ [6th c.AD: Agathias Historicus et Epigrammaticus 2.5, +others, 1st c.BC: Zosimus Epigrammaticus 5.18.10.]]

__IV
with Inf., only in indirect speech, ἐπειδὴ δὲ κατὰ σχολὴν σκέψασθαι, κόπτεσθαι (i.e. ἔφη) [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 619c, compare “Smp.” 174d, 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 4.10, 7.150.]]

__V
with other words:

__V.1
ἐ. τάχιστα as soon as, frequently separated by a word, ἐ. ἦλθε τάχιστα,.. ἀπέδοτο [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 7.2.6; ἐ. δὲ τάχιστα διέβη [prev. author] “Cyr.” 3.3.22; ἐ. θᾶττον 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Politica” 1284a40; ἐ. εὐθέως 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Historia Graeca (Hellenica)” 3.2.4; ἐ... αὐτίκα 5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “N.” 1.35; ἐπειδὴ τάχιστα 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Protagoras” 310c, 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 27.16; ἐπειδὰν τάχιστα 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 8.144, 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 3.1.9; rarely ἐπειδὴ θᾶττον 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 37.41; ἐπειδὰν θᾶττον 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Protagoras” 325c.]]

__V.1.b
ἐ. τὰ πρῶτα [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 12.420; ἐ. τὸ πρῶτον 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Agamemnon” 1287.]]

__V.2
with emphatic Particles, ἐπεὶ ἄρα when then, in continuing a narrative, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 6.426]]; ἐπεὶ οὖν when then, in resuming a narrative, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [1.57, 3.4; ἐπεὶ ὦν 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 3.9; ἐπεὶ γὰρ δή [prev. author] 9.90, etc.]]

__B
CAUSAL (ἐπεί more frequently in this sense in early Prose: ἐπειδή whereas is used in preambles of decrees, [Refs [“IG” 22.103, etc.; ἐπειδήπερ]]inasmuch as,  NT.Luke.1.1), since, seeing that, frequently from [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Homerus Epicus downwards:]]

__B.1
with Ind. (after both present and past tenses), ἐ. οὐδὲ ἔοικε [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 1.119, compare 153, 278, 5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “O.” 4.16, 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Memorabilia” 2.3.4; ἐπειδή 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 8.80; ἐπειδὴ οὐκ ἐθέλεις 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Protagoras” 335c; νίκη δ᾽ ἐπείπερ ἕσπετ᾽, ἐμπέδως μένοι 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Agamemnon” 854]]; frequently with past tenses with ἄν, ἐπεὶ οὔποτ᾽ ἂν στόλον ἐπλεύσατ᾽ ἄν [Refs 8th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Philoctetes” 1037; ἐπεὶ οὔ κεν ἀνιδρωτί γ᾽ ἐτελέσθη 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 15.228, compare 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 18.49]]; οὐ γὰρ ἂν σθένοντά γε εἷλέν μ᾽· ἐπεὶ οὐδ᾽ ἂν ὧδ᾽ ἔχοντ᾽ (i.e. εἷλεν) [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Philoctetes” 948]]: especially in the sense, for otherwise.., [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “O.” 9.29, 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Tyrannus” 433, 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Memorabilia” 2.7.14, 3rd c.BC: Herodas Mimographus 2.72, etc.: so with]]future, ἐξέστω δὲ μηδενὶ.. τεθῆναι.., ἐ. ἀποδώσει.. otherwise he shall pay.., [Refs [“Rev.Et.Anc.” 4.261 (near Smyrna): with _imperative_, ἐ. δίδαξον]] for teach me, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Electra” 352, “OC” 969, compare “OT” 390, 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Vespae” 73, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Gorgias” 473e]]: with an interrogative, ἐ. πῶς ἂν καλέσεια; for how would you call him? [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Nubes” 688, compare 5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “P.” 7.5, 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Choephori” 214, 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Trachiniae” 139 (Lyric poetry); ὦ Ἀλκιβιάδη, ἐπειδὴ περὶ τίνος Ἀθηναῖοι διανοοῦνται βουλεύεσθαι, ἀνίστασαι συμβουλεύσω; 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus Alcaeus1.106c.]]

__B.2
with Opt., ἐ. ἂν μάλα τοι σχεδὸν ἔλθοι [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 9.304, compare 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Ajax” 916]]; so after past tenses on the principle of indirect speech, ἐπείπερ ἡγήσαιντο since (as they said) they believed, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Memorabilia” 1.4.19.]]

__B.3
with Inf. in indirect speech, ἐ. γιγνώσκειν γε αὐτά [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Protagoras” 353a, compare 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 8.111, 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 2.93.]]

__B.4
in elliptical expressions, ἀδύνατός [εἰμι], ἐ. ἐβουλόμην ἂν οἷός τ᾽ εἶναι I am unable (and yet I am sorry), for I should like to have the power, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Protagoras” 335c]]; so εἶμι· ἐ. καὶ ταῦτ᾽ ἂν ἴσως οὐκ ἀηδῶς σου ἤκουον [Refs [[prev. passage] (here the sense may be given by]]and yet, although, compare [Refs 4th c.BC+ [[prev. work] 333c, 317a, “Ap.” 19e, “Smp.” 187a, 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Ethica Nicomachea” 1121a19)]]; ἐ. ὅ γε ἀποθανὼν πελάτης τις ἦν ἐμός and yet (moreover) the murdered man was my own hired man, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Euthyphro” 4c.]]

__B.4.b
sometimes after a vocative, where 'listen' may be supplied, Ἕκτορ, ἐ. με κατ᾽ αἶσαν ἐνείκεσας [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 3.59, compare 13.68, 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 3.103, 211.]]

__B.5
with other Particles, ἐ. ἄρα, ἐ. ἂρ δή since then, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 17.185]]; ἐ. γε (ἐπεί.. γε [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 1.352, 8th-7th c.BC: Hesiodus Epicus “Theogonia” 171), more emphatic than ἐ.,]] since indeed, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Cyclops” 181, “Hipp.” 955]]; ἐπειδή γε[Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. work] 946, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Phaedo” 77d, 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 54.29; sometimes separated, ἐπειδή.. γε 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Electra” 631, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Phaedo” 87c; ἐ. γε δή 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 3.9, 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Antigone” 923, ἐπειδή γε καί 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 6.18]]; ἐ. ἦ since in truth, ἐ. ἦ πολὺ φέρτερόν ἐστι [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 1.169, compare 156, 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 9.276]]; ἐπείπερ (ἐ... περ [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 13.447, 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 20.181) in Trag. and Prose, 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Agamemnon” 822, 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Coloneus” 75, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Phaedo” 114d]]; ἐπειδήπερ in Comedy texts and Prose, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Acharnenses” 437, 495, “Nu.” 1412, 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 6.18, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 350e]]; ἐ. τοι since surely, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Coloneus” 433; ἐ. νύ τοι 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 1.416; ἐ. τοι καί 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Medea” 677, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 567e. [ἐ.]] sometimes begins a verse in [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Homerus Epicus, 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 22.379, 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 4.13, 8.452, 21.25]]; sometimes coalesces by synizesis with οὐ, οὐδέ, etc., [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Philoctetes” 446, 948, etc.]]]

Abbott-Smith / STEPBible (TBESG)
ἐπει-δή-περ
conj.,
forasmuch as ("a stately compound," frequently in cl. and suitable for the formal introduction of Lk): Luk.1:1.†
(AS)

LSJ / STEPBible (TFLSJ)
Included with:  ἐπεί,
conjunction, both temporal and causal; also ἐπειδή, ἐπείτε. OF TIME (ἐπειδή is more frequently in this sense in Prose), after that, since, when, from [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Homerus Epicus downwards:]]

__I
with Ind.,

__I.1
of a definite occurrence in past time, mostly with aorist, ἐπεί π᾽ εὔξαντο after they had prayed, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 1.458; ἐπειδὴ ἐτελεύτησε Δαρεῖος καὶ κατέστη Ἀρταξέρξης]]after [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator had died and 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus had succeeded, 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 1.1.3]]: rarely with imperfect, ἐπειδὴ εἱστιώμεθ᾽ [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Nubes” 1354; ἐ. πόντον εἰσεβάλλομεν 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Iphigenia Taurica” 260; ἐ. ἠσθένει Δαρεῖος 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 1.1.1: with]]pluperfect, ἐπειδὴ ἐξηπάτησθε.. after you had been deceived.., [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 18.42]]; but generally the aorist is found, the pluperfect being used only for special emphasis: with imperfect to express an action not yet complete, ἐπεὶ ὑπηντίαζεν ἡ φάλαγξ καὶ ἡ σάλπιγξ ἐφθέγξατο after the phalanx began to advance and the trumpet had sounded, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 6.5.27.]]

__I.2
with implied reference to some later time, ἐ. or ἐπειδή, ={ἐξ οὗ}, from the time when, since, mostly with aorist, πολλὰ πλάγχθη, ἐ. ἔπερσε [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 1.2]]; ἐπείτε παρέλαβον τὸν θρόνον, τοῦτο ἐφρόντιζον ever since I came to the throne, I had this in mind, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 7.8. ; ἐπειδήπερ ὑπέστη 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 8.68; δέκατον μὲν ἔτος τόδ᾽ ἐ... ἦραν 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Agamemnon” 40: sometimes with]]present (used in perfect sense) and perfect, ἐ. δὲ φροῦδός ἐστι στρατός since the army is gone, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Antigone” 15]]; ἐπείτε ὑπὸ τῷ Πέρσῃ εἰσί, πεπόνθασι τοιόνδε ever since they have been, now that they are.., [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 3.117.]]

__II
with Subj., ἄν being always added in Attic dialect Prose, and ἄν or κε generally in Poetry: ἐπεί with ἄν becomes ἐπήν (so in Comedy texts, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Lysistrata” 1175, “Av.” 983), later ἐπάν (which see)]], Ionic dialect ἐπεάν [Refs 8th c.BC+ [“Schwyzer” 800 (6th c.BC), 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 3.153, +others, ἐπήν 5th c.BC: Hippocrates Medicus “περὶ ἀγμῶν” 6, +others, and ἐπειδή with ἄν ἐπειδάν (which see); 8th c.BC: Homerus Epicus has ἐπεί κε, ἐπήν (once ἐπεὶ ἄν 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 6.412):]]

__II.1
referring to future time with future apodosis, τέκνα ἄξομεν.. ἐπὴν πτολίεθρον ἕλωμεν when we shall have taken the city, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 4.238; ἐ. κ᾽ ἀπὸ λαὸς ὄληται 11.764. compare 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 17.23; ἐπεάν περ ἡμίονοι τέκωσι, τότε τὸ τεῖχος ἁλώσεσθαι 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 3.153]]; ταῦτ᾽, ἐπειδὰν περὶ τοῦ γένους εἴπω, τότ᾽ ἐρῶ I will speak of this, when I have spoken.., [Refs 8th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 57.16, compare 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 2.3.29; ἐ. ἂν σύ γε πότμον ἐπίσπῃς 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 6.412]]; χρὴ δέ, ὅταν μὲν τιθῆσθε τοὺς νόμους,.. σκοπεῖν, ἐπειδὰν δὲ θῆσθε, φυλάττειν whenever you are enacting your laws,.. and after you have enacted them.., [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 21.34.]]

__II.2
of repeated action, with a present apodosis, whenever, when once, δαμνᾷ, ἐ. κε λίπῃ ὀστέα θυμός [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 11.221, compare 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 9.409]]; ἐπειδὰν ἡ ἐκφορὰ ᾖ.. ἄγουσι whenever the burial takes place they bring, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 2.34]]; ἐπειδὰν κρύψωσι γῇ.. λέγει when they have covered them with earth, [Refs [[prev. passage]: sometimes without ἄν or]] κε in Poets, ἐ. ἂρ βλέφαρ᾽ ἀμφικαλύψῃ [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 20.86; ἐ. δὴ τόν γε δαμάσσεται.. ὀϊστός 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 11.478, compare 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Coloneus” 1225 (Lyric poetry), “Ant.” 1025.]]

__II.3
like [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus 1.2, δέκα ἡμερῶν ἐπειδὰν δόξῃ]] within ten days from the passing of the resolution, [Refs [“IG” 12.88.7.]]

__III
with Opt. (without ἄν):

__III.1
referring to future time, ἐπειδὴ πρὸς τὸ φῶς ἔλθοι, ὁρᾶν οὐδ᾽ ἂν ἓν δύνασθαι (i.e. οὐκ οἴει); after he had come into the light.., [Refs 8th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 516a: 8th c.BC: Homerus Epicus sometimes uses ἐπήν with _optative_ in same sense as ἐπεί, 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 24.227, 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 2.105 (codices), etc.]]

__III.2
more frequently of repeated action, with a past apodosis, ἐ. ζεύξειεν.., δησάσκετο [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 24.14; ἐπειδὴ δέ τι ἐμφάγοιεν, ἀνίσταντο 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 4.5.9; ἐ. πύθοιτο, ἐπῄνει [prev. author] “Cyr.” 5.3.55, compare 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 8.38, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Phaedo” 59d, “Prt.” 315b.]]

__III.3
in indirect speech after past tenses, representing a subjunctive in direct speech, αὐτὸς δὲ ἐπεὶ διαβαίης, ἀπιέναι ἔφησθα (the direct form being ἐπὴν διαβῶ) [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 7.2.27, compare 3.5.18, “Cyr.” 1.4.21]]; after optative in a final clause, ἐπορεύοντο, ὅπως ἐπειδὴ γένοιντο ἐπὶ τῷ ποταμῷ.. ἴοιεν [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 7.80.]]

__III.4
by assimilation to optative in principal clause, ἦ τ᾽ ἂν.. νῦν μὲν ἀνώγοιμι πτολεμίζειν.. ἐπὴν τεισαίμεθα λώβην [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 19.208; ὃς τὸ καταβρόξειεν ἐπεὶ κρητῆρι μιγείη 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 4.222.]]

__III.5
ἐπειδάν with optative is falsa lectio in some passages of early authors, as [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 1.3.11, 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 30.6 (with _indicative_, 2nd c.BC: Polybius Historicus 13.7.8)]]: found in later Gr., [Refs 1st c.BC+ [6th c.AD: Agathias Historicus et Epigrammaticus 2.5, +others, 1st c.BC: Zosimus Epigrammaticus 5.18.10.]]

__IV
with Inf., only in indirect speech, ἐπειδὴ δὲ κατὰ σχολὴν σκέψασθαι, κόπτεσθαι (i.e. ἔφη) [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 619c, compare “Smp.” 174d, 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 4.10, 7.150.]]

__V
with other words:

__V.1
ἐ. τάχιστα as soon as, frequently separated by a word, ἐ. ἦλθε τάχιστα,.. ἀπέδοτο [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 7.2.6; ἐ. δὲ τάχιστα διέβη [prev. author] “Cyr.” 3.3.22; ἐ. θᾶττον 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Politica” 1284a40; ἐ. εὐθέως 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Historia Graeca (Hellenica)” 3.2.4; ἐ... αὐτίκα 5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “N.” 1.35; ἐπειδὴ τάχιστα 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Protagoras” 310c, 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 27.16; ἐπειδὰν τάχιστα 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 8.144, 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 3.1.9; rarely ἐπειδὴ θᾶττον 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 37.41; ἐπειδὰν θᾶττον 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Protagoras” 325c.]]

__V.1.b
ἐ. τὰ πρῶτα [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 12.420; ἐ. τὸ πρῶτον 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Agamemnon” 1287.]]

__V.2
with emphatic Particles, ἐπεὶ ἄρα when then, in continuing a narrative, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 6.426]]; ἐπεὶ οὖν when then, in resuming a narrative, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [1.57, 3.4; ἐπεὶ ὦν 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 3.9; ἐπεὶ γὰρ δή [prev. author] 9.90, etc.]]

__B
CAUSAL (ἐπεί more frequently in this sense in early Prose: ἐπειδή whereas is used in preambles of decrees, [Refs [“IG” 22.103, etc.; ἐπειδήπερ]]inasmuch as,  NT.Luke.1.1), since, seeing that, frequently from [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Homerus Epicus downwards:]]

__B.1
with Ind. (after both present and past tenses), ἐ. οὐδὲ ἔοικε [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 1.119, compare 153, 278, 5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “O.” 4.16, 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Memorabilia” 2.3.4; ἐπειδή 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 8.80; ἐπειδὴ οὐκ ἐθέλεις 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Protagoras” 335c; νίκη δ᾽ ἐπείπερ ἕσπετ᾽, ἐμπέδως μένοι 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Agamemnon” 854]]; frequently with past tenses with ἄν, ἐπεὶ οὔποτ᾽ ἂν στόλον ἐπλεύσατ᾽ ἄν [Refs 8th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Philoctetes” 1037; ἐπεὶ οὔ κεν ἀνιδρωτί γ᾽ ἐτελέσθη 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 15.228, compare 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 18.49]]; οὐ γὰρ ἂν σθένοντά γε εἷλέν μ᾽· ἐπεὶ οὐδ᾽ ἂν ὧδ᾽ ἔχοντ᾽ (i.e. εἷλεν) [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Philoctetes” 948]]: especially in the sense, for otherwise.., [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “O.” 9.29, 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Tyrannus” 433, 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Memorabilia” 2.7.14, 3rd c.BC: Herodas Mimographus 2.72, etc.: so with]]future, ἐξέστω δὲ μηδενὶ.. τεθῆναι.., ἐ. ἀποδώσει.. otherwise he shall pay.., [Refs [“Rev.Et.Anc.” 4.261 (near Smyrna): with _imperative_, ἐ. δίδαξον]] for teach me, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Electra” 352, “OC” 969, compare “OT” 390, 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Vespae” 73, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Gorgias” 473e]]: with an interrogative, ἐ. πῶς ἂν καλέσεια; for how would you call him? [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Nubes” 688, compare 5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “P.” 7.5, 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Choephori” 214, 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Trachiniae” 139 (Lyric poetry); ὦ Ἀλκιβιάδη, ἐπειδὴ περὶ τίνος Ἀθηναῖοι διανοοῦνται βουλεύεσθαι, ἀνίστασαι συμβουλεύσω; 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus Alcaeus1.106c.]]

with Opt., ἐ. ἂν μάλα τοι σχεδὸν ἔλθοι [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 9.304, compare 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Ajax” 916]]; so after past tenses on the principle of indirect speech, ἐπείπερ ἡγήσαιντο since (as they said) they believed, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Memorabilia” 1.4.19.]]

in elliptical expressions, ἀδύνατός [εἰμι], ἐ. ἐβουλόμην ἂν οἷός τ᾽ εἶναι I am unable (and yet I am sorry), for I should like to have the power, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Protagoras” 335c]]; so εἶμι· ἐ. καὶ ταῦτ᾽ ἂν ἴσως οὐκ ἀηδῶς σου ἤκουον [Refs [[prev. passage] (here the sense may be given by]]and yet, although, compare [Refs 4th c.BC+ [[prev. work] 333c, 317a, “Ap.” 19e, “Smp.” 187a, 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Ethica Nicomachea” 1121a19)]]; ἐ. ὅ γε ἀποθανὼν πελάτης τις ἦν ἐμός and yet (moreover) the murdered man was my own hired man, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Euthyphro” 4c.]]

sometimes after a vocative, where 'listen' may be supplied, Ἕκτορ, ἐ. με κατ᾽ αἶσαν ἐνείκεσας [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 3.59, compare 13.68, 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 3.103, 211.]]

[in LXX: Num.19:10 A, Isa.16:2, 4Ma.6:3 * ;]

LSJ / STEPBible (TFLSJ)
ἔπειτα,
Ionic dialect and Doric dialect ἔπειτε(ν) (which see), adverb, (ἐπί, εἶτα):

__I
of mere Sequence, without any notion of cause, thereupon, thereafter, then, frequently from [Refs [Hom. downwards, as Il. 1.48, 2.169, etc.]]: when in strong opposition to the former act or state, with past tenses, thereafter, afterwards; with future, hereafter, ἢ πέφατ᾽ ἢ καὶ ἔ. πεφήσεται [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 15.140; opposed to αὐτίκα νῦν, 23.551]]; ὃς δ᾽ ἔπειτ᾽ ἔφυ, opposed to ὅστις πάροιθεν ἦν, [Refs [A. “Ag.” 171 (Lyric poetry)]]: in Hom.frequently with other Advs., αὐτίκ᾽ ἔ. [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 5.214; αἶψα, ὦκα ἔ., 24.783, 18.527]]; even ἔνθα.. ἔ. 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 10.297; δὴ ἔ. 8.378: usually with reference to a former act, just then, at the time, [Refs [1.106]]; frequently in narrative, πρῶτα μὲν.., αὐτὰρ ἔ. [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 16.497; πρῶτον μέν.., followed by ἔ. δέ.., Th. 2.55, Pl. “Ap.” 18a, etc.]]; by ἔ. alone, [Refs [Th. 1.33, etc.]]; by ἔ. δέ.. ἔ. δέ.. ἔ..., [Refs [X. “Cyr.” 1.3.14; ἐπεὶ δέ.. ἔ... ἔ... ἔ. δέ, [prev. work] 8.3.24, +others]]; πρὶν μέν.., ἔ. δέ.. 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Electra” 724; ἔ. γε 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Theaetetus” 147c, etc., falsa lectio in[Refs [Ar. “Th.” 556]]; κἄπειτα, frequently in Trag., [Refs [S. “Aj.” 61, 305, etc.]]

__I.2
with Article, τὸ ἔ. what follows, τό τ᾽ ἔ. καὶ τὸ μέλλον καὶ τὸ πρίν [Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. author] “Ant.” 611 (Lyric poetry); τά τε πρῶτα, τά τ᾽ ἔ., ὅσα τ᾽ ἔμελλε τυχεῖν 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Iphigenia Taurica” 1265 (Lyric poetry); οἱ ἔ. _future generations,?? 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Eumenides” 672; ὁ ἔ. βίος 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Phaedo” 116a; εἰς τὸν ἔ. χρόνον [prev. author] “Phlb.” 39e, X. “Cyr.” 1.5.9, “OGI” 90.43 (Rosetta, 2nd c.BC)]]; ἡ ἐς τὸ ἔ. δόξα [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 2.64; ἐν τῷ ἔ. 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Phaedo” 67d; ἐκ τοῦ ποτὲ εἰς τὸ ἔ. [prev. author] “Prm.” 152b.]]

__I.3
like{εἶτα}, with a finite Verb after a participle, μειδήσασα δ᾽ ἔ. ἑῷ ἐγκάτθετο κόλπῳ she smiled and then placed it in her bosom, [Refs [Il. 14.223, compare 11.730, etc.]]: frequently in Trag. and Attic dialect, [Refs [A. “Th.” 267, “Eu.” 29, Pl. “Phd.” 82c]]: so frequently when participle and Verb are opposed, marking surprise or the like, and then, and yet, nevertheless, τὸ μητρὸς αἷμα.. ἐκχέας πέδοι ἔ. δώματ᾽ οἰκήσει πατρό; [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Eumenides” 654, compare 438; χὤταν ἐν κακοῖσί τις ἁλοὺς ἔ. τοῦτο καλλύνειν θέλῃ 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Antigone” 496; ὅστις ἀνθρώπου φύσιν βλαστὼν ἔ. μὴ κατ᾽ ἄνθρωπον φρονῇ [prev. author] “Aj.” 761; εἰ πτωχὸς ὢν ἔπειτ᾽ ἐν Ἀθηναίοις λέγειν μέλλω 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Acharnenses” 498, compare “Av.” 29, Pl. “Grg.” 519e, “Prt.” 319d: adversatively, answering μέν, πολλάκις μὲν ὥρμα.., ἔ... διεκωλύετο [prev. author] “R.” 336b; ἔτι μὲν ἐνεχείρησα.., ἔ... [prev. author] “Prt.” 310c, etc.]]; also κἄπειτα after a participle, [Refs [Ar. “Nu.” 624, “Av.” 536; compare εἶτα 1.2.]]

__I.4
in apodosi (never at the beginning of the clause; in [Refs [Hom. frequently strengthened by other Particles):]]

__I.4.a
after a Temporal conjunction, then, thereafter, ἐπεὶ δὴ σφαίρῃ πειρήσαντο, ὀρχείσθην δὴ ἔ. when they had done playing at ball, then they danced, [Refs [Od. 8.378]]; after ἐπεί, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [Il. 16.247; ἐπὴν.. δὴ ἔ. 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 11.121]]; ὁπότε, [Refs [Il. 18.545]]; ὅτε,[Refs [3.223; ὡς.. ἄρ᾽ ἔ. 10.522; ἦμος.. καὶ τότ᾽ ἔ. 1.478.]]

__I.4.b
after a Conditional conjunction, then surely, εἰ δ᾽ ἐτεὸν δὴ.. ἀγορεύεις, ἐξ ἄρα δή τοι ἔ. θεοὶ φρένας ὤλεσαν if thou speakest sooth, then of a surety have the gods infatuated thee, [Refs [7.360, compare 10.453, Od. 1.290, etc.]]; so after ἤν, [Refs [Il. 9.394]]; also when the apodosis takes the form of a question, εἰ μὲν δὴ ἕταρόν γε κελεύετέ μ᾽ αὐτὸν ἑλέσθαι, πῶς ἂν ἔ. Ὀδυσῆος λαθοίμη; how can I in such a case? [Refs [10.243]]; when a condition is implied in relative pronoun, ὃν (={εἴ τινα}) μέν κ᾽ ἐπιεικὲς ἀκουέμεν, οὔ τις ἔ. τόν γ᾽ εἴσεται 1.547; ὃν (={εἴ τινα}) δέ κ᾽ ἐγὼν ἀπάνευθε μάχης ἐθέλοντα νοήσω μιμνάζειν, οὔ οἱ ἔ. ἄρκιον ἐσσεῖται 2.392.

__II
of Sequence in thought, i.e. Consequence or Inference, then, therefore, ξεῖν᾽, ἐπεὶ ἂρ δὴ ἔ... μενεαίνεις 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 17.185 [Refs [, cf. Il. 15.49, 18.357; οὐ σύ γ᾽ ἔ. Τυδέος ἔκγονός ἐσσι 5.812]]; rarely at the beginning, ἔπειθ᾽ ἑλοῦ γε θάτερα 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Electra” 345.

__II.2
in telling a story, νῆσος ἔ. τις ἔστι now, there is an island, [Refs [Od. 4.354, compare 9.116.]]

__II.3
in Attic dialect frequently to introduce emphatic questions, why then.. ? ἔ. τοῦ δέε; [Refs [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Plutus” 827, compare “Th.” 188, “Nu.” 226]]; mostly to express surprise, or to sneer, and so forsooth..? and so really..? ἔ. οὐκ οἴει φροντίζειν [τοὺς θεοὺς τῶν ἀνθρώπων]; [Refs 5th c.BC+ [X. “Mem.” 1.4.11; so κἄπειτα 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Med.” 1398 (_anapaest meter_), Ar. “Ach.” 126, “Av.” 963, X. “Smp.” 4.2]]; frequently with δῆτα added, ἔ. δῆτα δοῦλος ὢν κόμην ἔχει; [Refs [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Aves” 911, compare 1217, “Lys.” 985, E. “Alc.” 822.]]

ἐπ-έρχομαι,
[in LXX for בּוֹא, עָבַר, etc. ;]

__2. to come upon (as in Hom.): of calamities, Luk.21:26, Act.8:24 13:40, Jas.5:1; of an enemy, Luk.11:22; of the Holy Spirit, Luk.1:35, Act.1:8, [in LXX: γίγνομαι ἐπί, Jdg.14:6, 3Ki.11:6, al.].†

LSJ / STEPBible (TFLSJ)
ἐπέρχομαι,
imperfect [Refs 5th c.BC+ [ἐπηρχόμην 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 4.120]] (unless from ἐπάρχομαι: Attic dialect imperfect is ἐπῇα (but see at {ἔρχομαι}) and future ἔπειμι): aorist 2 ἐπῆλθον, Epic dialect -ήλῠθον: perfect -ελήλυθα:

__I
come upon:

__I.1
of persons, approach, with dative, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 12.200, 218]], etc.; especially come suddenly upon, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 19.155, 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 6.95: with _accusative_, ἐ. πόλιν 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Hercules Furens” 593]] codices (nisi to be read ἐσ-); come to for advice, μάντεις, μοῦσαν, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [[prev\. author] “Supp.” 155, “Hel.” 165, compare 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Lg.” 772d: with Preps., ἐ. ἐς ποταμόν 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 7.280, compare 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Aj.” 438: _metaphorically_, ἐ. ἐς λόγου στάσιν [prev\. author] “Tr.” 1180; ἐ. ἐς πόλεμον 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 3.47; ἐ. ἐνθάδε 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 24.651]].

__I.1.b
frequently in hostile sense, go or come against, attack, absolutely, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [12.136, +others, 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 1.90, etc.: with _dative_, 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 20.91, 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Ba.” 736, 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 6.34, etc.: rarely with _accusative_, τμήδην αὐχέν᾽ ἐπῆλθε 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 7.262]]; τὴν τῶν πέλας ἐ. invade it, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 2.39]]: hence, visit, reprove, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [ταῦτα μέν σε πρῶτ᾽ ἐπῆλθον 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Iphigenia Aulidensis” 349, compare “Andr.” 688: with a _preposition_]], invade, [Refs 2nd c.BC+ [ἐπὶ τὴν οἰκίαν “PFay.” 12.12 (2nd c.BC).]]

__I.1.c
come forward to speak, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Or.” 931, 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 1.119, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Lg.” 850c; ἐ. ἐπὶ τὸν δῆμον, ἐπὶ τοὺς ἐφόρους, 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 5.97, 9.7; ἐπὶ τὸ κοινόν 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 1.90]]; τοῖς Αακεδαιμονίοις [Refs [[prev. work] 91.]]

__I.1.d
in Law, proceed against, [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [ἐπί τινα “PEleph.” 3.3 (3rd c.BC); ἐπί τινα περί τινος “PAmh.” 2.96.8 (3rd c.AD); τινὶ περί τινος “POxy.” 489.11 (2nd c.AD); ἐπὶ πιττάκιον]] impugn, [Refs 1st c.BC+ [“BGU” 1167.14 (1st c.BC)]]: also in aorist 1 [Refs 2nd c.BC+ [ἐπελεύσασθαι “PStrassb.” 35.25 (2nd c.BC), etc. (ἐπιπορεύομαι (which see)]] is more common in the present in the Hellenistic period.)

__I.2
of events, conditions, etc., come upon, especially come suddenly upon, with accusative, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [μιν.. ἐπήλυθε νήδυμος ὕπνος 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 4.793, +others, compare 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 2.141; ἔρως γὰρ ἄνδρας οὐ μόνους ἐπέρχεται 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “fragment” 431]]: with dative, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [τοῖσιν ἐπήλυθε νήδυμος ὕπνος 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 12.311, compare 5.472; μοι νοῦσος ἐπήλυθεν 11.200]]; βροτοῖσιν.. [Refs 6th c.BC+ [ὅταν κλύδων κακῶν ἐπέλθῃ Aeschylus Tragicus [{4-5th c.BC}] “Persae” 600, compare “Ag.” 1256; ἐπῆλθέ μοι πάθος Plato Philosophus [{5-6th c.BC}] “Leges” 811d]], etc.

__I.3
with dative person, come into one's head, occur to one, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [ἵμερος ἐπειρέσθαι μοι ἐπῆλθε 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.30]]; ὅ τι ἂν ἐπέλθῃ Latin quicquid in buccam venerit, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Isocrates Orator 12.24: _impersonal_]] with infinitive, [Refs 6th c.BC+ [καί οἱ ἐπῆλθε πταρεῖν 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 6.107, compare 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Tr.” 134 (Lyric poetry); ἐμοὶ τοιαῦτ᾽ ἄττα ἐ. λέγειν Plato Philosophus [{5-6th c.BC}] “Gorgias” 485e, etc.; also ἐπέρχεταί με λέγειν [prev\. author] “Phd.” 88d]].

__I.4
come in, of revenues, etc., ἐπερχόμενοι τόκοι, ἐπιβολαί, [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [“BGU” 155.11 (2nd c.AD), 1049.16 (4th c.AD).]]

__II
of Time, come on, ἐπήλυθον ὧραι the season came round again, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 2.107]], etc.; also, come on, be at hand, [Refs 6th c.BC+ [νὺξ δ᾽ ἄρ᾽ ἐπῆλθε 14.457; γῆρας ἐ. 6th c.BC: Theognis Elegiacus 528, 728; ἕκαθεν ἐπελθὼν ὁ μέλλων χρόνος 5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “O.” 10(11).7]]; τὸ παρὸν τό τ᾽ ἐπερχόμενον πῆμα and that which is coming, the future, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Pr.” 98.]]

__II.2
come in after or over another, of a second wife, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 5.41.]]

__III
go over or on a space, traverse, mostly of persons, with accusative, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [πολλὴν γαῖαν 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 4.268; ἀγρόν 16.27; ἄγκεα πολλά 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 18.321, compare 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 14.139, 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.30]]; go the round of, visit, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [δόμους 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Electra” 1297; ναοὺς χοροῖς [prev\. author] “Ant.” 153]] (Lyric poetry); πόλιν, of a god, [Refs 1st c.AD+ [1st c.AD(?): Macedonius Epigrammaticus “Pac.” 29]]; of an officer, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [πύλας φυλακάς τ᾽ ἐπῆλθον 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Phoenissae” 699; τὰς ξυνωμοσίας ἐπελθών 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 8.54]]; walk on ice, [Refs [[prev\. author] 3.23; also of water, ἐπέρχεται ὁ Νεῖλος τὸ Δέλτα]] overflows it, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 2.19, compare 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Supp.” 559 (Lyric poetry), 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 3.89.]]

__III.2
go through or over, discuss, recount, with accusative, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th-7th c.BC: Hesiodus Epicus “fragment” 160.4 codices 1st c.BC-1st c.AD: Strabo Geographus, 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Eq.” 618]]; review, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [τὰ εἰρημένα περί τινος 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Ethica Nicomachea” 1172b8; also ἐ. περί τινος [prev\. author] “Ph.” 189b31]], +others; followed by an interrogative, [Refs [πειρατέον ἐπελθεῖν τίνες.. [prev\. author] “Pol.” 1289b24]]; πῶς δεῖ.. ἐπέλθωμεν συντόμως [Refs [[prev. work] 1317a15.]]

__III.3
accomplish, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [πολέμῳ καὶ διαχειρίσει πραγμάτων 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 1.97]].

__IV
come up to, imitate, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [πάτρῳ 5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “P.” 6.46]].

ἐπ-ερωτάω, -ῶ
[in LXX chiefly for שָׁאַל, also for דָּרַשׁ, etc. ;]
__1. to in­quire of, consult, question: with accusative of person(s), Mrk.12:34, Luk.2:46, al.; with dupl. accusative, Mrk.7:17 11:29, Luk.20:40, al.; with accusative of person(s), before λέγων, Mat.12:18, Mrk.9:11; εἰ, Mrk.8:23, Luk.23:6, al.; ἐ. θεόν, Rom.10:20 (LXX).

LSJ / STEPBible (TFLSJ)
ἐπερωτ-άω,
Ionic dialect ἐπειρ-, consult, inquire of, with accusative person, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [τὸ χρηστήριον, τὸν θεόν, εἰ.. 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.53, 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 1.118, etc.; τινὰ περί τινος 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.32]], cf. Oracle texts cited in [LXX+4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 43.66; later, ἐν τῷ θεῷ Vetus Testamentum Graece redditum LXX.Judg.18.5]]:—passive, to be questioned, asked a question, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 5.45, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Sph.” 250a.]]

__2
with accusative of things, ask a question, ταῦτα, τάδε, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.30, 55, compare 5th c.BC: Antipho Orator 1.10]]; also, ask about a thing, [[Refs 5th c.BC+ [τὰς ναῦς] καὶ τὸν πεζόν 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 7.100]]; σμικρόν τι τῶν ῥηθέντων call it in question, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Prt.” 329a; ἐ. θυσίαις καὶ οἰωνοῖς ὅ τι χρὴ ποιεῖν]] inquire what.., [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Oec.” 5.19; ἐ. ἐς..]] inquire about, [LXX.2Ki.11.7:—]passive, τὸ ἐπερωτηθέν the question asked, variant in [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Tht.” 146e.]]

__3
with accusative person et of things, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [ἐ. τοὺς προφήτας τὸ αἴτιον 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 9.93 codices; ἐπηρώτα ὑμᾶς τὸ ἐκ τοῦ νόμου κήρυγμα 4th c.BC: Aeschines Orator 1.79]].

__4
absolutely, put a question, especially of a chairman putting a question to the vote, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 22.9, “SIG” 898.17 (Chalcis, 3rd c.AD), +others]]

__5
in Roman Law, put a formal question in stipulatio, most frequently in passive, [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [“POxy.” 905.19 (2nd c.AD), etc.: also in]]active, [Refs 3rd c.AD+ [[prev. work] 1273.41 (3rd c.AD).]]

__5.b
hence later, guarantee, [Refs 6th c.AD+ [PIand. 48.9 (6th c.AD).]]

__6
ask a further question, [Refs 2nd c.BC+ [“SIG” 953.49 (Calymna, 2nd c.BC), +others]]

deep_entry:
Abbott-Smith / STEPBible (TBESG)
ἐπ-έχω
[in LXX for חָדַל, etc.; also Sir.8:1 34:2, 2Ma.5:25 2Mac 9:25, al. ;]
__1. to hold upon.
__2. Like παρέχω (as in Hom., al.), to hold out, offer: λόγον ζωῆς, Php.2:16.
__3. to hold or direct towards, Sc.νοῦν;
__(a) absol., to intend, purpose;
__(b) to observe, give attention to (see MM, Exp., xiv): before πῶς, Luk.14:7; with dative of person(s), Act.3:5, 1Ti.4:16.
__4. to stay, wait: Act.19:22 (in legal phrase, MM, Exp., l.with).†
(AS)

---

LSJ / STEPBible (TFLSJ)
ἐπέχω,
future ἐφέξω (see. infr. IV. [Refs 5th c.BC+ [1, 2) and ἐπισχήσω 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Andromache” 160, 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 45.88]]: aorist ἐπέσχον, imperative ἐπίσχες, infinitive ἐπισχεῖ; poetry [Refs 5th c.BC+ [ἐπισχέθοι Aeschylus Tragicus [{4-5th c.BC}] “Septem contra Thebas” 453 (Lyric poetry), ἐπέσχεθον 3rd c.BC: Apollonius Rhodius Epicus 4.1622]]: perfect [Refs [ἐπέσχηκα “Supp.epigram” 1.362.12]] (Samos, 4th c.BC):—have or hold upon, θρῆνυν.., τῷ κεν ἐπισχοίης (variant{ἐπίσχοιας}) [Refs 8th c.BC+ [λιπαροὺς πόδας 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 14.241, compare 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 17.410; ποτῷ κρωσσὸν ἐ.]] hold it to or for.., [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [3rd c.BC: Theocritus Poeta Bucolicus 13.46; λόγον ζωῆς ἐπέχοντες (i.e. κόσμῳ)]] holding it out like a torch, [NT.Phil.2.16:—]middle, hold by, [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [χειρός 3rd c.BC: Apollonius Rhodius Epicus 4.751]].

__II
hold out to, present, offer, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [οἶνον ἐπισχών 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 9.489; ἐπέσχε τε οἶνον ἐρυθρόν 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 16.444; κοτύλην.. ἐπέσχε 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 22.494]]; εἴ ποτέ τοι.. μαζὸν ἐπέσχον [Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. work] 83, compare 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Andr.” 225; also γάλακτι δ᾽ οὐκ ἐπέσχον οὐδὲ μαστῷ τροφεῖα ματρός]] I offered not mother's food with my breast, [Refs [[prev\. author] “Ion” 1492]]: with infinitive, [Refs 6th c.BC+ [πιεῖν ἐπέσχον Aristophanes Comicus [{5-6th c.BC}] “Nubes” 1382]]: absolutely, [Refs [[prev\. author] “Pax” 1167:]] —middle, ἐπισχόμενος (i.e. τὴν κύλικα) ἐξέπιεν having put it to his lips, [Refs 7th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Phd.” 117c, compare 7th-6th c.BC: Stesichorus Lyricus 7, 3rd c.BC: Apollonius Rhodius Epicus 1.472, 2nd c.AD: Lucianus Sophista “Tox.” 37; ἐπὶ χείλεσι.. μαστὸν ἐπισχομένη 3rd c.BC: Euphorio Epicus 92]]; present a sum of money, τῇ πόλει [Refs [“Supp.epigram” [prev. cited]]]

__II.2
extend, spread out, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [τὴν πλεκτάνην 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Historia Animalium” 550b6]].

__II.3
simply, hold, [Refs [σκῆπτρα “IPE” 2.37 (from Panticapaeum)]]; of writings, contain, [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd-3rd c.AD: Philostratus Sophista “VS” 2.24.2, compare 2.9.1.]]

__II.4
enjoin, impose a task, with dative person, [Refs 6th c.AD+ [6th c.AD: Procopius Caesariensis Historicus “Arc.” 17, “Vand.” 1.8.]]

__III
hold or direct towards, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [ἔπεχε τόξον σκοπῷ 5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “O.” 2.89; ἄλλῳ ἐπεῖχε τόξα 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Hercules Furens” 984]]:— middle, absolutely, ἐπισχόμενος βάλεν ἰῷ having aimed at him he hit him, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 22.15.]]

__III.b
intransitive, aim at, attack, τί μοι ὧδ᾽ ἐπέχει; why thus launch out against me? [Refs 8th c.BC+ [19.71; in tmesi, ἐπὶ αὐτῷ πάντες ἔχωμεν 22.75; ἀλλήλοις ἐ. {8-7th c.BC}: Hesiodus Epicus “Theogonia” 711; ἄνδρα ἐπέχοντα τῷ Πύρρῳ Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus [{1-2nd c.AD}] “Pyrrhus” 16; ἐπέχειν ἐπί τινα 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 9.59; τὰς ἐπὶ σφίσι ναῦς ἐπεχούσας 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 8.105; πρός τι Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus [{1-2nd c.AD}] “Antonius” 66]]: with dative, ἀκτῇσιν ἐπέσχεθον held straight for the beach, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [3rd c.BC: Apollonius Rhodius Epicus 4.1766: _absolutely_, 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Ba.” 1131.]]

__III.2
ἐπέχειν τὴν διάνοιαν ἐπί τινι direct one's mind to a thing, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Lg.” 926b; τῷ πολέμῳ τὴν γνώμην Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus [{1-2nd c.AD}] “Aemilius Paulus” 8]], etc.; also ἐ. ἑαυτόν τινι attend to him, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “R.” 399b codices]]

__III.2.b
absolutely, ἐπέχειν (i.e. τὸν νοῦν) intend, purpose, with infinitive, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [ἐπεῖχε ἐλλάμψεσθαι 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.80, compare 153, 6.96:]] with dative _of things_, to be intent upon, ταῖς ἀρχαῖς, διαβάσει, etc., [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Lys.” 490, 2nd c.BC: Polybius Historicus 3.43.2, etc.]]

__III.3
stand facing, face in a line of battle, οὗτοι (i.e. οἱ Μῆδοι) [Refs 5th c.BC+ [ἐπέσχον Κορινθίους 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 9.31]].

__IV
hold back, keep in check, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [ἐπέσχε δὲ καλὰ ῥέεθρα 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 21.244; καὶ πῶς ἐπέσχε χεῖρα μαιμῶσαν φόνο; 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Ajax” 50]]; ἐπισχὼν ἡνίαν [Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. work] 847; ἐπίσχωμεν τὸ πλεῖν [prev\. author] “Ph.” 881; ὀργάς 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Helena” 1642; οὐκ ἐφέξετε στόμ; [prev\. author] “Hec.” 1283]]; χρησμοὺς ἐ. withhold them, [Refs [[prev\. author] “Ph.” 866; ἐπέχειν τινὰ τῷ ξύλῳ]] keep him down with the stick, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Pax” 1121; τὸ εὐθέως ἐπιχειρεῖν 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 7.33]]; confine, as the earth a corpse, [Refs 1st c.BC+ [“AP” 7.461 (1st c.BC: Meleager Epigrammaticus); ἐ. τῇ χειρὶ τὸ στόμα _cover,_ Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus [{1-2nd c.AD}] “Cat.Mi.” 28; ἐπέχομεν τὴν ἐκπνοήν 2nd c.AD: Galenus Medicus 6.172; τὰς διαχωρήσεις ἐ. [prev\. author]  Vict. _Attic dialect_ 12]]:—middle, [Refs 6th c.BC+ [ἐπισχόμενος τὰ ὦτα Plato Philosophus [{5-6th c.BC}] “Symposium” 216a]]:—passive, [Refs 1st c.AD+ [τοῦ βάθους ἐπεσχημένου 1st c.AD: Josephus Historicus “Antiquitates Judaicae” 5.1.3]]; to be prevented, hindered, [Refs 4th c.AD+ [ὑπό τινος “PFreib.” 11.13 (4th c.AD)]]; of the menses, [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd c.AD: Galenus Medicus 1.184.]]

__IV.b
stay or adjourn proceedings, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [τὰ πρὸς Ἀργείους 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 5.46]]; τὴν ζημίαν καὶ τὴν κατασκαφήν [Refs 4th c.BC+ [[prev. work] 63; τὴν δίαιταν 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 21.84]]; suspend payments, in passive, [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [“PTeb.” 337.4 (2nd-3rd c.AD), compare “PGiss.” 48.11 (3rd c.AD).]]

__IV.c
[Refs 5th c.BC+ [ἐ. τινά τινος _stop, hinder from,?? 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Andromache” 160, 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Lys.” 742, 1st c.BC: Diodorus Siculus Historicus 13.87]]: with infinitive, σε μήτε νὺξ μήτε ἡμέρα ἐπισχέτω ὥστε ἀνεῖναι.. let them not stop thee so that thou neglect.., [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 1.129; ἐ. τινὰ μὴ πράσσειν τι 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Electra” 517, “Ph.” 349; κλαυθμυρίζον τὸ βρέφος ἐπισχεῖν μὴ δυνάμεναι 2nd c.AD: Soranus Medicus 1.88]]:—passive, μηδενὸς ἐπεχομένου no objection being taken, [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [PTeb. 327.37 (2nd c.AD).]]

__IV.d
impersonal, [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [ἐπέχει _there is a hindrance,?? 2nd c.AD: Astrampsychus Onirocriticus “Oracle texts” 97.3]].

__IV.2
absolutely, stay, pause, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [Ἀντίνοος δ᾽ ἔτ᾽ ἐπεῖχε 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 21.186]]; refrain, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.32, 5.51, 7.139; εἰ δ᾽ ἐφέξετον]] if you tarry, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “El.” 1369, etc.: followed by a _conjunction_, especially in _imperative_, ἐπίσχες ἢν..]] wait and see whether.., [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Supp.” 397; ἐπίσχες ἔστ᾽ ἂν.. προσμάθῃς Aeschylus Tragicus [{4-5th c.BC}] “Prometheus Vinctus” 697; ἐ. ἕως.. 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 4.1; μέχρι τοσούτου ἔως.. 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 1.90]]; ἐπίσχες, absolutely, hold! stop! [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Ch.” 896, 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “OC” 856, etc.; ἐπίσχετε, μηδὲ συρίξητε 4th c.BC: Timocles Comicus 2.6D.; ἐπίσχετον, μάθωμεν 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Philoctetes” 539, compare 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Hipp.” 567]]; in participle, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [ἐπισχὼν ὀλίγον χρόνον 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.132]], +others; τὸ ἐπισχεῖν, opposed to τὸ παραχρῆμα, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Antipho Orator 5.73; οὐ πολὺν χρόνον ἐπισχὼν ἧκεν]] came after a short interval, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Phd.” 59e; μικρὸν ἐπισχόντα διεφθείροντο]] they very shortly died, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th-3rd c.BC: Theophrastus Philosophus “HP” 4.4.13, cf. Diocl.fragment 43; in 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 2.81 οὐκ ἐπέσχον τὸ στρατόπεδον καταλαβεῖν]] did not halt for the purpose of occupying a camp (unless it, = 'had no intention of occupying').

__IV.2.b
with genitive of things, stop or cease from, [Refs 6th c.BC+ [ἐπίσχες τοῦ δρόμου Aristophanes Comicus [{5-6th c.BC}] “Aves” 1200; τῆς πορείας Xenophon Historicus [{5-6th c.BC}] “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 4.2.12; τούτου 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 8.31; also ἐ. περί τινος [prev\. author] 5.32, compare 8.5]]: so with infinitive, leave off, cease to do, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Mem.” 3.6.10]]: with participle, cease doing, [Refs 6th c.BC+ [ἀναλῶν οὐκ ἐφέξεις Aristophanes Comicus [{5-6th c.BC}] “Equites” 915 (Lyric poetry), compare 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Ph.” 449.]]

__IV.2.c
as technical term of the Sceptics, suspend judgement, doubt, [Refs 1st c.BC+ [1st c.BC-1st c.AD: Strabo Geographus 2.1.11, 1st c.AD: Philo Judaeus 1.387, 2nd c.AD: Sextus Empiricus Philosophus “P.” 1.196; ἐ. ἐν τοῖς ἀδήλοις Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus [{1-2nd c.AD}] 2.955c;  τὰ ἄδηλα 2nd c.AD: Arrianus Historicus “Epicteti Dissertationes” 1.7.5]].

__IV.3
middle, maintain reserve, [Refs 2nd c.BC+ [ἐπείχετο [ἡ σύγκλητος] κατὰ τοὺς Ἀθηναίους 2nd c.BC: Polybius Historicus 30.19.17]] (assuming variant).

__V
reach or extend over a space, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [ἐπτὰ δ᾽ ἐπέσχε πέλεθρα 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 21.407]]; ὁπόσσον ἐπέσχε πυρὸς μένος so far as the fire reached, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [23.238, compare 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 7.19, 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 2.77, _falsa lectio_ in 5th c.BC: Hippocrates Medicus]] “Aër.” 5, etc.: aorist middle, ἐπέσχετο he lay outstretched, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th-7th c.BC: Hesiodus Epicus “Th.” 177; βούβρωστις ἐπέσχετο κόσμον _prevailed over..,?? epigram Gr. 793.5 (from Apollonia); ἀφορία ἐ. τὸν βίον 3rd c.AD: Longinus Rhetor 44.1]].

__VI
have power over, occupy a country, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [οἱ Σκύθαι τὴν Ἀσίην πᾶσαν ἐπέσχον 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.104, compare 108, 8.32, 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 2.101, 7.62]], etc.; of things, ἐπ᾽ ὀκτὼ μῆνας Κυρηναίους ὀπώρη ἐ. occupies or engages them, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 4.199; τὴν πόλιν ἐπεῖχε κλαυθμός Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus [{1-2nd c.AD}] “Otho” 17]]; ὧν τὰς χρόας τὸ [Refs 6th c.BC+ [ἡμερινὸν φῶς ἐ. _overspreads,_ Plato Philosophus [{5-6th c.BC}] “Respublica” 508c: κραυγῆς ἐπεχούσης τὴν ἐκκλησίαν 1st c.BC: Diodorus Siculus Historicus 13.87; πρὸ τοῦ τὰ σώματα τὰς ὠδῖνας ἐπισχεῖν 2nd c.AD: Soranus Medicus 2.53]]: generally, occupy, τὴν κρατίστην μοῖραν ἐ. hold the foremost place, [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [3rd c.AD: Longinus Rhetor 9.1, compare 44.12; ὕλης ἐ. τάξιν “Stoicorum Veterum Fragmenta” 3.27; τὴν γῆν κέντρου λόγον ἐπέχουσαν 3rd c.AD: Diogenes Laertius 7.155, compare “Placit.” 3. “Praef.”; τὸν τέλειον ἐ. λόγον 2nd c.AD: Galenus Medicus 19.160]]; δίκην ἐπέχειν ἡμᾶς φυτῶν we are like plants, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Meno Medicus “Iatr.” 6.18.]]

__VI.2
absolutely, prevail, predominate, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [ἢν μὴ λαμπρὸς ἄνεμος ἐπέχῃ 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 2.96; σεισμοὶ ἐπέσχον ἐπὶ πλεῖστον μέρος γῆς 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 1.23]]; πάντῃ ἐπεῖχε γαλήνη Timo [Refs 5th c.BC+ [63; [τῶν νεῶν] ἐπὶ πολὺ τῆς θαλάσσης ἐπεχουσῶν _being spread over... 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 1.50; τὴν [τύχην].., ἣ νῦν ἐπέχει 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 18.253; ἐτησίων ἐπεχόντων 2nd c.BC: Polybius Historicus 5.5.6]].

__VI.2.b
of Time, continue, [Refs 6th c.BC+ [τὴν θύραν ἐπεῖχε κρούων Aristophanes Comicus [{5-6th c.BC}] “Ecclesiazusae” 317; ἐπέχων καὶ οὐκ ἀνιείς _continuously,_ Plato Philosophus [{5-6th c.BC}] “Theaetetus” 165e; ἐπὶ πλείους ἡμέρας ὁ σεισμὸς ἐπεῖχεν Dio Cassius Historicus [{2-3rd c.AD}] 68.25]]; σκότος, νὺξ ἐπέσχε, came on, [Refs 1st c.AD+ [1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus “Mar.” 20, “Crass.” 30, etc.]]

__VII
middle, future ἐπιέξομαι, meet, Oracle texts in [Refs 5th c.BC+ [“Michel” 855.39 (5th c.BC: Magnes Comicus Mae.).]]

ἐπηρε-άζω,
threaten abusively, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [λέγειν ἐπηρεάζοντες 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 6.9]]: with accusative, speak disparagingly of, [Refs [τὴν ἀγαθὴν ἀναστροφήν “1st Epistle of Peter” 3.16]].

deep_entry:
Abbott-Smith / STEPBible (TBESG)
ἐπί (before a smooth breathing ἐπ᾽, before a rough breathing ἐφ᾽),
prep. with genitive, dative, accusative (accusative most frequently in NT),
with primary sense of superposition, on, upon.
__I. C. genitive,
__1. of place, answering the question, where?
__(a) of the place on which, on, upon: ἐπὶ (τ.) γῆς, Mat.6:10, 19, al.; τ. κεφαλῆς, 1Co.11:10; τ. νεφελῶν, Mat.24:3o, al.; like ἐν, in constr. praegn. after verbs of motion: βάλλειν, Mrk.4:26; σπείρειν, ib. 31; ἔρχεσθαι, Heb.6:7, al.; figuratively, ἐπ᾽ ἀληθείας (MM, see word ἀ.); of the subject of thought or speech, Gal.3:16; of power or authority, over, πάντων, Rom.9:5: τ. γάζης, Act.8:27; ἐξουσία, Rev.2:26 20:6;
__(b) of vicinity, at, by: τ. θαλάσσης, Jhn.6:9; τ. ὁδοῦ, Mat.21:19; τοῦ βάτου, Mrk.12:26 (see Swete, in l.); with genitive of person(s), in the presence of, before, Mat.28:14, Act.23:30, 1Co.6:1, al.
__2. Of time,
__(a) with genitive of person(s), in the time of: ἐπὶ Ἐλισαίου, Luk.4:27; ἐπὶ Κλαυδίου, Act.11:28; ἐπὶ Ἀβιάθαρ ἀρχιερέως, when A. was high priest, Mrk.2:26;
__(b) with genitive of thing(s), at, at the time of: Mat.1:11, Heb.1:2, 2Pe.3:3; ἐπὶ τ. προσευχῶν, Rom.1:10, Eph.1:16, 1Th.1:2, Phm 4.
__II. C. dative, of place, answering the question, where?
__(a) lit., on, upon: Mat.9:16, 14:8, al.; after verbs of motion (see supr., I, 1, (a)), Mat.9:16 Act.8:16; above, Luk.23:38; at, by, Mrk.13:29, Jhn.5:2, Act.5:9, al.;
__(b) metaphorically, upon, on the ground of, Luk.4:4 (LXX); in the matter of, Mrk.6:52 (see Swete, in l.); upon, of, concerning, Act.5:35, 40; of the ground, reason or motive (Bl., §38, 2; 43, 3), Mat.18:3 19:9, Rom.12:12, al.; ἐφ᾽ ᾧ, for the reason that,  because, Rom.5:12 2Co.5:4; after verbs of motion, over, Mat.18:13, Rom.16:19, al.; of a condition (cl.), Rom.8:20, 1Co.9:10; ἐπὶ δυσὶ μάρτυσιν (see Westc. on Heb.9:10), Heb.10:28; of purpose or aim, Eph.2:10, Php.4:10; of authority, over, Mat.24:47 Luk.12:44; of hostility, with dative of person(s) (cl.), against, Luk.12:52; in addition to (cl.), 2Co.7:13; of an adjunct, in, at, on, Php.1:3 2:17.
__III. C. accusative,
__1. of place of motion upon or over, answering the question, whither?
__(a) lit., upon, over: Mat.14:28, 29, Luk.5:19, al. mult.; in NT also, answering the question, where? (as with genitive, dative), Mrk.4:38 11:2, Luk.2:25, Jhn.1:32; ἐπὶ τ. αὐτό, Act.1:15 2:1, al.; of motion to a vicinity, to, Mrk.16:2, Act.8:36, al.;
__(b) metaphorically (in wh. "the accusative is more widely prevalent than it strictly should be," Bl., §43, 1); of blessings, evils, etc., coming upon one, with accusative of person(s), Mat.10:13 12:28, Act.2:17, Jhn.18:4, Eph.5:6, al.; of addition (dative in cl.), λύπη ἐπὶ λύπην, Php.2:27; ἐπικαλεῖν ὄνομα ἐπί (see: ἐπικαλέω), Act.15:17, Jas.2:7; καλεῖν ἐπί, to call after, Luk.1:59; of number or degree: ἐπὶ τρίς (cl. εἰς τ.), thrice, Act.10:16 11:10; ἐπὶ πλεῖον, the more, further, Act.4:17 2Ti.2:16 3:9 (see also infr., 2, (a)); ἐφ᾽ ὅσον (see infr., ib.), forasmuch as, Mat.25:40, 45, Rom.11:13; of power, authority, control, Luk.1:33, Act.7:10 Rom.5:14, Heb.3:6, al.; of the direction of thoughts and feelings, unto, towards, Luk.1:17 23:28, Act.9:35, 42, Rom.11:22, Gal.4:9, Eph.2:7, 1Ti.5:5, al.; of purpose, for, Mat.3:7, Luk.23:48; ἐφ᾽ ὅ πάρει (Rec. ἐφ᾽ ᾧ, Mat.26:50; of hostility, against, Mat.24:7, Mrk.3:24-26 10:11 13:8, Luk.9:5, Jhn.13:18, Act.7:54, 1Co.7:36, 2Co.1:23; Of reference, concerning, for (cl. usually dative), Mrk.9:12 15:24, Jhn.19:24, Rom.4:9.
__2. Of time,
__(a) during, for: Luk.4:25 (WH, txt., omits ἐπί), Act.13:31 16:18, Heb.11:30, al.; ἐφ᾽ ὅσον (χρόνον), as long as, for so long time as, Mrk.9:15 Rom.7:1, al. (for ἐφ᾽ ὅ in another sense, see supr., 1, (b)); ἐφ᾽ ἱκανόν (see: ἱ), Act.20:11; ἐπὶ πλεῖον (see supr., 1, (b)), yet longer, further, Act.20:9 24:4;
__(b) on, about, towards (cl. εἰς): Luk.10:35 Act.3:1 4:5.
__IV. In composition, ἐπί signifies: up, ἐπαίρω; upon, ἐπίγειος, ἐπιδημέω, ὠπικαθίζω; towards, επιβλέπω, ὠπεκτείνω; over (of superintendence), ἐπιστάτης; again, in addition, ἐπαιτέω; against, ἐπιορκέω, ἐπιβουλή.
(AS)

LSJ / STEPBible (TFLSJ)
ἐπί,
Thess. (before τ) [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [ἐτ “IG” 9(2).517.14 (3rd c.BC), _preposition_ with _genitive_, _dative_, and _accusative_]], to denote the being upon or supported upon a surface or point.

__A
WITH GEN.:

__A.I

__C.III.1
. of the object or purpose for which one goes, ἀγγελίην ἔπι Τυδῆ στεῖλαν sent him for (i.e. to bring) tidings of.., [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 4.384 (uncertain); ἐ. βοῦν ἴτω]] let him go for an ox, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 3.421; ἐ. τεύχεα δ᾽ ἐσσεύοντο 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 2.808; ἐλθεῖν πρός τινα ἐπ᾽ ἀργύριον Xenophon Historicus [{5-6th c.BC}] “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 1.6.12]]; πέμπειν εἴς τινα ἐ. στράτευμα [Refs [[prev. work] 4.5.31; ἴτω τις ἐφ᾽ ὕδωρ [prev. work] 5.3.49; ἥκειν ἐ. τοὺς τόκους]] for (i.e. to demand) the interest, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 50.61: less frequently with _accusative_ _person_, ἐπ᾽ Ὀδυσσῆα ἤϊε 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 5.149, compare 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “OT” 555; κατῆλθον ἐ. ποιητήν Aristophanes Comicus [{5-6th c.BC}] “Ranae” 1418; κατέρχονται ἐ. τὸν Ἀγόρατον 5th c.BC: Lysias Orator 13.23]]: with accusative of a Noun of Action, ἐξιέναι ἐ. θήραν go out hunting, [Refs 6th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Cyr.” 1.2.9; ἔπλεον οὐχ ὡς ἐ. ναυμαχίαν (variant for{-μαχίᾳ}) 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 2.83; ἐ. μάχην ἰέναι Xenophon Historicus [{5-6th c.BC}] “Anabasis” 1.4.12]]; ἔρχεσθαι, ἵζειν ἐ. δεῖπνον, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 2.381, 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 24.394; ἐ. δόρπον ἀνέστη 12.439; κληθεὶς ἐ. δεῖπνον Plato Philosophus [{5-6th c.BC}] “Symposium” 174e, etc.; καλεῖν ἐ. ξείνια 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 2.107, 5.18; ἐ. τὴν θεωρίαν]] to see the sight, [NT+2nd c.BC+ [“NT.Luke.23.48”, compare “PTeb.” 33.6 (2nd c.BC): frequently with _neuter_ _pronoun_]] or adjective, ἐ. τοῦτο ἐλθεῖν for this purpose, [Refs 6th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “An.” 2.5.22, compare 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 5.87; ἐπ᾽ αὐτὸ τοῦτο Plato Philosophus [{5-6th c.BC}] “Gorgias” 447b]], etc.; ἐ. τ; to what end? [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Nu.” 256; ἐφ᾽ ὅ τι [prev\. author] “Lys.” 22, 481; ἐφ᾽ ἃ ἤλθομεν]] for which purpose, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 7.15, etc.; ἐπὶ ἴσα]] for like ends, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “N.” 7.5 (but ἐ. ἶσα μάχη τέτατο, ={ἴσως}, 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 12.436); ἐ. τὸ βέλτιον]] to a better result, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “An.” 7.8.4; ἀναστῆσαί τινα ἐ. χριστὸν Θεοῦ]] set up as God's anointed, [LXX.2Ki.23.1]: after an adjective, ἄριστοι πᾶσαν [Refs 8th c.BC+ [ἐπ᾽ ἰθύν 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 6.79, compare 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 4.434; ἄπορος ἐ. φρόνιμα 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Tyrannus” 691]] (Lyric poetry); χρήσιμος [Refs 6th c.BC+ [ἐ... οὐδέν 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 25.31: after a Noun, ὁδὸς ἐ. τι Xenophon Historicus [{5-6th c.BC}] “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 1.6.21]]; ὄργανα ἐ. τι [Refs [[prev. work] 6.2.34.]]

__C.III.2
. so far as regards, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [τοὐπὶ τήνδε τὴν κόρην 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Antigone” 889; ὅσον γε τοὐπ᾽ ἐμέ 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Orestes” 1345]]; τοὐπί σε, τὸ ἐ. σέ, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev\. author] “Hec.” 514, 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Cyr.” 1.4.12; τὸ ἐ. σφᾶς εἶναι 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 4.28]]; ὡς ἐ. τὸ πολύ for the most part, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Top.” 100b29, etc.; ἐ. πᾶν 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 2.51]]; τὸ πρὸς ἅπαν [Refs 3rd c.AD+ [ξυνετὸν ἐ. πᾶν ἀργόν [prev\. author] 3.82; κρείσσων ἐπ᾽ ἀρετήν 3rd c.AD: Democritus Epigrammaticus 181]]; ἐ. [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [μέγα 3rd c.BC: Callimachus Epicus “Hymnus in Dianam” 55]].

__C.III.3
. of persons set over others, ἐ. τοὺς πεζοὺς [Refs 6th c.BC+ [καθιστάναι ἄρχοντα Xenophon Historicus [{5-6th c.BC}] “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 4.5.58, compare “HG” 3.4.20; στρατηγὸς ἐ. τοὺς ὁπλίτας, ἐ. τὴν χώραν, 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Ath.” 61.1, “IG” 22.682.24; ἐ. τὸν Πειραιέα 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Ath.” [same place]; ἐ. Ῥαμνοῦντα “IG” 2.1206b (compare 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus 111.1); οἱ θεσμοθέται οἱ ἐ. τοὺς νόμους κληρούμενοι 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 20.90]].

__C.III.4
. according to, by, ἐ. στάθμην by the rule, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 5.245, 21.44, etc.]]

__D
. POSITION:—ἐπί may suffer anastrophe (ἔπι) and follow its case, as in [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 1.162; it may like wise follow its Verb, ἤλυθ᾽ ἔπι ψυχή 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 24.20, compare 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 9.539.]]

__D.II
. in Poets it is sometimes put with the second of two Nouns, though in sense it also governs the first, ἢ ἁλὸς ἢ ἐ. [Refs 8th c.BC+ [γῆς 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 12.27, compare 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “OT” 761, “Ant.” 367 (Lyric poetry).]]

__E
. AB[Refs 8th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus, used adverbially, without anastrophe, καὶ ἐ. σκέπας ἦν ἀνέμοιο 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 5.443]]; κτεῖνον δ᾽ ἐ. μηλοβοτῆρας as well, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 18.529; especially ἐ. δέ..]] and besides.. , [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 7.65, 75, etc.; πολιαί τ᾽ ἐ. ματέρες 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Tyrannus” 182]] (Lyric poetry).

__E.II
. ἔπι, for ἔπεστι, there is, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 1.515, 3.45, 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 16.315; οὐ γὰρ ἔπ᾽ ἀνήρ..]] there is no man.., [Refs 5th c.BC+ [2.58; σοὶ δ᾽ ἔ. μὲν μορφὴ ἐπέων 11.367; ἔ. δέ μοι γέρας Aeschylus Tragicus [{4-5th c.BC}] “Eumenides” 393]] codices (Lyric poetry).

__F
. PROSODY: in ἐπιόψομαι, ι is not elided before a vowel; also in some words where σ or ϝ has been lost, as ἐπιάλμενος, ἐπιείκελος, ἐπιεικής, ἐπιέξομαι (v. [Refs [ἐπέχω v11). _Doric dialect_ ἐπιεργάζομαι (v. ἐπιεργάζομαι).]]

__G
. IN COMPOSITION:

__G.I
. of Place, denoting,

__G.I.1
. Support or Rest upon, ἔπειμι (A), ἐπίκειμαι, ἐπικαθίζω, ἐπαυχένιος, ἐπιβώμιος, etc.

__G.I.2
. Motion,

__G.I.2.a
. upon or over, ἐπιβαίνω, ἐπιτρέχω.

__G.I.2.b
. to or towards, ἐπέρχομαι, ἐπιστέλλω, ἐπαρίστερος, ἐπιδέξιος.

__G.I.2.c
. against, [Refs [ἐπαΐσσω, ἐπιπλέω 11]], ἐπιστρατεύω, ἐπιβουλεύω.

__G.I.2.d
. up to a point, ἐπιτελέω.

__G.I.2.e
. over a place, as in ἐπαιωρέομαι, ἐπαρτάω.

__G.I.2.f
. over or beyond boundaries, as in ἐπινέμομαι.

__G.I.2.g
. implying reciprocity, as in ἐπιγαμία.

__G.I.3
. Extension over a surface, as in ἐπαλείφω, ἐπανθίζω, [Refs [ἐπιπέτομαι, ἐπιπλέω 1]], ἐπάργυρος, ἐπίχρυσος.

__G.I.4
. Accumulation of one thing over or besides another, as in ἐπαγείρω, ἐπιμανθάνω, ἐπαυξάνω, ἐπιβάλλω, ἐπίκτητος.

__G.I.5
. Accompaniment, to, with, as in ἐπᾴδω, ἐπαυλέω, ἐπαγρυπνέω: hence of Addition, ἐπίτριτος one and  1/3 more, 1 + 1/3; so ἐπιτέταρτος, ἐπίπεμπτος, ἐπόγδοος, etc.

__G.I.6
. with adjectives, somewhat, slightly, as in ἐπίξανθος, ἐπίπικρος.

__G.II
. of Time and Sequence, after, as in ἐπιβιόω, ἐπιβλαστάνω, ἐπιγίγνομαι, [Refs [ἐπακόλουθος, ἐπίγονος, ἐπιστάτης 1.2]].

__G.III
. in causal senses:

__G.III.1
. Superiority felt over or at, as in ἐπιχαίρω, ἐπιγελάω, ἐπαισχύνομαι.

__G.III.2
. Authority over, as in ἐπικρατέω, ἔπαρχος, ἐπιβουκόλος, ἐπιποιμήν.

__G.III.3
. Motive for, as in ἐπιθυμέω, ἐπιζήμιος, ἐπιθάνατος.

__G.III.4
. to give force or intensity to the Verb, as in ἐπαινέω, ἐπιμέμφομαι, ἐπικείρω, ἐπικλάω.

Abbott-Smith / STEPBible (TBESG)
ἐπι-βαίνω
[in LXX chiefly for רָכַב ;]
__1. to get up on, mount: before ἐπί, with accusative, Mat.21:5 (LXX); to embark in (a boat), go aboard: with dative, Act.27:2; before εἰς, Act.21:6 (Rec.); absol., Act.21:2.
__2. to go up to, go on to, enter: before εἰς, Act.20:18 21:4; with dative, Act.25:1.†
(AS)

---

LSJ / STEPBible (TFLSJ)
ἐπιβαίνω,
rarely ἐπηχ-βάω, imperative [Refs 6th c.BC+ [ἐπίβᾱ 6th c.BC: Theognis Elegiacus 847]], Doric dialect infinitive ἐπιβῆν (belowIV): future -βήσομαι: perfect -βέβηκα: aorist 2 ἐπέβην: aorist 1 middle ἐπεβησάμην (of which Hom.always uses the Epic dialect form ἐπεβήσετο, imperative [Refs 8th c.BC+ [ἐπιβήσεο 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 8.105, +others; later ἐπεβήσατο 3rd c.BC: Apollonius Rhodius Epicus 3.869, _Doric dialect_ -βάσατο 3rd c.BC: Callimachus Epicus “Lavacrum Palladis” 65).]]

__A
. in these tenses, intransitive, go upon:

__I
. with genitive, set foot on, tread, walk upon, γαίης, ἠπείρου, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 9.83, “Hymnus in Cererem” 127; πόληος, πατρίδος αἴης, Τροίης, 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 16.396, 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 4.521, 14.229; ἀδύτων ἐπιβάς 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Andromache” 1034]] (Lyric poetry); ἐ. τῶν οὔρων set foot on the confines, [Refs 6th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 4.125, compare 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 1.103, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Lg.” 778e; τῆς Λακωνικῆς ἐπὶ πολέμῳ Xenophon Historicus [{5-6th c.BC}] “Historia Graeca (Hellenica)” 7.4.6]]; πυρῆς ἐπιβάντ᾽ ἀλεγεινῆς, of a corpse, placed upon.. , [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 4.99; πλατείᾳ τῇ ῥινὶ ἐ. τοῦ χείλους Philostratus Sophista [{2-3rd c.AD}] “Philostrati majoris imagines” 2.18; also ἐ. ἐπί τινος 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 2.107]].

__I.2
. get upon, mount on, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [πύργων 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 8.165]]; νεῶν [Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. work] 512; ἵππων 5.328, 10.513; δίφρου 23.379; εὐνῆς 9.133; τοῦ τείχεος 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 9.70]]; λέκτρων ἐ. [Refs 8th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Supp.” 39; also ἐ. ἐπὶ νεός 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 8.118: frequently in 8th c.BC: Homerus Epicus]], in aorist middle, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [ἐπεβήσετ᾽ ἀπήνης 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 6.78]], +others

__I.2.b
. Architecture texts, to be superposed, [Refs [τὰ ἐπιβαίνοντα πάντα ἐπὶ τοὺς κρατευτάς “IG” 7.3073.104]], compare 111 (Lebad.).

__I.3
. of Time, arrive at, [Refs 6th c.BC+ [τετταράκοντα ἐ. ἐτῶν Plato Philosophus [{5-6th c.BC}] “Leges” 666b]]; δεκάτω (i.e. ἔτεος) ἐ. [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [3rd c.BC: Theocritus Poeta Bucolicus 26.29; δωδεκάτου ἐπιβάς “IG” 14.1728; τῆς μειρακίων ἡλικίας 2nd c.AD: Herodianus Grammaticus 1.3.1]].

__I.4
. metaphorically, ἀναιδείης ἐπέβησαν have trodden the path of shamelessness, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 22.424; ἐϋφροσύνης ἐπιβῆτον]] enter into joy, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [23.52; τέχνης ἐπιβήσομαι,-βήμεναι, “Hymnus ad Mamercus Elegiacus” 166, 465; ὁσίης [prev. work] 173; εὐσεβίας 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Coloneus” 189]] (Lyric poetry); ἐ. δόξης entertain an expectation, [Refs [[prev\. author] “Ph.” 1463 (_anapaest meter_); ἐ. σοφίας]] undertake it, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Epin.” 981a; λόγου 2nd c.AD: Lucianus Sophista “Astr.” 8]]; ἐ. τῆς ἀφορμῆς, τῆς προφάσεως, seize upon it, [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd c.AD: Appianus Historicus “Syr.” 2, “Sam.” 11]], etc.; preside over, τῆς ἀνθρωπίνης [Refs 4th c.AD+ [ψυχῆς 4th c.AD: Iamblichus Philosophus “de Mysteriis” 9.8]], +others

__II
. with dative, get upon, board, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [ναυσί 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 7.70]]; land on, [Refs 1st c.BC+ [ἐ. τῇ Σικελίᾳ 1st c.BC: Diodorus Siculus Historicus 16.66]]: metaphorically, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [ἐ. ἀνορέαις 5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “N.” 3.20]]; also, make forcible entry into, τινός οἰκίαις, γῇ, [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [“PHamb.” 10.6 (2nd c.AD), “PAmh.” 2.142.7 (4th c.AD).]]

__II.b
. with a preposition, ἐπὶ πύργῳ ἄλλος πύργος [Refs 5th c.BC+ [ἐπιβέβηκε 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.181]].

__II.2
. with dative person, set upon, assault, [Refs 6th c.BC+ [τινί Xenophon Historicus [{5-6th c.BC}] “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 5.2.26, 1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus “Cim.” 15]], etc.; simply, approach, uncertain in [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “fragment” 88.2.]]

__II.3
. trample on, [Refs 6th c.BC+ [λὰξ ἐπίβα δήμῳ 6th c.BC: Theognis Elegiacus 847]].

__III
. with accusative loci, light upon, in [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Homerus Epicus]] twice of gods lighting upon earth after their descent from Olympus, Πιερίην ἐπιβᾶσα, ἐπιβάς, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 14.226, 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 5.50; so πολλῶν ἐ. καιρόν]] light on the fit time, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “N.” 1.18]]; then simply, go on to a place, enter it, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [γῆν καὶ ἔθνος 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 7.50; λειμῶν᾽ 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Ajax” 144]] (anapaest meter): with preposition, ἐ. ἐπὶ χώραν Decrees Amphict. cited in [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 18.154; εἰς Βοιωτίαν 1st c.BC: Diodorus Siculus Historicus 14. 84.]]

__III.2
. rarely with accusative person, attack, only poetry, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Aj.” 138 (_anapaest meter_): _metaphorically_, of passion or suffering, [prev\. author] “El.” 492 (Lyric poetry), “Ph.” 194 (_anapaest meter_).]]

__III.3
. mount, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [νῶθ᾽ ἵππων ἐπιβάντες {8-7th c.BC}: Hesiodus Epicus “Scutum Herculis” 286]]: more frequently with preposition, ἐπὶ [Refs 5th c.BC+ [τὸν ἵππον 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 4.22; ἐπὶνέα [prev\. author] 8.120, compare 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 1.111; but ἐ. ἐπὶ τὸ θῆλυ]], of made quadrupeds, cover a female, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “HA” 539b26; so _absolutely_, [prev. work] 574a20, +others: with _dative_, 2nd c.AD: Lucianus Sophista “Asin.” 27: with _genitive_, 4th c.AD(?): Horapollo 1.46, 2.78.]]

__III.4
. ἐ. ἐπὶ τὸ σκέλος use, put one's weight on, a broken leg, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Hippocrates Medicus “Fract.” 18.]]

__III.5
. with accusative of the Instr. of Motion (compare [Refs 5th c.BC+ [βαίνω Aeschylus Tragicus [{4-5th c.BC}] 11.4), ἐπιβῆναι τῷ ἀριστερῷ ἐκείνης τὸν ἐμὸν δεξιόν 2nd c.AD: Lucianus Sophista “DMeretr.” 4.5, compare “Tox.” 48.]]

__IV
. absolutely, get a footing, stand on one's feet, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 5.666, 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 12.434; μἠπιβῆν]] it is forbidden to set foot here, [Refs [“IG” 12(3).1381 (from Thera).]]

__IV.2
. step onwards, advance, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [Τρώων δὲ πόλις ἐπὶ πᾶσα βέβηκε 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 16.69, compare 8th-7th c.BC: Hesiodus Epicus “Op.” 679, _falsa lectio_ in 5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “N.” 10.43; ἐπίβαινε πόρσω 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Coloneus” 179]] (assuming variant, Lyric poetry): me taph., advance in one's demands, [Refs 2nd c.BC+ [2nd c.BC: Polybius Historicus 1.68.8.]]

__IV.3
. mount on a chariot or on horseback, be mounted, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 3.84]]; go or be on board ship, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 15.387, 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Aj.” 358 (Lyric poetry), 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 8.90, 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 2.90, etc.]]

__B
. Causal in future -βήσω [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd c.AD: Lucianus Sophista “DMort.” 6.4]], Epic dialect infinitive -βησέμεν [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 8.197, 8th-7th c.BC: Hesiodus Epicus “Th.” 396]], but usually in aorist 1 active (ἐπιβιβάζω, ἐπιβάσκω serve as present):—make one mount, set him upon, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [ὅν ῥα τόθ᾽ ἵππων.. ἐπέβησε 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 8.129; πολλοὺς δὲ πυρῆς ἐπέβησ᾽ ἀλεγεινῆς 9.546]]; ὥς κ᾽ ἐμὲ.. ἐμῆς [Refs 8th c.BC+ [ἐπιβήσετε πάτρης 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 7.223; ἐ. τινὰς σκάφεσιν 1st c.AD: Josephus Historicus “Bellum Judaicum” 4.7.6]]; πλοίων [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [[prev. work] 11.5, cf. Luc.[same place]; ὁπλίτας ὁλκάσιν 2nd c.AD: Appianus Historicus “Bella Civilia” 5.92]]; τινὰς ἐπὶ τὰς ναῦς [Refs [[prev. work] 2.59]]: also in aorist 1 middle, [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [νιν ἑῶ ἐπεβάσατο δίφρω 3rd c.BC: Callimachus Epicus “Lavacrum Palladis” 65]].

__B.b
. of things, νευρὰν ἐπέβασε κορώνας set the string on his bow's tip, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Bacchylides Lyricus 5.73.]]

__B.2
. metaphorically (compare[Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus 1.4), ἐϋκλεΐης ἐπίβησον]] bring to great glory, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 8.285; τιμῆς καὶ γεράων {8-7th c.BC}: Hesiodus Epicus “Theogonia” 396]]; χαλιφρονέοντα σαοφροσύνης ἐπέβησαν they bring him to sobriety, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 23.13; λιγυρῆς ἐπέβησαν ἀοιδῆς {8-7th c.BC}: Hesiodus Epicus “Opera et Dies” 659]]; δουλοσύνας (probably) [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Hyps.fragment” 41(64).86; εἴ σε τύχη.. ἡλικίας ἐπέβησεν]] had brought thee to full age, [Refs [“IG” 2.2263.]]

__B.3
. [ἠὼς] πολέας ἐπέβησε κελεύθου dawn sets them on their way, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th-7th c.BC: Hesiodus Epicus “Op.” 580.]]
