Abbott-Smith / STEPBible (TBESG)
ἐπι-βάλλω
[in LXX for שָׁלַח, שִׁית, etc. ;]
__1. trans., to cast, lay or put upon: with accusative and dative, Mrk.11:7, 1Co.7:35; with accusative, before ἐπί with accusative, Rev.18:10, WH, mg.; τ. Χεῖρα (-ας) ἐπί (B1., § 37, 7), of seizing a prisoner, Mat.26:50, Luk.20:19 21:12, Jhn.7:30, Act.5:18 21:27; with dative (Polyb.), Mrk.14:46 Act.4:3; with inf., Act.12:1; τὴν χ. ἐπ᾽ ἄροτρον, Luk.9:62; ἐπίβλημα ἐπὶ ἱμάτιον, Luk.5:36; ἐπὶ ἱματίῳ, Mat.9:16.
__2. Intrans.,
__(a) to throw oneself or rush upon: τ. κύματα εἰς τ. πλοῖον, Mrk.4:37; metaphorically, to put one's mind upon (but see Field, Notes, 41 ff.), ἐπιβαλὼν ἔκλαιεν, when he thought thereon (sc. τ. ῥήματι), he wept (EV, txt.; R, mg., he began to weep; cf. M, Pr., 131): Mrk.14:72 (see also Swete, in l);
__(b) to fall to one's share: τὸ ἐπιβάλλον (sc. dative; Hdt., a1., a technical formula frequently in π.; Deiss., BS, 230, LAE, 152), Luk.15:12.†
(AS)

---

LSJ / STEPBible (TFLSJ)
ἐπιβάλλω:

__I
. transitive, throw or cast upon, θριξὶ.., ἃς ἐπέβαλλον (i.e. πυρί) [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 23.135; ἐπὶ δὲ χλαῖναν βάλεν αὐτῷ 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 14.520, compare 4.440; ἑωυτὸν ἐς τὸ πῦρ variant in 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 7.107; φάρη κόραις 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Electra” 1221]] (Lyric poetry); ἐ. [Refs 5th c.BC+ [τινὰς ἐπὶ ἁμάξας 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 4.48, compare 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 4.75, 5.112; ἐπιβάλλοντας (i.e. χοῦν)]] throwing on more and more, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 2.76.]]

__I.2
. lay on, [ἡμιόνοις] ἐπέβαλλεν [Refs 8th c.BC+ [ἱμάσθλην 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 6.320; ἐ. πληγάς τινι Xenophon Historicus [{5-6th c.BC}] “Respublica Lacedaemoniorum” 2.8]]; Ζεὺς ἐπὶ χεῖρα [Refs 5th c.BC+ [βάλοι Aeschylus Tragicus [{4-5th c.BC}] “Choephori” 395 (Lyric poetry), compare 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Nu.” 933 (_anapaest meter_); ἐ.τὴν χεῖρά τινι [prev\. author] “Lys.” 440]] (but τῷ καρπῷ τοῦ νοσοῦντος τὴν χεῖρα, of feeling the pulse, [NT+2nd c.BC+ [2nd c.AD: Galenus Medicus 18(2).40; so τὴν ἁφήν [prev\. author] 8.821, 4th c.AD(?): Marcellinus Biographus “Puls.” 119); τὰς χεῖρας τοῖς κατ᾽ Αἴγαιον 2nd c.BC: Polybius Historicus 3.2.8; Ῥωμαίοις [prev\. author] 18.51.8; ἐπί τινα NT.Matt.26.50]]; impose as a tax tribute, [LXX+5th c.BC+ [τινί τι 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.106, 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 8.108; as a fine or penalty, ζημίην, φυγὴν ἐ. τινί, 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 6.92 (_passive_), 7.3; ἀργύριον 5th c.BC: Lysias Orator 9.6; ἐπιβολάς [prev\. author] 20.14, compare 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Ath.” 61.2; λύτρα Vetus Testamentum Graece redditum LXX.Exo.21.30]] (passive); inflict, θνατοῖς ἐ. ἀνάλγητα, λύπην, etc., [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Tr.” 128 (Lyric poetry), 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Medea” 1115 (_anapaest meter_), etc.]]

__I.3
. ἐ. σφρηγῖδα, δακτύλιον, affix a seal, [Refs 6th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 3.128, 2.38; σφραγῖδ᾽ ἐπί τι Aristophanes Comicus [{5-6th c.BC}] “Aves” 559]]; σύμβολόν τινι [Refs [[prev. work] 1215.]]

__I.4
. add, contribute, μικρὸν [ἀληθεία] [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Metaphorical” 993b2; ἐ. ἐπὶ τὸ ὕδωρ Theophrastus Philosophus [{4-3rd c.BC}] “de Igne” 49]]; νέον [φῶς] [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Cra.” 409b: _metaphorically_]], throw in, mention, τι uncertain in [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “El.” 1246 (Lyric poetry) (in _middle_, χαίρειν τεοῖς προθύροις ἐπιβάλλομαι 3rd c.BC: Theocritus Poeta Bucolicus 23.27); Φαῖστος.. ἐπιβάλλων φησί Scholia 5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “P.” 4.28: _absolutely_]], bid higher, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Pol.” 1259a14.]]

__I.5
. place next in order, [Refs 2nd c.BC+ [2nd c.BC: Polybius Historicus 1.26.15.]]

__I.6
. let grow, [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [κλήματα Theophrastus Philosophus [{4-3rd c.BC}] “Historia Plantarum” 4.13.5]]; βλαστούς [Refs [[prev. work] 3.5.1.]]

__I.7
. let loose, [Refs 1st c.BC+ [πρόβατα ἐπὶ κνῆκον “PRyl.” 69.6 (1st c.BC).]]

__I.8
. causal of [Refs 5th c.BC+ [ἐπιβαίνω Aeschylus Tragicus [{4-5th c.BC}] 111.3, 1st-2nd c.AD: Dio Chrysostomus Sophista 7.134.]]

__II
. throw oneself upon, go straight towards, with accusative, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [ἡ δὲ Φεὰς ἐπέβαλλεν 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 15.297]]: later with dative loci, [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [2nd c.BC: Polybius Historicus 5.18.3, 1st c.BC: Diodorus Siculus Historicus 1.30, 3rd c.AD: Plotinus Philosophus 3.7.12, etc.; νήσοις 3rd c.BC: Rhianus Epicus 39]]; εἰς Ιταλίαν, ἐπὶ τὸν τόπον, [Refs 2nd c.BC+ [2nd c.BC: Polybius Historicus 2.24.17, 5.6.6, compare “PAmh.” 2.31.5 (2nd c.BC), etc.]]

__II.2
. fall upon, ὅπου ἂν ὁ ἥλιος ἐ. [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “HA” 598a3]]; especially in hostile sense, set upon, c.dative, [Refs 1st c.BC+ [[prev. work] 623b1, etc.; τοῖσ᾽ Αρβήλοις 1st c.BC: Diodorus Siculus Historicus 17.64]]: absolutely, [Refs 1st c.AD+ [ἐ.ληστρικῷ τρόπῳ “PRyl.” 127.10 (1st c.AD); ἐπιβάλλουσαι]] jostling, trampling, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Phdr.” 248a; obscene meaning, 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Av.” 1216.]]

__II.3
. (i.e. τὸν νοῦν) set to a thing, devote oneself to it, with dative, [Refs 1st c.BC+ [2nd c.AD: Marcus Antoninus Imperator 10.30; τοῖς αὐλοῖς 1st c.BC: Diodorus Siculus Historicus 3.59; τοῖς κοινοῖς πράγμασιν Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus [{1-2nd c.AD}] “Cicero” 4]] (in full τὴν διάνοιαν ἐ. πρός τι [Refs 1st c.BC+ [1st c.BC: Diodorus Siculus Historicus 20.43)]]: generally, give one's attention to, think on, NT.Mark.14.72.

__II.3.b
. apprehend, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-3rd c.BC: Epicurus Philosophus “fragment” 423]]; attain by intuition, c.dative, [Refs 5th c.AD+ [5th-6th c.AD: Damascius Philosophus “Pr.” 54.]]

__II.4
. fall in one's way, ὅταν ἐπιβάλλῃ περὶ τῆς τοιαύτης [Refs 4th c.BC+ [πολιτείας ἡ σκέψις 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Politica” 1266a25; κατὰ τὸν ἐπιβάλλοντα λόγον [prev\. author] “GA” 716a3]].

__II.5
. follow, come next, [Refs 2nd c.BC+ [2nd c.BC: Polybius Historicus 11.23.2; τισί Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus [{1-2nd c.AD}] “Aemilius Paulus” 33]]; ἐφ᾽ ὃν ἐπιβαλὼν ἔφη said thereupon, [Refs 2nd c.BC+ [2nd c.BC: Polybius Historicus 1.80.1]]; interrupt, [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [ἀποκρινομένῳ Theophrastus Philosophus [{4-3rd c.BC}] “Characteres” 7.2]].

__II.6
. belong to, fall to the share of, μόριον [Refs 5th c.BC+ [ὅσον αὐτοῖσι ἐπέβαλλε 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 7.23, compare 4th-3rd c.BC: Diphilus Comicus 43.16; εἰ μὴ τὸ ὅλον, μέρος γε, ἐπιβάλλει τῆς βλασφημίας ἅπασι 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 18.272; ὅσον ἐπιβάλλει αὐτοῖς 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Politica” 1260a19]]; ἑκάστῳ τῆς εὐδαιμονίας ἐπιβάλλει τοσοῦτον ὅσονπερ ἀρετῆς [Refs [[prev. work] 1323b21; τῶν κτημάτων τὸ ἐπιβάλλον (i.e. μέρος)]] the portion that falls to one, [NT+5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 4.115, cf. LXX.Tob.3.17, 6.12; so τὸ ἐ. ἐφ᾽ ἡμᾶς μέρος 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 18.254; τὸ ἐ. μέρος τῆς οὐσίας NT.Luke.15.12, compare “PGrenf.” 1.33.33 (2nd c.BC)]], etc.; fall due, of payments, [Refs 2nd c.BC+ [“PLond.” 1.3.21 (2nd c.BC); τόκον ὃν ἔφη ἐπιβάλλειν αὑτῷ]] which was payable by him, [Refs 2nd c.BC+ [“BCH” 6.21 (Delos, 2nd c.BC).]]

__II.6.b
. participle ἐπιβάλλων, in Law, next-of-kin, ὁ ἐ., οἱ ἐ., [Refs [“Leg.Gort.” 7.36, 11.42, +others]]

__II.7
. impersonal with accusative et infinitive, τοὺς Δελφοὺς δὴ ἐπέβαλλε.. παρασχεῖν it concerned them to provide, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 2.180: or with _dative_]] et infinitive, [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [ἐπιβάλλει τινὶ ποιεῖν τι 3rd c.BC: Chrysippus Stoicus 2.39, +others, 2nd c.BC: Polybius Historicus 18.51.1; ἐπιβάλλοντος ἡμῖν εὐεργετικοῖς εἶναι 1st c.AD: Cornutus Philosophus “de Natura Deorum” 15]]; κοινῇ πᾶσιν [Refs 2nd c.BC+ [ἐπιβάλλει “UPZ” 112.10 (2nd c.BC); καθότι ἐπέβαλλεν ἀνδρὶ καλῷ καὶ ἀγαθῷ “IG” 12(7).231.5 (from Amorgos)]]: frequently in participle, ἐπιβάλλουσαν ἡγεῖσθαι τὴν στρατείαν τινί incumbent upon.., [Refs 4th c.BC+ [3rd c.BC: Teles Philosophus p.61 H.; τὸ ἐπιβάλλον 4th-3rd c.BC: Cleanthes Stoicus 1.128, 2nd c.AD: Arrianus Historicus “Epict.” 2.11.3, etc.; τὰς -ούσας τάσεις τῆς φωνῆς 3rd c.BC: Chrysippus Stoicus 2.96]]; τὸ τῇ φύσει ἐ. [Refs [Antip.Stoic. 3.255]]; appropriate, ὑποδοχαί Teles[Refs 4th c.AD+ [p.41 H.; ἰήματα “IG” 22.1121.15; ἁρμονία 4th c.AD: Iamblichus Philosophus “Comm.” “in Mathematics texts” 30; ἡ στέρησις ἐπιβάλλοντός ἐστι παρεῖναι εἴδους τινός]] a specific form which ought to be present, [Refs 3rd c.AD+ [3rd c.AD: Plotinus Philosophus 1.8.11.]]

__II.8
. shut to, close, of the larynx, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “PA” 664b26.]]

__II.9
. in Logic, λόγοι ἐπιβάλλοντες, -όμενοι, overlapping and overlapped, of syllogisms in a sorites, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [3rd c.BC: Chrysippus Stoicus 2.85; so of Time, ἐπέβαλε τοῖς χρόνοις Ἰουλιανῷ Eunapius Historicus [{4-5th c.AD}] “Vitae Sophistarum” p.497 5th c.BC: Bacchylides Lyricus:]] —middle, [Refs [γηραιῷ τῷ Κυρηναίῳ ἐπεβάλετο Anonymus “Intr.Arat.” p.326M.]]

__II.10
. in Alchemy, make a `projection' (compare ἐπιβολή), Syn.Alch.p.68B.

__III
. middle, mostly like the intransitive usages, but also:

__III.1
. with genitive, throw oneself upon, desire eagerly, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [ἐνάρων ἐπιβαλλόμενος 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 6.68; παρθενίας ἐπιβάλλομαι Sappho Lyrica [{7-6th c.BC}] 102; τοῦ εὖ ζῆν ἐπιβάλλονται 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Politica” 1258a3]].

__III.2
. with accusative, put upon oneself, ἐπιβαλλομέναν [Refs 5th c.BC+ [.. πλόκον ἀνθέων 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Med.” 840]]; ἐπιβάλλεσθαι put on more wraps, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-3rd c.BC: Theophrastus Philosophus “Char.” 2.10 (cf. IV. 1); ὕπνον ἡδὺν -όμενος Dio Chrysostomus Sophista [{1-2nd c.AD}] 12.51]]: metaphorically, take possession of, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [καὶ ἐπὶ κλήρους ἐβάλοντο 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 14.209]]; αὐθαίρετον δουλείαν ἐπιβαλεῖται will take upon himself, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 6.40.]]

__III.2.b
. of trees, make fresh growth, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-3rd c.BC: Theophrastus Philosophus “HP” 3.5.1.]]

__III.3
. c.accusative, also, attempt, undertake, [Refs 6th c.BC+ [ἔργον Plato Philosophus [{5-6th c.BC}] “Sophista” 264b, “Ti.” 48c; μέθοδον 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Politica” 1260b36]]: c.infinitive, Decrees cited in [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 18.164, 4th-3rd c.BC: Zeno Citieus Stoicus 1.68, 2nd c.BC: Polybius Historicus 1.43.2, etc.: _absolutely_, πολλῶν -ημένων]] though many have made the attempt, [Refs 2nd c.BC+ [2nd c.BC: Agatharchides Geographus 76.]]

__III.4
. with dative, put one's hand to, [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [ἐχέτλῃ “AP” 7.650 (3rd c.BC: Phalaecus Epigrammaticus (?)): _metaphorically_]], apply or devote oneself to, [Refs 2nd c.BC+ [τόλμῃ καὶ πράξει 2nd c.BC: Polybius Historicus 5.81.1; ἐγχειρήματι μεγάλῳ 1st c.BC: Dionysius Halicarnassensis 5.25]], etc.

__III.5
. arrive at, [πολίεσσι] [Refs 1st c.BC+ [Callias Epigrammaticus “Del.” 68; ὅταν ἐπὶ τοὺς χρόνους ἐπιβαλώμεθα 1st c.BC: Diodorus Siculus Historicus 19.55]].

__III.6
. ἐπὶ πᾶσι -εβάλοντο brought up the rear, [Refs [[prev\. author] 18.33.]]

__IV
. in passive, lie upon, be put upon, ἐπιβεβλημένοι τοξόται archers with their arrows on the string, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “An.” 4.3.28, compare 5.2.12; λάσιον ἐπιβεβλημένος]] having a rough cloak on, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Theopompus Comicus 36]]; τὸ ἐν ψύχει κεῖσθαι -ημένον [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Hippocrates Medicus “ἐπιδημίαι” 2.3.1, compare 6.4.14; διφθέραν -ημένη Dio Chrysostomus Sophista [{1-2nd c.AD}] 5.25]].

__IV.2
. to be set over, [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [ὁ τελώνης ὁ ἐπιβεβλημένος τῷ Ζεύγματι Philostratus Sophista [{2-3rd c.AD}] “Vita Apollonii” 1.20]].

__IV.3
. Rhet., ornate (see. ἐπιβολή), ἰδέα λόγων οὔτ᾽ ἐπιβεβλημένη [Refs [οὔτ᾽ αὖος [prev\. author] “VS” 1.20.2]].

Abbott-Smith / STEPBible (TBESG)
ἐπί-βλημα, -τος, τό
[in LXX: Isa.3:22 * ;]
__1. that which is thrown over, a cover.

found only in the phrase ἄρτος ἐ., EV, daily; R, mg., for the coming day: Mat.6:11, Luk.11:3. (Several derivations find support, each pointing to a different meaning.

(σκοπός, a watcher), [in LXX for פָּקַד, its parts and derivatives, Num.4:16 31:14, Jdg.9:28, 4Ki.11:15 11:18, 2Ch.34:12 34:17, Neh.11:9, 14 11:22; אֵל, Job.20:29; נָגַשׂ:, Isa.60:17; Wis.1:6, 1Ma.1:51 * ;]
a superintendent, guardian, overseer (cl.; for exx. see LS, see word): Act.20:28, 1Pe.2:25 (ICC, in l); as technical term for a religious office (Deiss., BS, 230 f.), in later Paul. epp. of the head of a church (Vg. episcopus), a bishop: Php.1:1, 1Ti.3:2, Tit.1:7 (see reff. see word ἐπισκοπή).†

ἐπίσκοπ-ος, ὁ,

__A
(σκοπός 1) one who watches over, overseer, guardian, ἦ γὰρ ὄλωλας ἐπίσκοπος, ὅς τέ μιν αὐτὴν ῥύσκευ (i.e. τὴν πόλιν), of Hector, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 24.729, ἐ... ὁδαίων 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 8.163]]; ἐπίσκοποι ἁρμονιάων watchers over compacts, of the gods, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 22.255; νεκροῦ 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Antigone” 217; σῆς ἕδρας [prev. author] “OC” 112]]; ἐ. ὀϊστῶν, of an archer, variant in [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [3rd c.BC: Theocritus Poeta Bucolicus 24.107]]; in education, tutor, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Leges” 795d; ἐ. σωφροσύνης καὶ ὕβρεως [prev. work] 849a: with _dative_, ἀγυιαῖς ἔσσῃ καὶ λιμένεσσιν ἐ. 3rd c.BC: Callimachus Epicus “Hymnus in Dianam” 39]]; especially of tutelary gods (compare ἐπισκοπέὠ, Παλλὰς ἐ. [Refs 6th c.BC+ [6th c.BC: Solon Lyricus 4.3; Δίκη 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Leges” 872e; Κλειὼ ἐ. χερνίβων 4th-5th c.BC: Simonides Lyricus 45]]; Χάριτες Μινυᾶν ἐ. [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “O.” 14.3; θεοὶ ἐ. ἀγορᾶς 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Septem contra Thebas” 272]]; πατρῴων δωμάτων ἐ. [Refs [[prev. author] “Ch.” 126]]; τὸ δεινὸν.. φρενῶν ἐπίσκοπον guardian of the mind, [Refs [[prev. author] “Eu.” 518 (Lyric poetry)]]; νυχίων φθεγμάτων ἐ., of Bacchus, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Antigone” 1148 (lyr); Ἐρινύες “IG” 12(9).1179.33 (Euboea, 2nd c.AD)]]; [Χριστὸς] ἐ. τῶν ψυχῶν [NT+5th c.BC+ [NT.1Pet.2.25: rarely with _dative_, πᾶσι γὰρ ἐ. ἐτάχθη.. Νέμεσις 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Leges” 717d.]]

__A.2
. scout, watch, c.dative, ἐ. Τρώεσσι, νήεσσιν ἡμετέρῃσιν, one set to watch them, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 10.38, 342.]]

ἐπι-σπάω, -ῶ
[in LXX: Isa.5:18 (מָשַׁךְ), etc. ;]
to draw on: mid., in peculiar sense of effacing signs of Judaism (cf. 1Ma.1:15, FlJ, Ant., xii, 5, i; see Thayer, see word), to become as uncircumcised: 1Co.7:18.†

LSJ / STEPBible (TFLSJ)
ἐπι-σπάω,
draw or drag after one, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 2.121.δ]]; ἦγ᾽ ἐπισπάσας κόμης by the hair, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Helena” 116, compare “Tr.” 882, “Andr.” 710]]:— middle, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 4.7.14:]] —passive, ἐπισπασθῆναι τῇ χειρί with the hand, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 4.130.]]

__2
. metaphorically, bring on, cause, τοσόνδε πλῆθος πημάτων [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Persae” 477.]]

__3
. pull to, τὴν θύραν [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Historia Graeca (Hellenica)” 6.4.36]]; compare ἐπισπαστήρ: ἐπισπασθέντος τοῦ βρόχου being drawn tight, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 24.139.]]

__4
. attract, gain, win, πέποιθα τοῦτ᾽ ἐπισπάσειν κλέος [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Ajax” 769]]:—frequently in middle, ἐπισπᾶσθαι κέρδος [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 3.72; εὔνοιαν 2nd c.BC: Polybius Historicus 3.98.9; χάριν “SIG” 685.40 (5th c.BC: Magnes Comicus Mae., 2nd c.BC)]]; ἔχθραν [Refs 6th c.AD+ [“Anthologia Graeca” 11.340 (6th c.AD: Palladas Epigrammaticus)]]; welcome, [Refs 1st c.AD+ [1st c.AD: Philo Judaeus 1.384]]; ἐπισπᾶσθαι πώγωνα get one a beard, [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd c.AD: Lucianus Sophista “JTr.” 16]]; induce, ὕπνον ἐκπώμασιν [Refs 4th c.AD+ [4th c.AD: Libanius Sophista “Orationes” 56.26]]; attract, σίδηρον [Refs 1st c.BC+ [1st c.BC: Philodemus Philosophus “περὶ σημείων καὶ σημειώσεων” 1.]]

__5
. draw on, allure, persuade, τὴν ψυχήν [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Cratylus” 420a]]:—middle, ὁ λόγος.. ἂν ἐπισπάσαιτο [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 3.44, compare 5.111]]; ἐ. ἡ πέρδιξ [τὸν θηρεύοντα] [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Historia Animalium” 613b19]]; θάτερον παρεμπῖπτον ἐπεσπάσατο.. τὸ ἕτερον ἐπινόημα induced, provoked, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-3rd c.BC: Epicurus Philosophus “De rerum natura - Wien. Stud.” 137]] G.: c.infinitive, induce to do, ἐπισπάσασθαι [ἂν] αὐτοὺς ἡγεῖτο προθυμήσεσθαι he thought it would induce, invite them to make the venture, uncertain reading in [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 4.9]]; ἐπισπᾶσθαί τινα ἐμπλησθῆναι δακρύων τὰ ὄμματα [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 5.5.10; ἐ. τοὺσπολεμίους ἐφ᾽ ἑαυτόν 1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus “Philopoemen” 18, compare “Mar.” 11, 21, 26]]; but τοὺς πολεμίους εἰς τόπους allure, entice, [Refs 2nd c.BC+ [2nd c.BC: Polybius Historicus 3.110.2, etc.:]] —passive, ἐπισπώμενον εἰς τἀναντία πολλάκις ἅμα though often he is being drawn in opposite directionsatonce, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Leges” 863e]]; φοβοῦμαι μὴ πάντες.. ἐπισπασθῶσιν πέρα τοῦ συμφέροντος [πολεμῆσαι] [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 5.19; πολύ τι μᾶλλον ἐπεσπάσμεθα “OGI” 223.18 (3rd c.BC)]]; ἐπεσπάσθην φιλονεικεῖν [Refs 2nd c.BC+ [2nd c.BC: Demetrius Lacon Philosophus “Herc.” 1055.23F.]]

__6
. middle, absorb, τὰ σιτία -σπᾶται τὴν ὑγρότητα [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Problemata” 868b30; τὰ ἐριναστὰ [σῦκα] ἐ. τὸν ὀπόν 4th-3rd c.BC: Theophrastus Philosophus “de Causis Plantarum” 2.9.12]]; quaff, of a drinker, ἀπνευστὶ ἐ. [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd c.AD: Galenus Medicus 15.500, compare 2nd c.AD: Lucianus Sophista “DDeor.” 5.4]]; of infants, suck, γάλα [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd c.AD: Soranus Medicus 1.88]]; of cupping instruments, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Hippocrates Medicus “περὶ ἀρχαίης ἰητρικῇς” 22]]; draw in, πνεῦμα [Refs 1st c.BC+ [1st c.BC: Philodemus Gadarensis Epigrammaticus “D.” 3.13]]:—passive, of air, to be sucked in, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Problemata” 931b22.]]

__7
. middle, draw in, call in, Πύρρον [Refs 2nd c.BC+ [2nd c.BC: Polybius Historicus 1.6.5]]; φυλακὴν καὶ βοήθειαν παρά τινος[Refs 1st c.BC+ [[prev. work] 7.6; μάρτυρας -ᾶται τοὺς μουσικούς 1st c.BC: Philodemus Philosophus “περὶ ποιημάτων” 5.1425.8]]:—passive, to be called in, forced to work, εἴς τι [Refs 2nd c.BC+ [“PTeb.” 27.4 (2nd c.BC).]]

__8
. in passive, of the sea, ἐπισπωμένη βιαιότερον returning with a rush after having retired, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 3.89.]]

__II
. overturn: hence proverbial, ὅλην τὴν ἅμαξαν ἐπεσπάσω you have `upset the apple-cart', [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd c.AD: Lucianus Sophista “Pseudol.” 32.]]

__III
. middle, draw the prepuce forward, become as if uncircumcised, μὴ ἐπισπάσθω [NT.1Cor.7.18]; of the nurse, ἐπισπάσθω τὴν ἀκροποσθίαν [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd c.AD: Soranus Medicus 1.113.]]

ἐπίσταμαι
(prob. an old mid, of ἐφίστημι, which see), [in LXX chiefly for יָדַע ;]
to know, know of, understand: with accusative of person(s), Act.19:15; with ptcp., Act.24:10; with accusative of thing(s), Mrk.14:68, Act.18:25, 1Ti.6:4, Jas.4:14, Ju 10; before περί, Act.26:26; ὅτι, Act.15:7 19:25 22:19; ὡς, Act.10:28; πῶς, Act.20:18; ποῦ, Heb.11:8.†

LSJ / STEPBible (TFLSJ)
ἐπίστᾰμαι, 2
person -ασαι[Refs 6th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Prometheus Vinctus” 376, 982, 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Electra” 629, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Euthydemus” 296a, but ἐπίστᾳ 5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “P.” 3.80, 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Eumenides” 86, 581, ἐπίστῃ 6th c.BC: Theognis Elegiacus 1085, “PCair.Zen.” 41.19 (3rd c.BC), _Ionic dialect_ ἐπίστεαι ἐξ-) 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 7.135; _imperative_ ἐπίστασο [prev. work] 29, 209, 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Prometheus Vinctus” 840, 967, “PCair.Zen.” 57.4 (3rd c.BC), etc., but ἐπίσταο variant in 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 7.209]], contraction ἐπίστω [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Tyrannus” 658, etc.]]; subjunctive Ionic dialect ἐπιστέωμαι [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 3.134]], Attic dialect ἐπίστωμαι [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Euthydemus” 296a]]: imperfect ἠπιστάμην [Refs 8th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Prometheus Vinctus” 267, etc.; without augment ἐπίστατο 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 5.60: 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus has ἐπ- 5.42 (variant ἠπ-), ἠπ- 3.139]]; Ionic dialect 3rd.pers. plural ἠπιστέατο or ἐπιστέατο [Refs [8.132]]: future ἐπιστήσομαι [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 21.320, etc.]]: aorist 1 ἠπιστήθην [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 3.15, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Leges” 687a.]]

__I
. know how to do, be able to do, capable of doing, c.infinitive, οὐδέ οἱ ὀστέ᾽ ἐπιστήσονται Ἀχαιοὶ ἀλλέξαι [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 21.320, compare 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 13.207, 7th-6th c.BC: Sappho Lyrica 70, etc.: 8th c.BC: Homerus Epicus has it both of intellectual power, ὅς τις ἐπίσταιτο ᾗσι φρεσὶν ἄρτια βάζειν 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 14.92; ἐπιστάμεναι σάφα θυμῷ 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 4.730]]; and of artistic skill, ὃς χερσὶν ἐπίστατο δαίδαλα πάντα τεύχειν [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 5.60]]: frequently in Trag. and Attic dialect, οὔπω σωφρονεῖν ἐπίστασαι [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Prometheus Vinctus” 982, compare 1032, 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Tyrannus” 589; πένεσθαι δ᾽ οὐκ ἐ. δόμος 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Agamemnon” 962; ἐ... θεοὺς σέβειν 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Hippolytus” 996, cf. Alcaeus566]]; κιθαρίζειν οὐκ ἐ. [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Vespae” 989, compare 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Symposium” 223d, “R.” 420e, +others: without]]infinitive, σῷζ ὅπως ἐπίστασαι as best you can, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Prometheus Vinctus” 376, compare “Eu.” 581.]]

__I.2
. to be assured, feel sure that.., τοῦτον ἐπίστανται πλεῖστα εἰδέναι [Refs 5th c.BC+ [1st c.AD(?): Heraclitus 57, compare 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 3.134, 139, 6.139, +others: followed by ὡς, [prev. author] 1.122.]]

__II
. with accusative, understand a matter, know, be versed in or acquainted with, πολλὰ δ᾽ ἐπίστατο ἔργα [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 23.705, compare 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 2.117; Μουσέων δῶρον 7th c.BC: Archilochus Lyricus 1; τὴν τέχνην 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 3.130; τὸ μέλλον 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Persae” 373; ἐμπειρίᾳ ἐ. τὴν ναυτικήν 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 4.10; τὰς φύσεις ὑμῶν [prev. author] 7.14; πάσας τὰς δημιουργίας 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 598c]]; ἔγωγε γράμματ᾽ οὐδ᾽ ἐ. [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Cratinus Comicus 122]]; τὸ μὴ ἐ. γράμματα illiteracy, [Refs 1st c.BC+ [“PRyl.” 73.19 (1st c.BC), etc.]]; ἐ. ἱερατικὰ καὶ Αἰγύπτια γράμματα [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [“PTeb.” 291.41 (2nd c.AD)]]; ἐ. μύθους τοὺς Αἰσώπου know them by heart, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Phaedo” 61b, compare “Grg.” 484b: also with an]] adverb, Συριστὶ ἐ. know Syrian, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 7.5.31]]; with accusative and infinitive conjoined, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Eumenides” 276]]; with infinitive to explanation the accusative, ἔργον δὲ μοῦνον ἐσθίειν ἐ. [Refs 7th c.BC+ [7th-6th c.BC(?): Semonides Iambographus 7.24, compare 7th c.BC: Archilochus Lyricus 65.]]

__II.2
. after [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Homerus Epicus]], know as a fact, know for certain, ἐπισταμένοισι εὖ οὐκ ἄν τις λέγοι [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 7.8.ά, etc.]]; used convertibly with εἰδέναι, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Theaetetus” 163b, 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Analytica Priora” 66b31, “Ph.” 184a10]]; even χάριν ἐ., ={χάριν εἰδέναι}, [Refs 4th c.AD+ [4th c.AD: Julianus Imperator “Orationes” 8.246c (but sometimes εἰδέναι is general, ἐπίστασθαι]] being confined to scientific knowledge (ἐπιστήμη), διὰ τὸ εἰδέναι τὸ ἐπίστασθαι ἐδίωκον [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Metaphysica” 982b21): frequently strengthened, εὖ ἐ]]. Hdt.[same place]; σαφῶς ἐ. [Refs 6th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Prometheus Vinctus” 840, etc.: most frequently with _accusative_, τὰ διαφέροντα ἐ. 5th-6th c.BC: Andocides Orator 4.19, etc.; also ἐ. περί τινος 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 2.3, 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 6.60; περὶ θεῶν 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Fragmenta” 795.4: followed by a dependent clause, τί σφιν χρήσηται ἐ. 6th c.BC: Theognis Elegiacus 772]]; ἐ. ὅτι.., or ἐ. τοῦτο, ὅτι.., [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.3, 156, etc.; ὡς.. 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Persae” 599; τοῦτ᾽ ἐπίστασ᾽, ὡς 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Ajax” 1370; ἐ. αὐτὸν οἷς ψωμίζεται 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Equites” 715, etc.]]

__II.3
. rarely, know a person, Ἀρίγνωτον γὰρ οὐδεὶς ὅστις οὐκ ἐ. [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Equites” 1278, compare 1st c.AD: Musonius Philosophus “fragment” 3p.12H., 2nd c.AD: Lucianus Sophista “Asin.” 1]]; τὸν Ἰησοῦν γινώσκω καὶ τὸν Παῦλον ἐ. [NT.Act.19.15]; but ὁ παῖς τοὺς τεκόντας οὐκ ἐ. does not know who they are, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Ion” 51.]]

__III
. with participle, in Prose and Trag., know that one is, has, etc., εὖ ἐ. αὐτὸς σχήσων [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 5.42; ἐσθλὸς ὢν ἐπίστασο 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Ajax” 1399, compare 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 2.44]]; also ὡς ὧδ᾽ ἐχόντων τῶνδ᾽ ἐ. σε χρή [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Ajax” 281]]; ὡς φανέν γε τοὔπος ὧδ᾽ ἐ. [Refs 1st c.AD+ [[prev. author] “OT” 848: with double _accusative_, ἑαυτοὺς Φαυστύλου ἠπιστάμεθα παῖδας (i.e. ὄντας) 1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus “Romulus” 7]]: c.accusative et infinitive, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Antigone” 1092, 5th c.BC: Lysias Orator “Fragmenta” 53.1.]]

__IV
. present participle ἐπιστάμενος, η, ον, frequently as adjective, knowing, understanding, skilful, ἀνδρὸς ἐ. [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 14.359; χαλεπὸν ἐ. περ ἐόντι 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 19.80]]; καὶ μάλ᾽ ἐ. [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 13.313]]; even of a dancer's feet, θρέξασκον ἐπισταμένοισι πόδεσσι [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 18.599: also with _genitive_, φόρμιγγος ἐ. καὶ ἀοιδῆς]] skilled, versed in them, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 21.406: and with _dative_, ἄκοντι 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 15.282: hence,]]

__IV.2
. adverb ἐπιστᾰμένως skilfully, expertly,[Refs 8th c.BC+ [7.317, 8th-7th c.BC: Hesiodus Epicus “Theogonia” 87, etc.]]; εὖ καὶ ἐ. ἐπιτίθημι,
passive mostly furnished by ἐπίκειμαι: active, lay, put or place upon, of offerings laid on the altar, ἐπὶ μηρία θέντες Ἀπόλλωνι [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 21.267, compare 3.179; λιβανωτόν 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Nubes” 426, “V.” 96, 5th c.BC: Antipho Orator 1.18]]; set meats on the table, εἴδατα πόλλ᾽ ἐπιθεῖσα [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 1.140, compare 10.355]]; πάντ᾽ ἐπιθεῖτε on the car, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 24.264; [νέκυας] ἐπὶ νηυσὶ τιθέντες 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 24.419]]; τινὶ κύρτον καὶ κώπαν, as a grave-monument, [Refs 7th c.BC+ [“Anthologia Graeca” 7.505 (= 7th-6th c.BC: Sappho Lyrica 120): Constr. mostly ἐ. τινί τι, τῷ ἰσχυροτέρῳ πλέον βάρος 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Oeconomicus” 17.9, etc.]]: but also c.genitive, ἐ. λεχέων τινά [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 24.589; ἐ. τι ἐπί τινος 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 2.121.δ᾽]]; κεφαλὴν ἐπὶ στέρνα τινός [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 7.3.14]]: with accusative only, put upon, set up, ἐ. φάρμακα apply salves, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 4.190; δέελον δ᾽ ἐπὶ σῆμά τ᾽ ἔθηκε 10.466; στήλην λίθου 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 7.183; φάκελον ξύλων 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Cyclops” 243]]; ἐ. μνημεῖά τινι to him, [Refs [[prev. author] “IT” 702, compare “IG” 14.446 (from Tauromenium), 12.1068.]]

__2
set upon, turn towards, Ἑκτορέοις ἐπὶ φρένα θῆχ᾽ ἱεροῖσιν [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 10.46]]; but τῇ δ᾽ ἄρ᾽ ἐπὶ φρεσὶ θῆκε with infinitive, put it into her mind to.., [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 21.1.]]

__II
put on a covering or lid, ὡς εἴ τε φαρέτρῃ πῶμ᾽ ἐπιθείη [Refs [9.314; κεφαλῇ ἐπέθηκε (as variant for{ἐφύπερθἐ καλύπτρην} 5.232]]; λίθον δ᾽ ἐπέθηκε θύρῃσι, i.e. put a stone as a door to the cave, put it before the door, [Refs [13.370]]; also, put a door to, κολλητὰς ἐπέθηκα θύρας [Refs 5th c.BC+ [23.194; θύρας ἐπέθηκε φαεινάς 21.45; θυρεὸν μέγαν 9.240 (see. below 5th c.BC: Bacchylides Lyricus 11).]]

__II.2
set a seal on, [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [“BGU” 361 iii 22 (2nd c.AD)]]; apply a pessary, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Hippocrates Medicus “Steril.” 214 (_passive_)]]; a cupping instrument, [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd c.AD: Soranus Medicus 2.11 (_passive_).]]

__III
put to, add, grant or give besides, ὅσσα τε νῦν ὔμμ᾽ ἐστὶ καὶ εἴ ποθεν ἄλλ᾽ ἐπιθεῖτε [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 22.62, compare 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 7.364, etc.; κράτος, κῦδός τινι, 1.509 (tmesis), 23.400 (tmesis), 406 (tmesis); ἡμιτάλαντον χρυσοῦ [prev. work] 796.]]

__III.2
of Time, add, bring on, ἕβδομον ἦμαρ ἐπὶ Ζεὺς θῆκε [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 12.399; μάλα πολλὰ [ἔτεα] 8th-7th c.BC: Hesiodus Epicus “Opera et Dies” 697.]]

__IV
put on as a finish, χρυσέην ἐπέθηκε κορώνην [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 4.111; περόνην 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 19.256: _metaphorically_, οὐδὲ τέλος μύθῳ ἐπιθήσεις]] add fulfilment, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 19.107, compare 20.369; so later ἐ. κεφάλαἰ ἐφ᾽ ἅπασι 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 21.18; κολοφῶνα ἐ. τῇ σοφίᾳ 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Euthydemus” 301e]]; τέλος ἐπιτεθήκατον[Refs 4th c.BC+ [[prev. work] 272a; πέρας ἐ. τῇ γενέσει 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “de Generatione Animalium” 776a4; πίστιν ἐ. 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 12.22, 49.42; ὁ δὲ μισθωσάμενος πίστιν ἐπιθήσει πρὸς τοὺς νεωποίας “SIG” 963.34 (Arcesine, 4th c.BC)]]; πέρας ἐ. τῷ πράγματι [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [“PGiss.” 25.7 (2nd c.AD)]], etc.; ὅρον ἐ. τῷ πράγματι Mitteis [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [“Chr.” 87.2 (2nd c.AD).]]

__V
impose, inflict a penalty, σοὶ δέ, γέρον, θωὴν ἐπιθήσομεν [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 2.192]]; δίκην, ζημίην, ἄποινα ἐ. τινί, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.120, 144, 9.120, etc.; θάνατον δίκην ἐ. τινί 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Leges” 838c; δίκην τὴν πρέπουσαν [prev. author] “Criti.” 106b; ἔργων ἀντ᾽ ἀδίκων χαλεπὴν ἐ. ἀμοιβήν 8th-7th c.BC: Hesiodus Epicus “Opera et Dies” 334; τιμωρίαν ὑπέρ τινος 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 60.11 (compare below 5th c.BC: Bacchylides Lyricus IV)]]: so of burdens, grievances, etc., θήσειν..ἐπ᾽ ἄλγεα Τρωσί [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 2.39; οἷσιν ἐπὶ Ζεὺς θῆκε κακὸν μόρον 6.357; [ἄτην] οἱ ἐπὶ φρεσὶθῆκε..Ἐρινύς 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 15.234]]; ἀνάγκην ἐ. with infinitive, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Respublica Lacedaemoniorum” 10.7]]; ἐ...μὴ τυγχάνειν imposing as a penalty not to.., [Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. work] 3.3 (see. below 5th c.BC: Bacchylides Lyricus IV).]]

__VI
dispatch a letter, ἐ. τι ἐς Αἴγυπτον, ἐς Μυτιλήνην, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 3.42, 5.95; ἐ. [ἐπιστολάς] 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 34.28.]]

__VII
give a name, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 5.68, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Symposium” 205b, etc.]]

__VIII
contribute (capital) to a venture, ἐς πεῖραν [Refs [“Leg.Gort.” 9.44.]]

__B
middle, with perfect passive ἐπιτέθειμαι [Refs 1st c.AD+ [1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus 2.975d,]] also aorist passive, [Refs [“Inscription Prien.” (see. below)]], etc.:—put on oneself or for oneself, ἐπὶ στεφάνην κεφαλῆφιν..θήκατο placed a helmet on his head, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 10.30; κρατὶ δ᾽ ἐπὶ..κυνέην θέτο 5.743, compare 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Bacchae” 702 (tmesis), etc.]]; χεῖρας ἐπ᾽ ἀνδροφόνους θέμενος στήθεσσι laying one's hands upon.., [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 18.317]]; κτύπημα χειρὸς κάρᾳ on one's head, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Andromache” 1210 (Lyric poetry).]]

__B.II
put on or to, as a door, πύλας τοῖς ὠσὶν ἐπίθεσθε [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Symposium” 218b; θύρας 5th-6th c.AD: Orphica “Fragmenta” 245, +others, etc. (see. above 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus 11).]]

__B.III
apply oneself to, employ oneself on or in, with dative, ναυτιλίῃσι μακρῇσι [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.1]]; τῇ πείρᾳ, τοῖς ἔργοις, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 7.42, 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Memorabilia” 2.8.3, etc.; τοῖς πολιτικοῖς 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Gorgias” 527d]]: with infinitive, attempt to.., φιλοσοφεῖν ἐπέθετο [Refs 5th c.BC+ [2nd c.AD: Alexander Rhetor 36.3; γράφειν 5th-6th c.BC: Isocrates Orator 5.1, compare 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Sophista” 242b]]:—passive, ἐπετέθη πρὸς τὸν πόλεμον [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [“Inscription Prien.” 17.38 (3rd c.BC).]]

__B.III.2
make an attempt upon, attack, τῇ Εὐβοίῃ [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 5.31; Ἐφεσίοισι [prev. author] 1.26, compare 102, 8.27; τῷ δήμῳ 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 6.61; τῇ δημοκρατίᾳ 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Respublica Atheniensium” 3.12]]; ἐ. τῇ τοῦ δήμου καταλύσει attempt it, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aeschines Orator 3.235; τυραννίδι 4th c.BC: Lycurgus Orator 125; ἀρχῇ 1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus 2.772d]]; ἐ. ταῖς ἁμαρτίαις or τοῖς ἀτυχήμασί τινος take advantage of them, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Isocrates Orator 2.3, 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 23.70]]: absolutely, make an attack, κατ᾽ ἀμφότερα [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 7.42, compare 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Politica” 1302b25.]]

__B.III.3

__B.IV
bring on oneself, ἐπέθου θύος δημοθρόους τ᾽ ἀράς [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Agamemnon” 1409.]]

cause a penalty to be imposed, θάνατον ζημίαν ἐπιθέσθαι [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 2.24; φόβον τινί 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 4.5.41.]]

lay commands on, τί τινι [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.111, compare “OGI” 669.61 (Egypt, 1st c.AD)]]: also with infinitive, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 3.63, variant in 2nd c.AD: Athenaeus Epigrammaticus 11.465d.]]

give a name, τινί [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 8.554 (tmesis), compare 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Poetica” 1451b10.]]

contribute, πολλοὶ ἐπέθεντο τὰς ἐπιδόσεις εἰς τὴν παρασκευὴν τοῦ πολέμου probably in [Refs 4th c.BC+ [“SIG” 346.29 (4th c.BC).]]

commit, entrust to another as trustee, guardian, or vicegerent, οἱ.. ἐπέτρεπεν οἶκον ἅπαντα [Refs 8th c.BC+ [2.226; ἐπιτρέψειας ἕκαστα δμῳάων [ἐκείνῃ] ἥ τις..ἀρίστη 15.24, compare 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 17.509]]; θεοῖσι μῦθον ἐπιτρέψαι leave it to them, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 22.289, compare 19.502]]; so κάκοισι θῦμον ἐπιτρέπην (Aeolic dialect infinitive) [Refs 7th c.BC+ [7th-6th c.BC: Alcaeus Lyricus 35.1; σμικραῖς ἑαυτοὺς ἐ. ἐλπίσιν 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Fragmenta” 921]]; frequently in Prose, ἐ. τινὶ τὰ πρήγματα [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 6.26; τὴν πόλιν [prev. author] 4.202; Νάξον Λυγδάμι [prev. author] 1.64; τὰ πάντα 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 2.65; πλεῖστα τῷ ἀλογίστῳ [prev. author] 5.99; τὴν ἀρχήν 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 6.1.31, etc.]]; also a son for education, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Laches” 200d]]: with dative et infinitive, τινά τινι γερονταγωγεῖν [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Equites” 1098]]: frequently in Attic dialect, refer a legal issue to any one, τινὶ δίαιταν [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 59.45; διάγνωσις -τετράφθω τῷ ἐπιμελητῇ 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Leges” 936a; οἷς (attracted for ἃ) ἂν ἐπιτρέψωσιν οἱ δὲ τάξωσι, τούτοις ἐμμένειν, i.e. acquiesce in the court and abide by its decision, [prev. work] 784c]] (for the construction [Refs 5th c.BC+ [compare 5th-6th c.BC: Andocides Orator 3.34 near the end).]]

__4
with dative only, rely upon, leave to, τοῖσιν γὰρ ἐπετράπομέν γε μάλιστα [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 10.59; ἐπιτρέψαι δὲ θεοῖσιν 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 21.279; ἐ. τῇ ὀλιγαρχίῃ 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 3.81; ὥς οἱ (i.e. ἰατρῷ) ἐπέτρεψε [prev. work] 130: with _dative_ et]]infinitive, σοὶ ἐπέτρεψεν πονέεσθαι he left it to you to work, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 10.116, compare 421, 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 9.10]]: frequently in Attic dialect, refer the matter to a person, leave it to his arbitration, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Acharnenses” 1115, “V.” 521, “Ra.” 811]]; τινὶ δικαστῇ to one as a judge, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 4.83; τῷ ἐν Δελφοῖς μαντείῳ [prev. author] 1.28; ἐ. τῷ θεῷ περί τινος 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Gorgias” 512e, cf. Alcaeus1.117e; ὑμῖν ἐπιτρέπω καὶ τῷ θεῷ κρῖναι [prev. author] “Ap.” 35d]]; Ἀθηναίοις ἐ. περὶ σφῶν αὐτῶν πλὴν θανάτου to leave their case to the [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus]] save as to the penalty of death, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 4.54; περὶ ὧν διαφερόμεθα τοῖς οἰκείοις ἐ. 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 27.1]]:—passive, δίκης Λακεδαιμονίοις ἐπιτραπείσης [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 5.31.]]

__5
middle, entrust oneself, leave one's case to, τινί [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.96; διαιτητῇ [prev. author] 5.95, compare 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 1.5.8]]; also, to entrust what is one's own to another, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 3.155, 157.]]

__6
passive, to be entrusted, ᾧ λαοί τ᾽ ἐπιτετράφαται (3rd.pers. plural perfect for ἐπιτετραμμένοι εἰσί) [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 2.25]]; τῇς (i.e. Ὥραις) ἐπιτέτραπται μέγας οὐρανός heaven's gate is committed to them (to open and to shut),[Refs 5th c.BC+ [5.750, compare 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 3.142]]; ὑπό τινων ἐπιτρεφθῆναι (i.e. ἰατρῷ), of a patient, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Antipho Orator 4.3.5:]] with accusative _of things_, ἐπιτρέπομαί τι I am entrusted with a thing, ἐπιτραφθέντες τὴν ἀρχήν [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.7; ἐπιτετραμμένοι τὴν φυλακήν 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 1.126.]]

__II
give up, yield, Ποσειδάωνι δὲ νίκην πᾶσαν ἐπέτρεψας [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 21.473]]; later ἐ. τινί with infinitive, permit, suffer, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Plutus” 1078, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Charmides” 171e, etc.]]: with accusative et infinitive, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 7.7.8; also ἐ. Θηβαίοις αὐτονόμους εἶναι [prev. author] “HG” 6.3.9; οὐδενὶ ἐ. κακῷ εἶναι [prev. author] “An.” 3.2.31; ἐ. ἀδικέοντι τῷ ἀδελφεῷ 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 2.120; μὴ ἐ. τῷ ἀσεβοῦντι 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Euthyphro” 5e]]: absolutely, give way, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “O.” 6.21, 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Nubes” 799, “Pl.” 915, 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 1.71, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Apologia” 35b:]] — passive, ἄνευ τοῦ ἐπιτραπῆναι without leave, [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [POxy. 474.40 (2nd c.AD).]]

__II.2
intransitive, give way, οὐ μὲν ἐπέτρεπε γήραϊ λυγρῷ [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 10.79]]; indulge, μὴ πάντα ἡλικίῃ καὶ θυμῷ ἐπίτρεπε [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 3.36; ταις ἡδοναῖς καὶ ἐπιθυμίαις 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Leges” 802c; τῇ ὀργῇ 1st c.BC: Dionysius Halicarnassensis 7.45.]]

__III
command, τὴν μὲν [τάξιν] ἐπὶ τῷ δεξιῷ ἐπέτρεψεν ἐφέπεσθαι [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 6.5.11: elsewhere with _dative_, “PLond.” 3.1173.3 (2nd c.AD)]], etc.:—passive, ἐπετράπην ὑπὸ σοῦ [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [“POxy.” 51.5 (2nd c.AD).]]

generally, power to decide, ἐ. διδόναι τινὶ περί τινος [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Hippocrates Medicus “περὶ εὐσχημοσύνης” 17, compare “Schwyzer” 195.10 (Crete (from Delos), 2nd c.BC)]]; διδόναι τῇ συγκλήτῳ τὴν ἐ. NT.Act.26.12.]]

ἐπιτυγχάνω,
future -τεύξομαι[Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 431c:]]aorist 2 ἐπέτῠχον: perfect -τετύχηκα[Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Oeconomica” 1352b5]]:—properly hit the mark, τοῦ σκοποῦ, opposed to ἀποτυγχάνω, [Refs 1st c.AD+ [[prev. author] “EN” 1106b33; οἱ πολλὰ βάλλοντες ἐπιτυγχάνουσι πολλάκις 1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus 2.438a: hence,]]

__II
light or fall upon, meet with,

__I
with dative person, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Nubes” 195, 535, 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 3.75; ἐ. γυναικὶ βιαζομένῃ 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Leges” 874c: also c._dative_ _of things_, ἐ. σορῷ 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.68; ναυσί 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 8.34; βιβλίῳ 2nd c.AD: Lucianus Sophista “Dem.Enc.” 27]]; ἐ.[ταῖς θύραις] ἀνεῳγμέναις to find them open, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Symposium” 223b.]]

__I.2
c.genitive person, μετρίου ἀνδρός [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Plutus” 245, compare 1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus “Artoxerxes” 12: c._genitive_ _of things_, ἐ. ὁλκάδος ἀναγομένης 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 3.3]]; εὐώνων ἐ. a low market, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Oec.” [prev. cited]]]

__I.3
rarely c.accusative, τὰς ἁπλᾶς [ἐπιθυμίας] ἐν ὀλίγοις ἐπιτεύξῃ [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 431c; ἅττ᾽ ἂν ἐπιτύχῃς 4th c.BC: Eubulus Comicus 123.5.]]

__I.4
absolutely, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Ranae” 570, 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 6.38]]; mostly ὁ ἐπιτυχών the first person one meets, any chance person, especially in plural, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 2.2, 5th c.BC: Antipho Orator 2.1.1: with _negative_, οὐδὲ φαύλων ἀνδρῶν οὐδὲ τῶν ἐ. 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Cratylus” 390d; οὐ γὰρ οἶμαι τοῦ ἐ. εἶναι.. [prev. author] “Euthphr.” 4a]]; οὐ περὶ τοῦ ἐ. on no common matter, [Refs [[prev. author] “R.” 352d]]: without the Article, ἐπιτυχόντος ἀνθρώπου λόγος [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Hercules Furens” 1248, cf. Phot. p.140R. (=gloss on 5th c.BC: Eupolis Comicus 25D.).]]

__III
attain to, reach, gain one's end, c.genitive of things, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Memorabilia” 4.2.28, 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 48.3; εὐχωλᾶς “Inscription Cyprian dialect” 134 H.(4th c.BC)]]; πολιτείας [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [“BGU” 113.3 (2nd c.AD), etc.]]; τοῦ καλῶς [μειγνύναι] [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Philebus” 61d]]; ἐ. τοῦ ἀγῶνος gain one's suit, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 48.30]]; profit by, benefit by, φιλανθρωπίας [NT+2nd c.AD+ [“BGU” 522.8 (2nd c.AD): _absolutely_, οὐ δύνασθε ἐπιτυχεῖν NT.Jam.4.2.]]

__III.2
c.participle, succeed in doing, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 8.101, 103 (but ζητέων ἐπιτυγχάνειν]] find, light upon by searching, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Hippocrates Medicus “περὶ ἀρχαίης ἰητρικῇς” 24)]]: so with infinitive, [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd c.AD: Lucianus Sophista “Nec.” 6]]; γαμβροῦ ὁ ἐπιτυχὼν εὗρεν υἱόν he who is lucky in his son-in-law, [Refs 3rd c.AD+ [3rd c.AD: Democritus Epigrammaticus 272.]]

__III.3
c.dative modi, to be lucky, successful in a thing, μάχῃ [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aeschines Orator 3.165]]: absolutely, to be successful, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Meno” 97c, 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 3.42, 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Rhetorica” 1354a9]]; ἂν ἐπιτύχῃ if she succeeds, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th-3rd c.BC: Menander Comicus “Ἐπιτρέποντες” 346; τἆλλα ἐ. 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Historia Graeca (Hellenica)” 4.5.19: also _impersonal_, αὐτῷ οὐδὲν ἐπετύγχανε 2nd c.AD(?): Antoninus Liberalis Mythographus 41.6.]]

passive, turn out well, αἱ ἐπιτετευγμέναι πράξεις successful, [Refs 2nd c.BC+ [2nd c.BC: Polybius Historicus 6.53.2, compare 2nd c.BC: Hipparchus Astronomicus cited in 5th c.AD: Stobaeus, Joannes 4.44.81, 1st c.BC: Diodorus Siculus Historicus 1.1, 1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus 2.674a]]; φάρμακον -τετευγμένον proved remedy, Heraclid.Tarentum dialect cited in [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd c.AD: Galenus Medicus 12.403.]]

__IV
c.dative person, converse, talk with one, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Leges” 758c.]]

__b

__2

Sanskrit avocam, reduplicate aorist of vac- 'say'; compare ἔπος):—speak, say, ὣς εἰπών [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 1.68, etc.; τινί 17.692, etc.; εἰς ἅπαντας 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Hecuba” 303]]; εἰπεῖν ἔν τισιν or μετά τισιν speak among a number, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 10.445, 3.85, etc.: with _accusative_ _cognate_, ἔπος, μῦθον, θεοπρόπιον, οὐνόματα, etc., 3.204, 1.552, 85, 17.260, etc.]]; τινί τι [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 1.169, +others]]; τι [Refs 7th c.BC+ [7th-6th c.BC: Alcaeus Lyricus, 7th-6th c.BC: Sappho Lyrica]] [same places], etc.; τι ἔς or πρός τινα, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Trachiniae” 487, “Aj.” 292]]; εἰπεῖν περί τινος, ἀμφί τινι, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 15.347, 14.364: with _genitive_, πατρός τε καὶ υἱέος]] of them, [Refs [11.174]]; εἰπεῖν ὅτι or ὡς to say that.., [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 17.655, 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 22.373, etc.]]: but also with infinitive, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 2.30, 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 7.35, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Gorgias” 473a, etc.]] b. recite, ἔπη [Refs [[prev. author] “Ion” 535b.]]

__2
in parenthesis, ὡς ἔπος εἰπεῖν so to say, limiting a general statement, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Persae” 714, etc.]]; speaking loosely, opposed to ὄντως, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Leges” 656e]]; opposed to ἀκριβεῖ λόγῳ, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. author] “R.” 341b; ὡς εἰπεῖν 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 3.38, +others, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Phaedrus” 258e, +others; ὡς ἀξίως εἰπεῖν 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “de Partibus Animalium” 651b36: without ὡς, οὐ πολλῷ λόγῳ εἰπεῖν 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.61; ἐς τὸ ἀκριβὲς εἰπεῖν 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 6.82; σχεδὸν εἰπεῖν 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Sophista” 237c: καθόλου εἰπεῖν 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Categoriae” 12a27; ἡ ἁπλῶς εἰπεῖν ἀπόδειξις [prev. author] “APo.” 75b23]]; τὸ ξύμπαν εἶπαι, εἰπεῖν, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 7.143, 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 1.138.]]

__3
εἴποι τις as one might say, uncertain reading in [Refs 5th c.BC+ [2nd c.BC: Polybius Historicus 15.35.1; ὥσπερ εἴποι τις 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Aves” 180 (assuming variant); ὡς εἴποι τις 1st-2nd c.AD: Dio Chrysostomus Sophista 64.5 (assuming variant).]]

__II
with accusative person, address, accost one, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 12.210, etc.]]

__II.2
name, mention, [Refs [[prev. work] 1.90, etc.]]

__II.3
call one so and so, πολλοί τέ μιν ἐσθλὸν ἔειπον [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 19.334, compare 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Coloneus” 43, 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Medea” 465, etc.]]

__II.4
with double accusative person et of things, tell or proclaim so of one, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 6.479 (where ἀνιόντα depends on εἴποι)]]; εἰπεῖν τινα ὅτι.. [Refs 8th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “O.” 14.22; ἀτάσθαλόν τι εἰ. τινά 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 22.314; κακὰ εἰ. τινά 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Acharnenses” 649; μηδὲν φλαῦρον εἰ. τ. [prev. author] “Nu.” 834; ἐῢ εἰ. τινά 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 1.302]]; εἰ. τεθνεῶτ᾽ Ὀρέστην speak of him as dead, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Choephori” 682.]]

__II.5
celebrate, of poets, Αἴαντος βίαν [Refs [“Anthologia Graeca” 7.2.6 (Antip. Sid.).]]

__III
with dative person et infinitive, order or command one to.., [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 15.76, 22.262, etc.; also εἰπεῖν πρός τινα, with]]infinitive, [Refs [16.151]]: with accusative et infinitive, εἶπον τὰς παῖδας δεῦρ᾽ ἄγειν τινά [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Coloneus” 932, compare 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Phaedo” 59e, 3rd c.BC: Herodas Mimographus 6.26: followed by ἵνα]], frequently in NT, [NT.Matt.4.3, +others]

__IV
propose, move a measure in the assembly, εἰπὼν τὰ βέλτιστα [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 3.12; εἰπεῖν τὰ δέοντα [prev. work]15; εἶπε ψήφισμα [prev. author] 24.11]]: frequently as a formal prefix to decrees and laws, Λάχης εἶπε [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 4.118, compare “IG” 12.24, +others]]; compare ἀγορεύω.

__V
plead, δίκην [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 18.508; δικίδιον 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Equites” 347.]]

__VI
promise, offer, χρυσὸν εἶφ᾽ ὃς ἂν κτάνῃ [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Electra” 33.]]

__VII
imperative εἰπέ sometimes used in addressing several persons, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Acharnenses” 328, “Av.” 366, 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 4.10.]]
ἔπω,

__A
say, call, name, ἤν Πέρσειον ἔπουσιν [Refs 2nd c.BC+ [2nd c.BC: Nicander Epicus “Alexipharmaca” 429, compare 490, “Th.” 508. (Prob. invented by 2nd c.BC: Nicander Epicus, as _present_ of εἶπον.)]]

deep_entry:
Abbott-Smith / STEPBible (TBESG)
ἐργάζομαι
(ἔργον), [in LXX for עָבַד, פָּעַל, עָשָׂה, etc. ;]
__1. intrans.,
__(a) to work, labour: Mat.21:28, Luk.13:14, Jhn.5:17 9:4 b, Act.18:3, 1Co.9:6, 2Th.3:10-12; τ. χερσίν, 1Co.4:12, 1Th.4:11; νυκτὸς κ. ἡαέρας, 1Th.2:9, 2Th.3:8; of working for pay, Mat.21:28; for reward, Rom.4:4-5;
__(b) to work at a trade or business, to trade: before Iv (Dem.), Mat.25:16.
__2. Trans.,
__(a) to work, work out, do, produce, perform: with accusative, 2Co.7:10, Col.3:23, 2Th.3:11, Jas.1:20, 2Jn.8, before εἰς, III Jn 5; ἔργον, Act.13:41 (LXX); id. before εἰς, Mat.26:10; ἐν, Mrk.14:6; ἔργα, Jhn.3:21; τὰ ἔ. τ. θεοῦ, Jhn.6:28 9:4; τὸ ἔ. κυρίου, 1Co.16:10; τ. ἀγαθόν, Rom.2:10, Eph.4:28 (see AR, Eph.) 190); id. before πρός, Gal.6:10; κακόν, before dative of person(s) (more frequently dupl. accusative, in cl.), Rom.13:10; δικαιοσύνην, Act.10:35, Heb.11:33; ἀνομίαν, Mat.7:23; ἁμαρτίαν, Jas.2:9; σημεῖον, Jhn.6:30; τ. ἱερά, 1Co.9:13; τ. θάλασσαν (work the sea, i.e. make one's living from it), Rev.18:17;
__(b) to work for, earn by working (cl.): Jhn.6:27 (cf. κατ-, περι-, προσ-εργάζομαι; Cremer, 258; on the force of the aorist of this verb, see M, Pr., 116).†
(AS)

LSJ / STEPBible (TFLSJ)
ἐργάζομαι,
[Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 18.469]], etc., Cretan dialect ϝεργάδδομαι [Refs [“Schwyzer” 181v5]]: future -άσομαι [Refs 6th c.BC+ [6th c.BC: Theognis Elegiacus 1116]], etc., Doric dialect [LXX+3rd c.BC+ [ἐργαξοῦμαι 3rd c.BC: Theocritus Poeta Bucolicus 10.23, ἐργῶμαι “PCair.Zen.” 107.4 (3rd c.BC), LXX.Gen.29.27, +others, “IG” 7.3073.12 (Lebad., 2nd c.BC) (but 5th c.AD(?): Hesychius Legal icographus ἐργᾷ· ἐργάζει)]]: aorist εἰργασάμην, Ionic dialect [Refs 6th c.BC+ [ἐργ- 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 2.115, 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Th.” 845 (Lyric poetry), etc., 3rd._person_ etc for 1st._person_, 2nd._person_ _plural_ _optative_ ἐργασαίατο Aristophanes Comicus [{5-6th c.BC}] “Aves” 1147, “Lys.” 42; _Doric dialect_ ἠργάξαντο “SIG” 248 M (Delph., 4th c.BC)]]: perfect εἴργασμαι, Ionic dialect[Refs 5th c.BC+ [ἔργ- 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 2.121.έ, 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “fragment” 311, etc.]] —These tenses are used both in middle and passive significations: for other passive tenses, see below[Refs 4th c.BC+ [111:— _Attic dialect_ Inscrr. of 4th C have ἠργαζόμην, ἠργασάμην, (ἐξ-) “IG” 22.1585.11, 1669.10, +others, but εἴργασμαι [prev. work]1666 A 27; so also ἠργάσατο [prev. work]7.424 (Oropus, 4th c.BC), εἰργασμένος [prev. work]3073.51 (Lebad., 2nd c.BC), ἐξήργασατο “UPZ” 19.8 (2nd c.BC), εἴργασμαι “PCair.Zen.” 146.3 (3rd c.BC)]]; but this rule is often broken in later Papyrus, Inscrr., and codices:—work, labour, especially of husbandry, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th-7th c.BC: Hesiodus Epicus “Op.” 299, 309, 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 2.72, etc.; but also of all manual labour, of slaves, ἐ. ἀνάγκῃ 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 14.272]]; of quarrymen, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 2.124, etc.; τὴν οὐσίαν οὐ δικαζόμενον ἀλλ᾽ ἐργαζόμενον κεκτημένον 5th c.BC: Antipho Orator 2.2.12]]; ἐ. ἐν τοῖς ἔργοις in the mines, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 42.31: with _dative_ _instrumental_, χαλκῷ with brass, 8th-7th c.BC: Hesiodus Epicus “Op.” 151; also of animals, βοῦς ἐργάτης ἐργάζεται 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “fragment” 563]]; of birds working to get food, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “HA” 616b35]]; of bees, [Refs [[prev. work] 625b22]]; of Hephaestus' self-acting bellows, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 18.469; τὸ χρῆμ᾽ ἐργάζεται]] the matter works, i.e. goes on, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Ec.” 148]]; ὁ ἀὴρ ἐργάζεται produces an effect [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [Theophrastus Philosophus [{4-3rd c.BC}] “de Causis Plantarum” 5.12.7]]; οὐχ ὁμοίως ἐργάσεται τὸ θερμόν [Refs [[prev. work] 6.18.11.]]

__II
transitive, work at, make, ἔργα κλυτά, of Athena, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 20.72, compare 22.422; ἀγάλματα, ὕμνους, 5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “N.” 5.1, “I.” 2.46; τρίποδα, Νίκην, “SIG” 34 (Delph., 5th c.BC); ἁμαξίδας Aristophanes Comicus [{5-6th c.BC}] “Nubes” 880; οἰκοδόμημα 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 2.76]]; εἰκόνας, ἀνδριάντας, καλὰ ἔργα, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Cra.” 431c, 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Mem.” 2.6.6, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Men.” 91d; κηρόν, σχαδόνας, of bees, 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “HA” 627a6, 30; μέλι 2nd c.AD: Soranus Medicus “Vit. Hippocr.” 11]]; make so and so, [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [ξηρὸν ἐ. τινά 2nd c.AD: Lucianus Sophista “DMar.” 11.2; μέγαν Aelianus [{2-3rd c.AD}] “Varia Historia” 3.1]].

__II.2
do, perform, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [ἔργα ἀεικέα 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 24.733]]; ἔργον ἐπ᾽ ἔργῳ ἐ., of husbandmen, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th-7th c.BC: Hesiodus Epicus “Op.” 382, compare 397; ἐργασίας ἐ. 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Ethica Nicomachea” 1121b33, compare 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Oec.” 7.20; ἐναίσιμα, φίλα ἐ., 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 17.321, 24.210; θαυμαστά Plato Philosophus [{5-6th c.BC}] “Symposium” 213d; περὶ θεοὺς ἄδικον μηδέν [prev\. author] “Grg.” 522d]]; ἐ. πρᾶγμα, opposed to βουλεύειν, [NT+5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Ant.” 267, compare “OT” 347; τὸ ἔργον Κυρίου NT.1Cor.16.10]]: with double accusative, do something to.., [Refs 5th c.BC+ [τά περ νῦν ἐ. [ὁ ἥλιος] τὸν Νεῖλον 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 2.26]], etc.; chiefly in bad sense, do one ill, do one a shrewd turn, [Refs 6th c.BC+ [κακὰ ἐργάζεσθαί τινα 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Philoctetes” 786, 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 1.137, etc.; so οἷά μ᾽ εἰργάσω, τί μ᾽ ἐργάσε; 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Ph.” 928, 1172 (Lyric poetry), etc.; μὴ δῆτα τοῦτό μ᾽ ἐργάσῃ [prev\. author] “El.” 1206; αἴσχιστα ἐ. τινά Aristophanes Comicus [{5-6th c.BC}] “Vespae” 787]]; less frequently, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [ἀγαθὰ ἐ. τινά 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 8.79, compare 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 3.52, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Cri.” 53a; πολλὰ καὶ καλὰ τὴν Ἑλλάδα [prev\. author] “Phdr.” 244b]]; seldom [Refs 6th c.BC+ [τινί τι Aristophanes Comicus [{5-6th c.BC}] “Vespae” 1350; οἷν ἐμοὶ δυοῖν ἔργ᾽ ἐστὶ κρείσσον᾽ ἀγχόνης εἰργασμένα 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Tyrannus” 1374]].

__II.2.b
perform rites, [Refs [τὰ ἱερὰ ἐ. “1st Epistle to the Corinthians” 9.13]].

__II.2.c
in Law, ζημίαν ἐ. do damage, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Isaeus Orator 6.20, compare 4th c.BC: Hyperides Orator “Ath.” 22.]]

__II.3
work a material, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [ὅπλα..οἷσίν τε χρυσὸν ἐργάζετο 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 3.435]]; ἐ. γῆν till the land, [Refs 6th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.17, etc.; ἐ. [ἀγροὺς] ἐργάταις Xenophon Historicus [{5-6th c.BC}] “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 1.6.11; γῆν καὶ ξύλα καὶ λίθους [prev\. author] “HG” 3.3.7]]; [ἀργυρῖτιν] Docum. cited in [Refs 8th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 37.28; ἐ. θάλασσαν, of traders, 1st c.BC: Dionysius Halicarnassensis 3.46; γλαυκὴν ἐ., of fishers, 8th-7th c.BC: Hesiodus Epicus “Th.” 440.]]

__II.4
earn by working, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [χρήματα 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.24, 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Eq.” 840, etc.; καινὸν βίον ἐκ τοῦ δικαίου Andocides Orator [{5-6th c.BC}] 1.144, compare 8th-7th c.BC: Hesiodus Epicus “Op.” 43; ἀργύριον ἀπὸ σοφίας Plato Philosophus [{5-6th c.BC}] “Hp.Ma.” 282d; μισθοῦ τὰ ἐπιτήδεια Xenophon Historicus [{5-6th c.BC}] “Memorabilia” 2.8.2]].

__II.5
work at, practise, μουσικήν, τέχνας, etc., [Refs 6th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Phd.” 60e, “R.” 374a, etc.; ἐπιστήμας Xenophon Historicus [{5-6th c.BC}] “Oeconomicus” 1.7]]; ἀρετὴν καὶ σωφροσύνην variant in [NT+5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Isocrates Orator 13.6; δικαιοσύνην, ἀνομίαν, NT.Acts.10.35, NT.Matt.7.23.]]

__II.6
absolutely, work at a trade or business, traffic, trade, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [ἐν [γναφείῳ] 5th c.BC: Lysias Orator 23.2; ἐν ἐμπορίῳ καὶ χρήμασιν 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 36.44; ἐν τῇ ἀγορᾷ [prev\. author] 57.31]] (also οἱ τὴν τετράγωνον (i.e. ἀγοράν) ἐργαζόμενοι those who trade in the square, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [“BCH” 8.126 (compare “Glotta” 14.73)); κατὰ θάλατταν 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 56.48]]; τούτοις..ναυτικοῖς ἐ. trade with this money on bottomry, [Refs [[prev\. author] 33.4; δὶς ἢ τρὶς ἐ. τῷ αὐτῷ ἀργυρίῳ [prev\. author] 56.30]]; ταῦτα ἐ. thus he trades, [Refs [[prev\. author] 25.82; οἱ ἐργαζόμενοι _traders,_ [prev\. author] 34.51]]; οἱ ἐν Δήλῳ ἐ., = Latin qui Deli negotiantur, [Refs [“CIG” 2285b; especially of courtesans, σώματι ἐ.,]] Latin quaestum corpore facere, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 59.20; ἐπὶ τέγους ἀπὸ τοῦ σώματος 2nd c.BC: Polybius Historicus 12.13.2]]; ἀπὸ τῆς ὥρας Alexis Sam. cited in [Refs 1st c.AD+ [2nd c.AD: Athenaeus Epigrammaticus 13.572f, 1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus “Tim.” 14.]]

__II.7
cause, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [κολακείην 3rd c.AD: Democritus Epigrammaticus 268; πημονάς 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Antigone” 326; πόθον τινί 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 61.11; σύριγγας ἀνιάτους 7th c.AD: Paulus Aegineta Medicus 6.44]].

__III
passive, rarely in present and imperfect, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [1st c.BC: Dionysius Halicarnassensis 8.87 (ἐξ-), 4th c.BC: Hyperides Orator “Eux.” 35]]: future [Refs 5th c.BC+ [ἐργασθήσομαι 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Trachiniae” 1218, (ἐξ-) 5th-6th c.BC: Isocrates Orator “Ep.” 6.8]]: perfect εἴργασμαι (see. below): aorist 1 [Refs 6th c.BC+ [εἰργάσθην Plato Philosophus [{5-6th c.BC}] “Respublica” 353a, 4th-3rd c.BC: Theophrastus Philosophus “HP” 6.3.2, etc.]]

__III.1
to be made or built, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [ἔργαστο τὸ τεῖχος 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.179; ἐκ πέτρας εἰργασμένος Aeschylus Tragicus [{4-5th c.BC}] “Prometheus Vinctus” 244; οἰκοδόμημα διὰ ταχέων εἰργ. 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 4.8]]; λίθοι εἰργ. wrought stones, [Refs 6th c.BC+ [[prev\. author] 1.93; γῆ εἰργ. Xenophon Historicus [{5-6th c.BC}] “Oeconomicus” 19.8; θώρακας εὖ εἰργ. [prev\. author] “Mem.” 3.10.9]].

__III.2
to be done, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Ag.” 354, 1346, 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Hec.” 1085; εἰργασμένα _things done, deeds, 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 7.53 (ἐργ-), 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Ion” 1281, compare 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “OT” 1369.]]

ἐργᾰσ-ία,
Ionic dialect -ιη, Cretan dialect ϝεργασία [Refs [“Leg.Gort.” 8.44, ἡ, (ἐργάτης)]] work, business, [Refs [ἐργασίην φεύγουσα “hymnus ad Mercurium” 486]], etc.; opposed to ἀργία, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Mem.” 2.7.7; ἐ. ἀγαθή]] productive labour, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev\. author] “Vect.” 4.29; ἐργασίᾳ ἐγχειρεῖν, of bees, 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “HA” 625b24; ἡ περὶ τὴν θάλατταν ἐ., of seamen, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “R.” 371b; μὴ γενομένης ἐργασίας]] if no work was done, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 27.20; δὸς ἐργασίαν,]] with infinitive, Latin da operam ut.., NT.Luke.12.58, compare [Refs 6th c.BC+ [“OGI” 441.109 (_SC. de Stratonicensibus,_ 1st c.BC): _plural_, τὰς ἐν ὑπαίθρῳ ἐ. ἐργάζεσθαι Xenophon Historicus [{5-6th c.BC}] “Oeconomicus” 7.20; ἐ. ἀνελεύθεροι 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Ethica Nicomachea” 1121b33, compare 4th-3rd c.BC: Epicurus Philosophus “fragment” 196 (uncertain).]]

__2
function, [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [ἥπατος 2nd c.AD: Aretaeus Medicus “περὶ αἰτιῶν καὶ σημείων χρονίων παθῶν” 1.15]].

__II
working at, making, manufacture, ἱματίων, ὑποδημάτων, etc., [Refs 6th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Grg.” 449d, “Tht.” 146d, etc.; ἡ τῆς ἐσθῆτος ἐκ τῶν ἐρίων ἐ. Xenophon Historicus [{5-6th c.BC}] “Oeconomicus” 7.21]]; making up of a prescription, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Hippocrates Medicus “Ulc.” 14: _metaphorically_, Πέργαμος ἀμφὶ τεαῖς χερὸς ἐργασίαις ἁλίσκεται Troy is (i.e. is doomed to be)]] taken in the part wrought by thy hands, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “O.” 8.42; ἐ. ἡδονῆς]] production of pleasure, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Prt.” 353d; ἐ. χρημάτων]] money-making, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “EN” 1160a16 (but _administration_ of property, “Leg.Gort.” [same place]).]]

__II.2
working of a material, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [ἡ ἐ. τοῦ σιδήρου 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.68]]; χαλκοῦ, ἐρίων, ξύλων, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Chrm.” 173e; τῶν χρυσείων μετάλλων 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 4.105, compare 4th c.BC: Hyperides Orator “Eux.” 36; πίττης Theophrastus Philosophus [{4-3rd c.BC}] “Historia Plantarum” 9.2.6]]: most commonly, tillage of the ground, ἐ. γῆς, χώρας, [Refs 6th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Ra.” 1034 (_plural_), 5th-6th c.BC: Isocrates Orator 7.30, etc.; ἐ. κήπων Plato Philosophus [{5-6th c.BC}] “Minos” 316b]]; ἐ. περὶ τὴν τροφήν preparation (i.e. mastication and digestion) of food, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Juv.” 469a3]]; treatment of silphium, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-3rd c.BC: Theophrastus Philosophus “HP” 6.3.2]]

__II.3
generally, trade, business, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Mem.” 3.10.1; ἐπὶ τῆς ἐργασίας ὢν τῆς κατὰ θάλατταν]] engaged in trade by sea, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 33.4; ἡ ἐ. τῆς τραπέζης]] the banking business, [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [[prev\. author] 36.6; ἐ. χρυσοχοϊκή, ἀρωματική, “PLond.” 3.906.6 (2nd c.AD), “PFay.” 93.7 (2nd c.AD); βαφεῖς τὴν ἐ.]] dyers by trade, [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [PTeb. 287.3(2nd c.AD)]]; especially of a courtesan's trade, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 2.135, 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 18.129]]; of sexual intercourse, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Pr.” 876a39.]]

__II.3.b
ἐὰν ἐργασίαν εὕρῃ ὁ οἰκέτης if a slave brings in earnings, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Hyperides Orator “Ath.” 22.]]

__II.4
practising, exercising, [Refs 6th c.BC+ [τῶν τεχνῶν Plato Philosophus [{5-6th c.BC}] “Gorgias” 450c; Κύπριδος “AP” 5.218 (Paul. Sil.); ἀκαθαρσίας “Epistle to the Ephesians” 4.19]].

__II.5
work of art, production, τετράγωνος ἐ., of the Hermae, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 6.27 (non legit Scholia); τῶν τειχῶν αἱ ἐργασίαι]] the fortification works, [Refs [[prev\. author] 7.6.]]

__II.6
literary execution, [Refs 1st c.BC+ [ἐ. ποιητική 1st c.BC: Philodemus Philosophus “περὶ ποιημάτων” 5.11]]; elaboration of a topic, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [Scholia 5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “P.” 2.24.]]

__II.7
production of a play, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [Arg. 4th-3rd c.BC: Menander Comicus “Oxy.” 1235.108.]]

__III
guild or company of workmen, ἡ ἐ. τῶν βαφέων[Refs [Judeich “Altertümer von Hierapolis” 50]]; ἐριοπλυτῶν [Refs [[prev. work] 40; ἐ. θρεμματική uncertain meaning, [prev. work]227.]]

ἐργάτης, -ου, ὁ
(ἐργάζομαι, which see), [in LXX: Wis.17:17, Sir.19:1 40:18, 1Ma.3:6 * ;]
__1. prop., a field labourer, husbandman: Mat.9:37-38 20:1-2, 8, Luk.10:2, Jas.5:4 (cf. Wis, l.with).
__2. Generally, a workman, labourer: Mat.10:10, Luk.10:7, Act.19:25 (opposite to τεχνίτης), 1Ti.5:18; of Christian teachers, 2Co.11:13, Php.3:2, 2Ti.2:15.
__3. a worker, doer: τ. ἀδικίας, Luk.13:27 (cf. 1Mac, l.with).†
(AS)

ἐργᾰτ-ης, ου, ὁ,
workman, Hermes [17.5 (from Delos), “NT.Mat.10.10”], etc.; especially one who works the soil, husbandman, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [γῆς ἐ. 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 4.109, 5.6; οἱ ἐ. οἱ περὶ γεωργίαν 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 35.32]]: absolutely, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “OT” 859, 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “El.” 75]], etc.: also with substantive, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [ἐ. ἀνήρ 3rd c.BC: Theocritus Poeta Bucolicus 10.9, 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 59.50; οὑργάτης λεώς]] the country-folk, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Pax” 632]]; of animals, βοῦς ἐ. a working ox, [Refs 7th c.BC+ [7th c.BC: Archilochus Lyricus 39, 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “fragment” 563; ἐ. σφῆκες 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Historia Animalium” 627b32]]; also ἐ. θαλάττης, of a fisher, [Refs 4th c.AD+ [4th c.AD: Alciphro Epistolographus 1.11; ἐ. λίθων]] a stone-mason, [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd c.AD: Lucianus Sophista “Somn.” 2.]]

__b
in the religious sense, [NT.2Tim.2.15, “NT.2Cor.11.13” (_plural_).]

__2
adjective hard-working, strenuous, [Refs 6th c.BC+ [ἐ. στρατηγός Xenophon Historicus [{5-6th c.BC}] “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 1.6.18; σώφρων κἀ. Aristophanes Comicus [{5-6th c.BC}] “Acharnenses” 611]]; opposed to ἀργός, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Euthd.” 281c; φειδωλὸς καὶ ἐ. [prev\. author] “R.” 554a]].

__II
one who practises an art, [Refs 6th c.BC+ [τῶν ἐν πολέμῳ Xenophon Historicus [{5-6th c.BC}] “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 4.1.4]]; ἐ. δίκης, of a judge, [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [3rd c.BC: Lycophron Tragicus 128: _absolutely_]], practitioner in some special branch of surgery, e.g. lithotomy, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [ἐ. ἄνδρες 5th c.BC: Hippocrates Medicus “Jusj.”]]

__III
doer, [NT+6th c.BC+ [ἄσημος οὑργ. τις ἤν 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Antigone” 252; τῶν καλῶν Xenophon Historicus [{5-6th c.BC}] “Memorabilia” 2.1.27; ἀνομίας Vetus Testamentum Graece redditum “1 Maccabees” 3.6; τῆς ἀδικίας NT.Luke.13.27]].

__IV
producer, [Refs 1st c.AD+ [τῶν ἐν τῷ κόσμῳ γινομένων 1st c.AD: Heraclitus 75; [Αἰὼν] θείας φύσεως ἐ. “SIG” 1125.12 (from Eleusis).]]

__V
a sort of capstan or windlass, [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [3rd-2nd c.BC: Bito Mechanicus 58.12, 1st c.BC: Vitruvius Scriptor de Architectura Latinus 10.2.7, +others, 4th c.AD: Oribasius Medicus 49.4.1.]]

ἔργον, -ου, τό (originally Ϝέργον, work), [very frequently in LXX, chiefly for מַשֶׂה, מְלָאכָה, also for עֲבֹדָה, פֹּעַל, etc. ;]
