ἔργον,
Doric dialect ϝέργον [Refs 6th c.BC+ [“IG” 4.800 (6th c.BC)]], Elean ϝάργον [Refs 6th c.BC+ [“SIG” 9 (6th c.BC), τό: (ἔρδω, O 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus]] weorc (neuter) 'work', Avest. var[schwa]za-):— work, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 2.436, etc.; ἔ. οὐδὲν ὄνειδος, ἀεργίη δέ τ᾽ ὄνειδος {8-7th c.BC}: Hesiodus Epicus “Opera et Dies” 311; πλεόνων δέ τε ἔ. ἄμεινον 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 12.412; ἔ. ἐποίχεσθαι 6.492; νῦν ἔπλετο ἔ. ἅπασι 12.271]]; especially in plural, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [ἄλλος ἄλλοισιν..ἐπιτέρπεται ἔργοις 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 14.228; ἐπὶ ἔργα τράποντο 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 3.422; ἔργων παύσασθαι 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 4.683]]; τὰ σ᾽ αὐτῆς ἔργα κόμιζε see to thine own tasks, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 6.490: especially in the following relations,]]

__1
in [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” mostly of]]works or deeds of war, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [πολεμήϊα ἔ. 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 2.338, +others, 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 12.116; ἔργον μάχης 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 6.522; alone, ἀτελευτήτῳ ἐπὶ ἔργῳ 4.175, compare 539; ὑπέσχετο δὲ μέγα ἔργον 13.366; ἐπ᾽ αὐτῷ δ᾽ ἔργον ἐτύχθη ἀργαλέον 4.470; later, ἔργον.. Ἄρης κρινεῖ Aeschylus Tragicus [{4-5th c.BC}] “Septem contra Thebas” 414]]; ἐν τῷ ἔ. during the action, [Refs 6th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 2.89, compare 7.71; τὸ ἐν Πλαταιαῖς ἔ. Plato Philosophus [{5-6th c.BC}] “Menexenus” 241c; τῶν πρότερον ἔ. μέγιστον ἐπράχθη τὸ Μηδικόν 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 1.23]]; ἔργου ἔχεσθαι to engage in battle, [Refs [[prev. work] 49.]]

__2
of peaceful contests, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [κρατεῖν ἔ. 5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “O.” 9.85; ἔργου ἔχεσθαι [prev\. author] “P.” 4.233]]; also ἔργα θῆκε κάλλιστ᾽ ἀμφὶ κόμαις placed [the reward of] noble deeds about his hair, [Refs [[prev\. author] “O.” 13.38.]]

__3
of works of industry,

__3.a
of tillage, tilled lands, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [ἀνδρῶν πίονα ἔ. 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 12.283, etc.; ἔργ᾽ ἀνθρώπων 16.392, 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 6.259; βροτῶν 10.147]]; οὔτε βοῶν οὔτ᾽ ἀνδρῶν φαίνετο ἔργα [Refs [[prev. work] 98; ἔργα alone, 16.140, etc.; Ἔργα καὶ Ἡμέραι]] —the title of Hesiod's work; πατρώϊα ἔ. their father's lands, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 2.22; οὔτ᾽ ἐπὶ ἔργα..ἴμεν]] will neither go to our farms, [Refs [[prev. work] 127, compare 252; Ἰθάκης..ἔργα]] the tilled lands of Ithaca, [Refs [14.344; ἀμφὶ.. Τιταρησσὸν ἔργ᾽ ἐνέμοντο]] inhabited lands, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 2.751; τὰ τῶν Μυσῶν ἔ. 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.36; so later, “PBaden” 40.5 (2nd c.AD)]]: generally, property, wealth, possessions, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [θεὸς δ᾽ ἐπὶ ἔργον ἀέξῃ 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 14.65, compare 15.372.]]

__3.b
of women's work, weaving, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 9.390, etc.; ἀμύμονα ἔ. ἰδυίας [prev. work] 128; ἔργα ἐργάζεσθαι 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 22.422, 20.72]].

__3.c
of other occupations, θαλάσσια ἔ. fishing, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [5.67; a seaman's life, 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 2.614: periphrastic, δαιτὸς..ἔργα]] works of feasting, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [9.228; φιλοτήσια ἔ. 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 11.246; ἔργα γάμοιο 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 5.429; ἔργα Κυπρογενοῦς 6th c.BC: Solon Lyricus 26; Ἀφροδίτης “hymnus ad Venerem” 1; also τέκνων ἐς ἔ. Aeschylus Tragicus [{4-5th c.BC}] “Agamemnon” 1207]]: absolutely, [Refs 6th c.BC+ [ἔργον 2nd c.AD: Lucianus Sophista “DDeor.” 17.1, “AP” 12.209 (_plural_, 2nd c.AD: Strato Epigrammaticus, assuming variant); also ἔργα ἰσχύος καὶ τάχους Xenophon Historicus [{5-6th c.BC}] “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 1.2.12]]; φίλα ἔργα μελίσσαις, of flowers, [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [3rd c.BC: Theocritus Poeta Bucolicus 22.42]]; of mines, etc., [Refs 6th c.BC+ [ἔ. ἀργυρεῖα Xenophon Historicus [{5-6th c.BC}] “de Vectigalibus” 4.5, 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 21.167, etc.; ἔργα πίσσια uncertain reading in 1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus “Cat.Ma.” 21.]]

__4
deed, action, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [ἔργ᾽ ἀνδρῶν τε θεῶν τε 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 1.338; θέσκελα ἔ. Τρώων 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 3.130; ἀήσυλα ἔ. 5.876]]; καρτερά, ἀεικέα ἔ., [Refs 8th c.BC+ [[prev. work] 872, 22.395; παλίντιτα, ἄντιτα ἔ., 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 1.379, 17.51; ἔργα ἀποδέκνυσθαι 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.16, compare 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Alc.” 1.119e, 2nd-3rd c.AD: Dio Cassius Historicus 37.52; opposed to ἔπος,]] deed, not word (see. [Refs 8th c.BC+ [ἔπος 11.1); opposed to μῦθος, 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 9.443, 19.242, 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Pr.” 1080 (_anapaest meter_), etc.; opposed to λόγος, 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “El.” 358, 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Alc.” 339; ἔργῳ, opposed to λόγῳ, frequently in _Attic dialect_, etc., 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 2.65, etc.: so in _plural_, λόγῳ μὲν..τοῖσι δ᾽ ἔργοισιν 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Coloneus” 782, compare 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “fragment” 360.13; λόγοισιν εἴτ᾽ ἔργοισιν 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Tyrannus” 517]]; opposed to ῥήματα, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev\. author] “OC” 873; opposed to ὄνομα, 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “IA” 128 (_anapaest meter_), 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 8.78, 89; in many phrases, πέπρακται τοὔργον Aeschylus Tragicus [{4-5th c.BC}] “Prometheus Vinctus” 75, compare “Ag.” 1346; χωρῶ πρὸς ἔργον 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Ajax” 116]]; τὸ μὲν ἐνθύμημα χαρίεν.., τὸ δὲ ἔ. ἀδύνατον its execution, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “An.” 3.5.12; ἐν ἔργῳ χέρνιβες ξίφος τε]] ready for action, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “IT” 1190; ἡ κατάρα ὑπὸ τοῦ δαίμονος εἰς ἔ. ἤγετο 4th c.AD: Julianus Imperator “Orationes” 7.228b]].

__II
thing, matter, πᾶν ἔ...ὑπείξομαι in every point, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 1.294; ἃ Ζεὺς μήδετο ἔ. 2.38, etc.; πάρος τάδε ἔ. γενέσθαι 6.348, etc.; ὅπως ἔσται τάδε ἔ. 2.252, 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 17.78, etc.; μέμνημαι τόδε ἔ. 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 9.527; ἄκουε τοὔργον 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Trachiniae” 1157, compare “OT” 847, “Aj.” 466]]; in bad sense, mischief, trouble, of disease, [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [αἰτίη τοῦ ἔ. 2nd c.AD: Aretaeus Medicus “περὶ αἰτιῶν καὶ σημείων ὀξέων παθῶν” 1.9]]; μέγα ἔ. a serious matter, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 4.663, 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 3.3.]]

__II.2
μέγα ἔ., like{μέγα χρῆμα}, χερμάδιον λάβε χειρὶ Τυδεΐδης, μέγα ἔ. a monstrous thing, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 5.303, compare 20.286; φυλόπιδος μέγα ἔ.]] a mighty call to arms, [Refs [16.208.]]

__III
passive, that which is wrought or made, work, οἷ᾽ ἐπιεικὲς ἔργ᾽ ἔμεν ἀθανάτων, of the arms of Achilles, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 19.22; ἔ. Ἡφαίστοιο]] metal-work, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 4.617; πέπλοι.., ἔργα γυναικῶν 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 6.289, 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 7.97, compare 10.223; ὕφασμα, σῆς ἔ. χερός Aeschylus Tragicus [{4-5th c.BC}] “Choephori” 231; κολεόν..λώτινον ἔ. 3rd c.BC: Theocritus Poeta Bucolicus 24.45]]; of a wall, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Av.” 1125]]; of a statue, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Mem.” 3.10.7: in _plural_]], of siege-works, [Refs 2nd c.BC+ [ἔ. καὶ μηχαναί 2nd c.BC: Polybius Historicus 5.3.6]]; of a machine, [Refs 2nd c.BC+ [2nd c.AD: Apollodorus Damascenus Mechanicus “Poliorc.” 157.4, +others, 2nd c.BC: Athenaeus Mechanicus 15.2]], +others; of public buildings, [Refs [Mon.Anc.Gr. 18.20]]; of an author's works, [Refs 1st c.BC+ [1st c.BC: Dionysius Halicarnassensis “de Compositione Verborum” 25; τὸ περὶ ψυχῆς ἔργον Ἀριστοτέλους “AP” 11.354.8 (6th c.AD: Agathias Historicus et Epigrammaticus).]]

__III.2
result of work, profit or interest, ἔργον [χρημάτων] interest or profit on money, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Isaeus Orator 11.42, compare 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 27.10.]]

__IV
special phrases:

__IV.1
ἔργον ἐστί,

__IV.1.a
with genitive person, it is his business, his proper work, [Refs 6th c.BC+ [ἀνδρῶν τόδ᾽ ἐστὶν ἔ. Aeschylus Tragicus [{4-5th c.BC}] “Choephori” 673; ὅπερ ἐστὶν ἔ. ἀγαθοῦ πολίτου Plato Philosophus [{5-6th c.BC}] “Gorgias” 517c]]; of things, φραδέος νόου ἔργα τέτυκται it is a matter (which calls) for a wary mind, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 24.354]]; function, [Refs 6th c.BC+ [ἅπερ νεῶν ἄμεινον πλεουσῶν ἔργα ἐστίν 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 2.89; οὐ θερμότητος ἔργον ψύχειν Plato Philosophus [{5-6th c.BC}] “Respublica” 335d]]; τοῦτο ἑκάστου ἔ. ὃ ἂν ἢ μόνον τι ἢ κάλλιστα τῶν ἄλλων ἀπεργάζηται [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [[prev. work] 353a; ἔργα τοῦ ἐγκεφάλου _functions,_ 2nd c.AD: Galenus Medicus 16.518]]: with dative person, [Refs 6th c.BC+ [οἷς τοῦτο ἔ. ἦν Xenophon Historicus [{5-6th c.BC}] “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 4.5.36, compare 6.3.27: with the possessive _pronoun_, σὸν ἔ. [ἐστί]]] with infinitive, [Refs 6th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Pr.” 635; ἐμὸν τόδ᾽ ἔ. κρῖναι [prev\. author] “Eu.” 734; σὸν ἔ., θῦε θεοῖς Aristophanes Comicus [{5-6th c.BC}] “Aves” 862; ὑμέτερον ἐντεῦθεν ἔ. [prev\. author] “Pax” 426]]: with Article, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [νῦν ἡμέτερον τὸ ἔ. 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 5.1]].

__IV.1.b
with genitive of things, there is need of.., [Refs 6th c.BC+ [τί δῆτα τόξων ἔ.; 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Alcestis” 39; πολλῆς φυλακῆς ἔ. [ἐστί] Plato Philosophus [{5-6th c.BC}] “Respublica” 537d]]: especially with negative, [Refs 6th c.BC+ [οὐδὲν..ὀδόντων ἔ. ἐστ᾽ Aristophanes Comicus [{5-6th c.BC}] “Pax” 1310; οὐ δόλου νῦν ἔ. [prev\. author] “Pl.” 1158, compare 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Hipp.” 911: with _dative_ _person_, ἐπέδρης μὴ εἶναι ἔ. τῇ στρατιῇ 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.17]]: with Article, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [οὐκ ἂν μακρῶν λόγων ἡμῖν τόδ᾽ εἴη τοὔργον 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Electra” 1373]]: with a participle added, [Refs 1st c.AD+ [οὐδὲν ἦν ἔ. αὐτοῦ κατατείνοντος Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus [{1-2nd c.AD}] “Publicola” 13]]: also with infinitive, οὐδὲν ἔ. ἑστάναι there is no use in standing still, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Lys.” 424, compare “Av.” 1308; οὐδὲν ἔ. ταῦτα θρηνεῖσθαι 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Ajax” 852, compare 12.]]

__IV.1.c
with infinitive, it is hard work, difficult to do, [Refs 6th c.BC+ [πολὺ ἔ. ἂν εἴη διεξελθεῖν Xenophon Historicus [{5-6th c.BC}] “Memorabilia” 4.6.1; πολὺ ἔ. ἦν τῷ νομοθέτῃ πάντα γράφειν 5th c.BC: Lysias Orator 10.7; ἔ. ἐστὶν εἰ ἐροῦμεν 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 24.51; ἔ. εὑρεῖν πρόφασιν Menander Comicus [{4-3rd c.BC}] 76; also μέγα ἔ. ταῖς..ἐπιθυμίαις καλῶς χρῆσθαι Plato Philosophus [{5-6th c.BC}] “Symposium” 187e; χαλεπὸν ἔ. διαιρεῖν Aristophanes Comicus [{5-6th c.BC}] “Ranae” 1100]] (Lyric poetry): also in genitive, [Refs 6th c.BC+ [πλείονος ἔ. ἐστὶ..μαθεῖν Plato Philosophus [{5-6th c.BC}] “Euthyphro” 14b]]: rarely with a participle, [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [οὐδὲν ἔ. μαχομένῳ Philippides Comicus [{4-3rd c.BC}] 15.3]]; ἔ. [ἐστί] with accusative et infinitive, it can scarcely happen that.., [Refs 4th c.BC+ [ἔ. ἅμα πάντας ὀργισθῆναι καὶ ἁμαρτεῖν 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Politica” 1286a35]].

__IV.2
ἔργον παρασχεῖν τινί give one trouble, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Nu.” 523, compare “AP” 9.161 (Marc. argument, punning on Hesiod's Ἔργα); ἔργον ἔχειν]] take trouble, with participle, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Cyr.” 8.4.6]]; with infinitive, [Refs [[prev\. author] “Mem.” 2.10.6.]]

__IV.3
ἔ. γίγνεσθαι τῆς νόσου to be its victim, [Refs 1st c.AD+ [Anonymus cited in 10th c.AD: Suidas Legal icographus see at {ἄτολμοι}; κτεινόμενος ὑμέτερον ἔ. εἰμί Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus [{1-2nd c.AD}] “Eumenes” 17; τῆς ὑμετέρας γέγονεν ἔ. ὀλιγωρίας 2nd c.AD: Lucianus Sophista “Dem.Enc.” 29]].

__IV.4
ἔ. ποιεῖσθαί τι to make a matter one's business, attend to it, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Phdr.” 232a, 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Hier.” 9.10; so ἐν ἔργῳ τίθεσθαι Aelianus [{2-3rd c.AD}] “Varia Historia” 4.15]].

__V
={ἐργασία} III, [Refs [τὸ ἔ. βαφέων “CIG” “Corpus Inscriptionum Graecarum” “Corpus Inscriptionum Graecarum” 3498 (from Thyatira).]]

ἐρεθίζω
[in LXX: Dan LXX 11:10, 25 (גָּרָה hithp.), 1Ma.15:40, 2Ma.14:17, etc. ;]
__1. to stir up, provoke (as in cl.): Col.3:21.
__2. In good sense (cf. ἐρεθισμός, excitement, in MGr.), to stir up, stimulate: 2Co.9:2.†
(AS)

---

LSJ / STEPBible (TFLSJ)
ἐρεθίζω,
Epic dialect infinitive -ιζέμεν [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 4.5]]: imperfect [Refs 5th c.BC+ [ἠρέθιζον 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Antigone” 965]] (Lyric poetry), Epic dialect [Refs 8th c.BC+ [ἐρ- 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 5.419]]: future -ίσω [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd c.AD: Galenus Medicus 1.385]], -ιῶ [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Hippocrates Medicus “Mochl.” 2, 2nd c.BC: Polybius Historicus 13.4.2]]: aorist 1 [Refs 5th c.BC+ [ἠρέθισα 1st c.BC: Dionysius Halicarnassensis 3.72; poetry ἐρ- Aeschylus Tragicus [{4-5th c.BC}] “Prometheus Vinctus” 183]](Lyric poetry), infinitive [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [ἐρεθίξαι “AP” 12.37 (3rd c.BC: Dioscorides Epigrammaticus)]]: perfect [Refs 4th c.BC+ [ἠρέθικα 4th c.BC: Aeschines Orator 2.37]]:—passive, aorist 1 ἠρεθίσθην, participle [Refs 5th c.BC+ [ἐρεθισθείς 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 6.40, 1st c.BC: Dionysius Halicarnassensis 4.57]]: perfect [Refs 5th c.BC+ [ἠρέθισμαι 5th c.BC: Hippocrates Medicus]] (see. below), etc.: (ἐρέθω):—rouse to anger, rouse to fight, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 1.32; κερτομίοις ἐπέεσσι 5.419]]; κύνας τ᾽ ἄνδρας τε, of a lion, [Refs 6th c.BC+ [17.658; ἐ. τοὺς Πέρσας 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 3.146; φιλαύλους τ᾽ ἠρ. Μούσας 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Antigone” 965 (Lyric poetry); ὥσπερ σφηκιὰν ἐ. τινά Aristophanes Comicus [{5-6th c.BC}] “Lysistrata” 475; χεῖρον..ἐρεθίσαι γραῦν ἢ κύνα Menander Comicus [{4-3rd c.BC}] 802]]; πὺξ ἐ. challenge to a boxing-match, [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [3rd c.BC: Theocritus Poeta Bucolicus 22.2]]; provoke to curiosity, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [μητέρα σήν 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 19.45]]: generally, excite, chafe, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [φρένας ἐ. φόβος Aeschylus Tragicus [{4-5th c.BC}] “Prometheus Vinctus” 183]](Lyric poetry); of physical irritation, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Hippocrates Medicus “Mochl.” 2; βῆχες βραχέα -ουσαι]] causing brief irritation, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev\. author] “Aph.” 4.54: _metaphorically_, ἐ. πλανάτας χοροῖσιν 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Bacchae” 148]] (Lyric poetry); ἐ. μάγαδιν to touch it, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Telestes Lyricus 4; φλόγα 3rd c.AD: Heliodorus Scriptor Eroticus 8.9; τὸ φονικὸν καὶ θηριῶδες Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus [{1-2nd c.AD}] 2.822c]]; incite to rivalry, [NT.2Cor.9.2:—]passive, to be provoked, excited, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [ὑπό τινος 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 6.40, compare 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “V.” 1104; ἠρεθισμένος _under provocation, Menander Comicus [{4-3rd c.BC}] 574; ὀργῇ χεῖρας -ισμένας 3rd c.BC: Euphro Comicus 8.3]]; of love, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [τοῖς νέοισιν -ισμένος 4th c.BC: Timocles Comicus 30]]; of fire, [Refs 6th c.BC+ [φέψαλος.. -όμενος..ῥιπίδι Aristophanes Comicus [{5-6th c.BC}] “Acharnenses” 669 (Lyric poetry); αἰθὴρ -έσθω βροντῇ Aeschylus Tragicus [{4-5th c.BC}] “Prometheus Vinctus” 1045]] (anapaest meter); πνεῦμα ἠρεθισμένον, of one who has run till he is out of breath, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Medea” 1119; ἕλκος ἠρεθισμένον _irritated,_ 5th c.BC: Hippocrates Medicus “περὶ ἀγμῶν” 27, compare 31, 2nd c.BC: Polybius Historicus 1.81.6; ὀσμὴ -ισμένη 4th c.BC: Eubulus Comicus 75.9; ἐπὶ τὴν ὕβριν ἠρεθίσθαι 2nd c.AD: Lucianus Sophista “Am.” 22]].

__II
absolutely, to be quarrelsome or perverse, [Refs 1st c.AD+ [1st c.AD: Philo Judaeus 1.359.]]

ἐρείδω
(chiefly in poets and late prose for ἐρυγγάνω), [in LXX for תָּמַךְ (Pro.4:4 5:5 11:16, al.), etc. ;]
to prop, fix firmly: act., as mid., ἐρείσασα, of a ship driving ashore (RV, struck), Act.27:41.†

LSJ / STEPBible (TFLSJ)
ἐρείδω,
Epic dialect imperfect [Refs 8th c.BC+ [ἔρειδον 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 13.131]]: future [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [ἐρείσω 3rd c.BC: Callimachus Epicus “Hymnus in Delum” 234, 2nd c.AD: Aristides Rhetor “Or.” 17(15).10]] codices: aorist 1 [Refs 6th c.BC+ [ἤρεισα 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Antigone” 1236, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Phdr.” 254e, “Ti.” 91e; _Boeotian dialect_ 3rd._person_ etc for 1st._person_, 2nd._person_ _sing._ εἴρισε 6th c.BC: Corinna Lyrica “Supp.” 1.32]]; Epic dialect ἔρεισα (ἐπ-) [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 7.269]]: perfect ἤρεικα (συν-) [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Hippocrates Medicus “Morb.Sacr.” 7, (προσ-) 2nd c.BC: Polybius Historicus 5.60.8; but ἐρήρεικα 1st c.AD: Dioscorides (Dioscurides) Medicus “Eup.” 1.84, (προσ-) 1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus “Aem.” 19:]] —middle, future ἐρείσομαι (ἀπ-) [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Pr.” 885b29, 2nd c.BC: Polybius Historicus 15.25.25]]: aorist 1 [Refs 8th c.BC+ [ἠρεισάμην {8-7th c.BC}: Hesiodus Epicus “Scutum Herculis” 362, (ἀπ-) 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “R.” 508d; _Epic dialect_ ἐρ- 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 5.309]]:—passive, [Refs [3]] future [Refs 5th c.BC+ [ἐρηρείσεται 5th c.BC: Hippocrates Medicus “γυναικεῖα” 2.133]]: Epic dialect aorist 1 [Refs 8th c.BC+ [ἐρείσθην 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 7.145]]: perfect [Refs 7th c.BC+ [ἐρήρεισμαι 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 4.152, 5th c.BC: Hippocrates Medicus “περὶ ἄρθρων ἐμβολῆς” 78 (but _2nd pers._ _sing._ ἠρήρεισθα 7th c.BC: Archilochus Lyricus 94 is from ἀραρίσκω); also ἤρεισμαι Ti. _Locrian dialect_ 98e (ἐρήρ- [prev. work] 97e), 1st c.BC: Diodorus Siculus Historicus 4.12, 2nd c.AD: Pausanias Periegeta 6.25.5; _Ionic dialect_ 3rd._person_ etc for 1st._person_, 2nd._person_ _plural_]] perfect [Refs 8th c.BC+ [ἐρηρέδαται 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 23.284, 329, _Epic dialect_ ἐρήρεινται 3rd c.BC: Apollonius Rhodius Epicus 2.320]]: pluperfect [Refs 8th c.BC+ [ἠρήρειστο 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 4.136]]; 3rd.person etc for 1st.person, 2nd.person plural [Refs 8th c.BC+ [ἐρηρέδατο 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 7.95, ἠρήρειντο 3rd c.BC: Apollonius Rhodius Epicus 3.1398:— 8th c.BC: Homerus Epicus uses the augment only in ἠρήρειστο, 8th-7th c.BC: Hesiodus Epicus “Sc.” 362 in ἠρείσατο.—_Epic dialect_, _Ionic dialect_, and poet. Verb, also found in 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus]] and later Prose:—cause to lean, prop, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [δόρυ..πρὸς τεῖχος ἐρείσας 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 22.112; θρόνον πρὸς κίονα μακρὸν ἐρείσας 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 8.66; πύργῳ ἔπι προὔχοντι..ἀσπίδ᾽ ἐρείσας 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 22.97]]; [νέκυας] ἀλλήλοισιν ἐ. piling them against each other, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 22.450; ἐρείσατε..πλευρὸν ἀμφιδέξιον 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Coloneus” 1112]]; πρὸς στέρν᾽ ἐρείσας (i.e. τοὺς παῖδας) [Refs 6th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “HF” 1362, compare “Ba.” 684; τὰ ἰσχία πρὸς τὴν γῆν Plato Philosophus [{5-6th c.BC}] “Phaedrus” 254e; ἐ. τινὰ εἰς ἕδραν 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Heraclidae” 603; τὰς κεφαλὰς εἰς γῆν Plato Philosophus [{5-6th c.BC}] “Timaeus” 91e; ἐς χεῖρας ἐ. τι 3rd c.BC: Theocritus Poeta Bucolicus 7.104; ἐ. τὴν κεφαλὴν ἐπὶ γῆς Plato Philosophus [{5-6th c.BC}] “Timaeus” 43e; τὸ γόνυ κατὰ τοῦ ἰσχίου Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus [{1-2nd c.AD}] “Flamininus” 20; ῥόῳ ἔνι κάλπιν 3rd c.BC: Apollonius Rhodius Epicus 1.1234]]: generally, fix firmly, plant, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [ἄγκυραν χθονί 5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “P.” 10.51; εἰς γῆν ἐ. ὄμμα 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Iphigenia Aulidensis” 1123, compare 2nd c.AD: Aristides Rhetor “Or.” 17(15).10; ἐπὶ χθονὸς ὄμματ᾽ 3rd c.BC: Apollonius Rhodius Epicus 1.784]]; ἐ. πόδας ἐς βένθος plant the foot firm, [Refs [[prev. work] 1010: _metaphorically_, ἐ. τὰν γνώμαν]] fix one's mind firmly on a thing, [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [3rd c.BC: Theocritus Poeta Bucolicus 21.61.]]

__2
prop up, support, stay, ἀσπὶς ἄρ᾽ ἀσπίδ᾽ ἔρειδε, κόρυς κόρυν, ἀνέρα δ᾽ ἀνήρ, of close ranks of men-atarms, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 13.131; ἐπ᾽ ἀσπίδος ἀσπίδ᾽ ἔρεισον 7th c.BC: Tyrtaeus Elegiacus 11.31; πέλτην ἐρεῖσαι 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Rhesus” 487; κίον᾽ οὐρανοῦ τε καὶ χθονὸς ὤμοιν ἐ. Aeschylus Tragicus [{4-5th c.BC}] “Prometheus Vinctus” 352]].

__3
press hard, attack, τινα [Refs 6th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “O.” 9.32: obscene meaning, ἐ. γυναῖκα Aristophanes Comicus [{5-6th c.BC}] “Ecclesiazusae” 616, “fragment” 74.]]

__4
push, thrust, [Refs 6th c.BC+ [ὅπῃ κέ τις..ἐρείδῃ 5th c.BC: Empedocles Poeta Philosophus 12.3; ἔπη..ἤρειδε κατὰ τῶν ἱππέων _hurled forth..,?? Aristophanes Comicus [{5-6th c.BC}] “Equites” 627; ὁ χορὸς ἤρειδεν ὁρμαθοὺς μελῶν τέτταρας [prev\. author] “Ra.” 914]]:—middle, [Refs [ἔπος πρὸς ἔπος ἠρειδόμεσθ᾽ [prev\. author] “Nu.” 1375]].

__5
infix, plant in, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [πλευραῖς ἔγχος 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Antigone” 1236]]; ἀνταίαν πληγήν inflict it, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Andr.” 844 (Lyric poetry):]] —passive, ἄλγημα ἐρηρεισμένον fixed pain, [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd c.AD: Galenus Medicus 8.385.]]

__6
press down, depress, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [πλάστιγγα τοῦ βίου 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “fragment” 576.5]].

__7
of wagers or matches, match, set one pledge against another, [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [3rd c.BC: Theocritus Poeta Bucolicus 5.24.]]

__II
intransitive, press hard, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [ἀμφ᾽ αὐτῷ πελεμίξαι ἐρείδοντες βελέεσσιν 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 16.108; εἴς τινα Aristophanes Comicus [{5-6th c.BC}] “Nubes” 558; νέφος ἐ. ἐπὶ γῆν Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus [{1-2nd c.AD}] “Numa” 2; πνεῦμα κατὰ τῆς σχεδίας [prev\. author] “Crass.” 19]]; of an illness or pain, settle upon a particular part, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [νόσος ὁμότοιχος ἐ. Aeschylus Tragicus [{4-5th c.BC}] “Agamemnon” 1004 (Lyric poetry), compare 2nd c.AD: Rufus Medicus cited in 4th c.AD: Oribasius Medicus 45.30.27, 2nd c.AD: Galenus Medicus]] 11.61; exert pressure: hence, rest, [Refs 2nd c.BC+ [ἐπὶ τὸ ἔδαφος Hero Mechanicus [{2-1st c.BC} (?)] “Automatopoetica” 2.7]].

__II.2
set to work, fall to, especially of eating, [Refs 6th c.BC+ [ἔρειδε Aristophanes Comicus [{5-6th c.BC}] “Pax” 31, compare 25 (where, _accusative_ to Scholia, it is _metaphorically_ from rowers); ἐρείδετον [prev\. author] “fragment” 493]].

__II.3
become fixed, [Refs [πρῴρα ἐρείσασα “Act.Ap.” 27. 41.]]

__III

deep_entry:

λέγω,
[in LXX very freq., chiefly for אמר; λέγει for נְאֻם, Gen.22:16, al. ;]
__1. in Hom., to pick out, gather, reckon, recount.
__2. In Hdt. and Att., to say, speak, affirm, declare: absol., Act.13:15, 24:10; before orat. dir., Mat.9:34, Mrk.3:11, Jhn.1:29, al.; before ὅτι recit., Mrk.3:21, Luk.1:24, Jhn.6:14, al.; accusative and inf., Luk.11:18, Jhn.12:29, al.; after another verb of speaking, προσφωνεῖν κ. λέγειν, Mat.11:17, al.; ἀπεκρίθη (ἐλάλησεν) λέγων (καὶ λέγει; Dalman, Words, 24 ff.), Mat.25:9, Mrk.3:33, 7:28, Luk.24:6, 7, al.; of unspoken thought, λ. ἐν ἑαυτῷ, Mat.3:9, Luk.3:8, al.; of writing, 2Co.8:8, Php.4:11, al.; λέγει ἡ γραφή, Rom.4:3, Jas.2:23, al.; with accusative of thing(s), Luk.8:8, 9:33, Jhn.5:34, al.; σὺ λέγεις (a non-committal phrase; Swete, Mk., 359, 369f.), Mat.27:11, Mrk.15:2, Luk.23:3, Jhn.18:37; with dative of person(s), before orat. dir., Mat.8:20, Mrk.2:17, al. mult.; id. before ὅτι, Mat.3:9, al.; with prep., πρός, μετά, περί, etc., Mrk.4:41, Jhn.11:56, Heb.9:5, al.; to mean (cl.), Mrk.14:71, Jhn.6:71, 1Co.10:29, al.; to call, name, Mrk.10:18; pass., Mat.9:9, Mrk.15:7, al (cf. ἀντι-, δια- (-μαι), προ-, συλ-λέγω).
SYN.: λαλέω, which refers to the utterance, as λέγω to the meaning of what is said, its correspondence with thought (Tr., Syn., Ixxvi; Thayer, see word λαλέω). (AS)

---

ἐρῶ,
Attic dialect future of εἴρω (B), [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 6.9, 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Eumenides” 45, 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Ranae” 61, etc.]], Ionic dialect and Epic dialect ἐρέω (later as present, [Refs 2nd c.BC+ [2nd c.BC: Nicander Epicus “Theriaca” 484, 2nd c.AD: Athenaeus Epigrammaticus 9.400a, 2nd c.AD: Galenus Medicus 15.878, +others)]]; optative ἐροίην [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 3.1.14, 4th c.AD: Libanius Sophista “Orationes” 1.87:]]imperfect ἤρεον (variant{εἴρεον}) [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Hippocrates Medicus “ἐπιδημίαι” 2.2.9]]: perfect active εἴρηκα [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Prometheus Vinctus” 821, 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Ranae” 558, etc.]]: pluperfect εἰρήκειν [Refs 1st c.AD+ [1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus 2.184d]]:—passive, perfect εἴρημαι [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 4.363, 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Lysistrata” 13, etc.]]; Ionic dialect 3rd.pers. plural εἰρέαται [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 7.81]], contraction εἰρῆται [Refs 4th c.BC+ [“Schwyzer” 811.17 (Oropus, 4th c.BC)]]; participle εἰρημένος, Cretan dialect ϝερημένος [Refs [“Supp.epigram” 2.509, argument ϝεϝρημένος “Schwyzr” 98 (from Mycenae)]]: pluperfect εἴρητο [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 10.540, 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 8.27, etc.]]: aorist 1 passive ἐρρήθην [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Leges” 664d, later ἐρρέθην 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Categoriae” 11b12, +others; Ionic εἰρέθην 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 4.77, 156]]: future ῥηθήσομαι [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 1.73, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 473e, 5th-6th c.BC: Isocrates Orator 8.73, 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 27.53: more frequently εἰρήσομαι,]] mostly in 3rd.pers. singular -ήσεται[Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 23.795, 5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “I.” 6(5).59, 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Philoctetes” 1276, etc.]]; participle -όμενος[Refs 8th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Hippocrates Medicus “περὶ ἄρθρων ἐμβολῆς” 53. — 8th c.BC: Homerus Epicus uses only]]future ἐρέω, 3rd.pers. singular perfect and pluperfect passive, with participle εἰρημένος, aorist participle ῥήθείς in the phrase ἐπὶ ῥηθέντι δικαίῳ (see. below), and future passive —The place of the present εἴρω (which see) is supplied by φημί, λέγω or ἀγορεύ; εἶπον serves as aorist (ϝερε-: ϝρη-, compare ῥήτρα, ῥητός, Latin verbum, Engl. word.)

__I
I will say or speak, with accusative of things et dative person, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 1.297: _absolutely_, οὐδὲ πάλιν ἐρέει]] he will say nothing against it, [Refs [9.56]]; ἐν δ᾽ ὑμῖν ἐρέω among you,[Refs 8th c.BC+ [[prev. work] 528, compare 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 16.378]]: frequently in Attic dialect, ἐρεῖν τι πρός τινα [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 520a (_active_), 595b, “Tht.” 179a (both _passive_)]]; τι περί τινος [Refs [[prev. author] “Phlb.” 29d, etc.]]: with accusative person, speak of, κακῶς ἐρεῖν τινα [Refs 6th c.BC+ [6th c.BC: Theognis Elegiacus 796, 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Alcestis” 705: and with double _accusative_, ἐρεῖ δέ μ᾽..τάδε [prev. work] 954, compare 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Crito” 48a]]:—passive, μῦθος..εἰρημένος ἔστω [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 8.524; εἰρημένα μυθολογεύειν 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 12.453]]; λίαν εἰρημένος too true, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Prometheus Vinctus” 1031]]; ἐπὶ ῥηθέντι δικαίῳ after justice has been pronounced, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 18.414]]; ἐπὶ τοσοῦτον εἰρήσθω περί τινος let this suffice, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Ethica Nicomachea” 1117b21.]]

__II
I will tell, proclaim, ἔπος [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 1.419, etc.]]; Ἠὼς..Ζηνὶ φόως ἐρέουσα announce it,[Refs 7th c.BC+ [2.49; ἐρέω τιν᾽ ὑμῖν αἶνον 7th c.BC: Archilochus Lyricus 89.1.]]

__II.2
tell, order, with dative person et infinitive, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Historia Graeca (Hellenica)” 3.2.6, etc.]]: with accusative et infinitive, [Refs [[prev. author] “Cyr.” 8.3.6]]:—passive, εἴρητο συλλέγεσθαι τὸν στρατόν orders had been given.., [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 7.26, etc.]]

__III
passive, to be mentioned, οὗτοι μὲν οἱ παραθαλάσσιοι.. εἰρέαται [Refs 4th c.BC+ [[prev. author] 4.181, compare 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “de Mundo” 393b27.]]

__III.2
to be specified, agreed, promised, εἰρημένος μισθός [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th-7th c.BC: Hesiodus Epicus “Opera et Dies” 370, 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 6.23]]; εἰρημένον, absolutely, when it had been agreed, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 1.140]]; κὰ (τ) τὰ ϝεϝρημένα [Refs [“Schwyzer” [same place]]]

participle ἐνθών [Refs 6th c.BC+ [“IG” 9(1).867 (Corc., 6th c.BC), (κατ-) “Schwyzer” 657.4 (4th c.AD(?): Arcadius Grammaticus, 4th c.BC)]]; subjunctive ἔνθῃ [Refs [“Berl.Sitzb.” 1927.164 (from Cyrene)]]; Laconian dialect ἔλσῃ, ἔλσοιμι, ἐλσών, [NT+5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Lysistrata” 105, 118, 1081; later ἦλθα LXX.2Ki.24.7, NT.Matt.25.36, “BGU” 530.11 (1st c.AD), “IG” 14.1320, etc.]]; 3rd.pers. plural ἤλθοσαν [LXX+2nd c.BC+ [LXX.Josh.2.22, +others, “PTeb.” 179 (2nd c.BC), etc.]]; ἤλυθα [Refs 4th c.AD+ [“IG” 14.1971, 4th-5th c.AD(?): Nonnus Epicus “Dionysiaca” 37.424, (ἐπ-) “Anthologia Graeca” 14.44:]]perfect ἐλήλῠθα (not in [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Homerus Epicus) 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Prometheus Vinctus” 943, etc.]]; syncopated. plural ἐλήλῠμεν, -υτε, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Cratinus Comicus 235, 5th c.BC: Achaeus Tragicus 24, 43]]; Epic dialect εἰλήλουθα, whence I plural εἰλήλουθμεν [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 9.49, 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 3.81]], participle εἰληλουθώς [Refs 8th c.BC+ [19.28, 20.360; once ἐληλουθώς 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 15.81]], participle κατ-εληλευθυῖα [Refs [“Berl.Sitzb.” 1927.166 (from Cyrene)]]; Cretan dialect perfect infinitive ἀμφ-εληλεύθεν, see at {ἀμφέρχομαι}: Boeotian dialect perfect διεσσ-είλθεικε[Refs 3rd c.BC+ [“Schwyzer” 485.2 (Thesp., 3rd c.BC),]]participle κατηνθηκότι[Refs 4th c.BC+ [[prev. work]657.39 (4th c.AD(?): Arcadius Grammaticus, 4th c.BC)]]: pluperfect ἐληλύθειν [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Equites” 1306]]; Ionic dialect ἐληλύθεε [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 5.98]]; Epic dialect εἰληλούθει [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 4.520, εἰληλούθειν 3rd c.BC: Callimachus Epicus “Fragmenta” 532.]] —In _Attic dialect_ the oblative moods of present, as well as the imperfect and future were replaced by forms of εἶμι ibo (which see): in [Refs [LXX and Hellenistic Greek the place of the compounds, especially ἐξ-, εἰσέρχομαι, is commonly taken by ἐκ-, εἰσπορεύομαι, etc., the]]future, aorist, and perfect being supplied as before by ἐλυθ- (ἐλθ-):

__I
start, set out, ἦ μέν μοι μάλα πολλὰ..Λυκάων ἐρχομένῳ ἐπέτελλε when I was setting out, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 5.198, compare 150]]; τύχησε γὰρ ἐρχομένη νηῦς a ship was just starting, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 14.334]]; ἐς πλόον ἐρχομένοις (variant{ἀρχ-}) [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “P.” 1.34.]]

__I.2
walk,= περιπατέω, χαμαὶ ἐρχομένων ἀνθρώπων [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 5.442]]; σὲ δ᾽ ἐρχόμενον ἐν δίκᾳ πολὺς ὄλβος ἀμφινέμεται walking in justice, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “P.” 5.14: the two {ἔρχατος} rare significations belong only to the]]present ἔρχομαι.

__II
(much more frequently) come or go (the latter especially in Epic dialect and Lyric poetry), ἦλθες thou art come, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 16.461, etc.]]; χαίροισ᾽ ἔρχεο go and fare thee well, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [7th-6th c.BC: Sappho Lyrica “Papyrus fragments” in E. Diehl, 23.7, compare 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 9.43, 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 10.320, 1.281; ἀγγελίην στρατοῦ.. ἐρχομένοιο 2.30, compare 10.267; πάλιν ἐλθέμεν, αὖτε εἰλήλουθα, 19.533, 549]]; οἶκον ἐλεύσεται[Refs 4th c.BC+ [[prev. work] 313; οἴκαδε 5.220; ἐς οἴκους 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Persae” 833]]: as a hortatory exclamation, ἀλλ᾽ ἔρχευ, λέκτρονδ᾽ ἴομεν [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 23.254, compare 17.529.]]

__III
with accusative cognate, ὁδὸν ἐλθέμεναι to go a journey, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 1.151; ἄλλην ὁδόν, ἄλλα κέλευθα ἤλθομεν 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 9.262; τηϋσίην ὁδὸν ἔλθῃς 3.316: frequently in Trag., 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Prometheus Vinctus” 962, “Th.” 714 (also κατὰ τὴν αὐτὴν ὁδόν 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Leges” 707d)]]; νόστιμον ἐλθεῖν πόδα (variant{δόμον}) [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Alcestis” 1153]]; ἀγγε- λίην, ἐξεσίην ἐλθεῖν, go on an embassy, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 11.140, 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 21.20.]]

__III.2
with accusative loci, come to, arrive at, rare in [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Homerus Epicus, Ἀΐδαο δόμους ἔρχεαι 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 22.483; ἔρχεσθον κλισίην 1.322]]: frequently in later Poets, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “P.” 4.52, 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Trachiniae” 259, etc.]]; traverse, ὁ ἥλιος ἔρχεται τῆς Λιβύης τὰ ἄνω [Refs 8th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 2.24: with _accusative_ _person_, αῐ κέν τι νέκυς (_accusative_ _plural_) ῂσχυμμένος ἔλθῃ 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 18.180; σὲ δ᾽, ὦ τέκνον, τόδ᾽ ἐλήλυθεν πᾶν κράτος 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Philoctetes” 141 (Lyric poetry).]]

__III.3
with genitive loci, ἔρχονται πεδίοιο through or across the plain, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 2.801]]; but also, from a place, γῆς τινος [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Coloneus” 572.]]

__III.4
with dative person, come to, i.e. come to aid or relieve one, rare in [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Homerus Epicus, 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 16.453; frequently later, 5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “O.” 1.100, 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 1.13. etc.; ἀποροῦντι αὐτῷ ἔρχεται Προμηθεὺς ἐπισκεψόμενος τὴν νομήν 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Protagoras” 321c]]; also in hostile sense, ἔρχομαί σοι [NT.Rev.2.5.]

__IV
with future participle, to denote the object, ἔρχομαι ἔγχος οίσόμενος I go to fetch.., [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 13.256; ἔρχομαι ὀψομένη 14.301: frequently in Trag., μαρτυρήσων ἦλθον 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Eumenides” 576; ἐκσώσων 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Medea” 1303.]]

__IV.2
in [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus like an auxiliary Verb, ἔρχομαι ἐρέων, φράσων,]] I am going to tell, [Refs [1.5, 3.6, +others]]; σημανέων [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4.99; μηκυνέων 2.35: rare in _Attic dialect_, ἔ. κατηγορήσων, ἀποθανούμενος, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Euthyphro” 2c, “Thg.” 129a]]; ἔρχομαι ἐπιχειρῶν -σοι ἐπιδείξασθαι, for ἔ. σοι ἐπιδειξόμενος, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. author] “Phd.” 100b; οὐ τοῦτο λέξων ἔρχομαι, ὡς.. 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Agesilaus” 2.7.]]

__IV.3
with participle present, aorist, or perfect, in [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Homerus Epicus, to show the manner of moving, ἄγγελος ἦλθε θέουσα]] she came running, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 11.715, +others]]; μὴ πεφοβημένος ἔλθῃς lest thou come thither in full flight,[Refs [10.510]]; ἦλθε φθάμενος he came first,[Refs [23.779]]; κεχαρισμένος ἔλθυι [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 2.54.]]

__IV.4
aor, participle ἐλθών added to Verbs, οὐ δύναμαι..μάχεσθαι ἐλθών go and fight, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 16.521]]; κάθηρον ἐλθών come and cleanse,[Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. work] 668; λέγοιμ᾽ ἂν ἐλθών 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Supplices” 928; δρᾶ νυν τάδ᾽ ἐλθών 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Antigone” 1107.]]

__V
of any kind of motion, ἐξ ἁλὸς ἐλθεῖν to rise out of the sea, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 4.448, +others]]; ἐπὶ πόντον to go over it, [Refs [2.265]]; with qualifying phrase, πόδεσσιν ἔ. to go on foot, [Refs [6.40 (but πεζὸς εἰλήλουθα]]have come as a foot-soldier, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 5.204)]]; of birds, [Refs [17.755, etc.]]; of ships, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [15.549, 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 14.334]]; of spears or javelins, frequently in [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad”]]; of natural phenomena, as rivers, [Refs [5.91]]; wind and storm, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [9.6, 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 12.288; clouds, 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 4.276, 16.364]]; stars, rise, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 13.94; time, είς ὅ κεν ἔλθῃ νύξ 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 14.77, compare 24.351; ἐπὴν ἔλθῃσι θέρος 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 11.192; ἔτος ἦλθε 1.16]]; of events and conditions, είς ὅ κε γῆρας ἔλθῃ καὶ θάνατος [Refs [13.59, compare 11.135]]; of feelings, go, ἦ κέ μοι αίνὸν ἀπὸ πραπίδων ἄχος ἔλθοι [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 22.43; ἀπὸ πραπίδων ἦλθ᾽ ἵμερος 24.514]]; of sounds, etc., τὸν..περὶ φρένας ἤλυθ᾽ ίωή [Refs 8th c.BC+ [10.139; Κύκλωπα περὶ φρένας ἤλυθεν οἶνος 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 9.362]]; without φρένας, περὶ δέ σφεας ἤλυθ᾽ ι>ωή [Refs [17.261, compare 16.6]]; of battle, ὁμόσ᾽ ἦλθε μάχη [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 13.337]]; of things sent or taken, ὄφρα κε δῶρα ἐκ κλισίης ἔλθῃσι [Refs [19.191, compare 1.120]]; so later, especially of danger or evil, with dative, εἰ πάλιν ἔλθοι τῇ Ἑλλάδι κίνδυνος ὑπὸ βαρβάρων [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Historia Graeca (Hellenica)” 6.5.43; ἦλθεν αὐτῷ Ζηνὸς βέλος 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Prometheus Vinctus” 360; μηδ᾽ ὑπ᾽ ἀνάγκας γάμος ἔλθοι [prev. author] “Supp.” 1032 (Lyric poetry), compare “Pers.” 436]]; of reports, commands, etc., [Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. author] “Pr.” 663, 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 8.19]]; τοῖς Ἀθηναίοις ὡς ἦλθε τὰ γεγενημένα came to their ears, [Refs [[prev. work] 96]]; τὰ ἐρχόμενα ἐπ᾽ αὐτόν that which was about to happen to him, [NT.John.18.4]; of property, which comes or passes to a person by bequest, conveyance, gift, etc., τὰ ἐληλυθότα εἴς με ἀπὸ κληρονομίας [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [“BGU” 919.7 (2nd c.AD)]]; ἐ. εἴς τινα ἀπὸ παραχωρήσεως, κατὰ δωρεάν, [Refs 3rd c.AD+ [“PLond.” 3.1164e6 (3rd c.AD), “PMasp.” 96.22 (6th c.AD)]]: —Geometry texts, pass, fall, ἔ. ἐπὶ τὸ αὐτὸ σαμεῖον pass through the same point, [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [3rd c.BC: Archimedes Geometra “περὶ ἰσορροπιῶν” 1.15]]; ὅπου ἂν ἔρχηται τὸ ἕτερον σαμεῖον wherever the other point falls, [Refs [[prev. work] 2.10.]]

__B
Post-Homeric phrases:

__B.1
ἐς λόγους ἔρχεσθαί τινι come to speech with, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 6.86.α᾽, 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Coloneus” 1164 codices; so ἐς ὄψιν τινὶ ἐλθεῖν 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 3.42.]]

__B.2
εἰς χεῖρας ἐλθεῖν τινι (see. χείρ); so ἐς μάχην ἐλθεῖν τινι [Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. author] 7.9. ; είς ὸργάς τισιν 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 572a.]]

__B.3
ἐπὶ μεῖζον ἔ. increase, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Philoctetes” 259; ἐπὶ μηδέν [prev. author] “fragment” 871.8, “El.” 1000]]; ἐπὶ πᾶν ἐλθεῖν try everything, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 3.1.18.]]

__B.4
ἐς τὸ δεινόν, ἐς τὰ ἀλγεινὰ ἐλθεῖν, come into danger, etc., [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 3.45, 2.39; είς τοσοῦτον αίσχύνης ἐληλύθατον ὥστε.. 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Gorgias” 487b, etc.; εἰς τὸ ἔσχατον ἀδικίας [prev. author] “R.” 361d]]; ἐπ᾽ ἔσχατον ἐλθεῖν ἀηδίας Id [Refs [“Phdr.” 240d]]; ὅσοι ἐνταῦθα ἦλθον ἡλικίας arrived at that time of life, [Refs [[prev. author] “R.” 329b]]; ἐς ἀσθενὲς ἔ. come to an impotent conclusion, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.120]]; ἐς ἀριθμὸν ἐλθεῖν to be numbered, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 2.72; εἰς ἔρωτά τινος ἐλθεῖν 4th c.BC: Anaxilas Comicus 21.6; εἰς ἔλεγχον 4th-3rd c.BC: Philemo Comicus 93.3, etc.]]; εἰς ἑαυτὸν ἐλθεῖν come to oneself, [NT+2nd c.AD+ [NT.Luke.15.17, 2nd c.AD: Arrianus Historicus “Epicteti Dissertationes” 3.1.15.]]

__B.5
παρὰ μικρὸν ἐλθεῖν with infinitive, come within a little of, be near a thing, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Heraclidae” 296 (_anapaest meter_); παρ᾽ ὀλίγον ἐλθεῖν 1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus “Pyrrhus” 10]]; παρὰ τοσοῦτον ἡ Μυτιλήνη ἦλθε κινδύνου so narrow was her escape, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 3.49; παρ᾽ οὐδὲν ἐλθόντες τοῦ ἀποβαλεῖν 2nd c.BC: Polybius Historicus 1.45.14; παρ᾽ οὐδὲν ἐλθ. ἀπολέσθαι 1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus “Camillus” 8.]]

__B.6
with διά and genitive, periphrastic for a Verb, e.g. διὰ μάχης τινὶ ἐλθεῖν for μάχεσθαί τινι [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 6.9, 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Helena” 978, 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 4.92]]; διὰ πυρὸς ἐλθεῖν τινι rage furiously against.., [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Andromache” 488 (Lyric poetry)]]; but οί διὰ πάντων τῶν καλῶν ἐληλυθότες who have gone through the whole circle of duties, have fulfilled them all, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 1.2.15; διὰ πολλῶν κινδύνων ἐλθόντες 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus Alcaeus2.142a.]]

__B.7
ἔ. παρὰ τὴν γυναῖκα, παρὰ Ἀρίστωνα, of sexual intercourse, go in to her, to him, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 2.115, 6.68]]; πρός τινα, of marriage, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Oeconomicus” 7.5.]]

__B.8
ἔ. ἐπὶ πόλιν attack, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 2.11.]]

__B.9
ἔ. ἐς depend upon or be concerned with, τό γ᾽ εἰς ἀνθρώπους ἐλθόν [Refs 1st c.BC+ [2nd c.AD: Aristides Rhetor 1.149 1st c.AD: Josephus Historicus; τοῖς λογισμοῖς εἰς ἑαυτοὺς ἐρχόμενοι 1st c.BC: Diodorus Siculus Historicus 13.95; ὅσα εἰς ἀρετὴν ἔρχεται 4th c.AD: Libanius Sophista “Orationes” 22.18; τῶν πραττομένων οὐκ όλίγον εἰς ἐκεῖνον ἤρχετο [prev. work] 14.31.]]

ἐρωτάω, -ῶ
[in LXX chiefly for שָׁאַל ;]
__1. to ask, question (cl.): absol., Luk.19:31 22:68, Jhn.8:7 with accusative of person(s), Jhn.9:21 16:19, 30 8:21; before λέγων, Mat.16:13, Luk.23:3, Jhn.1:19, 21 5:12 9:19 16:5; with dupl. accusative (WM, § 32, 4a), Mat.21:24, Mrk.4:10, Luk.20:3, Jhn.16:23 (M, Pr., 66„); with accusative of person(s), before περί, Luk.9:45, Jhn.18:19.
__2. In late Gk. (Milligan, NTD, 51; not, as Cremer, 716, Thayer, see word, a "Hebraism"), = αἰτέω (which see), to ask, request: with accusative of person(s), Jhn.14:16; before imperat., Luk.14:18-19 Php.4:3; λέγων, Mat.15:23, Jhn.12:21; before ἵνα (M, Pr., 208), Mrk.7:26, Luk.7:36 16:27, Jhn.4:47 17:15 19:31, 38, 1Th.4:1, 2Jn.5; ὅπως, Luk.7:3 11:37, Act.23:20; with inf., Luk.5:3 8:37, Jhn.4:40, Act.3:3 10:48 23:18, 1Th.5:12; with accusative of person(s), before περί, Luk.4:38 Jhn.17:9, 20, 1Jn.5:16; ὑπέρ, 2Th.2:1-2; τὰ (WH, txt., om. τὰ) πρὸς εἰρήνην, Luk.14:32 (cf. δι-, ἐπ-ερωτάω)
SYN.: see: αἰτέω  (AS)

deep_entry:
Abbott-Smith / STEPBible (TBESG)
εἰμί,
with various uses and significations, like the English verb to be.
__I. As substantive verb.
__1. Of persons and things, to be, exist: Act.17:28, Jhn.1:1, 8:58, 17:5, al; ὁ ὢν καὶ ὁ ἦν (for past ptcp.), Rev.1:4, 8, 4:8, 11:17, 16:5 (see Swete, Ap., 5; M, Pr., 228); τὰ (μὴ) ὄντα, Rom.4:17, 1Co.1:28.
__2. Of times, events, etc., to be, happen, take place: Mat.24:3, Mrk.14:2, 15:42, Luk.21:23, Jhn.4:6, 23, 5:10, al.
__3. to be present, be in a place, have come: Mat.2:13, 15, Mrk.1:45, 5:21, 15:40, Luk.1:80, 5:29, Jhn.7:30, al.; before εἰς, Mrk.2:1; before  ἐκ, (ἐξ), Mat.1:20, 21:25, Mrk.11:30, Jhn.3:31, al.
__4. Impers.,  ἔστι, ἦν, etc.;
__(a) there is (Fr. il y a), was, etc.: Mat.16:28, Luk.16:19, Jhn.3:1, 5:2, Rom.3:10, al.; with dative (of the possessor; Bl., §37, 3), Mat.16:22, Luk.1:7, Jhn.18.10, Rom.9:2, al.;  ἔστιν ὅς, ὅστις (chiefly in pl), Mat.16:28, 19:2, Mrk.9:1, al.;
__(b) with inf., = ἔξεστιν (which see), it is possible: Heb.9:5, 1Co.11:20, RV (but see ICC, in l.).
__II. As copula uniting subject and predicate.
__1. Expressing simply identity or equivalence: Mat.5:13, 14:15, Luk.1:18, 19, Jhn.1:1, 4:19, Rev.3:9, al. mult.
__2. Explicative, as in parable, figure, type, etc.: Mat.13:19, 1Co.9:2, 10:4, 11:25, Gal.4:24, Rev.17:15, al.; ταῦτ᾽ ἔστιν, Mat.27:46, Mrk.7:2, Rom.7:18 al.; ὅ ἐστιν, Mrk.3:17, Col.1:24, Heb.7:2, al.; akin to this is the sacramental usage: Mat.26:26-28, Mrk.14:22, 24, Luk.22:19, 1Co.11:24 (see ICC on Mk, I Co, ll. with; DB, iii, 148 f.).
__3. C. genitive: qual., etc., Mrk.5:42, Luk.3:23, 1Co.14:33, Heb.12:11, al.; part., 1Ti.1:20, 2Ti.1:15; poss., Mat.5:3, 10, Mrk.12:7, Luk.4:7; of service or partisanship, Rom.8:9, 1Co.1:12, 2Co.10:7, 2Ti.2:19.
__4. C. dative (BL, §37, 3): Act.1:8, 9:15, Rom.4:12, 1Co.1:18, 2:14, Rev.21:7, al.
__5. C. ptcp., as a periphrasis for the simple verb (Bl., §62, 1, 2; M, Pr., 225 ff.);
__(a) with ptcp. pf. (cl.): Mat.10:30, Luk.9:32, Jhn.3:24, Act.21:35, 1Co.15:19, al;
__(b) with ptcp. pr. (esp. in impf., as in Heb. and Aram.; Dalman, Words, 35 f.), Mat.7:29, Mrk.1:22, Luk.4:31, 14:1, Act.1:10, al. mult., id. for imper. (M, Pr., 180f., 182f.), with ellipsis of εἰμί, Rom.12:9, 10, Heb.13:5, al.;
__(with) with ptcp. aor. (cl), Luk.23:9.
__6. Seq. εἰς (cf. Heb. הָיָה לְ), a vernac. usage (M, Pr., 71): Mat.19:5, Mrk.10:8, Heb.8:10, al.
__7. C. adv.: Mat.19:20, Mrk.4:26, Luk.18:11, al.
__8. Ellipses;
__(a) of the copula (Bl., §30, 3): Mat.8:29, 24:32, Jhn.21:22, 23, Heb.6:4, al.;
__(b) of the predicate: ἐγώ εἰμί, Mat.14:27, Mrk.6:50, al.; absol. (cf. Deu.32:39; אֲנִי הוּא), Mrk.13:6, Jhn.4:26, al. (cf. ἄπ-, ἔν-, πάρ-, συμ-πάρ-, σύν-ειμι).
(AS)

ἐ. ὅπῃ, ἔσθ᾽ ὅπου, somehow, somewhere, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Protagoras” 331d, 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Eumenides” 517, 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Tyrannus” 448, etc.]]; in questions expecting a negative answer, ἐ. ὁπόθεν, ὅπω; [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Philebus” 35a, “R.” 493e, etc.; οὐ γάρ ἐσθ᾽ ὅπως 5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “Fragmenta.” 61, compare 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 7.102, 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Agamemnon” 620]]; οὐκ ἔ. ὅπως οὐ in any case, necessarily, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Pax” 188; οὐκ ἔ. ὡς 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Meno” 76e, etc.]]; ἐ. ὅτε, ἔσθ᾽ ὅτε, sometimes, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “Fragmenta.” 180.2, 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Ajax” 56, 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 7.21, etc.]]

__A.V
ἦν is sometimes used with plural masculine and feminine, usually at the beginning of a sentence, there was, τῆς δ᾽ ἦν τρεῖς κεφαλαί [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th-7th c.BC: Hesiodus Epicus “Theogonia” 321; (but in ἦν δ᾽ ἐρῳδιοί τε πολλοί 5th c.BC: Epicharmus Comicus 46, compare 59, +others, it may be taken as _Doric dialect_ _3rd.pers._ _plural_)]]; ἦν δ᾽ ἀμφίπλεκτοι κλίμακες [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Trachiniae” 520 (Lyric poetry)]]; ἦν ἄρα κἀκεῖνοι ταλακάρδιοι epigram cited in [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aeschines Orator 3.184; less frequently ἔστι, ἔστι δὲ μεταξὺ.. ἑπτὰ στάδιοι 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.26, compare 7.34; ἔστι.. ἄρχοντές τε καὶ δῆμος 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 463a]]; before dual Nouns, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Vespae” 58, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Gorgias” 500d.]]

__A.VI
ἔστι impersonal, with infinitive, it is possible, ἔστι γὰρ ἀμφοτέροισιν ὀνείδεα μυθήσασθαι [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 20.246; ἔστι μὲν εὕδειν, ἔστι δὲ τερπομένοισιν ἀκούειν 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 15.392]]; εἴ τί πού ἐστι (i.e. πιθέσθαι)[Refs 5th c.BC+ [4.193; τοιάδε.. ἐστὶν ἀκοῦσαι 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Prometheus Vinctus” 1055 (_anapaest meter_); ἔστι τεκμήρια ὁρᾶν 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 3.2.13, compare 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Ranae” 1163, 4th c.BC: Aeschines Orator 3.105, 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 18.272, 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Ἀθηναίων Πολιτεία” 53.6, etc.]]; so in imperative, optative, and subjunctive, ἔστω ἀποφέρεσθαι τῷ βουλομένῳ [Refs 8th c.BC+ [“IG” 12.10.7; μυρία ἂν εἴη λέγειν 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Politicus” 271e; ὅπως ἂν ᾖ δρᾶν “IG” 2.1054.91: more frequently in _negative_ clauses, 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 6.267, etc.]]; followed by ὥστε with infinitive, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Philoctetes” 656]]: with accusative et infinitive, ἁδόντα δ᾽ εἴη με τοῖς ἀγαθοῖς ὁμιλεῖν [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “P.” 2.96; ἔστιν ἐκπεσεῖν ἀρχῆς Δία 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Prometheus Vinctus” 757]]: sometimes not impersonal in this sense, θάλασσα δ᾽ οὐκέτ᾽ ἦν ἰδεῖν [Refs [[prev. author] “Pers.” 419.]]

__A.VI.b
ἔστω in argument, let it be granted, ἔστω τοῦτο ἀληθὲς εἶναι [Refs 4th c.BC+ [1st c.BC: Dionysius Halicarnassensis “de Compositione Verborum” 25; ἔστω σοι τοῦθ᾽ οὕτως 1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus 2.987b; ἔστω εἶναί τινα τοιοῦτον 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator Chr.74.24.]]

__B
most frequently, to be, the Copula connecting the predicate with the Subject, both being in the same case: hence, signify, import, τὸ γὰρ εἴρειν λέγειν ἐστίν [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Cratylus” 398d]]; especially in the phrase τοῦτ᾽ ἔστι, hoc est; Σκαιόλαν, ὅπερ ἐστὶ Λαϊόν [Refs 1st c.AD+ [1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus “Publicola” 17: with numerals, τὰ δὶς πέντε δέκα ἐστίν]] twice five are ten, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Memorabilia” 4.4.7]]; εἶναί τις or τι, to be somebody, something, be of some consequence, see at {τι; οὐδὲν εἶναι} [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 562d, etc.]]

__B.2
periphrastic with the Participle to represent the finite Verb: with perfect participle once in [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Homerus Epicus, τετληότες εἰμέν, for τετλήκαμεν, 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 5.873]]; so in Trag. and Attic dialect, ἦν τεθνηκώς, for ἐτεθνήκει, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Agamemnon” 869]]; ἔσται δεδορκώς[Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. work] 1179; εἰμὶ γεγώς 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Ajax” 1299; πεφυκός ἐστι 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Aves” 1473; δεδρακότες εἰσίν 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 3.68; κατακεκονότες ἔσεσθε 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 7.6.36]]: with aorist participle, once in [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Homerus Epicus, βλήμενος ἦν 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 4.211]]; so προδείσας εἰμί, οὐ σιωπήσας ἔσε; [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Tyrannus” 90, 1146, compare 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Supplices” 460]]: with present participle, ἦν προκείμενον [Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. author] “Pers.” 371; φεύγων Ὀρέστης ἐστίν [prev. author] “Ch.” 136; εἴην οὐκ ἂν εὖ φρονῶν 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Ajax” 1330]]; τί δ᾽ ἐστί.. φέρο; [Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. author] “OT” 991, compare 274, 708; λέγων ἐστίν τις 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Hecuba” 1179; ἦν τίς σ᾽ ὑβρίζων [prev. author] “HF” 313; πόρρω ἤδη εἶ πορευόμενος 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Lysis” 204b; βαδίζων εἰμί 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Ranae” 36; frequently in 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus, ἦσαν ἱέντες 1.57, +others; even εἰσὶ διάφοροι ἐόντες 3.49 (assuming variant):]] — if the _Article_ is joined with the Part., the noun is made emphatic, Κᾶρές εἰσι οἱ καταδέξαντες the persons who showed her were Carians, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. author] 1.171; αὐτὸς ἦν ὁ μαρτυρῶν 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Eumenides” 798; δόλος ἦν ὁ φράσας 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Electra” 197 (_anapaest meter_).]]

__C
εἶναι is frequently modified in sense by the addition of adverbs, or the cases of Nouns without or with Preps.:

__C.I
εἶναι with adverbs, where the adverb often merely represents a Noun and stands as the predicate, ἅλις δέ οἱ ἦσαν ἄρουραι [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 14.122, etc.]]; ἀκέων, ἀκήν εἶναι, to be silent,[Refs 8th c.BC+ [4.22, 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 2.82; σῖγα πᾶς ἔστω λεώς 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Hecuba” 532; διαγνῶναι χαλεπῶς ἦν ἄνδρα ἕκαστον 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 7.424]]; ἀσφαλέως ἡ κομιδὴ ἔσται will go on safely, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 4.134]]; ἐγγύς, πόρρω εἶναι, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 6.88, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Protagoras” 356e: frequently _impersonal_ with words implying good or ill fortune, Κουρήτεσσι κακῶς ἦν]] it fared ill with them, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 9.551; εὖ γὰρ ἔσται 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Medea” 89, compare 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Plutus” 1188, etc.; ἡδέως ἂν αὐτοῖς εἴη 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 59.30.]]

__C.II
with genitive, to express descent or extraction, πατρὸς δ᾽ εἴμ᾽ ἀγαθοῖο [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 21.109; αἵματός εἰς ἀγαθοῖο 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 4.611, compare 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 3.71, 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 2.71, etc.; πόλεως μεγίστης εἶ 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 7.3.19.]]

__C.II.b
to express the material of which a thing is made, ἡ κρηπίς ἐστι λίθων μεγάλων consists of.., [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.93; τῆς πόλιος ἐούσης δύο φαρσέων [prev. work] 186]]; τοιούτων ἔργων ἐστὶ ἡ τυραννίς is made up of.., [Refs [[prev. author] 5.92]].ή, etc.

__C.II.c
to express the class to which a person or thing belongs, εἶ γὰρ τῶν φίλων you are one of them, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Plutus” 345; ἐτύγχανε βουλῆς ὤν 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 3.70; ὅσοι ἦσαν τῶν προτέρων στρατιωτῶν [prev. author] 7.44; Κριτίας τῶν τριάκοντα ὤν 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Memorabilia” 1.2.31]]; ἔστι τῶν αἰσχρῶν it is in the class of disgraceful things, i. e. it is disgraceful, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 2.2.]]

__C.II.d
to express that a thing belongs to another, Τροίαν Ἀχαιῶν οὖσαν [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Agamemnon” 269; τὸ πεδίον ἦν μέν κοτε Χορασμίων 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 3.117, etc.]]: hence, to be of the party of, ἦσαν.. τινὲς μὲν φιλίππου, τινὲς δὲ τοῦ βελτίστου [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 9.56, compare 37.53]]; to be de pendent upon, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Antigone” 737, etc.]]; to be at the mercy of, ἔστι τοῦ λέγοντος, ἢν φόβους λέγῃ [Refs [[prev. author] “OT” 917.]]

__C.II.e
to express one's duty, business, custom, nature, and the like, οὔτοι γυναικός ἐστι 'tis not a woman's part, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Agamemnon” 940; τὸ ἐπιτιμᾶν παντὸς εἶναι 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 1.16]]; τὸ δὲ ναυτικὸν τέχνης ἐστίν is matter of art, requires art, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 1.142, compare 83.]]

__C.II.f
in LXX, to be occupied about, ἦσαν τοῦ θύειν [LXX.2Ch.30.17]; ἔσεσθαι, with genitive, to be about to, ἐσόμεθα τοῦ σῶσαί σε [LXX.2Ki.10.11.]

__C.III
with the dative, ἐστί μοι I have, frequently in [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Homerus Epicus, etc.]]

__C.III.2
with two datives., σφίσι τε καὶ Ἀθηναίοισι εἶναι οὐδὲν πρῆγμα that they and the Athenians have nothing to do one with another, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 5.84; μηδὲν εἶναι σοὶ καὶ φιλίππῳ πρᾶγμα 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 18.283]]; more shortly, σοί τε καὶ τούτοισι πρήγμασι τί ἐστ; [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 5.33]]; τί τῷ νόμῳ καὶ τῇ βασάν; [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 29.36]]; τί ἐμοὶ καὶ σο; Latin quid tecum est mihi? [NT.Mark.5.7, etc.]; also ἐμοὶ οὐδὲν πρὸς τοὺς τοιούτους (i.e. ἐστίν) [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Isocrates Orator 4.12; ἐν οἷς πρὸς τοὺς ἐναντίους ἐστὶ τῷ δήμῳ 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 18.278]]; ἔσται αὐτῳ πρὸς τὸν θεόν, in tomb inscriptions, [Refs [“JHS” 18.113, etc.]]

__C.III.3
with ἄσμενος, βουλόμενος, etc., added, ἐμοὶ δέ κεν ἀσμένῳ εἴη 'twould be to my delight, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 14.108; οὐκ ἂν σφίσι βουλομένοις εἶναι 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 7.35; προσδεχομένῳ [prev. author] 6.46; θέλοντι 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Tyrannus” 1356 (Lyric poetry); ἡδομένοις 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Laches” 187c.]]

__C.IV
with Preps., εἶναι ἀπό τινος, ={εἶναί τινος}[Refs 5th c.BC+ [(above 11.a), 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Memorabilia” 1.6.9; εἰσὶν ἀπ᾽ ἐναντίων αὗται πραγμάτων 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Philebus” 12d]]; but εἶναι ἀπ᾽ οἴκου to be away from.., [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 1.99.]]

__C.IV.2
εἶναι ἔκ τινος to be sprung from, εἴμ᾽ ἐκ Παιονίης, Μυρμιδόνων ἔξ εἰμι, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 21.154, 24.397, etc.]]; ἔστιν ἐξ ἀνάγκης it is of necessity, i. e. necessary, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Sophista” 256d.]]

__C.IV.3
εἶναι ἐν.. to be in a certain state, ἐν εὐπαθείῃσι [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.22]]; ἐν ἀθυμία, etc., [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 6.46, etc.; ἐν ταραχαῖς 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 18.218]]; εἶναι ἐν ἀξιώματι to be in esteem, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 1.130]]; οἱ ἐν τέλεϊ ἐόντες those in office, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 3.18, etc.]]; but εἶναι ἐν τέχνῃ, ἐν φιλοσοφία to be engaged in.., [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Tyrannus” 562, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Phaedo” 59a.]]

__C.IV.3.b
ἐν σοί ἐστι it depends on thee, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 6.109, 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Philoctetes” 963; ἐν σοὶ γάρ ἐσμεν [prev. author] “OT” 314; so also ἐπί τινι [prev. author] “Ph.” 1003, 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 1.6.2, etc.]]

__C.IV.4
εἶναι διά.., much like{εἶναι ἐν}.., εἶναι διὰ φόβου, ={φοβεῖσθαι}, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 6.34]]; εἶναι δι᾽ ὄχλου, ={ὀχληρὸν εἶναι}, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. author] 1.73; εἶναι διὰ μόχθων 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 1.6.25]]; εἶναι δι᾽ αἰτίας, ={αἰτιᾶσθαι}, [Refs 1st c.BC+ [1st c.BC: Dionysius Halicarnassensis 1.70]]; Geometry texts, pass through, διὰ τᾶς ἑτέρας διαμέτρου ἐόντος τοῦ ἐπιπέδου [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [3rd c.BC: Archimedes Geometra “περὶ κωνοειδέων καὶ σφαιροειδέων” 20.]]

__C.IV.5
εἶναι ἐφ᾽ ἑαυτῆς to be by oneself, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 25.23]]; εἶναι ἐπὶ ὀνόματος to bear a name, [Refs [[prev. author] 39.21]]; εἶναι ἐπὶ τοῖς πράγμασιν to be engaged in.., [Refs [[prev. author] 2.12]]; εἶναι ἐπί τινα to be against him, [Refs [[prev. author] 6.33]]; εἶναι ἐφ᾽ ἑξήκοντα στάδια to reach sixty stadia, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 4.6.11]]; εἶναι ἐπὶ τὰς ἁφάς pass through the points of contact, [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd c.AD: Apollonius Biographus Perg. “Con.” 4.1]]; εἶναι ἐπί τινι, see above 3 b.

__C.IV.6
εἶναι πρός τινος to be in one's favour, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 4.10, 29, etc.]]; to suit, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 1.2.11, etc.]]; εἶναι πρός τινι engaged in, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Phaedo” 84c, 2nd-3rd c.AD: Philostratus Sophista “Vita Apollonii” 5.31]]; πρὸς τοῖς ἰδίοις mind one's own affairs, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Politica” 1309a6, “Ath.” 16.3; εἶναι πρὸς τὸ κωλύειν 2nd c.BC: Polybius Historicus 1.26.3]]; πρὸς τὸ πονεῖν[Refs 5th c.BC+ [Teles p.46 H.; εἶναι περί τι 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 3.5.7, etc.]]

__C.IV.7
εἶναι παρά τινι or τινα, = παρειναι, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. author] “Cyr.” 6.2.15, 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 8.140.ά]] (assuming variant).

__C.IV.8
εἶναι ὑπό τινα or τινι to be subject to.., [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Historia Graeca (Hellenica)” 5.2.17 (assuming variant), 6.2.4.]]

__C.IV.9
περὶ τούτων ἐστίν that is the question, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-3rd c.BC: Menander Comicus “Ἐπιτρέποντες” 30.]]

__C.IV.10
εἶναι ἀπό.., in Geometry texts, to be constructed upon, [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [3rd c.BC: Archimedes Geometra “περὶ σφαίρας καὶ κυλίνδρου” 2.9, “Con.Sph.” 7.]]

__D
ἐστί is very frequently omitted, mostly in the present indicative before certain predicates, as ἀνάγκη, ἄξιον, δυνατόν, εἰκός, ἕτοιμον, οἷόν τε, ῥᾴδιον, χρεών, etc., and after the neuter of Verbals in -τέος, and such forms as θαυμαστὸν ὅσον: less frequently with other persons and moods, εἰμί omitted, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Tyrannus” 92, “Aj.” 813]]; εἶ, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 4.206]]; ἐσμέν, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Antigone” 634]]; ἐστέ, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 10.463]]; εἰσί, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Tyrannus” 499 (Lyric poetry), “IG” 2.778 B]]; subjunctive ᾖ, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 14.376, 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Hippolytus” 659, 5th c.BC: Antipho Orator 5.32]]; optative εἴη, [Refs [“IG” 22.1183.12]]; imperfect ἦν, [Refs [[prev. work]2.778 B]]; future ἔσονται, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 14.394.]]

__E
the Inf. frequently seems redundant,

__E.1

after ἄρα, to express a fact which is and has always been the same, δέρμα δὲ ἀνθρώπου.. ἦν ἄρα σχεδὸν δερμάτων πάντων λαμπρότατον human skin then it appears is.., [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 4.64; Κύπρις οὐκ ἄρ᾽ ἦν θεός 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Hippolytus” 359]]; ὡς ἄρ᾽ ἦσθ᾽ ἐμὸς πατὴρ ὀρθῶς[Refs 3rd c.BC+ [[prev. work] 1169; ἦ πολύμοχθον ἄρ᾽ ἦν γένος.. ἁμερίων [prev. author] “IA” 1330; ἦ στωμύλος ἦσθα 3rd c.BC: Theocritus Poeta Bucolicus 5.79]]; so also when there is reference to a past thought, τουτὶ τί ἦ; what is this? Abbott-Smith / STEPBible (TBESG)
εἰμί,
with various uses and significations, like the English verb to be.
__I. As substantive verb.
__1. Of persons and things, to be, exist: Act.17:28, Jhn.1:1, 8:58, 17:5, al; ὁ ὢν καὶ ὁ ἦν (for past ptcp.), Rev.1:4, 8, 4:8, 11:17, 16:5 (see Swete, Ap., 5; M, Pr., 228); τὰ (μὴ) ὄντα, Rom.4:17, 1Co.1:28.
__2. Of times, events, etc., to be, happen, take place: Mat.24:3, Mrk.14:2, 15:42, Luk.21:23, Jhn.4:6, 23, 5:10, al.
__3. to be present, be in a place, have come: Mat.2:13, 15, Mrk.1:45, 5:21, 15:40, Luk.1:80, 5:29, Jhn.7:30, al.; before εἰς, Mrk.2:1; before  ἐκ, (ἐξ), Mat.1:20, 21:25, Mrk.11:30, Jhn.3:31, al.
__4. Impers.,  ἔστι, ἦν, etc.;
__(a) there is (Fr. il y a), was, etc.: Mat.16:28, Luk.16:19, Jhn.3:1, 5:2, Rom.3:10, al.; with dative (of the possessor; Bl., §37, 3), Mat.16:22, Luk.1:7, Jhn.18.10, Rom.9:2, al.;  ἔστιν ὅς, ὅστις (chiefly in pl), Mat.16:28, 19:2, Mrk.9:1, al.;
__(b) with inf., = ἔξεστιν (which see), it is possible: Heb.9:5, 1Co.11:20, RV (but see ICC, in l.).
__II. As copula uniting subject and predicate.
__1. Expressing simply identity or equivalence: Mat.5:13, 14:15, Luk.1:18, 19, Jhn.1:1, 4:19, Rev.3:9, al. mult.
__2. Explicative, as in parable, figure, type, etc.: Mat.13:19, 1Co.9:2, 10:4, 11:25, Gal.4:24, Rev.17:15, al.; ταῦτ᾽ ἔστιν, Mat.27:46, Mrk.7:2, Rom.7:18 al.; ὅ ἐστιν, Mrk.3:17, Col.1:24, Heb.7:2, al.; akin to this is the sacramental usage: Mat.26:26-28, Mrk.14:22, 24, Luk.22:19, 1Co.11:24 (see ICC on Mk, I Co, ll. with; DB, iii, 148 f.).
__3. C. genitive: qual., etc., Mrk.5:42, Luk.3:23, 1Co.14:33, Heb.12:11, al.; part., 1Ti.1:20, 2Ti.1:15; poss., Mat.5:3, 10, Mrk.12:7, Luk.4:7; of service or partisanship, Rom.8:9, 1Co.1:12, 2Co.10:7, 2Ti.2:19.
__4. C. dative (BL, §37, 3): Act.1:8, 9:15, Rom.4:12, 1Co.1:18, 2:14, Rev.21:7, al.
__5. C. ptcp., as a periphrasis for the simple verb (Bl., §62, 1, 2; M, Pr., 225 ff.);
__(a) with ptcp. pf. (cl.): Mat.10:30, Luk.9:32, Jhn.3:24, Act.21:35, 1Co.15:19, al;
__(b) with ptcp. pr. (esp. in impf., as in Heb. and Aram.; Dalman, Words, 35 f.), Mat.7:29, Mrk.1:22, Luk.4:31, 14:1, Act.1:10, al. mult., id. for imper. (M, Pr., 180f., 182f.), with ellipsis of εἰμί, Rom.12:9, 10, Heb.13:5, al.;
__(with) with ptcp. aor. (cl), Luk.23:9.
__6. Seq. εἰς (cf. Heb. הָיָה לְ), a vernac. usage (M, Pr., 71): Mat.19:5, Mrk.10:8, Heb.8:10, al.
__7. C. adv.: Mat.19:20, Mrk.4:26, Luk.18:11, al.
__8. Ellipses;
__(a) of the copula (Bl., §30, 3): Mat.8:29, 24:32, Jhn.21:22, 23, Heb.6:4, al.;
__(b) of the predicate: ἐγώ εἰμί, Mat.14:27, Mrk.6:50, al.; absol. (cf. Deu.32:39; אֲנִי הוּא), Mrk.13:6, Jhn.4:26, al. (cf. ἄπ-, ἔν-, πάρ-, συμ-πάρ-, σύν-ειμι).
