most frequently, to be, the Copula connecting the predicate with the Subject, both being in the same case: hence, signify, import, τὸ γὰρ εἴρειν λέγειν ἐστίν [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Cratylus” 398d]]; especially in the phrase τοῦτ᾽ ἔστι, hoc est; Σκαιόλαν, ὅπερ ἐστὶ Λαϊόν [Refs 1st c.AD+ [1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus “Publicola” 17: with numerals, τὰ δὶς πέντε δέκα ἐστίν]] twice five are ten, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Memorabilia” 4.4.7]]; εἶναί τις or τι, to be somebody, something, be of some consequence, see at {τι; οὐδὲν εἶναι} [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 562d, etc.]]

__B.2
periphrastic with the Participle to represent the finite Verb: with perfect participle once in [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Homerus Epicus, τετληότες εἰμέν, for τετλήκαμεν, 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 5.873]]; so in Trag. and Attic dialect, ἦν τεθνηκώς, for ἐτεθνήκει, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Agamemnon” 869]]; ἔσται δεδορκώς[Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. work] 1179; εἰμὶ γεγώς 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Ajax” 1299; πεφυκός ἐστι 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Aves” 1473; δεδρακότες εἰσίν 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 3.68; κατακεκονότες ἔσεσθε 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 7.6.36]]: with aorist participle, once in [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Homerus Epicus, βλήμενος ἦν 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 4.211]]; so προδείσας εἰμί, οὐ σιωπήσας ἔσε; [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Tyrannus” 90, 1146, compare 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Supplices” 460]]: with present participle, ἦν προκείμενον [Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. author] “Pers.” 371; φεύγων Ὀρέστης ἐστίν [prev. author] “Ch.” 136; εἴην οὐκ ἂν εὖ φρονῶν 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Ajax” 1330]]; τί δ᾽ ἐστί.. φέρο; [Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. author] “OT” 991, compare 274, 708; λέγων ἐστίν τις 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Hecuba” 1179; ἦν τίς σ᾽ ὑβρίζων [prev. author] “HF” 313; πόρρω ἤδη εἶ πορευόμενος 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Lysis” 204b; βαδίζων εἰμί 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Ranae” 36; frequently in 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus, ἦσαν ἱέντες 1.57, +others; even εἰσὶ διάφοροι ἐόντες 3.49 (assuming variant):]] — if the _Article_ is joined with the Part., the noun is made emphatic, Κᾶρές εἰσι οἱ καταδέξαντες the persons who showed her were Carians, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. author] 1.171; αὐτὸς ἦν ὁ μαρτυρῶν 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Eumenides” 798; δόλος ἦν ὁ φράσας 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Electra” 197 (_anapaest meter_).]]

__C
εἶναι is frequently modified in sense by the addition of adverbs, or the cases of Nouns without or with Preps.:

__C.I
εἶναι with adverbs, where the adverb often merely represents a Noun and stands as the predicate, ἅλις δέ οἱ ἦσαν ἄρουραι [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 14.122, etc.]]; ἀκέων, ἀκήν εἶναι, to be silent,[Refs 8th c.BC+ [4.22, 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 2.82; σῖγα πᾶς ἔστω λεώς 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Hecuba” 532; διαγνῶναι χαλεπῶς ἦν ἄνδρα ἕκαστον 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 7.424]]; ἀσφαλέως ἡ κομιδὴ ἔσται will go on safely, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 4.134]]; ἐγγύς, πόρρω εἶναι, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 6.88, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Protagoras” 356e: frequently _impersonal_ with words implying good or ill fortune, Κουρήτεσσι κακῶς ἦν]] it fared ill with them, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 9.551; εὖ γὰρ ἔσται 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Medea” 89, compare 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Plutus” 1188, etc.; ἡδέως ἂν αὐτοῖς εἴη 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 59.30.]]

__C.II
with genitive, to express descent or extraction, πατρὸς δ᾽ εἴμ᾽ ἀγαθοῖο [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 21.109; αἵματός εἰς ἀγαθοῖο 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 4.611, compare 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 3.71, 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 2.71, etc.; πόλεως μεγίστης εἶ 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 7.3.19.]]

__C.II.b
to express the material of which a thing is made, ἡ κρηπίς ἐστι λίθων μεγάλων consists of.., [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.93; τῆς πόλιος ἐούσης δύο φαρσέων [prev. work] 186]]; τοιούτων ἔργων ἐστὶ ἡ τυραννίς is made up of.., [Refs [[prev. author] 5.92]].ή, etc.

__C.II.c
to express the class to which a person or thing belongs, εἶ γὰρ τῶν φίλων you are one of them, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Plutus” 345; ἐτύγχανε βουλῆς ὤν 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 3.70; ὅσοι ἦσαν τῶν προτέρων στρατιωτῶν [prev. author] 7.44; Κριτίας τῶν τριάκοντα ὤν 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Memorabilia” 1.2.31]]; ἔστι τῶν αἰσχρῶν it is in the class of disgraceful things, i. e. it is disgraceful, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 2.2.]]

__C.II.d
to express that a thing belongs to another, Τροίαν Ἀχαιῶν οὖσαν [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Agamemnon” 269; τὸ πεδίον ἦν μέν κοτε Χορασμίων 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 3.117, etc.]]: hence, to be of the party of, ἦσαν.. τινὲς μὲν φιλίππου, τινὲς δὲ τοῦ βελτίστου [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 9.56, compare 37.53]]; to be de pendent upon, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Antigone” 737, etc.]]; to be at the mercy of, ἔστι τοῦ λέγοντος, ἢν φόβους λέγῃ [Refs [[prev. author] “OT” 917.]]

__C.II.e
to express one's duty, business, custom, nature, and the like, οὔτοι γυναικός ἐστι 'tis not a woman's part, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Agamemnon” 940; τὸ ἐπιτιμᾶν παντὸς εἶναι 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 1.16]]; τὸ δὲ ναυτικὸν τέχνης ἐστίν is matter of art, requires art, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 1.142, compare 83.]]

__C.II.f
in LXX, to be occupied about, ἦσαν τοῦ θύειν [LXX.2Ch.30.17]; ἔσεσθαι, with genitive, to be about to, ἐσόμεθα τοῦ σῶσαί σε [LXX.2Ki.10.11.]

__C.III
with the dative, ἐστί μοι I have, frequently in [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Homerus Epicus, etc.]]

__C.III.2
with two datives., σφίσι τε καὶ Ἀθηναίοισι εἶναι οὐδὲν πρῆγμα that they and the Athenians have nothing to do one with another, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 5.84; μηδὲν εἶναι σοὶ καὶ φιλίππῳ πρᾶγμα 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 18.283]]; more shortly, σοί τε καὶ τούτοισι πρήγμασι τί ἐστ; [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 5.33]]; τί τῷ νόμῳ καὶ τῇ βασάν; [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 29.36]]; τί ἐμοὶ καὶ σο; Latin quid tecum est mihi? [NT.Mark.5.7, etc.]; also ἐμοὶ οὐδὲν πρὸς τοὺς τοιούτους (i.e. ἐστίν) [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Isocrates Orator 4.12; ἐν οἷς πρὸς τοὺς ἐναντίους ἐστὶ τῷ δήμῳ 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 18.278]]; ἔσται αὐτῳ πρὸς τὸν θεόν, in tomb inscriptions, [Refs [“JHS” 18.113, etc.]]

__C.III.3
with ἄσμενος, βουλόμενος, etc., added, ἐμοὶ δέ κεν ἀσμένῳ εἴη 'twould be to my delight, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 14.108; οὐκ ἂν σφίσι βουλομένοις εἶναι 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 7.35; προσδεχομένῳ [prev. author] 6.46; θέλοντι 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Tyrannus” 1356 (Lyric poetry); ἡδομένοις 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Laches” 187c.]]

__C.IV
with Preps., εἶναι ἀπό τινος, ={εἶναί τινος}[Refs 5th c.BC+ [(above 11.a), 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Memorabilia” 1.6.9; εἰσὶν ἀπ᾽ ἐναντίων αὗται πραγμάτων 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Philebus” 12d]]; but εἶναι ἀπ᾽ οἴκου to be away from.., [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 1.99.]]

__C.IV.2
εἶναι ἔκ τινος to be sprung from, εἴμ᾽ ἐκ Παιονίης, Μυρμιδόνων ἔξ εἰμι, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 21.154, 24.397, etc.]]; ἔστιν ἐξ ἀνάγκης it is of necessity, i. e. necessary, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Sophista” 256d.]]

__C.IV.3
εἶναι ἐν.. to be in a certain state, ἐν εὐπαθείῃσι [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.22]]; ἐν ἀθυμία, etc., [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 6.46, etc.; ἐν ταραχαῖς 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 18.218]]; εἶναι ἐν ἀξιώματι to be in esteem, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 1.130]]; οἱ ἐν τέλεϊ ἐόντες those in office, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 3.18, etc.]]; but εἶναι ἐν τέχνῃ, ἐν φιλοσοφία to be engaged in.., [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Tyrannus” 562, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Phaedo” 59a.]]

__C.IV.3.b
ἐν σοί ἐστι it depends on thee, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 6.109, 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Philoctetes” 963; ἐν σοὶ γάρ ἐσμεν [prev. author] “OT” 314; so also ἐπί τινι [prev. author] “Ph.” 1003, 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 1.6.2, etc.]]

__C.IV.4
εἶναι διά.., much like{εἶναι ἐν}.., εἶναι διὰ φόβου, ={φοβεῖσθαι}, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 6.34]]; εἶναι δι᾽ ὄχλου, ={ὀχληρὸν εἶναι}, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. author] 1.73; εἶναι διὰ μόχθων 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 1.6.25]]; εἶναι δι᾽ αἰτίας, ={αἰτιᾶσθαι}, [Refs 1st c.BC+ [1st c.BC: Dionysius Halicarnassensis 1.70]]; Geometry texts, pass through, διὰ τᾶς ἑτέρας διαμέτρου ἐόντος τοῦ ἐπιπέδου [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [3rd c.BC: Archimedes Geometra “περὶ κωνοειδέων καὶ σφαιροειδέων” 20.]]

__C.IV.5
εἶναι ἐφ᾽ ἑαυτῆς to be by oneself, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 25.23]]; εἶναι ἐπὶ ὀνόματος to bear a name, [Refs [[prev. author] 39.21]]; εἶναι ἐπὶ τοῖς πράγμασιν to be engaged in.., [Refs [[prev. author] 2.12]]; εἶναι ἐπί τινα to be against him, [Refs [[prev. author] 6.33]]; εἶναι ἐφ᾽ ἑξήκοντα στάδια to reach sixty stadia, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 4.6.11]]; εἶναι ἐπὶ τὰς ἁφάς pass through the points of contact, [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd c.AD: Apollonius Biographus Perg. “Con.” 4.1]]; εἶναι ἐπί τινι, see above 3 b.

__C.IV.6
εἶναι πρός τινος to be in one's favour, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 4.10, 29, etc.]]; to suit, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 1.2.11, etc.]]; εἶναι πρός τινι engaged in, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Phaedo” 84c, 2nd-3rd c.AD: Philostratus Sophista “Vita Apollonii” 5.31]]; πρὸς τοῖς ἰδίοις mind one's own affairs, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Politica” 1309a6, “Ath.” 16.3; εἶναι πρὸς τὸ κωλύειν 2nd c.BC: Polybius Historicus 1.26.3]]; πρὸς τὸ πονεῖν[Refs 5th c.BC+ [Teles p.46 H.; εἶναι περί τι 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 3.5.7, etc.]]

__C.IV.7
εἶναι παρά τινι or τινα, = παρειναι, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. author] “Cyr.” 6.2.15, 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 8.140.ά]] (assuming variant).

__C.IV.8
εἶναι ὑπό τινα or τινι to be subject to.., [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Historia Graeca (Hellenica)” 5.2.17 (assuming variant), 6.2.4.]]

__C.IV.9
περὶ τούτων ἐστίν that is the question, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-3rd c.BC: Menander Comicus “Ἐπιτρέποντες” 30.]]

__C.IV.10
εἶναι ἀπό.., in Geometry texts, to be constructed upon, [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [3rd c.BC: Archimedes Geometra “περὶ σφαίρας καὶ κυλίνδρου” 2.9, “Con.Sph.” 7.]]

__D
ἐστί is very frequently omitted, mostly in the present indicative before certain predicates, as ἀνάγκη, ἄξιον, δυνατόν, εἰκός, ἕτοιμον, οἷόν τε, ῥᾴδιον, χρεών, etc., and after the neuter of Verbals in -τέος, and such forms as θαυμαστὸν ὅσον: less frequently with other persons and moods, εἰμί omitted, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Tyrannus” 92, “Aj.” 813]]; εἶ, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 4.206]]; ἐσμέν, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Antigone” 634]]; ἐστέ, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 10.463]]; εἰσί, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Tyrannus” 499 (Lyric poetry), “IG” 2.778 B]]; subjunctive ᾖ, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 14.376, 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Hippolytus” 659, 5th c.BC: Antipho Orator 5.32]]; optative εἴη, [Refs [“IG” 22.1183.12]]; imperfect ἦν, [Refs [[prev. work]2.778 B]]; future ἔσονται, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 14.394.]]

__E
the Inf. frequently seems redundant,

__E.1
in phrases implying power or will to do a thing, ἑκὼν εἶναι (see. ἑκών) κατὰ δύναμιν εἶναι [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Isaeus Orator 2.32; εἰς δύναμιν εἶναι 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Politicus” 300c]]; τὸ ἐπ᾽ ἐκείνοις εἶναι, quantum in illis esset, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 8.48, 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Historia Graeca (Hellenica)” 3.5.9, compare 5th c.BC: Lysias Orator 13.58; τὸ ἐπὶ σφᾶς εἶναι 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 4.28; τὸ κατὰ τοῦτον εἶναι 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 1.6.9; κατὰ τοῦτο εἶναι 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Protagoras” 317a]]; τὸ τήμερον, τὸ νῦν εἶναι, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [[prev. author] “Cra.” 396e, “La.” 201c, Theopomp. Comedy texts 98, Decrees cited in 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Ἀθηναίων Πολιτεία” 31.2, etc.]]

__E.2
after Verbs of naming or choosing, σοφιστὴν ὀνομάζουσι τὸν ἄνδρα εἶναι [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Protagoras” 311e; σύμμαχόν μιν εἵλοντο εἶναι 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 8.134]]; of giving, δῶκε ξεινήϊον εἶναι [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 11.20.]]

__F
imperfect ἦνissts. used where other languages take the present,

__F.1
after ἄρα, to express a fact which is and has always been the same, δέρμα δὲ ἀνθρώπου.. ἦν ἄρα σχεδὸν δερμάτων πάντων λαμπρότατον human skin then it appears is.., [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 4.64; Κύπρις οὐκ ἄρ᾽ ἦν θεός 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Hippolytus” 359]]; ὡς ἄρ᾽ ἦσθ᾽ ἐμὸς πατὴρ ὀρθῶς[Refs 3rd c.BC+ [[prev. work] 1169; ἦ πολύμοχθον ἄρ᾽ ἦν γένος.. ἁμερίων [prev. author] “IA” 1330; ἦ στωμύλος ἦσθα 3rd c.BC: Theocritus Poeta Bucolicus 5.79]]; so also when there is reference to a past thought, τουτὶ τί ἦ; what is this? [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Acharnenses” 157, compare 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Cratylus” 387c: so in the Aristotelian formula τὸ τί ἦν εἶναι (“APo.” 82b38, +others)]], used to express the essential nature of a thing, where τί ἦν (for ἐστί) takes the place of the dative in such phrases as τὸ ἀγαθῷ εἶναι, τὸ μεγέθει εἶναι, [Refs [“APr.” 67b12, “de An.” 429b10.]]

__G
ἐγώ εἰμι, in [LXX, pleonastic for ἐγώ, ἐγώ εἰμι οὐχ ἥμαρτον LXX.Judg.11.27, compare 6.18; also ἔσται πᾶς ἀποκτενεῖ με LXX.Gen.4.14.]

Abbott-Smith / STEPBible (TBESG)
ἔσχατος, -η, -ον
[in LXX chiefly for אַחֲרִית אַחֲרוֹן ;]
last, utmost, extreme;
__(a) of place: of the lowest or least honoured place, Luk.14:9-10; τ. ἔσχατον, with genitive part., Act.1:8 13:47;
__(b) of time: Mat.20:12, 14, Mrk.12:6, 22, opposite to πρῶτος, Mat.20:8, 1Co.15:45, Rev.2:19, al.; τὰ ἔ. καὶ T. πρῶτα, Mat.12:45, Luk.11:26, 2Pe.2:20; of the Eternal, ὁ πρῶτος καὶ ὁ ἔ., Rev.1:17 2:8 22:13; in phrases relating to the Messianic age and the consummation of the Kingdom of God: ἐπ᾽ ἐσχάτου (-ων) τ. ἡμερῶν, Heb.1:2, 2Pe.3:3; τ. χρόνων, 1Pe.1:20; ἔ. ὥρα, 1Jn.2:18; ἐπ᾽ ἐ. χόνου, Ju 18; ἐν ἐ. ἡμέραις, Act.2:17, Jas.5:3, 2Ti.3:1; neut., ἔσχατον, as adv., Mrk.12:22, 1Co.15:8;
__(with) of rank: Mrk.9:35, 1Co.4:9
(AS)

LSJ / STEPBible (TFLSJ)
ἔσχᾰτος, η, ον,
also ος, ον [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-3rd c.BC: Aratus Epicus 625](probably from ἐκ, ἐξ, perhaps eĝhzκατος (compare ἐχθός) like{ἔγ-κατα}):

__I

ἔσω  Ion, and old Att.. form of εἴσω
(εἰς),
adv., [in LXX for etc. ;]
__1. prop., after verbs of motion (to) within, into: Mat.26:58, Mrk.14:54; with genitive, Mrk.15:16.
__2. As frequently in cl. (= cl. ἔνδον), after verbs of rest, within: Jhn.20:26, Act.5:23; οἱ ἔ. (opposite to οἱ ἔξω), 1Co.5:12; ὁ ἔ. ἄνθρωπος, Rom.7:22, 2Co.4:16, Eph.3:16.†
(AS)

LSJ / STEPBible (TFLSJ)
εἴσω,
ἔσω, used by Epic dialect, Lyric poetry, and Trag. Poets accusative as a spondee or iambus is required; ἔσω (as ἐς for εἰς) prevailed in Ionic dialect and old Attic dialect Prose; but in other Prose and in Comedy texts εἴσω was the only form admitted, whereas ἔσωθεν with the comparative and superlative ἐσώτερος, ἐσώτατος, ἐσωτέρω, ἐσωτάτω, seem to have been the only forms in use:— adverb of εἰς, ἐς, to within, into: absolutely, μή πού τις ἐπαγγείιῃσι καὶ εἴσω lest some one may carry the news into the house, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 4.775, compare 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1. III, +others; so εἴπατε δ᾽ εἴσω 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 3.427]]; also εἴσω δ᾽ ἀσπίδ᾽ ἔαξε he brake it through to the inside, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 7.270; so ὀστέα δ᾽ εἴσω ἔθλασεν 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 18.96; εἴσω ἐπιγράψαι τέρενα χρόα 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 13.553; ἐσσύμενοι εἴσω 5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “P.” 4.135; εἴσω κομίζου 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Agamemnon” 1035]]; πέπληγμαι..ἔσω[Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. work] 1343; εἴσω.. δεῦρ᾽ εἴσιθ᾽ 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Plutus” 231]]; ἡγεῖσθαι εἴσω, φεύγειν εἴσω, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 2.3.21, 7.5.26; παρακαλέσαι εἴσω [prev. author] “An.” 1.6.5.]]

only Attic dialect-Ionic dialect with ἕ-, Doric dialect ἅτερος [ᾰ] [Refs [“IG” 4.914.9 (Epid.), etc. (and _Attic dialect_ in crasis, see.below)]], Aeolic dialect ἄτερος [Refs 7th c.BC+ [7th-6th c.BC: Alcaeus Lyricus 41.5, etc.]]:— but ἅτερος [ᾱ], Attic dialect crasis for ὁ ἅτερος, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [“Comica Adespota” 14.23 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator, +others]], Ionic dialect οὕτερος (from ὁ ἕτ-) [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.34, etc.]], Doric dialect ὥτερος [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [3rd c.BC: Theocritus Poeta Bucolicus 7.36]]; neuter θάτερον [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Agamemnon” 344, 5th-6th c.BC: Andocides Orator 2.7, etc.]], Ionic dialect τοὔτερον [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.32: _plural_ ἅτεροι, for οἱ ἅτεροι, 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Politica” 1255a20; θάτερα 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Electra” 345, 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 1.87, etc.; _genitive_ θατέρου 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Philoctetes” 597, etc.]], Ionic dialect τοὐτέρου [Refs 7th c.BC+ [7th-6th c.BC(?): Semonides Iambographus 7.113]], Doric dialect θατέρω [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-4th c.BC: Timaeus Locrus Philosophus 94a, θωτέρω 5th c.BC: Epicharmus Comicus 71 (uncertain reading); _dative_ θατέρῳ 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Prometheus Vinctus” 778; _feminine_ _nominative_ ἡτέρα “IG” 22.1498.76, 1615.14,87 (4th c.BC), 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Coloneus” 497, 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Lysistrata” 85, 90 codices, 2nd c.AD: Pausanias Grammaticus “fragment” 82; _dative_ θητέρᾳ 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Tyrannus” 782, “Tr.” 272, 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Hippolytus” 894, 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Aves” 1365, etc., compare 2nd c.AD: Pausanias Grammaticus [prev. cited] (in Mss. sometimes θατέρᾳ)]], Ionic dialect τἠτέρῃ [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [3rd c.BC: Phoenix Iambographus 5.2.]] —Later _masculine_ and _feminine_ θάτερος, θατέρα, even with the Article, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-3rd c.BC: Menander Comicus 846, Chrysipp. cited in 2nd c.AD: Pausanias Grammaticus “fragment” 82, 3rd c.BC: Lycophron Tragicus 590, 1st-2nd c.AD: Polemo Sophista “Cynegirus” 4, 2nd c.AD: Lucianus Sophista “D Mort.” 26.1 (condemned in “Pseudol.” 29), “Geoponica” 14.20.2, etc.; τῶν θατέρων 4th c.AD: Iamblichus Philosophus “in Nicomachi arithmeticam introductionem” p.83 P.]]; θάτερον accusative singular masculine, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Ion” [849].]]

__I
one or the other of two, usually with Article except in Poets; frequently of natural pairs, σκαιῇ (i.e. χειρὶ) ἔγχος ἔχων, ἑτέρηφι δὲ λάζετο πέτρον [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 16.734]]; τῇ ἑτέρῃ μὲν.. τῇ δ᾽ ἑτέρῃ[Refs 5th c.BC+ [.. 14.272, compare 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Cynegeticus” 10.11]]; χειρὶ ἑτέρῃ with one hand, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 12.452, 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 10.171 (but χεὶρ ἑτέρη]] commonly of the left hand, see infr. IV.I); ἑτέροιο διὰ κροτάφοιο [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 4.502; χωλὸς δ᾽ ἕτερον πόδα 2.217, compare 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Ecclesiazusae” 162, 4th-3rd c.BC: Dinarchus Orator 1.82; ἀμφότεραι αἱ γνάθοι, ἢ ἡ ἑτέρα 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “de Equitandi ratione” 1.9; ἐκκοπεὶς τὸν ἕ. τῶν ὀφθαλμῶν 1st c.BC: Dionysius Halicarnassensis 5.23; εἰς γόνυ θάτερον 2nd-3rd c.AD: Philostratus Sophista “Philostrati majoris imagines” 2.20]]; of pairs in general, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 5.258, etc.]]; τὴν ἑ. πύλην one of the two gates, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 3.156; ὁ ἕ. τῶν στρατηγῶν 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 4.43; τὸ ἕ. τοῖν δυοῖν τειχοῖν [prev. author] 7.24]]: frequently of alternatives presented, τῶνδε τὰ ἕ. ποιέειν [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 4.126]]; ἑλοῦ γε θάτερ᾽, ἢ.. ἢ.. [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Electra” 345]]; τοῖνδ᾽ ἑλοῦ δυοῖν πότμοιν τὸν ἕ. [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Phoenissae” 952; δυοῖν ἀγαθοῖν τοῦ ἑτέρου τεύξεσθαι 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 4.28]]; δυοῖν θάτερα, ἢ.. ἢ.. [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Theaetetus” 187c; ὅταν δυοῖν καλοῖν θάτερον κάλλιον ᾖ, ἢ τῷ ἑτέρῳ τούτοιν ἢ ἀμφοτέροις ὑπερβάλλον κάλλιόν ἐστιν [prev. author] “Grg.” 475a]]: in plural, one of two parties or sets, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 11.258]]; τῶν ἕτεροί γε παῖδα κλαύσονται one set of parents, either mine or thine, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 20.210; δώῃ δ᾽ ἑτέροισί γε νίκην 7.292; ἑτέροισι δὲ κῦδος ἔδωκαν 13.303: frequently with _negative_, οὐδ᾽ ἕτεροι 11.71.]]

__I.2
in double clauses ἕτερος (in Prose always ὁ ἕτερος) is generally repeated; ἑ. μὲν δουρὶ.., τῷ δ᾽ ἑ. [Refs [21.164]]; τὸν ἕ., ἕ. δὲ.. [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 5.266; ἕ. λευκόν, ἑτέρην δὲ μέλαιναν 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 3.103, etc.: but sometimes omitted in one clause, [ἕτερος μὲν] κακῶν, ἕ. δὲ ἐάων 24.528, compare 7.420, “IG” 22.1388.46 (probably), etc.; ἡ μὲν.., ἡ δ᾽ ἑτέρη 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 22.149, “IG” 12.76.50]]; ἕ..., ὁ δὲ.. [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 8.374; answered by ἄλλος, ἕτερον μὲν κεύθῃ ἐνὶ φρεσίν, ἄλλο δὲ εἴπῃ 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 9.313, compare 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 7.123]]; reversely ἄλλῳ ὀρχηστύν, ἑτέρῳ κίθαριν [ἔδωκε] [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 13.731, compare 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 439b, “Tht.” 184e]]; τότε μὲν ἕτερα.., τότε δὲ ἄλλα.. [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus Alcaeus1.116e]]; ὁ ἕτερος.., ὁ λοιπός.. [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 4.1.23]]; ἕτερα.., τὰ δὲ.. [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Coloneus” 1454 (Lyric poetry); later μίαν μὲν.. ἑτέραν δέ 2nd c.AD: Apollonius Dyscolus Grammaticus “de Syntaxi;” 172.5; τὴν μίαν.. τὴν δ᾽ ἑτέρην “Anthologia Graeca” 9.680.]]

__I.3
repeated in the same clause, ἐξ ἑτέρων ἕτερ᾽ ἐστίν one building follows on another, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 17.266]]; [ἀ] δ᾽ ἀτέρα τὰν ἀτέραν κύλιξ ὠθήτω let one cup push on the other, [Refs 7th c.BC+ [7th-6th c.BC: Alcaeus Lyricus 41.5]]; ἢ θάτερον δεῖ δυστυχεῖν ἢ θάτερον one party or the other, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Ion” [849]; ἕτεροι ἑτέρων ἠξίωσαν ἄρχειν 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 2.64]]; ἕτερος ἀφ᾽ ἑτέρου θεραπείας ἀναπιμπλάμενοι ἔθνῃσκον[Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. work] 51; εἴ τίς τι ἕτερος ἑτέρου προφέρει [prev. author] 7.64; ξυμμειγνυμένων ἑτέρων ἑτέροις 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Aves” 701]]; συμφορὰ ἑτέρα ἑτέρους πιέζει one calamity oppresses one, another others, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Alcestis” 893 (Lyric poetry); ἑτέρᾳ δ᾽ ἕτερος ἕτερον ὄλβῳ καὶ δυνάμει παρῆλθεν [prev. author] “Ba.” 905, compare 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Coloneus” 231 (_anapaest meter_); ἄλλη δ᾽ εἰς ἑτέρην ὀλυφύρετο 3rd c.BC: Apollonius Rhodius Epicus 1.250.]]

__I.4
={δεύτερος}, second, ἡ μὲν.., ἡ δ᾽ ἑτέρη.., ἡ δὲ τρίτη.. [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 10.352f, compare 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 16.179, +others, 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 2.3.22]]; ἡ ἑ. πρότασις the minor premiss, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Ethica Nicomachea” 1143b3: without _Article_, ἕ. τέρας 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 7.57]]; προσαγορεύεις αὐτὰ ἑτέρῳ ὀνόματι you call them further by a new name, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Philebus” 13a; cf. IV. 1b.]]

__I.4.b
with Pronouns of quantity, ordinals, etc., τόσσοι δ᾽ αὖθ᾽ ἕτεροι ποταμοί as many more, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th-7th c.BC: Hesiodus Epicus “Theogonia” 367]]; ἕτερον τοσοῦτον as much again, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 2.149]]; ἑτέρου τοσούτου χρόνου for as long again, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Isocrates Orator 4.153]]; ἕ. τοιαῦτα other things of like kind, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.120, 191; ἑτέρων τοιῶνδε (i.e. ἀνθρώπων) ἄρχεις [prev. work] 207]]; τῷ αὐτῷ τρόπῳ.. τῷ ἑτέρῳ in the same way over again, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. author] 2.127; ἄλλα τε τοιαῦθ᾽ ἕτερα μυρία 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Fragmenta” 333.4]]; χιλίας ἑτέρας [δραχμάς] [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 58.6]]; δεύτερον, τρίτον ἕ. δικαστήριον, [Refs [[prev. author] 23.71,74]]; ἕ. ἐγώ, of a friend, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Pythagoras Philosophus cited in 4th c.AD: Iamblichus Philosophus “in Nicomachi arithmeticam introductionem” p.35 P.]]; ἕτεροι αὐτοί second selves, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Ethica Nicomachea” 1161b28; εὕρηκε τὸν ἕ., τὸν σέ 4th-3rd c.BC: Menander Comicus 474.]]

__II
without Article, another, of many, with a sense of difference, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 4.306, 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 7.123, 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Acharnenses” 422, “Lys.” 66, etc.; ἕ.αὖ τις [prev. author] “Eq.” 949; ἕ. αὖ [prev. author] “Pax” 295, etc.; ἕτερα ἄττα 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Theaetetus” 188b; repeated ἑτέραν χἀτέραν τρικυμίαν 4th-3rd c.BC: Menander Comicus 536.8: with _negative_, οἷα οὐχ ἕτερα [ἐγένετο]]] such as none like them had happened, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 1.23; ναυμαχία.. οἵα οὐχ ἑτέρα τῶν προτέρων [prev. author] 7.70; οὐδεμιᾶς ἥσσων μᾶλλον ἑτέρας [prev. work] 29 (assuming variant)]]; οὐχ ἕτερον ἀλλά.. none other than, [Refs 2nd c.BC+ [1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus 2.671b, compare “UPZ” 71.9 (2nd c.BC).]]

__II.b
οἱ ἕ. the rest, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 4.169.]]

__II.c
ὁ ἑ. 'one's neighbour', ἀγαπᾶν τὸν ἕ. [NT.Rom.13.6, cf. NT.Gal.6.4.]

__III
of another kind, different, ἕ. δέ με θυμὸς ἔρυκεν [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 9.302]]; τὸ μὲν ἕ., τὸ δὲ ἕ., i.e. they are different, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Meno” 97d, compare “R.” 346a; ἕ. τε καὶ ἀνόμοιον [prev. author] “Smp.” 186b; τὸ δὲ ταὐτὸν ἕ. ἀποφαίνειν καὶ τὸ θάτερον ταὐτόν [prev. author] “Sph.” 259d; ἕ. ἤδη ἦν καὶ οὐχ ὁ αὐτός 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 34.12; ἑτέραν ἔδωκεν παντὶ τῷ κόσμῳ ὄψιν “OGI” 458.7 (1st c.BC)]]; ἕ. εὐαγγέλιον [NT.Gal.1.6: coupled with ἄλλος, χἀτέρους ἄλλους πόνους] and other different toils, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Supplices” 573 (assuming variant), compare “Or.” 345 (uncertain reading); Ῥόδον καὶ ἄλλας ἑτέρας πόλεις 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 15.27; ἕτερον τό τ᾽ ἀλγεῖν καὶ θεωρεῖν ἐστ᾽ ἴσως 4th-3rd c.BC: Philemo Comicus 75.7; ἕτερα φρονῶν καὶ δημηγορῶν 4th-3rd c.BC: Dinarchus Orator 1.17]]: c.genitive, other than, different from, φίλους.. ἑτέρους τῶν νῦν ὄντων [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 1.28, compare 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Protagoras” 333a, 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 10.44, etc.]]; ἕτερον, ἕτερα ἢ.., [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Orestes” 345, 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 1.6.2; παρὰ ταῦτα πάντα ἕτερόν τι 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Phaedo” 74a; ἕτερα πολιτείας εἴδη παρὰ μοναρχίαν 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Politica” 1294a25, compare 1286b21.]]

__III.2
other than should be, euphemistic for κακός, παθεῖν μὲν εὖ, παθεῖν δὲ θάτερα [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Philoctetes” 503; ἀγάθ᾽ ἢ θάτερα, ἵνα μηδὲν εἴπω φλαῦρον 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 22.12: _absolutely_, δαίμων ἕ. 5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “P.” 3.34]]; λέκτρα, συμφοραί, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Medea” 639 (Lyric poetry), “HF” 1238; ἐὰν τὰ ἕ. ψηφίσωνται οἱ δικασταί 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 48.30]]; πλέον θάτερον ἐποίησαν did more harm (than good), [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Isocrates Orator 19.25, compare 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Phaedo” 114e, “Euthd.” 280e, 2nd c.AD: Aristides Rhetor 2.117 1st c.AD: Josephus Historicus]]

__IV
Special Phrases:

__IV.1
elliptical, mostly in dative feminine,

__IV.1.a
τῇ ἑτέρᾳ (i.e. χειρί), Epic dialect ἑτέρῃ or ἑτέρηφι, with one hand (see. entry [near the start]); with the left hand, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 3.441, 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 22.80, 3rd c.BC: Theocritus Poeta Bucolicus 24.45: hence proverbial, οὐ τῇ ἑτέρᾳ ληπτός]] not to be caught with one hand, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Sophista” 226a; ἐκ δ᾽ ἑτέρης 3rd c.BC: Apollonius Rhodius Epicus 1.1115, “Anthologia Graeca” 9.650 (6th c.AD: Leontius Epigrammaticus).]]

__IV.1.b
θατέρᾳ (i.e. ἡμέρᾳ) on the morrow, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Tyrannus” 782, 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Rhesus” 449; τῆς ἑτέρας 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Crito” 44a]]; but τῇ ἑτέρᾳ on the following (i.e. the third) day, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 4.6.10.]]

__IV.1.c
(i.e. ὁδῷ) in another or a different way, καὶ τῇδε φῦναι χἀτέρᾳ [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Coloneus” 1444]]; another way, τρέπεσθαι [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Nubes” 812; ἑτέρᾳ πῃ [prev. author] “Eq.” 35]]; τότ᾽ ἄλλοσ᾽.., θατέρᾳ δὲ.. [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Trachiniae” 272]]; θατέρᾳ.., θατέρᾳ.. in one way.., in the other.., [Refs 8th c.BC+ [4th c.AD: Heniochus Comicus 5.16; ἑτέρηφι 8th-7th c.BC: Hesiodus Epicus “Opera et Dies” 216: _accusative_ ἑτέραν ἐκτρέπεσθαι 2nd c.AD: Lucianus Sophista “Tim.” 5.]]

__IV.2
adverbial with Preps.:

__IV.2.a
ἐπὶ θάτερα to the one or the other side, one or the other way, ἐπὶ μὲν θάτερα.., ἐπὶ θ. δὲ.. [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Hippocrates Medicus “περὶ ἄρθρων ἐμβολῆς” 7]]; τότε μὲν ἐπὶ θάτερα, τότε δ᾽ ἐπὶ θ. [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Sophista” 259c: also with another _preposition_, ἐς τὰ ἐπὶ θάτερα]] to or on the other side, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 1.87]]; ἐκ τοῦ ἐπὶ θάτερα from the other side, [Refs [[prev. author] 7.37]]; ἐκ μὲν τοῦ ἐπὶ θ., ἐκ δὲ τοῦ ἐπὶ θ. [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Protagoras” 314e: with _genitive_, ἐς τὰ ἐπὶ θ. τοῦ ποταμοῦ 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 7.84; εἰς τἀπὶ θ. τῆς πόλεως 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Historia Graeca (Hellenica)” 6.2.7; τὸ ἐπὶ θάτερον τῆς ῥινός 5th c.BC: Hippocrates Medicus “περὶ ἄρθρων ἐμβολῆς” 35.]]

__IV.2.b
κατὰ θάτερα on the one or other side, κατὰ θ. ἀστός [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 57.30; ψόφου κατὰ θ. προσπεσόντος 1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus “Brutus” 51, etc.]]; but καθ᾽ ἕτερα at other points, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 7.42.]]

__V
adverb ἑτέρως in one or the other way, opposed to ἀμφοτέρως, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Theaetetus” 181e]]; ἑ. τε καὶ ἑ., ={ἀμφοτέρως}, [Refs [[prev. author] “Phdr.” 235a]]; τοῦ σκέλους ἑ. ἔχειν, ={ἑτεροσκελὴς εἶναι}, [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd-3rd c.AD: Philostratus Sophista “Vita Apollonii” 3.39.]]

__V.2
differently, rarely in Poetry, οὐχ ἑ. τις ἐρεῖ [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [3rd c.BC: Theocritus Poeta Bucolicus “Epigrammata” 10.3]]; ἑ. ἔχειν to be different, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Plutus” 371: frequently in Prose, ὡς ἑ]]. in the other way (compare ὡς), ἢν ἡ ἑτέρη γνάθος ἐκστῇ ὡς ἑ. χρὴ τὴν ἐπίδεσιν ἄγειν [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Hippocrates Medicus “περὶ ἄρθρων ἐμβολῆς” 34, compare 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Sophista” 266a, etc.]]; ἐάν τε καλῶς, ἐάν θ᾽ ὡς ἑ. [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 18.85, compare 212]]: with genitive, differently from, ἑ. πως τῶν εἰωθότων [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Politicus” 295d]]; ἑ. ἤπερ.. [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd-3rd c.AD: Aelianus “De Natura Animalium - Ar.Byzantine Epit.” 12.28.]]

__V.3
otherwise than should be, badly, wrongly, once in [NT+8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Homerus Epicus, ἑ. ἐβόλοντο 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 1.234; εἰ καὶ ἑ. τοῦτο ἀπέβη “SIG” 851.10 (Marc.Aur.); εἴ τι ἑ. φρονεῖτε NT.Phil.3.15.]]

Included with:  ἕτερος, α, ον,
only Attic dialect-Ionic dialect with ἕ-, Doric dialect ἅτερος [ᾰ] [Refs [“IG” 4.914.9 (Epid.), etc. (and _Attic dialect_ in crasis, see.below)]], Aeolic dialect ἄτερος [Refs 7th c.BC+ [7th-6th c.BC: Alcaeus Lyricus 41.5, etc.]]:— but ἅτερος [ᾱ], Attic dialect crasis for ὁ ἅτερος, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [“Comica Adespota” 14.23 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator, +others]], Ionic dialect οὕτερος (from ὁ ἕτ-) [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.34, etc.]], Doric dialect ὥτερος [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [3rd c.BC: Theocritus Poeta Bucolicus 7.36]]; neuter θάτερον [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Agamemnon” 344, 5th-6th c.BC: Andocides Orator 2.7, etc.]], Ionic dialect τοὔτερον [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.32: _plural_ ἅτεροι, for οἱ ἅτεροι, 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Politica” 1255a20; θάτερα 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Electra” 345, 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 1.87, etc.; _genitive_ θατέρου 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Philoctetes” 597, etc.]], Ionic dialect τοὐτέρου [Refs 7th c.BC+ [7th-6th c.BC(?): Semonides Iambographus 7.113]], Doric dialect θατέρω [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-4th c.BC: Timaeus Locrus Philosophus 94a, θωτέρω 5th c.BC: Epicharmus Comicus 71 (uncertain reading); _dative_ θατέρῳ 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Prometheus Vinctus” 778; _feminine_ _nominative_ ἡτέρα “IG” 22.1498.76, 1615.14,87 (4th c.BC), 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Coloneus” 497, 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Lysistrata” 85, 90 codices, 2nd c.AD: Pausanias Grammaticus “fragment” 82; _dative_ θητέρᾳ 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Tyrannus” 782, “Tr.” 272, 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Hippolytus” 894, 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Aves” 1365, etc., compare 2nd c.AD: Pausanias Grammaticus [prev. cited] (in Mss. sometimes θατέρᾳ)]], Ionic dialect τἠτέρῃ [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [3rd c.BC: Phoenix Iambographus 5.2.]] —Later _masculine_ and _feminine_ θάτερος, θατέρα, even with the Article, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-3rd c.BC: Menander Comicus 846, Chrysipp. cited in 2nd c.AD: Pausanias Grammaticus “fragment” 82, 3rd c.BC: Lycophron Tragicus 590, 1st-2nd c.AD: Polemo Sophista “Cynegirus” 4, 2nd c.AD: Lucianus Sophista “D Mort.” 26.1 (condemned in “Pseudol.” 29), “Geoponica” 14.20.2, etc.; τῶν θατέρων 4th c.AD: Iamblichus Philosophus “in Nicomachi arithmeticam introductionem” p.83 P.]]; θάτερον accusative singular masculine, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Ion” [849].]]

__I
one or the other of two, usually with Article except in Poets; frequently of natural pairs, σκαιῇ (i.e. χειρὶ) ἔγχος ἔχων, ἑτέρηφι δὲ λάζετο πέτρον [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 16.734]]; τῇ ἑτέρῃ μὲν.. τῇ δ᾽ ἑτέρῃ[Refs 5th c.BC+ [.. 14.272, compare 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Cynegeticus” 10.11]]; χειρὶ ἑτέρῃ with one hand, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 12.452, 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 10.171 (but χεὶρ ἑτέρη]] commonly of the left hand, see infr. IV.I); ἑτέροιο διὰ κροτάφοιο [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 4.502; χωλὸς δ᾽ ἕτερον πόδα 2.217, compare 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Ecclesiazusae” 162, 4th-3rd c.BC: Dinarchus Orator 1.82; ἀμφότεραι αἱ γνάθοι, ἢ ἡ ἑτέρα 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “de Equitandi ratione” 1.9; ἐκκοπεὶς τὸν ἕ. τῶν ὀφθαλμῶν 1st c.BC: Dionysius Halicarnassensis 5.23; εἰς γόνυ θάτερον 2nd-3rd c.AD: Philostratus Sophista “Philostrati majoris imagines” 2.20]]; of pairs in general, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 5.258, etc.]]; τὴν ἑ. πύλην one of the two gates, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 3.156; ὁ ἕ. τῶν στρατηγῶν 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 4.43; τὸ ἕ. τοῖν δυοῖν τειχοῖν [prev. author] 7.24]]: frequently of alternatives presented, τῶνδε τὰ ἕ. ποιέειν [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 4.126]]; ἑλοῦ γε θάτερ᾽, ἢ.. ἢ.. [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Electra” 345]]; τοῖνδ᾽ ἑλοῦ δυοῖν πότμοιν τὸν ἕ. [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Phoenissae” 952; δυοῖν ἀγαθοῖν τοῦ ἑτέρου τεύξεσθαι 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 4.28]]; δυοῖν θάτερα, ἢ.. ἢ.. [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Theaetetus” 187c; ὅταν δυοῖν καλοῖν θάτερον κάλλιον ᾖ, ἢ τῷ ἑτέρῳ τούτοιν ἢ ἀμφοτέροις ὑπερβάλλον κάλλιόν ἐστιν [prev. author] “Grg.” 475a]]: in plural, one of two parties or sets, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 11.258]]; τῶν ἕτεροί γε παῖδα κλαύσονται one set of parents, either mine or thine, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 20.210; δώῃ δ᾽ ἑτέροισί γε νίκην 7.292; ἑτέροισι δὲ κῦδος ἔδωκαν 13.303: frequently with _negative_, οὐδ᾽ ἕτεροι 11.71.]]

__I.2
in double clauses ἕτερος (in Prose always ὁ ἕτερος) is generally repeated; ἑ. μὲν δουρὶ.., τῷ δ᾽ ἑ. [Refs [21.164]]; τὸν ἕ., ἕ. δὲ.. [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 5.266; ἕ. λευκόν, ἑτέρην δὲ μέλαιναν 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 3.103, etc.: but sometimes omitted in one clause, [ἕτερος μὲν] κακῶν, ἕ. δὲ ἐάων 24.528, compare 7.420, “IG” 22.1388.46 (probably), etc.; ἡ μὲν.., ἡ δ᾽ ἑτέρη 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 22.149, “IG” 12.76.50]]; ἕ..., ὁ δὲ.. [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 8.374; answered by ἄλλος, ἕτερον μὲν κεύθῃ ἐνὶ φρεσίν, ἄλλο δὲ εἴπῃ 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 9.313, compare 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 7.123]]; reversely ἄλλῳ ὀρχηστύν, ἑτέρῳ κίθαριν [ἔδωκε] [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 13.731, compare 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 439b, “Tht.” 184e]]; τότε μὲν ἕτερα.., τότε δὲ ἄλλα.. [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus Alcaeus1.116e]]; ὁ ἕτερος.., ὁ λοιπός.. [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 4.1.23]]; ἕτερα.., τὰ δὲ.. [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Coloneus” 1454 (Lyric poetry); later μίαν μὲν.. ἑτέραν δέ 2nd c.AD: Apollonius Dyscolus Grammaticus “de Syntaxi;” 172.5; τὴν μίαν.. τὴν δ᾽ ἑτέρην “Anthologia Graeca” 9.680.]]

__I.3
repeated in the same clause, ἐξ ἑτέρων ἕτερ᾽ ἐστίν one building follows on another, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 17.266]]; [ἀ] δ᾽ ἀτέρα τὰν ἀτέραν κύλιξ ὠθήτω let one cup push on the other, [Refs 7th c.BC+ [7th-6th c.BC: Alcaeus Lyricus 41.5]]; ἢ θάτερον δεῖ δυστυχεῖν ἢ θάτερον one party or the other, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Ion” [849]; ἕτεροι ἑτέρων ἠξίωσαν ἄρχειν 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 2.64]]; ἕτερος ἀφ᾽ ἑτέρου θεραπείας ἀναπιμπλάμενοι ἔθνῃσκον[Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. work] 51; εἴ τίς τι ἕτερος ἑτέρου προφέρει [prev. author] 7.64; ξυμμειγνυμένων ἑτέρων ἑτέροις 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Aves” 701]]; συμφορὰ ἑτέρα ἑτέρους πιέζει one calamity oppresses one, another others, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Alcestis” 893 (Lyric poetry); ἑτέρᾳ δ᾽ ἕτερος ἕτερον ὄλβῳ καὶ δυνάμει παρῆλθεν [prev. author] “Ba.” 905, compare 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Coloneus” 231 (_anapaest meter_); ἄλλη δ᾽ εἰς ἑτέρην ὀλυφύρετο 3rd c.BC: Apollonius Rhodius Epicus 1.250.]]

__I.4
={δεύτερος}, second, ἡ μὲν.., ἡ δ᾽ ἑτέρη.., ἡ δὲ τρίτη.. [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 10.352f, compare 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 16.179, +others, 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 2.3.22]]; ἡ ἑ. πρότασις the minor premiss, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Ethica Nicomachea” 1143b3: without _Article_, ἕ. τέρας 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 7.57]]; προσαγορεύεις αὐτὰ ἑτέρῳ ὀνόματι you call them further by a new name, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Philebus” 13a; cf. IV. 1b.]]

__I.4.b
with Pronouns of quantity, ordinals, etc., τόσσοι δ᾽ αὖθ᾽ ἕτεροι ποταμοί as many more, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th-7th c.BC: Hesiodus Epicus “Theogonia” 367]]; ἕτερον τοσοῦτον as much again, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 2.149]]; ἑτέρου τοσούτου χρόνου for as long again, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Isocrates Orator 4.153]]; ἕ. τοιαῦτα other things of like kind, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.120, 191; ἑτέρων τοιῶνδε (i.e. ἀνθρώπων) ἄρχεις [prev. work] 207]]; τῷ αὐτῷ τρόπῳ.. τῷ ἑτέρῳ in the same way over again, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. author] 2.127; ἄλλα τε τοιαῦθ᾽ ἕτερα μυρία 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Fragmenta” 333.4]]; χιλίας ἑτέρας [δραχμάς] [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 58.6]]; δεύτερον, τρίτον ἕ. δικαστήριον, [Refs [[prev. author] 23.71,74]]; ἕ. ἐγώ, of a friend, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Pythagoras Philosophus cited in 4th c.AD: Iamblichus Philosophus “in Nicomachi arithmeticam introductionem” p.35 P.]]; ἕτεροι αὐτοί second selves, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Ethica Nicomachea” 1161b28; εὕρηκε τὸν ἕ., τὸν σέ 4th-3rd c.BC: Menander Comicus 474.]]

__II
without Article, another, of many, with a sense of difference, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 4.306, 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 7.123, 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Acharnenses” 422, “Lys.” 66, etc.; ἕ.αὖ τις [prev. author] “Eq.” 949; ἕ. αὖ [prev. author] “Pax” 295, etc.; ἕτερα ἄττα 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Theaetetus” 188b; repeated ἑτέραν χἀτέραν τρικυμίαν 4th-3rd c.BC: Menander Comicus 536.8: with _negative_, οἷα οὐχ ἕτερα [ἐγένετο]]] such as none like them had happened, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 1.23; ναυμαχία.. οἵα οὐχ ἑτέρα τῶν προτέρων [prev. author] 7.70; οὐδεμιᾶς ἥσσων μᾶλλον ἑτέρας [prev. work] 29 (assuming variant)]]; οὐχ ἕτερον ἀλλά.. none other than, [Refs 2nd c.BC+ [1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus 2.671b, compare “UPZ” 71.9 (2nd c.BC).]]

__II.b
οἱ ἕ. the rest, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 4.169.]]

__II.c
ὁ ἑ. 'one's neighbour', ἀγαπᾶν τὸν ἕ. [NT.Rom.13.6, cf. NT.Gal.6.4.]

__III
of another kind, different, ἕ. δέ με θυμὸς ἔρυκεν [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 9.302]]; τὸ μὲν ἕ., τὸ δὲ ἕ., i.e. they are different, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Meno” 97d, compare “R.” 346a; ἕ. τε καὶ ἀνόμοιον [prev. author] “Smp.” 186b; τὸ δὲ ταὐτὸν ἕ. ἀποφαίνειν καὶ τὸ θάτερον ταὐτόν [prev. author] “Sph.” 259d; ἕ. ἤδη ἦν καὶ οὐχ ὁ αὐτός 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 34.12; ἑτέραν ἔδωκεν παντὶ τῷ κόσμῳ ὄψιν “OGI” 458.7 (1st c.BC)]]; ἕ. εὐαγγέλιον [NT.Gal.1.6: coupled with ἄλλος, χἀτέρους ἄλλους πόνους] and other different toils, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Supplices” 573 (assuming variant), compare “Or.” 345 (uncertain reading); Ῥόδον καὶ ἄλλας ἑτέρας πόλεις 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 15.27; ἕτερον τό τ᾽ ἀλγεῖν καὶ θεωρεῖν ἐστ᾽ ἴσως 4th-3rd c.BC: Philemo Comicus 75.7; ἕτερα φρονῶν καὶ δημηγορῶν 4th-3rd c.BC: Dinarchus Orator 1.17]]: c.genitive, other than, different from, φίλους.. ἑτέρους τῶν νῦν ὄντων [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 1.28, compare 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Protagoras” 333a, 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 10.44, etc.]]; ἕτερον, ἕτερα ἢ.., [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Orestes” 345, 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 1.6.2; παρὰ ταῦτα πάντα ἕτερόν τι 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Phaedo” 74a; ἕτερα πολιτείας εἴδη παρὰ μοναρχίαν 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Politica” 1294a25, compare 1286b21.]]

__III.2
other than should be, euphemistic for κακός, παθεῖν μὲν εὖ, παθεῖν δὲ θάτερα [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Philoctetes” 503; ἀγάθ᾽ ἢ θάτερα, ἵνα μηδὲν εἴπω φλαῦρον 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 22.12: _absolutely_, δαίμων ἕ. 5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “P.” 3.34]]; λέκτρα, συμφοραί, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Medea” 639 (Lyric poetry), “HF” 1238; ἐὰν τὰ ἕ. ψηφίσωνται οἱ δικασταί 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 48.30]]; πλέον θάτερον ἐποίησαν did more harm (than good), [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Isocrates Orator 19.25, compare 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Phaedo” 114e, “Euthd.” 280e, 2nd c.AD: Aristides Rhetor 2.117 1st c.AD: Josephus Historicus]]

__IV
Special Phrases:

__IV.1
elliptical, mostly in dative feminine,

__IV.1.a
τῇ ἑτέρᾳ (i.e. χειρί), Epic dialect ἑτέρῃ or ἑτέρηφι, with one hand (see. entry [near the start]); with the left hand, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 3.441, 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 22.80, 3rd c.BC: Theocritus Poeta Bucolicus 24.45: hence proverbial, οὐ τῇ ἑτέρᾳ ληπτός]] not to be caught with one hand, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Sophista” 226a; ἐκ δ᾽ ἑτέρης 3rd c.BC: Apollonius Rhodius Epicus 1.1115, “Anthologia Graeca” 9.650 (6th c.AD: Leontius Epigrammaticus).]]

__IV.1.b
θατέρᾳ (i.e. ἡμέρᾳ) on the morrow, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Tyrannus” 782, 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Rhesus” 449; τῆς ἑτέρας 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Crito” 44a]]; but τῇ ἑτέρᾳ on the following (i.e. the third) day, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 4.6.10.]]

__IV.1.c
(i.e. ὁδῷ) in another or a different way, καὶ τῇδε φῦναι χἀτέρᾳ [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Coloneus” 1444]]; another way, τρέπεσθαι [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Nubes” 812; ἑτέρᾳ πῃ [prev. author] “Eq.” 35]]; τότ᾽ ἄλλοσ᾽.., θατέρᾳ δὲ.. [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Trachiniae” 272]]; θατέρᾳ.., θατέρᾳ.. in one way.., in the other.., [Refs 8th c.BC+ [4th c.AD: Heniochus Comicus 5.16; ἑτέρηφι 8th-7th c.BC: Hesiodus Epicus “Opera et Dies” 216: _accusative_ ἑτέραν ἐκτρέπεσθαι 2nd c.AD: Lucianus Sophista “Tim.” 5.]]

__IV.2
adverbial with Preps.:

__IV.2.a
ἐπὶ θάτερα to the one or the other side, one or the other way, ἐπὶ μὲν θάτερα.., ἐπὶ θ. δὲ.. [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Hippocrates Medicus “περὶ ἄρθρων ἐμβολῆς” 7]]; τότε μὲν ἐπὶ θάτερα, τότε δ᾽ ἐπὶ θ. [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Sophista” 259c: also with another _preposition_, ἐς τὰ ἐπὶ θάτερα]] to or on the other side, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 1.87]]; ἐκ τοῦ ἐπὶ θάτερα from the other side, [Refs [[prev. author] 7.37]]; ἐκ μὲν τοῦ ἐπὶ θ., ἐκ δὲ τοῦ ἐπὶ θ. [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Protagoras” 314e: with _genitive_, ἐς τὰ ἐπὶ θ. τοῦ ποταμοῦ 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 7.84; εἰς τἀπὶ θ. τῆς πόλεως 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Historia Graeca (Hellenica)” 6.2.7; τὸ ἐπὶ θάτερον τῆς ῥινός 5th c.BC: Hippocrates Medicus “περὶ ἄρθρων ἐμβολῆς” 35.]]

__IV.2.b
κατὰ θάτερα on the one or other side, κατὰ θ. ἀστός [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 57.30; ψόφου κατὰ θ. προσπεσόντος 1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus “Brutus” 51, etc.]]; but καθ᾽ ἕτερα at other points, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 7.42.]]

__V
adverb ἑτέρως in one or the other way, opposed to ἀμφοτέρως, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Theaetetus” 181e]]; ἑ. τε καὶ ἑ., ={ἀμφοτέρως}, [Refs [[prev. author] “Phdr.” 235a]]; τοῦ σκέλους ἑ. ἔχειν, ={ἑτεροσκελὴς εἶναι}, [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd-3rd c.AD: Philostratus Sophista “Vita Apollonii” 3.39.]]

__V.2
differently, rarely in Poetry, οὐχ ἑ. τις ἐρεῖ [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [3rd c.BC: Theocritus Poeta Bucolicus “Epigrammata” 10.3]]; ἑ. ἔχειν to be different, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Plutus” 371: frequently in Prose, ὡς ἑ]]. in the other way (compare ὡς), ἢν ἡ ἑτέρη γνάθος ἐκστῇ ὡς ἑ. χρὴ τὴν ἐπίδεσιν ἄγειν [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Hippocrates Medicus “περὶ ἄρθρων ἐμβολῆς” 34, compare 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Sophista” 266a, etc.]]; ἐάν τε καλῶς, ἐάν θ᾽ ὡς ἑ. [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 18.85, compare 212]]: with genitive, differently from, ἑ. πως τῶν εἰωθότων [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Politicus” 295d]]; ἑ. ἤπερ.. [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd-3rd c.AD: Aelianus “De Natura Animalium - Ar.Byzantine Epit.” 12.28.]]

__V.3
otherwise than should be, badly, wrongly, once in [NT+8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Homerus Epicus, ἑ. ἐβόλοντο 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 1.234; εἰ καὶ ἑ. τοῦτο ἀπέβη “SIG” 851.10 (Marc.Aur.); εἴ τι ἑ. φρονεῖτε NT.Phil.3.15.]]

ἔτι
adv.,
yet, as yet, still;

[Refs [2.938]]:—at hand, ready, prepared, ὀνείαθ᾽ ἑτοῖμα προκείμενα [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 14.453, etc.; τὶν δ᾽ αἶνος ἑτοῖμος 5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “O.” 6.12; [τὰ κρέα] εἶχε ἕτοιμα 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.119, compare 3.123; ἑτοιμοτάταν ἐπὶ δαῖτα 3rd c.BC: Theocritus Poeta Bucolicus 13.63, compare 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Cyclops” 357 (Lyric poetry)]]; ἕ. χρήματα money in hand, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 5.31; ἐξ ἑ.]]in ready money, [Refs 4th c.AD+ [POxy. 2106.23 (4th c.AD)]]; ἕ. ἀεὶ παρακείμενον ἐκμαγεῖον [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Timaeus” 72c]]; ἕ. ποιήσασθαι to make ready, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.11; ὡς ἑτοῖμα ἦν 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 2.3; ἐπειδὴ αὐτῷ ἑ. ἦν [prev. work] 98]]; ἐξ ἑτοίμου at once and without hesitation, immediately, offhand, ἐξ ἑ. λαμβάνειν [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Isocrates Orator 5.96; ἐξ ἑ. ὑπακούειν 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Oeconomicus” 14.3; ἐξ ἑτοιμοτάτου διώκειν [prev. author] “Cyr.” 5.3.57; ἐξ ἑ. φίλον εἶναι [prev. author] “Mem.” 2.6.16]]; γίνεται ταῦτα ἐξ -οτάτου are most likely to attack, [NT+5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Hippocrates Medicus “προγνωστικόν” 24; ἐν ἑτοίμῳ ἐστί 4th-3rd c.BC: Epicurus Philosophus “Epistulae” 3p.62U., compare 3rd c.BC: Theocritus Poeta Bucolicus 22.61; ἐν ἑ. ἔχειν 2nd c.BC: Polybius Historicus 2.34.2, NT.2Cor.10.6, etc.]]; ἑτοιμότερα γέλωτος λίβη tears that came more readily than.., [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Choephori” 448]]; τὰ ἑ. that which is ready to hand, ἐπὶ τὰ ἑ. μᾶλλον τρέπονται [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 1.20]]; τὰ ἑ. βλάψαι[Refs [[prev. work] 70; τοῖς ἑ. περὶ τῶν ἀφανῶν.. κινδυνεύειν [prev. author] 6.9.]]

__2
of the future, sure to come, certain, αὐτίκα γάρ τοι ἔπειτα μεθ᾽ Ἕκτορα πότμος ἑ. [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 18.96; χώλωσις ἑτοίμη τοῖσι περιγινομένοισι 5th c.BC: Hippocrates Medicus “περὶ ἄρθρων ἐμβολῆς” 66]]; also, easy to be done, feasible, ἐπεὶ οὔ σφισιν ἥδε γ᾽ ἑτοίμη (i.e. μῆτις) [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 9.425]]; ἕ. [ἐστι] τὸ διαφθαρῆναι imminent, [Refs 1st c.AD+ [1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus 2.706c]]: with infinitive, ἕ. μᾶλλόν [ἐστι] ἀπεχθάνεσθαι [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 567a, compare 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Hercules Furens” 86]]; οὐ γάρ τι ἕ. μεταπεῖσαι it is not easy.., [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd c.AD: Pausanias Periegeta 2.23.6.]]

__3
of the past, carried into effect, realized, ταῦτα ἑ. τετεύχαται [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 14.53]]; ἠδ᾽ ἄρ᾽ ἑτοῖμα τέτυκτο and this promise has been made good, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 8.384.]]

__II
of persons, ready, active, zealous, ἕ. ἦν ἐμοὶ σειραφόρος [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Agamemnon” 842]]; τινι in or for a thing, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “O.” 4.16]]; ἐς τι for a thing, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 8.96; πρός τι 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Memorabilia” 4.5.12]]: with dative person, ready to assist or go with him, etc., [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “N.” 4.74, 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.70]]: c.infinitive, ready to do, [Refs [[prev. work] 42, 113, +others]]; ἐπιστενάχειν πᾶς τις ἕ. [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Agamemnon” 791; χωρεῖν ἑ. 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Ajax” 813, compare “Ant.” 264, 5th c.BC: Antipho Orator 6.23, 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Vespae” 341 (Lyric poetry)]]; ὑπακούειν ἑτοιμότεροι too ready.., [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 4.61; θηρία ἕ. διαμάχεσθαι 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Symposium” 207b: with _Article_, τὸ μὴ βλέπειν ἑτοίμα 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Electra” 1079 (Lyric poetry)]]; ἦν ἕτοιμος, absolutely, he was ready, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.10; ἑ. ἔχειν τινάς [prev. author] 3.45; ἑ. ποιέεσθαί τινας [prev. author] 5.86.]]

__II.2
of the mind, ready, bold, λῆμα [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Nubes” 458 (Lyric poetry); ἡ γνώμη 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 4.123]]; τὸ ἕ. readiness, resolution, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Orestes” 1106; τὸ ἕ. τῆς γνώμης 2nd-3rd c.AD: Philostratus Sophista “Heroicus” 8.1; τὰ θερμά τε καὶ ἕ. τῶν θηρίων [prev. author] “VA” 7.14.]]

__III
adverb -μως readily, willingly, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 1.80]]; ἑ. ἔχω τελευτᾶν I am ready to die, [NT+5th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demades Orator 4, compare 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 18.161, “PAmh.” 2.32.6 (2nd c.BC), NT.Act.21.13; ἑ. ἥκειν 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 2.5.2; διδόναι “IG” 22.956.24]]; ἑ. παρορᾷς evidently, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Hp.Ma.” 300c]]: comparative ἑτοιμότερον [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Isaeus Orator 4.14, -οτέρως 2nd c.AD: Alexander Rhetor Trall. 12]]: superlative -ότατα [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Politicus” 290a.]]

[in LXX for שָׁנֶה ;]

irregular dative ἔτῃ [Refs [“IG” 2.1059.18]]:—year, τῶν προτέρων ἐτέων in bygone years, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 11.691]]; τόδ᾽ ἐεικοστὸν ἔ. ἐστὶν ἐξ οὗ[Refs 8th c.BC+ [.. 24.765, compare 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 2.89, 19.222; ὅτε.. ὄγδοόν μοι ἐπιπλόμενον ἔ. ἦλθε 7.261]]; ἔ. ἐνιαυτῶν, see at {ἐνιαυτό; ἑκάστου ἔτους} [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Phaedo” 58b; ἀν᾽ ἕκαστον ἔ. 4th-3rd c.BC: Theophrastus Philosophus “Historia Plantarum” 4.4.4; ἀνὰ πᾶν ἔ. “Anthologia Graeca” 9.430 (1st c.BC-1st c.AD: Crinagoras Epigrammaticus); ἀνὰ πάντα ἔτεα 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 8.65]]; δι᾽ ἔτους πέμπτου every fifth year, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Plutus” 584]]; κατὰ ἔ. every year, [NT+5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 4.53, 1st c.BC: Diodorus Siculus Historicus 3.2, NT.Luke.2.41, etc. (frequently καθ᾽ ἕ., as “PPetr.” 3p.34 (3rd c.BC) and later)]]; ἔ. εἰς ἔ. year after year, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Antigone” 340 (Lyric poetry)]]; δι᾽ ἔτους annually, [LXX+3rd c.BC+ [1st c.AD: Philo Judaeus 1.19, 378; εἰς ἔ. 3rd c.BC: Theocritus Poeta Bucolicus “Epigrammata” 13.4; εἰς ἔ. ἐξ ἔτεος [prev. author] 18.15; ἔ. ἐξ ἔτους LXX.Lev.25.50]]; παρὰ ἔ. every other year, [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd c.AD: Pausanias Periegeta 9.32.3 (but πὰρ ϝέτος]]yearly, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [Tab.Heracl. 1.101); πάλαι πολλὰ ἤδη ἔτη 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Apologia” 18b; τρίτῳ ἔτει 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 1.101; τρίτῳ ἔτεϊ πρότερον 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 6.40]]; τρίτῳ ἔτεϊ τούτων in the third year after this, [Refs [[prev. passage], etc.]]; frequently in accusative, ἔ. τόδ᾽ ἤδη δέκατον.. βόσκων now for these ten years, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Philoctetes” 312; τύραννος ἐγεγόνει ἤδη χιλιοστὸν ἔτος 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 615c, compare 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 3.4, 33.23]]; of a person's age, γεγονὼς ἔτη τρία ἀπολείποντα τῶν ἑκατόν [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Isocrates Orator 12.270; οἱ ὑπὲρ τὰ στρατεύσιμα ἔτη γεγονότες 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 1.2.4, compare 13, etc.]]; without γεγονώς, τοὺς ὑπὲρ τετταράκοντα ἔτη [Refs [[prev. author] “An.” 5.3.1; οἱ μέχρι τετταράκοντα ἐτῶν [prev. work] 6.4.25]], etc.: in genitive, ἐπειδὰν ἐτῶν ᾖ τις τριάκοντα [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Leges” 721b]]; μυρίων ἐτῶν within a period of [Refs [10, 000]]years, [Refs [[prev. author] “Phdr.” 248e; ὥρα ἔτους, see at {ὥρα} 1.]]

εὖ
adv. (prop. neuter of old Epic ἐΰς, good, noble) [in LXX, εὖ γίγνεσθαι, εὖ ποιεῖν (יָטַב) ;]
well: εὖ γιν., Eph.6:3 (LXX); εὖ ποιεῖν, with dative (cf. Sir.12:1-2), to do good, Mrk.14:7 (where Nestle suggests εὐποιεῖν, which see); εὖ πράσστειν, to fare well, Act.15:29; in replies (= εὖγε), good! well done! Mat.25:21, 23 Luk.19:17 (εὖγε, WH, txt.).†
εὖ-γε,
adv.,
in replies, well! good! well done!: Luk.19:17 (WH for Rec. εὖ, which see).†
(AS)

---

LSJ / STEPBible (TFLSJ)
εὖ,
Epic dialect also ἐΰ [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 1.302, etc., compare 2nd c.AD: Apollonius Dyscolus Grammaticus “de Adverbiis;” 200.20:]] adverb (properly neuter of ἐΰς):—well, opposed to κακῶς (as in [Refs 8th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 4.63), 8th c.BC: Homerus Epicus, etc.]]

__I
of knowledge or action, well, thoroughly, competently, εὖ μέν τις δόρυ θηξάσθω, εὖ δ᾽ ἀσπίδα θέσθω [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 2.382; εὖ καὶ ἐπισταμένως κέασαν ξύλα 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 20.161; τὴν πόλιν κοσμέων καλῶς τε καὶ εὖ 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.59; τὸ πρᾶγμα βασανίσας καλῶς τε καὶ εὖ 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Euthydemus” 307b, etc.]]; τόξων ἐῢ εἰδώς cunning with the bow, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 2.718, etc.; εὖ τόδ᾽ ἴσθι 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Persae” 173 (troch.); εὖ γὰρ σαφῶς τόδ᾽ ἴστε [prev. work] 784]]; εὖ οἶδ᾽ ὅτι parenthetic in colloquial speech, σὺ γὰρ εὖ οἶδ᾽ ὅτι οὐ πράγματ᾽ ᾄσει [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Pax” 1296, compare 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 14.2, etc.]]; εὖ οἶδα, in answers, Dioxipp.4; εὖ μήδεο consider well, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 2.360]]; εὖ λέγεις well spoken ! [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Apologia” 24e, compare 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 5.2, etc.: with λέγω omitted, οὐδὲ τοῦτ᾽ εὖ Ἐρατοσθένης 1st c.BC-1st c.AD: Strabo Geographus 1.3.1.]]

__I.2
morally well, kindly, εὖ ἔρδειν, ={εὐεργετεῖν}, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 5.650]]; εὖ εἰπεῖν τινα to speak well of him, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 1.302; εὖ δρᾶν εὖ παθών 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Philoctetes” 672, etc.]]

__I.3
with passive or intransitive Verbs, fortunately, happily, in good case, εὖ ζώουσι [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 19.79]]; εὖ οἴκαδ᾽ ἱκέσθαι safely, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 1.19, compare 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 3.188; τοῦ βίου εὖ ἥκειν 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.30]]; εὖ φρονῶν in one's right mind, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Prometheus Vinctus” 387, etc. (but εὖ φρονεῖν εἴς τινας, τὰ σά]], to be well-disposed towards, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Andocides Orator 2.4, 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Ajax” 491)]]; standing last for emphasis, ἄνδρες γεγονότες εὖ [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 7.134; νόμους μὴ λύειν ἔχοντας εὖ [prev. author] 3.82; τελευτήσει τὸν βίον εὖ [prev. author] 1.32, compare 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 1.71, 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Ethica Nicomachea” 1124b13, etc.]]: separated from its Verb, εὖ πρᾶγμα συντεθέν [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 18.144.]]

__II
coupled with other Adverbs, especially when qualifying nouns, adjectives, and adverbs, εὖ μάλα [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 4.96, etc.; ἡ ἀορτὴ εὖ μάλα κοίλη 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Historia Animalium” 514b22; εὖ μάλα πᾶσαι “hymnus ad Apollinem” 171; εὖ μάλα πολλά 1st c.AD(?): Heraclitus 35; εὖ μάλα πρεσβύτης 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Euthyphro” 4a; μάλα εὖ καὶ κομψῶς [prev. author] “Sph.” 236d; εὖ καὶ μάλα [prev. author] “Smp.” 194a (sed compare “CQ” 15.4); κάρτα εὖ 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 3.150]]; εὖ.. πάνυ or πάνυ εὖ, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Plutus” 198, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Meno” 80b; εὖ σφόδρα 4th c.BC: Nicostratus Philosophus 8, 4th-3rd c.BC: Philemo Comicus 75.4]]; εὖ κἀνδρικῶς, εὖ κἀνδρείως, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Equites” 379 (Lyric poetry), “Th.” 656]]; καλῶστεκαὶ εὖ[Refs 5th c.BC+ [(see.above 1.1); εὖ τε καὶ καλῶς 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 503d.]]

__III
as substantive, τὸ εὖ the right, the good cause, τὸ δ᾽ εὖ νικάτω [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Agamemnon” 121; τὸ γὰρ εὖ μετ᾽ ἐμοῦ 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Acharnenses” 661; the “Good”, final cause, τὸ εὖ τεκταινόμενος ἐν πᾶσιν τοῖς γιγνομένοις 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Timaeus” 68e; τοῦ εὖ ἕνεκα 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “de Sensu” 437a1, compare [same work] “Metaphorical” 1092b26]]: in Art, perfection, the ideal, τὸ εὖ διὰ πολλῶν ἀριθμῶν γίνεται [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Polyclitus Philosophus 2.]]

__IV
as the Predicate of a proposition, τί τῶνδ᾽ ε; [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Choephori” 338 (Lyric poetry), compare 116]]; εὖ εἴη may it be well, [Refs [[prev. author] “Ag.” 216 (Lyric poetry)]]; εὐορκεῦντι μέμ μοι εὖ εἶμεν or εἴη, [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [“SIG” 953.9 (Calymna, 2nd c.BC), “PEleph.” 23.19 (3rd c.BC)]]; εὖ σοι γένοιτο well be with thee, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Alcestis” 627, compare “fragment” 707.]]

__V
Interjection, well done! to cheer on dogs, εὖ κύνες [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Cynegeticus” 9.20]]; ahoy! ho! [Refs [Lyric poetry Alex.Adesp. 20.11]]; compare εὖγε.

__VI
in Compds., implying abundance (εὐανδρία), prosperity (εὐδαίμων, opposed to κακοδαίμων), ease (εὔβατος, opposed to δύσβατος): compounded only with Nouns and adjectives (hence εὖ πάσχω, εὖ ποιέω are better written divisim, but εὐποιητικός implies εὐποιέω: see at {ἀντευποιέω}); εὐδοκέω is exceptional. (Replaced by καλῶς in later Gr., except in set phrases.)

εὐθύ, of Place, straight, usually of motion or direction, εὐθὺ Πύλονδε straight to.., [Refs 5th c.BC+ [hymnus ad Mercurium 342; εὐθὺ πρὸς τὰ νυμφικὰ λέχη 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Tyrannus” 1242]]; εὐ. [τὴν ἐπὶ] Βαβυλῶνος straight towards.., [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 5.2.37: and so with _genitive_, εὐ. τῶν κυρηβίων, εὐθὺ Πελλήνης, 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Equites” 254, “Av.” 1421; εὐ.τοῦ Διός [prev. author] “Pax” 68; εὐ. τοὐρόφου 5th c.BC: Eupolis Comicus 47; εὐ. τῆς σωτηρίας 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Pax” 301, compare 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 8.88, etc.]]; ἀποθανούμενος ᾔει εὐ. τοῦ δαιμονίου in opposition to.., [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Theages” 129a (assuming variant)]]; compare ἰθύς.

__B.I.b
νῆσον οἰκεῖ εὐθὺ Ἴστρου opposite.., [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd c.AD: Maximus Tyrius Sophista 15.7.]]

__B.I.2
={ἁπλῶς}, simply, καλεῖν [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-3rd c.BC: Theophrastus Philosophus “Historia Plantarum” 3.8.2, compare 9.13.2.]]

__B.I.3
rarely of Time, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Philochorus Historicus 144, 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Rhetorica” 1414b25, “UPZ” 77.27 (2nd c.BC), “PGrenf.” 1.1.24 (2nd c.BC), Aristeas 24, 2nd c.AD: Lucianus Sophista “Nav.” 22.]]

__B.II
εὐθύς,

__B.II.1
of Time, straightway, forthwith, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “O.” 8.41; ὁ δ᾽ εὐ. ὡς ἤκουσε 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Persae” 361; ὁ δ᾽ εὐ. ἐξῴμωξεν 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Ajax” 317; τὸ μὲν εὐ. τὸ δὲ καὶ διανοούμενον 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 1.1, compare 5.3, 7.77]]; joined with other adverbial words, τάχα δ᾽ εὐ. ἰών [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “P.” 4.83; εὐ. κατὰ τάχος 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 6.101]]; εὐ. παραχρῆμα (see. entry παραχρῆμα); εὐ. ἀπ᾽ αρχῆς [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Pax” 84 (_anapaest meter_); εὐ. ἐξ ἀρχῆς 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 7.2.16]]; ἐξ ἀρχῆς εὐ. [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Politica” 1287b10; εὐ. κατ᾽ ἀρχάς 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Timaeus” 24b; ἀφ᾽ ἑσπέρας εὐ. ἤδη 2nd c.AD: Lucianus Sophista “Gall.” 1]]; εὐ. ἐκ νέου, ἐκ παιδός, even from one's youth, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 485d, 519a; εὐ. ἐκ παιδίου 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 1.6.20]]: with a participle, εὐ. νέοι ὄντες [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 2.39; εὐ. ἥκων 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 4.7.2; εὐ. ἀπεκτονώς 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 23.127]]; τοῦ θέρους εὐ. ἀρχομένου just at the beginning of summer, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 2.47]]; ἀρξάμενος εὐ. καθισταμένου [τοῦ πολέμου] from the very beginning of the war, [Refs [[prev. author] 1.1]]; εὐ. ἀποβεβηκότι immediately on disembarking, [Refs [[prev. author] 4.43]]; εὐ. γενομένοις at the moment of birth, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Theaetetus” 186b]]: metaphorically, at once, naturally, ὑπάρχει εὐθὺς γένη ἔχον τὸ ὄν Being falls at once into genera, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Metaphysica” 1004a5, compare “Po.” 1452a14]]: with substantive, ἡ τῶν Ἰταλιωτῶν εὐθὺς φυγή [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd c.AD: Herodianus Grammaticus 8.1.5.]]

__B.II.2
less frequently in a local relation, ὑπὲρ τῆς πόλεως εὐ. just above the city, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 6.96]]; παρ᾽ αὐτὴν εὐ. ὁ ἔσπλους ἐστίν directly past it (the mole), [Refs [[prev. author] 8.90]]; ἐγγύτατα τούτου εὐ. ἐχομένη immediately adjoining this, [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [[prev. passage],compare 3rd c.BC: Theocritus Poeta Bucolicus 25.23]]; εὐ. ἐπὶ τὴν γέφυραν Foed. cited in [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 4.118, compare 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 7.2.1, 2, 2.4.24, “Ages.” 1.29]]; τὴν εὐ. Ἄργους κἀπιδαυρίας ὁδόν the road leading straight to Argos, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Hippolytus” 1197 (condemned by 9th c.AD: Photius Legal icographus, etc.); εὐ. Λυκείου 5th c.BC: Pherecrates Comicus 110, compare 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Historia Animalium” 498a32, etc.]]

__B.II.3
of Manner, directly, simply, variant in [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Meno” 100a.]]

__B.II.4
like{αὐτίκα} [Refs [11:]]for instance, to take the first example that occurs, ὥσπερ ζῷον εὐθύς [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Politica” 1277a6, compare “Cael.” 284b10, etc.; οἷον εὐθύς 2nd c.AD: Cleomedes Astronomus 1.1, 1st-2nd c.AD: Dio Chrysostomus Sophista 11.145.]]

__C
regular adverb εὐθέως, used just as εὐθύς, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Ajax” 31, “OC” 994, 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Fragmenta” 31, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Phaedo” 63a, etc.]]; αἰσθόμενος εὐθέως as soon as he perceived, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Lysias Orator 3.11; ἐπεὶ εὐθέως ᾔσθοντο 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Historia Graeca (Hellenica)” 3.2.4; εὐθέως παραχρῆμα 5th c.BC: Antipho Orator 1.20, 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 52.6.]]

__C.2
={εὐθύς} [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Bacchylides Lyricus 11.4, οἷον εὐθέως]] as for example, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [2nd c.BC: Polybius Historicus 6.52.1, 12.5.6 (uncertain meaning in 5th c.BC: Hippocrates Medicus “περὶ ἄρθρων ἐμβολῆς” 55)]]; so εὐ. alone, [Refs 1st c.AD+ [1st c.AD: Philo Judaeus 2.589. LSJ / STEPBible (TFLSJ)
εὐθῡν-ω,
(εὐθύς) = the Homeric ἰθύνω (which is a frequently variant, as in [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Persae” 773)]]: — guide straight, direct, οἰωνὸν γνώμῃ στομίων ἄτερ εὐθύνων [Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. author] “Pr.” 289; εὐ. ἡνίας 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Aves” 1739 (Lyric poetry)]]; [ἅρματα] [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Isocrates Orator 1.32]]; εὐ. δόρυ steer the bark straight, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Cyclops” 15; εὐ. πλάτην [prev. author] “Hec.” 39; ὁ εὐθύνων]]the helmsman, [NT.Jam.3.4]; εὐ. ἀγέλας lead or drive them, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 1.1.2]]; εὐ. χερσί manage, guide him, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Ajax” 542; εὐ. πόδα 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Heraclidae” 728, etc.]]

__2
metaphorically, direct, govern, Κύρου δὲ παῖς.. ηὔθυνε στρατόν [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Persae” 773; πᾶσαν εὐθύνων πόλιν 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Antigone” 178, compare 1164, 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Hecuba” 9, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Minos” 320d.]]

__3
make straight, straighten, opposed to κάμπτειν, πτέρυγας [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “de Incessu Animalium” 709b10]]:— passive, [Refs [[prev. author] “Mete.” 385b32.]]

__II
make or put straight, εὐ. δίκας σκολιάς make crooked judgements straight, [Refs 6th c.BC+ [6th c.BC: Solon Lyricus 4.37; εὐ. λαοῖς δίκας 5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “P.” 4.153]]; εὐ. οὖρον send a straight fair wind, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. author] “O.” 13.28; εὐ. ὄλβον [prev. author] “P.” 1.46; ὥσπερ ξύλον διαστρεφόμενον.. εὐ. ἀπειλαῖς καὶ πληγαῖς 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Protagoras” 325d, compare 326e.]]

__III
examine the conduct of an official, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [[prev. author] “Plt.” 299a; εὐ. τὰς ἀρχάς 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Politica” 1271a6, 1274a17, +others]]:—passive, with genitive, - όμενος τῆς ἐφορείας [Refs [[prev. author] “Rh.” 1419a31.]]

__III.2
with genitive criminis, call to account for.., τινα κλοπῆς [Refs 1st c.AD+ [1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus “Cicero” 9:]] —passive, τῶν ἀδικημάτων ηὐθύνθη [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 1.95]]; οἱ -όμενοι the culprits, Mitteis [Refs 2nd c.BC+ [“Chr.” 31 iii 10 (2nd c.BC),compare “Notiz.Arch.” 4.21 (Cyrene, 1st c.BC)]]: with dative, εὐ. φόνῳ [Refs 2nd c.BC+ [“PTeb.” 14.4 (2nd c.BC)]]; to be mulcted, punished, ἐπί τινι [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd-3rd c.AD: Dio Cassius Historicus “fragment” 90, +others: _absolutely_, “IG” 12.41.6; ἑκατὸν δραχμῆσι [prev. work]4.15, +others]]

__III.3
generally, refute or censure, τοὺς λόγους τινός [Refs 1st c.BC+ [1st c.BC: Philodemus Philosophus “de Pietate - Herkulanische Studien” 67; τὴν Φιλίστου διάλεκτον 1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus “Nicias” 1]]:—passive, to be refuted, δι᾽ αὐτῶν τῶν φαινομένων [Refs 1st c.BC+ [1st c.BC: Philodemus Philosophus “περὶ σημείων καὶ σημειώσεων” 30, compare 3rd c.AD: Plotinus Philosophus 3.6.13]]; but also, to be critically examined, [Refs [[prev. author] 4.6.13.]]

examine by torture, [Refs 6th c.AD+ [6th c.AD: Procopius Caesariensis Historicus “de Bello Gothico” 3.32 (from Pass).]]

intransitive, serve as εὔθυνος, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Leges” 946d.]]

__A
straight, direct, whether vertically or horizontally, opposed to σκολιός, καμπύλος, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Theaetetus” 194b, “R.” 602c, etc.]]; κατὰ τὸ εὐθὺ ἑστάναι stands still with reference to the vertical, of a spinning top, [Refs [[prev. work] 436e]]; εὐ. πλόος, ὁδοί, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “O.” 6.103, “N.” 1.25, etc.; εὐθυτέρα ὁδός 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 1.3.4; ὁδοὺς εὐθείας ἔτεμε 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 2.100; ῥόμβος ἀκόντων 5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “O.” 13.93]]; εὐθείᾳ (i.e. ὁδῷ) by the straight road, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Leges” 716a; εὐθεῖαν ἕρπε 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Fragmenta - American Journal of Philology” 195]]; τὴν εὐ. [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Medea” 384; ἐπ᾽ εὐθείας 1st c.BC: Diodorus Siculus Historicus 19.38, 1st c.BC: Asclepiodotus Tacticus “Tact.” 2.6, 3rd c.AD: Plotinus Philosophus 2.1.8; so also εἰς τὸ εὐ.βλέπειν 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “de Equitandi ratione” 7.17, etc.]]; πλήρης τοῦ εὐθέος tired of going straight forward, [Refs [[prev. work] 14]]; ἡ ἐς τὸ εὐ. τῆς ῥητορικῆς ὁδός the direct road to.., [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd c.AD: Lucianus Sophista “Rh.Pr.” 10]]; κατ᾽ εὐθύ on level ground, [LXX.1Ki.21.23]; but ἡ κατ᾽ εὐ. τάσις in the direct line, [Refs 1st c.BC+ [1st c.BC: Apollonius Citiensis Medicus 2]]; on the same side, [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd c.AD: Galenus Medicus 8.62]]; also, opposed to εἰς τὸ ἐντός, [Refs 3rd c.AD+ [3rd c.AD: Plotinus Philosophus 6.7.14.]]

__A.2
in moral sense, straightforward, frank, of persons, εὐθὺν χρὴ τὸν ἑταῖρον ἔμμεν καὶ μὴ σκολιὰ φρονεῖν [Refs 7th c.BC+ [“Scol.” 16; κοινᾶνι παρ᾽ εὐθυτάτῳ 5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “P.” 3.28; ῥῆτραι 7th c.BC: Tyrtaeus Elegiacus 4.6; τόλμα 5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “O.” 13.12; δίκα [prev. author] “N.” 10.12; κρῖνε δ᾽ εὐθεῖαν δίκην 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Eumenides” 433, compare Ἀρχ. Ἐφ. 1911.134 (from Gonni)]]; ὁ εὐθὺς λόγος [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Hippolytus” 492; τὸ εὐ. τε καὶ τὸ ἐλεύθερον 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Theaetetus” 173a]]; ἀπὸ τοῦ εὐθέος λέγειν to speak straight out, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 3.43]]; ἐκ τοῦ εὐ. ὑπουργεῖν outright, openly, without reserve, [Refs [[prev. author] 1.34]]; ἐκ τοῦ εὐ., opposed to δι᾽ αἰνιγμάτων, [Refs 1st c.AD+ [2nd c.AD: Pausanias Periegeta 8.8.3: in _feminine_, τὴν εὐθεῖάν τινι συνειπεῖν 1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus “Cicero” 7; ἁπλῶς καὶ δι᾽ εὐθείας [prev. author] 2.408e]]; ἀπ᾽ εὐθείας [Refs [[prev. work]57a, “Fab.” 3]]; κατ᾽ εὐθεῖαν by direct reasoning, [Refs 5th c.AD+ [5th-6th c.AD: Damascius Philosophus “de Principiis” 432]]; μηδὲν ἐξ εὐθείας παρέχει (an amulet) does no good directly, [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd c.AD: Soranus Medicus 2.42.]]

__A.3
εὐθεῖα, ἡ, as substantive,

__A.3.a
(i.e. γραμμή) straight line, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Analytica Priora” 49b35, +others, 3rd c.BC: Euclides Geometra 1 “Def.” 7, +others]]; ἐπ᾽ εὐθείας εἶναι lie in a straight line, [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [3rd c.BC: Archimedes Geometra “περὶ κωνοειδέων καὶ σφαιροειδέων” 7, +others]]; ἐπὶ τὴν αὐτὴν εὐ., ἐπὶ τῆς αὐτῆς εὐ. ἐκτείνειν, in the same line, [Refs 2nd c.BC+ [2nd c.BC: Polybius Historicus 3.113.2, 3; ἐπὶ μίαν εὐ. [prev. work] 8]]: comparative, εὐθυτέρα ἡ γραμμὴ γίνεται [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Mechanica” 855a24.]]

__A.3.b
(i.e. πτῶσις) nominative case, [Refs 2nd c.BC+ [2nd c.BC: Dionysius Thrax Grammaticus 636.5, 2nd c.AD: Apollonius Dyscolus Grammaticus “de Pronominibus;” 6.11, etc.]]; κατ᾽ εὐθύ in the nominative, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Sophistici Elenchi” 182a3.]]

__B

[τὴν ἐπὶ] Βαβυλῶνος straight towards.., [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 5.2.37: and so with _genitive_, εὐ. τῶν κυρηβίων, εὐθὺ Πελλήνης, 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Equites” 254, “Av.” 1421; εὐ.τοῦ Διός [prev. author] “Pax” 68; εὐ. τοὐρόφου 5th c.BC: Eupolis Comicus 47; εὐ. τῆς σωτηρίας 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Pax” 301, compare 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 8.88, etc.]]; ἀποθανούμενος ᾔει εὐ. τοῦ δαιμονίου in opposition to.., [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Theages” 129a (assuming variant)]]; compare ἰθύς.
