deep_entry:
Abbott-Smith / STEPBible (TBESG)
εὑρίσκω,
[in LXX chiefly for מצא, also for נשׂג hi., etc. ;]
to find, with or without previous search: absol., opposite to ζητέω, Mat.7:7, 8 Luk.11:9, 10; with accusative, Mat.2:8, Mrk.1:37, Act.13:22, 2Ti.1:17, al.; pass., οὐχ εὑ., of disappearance, Heb.11:5, Rev.16:20, al.; γῆ κ. τὰ ἐν αὐτῇ ἔργα εὑρεθήσεται (for conjectures as to the meaning of this reading, see Mayor, ICC, in l.),  2Pe.3:10, WH, R, mg. Metaphorical, to find, find out by inquiry, learn, discover: Luk.19:48, Act.4:21; αἰτίαν, Jhn.18:38, Act.13:28, al.; pass., Mat.1:18, Luk.17:18, Rom.7:10, 1Co.4:2, Gal.2:17, 1Pe.1:7, Rev.5:4, al.; of attaining to the knowledge of God, εὑ. θεόν, Act.17:27; pass., Rom.10:20 (LXX). Mid., to find for oneself, gain, procure, obtain: with accusative of thing(s), λύτρωσιν, Heb.9:12; act. in same sense (so cl. poets, but not in Attic prose), Mat.10:39 11:29, Luk.1:30, Act.7:46, 2Ti.1:18, al. (cf. ἀν-ευρίσκω).
(AS)

---

LSJ / STEPBible (TFLSJ)
εὑρίσκω,
imperfect ηὕρισκον or εὕρ- [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Tyrannus” 68, etc.]]: future εὑρήσω [Refs 5th c.BC+ [“hymnus ad Mercurium” 302, 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 7.67, etc.]]: aorist 2 εὗρον [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 1.498, etc., later ηὗρον or εὗρον 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Medea” 553, etc.]]; 3rd.pers. plural εὕροσαν [LXX+1st c.AD+ [LXX.Deu.31.17, “BGU” 1201.16 (1st c.AD); _imperative_ εὑρέ Hdn.Gr. 2.23]]; Epic dialect infinitive εὑρέμεναι [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 12.393]]: later aorist 1 εὕρησα [Refs 4th c.AD+ [4th c.AD(?): Manetho Astrologus 5.137]]; εὗρα variant in [NT+2nd c.AD+ [NT.Luke.8.35, NT.Act.5.10, (ἐν-) “PGen.” 3.19 (2nd c.AD)]]: perfect εὕρηκα [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Tyrannus” 546, etc.]], perfect imperative 2nd pers. singular εὕρηκε [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Nausicrates Comicus 1 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator]]:—middle, future εὑρήσομαι [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 9.6, 5th c.BC: Lysias Orator 13.9, etc.]]: aorist 2 εὑρόμην [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Homerus Epicus, _Attic dialect_ ηὑρ- or εὑρ- 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Prometheus Vinctus” 269, 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 1.58, etc.]]: aorist 1 εὑράμην [NT+8th c.BC+ [8th-7th c.BC: Hesiodus Epicus “Fragmenta” 116.3 (testes omnes), 1st c.BC-1st c.AD: Strabo Geographus 12.34.4, 4th c.AD: Iamblichus Philosophus “de vita Pythagorica” 35.255, “Anthologia Graeca” 9.29 (1st c.AD: Antiphilus Epigrammaticus), epigram cited in 2nd c.AD: Pausanias Periegeta 6.20.14, NT.Heb.9.12, “IG” 3.900 (2nd c.AD)]]:—passive, future εὑρεθήσομαι [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Tyrannus” 108, 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Iphigenia Aulidensis” 1105, 5th-6th c.BC: Isocrates Orator 9.41]]: aorist 1 ηὑρέθην or εὑρέθην [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Ajax” 1135]], etc.: perfect ηὕρημαι or εὕρ- [Refs 8th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Persae” 743 (troch), etc.— 8th c.BC: Homerus Epicus]] has only aorist active and middle, except ἔθ᾽ εὑρίσκω (variant{ἐφευρίσκω}) [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 19.158. (Earlier _Attic dialect_ Inscrr. have ηὑρέθην, ηὕρημαι, as “IG” 22.1636.32, +others, “epigram Gr.” 35 (4th c.BC): εὑρέθην “SIG” 679.80 (5th c.BC: Magnes Comicus Mae., 2nd c.BC)]]: the augment is seldom found in Papyri, ηὕρισκεν [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [“PPetr.” 3p.101 (3rd c.BC)]]; never in those of [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-3rd c.BC: Menander Comicus or 1st c.BC: Philodemus Gadarensis Epigrammaticus)]]:—find, εὗρεν δ᾽ εὐρύοπα Κρονίδην ἄτερ ἥμενον ἄλλων [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 1.498, etc.]]; εὕρημα εὑ., see at {εὕρημα}.

__2
with participle, find that.., εὕρισκε Λακεδαιμονίους.. προέχοντας [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.56, compare 1.5]]:—and in passive, ἤν εὑρεθῇς μὴ δίκαιος ὤν [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Trachiniae” 411, compare “OT” 839, “OC” 946: with]]participle omitted, ὅταν τοὺς θεοὺς εὕρω κακούς (i.e. ὄντας) [Refs [[prev. author] “Ph.” 452]]; εὑρήσει τοσαῦτα ἔτη (i.e. ὄντα) [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 5.26]]; θῆλυς εὕρημαι (i.e. ὤν) [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Trachiniae” 1075; ἄνους ηὑρέθη [prev. author] “Aj.” 763.]]

__3
with infinitive, εὕρισκε πρῆγμά οἱ εἶναι.. found that the thing for him was.., [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.79:]] —middle, εὑρίσκεται (sed to be read εὕρισκέ τε) ταῦτα καιριώτατα εἶναι[Refs [[prev. work] 125]]:—active, also, find means, be able, οὐχ εὑρίσκει χρήσασθαι [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd c.AD: Arrianus Historicus “Epicteti Dissertationes” 2.12.2.]]

__4
εὑ. ὅπως.. to find by what means.., [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 7.67]]:—middle, c.infinitive, find out or discover how to.., ηὕρετο.. παύειν [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Medea” 196 (_anapaest meter_).]]

__5
passive, εὑρέθη ὅτι.. it was found that.., [LXX.1Esd.2.22(26).]

__6
befall, of evils, τινα[LXX.Gen.44.34, LXX.Deu.31.17.]

__II
find out, discover, οὐδέ τι μῆχος εὑρέμεναι δυνάμεσθα [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 12.393; οὐδέ τι τέκμωρ εὑρέμεναι δύνασαι 4.374, compare 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 7.31; εὑ. ὁδόν 5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “P.” 10.29; ἐξ ἀμηχάνων πόρον 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Prometheus Vinctus” 59; μηχανὴν σωτηρίας [prev. author] “Th.” 209; πημάτων ἄρηξιν 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Electra” 875; τινα ἐμοῦ βελτίονα 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Plutus” 104, etc.: _absolutely_, εὕρηκα 3rd c.BC: Archimedes Geometra cited in 1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus 2.1094c]]:—middle, εὕρετο τέκμωρ [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 16.472]]; ὄνομ᾽ εὕρεο think of a name to give him, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 19.403; εἴ τιν᾽ ἑταίροισιν θανάτου λύσιν.. εὑροίμην 9.422.]]

__II.2
with infinitive, get a chance of, be able, ἵνα εὕρωμεν ἐπιστολὴν γράψαι [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [“BGU” 822.28 (2nd-3rd c.AD), compare 17, 20, “PGrenf.” 1.64.3 (6th c.AD), etc.]]

__III
devise, invent, ὀχήματα [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Prometheus Vinctus” 468, etc.; πρόφασιν 5th c.BC: Antipho Orator 5.65:]] —middle, τὰ δ᾽ ἔργα τοὺς λόγους εὑρίσκεται deeds make themselves words, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Electra” 625.]]

__IV
get, gain, ἀρετάν, δόξαν, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “O.” 7.89, “P.” 2.64; τὰ χρήματ᾽ ἀνθρώποισιν εὑρίσκει φίλους 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Fragmenta” 88; ἐξ ὀλβίων ἄζηλον εὑροῦσαι βίον [prev. author] “Tr.” 284, compare 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Medea” 1107 (_anapaest meter_); δεινὰ δ᾽ εὑροῦσαν πρὸς αὐθαίμων πάθη 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Coloneus” 1078 (Lyric poetry); ἀφ᾽ ὧν ὄνασιν εὕρωσι [prev. author] “El.” 1061]]; μέγ᾽ εὑρεῖν κέρδος[Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. work] 1305; εὑ. σωτηρίαν τῷ ἀνθρώπῳ 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Protagoras” 321c]]; εὑ. μητρὶ φόνον bring about murder, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Electra” 650]]: absolutely, acquire wealth, [LXX.Lev.25.47]:—middle, find or get for oneself, bring on oneself, οἷ.. αὐτῷ πρώτῳ κακὸν εὕρετο [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 21.304]] (so in active, μή πού τις ἐπίσπαστον κακὸν εὕρῃ [Refs 4th c.BC+ [24.462); αὐτὸς ηὑρόμην πόνους 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Prometheus Vinctus” 269; μοῖραν ηὕρετ᾽ ἀσφαλῆ [prev. author] “Ag.” 1588, compare “Th.” 880 (Lyric poetry)]]: so in perfect passive, μέγα πένθος ηὕρηται [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Ajax” 615 (Lyric poetry)]]; εὑρήσεται τιμωρίην will get for himself, obtain, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 3.148, compare 9.26; ἀλεωρήν [prev. author] 9.6; κλέος 5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “P.” 3.111; ἄδειαν εὑρόμενος 5th-6th c.BC: Andocides Orator 1.15; ἀτέλειαν 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 20.1; εὑρίσκεσθαι ὠφελίαν ἀπό τινος 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 1.31; τι παρά τινος “IG” 12.108.47, 5th c.BC: Lysias Orator 13.9]]; εὑ. παρά τινος with infinitive, procure from him that.., [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 9.28; δεηθέντες οὐκ ἐδύναντο εὑρέσθαι 5th c.BC: Lysias Orator 14.20.]]

__V
especially of merchandise, etc., fetch, earn money, εὑροῦσα πολλὸν χρυσίον having fetched a large sum, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.196; ηὗρε πλέον ἢ ἐνενήκοντα τάλαντα 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Historia Graeca (Hellenica)” 3.4.24, compare “Vect.” 4.40]]; οἰκία εὑρίσκουσα δισχιλίας (i.e. δραχμάς) [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Isaeus Orator 8.35]]; ἐγδίδομεν.. τοὺς θριγκοὺς.. ὅτι ἂν εὕρωσιν for what they will fetch, [Refs [Inscriptiones Graecae 7.3073.7 (Lebad.)]]; ἐρωτᾶν τί εὑρίσκει what it will fetch, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-3rd c.BC: Theophrastus Philosophus “Characteres” 15.4.]]

__V.2
of the sum or bid which secures an article or contract, οἰκέτην.. ἀποδίδοται τοῦ εὑρόντος sells for what he will fetch, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Memorabilia” 2.5.5; τοῦ ἤδη εὑρίσκοντος ἀπεδίδοτο 4th c.BC: Aeschines Orator 1.96, compare “SIG” 966.37 (Attica, 4th c.BC), 581.99 (Rhodes-Hierapytna, 2nd c.BC)]]; ἐκτιθέτωσαν τὸ εὑρίσκον ἐφ᾽ ἡμέρας δέκα the highest or winning bid, [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [“PRev.Laws” 48.16 (3rd c.BC),compare “UPZ” 112vi9 (3rd c.BC)]]; προσέβαλον αὐτῷ τοῦ εὑρίσκοντος ἀνὰ [x] ἱερεῖα [x] I have placed at his disposal [x] pigs at the current price of [x], [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [“PCair.Zen.” 161.5 (3rd c.BC),compare “UPZ” 114(1).24 (2nd c.BC).]]

short_definition: a north wind — Εὐρ-ακύλων (Rec. εὐροκλύδων, which see), -ωνος
deep_entry:
Abbott-Smith / STEPBible (TBESG)
Εὐρ-ακύλων (Rec. εὐροκλύδων, which see), -ωνος
(Εὖρος, the East wind, and Lat. Aquilo; Vg., Euroaquilo),
the Euraquilo, a N.E. wind (i.e. between Eurus and Aquilo): Act.27:14.†
εὐρο-κλύδων (G, εὐροκλ-), -ωνος, ὁ
(Εὖρος (seel.  εὐρύς, broad), κλύδων),
Euroclydon (prob. a sailor's corruption of Εὐρακύλων, which see): Act.17:14, Rec,†
(AS)

---

LSJ / STEPBible (TFLSJ)
εὐρακύλων, ωνος, ὁ,
name of a north-east wind, = Latin (Vulg.) euroaquilo, ἄνεμος τυφωνικὸς ὁ καλούμενος εὐ. [NT.Act.27.14], with many variants, including εὐροκλύδων.
source_notes: STEPBible TBESG (CC BY), STEPBible TFLSJ (CC BY)

deep_entry:
Abbott-Smith / STEPBible (TBESG)
εὐ-σέβεια, -ας, ἡ
(εὐσεβής, which see), [in LXX: Pro.1:7, Isa.33:6 (יִרְאָה), Pro.13:11 (aliter in Heb.), Isa.11:2 (יְהוָֹה יִרְאָה), I Est.1:23, Wis.10:12, Sir.49:3, and very frequently in 4Mac ;]
__1. piety, reverence (towards parents and others).
__2. piety towards God, godliness: Act.3:12, 1Ti.2:2 4:7-8 6:5-6 6:11, 2Pe.1:3 1:6-7; τὸ τῆς εὐ. μυστήριον, 1Ti.3:16; ἡ κατ᾽ εὐ. διδασκαλία, 1Ti.6:3; ἡ ἀλήθεια ἡ κατ᾽ εὐ., Tit.1:1; μόρφωσις εὐσεβείας, 2Ti.3:5; pl. (see Bl., § 32, 6; Mayor on Jas.2:1), 2Pe.3:11 (on the use of εὐ. and cognates in Past. Epp., see CGT, on 1Ti.2:2; cf. also Cremer, 524).†
(AS)

---

LSJ / STEPBible (TFLSJ)
εὐσέβεια, ἡ
(compare εὐσεβία), reverence towards the gods or parents, piety or filial respect, εὐ. εἰς θεοὺς καὶ γονέας [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 615c, etc.; μιαίνων εὐσέβειαν Ἄρης 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Septem contra Thebas” 344 (Lyric poetry)]]; εὐ. Ζηνός towards him, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Electra” 1097 (Lyric poetry); πρὸς εὐσέβειαν, ={εὐσεβῶς}, [prev. work] 464]]; εὐ. πρός, περὶ τοὺς θεούς, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Symposium” 193d, 5th-6th c.BC: Isocrates Orator 12.124, compare 10.58; πρὸς ἀδελφόν 2nd-3rd c.AD: Dio Cassius Historicus 48.5]]; ἡ πρὸς τὸ θεῖον εὐ. [Refs 1st c.BC+ [“Inscription Prien.” 117.63 (1st c.BC), etc.]]; τὴν εὐ. τῶν πραχθέντων [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Antipho Orator 3.2.12]]: plural, acts of piety, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Rhetorica ad Alexandrum” 1423b28.]]

__2
loyalty, ἡ ὑμετέρα πρός με εὐ. [Refs [“PLond.” 3.1178.14 (from Claudius)]]; ἡ εἴς με εὔνοια καὶ εὐ. [Refs [“SIG” 814.2 (from Nero).]]

__3
= Latin [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [“Pietas”, 2nd c.AD: Appianus Historicus “Bella Civilia” 2.104, Mitteis “Chr.” 71.12 (V 2nd c.AD: Apollonius Dyscolus Grammaticus), 5th-6th c.AD: Orphica “Fragmenta” 159, etc.]]

__4
credit or character for piety, εὐσέβειαν οἴσῃ [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Electra” 968.]]

deep_entry:
Abbott-Smith / STEPBible (TBESG)

(εὐσεβής, which see), [in LXX: Dan LXX Sus 1:64, 4Ma.9:6 אR, 4Ma.11:5 4Mac 11:8 4Mac 11:23 4Mac 18:2 * ;]
to reverence, show piety towards; with accusative (else­where more frequently before εἰς., περί, πρός): οἶκον, 1Ti.5:4; θεόν, Act.17:23 (Cremer, 525).†
(AS)

---

LSJ / STEPBible (TFLSJ)
εὐσεβ-έω,
live or act piously or reverently, absolutely, [Refs 6th c.BC+ [6th c.BC: Theognis Elegiacus 145, “Berl.Sitzb.” 1927.8 (_Locrian dialect_, 5th c.BC), 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Ajax” 1350, etc.]]; εἴς τινα towards one, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. author] “Ant.” 731; περί τινα 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Alcestis” 1148; περὶ θεούς 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Symposium” 193a; πρὸς τὸν θεόν 4th-3rd c.BC: Menander Comicus “Μονόστιχοι - Fragmenta Comicorum Graecorum” 567; πρὸς θεούς “Anthologia Graeca” 10.107 (5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus); εὐ. τὰ πρὸς θεούς 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Philoctetes” 1441; τὰ περὶ τοὺς θεούς 5th-6th c.BC: Isocrates Orator 3.2]]; of outward acts of service, θύουσα καὶ εὐσεβοῦσα τοῖς θεοῖς [Refs 3rd c.AD+ [“PRyl.” 112 (a). 4 (3rd c.AD)]]; εὐ. θεούς to reverence them, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Agamemnon” 338 (nisi to be read εὖ σέβειν); εὐσεβήσασαν τὴν θεόν “BCH” 44.77 (from Lagina):]] —passive, εὐσεβεῖσθαι to be reverenced, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Antipho Orator 3.3.11, 1st c.AD: Philo Judaeus 2.201]]; of a duty, to be reverently discharged, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Axiochus” 364c.]]

deep_entry:

[Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd c.AD: Soranus Medicus 1.97 (hence ἐπίσταμαι, ἐπιστήμη, which see).]]

with accusative person, arrest the attention of, [Refs 1st c.AD+ [1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus “Tiberius Gracchus” 17, compare 2.17e, 2nd c.AD: Galenus Medicus 18(2).105]]; ἐπιστῆσαί τινα ἐπί τι call his attention to, [Refs 2nd c.BC+ [2nd c.BC: Polybius Historicus 2.61.11, compare 4.34.9]]; τοῦ καιροῦ τοῦ κατὰ τὴν διήγησιν ἐφεστακότος ἡμᾶς ἐπί τι having led us to.., [Refs [[prev. author] 10.21.2, compare 31.23.1]]: hence, object, [Refs 3rd c.AD+ [3rd c.AD: Plotinus Philosophus 1.4.5.]]

__B
intransitive in middle and passive, ἐφίσταμαι, aorist 1 ἐπεστάθην [[Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus] “fragment” [1127.5], 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Hippolytus” 819, “IT” 1375, etc.]], with perfect, pluperfect (Aeolic dialect pluperfect 3rd.pers. singular ἐπήστᾱκε [Refs 2nd c.BC+ [“Schwyzer” 646.16 (Cyme, 2nd c.BC): _Doric dialect_]]pluperfect 3rd.pers. plural ἐφεστάκεον [ᾱ] [Refs 4th c.BC+ [“SIG” 241.146 (Delph., 4th c.BC))]], and aorist 2 active: (the causal tenses are not found in [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Homerus Epicus]], the middle or passive only in imperfect ἐφίστατο [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 11.644]]; elsewhere always aorist 2 or perfect active with Epic dialect infinitive ἐφεστάμεναι [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 24.380)]]:—stand upon, τεῖχος.. ῥύατ᾽ ἐφεσταότες [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 18.515; πύργῳ ἐφεστήκει 6.373; δίφρῳ ἐφεσταότος 17.609, etc.; ἐπέστη βηλῷ ἔπι λιθέῳ 23.201; ἡ.. ἐπισταθεῖσα ὀρθή 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Metaphysica” 1051a28; ἐπὶ τὰς.. σχεδίας 2nd c.BC: Polybius Historicus 3.46.8.]]

__B.2
to be imposed upon, μόχθων τῶν ἐφεστώτων ἐμοί [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Trachiniae” 1170.]]

__B.3
stand on the top or surface, τὸ ἐπιστάμενον [τοῦ γάλακτος], i. e. cream, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 4.2; λιπαρότητες ἄνω ἐφιστάμεναι 5th c.BC: Hippocrates Medicus “προγνωστικόν” 12]]; ἐ. καθάπερ ὀρρὸς [γάλακτι] [Refs 1st c.AD+ [1st c.AD: Dioscorides (Dioscurides) Medicus 1.72]]; of vapour, form, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “de Juventute” 469b31.]]

__B.II
to be set over, ἐφίσταται πύλαις [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Septem contra Thebas” 538; οἷός τε πολλοῖς προβατίοις ἐφεστάναι 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Vespae” 955; οἷοι νῷν ἐφεστᾶσι σκοποί 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Ajax” 945; ἄρχοντες ἐφ᾽ ἑκάστῳ μέρει ἐ. 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Hiero” 9.5; ἐπί τινος 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 460b; ἐπὶ τῆς πολιτείας 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 19.298: rarely with _genitive_, τὸν ἐπεστεῶτα τῆς διώρυχος 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 7.117; ὅσοι θεοῦ χρημάτων ἐφέστασαν 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Andromache” 1098: _absolutely_ in]]participle, ὁ ἐφεστηκώς the person in authority, the officer in command, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Oeconomicus” 21.9]]; οἱ ἐφεστῶτες, Ionic dialect οἱ ἐπεστεῶτες, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 2.148, 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Ajax” 1072, 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Memorabilia” 3.5.19.]]

__B.III
stand by or near, ὣς πυκνοὶ ἐφέστασαν ἀλλήλοισιν [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 13.133; ἐπ᾽ ἄκρῳ χείλει ἐφεσταότες, ἐ. παρὰ τάφρῳ, 12.52, 199; θύρῃσιν ἐφίστατο 11.644]]; ἐπὶ τὰς πύλας, ἐπὶ τὰς θύρας, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 3.77, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Symposium” 212d; ἐπὶ τοῖς προθύροις [prev. author] “Phlb.” 64c]]; especially of dreams or visions, appear to, εὕδοντι ἐπέστη ὄνειρος [NT+8th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.34, compare 7.14; ὄναρ κεφαλῆφιν ἐπέστη 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 10.496; ἐπιστᾶσα τῆς νυκτός 5th-6th c.BC: Isocrates Orator 10.65; ἄγγελος ἐπέστη αὐτοῖς NT.Luke.2.9]]: absolutely, stand by, [NT+5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 3.78; πολλῶν ἐφεστώτων 2nd c.AD: Appianus Historicus “Συριακή” 10; ἤμην ἐφεστώς NT.Act.22.20; οἱ λέβητες ἐπεστεῶτες 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.59; ὁ ἀντίδικος ἐφέστηκε 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Theaetetus” 172e, compare 4th c.BC: Aeschines Orator 3.79]]; without hostile sense, ἐπέστης [NT+5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Coloneus” 558, cf. NT.Luke.2.38, etc.]]; of troops, to be posted after or behind, κατόπιν ἐ. τοῖς θηρίοις [Refs 2nd c.BC+ [2nd c.BC: Polybius Historicus 16.18.7.]]

__B.III.2
in hostile sense, stand against, τὰ φρονέοντες ἐφέστασαν ἀλλήλοισιν [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 15.703, compare 5.624; ἔνθα μένος πνείοντες ἐφέστασαν 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 22.203, compare 24.380]]; appear before, of an army, ἐπὶ τῇ πόλι [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 4.203; ἐπὶ τὸ βασίλειον 5th-6th c.BC: Isocrates Orator 9.58]]; come upon suddenly or by surprise, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 8.69; ἐξαίφνης ἐπιστὰς τοῖς γιγνομένοις 5th-6th c.BC: Isocrates Orator 8.41, compare 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 6.5, 2nd c.AD: Lucianus Sophista “DDeor.” 17.1; εἰς τοὺς ὄχλους 5th-6th c.BC: Isocrates Orator 18.9]]; so of events, etc., αἰφνίδιος αὐτοῖς ἐ. ὄλεθρος [NT+2nd c.BC+ [NT.1Thes.5.3, cf. NT.Luke.21.34; διὰ τὸν ἐφεστῶτα ζόφον 2nd c.BC: Polybius Historicus 18.20.7; διὰ τὸν ὑετὸν τὸν ἐφεστῶτα NT.Act.28.2.]]

__B.III.3
metaphorically, of events, spring upon one, occur, πρίν μοι τύχη τοιάδ᾽ ἐπέστη [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Tyrannus” 777, compare 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 3.82]]; in perfect, impend, be at hand, τὸν ἐφεστηκότα κίνδυνον τῇ πόλει [NT+4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 18.176; ὁ καιρός.. ἐφέστηκε NT.2Tim.4.6; περὶ τοῦ βασιλέως.. ὁ λόγος ἐφέστηκε νῦν 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Politica” 1287a2, compare “Metaphorical” 999a25]]; of a more remote future, to be in store, lie in wait for, κῆρες ἐφεστᾶσιν θανάτοιο [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 12.326.]]

__B.IV
halt, stop, as in a march, ἄλλοτε καὶ ἄλλοτε ἐφιστάμενος [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 2.4.26 (compare 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus V); ἐπιστὰς περιέμεινα 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Symposium” 172a: with _genitive_, ἐ. τοῦ πλοῦ 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 2.91.]]

__B.V
fix one's mind on, give one's attention to, σφαγῇ [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Andromache” 547; τῇ τρύγῃ “PFlor.” 236.4 (3rd c.AD)]]; ἐπί τι [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Isocrates Orator 10.29, 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 18.60; τοῖς πράγμασιν.. ἐπιστάντες [prev. author] 4.12]]; ἐπιστάς absolutely (i.e. τοῖς πράγμασι), [Refs [[prev. author] 18.233; διὰ ταῦτ᾽ ἐγρήγορεν, ἐφέστηκεν [prev. author] 6.19.]]

__C
aorist 1 middle in causal sense, set up, τὰς θύρας [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Agesilaus” 8.7]]; set, post, φρουροὺς ἐπεστησάμην [Refs [[prev. author] “Cyr.” 8.2.19]]; τέλος ἐπιστήσασθαι, Latin finem imponere, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Leges” 802a:]]present is once so used, τοῦ με τήνδ᾽ ἐφίστασαι βάσι; why dost thou cause me to halt? [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Trachiniae” 339.]]

__C.2
ἐπιστησάμενος, intransitive, having been ἐπιστάτης, [Refs [“IGRom.” 4.1265 (from Thyatira).]]

ἔχθρ-α,
Ionic dialect ἔχθρη, ἡ, hatred, enmity, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 5.81, 5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “P.” 4.145, etc.]]: in philosophical sense, ={νεῖκος}[Refs 3rd c.AD+ [1.5, 3rd c.AD: Plotinus Philosophus 3.2.2]]; ἔ. τινός hatred for, enmity to one, [NT+5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Antipho Orator 2.4.1, 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 3.10; κατ᾽ ἔχθραν τινός 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Pax” 133; ἔ. ἔς τινα 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.5, 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 2.68; εἴς θεόν NT.Rom.8.7; πρός τινα 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Prometheus Vinctus” 491 (_plural_), 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 2.68]]; δι᾽ ἔχθρας μολεῖν, ἀφῖχθαί τινι, to be at feud with one, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Phoenissae” 479, “Hipp.” 1164; δι᾽ ἔχθρας οὐδετέρῳ γενήσομαι 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Ranae” 1412; εἰς ἔ. βάλλειν τινά 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Prometheus Vinctus” 390; εἰς ἔ. ἐλθεῖν 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 21.62; καταστῆσαί τινας εἰς ἔχθραν τῷ δήμῳ 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Historia Graeca (Hellenica)” 3.5.9; πολλὴν εἰς ἔχθραν ἀλλήλοις καὶ πολλῶν πέρι καθίστανται 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Politicus” 307d, compare 5th-6th c.BC: Isocrates Orator 9.67]]; πρὸς ἔχθραν from personal enmity, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 18.141]]; ἔ. συμβάλλειν, συνάπτειν τινί, to engage in hostility with.., [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Medea” 45, “Heracl.” 459; ἔ. τισὶν ἄρασθαι 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 21.132; καταλλάσσεσθαι τὰς ἔ. 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 7.145; λύσασαν ἔ. τὴν πάρος 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Troades” 50; τὰς μεγάλας ἔ. διαλύεσθαι 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 4.19; πρὸς ἀλλήλους ἔ. ἀνείλοντο 4th c.BC: Isaeus Orator 1.9; διαλλαχθῆναι τῆς ἔ. 5th-6th c.BC: Andocides Orator 2.26: proverbial, Ἐμπεδοκλέους ἔ.]], of undying hatred, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Lysias Orator “Fragmenta” 261 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus]]

Actively, hating, hostile: Rom.5:10, 1Co.15:25, 2Th.3:15; with genitive of person(s) (cl.), Jas.4:4; τ. διανοίᾳ, Col.1:21; ἐ. ἄνθρωπος, Mat.13:28; as subst., ὁ ἐ., an enemy, 1Co.15:26; the devil, Mat.13:39, Luk.10:19; with genitive of person(s), Mat.22:44 Mrk.12:36, Luk.20:43, Act.2:35, 1Co.15:25, Heb.1:13 10:13" (LXX) ; Mat.5:43-44 10:36 13:25, Luk.1:71, 74 6:27, 35 19:27, 43, Rom.12:20, Gal.4:16, Rev.11:5, 12; with genitive of thing(s), Act.13:10, Php.3:18.†

LSJ / STEPBible (TFLSJ)
ἐχθρός, ά, όν,
(ἔχθος) hated, hateful, of persons and things, frequently from [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Homerus Epicus downwards (8th c.BC: Homerus Epicus has it only in this _passive_ sense)]]; ἐ. γάρ μοι κεῖνος ὁμῶς Ἀΐδαο πύλῃσι [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 14.156, 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 9.312]]; ἐχθρὸν δέ μοί ἐστιν c.infinitive, 'tis hateful to me to.., [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 12.452; θεοῖσιν ἐ. 8th-7th c.BC: Hesiodus Epicus “Theogonia” 766, 6th c.BC: Theognis Elegiacus 601, 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Equites” 34; ὁ θεοῖσιν ἐ. 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Comicus 74, etc.]]; compare θεοισεχθρός.

__II
active, hating, hostile, first in [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th-7th c.BC: Hesiodus Epicus and 5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus (see. below 111), τινι 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 10.11, 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Agesilaus” 6.1, etc.: with _genitive_, ὕβριος ἐχθρὰν ὁδόν]] averse from insolence, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “O.” 7.90: _absolutely_, ἐ. γλῶσσα 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Choephori” 309 (_anapaest meter_); ὀργαί [prev. author] “Eu.” 937 (_anapaest meter_), etc.; ἀστέρες 2nd c.AD: Vettius Valens Astrologus 143.5.]]

__III
as substantive, ἐχθρός, ὁ, enemy, where the active and passive senses frequently coincide, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th-7th c.BC: Hesiodus Epicus “Opera et Dies” 342, 5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “P.” 2.84, etc.; ἀνὴρ ἐ. 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.92; ὁ Διὸς ἐ. 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Prometheus Vinctus” 120 (_anapaest meter_); ἐχθροῖς ἐχθρὰ πορσύνων [prev. author] “Ag.” 1374; εἴ.. τινα ἴδοι ἐχθρὸν ἑαυτοῦ 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 4.47; οἱ ἐμοὶ ἐ. [prev. author] 6.89, etc.—Acc. to 1st-2nd c.AD: Ammonius Grammaticus “περὶ ὁμοίων καὶ διαφόρων λέξεων” p.63 V., ἐχθρός]] is one who has been φίλος, but is alienated; πολέμιος one who is at war; δυσμενής one who has long been alienated and refuses to be reconciled.

__IV
regular comparative ἐχθρότερος [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator “Prooemia” 40.3, “Anthologia Graeca” 5.160 (3rd c.BC: Hedylus Epigrammaticus or 3rd c.BC: Asclepiades Epigrammaticus)]]; superlative -ότατος [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “N.” 1.65, 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Tyrannus” 1346 (Lyric poetry), 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 19.300: but more frequently irregular ἐχθίων, ἔχθιστος (which see).]]

__V
adverb ἐχθρῶς, μισοῦντες [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Leges” 697d, etc.]]: comparative -οτέρως [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 5.18]]: superlative -ότατα [Refs [[prev. author] 23.149.]]

Abbott-Smith / STEPBible (TBESG)
ἔχω,
[in LXX for אָצֵל (ἐχόμενος), יֵשׁ,בַּעַל, etc., 59 words in all ;]
(on the Aktionsart of the various tenses, see M, Pr., 110, 145, 150, 183), to have, as in cl., in various senses and constructions.
__I. Trans.;
__1. 1. to have, hold, hold fast, etc.;
__(a) to hold, as, in the hand: Rev.5:8  14:6, al.; ἐν τ. χειρί, Rev.1:16  10:2, al.;
__(b) of arms and clothing, = φέρω, φορέω, to bear, wear: Mat.3:4  22:12, al.; so frequently present ptcp. (LS, see word, A, I, 6; Bl., 74, 2), Mrk.11:13, Jhn.18:10, Rev.9:17, al.;
__(with) of a woman, ἐν γαστρὶ ἔ, to be with child: Mrk.13:17, Rom.9:10;
__(d) to hold fast, keep: Luk.19:20; metaphorically, of the mind and conduct, Mrk.16:8 (cf. Job.21:6, Isa.13:8; Deiss., BS, 293; Field, Notes, 44f.), Jhn.14:21, Rom.1:28, 1Ti.3:9, 2Ti.1:13, Rev.6:9, al.;
__(e) to involve: Heb.10:35 (LXX), Jas.1:4, 1Jn.4:18; (f) = Lat. habere (Bl., §34, 5; 73, 5), to hold, consider: with accusative and predic. ptcp., Luk.14:18; with accusative, before ὡς, Mat.14:5; εἰς (Hebraism), Mat.21:46; on (Bl., §70, 2), Mrk.11:32.
__2. to have, possess;
__(a) in general, with accusative of thing(s): Mat.19:22, Mrk.10:22, Luk.12:19, Jhn.10:16, 1Co.11:22, al.; of wealth or poverty, absol., ἔχειν (neg. οὐκ, μή), Mat.13:12  25:29, 2Co.8:12; ἐκ τ. ἔχειν, according to your means, 2Co.8:11;

(BL, §53, 1), to be in a certain condition: ἑτοίμως ἔ., with inf., Act.21:13, 2Co.12:14; ἐσχάτως (which see), Mrk.5:23; κακῶς, to be ill, Mat.4:24, al.; καλῶς, Mk 16:[18]; κομψότερον, Jhn.4:52; πῶς, Act.15:36; impers., ἄλλως εἴχει, it is otherwise, 1Ti.5:25; οὕτως, Act.7:1, al.; τὸ νῦν ἔχον, as things now are (Tob.7:11), Act.24:25.

Mid., -ομαι, to hold oneself fast, hold on or cling to, be next to: with genitive, τ. ἐχόμενα σωτηρίας, Heb.6:9 (Rendall, in l.); ptcp., ὁ ἐχόμενος, near, next: of place, Mrk.1:38; of time, τ. ἐχομένη (ἡμέρα, expressed or understood), Luk.13:33, Act.20:15 21:26; (σαββάτῳ), Act.13:44. with Preps., to be engaged or busy, ἀμφί τι [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Septem contra Thebas” 102 (Lyric poetry), 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 5.2.26, etc.; περί τινας [prev. author] “HG” 7.4.28.]]

__B.II
simply, be, ἑκὰς εἶχον [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 12.435; ἔ. κατ᾽ οἴκους 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 6.39; περὶ πολλῶν ἔ. πρηγμάτων [prev. author] 3.128]]; ἀγῶνα διὰ πάσης ἀγωνίης ἔχοντα consisting in.., [Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. author] 2.91; ἔ. ἐν ἀνάγκαισι 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Bacchae” 88 (Lyric poetry); ὅπου συμφορᾶς ἔχεις [prev. author] “El.” 238; ἐκποδὼν ἔχειν [prev. author] “IT” 1226, etc.]]

__B.II.2
frequently with adverbs of manner, εὖ ἔχει [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 24.245, etc.]]; καλῶς ἔχει, κακῶς ἔχει, it is, is going on well or ill, see at {καλός, κακός} (but future σχήσειν καλῶς will turn out well, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 1.9, compare 18.45; εὖ σχήσει 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Ajax” 684)]]; οὕτως.. σχεῖν to turn out, happen thus, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Apologia” 39b]]; οὕτως ἔχει so the case stands, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Plutus” 110]]; οὕτως ἐχόντων, Latin cum res ita se habeant, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 3.2.10; ὡς ὧδ᾽ ἐχόντων 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Ajax” 981; οὕτω χρὴ διὰ στέρνων ἔχειν [prev. author] “Ant.” 639; οὕτως ἔ. περί τινος 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Memorabilia” 4.8.7, compare 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 6.16; πρός τι 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 9.45; τῇδ᾽ ἔ. 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Philoctetes” 1336; κοσμίως ἔ. 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Thesmophoriazusae” 854; ἥδιον ἔ. πρός τινας 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 9.63]]; ὡς εἶχε just as he was, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.114; ὥσπερ εἶχε 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 1.134, 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Historia Graeca (Hellenica)” 4.1.30]]; ὡς ἔχω how I am, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Lysistrata” 610; ὥσπερ ἔχομεν 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 3.30; τἀναντία εἶχεν 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 9.41]]; ἀσφαλέως, ἀναγκαίως ἔχει, ={ἀσφαλές, ἀναγκαῖόν ἐστι}, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.86, 9.27]]; καλῶς ἔχει no, I thank you, see at {καλός}.

__B.II.2.b
with genitive modi, εὖ ἔ. τινός to be well off for a thing, abound in it; καλῶς ἔ. μέθης to be well off for drink, i.e. to be pretty well drunk, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 5.20]]; σπόρου ἀνακῶς ἐ. to be busy with sowing, [Refs [[prev. author] 8.109]]; εὖ ἐ. φρενῶν, σώματος, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Hippolytus” 462, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 404d; εὖ ὥρας ἔχον χωρίον 2nd c.AD(?): Pollianus Epigrammaticus 5.108]]; compare ἥκ; so ὡς ποδῶν εἶχον as fast as they could go, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 6.116, 9.59; ὡς τάχεος εἶχε ἕκαστος [prev. author] 8.107; ὡς.. τις εὐνοίας ἢ μνήμης ἔχοι 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 1.22; ὡς ὀργῆς ἔχω 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Tyrannus” 345, compare 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Helena” 313, 857, etc.]]; πῶς ἔχεις δόξη; [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 456d; οὕτω τρόπου ἔχεις 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 7.5.56; μετρίως ἔ. βίου 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.32; ὑγιεινῶς ἔ. αὐτὸς αὑτοῦ καὶ σωφρόνως 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 571d; οὐκ εὖ σεαυτοῦ τυγχάνεις ἔχων 4th-3rd c.BC: Philemo Comicus 4.11: also with _accusative_, εὖ ἔ. τὸ σῶμα καὶ τὴν ψυχήν 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Gorgias” 464a, compare 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Oeconomicus” 21.7: with _dative_, οὕτως ἐχόντων τούτων τῇ φύσει 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 18.315; πῶς ἔχετε ταῖς διανοίαις 4th c.BC: Lycurgus Orator 75; τῇ λέξει κακῶς ἔ. 5th-6th c.BC: Isocrates Orator 9.10.]]

__B.III
of direction, hold or turn towards, see above [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus 11.8.]]

__B.III.2
stand up, jut out, κίονες ὑψόσ᾽ ἔχοντες [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 19.38; δι᾽ ὤμου ἔγχος ἔσχεν 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 13.520.]]

__B.III.3
lead towards, ὁδοὶ ἐπὶ τὸν ποταμὸν ἔ. [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.180, compare 191, 2.17]]; ἔ. εἴς τι to be directed, point towards, ἔχθρης ἐχούσης ἐς Ἀθηναίους [Refs [[prev. author] 5.81]]; τὸ ἐς τοὺς Ἀργείους ἔχον what concerns them, [Refs [[prev. author] 6.19; ταῦτα ἐς τὴν ἀπόστασιν ἔχοντα [prev. work] 2]], etc.; of Place, extend, reach to, ἐπ᾽ ὅσον ἔποψις τοῦ ἱροῦ εἶχε [Refs [[prev. author] 1.64.]]

__B.III.4
ἐπί τινι ἔ. have hostile feelings to wards.., [Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. author] 6.49, 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Antigone” 987 (Lyric poetry).]]

__B.IV
after [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Homerus Epicus, ἔχω]] as auxiliary, with aorist participle giving a perfect sense, κρύψαντες ἔχουσι [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th-7th c.BC: Hesiodus Epicus “Opera et Dies” 42; ἀποκληΐσας ἔχεις 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.37; ἐγκλῄσασ᾽ ἔχει 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Ecclesiazusae” 355, compare “Th.” 706; frequently in 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus, θαυμάσας ἔχω “OC” 1140, compare “Ant.” 22, +others]]: also in late Prose, ἀναλώσας ἔχεις [Refs 5th c.BC+ [2nd c.AD: Aristides Rhetor “Orationes” 18(20).1; ὅς σφε νῦν ἀτιμάσας ἔχει 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Medea” 33]]: less frequently with perfect participle, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Tyrannus” 701, “Ph.” 600, 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 1.3.14, 4.7.1]]: rarely with present participle, πατρίδα καταστένουσ᾽ ἔχεις [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Troades” 318 (Lyric poetry), compare 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Cynegeticus” 10.11.]]

__B.IV.2
participle ἔχων, with present, adds a notion of duration to that of present action, τί κυπτάζεις ἔ.; why do you keep poking about there? [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Nubes” 509]]; τί δῆτα διατρίβεις ἔ.; why then keep wasting time? [Refs [[prev. author] “Ec.” 1151]]; τί γὰρ ἕστηκ᾽ ἔ.[Refs [; [prev. work] 853, compare “Th.” 473, 852: without _interrogative_, φλυαρεῖς ἔ., ἔ. φλυαρεῖς]], you keep chattering, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Gorgias” 490e, “Euthd.” 295c; κακοῦν ἔχοντ᾽ αὐτὸν ἀποκτιννύναι 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 23.35 (and so possibly ἐνεργεῖ ἔ. 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Metaphysica” 1072b23); παίσδεις ἔ. 3rd c.BC: Theocritus Poeta Bucolicus 14.8]]: so in later Prose, παίζεις ἔ. [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd c.AD: Lucianus Sophista “Icar.” 24]]; but ῥιπτεῖς ἔ.; do you throw away the prize when it is in your grasp? [Refs 1st c.AD+ [2nd c.AD: Aristides Rhetor 1.443 1st c.AD: Josephus Historicus]]

__C
middle, hold oneself fast, cling closely, τῷ προσφὺς ἐχόμην [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 12.433, compare 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 1.513, etc.; πρὸς ἀλλήλῃσιν 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 5.329]]: mostly with genitive, hold on by, cling to, [πέτρης[Refs 5th c.BC+ [] [prev. work] 429; χερσὶν ἀώτου 9.435; βρετέων 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Septem contra Thebas” 98 (Lyric poetry); ἑξόμεσθάσου 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Plutus” 101]]; τῆς πληγῆς ἔχ εται claps his hand on the place struck, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 4.40.]]

__C.2
metaphorically, cleave, cling to, ἔργου [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 8.11, 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Historia Graeca (Hellenica)” 7.2.19; γεωργίας “BGU” 7.6 (3rd c.AD)]]; τῶν πραγμάτων [Refs 4th c.AD+ [4th c.AD: Julianus Imperator “Orationes” 1.19a]]; βιοτᾶς, ἐλπίδος, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Ion” 491, “fragment” 409; τῆς αὐτῆς γνώμης 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 1.140]]; lay hold on, take advantage of, τῶν ἀγαθῶν ἔχεο [Refs 6th c.BC+ [6th c.BC: Theognis Elegiacus 32; προφάσιος ἔχεσθαι 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 6.94]]; fasten upon, attack, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 18.79]]; lay claim to, ἀμφοτέρων τῶν ἐπωνυμιέων [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 2.17]]; to be zealous for, [μάχης] [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Coloneus” 424; ἀληθείας 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Leges” 709c; κοινῇ τῆς σωτηρίας 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 6.3.17, etc.]]

__C.3
come next to, follow closely,[Refs [[prev. work] 1.8.4; ἕπεσθαι ἐχομένους ὅτι μάλιστα τῶν ἁρμάτων [prev. author] “Cyr.” 7.1.9]]; of peoples or places, to be close, border on, with genitive, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 4.169, 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 2.96, etc.; frequently in]]participle, τὴν ἐχομένην [τῶν νεωρίων] στοάν Aen. Tact.[Refs [11.3]]; οἱ ἐ. the neighbouring people, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.134]]; ὁ ἐχόμενος the next man, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aeneas Tacticus 22.27]]; of Time, τὸ ἐχόμενον ἔτος the next year, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 6.3; ὁ ἐ. διαλογισμός “PRev.Laws” 16.15 (3rd c.BC)]]; τὰ ἐχόμενα τούτοις what follows, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Gorgias” 494e (without τούτοις 5th-6th c.BC: Isocrates Orator 6.29).]]

__C.4
depend, ἔκ τινος [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 6.197, 11.346: with _genitive_, σέο δ᾽ ἕξεται 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 9.102.]]

__C.4.b
to be connected with by etymology, τὸ θύειν τοῦ θυμιᾶν εἴχετο [Refs 3rd c.AD+ [3rd c.AD: Porphyrius Tyrius Philosophus “de Abstinentia - Porphyrii Opuscula” 2.59.]]

__C.5
pertain to, ὅσα ἔχεται τῶν αἰσθήσεων [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Leges” 661b; ἃ διδασκάλων εἴχετο [prev. author] “Prt.” 319e; ὅσα τέχνης ἔχεται [prev. author] “Men.” 94b, etc.: especially in 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus in periphrases, τὰ τῶν ὀνειράτων, καρπῶν ἐχόμενα, 1.120, 193]]; ὀρνίθων ἢ ἰχθύων [Refs [2.77; σιτίων, ἐσθῆτος, 3.25, 66.]]

__C.II
bear or hold for oneself, κρήδεμνα ἄντα παρειάων σχομένη before her cheeks, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 1.334]]; ἀσπίδα πρόσθ᾽ ἔσχετο his shield, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 12.294, compare 298, 20.262.]]

__C.III
maintain oneself, hold one's ground,[Refs [12.126; ἔχεο κρατερῶς 16.501.]]

__C.III.2
with accusative, keep off from oneself, repel, [Refs [17.639 (unless σχήσεσθαι is _passive_, compare 9.235).]]

__C.IV
keep oneself back, abstain or refrain from, ἀϋτῆς, μάχης, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [2.98, 3.84; βίης 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 4.422; ἐχώμεθα δηϊοτῆτος ἐκ βελέων 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 14.129; τῆς ἀγωγῆς 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 6.85; τῆς τιμωρίης [prev. author] 7.169; τῶν ἀθίκτων 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Tyrannus” 891 (Lyric poetry, assuming variant)]]: c.infinitive, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [3rd c.BC: Apollonius Rhodius Epicus 1.328; οὐκ ἂν ἐσχόμην τὸ μὴ ἀποκλῇσαι 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Tyrannus” 1387]]; κακῶν ἄπο χεῖρας ἔχεσθαι to keep one's hands from ill, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 22.316; Μενέλεω σχέσθαι χέρα 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Rhesus” 174: _absolutely_, σχέο, σχέσθε]], hold! cease! [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 21.379, 22.416.]]

__C.V
passive of ἔχω [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Bacchylides Lyricus 1, ἐπὶ ξυροῦ ἀκμῆς ἔχεται ἡμῖν τὰ πρήγματα]] are balanced on.., [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 6.11.]]

deep_entry:
Abbott-Smith / STEPBible (TBESG)
ἕως,
relative particle (Lat. donee, usque),
expressing the terminus ad quem (cf. Burton, §321ff.).
__I. As conjunction;
__1. till, until;
__(a) of a fact in past time, with indic.: Mat.2:9, al. (Wis.10:14, al.);
__(b) ἕως ἄν, with subjc. aor.: Mat.2:13  5:18, Mrk.6:10, al.; without ἄν (M. Pr., 168f.; Lft., Notes, 115), Mrk.14:32 (Burton, §325), Luk.12:59, 2Th.2:7, al.;
__(with) with indic., present (Burton, §328; BL, §65, 10): Mrk.6:45, Jhn.21:22,  23 1Ti.4:13.
__2. C. indic., as long as, while (Burton, §327): Jhn.9:4 (Plat., Phaedo, 89c).
__II. As an adverb (chiefly in late writers).
__1. Of time, until, unto;
__(a) as prep. with genitive (BL, §40, 6; M, Pr., 99): τ. ἡμέρας, Mat.26:29, Luk.1:80, Rom.11:8, al.; ὥρας, Mat.27:45, al.; τέλους, 1Co.1:8, 2Co.1:13; τ. νῦν, Mat.24:21, Mrk.13:19 (1Ma.2:33); ἐτῶν ὀγ. (Field, Notes, 49f.), Luk.2:37; τ. ἐλθεῖν, Act.8:40; before names and events, Mat.1:17  2:15, Luk.11:51, Jas.5:7, al.;
__(b) before οὗ, ὅτου, with the force of a conjc. (Burton, §330; M, Pr., 91);
__(α) ἕ. οὗ (Hdt., ii, 143; Plut., al.): with indic., Mat.1:25 (WH br., οὗ) 13:33, al.; with subjc. aor., Mat.14:22, al.;
__(β) ἔ. ὅτου: with subjc., Luk.13:8; with indic., Mat.5:25 (until), Jhn.9:18;
__(with) with adv. (ἔ. ὀψέ, Thuc, iii, 108): ἄρτι, Mat.11:12, Jhn.2:10, 1Co.4:13, al.; πότε (M, Pr., 107), Mat.17:17, Mrk.9:19, Jhn.10:24, al.
__2. Of place, as far as, even to, unto (Arist., al.);
__(a) as prep. with genitive (see supr.): Mt 1123, Lk 1015, al.;
__(b) with adv. (BL, §40, 6): ἄνω, Jhn.2:7; ἔσω, Mrk.14:54; κάτω, Mat.27:51, Mrk.15:38; ὧδε, Luk.23:5;
__(with) with prep.: ἔξω, Act.21:5; πρός, Luk.24:50 (Field, Notes, 83).
__3. Of quantity, measure, etc.: Mat.18:21, Mrk.6:23, Luk.22:51, al.
(AS)

LSJ / STEPBible (TFLSJ)
ἕως,

__B
Epic dialect εἵως, ἧος (see. entry near the end), Doric dialect ἇς, Aeolic dialect ἆς (which see), Boeotian dialect ἇς [Refs [“IG” 7.3303, +others]], and ἅως [Refs [[prev. work]2228, 3315.]] Relat. Particle, expressing the point of Time up to which an action goes, with reference to the end of the action, until, till; or to its continuance, while:

__B.I
until, till,

__B.I.1
with Ind., of a fact in past time, θῦνε διὰ προμάχων, ἧος φίλον ὤλεσε θυμόν [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 11.342, compare 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 5.123; ἕ. ἀπώλεσέν τε καὐτὸς ἐξαπώλετο 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Fragmenta” 236, compare 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Persae” 428, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Charmides” 155c, etc.; for πρίν, μὴ πρότερον ἀπελθεῖν ἕως ἀποκατέστησε τὰ πράγματα 1st c.BC: Diodorus Siculus Historicus 27.4: with]]imperfect with ἄν in apodosi, of an unaccomplished action, ἡδέως ἂν Καλλικλεῖ διελεγόμην, ἕ. ἀπέδωκα I would have gone on conversing till I had.., [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Gorgias” 506b, compare “Cra.” 396c.]]

__B.I.2
ἕ. ἄν or κε with Subj. (mostly of aorist), of an event at an uncertain future time, μαχήσομαι.. ἧός κε τέλος πολέμοιο κιχείω till I find, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 3.291, compare 24.183, 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Prometheus Vinctus” 810, etc.: ἄν]] is sometimes omitted in Trag., ἕ. μάθῃς [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Ajax” 555; ἕ. κληθῇ [prev. author] “Tr.” 148; ἕ. ἀνῇ τὸ πῆμα [prev. author] “Ph.” 764]]: so frequently in later Gr., [NT+2nd c.BC+ [“UPZ” 18.10 (2nd c.BC), “PGrenf.” 2.38.16 (1st c.BC), NT.Mark.14.32, Vett. Val. 68.18, etc.; ἕ. οὗ γένηται 1st c.BC: Geminus Astronomicus 8.32.]]

__B.I.3
ἕ. with Opt. (mostly of aorist), relating to an event future in relation to past time, ὦρσε.. Βορέην, ἧος ὃ Φαιήκεσσι.. μιγείη caused it to blow, till he should reach.., [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 5.386, compare 9.376, 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Ranae” 766, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Phaedo” 59d; ἕως δέοι βοηθεῖν 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 3.102, compare 5th c.BC: Lysias Orator 13.25: ἄν]] or κε is added to the Opt. (not to ἕως), if the event is represented as conditional, ἕ. κ᾽ ἀπὸ πάντα δοθείη till (if possible) all things should be given back, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 2.78; οὐκ [ἂν] ἀποκρίναιο, ἕ. ἂν σκέψαιο 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Phaedo” 101d, compare 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Trachiniae” 687 codices, 5th-6th c.BC: Isocrates Orator 17.15, “IG” 22.1328 (2nd c.BC).]]

__B.I.3.b
in indirect speech, ἔδωκεν.. ἕ. ἀνὴρ εἶναι δοκιμασθείην [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 27.5.]]

__B.I.3.c
by assimilation to an optative with ἄν, [λόγον] ἂν διδοίης ἕ. ἔλθοις [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Phaedo” 101d.]]

__B.I.4
with subjunctive or optative, expressing purpose, in order that, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 4.800, 6.80, 19.367; πορεύου εἰς Διονυσιάδα.. ἕως τὸν ἐκεῖ ἐλαιῶνα ποτίσῃς “PFay.” 118.12 (2nd c.AD)]]; σπούδασον ἕως οὗ ἀγοράσῃ κτλ. ζάω, -ῶ,
[in LXX chiefly for חיה (most frequently ptcp., ζῶν, inf., ζῆν, for חַי ;]
__1. prop., to live, be alive (see Syn., see word βίος; in cl. usually of animal life, but sometimes of plants, as Arist., Eth. N, i, 7, 12): Act.20:12, Rom.7:1-3, 1Co.7:39, Rev.19:20, al.; ἐν αὐτῷ ζῶμεν, Act.17:28; ἐμοὶ τὸ ζῆν Χριστός, Php.1:21; διὰ παντὸς τοῦ ζῆν (M, Pr., 215, 249), Heb.2:15; ὃ δὲ νῦν ζῶ ἐν σαρκί, Gal.2:20; ζῇ ἐν ἐμοὶ Χριστός, Gal.2:20; (ὁ) ζῶν, of God (אֵל חַי and cognate phrases, Jos.3:10, Hos.2:1 (1:10), Isa.37:4, al.; see DCG, ii, 39a), Mat.16:16, Jhn.6:57, Rom.9:26, 1Th.1:9, Heb.3:12, Rev.7:2, al.; in juristic phrase, ζῶ ἐγώ (חַי־אָנִי, Num.14:21, al.), as I live, Rom.14:11; ζῆν ἐπ᾽ ἄρτῳ, Mat.4:4, al.; ἐκ, 1Co.9:14; of coming to life, Mrk.16:[11], Rom.6:10 14:9, 2Co.13:4; opposite to νεκρός, Rev.1:18 2:8; metaphorically, Luk.15:32; ζῆν ἐκ νεκρῶν, Rom.6:13; of the spiritual life of Christians, Luk.10:28, Jhn.5:25, Rom.1:17 8:13; εἰς τ. αἰῶνα, Jhn.6:51, 58; σὺν Χριστῷ, 1Th.5:10; ὄνομα ἔχεις ὅτι ζῇς, Rev.3:1.
__2. As sometimes in cl., = βιόω, to live, pass one's life: Luk.2:36, Act.26:5, Rom.7:9, Col.2:20; ἐν πίστει, Gal.2:20; ἐν τ. ἁμαρτίᾳ, Rom.6:2; εὐσεβῶς, 2Ti.3:12; ἀσώτως, Luk.15:13; with dative (cl.), ἑαυτῳ (Field, Notes, 164), Rom.14:7, 2Co.5:15; τ. δικαιοσύνῃ, Luk.20:38, Rom.6:10, 11 Gal.2:19; τ. Χριστῷ, 2Co.5:15; τ. θεῷ, 1Pe.2:24; πνεύματι, Gal.5:25; κατὰ σάρκα, Rom.8:12, 13;
__3. Of inanimate things, metaphorically: ὕδωρ ζῶν (i.e. springing water, as opposite to still water), in a spiritual sense, Jhn.4:10, 11 7:38 (DCG, ii, 39f.): ἐλπὶς ζῶσα, 1Pe.1:3; ὁδὸς ζῶσα, Heb.10:20 (cf. ἀνα-, συν-ζάω; Cremer, 270, 721).
(AS)

deep_entry:
Abbott-Smith / STEPBible (TBESG)
ζῷον (Rec. ζῶον, see LS, see word), -ου, τό
(ζωός, alive), [in LXX for חַי (chiefly) and cognate forms; frequently in Wis ;]
a living creature, an animal: Rev.4:6-9 5:6 ff. Rev.6:1 ff. Rev.7:11 14:3 15:7 19:4; ζῴων τ. αἷμα, Heb.13:11; ἄλογα ζ., 2Pe.2:12, Ju 10.†
SYN.: θηρίον, in which the brutal, bestial element is emphasized, and which is never used of sacrificial animals. On the other hand, ζ. is the more comprehensive, as expressing the vital element common to the whole anima] creation (see Tr., Syn., LXXxi; Cremer, 274).  (AS)

---

LSJ / STEPBible (TFLSJ)
ζῷον, τό,
living being, animal, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 5.10 (of bees), 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Vespae” 551, “Pl.” 443, etc.; πᾶν ὅ τι περ ἂν μετάσχῃ τοῦ ζῆν ζῷον ἂν λέγοιτο 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Timaeus” 77b]]; ζῷα, opposed to φυτά, [Refs [[prev. author] “Phd.” 70d, 110e, etc.]]; ζ. θαλάττιον, χερσαῖον, [Refs 1st c.BC+ [1st c.BC: Philodemus Gadarensis Epigrammaticus “Rh.” 1.98 S]].; contemptuously, ὅπως ἡ χώρα τοῦ τοιούτου ζῴου καθαρὰ γίγνηται may be free from this kind of animal (i.e. beggars), [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Leges” 936c]]; ζ. πονηρόν, of women, [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd c.AD: Secundus Gnomologus “Sententiae - FPG” 8.]]

__II
in art, figure, image, not necessarily of animals (compare ζῴδιον), ζῷον δέ οἱ ἐνῆν, ἀνὴρ ἱππεύς [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 3.88]]: mostly in plural, ζῷα ἐς τὴν ἐσθῆτα ἐγγράφειν [Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. author] 1.203, compare 2.4, 124, 148, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 515a, etc.]]; ζῷα γράψασθαι τὴν ζεῦξιν τοῦ Βοσπόρου to have pictures of the bridging of the Bosporus painted, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 4.88]]; compare ζωγραφέω: ζῷα ποιεῖν [Refs 1st c.AD+ [1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus “Pericles” 13.]]

__III
sign of the Zodiac, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [4th c.AD(?): Manetho Astrologus 2.166.—The word is post- 8th c.BC: Homerus Epicus]], no generic word used for animal being found till after the middle of the fifth cent. BC [Refs 7th c.BC+ [5th c.BC(ζώϊον 7th-6th c.BC(?): Semonides Iambographus 13, whence _Attic dialect_ ζῷον]] by contraction: ι is found in [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [“IG” 12.372.42, +others,11(2).161 B 76 (Delos, 3rd c.BC), 1st c.BC: Philodemus Gadarensis Epigrammaticus “Rh.” 2.166 S]]., and in codices optative in the Noun; the adjective ζωός (which see) had no ι: for the compounds (except ζωγλύφος, ζωγράφος) decisive evidence is lacking: ζῳάγρια with ι was read by [Refs 8th c.BC+ [3rd-2nd c.BC: Aristarchus Grammaticus in 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 18.407.)]]

deep_entry:
Abbott-Smith / STEPBible (TBESG)
ἤ,
disjunctive and comparative particle (Bl., §36, 12; 77, 11);
__1. disjunctive, or;
__(a) between single words: Mat.5:17 Mrk.6:56, Luk.2:24, Jhn.6:19, Rom.1:21, al.;
__(b) before a sentence expressing a variation, denial or refutation of a previous statement, frequently in interrog. form: Mat.7:4, 9 Mrk.12:14, Luk.13:4, Rom.3:29 6:3 9:21, 1Co.6:9, 16 9:6, 2Co.11:7; ἤ . . . ἤ, either . . . or, Mat.6:24, Luk.16:13, 1Co.14:6;
__(with) in a disjunctive question (as Lat. an after utrum): Mat.9:5, Mrk.2:9, Luk.7:19, al.; after πότερον, Jhn.7:17; μή, 1Co.9:8; μήτι, 2Co.1:17; ἤ . . . ἤ . . . ἤ, Mrk.13:35.
__2. Comparative, than: after comparatives, Mat.10:15, Luk.9:13, Jhn.3:19, Rom.13:11, al.; after ἕτερον, Act.17:21; θέλω (Khüner 3, iv, 303), 1Co.14:19; πρὶν ἤ,  before, before accusative and inf., Mat.1:18 Mrk.14:30; after a positive adj. (Gen.49:12; cf. Robertson, Gr., 661), Mat.18:8, 9 Mrk.9:43, 45 47.
__3. with other particles: ἀλλ᾽ ἤ, see: ἀλλά; ἤ γάρ, see: γάρ; ἢ καί, or even, or also, Mat.7:10, Luk.11:11, 12 Rom.2:15 4:9, al; ἤτοι . . . ἤ, Rom.6:16 (cf. Wis.11:19).
(AS)

---

LSJ / STEPBible (TFLSJ)
ἤ,
Epic dialect also ἠέ (in signification [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus 11 ἤ (or ἠέ) followed by ἦ (or ἦε), see below)]], conjunction with two chief senses, Disj. (or) and comparative (than).

__A
DISJUNCTIVE, or, ἐγὼ.. ἢ ἄλλος Ἀχαιῶν [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 2.231, compare 397, 800, 4.142, 7.236, +others]]; θεόσυτος ἢ βρότειος ἢ κεκραμένη [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Prometheus Vinctus” 116.]]

__A.2
ἢ.. ἤ either.. or, ἢ νῦν δηθύνοντ᾽ ἢ ὕστερον αὖτις ἰόντα [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 1.27, compare 151, 5.484]], etc.; so ἢ.. ἤτοι.. [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “N.” 6.4, “fragment” 138; ἤτοι.. ἤ.. 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Agamemnon” 662, 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Antigone” 1182, 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 2.40, etc. (in Classical Gr. the alternative introduced by ἤτοι]] is emphasized, later no distinction is implied, [NT+2nd c.BC+ [NT.Rom.6.16; ἤτοι.. ἢ.. ἤ.. “PTeb.” 5.59 (2nd c.BC))]]; ἤ repeated any number of times, ἐγὼ δέ κεν αὐτὸς ἕλωμαι ἢ τεὸν ἢ Αἴαντος ἰὼν γέρας ἢ Ὀδυσῆος [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 1.138, compare 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 15.84, 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Antigone” 707]]; ἤ is probably wrongly accented in codices of [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 2.289, 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 3.348, 19.109, see.{ἦ}]] adverb [Refs 4th c.BC+ [1.3: ἢ πόλις βροτός θ᾽ ὁμοίως 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Eumenides” 524 (Lyric poetry) is exceptional.]]

__A.3
or else, otherwise, εἰδέναι δεῖ περὶ οὗ ἂν ᾖ ἡ βουλή, ἢ παντὸς ἁμαρτάνειν ἀνάγκη [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Phaedrus” 237c; μή με λυπεῖτε, ἢ φεύξομ᾽ ἐκ τῆς οἰκίης 3rd c.BC: Herodas Mimographus 5.74]]; ζῶντα κακῶς λέγειν ἐκώλυσε.., ἢ τρεῖς δραχμὰς ἀποτίνειν ἔταξε Legal [Refs 6th c.BC+ [6th c.BC: Solon Lyricus cited in 1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus “Solon” 21, compare 24, “IG” 12.94.10, 4th c.AD: Themistius Sophista “Orationes” 21.260a.]]

__A.II
in Questions or Deliberations in Disj. form(the accentuation is ἢ (ἠέ) followed by ἦ (ἦε), [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd c.AD: Herodianus Grammaticus Gr. 2.24, +others, 2nd c.AD: Apollonius Dyscolus Grammaticus “de Conjunctionibus;” 224.28):]]

__A.II.1
Direct questions,

__A.II.1.a
introduced by ἢ (ἠέ), ἢ δολιχὴ νοῦσος ἦ Ἄρτεμις ἰοχέαιρα.. κατέπεφνε; [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 11.172; ἤ τι κατὰ πρῆξιν ἦ μαψιδίως ἀλάλησθε..; 3.72, compare 1.408, 16.462, 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 6.378, 15.735, 16.12, etc.]]

__A.II.1.b
without an introductory Particle, θεός νύ τις ἦ βροτός ἐσσ; art thou a goddess or a mortal? [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 6.149, compare 1.226, 4.314, 372, 643, 20.130, 21.194, 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 10.63, 425, 534, 15.203: accented ἦ, Hdn.Gr. 2.145, +others, but ἤ]] frequently in codices of [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Homerus Epicus and always in codices of later writers: ἤκουσας ἢ οὐκ ἤκουσας ἢ κωφῇ λέγ; 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Septem contra Thebas” 202]]; ἄρτι δὲ ἥκεις ἢ πάλα; [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Crito” 43a; κακουργεῖν δεῖ ἢ ο; [prev. work] 49c]]; preceded by πότερον, πότερον δοκεῖ σοι κάκιον εἶναι, τὸ ἀδικεῖν ἢ τὸ ἀδικεῖσθα; [Refs [[prev. author] “Grg.” 474c, etc.]]

__A.II.2
Indirect questions, frequently epexegetic of a preceding question and identical in form with direct questions.

__A.II.2.a
εἴπ᾽ ἄγε,.. ἤ ῥ᾽ ἐθέλει.., ἦ ἀπέειπε.. [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 9.674; ὄφρα δαῶμεν ἢ ἐτεὸν Κάλχας μαντεύεται ἦε καὶ οὐκί 2.300; διάνδιχα μερμήριξεν ἢ ὅ γε.. ἐναρίζοι ἦε χόλον παύσειεν 1.190; later with εἰ.. ἤ 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Choephori” 890, “Ag.” 478, 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Coloneus” 80, etc.]]; πότερον or πότερα.. ἤ.. [Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. author] “Pers.” 148, 352, “Ag.” 630, etc.; sometimes εἴτε.. ἤ 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Electra” 897; ἢ.. εἴτε 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Ajax” 177.]]

__A.II.2.b
without introductory Particle, οὐδέ τι οἶδα ζώει ὅ γ᾽ ἦ τέθνηκε [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 11.464, compare 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 10.546, 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 24.238.]]

__B
COMPARATIVE, than, as, after a comparative, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 11.162, etc.: after positive _adjectives_ which imply comparison, ἄλλος, ἕτερος ἤ.., 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Tyrannus” 595, “Tr.” 835 (Lyric poetry); ἐναντίος ἤ 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Gorgias” 481c; ἴδιόν τι πάσχειν πάθος ἢ οἱ ἄλλοι [prev. passage]: after _adverbs_ or adverbial phrases, πλήν, πρίν, πρόσθεν, χωρίς (which see), ἀλλά (see. ἀλλ᾽ ἤ); τῇ ὑστεραίᾳ ἤ.. [prev. author] “Cri.” 44a (_falsa lectio_ in “Smp.” 173a); ἐν τῷ πέμπτῳ καὶ δεκάτῳ ϝέτει ἀπὸ τῶ ποτεχεῖ ϝέτεος ἢ Ἀριστίων ἐφορεύει “Tab.Heracl.” 1.121; παρὰ δόξαν ἢ ὡς αὐτὸς κατεδόκεε 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.79, compare 8.4; διαφερόντως ἤ.. 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Phaedo” 85b]]; οὐδ᾽ ὅσον ἤ.. not so much as.. , not more than.. , [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [3rd c.BC: Theocritus Poeta Bucolicus 9.21: after Verbs implying comparison, βούλεσθαι ἤ..]] to wish rather than.. , see at {βούλομαι} IV, αἱρέω [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Bacchylides Lyricus 11.1b]]; so φθάνειν ἤ.. to come sooner than.. , [NT+8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 23.445, 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 11.58; ἐπιθυμεῖν ἤ.. 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 1.4.3; δέχεσθαι ἤ.. 5th c.BC: Lysias Orator 10.21: less frequently after a word not implying comparison, δίκαιον ἡμέας ἔχειν.. (i.e. μᾶλλον) ἤ περ Ἀθηναίους 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 9.26; ἐμοὶ πικρὸς.. ἢ κείνοις γλυκύς 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Ajax” 966 (assuming variant); δεδικαιωμένος ἢ ἐκεῖνος NT.Luke.18.14.]]

__B.2
joining two Comparatives which refer to the same subject, πάντες κ᾽ ἀρησαίατ᾽ ἐλαφρότεροι πόδας εἶναι ἢ ἀφνειότεροι [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 1.165; ταχύτερα ἢ σοφώτερα 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 3.65; μανικώτεροι ἢ ἀνδρειότεροι 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Theaetetus” 144b, compare 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Acharnenses” 1078.]]

__B.3
rarely after a superlative, πλεῖστα θωμάσια ἔχει Αἴγυπτος ἢ ἄλλη πᾶσα χώρη [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 2.35 (assuming variant); πίθοιτό κεν ὔμμι μάλιστα ἢ ἐμοί 3rd c.BC: Apollonius Rhodius Epicus 3.91.]]

__B.4
ἢ οὐ is used when a negative precedes, οὐδέν τι μᾶλλον ἐπ᾽ ἡμέας ἢ οὐ καὶ ἐπ᾽ ὑμέας [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 4.118, compare 5.94, 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 2.62, etc.]]: after an implied negative, ὠμὸν.. πόλιν ὅλην διαφθεῖραι μᾶλλον ἢ οὐ τοὺς αἰτίους [Refs [[prev. author] 3.36.]]

__B.5
frequently omitted with numerals after πλείων, ἐλάττων, μείων, ἔτη.. πλείω ἑβδομήκοντα variant in [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Apologia” 17d; οὐ μεῖον πεντακοσίους 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 6.4.24]]: sometimes with an infinitive or conditional clause, τί γὰρ ἀνδρὶ κακὸν μεῖζον ἁμαρτεῖν [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Alcestis” 879]]; τίς εὐπραξία σπανιωτέρα.., εἰ [δύναμις] πάρεστιν (for ἢ δύναμιν παρεῖναι); [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 1.33.]]

__B.6
pleonastic with a genitive, τίς ἂν αἰσχίων εἴη ταύτης δόξα, ἢ δοκεῖν.. [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Crito” 44c, compare 5th c.BC: Lysias Orator 10.28.]]

__B.7
the Disj. and comparative uses are found together in [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 15.511 βέλτερον, ἢ ἀπολέσθαι ἕνα χρόνον ἠὲ βιῶναι, ἢ δηθὰ στρεύγεσθαι ἐν αἰνῆ δηϊοτῆτι]] better, either to die once for all or win life, than long to toil in battle. [ἢ οὐ, ἢ οὐκ combine by Synizesis into one syllable in Trag. and Comedy texts, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Prometheus Vinctus” 330, 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Ajax” 334, 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Lysistrata” 128]]; so usually in Epic dialect, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 1.298, +others; ἢ αὐτός 8th-7th c.BC: Hesiodus Epicus “Fragmenta” 194; ἢ εἰ 2nd c.AD: Alexander Rhetor 201.]]]

ἦ (μήν), see: εἰ, iii, 7.
εἰ,
conjunctive particle, used in conditions and in indirect   questions.
__I. Conditional, if;
__1. with indic, expressing a general assumption;
__(a) pres.: before indic, pres., Mat.11:14, Rom.8:25, al.; before imperat., Mrk.4:23  9:22, Jhn.15:18, 1Co.7:9, al.; before fut. indic., Luk.16:31, Rom.8:11, al.; before pf. or aor., with negation in apodosis, Mat.12:26, Rom.4:14, al.; similarly, before impf., Luk.17:6, Jhn.8:39; before quæst., Mat.6:23, Jhn.5:47  7:23 8:46, 1Pe.2:20;
__(b) fut.: Mat.26:33, 1Pe.2:20;
__(with) pf.: Jhn.11:12, Rom.6:5, al.;
__(d) aor.: Luk.16:11  19:8, Jhn.13:32, 18:23, Rev.20:15, al.
__2. Where the assumption is certain = ἐπεί: Mat.12:28, Jhn.7:4, Rom.5:17, al.
__3. Of an unfulfilled condition, with indic, impf., aor. or plpf., before ἄν, with imp. or aor. (see: ἄν, I, i).
__4. C. indic., after verbs denoting wonder, etc., sometimes, but not always, coupled with an element of doubt: Mrk.15:44, 1Jn.3:13, al.
__5. C. indic., as in LXX (Num.14:3o, 1Ki.14:45, al. = Heb. אִם), in oaths, with the formula of imprecation understood in a suppressed apodosis (WM, 627; Burton, §272): Mrk.8:12, Heb.3:11" (LXX)  4:3 (LXX).
__6. Rarely (cl.) with optative, to express a merely possible condition: Act.24:19 27:39, 1Co.14:10 15:37, I Pe3:14, 17.
__II. Interrogative, if, whether.
__1. As in cl., in indir. questions after verbs of seeing, asking, knowing, saying, etc.: with indic. pres., Mat.26:63, Mrk.15:36, Act.19:2, 2Co.13:5, al.; fut., Mrk.3:2, Act.8:22, al.; aor., Mrk.15:44, 1Co.1:16, al.; with subjc. aor. (M, Pr., 194), Php.3:12.
__2. As in LXX (= Heb. אִם and interrog. הֲ, Gen.17:17, al.; see WM, 639f.; Viteau, i, 22), in direct questions: Mrk.8:23 (Tr., WH, txt.), Luk.13:23, 22:49, Act.19:2, al.
__III. With other particles.
__1. εἰ ἄρα, εἴγε, εἰ δὲ μήγε, see: ἄρα, γε.
__2. εἰ δὲ καί, but if also: Luk.11:18; but even if, 1Co.4:7, 2Co.4:3 11:16.
__3. εἰ δὲ μή, but if not, but if otherwise: Mrk.2:21, 22 Jhn.14:2, Rev.2:5, al.
__4. εἰ καί, if even, if also, although: Mrk.14:29, Luk.11:8, 1Co.7:21, 2Co.4:16, Php.2:17, al.
__5. καὶ εἰ, even if, see: καί
__6. εἰ μή, if not, unless, except, but only: Mat.24:22, Mrk.2:26 6:5, Jhn.9:33, 1Co.7:17 (only), Gal.1:19 (cf. ἐὰν μή, 2:16; see Hort., Ja., xvi); ἐκτὸς εἰ μή, pleonastic (Bl., §65, 6), 1Co.14:5 15:2, 1Ti.5:19.
__7. εἰ μήν = cl. ἦ μήν (M, Pr., 46), in oaths, surely (Eze.33:27, al.): Heb.6:14.
__8. εἴ πως, if haply: Act.27:12, Rom.1:10.
__9. εἴτε . . . εἴτε, whether . . . or; Rom.12:6-8, 1Co.3:22 13:8, al.
(AS)

ἦ,
adverb, never in the form ἦε (ἠέ):

__I
TO CONFIRM an assertion, in truth, of a surety, ἦ ὀλίγον οἷ παῖδα ἐοικότα γείνατο Τυδεύς [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 5.800, etc.; ironically, 1.229, +others]]; with concessive force, it is true that.. : hence, although.. , ἦ καὶ γένει ὕστερος ἦεν [Refs [3.215]]: frequently strengthened by the addition of one or two other Particles, as ἦ ἄρα [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 24.193; ἦ ἄρα δή 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 13.446; ἦ ῥα 4.82; ἦ ῥά νυ 6.215; ἦ γάρ 1.78; ἦ γάρ τοι 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 16.199; ἦ δή 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 2.272; ἦ δή που 21.583; ἦ δῆτα 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Tyrannus” 429; ἦ θην 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 20.452; ἦ κάρτα 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Electra” 1279; ἦ μάλα 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 3.204; ἦ μάλα δή 5.422]]; ἦ μήν and ἦ μέν (see. below); ἦ νυ [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 22.11; ἦ τάχα 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 18.73; ἦ τε 13.211: and to express doubt, ἦ που, see at {ἦ που} and ποῦ: especially ἦ μήν]] used in oaths and asseverations, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 2.291, 7.393, 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Prometheus Vinctus” 73, 168, etc.; also ἦ μάν 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 2.370, 13.354, 7th-6th c.BC: Sappho Lyrica “Papyrus fragments” in E. Diehl, 23.5; ἦ μέν 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 10.65 (later εἶ μήν, see at {εἷ})]]: with infinitive in indirect speech, after Verbs of swearing, etc., σὺ δὲ σύνθεο, καί μοι ὄμοσσον, ἦ μέν μοι πρόφρων ἔπεσιν καὶ χερσὶν ἀρήξειν [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 1.77]]; ἦ μέν also in Ionic dialect historical Prose, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 4.154, 5.93, +others; ἐγγυᾶσθαι, ἦ μὴν παραμενεῖν 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Phaedo” 115d]]; ἐγγυητὰς καταστῆσαι ἦ μὴν ἐκτείσειν Legal cited in [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 24.39]]: with other Particles, ἦ μὲν δή [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 2.798, 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 18.257, +others; ἦ δὴ μάν 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 17.538.]]

__I.2
in the combinations ἐπεὶ ἦ, ὅτι ἢ and τί ; [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd c.AD: Apollonius Dyscolus Grammaticus “de Conjunctionibus;” 255.5, “Synt.” 307.19 (cf. Hdn.Gr. 1.520), recognizes an 'expletive' ἠ]] (παραπληρωματικὸς σύνδεσμος) perispomenon after ἐπεί, barytone after ὅτι or τί. It is probably the same as the affirmative ἦ [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [compare (2nd c.AD: Apollonius Dyscolus Grammaticus “Conj.”[same place])]], and occurs in the same combinations, ἐπεὶ ἦ πολύ.. [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 1.169, +others]]; ἐπεὶ ἦ μάλα[Refs 8th c.BC+ [[prev. work] 156, 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 10.465; ἐπεὶ ἦ καί.. 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 20.437, 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 16.442. 1st c.BC: Trypho Grammaticus took τίη]] as one word, and this can be supported by τί ἢ δὲ σύ.. [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 6.55, but 2nd c.AD: Apollonius Dyscolus Grammaticus (“Conj.”[same place]) infers from the accent of ὅτι ἢ that τί ἢ]] was two words. The Attic accentuation is said by [Refs [12th c.AD: Eustathius Episcopus Thessalonicensis 45 [near the start], 118.39, 907.14 to be τιή, ὁτιή(which see).]]

__I.3
this ἦ (or ἢ) is probably to be recognized in ὥς τε γὰρ ἦ [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 2.289, ὥς τέ τευ ἦ 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 3.348, 19.109, where codices have ἢ (in 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 3.348 ἠδέ (conjecture Bekker) should perhaps be read for ἠέ).]]

__II
in Questions not involving alternatives:

__II.1
Direct questions,

__II.1.a
epexegetic of a preceding question, suggesting the answer to it, τίπτ᾽ εἰλήλουθα; ἦ ἵνα ὕβριν ἴδῃ Ἀγαμέμνονο; why hast thou come? is it that thou mayst see.. ? [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 1.203, compare 5.466, 7.26, 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 4.710, 13.418, 17.376, 5th c.BC: Bacchylides Lyricus 17.5]]; τί δῆτα χρῄζει; ἦ με γῆς ἔξω βαλεῖ; [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Tyrannus” 622, compare 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Orestes” 1425 (ἤ codices)]]; τίς σοι διηγεῖτ; ἦ αὐτὸς Σωκράτη; [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Symposium” 173a (_perispomenon_, codex B): on the accent, 2nd c.AD: Herodianus Grammaticus Gr. 2.112.]]

__II.1.b
not epexegetic of a preceding question, ἦ σύ γ᾽ Ὀδυσσεύς ἐσσι πολύτροπο; art thou the wily Odysseus? [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 10.330, compare 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 11.666, 15.504]]; ἦ οὐκ ὀτρύνοντος ἀκούετε.. Ἕκτορο; do you not hear.[Refs 8th c.BC+ [.? [prev. work] 506, compare 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 16.424]]; ἦ τὸ πλοῖον ἀφῖκτα; [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Crito” 43c]]; ἦ οὐ δοκεῖ καὶ σοὶ οὕτ; don't you think so too? [Refs [[prev. author] “Grg.” 479b (_perispomenon_, codex T); ἦ βούλει συλλογισώμεθα αὐτ; shall we work them (the consequences) out? [prev. work] 479c (_perispomenon_, codex T)]]; ἦ τορῶς λέγ; [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Agamemnon” 269]]; ἦ κἀν δόμοισι τυγχάνει τανῦν παρώ; [Refs 8th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Tyrannus” 757: frequently with other Particles, ἦ ἄρ..; 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 20.166, 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 19.56; mostly ἦ ῥα..; 5.421, 762, 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 4.632]]; also in Trag. (in Lyric poetry), [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Persae” 633, 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Ajax” 172, 955]]: especially to mark the first of several questions, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “I.” 7(6).3]] ff.; ἦ ἄρα δή..; [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 13.446; ἦ ῥά νυ..; 4.93; ἦ νυ..; 15.128]]; ἦ ταῦτα δή..; [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Philoctetes” 565, “El.” 385]]; ἦ ταῦτα δῆτα..; [Refs [[prev. author] “OT” 429]]; ἦ γάρ..; [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Prometheus Vinctus” 745, 757, 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Tyrannus” 1000: in _Attic dialect_ Prose, ἦ γάρ]]; standing alone, is it not so? [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Theaetetus” 160e, “Grg.” 449d, 468d]]; ἦ καί..; [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Agamemnon” 1207, 1362:]] —ἦ usually begins the sentence, except that the vocative may precede, as in [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 5.421, 762, 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 4.632, 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Coloneus” 863, 1102, or ἀλλά, as in 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Agamemnon” 276, “Ch.” 774:]] —by Crasis ἦ combines with ἄρα in _Attic dialect_ and the κοινή to ἆρα (which see), in all other dialects [Refs 7th c.BC+ [compare (2nd c.AD: Apollonius Dyscolus Grammaticus “de Conjunctionibus;” 223.24) to ἦρα (which see), but ἆρα is found in 5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “P.” 4.78 (ἄρα codices), +others, 7th c.BC: Archilochus Lyricus 86, 89.]]

__II.2
Indirect questions, οἴχετο πευσόμενος μετὰ σὸν κλέος ἤ που ἔτ᾽ εἴης [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 13.415 (variant{εἰ}]], which alone has Ms. authority in [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 1.83, 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 19.325); ὄφρα καὶ Ἕκτωρ εἴσεται ἢ καὶ ἐμὸν δόρυ μαίνεται ἐν παλάμῃσιν 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 8.111 (variant{εἰ})]]; ἀλλ᾽ ἄγε μοι τόδε εἰπὲ.. ἢ καὶ Λαέρτῃ αὐτὴν ὁδὸν ἄγγελος ἔλθ; [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 16.138 (variant{εἰ})]]; ἀμφίστασθαι ἦ κα πεφυτεύκωντι πάντα κὰτ τὰν συνθήκαν they shall investigate whether.. [Refs 8th c.BC+ [Tab.Heracl. 1.125; μαντεύσασθαί οἱ.. ἦ λώϊόν οἵ κα εἴη 3rd c.BC: Isyllus Lyricus 34; διαφαφίξασθαι ἦ δοκεῖ αὐτὸν στεφανῶσαι “IG” 12(3).170.12 (from Astypalaea): accented ἤ in codices 8th c.BC: Homerus Epicus, but it should perhaps be _perispomenon_]]

__A
ἦ, for ἔφη, 3rd.pers. singular imperfect or aorist 2 of ἠμί (which see). ἦ, for ἦν, Attic dialect contraction from Ionic ἔα, imperfect of εἰμί (sum).

leading the way, going first, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 2.93]]; τῇ τῶν δυναστευόντων ἡ. by their example, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Leges” 711c.]]

__II
authority, rule, of dynasties or nations, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.7, 3.65, etc.]]; of a general or officer, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 4.91; ἐν ἡγεμονίαις [prev. author] 7.15]]; ἡ ἡ. τῶν Ἰώνων τοῦ πολέμου [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 6.2]]; ἡ κατὰ πόλεμον ἡ., τῶν πολεμικῶν ἡ ἡ., [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Politica” 1285b9, 18; αἱ ἡ. τῶν στρατοπέδων 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Euthydemus” 273c; τῶν ὀπισθοφυλάκων 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 4.7.8]]; ἡ. δικαστηρίου presidency in a court, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aeschines Orator 3.14]]; headship of a philosophical school, [Refs 1st c.BC+ [1st c.BC: Philodemus Philosophus “Academicorum Index” p.59 M.]]

ἡγεμών, -όνος, ὁ
(ἡγέομαι) [in LXX for אַלּוּף, שַׂר, etc. ;]
__1. a leader, guide.
__2. a commander.
__3. a governor of a province (pro­consul, proprietor, legate, or procurator; but cf. ἀνθύπατος): Mat.10:18, Mrk.13:9, Luk.21:12, 1Pe.2:14; of the Procurator of Judæa, Mat.27:2, 11 27:14-15, 21 27:27 28:14, Luk.20:20, Act.23:24, 26 23:33 24:1, 10 26:30.
__4. For Heb. אַלְפֵי (LXX, χίλιαι) misread אַלֻּפֵי, leaders: Mat.2:6 (OT).†
(AS)

LSJ / STEPBible (TFLSJ)
ἡγεμών,
Doric dialect ἁγ-, Aeolic dialect ἀγίμων [Refs [“IG” 12(2).164 (Mytil.), +others]], όνος, ; also ἡ, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “I.” 8(7).22, 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Supplices” 722, 4th c.BC: Aeschines Orator 1.171, 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Oec.” (below 11)]]:— one who leads; and so,

__I
in [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey”]], guide, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [10.505, 15.310, 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 5.14, 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Antigone” 1014, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Meno” 97b; ἡγεμόνες γενέσθαι τινὶ τῆς ὁδοῦ 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 8.31, compare 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Hecuba” 281, 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Memorabilia” 1.3.4; ἡ. ποδὸς τυφλοῦ 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Phoenissae” 1616; ἡγεμόνες τοῦ πλοῦ 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 7.50]]; of a charioteer, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Tyrannus” 804.]]

__I.2
one who does a thing first, shows the way to others, τοῖς νεωτέροις ἡ. ἠθῶν χρηστῶν γίγνεσθαι [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Leges” 670e; πατέρες τῆς σοφίας καὶ ἡ. [prev. author] “Ly.” 214a; πόνους τοῦ ζῆν ἡδέως ἡγεμόνας νομίζετε 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 1.5.12; τῆς εἰρήνης ἡ. 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 18.24; [ἀχαριστία] ἐπὶ πάντα τὰ αἰσχρὰ ἡ. 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 1.2.7]]: absolutely, of choir-leaders, Mnemos.[Refs 2nd c.BC+ [47.253 (Argos, 2nd-1st c.BC).]]

__II
in [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad”]], leader, commander, chief, opposed to λαοί, πληθύς, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [2.365, 11.304: with _genitive_, ἡγεμόνες Δαναῶν, φυλάκων, etc., 2.487, 9.85, compare 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 6.43, 7.62, +others]]; στρατηγὸς καὶ ἡ. τῶν 'Ελλήνων πρὸς τὸν βάρβαρον[Refs [[prev. work] 158; ἡ. τῶν πολέμων [prev. author] 9.33]]; ἔχοντες ἡγεμόνας τῶν πάνυ [στρατηγῶν] [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 8.89]]; ={λοχαγός}, [Refs 2nd c.BC+ [2nd c.AD: Arrianus Historicus “Tactica” 5.6; ἡ. τῶν ἐν προχειρισμῷ “PAmh.” 2.39 (2nd c.BC)]]; chief, sovereign, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “I.” 8(7).22, etc.; ἡ. γῆς τῆσδε 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Tyrannus” 103, compare “OC” 289; πάντων.. καὶ αὐτοῦ βασιλέως ἡ. 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Historia Graeca (Hellenica)” 3.5.14; ἡ. συμμορίας 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 21.157]]; of the queen-bee and queen-wasp, regarded by [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus as males, 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Historia Animalium” 553a25, 629a3 (but ἡ τῶν μελισσῶν ἡ. 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Oeconomicus” 7.32, compare 38)]]; ὁ ἡ. τῶν προβάτων, of the bell-wether, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Historia Animalium” 573b24]]; τῶν βοῶν[Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. work] 575b1; νέμειν τὰ κρέα τοῦ ἡγεμόνος βοός “SIG” 144.36 (Piraeus, 4th c.BC),compare 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Historia Graeca (Hellenica)” 6.4.29.]]

__II.b
ἡ. χοροῦ leader of a chorus, [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd c.AD(?): Pollianus Epigrammaticus 4.106; παῖδες ἡ. “IG” 7.3196 (Orchom. _Boeotian dialect_)]]; president of a gymnasium, [Refs [[prev. work]3.1086, +others]]

__II.c
a Roman Emperor, [Refs 1st c.BC+ [1st c.BC-1st c.AD: Strabo Geographus 4.3.2, 1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus “Cicero” 2, +others]]; as translation of princeps, [Refs [Mon.Anc.Gr. 7.9]]; ἡ. νεότητος, = Latin princeps juventutis, [Refs [[prev. work]18]]; a provincial governor, [NT+1st c.BC+ [1st c.BC-1st c.AD: Strabo Geographus 17.3.25, NT.Matt.27.2, NT.Act.23.24]]: frequently of the praefectus Aegypti, [Refs 1st c.AD+ [PRyl. 119.4 (1st c.AD)]], etc.; ἡ. ἀμφοτέρων, i.e. of Upper and Lower Egypt, [Refs 1st c.AD+ [“POxy.” 39.6 (1st c.AD)]]; ἡ. Κύπρου [Refs 3rd c.AD+ [“Tab. Defix.Aud.” 25.13 (3rd c.AD).]]

__II.2
as adjective, ἀνήρ [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Critias” 119a]]; [ναῦς], of the flagship, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Supplices” 722; ἡ. τῆς φυλῆς κορυφαῖος 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 21.60 (assuming variant); ἡ. πόδες 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Historia Animalium” 490b5, “IA” 713b32: as _neuter_, ἡγεμόσι μέρεσι 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Timaeus” 91e.]]

__III
in Prosody, ={πυρρίχιος}, [Refs 1st c.BC+ [1st c.BC: Dionysius Halicarnassensis “de Compositione Verborum” 17, “Dem.” 47.]]

__IV
ἡγεμόνες, Doric dialect ἁγ-, αἱ, in Architecture, coping-tiles of the roof, [Refs [“IG” 22.463.70, 1627.303, 4.1484.100 (Epid.).]]

__V
a kind of fish, ={ἡγητήρ} 2, [Refs 1st c.AD+ [1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus 2.980f.]]

ἡγέομαι, -οῦμαι depon. mid.,
[in LXX (chiefly Pres. ptcp.) for נָגִיד, רֹאשׁ, שַׂר, etc. ;]
__1. to lead;
__(a) to guide, go before;

Lat. duco): with dupl. accusative, Act.26:2, Php.2:3, 6 3:7, 1Ti.1:12 6:1, Heb.10:29 11:11, 26, 2Pe.1:13 2:13 3:9 3:15; with accusative before ὡς, with accusative, 2Th.3:15; with accusative before adv., 1Th.5:13; ὅταν, Jas.1:2; ἀναγκαῖον, with inf., 2Co.9:5, Php.2:25; δίκαιον, with inf., 2Pe.1:13; with accusative and inf., Php.3:8 (of. δι-, ἐκ-δι-, ἐξ- προ-ηγέομαι).†
