ἡγέομαι,
Doric dialect ἁγ- (irregular present participle ἁγώμενος [Refs [“Hymnus Curetum [3rd c.BC (?)]” 4),]]imperfect ἡγούμην[Refs [lines12.28, etc.]], Ionic dialect -εύμην[Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 2.115, ἡγέοντο [prev. author] 9.15]]: future ἡγήσομαι [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 14.374, etc.]]: aorist 1 ἡγησάμην [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 14.48, etc.:]]aorist 1 ἡγήθην[Refs 3rd c.AD+ [in _passive_ sense, “PGiss.” 48.20 (3rd c.AD) (compare περιηγ-)]]: perfect ἥγημαι [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.126, 2.115, ἅγημαι 5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “P.” 4.248]]:—go before, lead the way, ὣς εἰπὼν ἡγεῖθ᾽, ἡ δ᾽ ἕσπετο Παλλὰς 'Αθήνη [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 1.125; ἂν πάϊς ἡγήσαιτο νήπιος 6.300, etc.; πρόσθεν δὲ.. Ἶρις ἡγεῖτ᾽ 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 24.96; ἡγοῦ πάροιθε 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Phoenissae” 834; ἡ. ἐπὶ νῆα 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 13.65; ἐς τεῖχος 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 20.144; κλισίηνδε 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 14. 48, compare 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 2.93, etc.; ἡγησόμενος οὐδεὶς ἔσται 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 2.4.5]]: Astron., precede in the daily movement, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Autolycus Astronomus 2.3, +others]]

__b
with dative person, Τρωσὶ ποτὶ πτόλιν ἡγήσασθαι [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 22.101; ἐκ Δουλιχίου.. ἡγεῖτο μνηστῆρσι 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 16.397; οἱ γὰρ βλέποντες τοῖς τυφλοῖς ἡγούμεθα 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Plutus” 15; ἡ. τοῖς πολίταις πρὸς ἀρετήν 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Agesilaus” 10.2.]]

__c
with ὁδόν added, ὁδὸν ἡγήσασθαι to go before on the way, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 10.263; ἡ. τινὶ τὴν ὁδόν 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 9.15.]]

__d
with accusative loci, ἥ οἱ.. πόλιν ἡγήσαιτο who might guide him to the city, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 6.114, compare 7.22, 15.82; ἡ. βωμοὺς ἀστικούς 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Supplices” 501.]]

__e
ἅρματα ἡ. drive chariots, [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd-3rd c.AD: Philostratus Sophista “Philostrati majoris imagines” 2.23.]]

__f
of logical priority, to be antecedent, opposed to ἕπεσθαι, [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [“Stoicorum Veterum Fragmenta” 2.71, 88, 2nd c.AD: Sextus Empiricus Philosophus “adversus Mathematicos” 8.110, +others, 5th-6th c.AD: Damascius Philosophus “de Principiis” 241, 6th c.AD: Philoponus, Joannes Philosophus “in Aristotelis libros de Generatione et Corruptione commentaria - pars” 195.13, “in Ph.” 496.14.]]

__g
ἡγούμενον, τό, the leading principle, the main thing, [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [3rd-2nd c.BC: Philo Mechanicus “(Belopoeica) Excerpte aus Philons Mechanik - Ath. Berl. Akad.” 63.14, compare 3rd c.BC(?): Sosipater Comicus 1.47.]]

__2
with dative person et genitive of things, to be one's leader in a thing, θεῖος ἀοιδὸς.. ἡμῖν ἡγείσθω.. ὀρχηθμοῖο [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 23.134]]; ἡ. τινὶ σοφίας, ᾠδῆς, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “P.” [same place], 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus Alcaeus1.125d; ἀλήθεια δὴ πάντων μὲν ἀγαθῶν θεοῖς ἡγεῖται πάντων δὲ ἀνθρώποις [prev. author] “Lg.” 730c; ἡ. τοῦ χοροῦ Πέρσαις 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 8.7.1, compare 3rd c.BC: Callimachus Epicus “Hymnus in Delum” 313:]] with genitive _of things_, ἁ. νόμων to lead the song, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “N.” 5.25; φρόνησις ἡ. τοῦ ὀρθῶς πράττειν 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Meno” 97c; ἡ. παντὸς καὶ λόγου καὶ ἔργου 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Memorabilia” 2.3.15: also, τὸ ὀρθῶς τοῖς τοιούτοις χρῆσθαι ἐπιστήμη ἦν ἡγουμένη 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Euthydemus” 281a.]]

__3
with dative of things, to be leader in.. , κερδοσύνῃ, νηπιέῃσι ἡ. τινί, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 22.247, 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 24.469.]]

__4
with accusative of things, lead, conduct, ἡ. τὰς πομπάς [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 21.174]]; τὴν ἀποδημίαν (variant for{ᾐτήσατο}) [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Dinon Historicus 7; τὰς τύχας 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Supplices” 226]]: with adverbial accusative, ἡ γλῶσσα πάνθ᾽ ἡγουμένη [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Philoctetes” 99.]]

__5
participle ἡγούμενος, η, ον, as adjective, σκέλη ἡγούμενα, opposed to ἑπόμενα, the front legs, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “de Incessu Animalium” 713b6]]; ὁ ἡ. πούς the advanced foot, [Refs [[prev. author] “fragment” 74.]]

__II
lead, command in war, with dative, νῆες θοαί, ᾗσιν 'Αχιλλεὺς ἐς Τροίην ἡγεῖτο [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 16.169, compare 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 14.238]]; οὐ γὰρ ἔην ὅς τίς σφιν ἐπὶ στίχας ἡγήσαιτο might lead them to their ranks, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 2.687; ἡ. Τρώεσσιν ἐς Ἴλιον 5.211; ἡ. Μῄοσιν 2.864; λόγχαισιν 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Bacchae” 1360; ἑτέροις 5th c.BC: Lysias Orator 31.17, compare 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 5.2.6; ἐν ταῖς στρατείαις, αἷς ἡγεῖται βασιλεύς 5th-6th c.BC: Isocrates Orator 12.180: also generally, πόλει 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Fragmenta” 282.24; but usually with _genitive_, Σαρπηδὼν δ᾽ ἡγήσατ᾽.. ἐπικούρων 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 12.101; ἡγήσατο λαῶν 15.311, compare 2.567, +others; ἡ. τῆς ἐξόδου 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 2.10; ἡγούμενος τῶν ἡδονῶν ἀλλ᾽ οὐκ ἀγόμενος ὑπ᾽ αὐτῶν 5th-6th c.BC: Isocrates Orator 9.45]]: absolutely, to be in command, [Refs [[prev. author] 16.21, etc.]]

__II.2
rule, have dominion, with genitive, τῆς 'Ασίης, τῆς συμμαχίης, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.95, 7.148; οἱ Θεσσαλίης ἡγεόμενοι [prev. author] 9.1: _absolutely_, οἱ ἡγούμενοι]] the rulers, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Philoctetes” 386, compare 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Agamemnon” 1363; ἡ. ἐν τοῖς ἀδελφοῖς]]leading men, [NT.Acts.15.22]; ἡ. σχολῆς to be the head of a philosophical school, [Refs 1st c.BC+ [1st c.BC: Philodemus Gadarensis Epigrammaticus “Acad. Ind.” p.107 M., +others]]

__II.3
as official title, ἡγούμενος, ὁ, president, συνόδου [Refs 1st c.AD+ [“PGrenf.” 2.67.3 (3rd c.AD); γερδίων [prev. work] 43.9 (1st c.AD)]]; ἱερέων [Refs 1st c.AD+ [“PLond.” 2.281.2 (1st c.AD): _absolutely_, “PFay.” 110.26 (1st c.AD).]]

__II.3.b
of Roman governors, ἡ. ἔθνους,= Latin praeses provinciae, [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [POxy. 1020.5 (2nd-3rd c.AD)]]; ἡ. τῆς Γαλατίας [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd c.AD: Lucianus Sophista “Alex.” 44.]]

__II.3.c
of subordinate officials, ἡ. τοῦ στρατηγοῦ [Refs 1st c.AD+ [“POxy.” 294.19 (1st c.AD)]]; κώμης [Refs 1st c.AD+ [“PRyl.” 125.3 (1st c.AD).]]

__II.3.d
abbot, [Refs 6th c.AD+ [6th c.AD: Justinianus Imperator “Novellae” 7.1, +others: _feminine_ -μένη]] abbess, [Refs [[prev. passage]]]

__II.4
ἡγούμενος as adjective, principal, πυλών [Refs 3rd c.AD+ [“PFlor.” 382.15 (3rd c.AD), “POxy.” 55.9 (3rd c.AD).]]

__III
post-[Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Homerus Epicus]], believe, hold, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus (usually in _perfect_ ἥγημαι, _3rd.pers._ _plural_ ἡγέαται)]], etc.; ἡ. τι εἶναι [Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. author] 1.126, +others; ἡγεῖσθε δὲ [θεοὺς] βλέπειν.. πρὸς τὸν εὐσεβῆ βροτῶν 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Coloneus” 278, compare 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 2.89, 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Nubes” 1020 (Lyric poetry), etc.]]

__III.2
with an attributive word added, ἡ. τινὰ βασιλέα hold or regard as king, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 6.52; μηδ᾽ αὐθαδίαν εὐβουλίας ἀμείνον᾽ ἡγήσῃ ποτέ 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Prometheus Vinctus” 1035; ἅπαντας ἐχθροὺς τῶν θεῶν ἡγοῦ πλέον [prev. author] “Ch.” 902, compare 905]]; ἡ. τἄλλα πάντα δεύτερα to hold everything else secondary, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Philoctetes” 1442]]; οὐκ αἰσχρὸν ἡγῇ.. τὰ ψευδῆ λέγειν[Refs 5th c.BC+ [; [prev. work] 108, compare “Ant.” 1167; τὰς τούτων ἀπορίας ἀντιπάλους ἡ. τῷ ἡμετέρῳ πλήθει 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 4.10; περὶ πολλοῦ ἥγημαι μὴ ξεινοκτονέειν 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 2.115; περὶ πλείονος 5th-6th c.BC: Isocrates Orator 19.10; περὶ πλείστου 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 2.89; περὶ οὐδενός 5th c.BC: Lysias Orator 7.26]]; παρ᾽ οὐδέν Decrees cited in [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 18.164]]: with participle, πᾶν κέρδος ἡγοῦ ζημιουμένη φυγῇ [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Medea” 454.]]

__III.3
especially of belief in gods, τὴν μεγίστην δαίμονα ἥγηνται εἶναι [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 2.40, compare 3.8]]; ἡ. θεούς to believe in gods, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Equites” 32, 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Hecuba” 800, “Ba.” 1326; δαίμονας ἡ. 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Apologia” 27d.]]

__III.4
ἡγοῦμαι δεῖν think fit, deem necessary, with infinitive, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Andocides Orator 1.23, 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 1.20: without δεῖν, παθεῖν μᾶλλον ἡγησάμενοι ἤ.. 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 2.42 (assuming variant); ἡγησάμην διατάγματι αὐτοὺς σωφρονίσαι “Inscription Magn.” 114 (2nd c.AD)]]; ἡγήσατο ἐπαινέσαι [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Protagoras” 346b]].

__IV
perfect in passive sense, τὰ ἁγημένα,= τὰ νομιζόμενα, Oracle texts cited in [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 43.66]]; ἡγεόμενον being led, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 3.14 (ἀγόμενον Dind.): hence _active_ form ἡγέω, Hdn.Gr. 2.950]]. (sāg-, cf. Latin praesagio.)

__II.2
disposition, character, ἐπίκλοπον ἦθος [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th-7th c.BC: Hesiodus Epicus “Opera et Dies” 67, 78; ἦ. ἐμφυές 5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “O.” 11(10).21]]; ἀκίχητα ἤ., of Zeus, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Prometheus Vinctus” 187; τοὐμὸν ἦ. παιδεύειν 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Ajax” 595]]; ὦ μιαρὸν ἦ. [Refs [[prev. author] “Ant.” 746]]; τὸ τῆς πόλεως ἦ. [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Isocrates Orator 2.31]]; βελτίων τῆς πόλεως τὸ ἦ. [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 20.14]]; especially moral character, opposed to διάνοια, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Ethica Nicomachea” 1139a1]]; as the result of habit, τὸ πᾶν ἦ. διὰ ἔθος [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Leges” 792e, compare 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Ethica Eudemia” 1220a39; ἦ. ἀνθρώπῳ δαίμων 1st c.AD(?): Heraclitus 119]]; ἦ. πηγὴ βίου Stoic. cited in [Refs 5th c.AD+ [5th c.AD: Stobaeus, Joannes 2.7.1]]; τῆς ψυχῆς, τῆς γνώμης, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 400d, 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 61.16: frequently opposed to πάθος, 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Rhetorica” 1356a23 (_plural_), etc.; ἠθῶν τε καὶ παθῶν μίμησις 1st c.BC: Dionysius Halicarnassensis “Epistula ad Pompeium” 3; τὸ ἦ. πρᾶος 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Phaedrus” 243c: less frequently in _dative_, ἀγοραῖος τῷ ἤ. 4th-3rd c.BC: Theophrastus Philosophus “Characteres” 6.2, compare “Inscription Magn.” 164.3 (1st-2nd c.AD)]]: plural, traits, characteristics, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 402d, 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Ethica Nicomachea” 1144b4 (in _sing._, τὸ τῆς ἀνδρείας ἦ. 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Leges” 836d)]]: seldom in plural, of an individual, στερρὸν τὰ ἤθεα [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Hippocrates Medicus “ἐπιστολαί” 11; ἱερὸς κατὰ τὰ ἤθη 2nd c.AD: Athenaeus Epigrammaticus 1.1e.]]

__II.2.b
of outward bearing, ὡς ἱλαρὸν τὸ ἦ. [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Symposium” 8.3; ὑγρότης ἤθους 4th c.BC: Lycurgus Orator 33]]; ὑψηλὸς τῷ ἤ. [Refs 1st c.AD+ [1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus “Dio” 4]]: in plural, of facial expression, ὀφθαλμῶν ἤθη [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd-3rd c.AD: Philostratus Sophista “de gymnastica” 25.]]

__II.2.c
in Rhet., delineation of character, ἦ. ἔχουσιν οἱ λόγοι ἐν ὅσοις δήλη ἡ προαίρεσις [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Rhetorica” 1395b13; ἦ. ἐμφαίνειν 1st c.BC: Philodemus Gadarensis Epigrammaticus “Rh.” 1.200S.]]; especially opposed to πάθος, [Refs 3rd c.AD+ [3rd c.AD: Longinus Rhetor 9.15, etc.]]; κατ᾽ ἦ. λέγεσθαι, opposed to κατὰ πάθος, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [1st c.BC: Dionysius Halicarnassensis “de Compositione Verborum” 22, compare “Lys.” 19: in _plural_, πραγμάτων καὶ ἠθῶν 1st c.BC: Philodemus Philosophus “περὶ ποιημάτων” 5.5; ἐν πάθεσι καὶ ἤθεσιν 4th c.BC: Demetrius Phalereus Rhetor “Demetrius on Style” 28, etc.]]; so of works of art, ἡ Ζεύξιδος γραφὴ οὐδὲν ἔχει ἦ. [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Poetica” 1450a29; πάθος καὶ ἦ. καὶ σχημάτων χρῆσις 2nd-3rd c.AD: Aelianus “Varia Historia” 4.3; πολλὰ ἤθη ἐπιφαίνει 2nd-3rd c.AD: Philostratus Sophista “Heroicus” 2.10]]; also of Music, [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd c.AD: Sextus Empiricus Philosophus “adversus Mathematicos” 6.49.]]

__II.2.d
dramatis persona, εἰσάγει ἄνδρα ἢ γυναῖκα ἢ ἄλλο τι ἦ. [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Poetica” 1450a11, +others]]

__II.3
also of animals, ἦ. τὸ πρὸς τοκέων (probable reading for ἔθος) [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Agamemnon” 727, compare 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Hippolytus” 1219, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 375e, 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Historia Animalium” 487a12 (_plural_); τὸ ἦ. ἀσθενής, of a bird, [prev. work] 615a18]]; of things, nature, kind, παρὰ δ᾽ ἦ. ἑκάστῳ (to each of the four elements) [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Empedocles Poeta Philosophus 17.28; τοῦ πυρετοῦ 2nd c.AD: Galenus Medicus 7.353.]]

__II.4
ἐν ἤθει tactfully [Refs 1st c.AD+ [compare (ἠθικός 11.2), προσφέρεσθαι τοῖς ἁμαρτάνουσιν 1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus 2.73e. compare 5th c.AD: Hermias Alexandrinus Philosophus “in Platonis Phaedrum scholia” p.195A.]]; διὰ μέτριον ἦθος, of the expression δοκεῖ μοι, [Refs 7th c.AD+ [7th c.AD: Stephanus Medicus “in Hp.” 1.59D.]]

deep_entry:
Abbott-Smith / STEPBible (TBESG)
ἥκω
[in LXX chiefly for בּוֹא ;]
pf. with present meaning (hence imperfect = plpf.), to have come, be present: Mat.24:50, Mrk.8:3 (late pf., ἧκα, see Swete, in l; WH, App., 169), Luk.12:46 15:27, Jhn.8:42, Heb.10:7, 9 10:37, I Jn  5:20, Rev.2:25 3:3, 9 15:4; before ἀπό, with genitive loc., Mat.8:11, Luk.13:29; ἐκ, Rom.11:26; id. before εἰς, Jhn.4:47; μακρόθεν, Mrk.8:3; ἐπί, with accusative, Rev.3:3. Metaphorical, of discipleship: Jhn.6:37; of time and events: absol., Mat.24:14, Jhn.2:4, 2Pe.3:10, Rev.18:8; before ἐπί with accusative of person(s), Mat.23:36, Luk.19:43 (cf. ἀν-, καθ-ήκω).†
(AS)

LSJ / STEPBible (TFLSJ)
ἥκω,
[Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 5.478:]]imperfect ἧκον (see. below): future ἥξω (see. below); Doric dialect ἡξῶ [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [3rd c.BC: Theocritus Poeta Bucolicus 4.47, 3rd c.BC: Callimachus Epicus “Fragmenta” 1.65]] P. (in Doric dialect and [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Homerus Epicus more commonly ἵκω)]]: all other tenses late; aorist 1 participle ἥξας [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd c.AD: Pausanias Periegeta 2.11.5, 2nd c.AD: Galenus Medicus 6.56, 10.609]]: perfect ἧκα [Refs 2nd c.BC+ [2nd-3rd c.AD: Philostratus Sophista “Vita Apollonii” 3.24, 2nd c.BC: Scymnus Geographus 62]], 1st pers. plural ἥκαμεν [Refs 2nd c.BC+ [“UPZ” 72.9 (2nd c.BC), “CIG” “Corpus Inscriptionum Graecarum” “Corpus Inscriptionum Graecarum” 4762 (Egypt, 1st c.AD), _Doric dialect_ ἥκαμες]] falsa lectio in [Refs 1st c.AD+ [1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus 2.225b]], 2nd pers. plural ἥκατε [Refs 1st c.BC+ [“PGrenf.” 2.36.18 (1st c.BC)]], 3rd.pers. plural ἥκασι [LXX+NT [LXX.2Ki.20.14, NT.Mark.8.3]]; infinitive ἡκέναι [Refs 2nd c.BC+ [“UPZ” 6.30 (2nd c.BC)]]: pluperfect ἥκεσαν [Refs 1st c.AD+ [1st c.AD: Josephus Historicus “Antiquitates Judaicae” 19.1.14]]: —middle, present subjunctive ἥκηται [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd c.AD: Aretaeus Medicus “περὶ αἰτιῶν καὶ σημείων χρονίων παθῶν” 2.1:]]future ἥξομαι[Refs 2nd c.AD+ [variant in 2nd c.AD: Marcus Antoninus Imperator 2.4]]:—to have come, be present, properly in a perfect sense, with imperfect ἧκον as pluperfect, I had come, and future ἥξω as future perfect, I shall have come, μάλα τηλόθεν ἥκω [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 5.478, compare 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 13.325, 5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “O.” 4.12 (ἵκω codices vett.)]]: imperfect ἧκον [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Prometheus Vinctus” 661, 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 1.91, +others, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 327c, 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 8.50, etc.]]: future ἥξω [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Prometheus Vinctus” 103, +others, 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Andromache” 738, 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Pax” 265, Oracle texts cited in 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 2.54, etc.]]; ἧκε imperative, [NT+5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Ajax” 1116, 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Pax” 275, 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 4.5.25; ἡκέτω 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Rhesus” 337:—Constr. mostly with εἰς, 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 8.50, 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Choephori” 3, etc.; παρά τινα 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 7.157, 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 1.137; πρός τινα 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Choephori” 659; πρὸς δαίμονα 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Fragmenta” 770; especially in worship, ἥκω πρὸς τὴν κυρίαν Ἶσιν “OGI” 186.6 (Egypt, 1st c.BC),cf. NT.John.6.37; πρὸς πόλιν 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Coloneus” 734]]; ἐπί τινα to set upon, attack, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 336b, 4th c.BC: Aeschines Orator 2.178]]; but ἥ. ἐπὶ τὸ στράτευμα to have come to fetch the army, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 7.6.2; οἱ ἐπὶ ταῦθ᾽ ἥκοντες 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 18.28; ἐπ᾽ ὀλέθρῳ 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Iphigenia Aulidensis” 886 (troch.); περὶ σπονδῶν 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 2.3.4: with _accusative_, ἥξεις ποταμόν 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Prometheus Vinctus” 717, compare 724, 730; ἥ. δῆμον τὸν Λυρκείου 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Fragmenta” 271.6, compare 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Bacchae” 1; ἥκουσιν αὐτῷ ἄγγελοι 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 5.3.26]]; ἐς ταὐτὸν ἥ. to have come to the same point, to agree, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Hecuba” 748, “Hipp.” 273: with]] adverb of motion, ἥ. ἐνθάδε, δεῦρο[Refs 5th c.BC+ [, 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Philoctetes” 377, 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 19.58; βῆναι κεῖθεν ὅθενπερ ἥκει 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Coloneus” 1227: with _neuter_ _pronoun_, αὐτὰ ταῦτα ἥκω παρά σε 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Protagoras” 310e]]; ἐρωτώμενοι ὅ τι ἥκοιεν for what they had come, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Historia Graeca (Hellenica)” 4.5.9: with _accusative_ _cognate_, ὁδὸν μακρὰν ἥκειν [prev. author] “Cyr.” 5.5.42: c.]]infinitive, μανθάνειν γὰρ ἥκομεν we are here to learn, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Coloneus” 12.]]

__2
to have reached a point, ἐς τοσήνδ᾽ ὕβριν[Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. work] 1030; εἰς τοῦτο ἀμαθίας 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Andromache” 170; εἰς τοσοῦτον ἀμαθίας 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Apologia” 25e; εἰς ὅσον ἡλικίας [prev. author] “Chrm.” 157d, etc.; πρὸς γάμων ἀκμάς 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Tyrannus” 1492; ὁρᾷς ἵν᾽ ἥκει; [prev. work] 687]], etc.; Geometry texts, pass through a point, διὰ τῶν πόλων [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Autolycus Astronomus “Sph.” 10, compare 3rd c.BC: Archimedes Geometra “περὶ κωνοειδέων καὶ σφαιροειδέων” 9.]]

__2.b
διὰ μάχης, δι᾽ ὀργῆς ἥκειν, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Supplices” 475, 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Coloneus” 905; compare διά 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus IV.]]

__2.c
with an adverb followed by genitive, οὕτω πόρρω σοφίας ἥκεις [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Euthydemus” 294e]]; εὖ ἥκειν τινός to be well off for a thing, have plenty of it, τοῦ βίου, χρημάτων, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.30, 5.62; ἑωυτῶν [prev. author] 1.102; θεῶν χρηστῶν [prev. author] 8.111]]; πιθανότητος Demetr.[Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Magnes Comicus cited in 1st c.BC: Dionysius Halicarnassensis “de Dinarcho” 1]]; οὐκ ὁμοίως ἥ. τινός not to be equally well off in respect of.., [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.149]]; πῶς ἀγῶνος ἥκομε; how have we sped in the contest? [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Electra” 751]]; ὧδε γένους ἥ. τινί to be this degree of kin to him, [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [[prev. author] “Heracl.” 213; ὡς δυνάμεως ἥκεις 2nd c.AD: Pausanias Periegeta 4.21.10; ἐς μῆκος εὖ ἥκων 2nd-3rd c.AD: Aelianus “De Natura Animalium - Ar.Byzantine Epit.” 4.34: _absolutely_, εὖ ἥκειν]] to be flourishing, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.30: rarely with _genitive_ only, σὺ δὲ δυνάμιος ἥκεις μεγάλης]] thou art in great power, [Refs [[prev. author] 7.157 (nisi to be read μεγάλως).]]

__3
to have come back, returned, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 20.73; from exile, 5th-6th c.BC: Andocides Orator 2.13]]; αὐτίκα ἥξω I shall be back in a moment, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 2.1.9]]; ἧκέ νυν ταχύ come back soon, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Pax” 275; ἄψορρον ἥξεις 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Prometheus Vinctus” 1021; ἄψορρον ἥξομεν πάλιν 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Electra” 53.]]

__4
with participle, ἥκω φέρων I have come bringing (i.e. with), [Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. author] “OC” 579, compare 357, 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Pax” 265, 5th c.BC: Eupolis Comicus 22 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Gorgias” 518d; ἧκεν ἄγων [prev. author] “Phd.” 117a; ἕτερόν τι ἥκεις ἕχων [prev. author] “Grg.” 491c, etc.: with]]future participle, like{ἔρχομαι}, ἥκω φράσων, ἀγγελῶν, etc., I am going, I intend to say, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Phoenissae” 706, 1075, etc.]]

__5
to have come to be, θεοῖς ἔχθιστος ἥκω [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Tyrannus” 1519 (troch.), compare “Aj.” 636 (Lyric poetry), “El.” 1201, etc.]]; take one's origin, ἀπὸ πολιτειῶν τοιούτων ἥκετε, ἐν αἷς.. [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 4.126.]]

__II
of things, in various uses: of meats, to have come to table, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [2nd c.AD: Alexander Rhetor 132; ὡς τὰ περιφερόμενα ἧκε πρὸς ἡμᾶς 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 2.2.3]]; of reports, ἐμοὶ ἀγγελίη ἥκει παρὰ βασιλέος [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 8.140.ά, compare 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Coloneus” 1177]]; of events, πῆμα ἥκει τινί [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Prometheus Vinctus” 103, compare 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Ranae” 606, etc.; ἐπ᾽ ἀνδρὶ ἥκει βίον τελευτή 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Coloneus” 1472]]; ἵν᾽ ἥκειτὰ μαντεύματα what they have come to, [Refs [[prev. author] “OT” 953; ὡς αὐτὸν ἥξοι μοῖρα [prev. work] 713]] codices; ἥξει πόλεμος Oracle texts cited in [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 2.54; ἐς αὐτὸν ἥξει τὸ δεινόν [prev. author] 6.77]]; of Time, ἥκει ἦμαρ, νύξ, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Agamemnon” 1301, 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Iphigenia Taurica” 42; ἥκει ὑμῖν ὁ καιρός 5th c.BC: Lysias Orator 12.79; τὸ μέλλον ἥξει 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Agamemnon” 1240.]]

__II.2
concern, relate to, ποῖ λόγος ἥκε; to what do the words relate? [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Troades” 154 (Lyric poetry); εἰς ἔμ᾽ ἥκει.. τὰ πράγματα 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Plutus” 919]]; εἰς ἐμὲ τὸ ἐλλεῖπον ἥξει will fall upon me, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 1.5.13]]: frequently in participle, τὰ εἰς τοὺς κινδύνους ἥκοντα [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Antipho Orator 5.81]]; τὰ εἰς πλοῦτον ἥ. [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Eryxias” 392d]]; τὰ πρὸς ἔπαινον, εἰς φιλανθρωπίαν ἥ., [Refs 2nd c.BC+ [2nd c.BC: Polybius Historicus 12.15.9, 28.17.2, etc.]]

__II.3
depend upon, ὅσα τῆς Φωκέων σωτηρίας ἐπὶ τὴν πρεσβείαν ἧκε [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 19.30; τό γε ἐπ᾽ αὐτοὺς ἧκον μέρος 1st c.AD: Philo Judaeus 2.21; ὅσα γ᾽ εἰς βούλησιν ἥκειν τὴν ἐμήν 3rd c.AD: Heliodorus Scriptor Eroticus 4.7.]]

__II.4
with infinitive, ἧκέ μοι γένει.. πενθεῖν it has come to me by birth.., my birth lays it on me.., [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Coloneus” 738, compare “Ichn.” 356]]; καλῶς αὐτοῖς κατθανεῖν ἧκον βίου it being well for them at their age to die, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Alcestis” 291.]]

__II.5
with participle, ὃ καὶ νῦν ἥκει γινόμενον which commonly happens even now, [Refs 2nd c.BC+ [2nd c.BC: Polybius Historicus 24.9.11 codices (variant{γενόμενον}). (Prob. from same root as ἵκω.)]]

deep_entry:
Abbott-Smith / STEPBible (TBESG)
ἐγώ, genitive, etc., ἐμοῦ, ἐμοί, ἐμέ (enclitic μου, μοι, με), pl. ἡμεῖς, -ῶν, -ῖν, -ᾶς,
of person(s) pron.
I.
__(a) The nom. is usually emphatic, when expressed as subjc, as in Mat.3:11, Mrk.1:8, Luk.3:16, al. But often there is no apparent emphasis, as Mat.10:16, Jhn.10:17; ἰδοὺ ἐ. (= Heb. הִנֵּנִי, cf. 1Ki.3:8), Act.9:10; ἐ. (like Heb. אֲנִי), I am, Jhn.1:23 (LXX), Act.7:32 (LXX).
__(b) The enclitic forms (see supr.) are used with nouns, adjectives, verbs, adverbs, where there is no emphasis: ἐν τ. πατρί μου, Jhn.14:20; μου τ. λόγους, Mat.7:24; ὀπίσω μου, Mat.3:11; ἰσχυρότερός μου, ib.; λέγει μοι, Rev.5:5; also with the prep. πρός, as Mrk.9:19, al. The full forms (ἐμοῦ, etc.) are used with the other prepositions, as δι᾽ ἐμοῦ, ἐν ἐμοί, εἰς ἐμέ, etc., also for emphasis, as Luk.10:16, Jhn.7:23, Mrk.14:7, al.

ἡμέρα, -ας, ἡ,
[in LXX chiefly (very freq.) for יוֹם ;]
day;
__1. as distinct from night: genitive ἡμέρας, by day (WM, §30, 11), Rev.21:25; ἡ. κ. νυκτός (ν. κ. ̔ἡ.), Act.9:24, 1Th.2:9, 2Th.3:8, Rev.4:8 (BL, §36, 13); ἡμέρας μέσης, at mid-day, Act.26:13; accusative durat., τ. ἡμέρας, Luk.21:37; ὅλην τὴν ἡ., Rom.8:36; ἐν ἡμέρα, Jhn.11:9, Rom.13:13; ἡμέρας ὁδός, a day's journey, Luk.2:44; ἡ. γίνεται, Lk 4:42 22:66; κλίνει, Luk.9:12, al.; metaphorically, Jhn.9:4, Rom.13:12, 1Th.5:4, 5 8, 2Pe.1:19.
__2. Of a civil day of 24 hours, incl. night: Mat.6:34, Mrk.6:21, Luk.13:14, al.; τρίτῃ ἡ., Mat.16:21; ἡμέρᾳ κ. ἡ. (cf. יוֹם בְּיוֹם, Est.3:4), 2Co.4:16; ὅλην τ. ἡ., Rom.8:36 10:21; pl., Jhn.2:12, Act.9:19, al.; ἡ. τῶν ἀζύμων, Act.12:3; τ. σαββάτου, Luk.13:14, 16; ἡ κυριάκη ἡ., Rev.1:10.
__3. In Messianic sense, of the last day: ἡ ἡ. (ἐκείνη, τ. κυρίου,  etc.), Mat.7:22, Luk.6:23, Rom.13:12, 1Co.1:8, 1Th.5:2, 2Th.2:2, 2Pe.3:10, al; by meton., as compared with the divine judgment on that day, ἡ. ἀνθρωπίνη, of a human tribunal, 1Co.4:3 (EV, man's judgment).
__4. As in Heb. (also in Gk. writers; Bl, §46, 9; M, Pr., 81), of time in general: Jhn.8:56 14:20, 2Co.6:2, Eph.6:13, 2Pe.3:18; pl. Act.15:7, Eph.5:16, Heb.10:32; πᾶσας τὰς ἡ. (cf. כָּל הַיָּמִים, Deu.4:40, al.; MM, Exp., xv), Mat.28:20; ἐλεύσονται ἡ. ὅταν (ὅτε), Mat.9:15, Mrk.2:20, Luk.5:35 17:22; αἱ ἡ., with genitive of person(s) (Gen.26:1, al.), Mat.2:1, Luk.1:5, Act.7:45, 1Pe.3:20; ἀρχ̀ ἡμερῶν, Heb.7:3.
(AS)

LSJ / STEPBible (TFLSJ)
ἡμέρα,
Epic dialect and Ionic dialect ἡμέρη [Refs [“IG” 12(5).1 (from Ios)]], Doric dialect ἀμέρα [Refs 8th c.BC+ [[prev. work = 8th-7th c.BC: Hesiodus Epicus “Opera et Dies”]5(1).213.43, +others, 1390.109, 1432.25, “Test.Epict.” 4.12, “Michel” 995 A 32, etc.]], Locrian dialect ἀμάρα [Refs [“IG” 9(1).334.42]] (aspirated perhaps only in Attic dialect and West Ionic dialect, compare ἐπάμερος [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus, etc., αὐθημερόν “IG” 7.235.18 (from Oropus)]], etc.; usually unaspirated in early Attic dialect Inscrr., [Refs [“IG” 12.49.6, +others]]; aspirated in codices even in dialects: original ἀμέρα probably took aspirate from ἑσπέρα): ἡ:—day, less frequently than ἦμαρ in [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Homerus Epicus, ἡ. ἥδε κακὸν φέρει 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 8.541, 13.828]]; τίς νύ μοι ἡ. ἥδ; [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 24.514; νύκτες τε καὶ ἡ. 14.93]]; μῆνές τε καὶ ἡ[Refs 8th c.BC+ [. [prev. work] 293; νοῦσοι ἐφ᾽ ἡμέρῃ αἳ δ᾽ ἐπὶ νυκτί 8th-7th c.BC: Hesiodus Epicus “Opera et Dies” 102]]; ἡ σήμερον ἡ., see at {σήμερον· ἅμα ἡμέρᾳ} or ἅμα τῇ ἡμέρᾳ at daybreak, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 6.3.6, 4th c.BC: Aeschines Orator 3.76; ἅμ᾽ ἡμέρῃ διαφωσκούσῃ 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 3.86]]; ἡ. διέλαμψεν, ἐξέλαμψεν, ὑπέφαινε, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Plutus” 744, “Pax” 304, 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 4.5.14]]; τῆς ἡ. ὀψέ late in the day, [Refs [[prev. author] “HG” 2.1.23.]]

__2
sometimes like Epic dialect ἦμαρ, with adjectives to describe a state or time of life, ἐπίπονος ἁ. a life of misery, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Trachiniae” 654 (Lyric poetry)]]; λυπρὰν ἄγειν ἡ. [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Hecuba” 364]]; ἐχθρὰ ἡ. [Refs [[prev. author] “Ph.” 540]]; παλαιὰ ἁ. old age, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Ajax” 623 (but θεία ἡ. [prev. author] “fragment” 950 is uncertain reading)]]; τερμία ἁ. [Refs [[prev. author] “Ant.” 1330 (Lyric poetry)]]; αἱ μακραὶ ἁμέραι length of days, [Refs [[prev. author] “OC” 1216 (Lyric poetry)]]; νέα ἁ. youth, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Ion” 720 (Lyric poetry)]]; so τῇ πρώτῃ ἡ. [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Rhetorica” 1389a24]]; ἐπὶ τῇ τελευταίᾳ ἡ. at the close of life,[Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. work] 1389b33, compare 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Tyrannus” 1529]]; ζοὴν βλέπουσιν ἡ. look life-like, [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [3rd c.BC: Herodas Mimographus 4.68.]]

__3
poetry for time, ἡ. κλίνει τε κἀνάγει πάλιν ἅπαντα τἀνθρώπεια [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Ajax” 131; ἐς τόδ᾽ ἡμέρας [prev. author] “OC” 1138: _plural_, ἐν ἡμέραις τινός]] in the days of.., [LXX.1Ch.4.41, etc.]; ἡ. ἀρχαῖαι[LXX.Psa.142(143).5.]

__4
birthday, [Refs 3rd c.AD+ [3rd c.AD(?): Diogenes Laertius 4.41.]]

__5
a fixed day, τακτὴ ἡ. [NT.Act.12.21]; ῥητὴ ἡ. [NT+1st c.BC+ [2nd c.AD: Lucianus Sophista “Alex.” 19; ἡ. ἔστησαν ἀρχαιρεσιῶν 1st c.BC: Dionysius Halicarnassensis 6.48, cf. NT.Act.17.31; ἡ. Κυρίου LXX.Joel.2.1, cf. NT.2Pet.3.12, etc.; ἡ. κρίσεως NT.Matt.10.15: so _absolutely_, ὑπὸ ἀνθρωπίνης ἡμέρας]] a human tribunal, [NT.1Cor.4.3; ἡμέραι καὶ ἀγῶνες “Jahresh.” 23 “Beibl.” 93 (Pamphyl.).]

__6
in plural, age, προβεβηκὼς ἐν ταῖς ἡ. [LXX+NT [NT.Luke.1.7, cf. LXX.Gen.47.8, etc.]]

__II
absolutely usages,

__II.1
genitive, τριῶν ἡμερέων within three days, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 2.115, compare 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 7.3]]; ἡμερῶν ὀλίγων within a few days, [Refs [[prev. author] 4.26, etc.]]; ἄλλης ἡ. another day, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Electra” 698]]; τῆς αὐτῆς ἡ. [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Isocrates Orator 4.87; μιᾶς ἀμέρας “IG” 5(1).213.43 (Sparta, 5th c.BC)]]; ἡμέρας by day, opposed to νυκτός, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Fragmenta” 65; οὔθ᾽ ἡμέρας οὔτε νυκτός 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Phaedrus” 240c]]; τοὺς.. τῆς ἡ. ἄρτους δ ¯ daily, [Refs 2nd c.BC+ [“UPZ” 47.21 (2nd c.BC)]]; δὶς τῆς ἡμέρης ἑκάστης twice every day, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 2.37]]; δίς τῆς ἡ. [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Comicus 207]]; πεντάκις τῆς ἡ. [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-3rd c.BC: Menander Comicus 326]]; κατεσθίω.. τῆς ἡ. πένθ᾽ ἡμιμέδιμνα five every day, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Pherecrates Comicus 1.]]

__II.2
_dative_, τῇδε θἠμέρᾳ,= σήμερον, (5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Tyrannus” 1283; τῇ τόθ᾽ ἡ [prev. author] “El.” 1134.

__II.3
_accusative_, πᾶσαν ἡ. any day, i.e. soon, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.111, 7.203]]; τὴν μὲν αὐτίχ᾽ ἡ. [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Coloneus” 433]]; ὅλην τὴν ἡ. [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Eupolis Comicus 233]]; τρίτην ἡ. ἥκων two days after one's arrival, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 8.23; οὐδεμίαν ἡ. ὑπεύθυνος εἶναί φημι 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 18.112]]; πέντε ἡμέρας during five days, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 8.103]]; τὰς ἡ. in the daytime, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 1.3.12]]; τὴν ἡ. daily, [LXX.Exo.29.38.]

__III
with Preps., μίαν ἀν᾽ ἁμέραν on one day, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “O.” 9.85]]; ἀνὰ πᾶσαν ἡ. every day, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 7.198]]; ἀφ᾽ ἡμέρας τῆς νῦν from this day, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Tyrannus” 351]]; but ἀφ᾽ ἡμέρας γίνεσθαι ἐν τῷ Μουσείῳ from early in the day, [Refs 2nd c.BC+ [2nd c.BC: Polybius Historicus 8.25.11: δι᾽ ἡμέρης, _Attic dialect_ -ρας]], the whole day long, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.97, 2.173, 5th c.BC: Pherecrates Comicus 64, 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Ranae” 260 (Lyric poetry)]]; διὰ τρίτης ἡ. every other day, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 2.37]]; διὰ πολλῶν ἡ. at a distance of many days, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 2.29; δι᾽ ἡμερῶν τινων 4th-3rd c.BC: Theophrastus Philosophus “Historia Plantarum” 4.3.6]]; εἰσ ἡμέραν yearly, [LXX.Judg.17.10]; ἐν ἡμέρῃ in a single day, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.126, compare 4th-3rd c.BC: Menander Comicus “Περικειρομένη” 377; ἐνἡ. μιᾷ 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Tyrannus” 615]]; τῇδ᾽ ἐν ἡ. [Refs [[prev. author] “OC” 1612]]; ἐν ἐκείνῃ τῇ ἡ. [NT.John.14.20]; ἐν ἑστέραισιν ἡ. [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Agamemnon” 1666]]; ἐν ὀκτὼ ἡ. [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Lysias Orator 20.10]]; but ἐν τρισὶν ἡ. within three days, [NT.John.2.19]; ἐξ ἡμέρας by day, οὔτε νυκτὸς οὔτ᾽ ἐξ ἡ. [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Electra” 780]]; ἡμέραν ἐξ ἡμέρας day after day, [NT+4th c.AD+ [4th c.AD: Heniochus Comicus 5.13, LXX.Gen.39.10, NT.2Pet.2.8 (but ἐξ ἡμερῶν εἰς ἡμέρας LXX.2Ch.21.15)]]; ἐπ᾽ ἡμέρην ἔχειν, ἐφ᾽ -ραν χρῆσθαι, sufficient for the day, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.32, 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 4.69; τὸ γὰρ βρότειον σπέρμ᾽ ἐφ᾽ ἡ. φρονεῖ 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Fragmenta - American Journal of Philology” 399; τῆς ἐφ᾽ ἡ. βορᾶς 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Electra” 429]]; but τοὐφ᾽ ἡμέραν day by day, [Refs [[prev. author] “Cyc.” 336: with _dative_, ἐπ᾽ ἡμέρῃ ἑκάστῃ (variant{-ρης -της})]] every day, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 5.117; ὁ ἥλιος νέος ἐφ᾽ ἡμέρῃ 1st c.AD(?): Heraclitus 6]]; καθ᾽ ἡμέραν by day, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Choephori” 818 (Lyric poetry)]]; καθ᾽ ἡ. τὴν νῦν to-day, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Coloneus” 3, “Aj.” 801]]; but καθ᾽ ἡ. commonly means day by day, [Refs [Inscriptiones Graecae 12.84.40, etc.]]; καθ᾽ ἡ. ἀεί [[Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus] “fragment” 1120.4: with _Article_, τὸν καθ᾽ ἡ. βίον [prev. author] “OC” 1364; ἡ καθ᾽ ἡ. ἀναγκαία τροφή 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 1.2; τὰ καθ᾽ ἡ. ἐπιτηδεύματα [prev. author] 2.37; τὸ καθ᾽ ἡ. ἀδεές [prev. author] 3.37, etc.]]; τὸ καθ᾽ ἡ. every day, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Equites” 1126 (Lyric poetry), etc.; also τὰ καθ᾽ ἑκάστην τὴν ἡ. ἐπιτηδεύματα 5th-6th c.BC: Isocrates Orator 4.78]]; μετ᾽ ἡμέρην in broad daylight, opposed to νυκτός, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 2.150, compare 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Plutus” 930]]; opposed to νύκτωρ, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aeschines Orator 3.77]]; μεθ᾽ ἡμέρας some days after, [LXX.Judg.15.1]; ἡμέρα παρ᾽ ἡμέραν γιγνομένη day following on day, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Antipho Orator 5.72]]; but παρ᾽ ἡμέραν every other day, [Refs 1st c.AD+ [1st c.AD: Dioscorides (Dioscurides) Medicus 3.137, 2nd c.AD: Lucianus Sophista “DDeor.” 24.2; παρ᾽ ἡ. ἄρχειν 1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus “Fabius Maximus” 15; καθ᾽ ἡμέραν εἰώθειν ὀργίζεσθαι, νῦν παρ᾽ ἡμέραν, εἶτα παρὰ δύο, εἶτα παρὰ τρεῖς 2nd c.AD: Arrianus Historicus “Epicteti Dissertationes” 2.18.13]]; πρὸ ἡμέρας before day-break, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-3rd c.BC: Diphilus Comicus 22]]; but πρὸ ἀμερᾶν δέκα ἤ κα μέλλωντι ἀναγινώσκεν [Refs [“GDI” 5040.42 (from Crete)]]; πρὸ ἡμερῶν ἑπτὰ εἰδυῶν Ὀκτωμβρίων [Refs 2nd c.BC+ [“SIG” 646.2 (Thisbe, 2nd c.BC)]]; γίγνεται, ἔστι πρὸς ἡμέραν, towards day, near day, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Historia Graeca (Hellenica)” 2.4.6, 5th c.BC: Lysias Orator 1.14]]; also, for the day, daily, [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd c.AD(?): Charito Scriptor Eroticus 4.2.]]

__IV
as proper name, the goddess of day, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th-7th c.BC: Hesiodus Epicus “Theogonia” 124.]]

__IV.2
see at {ἥμερος} [Refs [11.]]

ἡμέτερος,
Doric dialect ἁμέτ-, Aeolic dialect ἀμμέτ-, α, ον, (ἡμεῖς) our, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 2.374, etc.]]; εἰς ἡμέτερον (i.e. δῶμα) [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 2.55, 17.534; so ἡμέτερόνδε 8.39, 15.513]]; ἐφ᾽ ἡμέτερ[Refs 8th c.BC+ [' [prev. work] 88, 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 9.619; ἐν ἡμετέρου 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.35, 7.8]].; ἡ ἡ. (i.e. χώρα) [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 6.21, etc.]]; τὸ ἡ. our case, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Timaeus” 27d; τὸ ἡ. γέλωτ᾽ ἂν πάμπολυν ὄφλοι [prev. author] “Lg.” 778e, etc.]]; τὰ ἡ. φρονεῖν to take our part, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Historia Graeca (Hellenica)” 6.3.14, etc.]]; ἄνδρες ἡ. they are in our power, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 556d, compare 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 2.3.2]]; ἡ. κέρδη τῶν σοφῶν,= ἡμῶν τῶν σοφῶν, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Nubes” 1202]]; ἡμέτερον αὐτῶν [οἰκοδόμημα],= ἡμῶν αὐτῶν, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Gorgias” 514b]]; representing an objective genitive, τὸ ἡ. δέος fear of us, [NT+5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 1.77; εἰς τὴν ἡ. διδασκαλίαν NT.Rom.15.4.]]

__II
sometimes for ἐμός, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 11.562, +others, 3rd c.BC: Theocritus Poeta Bucolicus 2.31, etc.]]; τὰ ἡ. my property, [Refs 3rd c.AD+ [“PRyl.” 114.18 (3rd c.AD)]]; so in Imperial titles, as ἡ ἡ. ἡμερότης [Refs 6th c.AD+ [6th c.AD: Justinianus Imperator “Novellae” 115 “Pr.”]]

οὐκ ἔ. ὅπως οὐ in any case, necessarily, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Pax” 188; οὐκ ἔ. ὡς 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Meno” 76e, etc.]]; ἐ. ὅτε, ἔσθ᾽ ὅτε, sometimes, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “Fragmenta.” 180.2, 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Ajax” 56, 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 7.21, etc.]]

__A.V
ἦν is sometimes used with plural masculine and feminine, usually at the beginning of a sentence, there was, τῆς δ᾽ ἦν τρεῖς κεφαλαί [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th-7th c.BC: Hesiodus Epicus “Theogonia” 321; (but in ἦν δ᾽ ἐρῳδιοί τε πολλοί 5th c.BC: Epicharmus Comicus 46, compare 59, +others, it may be taken as _Doric dialect_ _3rd.pers._ _plural_)]]; ἦν δ᾽ ἀμφίπλεκτοι κλίμακες [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Trachiniae” 520 (Lyric poetry)]]; ἦν ἄρα κἀκεῖνοι ταλακάρδιοι epigram cited in [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aeschines Orator 3.184; less frequently ἔστι, ἔστι δὲ μεταξὺ.. ἑπτὰ στάδιοι 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.26, compare 7.34; ἔστι.. ἄρχοντές τε καὶ δῆμος 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 463a]]; before dual Nouns, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Vespae” 58, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Gorgias” 500d.]]

__A.VI
ἔστι impersonal, with infinitive, it is possible, ἔστι γὰρ ἀμφοτέροισιν ὀνείδεα μυθήσασθαι [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 20.246; ἔστι μὲν εὕδειν, ἔστι δὲ τερπομένοισιν ἀκούειν 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 15.392]]; εἴ τί πού ἐστι (i.e. πιθέσθαι)[Refs 5th c.BC+ [4.193; τοιάδε.. ἐστὶν ἀκοῦσαι 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Prometheus Vinctus” 1055 (_anapaest meter_); ἔστι τεκμήρια ὁρᾶν 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 3.2.13, compare 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Ranae” 1163, 4th c.BC: Aeschines Orator 3.105, 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 18.272, 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Ἀθηναίων Πολιτεία” 53.6, etc.]]; so in imperative, optative, and subjunctive, ἔστω ἀποφέρεσθαι τῷ βουλομένῳ [Refs 8th c.BC+ [“IG” 12.10.7; μυρία ἂν εἴη λέγειν 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Politicus” 271e; ὅπως ἂν ᾖ δρᾶν “IG” 2.1054.91: more frequently in _negative_ clauses, 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 6.267, etc.]]; followed by ὥστε with infinitive, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Philoctetes” 656]]: with accusative et infinitive, ἁδόντα δ᾽ εἴη με τοῖς ἀγαθοῖς ὁμιλεῖν [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “P.” 2.96; ἔστιν ἐκπεσεῖν ἀρχῆς Δία 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Prometheus Vinctus” 757]]: sometimes not impersonal in this sense, θάλασσα δ᾽ οὐκέτ᾽ ἦν ἰδεῖν [Refs [[prev. author] “Pers.” 419.]]

__A.VI.b
ἔστω in argument, let it be granted, ἔστω τοῦτο ἀληθὲς εἶναι [Refs 4th c.BC+ [1st c.BC: Dionysius Halicarnassensis “de Compositione Verborum” 25; ἔστω σοι τοῦθ᾽ οὕτως 1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus 2.987b; ἔστω εἶναί τινα τοιοῦτον 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator Chr.74.24.]]

__B
most frequently, to be, the Copula connecting the predicate with the Subject, both being in the same case: hence, signify, import, τὸ γὰρ εἴρειν λέγειν ἐστίν [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Cratylus” 398d]]; especially in the phrase τοῦτ᾽ ἔστι, hoc est; Σκαιόλαν, ὅπερ ἐστὶ Λαϊόν [Refs 1st c.AD+ [1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus “Publicola” 17: with numerals, τὰ δὶς πέντε δέκα ἐστίν]] twice five are ten, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Memorabilia” 4.4.7]]; εἶναί τις or τι, to be somebody, something, be of some consequence, see at {τι; οὐδὲν εἶναι} [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 562d, etc.]]

__B.2
periphrastic with the Participle to represent the finite Verb: with perfect participle once in [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Homerus Epicus, τετληότες εἰμέν, for τετλήκαμεν, 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 5.873]]; so in Trag. and Attic dialect, ἦν τεθνηκώς, for ἐτεθνήκει, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Agamemnon” 869]]; ἔσται δεδορκώς[Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. work] 1179; εἰμὶ γεγώς 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Ajax” 1299; πεφυκός ἐστι 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Aves” 1473; δεδρακότες εἰσίν 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 3.68; κατακεκονότες ἔσεσθε 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 7.6.36]]: with aorist participle, once in [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Homerus Epicus, βλήμενος ἦν 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 4.211]]; so προδείσας εἰμί, οὐ σιωπήσας ἔσε; [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Tyrannus” 90, 1146, compare 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Supplices” 460]]: with present participle, ἦν προκείμενον [Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. author] “Pers.” 371; φεύγων Ὀρέστης ἐστίν [prev. author] “Ch.” 136; εἴην οὐκ ἂν εὖ φρονῶν 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Ajax” 1330]]; τί δ᾽ ἐστί.. φέρο; [Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. author] “OT” 991, compare 274, 708; λέγων ἐστίν τις 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Hecuba” 1179; ἦν τίς σ᾽ ὑβρίζων [prev. author] “HF” 313; πόρρω ἤδη εἶ πορευόμενος 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Lysis” 204b; βαδίζων εἰμί 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Ranae” 36; frequently in 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus, ἦσαν ἱέντες 1.57, +others; even εἰσὶ διάφοροι ἐόντες 3.49 (assuming variant):]] — if the _Article_ is joined with the Part., the noun is made emphatic, Κᾶρές εἰσι οἱ καταδέξαντες the persons who showed her were Carians, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. author] 1.171; αὐτὸς ἦν ὁ μαρτυρῶν 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Eumenides” 798; δόλος ἦν ὁ φράσας 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Electra” 197 (_anapaest meter_).]]

__C
εἶναι is frequently modified in sense by the addition of adverbs, or the cases of Nouns without or with Preps.:

__C.I
εἶναι with adverbs, where the adverb often merely represents a Noun and stands as the predicate, ἅλις δέ οἱ ἦσαν ἄρουραι [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 14.122, etc.]]; ἀκέων, ἀκήν εἶναι, to be silent,[Refs 8th c.BC+ [4.22, 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 2.82; σῖγα πᾶς ἔστω λεώς 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Hecuba” 532; διαγνῶναι χαλεπῶς ἦν ἄνδρα ἕκαστον 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 7.424]]; ἀσφαλέως ἡ κομιδὴ ἔσται will go on safely, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 4.134]]; ἐγγύς, πόρρω εἶναι, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 6.88, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Protagoras” 356e: frequently _impersonal_ with words implying good or ill fortune, Κουρήτεσσι κακῶς ἦν]] it fared ill with them, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 9.551; εὖ γὰρ ἔσται 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Medea” 89, compare 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Plutus” 1188, etc.; ἡδέως ἂν αὐτοῖς εἴη 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 59.30.]]

__C.II
with genitive, to express descent or extraction, πατρὸς δ᾽ εἴμ᾽ ἀγαθοῖο [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 21.109; αἵματός εἰς ἀγαθοῖο 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 4.611, compare 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 3.71, 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 2.71, etc.; πόλεως μεγίστης εἶ 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 7.3.19.]]

__C.II.b
to express the material of which a thing is made, ἡ κρηπίς ἐστι λίθων μεγάλων consists of.., [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.93; τῆς πόλιος ἐούσης δύο φαρσέων [prev. work] 186]]; τοιούτων ἔργων ἐστὶ ἡ τυραννίς is made up of.., [Refs [[prev. author] 5.92]].ή, etc.

__C.II.c
to express the class to which a person or thing belongs, εἶ γὰρ τῶν φίλων you are one of them, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Plutus” 345; ἐτύγχανε βουλῆς ὤν 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 3.70; ὅσοι ἦσαν τῶν προτέρων στρατιωτῶν [prev. author] 7.44; Κριτίας τῶν τριάκοντα ὤν 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Memorabilia” 1.2.31]]; ἔστι τῶν αἰσχρῶν it is in the class of disgraceful things, i. e. it is disgraceful, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 2.2.]]

__C.II.d
to express that a thing belongs to another, Τροίαν Ἀχαιῶν οὖσαν [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Agamemnon” 269; τὸ πεδίον ἦν μέν κοτε Χορασμίων 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 3.117, etc.]]: hence, to be of the party of, ἦσαν.. τινὲς μὲν φιλίππου, τινὲς δὲ τοῦ βελτίστου [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 9.56, compare 37.53]]; to be de pendent upon, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Antigone” 737, etc.]]; to be at the mercy of, ἔστι τοῦ λέγοντος, ἢν φόβους λέγῃ [Refs [[prev. author] “OT” 917.]]

__C.II.e
to express one's duty, business, custom, nature, and the like, οὔτοι γυναικός ἐστι 'tis not a woman's part, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Agamemnon” 940; τὸ ἐπιτιμᾶν παντὸς εἶναι 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 1.16]]; τὸ δὲ ναυτικὸν τέχνης ἐστίν is matter of art, requires art, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 1.142, compare 83.]]

__C.II.f
in LXX, to be occupied about, ἦσαν τοῦ θύειν [LXX.2Ch.30.17]; ἔσεσθαι, with genitive, to be about to, ἐσόμεθα τοῦ σῶσαί σε [LXX.2Ki.10.11.]

__C.III
with the dative, ἐστί μοι I have, frequently in [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Homerus Epicus, etc.]]

__C.III.2
with two datives., σφίσι τε καὶ Ἀθηναίοισι εἶναι οὐδὲν πρῆγμα that they and the Athenians have nothing to do one with another, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 5.84; μηδὲν εἶναι σοὶ καὶ φιλίππῳ πρᾶγμα 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 18.283]]; more shortly, σοί τε καὶ τούτοισι πρήγμασι τί ἐστ; [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 5.33]]; τί τῷ νόμῳ καὶ τῇ βασάν; [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 29.36]]; τί ἐμοὶ καὶ σο; Latin quid tecum est mihi? [NT.Mark.5.7, etc.]; also ἐμοὶ οὐδὲν πρὸς τοὺς τοιούτους (i.e. ἐστίν) [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Isocrates Orator 4.12; ἐν οἷς πρὸς τοὺς ἐναντίους ἐστὶ τῷ δήμῳ 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 18.278]]; ἔσται αὐτῳ πρὸς τὸν θεόν, in tomb inscriptions, [Refs [“JHS” 18.113, etc.]]

__C.III.3
with ἄσμενος, βουλόμενος, etc., added, ἐμοὶ δέ κεν ἀσμένῳ εἴη 'twould be to my delight, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 14.108; οὐκ ἂν σφίσι βουλομένοις εἶναι 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 7.35; προσδεχομένῳ [prev. author] 6.46; θέλοντι 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Tyrannus” 1356 (Lyric poetry); ἡδομένοις 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Laches” 187c.]]

__C.IV
with Preps., εἶναι ἀπό τινος, ={εἶναί τινος}[Refs 5th c.BC+ [(above 11.a), 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Memorabilia” 1.6.9; εἰσὶν ἀπ᾽ ἐναντίων αὗται πραγμάτων 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Philebus” 12d]]; but εἶναι ἀπ᾽ οἴκου to be away from.., [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 1.99.]]

__C.IV.2
εἶναι ἔκ τινος to be sprung from, εἴμ᾽ ἐκ Παιονίης, Μυρμιδόνων ἔξ εἰμι, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 21.154, 24.397, etc.]]; ἔστιν ἐξ ἀνάγκης it is of necessity, i. e. necessary, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Sophista” 256d.]]

__C.IV.3
εἶναι ἐν.. to be in a certain state, ἐν εὐπαθείῃσι [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.22]]; ἐν ἀθυμία, etc., [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 6.46, etc.; ἐν ταραχαῖς 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 18.218]]; εἶναι ἐν ἀξιώματι to be in esteem, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 1.130]]; οἱ ἐν τέλεϊ ἐόντες those in office, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 3.18, etc.]]; but εἶναι ἐν τέχνῃ, ἐν φιλοσοφία to be engaged in.., [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Tyrannus” 562, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Phaedo” 59a.]]

__C.IV.3.b
ἐν σοί ἐστι it depends on thee, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 6.109, 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Philoctetes” 963; ἐν σοὶ γάρ ἐσμεν [prev. author] “OT” 314; so also ἐπί τινι [prev. author] “Ph.” 1003, 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 1.6.2, etc.]]

__C.IV.4
εἶναι διά.., much like{εἶναι ἐν}.., εἶναι διὰ φόβου, ={φοβεῖσθαι}, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 6.34]]; εἶναι δι᾽ ὄχλου, ={ὀχληρὸν εἶναι}, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. author] 1.73; εἶναι διὰ μόχθων 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 1.6.25]]; εἶναι δι᾽ αἰτίας, ={αἰτιᾶσθαι}, [Refs 1st c.BC+ [1st c.BC: Dionysius Halicarnassensis 1.70]]; Geometry texts, pass through, διὰ τᾶς ἑτέρας διαμέτρου ἐόντος τοῦ ἐπιπέδου [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [3rd c.BC: Archimedes Geometra “περὶ κωνοειδέων καὶ σφαιροειδέων” 20.]]

__C.IV.5
εἶναι ἐφ᾽ ἑαυτῆς to be by oneself, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 25.23]]; εἶναι ἐπὶ ὀνόματος to bear a name, [Refs [[prev. author] 39.21]]; εἶναι ἐπὶ τοῖς πράγμασιν to be engaged in.., [Refs [[prev. author] 2.12]]; εἶναι ἐπί τινα to be against him, [Refs [[prev. author] 6.33]]; εἶναι ἐφ᾽ ἑξήκοντα στάδια to reach sixty stadia, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 4.6.11]]; εἶναι ἐπὶ τὰς ἁφάς pass through the points of contact, [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd c.AD: Apollonius Biographus Perg. “Con.” 4.1]]; εἶναι ἐπί τινι, see above 3 b.

__C.IV.6
εἶναι πρός τινος to be in one's favour, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 4.10, 29, etc.]]; to suit, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 1.2.11, etc.]]; εἶναι πρός τινι engaged in, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Phaedo” 84c, 2nd-3rd c.AD: Philostratus Sophista “Vita Apollonii” 5.31]]; πρὸς τοῖς ἰδίοις mind one's own affairs, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Politica” 1309a6, “Ath.” 16.3; εἶναι πρὸς τὸ κωλύειν 2nd c.BC: Polybius Historicus 1.26.3]]; πρὸς τὸ πονεῖν[Refs 5th c.BC+ [Teles p.46 H.; εἶναι περί τι 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 3.5.7, etc.]]

__C.IV.7
εἶναι παρά τινι or τινα, = παρειναι, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. author] “Cyr.” 6.2.15, 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 8.140.ά]] (assuming variant).

__C.IV.8
εἶναι ὑπό τινα or τινι to be subject to.., [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Historia Graeca (Hellenica)” 5.2.17 (assuming variant), 6.2.4.]]

__C.IV.9
περὶ τούτων ἐστίν that is the question, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-3rd c.BC: Menander Comicus “Ἐπιτρέποντες” 30.]]

__C.IV.10
εἶναι ἀπό.., in Geometry texts, to be constructed upon, [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [3rd c.BC: Archimedes Geometra “περὶ σφαίρας καὶ κυλίνδρου” 2.9, “Con.Sph.” 7.]]

__D
ἐστί is very frequently omitted, mostly in the present indicative before certain predicates, as ἀνάγκη, ἄξιον, δυνατόν, εἰκός, ἕτοιμον, οἷόν τε, ῥᾴδιον, χρεών, etc., and after the neuter of Verbals in -τέος, and such forms as θαυμαστὸν ὅσον: less frequently with other persons and moods, εἰμί omitted, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Tyrannus” 92, “Aj.” 813]]; εἶ, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 4.206]]; ἐσμέν, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Antigone” 634]]; ἐστέ, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 10.463]]; εἰσί, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Tyrannus” 499 (Lyric poetry), “IG” 2.778 B]]; subjunctive ᾖ, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 14.376, 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Hippolytus” 659, 5th c.BC: Antipho Orator 5.32]]; optative εἴη, [Refs [“IG” 22.1183.12]]; imperfect ἦν, [Refs [[prev. work]2.778 B]]; future ἔσονται, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 14.394.]]

__E
the Inf. frequently seems redundant,

__E.1
in phrases implying power or will to do a thing, ἑκὼν εἶναι (see. ἑκών) κατὰ δύναμιν εἶναι [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Isaeus Orator 2.32; εἰς δύναμιν εἶναι 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Politicus” 300c]]; τὸ ἐπ᾽ ἐκείνοις εἶναι, quantum in illis esset, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 8.48, 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Historia Graeca (Hellenica)” 3.5.9, compare 5th c.BC: Lysias Orator 13.58; τὸ ἐπὶ σφᾶς εἶναι 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 4.28; τὸ κατὰ τοῦτον εἶναι 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 1.6.9; κατὰ τοῦτο εἶναι 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Protagoras” 317a]]; τὸ τήμερον, τὸ νῦν εἶναι, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [[prev. author] “Cra.” 396e, “La.” 201c, Theopomp. Comedy texts 98, Decrees cited in 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Ἀθηναίων Πολιτεία” 31.2, etc.]]

__E.2

deep_entry:
Abbott-Smith / STEPBible (TBESG)
ἐγώ, genitive, etc., ἐμοῦ, ἐμοί, ἐμέ (enclitic μου, μοι, με), pl. ἡμεῖς, -ῶν, -ῖν, -ᾶς,
of person(s) pron.
I.
__(a) The nom. is usually emphatic, when expressed as subjc, as in Mat.3:11, Mrk.1:8, Luk.3:16, al. But often there is no apparent emphasis, as Mat.10:16, Jhn.10:17; ἰδοὺ ἐ. (= Heb. הִנֵּנִי, cf. 1Ki.3:8), Act.9:10; ἐ. (like Heb. אֲנִי), I am, Jhn.1:23 (LXX), Act.7:32 (LXX).
__(b) The enclitic forms (see supr.) are used with nouns, adjectives, verbs, adverbs, where there is no emphasis: ἐν τ. πατρί μου, Jhn.14:20; μου τ. λόγους, Mat.7:24; ὀπίσω μου, Mat.3:11; ἰσχυρότερός μου, ib.; λέγει μοι, Rev.5:5; also with the prep. πρός, as Mrk.9:19, al. The full forms (ἐμοῦ, etc.) are used with the other prepositions, as δι᾽ ἐμοῦ, ἐν ἐμοί, εἰς ἐμέ, etc., also for emphasis, as Luk.10:16, Jhn.7:23, Mrk.14:7, al.
__(with) The genitive μου and ἡμῶν are often used for the poss. pronouns ἐμός, ἡμέτερος: τ. λαόν μου, Mat.2:6; μου τῂ ἀπιστιᾳ, Mrk.9:24.
__(d) τί ἐμοὶ καὶ σοί ( = Heb. מַה־לִי וָלָךְ, Jdg.11:12, al.), i.e. what have we in common: Mat.8:29, Mrk.1:24, 5:7, Luk.8:28, Jhn.2:4; τί γάρ μοι, 1Co.5:2.
__(e) The interchange of ἐγώ and ἡμεῖς, common in π., appears in Pauline Epp. (see M, Pr., 86f., M, Th., 131f.).
__(f) κἀγώ (= καὶ ἐγώ), and I, even I, I also: Mat.2:8, Luk.2:48, Jhn.6:56, Rom.3:7, 1Co.7:40, al.; κἀγώ . . . καί, both . . . and, Jhn.7:28.
(AS)

__II

Diehl, 23.7; ἐμεῖο “IG” 3.1337; μεθέν 5th c.BC: Sophron Comicus 20]]; Doric dialect ἐμέος, ἐμεῦς, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Epicharmus Comicus 144]]; Boeotian dialect ἐμοῦς [Refs 6th c.BC+ [6th c.BC: Corinna Lyrica 37; also ἐμῶς, ἐμίο, ἐμίω, ἐμίως 2nd c.AD: Apollonius Dyscolus Grammaticus “de Pronominibus;” 74.17:]] — _dative_ ἐμοί, enclitic μοι (which may be compared with Sanskrit genitive me in κλῦθί μοι [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 5.115, +others); ὅ μοι πόσις “Schwyzer” 683 (5th c.AD: Cypria)]]; Doric dialect ἐμίν [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Epicharmus Comicus 99, “AJA” 29.461 (Rhodian, 5th c.BC), 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Acharnenses” 733, 3rd c.BC: Theocritus Poeta Bucolicus 4.30]]; Tarentum dialect ἐμίνη [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [3rd c.BC: Rhinthon Comicus 13: _accusative_ ἐμέ]], enclitic μ; [Refs 5th c.AD+ [5th c.AD: Cypria μι “Inscription Cyprian dialect” 59,60 H.]]

__III
dual, nominative and accusative, νῶι, we two, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 5.34, etc.]]; accusative νῶιν Zenod.ad [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 8.377]]; Attic dialect νώ [Refs 8th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Phaedrus” 278b (also 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 5.219, 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 15.475); νῶε 5th-6th c.BC: Antimachus Colophonius Elegiacus et Epicus 39, 6th c.BC: Corinna Lyrica 5: _genitive_, _dative_ νῶι; νῷν 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Antigone” 3]]; νῶι dative, [Refs 5th c.AD+ [5th-6th c.AD: Orphica “Lithica” 773]]; νῶιν, ={ἡμῖν}, [Refs 4th c.AD+ [4th c.AD(?): Quintus Smyrnaeus Epicus 1.213, etc.]]

__IV

ἄμμων [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [[prev. work]74, 2nd c.AD: Apollonius Dyscolus Grammaticus “de Pronominibus;” 95.3]]; Doric dialect ἁμέων [Refs 7th c.BC+ [7th c.BC: Alcman Lyricus 66]]; ἁμῶν [[Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Epicharmus Comicus] 266, 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Lysistrata” 168, 3rd c.BC: Theocritus Poeta Bucolicus 2.158]]; ἄμμεσιν 7th-6th c.BC: Alcaeus Lyricus 100]]; Doric dialect also ἁμίν or ἇμιν, [Refs 7th c.BC+ [7th c.BC: Alcman Lyricus 77, 78, 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Eumenides” 347 (Lyric poetry), 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Lysistrata” 1081]]; deep_entry:
Abbott-Smith / STEPBible (TBESG)
ἥμισυς, -εια, -υ genitive, -ους (late, as in π., for cl., -εος Bl., § 8, 4; Mayser, 294), n. p1., ἡμίσια (Rec., cl., -εια),
[in LXX for חֵצִי, מַחֲצִית ;] half;
__1. as adj., agreeing in gender and number with the substantive following, τὰ ἡμίσια τ. ὑταρχόντων, Luk.19:8.
__2. As neut. subst., τὸ ἥμισυ, the half; ἥ. (anarth.), a half: with genitive, ἥ. καιροῦ, Rev.12:14; ἕως ἡμίσους τ. βασιλείας μου, Mrk.6:23; after a cardinal number, ἡμέρας τρεῖς κ. ἥμισυ, Rev.11:9, 11.†

ἥμῐσυς, εια, υ,
genitive ἡμίσεος [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 2.126, 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 2.78, 4.83, 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Oeconomicus” 18.8, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Symposium” 205e, “IG” 22.1612.267, 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 23.213, etc. (ἡμίσεως]] is sometimes a variant, as in [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus]] [same places], and is found in later writers, as [Refs 5th c.BC+ [1st c.AD: Dioscorides (Dioscurides) Medicus 2.70); also as _feminine_, 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 4.104]]; later contraction ἡμίσους [LXX+8th c.BC+ [1st c.BC: Dionysius Halicarnassensis 4.17, 1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus “Marius” 34, etc. (as _feminine_, LXX.1Ki.16.9): _nominative_ and _accusative_ _plural_ _masculine_, _Ionic dialect_ ἡμίσεες, -εας, 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 21.7, 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 9.51]], Attic dialect ἡμίσεις [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 3.20, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Theaetetus” 154c (ἡμίσεας is preferred by 2nd c.AD: Phrynichus Atticista “Praeparatio Sophistica” p.73B.): _neuter_ _plural_ ἡμίσεα 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 4.16, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 438c, later ἡμίση 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 36.36 (codex S), +others, “IG” 22.1678.23, 4th-3rd c.BC: Theophrastus Philosophus “Characteres” 30.16, “IG” 12 (5).872.107 (from Tenos), “SIG” 2588.4(Delos, 2nd c.BC)]], etc.: Ionic dialect feminine ἡμίσεᾰ [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 5.111 (hyperion. -σέη 2nd c.AD: Lucianus Sophista “Syr.D.” 14]]), accusative plural -έας [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 8.27, also _accusative_ _sing._ ἡμίσεαν “IG” 2.1055.16, 1059.14, _genitive_ ἡμισέας 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Meno” 83c]]: ἥμυσυς (assim.), [Refs 5th c.BC+ [“Rev.Phil.” 54.192 (Erythrae, 5th c.BC), “IG” 22.43 A 45 (4th c.BC), “PEleph.” 20.40 (4th c.BC), “IG” 11(2).161 A 23(Delos, 3rd c.BC), “UPZ” 54.6 (2nd c.BC)]], etc.: neuter ἥμισον, τό, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [“Berl.Sitzb.” 1927.8 (_Locrian dialect_, 5th c.BC), “SIG” 1011.7 (Chalcedon, 3rd-2nd c.BC), [prev. work]671 A 13 (Delph., 2nd c.BC), “BGU” 183.41 (1st c.AD): _plural_ ἥμισα “SIG” 56.7 (Argos, 5th c.BC)]]; also ἥμισσον, τό, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [[prev. work]306.14 (4th c.AD(?): Arcadius Grammaticus, 4th c.BC), 1009.20 (Ephesus, 3rd-2nd c.BC): _plural_ ἥμισσα [prev. work] 240 P (Delph., 4th c.BC)]]: accusative plural τοὺς ἡμίσους [Refs [“Not.Arch.” 4.20 (Cyrene, Aug.)]]:—half,

__I
as adjective, ἡμίσεες λαοί half the people, ἡ. δ᾽ ἄρα λαοὶ ἐρητύοντο.. ἡ. δ᾽ ἀναβάντες ἐλαύνομεν [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 3.155 {ἡμισύτριτον}, compare 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 21.7 (elsewhere 8th c.BC: Homerus Epicus uses only _neuter_ ἥμισυ]] as substantive (see.[Refs 5th c.BC+ [below 11)); τοὺς ἡμίσεας ἀποστέλλειν 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 9.51, compare 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 3.20, 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 2.16, etc.]]; ἥμισυς λόγος half the tale, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Eumenides” 428 (λόγου codex _middle_)]]; τὸ ἥμισυ τεῖχος [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 2.78; ὁ ἥ. ἀριθμός 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Leges” 946a: with _genitive_, like a _comparative_, τὸ ὕψος ἥμισυ ἐτελέσθη οὗ διενοεῖτο]] half of what he intended, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 1.93: _metaphorically_, οὐδ᾽ ἂν ἥμισυς ἑαυτοῦ γένοιτο πρὸς ἀρετήν 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Leges” 647d (οὐ δι᾽ ἥμισυν stands for οὐ διήμ]]. 'half-and-half', [Refs [[prev. work] 806c).]]

__I.2
in Prose also with the substantive in genitive and giving its gender and number to ἥμισυς, τῶν νήσων τὰς ἡμισέας [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 2.10; τῶν ἀνδραπόδων τὰ ἡμίσεα [prev. author] 6.23]]; αἱ ἡμίσειαι τῶν νεῶν half of the ships, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 8.8; οἱ ἡμίσεις τῶν ἄρτων 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 4.5.4; ὁ ἥμισυς τοῦ ἀριθμοῦ 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Phaedo” 104a; τοῦ χρόνου 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 20.8: _absolutely_, οἱ ἡ]]. half of them, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 3.20.]]

__II

deep_entry:
Abbott-Smith / STEPBible (TBESG)
ἐγώ, genitive, etc., ἐμοῦ, ἐμοί, ἐμέ (enclitic μου, μοι, με), pl. ἡμεῖς, -ῶν, -ῖν, -ᾶς,
of person(s) pron.
I.
__(a) The nom. is usually emphatic, when expressed as subjc, as in Mat.3:11, Mrk.1:8, Luk.3:16, al. But often there is no apparent emphasis, as Mat.10:16, Jhn.10:17; ἰδοὺ ἐ. (= Heb. הִנֵּנִי, cf. 1Ki.3:8), Act.9:10; ἐ. (like Heb. אֲנִי), I am, Jhn.1:23 (LXX), Act.7:32 (LXX).
__(b) The enclitic forms (see supr.) are used with nouns, adjectives, verbs, adverbs, where there is no emphasis: ἐν τ. πατρί μου, Jhn.14:20; μου τ. λόγους, Mat.7:24; ὀπίσω μου, Mat.3:11; ἰσχυρότερός μου, ib.; λέγει μοι, Rev.5:5; also with the prep. πρός, as Mrk.9:19, al. The full forms (ἐμοῦ, etc.) are used with the other prepositions, as δι᾽ ἐμοῦ, ἐν ἐμοί, εἰς ἐμέ, etc., also for emphasis, as Luk.10:16, Jhn.7:23, Mrk.14:7, al.
__(with) The genitive μου and ἡμῶν are often used for the poss. pronouns ἐμός, ἡμέτερος: τ. λαόν μου, Mat.2:6; μου τῂ ἀπιστιᾳ, Mrk.9:24.
__(d) τί ἐμοὶ καὶ σοί ( = Heb. מַה־לִי וָלָךְ, Jdg.11:12, al.), i.e. what have we in common: Mat.8:29, Mrk.1:24, 5:7, Luk.8:28, Jhn.2:4; τί γάρ μοι, 1Co.5:2.
__(e) The interchange of ἐγώ and ἡμεῖς, common in π., appears in Pauline Epp. (see M, Pr., 86f., M, Th., 131f.).
__(f) κἀγώ (= καὶ ἐγώ), and I, even I, I also: Mat.2:8, Luk.2:48, Jhn.6:56, Rom.3:7, 1Co.7:40, al.; κἀγώ . . . καί, both . . . and, Jhn.7:28.
(AS)

deep_entry:
Abbott-Smith / STEPBible (TBESG)
εἰμί,
with various uses and significations, like the English verb to be.
__I. As substantive verb.
__1. Of persons and things, to be, exist: Act.17:28, Jhn.1:1, 8:58, 17:5, al; ὁ ὢν καὶ ὁ ἦν (for past ptcp.), Rev.1:4, 8, 4:8, 11:17, 16:5 (see Swete, Ap., 5; M, Pr., 228); τὰ (μὴ) ὄντα, Rom.4:17, 1Co.1:28.
__2. Of times, events, etc., to be, happen, take place: Mat.24:3, Mrk.14:2, 15:42, Luk.21:23, Jhn.4:6, 23, 5:10, al.
__3. to be present, be in a place, have come: Mat.2:13, 15, Mrk.1:45, 5:21, 15:40, Luk.1:80, 5:29, Jhn.7:30, al.; before εἰς, Mrk.2:1; before  ἐκ, (ἐξ), Mat.1:20, 21:25, Mrk.11:30, Jhn.3:31, al.
__4. Impers.,  ἔστι, ἦν, etc.;
__(a) there is (Fr. il y a), was, etc.: Mat.16:28, Luk.16:19, Jhn.3:1, 5:2, Rom.3:10, al.; with dative (of the possessor; Bl., §37, 3), Mat.16:22, Luk.1:7, Jhn.18.10, Rom.9:2, al.;  ἔστιν ὅς, ὅστις (chiefly in pl), Mat.16:28, 19:2, Mrk.9:1, al.;
__(b) with inf., = ἔξεστιν (which see), it is possible: Heb.9:5, 1Co.11:20, RV (but see ICC, in l.).
__II. As copula uniting subject and predicate.
__1. Expressing simply identity or equivalence: Mat.5:13, 14:15, Luk.1:18, 19, Jhn.1:1, 4:19, Rev.3:9, al. mult.
__2. Explicative, as in parable, figure, type, etc.: Mat.13:19, 1Co.9:2, 10:4, 11:25, Gal.4:24, Rev.17:15, al.; ταῦτ᾽ ἔστιν, Mat.27:46, Mrk.7:2, Rom.7:18 al.; ὅ ἐστιν, Mrk.3:17, Col.1:24, Heb.7:2, al.; akin to this is the sacramental usage: Mat.26:26-28, Mrk.14:22, 24, Luk.22:19, 1Co.11:24 (see ICC on Mk, I Co, ll. with; DB, iii, 148 f.).
__3. C. genitive: qual., etc., Mrk.5:42, Luk.3:23, 1Co.14:33, Heb.12:11, al.; part., 1Ti.1:20, 2Ti.1:15; poss., Mat.5:3, 10, Mrk.12:7, Luk.4:7; of service or partisanship, Rom.8:9, 1Co.1:12, 2Co.10:7, 2Ti.2:19.
__4. C. dative (BL, §37, 3): Act.1:8, 9:15, Rom.4:12, 1Co.1:18, 2:14, Rev.21:7, al.
__5. C. ptcp., as a periphrasis for the simple verb (Bl., §62, 1, 2; M, Pr., 225 ff.);
__(a) with ptcp. pf. (cl.): Mat.10:30, Luk.9:32, Jhn.3:24, Act.21:35, 1Co.15:19, al;
__(b) with ptcp. pr. (esp. in impf., as in Heb. and Aram.; Dalman, Words, 35 f.), Mat.7:29, Mrk.1:22, Luk.4:31, 14:1, Act.1:10, al. mult., id. for imper. (M, Pr., 180f., 182f.), with ellipsis of εἰμί, Rom.12:9, 10, Heb.13:5, al.;
__(with) with ptcp. aor. (cl), Luk.23:9.
__6. Seq. εἰς (cf. Heb. הָיָה לְ), a vernac. usage (M, Pr., 71): Mat.19:5, Mrk.10:8, Heb.8:10, al.
__7. C. adv.: Mat.19:20, Mrk.4:26, Luk.18:11, al.
__8. Ellipses;
__(a) of the copula (Bl., §30, 3): Mat.8:29, 24:32, Jhn.21:22, 23, Heb.6:4, al.;
__(b) of the predicate: ἐγώ εἰμί, Mat.14:27, Mrk.6:50, al.; absol. (cf. Deu.32:39; אֲנִי הוּא), Mrk.13:6, Jhn.4:26, al. (cf. ἄπ-, ἔν-, πάρ-, συμ-πάρ-, σύν-ειμι).
(AS)
