ἐ. ὅπῃ, ἔσθ᾽ ὅπου, somehow, somewhere, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Protagoras” 331d, 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Eumenides” 517, 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Tyrannus” 448, etc.]]; in questions expecting a negative answer, ἐ. ὁπόθεν, ὅπω; [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Philebus” 35a, “R.” 493e, etc.; οὐ γάρ ἐσθ᾽ ὅπως 5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “Fragmenta.” 61, compare 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 7.102, 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Agamemnon” 620]]; οὐκ ἔ. ὅπως οὐ in any case, necessarily, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Pax” 188; οὐκ ἔ. ὡς 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Meno” 76e, etc.]]; ἐ. ὅτε, ἔσθ᾽ ὅτε, sometimes, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “Fragmenta.” 180.2, 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Ajax” 56, 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 7.21, etc.]]

__A.V
ἦν is sometimes used with plural masculine and feminine, usually at the beginning of a sentence, there was, τῆς δ᾽ ἦν τρεῖς κεφαλαί [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th-7th c.BC: Hesiodus Epicus “Theogonia” 321; (but in ἦν δ᾽ ἐρῳδιοί τε πολλοί 5th c.BC: Epicharmus Comicus 46, compare 59, +others, it may be taken as _Doric dialect_ _3rd.pers._ _plural_)]]; ἦν δ᾽ ἀμφίπλεκτοι κλίμακες [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Trachiniae” 520 (Lyric poetry)]]; ἦν ἄρα κἀκεῖνοι ταλακάρδιοι epigram cited in [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aeschines Orator 3.184; less frequently ἔστι, ἔστι δὲ μεταξὺ.. ἑπτὰ στάδιοι 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.26, compare 7.34; ἔστι.. ἄρχοντές τε καὶ δῆμος 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 463a]]; before dual Nouns, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Vespae” 58, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Gorgias” 500d.]]

__A.VI
ἔστι impersonal, with infinitive, it is possible, ἔστι γὰρ ἀμφοτέροισιν ὀνείδεα μυθήσασθαι [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 20.246; ἔστι μὲν εὕδειν, ἔστι δὲ τερπομένοισιν ἀκούειν 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 15.392]]; εἴ τί πού ἐστι (i.e. πιθέσθαι)[Refs 5th c.BC+ [4.193; τοιάδε.. ἐστὶν ἀκοῦσαι 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Prometheus Vinctus” 1055 (_anapaest meter_); ἔστι τεκμήρια ὁρᾶν 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 3.2.13, compare 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Ranae” 1163, 4th c.BC: Aeschines Orator 3.105, 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 18.272, 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Ἀθηναίων Πολιτεία” 53.6, etc.]]; so in imperative, optative, and subjunctive, ἔστω ἀποφέρεσθαι τῷ βουλομένῳ [Refs 8th c.BC+ [“IG” 12.10.7; μυρία ἂν εἴη λέγειν 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Politicus” 271e; ὅπως ἂν ᾖ δρᾶν “IG” 2.1054.91: more frequently in _negative_ clauses, 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 6.267, etc.]]; followed by ὥστε with infinitive, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Philoctetes” 656]]: with accusative et infinitive, ἁδόντα δ᾽ εἴη με τοῖς ἀγαθοῖς ὁμιλεῖν [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “P.” 2.96; ἔστιν ἐκπεσεῖν ἀρχῆς Δία 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Prometheus Vinctus” 757]]: sometimes not impersonal in this sense, θάλασσα δ᾽ οὐκέτ᾽ ἦν ἰδεῖν [Refs [[prev. author] “Pers.” 419.]]

__A.VI.b
ἔστω in argument, let it be granted, ἔστω τοῦτο ἀληθὲς εἶναι [Refs 4th c.BC+ [1st c.BC: Dionysius Halicarnassensis “de Compositione Verborum” 25; ἔστω σοι τοῦθ᾽ οὕτως 1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus 2.987b; ἔστω εἶναί τινα τοιοῦτον 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator Chr.74.24.]]

__B
most frequently, to be, the Copula connecting the predicate with the Subject, both being in the same case: hence, signify, import, τὸ γὰρ εἴρειν λέγειν ἐστίν [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Cratylus” 398d]]; especially in the phrase τοῦτ᾽ ἔστι, hoc est; Σκαιόλαν, ὅπερ ἐστὶ Λαϊόν [Refs 1st c.AD+ [1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus “Publicola” 17: with numerals, τὰ δὶς πέντε δέκα ἐστίν]] twice five are ten, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Memorabilia” 4.4.7]]; εἶναί τις or τι, to be somebody, something, be of some consequence, see at {τι; οὐδὲν εἶναι} [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 562d, etc.]]

__B.2
periphrastic with the Participle to represent the finite Verb: with perfect participle once in [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Homerus Epicus, τετληότες εἰμέν, for τετλήκαμεν, 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 5.873]]; so in Trag. and Attic dialect, ἦν τεθνηκώς, for ἐτεθνήκει, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Agamemnon” 869]]; ἔσται δεδορκώς[Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. work] 1179; εἰμὶ γεγώς 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Ajax” 1299; πεφυκός ἐστι 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Aves” 1473; δεδρακότες εἰσίν 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 3.68; κατακεκονότες ἔσεσθε 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 7.6.36]]: with aorist participle, once in [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Homerus Epicus, βλήμενος ἦν 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 4.211]]; so προδείσας εἰμί, οὐ σιωπήσας ἔσε; [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Tyrannus” 90, 1146, compare 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Supplices” 460]]: with present participle, ἦν προκείμενον [Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. author] “Pers.” 371; φεύγων Ὀρέστης ἐστίν [prev. author] “Ch.” 136; εἴην οὐκ ἂν εὖ φρονῶν 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Ajax” 1330]]; τί δ᾽ ἐστί.. φέρο; [Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. author] “OT” 991, compare 274, 708; λέγων ἐστίν τις 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Hecuba” 1179; ἦν τίς σ᾽ ὑβρίζων [prev. author] “HF” 313; πόρρω ἤδη εἶ πορευόμενος 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Lysis” 204b; βαδίζων εἰμί 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Ranae” 36; frequently in 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus, ἦσαν ἱέντες 1.57, +others; even εἰσὶ διάφοροι ἐόντες 3.49 (assuming variant):]] — if the _Article_ is joined with the Part., the noun is made emphatic, Κᾶρές εἰσι οἱ καταδέξαντες the persons who showed her were Carians, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. author] 1.171; αὐτὸς ἦν ὁ μαρτυρῶν 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Eumenides” 798; δόλος ἦν ὁ φράσας 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Electra” 197 (_anapaest meter_).]]

__C
εἶναι is frequently modified in sense by the addition of adverbs, or the cases of Nouns without or with Preps.:

__C.I
εἶναι with adverbs, where the adverb often merely represents a Noun and stands as the predicate, ἅλις δέ οἱ ἦσαν ἄρουραι [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 14.122, etc.]]; ἀκέων, ἀκήν εἶναι, to be silent,[Refs 8th c.BC+ [4.22, 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 2.82; σῖγα πᾶς ἔστω λεώς 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Hecuba” 532; διαγνῶναι χαλεπῶς ἦν ἄνδρα ἕκαστον 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 7.424]]; ἀσφαλέως ἡ κομιδὴ ἔσται will go on safely, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 4.134]]; ἐγγύς, πόρρω εἶναι, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 6.88, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Protagoras” 356e: frequently _impersonal_ with words implying good or ill fortune, Κουρήτεσσι κακῶς ἦν]] it fared ill with them, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 9.551; εὖ γὰρ ἔσται 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Medea” 89, compare 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Plutus” 1188, etc.; ἡδέως ἂν αὐτοῖς εἴη 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 59.30.]]

__C.II
with genitive, to express descent or extraction, πατρὸς δ᾽ εἴμ᾽ ἀγαθοῖο [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 21.109; αἵματός εἰς ἀγαθοῖο 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 4.611, compare 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 3.71, 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 2.71, etc.; πόλεως μεγίστης εἶ 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 7.3.19.]]

__C.II.b
to express the material of which a thing is made, ἡ κρηπίς ἐστι λίθων μεγάλων consists of.., [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.93; τῆς πόλιος ἐούσης δύο φαρσέων [prev. work] 186]]; τοιούτων ἔργων ἐστὶ ἡ τυραννίς is made up of.., [Refs [[prev. author] 5.92]].ή, etc.

__C.II.c
to express the class to which a person or thing belongs, εἶ γὰρ τῶν φίλων you are one of them, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Plutus” 345; ἐτύγχανε βουλῆς ὤν 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 3.70; ὅσοι ἦσαν τῶν προτέρων στρατιωτῶν [prev. author] 7.44; Κριτίας τῶν τριάκοντα ὤν 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Memorabilia” 1.2.31]]; ἔστι τῶν αἰσχρῶν it is in the class of disgraceful things, i. e. it is disgraceful, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 2.2.]]

__C.II.d
to express that a thing belongs to another, Τροίαν Ἀχαιῶν οὖσαν [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Agamemnon” 269; τὸ πεδίον ἦν μέν κοτε Χορασμίων 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 3.117, etc.]]: hence, to be of the party of, ἦσαν.. τινὲς μὲν φιλίππου, τινὲς δὲ τοῦ βελτίστου [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 9.56, compare 37.53]]; to be de pendent upon, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Antigone” 737, etc.]]; to be at the mercy of, ἔστι τοῦ λέγοντος, ἢν φόβους λέγῃ [Refs [[prev. author] “OT” 917.]]

__C.II.e
to express one's duty, business, custom, nature, and the like, οὔτοι γυναικός ἐστι 'tis not a woman's part, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Agamemnon” 940; τὸ ἐπιτιμᾶν παντὸς εἶναι 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 1.16]]; τὸ δὲ ναυτικὸν τέχνης ἐστίν is matter of art, requires art, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 1.142, compare 83.]]

__C.II.f
in LXX, to be occupied about, ἦσαν τοῦ θύειν [LXX.2Ch.30.17]; ἔσεσθαι, with genitive, to be about to, ἐσόμεθα τοῦ σῶσαί σε [LXX.2Ki.10.11.]

__C.III
with the dative, ἐστί μοι I have, frequently in [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Homerus Epicus, etc.]]

__C.III.2
with two datives., σφίσι τε καὶ Ἀθηναίοισι εἶναι οὐδὲν πρῆγμα that they and the Athenians have nothing to do one with another, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 5.84; μηδὲν εἶναι σοὶ καὶ φιλίππῳ πρᾶγμα 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 18.283]]; more shortly, σοί τε καὶ τούτοισι πρήγμασι τί ἐστ; [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 5.33]]; τί τῷ νόμῳ καὶ τῇ βασάν; [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 29.36]]; τί ἐμοὶ καὶ σο; Latin quid tecum est mihi? [NT.Mark.5.7, etc.]; also ἐμοὶ οὐδὲν πρὸς τοὺς τοιούτους (i.e. ἐστίν) [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Isocrates Orator 4.12; ἐν οἷς πρὸς τοὺς ἐναντίους ἐστὶ τῷ δήμῳ 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 18.278]]; ἔσται αὐτῳ πρὸς τὸν θεόν, in tomb inscriptions, [Refs [“JHS” 18.113, etc.]]

__C.III.3
with ἄσμενος, βουλόμενος, etc., added, ἐμοὶ δέ κεν ἀσμένῳ εἴη 'twould be to my delight, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 14.108; οὐκ ἂν σφίσι βουλομένοις εἶναι 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 7.35; προσδεχομένῳ [prev. author] 6.46; θέλοντι 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Tyrannus” 1356 (Lyric poetry); ἡδομένοις 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Laches” 187c.]]

__C.IV
with Preps., εἶναι ἀπό τινος, ={εἶναί τινος}[Refs 5th c.BC+ [(above 11.a), 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Memorabilia” 1.6.9; εἰσὶν ἀπ᾽ ἐναντίων αὗται πραγμάτων 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Philebus” 12d]]; but εἶναι ἀπ᾽ οἴκου to be away from.., [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 1.99.]]

__C.IV.2
εἶναι ἔκ τινος to be sprung from, εἴμ᾽ ἐκ Παιονίης, Μυρμιδόνων ἔξ εἰμι, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 21.154, 24.397, etc.]]; ἔστιν ἐξ ἀνάγκης it is of necessity, i. e. necessary, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Sophista” 256d.]]

__C.IV.3
εἶναι ἐν.. to be in a certain state, ἐν εὐπαθείῃσι [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.22]]; ἐν ἀθυμία, etc., [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 6.46, etc.; ἐν ταραχαῖς 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 18.218]]; εἶναι ἐν ἀξιώματι to be in esteem, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 1.130]]; οἱ ἐν τέλεϊ ἐόντες those in office, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 3.18, etc.]]; but εἶναι ἐν τέχνῃ, ἐν φιλοσοφία to be engaged in.., [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Tyrannus” 562, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Phaedo” 59a.]]

__C.IV.3.b
ἐν σοί ἐστι it depends on thee, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 6.109, 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Philoctetes” 963; ἐν σοὶ γάρ ἐσμεν [prev. author] “OT” 314; so also ἐπί τινι [prev. author] “Ph.” 1003, 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 1.6.2, etc.]]

__C.IV.4
εἶναι διά.., much like{εἶναι ἐν}.., εἶναι διὰ φόβου, ={φοβεῖσθαι}, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 6.34]]; εἶναι δι᾽ ὄχλου, ={ὀχληρὸν εἶναι}, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. author] 1.73; εἶναι διὰ μόχθων 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 1.6.25]]; εἶναι δι᾽ αἰτίας, ={αἰτιᾶσθαι}, [Refs 1st c.BC+ [1st c.BC: Dionysius Halicarnassensis 1.70]]; Geometry texts, pass through, διὰ τᾶς ἑτέρας διαμέτρου ἐόντος τοῦ ἐπιπέδου [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [3rd c.BC: Archimedes Geometra “περὶ κωνοειδέων καὶ σφαιροειδέων” 20.]]

__C.IV.5
εἶναι ἐφ᾽ ἑαυτῆς to be by oneself, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 25.23]]; εἶναι ἐπὶ ὀνόματος to bear a name, [Refs [[prev. author] 39.21]]; εἶναι ἐπὶ τοῖς πράγμασιν to be engaged in.., [Refs [[prev. author] 2.12]]; εἶναι ἐπί τινα to be against him, [Refs [[prev. author] 6.33]]; εἶναι ἐφ᾽ ἑξήκοντα στάδια to reach sixty stadia, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 4.6.11]]; εἶναι ἐπὶ τὰς ἁφάς pass through the points of contact, [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd c.AD: Apollonius Biographus Perg. “Con.” 4.1]]; εἶναι ἐπί τινι, see above 3 b.

__C.IV.6
εἶναι πρός τινος to be in one's favour, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 4.10, 29, etc.]]; to suit, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 1.2.11, etc.]]; εἶναι πρός τινι engaged in, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Phaedo” 84c, 2nd-3rd c.AD: Philostratus Sophista “Vita Apollonii” 5.31]]; πρὸς τοῖς ἰδίοις mind one's own affairs, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Politica” 1309a6, “Ath.” 16.3; εἶναι πρὸς τὸ κωλύειν 2nd c.BC: Polybius Historicus 1.26.3]]; πρὸς τὸ πονεῖν[Refs 5th c.BC+ [Teles p.46 H.; εἶναι περί τι 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 3.5.7, etc.]]

__C.IV.7
εἶναι παρά τινι or τινα, = παρειναι, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. author] “Cyr.” 6.2.15, 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 8.140.ά]] (assuming variant).

__C.IV.8
εἶναι ὑπό τινα or τινι to be subject to.., [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Historia Graeca (Hellenica)” 5.2.17 (assuming variant), 6.2.4.]]

__C.IV.9
περὶ τούτων ἐστίν that is the question, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-3rd c.BC: Menander Comicus “Ἐπιτρέποντες” 30.]]

__C.IV.10
εἶναι ἀπό.., in Geometry texts, to be constructed upon, [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [3rd c.BC: Archimedes Geometra “περὶ σφαίρας καὶ κυλίνδρου” 2.9, “Con.Sph.” 7.]]

__D
ἐστί is very frequently omitted, mostly in the present indicative before certain predicates, as ἀνάγκη, ἄξιον, δυνατόν, εἰκός, ἕτοιμον, οἷόν τε, ῥᾴδιον, χρεών, etc., and after the neuter of Verbals in -τέος, and such forms as θαυμαστὸν ὅσον: less frequently with other persons and moods, εἰμί omitted, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Tyrannus” 92, “Aj.” 813]]; εἶ, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 4.206]]; ἐσμέν, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Antigone” 634]]; ἐστέ, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 10.463]]; εἰσί, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Tyrannus” 499 (Lyric poetry), “IG” 2.778 B]]; subjunctive ᾖ, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 14.376, 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Hippolytus” 659, 5th c.BC: Antipho Orator 5.32]]; optative εἴη, [Refs [“IG” 22.1183.12]]; imperfect ἦν, [Refs [[prev. work]2.778 B]]; future ἔσονται, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 14.394.]]

__E
the Inf. frequently seems redundant,

__E.1

__b
ὁ -άζων, with or without λόγος, a fallacy, [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [3rd c.BC: Chrysippus Stoicus 2.8 (_plural_), 2nd c.AD: Gellius, Aulus Grammaticus Latinus 1.2.4 (_plural_).]]

__II
transitive, bring to rest, ἡσυχάσας τὼ δύο εἴδη, τὸ τρίτον δὲ κινήσας [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 572a.]]

__II.b
absolutely, impose silence, [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd-3rd c.AD: Dio Cassius Historicus 69.6.]]

leave unspoken, ἃ χρὴ λέγειν [Refs 1st c.AD+ [1st c.AD: Philo Judaeus 1.254, compare 2.268; τὰς ἀπειλάς 1st c.AD: Josephus Historicus “Antiquitates Judaicae” 7.7.3]].

ἥσσων,
ἧσσον, genitive ονος; Attic dialect ἥττων, Ionic dialect ἥσσων (not ἕσσων) [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus (see. below), 3rd c.AD: Democritus Epigrammaticus 50, 5th c.BC: Hippocrates Medicus “περὶ τῶν ἐν κεφαλη—ͅ τρωμάτων” 2: formed from ἦκα (properly ἠσσ-, compare ἤκιστος), but in sense _comparative_ of κακός, μικρός]]:

__I
with genitive person, inferior; especially in force, weaker, αἴθ᾽ ὅσον ἥ. εἰμὶ τόσον σέο φέρτερος εἴην [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 16.722]]; of horses, [Refs [23.322, +others]]; ῥώμῃ ἥσσονες τῶν Περσέων [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 8 113, compare 9.62; γυναικῶν ἥσσονες 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Antigone” 680; Κύπριδος 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Andromache” 631]]; ἔς τι in a thing, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 3.102: with]]infinitive modi, ἥσς. τινὸς θέειν not so good at running, [Refs [[prev. work] 105]]; οὐδενὸς ἥσς. γνῶναι second to none in judging, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 2.60]]; ἱππεύειν ἥττ. τῶν ἡλίκων inferior to them in riding, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 1.3.15.]]

__I.2
absolutely, οἱ ἥσς. the weaker party, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Supplices” 203, 489]]; οὐχ ἥσσους γενέσθαι to have the best of it, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 4.72]]; τὸ λαμβάνειν τὰ τῶν ἡττ. deep_entry:
Abbott-Smith / STEPBible (TBESG)
1. as Substantive Verb, to be, to exist , οὐκ ἔσθ᾽ οὗτος ἀνήρ, οὐδ᾽ ἔσσεται (Odyssey by Homer); τεθνηῶτος, μηδ᾽ ἔτ᾽ ἐόντος (Odyssey by Homer); οὐκέτ᾽ ἔστι he is no more , (Euripides); θεοὶ αἰὲν ἐόντες (Iliad by Homer); ἐσσόμενοι posterity, (Iliad by Homer); ζώντων καὶ ὄντων Ἀθηναίων (Demosthenes Orator):—;so of cities, etc., ὄλωλεν, οὐδ᾽ ἔτ᾽ ἔστι Τροία (compare Troja fuit) , (Euripides)
2. of things, to be, exist , εἰ ἔστιν ἀληθέως [ ἡ τράπεζα] (Herdotus Historicus); ἕως ἂν ὁ πόλεμος ἦι so long as it last , (Thucydides)
3. to be , opposite to appearing to be , as esse  to videri , τὸν ἐόντα λόγον the true  story, (Herdotus Historicus); τὰ ὄντα ἀπαγγέλλειν (Thucydides); τῶι ὄντι, Lat. revera, in reality, in fact, (Plato Philosophus)
4. followed by the Relative, οὐκ ἔστιν ὅς, no one , (Iliad by Homer), etc.; εἰσὶν οἵ, Lat. sunt qui, (Thucydides), etc.; ἐστὶν ἅ some things , (Thucydides); also ἔστιν οἵ, for εἰσὶν οἵ, (Herdotus Historicus), etc.:—;so withrelat. Particles, ἔστιν ἔνθα, Lat. est ubi, (Xenophon Historicus), etc.; ἔστιν ὅπη, ἔσθ᾽ ὅπου, somewhere , or somehow , (Plato Philosophus), etc.; ἔστιν ὅπως in some manner , (Herdotus Historicus), etc.; ἔστιν ὅτε, ἔσθ᾽ ὅτε, sometimes , (Sophocles Tragicus), etc.
5. ἔστι impersonal, with infinitive, like πάρεστι, it is possible , (Homer), attic
6. to be , Copula connecting predicate with subject, both being in the same case, (Homer), etc.
7. sometimes εἶναι with Part. represents finite Verb, ἦν τεθνηκώς, for ἐτεθνήκει, (Aeschulus Tragicus); πεφυκός ἐστι = πέφυκε, (Aristophanes Comicus)
8. the Inf. is redundant in some phrases, ἑκὼν εἶναι (see. ἑκών II); τὸ ἐπ᾽ ἐκείνοις εἶναι quantum in illis esset , (Thucydides); τὸ σύμπαν εἶναι (Herdotus Historicus); τὸ νῦν εἶναι (Plato Philosophus), etc. (ML)

__2.b
honour, admire, worship, once in [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Homerus Epicus (but compare θαυμαίνω), οὔτε τι θαυμάζειν.. οὔτ᾽ ἀγάασθαι 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 16.203; frequently later, as 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 3.80, 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Septem contra Thebas” 772 (Lyric poetry), 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Ajax” 1093, etc.; θ. τύμβον πατρός 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Electra” 519; μηδὲ τὸν πλοῦτον μηδὲ τὴν δόξαν τὴν τούτων θαυμάζετε, ἀλλ᾽ ὑμᾶς αὐτούς 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 21.210]]; μηδὲν θ., Latin nil admirari, [Refs 1st c.AD+ [1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus 2.44b]]; technically, of the attendance of small birds on the owl, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Historia Animalium” 609a15]]; θ. πρόσωπον to show respect to a person, i.e. comply with their request, [LXX.Gen.19.21]; θ. τινά τινος for a thing, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 6.36; θ. τινὰ ἐπὶ σοφίᾳ 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Theaetetus” 161c, 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Memorabilia” 1.4.2; ἀπὸ τοῦ σώματος τὸν νεανίσκον 1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus “Romulus” 7]]:— passive, to be admired, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 7.204; ὑπό τινος [prev. author] 3.82; ἔν τινι 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 2.39; τῶν προγεγενημένων μᾶλλον -θησόμεθα 5th-6th c.BC: Isocrates Orator 6.105]]; τοὺς ὁμοίως τεθαυμασμένους [ποιητάς] [Refs 5th c.BC+ [1st c.BC: Philodemus Philosophus “περὶ ποιημάτων” 5.31; διά τι 5th-6th c.BC: Isocrates Orator 4.59: with _genitive_, τῆς ῥώμης 2nd-3rd c.AD: Philostratus Sophista “Vita Apollonii” 7.42; χάρις δ᾽ ἀφ᾽ ἡμῶν ὀλομένων -άζεται 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Septem contra Thebas” 703]]; τὰ εἰκότα θ. to receive proper marks of respect, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 1.38; θ. τινί [prev. author] 7.63.]]

[prev. work] 383)]]; σὺν θ. εἰρημένον [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.86, compare 3.153; σὺν θ. εἰπεῖν 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Protagoras” 317b]]: so in plural, σύν γε θεοῖσιν [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 24.430; οὔ τοι ἄνευ θεοῦ 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 2.372]]; οὐ θεῶν ἄτερ pi.[Refs 8th c.BC+ [“P.” 5.76; ἐκ θεόφι 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 17.101]]; ὑπὲρ θεόν against his will,[Refs 4th c.BC+ [17.327; ἂν θ. θέλῃ 2nd c.AD: Alexander Rhetor 231; θ. θέλοντος 4th-3rd c.BC: Menander Comicus “Μονόστιχοι - Fragmenta Comicorum Graecorum” 671: in _plural_, ἂν θεοὶ θέλωσιν 2nd c.AD: Alexander Rhetor 247]]; θεῶν συνεθελόντων, βουλομένων, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “de Equitum magistro” 9.8, 2nd c.AD: Lucianus Sophista “Macr.” 29; εἰ ὀρθῶς ἢ μή, θ. οἶδε 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Phaedrus” 266b, compare “R.” 517b, etc.; in oaths, θ. ἴστω 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Coloneus” 522 (Lyric poetry), etc.; πρὸς θεῶν 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 5.49, 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 1.15, etc.: τοὺς θεούς σοι]]bless you! good heavens! for heaven's sake! [Refs 8th c.BC+ [2nd c.AD: Marcus Antoninus Imperator 7.17, 2nd c.AD: Arrianus Historicus “Epicteti Dissertationes” 2.19.15, +others; τὸν θ. σοι [prev. work] 3.7.19, +others: qualified by τις, 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 9.142, etc.; οὐκ ἄνευ θεῶν τινος 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Persae” 164 (troch.), 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Bacchae” 764; κατὰ θεόν τινα [prev. author] “IA” 411, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Euthydemus” 272e; κατὰ θεόν πως εἰρημένα [prev. author] “Lg.” 682a]]: doubled in poets, θεὸν θεόν τις ἀγλαϊζέτω [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Bacchylides Lyricus 3.21, compare 5th c.BC: Diagoras Lyricus 1; θεοὶ θεοὶ τῶν ἀδίκων μέλουσι 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Hercules Furens” 772, compare 2nd c.AD: Pausanias Grammaticus “fragment” 203]]; θεοί (Cretan dialect θιοί) as an opening formula in Inscrr. (i.e. τύχην ἀγαθὴν διδοῖεν), [Refs [“Leg.Gort.” 1.1, “IG” 12.52, etc.: _sing._, θ. τύχη [prev. work]5(2)]].1, etc.: in Prose also with the Article, ὁ θ. πάντων ἂν εἴη αἴτιος [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 379c, compare “Lg.” 716c, etc.]]; τὰ πρὸς τοὺς θ., τὰ παρὰ τῶν θ., [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Memorabilia” 1.3.1, 2.6.8.]]

__b

__d

(i.e. Ποσειδῶν) [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Historia Graeca (Hellenica)” 4.7.4]]; of the sun, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 2.24, 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Persae” 502, 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Alcestis” 722]]; δύνοντος τοῦ θ. [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd c.AD: Appianus Historicus “Bella Civilia” 4.79]]; the weather, τί δοκεῖ τὰ τοῦ θεο; [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-3rd c.BC: Theophrastus Philosophus “Characteres” 25.2.]]

__e

__f
θεός (i.e. Ἥλιος), name of the 9th τόπος, Rhetor.[Refs [[prev. work]163, etc.]]

__2

__3
as title of rulers, θεῶν ἀδελφῶν (i.e. Ptolemy Il and Arsinoe), [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [3rd c.BC: Herodas Mimographus 1.30, etc.; Πτολεμαῖος ὑπάρχων θεὸς ἐκ θεοῦ καὶ θεᾶς “OGI” 90.10 (Rosetta, 2nd c.BC)]]; Ἀντίοχος ὅτῳ θεὸς ἐπώνυμον γίγνεται [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd c.AD: Appianus Historicus “Συριακή” 65]]; θεὸς ἐκ θεοῦ, of Augustus, [Refs 1st c.BC+ [“OGI” 655.2 (Egypt, 1st c.BC); θ. ἡμῶν καὶ δεσπότης “IPE” 4.71 (Cherson., 2nd c.AD).]]

θερᾰπ-εία,
Ionic dialect θερᾰπ-ηΐη (θερᾰπ-είη [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Hippocrates Medicus “περὶ ἄρθρων ἐμβολῆς” 80, +others)]], ἡ, service, attendance:

__I
of persons, θ. τῶν θεῶν service paid to the gods, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Euthyphro” 13d, compare 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Electra” 744 (Lyric poetry); θεῶν καὶ ἡρώων θεραπεῖαι 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 427b, etc.; ἡ περὶ τοὺς θεοὺς θ. 5th-6th c.BC: Isocrates Orator 11.24]]; ἀγυιάτιδες θ. worship of Apollo Agyieus, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Ion” 187; τὴν θ. ἀποδιδόναι τοῖς θεοῖς 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Politica” 1329a32; θ. τῆς μήνιδος 4th c.AD: Julianus Imperator “Orationes” 5.159b: _absolutely_, πᾶσαν θ. ὡς ἰσόθεος θεραπευόμενος 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Phaedrus” 255a, compare 5th c.BC: Antipho Orator 4.2.4]]; of parents, γονέων θεραπείας καὶ τιμάς [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Leges” 886c, compare 5th c.BC: Gorgias Rhetor et Sophista “fragment” 6 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator]]; of children, nurture, care, μικροὺς παῖδας θεραπείας δεομένους [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Lysias Orator 13.45; θ. καὶ ἐσθής 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Memorabilia” 3.11.4]]; θ. σώματος, ψυχῆς, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Gorgias” 464b, “La.” 185e.]]

__I.2
service done to gain favour, paying court, θ. τοῦ κοινοῦ καὶ τῶν αἰεὶ προεστώτων [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 3.11; ἐν θεραπείᾳ ἔχειν πολλῇ [prev. author] 1.55; πάσῃ θεραπείᾳ θεραπεύειν τινά 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Historia Graeca (Hellenica)” 2.3.14; θεραπείαις προσαγαγέσθαι 5th-6th c.BC: Isocrates Orator 3.22; τῇ θ. ψυχαγωγούμενος 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 59.55.]]

__II
medical or surgical treatment or cure, χειρός, ποδός, Hp.[same place]; αἱ ὑπὸ τῶν ἰατρῶν θ. αἱ διὰ καύσεων γιγνόμεναι cures by cautery, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Protagoras” 354a]]; ἡ ἐκ τῶν γραμμάτων θ. treatment secundum artem, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Politica” 1287a40, compare 2nd c.AD: Galenus Medicus 1.400, etc.; τῶν καμνόντων 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Protagoras” 345a, compare 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 2.51, 1st c.BC: Philodemus Gadarensis Epigrammaticus “Ir.” p.21 W.; τοῦ σώματος [prev. author] “Lib.” p.19 O., “Vita Philonidis Epicurei” p.9 C.]]; healing, θεραπείας ἐπιτυχών [Refs [“Sammelb.” 1537b]]: in plural, cures, ἰατρὸς ποιεῖ -είας [Refs [“POxy.” 1r. 13.]]

__III
of animals, care, tendance, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Euthyphro” 13a, 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Historia Animalium” 578a7 (_plural_).]]

__III.2
of plants, cultivation, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Theaetetus” 149e, 4th-3rd c.BC: Theophrastus Philosophus “Historia Plantarum” 2.2.12.]]

__III.3
maintenance or repairs of temples, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [“SIG” 1106.49 (Cos, 4th-3rd c.BC), 1102.8 (2nd c.BC).]]

__III.4
preparation of fat for medical use, [Refs 1st c.AD+ [1st c.AD: Dioscorides (Dioscurides) Medicus 2.76.]]

in collective sense, body of attendants, retinue, [LXX+5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.199, 5.21, 7.184, LXX.Gen.45.16; σὺν ἱππικῇ θ. 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 4.6.1; ὁ ἐπὶ τῆς θ. τεταγμένος 2nd c.BC: Polybius Historicus 4.87.5.]]

(in form diminutive of θήρ), wild animal, especially of such as are hunted, μάλα γὰρ μέγα θηρίον ἦεν, of a stag, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 10.171, 180 (never in 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad”)]]; in Trag. only in Satyric drama, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Ichn.” 147 (uncertain in 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Fragmenta - American Journal of Philology” 26): used in Prose for θήρ, 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 1.2.7, 5th-6th c.BC: Isocrates Orator 12.163, etc.]]; of the spider's prey, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Historia Animalium” 623a27]]; frequently of elephants, [Refs 2nd c.BC+ [2nd c.BC: Polybius Historicus 11.1.12, +others]]: plural, beasts, opposed to men, birds, and fishes, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [“hymnus ad Venerem” 4, 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 3.108.]]

soul, spirit, as the principle of life, feeling and thought, especially of strong feeling and passion (rightly derived from θύω (B) by [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Cratylus” 419e ἀπὸ τῆς θύσεως καὶ ζέσεως τῆς ψυχῆς):]]

__I
in physical sense, breath, life, θ. ἀπηύρα, ἀφελέσθαι, ἐξαίνυσθαι, ὀλέσαι, frequently in [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Homerus Epicus, 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 6.17, 5.852, 155, 1.205: with double _accusative_, ἄμφω θ. ἀπηύρα 6.17; ἐπεί κε.. ῥεθέων ἐκ θ. ἕληται 22.68; λίπε δ᾽ ὀστέα θ. 12.386]]; ἀπὸ δ᾽ ἔπτατο θ. [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 10.163; ὀλίγος δ᾽ ἔτι θ. ἐνῆεν 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 1.593; μόγις δ᾽ ἐσαγείρετο θυμόν 21.417; ἄψορρόν οἱ θ. ἐνὶ στήθεσσιν ἀγέρθη 4.152; θυμοῦ καὶ ψυχῆς κεκαδών 11.334]]; of animals, [Refs [3.294, 12.150]], etc.: less frequently in Trag., [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Agamemnon” 1388, 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Bacchae” 620 (troch.).]]

__I.2
spirit, strength, τείρετο δ᾽ ἀνδρῶν θ. ὑπ᾽ εἰρεσίης [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 10.78; ἐν δέ τε θ. τείρεθ᾽ ὁμοῦ καμάτῳ τε καὶ ἱδρῷ 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 17.744.]]

__I.3
πάτασσε δὲ θ. ἑκάστου each man's heart beat high, [Refs [23.370, compare 7.216.]]

__II
soul, as shown by the feelings and passions; and so,

__II.1
desire or inclination, especially desire for meat and drink, appetite, πιέειν ὅτε θ. ἀνώγοι [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 4.263; πλησάμενος.. θυμὸν ἐδητύος ἠδὲ ποτῆτος 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 17.603: generally, τά με θ. ἐνὶ στήθεσσι κελεύει 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 7.68]]; βαλέειν δέ ἑ ἵετο θ[Refs [. 8.301; αἲ γάρ με μένος καὶ θ. ἀνείη 22.346]]; θ. ἐποτρύνῃ [τινά] [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 9.139]]; θ. ἐπέσσυταί τινι, ἐφορμᾶται, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 1.173, 13.73]]; ἤθελε θυμῷ he wished in his heart or with all his heart, [Refs [16.255, 21.65; ἵετο θυμῷ 2.589]]; so later θυμῷ βουλόμενοι wishing with all their heart, [Refs 7th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 5.49; [ὄσσα ϝ] οι θ. κε θέλῃ γένεσθαι 7th-6th c.BC: Sappho Lyrica “Papyrus fragments” in E. Diehl, 1.3; θυμὸς ὥρμα 5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “O.” 3.25, compare 38; θυμὸς ἡδονὴν φέρει 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Electra” 286; ὧν ἐρᾷ θυμός 3rd c.BC: Herodas Mimographus 7.61; τῶν σφι θ. ἦν μάλιστα 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.1; ἄλλως σφι θ. ἐγένετο θεήσασθαι τὸν πόλεμον [prev. author] 8.116, etc.: with Verb omitted, σὲ γάρ μοι θῦμος ὔμνην 7th-6th c.BC: Alcaeus Lyricus 5]]; ἄρχ᾽ αὐτὸς ὥς σοι θ. [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Electra” 1319]]; ὅπου ὑμῖν θ. [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 3.1.37; βῆξαι θυμός ἐγγίνεται 5th c.BC: Hippocrates Medicus “προγνωστικόν” 8.]]

__II.2
mind, temper, will, θ. πρόφρων, ἵλαος, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 8.39, 9.639; θ. ὑπερφίαλος καὶ ἀπηνής, νηλέα θ. ἔχοντας, σιδήρεος θ., 15.94, 19.229, 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 5.191]]; ἕνα θ. ἔχειν to be of one mind, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 15.710, etc.; οὐδὲ λύκοι τε καὶ ἄρνες ὁμόφρονα θ. ἔχουσιν 22.263; ἕτερος δέ με θ. ἔρυκε 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 9.302]]; ἐμὸν θ. ἔπειθεν[Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. work] 33; θωπείας κολακικάς, αἳ.. τοὺς θ. ποιοῦσιν κηρίνους 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Leges” 633d.]]

__II.3
spirit, courage, μένος καὶ θ. [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 20.174; θ. ἐνὶ στήθεσσι λαβεῖν 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 10.461]]; πᾶσιν δὲ παραὶ ποσὶ κάππεσε θ. [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 15.280]]; ψῦχρος ἔγεντο θ., of doves, [Refs 7th c.BC+ [7th-6th c.BC: Sappho Lyrica 16; θ. ἔχειν ἀγαθόν 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.120; θ. οὐκ ἀπώλεσεν 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Electra” 26; ὁ θυμὸς εὐθὺς ἦν Ἀμυνίας 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Equites” 570]]; ἴωμεν ῥώμῃ καὶ θυμῷ ἐπί.. [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 4.2.21; φρονήματός τε καὶ θυμοῦ ἐμπίπλασθαι 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 411c: so in Philos., opposed to λόγος, ἐπιθυμία, [prev. work] 440b, +others,compare 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Politica” 1328a7, 1327b24, 1st c.BC: Philodemus Gadarensis Epigrammaticus “Mus.” p.26K., etc.]]; personified, Passion, Emotion, opposed to Λογισμός, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-3rd c.BC: Cleanthes Stoicus 1.129.]]

__II.4
the seat of anger, χωόμενον κατὰ θυμόν [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 1.429; νεμεσιζέσθω ἐνὶ θυμῷ 17.254; θυμὸν ἐχώσατο 16.616, etc.]]: hence, anger, wrath, δάμασον θυμόν [Refs [9.496]]; εἴξας ᾧ θυμῷ[Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. work] 598; θυμὸς μέγας ἐστὶ.. βασιλήων 2.196; θ. ὀξύς 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Coloneus” 1193; θ. κρείσσων τῶν ἐμῶν βουλευμάτων 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Medea” 1079, etc.]]; θυμῷ falsa lectio for{θυμοῦ} in [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Antigone” 718; οἱ τῷ θ. πραχθέντες φόνοι 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Leges” 867b]]; opposed to λογισμός, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 2.11, etc.]]; ἐπανάγειν τὸν θ. [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 7.160; ἐκτείνειν 5th-6th c.BC: Andocides Orator 3.31; καταθέσθαι 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Vespae” 567; δακεῖν [prev. author] “Nu.” 1369; θυμῷ χρᾶσθαι 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.137, +others; ὀργῆς καὶ θυμοῦ μεστοί 5th-6th c.BC: Isocrates Orator 12.81 (so τὴν ὀργὴν καὶ τὸν θ., i.e. the outward manifestation of ὀ., 1st c.BC: Philodemus Gadarensis Epigrammaticus “Ir.” p.90W.)]]; of horses, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “de Equitandi ratione” 9.2: _plural_ (not earlier than 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus, _falsa lectio_ in 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Ajax” 718 (Lyric poetry))]], fits of anger, passions, περὶ φόβων τε καὶ θυμῶν [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Philebus” 40e; οἵ τε θ. καὶ αἱ κολάσεις [prev. author] “Prt.” 323e, compare 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Rhetorica” 1390a11.]]

__II.5
the heart, as the seat of the emotions, especially joy or grief, χαῖρε, γήθησε δὲ θυμῷ, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 14.156, 7.189; θ. ἐνὶ στήθεσσι γεγήθει 13.494; μιν ἄχος κραδίην καὶ θ. ἵκανεν 2.171; ἄχνυτο θ. 14.39, etc.]]; δόκησε δ᾽ ἄρα σφίσι θ. ὣς ἔμεν ὡς εἰ.. they felt as glad at heart as if.., [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 10.415]]; μηδ᾽ ὀνίαισι δάμνα.. θ. [Refs 7th c.BC+ [7th-6th c.BC: Sappho Lyrica 1.4]]; of fear, δέος ἔμπεσε θυμῷ [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 17.625, compare 8.138]]; of love, τὴν ἐκ θυμοῦ φίλεον [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [9.343; ἐκ θυμοῦ στέργοισα 3rd c.BC: Theocritus Poeta Bucolicus 17.130]]; ἐμῷ κεχαρισμένε θυμῷ my heart's beloved, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 5.243]]; reversely, ἀπὸ θ. μᾶλλον ἐμοὶ ἔσεαι wilt be alien from my heart, [Refs [1.562]]; ἐκ θ. πεσέειν, i.e. to lose thy favour,[Refs 5th c.BC+ [23.595; ἔρωτι θυμὸν ἐκπλαγεῖσα 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Medea” 8; ἐκ θ. κλαῦσαι 4th-3rd c.BC: Philetas 11.]]

__II.6
mind, soul, as the seat of thought, ταῦθ᾽ ὥρμαινε κατὰ φρένα καὶ κατὰ θ. [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 1.193, etc.; ᾔδεε γὰρ κατὰ θ. 2.409, compare 4.163, etc.]]; φράζετο θυμῷ [Refs 5th c.BC+ [16.646; ἐν θ. ἐβάλοντο ἔπος 15.566; τοὺς λόγους θυμῷ βάλε 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Prometheus Vinctus” 706; εἰς θ. βαλεῖν τι 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Tyrannus” 975]]; οὐκ ἐς θ. φέρω I bring him not into my mind or thoughts, [Refs [[prev. author] “El.” 1347.]]

(θυμός) [in LXX (chiefly in pass.) for חָרָה, אַף חָרָה hith., etc. ;] (no act. in Attic.);
pass. (and mid.),

LSJ / STEPBible (TFLSJ)
θῡμόω,
make angry, provoke, [LXX.Hos.12.14(15)]: once in Trag., ὥστε θυμῶσαι φρένας [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Supplices” 581.]]

__II
middle and passive, 2nd pers. singular θυμοῖ [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Ranae” 584]]: future -ώσομαι[Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Agamemnon” 1069]], -ωθήσομαι [LXX+1st c.BC+ [LXX.Job.21.4, 1st c.BC: Philodemus Gadarensis Epigrammaticus “Ir.” p.89 W]].: aorist ἐθυμωσάμην [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Helena” 1343 (Lyric poetry), more frequently ἐθυμώθην 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 3.1, +others]]; participle -θείς[Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Phoenissae” 461, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Leges” 931b]]: perfect infinitive τεθυμῶσθαι [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 3.52, 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Fragmenta - American Journal of Philology” 478, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Epistulae” 346a]]:—to be wroth or angry, absolutely, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 3.1, 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Ag.” [same place], 2nd c.AD: Soranus Medicus 1.88, etc.; θυμοῦ δι᾽ ὀργῆς ἥτις ἀγριωτάτη 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Tyrannus” 344]]; εἰς ἔριν θ. [Refs [[prev. author] “Aj.” 1018]]; of animals, to be wild, restive, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. author] “Ant.” 477, 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “de Equitandi ratione” 1.10]]; θυμοῦσθαι εἰς κέρας vent fury with the horns, Virgil's irasci in cornua, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Bacchae” 743; compare ἀοιδὸς ἐς κέρας τεθύμωται 3rd c.BC: Callimachus Epicus “Iambi” 1.321]]; τὸ θυμούμενον passion, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Antipho Orator 2.3.3, 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 7.68]]; θυμοῦσθαί τινι to be angry with one, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Eumenides” 733, 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Trachiniae” 543, 1230, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Protagoras” 324a; ἔς τινα 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 3.52; περί τινος 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Agamemnon” 1368 (probably to be read instead of μυθοῦσθαι); βοῦς πρὸς τὸν ἐλαύνοντα -ωθείς 1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus “Dio” 38; σοι θυγατέρος -ούμενος 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Orestes” 751 (troch.): with _dative_ _of things_, τῇ ξυντυχίᾳ 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Ranae” 1006.]]

Abbott-Smith / STEPBible (TBESG)
θύρα, -ας, ἡ
[in LXX chiefly for פֶּתַח, also for דַּל, דֶּלֶת, etc. ;]
a door: κλείειν (ἀποκ-) τὴν θ., Mat.6:6, Luk.13:25; pass., Mat.25:10, Luk.11:7, Jhn.20:19, 26, Act.21:30; ἀνοίγειν, Act.5:19; pass., Act.16:26-27; κρούειν, Act.12:13; διὰ τῆς θ., Jhn.10:1-2; πρὸς τὴν θ., Mrk.1:33 11:4 (WH om. τήν), Act.3:2; τὰ πρὸς τὴν θ., the space by the door, Mrk.2:2; πρὸς τῇ θ., Jhn.18:16; ἐπὶ τῇ θ, Act.5:9; πρὸ τῆς θ., Act.12:6; ἐπὶ τῶν θ., Act.5:23; ἡ θ. τ. μνημείου, Mat.27:60, Mrk.15:46 16:3. Metaphorical, of Christ, ἡ θ. τ. προβάτων, Jhn.10:7, 9; of the Kingdom of Heaven, Luk.13:24; of opportunities, θ. πίστεως, Act.14:27; θ. μεγάλη, 1Co.16:9; θ. τ. λόγου, Col.4:3; θ. ἀνεῳγμένη (ἠνεῳγ-), 2Co.2:12, Rev.3:8 4:1; of Christ, ἑστηκὼς ἐπὶ τὴν θ. καὶ κρούων, Rev.3:20; of his second coming, ἐπὶ θύραις εἶναι, Mat.24:33, Mrk.13:29; πρὸ θυρῶν ἑστηκέναι, Jas.5:9.†
(AS)

LSJ / STEPBible (TFLSJ)
θύρα [ῠ],
Ionic dialect θύρη, ἡ, Ionic dialect genitive plural θυρέων [Refs 7th c.BC+ [7th c.BC: Archilochus Lyricus 127, 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.9]]:— door, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 24.317, etc.]]: frequently in plural of double or folding doors, θ. δικλίδες [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 17.267; θ. φαειναί 6.19, +others; θυρῶν ζεῦγος καινῶν “IG” 12.313.123, compare 4.1488.25(Epid.)]]; ἡ δεξιὰ θ. the right valve, [Refs [[prev. work]22.1457.16]]; θ. μονόθυρος [Refs [[prev. work]1627.418]]; θύραι λίθιναι (including the framework) [Refs [[prev. work] 12.372.195]]; θύραι αὔλειαι, see at {αὔλειο; ἡ θ. ἡ εἰς τὸν κῆπον φέρονσα} [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 47.53, compare κηπαῖος 11]]; rarely for πύλαι, gates, [Refs 1st c.AD+ [1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus “Cat.Mi.” 65]]; of the carceres in the Roman circus, barriers, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [Tab.Defix.Aud. 187.59. —Phrases: προσθεῖναι τὰς θ., προστιθέναι τὴν θ., 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 3.78, 5th c.BC: Lysias Orator 1.13; ἐπισπάσαι 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Historia Graeca (Hellenica)” 6.4.36; κλείειν 4th c.BC: Aristopho Comicus 7, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Protagoras” 314d; ἐφέλκεσθαι 2nd c.AD: Lucianus Sophista “Am.” 16]]; τὴν θ. βαλανοῦν, μοχλοῦν, bar the door, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Fragmenta” 251, 369]]; θύραν κόπτειν, πατάσσειν, κρούειν, knock, rap at the door, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. author] “Nu.” 132, “Ra.” 38, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Protagoras” 310b]]; ἀράττειν, ἐπαράξαι, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Ecclesiazusae” 977, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Protagoras” 314d]]; τὴν θ. ἀνοιγνύναι open it, see at {ἀνοίγνυμ; ὦσαι} push it open, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Lysias Orator 1.24]]; μικρὸν ἐνδοῦναι open it a little, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus 2.597d; δόμου ἐν πρώτῃσι θύρῃσι στῆναι 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 1.255; ἷζε δ᾽ ἐπὶ.. οὐδοῦ ἔντοσθε θυράων 17.339; θυρῶν ἔνδον 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Electra” 78; πρὸ θυρῶν [prev. work] 109 (_anapaest meter_)]]; ἐπί or παρὰ Πριάμοιο θύρῃσι at Priam's door, i.e. before his dwelling, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 2.788, 7.346: _metaphorically_, ἐπὶ ταῖς θύραις τῆς Ἑλλάδος εἶναι 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 6.5.23, compare 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 10.34; τῆς πατρίδος 1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus “Sulla” 29, “Arat.” 37; ἐπὶ θύραις τῆς Πίσης 2nd-3rd c.AD: Philostratus Sophista “Vita Apollonii” 8.15]]; πυρετοῦ περὶ θύρας ὄντος being at the door, [Refs 1st c.AD+ [1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus 2.128f (but χειμῶνος ἐπὶ θύραις ὄντος 6th c.AD: Philoponus, Joannes Philosophus “in Aristotelis Meteorologicorum librum primum commentarium - Comm. in Arist. Graeca” 130.25).]]

__2
especially of kings and potentates, οἱ τῶν ἀρίστων Περσῶν παῖδες ἐπὶ ταῖς βασιλέως θύραις παιδεύονται are educated at court, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 1.9.3]]; γυνὴ φοιτῶσα ἐπὶ τὰς θύρας τοῦ βασιλέος, of a petitioner, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 3.119, compare 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 2.1.8]]; αἱ ἐπὶ τὰς θ. φοιτήσεις dangling after the court, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [[prev. author] “HG” 1.6.7; ἐπὶ ταῖς τῶν πλουσίων θ. διατρίβειν 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Rhetorica” 1391a12; περὶ θύρας διατρίβειν [prev. author] “Pol.” 1313b7, 4th c.BC: Theopompus Historicus 121]]; applied also to lovers, clients, disciples, etc., ἐπὶ τὴν θύραν (or τὰς θύρας) τινὸς βαδίζειν, ἰέναι, etc., [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Plutus” 1007, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 364b, compare “Phdr.” 233e, etc.; ἐπὶ ταῖσι θύραις ἀεὶ καθῆσθαι 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Nubes” 467: _metaphorically_, Μουσῶν ἐπὶ ποιητικὰς θ. ἀφικέσθαι 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Phaedrus” 245a.]]

[Refs [[prev. author] 3.62, 6.76]]; οὐκ ἐν ταῖς αὐταῖς ἰ. not in the same relations, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Isocrates Orator 3.44: εἰς μίαν τινὰ ἰ]]. into one kind of existence, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Theaetetus” 184d; ἄλλη ἰ. πολιτείας [prev. author] “R.” 544c, etc.; ἀγοραίας.. ἰδέας τοῦ βίου 4th-3rd c.BC: Epicurus Philosophus “Fragmenta” 196.]]

deep_entry:
Abbott-Smith / STEPBible (TBESG)
ἴδιος, -α, -ον (in Attic usually -ος, -ον),
[in LXX chiefly for of person(s) suff., also for לָהֶם, etc.; (τὰ ἴ.) בֵּיתוֹ ;]
__1. one's own;
__(a) of that which is private and personal (in cl. opposite to κοινός, δημόσιος; cf. infr. 3);
__(b) of property, friends, home, country, etc. (in cl. opposite to ἀλλότριος; in late writers often, like ἑαυτοῦ, with weakened sense, see M, Pr., 87ff.; Deiss., BS, 123f.): Luk.6:41, Jhn.1:42 5:43, Act.2:6 20:28, 1Co.11:21, Gal.6:5, 2Ti.1:9, Heb.7:27, Ju 6, al.; πράσσειν τὰ ἴ., 1Th.4:11; κατὰ τὰς ἰ. ἐπιθυμίας, 2Ti.4:3; οἱ ἴδιοι, Jhn.1:11 (M, Pr., 90f.; Field, Notes, 84) 13:1, Act.4:23, 1Ti.5:8; τὰ ἴδια, one's home (Field, Notes, l.with), Luk.18:28, Jhn.1:11 16:32 19:27.
__2. peculiar, distinct, appropriate, proper: τὸ ἴ. σῶμα, 1Co.15:38; ἐν τ. ἰ. τάγματι, 1Co.15:23; εἰς τ. τόπον τ. ἴ., Act.1:25; = αὐτοῦ (see Deiss., ut. supr.), Mat.22:5, Jhn.1:42 (cf. Wis.10:1).
__3. Adverbially (see supr., 1 (a);  and cf. WM, 739:2);
__(a) ἰδίᾳ, severally, separately: 1Co.12:11;
__(b) κατ᾽ ἰδίαν, apart, privately, in private: Mat.14:13, 23 20:17, Mrk.4:34 7:33, Luk.10:23, Act.23:19, al.
(AS)

---

LSJ / STEPBible (TFLSJ)
ἴδιος [ῐδ], α, ον,
Attic dialect also ος, ον [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Protagoras” 349b, 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Historia Animalium” 532b32 (see. entry near the end)]]:

__I
one's own, pertaining to oneself: hence,

__I.1
private, personal (opposed to κοινός): twice in [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Homerus Epicus, πρῆξις δ᾽ ἥδ᾽ ἰδίη οὐ δήμιος]] this business is private, not public, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 3.82; δήμιον ἦ ἴδιο; 4.314]]; ἴδιος ἐν κοινῷ σταλείς embarking as a private man in a public cause, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “O.” 13.49]]; ἰ. στόλῳ χρᾶσθαι, opposed to δημοσίῳ, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 5.63; γῆς.. νοσούσης ἴ. κινοῦντες κακά 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Tyrannus” 636; κοινὸν ἐξ ἰδίας ἀνοίας κακόν 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Hecuba” 641 (Lyric poetry), compare “Or.” 766 (troch.)]]; ἴδια πράσσων ἢ στρατοῦ ταχθεὶς ὕπ; [Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. author] “IA” 1363 (troch.); ἴ. κέρδεα 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 6.100; συμφορά 5th c.BC: Antipho Orator 2.1.11; πρόσοδος 5th-6th c.BC: Andocides Orator 4.11; τὰ ἴ. διάφορα 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 2.37; πλοῦτος ἴ. καὶ δημόσιος [prev. author] 1.80, compare 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 521a; ἴ. οὐ κοινὸς πόνος [prev. work] 535b, compare 543b]]; ξυμβόλαια[Refs [[prev. work] 443e; ἰ. ἢ πολιτικὴ πρᾶξις [prev. author] “Grg.” 484d; πόλεις καὶ ἴ. οἶκοι [prev. author] “Lg.” 890b, compare 796d]], etc.; τὰ ἱρά, opposed to τὰ ἴ., temples, opposed to private buildings, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 6.9, 8.109]]; τὸ ἐν ἰδίοις discussion among private persons, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Sophista” 225b.]]

__I.2
one's own, opposed to ἀλλότριος, ἐπικώμια [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “N.” 6.32; ἡ ἰ. ἐλευθερίη 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 7.147; Ζεὺς ἰδίοις νόμοις κρατύνων 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Prometheus Vinctus” 404 (Lyric poetry); ἰδίᾳ γνώμᾳ [prev. work] 543 (Lyric poetry)]]; οὔτοι τὰ χρήματ᾽ ἴ. κέκτηνται βροτοί [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Phoenissae” 555]]; φίλων οὐδὲν ἴ., ={κοινὰ τὰ τῶν φίλων}, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [[prev. author] “Andr.” 376: with _pronoun_, χωρίον ἡμέτερον ἴδιον 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 55.8.]]

__I.3
τὰ ἴ. private interests, opposed to public, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 1.82, 2.61, etc.]]; one's own property, [Refs [[prev. author] 1.141, etc.]]; τὰ ἴ. πράττειν mind one's own business, in later Gr., [NT+2nd c.AD+ [2nd c.AD: Phrynichus Atticista 405, cf. NT.1Thes.4.11]]; μένειν ἐπὶ τῶν ἰ. [Refs 2nd c.BC+ [2nd c.BC: Polybius Historicus 2.57.5]]; εἰς τὸ ἴ. καταθέσθαι for self, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 1.3.3, etc.: with _pronoun_, τοὐμὸν ἴ. εἰπεῖν]] my personal opinion, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Isocrates Orator 6.8]]; τὰ ἐμὰ ἴ. [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 50.66]]; τὰ αὑτοῦ ἴ. [Refs 6th c.BC+ [6th c.BC: Theognis Elegiacus 440 (uncertain reading), compare 5th c.BC: Antipho Orator 5.61, 5th-6th c.BC: Isocrates Orator 8.127]]; τὰ ὑμέτερα ἴ. [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 19.307]]; τὰ ἴ. σφῶν αὐτῶν, τὰ ἴ. τὰ σφέτερα αὐτῶν, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Andocides Orator 2.2, 3.36]]; ἔγωγε τοὐμὸν ἴ. I for my own part, [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd c.AD: Lucianus Sophista “Merc.Cond.” 9.]]

__I.4
of persons, personally attached to one, ἴδιοι Σελεύκου [Refs 4th c.BC+ [2nd c.BC: Polybius Historicus 21.6.4, compare 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Politica” 1315a36, “UPZ” 146.38 (2nd c.BC), 109.18 (1st c.BC)]]; ἄνθρωπος ἴδιος τῇ εὐνοίᾳ τῇ πρὸς.. [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [“PCair.Zen.” 32 (3rd c.BC)]]; ταῖς εὐνοίαις ἴδιοι [Refs 1st c.BC+ [1st c.BC: Diodorus Siculus Historicus 11.26]]; ἴδιοι, οἱ, members of one's family, relatives, [Refs 1st c.AD+ [“BGU” 665 ii 1 (1st c.AD), 2nd c.AD: Vettius Valens Astrologus 70.5, etc.]]

__I.5
ἡ ἰ. (sometimes with κώμη added, [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [“BGU” 15.13 (2nd c.AD))]], one's place of origin, [Refs 2nd c.BC+ [PTeb. 327.28 (2nd c.AD), etc.: _plural_, καταπορεύεσθαι εἰς τὰς ἰ.[prev. work]5.7 (2nd c.BC).]]

__I.6
in later Gr., almost as a possessive pronoun,= ἑαυτοῦ, ἑαυτῶν, ἡ ἰ. φιλαγαθία [Refs 2nd c.BC+ [“IG” 22.1011.71 (2nd c.BC)]], etc.; χρῶνται ὡς ἰδίοις [Refs 2nd c.BC+ [“UPZ” 11.14 (2nd c.BC)]]; περὶ τῶν ἰ. βιβλίων, title of work by Galen.

__I.6.b
ἴ. θάνατος one's own, i.e. a natural death, Ramsay Cities and Bishoprics[Refs 2nd c.AD+ [No. 133; ἰδίοις τελευτῶσι θανάτοις 2nd c.AD: Ptolemaeus Mathematicus “Tetrabiblos” 199; also ἰδία μοίρῃ Ramsay op.cit. No. 187.]]

__II
separate, distinct, ἔθνος ἴ. καὶ οὐδαμῶς Σκυθικόν [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 4.18, compare 22]]; ἴδιοί τινές σοι [θεοί]; [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Ranae” 890; ἑκάστῳ τῶν ὀνομάτων ὑπόκειταί τις ἴδιος οὐσία 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Protagoras” 349b]]; πόλεις.. βαρβάρους καὶ ἰδίας Decrees cited in [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 18.183]]; ὁ βάτραχος ἰδίαν ἔχει τὴν γλῶτταν, τὴν ἰ. ἀφίησι φωνήν, a peculiar kind of tongue,.. its peculiar note, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Historia Animalium” 536a8, 11: followed by ἤ, ἴδιον ἔπασχεν πάθος ἢ οἱ ἄλλοι]] unique and different from others, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Gorgias” 481c; so ἴδιον παρὰ τὰ ἄλλα 4th-3rd c.BC: Theophrastus Philosophus “Historia Plantarum” 6.4.10.]]

__II.b
ἴ. λόγος, in Ptolemaic and Roman Egypt, private account, δεδώκαμεν Πύρωνι τὸν ἔσχατόν σου ἴ. λόγον [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [“PCair.Zen.” 253 (3rd c.BC),compare “PGrenf.” 1.16 (2nd c.BC)]], etc.; later, special account, a branch of the fiscal administration, Wilcken [Refs 2nd c.BC+ [“Chr.” 162 (2nd c.BC), “PAmh.” 2.31 (2nd c.BC), “PGnom.Prooem.” (2nd c.AD)]], etc.; ὁ γνώμων τοῦ ἰ. λόγου [Refs 1st c.AD+ [“OGI” 669.44 (1st c.AD)]]; also as the title of the Controller, [Refs 1st c.BC+ [1st c.BC-1st c.AD: Strabo Geographus 17.1.12 codices, “OGI” 408 (2nd c.AD), Mitteis “Chr.” 372 vi 1 (2nd c.AD).]]

__II.2
strange, unusual, ἰδίοισιν ὑμεναίοισι κοὐχὶ σώφροσιν [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Orestes” 558]]; peculiar, exceptional, περιττὸν καὶ ἴ. γένος [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “de Generatione Animalium” 760a5; τὰ περιττὰ καὶ ἴ. τῶν δένδρων 4th-3rd c.BC: Theophrastus Philosophus “de Causis Plantarum” 2.7.1]]; παράδοξον εἰπεῖν τι καὶ περιττὸν καὶ ἴ. [Refs 1st c.AD+ [1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus 2.1068b]]; eccentric, of persons, [Refs [[prev. work]57e]]; ἴ. τις ἐν πᾶσι βουλόμενος εἶναι [Refs [[prev. author] “Them.” 18.]]

__II.3
peculiar, appropriate, ἴδια ὀνόματα proper, specific words, opposed to περιέχοντα, class-names, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Rhetorica” 1407a31; ὄνομα ἴ. τινος 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 580e; τὸ ἴ. τοῦ ἐπαίνου 2nd c.AD: Lucianus Sophista “Pr.Im.” 19.]]

__III
ἴ. λόγοι ordinary private conversation, opposed to ποίησις, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 366e, compare “Euthd.” 305d; see infr. VI. 2b.]]

__IV
τὸ ἴ. characteristic property of a species, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Topica” 102a18, 103b11, 3rd c.BC: Chrysippus Stoicus 2.75, 3rd c.AD: Plotinus Philosophus 5.5.13]]; but also, distinguishing feature in a relative sense, ἴ. πρός τι [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Topica” 128b25.]]

__V
regular comparative ἰδιώτερος [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Isocrates Orator 12.73, 4th-3rd c.BC: Theophrastus Philosophus “Historia Plantarum” 3.1.6]]: superlative -ώτατος[Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 23.65, 4th-3rd c.BC: Theophrastus Philosophus “Historia Plantarum” 1.14.2]]; also ἰδιαίτερος, -αίτατος, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “de Partibus Animalium” 656a26, 658b33; -αίτατος but not -αίτερος _accusative_ to Thom.Mag. p.189R.]]

__VI
adverb ἰδίως, peculiarly, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Isocrates Orator 5.108]]; severally, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Leges” 807b]]: comparative ἰδιωτέρως [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-3rd c.BC: Theophrastus Philosophus “Historia Plantarum” 1.13.4; ὡς -ώτερον εἰπεῖν 1st c.BC: Philodemus Philosophus “περὶ οἰκονομίας” p.68 1st c.AD: Josephus Historicus; ἰδιαίτερον 2nd c.AD: Herodianus Grammaticus 7.6.7: _superlative_ ἰδιώτατα (variant{-αίτατα}) 1st c.BC: Diodorus Siculus Historicus 19.1]]; ἰδίως καλεῖσθαι to be called specifically, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “de Mundo” 394b28; -αίτατα λέγεσθαι [prev. author] “Mete.” 382a3]]; ἰδίως, opposed to κοινῶς, λέγεσθαι [Refs 2nd c.BC+ [2nd c.BC: Demetrius Lacon Philosophus “Herc.” 1014.41]] F. (but in Grammars, to be used as a proper name, [Refs 2nd c.BC+ [2nd c.BC: Dionysius Thrax Grammaticus 634.13)]]; in a peculiar sense or usage, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [Scholia 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Plutus” 115; ἰ.Αἰσχύλος τὸν Ἀγαμέμνονα ἐπὶ σκηνῆς ἀναιρεῖσθαι ποιεῖ 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Ag.” argument, cf. Scholia 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Phoenissae” 1116]]; also,= extra versum, τὸ φεῦ ἰδίως [Refs 5th c.BC+ [Scholia 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Nubes” 41 (variant{ἰδίᾳ}).]]

__VI.2
ἰδίᾳ, Ionic dialect -ιη, as adverb, by oneself, privately, on one's own account, θύοντι ἰδίῃ μούνῳ [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.132, compare 192, 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Equites” 467; οὔτε ἰδίᾳ οὔτε ἐν κοινῷ 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 1.141; καὶ ἰ. καὶ δημοσίᾳ [prev. author] 3.45, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Apologia” 30b; καὶ ἰ. καὶ κοινῇ 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Ἀθηναίων Πολιτεία” 40.3; ἰδίᾳ ἕκαστος 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 8.1, compare 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Leges” 946d, etc.: with _genitive_, ἰ. τῆς φρενός]] apart from.. , [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Ranae” 102.]]

__VI.2.b
in ordinary talk, opposed to ὑπὸ ποιητῶν, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 363e, compare 606c; see above 111.]]

__VI.3
κατ᾽ ἰδίαν in private, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-3rd c.BC: Philemo Comicus 169; κατ᾽ ἰδίαν εἰπεῖν τινι 1st c.BC: Diodorus Siculus Historicus 1.21]]; κατ᾽ ἰ. λαβεῖν τινα to take him aside, [Refs 2nd c.BC+ [2nd c.BC: Polybius Historicus 4.84.8]]; also, separately, apart, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus 2.120d; οἱ κατ᾽ ἰ. βίοι 2nd c.BC: Polybius Historicus 1.71.1. (ϝίδιος “Tab.Heracl.” 1.13, +others, “Schwyzer” 324.4 (Delph., 4th c.BC), “IG” 9(1).333.12 (_Locrian dialect_, 5th c.BC)]], etc.; with spiritus asper, ἐκ τοῦ ηιδίου [Refs 5th c.BC+ [“Jahresh.” 14 “Beibl.” 141 (Argos, 5th c.BC)]]; καθ᾽ ἱδίαν [Refs 6th c.AD+ [“IG” 22.891.6, 5(1).6 (_Laconian dialect_), 9(2).66 (from Lamia), 6th c.AD: Aëtius Medicus 3.159, etc.]]; καθ᾽ ἱδδίαν probably in [Refs [“IG” 9(2).461.26 (Thess.).)]]

(ἴδιος), [in LXX: Pro.6:8 (no Heb.)* ;]

LSJ / STEPBible (TFLSJ)
ἰδῐώτ-ης, ου, ὁ,
(ἴδιος) private person, individual, opposed to the State, ξυμφέροντα καὶ πόλεσι καὶ ἰδιώταις [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 1.124, compare 3.10, “SIG” 37.3 (Teos, 5th c.BC), 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Symposium” 185b, 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “de Vectigalibus” 4.18, etc.]]; opposed to γένος, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [“SIG” 1013.6 (Chios, 4th c.BC); opposed to φατρία, [prev. work]987.28 ([prev. passage], 4th c.BC).]]

__II
one in a private station, opposed to to one holding public office, or taking part in public affairs, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.59, 123, +others, cf. Decrees cited in 5th-6th c.BC: Andocides Orator 1.84, 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 4.2, etc.]]; opposed to βασιλεύς, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 7.3]]; opposed to ἄρχων, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Lysias Orator 5.3, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Politicus” 259b, “SIG” 305.71 (4th c.BC)]]; opposed to δικαστής, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Antipho Orator 6.24]]; opposed to πολιτευόμενος, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 10.70]]; opposed to ῥήτωρ, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Hyperides Orator “pro Euxenippo” 27]]; private soldier, opposed to στρατηγός, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 1.3.11, compare “PHib.” 1.30.21 (3rd c.BC)]]; layman, opposed to priest, [NT+2nd c.BC+ [“OGI” 90.52 (Rosetta, 2nd c.BC), “PGnom.” 200 (2nd c.AD), NT.1Cor.14.16]]: as adjective, ἰ. ἄνδρες [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.32, 70, 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 1.115]]; ἰ. θεοί homely (with play on ἴδιος), [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Ranae” 891.]]

__II.2
common man, plebeian, οἱ ἰ. καὶ πένητες [Refs 1st c.AD+ [1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus “Theseus” 24]]; ἰ. καὶ εὐτελής, opposed to βασιλεύς, [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd c.AD: Herodianus Grammaticus 4.10.2.]]

__II.3
as adjective, ἰ. βίος private station, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 578c]]; ἰ. λόγος everyday speech, [Refs 1st c.BC+ [1st c.BC: Dionysius Halicarnassensis “de Demosthene” 2, compare 3rd c.AD: Longinus Rhetor 31.2.]]

__III
one who has no professional knowledge, layman, καὶ ἰατρὸς καὶ ἰ. [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 2.48, compare 5th c.BC: Hippocrates Medicus “περὶ ἀρχαίης ἰητρικῇς” 4, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Theaetetus” 178c, “Lg.” 933d; ἰ. ἤ τινα τέχνην ἔχων [prev. author] “Sph.” 221c]]; of prose-writers, ἐν μέτρῳ ὡς ποιητής, ἢ ἄνευ μέτρου ὡς ἰ. [Refs [[prev. author] “Phdr.” 258d, compare “Smp.” 178b; ἰ. καὶ μηδὲν αὐλήσεως ἐπαΐων [prev. author] “Prt.” 327c]]; opposed to to a professed orator, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Isocrates Orator 4.11]]; to a trained soldier, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “de Equitum magistro” 8.1]]; ἰδιώτας, ὡς εἰπεῖν, χειροτέχναις (-νας codices) ἀνταγωνισαμένους [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 6.72]]; opposed to ἀσκητής, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Memorabilia” 3.7.7, compare 12.1]]; opposed to ἀθλητής, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Ethica Nicomachea” 1116b13]]; opposed to a professed philosopher, [Refs 1st c.BC+ [[prev. author] “Pol.” 1266a31, 1st c.BC: Philodemus Philosophus “περὶ παρρησίας” p.51 O., “D.” 1.25; in Music, [prev. author] “Mus.” p.42]] K.; opposed to δημιουργός, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Protagoras” 312a, “Thg.” 124c: as]] adjective, ὁ ἰ. ὄχλος, opposed to artificers, [Refs 1st c.AD+ [1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus “Pericles” 12.]]

__III.2
with genitive of things, unpractised, unskilled in a thing, ἰατρικῆς [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Protagoras” 345a, compare “Ti.” 20a; ἔργου 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Oeconomicus” 3.9]]; ἰ. κατὰ τοὺς πόνους, κατὰ τὸν ὕπνον, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. author] “Cyr.” 1.5.11; ἰ. τὰ ἄλλα 2nd c.AD: Herodianus Grammaticus 4.12.1; ἰ. ὡς πρὸς ἡμᾶς ἀγωνίζεσθαι 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Cyr.” [same place], compare 2nd c.AD: Lucianus Sophista “Herm.” 81.]]

__III.3
generally, raw hand, ignoramus, ἄν τε δεινοὶ λάχωσιν ἄν τε ἰδιῶται.. [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 4.35]]; παιδάρια καὶ ἰ., of slaves, [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd c.AD: Sextus Empiricus Philosophus “adversus Mathematicos” 1.234 (compare ἰ. οἰκέται 2nd c.AD: Lucianus Sophista “Alex.” 30)]]; ἀμαθὴς καὶ ἰ., opposed to τεχνίτης, [Refs [[prev. author] “Ind.” 29]]; vocative ἰδιῶτα, as a term of abuse, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-3rd c.BC: Menander Comicus “Σαμία” 71.]]

__III.4
'average man', opposed to a person of distinction, [Refs 1st c.AD+ [1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus 2.1104a.]]

__IV
ἰδιῶται, οἱ, one's own countrymen, opposed to ξένοι, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Ranae” 459.]]

generally, sacred objects or rites, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.172, 4.33; τῶν ὑμετέρων ἱ. καὶ κοινῶν μετεῖχον 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 57.3]]; of cult-images, IG Rom.[Refs [3.800 (syllium).]]

__III.2
after [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Homerus Epicus]], ἱερόν, Ionic dialect ἱρόν, τό, holy place, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 5.119, +others]]; opposed to νηός, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. author] 2.170, compare 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 4.90, 5.18]]; frequently of a temple, ἔστι δὲ ἐν τῷ τεμένεϊ.. ἱρόν κτλ. [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 2.112]]; of the Jewish temple, [LXX+2nd c.BC+ [LXX.1Ch.29.4, 2nd c.BC: Polybius Historicus 16.39.4, 1st c.BC-1st c.AD: Strabo Geographus 16.2.34, NT.Matt.24.1.]]

__III.3
ἱερὸν τῆς δίκης a sacred principle of right, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Helena” 1002.]]

__III.4
ἱερός, ὁ (i.e. μήν), name of month at Delos, [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [“IG” 12.377.22, 11(2).203 A 31 (3rd c.BC).]]

__III.5
ἱεροί, οἱ, members of a religious college or guild, [Refs 1st c.BC+ [[prev. work]5(1).1390.1, +others (Andania, 1st c.BC), probably in “SIG” 1010.7 (from Chalcedon)]], etc.; also of women, ἱεραί, αἱ, [Refs [“IG” 5(1). [same place], compare 1511 (from Sparta).]]

__III.5.b
={ἱερόδουλος}, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. work] 1356 (Messenia, 5th c.BC), “Inscription Perg.” 572, “GDI” 5702.39 (from Samos).]]

__IV
special phrases, post-[Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Homerus Epicus,]]

__IV.1
proverbial, ἱ. ἄγκυρα one's last hope, [Refs 1st c.AD+ [1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus 2.815d, 2nd c.AD: Lucianus Sophista “JTr.” 51, “Fug.” 13, 2nd c.AD(?): Pollianus Epigrammaticus 1.93, 2nd c.AD: Galenus Medicus 11.182.]]

__IV.2
ἱ. βόλος, name of a throw at dice, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Eubulus Comicus 57.1.]]

__IV.3
ἱ. βοτάνη, see at {βοτάνη}.

__IV.4
ἱ. (i.e. γραμμή) [Refs [compare (γραμμή 111.1)]], last line of draught-board, κινήσαις τὸν ἀπ᾽ ἴρας.. λίθον [Refs 7th c.BC+ [7th-6th c.BC: Alcaeus Lyricus 82, compare 5th c.BC: Epicharmus Comicus 225, 5th c.BC: Sophron Comicus 127]]; τὴν ἀφ᾽ ἱερᾶς (variant{τὴν ἱεράν}) [Refs 1st c.AD+ [1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus “Coriolanus” 32.]]

__IV.5
ἱ. ἰχθύς,= ἀνθίας, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Historia Animalium” 620b35, compare 2nd c.AD: Athenaeus Epigrammaticus 7.282e, 1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus 2.981d.]]

__IV.6
ἱ. λόχος, see at {λόχος}.

__IV.7
ἱερά (i.e. νίκη), ἡ, drawn contest, dead heat (because the prize was assigned to the god), [Refs 6th c.AD+ [“SIG” 1073.48 (6th c.AD: Olympiodorus Philosophus); ποιῆσαι ἱεράν, of the competitor, Wood “Ephesus, App.” vi p.70; so ἱ. ἀθλήματα “Inscription Olymp.” 56; ἱερὸς ὁ στέφανος ἐκρίθη “IG” 9(2).525 (from Larissa); τὸ παγκράτιον ἱ. ἐγένετο [prev. work]527 ([prev. passage]); ἱερός (i.e. ἀγών) [prev. work]7.2727.19, 24 (Acraeph.): _metaphorically_, ἱερὸν ποιῆσαι τὸν στέφανον]] 'divide the honours', [Refs 2nd c.BC+ [2nd c.BC: Polybius Historicus 1.58.5, 29.8.9.]]

__IV.8
ἱ. νόσος epilepsy, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 3.33, 5th c.BC: Hippocrates Medicus “Morb. Sacr.” at Title Page, 4th-3rd c.BC: Theophrastus Philosophus “Historia Plantarum” 9.11.3, etc., compare 3rd c.BC: Callimachus Epicus “Aetia” 3.1.14: _metaphorically_, τὴν οἴησιν ἱ. νόσον ἔλεγε 1st c.AD(?): Heraclitus 46 (= 4th-3rd c.BC: Epicurus Philosophus “Fragmenta” 224).]]

__IV.9
ἡ ἱ. ὁδός the sacred road to Delphi, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 6.34; also, from Athens to Eleusis, 5th c.BC: Cratinus Comicus 61, 2nd c.AD: Pausanias Periegeta 1.36.3, 1st-2nd c.AD: Harpocratio Grammaticus]] see entry ; and that from Elis to Olympia, [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd c.AD: Pausanias Periegeta 5.25.7.]]

__IV.10
ἱ. ὀστέον, os sacrum, the last bone of the spine, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Hippocrates Medicus “περὶ ἄρθρων ἐμβολῆς” 45, 1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus 2.981d, 2nd c.AD: Galenus Medicus “de Usu Partium” 5.8, etc.]]

__IV.11
ἱ. συμβουλή sacred duty of an adviser, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Epistulae” 321c, 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 5.6.4, compare 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Theages” 122b, 2nd c.AD: Lucianus Sophista “Rh.Pr.” 1.]]

__IV.12
ἱ. σῦριγξ spinal canal, [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd c.AD(?): Pollianus Epigrammaticus 2.180.]]

__IV.13
ἱερὰ τριήρης, of the Delian ship, or one of the state-ships (Salaminia or Paralos), [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 4.34.]]

__IV.14
frequently in geographical names, e.g. ἱ ἄκρα, in Lycia, [Refs 1st c.BC+ [1st c.BC-1st c.AD: Strabo Geographus 14.3.8]]; ἱ. ἀκρωτήριον, in Spain, Cape St. Vincent, [Refs [[prev. author] 2.4.3]]; ἱ. κώμη, in Lydia, [Refs 2nd c.BC+ [2nd c.BC: Polybius Historicus 16.1.8]]; ἱ. νῆσος, one of the Liparean group, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 3.88]]; one of the insulae Aegates, [Refs 2nd c.BC+ [2nd c.BC: Polybius Historicus 1.60.3.]]

__V
adverb -ρῶς holily, ἀποθανεῖν variant in [Refs 8th c.BC+ [1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus “Lycurgus” 27. [ῐ by nature, but sometimes ῑ in _Epic dialect_, especially in endings of hexameters, ἱ. ἰχθύς, ἱ. ἦμαρ, ἱερὰ ῥέξας, ἀλφίτου ἱεροῦ ἀκτή, 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 16.407, 8.66, 1.147, 11.631]]; ῑερόν in the first foot of a hexameters, [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [3rd c.BC: Theocritus Poeta Bucolicus 5.22]]; also in compounds ἱεραγωγός, ἱεροθαλλής, ἱερόφωνος: ῑ always in contraction form ἱρός which is used in Epic dialect, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus]], and some Ionic dialect inscriptions, as [Refs 7th c.BC+ [“IG” 12(8).265.9 (from Thasos), compare 7th-6th c.BC(?): Semonides Iambographus 7.56, 3rd c.BC: Herodas Mimographus 4.79, +others]], but is rarely found in codices of [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Hippocrates Medicus (never in 1st c.AD(?): Heraclitus or 3rd c.AD: Democritus Epigrammaticus)]]; also in Trag., [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Septem contra Thebas” 268, etc., but never required by metre in Lyric poetry of Comedy texts]]]

Abbott-Smith / STEPBible (TBESG)
ἱερός, -ά, όν
[in LXX: Eze.28:18 (מִקְדָּשׁ); τό ἱ, 1Ch.29:4 (בַּיִת), Eze.45:19 (עֲזָרָה); very frequently in I Est.1:1-58 -4 Mac ;]
__1. in Hom., marvellous, mighty, divine.
__2. (Also in Hom, and later cl.) consecrated to the deity, sacred: pl., ἱ. γράμματα, 2Ti.3:15.
__3. As subst.,
__(a) (so in Hom.), τὰ ἱ., sacrifices, sacred rites, sacred things: 1Co.9:13;
__(b) later, τὸ ἱ.,., a consecrated or sacred place, a temple: τ. Ἀρτέμιδος, Act.19:27; of the temple at Jerusalem, i.e. the entire precincts or some part thereof (as distinct from ὁ ναός, which see, the Sanctuary proper): 1Co.9:13, and frequently in Gosp. and esp. in Ac, Mat.12:6, Mrk.13:3, Act.4:1, al. (on the use of ἱ. in Imperial Iuser., see Deiss., LAE, 380 f.)
(AS)

(for ἱερὸν  see. III.2), ά, όν, also ός, όν in the phrase ἱερὸς ἀκτή [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th-7th c.BC: Hesiodus Epicus “Opera et Dies” 597, 805, Oracle texts cited in 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 8.77]]: Ionic dialect and poetry ἱρός, ή, όν (see. entry near the end): Doric dialect and N. Greek ἱᾰρός [Refs [“IG” 22.1126.20, etc.]]: Aeolic dialect ἶρος [Refs 7th c.BC+ [7th-6th c.BC: Sappho Lyrica “Papyrus fragments” in E. Diehl, 23.25, 7th-6th c.BC: Alcaeus Lyricus “Supp.” 8.4]], but ἴαρος (correlated from ἴερ-) [Refs 7th c.BC+ [7th-6th c.BC: Sappho Lyrica “Papyrus fragments” in E. Diehl, 20a. 6]]: superlative ἱερώτατος [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Equites” 582 (Lyric poetry), 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Leges” 755e.]]

__I
filled with or manifesting divine power, supernatural, ἱ. ἲς Τηλεμάχοιο [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 2.409, +others; ἱ. μένος Ἀλκινόοιο 8.421, etc.]]; ἄλφιτον, ἀλωαί, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 11.631, 5.499; Δημήτερος ἱερὸς ἀκτή 8th-7th c.BC: Hesiodus Epicus “Op.” I [prev. cited]]]; of natural objects or phenomena, rivers, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 10.351, 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 11.726, 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Medea” 410 (Lyric poetry)]]; λιβάς, of the Spercheus, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Philoctetes” 1215 (Lyric poetry)]]; ἱεραὶ βῆσσαι Κίρκης 'faery', [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 10.275]]; ἱ. ἦμαρ, κνέφας, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 8.66, 11.194; φάος 8th-7th c.BC: Hesiodus Epicus “Opera et Dies” 339]]; ἱερὸς δίφρος (where δ. perhaps = ἵπποι) [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 17.464; after 8th c.BC: Homerus Epicus, ἱ. χεῦμα θαλάσσης 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Fragmenta - American Journal of Philology” 192 (_anapaest meter_); ἱ. κῦμα 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Hippolytus” 1206, compare “Cyc.” 265; ὄμβρος 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Tyrannus” 1428; δρόσοι 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Ion” 117 (Lyric poetry)]]; ὕπνος, of death, [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [3rd c.BC: Callimachus Epicus “Epigrammata” 11]]; ἔστι μὲν οὐδὲν ἱ. no great matter, [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [3rd c.BC: Theocritus Poeta Bucolicus 5.22.]]

__II
of divine things, holy, ἱεροῖς ἐν δώμασι Κίρκης [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 10.426; ἱ. γένος ἀθανάτων 8th-7th c.BC: Hesiodus Epicus “Theogonia” 21; λέχος, of Zeus, [prev. work] 57]]; δόσις the gift of God, [Refs [[prev. work] 93]]; πόλεμος holy war, 'crusade', [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Aves” 556, etc.]]

__II.2
of earthly things, hallowed, consecrated, βωμοί [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 2.305]]; ἱ. δόμος, of the temple of Athena,[Refs 8th c.BC+ [6.89; ἱ. ἑκατόμβη 1.99, 431, etc.; ἐλαίη 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 13.372; χοαί 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Coloneus” 469, etc.]]; ἱρὰ γράμματα hieroglyphics, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 2.36]]; but ἱ. γράμματα of the “Holy Scriptures”, [NT.2Tim.3.15]; ἱ. βύβλοι [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [“OGI” 56.70 (Canopus, 3rd c.BC)]]; ἱ. ἄγαλμα, τρίπους, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Tyrannus” 1379, 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Ion” 512, etc.; χρήματα 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 568d, etc.; ἱ. τὸ σῶμα τῷ θεῷ δίδωμ᾽ ἔχειν 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Ion” 1285]]; ἱ. σώματα, of ἱερόδουλοι, [Refs 1st c.BC+ [1st c.BC-1st c.AD: Strabo Geographus 6.2.6; χῆνες 1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus 2.325c]]; of animals regarded as 'taboo', [κριοί] εἰσί σφι ἱ. διὰ τοῦτο [Refs 8th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 2.42; so perhaps ἱ. ἰχθύς 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 16.407]]; of the Roman Tribunes,= Latin sacrosanctus, ἱ. καὶ ἄσυλος [Refs 1st c.AD+ [1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus “Tiberius Gracchus” 15, etc.]]; of Augustus, [Refs [“Mon.Anc.Gr.” 5.17]]; ἱ. νόμος law of sacrifice, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 21.35, compare “SIG” 685.81 (2nd c.BC)]]; ἱ. λόγος legend, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 2.81, etc.; οἱ παλαιοὶ καὶ ἱ. λόγοι 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Epistulae” 335a]]; ἱ. γάμος mystical marriage, a religious ceremony, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-3rd c.BC: Menander Comicus 320, 9th c.AD: Photius Legal icographus, etc.]] see entry ; opposed to βέβηλος, as sacred to profane, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [1st c.BC: Dionysius Halicarnassensis 7.8, “Anecdota Graeca - Bekker” 223; but more frequently ἱ. καὶ ὅσιος 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 2.52, 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “de Vectigalibus” 5.4, etc.]]; compare ὅσιος.

__II.3
under divine protection, frequently of places, Ἴλιος [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 5.648, 7th-6th c.BC: Alcaeus Lyricus “Supp.” 8.4; Πύλος 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 21.108; Θήβη 7th-6th c.BC: Sappho Lyrica “Papyrus fragments” in E. Diehl, 20a. 6]]; Τροίης ἱερὸν πτολίεθρον, Τροίης ἱερὰ κρήδεμνα, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 1.2, 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 16.100; Ἀθῆναι 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 11.323, compare 5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “Fragmenta.” 75, 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Ajax” 1221 (Lyric poetry), Ps.-Oracle texts cited in 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Equites” 1037; Σούνιον ἱρόν 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 3.278]]; ἱ. κύκλος the judge's seat under the protection of Zeus, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 18.504: with _genitive_ of the divinity, ἄλσος ἱρὸν Ἀθηναίης, ἄντρον ἱρὸν νυμφάων, 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 6.322, 13.104, compare 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.80, 2.41, 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Plutus” 937, 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 5.3.13, etc.; γῆ καὶ ἑστία ἱερὰ πᾶσι πάντων θεῶν 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Leges” 955e]]; χωρίον ὡς -ώτατον[Refs [[prev. work] 755e, compare “Ti.” 45a]]; with genitive of a human being, Γναθίου.. ἱ. εἰμι [Refs [“IG” 12.920.]]

__II.3.b
of persons, φυλάκων ἱ. τέλος [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 10.56; ἱ. πυλαωροί 24.681; στρατός 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 24.81; βασιλέες 5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “P.” 5.97]]; ἱ. εὐσεβής τε, of Oedipus, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Coloneus” 287]]; ἅνθρωπος ἱ. initiated, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Ranae” 652]]; with genitive of a divinity, deuoted, dedicated, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Alcestis” 75, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Phaedo” 85b.]]

__II.3.c
under the Roman Empire,= sacer, imperial, ἐκ τῶν ἱερῶν τοῦ Καίσαρος γραμμάτων [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [“IGRom.” 4.571 (Aezani, 2nd c.AD); ὁ -ώτατος φίσκος, τὸ -ώτατον ταμιεῖον, [prev. work]3.727 (from Lycia), “SIG” 888.10 (Scaptopara, 3rd c.AD)]], etc.; τὸ -ώτατον βῆμα (of the praefectus Aegypti), [Refs 1st c.AD+ [“PHamb.” 4.8 (1st c.AD)]]: generally, worshipful, ἱ. σύνοδος [Refs 3rd c.AD+ [“OGI” 713.9 (Egypt, 3rd c.AD), etc.]]

__III
as substantive,

__III.1
ἱερά, Ionic dialect ἱρά, τά, offerings, victims, ἱερὰ ῥέξας [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 1.147, etc.; ἔρδειν 8th-7th c.BC: Hesiodus Epicus “Opera et Dies” 336; διδόναι 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 16.184; ἀλλ᾽ ὅ γε δέκτο μὲν ἱρά 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 2.420, compare 23.207: less frequently in _sing._, ὄφρ᾽ ἱρὸν ἑτοιμασσαίατ᾽ Ἀθήνῃ 10.571; θῦσαι ἱρά 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.59, 8.54, etc.; θυσίας καὶ ἱρὰ ποιέειν [prev. author] 2.63; αἴθειν 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Philoctetes” 1033; ἱ. πατρῷα 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Septem contra Thebas” 1015; ἱ. ἐπιχώρια 3rd c.AD: Democritus Epigrammaticus 259.]]

__III.1.b
after [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Homerus Epicus]], omens afforded by sacrifice, τὰ ἱρὰ οὐ προεχώρεε χρηστά [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 5.44]]; τὰ ἱερὰ καλὰ [ἦν] [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 1.8.15; simply οὐκ ἐγίγνετο τὰ ἱ. [prev. work] 2.2.3.]]

__III.1.c
generally, sacred objects or rites, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.172, 4.33; τῶν ὑμετέρων ἱ. καὶ κοινῶν μετεῖχον 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 57.3]]; of cult-images, IG Rom.[Refs [3.800 (syllium).]]

__III.2
after [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Homerus Epicus]], ἱερόν, Ionic dialect ἱρόν, τό, holy place, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 5.119, +others]]; opposed to νηός, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. author] 2.170, compare 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 4.90, 5.18]]; frequently of a temple, ἔστι δὲ ἐν τῷ τεμένεϊ.. ἱρόν κτλ. deep_entry:
Abbott-Smith / STEPBible (TBESG)
ἵνα,
__I. adverb (poët., Hom., al.),
__1. of place, where, whither.
__2. of circumstance, when.
__II. Conjunction,
__1. prop., final, denoting purpose or end (cl.), that, in order that, usually the first word in the clause, but sometimes (cl. also) preceded by an emphatic word (Act.19:4, Rom.11:31 (?), Gal.2:10, al.);
__(a) with optative (so in cl. after historic tenses): after a pres., Eph.1:17 (but WH, mg., subjc.; see Burton, §225, Rem., 2);
__(b) with subjc.: after a pres., Mrk.4:21, Luk.6:34, Jhn.3:15, Act.2:25, Rom.1:11, al.; after a pf., Mat.1:22, Jhn.5:23 1Co.9:22, al.; after an imperat. (present or aor.), Mat.7:1, Mrk.11:25, Jhn.10:38, 1Co.7:5, al.; after a delib. subjc., Mrk.1:38, al.; after a fut., Luk.16:4, Jhn.14:3, 1Co.15:28, al.; after historic tenses (where optative in cl.; WM, 359f.; M, Pr., 196f.), Mrk.6:41 (impf.), Jhn.4:8 (plpf.), Mrk.3:14 (aor.), al.;
__(with) in late writers (M, Pr., 35; Burton, §§198, 199), with indic., fut: Luk.20:10, 1Pe.3:1, al.;
__(d) as often in eccl. writers (Thayer, see word), with indic. pres.: 1Co.4:6, Gal.4:17, al. (?; but V. Burton, §198, Rem.);
__(e) εἰς (διὰ) τοῦτο, ἵνα: Jhn.18:37, 1Ti.1:16, al.; τούτου χάριν, Tit.1:5;
__(f) elliptical constructions: omission of the principal verb, Jhn.1:8, 2Th.3:9, 1Jn.2:19, al.; of the final verb, Rom.4:16, 2Co.8:13, al.
__2. In late writers, definitive, = inf. (WM, 420; Bl, §69, 1), that;
__(a) after verbs of wishing, caring, striving, etc.: θέλω, Mat.7:12, al.; ζητῶ, 1Co.4:2 14:12; ζηλόω, 1Co.14:1, al.;
__(b) after verbs of saying, asking, exhorting: εἰπεῖν, Mat.4:3, al.; ἐρωτῶ, Mrk.7:26, al.; παρακαλῶ, Mat.14:36, 1Co.1:10, al., etc.;
__(with) after words expressing expediency, etc.: συμφέρει, Mat.18:6, Jhn.11:50, al.; ἱκανός, Mat.8:8, Luk.7:6; χρείαν ἔχω, Jhn.2:25, al, etc.;
__(d) after substantives, adding further definition: ὥρα, Jhn.12:23 13:1; χρόνος, Rev.2:21; συνήθεια, Jhn.18:39; μισθός, 1Co.9:18.
__3. In late writers, ecbatic, denoting the result, = ὥστε, that, so that (M, Pr., 206ff.; WM, 572; Bl., §69, 3; Burton, §223): Rom.11:11, 1Co.7:29, 1Th.5:4, al. (but see Thayer, see word); so with the formula referring to the fulfilment of prophecy, ἵνα πληρωθῇ, Mat.1:22 2:14, Jhn.13:18, al.
(AS)

__I.1
