__I.2
elsewhere relative, in which place, where,[Refs 8th c.BC+ [2.558, 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 9.136, 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 2.133, 9.27, 54, 5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “O.” 1.95, 5th c.BC: Bacchylides Lyricus 10.79, 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Prometheus Vinctus” 21, +others, 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Electra” 22, 855, 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Ranae” 1231, etc.]]: rarely in Attic dialect Prose, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Lysias Orator 13.72 (see. below), 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Apologia” 17c, “Phlb.” 61b]]; ἵ. ἡ Νίκη (i.e. ἐστίν) [Refs 8th c.BC+ [“IG” 22.1407.13: rare in later Greek, 2nd c.AD: Arrianus Historicus “Anabasis” 1.3.2, 2nd c.AD: Lucianus Sophista “Cont.” 22, “Ind.” 3: with particles, ἵ. τε 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 20.478; ἵ. περ 24.382, 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 13.364, 5th c.BC: Lysias Orator]] [same place]; ἵν᾽ ἄν with subjunctive, wherever, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Coloneus” 405, 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Ion” 315]]; as indirect interrogative, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.179, 2.150, 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Hecuba” 1008.]]

__I.2.b
after [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Homerus Epicus, like other Advs. of Place, with _genitive_, ἵ. τῆς χώρης 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.98]]; ἔμαθε ἵ. ἦν κακοῦ in what a calamity, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. author] 1.213; οὐδ᾽ ὁρᾶν ἵν᾽ ἐ̄ κακοῦ 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Tyrannus” 367]]; ἵν᾽ ἕσταμεν χρείας[Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. work] 1442; ἵν᾽ ἦμεν ἄτης [prev. author] “El.” 936; ὁρᾷς ἵν᾽ ἐσμὲν αὐτοῦ πέρι τῆς ἀπορίας 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Sophista” 243b.]]

__I.2.c
with Verbs of motion, whither, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 4.821, +others; ὁρᾷς ἵν᾽ ἥκεις 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Tyrannus” 687, +others, 4th-3rd c.BC: Dinarchus Orator 2.10; ιναπερ ὥρμητο 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 4.74.]]

__II
of circumstance, γάμος.., ἵ. χρή at which, when, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 6.27]]; ἵ. μὲν ἐξῆν αὐτοῖς.., ἐνταῦθα.. when it was in their power, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Antipho Orator 6.9.]]

__II.2
={ἐάν}, uncertain in [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 7.353 (variant{ἵν᾽ ἄν}, cf. Scholia), 7th c.BC: Archilochus Lyricus 74.7 codices, variant in 4th-3rd c.BC: Dinarchus Orator 1.1, and 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Charmides” 176b.]]

__B
Final conjunction, that, in order that, from [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Homerus Epicus]] downwards, mostly first word in the clause, but sometimes preceded by an emphatic word, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Charmides” 169d; ἵ. δή 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 7.26, 23.207, 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.29, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 420e, 610c: never with ἄν]] or κε (if found, these particles belong to the Verb, as in [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 12.156, 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Iphigenia Aulidensis” 1579).]]

__B.I
general usage:

__B.I.1
with subjunctive,

__B.I.1.a
after primary tenses of indicative, also subjunctive and imperative: present indicative, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 3.252, 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 2.111, 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Memorabilia” 3.2.3, “Cyr.” 1.2.11, 5th-6th c.BC: Isocrates Orator 3.2]]: perfect indicative, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 1.203, 5th-6th c.BC: Isocrates Orator 4.129]]: future, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 2.307, 4.591, 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 1.2.15]]; subjunctive, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Tyrannus” 364; _imperative_, 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 19.348, +others, 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Prometheus Vinctus” 61, 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Philoctetes” 880, 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Ranae” 297, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 341b, “Men.” 71d.]]

__B.I.1.b
after historical tenses, in similes, where the aorist is gnomic, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 5.490 (αὔοι codices)]]; where aorist is treated as equivalent to perfect, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 9.99, 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 8.580, 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 5.91, 5th c.BC: Lysias Orator 1.4, 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 9.26]]: when the purpose is regarded from the point of view of the speaker's present, σὲ παῖδα ποιεύμην ἵ. μοι.. λοιγὸν ἀμύνῃς [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 9.495, compare 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.29, 6.100, 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 1.44, +others, 5th c.BC: Lysias Orator 1.11,12, +others]]

__B.I.1.c
after optative and ἄν, when optative with οὐκ ἄν is used with sense of imperative, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 24.264, 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 6.58]]; after βουλοίμην ἄν.., [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Lysias Orator 7.12.]]

__B.I.1.d
after imperfect with ἄν, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 23.7.]]

__B.I.2
with optative,

__B.I.2.a
after historical tenses, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 5.3, 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 3.2, 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Septem contra Thebas” 215, 5th c.BC: Lysias Orator 3.11, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Protagoras” 314c, etc.]]: after the historical present, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Hecuba” 11]]: sometimes both moods, subjunctive and optative, follow in consecutive clauses, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 3.77, 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 8.76, 9.51, 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 23.93, 49.14.]]

__B.I.2.b
after optative, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 18.369, 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Philoctetes” 325; βούλοιντ᾽ ἂν ἡμᾶς ἐξολωλέναι, ἵνα.. λάβοιεν 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Pax” 413.]]

__B.I.2.c
rarely after primary tenses, by a shifting of the point of view, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 17.250, 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Ranae” 24, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 410c.]]

__B.I.3
with past tenses of indicative,

__B.I.3.a
after unfulfilled wishes, [Refs [[prev. author] “Cri.” 44d.]]

__B.I.3.b
after indicative with ἄν, to express a consequence which has not followed or cannot follow, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Tyrannus” 1389, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Meno” 89b, 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 29.17: especially after ἐβουλόμην ἄν.., 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Vespae” 961, 5th c.BC: Lysias Orator 4.3.]]

__B.I.3.c
after such Verbs as ἐχρῆν, ἔδει, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Hippolytus” 647, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Protagoras” 335c, “Smp.” 181e, “Euthd.” 304e, 5th-6th c.BC: Isocrates Orator 9.5, 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 24.48, 4th-3rd c.BC: Menander Comicus 349.5, etc.: whenan unfulfilled obligation is implied, τεθαύμακα ὅτι οὐκ εἶπεν (={ἔδει εἰπεῖν}).. ἵ... 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Theaetetus” 161c]]; ἀντὶ τοῦ κοσμεῖν (={δέον κοσμεῖν}).. ἵ... [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 36.47.]]

__B.I.3.d
after present indicative in general statements (including the past), οὐδὲ γὰρ τὸ εἶναι ἔχει ἡ ὕλη, ἱ. ἀγαθοῦ ταύτῃ μετεῖχεν [Refs 3rd c.AD+ [3rd c.AD: Plotinus Philosophus 1.8.5.]]

__B.I.4
ἵ. μή as the negative of ἵνα, that not, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 19.348, etc.]]

__B.II
special usages:

__B.II.1
like{ὅπως}, after Verbs of command and entreaty, is common only in later Gr. (but[NT+8th c.BC+ [compare 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 3.327 with [prev. work] 19), ἀξιοῦν ἵ... Decrees cited in 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 18.155; δεήσεσθαι ἵ... 1st c.BC: Dionysius Halicarnassensis 1.83; παρακαλεῖν ἵ... 2nd c.AD: Arrianus Historicus “Epicteti Dissertationes” 3.23.27: frequently in “NT”, ἐκήρυξαν ἵ. μετανοήσωσιν NT.Mark.6.12, +others; of will, ὅσα ἐὰν θέλητε ἵ. ποιῶσιν.. [prev. work] 25: hence ἵ. with _subjunctive_ stands for infinitive, ἐν τούτῳ ἵ. καρπὸν φέρητε (={ἐν τῷ φέρειν}) NT.John.15.8, etc.; πρῶτόν ἐστιν ἵ. κοιμηθῶ 2nd c.AD: Arrianus Historicus “Epicteti Dissertationes” 1.10.8, compare 2nd c.AD: Marcus Antoninus Imperator 8.29]]; also for ὥστε, [LXX+1st c.AD+ [LXX.Gen.22.14, +others, 1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus 2.333a, 3rd c.AD: Porphyrius Tyrius Philosophus “de Abstinentia - Porphyrii Opuscula” 2.33, etc.]]

__B.II.2
because, ἵ. ἀναγνῶ ἐτιμήθην I was honoured because I read, [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [Anonymus cited in 2nd c.AD: Apollonius Dyscolus Grammaticus “de Syntaxi;” 266.5, compare “Conj.” 243.21, 4th-5th c.AD: Choeroboscus Grammaticus “Scholia in Theodosii Canones” 2.257, +others]]; not found in literature.

__B.II.3
elliptical usages,

__B.II.3.a
where the purpose of the utterance is stated, Ζεὺς ἔσθ᾽, ἵν᾽ εἰδῇς 'tis Zeus,— [I tell thee this] that thou may'st know it, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Philoctetes” 989; ἵ. μὴ εἴπω ὅτι οὐδεμιᾷ 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 507d; ἵ. συντέμω 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 45.5; ἵν᾽ ἐκ τούτων ἄρξωμαι [prev. author] 21.43]]; ἵ. δῶμεν.. granted that.. , [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd c.AD: Sextus Empiricus Philosophus “Πυρρώνειοι ὑποτυπώσεις” 2.34, compare 1.79.]]

__B.II.3.b
in commands, introducing a principal sentence, ἵ. συντάξῃς order him.., [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [“PCair.Zen.” 240.12 (3rd c.BC)]]; ἵ. λαλήσῃς [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [“PSI” 4.412.1 (3rd c.BC)]]; ἵ. ἐλθὼν ἐπιθῇς τὰς χεῖρας αὐτῇ [LXX+NT+5th c.BC+ [NT.Mark.5.23,cf. NT.2Cor.8.7, LXX.2Mac.1.9, 2nd c.AD: Arrianus Historicus “Epicteti Dissertationes” 4.1.41, 1st c.BC: Didymus Grammaticus cited in Scholia 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Coloneus” 156.]]

__B.II.3.c
ἵ. τί (i.e. γένηται); to what end? either absolutely or as a question, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Ecclesiazusae” 719]]; or with a Verb following, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. author] “Pax” 409, compare 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Apologia” 26d, etc.]]; ἵ. δὴ τ; [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Nubes” 1192.]]

__B.II.3.d
in indignant exclamations, to think that.. ! Σωκράτης ἵ. πάθῃ ταῦτα [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd c.AD: Arrianus Historicus “Epicteti Dissertationes” 1.29.16.]]

__B.III
in later Gr. with indicative, [LXX+NT [LXX.Exo.1.11, +others, NT.Gal.2.4, 4.17, etc.]]

elsewhere relative, in which place, where,[Refs 8th c.BC+ [2.558, 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 9.136, 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 2.133, 9.27, 54, 5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “O.” 1.95, 5th c.BC: Bacchylides Lyricus 10.79, 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Prometheus Vinctus” 21, +others, 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Electra” 22, 855, 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Ranae” 1231, etc.]]: rarely in Attic dialect Prose, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Lysias Orator 13.72 (see. below), 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Apologia” 17c, “Phlb.” 61b]]; ἵ. ἡ Νίκη (i.e. ἐστίν) [Refs 8th c.BC+ [“IG” 22.1407.13: rare in later Greek, 2nd c.AD: Arrianus Historicus “Anabasis” 1.3.2, 2nd c.AD: Lucianus Sophista “Cont.” 22, “Ind.” 3: with particles, ἵ. τε 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 20.478; ἵ. περ 24.382, 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 13.364, 5th c.BC: Lysias Orator]] [same place]; ἵν᾽ ἄν with subjunctive, wherever, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Coloneus” 405, 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Ion” 315]]; as indirect interrogative, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.179, 2.150, 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Hecuba” 1008.]]

__I.2.b
after [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Homerus Epicus, like other Advs. of Place, with _genitive_, ἵ. τῆς χώρης 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.98]]; ἔμαθε ἵ. ἦν κακοῦ in what a calamity, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. author] 1.213; οὐδ᾽ ὁρᾶν ἵν᾽ ἐ̄ κακοῦ 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Tyrannus” 367]]; ἵν᾽ ἕσταμεν χρείας[Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. work] 1442; ἵν᾽ ἦμεν ἄτης [prev. author] “El.” 936; ὁρᾷς ἵν᾽ ἐσμὲν αὐτοῦ πέρι τῆς ἀπορίας 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Sophista” 243b.]]

__I.2.c
with Verbs of motion, whither, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 4.821, +others; ὁρᾷς ἵν᾽ ἥκεις 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Tyrannus” 687, +others, 4th-3rd c.BC: Dinarchus Orator 2.10; ιναπερ ὥρμητο 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 4.74.]]

__II
of circumstance, γάμος.., ἵ. χρή at which, when, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 6.27]]; ἵ. μὲν ἐξῆν αὐτοῖς.., ἐνταῦθα.. when it was in their power, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Antipho Orator 6.9.]]

__II.2
={ἐάν}, uncertain in [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 7.353 (variant{ἵν᾽ ἄν}, cf. Scholia), 7th c.BC: Archilochus Lyricus 74.7 codices, variant in 4th-3rd c.BC: Dinarchus Orator 1.1, and 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Charmides” 176b.]]

__B
Final conjunction, that, in order that, from [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Homerus Epicus]] downwards, mostly first word in the clause, but sometimes preceded by an emphatic word, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Charmides” 169d; ἵ. δή 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 7.26, 23.207, 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.29, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 420e, 610c: never with ἄν]] or κε (if found, these particles belong to the Verb, as in [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 12.156, 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Iphigenia Aulidensis” 1579).]]

__B.I
general usage:

__B.I.1
with subjunctive,

__B.I.1.a
after primary tenses of indicative, also subjunctive and imperative: present indicative, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 3.252, 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 2.111, 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Memorabilia” 3.2.3, “Cyr.” 1.2.11, 5th-6th c.BC: Isocrates Orator 3.2]]: perfect indicative, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 1.203, 5th-6th c.BC: Isocrates Orator 4.129]]: future, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 2.307, 4.591, 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 1.2.15]]; subjunctive, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Tyrannus” 364; _imperative_, 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 19.348, +others, 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Prometheus Vinctus” 61, 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Philoctetes” 880, 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Ranae” 297, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 341b, “Men.” 71d.]]

__B.I.1.b
after historical tenses, in similes, where the aorist is gnomic, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 5.490 (αὔοι codices)]]; where aorist is treated as equivalent to perfect, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 9.99, 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 8.580, 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 5.91, 5th c.BC: Lysias Orator 1.4, 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 9.26]]: when the purpose is regarded from the point of view of the speaker's present, σὲ παῖδα ποιεύμην ἵ. μοι.. λοιγὸν ἀμύνῃς [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 9.495, compare 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.29, 6.100, 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 1.44, +others, 5th c.BC: Lysias Orator 1.11,12, +others]]

__B.I.1.c
after optative and ἄν, when optative with οὐκ ἄν is used with sense of imperative, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 24.264, 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 6.58]]; after βουλοίμην ἄν.., [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Lysias Orator 7.12.]]

__B.I.1.d
after imperfect with ἄν, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 23.7.]]

__B.I.2
with optative,

__B.I.2.a
after historical tenses, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 5.3, 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 3.2, 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Septem contra Thebas” 215, 5th c.BC: Lysias Orator 3.11, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Protagoras” 314c, etc.]]: after the historical present, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Hecuba” 11]]: sometimes both moods, subjunctive and optative, follow in consecutive clauses, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 3.77, 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 8.76, 9.51, 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 23.93, 49.14.]]

__B.I.2.b
after optative, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 18.369, 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Philoctetes” 325; βούλοιντ᾽ ἂν ἡμᾶς ἐξολωλέναι, ἵνα.. λάβοιεν 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Pax” 413.]]

__B.I.2.c
rarely after primary tenses, by a shifting of the point of view, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 17.250, 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Ranae” 24, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 410c.]]

__B.I.3
with past tenses of indicative,

__B.I.3.a
after unfulfilled wishes, [Refs [[prev. author] “Cri.” 44d.]]

__B.I.3.b
after indicative with ἄν, to express a consequence which has not followed or cannot follow, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Tyrannus” 1389, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Meno” 89b, 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 29.17: especially after ἐβουλόμην ἄν.., 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Vespae” 961, 5th c.BC: Lysias Orator 4.3.]]

__B.I.3.c
after such Verbs as ἐχρῆν, ἔδει, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Hippolytus” 647, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Protagoras” 335c, “Smp.” 181e, “Euthd.” 304e, 5th-6th c.BC: Isocrates Orator 9.5, 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 24.48, 4th-3rd c.BC: Menander Comicus 349.5, etc.: whenan unfulfilled obligation is implied, τεθαύμακα ὅτι οὐκ εἶπεν (={ἔδει εἰπεῖν}).. ἵ... 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Theaetetus” 161c]]; ἀντὶ τοῦ κοσμεῖν (={δέον κοσμεῖν}).. ἵ... [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 36.47.]]

__B.I.3.d
after present indicative in general statements (including the past), οὐδὲ γὰρ τὸ εἶναι ἔχει ἡ ὕλη, ἱ. ἀγαθοῦ ταύτῃ μετεῖχεν [Refs 3rd c.AD+ [3rd c.AD: Plotinus Philosophus 1.8.5.]]

__B.I.4
ἵ. μή as the negative of ἵνα, that not, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 19.348, etc.]]

__B.II
special usages:

__B.II.1
like{ὅπως}, after Verbs of command and entreaty, is common only in later Gr. (but[NT+8th c.BC+ [compare 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 3.327 with [prev. work] 19), ἀξιοῦν ἵ... Decrees cited in 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 18.155; δεήσεσθαι ἵ... 1st c.BC: Dionysius Halicarnassensis 1.83; παρακαλεῖν ἵ... 2nd c.AD: Arrianus Historicus “Epicteti Dissertationes” 3.23.27: frequently in “NT”, ἐκήρυξαν ἵ. μετανοήσωσιν NT.Mark.6.12, +others; of will, ὅσα ἐὰν θέλητε ἵ. ποιῶσιν.. [prev. work] 25: hence ἵ. with _subjunctive_ stands for infinitive, ἐν τούτῳ ἵ. καρπὸν φέρητε (={ἐν τῷ φέρειν}) NT.John.15.8, etc.; πρῶτόν ἐστιν ἵ. κοιμηθῶ 2nd c.AD: Arrianus Historicus “Epicteti Dissertationes” 1.10.8, compare 2nd c.AD: Marcus Antoninus Imperator 8.29]]; also for ὥστε, [LXX+1st c.AD+ [LXX.Gen.22.14, +others, 1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus 2.333a, 3rd c.AD: Porphyrius Tyrius Philosophus “de Abstinentia - Porphyrii Opuscula” 2.33, etc.]]

__B.II.2
because, ἵ. ἀναγνῶ ἐτιμήθην I was honoured because I read, [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [Anonymus cited in 2nd c.AD: Apollonius Dyscolus Grammaticus “de Syntaxi;” 266.5, compare “Conj.” 243.21, 4th-5th c.AD: Choeroboscus Grammaticus “Scholia in Theodosii Canones” 2.257, +others]]; not found in literature.

__B.II.3
elliptical usages,

__B.II.3.a
where the purpose of the utterance is stated, Ζεὺς ἔσθ᾽, ἵν᾽ εἰδῇς 'tis Zeus,— [I tell thee this] that thou may'st know it, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Philoctetes” 989; ἵ. μὴ εἴπω ὅτι οὐδεμιᾷ 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 507d; ἵ. συντέμω 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 45.5; ἵν᾽ ἐκ τούτων ἄρξωμαι [prev. author] 21.43]]; ἵ. δῶμεν.. granted that.. , [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd c.AD: Sextus Empiricus Philosophus “Πυρρώνειοι ὑποτυπώσεις” 2.34, compare 1.79.]]

__B.II.3.b
in commands, introducing a principal sentence, ἵ. συντάξῃς order him.., [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [“PCair.Zen.” 240.12 (3rd c.BC)]]; ἵ. λαλήσῃς [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [“PSI” 4.412.1 (3rd c.BC)]]; ἵ. ἐλθὼν ἐπιθῇς τὰς χεῖρας αὐτῇ [LXX+NT+5th c.BC+ [NT.Mark.5.23,cf. NT.2Cor.8.7, LXX.2Mac.1.9, 2nd c.AD: Arrianus Historicus “Epicteti Dissertationes” 4.1.41, 1st c.BC: Didymus Grammaticus cited in Scholia 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Coloneus” 156.]]

__B.II.3.c
ἵ. τί (i.e. γένηται); to what end? either absolutely or as a question, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Ecclesiazusae” 719]]; or with a Verb following, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. author] “Pax” 409, compare 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Apologia” 26d, etc.]]; ἵ. δὴ τί; [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Nubes” 1192.]]

__B.II.3.d
in indignant exclamations, to think that.. ! Σωκράτης ἵ. πάθῃ ταῦτα [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd c.AD: Arrianus Historicus “Epicteti Dissertationes” 1.29.16.]]

__B.III
in later Gr. with indicative, [LXX+NT [LXX.Exo.1.11, +others, NT.Gal.2.4, 4.17, etc.]]

ἱππεύς, -έως (on accusative pl., -εῖς, ν. BI., § 8, 2; Thack., Gr., 148), ὁ

LSJ / STEPBible (TFLSJ)
ἱππ-εύς,
genitive έως (-έω uncertain in [Refs 5th c.AD+ [5th c.AD(?): Hesychius Legal icographus)]], Epic dialect ῆος, ὁ, (ἵππος) one who fights from a chariot, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Homerus Epicus (only in 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad”), opposed to πεζός, 2.810]]; either of the driver or of the hero who fights, [Refs [12.66, 15.270]]; also of one who drives in a chariot-race, [Refs [23.262.]]

__2
horseman, rider, cavalryman, ἰππήων στρότος [Refs 7th c.BC+ [7th-6th c.BC: Sappho Lyrica “Papyrus fragments” in E. Diehl, 5.1, compare 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 3.88, 9.49, 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Persae” 14 (_anapaest meter_), 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Politica” 1270a29, etc.]]; τῆς πολιτείας ἱ. a public courier, [Refs 5th c.AD+ [5th c.AD: Aristaenetus Rhetor 1.26.]]

__3
groom, Class.Rev.[Refs [27.12 (Laodicea Combusta), 24.12, “JHS” 18.108 (near Lysias).]]

__II
ἱππεῖς, in social and political sense, knights, forming an aristocracy in early Greek communities, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Politica” 1297b18, etc.; at Eretria, [prev. work] 1306a35, “Ath.” 15.2]]; at Sparta, a royal bodyguard, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 8.124, compare 1.67, etc.; especially at Athens, the Second Class in Solon's constitution, 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Ἀθηναίων Πολιτεία” 7.3]]; later, an aristocratic corps of cavalry, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Equites” 225, 5th-6th c.BC: Andocides Orator 3.5, 4th c.BC: Philochorus Historicus 100, etc.]]

__II.2
of the Roman equites, [Refs 1st c.BC+ [1st c.BC: Diodorus Siculus Historicus 37.8, 1st c.BC: Dionysius Halicarnassensis 4.24, 2nd c.AD: Appianus Historicus “Bella Civilia” 1.22, etc.]]; ἱππεὺς Ῥωμαίων,= Latin eques Romanus, [Refs [Mon.Anc.Gr. 7.17, “IG” 3.768a, “IGRom.” 3.204 (from Ancyra), “OGI” 547.2 ([prev. passage]), 645.7 (from Palmyra), probably in “IGRom.” 4.1213 (from Thyatira).]]

__III
nimble kind of crab, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Historia Animalium” 525b8.]]

__IV
kind of comet, [Refs 1st c.AD+ [1st c.AD: Plinius Rerum Naturalium Scriptor “Historia Naturalis” 2.90, 6th c.AD: Lydus, Joannes Laurentius Historicus “de Ostentis” 11.]]

__V
girl's ornament, [Refs 2nd c.BC+ [5th c.AD(?): Hesychius Legal icographus, compare “Ostr.” 323 (2nd c.BC).]]

__VI
a measure, πυρῶν, ἀμυγδάλων, ἀλεύρων, [Refs [“Supp.epigram” 2.710 (from Pednelissus).]]

of horsemen or chariots, ἀγών [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.167, 5th-6th c.BC: Andocides Orator 4.26 (_plural_); in ἱππικῶν ἀγών 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Electra” 698, ἱππικῶν is probably _neuter_ (see. below iv); δρόμος [prev. work] 754]]; ναυάγια[Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. work] 730; ἆθλον 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Leges” 949a.]]

of riding or horsemanship, equestrian, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Historia Graeca (Hellenica)” 5.3.20]]; ἱ. ἄσκησις training in horsemanship, [Refs [Inscriptiones Graecae 22.1042.21, +others]]; ἱ. ἡγήτωρ leader of the knights, [Refs [[prev. work]3.693]]; skilled in riding, opposed to ἄφιππος, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Protagoras” 350a, +others]]: comparative, [Refs 1st c.BC+ [1st c.BC(?): Satyrus Epigrammaticus 1, 1st c.BC: Philodemus Gadarensis Epigrammaticus “Mus.” p.6]] K.: superlative, [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd c.AD: Arrianus Historicus “Tactica” 16.9.]]

[πράγματα] [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus Alcaeus1.124e, compare “Thg.” 126a]]; ἡ ἐμὴ ἱ. this riding of mine, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Lysias Orator 24.10.]]

__III
fit for riding, superlative -ώτατον, χρῆμα γυνή [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Lysistrata” 677.]]

τὸ ἱ. the horse, cavalry, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 7.87, 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Supplices” 682, 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 6.5.29, etc.]]; τὰ ἱ. [Refs 2nd c.BC+ [2nd c.BC: Polybius Historicus 3.114.5.]]

__IV.2
course or space of four stadia, [Refs 1st c.AD+ [1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus “Solon” 23.]]

the circus at Rome, [Refs [“Tab.Defix.Aud.” 187.59.]]

__2
the constellation [Refs 4th c.BC+ [“Pegasus”, 4th c.BC: Eudoxus Astronomus cited in 2nd c.BC: Hipparchus Astronomicus 1.2.12, 2nd c.AD: Ptolemaeus Mathematicus “Tetrabiblos” 27, 2nd c.AD: Vettius Valens Astrologus 12.11.]]

__3
title of Hecate in the Mithraic cult, [Refs 3rd c.AD+ [3rd c.AD: Porphyrius Tyrius Philosophus “de Abstinentia - Porphyrii Opuscula” 4.16.]]

perhaps an instrument of torture, Latin eculeus, [Refs 1st c.AD+ [1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus “Lucullus” 20 (_plural_).]]

as Collective Noun, ἵππος, ἡ, horse, cavalry, ἡ τῶν Θεσσαλῶν ἵ. [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 5.64, etc.: always in _sing._, even with numerals, ἵ. χιλίη]] a thousand horse, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [[prev. author] 7.41; μυρίη [prev. passage]; μυρία, τρισμυρία, 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Persae” 302, 315]]; ἡ διακοσία ἵ. [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 1.62; ἵππον ἔχω εἰς χιλίαν 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 4.6.2.]]

__III
a sea-fish, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Antimachus Colophonius Elegiacus et Epicus et 2nd c.AD: Numenius Apamensis Platonicus cited in 2nd c.AD: Athenaeus Epigrammaticus 7.304e]]; but ὁ ἵ. ὁ ποτάμιος the hippopotamus, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 2.71, 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Historia Animalium” 502a9; ὁ ἵ. τοῦ Νείλου 3rd c.AD(?): Achilles Tatius Astronomus 4.2.]]

as appellative, ἶρις, ἡ, genitive ἴριδος [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-3rd c.BC: Theophrastus Philosophus “de Causis Plantarum” 6.11.13, also εως 1st c.AD: Andromachus Poeta Medicus cited in 2nd c.AD: Galenus Medicus 14.43, “POxy.” 1088.34 (1st c.AD), “Geoponica” 6.8.1]]; accusative ἶριν [Refs 2nd c.BC+ [“Michel” [same place], 1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus 2.664e, ἴριδα 2nd c.BC: Nicander Epicus “Alexipharmaca” 406]]; Epic dialect dative plural ἴρισσιν (see. below):—rainbow, δράκοντες.., ἴρισσιν ἐοικότες, ἅς τε Κρονίων ἐν νέφεϊ στήριξε, τέρας μερόπων ἀνθρώπων [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 11.27, compare 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Meteorologica” 375a1, 4th-3rd c.BC: Epicurus Philosophus “Epistulae” 2p.51U.]]

__II.2
any bright-coloured circle surrounding another body, as the lunar rainbow, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Meteorologica” 375a18;]]halo of candle, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-3rd c.BC: Theophrastus Philosophus “de Signis Tempestatum” 13; round the eyes of a peacock's tail, 2nd c.AD: Lucianus Sophista “Dom.” 11]]; the iris of the eye, [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd c.AD: Rufus Medicus “περὶ ὀνομασίας” 24, [2nd c.AD: Galenus Medicus] 14.702]]; also, section through the ciliary region, [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd c.AD: Galenus Medicus “de Usu Partium” 10.2.]]

__II.3
iridescent garment, [Refs [Michel [prev. cited]]]

__II.4
various species of the botanical genus iris, e.g. the purple Iris, I. germanica or pallida, εὐάνθεμον ἶριν [Refs 4th c.BC+ [“Anthologia Graeca” 4.1.9 (1st c.BC: Meleager Epigrammaticus); τὸ ἄνθος πολλὰς ἔχει ἐν αὑτῷ ποικιλίας 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “de Coloribus” 796b26, compare 1st c.AD: Plinius Rerum Naturalium Scriptor “Historia Naturalis” 21.40]]; also, the white variety of it, I. florentina, from the rhizome of which the orris-root of commerce is made, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-3rd c.BC: Theophrastus Philosophus “Historia Plantarum” 1.7.2, “CP” 6.11.13, etc.; ἶρις Ἰλλυρική 1st c.AD: Dioscorides (Dioscurides) Medicus 1.1, compare 1st c.AD: Plinius Rerum Naturalium Scriptor “Historia Naturalis” 13.14]]: in this sense some wrote it oxytone ἰρίς, ίδος, [Refs [12th c.AD: Eustathius Episcopus Thessalonicensis 391.33, Scholia Nic. [prev. cited]]]

__II.5
a precious stone, [Refs 1st c.AD+ [1st c.AD: Plinius Rerum Naturalium Scriptor “Historia Naturalis” 37.136.]]

deep_entry:
Abbott-Smith / STEPBible (TBESG)
- to know, see, understand
Occurs as Perfect with Present meaning

---

LSJ / STEPBible (TFLSJ)
Related to:  εἴδω,
no active present in use, ὁράω being used:—middle, see.below [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus 11]]: aorist 2 εἶδον always in sense of see (so in present and aorist 1 middle, to be seen, i.e. seem): but perfect οἶδα, in present sense, know. (With ἔ-ϝιδον, compare (ϝ) είδομαι, (ϝ) εῖδος, Latin videre; with (ϝ) οῖδα, cf. Sanskrit véda, Gothic wait, O[Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus]] wát 'know'.)

__A
aorist 2 εἶδον (late εἶδα [Refs 5th c.AD+ [5th-6th c.AD: Orphica “Argonautica” 118), serving as]]aorist to ὁράω, Epic dialect ἴδον, iterative ἴδεσκε [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 3.217]], late Aeolic dialect εὔιδον [Refs [“epigram Gr.” 990.11 (from Balbilla)]]; imperative ἴδε (in Attic dialect written as adverb ἰδέ, behold! Hdn.Gr.2.23), ἴδετ; subjunctive ἴδω, Epic dialect ἴδωμι [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 18.63]]; optative ἴδοιμ; infinitive ἰδεῖν, Epic dialect ἰδέει; participle ἰδών: hence, future ἰδησῶ [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [3rd c.BC: Theocritus Poeta Bucolicus 3.37:]] —middle, aorist 2 εἰδόμην, Epic dialect ἰδόμην, in same sense, poetry, Ionic dialect, and later Prose (with genitive, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-3rd c.BC: Aratus Epicus 430) (so in compounds, even in _Attic dialect_ Prose, see at {ἐπ-}, προ-, ὑπ-ειδόμην)]]; imperative ἰδοῦ (frequently written as adverb ἰδού, ={ἰδέ}); subjunctive ἴδωμα; optative ἰδοίμη; infinitive ἰδέσθα; participle ἰδόμενος [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.88, +others:]]

__1
see, perceive, behold, ὀφθαλμοῖσι or ἐν ὀφθαλμοῖσι ἰδέσθαι see before the eyes, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 1.587, etc.; ἰδεῖν ἐν ὄμμασιν 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Orestes” 1020]]; ἄγε, πειρήσομαι ἠδὲ ἴδωμαι well, I will try and see, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 6.126, compare 21.159]]; mark, observe, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 4.476, 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 4.412, etc.: followed by _relative_ clause, ἴδωμ᾽ ὅτιν᾽ ἔργα τέτυκται 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 22.450; ἀλλ᾽ ἄγε θᾶσσον ἰδώμεθα ὅττι τάδ᾽ ἐστίν 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 10.44]]: frequently in infinitive after substantive or adjective, θαῦμα ἰδέσθαι a marvel to behold, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 5.725; οἰκτραῖσιν ἰδεῖν 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Prometheus Vinctus” 240; ἐλεινὸς ἰδεῖν 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 620a.]]

__1.b
see a person, i.e. meet him, speak with him, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 4.125, 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 2.4.15, etc.]]

__1.c
see, i.e. experience, νόστιμον ἦμαρ ἰδέσθαι [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 3.233, etc.; δούλειον ἦμαρ ἰδεῖν 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Hecuba” 56; ἀέλιον ἕτερον ἰδεῖν 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Trachiniae” 835; τὴν δίκην ἰδεῖν [prev. author] “Ant.” 1270 (Lyric poetry)]]; ἀλόχου κουριδίης.. οὔ τι χάριν ἴδε he saw (i.e. enjoyed) not the favour of his wedded wife, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 11.243.]]

__2
look, ἰδεῖν ἐς.. look at or towards, [Refs [2.271, etc.; ἰδεῖν ἐπί.. 23.143]]; πρός.. [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 12.244]]; εἰς ὦπα ἰδέσθαι look him in the face, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 9.373, etc.; κατ᾽ ἐνῶπα ἰδών 15.320; ἄντα, ἐσάντα, or ἄντην ἰδεῖν, 13.184, 17.334, 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 5.78, etc.: qualified by]] adverb or adjective, ὑπόδρα ἰδών looking askance, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 1.148, +others]]; ἀχρεῖον ἰδών looking helpless, [Refs [2.269]]; κέρδος ἰδεῖν look to gain, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Eumenides” 541 (Lyric poetry).]]

__3
see mentally, perceive, ἰδέσθαι ἐν φρεσίν 'to see in his mind's eye', [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 21.61, compare 4.249; ἰδεῖν τῇ διανοίᾳ 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 511a.]]

__3.b
examine, investigate, [Refs [[prev. author] “Phd.” 70e, “Tht.” 192e]]; consider, ἴδωμεν τί λέγομεν [Refs [[prev. author] “Grg.” 455a.]]

__II
middle, present εἴδομαι, Epic dialect ἐείδεται [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [3rd c.BC: Theocritus Poeta Bucolicus 25.58]], participle ἐειδόμενος [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “N..” 10.15:]]aorist εἰσάμην, Epic dialect participle ἐεισάμενος [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 2.22, +others]]:—only Epic dialect and Lyric poetry, to be seen, appear, εἴδεται ἄστρα they are visible, appear,[Refs 8th c.BC+ [8.559; εἰ. ἦμαρ ὑπὸ Τρώεσσι δαμῆναι 13.98; εἴσατο δέ σφι δεξιός 24.319; ὅπη τὸ Ταρτάρειον εἴδεται βάθρον “epigram Gr.” 1034.19 (from Callipolis), compare 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 5.283]]; perhaps also οὔ πῃ χροὸς εἴσατο none of the skin was visible, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 13.191.]]

__II.2
with infinitive, appear or seem to be, τὸ δέ τοι κὴρ εἴδεται εἶναι [Refs 8th c.BC+ [1.228; τοῦτό τί μοι κάλλιστον ἐνὶ φρεσὶν εἴδεται εἶναι 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 9.11, etc.]]: with infinitive omitted, οἱ τό γε κέρδιον εἴσατο θυμῷ [Refs 8th c.BC+ [19.283, etc.; οὐ μέν μοι κακὸς εἴδεται 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 14.472, compare 3rd c.BC: Theocritus Poeta Bucolicus 25.58]]; also, look like or make a show of.., εἴσατ᾽ ἴμεν ἐς Λῆμνον he made a show of going to Lemnos, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 8.283]]; εἴσατο δ᾽ ὡς ὅτε ῥινόν it had the look as of a shield, [Refs [5.281.]]

__II.3
strictly middle, with dative, εἴσατο φθογγὴν Πολίτῃ she made herself like Polites in voice, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 2.791, compare 20.81; αὐδὴν εἰσάμενός τινι 3rd c.BC: Rhianus Epicus 50]]: especially in participle, like, εἰδομένη κήρυκι [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 2.280, etc.; τῷ δ᾽ ὄψιν ἐειδόμενος 5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “N.” 10.15; εἰδόμενος τοκεῦσιν 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Agamemnon” 771 (Lyric poetry); φάσμα εἰδόμενόν τινι 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 6.69.]]

__B
perfect, οἶδα I know, used as present: pluperfect ᾔδεα (see. below), I knew, used as imperfect:—perfect οἶδα, Aeolic dialect ὄϊδα [Refs 7th c.BC+ [7th-6th c.BC: Alcaeus Lyricus 145]]; 2nd pers. singular οἶδας once in [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Homerus Epicus, 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 1.337, compare “hymnus ad Mercurium” 456, 6th c.BC: Theognis Elegiacus 491, 6th c.BC: Hipponax Iambographus 89, 5th c.BC: Hippocrates Medicus “περὶ διαίτης ὀξέων” 67, 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Alcestis” 780, 4th-3rd c.BC: Philemo Comicus 44.3 codices]]; οἶσθα elsewhere in [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Homerus Epicus]], Attic dialect, etc.; in Comedy texts also sometimes οἶσθας [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Cratinus Comicus 105, 2nd c.AD: Alexander Rhetor 15.11, 4th-3rd c.BC: Menander Comicus 348.5, compare 3rd c.BC: Herodas Mimographus 2.55]]; plural, ἴσμεν, Epic dialect, Aeolic dialect, and Doric dialect ἴδμεν, also Ionic dialect, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.6, +others]]; ἴστε, ἴσασι [ῐς- [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 2.211, +others, but ῑς- [prev. work] 283, +others]]; οἴδαμεν [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 2.17, οἴδατε “Anthologia Graeca” 12.81 (1st c.BC: Meleager Epigrammaticus), οἴδᾱσι 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 2.43, 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Oeconomicus” 20.14 codices; dual, οἴδατον 5th-4th c.BC: Socratis et Socraticorum Epistulae “Ep.” 22.1: _imperative_ ἴσθι, ἴστω, _Boeotian dialect_ ἴττω, late ἰδέτω 3rd-2nd c.BC: Phalaris Epistolographus “Epistulae - Epistolographi” 122 codices: from _3rd.pers._ _plural_ ἴσασι (ἴσαντι 5th c.BC: Epicharmus Comicus 53)]] were formed Doric dialect 1st pers. singular ἴσᾱμι [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Epicharmus Comicus 254, 5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “P.” 4.248]]; 3rd.pers. singular ἴσατι [Refs [“IG” 14.644.4 (from Bruttii)]]; 1st pers. plural ἴσᾰμεν [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “N.” 7.14, ἴσαμες probably in “Dialexeis 5th c.BC” 6.12]]; Cretan dialect 3rd.pers. plural subjunctive ἴθθαντι [Refs [“GDI” 5024]]; infinitive ϝισάμην[Refs [Kohler-Ziebarth “Stadtrecht von Gortyn” 34 No.3.19]]; participle ἴσας [Refs 5th c.BC+ [2nd c.AD: Apollonius Dyscolus Grammaticus “de Adverbiis;” 175.19, _dative_ _sing._ ἴσαντι 5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “P.” 3.29, Cretan dialect _plural_ ἴθθαντες “GDI” 5024:]]subjunctive εἰδῶ (εἰδέω, ἰδέω, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 14.235, 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 16.236)]], Ionic dialect 3rd.pers. plural εἰδέωσι [Refs 5th c.BC+ [“SIG” 45.21 (Halic., 5th c.BC)]]; Epic dialect also εἴδω [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 1.174, +others (compare 2nd c.AD: Herodianus Grammaticus Gr. 2.131), εἴδομεν 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 1.363, εἴδετε 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 9.17: _optative_ εἰδείην]], 1st pers. plural εἰδεῖμεν [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Laches” 190b, “R.” 582a]]: infinitive εἰδέναι, Epic dialect ἴδμεναι, ἴδμεν, also ἰδέμεν [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “N.” 7.25]]: participle εἰδώς, εἰδυῖα, Epic dialect also ἰδυῖα, Elean ϝειζώς [Refs [“Schwyzer” 409]]:—pluperfect ᾔδεα [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 14.71, 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 2.150]], contraction ᾔδη [Refs 8th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Antigone” 18, 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Aves” 511, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Symposium” 119a, ᾔδησθα 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 19.93, 5th c.BC: Eupolis Comicus 416, etc. (but ᾔδεισθα]] frequently in codices, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Ecclesiazusae” 551, 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Cyclops” 108, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Meno” 80d, +others), ᾔδεε (ν) 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 17.402, +others, ᾔδη 1.70, +others]] (also later Attic dialect, accusative to [Refs 5th c.BC+ [3rd-2nd c.BC: Aristarchus Grammaticus cited in 4th-5th c.AD: Choeroboscus Grammaticus “Scholia in Theodosii Canones” 2.86), _Attic dialect_ _contraction_ ᾔδει (ν) 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Ion” 1187, 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Vespae” 558, etc.; _Epic dialect_ 2 and _3rd.pers._ _sing._ ἠείδης, ἠείδη]] (variant -εις, - ει), [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 22.280, 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 9.206]]; Attic dialect also 1st pers. singular ᾔδειν [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 37.24]], 2nd pers. singular ᾔδεις [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Thesmophoriazusae” 554, etc.; _plural_, ᾔδειμεν 4th c.BC: Aeschines Orator 3.82, 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Analytica Posteriora” 87b40, ᾔδεμεν 4th-3rd c.BC: Menander Comicus 14D. (to be read in 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Tyrannus” 1232), ᾔδειτε 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 55.9, etc. (ᾔδετε probably in 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Bacchae” 1345)]], Ionic dialect ᾐδέατε [LXX+6th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 9.58 (συν-), ᾔδεισαν LXX.Gen.42.23, 1st c.BC-1st c.AD: Strabo Geographus 15.3.23, ᾔδεσαν 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 7.175, 6th c.BC: Theognis Elegiacus 54, etc.]]; late Epic dialect ᾔδειν, ἠείδειν, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [3rd c.BC: Apollonius Rhodius Epicus 2.65, 4.1700, also ᾖσμεν, ᾖστε, ᾖσαν, 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Fragmenta” 149.4 (probably), 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Fragmenta” 340, 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Cyclops” 231, etc.]]; Epic dialect 3rd.pers. plural ἴσαν [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 18.405, 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 4.772]]:—future, in this sense, εἴσομαι [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 1.548, 5th c.BC: Hippocrates Medicus “περὶ ἀρχαίης ἰητρικῇς” 20, 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Acharnenses” 332, etc.; also εἰδήσω 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 7.327, 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 7.234, 5th-6th c.BC: Isocrates Orator 1.44, 4th c.BC: Aeneas Tacticus 31.5, 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Topica” 108a28, 3rd c.BC: Herodas Mimographus 5.78, 3rd-2nd c.BC: Apollonius Pergaeus Geometra “Conica” 1 “Praef.”, etc.]]; infinitive εἰδησέμεν [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 6.257.]] —The aorist and perfect are usually supplied by γιγνώσκ; aorist 1 infinitive εἰδῆσαι is found in [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Hippocrates Medicus “Acut.(Sp.”) 22, “Epid.” 6.8.25 (ἐξ-), 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Ethica Nicomachea” 1156b27, 4th-3rd c.BC: Theophrastus Philosophus “Char. __B.2
with infinitive, know how to do, οἶδ᾽ ἐπὶ δεξιά, οἶδ᾽ ἐπ᾽ ἀριστερὰ νωμῆσαι βῶν [Refs 5th c.BC+ [7.238, compare 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Philoctetes” 1010, 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Vespae” 376]]; also, to be in a condition, be able, have the power, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Medea” 664, 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 4.40]]; of drugs, ὅσα λεπτύνειν οἶδε [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd c.AD: Alexander Rhetor Trall. “Febr.” 6]]; of a festival, οἶδε ἐκπέμπουσα δάκνειν Chor.p.124 [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Bacchylides Lyricus]]; learn, ἵν᾽ εἰδῇ μὴ 'πὶ τοῖς ἐμοῖς κακοῖς ὑψηλὸς εἶναι [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Hippolytus” 729.]]

__B.3
with participle, to know that such and such is the fact, the participle being in nominative when it is a predicate of the Subject of the Verb, ἴσθι μοι δώσων know that thou wilt give, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Agamemnon” 1670; ἴστω ὑπὸ τοῦ ἀδελφεοῦ ἀποθανών 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 4.76; οὐ γὰρ οἶδα δεσπότας κεκτημένος 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Hecuba” 397]]: in accusative when it is predicate of the Object, τοὺς φιλτάτους γὰρ οἶδα νῷν ὄντας πικρούς [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Choephori” 234; τὸν Μῆδον ἴσμεν ἐκ περάτων γῆς ἐλθόντα 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 1.69: with]]participle omitted, γῆν αὐτὰ οἶδεν ἀμφότερα (i.e. ὄντα) [Refs 4th c.AD+ [4th c.AD: Julianus Imperator “Orationes” 7.226a.]]

__B.4
less frequently c.accusative et infinitive, πλήθους.. ἂν σάφ᾽ ἴσθ᾽ ἕκατι βάρβαρον ναυσὶν κρατῆσαι [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Persae” 337, compare 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Philoctetes” 1329; εὖ ἴσθι τοῦτον.. ἰσχυρῶς ἀνιᾶσθαι 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 8.3.44; also εὖ τόδ᾽ ἴσθι, μηδάμ᾽ ἡμέρᾳ μιᾷ πλῆθος τοσουτάριθμον ἀνθρώπων θανεῖν 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Persae” 431; ἕν γ᾽ ἀκούσασ᾽ ἴσθι, μὴ ψευδῶς μ᾽ ἐρεῖν 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Iphigenia Aulidensis” 1005.]]

__B.5
with accusative followed by ὡς, ὅτι, etc., οἶδα κἀμαυτὴν ὅτι ἀλγῶ [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Electra” 332; ἐάν τινα εἰδῶσιν ὅτι ἄδικός ἐστι 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Protagoras” 323b, etc.]]

__B.6
οὐκ οἶδ᾽ εἰ.. I know not whether, to express disbelief or doubt, sometimes with ἄν transposed, οὐκ οἶδ᾽ ἂν εἰ πείσαιμί σε [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Alcestis” 48, compare 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 45.7: with Verb omitted after εἰ, as οὐκ οἶδ᾽ εἴ τις ἄλλος]] perhaps no other, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Isocrates Orator 6.1, 12.10.]]

__B.7
in similar ellipses with other Conjunctions, οὐκ οἶδ᾽ ὅπως I know not how, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 40c b; οὐκ οἶδ᾽ ὁπόθεν [prev. author] “Cra.” 396d.]]

__B.8
οἶδα, ἴσθι are frequently parenthetic, οἶδ᾽ ἐγώ [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Medea” 948; σάφ᾽ οἶδα [prev. work] 94, 963]]; also οἶδ᾽ ὅτι, οἶσθ᾽ ὅτι, ἴσθ᾽ ὅτι, πάρειμι δ᾽ ἄκων οὐχ ἑκοῦσιν, οἶδ᾽ ὅτι (i.e. πάρειμι) I know it well, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Antigone” 276]]; οἶδ᾽ ὅτι, frequently in [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator, as 9.1, +others; σάφ᾽ ἴσθ᾽ ὅτι 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Plutus” 889:]] —οἶσθ᾽ ὅ, οἶσθ᾽ ὡς, with _imperative_, are common in Trag. and Comedy texts, οἶσθ᾽ οὖν ὃ δρᾶσον; do—thou know'st what, i.e. make haste and do, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Equites” 1158, compare “Pax” 1051, etc.]]; οἶσθ᾽ ὡς πόησο; [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Tyrannus” 543]]; also οἶσθ᾽.. ὡς νῦν μὴ σφαλῇ; [Refs [[prev. author] “OC” 75]]; οἶσθα νῦν ἅ μοι γενέσθ; [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Iphigenia Taurica” 1203: rarely with the]]future, οἶσθ᾽ οὖν ὃ δράσεις (nisileg. δρᾶσον); [Refs [[prev. author] “Cyc.” 131, compare “Med.” 600 codices]]

Abbott-Smith / STEPBible (TBESG)
εἰμί,
with various uses and significations, like the English verb to be.
__I. As substantive verb.
__1. Of persons and things, to be, exist: Act.17:28, Jhn.1:1, 8:58, 17:5, al; ὁ ὢν καὶ ὁ ἦν (for past ptcp.), Rev.1:4, 8, 4:8, 11:17, 16:5 (see Swete, Ap., 5; M, Pr., 228); τὰ (μὴ) ὄντα, Rom.4:17, 1Co.1:28.
__2. Of times, events, etc., to be, happen, take place: Mat.24:3, Mrk.14:2, 15:42, Luk.21:23, Jhn.4:6, 23, 5:10, al.
__3. to be present, be in a place, have come: Mat.2:13, 15, Mrk.1:45, 5:21, 15:40, Luk.1:80, 5:29, Jhn.7:30, al.; before εἰς, Mrk.2:1; before  ἐκ, (ἐξ), Mat.1:20, 21:25, Mrk.11:30, Jhn.3:31, al.
__4. Impers.,  ἔστι, ἦν, etc.;
__(a) there is (Fr. il y a), was, etc.: Mat.16:28, Luk.16:19, Jhn.3:1, 5:2, Rom.3:10, al.; with dative (of the possessor; Bl., §37, 3), Mat.16:22, Luk.1:7, Jhn.18.10, Rom.9:2, al.;  ἔστιν ὅς, ὅστις (chiefly in pl), Mat.16:28, 19:2, Mrk.9:1, al.;
__(b) with inf., = ἔξεστιν (which see), it is possible: Heb.9:5, 1Co.11:20, RV (but see ICC, in l.).
__II. As copula uniting subject and predicate.
__1. Expressing simply identity or equivalence: Mat.5:13, 14:15, Luk.1:18, 19, Jhn.1:1, 4:19, Rev.3:9, al. mult.
__2. Explicative, as in parable, figure, type, etc.: Mat.13:19, 1Co.9:2, 10:4, 11:25, Gal.4:24, Rev.17:15, al.; ταῦτ᾽ ἔστιν, Mat.27:46, Mrk.7:2, Rom.7:18 al.; ὅ ἐστιν, Mrk.3:17, Col.1:24, Heb.7:2, al.; akin to this is the sacramental usage: Mat.26:26-28, Mrk.14:22, 24, Luk.22:19, 1Co.11:24 (see ICC on Mk, I Co, ll. with; DB, iii, 148 f.).
__3. C. genitive: qual., etc., Mrk.5:42, Luk.3:23, 1Co.14:33, Heb.12:11, al.; part., 1Ti.1:20, 2Ti.1:15; poss., Mat.5:3, 10, Mrk.12:7, Luk.4:7; of service or partisanship, Rom.8:9, 1Co.1:12, 2Co.10:7, 2Ti.2:19.
__4. C. dative (BL, §37, 3): Act.1:8, 9:15, Rom.4:12, 1Co.1:18, 2:14, Rev.21:7, al.
__5. C. ptcp., as a periphrasis for the simple verb (Bl., §62, 1, 2; M, Pr., 225 ff.);
__(a) with ptcp. pf. (cl.): Mat.10:30, Luk.9:32, Jhn.3:24, Act.21:35, 1Co.15:19, al;
__(b) with ptcp. pr. (esp. in impf., as in Heb. and Aram.; Dalman, Words, 35 f.), Mat.7:29, Mrk.1:22, Luk.4:31, 14:1, Act.1:10, al. mult., id. for imper. (M, Pr., 180f., 182f.), with ellipsis of εἰμί, Rom.12:9, 10, Heb.13:5, al.;
__(with) with ptcp. aor. (cl), Luk.23:9.
__6. Seq. εἰς (cf. Heb. הָיָה לְ), a vernac. usage (M, Pr., 71): Mat.19:5, Mrk.10:8, Heb.8:10, al.
__7. C. adv.: Mat.19:20, Mrk.4:26, Luk.18:11, al.
__8. Ellipses;
__(a) of the copula (Bl., §30, 3): Mat.8:29, 24:32, Jhn.21:22, 23, Heb.6:4, al.;
__(b) of the predicate: ἐγώ εἰμί, Mat.14:27, Mrk.6:50, al.; absol. (cf. Deu.32:39; אֲנִי הוּא), Mrk.13:6, Jhn.4:26, al. (cf. ἄπ-, ἔν-, πάρ-, συμ-πάρ-, σύν-ειμι).

ἔστι impersonal, with infinitive, it is possible, ἔστι γὰρ ἀμφοτέροισιν ὀνείδεα μυθήσασθαι [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 20.246; ἔστι μὲν εὕδειν, ἔστι δὲ τερπομένοισιν ἀκούειν 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 15.392]]; εἴ τί πού ἐστι (i.e. πιθέσθαι)[Refs 5th c.BC+ [4.193; τοιάδε.. ἐστὶν ἀκοῦσαι 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Prometheus Vinctus” 1055 (_anapaest meter_); ἔστι τεκμήρια ὁρᾶν 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 3.2.13, compare 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Ranae” 1163, 4th c.BC: Aeschines Orator 3.105, 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 18.272, 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Ἀθηναίων Πολιτεία” 53.6, etc.]]; so in imperative, optative, and subjunctive, ἔστω ἀποφέρεσθαι τῷ βουλομένῳ [Refs 8th c.BC+ [“IG” 12.10.7; μυρία ἂν εἴη λέγειν 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Politicus” 271e; ὅπως ἂν ᾖ δρᾶν “IG” 2.1054.91: more frequently in _negative_ clauses, 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 6.267, etc.]]; followed by ὥστε with infinitive, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Philoctetes” 656]]: with accusative et infinitive, ἁδόντα δ᾽ εἴη με τοῖς ἀγαθοῖς ὁμιλεῖν [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “P.” 2.96; ἔστιν ἐκπεσεῖν ἀρχῆς Δία 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Prometheus Vinctus” 757]]: sometimes not impersonal in this sense, θάλασσα δ᾽ οὐκέτ᾽ ἦν ἰδεῖν [Refs [[prev. author] “Pers.” 419.]]

__A.VI.b
ἔστω in argument, let it be granted, ἔστω τοῦτο ἀληθὲς εἶναι [Refs 4th c.BC+ [1st c.BC: Dionysius Halicarnassensis “de Compositione Verborum” 25; ἔστω σοι τοῦθ᾽ οὕτως 1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus 2.987b; ἔστω εἶναί τινα τοιοῦτον 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator Chr.74.24.]]

__B
most frequently, to be, the Copula connecting the predicate with the Subject, both being in the same case: hence, signify, import, τὸ γὰρ εἴρειν λέγειν ἐστίν [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Cratylus” 398d]]; especially in the phrase τοῦτ᾽ ἔστι, hoc est; Σκαιόλαν, ὅπερ ἐστὶ Λαϊόν [Refs 1st c.AD+ [1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus “Publicola” 17: with numerals, τὰ δὶς πέντε δέκα ἐστίν]] twice five are ten, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Memorabilia” 4.4.7]]; εἶναί τις or τι, to be somebody, something, be of some consequence, see at {τι; οὐδὲν εἶναι} [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 562d, etc.]]

__B.2
periphrastic with the Participle to represent the finite Verb: with perfect participle once in [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Homerus Epicus, τετληότες εἰμέν, for τετλήκαμεν, 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 5.873]]; so in Trag. and Attic dialect, ἦν τεθνηκώς, for ἐτεθνήκει, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Agamemnon” 869]]; ἔσται δεδορκώς[Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. work] 1179; εἰμὶ γεγώς 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Ajax” 1299; πεφυκός ἐστι 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Aves” 1473; δεδρακότες εἰσίν 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 3.68; κατακεκονότες ἔσεσθε 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 7.6.36]]: with aorist participle, once in [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Homerus Epicus, βλήμενος ἦν 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 4.211]]; so προδείσας εἰμί, οὐ σιωπήσας ἔσε; [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Tyrannus” 90, 1146, compare 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Supplices” 460]]: with present participle, ἦν προκείμενον [Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. author] “Pers.” 371; φεύγων Ὀρέστης ἐστίν [prev. author] “Ch.” 136; εἴην οὐκ ἂν εὖ φρονῶν 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Ajax” 1330]]; τί δ᾽ ἐστί.. φέρο; [Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. author] “OT” 991, compare 274, 708; λέγων ἐστίν τις 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Hecuba” 1179; ἦν τίς σ᾽ ὑβρίζων [prev. author] “HF” 313; πόρρω ἤδη εἶ πορευόμενος 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Lysis” 204b; βαδίζων εἰμί 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Ranae” 36; frequently in 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus, ἦσαν ἱέντες 1.57, +others; even εἰσὶ διάφοροι ἐόντες 3.49 (assuming variant):]] — if the _Article_ is joined with the Part., the noun is made emphatic, Κᾶρές εἰσι οἱ καταδέξαντες the persons who showed her were Carians, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. author] 1.171; αὐτὸς ἦν ὁ μαρτυρῶν 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Eumenides” 798; δόλος ἦν ὁ φράσας 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Electra” 197 (_anapaest meter_).]]

__C
εἶναι is frequently modified in sense by the addition of adverbs, or the cases of Nouns without or with Preps.:

__C.I
εἶναι with adverbs, where the adverb often merely represents a Noun and stands as the predicate, ἅλις δέ οἱ ἦσαν ἄρουραι [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 14.122, etc.]]; ἀκέων, ἀκήν εἶναι, to be silent,[Refs 8th c.BC+ [4.22, 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 2.82; σῖγα πᾶς ἔστω λεώς 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Hecuba” 532; διαγνῶναι χαλεπῶς ἦν ἄνδρα ἕκαστον 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 7.424]]; ἀσφαλέως ἡ κομιδὴ ἔσται will go on safely, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 4.134]]; ἐγγύς, πόρρω εἶναι, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 6.88, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Protagoras” 356e: frequently _impersonal_ with words implying good or ill fortune, Κουρήτεσσι κακῶς ἦν]] it fared ill with them, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 9.551; εὖ γὰρ ἔσται 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Medea” 89, compare 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Plutus” 1188, etc.; ἡδέως ἂν αὐτοῖς εἴη 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 59.30.]]

__C.II
with genitive, to express descent or extraction, πατρὸς δ᾽ εἴμ᾽ ἀγαθοῖο [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 21.109; αἵματός εἰς ἀγαθοῖο 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 4.611, compare 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 3.71, 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 2.71, etc.; πόλεως μεγίστης εἶ 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 7.3.19.]]

__C.II.b
to express the material of which a thing is made, ἡ κρηπίς ἐστι λίθων μεγάλων consists of.., [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.93; τῆς πόλιος ἐούσης δύο φαρσέων [prev. work] 186]]; τοιούτων ἔργων ἐστὶ ἡ τυραννίς is made up of.., [Refs [[prev. author] 5.92]].ή, etc.

__C.II.c
to express the class to which a person or thing belongs, εἶ γὰρ τῶν φίλων you are one of them, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Plutus” 345; ἐτύγχανε βουλῆς ὤν 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 3.70; ὅσοι ἦσαν τῶν προτέρων στρατιωτῶν [prev. author] 7.44; Κριτίας τῶν τριάκοντα ὤν 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Memorabilia” 1.2.31]]; ἔστι τῶν αἰσχρῶν it is in the class of disgraceful things, i. e. it is disgraceful, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 2.2.]]

__C.II.d
to express that a thing belongs to another, Τροίαν Ἀχαιῶν οὖσαν [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Agamemnon” 269; τὸ πεδίον ἦν μέν κοτε Χορασμίων 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 3.117, etc.]]: hence, to be of the party of, ἦσαν.. τινὲς μὲν φιλίππου, τινὲς δὲ τοῦ βελτίστου [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 9.56, compare 37.53]]; to be de pendent upon, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Antigone” 737, etc.]]; to be at the mercy of, ἔστι τοῦ λέγοντος, ἢν φόβους λέγῃ [Refs [[prev. author] “OT” 917.]]

__C.II.e
to express one's duty, business, custom, nature, and the like, οὔτοι γυναικός ἐστι 'tis not a woman's part, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Agamemnon” 940; τὸ ἐπιτιμᾶν παντὸς εἶναι 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 1.16]]; τὸ δὲ ναυτικὸν τέχνης ἐστίν is matter of art, requires art, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 1.142, compare 83.]]

__C.II.f
in LXX, to be occupied about, ἦσαν τοῦ θύειν [LXX.2Ch.30.17]; ἔσεσθαι, with genitive, to be about to, ἐσόμεθα τοῦ σῶσαί σε [LXX.2Ki.10.11.]

__C.III
with the dative, ἐστί μοι I have, frequently in [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Homerus Epicus, etc.]]

__C.III.2
with two datives., σφίσι τε καὶ Ἀθηναίοισι εἶναι οὐδὲν πρῆγμα that they and the Athenians have nothing to do one with another, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 5.84; μηδὲν εἶναι σοὶ καὶ φιλίππῳ πρᾶγμα 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 18.283]]; more shortly, σοί τε καὶ τούτοισι πρήγμασι τί ἐστ; [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 5.33]]; τί τῷ νόμῳ καὶ τῇ βασάν; [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 29.36]]; τί ἐμοὶ καὶ σο; Latin quid tecum est mihi? [NT.Mark.5.7, etc.]; also ἐμοὶ οὐδὲν πρὸς τοὺς τοιούτους (i.e. ἐστίν) [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Isocrates Orator 4.12; ἐν οἷς πρὸς τοὺς ἐναντίους ἐστὶ τῷ δήμῳ 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 18.278]]; ἔσται αὐτῳ πρὸς τὸν θεόν, in tomb inscriptions, [Refs [“JHS” 18.113, etc.]]

__C.III.3
with ἄσμενος, βουλόμενος, etc., added, ἐμοὶ δέ κεν ἀσμένῳ εἴη 'twould be to my delight, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 14.108; οὐκ ἂν σφίσι βουλομένοις εἶναι 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 7.35; προσδεχομένῳ [prev. author] 6.46; θέλοντι 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Tyrannus” 1356 (Lyric poetry); ἡδομένοις 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Laches” 187c.]]

__C.IV
with Preps., εἶναι ἀπό τινος, ={εἶναί τινος}[Refs 5th c.BC+ [(above 11.a), 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Memorabilia” 1.6.9; εἰσὶν ἀπ᾽ ἐναντίων αὗται πραγμάτων 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Philebus” 12d]]; but εἶναι ἀπ᾽ οἴκου to be away from.., [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 1.99.]]

__C.IV.2
εἶναι ἔκ τινος to be sprung from, εἴμ᾽ ἐκ Παιονίης, Μυρμιδόνων ἔξ εἰμι, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 21.154, 24.397, etc.]]; ἔστιν ἐξ ἀνάγκης it is of necessity, i. e. necessary, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Sophista” 256d.]]

__C.IV.3
εἶναι ἐν.. to be in a certain state, ἐν εὐπαθείῃσι [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.22]]; ἐν ἀθυμία, etc., [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 6.46, etc.; ἐν ταραχαῖς 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 18.218]]; εἶναι ἐν ἀξιώματι to be in esteem, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 1.130]]; οἱ ἐν τέλεϊ ἐόντες those in office, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 3.18, etc.]]; but εἶναι ἐν τέχνῃ, ἐν φιλοσοφία to be engaged in.., [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Tyrannus” 562, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Phaedo” 59a.]]

__C.IV.3.b
ἐν σοί ἐστι it depends on thee, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 6.109, 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Philoctetes” 963; ἐν σοὶ γάρ ἐσμεν [prev. author] “OT” 314; so also ἐπί τινι [prev. author] “Ph.” 1003, 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 1.6.2, etc.]]

__C.IV.4
εἶναι διά.., much like{εἶναι ἐν}.., εἶναι διὰ φόβου, ={φοβεῖσθαι}, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 6.34]]; εἶναι δι᾽ ὄχλου, ={ὀχληρὸν εἶναι}, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. author] 1.73; εἶναι διὰ μόχθων 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 1.6.25]]; εἶναι δι᾽ αἰτίας, ={αἰτιᾶσθαι}, [Refs 1st c.BC+ [1st c.BC: Dionysius Halicarnassensis 1.70]]; Geometry texts, pass through, διὰ τᾶς ἑτέρας διαμέτρου ἐόντος τοῦ ἐπιπέδου [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [3rd c.BC: Archimedes Geometra “περὶ κωνοειδέων καὶ σφαιροειδέων” 20.]]

__C.IV.5
εἶναι ἐφ᾽ ἑαυτῆς to be by oneself, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 25.23]]; εἶναι ἐπὶ ὀνόματος to bear a name, [Refs [[prev. author] 39.21]]; εἶναι ἐπὶ τοῖς πράγμασιν to be engaged in.., [Refs [[prev. author] 2.12]]; εἶναι ἐπί τινα to be against him, [Refs [[prev. author] 6.33]]; εἶναι ἐφ᾽ ἑξήκοντα στάδια to reach sixty stadia, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 4.6.11]]; εἶναι ἐπὶ τὰς ἁφάς pass through the points of contact, [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd c.AD: Apollonius Biographus Perg. “Con.” 4.1]]; εἶναι ἐπί τινι, see above 3 b.

__C.IV.6
εἶναι πρός τινος to be in one's favour, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 4.10, 29, etc.]]; to suit, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 1.2.11, etc.]]; εἶναι πρός τινι engaged in, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Phaedo” 84c, 2nd-3rd c.AD: Philostratus Sophista “Vita Apollonii” 5.31]]; πρὸς τοῖς ἰδίοις mind one's own affairs, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Politica” 1309a6, “Ath.” 16.3; εἶναι πρὸς τὸ κωλύειν 2nd c.BC: Polybius Historicus 1.26.3]]; πρὸς τὸ πονεῖν[Refs 5th c.BC+ [Teles p.46 H.; εἶναι περί τι 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 3.5.7, etc.]]

__C.IV.7
εἶναι παρά τινι or τινα, = παρειναι, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. author] “Cyr.” 6.2.15, 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 8.140.ά]] (assuming variant).

__C.IV.8
εἶναι ὑπό τινα or τινι to be subject to.., [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Historia Graeca (Hellenica)” 5.2.17 (assuming variant), 6.2.4.]]

__C.IV.9
περὶ τούτων ἐστίν that is the question, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-3rd c.BC: Menander Comicus “Ἐπιτρέποντες” 30.]]

__C.IV.10
εἶναι ἀπό.., in Geometry texts, to be constructed upon, [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [3rd c.BC: Archimedes Geometra “περὶ σφαίρας καὶ κυλίνδρου” 2.9, “Con.Sph.” 7.]]

__D
ἐστί is very frequently omitted, mostly in the present indicative before certain predicates, as ἀνάγκη, ἄξιον, δυνατόν, εἰκός, ἕτοιμον, οἷόν τε, ῥᾴδιον, χρεών, etc., and after the neuter of Verbals in -τέος, and such forms as θαυμαστὸν ὅσον: less frequently with other persons and moods, εἰμί omitted, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Tyrannus” 92, “Aj.” 813]]; εἶ, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 4.206]]; ἐσμέν, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Antigone” 634]]; ἐστέ, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 10.463]]; εἰσί, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Tyrannus” 499 (Lyric poetry), “IG” 2.778 B]]; subjunctive ᾖ, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 14.376, 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Hippolytus” 659, 5th c.BC: Antipho Orator 5.32]]; optative εἴη, [Refs [“IG” 22.1183.12]]; imperfect ἦν, [Refs [[prev. work]2.778 B]]; future ἔσονται, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 14.394.]]

__E
the Inf. frequently seems redundant,

__E.1
in phrases implying power or will to do a thing, ἑκὼν εἶναι (see. ἑκών) κατὰ δύναμιν εἶναι [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Isaeus Orator 2.32; εἰς δύναμιν εἶναι 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Politicus” 300c]]; τὸ ἐπ᾽ ἐκείνοις εἶναι, quantum in illis esset, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 8.48, 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Historia Graeca (Hellenica)” 3.5.9, compare 5th c.BC: Lysias Orator 13.58; τὸ ἐπὶ σφᾶς εἶναι 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 4.28; τὸ κατὰ τοῦτον εἶναι 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 1.6.9; κατὰ τοῦτο εἶναι 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Protagoras” 317a]]; τὸ τήμερον, τὸ νῦν εἶναι, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [[prev. author] “Cra.” 396e, “La.” 201c, Theopomp. Comedy texts 98, Decrees cited in 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Ἀθηναίων Πολιτεία” 31.2, etc.]]

__E.2
after Verbs of naming or choosing, σοφιστὴν ὀνομάζουσι τὸν ἄνδρα εἶναι [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Protagoras” 311e; σύμμαχόν μιν εἵλοντο εἶναι 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 8.134]]; of giving, δῶκε ξεινήϊον εἶναι [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 11.20.]]

__F
imperfect ἦνissts. used where other languages take the present,

__F.1
after ἄρα, to express a fact which is and has always been the same, δέρμα δὲ ἀνθρώπου.. ἦν ἄρα σχεδὸν δερμάτων πάντων λαμπρότατον human skin then it appears is.., [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 4.64; Κύπρις οὐκ ἄρ᾽ ἦν θεός 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Hippolytus” 359]]; ὡς ἄρ᾽ ἦσθ᾽ ἐμὸς πατὴρ ὀρθῶς[Refs 3rd c.BC+ [[prev. work] 1169; ἦ πολύμοχθον ἄρ᾽ ἦν γένος.. ἁμερίων [prev. author] “IA” 1330; ἦ στωμύλος ἦσθα 3rd c.BC: Theocritus Poeta Bucolicus 5.79]]; so also when there is reference to a past thought, τουτὶ τί ἦ; what is this? [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Acharnenses” 157, compare 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Cratylus” 387c: so in the Aristotelian formula τὸ τί ἦν εἶναι (“APo.” 82b38, +others)]], used to express the essential nature of a thing, where τί ἦν (for ἐστί) takes the place of the dative in such phrases as τὸ ἀγαθῷ εἶναι, τὸ μεγέθει εἶναι, [Refs [“APr.” 67b12, “de An.” 429b10.]]

__G
ἐγώ εἰμι, in [LXX, pleonastic for ἐγώ, ἐγώ εἰμι οὐχ ἥμαρτον LXX.Judg.11.27, compare 6.18; also ἔσται πᾶς ἀποκτενεῖ με LXX.Gen.4.14.]

ἴσος
(epic ἶσος, so sometimes Rec.), -η, -ον, [in LXX for כְּ֜, Jb  5:14; Job.10:10, al.; אֶחָד, Eze.40:5 ff.; 2Ma.9:15, 4Ma.13:20-21, al. ;]
equal, the same in size, number, quality, etc.: δωρεά, Act.11:17; μαρτυρίαι, Mrk.14:56, 59; ἴ. ποιεῖν, with accusative and dative, Mat.20:12; ἑαυτὸν τ. θεῷ, Jhn.5:18; τὰ ἴ. ἀπολαβεῖν, Luk.6:34, n. pl., ἴσα, adverbially, Rev.21:16; τ. θεῷ, Php.2:6.†

LSJ / STEPBible (TFLSJ)
ἴσος, η, ον,
Epic dialect ἶσος and ἔϊσος (see. below); Cretan dialect, [Refs 4th c.AD+ [4th c.AD(?): Arcadius Grammaticus]] ϝίσϝος [Refs 5th c.AD+ [“GDI” 4998ii2, 4982.2, “Schwyzer” 665, compare γισγόν· ἴσον, 5th c.AD(?): Hesychius Legal icographus]]; later ἵσος [Refs 4th c.BC+ [“Schwyzer” 708a (1) (Ephesus, 4th c.BC), “Tab.Heracl.” 1.175, etc.]]:— equal in size, strength, or number, with dative, κύματα ἶσα ὄρεσσιν [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 3.290, etc.]]; frequently of appearance, like, ἶσος ἀναύδῳ [Refs 7th c.BC+ [10.378; ἶσος Ἄρευι 7th-6th c.BC: Sappho Lyrica 91 (uncertain)]]; ἴσος θεοῖσιν Ead.2.1: frequently absolutely, ἴσην.. βίην καὶ κῦδος [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 7.205]]; ἶσον θυμὸν ἔχειν to be of like mind, [Refs [13.704, 17.720: _neuter_ as]] adverb, ἶσον ἐμοὶ φρονέουσα [Refs [15.50; θεοῖσιν ἶσ᾽ ἔθελε φρονέειν 5.441, compare 21.315]], etc.; ἴσος τινὶ τὸ μέγαθος, ὕψος, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 2.32, 124]]; τὸ μῆκος, τὸ πλάτος, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 5.4.32; ἀριθμόν 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Supplices” 662]]; ἴσα τὸν ἀ. [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 441c]]; ποτὴν ἴσον equal in flight of song, [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [3rd c.BC: Alexander Aetolus Elegiacus 5.5]]; ἴσον, τό, copy of a document, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [“PLond.” 3.1222.5 (2nd c.AD), etc.: with _dative_ _person_ in place of an object of comparison, οὐ μὲν σοί ποτε ἶσον ἔχω γέρας (i.e. τῷ σῷ γέραϊ) 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 1.163]]; τοῖσδ᾽ ἴσας ναῦς (i.e. ταῖς τῶνδε) [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Iphigenia Aulidensis” 262 (Lyric poetry); ἴσα τοῖς νῦν στρατηγοῖς ἀγάθ᾽ εἰργασμένους 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 13.21: followed by a relative word, ἐμοὶ ἴσον.., ὅσονπερ ὑμῖν]] the same to me as to you, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Ecclesiazusae” 173; τὰ ἐκεῖ ἴσα, ὥσπερ τὰ ἐνθάδε 5th c.BC: Lysias Orator 19.36 codices (perhaps σᾶ)]]; τὰ ἴσα ὅσαπερ.. Legal cited in [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 23.44; ἴσον.. ὅπερ 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Eryxias” 405b.]]

__2
repeated to denote equal relations, ἴσα πρὸς ἴσα tit for tat, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.2; ταχθέντες ἴσοι πρὸς ἴσους 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Antigone” 142 (_anapaest meter_); ἴσους ἴσοισι.. ἀντιθείς 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Phoenissae” 750; ἴσα ἀντὶ ἴσων λαμβάνειν, ἐκδοῦναι 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Leges” 774c]]; ἴσος ἴσῳ (i.e. οἶνος ὕδατι) [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Cratinus Comicus 184, “Comica Adespota” 107, etc.]]; κύλικος ἴσον ἴσῳ κεκραμένης (where ἴσον is adverbial) [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Plutus” 1132; διδόναι γάλα καὶ οἶνον πίνειν ἴσον ἴσῳ 5th c.BC: Hippocrates Medicus “ἐπιδημίαι” 2.5.1: _metaphorically_, 'fairly blended', μηδὲν ἴσον ἴσῳ φέρων 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Acharnenses” 354.]]

__3
of persons, equal in rights, βούλεται ἡ πόλις ἐξ ἴσων εἶναι καὶ ὁμοίων [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Politica” 1295b25; ἡ πολιτικὴ ἐλευθέρων καὶ ἴσων ἀρχή [prev. work] 1255b20; τὸ κατ᾽ ἀξίαν ἴ. [prev. work] 1307a26, +others]]

__II
equally divided or distributed, ἴση μοῖρα [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 9.318]]; ἴση alone, one's equal share, μή τίς μοι ἀτεμβόμενος κίοι ἴσης [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 9.42 (ἴσσης conjecture Fick, compare ἴσσασθαι); τὴν ἴ. ἔχων 5th c.BC: Cratinus Comicus 250]]; οὐ μὴν ἴ. ἔτεισεν (i.e. τίσιν) [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Tyrannus” 810]]; ἄχρι τῆς ἴ. up to the point of equality, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 5.17: _neuter_, μὴ ἴσον νεῖμαι ἑκατέρῳ 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Protagoras” 337a; οὐ μόνον ἴσον, ἀλλὰ καὶ πλέον ἔχειν 5th-6th c.BC: Isocrates Orator 17.57]]; οὐκ ἀνέξῃ δωμάτων ἔχων ἴσον καὶ τῷδε νεῖμα; [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Phoenissae” 547]]; τὰ ἴσα fair measure, τὰ ἴ. νέμειν [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 6.11]]; μὴ ἴσων ἕκαστον τυγχάνειν ἀλλὰ πλεονεκτεῖν, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 2.2.20]]; προστυχεῖν τῶν ἴ. to obtain fair terms, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Philoctetes” 552]]; κἂν ἴσαι (i.e. ψῆφοι) γένωνται equally divided, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Ranae” 685.]]

__II.2
based on equality of rights, ἴ. καὶ ἔννομος πολιτεία [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aeschines Orator 1.5; τὴν πολιτείαν ἰσαιτέραν καθιστάναι 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 8.89]]; τὰ ἴ. equal rights, equality, frequently joined with τὰ ὅμοια or τὰ δίκαια, ὡς τῆς πολιτείας ἐσομένης ἐν τοῖς ἴ. καὶ ὁμοίοις [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Historia Graeca (Hellenica)” 7.1.45; τῶν ἴ. καὶ τῶν δικαίων ἕκαστος ἡγεῖται ἑαυτῷ μετεῖναι ἐν τῇ δημοκρατίᾳ 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 21.67; οὐ μέτεστι τῶν ἴ. οὐδὲ τῶν ὁμοίων πρὸς τοὺς πλουσίους τοῖς λοιποῖς [prev. work]112; τῶν ἴ. μετεῖχε τοῖς ἄλλοις [prev. work]96; also ἡ ἴ. καὶ ὁμοία (i.e. δίκη), τῆς ἴ. καὶ ὁμοίας μετέχειν 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 4.105]]; ἐπ᾽ ἴ. τε καὶ ὁμοίῃ on fair and equal terms, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 9.7, ά,compare 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 1.145]]; ἐπὶ τῇ ἴ. καὶ ὁμοίᾳ[Refs 4th c.BC+ [[prev. work] 27, compare “SIG” 312.27 (Samos, 4th c.BC), “OGI” 229.44 (Smyrna, 3rd c.BC)]], etc.: generally, just, fair, ἐκ ποίας ἴ. καὶ δικαίας προφάς εω; [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 18.284.]]

__II.3
of persons, fair, impartial, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Philoctetes” 684 (Lyric poetry), “OT” 677; ἴ. δικαστής 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Leges” 957c; ἴ. καὶ κοινοὶ ἀκροαταί 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 29.1, compare 18.7; ἴ. καὶ κοινὸν δικαστήριον [prev. author] 7.36; κοινοὺς μὲν.., ἴ. δὲ μή 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Protagoras” 337a; ἴ. ἴσθι κρινων 4th-3rd c.BC: Menander Comicus “Μονόστιχοι - Fragmenta Comicorum Graecorum” 266, compare 257; κριταὶ ἴ. καὶ δίκαιοι 2nd c.BC: Polybius Historicus 24.15.3, etc.]]

__II.4
adequate, ἡ ἴ. φρουρά [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 7.27]] (explained by Scholia as regular, τεταγμένη); ἴσος τοῖς παροῦσι [Refs [[prev. author] 1.132.]]

__III
of ground, even, flat, εἰς τὸ ἴ. καταβαίνειν, of an army, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 4.6.18 (but ἐν ἴσῳ προσιέναι]] to advance with even step, [Refs [[prev. work] 1.8.11)]]; λέουσιν εἰς τὸ ἴ. καθιστάμενοι μάχεσθαι, opposed to μετὰ πλεονεξίας ἀγωνίζεσθαι, on even terms, [Refs [[prev. author] “Cyr.” 1.6.28]]; ἴ. τοῖχος, opposed to κεκλικώς, perpendicular, [Refs 6th c.AD+ [6th c.AD: Philoponus, Joannes Philosophus “in Aristotelis Analytica Posteriora commentaria - pars” 2.27.]]

__IV
adverb ἴσως (see. entry): but also,

__IV.1
neuter singular and plural from [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Homerus Epicus downwards (see. entry [near the start]), ἶσον.. ἀπήχθετο κηρὶ μελαίνῃ]] even as Death, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 3.454]]; ἶσον ἐμοὶ βασίυε be king like me, [Refs [9.616]]; ἶσον γάρ σε θεῷ τίσουσιν Ἀχαιοί[Refs 8th c.BC+ [[prev. work] 603; ἶσον ἐμῇ κεφαλῇ 18.82; τὸν.. ἶσα θεῷ.. εἰσορόωσιν 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 15.520; ἶσα φίλοισι τέκεσσι 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 5.71, compare 13.176, 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 1.432, 11.304, etc.]]: later absolutely, alike, δείλαιε τοῦ νοῦ τῆς τε συμφορᾶς ἴσον [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Tyrannus” 1347; τὴν Σάμον καὶ Ἡρακλέας στήλας ἴσον ἀπέχειν 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 8.132: with _dative_, ἴσον ναοῖς θεῶν 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Helena” 801]]; ἴσον ἄπεσμεν τῷ πρίν equally as before, [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [[prev. author] “Hipp.” 302 (variant{τῶν πρίν}); ἴσα τοῖς πάνυ 2nd-3rd c.AD: Dio Cassius Historicus “fragment” 70.6]]; ἴσα καί.. like as, as if, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Tyrannus” 1187 (Lyric poetry), 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Electra” 994 (_anapaest meter_), 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 3.14; ἴσον ὡς.. 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Ion” 1363]]; ὥσπερ.. [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Electra” 532; ὥστε.. 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Orestes” 882; ἅτε.. [prev. author] “HF” 667 (Lyric poetry); ὅσονπερ.. 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 15.1.]]

__IV.2
with Preps.: ἀπὸ τῆς ἴσης equally, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 1.15; ὁ ἀπὸ τῆς ἴ. ἐχθρός [prev. author] 3.40; ἀπ᾽ ἴσης εἶναι 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 14.6; ἀφ᾽ ἵσου “SIG” 426.14 (Teos, 3rd c.BC)]]; δι᾽ ἴσου [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd-3rd c.AD: Dio Cassius Historicus 43.37]]; at equal distance, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 617b]]: also in in Mathematics texts, ex aequali, of proportions, [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [3rd c.BC: Euclides Geometra 5 “Def.” 17, +others]]; δι᾽ ἴ. ἐν τεταραγμένῃ ἀναλογίᾳ ex aequali in disturbed proportion, [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [3rd c.BC: Archimedes Geometra “περὶ σφαίρας καὶ κυλίνδρου” 2.4, +others, 3rd c.AD(?): Pappus Mathematicus 932.11]]; ἐν ἴσῳ equally, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 2.53, 4.65]]; ἐν ἴσῳ ἐστί it matters not, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Iphigenia Aulidensis” 1199; ἐν ἴσῳ [ἐστὶ] καὶ εἰ.. 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 2.60; ἐν τῷ ἴσῳ εἶναι [prev. author] 4.10; ἐξ ἴσης 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Leges” 861a: more frequently ἐξ ἴσου 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 7.135, 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Tyrannus” 563, etc.; ἐξ ἴ. τινί [prev. author] “Ant.” 516, 644, 5th c.BC: Antipho Orator 5.1, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Gorgias” 517a]]; evenly, εὐθεῖα γραμμή ἐστιν ἥτις ἐξ ἴ. τοῖς ἐφ᾽ ἑαυτῆς σημείοις κεῖται [Refs 5th c.BC+ [3rd c.BC: Euclides Geometra 1 “Def.” 4; ἐξ ἴ. καὶ.. 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Coloneus” 254; ὡς.. [prev. author] “OT” 61]]; οἱ ἐξ ἴ. persons of equal station, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Leges” 777d, compare 919d; ὁ ἐξ ἴ. κίνδυνος 2nd c.BC: Polybius Historicus 9.4.4; ἐκ τοῦ ἴ. γίγνεσθαί τινι 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 2.3; τοῖς ἐκ τοῦ ἴσου ἡμῖν οὖσι 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Hiero” 8.5; ἐξ ἴσου τισὶ τῆς πολιτείας μεταδιδόναι 5th c.BC: Lysias Orator 25.3]]; ἐκ τοῦ ἴ. μάχεσθαι to be evenly matched, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Historia Graeca (Hellenica)” 2.4.16; ἐξ ἴ. πολεμεῖν 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 8.47]]; κατὰ μῆνα τὸ αἱροῦν ἐξ ἴ. the sum due in equal monthly instalments, [Refs [“PAmh.” 2.92.14, etc.]]; ἐπὶ or ἐπ᾽ ἴσης, ἐπὶ ἴ. διαφέρειν τὸν πόλεμον [Refs 8th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.74; τοῦτο ἐπ᾽ ἴσης ἔχει [prev. author] 7.50, compare 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Electra” 1062 (Lyric poetry), etc.; ἐπ᾽ ἴσου 2nd c.BC: Polybius Historicus 1.18.10; ἐπ᾽ ἴσον [prev. author] 6.38.4, cf. Docum. cited in 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 18.106, 1st c.BC: Philodemus Gadarensis Epigrammaticus “Ir.” p.21 W.; ἐπὶ ἶσα μάχη τέτατο 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 12.436; compare κατὰ ἶσα μάχην ἐτάνυσσε 11.336; κατ᾽ ἴσον 1st c.AD: Dioscorides (Dioscurides) Medicus 1.68.6, 2nd c.AD: Galenus Medicus “de Usu Partium” 1.19]]; μετ᾽ ἴσου equally, [Refs 2nd c.BC+ [2nd c.BC: Demetrius Lacon Philosophus “Herc.” 124.12.]]

__V
comparative ἰσαίτερος [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Supplices” 441, 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 8.89, 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Historia Graeca (Hellenica)” 7.1.14: _superlative_ ἰσότατος Timo 68; ἰσαίτατος 1st c.AD: Philo Judaeus 1.462]]. adverb ὡς ἰσαίτατα [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Leges” 744c, but ὡς ἰσότατα “SIG” 531.30 (from Dyme)]]. [ῑ in early Epic dialect (except [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th-7th c.BC: Hesiodus Epicus “Opera et Dies” 752), compare 6th c.BC: Solon Lyricus 24.1: ῐ first in 6th c.BC: Theognis Elegiacus 678, 7th-6th c.BC: Sappho Lyrica 2.1 (but ἶσος Ead.91 assuming variant), 5th c.BC: Bacchylides Lyricus 5.46 (but ἶσον 1.62, “fragment” 2.2), and always in 5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus]] (except in compound ῑσοδαίμων) and Trag. [Refs 4th c.BC+ [(4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Fragmenta - American Journal of Philology” 216 is uncertain reading) except in _compound_ ῑσό-θεος (which see)]]; uncertain in ἰσ-όνειρος. Both quantities are found in later poetry, sometimes in same line, ἔχοισαν ἴσον κάτω, ἶσον ἄνωθεν [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [3rd c.BC: Theocritus Poeta Bucolicus 8.19; πρέσβυν ἴσον κούροις, ἶσον ἁδόντα κόραις “APl.” 4.309.]]]

Abbott-Smith / STEPBible (TBESG)
ἰσότης, -ητος, ἡ
(ἴσος), [in LXX: Job.36:30, Zec.4:7 * ;]
__1. equality: 2Co.8:13-14.
__2. equity, fairness: τὸ δίκαιον κ. τὴν ἰ., Col.4:1 (for dis­tinction bet. τὸ δ. and ἡ ἰ, see ICC, in l).†
(AS)

---

LSJ / STEPBible (TFLSJ)
ἰσότης, ητος, ἡ,
(ἴσος) equality, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Metaphysica” 1054b3, etc.: in _plural_, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Leges” 733b; ἰ. χρόνου [prev. author] “Prm.” 140e: in Mathematics texts, ἰ. γεωμετρική]] equality of ratios, proportion, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [[prev. author] “Grg.” 508a; ἀναλογία ἰ. λόγων 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Ethica Nicomachea” 1131a31.]]

__2
especially political equality or justice, personified in [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Phoenissae” 536, compare 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Leges” 757a; ἰ. πολιτική 2nd c.BC: Polybius Historicus 6.8.4, etc.: in dual, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Leges” 757b, compare 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Politica” 1302a7, 5th-6th c.BC: Isocrates Orator 7.21.]]

__II
fair dealing, impartiality, [NT+4th c.BC+ [4th-3rd c.BC: Menander Comicus “Μονόστιχοι - Fragmenta Comicorum Graecorum” 259, 2nd c.BC: Polybius Historicus 2.38.8, NT.Col.4.1.]]

__III
equiformity, of the earth, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-3rd c.BC: Epicurus Philosophus “De rerum natura - Wien. Stud.” 11.10. (On the accent see Hdn.Gr. 1.83, 2.945]]; ἰσοτής is said to be Hellenistic by [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd c.AD: Moeris Grammaticus 202.)]]

(ἴσος, τιμή),
equally privileged, held in equal honour: πίστις, 2Pe.1:1 (R, mg., equally precious, but v Field, Notes, 240; Mayor, in l).†
(AS)

---

LSJ / STEPBible (TFLSJ)
ἰσότιμ-ος, ον,
equal in honour or privilege, Απόλλων (i.e. sharing the honours paid to Zeus) [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [“OGI” 234.25 (Delph., 3rd c.BC), “CR Acad.Inscription” 1906.419 (from Alabanda); ὁ θεὸς.. -ον παρέχι τράπεζαν τοῖς ὁποθενοῦν ἀφικνουμένοις “BCH” 51.73 (from Panamara)]]; πίστις [NT.2Pet.1.1]; οἱ πρῶτοι καὶ ἰ.
