deep_entry:
Abbott-Smith / STEPBible (TBESG)
ἵστημι, and in late writers, also ἱστάνω (Veitch, see word; Bl., §23, 2; M, Pr., 55), [in LXX chiefly for עמד, קוּם, also for נצב ni., hi., יצב hith., etc.].
__I. Trans, in pres., impf., fut. and 1 aor. act. and in the tenses of the pass.
__1. to make to stand, to place, set, set up, establish, appoint: with accusative of person(s), Mrk.7:9, Act.1:23 6:13 17:31, Heb.10:9; id. before ἐπί, with accusative loc, Mat.4:5, Luk.4:9; ἐν μέσῳ, Mat.18:2, Mrk.9:36, Jhn.8:[3]; ἐνώπιον, Act.6:6; παρ᾽ ἑαυτῷ, Luk.9:47; ἐκ δεξιῶν, Mat.25:33; mid., to place oneself, to stand: Rev.18:15; so also pass., to be made to stand, to stand: Mat.2:9, Luk.11:18 19:8, 2Co.13:1, al.
__2. to set in a balance, to weigh (cl.; LXX for שׁקל, Isa.46:6, al.): Mat.26:15,
__II. Intrans., in pf., plpf. (with sense of present and impf.; M, Pr., 147f.) and 2 aor. act., to stand, stand by, stand still: Mat.20:32 26:73, Mrk.10:49, Luk.8:44, Jhn.1:35 3:29, Act.16:9, al.; before ἐν, Mat.6:5, al.; ἐνώπιον, Act.10:30, al.; πρός, with dative loc., Jhn.18:16; ἐπί, with genitive loc., Luk.6:17, Act.5:23 25:10, al.; ἔμπροσθεν, Mat.27:11; κύκλῳ, Rev.7:11; ἐκ δεξιῶν, Luk.1:11; ἐπί, with accusative, Mat.13:2, Rev.3:20; παρά, Luk.5:2; ἐκεῖ, Mrk.11:5; ὧδε, Mrk.9:1; ὅπου, Mrk.13:14; ἔξω, Mat.12:46; μακρόθεν, Luk.18:13; πόρρωθεν, Luk.17:12. Metaphorical, to stand ready, stand firm, be steadfast: 1Co.7:37 10:12, Eph.6:11, 13 14, Col.4:12; τ. πίστει, Rom.11:20; ἐν τ. ἀληθείᾳ, Jhn.8:44; εν τ. χάριτι, Rom.5:2; ἐν τ. εὐαγγελίῳ, 1Co.15:1 (cf. ἀν-, ἐπ-ἀν-, ἐξ-ἀν, ἀνθ-, ἀφ-, δι-, ἐν-, ἐξ-, ἐπ- (-μαι), ἐφ-, κατ-ἐφ-, συν-ἐφ-, καθ-, ἀντι-καθ-, ἀπο-καθ-, μεθ-, παρ-, περι-, προ-, συν-ίστημι).
(AS)

LSJ / STEPBible (TFLSJ)
ἵστημι
(compare ἱστάω, ἱστάνω),

__I
causal, make to stand, imperative ἵστη [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 21.313, 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Supplices” 1230, καθ-ίστα 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 9.202:]]imperfect ἵστην, Epic dialect ἵστασκε [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 19.574]]; 3rd.pers. plural ἵσταν [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Bacchylides Lyricus 10.112:]]future στήσω, Doric dialect στᾱσῶ [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [3rd c.BC: Theocritus Poeta Bucolicus 5.54]]: aorist 1 ἔστησα, Epic dialect 3rd.pers. plural ἔστᾰσαν for ἔστησαν uncertain in [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 18.307, 3.182, 8.435, +others (see. ἔστᾰσαν): hence, in late Poets, ἔστᾰσας, ἔστᾰσε, “Anthologia Graeca” 9.714,708 (1st c.AD: Philippus Epigrammaticus)]]: aorist 1 middle ἐστησάμην (never intransitive)[Refs 4th c.BC+ [, see below 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus 111.2, 3]]: perfect ἕστᾰκα [LXX+5th c.BC+ [3rd c.BC: Cercidas Iambographus 3, (καθ-) 4th c.BC: Hyperides Orator “pro Euxenippo” 28, “UPZ” 112.5 (2nd c.BC), (περι-) 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Axiochus” 370d, (ἀφ-) LXX.Jer.16.5, (παρ-) 1st c.BC: Philodemus Gadarensis Epigrammaticus “Rh.” 1.9S., +others, (συν-) 2nd c.AD: Sextus Empiricus Philosophus “adversus Mathematicos” 7.109]]; also ἕστηκα (see. below) in transitive sense, (δι-) [LXX+4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “de Ventis” 973a18, (ἀφ-) variant in LXX]] [same place]; ἑστακεῖα transitive in [Refs [“Test.Epict.” 1.25.]]

__II
intransitive, stand,

__II.1
active, aorist 2 ἔστην, Epic dialect στάσκον [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 3.217]]; 3rd.pers. plural ἔστησαν, more frequently in [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Homerus Epicus ἔσταν, στάν [ᾰ]]]; imperative στῆθι, Doric dialect στᾶθι [Refs 7th c.BC+ [7th-6th c.BC: Sappho Lyrica 29, 3rd c.BC: Theocritus Poeta Bucolicus 23.38;]]subjunctive στῶ, Epic dialect [Refs 8th c.BC+ [2 and _3rd.pers._ _sing._ στήῃς, στήῃ (for στῇς, στῇ), 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 17.30, 5.598]]; 1st pers. plural στέωμεν (as disyllable)[Refs [22.231, στείομεν 15.297]]; optative σταῖεν, Epic dialect 3rd.pers. plural σταίησαν [Refs [17.733]]; infinitive στῆναι, Epic dialect στήμεναι [Refs 8th c.BC+ [17.167, 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 5.414]], Doric dialect στᾶμεν [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “P.” 4.2]]; participle στάς: perfect ἕστηκα: pluperfect ἑστήκειν, sometimes with strengthened augment εἱστήκειν, as [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Hercules Furens” 925, 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Aves” 513, 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 1.89, etc.]]; Ionic dialect 3rd.pers. singular ἑστήκεε [Refs 8th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 7.152:—from 8th c.BC: Homerus Epicus downwards the shorter dual and _plural_ forms of the]]perfect are preferred, ἕστᾰτον, ἕστᾰμεν, ἕστᾰτε, ἑστᾶσι [Refs 6th c.BC+ [(“IG” 12(8).356 (Thasos, 6th c.BC), etc.), in 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus ἑστέᾱσι]]; imperative ἕστᾰθι [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristomenes Comicus 5]]; subjunctive ἑστ; optative ἑσταίη; infinitive ἑστάναι, Epic dialect ἑστάμεν, ἑστάμεναι (ἑστηκέναι only late, as [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd-3rd c.AD: Aelianus “Varia Historia” 3.18)]]; participle ἑστώς (ἑστηκώς rare in early Gr., [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 2.126, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Meno” 93d, “Lg.” 802c, 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus (below 5th c.BC: Bacchylides Lyricus 11.2), 2nd c.AD: Alexander Rhetor 126.16, εἱστηκότα “IG” 12.374.179), _feminine_ ἑστῶσα (not ἑστυῖα]]; but συνεστηκυιῶν probably in [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Hippocrates Medicus “Aër.” 10), _neuter_ ἑστός 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Timaeus” 40b, “Tht.” 183e, “SIG” 1234 (from Lycia), etc., (καθ-) “POxy.” 68.32 (2nd c.AD), (ἐν-) “PRyl.” 98 (a). 10 (2nd c.AD), (παρ-) 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Equites” 564 (-ώς]] frequently variant as in [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus and 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus [same places], preferred by 4th-5th c.AD: Choeroboscus Grammaticus “Scholia in Theodosii Canones” 2.313)]]; genitive ἑστῶτο; Ionic dialect ἑστεώς, ἑστεός, ῶτο; Epic dialect ἑστηώς [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th-7th c.BC: Hesiodus Epicus “Theogonia” 747]]; dative plural ἑστηῶσι conjecture in [Refs 8th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Antimachus Colophonius Elegiacus et Epicus 16.5, compare 3rd c.BC: Callimachus Epicus “Hymnus in Dianam” 134; 8th c.BC: Homerus Epicus does not use the _nominative_, but has _genitive_ ἑστᾰότος, _accusative_ ἑστᾰότα, _nominative_ _plural_ ἑστᾰότες, as if from ἑσταώς: so also]]pluperfect ἑστάτην, ἕστᾰμεν, ἕστᾰτε, ἕστᾰσαν: late present ἑστήκω, formed from perfect, [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [3rd c.BC: Posidippus Comicus cited in 2nd c.AD: Athenaeus Epigrammaticus 10.412e]]: hence, future ἑστήξω [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Homerus Epicus “Epigrammata” 15.14, 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 6.2.17, Hegesippus Epigrammaticus 1.25, ἑστήξομαι 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Cynegeticus” 10.9 codices]]

__II.2
passive, ἵσταμαι: imperative ἵστασο [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th-7th c.BC: Hesiodus Epicus “Scutum Herculis” 449, ἵστω 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Philoctetes” 893, 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Ecclesiazusae” 737:]]imperfect ἱστάμην: future στᾰθήσομαι [Refs 8th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Andocides Orator 3.34, 4th c.BC: Aeschines Orator 3.103: more frequently στήσομαι 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 20.90, etc.]]: aorist ἐστάθην [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 17.463, etc.]]; rarely ἔστην, Doric dialect 3rd.pers. singular ἔσστα [Refs 5th c.BC+ [“SIG” 56.43 (Argos, 5th c.BC):]]perfect ἕσταμαι [Refs 5th c.BC+ [(δι-) variant in 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Timaeus” 81d, κατεστέαται variant in 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.196. (From I.- 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus]] sthā-, cf. Sanskrit sthā- (aorist á-sthā-t), Latin stare, etc.; Gr. reduplicate present and perfect from si-sthā-, se-sthā-.)

__A
Causal, make to stand, set up, πελέκεας ἑξείης [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 19.574]]; ἔγχος μέν ῥ᾽ ἔστησε φέρων πρὸς κίονα he set it against the pillar,[Refs 8th c.BC+ [1.127, compare 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 15.126]]; ἱ. ἱστόν set up the loom, or raise the mast (see. ἱστός [Refs [1 and 11)]]; κρητῆρας στήσασθαι to have bowls set up, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 2.431]]; θεοῖς.. κρητῆρα στήσασθαι in honour of the gods, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 6.528]]; στῆσαί τινα ὀρθόν, στ. ὀρθὰν καρδίαν, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “P.” 3.53, 96; ὀρθῷ στ. ἐπὶ σφυρῷ [prev. author] “I.” 7(6).13; ἐς ὀρθὸν ἱ. τινά 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Supplices” 1230; ὁ Ξανθίας τὸν φαλλὸν ὀρθὸν στησάτω 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Acharnenses” 243; ὀρθὸν οὖς ἵστησιν 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Electra” 27]]; στῆσαι λόγχας, for battle, [Refs [[prev. author] “Ant.” 145 (Lyric poetry)]]; especially raise buildings, statues, trophies, etc., ἱ. ἀνδριάντα [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 2.110; τροπαῖα 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Trachiniae” 1102; τροπαῖον ἱ. τῶν πολεμίων 5th-6th c.BC: Isocrates Orator 4.150, compare “IG” 22.1457.26; τροπαῖον στησάμενοι 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Historia Graeca (Hellenica)” 2.4.7; τροπαῖον ἂν στήσαιτο τῶν ταύτης τρόπων 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Plutus” 453; τὰ μακρὰ στῆσαι τείχη 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 1.69]]; ἱ. τινὰ χαλκοῦν set him up in brass, raise a brazen statue to him, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 13.21, 19.261]] (so in perfect, stand, οὗτος ἕστηκε λίθινος [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 2.141]]:—passive, σφυρήλατος ἐν Ὀλυμπία στάθητι [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Phaedrus” 236b; σταθῆναι χαλκοῦς 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Rhetorica” 1410a33).]]

__A.II
set, place, of things or persons, τρίποδ᾽ ἔστασαν ἐν πυρί [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 8.435, etc.; ὥς σ᾽ ἄγχι γῆς στήσωσι Καδμείας 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Coloneus” 399, etc.]]; fix, τοὺς ὀφθαλμοὺς εἰς τὴν γῆν [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd-3rd c.AD: Philostratus Sophista “Vita Apollonii” 1.10]]; especially set men in order or array, πεζοὺς δ᾽ ἐξόπιθε στῆσεν [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 4.298, compare 2.525, etc.; στῆσαί τινας τελευταίους 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 6.3.25, etc.]]

__A.III
bring to a standstill, stay, check, λαὸν δὲ στῆσον [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 6.433]]; νέας, ἵππους, ἡμιόνους στῆσαι, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 3.182, 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 5.755, 24.350]]; μύλην στῆσαι to stop the mill, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 20.111; στῆσεν ἄρ᾽ (i.e. ἡμιόνους) 7.4]]; στῆσε δ᾽ ἐν Ἀμνισῷ (i.e. νῆα)[Refs 4th c.AD+ [19.188; βᾶριν 4th c.AD: Iamblichus Philosophus “de Mysteriis” 6.5]]; στῆσαι τὴν φάλαγγα halt it, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 7.1.5; ἵστησι ῥοῦν 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Cratylus” 437b, etc.; ἵ. τὴν ψυχὴν ἐπὶ τοῖς πράγμασιν [prev. work] 437a]]; στ. τὰ ὄμματα fix them, of a dying man, [Refs [[prev. author] “Phd.” 118]]; στ. τὸ πρόσωπον compose the countenance, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 1.3.9; στήσαντες ἐπὶ τούτων τὴν διήγησιν 2nd c.BC: Polybius Historicus 3.2.6: especially in in Medicine texts, ἵ. κοιλίαν 1st c.AD: Dioscorides (Dioscurides) Medicus 1.20]]; τὰς κοιλίας Philotim. cited in [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.AD: Oribasius Medicus 4.10.1; αἱμορραγίας 1st c.AD: Dioscorides (Dioscurides) Medicus 1.129: _absolutely_, 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Historia Animalium” 605a29]]:—middle, ἱστάμενος τῷ νοσήματι [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Hippocrates Medicus “ἐπιστολαί” 19 (“Hermes” 53.65).]]

__A.III.2
set on foot, stir up, κονίης.. ἱστᾶσιν ὀμίχλην [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 13.336; ἵστη δὲ μέγα κῦμα 21.313; νεφέλην ἔστησε Κρονίων 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 12.405, compare 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 5.523]]; of battle, etc., φυλόπιδα στήσειν stir up strife, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 11.314; ἔριν στήσαντες 16.292 (so _intransitive_ φύλοπις ἕστηκε]] the fray is on foot, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 18.172):]] —also in middle, στησάμενοι δ᾽ ἐμάχοντο[Refs 8th c.BC+ [[prev. work] 533, 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 9.54; πολέμους ἵστασθαι 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 7.9.β᾽, 175, 236; so ἱστάναι βοήν 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Choephori” 885; κραυγήν 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Orestes” 1529 (_passive_, θόρυβος ἵσταται βοῆς]] arises, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Philoctetes” 1263)]]; also of passions and states of mind, μῆνιν, ἐλπίδα στῆσαι, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. author] “OT” 699, 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Iphigenia Aulidensis” 788 (Lyric poetry).]]

__A.III.3
set up, appoint, τινὰ βασιλέα [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.97; τύραννον 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Tyrannus” 940, compare “OC” 1041, “Ant.” 666]]:—middle, ἐστάσαντο τύραννον [Refs 7th c.BC+ [7th-6th c.BC: Alcaeus Lyricus 37 A; φύλακας στησόμεθα 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 484d]]:—passive, ὁ ὑπὸ Δαρείου σταθεὶς ὕπαρχος [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 7.105, compare “IG” 9(1).32.23 (Stiris, 2nd c.BC).]]

__A.III.4
establish, institute, χορούς, παννυχίδα, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 3.48, 4.76 (so στήσασθαι ἤθεά τε καὶ νόμους [prev. author] 2.35; ἀγῶνα “hymnus ad Apollinem” 150)]]; στῆσαι χορόν, Ὀλυμπιάδα, ἑορτάν, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “P.” 9.114, “O.” 2.3, 10(11).58; κτερίσματα 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Electra” 433; χορούς 5th c.BC: Bacchylides Lyricus 10.112, 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 21.51]]; οὐχ ὑγιῶς ἱστάμενος λόγον setting up a bad argument, [Refs 1st c.AD+ [1st c.AD: Anonymus Londinensis 26.34]]:—passive, ἀγορὴ ἵσταταί τινι [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 6.58.]]

__A.III.5
= Latin statuere, determine, γνῶναι καὶ στῆσαι [Refs 1st c.BC+ [1st c.BC: Dionysius Halicarnassensis 8.68; διαγεινώσκειν καὶ ἱστάναι “Not. Arch.” 4.21 (Aug.)]]:—passive, τὰ ὑπό τινος σταθέντα [Refs 1st c.AD+ [“OGI” 665.27 (Egypt, 1st c.AD)]]; τὰ ἑσταμένα Wilcken [Refs 2nd c.BC+ [“Chr.” 167.27 (2nd c.BC).]]

__A.III.6
fix by agreement, ὁ σταθεὶς τόκος [Refs 1st c.BC+ [“PGrenf.” 1.31.1 (1st c.BC),compare “PFlor.” 14.11 (4th c.AD)]]; τὸ ἑσταμένον ἐνοίκιον [Refs 3rd c.AD+ [“BGU” 253.15 (3rd c.AD).]]

__A.III.7
bring about, cause, ἀμπνοάν [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “P.” 4.199]]; στῆσαι δύσκηλον χθόνα make its case desperate, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Eumenides” 825.]]

__A.IV
place in the balance, weigh, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 19.247, 22.350, 24.232, 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Vespae” 40]]; [ἐκπώματα] [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th-3rd c.BC: Theophrastus Philosophus “Characteres” 18.7; ἀριθμοῦντες καὶ μετροῦντες καὶ ἱστάντες 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 8.2.21, etc.]]; ἱστάναι τι πρὸς ἀργύριον weigh a thing against silver, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 2.65]]; ἀγαθὸς ἱστάναι good at weighing, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Protagoras” 356b]]; τὸ ἐγγὺς καὶ τὸ πόρρω στήσας ἐν τῷ ζυγῷ [Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. passage],compare 5th c.BC: Lysias Orator 10.18]]; ἐπὶ τὸ ἱστάναι ἐλθεῖν have recourse to the scales, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Euthyphro” 7c]]:—passive, ἵστασθαι ἐπὶ ζυγοῦ [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd c.AD: Arrianus Historicus “Epicteti Dissertationes” 1.29.15; σταθείς]]weighed, [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [Inscriptiones Graecae 11(2).161 B 113 (Delos, 3rd c.BC).]]

__A.IV.2
weigh out, pay, [LXX+NT [LXX.1Ki.21.39, cf. LXX.Zech.11.12, NT.Matt.26.15.]]

__B
passive and intransitive tenses of active, to be set or placed, stand, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Homerus Epicus etc., ἀγχοῦ, ἆσσον, 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 2.172, 23.97; ἄντα τινός 17.30; ἐς μέσσον 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 17.447; σταθεὶς ἐς μέσον 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 3.130]]; ἀντίοι ἔσταν, ἐναντίοι ἔστησαν, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 1.535, 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 10.391]]: proverbial of critical circumstances, ἐπὶ ξυροῦ ἵσταται ἀκμῆς [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 10.173: frequently merely a stronger form of εἶναι]], to be in a certain place or state, ἀργύρεοι σταθμοὶ ἐν χαλκέῳ ἕστασαν οὐδῷ [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 7.89, etc.]]; ἑστάτω for ἔστω, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Ajax” 1084]]; τὰ νῦν ἑστῶτα,= τὰ νῦν, [Refs [[prev. author] “Tr.” 1271 (_anapaest meter_); ἐμοὶ δ᾽ ἄχος ἕστᾱκεν [prev. author] “Aj.” 200 (Lyric poetry): with]] adverb, ξυμφορᾶς ἵν᾽ ἕσταμεν, ἵν᾽ ἕστ. χρείας, in what case or need we are, [Refs [[prev. author] “Tr.” 1145, “OT” 1442]]; ποῦ τύχης ἕστηκε; [Refs [[prev. author] “Aj.” 102]]; later also ἀδίκως, ὀρθῶς, εὐλαβῶς ἵστασθαι, behave wrongly, etc., [Refs 2nd c.BC+ [2nd c.BC: Polybius Historicus 18.3.2, 33.6.3, 18.33.4.]]

__B.2
take up an intellectual attitude, ὡς ἵστασθαι δεῖ περὶ χρημάτων κτήσεως [Refs 1st c.BC+ [1st c.BC: Philodemus Philosophus “περὶ οἰκονομίας” p.38J.]]; οὐκ ὀρθῶς ἵ. [Refs [[prev. author] “Rh.” 1.53S.]]

__B.3
in pregnant sense, στῆναι ἐς.. [Refs 8th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 9.21; στ. ἐς δίκην 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Iphigenia Taurica” 962; στ. παρά τινα 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 24.169 (but οἱ μὴ στάντες παρὰ τὰ δεινά]] those who did not face the danger, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [1st c.BC: Dionysius Halicarnassensis 9.28): with _accusative_ loci, τί τοῦτ᾽ αἰθερίαν ἕστηκε πέτρα; 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Supplices” 987 (Lyric poetry); στῆτε τόνδε τρίβον [prev. author] “Or.” 1251:with _accusative_ _cognate_, ποίαν μ᾽ ἀνάστασιν δοκεῖς.. στῆνα; 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Philoctetes” 277.]]

__B.II
stand still, halt, ἀλλ᾽ ἄγε δὴ στέωμεν [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 11.348, compare 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 6.211, 10.97; opposed to φεύγω, 6.199]], etc.; stand idle, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 4.243, +others]]; ἑστάναι to be stationary, opposed to κινεῖσθαι, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 436c, etc.; κατὰ χώρην ἑστάναι 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 4.97]]; οὐ μὴν ἐνταῦθ᾽ ἕστηκε τὸ πρᾶγμα does not rest here, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 21.102, compare 10.36]]; ἐὰν ἡ κοιλία στῇ if the bowels are constipated, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Historia Animalium” 588a8]]: with participle, οὐ στήσεται ἀδικῶν [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 10.10]]; come to a stop, rest satisfied, ἄν τις ὀρθῶς ἐπιβάλῃ, ἔπειτα σταθῇ [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-3rd c.BC: Epicurus Philosophus “Fragmenta” 423; οὐχ ἱστάμενοι 3rd c.AD: Plotinus Philosophus 3.1.2: _impersonal_, ἵσταται]] there is a stop, one comes to a stop, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Analytica Priora” 43a37, +others; οὐκ ἔστη ἐνταῦθα κακοῖς γενομένοις ἀποθανεῖν 3rd c.AD: Plotinus Philosophus 3.2.8; also ἵστασθαι μέχρι τοῦ γένους 4th c.AD: Themistius Sophista “Aristotelis Analyticorum Posteriorum paraphrasis - pars” 55.8, +others]]

__B.II.2
metaphorically, stand firm, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Historia Graeca (Hellenica)” 5.2.23; τῇ διανοίᾳ 2nd c.BC: Polybius Historicus 21.11.3]]; of arguments or propositions, hold good, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [1st c.BC: Philodemus Gadarensis Epigrammaticus “Rh.” 1.83, 2.192 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus:]]participle, ἑστηκώς fixed, stable, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “de Generatione Animalium” 776a35, “EN” 1104a4, “Metaphorical” 1047a15; δεῖ τὸ κρίμα ἑστηκὸς καὶ κύριον εἶναι “SIG” 826ii29 (Delph., 2nd c.BC)]]; λογισμὸς ἑστὼς καὶ νουνεχής [Refs 2nd c.BC+ [2nd c.BC: Polybius Historicus 3.105.9; τέχναι οὐκ ἔχουσαι τὸ ἑστηκός, ἀλλὰ τὸ στοχαστικόν 1st c.BC: Philodemus Gadarensis Epigrammaticus “Rh.” 1.71S. (so]] adverb ἑστηκότως, opposed to στοχαστικῶς[Refs 2nd c.BC+ [, [prev. work]70S.),compare 4th c.AD: Iamblichus Philosophus “Protrepticus” 21. κ; χρεία ἑστηκυῖα καὶ τεταγμένη 2nd c.BC: Polybius Historicus 6.25.10]]; ἑστηκότα θεωρήματα, ἑστηκότες σκοποί, [Refs 1st c.BC+ [1st c.BC: Philodemus Gadarensis Epigrammaticus “Rh.” 1.2S., “Po.” 5.22]]; of age, ἑστηκυῖα ἡλικία [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Leges” 802c]]; τιμαὶ ἑστηκυῖαι fixed prices, PTeb.unpublished[Refs [703.177.]]

__B.III
to be set up or upright, stand up, rise up, κρημνοὶ ἕστασαν [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 12.55; ὀρθαὶ τρίχες ἔσταν 24.359, compare 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Septem contra Thebas” 564 (Lyric poetry), 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Ion” 535c, etc.; κονίη ἵστατο 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 2.151; ἵστατο κῦμα 21.240]]; of a horse, ἵστασθαι ὀρθός to rear, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 5.111]]; ἵστασθαι βάθρων from the steps, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Tyrannus” 143.]]

__B.III.2
to be set up, erected, or built, στήλη, ἥ τ᾽ ἐπὶ τύμβῳ ἑστήκῃ [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 17.435; ἕστακε τροπαῖον 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Septem contra Thebas” 954 (Lyric poetry); μνημεῖον 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Equites” 268, etc.]]; see above [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus 11.]]

__B.III.3
generally, arise, begin, ἵστατο νεῖκος [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 13.333; compare 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus 111.2.]]

__B.III.4
in marking Time, ἔαρος νέον ἱσταμένοιο when spring is not long begun, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 19.519]]; ἕβδομος ἑστήκει μείς the seventh month was begun, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 19.117]]; τοῦ μὲν φθίνοντος μηνός, τοῦ δ᾽ ἱσταμένοιο as one month ends and the next begins, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 14.162, compare 8th-7th c.BC: Hesiodus Epicus “Opera et Dies” 780]]; later μὴν ἱστάμενος, μεσῶν, φθίνων, first in [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 6.57, 106, compare 5th-6th c.BC: Andocides Orator 1.121, 4th c.BC: Aeschines Orator 3.67; σχεδὸν ἤδη μεσημβρία ἵσταται 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Phaedrus” 242a.]]

__B.III.5
to be appointed, στῆναι ἐς ἀρχήν [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 3.80]]; see above [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus 111.3.]]

ἱστορέω, -ῶ
(ἵστωρ, one learned or skilled in) [in LXX: 1Es.1:33 Est.1:42 * ;]
__1. with accusative of thing(s), to inquire into, learn by inquiry.
__2. C. accusative of person(s), to inquire of or about.
__3. to narrate, record.
__4. In late writers, to visit, become acquainted with: Gal.1:18 (see Ellic., in l, and cf. MM, Exp., xv).†
(AS)

---

LSJ / STEPBible (TFLSJ)
ἱστορ-έω,
(ἵστωρ) inquire into or about a thing, τι [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 2.113, 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Prometheus Vinctus” 632, etc.; περί τινος 2nd c.BC: Polybius Historicus 3.48.12]]; also, inquire about a person, τινα [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Tyrannus” 1150, 1156; ὅδ᾽ εἴμ᾽ Ὀρέστης.. ὃν ἱστορεῖς 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Orestes” 380, compare “Tr.” 261: followed by _relative_ clause, Αἴγισθον ἔνθ᾽ ᾤκηκεν ἱστορῶ 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Electra” 1101.]]

__2
examine, observe, χώραν, πόλιν, [Refs 1st c.AD+ [1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus “Theseus” 30, “Pomp.” 40, compare 1st c.AD: Josephus Historicus “Antiquitates Judaicae” 1.11.4]]; τὴν τοῦ Μέμνονος [σύριγγα] [Refs 1st c.AD+ [“OGI” 694.7; τὴν σύνεσίν τινος 1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus “Cicero” 2, etc.; τινὰς ἀπολουμένους 2nd c.AD: Galenus Medicus 11.109]]: hence, to be informed about, know, κακῶς τὸ μέλλον ἱστορῶν [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Persae” 454; πατέρα ἱστορεῖς καλῶς [prev. author] “Eu.” 455, compare 5th c.BC: Hippocrates Medicus “παραγγελίαι” 12: _metaphorically_, εἴ τις ἀκτὶς ἡλίου νιν ἱστορεῖ βλέποντα]] has news of him, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Agamemnon” 676: followed by _relative_, τὴν πορείαν ἱστορῶν, ὡς δυσδίοδος ὑπάρχει 2nd c.BC: Polybius Historicus 3.61.3]]; read in history, [Refs [[prev. author] 1.63.7.]]

__2
with accusative person, inquire of, ask, ἱστορέων αὐτοὺς ἥντινα δύναμιν ἔχει ὁ Νεῖλος [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 2.19, compare 3.77]]; inquire of an oracle, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Ion” 1547]]; visit a person for the purpose of inquiry, Κηφᾶν [NT.Gal.1.18]:— passive, to be questioned, κληθέντας ἱστορέεσθαι εἰ.. [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.24; ἱστορούμενος 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Trachiniae” 415, 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Helena” 1371.]]

__2.b
with doubleaccusative, inquire of one about a thing, τί μ᾽ ἱστορεῖς τόδε [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [[prev. author] “Ph.” 621, compare 3rd c.BC: Lycophron Tragicus 1.]]

__4
absolutely, inquire, ἀκοῆ ἱ. [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 2.29, etc.]]; especially in participle, ἱστορέων εὕρισκε [Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. author] 1.56, etc.; οὔθ᾽ ὁρῶν οὔθ᾽ ἱστορῶν 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Tyrannus” 1484]]; followed by a relative word, ἱστόρεόν τε ὅτεῳ τρόπῳ περιγένοιτο [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.122.]]

__II
give an account of what one has learnt, record, τοὺς βίους τῶν χερσαίων [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-3rd c.BC: Theophrastus Philosophus “Historia Plantarum” 4.13.1, compare 2nd c.AD: Lucianus Sophista “Hist.Conscr.” 7, etc.]]; ἱστοροῦσί τινες.. it is stated that.. , [Refs 1st c.AD+ [1st c.AD: Dioscorides (Dioscurides) Medicus 4.75, etc.]]:—frequently in passive, ὁ καρπὸς.. ἐπιλημπτικοὺς ἱστορεῖται ὠφελεῖν [Refs 1st c.BC+ [[prev. author] 1.83; περί τινος ἱστορεῖται διότι 1st c.BC: Philodemus Gadarensis Epigrammaticus “Mus.” p.18K.; ἱστορεῖται περὶ Γοργοῦς τοιοῦτον 1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus 2.227e, compare [prev. author] “Cic.” 1, 2nd-3rd c.AD: Aelianus “Tactica - Griechische Kriegsschriftsteller” 34.3, etc.]]; Ἀπολλόδωρος εἴρηκεν ἀπελθόντας Ὕαντας ἱστορεῖσθαι are represented as having gone, [Refs 1st c.BC+ [1st c.BC-1st c.AD: Strabo Geographus 10.3.4]]; τῶν ἱστορουμένων οὐδενὸς ἧττον πολυπράγμων the most in dustrious person on record, [Refs 1st c.BC+ [1st c.BC: Philodemus Gadarensis Epigrammaticus “Mus.” p.108K.]]

ἰσχυρός, -ά, -όν

deep_entry:
Abbott-Smith / STEPBible (TBESG)
κἀγώ see: ἐγώ.
ἐγώ, genitive, etc., ἐμοῦ, ἐμοί, ἐμέ (enclitic μου, μοι, με), pl. ἡμεῖς, -ῶν, -ῖν, -ᾶς,
of person(s) pron.
I.
__(a) The nom. is usually emphatic, when expressed as subjc, as in Mat.3:11, Mrk.1:8, Luk.3:16, al. But often there is no apparent emphasis, as Mat.10:16, Jhn.10:17; ἰδοὺ ἐ. (= Heb. הִנֵּנִי, cf. 1Ki.3:8), Act.9:10; ἐ. (like Heb. אֲנִי), I am, Jhn.1:23 (LXX), Act.7:32 (LXX).
__(b) The enclitic forms (see supr.) are used with nouns, adjectives, verbs, adverbs, where there is no emphasis: ἐν τ. πατρί μου, Jhn.14:20; μου τ. λόγους, Mat.7:24; ὀπίσω μου, Mat.3:11; ἰσχυρότερός μου, ib.; λέγει μοι, Rev.5:5; also with the prep. πρός, as Mrk.9:19, al. The full forms (ἐμοῦ, etc.) are used with the other prepositions, as δι᾽ ἐμοῦ, ἐν ἐμοί, εἰς ἐμέ, etc., also for emphasis, as Luk.10:16, Jhn.7:23, Mrk.14:7, al.
__(with) The genitive μου and ἡμῶν are often used for the poss. pronouns ἐμός, ἡμέτερος: τ. λαόν μου, Mat.2:6; μου τῂ ἀπιστιᾳ, Mrk.9:24.
__(d) τί ἐμοὶ καὶ σοί ( = Heb. מַה־לִי וָלָךְ, Jdg.11:12, al.), i.e. what have we in common: Mat.8:29, Mrk.1:24, 5:7, Luk.8:28, Jhn.2:4; τί γάρ μοι, 1Co.5:2.
__(e) The interchange of ἐγώ and ἡμεῖς, common in π., appears in Pauline Epp. (see M, Pr., 86f., M, Th., 131f.).
__(f) κἀγώ (= καὶ ἐγώ), and I, even I, I also: Mat.2:8, Luk.2:48, Jhn.6:56, Rom.3:7, 1Co.7:40, al.; κἀγώ . . . καί, both . . . and, Jhn.7:28.
(AS)

__1
physically clean, spotless (not in [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad”), εἵματα 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 6.61, 7th c.BC: Archilochus Lyricus 12, compare 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Cyclops” 35, 562, etc.]]; of persons, cleanly, κ. περὶ ἐσθῆτα [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “de Virtutibus et Vitiis” 1250b28, compare “Rh.” 1416a23 (nisi to be read καθάριος).]]

__2
clear of admixture, clear, pure, especially of water, Βορυσθένης ῥέει καθαρὸς παρὰ θολεροῖσι [LXX+5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 4.53; κ. ὕδατα 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Hippolytus” 209 (_anapaest meter_); ὕδωρ κ. ζῶν LXX.Num.5.17; δρόσοι 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Ion” 96 (_anapaest meter_); κ. καὶ διαφανῆ ὑδάτια 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Phaedrus” 229b; οὖρον 5th c.BC: Hippocrates Medicus “ἐπιδημίαι” 1.3; διαχώρημα [prev. author] “Coac.” 640]]; κ. φάος, φέγγος, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “P.” 6.14, 9.90; πνεῦμα κ. οὐρανοῦ 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Helena” 867; κ. ἄρτος 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 2.40]]; of white bread, Wilcken [LXX+3rd c.BC+ [“Chr.” 30i17 (3rd-2nd c.BC), LXX.Jdt.10.5, 2nd c.AD: Galenus Medicus 6.482, 19.137]]; ἄλευρον κ. [Refs [Diocl.fragment 139]]; χρυσίον, ἀργύριον -ώτατον, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 4.166, compare 3rd c.BC: Theocritus Poeta Bucolicus 15.36, 1st c.AD: Philo Judaeus 1.190, etc.; σῖτος 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Oeconomicus” 18.8; σῖτος κ. ἀπὸ πάντων “PHib.” 1.84 (a). 6 (4th-3rd c.BC): frequently of grain,]]winnowed, πυρὸς κ. ἄδολος [Refs 2nd c.BC+ [“POxy.” 1124.11 (1st c.AD),compare “PTeb.” 93.36 (2nd c.BC)]], etc.; of metals, etc., σίδηρος [Refs 5th c.AD+ [“Sammelb.” 4481.13 (5th c.AD)]], etc.; ἀρωμάτων, καθαρῶν, λαχάνων, uncertain meaning in [Refs 4th c.AD+ [“PLond.” 2.429.6 (4th c.AD)]]; ἄκρατος καὶ κ. νοῦς [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 8.7.30; χρόαι 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “de Sensu” 440a5; φωναί [prev. author] “Aud.” 801b28]]; of feelings, unmixed, μῖσος τῆς ἀλλοτρίας φύσεως [Refs 6th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Menexenus” 245d, compare 6th c.BC: Theognis Elegiacus 89]]; serene, φρήν [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Hippolytus” 1120 (Lyric poetry).]]

__3
clear of objects, free, ἐν καθαρῷ (i.e. τόπῳ) in an open space, ἐν κ., ὅθι δὴ νεκύων διεφαίνετο χῶρος [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 8.491; ἐν κ., ὅθι κύματ᾽ ἐπ᾽ ἠϊόνος κλύζεσκον 23.61, compare 1st c.AD: Philo Judaeus 2.535 (_superlative_)]]; πάξαις Ἄλτιν ἐν κ. in a clearing, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “O.” 10 (11). 45]]; ἐν κ. βῆναι to leave the way clear, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Coloneus” 1575 (Lyric poetry)]]; ἐν τῷ κ. οἰκεῖν live in the clear sunshine, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 520d]]; διὰ καθαροῦ ῥέειν, of a river whose course is clear and open, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.202: with]] substantive, κελεύθῳ ἐν κ[Refs 5th c.BC+ [. 5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “O.” 6.23]]; χῶρος κ. [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.132; ἐν κ. λειμῶνι 3rd c.BC: Theocritus Poeta Bucolicus 26.5]]; ἐν ἡλίῳ κ. in the open sun, opposed to σκιά, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Phaedrus” 239c]]; ὥς σφι τὸ ἐμποδὼν ἐγεγόνεε κ. was cleared away, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 7.183]]; κ. ποιεῖσθαι τὰς ἀρκυστασίας set up the nets in open ground, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Cynegeticus” 6.6]]; frequently of land, free from weeds, etc., παραδώσω τὸν κλῆρον κ. ἀπὸ θρύου καλάμου ἀγρώστεως κτλ. [Refs 2nd c.BC+ [“PTeb.” 105.59 (2nd c.BC)]]; παραδώσω τὰς ἀρούρας κ. ὡς ἔλαβον [Refs 3rd c.AD+ [“BGU” 1018.25 (3rd c.AD): with _genitive_, γλῶσσα καθαρὴ τῶν σημηΐων]] clear of the marks, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 2.38]]; καθαρὸν τῶν προβόλων, of a fort, [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd c.AD: Arrianus Historicus “Anabasis” 2.21.7]]; of documents, free from mistakes, [Refs 3rd c.AD+ [POxy. 1277.13 (3rd c.AD)]]; χειρόγραφον κ. ἀπὸ ἐπιγραφῆς καὶ ἀλείφαδος free from interlineation and erasure, [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [“PLond.” 2.178.13 (2nd c.AD).]]

__3.b
metaphorically, free, clear of debt, liability, etc., κ. ἀπὸ δημοσίων καὶ παντὸς εἴδους [Refs 1st c.AD+ [“BGU” 197.14 (1st c.AD); κ. ἀπό τε ὀφειλῆς καὶ ὑποθήκης καὶ παντὸς διεγγυήματος [prev. work] 112.11 (1st c.AD)]]; γῆ κ. ἀπὸ γεωργίας βασιλικῆς [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [“POxy.” 633 (2nd c.AD)]]; καθαρὰ ποιῆσαι to give a discharge, [Refs [PAvrom. 1 A 22]]; in moral sense, free from pollution, καθαρῷ θανάτῳ an honourable death, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 22.462; θάνατον οὐ κ., τὸν δι᾽ ἀγχόνης 1st c.AD: Philo Judaeus 2.491; ψυχαὶ ἀρηΐφατοι καθαρώτεραι ἢ ἐνὶ νούσοις 1st c.AD(?): Heraclitus 136]]; frequently free from guilt or defilement, pure, χεῖρες [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Eumenides” 313 (_anapaest meter_); καθαρὸς χεῖρας 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.35, 5th c.BC: Antipho Orator 5.11, 5th-6th c.BC: Andocides Orator 1.95; κ. παρέχειν τινὰ κατὰ τὸ σῶμα καὶ κατὰ τὴν ψυχήν 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Cratylus” 405b]]; ἔρχομαι ἐκ κοθαρῶν κοθαρά Orph[Refs [“fragment” 32c.1, +others]]; of ceremonial purity, καθαρὰ καὶ ἁγνή εἰμι ἀπό τε τῶν ἄλλων τῶν οὐ καθαρευόντων καὶ ἀπ᾽ ἀνδρὸς συνουσίας Jusj. cited in [LXX+4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 59.78, compare “UPZ” 78.28 (2nd c.BC), LXX.Num.8.7, +others; ἀπὸ τάφου καὶ ἐκφορᾶς καθαροί “SIG” 982.9 (2nd c.BC)]]; especially of persons purified after pollution, ἱκέτης προσῆλθες κ. [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Eumenides” 474, compare 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Coloneus” 548, etc.]]; also of things, βωμοί, θύματα, δόμος, μέλαθρα, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Supplices” 654 (Lyric poetry), 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Iphigenia Taurica” 1163, 1231 (troch.), 693]]: with genitive, clear of or from.. , κ. ἐγκλημάτων [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Antipho Orator 2.4.11]]; ἀδικίας, κακῶν, [NT+5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 496d, “Cra.” 404a; ὁ τῶν κακῶν κ. τόπος [prev. author] “Tht.” 177a; κ. τὰς χεῖρας φόνου [prev. author] “Lg.” 864e; Κόρινθον.. ἀποδεῖξαι τῶν μιαιφόνων καθαράν 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Historia Graeca (Hellenica)” 4.4.6; κ. εἰμι ἀπὸ τοῦ αἵματος πάντων NT.Act.20.26, compare 2nd-3rd c.AD: Dio Cassius Historicus 37.24; κ. ἀπὸ ὅρκου LXX.Gen.24.8]]; ceremonially pure, of food, ὄσπριον [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 2.37]]; of victims, [LXX+2nd c.AD+ [LXX.Gen.7.2, +others, “PGen.” 32.9 (2nd c.AD)]], etc.; κ. ἡμέραι, opposed to ἀποφράδες, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Leges” 800d.]]

__3.c
in active sense, purifying, cleansing, λέβης [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “O.” 1.26; θέειον 3rd c.BC: Theocritus Poeta Bucolicus 24.96.]]

__4
of birth, pure, genuine, σπέρμα θεοῦ [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “P.” 3.15]]; πόλις [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Ion” 673]]; τῶν Ἀθηναίων ὅπερ ἐστράτευε καθαρὸν ἐξῆλθε, i.e. were citizens of pure blood, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 5.8]]; οἱ τῷ γένει μὴ κ. [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Ἀθηναίων Πολιτεία” 13.5]]; κ. ἀστοί [Refs 5th c.BC+ [Scholia 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Acharnenses” 506]]; καθαρόν a real, genuine saying, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Vespae” 1015]]; κ. Τίμων a Timon pure and simple, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [[prev. author] “Av.” 1549; κ. δοῦλος 4th c.BC: Antiphanes Comicus 9 (glossed by ἀπηκριβωμένος, “Anecdota Graeca - Bekker” 105)]]; ζημία κ., of a person, Alciphro 3.21.

__5
of language, pure, ὀνόματα, λέξις, [Refs 1st c.BC+ [1st c.BC: Dionysius Halicarnassensis “de Compositione Verborum” 1, 3; διάλεκτος [prev. author] “Dem.” 5]]; so of writers, [Λυσίας] κ. τὴν ἑρμηνείαν [Refs [[prev. author] “Lys.” 2; [Ξενοφῶν] κ. τοῖς ὀνόμασι [prev. author] “Pomp.” 4]]; also, clear, simple, σεμνὸς καὶ κ. [Refs 4th c.AD+ [4th c.AD: Julianus Imperator “Orationes” 2.77a.]]

__5.b
Grammars, preceded by a vowel, pure, [Refs 2nd c.BC+ [2nd c.BC: Dionysius Thrax Grammaticus 635.10, 639.5, Hdn.Gr. 2.930, +others]]; containing a 'pure' syllable, [Refs [[prev. work] 928.]]

__6
without blemish, sound, ὁ κ. στρατός, τὸ κ. τοῦ στρατοῦ, the sound portion of the army, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.211, 4.135; see above 4.]]

[NT+5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Electra” 315; κ. πρὸς τάφῳ [prev. author] “Hel.” 1084; πρὸς τὸ πῦρ 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Vespae” 773; ἐπὶ δίφρου 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 328c; ἐπὶ τῶν ἵππων 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 4.5.54; ἐπὶ τοῦ ἅρματος NT.Act.8.28; ἐς τοὐργαστήριον 4th c.AD: Alciphro Epistolographus 3.27: with _accusative_ _cognate_, ἕδραν κ. 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Heraclidae” 55]]: with accusative loci, sit on, ὀφρύην [Refs [[prev. work] 394.]]

__2
especially of courts, councils, assemblies, etc., sit: οἱ καθήμενοι the judges, the court, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Andocides Orator 1.139, 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 6.3, etc.; δικαστὰς οὐχ ὁρῶ καθημένους 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Nubes” 208]]; ὑμεῖς οἱ καθήμενοι you who sit as judges, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 5.85; οὐκ ἐπὶ τούτῳ κ. ὁ δικαστής 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Apologia” 35c; κ. ὑπὲρ τῶν νόμων 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 58.25]]; of the βουλή, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Andocides Orator 1.43; βουλῆς περὶ τούτων καθημένης 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 21.116]]; of an assembly, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 5.10.5]]; οἱ κ. the spectators in a theatre, [Refs [Hegesippus Epigrammaticus 1.29.]]

__3
sit still, sit quiet, ὕψι περ ἐν νεφέεσσι καθημένω [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 16.264]]; σφοῖσιν ἐνὶ μεγάροισι καθήατο (for ἐκάθηντο) [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 11.76; ἐν πένθεϊ μεγάλῳ κατῆστο 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.46]]; μετὰ κόπον κ. rest after labour, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Fragmenta” 479.3]]: and, in bad sense, sit doing nothing, lie idle, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 24.403, 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 3.134]]; of an army, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. author] 9.56, 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 4.124]]; of a boat's crew, [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [“PCair.Zen.” 107.6 (3rd c.BC)]]; οὐδὲν ποιοῦντες ἐνθάδε καθήμεθα, μέλλοντες ἀεί [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 11.17, compare 2.23, 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Fragmenta” 142.20, etc.]]; also, of an army, to have its quarters, be encamped, περὶ τὰς Ἀχαρνάς [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 2.20, compare 101; ἐχθρῶν ὑπ᾽ αὐτοῖς τείχεσιν καθημένων 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Phoenissae” 752.]]

__4
reside in a place, [LXX+NT [LXX.Neh.11.6; λαὸς καθήμενος ἐν σκοτίᾳ NT.Matt.4.16]]; settle, εἰς Σινώπην [Refs 1st c.AD+ [1st c.AD: Musonius Philosophus “fragment” 9p.43H.]]

__5
lead a sedentary, obscure life, ἐν σκότῳ καθήμενος [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “O.” 1.83; ἔσω καθημένη 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Choephori” 919]]; αἱ βαναυσικαὶ [τέχναι] ἀναγκάζουσι καθῆσθαι [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Oeconomicus” 4.2]]; to be engaged or employed, especially in a sedentary business, ἐπ᾽ αὐτῷ τούτῳ [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 2.86]]; κ. ἐπὶ τῇ τραπέζῃ, of bankers, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 49.42, compare 45.33; ἐπ᾽ ἐργαστηρίου [prev. author] 59.67; ἐπὶ τοῦ.. ἰατρείου 4th c.BC: Aeschines Orator 1.40]]; καθῆσθαι ἐν πόλει, opposed to ζῆν ἐν Χωρίῳ, [Refs 1st c.AD+ [1st c.AD: Musonius Philosophus “fragment” 11p.59H.]]

__6
sit as a suppliant, ἐν Δελφοῖσι [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 5.63, cf. Oracle texts [prev. work] 7.140.]]

__7
of districts and countries, lie, Χωρία ὁμοίως καθήμενα [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-3rd c.BC: Theophrastus Philosophus “Historia Plantarum” 8.8.7.]]

__7.b
to be low-lying, τὰ λεῖα καὶ καθήμενα [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd-3rd c.AD: Aelianus “Varia Historia” 3.1, compare “NA” 16.12]]; πεδίον κ. [Refs 4th c.AD+ [4th c.AD: Himerius Sophista “Orationes” 14.17]]; πόπανον.. κ. δωδεκόμφαλον probably flat in the middle, [Refs [“IG” 22.1367.]]

__8
of a statue, to be placed, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Symposium” 215b, 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Politica” 1315b21.]]

__9
of things, to be set or placed, λαγῴοις ἐπ᾽ ἀμύλῳ καθημένοις [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Teleclides Comicus 32, compare 5th c.BC: Pherecrates Comicus 108.17; τὸ πηδάλιον κ. πλάγιον 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Mechanica” 851a4, compare [prev. work] 13.]]

καθ-ίζω
[in LXX chiefly for יָשַׁב ;]
__1. causal, to make to sit down, set, appoint: Act.2:30, 1Co.6:4, Eph.1:20.
__2. Intrans., to sit down, be seated, sit: Mat.5:1, Mrk.9:35, Luk.7:15, Jhn.8:2, al.; with inf. tel., 1Co.10:7; before εἰς, 2Th.2:4; ἐπί, with accusative, Mrk.11:2, Jhn.12:14; id. with genitive, Jhn.19:13, Act.12:21; ὧδε, Mrk.14:32; αὐτοῦ, Mat.26:36; ἐν δεξιᾷ, Heb.1:3; ἐκ δεξιῶν, Mat.20:21, 23; ἐν, Rev.3:21; καθίσας pleonastic (M, Pro.14:1-35; Dalman, Words, 22), Mat.13:48, Luk.5:3 14:31 16:6; of settling in a place (ἐς χωρίον, Thuc., iv, 93), before ἐν, Luk.24:49 (cf. ἀνα-, ἐπι-, παρα-, περι-, συν-καθίζω)
(AS)

LSJ / STEPBible (TFLSJ)
καθίζω,
Ionic dialect κατ-, imperfect κάθιζον [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 3.426, +others; in Prose ἐκάθιζον 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Historia Graeca (Hellenica)” 5.4.6, 4th-3rd c.BC: Dinarchus Orator 2.13]]: future καθέσω [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Eupolis Comicus 12.11 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator]]; καθίσω (intransitive) [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd c.AD: Apollodorus Damascenus Mechanicus Comedy texts 5]]; Ionic dialect κατίσω (transitive) [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 4.190]]; Attic dialect also καθιῶ [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 2. 1.4, 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 24.25, 39.11, “IG” 22.778.13 (3rd c.BC)]]; Doric dialect καθιξῶ [Refs 2nd c.BC+ [2nd c.BC: Bion Bucolicus “fragment” 10.16]]: aorist 1 καθεῖσα [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 18.389, +others,]]subjunctive καθέσω [Refs 5th c.BC+ [“hymnus ad Apollinem” cited in 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 3.104]]; infinitive καθέσαι [Refs 5th c.BC+ [“IG” 22.46 aB*21, 25 (5th-4th c.BC)]]; poetry κάθεσσα [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “P.” 5.42]] codices; this aorist καθεῖσα has Ms. authority in [Refs 8th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Hippolytus” 31 (ἐγκαθ-, _middle_), “Ph.” 1188, 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.88, 4.79, 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 7.82, but we also find _Epic dialect_ κάθῐσα, _Ionic dialect_ κάτ- (for which κάθεσα, κάτεσον, etc., should perhaps be restored), 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 19.280 (variant{κάθεσαν}), +others, 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.89, 2.126, καθῖσα 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Ranae” 911, 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 6.66 (to be read καθεῖσα), later ἐκάθῐσα 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 6.1.23, 4th-3rd c.BC: Menander Comicus 544, etc., compare 2nd c.AD(?): Pollianus Epigrammaticus 3.89]]; also Epic dialect participle καθίσσας [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 9.488]]; Doric dialect καθίξας [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [3rd c.BC: Theocritus Poeta Bucolicus 1.12,]]subjunctive καθίξῃ[Refs [[prev. work] 51]]; late participle καθιζήσας, subjunctive -ζήσῃ, [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd-3rd c.AD: Dio Cassius Historicus 54.30, 37.27]]: perfect κεκάθῐκα [NT+1st c.BC+ [1st c.BC: Diodorus Siculus Historicus 17.115, NT.Heb.12.2, 2nd c.AD: Apollonius Dyscolus Grammaticus “de Syntaxi;” 323.23]]:—middle, imperfect ἐκαθιζόμην [Refs 8th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Vespae” 824, κὰδ.. ἵζ- 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 19.50]]: future καθιζήσομαι [NT+5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Phaedrus” 229a, “Euthd.” 278b, (προσ-) 4th c.BC: Aeschines Orator 3.167, later καθίσομαι NT.Matt.19.28, 1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus 2.583f,]] -ιοῦμαι [LXX.Mal.3.3, +others]: aorist 1 καθεσσάμην [Refs 6th c.BC+ [6th c.BC: Anacreon Lyricus 111; also ἐκαθισάμην “SIG” 975.6 (Delos, 3rd c.BC), 5th c.AD(?): Hesychius Legal icographus, (ἐπ-, παρ-) 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 4.130 codices, 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 33.14]]; Epic dialect ἐκαθισσάμην [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [3rd c.BC: Callimachus Epicus “Hymnus in Dianam” 233, καθισσάμην 3rd c.BC: Apollonius Rhodius Epicus 4.278, 1219]]:—passive, aorist 1 participle καθιζηθείς [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd-3rd c.AD: Dio Cassius Historicus 63.5:]]

__I
causal, make to sit down, seat, ἄλλους μὲν κάθισον Τρῶας [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 3.68; μή με κάθιζ᾽ 6.360; σ᾽ ἐπ᾽ ἐμοῖσιν ἐγὼ γούνεσσι καθίσσας 9.488; κὰδ δ᾽ εἷσ᾽ ἐν θαλάμῳ 3.382; τὴν μὲν.. καθεῖσεν ἐπὶ θρόνου 18.389; κατίσαι τινὰ ἐπ᾽ οἰκήματος 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 2.121]].; καθιεῖν τινα εἰς τὸν θρόνον, i.e. to make him king, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 2.1.4; ἐπὶ θρόνον 1st c.BC: Philodemus Philosophus “περὶ κακιῶν ί” p.22 1st c.AD: Josephus Historicus]]

__I.2
set, place, τὸν μὲν.. καθεῖσεν ἐπ᾽ ἠϊόεντι Σκαμάνδρῳ [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 5.36; κὰδ δ᾽ ἐν Ἀθήνῃς εἷσεν 2.549; Κρόνον.. Ζεὺς γαίης νέρθε καθεῖσε 14.204; καθίζειν τινὰ εἰς δόμον 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Ion” 1541]]; κ. στρατόν encamp it, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. author] “Heracl.” 664, compare 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 4.90; κ. τὸ στράτευμα ἐς Χωρίον ἐπιτήδειον [prev. author] 6.66; σύλλογον εἰς Χωρίον κ., Χωρὶς μὲν τοὺς ὁπλίτας, Χωρὶς δὲ τοὺς ἱππέας 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Leges” 755e.]]

__I.2.b
post watchers, guards, etc., σκοπὸς ὅν ῥα καθεῖσεν Αἴγισθος [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 4.524]]; κατίσαι φυλάκους set guards, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.89, compare 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 2.2.14; ἄλλους κάτισον ἀγαγὼν κατὰ τὰς.. πύλας 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 3.155; κ. ἐνέδραν 1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus “Publicola” 19]]: rarely of things, τι ἐπὶ τηγάνοις [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Pherecrates Comicus 127.]]

__I.3
set up, ἀνδριάντα κάθεσσαν [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “P.” 5.42]] codices:—middle, καθέσσασθαι [Refs 6th c.BC+ [6th c.BC: Anacreon Lyricus 111, 3rd c.BC: Apollonius Rhodius Epicus 4.1219.]]

__I.4
cause an assembly, court, etc., to take their seats, convene, ἀγορὰς ἠμὲν λύει ἠδὲ καθίζει [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 2.69]]; ὅταν καθέσωσιν ἀγῶνα [Refs 5th c.BC+ [“hymnus ad Apollinem” cited in 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 3.104; κ. τὸ δικαστήριον 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Vespae” 305, compare 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 39.11, “IG” 22.778.13; νομοθέτας 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 24.25, probably in [prev. author] 3.10]]; but κ. τινὶ δικαστήν appoint a judge to try a person, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Leges” 874a; ἐάν τε Χιλίους ἐάν θ᾽ ὁποσουσοῦν ἡ πόλις καθίσῃ 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 21.223]]; constitute, establish, δικαστήρια [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Politicus” 298e; βουλὴν ἐπίσκοπον πάντων 1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus “Solon” 19.]]

__I.5
put into a certain condition, especially in the phrase κλαίοντά τινα κ set him aweeping, κλάοντα καθέσω ς᾽ [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Eupolis Comicus [same place], compare 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Ion” 535e, 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 2.2.15; but [prev. work] 14 κλαίειν τινὰ κ]]. to make him weep: for [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [3rd c.BC: Theocritus Poeta Bucolicus 1.51, see at {ἀκράτιστος}.]]

__I.6
marry, γυναῖκας ἀλλοτρίας [LXX.Neh.13.27, compare 23.]

__II
intransitive, take one's seat, sit, absolutely, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 3.394, etc.]]; μετ᾽ ἀθανάτοισι, ἐν θρόνοισι καθίζειν,[Refs 8th c.BC+ [15.50, 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 8.422]]; ἐν [θώκοισι] [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.181]]; ἐπὶ τοῖς ἐργαστηρίοις or τῶν -ίων, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Isocrates Orator 18.9, 7.15; ἐπὶ σκίμποδα 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Nubes” 254; ἐπὶ δένδρου 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Historia Animalium” 614a34 (but κ. ἐπὶ κώπην]], of rowers, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Ranae” 197)]]; of suppliants, κ. ἐπὶ τὸν βωμόν [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 1.126, 5th c.BC: Lysias Orator 13.24; εἰς γόνυ 1st c.BC: Diodorus Siculus Historicus 17.115: in Poets also with _accusative_, κ. τρίποδα 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Ion” 366, “El.” 980]]; βωμόν, ὀμφαλόν, ἱερά, [Refs [[prev. author] “HF” 48, “Ion” 6, 1317.]]

__II.2
sit, recline at meals, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 8.4.2.]]

__II.3
sit as judge, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.97, 5.25, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Leges” 659b, 1st c.AD: Philo Judaeus 1.382]]; hold a session, of the πρόεδροι, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 24.89, compare “Hermes” 17.5 (from Delos).]]

__II.4
reside, μετά τινος [LXX.Ruth.2.23 (3.1)]; ἐν πόλει[LXX.Neh.11.1.]

__II.5
settle, sink down, ἐπὶ τὰ ἰσχία καθίσαι τὼ ἵππω [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Phaedrus” 254c; καθίσας ὁ φελλὸς ἀνοίξει τὸν κρουνόν 2nd-1st c.BC(?): Hero Mechanicus “(Spiritalia) Pneumatica” 1.20.]]

__II.6
of ships, run aground, be stranded, [Refs 2nd c.BC+ [2nd c.BC: Polybius Historicus 1.39.3, 1st c.BC-1st c.AD: Strabo Geographus 2.3.4.]]

__III
middle in intransitive sense, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 19.50 (in tmesi), 3rd c.BC: Theocritus Poeta Bucolicus 15.3, etc.; εἰς τὸν αὐτὸν θᾶκον 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 516e]]; ἐὰν δὲ καθίζεσθαι κελεύσῃ if he order them to take their seats (among the spectators in the theatre), [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 21.56 (nisi to be read καθέζεσθαι, as also [prev. work]162, both readings are found [prev. work]119)]]; καθίζεσθαι ἢ κατακλινῆναι [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Phaedrus” 228e.]]

__III.2
of birds, settle, alight, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Historia Animalium” 614b23.]]

__III.3
leave goods purchased in a market, [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [“SIG” 975.6 (Delos, 3rd c.BC)]].--Attic dialect in this signification accusative to [Refs 5th c.AD+ [5th c.AD(?): Hesychius Legal icographus]]

καθίημι,
Ionic dialect κατ-, future καθήσω [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Eumenides” 555 (Lyric poetry):]]aorist 1 καθῆκα, Epic dialect καθέηκα [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 24.642]]: 2nd pers. dual aorist 2 κάθετον [Refs [“hymnus ad Apollinem” 487]]: perfect καθεῖκα [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Lysippus Comicus 1, 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 29.46: (see. ἵημι)]]:—let fall, drop, send down, κὰδ δὲ [κεραυνὸν].. ἧκε Χαμᾶζε [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 8.134; κατὰ δ᾽ ὑψόθεν ἧκεν ἐέρσας 11.53]]; οἶνον λαυκανίης καθέηκα I have sent the wine down my throat, [Refs [24.642]]; καθίετε ἵππους ἐν δίνῃσι sink them in the stream, as an offering to the river-god, [Refs [21.132]]; [ἱστία] ἐς νῆας κάθεμεν we let them down, lowered them, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 9.72; λαῖφος καθήσειν 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Eu.”]] [same place]; σχοίνῳ σπυρίδα κ. let it down by a cord, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 5.16]]; σῶμα πύργων κ. [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Troades” 1011]]; κοντὸν ἐς [τὴν λίμνην] κ. [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 4.195; ἐμαυτὸν εἰς ἅλα 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Helena” 1614]]; ὅπλα εἰς ἅλἀ[Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. work] 1375; καθεῖσαν δέλεάρ μοι φρενῶν [prev. author] “IT” 1181 (so _metaphorically_ τοῦτον τὸν λόγον καθεῖκε 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 29.46); κ. τι ἐς πῶμα 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Ion” 1034; νάρθηκ᾽ ἐς πέδον [prev. author] “Ba.” 706]]; κ. σπονδάς pour them, [Refs [[prev. author] “IA” 60]]; τὸν κλῆρον ἐς μέσον καθείς, of putting lots into a helmet or urn, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Ajax” 1285; ἄγκυραν 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 7.36; τὰ δίκτυα 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Historia Animalium” 533b18]]; κατιεμένην καταπειρητηρίην, of a sounding-line, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 2.28: _absolutely_, καθιέναι]] reach by sounding, sound, οὐδεὶς καθεὶς ἐδυνήθη πέρας εὑρεῖν [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Meteorologica” 351a13: in Medicine texts, [αὐλίσκον]]] pass a catheter, [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd c.AD: Rufus Medicus “de renum et vesicae affectionibus” 7.11]]; οἵαν πρόφασιν καθῆκε (παρὰ προσδοκίαν for οἷον ἄγκιστρον) [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Vespae” 174]]; λόγους συμβατηρίους κ. make offers of peace, [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd-3rd c.AD: Dio Cassius Historicus 41.47]]; κ. πεῖραν make an attempt, [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd-3rd c.AD: Aelianus “Varia Historia” 2.13, “NA” 1.57]]; εἰς ὤμους κ. κόμας let one's hair flow loose, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Bacchae” 695, compare “IT” 52]]; κ. πώγωνα let one's beard grow long, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Ecclesiazusae” 100, compare “Th.” 841, 2nd c.AD: Arrianus Historicus “Epicteti Dissertationes” 2.23.21]] (passive, τὰς τρίχας καθειμέναι [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Crates Comicus 27; πώγωνα καθειμένος 1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus “Phocion” 10; τὸ γένειον αὐτῷ καθεῖτο 2nd-3rd c.AD: Aelianus “Varia Historia” 11.10)]]; [αἱ ὄϊες] μείζω τὰ οὔθατα καθιᾶσιν [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Historia Animalium” 596a24]] (passive, of a mare's udder, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 4.2)]]; also τείχη καθεῖναι ἐς θάλασσαν carry them down to the sea, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 5.52]] (passive, καθεῖτο τείχη [Refs [4.103)]]; καθῆκε τὰ σκέλη let down his legs, of one who had been lying, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Phaedo” 61c]]; κατ᾽ ἀμφοῖν ἄμφω (i.e. τὰ σκέλη) καθέντος, of a wrestler, [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd c.AD: Galenus Medicus 6.143]]; κ. δόρατα let down one's pike, bring it to the rest, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 6.5.25]]; κ. τὰς κώπας let down the oars, so as to stop the ship's way, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 2.91]]; rarely of striking, δι᾽ ὀμφαλοῦ καθῆκεν ἔγχος [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Phoenissae” 1413; καθῆκε ξύλον παιδὸς ἐς κάρα [prev. author] “HF” 993]]; κ. πρὸς γαῖαν γόνυ to kneel down, [Refs [[prev. author] “Hec.” 561; ἐς δὲ γῆν γόνυ καμάτῳ καθεῖσαν [prev. author] “IT” 333]]; κ. τινὰ ἐς ὕπνον let him fall asleep, [Refs 1st c.BC+ [[prev. author] “HF” 1006; εἰς κίνδυνον ἐμαυτόν 1st c.BC: Dionysius Halicarnassensis 5.27]]; [πώλους] ἐς λειμώνων Χλόην [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Iphigenia Aulidensis” 423]]; of a general, κ. στρατόπεδα εἰς.. let them march into.., [Refs 2nd c.BC+ [2nd c.BC: Polybius Historicus 3.70.11; εἰς τὸ πεδίον τὴν δύναμιν [prev. author] 3.92.7]]; κ. ἐπί τινας τόπους ἐνέδρας lay an ambush, [Refs [[prev. author] 4.63.9]]:—passive, stretch down seawards, ὄρεα μέχρι πρὸς τὴν θάλατταν καθειμένα [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Critias” 118a; ἕως γῆς τοῦ πρηστῆρος καθιεμένου 4th-3rd c.BC: Epicurus Philosophus “Epistulae” 2p.47U., compare p.51]] U.; τὸ καθειμένον τῆς φωνῆς low tone of voice, [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd c.AD: Herodianus Grammaticus 5.2.3.]]

__2
send down into the arena, enter for racing, ἅρματα, ζεύγη, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 6.16, 5th-6th c.BC: Isocrates Orator 16.34]]; of plays, produce, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [3rd c.BC: Eratosthenes Epicus cited in Scholia 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Nubes” 552 (_passive_)]]; διδασκαλίαν [Refs 1st c.AD+ [1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus “Cimon” 8]]; so ἔδοξε τοῖς πρυτάνεσι.. γνώμας καθεῖναι (Comedy texts for προθεῖναι) [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Ecclesiazusae” 397]]; κατὰ τὴν ἀγορὰν λογοποιοὺς κ. [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 24.15]]: frequently in later Greek in a general sense, set in motion, employ, [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd c.AD: Lucianus Sophista “DMeretr.” 7.4; κ. ἔς τινας ὑποψίας 2nd-3rd c.AD: Philostratus Sophista “Vita Apollonii” 6.38]]; φίλους καὶ ῥήτορας κ. employ them, [Refs 1st c.AD+ [1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus “Pericles” 7, compare 2nd-3rd c.AD: Philostratus Sophista “Vita Apollonii” 4.42]]:—passive, to be put in motion, ἡ στρατηλασίη κατίετο ἐς πᾶσαν τὴν Ἑλλάδα [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 7.138.]]

__3
allow to return from exile, φυγάδας [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Historia Graeca (Hellenica)” 2.2.20.]]

__II
intransitive, swoop down like a wind, λαμπρὸς καὶ μέγας καθιείς [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Equites” 430]]; of rivers, run down, ἑκατέρωσε μέχρι τοῦ μέσου [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Phaedo” 112e]]; κ. εἰς γόνυ sink on the knee, [Refs 1st c.AD+ [1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus “Antonius” 45]]; κ. εἰς ἀγῶνα, Latin descendere in arenam, [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [[prev. author] 2.616d, 2nd c.AD: Lucianus Sophista “Alex.” 6]]; κ. ἐς Ῥόδον arrive there, variant for{κατῆγεν}, [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd c.AD: Polyaenus Historicus 5.17.2.]]

καθ-ίστημι
(and καθιστάνω, Act.17:15), [in LXX for פָּקַד, קוּם, שׂוּם, etc., 24 words in all* ;]
__1.
__(a) to set down;
__(b) to bring down to a place (Hom., Xen., al.; 2Ch.28:15, 1Ki.5:3): Act.17:15.
__2. to set in order, appoint, make, constitute: Tit.1:5, 2Pe.1:8; with dupl. accusative, κριτήν, Luk.12:14; ἡγούμενον, Act.7:10; ἄρχοντα, Act.7:27, 35" (LXX) ; ἀρχιερεῖς, Heb.7:28; before ἐπί, with genitive, Mat.24:45 25:21, 23, Luk.12:42, Act.6:3; id. with dative, Mat.24:47, Luk.12:44; id. with accusative, Heb.2:7 (LXX) (WH, R, mg. omit); pass. (see Mayor, Ja., 115 f.), Rom.5:19, Jas.3:6 4:4; before εἰς with inf., Heb.8:3; τὰ πρὸς τ. θεόν, Heb.5:1 (cf. ἀντι-, ἀπο-καθίστημι).
† (AS)

LSJ / STEPBible (TFLSJ)
καθίστημι,

__A
in causal sense:—active, in present, imperfect, future, and perfect καθέστᾰκα [LXX+4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Hyperides Orator “pro Euxenippo” 28, LXX.Jer.1.10, 1st c.BC: Dionysius Halicarnassensis “de Demosthene” 54, 1st c.BC: Diodorus Siculus Historicus 32.11, etc.; once καθέστηκα “PHib.” 1.82i14 (3rd c.BC)]]: pluperfect -εστάκει[Refs 2nd c.AD+ [Demetrius Astrologus Sceps. cited in 2nd c.AD: Athenaeus Epigrammaticus 15.697d]]:—also in middle, future [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [(2nd c.AD: Pausanias Periegeta 3.5.1)]], aorist 1, more rarely present (below [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus 11.2)]]:—set down, κρητῆρα καθίστα [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 9.202]]; νῆα κατάστησον bring it to land, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 12.185]]; κ. δίφρους place, station them, before starting for the race, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Electra” 710]]; ποῖ [δεῖ] καθιστάναι πόδ; [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Bacchae” 184; κ. τινὰ εἰς τὸ φανερόν 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 7.7.22]]; set up, erect, of stones, [Refs [“Inscription Cyprian dialect” 94, 95 H.:]] —middle, [λαῖφος] κατεστήσαντο βοεῦσι steadied it, [Refs [“hymnus ad Apollinem” 407.]]

__A.2
bring down to a place, τούς μ᾽ ἐκέλευσα Πύλονδε καταστῆσαι [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 13.274]]: generally, bring, κ. τινὰ ἐς Νάξον [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.64, compare 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 4.78]]; especially bring back, πάλιν αὐτὸν κ. ἐς τὸ τεῖχος σῶν καὶ ὑγιᾶ [Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. author] 3.34; κ. τοὺς Ἕλληνας εἰς Ἰωνίαν πάλιν 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 1.4.13]]; without πάλιν, replace, restore, ἐς φῶς σὸν κ. βίον [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Alcestis” 362]]; ἃς (i.e. τὰς κόρας) οὐδ᾽ ὁ Μελάμπους.. καταστήσειεν ἄν cure their squint, [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd c.AD: Alexander Rhetor 112.5]]; ἰκτεριῶντας κ. [Refs 1st c.AD+ [1st c.AD: Dioscorides (Dioscurides) Medicus 4.1]]; τὸ σῶμα restore the general health, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Hippocrates Medicus “γυναικεῖα” 2.133]]:—middle, κατεστήσαντο (variant for{κατεκτήσαντο}) εὐδαιμονίαν [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Isocrates Orator 4.62]]:—passive, οὐκ ἂν ἀντὶ πόνων Χάρις καθίσταιτο would be returned, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 4.86.]]

__A.3
bring before a ruler or magistrate, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.209, “PRyl.” 65.10 (1st c.BC)]], etc.; τινὰ ἐπί τινα [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [“PCair.Zen.” 202.6 (3rd c.BC), “POxy.” 281.24 (1st c.AD).]]

__A.II
set in order, array, of soldiers, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 1.10.10]]; set as guards, προφυλακάς [Refs [[prev. work] 3.2.1, etc.]]

__A.II.2
ordain, appoint, κατέστησε τύραννον εἶναι παῖδα τὸν ἑωυτοῦ [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 5.94, compare 25]]: usually without the infinitive, κ. τινὰ ὕπαρχον [Refs [[prev. author] 7.105]]; ἄλλον [ἄρχοντα] ἀντὶ αὐτοῦ [LXX+5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 3.1.12, etc.; βασιλέα ἐπί τινας LXX.1Ki.8.5, +others; τινὰ ἐς μοναρχίαν 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Supplices” 352; ἐπὶ τὰς ἀρχάς 5th-6th c.BC: Isocrates Orator 12.132; τινὰ τύραννον 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Aves” 1672; κ. ἐγγυητάς 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.196, 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Ecclesiazusae” 1064]]; δικαστάς, ἐπιμελητάς, νομοθέτας, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. author] “Pl.” 917, 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 8.1.9, 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 3.10 (sed to be read καθίσατε,compare καθίζω 1.4)]]; of games, etc., γυμνικοὺς ἀγῶνας κ. [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Isocrates Orator 4.1]]: rarely with infinitive, οἱ καθιστάντες μουσικῇ.. παιδεύειν [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 410b]]:—so in passive, κυβερνᾶν κατασταθείς [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Memorabilia” 1.7.3]]: aorist middle, appoint for oneself, τύραννον καταστησάμενοι παρὰ. σφίσι αὐτοῖσι [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 5.92.á; ἄρχοντας 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 3.1.39, etc.]]

__A.II.2.b
especially of laws, constitutions, ceremonies, etc., establish, νόμους, τελετάς, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Orestes” 892, “Ba.” 21, etc.]]; πολιτείαν, δημοκρατίαν, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Ἀθηναίων Πολιτεία” 7.1, Decrees [prev. work] 29.3; ὀλιγαρχίαν 5th c.BC: Lysias Orator 12.42]]; also, set in order, arrange, πολιτείαν [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 590e]]:—also in middle, τοῦτο βουλευτήριον φρούρημα γῆς καθίσταμαι [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Eumenides” 706; τὴν Ἱππίου καθίσταμαι τυραννίδα 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Vespae” 502; καθίστατο τὰ περὶ τὴν Μυτιλήνην ᾗ αὐτῷ ἐδόκει 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 3.35; πόλεις ἐπὶ τὸ ὠφέλιμον [prev. author] 1.76; [Εὔβοιαν] ὁμολογίᾳ [prev. work] 114]]; πρὸς ἐμὲ τὸ πρᾶγμα καταστήσασθαι settle it with me, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 21.90.]]

__A.II.3
bring into a certain state, τινὰ ἐς ἀπόνοιαν [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 1.82; ἐς ἀπορίαν [prev. author] 7.75; εἰς ἀνάγκην 5th c.BC: Lysias Orator 3.3; εἰς αἰσχύνην 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Sophista” 230d; εἰς ἐρημίαν φίλων [prev. author] “Phdr.” 232d; εἰς ἀγῶνα [prev. author] “Ap.” 24c; τινὰ εἰς ἀσφάλειαν 5th-6th c.BC: Isocrates Orator 5.123]]; τίνας εἰς ἀγῶνα καθέστακ; [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Hyperides Orator “pro Euxenippo” 28, compare 4th c.BC: Lycurgus Orator 2; κ. τινὰ ἐν ἀγῶνι καὶ κινδύνῳ 5th c.BC: Antipho Orator 5.61; τὴν πόλιν ἐν πολέμῳ 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Menexenus” 242a; τοὺς φίλους ἐν ἀκινδύνῳ 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 4.5.28]]; κ. ἑαυτὸν ἐς κρίσιν present himself for trial, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 1.131, compare 4th c.BC: Lycurgus Orator 6]]; κ. τινὰ εἰς τοὺς ἀρχικούς reckon him as one of.., [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Memorabilia” 2.1.9.]]

__A.II.4
with double accusative, make, render so and so, ψευδῆ γ᾽ ἐμαυτόν [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Antigone” 657; ἡ ἐπιθυμία κ. τινὰ ἀμνήμονα 5th c.BC: Antipho Orator 2.1.7]]; τὸ πιστὸν ὑμᾶς ἀπιστοτέρους κ. [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 1.68]]; κ. τι φανερόν, σαφές, [Refs [[prev. author] 2.42, 1.32]]; τινὸς ἐπίπονον τὸν βίον κ. [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Isocrates Orator 10.17: with]]participle, κλαίοντα καθιστάναι τινά bring one to tears, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Andromache” 635: rarely with]]infinitive, κ. τινὰ φεύγειν make him fly, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 2.84, compare 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Alcestis” 283, 2nd c.AD: Lucianus Sophista “Charid.” 8]]:—passive, ἀνάγκη τὴν ναυμαχίαν πεζομαχίαν καθίστασθαι [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 2.89.]]

__A.II.5
middle, get for oneself, τὴν ζόην καταστήσασθαι ἀπ᾽ ἔργων ἀνοσιωτάτων [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 8.105.]]

__A.II.6
make, in periphrases, πάννυχοι.. διάπλοον καθίστασαν [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Persae” 382:]] —middle, κρυφαῖον ἔκπλουν οὐδαμῇ καθίστατο[Refs [[prev. work] 385.]]

__B
intransitive in aorist 2, perfect καθέστηκα, and pluperfect of active (also future καθεστήξω [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 3.37, 102), and all tenses of]]middle (except aorist 1) and passive: perfect καθέσταμαι[LXX+2nd c.BC+ [in later Greek, “IG” 22.1006.24 (2nd c.BC), LXX.Num.3.32, etc.]]:—to be set, set oneself down, settle, ἐς [Αἴγιναν] [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 3.131, compare 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 4.75]]; [ὀδύναι] καθίσταντο ἐς ὑπογάστριον [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Hippocrates Medicus “ἐπιδημίαι” 7.97]]; of joints, ἐξίσταται ἀνωδύνως καὶ κ. goes out of joint and in again, [Refs [[prev. author] “Art.” 8]]; κ. ἐς Ῥήγιον to make R. a base of operations, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 3.86]]; simply, to be come to a place, ὅποι καθέσταμεν [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Coloneus” 23.]]

__B.b

Abbott-Smith / STEPBible (TBESG)
καί,
conj.,
and
__I. Copulative.
__1. Connecting single words;
__(a) in general: Mat.2:18, 16:1, Mrk.2:15, Luk.8:15, Heb.1:1, al. mult.; repeated before each of the terms in a series, Mat.23:23, Luk.14:21, Rom.7:12, 9:4, al.
__(b) connecting numerals (WM, §37, 4): Jhn.2:20, Act.13:20;
__(with) joining terms which are not mutually exclusive, as the part with the whole: Mat.8:33, 26:59, Mrk.16:17, Act.5:29, al.
__2. Connecting clauses and sentences: Mat.3:12, Act.5:21, al. mult.; esp.
__(a) where, after the simplicity of the popular language, sentences are paratactically joined (WM, §60, 3; M, Pr., 12; Deiss., LAE, 128ff.): Mat.1:21, 7:25, Mrk.9:5, Jhn.10:3, al.;
__(b) joining affirmative to negative sentences: Luk.3:14, Jhn.4:11, IIIJhn.10;
__(with) consecutive, and so: Mat.5:1, 23:32, Heb.3:19, al.; after imperatives, Mat.4:19, Luk.7:7, al.;
__(d) = καίτοι, and yet: Mat.3:14, 6:26, Mrk.12:12, Luk.18:7 (Field, Notes, 72), 1Co.5:2, al.;
__(e) beginning an apodosis (= Heb. וְ; so sometimes δέ in cl.), then: Luk.2:21, 7:12, Act.1:10; beginning a question (WM, §53, 3a): Mrk.10:26, Luk.10:29, Jhn.9:36.
__3. Epexegetic, and, and indeed, namely (WM, §53, 3c): Luk.3:18, Jhn.1:16, Act.23:6, Rom.1:5, 1Co.3:5, al.
__4. In transition: Mat.4:23, Mrk.5:1, 21, Jhn.1:19, al.; so, Hebraistically, καὶ ἐγένετο (וַי:הִי; also ἐγένετο δέ), Mrk.1:9 (cf. Luk.5:1; V. Burton, §§357-60; M, Pr., 14, 16).
__5. καὶ . . . καί, both . . . and (for τε . . . καί, see: τε);
__(a) connecting single words: Mat.10:28, Mrk.4:41, Rom.11:33, al.;
__(b) clauses and sentences: Mrk.9:13, Jhn.7:28, 1Co.1:22, al.
__II. Adjunctive, also, even, still: Mat.5:39, 40; Mrk.2:28, al. mult.; esp. with pron., adv., etc., Mat.20:4, Jhn.7:47, al; ὡς κ., Act.11:17; καθὼς κ., Rom.15:7; οὑτω κ., Rom.6:11; διὸ κ., Luk.1:35; ὁ κ. (Deiss., BS, 313ff.), Act.13:9; pleonastically, μετὰ κ.. (Bl., §77, 7; Deiss., BS, 265f,), Php.4:3; τί κ., 1 Co 15:29; ἀλλὰ κ., Luk.14:22, Jhn.5:18, al.; καίγε (M, Pr., 230; Burton, §437), Act.17:27; καίπερ, Heb.5:8; κ. ἐάν, see: ἐάν.
ἐάν, contr. fr. εἰ ἄν,
conditional particle,
representing something as "under certain circumstances actual or liable to happen," but not so definitely expected as in the case of εἰ with ind. (Bl., §65, 4; cf. Jhn.13:17, 1Co.7:36), if haply, if;
__1. with subjc. (cl.);
__(a) pres.: Mat.6:22, Luk.10:6, Jhn.7:17, Rom.2:25, 26 al.;
{ __(b) aor. (= Lat. fut. pf.): Mat.4:9 16:26 (cf. ptcp. in Luk.9:25; M, Pr., 230), Mrk.3:24, Luk.14:34, Jhn.5:43, Rom.7:2, al.; = cl. εἰ, with opt., Jhn.9:22 11:57, Act.9:2; as Heb. אִם = ὅταν, Jhn.12:32 14:3, I Jhn.2:28 3:2, Heb.3:7" (LXX) .
__2. C. indic, (as in late writers, fr. Arist. on; see WH, App., 171; VD, MGr. 2, App., §77; Deiss., BS, 201f., LAE, 155, 254; M, Pr., 168, 187; Bl., §65, 4);
__(a) fut.: Mat.18:19 T, Luk.19:40,  Act.7:7;
__(b) pres.: 1Th.3:8 (see Milligan, in l.).
__3. With other particles: ἐ. καί (Bl., §65, 6), Gal.6:1; ἐ. μή (M, Pr., 185, 187; Bl., l.with), with subjc. pres., Mat.10:13, 1Co.8:8, Jas.2:17, 1Jn.3:21; aor., Mat.6:15, Mrk.3:27, Jhn.3:3, Rom.10:15, Gal.1:8 2:16 (see Lft., Ellic., in ll.); ἐ. τε . . . ἐ. τε, [in LXX for אִם . . . אִם, Est.19:13, al.,] Rom.14:8.
__4. = cl. ἄν (which see) after relat. pronouns and adverbs (Tdf., Pr., 96; WH, App., 173; M, Pr., 42f.; Bl., §26, 4; Mayser, 152f.; Deiss., BS, 202ff.): ὃς ἐ., Mat.5:19, Mrk.6:22, 23 Luk.17:32, 1Co.6:18, al.; ὅπου ἐ., Mat.8:19; ὁσάκις ἐ., Rev.11:6; οὗ ἐ., 1Co.16:6; καθὸ ἐ., 2Co.8:12; ὅστις ἐ., Gal.5:10.
(AS)
