καί,
conjunction, copulative, joining words and sentences,

__A
and; also adverb, even, also, just, frequently expressing emphatic assertion or assent, corresponding as positive to the negative οὐ (μή) or οὐδέ (μηδέ). copulative, and,

__A.I
joining words or sentences to those preceding, ἦ, καὶ κυανέῃσιν ἐπ᾽ ὀφρύσινεῦσε Κρονίων [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 1.528, etc.]]: repeated with two or more Nouns, αἱ δὲ ἔλαφοι κ. δορκάδες κ. οἱ ἄγριοι οἶες κ. οἱ ὄνοι οἱ ἄγριοι [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 1.4.7]]; joining only the last pair, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [2nd c.AD: Cleomedes Astronomus 2.1 (p.168.5 Z.), 6th c.AD: Philoponus, Joannes Philosophus “in Aristotelis Analytica Priora commentaria - pars” 239.30, etc., see reading in 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Poetica” 1451a20]]; ὁ ὄχλος πλείων κ. πλείων ἐπέρρει more and more, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 7.5.39]]; to add epithets after πολύς, πολλὰ κ. ἐσθλά [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 9.330; πολλὰ κ. μεγάλα 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 28.1, etc.]]

__A.I.2
to addalimiting or defining expression, πρὸς μακρὸν ὄρος κ. Κύνθιον ὄχθον to the mountain and specially to.., [Refs 5th c.BC+ [“hymnus ad Apollinem” 17, compare 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Agamemnon” 63 (_anapaest meter_), 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Trachiniae” 1277 (_anapaest meter_)]] (sometimes in reverse order, πρὸς δῶμα Διὸς κ. μακρὸν Ὄλυμπον [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 5.398)]]; to add by way of climax, θεῶν.. κ. Ποσειδῶνος all the gods, and above all.. , [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Persae” 750, etc.; ἐχθροὶ κ. ἔχθιστοι 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 7.68; τινὲς κ. συχνοί 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Gorgias” 455c]]; frequently ἄλλοι τε καί.., ἄλλως τε καί.., see at {ἄλλος} [Refs [11.6, ἄλλως 1.3]]; ὀλίγου τινὸς ἄξια κ. οὐδενός little or nothing, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. author] “Ap.” 23a: joined with the _demonstrative_ _pronoun_ οὗτος (which see), εἶναι.. δούλοισι, κ. τούτοισι ὡς δρηπέτῃσι 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 6.11, compare 1.147]]; κ. ταῦτα and this too.. , γελᾶν ἀναπείθειν, κ. ταῦθ᾽ οὕτω πολέμιον ὄντα τῷ γέλωτι [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 2.2.16, etc.]]

__A.II
at the beginning of a sentence,

__A.II.1
in appeals or requests, καί μοι δὸς τὴν Χεῖρα [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 23.75]]; καί μοι λέγε.., καί μοι ἀπόκριναι.., [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Euthyphro” 3a, “Grg.” 462b]]; frequently in Oratt., καί μοι λέγε.. τὸ ψήφισμα, καί μοι ἀνάγνωθι.., [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 18.105, 5th c.BC: Lysias Orator 14.8, etc.]]

__A.II.2
in questions, to introduce an objection or express surprise, κ. τίς τόδ᾽ ἐξίκοιτ᾽ ἂν ἀγγέλων τάχο; [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Agamemnon” 280]]; κ. πῶς..; pray how..? [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Phoenissae” 1348]]; κ. δὴ τί..; but then what..? [Refs [[prev. author] “Hel.” 101]]; κ. ποῖον..; [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Ajax” 462]]; κ. τίς εἶδε πώποτε βοῦς κριβανίτα; [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Acharnenses” 86]]; κἄπειτ᾽ ἔκανε; [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Medea” 1398 (_anapaest meter_)]]; κ. τίς πώποτε Χαριζόμενος ἑτέρῳ τοῦτο εἰργάσατ; [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Antipho Orator 5.57, compare 4th c.BC: Isaeus Orator 1.20, 5th-6th c.BC: Isocrates Orator 12.23, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Theaetetus” 163d, +others]]

__A.II.3
={καίτοι}, and yet, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Equites” 1245, 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Hercules Furens” 509.]]

__A.II.4
at the beginning of a speech, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Lysias Orator “Fragmenta” 36a.]]

__A.III
after words implying sameness or like ness, as, γνώμῃσι ἐχρέωντο ὁμοίῃσι κ. σύ they had the same opinion as you, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 7.50, compare 84]]; ἴσον or ἴσα κ..., [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Tyrannus” 611, 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Electra” 994]]; ἐν ἴσῳ (i.e. ἐστὶ) κ. εἰ.. [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 2.60, etc.]]

__A.III.2
after words implying comparison or opposition, αἱ δαπάναι οὐχ ὁμοίως κ. πρίν [Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. author] 7.28; πᾶν τοὐναντίον ἔχει νῦν τε κ. ὅτε.. 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Leges” 967a.]]

__A.III.3
to express simultaneity, ἦν ἦμαρ δεύτερον.., κἀγὼ κατηγόμην [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Philoctetes” 355, compare 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 1.50]]; παρέρχονταί τε μέσαι νύκτες κ. ψύχεται [τὸ ὕδωρ] [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 4.181, compare 3.108]]; [οἱ Λακεδαιμόνιοι] οὐκ ἔφθασαν τὴν ἀρχὴν κατασχόντες κ. Θηβαίοις εὐθὺς ἐπεβούλευσαν [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Isocrates Orator 8.98.]]

__A.IV
joining an affirmative clause with a negative, ἀλλ᾽ ὥς τι δράσων εἷρπε κοὐ θανούμενος [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Trachiniae” 160, etc.]]

__A.V
καί.., καί.. correlative, not only.., but also.. , κ. ἀεὶ κ. νῦν, κ. τότε κ. νῦν, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Gorgias” 523a, “Phlb.” 60b; κ. κατὰ γῆν κ. κατὰ θάλατταν 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 1.1.7.]]

__A.VI
by anacoluthon, ὣς φαμένη κ. κερδοσύνῃ ἡγήσατ᾽ Ἀθήνη, for ὣς ἔφη κ..., [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 22.247]]; ἔρχεται δὲ αὐτή τε.. κ. τὸν υἱὸν ἔχουσα, for κ. ὁ υἱός, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 1.3.1; ἄλλας τε κατηγεόμενοί σφι ὁδούς, κ. τέλος ἐγίνοντο 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 9.104; τοιοῦτος ὤν, κᾆτ᾽ ἀνὴρ ἔδοξεν εἶναι 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Equites” 392, compare “Nu.” 624.]]

__B
even, also, just,

__B.1
τάχα κεν κ. ἀναίτιον αἰτιόῳτο even the innocent, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 11.654, compare 4.161, etc.]]; δόμεναι κ. μεῖζον ἄεθλον an even greater prize, [Refs [23.551, compare 10.556, 5.362: with numerals, κ. πέντε]]full five,[Refs 5th c.BC+ [23.833; γενομένης κ. δὶς ἐκκλησίας 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 1.44, compare 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 2.44, 60, 68, +others (but ἐτῶν δύο κ. τριῶν]] two or three, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 1.82, compare 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “de Equitandi ratione” 4.4).]]

__B.2
also, κ. ἐγώ I also, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 4.40]]; κ. αὐτοί they also, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 3.4.44, etc.]]; Ἀγίας καὶ Σωκράτης κ. τούτω ἀπεθανέτην likewise died, [Refs [[prev. work] 2.6.30]]; in adding surnames, etc., Ὦχος ὁ κ. Δαρειαῖος [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Ctesias Historicus “fragment” 29.49 (sed Photii est): 1st c.BC: Ptolemaeus Epigrammaticus Papyri have _nominative_ ὃς κ., _genitive_ τοῦ κ. etc., Πανίσκος ὃς κ. Πετεμῖνις “PLond.” 2.219 (b) 2 (2nd c.BC); _dative_ τῷ κ. [prev. work](a) v2, “PRein.” 26.5 (2nd c.BC)]]; nominative ὁ κ. first in [Refs 1st c.BC+ [“PTeb.” 110.1 (1st c.BC)]], frequently later, [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [“BGU” 22.25 (2nd c.AD)]], etc.; Ἰούδας ὁ κ. Μακκαβαῖος [NT+8th c.BC+ [1st c.AD: Josephus Historicus “Antiquitates Judaicae” 12.6.4; Σαῦλος ὁ κ. Παῦλος NT.Act.13.9: with ἄλλος, λαβέτω δὲ κ. ἄλλος 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 21.152]]; εἴπερ τι κ. ἄλλο, ὥς τις κ. ἄλλος, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Memorabilia” 3.6.2, “An.” 1.3.15, compare 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Phaedo” 59a, 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Nubes” 356: frequently in antithetic phrases, οὐ μόνον.., ἀλλὰ καὶ..]], not only.., but also.. , see at {μόνος}; οὐδὲν μᾶλλον.. ἢ οὐ καὶ.. [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 5.94, +others]]

__B.2.b
frequently used both in the antecedent and relative clause, where we put also in the antecedent only, εἰ μὲν κ. σὺ εἶ τῶν ἀνθρώπων ὧνπερ κ. ἐγώ [Refs 8th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Gorgias” 458a, compare 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 6.476, 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 2.1.21.]]

__B.3
frequently in apodosi, after temporal Conjs., ἀλλ᾽ ὅτε δή ῥα.., κ. τότε δή.. [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 1.494, compare 8.69, 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 14.112]]; also after εἰ, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 5.897: in Prose, ὡς δὲ ἔδοξεν, κ. ἐχώρουν 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 2.93]]: as a Hebraism, κ. ἐγένετο.. κ... [LXX+NT [LXX.Gen.24.30, +others, NT.Luke.1.59, etc.]]

__B.4
with Advs., to give emphasis, κ. κάρτα [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 6.125]]; κ. λίην full surely, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 19.408, 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 1.46; κ. μᾶλλον 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 8.470, compare 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Heraclidae” 386]]; κ. πάλαι, κ. πάνυ, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Coloneus” 1252, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Charmides” 154e]]; κ. μάλα, κ. σφόδρα, in answers, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Nubes” 1326, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Laches” 191e.]]

__B.5
with words expressing a minimum, even so much as, were it but, just, ἱέμενος κ. καπνὸν ἀποθρῴσκοντα νοῆσαι [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 1.58]]; οἷς ἡδὺ κ. λέγειν [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Nubes” 528]]; τίς δὲ κ. προσβλέψετα; who will so much as look at you? [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Iphigenia Aulidensis” 1192, compare 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Ranae” 614, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Apologia” 28b, 35b.]]

__B.6
just, τοῦτ᾽ αὐτὸ κ. νοσοῦμεν 'tis just that that ails me, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Andromache” 906, compare “Ba.” 616, 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Trachiniae” 490, 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Pax” 892, “Ra.” 73, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Gorgias” 456a, “Tht.” 166d]]: frequently with a relative, τὸ κ. κλαίουσα τέτηκα [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 3.176; διὸ δὴ καὶ.. 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 1.128, etc.: also in interrogations (usually to be rendered by emphasis in intonation), ποίου Χρόνου δὲ καὶ πεπόρθηται πόλις]]; and how long ago was the city sacked? [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Agamemnon” 278]]; ποῦ καί σφε θάπτε; where is he burying her? [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Alcestis” 834, compare 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Ajax” 1290, +others, 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 5.8.2, 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Pax” 1289, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Euthyphro” 6b, 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 4.46, etc.]]

__B.7
even, just, implying assent, ἔπειτά με κ. λίποι αἰών thereafter let life e'en leave me, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 5.685, compare 17.647, 21.274, 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 7.224.]]

__B.8
κ. εἰ even if, of a whole condition represented as an extreme case, opposed to εἰ κ. although, notwithstanding that, of a condition represented as immaterial even if fulfilled,[Refs 8th c.BC+ [compare 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 4.347, 5.351, 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 13.292, 16.98 with 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 5.410, 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 6.312, 8.139, etc.]]; εἰ κ. ἠπιστάμην if I had been able, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Phaedo” 108d, compare “Lg.” 663d. (This remark does not apply to cases where εἰ and καί]] each exert their force separtely, as εἴ περ ἀδειής τ᾽ ἐστί, καὶ εἰ.. and if..  [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 7.117, compare 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 5.78, etc.)]]

__B.9
before a Participle, to represent either καὶ εἰ.., or εἰ καί.., although, albeit, Ἕκτορα κ. μεμαῶτα μάχης σχήσεσθαι ὀΐω, for ἢν κ. μεμάῃ, how much soever he rage, although he rage, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 9.655; τί σὺ ταῦτα, κ. ἐσθλὸς ἐών, ἀγορεύει; (for εἰ κ. ἐσθλὸς εἶ) 16.627, compare 13.787, 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 2.343, etc.; κ. τύραννος ὢν ὅμως 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Coloneus” 851.]]

__C
Position: καί and, is by Poets sometimes put after another word, ἔγνωκα, τοῖσδε κοὐδὲν ἀντειπεῖν ἔχω, for καὶ τοῖσδε οὐδέν [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Prometheus Vinctus” 51, compare 3rd c.BC: Euphorio Epicus 51.7, etc.]]

__C.2

Abbott-Smith / STEPBible (TBESG)
κακός, -ή, -όν
[in LXX chiefly for רַע ;]
__1. in general, opposite to ἀγαθός, καλός, in various senses, bad, mean, base, worthless (cl.).
__2. In ethical sense, base, evil, wicked: of persons, Mat.21:41 24:48, Php.3:2, Rev.2:2; διαλογισμοί, Mrk.7:21; ὁμιλίαι, 1Co.15:33; ἐπιθυμία (Pro.12:12), Col.3:5; ἔργον, Rom.13:3; neut., κακόν, τὸ κ., evil: Jhn.18:23, Act.23:9, Rom.7:21 14:20 16:19, 1Co.13:5, Heb.5:14, 1Pe.3:10-11, 3Jn.11; pl., Rom.1:30, 1Co.10:6, 1Ti.6:10, Jas.1:13; κ. (τὸ, τὰ κ.) ποιεῖν (πράσσειν), Mat.27:23, Mrk.15:14, Luk.23:22, Jhn.18:30, Rom.3:8 7:19 13:4, 2Co.13:7, 1Pe.3:12; κατεργάζεσθαι, Rom.2:9; of wrongs inflicted, Act.9:13, Rom.12:17, 21 13:10, 1Th.5:15, 2Ti.4:14, 1Pe.3:9.
__3. pernicious, harmful, evil: Luk.16:25, Act.16:28 28:5, Tit.1:12, Jas.3:8, Rev.16:2 (Cremer, 325, 741).
† SYN.: see: (ἄθεσμος)  (AS)

LSJ / STEPBible (TFLSJ)
κᾰκός, ή, όν,

__A
bad:

__A.I
of persons,

__A.I.1
of appearance, ugly, εἶδος μὲν ἔην κακός [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 10.316, compare 2nd c.AD: Pausanias Periegeta 8.49.3.]]

__A.I.2
of birth, ill-born, mean, γένος ἐστὲ διοτρεφέων βασιλήων.., ἐπεὶ οὔ κε κακοὶ τοιούσδε τέκοιεν [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 4.64; Ζεὺς δ᾽ αὐτὸς νέμει ὄλβον.. ἐσθλοῖς ἠδὲ κακοῖσι 6.189; οὐ κακὸν οὐδὲ μὲν ἐσθλόν 22.415; οὐδ᾽ ἐὰν.. φανῶ τρίδουλος, ἐκφανῇ κακή 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Tyrannus” 1063; κακός τ᾽ ὢν κἀκ κακῶν [prev. work] 1397.]]

__A.I.3
of courage, craven, base, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 2.365, 6.489; κακοῦ τρέπεται Χρὼς ἄλλυδις ἄλλῃ (called δειλὸς ἀνήρ in the line above) 13.279]]; Ἕκτωρ σε κ. καὶ ἀνάλκιδα φήσει [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8.153, compare 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 3.375; κ. καὶ ἀνήνορα 10.301; οἵτινες.. ἐγένοντο ἄνδρες κ. ἢ ἀγαθοὶ ἐν τῇ ναυμαχίῃ 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 6.14; κ. καὶ ἄθυμος [prev. author] 7.11]]; οὐδαμῶν κακίονες[Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. work] 104; κακοὺς πρὸς αἰχμήν 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Philoctetes” 1306; κακή τ᾽ ἐς ἀλκὴν καὶ σίδηρον εἰσορᾶν 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Medea” 264; οὐδενὶ ἐπιτρέψοντας κακῷ εἶναι 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 3.2.31.]]

__A.I.4
bad of his kind, i. e. worthless, sorry, unskilled, ἡνίοχοι [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 17.487]]; [τοξότης] ἢ κ. ἢ ἀγαθός[Refs 8th c.BC+ [[prev. work] 632; νομῆες 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 17.246]]; κ. ἀλήτης a bad beggar,[Refs 4th c.BC+ [[prev. work] 578; ἰατρός 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Prometheus Vinctus” 473]]; κυβερνήτης, ναύτης, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Supplices” 880, “Andr.” 457; μάγειρος 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Phaedrus” 265e: with _accusative_ modi, πάντα γὰρ οὐ κακός εἰμι]] I am not bad in all things, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 8.214; κ. γνώμην 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Philoctetes” 910: also with _dative_, κακοὶ γνώμαισι [prev. author] “Aj.” 964]]: with infinitive, κ. μανθάνειν [Refs [[prev. author] “OT” 545]]; [νῆσος] φυτεύεσθαι κακή [Refs [“Tragica Adespota” 393]]; compare 11.

__A.I.5
in moral sense, base, evil, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 11.384, 8th-7th c.BC: Hesiodus Epicus “Opera et Dies” 240]]; opposed to Χρηστός, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Antigone” 520; ὦ κακῶν κάκιστε [prev. author] “OT” 334, “Ph.” 984; πλεῖστον κάκιστος [prev. author] “OC” 744; κ. πρός τινας 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 1.86; εἰς φίλους 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Orestes” 424 codices; περὶ τὰ Χρήματα 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Clitopho” 407c.]]

__A.I.6
wretched, [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [3rd c.BC: Herodas Mimographus 3.42.]]

__A.II
of things, evil, pernicious, frequently in [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Homerus Epicus, etc., as δαίμων, θάνατος, μοῖρα, αἶσα, κῆρες, νοῦσος, ἕλκος, φάρμακα, ὀδύναι, 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 10.64, 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 3.173, 13.602, 1.418, 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 2.316, 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 1.10, 2.723, 22.94, 5.766]]; Χόλος, ἔρις, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 16.206, 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 3.161]]; πόλεμος, ἔπος, ἔργα, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 4.82, 24.767, 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 2.67, +others]]; ἦμαρ, ἄνεμος, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 9.251, 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 5.109]]; of omens and the like, unlucky, ὄρνις, ὄναρ, σῆμα, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 24.219, 10.496, 22.30: also in Trag., κ. τύχη, δαίμων, μόρος, 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Trachiniae” 328, 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Persae” 354, 369, etc.]]; of words, abusive, foul, κ. λόγοι [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Antigone” 259, compare “Tr.” 461]]; κ. ποιμήν, i.e. the storm, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Agamemnon” 657]]: Astrology texts, unlucky, τόποι [Refs 4th c.AD+ [4th c.AD: Hephaestio Astrologus 1.12]]; κ. τύχη, name for the sixth region, [Refs 4th c.AD+ [4th c.AD: Paulus Alexandrinus Astrologus “M.” 1.]]

__B
κακόν, τό, and κακά, τά, as substantive, evil, ill, δίδου δ᾽ ἀγαθόν τε κακόν τε [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 8.63; ἀθάνατον κακόν 12.118; ἐκ μεγάλων κακῶν πεφευγέναι 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.65]]; so κ. ἄμαχον, ἄπρηκτα, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “P.” 2.76, “I.” 8(7).8]]; ἔκπαγλον, ἄφερτον, ἀμήχανον, etc., [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Agamemnon” 862, 1102, 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Medea” 447, etc.]]; κακὸν ἥκει τινί there's trouble in store for some one, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Ranae” 552]]; δυοῖν ἀποκρίνας κακοῖν the least of two evils, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Tyrannus” 640, compare “OC” 496]]; κακῶν Ἰλιάς, see at {Ἰλιά; κακόν τι ῥέξαι τινά} to do harm or ill to any one, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 2.195, etc.; πολλὰ κάκ᾽ ἀνθρώποισιν ἐώργει 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 14.289]]; κακὰ φέρειν, τεύχειν τινί, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 2.304, 8th-7th c.BC: Hesiodus Epicus “Opera et Dies” 265]]; κακόν τι (or κακὰ) ποιεῖν τινα (see. δράω, ποιέω, ἐργάζομαι); κακὸν πάσχειν ὑπό τινος to suffer evil from one, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 8.48, etc.: in Trag. frequently repeated, κακὰ κακῶν, ={τὰ κάκιστα}, 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Coloneus” 1238 (Lyric poetry); εἴ τι πρεσβύτερον ἔτι κακοῦ κακόν [prev. author] “OT” 1365 (Lyric poetry); δεινὰ πρὸς κακοῖς κακά [prev. author] “OC” 595, compare “Ant.” 1281; δόσιν κακὰν κακῶν κακοῖς 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Persae” 1041 (Lyric poetry).]]

__B.2
κακά, τά, evil words, reproaches, πολλά τε καὶ κακὰ λέγειν [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 8.61, compare 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Septem contra Thebas” 571, 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Ajax” 1244, “Ph.” 382, etc.]]

__B.3
Philos., κακόν, τό, Evil, [Refs 3rd c.AD+ [Stoic. 3.18, +others, 3rd c.AD: Plotinus Philosophus 1.8.1, +others]]

__B.4
of a person, pest, nuisance, τουτὶ παρέξει τὸ κ. ἡμῖν πράγματα [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Aves” 931]]; also, comically, ὅσον συνείλεκται κακὸν ὀρνέων what a devil of a lot of birds, [Refs [[prev. work] 294.]]

__C
degrees of Comparison:

__C.1
regular comparative in Epic dialect, κακώτερος [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 6.275, 15.343, 3rd c.BC: Theocritus Poeta Bucolicus 27.22, 3rd c.BC: Apollonius Rhodius Epicus 3.421, etc.]]: also in late Prose, [Refs 4th c.AD+ [4th c.AD: Alciphro Epistolographus 3.62]]: irregular κακίων, ον [with ῐ], [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 2.277, 6th c.BC: Theognis Elegiacus 262, etc.]], with ῑ in Trag., except [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Fragmenta” 546 (_anapaest meter_); κακῑότερος “Anthologia Graeca” 12.7 (from Strato).]]

__C.2
superlative κάκιστος [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Homerus Epicus, etc.--Cf. also Χείρων, Χείριστος, and ἥσσων, ἥκιστος.]]

__D
adverb κακῶς ill, ἢ εὖ ἦε κακῶς [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 2.253, etc.]]; κακῶς ποιεῖν τινα to treat one ill; κακῶς ποιεῖν τι to hurt, damage a thing; κακῶς ποιεῖν τινά τι to do one any evil or harm; κ. πράσσειν to fare ill, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Prometheus Vinctus” 266, etc.; κάκιον ἢ πρότερον πράττειν 5th-6th c.BC: Andocides Orator 4.11; κ. ἔχειν 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Ranae” 58, etc.]]; of illness, [NT+4th c.BC+ [NT.Matt.4.24; rarely κακῶς πάσχειν 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Prometheus Vinctus” 759, 1041 (_anapaest meter_)]]; Χρῆν Κανδαύλῃ γενέσθαι κ. [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.8; κ. ὄλοισθε 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Philoctetes” 1035, etc.]]; with play on two senses, ὡς κ. ἔχει ἅπας ἰατρός, ἂν κ. μηδεὶς ἔχῃ [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [3rd c.BC(?): Philemo Junior Comicus 2]]; κ. ἐρεῖν τινά, λέγειν τὴν πόλιν, [Refs 6th c.BC+ [6th c.BC: Mimnermus Lyricus 7.4, 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Acharnenses” 503]]; κ. εἰδότες, ={ἀγνοοῦντες}, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 2.3.13, 5th-6th c.BC: Isocrates Orator 8.32, compare 4th c.BC: Hyperides Orator “pro Euxenippo” 33]]; κακῶς ἐκπέφευγα I have barely escaped, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 21.126]]: comparative κάκιον [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.109, 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Tyrannus” 428, And.[same place], 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Menexenus” 236a, etc.]]: superlative κάκιστα [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Ranae” 1456, “Pax” 2, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 420b, etc.]]

__D.2
adverb and adjective frequently coupled in Trag., Attic dialect, etc., κακὸν κακῶς νιν.. ἐκτρῖψαι βίον [NT+5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Tyrannus” 248; κακὸς κακῶς ταφήσῃ 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Troades” 446 (troch.); ἀπό σ᾽ ὀλῶ κακὸν κακῶς 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Plutus” 65, compare “Eq.” 189, 190, 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 32.6, 6th c.AD: Procopius Caesariensis Historicus “de Bello Persico” 1.24; κακοὺς κακῶς ἀπολέσει αὐτούς NT.Matt.21.41; κακοὺς κάκιστα 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Ajax” 839]]; in reversed order, ὥσπερ ἀξία κακῶς κακὴ θανεῖται [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Troades” 1055]]; with intervening words, κακῶς.. ἀπόλλυσθαι κακούς [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Philoctetes” 1369, compare 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Cyclops” 268, 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Equites” 2]]. (Perh. cognate with Avest. kasu-, comparative kasyah-, superlative kasišta- 'small', Lithuanian nukašëti 'grow feeble, thin', [Refs 1st c.BC+ [\{1st c.BC-1st c.AD\}: Germanicus Caesar Epigrammaticus]] hager.)

(κακός),
adv., [in LXX: Wis.18:19, 4Ma.6:17.al.; κ. εἰπεῖν, ἐρεῖν (אָרַר, קָלַל pi.), Exo.22:28 (27), Lev.19:14, Isa.8:21; κ. ἔχειν (חָלָה, Eze.34:4, al. ;]

__(a) in physical sense: κ. ἔχειν, to be ill, Mat.4:24 8:16 9:12 14:35 17:15, Mrk.1:32, 34 2:17 6:55 5:31 7:2; πάσχειν, Mat.17:15 (WH, mg.); δαιμονίζεσθαι, Mat.15:22; κακοὺς κ. ἀπολέσει (as frequently in cl., see LS, see word; MM, Exp., xv), evil that they are, he will evilly, etc., Mat.21:41;
__(b) in moral sense, wrongly (1Ma.7:42, 4Mac, l.with, al.): κ. λαλεῖν, Jhn.18:23; είπεῖν, with accusative of person(s), Act.23:5; αἰτεῖσθαι, Jas.4:8,†

LSJ / STEPBible (TFLSJ)
Included with:  κᾰκός, ή, όν,

__A
bad:

__A.I
of persons,

__A.I.1
of appearance, ugly, εἶδος μὲν ἔην κακός [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 10.316, compare 2nd c.AD: Pausanias Periegeta 8.49.3.]]

__A.I.2
of birth, ill-born, mean, γένος ἐστὲ διοτρεφέων βασιλήων.., ἐπεὶ οὔ κε κακοὶ τοιούσδε τέκοιεν [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 4.64; Ζεὺς δ᾽ αὐτὸς νέμει ὄλβον.. ἐσθλοῖς ἠδὲ κακοῖσι 6.189; οὐ κακὸν οὐδὲ μὲν ἐσθλόν 22.415; οὐδ᾽ ἐὰν.. φανῶ τρίδουλος, ἐκφανῇ κακή 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Tyrannus” 1063; κακός τ᾽ ὢν κἀκ κακῶν [prev. work] 1397.]]

__A.I.3
of courage, craven, base, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 2.365, 6.489; κακοῦ τρέπεται Χρὼς ἄλλυδις ἄλλῃ (called δειλὸς ἀνήρ in the line above) 13.279]]; Ἕκτωρ σε κ. καὶ ἀνάλκιδα φήσει [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8.153, compare 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 3.375; κ. καὶ ἀνήνορα 10.301; οἵτινες.. ἐγένοντο ἄνδρες κ. ἢ ἀγαθοὶ ἐν τῇ ναυμαχίῃ 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 6.14; κ. καὶ ἄθυμος [prev. author] 7.11]]; οὐδαμῶν κακίονες[Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. work] 104; κακοὺς πρὸς αἰχμήν 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Philoctetes” 1306; κακή τ᾽ ἐς ἀλκὴν καὶ σίδηρον εἰσορᾶν 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Medea” 264; οὐδενὶ ἐπιτρέψοντας κακῷ εἶναι 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 3.2.31.]]

__A.I.4
bad of his kind, i. e. worthless, sorry, unskilled, ἡνίοχοι [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 17.487]]; [τοξότης] ἢ κ. ἢ ἀγαθός[Refs 8th c.BC+ [[prev. work] 632; νομῆες 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 17.246]]; κ. ἀλήτης a bad beggar,[Refs 4th c.BC+ [[prev. work] 578; ἰατρός 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Prometheus Vinctus” 473]]; κυβερνήτης, ναύτης, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Supplices” 880, “Andr.” 457; μάγειρος 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Phaedrus” 265e: with _accusative_ modi, πάντα γὰρ οὐ κακός εἰμι]] I am not bad in all things, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 8.214; κ. γνώμην 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Philoctetes” 910: also with _dative_, κακοὶ γνώμαισι [prev. author] “Aj.” 964]]: with infinitive, κ. μανθάνειν [Refs [[prev. author] “OT” 545]]; [νῆσος] φυτεύεσθαι κακή [Refs [“Tragica Adespota” 393]]; compare 11.

__A.I.5
in moral sense, base, evil, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 11.384, 8th-7th c.BC: Hesiodus Epicus “Opera et Dies” 240]]; opposed to Χρηστός, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Antigone” 520; ὦ κακῶν κάκιστε [prev. author] “OT” 334, “Ph.” 984; πλεῖστον κάκιστος [prev. author] “OC” 744; κ. πρός τινας 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 1.86; εἰς φίλους 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Orestes” 424 codices; περὶ τὰ Χρήματα 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Clitopho” 407c.]]

__A.I.6
wretched, [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [3rd c.BC: Herodas Mimographus 3.42.]]

__A.II
of things, evil, pernicious, frequently in [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Homerus Epicus, etc., as δαίμων, θάνατος, μοῖρα, αἶσα, κῆρες, νοῦσος, ἕλκος, φάρμακα, ὀδύναι, 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 10.64, 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 3.173, 13.602, 1.418, 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 2.316, 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 1.10, 2.723, 22.94, 5.766]]; Χόλος, ἔρις, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 16.206, 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 3.161]]; πόλεμος, ἔπος, ἔργα, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 4.82, 24.767, 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 2.67, +others]]; ἦμαρ, ἄνεμος, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 9.251, 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 5.109]]; of omens and the like, unlucky, ὄρνις, ὄναρ, σῆμα, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 24.219, 10.496, 22.30: also in Trag., κ. τύχη, δαίμων, μόρος, 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Trachiniae” 328, 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Persae” 354, 369, etc.]]; of words, abusive, foul, κ. λόγοι [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Antigone” 259, compare “Tr.” 461]]; κ. ποιμήν, i.e. the storm, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Agamemnon” 657]]: Astrology texts, unlucky, τόποι [Refs 4th c.AD+ [4th c.AD: Hephaestio Astrologus 1.12]]; κ. τύχη, name for the sixth region, [Refs 4th c.AD+ [4th c.AD: Paulus Alexandrinus Astrologus “M.” 1.]]

__B
κακόν, τό, and κακά, τά, as substantive, evil, ill, δίδου δ᾽ ἀγαθόν τε κακόν τε [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 8.63; ἀθάνατον κακόν 12.118; ἐκ μεγάλων κακῶν πεφευγέναι 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.65]]; so κ. ἄμαχον, ἄπρηκτα, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “P.” 2.76, “I.” 8(7).8]]; ἔκπαγλον, ἄφερτον, ἀμήχανον, etc., [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Agamemnon” 862, 1102, 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Medea” 447, etc.]]; κακὸν ἥκει τινί there's trouble in store for some one, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Ranae” 552]]; δυοῖν ἀποκρίνας κακοῖν the least of two evils, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Tyrannus” 640, compare “OC” 496]]; κακῶν Ἰλιάς, see at {Ἰλιά; κακόν τι ῥέξαι τινά} to do harm or ill to any one, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 2.195, etc.; πολλὰ κάκ᾽ ἀνθρώποισιν ἐώργει 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 14.289]]; κακὰ φέρειν, τεύχειν τινί, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 2.304, 8th-7th c.BC: Hesiodus Epicus “Opera et Dies” 265]]; κακόν τι (or κακὰ) ποιεῖν τινα (see. δράω, ποιέω, ἐργάζομαι); κακὸν πάσχειν ὑπό τινος to suffer evil from one, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 8.48, etc.: in Trag. frequently repeated, κακὰ κακῶν, ={τὰ κάκιστα}, 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Coloneus” 1238 (Lyric poetry); εἴ τι πρεσβύτερον ἔτι κακοῦ κακόν [prev. author] “OT” 1365 (Lyric poetry); δεινὰ πρὸς κακοῖς κακά [prev. author] “OC” 595, compare “Ant.” 1281; δόσιν κακὰν κακῶν κακοῖς 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Persae” 1041 (Lyric poetry).]]

__B.2
κακά, τά, evil words, reproaches, πολλά τε καὶ κακὰ λέγειν [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 8.61, compare 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Septem contra Thebas” 571, 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Ajax” 1244, “Ph.” 382, etc.]]

__B.3
Philos., κακόν, τό, Evil, [Refs 3rd c.AD+ [Stoic. 3.18, +others, 3rd c.AD: Plotinus Philosophus 1.8.1, +others]]

__B.4
of a person, pest, nuisance, τουτὶ παρέξει τὸ κ. ἡμῖν πράγματα [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Aves” 931]]; also, comically, ὅσον συνείλεκται κακὸν ὀρνέων what a devil of a lot of birds, [Refs [[prev. work] 294.]]

__C
degrees of Comparison:

__C.1
regular comparative in Epic dialect, κακώτερος [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 6.275, 15.343, 3rd c.BC: Theocritus Poeta Bucolicus 27.22, 3rd c.BC: Apollonius Rhodius Epicus 3.421, etc.]]: also in late Prose, [Refs 4th c.AD+ [4th c.AD: Alciphro Epistolographus 3.62]]: irregular κακίων, ον [with ῐ], [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 2.277, 6th c.BC: Theognis Elegiacus 262, etc.]], with ῑ in Trag., except [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Fragmenta” 546 (_anapaest meter_); κακῑότερος “Anthologia Graeca” 12.7 (from Strato).]]

__C.2
superlative κάκιστος [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Homerus Epicus, etc.--Cf. also Χείρων, Χείριστος, and ἥσσων, ἥκιστος.]]

__D
adverb κακῶς ill, ἢ εὖ ἦε κακῶς [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 2.253, etc.]]; κακῶς ποιεῖν τινα to treat one ill; κακῶς ποιεῖν τι to hurt, damage a thing; κακῶς ποιεῖν τινά τι to do one any evil or harm; κ. πράσσειν to fare ill, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Prometheus Vinctus” 266, etc.; κάκιον ἢ πρότερον πράττειν 5th-6th c.BC: Andocides Orator 4.11; κ. ἔχειν 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Ranae” 58, etc.]]; of illness, [NT+4th c.BC+ [NT.Matt.4.24; rarely κακῶς πάσχειν 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Prometheus Vinctus” 759, 1041 (_anapaest meter_)]]; Χρῆν Κανδαύλῃ γενέσθαι κ. [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.8; κ. ὄλοισθε 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Philoctetes” 1035, etc.]]; with play on two senses, ὡς κ. ἔχει ἅπας ἰατρός, ἂν κ. μηδεὶς ἔχῃ [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [3rd c.BC(?): Philemo Junior Comicus 2]]; κ. ἐρεῖν τινά, λέγειν τὴν πόλιν, [Refs 6th c.BC+ [6th c.BC: Mimnermus Lyricus 7.4, 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Acharnenses” 503]]; κ. εἰδότες, ={ἀγνοοῦντες}, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 2.3.13, 5th-6th c.BC: Isocrates Orator 8.32, compare 4th c.BC: Hyperides Orator “pro Euxenippo” 33]]; κακῶς ἐκπέφευγα I have barely escaped, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 21.126]]: comparative κάκιον [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.109, 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Tyrannus” 428, And.[same place], 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Menexenus” 236a, etc.]]: superlative κάκιστα [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Ranae” 1456, “Pax” 2, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 420b, etc.]]

__D.2
adverb and adjective frequently coupled in Trag., Attic dialect, etc., κακὸν κακῶς νιν.. ἐκτρῖψαι βίον [NT+5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Tyrannus” 248; κακὸς κακῶς ταφήσῃ 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Troades” 446 (troch.); ἀπό σ᾽ ὀλῶ κακὸν κακῶς 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Plutus” 65, compare “Eq.” 189, 190, 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 32.6, 6th c.AD: Procopius Caesariensis Historicus “de Bello Persico” 1.24; κακοὺς κακῶς ἀπολέσει αὐτούς NT.Matt.21.41; κακοὺς κάκιστα 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Ajax” 839]]; in reversed order, ὥσπερ ἀξία κακῶς κακὴ θανεῖται [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Troades” 1055]]; with intervening words, κακῶς.. ἀπόλλυσθαι κακούς [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Philoctetes” 1369, compare 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Cyclops” 268, 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Equites” 2]]. (Perh. cognate with Avest. kasu-, comparative kasyah-, superlative kasišta- 'small', Lithuanian nukašëti 'grow feeble, thin', [Refs 1st c.BC+ [\{1st c.BC-1st c.AD\}: Germanicus Caesar Epigrammaticus]] hager.)

(see. κάλαμος) stalk, especially the stalk or straw of corn, metaphorically in [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Homerus Epicus, αἶψά τε φυλόπιδος πέλεται κόρος ἀνθρώποισιν, ἧς τε πλείστην μὲν καλάμην Χθονὶ Χαλκὸς ἔχευεν, ἄμητος δ᾽ ὀλίγιστος]], i.e. when there is much straw and little harvest, much slaughter and little profit, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 19.222]]; κ. πυρῶν wheat-straw, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 4.33; σῖτος σὺν τῇ καλάμῃ ἀποκείμενος 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 5.4.27; καλάμαν τε καὶ ἱερὰ δράγματα.. ἀσταχύων 3rd c.BC: Callimachus Epicus “Hymnus in Cererem” 20]]; proverbial of a greedy farmer, πυροὺς ἐπὶ καλάμῃ ἀροῦν to exhaust ground by one corn-crop after another, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Lysias Orator “Fragmenta” 77: _plural_, σῖτος ἐπὶ ταῖς κ. 1st c.BC: Dionysius Halicarnassensis 5.13.]]

__2
stubble, [NT+4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Meteorologica” 341b27, “PSI” 4.380.6 (3rd c.BC), NT.1Cor.3.12, etc.: _metaphorically_, of an old man, καλάμην γέ σ᾽ ὀΐομαι εἰσορόωντα γιγνώσκειν]] thou mayst still, I ween, perceive the stubble (i.e. the residue) of former strength, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 14.214; τὸ γῆρας καλάμη 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Rhetorica” 1410b14; τὴν κ. δωρῇ, δοὺς ἑτέροις τὸ θέρος “Anthologia Graeca” 11.36 (1st c.AD: Philippus Epigrammaticus)]]; Ῥήσου κ. the remains of Rhesus, i.e. his corpse, Oracle texts cited in [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd c.AD: Polyaenus Historicus 6.53]]; ἀπὸ τῆς κ. τεκμαίρεσθαι to judge from the remains, [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd c.AD: Lucianus Sophista “Alex.” 5.]]

__3
κολχὶς κ., ={λίνον}, [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [3rd c.BC: Callimachus Epicus “Fragmenta” 265.]]

__II
={κάλαμος}, [Refs 3rd c.AD+ [3rd c.AD: Heliodorus Scriptor Eroticus 8.9.]]

κάλαμος, -ου, ὁ
[in LXX chiefly for קָנֶה, Isa.42:3, Eze.40:3 ff., al. ;]
a reed: Mat.11:7 12:20" (LXX) Luk.7:24; hence, accusative, to its various uses,
__(a) a reed-pipe, flute;
__(b) a reed-staff, staff (cf. 4Ki.18:21, ῥάβδος καλαμίνη): Mat.27:29-30, 48, Mrk.15:19, 36;
__(with) a measuring reed or rod (Ez, l.with): Rev.11:1 21:15-16;
__(d) a writing reed, a pen: III Jn 13 (cf. Milligan, NTD, 9, 7).†
(AS)

κάλᾰμος [κᾰ], ὁ,
reed, used for thatching or wattling, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 5.101, +others, 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 2.76; for wreaths, κ. λευκός 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Nubes” 1006 (_anapaest meter_); for bedding, 1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus “Lycurgus” 16; for fuel, “PCair.Zen.” 85 (3rd c.BC)]]; various species, κ. εὐώδης, ἀρωματικός, sweet flag, Acorus Calamus, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-3rd c.BC: Theophrastus Philosophus “Historia Plantarum” 4.8.4, 9.7.1, “Od.” 33, 1st c.AD: Dioscorides (Dioscurides) Medicus 1.18]]; κ. αὐλητικός pole-reed, Arundo Donax, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-3rd c.BC: Theophrastus Philosophus “Historia Plantarum” 4.11.1, 9]]; κ. εἰλετίας marram, Ammophila arundinacea, [Refs [[prev. work] 13]]; κ. ἐπίγειος bush-grass, Calamagrostis epigeios, [Refs [[prev. passage]]]; κ. Ἰνδικός bamboo, Bambusa arundinacea, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. passage], 1st c.AD: Dioscorides (Dioscurides) Medicus 5.92, “PLond.” 2.191.11 (2nd c.AD), “Geoponica” 2.6.23, compare 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 3.98]]; κ. Ἰνδικὸς ὁ ἄρρην male bamboo, Dendrocalamus strictus, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-3rd c.BC: Theophrastus Philosophus “Historia Plantarum” 4.11.13]]; κ. κύπριος, ={δόναξ}, [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [3rd c.BC: Asclepiades Epigrammaticus cited in 2nd c.AD: Galenus Medicus 12.414]]; κ. πλόκιμος spear-grass, Phragmites communis, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-3rd c.BC: Theophrastus Philosophus “Historia Plantarum” 4.11.1]]; κ. Χαρακίας, Arundo Donax, [Refs [[prev. passage]]]

__II
applied to various uses,

__II.1
reed-pipe, flute, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “O.” 10(11).84, “N.” 5.38, 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Electra” 702 (Lyric poetry), “IT” 1126 (Lyric poetry).]]

__II.2
fishing-rod, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Comicus 11, 3rd c.BC: Theocritus Poeta Bucolicus 21.43, 2nd c.AD: Lucianus Sophista “DMort.” 27.9; κ. ἁλιευτικός 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “de Partibus Animalium” 693a23.]]

__II.3
limed twig used by fowlers, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [2nd c.BC: Bion Bucolicus “fragment” 10.5, 5th-4th c.BC: Aesopus Fabularum Scriptor 171, 296.]]

__II.4
shaft of an arrow, [Refs 1st c.BC+ [1st c.BC: Ptolemaeus Epigrammaticus “Alm.” 7.5]]; made of κ. τοξικός, or Κρητικός, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-3rd c.BC: Theophrastus Philosophus “Historia Plantarum” 4.11.11.]]

__II.5
reed-pen, [LXX+NT+1st c.BC+ [LXX.Psa.44(45).1, NT.3John.13, 1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus “Demosthenes” 29, 2nd c.AD: Lucianus Sophista “Hist.Conscr.” 38; κάλαμοι γραφικοί “PGrenf.” 2.38.7 (1st c.BC)]]; κ. γραφεῖς [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd c.AD(?): Pollianus Epigrammaticus 10.61.]]

__II.6
measuring-rod, [NT+2nd c.AD+ [NT.Rev. 11.1, +others: hence, a definite measure, “IG” 9(1).61.50 (Daulis, 2nd c.AD)]]; = 5 πήχεις, [Refs 2nd c.BC+ [2nd-1st c.BC(?): Hero Mechanicus]] “*Geometry texts” 4.11; = 6 2/3 πήχεις, [Refs [[prev. work]23.13.]]

__II.7
in Medicine texts, tube for insufflation, [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [2nd c.AD: Aretaeus Medicus “ὀξέων νούσων θεραπευτικόν” 1.9, 3rd c.BC: Asclepiades Epigrammaticus cited in 2nd c.AD: Galenus Medicus 12.985; for fumigation, 1st c.AD: Dioscorides (Dioscurides) Medicus “Eup.” 1.56; for extraction, 1st c.AD: Celsus Medicus 7.5.2]]; also, splint, [Refs 6th c.AD+ [6th c.AD: Palladas Epigrammaticus]]in Hp.Fract.[Refs [12.282 C.]]

__II.8
ornament of female dress, [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [“Anthologia Graeca” 6.292 (3rd c.BC: Hedylus Epigrammaticus).]]

__II.9
stake to which vines were tied, [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [“PFlor.” 369.4 (2nd c.AD), 4th c.AD: Julianus Imperator “Orationes” 3.125b, etc.]]

__III
collectively,

__III.1
reed, i.e. reeds, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Meteorologica” 359b1, “POxy.” 742.2 (1st c.BC)]], etc.: in plural, reed-beds, [Refs 2nd c.BC+ [2nd c.BC: Polybius Historicus 3.71.4.]]

__III.2
of plants, which are neither shrub nor bush (ὕλη), nor tree (δένδρον), [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 1.5.1.]]

__III.3
mat of reeds, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 372b]]; roof of reeds [Refs 5th c.AD+ [(from Coan), 5th c.AD(?): Hesychius Legal icographus]]

__IV
={καλάμη}, stalk of wheat, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Oeconomicus” 18.2.]]

__V
ὁ κ. τοῦ σκέλους the shinbone, [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [Scholia 2nd c.AD: Lucianus Sophista “VH” 1.23.]]

__VI
ticket for obtaining corn-rations, = tessera frumentaria, [Refs [“Corpus Glossariorum Latinorum”]] (Cf. Latin culmus, OHG. halm, etc.)

short_definition: to call: call — καλέω, -ῶ, — to call: name — καλέω, -ῶ,
deep_entry:
Abbott-Smith / STEPBible (TBESG)
καλέω, -ῶ,
[in LXX chiefly for קרא ;]
__1. to call, summon: with accusative of person(s), Mat.20:8 25:14, Mrk.3:31, Luk.19:13, Act.4:18; before ἐκ, Mat.2:15 (LXX); metaphorically, 1Pe.2:9.
__2. to call to one's house, invite: Luk.14:16, 1Co.10:27, Rev.19:9; εἰς τ. γάμους, Mat.22:3, 9 Luk.14:8, 9 Jhn.2:2; ὁ καλέσας, Luk.7:39; οἱ κεκλημένοι, Mat.22:8; metaphorically, of inviting to partake of the blessings of the kingdom of God (Dalman, Words, 118f.): Rom.8:30 9:24, 25 1Co.7:17, 18; before εἰς, 1Co.1:9, 1Th.2:12, 1Ti.6:12; ὁ καλῶν (καλέσας), of God, Gal.1:6 5:8, 1Th.5:24, 1Pe.1:15, 2Pe.1:3; οἱ κεκλκλημένοι, Heb.9:15; before ἐν (ἐπί), 1Co.7:15, Gal.5:13, Eph.4:4, 1Th.4:7; κλήσει, Eph.4:1, 2Ti.1:9.
__3. to call, name call by name: pass., Mat.2:23, Luk.1:32, al.; καλούμενος, Luk.7:11, Act.7:58, al.; ὁ κ. (Deiss., BS, 210), Luk.6:15 22:3 23:33, Act.10:1, Rev.12:9, al.; with pred nom., Mat.5:9, Luk.1:35, Rom.9:26, Jas.2:23, 1Jn.3:1. (Cf. ἀντι-, ἐν-, εἰσ- (-μαι), ἐπι-, μετα-, παρα-, συν-παρα-, προ-, προσ-, συν-καλέω.)
(AS)

κᾰλέω,
Aeolic dialect κάλημι (which see), Epic dialect infinitive καλήμεναι [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 10.125]]: Ionic dialect imperfect καλέεσκον [Refs [6.402]]; 3rd.pers. singular κάλεσκε [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [3rd c.BC: Apollonius Rhodius Epicus 4.1514]]: future, Ionic dialect καλέω [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 3.383]], Attic dialect καλῶ [LXX+5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Symposium” 175a, 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Symposium” 1.15, etc.; later καλέσω LXX.Gen.16.11, +others, 1st c.AD: Philo Judaeus 1.69, (παρα-) 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 8.14 codices, “SIG” 656.40 (Teos, 2nd c.BC), (ἐγ-) variant in 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 19.133, compare 23.123 codices (καλέσω in 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Philoctetes” 1452 (_anapaest meter_), 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Plutus” 964, etc., is]]aorist 1 subjunctive): aorist 1 ἐκάλεσα, Epic dialect ἐκάλεσσα, κάλεσσα, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 17.379, 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 16.693]] (late Epic dialect ἔκλησα [Refs 2nd c.BC+ [2nd c.BC: Nicander Epicus “fragment” 86, late Prose ἐκάλησα Ps.Callisth. 3.35)]]: perfect κέκληκα [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Plutus” 260, etc.]]:—middle, Attic dialect future καλοῦμαι [Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. author] “Nu.” 1221, “Ec.” 864; in _passive_ sense, 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Electra” 971, 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Orestes” 1140, etc.]]; later καλέσομαι (ἐκ-, ἐπι-) uncertain reading in [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aeschines Orator 1.174, 4th c.BC: Lycurgus Orator 17]]: aorist 1 ἐκαλεσάμην [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 7.189, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Leges” 937a]]; Epic dialect καλεσσάμην [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 1.54, _3rd.pers._ _plural_ καλέσαντο [prev. work] 270]]:—passive, future κεκλήσομαι [LXX+8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 3.138, 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Septem contra Thebas” 698 (Lyric poetry), “Pr.” 840, etc.; κληθήσομαι 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Leges” 681d, LXX.Gen.48.6, variant in 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Troades” 13]]: aorist ἐκλήθην [Refs 7th c.BC+ [7th c.BC: Archilochus Lyricus 78, 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Tyrannus” 1359, 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Thesmophoriazusae” 862, etc.:]]perfect κέκλημαι, Epic dialect 3rd.pers. plural κεκλήαται [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [3rd c.BC: Apollonius Rhodius Epicus 1.1128]], Ionic dialect κεκλέαται [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 2.164]]; Epic dialect 3rd.pers. plural pluperfect κεκλήατο [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 10.195; _optative_ κεκλῄμην, κεκλῇο 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Philoctetes” 119, κεκλῄμεθα 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Lysistrata” 253: late]]perfect κεκάλεσμαι Suid. see at {κλητή}.

__I
call, summon, εἰς ἀγορὴν καλέσαντα [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 1.90; ἐς Ὄλυμπον 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 1.402]]; ἀγορήνδε, θάλαμόνδε, θάνατόνδε, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 20.4, 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 2.348, 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 16.693: with _accusative_ only, κεκλήατο (for -ηντο) βουλήν]] they had been summoned to the council, [Refs [10.195: followed by]]infinitive, αὐτοὶ γὰρ κάλεον συμμητιάασθαι[Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. work] 197; καιρὸς καλεῖ.. 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Philoctetes” 466; κἄμ᾽ ὑπηρετεῖν καλεῖς [prev. author] “El.” 996]]; κ. τινὰ εἰς ἕ, ἐπὶ οἷ, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 23.203, 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 17.330, etc.; εἰς μαρτυρίαν κληθείς 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Leges” 937a; ἐμὲ νῦν ἤδη καλεῖ ἡ εἱμαρμένη [prev. author] “Phd.” 115a]]; demand, require, ἡ ἡμέρα 'κείνη εὔνουν καὶ πλούσιον ἄνδρα ἐκάλει [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 18.172:]]aorist middle, καλέσασθαί τινα call to oneself, frequently in Epic dialect, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 1.270, 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 8.43, etc.; φωνῇ 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 3.161; ἀγορήνδε λαόν 1.54]]; call a witness, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Lg.” [prev. cited]]]

__I.2
call to one's house or to a repast, invite (not in [NT+8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad”), 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 10.231, 17.382, +others, NT.1Cor.10.27]]; later usually with a word added, κ. ἐπὶ δεῖπνον [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 9.16 (_passive_), 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 2.1.30, etc.; ἐς ἔρανον 5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “O.” 1.37; ἐς θοίνην 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Ion” 1140; ὑπὸ σοῦ κεκλημένος 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Symposium” 174d, etc.]]; κληθέντες πρός τινα invited to his house, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 19.196]]; ὁ κεκλημένος the guest, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-3rd c.BC: Damoxenus Comicus 2.26.]]

__I.3
invoke, Δία [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.44, compare 5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “O.” 6.58, 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Septem contra Thebas” 223; at sacrifices, Scholia 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Ranae” 482; μάρτυρας κ. θεούς 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Trachiniae” 1248, compare 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 18.141]]:—middle, τοὺς θεοὺς καλούμεθα [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Choephori” 201, compare 216; also μαρτύριά τε καὶ τεκμήρια καλεῖσθε [prev. author] “Eu.” 486]]; but ἀράς, ἅς σοι καλοῦμαι which I call down on thee, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Coloneus” 1385]]:—passive, of the god, to be invoked, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Eumenides” 417.]]

__I.4
as law-term, summon, of the judge, καλεῖν τινας εἰς τὸ δικαστήριον cite or summon before the court, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 19.211, etc.]]; simply καλεῖν [Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. work]212, 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Vespae” 851, etc.; ἐὰν μὲν καλέσῃ 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 21.56]]; also ὁ ἄρχων τὴν δίκην καλεῖ calls on the case, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Vespae” 1441]]:—passive, ἡ πατροκτόνος δίκη κεκλῇτ᾽ ἂν αὐτῷ [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Fragmenta” 696]]; πρὶν τὴν ἐμὴν [δίκην] καλεῖσθαι before it is called on, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Nubes” 780; καλουμένης τῆς γραφῆς 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 58.43]]; but,

__I.4.b
of the plaintiff in middle, καλεῖσθαί τινα to sue at law, bring before the court, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Nubes” 1221, +others, 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 23.63; κ. τινὰ ὕβρεως 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Aves” 1046; κ. τινὰ πρὸς τὴν ἀρχήν 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Leges” 914c]]; ὁ καλεσάμενος the plaintiff, [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [PHal. 1.224 (3rd c.BC).]]

__I.5
with an abstract subject, demand, require, καλεῖ ἡ τάξις with infinitive, [Refs 3rd c.AD+ [“CPHerm.” 25ii7 (3rd c.AD).]]

__I.6
metaphorically in passive, καλουμένης τῆς δυνάμεως πρὸς τὴν συναναληψίαν called forth, summoned, [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd c.AD: Soranus Medicus 1.29.]]

__II
call by name, name, ὃν Βριάρεων καλέουσι θεοί [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 1.403, compare 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 5.273, etc.; κοτύλην δέ τέ μιν καλέουσι 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 5.306; ὥς σφας καλοῦμεν Εὐμενίδας 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Coloneus” 486, compare 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Prometheus Vinctus” 86, etc.]]; ὄνομα καλεῖν τινα call him by a name, εἴπ᾽ ὄνομ᾽ ὅττι σε κεῖθι κάλεον [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 8.550, compare 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Ion” 259, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Cratylus” 383b, etc.]] (in passive, οὔνομα καλέεσθαι [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.173, compare 5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “O.” 6.56): without ὄνομα, τί νιν καλοῦσα τύχοιμ᾽ ἄ; 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Agamemnon” 1232; τοῦτο αὐτὴν κάλεον 3rd c.BC: Callimachus Epicus “Fragmenta” 66b; τούτοις τὸ ὄνομα ἱμάτια ἐκαλέσαμεν 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Politicus” 279e (_passive_, τύμβῳ δ᾽ ὄνομα σῷ κεκλήσεται]] shall be given to thy tomb, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Hecuba” 1271)]]; κ. ὄνομα ἐπί τινι give a name to something, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Parmenides” 147d]]; but call (a man) a name because of some function, [NT+2nd c.BC+ [[prev. author] “Sph.” 218c; κ. τινὰ ἐπὶ τῷ ὀνόματι τοῦ πατρός NT.Luke.1.59; ἐπ᾽ ὀνόματος καλεῖν τινα 2nd c.BC: Polybius Historicus 35.4.11]]:—passive, to be named or called, Μυρμιδόνες δὲ καλεῦντο [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 2.684; εἰ τόδ᾽ αὐτῷ φίλον κεκλημένῳ 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Agamemnon” 161 (Lyric poetry)]]; ὁ καλούμενος the socalled, ἐν τῇ Θεράπνῃ καλεομένῃ [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 6.61; ὁ κ. θάνατος 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Phaedo” 86d]]; οἱ τῶν ὁμοτίμων κ. [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 2.1.9]]; κεκλημένος τινός called from or after him, [LXX+5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “P.” 3.67; καλεῖσθαι ἐπί τινι LXX.Gen.48.6; κέκληνται δέ σφιν ἕδραι 5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “O.” 7.76.]]

__II.2
passive, to be called, almost ={εἰμί}, especially with words expressing kinship or status, ἐμὸς γαμβρὸς καλέεσθαι [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 7.313, compare 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Persae” 2 (_anapaest meter_); ἀφνειοὶ καλέονται 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 15.433]]; especially in perfect passive κέκλημαι, οὕνεκα σὴ παράκοιτις κέκλημαι because I am thy wife, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 4.61; φίλη κεκλήσῃ ἄκοιτις 3.138; αἲ γὰρ ἐμοὶ τοιόσδε πόσις κεκλημένος εἴη 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 6.244; ἠγάγετ᾽ ἐς μέγα δῶμα φίλην κεκλῆσθαι ἄκοιτιν 8th-7th c.BC: Hesiodus Epicus “Theogonia” 410; σὴ κεκλημένη.. ἦα “hymnus ad Apollinem” 324; μηδ᾽ ἔτι Τηλεμάχοιο πατὴρ κεκλημένος εἴην 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 2.260; οὔτινος δοῦλοι κέκληνται 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Persae” 242, compare 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Electra” 366, etc.]]

__II.3
special constructions, a. Ἀλησίου ἔνθα κολώνη κέκληται where is the hill called the hill of Alesios, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 11.758; ἵνα κριοῦ καλέονται εὐναί 3rd c.BC: Apollonius Rhodius Epicus 4.115; ἔνθα ἡ Τριπυργία καλεῖται 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Historia Graeca (Hellenica)” 5.1.10, etc.: -so in]]active, ἔνθα Ῥέας πόρον ἄνθρωποι καλέοισιν where is the ford men call the ford of Rhea, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “N.” 9.41, compare κικλήσκω, κλῄζω, κλέω.]]

__II.3.b
folld by a dependent clause, ἐκάλεσσέ νιν ἰσώνυμον ἔμμεν said that his name should be the same, [Refs [[prev. author] “O.” 9.63]]; καλεῖ με πλαστὸς ὡς εἴην πατρί, i.e. καλεῖ με πλαστόν [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Tyrannus” 780]]; καλοῦμέν γε παραδιδόντα μὲν διδάσκειν we say that one who delivers teaches, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Theaetetus” 198b, compare “Smp.” 205d; τὰς ἀμπέλους τραγᾶν καλοῦσιν 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Historia Animalium” 546a3.]]

deep_entry:
Abbott-Smith / STEPBible (TBESG)
καλλίων, -ον
compar. of καλός, see: καλῶς
καλῶς
adv. (καλός), [in LXX for parts and derivatives of יָטַב ;]
finely, rightly, well: Luk.6:48, 1Co.14:17, Gal.4:17 5:7, Jas.2:3; λέγειν, λαλεῖν, etc., Mat.15:7, Mrk.7:6 12:28, Luk.6:26 20:39, Jhn.4:17 8:48 13:13 18:23, Act.28:25; as exclamation of approval, Mrk.12:32, Rom.11:20; κ. ποιεῖν, Mat.12:12, 1Co.7:37-38 Jas.2:8, 19; with dative of person(s) (cl. accusative; WM, § 32, 1 β), Luk.6:27; with accusative of thing(s), Mrk.7:37; with ptcp., Act.10:33 (M, Pr., 131), Php.4:14, 2Pe.1:19, 3Jn.6; προϊστάναι (-ασθαι), 1Ti.3:4 3:12 5:17; διακονεῖν, 1Ti.3:13; ἀνατρέφεσθαι, Heb.13:18; ironically, Mrk.7:9, 2Co.11:4 (but see CGT, in l); κ. ἔχειν, to be well: Mrk.16:18. Compar., κάλλιον (for superl., B1., § 44, 3), very well: Act.25:10.†
(AS)

LSJ / STEPBible (TFLSJ)
καλός, ή, όν,
Aeolic dialect κάλος (see. below), α, ον, Boeotian dialect καλϝός [Refs 6th c.BC+ [“Schwyzer” 538 (6th c.BC)]]:—

__A
beautiful, of outward form, frequently of persons, κάλλιστος ἀνὴρ ὑπὸ Ἴλιον ἦλθεν [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 2.673: in 8th c.BC: Homerus Epicus]] usually in the phrase κ. τε μέγας τε [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 21.108, +others]]; μέγας καὶ κ. [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 9.513; καλή τε μεγάλη τε 13.289, 15.418]]; καλὸς δέμας beautiful of form,[Refs 5th c.BC+ [17.307; κ. ἰδέᾳ 5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “O.” 10 (11). 103; εἶδος κάλλιστος 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 1.2.1; κ. τὸ σῶμα [prev. author] “Mem.” 2.6.30; τὰς ὄψεις 4th c.BC: Theopompus Historicus 195]]; Χορῷ καλή beauteous in the dance, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 16.180]]: with infinitive, καλλίονες καὶ μείζονες εἰσοράασθαι [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 10.396]]; ἐσορᾶν κ. [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “O.” 8.19]]: frequently of parts of the body, fair, shapely, κ. πρόσωπα, ὅμματα, παρήϊα, σφυρά, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 19.285, 23.66, 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 19.208, 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 4.147; Χρώς 5.354, +others]]; of clothes, εἵματα, φάρεα, Χιτών, Χλαῖνα, πέδιλα, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 6.111, 24.277, 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 2.43, 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 10.365, 1.96; πέπλος κάλλιστος ποικίλμασιν ἠδὲ μέγιστος 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 6.294]]; of arms and armour, κνημῖδες, ἀσπίς, σάκος, κόρυς, φάσγανα, ἔντεα, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [3.331, 11.33, 22.314, 18.612, 15.713, 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 19.18]]; of buildings, manufactured articles, etc., αὐλὴ κ. τε μεγάλη τε [Refs [14.7]]; κ. δώματα, τεῖχος, πόλιες,[Refs 8th c.BC+ [3.387, 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 21.447, 18.491; ἄμαξα, τράπεζα, θρόνος, 24.267, 11.629, 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 1.131]]; also τέμενος, ἀγρός, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 12.314, 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 24.206; so after 8th c.BC: Homerus Epicus, Λύδιον κ. ἔργον 7th-6th c.BC: Sappho Lyrica 19, etc.]]; ἐέρσα κ. ead.[Refs [“Supp.” 25.12.]]

__A.2
in Attic dialect added to a name in token of love or admiration, as Ἀρίσημος κ. [Refs [“IG” 12.921, etc.]]; ἐν τοῖσι τοίχοις ἔγραφ᾽ Ἀθηναῖοι καλοί” [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Acharnenses” 144, compare “V.” 98]]; Ἀλκιβιάδης ὁ καλός, Σαπφὼ ἡ καλή, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus Alcaeus1.113b, “Phdr.” 235c.]]

__A.2.b
ἡ Καλή or Καλλίστη, as epithet, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Agamemnon” 140 (Lyric poetry), 2nd c.AD: Pausanias Periegeta 1.29.2, “CIG” “Corpus Inscriptionum Graecarum” “Corpus Inscriptionum Graecarum” 4445 (from Beroea).]]

__A.2.c
Καλοί, οἱ, divinities worshipped in childbirth, [Refs 2nd c.BC+ [“IG” 5(1).1445 (Messene, 2nd c.BC).]]

__A.3
τὸ καλόν beauty, [Refs 7th c.BC+ [7th-6th c.BC: Sappho Lyrica 79, 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Iphigenia Aulidensis” 21 (_anapaest meter_)]], etc.; τὰ καλά the proprieties or elegancies of life, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.8, 207; ἁπάντων καλῶν ἄμμορος 5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “O.” 1.84; αἱ τέχναι ἃς πηγάς φασι τῶν κ. εἶναι 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 7.2.13.]]

__A.II
with reference to use, good, of fine quality, κ. λιμήν [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 6.263]]; Βορέῃ ἀνέμῳ.. καλῷ fair, [Refs [14.253, 299]]; κ. ἀργύριον, opposed to κίβδηλον, genuine silver, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Memorabilia” 3.1.9]]; opposed to ἀποτετριμμένον, good silver currency, [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [“PCair.Zen.” 21.33 (3rd c.BC)]]; ἐλαῖαι [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [“PHib.” 1.49.12 (3rd c.BC)]]; γῆ [NT+4th c.AD+ [NT.Luke.8.15; κ. οἶνος “PFay.” 133.8 (4th c.AD)]]; στρατόπεδον κάλλιστον [LXX+5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 5.60; ἀνταπεδώκατε πονηρὰ ἀντὶ καλῶν LXX.Gen.44.4; κ. ἐς στρατιάν 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 3.3.6; πρός τι 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Hp.Ma.” 295c, “Grg.” 474d, etc.]]: with infinitive, λόφος κάλλιστος τρέχειν [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 4.8.26]]; ἐν καλῷ [τόπῳ] in a good place, καθίζεσθαι, ὁρμεῖν, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Thesmophoriazusae” 292, 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Historia Graeca (Hellenica)” 2.1.25; ἐν καλῷ μὲν τοῦ κόλπου καὶ τῶν πόλεων, ἐν κ. δὲ τοῦ τὴν Χώραν βλάπτειν, [prev. work] 6.2.9]]; ἐν καλῷ under favourable circumstances, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 5.59.60]]; ἐν κ. (i.e. Χρόνῳ) in good time, in season, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Iphigenia Aulidensis” 1106]]; ἐν οὐ κ. [Refs [[prev. author] “Or.” 579]]; ἐν καλῷ [ἐστι] with infinitive, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Electra” 384 (so καλόν ἐστι]] with infinitive, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. author] “Ph.” 1155 (Lyric poetry), 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Pax” 278, 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 8.2); ἐς καλόν 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Tyrannus” 78, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Meno” 89e, “Smp.” 174e]]; τί γὰρ ἐμοὶ ζῆν καλό; what is the good of life to me? [Refs 1st c.AD+ [1st c.AD: Philo Judaeus 2.594]]; καλῇ πίστει, = Latin bona fide, [Refs 3rd c.AD+ [PTeb. 418.14 (3rd c.AD).]]

__A.II.2
of sacrifices, auspicious, σφάγια [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Septem contra Thebas” 379; οἰωνοί 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Ion” 1333; ἱερά 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 4.92; τὸ τέλος κ. τῆς ἐξόδου 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 5.2.9; κ. τὰ ἱερὰ ἦν αὐτῷ [prev. author] “Cyr.” 3.2.3]]: with infinitive, ἰέναι.. κ. ἡμῖν τὰ ἱερὰ ἦν [Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. author] “An.” 2.2.3: Comedy texts, τὰ τῆς πυγῆς κ. (for τοῦ θεοῦ) 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Pax” 868.]]

__A.III
in a moral sense, beautiful, noble, honourable, in [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Homerus Epicus]] only in neuter, οὐ καλὸν ἔειπες [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 8.166, compare 17.381; μεῖζον κλέος.. καὶ κάλλιον 18.255]]; frequently καλόν [ἐστι] with infinitive, κ. τοι σὺν ἐμοὶ τὸν κήδειν ὅς κ᾽ ἐμὲ κήδῃ [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 9.615]]; οὐ γὰρ ἔμοιγε κ. (i.e. ἄρχειν)[Refs 8th c.BC+ [21.440; οὐ κ. ἀτέμβειν οὐδὲ δίκαιον 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 20.294]]; so in Trag., καλόν μοι τοῦτο ποιούσῃ θανεῖν [LXX+5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Antigone” 72, etc.; μάθετε καλὸν ποιεῖν LXX.Isa.1.17]]: comparative, οὐ μέν τοι τόδε κάλλιον οὐδὲ ἔοικε [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 7.159, compare 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 24.52; after 8th c.BC: Homerus Epicus frequently of actions, etc., κάλων κἄσλων 7th-6th c.BC: Sappho Lyrica “Papyrus fragments” in E. Diehl, 2.4 (unless of persons here)]]; κ. ἔργματα noble deeds, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “I.” 4(3).42, compare 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Fragmenta” 839, etc.]]; ἀναστροφὴ κ. [NT.1Pet.2.12]: in plural, excellences, πλῆθος καλῶν [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “O.” 13.45; πολλῶν καλῶν δεῖ τῷ καλόν τι μωμένῳ 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Fragmenta” 938]]; τὰ τοῦ παιδὸς κ. [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Symposium” 8.17.]]

__A.III.2
τὸ κ. moral beauty, virtue, honour, opposed to τὸ αἰσχρόν, [Refs 6th c.BC+ [[prev. author] “Mem.” 1.1.16, compare 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Symposium” 183d, etc.; ὅττι καλόν, φίλον ἐστί, τὸ δ᾽ οὐ καλὸν οὐ φίλον ἐστίν 6th c.BC: Theognis Elegiacus 17, compare 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Bacchae” 881 (Lyric poetry), 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Lysis” 216c; οὐ ταὐτὸν ἡγῇ σύ, ὡς ἔοικας, κ. τε καὶ ἀγαθὸν καὶ κακὸν καὶ αἰσχρόν [prev. author] “Grg.” 474d, compare “Smp.” 201e]]; τοὐμὸν κ. [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Supplices” 300.]]

__A.III.3
of persons, in early writers coupled with ἀγαθός, see at {καλοκἀγαθός}; later κ. ποιμήν [NT.John.10.11]; κ. στρατιώτης [NT.2Tim.2.3.]

__A.IV
in Attic dialect and Trag. frequently ironically, fine, specious, γέρας κ. [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Eumenides” 209; κ. γὰρ οὑμὸς βίοτος ὥστε θαυμάσαι 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Electra” 393, compare 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Bacchae” 652; κ. Χάρις 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 9.65; κ. ὕβριν ὑβρισμένοι [prev. author] 23.121; καί σοι.. θωπεῦσαι καλόν 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Coloneus” 1003; μετ᾽ ὀνομάτων καλῶν 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 5.89.]]

__B
Degrees of comparative: comparative καλλίων, ον, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 24.52, 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 10.396, etc.: _neuter_ κάλιον [ᾰ] 7th-6th c.BC: Alcaeus Lyricus 134]]: superlative κάλλιστος, η, ον, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 20.233, etc.]]; late καλλιώτερος or -ότερος, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [“POxy.” 1672.6 (1st c.AD), Scholia 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Troades” 966; also καλώτερος 2nd c.AD: Herodianus Grammaticus “Epim.” 69.]]

__C
adverb:—Poets frequently use neuter καλόν as adverb, κ. ἀείδειν [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 18.570, 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 1.155; καλά 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 6.326]]; later τὸ κ. [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [3rd c.BC: Theocritus Poeta Bucolicus 3.3, 18, 3rd c.BC: Callimachus Epicus “Epigrammata” 53, 3rd c.BC: Herodas Mimographus 1.54.]]

__C.II
regular adverb καλῶς (Doric dialect καλώς [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophron Comicus 22)]], well, rightly, οὐδ᾽ ἔτι κ. οἶκος ἐμὸς διόλωλε [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 2.64]]; κ. ζῆν, τεθνηκέναι, etc., [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Ajax” 479, etc.]]; κ. φρονεῖν to be in one's right mind, [Refs [[prev. author] “fragment” 836; οὐ κ. ταρβεῖς [prev. author] “Tr.” 457]]; κ. ἀγωνιεῖσθαι fairly, on the merits of the case, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Lysias Orator 13.88]]; Χρήματα δατῆθθαι κ. [Refs 5th c.BC+ [“Leg.Gort.” 4.39; κ. εἰρημένα 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Fragmenta” 576.6; κάλλιον λέγεις 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Theaetetus” 161b; κάλλιστ᾽ ἂν εἴποι 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Tyrannus” 1172: frequently in phrase καλῶς καὶ εὖ, καλῶς τε καὶ εὖ, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Protagoras” 319e, “Prm.” 128b, etc.]]

__C.II.2
of good fortune, well, happily, κ. πράσσειν, ={εὖ π}., [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Prometheus Vinctus” 979, 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Antigone” 271; κ. καὶ εὖ πράττειν 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Charmides” 172a]]; κ. ἔχειν to be well, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Septem contra Thebas” 799, etc.; κ. ἔχει σοι 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Acharnenses” 946, compare 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Electra” 816]]; κ. ἔχει with infinitive, 'tis well to.., [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Memorabilia” 3.11.1: with _genitive_, κ. ἔχειν τινός]] to be well off in respect to a thing, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Hippocrates Medicus “περὶ ἐπικυήσιος” 29; κ. παράπλου κεῖσθαι 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 1.36; εἰ κ. σφίσιν ἔχοι [prev. author] 4.117; οὔτε τοῖς θεοῖς ἔφη κ. ἔχειν, εἰ.. 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Memorabilia” 1.3.3; καλλιόνως ἔχει 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Theaetetus” 169e, etc.; κάλλιστα ἕζει [prev. author] “Hp.Ma.” 295b.]]

__C.II.3
καλῶς, ={πάνυ}, thoroughly, altogether, τὸν κ. εὐδαίμονα [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Fragmenta - American Journal of Philology” 317, = 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Fragmenta” 934; κ. ἔξοιδα [prev. author] “OC” 269, compare “OT” 1008; κ. ὑπὸ τοῦ πυρὸς διεφθάρθαι 1st c.BC: Diodorus Siculus Historicus 13.108]]: comparative, κάλλιον εἰδέναι [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Hp.Ma.” 300d]]; κάλλιον ἐοικέναι to be just like, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Hippocrates Medicus “Genit.” 8.]]

__C.II.4
κ. ἀκούειν to be well spoken of, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-3rd c.BC: Menander Comicus “Μονόστιχοι - Fragmenta Comicorum Graecorum” 285, 1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus 2.177e.]]

__C.II.5
κ. ποιῶν rightly, deservedly, κ. ποιῶν ἀπόλλυται [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Plutus” 863, compare 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 1.28, +others, 4th c.BC: Aeschines Orator 3.232]]; in requests, κ. ποιήσεις πριάμενος, etc., [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [“PPetr.” 3p.143 (3rd c.BC)]], etc.; also with infinitive, κ. π. γράψαι [Refs 1st c.BC+ [“BGU” 1203.7 (1st c.BC), etc.]]

__C.II.6
in answers, to approve the words of the former speaker, well said! [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Orestes” 1216, 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 39.15]]; also, to decline an offer courteously, no, thank you! [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Ranae” 888; κ. ἔχει 4th c.BC: Antiphanes Comicus 165, 4th-3rd c.BC: Menander Comicus “Περικειρομένη” 266]]; πάνυ κ. [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Ranae” 512; ἀμέλει κ. [prev. work] 532: _superlative_, κάλλιστ᾽, ἐπαινῶ [prev. work] 508; ἔχει κάλλιστα 3rd c.BC: Theocritus Poeta Bucolicus 15.3.]]

__C.II.7
ironically, finely, καλῶς ἐρήμης γ᾽ ἂν σὺ γῆς ἄρχοις μόνος [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Antigone” 739, compare 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Medea” 588, 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Equites” 344, 4th-3rd c.BC: Dinarchus Orator 1.69.]]

__C.II.8
κ. ὁ ἱερεύς hurrah for the priest! [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [“SIG” 1109.14 (Athens, 2nd c.AD).]]

__C.II.9
repeated with the adjective, καλὴ καλῶς [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Acharnenses” 253, “Pax” 1330, “Ec.” 730; καλὸς κάλλιστά τε ῥέξαις 5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “O.” 9.94.]]

__C.II.10
comparative καλλιόνως [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Tht.” [same place], “Lg.” 660d]]: superlative καλλίστως [Refs 5th c.BC+ [“PMag.Par.” 1.2443,2465, Scholia 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Hecuba” 310.]]

__D
for compounds, see at {καλλι-, καλο-}.

__E
Quantity: ᾱ in Epic dialect and early [Refs 8th c.BC+ [4th c.AD: Iamblichus Philosophus Poets (except “hymnus ad Venerem” 29, 8th-7th c.BC: Hesiodus Epicus “Opera et Dies” 63, “Th.” 585)]]: ᾰ in Lyric poetry (except κᾱλῶς [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Bacchylides Lyricus 12.206) and Trag. (4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Fragmenta - American Journal of Philology” 314, 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Philoctetes” 1381 are corrupt).--In Eleg., epigram, and Bucol. Poets ᾰ or ᾱ (the latter usually in thesi)]]; τὰ μὴ κᾰλὰ κᾱλὰ πέφανται [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [3rd c.BC: Theocritus Poeta Bucolicus 6.19, compare 3rd c.BC: Herodas Mimographus 7.115, 3rd c.BC: Callimachus Epicus “Hymnus in Jovem” 55]].--In comparative, ῐ in [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Homerus Epicus, ῑ in Trag. and later.]]

deep_entry:
Abbott-Smith / STEPBible (TBESG)
καλός, -ή, -όν,
[in LXX chiefly for טוֹבָה ,טוֹב, also for יָפֶה, etc. ;]
__1. primarily, of outward form ("related to . . . ἀγαθός as the appearance to the essence," Cremer, 339), fair, beautiful: λίθοι (BV, goodly), Luk.21:5.
__2. In reference to use, of that which is well adapted to its ends, good, excellent: of fish, τ. καλά (opposite to σαπρά), Mat.13:48; σπέρμα, Mat.13:24, 27, 37, 38; καρπός, Mat.3:10 7:17-19 12:33, Luk.3:9 [WH] 6:43; δένδρον (opposite to σαρπόν), Mat.12:33, Luk.6:43; γῆ, Mat.13:8, 23 Mrk.4:8, 20 Luk.8:15; τ. ἅλας, Mrk.9:50, Luk.14:34; ὁ νόμος, Rom.7:16, 1Ti.1:8; διδασκαλία, 1Ti.4:6;  καρδία κ. καὶ ἀγαθή, Luk.8:15; παραθήκη, 2Ti.1:14; μέτρον, Luk.6:38; βαθμός, 1Ti.3:13; θεμέλιος, 1Ti.6:19; τὸ κ., 1Th.5:21; μαργαρίται, Mat.13:45; οἶνος, Jhn.2:10; ποιμήν, Jhn.10:11, 14; διάκονος, 1Ti.4:6; οἰκονόμος, 1Pe.4:10; στρατιώτης, 2Ti.2:3; στρατεία, 1Ti.1:18; ἀγών, 1Ti.6:12, 2Ti.4:7; ὁμολογία, 1Ti.6:12, 13; ἔργον, Mat.26:10, Mrk.14:6, Jhn.10:33, 1Ti.3:1; pl., Jhn.10:32; καλόν, with inf. and dative, Mat.18:8, 9 1Co.7:1, 26 9:15; id. with accusative and inf., Mat.17:4, Mrk.9:5, 43, 45, 47, Luk.9:33, Heb.13:9; before εἰ, Mat.26:24, Mrk.9:42 14:21; ἐάν, 1Co.7:8.
__3. Ethically, good, in the sense of right, fair, noble, honourable: Gal.4:18, Heb.5:14; ἔργα, Mat.5:16, 1Ti.5:10, 25 6:18, Tit.2:7, 14 3:8, 14 (Field, Notes, 223f.), Heb.10:24, 1Pe.2:12; ἀναστροφή, Jas.3:13, 1Pe.2:12; συνείδησις, Heb.13:18; before ἐνώπιον, Rom.12:17, 2Co.8:21, 1Ti.2:3; το] κ. ποιεῖν (κατεργάζεσθαι), Rom.7:18, 21 2Co.13:7, Gal.6:9, Jas.4:17; καλόν ἐστιν, with inf., Mat.15:26 (T, ἔξεστιν), Mrk.7:27, Rom.14:21, Gal.4:18; μαρτυρία, 1Ti.3:7; ὄνομα, Jas.2:7; καύχημα, 1Co.5:6 (neg.); θεοῦ ῥῆμα, Heb.6:5. κ. does not occur in Re.†
SYN.: see: ἀγαθός. (AS)
