LSJ / STEPBible (TFLSJ)
καλός, ή, όν,
Aeolic dialect κάλος (see. below), α, ον, Boeotian dialect καλϝός [Refs 6th c.BC+ [“Schwyzer” 538 (6th c.BC)]]:—

__A
beautiful, of outward form, frequently of persons, κάλλιστος ἀνὴρ ὑπὸ Ἴλιον ἦλθεν [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 2.673: in 8th c.BC: Homerus Epicus]] usually in the phrase κ. τε μέγας τε [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 21.108, +others]]; μέγας καὶ κ. [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 9.513; καλή τε μεγάλη τε 13.289, 15.418]]; καλὸς δέμας beautiful of form,[Refs 5th c.BC+ [17.307; κ. ἰδέᾳ 5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “O.” 10 (11). 103; εἶδος κάλλιστος 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 1.2.1; κ. τὸ σῶμα [prev. author] “Mem.” 2.6.30; τὰς ὄψεις 4th c.BC: Theopompus Historicus 195]]; Χορῷ καλή beauteous in the dance, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 16.180]]: with infinitive, καλλίονες καὶ μείζονες εἰσοράασθαι [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 10.396]]; ἐσορᾶν κ. [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “O.” 8.19]]: frequently of parts of the body, fair, shapely, κ. πρόσωπα, ὅμματα, παρήϊα, σφυρά, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 19.285, 23.66, 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 19.208, 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 4.147; Χρώς 5.354, +others]]; of clothes, εἵματα, φάρεα, Χιτών, Χλαῖνα, πέδιλα, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 6.111, 24.277, 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 2.43, 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 10.365, 1.96; πέπλος κάλλιστος ποικίλμασιν ἠδὲ μέγιστος 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 6.294]]; of arms and armour, κνημῖδες, ἀσπίς, σάκος, κόρυς, φάσγανα, ἔντεα, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [3.331, 11.33, 22.314, 18.612, 15.713, 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 19.18]]; of buildings, manufactured articles, etc., αὐλὴ κ. τε μεγάλη τε [Refs [14.7]]; κ. δώματα, τεῖχος, πόλιες,[Refs 8th c.BC+ [3.387, 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 21.447, 18.491; ἄμαξα, τράπεζα, θρόνος, 24.267, 11.629, 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 1.131]]; also τέμενος, ἀγρός, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 12.314, 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 24.206; so after 8th c.BC: Homerus Epicus, Λύδιον κ. ἔργον 7th-6th c.BC: Sappho Lyrica 19, etc.]]; ἐέρσα κ. ead.[Refs [“Supp.” 25.12.]]

__A.2
in Attic dialect added to a name in token of love or admiration, as Ἀρίσημος κ. [Refs [“IG” 12.921, etc.]]; ἐν τοῖσι τοίχοις ἔγραφ᾽ Ἀθηναῖοι καλοί” [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Acharnenses” 144, compare “V.” 98]]; Ἀλκιβιάδης ὁ καλός, Σαπφὼ ἡ καλή, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus Alcaeus1.113b, “Phdr.” 235c.]]

__A.2.b
ἡ Καλή or Καλλίστη, as epithet, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Agamemnon” 140 (Lyric poetry), 2nd c.AD: Pausanias Periegeta 1.29.2, “CIG” “Corpus Inscriptionum Graecarum” “Corpus Inscriptionum Graecarum” 4445 (from Beroea).]]

__A.2.c
Καλοί, οἱ, divinities worshipped in childbirth, [Refs 2nd c.BC+ [“IG” 5(1).1445 (Messene, 2nd c.BC).]]

__A.3
τὸ καλόν beauty, [Refs 7th c.BC+ [7th-6th c.BC: Sappho Lyrica 79, 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Iphigenia Aulidensis” 21 (_anapaest meter_)]], etc.; τὰ καλά the proprieties or elegancies of life, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.8, 207; ἁπάντων καλῶν ἄμμορος 5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “O.” 1.84; αἱ τέχναι ἃς πηγάς φασι τῶν κ. εἶναι 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 7.2.13.]]

__A.II
with reference to use, good, of fine quality, κ. λιμήν [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 6.263]]; Βορέῃ ἀνέμῳ.. καλῷ fair, [Refs [14.253, 299]]; κ. ἀργύριον, opposed to κίβδηλον, genuine silver, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Memorabilia” 3.1.9]]; opposed to ἀποτετριμμένον, good silver currency, [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [“PCair.Zen.” 21.33 (3rd c.BC)]]; ἐλαῖαι [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [“PHib.” 1.49.12 (3rd c.BC)]]; γῆ [NT+4th c.AD+ [NT.Luke.8.15; κ. οἶνος “PFay.” 133.8 (4th c.AD)]]; στρατόπεδον κάλλιστον [LXX+5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 5.60; ἀνταπεδώκατε πονηρὰ ἀντὶ καλῶν LXX.Gen.44.4; κ. ἐς στρατιάν 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 3.3.6; πρός τι 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Hp.Ma.” 295c, “Grg.” 474d, etc.]]: with infinitive, λόφος κάλλιστος τρέχειν [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 4.8.26]]; ἐν καλῷ [τόπῳ] in a good place, καθίζεσθαι, ὁρμεῖν, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Thesmophoriazusae” 292, 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Historia Graeca (Hellenica)” 2.1.25; ἐν καλῷ μὲν τοῦ κόλπου καὶ τῶν πόλεων, ἐν κ. δὲ τοῦ τὴν Χώραν βλάπτειν, [prev. work] 6.2.9]]; ἐν καλῷ under favourable circumstances, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 5.59.60]]; ἐν κ. (i.e. Χρόνῳ) in good time, in season, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Iphigenia Aulidensis” 1106]]; ἐν οὐ κ. [Refs [[prev. author] “Or.” 579]]; ἐν καλῷ [ἐστι] with infinitive, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Electra” 384 (so καλόν ἐστι]] with infinitive, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. author] “Ph.” 1155 (Lyric poetry), 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Pax” 278, 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 8.2); ἐς καλόν 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Tyrannus” 78, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Meno” 89e, “Smp.” 174e]]; τί γὰρ ἐμοὶ ζῆν καλό; what is the good of life to me? [Refs 1st c.AD+ [1st c.AD: Philo Judaeus 2.594]]; καλῇ πίστει, = Latin bona fide, [Refs 3rd c.AD+ [PTeb. 418.14 (3rd c.AD).]]

__A.II.2
of sacrifices, auspicious, σφάγια [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Septem contra Thebas” 379; οἰωνοί 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Ion” 1333; ἱερά 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 4.92; τὸ τέλος κ. τῆς ἐξόδου 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 5.2.9; κ. τὰ ἱερὰ ἦν αὐτῷ [prev. author] “Cyr.” 3.2.3]]: with infinitive, ἰέναι.. κ. ἡμῖν τὰ ἱερὰ ἦν [Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. author] “An.” 2.2.3: Comedy texts, τὰ τῆς πυγῆς κ. (for τοῦ θεοῦ) 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Pax” 868.]]

__A.III
in a moral sense, beautiful, noble, honourable, in [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Homerus Epicus]] only in neuter, οὐ καλὸν ἔειπες [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 8.166, compare 17.381; μεῖζον κλέος.. καὶ κάλλιον 18.255]]; frequently καλόν [ἐστι] with infinitive, κ. τοι σὺν ἐμοὶ τὸν κήδειν ὅς κ᾽ ἐμὲ κήδῃ [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 9.615]]; οὐ γὰρ ἔμοιγε κ. (i.e. ἄρχειν)[Refs 8th c.BC+ [21.440; οὐ κ. ἀτέμβειν οὐδὲ δίκαιον 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 20.294]]; so in Trag., καλόν μοι τοῦτο ποιούσῃ θανεῖν [LXX+5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Antigone” 72, etc.; μάθετε καλὸν ποιεῖν LXX.Isa.1.17]]: comparative, οὐ μέν τοι τόδε κάλλιον οὐδὲ ἔοικε [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 7.159, compare 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 24.52; after 8th c.BC: Homerus Epicus frequently of actions, etc., κάλων κἄσλων 7th-6th c.BC: Sappho Lyrica “Papyrus fragments” in E. Diehl, 2.4 (unless of persons here)]]; κ. ἔργματα noble deeds, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “I.” 4(3).42, compare 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Fragmenta” 839, etc.]]; ἀναστροφὴ κ. [NT.1Pet.2.12]: in plural, excellences, πλῆθος καλῶν [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “O.” 13.45; πολλῶν καλῶν δεῖ τῷ καλόν τι μωμένῳ 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Fragmenta” 938]]; τὰ τοῦ παιδὸς κ. [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Symposium” 8.17.]]

__A.III.2
τὸ κ. moral beauty, virtue, honour, opposed to τὸ αἰσχρόν, [Refs 6th c.BC+ [[prev. author] “Mem.” 1.1.16, compare 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Symposium” 183d, etc.; ὅττι καλόν, φίλον ἐστί, τὸ δ᾽ οὐ καλὸν οὐ φίλον ἐστίν 6th c.BC: Theognis Elegiacus 17, compare 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Bacchae” 881 (Lyric poetry), 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Lysis” 216c; οὐ ταὐτὸν ἡγῇ σύ, ὡς ἔοικας, κ. τε καὶ ἀγαθὸν καὶ κακὸν καὶ αἰσχρόν [prev. author] “Grg.” 474d, compare “Smp.” 201e]]; τοὐμὸν κ. [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Supplices” 300.]]

__A.III.3
of persons, in early writers coupled with ἀγαθός, see at {καλοκἀγαθός}; later κ. ποιμήν [NT.John.10.11]; κ. στρατιώτης [NT.2Tim.2.3.]

__A.IV
in Attic dialect and Trag. frequently ironically, fine, specious, γέρας κ. [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Eumenides” 209; κ. γὰρ οὑμὸς βίοτος ὥστε θαυμάσαι 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Electra” 393, compare 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Bacchae” 652; κ. Χάρις 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 9.65; κ. ὕβριν ὑβρισμένοι [prev. author] 23.121; καί σοι.. θωπεῦσαι καλόν 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Coloneus” 1003; μετ᾽ ὀνομάτων καλῶν 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 5.89.]]

__B
Degrees of comparative: comparative καλλίων, ον, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 24.52, 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 10.396, etc.: _neuter_ κάλιον [ᾰ] 7th-6th c.BC: Alcaeus Lyricus 134]]: superlative κάλλιστος, η, ον, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 20.233, etc.]]; late καλλιώτερος or -ότερος, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [“POxy.” 1672.6 (1st c.AD), Scholia 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Troades” 966; also καλώτερος 2nd c.AD: Herodianus Grammaticus “Epim.” 69.]]

__C
adverb:—Poets frequently use neuter καλόν as adverb, κ. ἀείδειν [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 18.570, 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 1.155; καλά 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 6.326]]; later τὸ κ. [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [3rd c.BC: Theocritus Poeta Bucolicus 3.3, 18, 3rd c.BC: Callimachus Epicus “Epigrammata” 53, 3rd c.BC: Herodas Mimographus 1.54.]]

__C.II
regular adverb καλῶς (Doric dialect καλώς [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophron Comicus 22)]], well, rightly, οὐδ᾽ ἔτι κ. οἶκος ἐμὸς διόλωλε [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 2.64]]; κ. ζῆν, τεθνηκέναι, etc., [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Ajax” 479, etc.]]; κ. φρονεῖν to be in one's right mind, [Refs [[prev. author] “fragment” 836; οὐ κ. ταρβεῖς [prev. author] “Tr.” 457]]; κ. ἀγωνιεῖσθαι fairly, on the merits of the case, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Lysias Orator 13.88]]; Χρήματα δατῆθθαι κ. [Refs 5th c.BC+ [“Leg.Gort.” 4.39; κ. εἰρημένα 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Fragmenta” 576.6; κάλλιον λέγεις 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Theaetetus” 161b; κάλλιστ᾽ ἂν εἴποι 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Tyrannus” 1172: frequently in phrase καλῶς καὶ εὖ, καλῶς τε καὶ εὖ, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Protagoras” 319e, “Prm.” 128b, etc.]]

__C.II.2
of good fortune, well, happily, κ. πράσσειν, ={εὖ π}., [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Prometheus Vinctus” 979, 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Antigone” 271; κ. καὶ εὖ πράττειν 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Charmides” 172a]]; κ. ἔχειν to be well, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Septem contra Thebas” 799, etc.; κ. ἔχει σοι 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Acharnenses” 946, compare 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Electra” 816]]; κ. ἔχει with infinitive, 'tis well to.., [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Memorabilia” 3.11.1: with _genitive_, κ. ἔχειν τινός]] to be well off in respect to a thing, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Hippocrates Medicus “περὶ ἐπικυήσιος” 29; κ. παράπλου κεῖσθαι 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 1.36; εἰ κ. σφίσιν ἔχοι [prev. author] 4.117; οὔτε τοῖς θεοῖς ἔφη κ. ἔχειν, εἰ.. 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Memorabilia” 1.3.3; καλλιόνως ἔχει 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Theaetetus” 169e, etc.; κάλλιστα ἕζει [prev. author] “Hp.Ma.” 295b.]]

__C.II.3
καλῶς, ={πάνυ}, thoroughly, altogether, τὸν κ. εὐδαίμονα [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Fragmenta - American Journal of Philology” 317, = 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Fragmenta” 934; κ. ἔξοιδα [prev. author] “OC” 269, compare “OT” 1008; κ. ὑπὸ τοῦ πυρὸς διεφθάρθαι 1st c.BC: Diodorus Siculus Historicus 13.108]]: comparative, κάλλιον εἰδέναι [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Hp.Ma.” 300d]]; κάλλιον ἐοικέναι to be just like, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Hippocrates Medicus “Genit.” 8.]]

__C.II.4
κ. ἀκούειν to be well spoken of, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-3rd c.BC: Menander Comicus “Μονόστιχοι - Fragmenta Comicorum Graecorum” 285, 1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus 2.177e.]]

__C.II.5
κ. ποιῶν rightly, deservedly, κ. ποιῶν ἀπόλλυται [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Plutus” 863, compare 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 1.28, +others, 4th c.BC: Aeschines Orator 3.232]]; in requests, κ. ποιήσεις πριάμενος, etc., [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [“PPetr.” 3p.143 (3rd c.BC)]], etc.; also with infinitive, κ. π. γράψαι [Refs 1st c.BC+ [“BGU” 1203.7 (1st c.BC), etc.]]

__C.II.6
in answers, to approve the words of the former speaker, well said! [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Orestes” 1216, 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 39.15]]; also, to decline an offer courteously, no, thank you! [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Ranae” 888; κ. ἔχει 4th c.BC: Antiphanes Comicus 165, 4th-3rd c.BC: Menander Comicus “Περικειρομένη” 266]]; πάνυ κ. [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Ranae” 512; ἀμέλει κ. [prev. work] 532: _superlative_, κάλλιστ᾽, ἐπαινῶ [prev. work] 508; ἔχει κάλλιστα 3rd c.BC: Theocritus Poeta Bucolicus 15.3.]]

__C.II.7
ironically, finely, καλῶς ἐρήμης γ᾽ ἂν σὺ γῆς ἄρχοις μόνος [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Antigone” 739, compare 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Medea” 588, 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Equites” 344, 4th-3rd c.BC: Dinarchus Orator 1.69.]]

__C.II.8
κ. ὁ ἱερεύς hurrah for the priest! [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [“SIG” 1109.14 (Athens, 2nd c.AD).]]

__C.II.9
repeated with the adjective, καλὴ καλῶς [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Acharnenses” 253, “Pax” 1330, “Ec.” 730; καλὸς κάλλιστά τε ῥέξαις 5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “O.” 9.94.]]

__C.II.10
comparative καλλιόνως [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Tht.” [same place], “Lg.” 660d]]: superlative καλλίστως [Refs 5th c.BC+ [“PMag.Par.” 1.2443,2465, Scholia 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Hecuba” 310.]]

__D
for compounds, see at {καλλι-, καλο-}.

__E
Quantity: ᾱ in Epic dialect and early [Refs 8th c.BC+ [4th c.AD: Iamblichus Philosophus Poets (except “hymnus ad Venerem” 29, 8th-7th c.BC: Hesiodus Epicus “Opera et Dies” 63, “Th.” 585)]]: ᾰ in Lyric poetry (except κᾱλῶς [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Bacchylides Lyricus 12.206) and Trag. (4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Fragmenta - American Journal of Philology” 314, 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Philoctetes” 1381 are corrupt).--In Eleg., epigram, and Bucol. Poets ᾰ or ᾱ (the latter usually in thesi)]]; τὰ μὴ κᾰλὰ κᾱλὰ πέφανται [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [3rd c.BC: Theocritus Poeta Bucolicus 6.19, compare 3rd c.BC: Herodas Mimographus 7.115, 3rd c.BC: Callimachus Epicus “Hymnus in Jovem” 55]].--In comparative, ῐ in [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Homerus Epicus, ῑ in Trag. and later.]]

Aeolic dialect κάλος (see. below), α, ον, Boeotian dialect καλϝός [Refs 6th c.BC+ [“Schwyzer” 538 (6th c.BC)]]:—

__A
beautiful, of outward form, frequently of persons, κάλλιστος ἀνὴρ ὑπὸ Ἴλιον ἦλθεν [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 2.673: in 8th c.BC: Homerus Epicus]] usually in the phrase κ. τε μέγας τε [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 21.108, +others]]; μέγας καὶ κ. [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 9.513; καλή τε μεγάλη τε 13.289, 15.418]]; καλὸς δέμας beautiful of form,[Refs 5th c.BC+ [17.307; κ. ἰδέᾳ 5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “O.” 10 (11). 103; εἶδος κάλλιστος 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 1.2.1; κ. τὸ σῶμα [prev. author] “Mem.” 2.6.30; τὰς ὄψεις 4th c.BC: Theopompus Historicus 195]]; Χορῷ καλή beauteous in the dance, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 16.180]]: with infinitive, καλλίονες καὶ μείζονες εἰσοράασθαι [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 10.396]]; ἐσορᾶν κ. [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “O.” 8.19]]: frequently of parts of the body, fair, shapely, κ. πρόσωπα, ὅμματα, παρήϊα, σφυρά, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 19.285, 23.66, 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 19.208, 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 4.147; Χρώς 5.354, +others]]; of clothes, εἵματα, φάρεα, Χιτών, Χλαῖνα, πέδιλα, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 6.111, 24.277, 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 2.43, 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 10.365, 1.96; πέπλος κάλλιστος ποικίλμασιν ἠδὲ μέγιστος 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 6.294]]; of arms and armour, κνημῖδες, ἀσπίς, σάκος, κόρυς, φάσγανα, ἔντεα, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [3.331, 11.33, 22.314, 18.612, 15.713, 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 19.18]]; of buildings, manufactured articles, etc., αὐλὴ κ. τε μεγάλη τε [Refs [14.7]]; κ. δώματα, τεῖχος, πόλιες,[Refs 8th c.BC+ [3.387, 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 21.447, 18.491; ἄμαξα, τράπεζα, θρόνος, 24.267, 11.629, 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 1.131]]; also τέμενος, ἀγρός, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 12.314, 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 24.206; so after 8th c.BC: Homerus Epicus, Λύδιον κ. ἔργον 7th-6th c.BC: Sappho Lyrica 19, etc.]]; ἐέρσα κ. ead.[Refs [“Supp.” 25.12.]]

__A.2
in Attic dialect added to a name in token of love or admiration, as Ἀρίσημος κ. [Refs [“IG” 12.921, etc.]]; ἐν τοῖσι τοίχοις ἔγραφ᾽ Ἀθηναῖοι καλοί” [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Acharnenses” 144, compare “V.” 98]]; Ἀλκιβιάδης ὁ καλός, Σαπφὼ ἡ καλή, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus Alcaeus1.113b, “Phdr.” 235c.]]

__A.2.b
ἡ Καλή or Καλλίστη, as epithet, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Agamemnon” 140 (Lyric poetry), 2nd c.AD: Pausanias Periegeta 1.29.2, “CIG” “Corpus Inscriptionum Graecarum” “Corpus Inscriptionum Graecarum” 4445 (from Beroea).]]

__A.2.c
Καλοί, οἱ, divinities worshipped in childbirth, [Refs 2nd c.BC+ [“IG” 5(1).1445 (Messene, 2nd c.BC).]]

__A.3
τὸ καλόν beauty, [Refs 7th c.BC+ [7th-6th c.BC: Sappho Lyrica 79, 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Iphigenia Aulidensis” 21 (_anapaest meter_)]], etc.; τὰ καλά the proprieties or elegancies of life, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.8, 207; ἁπάντων καλῶν ἄμμορος 5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “O.” 1.84; αἱ τέχναι ἃς πηγάς φασι τῶν κ. εἶναι 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 7.2.13.]]

__A.II
with reference to use, good, of fine quality, κ. λιμήν [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 6.263]]; Βορέῃ ἀνέμῳ.. καλῷ fair, [Refs [14.253, 299]]; κ. ἀργύριον, opposed to κίβδηλον, genuine silver, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Memorabilia” 3.1.9]]; opposed to ἀποτετριμμένον, good silver currency, [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [“PCair.Zen.” 21.33 (3rd c.BC)]]; ἐλαῖαι [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [“PHib.” 1.49.12 (3rd c.BC)]]; γῆ [NT+4th c.AD+ [NT.Luke.8.15; κ. οἶνος “PFay.” 133.8 (4th c.AD)]]; στρατόπεδον κάλλιστον [LXX+5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 5.60; ἀνταπεδώκατε πονηρὰ ἀντὶ καλῶν LXX.Gen.44.4; κ. ἐς στρατιάν 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 3.3.6; πρός τι 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Hp.Ma.” 295c, “Grg.” 474d, etc.]]: with infinitive, λόφος κάλλιστος τρέχειν [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 4.8.26]]; ἐν καλῷ [τόπῳ] in a good place, καθίζεσθαι, ὁρμεῖν, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Thesmophoriazusae” 292, 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Historia Graeca (Hellenica)” 2.1.25; ἐν καλῷ μὲν τοῦ κόλπου καὶ τῶν πόλεων, ἐν κ. δὲ τοῦ τὴν Χώραν βλάπτειν, [prev. work] 6.2.9]]; ἐν καλῷ under favourable circumstances, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 5.59.60]]; ἐν κ. (i.e. Χρόνῳ) in good time, in season, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Iphigenia Aulidensis” 1106]]; ἐν οὐ κ. [Refs [[prev. author] “Or.” 579]]; ἐν καλῷ [ἐστι] with infinitive, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Electra” 384 (so καλόν ἐστι]] with infinitive, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. author] “Ph.” 1155 (Lyric poetry), 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Pax” 278, 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 8.2); ἐς καλόν 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Tyrannus” 78, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Meno” 89e, “Smp.” 174e]]; τί γὰρ ἐμοὶ ζῆν καλό; what is the good of life to me? [Refs 1st c.AD+ [1st c.AD: Philo Judaeus 2.594]]; καλῇ πίστει, = Latin bona fide, [Refs 3rd c.AD+ [PTeb. 418.14 (3rd c.AD).]]

__A.II.2
of sacrifices, auspicious, σφάγια [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Septem contra Thebas” 379; οἰωνοί 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Ion” 1333; ἱερά 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 4.92; τὸ τέλος κ. τῆς ἐξόδου 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 5.2.9; κ. τὰ ἱερὰ ἦν αὐτῷ [prev. author] “Cyr.” 3.2.3]]: with infinitive, ἰέναι.. κ. ἡμῖν τὰ ἱερὰ ἦν [Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. author] “An.” 2.2.3: Comedy texts, τὰ τῆς πυγῆς κ. (for τοῦ θεοῦ) 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Pax” 868.]]

__A.III
in a moral sense, beautiful, noble, honourable, in [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Homerus Epicus]] only in neuter, οὐ καλὸν ἔειπες [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 8.166, compare 17.381; μεῖζον κλέος.. καὶ κάλλιον 18.255]]; frequently καλόν [ἐστι] with infinitive, κ. τοι σὺν ἐμοὶ τὸν κήδειν ὅς κ᾽ ἐμὲ κήδῃ [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 9.615]]; οὐ γὰρ ἔμοιγε κ. (i.e. ἄρχειν)[Refs 8th c.BC+ [21.440; οὐ κ. ἀτέμβειν οὐδὲ δίκαιον 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 20.294]]; so in Trag., καλόν μοι τοῦτο ποιούσῃ θανεῖν [LXX+5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Antigone” 72, etc.; μάθετε καλὸν ποιεῖν LXX.Isa.1.17]]: comparative, οὐ μέν τοι τόδε κάλλιον οὐδὲ ἔοικε [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 7.159, compare 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 24.52; after 8th c.BC: Homerus Epicus frequently of actions, etc., κάλων κἄσλων 7th-6th c.BC: Sappho Lyrica “Papyrus fragments” in E. Diehl, 2.4 (unless of persons here)]]; κ. ἔργματα noble deeds, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “I.” 4(3).42, compare 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Fragmenta” 839, etc.]]; ἀναστροφὴ κ. [NT.1Pet.2.12]: in plural, excellences, πλῆθος καλῶν [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “O.” 13.45; πολλῶν καλῶν δεῖ τῷ καλόν τι μωμένῳ 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Fragmenta” 938]]; τὰ τοῦ παιδὸς κ. [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Symposium” 8.17.]]

__A.III.2
τὸ κ. moral beauty, virtue, honour, opposed to τὸ αἰσχρόν, [Refs 6th c.BC+ [[prev. author] “Mem.” 1.1.16, compare 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Symposium” 183d, etc.; ὅττι καλόν, φίλον ἐστί, τὸ δ᾽ οὐ καλὸν οὐ φίλον ἐστίν 6th c.BC: Theognis Elegiacus 17, compare 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Bacchae” 881 (Lyric poetry), 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Lysis” 216c; οὐ ταὐτὸν ἡγῇ σύ, ὡς ἔοικας, κ. τε καὶ ἀγαθὸν καὶ κακὸν καὶ αἰσχρόν [prev. author] “Grg.” 474d, compare “Smp.” 201e]]; τοὐμὸν κ. [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Supplices” 300.]]

__A.III.3
of persons, in early writers coupled with ἀγαθός, see at {καλοκἀγαθός}; later κ. ποιμήν [NT.John.10.11]; κ. στρατιώτης [NT.2Tim.2.3.]

__A.IV
in Attic dialect and Trag. frequently ironically, fine, specious, γέρας κ. [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Eumenides” 209; κ. γὰρ οὑμὸς βίοτος ὥστε θαυμάσαι 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Electra” 393, compare 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Bacchae” 652; κ. Χάρις 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 9.65; κ. ὕβριν ὑβρισμένοι [prev. author] 23.121; καί σοι.. θωπεῦσαι καλόν 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Coloneus” 1003; μετ᾽ ὀνομάτων καλῶν 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 5.89.]]

__B
Degrees of comparative: comparative καλλίων, ον, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 24.52, 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 10.396, etc.: _neuter_ κάλιον [ᾰ] 7th-6th c.BC: Alcaeus Lyricus 134]]: superlative κάλλιστος, η, ον, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 20.233, etc.]]; late καλλιώτερος or -ότερος, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [“POxy.” 1672.6 (1st c.AD), Scholia 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Troades” 966; also καλώτερος 2nd c.AD: Herodianus Grammaticus “Epim.” 69.]]

__C
adverb:—Poets frequently use neuter καλόν as adverb, κ. ἀείδειν [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 18.570, 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 1.155; καλά 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 6.326]]; later τὸ κ. [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [3rd c.BC: Theocritus Poeta Bucolicus 3.3, 18, 3rd c.BC: Callimachus Epicus “Epigrammata” 53, 3rd c.BC: Herodas Mimographus 1.54.]]

__C.II
regular adverb καλῶς (Doric dialect καλώς [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophron Comicus 22)]], well, rightly, οὐδ᾽ ἔτι κ. οἶκος ἐμὸς διόλωλε [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 2.64]]; κ. ζῆν, τεθνηκέναι, etc., [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Ajax” 479, etc.]]; κ. φρονεῖν to be in one's right mind, [Refs [[prev. author] “fragment” 836; οὐ κ. ταρβεῖς [prev. author] “Tr.” 457]]; κ. ἀγωνιεῖσθαι fairly, on the merits of the case, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Lysias Orator 13.88]]; Χρήματα δατῆθθαι κ. [Refs 5th c.BC+ [“Leg.Gort.” 4.39; κ. εἰρημένα 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Fragmenta” 576.6; κάλλιον λέγεις 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Theaetetus” 161b; κάλλιστ᾽ ἂν εἴποι 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Tyrannus” 1172: frequently in phrase καλῶς καὶ εὖ, καλῶς τε καὶ εὖ, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Protagoras” 319e, “Prm.” 128b, etc.]]

__C.II.2
of good fortune, well, happily, κ. πράσσειν, ={εὖ π}., [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Prometheus Vinctus” 979, 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Antigone” 271; κ. καὶ εὖ πράττειν 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Charmides” 172a]]; κ. ἔχειν to be well, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Septem contra Thebas” 799, etc.; κ. ἔχει σοι 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Acharnenses” 946, compare 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Electra” 816]]; κ. ἔχει with infinitive, 'tis well to.., [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Memorabilia” 3.11.1: with _genitive_, κ. ἔχειν τινός]] to be well off in respect to a thing, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Hippocrates Medicus “περὶ ἐπικυήσιος” 29; κ. παράπλου κεῖσθαι 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 1.36; εἰ κ. σφίσιν ἔχοι [prev. author] 4.117; οὔτε τοῖς θεοῖς ἔφη κ. ἔχειν, εἰ.. 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Memorabilia” 1.3.3; καλλιόνως ἔχει 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Theaetetus” 169e, etc.; κάλλιστα ἕζει [prev. author] “Hp.Ma.” 295b.]]

__C.II.3
καλῶς, ={πάνυ}, thoroughly, altogether, τὸν κ. εὐδαίμονα [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Fragmenta - American Journal of Philology” 317, = 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Fragmenta” 934; κ. ἔξοιδα [prev. author] “OC” 269, compare “OT” 1008; κ. ὑπὸ τοῦ πυρὸς διεφθάρθαι 1st c.BC: Diodorus Siculus Historicus 13.108]]: comparative, κάλλιον εἰδέναι [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Hp.Ma.” 300d]]; κάλλιον ἐοικέναι to be just like, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Hippocrates Medicus “Genit.” 8.]]

__C.II.4
κ. ἀκούειν to be well spoken of, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-3rd c.BC: Menander Comicus “Μονόστιχοι - Fragmenta Comicorum Graecorum” 285, 1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus 2.177e.]]

__C.II.5
κ. ποιῶν rightly, deservedly, κ. ποιῶν ἀπόλλυται [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Plutus” 863, compare 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 1.28, +others, 4th c.BC: Aeschines Orator 3.232]]; in requests, κ. ποιήσεις πριάμενος, etc., [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [“PPetr.” 3p.143 (3rd c.BC)]], etc.; also with infinitive, κ. π. γράψαι [Refs 1st c.BC+ [“BGU” 1203.7 (1st c.BC), etc.]]

__C.II.6
in answers, to approve the words of the former speaker, well said! [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Orestes” 1216, 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 39.15]]; also, to decline an offer courteously, no, thank you! [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Ranae” 888; κ. ἔχει 4th c.BC: Antiphanes Comicus 165, 4th-3rd c.BC: Menander Comicus “Περικειρομένη” 266]]; πάνυ κ. [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Ranae” 512; ἀμέλει κ. [prev. work] 532: _superlative_, κάλλιστ᾽, ἐπαινῶ [prev. work] 508; ἔχει κάλλιστα 3rd c.BC: Theocritus Poeta Bucolicus 15.3.]]

__C.II.7
ironically, finely, καλῶς ἐρήμης γ᾽ ἂν σὺ γῆς ἄρχοις μόνος [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Antigone” 739, compare 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Medea” 588, 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Equites” 344, 4th-3rd c.BC: Dinarchus Orator 1.69.]]

__C.II.8
κ. ὁ ἱερεύς hurrah for the priest! [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [“SIG” 1109.14 (Athens, 2nd c.AD).]]

__C.II.9
repeated with the adjective, καλὴ καλῶς [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Acharnenses” 253, “Pax” 1330, “Ec.” 730; καλὸς κάλλιστά τε ῥέξαις 5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “O.” 9.94.]]

__C.II.10
comparative καλλιόνως [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Tht.” [same place], “Lg.” 660d]]: superlative καλλίστως [Refs 5th c.BC+ [“PMag.Par.” 1.2443,2465, Scholia 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Hecuba” 310.]]

__D
for compounds, see at {καλλι-, καλο-}.

__E
Quantity: ᾱ in Epic dialect and early [Refs 8th c.BC+ [4th c.AD: Iamblichus Philosophus Poets (except “hymnus ad Venerem” 29, 8th-7th c.BC: Hesiodus Epicus “Opera et Dies” 63, “Th.” 585)]]: ᾰ in Lyric poetry (except κᾱλῶς [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Bacchylides Lyricus 12.206) and Trag. (4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Fragmenta - American Journal of Philology” 314, 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Philoctetes” 1381 are corrupt).--In Eleg., epigram, and Bucol. Poets ᾰ or ᾱ (the latter usually in thesi)]]; τὰ μὴ κᾰλὰ κᾱλὰ πέφανται [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [3rd c.BC: Theocritus Poeta Bucolicus 6.19, compare 3rd c.BC: Herodas Mimographus 7.115, 3rd c.BC: Callimachus Epicus “Hymnus in Jovem” 55]].--In comparative, ῐ in [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Homerus Epicus, ῑ in Trag. and later.]]

LSJ / STEPBible (TFLSJ)
κάμνω,
future κᾰμοῦμαι, καμῇ, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Eumenides” 881, 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Trachiniae” 1215]]; καμεῖται [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 2.389, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Leges” 921e]]; Epic dialect infinitive -έεσθαι[Refs 3rd c.BC+ [3rd c.BC: Apollonius Rhodius Epicus 3.580:]]aorist 2 ἔκᾰμον, Epic dialect κάμον [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 4.187, +others]]; infinitive καμεῖν, Epic dialect subjunctive reduplicate κεκάμω, κεκάμῃσι, κεκάμωσιν, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 1.168, 17.658, 7.5 (but 3rd-2nd c.BC: Aristarchus Grammaticus read κε κάμω, etc., probably rightly)]]: perfect κέκμηκα [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 6.262, etc.]]: pluperfect ἐκεκμήκεσαν [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 3.98]]; Epic dialect participle κεκμηώς, κεκμηῶτι, κεκμηῶτα, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 23.232, 6.261, 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 10.31; κεκμηότας 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 11.802]]; κεκμηῶτας is variant for{κεκμηκότας} in [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 3.59]]:— middle, aorist 2 ἐκᾰμόμην [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 9.130]], Epic dialect καμ- [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 18.341.]]

__I
transitive, work, μίτρη, τὴν Χαλκῆες κάμον ἄνδρες wrought it, [Refs [4.187, 216]]; ἐπεὶ πάνθ᾽ ὅπλα κάμε [Refs 8th c.BC+ [18.614; σκῆπτρον.., τὸ μὲν Ἥφαιστος κάμε τεύχων 2.101, compare 8.195; κ. νῆας 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 9.126; πέπλον 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 5.338, compare 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 15.105; ἵππον 11.523; λέχος 23.189]]; ἄστυ build, [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [3rd c.BC: Apollonius Rhodius Epicus 1.1322]]: also in aorist middle, ἱρόν [Refs [[prev. author] 2.718.]]

__I.2
aorist middle, win by toil, τὰς (i.e. γυναῖκας) αὐτοὶ καμόμεσθα βίηφί τε δουρί τε μακρῷ [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 18.341.]]

__I.3
aorist middle, labour, till, οἵ κέ σφιν καὶ νῆσον.. ἐκάμοντο [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 9.130; οἴκους 4th-3rd c.BC: Philetas 8.]]

__II
intransitive, toil, labour, τινι for one, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 14.65; ὑπὲρ τῆς πόλεως 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 2.41]]: then, from the effect of continued work, to be weary, ἀνδρὶ δὲ κεκμηῶτι μένος μέγα οἶνος ἀέξει [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 6.261, compare 11.802: with _accusative_ of the part, οὐδέ τι γυῖα.. κάμνει]] nor is he weary in limb, [Refs [19.170]], etc.; περὶ δ᾽ ἔγχεϊ Χεῖρα καμεῖται [Refs [2.389; ὁ δ᾽ ἀριστερὸν ὦμον ἔκαμνεν 16.106: frequently with]]participle, κ. πολεμίζων, ἐλαύνοντες, ἐρεθίζων, is weary of fighting, rowing, etc., [Refs [1.168, 7.5, 17.658]], etc.; οὐ μέν θην κάμετον.. ὀλλῦσαι Τρῶας [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8.448; ἔκαμον δέ μοι ὄσσε πάντῃ παπταίνοντι 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 12.232]]; but οὐδέ τι τόξον δὴν ἔκαμον τανύων I did not long strain over stringing the bow, i.e. did it without effort,[Refs 8th c.BC+ [21.426, compare 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 8.22: later frequently with _negative_, οὔτοι καμοῦμαι.. λέγουσα]] I shall never be tired of saying, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Eumenides” 881; μὴ κάμῃς λέγων 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Iphigenia Aulidensis” 1143; οὐκ ἂν κάμοιμι τὰς κακὰς κτείνων [prev. author] “Or.” 1590; οὔποτε κάμοιμ᾽ ἂν ὀρχουμένη 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Lysistrata” 541 (Lyric poetry)]]; κ. εὐεργετῶν, ἐπαινῶν, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Gorgias” 470c, “Lg.” 921e: with _dative_, κ. δαπάναις]] to grow tired in spending, spare expense, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “P.” 1.90.]]

__II.2
to be hard-pressed, worsted, in battle or contest, [Refs [[prev. work] 1.78, 80]]; τὸ κάμνον στρατοῦ [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Supplices” 709.]]

__II.3
to be sick or suffering, τί πάσχει; τί κάμνει; [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Nubes” 708]]; οἱ κάμνοντες the sick, [NT+5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.197, compare 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Philoctetes” 282, 5th-6th c.BC: Andocides Orator 1.64, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 407c, NT.Jam.5.15, etc.]]; of a doctor's patients, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Hippocrates Medicus “περὶ διαίτης ὀξέων” 1, 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 18.243, “SIG” 943.10 (from Cos)]]; καμοῦσα ἀπέθανε having fallen sick, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Andocides Orator 1.120: with _accusative_ _cognate_, κάμνειν νόσον 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Heraclidae” 990, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 408e]]; [τὴν ποδάγραν] variant in [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Historia Animalium” 604a23; τοὺς ὀφθαλμούς 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 2.111]]; τὰ σώματα to be ill or distempered in body, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Gorgias” 478a; ὠσίν τε κὤμμασιν 3rd c.BC: Herodas Mimographus 3.32; πάθᾳ 5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “P.” 8.48; νοσήμασι 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Historia Animalium” 603a30; ἀπὸ τοῦ τραύματος 2nd c.AD: Lucianus Sophista “Tox.” 60; ὑπὸ νόσου 2nd c.AD: Herodianus Grammaticus 3.14.2.]]

__II.4
generally, to be distressed, meet with disaster, στρατοῦ καμόντος [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Agamemnon” 670; τῷ πεποιημένῳ κ. μεγάλως 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.118, compare 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Agamemnon” 482 (Lyric poetry), 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Medea” 1138, “HF” 293]]; οὐ καμῇ τοὐμὸν μέρος wilt not have to complain.., [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Trachiniae” 1215; κ. ἔν τινι 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Hecuba” 306, “IA” 966]]; of a ship, νεὼς καμούσης ποντίῳ πρὸς κύματι [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Septem contra Thebas” 210: with _accusative_ _cognate_, οὐκ ἴσον καμὼν ἐμοὶ λύπης]] not having borne an equal share of grief, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Electra” 532.]]

__II.5
in aorist participle, of the dead, i. e. either outworn, or those whose work is done, or those who have met with disaster, οἳ ὑπένερθε καμόντας ἀνθρώπους τίνυσθον [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 3.278, compare 3rd c.BC: Theocritus Poeta Bucolicus 17.49; βροτῶν εἴδωλα καμόντων 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 11.476]]; εἴδωλα κ[Refs 8th c.BC+ [. 24.14, 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 23.72, compare 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Supplices” 231, etc.]]: also in perfect participle in Trag. and Prose, κεκμηκότες [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Fragmenta” 284, 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Supplices” 756, 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 3.59, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Leges” 718a, 927b, 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Ethica Nicomachea” 1101a35]]; ἱερὰ τῶν κ. [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Troades” 96]]; also in the finite Verb, ὅπη ἄνθρωπος ἔκαμε [Refs [“Berl.Sitzb.” 1927.158 (from Cyrene)]].--The perfect is always intransitive (Cf. Sanskrit śamnīte 'work hard', 'serve zealously', śamitár- 'sacrificing priest', Gr. εἰρο-κόμος, κομέω, κομίζω.)

κάμπτω
[in LXX chiefly for כָּרַע, 4Ki.1:13, 2Ch.29:29, Isa.45:24 (23), al. ;]
to bend, bow: with accusative of thing(s), γόνυ, τὰ γ.; with dative of person(s), τῇ Βάαλ, Rom.11:4 (LXX); πρὸς τ. πατέρα, Eph.3:14; by meton., πᾶν γόνυ for πᾶς, Rom.14:11 (LXX) Php.2:10 (cf. ἀνα-, συν-κάμπτω).†
(AS)

---

LSJ / STEPBible (TFLSJ)
κάμπτω,
future κάμψω [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 7.118, 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Coloneus” 91]]: aorist 1 ἔκαμψα [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 5.453, 5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “P.” 2.51, etc.]]:—passive, future καμφθήσομαι [Refs 1st c.AD+ [1st-2nd c.AD: Dio Chrysostomus Sophista 77.33, 2nd c.AD: Galenus Medicus “de Usu Partium” 2.15]]: aorist ἐκάμφθην [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Prometheus Vinctus” 513, 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 3.58]]: perfect infinitive κεκάμφθαι [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Hippocrates Medicus “περὶ ἄρθρων ἐμβολῆς” 67]], participle κεκαμμένος [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Metaphysica” 1016a12, (ἐπι-, συγ-) 5th c.BC: Hippocrates Medicus “προγνωστικόν” 3, 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “de Equitandi ratione” 7.2]]. (Cogn. with Lithuanian ka[mtilde]p-as 'corner', ku[mtilde]p-as 'curved', and probably Latin campus):—bend, curve, ὄφρα ἴτυν κάμψῃ that he may bend it into a chariot-rail, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 4.486 (so _metaphorically_, κ. νέας ἁψῖδας ἐπῶν 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Thesmophoriazusae” 53): frequently in phrase, γόνυ κ]]. bend the knee so as to sit down and rest, φημί μιν ἀσπασίως γόνυ κάμψειν [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 7.118, compare 19.72; ὁ δ᾽ ἄρ᾽ ἄμφω γούνατ᾽ ἔκαμψε Χεῖράς τε στιβαράς 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 5.453]]; οὐ κάμπτων γόνυ, i.e. never resting, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Prometheus Vinctus” 32]]; ἄσμενός τἂν.. κάμψειεν γόνυ[Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. work] 398; ἵζω.. κάμψας γόνυ 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Hecuba” 1150; so κ. κῶλα 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Coloneus” 19]]; then κάμπτειν alone, sit down, rest,[Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. work] 85, 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Hecuba” 1080 (Lyric poetry)]]; also γόνυ κ. bend the knee in worship, [LXX.Isa.45.23, etc.]:—passive, bend oneself, opposed to ἐκτείνεσθαι, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Timaeus” 74b; ὥσπερ ξύλον καμπτόμενον εὐθύνουσιν [prev. author] “Prt.” 325d]]; ἡ κεκαμμένη (i.e. γραμμή) a bent line, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Metaphorical” [prev. cited]]]

__II
turn or guide a horse or chariot round the turning-post [Refs [compare (καμπτήρ 11), κάμψαι διαύλου θάτερον κῶλον πάλιν]] to double the post and return along the second half of the δίαυλος, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Agamemnon” 344; κ. δρόμον 5th c.BC: Bacchylides Lyricus 9.26]]; κάμπτοντος ἵππου as the horse was turning, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Electra” 744; κ. περὶ νύσσαν 3rd c.BC: Theocritus Poeta Bucolicus 24.120: _metaphorically_, κ. βίον]] to make the last turn in the course of life, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Coloneus” 91; κ. βίου τέλος 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Hippolytus” 87, “El.” 956; ὅταν κάμψῃς καὶ τελευτήσῃς βίον [prev. author] “Hel.” 1666]]; ἑξηκοστὸν ἥλιον κ. [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [3rd c.BC: Herodas Mimographus 10.1]]; διὰ λόγου κάμψαι κακά to end evils by reasoning, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Supplices” 748.]]

__II.2
of seamen, double a headland, Ἡρακλέας στήλας [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 4.42]]; τὸ ἀκρωτήριον, τὴν ἄκρην, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [[prev. author] 4.43, 7.122; ὡς δὲ τὴν ἄκραν κάμπτοντας ἡμᾶς εἶδον 4th-3rd c.BC: Menander Comicus 15, compare 4th c.BC: Aeschrio Lyricus 8.3]]; Μαλέαν κ. poetical cited in [Refs 5th c.BC+ [1st c.BC-1st c.AD: Strabo Geographus 8.6.20, 1st c.BC: Diodorus Siculus Historicus 13.64, etc.; κ. περὶ ἄκραν 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Acharnenses” 96]]; κ. κόλπον wind round the bay, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 7.58.]]

__II.3
absolutely, πάλιν κ. turn back, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Bacchae” 1225, “Rh.” 234 (Lyric poetry)]]; ἐγγὺς τῶν ἐμῶν κάμπτεις φρενῶν (κάμπτῃ codices) thou comest near my meaning, [Refs [[prev. author] “IT” 815.]]

__III
in Music, κάμπτων με καὶ στρέφων ὅλην διέφθορεν (i.e. Phrynis) with his turns and twists, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Pherecrates Comicus 145.15; κ. καμπήν 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Nubes” 969; κ. ᾠδάς 2nd-3rd c.AD: Philostratus Sophista “Vita Apollonii” 4.39.]]

__IV
metaphorically, κάμπτειν τινά bow down, humble, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “P.” 2.51; ὁ Χρόνος μ᾽ ἔκαμψε 4th c.BC: Crates Thebanus Poeta Philosophus 17]]:—passive, to be bent or bowed down, πημοναῖσι [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Prometheus Vinctus” 239, 308, compare 513]]; κάμπτομαι I submit, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Protagoras” 320b, etc.; κάμπτεσθαι καὶ ἕλκεσθαι πρὸς φιλοσοφίαν [prev. author] “R.” 494e]]; πολλὰ κάμπτονται καὶ συγκλῶνται are warped, [Refs [[prev. author] “Tht.” 173b]]: absolutely, to be moved to pity, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 3.58 (in full κ. εἰς ἔλεον 4th c.AD: Libanius Sophista “Orationes” 59.85).]]

Abbott-Smith / STEPBible (TBESG)
κἄν
by crasis for καὶ ἄν (= ἐάν; WH, App., 145b; Thayer, see word), with subjunc.,
__1. and if: Mrk.16:18 Luk.12:38, Jhn.8:55, 1Co.13:2-3, Jas.5:15; with ellips., Luk.13:9.
__2. Concessive, even if: Mat.21:21 26:35, Jhn.8:14 10:38 11:25, Heb.12:20.
__3. As intensive of simple καί (M, Pr., 167; WM, 730; Jannaris, Gr., 598), even, at least: Mrk.5:28 6:56, Act.5:15, 2Co.11:16.†
(AS)

---

LSJ / STEPBible (TFLSJ)
κἄν
(not κᾄν), by crasis,

__I
for καὶ ἄν.., variant in [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th-7th c.BC: Hesiodus Epicus “Opera et Dies” 357, frequently in _Attic dialect_: not often when καί]] is simply copulative, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Phaedo” 79a, “Grg.” 514d]]; but frequently when καί is intensive, ὅ γε κ. μέγα δοίη even a great thing, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th-7th c.BC: Hesiodus Epicus [same place]; κακὸν δὲ κ. ἐν ἡμέρᾳ γνοίης μιᾷ 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Tyrannus” 615, compare 591, “Aj.” 45, 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Nubes” 1130, 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 7.61, etc.]]; sometimes repeated after or before a Verb with ἄν, ἐπεὶ κ. σὺ.., εἴ τίς σε διδάξειεν.., βελτίων ἂν γένοιο [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Protagoras” 318b, compare “R.” 515e]]; frequently in the phrase κ. εἰ, where καί properly belongs to εἰ, even if, and ἄν to the Verb that follows in apodosi, νῦν δέ μοι δοκεῖ, κ. ἀσέβειαν εἰ καταγιγνώσκοι, τὰ προσήκοντα ποιεῖν (for καὶ εἰ καταγιγνώσκοι, ποιεῖν ἄν) [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 21.51: hence,]]

__I.2
even when the Verb in apodosi was of a tense that could not be joined with ἄν, κ. εἰ πολλαὶ [αἱ ἀρεταί].. εἰσιν, ἕν γέ τι εἶδος ταὐτὸν ἅπασαι ἔχουσι [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Meno” 72c; κ. εἰ μή τῳ δοκεῖ [prev. author] “R.” 473a, 579d, compare 408b, “Phd.” 71b, “Sph.” 247e, 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Topica” 136a31, +others]]

__I.3

deep_entry:
Abbott-Smith / STEPBible (TBESG)
κατά (bef. a vowel κατ᾽, καθ᾽; on the frequently neglect of elision, see Tdf., Pr., 95; WH, App., 146a),
prep. with genitive, accusative,
down, downwards.
__I. C. genitive (WM, §47, k; Bl., §42, 2).
__1. C. genitive of thing(s), in local sense;
__(a) down, down from: Mat.8:32, Mrk.5:13, Luk.8:33, 1Co.11:4;
__(b) throughout (late usage; Bl, l.with): κ. ὅλης κ.τ.λ., Luk.4:14  23:5, Act.9:31  10:37;
__(with) in a peculiar adjectival phrase: ἡ κ. βάθους, deep or extreme poverty, 2Co.8:2.
__     __2. C. genitive of person(s), usually in hostile sense;
__(a) against (in cl. only after verbs of speaking, witnessing, etc.): opposite to ὑπέρ, Mrk.9:40; μετά, Mat.12:30; after ἐπιθυμεῖν, Gal.5:17; λαλεῖν, Act.6:13; διδάσκειν, Act.21:28; ψεύδεσθαι, Jas.3:14; after verbs of accusing, etc., Mat.5:23, Luk.23:14, Rom.8:33, al.; verbs of fighting, prevailing, etc., Mat.10:35, Act.14:2, 1Co.4:6, al.;
__(b) of swearing, by: όμνυμι κ. (BL, §34, 1), He  6:13,16, cf. Mat.26:63.
__II. C. accusative (WM, §49d; BL, §42, 2).
__1. Of motion or direction;
__(a) through, throughout: Luk.8:39  9:6 10:4, Act.8:1,  36 al.;
__(b) to, towards, over against: Luk.10:32 (Field, Notes, 62), Act.2:1o 16:7, Gal.2:11, Php.3:14, al.;
__       __(with) in adverbial phrases, at, in, by, of: κατ᾽  οἶκον, at home, Act.2:46; κατ᾽ ἰδίαν (see: ἴδιος); καθ᾽ ἑαυτόν, Act.28:16, Rom.14:22, Jas.2:17; with pron. of person(s), Act.17:28  18:15, Rom.1:15, Eph.1:15, al.
__2. Of time, at, during, about: Act.8:26  12:1 19:23, Rom.9:9 Heb.1:10, al.
__3. Distributive;
__(a) of place: κ. τόποὐς, Mat.24:7, al.; κ. πόλιν, Luk.8:1,  4 al.; κ. ἐκκλησίαν, Act.14:23.
__(b) of time: κ. ἔτος, Luk.2:41; ἑορτήν, Mat.27:15, al.;
__(with) of numbers, etc.: καθ᾽ ἕνα πάντες, 1Co.14:31 (on καθ᾽ εἷς, see: εἷς); κ. ἑκατόν, Mrk.6:40; κ. μέρος, Heb.9:5; κ. ὄνομα, Jhn.10:3.
__4. Of fitness, reference, conformity, etc.;
__(a) in relation to, concerning: Rom.1:3, 4 7:22 9:3, 5, 1Co.12:6 10:18, Php.1:12; κ. πάντα, Act.17:22, Col.3:20, 22 Heb.2:17 4:15;
__(b) according to, after, like: Mrk.7:5, Luk.2:27, 29 Jhn.7:24 Rom.8:4 14:15, Eph.2:2, Col.2:8, Jas.2:8, al.
__III. In composition, κ. denotes,
__1. down, down from (καταβαίνω), etc.), hence, metaphorically;
__(a) victory or rule over (καταδουλόω, -κυριεύω, etc.);
__(b) "perfective" action (M, Pr., 111ff.).
__2. under (κατακαλύπτω), etc.).
__3. in succession (καθεξῆς).
__4. after, behind (καταλείπω).
__5. Hostility, against (καταλαλέω).
(AS)

κατά [κᾰτᾰ],
poetry καταί accusative to [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd c.AD: Apollonius Dyscolus Grammaticus “de Syntaxi;” 309.28, found in Compds., as καταιβάτης]]: preposition with genitive or accusative:— downwards.

__A
WITH GEN.,

__A.I
denoting motion from above, down from, βῆ δὲ κατ᾽ Οὐλύμποιο καρήνων, κατ᾽ Ἰδαίων ὀρέων, βαλέειν κ. πέτρης, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 22.187, 16.677, 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 14.399; κατ᾽ οὐρανοῦ εἰλήλουθας 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 6.128]]; καθ᾽ ἵππων ἀΐξαντε[Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. work] 232; δάκρυα.. κ. βλεφάρων Χαμάδις ῥέε 17.438; ἵεις σαυτὸν κ. τοῦ τείχους 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Vespae” 355; ἁλόμενοι κ. τῆς πέτρας 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 4.2.17; κ. τῶν πετρῶν ὦσαι 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Phaedrus” 229c; κ. κρημνῶν ῥιφέντες [prev. author] “Lg.” 944a:]] — for κατ᾽ ἄκρης see.{ἄκρα}: Μοῖσα κ. στόματος Χέε νέκταρ [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [3rd c.BC: Theocritus Poeta Bucolicus 7.82 (but perhaps in sense 11.1).]]

__A.II
denoting downward motion,

__A.II.1
down upon or over, κ. Χθονὸς ὄμματα πήξας [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 3.217]]; of the dying, κατὰ.. ὀφθαλμῶν κέχυτ᾽ ἀχλύς a cloud settled upon the eyes, [Refs [5.696, compare 20.321; τὸν δὲ κατ᾽ ὀφθαλμῶν.. νὺξ ἐκάλυψεν 13.580]]; φᾶρος κὰκ κεφαλῆς εἴρυσσε down over.. , [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 8.85]]; [κόπρος] κ. σπείους κέχυτο.. πολλή [Refs [9.330]]; ὕδωρ κ. Χειρός, see at {Χεί; μύρον κ. τῆς κεφαλῆς καταχέαντες} [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 398a; νάρκη μου κ. τῆς Χειρὸς καταχεῖται 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Vespae” 713; κ. τῆς τραπέζης καταπάσας τέφραν [prev. author] “Nu.” 177]]; ξαίνειν κ. τοῦ νώτου πολλὰς [πληγάς] [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 19.197; ἐσκεδασμένοι κ. τῆς Χώρας 2nd c.BC: Polybius Historicus 1.17.10; οἱ κ. νώτου πονοῦντες [prev. author] 3.19.7; ῥόπαλον ἤλασα κὰκ κεφαλῆς 3rd c.BC: Theocritus Poeta Bucolicus 25.256]]; κ. κόρρης παίειν, ={ἐπὶ κόρρης}, [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd c.AD: Lucianus Sophista “Cat.” 12, +others]]

__A.II.1.b
Geometry texts, along, upon, πίπτειν κατ᾽ [εὐθείας] [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [3rd c.BC: Archimedes Geometra “περὶ σφαίρας καὶ κυλίνδρου” 1 “Def.” 2;]] αἱ γωνίαι κ. κύκλων περιφερειῶν ἐνεχθήσονται will move on.. , [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [[prev. work]1.23, +others,compare 3rd c.BC: Aristarchus Samius Astronomus 1.]]

__A.II.2
down into, νέκταρ στάξε κ. ῥινῶν [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 19.39]]; of a dart, κ. γαίης ᾤχετο [Refs [13.504, etc.; ἔθηκε κατ᾽ ὄχθης μείλινον ἔγχος 21.172; ψυχὴ κ. Χθονὸς ᾤχετο 23.100]]; κ. γᾶς underground, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “O.” 2.59]]; κατ᾽ ὕδατος under water, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 2.149]]; [ποταμὸς] δὺς κ. τῆς γῆς [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Phd.” 113c, compare “Ti.” 25d; κ. γῆς σύμεναι 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Eumenides” 1007 (_anapaest meter_)]]; κ. Χθονὸς κρύψαι to bury. [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Antigone” 24]]; ὁ κ. γῆς one dead and buried, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 4.6.5; οἱ κ. Χθονὸς θεοί 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Persae” 689, etc.; θεοὶ[οἱ] κ. γᾶς [prev. author] “Ch.” 475 (Lyric poetry)]], etc.; so κ. θαλάσσης ἀφανίζεσθαι, καταδεδυκέναι, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 7.6, 235]]; also βᾶτε κατ᾽ ἀντιθύρων go down by or through.. , [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Electra” 1433.]]

__A.II.3
later, towards a point, τοξεύειν κ. σκοποῦ to shoot at, [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd c.AD: Herodianus Grammaticus 6.7.8; κατ᾽ ἰχνῶν τινος ὁδεύειν 2nd c.AD: Lucianus Sophista “Rh.Pr.” 9.]]

__A.II.4
of vows or oaths, by, καθ᾽ ἡμῶν ὀμνύναι [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 29.26, compare 54.38; ἐπιορκήσασα κ. τῶν παίδων 5th c.BC: Lysias Orator 32.13]]; especially of the victims, etc., over which the oath is taken, ὀμνυόντων τὸν ἐπιχώριον ὅρκον καθ᾽ ἱερῶν τελείων Foed. cited in [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 5.47, compare 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Ἀθηναίων Πολιτεία” 29.5, “Foed.Delph.Pell.” 1 A 9, etc.; κ. τῶν νικητηρίων εὐξάμενοι 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator “Epistulae” 1.16]]; also κατ᾽ ἐξωλείας ὀμνύναι to imprecate destruction on oneself, [Refs [[prev. author] 21.119; κατ᾽ ἐξ. ἐπιορκεῖν [prev. author] 57.22.]]

__A.II.4.b
to make a vow towards, i.e. make a vow of offering.., κ. Χιλίων εὐχὴν ποιήσασθαι Χιμάρων [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Equites” 660.]]

__A.II.5
in hostile sense, against, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Choephori” 221, 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Ajax” 304, etc.; κ. πάντων φύεσθαι 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 18.19]]; especially of judges giving sentence against a person, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Septem contra Thebas” 198, 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Ajax” 449, etc.; ψεύδεσθαι κατά τινος 5th c.BC: Lysias Orator 22.7; λέγειν κατά τινος κακά 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Philoctetes” 65, compare 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Historia Graeca (Hellenica)” 1.5.2, etc.]]; of speeches, [λόγος] κ. Μειδίου, etc. (opposed to πρὸς Λεπτίνην, in reply to L.); δῶρα εἰληφέναι κατά τινος [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-3rd c.BC: Dinarchus Orator 3.6, compare 18.]]

__A.II.6
of Time,for, μισθοῦν κ. εἴκοσι ἐτῶν [Refs [“IG” 12.94.37]]; κ. βίου for life, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [“Tab.Heracl.” 1.50; κὰπ παντὸς Χρόνοι “IG” 9(2).517.20 (from Larissa) (but κ. παντὸς τοῦ Χρόνου σκέψασθε 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 22.72 falls under 7)]]; κ. παντὸς τοῦ αἰῶνος ἀείμνηστον [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Lycurgus Orator 7.]]

__A.II.7
in respect of, concerning, μὴ κατ᾽ ἀνθρώπων σκόπει μόνον τοῦτο [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Phaedo” 70d; κ. τῶν ἄλλων τεχνῶν τοιαῦτα εὑρήσομεν [prev. author] “Sph.” 253b]]; οἱ κ. Δημοσθένους ἔπαινοι praises bestowed on [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator, 4th c.BC: Aeschines Orator 3.50]]; ἐρεῖν or λέγειν κατά τινος to say of one, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Apologia” 37b, “Prt.” 323b, etc.; εἰ κ. θηλείας φαίης 2nd c.AD: Apollonius Dyscolus Grammaticus “de Syntaxi;” 198.10; εἴπερ ἕν γέ τι ζητεῖς κ. πάντων 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Meno” 73d, compare 74b; ὅπερ εἴρηται καθόλου κ. πασῶν τῶν πολιτειῶν 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Politica” 1307b2]]; frequently in the Logic of [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus, κατά τινος λέγεσθαι or κατηγορεῖσθαι]] to be predicated of.., [Refs [“Int.” 16b10, “Cat.” 1b10, etc.]]; καταφῆσαί (or ἀποφῆσαί) τι κατά τινος to affirm (or deny) of.., Metaphorical[Refs [1007b21]]; so κ. τινὸς ὑπάρχειν [Refs [“Int.” 16b13: and in]] adverb καθόλου (which see).

__B
WITH Acc.,

__B.I
of motion downwards, κ. ῥόον down stream, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 14.254, 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 12.33]]; opposed to ἀνὰ τὸν ποταμόν, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 2.96]]; κ. τὸν ποταμόν, κ. τὸ ὑδάτιον, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. author] 1.194, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Phaedrus” 229a]]; κατ᾽ οὖρον ἰέναι, ῥεῖν, down (i.e. with) the wind, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Septem contra Thebas” 690, 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Trachiniae” 468]]; κ. πνεῦμα, κατ᾽ ἄνεμον ἵστασθαι to leeward, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Historia Animalium” 535a19, 560b13, 1st c.AD: Dioscorides (Dioscurides) Medicus 4.153.]]

__B.I.2
with or without signification of motion, on, over, throughout a space, frequently in [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Homerus Epicus, καθ᾽ Ἑλλάδα καὶ μέσον Ἄργος 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 1.344]]; κατ᾽ Ἀχαΐδα, κ. Τροίην, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 11.770, 9.329; κατ᾽ ἠερόεντα κέλευθα 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 20.64]]; κ. πόντον, κῦμα, ὕλην, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 4.276, 6.136, 3.151; κ. πτόλιν 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 2.383]]; κ. ἄστυ, οἶκον, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 18.286, 6.56; κ. ὅμιλον, στρατόν, 3.36, 1.229]]; κ. κλισίας τε νέας τε[Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. work] 487; πόλεμον κάτα δακρυόεντα 17.512; κ. ὑσμίνην, μόθον, κλόνον, 5.84, 18.159, 16.331; τὸ ὕδωρ κ. τοὺς ταφροὺς ἐχώρει 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 7.5.16, etc.]] (in later Gr.of motion to a place, κ. τὴν Ἰταλίαν [Refs 5th c.BC+ [1st c.BC: Zosimus Epigrammaticus 3.1); καθ᾽ Ἑλλάδα 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Agamemnon” 578; κ. πτόλιν [prev. author] “Th.” 6; αἱ σκηναὶ αἱ κ. τὴν ἀγοράν 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 18.169; τὰ κατ᾽ ἀγροὺς Διονύσια 4th c.BC: Aeschines Orator 1.157, etc.; κ. τὸ προάστιον 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 3.54; τύμβον κατ᾽ αὐτόν 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Septem contra Thebas” 528, compare “Supp.” 869 (Lyric poetry)]]: Geometry texts, at a point, [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [3rd c.BC: Euclides Geometra 1.1, +others]]; τέμνειν [σφαῖραν] κ. κύκλον in a circle, [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [3rd c.BC: Archimedes Geometra “ψαμμίτης” 1.17]]; also, in the region of, οἱ κ. τὸν ἥλιον γινόμενοι ἀστέρες [Refs 8th c.BC+ [1st c.BC: Geminus Astronomicus 12.7: frequently in 8th c.BC: Homerus Epicus in describing the place of a wound, βαλεῖν κ. στῆθος, γαστέρα, etc., 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 11.108, 16.465, +others; νύξε κ. δεξιὸν ὦμον 5.46; οὔτασε κατ᾽ ἰσχίον 11.339; so βαλεῖν κατ᾽ ἀσπίδα, κ. ζωστῆρα, 5.537, 615]]; βέλος κ. καίριον ἦλθεν struck upon a vital part, variant in [Refs [11.439: _metaphorically_, ἄχος κ. φρένα τύψε 19.125: generally, κ. φρένα καὶ κατὰ θυμόν]] in heart and soul, [Refs [4.163, +others]]

__B.I.3
opposite, over against, κ. Σινώπην πόλιν [LXX+5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.76, compare 2.148, 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 2.30, etc.; ἀνὴρ κατ᾽ ἄνδρα 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Septem contra Thebas” 505; μολὼν.. μοι κ. στόμα [prev. author] “Ch.” 573; κατ᾽ ὀφθαλμούς τινος LXX.2Ki.12.11; οἱ μὲν Ἀθηναῖοι κ. Λακεδαιμονίους ἐγένοντο 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Historia Graeca (Hellenica)” 4.2.18; κατ᾽ Ἀχαιοὺς ἀντετάχθησαν [prev. passage]; ἐν συμποσίῳ.., περίμενε, μέχρις ἂν γένηται κατὰ σέ 1st-2nd c.AD: Epictetus Philosophus “Enchiridion” 15, compare 3rd c.AD(?): Diogenes Laertius 7.108.]]

__B.II
distributively, of a whole divided into parts, κρῖν᾽ ἄνδρας κ. φῦλα, κ. φρήτρας by tribes, by clans, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 2.362]]; κ. σφέας μαχέονται by themselves, separately,[Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. work] 366, compare 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 4.64; ἐσκήνουν κ. τάξεις 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 2.1.25; αὐτὴ καθ᾽ αὑτήν 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Prometheus Vinctus” 1013]]; κ. κώμας κατοικημένοι in separate villages, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.96]]; κατ᾽ ἑωυτοὺς ἕκαστοι ἐτράποντο each to his own home, [Refs [[prev. author] 5.15]]; κ. πόλεις ἀποπλεῦσαι, διαλυθῆναι, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 1.89, 3.1: στρατιὰ κ. ἕνδεκα μέρη κεκοσμημένη 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Phaedrus” 247a; later οἱ κατ᾽ ἄνδρα λόγοι “PLond.” 2.259.72 (1st c.AD),compare 1st-2nd c.AD: Dio Chrysostomus Sophista 32.6, etc.; ἡ κατ᾽ οἰκίαν ἀπογραφή “PLond.” 3.904.20 (2nd c.AD)]], etc.; κατ᾽ ἔπος word by word, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Ranae” 802]]; κατ᾽ ὄνομα individually, [NT.3John.15, etc.]; παῖδα κ. κρήνην at each fount a boy, [Refs 3rd c.AD+ [“Lyrica Alexandrina Adespota” 37.13, compare “POxy” 2108.9 (3rd c.AD).]]

__B.II.2
of Time, καθ᾽ ἡμέραν, κατ᾽ ἦμαρ, day by day, daily, see at {ἡμέρα} 111; καθ᾽ ἑνιαυτόν, κατ᾽ ἔτος, [NT+1st c.AD+ [“Test.Epict.” 6.24, NT.Luke.2.41, etc.; κ. μῆνα “POxy.” 275.18 (1st c.AD).]]

__B.II.3
of Numbers, by so many at a time, καθ᾽ ἕνα one at a time, individually, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 7.104 (later τὸ καθ᾽ ἕν]]detailed list, [Refs 2nd c.BC+ [PTeb. 47.34 (2nd c.BC), etc.)]]; κ. μίαν τε καὶ δύο by ones and twos, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 4.113; δύο μνέαι τεταγμέναι κατ᾽ ἄνδρα αἰχμάλωτον ἕκαστον [prev. author] 6.79; ἐκ τῶν συμμάχων ἐξελέγετο κατ᾽ ὀλίγους [prev. author] 8.113; κ. τὰς πέντε καὶ εἴκοσι μνᾶς πεντακοσίας δραχμὰς εἰσφέρειν to pay 500]] drachmae on every [Refs 4th c.BC+ [25 minae, 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 27.7; κ. διακοσίας καὶ τριακοσίας ὁμοῦ τι τάλαντον διακεχρημένον]]in separate sums of 200[Refs [and 300 drachmae, [prev. author] 27.11]]; of ships, κ. μίαν (i.e. ναῦν) in column, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 2.90; κ. μίαν ναῦν ἐπιτάττειν 2nd c.BC: Polybius Historicus 1.26.12, compare 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 2.84: Geometry texts, μετρεῖν, μετρεισθαι κατά..]], measure, be measured a certain number of times, [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [3rd c.BC: Euclides Geometra 7 “Def.” 8,9, +others]]; μετρεῖν κ. τὰς ἐν τῷ Β μονάδας as many times as there are units in B, [Refs [[prev. author] 7.16.]]

__B.III

__B.III.2
of pursuit, κ. πόδας τινὸς ἐλαύνειν [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 9.89]]; simply κ. τινά after him, [Refs [[prev. author] 1.84; ἰέναι κ. τοὺς ἄλλους [prev. author] 9.53]]; κατ᾽ ἴχνος on the track, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Ajax” 32, 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Agamemnon” 695 (Lyric poetry); ὥσπερ κατ᾽ ἴχνη κ. τὰ νῦν εἰρημένα ζῆν 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Phaedo” 115b.]]

Geometry texts, in adverbial phrases, κ. κάθετον in the same vertical line, [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [3rd c.BC: Archimedes Geometra “τετραγωνισμὸς παραβολῆς” 6]]; κατ᾽ εὐθεῖάν τινι in the same straight line with.., [Refs 3rd c.AD+ [3rd c.AD(?): Pappus Mathematicus 58.7.]]

Πίνδαρον 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Phaedrus” 227b, etc.]]

__B.IV.2
in relation to, concerning, τὰ κατ᾽ ἀνθρώπους ={τὰ ἀνθρώπινα}, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Eumenides” 930, 310; τὰ κ. τὸν Τέλλον 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.31; τὰ κ. τὴν Κύρου τελευτήν [prev. work] 214]]; τὰ κ. πόλεμον military matters, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aeschines Orator 1.181]]; αἱ κ. τὴν πόλιν οἰκονομίαι (opposed to αἱ πολεμικαὶ πράξεις) the management of public affairs, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-3rd c.BC: Dinarchus Orator 1.97; τὰ κ. τὰς θυσίας “SIG” 506.7 (Delph., 3rd c.BC)]]; so τὸ κατ᾽ ὑμέας as far as concerns you, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 7.158]]; τὸ κατ᾽ ἐμέ as far as I am concerned, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 18.247]]; κ. τοῦτο in this respect, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 5.3, etc.]]; κ. ταὐτά in the same way, [Refs [[prev. author] 2.20]]; καθ᾽ ὅτι so far as, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 1.82, etc.]]

__B.IV.3
in Comparisons, corresponding with, after the fashion of, κρομύοιο λοπὸν κ. like the coat of an onion, uncertain in [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 19.233; μέλος κ. Φοίνισσαν ἐμπολὰν πέμπεται 5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “P.” 2.67]]; κ. Μιθραδάτην answering to the description of him, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.121]]; τὴν ἰδέαν κ. πνιγέα like an oven in appearance, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Aves” 1001]]; κηδεῦσαι καθ᾽ ἑαυτόν to marry in one's own rank of life, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Prometheus Vinctus” 890; οὐ κατ᾽ ἄνθρωπον φρονεῖν [prev. author] “Th.” 425; λέγω κατ᾽ ἄνδρα, μὴ θεόν, σέβειν ἐμέ [prev. author] “Ag.” 925]]; οὐ κατὰ σέ none of your sort, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Chionides Comicus 1 (but ἵνα προσείπω σε κατὰ σέ]] to address you in your own style, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Gorgias” 467c); τὸ κατ᾽ ἐμὲ καὶ οὐ κατ᾽ ἐμέ 2nd c.AD: Arrianus Historicus “Epicteti Dissertationes” 1.28.5; οὐ κ. τὰς Μειδίου λῃτουργίας 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 21.169; ἡ βασιλεία κ. τὴν ἀριστοκρατίαν ἐστί 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Politica” 1310b3]]: frequently after a comparative, μέζων ἢ κατ᾽ ἀνθρώπων φύσιν [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 8.38, compare 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Apologia” 20e, etc.]]; μείζω ἢ κ. δάκρυα too great for tears, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 7.75]]; ἤθεα βαθύτερα ἢ κ. Θρήϊκας morerefined than was common among the Thracians, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 4.95.]]

__B.V
by the favour of a god, etc., κ. δαίμονα [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “O.” 9.28, compare “P.” 8.68; κ. θεῖον 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Equites” 147 codices (κ. θεὸν Cobet)]]; κ. τύχην τινά [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 48.24.]]

__B.VI
of round numbers (see. below v11.2), nearly, about, κ. Χίλια ἑξακόσια ἔτεα 1600 years more or less, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 2.145, compare 6.44, +others]]; κατ᾽ οὐδέν next to nothing, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Politicus” 302b.]]

__B.VII

Χειμῶνα, κ. θερείαν, [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [“PLille” 1r14 (3rd c.BC), “PTeb.” 27.60 (2nd c.BC).]]

__B.VII.2
about, κ. τὸν αὐτὸν τοῦτον Χρόνον [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 3.131, etc.; κ. τοὺς θανάτους τῶν βασιλέων [prev. author] 6.58]]; especially with names of persons, κ. Ἄμασιν βασιλεύοντα about the time of Amasis, [Refs [[prev. author] 2.134; κ. τὸν κ. Κροῖσον Χρόνον [prev. author] 1.67]]; οἱ κατ᾽ ἐκεῖνον (i.e. τὸν Ἀλκιβιάδην) ὑμέτεροι πρόγονοι [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 21.146 (variant{κατ᾽ ἐκ. τὸν Χρόνον}); κ. τοὺς Ἡρακλείδας 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Respublica Lacedaemoniorum” 10.8]]; οἱ καθ᾽ ἑαυτοὺς ἄνθρωποι their contemporaries, [Refs [[prev. author] “Mem.” 3.5.10.]]

__B.VII.3
καθ᾽ ἕτος this year, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [“SIG” 284.24 (Erythrae, 4th c.BC), “OGI” 458.64 1st c.BC-1st c.AD, “CIG” “Corpus Inscriptionum Graecarum” “Corpus Inscriptionum Graecarum” 3641b5,38 (from Lampsacus).]]

__B.VIII
periphrastically with abstract substantive, κατ᾽ ἡσυχίην, κ. τάχος, ={ἡσύχως, ταχέως}, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.9, 7.178]]; κ. κράτος by force, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Historia Graeca (Hellenica)” 2.1.19, etc.]]; κ. μέρος partially, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Poetica” 1456a16]]; individually, severally, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Theaetetus” 157b, “Lg.” 835a]]; κ. φύσιν naturally, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 2.38, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 428e]]; κ. τὴν τέχνην skilfully, [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd c.AD: Lucianus Sophista “DDeor.” 20.7]]; οὔτ᾽ ἐμοὶ λέγειν καθ᾽ ἡδονήν [ἐστι] it is not pleasant for me to tell you, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Prometheus Vinctus” 263.]]

__C
Position: κατά may follow both its cases, and is then written with anastrophe κάτα, as [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 20.221, etc.]]; so also in tmesi, when it follows its Verb, [Refs [17.91.]]

__D
absolutely as adverb. in all the above senses, especially like{κάτω}, downwards, from above, down, frequently in [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Homerus Epicus]]

__E
κατά in COMPOSITION (joined with other words),

__E.I
downwards, down, as in καταβαίνω, καταβάλλω, κατάκειμαι, καταπέμπω, καταπίπτω, καταπλέω 1.

__E.II
in answer to, in accordance with, as in κατᾴδω (occino), καταινέω, καταθύμιος.

__E.III
against, in hostile sense [Refs 4th c.BC+ [compare (4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus 11.5), as in καταγιγνώσκω, κατακρίνω, καταψηφίζομαι: more rarely with a]] substantive, as καταδίκη.

__E.IV
back, back again, as in κάτειμι, καταπορεύομαι, καταπλέω 11.

__E.V
frequently only to strengthen the notion of the simple word, as in κατακόπτω, κατακτείνω, καταφαγεῖν, etc.; also with Substantives and adjectives, as in κατάδηλος, κάτοξος.

__E.VI
sometimes to give a transitive force to an intransitive Verb, our be-, as in καταθρηνέω bewail.

__E.VII
implying waste or consumption, as in καταλειτουργέω, καθιπποτροφέω, καταζευγοτροφέω: and generally in a disparaging sense, as in καταγιγνώσκω 1.

__F
κατά as a preposition was shortened in some dialects, especially in Epic dialect, into κάγ, κάδ, κάκ, κάμ, κάν, κάπ, κάρ, κάτ, before γ, δ, κ, μ, ν, π (or φ), ῥ, τ (or θ), respectively; see these forms in their own places. Mss. and the older Edd. join the preposition with the following word, as καγγόνυ, καδδέ, κακκεφαλῆς, καππεδίον, καπφάλαρα, καρρόον, καττάδε, καττόν, etc. In compound Verbs, κατά sometimes changes into καβ, καλ, καρ, κατ, before β, λ, ρ, θ, respectively, as κάββαλε, κάλλιπε, καρρέζουσα, κάτθαν; and before στ, σχ, the second syllable sometimes disappears, as in καστορνῦσα, κάσχεθε, as also in the Doric dialect forms καβαίνων, κάπετον.
καθεῖς,
for καθ᾽ εἷς, one by one, one after antoher, [LXX+NT+2nd c.AD+ [LXX.3Mac.5.34; εἷς καθεῖς NT.Mark.14.19, etc.: formed backwards from the _neuter_ ἓν καθέν, noted by 2nd c.AD: Lucianus Sophista “Sol.” 9.]]

Latin catabolicus.

perhaps outer wrapper [Refs [compare (κατάβλημα 11.4)]] of a bandage, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Hippocrates Medicus “κατ᾽ ἰητρεῖον” 9.]]

to blame, condemn: with genitive of person(s), 1Jn.3:20-21; pass., κατεγνωσμένος ἦν (RV, he stood condemned, see Ellie., in l; but cf. Field, Notes, 188): Gal.2:11.†

LSJ / STEPBible (TFLSJ)
καταγιγνώσκω,
Ionic dialect and later καταγηρ-γῑνώσκω, future -γνώσομαι[Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Euthyphro” 2b]]:—remark, observe, especially something to one's prejudice, with genitive person:

__I
generally, καταγνοὺς τοῦ γέροντος τοὺς τρόπους having observed his foibles, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Equites” 46]]; πολλήν γέ μου δυστυχίαν κατέγνωκας I have been very unfortunate by your way of it, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Apologia” 25a; πολλὴν ἡμῶν ἐρημίαν 4th c.BC: Isaeus Orator 1.2]]; οὐκ ἐπιτήδεα κατά τινος κ. having formed unfavourable prejudices against one, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 6.97]]: with infinitive, of an unfavourable judgement, κ. ἑαυτοῦ μὴ περιέσεσθαι [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 3.45, compare 7.51; αὐτὸς ἐμαυτοῦ κατέγνων μὴ ἂν καρτερῆσαι 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 6.1.36, compare 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Timaeus” 19d: followed by ὅτι, ὡς, ἐμοῦ κατέγνωκας ὅτι εἰμὶ ἥττων τῶν καλῶν 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Meno” 76c; οὐκ ἂν καταγνοίην ὑμῶν οὐδενὸς ὡς.. ἀμελήσετε 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 21.4 (but κατεγνωκότες ὅτι.. ἐφθείρομεν]] despising us because.. [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 6.34, compare “PMagd.” 42.4 (3rd c.BC), 4th c.AD: Julianus Imperator “Orationes” 3.108b)]]: with participle, κ. τινὰ πράττοντα [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Oeconomicus” 2.18, compare “Cyr.” 8.4.9; τὸ Χωρίον νοσερὸν [ὂν] καταγνόντες 3rd c.AD(?): Diogenes Laertius 2.109]]:—passive, to be judged unfavourably, lightly esteemed, παρολιγωρεῖσθαι καὶ καταγινώσκεσθαι [Refs 2nd c.BC+ [2nd c.BC: Polybius Historicus 5.27.6]]; κατεγνωσμένος despised, [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd-3rd c.AD: Philostratus Sophista “Vitae Sophistarum” 2.29.]]

__II
with accusative criminis, lay as a charge against a person, κ. ἑωυτῶν ἀνανδρείην [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Hippocrates Medicus “Aër.” 22; κ. τινὸς μηδὲν ἀνόσιον 5th c.BC: Antipho Orator 2.2.12]]; δειλίαν, δωροδοκίαν κ. τινός, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Lysias Orator 14.16, 21.21; οὐδὲν ἀγεννὲς ὑμῶν καταγιγνώσκω 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 21.152; ἑαυτῶν ἀδικίαν 5th-6th c.BC: Andocides Orator 1.3]]; πολλὴν μανίαν, μωρίαν, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Isocrates Orator 4.133, 5.21; σκληρότητα ἡμῶν καὶ ἀγροικίαν 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 607b; τοσαύτην ὑμῶν εὐήθειαν 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 30.38: with _genitive_ understood, οὐ γὰρ ἐκεῖνό γε (i.e. σοῦ) καταγνώσομαι, ὡς.. 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Euthyphro” 2b; later κ. κατά τινος τὸν φόνον 3rd c.AD: Porphyrius Tyrius Philosophus “de Abstinentia - Porphyrii Opuscula” 2.30:]] —passive, καταγνωσθεὶς δειλίαν being convicted of cowardice, [Refs 1st c.BC+ [1st c.BC: Dionysius Halicarnassensis 11.22; κ. ἐπὶ λογοκλοπίᾳ 3rd c.AD(?): Diogenes Laertius 8.54; κατεγνωσμένος]]self-condemned, [NT.Gal.2.11.]

__II.2
with genitive criminis, παρανόμων κ. τινός [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 25.67; παρανοίας ὑμῶν αὐτῶν [prev. author] “Prooem.” 35: with _accusative_ _person_, κ. τινὰ φόνου]] pronounce a verdict of murder against.. , Legal cited in [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Lysias Orator 1.30]]; μὴ καταγιγνώσκωμεν τὸ (perhaps τοῦ) μηδὲν εἰρηκέναι τὸν ἀποφηνάμενον [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Theaetetus” 206e.]]

__II.3
with infinitive, κ. σφῶν αὐτῶν, ἑαυτοῦ ἀδικεῖν, charge oneself with.. , [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Lysias Orator 20.6, 4th c.BC: Aeschines Orator 2.6, compare 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 21.175, 206; κ. ὡς.. 5th-6th c.BC: Isocrates Orator 9.78:]] —so in passive, καταγνωσθεὶς νεώτερα πρήσσειν being suspected of doing, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 6.2]]; κ. αὐθέντης (i.e. εἶναι) [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Antipho Orator 3.3.11]]; to be detected, ἔν τινι [Refs 3rd c.AD+ [“PFlor.” 175.16 (3rd c.AD)]]; also κατέγνωσται μελίκρητον ὑπὸ τῶν ἀνθρώπων ὡς καταγυιοῖ τοὺς πίνοντας [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Hippocrates Medicus “περὶ διαίτης ὀξέων” 56.]]

__II.4
with genitive person only, condemn, τοῦ ἀνθρώπου [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Demodocus” 382e.]]

__III
with accusative poenae, give judgement or sentence against a person, κ. τινὸς θάνατον pass sentence of death on one, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 6.60]]; Μηδισμοῦ κ. τινὸς θάνατον for Medism, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Isocrates Orator 4.157; κ. τινὸς φυγήν 5th-6th c.BC: Andocides Orator 1.106; φυγὴν αὑτοῦ καταγνούς 5th c.BC: Lysias Orator 14.38]]: with infinitive, κ. αὐτοῦ ἀποτεῖσαι τὰ Χρήματα [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 56.18]]; later θάνατον, φυγὴν κ. κατά τινος, [Refs 1st c.BC+ [1st c.BC: Diodorus Siculus Historicus 18.62, 19.51]]:—passive, θάνατός τινος κατέγνωστο [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Antipho Orator 5.70, compare 5th c.BC: Lysias Orator 13.39, Jusj. cited in 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 24.149; later καταγνωσθεὶς θανάτῳ 2nd-3rd c.AD: Aelianus “Varia Historia” 12.49: _absolutely_, κατεγνώσθησαν]] they were condemned, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 4.74, compare 5th-6th c.BC: Andocides Orator 4.8; τὸ ἀδίκημα κεκριμένον ἐστὶ καὶ κατεγνωσμένον 4th c.BC: Lycurgus Orator 52.]]

__III.2
decide a suit, δίκην [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Equites” 1360]]:— passive, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Eumenides” 573 codices; δίκη μὴ ὀρθῶς -γνωσθεῖσα 5th c.BC: Antipho Orator 6.3.]]

κ. τι ἀπό or ἔκ τινος, metaphorically, establish securely, τὴν διὰ πάντων διήκουσαν ὠφέλειαν ἀπὸ [τοῦ συλλογισμοῦ] [Refs 5th c.AD+ [5th c.AD: Proclus Philosophus “in Platonis Alcibiadem” p.252 C., compare 6th c.AD: Simplicius Philosophus in “de An.” 15.34.]]

of death, fatigue, disaster, etc., τὸν δὲ κατ᾽ ὄσσε ἔλλαβε.. θάνατος [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 5.82; Ἄργον.. κατὰ μοῖρ᾽ ἔλαβεν.. θανάτοιο 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 17.326: with double _accusative_, εὖτ᾽ ἄν μιν κάματος κατὰ γυῖα λάβῃσιν 1.192; Δίκη καταλήψεται ψευδῶν τέκτονας 1st c.AD(?): Heraclitus 28]]; befall, overtake, συμφορὰ κ. πόλεις [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Hippolytus” 1161: frequently in 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus, θεῖα πρήγματα καταλαμβάνει τοὺς αἰελούρους 2.66; πένθεα μεγάλα τοὺς Αἰγυπτίους κ. [prev. passage], compare 3.42]]; ὅσα φεύγοντας ἐκ τῆς πατρίδος κακὰ ἐπίδοξα καταλαμβάνειν may be expected to befall them,[Refs [4.11; ἤν τι καταλαμβάνῃ νεώτερον τὸν πεζόν 8.21]]: followed by infinitive, νοῦσός τινα κ. νοσῆσαι [Refs [3.149, compare 3.75]]; πρίν τι ἀνήκεστον ἡμᾶς κ. NT.Act.4.13; τί τὸ πλάτος NT.Eph.3.18]]:— passive, [Refs 1st c.BC+ [1st c.BC: Philodemus Philosophus “περὶ σημείων καὶ σημειώσεων” 22, “Mus.” p.62K., 2nd c.AD: Numenius Apamensis Platonicus cited in 4th c.AD: Eusebius Caesariensis Scriptor Ecclesiasticus “Praeparatio Evangelica” 14.8.]]

__4
accept, παρὰ τοῦ βασιλέως.. δωροδοκήματα uncertain reading in [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Comicus 119.1 (κᾆτ᾽ ἔλαβον Mein.).]]

__II
catch, overtake, come up with, τοὺς φεύγοντας [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.63, compare 2.30]], etc.:—passive, [Refs 2nd c.BC+ [[prev. author] 7.211, 2nd c.BC: Polybius Historicus 1.47.8.]]

__III

κατα-λέγω
[in LXX: Deu.19:16 (עָנָה), 2Ma.7:30 R * ;]
__1. to lay down; mid. (in Hom.), to lie down.
__2. to narrate (LXX, ll. with).
__3. to choose out, hence, to enrol (as of soldiers, Hdt., Thuc., a1., see LS, see word): of widows, pass., 1Ti.5:9 (cf. Ellic.; CGT, in l).†

__B.b
repeat, recite, τῶν Χρησμῶν [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 7.6; τετράμετρα πρὸς τὸν αὐλόν 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Symposium” 6.3; τὰς πατρίους εὐχάς 4th c.BC: Hermias Historicus 2]]; καταλέγεσθαι· ὀδύρεσθαι τὸν τεθνεῶτα, [Refs 5th c.AD+ [5th c.AD(?): Hesychius Legal icographus; compare κατάλεγμα, καταλογή 111.]]

__B.2

[Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Historia Graeca (Hellenica)” 3.4.15]]:—in middle, enrol for oneself, δορυφόρους, ὁπλίτας, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.98, 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 7.31:]] —passive (aorist 2 κατελέγην more common in Attic dialect than aorist 1,[Refs 5th c.BC+ [compare “IG” 22.896.9, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Leges” 762e, 943a)]], to be enlisted or enrolled, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 7.1]]; τῶν τρισχιλίων κ. to be enrolled of their number, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Lysias Orator 30.8; κ. στρατιώτης [prev. author] 9.4; κατειλεγμένος ἱππεύειν [prev. author] 16.13; καταλεγεὶς τῶν τριηράρχων 4th c.BC: Isaeus Orator 7.5; ὁ κατειλεγμένος 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 39.8]]; εἰς τὴν σύγκλητον κ. [Refs 1st c.AD+ [1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus “Pompeius” 13]]; ἀγορανόμον -λεγέντα, = Latin adlectum inter aedilicios, Ann.epigram [Refs [1905.120.]]

Plato Philosophus [{5-6th c.BC}] “Respublica” 369e]]; κ. εἰς τὸ μέσον or εἰς τὸ κοινόν, propose for common discussion, [Refs [[prev\. author] “Phlb.” 14b, “Cra.” 384c.]]

[in LXX for אָחַז, חָזַק hi., etc. ;]
__1. perfective of ἔχω (M, Pr., 116; M, Th., 155),
__(a) to possess, hold fast: Luk.8:15, Jhn.5:4, Rom.1:18 (Lft., Notes, 251), 1Co.7:30 11:2, 2Co.6:10, 1Th.5:21, Heb.3:6, 14 10:23;
__(b) to lay hold of, get possession of: Luk.14:9.
__2. to hold back, detain, restrain (M, Th., 156 f.): with accusative before τοῦ μή with inf., Luk.4:42; before πρός, with accusative, Phm 13; absol., τὸ κατέχον (ὁ κ.), 2Th.2:6-7.
__3. Intrans., as nautical term, to put in, make for (LS, see word): Act.27:40.†
(AS)
