κεῖσθαι, posture, attitude, as a category, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Categoriae” 2a2.]]

__III
to be laid up, in store, of goods, property, etc., δόμοις ἐν κτήματα κεῖται [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 9.382; πολλὰ δ᾽ ἐν ἀφνειοῦ πατρὸς κειμήλια κ. 6.47]]; βασιλῆϊ δὲ κεῖται ἄγαλμα is reserved.., [Refs [4.144]]; μνῆμα ξείνοιο.. κέσκετ᾽ ἐνὶ μεγάροισι was left lying.., [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 21.41]]; of things dedicated to a god, κ. ἐν θησαυρῷ [Refs 7th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.51, compare 52, 7th-6th c.BC: Alcaeus Lyricus 94]]; of money, κείμενα deposits, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 6.86. ; κ. σοι εὐεργεσία ἐν τῷ ἡμετέρῳ οἴκῳ 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 1.129, compare “SIG” 22.15 (Epist. Darei), 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 345a]]; πολλὰ χρήματα ἐπὶ τῇ τούτου τραπέζῃ κεῖταί μοι at his bank, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Isocrates Orator 17.44; παρά τινι 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Epistulae” 346c]]; τἀργύριόν σοι κείσεται the caution-money shall be deposited, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Ranae” 624]]; δραχ μὴν ὑπόθες.—Answ. κεῖται πάλαι [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-3rd c.BC: Diphilus Comicus 73.2: _metaphorically_, εἰ ταῦτ᾽ ἀνατὶ τῇδε κείσεται κράτη]] shall be placed to her credit, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Antigone” 485, compare 5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “I.” 5(4).18.]]

__IV
to be placed in position, τῶν ἐπὶ τοῦ τοίχου.. κειμένων κιόνων [Refs [“IG” 12.372.46.]]

__IV.2
to be set up, ordained, ἄεθλα κεῖτ᾽ ἐν ἀγῶνι [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 23.273, compare 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 8.26, 93, 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 2.46; ὅπλων ἔκειτ᾽ ἀγὼν πέρι 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Ajax” 936 (Lyric poetry).]]

__IV.3
of laws, κεῖται νόμος the law is laid down, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Hecuba” 292; νόμοι ἐπ᾽ ὠφελίᾳ τῶν ἀδικουμένων κεῖνται 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 2.37; νόμοι κεῖνται περί τινος 5th c.BC: Antipho Orator 6.2]]; οἱ νόμοι οἱ κείμενοι the established laws, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Plutus” 914, compare 5th c.BC: Lysias Orator 1.48, etc.; οἱ ὑπὸ τῶν θεῶν κείμενοι νόμοι 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Memorabilia” 4.4.21; οἱ νόμοι οἱ ὑπὸ οἱ τῶν βασιλέων κείμενοι 5th-6th c.BC: Isocrates Orator 1.36, compare 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 24.62; καινὰ κεῖσθαι θέσμι᾽ ἀνθρώποις 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Medea” 494]]; αἱ κείμεναι ὑπὸ τῶν ὑπατικῶν γνῶμαι the votes given by.., [Refs 1st c.BC+ [1st c.BC: Dionysius Halicarnassensis 7.47]]; οὐκέτι κ. ἡ διαθήκη no longer holds, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Isaeus Orator 6.32]]; so of philosophical arguments, hold good, κατά τινων [Refs 5th c.BC+ [1st c.BC: Philodemus Gadarensis Epigrammaticus “Rh.” 1.51 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus; θάνατος ὧν κεῖται πέρι 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Ion” 750; κείμεναι ζημίαι 5th c.BC: Lysias Orator 14.9, compare 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 3.45.]]

__IV.4
to be laid down in argument, posited, assumed, τοῦτο ἡμῖν οὕτω κείσθω [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 350d, etc.; ὡμολογημένον ἡμῖν κ. [prev. author] “Plt.” 300e; frequently in 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus, κείσθω]]let it be assumed, [Refs [“Apr.” 34b23, +others]]; τὸ ἐξ ἀρχῆς κείμενον the assumption, [Refs [“Metaphorical” 1008b2, 1047b10]](plural); τὰ περὶ τὴν διάνοιαν ἐν τοῖς περὶ ῥητορικῆς κ. [Refs [“Po.” 1456a35.]]

__IV.5
of names, οὔνομα κεῖται the name is given, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 4.184, 7.200, compare 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 2.2.12, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Sophista” 257c, etc.]]; ὑπὸ τοῦ πατρὸς κείμενον [ὄνομα] [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Isaeus Orator 3.32]]; κεῖσθαι without ὄνομα, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Cratylus” 392d]]; κείμενα ὀόματα established terms, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Topica” 140a3, 4th c.BC: Demetrius Phalereus Rhetor “Demetrius on Style” 96.]]

__IV.6
metaphorically, πάντα δεινὰ κἀπικινδύνως βροτοῖς κεῖται, παθεῖν μὲν εὖ, παθεῖν δὲ θάτερα danger is set before men, that they may.., [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Philoctetes” 503.]]

__V
metaphorically, of continuing conditions, ἐνὶ φρεσὶ πένθος ἔκειτο lay heavy, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 24.423]]; εὔστομα κείσθω remain unspoken, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 2.171]]; νεῖκος ἔκειτό τισι there was an enduring feud, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Tyrannus” 491 (Lyric poetry)]]; Ἑλλήνων κείσομαι ἐν στόματι my name shall be a household word, [Refs 6th c.BC+ [Anthologia Graeca 9.62 (5th c.BC: Evenus Elegiacus); πολλῶν κείμενος ἐν στόμασιν 6th c.BC: Theognis Elegiacus 240; εὖ κείμενα 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Choephori” 693]]; μὴ κινεῖν (i.e. κακὸν) εὖ κείμενον 'let sleeping dogs lie', [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Philebus” 15c, compare 4th c.BC: Hyperides Orator “Fragmenta” 30, 10th c.AD: Suidas Legal icographus]]

__V.2
ταῦτα θεῶν ἐν γούνασι κεῖται, i.e. these things are yet in the power of the gods, to give or not, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 17.514, 20.435.]]

__V.3
κεῖσθαι ἔν τινι to rest entirely or be dependent on him, ἐν ἀγαθοῖσι κ. πολίων κυβερνάσιες [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “P.” 10.71; ἐν ὔμμι ὡς θεῷ κείμεθα 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Coloneus” 248 (Lyric poetry); also ἐπί τινι, τὰ δ᾽ οὐκ ἐπ᾽ ἀνδράσι κ. 5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “P.” 8.76]]: also with simple dative, Λεωφίλῳ πάντα κεῖται [Refs 7th c.BC+ [7th c.BC: Archilochus Lyricus 69, probably in “Comica Adespota” 1325]]; of things, depend upon, τὸ πανηγυρικὸν ἐν μελέτῃ καὶ τριβῇ κ. [Refs 5th c.BC+ [1st c.BC: Philodemus Gadarensis Epigrammaticus “Rh.” 1.93 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus; τὰ.. γυμνάσια ἐν τῇ κινήσει κ. 2nd c.AD: Antyllus Medicus cited in 4th c.AD: Oribasius Medicus 6.23.1.]]

__V.4
in Medicine texts, to be left to settle, of urine, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Hippocrates Medicus “ἐπιδημίαι” 1.26.β.]]

__V.4.b
φάρυγξ οὐ φλεγμαίνουσα, κειμένη δέ[Refs [, i.e. not swollen, [prev. work] 2.2.24.]]

__V.5
Grammars, of words and phrases, to be found, occur, παρὰ τῷ ποιητῃ [Refs 1st c.BC+ [1st c.BC-1st c.AD: Strabo Geographus 7.3.6, compare 2nd c.AD: Athenaeus Epigrammaticus 2.58b; κεῖται ἐν τῷ Περὶ Πλούτου 1st c.BC: Philodemus Philosophus “περὶ οἰκονομίας” p.39 1st c.AD: Josephus Historicus]]; ποῦ κεῖτα; [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd c.AD: Athenaeus Epigrammaticus 4.165d]], compare Κειτούκειτο; κ. ἀντί τινος to be used instead of.., [Refs 1st c.BC+ [1st c.BC-1st c.AD: Strabo Geographus 8.6.7]]; τὸ κείμενον the received text, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [Scholia vulgar form 5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “O.” 2.48.]]

LSJ / STEPBible (TFLSJ)
κειρία, ἡ,
girth of a bedstead, [LXX+5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Aves” 816, LXX.Pro.7.16, 1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus “Alcibiades” 16.]]

__II
swathing-band, bandage, written κηρία, [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [“PMed.Lond.” 155 IV10, 28, +others, 2nd c.AD: Soranus Medicus 1.83, 2.59, 61, 5th c.AD(?): Hesychius Legal icographus (-ρεί-)]]; καιρία (which see); κιρία, [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [“PCair.Zen.” 69.9, 11, “PSI” 4.341.7, 387.4 (3rd c.BC)]]; grave-clothes, in form κειρίαι (variant{κηρίαι}) [NT.John.11.44.]

κηρίαι, tapeworms, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Hippocrates Medicus cited in 1st c.AD: Erotianus Grammaticus; κειρίαι 2nd c.AD: Galenus Medicus 14.755.]]

LSJ / STEPBible (TFLSJ)
κείρω,
future κερῶ [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 471a]], Ionic dialect κερέω [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 23.146]]: aorist ἔκειρα [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “P.” 9.37, 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Troades” 1173, etc.]], Epic dialect ἔκερσα [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 13.546 (ἀπο-, in tmesi), 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Supplices” 666 (Lyric poetry)]]: perfect κέκαρκα [Refs 2nd c.BC+ [“Sammelb.” 6002 (2nd c.BC), (περι-) 2nd c.AD: Lucianus Sophista “Symp.” 32]]:—middle, future κεροῦμαι [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Troades” 1183, (ἀπο-) 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Phaedo” 89b]]: aorist ἐκειράμἡν [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Lysias Orator 2.60, etc.]], Epic dialect ἐκερσάμην [Refs 4th c.BC+ [3rd c.BC: Callimachus Epicus “Fragmenta” 311, 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Persae” 953 (Lyric poetry):]] —passive, aorist 1 participle κερθείς[Refs 5th c.BC+ [(variant καρθ-) 5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “P.” 4.82:]]aorist 2 ἐκάρην [ᾰ] [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [“PSI” 4.368.45 (3rd c.BC)]], subjunctive κᾰρῇ [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 4.127,]]infinitive κᾰρῆναι, participle καρείς, [Refs 1st c.AD+ [2nd c.AD: Lucianus Sophista “Sol.” 6, 1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus “Lysander” 1]]: perfect infinitive κεκάρθαι [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 2.36]]: Attic dialect pluperfect ἐκεκάρμην [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd c.AD: Lucianus Sophista “Lex.” 5]]. (Cf. Sanskrit kṛṇā´ti 'wound', Latin caro: probably also O[Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus]] scieran, Eng. shear.):—cut short, shear, clip, especially of hair, σοί τε κόμην κερέειν (i.e. Σπερχειῷ) [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 23.146, compare 2nd c.AD: Pausanias Periegeta 1.37.3]]; κ. ἐν χρ [τὰς τρίχας] crop it close, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 4.175; ἀλόχων κείραντες ἔθειραν 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Helena” 1124 (Lyric poetry)]]: —more frequently in middle, cut off one's hair or have it cut off, as a sign of mourning (compare κουρά), τοῦτο.. γέρας οἶον ὀϊζυροῖσι βροτοῖσι, κείρασθαί τε κόμην βαλέειν τ᾽ ἀπὸ δάκρυ παρειῶν [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 4.198, compare 24.46, 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 23.46; πολύν σοι βοστρύχων πλόκαμον κεροῦμαι 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Troades” 1183; κείρομαι κόμαν [prev. author] “Ph.” 322 (Lyric poetry)]]: absolutely, cut off one's hair, κείρασθε, συμπενθήσατ᾽ [Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. author] “HF” 1390; ἐφ᾽ οἷς ἡ πόλις ἐπένθησε καὶ ἐκείρατο 4th c.BC: Aeschines Orator 3.211, etc.; ἄξιον ἦν ἐπὶ τῷδε τῷ τάφῳ κείρασθαι τῇ Ἑλλάδι 5th c.BC: Lysias Orator [same place]: Comedy texts, πρὸς φθεῖρα κείρασθαι]] to have oneself close shorn, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Eubulus Comicus 32]]:—passive, κουρᾷ.. πενθίμῳ κεκαρμένος [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Orestes” 458]]; σύμβολον κ. half-cropped, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Hermippus Comicus 14; τὰ ῥόδα κ. 5th c.BC: Pherecrates Comicus 108.29]]; also, of the hair, to be cut off, πλόκαμοι κερθέντες [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “P.” 4.82; βοστρύχους κεκαρμένους 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Electra” 515.]]

__2
crop a person, σφέας αὐτοὺς καὶ τοὺς ἵππους, in sign of mourning, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 9.24]]; κεκάρθαι τὰς κεφαλάς to have their heads shorn, [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [[prev. author] 2.36; Θρᾳκιστὶ κέκαρμαι 3rd c.BC: Theocritus Poeta Bucolicus 14.46; see at {χρώς} I.2, ἐγκυτί]]; shear sheep, μάχαιραι κουρίδες, αἷς κείρομεν τὰ πρόβατα καὶ τοὺς ποιμένας [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Cratinus Comicus 37]]; κείρεσθαί (tonderi) μου τὰ πρόβατα, ἀλλ᾽ οὐκ ἀποξύρεσθαι (deglubi) βούλομαι Tiber. cited in [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd-3rd c.AD: Dio Cassius Historicus 57.10 (compare below 3)]]; τὸ μὲν [καρῆναι] ἐπὶ προβάτων τιθέασι καὶ ἐπὶ ἀτίμου κουρᾶς [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [compare (2nd c.AD: Lucianus Sophista “Sol.” 6), κείρασθαι δὲ ἐπὶ ἀνθρώπων 2nd c.AD: Phrynichus Atticista 292]]; but τῶν Ἀργείων ἐπὶ πένθει καρέντων Plu.[same place]; τῷ σε χρὴ δρεπάνοισι καὶ οὐ ψαλίδεσσι καρῆναι [Refs 4th c.AD+ [“Anthologia Graeca” 11.368 (4th c.AD: Julianus Imperator Antec.).]]

__3
metaphorically, 'fleece', plunder, τὴν μάμμην [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [3rd c.BC: Herodas Mimographus 3.39.]]

__II
cut down, δοῦρ᾽ ἐλάτης κέρσαντες [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 24.450; ὕλην 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Trachiniae” 1196]]; crop close, opposed to ἐπιτέμνειν, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-3rd c.BC: Theophrastus Philosophus “de Causis Plantarum” 3.23.3]]; pluck, ἄνθη [Refs 5th c.BC+ [2nd-3rd c.AD: Philostratus Sophista “Vita Apollonii” 1.5: _metaphorically_, ἐκ λεχέων κ. μελιαδέα ποίαν 5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “P.” 9.37; Ἄρης κέρσειεν ἄωτον 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Supplices” 666 (Lyric poetry).]]

__II.2
ravage a country, especially by cutting down crops and fruit-trees, τὸ πεδίον [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 5.63; τέμενος [prev. author] 6.75, compare “OGI” 765.10 (from Priene)]]; τὴν γῆν [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 6.99, 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 1.64; χώραν 4th c.BC: Aeneas Tacticus 15.9]]; destroy, πόλιν [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [3rd c.BC: Callimachus Epicus “Fragmenta” 1.60]] P.; also, clear, of pioneers, ὄρος [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 7.131]]:—passive, of a country, to be ravaged, καρῆναι [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [[prev. author] 4.127, compare 8.65; κεκαρμένα κτήματα “SIG” 364.67 (Ephesus, 3rd c.BC):]] —middle, χθὼν πεύκας κειραμένη having its pine-trees cut down, [Refs 1st c.AD+ [Anthologia Graeca 9.106 (1st c.AD: Leonidas Alexandrinus Epigrammaticus); ἄρουραι λήϊα κειράμεναι 1st c.AD(?): Pseudo-Phocylidea 166: _metaphorically_, Σπάρτη.. ἐκείρατο δόξαν]] had her glory shorn off, epigram cited in [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd c.AD: Pausanias Periegeta 9.15.6]]; Ἄρης νυχίαν πλάκα κερσάμενος having had the plain swept clean (by destroying the men), [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Persae” 953 (Lyric poetry).]]

__II.3
ἔκειρε πολύκερων φόνον slaughtered many a horned beast by hewing, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Ajax” 55.]]

__II.4
hew, carve, ἐπίβασιν [Refs [“Inscription Cyprian dialect” 99 H.]]

__II.5
cut through transversely, opposed to σχίζειν (slit longitudinally), φλέβα [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd c.AD: Antyllus Medicus cited in 4th c.AD: Oribasius Medicus 7.11.3.]]

__III
generally, destroy, consume:

__III.1
tear, eat greedily, of beasts, κείρει τ᾽ εἰσελθὼν βαθὺ λήϊον [ὄνος] [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 11.560]]; of fish, δημὸν.. ἐπινεφρίδιον κείροντες [Refs [21.204]]; of vultures, ἧπαρ ἔκειρον [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 11.578, compare 2nd c.AD: Lucianus Sophista “DDeor.” 1.1, “DMort.” 30.1.]]

__III.2
metaphorically, waste, devour, ἐκείρετε πολλὰ καὶ ἐσθλὰ κτήματ᾽ ἐμά [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 2.312; ἔκειρον κτήματ᾽ ἐνὶ μεγάρῳ 22.369, etc.: _absolutely_, κείρετε (i.e. βίοτον) 1.378.]]

LSJ / STEPBible (TFLSJ)
κέλ-ευσμα
or κέλ-ευμα (see. below), ατος, τό, (κελεύω) order, command, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Eumenides” 235, 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Antigone” 1219 (_plural_)]], etc.; call, summons, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Choephori” 751 (_plural_)]]: in Prose, word of command in battle, [NT+5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 4.141, 7.16, compare 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Hecuba” 929 (Lyric poetry); ὁ Κύριος ἐν κ. καταβήσεται ἀπ᾽ οὐρανοῦ NT.1Thes.4.16]]; also, the call of the κελευστής (which see), which gave the time to the rowers, ἀπὸ ἑνὸς κελεύσματος all at once, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 2.92, 1st c.BC: Diodorus Siculus Historicus 3.15; ἐξ ἑνὸς κελεύματος 5th c.BC: Sophron Comicus 25]]; ἐκ κελεύματος at the word of command, [LXX+5th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Persae” 397, compare 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Iphigenia Taurica” 1405; καχάζετε.. ἀπὸ κ. 4th c.BC: Eubulus Comicus 8; στρατεύσονται ἀφ᾽ ἑνὸς κ. LXX.Pro.30.27]]; of the boatswain's pipe, κέλευσμα προσαυλεῖν [Refs 1st c.BC+ [1st c.BC: Philodemus Gadarensis Epigrammaticus “Mus.” p.15]] K.; also, the call of the driver to his horses, κελεύματι μόνον καὶ λόγῳ ἡνιοχεῖται [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Phaedrus” 253d]]; of the huntsman to his hounds, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Cynegeticus” 6.20; κ. κυνηγετῶν 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Ichn.” 225. Epic dialect imperfect κέλευον [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 23.767]]: future κελεύ-σω, Epic dialect infinitive - σέμεναι [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 4.274:]]aorist ἐκέλευσα, Epic dialect κέλ- [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 20.4]]: perfect κεκέλευκα [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Lysias Orator 1.34, 2nd c.AD: Lucianus Sophista “Demon.” 44]]:—middle, aorist ἐκελευσάμην [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Hippocrates Medicus “περὶ φύσιος παιδίου” 13: more frequently in compounds δια-, ἐπι-, παρα-κελεύομαι (which see)]]:—passive, future -ευσθήσομαι [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd-3rd c.AD: Dio Cassius Historicus 68.9]]: aorist ἐκελεύσθην [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 7.9.ά, 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Coloneus” 738, 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 7.70]]: perfect κεκέλευσμαι [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 8.3.14, 2nd c.AD: Lucianus Sophista “Sacr.” 11]]: pluperfect ἐκεκέλευστο [Refs 5th c.BC+ [2nd-3rd c.AD: Dio Cassius Historicus 78.4 (ἐκελεύθην variant in 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 7.9.ά, and κεκέλευμαι “IG” 22.1121.13 (4th c.AD), variant in 2nd c.AD: Appianus Historicus “Bella Civilia” 5.141 are later forms). (A lengthened form of κέλομαι, which see)]]:—properly urge, drive on, [ἵππους] ὁ γέρων ἐφέπων μάστιγι κέλευε.. κατὰ ἄστυ [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 24.326]]: hence, exhort, bid,

__1
c.accusative person et infinitive, order one to do, σ᾽ ἔγωγε.. κελεύω ἐς πληθὺν ἰέναι [Refs 5th c.BC+ [17.30, compare 2.11, +others, 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.8, 24, etc.]]; ἐκέλευσε τὸν παῖδα περιμεῖναί ἑ κελεῦσαι he bade the lad bid us to wait for him, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 327b]]; ὁ νόμος τὸν ἐπιβουλεύσαντα κελεύει φονέα εἶναι, i.e. bids that he be held guilty, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Antipho Orator 4.2.5; ὁ τὸν νόμον κελεύων ἄρχειν δοκεῖ κελεύειν ἄρχειν τὸν θεὸν καὶ τὸν νοῦν 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Politica” 1287a29; ἐς τὴν Μίλητον ἔπεμπον κελεύοντες σφίσι τὸν Ἀστύοχον βοηθεῖν 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 8.38]]; request, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Lysias Orator 16.16]]; opposed to ἐπιτάττειν, [Refs [“IG” 12.76.33.]]

__2
with accusative person et of things, σφῶϊ μὲν οὔ τι κελεύω [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 4.286; τά με θυμὸς.. κελεύει (i.e. εἰπεῖν) 7.68, etc.: with]]infinitive subjoined, τί με ταῦτα κελεύεις.. μάχεσθα; [Refs [20.87.]]

__3
with accusative person only, εἰ μὴ θυμός με κελεύοι (i.e. φείδεσθαι) [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 9.278; ὥς με κελεύεις (i.e. μυθεῖσθαι) 11.507: in Prose, ἐκέλευσε τοὺς ἕνδεκα ἐπὶ τὸν Θηραμένην]] ordered them [to go] against him, ordered them to seize him, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Historia Graeca (Hellenica)” 2.3.54; κ. τινὰς ἐπὶ τὰ ὅπλα [prev. work] 20]]:—passive, receive orders, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Politica” 1253b34.]]

__4
c.accusative of things only, ὃ μὴ κελεύσαι Ζεύς [Refs 4th c.BC+ [(2nd-3rd c.AD: Hermes Trismegistus for -σει) 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Eumenides” 618; ὁ νόμος τὰ μὲν κελεύων τὰ δ᾽ ἀπαγορεύων 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Ethica Nicomachea” 1129b24:]] — passive, τὸ κελευόμενον commands, orders, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 7.16, 5th c.BC: Antipho Sophista 61, 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 4.1.3: _plural_, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 340a.]]

__5
with dative person followed by infinitive, urge or order one to do, κηρύκεσσι.. κέλευσε κηρύσσειν.. [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 2.50, 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 2.6, etc.]]; ἀλλήλοισι κέλευον ἅπτεσθαι νηῶν.. [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 2.151; ἑτάροισι.. ἐκέλευσα ἐμβαλέειν 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 9.488: in later Prose, 1st c.BC: Diodorus Siculus Historicus 19.17, 1st c.AD: Cebes Philosophus 32.4 codices, 2nd c.AD: Lucianus Sophista “DMort.” 1.1, 3rd-2nd c.BC: Phalaris Epistolographus “Epistulae - Epistolographi” 121.1, etc.]]

__6
rarely with dative person et accusative of things, τί δ᾽ ἐστὶν ὃ κελεύεις ἐμο; [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-3rd c.BC: Menander Comicus “Περικειρομένη” 224, compare 2nd-3rd c.AD: Aelianus “De Natura Animalium - Ar.Byzantine Epit.” 9.1.]]

__7
with dative person only, ἵπποισι καὶ Αὐτομέδοντι κελεύσας [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 16.684; compareinfr. 111.]]

__8
absolutely, frequently in [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Homerus Epicus, ὡς σὺ κελεύεις 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 23.96, +others; λέξω, κελεύεις γάρ 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Choephori” 107]]; κελεύων, opposed to αὐτοχειρίῃ, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [3rd c.AD: Democritus Epigrammaticus 260; κελευούσης τῆς Πυθίης 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 6.36; κελεύοντος καὶ δεομένου 5th c.BC: Lysias Orator 5.1.]]

__9
with infinitive only, σιγᾶν κελεύω I order silence, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Philoctetes” 865; οὐκ ἂν κελεύσαιμ᾽ εὐσεβεῖν [prev. author] “Ant.” 731]]; recommend, propose, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Lysias Orator 12.25, 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 4.21, etc.]]; opposed to οὐκ ἐάω, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 6.109, 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Respublica Atheniensium” 2.18.]]

__II
of inferiors, urge, entreat, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 24.599, 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 10.17, 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.116.]]

__III
of the boatswain, give time to rowers, c.dative, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 396b: _absolutely_, 2nd c.AD: Athenaeus Epigrammaticus 12.535d.]]

__III.2
sing a chanty, [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd c.AD: Sextus Empiricus Philosophus “adversus Mathematicos” 6.24.]]

__(a) empty, vain: λόγοι, Eph.5:6; ἀπάτη, Col.2:8; κήρυγμα, πίστις, 1Co.15:14;

Oxon.” 3.356.18]]; but οἱ Αἰολεῖς.. οὐ λέγουσι κέννος Choerob.in [Refs [“Anecdota Graeca - MSS. Bibl. Oxon.” 2.242, cf. __I
mostly of things, empty, opposed to πλέως, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Equites” 280]]; opposed to πλήρης, [Refs [[prev. author] “Nu.” 1054]]; opposed to μεστός, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [4th-3rd c.BC: Diphilus Comicus 12; κενεὰς σὺν χεῖρας ἔχοντες 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 10.42; νοστήσαντας κεινῇσι χερσί 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.73; κεναῖς χερσίν 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Leges” 796b (see. below 11.2)]]; τὸ κ. (i.e. τάλαντον) the empty one, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Fragmenta” 488.5; κ. οἴκησις 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Philoctetes” 31; γῆ [prev. author] “OT” 55; εὐνή [prev. author] “Ant.” 424]]; χώματα κεινά, ={κενοτάφια}, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 9.85; κ. τάφος 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Helena” 1057]]; κατέθισαν ἐπὶ κενευϝῶν (i.e. τάφων genitive singular) [Refs 5th c.AD+ [“Schwyzer” [prev. cited] (5th c.AD: Cypria)]]; κ. χρόνος a pause in music, Anon.[Refs 1st c.AD+ [Bellerm. 83; σφυγμὸς κ. 1st c.AD: Agathinus Medicus cited in 2nd c.AD: Galenus Medicus 8.936]]; of wool and wine, uncertain meaning in [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd c.AD: Archigenes Medicus cited in 2nd c.AD: Galenus Medicus 8.945]]; τὸ κ. the void of space, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [3rd c.AD: Democritus Epigrammaticus 9, Meliss.[same place], 5th c.BC: Empedocles Poeta Philosophus 13, +others, 4th-3rd c.BC: Epicurus Philosophus “Epistulae” 1p.6U., etc.]]; τὸ κ., ={τόπος ἐστερημένος σώματος}, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Physica” 208b26, compare 213a13 ff., “Cael.” 279a13; κ. χώρα 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Timaeus” 58a]]; ἢν κενεὸν λάβῃ [ἡ διακοπή] if it penetrates the (brain-) cavity, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Hippocrates Medicus “Aph.”]][same place]; especiallyAstrology texts, not occupied by a planet, κ. δρόμος [Refs 4th c.AD+ [4th c.AD(?): Manetho Astrologus 2.452, compareVett. Val. 94.27]]; compare κενοδρομέω.

empty, fruitless, void, κενὰ εὔγματα εἰπών [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 22.249 (see. above)]]; ἐλπίς, ἐλπίδες, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Simonides Lyricus 5.16, 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Persae” 804; γνώμα 5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “N.” 4.40, compare 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Antigone” 753; ἔξοδοι [prev. author] “Aj.” 287; φροντίδες [prev. author] “fragment” 949]]; τέρψις[Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. work] 577; φόβοι 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Supplices” 548, compare 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 2.2.21; φρόνημα 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 494d, etc.; κ. πρόφασις καὶ ψευδής 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 18.150; λοιδορία κ. [prev. work]12; κενὸν ἆρα καὶ τὸ φάρμακον πρὸς τὸ κ. probably in 4th-3rd c.BC: Menander Comicus 530.19]]; ἀπόντων κενὴν κατηγορεῖν bring an idle charge, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “de Respiratione” 470b12]]; ineffectual, λύγξ [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 2.49]]; πουλυμαθημοσύνης, τῆς οὐ κενεώτερον ἄλλο Timo [same place]; πολλὰ κ. τοῦ πολέμου [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Ethica Nicomachea” 1116b7; κ. δόξαι 4th-3rd c.BC: Epicurus Philosophus “Sententiae” 15]]; ἐπιθυμίαι, opposed to φυσικαί, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. author] “Ep.” 3p.62U., 2nd c.AD: Diogenes Oenoandensis Epicureus 59; κ. ὀρέξεις 4th c.AD: Metrodorus Epigrammaticus “Herc.” 831.16; frequently in adverbial usages, _neuter_ _plural_, κενεὰ πνεύσαις 5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “O.” 10(11).93]]; ἡ διὰ κενῆς ἐπανάσεισις τῶν ὅπλων empty flourishing of arms, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 4.126]]; διὰ κενῆς ῥίπτειν throw without a projectile, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Problemata” 881a39]]; κεκλάγγω διὰ κενῆς ἄλλως to no purpose, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Vespae” 929; μάτην διὰ κ. 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Comicus 174.21; οὐ μαχοῦμαί σοι διὰ κ. 4th-3rd c.BC: Menander Comicus “Σαμία” 260; ἐν κενοῖς 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Ajax” 971; κατὰ κενῆς 5th c.AD: Proclus Philosophus “in Platonis Timaeum commentarii” 2.167 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator; εἰς κενόν 1st c.BC: Diodorus Siculus Historicus 19.9, 3rd c.AD: Heliodorus Scriptor Eroticus 10.30; εἰς κ. ἡ δαπάνη “IG” 14.1746; εἰς κ. μοχθεῖν 4th-3rd c.BC: Menander Comicus “Μονόστιχοι - Fragmenta Comicorum Graecorum” 51]]; κατὰ κενοῦ χανεῖν Suid. see at {λύκος ἔχανε; κατὰ κενοῦ φέρειν τὰς χεῖρας} [Refs 1st c.AD+ [1st c.AD: Philo Judaeus 1.153]]; κατὰ κ. βαίνειν, ={κενεμβατεῖν}, [Refs 1st c.AD+ [1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus 2.463c]]: regular adverb κενῶς, διαλεκτικῶς καὶ κ. __II

also κεραννύω [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Alcaeus Comicus 15, 4th c.BC: Hyperides Orator “Fragmenta” 69]]; Epic dialect κεραίω and κεράω (which see); subjunctive κεραννύω [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Philebus” 61b]]: imperfect ἐκεράννυν [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd c.AD: Lucianus Sophista “VH” 1.7:]]future κεράσω [ᾰ] [Refs 4th c.AD+ [4th c.AD: Themistius Sophista “Or.” 27 p]].340D.: aorist ἐκέρᾰσα [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Hippocrates Medicus “περὶ ἀρχαίης ἰητρικῇς” 3, (ἐν-) 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Cratylus” 427c, poetry κέρᾰσα 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Bacchae” 127 (Lyric poetry)]], Epic dialect κέρασσα [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 5.93]], Ionic dialect ἔκρησα [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Hippocrates Medicus “περὶ τῶν ἐντὸς παθῶν” 35]]:—middle, aorist ἐκερᾰσάμην [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-4th c.BC: Timaeus Locrus Philosophus 95e]], Epic dialect κεράσσατο [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 18.423:]] —passive, future κραθήσομαι [ᾱ] [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Epistulae” 326c, (συγ-) 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Ion” 406:]]aorist ἐκράθην [ᾱ] [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 6.5, 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Ion” 1016, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Phaedo” 86c]]; Ionic dialect ἐκρήθην [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Hippocrates Medicus “περὶ ἀρχαίης ἰητρικῇς” 19; ἐκεράσθην 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Philebus” 47c, “Ti.” 85a, 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 5.4.29, 3rd c.BC: Phylarchus Historicus 10J.]]: perfect κέκρᾱμαι [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “P.” 10.41, etc.]]; Ionic dialect κέκρημαι [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Hippocrates Medicus “περὶ ἀρχαίης ἰητρικῇς” 13, “Acut.” 21; κεκέρασμαι 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Fragmenta” 549, 1st c.BC: Dionysius Halicarnassensis “de Compositione Verborum” 24, “Anacreontea” 16.13, etc.]]: pluperfect ἐκέκρᾱτο [Refs 7th c.BC+ [7th-6th c.BC: Sappho Lyrica 51.1]]:—mix, mingle (different from μείγνυμι, see at {κρᾶσις}):

__1
mostly of diluting wine with water, κερῶντάς τ᾽ αἴθοπα οἶνον [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 24.364; κέρασσε δὲ νέκταρ ἐρυθρόν 5.93; κέρασον ἄκρατον 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Ecclesiazusae” 1123, compare 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 6.32: _absolutely_, τοῖς θεοῖς εὐχόμενοι κεραννύωμεν]] let us mix a cup of wine, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Philebus” 61b; ἂν μὴ κεράσῃ τις 4th c.BC: Antiphanes Comicus 85.2]]: with dative person, give to drink, ἐν τῷ ποτηρίῳ ᾧ ἐκέρασε κεράσατε αὐτῇ διπλοῦν [NT+8th c.BC+ [NT.Rev.18.6:— 8th c.BC: Homerus Epicus mostly in]]middle, ὅτε περ.. οἶνον.. ἐνὶ κρητῆρι κέρωνται mix their wine in the bowl, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 4.260, compare 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 20.253]]; κρητῆρα κεράσσατο he mixed a bowl, [Refs [3.393, 18.423]]:—passive, πῶς οὖν κέκραται [σκύφος]; [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Cyclops” 557]]; κύλιξ ἴσον ἴσῳ κεκραμένη a cup mixed half and half, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Plutus” 1132]]; κεκρ. τρία καὶ δύο [Refs 1st c.AD+ [[prev. author] “Eq.” 1187, compare “Anthologia Graeca” 11.137 (1st c.AD: Lucillius Epigrammaticus).]]

__2
temper, cool by mixing, θυμῆρες κεράσασα having mixed (the water) to an agreeable temperature, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 10.362.]]

__3
generally, mix, blend, ἡδονὴν φθόνῳ [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Philebus” 50a; τοῖς ὀνόμασι τὰ ῥήματα [prev. author] “Sph.” 262c; νοῦς μετ᾽ αἰσθήσεων κραθείς [prev. author] “Lg.” 961d, compare “Ti.” [same place]; πίστεως αἰσθήσει κεκραμένης 3rd c.AD: Plotinus Philosophus 4.7.15; ἀγωγὴν ἐξἀμφοῖν κ. 1st c.BC: Philodemus Philosophus “Academicorum Index” p.77 M.; [οὐσία] οὐκ ἀπὸ τῶν ἄκρων κραθεῖσα 4th c.AD: Julianus Imperator “Orationes” 4.139a]]; of metals, ἀργυρίῳ πρὸς χαλκὸν κεκραμένῳ χρῆσθαι [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 24.214]]: metaphorically, temper, regulate, of climates, ὧραι κάλλιστα κεκρημέναι most temperate, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 3.106; ὧραι μετριώτατα κ. 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Critias” 111e; ἔαρ κ. τῇ ὥρᾳ 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Cynegeticus” 5.5; [πλοῦτον] ἀρετᾷ κεκραμένον 5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “P.” 5.2]]; οὐ γῆρας κέκραται γενεᾷ no old age is mingled with the race, i.e.it knows no old age,[Refs 4th c.BC+ [[prev. work] 10.41, compare “O.” 10(11).104; ἐν ταῖς εὖ κεκρ. πολιτείαις 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Politica” 1307b30]]; of tempers of mind, ἤθει γεννικωτέρῳ κεκρᾶσθαι [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Phaedrus” 279a; τοῖς ἤθεσιν.. τούτοις ἡ φύσις κεράννυται 2nd c.AD: Alexander Rhetor 278b (iii p.744 K.)]]; of Music, ἁρμονίας ῥυθμοῖς κραθείσας [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Leges” 835b; τῆς εὖ κεκραμένης ἁρμονίας 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Politica” 1290a26; μετρίως κραθῆναι πρὸς ἄλληλα 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Phd.” [prev. cited]]]

__II
compound, ἐκ τῶν ἐπιτηδευμάτων τὸ ἀνδρείκελον [Refs [[prev. author] “R.” 501b; οὐκ ἀπίθανον λόγον [prev. author] “Phdr.” 265b]]; θεόσυτος ἢ βρότειος ἢ κεκραμέν; [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Prometheus Vinctus” 116; φωνὴ μεταξὺ τῆς τε Χαλκιδέων καὶ Δωρίδος ἐκράθη 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 6.5.]]

__III
Grammars, in passive, coalesce by crasis, τὸ ῥῆμα καὶ ὁ σύνδεσμος συναλοιφῇ κερασθέντα [Refs 1st c.BC+ [1st c.BC: Dionysius Halicarnassensis “de Compositione Verborum” 22.]]

__IV
multiply into, ὅταν ὁ τῆς δεκάδος λόγος τῷ τῆς ἑβδομάδος κερασθῇ [Refs [“Theologumena Arithmeticae” 50.]]

deep_entry:
Abbott-Smith / STEPBible (TBESG)
κέρας, -ατος
(pl. not irreg. as in Attic), τό, [in LXX chiefly for קָרַן ;]
a horn: Rev.5:6 12:3 13:1, 11 17:3, 7 17:12, 16; of the projections at the corners of the altar (Exo.29:12, al.): Rev.9:13. Metaphorical, as symbol of strength, κ. σωτηρίας (cf. Psa.18:3, al.): Luk.1:69.†
(AS)

---

LSJ / STEPBible (TFLSJ)
κέρᾰς, τό,
Epic dialect genitive Κέρᾰος, Attic dialect contraction κέρως; Epic dialect dative κέρᾰϊ (elided) or κέραι or κέρᾳ [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 11.385, cf. Hdn.Gr. 2.75, κέρᾳ also in 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 2.90, 7.6:]] nominative plural κέρᾱ (see. below), genitive κεράων, κερῶν, dative κέρασι, _Epic dialect_ κεράεσσι:—Attic dialect Inscrr. have dual [κέρ]ατε [Refs [“IG” 12.301.109: _plural_ κέρατα [prev. work] 237.59;]] later Epic dialect κεράατα ([music notation]) [Refs 8th c.BC+ [2nd c.BC: Nicander Epicus “Theriaca” 291, κεράατος ([music notation]) 4th-3rd c.BC: Aratus Epicus 174, 4th c.AD(?): Quintus Smyrnaeus Epicus 6.225; _dative_ κεράασι [musical notation] A.R.4.978::—Hdt.has _genitive_ κέρεος 6.111, _dative_ κέρεϊ 9.102: _plural_ κέρεα 2.38, κερέων [prev. work] 132; but 5th c.BC: Hippocrates Medicus has _genitive_ _sing._ κέρως, _plural_ κέρατα, “Aër.” 18. [In _nominative_ and _accusative_ κέρας, ᾰ always: in the oblative cases ᾰ in _Epic dialect_, as κέρᾰσιν 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 3.384 (in _contraction_ _dative_ κέρᾱ, _nominative_ _plural_ κέρᾱ compare (Batrachomyomachia 165)]], a is shortened before a vowel, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 11.385, 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 19.211)]]; but ᾱ in Trag.and Comedy texts, κέρᾱτος [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Hermippus Comicus 43, κέρᾱτα 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Bacchae” 921, κεράτων [ᾱ] probably in 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Trachiniae” 519 (Lyric poetry), κέρᾱσι 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Fragmenta - American Journal of Philology” 185. In later _Epic dialect_ the quantity varies.] (κέρας is probably related to κάρα]]; compare κεραός.)

__I
the horn of an animal, in [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Homerus Epicus]] mostly of oxen, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 17.521, etc.; ταῦροι.. εἰς κέρας θυμούμενοι 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Bacchae” 743]]; ὀφθαλμοὶ δ᾽ ὡς εἰ κέρα ἕστασαν his eyes stood fixed and stiff like horns, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 19.211]]; as a symbol of strength, [LXX+4th c.BC+ [LXX.Psa.17(18).3, 4th-5th c.AD: Diogenianus Paroemiographus 7.89, compare 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “de Partibus Animalium” 662a1]]; of elephants' tusks, [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd c.AD: Aretaeus Medicus “περὶ αἰτιῶν καὶ σημείων χρονίων παθῶν” 2.13, 3rd c.AD: Oppianus Apamensis Epicus “Cynegetica” 2.494.]]

__I.2
antennae of crustaceans, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Historia Animalium” 526a31, 590b27]]; of the silkworm's grub, [Refs [[prev. work] 551b10.]]

__II
horn, as a material, αἱ μὲν γὰρ [πύλαι] κεράεσσι τετεύχαται [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 19.563]]; the horn of animals' hoofs, [Refs 3rd c.AD+ [3rd c.AD(?): Longus Scriptor Eroticus 2.28.]]

__III
anything made of horn,

__III.1
bow, τόξον ἐνώμα.. πειρώμενος.. μὴ κέρα ἶπες ἔδοιεν [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 21.395, compare 3rd c.BC: Theocritus Poeta Bucolicus 25.206, 3rd c.BC: Callimachus Epicus “Epigrammata” 38, “Anthologia Graeca” 6.75 (6th c.AD: Paulus Silentiarius Epigrammaticus); for 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 11.385 see below variant]]

__III.2
of musical instruments, horn for blowing, σημῆναι τῷ κέρατι [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 2.2.4, compare 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “de Audibilibus” 802a17]]; also, the Phrygian flute, because it was tipped with horn [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [compare (2nd c.AD(?): Pollianus Epigrammaticus 4.74), αὐλεῖν τῷ κ. 2nd c.AD: Lucianus Sophista “DDeor.” 12.1; καὶ κέρατι μὲν αὐλεῖν Τυρρηνοὶ νομίζουσι 2nd c.AD(?): Pollianus Epigrammaticus 4.76, compare 2nd c.AD: Athenaeus Epigrammaticus 4.184a.]]

__III.3
drinking-horn, ἐκ τοῦ κέρατος αὖ μοι δὸς πιεῖν [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Hermippus Comicus 43, compare 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 7.2.23, “OGI” 214.43 (Didyma, 3rd c.BC)]]; ἐξ ἀργυρέων κ. πίνειν [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “Fragmenta.” 166, compare “IG” 12.280.77; ἀργυρηλάτοις κέρασι χρυσᾶ στόμια προσβεβλημένοις 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Fragmenta - American Journal of Philology” 185; ἐκπιόντι χρύσεον κ. 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Fragmenta” 483]]; for measuring liquids, [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd c.AD: Galenus Medicus 13.435.]]

__III.4
Ἀμαλθείας κ. cornucopiae, see at {Ἀμάλθεια}.

__IV
βοὸς κ. probably a horn guard or cover attached to a fishing-line, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 24.81, cf. Scholia; ἐς πόντον προΐησι βοὸς κέρας 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 12.253; ψάμμῳ κ. αἰὲν ἐρείδων “Anthologia Graeca” 6.230 (1st c.AD(?): Maecius Epigrammaticus), compare 3rd-2nd c.BC: Aristarchus Grammaticus cited in 2nd c.AD: Apollonius Biographus “Lex.” see {κέρᾳ ἀγλαέ}, 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus cited in 1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus 2.977a]] (also explained as a fishing-line of ox-hair (compare belowsee.l), cited in [Refs 1st c.AD+ [1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus 2.976f, compare 2nd c.AD(?): Pollianus Epigrammaticus 2.31]]; perhaps an artificial bait).

__IV.2
clyster-pipe, [Refs 4th c.AD+ [4th c.AD: Oribasius Medicus 8.32 7.]]

__IV.3
in plural, horn points with which the writing-reed was tipped, [Refs 1st c.BC+ [“Anthologia Graeca” 6.227 (1st c.BC-1st c.AD: Crinagoras Epigrammaticus).]]

__V
of objects shaped like horns,

__V.1
a mode of dressing the hair, κέρᾳ ἀγλαέ [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 11.385]] (unless the meaning be bow),[Refs 3rd c.BC+ [compare 3rd-2nd c.BC: Aristarchus Grammaticus (at [prev. work]), Herodorus and Apionap. 12th c.AD: Eustathius Episcopus Thessalonicensis (at [prev. work]): hence κέρας is explained as ={θρίξ} or κόμη, 2nd c.AD: Apollonius Biographus “Lex.”, Hdn.Gr. cited in Eust.[same place], 2nd c.AD(?): Pollianus Epigrammaticus 2.31, 5th c.AD(?): Hesychius Legal icographus]]; compare iv. l, and see at {κεροπλάστης}.

__V.2
arm or branch of a river, Ὠκεανοῖο κ. [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th-7th c.BC: Hesiodus Epicus “Theogonia” 789; Νείλου 5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “Fragmenta.” 201; τὸ Μενδήσιον κέρας 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 1.110; ἐν Ἰνδοῖς ἐν τῷ Κέρατι καλουμένῳ 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Mirabilia” 835b5, compare “Mu.” 393b5]]; τὸ κ. τὸ Βυζαντίων the 'Golden Horn', [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [1st c.BC-1st c.AD: Strabo Geographus 7.6.2, compare 2nd c.BC: Polybius Historicus 4.43.7, Scholia 3rd c.BC: Apollonius Rhodius Epicus 4.282]]; Ἑσπέρου K., name of a bay, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Hanno Geographus “Periplus - GGM” 14, compare 2nd-3rd c.AD: Philostratus Sophista “Vitae Sophistarum” 1.21.2.]]

__V.3
wing of an army, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 9.26, etc.; or fleet, [prev. author] 6.8, 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 2.90, etc.]]; κ. δεξιόν, λαιόν, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Persae” 399, 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Supplices” 704; τὸ εὐώνυμον κ. ἀναπτύσσειν 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 1.10.9.]]

__V.3.b
κατὰ κέρας προσβάλλειν, ἐπιπεσεῖν, to attack in flank, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 3.78, 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Historia Graeca (Hellenica)” 6.5.16, etc.]]; κατὰ κ. προσιέναι, ἕπεσθαι, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. author] “Cyr.” 7.1.8 and 28; κατὰ κ. συμπεσών 2nd c.BC: Polybius Historicus 1.40.14; πρὸς κ. μάχεσθαι 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 7.1.22.]]

__V.3.c
ἐπὶ κέρας ἀνάγειν τὰς νέας to lead a fleet in column, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 6.12, compare 14; κατὰ μίαν ἐπὶ κέρως παραπλεῖν 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 2.90, compare 6.32, 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 6.3.34, 4th c.BC: Eubulus Comicus 67.4]]; of armies, κατὰ κέρας, opposed to ἐπὶ φάλαγγος, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 1.6.43, compare “An.” 4.6.6, “HG” 7.4.23; εἰς κ. [prev. author] “Eq.Mag.” 4.3; ἐκ κέρατος εἰς φάλαγγα καταστῆσαι [prev. author] “Cyr.” 8.5.15]]; οὐκ ἐλᾶτε πρὸς τὸ δεξιὸν κ.; [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Equites” 243.]]

__V.4
corps of[Refs [8192]]men, ={διφαλαγγαρχία}, [Refs 1st c.BC+ [1st c.BC: Asclepiodotus Tacticus “Tact.” 2.6, 2nd c.AD: Arrianus Historicus “Tactica” 10.7.]]

__V.4.b
= {μεραρχία}, [Refs 1st c.BC+ [1st c.BC: Asclepiodotus Tacticus “Tact.” 2.10.]]

__V.4.c
contingent of thirty-two chariots, [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [[prev. work] 8, 2nd-3rd c.AD: Aelianus “Tactica - Griechische Kriegsschriftsteller” 22.2.]]

__V.5
sailyard, ={κεραία}, [Refs 1st c.BC+ [“Anthologia Graeca” 5.203 (1st c.BC: Meleager Epigrammaticus), “OGI” 674.30 (Egypt, 1st c.AD), 2nd c.AD: Lucianus Sophista “Am.” 6, “POxy.” 2136.6 (3rd c.AD).]]

__V.6
mountainpeak, variant in [Refs [“Hymni Homerici” 1.8]]; spur, τὸ κ. τοῦ ὄρους [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 5.6.7, compare 3rd c.BC: Lycophron Tragicus 534]]: in plural, extremities of the earth, γῆς [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd-3rd c.AD: Philostratus Sophista “Vita Apollonii” 2.18 (_plural_).]]

__V.7
in Anatomy, extremities of the uterus, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Hippocrates Medicus “περὶ ἐπικυήσιος” 1, 2nd c.AD: Galenus Medicus 7.266]]; of the diaphragm, [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd c.AD: Soranus Medicus 1.57.]]

__V.7.b
ἁπαλὸν κ., = {πόσθη}, [Refs 7th c.BC+ [7th c.BC: Archilochus Lyricus 171, compareNeophro (?) in “PLit.Lond.” 77 “fragment” 2.19, 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Fragmenta” 278, “Anthologia Graeca” 12.95.6 (1st c.BC: Meleager Epigrammaticus).]]

__V.8
of the πήχεις of the lyre, χρυσόδετον κ. [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Fragmenta” 244 (Lyric poetry)]] (rather than the bridge, because made of horn, [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd c.AD: Aelius Dionysius Grammaticus “fragment” 133, 2nd c.AD(?): Pollianus Epigrammaticus 4.62).]]

__VI
κέρατα ποιεῖν τινι to give him horns, cuckold him, proverbial in [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd c.AD: Artemidorus Daldianus Onirocriticus 2.11; compare κερασφόρος 11.]]

__VII
= {κερατίνης}, [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd c.AD: Lucianus Sophista “DMort.” 1.2.]]

__VIII
= {σταφυλῖνος ἄγριος}, [Refs 1st c.AD+ [1st c.AD: Dioscorides (Dioscurides) Medicus 3.52]]; ={οἰνάνθη}, uncertain in Ps.-[Refs 1st c.AD+ [1st c.AD: Dioscorides (Dioscurides) Medicus 3.120.]]

Abbott-Smith / STEPBible (TBESG)
κεράτιον, -ου, τό
(dimin. of κέρας),
__1. a little horn (Arist.).
__2. In pl. (the fruit of the κερατέα), carob-pods: Luk.15:16.†
(AS)

LSJ / STEPBible (TFLSJ)
κερᾱτ-ιον, τό,

[Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 9.18]]; κ. τοῖς ὅλοις πράγμασι, τῷ βίῳ, [Refs 2nd c.BC+ [2nd c.BC: Polybius Historicus 1.70.1, 5.61.4; τῷ ζῆν “PTeb.” 44.21 (2nd c.BC)]]: frequently with Preps., κ. ἐν τοῖς σώμασι [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Lysias Orator 2.63; οὐκ ἐν τῷ Καρὶ ἀλλ᾽ ἐν υἱέσι 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Laches” 187b (_passive_)]]; κ. περὶ [τῆς Πελοποννήσου] [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 8.74; περὶ τῆς ψυχῆς 5th c.BC: Antipho Orator 2.4.5, 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Plutus” 524; περὶ τοῦ σώματος 5th-6th c.BC: Andocides Orator 1.4; περὶ ἀνδραποδισμοῦ 5th-6th c.BC: Isocrates Orator 8.37; περὶ τῆς μεγίστης ζημίας 5th c.BC: Lysias Orator 7.15; περὶ τῆς βασιλείας πρὸς Κῦρον 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 15.24; περὶ αὑτῷ 5th c.BC: Antipho Orator 5.6; περὶ τοῖς φιλτάτοις 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Protagoras” 314a]]; but κ. περὶ δισχιλίους go into battle with a force of [Refs 5th c.BC+ [2, 000, 4th-5th c.AD: Eunapius Historicus “Fragmenta Historica - HGM” p.244 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator; ὑπὲρ καλλίστων 5th c.BC: Lysias Orator 2.79.]]

__3

[Refs [[prev. author] “Grg.” 485e]]: with future infinitive, uncertain in [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 4.117]]; κινδυνεύει impersonal, it may be, possibly, as an affirmatative answer, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Sophista” 256e, “Phdr.” 262c]]; out of courtesy, when no real doubt is implied, κινδυνεύεις ἀληθῆ λέγειν you may very likely be right, [Refs [[prev. author] “Smp.” 205d.]]

disturb, of a wasps' nest, τοὺς δ᾽ εἴ πέρ τις.. κινήσῃ ἀέκων [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 16.264]]; arouse, κ. τινὰ ἐξ ὕπνου [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Bacchae” 690]]; urge on, φόβος κ. τινά [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Choephori” 289]]; φυγάδα πρόδρομον κινήσασα having driven him in headlong flight, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Antigone” 109 (Lyric poetry)]]; κ. ἐπιρρόθοις κακοῖσιν attack, assail,[Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. work] 413; μήτηρ κ. κραδίαν, κ. δὲ χόλον 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Medea” 99 (_anapaest meter_); ἐάν με κινῇς καὶ ποιήσῃς τὴν χολὴν.. ζέσαι 4th c.BC: Anaxippus Comicus 2]]; κ. τινά incite or stir one up to speak, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 329e, “Ly.” 223a, 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Memorabilia” 4.2.2]]; κ. τὰ πολλὰ καὶ ἄτοπα stir up.. questions, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Theaetetus” 163a]]; call in question an assumption, τὰ μέγιστα κ. τῶν μαθηματικῶν [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “de Caelo” 271b11, compare 1st c.BC: Philodemus Philosophus “περὶ σημείων καὶ σημειώσεων” 27; κ. τὸ τὰ ἄκρα.. ἀνταίρειν 1st c.BC-1st c.AD: Strabo Geographus 2.1.12, compare 3rd c.AD: Plotinus Philosophus 2.1.6; ὁ κινῶν [τὰ φαινόμενα] λόγος 2nd c.AD: Sextus Empiricus Philosophus “adversus Mathematicos” 8.360]]:—passive, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Coloneus” 1526]]; κινεῖται γὰρ εὐθύς μοι χολή my bile is stirred, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Pherecrates Comicus 69.5; κεκινῆσθαι πρός τι 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Oeconomicus” 8.1.]]

__II.2
set going, cause, call forth, φθέγματα [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Electra” 18; πατρὸς στόμα [prev. author] “OC” 1276; μῦθον 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Electra” 302; λόγον περί τινος 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 450a; πάντα κ. λόγον [prev. author] “Phlb.” 15e; κ. ὀδύνην 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Trachiniae” 974 (_anapaest meter_); κακά [prev. author] “OT” 636; πάθος 1st c.BC: Philodemus Gadarensis Epigrammaticus “Mus.” p.4]] K.; πόλεμον, πολέμους, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 6.34, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 566e; Ἐμπεδοκλέα.. πρῶτον ῥητορικὴν κεκινηκέναι 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Fragmenta” 65.]]

__II.3
in Medicine texts, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [κ. οὔρησιν, οὖρα, 1st c.AD: Dioscorides (Dioscurides) Medicus 2.109, 127; κοιλίαν [prev. work]6.]]

__II.4
obscene meaning, κ. γυναῖκα [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Eupolis Comicus 233.3 (nisi to be read ἐβίνουν),compare 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Acharnenses” 1052 (variant), “Eq.” 364, “Nu.” 1103 (Lyric poetry, _passive_), +others, “Anthologia Graeca” 11.7 (from Nicander)]]; κ. τὰ σκέλεα [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [3rd c.BC: Herodas Mimographus 5.2.]]

__II.5
phrases: κ. πᾶν χρῆμα turn every stone, try every way, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 5.96]]; μὴ κ. εὖ κείμενον 'let sleeping dogs lie', [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Philebus” 15c]]; μὴ κίνει Καμάριναν, ἀκίνητος γὰρ ἀμείνων Oracle texts cited in [Refs 5th c.AD+ [5th c.AD(?): Stephanus Byzantius]]; κινεῦντα μηδὲ κάρφος 'not stirring a finger', [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [3rd c.BC: Herodas Mimographus 3.67, compare 1.55; μηδ᾽ ὀδόντα κινῆσαι [prev. author] 3.49]]; κ. τὸν ἀπ᾽ ἴρας πύματον λίθον 'play the last card', [Refs 7th c.BC+ [7th-6th c.BC: Alcaeus Lyricus 82 (assuming variant).]]

__II.6
in Law, πολιτικῶς κ. κατά τινος employ civil action against, [Refs [“Codex Justinianus [4th-6th c.AD]” 4.20.13.1.]]

__B
passive, to be put in motion, go, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 1.47]]; νηθεὶς ἐπῄει uncertain in [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “Fragmenta.” 101]]: generally, to be moved, stir, κινήθη ἀγορή, ἐκίνηθεν φάλαγγες, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 2.144, 16.280]]; of an earthquake, Δῆλος ἐκινήθη [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 6.98, 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 2.8; θύελλα κινηθεῖσα 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Coloneus” 1660]]; τί κεκίνητα; what motion is this? [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Andromache” 1226 (_anapaest meter_)]]; κινεῖσθαι, opposed to ἑστάναι, motion, opposed to rest, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Sophista” 250b, etc.]]; ὥσπερ χορδαὶ ἐν λύρᾳ συμπαθῶς κινηθεῖσαι vibrating in unison, [Refs 3rd c.AD+ [3rd c.AD: Plotinus Philosophus 4.4.8.]]

__B.2
of persons, to be moved, stirred, ὁ κεκινημένος one who is agitated, excited, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Phaedrus” 245b, compare 2nd c.AD: Vettius Valens Astrologus 45.25, +others; κ. παθητικῶς 1st c.BC: Philodemus Gadarensis Epigrammaticus “Rh.” 1.193 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus]]

__B.3
of dancing, κ. τῷ σώματι [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Leges” 656a.]]

__B.4
move forward, of soldiers, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Coloneus” 1371, 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Rhesus” 139, “Ph.” 107]]; but κ. ἐκ τῆς τάξεως leave the ranks, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Historia Graeca (Hellenica)” 2.1.22.]]

__B.5
to be disturbed or in rebellion, [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd-3rd c.AD: Dio Cassius Historicus 39.54, 42.15, +others]]

__B.6
κεκινημένος περί τι, Latin versatus in.., [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Leges” 908d.]]

κίνησις [ῑ], εως, ἡ,
motion, opposed to rest (στάσις), [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Sophista” 250a]]; opposed to ἠρεμία, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Physica” 202a5, etc.]]

__2
in Cyrenaic philosophical, λεία κ., ={ἡδονή}, τραχεῖα κ., ={πόνος}, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [3rd c.AD(?): Diogenes Laertius 2.86; also αἱ διὰ μορφῆς κατ᾽ ὄψιν ἡδεῖαι κ. 4th-3rd c.BC: Epicurus Philosophus “Fragmenta” 67]]; αἱ κ. αἱ ἀνθρωπικαί human emotions, [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd c.AD: Arrianus Historicus “Epicteti Dissertationes” 2.20.19.]]

__3
dance, Ἄρεος κίνασις (sic) [Refs 7th c.BC+ [7th c.BC: Tyrtaeus Elegiacus 16, compare 2nd c.AD: Lucianus Sophista “Salt.” 63, “Ephes.” 2 No.71; τραγικὴ ἔνρυθμος κ. “Inscription Magn.” 165.]]

__4
movement, in a political sense, ἐν κ. εἶναι [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 3.75, compare 2nd c.BC: Polybius Historicus 3.4.12]]; ἡ κ. ἡ Ἰουδαϊκή the Jewish revolt, [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [“OGI” 543.15 (Ancyra, 2nd c.AD)]]; of the Peloponn. war, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 1.1.]]

__5
change, revolution, κινήσεις πολιτείας [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Politica” 1268b25.]]

__6
movement of an army, [Refs 2nd c.BC+ [2nd c.BC: Polybius Historicus 10.23.1 (_plural_); πολεμικαὶ κ. 2nd-3rd c.AD: Aelianus “Tactica - Griechische Kriegsschriftsteller” 3.4, compare 2nd c.AD: Arrianus Historicus “Tactica” 20.1.]]

__6.b
removal, change of abode, [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd c.AD: Vettius Valens Astrologus 97.17 (_plural_), +others]]

__7
Grammars, inflexion, τοῦ ζῆμι κ. οὐχ εὕρηται [Refs [“Etymologicum Magnum” 410.38.]]

__8
in Law, punitive action, βασιλικὴ κ. [Refs [“Codex Justinianus [4th-6th c.AD]” 1.3.43.10]], compare 10.27.2.7; also, setting a process in motion, [Refs 6th c.AD+ [PLond. 5.1663.13 (6th c.AD).]]

LSJ / STEPBible (TFLSJ)
κλάδος [ᾰ], ου, ὁ,
branch, shoot of a tree, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “de Juventute” 468b25, “GA” 752a20]]; twig, opposed to ἀκρεμών, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-3rd c.BC: Theophrastus Philosophus “Historia Plantarum” 1.1.9, 1.10.7]]: generally, branch, τῆς ἐλαίης τοὺς κλάδους [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 7.19]]: presented by suppliants, ἐλαίας θ᾽ ὑψιγέννητον κλάδον [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Eumenides” 43, compare “Supp.” 22 (_anapaest meter_), 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Tyrannus” 3, 143]]; also of laurel branches used in temples, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Ion” 80.]]

__2
plank, [Refs 3rd c.AD+ [POxy. 1738.4, +others (3rd c.AD).]]

__3
branch of a blood-vessel, [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd c.AD: Galenus Medicus 15.141.]]

__4
metaphorically, ἀπὸ νώτοιο δύο κλάδοι ἀΐσσονται two arms, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Empedocles Poeta Philosophus 29.1.]]

__5
κ. ἐλέας, of a young girl, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [“epigram Gr.” 368.7:—metapl. forms, _dative_ κλαδί “Scol.” 9, probably in “SIG” 1025.33 (Cos, 4th-3rd c.BC)]]; τῇ κ. [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd-3rd c.AD: Aelianus “De Natura Animalium - Ar.Byzantine Epit.” 4.38 codices (compare 12th c.AD: Eustathius Episcopus Thessalonicensis 58.37); τῷ κ. 4th-5th c.AD: Choeroboscus Grammaticus “Scholia in Theodosii Canones” 1.138; _accusative_ κλάδα “Lyrica Adespota” 122]]; compare κλάδα[ν]· κλάδον, [Refs 5th c.AD+ [5th c.AD(?): Hesychius Legal icographus]]; genitive plural κλαδέων probably in [Refs 5th c.BC+ [3rd c.BC: Philoxenus Epigrammaticus 1.3; _dative_ _plural_ κλάδεσι 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Aves” 239 (Lyric poetry)]], Epic dialect κλαδέεσσι [Refs 2nd c.BC+ [2nd c.BC: Nicander Epicus “fragment” 74.19; _accusative_ κλάδας [prev. work]53.]]

deep_entry:
Abbott-Smith / STEPBible (TBESG)
κλαίω
[in LXX chiefly for בָּכָה ;]
of any loud expression of pain or sorrow, esp. for the dead, to weep, lament;
__(a) intrans.: Mrk.5:38-39 14:72 (M, Pr., 131) Mrk.16:10, Luk.7:13, 32 7:38 8:52, Jhn.11:31, 33 16:20 20:11, 13 20:15 Act.9:39 21:13, 1Co.7:30, Php.3:18, Jas.4:9 5:1, Rev.5:5 18:15, 19; πολύ, Rev.5:4; πολλά, Act.8:24 (WH, mg.); πικρῶς, Mat.26:75, Luk.22:62; opposite to γελάω, Luk.6:21, 25; χαίρω, Rom.12:15; before ἐπί, with accusative, Luk.19:41 23:28, Rev.18:9;
__(b) trans., with accusative of person(s), to weep or lament for, bewail: Mat.2:18.†
SYN.: see: δακρύω  (AS)

---

LSJ / STEPBible (TFLSJ)
κλαίω,
old Attic dialect κλάω (see. below) [ᾱ] never contracted; Aeolic dialect κλαΐω [Refs [“Lyrica Adespota” 65]]; Epic dialect 2nd pers. singular optative κλαίοισθα [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 24.619: _Attic dialect_]]imperfect ἔκλᾱον, Epic dialect κλαῖον [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 10.201]], Ionic dialect κλαίεσκον [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 8.364, 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 3.119, 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Fragmenta - American Journal of Philology” 312:]]future κλαύσομαι, 2nd pers. singular κλαύσῃ or κλαύσει, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 18.340, 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Vespae” 1327 (Lyric poetry), “Nu.” 58, 933 (_anapaest meter_), 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Cyclops” 554, etc., rarely κλαυσοῦμαι 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Pax” 1081, 1277 (in mock heroic verses)]]; Attic dialect also κλαιήσω [NT+4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Hyperides Orator “Dem.fragment” 10, κλᾱήσω 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 19.310, 21.99, later κλαύσω 3rd c.BC: Theocritus Poeta Bucolicus 23.34, 1st c.BC: Dionysius Halicarnassensis 4.70, NT.John.16.20, 4th c.AD(?): Manetho Astrologus 3.143:]]aorist ἔκλαυσα, Epic dialect κλαῦσα [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 3.261]]:—middle, aorist ἐκλαυσάμην [Refs 7th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Trachiniae” 153, “Anthologia Graeca” 7.412 (7th-6th c.BC: Alcaeus Lyricus Mess.)]]:—passive, future κλαυσθήσομαι [LXX+5th c.BC+ [LXX.Psa.77(78).64, κεκλαύσομαι 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Nubes” 1436]]: aorist ἐκλαύσθην [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [3rd c.BC: Lycophron Tragicus 831, 1st c.AD: Josephus Historicus “Antiquitates Judaicae” 8.11.1 (variant{κλαυθείς}), “IG” 14.2128]]: perfect κέκλαυμαι [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Choephori” 687, 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Tyrannus” 1490, κέκλαυσμαι 3rd c.BC: Lycophron Tragicus 273, 1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus 2.115b. [κλάω [ᾱ]]] is recognized as Attic dialect by [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd c.AD: Apollonius Dyscolus Grammaticus “de Adverbiis;” 187.26]], and is found in codices of [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Aves” 341, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Leges” 792a, “Phlb.” 48a: ἔκλᾰε in later poetry, 3rd c.BC: Theocritus Poeta Bucolicus 14.32, uncertain in 4th-3rd c.BC: Hermesianax Elegiacus 7.33 (compare κλέω A).] (κλᾰϝ-ψω, compare κλαυ-θμός, etc.)]]

__I
intransitive, cry, wail, lament, of any loud expression of pain or sorrow, κλαῖον δὲ λιγέως [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 10.201; πρὸς οὐρανόν 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 8.364; τῆς ἄρα κλαιούσης ὄπα σύνθετο 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 20.92]]; for the dead, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 19.297, etc.; ἀμφὶ δὲ σὲ Τρῳαὶ καὶ Δαρδανίδες κλαύσονται 18.340; κλαίοντα καὶ ὀδυρόμενον 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 388b, etc.]]; διὰ τί οἱ κλαίοντες ὀξὺ φθέγγοντα; [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Problemata” 900a20; δάκρυσι κ. 2nd-3rd c.AD: Dio Cassius Historicus 59.27]]; of infants, [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd c.AD: Soranus Medicus 1.107, +others]]; of crying for joy, κλαῖον δὲ λιγέως, ἁδινώτερον ἤ τ᾽ οἰωνοί κτλ. [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 16.216, compare 12th c.AD: Eustathius Episcopus Thessalonicensis 1799.57.]]

__I.2
αὐτὸν κλαίοντα ἀφήσω [Refs [1]] shall send him home crying, howling, i.e. well beaten, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 2.263: frequently in _Attic dialect_, κλαύσεται]] he shall howl, i.e. he shall suffer for it, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Vespae” 1327 (Lyric poetry), “Pl.” 174, +others; κλαύσομαι [prev. author] “Nu.” 58]]; κλαύσει μακρά you shall howl loudly, i.e. suffer severely, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. author] “Pax” 255, compare 1277; κλαύσῃ φιλῶν τὸν οἶνον 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Cyclops” 554; κλάοις ἄν, εἰ ψαύσειας 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Supplices” 925]]; κλαίων to your sorrow or loss, at your peril, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Tyrannus” 401, 1152, “Ant.” 754; κλάων ἅψῃ τῶνδε 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Heraclidae” 270, compare “Hipp.” 1086; δεῦρ᾽ ἔλθ᾽ ἵνα κλάῃς 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Nubes” 58]]; κλάειν ἔγωγέ σε λέγω (opposed to χαίρειν σοι λέγω) [Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. author] “Pl.” 62, compare 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 4.127; κλάειν εἴπωμεν 5th c.BC: Eupolis Comicus 363; κλάειν κελεύων Λάμαχον 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Acharnenses” 1131; κλάειν σε μακρὰ κελεύσας [prev. author] “Eq.” 433]]; σέ δ᾽ ἐᾶν κλάειν μακρὰ τὴν κεφαλήν suffer terribly in the head, [Refs [[prev. author] “Pl.” 612 (_anapaest meter_), compare “V.” 584.]]

__II
transitive, weep for, lament, κλαῖεν ἔπειτ᾽ Ὀδυσῆα, φίλον πόσιν [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 1.363, compare 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 20.210]]; τι [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Agamemnon” 890, 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Electra” 1117; τὰ αὑτοῦ πάθη 1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus “Alcibiades” 33]]:— passive, to be mourned or lamented, ἀνδρὸς εὖ κεκλαυμένου [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Choephori” 687: _impersonal_, μάτην ἐμοὶ κεκλαύσεται 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Nubes” 1436.]]

__II.2
cry for, of infants, μάμμας καὶ τιτθάς [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd c.AD: Arrianus Historicus “Epicteti Dissertationes” 2.16.39.]]

__III

__A.2
Geometry texts, deflect, inflect, usually of drawing a straight line 'broken back' at a line or surface, κλάσαι εὐθεῖαν τὴν ΑΓΒ ἐν λόγῳ τῷ δοθέντι [Refs 3rd c.AD+ [3rd c.AD(?): Pappus Mathematicus 904.17]]; ἀπὸ δύο σημείων τῶν B, E κλάσαι τὴν ΒΝΞΕ [Refs [[prev. author] 122.3]]:—more frequently in passive, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Analytica Posteriora” 1.c]].; ἡ κεκλασμένη (i.e. γραμμή) [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [[prev. author] “Ph.” 228b24; αἱ κλώμεναι εὐθεῖαι 3rd-2nd c.BC: Apollonius Pergaeus Geometra “Conica” 2.52]]; ἐὰν ἀπὸ τῶν σημείων κλασθῶσιν[Refs 3rd c.BC+ [[prev. work] 3.52; κεκλάσθω 3rd c.BC: Euclides Geometra 3.20, +others]]; of visual rays, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Meteorologica” 377b22, “Pr.” 912b29]]; of arteries, [Refs 1st c.AD+ [2nd c.AD: Galenus Medicus 9.84: generally, καμπαῖς κεκλασμένας ὑποπορεύσεις 1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus 2.968b; κεκλ. στολίδες [prev. work]64a; τὰ κλώμενα τῶν ῥευμάτων]] their broken courses, [Refs [[prev. work]747d.]]

(κλᾱϝῑς, cf. Latin clavis, claudo.)

__1
bar, bolt, θύρας σταθμοῖσιν ἐπῆρσε (i.e. Hera, from within) κληῗδι κρυπτῇ [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 14.168, compare 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 21.241; κληῗδος ἱμάς [prev. work] 4.802, compare 838; ἐπὶ δὲ κληῗδ᾽ ἐτάνυσσεν ἱμάντι 1.442]]; ={ἐπιβλής}, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 24.455.]]

catch or hook, passed through the door from the outside to catch the strap (ἱμάς) attached to the bar (ὀχεύς), ἐν δὲ κληῗδ᾽ ἧκε, θυρέων δ᾽ ἀνέκοπτεν ὀχῆας ἄντα τιτυσκομένη [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 21.47, compare 50; οἴξασα κληῗδι θύρας 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 6.89; δοιοὶ δ᾽ ἔντοσθεν ὀχῆες εἶχον ἐπημοιβοί, μία δὲ κληῒς ἐπαρήρει 12.456, compare 4th-5th c.BC: Parmenides Poeta Philosophus 1.14.]]

__3
later, key, τὴν κλεῖν ἐφέλκεται [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Lysias Orator 1.13]]; κλεῖν παρακλείδιον a false key, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Comicus 77: _plural_, κλῇδας οἶδα δώματος 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Eumenides” 827, compare 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Bacchae” 448; Λακωνικὴ κ. 4th-3rd c.BC: Menander Comicus 343; κυριεύσοντα τῶν κ. “OGI” 229.56 (Smyrna, 3rd c.BC)]]; of a sacred key carried in processions, [Refs 1st c.AD+ [“SIG” 900.14 (Panamara, 4th c.AD), 996.24 (Smyrna, perhaps 1st c.AD).]]

__4
metaphorically, Ἁσυχία βουλᾶν τε καὶ πολέμων ἔχοισα κλαῗδας [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “P.” 8.4, compare 9.39]]; ἔστι κἀμοὶ κλῂς ἐπὶ γλώσσῃ, of silence, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Fragmenta - American Journal of Philology” 316, compare 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Coloneus” 1052 (Lyric poetry); καθαρὰν ἀνοῖξαι κλῇδα φρενῶν 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Medea” 661 (Lyric poetry)]]; κλῇδας γάμου φυλάττει, of Hera, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Thesmophoriazusae” 976 (Lyric poetry)]]; of the key to a problem, [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd c.AD: Vettius Valens Astrologus 179.4.]]

hook or tongue of a clasp, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 18.294.]]

collar-bone, probably so called from its hook shape (see.[Refs 8th c.BC+ [above 1.2), 8th c.BC: Homerus Epicus (only in 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad”), ὅθι κληῒς ἀποέργει αὐχένα τε στῆθός τε 8.325; κληῗδα παρ᾽ ὦμον πλῆξ᾽, ἀπὸ δ᾽ αὐχένος ὦμον ἐέργαθεν ἠδ᾽ ἀπὸ νώτου 5.146; ᾗ κληῗδες ἀπ᾽ ὤμων αὐχέν᾽ ἔχουσι 22.324, compare 5th c.BC: Hippocrates Medicus “Aër.” 7, “Art.” 13; πᾳῖσον ἐμᾶς ὑπὸ κλῇδος 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Trachiniae” 1035; τὴν κλεῖν συνετρίβην 5th-6th c.BC: Andocides Orator 1.61; τὴν κλεῖν κατεαγώς 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 18.67: _plural_, 4th c.BC: Diogenes Cynicus Philosophus Apoll.6, etc.; τὰ πλάγια καὶ τὰς κλεῖδας 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Historia Animalium” 513b35; αἱ κλεῖδες (variant{κλεῖς}) καὶ αἱ πλευραί, of the crocodile, [prev. work] 516a28]]; κλεῖδες ὀπταί roast shoulder-bones of the tunny (with play on [Refs [1.3,]]visible keys, opposed to κρυπταὶ κλεῖδες of the Laconians), [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aristopho Comicus 7.2, compare 3rd c.BC: Diphilus Siphnius Rerum Naturalium Scriptor cited in 2nd c.AD: Athenaeus Epigrammaticus 8.357a.]]

rowing bench in a ship, frequently in [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey”,]] always in plural; ἐπὶ κληῗσι καθίζειν [Refs 8th c.BC+ [2.419, etc.; κληΐδεσσιν ἐφήμενοι 12.215; once in 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad”, πεντήκοντ᾽ ἔσαν ἄνδρες ἐπὶ κληῗσιν 16.170; δησάμενοι.. ἐπὶ κληῗσιν ἐρετμά 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 8.37.]]

__1. the belly (stomach or intestines or both): Mat.12:40 15:17, Mrk.7:19, Luk.15:16, Rom.16:18, 1Co.6:13, Php.3:19, Rev.10:9-10.
__2. (As often in LXX) the womb: Luk.1:41-42, 44 2:21 11:27 23:29, Jhn.3:4; ἐκ κ. μητρός (cf. Psa.22:11, Job.1:21, al.), Mat.19:12, Luk.1:15, Act.3:2 14:8, Gal.1:15.
__3. Metaphorical (as Heb. בֶּטֶן, cf. Job.15:35, Pro.20:27, Sir.19:12), of the heart: Jhn.7:38.†
(AS)

κοιλί-α,
Ionic dialect κοιλί-η, ἡ, (κοῖλος) cavity of the body, i.e. thorax with abdomen, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Hippocrates Medicus “περὶ ἄρθρων ἐμβολῆς” 46 (including ἡ ἄνω κ.]], = thorax, ἡ κάτω, = abdomen, accusative to [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd c.AD: Galenus Medicus 15.896)]]; τὰ κατὰ κ. νουσήματα diseases of the thoracic cavity, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Hippocrates Medicus “περὶ παθῶν” 6.]]

__2
belly, abdomen, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 2.87, “IG” 42(1).122.32 (Epid.), etc.: specified as ἡ κάτω κ. 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Ranae” 485, 5th c.BC: Hippocrates Medicus “περὶ ἑλκῶν” 3, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Timaeus” 73a, 85e, 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “de Somno et Vigilia” 456a3, “PA” 650a13, etc.]]; opposed to ἡ ἄνω κ., stomach, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Timaeus” 85e, 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “PA”]][same place]; κ. alone frequently = stomach, [Refs [[prev. author] “HA” 489a2, etc.]]; of birds, [Refs [[prev. author] “PA” 674b22]]; also, paunch or rumen of animals, [[prev. author] “HA” 507b5: hence, of gluttons, δουλεύειν τῇ ἑαυτῶν κ. NT.Rom.16.18, cf. NT.Phil.3.19.]

__3
intestines, κ. κείνη [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 2.40, compare 86, 92]], etc.; of animals, κ. ὑεία pig's tripe, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Equites” 356; κοιλίας ἥμισυ “SIG” 1025.51 (Cos, 4th-3rd c.BC)]]: plural, tripe and puddings, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Equites” 160, “Pl.” 1169.]]

__3.b
phrases, κ. σκληρὰν ἔχειν to be costive, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Theopompus Comicus 62.2; κατὰ κοιλίαν νοσεῖν “Comica Adespota” 730]]; τὴν κ. λύειν to relax the bowels, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Problemata” 863b29, 864b14]]; αἱ κ. λύονται, ἀναλύονται,[Refs [[prev. work] 947b13, “GA” 728a15]]; εὔλυτοί [εἰσι] [Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. author] “Pr.” 876b31; ἐὰν ἡ κ. στῇ [prev. author] “HA” 588a7; κ. καταρραγεῖσα 5th c.BC: Hippocrates Medicus “Κωακαὶ προγνώσιες” 126]]; [οἶνος] κοιλίας μαλακτικός, κοιλίας ἐφεκτικά, Mnesith. cited in [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd c.AD: Athenaeus Epigrammaticus 1.33b, 2.59c]]; κ. ἐκλύειν, ὑπάγειν, μαλάσσειν, [Refs 1st c.BC+ [1st c.AD: Dioscorides (Dioscurides) Medicus 2.72, 163, 171; κ. ῥέουσαι 1st c.BC: Diodorus Siculus Historicus 5.41.]]

__4
excrement, especiallyin plural, κ. συνεστηκυῖαι excrements of firm consistency, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Hippocrates Medicus “Aër.” 10; opposed to κ. ἐφυγραινόμεναι [prev. author] “Epid.” 1.10; κ. ὑγρή [prev. author] “Prorrh.” 1.38; στερεή, σκληρή, [prev. author] “Acut.(Sp.”) 56, “Epid.” 4.23; οὔρησις καὶ κ. ἀχρόως [prev. passage]]]

__II
any cavity in the body, ventricle, chamber, as in the lungs, heart, liver, brain, κ. αἱ τὸ πνεῦμα δεχόμεναι καὶ προπέμπουσαι [Refs 4th c.BC+ [[prev. author] “Art.” 41; ἡ δὲ καρδία ἔχει μὲν τρεῖς κ. 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Historia Animalium” 496a4, compare 513a27.]]

__II.2
socket of a bone, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Hippocrates Medicus “περὶ ἄρθρων ἐμβολῆς” 61.]]

__II.3
supposed cavities inside the muscles, [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [3rd c.BC: Erasistratus Medicus cited in 2nd c.AD: Galenus Medicus 4.375, 707, 2nd c.AD: Antyllus Medicus cited in 4th c.AD: Oribasius Medicus 8.6.30, 7.9.4]]; compare νηδύς.

__II.4
womb, [NT+5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Hippocrates Medicus “γυναικεῖα” 1.38, +others, NT.John.3.4.]]

__III
any hollow or cavity, in the earth, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Meteorologica” 349b4, 350b23, +others]]; in the clouds,[Refs [[prev. work] 369b2, +others]]

__IV
perhaps finger-tip, [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd c.AD: Aretaeus Medicus “περὶ αἰτιῶν καὶ σημείων χρονίων παθῶν” 1.8 (_plural_).]]

κοιμάω, -ῶ
[in LXX chiefly for שָׁכַב ;]
to lull to sleep, put to sleep. Mid and pass., to fall asleep (M, Pr., 162; M, Th., 1, 4, 13): Mat.28:13, Luk.22:45, Jhn.11:12, Act.12:6. Metaph, of death: Mat.27:52, Jhn.11:11 Act.7:60 13:36, 1Co.7:39 11:30 15:6 15:18 15:20 15:51, 1Th.4:13-15, 2Pe.3:4 (cf. Isa.14:8 43:17, 2Ma.12:45).†
SYN.: καθεύδω  (AS)

---

LSJ / STEPBible (TFLSJ)
κοιμ-άω,
future -ήσω, Doric dialect -άσω [ᾱ]: aorist ἐκοίμησα, Epic dialect κοίμησα [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 12.372]]:—middle, future -ήσομαι [Refs 1st c.BC+ [“OGI” 383.43 (Commagene, 1st c.BC), 1st c.BC: Dionysius Halicarnassensis 4.64, 2nd c.AD: Lucianus Sophista “DDeor.” 4.4, etc.: _Epic dialect_]]aorist κοιμήσατο, -αντο, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 11.241, 1.476]]:—passive, future -ηθήσομαι [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Fragmenta” 574.6, 2nd c.AD: Lucianus Sophista “Asin.” 40, 4th c.AD: Alciphro Epistolographus 1.37.3, etc.]]: aorist ἐκοιμήθην [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 14.411, +others, 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Andromache” 390, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 571e, etc.]]: perfect κεκοίμημαι [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aeschrio Lyricus 8.2, 2nd c.AD: Lucianus Sophista “Gall.” 6]]:—lull, put to sleep, κοίμησον.. Ζηνὸς ὑπ᾽ ὀφρύσιν ὄσσε φαεινώ [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 14.236; ἦ με.. κοιμήσατε νηλέϊ ὕπνῳ 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 12.372; βλέφαρα μὴ κοιμῶν ὕπνῳ 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Septem contra Thebas” 3]]; put to bed, τὸν δ᾽ αὐτοῦ κοίμησε [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 3.397]]; of a hind, ἐν ξυλόχῳ.. νεβροὺς κοιμήσασα [Refs [4.336.]]

__2
metaphorically, still, calm, ἀνέμους, κύματα, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 12.281, 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 12.169; φλόγα 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Agamemnon” 597; κύματος μένος [prev. author] “Eu.” 832; εὔφημον.. κοίμησον στόμα [prev. author] “Ag.” 1247]]; also, soothe, assuage, κοίμησον δ᾽ ὀδύνας [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 16.524]]; ᾧ (i.e. φύλλῳ) κοιμῶ τόδ᾽ ἕλκος [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Philoctetes” 650.]]

__II
middle and passive, fall asleep, go to bed, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 1.476, +others, 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.9, etc.]]; of animals, lie down, κατὰ ἤθεα κοιμηθῆναι [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 14.411: with _accusative_ _cognate_, ποῖόν τινα ὕπνον ἐκοιμ; 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Hiero” 6.7]]; βαθὺν κοιμηθῆναι (i.e. ὕπνον) [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd c.AD: Lucianus Sophista “DMar.” 2.3.]]

__II.2
metaphorically, ὅπως ἂν κοιμηθῇ [τὸ ἐπιθυμητικόν] [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus [prev. cited]]]

__II.3
of the sleep of death, κοιμήσατο χάλκεον ὕπνον [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 11.241; ἱερὸν ὕπνον κ. Callias Epigrammaticus “Ep.” 11.2]]: absolutely, fall asleep, die, [NT+5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Electra” 509 (Lyric poetry), 4th c.BC: Aeschrio Lyricus [same place]; ἐκοιμήθη μετὰ τῶν πατέρων LXX.3Ki.2.10, +others, compare “PFay.” 22.28 (1st c.AD), NT.Matt.27.52, NT.John.11.11, etc.; in epitaphs, “IG” 14.1683, etc.; κ. τὸν αἰώνιον ὕπνον [prev. work]929.]]

__II.4
κοιμῶντο.. παρὰ μνηστῇς ἀλόχοισι [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 6.246, compare 250]]: hence, of sexual intercourse, lie with another, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 8.295, 5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “I.” 8(7).23; οὔ τινι κοιμηθεῖσα 8th-7th c.BC: Hesiodus Epicus “Theogonia” 213; παρά τινι 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 3.68; σὺν δεσπόταισι 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus [same place]; μετά τινος 4th c.BC: Timocles Comicus 22.2; ἀπὸ γυναικὸς ἀνὴρ τὰν νύκτα κοιμαθές “Berl.Sitzb.” 1927.157 (from Cyrene).]]

__II.5
keep watch at night, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Agamemnon” 2, 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 1.2.4, 9, “POxy.” 933.25 (2nd c.AD), etc.]]

__II.6
of things, remain during the night, οὐ μὴ κοιμηθήσεται ὁ μισθὸς παρά σοι ἕως πρωί [LXX.Lev.19.13]; ἡ κιβωτὸς ἐκοιμήθη ἐκεῖ[LXX.Josh.6.10.]

__II.7
with accusative, dream of, μέταλλα χρύσεια [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd c.AD: Lucianus Sophista “Gall.” 6.]]

κοινός, -ή, -όν
[in LXX: Pro.1:14 (אֶחָד) Pro.21:9 25:24 (חֶבֶר), Wis.7:3, al. ;]
__1. common (general; = Lat. communis): Act.2:44 4:32; κ. πίστις, Tit.1:4; σωτηρία, Ju 3
__2. common (ordinary; = vulgaris); hence in LXX (1Ma.1:47, al.) and NT, unhallowed, unclean (cl., βέβηλος, which see): Mrk.7:2, 5, Act.10:14, 28 11:8, Rom.14:14, Heb.10:29, Rev.21:27.†
(AS)
