κοινός, ή, όν,
also ός, όν [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Trachiniae” 207 (Lyric poetry)]]:— common (opposed to ἴδιος), not in [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Homerus Epicus (see. ξυνός)]]; ἐκ κοινοῦ shared in common, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th-7th c.BC: Hesiodus Epicus “Opera et Dies” 723; ἔσται γὰρ βίος ἐκ κ. 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Ecclesiazusae” 610]]; of a common altar, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Simonides Lyricus 140; τὸ τέμενος εἶναι κ. “SIG” 1044.29 (Halic., 4th-3rd c.BC)]]; κ. ἔρχεται κῦμ᾽ Ἀΐδα [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “N.” 7.30]]; τρεῖς.. κ. ὄμμ᾽ ἐκτημέναι, of the Gorgons, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Prometheus Vinctus” 795]]; κ. ὠφέλημα θνητοῖσιν φανείς, of Prometheus,[Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. work] 613; τὰς γυναῖκας εἶναι κοινάς 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 457d: proverbial, κοινὸν τύχη 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Fragmenta - American Journal of Philology” 389, compare 4th-3rd c.BC: Menander Comicus “Μονόστιχοι - Fragmenta Comicorum Graecorum” 356; κοινὰ τὰ τῶν φίλων 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Orestes” 735 (troch.), 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Phaedrus” 279c, 4th-3rd c.BC: Menander Comicus 9, etc.]]; κ. Ἑρμῆς 'share the luck', [Refs [[prev. author] “Epit.” 67, 100]]; κ. ἀρωγά common aid (i.e. for all), [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Philoctetes” 1145 (Lyric poetry)]]; ἐν δὲ κοινὸς ἀρσένων ἴτω κλαγγά and let the shouts of males rise jointly, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. author] “Tr.” 207 (Lyric poetry); κ. πόλεμον πολεμεῖν 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Hiero” 2.8; τὸν ἀέρα τὸν κ. 4th-3rd c.BC: Menander Comicus 531.8; κ. τὸν ᾅδην ἔσχον οἱ πάντες βροτοί [prev. author] 538.8; κ. ἀγαθὸν τοῦτ᾽ ἐστί, χρηστὸς εὐτυχῶν [prev. author] 791: with _dative_, κ. τινί]] common to or with another, ὑμῖν φῶς.. καὶ τοῖσδ᾽ ἅπασι κ. [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Agamemnon” 523; ὁ δαίμων κ. ἦν ἀμφοῖν ἅμα [prev. author] “Th.” 812; θάλατταν κ. ἐᾶν τοῖς ἡττημένοις 5th-6th c.BC: Andocides Orator 3.19; οἰκία.. κοινοτάτη ἀεὶ τῷ δεομένῳ [prev. author] 1.147]]; [πολιτεία] τίς κοινοτάτ; [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Politica” 1289b14, compare 1265b29; κοινόν τι χαρᾷ καὶ λύπῃ δάκρυα 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Historia Graeca (Hellenica)” 7.1.32; τὸν ἥλιον τὸν κ. ἡμῖν 4th-3rd c.BC: Menander Comicus 611: with _genitive_, πάντων αἰθὴρ κ. φάος εἱλίσσων 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Prometheus Vinctus” 1092 (_anapaest meter_), compare “Pers.” 132 (Lyric poetry), “Eu.” 109, 5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “N.” 1.32]]; κ. τῶν Λακεδαιμονίων τε καὶ Ἀθηναίων shared in by both.., [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Menexenus” 241c, etc.: with Preps., τὸ ἐπὶ πᾶσι κ.]], see below see; κ. κατ᾽ ἀμφοτέρων [Refs 1st c.AD+ [2nd c.AD: Apollonius Dyscolus Grammaticus “de Syntaxi;” 144.19; οὐ γίγνεταί μοί τι κ. πρός τινα “Anthologia Graeca” 11.141 (1st c.AD: Lucillius Epigrammaticus), compare 4th c.AD: Iamblichus Philosophus “de Mysteriis” 5.7]]; μέρος κ. πρός τινα shared with.., [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [“CPR” 22.11 (2nd c.AD)]], etc.; κ. μεταξύ τινων [Refs 5th c.AD+ [“Stud.Pal.” 1.7 ii 11 (5th c.AD).]]

__II
in social and political relations, public, general, τὸ κ. ἀγαθόν the common weal, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 5.90; κ. λόγῳ [prev. author] 5.37, 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.141]]; κ. στόλῳ[Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. work] 170; ἀδικήματα 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 21.45; ὁ τῆς πόλεως κ. δήμιος 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Leges” 872b]]; κοινότατον of public or general interest,[Refs 4th c.BC+ [[prev. work] 724b, compare 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Rhetorica” 1354b29]]; of constitutions, popular, free, κοινοτέραν εἶναι τὴν ἐκείνου μοναρχίαν τῆς αὑτῶν δημοκρατίας [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Isocrates Orator 10.36.]]

__II.2
τὸ κ. the state, τὸ κ. Σπαρτιητέων [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.67: _absolutely_, of one's own state, 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Ecclesiazusae” 208, etc.; τὸ κ. ὠφελεῖται 5th c.BC: Antipho Orator 3.2.3, compare 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 2.2.20; τὰς ὠφελείας ἅπασιν εἰς τὸ κ. ἀπεδίδου 5th-6th c.BC: Isocrates Orator 10.36.]]

__II.2.b
especially of leagues or federations, τὸ κ. τῶν Ἰώνων [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 5.109; τῶν συμμάχων 5th-6th c.BC: Isocrates Orator 14.21; τῶν Βοιωτῶν “SIG” 457.10 (Thespiae, 3rd c.BC), 2nd c.BC: Polybius Historicus 20.6.1 (_plural_)]], etc.; ἄνευ τοῦ πάντων κοινοῦ (i.e. τῶν Θεσσαλῶν) [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 4.78]]; also, of private associations, [Refs [Test.Epict. 1.22, “SIG” 1113 (from Loryma), +others]]; of guilds or corporations, τὸ κ. τῶν τεκτόνων [Refs 4th c.AD+ [“POxy.” 53.2 (4th c.AD)]]; of boards of magistrates, τὸ κ. τῶν ἀρχόντων [Refs 3rd c.AD+ [[prev. work] 54.12 (3rd c.AD).]]

__II.2.c
the government, public authorities, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 1.90, 2.12, etc.; τὰ κ. 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 3.156; ἀπαγγεῖλαι ἐπὶ τὰ κ. 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 5.37]]; ἀπὸ τοῦ κ. by public authority, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 5.85, 8.135]]; σὺν τῷ κ. by common consent, [Refs [[prev. author] 9.87.]]

__II.2.d
the public treasury, χρημάτων μεγάλων ἐν τῷ κ. γενομένων [Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. author] 7.144; ἐν τῷ κ. καὶ ἐν τοῖς ίεροῖς 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 6.6, compare 17; χρήματα δοῦναι ἐκ τοῦ κ. 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 9.87]]; ἔχειν ἐν κοινῷ (without the Article), [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 1.80, cf. Scholia (at [prev. work])]]

__II.2.e
common right or rights of citizens, τὸ κ. τὸ τῶν πολιτῶν [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Politica” 1283b41.]]

__II.3
τὰ κ. public affairs: πρὸς τὰ κ. προσελθεῖν, προσιέναι, to enter public life, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 18.257, 4th c.BC: Aeschines Orator 1.165]]; but also, the public money, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Plutus” 569, 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 8.23 (in full, τὰ κ. χρήματα 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Historia Graeca (Hellenica)” 6.5.34, 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Politica” 1271b11)]]; τὰ κ. τῆς πόλεως, opposed to τὰ ἁγνά, [Refs [“BMus.Inscription” 4.481]]*.383; ἀπὸ κοινοῦ at the public expense, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 4.7.27, 5.1.12; ἐκ κοινοῦ φαγεῖν 3rd c.BC: Euphro Comicus 8.4, compare 4th c.BC: Antiphanes Comicus 230]]; ἐκ κ. from common funds, at joint expense, [Refs 2nd c.BC+ [PGrenf. 1.21.19 (2nd c.BC).]]

__III

Ind.” p.53 M.]]

[Refs 2nd c.BC+ [Scholia 2nd c.BC: Dionysius Thrax Grammaticus p.14 H., compare 1st c.BC: Diodorus Siculus Historicus 1.16, 4th c.AD(?): Theodosius Alexandrinus Grammaticus “Canones - Grammatici Graeci, pars” p.37]] H., etc.; ἡ κ. alone, [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd c.AD: Apollonius Dyscolus Grammaticus “de Conjunctionibus;” 223.24]]; τὸ κ. ἔθος, ἡ κ. ἐκφορά, [Refs [[prev. author] “Adv.” 155.10, “Pron.” 4.27]]; οἱ κ. the writers who use this language,[Refs [Scholia 2nd c.BC: Dionysius Thrax Grammaticus p.469 H., “Etymologicum Magnum” 405.23.]]

in magical formulae, of words added at will by the user, 'and so forth', frequently in Papyrus, [Refs [“PMag.Osl.” 1.255, “PMag.Par.” 1.273, +others; κοινὰ ὅσα θέλεις [prev. work]2.53; ὁ κ. λόγος “PMag.Lond.” 46.435]]; compare κοινολογία.

Χάριτες [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “O.” 2.50.]]

Grammars,

κ. συλλαβή common syllable, capable of being long or short, [Refs 2nd c.BC+ [2nd c.BC: Dionysius Thrax Grammaticus 633.17, 7th c.AD: Hephaestio Grammaticus 1.4.]]

see.above[Refs [111.2.]]

of gender, κ. γένος [Refs 2nd c.BC+ [2nd c.BC: Dionysius Thrax Grammaticus 634.19]]; of nouns, [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd c.AD: Apollonius Dyscolus Grammaticus “de Pronominibus;” 30.7, +others, “Etymologicum Magnum” 143.33, 305.19, etc.]]

ἀπὸ κοινοῦ λαμβάνειν, of two clauses taking a word in common, [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd c.AD: Apollonius Dyscolus Grammaticus “de Syntaxi;” 122.14, +others; κοινὸν or ἐκ κοινοῦ παραλαμβάνεσθαι, [prev. work] 20, 28, +others]]

__VIII
κοινόν, τό, name of an eye-salve, [Refs [“CIL” 13.10021.3, +others]]

__B
adverb κοινῶς in common, jointly, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Ion” 1462; τὰ κοινὰ κ. δεῖ φέρειν συμπτώματα 4th-3rd c.BC: Menander Comicus 817: _comparative_, ἐν Κρήτῃ -οτέρως [ἔχει τὰ τῶν συσσιτίων] 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Politica” 1272a16.]]

feminine dative κοινῇ; Doric dialect κοινᾷ [Refs 5th c.BC+ [“SIG” 56.11 (Argos, 5th c.BC)]]; Boeotian dialect κυνῆ [Refs 2nd c.BC+ [[prev. work]635.31 (Acraeph., 2nd c.BC)]]:—in common, by common consent, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.148, 3.79, 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Tyrannus” 606, “OC” 1339, 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Hippolytus” 731, 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 1.3, etc.; κ. πᾶσι καὶ χωρίς 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Politica” 1278b23, compare “Ath.” 40.3]]; κ. μετά τινος, κ. σύν τινι, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Symposium” 209c, “SIG” 346.27 (4th c.BC), 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Memorabilia” 1.6.14, etc.; ἰδίᾳ τε καὶ κ. 2nd c.AD: Alexander Rhetor 291: also _neuter_ _plural_ κοινά 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Antigone” 546.]]

publicly, καὶ κ. καὶ ἰδίᾳ [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Historia Graeca (Hellenica)” 1.2.10, “Mem.” 2.1.12, etc.]]

__B.II.3
as preposition with dative, together with, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Ion” 1228, “Hel.” 829, “fragment” 823.]]

__B.III
with Preps., εἰς κοινόν in common, in public, ὑμῖν τῇδέ τ᾽ ἐς κ. φράσω [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Prometheus Vinctus” 844; πᾶσιν ἐς κ. λέγω [prev. author] “Eu.” 408, compare 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Aves” 457 (Lyric poetry), 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Leges” 796e; εἰς κ. γνώμην ἀποφαίνεσθαι 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 19.156]]; εἰς τὸ κ. λέγειν, ἀγορεύειν, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Theaetetus” 165a, 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 5.6.27]]; εἰς τὸ κ. for public use, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Leges” 681c.]]

ἀφεῖσαν ἐν κοινῷ ζητεῖν, Latin rem in medio reliquerunt, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Metaphysica” 987b14]]; but οἱ ἐν κ. γιγνόμενοι λόγοι, ={οἱ ἐξωτερικοὶ λόγοι}, [Refs [[prev. author] “de An.” 407b29.]]

κοσμέω, -ῶ
(κόσμος), [in LXX for עָדָה, תָּקַן, etc. ;]
__1. to order, arrange, prepare (in Hom. esp. of marshalling armies): Mat.25:7 (cf.  Sir.50:9, al.).
__2. to adorn, furnish: οἶκον, pass., Mat.12:44, Luk.11:25; μνημεῖα, Mat.23:29; τὸ ἱερόν, pass., Luk.21:5; θεμέλιοι, Rev.21:19; νύμφην, pass., Rev.21:2; ἐαυτάς, before ἐν, 1Ti.2:9. Metaphorical, with accusative of person(s), 1Pe.3:5; with accusative of thing(s), Tit.2:10.†
(AS)

---

LSJ / STEPBible (TFLSJ)
κοσμ-έω,
order, arrange, especially set an army in array, marshal it, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 14.379; κοσμῆσαι ἵππους τε καὶ ἀνέρας 2.554]]:—passive, ἐπεὶ κόσμηθεν ἅμ᾽ ἡγεμόνεσσιν ἕκαστοι [Refs [3.1]]; πένταχα κοσμηθέντες marshalled in five bodies, [Refs [12.87]]; of a population, διὰ τρίχα κοσμηθέντες [Refs 8th c.BC+ [2.655; once in 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey”, of hunters, διὰ δὲ τρίχα κοσμηθέντες 9.157:]] —middle, κοσμησάμενος πολιήτας having arranged his men, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 2.806]]; so after Homer, κ. στρατόν (variant for{κοιμήσων}) [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Rhesus” 662; τάξεις κεκοσμημέναι 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 2.1.26, compare 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Phaedrus” 247a; ἐπὶ τάξις πλεῦνας ἐκεκοσμέατο 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 9.31.]]

__2
generally, arrange, prepare, δόρπον ἐκόσμει [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 7.13; κ. ἀοιδήν η “Bacch.” 59; ἔργα 8th-7th c.BC: Hesiodus Epicus “Opera et Dies” 306; στέφανον 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Hippolytus” 74; τράπεζαν 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 8.2.6; εἰς τάφον λέβητα 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Electra” 1401]]:—passive, δεῖπνον κεκόσμηται [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “N.” 1.22]]; δεῖ οὕτω κοσμηθῆναι ὅκως.. [Refs 3rd c.AD+ [3rd c.AD: Democritus Epigrammaticus 266]]; τὸ κοσμηθὲν αἷμα, ={τὸνοἰκεῖον κόσμον κτησάμενον}, [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd c.AD: Galenus Medicus 5.551.]]

__II
order, rule, τὴν πόλιν κ. καλῶς τε καὶ εὖ [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.59, compare 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Ajax” 1103; Σπάρτην ἔλαχες, κείνην κόσμει 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Fragmenta” 723 (_anapaest meter_)]]; κ. ἐμαυτόν restrain myself, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. author] “Hyps.fragment” 34(60).46; τὰ ἄλλα ἐκεκοσμέατό οἱ 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.100; τόν γε νοῦν κοσμοῦντα πάντα κοσμεῖν 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Phaedo” 97 c:]] —passive, τὰ κοσμούμενα orderly institutions, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Antigone” 677]]: perfect participle, of persons, orderly, ταπεινὸς καὶ κεκοσμημένος [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Leges” 716a; τεταγμένον τε καὶ κ. πρᾶγμα [prev. author] “Grg.” 504 a.]]

__II.2
in Crete, hold office of κόσμος [Refs 4th c.BC+ [111, οἱ κεκοσμηκότες 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Politica” 1272a35, compare 2nd c.BC: Polybius Historicus 22.15.1]]; Cretan dialect κοσμίω [Refs [“Leg.Gort.” 1.51, etc.]]; also κορμίω (which see).

__III
adorn, equip, dress, especially of women, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [“Hymni Homerici” 6.11, 8th-7th c.BC: Hesiodus Epicus “Opera et Dies” 72; κοσμῆσαί τινα πανοπλίῃ 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 4.180; τριπόδεσσι κ. δόμον 5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “I.” 1.19; τινὰ πλούτῳ ὑπερβάλλοντι 2nd c.AD: Herodianus Grammaticus 3.10.6: with double _accusative_, πρίν σε νυμφικὸν ἰστέφανον κοσμήσαμεν “JRS” 17.51 (Phrygia, 4th c.AD):—frequently in]]middle, κοσμέεσθαι τὰς κεφαλάς to adorn their heads, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 7.209; κοσμεῖσθαι σῶμα ὅπλοις 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Phoenissae” 1359]]; ἐν φοινικίσι κοσμησάμενοι having decked themselves who roasts [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Comicus 208]]:—passive, χρυσῷ κοσμηθεῖσα [Refs 7th c.BC+ [“hymnus ad Venerem” 65; παῖσα δ᾽ Ἄρῃ κεκόσμηται στέγα 7th-6th c.BC: Alcaeus Lyricus 15.1; ἵπποι κεκοσμημένοι ὡς κάλλιστα 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 7.40; κεκ. ἐσθῆτι ποικίλῃ καὶ χρυσοῖσι στεφάνοις 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Ion” 535 d, compare 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Philoctetes” 1064, 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 6.41, etc.]]

__III.2
metaphorically, adorn, embellish, λόγους [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Medea” 576; λόγους ῥήμασί τε καὶ ὀνόμασι κεκοσμημένους 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Apologia” 17 c; τραγικὸν λῆρον 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Ranae” 1005]]; κ. ἔργον ἄριστον[Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. work] 1027; τὸ λογικὸν ἔχεις ἐξαίρετον, τοῦτο κόσμει 2nd c.AD: Arrianus Historicus “Epicteti Dissertationes” 3.1.26; λόγον εὐρυθμίαις 5th-6th c.BC: Isocrates Orator 5.27; αὑτὸν λόγοις 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Laches” 196 b, compare 197 c; ἐπὶ τὸ μεῖζον κ. 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 1.21]]; τὸν.. τὴν ἐκείνων ἀρετὴν κοσμήσοντα (in speaking) [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 18.287]]:—passive, ἦθος σεμνότητι -μημένον [Refs 1st c.BC+ [1st c.BC: Philodemus Philosophus “Academicorum Index” p.52 M.]]

__III.3
honour, λουτροῖς σ᾽ ἐκόσμης᾽ [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Electra” 1139; κ. τάφον [prev. author] “Ant.” 396; νέκυν 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Troades” 1147; κ. καὶ τιμᾶν 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 1.3.3]]; of persons, adorn, be an honour to, πατρίδα [Refs 6th c.BC+ [6th c.BC: Theognis Elegiacus 947; νᾶσον εὐκλέα 5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “N.” 6.46; Σαλαμῖνα κ. πατρίδα 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Fragmenta” 530.3; [τὴν πόλιν] αἱ τῶνδε ἀρεταὶ ἐκόσμησαν 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 2.42.]]

__III.4
bury, [Refs [“JHS” 25.172, +others (from Isauria).]]

__IV
passive, to be assigned, ascribed to, ἐς τὸν Αἰγύπτιον νομὸν αὗται [αἱ πόλεις] ἐκεκοσμέατο [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 3.91; ἐς Πέρσας κεκοσμέαται [prev. author] 6.41]]; especially of philosophic schools, κατὰ τὴν Ἀκαδημίαν κοσμεῖσθαι [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd c.AD: Sextus Empiricus Philosophus “Πυρρώνειοι ὑποτυπώσεις” 1.231; οἱ κατὰ διαφόρους αἱρέσεις κοσμούμενοι [prev. author] “M.” 11.77.]]

(-ος, ον, [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd c.AD: Galenus Medicus 16.606, 2nd c.AD: Soranus Medicus 1.3)]], well-ordered, regular, moderate, δαπάνη [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 56o d; οἴκησις [prev. author] “Criti.” 112]] c; κόσμιόν ἐστι, with infinitive, is a regular practice, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Plutus” 565.]]

__2
of persons, orderly, well-behaved, δίκαιοι καὶ σοφοὶ καὶ κ.[Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. work] 89; κ. καὶ σώφρων 5th c.BC: Lysias Orator 21.19; κ. καὶ εὔκολοι 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 329 d; κ. καὶ φρόνιμος ψυχή [prev. author] “Phd.” 108 a; χρηστὸς εἶ καὶ κ. 5th-6th c.BC: Nicopho Comicus 16; ἥτις ἐστὶ κοσμία γυνή 4th c.BC: Anaxandrides Comicus 56, compare 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Politica” 1277b23; κ. ἐν διαίτῃ 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 408 b; πρὸς τοὺς θεούς [prev. author] “Smp.” 193 a; οἱ κοσμιώτατοι φύσει [prev. author] “R.” 564]] e; of a patient, quiet, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Hippocrates Medicus “περὶ διαίτης ὀξέων” 65]]: frequently in Oratt., of honest, orderly citizens, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Lysias Orator 26.3, etc.; τοὺς πολίτας -ιωτέρους ποιεῖν 5th-6th c.BC: Isocrates Orator 20.18]]; modest, ὁμιλία [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Memorabilia” 3.11.14 (_superlative_)]]; τὸ κ. decency, order, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Electra” 872, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Leges” 802 e.]] adverb κοσμίως regularly, decently, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Plutus” 709, 978, +others; κ. ἔχειν 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Phaedo” 68]] c; κ. ἥκομεν as befits us, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. author] “Sph.” 216 a; κ. βιοῦν 5th c.BC: Lysias Orator 3.6]]: comparative -ιώτερον, βεβιωκέναι [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Isocrates Orator 15.162]]: superlative -ώτατα, τὰς συμφορὰς φέρειν [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Lysias Orator 3.4]].

κόσμος, -ου, ὁ
[in LXX: Gen.2:1, Deu.4:19 17:3, Isa.24:21 40:26 (צבא), Exo.33:5, 6 Jer.2:32 4:30, Eze.7:20 16:11 23:40 (עֲדִי), Isa.61:10 (כְּלִי), al., Wis.2:24 and freq., Sir.6:30, al ;]
__1. order (Hom., Plat., al.).
__2. ornament, adornment, esp. of women (Hom., al.): 1Pe.3:3.
__3. Later, the world or universe, as an ordered system (Plat., al.): Act.17:24, Rom.4:13, 1Co.3:22, Php.2:15, Heb.4:3, al.
__4. In late writers only, the world, i.e. the earth (= ἡ οἰκουμένη, cf. Mat.4:8 with Luk.4:5): Mat.4:8, Mrk.16:[15], Col.2:20, 1Ti.6:7, al.; hence by meton.,
__(a) of the human inhabitants of the world: Mat.5:14 15:38, Mrk.14:9, Jhn.1:10 4:42 12:47, Rom.3:6, 1Co.4:13, 2Co.5:19, 2Pe.2:5, al.;
__(b) of worldly affairs or possessions: Mat.16:26, Mrk.8:36, Luk.9:25, 1Co.7:31, 1Jn.2:16, al.;
__(with) in ethical sense, of the ungodly: Jhn.7:7 14:17, 27 1Co.1:21, Jas.1:27, 1Jn.4:4, al.;
__(d) metaphorically: ὁ κ. τῆς ἀδικίας, Jas.3:6.
SYN.: αἰών, which see (cf . also Dalman, Words, 162ff.; Tr., Syn., §lix; Westc., additional note on Jhn.1:10; DB, iv, 938ff.). (AS)

κόσμος, ὁ,
order, κατὰ κόσμον in order, duly, εὖ κατὰ κ. [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 10.472, +others]]; οὐ κατὰ κ. shamefully, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 8.179; μὰψ ἀτὰρ οὐ κατὰ κ. 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 2.214: frequently in _dative_, κόσμῳ καθίζειν]] to sit in order, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 13.77, compare 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 8.67; οὐ κ... ἐλευσόμεθα 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 12.225; κ. θεῖναι τὰ πάντα 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 2.52, compare 7.36, etc.; διάθες τάδε κ. 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Aves” 1331]]; κ. φέρειν bear becomingly, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “P.” 3.82; δέξασθαί τινα κ. 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Agamemnon” 521; σὺν κόσμῳ 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 8.86, 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “de Mundo” 398b23; ἐν κόσμῳ 5th c.BC: Hippocrates Medicus “γυναικεῖα”  fragment 378, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Smp.” 223b]]; κόσμῳ οὐδενὶ κοσμηθέντες in no sort of order, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 9.59]]; φεύγειν, ἀπιέναι οὐδενὶ κ., [Refs [[prev. author] 3.13, 8.60.γ]], etc.; ἀτάκτως καὶ οὐδενὶ κ. [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 3.108, compare 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Persae” 400]]; οὐκέτι τὸν αὐτὸν κ. no longer in the same order, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 9.66; οὐδένα κ. [prev. work] 65, 69; ἦν δ᾽ οὐδεὶς κ. τῶν ποιουμένων 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 3.77]]: generally, of things, natural order, γίνεται τῶν τεταρταίων ἡ κατάστασις ἐκ τούτου τοῦ κ. [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Hippocrates Medicus “προγνωστικόν” 20.]]

__2
good order, good behaviour  [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Trachiniae” 901]]; κ. χείρ, of a beggar, [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [“Anthologia Graeca” 12.212 (2nd c.AD: Strato Epigrammaticus); κ. ἱστίον 2nd c.AD(?): Pollianus Epigrammaticus 1.107]]; κοῖλος μήν short month, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [1st c.BC: Geminus Astronomicus 8.3, compare κοιλοποιέομαι, κοῖλος 11.3: _comparative_ 492  ότερος ὁλμοῦ 4th-5th c.BC: Parmenides Poeta Philosophus 8.52]]; ἐξηγεομένων.. τὸν κ. αὐτοῦ the fashion of it, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 3.22]]; κ. τόνδε.. ὁ καταστησάμενος who established this order or from, [Refs [[prev. author] 1.99.]]

__4
of states, order, government, μεταστῆσαι τὸν κ. [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 4.76, compare 8.48, 67; μένειν ἐν τῷ ὀλιγαρχικῷ κ. 8.72, etc.]]; especially of the Spartan constitution, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.65, 4th-3rd c.BC: Clearchus Historicus 3: _plural_, πόλεων κόσμοι 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Protagoras” 322c.]]

__II
ornament, decoration, especially of women, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 14.187, 8th-7th c.BC: Hesiodus Epicus “Opera et Dies” 76, 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 5.92. ; γυναικεῖος κ. 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 373c, etc.]]; of a horse, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 4.145]]; of men, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 3.123, 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Septem contra Thebas” 397, etc.]]; γλαυκόχροα κόσμον ἐλαίας, of an olive-wreath, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “O.” 3.13, compare 8.83, “P.” 2.10, etc.; κ. κυνῶν 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Cynegeticus” 6.1; κ. καὶ ἔπιπλα 5th c.BC: Lysias Orator 12.19]]; κ. ἀργυροῦς a service of plate, [Refs 2nd c.BC+ [2nd c.AD: Athenaeus Epigrammaticus 6.231b; ἱερὸς κ. “OGI” 90.40 (Rosetta, 2nd c.BC)]]: plural, ornaments, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Agamemnon” 1271; οἱ περὶ τὸ σῶμα κ. 5th-6th c.BC: Isocrates Orator 2.32]]: metaphorically, of ornaments of speech, such as epithets, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [[prev. author] 9.9 (_plural_), 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Rhetorica” 1408a14, “Po.” 1457b2, 1458a33]]; ἁδυμελῆ κ. κελαδεῖν to sing sweet songs of praise, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “O.” 11 (10). b2.595, 2nd c.BC: Polybius Historicus 1.60.6.]]

__II.4
κ. νοσήματα internal complaints, [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd-3rd c.AD: Philostratus Sophista “Vita Apollonii” 3.44. ει τινί]] it does one credit, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 8.60, 142; γύναι, γυναιξὶ κόσμον ἡ σιγὴ φέρει 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Ajax” 293; κ. τοῦτ᾽ ἐστὶν ἐμοί 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Nubes” 914; οἷς κόσμος [ἐστὶ] καλῶς τοῦτο δρᾶν 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 1.5; ἐν κόσμῳ καὶ τιμῇ εἶναί τινι 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 60.36]]; of persons, σὺ ἔμοιγε μέγιστος κ. ἔσει [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 6.4.3; ἡ μεγαλοψυχία οἷον κ. τις τῶν ἀρετῶν 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Ethica Nicomachea” 1124a1.]]

__III
ruler, regulator, title of chief magistrate in Crete, [Refs [“SIG” 712.57, etc.]]; collectively, body of κόσμοι, [Refs [[prev. work]524.1]]; τοῦ κ. τοῖς πλίασι [Refs 4th c.BC+ [[prev. work]527.74: also frequently in _plural_, [prev. work]528.1, +others, 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Politica” 1272a6, 1st c.BC-1st c.AD: Strabo Geographus 10.4.18, 22]]; compare κόρμος.

__IV
Philos., world-order, universe, first in [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Pythagoras Philosophus, _accusative_ to “Placita Philosophorum” 2.1.1, 3rd c.AD(?): Diogenes Laertius 8.48 (compare [5th-6th c.BC: Philolaus Philosophus] 21), or 4th-5th c.BC: Parmenides Poeta Philosophus, _accusative_ to 4th-3rd c.BC: Theophrastus Philosophus cited in D.L.[same place]; κόσμον τόνδε οὔτε τις θεῶν οὔτε ἀνθρώπων ἐποίησεν, ἀλλ᾽ ἦν ἀεὶ καὶ ἔστιν καὶ ἔσται πῦρ 1st c.AD(?): Heraclitus 30; ὁ καλούμενος ὑπὸ τῶν σοφιστῶν κ. 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Memorabilia” 1.1.11: frequently in 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus, “Grg.” 508a, “Ti.” 27a, +others; ἡ τοῦ ὅλου σύστασίς ἐστι κ. καὶ οὐρανός 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “de Caelo” 280a21, compare 4th-3rd c.BC: Epicurus Philosophus “Epistulae” 2p.37U., 3rd c.BC: Chrysippus Stoicus 2.168, etc.; ὁ κ. ζῷον ἔμψυχον καὶ λογικόν 2nd-1st c.BC: Posidonius Historicus cited in 3rd c.AD(?): Diogenes Laertius 7.139, compare 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Timaeus” 30b]]: sometimes of the firmament, γῆς ἁπάσης τῆς ὑπὸ τῷ κόσμῳ κειμένης [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Isocrates Orator 4.179; ὁ περὶ τὴν γῆν ὅλος κ. 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Meteorologica” 339a20]]; μετελθεῖν εἰς τὸν ἀέναον κ., of death, [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [“OGI” 56.48 (Canopus, 3rd c.BC)]]; but also, of earth, as opposed to heaven, ὁ ἐπιχθόνιος κ. [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd-3rd c.AD: Hermes Trismegistus cited in 5th c.AD: Stobaeus, Joannes 1.49.44; or as opposed to the underworld, ὁ ἄνω κ. 4th c.AD: Iamblichus Philosophus “de vita Pythagorica” 27.123]]; of any region of the universe, ὁ μετάρσιος κ. [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd-3rd c.AD: Hermes Trismegistus cited in 5th c.AD: Stobaeus, Joannes 1.49.44]]; of the sphere whose centre is the earth's centre and radius the straight line joining earth and sun, [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [3rd c.BC: Archimedes Geometra “ψαμμίτης” 4]]; of the sphere containing the fixed stars, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Epinomis” 987b]]: in plural, worlds, coexistent or successive, [Refs 6th c.BC+ [6th c.BC: Anaximander Philosophus et alii cited in “Placita Philosophorum” 2.1.3, cf. Epicur.[same place]]]; also, of stars, Νὺξ μεγάλων κ. κτεάτειρα [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Agamemnon” 356 (_anapaest meter_), cf. Heraclid.et Pythagorei cited in “Placita Philosophorum” 2.13.15 (= 5th-6th c.AD: Orphica “Fragmenta” 22)]]; οἱ ἑπτὰ κ. the Seven planets, [Refs [Corp.Herm. 11.7.]]

__IV.2
metaphorically, microcosm, ἄνθρωπος μικρὸς κ. [Refs 1st c.AD+ [3rd c.AD: Democritus Epigrammaticus 34; ἄνθρωπος βραχὺς κ. 1st c.AD: Philo Judaeus 2.155]]; of living beings in general, τὸ ζῷον οἷον μικρόν τινα κ. εἶναί φασιν ἄνδρες παλαιοί [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd c.AD: Galenus Medicus “de Usu Partium” 3.10.]]

__IV.3
in later Gr., ={οἰκουμένη}, the known or inhabited world, [NT+1st c.BC+ [“OGI” 458.40 (1st c.BC), NT.Rom.1.8, etc.]]; ὁ τοῦ παντὸς κ. κύριος, of Nero, [Refs [“SIG” 814.31, compare “IGRom.” 4.982 (from Samos)]]; ἐὰν τὸν κ. ὅλον κερδήσῃ [NT.Matt.16.26.]

__IV.4
men in general, φανέρωσον σεαυτὸν τῷ κ. [NT.John.7.4, compare 12.19]; especially of the world as estranged from God by sin, [[prev. work] 16.20, 17.9, +others, NT.1Cor.1.21, etc.]

__IV.5
οὗτος ὁ κ. this present world, i.e. earth, opposed to heaven, [NT.John.13.1; regarded as the kingdom of evil, ὁ ἄρχων τοῦ κ. τούτου [prev. work] 12.31.]

__V
Pythag.name for six, [Refs [Theol.Ar. 37]]; for ten, [Refs [[prev. work]59.]]

(κοῦφος, light), [in LXX: Exo.18:22, Jon.1.5, al. (קָלַל hi.), Est.5:1, al. ;]

LSJ / STEPBible (TFLSJ)
κουφ-ίζω,
Attic dialect future - ῐῶ [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Ajax” 1287]]: perfect κεκούφικα [Refs 2nd c.BC+ [“OGI” 90.12 (Rosetta, 2nd c.BC):]]

__I
to be light, κουφίζουσαν ἄρουραν [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th-7th c.BC: Hesiodus Epicus “Opera et Dies” 463, compare 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Helena” 1555]]; of a sufferer, to be relieved, κουφίζειν δοκῶ [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Philoctetes” 735, compare 5th c.BC: Hippocrates Medicus “ἀφορισμοί” 2.27.]]

__II
transitive, lighten, make light, τὸ κενὸν ἐμπεριλαμβανόμενον κ. τὰ σώματα [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “de Caelo” 309a6]]:—passive, [Refs [[prev. author] “PA” 663b13: hence,]]

__II.1
lift up, raise, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Antigone” 43, “Tr.” 1025 (Lyric poetry); αἴρων κουφιῶ σ᾽ ἐγώ 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Aves” 1762 (Lyric poetry); ἀσπίδ᾽ ἀμφὶ βραχίονι κουφίζων 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Phoenissae” 121 (Lyric poetry)]]; ἅλμα κουφιεῖν make a light leap, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Aj.” [same place]; κ. πήδημα 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Electra” 861 (Lyric poetry)]]; δύστηνον αἰώρημα κουφίζω, ={δύστηνος αἰωροῦμαι}, [Refs [[prev. author] “Supp.” 1047]]:—passive, to be lifted up, soar, [τῷ πτερῷ] ᾧ ψυχὴ κουφίζεται [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Phaedrus” 248c, compare 249a; σώματα -όμενα ὑπὸ τοῦ κύματος 4th c.AD: Julianus Imperator “Orationes” 1.27c.]]

__II.2
lighten of a load, ὄχλου πλήθους τε κ. χθόνα lighten earth of a multitude, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Helena” 40; κουφισθεὶς τοῦ βάρους 4th-3rd c.BC: Theophrastus Philosophus “Historia Plantarum” 4.16.2]]: absolutely, lighten ships of their cargo, τῷ ταχυναυτοῦντι κουφίσαντες προσβάλλειν [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 6.34; κουφισθεισῶν τῶν νεῶν 2nd c.BC: Polybius Historicus 20.5.11, compare 1.60.8.]]

__II.2.b
of persons, relieve from burdens, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Memorabilia” 2.7.1, “Cyr.” 6.3.24; τὸν δῆμον τῶν εἰσφορῶν 1st c.BC: Diodorus Siculus Historicus 13.64, compare “IG” 12(7).506.16 (Amorgos, 3rd c.BC)]]; τόκων τοὺς χρεωφειλέτας [Refs 1st c.AD+ [1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus “Caesar” 37]]; relieve (contractors), [Refs 2nd c.BC+ [2nd c.BC: Polybius Historicus 6.17.5; τῆς ὑπερηφανίας 1st c.BC: Philodemus Philosophus “περὶ κακιῶν ί” p.16 1st c.AD: Josephus Historicus; κ. τοὺς νοσοῦντας 1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus 2.1106c]]:—passive, to be relieved, ὅταν σῶμα κουφισθῇ νόσου from.., [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Orestes” 43; τοῦ πάθους 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Problemata” 873b22; λέξασα κουφισθήσομαι ψυχήν 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Medea” 473:]]future middle κουφιεῖσθαι[Refs 1st c.AD+ [in _passive_ sense, 2nd c.AD: Aristides Rhetor 2.145 1st c.AD: Josephus Historicus: _metaphorically_, τῇ τῶνδε εὐκλείᾳ κουφίζεσθε]] feel your burdens lightened by.., [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 2.44; κουφίζονται οἱ λυπούμενοι 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Ethica Nicomachea” 1171a29, compare “Pol.” 1342a14; ἐλπίδι κ. ματαίᾳ 2nd-3rd c.AD: Aelianus “De Natura Animalium - Ar.Byzantine Epit.” 11.33.]]

__II.3
with accusative of things, lighten, assuage, ἀλγηδόνας [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Fragmenta” 573; συμφορὰς λόγῳ κ. 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 60.35; κ. ἔρωτα 3rd c.BC: Theocritus Poeta Bucolicus 23.9; τὸ πάθος 1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus “Alexander” 52; τὰ ὀφλήματα [prev. author] 2.807d]]: absolutely, give or procure relief, κ. οὐδέν, ἀλλά.. [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Hippocrates Medicus “ἐπιδημίαι” 1.7, compare 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “de Generatione Animalium” 725b9]]:—passive, νομίζοντες κεκουφίσθαι τὸν πόλεμον αὐτοῖς [Refs 2nd c.BC+ [2nd c.BC: Polybius Historicus 1.17.2.]]

__II.3.b
cancel a debt, [Refs 6th c.AD+ [“POxy.” 126.8 (6th c.AD)]], etc.:—middle, [Refs 6th c.AD+ [“PMasp.” 95.10 (6th c.AD).]]

__II.4
ἑαυτοὺς κ. cheapen themselves, uncertain in [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-3rd c.BC: Epicurus Philosophus “De rerum natura - Wien. Stud.” 112 G.]]

__II.5
subtract, ἀπὸ τῶν μοιρῶν [Refs 4th c.AD+ [4th c.AD: Hephaestio Astrologus 2.1.]]

with genitive, to be lord or master of, rule over, πάντων Ἀργείων, πάντων, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 1.79, 288, compare 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 15.274; Ὀλύμπου 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Prometheus Vinctus” 149 (Lyric poetry); δωμάτων [prev. author] “Ag.” 1673; ὅπλων 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Ajax” 1337]]; κ. τοῦ βίου to be master of.., [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Andocides Orator 1.137; αὑτοῦ κ. 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Ajax” 1099, 5th c.BC: Antipho Orator 5.26, compare 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Coloneus” 405; ἡδονῶν καὶ ἐπιθυμιῶν 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Symposium” 196c, etc.; τῶν πραγμάτων 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 2.27]]; τοῦ μὴ πείθεσθαι τοῖς νόμοις κρατῆσαι to be above obedience.., [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Respublica Lacedaemoniorum” 4.6.]]

__II

__II.b
to be superior, πλήθους ἕκατι ναυσὶν κρατῆσαι [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Persae” 338]]: absolutely, to be the best, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Critias Philosophus, Tragicus, Elegiacus 2.7 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator]]

of reports, etc., prevail, become current, φάτις κρατεῖ [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Supplices” 293, 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Ajax” 978; λόγος κ. 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Persae” 738; νόμιμα δὲ τὰ Χαλκιδικὰ ἐκράτησεν 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 6.5; κρατεῖ ἡ φήμη παρά τισι 2nd c.BC: Polybius Historicus 9.26.11.]]

__II.2
c.infinitive, prevail so that, κ. τῷ πλήθει ὥστε μὴ αὐτίκα τὰς πύλας ἀνοίγεσθαι [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 4.104: _impersonal_, κατθανεῖν κρατεῖ]] 'tis better to.., [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Agamemnon” 1364; κρατεῖ μὴ γιγνώσκοντ᾽ ἀπολέσθαι 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Hippolytus” 248 (_anapaest meter_).]]

__II.3
c.genitive, conquer, prevail over, τῶν ἐναντίων [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Fragmenta” 85, compare “OC” 646, 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Septem contra Thebas” 955 (Lyric poetry), etc.; κ. τινὸς τὸν ἀγῶνα 2nd-3rd c.AD: Philostratus Sophista “Heroicus” 2.5: _metaphorically_, τό τοι νομισθὲν τῆς ἀληθείας κρατεῖ 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Fragmenta” 86]]; κ. τῆς διαβολῆς get the better of it, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Lysias Orator 19.53]]; ὁ λόγος τοῦ ἔργου ἐκράτει surpassed, went beyond it, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 1.69]]; ἡ φύσις.. τῶν διδαγμάτων κρατεῖ is better than.., [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-3rd c.BC: Menander Comicus “Μονόστιχοι - Fragmenta Comicorum Graecorum” 213, compare 169.]]

__II.3.b
of food, digest, assimilate, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Hippocrates Medicus “περὶ ἀρχαίης ἰητρικῇς” 3, 14, Mnesith. cited in 2nd c.AD: Athenaeus Epigrammaticus 2.54b, Phylotim.[prev. work] 3.79c]]:—passive, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Hippocrates Medicus “ἐπιδημίαι” 6.5.15; τῆς τροφῆς μὴ κρατηθείσης 1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus 2.654b.]]

__II.4
c.accusative, conquer, master, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “N.” 10.25, 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Prometheus Vinctus” 215, “Th.” 189, 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Alcestis” 490, 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Nubes” 1346, “Av.” 420, 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 7.6.32, etc.]]; μάχῃ, τῷ πολέμῳ τινά, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 6.2, 4th c.BC: Aeschines Orator 2.30; τῷ λόγῳ τινά 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Vespae” 539]]; πάχει μάκει τε in.., [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “P.” 4.245]]; outdo, τοὺς φίλους εὖ ποιῶν [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Hiero” 11.15; τῷ διαφθαρῆναι χρήμασιν ἢ μὴ κεκράτηκα Φίλιππον 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 18.247]]; surpass, κρατεῖ δὲ ὁ τῆς ἡδονῆς [βίος] τὸν τῆς φρονήσεως [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Philebus” 12a]]:—passive, to be overcome, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Septem contra Thebas” 750 (Lyric poetry), etc.; ὕπνῳ [prev. author] “Eu.” 148 (Lyric poetry); ὑπὸ τοῦ ὕπνου 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 2.121. δ᾽; ὑπὸ τῶν ἡδονῶν 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Leges” 633e.]]

__III
become master of, get possession of, τῆς ἀρχῆς, τῶν νεκρῶν, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.92, 4.111; πολλὰ φρονέοντα μηδενὸς κ. [prev. author] 9.16; σέθεν 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Supplices” 387; οὔπω ἡ βουλή σου ἐκράτει 5th c.BC: Lysias Orator 13.26; κ. τῆς γῆς 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 3.6; ναυσὶ τῆς θαλάσσης 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Menexenus” 240a]]; κ. τῆς λέξεως have it at command, remember it, [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd c.AD: Athenaeus Epigrammaticus 7.275b]]; master by the intellect, πάντων τῶν τῆς ἱστορίας μερῶν [Refs 2nd c.BC+ [2nd c.BC: Polybius Historicus 16.20.2]]:—passive, to be mastered, δεῖ ἐν ταῖς τέχναις καὶ ἐπιστήμαις ταῦτα κρατεῖσθαι [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Politica” 1331b38, compare “Po.” 1456a10 (probably to be read instead of κροτεῖσθαι).]]

__IV
lay hold of, τῆς χειρός [LXX+NT [LXX.Gen.19.16, NT.Matt.9.25, NT.Mark.9.27.]]

__IV.2
c.accusative of things, seize, win and keep, especiallyby force, πᾶσαν αἶαν [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Supplices” 255; θρόνους 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Coloneus” 1381]]; seize, hold fast, arrest, τινα [NT+2nd c.BC+ [Batrachomyomachia 63, 2nd c.BC: Polybius Historicus 8.18.8, NT.Matt.14.3; τένοντα Batrachomyomachia 233; τὰς χεῖράς τινος “PLips.” 40iii2 (4th-5th c.AD)]]; secure, grasp, τὴν ἀκατονόμαστον Τριάσα[Refs 5th c.BC+ [Zos.Alch. p.230 5th c.BC: Bacchylides Lyricus]]

__IV.3
hold up, support, τινα [Refs 1st c.BC+ [1st c.BC: Dionysius Halicarnassensis 4.38]]; maintain a military post, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 5.6.7]]; hold fast, τὰς παραδόσεις [NT.2Thes.2.15]; keep, retain, [Refs 2nd c.BC+ [PTeb. 61 (b).229 (2nd c.BC)]]:—passive, οὐκ ἦν δυνατὸν κρατεῖσθαι αὐτὸν ὑπ᾽ αὐτοῦ (i.e. τοῦ θανάτου) [NT.Act.2.24]; ἡ κτῆσις τοῖς τέκνοις κεκράτηται has been reserved for, settled upon, [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [“POxy.” 237 viii 36 (2nd c.AD).]]

__IV.4
in Law, possess a title to, κ. καὶ κυριεύειν c.genitive, [Refs 3rd c.AD+ [“PTeb.” 319.19 (3rd c.AD), etclass=bibl [prev. author] “Pl.” 536]]: absolutely, tumult, uproar, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th-7th c.BC: Hesiodus Epicus “Theogonia” 880:_passive_, Egypt, 1st c.AD), “BGU” 742 iii 6 (_passive_, 2nd c.AD).]]

__IV.5
hold in the hand, ὁ κρατῶν τοὺς ἑπτὰ ἀδτέρας ἐν τῇ δεξιᾷ αὐτοῦ [NT+1st c.AD+ [NT.Rev.2.1; πόαν 1st c.AD: Dioscorides (Dioscurides) Medicus 3.93; ἄρτον 1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus 2.99d; σκῆπτρον 2nd c.AD: Athenaeus Epigrammaticus 7.289c, compare 2nd c.AD: Lucianus Sophista “Am.” 44, 3rd c.AD(?): Achilles Tatius Astronomus 1.6]], etc.; δακτύλιον [Refs 4th c.AD+ [“PMag.Lond” 46.451(4th c.AD).]]

__IV.6
endure, put up with, τὸν ἀργυροπράτην [Refs 6th c.AD+ [“POxy.” 1844 (6th c.AD).]]

__V
control, command, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Agamemnon” 10, 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Hecuba” 282:]] —passive, αἰσχρὰ τῷ νόμῳ κρατούμενα controlled by.., [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Aves” 755; κρατεῖσθαι ὑπὸ τοῦ προβουλεύματος 1st c.BC: Dionysius Halicarnassensis 9.52; διαθέσει 3rd c.AD: Porphyrius Tyrius Philosophus “Sententiae ad intelligibilia ducentes” 27.]]

Abbott-Smith / STEPBible (TBESG)
κράτιστος, -η, -ον
superl, of κρατύς (Hom.),
__1. strongest, mightiest (Hom.).
__2. noblest, best (cf. κρείσσων), most excellent (find., Soph., al.): voc., κρατίστε, as title of honour and respect (DCG, ii, 727a), Luk.1:3, Act.23:26 24:3 26:25.†
(AS)

κρᾰτιστ-ος, η, ον,
Epic dialect κάρτ- (as always in [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Homerus Epicus), isolated Superl. from κρατύς]], strongest, mightiest, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 1.266, etc.; θεῶν κ., i.e. Zeus. 5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “O.” 14.13; κ. Ἑλλήνων, i.e. Achilles, 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Ph.” 3: in Prose, εἰ τοὺς κ. ἐνικήσαμεν 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 7.67]]; Λημνίων τὸ κ. the best of their men, [Refs [[prev\. author] 5.8; τὸ δυνάμεως κ.]] the strength or flower of.., [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Cyr.” 6.1.28]], etc.; of things, καρτίστην.. μάχην fiercest fight, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 6.185; δεσμὸς κ. Ti.Locrian dialect 99a]].

__2
generally, best, most excellent, as superlative of ἀγαθός, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “I.” 1.17, 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Ant.” 1050, etc.: colloquially, ἄνδρα κ. εἰπών Theophrastus Philosophus [{4-3rd c.BC}] “Characteres” 5.2]]; οἱ κράτιστοι the aristocracy, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “HG” 7.1.42, see at {ἀγαθός} 1; τὰ κ. τῆς χώρας [prev. work] 3.4.20.]]

__2.b
as a title or mode of address, [κράτιστε Θεόφιλε NT.Luke.1.3]; especially = Latin egregius, [Refs 1st c.AD+ [ὁ κ. ἡγεμών “PFay.” p.33 (1st c.AD); ὁ κ. ἐπίτροπος “BGU” 891 (2nd c.AD); ἡ κ.]], of a woman of the equester ordo, [Refs [Inscriptiones Graecae 14. 1346; also, =]] Latin clarissimus, of Senators, ὁ κ. ἀνθὐπατος [Refs 3rd c.AD+ [[prev. work]9(1).61; ὁ κ. συγκλητικός “IGRom.” 3.581, etc.; ἡ κ. βουλή “POxy.” 2108.6 (3rd c.AD).]]

__2.c
with modal words added, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [κ. τὴν ψυχήν 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 2.40]]; πάντων πάντα κ. best of all in.., [Refs 6th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “An.” 1.9.2; ἔν τινι [prev\. author] “Mem.” 3.4.5; εἴς τι Plato Philosophus [{5-6th c.BC}] “Philebus” 67b; περί τι [prev\. author] “Plt.” 257a; πρός τι Xenophon Historicus [{5-6th c.BC}] “Historia Graeca (Hellenica)” 3.4.16]]: with infinitive, best at doing, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 2.81, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Phdr.” 267d, 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Mem.” 1.4.1]], etc.: with participle, [Refs [τῶν ἡλίκων κ. εἶναι ἀκοντίζων καὶ τοξεύων [prev\. author] “Cyr.” 1.3.15]].

__3
neuter followed by infinitive, φυγέειν κάρτιστον to flee were best, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 12.120, compare 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “El.” 379, 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Eq.” 80, etc.: in _plural_, κράτιστα.. ἑλεῖν 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Med.” 384]]: absolutely, ὅπερ κ. the main point, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 1.143.]]

__4
adverb usages, ἀπὸ τοῦ κρατίστου in all good faith, [Refs 2nd c.BC+ [2nd c.BC: Polybius Historicus 8.17.4; κατὰ τὸ κ. 1st c.BC: Dionysius Halicarnassensis 2.22]]: neuter plural κράτιστα as adverb, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “HG” 3.4.16, “Ages.” 1.25.]] —The _comparative_ in use is κρείσσων (which see).

κράτος, -εος (-ους), τό
[in LXX chiefly for עֹז, Job.12:16, Psa.90:11 al. ;]

Aeschylus Tragicus [{4-5th c.BC}] “Supplices” 207]]; κατὰ κράτος with all one's might or strength, [Refs 6th c.BC+ [πολιορκεῖσθαι 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 1.64; πολεμεῖν Plato Philosophus [{5-6th c.BC}] “Leges” 692d; ἐξελέγχεσθαι 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 34.20]], etc.: frequently in phrase αἱρεῖν κατὰ κ. take by storm, [Refs 6th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 8.100, 5th-6th c.BC: Isocrates Orator 4.119, etc.; also ἀνὰ κράτος διώκειν Xenophon Historicus [{5-6th c.BC}] “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 1.4.23; ἐλαύνειν [prev\. author] “An.” 1.8.1, etc.; ἀπὸ κράτους 1st c.BC: Diodorus Siculus Historicus 17.34]]; πρὸς ἰσχύος κράτος, opposed to λόγῳ, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Ph.” 594.]]

personified, K. [Refs 5th c.BC+ [Βία τε Aeschylus Tragicus [{4-5th c.BC}] “Prometheus Vinctus” 12; K. καὶ Δίκη [prev\. author] “Ch.” 244]].

power, τοῦ γὰρ κ. ἐστὶ μέγιστον, of Zeus, [LXX+8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 2.118, etc.; τοῦ γὰρ κ. ἔστ᾽ ἐνὶ οἴκῳ 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 1.359, compare 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 12.214; Ζηνὸς κ. 5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “O.” 6.96, compare 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Pr.” 527 (Lyric poetry); ἐκπίπτειν κράτους, of Zeus, [prev. work] 948; τὸ κ. τοῦ θεοῦ Vetus Testamentum Graece redditum LXX.Psa.61(62).11]], etc.: plural, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [ὑποχείριος κράτεσιν ἀρσένων Aeschylus Tragicus [{4-5th c.BC}] “Supplices” 393 (Lyric poetry), compare 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Ant.” 485]]; especially of political power, rule, sovereignty, [Refs 7th c.BC+ [ὁ μαιόμενος τὸ μέγα κρέτος ὀντρέψει τάχα τὰν πόλιν Alcaeus Lyricus [{7-6th c.BC}] [same place]; τὸ κ. περιθεῖναί τινι 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.129; ἐς τὸ πλῆθος φέρειν τὸ κ. [prev\. author] 3.81]]; τὸ πᾶν κ. ἔχειν to be all-powerful, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev\. author] 7.3; ἀρχὴ καὶ κ. τυραννικόν 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Coloneus” 373]]; βασιλεὺς πρῶτος ἐν κράτει Ὀδρυσῶν ἐγένετο in real power, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 2.29; later τὸ κ. τῶν Ῥωμαίων “POxy.” 41i2 (3rd-4th c.AD): in _plural_, κράτη καὶ θρόνους 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Antigone” 173, compare “OT” 586, etc.; θρόνων κράτη]] sovereign power, [Refs [[prev\. author] “Ant.” 166.]]

with genitive, power over, [Refs 6th c.BC+ [τὸ Περσέων κ. ἔχοντα 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 3.69; τὸ κ. εἶχε τῆς στρατιῆς [prev\. author] 9.42; πᾶν κ. ἔχων χθονός Aeschylus Tragicus [{4-5th c.BC}] “Supplices” 425 (Lyric poetry); τῶν ἄλλων δαιμόνων 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Troades” 949; δὸς κ. τῶν σῶν δόμων Aeschylus Tragicus [{4-5th c.BC}] “Choephori” 480; δωμάτων ἔχειν κ. of persons, a power, an authority, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [Ἀχαιῶν δίθρονον κ. Aeschylus Tragicus [{4-5th c.BC}] “Agamemnon” 109 (Lyric poetry), compare 619, “Th.” 127 (Lyric poetry).]]

mastery, victory, frequently in [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Homerus Epicus, 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 1.509, 6.387, 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 21.280; κ. ἄρνυσθαι 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Philoctetes” 838 (Lyric poetry); νίκη καὶ κράτη Aeschylus Tragicus [{4-5th c.BC}] “Supplices” 951]]; ἀέθλων κ. victory in.., [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “I.” 8(7).4; νίκη καὶ κ. τῶν δρωμένων 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Electra” 85]]; κ. ἀριστείας the meed of highest valour, [Refs 6th c.BC+ [[prev\. author] “Aj.” 443; νίκη καὶ κ. πολεμίων Plato Philosophus [{5-6th c.BC}] “Leges” 962a; κ. πολέμου καὶ νίκη 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 19.130]].

in Medicine texts, in plural, ligaments, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Hippocrates Medicus “Mul.” 2.167.]]

={ταρσός}, back of the hand, [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd c.AD(?): Pollianus Epigrammaticus 2.144.]]

[Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Pythagoras Philosophus]] name for ten, [Refs [Theol.Ar. 59]].—This word and its derivations take two forms, κρατ- and καρτ-; the latter is mostly Epic dialect, as κάρτος, κάρτιστος, καρτύνω, but in κρατερός and καρτερός the reverse holds, see at {κρατερός} near the end; κρατέω, κρατύς have no form καρτ-. Abbott-Smith / STEPBible (TBESG)
κρείσσων
(Epic and old Att..) and κρείττων (later Att..), prop. comparat. of κρατύς, strong, but in sense often (as in cl., see LS, see word) as comparat. of ἀγαθός,   [in LXX chiefly for טוֹב ;]
better;
__(a) as to ad­vantage or usefulness: 1Co.11:17, Heb.11:40 12:24; πολλῷ μᾶλλον κ., Php.1:23; κρεῖσσον ποιεῖν, 1Co.7:38; ἐστιν, before inf., 1Co.7:9, 2Pe.2:21;
__(b) as to excellence: Heb.1:4 6:9 7:7, 19 7:22 8:6 9:23 10:34 11:16, 35; κ. ἐστι, before inf., 1Pe.3:17.†
(AS)

---

LSJ / STEPBible (TFLSJ)
κρείσσων, ον,
genitive ονος, as always in Epic dialect and old Attic dialect; later Attic dialect κρείττων; Ionic dialect κρέσσων [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Hippocrates Medicus “Fract.” 3, +others, variant in 4th c.BC: Dionysius Tragicus (see. below 11); _Doric dialect_]] κάρρων (which see); Cretan dialect κάρτων [Refs [“Leg.Gort.” 1.15:]] — _comparative_ of κρατύς (see. κράτιστος), stronger, mightier, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [κ. βασιλεύς, ὅτε χώσεται ἀνδρὶ χέρηϊ 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 1.80]]; especially in battle, [Refs 6th c.BC+ [κρείσσοσιν ἶφι μάχεσθαι 21.486; Διὸς κ. νόος ἠέ περ ἀνδρῶν 16.688; κεραυνοῦ κρέσσον.. βέλος 5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “I.” 8(7).36, compare 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 7.172, Hp.[same place], etc.; κρείσσων χεῖρας 5th c.BC: Antipho Orator 4.4.7; τὸ τοῦ κ. συμφέρον Plato Philosophus [{5-6th c.BC}] “Respublica” 338c, compare 3rd c.AD: Democritus Epigrammaticus 267]]: hence, having the upper hand, superior, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [ὁππότερος δέ κε νικήσῃ κ. τε γένηται 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 3.71; κ. ἀρετῇ τε βίῃ τε 23.578]]: as Law-term, of witnesses, [Refs [κάρτονανς ἦμεν _prevail,_ Leges Gortynensium]] [prev. cited]

__2
frequently as comparative of ἀγαθός, better, κρέσσονες one's betters, especially in point of rank, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “O.” 10(11).39, “N.” 10.72 (but also, _the stronger, more powerful_, 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Or.” 710, 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 1.8, etc.); ἐς τοὺς τοκέας καὶ ἐς τοὺς κρέσσονας τεθυμῶσθαι 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 3.52, compare “SIG” 685.134 (5th c.BC: Magnes Comicus Mae., 2nd c.BC); οἱ κ. corps of guards at Thebes, 1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus 2.598e; κρείσσονες θεοί]], of the greater gods, as opposed to to Oceanus, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Pr.” 902 (Lyric poetry); ὁ κ. Ζεύς [prev\. author] “Ag.” 60]] (anapaest meter); οἱ κ. the Higher Powers, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev\. author] “fragment” 10, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Sph.” 216b, “Euthd.” 291a, etc.; τὰ κρείσσω, ={τὰ θεῖα}, 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Ion” 973; τὸ κ.]] the Almighty, Providence, [Refs 4th c.AD+ [Corp.Herm. 18.11, 4th c.AD: Julianus Imperator “Ep.” 204, 6th c.AD: Agathias Historicus et Epigrammaticus 1.16, 5th-6th c.AD: Procopius Gazaeus Rhetor “Pan.” p.492; τὰ κρείσσονα]] one's advantages, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [τὰ ὑπάρχοντα ἡμῖν κρείσσω καταπροδοῦναι 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 4.10]].

__3
with infinitive, οὔ τις ἐμεῖο κρείσσων.. δόμεναι no one has a better right to.., [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 21.345; οὐκ ἄλλος κ. παραμυθεῖσθαι Plato Philosophus [{5-6th c.BC}] “Politicus” 268b]]; κρεῖσσόν ἐστι with infinitive, 'tis better to.., [Refs 5th c.BC+ [κ. γάρ ἐστιν εἰσάπαξ θανεῖν ἢ.. πάσχειν κακῶς Aeschylus Tragicus [{4-5th c.BC}] “Prometheus Vinctus” 750, compare 624, 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 3.52, etc.; τὸ μὴ εἶναι κ. ἢ τὸ ζῆν κακῶς 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “fragment” 488, compare 4th-3rd c.BC: Apollodorus Comicus 6; also κρείσσων εἰμί]] with participle, κ. γὰρ ἦσθα μηκέτ᾽ ὢν ἢ ζῶν τυφλός thou wert better not alive, than living blind, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “OT” 1368, compare “Aj.” 635 (Lyric poetry); κ. ἦν ὁ ἀγὼν μὴ γεγενημένος 4th c.BC: Aeschines Orator 1.192, compare 1st c.BC: Dionysius Halicarnassensis 6.9.]]

__II
with genitive or ἤ, too great for, surpassing, beyond, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [ὕψος κ. ἐκπηδήματος Aeschylus Tragicus [{4-5th c.BC}] “Agamemnon” 1376]]; of evil deeds, κρείσσον᾽ ἀγχόνης too bad for hanging, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “OT” 1374; κρεῖσσον δεργμάτων]] too bad to look on, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Hipp.” 1217; θαυμάτων [prev\. author] “Ba.” 667]]; λέγετι σιγῆς κρεῖσσον [Refs 5th c.BC+ [(κρέσσον “PSI” 9.1093) ἢ σιγὴν ἔχε 4th c.BC: Dionysius Tragicus 6; κρείσσον᾽ ἢ λέξαι λόγῳ τολμήματα 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Supplices” 844]]; κ. ἢ λόγοισιν (i.e. εἰπεῖν) [Refs [[prev\. author] “IT” 837; ἀναρχία κ. πυρός [prev\. author] “Hec.” 608]]; πρᾶγμα ἐλπίδος κ. γεγενημένον worse than one expected, [Refs 6th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 2.64; κ. λόγου τὸ κάλλος Xenophon Historicus [{5-6th c.BC}] “Memorabilia” 3.11.1; κ. τῆς ἡμετέρας δυνάμεως [prev\. author] “Cyr.” 7.5.9]].

__III
having control over, master of, especially of desires and passions, [Refs 6th c.BC+ [τῶν ἡδονῶν 3rd c.AD: Democritus Epigrammaticus 214; τοῦ ἔρωτος Xenophon Historicus [{5-6th c.BC}] “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 6.1.34]]; γαστρὸς καὶ κερδέων [Refs [[prev. work] 4.2.45; αὑτῶν]] over themselves, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Phdr.” 232a, +others; κ. χρημάτων]] superior to the influence of money, [Refs 6th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 2.60, 5th-6th c.BC: Isocrates Orator 1.19; τῶν συμμάχων κ. Xenophon Historicus [{5-6th c.BC}] “Respublica Atheniensium” 2.1]]; also, putting oneself above, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [κ. τοῦ δικαίου 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 3.84]]; κρείσσους ὄντες.. τῷ λογισμῷ ἐς τὸ ἀνέλπιστον τοῦ βεβαίου having reasoned themselves into an absolute belief of the hopelessness of certainty, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [[prev. work] 83; φαύλους καὶ κρείττους τῆς παιδείας, ={οὓς παιδευθῆναι ἀδύνατον} (just below), 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Pol.” 1316a9.]]

__IV
better, more excellent, [Refs 1st c.AD+ [ἁρμονίη ἀφανὴς φανερῆς κ. 1st c.AD: Heraclitus 54; κ. ἐπ᾽ ἀρετήν 3rd c.AD: Democritus Epigrammaticus 181]]; ὁ κρείττων λόγος (opposed to ὁ ἥσσων) [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Nu.” 113; κατὰ τὸ κ.]] in a higher sense, opposed to κατὰ τὸ χεῖρον, [Refs 5th c.AD+ [5th-6th c.AD: Damascius Philosophus “Pr.” 7.]]

__V
adverb [Refs 5th c.BC+ [κρεισσόνως 5th c.BC: Antipho Orator 4.4.6, 4th c.AD: Iamblichus Philosophus “Myst.” 7.4; also κρεῖσσον 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Tyrannus” 176 (Lyric poetry), “OGI” 90.31 (Rosetta, 2nd c.BC). (κρέσσων from κρέτ-yων, compare κρέτο; κάρτων and κάρρων from κάρτ-yων, compare κάρτο; κρείσσων (like μείζων)]] probably took ει from ὀλείζων.)

Abbott-Smith / STEPBible (TBESG)
κρίνω,
[in LXX chiefly for שׁפט, also for ריב ,דּין, etc. ;]
__1. to  separate, select, choose (cl.; in LXX: 2Ma.13:15).
__2. to approve, esteem: Rom.14:5.
__3. to be of opinion, judge, think: Luk.7:43, 1Co.11:13; before τοῦτο ὅτι, 2Co.5:14; with accusative and inf., Act.16:15; with accusative and pred., Act.13:46 26:8.
__4. to decide, determine, decree: with accusative, Act.16:4, Rom.14:13, 1Co.7:37, 2Co.2:1; with inf. (Field, Notes, 167), Act.20:16 25:25, 1Co.2:2 5:3, Tit.3:12 (cf. 1Ma.11:33, Wis.8:9, al.); with accusative and inf., Act.21:25 27:1.
__5. to judge, adjudge, pronounce judgment: absol., Jhn.8:16, 26; before κατά, with accusative, Jhn.7:24 8:15; κρίσιν κ., Jhn.7:24; τ. δίκαιον, Luk.12:57 (Deiss., LAE, 118); in forensic sense, Jhn.18:31, Act.23:3, al.; pass., Rom.3:4 (LXX); of God's judgment, Jhn.5:30 8:50, Rom.2:16 3:6, 2Ti.4:1, 1Pe.4:5, al.
__6. = κατακρίνω, to condemn (cl.): Act.13:27; of God's judgment, Jhn.3:18 5:22 12:47, 48, Act.7:7, Rom.2:12, 1Co.11:32, Heb.10:30" (LXX), Jas.5:9, Rev.19:2, al.
__7. As in LXX (for שׁפט), to rule, govern ( 4Ki.15:5, Psa.2:10, al.): Mat.19:28, Luk.22:30, 1Co.6:3.
__8. to bring to trial (cl.); mid., to go to law: with dative of person(s), Mat.5:40; before μετά, with genitive of person(s) (of the opponent), ἐπί, with genitive (of the judge), 1Co.6:1, 6 (cf. ἀνα-, ἀπο-, ἀντ-απο- (-μαι), δια-, ἐν-, ἐπι-, κατα-, συν-, ὑπο- (-μαι), συν-υπο- (-μαι)).
SYN.: see: δικάστης. (AS)

__II

__II.2
decide disputes, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [κρίνων νείκεα πολλά 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 12.440; ἔκριναν μέγα νεῖκος.. πολέμοιο 18.264]]: c.accusative cognate, οἳ.. σκολιὰς κρίνωσι θέμιστας judge crooked judgements, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 16.387; κ. δίκας 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 2.129; κρῖνε δ᾽ εὐθεῖαν δίκην Aeschylus Tragicus [{4-5th c.BC}] “Eumenides” 433]], etc.; πρώτας δίκας κρίνοντες αἵματος [Refs 6th c.BC+ [[prev. work] 682; κρινεῖ δὲ δὴ τίς ταῦτ; 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Ra.” 805; κ. κρίσιν Plato Philosophus [{5-6th c.BC}] “Respublica” 36o e; ἄριστα κ. 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 6.39]]; κρίνουσι βοῇ καὶ οὐ ψήφῳ they decide the question.., [Refs 6th c.BC+ [[prev\. author] 1.87; μίσει πλέον ἢ δίκῃ κ. [prev\. author] 3.67; τὸ δίκαιον κ. Isocrates Orator [{5-6th c.BC}] 14.10]]; τῷ τοῦτο κρίνει; by what do you form this judgement? [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Pl.” 48; κ. περί τινος 5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “N.” 5.40, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Ap.” 35d, 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Rh.” 1391b9, etc.:]] — passive, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [ἀγὼν κριθήσεται Aeschylus Tragicus [{4-5th c.BC}] “Eumenides” 677]]; κἂν ἰσόψηφος κριθῇ (i.e. ἡ δίκη) [Refs [[prev. work] 741: _impersonal_, κριθησόμενον]] a decision being about to be taken, [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd c.AD: Arrianus Historicus “An.” 3.9.6.]]

conceal, keep secret, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [οὐδέν τοι ἐγὼ κρύψω ἔπος 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 4.350, compare 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Th.” 74, etc.; κ. τι ἔνθα μή τις ὄψεται 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Ajax” 658, compare “Tr.” 903, “El.” 436:]] —middle, [Refs [πᾶν σοι φράσω τἀληθές, οὐδὲ κρύψομαι [prev\. author] “Tr.” 474]]:—passive, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [τὸ μὲν φάσθαι, τὸ δὲ καὶ κεκρυμμένον εἶναι 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 11.443]]; φάρμακα κεκρ. secret, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Andr.” 32; κεκρ. νάπη]] secret, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “OT” 1398; κεκρ. παγίς Menander Comicus [{4-3rd c.BC}] 689]]; κεκρ. σκευωρία secret intrigue, Mitteis [Refs 2nd c.BC+ [“Chr.” 31 vi 14 (2nd c.BC); κρυπτόμενα πράσσεται]] in secret, opposed to ἐπὶ μαρτύρων, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Antipho Orator 2.3.8, compare 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 6.72.]]

in Medicine texts, in passive, to be suppressed, of the menses or lochia, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Hippocrates Medicus “Mul.” 1.36, 154, 2.163.]]

intransitive, lie hidden, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [τὰ μὲν.. ὄμματα βλέποντα, τὰ δὲ κρύπτοντα 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Phoenissae” 1117]] (assuming variant); also [Refs [κ. τινά _conceal oneself from_ Hymni Homerici 1.7]].— (καλύπτω is simply cover; κεύθω cover so that no trace of it can be seen; κρύπτω keep covered, especially for purposes of concealment.)

Ionic dialect 3rd.pers. plural ἐκτέαται [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 4.23]]; subjunctive κέκτωμαι [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Isocrates Orator 3.49, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Leges” 936b; poetry κεκτήμην 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Iphigenia Aulidensis” 404]]; Ionic dialect 3rd.pers. plural ἔκτηντο [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 2.108]]; Attic dialect 1st pers. plural ἐκτήμεθα falsa lectio in [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Andocides Orator 3.37]]: for future and aorist passive, see below[Refs [111.]]

__I
present, imperfect, future, and aorist,

__I.1
procure for oneself, get, acquire, κτήμασι τέρπεσθαι τὰ γέρων ἐκτήσατο Πηλεύς [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 9.400, etc.]]; [οἰκῆας] Od.[same place]; γῆν [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Eu.” [same place], compare “Pers.” 770]]; of horses, win (as a prize), [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “N.” 9.52]]; κτήσασθαι βίον ἀπό τινος to get one's living from a thing, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 8.106]]; win favour, and the like, χάριν ἀπό τινος, ἔκ τινος, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Trachiniae” 471, “Ph.” 1370; παρά τινος 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Symposium” 4.43; τὴν εὔνοιαν τὴν παρὰ τῶν Ἑλλήνων 5th-6th c.BC: Isocrates Orator 5.68]]; κ. φίλους, ἑταίρους, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Ajax” 1360, 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Orestes” 804 (troch.); κτήσασθαι παῖδας ἐξ ὁμοσπόρου [prev. author] “IT” 696, compare 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Tyrannus” 1499, 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 8.105; παῖδας ἐς δόμους κτήσασθαι 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Fragmenta” 491, compare “Supp.” 225; πολλάκις δοκεῖ τὸ φυλάξαι τἀγαθὰ τοῦ κτήσασθαι χαλεπώτερον εἶναι 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 1.23.]]

__I.1.b
of consequences, bring upon oneself, αὑτῷ θάνατον [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Ajax” 968]]; incur, θεᾶς ὀργήν[Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. work] 777; κακά [prev. author] “El.” 1004; ξυμφοράς 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Orestes” 543; ἔχθραν πρός τινα 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 1.42]]; δυσσέβειαν κ. get a name for impiety, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Antigone” 924; κακὸν λόγον πρὸς ἀστῶν 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Heraclidae” 166, compare “IT” 676; ἐκ τῶν πόνων τὰς ἀρετὰς κ. 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 1.123.]]

__I.1.c
κ. τινὰς πολεμίους make them so, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 5.5.17; οὔ ποτ᾽ εὔνουν τὴν ἐμὴν κτήσῃ φρένα 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Philoctetes” 1281.]]

__I.2
procure or get for another, ἐμοὶ δ᾽ ἐκτήσατο κεῖνος [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 20. 265; μέγαν τέκνοις πλοῦτον ἐκτήσω 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Persae” 755 (troch.), compare 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Oeconomicus” 15.1.]]

[Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Timaeus” 91e; τὰ ἔμπροσθεν καὶ τὰ ὄπισθεν κ. 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Historia Animalium” 498a3, compare “PA” 690a20, etc.; δέρμα, τρίχας, ὄνυχάς τε ἐπ᾽ ἄκροις τοῖς κώλοις ἔφυσαν 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Timaeus” 76e.]]

__3

future -ύσω [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Nubes” 1448]]: aorist ἐκώλῡσα [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Alcestis” 897 (_anapaest meter_), 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Menexenus” 244c]]; perfect κεκώλῡκα [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th-3rd c.BC: Dinarchus Orator 1.101, 1st c.BC: Philodemus Gadarensis Epigrammaticus “Rh.” 2.63 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus]]:—passive, future κωλυθήσομαι [LXX+2nd c.AD+ [LXX.Sir.20.2(1), 2nd c.AD: Lucianus Sophista “VH” 2.25]]: also in middle form -ύσομαι [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 1.142]]: aorist ἐκωλύθην [Refs [[prev. author] 2.64, etc.:]]perfect κεκώλῡμαι[Refs [[prev. work] 37]]. [ῡ always before a consonant: common before a vowel, κωλῡόμεσθα [Refs 7th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Ion” 391, κωλῡέτω [prev. author] “Ph.” 990, κωλῠεν 5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “P.” 4.33, κώλῠει 7th-6th c.BC: Alcaeus Lyricus 55 (= 7th-6th c.BC: Sappho Lyrica 22 Lobel), 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Eq.” (see.below), “fragment” 100, 4th c.BC: Anaxilas Comicus 25, 4th-3rd c.BC: Menander Comicus “Ἐπιτρέποντες” 10]].]:—hinder, prevent:—Constr.:

__1
with accusative et infinitive, κ. ἐκρέειν τὸν Νεῖλον [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 2.20]]; κώλυεν [μιν] μεῖναι Pi.[same place]; τί δῆτα καὶ σὲ κωλύει  κέρδο; [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Fragmenta” 794, compare “IT” 507, etc.; ὅς σε κ. τὸ δρᾶν 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Philoctetes” 1241; φεύγειν οὐδεὶς κ. νόμος 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 23.52: with _negative_ added (rare in _Attic dialect_ Prose), κ. τινὰ μὴ θανεῖν 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Phoenissae” 1268; μὴ προσεύχεσθαι 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Historia Graeca (Hellenica)” 3.2.22, etc.]]:— passive, χρημάτων σπάνει [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 1.142]]; τοῦ ὕδατος πιεῖν from drinking the water, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 621b; κωλυόμεσθα μὴ μαθεῖν 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Ion” 391; μὴ οὐ πονηρὸν εἶναι 1st c.BC: Dionysius Halicarnassensis 2.3.]]

__1.c
with relative clause, κωλύειν εἴ τις ἐπαγγέλλεται, = {τινὰ μὴ ἐπαγγέλλεσθαι}, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 4.15]]; ἐκωλύσαμεν, ἵνα γένησθε.. [Refs 1st c.AD+ [1st c.AD: Josephus Historicus “Bellum Judaicum” 6.6.2.]]

with accusative of things, prevent, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Iphigenia Aulidensis” 1390 (troch.), 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 4.2.24]]:—passive, ἐν τούτῳ κεκωλῦσθαι ἐδόκει τὰ πράγματα [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 2.8, compare 4.14; ταῦτα.. μὴ ἐν ὑμῖν κωλυθῇ [prev. author] 2.64]]; μηδὲ.. δαπάνῃ κεκωλύσθω let there be no hindrance by reason of expense, [Refs [[prev. author] 1.129.]]

[prev. author] “Grg.” 458d; μὴ τὸ σὸν κωλυέτω 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Phoenissae” 990; οὐ τἀμὰ κωλύσει 1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus 2.151c, etc.]]; οὔτε ἐκεῖνο κωλύει ἐν ταῖς σπονδαῖς neither is that any hindrance, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 1.144 (wrongly explained as ={κωλύεται} by 1st c.BC: Dionysius Halicarnassensis “Amm.” 2.7)]]; οὔτε μίαν δυοῖν τὴν αὐτὴν εἶναι κ. nor is there any hindrance to one of two being the same, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Physica” 202b9.]]

κωφός, -ή, -όν
(κόπτω), [in LXX chiefly (Exo.4:11, al.) for אִלֵּם; for חָרָשׁ, Hab.2:18 ;]
blunt, dull. Metaphorical, of the senses, esp.
__(a) of speech, dumb: Mat.9:32-33 12:22 15:30-31, Luk.1:22 11:14;
__(b) of hearing, deaf: Mat.11:5, Mrk.7:32, 37 9:25, Luk.7:22.†

LSJ / STEPBible (TFLSJ)
κωφ-ός, ή, όν,
blunt, dull, obtuse, opposed to ὀξύς, κ. βέλος [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 11.390, compare 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Fragmenta” 495.27; κ. καλάμη “Anthologia Graeca” 12.25 (1st c.BC-1st c.AD: Statyllius Flaccus Epigrammaticus).]]

__II
metaphorically,

__II.1
of sound, mute, noiseless, κύματι κωφῷ [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 14.16]]; κωφὴν γὰρ δὴ γαῖαν ἀεικίζει is maltreating dumb, senseless earth, [Refs [24.54]]; τὰ μὲν ἄλλα ἔσκε κωφά the other parts sounded dull, opposed to to the ringing of the hollow parts when struck, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 4.200]]: neuter plural as adverb, κωφὰ δὲ πόντος κεῖτο [Refs 5th c.AD+ [5th-6th c.AD: Orphica “Argonautica” 1103]]; ὁ κ. λιμήν, probably the bay of Munychia, as opposed to to the noisy Piraeus, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Historia Graeca (Hellenica)” 2.4.31]]; κωφότερος ὁ ψόφος ἔσται, i.e. muffled, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aeneas Tacticus 19]]; τῶν μεταλλικῶν κωφότατος [ὁ σίδηρος] rings least, [Refs 1st c.BC+ [1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus 2.721f; κωφοὶ ἄνεμοι 1st c.BC: Diodorus Siculus Historicus 3.51.]]

__II.2
after [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Homerus Epicus]], of men or animals, dumb, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Parmenides Poeta Philosophus 6.7, etc.]]; καὶ κωφοῦ συνίημι καὶ οὐ φωνεῦντος ἀκούω Oracle texts cited in [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.47]]; οὐ.. παρὰ κωφὸν ὁ τυφλὸς ἔοικε λαλῆσαι, i.e. is not so dumb but that he will answer the blind fool who assails him, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Cratinus Comicus 6; κωφότερος κίχλης 4th c.BC: Eubulus Comicus 29]]; κ. χάρις a mute gift (i.e. an epitaph), [Refs [“epigram Gr.” 298 (from Teos)]]; so κωφοῖς δάκρυσι [Refs [“IPE” 2.299 (from Panticapaeum)]]; κ. τάφοι probably in [Refs [“IG” 12(8).441.26]]; κ. προσωπεῖον mute figure on the stage, [Refs 1st c.BC+ [1st c.AD: Philo Judaeus 2.520, compare 1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus 2.791e; κ. πρόσωπον 1st c.BC: Cicero, M. Tullius Orator et Philosophus “Epistulae ad Atticum” 13.19.3]]; κ. καὶ ἄλογος, of a house, with no echoes, [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd c.AD: Lucianus Sophista “Dom.” 1.]]

__II.2.b
deaf, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [hymnus ad Mercurium 92, 1st c.AD(?): Heraclitus 34. 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Septem contra Thebas” 202, “Ch.” 881; λήθην κωφήν, ἄναυδον 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Fragmenta” 670]]; ὅσοι γίνονται κ. ἐκ γενετῆς, πάντες καὶ ἐνεοὶ γίνονται [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Historia Animalium” 536b3]] (hence of a deaf and dumb person, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.34, “BGU” 1196.49 (1st c.BC),compare 5th c.AD(?): Hesychius Legal icographus); with _genitive_, κωφὴ ἀκοῆς αἴσθησις 4th c.BC: Antiphanes Comicus 196.5, conjecture in 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Leges” 932a]]; κ. Ἑλλάδος φωνᾶς deaf of one's Greek ear, i.e. ignorant of Greek, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [“Dialexeis 5th c.BC” 6.12; σπαράγματα κωφὰ τοῦ βεβαιοῦντος 1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus 2.1108d.]]

__II.2.c
metaphorically, νοῦς ὁρῇ καὶ νοῦς ἀκούει· τἆλλα κωφὰ καὶ τυφλά [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Epicharmus Comicus 249; κ. πέτρος 4th c.BC: Moschio Tragicus Trag. 7; μαψαῦραι 3rd c.BC: Callimachus Epicus “Fragmenta” 67; ἐρημία 1st c.BC: Diodorus Siculus Historicus 3.40]]: neuter plural as adverb, κωφὰ χλιαίνεσθαι feebly, [Refs 1st c.BC+ [Anthologia Graeca 12.125 (1st c.BC: Meleager Epigrammaticus).]]

__II.3
ὄμμα κ. vacant, lack-lustre eye, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Physiognomonica” 807b23.]]

__II.4
of the senses in general, dull, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-3rd c.BC: Theophrastus Philosophus “de Sensu” 19 (_comparative_).]]

__II.5
of the mind, dull, obtuse, ἐγὼ ὁ πάντα κ. [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Ajax” 911, compare 5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “P.” 9.87; τὸ τῆς ψυχῆς ποιεῖν κ. 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Timaeus” 88b: κωφοί, οἱ, 'the Dullards', title of satyr-play by Sophocles.]]

__II.5.b
of things, senseless, unmeaning, obscure, κ. καὶ παλαί᾽ ἔπη [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Tyrannus” 290; κ. διήγησις 2nd c.BC: Polybius Historicus 3.36.4, compare 5.21.4; ὑπόνοια 1st c.BC: Philodemus Gadarensis Epigrammaticus “Mus.” p.71 K.; σκῶμμα 1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus 2.712a]]; but κ. εὐπραγίαι is probably falsa lectio for{κοῦφαι}, [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd-3rd c.AD: Dio Cassius Historicus 38.27.]] adverb -φῶς obscurely, [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd c.AD: Vettius Valens Astrologus 251.25]]: comparative -ότερον, ἐνοχλεῖν less acutely, [Refs 1st c.BC+ [1st c.BC: Philodemus Philosophus “περὶ κακιῶν ί” p.21 1st c.AD: Josephus Historicus]]

λαγχάνω
[in LXX: 1Ki.14:47 (לָכַד, see Th., Gr., 38), Wis.8:19, 3Mac 61 * ;]
__1. to obtain by lot, to obtain (in cl., with genitive): with inf. art. (B1., § 36, 3; 71, 3), Luk.1:9; with accusative of thing(s), Act.1:17, 2Pe.1:1.
__2. to draw lots: before περί, Jhn.19:24
