---

LSJ / STEPBible (TFLSJ)
λαγχάνω,
future λήξομαι [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 617e]]; Ionic dialect λάξομαι (compare λάξις) [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 7.144]]: aorist ἔλᾰχον [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 9.367, etc.]]; Epic dialect ἔλλαχον [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [“hymnus ad Cererem” 87, variant for{ἔλλαβεν} in 3rd c.BC: Theocritus Poeta Bucolicus 25.271]]; Epic dialect λάχον [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 4.49, +others]]; Aeolic dialect optative 1st pers. singular λαχόην [Refs 7th c.BC+ [7th-6th c.BC: Sappho Lyrica 9 (λαχοίην 2nd c.AD: Apollonius Dyscolus Grammaticus “de Syntaxi;” 247.25)]]; for λέλᾰχον see infr. IV: perfect εἴληχα [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Septem contra Thebas” 376, 423, etc.]]: pluperfect εἰλήχει [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Phaedo” 107d]]; poetry and Ionic dialect λέλογχα [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “O.” 1.53, 5th c.BC: Bacchylides Lyricus 9.39, 5th c.BC: Empedocles Poeta Philosophus 20.3, 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Troades” 282 (Lyric poetry), 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 7.53, Test. cited in 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 21.82, 1st c.BC: Dionysius Halicarnassensis 4.83, etc.]], but not in early Attic dialect Prose; 3rd.pers. plural λελογχᾰσι (ν) [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 11.304, 5th c.BC: Empedocles Poeta Philosophus 102, but λελᾰχᾱσι [prev. author] 115.5]]; participle λελαχώς [Refs 1st c.BC+ [1st c.BC: Philodemus Gadarensis Epigrammaticus “D.” 1.17]]; Doric dialect 3rd.pers. singular λελόγχει [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [3rd c.BC: Theocritus Poeta Bucolicus 4.40]]: pluperfect ἐλελόγχει [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd c.AD: Lucianus Sophista “Am.” 18]]:—passive, aorist ἐλήχθην [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Lysias Orator 17.8, 4th c.BC: Isaeus Orator 9.24, 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 38.20]]: perfect εἴληγμαι [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Troades” 296, 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 30.34]]; 3rd.pers. plural λελάχαται [Refs 5th c.AD+ [Perictione Philosophus cited in 5th c.AD: Stobaeus, Joannes 4.28.19:]]

__I
with accusative of things, obtain by lot, of spoils, opposed to ἐξαιρεῖσθαι, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 14.233, compare 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 9.367, etc.]]: generally, obtain as one's portion, τὸ γὰρ λάχομεν γέρας ἡμεῖς [Refs 8th c.BC+ [4.49; λαχόντα τε ληΐδος αἶσαν 18.327; πρὸς δαιμόνων ὄλβον 5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “N.” 9.45; μέζονας μοίρας λ. 1st c.AD(?): Heraclitus 25; μοῖραν ἴσην, ὡς αὐτοί περ ἐλάγχανον 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 20.282, compare 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 7.144: with]]infinitive added, ἔλαχον πολιὴν ἅλα ναιέμεν I had the sea for my portion to dwell in, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 15.190, compare 5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “O.” 6.34, 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Eumenides” 931 (_anapaest meter_); ἔλαχ᾽ ἄναξ δούλην σ᾽ ἔχειν 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Troades” 278, compare 282 (Lyric poetry)]]; of a deity as presiding over one's life, ἐμὲ μὲν Κὴρ.. λάχε γεινόμενόν περ [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 23.79; τῶ σκληρῶ μάλα δαίμονος ὅς με λελόγχει 3rd c.BC: Theocritus Poeta Bucolicus 4.40; δαίμων ὁ τὴν ἡμετέραν μοῖραν εἰληχώς 5th c.BC: Lysias Orator 2.78; ὦ δαῖμον, ὅς με.. εἴληχας 4th c.AD: Alciphro Epistolographus 3.49]]: also, especially in perfect, to be the tutelary deity of a place, protect it. [Πὰν] πάντα λόφον.. λέλογχε [Refs 5th c.BC+ [“Hymni Homerici” 19.6; θεοῖσι οἳ Περσίδα γῆν λελόγχασι 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 7.53; παῖ Ῥέας, ἃ πρυτανεῖα λέλογχας 5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “N.” 11.1]]; of Athena, ἣ τὴν ὑμετέραν πόλιν ἔλαχε [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Timaeus” 23d, compare 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Orestes” 319 (Lyric poetry), “Ph.” 1576 (Lyric poetry): _metaphorically_, ἀκέρδεια λέλογχεν θαμινὰ κακαγόρος 5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “O.” 1.53]]: frequently of persons who have a post assigned to them by lot, κλήρῳ νῦν πεπάλασθε διαμπερές, ὅς κε λάχῃσι [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 7.171, compare 179, 23.354, 862]]: with infinitive, κλήρῳ λάχον ἐνθάδ᾽ ἕπεσθαι [Refs 5th c.BC+ [24.400; so πάλῳ λαχεῖν 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Septem contra Thebas” 55, 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 4.94, compare 3.128; ὡς ἐν πύλαις ἕκαστος εἴληχεν πάλον 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Septem contra Thebas” 376: _absolutely_, πρὸς Θύμβρης ἔλαχον Δύκιοι]] had their post assigned near Thymbra, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 10.430]]; ἐπί, ἐν πύλαις λ., [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Septem contra Thebas” 423, 451, etc.]]; λαχών alone, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 3.128, etc.]]; λ. τινὰ διδάσκαλον have him assigned to one by lot, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Antipho Orator 6.11.]]

__I.2
at Athens, obtain an office by lot, ἀρχὰς λαχεῖν, opposed to χειροτονηθῆναι (to be elected), [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 57.25, compare 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Aves” 1111; οὐδεμίαν [ἀρχὴν] λαχὼν οὐδὲ χειροτονηθείς 4th c.BC: Aeschines Orator 1.106: more frequently with]]infinitive, ὁ τῷ κυάμῳ λαχὼν πολεμαρχέειν he who had the lot to be polemarch, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 6.109; ἔλαχον πρότεροι ἀποδιδόναι 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 5.21, compare 35; λαχὼν.. ἱερομνημονεῖν 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Nubes” 623]]; λαχόντος βουλεύειν when I became Member of Council by lot, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 21.111, compare 59.3, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Gorgias” 473e: with _genitive_, λαχεῖν τῶν ἐξιόντων]] to be chosen by lot as one of.., [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 21.133; also οἱ ταμίαι οἱ λαχόντες “IG” 12.91.21]]; λαχεῖν βασιλεύς, ἐπιμελητής, ἱερεύς, etc., [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Lysias Orator 6.4, 4th-3rd c.BC: Dinarchus Orator 2.10, 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 57.47, etc.; ἐπίσκοπος τῷ κυάμῳ λαχών 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Aves” 1022]]; οἱ πεντακόσιοι [οἱ] λαχόντες τῷ κυάμῳ Legal cited in [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Andocides Orator 1.96: _absolutely_, κληρούχους τοὺς λαχόντας]] those on whom the lot fell, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 3.50, compare 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Leges” 765c; τοὺς λαχόντας προέδρους “SIG” 465.6 (Athens, 3rd c.BC); rare except in Athens, λαχὼν ἱερεύς [prev. work]762.12 (Dionysopolis, 1st c.BC), etc.]]

__I.3
as Attic dialect law-term, λαγχάνειν δίκην obtain leave to bring a suit (especially a private suit), probably because the presiding magistrates decided the order of hearing by lot; λ. δίκην τινί against one, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Euthyphro” 5b, “Lg.” 938b, compare 4th c.BC: Aeschines Orator 2.99; ἔγκλημά τινι 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 34.16]]; τὸν εἰληχότα τοῦ κλήρου τὴν δίκην the person suing for the inheritance, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Isaeus Orator 8.3: without τὴν δίκην, εἴληχε μὲν αὑτῷ τῆς θυγατρὸς τῆς Εὐκτήμονος ὡς οὔσης ἐπικλήρου]] he has claimed Euctemon's daughter.., [Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. author] 6.46, compare 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 48.20; λ. τινὶ τοῦ συμβολαίου 5th c.BC: Lysias Orator 17.3; λ. φόνου ἐμαυτῷ 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 21.120]]; also λ. τῷ υἱεῖ τῆς ἐπικλήρου prosecute the claim on his son's behalf, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Andocides Orator 1.121, compare 124; λ. δίκην τινὶ εἰς τοὺς Ἀμφικτύονας χιλίων ταλάντων ὑπέρ τινος 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 59.98, compare 5th-6th c.BC: Isocrates Orator 16.2: _absolutely_, λ. πρὸς τὸν ἄρχοντα 4th c.BC: Isaeus Orator 11.33: _metaphorically_, τοῦ σώματος [τῇ ψυχῇ] δίκην λαχόντος 3rd c.AD: Democritus Epigrammaticus 159]]:—passive, πρὸς οὓς αἱ δίκαι ἐλήχθησαν [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Lysias Orator 17.8; πρὸ τοῦ τὴν δίκην ληχθῆναι 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 54.28: _impersonal_, τούτοις λαγχάνεται]] proceedings are taken, [Refs [[prev. author] 23.76.]]

__II
with genitive partitive, become possessed of a thing, ὥς κεν Ἀχιλλεὺς δώρων ἐκ Πριάμοιο λάχῃ [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 24.76; ἔλαχον κτερέων 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 5.311, compare 6th c.BC: Theognis Elegiacus 934, 5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “I.” 8(7).69, “fragment” 75.6, 5th c.BC: Bacchylides Lyricus 1.56, 9.39, “Lyrica Adespota” 53, 5th c.BC: Empedocles Poeta Philosophus 102, 115.5, 3rd c.AD: Democritus Epigrammaticus 21; εὖ πραπίδων λαχόντα 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Agamemnon” 380 (Lyric poetry); χρυσῆς.. τιμῆς λαχεῖν 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Antigone” 699; οὔ τι μὴ λάχωσι τοῦδε συμμάχου [prev. author] “OC” 450]]; γέννας ἀφθίτου λαχόντες [Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. author] “fragment” 278; διπλοῦ βίου λαχόντες 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Supplices” 1086]]; πατρῴων οὐ λαχών not having obtained thy patrimony, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. author] “Tr.” 1192; τῆς εὐπρεπεστάτης τελευτῆς 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 2.44; δείπνου τε καὶ ὕπνου λαγχάνομεν 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Hiero” 6.9; also χθονὸς λαχεῖν τοσοῦτον ἐνθανεῖν μόνον 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Coloneus” 790; γάμου μέρος λαχοῦσα [prev. author] “Ant.” 918; τύμβου κοινὸν εἰληχὼς μέρος [prev. author] “El.” 1135; τῆς γῆς τὸ πρὸς Νότον εἴληχε Παλλάς [prev. author] “fragment” 24.8.]]

__III
absolutely, draw lots, κατάστασις ἡ διὰ τοῦ λαγχάνειν γιγνομένη [NT+5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Isocrates Orator 7.23, compare 1st c.BC: Diodorus Siculus Historicus 4.63, etc.; περί τινος 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 21 argument 2__ 3, 4, NT.John.19.24.]]

__IV
causal only in Epic dialect reduplicate aorist λέλᾰχον, put in possession of a thing, grant one the rights of.., ὄφρα πυρός με Τρῶες.. λελάχωσι θανόντα [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 7.80, compare 15.350, 23.76]]: later this aorist is used intransitive in [Refs 5th c.AD+ [“Anthologia Graeca” 7.341 (5th c.AD: Proclus Philosophus).]]

__V
intransitive, fall to one's lot or share, ἐς ἑκάστην [νῆα] ἐννέα λάγχανον αἶγες nine goats were allotted to each, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 9.160; αἰὼν δυσαίων ἔλαχεν 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Helena” 214 (Lyric poetry); ὅσοις.. τὸ σωφρονεῖν εἴληχεν [prev. author] “Hipp.” 80; τὸ λαχὸν μέρος ἑκάστῳ τῷ θεῷ 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Leges” 745e, compare “Epin.” 992d; τὴν πρὸς Νότον λαχεῖν φασι Δευκαλίωνι 1st c.BC-1st c.AD: Strabo Geographus 9.5.23.]]

of persons conceiving feelings and the like, λ. θυμόν take heart, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 10.461: frequently in periphrasis, λ. φόβον, ={φοβεῖσθαι}, 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Coloneus” 729]]; αἰδῶ λ., ={αἰδεῖσθαι}, [Refs [[prev. author] “Aj.” 345]]; λ. ὀργήν, ={ὀργίζεσθαι}, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Supplices” 1050: so generally λ. ἀρχήν, ={ἄρχεσθαι}, [prev. author] “IA” 1124]]; λ. ὕψος, ἐπίδοσιν, αὔξησιν, ={ὑψοῦσθαι, ἐπιδιδόναι, αὐξάνεσθαι}, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 1.91, 5th-6th c.BC: Isocrates Orator 4.10, 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “de Generatione Animalium” 732b5, etc.; λ. κακόν τι 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Nubes” 1310]]; λ. νόσον take a disease, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 610d]]; λ. μορφήν, τέλος, etc., [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “de Generatione Animalium” 762a13, 744a21, etc.]]; αἱ οἰκίαι ἐπάλξεις λαμβάνουσαι receiving battlements, having battlements added, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 4.69, compare 115.]]

__4
with infinitive, receive permission to.. , [Refs 1st c.AD+ [“SIG” 996.6 (Smyrna, 1st c.AD).]]

__B
middle, take hold of, lay hold on, with genitive, [σχεδίης] [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 5.325]]; τῆς κεφαλῆς, τῶν γουνάτων, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 4.64, 9.76; χειρός 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Medea” 899, etc.; τοῦ βωμοῦ 5th-6th c.BC: Andocides Orator 1.126, etc.: with double _genitive_, μου λαβόμενος τῆς χειρός 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Charmides” 153b.]]

__B.2
seize and keep hold of, obtain possession of, ἀρχῆς [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Coloneus” 373]]; καιροῦ λαβόμενος seizing the opportunity, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Isaeus Orator 2.28; λ. ἀληθείας 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Politicus” 309d: rarely with _accusative_, τόν.. λελαβέσθαι 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 4.388.]]

__B.3
lay hands upon, χαλεπῶς λαμβάνεσθαί τινος lay rough hands on him, deal hardly with him, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 2.121. δ.]]

__B.4
of place, λ. τῶν ὀρῶν take to the mountains, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 3.24, compare 106]]; Δήλου λαβόμεναι (i.e. αἱ νῆες) reaching Delos, [Refs [[prev. author] 8.80.]]

__B.5
find fault with, censure, τινος [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Leges” 637c, 2nd-3rd c.AD: Philostratus Sophista “Vita Apollonii” 4.22.]]

__B.6
λαβέσθαι ἑαυτοῦ check oneself, [Refs 3rd c.AD+ [3rd c.AD: Heliodorus Scriptor Eroticus 2.24.]]

deep_entry:
Abbott-Smith / STEPBible (TBESG)
λαμπάς, -άδος, ἡ
(λάμπω), [in LXX for לַפִּיד ;]
a torch (frequently fed, like a lamp, with oil): Mat.25:1 ff., Jhn.18:3, Act.20:8, Rev.4:5 8:10.†
(AS)

---

LSJ / STEPBible (TFLSJ)
λαμπάς, άδος, ἡ,

__A
torch, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Septem contra Thebas” 433, 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 3.24, etc.; πευκίνη λ. 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Trachiniae” 1198]]; beacon-light, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Agamemnon” 8, 28, etc.]]; λαμπάδας ἅψασθαι light torches, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Thesmophoriazusae” 655]]; λαμπάδας τινάσσων, in Bacchic ceremonies, [Refs [[prev. author] “Ra.” 340 (Lyric poetry); used in festal processions, φαίνετε τούτῳ (i.e. τῷ Αἰσχύλῳ) λαμπάδας ἱεράς [prev. work] 1525 (_anapaest meter_),compare “Th.” 102 (Lyric poetry).]]

__A.2
faggot, [Refs 2nd c.BC+ [2nd c.BC: Polybius Historicus 3.93.4]]; any light, lamp, λαμπάδες ἀργυραῖ [LXX.Jdt.10.22]; wax-light, [Refs 1st c.AD+ [1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus 2.263f; λ. κηροχίτων “Anthologia Graeca” 6.249 (Antip.)]]; later of oillamps, [NT.Matt.25.3.]

__A.3
metaphorically, of the sun, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Parmenides Poeta Philosophus 10.3, 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Antigone” 879 (Lyric poetry), etc.]]; ἡ 'πιοῦσα λ. the coming light, i.e. the next day, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Medea” 352]]; of lightning, δαμασθεὶς λαμπάσιν κεραυνίοις [Refs [[prev. author] “Supp.” 1011, compare “Ba.” 244, 594 (Lyric poetry)]]; of the Cyclops' eye, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Cratinus Comicus 459.]]

__A.4
meteor, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “de Mundo” 395b11, 1st c.BC: Diodorus Siculus Historicus 16.66, 2nd-3rd c.AD: Dio Cassius Historicus 37.25.]]

__A.II
torch-race, ={λαμπαδηδρομία}, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 6.105, 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “de Vectigalibus” 4.52]]; λαμπάδα δραμεῖν, τρέχειν, run the race, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Vespae” 1203, 4th-3rd c.BC: Theophrastus Philosophus “Characteres” 27.4; τὰς λ. δραμεῖν “IG” 22.1030.9; ἐν ταῖς λ. διηγωνίσθαι [prev. work]1039.20; λαμπάδα φέρειν 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Ranae” 1087 (_anapaest meter_)]]; ἀφιεμένην τὴν λ. θεῶ see the start,[Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. work] 131; τὰς λ. συντελεῖν “IG” 22.1011.9; λ. ἔσται.. ἀφ᾽ ἵππων τῇ θεῷ 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 328a]]; λαμπάδι νικᾶν win in it, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Andocides Orator 4.42, compare “IG” 22.957, +others; λαμπάδα ν. win it, [prev. work]3.106, +others; οἱ νικήσαντες τὴν λ. [prev. work]122,compare “Milet.” 1(7).203a14 (2nd c.BC).]]

__A.II.2
metaphorically, of life, λαμπάδα γὰρ ζωᾶς με δραμεῖν.. ἤθελε δαίμων [Refs [“epigram Gr.” 231 (from Chios)]]; καθάπερ λαμπάδα τὸν βίον παραδιδόντας ἄλλοις ἐξ ἄλλων [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Leges” 776b.]]

__A.III
={λυχνὶς ἀγρία}, Ps.-[Refs 1st c.AD+ [1st c.AD: Dioscorides (Dioscurides) Medicus 3.101.]]

deep_entry:
Abbott-Smith / STEPBible (TBESG)
λαμπρός, -ά, -όν
(λάμπω), [in LXX: Tob.13:11, Wis.6:12 17:20, Sir.29:22 33:13 (Sir.30:25) Sir.31:23, Ep. Je 60 * ;]
bright, brilliant: ποταμός, Rev.22:1 (ΕΥ, clear); ἀστήρ, Rev.22:16; of clothing, brilliant, splendid: Luk.23:11, Act.10:30, Jas.2:2-3, Rev.15:6 18:14 19:8.†
(AS)

---

LSJ / STEPBible (TFLSJ)
λαμπρός, ά, όν,
feminine -ή in Epic dialect [Refs 8th c.BC+ [(8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 17.269, 8th c.BC: Homerus Epicus “Epigrammata” 3.3), but -ά in 8th-7th c.BC: Hesiodus Epicus “Theogonia” 19, 371]]:— bright, radiant, of the sun and stars, λ. φάος ἠελίοιο [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 1.605; ἀστήρ 4.77]]; -ότατος, of Sirius, [Refs [22.30 (and of the same, λαμπρὸν παμφαίνῃσι 5.6)]]; λαμπρὰ σελήνη Hes.[same places],[Refs 5th c.BC+ [compare 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 7.44; πρὶν ἡμέραν λ. γενέσθαι 1st c.BC: Dionysius Halicarnassensis 3.27]]; of the eyes, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Tyrannus” 1483, 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Hecuba” 1045, etc., see below 11.3]]; of metallic bodies, λ. φάλοι, κόρυθες, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 13.132, 17.269]]: neuter as adverb, θώρηκες λαμπρὸν γανόωντες [Refs [13.265.]]

__2
of white cloths and the like, bright, λαμπρὸς δ᾽ ἦν ἠέλιος ὥς [ὁ χιτών] [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 19.234; δέρμα.. -ότατον λευκότητι 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 4.64]]; λ. ἐσθής, = Latin toga candida, [Refs 2nd c.BC+ [2nd c.BC: Polybius Historicus 10.5.1.]]

__3
of water, clear, limpid, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Eumenides” 695, 5th c.BC: Hippocrates Medicus “Aër.” 5, 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Historia Graeca (Hellenica)” 5.3.19]]; of air, λ. ἠήρ [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Hippocrates Medicus “Aër.” 15; αἰθήρ 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Medea” 829 (_superlative_, Lyric poetry).]]

__4
of sound or voice, clear, distinct, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Philebus” 51d, 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 19.199; λαμπρὰ κηρύσσειν 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Heraclidae” 864; φωνὴ -οτέρα 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Historia Animalium” 545a12]]; opposed to φ. ἀσαφής, [Refs 1st c.AD+ [[prev. author] “Aud.” 801b22; λαμπρὸν ἀνολολύξαι 1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus 2.768d; compare λάμπω 1.2.]]

__5
metaphorically, of vigorous action, λ. ἄνεμος a keen wind, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 2.96, compare 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Agamemnon” 1180]]; λ. ἤδη καὶ μέγας καθιείς swooping down like a fresh and mighty breeze, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Equites” 430, compare 760]]; λαμπρὸς φανήσεται he will come furiously forth, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Heraclidae” 280]]; λ. μάχη a keenly contested battle, [Refs 2nd c.BC+ [2nd c.BC: Polybius Historicus 10.12.5; - ότερος κίνδυνος [prev. author] 1.45.9.]] adverb -ρῶς, ἐπικείμενοι vigorously, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 7.71]]; utterly, λ. ἡττῆσθαι, λ. περιεστοιχίσθαι, [Refs 3rd c.AD+ [3rd c.AD: Heliodorus Scriptor Eroticus 4.4, 9.1.]]

__6
metaphorically also, clear, manifest, μαρτύρια [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Eumenides” 797; ταῦτ᾽ ἐπειδὴ λαμπρὰ συμβαίνει 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Trachiniae” 1174; ἴχνη 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Cynegeticus” 5.5; γεγενημένης τῆς νίκης λ. ἤδη 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 7.55]]; λ. φυγή decisive, [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd c.AD: Arrianus Historicus “Anabasis” 2.11.3]]. adverb - ρῶς, κοὐδὲν αἰνικτηρίως [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Prometheus Vinctus” 833; λελυμένων λ. τῶν σπονδῶν 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 2.7; λ. νικᾶν 2nd c.AD: Arrianus Historicus “Anabasis” 2.10.4]]; λαμπρῶς ἐλέγετο it was said without concealment, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 8.67.]]

__II
of persons, well-known, illustrious by deeds, station, etc., λ. ἐν τῇσι Ἀθήνῃσι [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 6.125; ἐν τοῖσι πολέμοισι ἐὼν -ότατος [prev. author] 7.154]]; λ. ἐν [τοῖς κινδύνοις] [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 19.269; - οτάτους γενομένους τῶν καθ᾽ ἑαυτούς 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 1.138; ἐξ ἀδόξων γενέσθαι λ. 5th-6th c.BC: Isocrates Orator 5.89; λ. ἐς γένος 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Electra” 37; ἐν λόγοις [prev. author] “Supp.” [902]]]; as honorary title, -ότατος, = Latin clarissimus, [Refs [Inscriptiones Graecae 14.911, 7.91, etc.]]; of cities, councils, etc., ἡ λαμπρὰ τῶν Μιλησίων μητρόπολις [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [“SIG” 906 A 4 (4th c.AD), compare 867.4 (_superlative_, Ephesus, 2nd c.AD)]]; of actions, etc., ἔργον οὐδὲν ἀπ᾽ αὐτῶν λ. γίνεται [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 3.72; τὸν βίον λ. ποιεῖσθαι 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Coloneus” 1144; τὸ λ. φῶς ἀποσβεννὺς γένους “Tragica Adespota” 9.]]

__II.2
magnificent, munificent, λ. ἐν ταῖς λειτουργίαις [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Isocrates Orator 3.56, compare 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 21.153 (_superlative_)]]; ὁ λ. καὶ πλούσιος οὗτος [Refs [[prev. work] 174.]] adverb - ρῶς, χορηγεῖν [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Antipho Orator 2.2.12, 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Ethica Nicomachea” 1122b22.]]

__II.3
bright, joyous, λ. ὥσπερ ὄμματι, of the bearer of good news, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Tyrannus” 81, compare 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Historia Graeca (Hellenica)” 4.5.10]]; λαμπρὸν ἐξέπεμψα with bright hopes, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Electra” 1130; λ. ταῖς ἐλπίσιν 4th c.AD: Julianus Imperator “Orationes” 2.64b]]; also ὄμματι δέρκομαι λαμπρόν, of one clear in conscience, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “N.” 7.66.]]

__III
of outward appearance, splendid, brilliant, νυμφίον.. λ. ὄντα [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Pax” 859]]; of a horse, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [“IG” 22.956.87, 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “de Equitandi ratione” 11.1; in dress, [prev. author] “Cyn.” 2.4.5 (_superlative_)]]; of youthful bloom, ὥρᾳ ἡλικίας λ. [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 6.54]]; of healthy look, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Hippocrates Medicus “Aër.” 24;]] of property, dress, etc., εἴ τί γ᾽ ἔστι λ. καὶ καλόν [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Plutus” 144, compare 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Fragmenta” 316.5; κατασκευή 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Symposium” 1.4 (_comparative_)]]; λ. κάλλος beaming beauty, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Phaedrus” 250b, etc.: more generally λ. τι ποιεῖν 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 5.4.15]]; τὸ λ. splendour, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “N.” 8.34; λ. γενέσθαι βουλόμεσθα τοὺς γάμους Euangelus Comicus 1.3]]. adverb -ῶς, opposed to λιτῶς, [Refs 1st c.BC+ [1st c.BC: Philodemus Philosophus “de Morte - Papiri Ercolanesi” 30]]: superlative -ότατα [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 2.4.1]]; later -οτάτως [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [“JHS” 44.26 (Ancyra, 2nd c.AD).]]

__III.2
of language, brilliant, τῶν διθυράμβων τὰ λ. [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Aves” 1388]]; λ. λέξις ornamental diction, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Poetica” 1460b4; λόγος 2nd c.AD: Hermogenes Rhetor “περὶ ἰδεῶν” 1.9.]]

__IV
Astrology texts, of degrees in a zodiacal sign, ἑκάστου ζῳδίου λαμπρὰς μοίρας ἐξέθεντο [Refs 4th c.AD+ [4th c.AD: Hephaestio Astrologus 1.1, +others]]

__V
for adverb -ρῶς, see above [Refs [1.5 and 6, 11.2, 111.1.]]

brilliancy, splendour, λ. καὶ τάξις τοῦ στρατεύματος [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 1.2.18]]; of a horse, [Refs [[prev. author] “Eq.” 11.9]]; of arms, [Refs 2nd c.BC+ [2nd c.BC: Polybius Historicus 11.9.1, 2nd c.AD: Arrianus Historicus “Anabasis” 1.14.4.]]

feminine -ή in Epic dialect [Refs 8th c.BC+ [(8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 17.269, 8th c.BC: Homerus Epicus “Epigrammata” 3.3), but -ά in 8th-7th c.BC: Hesiodus Epicus “Theogonia” 19, 371]]:— bright, radiant, of the sun and stars, λ. φάος ἠελίοιο [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 1.605; ἀστήρ 4.77]]; -ότατος, of Sirius, [Refs [22.30 (and of the same, λαμπρὸν παμφαίνῃσι 5.6)]]; λαμπρὰ σελήνη Hes.[same places],[Refs 5th c.BC+ [compare 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 7.44; πρὶν ἡμέραν λ. γενέσθαι 1st c.BC: Dionysius Halicarnassensis 3.27]]; of the eyes, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Tyrannus” 1483, 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Hecuba” 1045, etc., see below 11.3]]; of metallic bodies, λ. φάλοι, κόρυθες, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 13.132, 17.269]]: neuter as adverb, θώρηκες λαμπρὸν γανόωντες [Refs [13.265.]]

__2
of white cloths and the like, bright, λαμπρὸς δ᾽ ἦν ἠέλιος ὥς [ὁ χιτών] [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 19.234; δέρμα.. -ότατον λευκότητι 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 4.64]]; λ. ἐσθής, = Latin toga candida, [Refs 2nd c.BC+ [2nd c.BC: Polybius Historicus 10.5.1.]]

__3
of water, clear, limpid, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Eumenides” 695, 5th c.BC: Hippocrates Medicus “Aër.” 5, 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Historia Graeca (Hellenica)” 5.3.19]]; of air, λ. ἠήρ [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Hippocrates Medicus “Aër.” 15; αἰθήρ 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Medea” 829 (_superlative_, Lyric poetry).]]

__4
of sound or voice, clear, distinct, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Philebus” 51d, 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 19.199; λαμπρὰ κηρύσσειν 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Heraclidae” 864; φωνὴ -οτέρα 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Historia Animalium” 545a12]]; opposed to φ. ἀσαφής, [Refs 1st c.AD+ [[prev. author] “Aud.” 801b22; λαμπρὸν ἀνολολύξαι 1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus 2.768d; compare λάμπω 1.2.]]

__5
metaphorically, of vigorous action, λ. ἄνεμος a keen wind, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 2.96, compare 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Agamemnon” 1180]]; λ. ἤδη καὶ μέγας καθιείς swooping down like a fresh and mighty breeze, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Equites” 430, compare 760]]; λαμπρὸς φανήσεται he will come furiously forth, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Heraclidae” 280]]; λ. μάχη a keenly contested battle, [Refs 2nd c.BC+ [2nd c.BC: Polybius Historicus 10.12.5; - ότερος κίνδυνος [prev. author] 1.45.9.]] adverb -ρῶς, ἐπικείμενοι vigorously, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 7.71]]; utterly, λ. ἡττῆσθαι, λ. περιεστοιχίσθαι, [Refs 3rd c.AD+ [3rd c.AD: Heliodorus Scriptor Eroticus 4.4, 9.1.]]

__6
metaphorically also, clear, manifest, μαρτύρια [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Eumenides” 797; ταῦτ᾽ ἐπειδὴ λαμπρὰ συμβαίνει 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Trachiniae” 1174; ἴχνη 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Cynegeticus” 5.5; γεγενημένης τῆς νίκης λ. ἤδη 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 7.55]]; λ. φυγή decisive, [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd c.AD: Arrianus Historicus “Anabasis” 2.11.3]]. adverb - ρῶς, κοὐδὲν αἰνικτηρίως [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Prometheus Vinctus” 833; λελυμένων λ. τῶν σπονδῶν 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 2.7; λ. νικᾶν 2nd c.AD: Arrianus Historicus “Anabasis” 2.10.4]]; λαμπρῶς ἐλέγετο it was said without concealment, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 8.67.]]

__II
of persons, well-known, illustrious by deeds, station, etc., λ. ἐν τῇσι Ἀθήνῃσι [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 6.125; ἐν τοῖσι πολέμοισι ἐὼν -ότατος [prev. author] 7.154]]; λ. ἐν [τοῖς κινδύνοις] [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 19.269; - οτάτους γενομένους τῶν καθ᾽ ἑαυτούς 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 1.138; ἐξ ἀδόξων γενέσθαι λ. 5th-6th c.BC: Isocrates Orator 5.89; λ. ἐς γένος 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Electra” 37; ἐν λόγοις [prev. author] “Supp.” [902]]]; as honorary title, -ότατος, = Latin clarissimus, [Refs [Inscriptiones Graecae 14.911, 7.91, etc.]]; of cities, councils, etc., ἡ λαμπρὰ τῶν Μιλησίων μητρόπολις [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [“SIG” 906 A 4 (4th c.AD), compare 867.4 (_superlative_, Ephesus, 2nd c.AD)]]; of actions, etc., ἔργον οὐδὲν ἀπ᾽ αὐτῶν λ. γίνεται [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 3.72; τὸν βίον λ. ποιεῖσθαι 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Coloneus” 1144; τὸ λ. φῶς ἀποσβεννὺς γένους “Tragica Adespota” 9.]]

__II.2
magnificent, munificent, λ. ἐν ταῖς λειτουργίαις [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Isocrates Orator 3.56, compare 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 21.153 (_superlative_)]]; ὁ λ. καὶ πλούσιος οὗτος [Refs [[prev. work] 174.]] adverb - ρῶς, χορηγεῖν [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Antipho Orator 2.2.12, 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Ethica Nicomachea” 1122b22.]]

__II.3
bright, joyous, λ. ὥσπερ ὄμματι, of the bearer of good news, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Tyrannus” 81, compare 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Historia Graeca (Hellenica)” 4.5.10]]; λαμπρὸν ἐξέπεμψα with bright hopes, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Electra” 1130; λ. ταῖς ἐλπίσιν 4th c.AD: Julianus Imperator “Orationes” 2.64b]]; also ὄμματι δέρκομαι λαμπρόν, of one clear in conscience, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “N.” 7.66.]]

__III
of outward appearance, splendid, brilliant, νυμφίον.. λ. ὄντα [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Pax” 859]]; of a horse, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [“IG” 22.956.87, 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “de Equitandi ratione” 11.1; in dress, [prev. author] “Cyn.” 2.4.5 (_superlative_)]]; of youthful bloom, ὥρᾳ ἡλικίας λ. [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 6.54]]; of healthy look, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Hippocrates Medicus “Aër.” 24;]] of property, dress, etc., εἴ τί γ᾽ ἔστι λ. καὶ καλόν [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Plutus” 144, compare 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Fragmenta” 316.5; κατασκευή 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Symposium” 1.4 (_comparative_)]]; λ. κάλλος beaming beauty, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Phaedrus” 250b, etc.: more generally λ. τι ποιεῖν 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 5.4.15]]; τὸ λ. splendour, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “N.” 8.34; λ. γενέσθαι βουλόμεσθα τοὺς γάμους Euangelus Comicus 1.3]]. adverb -ῶς, opposed to λιτῶς, [Refs 1st c.BC+ [1st c.BC: Philodemus Philosophus “de Morte - Papiri Ercolanesi” 30]]: superlative -ότατα [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 2.4.1]]; later -οτάτως [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [“JHS” 44.26 (Ancyra, 2nd c.AD).]]

__III.2
of language, brilliant, τῶν διθυράμβων τὰ λ. [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Aves” 1388]]; λ. λέξις ornamental diction, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Poetica” 1460b4; λόγος 2nd c.AD: Hermogenes Rhetor “περὶ ἰδεῶν” 1.9.]]

__IV
Astrology texts, of degrees in a zodiacal sign, ἑκάστου ζῳδίου λαμπρὰς μοίρας ἐξέθεντο [Refs 4th c.AD+ [4th c.AD: Hephaestio Astrologus 1.1, +others]]

__V
for adverb -ρῶς, see above [Refs [1.5 and 6, 11.2, 111.1.]]

λάμπω,
[Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 13.474, etc.]]; Ionic dialectIterat. λάμπεσκεν [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Empedocles Poeta Philosophus 84.6, 3rd c.BC: Theocritus Poeta Bucolicus (see. below)]]: future -ψω [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Electra” 66, “Anthologia Graeca” 6.249 (Antip.)]]: aorist ἔλαμψα [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 6.82 (variant), 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Tyrannus” 473 (Lyric poetry), 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Vespae” 62, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Epistulae” 335d:]]perfect λέλαμπα (in present sense) [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Andromache” 1025, “Tr.” 1295 (both Lyric poetry)]]:—middle, [Refs [“Hymni Homerici” 31.13, etc.:]]imperfect ἐλαμπόμην, Epic dialect λαμπ-, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 6.319, 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Medea” 1194]]: future λάμψομαι (ἐλλ-) [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.80]]:—passive, future λαμφθήσομαι (ἐλλ-) [Refs 3rd c.AD+ [3rd c.AD: Plotinus Philosophus 2.9.3]]: aorist ἐλάμφθην [Refs 1st c.AD+ [1st c.AD: Josephus Historicus “Bellum Judaicum” 4.10.1]] (περι-): from these late forms of passive must be distinguished the similar Ionic dialect forms of λαμβάνω:—give light, shine, of the gleam of arms, τῆλε δὲ χαλκὸς λάμφ᾽ ὥς τε στεροπή [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 10.154, compare 11.66]]; λάμπε δὲ χαλκῷ, of Hector,[Refs 5th c.BC+ [12.463; φῶς λάμπεσκεν 5th c.BC: Empedocles Poeta Philosophus [same place]; ἀπ᾽ ὀφθαλμῶν δὲ κακὸν πῦρ.. λάμπεσκε 3rd c.BC: Theocritus Poeta Bucolicus 24.19]]; of the eyes, ὀφθαλμὼ δ᾽ ἄρα οἱ πυρὶ λάμπετον [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 13.474]]; of the sun, [Refs 6th c.BC+ [6th c.BC: Solon Lyricus 13.23, etc.]]; of fire, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Antigone” 1007; ἄλσος λάμπεν ὑπὸ δεινοῖο θεοῦ 8th-7th c.BC: Hesiodus Epicus “Scutum Herculis” 71]]:—middle, κόρυθος -ομένης [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 16.71; λάμπετο δουρὸς αἰχμή 6.319; τεύχεσι λ. 20.46, 8th-7th c.BC: Hesiodus Epicus “Scutum Herculis” 60; ὄσσε -έσθην 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 15.608; πεδίον.. λάμπετο χαλκῷ 20.156, etc.]]

__2
of sound, ring loud and clear, παιὰν δὲ λάμπει [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Tyrannus” 186 (Lyric poetry), compare 473 (Lyric poetry);compare λαμπρός 1.4.]]

__3
metaphorically, shine forth, be famous or conspicuous, λάμπει κλέος [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “O.” 1.23; ἀρετά [prev. author] “I.” 1.22, 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Andromache” 776 (Lyric poetry); δίκα δὲ λάμπει μὲν ἐν δυσκάπνοις δώμασιν 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Agamemnon” 773 (Lyric poetry); τέκνων οἷς ἂν λάμπωσιν νεάνιδες ἧβαι 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Ion” 476 (Lyric poetry); κάλλος 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Phaedrus” 250d.]]

__3.b
Astrology texts, of a planet, occupy a favourable position, [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd c.AD: Ptolemaeus Mathematicus “Tetrabiblos” 51.]]

__4
of persons, φαιδρὸς λάμποντι μετώπῳ with beaming face, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Equites” 550 (_anapaest meter_)]]; shine, gain glory, οὐδ᾽ εἰ Κλέων γ᾽ ἔλαμψε [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [[prev. author] “V.” [same place]; ἐν ἄλλοις βουσὶν ἰὼν λάμπεσκεν 3rd c.BC: Theocritus Poeta Bucolicus 25.141.]]

__II
transitive, cause to shine, illumine, δόλιον ἀκταῖς ἀστέρα λάμψας [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Helena” 1131 (Lyric poetry), compare “Ion” 83 (_anapaest meter_), “Ph.” 226, “Anthologia Graeca” [where cited], “Tragica Adespota” 33, etc.]]—Found chiefly in poetry and Comedy texts, though the present and imperfect occur in [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 3.1.11 (_middle_), “Mem.” 4.7.7, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Phaedrus” 250d, 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “de Anima” 419a4]], and late Prose, and the aorist in [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 6.82 (variant), 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “de Mundo” 395a15, 1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus “Timoleon” 3, etc.]]

λανθάνω
[in LXX for עָלַם ni., etc. ;]
to escape notice, be hidden (from): Mrk.7:24, Luk.8:47; with accusative of person(s), Act.26:26, 2Pe.3:5 3:8; as in common cl. idiom, before ptcp., ἔλαθον ξενίσαντες, entertained unawares, Heb.13:2 (cf. ἐκ-, ἐπι-λανθάνω).†
(AS)

---

LSJ / STEPBible (TFLSJ)
λανθάνω,
[Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “Fragmenta.” 75.13, etc.]]:—also λήθω (which is the form of the active generally used in compounds, δια-λανθάνω being the sole exception), [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 23.323, 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Tyrannus” 1325 (Lyric poetry), 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Symposium” 4.48]]; Doric dialect λάθω [ᾱ] [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “El.” 222 (Lyric poetry)]]; infinitive

__A
λᾱθέμεν [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “O.” 1.64]]: imperfect ἐλάνθανον [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 13.721, etc.; ἔληθον 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 19.151, 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Electra” 1359]]; Epic dialect λῆθον [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 15.461]]; Ionic dialect λήθεσκεν [Refs [24.13]]: future λήσω [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 11.102, 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Ecclesiazusae” 98, etc.]]; Aeolic dialect infinitive λᾱσην [Refs 7th c.BC+ [7th-6th c.BC: Alcaeus Lyricus “Supp.” 22.8]]; Doric dialect λᾱσῶ [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [3rd c.BC: Theocritus Poeta Bucolicus 14.9, +others, so (in late writers) λήσομαι, see below with 11]]: aorist 1 ἔλησα [Refs 8th c.BC+ [2nd c.BC: Nicander Epicus “Alexipharmaca” 280 (but 8th c.BC: Homerus Epicus has ἐπ-έλησα, 7th-6th c.BC: Alcaeus Lyricus ἐξ-έλᾱσα, in causal sense)]]: aorist 2 ἔλᾰθον [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 17.676, etc. (for λέλᾰθον, see infr. B)]]: perfect λέληθα [Refs 7th c.BC+ [7th-6th c.BC(?): Semonides Iambographus 7.9, 6th c.BC: Solon Lyricus 13.27]]; Aeolic dialect participle λελᾱθων [Refs 7th c.BC+ [7th-6th c.BC: Alcaeus Lyricus “Supp.” 26.8:]]pluperfect ἐλελήθειν, Attic dialect -ήθη, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 8.33, 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Equites” 822, “Nu.” 380, 2nd c.AD: Lucianus Sophista “Pr.Im.” 15]]; Ionic dialect3rd.pers. singular ἐλελήθεε [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 6.79.]]

__B
causal ληθάνω, aorist 2 λέλᾰθον, see below [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Bacchylides Lyricus]]

__C
middle and passive, λανθάνομαι [Refs 8th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Poetica” 1455a25 (assuming variant), λήθομαι 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 11.790, 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Agamemnon” 39]]; Doric dialect λάθομαι [ᾱ] [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “O.” 8.72]]: Epic dialect imperfect λανθανόμην [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 12.227]]: future λήσομαι [Refs [1.308]]; Doric dialect λᾱσεῦμαι [Refs 5th c.BC+ [3rd c.BC: Theocritus Poeta Bucolicus 4.39, also λελήσομαι 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Alcestis” 198:]]aorist 1 ἐλησάμην or λησάμην only in late Epic dialect, [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [3rd c.BC: Maiistas Epicus 47, 2nd c.BC: Moschus Bucolicus 3.62]] (Doric dialect λᾱς-), [Refs 4th c.AD+ [4th c.AD(?): Quintus Smyrnaeus Epicus 3.99, etc.]]; also ἐλήσθην, Doric dialect infinitive λασθῆμεν [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [3rd c.BC: Theocritus Poeta Bucolicus 2.46, compare διαλανθάνω:]]aorist 2 ἐλᾰθόμην, Epic dialect λαθ-, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 13.835, 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Hippolytus” 289]]: rare in Prose except in compounds, [Refs 1st c.AD+ [1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus “Caesar” 38]]; also Epic dialect reduplicate λελάθοντο, etc., see below c: perfect λέλησμαι [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Electra” 342, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Phaedrus” 252a]]; Epic dialect λέλασμαι, participle λελασμένος, etc.; compare ἐπιλήθω.

__A
in most of the active tenses, escape notice (frequently joined with a negative):—Constr.:

__A.1
with accusative person only, escape his notice, λάθε δ᾽ Ἕκτορα [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 22.277; οὐδέ σε λήσει 23.326; οὐ λῆθε Διὸς πυκινὸν νόον 15.461, compare 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 11.102, +others; [τοῦτον] οὐκ ἔστι λαθεῖν ὄμματα φωτός 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Agamemnon” 796 (_anapaest meter_); οὐ λάθει μ᾽ ὀργά 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Electra” 222 (Lyric poetry), compare “Ph.” 207 (Lyric poetry); τουτί μ᾽ ἐλελήθειν 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Nubes” 380]]; εἰ λανθάνει σε perhaps you don't know, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-3rd c.BC: Menander Comicus “Σαμία” 78: _impersonal_, λεληθέναι οὐ θαυμάζω τὸ πλῆθος περὶ τούτου]] it escaped the notice of the people, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Hiero” 2.5]]; σὲ δὲ λέληθεν περὶ τοῦτο ὡς.. [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Leges” 903c.]]

__A.2
most frequently with a participle added, in which case we usually translate the participle by a Verb, and express λανθάνω by an adverb, unawares, without being observed; either,

__A.2.a
with accusative person, ἄλλον τινὰ λήθω μαρνάμενος I am unseen by others while fighting, i.e. [Refs [1 fight]]unseen by them, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 13.273; πάντας ἐλάνθανε δάκρυα λείβων 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 8.93, compare 12.17, 220, 19.88, +others, 5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “O.” 1.64, 6.36, 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 8.25: frequently in Trag. and _Attic dialect_, μὴ λάθῃ με προσπεσών]] lest he come on unseen by me, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Philoctetes” 46, compare 156 (Lyric poetry)]]; ὅπως μὴ λήσουσιν αὐτοὺς αἱ νῆες.. ἀφορμηθεῖσαι should put to sea without their observing them, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 8.10]]; or,

__A.2.b
without an accusative, φονέα ἐλάνθανε βόσκων he maintained the murderer unawares, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.44; λέληθας ἐχθρὸς ὤν 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Tyrannus” 415; δουλεύων λέληθας 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Vespae” 517; συνέβη δὲ ὑπερημέρῳ γενομένῳ λαθεῖν 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 21.89]]: the reflexive pronoun may be supplied and is sometimes added, λέληθεν αὑτὸν τοῖς ξυνοῦσιν ὢν βαρύς [Refs 8th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Fragmenta” 103; ἕως σαυτὸν λάθοις διαρραγείς 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Pax” 32, compare “Nu.” 242, 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 6.3.22: sometimes, however, a different object must be supplied from the context, βάλλοντες ἐλάνθανον (not ἑαυτούς, but Τρῶας) 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 13.721; ἐλάνθανε [πάντας] ἔχων 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 8.5]]; μὴ διαφθαρεὶς λάθῃ [τινὰ ὁ βίος] [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Philoctetes” 506; μὴ λάθῃ [ἡμᾶς] φύγδα βάς 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Eumenides” 256 (Lyric poetry), compare 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 4.133, etc.]] —In a few examples this _construction_ is reversed, and λαθών is put in the participle, as in our idiom, ἀπὸ τείχεος ἆλτο λαθών (for ἔλαθεν ἁλόμενος) [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 12.390; ἣ.. λήθουσά μ᾽ ἐξέπινες 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Antigone” 532.]]

__A.3
rarely with accusative et infinitive, μή σε λαθέτω ὑπερτιθέμεν let it not escape thee to.., i.e. forget not to.., [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “P.” 5.23; ἔλαθεν αὐτὸν σύνθημα δοῦναι 1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus “Aristides” 17]]; σφᾶς λέληθε Θεόδωρον εἶναι it has been unnoticed that it was.., [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd c.AD: Pausanias Periegeta 9.41.1.]]

__A.4
followed by a relative clause, οὐδέ με λήθεις, ὅττι θεῶν τίς σ᾽ ἦγε thou escapest me not, it is not unknown to me, that some god led thee, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 24.563; οὐδέ ἑ λήθει, ὅππως.. 23.323]]; ἐδόκεες θεοὺς λήσειν οἷα ἐμηχανῶ thou thought'st to escape the gods' notice in.., [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 8.106; οὔκουν με.. οἷα πράττεις λανθάνει 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Equites” 465]]; οὐ λανθάνεις με, ὅτι.. [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Memorabilia” 3.5.24, compare “Smp.” 3.6, 13]]; ὁ γείτων λ. τινὰ οὐ μόνον ὅτι πράττει, ἀλλ᾽ εἰ.. [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Theaetetus” 174b.]]

__A.5
absolutely, escape notice or detection, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Trachiniae” 455, 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 1.37, 69, +others; λάθε βιώσας 4th-3rd c.BC: Epicurus Philosophus “Fragmenta” 551; λανθάνει τὸ οὖρον προσπῖπτον 5th c.BC: Hippocrates Medicus “Κωακαὶ προγνώσιες” 464.]]

__B
causal, make one forget a thing, with genitive of things, in compounds ἐκληθάνω, ἐπι-λήθ; the simple Verb only in Epic dialect reduplicate aorist 2, ὄφρα.. λελάθῃ ὀδυνάων that.. he may cause him to forget his pains, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 15.60; πόλιν λελάθοιτε συντυχιᾶν “Lyrica Adespota” 140.9: but]]

__B.II
in late Epic dialect, λέλαθον, ={ἔλαθον}, escaped notice of, ἑὸν νόον, τοκῆας, [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [3rd c.BC: Apollonius Rhodius Epicus 2.226, 3.779, compare 5th-6th c.AD: Orphica “Argonautica” 876.]]

__C
middle and passive, let a thing escape one, forget,

__C.1
forget simply, in present (absolutely), σὺ δὲ λήθεαι [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 11.790: with _genitive_, Κίρκης μὲν ἐφημοσύνης.. λανθανόμην 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 12.227, compare 5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “O.” 8.72; οὔ ποτε λήσομαι αὐτῶν 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 1.308; ἄλγος, οὗ ποτ᾽ οὐ λελήσεται 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Alcestis” 198]]: mostly in aorist 2, ἀλκῆς λαθέσθαι [Refs 8th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Supplices” 731; νόστου τε λαθέσθαι 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 9.97; πῶς ἂν.. Ὀδυσῆος.. λαθοίμη; 1.65]]: also in reduplicate aorist, οὐδὲ σέθεν.. θεοὶ μάκαρες λελάθοντο [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 4.127; μή τίς μοι ἀπειλάων λελαθέσθω 16.200; οὐ δυνάμην λελαθέσθ᾽ Ἄτης 19.136 (but in 8th-7th c.BC: Hesiodus Epicus “Theogonia” 471 like the _active_, ὅπως λελάθοιτο τεκοῦσα]] that she might bear unknown): so in perfect, τῶν δὲ λέλασται [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 5.834; ἐμεῖο λελασμένος 23.69; κείνου λελῆσθαι 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Electra” 342, etc.; ἑταίρων πάντων λέλησται 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Phaedrus” 252a]]: with a relative clause, λελασμένος ὅσσ᾽ ἐπεπόνθει [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 13.92]]: future middle in passive sense, once in [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus, οὐδέ ποτε λησόμενον οἷον ἔφυ κακόν]] never will be forgotten, El.1249 (Lyric poetry); compare ἐπιλανθάνω.

__C.2
forget purposely, pass over, ἢ λάθετ᾽ ἢ οὐκ ἐνόησεν either he chose to forget it.., [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 9.537; μαθοῦσιν αὐδῶ, κοὐ μαθοῦσι λήθομαι 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Agamemnon” 39.]]

__C.II
in later writers future middle is used like active, escape notice, ἡμᾶς [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Analytica Priora” 66a31, compare 3rd c.BC: Apollonius Rhodius Epicus 3.737, 2nd c.AD: Lucianus Sophista “Sacr.” 14: _absolutely_, 4th c.AD: Alciphro Epistolographus 3.52.]]

λαός, -οῦ, ὁ,
[in LXX very frequently for עַם, Gen.14:16, al.; occasionally for לְאֹם ( Gen.25:23, al.), etc. ;]
a word rarely found in Att. prose;
__1. the people at large (Hom., al.), esp. of people assembled: Mat.27:25, Luk.1:21 3:15 al.; pl. (Hom., al., π.; see MM, xvi), Act.4:27.
__2. a people, those of the same race and language (Pind., Æsch., al.: in LXX, Gen.26:11, Exo.9:16, al.): joined with γλῶσσα, φυλή, ἔθνος, Rev.5:9 7:9 11:9, al.; pl., Luk.2:31, Rom.15:11; esp. as almost always in LXX, of Israel, Mat.4:23, Mrk.7:6, Luk.2:10, Jhn.11:50, Heb.2:17, al.; opposite to τ. ἔθνη, Act.26:17, 23 Rom.15:10; πρεσβύτεροι (πρῶτοι, etc.) τοῦ λ., Mat.21:23, Luk.19:17, Act.4:8, al.; ὁ λ. μου (αὐτοῦ, τ. θεοῦ), Mat.2:6, Luk.1:68, Heb.11:25, al.; of the people disting. from the rulers and priests ( I Est.1:10, Jdth.8:9, al.), Mat.26:5, Luk.20:19, Heb.5:3,  al.; of Christians, as the people of God, Act.15:14, Rom.9:25, 26 Heb.4:9; περιούσιος, Tit.2:14; εἰς περιποίησιν, 1Pe.2:9 (LXX).
SYN.: see: δῆμος. (AS)

LSJ / STEPBible (TFLSJ)
λᾱός, ὁ,
Ionic dialect ληός [Refs 6th c.BC+ [6th c.BC: Hipponax Iambographus 88, 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 5.42]] (variant{λαόν}, which is in all Mss. in [Refs 6th c.BC+ [4.148), conjecture in 6th c.BC: Mimnermus Lyricus 14.9]]; Attic dialect λεώς, which is also used in [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.22, 8.136, while the form λαός is sometimes used in Trag., and once or twice even in Comedy texts (see. below 1.3): also in Inscrr. and Papyrus (see. below)]] and in late Prose, as Foed.Byzantine cited in [Refs 5th c.BC+ [2nd c.BC: Polybius Historicus 4.52.7 (_plural_), 1st c.BC-1st c.AD: Strabo Geographus 14.4.3 (_plural_), 1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus 2.1096b, etc. (both forms in proper nouns, Λεωβώτης 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 7.204, Λαβώτας 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Historia Graeca (Hellenica)” 1.2.18, etc.).]]

__1
in [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad”, λαός]] (λαοί) usually means men, i.e. soldiers, both of the whole army and smaller divisions, κριτὸς ἔγρετο λ. Ἀχαιῶν [Refs [7.434; λαὸν ἀγείρειν 16.129; πολὺν ὤλεσα λαόν 2.115: _plural_, ἅμα τῷ γε.. ἄριστοι λ. ἕποντ᾽ [prev. work] 578; στίχες ἀσπιστάων λ. 4.91]]; periphrastic, στρατὸς λαῶν[Refs [[prev. work] 76; λαῶν ἔθνος 13.495]]; mostly including both foot and horse, as [Refs [2.809]]; but sometimes λαός denotes foot, as opposed to horse, [Refs [7.342]]; also, a land army, opposed to a fleet, [Refs [4.76, 9.424, 10.14]]; also, the common men, opposed to their leaders, [Refs [2.365, 13.108]]; but

__2
in [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey”, λαοί, more rarely λαός]], almost always means men or people; as subjects of a prince, e.g. [Refs 8th c.BC+ [3.214, 305, +others (λαοί is sometimes so used in 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad”, e.g. 17.226, 24.611]]; λαοὶ ἀγροιῶται country-folk, [Refs [11.676]]; work-people, [Refs [17.390)]]; of sailors, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 14.248; so after 8th c.BC: Homerus Epicus, ναυτικὸς λεώς]] seafaring folk, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Persae” 383; πᾶς ὁ χειρῶναξ λεώς 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Fragmenta” 844; ὁ γεωργικὸς λεώς 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Pax” 920 (Lyric poetry)]]: in singular, slave, τὸν Εὐρυσθέως λεών, of Heracles, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Hecataeus Milesius Historicus 23 1st c.AD: Josephus Historicus]]; and so perhaps λεὼς αὔτοικος [Refs [“GDI” 5533e (from Zeleia): more generally, μέροπες λαοί]], i.e. mankind, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Supplices” 90 (Lyric poetry)]]; λ. ἐγχώριοι the natives,[Refs 8th c.BC+ [[prev. work] 517, compare 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 6.194]]; especially in Egypt, of the fellahin, [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [“PRev.Laws” 42.11 - 16 (3rd c.BC), “PSI” 4.380.5 (3rd c.BC), etc.]]; civil population, opposed to priests and soldiers, [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [“OGI” 90.12 (Rosetta, 2nd c.BC), compare 225.8 (Milet., 3rd c.BC), +others]]

__3
people assembled, as in the theatre, ὁ πολὺς λαῶν ὄχλος [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Ranae” 676, compare 219 (both Lyric poetry)]]; especially in the Ecclesia, αἱ στίχες τῶν λαῶν [Refs [[prev. author] “Eq.” 163: hence the phrase ἀκούετε λεῴ]] hear O people!—the usual way of beginning proclamations at Athens, like our [Refs 6th c.BC+ [“Oyez” ! 6th c.BC: Susario Comicus 1.1, 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Pax” 551, “Av.” 448]]; τιμῶσιν οἱ πάντες λεῴ[Refs 4th c.BC+ [[prev. work] 1275; δεῦρ᾽ ἴτε, πάντες λεῴ 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Fragmenta” 384; Ἀττικὸς λεώς 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Eumenides” 681]]; ὁ πολὺς λεώς the multitude, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 458d, etc.]]

__4
in LXX, of the people, as opposed to priests and Levites, [“1 Es.” 5.46; in “NT”, of “Jews”, opposed to Gentiles, NT.Matt.2.6, NT.Luke.2.10, +others, compare “SIG” 1247 (Jewish tombstones)]; of [“Christians”, opposed to heathen, NT.Act.15.14, +others]

__II
a people, i.e. all who are called by one name, first in [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus, Δωριεῖ λαῷ “O.” 8.30; Λυδῶν δὲ λαὸς καὶ Φρυγῶν 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Persae” 770; ξύμπας Ἀχαιῶν λαός 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Philoctetes” 1243, compare “OT” 144, etc.]]; ἱππόται λαοί, i.e. the Thessalians, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “P.” 4.153, compare 9.54, “N.” 1.17. (The resemblance between λαός]] people and λᾶος stone (compare λᾶας) is implied in [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 24.611 λαοὺς δὲ λίθους ποίησε Κρονίων (in the story of Niobe)]]; and so [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus]] explains the word from the legend of Deucalion, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [“O.” 9.46, compare 5th c.BC: Epicharmus Comicus 122, 2nd c.AD: Apollodorus Damascenus Mechanicus 1.7.2; but compare 4th c.BC: Philochorus Historicus 12.)]] (From λᾱϝ-, as shown by the proper noun  Λαϝοπτόλεμος [Refs [“GDI” 3151, ϝιόλαϝος [prev. work]3132 (from Corinth): hence probably λήϊτον.)]]

LSJ / STEPBible (TFLSJ)
λάσκω,
imperfect ἔλασκον [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Electra” 1214 (Lyric poetry)]]: future λᾰκήσομαι [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Pax” 381, 384:]]aorist 1 ἐλάκησα [ᾰ[Refs [] [prev. work] 382 (δια-λᾱκήσας [prev. author] “Nu.” 410 is probably from διαλᾱκέω, _Doric dialect_ for -ληκέω):]]aorist 2 ἔλᾰκον, Epic dialect λάκον [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 14.25, +others]]: aorist 1 ἔληξα [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [3rd c.BC: Herodas Mimographus 8.65]]: perfect λέληκα [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 22.141, 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Historia Animalium” 618b31, λέλᾱκα 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Prometheus Vinctus” 407 (Lyric poetry), 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Acharnenses” 410 (_paratragoedia_)]]; participle feminine λελᾰκυῖα [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 12.85:]] —middle, see below [Refs [11]]:—ring, rattle, crash:

__I
of things, ring when struck, λάκε χαλκὸς νυσσομένων ξίφεσίν τε καὶ ἔγχεσι [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 14.25; λάκε δ᾽ ἀσπίς 20.277]]; also λάκε δ᾽ ὀστέα the bones cracked, broke with a crash, [Refs [13.616]]; λάκε δ᾽ ἀμφὶ πυρὶ ὕλη crackled, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th-7th c.BC: Hesiodus Epicus “Theogonia” 694]]; ἔλακον ἀξόνων βριθομένων χνόαι creaked under the weight, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Septem contra Thebas” 153 (Lyric poetry):]] —this sense occurs only in aorist 2 active

__1. in Hom., to pick out, gather, reckon, recount.
__2. In Hdt. and Att., to say, speak, affirm, declare: absol., Act.13:15, 24:10; before orat. dir., Mat.9:34, Mrk.3:11, Jhn.1:29, al.; before ὅτι recit., Mrk.3:21, Luk.1:24, Jhn.6:14, al.; accusative and inf., Luk.11:18, Jhn.12:29, al.; after another verb of speaking, προσφωνεῖν κ. λέγειν, Mat.11:17, al.; ἀπεκρίθη (ἐλάλησεν) λέγων (καὶ λέγει; Dalman, Words, 24 ff.), Mat.25:9, Mrk.3:33, 7:28, Luk.24:6, 7, al.; of unspoken thought, λ. ἐν ἑαυτῷ, Mat.3:9, Luk.3:8, al.; of writing, 2Co.8:8, Php.4:11, al.; λέγει ἡ γραφή, Rom.4:3, Jas.2:23, al.; with accusative of thing(s), Luk.8:8, 9:33, Jhn.5:34, al.; σὺ λέγεις (a non-committal phrase; Swete, Mk., 359, 369f.), Mat.27:11, Mrk.15:2, Luk.23:3, Jhn.18:37; with dative of person(s), before orat. dir., Mat.8:20, Mrk.2:17, al. mult.; id. before ὅτι, Mat.3:9, al.; with prep., πρός, μετά, περί, etc., Mrk.4:41, Jhn.11:56, Heb.9:5, al.; to mean (cl.), Mrk.14:71, Jhn.6:71, 1Co.10:29, al.; to call, name, Mrk.10:18; pass., Mat.9:9, Mrk.15:7, al (cf. ἀντι-, δια- (-μαι), προ-, συλ-λέγω).
SYN.: λαλέω, which refers to the utterance, as λέγω to the meaning of what is said, its correspondence with thought (Tr., Syn., Ixxvi; Thayer, see word λαλέω). (AS)

[Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 13.275]]; and so, μηκέτι ταῦτα λεγώμεθα νηπύτιοι ὥς[Refs 8th c.BC+ [[prev. work] 292, compare 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 3.240, 13.296; μηκέτι νῦν δήθ᾽ αὖθι λεγώμεθα 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 2.435.]]

say, speak, first in [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th-7th c.BC: Hesiodus Epicus “Theogonia” 27 (see. above 11.2)]]: future λέξω [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Empedocles Poeta Philosophus 38.1, 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Agamemnon” 859, 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 4.14, 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 2.48, 5th c.BC: Antipho Orator 6.33, etc.]]: aorist ἔλεξα [Refs 6th c.BC+ [6th c.BC: Anacreon Lyricus 45, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Sophista” 217e, 5th c.BC: Antipho Orator 1.15 (rare in 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus]] and the Orators, common in some dialects, as Boeotian, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [“IG” 7.504.2 (from Tanagra), Thessalian, [prev. work]9(2).461.21, Ionic, variant in 5th c.BC: Hippocrates Medicus “Aër.” 12):]]perfect λέλεχα [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd c.AD: Galenus Medicus 16.249, λέλεγα and λέλογας 5th c.AD(?): Hesychius Legal icographus (εἴρηκα in correct writers)]]:—passive, future λεχθήσομαι [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 5.86, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Timaeus” 67c, etc.]]: also future middle in passive sense, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Coloneus” 1186, 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Hecuba” 906 (Lyric poetry), etc.; and λελέξομαι 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 3.53 (variant{λέξεται}), 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 457b:]]aorist ἐλέχθην (never ἐλέγην in this sense) [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Tyrannus” 1442, 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 6.32, etc.]]: perfect λέλεγμαι [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “N.” 8.20, 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 2.21, 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Philoctetes” 389, etc. (εἴλεγμαι]] in this sense only in compound δι-): rare in compounds (only ἀντιλέγω, ἐπιλέγω, καταλέγω, προλέγω), the present in most compounds being supplied by ἀγορεύω, the future by ἐρῶ, the aorist by εἶπον, the perfect by εἴρηκα:

__B.III.1
say, speak, never in [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Homerus Epicus, first in 8th-7th c.BC: Hesiodus Epicus [same place], frequently from 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus]] and Trag. downwards; of all kinds of oral communications, ἐκέλευε λέγειν εἴ τι θέλοι [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 8.58]]; so λέγοις ἄν speak, say on, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Politicus” 268e, etc.; λ. μῦθον 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Persae” 698 (troch.); ψευδῆ λ. [prev. author] “Ag.” 625; ἀληθῆ λ. 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Philebus” 12b]] (so in passive, λόγος λέλεκται πᾶς [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Philoctetes” 389)]]; of oracles, say, declare, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 8.136]]; ὥσπερ τοὔνομα λέγει indicates, [Refs 6th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Protagoras” 312c: with Preps., λ. ἀμφί τινος 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Septem contra Thebas” 1017, 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Hecuba” 580; περί τινος 6th c.BC: Xenophanes Poeta Philosophus 34.2, 3rd c.AD: Democritus Epigrammaticus 165, 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Ajax” 151 (_anapaest meter_), 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 2.48]]; ὑπέρ τινος in his defence, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Electra” 555, 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Historia Graeca (Hellenica)” 1.7.16]]; κατά τινος against him, [Refs 6th c.BC+ [6th c.BC: Theognis Elegiacus 1240a, 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Historia Graeca (Hellenica)” 1.5.2]]; λ. ἐπί τισι εὐχὰς ἀγαθάς express good wishes for them, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Supplices” 625 (_anapaest meter_)]]; λ. τά τινος take his part, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 8.64]]; λ. πρός τι in reference or in answer to.., [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Antigone” 753, etc.; εἴς τι 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Memorabilia” 1.5.1.]]

__B.III.2
with accusative et infinitive, say that.., [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “P.” 2.59, etc.: with _negative_ οὐ, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 348c, etc., but μή [prev. work] 346e, 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Symposium” 4.5 (_passive_)]], and usually in later Gr., [LXX+NT+5th c.BC+ [LXX.Gen.38.22; λ. μὴ εἶναι ἀνάστασιν NT.Matt.22.23: frequently also followed by ὡς, ὅτι (generally so in the _active_ voice) when the subject of the relative clause may become the object of the principal Verb, γυναῖκα λέγουσιν, ὡς κάθηται.. 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 7.3.5, etc.: rarely with]]participle, λ. Οἰδίπουν ὀλωλότα speak of him as dead, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Coloneus” 1580; λέγουσιν ἡμᾶς ὡς ὀλωλότας 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Agamemnon” 672; λέξασ᾽ ἀδελφῷ σ᾽ ἐνθάδ᾽ ὄντα 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Helena” 888]]:—passive, λέξεται ἔχων [Refs 4th c.BC+ [[prev. author] “IT” 1047, compare 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Agamemnon” 170 (conjecture).]]

__B.III.3
λέγειν τινά τι say something of another, especially κακὰ λ. τινά speak ill of him, revile him, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 8.61; ἀγαθὰ λ. τινάς 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Ecclesiazusae” 435]]; τὰ ἔσχατα, τὰ ἀπόρρητα λ. ἀλλήλους, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Memorabilia” 2.2.9, 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 18.123]]; also εὖ or κακῶς λ. τινά, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Agamemnon” 445 (Lyric poetry), 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Electra” 524, compare 1028; εὖ λ. τὸν εὖ λέγοντα 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Memorabilia” 2.3.8.]]

__B.III.4
call by name, ἃς τρέμομεν λ. [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Coloneus” 128 (Lyric poetry)]]: with double accusative, call so and so, λέγοιμ᾽ ἂν ἄνδρα τόνδε τῶν σταθμῶν κύνα [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Agamemnon” 896, compare 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Coloneus” 939 codices, 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.32, etc.]]

__B.III.5
λ. τινὰ ποιεῖν τι tell, command one to do, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Choephori” 553, 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Philoctetes” 101, 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 4.1.22, etc.]]: so with τινι, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Coloneus” 840, 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 19.150 (no object expressed in 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Agamemnon” 925, 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Coloneus” 856)]]; λέγε τὸν ἐρωτῶντα ἵνα.. εἴπῃ σοι.. [NT+4th c.BC+ [2nd c.AD: Astrampsychus Onirocriticus “Oracula” p.1 H.; ὡς ὁ νόμος λέγει 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 22.20; ὁ λέγων μὴ μοιχεύειν NT.Rom.2.22.]]

__B.III.6
λ. τι say something, i.e. speak to the point or purpose, βούλῃ λέγειν τι, καὶ λέγων μηδὲν κλύει; [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Antigone” 757]]; λέγω τ; am I right? the answer being λέγεις, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. author] “OT” 1475; κινδυνεύεις τι λέγειν 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Cratylus” 404a; ἴσως ἄν τι λέγοις 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Memorabilia” 2.1.12, compare “Cyr.” 1.4.20]]; opposed to οὐδὲν λέγει has no meaning, no authority, οὐδὲν λ. τὸ σωφρόνως τραφῆναι [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Equites” 334, compare “V.” 75]]; οὐδὲν λέγεις nonsense! [Refs [[prev. author] “Th.” 625]]; but οὐδὲν λέγειν, also, say what is not, lie, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. author] “Av.” 66, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Apologia” 30b]]; also εὖ γε λέγεις, εὖ λέγεις, εὖ ἂν λέγοις, good news!, that is well!,[Refs [[prev. work] 24e, “Grg.” 447b, “Prt.” 310b]]; καλῶς, ὀρθῶς λ., you are right, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Memorabilia” 3.3.4, 3.6.8]]; κοὔπω λέγω and what is more, [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [3rd c.BC: Herodas Mimographus 7.44]]; τί λέγει; τὸν ἔποπα παῖ καλεῖ; [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Aves” 57, compare “Ec.” 298 (Lyric poetry).]]

__B.III.7
pleonastic, ἔφη λέγων [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 3.156, 5.36; ἔλεγε φάς [prev. author] 1.122; ἔφασκε λέγων 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Aves” 472; ἦ δ᾽ ὃς λέγων [prev. author] “V.” 795; ὡς ἔφη λέγων 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Ajax” 757; καὶ λέγων εἶπεν οὕτω πως 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 8.74, etc.]]

__B.III.8
at the beginning of letters or documents, Ἄμασις Πολυκράτεϊ ὧδε λέγει.., Μαρδόνιος τάδε λέγει.., etc., [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 3.40, 8.140]]. ά, etc.; τὰ γράμματα ἔλεγε τάδε [Refs [[prev. author] 1.124, etc.]]; γράμμασι λέγον τάδε, of an inscription, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 6.54]]: in roman edicts, Μάρκος Μέττιος Ῥοῦφος.. λέγει [Refs 1st c.AD+ [“POxy.” 237 viii 28 (1st c.AD).]]

__B.III.9
wish to say, mean, οὔτοι γυναῖκας ἀλλὰ Γοργόνας λέγω [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Eumenides” 48]]; τί τοῦτο λέγει, πρὸ Πύλοι; what does πρὸ Πύλοιο mean? [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Equites” 1059, compare 1021, 1375, “Ec.” 989, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Phaedo” 60e: frequently in Platonic dialogue, πῶς λέγεις]]; how do you mean? in what sense do you say this? Ap.[Refs [24e, +others]]; ἢ πῶς λέγομε; or what do we mean to say? Grg.[Refs [480b]]; πῶς δὴ οὖν αὐτὸ λέγει; [Refs [“Phdr.” 265c]]; ποῖόν τί ποτε ἄρα λέγοντές φασι.. what they can possibly mean by saying.., [Refs [“Tht.” 181c, +others: with double _accusative_, τοιοῦτόν τι σὲ λέγειν τὸ κρεῖττον “Grg.” 489d, +others: frequently (especially in Trag.) to explain more fully, εἴσω κομίζου καὶ σύ, Κασάνδραν λέγω]] you, I mean Cassandra, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Agamemnon” 1035; ὁ μάντις, υἱὸν Οἰκλέους λ. [prev. author] “Th.” 609, compare 658 (variant), “Pr.” 946; ποταμός, Ἀχελῷον λέγω 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Trachiniae” 9, compare 1220, “Ph.” 1261, 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Phoenissae” 987]]; ἐμὲ λέγων meaning me, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Isocrates Orator 12.215; τὸ δ᾽ ὑμεῖς ὅταν λέγω, τὴν πόλιν λ. 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 18.88: sometimes, however, the word after λέγω]] is put in apposition with the word to be explained, Ἀντικλείας.., τῆς σῆς λέγω τοι μητρός [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Fragmenta - American Journal of Philology” 175, compare “Th.” 658 codex M; περὶ τῶνδε.., λέγω δὲ Φωκέων 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 19.152; παρ᾽ ὧν.., τούτων τῶν τὴν Ἀσίαν οἰκούντων λέγω [prev. author] 8.24, compare 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Symposium” 202b: _absolutely_, μηδενὸς ὄντος ἐν [τῇ χώρᾳ] λέγω 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 1.27.]]

__B.III.9.b
περὶ ἃς (i.e. ἀπολαύσεις) λέγομεν τὸν σώφρονα in regard to which we use the term 'temperate', [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Ethica Nicomachea” 1148a5, compare 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Gorgias” 494b.]]

__B.III.10
ὡς λέγουσι as they say, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Antigone” 23, etc.; ὡς λ. μοι [prev. author] “OC” 1161:]] —passive, λέγεται it is said, c.accusative et infinitive, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Memorabilia” 1.2.30, +others]]; but also πατρὸς λέγεται γενέσθαι.. [Refs [[prev. author] “Cyr.” 1.2.1]]; θανεῖν ἐλέχθη he was said to have been killed, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Tyrannus” 292; so λεγόμενον ἐρέω 5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “P.” 5.108: τὸ λεγόμενον]] absolutely, as the saying goes, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 7.68, compare 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Gorgias” 447a, “Smp.” 217e, etc.; τὸ λ. δὴ τοῦτο [prev. author] “Grg.” 514e: ὁ λεγόμενος γραῶν ὕθλος]] the so-called.., [Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. author] “Tht.” 176b; οἱ λ. αὐτόνομοι εἶναι 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Historia Graeca (Hellenica)” 6.3.8]]; οἱ λ. ὅτι.. of whom it is said that.., [Refs [[prev. author] “Cyr.” 8.6.16.]]

__B.III.11
of orators, speak (emphatically), λέγειν δεινός [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Tyrannus” 545, 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 1.5.9, etc.; λέγειν ἠσκηκότες 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Fragmenta” 963, compare 5th c.BC: Eupolis Comicus 95 (see. λαλέω); λ. τε καὶ πράσσειν δυνατώτατος 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 1.139; οἱ ἐν τῷ πλήθει λέγειν δυνάμενοι 5th-6th c.BC: Isocrates Orator 3.8, compare 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 19.286]]; plead one's cause in a court of law, [Refs [[prev. author] 23.78]]; δίκας λέγειν ὑπέρ τινος speak as an advocate for.., [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-3rd c.BC: Dinarchus Orator 1.111.]]

__B.III.12
boast of, tell of, τὴν ἑαυτοῦ ῥώμην [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 1.3.10]]; in Poets, sing of, θέλω λ. Ἀτρείδας [Refs [“Anacreontea” 23.1.]]

__B.III.13
recite what is written, λαβὲ τὸ βιβλίον καὶ λέγε [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Theaetetus” 143c; and frequently in Oratt., as λέγε τὸν νόμον 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 21.8]] and 10, etc.; of lectures, ἀκούσατέ μου σχόλια λέγοντος [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd c.AD: Arrianus Historicus “Epicteti Dissertationes” 3.21.6, compare 15.8]] (the sense of Latin lego, read, occurs only in the compounds ἀναλέγομαι, ἐπιλέγομαι).

__B.III.14
say or send word by another, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 1.9.25, 7.4.5.]]

__B.III.15
maintain as a thesis, οἱ τὰς ἰδέας λέγοντες [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Physica” 193b36, “Metaphorical” 1036b14.]]

__B.III.16
nominate, Latin dicere [dictatorem], [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd-3rd c.AD: Dio Cassius Historicus “fragment” 36.26 (_passive_)]]. (Cf. Latin lègo, legio, legulus ('olivegatherer').)

LSJ / STEPBible (TFLSJ)
λεῖος, α, ον,
smooth to the touch, [αἴγειρος] [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 4.484; λ. ὥσπερ ἔγχελυς 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Fragmenta” 218, compare 5th c.BC: Eupolis Comicus 338]]; χῆμαι, χηραμβίς, [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [“PCair.Zen.” 82.12 (3rd c.BC)]], [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.AD(?): Hesychius Legal icographus see at {χήμ; τὰ τραχέα καὶ τὰ λ}. 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Memorabilia” 3.10.1; frequently in 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus, “Cra.” 414b, +others, 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Categoriae” 10a17, etc.]]; also, of cloths, smooth, plain, not embroidered, ὑφαντά τε καὶ λ. [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 2.97; λ. ὕφασμα 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Politicus” 310e]]; λεῖα ἐκπεποιημένα worked smooth, of marble, [Refs [“IG” 12.372.134; also λεία ἐργασία [prev. work]372.165;]] unsculptured, Ἀθήνης ἕδος [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [3rd c.BC: Callimachus Epicus “Fragmenta” 105.4]]; of plate, unembossed, φιάλαι [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [“IG” 11(2).161 B 27 (Delos, 3rd c.BC), “Inscription Délos” 442 B 78 (2nd c.BC).]]

__2
in [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Homerus Epicus]], chiefly of level places or countries, λεῖος δ᾽ ἱππόδρομος ἀμφίς [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 23.330]]; ἐν λείῳ πεδίῳ[Refs 8th c.BC+ [[prev. work] 359; λ. ὁδός 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 10.103, 8th-7th c.BC: Hesiodus Epicus “Opera et Dies” 288 (cited in 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus, etc., ὀλίγη codices)]]; λ. ἄροσις [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 9.134]]; λεῖα δ᾽ ἐποίησεν made a smooth place, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 12.30; πεδίον λ. 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 2.29; χωρίον λειότατον [prev. author] 7.9. ; ἡ -οτάτη τῶν ὁδῶν [prev. author] 9.69]]; λ. θάλασσα a smooth sea, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. author] 2.117; λ. χώρα καὶ ἄξυλος 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Respublica Atheniensium” 2.12]]; λ. βάσεις flat feet, [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd c.AD: Galenus Medicus 6.856.]]

__2.b
with genitive, χῶρος.. λεῖος πετράων smooth (i.e. free) from rocks, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 5.443, 7.282.]]

__3
smoothskinned, without hair, of animals, [LXX+4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Historia Animalium” 582b35, LXX.Gen.27.11; - ότατον τῶν ζῴων ἐστὶν ἄνθρωπος 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Historia Animalium” 583a6]]; especially of youths, smooth-chinned, beardless (compare λείαξ), [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [3rd c.BC: Theocritus Poeta Bucolicus 5.90, compare “Anthologia Graeca” 12.13 (2nd c.AD: Strato Epigrammaticus)]]; also, of fish, smooth, ἱππίδια [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Epicharmus Comicus 44]]; opposed to λεπιδωτοί, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Historia Animalium” 505a26]]; [γαλεός] the smooth shark, Mustelus laevis,[Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. work] 565b2, 2nd-3rd c.AD: Oppianus Anazarbensis Epicus “Halieutica - Poetae Bucolici et Didactici” 1.380; τὸ λ. 5th c.BC: Hippocrates Medicus “ἐπιδημίαι” 3.14, 6.3.16]]; λείη ὑπόστασις a smooth or uniform sediment, [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [[prev. author] “Coac.” 462; [γάλα] λ. καὶ ὁμαλὸν καὶ συνεχὲς ἑαυτῷ 2nd c.AD: Soranus Medicus 1.91.]]

__4
metaphorically, smooth, soft, πνεῦμα [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Ranae” 1003]]; of the sound of the voice, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Politicus” 307a, “Ti.” 67b, “Phlb.” 51d; διάλεκτος 1st c.BC: Philodemus Gadarensis Epigrammaticus “Po.Herc.” 994.36]]; of the taste, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-4th c.BC: Timaeus Locrus Philosophus 100ef; also λ. μῦθοι 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Prometheus Vinctus” 647]]; [τὸ] ἥμερόν τε καὶ λ. [τοῦ ἤθους] [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Cratylus” 406a]]; λ. πάθημα, opposed to τραχύ, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [[prev. author] “Ti.” 63e; λ. κινήματα τῆς σαρκός 4th-3rd c.BC: Epicurus Philosophus “Fragmenta” 411]]; λ. κίνησις, Cyrenaic phrase for ἡδονή, [Refs 1st c.BC+ [3rd c.AD(?): Diogenes Laertius 2.86, compare 2nd c.AD: Lucianus Sophista “Par.” 10, 3rd c.AD: Alexander Aphrodisiensis Philosophus “in Aristotelis Topicorum libros octo commentaria - pars” 94.32; λ. ἡσυχίη “Anthologia Graeca” 7.278 (1st c.BC: Archias Byzantine)]]; ὡς -οτέρου ἐλέους ὑπάρξοντος (sed to be read τελειοτέρου) [Refs 2nd c.BC+ [2nd c.BC: Polybius Historicus 20.9.11]]; τὸ λ., ={λειότης, τῆς ἑρμηνείας} [Refs 4th c.BC+ [1st c.BC: Dionysius Halicarnassensis “de Lysia” 24; τὸ λ. καὶ ὁμαλὲς τῆς συνθέσεως 4th c.BC: Demetrius Phalereus Rhetor “Demetrius on Style” 48.]] adverb λείως smoothly, gently, [Refs 6th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Theaetetus” 144b, 1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus 2.384a; καί με κωτίλλοντα λ. τραχὺν ἐκφανεῖν νόον 6th c.BC: Solon Lyricus cited in 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Ἀθηναίων Πολιτεία” 12.3.]]

__II
rubbed or ground down, [Refs 1st c.AD+ [1st c.AD: Dioscorides (Dioscurides) Medicus 1.3, +others, “PHolm.” 19.39; compare λειόω 11: λεῖον, τό]], fine sand, [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [Inscription Délos 500 A 9 (3rd c.BC)]]. (Prob. λειϝος, cf. Latin lēvis.)
