deep_entry:
Abbott-Smith / STEPBible (TBESG)
λείπω
[in LXX: Job.4:11, Pro.19:4 (פָּרַד), al. ;]
__1. trans., to leave, leave behind; pass., to be left behind, to lack before prep. (as more usual in cl.), ἐν, Jas.1:4; with genitive of thing(s), Jas.1:5 2:15.
__2. Intrans., to be gone, to be wanting: with dative of person(s), Luk.18:22, Tit.3:13; τὰ λείποντα, Tit.1:5
(cf. ἀπο-, δια-, ἐκ-, ἐπι-, κατα-, ἐν-κατα-, περι-, ὑπο-λείπω).†
(AS)

---

LSJ / STEPBible (TFLSJ)
λείπω,
imperfect ἔλειπον [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 19.288, etc.]]: future λείψω [Refs [18.11:]]aorist 1 ἔλειψα, participle λείψας [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Fragmenta” 965 (= 4th c.BC: Antiphanes Comicus 32), elsewhere only late, 2nd c.BC: Polybius Historicus 12.15.12 (παρ-), 1st c.BC-1st c.AD: Strabo Geographus 6.3.10 (παρ-), 1st c.AD(?): Pseudo-Phocylidea 77 (ἀπ-), etc.]]; uncompounded, [Refs 1st c.BC+ [1st c.BC: Ptolemaeus Epigrammaticus “Alm.” 10.4, 2nd c.AD: Lucianus Sophista “Par.” 42, 3rd c.AD: Pseudo-Callisthenes Historicus 1.44 (codex C)]]; also in later Poets, [Refs 3rd c.AD+ [4th c.AD(?): Manetho Astrologus 1.153, 3rd c.AD: Oppianus Apamensis Epicus “Cynegetica” 2.33, and in Inscrr., “epigram Gr.” 522.16 (from Thessalonica), 314.27 (from Smyrna)]], etc.: but correct writers normally use aorist 2 ἔλῐπον [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 2.35, 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Persae” 984 (Lyric poetry)]], etc.: perfect λέλοιπα [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 14.134:]]pluperfect ἐλελοίπειν (Attic dialect -η) [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 2.1.21]]:—middle, in properly sense chiefly in compounds: aorist 2 ἐλιπόμην [Refs 8th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.186, 2.40, 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Hercules Furens” 169, etc. (in _passive_ sense, 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 11.693, +others)]]:—passive, future middle in passive sense λείψομαι [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th-7th c.BC: Hesiodus Epicus “Opera et Dies” 200, 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 7.8.ά, 48]]; also λειφθήσομαι [Refs 8th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Philoctetes” 1071, λελείψομαι 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 24.742, 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 5.105, etc.]]: aorist ἐλείφθην, λείφθην [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “O.” 2.43]]; Epic dialect 3rd.pers. plural ἔλειφθεν [Refs [“hymnus ad Mercurium” 195]]: perfect λέλειμμαι [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 13.256, 3rd c.AD: Democritus Epigrammaticus 228, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Timaeus” 61a, etc.]]: pluperfect ἐλελείμμην [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 2.700]]; Epic dialect λέλειπτο [Refs [10.256]]: Epic dialect aorist also ἔλειπτο [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [3rd c.BC: Apollonius Rhodius Epicus 1.45, etc.:]]

__1
leave, quit, Ἑλλάδα, δώματα, etc., [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 9.447, 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 21.116, etc.: with a _negative_, [σκόπελον] οὔ ποτε κύματα λείπει 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 2.396; νιν.. χιὼν οὐδαμὰ λ. 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Antigone” 830 (Lyric poetry)]]; χερσὶν ὕπο Τρώων λείψειν φάος ἠελίοιο, i.e. die, be killed, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 18.11; λ. τὸν βίον ὑπό τινος 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Leges” 872e]]; λ. βίον, βίοτον, etc., [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Electra” 1444, 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Helena” 226 (Lyric poetry), etc.; αὐτόχειρι σφαγῇ λ. βίον [prev. author] “Or.” 948.]]

__1.b
conversely, τὸν δ᾽ ἔλιπε ψυχή [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 5.696, 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 14.426; τὸν.. λίπε θυμός 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 4.470; ἔπειτά με καὶ λίποι αἰών 5.685, compare 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 7.224; λίπε δ᾽ ὀστέα θυμός 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 16.743]]; ψυχὴ δὲ λέλοιπεν (i.e. ὀστέα) [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 14.134; νῦν δ᾽ ἤδη πάντα λέλοιπεν (i.e. ἐμέ) [prev. work] 213]]; in these two last passages some take it intransitive, is gone, see below [Refs [11.]]

__2
leave behind, leave at home, παιδὶ τὸν ἐν μεγάροισιν ἔλειπες [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 13.403, compare 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 5.480]]; especially of dying men, leave (as a legacy), Ἀτρεὺς δὲ θνῄσκων ἔλιπεν πολύαρνι Θυέστῃ [τὸσκῆπτρον[Refs 5th c.BC+ [] 2.106; πατέρι γόον καὶ κήδεα λυγρά 5.157, compare 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Ajax” 973; παῖδα ὀρφανὸν λ. [prev. work] 653]]; λ. ἄρρενας, θυγατέρας, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Leges” 923e, 924e; λ. εὔκλειαν ἐν δόμοισι 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Choephori” 348 (Lyric poetry)]]:—also in middle, leave behind one (as a memorial to posterity), μνημόσυνον λιπέσθαι [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.186, 6.109, +others; λιπέσθαι τιμωρούς 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Hercules Furens” 169; διαδόχους ἐμαυτῷ 1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus “Aemilius Paulus” 36, etc.]]

__2.b
leave standing, leave remaining, spare, οἰκίαν οὐδεμίαν [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 7.4.1; μηδένα [prev. author] “HG” 2.3.41, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 567b, etc.]]

__3
leave, forsake, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 17.13, etc.; λ. τινὰ χαμαί 5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “O.” 6.45; εὕδοντα 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Philoctetes” 273]]; τὴν αὑτοῦ φύσιν λ.[Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. work] 903; λ. τὴν τάξιν 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Apologia” 29a, etc.]]; λ. ἐράνους fail in paying.., [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 27.25, compare 25.22]]; λ. δασμόν, φοράν, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 3.1.1, 34]]; λ. μαρτυρίαν, ὅρκον, fail in.., [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 49.19, 59.60, λ. δίκην]] allow it to go by default, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [“SIG” 134b24 (Milet., 4th c.BC)]]; λοιβὰς.. οὐ λίπε neglected them not, [Refs [“IG” 3.1337.8.]]

__3.b
conversely, λίπον ἰοὶ ἄνακτα they failed him, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 22.119.]]

__4
in Mathematics texts, lose or drop something, i.e. have something subtracted from it, τὸ KP λιπὸν τὸ BO the area KP minus the area BO, [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [3rd-2nd c.BC: Apollonius Pergaeus Geometra 3.12, compare 1st c.BC: Ptolemaeus Epigrammaticus “Alm.” 10.4, +others, 3rd c.AD: Diophantus Mathematicus 2.21.]]

__II
intransitive, to be gone, depart, [Refs [epigram Gr. 149.2 (from Rhenea)]]; see above 1.1b.

__II.2
to be wanting or missing, οὔ τί πω ἔλιπεν ἐκ τοῦδ᾽ οἴκου.. αἰκία [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Electra” 514 (Lyric poetry); οὔποτ᾽ ἔρις λείψει κατὰ πόλεις 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Helena” 1157 (Lyric poetry); τὸ κακοτυχὲς οὐ λέλοιπεν ἐκ τέκνων [prev. author] “HF” 133 (Lyric poetry)]]; λείπουσιν αἱ ἐκ τῆς κεφαλῆς [τρίχες] [NT+4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Historia Animalium” 518a24; ἔτι ἕν σοι λείπει NT.Luke.18.22]]; τί λείπει τῶν ἐπιτηδείων αὐταῖ; [Refs 2nd c.BC+ [2nd c.BC: Polybius Historicus 10.18.8]]; τί γάρ σοι λείπε; [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd c.AD: Arrianus Historicus “Epicteti Dissertationes” 2.22.5, compare 2nd c.AD: Diogenes Oenoandensis Epicureus 64]]; [εἰς τὴν προκειμένην πραγματείαν] τὸ ὑφ᾽ οὗ γίνεται.. μὴ ῥηθὲν οὐ λείπει is not needed, [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd c.AD(?): Marcellinus Medicus “de Pulsibus - Festschrift zur 49. Versammlung deutscher Philologen und Schulmänner” 69: with]]infinitive, λείπει μὲν οὐδ᾽ ἃ πρόσθεν ἤδεμεν τὸ μὴ οὐ βαρύστον᾽ εἶναι nihil absunt quin.., [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Tyrannus” 1232: so with _genitive_, βραχὺ λείπει τοῦ μὴ συνάπτειν 2nd c.BC: Polybius Historicus 2.14.6, etc.]]; πρότασις τῆς προειρημένης λείπουσα ὑποθέσει a proposition containing less in the hypothesis than that aforesaid, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [3rd c.AD(?): Pappus Mathematicus 648.1: frequently with numerals, κεφάλαιον γίγνεται μικροῦ λείποντος πέντε καὶ δέκα τάλαντα 5th c.BC: Lysias Orator 19.43; οὐ πολὺ λεῖπον τῶν ἐνενήκοντα ἐτῶν 2nd c.BC: Polybius Historicus 12.16.13; τριήρεις πέντε λείπουσαι τῶν ἑκατὸν εἴκοσι 1st c.BC: Diodorus Siculus Historicus 13.14: generally, παντὸς μὲν οὖν λείπει 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Leges” 728a; ὁ λιπών [prev. work] 759e]]; τὸ λεῖπον what is lacking, [Refs 2nd c.BC+ [2nd c.BC: Polybius Historicus 4.38.9, etc.]]; esp. Grammars, to be incomplete, of a phrase, λειπούσης τῆς φράσεως [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd c.AD: Apollonius Dyscolus Grammaticus “de Adverbiis;” 159.28, +others]]; to be wanting, omitted, λείποντος τοῦ καί [Refs [[prev. author] “Conj.” 225.24: also with _dative_, λείπει ἡ κεῖνος φωνὴ τῷ ε ¯ [prev. author] “Adv.” 147.17.]]

__II.2.b
of the moon, to be invisible (compare λειψιφαής), [Refs 3rd c.AD+ [3rd c.AD: Plotinus Philosophus 2.3.5.]]

__II.2.c
λείποντα εἴδη, in Algebra, ={λείψεις}, negative terms, [Refs 3rd c.AD+ [3rd c.AD: Diophantus Mathematicus 1 “Def.” 10.]]

__B
passive, to be left, left behind, ἄλοχος Φυλάκῃ ἐλέλειπτο [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 2.700; οἱ δ᾽ οἶοι λείπονται 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 22.250, etc.]]; also ὀπίσσω, μετόπισθε, κατόπισθε λ., [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 3.160, 22.334, 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 21.116]]; παῖδες.. μετόπισθε λελειμμένοι left behind in Troy, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 24.687; μόνα.. νὼ λελειμμένα 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Antigone” 58, etc.]]; τὸ λειπόμενον βίου (variant{βιοτᾶς}) [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Ariphron Lyricus 1 (= “IG” 3.171).]]

__B.b
in Mathematics texts, to be subtracted: τὸ ἀπὸ τῆς ΔΦ λειφθὲν ὑπὸ τοῦ ἀπὸ τῆς ΔΑ ποιεῖ.., the square on ΔΦ subtracted from the square on ΔΑ gives.., [Refs 1st c.BC+ [1st c.BC: Ptolemaeus Epigrammaticus “Alm.” 10.7.]]

__B.2
remain, remain over and above, τριτάτη δ᾽ ἔτι μοῖρα λέλειπται [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 10.253; ἐμοὶ δὲ λελείψεται ἄλγεα λυγρά 24.742; ὀλίγων σφι ἡμερέων λείπεται σιτία 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 9.45; ὃ πᾶσι λ. βροτοῖς.. ἐλπίς 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Troades” 681; αὐτόνομοι ἐλείφθημεν 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 3.11; ἕως ἄν τι λείπηται [prev. author] 8.81: _impersonal_, λείπεται]] it remains, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Theaetetus” 157e]]: c.accusative et infinitive, πεπληρῶσθαί με [Refs [[prev. author] “Phdr.” 235c.]]

__B.3
remain alive, πολλοὶ δὲ λίποντο [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 4.495, compare 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Persae” 480, 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 3.1.2.]]

__B.II
with genitive,

__B.II.1
to be left without, to be forsaken of, κτεάνων λειφθεὶς καὶ φίλων [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “I.” 2.11; σοῦ λελειμμένη 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Antigone” 548]]; but στρατὸν λελειμμένον δορός which has been left by the spear, i.e. not slain, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Agamemnon” 517.]]

λειτουργέω, -ῶ
(λειτουργός), [in LXX chiefly for שָׁרַת pi., also for עָבַד, צָבָא, etc. ;]
__1. in cl., at Athens, to supply public offices at one's own cost, render public service to the State, hence, generally,
__2. to serve the State, do a service, serve (of service to the Gods, Diod., i, 21): of the official service of priests and Levites (Exo.29:30, Num.16:9, Sir.4:14, 1Ma.10:42, al.; cf. Deiss., BS, 140 f.), Heb.10:11; of Christians: with dative of person(s) before ἐν, Rom.15:27 (cf. Sir.10:25); τ. κυρίῳ, Act.13:2.†
SYN.: λατρεύω (which see), prop., to serve for hire, LXX (as some­times in cl.), always of service to the deity on the part of both priests and people (Exo.4:3, Deu.10:12, and similarly in NT). λειτουργέω "is the fulfilment of an office: it has a definite representative character, and corresponds with a function to be discharged". It is therefore used of serving in an office or ministry: in LXX always of priests and Levites, in NT, with its cognates (Rom.13:6 15:27, are not really exceptions), of services rendered either to God or man by apostles, prophets, teachers, and other officers of the church (cf. Tr., Syn., § xxxv; ICC on Rom.1:9; Westc., He., 232 ff.)  (AS)

leprous, [LXX+4th c.BC+ [4th-3rd c.BC: Theophrastus Philosophus “de Causis Plantarum” 2.6.4, LXX.Lev.13.44]]: as substantive, leper, [NT.Mark.1.40, etc.]; λ. ὄνυχες, probably psoriasis unguium, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Hippocrates Medicus “περὶ ὑγρῶν χρήσιος” 4, 1st c.AD: Dioscorides (Dioscurides) Medicus 2.114]]; τὸ λ., = λέπρα, ἡ, [LXX.4Ki.5.11]; ἱμάντας ἐκ λεπρῶν (i.e. δερμάτων, for the toughest leather, accusative to Scholia, was supposed to be made of mangy skins) [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Acharnenses” 724 (but Scholia prefers ἐκ Λεπρῶν]], proper name of a  “Tannery” outside the walls); λ. βαυβών [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [3rd c.BC: Herodas Mimographus 6.36.]]

LSJ / STEPBible (TFLSJ)
λεπτός, ή, όν,
(λέπω) rare in literal sense, peeled, husked, ῥίμφα τε λέπτ᾽ ἐγένοντο, of barley being threshed out, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 20.497.]]

__2
fine, small, κονίη [Refs 5th c.BC+ [23.506; κόνις 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Antigone” 256; τέφρα 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Nubes” 177; λεπτοῖς ἁλσί 2nd c.AD: Alexander Rhetor 187.5: frequently in 5th c.BC: Hippocrates Medicus, διατρήσεις λ. “Loc.Hom.” 10, +others]]; of soil, light, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-3rd c.BC: Theophrastus Philosophus “Historia Plantarum” 1.8.1.]]

__3
thin, fine, delicate, frequently in [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Homerus Epicus]], mostly of garments and the [Refs 8th c.BC+ [like, ὀθόναι 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 18.595]]; πέπλοι, φᾶρος, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 7.97, 10.544; ἀράχνια 8.280; μήρινθος 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 23.854; - ότατος χαλκός 20.275; ἔβενος, ἐλέφας, σίδηρος “BCH” 35.286 (Delos, 2nd c.BC)]]; ῥινὸς βοός [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 20.276 (_superlative_)]]; δέρμα [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Historia Animalium” 517b27 (_superlative_)]]; τρίχες [Refs [[prev. author] “GA” 783a4 (_comparative_)]]; σάρξ [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Medea” 1189; χαλκὸς καὶ δόνακες 5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “P.” 12.25, compare 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Medea” 949, 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 2.49, etc.]]; λεπτὰ τὰ πρῴραθεν ἔχειν, of ships, to have the bows thin and weak, [Refs [[prev. author] 7.36.]]

__4
of the human figure, mostly in bad sense, thin, lean, [Refs 7th c.BC+ [7th-6th c.BC: Alcaeus Lyricus 39]]; opposed to παχύς, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Hippocrates Medicus “περὶ ἄρθρων ἐμβολῆς” 8 (_comparative_)]]; ἐγὼ δὲ λεπτὴ κἀσθενής [Refs 8th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Ecclesiazusae” 539; σοφιστῶν λεπτῶν, ἀσίτων 4th c.BC: Antiphanes Comicus 122.4; λ. καὶ αὐχμῶν 4th-3rd c.BC: Theophrastus Philosophus “Characteres” 26.5, compare 1st c.AD: Cebes Philosophus 10; λ. χείρ 8th-7th c.BC: Hesiodus Epicus “Opera et Dies” 497; στῆθος 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Nubes” 1018 (_anapaest meter_); τράχηλος 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Cynegeticus” 5.30; λεπτὸς [ἐκ] τοῖν σκελοῖν 2nd c.AD: Lucianus Sophista “Nav.” 2; λ. ὑπὸ μεριμνῶν 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Amatores” 134b]]; of animals, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 1.4.11]]; also, slender, taper (opposed to παχύς), δάκτυλος [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 523d]]; ἀπολήγειν εἰς λεπτόν, of the fingers of a statue, [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd c.AD: Lucianus Sophista “Im.” 6.]]

__5
of space, strait, narrow, εἰσίθμη [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 6.264; ἀταρπός 7th c.BC: Alcman Lyricus 81]]; ἐπὶ λεπτὸν τετάχθαι in a thin line, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 5.4.46, compare 2nd c.BC: Polybius Historicus 3.115.6; οὔτε εὐρεῖαν οὔτε λεπτὴν.. ὁδόν 1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus 2.964c (cited in 3rd c.AD: Porphyrius Tyrius Philosophus “de Abstinentia - Porphyrii Opuscula” 1.6).]]

__6
generally, small, weak, impotent, λεπτὴ μῆτις [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 10.226, 23.590; ἐλπίς 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Equites” 1244, compare ὀχέω 11.3; ἀσφάλεια 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator “Epistulae” 2.20]]; λ. ἴχνη faint traces, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Cynegeticus” 5.5]]; λ. οὖας, of a child's ear, tiny, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Simonides Lyricus 37.14]]; τὰ λ. τῶν προβάτων small cattle, i.e. sheep and goats, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 8.137]]; λ. πλοῖα small craft, [Refs [[prev. author] 7.36]]; ἄκραι λ. small headlands, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. author] 8.107; λ. κλιμάκια 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Pax” 69; τὸ -ότατον τοῦ χαλκοῦ νομίσματος 1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus “Cicero” 29; λ. χαλκός “OGI” 485.12 (5th c.BC: Magnes Comicus Mae.): without χαλκός, “Inscription Perg.” 374 D 7; ἀργύριον Ῥόδιον λ. “CIG” “Corpus Inscriptionum Graecarum” “Corpus Inscriptionum Graecarum” 2693e5 (from Mylasa), compare “TAM” 2(1).15 (from Telmessus)]]; see below 111.2. adverb -τῶς, ζῆν poorly, meanly, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-3rd c.BC: Menander Comicus “Μονόστιχοι - Fragmenta Comicorum Graecorum” 682]]: neuter plural as adverb, λεπτὰ λεύσσω κόραις [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Orestes” 224.]]

__7
light, slight, λεπταῖς ὑπαὶ κώνωπος.. ῥιπαῖσι [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Agamemnon” 892]]; λ. πνοαί light breezes, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Iphigenia Aulidensis” 813]]; λεπταῖς ἐπὶ ῥοπῇσιν on slight turns of fortune, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Fragmenta” 555.]]

__8
of size or quantity, λ. πυρίδια small, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Lysistrata” 1206; λ. κύλικες 5th c.BC: Pherecrates Comicus 143.5 (but _falsa lectio_): _neuter_ _plural_ as]] adverb, λ. τῖλαι 'pluck into small pieces', [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [3rd c.BC: Theocritus Poeta Bucolicus 3.21.]]

__9
of liquids, thin, γάλα [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Hippocrates Medicus “περὶ διαίτης” 2.46; λεπτὰ ἀνεμέειν [prev. author] “Coac.” 310]]; λ. οἶνος light wine, [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd c.AD: Lucianus Sophista “Merc.Cond.” 18]]; also of food, λ. δίαιται [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Hippocrates Medicus “ἀφορισμοί” 1.4; λ. ὀψάρια “OGI” 484.16 (Pergam.).]] adverb -τῶς, διαιτᾶσθαι, διαιτᾶν[Refs 2nd c.AD+ [, 2nd c.AD: Galenus Medicus 19.191, 7th c.AD: Paulus Aegineta Medicus 3.43.]]

__10
={λεπτομερής}, consisting of fine parts, ὅσῳ -ότερον ἀὴρ ὕδατος [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Physica” 215b4, compare “Cael.” 303b26, +others]]

__II
metaphorically, subtle, refined, νοῦς [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Medea” 529; -ότεροι μῦθοι [prev. work] 1082 (_anapaest meter_)]]; - ότατοι λῆροι [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Nubes” 359; πυκνῇ.. λεπτὰ μηχανᾷ φρενί [prev. author] “Ach.” 445; λ. λογιστά [prev. author] “Av.” 318; λ. καὶ ἀκριβής 5th c.BC: Antipho Orator 3.4.2; ἐς τὰς τέχνας παχέες, οὐ λεπτοί 5th c.BC: Hippocrates Medicus “Aër.” 24; λόγοι λ... τρέφουσ᾽ ἐκείνους 2nd c.AD: Alexander Rhetor 220.8]]; compare λεπτολόγος. adverb - τῶς, μεριμνᾶν [Refs 4th c.BC+ [“Lyrica Adespota” 135; λ. καὶ πυκνῶς ἐξετάζειν 4th c.BC: Amphis Comicus 33.5]]: comparative -οτέρως [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Anaxandrides Comicus 36: also κατὰ λεπτόν]]in detail, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [PPetr. 2p.118 (3rd c.BC), 1st c.BC: Cicero, M. Tullius Orator et Philosophus “Epistulae ad Atticum” 2.18.2, 2nd c.AD: Phrynichus Atticista “Praeparatio Sophistica” p.83 5th c.BC: Bacchylides Lyricus, 9th c.AD: Photius Legal icographus, etc.]] see at {νιφετός}; compare κατάλεπτον, καταλεπτολογέω: τὰ κατὰ λεπτόν, title of poems by Aratus, [Refs 1st c.BC+ [3rd c.AD(?): Achilles Tatius Astronomus “Introductio in Aratum” p.79 M., 1st c.BC-1st c.AD: Strabo Geographus 10.5.3]]; also of minor poems of Virgil; τῶν κατὰ λεπτὸν πόρων ἀραίωσις, perhaps small pores, [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd c.AD: Galenus Medicus 15.201.]]

__II.2
rarely of the voice, fine, delicate, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Historia Animalium” 545a7, 3rd c.BC: Lycophron Tragicus 687; ἁρμονία 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Fragmenta” 773.23 (Lyric poetry)]]: neuter as adverb, λεπτὸν ἀμφιτιττυβίζειν [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Aves” 235 (Lyric poetry)]]; of sound, λ. ὑποτρύζουσα [Refs 6th c.AD+ [“Anthologia Graeca” 11.352.5 (6th c.AD: Agathias Historicus et Epigrammaticus)]]; compare λεπταλέος.

__II.3
of smell, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Timaeus” 66e (_comparative_).]]

__II.4
of persons, οἱ λ. the poor, [Refs 2nd c.BC+ [2nd c.BC: Polybius Historicus 24.7.3]]; λεπτὴν πλέκειν, proverbial of poor people, [Refs 5th c.AD+ [5th c.AD(?): Hesychius Legal icographus; λεπτὰ ξαίνεις 10th c.AD: Suidas Legal icographus]]

__III
substantive λεπτόν (i.e. ἔντερον), τό, the small intestine, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Hippocrates Medicus “Κωακαὶ προγνώσιες” 311, 449.]]

__III.2
(i.e. νόμισμα) a very small coin, [NT.Luke.21.2], Phot. see at {ὀβολός}; compare#1.6.

__III.3
(i.e. κεράμιον) jar, [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [POxy. 920.4 (2nd-3rd c.AD), “PStrassb.” 40.48 (6th c.AD)]]; compare λεπτίον, λεπτοκεραμεύς.

__III.4
Astron. (i.e. ἑξηκοστόν), division of a degree, πρῶτα λεπτά, = minutes, δεύτερα λ., = seconds, [Refs 1st c.BC+ [1st c.BC: Geminus Astronomicus 18.11, 18]]; λεπτά alone, = minutes, [Refs 1st c.AD+ [PLond. 1.98r.47 (1st-2nd c.AD), “POxy.” 1476 (3rd c.AD).]]

λευκαίνω,
late aorist 1 infinitive λευκᾶναι (see. below): perfect passive λελεύκασμαι [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [3rd c.BC: Diphilus Siphnius Rerum Naturalium Scriptor cited in 2nd c.AD: Athenaeus Epigrammaticus 2.54b, 4th c.AD: Oribasius Medicus “fragment” 102]]:—make white, λεύκαινον ὕδωρ ξεστῇς ἐλάτῃσιν [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 12.172; ἅλα ῥοθίοισι λ. 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Cyclops” 17; ἐς γένυν ἕρπει λευκαίνων ὁ χρόνος 3rd c.BC: Theocritus Poeta Bucolicus 14.70]]; plaster with whitening, λευκᾶναι τὰ λευκώματα [Refs [“Ephes.” 3p.148]]:—passive, to be or become white, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “de Generatione Animalium” 730a6, 4th c.BC: Sopater Comicus 8, 3rd c.BC: Apollonius Rhodius Epicus 1.545]], Diph.Siph.[same place]; to be clarified, of oil, Orib. LSJ / STEPBible (TFLSJ)
λευκός, ή, όν,
light, bright, clear (opposed to μέλας in all senses), αἴγλη [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 6.45]]; λευκὸν (variant{λαμπρόν}).. ἠέλιος ὥς [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 14.185; λ. φάος 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Ajax” 708 (Lyric poetry),compare below 11.3; αἰθήρ 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Andromache” 1228 (_anapaest meter_)]]; of metallic surfaces, λέβης [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 23.268]]; λ. γαλήνη a glassy calm, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 10.94]]; of water, clear, limpid, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 23.282, 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 5.70, 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Supplices” 23 (_anapaest meter_); λ. νᾶμα 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Hercules Furens” 573; - ότατος ποταμῶν 3rd c.BC: Callimachus Epicus “Hymnus in Jovem” 19.]]

__2
metaphorically, clear, distinct, of the voice, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Topica” 106a25, 2nd c.AD: Sextus Empiricus Philosophus “adversus Mathematicos” 6.41]]: in literary sense, clear, λ. στίχος [Refs 1st c.AD+ [“Anthologia Graeca” 11.347 (1st c.AD: Philippus Epigrammaticus): proverbial, λευκὸς Ἑρμῆς]], when a rogue was detected, [Refs [15th c.AD: Macarius Paroemiographus 5.53.]] adverb -κῶς, πάντα φαίνειν, of Hermes, [Refs 1st c.AD+ [1st c.AD: Cornutus Philosophus “de Natura Deorum” 16]]: comparative -ότερον, διαλεχθῆναι [Refs 3rd c.AD+ [3rd c.AD: Heliodorus Scriptor Eroticus 7.20.]]

__II
of colour, white, frequently in [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Homerus Epicus]], varying from the pure white of snow ([ἵπποι] -ότεροι χιόνος [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 10.437)]] to the grey of dust (λευκοὶ ἐγένοντο κονισάλῳ [Refs [5.503); γάλα λ. 4.434; κρῖ 5.196; ἄλφιτα 18.560; ἡνία λεύκ᾽ ἐλέφαντι 5.583; ὀδόντες 10.263; ὀστέα 16.347; ἱστία 1.480; φᾶρος 18.353, etc.]]; λ. ἅρμα, ={λεύκιππον}, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Phoenissae” 172]]; of the white horses used by tyrants, λ. ζεῦγος [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 21.158]], compare λεύκιππο; λ. λίθος marble, [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [“OGI” 219.36 (Sigeum, 3rd c.BC)]], etc., compare λευκόλιθο; λευκῷ[ν]λίθῳ λ. στάθμη a white line on a white stone, proverbial of explanations which do not explain, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Fragmenta” 330]]; ἡ λ. ῥίζα white root (= ἡ τοῦ δρακοντίου, accusative to [Refs 5th c.BC+ [2nd c.AD: Galenus Medicus 19.118), 5th c.BC: Hippocrates Medicus “περὶ νούσων” 2.48, “Nat.Mul.” 32]]; frequently of white or grey hair, λ. κάρη [Refs 7th c.BC+ [7th c.BC: Tyrtaeus Elegiacus 10.23; θρίξ 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Antigone” 1092; λ. γῆρας [prev. author] “Aj.” 625 (Lyric poetry); λευκὰ γήρᾳ σώματα 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Hercules Furens” 909, etc.]]

__II.b
of the human skin, white, fair, sometimes as a sign of youth and beauty, χρώς, πήχεε, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 11.573, 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 23.240]]; λ. παρειά, παρηΐς, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Antigone” 1239, 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Medea” 923; σάρξ, δέρη, [prev. work] 1189 (variant), “IA” 875 (troch.)]]; frequently with the notion of bare, κῶλον, πούς, [Refs [[prev. author] “Ba.” 665, 863 (Lyric poetry), “Ion” 221 (Lyric poetry)]]; compare λευκόπους.

__II.c
of persons, white-skinned, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 474e]]: hence, weakly, womanish, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Thesmophoriazusae” 191, “Ec.” 428, 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Historia Graeca (Hellenica)” 3.4.19; λευκῶν ἀνδρῶν οὐδὲν ὄφελος 15th c.AD: Macarius Paroemiographus 5.55]]; compare λευκόπρωκτος, λευκόχρως.

__II.d
λευκαὶ φρένες in [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “P.” 4.109 is explained by 5th c.AD(?): Hesychius Legal icographus μαινόμεναι]], frantic, passionate (compare λευκῶν πραπίδων· κακῶν φρενῶν, [Refs [[prev. author]).]]

__II.2
λ. χρυσός, pale gold, i.e. gold alloyed with silver (probably the same as ἤλεκτρον), opposed to ἄπεφθος χρυσός, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.50.]]

__II.3
metaphorically, bright, fortunate, happy, λευκὸν ἦμαρ νυκτὸς ἐκ μελαγχίμου [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Persae” 301, compare “Ag.” 668]]; a joyful day or holiday, [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [3rd c.BC: Callimachus Epicus “Aetia” 1.1.2]]; λ. ἡμέρα a happy day, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Fragmenta” 6, cf. Scholia Callias Epigrammaticus “Iamb.” in “PSI” 9.1094.39; variously explained in 3rd c.BC: Phylarchus Historicus 83 1st c.AD: Josephus Historicus, 1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus “Pericles” 27]]; ἡ λ. ψῆφος the vote of acquittal, [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd c.AD: Lucianus Sophista “Harm.” 3, compare 5th c.AD(?): Hesychius Legal icographus]]

__III
λεύκη, ἡ, leuko/n, τό, as substantive, (see entry). (Cogn. with Latin lux, etc.)

λόγος, -ου, ὁ (λέγω)
[in LXX chiefly for  דָּבָר, also for מִלָּה ,אֵמֶר, etc. ;]
__I. Of that by which the inward thought is expressed, Lat. oratio, sermo, vox, verbum.
__1. a word, not in the grammatical sense of a mere name (ἔπος, ὄνομα, ῥῆμα), but a word as  embodying a conception or idea: Mat.8:8, Luk.7:7, 1Co.14:9, 19 Heb.12:19, al.
__2. a saying, statement, declaration: Mat.19:22 (T om.), Mrk.5:36 7:29, Luk.1:29, Jhn.2:22 6:60, Act.7:29, al.; with genitive attrib., Act.13:15, Rom.9:9, Heb.7:28, al.; of the sayings, commands, promises, etc., of teachers, Mat.7:24 10:14, Mrk.8:38, Luk.9:4, Jhn.14:24, al.; λ. κενοί, Eph.5:6; ἀληθινοί, Rev.19:9; πιστοί, Rev.22:6; esp. of the precepts, decrees and promises of God, ὁ λ. τ. θεοῦ, the word of God: Mrk.7:13, Jhn.10:35, Rom.13:9, 1Co.14:36, Php.1:14, al.; absol., ὁ λ., Mat.13:21, 22 Mrk.16:[20], Luk.1:2, Act.6:4, Heb.4:12, al.
__3. speech, discourse: Act.14:12, 2Co.10:10, Jas.3:2; opposite to ἐπιστολή, 2Th.2:15; disting, from σοφία, 1Co.2:1; ἀναστροφή, 1Ti.4:12; δύναμις, 1Co.4:19, 1Th.1:5; ἔργον, Rom.15:18; οὐδενὸς λ. τίμιον (not worthy of mention), Act.20:24; of the faculty of speech, Luk.24:19, 2Co.11:6; of the style of speech, Mat.5:37, 1Co.1:5; of instruction, Col.4:3, 1Pe.3:1; with genitive of person(s), Jhn.5:24 8:52, Act.2:41, al.; ὁ λ. ὁ ἐμός, Jhn.8:31; with genitive obj. (τ.) ἀληθείας, 2Co.6:7, Col.1:5, Jas.1:18; τ. καταλλαγῆς, 2Co.5:19; τ. σταυροῦ, 1Co.1:18; of mere talk, 1Co.4:19, 2o, Col.2:23, 1Jn.3:18; of the talk which one occasions, hence, repute: Col.2:23.
__4. subject-matter, hence, teaching, doctrine: Act.18:15, 2Ti.2:17, al.; esp. of Christian doctrine: Mat.13:20-23, Mrk.4:14-20 8:32, Luk.1:2, Act.8:4, Gal.6:6, 1Th.1:6, al.; with genitive of person(s), τ. θεοῦ, Luk.5:1, Jhn.17:6, Act.4:29, 1Co.14:36, I Jhn.1:10, Rev.6:9, al.; τ. Κυρίου, Act.8:25, 1Th.1:8, al.; τ. Χριστοῦ, Col.3:16, Rev.3:8; with genitive appos., Act.15:7; with genitive attrib., Heb.5:13.
__5. a story, tale, narrative: Mat.28:15, Jhn.21:23, Act.1:1 11:22; before περί, Luk.5:15.
__6. That which is spoken of (Plat., al.; V. Kennedy, Sources, 124), matter, affair, thing: Mat.21:24, Mrk.1:45 11:29, Luk.20:3, Act.8:21; of a matter in dispute, as a case or suit at law, Act.19:38; pl. (1Ma.7:33, al.), Luk.1:4.
__II. Of the inward thought itself, Lat. ratio.
__1. reason,
__(a) of the mental faculty (Hdt., Plat., al.): κατὰ λόγον, Act.18:14;
__(b) a reason, cause: τίνι λόγῳ, Act.10:29; παρεκτὸς λόγου πορνείας, Mat.5:32 19:9, WH, mg., R, mg.
__2. account,
__(a) regard: Act.20:24, Rec.;
__(b) reckoning: Php.4:15, 17; συναίρειν (which see) λ., Mat.18:23 25:19; in forensic sense, Rom.14:12, Heb.13:17, 1Pe.4:5; with genitive of thing(s), Luk.16:2; before περί, Mat.12:36, Act.19:40, 1Pe.3:15.
__3. proportion, analogy: Php.2:16 (Field, Notes, 193 f.).
__III. ὁ λ., the Divine Word or Logos: Jhn.1:1, 14; τ. ζωῆς, 1Jn.1:1; τ. θεοῦ, Rev.19:13 (see Westc, Swete, CGT, in ll.; reff. in Artt., Logos, DB, DCG).

[prev. author] “Ax.” 371a]]; dissolution, πολιτείας [Refs 4th c.BC+ [[prev. author] “Lg.” 945c; νόμων ἢ πολιτείας 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Politica” 1268b30; βίου λύσιν ἔσχε “IG” 14.140 (from Syracuse)]]; λ. κομήτου [Refs 6th c.AD+ [6th c.AD: Philoponus, Joannes Philosophus “in Aristotelis Meteorologicorum librum primum commentarium - Comm. in Arist. deep_entry:
Abbott-Smith / STEPBible (TBESG)
λυσιτελέω, -ῶ
(λυσιτελής, useful, prop., τὰ τέλη λύων), [in LXX: Tob.3:6, Sir.20:10, 14 29:11 * ;]
__1. prop., to indemnify, pay expenses.
__2. to be useful, to profit; usually impers., λυσιτελεῖ, it profits: with, dative of person(s), before εἰ . . . ἤ, Luk.17:2.†
(AS)

---

LSJ / STEPBible (TFLSJ)
λῡσῐτελ-έω,
properly indemnify for expenses incurred, or pay what is due, and then 'pay', i.e. profit, avail (compare λύω see 2), with dative,

__I
with subject expressed, οὔ φημ᾽ ἂν λυσιτελεῖν σφῷν [τοῦτο] [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Plutus” 509; λυσιτελεῖ ἡμῖν ἡ δικαιοσύνη 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Protagoras” 327b; δοῦλος τοιοῦτος οἷος μηδενὶ δεσπότῃ λυσιτελεῖν 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Memorabilia” 2.1.15.]]

__I.2
mostly impersonal, λυσιτελεῖ μοι it profits me, is better for me, with participle, οἷς οὐδ᾽ ἅπαξ ἐλυσιτέλησε πειθομένοις [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Lysias Orator 25.27; πολλοῖς δὴ ἐλυσιτέλησεν ἀδικήσασι 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus Alcaeus1.113d]]: with infinitive, λ. προϊέναι [Refs [[prev. author] “Tht.” 181b]]; τεθνάναι νομίσασα λυσιτελεῖν ἢ ζῆν thinking it better to be dead than alive, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Andocides Orator 1.125, compare 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 407a, 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 2.4.12 (variant), “PHamb.” 27.17 (3rd c.BC)]], etc.: with dative person, it profits one to do so and so, οὐ γάρ οἱ λυσιτελέειν.. δικάζειν [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.97; ὅτι μοι λυσιτελοῖ ὥσπερ ἔχω ἔχειν 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Apologia” 22e, compare 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Hiero” 7.13]]: sometimes with accusative person, it is good that.., λυσιτελεῖ τὸν μέλλοντα κακῶς ἰητρεύεσθαι ἀμφότερα καταγῆναι τὰ σκέλεα [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Hippocrates Medicus “περὶ ἀγμῶν” 19, compare 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 406d: _absolutely_, ἐλυσιτέλει γάρ 4th c.BC: Axionicus Comicus 6.6.]]

__I.3
in bad sense, conspire, as gloss on{ἐς τὸ κακὸν ἀλλήλοισι συντιμωρεῖ} [Refs 5th c.BC+ [(5th c.BC: Hippocrates Medicus “περὶ διαίτης ὀξέων” 17), 2nd c.AD: Galenus Medicus 15.494 (variant{συντελεῖ}).]]

__II
neuter participle as substantive, τὸ λυσιτελοῦν profit, gain, advantage, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 6.85, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 336d, 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 2.28]]; a wrong etymology is given in [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Cratylus” 417c.]]

__1.b
sum paid for redemption of a pledge, in plural, [Refs 2nd c.BC+ [“PBad.” 3.4 (2nd c.BC), etc.]]

__2
atonement, τί γὰρ λ. πεσόντος αἵματο; (so Canter for λυγρόν) [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Choephori” 48]]; of blood-money, [LXX.Exo.21.30, +others]

__3
generally, recompense, λύτρον καμάτων for toil, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “I.” 8(7).1; συμφορᾶς [prev. author] “O.” 7.77.]]

__II
a plant, ={λυσιμάχειος}, Ps.-[Refs 1st c.AD+ [1st c.AD: Dioscorides (Dioscurides) Medicus 4.3.]]

μακρός, ά, όν [ᾰ
by nature], long, whether of Space or Time,

__I
of Space,

__I.1
in length, long, δόρυ [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 7.140]]; νέες, νῆες μ. ships of war, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 7.21, 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 1.41, etc. (_collective_ in _sing._, 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Persae” 380); πλοῖα μ. 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 5.30, 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 1.14]]; ἐπὶ τὰ -ότερα measured by the longer sides, i. e. length-wise, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.50]]; τὰ μ. τείχη the long walls of Athens, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 8.71, etc.; ἐν τῷ μακρῷ σκέλει τῷ πὸτ τῷ Ποτειδανίῳ “SIG” 247 iii 11 (Delph., 4th c.BC)]]; ἡ μακρά (i.e. γραμμή), line traced by δικασταί to indicate the heavier penalty, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Vespae” 106]]; ὁ μ. δρόμος the long-distance torch-race, [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [“SIG” 1068.9 (Patmos, 3rd-2nd c.BC), +others, “OGI” 339.83 (Sestos, 2nd c.BC).]]

__I.2
in height, tall, high, μ. Ὄλυμπος, οὔρεα, δένδρεα, κίων, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 15.193, 13.18, 9.541, 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 1.127, etc.]]; of a man, μακρότερον καὶ πάσσονα θῆκεν ἰδέσθαι [Refs 3rd c.AD+ [8.20, compare 18.195; μ. πύκτης “PLond.” 3.1158.6 (3rd c.AD).]]

__I.2.b
reversely, deep, φρείατα [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 21.197; φάραγξ 3rd c.BC: Herodas Mimographus 8.17.]]

__I.3
in distance, long, far, remote, κέλευθος [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 15.358; οἶμος 8th-7th c.BC: Hesiodus Epicus “Opera et Dies” 290; ναυτιλίαι 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.1; στόλος 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Philoctetes” 490]]; μ. ἐπιβοήθειαι long marches to aid, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 5.4.47]]; remote, ἀποικία [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Prometheus Vinctus” 814]]; τὰ μακρότατα the remotest parts, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 2.32: frequently in _neuter_ _sing._ and _plural_ as]] adverb, μακρὰ βιβάς, βιβάσθων, with long strides, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 7.213, 13.809]]; μακρὰ ῥίψαις, δισκήσαις, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “P.” 1.45, “I.” 2.35; - ότερον σφενδονᾶν 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 3.4.16]]; μακρὸν ἀῧσαι, βοᾶν, to shout so as to be heard afar, i. e. loudly, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 3.81, 2.224; μακρὰ μεμυκώς 18.580; μακρὸν ἠχεῖν 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Protagoras” 329a; κλάειν σε μακρὰ κελεύσας 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Equites” 433 (see. κλαίω and below see)]]; later by analogy, μακρὰ χαίρειν φράσας τῷ ναυπηγῷ [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd c.AD: Lucianus Sophista “Nav.” 2, compare “Apol.” 3, +others, 2nd-3rd c.AD: Dio Cassius Historicus 46.3]]; compare μακράν.

__I.4
generally, large in size or degree, great, ἤπειρος [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Eumenides” 75; ὄλβος 5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “P.” 2.26; πλοῦτος 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Ajax” 130; τιμήματα 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Politica” 1278a23, compare 1297b4 (_superlative_); οὐσία [prev. work] 1290b16, 1321a11; μακροτέρα ἀρετά 5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “I.” 4(3).13; ἐλπίσαντες μακρότερα μὲν τῆς δυνάμεως, ἐλάσσω δὲ τῆς βουλήσεως 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 3.39]]; μ. τραπεζῖται, perhaps big bankers, Cat.Codex Astr.[Refs [7.222.]]

__I.5
dative μακρῷ, to strengthen comparative and superlative, by far, μ. πρῶτος [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.34; ἄριστος μ. [prev. author] 9.71; ἀσθενεστέρα μ. 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Prometheus Vinctus” 514, compare 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Philebus” 66e; μ. μάλιστα 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.171, compare 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Eumenides” 30, etc.; κάκιστα δὴ μ. 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Antigone” 895]]: also with Verbs implying comparison, ἀριστεύει μ. [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Prometheus Vinctus” 890 (Lyric poetry), compare 1st c.BC: Dionysius Halicarnassensis 1.2.]]

__II
of Time, long [Refs 8th c.BC+ [(8th c.BC: Homerus Epicus only in 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey”), ἤματα, νύξ, 10.470, 11.373]]; αἰών see reading in [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “N.” 3.75; μ. χρόνος 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.32, etc.]]; οὐ μ. χρόνου for no long time, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Antigone” 1078, etc.; διὰ μ. χρόνου 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Persae” 741 (troch.); ἐν χρόνῳ μ. 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Coloneus” 88, etc.; δι᾽ αἰῶνος μ. 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Supplices” 582 (Lyric poetry); τὸν μ. βίον [prev. author] “Pr.” 449; τοῦ μ. βίου 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Ajax” 473]]; μηνὶ -ότερος by a month, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.32]]; μακρῷ[Refs 2nd c.AD+ [(compare 1.5) πρότερον 2nd c.AD: Galenus Medicus 8.958]]; μ. ἐέλδωρ a long-cherished wish, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 23.54]]; μ. γόοι, ὀδύρματα, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Electra” 375, 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Hecuba” 297.]]

__II.2
long, tedious, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “N.” 4.33, etc.; λόγοι 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Electra” 1335, 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 3.60, etc.]]; μακρὰν ἔοικε λέξειν (i.e. ῥῆσιν) [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Thesmophoriazusae” 382; οὐδὲ εἷς Ὅμηρον εἴρηκεν μακρόν 4th-3rd c.BC: Philemo Comicus 97.7]]; μακρόν [ἐστι] with infinitive, Latin longum est, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “I.” 6(5).56; μ. ἂν εἴη γράφειν 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Agesilaus” 7.1]]. adverb - ρῶς, λέγεσθαι [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Antiphanes Comicus 268]]: comparative -ότερον, ποιεῖς you are taking too long, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [3rd c.BC: Zenon Papyri du Caire 48.4 (3rd c.BC),compare 4th-3rd c.BC: Philippides Comicus 21.]]

__II.3
Grammars, long in quantity, φωνήεντα [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Poetica” 1458a11, 1st c.BC: Dionysius Halicarnassensis “de Compositione Verborum” 15]]; μακρά (i.e. συλλαβή), ἡ, [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd c.AD: Apollonius Dyscolus Grammaticus “de Pronominibus;” 92.12; ἡ φύσει μ. [prev. author] “Adv.” 179.16]]: comparative, φωνήεντι μακροτέρῳ [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Poetica” 1458a1]]; also μακρά (i.e. προσῳδία), ἡ, mark of long quantity, [Refs 2nd c.BC+ [2nd c.AD: Sextus Empiricus Philosophus “adversus Mathematicos” 1.113, 2nd c.BC: Dionysius Thrax Grammaticus “Supp.” 674.7; ᾱ μακρόν 2nd c.AD: Apollonius Dyscolus Grammaticus “de Pronominibus;” 112. 6.]]

__III
neuter with Preps. in adverbial sense, διὰ μακροῦ (i.e. χρόνου) after a long time, long delayed, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Hecuba” 320, “Ph.” 1069]]; οὐ διὰ μακροῦ not long after, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 6.15, 91, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus Alcaeus2.151b (also of place, οὐ διὰ μ. τῆς Ῥώμης 1st c.BC: Dionysius Halicarnassensis 9.56); διὰ μακρῶν 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Fragmenta” 420.1; διὰ μακρᾶς 3rd-2nd c.BC: Phalaris Epistolographus “Epistulae - Epistolographi” 69.1]]; but διὰ μακρῶν at great length, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Gorgias” 449b, etc.; διὰ μακροτέρων 5th-6th c.BC: Isocrates Orator 4.106]]; μικρῷ διὰ μ. at somewhat greater length, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Politica” 1279b11.]]

__III.2
ὄλβος οὐκ ἐς μακρὸν ἔρχεται for no long time, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “P.” 3.105]]; ἐς τὰ μακρότατα to the utmost, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 6.31; see at {μακράν} 11.]]

__III.3
ἐπὶ μακρόν far, a long way, πορεύεσθαι [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 5.4.47]]; of Time, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [3rd c.BC: Callimachus Epicus “Hymnus in Delum” 255; ὅσον ἐπὶ μακρότατον οἷοί τε ἐγενόμεθα ἐξικέσθαι ἀκοῇ 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 4.16, compare 2.34 (ἐπὶ omitted 1.171 codices)]]; τοσόνδε ἐπὶ μ. ἐπυθόμην [Refs [[prev. author] 2.29]]; ἐπὶ μακρότερον yet more, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 4.41.]]

__IV
regular comparative and superlative, see above: irregular comparative μάσσων, superlative μήκιστος, (see entry).

__V
adverb -ρῶς at great length, opposed to συντόμως, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Rhetorica” 1416b4]]; slowly, [Refs 2nd c.BC+ [2nd c.BC: Polybius Historicus 3.51.2]]; μ. ἔχειν τοῖν σκέλοιν have long legs, [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd-3rd c.AD: Philostratus Sophista “de gymnastica” 31]]; of pronunciation, [Refs 1st c.BC+ [1st c.BC: Dionysius Halicarnassensis “de Compositione Verborum” 15; μ. ἐκφέρειν συλλαβήν 1st c.BC-1st c.AD: Strabo Geographus 13.1.68: but the]] adverb is usually expressed by neuter μακρόν or μακρά, compare above [Refs [1.3]]; μακρὰ κλάειν to howl loudly, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Thesmophoriazusae” 211; οἰμώξει μ. [prev. author] “Av.” 1207, “Pl.” 111; ὀτοτύζεσθαι μ. [prev. author] “Lys.” 520]]; τί μακρὰ δεῖ λέγει; [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Antiphanes Comicus 33.5; also by μακράν (see. entry); or by _neuter_ with a _preposition_, see above 111]]: for comparative and superlative of the adverb, see at {μακροτέρως, μακροτάτω}: neuter plural -ότερα as adverb, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Phaedrus” 250c, +others]] — Fem. μακρά not to be confused with μάκρα (which see). (Cf. Avest. mas-'long', Latin ma?~Xcer.)

soft:

__I
of things subject to touch, εὐνή [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 9. 618; κώεα 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 3.38; τάπης μαλακοῦ ἐρίοιο 4.124; χιτών 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 2.42, “PSI” 4.364.5 (3rd c.BC)]]; πέπλοι [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 24.796]]; νειὸς μ. fresh-ploughed fallow, [Refs [18.541]]; λειμῶνες μ. soft grassy meadows, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 5.72, compare 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 14.349; πόας ἄνθος 7th-6th c.BC: Sappho Lyrica 54; τάπητες.. -ώτεροι ὕπνω 3rd c.BC: Theocritus Poeta Bucolicus 15.125]]; of the skin or flesh, μ. παρειαί [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Antigone” 783 (Lyric poetry); χρώς 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Medea” 1403 (_anapaest meter_); σώματα 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Memorabilia” 3.10.1]]; πρόβατα μ. soft-fleeced, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 47.52]]; τόποι πεδινοὶ καὶ μ., opposed to hard, rugged ground, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Historia Animalium” 607a10]]; οἱ κρημνοὶ οἱ μ.[Refs 3rd c.BC+ [[prev. work] 615b31; μ. πέτρα “SIG” 970.8 (3rd c.BC), “PPetr.” 2p.6 (3rd c.BC)]]; μ. τέφρα a slow fire, [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [3rd-2nd c.BC: Philo Mechanicus “(Belopoeica) Excerpte aus Philons Mechanik - Ath. Akad.” 89.36; so μ. πῦρ 1st c.AD: Andromachus Poeta Medicus cited in 2nd c.AD: Galenus Medicus 13.26; μ. ἀνθρακιά 1st c.AD: Dioscorides (Dioscurides) Medicus 2.76]]; ὕδωρ μ., of marsh water, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Fragmenta - American Journal of Philology” 192.8 (_anapaest meter_), 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Timaeus” 59d (compare μαλθακός)]]; of soil, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Oeconomicus” 19.8, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Critias” 111b.]] adverb, μαλακῶς ἐνεύδειν, εὑδέμεναι, to sleep softly, i.e. on soft bedding, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 3.350, 24.255; μαλακώτατα καθεύδειν 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Memorabilia” 2.1.24]]; καθίζου μ. sit softly, i.e. on a cushion, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Equites” 785; ὑποστορεῖτε μ. τῷ κυνί 4th c.BC: Eubulus Comicus 90, compare 108]]; but ὡς μ. ἐσθίεις what dainty food you have! of persons or modes of life, soft, mild, gentle, μαλακώτερος ἀμφαφάασθαι easier to handle, of a fallen hero, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 22.373; ἐκ τῶν μ. χώρων μ. ἄνδρας γίνεσθαι 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 9.122; - ώτερον ἐκ σκληροτέρου τὸ τῆς ψυχῆς ἦθος 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Leges” 666b; ἀρνίου -ώτερος 4th-3rd c.BC: Philippides Comicus 29; - ώτερον τὸ ἦθος τὸ τῶν θηλειῶν 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Historia Animalium” 608a25; ἀρρένων καὶ μ. ἠθῶν καὶ πράξεων 1st c.BC: Philodemus Gadarensis Epigrammaticus “Mus.” p.92 K.]]

in bad sense, soft, μ. ἐν τῇ ξυναγωγῇ τοῦ πολέμου [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 2.18; μ. ἦν περὶ τοῦ μισθοῦ [prev. author] 8.29; πρὸς τὸ πονεῖν 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Memorabilia” 1.2.2]]. adverb - κῶς, ξυμμαχεῖν [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 6.78]]; -ωτέρως ἀνθήπτετο attacked him somewhat feebly, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. author] 8.50; μ. φιλεῖν 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Memorabilia” 3.11.10.]]

__III.2.b
faint-hearted, cowardly, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 6.13, 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Historia Graeca (Hellenica)” 4.5.16 (_comparative_), etc.]]

__III.2.c
morally weak, lacking in self-control, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 7.153 (_comparative_)]]; ἀντίκειται τῷ μ. ὁ καρτερικός [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Ethica Nicomachea” 1150a33]]: with infinitive, μαλακὸς καρτερεῖν πρὸς ἡδονάς τε καὶ λύπας [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 556c; τὸ τρυφῶν καὶ μ. 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Vespae” 1455 (Lyric poetry)]]; μ. οὐδὲν ἐνδιδόναι not to give in from weakness or want of spirit, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 3.51, 105, 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Plutus” 488]]; τὰ μ. indulgences, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Epicharmus Comicus 288, compare 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 7.2.28.]]

__III.2.d
={παθητικός}, [NT+3rd c.BC+ [“PHib.” 1.54.11 (3rd c.BC), NT.1Cor.6.9, 2nd c.AD: Vettius Valens Astrologus 113.22, 3rd c.AD(?): Diogenes Laertius 7.173.]]

__III.2.e
of music, soft, effeminate, μ. ἁρμονίαι [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 398e, 411a, compare 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Politica” 1290a28]]; tuned to a low pitch, opposed to σύντονος, χρῶμα μ. [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd c.AD: Cleonides Musicus “Introductio Harmonica - Musici Scriptores Graeci” 7, etc.]]

__III.2.f
of style, feeble, τὸ -ώτερον καὶ ταπεινότερον [Refs 5th c.BC+ [1st c.BC: Philodemus Gadarensis Epigrammaticus “Rh.” 1.197 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus]]

__III.2.g
of reasoning, weak, loose, λόγος [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Isocrates Orator 12.4 (_comparative_), compare 5.149 (_comparative_)]]; λόγος λίαν μ. [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Metaphysica” 1090b8.]] adverb -κῶς, συλλογίζεσθαι to reason loosely, [Refs [[prev. author] “Rh.” 1396b1 (_comparative_)]]; ἀποδεικνύειν -ώτερον [Refs [[prev. author] “Metaphorical” 1025b13.]]

__III.3
weakly, sickly, -κῶς ἔχειν to be ill, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Hermippus Comicus 58, Pseudo-Herodotus Historicus “Vitae Homeri” 34, 2nd c.AD: Lucianus Sophista “DDeor.” 9.1; - κῶς διάκειται “PCair.Zen.” 263.3 (3rd c.BC).]]

adverb -κῶς, see supr. I, II, III.

Abbott-Smith / STEPBible (TBESG)
μάλιστα, see: μάλα.
μάλα
adv., [in LXX for אֲבָל, 3Ki.1:43, Dan LXX 10:21, al.; compar. for מ, Num.13:32 (31), al.; μᾶλλον ἠ (מ), Gen.19:9, al.; superlat., 2Ma.8:7, 4Ma.4:22 12:9 15:4 ;]
__I. Pos., very, very much, exceedingly (cl.; LXX ut supr.; in NT its place is taken by λίαν, σφόδρα, etc.).
__II. Compar., μᾶλλον.
__1. Of increase, more; with qualifying words: πολλῷ, Mrk.10:48, Luk.18:39, Rom.5:15, 17, Php.2:12, al.; πόσῳ, Luk.12:24, Rom.11:12, al.; τοσούτῳ . . . ὅσῳ, Heb.10:25.
__2. Of comparison, the more: Luk.5:15, Jhn.5:18, Act.5:14, 1Th.4:1, 10, 2Pe.1:10; ἔτι μ. καὶ μ., Php.1:9; with compar., Mrk.7:36, 2Co.7:13; πολλῴ μ. κρεῖσον, Php.1:23; μ. διαφέρειν, with genitive, Mat.6:26; μ. ἤ, Mat.18:13; with genitive, 1Co.14:18; as periphr. for compar., Act.20:35, 1Co.9:15, Gal.4:27; μ. δέ (EV, yea rather), Rom.8:34.
__3. Of preference, rather, the rather, sooner: with qualifying words, πολλῷ, Mat.6:30, al.; πολύ, Heb.12:25; πόσῳ, Mat.7:11, al.; in a question, οὐ μ., 1Co.9:12; after a neg., Mat.10:6, al.; θέλω (εὐδοκῶ) μ., 1Co.14:5, 2Co.5:8; ζηλῶ, 1Co.14:1; with subst., τ. σκότος ἢ τ. φῶς, Jhn.3:19; μ. δέ, Gal.4:9.
__III. Superl., μάλιστα
, most, most of all, above all: Act.20:38 25:26, Gal.6:10, Php.4:22, 1Ti.4:10 5:8, 17, 2Ti.4:13, Tit.1:10, Phm 16, 2Pe.2:10; μ. γνώστης, Act.26:3
(AS)

but [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Homerus Epicus]] sometimes uses the ultima  long before λ, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 3.214, 4.379]]; before μ, [Refs [10.172],]] adverb very, exceedingly, prefixed or subjoined to Adjectives, Verbs, and Adverbs:

__1
strengthening the word with which it stands,

with adjectives, in [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Homerus Epicus most frequently, μάλα πολλά]] very many, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 1.1]]; μ. πᾶσα, μ. πάντα, every one, all together, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 13.741, 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 2.306, etc.]]; μάλ᾽ ἀσκηθής all unhurt, [Refs [5.26]]; ἀβληχρὸς μ. τοῖος quite gentle, [Refs [11.135]]; σαρδάνιον μ. τοῖον a quite sardonic smile,[Refs [20.302; μάλα μυρίοι 15.556, 16.121, etc.]]; ἐμέο πρότερος μ. actually before me, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 10.124]]; later, μ. φιλόσοφοι, πλάτανος μάλ᾽ ἀμφιλαφής, etc., [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Parmenides” 126b, “Phdr.” 230b, etc.: strengthened, μ. δὴ πρεσβύτης]] very old, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 8.7.1; μ. γέ τινες ὀλίγοι 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 531e.]]

__1.b
with Advs., πάγχυ μ., μ. πάγχυ, quite utterly, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 12.165, 14.143; πάνυ μ. 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Phaedo” 80c]]; εὖ μ. right well, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 22.190, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Phaedo” 92d, etc.; μάλα.. εὖ 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 23.175, compare 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Theaetetus” 156a]]; μάλ᾽ αὐτίκα (see. αὐτίκα); μάλ᾽ αἰεί for ever and aye, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 13.557, 23.717]]; ἄχρι μ. κνέφαος until quite dark, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 18.370]]; μάλ᾽ ὧδε just in this way, [Refs [6.258]]; μ. διαμπερές right through, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 20.362]]; μ. μόλις (see. μόλις); to express repeated action, μάλ᾽ αὖθις [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Agamemnon” 1345, “Ch.” 654; μάλ᾽ αὖ 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Electra” 1410, etc.]]; μ. alone, ἔα, ἔα μ. [Refs 8th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Choephori” 870; οἲ μ. καὶ τόδ᾽ ἀλγῶ [prev. author] “Pers.” 1045 (Lyric poetry); εἶα μ. 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Pax” 460s q. (so ἄλλος πύργος.., καὶ ἕτερος μ. ἐπὶ τούτῳ 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.181, compare 7.186): frequently after καί, αὗταί σ᾽ ὁδηγήσουσι καὶ μάλ᾽ ἀσμένως 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Prometheus Vinctus” 728, compare “Ch.” 879: with _negative_, μάλ᾽ οὐ, μάλ᾽ οὔ πως, 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 2.241, 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 5.103; οὐ μ. 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.93, 2.37, 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Philoctetes” 676 (Lyric poetry).]]

__1.c
with Verbs, μήτ᾽ ἄρ με μάλ᾽ αἴνεε [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 10.249; μ. τ᾽ ἔκλυον αὐτοῦ 1.218]]; ἡ δὲ μάλ᾽ ἡνιόχευεν drove carefully, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 6.319]]; μ... προπέμπει in earnest, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Septem contra Thebas” 915 (Lyric poetry), compare “Eu.” 368 (Lyric poetry); καὶ μ. δοκοῦντας φρονίμους εἶναι 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 6.1.36; μ. πολιορκούμενοι [prev. author] “HG” 7.1.25.]]

__2
strengthening an assertion, νῦν σε μ. χρὴ αἰχμητὴν ἔμεναι, i.e. now or never, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 16.492]]; τῷ κε μάλ᾽ ἤ κεν μεῖνε.. then doubtless he would have stayed, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 4.733]]; σοὶ δὲ μάλ᾽ ἕψομ᾽ ἐγώ yes indeed.., [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 10.108]]; ἀλλὰ μάλ᾽ ὤφελλες why plainly.., [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 4.472: frequently with another word, as ἦ μ. δή]].. now in very truth, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 5.422, etc.; ἦ δή που μ. 21.583; frequently ἦ μ. (without δή) 3.204, etc.]]

__3
in [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Homerus Epicus sometimes after εἰ, as εἰ μ. μιν χόλος ἵκοι]] if wrath come on him ever so much, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 17.399, compare 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 5.485, +others; καὶ εἰ μ. τις πολεμίζοι 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 9.318]]; also μ. περ with participle, μ. περ μεμαώς though desiring never so much, [Refs [13.317, compare 14.58, 17.710, +others]]; καὶ μ. περ [Refs 8th c.BC+ [1.217, compare 17.571; καὶ εὐρέα περ μάλ᾽ ἐόντα 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 18.385.]]

__4
in Attic dialect frequently in answers, yes, certainly, μ. γε [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 555d, 564e, etc.; μ. τοι 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Memorabilia” 1.2.46; καὶ μ. 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Phaedrus” 258c; καὶ μ. γε [prev. author] “Tht.” 148c, etc.; καὶ μ. δή [prev. work] 177a]]; καὶ μ. ἐπαύσατο certainly it stopped, [Refs [[prev. author] “Smp.” 189a, etc.]]

Oxon.” 2.240]]; late Doric dialect μαλλότερον [Refs 5th c.AD+ [Pempelus Philosophus cited in 5th c.AD: Stobaeus, Joannes 4.25.52]]:—more, rather, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 5.231, 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 1.351, +others: mostly followed by ἤ, but in Prose also by a _genitive_, μ. τοῦ ξυμφέροντος]] more than is expedient, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Antipho Orator 5.1; μ. τοῦ δέοντος 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Gorgias” 487b, 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Memorabilia” 4.3.8 (sometimes expressed by μᾶλλον alone, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Phaedo” 63d); οὐπώποτ᾽ ἔργου μ. εἱλόμην λόγους 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Fragmenta” 394]]; παντὸς μ. most assuredly, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Leges” 715d (see. below 8); in [prev. author] “Ap.” 36d, οὐκ ἔσθ᾽ ὅτι μ. πρέπει οὕτως, ὡς.., ὡς is probably ={ἤ} (see. ὡς)]]: denoting a constant increase, more and more, sometimes doubled, μ. μ. [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Iphigenia Taurica” 1406, 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Ranae” 1001 (Lyric poetry), 2nd c.AD: Alexander Rhetor 29]]: in positive sense, exceedingly, κηρόθι μ. [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 9.300, 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 15.370, +others:]] —Usage:

__II.1
frequently strengthened by other words, πολὺ μ. [NT+8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 9.700, etc.; ἔτι μ. 14.97, +others; μ. ἔτ᾽ ἢ τὸ πάροιθεν 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 1.322; καὶ μ. 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 8.470; καὶ μ. ἔτι 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 18.22; ἔτι καὶ μ. 5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “P.” 10.57; ἔτι καὶ πολὺ μ. 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 23.386, 429, 8th-7th c.BC: Hesiodus Epicus “Theogonia” 428; ἐπὶ μ. 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 3.104; ἔτι ἐπὶ μ. μᾶλλον δέ much more.., or rather.., to correct a statement already made, ὁ δεσπότης πέπραγεν εὐτυχέστατα, μ. δ᾽ ὁ Πλοῦτος αὐτός [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Plutus” 634; πολλοί, μ. δὲ πάντες 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 18.65, compare 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Symposium” 173e; so ἢ μ. 1st c.AD: Cornutus Philosophus “de Natura Deorum” 20, 6th c.AD: Simplicius Philosophus “in Aristotelis Physica commentaria - Comm. in Arist. __III

[Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Isaeus Orator 2.20]]; μ. μὲν.., εἰ δὲ μὴ.. [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Philoctetes” 617]]; δοκέων μιν μ. ταύτης ἂν πείθεσθαι certainly, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 3.53]]; τί μ.; what precisely? __III.1
strengthened, ὡς μ. certainly, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Supplices” 294, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 460a, etc.; ὅσον μ. 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Prometheus Vinctus” 524; ὅσα ἐδύνατο μ. 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.185; ὡς δύναμαι μ. 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 367b; ὡς οἷόν τε μ. μάλα
adv., [in LXX for אֲבָל, 3Ki.1:43, Dan LXX 10:21, al.; compar. for מ, Num.13:32 (31), al.; μᾶλλον ἠ (מ), Gen.19:9, al.; superlat., 2Ma.8:7, 4Ma.4:22 12:9 15:4 ;]
__I. Pos., very, very much, exceedingly (cl.; LXX ut supr.; in NT its place is taken by λίαν, σφόδρα, etc.).
__II. Compar., μᾶλλον.
__1. Of increase, more; with qualifying words: πολλῷ, Mrk.10:48, Luk.18:39, Rom.5:15, 17, Php.2:12, al.; πόσῳ, Luk.12:24, Rom.11:12, al.; τοσούτῳ . . . ὅσῳ, Heb.10:25.
__2. Of comparison, the more: Luk.5:15, Jhn.5:18, Act.5:14, 1Th.4:1, 10, 2Pe.1:10; ἔτι μ. καὶ μ., Php.1:9; with compar., Mrk.7:36, 2Co.7:13; πολλῴ μ. κρεῖσον, Php.1:23; μ. διαφέρειν, with genitive, Mat.6:26; μ. ἤ, Mat.18:13; with genitive, 1Co.14:18; as periphr. for compar., Act.20:35, 1Co.9:15, Gal.4:27; μ. δέ (EV, yea rather), Rom.8:34.
__3. Of preference, rather, the rather, sooner: with qualifying words, πολλῷ, Mat.6:30, al.; πολύ, Heb.12:25; πόσῳ, Mat.7:11, al.; in a question, οὐ μ., 1Co.9:12; after a neg., Mat.10:6, al.; θέλω (εὐδοκῶ) μ., 1Co.14:5, 2Co.5:8; ζηλῶ, 1Co.14:1; with subst., τ. σκότος ἢ τ. φῶς, Jhn.3:19; μ. δέ, Gal.4:9.
__III. Superl., μάλιστα
, most, most of all, above all: Act.20:38 25:26, Gal.6:10, Php.4:22, 1Ti.4:10 5:8, 17, 2Ti.4:13, Tit.1:10, Phm 16, 2Pe.2:10; μ. γνώστης, Act.26:3

[prev. author] 18.21]]; ἀνὴρ δόκιμος ὁμοῖα τῷ μ. as famous as he that is most [famous], [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 7.118, compare 3.8; τοῖς μάλισθ᾽ ὁμοίως 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator “Epistulae” 2.24.]]

__III.2.b
ἐν τοῖς μ. especially, as much as any, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 8.90, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Symposium” 173b, etc.]]: with a superlative, ἐν τοῖς μ. ὠμότατος [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd-3rd c.AD: Aelianus “Varia Historia” 14.40; φιλτάτη καὶ ἀναγκαιοτάτη ἐν τοῖς μ. 6th c.AD: Procopius Caesariensis Historicus “Historia Arcana” 4.]]

__III.3
added to a superlative (see. μάλα [Refs 8th c.BC+ [11.2, πλεῖστον), ἔχθιστος μ., μ. φίλτατος, 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 2.220, 24.334; μ. κῃ ἐμφερέστατα 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 2.76; μ. φίλτατος 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Hippolytus” 1421: to a _comparative_ (?), μ. δὴ ὀκνηρότεροι ἐγένοντο 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 4.55.]]

__III.4
μάλιστα for μᾶλλον, μ. τῆς κόρης [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Iphigenia Aulidensis” [1594]; μ. ἤ ἐμοί 3rd c.BC: Apollonius Rhodius Epicus 3.91.]]

__III.5
with numerals, in round numbers, about, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 3.29, 92, 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Historia Graeca (Hellenica)” 5.2.31, etc.]]; πεντήκοντα μάλιστα[Refs 5th c.BC+ [is 49 in 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 1.118; ἑκατοστὸς μ. 99t h, [prev. author] 8.68]]; ἐς μέσον μάλιστά κῃ about the middle, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.191, compare 76; ἥμισυ μ. 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 1.93]]; μ. σφᾶς μεσοῦν δειπνοῦντας that they were about the middle of supper, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Symposium” 175c; κου μ. 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 7.22; μ. πως 2nd c.BC: Polybius Historicus 2.41.13.]]

__III.6
in answers, most certainly, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Plutus” 827, etc.; μ. γε 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Tyrannus” 994, 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Nubes” 253; μ. πάντων [prev. author] “Av.” 1531; πάντων μ. 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Gorgias” 453d; see above 1.4]]. (Orig. perhaps fiercely, compare μαλερός.)

Abbott-Smith / STEPBible (TBESG)
μανθάνω
[in LXX chiefly for לָמַד ;]
__1. to learn, esp. by inquiry: absol., 1Co.14:31, 1Ti.2:11, 2Ti.3:7; with accusative of thing(s), Jhn.7:15 (sc. αὐτά), Rom.16:17, 1Co.14:35, Php.4:9, 2Ti.3:14, Rev.14:3; before quaes. indir., Mat.9:13; Χριστόν, Eph.4:20 (ICC, in l); before ἀπό, with genitive of thing(s), Mat.24:32, Mrk.13:28; ἀπό, with genitive of person(s), Mat.11:29, Col.1:7; παρά, with genitive of person(s), 2Ti.3:14; ἐν, with dative of person(s), 1Co.4:6; "point" aorist (M, Pr., 117), to ascertain, before ὅτι, Act.23:27; with accusative before ἀπό, Gal.3:2.
__2. to learn by use and practice, acquire the habit of, be accustomed to: with inf. (Bl., § 69, 4), 1Ti.5:4, Tit.3:14; id. with nom, in pred. (El., § 72, 1), Php.4:11; with accusative of thing(s) before ἀπό, Heb.5:8; ἀργαὶ μανθάνουσιν (EV, they learn to be idle; Bl., § 73, 5; Field, Notes, 210), 1Ti.5:13.†
(AS)

μανθάνω,
[Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “P.” 3.80, etc.]]: future μᾰθήσομαι [Refs 6th c.BC+ [6th c.BC: Theognis Elegiacus 35, 4th-5th c.BC: Parmenides Poeta Philosophus 1.31, 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Prometheus Vinctus” 926, 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Ajax” 667, “OC” 1527, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Philebus” 53e, etc.]]; Doric dialect μᾰθεῦμαι uncertain in [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [3rd c.BC: Theocritus Poeta Bucolicus 11.60; late μαθήσω 2nd c.AD: Galenus Medicus 13.450, “Sect.Intr.” 9 (codex L)]]: aorist ἔμᾰθον [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “N.” 7.18, etc.]]; Epic dialect ἔμμαθον [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 17.226, μάθον (see. below)]]: perfect μεμάθηκα [Refs 6th c.BC+ [6th c.BC: Anacreon Lyricus 74, 6th c.BC: Xenophanes Poeta Philosophus 10, 5th c.BC: Empedocles Poeta Philosophus 17.9, 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Nubes” 1148, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Euthyphro” 9c, etc.:]]pluperfect ἐμεμαθήκη[Refs [[prev. work] 14c]]; 3rd.pers. singular ἐμεμαθήκει [Refs [[prev. author] “Men.” 86a]]; 3rd.pers. plural μεμαθήκεσαν [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Hippocrates Medicus “περὶ ἀρχαίης ἰητρικῇς” 10]]:—passive, used by good writers only in present, as [Refs 8th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Timaeus” 87b, “Men.” 88b.— 8th c.BC: Homerus Epicus uses only the _Epic dialect_]]aorist forms μάθον, ἔμμαθες, ἔμμαθε:—learn, especially by study (but also, by practice, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Simonides Lyricus 147, 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Ethica Nicomachea” 1103a32, “Metaphorical” 1049b31, 980b24]]; by experience, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Agamemnon” 251 (Lyric poetry), 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Anthologia Graeca” 0.81a40), thrice in 8th c.BC: Homerus Epicus, ἔργα κακά 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 17.226, 18.362]]: with infinitive, μάθον ἔμμεναι ἐσθλός [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 6.444: frequently later, οὐδὲ μαθόντες γινώσκουσιν 1st c.AD(?): Heraclitus 17; ἀεὶ γὰρ ἡβᾷ τοῖς γέρουσιν εὖ μαθεῖν 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Agamemnon” 584]]; ταλάντου τοῦτ᾽ ἔμαθεν for a talent, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Nubes” 876]]; οἱ μανθάνοντες learners, pupils, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Memorabilia” 1.2.17]]; μ. τὰ Ὁμήρου ἔπη learn by heart, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. author] “Smp.” 3.5; μ. βέμβικα 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Aves” 1461]]; μ. τί τινος learn from.., [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “P.” 3.80, 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Prometheus Vinctus” 701, 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Tyrannus” 575, etc.: with Preps., ἐσθλῶν ἄπ᾽ ἐσθλὰ μαθήσεαι]] Thgn.[same place]; μ. καθ᾽ Ὅμηρον Xenoph.[same place]; τι ἔκ τινος [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Electra” 352; ἐκ ποίων ὀνομάτων μεμαθηκὼς ἦν τὰ πράγματα 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Cratylus” 438a; παρά τινος 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Agamemnon” 859, 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Antigone” 1012, etc.]]; παρά τινος ὅτι.. [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Isocrates Orator 8.67; πρός τινος 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Coloneus” 12]]; πρὶν μάθοιμ᾽ εἰ.. [Refs [[prev. author] “Ph.” 961]]: with infinitive, learn to.., or how to.., [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” [same place], 5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “P.” 4.284, 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Prometheus Vinctus” 1068 (_anapaest meter_), 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Ajax” 667; μ. σεαυτὸν αἰς χύνεσθαι 3rd c.AD: Democritus Epigrammaticus 244.]]

__II
acquire a habit of, and in past tenses, to be accustomed to.., with infinitive, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Empedocles Poeta Philosophus 17.9, 5th c.BC: Hippocrates Medicus “περὶ ἀρχαίης ἰητρικῇς” 10; τοὺς μεμαθηκότας ἀριστᾶν [prev. author] “Acut.” 28]]; τὸ μεμαθηκός that which is usual, πρότερον ἢ ὕστερον τοῦ μ. [Refs [[prev. author] “Mul.” 2.128]]; ἀργαὶ μανθάνουσι acquire a habit of idleness, [NT.1Tim.5.13.]

__III
perceive, remark, notice, τὸ πλῆθος [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 7.208; ἀλλήλους μ. ὁπόσοι εἴησαν 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Historia Graeca (Hellenica)” 2.1.1.]]

__III.2
frequently with participle, μ. τὴν νέα ἐμβαλοῦσαν [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 8.88; ἔμαθον ταῦτα πρησσόμενα [prev. author] 1.160; ἵνα μάθῃ σοφιστὴς ὤν 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Prometheus Vinctus” 62; μὴ μάθῃ μ᾽ ἥκοντα 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Philoctetes” 13, compare 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Bacchae” 1113]]; μάνθανε ὤν know that you are, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Electra” 1342; διαβεβλημένος οὐ μανθάνεις 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 3.1; εἰ μὴ μανθάνετε κακὰ σπεύδοντες 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 6.39.]]

__III.3
with ὅτι, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 394b]]; with ὡς, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 1.34, etc.]]

__IV
understand [Refs 5th c.BC+ [cf (5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Euthydemus” 277e), ὡς μάθω σαφέστερον 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Choephori” 767; ὄψ᾽ ἐμάθεθ᾽ ἡμᾶς 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Bacchae” 1345; τὰλεγόμενα 5th c.BC: Lysias Orator 10.15, etc.: with _dative_ _person_, εἴ μοι μανθάνεις]] if you take me, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 394c: frequently in Dialogue, μανθάνεις]]; d'ye see? Answ., πάνυ μανθάνω perfectly! [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Ranae” 195, compare 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Meno” 84d. “Tht.” 174b; εἶεν, μανθάνω [prev. author] “R.” 372e, compare “Phd.” 117b, etc.]]

__V
τί μαθών..; frequently in questions, literal under what persuasion, with what idea? hence ironically for why on earth? τί δὴ μ. φαίνεις ἄνευ θρυαλλίδο; [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Acharnenses” 826, compare “Nu.” 402, 1506, “Lys.” 599, “Pl.” 908]]; τί τοῦτο μ. προσέγραψε; [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 20.127]] (sometimes with variant{τί παθών}; what possessed you to.. ? compare πάσχω); imitated in later Greek, [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd-3rd c.AD: Aelianus “Fragmenta” 67]]; also indirectly, because (with a sense of disapprobation), ὅ τι μαθόντες τοὺς ξένους μὲν λέγετε ποιητὰς σοφούς [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Eupolis Comicus 357; ὅ τι μαθὼν.. οὐχ ἡσυχίαν ἦγον 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Apologia” 36b; σοὶ εἰς κεφαλήν, ὅ τι μαθών μου καὶ τῶν ἄλλων καταψεύδη τοιοῦτο πρᾶγμα [prev. author] “Euthd.” 283e, compare 299a]]: even with neuter subject, ὅμως δ᾽ ἂν κακὰ ἦν, ὅ τι μαθόντα χαίρειν ποιεῖ [Refs [[prev. author] “Prt.” 353d.]]

μάχαιρα, -ης
(Att.. -ας; see WH, App., 1568; ΒΙ., § 7, 1), ἡ, [in LXX chiefly for חֶרֶב; also for מַאֲכֶלֶת, etc. ;]

of sounds, great, loud, ἀλαλητός, ἰαχή, πάταγος, ὀρυμαγδός, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 12.138, 15.384, 21.9, 256]]; θόρυβοι, κωκυτός, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Ajax” 142 (_anapaest meter_), 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Medea” 1176; οὐκ ἔστι ὅκως τι νεῖκος ἔσται ἢ μέγα ἢ σμικρόν 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 3.62; μὴ φώνει μέγα 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Philoctetes” 574.]]

__A.II.4
generally, great, mighty, ὅρκος [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 19.113]]; ὄλβος, τιμά, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “O.” 1.56, “P.” 4.148]]; μ. λόγος, μῦθος, a great story, rumour, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Prometheus Vinctus” 732, 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Ajax” 226 (Lyric poetry)]]; ἐρώτημα a big, i. e. difficult, question, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Euthydemus” 275d, “Hp.Ma.” 287b]]; weighty, important, τόδε μεῖζον [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 16.291]]; μέγα ποιέεσθαί τι to esteem of great importance, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 3.42, compare 9.111; μέγα γενέσθαι εἴς τι 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Historia Graeca (Hellenica)” 7.5.6; μ. ὑπάρχειν πρός τι [prev. author] “Mem.” 2.3.4; μέγα διαφέρειν εἴς τι 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Leges” 78o c]]; οὐκ ἂν εἴη παρὰ μέγα τὸ δικολογεῖν not of great importance, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [1st c.BC: Philodemus Gadarensis Epigrammaticus “Rh.” 2.85 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus]]; τὸ δὲ μέγιστον and what is most important, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 4.70, compare 1.142]]; οἱ μέγιστοι καιροί the most pressing emergencies, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 20.44]]; μ. ὠνησάμενοι χρημάτων for large sums, [Refs 2nd c.BC+ [2nd c.BC: Polybius Historicus 4.50.3, etc.]]

__A.II.5
with a bad sense, over-great, μέγα εἰπεῖν to speak big, and so provoke divine wrath, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 22.288; λίην μέγα εἶπες 3.227, 16.243; μέγα ἔργον 3.261, 5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “N.” 10.64; ἔργων μ. 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Agamemnon” 1546 (_anapaest meter_); ὠμὸν τὸ βούλευμα καὶ μ. 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 3.36]]; ἔπος μ., μ. λόγοι, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Ajax” 423 (Lyric poetry), “Ant.” 1350 (_anapaest meter_); μ. γλῶσσα [prev. work] 127 (_anapaest meter_)]]; μηδὲν μέγ᾽ εἴπῃς [Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. author] “Aj.” 386; μὴ μέγα λέγε 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Phaedo” 95b; μὴ μεγάλα λίαν λέγε 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Ranae” 835; μέγα φρονεῖν 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Tyrannus” 1078, 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Hippolytus” 6; μεγάλα φρονεῖν 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Acharnenses” 988]]; μεγάλα, μεῖζον ἢ δικαίως πνεῖν, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Andromache” 189, 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Agamemnon” 376 (Lyric poetry); μέγα τι παθεῖν 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 5.8.17; μὴ μέγα λέγων μεῖζον πάθῃς 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Hercules Furens” 1244.]]

__A.II.6
of style. impressive, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demetrius Phalereus Rhetor “Demetrius on Style” 278]]; μεῖζον more striking, [Refs [[prev. work] 103.]]

__A.II.7
of days, long, [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd c.AD: Galenus Medicus 12.714.]]

__B
adverb μεγάλως [ᾰ] greatly, mightily, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 16.432, 8th-7th c.BC: Hesiodus Epicus “Theogonia” 429, 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.16, 30, +others, 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 8.2.10, 1st c.BC: Parthenius Mythographus 28.1, etc.; strengthened, μάλα μ. 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 17.723; δμαθέντες μ. 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Persae” 907 (Lyric poetry); with _adjectives_, 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.4, 7.190.]]

__B.II
more frequently neuter singular μέγα as adverb, very much, exceedingly, μ. χαῖρε all hail!, see l. for μάλα in [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 24.402]]; especially with Verbs expressing strong feeling, μ. κεν κεχαροίατο [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 1.256; μ. κήδεται 2.27, etc.: with Verbs expressing power, might, μ. πάντων.. κρατέει 1.78; ὃς μ. πάντων.. ἤνασσε 10.32; πατρὸς μ. δυναμένοιο 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 1.276, compare 8th c.BC: Homerus Epicus “Epigrammata” 15.1, 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Eumenides” 950 (_anapaest meter_), 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Helena” 1358 (Lyric poetry), 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Ranae” 141, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 366a; μ. δύνασθαι παρά τινι 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 2.29; πλουτέειν μ. 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.32]]; or those expressing sound, loudly, μ. ἰάχειν, ἀῧσαι, βοῆσαι, εὔξασθαι, ἀμβῶσαι, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 2.333, 14.147, 17.334, 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 17.239, 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.8 (also _plural_, μεγάλ᾽ εὔχετο 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 1.450]]; μ. αὐδήσαντος, μ. ἤπυεν, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 4.505, 9.399): strengthened, μάλα μ. 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 15.321; μ. δ᾽ ἔβραχε φήγινος ἄξων 5.838, etc.: so in Trag. with all kinds of Verbs, μ. στένειν, σθένειν, χλίειν, 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Agamemnon” 711 (Lyric poetry), 938, “Ch.” 137]]: also in plural, μεγάλα.. δυστυχεῖς [Refs [[prev. author] “Eu.” 791 (Lyric poetry).]]

__B.II.2
of Space, far, μέγα προθορών [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 14.363]]; ἄνευθε μέγα far away,[Refs 5th c.BC+ [22.88; οὐκ ἂν μέγα τι τῆς ἀληθείας παρεξέλθοις 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Philebus” 66b.]]

__B.II.3
with adjectives, as μέγ᾽ ἔξοχος, μέγα νήπιος, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 2.480, 16.46]]; μ. νήπιε Oracle texts cited in [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.85; μ. πλούσιος [prev. author] 1.32, 7.190; ὦ μέγ᾽ εὔδαιμον κόρη 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Prometheus Vinctus” 647]]: with comparative and superlative, by far, μέγ᾽ ἀμείνονες, ἄριστος, φέρτατος, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 4.405, 2.82, 16.21.]]

__C
degrees of Comparison (regular μεγαλώτερος, -ώτατος late, [Refs [“Etymologicum Magnum” 780.1, 2):]]

__C.1
comparative μείζων, ον, genitive ονος, Epic dialect, Attic dialect (also Delph., [Refs 4th c.BC+ [“SIG” 246 H 260 (4th c.BC))]]; Ionic dialect, [Refs 4th c.AD+ [4th c.AD(?): Arcadius Grammaticus]], Doric dialect, Aeolic dialect μέζων, ον, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [1st c.AD(?): Heraclitus 25, 5th c.BC: Hippocrates Medicus “περὶ διαίτης ὀξέων” 44, 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.26, “IG” 7.235.16 (from Oropus), 5(2).3.18 (from Tegea), 5th c.BC: Epicharmus Comicus 62]] (also early Attic dialect, [Refs [“IG” 12.22.65, but [με] ίζων [prev. work]6.93, by analogy of ὀλείζων [prev. work]76,95)]]; dative plural μεζόνεσσι [Refs 7th c.BC+ [Diotogenes Philosophus cited in 5th c.AD: Stobaeus, Joannes 4.7.62: written μέσδων in 7th-6th c.BC: Sappho Lyrica “Papyrus fragments” in E. Diehl, 7.6, 1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus “Lycurgus” 19]]: compare μέττον· μεῖζον, [NT+5th c.AD+ [5th c.AD(?): Hesychius Legal icographus (uncertain); later μειζότερος NT.3JOhn.4]] (used as title, elder, [Refs 6th c.AD+ [POxy. 943.3 (6th c.AD), etc.)]]; μειζονώτερος [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Fragmenta - American Journal of Philology” 434]]:—greater, longer, taller, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 3.168, 9.202, etc.]]; frequently also, too great, γέρας [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Sophista” 231a]]; Μηνόφιλος μείζων M. the elder, [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [Ostr.Bodl. see C 2 (2nd c.AD)]]; as title, μειζων κώμης headman of a village, [Refs 4th c.AD+ [“POxy.” 1626.5 (4th c.AD)]], etc.: generally, the higher authority, [Refs 3rd c.AD+ [PLond. 2.214.22 (3rd c.AD), “POxy.” 1204.17 (_plural_, 3rd c.AD)]]; οὔτε μεῖζον οὔτε ἔλαττον, a strong form of denial, nothing whatever, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [1st c.BC: Dionysius Halicarnassensis “de Compositione Verborum” 4; οὐδαμὰ προὔφηνεν οὔτε μείζον᾽ οὔτ᾽ ἐλάττονα 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Trachiniae” 324]]. adverb μειζόνως [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Hecuba” 1121, 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 1.130, 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Cynegeticus” 13.3, 5th-6th c.BC: Isocrates Orator 9.21, etc.]]; Ionic dialect μεζόνως [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 3.128, 3rd c.BC: Herodas Mimographus 4.80, etc.]]: neuter as adverb, μεῖζον σθένειν [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Philoctetes” 456, 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Supplices” 216; μ. ἰσχύειν 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator “Epistulae” 3.28; ἐπὶ μ. ἔρχεται 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Philoctetes” 259.]]

__C.2
superlative μέγιστος, η, ον, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 2.412, etc.]]: neuter as adverb, μέγιστον ἴσχυσε [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Ajax” 502]]; δυνάμενος μ., with genitive, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 7.5, 9.9]]: with another superlative, μέγιστον ἐχθίστη [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Medea” 1323: in _plural_, χαῖρ᾽ ὡς μέγιστα 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Philoctetes” 462; θάλλει μ. [prev. author] “OC” 700 (Lyric poetry); τὰ μέγιστ᾽ ἐτιμάθης [prev. author] “OT” 1203 (Lyric poetry)]]; ἐς μέγιστον[Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. work] 521; ἐς τὰ μ. 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 8.111]]:—late superlative μεγιστότατος [Refs 1st c.AD+ [“PLond.” 1.130.49 (1st-2nd c.AD)]]. (Cf. Sanskrit majmán- 'greatness', Latin magnus, Gothic mikils 'great'.)
