Abbott-Smith / STEPBible (TBESG)
μέγας, μεγάλη, μέγα,
[in LXX chiefly for גָּדוֹל, also for מַרְבֶּה ,רַב (incl. μείζων), רֹב (μέγιστος) ;]
great;
__1. of external form, bodily size, measure, extent: λίθος, Mat.2:60; δράκων, Rev.12:3; ἰχθῦς, Jhn.21:11; πόλις, Rev.11:8; μάχαιρα, Rev.6:4, al.
__2. Of intensity and degree: δύναμις, Act.4:33; φόβος, Mrk.4:41; ἀγάπη, Jhn.15:13; ἄνεμος, 'ib. 6:18; κραυγή, Act.23:9; φῶς, Mat.4:16; πυρετός, Luk.4:38; θλίψις, Mat.24:21.
__3. Of rank;
__(a) of persons: θεός (MM, xvi), Tit.2:13; Ἄρτεμις, Act.19:27; compar. (see infr.), Mat.18:1 (cf. Dalman, Words, 113f.); neut. for masc. (Bl., §32, 1), Mat.12:6;
__(b) of things: ἁμαρτία, Jhn.19:11; μυστήριον, Eph.5:32; = μεγίστη (see infr., and cf. Field, Notes, 16f.), Mat.22:36; compar. for superl. (M, Pr., 78), 1Co.13:13.
__4.
__(a) Compar., μείζων: Mat.11:11 23:17, al.; neut. pl., μείζονα, contr. μείζω, Jhn.1:51; double compar., μειζότερος (M, Pr., 236; Bl., §11, 4), III Jo 4;
__(b) superl, μέγιστος (Deiss., BS, 365), 2Pe.1:4.
(AS)

LSJ / STEPBible (TFLSJ)
μέγᾰς, μεγάλη [ᾰ], μέγα [ᾰ],
genitive μεγάλου, ης, ου, dative μεγάλῳ, ῃ, ῳ, accusative μέγᾰν, μεγάλην, μέγα [ᾰ]; dual μεγάλω, α, w; plural μεγάλοι, μεγάλαι, μεγάλα, etc.: the stem μεγάλο- is never used in singular nominative and accusative masculine and neuter, and only once in vocative masculine,

__A
ὦ μεγάλε Ζεῦ [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Septem contra Thebas” 822 (_anapaest meter_).]]

__A.I
big, of bodily size: frequently of stature, εἶδος.. μ. ἦν ὁράασθαι [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 18.4; κεῖτο μ. μεγαλωστί 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 16.776; ἠΰς τε μ. τε 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 9. 508]]; φῶτα μέγαν καὶ καλόν[Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. work] 513; καλή τε μεγάλη τε 15.418; κάρτα μεγάλη καὶ εὐειδής 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 3.1]]; φύσιν τίν᾽ εἶχε φράζ; Answ. μέγας [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Tyrannus” 742.]]

__A.I.b
full-grown, of age as shown by stature, νῦν δ᾽ ὅτε δὴ μ. εἰμί [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 2.314; μήτε μέγαν μήτ᾽ οὖν νεαρῶν τινα 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Agamemnon” 358 (_anapaest meter_)]]; later, elder of two persons of the same name, Wilcken [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [“Chr.” 305 (3rd c.BC)]]; Σκιπίων ὁ μ. [Refs 2nd c.BC+ [2nd c.BC: Polybius Historicus 18.35.9.]]

__A.I.c
of animals, μ. ἵπποι, βοῦς, σῦς, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 2.839, 18.559, 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 19.439; αἰετός 5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “I.” 6(5).50.]]

__A.I.2
generally, vast, high, οὐρανός, ὄρος, πύργος, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 1.497, 16.297, 6.386]]; wide, πέλαγος, λαῖτμα θαλάσσης, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 3.179, 5.174]]; long, ἠϊών, αἰγιαλός, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 12.31, 2.210: sometimes opposed to ὀλίγος, κῦμα οὔτε μέγ᾽ οὔτ᾽ ὀ. 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 10.94]]; but usually opposed to μικρός or σμικρός, πρὸς ἑαυτὸ ἕκαστον καὶ μ. καὶ σμικρόν [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Anaxagoras Philosophus 3; τὸ ἄπειρον ἐκ μεγάλου καὶ μικροῦ 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Metaphysica” 987b26, etc.]]

__A.II
of quality or degree, great, mighty, frequently epithet of gods, ὁ μ. Ζεύς [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Supplices” 1052 (Lyric poetry), etc.]]; μεγάλα θεά, of Demeter and Persephone, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Coloneus” 683 (Lyric poetry)]]; θεοὶ μεγάλοι, of the Cabiri, [Refs [“IG” 12(8).71 (from Imbros), etc.]]; Μήτηρ μ., of Cybele, [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [“SIG” 1014.83 (Erythrae, 3rd c.BC), 1138.3 (Delos, 2nd c.BC)]]; Μήτηρ θεῶν μ. [Refs [“OGI” 540.6 (from Pessinus), etc.]]; Ἴσιδος μ. μητρὸς θεῶν [Refs 2nd c.BC+ [“PStrassb.” 81.14 (2nd c.BC)]]; μ. ἡ Ἄρτεμις Ἐφεσίων [NT.Act.19.28]; τίς θεὸς μ. ὡς ὁ θεὸς ἡμῶ; [LXX+NT [LXX.Psa.76(77).13; ὁ μ. θεός NT.Tit.2.13]]; of men, μ. ἠδὲ κραταιός [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 18.382; ὀλίγος καὶ μ. 7th c.BC: Callinus Epicus 1.17, etc.]]; μέγας ηὐξήθη rose to greatness, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 2.5; ἤρθη μ. [prev. work]8; βασιλεὺς ὁ μ.]], i. e. the King of Persia, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.188, etc. (θεῶν β. ὁ μ., of Zeus, 5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “O.” 7.34); βασιλεὺς μ. 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Persae” 24 (_anapaest meter_)]]; as a title of special monarchs, Ἀρδιαῖος ὁ μ. [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 615c; ὁ μ. Ἀλέξανδρος 2nd c.AD: Athenaeus Epigrammaticus 1.3d; ὁ μ. ἐπικληθεὶς Ἀντίοχος 2nd c.BC: Polybius Historicus 4.2.7, etc.; μ. φίλος 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Medea” 549; πλούτῳ τε κἀνδρείᾳ μ. [prev. author] “Tr.” 674; ἐπὶ μέγα ἦλθεν ἰσχύος 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 2.97.]]

__A.II.2
strong, of the elements, etc., ἄνεμος, λαῖλαψ, Ζέφυρος, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 19.200, 12.408, 14.458]]; of properties, passions, qualities, feelings, etc., of men, θάρσος, πένθος, ποθή, etc.,[NT+8th c.BC+ [9.381, 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 1.254, 11.471, etc.; ἀρετή 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 24.193, 5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “O.” 8.5; θυμός 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 9.496, 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Orestes” 702; κλέος 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 6.446; ἄχος 9.9; πυρετός NT.Luke.4.38 (incorrect _accusative_ to 2nd c.AD: Galenus Medicus 7.275)]]; ἡ μ. νοῦσος epilepsy, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Hippocrates Medicus “ἐπιδημίαι” 6.6.5, compare 2nd c.AD: Galenus Medicus 17(2).341.]]

__A.II.3
of sounds, great, loud, ἀλαλητός, ἰαχή, πάταγος, ὀρυμαγδός, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 12.138, 15.384, 21.9, 256]]; θόρυβοι, κωκυτός, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Ajax” 142 (_anapaest meter_), 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Medea” 1176; οὐκ ἔστι ὅκως τι νεῖκος ἔσται ἢ μέγα ἢ σμικρόν 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 3.62; μὴ φώνει μέγα 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Philoctetes” 574.]]

__A.II.4
generally, great, mighty, ὅρκος [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 19.113]]; ὄλβος, τιμά, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “O.” 1.56, “P.” 4.148]]; μ. λόγος, μῦθος, a great story, rumour, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Prometheus Vinctus” 732, 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Ajax” 226 (Lyric poetry)]]; ἐρώτημα a big, i. e. difficult, question, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Euthydemus” 275d, “Hp.Ma.” 287b]]; weighty, important, τόδε μεῖζον [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 16.291]]; μέγα ποιέεσθαί τι to esteem of great importance, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 3.42, compare 9.111; μέγα γενέσθαι εἴς τι 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Historia Graeca (Hellenica)” 7.5.6; μ. ὑπάρχειν πρός τι [prev. author] “Mem.” 2.3.4; μέγα διαφέρειν εἴς τι 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Leges” 78o c]]; οὐκ ἂν εἴη παρὰ μέγα τὸ δικολογεῖν not of great importance, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [1st c.BC: Philodemus Gadarensis Epigrammaticus “Rh.” 2.85 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus]]; τὸ δὲ μέγιστον and what is most important, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 4.70, compare 1.142]]; οἱ μέγιστοι καιροί the most pressing emergencies, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 20.44]]; μ. ὠνησάμενοι χρημάτων for large sums, [Refs 2nd c.BC+ [2nd c.BC: Polybius Historicus 4.50.3, etc.]]

__A.II.5
with a bad sense, over-great, μέγα εἰπεῖν to speak big, and so provoke divine wrath, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 22.288; λίην μέγα εἶπες 3.227, 16.243; μέγα ἔργον 3.261, 5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “N.” 10.64; ἔργων μ. 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Agamemnon” 1546 (_anapaest meter_); ὠμὸν τὸ βούλευμα καὶ μ. 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 3.36]]; ἔπος μ., μ. λόγοι, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Ajax” 423 (Lyric poetry), “Ant.” 1350 (_anapaest meter_); μ. γλῶσσα [prev. work] 127 (_anapaest meter_)]]; μηδὲν μέγ᾽ εἴπῃς [Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. author] “Aj.” 386; μὴ μέγα λέγε 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Phaedo” 95b; μὴ μεγάλα λίαν λέγε 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Ranae” 835; μέγα φρονεῖν 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Tyrannus” 1078, 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Hippolytus” 6; μεγάλα φρονεῖν 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Acharnenses” 988]]; μεγάλα, μεῖζον ἢ δικαίως πνεῖν, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Andromache” 189, 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Agamemnon” 376 (Lyric poetry); μέγα τι παθεῖν 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 5.8.17; μὴ μέγα λέγων μεῖζον πάθῃς 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Hercules Furens” 1244.]]

__A.II.6
of style. impressive, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demetrius Phalereus Rhetor “Demetrius on Style” 278]]; μεῖζον more striking, [Refs [[prev. work] 103.]]

__A.II.7
of days, long, [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd c.AD: Galenus Medicus 12.714.]]

__B
adverb μεγάλως [ᾰ] greatly, mightily, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 16.432, 8th-7th c.BC: Hesiodus Epicus “Theogonia” 429, 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.16, 30, +others, 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 8.2.10, 1st c.BC: Parthenius Mythographus 28.1, etc.; strengthened, μάλα μ. 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 17.723; δμαθέντες μ. 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Persae” 907 (Lyric poetry); with _adjectives_, 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.4, 7.190.]]

__B.II
more frequently neuter singular μέγα as adverb, very much, exceedingly, μ. χαῖρε all hail!, see l. for μάλα in [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 24.402]]; especially with Verbs expressing strong feeling, μ. κεν κεχαροίατο [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 1.256; μ. κήδεται 2.27, etc.: with Verbs expressing power, might, μ. πάντων.. κρατέει 1.78; ὃς μ. πάντων.. ἤνασσε 10.32; πατρὸς μ. δυναμένοιο 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 1.276, compare 8th c.BC: Homerus Epicus “Epigrammata” 15.1, 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Eumenides” 950 (_anapaest meter_), 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Helena” 1358 (Lyric poetry), 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Ranae” 141, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 366a; μ. δύνασθαι παρά τινι 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 2.29; πλουτέειν μ. 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.32]]; or those expressing sound, loudly, μ. ἰάχειν, ἀῧσαι, βοῆσαι, εὔξασθαι, ἀμβῶσαι, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 2.333, 14.147, 17.334, 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 17.239, 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.8 (also _plural_, μεγάλ᾽ εὔχετο 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 1.450]]; μ. αὐδήσαντος, μ. ἤπυεν, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 4.505, 9.399): strengthened, μάλα μ. 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 15.321; μ. δ᾽ ἔβραχε φήγινος ἄξων 5.838, etc.: so in Trag. with all kinds of Verbs, μ. στένειν, σθένειν, χλίειν, 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Agamemnon” 711 (Lyric poetry), 938, “Ch.” 137]]: also in plural, μεγάλα.. δυστυχεῖς [Refs [[prev. author] “Eu.” 791 (Lyric poetry).]]

__B.II.2
of Space, far, μέγα προθορών [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 14.363]]; ἄνευθε μέγα far away,[Refs 5th c.BC+ [22.88; οὐκ ἂν μέγα τι τῆς ἀληθείας παρεξέλθοις 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Philebus” 66b.]]

__B.II.3
with adjectives, as μέγ᾽ ἔξοχος, μέγα νήπιος, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 2.480, 16.46]]; μ. νήπιε Oracle texts cited in [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.85; μ. πλούσιος [prev. author] 1.32, 7.190; ὦ μέγ᾽ εὔδαιμον κόρη 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Prometheus Vinctus” 647]]: with comparative and superlative, by far, μέγ᾽ ἀμείνονες, ἄριστος, φέρτατος, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 4.405, 2.82, 16.21.]]

__C
degrees of Comparison (regular μεγαλώτερος, -ώτατος late, [Refs [“Etymologicum Magnum” 780.1, 2):]]

__C.1
comparative μείζων, ον, genitive ονος, Epic dialect, Attic dialect (also Delph., [Refs 4th c.BC+ [“SIG” 246 H 260 (4th c.BC))]]; Ionic dialect, [Refs 4th c.AD+ [4th c.AD(?): Arcadius Grammaticus]], Doric dialect, Aeolic dialect μέζων, ον, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [1st c.AD(?): Heraclitus 25, 5th c.BC: Hippocrates Medicus “περὶ διαίτης ὀξέων” 44, 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.26, “IG” 7.235.16 (from Oropus), 5(2).3.18 (from Tegea), 5th c.BC: Epicharmus Comicus 62]] (also early Attic dialect, [Refs [“IG” 12.22.65, but [με] ίζων [prev. work]6.93, by analogy of ὀλείζων [prev. work]76,95)]]; dative plural μεζόνεσσι [Refs 7th c.BC+ [Diotogenes Philosophus cited in 5th c.AD: Stobaeus, Joannes 4.7.62: written μέσδων in 7th-6th c.BC: Sappho Lyrica “Papyrus fragments” in E. Diehl, 7.6, 1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus “Lycurgus” 19]]: compare μέττον· μεῖζον, [NT+5th c.AD+ [5th c.AD(?): Hesychius Legal icographus (uncertain); later μειζότερος NT.3JOhn.4]] (used as title, elder, [Refs 6th c.AD+ [POxy. 943.3 (6th c.AD), etc.)]]; μειζονώτερος [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Fragmenta - American Journal of Philology” 434]]:—greater, longer, taller, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 3.168, 9.202, etc.]]; frequently also, too great, γέρας [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Sophista” 231a]]; Μηνόφιλος μείζων M. the elder, [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [Ostr.Bodl. see C 2 (2nd c.AD)]]; as title, μειζων κώμης headman of a village, [Refs 4th c.AD+ [“POxy.” 1626.5 (4th c.AD)]], etc.: generally, the higher authority, [Refs 3rd c.AD+ [PLond. 2.214.22 (3rd c.AD), “POxy.” 1204.17 (_plural_, 3rd c.AD)]]; οὔτε μεῖζον οὔτε ἔλαττον, a strong form of denial, nothing whatever, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [1st c.BC: Dionysius Halicarnassensis “de Compositione Verborum” 4; οὐδαμὰ προὔφηνεν οὔτε μείζον᾽ οὔτ᾽ ἐλάττονα 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Trachiniae” 324]]. adverb μειζόνως [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Hecuba” 1121, 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 1.130, 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Cynegeticus” 13.3, 5th-6th c.BC: Isocrates Orator 9.21, etc.]]; Ionic dialect μεζόνως [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 3.128, 3rd c.BC: Herodas Mimographus 4.80, etc.]]: neuter as adverb, μεῖζον σθένειν [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Philoctetes” 456, 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Supplices” 216; μ. ἰσχύειν 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator “Epistulae” 3.28; ἐπὶ μ. ἔρχεται 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Philoctetes” 259.]]

__C.2
superlative μέγιστος, η, ον, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 2.412, etc.]]: neuter as adverb, μέγιστον ἴσχυσε [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Ajax” 502]]; δυνάμενος μ., with genitive, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 7.5, 9.9]]: with another superlative, μέγιστον ἐχθίστη [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Medea” 1323: in _plural_, χαῖρ᾽ ὡς μέγιστα 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Philoctetes” 462; θάλλει μ. [prev. author] “OC” 700 (Lyric poetry); τὰ μέγιστ᾽ ἐτιμάθης [prev. author] “OT” 1203 (Lyric poetry)]]; ἐς μέγιστον[Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. work] 521; ἐς τὰ μ. 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 8.111]]:—late superlative μεγιστότατος [Refs 1st c.AD+ [“PLond.” 1.130.49 (1st-2nd c.AD)]]. (Cf. Sanskrit majmán- 'greatness', Latin magnus, Gothic mikils 'great'.)

LSJ / STEPBible (TFLSJ)
μέγεθος,
Ionic dialect (not [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Hippocrates Medicus)]] μέγᾰθος [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus (see. below), also 3rd c.BC: Philoxenus Epigrammaticus 2.19]], εος, τό: (μέγας):— greatness, magnitude, opposed to πλῆθος, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Anaxagoras Philosophus 1, etc.; πλῆθος μὲν.. ἐὰν ἀριθμητὸν ᾖ, μ. δὲ ἐὰν μετρητὸν ᾖ 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Metaphysica” 1020a9.]]

__I
in [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Homerus Epicus]] always stature, of men and women, εἶδος ἀκιδνοτέρη μέγεθός τ᾽ εἰσάντα ἰδέσθαι [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 5.217, compare 6.152; ἐς μ. καὶ κάλλος ὁρώμενος 18.219, compare 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Charmides” 154c; θηλειῶν ἀρετὴ σώματος κάλλος καὶ μ. 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Rhetorica” 1361a7]]: then, generally, size, μύρμηκες μεγάθεα ἔχοντες κυνῶν ἐλάσσονα [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 3.102; μ. λαβεῖν 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 1.4.3; ἡ ἐπίδοσις εἰς τὸ μ. 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Historia Animalium” 560a20]]; of sound, loudness, βοῆς μ. [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 4.126: _accusative_ as]] adverb, λίθου λάμποντος μέγαθος, ={μεγάλως}, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 2.44]]; but usually, in size, τεῖχος κατὰ τὸν Ἀθηνέων κύκλον.. τὸ μ. [Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. author] 1.98; [δένδρεον] μέγαθος κατὰ συκέην μάλιστά κῃ [prev. author] 4.23; ὅσην δεῖ τὸ μ. τὴν πόλιν ποιεῖσθαι 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 423b]]: also in plural, ποταμοὶ οὐ κατὰ τὸν Νεῖλον ἐόντες μεγάθεα [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 2.10, compare 1.202; σμικροὶ τὰ μεγάθεα [prev. author] 3.107; κυαμιαῖοι τὰ μ. 2nd c.AD: Lucianus Sophista “Herm.” 40; μεγέθη ἔργων καὶ διαθέσεων 4th-3rd c.BC: Epicurus Philosophus “De rerum natura - Wien. Stud.” 43 G.]]

__I.2
frequently in dative, μεγέθει.. ἐκπρεπεστάτη in stature, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Persae” 184; ἀνθρώπους μεγέθει μεγίστους καὶ ἥκιστα διαφόρους ἐς.. τὰ μεγέθεα 5th c.BC: Hippocrates Medicus “Aër.” 12; πλήθεϊ μέγιστον καὶ μεγάθεϊ ὑψηλότατον, of a mountain, 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.203]]; κρητῆρες μεγάθεϊ μεγάλοι[Refs [[prev. work] 51; μεγάθεϊ μέγιστος [prev. author] 7.117; μ. περιμήκεας [prev. author] 2.108]]; σμικρός[Refs 4th c.BC+ [[prev. work] 74; ἐλάττω τῷ μ. 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Historia Animalium” 560b5.]]

__II
of quality and degree, greatness, magnitude, πόνων [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Helena” 593; τῆς παρανομίας 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 6.15; τῆς ζημίας 5th c.BC: Lysias Orator 1.3; τῆς κολάσεως 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Leges” 934b]]; importance, μ. ἐχούσας πράξεις [Refs 1st c.BC+ [1st c.BC: Dionysius Halicarnassensis “de Isocrate” 6.]]

__II.2
might, power, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Bacchae” 273; δαίμονος μεγέθει πάντα ἐπέχοντος 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Symposium” 8.1.]]

__II.3
greatness, magnanimity, [Refs 1st c.AD+ [1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus “Alexander” 14; περί τι [prev. author] “Ant.” 24.]]

__II.4
Rhet., loftiness, sublimity, μ. περιτιθέναι τοῖς πράγμασιν [Refs 4th c.BC+ [1st c.BC: Dionysius Halicarnassensis “de Compositione Verborum” 17, compare 4th c.BC: Demetrius Phalereus Rhetor “Demetrius on Style” 5, 2nd c.AD: Hermogenes Rhetor “περὶ ἰδεῶν” 1.5, etc.; λόγων μ. 3rd c.AD: Longinus Rhetor 4.1, +others]]: in plural, sublime objects, [Refs [[prev. author] 9.1, +others]]

__III
in Mathematics texts, magnitude, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Gorgias Rhetor et Sophista 3; μ. ἔχειν 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Timaeus” 57d, compare 4th c.AD: Iamblichus Philosophus “de communi mathematica scientia” 3, etc.]]; extension, [Refs 3rd c.AD+ [3rd c.AD: Plotinus Philosophus 2.4.11]]: in plural, magnitudes, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Protagoras” 356c; τὰ μ. τὰ γεγραμμένα “IG” 7.3073.102 (Lebad.).]]

__III.2
Astron., magnitude, of stars, [Refs 1st c.BC+ [2nd c.AD: Cleomedes Astronomus 1.11, 1st c.BC: Ptolemaeus Epigrammaticus “Alm.” 7 passim.]]

__IV
Grammars, metrical length, τὸ μέγιστον μ. τρίχρονον [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd c.AD: Apollonius Dyscolus Grammaticus “de Syntaxi;” 133.26, compare “Etymologicum Magnum” 419.50.]]

__IV.2
τὰ ἐν τῷ μέτρῳ μ. the recognized lengths of lines in a metre, [Refs 7th c.AD+ [7th c.AD: Hephaestio Grammaticus 12.3.]]

__V
τὸ μ. τινός, as title, his Highness, [Refs 3rd c.AD+ [POxy. 2107.8 (3rd c.AD)]]; τὸ σὸν μ. [Refs [“Codex Justinianus [4th-6th c.AD]” 8.10.12.1a.]]

Abbott-Smith / STEPBible (TBESG)
μέγιστος, see: μέγας.
μέγας, μεγάλη, μέγα,
[in LXX chiefly for גָּדוֹל, also for מַרְבֶּה ,רַב (incl. μείζων), רֹב (μέγιστος) ;]
great;
__1. of external form, bodily size, measure, extent: λίθος, Mat.2:60; δράκων, Rev.12:3; ἰχθῦς, Jhn.21:11; πόλις, Rev.11:8; μάχαιρα, Rev.6:4, al.
__2. Of intensity and degree: δύναμις, Act.4:33; φόβος, Mrk.4:41; ἀγάπη, Jhn.15:13; ἄνεμος, ib. 6:18; κραυγή, Act.23:9; φῶς, Mat.4:16; πυρετός, Luk.4:38; θλίψις, Mat.24:21.
__3. Of rank;
__(a) of persons: θεός (MM, xvi), Tit.2:13; Ἄρτεμις, Act.19:27; compar. (see infr.), Mat.18:1 (cf. Dalman, Words, 113f.); neut. for masc. (Bl., §32, 1), Mat.12:6;

of things, to be drenched, steeped in any liquid, with dative, e.g. βοείην.. μεθύουσαν ἀλοιφῇ [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 17.390; μεθύων ἐλαίῳ λύχνος 2nd c.AD: Babrius Fabularum Scriptor 114.1; [χείμαρρος] ὄμβροισι μ. “Anthologia Graeca” 9.277 (1st c.AD: Antiphilus Epigrammaticus).]]

__II.2
of persons, to be intoxicated with passion, pride, etc., ὑπὸ τῆς Ἀφροδίτης [Refs 6th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Symposium” 8.21; ὑπὸ τρυφῆς 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Critias” 121a; ἔρωτι 6th c.BC: Anacreon Lyricus 19; τῷ μεγέθει τῶν πεπραγμένων 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 4.49; περὶ τὰς ἡδονάς 2nd-3rd c.AD: Philostratus Sophista “Vitae Sophistarum” 1.22.1; οὐ μ. τὴν φρόνησιν 2nd c.AD: Alexander Rhetor 301; μ. τὸ φίλημα “Anthologia Graeca” 5.304.]]

__II.2.b
to be stupefied, stunned, πληγαῖς μεθύων [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [3rd c.BC: Theocritus Poeta Bucolicus 22.98; ἐξ ὀδυνάων 2nd-3rd c.AD: Oppianus Anazarbensis Epicus “Halieutica - Poetae Bucolici et Didactici” 5.228, cf. Nonn.[same place]]]

LSJ / STEPBible (TFLSJ)
μέγᾰς, μεγάλη [ᾰ], μέγα [ᾰ],
genitive μεγάλου, ης, ου, dative μεγάλῳ, ῃ, ῳ, accusative μέγᾰν, μεγάλην, μέγα [ᾰ]; dual μεγάλω, α, w; plural μεγάλοι, μεγάλαι, μεγάλα, etc.: the stem μεγάλο- is never used in singular nominative and accusative masculine and neuter, and only once in vocative masculine,

__A
ὦ μεγάλε Ζεῦ [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Septem contra Thebas” 822 (_anapaest meter_).]]

__A.I
big, of bodily size: frequently of stature, εἶδος.. μ. ἦν ὁράασθαι [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 18.4; κεῖτο μ. μεγαλωστί 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 16.776; ἠΰς τε μ. τε 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 9. 508]]; φῶτα μέγαν καὶ καλόν[Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. work] 513; καλή τε μεγάλη τε 15.418; κάρτα μεγάλη καὶ εὐειδής 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 3.1]]; φύσιν τίν᾽ εἶχε φράζ; Answ. μέγας [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Tyrannus” 742.]]

__A.I.b
full-grown, of age as shown by stature, νῦν δ᾽ ὅτε δὴ μ. εἰμί [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 2.314; μήτε μέγαν μήτ᾽ οὖν νεαρῶν τινα 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Agamemnon” 358 (_anapaest meter_)]]; later, elder of two persons of the same name, Wilcken [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [“Chr.” 305 (3rd c.BC)]]; Σκιπίων ὁ μ. [Refs 2nd c.BC+ [2nd c.BC: Polybius Historicus 18.35.9.]]

__A.I.c
of animals, μ. ἵπποι, βοῦς, σῦς, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 2.839, 18.559, 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 19.439; αἰετός 5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “I.” 6(5).50.]]

__A.I.2
generally, vast, high, οὐρανός, ὄρος, πύργος, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 1.497, 16.297, 6.386]]; wide, πέλαγος, λαῖτμα θαλάσσης, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 3.179, 5.174]]; long, ἠϊών, αἰγιαλός, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 12.31, 2.210: sometimes opposed to ὀλίγος, κῦμα οὔτε μέγ᾽ οὔτ᾽ ὀ. 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 10.94]]; but usually opposed to μικρός or σμικρός, πρὸς ἑαυτὸ ἕκαστον καὶ μ. καὶ σμικρόν [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Anaxagoras Philosophus 3; τὸ ἄπειρον ἐκ μεγάλου καὶ μικροῦ 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Metaphysica” 987b26, etc.]]

__A.II
of quality or degree, great, mighty, frequently epithet of gods, ὁ μ. Ζεύς [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Supplices” 1052 (Lyric poetry), etc.]]; μεγάλα θεά, of Demeter and Persephone, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Coloneus” 683 (Lyric poetry)]]; θεοὶ μεγάλοι, of the Cabiri, [Refs [“IG” 12(8).71 (from Imbros), etc.]]; Μήτηρ μ., of Cybele, [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [“SIG” 1014.83 (Erythrae, 3rd c.BC), 1138.3 (Delos, 2nd c.BC)]]; Μήτηρ θεῶν μ. [Refs [“OGI” 540.6 (from Pessinus), etc.]]; Ἴσιδος μ. μητρὸς θεῶν [Refs 2nd c.BC+ [“PStrassb.” 81.14 (2nd c.BC)]]; μ. ἡ Ἄρτεμις Ἐφεσίων [NT.Act.19.28]; τίς θεὸς μ. ὡς ὁ θεὸς ἡμῶ; [LXX+NT [LXX.Psa.76(77).13; ὁ μ. θεός NT.Tit.2.13]]; of men, μ. ἠδὲ κραταιός [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 18.382; ὀλίγος καὶ μ. 7th c.BC: Callinus Epicus 1.17, etc.]]; μέγας ηὐξήθη rose to greatness, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 2.5; ἤρθη μ. [prev. work]8; βασιλεὺς ὁ μ.]], i. e. the King of Persia, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.188, etc. (θεῶν β. ὁ μ., of Zeus, 5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “O.” 7.34); βασιλεὺς μ. 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Persae” 24 (_anapaest meter_)]]; as a title of special monarchs, Ἀρδιαῖος ὁ μ. [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 615c; ὁ μ. Ἀλέξανδρος 2nd c.AD: Athenaeus Epigrammaticus 1.3d; ὁ μ. ἐπικληθεὶς Ἀντίοχος 2nd c.BC: Polybius Historicus 4.2.7, etc.; μ. φίλος 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Medea” 549; πλούτῳ τε κἀνδρείᾳ μ. [prev. author] “Tr.” 674; ἐπὶ μέγα ἦλθεν ἰσχύος 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 2.97.]]

__A.II.2
strong, of the elements, etc., ἄνεμος, λαῖλαψ, Ζέφυρος, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 19.200, 12.408, 14.458]]; of properties, passions, qualities, feelings, etc., of men, θάρσος, πένθος, ποθή, etc.,[NT+8th c.BC+ [9.381, 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 1.254, 11.471, etc.; ἀρετή 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 24.193, 5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “O.” 8.5; θυμός 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 9.496, 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Orestes” 702; κλέος 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 6.446; ἄχος 9.9; πυρετός NT.Luke.4.38 (incorrect _accusative_ to 2nd c.AD: Galenus Medicus 7.275)]]; ἡ μ. νοῦσος epilepsy, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Hippocrates Medicus “ἐπιδημίαι” 6.6.5, compare 2nd c.AD: Galenus Medicus 17(2).341.]]

__A.II.3
of sounds, great, loud, ἀλαλητός, ἰαχή, πάταγος, ὀρυμαγδός, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 12.138, 15.384, 21.9, 256]]; θόρυβοι, κωκυτός, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Ajax” 142 (_anapaest meter_), 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Medea” 1176; οὐκ ἔστι ὅκως τι νεῖκος ἔσται ἢ μέγα ἢ σμικρόν 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 3.62; μὴ φώνει μέγα 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Philoctetes” 574.]]

__A.II.4
generally, great, mighty, ὅρκος [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 19.113]]; ὄλβος, τιμά, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “O.” 1.56, “P.” 4.148]]; μ. λόγος, μῦθος, a great story, rumour, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Prometheus Vinctus” 732, 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Ajax” 226 (Lyric poetry)]]; ἐρώτημα a big, i. e. difficult, question, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Euthydemus” 275d, “Hp.Ma.” 287b]]; weighty, important, τόδε μεῖζον [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 16.291]]; μέγα ποιέεσθαί τι to esteem of great importance, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 3.42, compare 9.111; μέγα γενέσθαι εἴς τι 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Historia Graeca (Hellenica)” 7.5.6; μ. ὑπάρχειν πρός τι [prev. author] “Mem.” 2.3.4; μέγα διαφέρειν εἴς τι 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Leges” 78o c]]; οὐκ ἂν εἴη παρὰ μέγα τὸ δικολογεῖν not of great importance, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [1st c.BC: Philodemus Gadarensis Epigrammaticus “Rh.” 2.85 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus]]; τὸ δὲ μέγιστον and what is most important, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 4.70, compare 1.142]]; οἱ μέγιστοι καιροί the most pressing emergencies, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 20.44]]; μ. ὠνησάμενοι χρημάτων for large sums, [Refs 2nd c.BC+ [2nd c.BC: Polybius Historicus 4.50.3, etc.]]

__A.II.5
with a bad sense, over-great, μέγα εἰπεῖν to speak big, and so provoke divine wrath, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 22.288; λίην μέγα εἶπες 3.227, 16.243; μέγα ἔργον 3.261, 5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “N.” 10.64; ἔργων μ. 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Agamemnon” 1546 (_anapaest meter_); ὠμὸν τὸ βούλευμα καὶ μ. 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 3.36]]; ἔπος μ., μ. λόγοι, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Ajax” 423 (Lyric poetry), “Ant.” 1350 (_anapaest meter_); μ. γλῶσσα [prev. work] 127 (_anapaest meter_)]]; μηδὲν μέγ᾽ εἴπῃς [Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. author] “Aj.” 386; μὴ μέγα λέγε 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Phaedo” 95b; μὴ μεγάλα λίαν λέγε 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Ranae” 835; μέγα φρονεῖν 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Tyrannus” 1078, 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Hippolytus” 6; μεγάλα φρονεῖν 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Acharnenses” 988]]; μεγάλα, μεῖζον ἢ δικαίως πνεῖν, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Andromache” 189, 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Agamemnon” 376 (Lyric poetry); μέγα τι παθεῖν 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 5.8.17; μὴ μέγα λέγων μεῖζον πάθῃς 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Hercules Furens” 1244.]]

__A.II.6
of style. impressive, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demetrius Phalereus Rhetor “Demetrius on Style” 278]]; μεῖζον more striking, [Refs [[prev. work] 103.]]

__A.II.7
of days, long, [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd c.AD: Galenus Medicus 12.714.]]

__B
adverb μεγάλως [ᾰ] greatly, mightily, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 16.432, 8th-7th c.BC: Hesiodus Epicus “Theogonia” 429, 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.16, 30, +others, 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 8.2.10, 1st c.BC: Parthenius Mythographus 28.1, etc.; strengthened, μάλα μ. 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 17.723; δμαθέντες μ. 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Persae” 907 (Lyric poetry); with _adjectives_, 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.4, 7.190.]]

__B.II
more frequently neuter singular μέγα as adverb, very much, exceedingly, μ. χαῖρε all hail!, see l. for μάλα in [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 24.402]]; especially with Verbs expressing strong feeling, μ. κεν κεχαροίατο [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 1.256; μ. κήδεται 2.27, etc.: with Verbs expressing power, might, μ. πάντων.. κρατέει 1.78; ὃς μ. πάντων.. ἤνασσε 10.32; πατρὸς μ. δυναμένοιο 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 1.276, compare 8th c.BC: Homerus Epicus “Epigrammata” 15.1, 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Eumenides” 950 (_anapaest meter_), 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Helena” 1358 (Lyric poetry), 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Ranae” 141, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 366a; μ. δύνασθαι παρά τινι 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 2.29; πλουτέειν μ. 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.32]]; or those expressing sound, loudly, μ. ἰάχειν, ἀῧσαι, βοῆσαι, εὔξασθαι, ἀμβῶσαι, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 2.333, 14.147, 17.334, 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 17.239, 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.8 (also _plural_, μεγάλ᾽ εὔχετο 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 1.450]]; μ. αὐδήσαντος, μ. ἤπυεν, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 4.505, 9.399): strengthened, μάλα μ. 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 15.321; μ. δ᾽ ἔβραχε φήγινος ἄξων 5.838, etc.: so in Trag. with all kinds of Verbs, μ. στένειν, σθένειν, χλίειν, 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Agamemnon” 711 (Lyric poetry), 938, “Ch.” 137]]: also in plural, μεγάλα.. δυστυχεῖς [Refs [[prev. author] “Eu.” 791 (Lyric poetry).]]

__B.II.2
of Space, far, μέγα προθορών [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 14.363]]; ἄνευθε μέγα far away,[Refs 5th c.BC+ [22.88; οὐκ ἂν μέγα τι τῆς ἀληθείας παρεξέλθοις 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Philebus” 66b.]]

__B.II.3
with adjectives, as μέγ᾽ ἔξοχος, μέγα νήπιος, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 2.480, 16.46]]; μ. νήπιε Oracle texts cited in [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.85; μ. πλούσιος [prev. author] 1.32, 7.190; ὦ μέγ᾽ εὔδαιμον κόρη 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Prometheus Vinctus” 647]]: with comparative and superlative, by far, μέγ᾽ ἀμείνονες, ἄριστος, φέρτατος, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 4.405, 2.82, 16.21.]]

__C
degrees of Comparison (regular μεγαλώτερος, -ώτατος late, [Refs [“Etymologicum Magnum” 780.1, 2):]]

__C.1
comparative μείζων, ον, genitive ονος, Epic dialect, Attic dialect (also Delph., [Refs 4th c.BC+ [“SIG” 246 H 260 (4th c.BC))]]; Ionic dialect, [Refs 4th c.AD+ [4th c.AD(?): Arcadius Grammaticus]], Doric dialect, Aeolic dialect μέζων, ον, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [1st c.AD(?): Heraclitus 25, 5th c.BC: Hippocrates Medicus “περὶ διαίτης ὀξέων” 44, 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.26, “IG” 7.235.16 (from Oropus), 5(2).3.18 (from Tegea), 5th c.BC: Epicharmus Comicus 62]] (also early Attic dialect, [Refs [“IG” 12.22.65, but [με] ίζων [prev. work]6.93, by analogy of ὀλείζων [prev. work]76,95)]]; dative plural μεζόνεσσι [Refs 7th c.BC+ [Diotogenes Philosophus cited in 5th c.AD: Stobaeus, Joannes 4.7.62: written μέσδων in 7th-6th c.BC: Sappho Lyrica “Papyrus fragments” in E. Diehl, 7.6, 1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus “Lycurgus” 19]]: compare μέττον· μεῖζον, [NT+5th c.AD+ [5th c.AD(?): Hesychius Legal icographus (uncertain); later μειζότερος NT.3JOhn.4]] (used as title, elder, [Refs 6th c.AD+ [POxy. 943.3 (6th c.AD), etc.)]]; μειζονώτερος [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Fragmenta - American Journal of Philology” 434]]:—greater, longer, taller, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 3.168, 9.202, etc.]]; frequently also, too great, γέρας [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Sophista” 231a]]; Μηνόφιλος μείζων M. the elder, [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [Ostr.Bodl. see C 2 (2nd c.AD)]]; as title, μειζων κώμης headman of a village, [Refs 4th c.AD+ [“POxy.” 1626.5 (4th c.AD)]], etc.: generally, the higher authority, [Refs 3rd c.AD+ [PLond. 2.214.22 (3rd c.AD), “POxy.” 1204.17 (_plural_, 3rd c.AD)]]; οὔτε μεῖζον οὔτε ἔλαττον, a strong form of denial, nothing whatever, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [1st c.BC: Dionysius Halicarnassensis “de Compositione Verborum” 4; οὐδαμὰ προὔφηνεν οὔτε μείζον᾽ οὔτ᾽ ἐλάττονα 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Trachiniae” 324]]. adverb μειζόνως [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Hecuba” 1121, 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 1.130, 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Cynegeticus” 13.3, 5th-6th c.BC: Isocrates Orator 9.21, etc.]]; Ionic dialect μεζόνως [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 3.128, 3rd c.BC: Herodas Mimographus 4.80, etc.]]: neuter as adverb, μεῖζον σθένειν [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Philoctetes” 456, 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Supplices” 216; μ. ἰσχύειν 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator “Epistulae” 3.28; ἐπὶ μ. ἔρχεται 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Philoctetes” 259.]]

__C.2
superlative μέγιστος, η, ον, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 2.412, etc.]]: neuter as adverb, μέγιστον ἴσχυσε [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Ajax” 502]]; δυνάμενος μ., with genitive, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 7.5, 9.9]]: with another superlative, μέγιστον ἐχθίστη [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Medea” 1323: in _plural_, χαῖρ᾽ ὡς μέγιστα 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Philoctetes” 462; θάλλει μ. [prev. author] “OC” 700 (Lyric poetry); τὰ μέγιστ᾽ ἐτιμάθης [prev. author] “OT” 1203 (Lyric poetry)]]; ἐς μέγιστον[Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. work] 521; ἐς τὰ μ. 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 8.111]]:—late superlative μεγιστότατος [Refs 1st c.AD+ [“PLond.” 1.130.49 (1st-2nd c.AD)]]. (Cf. Sanskrit majmán- 'greatness', Latin magnus, Gothic mikils 'great'.)

Abbott-Smith / STEPBible (TBESG)
μειζότερος, see: μέγας.
μέγας, μεγάλη, μέγα,
[in LXX chiefly for גָּדוֹל, also for מַרְבֶּה ,רַב (incl. μείζων), רֹב (μέγιστος) ;]
great;
__1. of external form, bodily size, measure, extent: λίθος, Mat.2:60; δράκων, Rev.12:3; ἰχθῦς, Jhn.21:11; πόλις, Rev.11:8; μάχαιρα, Rev.6:4, al.
__2. Of intensity and degree: δύναμις, Act.4:33; φόβος, Mrk.4:41; ἀγάπη, Jhn.15:13; ἄνεμος, ib. 6:18; κραυγή, Act.23:9; φῶς, Mat.4:16; πυρετός, Luk.4:38; θλίψις, Mat.24:21.
__3. Of rank;
__(a) of persons: θεός (MM, xvi), Tit.2:13; Ἄρτεμις, Act.19:27; compar. (see infr.), Mat.18:1 (cf. Dalman, Words, 113f.); neut. for masc. (Bl., §32, 1), Mat.12:6;
__(b) of things: ἁμαρτία, Jhn.19:11; μυστήριον, Eph.5:32; = μεγίστη (see infr., and cf. Field, Notes, 16f.), Mat.22:36; compar. for superl. (M, Pr., 78), 1Co.13:13.
__4.
__(a) Compar., μείζων: Mat.11:11 23:17, al.; neut. pl., μείζονα, contr. μείζω, Jhn.1:51; double compar., μειζότερος (M, Pr., 236; Bl., §11, 4), III Jo 4;
__(b) superl, μέγιστος (Deiss., BS, 365), 2Pe.1:4.
(AS)

μέγᾰς, μεγάλη [ᾰ], μέγα [ᾰ],
genitive μεγάλου, ης, ου, dative μεγάλῳ, ῃ, ῳ, accusative μέγᾰν, μεγάλην, μέγα [ᾰ]; dual μεγάλω, α, w; plural μεγάλοι, μεγάλαι, μεγάλα, etc.: the stem μεγάλο- is never used in singular nominative and accusative masculine and neuter, and only once in vocative masculine,

__A
ὦ μεγάλε Ζεῦ [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Septem contra Thebas” 822 (_anapaest meter_).]]

__A.I
big, of bodily size: frequently of stature, εἶδος.. μ. ἦν ὁράασθαι [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 18.4; κεῖτο μ. μεγαλωστί 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 16.776; ἠΰς τε μ. τε 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 9. 508]]; φῶτα μέγαν καὶ καλόν[Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. work] 513; καλή τε μεγάλη τε 15.418; κάρτα μεγάλη καὶ εὐειδής 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 3.1]]; φύσιν τίν᾽ εἶχε φράζ; Answ. μέγας [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Tyrannus” 742.]]

__A.I.b
full-grown, of age as shown by stature, νῦν δ᾽ ὅτε δὴ μ. εἰμί [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 2.314; μήτε μέγαν μήτ᾽ οὖν νεαρῶν τινα 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Agamemnon” 358 (_anapaest meter_)]]; later, elder of two persons of the same name, Wilcken [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [“Chr.” 305 (3rd c.BC)]]; Σκιπίων ὁ μ. [Refs 2nd c.BC+ [2nd c.BC: Polybius Historicus 18.35.9.]]

__A.I.c
of animals, μ. ἵπποι, βοῦς, σῦς, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 2.839, 18.559, 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 19.439; αἰετός 5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “I.” 6(5).50.]]

__A.I.2
generally, vast, high, οὐρανός, ὄρος, πύργος, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 1.497, 16.297, 6.386]]; wide, πέλαγος, λαῖτμα θαλάσσης, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 3.179, 5.174]]; long, ἠϊών, αἰγιαλός, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 12.31, 2.210: sometimes opposed to ὀλίγος, κῦμα οὔτε μέγ᾽ οὔτ᾽ ὀ. 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 10.94]]; but usually opposed to μικρός or σμικρός, πρὸς ἑαυτὸ ἕκαστον καὶ μ. καὶ σμικρόν [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Anaxagoras Philosophus 3; τὸ ἄπειρον ἐκ μεγάλου καὶ μικροῦ 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Metaphysica” 987b26, etc.]]

__A.II
of quality or degree, great, mighty, frequently epithet of gods, ὁ μ. Ζεύς [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Supplices” 1052 (Lyric poetry), etc.]]; μεγάλα θεά, of Demeter and Persephone, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Coloneus” 683 (Lyric poetry)]]; θεοὶ μεγάλοι, of the Cabiri, [Refs [“IG” 12(8).71 (from Imbros), etc.]]; Μήτηρ μ., of Cybele, [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [“SIG” 1014.83 (Erythrae, 3rd c.BC), 1138.3 (Delos, 2nd c.BC)]]; Μήτηρ θεῶν μ. [Refs [“OGI” 540.6 (from Pessinus), etc.]]; Ἴσιδος μ. μητρὸς θεῶν [Refs 2nd c.BC+ [“PStrassb.” 81.14 (2nd c.BC)]]; μ. ἡ Ἄρτεμις Ἐφεσίων [NT.Act.19.28]; τίς θεὸς μ. ὡς ὁ θεὸς ἡμῶ; [LXX+NT [LXX.Psa.76(77).13; ὁ μ. θεός NT.Tit.2.13]]; of men, μ. ἠδὲ κραταιός [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 18.382; ὀλίγος καὶ μ. 7th c.BC: Callinus Epicus 1.17, etc.]]; μέγας ηὐξήθη rose to greatness, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 2.5; ἤρθη μ. [prev. work]8; βασιλεὺς ὁ μ.]], i. e. the King of Persia, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.188, etc. (θεῶν β. ὁ μ., of Zeus, 5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “O.” 7.34); βασιλεὺς μ. 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Persae” 24 (_anapaest meter_)]]; as a title of special monarchs, Ἀρδιαῖος ὁ μ. [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 615c; ὁ μ. Ἀλέξανδρος 2nd c.AD: Athenaeus Epigrammaticus 1.3d; ὁ μ. ἐπικληθεὶς Ἀντίοχος 2nd c.BC: Polybius Historicus 4.2.7, etc.; μ. φίλος 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Medea” 549; πλούτῳ τε κἀνδρείᾳ μ. [prev. author] “Tr.” 674; ἐπὶ μέγα ἦλθεν ἰσχύος 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 2.97.]]

__A.II.2
strong, of the elements, etc., ἄνεμος, λαῖλαψ, Ζέφυρος, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 19.200, 12.408, 14.458]]; of properties, passions, qualities, feelings, etc., of men, θάρσος, πένθος, ποθή, etc.,[NT+8th c.BC+ [9.381, 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 1.254, 11.471, etc.; ἀρετή 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 24.193, 5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “O.” 8.5; θυμός 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 9.496, 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Orestes” 702; κλέος 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 6.446; ἄχος 9.9; πυρετός NT.Luke.4.38 (incorrect _accusative_ to 2nd c.AD: Galenus Medicus 7.275)]]; ἡ μ. νοῦσος epilepsy, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Hippocrates Medicus “ἐπιδημίαι” 6.6.5, compare 2nd c.AD: Galenus Medicus 17(2).341.]]

__A.II.3
of sounds, great, loud, ἀλαλητός, ἰαχή, πάταγος, ὀρυμαγδός, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 12.138, 15.384, 21.9, 256]]; θόρυβοι, κωκυτός, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Ajax” 142 (_anapaest meter_), 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Medea” 1176; οὐκ ἔστι ὅκως τι νεῖκος ἔσται ἢ μέγα ἢ σμικρόν 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 3.62; μὴ φώνει μέγα 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Philoctetes” 574.]]

__A.II.4
generally, great, mighty, ὅρκος [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 19.113]]; ὄλβος, τιμά, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “O.” 1.56, “P.” 4.148]]; μ. λόγος, μῦθος, a great story, rumour, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Prometheus Vinctus” 732, 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Ajax” 226 (Lyric poetry)]]; ἐρώτημα a big, i. e. difficult, question, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Euthydemus” 275d, “Hp.Ma.” 287b]]; weighty, important, τόδε μεῖζον [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 16.291]]; μέγα ποιέεσθαί τι to esteem of great importance, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 3.42, compare 9.111; μέγα γενέσθαι εἴς τι 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Historia Graeca (Hellenica)” 7.5.6; μ. ὑπάρχειν πρός τι [prev. author] “Mem.” 2.3.4; μέγα διαφέρειν εἴς τι 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Leges” 78o c]]; οὐκ ἂν εἴη παρὰ μέγα τὸ δικολογεῖν not of great importance, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [1st c.BC: Philodemus Gadarensis Epigrammaticus “Rh.” 2.85 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus]]; τὸ δὲ μέγιστον and what is most important, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 4.70, compare 1.142]]; οἱ μέγιστοι καιροί the most pressing emergencies, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 20.44]]; μ. ὠνησάμενοι χρημάτων for large sums, [Refs 2nd c.BC+ [2nd c.BC: Polybius Historicus 4.50.3, etc.]]

__A.II.5
with a bad sense, over-great, μέγα εἰπεῖν to speak big, and so provoke divine wrath, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 22.288; λίην μέγα εἶπες 3.227, 16.243; μέγα ἔργον 3.261, 5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “N.” 10.64; ἔργων μ. 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Agamemnon” 1546 (_anapaest meter_); ὠμὸν τὸ βούλευμα καὶ μ. 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 3.36]]; ἔπος μ., μ. λόγοι, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Ajax” 423 (Lyric poetry), “Ant.” 1350 (_anapaest meter_); μ. γλῶσσα [prev. work] 127 (_anapaest meter_)]]; μηδὲν μέγ᾽ εἴπῃς [Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. author] “Aj.” 386; μὴ μέγα λέγε 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Phaedo” 95b; μὴ μεγάλα λίαν λέγε 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Ranae” 835; μέγα φρονεῖν 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Tyrannus” 1078, 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Hippolytus” 6; μεγάλα φρονεῖν 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Acharnenses” 988]]; μεγάλα, μεῖζον ἢ δικαίως πνεῖν, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Andromache” 189, 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Agamemnon” 376 (Lyric poetry); μέγα τι παθεῖν 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 5.8.17; μὴ μέγα λέγων μεῖζον πάθῃς 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Hercules Furens” 1244.]]

__A.II.6
of style. impressive, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demetrius Phalereus Rhetor “Demetrius on Style” 278]]; μεῖζον more striking, [Refs [[prev. work] 103.]]

__A.II.7
of days, long, [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd c.AD: Galenus Medicus 12.714.]]

__B
adverb μεγάλως [ᾰ] greatly, mightily, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 16.432, 8th-7th c.BC: Hesiodus Epicus “Theogonia” 429, 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.16, 30, +others, 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 8.2.10, 1st c.BC: Parthenius Mythographus 28.1, etc.; strengthened, μάλα μ. 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 17.723; δμαθέντες μ. 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Persae” 907 (Lyric poetry); with _adjectives_, 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.4, 7.190.]]

__B.II
more frequently neuter singular μέγα as adverb, very much, exceedingly, μ. χαῖρε all hail!, see l. for μάλα in [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 24.402]]; especially with Verbs expressing strong feeling, μ. κεν κεχαροίατο [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 1.256; μ. κήδεται 2.27, etc.: with Verbs expressing power, might, μ. πάντων.. κρατέει 1.78; ὃς μ. πάντων.. ἤνασσε 10.32; πατρὸς μ. δυναμένοιο 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 1.276, compare 8th c.BC: Homerus Epicus “Epigrammata” 15.1, 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Eumenides” 950 (_anapaest meter_), 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Helena” 1358 (Lyric poetry), 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Ranae” 141, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 366a; μ. δύνασθαι παρά τινι 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 2.29; πλουτέειν μ. 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.32]]; or those expressing sound, loudly, μ. ἰάχειν, ἀῧσαι, βοῆσαι, εὔξασθαι, ἀμβῶσαι, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 2.333, 14.147, 17.334, 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 17.239, 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.8 (also _plural_, μεγάλ᾽ εὔχετο 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 1.450]]; μ. αὐδήσαντος, μ. ἤπυεν, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 4.505, 9.399): strengthened, μάλα μ. 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 15.321; μ. δ᾽ ἔβραχε φήγινος ἄξων 5.838, etc.: so in Trag. with all kinds of Verbs, μ. στένειν, σθένειν, χλίειν, 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Agamemnon” 711 (Lyric poetry), 938, “Ch.” 137]]: also in plural, μεγάλα.. δυστυχεῖς [Refs [[prev. author] “Eu.” 791 (Lyric poetry).]]

__B.II.2
of Space, far, μέγα προθορών [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 14.363]]; ἄνευθε μέγα far away,[Refs 5th c.BC+ [22.88; οὐκ ἂν μέγα τι τῆς ἀληθείας παρεξέλθοις 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Philebus” 66b.]]

__B.II.3
with adjectives, as μέγ᾽ ἔξοχος, μέγα νήπιος, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 2.480, 16.46]]; μ. νήπιε Oracle texts cited in [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.85; μ. πλούσιος [prev. author] 1.32, 7.190; ὦ μέγ᾽ εὔδαιμον κόρη 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Prometheus Vinctus” 647]]: with comparative and superlative, by far, μέγ᾽ ἀμείνονες, ἄριστος, φέρτατος, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 4.405, 2.82, 16.21.]]

__C
degrees of Comparison (regular μεγαλώτερος, -ώτατος late, [Refs [“Etymologicum Magnum” 780.1, 2):]]

__C.1
comparative μείζων, ον, genitive ονος, Epic dialect, Attic dialect (also Delph., [Refs 4th c.BC+ [“SIG” 246 H 260 (4th c.BC))]]; Ionic dialect, [Refs 4th c.AD+ [4th c.AD(?): Arcadius Grammaticus]], Doric dialect, Aeolic dialect μέζων, ον, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [1st c.AD(?): Heraclitus 25, 5th c.BC: Hippocrates Medicus “περὶ διαίτης ὀξέων” 44, 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.26, “IG” 7.235.16 (from Oropus), 5(2).3.18 (from Tegea), 5th c.BC: Epicharmus Comicus 62]] (also early Attic dialect, [Refs [“IG” 12.22.65, but [με] ίζων [prev. work]6.93, by analogy of ὀλείζων [prev. work]76,95)]]; dative plural μεζόνεσσι [Refs 7th c.BC+ [Diotogenes Philosophus cited in 5th c.AD: Stobaeus, Joannes 4.7.62: written μέσδων in 7th-6th c.BC: Sappho Lyrica “Papyrus fragments” in E. Diehl, 7.6, 1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus “Lycurgus” 19]]: compare μέττον· μεῖζον, [NT+5th c.AD+ [5th c.AD(?): Hesychius Legal icographus (uncertain); later μειζότερος NT.3JOhn.4]] (used as title, elder, [Refs 6th c.AD+ [POxy. 943.3 (6th c.AD), etc.)]]; μειζονώτερος [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Fragmenta - American Journal of Philology” 434]]:—greater, longer, taller, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 3.168, 9.202, etc.]]; frequently also, too great, γέρας [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Sophista” 231a]]; Μηνόφιλος μείζων M. the elder, [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [Ostr.Bodl. see C 2 (2nd c.AD)]]; as title, μειζων κώμης headman of a village, [Refs 4th c.AD+ [“POxy.” 1626.5 (4th c.AD)]], etc.: generally, the higher authority, [Refs 3rd c.AD+ [PLond. 2.214.22 (3rd c.AD), “POxy.” 1204.17 (_plural_, 3rd c.AD)]]; οὔτε μεῖζον οὔτε ἔλαττον, a strong form of denial, nothing whatever, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [1st c.BC: Dionysius Halicarnassensis “de Compositione Verborum” 4; οὐδαμὰ προὔφηνεν οὔτε μείζον᾽ οὔτ᾽ ἐλάττονα 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Trachiniae” 324]]. adverb μειζόνως [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Hecuba” 1121, 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 1.130, 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Cynegeticus” 13.3, 5th-6th c.BC: Isocrates Orator 9.21, etc.]]; Ionic dialect μεζόνως [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 3.128, 3rd c.BC: Herodas Mimographus 4.80, etc.]]: neuter as adverb, μεῖζον σθένειν [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Philoctetes” 456, 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Supplices” 216; μ. ἰσχύειν 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator “Epistulae” 3.28; ἐπὶ μ. ἔρχεται 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Philoctetes” 259.]]

__C.2
superlative μέγιστος, η, ον, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 2.412, etc.]]: neuter as adverb, μέγιστον ἴσχυσε [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Ajax” 502]]; δυνάμενος μ., with genitive, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 7.5, 9.9]]: with another superlative, μέγιστον ἐχθίστη [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Medea” 1323: in _plural_, χαῖρ᾽ ὡς μέγιστα 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Philoctetes” 462; θάλλει μ. [prev. author] “OC” 700 (Lyric poetry); τὰ μέγιστ᾽ ἐτιμάθης [prev. author] “OT” 1203 (Lyric poetry)]]; ἐς μέγιστον[Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. work] 521; ἐς τὰ μ. 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 8.111]]:—late superlative μεγιστότατος [Refs 1st c.AD+ [“PLond.” 1.130.49 (1st-2nd c.AD)]]. (Cf. Sanskrit majmán- 'greatness', Latin magnus, Gothic mikils 'great'.)

Abbott-Smith / STEPBible (TBESG)
μείζων, see: μέγας.
μέγας, μεγάλη, μέγα,
[in LXX chiefly for גָּדוֹל, also for מַרְבֶּה ,רַב (incl. μείζων), רֹב (μέγιστος) ;]
great;
__1. of external form, bodily size, measure, extent: λίθος, Mat.2:60; δράκων, Rev.12:3; ἰχθῦς, Jhn.21:11; πόλις, Rev.11:8; μάχαιρα, Rev.6:4, al.
__2. Of intensity and degree: δύναμις, Act.4:33; φόβος, Mrk.4:41; ἀγάπη, Jhn.15:13; ἄνεμος, ib. 6:18; κραυγή, Act.23:9; φῶς, Mat.4:16; πυρετός, Luk.4:38; θλίψις, Mat.24:21.
__3. Of rank;
__(a) of persons: θεός (MM, xvi), Tit.2:13; Ἄρτεμις, Act.19:27; compar. (see infr.), Mat.18:1 (cf. Dalman, Words, 113f.); neut. for masc. (Bl., §32, 1), Mat.12:6;
__(b) of things: ἁμαρτία, Jhn.19:11; μυστήριον, Eph.5:32; = μεγίστη (see infr., and cf. Field, Notes, 16f.), Mat.22:36; compar. for superl. (M, Pr., 78), 1Co.13:13.
__4.
__(a) Compar., μείζων: Mat.11:11 23:17, al.; neut. pl., μείζονα, contr. μείζω, Jhn.1:51; double compar., μειζότερος (M, Pr., 236; Bl., §11, 4), III Jo 4;
__(b) superl, μέγιστος (Deiss., BS, 365), 2Pe.1:4.
(AS)

μέγᾰς, μεγάλη [ᾰ], μέγα [ᾰ],
genitive μεγάλου, ης, ου, dative μεγάλῳ, ῃ, ῳ, accusative μέγᾰν, μεγάλην, μέγα [ᾰ]; dual μεγάλω, α, w; plural μεγάλοι, μεγάλαι, μεγάλα, etc.: the stem μεγάλο- is never used in singular nominative and accusative masculine and neuter, and only once in vocative masculine,

__A
ὦ μεγάλε Ζεῦ [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Septem contra Thebas” 822 (_anapaest meter_).]]

__A.I
big, of bodily size: frequently of stature, εἶδος.. μ. ἦν ὁράασθαι [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 18.4; κεῖτο μ. μεγαλωστί 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 16.776; ἠΰς τε μ. τε 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 9. 508]]; φῶτα μέγαν καὶ καλόν[Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. work] 513; καλή τε μεγάλη τε 15.418; κάρτα μεγάλη καὶ εὐειδής 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 3.1]]; φύσιν τίν᾽ εἶχε φράζ; Answ. μέγας [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Tyrannus” 742.]]

__A.I.b
full-grown, of age as shown by stature, νῦν δ᾽ ὅτε δὴ μ. εἰμί [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 2.314; μήτε μέγαν μήτ᾽ οὖν νεαρῶν τινα 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Agamemnon” 358 (_anapaest meter_)]]; later, elder of two persons of the same name, Wilcken [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [“Chr.” 305 (3rd c.BC)]]; Σκιπίων ὁ μ. [Refs 2nd c.BC+ [2nd c.BC: Polybius Historicus 18.35.9.]]

__A.I.c
of animals, μ. ἵπποι, βοῦς, σῦς, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 2.839, 18.559, 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 19.439; αἰετός 5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “I.” 6(5).50.]]

__A.I.2
generally, vast, high, οὐρανός, ὄρος, πύργος, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 1.497, 16.297, 6.386]]; wide, πέλαγος, λαῖτμα θαλάσσης, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 3.179, 5.174]]; long, ἠϊών, αἰγιαλός, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 12.31, 2.210: sometimes opposed to ὀλίγος, κῦμα οὔτε μέγ᾽ οὔτ᾽ ὀ. 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 10.94]]; but usually opposed to μικρός or σμικρός, πρὸς ἑαυτὸ ἕκαστον καὶ μ. καὶ σμικρόν [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Anaxagoras Philosophus 3; τὸ ἄπειρον ἐκ μεγάλου καὶ μικροῦ 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Metaphysica” 987b26, etc.]]

__A.II
of quality or degree, great, mighty, frequently epithet of gods, ὁ μ. Ζεύς [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Supplices” 1052 (Lyric poetry), etc.]]; μεγάλα θεά, of Demeter and Persephone, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Coloneus” 683 (Lyric poetry)]]; θεοὶ μεγάλοι, of the Cabiri, [Refs [“IG” 12(8).71 (from Imbros), etc.]]; Μήτηρ μ., of Cybele, [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [“SIG” 1014.83 (Erythrae, 3rd c.BC), 1138.3 (Delos, 2nd c.BC)]]; Μήτηρ θεῶν μ. [Refs [“OGI” 540.6 (from Pessinus), etc.]]; Ἴσιδος μ. μητρὸς θεῶν [Refs 2nd c.BC+ [“PStrassb.” 81.14 (2nd c.BC)]]; μ. ἡ Ἄρτεμις Ἐφεσίων [NT.Act.19.28]; τίς θεὸς μ. ὡς ὁ θεὸς ἡμῶ; [LXX+NT [LXX.Psa.76(77).13; ὁ μ. θεός NT.Tit.2.13]]; of men, μ. ἠδὲ κραταιός [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 18.382; ὀλίγος καὶ μ. 7th c.BC: Callinus Epicus 1.17, etc.]]; μέγας ηὐξήθη rose to greatness, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 2.5; ἤρθη μ. [prev. work]8; βασιλεὺς ὁ μ.]], i. e. the King of Persia, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.188, etc. (θεῶν β. ὁ μ., of Zeus, 5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “O.” 7.34); βασιλεὺς μ. 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Persae” 24 (_anapaest meter_)]]; as a title of special monarchs, Ἀρδιαῖος ὁ μ. [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 615c; ὁ μ. Ἀλέξανδρος 2nd c.AD: Athenaeus Epigrammaticus 1.3d; ὁ μ. ἐπικληθεὶς Ἀντίοχος 2nd c.BC: Polybius Historicus 4.2.7, etc.; μ. φίλος 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Medea” 549; πλούτῳ τε κἀνδρείᾳ μ. [prev. author] “Tr.” 674; ἐπὶ μέγα ἦλθεν ἰσχύος 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 2.97.]]

__A.II.2
strong, of the elements, etc., ἄνεμος, λαῖλαψ, Ζέφυρος, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 19.200, 12.408, 14.458]]; of properties, passions, qualities, feelings, etc., of men, θάρσος, πένθος, ποθή, etc.,[NT+8th c.BC+ [9.381, 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 1.254, 11.471, etc.; ἀρετή 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 24.193, 5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “O.” 8.5; θυμός 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 9.496, 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Orestes” 702; κλέος 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 6.446; ἄχος 9.9; πυρετός NT.Luke.4.38 (incorrect _accusative_ to 2nd c.AD: Galenus Medicus 7.275)]]; ἡ μ. νοῦσος epilepsy, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Hippocrates Medicus “ἐπιδημίαι” 6.6.5, compare 2nd c.AD: Galenus Medicus 17(2).341.]]

__A.II.3
of sounds, great, loud, ἀλαλητός, ἰαχή, πάταγος, ὀρυμαγδός, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 12.138, 15.384, 21.9, 256]]; θόρυβοι, κωκυτός, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Ajax” 142 (_anapaest meter_), 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Medea” 1176; οὐκ ἔστι ὅκως τι νεῖκος ἔσται ἢ μέγα ἢ σμικρόν 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 3.62; μὴ φώνει μέγα 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Philoctetes” 574.]]

__A.II.4
generally, great, mighty, ὅρκος [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 19.113]]; ὄλβος, τιμά, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “O.” 1.56, “P.” 4.148]]; μ. λόγος, μῦθος, a great story, rumour, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Prometheus Vinctus” 732, 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Ajax” 226 (Lyric poetry)]]; ἐρώτημα a big, i. e. difficult, question, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Euthydemus” 275d, “Hp.Ma.” 287b]]; weighty, important, τόδε μεῖζον [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 16.291]]; μέγα ποιέεσθαί τι to esteem of great importance, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 3.42, compare 9.111; μέγα γενέσθαι εἴς τι 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Historia Graeca (Hellenica)” 7.5.6; μ. ὑπάρχειν πρός τι [prev. author] “Mem.” 2.3.4; μέγα διαφέρειν εἴς τι 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Leges” 78o c]]; οὐκ ἂν εἴη παρὰ μέγα τὸ δικολογεῖν not of great importance, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [1st c.BC: Philodemus Gadarensis Epigrammaticus “Rh.” 2.85 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus]]; τὸ δὲ μέγιστον and what is most important, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 4.70, compare 1.142]]; οἱ μέγιστοι καιροί the most pressing emergencies, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 20.44]]; μ. ὠνησάμενοι χρημάτων for large sums, [Refs 2nd c.BC+ [2nd c.BC: Polybius Historicus 4.50.3, etc.]]

__A.II.5
with a bad sense, over-great, μέγα εἰπεῖν to speak big, and so provoke divine wrath, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 22.288; λίην μέγα εἶπες 3.227, 16.243; μέγα ἔργον 3.261, 5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “N.” 10.64; ἔργων μ. 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Agamemnon” 1546 (_anapaest meter_); ὠμὸν τὸ βούλευμα καὶ μ. 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 3.36]]; ἔπος μ., μ. λόγοι, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Ajax” 423 (Lyric poetry), “Ant.” 1350 (_anapaest meter_); μ. γλῶσσα [prev. work] 127 (_anapaest meter_)]]; μηδὲν μέγ᾽ εἴπῃς [Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. author] “Aj.” 386; μὴ μέγα λέγε 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Phaedo” 95b; μὴ μεγάλα λίαν λέγε 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Ranae” 835; μέγα φρονεῖν 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Tyrannus” 1078, 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Hippolytus” 6; μεγάλα φρονεῖν 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Acharnenses” 988]]; μεγάλα, μεῖζον ἢ δικαίως πνεῖν, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Andromache” 189, 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Agamemnon” 376 (Lyric poetry); μέγα τι παθεῖν 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 5.8.17; μὴ μέγα λέγων μεῖζον πάθῃς 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Hercules Furens” 1244.]]

__A.II.6
of style. impressive, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demetrius Phalereus Rhetor “Demetrius on Style” 278]]; μεῖζον more striking, [Refs [[prev. work] 103.]]

__A.II.7
of days, long, [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd c.AD: Galenus Medicus 12.714.]]

__B
adverb μεγάλως [ᾰ] greatly, mightily, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 16.432, 8th-7th c.BC: Hesiodus Epicus “Theogonia” 429, 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.16, 30, +others, 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 8.2.10, 1st c.BC: Parthenius Mythographus 28.1, etc.; strengthened, μάλα μ. 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 17.723; δμαθέντες μ. 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Persae” 907 (Lyric poetry); with _adjectives_, 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.4, 7.190.]]

__B.II
more frequently neuter singular μέγα as adverb, very much, exceedingly, μ. χαῖρε all hail!, see l. for μάλα in [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 24.402]]; especially with Verbs expressing strong feeling, μ. κεν κεχαροίατο [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 1.256; μ. κήδεται 2.27, etc.: with Verbs expressing power, might, μ. πάντων.. κρατέει 1.78; ὃς μ. πάντων.. ἤνασσε 10.32; πατρὸς μ. δυναμένοιο 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 1.276, compare 8th c.BC: Homerus Epicus “Epigrammata” 15.1, 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Eumenides” 950 (_anapaest meter_), 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Helena” 1358 (Lyric poetry), 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Ranae” 141, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 366a; μ. δύνασθαι παρά τινι 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 2.29; πλουτέειν μ. 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.32]]; or those expressing sound, loudly, μ. ἰάχειν, ἀῧσαι, βοῆσαι, εὔξασθαι, ἀμβῶσαι, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 2.333, 14.147, 17.334, 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 17.239, 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.8 (also _plural_, μεγάλ᾽ εὔχετο 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 1.450]]; μ. αὐδήσαντος, μ. ἤπυεν, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 4.505, 9.399): strengthened, μάλα μ. 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 15.321; μ. δ᾽ ἔβραχε φήγινος ἄξων 5.838, etc.: so in Trag. with all kinds of Verbs, μ. στένειν, σθένειν, χλίειν, 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Agamemnon” 711 (Lyric poetry), 938, “Ch.” 137]]: also in plural, μεγάλα.. δυστυχεῖς [Refs [[prev. author] “Eu.” 791 (Lyric poetry).]]

__B.II.2
of Space, far, μέγα προθορών [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 14.363]]; ἄνευθε μέγα far away,[Refs 5th c.BC+ [22.88; οὐκ ἂν μέγα τι τῆς ἀληθείας παρεξέλθοις 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Philebus” 66b.]]

__B.II.3
with adjectives, as μέγ᾽ ἔξοχος, μέγα νήπιος, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 2.480, 16.46]]; μ. νήπιε Oracle texts cited in [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.85; μ. πλούσιος [prev. author] 1.32, 7.190; ὦ μέγ᾽ εὔδαιμον κόρη 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Prometheus Vinctus” 647]]: with comparative and superlative, by far, μέγ᾽ ἀμείνονες, ἄριστος, φέρτατος, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 4.405, 2.82, 16.21.]]

__C
degrees of Comparison (regular μεγαλώτερος, -ώτατος late, [Refs [“Etymologicum Magnum” 780.1, 2):]]

__C.1
comparative μείζων, ον, genitive ονος, Epic dialect, Attic dialect (also Delph., [Refs 4th c.BC+ [“SIG” 246 H 260 (4th c.BC))]]; Ionic dialect, [Refs 4th c.AD+ [4th c.AD(?): Arcadius Grammaticus]], Doric dialect, Aeolic dialect μέζων, ον, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [1st c.AD(?): Heraclitus 25, 5th c.BC: Hippocrates Medicus “περὶ διαίτης ὀξέων” 44, 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.26, “IG” 7.235.16 (from Oropus), 5(2).3.18 (from Tegea), 5th c.BC: Epicharmus Comicus 62]] (also early Attic dialect, [Refs [“IG” 12.22.65, but [με] ίζων [prev. work]6.93, by analogy of ὀλείζων [prev. work]76,95)]]; dative plural μεζόνεσσι [Refs 7th c.BC+ [Diotogenes Philosophus cited in 5th c.AD: Stobaeus, Joannes 4.7.62: written μέσδων in 7th-6th c.BC: Sappho Lyrica “Papyrus fragments” in E. Diehl, 7.6, 1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus “Lycurgus” 19]]: compare μέττον· μεῖζον, [NT+5th c.AD+ [5th c.AD(?): Hesychius Legal icographus (uncertain); later μειζότερος NT.3JOhn.4]] (used as title, elder, [Refs 6th c.AD+ [POxy. 943.3 (6th c.AD), etc.)]]; μειζονώτερος [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Fragmenta - American Journal of Philology” 434]]:—greater, longer, taller, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 3.168, 9.202, etc.]]; frequently also, too great, γέρας [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Sophista” 231a]]; Μηνόφιλος μείζων M. the elder, [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [Ostr.Bodl. see C 2 (2nd c.AD)]]; as title, μειζων κώμης headman of a village, [Refs 4th c.AD+ [“POxy.” 1626.5 (4th c.AD)]], etc.: generally, the higher authority, [Refs 3rd c.AD+ [PLond. 2.214.22 (3rd c.AD), “POxy.” 1204.17 (_plural_, 3rd c.AD)]]; οὔτε μεῖζον οὔτε ἔλαττον, a strong form of denial, nothing whatever, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [1st c.BC: Dionysius Halicarnassensis “de Compositione Verborum” 4; οὐδαμὰ προὔφηνεν οὔτε μείζον᾽ οὔτ᾽ ἐλάττονα 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Trachiniae” 324]]. adverb μειζόνως [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Hecuba” 1121, 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 1.130, 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Cynegeticus” 13.3, 5th-6th c.BC: Isocrates Orator 9.21, etc.]]; Ionic dialect μεζόνως [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 3.128, 3rd c.BC: Herodas Mimographus 4.80, etc.]]: neuter as adverb, μεῖζον σθένειν [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Philoctetes” 456, 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Supplices” 216; μ. ἰσχύειν 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator “Epistulae” 3.28; ἐπὶ μ. ἔρχεται 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Philoctetes” 259.]]

__C.2
superlative μέγιστος, η, ον, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 2.412, etc.]]: neuter as adverb, μέγιστον ἴσχυσε [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Ajax” 502]]; δυνάμενος μ., with genitive, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 7.5, 9.9]]: with another superlative, μέγιστον ἐχθίστη [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Medea” 1323: in _plural_, χαῖρ᾽ ὡς μέγιστα 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Philoctetes” 462; θάλλει μ. [prev. author] “OC” 700 (Lyric poetry); τὰ μέγιστ᾽ ἐτιμάθης [prev. author] “OT” 1203 (Lyric poetry)]]; ἐς μέγιστον[Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. work] 521; ἐς τὰ μ. 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 8.111]]:—late superlative μεγιστότατος [Refs 1st c.AD+ [“PLond.” 1.130.49 (1st-2nd c.AD)]]. (Cf. Sanskrit majmán- 'greatness', Latin magnus, Gothic mikils 'great'.)

LSJ / STEPBible (TFLSJ)
μέλᾱς
(μέλᾰς [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [3rd c.BC: Rhianus Epicus 58, where μέγας is corrupt for μέλας), μέλαινα, μέλᾰν]]; genitive μέλᾰνος, μελαίνης, μέλᾰνος, etc.; Epic dialect dative μείλανι (for the sake of meter) [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 24.79]]: Aeolic dialect nominative μέλαις, from *μέλανς, [Refs 7th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.AD: Choeroboscus Grammaticus “Scholia in Theodosii Canones” 1.123, Greg.Cor. p.599 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus, hence restored in 7th-6th c.BC: Sappho Lyrica 57]]:—black, dark: in [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Homerus Epicus]] generally, dark in colour, οἶνος [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 5.265]]; μέλαν αἷμα, κῦμα, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 4.149, 23.693; γαῖα μέλαινα 2.699, compare 7th-6th c.BC: Sappho Lyrica “Papyrus fragments” in E. Diehl, 5.2; ὕδωρ μέλαν Αἰσήποιο 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 2.825, compare 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 4.359, νηῦς μ.]], from its being pitched over, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 1.300, +others]]; of men, dark, swarthy, μέλανας δὲ ἀνδρικοὺς ἰδεῖν [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 474e; ἰσχυρός τις ἦν, μ. 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 21.71]]; τὰ μ. black marks about the ears of dogs, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Cynegeticus” 5.23.]]

__II
dark, murky, ἕσπερος [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 1.423; εὐφρόνα 5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “N.” 7.3.]]

__III
metaphorically, black, dark, θάνατος [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 2.834, etc.; κήρ [prev. work] 859, etc.]]; ὀδύναι [Refs [4.117, etc. (the origin of the metaphor is seen in the phrases θανάτου μ. νέφος, ἄχεος νεφέλη μ., 16. 350, 18.22)]]; μ. τύχα, ἀρά, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Supplices” 89 (Lyric poetry), “Th.” 832 (Lyric poetry); Ἐρινύς [prev. work] 993 (Lyric poetry),compare “Eu.” 52; ἄτα [prev. author] “Ag.” 769 (Lyric poetry); Ἄρης [prev. work] 1511 (Lyric poetry)]]; Ἅιδης [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Tyrannus” 29; Ἅιδου μ. ἀνάγκα 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Hippolytus” 1388 (Lyric poetry), etc.]]; ἡμέραι μέλαιναι, = Latin dies atri, [Refs 1st c.AD+ [1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus “Lucullus” 27.]]

__III.2
of the voice, indistinct, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Topica” 106a25, 2nd-3rd c.AD: Philostratus Sophista “Vita Apollonii” 4.44]]; βραχὺ καὶ μ. φώνημα, of Nero, [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd-3rd c.AD: Dio Cassius Historicus 61.20.]]

__III.3
dark, obscure, enigmatical, ἱστορίη [Refs 1st c.AD+ [“Anthologia Graeca” 11.347 (1st c.AD: Philippus Epigrammaticus).]]

__III.4
of character, dark, malignant, μ. φρήν, καρδία, [Refs 6th c.BC+ [6th c.BC: Solon Lyricus 42.4, 5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “Fragmenta.” 123.4; μ. ἄνθρωποι 1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus 2.12d]]; μ. ἦθος M. Ant.4.28.

__IV
comparative μελάντερος, α, ον, blacker, very black, τοῦ δ᾽ οὔ τι μελάντερον ἔπλετο ἔσθος [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 24.94: proverbial of thick darkness, [νέφος] μελάντερον ἠΰτε πίσσα (see. ἠΰτε) 4.277]]: superlative μελάντατος [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Hippocrates Medicus “περὶ τῶν ἐν κεφαλη—ͅ τρωμάτων” 14, 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Fragmenta” 580, etc.]]:— comparative also μελανώτερος [Refs 1st c.BC+ [1st c.BC-1st c.AD: Strabo Geographus 16.4.12]]: superlative μελαινότατος [Refs 1st c.AD+ [“Anthologia Graeca” 11.68 (1st c.AD: Lucillius Epigrammaticus), “epigram Gr.” 320.4 (from Thyatira).]]

__V
μέλαινα (i.e. νοῦσος), ἡ, in Medicine texts, of diseases causing black secretions (such as melaena), [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Hippocrates Medicus “περὶ νούσων” 2.73.]]

__VI
μέλαν, τό, see entry (Cf. Sanskrit málam 'dirt', malinás 'dirty', Lett. melns 'black'.)

deep_entry:
Abbott-Smith / STEPBible (TBESG)
μελετάω, -ῶ
(μελέτη, care), [in LXX chiefly for הָגָה m ;]
__1. with genitive, to care for (Hes.).
__2. C. accusative to attend to, practise: 1Ti.4:15 (RV, be diligent in; cf. Souter in Exp., VIII, vi, 429, but see infr.).
__3. to study, ponder: Act.4:25 (LXX) 1Ti.4:15 (AV, meditate on; cf. CGT, in l, but see supr.; cf. προ-μελετάω).†
(AS)

---

LSJ / STEPBible (TFLSJ)
μελετ-άω,
future -ήσω [Refs 8th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 1.80, etc., -ήσομαι 2nd c.AD: Lucianus Sophista “Sol.” 6, 2nd-3rd c.AD: Philostratus Sophista “Vitae Sophistarum” 1.24.2:—post- 8th c.BC: Homerus Epicus]] Verb, take thought or care for, with genitive, βίου, ἔργου, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th-7th c.BC: Hesiodus Epicus “Opera et Dies” 316, 443: with _accusative_ _of things_, δόξαν ἀρετῆς 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 6.11]]; of a physician, treat a case, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Hippocrates Medicus “περὶ τῶν ἐντὸς παθῶν” 27, etc.:]] —passive [Refs [, of the patient, [prev. work] 26, etc.]]

__2
attend to, study, οὐ δύναμαι ἀκοῦσαι, τοῦτο μελετῶν (i.e. τὸ ἀκοῦσαι) [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 3.115; πλήθους δόξας μεμελετηκώς 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Phaedrus” 260c.]]

__II
pursue, exercise, [μαντείην] [Refs [“hymnus ad Mercurium” 557]]; μ. τοῦτο (i.e. ἡμεροδρόμην εἶναι) [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 6.105]]: frequently in Attic dialect, μ. σοφίαν [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Plutus” 511]]; τέχνας, ῥητορικήν, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Gorgias” 511b, 511c, 448d]]; practise, ἤθη, γαστριμαργίας, ὕβρεις, [Refs [[prev. author] “Phd.” 81e; ὄρχησιν [prev. author] “Lg.” 813e]]; [νόμους] [NT+5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Bacchae” 892 (Lyric poetry); ἀστοῖς ἴσα χρὴ μελετᾶν 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Coloneus” 171 (_anapaest meter_); τὴν τῶν πολεμικῶν ἄσκησιν 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Politica” 1333b39: generally, μ. ἄδικα LXX.Job.27.4; ταῦτα μελέτα NT.1Tim.4.15]]; especially practise speaking, con over a speech in one's mind, λογάρια δύστηνα μελετήσας [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 19.255; ἀπολογίαν [prev. author] 46.1]]; also, deliver, declaim[Refs 2nd c.AD+ [(compare 11.5 b), λόγους 2nd-3rd c.AD: Dio Cassius Historicus 40.54:]] —passive, τὸ ναυτικὸν οὐκ ἐνδέχεται ἐκ παρέργου μελετᾶσθαι naval warfare cannot be practised 'en amateur', [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 1.142]]; εὐταξία μετὰ κινδύνων μελετωμένη discipline put in practice on the battle-field, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. author] 6.72, compare 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 455c.]]

__II.2
with infinitive, μετρίως ἀλγεῖν μελετᾷ σοφία practises moderation in grief, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Fragmenta” 46; λαλεῖν μεμελετήκασί που 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Ecclesiazusae” 119; also μ. τοξεύειν καὶ ἀκοντίζειν 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 1.2.12, compare 5th c.BC: Antipho Orator 3.2.3; μ. ποιεῖν καὶ λέγειν 5th c.BC: Lysias Orator 10.9]]; μ. ἀποθνῄσκειν, τεθνάναι, practise dying, death, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Phaedo” 67e, 81a, compare 4th-3rd c.BC: Epicurus Philosophus “Fragmenta” 470.]]

__II.3
less frequently with participle, μ. κυβερνῶντες [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Respublica Atheniensium” 1.20]]; with ὡς and participle, [Refs [[prev. author] “Cyr.” 5.5.47.]]

__II.4
with preposition, μ. ἔν τινι [LXX.Josh.1.8, +others]

__II.5
absolutely, study, train oneself, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Ecclesiazusae” 164, 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 1.80, 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Historia Graeca (Hellenica)” 3.4.16; ἦν τὸ ἱππικὸν μεμελετηκός [prev. work] 6.4.10]]: with dative modi, τόξῳ μ. καὶ ἀκοντίῳ [Refs [[prev. author] “Cyr.” 2.1.21]]; ἐν τῷ μὴ μελετῶντι by want of practice, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 1.142.]]

__II.5.b
especially practise oratory, declaim, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Phaedrus” 228b]]; ἐπὶ τῶν καιρῶν μ. extemporize a speech, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 61.43; Ἑλληνιστὶ μ. 1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus “Cicero” 4, compare 2.131a, 2nd c.AD: Lucianus Sophista “Sol.” 6, 2nd-3rd c.AD: Philostratus Sophista “Vitae Sophistarum” 1.24.2, “Anthologia Graeca” 11.145]]; of actors, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Problemata” 904b3.]]

__II.6
in Medicine texts, of disease, threaten, μ. τὴν τοῦ καρκινώματος γένεσιν [Refs 1st c.AD+ [1st-2nd c.AD: Leonidas Medicus cited in 6th c.AD: Aëtius Medicus 16.43: _absolutely_, ἢν κρύβδην μελετήσῃ.. ἡ νοῦσος 2nd c.AD: Aretaeus Medicus “περὶ αἰτιῶν καὶ σημείων χρονίων παθῶν” 2.12]]:—passive, ἀπειλᾷ καὶ μελετᾶται μανία [Refs 4th c.BC+ [7th c.AD: Stephanus Medicus “in Hp.” 1.99 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator, compare 6th c.AD: Aëtius Medicus 16.63.]]

__II.7
with accusative person, exercise, train persons, ἐμελέτησεν [αὐτοὺς] ὡς εἶεν.. [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 8.1.42]]: with infinitive, οὓς ἀναβαίνειν ἐπὶ τοὺς ἵππους μελετᾷ Φείδων [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Mnesimachus Comicus 4.7:]] —passive, μελετώμενοι ὑπ᾽ αὐτῶν τὴν πτῆσιν, of eaglets, [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd-3rd c.AD: Philostratus Sophista “Vita Apollonii” 1.7.]]

__III
Grammars, to be accustomed, with infinitive, μεμελέτηκε τὸ τ ¯ εἰς θ ¯ τρέπεσθαι [Refs 9th c.AD+ [“Anecdota Graeca - MSS. Bibl. Oxon.” 1.66; τὰ μὴ μελετήσανταπάσχεινσυναίρεσιν 9th c.AD: Theognostus Grammaticus “Can.” 145.25.]]

__III.b
in Medicine texts, acquire a habit, μελετησάντων ἐκπίπτειν βραχιόνων [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd c.AD: Galenus Medicus 14.782]]:— passive, become chronic, μελετηθὲν τὸ πάθος [Refs 6th c.AD+ [6th c.AD: Aëtius Medicus 16.67.]]

μέλῐ, τό,
genitive ῐτος, etc.; dative μέλι [Refs 5th c.BC+ [3rd c.BC: Philoxenus Epigrammaticus 3.17; _genitive_ _plural_ μελίτων 5th c.BC: Empedocles Poeta Philosophus 128.7 (nisi to be read μελιτῶν, compare μελιτόν)]]:—honey, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 20.69, etc.; μ. χλωρόν 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 11.631, 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 10.234, 6th c.BC: Xenophanes Poeta Philosophus 38.1; ξανθόν 4th-5th c.BC: Simonides Lyricus 47; παμφαές 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Persae” 612; τὸ μέλι τἀττικόν 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Pax” 252, compare 4th-3rd c.BC: Menander Comicus 708; various kinds, 4th-3rd c.BC: Theophrastus Philosophus “Fragmenta” 190]]; said to be made from the palm (φοῖνιξ), [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.193, compare 4.194; μ. θανάτου σύμβολον 3rd c.AD: Porphyrius Tyrius Philosophus “de Antro Nympharum - Porphyrii Opuscula” 18.]]

__2
in comparisons, of anything sweet, especially of eloquence, μέλιτος γλυκίων ῥέεν αὐδή [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 1.249, compare 5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “O.” 10 (11). 98; Σοφοκλέους τοῦ μέλιτι κεχριμένου 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Fragmenta” 581; ὕπνος γλυκίων μέλιτος 2nd c.BC: Moschus Bucolicus 2.3; ἡ τῶν ἀνδρῶν [χολή] ἐστι πρὸς ἐκείνην μέλι 2nd c.AD: Alexander Rhetor 146.6: proverbial μήτε μοι μ. μήτε μέλισσα]], of those who refuse to take 'the rough with the smooth', [Refs 7th c.BC+ [7th-6th c.BC: Sappho Lyrica 113.]]

__II
sweet gum collected from certain trees, manna, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Mirabilia” 831b23; τὸ ὕον μ. 2nd c.AD: Polyaenus Historicus 4.3.32]]; μ. ἄγριον, μαινόμενον, [Refs 1st c.BC+ [1st c.BC: Diodorus Siculus Historicus 19.94, 1st c.BC-1st c.AD: Strabo Geographus 12.3.18]]. (Cf. Gothic milip, Latin mel.)
