deep_entry:
Abbott-Smith / STEPBible (TBESG)
μέλλω,
[in LXX: Job.3:8 (עָתִיד) 19:25 (אַחֲרוֹן); elsewhere for fut., and frequently in Wi, II, 4Mac ;]
to be about to be or do;
__1. with inf. (Bl., §62, 4; 68, 2; M, Pr., 114);
__(a) of intending or being about to do of  one's own free will: with inf. praes., Mat.2:13, Luk.10:1, Act.3:3 5:35, Heb.8:5, 2Pe.1:12 (Field, Notes, 240), al.; with inf. aor. (Bl., §58, 3), Act.12:6, Rev.3:16;
__(b) of compulsion, necessity or certainty: with inf. praes., Mat.16:27, Luk.9:31, Jhn.6:71, Rom.4:24, al.; with inf. aor., Rom.8:18, Gal.3:23, Rev.3:2 12:4.
__2. Ptcp., ὁ μέλλων: absol., Rom.8:38, 1Co.3:22; τὰ μ., Col.2:17; εἰς τὸ μ. (Field, Notes, 65); with subst., Mat.3:7 12:32 (ὁ αἰὼν ὁ μ.; LXX for עַד), Act.24:25, 1Ti.4:8, Heb.2:5, al.
(AS)

---

LSJ / STEPBible (TFLSJ)
μέλλω,
imperfect ἔμελλον and ἤμελλον (see. below), Epic dialect μέλλον [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 17.278, 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 1.232, 9.378, 5th c.BC: Bacchylides Lyricus 12.164]]; Epic dialect, Ionic dialect μέλλεσκον [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [3rd c.BC: Theocritus Poeta Bucolicus 25.240, 2nd c.BC: Moschus Bucolicus 2.109]]: future μελλήσω [NT+4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 6.15, NT.Matt.24.6]]: aorist ἐμέλλησα [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 3.55, 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Historia Graeca (Hellenica)” 5.4.65, etc., and ἠμ- (see. below)]]:—passive and middle, see below see.—Only present and imperfect in [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Homerus Epicus, 8th-7th c.BC: Hesiodus Epicus]], Lyric poetry, and Trag.: aorist only in Prose (except [Refs 6th c.BC+ [6th c.BC: Theognis Elegiacus, see below): the]]imperfect ἤμελλον with long augment is established by the metre in [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th-7th c.BC: Hesiodus Epicus “Theogonia” 898, 6th c.BC: Theognis Elegiacus 906, 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Ecclesiazusae” 597, “Ra.” 1038 (both _anapaest meter_), 3rd c.BC: Apollonius Rhodius Epicus 1.1309 (cf. Scholia (at [prev. work])), 3rd c.BC: Callimachus Epicus “Hymnus in Delum” 58]]: aorist 1 ἠμέλλησα [Refs 6th c.BC+ [6th c.BC: Theognis Elegiacus 259]]; ἤμελλον is not found in earlier Attic dialect Inscrr., but occurs in Papyrus, as [Refs 5th c.BC+ [“PPetr.” 2p.146 (3rd c.BC), 1st c.BC: Philodemus Gadarensis Epigrammaticus “Rh.” 1.145 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus (but ἔμελλον 4th c.BC: Hyperides Orator “adv. Athenogenem” 7, 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Ἀθηναίων Πολιτεία” 25.3).]]

__I
to be destined or likely to, indicating an estimated certainty or strong probability in the present, past, or future (cf. Aristonic. cited in [Refs 8th c.BC+ [Scholia 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 10.326, 11.817, 16.46, +others): a. with]]present infinitive (or its equivalent), of a probability in the present, ὅθι που μέλλουσιν ἄριστοι βουλὰς βουλεύειν where belike the best are holding counsel, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 10.326]]; ᾧ μέλλεις εὔχεσθαι to whom thou doubtless prayest, [Refs [11.364]]; μέλλεις δὲ σὺ ἴδμεναι doubtless thou knowest, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 4.200]]; τὰ δὲ μέλλετ᾽ ἀκουέμεν belike you have heard it, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 14.125, compare 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 4.94; οὕτω που Διὶ μέλλει ὑπερμενέϊ φίλον εἶναι 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 2.116]]; ὄλβον δὲ θεοὶ μέλλουσιν ὀπάζειν methinks it is the gods who give wealth, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 18.19]]; εἰ δ᾽ οὕτω τοῦτ᾽ ἐστίν, ἐμοὶ μέλλει φίλον εἶναι you may be sure it is my good pleasure, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 1.564. b. with]]aorist infinitive, of a probability in the past, μέλλω που ἀπεχθέσθαι Διὶ πατρί I must have become hateful to father Zeus, [Refs [21.83]]; κελευσέμεναι δέ σ᾽ ἔμελλε δαίμων a god must surely have bidden thee, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 4.274]]; πολλάκι που μέλλεις ἀρήμεναι you must often have prayed, [Refs [22.322]]; μέλλω ἀθανάτους ἀλιτέσθαι I must have sinned against the immortals, [Refs [4.377]]; ἄλλοτε δή ποτε μᾶλλον ἐρωῆσαι πολέμοιο μέλλω at any other time rather than this I may have drawn back.., [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 13.777]]; μέλλει μέν πού τις καὶ φίλτερον ἄλλον ὀλέσσαι before now, no doubt, a man has lost.., [Refs 8th c.BC+ [24.46, compare 18.362; τοῦ δ᾽ ἤδη μέλλουσι κύνες ταχέες τ᾽ οἰωνοὶ ῥινὸν ἀπ᾽ ὀστεόφιν ἐρύσαι 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 14.133]]; of a destiny in the past, ἔμελλεν οἷ αὐτῷ θάνατον.. λιτέσθαι he was fated to have been praying for his own death, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 16.46]]; ἐπεὶ οὐκ ἄρ᾽ ἔμελλον ἑταίρῳ κτεινομένῳ ἐπαμῦναι since I was (i.e. am) not destined to have succoured my comrade when they were slaying him, [Refs [18.98: with]]present infinitive, οὐκ ἄρ᾽ ἔμελλες ἀνάλκιδος ἀνδρὸς ἑταίρους ἔδμεναι he was to turn out no helpless man whose comrades you ate, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 9.475. with with]]future infinitive, of a destin y or probability in the future, ἅ οὐ τελέεσθαι ἔμελλον which were not to be accomplished, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 2.36]]; τάχα δ᾽ ἀνστήσεσθαι ἔμελλεν[Refs 8th c.BC+ [[prev. work] 694; ἐπεὶ οὐκ ἄρ᾽ ἔμελλον ἔγωγε νοστήσας οἶκόνδε.. εὐφρανέειν ἄλοχον 5.686, compare 12.113, 22.356, 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 13.293, 384; μέλλον ἔτι ξυνέσεσθαι ὀϊζυῖ πολλῇ 7.270]]; περὶ τρίποδος γὰρ ἔμελλον θεύσεσθαι they were to have run.., [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 11.700, compare 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Hercules Furens” 463; χρόνῳ ἔμελλέ σ᾽ Ἕκτωρ.. ἀποφθίσειν 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Ajax” 1027; ἔμελλον ἄρα παύσειν ποθ᾽ ὑμᾶς τοῦ κοάξ 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Ranae” 268; φεύγει; ἔμελλόν σ᾽ ἆρα κινήσειν ἐγώ [prev. author] “Nu.” 1301, compare “V.” 460, “Pl.” 103, “Ach.” 347: with]]present infinitive, καὶ γὰρ ἐγώ ποτ᾽ ἔμελλον ἐν ἀνδράσιν ὄλβιος εἶναι I had a chance of being, might have been.., [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 18.138; μέλλεν ποτὲ οἶκος ὅδ᾽ ἀφνειὸς καὶ ἀμύμων ἔμμεναι, ὄφρ᾽ ἔτι κεῖνος ἀνὴρ ἐπιδήμιος ἦεν 1.232]]: with aorist infinitive [Refs 4th c.BC+ [compare(below 11), οὐδεὶς ἂν οὐδὲ μελλήσειε γενέσθαι ἀγαθός 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Ethica Nicomachea” 1105b11: with]]infinitive understood, [τὰ μὲν] πάσχουσι, τὰ δὲ μέλλουσι [πάσχειν] [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Persae” 814]]; ἀλλ᾽ οὐχ οὑμὸς τοῦτο πέπονθεν βίος οὐ μὰ Δί᾽ οὐδέ γε μέλλει no, not likely! [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Plutus” 551; οὐδὲν.. οὔτε ἐπάθετε οὔτε ἐμελλήσατε 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 3.55; οὔτ᾽ ἐμὲ ἀπέφηνεν ἡ βουλὴ οὔτ᾽ ἐμέλλησεν 4th-3rd c.BC: Dinarchus Orator 1.49.]]

__I.d
in εἰ clauses, εἰ μέλλει πόλις εἶναι if it is to be a city, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Protagoras” 324e: with]]future infinitive, εἰ ἐμέλλομεν.. ἀνοίσειν if we were to refer.., [Refs [[prev. author] “Phd.” 75b]]: with aorist infinitive, εἰ μέλλομεν.. δηλῶσαι [Refs [[prev. author] “Lg.” 713a, compare “Smp.” 184d, “Plt.” 268d, +others]]: so in participle, τὴν μέλλουσαν οἰκήσεσθαι πόλιν καλῶς [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Politica” 1261a3, etc.]]

__I.e
in final clauses, ξυνεπιμέλεσθαι ᾗ μέλλει ἄριστα ἕξειν, = {ᾗ ἄριστα ἕξει}, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 8.39; εἴχομεν ἂν.. ἐπιστάτην λαβεῖν.. ὃς ἔμελλεν.. ποιήσειν 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Apologia” 20b, compare 2nd c.AD: Appianus Historicus “Συριακή” 46, etc.]]

__I.f
in questions, the infinitive being understood, τί οὐ μέλλω (μέλλεις, etc.); why shouldn't I? why is it not likely that I should?, i. e. yes, of course, τὸν υἱὸν ἑόρακας αὐτο; Answ. τί δ᾽ οὐ μέλλω (i.e. ἑορακέναι); of course I have, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Historia Graeca (Hellenica)” 4.1.6]]; τί δ᾽ οὐ μέλλει, εἴπερ γε δρᾷ αὐτ; [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 605c]]; πῶς γὰρ οὐ μέλλε; [Refs [[prev. author] “Phd.” 78b, etc.]]; ἀλλὰ τί μέλλε; what (else) would you expect? i. e. yes, of course, [Refs [[prev. author] “R.” 349d, “Hp.Mi.” 373d.]]

__II
to be about to, in purely temporal sense, with future infinitive, Ἕκτορα δῖον ἔτετμεν ἀδελφεόν, εὖτ᾽ ἄρ᾽ ἔμελλε στρέψεσθ᾽ ἐκ χώρης [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 6.515]]; ὁ μέν μιν ἔμελλε γενείου.. ἁψάμενος λίσσεσθαι (perhaps present infinitive), ὁ δ᾽ αὐχένα μέσσον ἔλασσε [Refs 8th c.BC+ [10.454; ἄλεισον ἀναιρήσεσθαι ἔμελλε 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 22.9, compare 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 23.544, 2.39, 6.52, 393]]; δειπνήσειν μέλλομεν, ἢ τ; [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Aves” 464, compare “Eq.” 931 (Lyric poetry), 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 2.8, etc.: with]]present infinitive, τί μέλλεις δρᾶ; [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Vespae” 1379, “Th.” 215, compare “Ec.” 760, “Ach.” 493, “Av.” 498, +others; μέλλω μαίνεσθαι “Lyrica Alexandrina Adespota” 1.23]]: more rarely with aorist infinitive, παθεῖν [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Prometheus Vinctus” 625; κτανεῖν 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Tyrannus” 967 (nisi to be read κτενεῖν)]]; ἀναλαβεῖν, λιπεῖν, θανεῖν, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Orestes” 292, “Heracl.” 709, “Med.” 393]]; ἀπολέσαι, λαβεῖν, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Aves” 366, “Ach.” 1159 (Lyric poetry); προσθεῖναι 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 3.92; οὐδὲ ἐμέλλησαν οὐδὲ διενοήθησαν ἐνθέσθαι 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 35.19: 2nd c.AD: Phrynichus Atticista 316 wrongly condemns this _construction_]] —The infinitive is sometimes omitted, τὸ μέλλειν ἀγαθά (i.e. πράσσειν or πράξειν) the expectation of good things, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Orestes” 1182, compare “IA” 1118.]]

__III
to be always going to do without ever doing: hence, delay, put off, frequently in Trag. (also in middle μέλλομαι, see infr. IV near the end): in this signification usually followed by present infinitive, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Tyrannus” 678 (Lyric poetry), “OC” 1627, etc.]]; τοὺς ξυμμάχους.. οὐ μελλήσομεν τιμωρεῖν· οἱ δ᾽ οὐκέτι μέλλουσι κακῶς πάσχειν we shall not delay to succour our allies, for their sufferings are not being delayed, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 1.86: frequently with μὴ οὐ, 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Prometheus Vinctus” 627, 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Ajax” 540: with μή, τί μέλλομεν.. μὴ πράσσειν κακ; 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Medea” 1242]]: rarely followed by aorist infinitive, [Refs [[prev. author] “Ph.” 299 (Lyric poetry), “Rh.” 673:]]infinitive is frequently omitted, τί μέλλει; why delayest thou? [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Prometheus Vinctus” 36, compare “Pers.” 407, “Ag.” 908, 1353, 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Fragmenta” 917, 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 8.78, etc.; μακρὰ μ. 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Coloneus” 219 (Lyric poetry); Ἄρης στυγεῖ μέλλοντας 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Heraclidae” 723; ἴωμεν καὶ μὴ μέλλωμεν ἔτι 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Leges” 712b]]; μέλλον τι.. ἔπος a hesitating word, which one hesitates to speak, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Ion” 1002]]; μέλλων σφυγμός a hesitating pulse, [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd c.AD: Galenus Medicus 8.653.]]

__IV
participle μέλλων is used quasi-adjectivally, ὁ μ. χρόνος the future time, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “O.” 10(11).7, 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Prometheus Vinctus” 839, 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Topica” 111b28: Grammars, ὁ μέλλων]] the future tense, [Refs 2nd c.BC+ [2nd c.BC: Dionysius Thrax Grammaticus 638.23, 2nd c.AD: Apollonius Dyscolus Grammaticus “de Syntaxi;” 69.28, etc.]]; ἡ μ. αὐτοῦ δύναμις his future power, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 494c; μ. φυλάξασθαι χρέος 5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “O.” 7.40]]; τὸν μ. βλαστόν (καρπόν codices) [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-3rd c.BC: Theophrastus Philosophus “Historia Plantarum” 4.15.1: especially in _neuter_, τὸ μέλλον, τὰ μέλλοντα]] things to come, the future, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “O.” 2.56, 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Prometheus Vinctus” 102, 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 1.138, 4.71, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Theaetetus” 178e, etc.]]; opposed to to what is simply future (τὸ ἐσόμενον), [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “de Divinatione per Somnia” 463b29, compare “GC” 337b4]]; εἰς τὸ μέλλον (i.e. ἔτος) [NT+1st c.AD+ [NT.Luke.13.9, compare “PLond.” 3.1231.4 (2nd c.AD), 1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus “Caesar” 14:—also in]]middle, τὰ ἰσχυρότατα ἐλπιζόμενα μέλλεται your strongest pleas are hopes in futurity, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 5.111:]] — but

__V
passive μέλλομαι, ὡς μὴ μέλλοιτο τὰ δέοντα that the necessary steps might not be delayed, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 3.1.47]]; ἐν ὅσῳ ταῦτα μέλλεται while these delays are going on, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 4.37:]]future μελλήσομαι uncertain reading in [Refs 6th c.AD+ [6th c.AD: Procopius Caesariensis Historicus “de Bello Gothico” 2.30:]]perfect participle μεμελλημένος, = {μέλλων, σφυγμός} [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd c.AD: Galenus Medicus 9.308.]]

μέλος, -ους, τό
[in LXX chiefly for נֵתַח ;]
a member, limb of the body: 1Co.12:14 12:19 12:26 Eph.4:16 (WH, mg.), Jas.3:5; pl. (as always in cl.), τὰ μ. : Mat.5:29-30, Rom.6:13, 19 7:5, 23 12:4, 1Co.12:12 ff, Col.3:5, Jas.3:6 4:1. Metaphorical, πόρνης, 1Co.6:15; of Christians, μ. ἀλλήλων, Rom.12:5, Eph.4:25; Χριστοῦ, 1Co.6:15; σώματος Χριστοῦ, 1Co.12:27, Eph.5:30.†
(AS)

---

LSJ / STEPBible (TFLSJ)
μέλος, εος, τό,
limb, in early writers always in plural, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 7.131, 5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “N.” 1.47, etc. (κατὰ μέλος is corrupt for κατὰ μέρος in “hymnus ad Mercurium” 419)]]; μελέων ἔντοσθε within my bodily frame, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Persae” 991 (Lyric poetry), compare “Eu.” 265 (Lyric poetry)]]; κατὰ μέλη (-εα) limb by limb, like{μελεϊστί}, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “O.” 1.49, 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.119; τὰ τοῦ σώματος μέλη καὶ μέρη 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Leges” 795e]]; μέλη ποιεῖν dismember, [LXX.2Mac.1.16]: later in singular, [Refs 1st c.BC+ [“Anthologia Graeca” 9.141, 2nd c.AD: Galenus Medicus “de Usu Partium” 12.3, +others; ἡ κατὰ μέλος τομή 1st c.BC-1st c.AD: Strabo Geographus 2.1.30.]]

__2
metaphorically, ἐσμὲν.. ἀλλήλων μέλη [NT.Rom.12.5, cf. NT.1Cor.6.15.]

__3
features, form, οὐκέτ᾽ ἐγὼ.. γονέων μ. ὄψομαι [Refs [“BMus.Inscription” 1077 (from Sudan).]]

__B
especially musical member, phrase: hence, song, strain, first in [Refs [“Hymni Homerici” 19.16 (_plural_)]], of the nightingale (the [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Homerus Epicus word being μολπή),compare 6th c.BC: Theognis Elegiacus 761, etc.; μέλη βοῶν ἄναυλα 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Fragmenta” 699]]; especially of lyric poetry, τὸ Ἀρχιλόχου μ. [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “O.” 9.1]]; ἐν μέλεϊ ποιέειν to write in lyric strain, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 5.95, compare 2.135; ἐν μέλει ἤ τινι ἄλλῳ μέτρῳ 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 607d, compare 1st c.BC: Dionysius Halicarnassensis “de Compositione Verborum” 11; Ἀδμήτου μ. 5th c.BC: Cratinus Comicus 236]]; μέλη, τά, lyric poetry, choral songs, opposed to Epic or Dramatic verse, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 379a, 607a, +others; [μ.] ἐκ τριῶν συγκείμενον, λόγου τε καὶ ἁρμονίας καὶ ῥυθμοῦ [prev. work] 398d.]]

__B.b
lyric portion of the Comic παράβασις, [Refs 7th c.AD+ [7th c.AD: Hephaestio Grammaticus “Poëm.” 8.2.]]

__B.2
music to which a song is set, tune, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Poetica” 1450a14]]; opposed to ῥυθμός, μέτρον, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Gorgias” 502c]]; opposed to ῥυθμός, ῥῆμα, [Refs [[prev. author] “Lg.” 656c]]; Κρητικόν, Καρικόν, Ἰωνικὸν μ., [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Cratinus Comicus 222, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Comicus 69.12, 14: _metaphorically_, ἐν μέλει]] properly, correctly, ἐν μ. φθέγγεσθαι [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Sophista” 227d]]; παρὰ μέλος incorrectly, inopportunely, πὰρ μ. ἔρχομαι [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “N.” 7.69; παρὰ μ. φθέγξασθαι 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Philebus” 28b, “Lg.” 696d; παρὰ μέλος λαμπρύνεσθαι 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Ethica Nicomachea” 1123a22, compare “EE” 1233a39.]]

__B.3
melody of an instrument, φόρμιγξ δ᾽ αὖ φθέγγοιθ᾽ ἱερὸν μ. ἠδὲ καὶ αὐλός [Refs 6th c.BC+ [6th c.BC: Theognis Elegiacus 761; αὐλῶν πάμφωνον μ. 5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “P.” 12.19; πηκτίδων μέλη 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Fragmenta” 241]]: generally, tone, μ. βοῆς [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Electra” 756. [In “hymnus ad Mercurium” 502 θεὸς δ᾽ ὑπὸ καλὸν ἄεισεν must be read for θεὸς δ᾽ ὑπὸ μέλος ἄεισεν, and Ἕλλησιν δ᾽ ᾄδων μέλεα καὶ ἐλέγους]] is corrupt in epigram cited in [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd c.AD: Pausanias Periegeta 10.7.6.]]]

μέλω
[in LXX: Job.22:3 (חֵפֶץ), Tob.10:5, Wis.12:13, 1Ma.14:42-43 * ;]
__1. intrans., to be an object of care, be a care; commonly in third of person(s): with dative of person(s), Act.18:17; very frequently impers., 1Co.7:21; before ὅτι, Mrk.4:38, Luk.10:40; with genitive of thing(s) (as frequently in Att..), 1Co.9:9; before περί, Mat.22:16, Mrk.12:14, Jhn.10:13 12:6, 1Pe.5:7.
__2. Trans., in act. and mid., to care for (not in LXX or NT).†
(AS)

LSJ / STEPBible (TFLSJ)
μέλω,
middle μέλομαι, used in both voices, either in neuter sense, to be an object of care or thought, or in active sense, care for, take an interest in.

__A
present μέλω: imperfect ἔμελον, Epic dialect μέλον [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 5.6:]]future μελήσω, Epic dialect infinitive μελησέμεν [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 10.51:]]aorist ἐμέλησα: perfect μεμέληκ; also Epic dialect and Lyric poetry μέμηλα, Doric dialect participle μεμᾱλώς uncertain in [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “O.” 1.89 (for _Epic dialect_ forms of _middle_ see.below 111.2): almost always _3rd.pers.??]]singular and plural, except in present (see. below):—to be an object of care or thought, sometimes with a personal subject (not in Attic dialect Prose):

__A.I
πᾶσι δόλοισιν ἀνθρώποισι μέλω by all manner of wiles am I in men's thoughts, i. e. am well known to them, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 9.20; Ἀργὼ πᾶσι μέλουσα 12.70; μελήσεις ἄφθιτον ἀνθρώποις αἰὲν ἔχων ὄνομα 6th c.BC: Theognis Elegiacus 245; Εὐθυμίᾳ μέλων εἴην 5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “Fragmenta.” 155; μέλει σφισὶ Καλλιόπα [prev. author] “O.” 10(11).14; ἵνα θανοῦσα νερτέροισιν μέλω 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Andromache” 850 (Lyric poetry); Ἔρως.. οὐρανίδαισι μέλων [prev. author] “Tr.” 842; μέλων πολλοῖσι “Anthologia Graeca” 5.121 (1st c.BC-1st c.AD: Diodorus Epigrammaticus); ἡ μέλουσα ἀγέλη 4th c.AD: Themistius Sophista “Orationes” 1.10a:]]perfect participle, ἀρεταῖσι μεμαλότας dear to virtue, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “O.” 1.89 (uncertain)]]; μέλεγάρ οἱ [Ὀδυσσεύς] [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 5.6; τὸν ξεῖνον δὲ ἐῶμεν... Τηλεμάχῳ μελέμεν 18.420: but more frequently of things, μή τοι ταῦτα... μελόντων]] let not these things weigh on thy soul, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 18.463, 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 13.362; μηδέ τί οἱ θάνατος μελέτω φρεσί 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 24.152]]; σοὶ χρὴ τάδε πάντα μέλειν 'tis good these things should be a care to thee,[Refs 8th c.BC+ [5.490; πόλεμος δ᾽ ἄνδρεσσι μελήσει 6.492; μελήσουσιν δ᾽ ἐμοὶ ἵπποι 5.228; ᾧ τόσσα μέμηλε 2.25; οἷς ὕβρις μέμηλε κακή 8th-7th c.BC: Hesiodus Epicus “Opera et Dies” 238; τοῖσιν.. ἐνὶ φρεσὶν ἄλλα μεμήλει 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 1.151, compare 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 2.614; ὅσα φημὶ μελησέμεν Ἀργείοισι 10.51; ἔλεγε.. κομιδῆς πέρι τὴν ὥρην αὐτῷ μελήσειν 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 8.19; μέλει γὰρ ἀνδρὶ.. τἄξωθεν 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Septem contra Thebas” 200; σοὶ χρὴ μέλειν ἐπιστολάς [prev. author] “Pr.” 3; οὗτος.. δμωσὶν ἂν μέλοι πόνος 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Supplices” 939; ἃ τοῖσιν ἀστοῖς ἔμελεν 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Ecclesiazusae” 459; τοῖσδε μελήσει γάμος 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Electra” 1342 (_anapaest meter_); τοῦτο ἴσασιν ἐμοὶ μεμεληκός 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Apologia Socratis” 20.]]

__I.2
impersonal with infinitive, οὐκ ἔμελέν μοι ταῦτα μεταλλῆσαι [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 16.465; so in 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Agamemnon” 1250, 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 1.141, etc.; also, μοι ἐμέλησεν ὥστε εἰδέναι 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 6.3.19]]: united with the personal construction, οὗτος μητρὶ κηδεύειν μέλει [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Rhesus” 983.]]

__I.3
less frequently with a conjunction, οὐ μέλειν οἱ ὅτι ἀποθνῄσκει [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 9.72]]; σοὶ μελέτω ὅκως.. [Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. author] 1.9, compare 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 1.8.13, etc.; ὡς δὲ καλῶς ἕξει.., ἐμοὶ μελήσει [prev. author] “Cyr.” 3.2.13]]; ἐμοὶ τοῦτο μέλει, μὴ.. [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Philoctetes” 1121 (Lyric poetry)]]; οὐ τοσοῦτόν μοι μέλει εἰ.. [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Lysias Orator 21.12.]]

__I.4
3rd.pers. singular is frequently used impersonal with the object in genitive, and person in dative, ᾧ μέλει μάχας to whom there is care for the battle, who careth for it, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Choephori” 946 (Lyric poetry), compare “Ag.” 974; ἐμοὶ δ᾽ ἔλασσον Ζηνὸς ἢ μηδὲν μέλει [prev. author] “Pr.” 938; θεοῖσιν εἰ δίκης μέλει 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Philoctetes” 1036; Ζηνὶ τῶν σῶν μέλει πόνων 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Heraclidae” 717; πάνυ μοι τυγχάνει μεμεληκὸς τοῦ ᾄσματος 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Protagoras” 339b; also μέλει μοι περί τινος 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Choephori” 780, 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Lysistrata” 502, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus Alcaeus2.150d; μεμέληκέ μοι περὶ αὐτῶν [prev. author] “Cra.” 428b: less frequently with ὑπέρ, εἴπερ ὑπὲρ τοῦ κοινῇ βελτίστου δεῖ μέλειν ὑμῖν 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 21.37.]]

__I.5
absolutely, μηδέ σοι μελησάτω [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Prometheus Vinctus” 334]]; οἶμαι θεοῖς τοῖς κάτω μέλειν, οἳ (nisi to be read οἷς) ἠδίκηνται [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Antipho Orator 1.31.]]

__I.6
frequently with a negative, οὐδέν μοι μέλει I care not, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Ranae” 655; μή νυν μελέτω σοι μηδέν [prev. author] “Pl.” 208; τῷ δ᾽ οὐδὲν μ. 2nd c.AD: Alexander Rhetor 178.2]]; so τί δέ σοι μέλε; [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-3rd c.BC: Diphilus Comicus 73.10.]]

__A.II
μέλον ἔστι periphrastic for μέλει, as τοῖσδ᾽ ἔσται μ. [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Coloneus” 653, compare 1433.]]

__II.2
neuter participle used absolutely, οὐδὲν ἄρ᾽ ἐμοῦ μέλον for they took no thought of me, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Vespae” 1288]]; δῆλον ὅτι οἶσθα, μέλον γέ σοι since you care about it, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Apologia” 24d; οὐδὲν αὐτῷ μ. τοῦ τοιούτου [prev. author] “Phdr.” 235a; μ. αὐτοῖς ἰσχυρῶς ὅπῃ τὸ μέλλον ἀποβήσοιτο 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 5.2.24; οὔτε σκοπούμεναι οὔτε μ. αὐταῖς ἄλλο ἢ χαρίζεσθαι 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Gorgias” 501b.]]

__A.III
middle is used by Poets and in [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Hippocrates Medicus like]]active, μελόμεθα, -ησόμεθα, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Hippocrates Medicus “ἐπιστολαί” 27]]; to be an object of care, Ἄρτεμιν ᾇ μελόμεσθα [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Hippolytus” 60]]: mostly in 3rd.pers. singular, ἐμοὶ δέ κε ταῦτα μελήσεται [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 1.523]]; μή τί τοι ἡγεμόνος γε ποθὴ μελέσθω let it not weigh on thy mind, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 10.505]]; τἀντεῦθεν.. αὐτῷ μελέσθω Λοξίᾳ [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Eumenides” 61; τἀνθάδ᾽ ἂν μέλοιτ᾽ ἐμοί 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Electra” 1436; γάμους.. σοὶ χρὴ μέλεσθαι 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Phoenissae” 759, etc.; ἰαχὰν μελομέναν νεκροῖς [prev. work] 1302]]: rarely impersonal, σοὶ.. μελέσθω φρουρῆσαι [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Electra” 74; μέλεταί τινί τινος 3rd c.BC: Theocritus Poeta Bucolicus 1.53, Oracle texts cited in 2nd c.AD: Lucianus Sophista “Alex.” 24.]]

__III.2
Epic dialect perfect and pluperfect passive μέμβλεται, μέμβλετο (from μέ-μλ-εται, μέ-μλ-ετο), with present and imperfect sense, ἦ νύ τοι οὐκέτι πάγχυ μετὰ φρεσὶ μέμβλετ᾽ Ἀχιλλεύς (for μέλει); [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 19.343]]; μέμβλετο γάρ οἱ τεῖχος (for ἔμελε)[Refs 8th c.BC+ [21.516; φόνος δέ οἱ οὐκ ἐνὶ θυμῷ μέμβλετο 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 22.12; ᾗσιν ἀοιδὴ μέμβλεται ἐν στήθεσσιν 8th-7th c.BC: Hesiodus Epicus “Theogonia” 61: hence later _Epic dialect_ formed a]]present μέμβλομαι, 2nd pers. plural μέμβλεσθε [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [3rd c.BC: Apollonius Rhodius Epicus 2.217]]; 3rd.pers. plural μέμβλονται, in active sense [Refs 5th c.BC+ [compare (5th c.BC: Bacchylides Lyricus 11 below), μ. πόνοισι 2nd-3rd c.AD: Oppianus Anazarbensis Epicus “Halieutica - Poetae Bucolici et Didactici” 4.77: the regular]]perfect and pluperfect (with present and imperfect sense) also occur in later Poets, μεμέληται [Refs 1st c.AD+ [3rd c.AD: Oppianus Apamensis Epicus “Cynegetica” 1.436; Φοίβῳ μεμελήμεθα “Anthologia Graeca” 10.17 (1st c.AD: Antiphilus Epigrammaticus); μεμέληνται Callias Epigrammaticus “anonymous fragment” 119, 3rd c.AD: Oppianus Apamensis Epicus “Cynegetica” 1.349: 2 and 3]]pluperfect μεμέλησο, -το, [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [“Anthologia Graeca” 5.219 (6th c.AD: Agathias Historicus et Epigrammaticus), 3rd c.BC: Theocritus Poeta Bucolicus 17.46]]; participle μεμελημένος, α, ον, cared for, πολλοῖς μεμελημέναι ἡρωῖναι [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [[prev. author] 26.36, compare “Anthologia Graeca” 7.199 (3rd c.BC: Tymnes Epigrammaticus):]]aorist participle passive μεληθέν[Refs [[prev. work] 5.200]]; compare βέβλεσθαι.

__B
with an object, care for, take an interest in a thing, with genitive, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Homerus Epicus only in]]perfect participle, μέγα πλούτοιο μεμηλώς busied with, attending to.., [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 5.708; μέγα πτολέμοιο μεμηλώς 13.297]]: later in present, οὐκ ἔφα τις θεοὺς βροτῶν ἀξιοῦσθαι μέλειν [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Agamemnon” 370 (Lyric poetry); μέλειν μὲν ἡμῶν 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Ajax” 689; δεινόν σε.. τικτούσης μέλειν [prev. author] “El.” 342]]: later with dative, care for, μέλω κύρτοις [Refs 1st c.BC+ [“Anthologia Graeca” 10.10 (1st c.BC: Archias Jun.); θεοῖς μέλοντες 1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus “Sulla” 7]]: absolutely, to be anxious, μέλει.. κέαρ [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Septem contra Thebas” 288, compare “Pers.” 1049 (both Lyric poetry); μελούσῃ καρδίᾳ 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Rhesus” 770.]]

__B.2
rarely with accusative, πεντήκοντα βοῶν ἀντάξια ταῦτα μέμηλας thou hastinvented, [Refs [hymnus ad Mercurium 437]] (perhaps μέμηδας).

__B.3
with _infinitive_, θεοὶ τῶν ἀδίκων μέλουσι (μέλλουσι codices _optative_) [Refs 5th c.BC+ [καὶ τῶν ὁσίων ἐπᾴειν 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Hercules Furens” 773 (assuming variant).]]

__B.II
_middle_ μέλομαι, care for, take care of, with genitive, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Septem contra Thebas” 177 (Lyric poetry), 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Tyrannus” 1466, 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Hippolytus” 109, “Heracl.” 354 (Lyric poetry), 3rd c.BC: Apollonius Rhodius Epicus 1.967]]; τὰ λοιπά μου μέλου (where τὰ λ. is adverbial) [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Coloneus” 1138; μεμελημένοι ἀέθλων 2nd-3rd c.AD: Oppianus Anazarbensis Epicus “Halieutica - Poetae Bucolici et Didactici” 4.101: with _dative_, ἐτητυμίῃ μεμελημένος 3rd c.BC: Callimachus Epicus “Aetia” 3.1.76; ἱππασίῃ μεμελημένον ἦτορ 4th c.AD(?): Quintus Smyrnaeus Epicus 4.500: with _accusative_, μέλομαι ῥόδον (probable reading for μέλπομαι) “Anacreontea” 53.2: with Preps., μέλεσθαι ἀμφί τι or τινος, 3rd c.BC: Apollonius Rhodius Epicus 2.376, 4.491; ἀμφ᾽ αἰγῶν μεμελημένοι “Anthologia Graeca” 6.221 (1st c.AD: Leonidas Alexandrinus Epigrammaticus); ἐμέλοντο περὶ σφίσιν 3rd c.BC: Apollonius Rhodius Epicus 3.1172]]: with infinitive, μέλομαι.. ἀείδειν [Refs 6th c.BC+ [6th c.BC: Anacreon Lyricus 65; μελέσθω λαὸς ἐκπονεῖν ἄκη 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Supplices” 367, compare 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Heraclidae” 96 (Lyric poetry)]]: aorist in same sense, with genitive, τάφου μεληθείς [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Ajax” 1184.]]

LSJ / STEPBible (TFLSJ)
μέμφομαι,
[Refs 6th c.BC+ [6th c.BC: Theognis Elegiacus 797, etc.]]: imperfect ἐμέμφετο [Refs [Batrachomyomachia 70]]: future μέμψομαι [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th-7th c.BC: Hesiodus Epicus “Opera et Dies” 186, etc.]]: aorist ἐμέμφθην [Refs 6th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.77, 3.13, 5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “N.” 11.30 (κατα-), 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Hippolytus” 1402, +others, 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 4.85 (in _passive_ sense, 1st c.AD: Philo Judaeus 1.301, 2nd c.AD: Apollonius Dyscolus Grammaticus “de Syntaxi;” 67.22): but in _Attic dialect_ and Trag. commonly ἐμεμψάμην, as 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Prometheus Vinctus” 1073 (_anapaest meter_), 5th-6th c.BC: Andocides Orator 4.3, 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 1.143, also in 6th c.BC: Mimnermus Lyricus 14.5, 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 2.24]]: present in passive sense, [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [3rd c.AD(?): Diogenes Laertius 6.47, 2nd c.AD: Aspasius Philosophus “in Ethica Nicomachea commentaria - pars” 133.14:]]future μεμφθήσομαι Ps.-[Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-3rd c.BC: Menander Comicus in Meineke “Fragm.Comedy texts Gr.” iv p.337]]:—blame, censure, first in [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th-7th c.BC: Hesiodus Epicus (though ἐπιμέμφομαι occurs in 8th c.BC: Homerus Epicus):]]

__1
with accusative person, μέμψονται δ᾽ ἄρα τούς [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th-7th c.BC: Hesiodus Epicus “Opera et Dies” 186, compare 6th c.BC: Theognis Elegiacus 797, 5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “N.” 7.64, 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Electra” 384, etc.; μ. τύχην 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Prometheus Vinctus” 1073 (_anapaest meter_); μ. τὸν θέντα τὸν νόμον 5th-6th c.BC: Andocides Orator 4.3]]; κατὰ τὸ μαντήϊον οὐκ ὀρθῶς ὁ Κροῖσος μέμφεται (i.e. τὸν Λοξίαν) [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.91; μ. τινὰ πρὸς τοὺς φίλους 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Oeconomicus” 11.23; μ. τινὰ εἴς τι [prev. author] “An.” 2.6.30.]]

__1.b
c.accusative of things, οἶνε, τὰ μέν σ᾽ αἰνῶ, τὰ δὲ μέμφομαι [Refs 6th c.BC+ [6th c.BC: Theognis Elegiacus 873]]; μ. τὴν γνώμην, τὰ δῶρα, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.207, 3.13; μ. τὴν φιλοσοφίαν 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Euthydemus” 305b; ἄλλο οὐδὲν μ. 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 7.6.39; μεμφθεὶς κατὰ τὸ πλῆθος τὸ ἑωυτοῦ στράτευμα 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.77; ταῦτα.. προτ᾽ ἐμὸν θυμὸν ἐμεμψάμαν 3rd c.BC: Theocritus Poeta Bucolicus 30.24.]]

__2
with dative person et accusative of things, impute as blameworthy, cast in one's teeth, [Refs 7th c.BC+ [7th-6th c.BC: Sappho Lyrica “Papyrus fragments” in E. Diehl, 14.7 (probably), 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 3.4, 4.180, 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Nubes” 525, “Av.” 137, 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 1.143, etc.: also with _accusative_ _cognate_, τῷ Λοξίᾳ μέμψιν μ. 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Plutus” 10, etc.]]; μ. τινὶ ὅτι.. [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 9.6, compare 6.92]]; οὕνεκα.. [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Helena” 31]]; εἰ.. [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 4.85: with _dative_ _person_ et _genitive_ _of things_, οὔποτ᾽ ἀνδρὶ τῷδε κηρυκευμάτων μέμψει 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Septem contra Thebas” 652:]] with genitive person et accusative _of things_, ὃ μάλιστα μέμφονται ἡμῶν which is the chief complaint they make against us, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 1.84.]]

__3
with dative person only, to be dissatisfied with, find fault with, [NT+5th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Septem contra Thebas” 560, “Pr.” 63, 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Trachiniae” 470, 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Orestes” 285, “IA” 899 (troch.), 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Memorabilia” 3.5.20, NT.Heb.8.8]]: with participle added, μ. ἡμῖν λογισαμένοις [Refs 5th c.BC+ [2nd c.AD: Lucianus Sophista “Charid.” 20; ὡς κακῶς βουλευομένοις 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Phaedrus” 234b, compare “Cri.” 50d.]]

__4
with genitive of things only, complain of, οὐ μάχης.. μέμψει [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Fragmenta - American Journal of Philology” 199.3; εἴ τι μέμφῃ τῆς ἐμῆς ἀπουσίας 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Hecuba” 962]]; τιμῆς ἐμέμφθη of her [neglected] honour [Refs 8th c.BC+ [compare (εὐχωλῆς ἐπιμέμφεται 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 1.93), 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Hippolytus” 1402; μ. τῶν γεγενημένων 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 8.109.]]

__5
with infinitive with μή, μ. μὴ πολλάκις βουλεύεσθαι object that one ought not.., [Refs [[prev. author] 3.42.]]

__6
absolutely, find fault, complain, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Supplices” 137 (Lyric poetry); ὅτι 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Ethica Nicomachea” 1162b18. in Law, οἱ μεμφόμενοι]] the plaintiffs, [Refs [“GDI” 4998 (from Gortyn).]]

μεμψῐ-μοιρος, ον,
faultfinding, criticizing, querulous, [NT+5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Isocrates Orator 12.8, 4th-3rd c.BC: Theophrastus Philosophus “Characteres” 17.2, 1st c.BC: Philodemus Philosophus “περὶ παρρησίας” p.42 O., NT.Jude.16, 2nd c.AD: Lucianus Sophista “Tim.” 13, etc.; τὸ μ. 1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus 2.50b]]: comparative, γυνὴ ἀνδρὸς -ότερον [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Historia Animalium” 608b10.]]

Abbott-Smith / STEPBible (TBESG)
μέν,
conjunctive particle (originally a form of μήν), usually related to a following δέ or other adversative conjunction, and distinguishing the word or clause with which it stands from that which follows.
It is generally untranslatable and is not nearly so frequent in NT as in cl. Like δέ, it never stands first in a clause.
__1. Answered by δέ or some other particle: μὲν . . . δέ, indeed . . . but, Mat.3:11, Luk.3:16, al.; with pronouns, ὃς μὲν . . . ὃς δέ, one . . . another, Mat.21:35, al.; pl., Php.1:16, 17; ὃ μὲν . . . ὃ δὲ . . . ὃ δέ, some . . . some . . . some, Mat.13:8; τοῦτο μὲν . . . τοῦτο δέ, partly . . . partly, Heb.10:33; μὲν . . . ἔπειτα, Jhn.11:6; μὲν . . . καί, Luk.8:5.

__2. μέν solitarium, answered by no other particle: πρῶτον μέν (Bl., l.with), Rom.1:8 3:2, 1Co.11:18; μὲν οὖν in narrative, summing up what precedes or introducing something further (Bl., §78, 5), so then, rather, nay rather: Luk.11:28 (WH, μενοῦν), Act.1:6 9:31, al.; μὲν οὖν γε (Php.3:8, WH): see: μενοῦνγε.
(AS)

LSJ / STEPBible (TFLSJ)
μέν,
Particle, used partly to express certainty on the part of the speaker or writer; partly, and more commonly, to point out that the word or clause with which it stands is correlative to another word or clause that is to follow, the latter word or clause being introduced by δέ.

__A

__A.I
μέν used absolutely to express certainty, not followed by correlative δέ, indeed, of a truth, synonymous with μήν, as appears from the Epic dialect and Ionic dialect form ἦ μέν in protestations and oaths (where Attic dialect used ἦ μήν), καί μοι ὄμοσσον, ἦ μ. μοι πρόφρων ἔπεσιν καὶ χερσὶν ἀρήξειν [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 1.77, compare 14.275; ἦ μέν τοι τάδε πάντα τελείεται 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 14.160, compare 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 24.416; τοῦτον ἐξορκοῖ, ἦ μέν οἱ διηκονήσειν 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 4.154, compare 5.93, etc.: with _negative_, οὐ μὲν γάρ τι κακὸν βασιλευέμεν 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 1.392, etc.; ὤμοσα, μὴ μὲν.. ἀναφῆναι 4.254, compare 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 2.118, 179; ἔξαρνος ἦν, μὴ μὲν ἀποκτεῖναι [prev. author] 3.67, compare 99: without _negative_, ἀνδρὸς μὲν τόδε σῆμα πάλαι κατατεθνηῶτος 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 7.89]]: also in Trag., ἀκτὴ μὲν ἥδε τῆς περιρρύτου χθονός [Refs 8th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Philoctetes” 1, compare 159 (_anapaest meter_), “OC” 44, 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Medea” 676, 1129, etc.; καὶ μέν 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 1.269, 9.632, etc.; οὐδὲ μὲν οὐδὲ.. 2.703, 12.212]]; γε μέν, compare γε [Refs [1.5.]]

__A.I.2
an answering clause with δέ is sometimes implied, τὴν μὲν ἐγὼ σπουδῇ δάμνημ᾽ ἐπέεσσι her can I hardly subdue, [but all others easily], [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 5.893]]; ὡς μὲν λέγουσι as indeed they say, [but as I believe not], [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Orestes” 8]]; καὶ πρῶτον μὲν ἦν αὐτῷ πόλεμος (with no ἔπειτα δέ to follow), [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 1.9.14]]; so νῦν μέν σ᾽ ἀφήσω I will let you go this time, [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [3rd c.BC: Herodas Mimographus 5.81]]: to give force to assertions made by a person respecting himself, wherein opposition to other persons is implied, ὡς μὲν ἐμῷ θυμῷ δοκεῖ [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 13.154]]; δοκεῖν μέν μοι ἥξει τήμερον [τὸ πλοῖον] [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Crito” 43d]]: hence with the person pronoun, ἐγὼ μέν νυν θεοῖσι ἔχω χάριν [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.71]]; ἐγὼ μὲν οὐδέν (i.e. θέλω) [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Antigone” 498; ἐμοῦ μὲν οὐχ ἑκόντος [prev. author] “Aj.” 455; ἐγὼ μὲν οὐκ οἶδα 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 1.4.12, compare 4.2.45, etc.]]: with the demonstrative pronoun, τούτου μὲν τοῦ ἀνθρώπου ἐγὼ σοφώτερός εἰμι [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Apologia” 21d: generally, to emphasize the preceding word, πολλὴ μὲν ἡ μεταβολή μοι γέγονεν]] great indeed has been the change, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Isaeus Orator 1.1, compare 4th-5th c.BC: Simonides Lyricus 5.1, etc.]]

__A.I.3
μέν is used alone in questions, when the answer is assumed, I take it, θέμις μὲν ἡμᾶς χρησμὸν εἰδέναι θεο; [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Medea” 676, compare “Ion” 520 (troch.), “Hipp.” 316, 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Antigone” 634, 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Aves” 1214]]; Ἕλλην μέν ἐστι καὶ Ἑλληνίζε; [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Meno” 82b.]]

__A.II
μέν followed by δέ in the correlative clause or clauses, on the one hand, on the other hand; commonly in Classical Gr., less frequently in later Gr. (rare in NT

__A.II.1
μέν.., δέ.. (or when the correlative clause is negative, μέν.., οὐδέ.., [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 1.318, 536)]], to mark opposition, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Homerus Epicus, etc.]]—The opposed clauses commonly stand together, but are frequently separated by clauses, parenthetic or explanatory; e.g. μέν in [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 2.494 is answered by δέ in 511, 527f]]; in [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 1.9.2, πρῶτον μέν is answered by ἐπεὶ δέ]] in  6; in [prev. author] “Mem.” 1.1.2, πρῶτον μέν is answered by θαυμαστὸν δέ in 1.2.1.]]

__A.II.2
to connect a series of clauses containing different matter, though with no opposition, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 1.18s q., 306f (five δέ-clauses), 433f (eight δέ-clauses),compare 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 1.3.14, 7.10s q.: frequently when the members of a group or class are distinctly specified, παῖδες δύο, πρεσβύτερος μὲν Ἀρταξέρξης, νεώτερος δὲ Κῦρος [prev. work] 1.1.1; τάφρος.., τὸ μὲν εὖρος ὀργυιαὶ πέντε, τὸ δὲ βάθος ὀργυιαὶ τρεῖς [prev. work] 1.7.14; πρῶτος μέν.., δεύτερος δέ.., τρίτος δέ.. [prev. work] 5.6.9]]; τότε μέν.., τότε δέ.., at one time.., at another.., [Refs [[prev. work] 6.1.9, etc.: especially with the _Article_ used as a _pronoun_,]] ὁ μέν.., ὁ δέ..; τὸ μέν.., τὸ δέ.., etc.

__A.II.3
the principal word is frequently repeated, οἳ περὶ μὲν βουλὴν Δαναῶν, περὶ δ᾽ ἐστὲ μάχεσθαι [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 1.258, compare 288, 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 15.70; ἔνι μὲν φιλότης, ἐν δ᾽ ἵμερος, ἐν δ᾽ ὀαριστύς 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 14.216; Ξέρξης μὲν ἄγαγεν.., Ξέρξης δ᾽ ἀπώλεσεν 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Persae” 550, compare 560, 694, 700 (all Lyric poetry)]]; χαλεπαίνει μὲν πρῳρεύς, χαλεπαίνει δὲ κυβερνήτης [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 5.8.20.]]

__A.II.4
one of the correlative clauses is sometimes independent, while the other takes the participle or some other dependent form, ἐβλασφήμει κατ᾽ ἐμοῦ.., μάρτυρα μὲν.. οὐδένα παρασχόμενος.., παρεκελεύετο δέ.. [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 57.11; οἱ ἀμφὶ βασιλέα, πεζοὶ μὲν οὐκέτι, τῶν δὲ ἱππέων ὁ λόφος ἐνεπλήσθη 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 1.10.12, compare 2.1.7, 5.6.29; ὧν ἐπιμεμφομένα σ᾽ ἁδεῖα μὲν ἀντία δ᾽ οἴσω 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Trachiniae” 123, compare “OC” 522 (bothlyr.); χωρὶς μὲν τοῦ ἐστερῆσθαι.., ἔτι δὲ καὶ.. δόξω ἀμελῆσαι 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Crito” 44]] b.

__A.II.5
μέν and δέ frequently oppose two clauses, whereof one is subordinate to the other in meaning or emphasis, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [ἀλλ᾽ ἐκεῖνο θαυμάζω, εἰ Λακεδαιμονίοις μέν ποτε.. ἀντήρατε,.. νυνὶ δὲ ὀκνεῖτ᾽ ἐξιέναι (for εἰ.. ἀντάραντες νυνὶ ὀκνεῖτε) 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 2.24, compare 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Iphigenia Taurica” 116, 5th c.BC: Lysias Orator 34.11, 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Memorabilia” 2.7.11, etc.]]: so in an anacoluthon, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [τρία μὲν ὄντα.. ναυτικά.., τούτων δ᾽ εἰ περιόψεσθε τὰ δύο, κτλ., 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 1.36.]]

__A.II.6
μέν is not always answered by δέ, but frequently by other equivalent Particles, as ἀλλά, Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 1.22f, 2.703f, 5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “O.” 9.1, 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Persae” 176, 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 1.7.17:—by μέντοι, 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.36, 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Philoctetes” 350, 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 21.189, etc.:—by ἀτάρ, 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 6.84, 124, 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Prometheus Vinctus” 342, 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Tyrannus” 1051s q., 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Theaetetus” 172c, etc. (so μέν.., αὐτάρ]] in Epic dialect, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 1.50, 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 19.513, etc.):— by αὖ, 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 11.108, 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 4.210:—by αὖθις, 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Antigone” 165:—by αὖτε, 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 1.234, 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 22.5:—by temporal Particles, πρῶτα μέν.., εἶτα.. 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Electra” 261]]; πρῶτον μέν.., μετὰ τοῦτο.. [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 6.1.5 - 7]]; μάλιστα μὲν δὴ.., ἔπειτα μέντοι.. [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Philoctetes” 350, compare “OT” 647:]] —rarely by μήν with negative, οὐδὲν μὴν κωλύει [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Phaedrus” 268e; οὐ μὴν αὐταί γε [prev. author] “Phlb.” 12d.]]

__A.II.6.b
when the opposition is emphatic, δέ is sometimes strengthened, as ὅμως δέ.. [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Tyrannus” 785, “Ph.” 473, 1074, etc. (so ἀλλ᾽ ὅμως “El.” 450)]]; δ᾽ αὖ.. [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 4.415, 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 1.10.5]]; δ᾽ ἔμπης.. [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 1.561 - 2.]]

__A.II.6.c
μέν is sometimes answered by a copulative Particle, κάρτιστοι μὲν ἔσαν καὶ καρτίστοις ἐμάχοντο[Refs 8th c.BC+ [[prev. work] 267, compare 459, 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 22.475, 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Ajax” 1, “Tr.” 689, 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Medea” 125 (_anapaest meter_)]], etc.: rarely in Prose, τρία μὲν ἔτη ἀντεῖχον.., καὶ οὐ πρότερον ἐνέδοσαν [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 2.65 (uncertain).]]

__B
μέν before other Particles:

__B.I
where each Particle retains its force,

__B.I.1
μὲν ἄρα, in [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Homerus Epicus μέν ῥα, 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 2.1, 6.312, 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 1.127, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Phaedrus” 258d, “R.” 467d, etc.]]

__B.I.2
μὲν γάρ [Refs 8th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Tyrannus” 62, 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 1.142, etc.:— in 8th c.BC: Homerus Epicus]] there is frequently no second clause, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 1.173, 392, compare 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Tyrannus” 1062, etc.; μὲν γὰρ δή 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 11.825; μὲν γάρ τε 17.727.]]

__B.I.3
μέν γε, when a general statement is explained in detail, Κορινθίοις μέν γε ἔνσπονδοί ἐστε [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 1.40, compare 70, 6.86, 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 6.46, 5th c.BC: Antipho Orator 5.14, 5th c.BC: Lysias Orator 13.27, 4th c.BC: Isaeus Orator 4.8, 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Nubes” 1382, “V.” 564, 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Fragmenta” 909.4.]]

__B.I.4
μὲν δή [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 1.514, 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.32, etc.]]: frequently used to express positive certainty, ἀλλ᾽ οἶσθα μὲν δή [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Trachiniae” 627, compare “OT” 294; τὰ μὲν δὴ τόξ᾽ ἔχεις [prev. author] “Ph.” 1308]]; especially as a conclusion, τοῦτο μὲν δὴ.. ὁμολογεῖται [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Gorgias” 470b, compare 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 1.1.6, etc.]]: in closing a statement, τοιαῦτα μὲν δὴ ταῦτα [Refs 8th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Prometheus Vinctus” 500, etc.: used in answers to convey full assent, ἦ μὲν δή (compare supr. A) 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 9.348, 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 4.33; καὶ μὲν δή.. γε 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 409b]]; οὐ μὲν δή, to deny positively, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 8.238, 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 1.6.9, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Theaetetus” 148e, etc.; οὐ μὲν δή.. γε 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 2.2.3, 3.2.14]]; ἀλλ᾽ οὔ τι μὲν δή.. [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Theaetetus” 187a.]]

__B.I.5
μὲν οὖν, see below 11.2.

__B.II
where the Particles combine so as to form a new sense,

__B.II.1
μέν γε at all events, at any rate (not in Trag.), τοῦτο μέν γ᾽ ἤδη σαφές [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Acharnenses” 154, compare “Nu.” 1172, “Lys.” 1165, “Ra.” 80, 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 3.39; μέν γέ που 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 559b, “Tht.” 147a.]]

__B.II.2
μὲν οὖν is frequently used with a corresponding δέ, so that each Particle retains its force, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 4.780, 5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “O.” 1.111, 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Tyrannus” 244, 843; “Ph.” 359, 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 2.5, etc.]]: but frequently also absolutely, so then, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Antigone” 65; ταῦτα μὲν οὖν παραλείψω 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 2.3]]; especially in replies, sometimes in strong affirmation, παντάπασι μὲν οὖν [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Theaetetus” 158d; κομιδῇ μὲν οὖν [prev. work] 159e; πάνυ μὲν οὖν [prev. work] 159b; ἀνάγκη μὲν οὖν [prev. work] 189e]]; also to substitute a new statement so as to correct a preceding statement, nay rather, κακοδαίμω; Answ. βαρυδαίμων μὲν οὖν! [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Ecclesiazusae” 1102]]; μου πρὸς τὴν κεφαλὴν ἀποψῶ wipe your nose on my head: Answ. ἐμοῦ μὲν οὖν.. nay on mine, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. author] “Eq.” 911, compare 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Persae” 1032 (Lyric poetry), “Ag.” 1090 (Lyric poetry), 1396, 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Ajax” 1363, “El.” 1503, “OT” 705, 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Ranae” 241, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Crito” 44b, “Grg.” 466a, 470b, “Prt.” 309d, etc.; also μὲν οὖν δή 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Trachiniae” 153; καὶ δὴ μὲν οὖν [prev. author] “OC” 31]]; compare οὐμενοῦν: in  “NT” μενοῦν and μενοῦνγε", to begin a sentence, yea rather, [NT+5th c.BC+ [NT.Luke.11.28, NT.Rom.9.20, etc., compare 2nd c.AD: Phrynichus Atticista 322, 5th c.AD(?): Hesychius Legal icographus —In _Ionic dialect_, μέν νυν is used for μὲν οὖν, 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.18, 4.145, etc.]]

__B.II.3
by μέν τε, if δέ τε follows, the two clauses are more closely combined than by τε.., τε.., [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 5.139, +others; μέν τε is frequently answered by δέ alone, 16.28, +others]]; by ἀλλά, αὐτάρ,[Refs 8th c.BC+ [17.727, 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 1.215, +others]]; perhaps by ἠδέ, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 4.341:— 8th c.BC: Homerus Epicus also uses μέν τε]] absolutely, when τε loses its force, as after ἦ, τίς, etc., [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 2.145, +others]]

__B.II.4
μέν τοι in [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Homerus Epicus]] always occurs in speeches, where τοι can be regarded as the dative of the pronoun: later, μέντοι is written as a single word, and is used:

__B.II.4.a
with a conjunctive force, yet, nevertheless, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Prometheus Vinctus” 320, 1054 (_anapaest meter_), 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Trachiniae” 413, etc.]]; and sometimes stands for δέ, answering to μέν, see above [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus 11.6 a.]]

__B.II.4.b
as an  adverb, in strong protestations, οὐ μέντοι μὰ Δία[Refs 4th c.BC+ [.. 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 4.49]]; in eager or positive assent, of course, φαμέν τι εἶναι..; Answ. φαμὲν μέντοι νὴ Δία [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Phaedo” 65d, +others: with a _negative_ to give emphasis to a question, οὐ σὺ μέντοι..]]; why, are you not.. ? [Refs [[prev. author] “Prt.” 309a, compare “Phdr.” 229b, “R.” 339b, etc.: sometimes to express impatience, ὄμνυμι γάρ σοι—τίνα μέντοι, τίνα θεῶ; [prev. author] “Phdr.” 236d]]; τί μ. πρῶτον ἦν, τί πρῶτον ἦ; nay what was the first? [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Nubes” 787; οὗτος, σὲ λέγω μ. [prev. author] “Ra.” 171]]; σὺ μέντοι.. [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd c.AD: Lucianus Sophista “Alex.” 44: with _imperative_, to enforce the command, τουτὶ μ. σὺ φυλάττου]] only take heed.., [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Pax” 1100, compare “Av.” 661, 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 1.4.8: in answers, γελοῖον μέντἂν εἴη]] nay it would be absurd, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Theaetetus” 158e]]; summing up a long temporal clause, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Andocides Orator 1.130.]]

__B.II.4.c
μέντοι γε [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 5.5.24, etc.; οὐ μ. γε 5th c.BC: Diogenes Apolloniates Philosophus 5: in later Gr. μέντοιγε]] stands first in the sentence, μ. οὐ θέλω [Refs 1st c.AD+ [“PLond.” 3.897.13 (1st c.AD)]]; also γε μέντοι [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Agamemnon” 938, 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Tyrannus” 778, 1292, 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Hecuba” 600; ὅμως γε μ. 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Ranae” 61.]]

__B.II.4.d
καὶ μ. καί is used to add a point to be noted, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [1st c.AD(?): Heraclitus 28, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 331d]]; also καί.. μ., νῦν σοι καιρός ἐστιν ἐπιδείξασθαι τὴν παιδείαν, καὶ φυλάξασθαι μέντοι.. and of course to take care.., [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 4.6.15 (variant), compare 1.8.20, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Protagoras” 339c, “Tht.” 143a.]]

__B.II.4.e
ἀλλὰ μέντοι well, if it comes to that, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 4.6.16]]; well, of course, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 331e, etc.]]; compare μέντον.

__C
for μέν after other Particles, see each Particle.

__D
Position of μέν. Like δέ, it usually stands as the second word in a sentence. But when a sentence begins with words common to its subordinate clauses, μέν stands second in the first of these clauses, as ἥδε γὰρ γυνὴ δούλη μέν, εἴρηκεν δ᾽ ἐλεύθερον λόγον [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Trachiniae” 63]]; οἱ Ἀθηναῖοι ἐτάξαντο μέν.., ἡσύχαζον δέ.. [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 4.73, compare 113, etc. It also attaches itself to words which mark opposition, as πρῶτον μέν, τότε μέν, ἐγὼ μέν]], even when these do not stand first: sometimes however it precedes them, ὡς μὲν ἐγὼ οἶμαι [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Phaedrus” 228b; ὡς μέν τινες ἔφασαν 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 5.2.28]]. It generally stands between the Article and Noun, or the preposition and its Case: but if special stress is laid on the Noun, this is sometimes neglected, as οἱ Τεγεᾶται μὲν ἐπηυλίσαντο, Μαντινῆς δὲ ἀπεχώρησαν [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 4.134]]; ἀνὰ τὸ σκοτεινὸν μέν.. [Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. author] 3.22; also τῇ σῇ μὲν εὐδαιμονίῃ, τῇ ἐμεωυτοῦ δὲ κακοδαιμονίῃ 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.87]].

__D.II
μέν is frequently repeated:

__D.II.1
when, besides the opposition of two main clauses, a subordinate opposition is introduced into the first, ὁ μὲν ἀνὴρ τοιαῦτα μὲν πεποίηκε τοιαῦτα δὲ λέγει, ὑμῶν δέ.. [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 1.6.9, compare 5.8.24, 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 8.104, 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 18.214, 23.208.]]

__D.II.2
in apodosi with the demonstrative pronoun or adverb, τὸν μὲν καλέουσι θέρος, τοῦτον μὲν προσκυνέουσι, τὸν δὲ χειμῶνα[Refs 5th c.BC+ [.. 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 2.121; ὅσοι μὲν δὴ νομοῦ τοῦ Θηβαίου εἰσί, οὗτοι μέν [νυν].. αἶγας θύουσι· ὅσοι δὲ.. νομοῦ τοῦ Μενδησίου εἰσί, οὗτοι δὲ.. ὄϊς θύουσι [prev. work] 42, compare 3.108, +others]]; ὅτε μέν με οἱ ἄρχοντες ἔταττον.., τότε μὲν ἔμενον.., τοῦ δὲ θεοῦ τάττοντος,.. ἐνταῦθα δέ.. [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Apologia” 28e, compare “Grg.” 512a.]]

__D.II.3
μέν used absolutely is frequently followed by a correlative μέν, εἰ μὲν οὖν ἡμεῖς μὲν.. ποιοῦμεν [Refs [[prev. author] “R.” 421a.]]

__D.III
μέν is sometimes omitted (especially in Poetry) where it is implied in the following δέ, φεύγων, ὁ δ᾽ ὄπισθε διώκων [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 22.157; ἐλευθεροῦτε πατρίδ᾽, ἐλευθεροῦτε δὲ παῖδας 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Persae” 403; σφραγῖδε.. χρυσοῦν ἔχουσα τὸν δακτύλιον, ἡ δ᾽ ἑτέρα ἀργυροῦν “IG” 22.1388.45, compare 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Nubes” 396, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Sophista” 221e, 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Poetica” 1447b14, etc.]]

LSJ / STEPBible (TFLSJ)
Included with:  μέν,
Particle, used partly to express certainty on the part of the speaker or writer; partly, and more commonly, to point out that the word or clause with which it stands is correlative to another word or clause that is to follow, the latter word or clause being introduced by δέ.

__A

__A.I
μέν used absolutely to express certainty, not followed by correlative δέ, indeed, of a truth, synonymous with μήν, as appears from the Epic dialect and Ionic dialect form ἦ μέν in protestations and oaths (where Attic dialect used ἦ μήν), καί μοι ὄμοσσον, ἦ μ. μοι πρόφρων ἔπεσιν καὶ χερσὶν ἀρήξειν [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 1.77, compare 14.275; ἦ μέν τοι τάδε πάντα τελείεται 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 14.160, compare 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 24.416; τοῦτον ἐξορκοῖ, ἦ μέν οἱ διηκονήσειν 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 4.154, compare 5.93, etc.: with _negative_, οὐ μὲν γάρ τι κακὸν βασιλευέμεν 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 1.392, etc.; ὤμοσα, μὴ μὲν.. ἀναφῆναι 4.254, compare 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 2.118, 179; ἔξαρνος ἦν, μὴ μὲν ἀποκτεῖναι [prev. author] 3.67, compare 99: without _negative_, ἀνδρὸς μὲν τόδε σῆμα πάλαι κατατεθνηῶτος 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 7.89]]: also in Trag., ἀκτὴ μὲν ἥδε τῆς περιρρύτου χθονός [Refs 8th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Philoctetes” 1, compare 159 (_anapaest meter_), “OC” 44, 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Medea” 676, 1129, etc.; καὶ μέν 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 1.269, 9.632, etc.; οὐδὲ μὲν οὐδὲ.. 2.703, 12.212]]; γε μέν, compare γε [Refs [1.5.]]

__A.I.2
an answering clause with δέ is sometimes implied, τὴν μὲν ἐγὼ σπουδῇ δάμνημ᾽ ἐπέεσσι her can I hardly subdue, [but all others easily], [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 5.893]]; ὡς μὲν λέγουσι as indeed they say, [but as I believe not], [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Orestes” 8]]; καὶ πρῶτον μὲν ἦν αὐτῷ πόλεμος (with no ἔπειτα δέ to follow), [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 1.9.14]]; so νῦν μέν σ᾽ ἀφήσω I will let you go this time, [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [3rd c.BC: Herodas Mimographus 5.81]]: to give force to assertions made by a person respecting himself, wherein opposition to other persons is implied, ὡς μὲν ἐμῷ θυμῷ δοκεῖ [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 13.154]]; δοκεῖν μέν μοι ἥξει τήμερον [τὸ πλοῖον] [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Crito” 43d]]: hence with the person pronoun, ἐγὼ μέν νυν θεοῖσι ἔχω χάριν [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.71]]; ἐγὼ μὲν οὐδέν (i.e. θέλω) [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Antigone” 498; ἐμοῦ μὲν οὐχ ἑκόντος [prev. author] “Aj.” 455; ἐγὼ μὲν οὐκ οἶδα 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 1.4.12, compare 4.2.45, etc.]]: with the demonstrative pronoun, τούτου μὲν τοῦ ἀνθρώπου ἐγὼ σοφώτερός εἰμι [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Apologia” 21d: generally, to emphasize the preceding word, πολλὴ μὲν ἡ μεταβολή μοι γέγονεν]] great indeed has been the change, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Isaeus Orator 1.1, compare 4th-5th c.BC: Simonides Lyricus 5.1, etc.]]

__A.I.3
μέν is used alone in questions, when the answer is assumed, I take it, θέμις μὲν ἡμᾶς χρησμὸν εἰδέναι θεο; [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Medea” 676, compare “Ion” 520 (troch.), “Hipp.” 316, 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Antigone” 634, 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Aves” 1214]]; Ἕλλην μέν ἐστι καὶ Ἑλληνίζε; [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Meno” 82b.]]

__A.II
μέν followed by δέ in the correlative clause or clauses, on the one hand, on the other hand; commonly in Classical Gr., less frequently in later Gr. (rare in NT

__A.II.1
μέν.., δέ.. (or when the correlative clause is negative, μέν.., οὐδέ.., [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 1.318, 536)]], to mark opposition, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Homerus Epicus, etc.]]—The opposed clauses commonly stand together, but are frequently separated by clauses, parenthetic or explanatory; e.g. μέν in [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 2.494 is answered by δέ in 511, 527f]]; in [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 1.9.2, πρῶτον μέν is answered by ἐπεὶ δέ]] in  6; in [prev. author] “Mem.” 1.1.2, πρῶτον μέν is answered by θαυμαστὸν δέ in 1.2.1.]]

__A.II.2
to connect a series of clauses containing different matter, though with no opposition, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 1.18s q., 306f (five δέ-clauses), 433f (eight δέ-clauses),compare 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 1.3.14, 7.10s q.: frequently when the members of a group or class are distinctly specified, παῖδες δύο, πρεσβύτερος μὲν Ἀρταξέρξης, νεώτερος δὲ Κῦρος [prev. work] 1.1.1; τάφρος.., τὸ μὲν εὖρος ὀργυιαὶ πέντε, τὸ δὲ βάθος ὀργυιαὶ τρεῖς [prev. work] 1.7.14; πρῶτος μέν.., δεύτερος δέ.., τρίτος δέ.. [prev. work] 5.6.9]]; τότε μέν.., τότε δέ.., at one time.., at another.., [Refs [[prev. work] 6.1.9, etc.: especially with the _Article_ used as a _pronoun_,]] ὁ μέν.., ὁ δέ..; τὸ μέν.., τὸ δέ.., etc.

__A.II.3
the principal word is frequently repeated, οἳ περὶ μὲν βουλὴν Δαναῶν, περὶ δ᾽ ἐστὲ μάχεσθαι [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 1.258, compare 288, 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 15.70; ἔνι μὲν φιλότης, ἐν δ᾽ ἵμερος, ἐν δ᾽ ὀαριστύς 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 14.216; Ξέρξης μὲν ἄγαγεν.., Ξέρξης δ᾽ ἀπώλεσεν 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Persae” 550, compare 560, 694, 700 (all Lyric poetry)]]; χαλεπαίνει μὲν πρῳρεύς, χαλεπαίνει δὲ κυβερνήτης [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 5.8.20.]]

__A.II.4
one of the correlative clauses is sometimes independent, while the other takes the participle or some other dependent form, ἐβλασφήμει κατ᾽ ἐμοῦ.., μάρτυρα μὲν.. οὐδένα παρασχόμενος.., παρεκελεύετο δέ.. [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 57.11; οἱ ἀμφὶ βασιλέα, πεζοὶ μὲν οὐκέτι, τῶν δὲ ἱππέων ὁ λόφος ἐνεπλήσθη 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 1.10.12, compare 2.1.7, 5.6.29; ὧν ἐπιμεμφομένα σ᾽ ἁδεῖα μὲν ἀντία δ᾽ οἴσω 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Trachiniae” 123, compare “OC” 522 (bothlyr.); χωρὶς μὲν τοῦ ἐστερῆσθαι.., ἔτι δὲ καὶ.. δόξω ἀμελῆσαι 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Crito” 44]] b.

__A.II.5
μέν and δέ frequently oppose two clauses, whereof one is subordinate to the other in meaning or emphasis, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [ἀλλ᾽ ἐκεῖνο θαυμάζω, εἰ Λακεδαιμονίοις μέν ποτε.. ἀντήρατε,.. νυνὶ δὲ ὀκνεῖτ᾽ ἐξιέναι (for εἰ.. ἀντάραντες νυνὶ ὀκνεῖτε) 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 2.24, compare 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Iphigenia Taurica” 116, 5th c.BC: Lysias Orator 34.11, 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Memorabilia” 2.7.11, etc.]]: so in an anacoluthon, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [τρία μὲν ὄντα.. ναυτικά.., τούτων δ᾽ εἰ περιόψεσθε τὰ δύο, κτλ., 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 1.36.]]

__A.II.6
μέν is not always answered by δέ, but frequently by other equivalent Particles, as ἀλλά, Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 1.22f, 2.703f, 5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “O.” 9.1, 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Persae” 176, 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 1.7.17:—by μέντοι, 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.36, 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Philoctetes” 350, 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 21.189, etc.:—by ἀτάρ, 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 6.84, 124, 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Prometheus Vinctus” 342, 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Tyrannus” 1051s q., 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Theaetetus” 172c, etc. (so μέν.., αὐτάρ]] in Epic dialect, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 1.50, 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 19.513, etc.):— by αὖ, 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 11.108, 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 4.210:—by αὖθις, 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Antigone” 165:—by αὖτε, 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 1.234, 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 22.5:—by temporal Particles, πρῶτα μέν.., εἶτα.. 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Electra” 261]]; πρῶτον μέν.., μετὰ τοῦτο.. [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 6.1.5 - 7]]; μάλιστα μὲν δὴ.., ἔπειτα μέντοι.. [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Philoctetes” 350, compare “OT” 647:]] —rarely by μήν with negative, οὐδὲν μὴν κωλύει [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Phaedrus” 268e; οὐ μὴν αὐταί γε [prev. author] “Phlb.” 12d.]]

__A.II.6.b
when the opposition is emphatic, δέ is sometimes strengthened, as ὅμως δέ.. [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Tyrannus” 785, “Ph.” 473, 1074, etc. (so ἀλλ᾽ ὅμως “El.” 450)]]; δ᾽ αὖ.. [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 4.415, 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 1.10.5]]; δ᾽ ἔμπης.. [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 1.561 - 2.]]

__A.II.6.c
μέν is sometimes answered by a copulative Particle, κάρτιστοι μὲν ἔσαν καὶ καρτίστοις ἐμάχοντο[Refs 8th c.BC+ [[prev. work] 267, compare 459, 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 22.475, 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Ajax” 1, “Tr.” 689, 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Medea” 125 (_anapaest meter_)]], etc.: rarely in Prose, τρία μὲν ἔτη ἀντεῖχον.., καὶ οὐ πρότερον ἐνέδοσαν [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 2.65 (uncertain).]]

__B
μέν before other Particles:

__B.I
where each Particle retains its force,

__B.I.1
μὲν ἄρα, in [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Homerus Epicus μέν ῥα, 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 2.1, 6.312, 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 1.127, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Phaedrus” 258d, “R.” 467d, etc.]]

__B.I.2
μὲν γάρ [Refs 8th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Tyrannus” 62, 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 1.142, etc.:— in 8th c.BC: Homerus Epicus]] there is frequently no second clause, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 1.173, 392, compare 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Tyrannus” 1062, etc.; μὲν γὰρ δή 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 11.825; μὲν γάρ τε 17.727.]]

__B.I.3
μέν γε, when a general statement is explained in detail, Κορινθίοις μέν γε ἔνσπονδοί ἐστε [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 1.40, compare 70, 6.86, 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 6.46, 5th c.BC: Antipho Orator 5.14, 5th c.BC: Lysias Orator 13.27, 4th c.BC: Isaeus Orator 4.8, 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Nubes” 1382, “V.” 564, 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Fragmenta” 909.4.]]

__B.I.4
μὲν δή [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 1.514, 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.32, etc.]]: frequently used to express positive certainty, ἀλλ᾽ οἶσθα μὲν δή [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Trachiniae” 627, compare “OT” 294; τὰ μὲν δὴ τόξ᾽ ἔχεις [prev. author] “Ph.” 1308]]; especially as a conclusion, τοῦτο μὲν δὴ.. ὁμολογεῖται [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Gorgias” 470b, compare 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 1.1.6, etc.]]: in closing a statement, τοιαῦτα μὲν δὴ ταῦτα [Refs 8th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Prometheus Vinctus” 500, etc.: used in answers to convey full assent, ἦ μὲν δή (compare supr. A) 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 9.348, 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 4.33; καὶ μὲν δή.. γε 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 409b]]; οὐ μὲν δή, to deny positively, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 8.238, 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 1.6.9, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Theaetetus” 148e, etc.; οὐ μὲν δή.. γε 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 2.2.3, 3.2.14]]; ἀλλ᾽ οὔ τι μὲν δή.. [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Theaetetus” 187a.]]

__B.I.5
μὲν οὖν, see below 11.2.

__B.II
where the Particles combine so as to form a new sense,

__B.II.1
μέν γε at all events, at any rate (not in Trag.), τοῦτο μέν γ᾽ ἤδη σαφές [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Acharnenses” 154, compare “Nu.” 1172, “Lys.” 1165, “Ra.” 80, 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 3.39; μέν γέ που 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 559b, “Tht.” 147a.]]

__B.II.2
μὲν οὖν is frequently used with a corresponding δέ, so that each Particle retains its force, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 4.780, 5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “O.” 1.111, 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Tyrannus” 244, 843; “Ph.” 359, 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 2.5, etc.]]: but frequently also absolutely, so then, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Antigone” 65; ταῦτα μὲν οὖν παραλείψω 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 2.3]]; especially in replies, sometimes in strong affirmation, παντάπασι μὲν οὖν [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Theaetetus” 158d; κομιδῇ μὲν οὖν [prev. work] 159e; πάνυ μὲν οὖν [prev. work] 159b; ἀνάγκη μὲν οὖν [prev. work] 189e]]; also to substitute a new statement so as to correct a preceding statement, nay rather, κακοδαίμω; Answ. βαρυδαίμων μὲν οὖν! [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Ecclesiazusae” 1102]]; μου πρὸς τὴν κεφαλὴν ἀποψῶ wipe your nose on my head: Answ. ἐμοῦ μὲν οὖν.. nay on mine, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. author] “Eq.” 911, compare 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Persae” 1032 (Lyric poetry), “Ag.” 1090 (Lyric poetry), 1396, 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Ajax” 1363, “El.” 1503, “OT” 705, 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Ranae” 241, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Crito” 44b, “Grg.” 466a, 470b, “Prt.” 309d, etc.; also μὲν οὖν δή 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Trachiniae” 153; καὶ δὴ μὲν οὖν [prev. author] “OC” 31]]; compare οὐμενοῦν: in  “NT” μενοῦν and μενοῦνγε", to begin a sentence, yea rather, [NT+5th c.BC+ [NT.Luke.11.28, NT.Rom.9.20, etc., compare 2nd c.AD: Phrynichus Atticista 322, 5th c.AD(?): Hesychius Legal icographus —In _Ionic dialect_, μέν νυν is used for μὲν οὖν, 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.18, 4.145, etc.]]

__B.II.3
by μέν τε, if δέ τε follows, the two clauses are more closely combined than by τε.., τε.., [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 5.139, +others; μέν τε is frequently answered by δέ alone, 16.28, +others]]; by ἀλλά, αὐτάρ,[Refs 8th c.BC+ [17.727, 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 1.215, +others]]; perhaps by ἠδέ, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 4.341:— 8th c.BC: Homerus Epicus also uses μέν τε]] absolutely, when τε loses its force, as after ἦ, τίς, etc., [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 2.145, +others]]

__B.II.4
μέν τοι in [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Homerus Epicus]] always occurs in speeches, where τοι can be regarded as the dative of the pronoun: later, μέντοι is written as a single word, and is used:

__B.II.4.a
with a conjunctive force, yet, nevertheless, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Prometheus Vinctus” 320, 1054 (_anapaest meter_), 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Trachiniae” 413, etc.]]; and sometimes stands for δέ, answering to μέν, see above [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus 11.6 a.]]

__B.II.4.b
as an  adverb, in strong protestations, οὐ μέντοι μὰ Δία[Refs 4th c.BC+ [.. 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 4.49]]; in eager or positive assent, of course, φαμέν τι εἶναι..; Answ. φαμὲν μέντοι νὴ Δία [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Phaedo” 65d, +others: with a _negative_ to give emphasis to a question, οὐ σὺ μέντοι..]]; why, are you not.. ? [Refs [[prev. author] “Prt.” 309a, compare “Phdr.” 229b, “R.” 339b, etc.: sometimes to express impatience, ὄμνυμι γάρ σοι—τίνα μέντοι, τίνα θεῶ; [prev. author] “Phdr.” 236d]]; τί μ. πρῶτον ἦν, τί πρῶτον ἦ; nay what was the first? [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Nubes” 787; οὗτος, σὲ λέγω μ. [prev. author] “Ra.” 171]]; σὺ μέντοι.. [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd c.AD: Lucianus Sophista “Alex.” 44: with _imperative_, to enforce the command, τουτὶ μ. σὺ φυλάττου]] only take heed.., [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Pax” 1100, compare “Av.” 661, 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 1.4.8: in answers, γελοῖον μέντἂν εἴη]] nay it would be absurd, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Theaetetus” 158e]]; summing up a long temporal clause, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Andocides Orator 1.130.]]

__B.II.4.c
μέντοι γε [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 5.5.24, etc.; οὐ μ. γε 5th c.BC: Diogenes Apolloniates Philosophus 5: in later Gr. μέντοιγε]] stands first in the sentence, μ. οὐ θέλω [Refs 1st c.AD+ [“PLond.” 3.897.13 (1st c.AD)]]; also γε μέντοι [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Agamemnon” 938, 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Tyrannus” 778, 1292, 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Hecuba” 600; ὅμως γε μ. 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Ranae” 61.]]

__B.II.4.d
καὶ μ. καί is used to add a point to be noted, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [1st c.AD(?): Heraclitus 28, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 331d]]; also καί.. μ., νῦν σοι καιρός ἐστιν ἐπιδείξασθαι τὴν παιδείαν, καὶ φυλάξασθαι μέντοι.. and of course to take care.., [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 4.6.15 (variant), compare 1.8.20, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Protagoras” 339c, “Tht.” 143a.]]

__B.II.4.e
ἀλλὰ μέντοι well, if it comes to that, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 4.6.16]]; well, of course, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 331e, etc.]]; compare μέντον.

__C
for μέν after other Particles, see each Particle.

__D
Position of μέν. Like δέ, it usually stands as the second word in a sentence. But when a sentence begins with words common to its subordinate clauses, μέν stands second in the first of these clauses, as ἥδε γὰρ γυνὴ δούλη μέν, εἴρηκεν δ᾽ ἐλεύθερον λόγον [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Trachiniae” 63]]; οἱ Ἀθηναῖοι ἐτάξαντο μέν.., ἡσύχαζον δέ.. [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 4.73, compare 113, etc. It also attaches itself to words which mark opposition, as πρῶτον μέν, τότε μέν, ἐγὼ μέν]], even when these do not stand first: sometimes however it precedes them, ὡς μὲν ἐγὼ οἶμαι [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Phaedrus” 228b; ὡς μέν τινες ἔφασαν 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 5.2.28]]. It generally stands between the Article and Noun, or the preposition and its Case: but if special stress is laid on the Noun, this is sometimes neglected, as οἱ Τεγεᾶται μὲν ἐπηυλίσαντο, Μαντινῆς δὲ ἀπεχώρησαν [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 4.134]]; ἀνὰ τὸ σκοτεινὸν μέν.. [Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. author] 3.22; also τῇ σῇ μὲν εὐδαιμονίῃ, τῇ ἐμεωυτοῦ δὲ κακοδαιμονίῃ 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.87]].

__D.II
μέν is frequently repeated:

__D.II.1
when, besides the opposition of two main clauses, a subordinate opposition is introduced into the first, ὁ μὲν ἀνὴρ τοιαῦτα μὲν πεποίηκε τοιαῦτα δὲ λέγει, ὑμῶν δέ.. [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 1.6.9, compare 5.8.24, 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 8.104, 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 18.214, 23.208.]]

__D.II.2
in apodosi with the demonstrative pronoun or adverb, τὸν μὲν καλέουσι θέρος, τοῦτον μὲν προσκυνέουσι, τὸν δὲ χειμῶνα[Refs 5th c.BC+ [.. 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 2.121; ὅσοι μὲν δὴ νομοῦ τοῦ Θηβαίου εἰσί, οὗτοι μέν [νυν].. αἶγας θύουσι· ὅσοι δὲ.. νομοῦ τοῦ Μενδησίου εἰσί, οὗτοι δὲ.. ὄϊς θύουσι [prev. work] 42, compare 3.108, +others]]; ὅτε μέν με οἱ ἄρχοντες ἔταττον.., τότε μὲν ἔμενον.., τοῦ δὲ θεοῦ τάττοντος,.. ἐνταῦθα δέ.. [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Apologia” 28e, compare “Grg.” 512a.]]

__D.II.3
μέν used absolutely is frequently followed by a correlative μέν, εἰ μὲν οὖν ἡμεῖς μὲν.. ποιοῦμεν [Refs [[prev. author] “R.” 421a.]]

__D.III
μέν is sometimes omitted (especially in Poetry) where it is implied in the following δέ, φεύγων, ὁ δ᾽ ὄπισθε διώκων [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 22.157; ἐλευθεροῦτε πατρίδ᾽, ἐλευθεροῦτε δὲ παῖδας 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Persae” 403; σφραγῖδε.. χρυσοῦν ἔχουσα τὸν δακτύλιον, ἡ δ᾽ ἑτέρα ἀργυροῦν “IG” 22.1388.45, compare 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Nubes” 396, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Sophista” 221e, 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Poetica” 1447b14, etc.]]
