LSJ / STEPBible (TFLSJ)
Included with:  μέν,
Particle, used partly to express certainty on the part of the speaker or writer; partly, and more commonly, to point out that the word or clause with which it stands is correlative to another word or clause that is to follow, the latter word or clause being introduced by δέ.

__A

__A.I
μέν used absolutely to express certainty, not followed by correlative δέ, indeed, of a truth, synonymous with μήν, as appears from the Epic dialect and Ionic dialect form ἦ μέν in protestations and oaths (where Attic dialect used ἦ μήν), καί μοι ὄμοσσον, ἦ μ. μοι πρόφρων ἔπεσιν καὶ χερσὶν ἀρήξειν [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 1.77, compare 14.275; ἦ μέν τοι τάδε πάντα τελείεται 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 14.160, compare 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 24.416; τοῦτον ἐξορκοῖ, ἦ μέν οἱ διηκονήσειν 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 4.154, compare 5.93, etc.: with _negative_, οὐ μὲν γάρ τι κακὸν βασιλευέμεν 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 1.392, etc.; ὤμοσα, μὴ μὲν.. ἀναφῆναι 4.254, compare 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 2.118, 179; ἔξαρνος ἦν, μὴ μὲν ἀποκτεῖναι [prev. author] 3.67, compare 99: without _negative_, ἀνδρὸς μὲν τόδε σῆμα πάλαι κατατεθνηῶτος 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 7.89]]: also in Trag., ἀκτὴ μὲν ἥδε τῆς περιρρύτου χθονός [Refs 8th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Philoctetes” 1, compare 159 (_anapaest meter_), “OC” 44, 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Medea” 676, 1129, etc.; καὶ μέν 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 1.269, 9.632, etc.; οὐδὲ μὲν οὐδὲ.. 2.703, 12.212]]; γε μέν, compare γε [Refs [1.5.]]

__A.I.2
an answering clause with δέ is sometimes implied, τὴν μὲν ἐγὼ σπουδῇ δάμνημ᾽ ἐπέεσσι her can I hardly subdue, [but all others easily], [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 5.893]]; ὡς μὲν λέγουσι as indeed they say, [but as I believe not], [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Orestes” 8]]; καὶ πρῶτον μὲν ἦν αὐτῷ πόλεμος (with no ἔπειτα δέ to follow), [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 1.9.14]]; so νῦν μέν σ᾽ ἀφήσω I will let you go this time, [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [3rd c.BC: Herodas Mimographus 5.81]]: to give force to assertions made by a person respecting himself, wherein opposition to other persons is implied, ὡς μὲν ἐμῷ θυμῷ δοκεῖ [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 13.154]]; δοκεῖν μέν μοι ἥξει τήμερον [τὸ πλοῖον] [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Crito” 43d]]: hence with the person pronoun, ἐγὼ μέν νυν θεοῖσι ἔχω χάριν [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.71]]; ἐγὼ μὲν οὐδέν (i.e. θέλω) [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Antigone” 498; ἐμοῦ μὲν οὐχ ἑκόντος [prev. author] “Aj.” 455; ἐγὼ μὲν οὐκ οἶδα 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 1.4.12, compare 4.2.45, etc.]]: with the demonstrative pronoun, τούτου μὲν τοῦ ἀνθρώπου ἐγὼ σοφώτερός εἰμι [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Apologia” 21d: generally, to emphasize the preceding word, πολλὴ μὲν ἡ μεταβολή μοι γέγονεν]] great indeed has been the change, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Isaeus Orator 1.1, compare 4th-5th c.BC: Simonides Lyricus 5.1, etc.]]

__A.I.3
μέν is used alone in questions, when the answer is assumed, I take it, θέμις μὲν ἡμᾶς χρησμὸν εἰδέναι θεο; [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Medea” 676, compare “Ion” 520 (troch.), “Hipp.” 316, 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Antigone” 634, 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Aves” 1214]]; Ἕλλην μέν ἐστι καὶ Ἑλληνίζε; [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Meno” 82b.]]

__A.II
μέν followed by δέ in the correlative clause or clauses, on the one hand, on the other hand; commonly in Classical Gr., less frequently in later Gr. (rare in NT

__A.II.1
μέν.., δέ.. (or when the correlative clause is negative, μέν.., οὐδέ.., [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 1.318, 536)]], to mark opposition, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Homerus Epicus, etc.]]—The opposed clauses commonly stand together, but are frequently separated by clauses, parenthetic or explanatory; e.g. μέν in [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 2.494 is answered by δέ in 511, 527f]]; in [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 1.9.2, πρῶτον μέν is answered by ἐπεὶ δέ]] in  6; in [prev. author] “Mem.” 1.1.2, πρῶτον μέν is answered by θαυμαστὸν δέ in 1.2.1.]]

__A.II.2
to connect a series of clauses containing different matter, though with no opposition, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 1.18s q., 306f (five δέ-clauses), 433f (eight δέ-clauses),compare 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 1.3.14, 7.10s q.: frequently when the members of a group or class are distinctly specified, παῖδες δύο, πρεσβύτερος μὲν Ἀρταξέρξης, νεώτερος δὲ Κῦρος [prev. work] 1.1.1; τάφρος.., τὸ μὲν εὖρος ὀργυιαὶ πέντε, τὸ δὲ βάθος ὀργυιαὶ τρεῖς [prev. work] 1.7.14; πρῶτος μέν.., δεύτερος δέ.., τρίτος δέ.. [prev. work] 5.6.9]]; τότε μέν.., τότε δέ.., at one time.., at another.., [Refs [[prev. work] 6.1.9, etc.: especially with the _Article_ used as a _pronoun_,]] ὁ μέν.., ὁ δέ..; τὸ μέν.., τὸ δέ.., etc.

__A.II.3
the principal word is frequently repeated, οἳ περὶ μὲν βουλὴν Δαναῶν, περὶ δ᾽ ἐστὲ μάχεσθαι [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 1.258, compare 288, 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 15.70; ἔνι μὲν φιλότης, ἐν δ᾽ ἵμερος, ἐν δ᾽ ὀαριστύς 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 14.216; Ξέρξης μὲν ἄγαγεν.., Ξέρξης δ᾽ ἀπώλεσεν 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Persae” 550, compare 560, 694, 700 (all Lyric poetry)]]; χαλεπαίνει μὲν πρῳρεύς, χαλεπαίνει δὲ κυβερνήτης [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 5.8.20.]]

__A.II.4
one of the correlative clauses is sometimes independent, while the other takes the participle or some other dependent form, ἐβλασφήμει κατ᾽ ἐμοῦ.., μάρτυρα μὲν.. οὐδένα παρασχόμενος.., παρεκελεύετο δέ.. [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 57.11; οἱ ἀμφὶ βασιλέα, πεζοὶ μὲν οὐκέτι, τῶν δὲ ἱππέων ὁ λόφος ἐνεπλήσθη 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 1.10.12, compare 2.1.7, 5.6.29; ὧν ἐπιμεμφομένα σ᾽ ἁδεῖα μὲν ἀντία δ᾽ οἴσω 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Trachiniae” 123, compare “OC” 522 (bothlyr.); χωρὶς μὲν τοῦ ἐστερῆσθαι.., ἔτι δὲ καὶ.. δόξω ἀμελῆσαι 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Crito” 44]] b.

__A.II.5
μέν and δέ frequently oppose two clauses, whereof one is subordinate to the other in meaning or emphasis, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [ἀλλ᾽ ἐκεῖνο θαυμάζω, εἰ Λακεδαιμονίοις μέν ποτε.. ἀντήρατε,.. νυνὶ δὲ ὀκνεῖτ᾽ ἐξιέναι (for εἰ.. ἀντάραντες νυνὶ ὀκνεῖτε) 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 2.24, compare 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Iphigenia Taurica” 116, 5th c.BC: Lysias Orator 34.11, 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Memorabilia” 2.7.11, etc.]]: so in an anacoluthon, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [τρία μὲν ὄντα.. ναυτικά.., τούτων δ᾽ εἰ περιόψεσθε τὰ δύο, κτλ., 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 1.36.]]

__A.II.6
μέν is not always answered by δέ, but frequently by other equivalent Particles, as ἀλλά, Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 1.22f, 2.703f, 5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “O.” 9.1, 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Persae” 176, 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 1.7.17:—by μέντοι, 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.36, 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Philoctetes” 350, 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 21.189, etc.:—by ἀτάρ, 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 6.84, 124, 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Prometheus Vinctus” 342, 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Tyrannus” 1051s q., 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Theaetetus” 172c, etc. (so μέν.., αὐτάρ]] in Epic dialect, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 1.50, 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 19.513, etc.):— by αὖ, 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 11.108, 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 4.210:—by αὖθις, 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Antigone” 165:—by αὖτε, 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 1.234, 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 22.5:—by temporal Particles, πρῶτα μέν.., εἶτα.. 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Electra” 261]]; πρῶτον μέν.., μετὰ τοῦτο.. [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 6.1.5 - 7]]; μάλιστα μὲν δὴ.., ἔπειτα μέντοι.. [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Philoctetes” 350, compare “OT” 647:]] —rarely by μήν with negative, οὐδὲν μὴν κωλύει [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Phaedrus” 268e; οὐ μὴν αὐταί γε [prev. author] “Phlb.” 12d.]]

__A.II.6.b
when the opposition is emphatic, δέ is sometimes strengthened, as ὅμως δέ.. [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Tyrannus” 785, “Ph.” 473, 1074, etc. (so ἀλλ᾽ ὅμως “El.” 450)]]; δ᾽ αὖ.. [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 4.415, 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 1.10.5]]; δ᾽ ἔμπης.. [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 1.561 - 2.]]

__A.II.6.c
μέν is sometimes answered by a copulative Particle, κάρτιστοι μὲν ἔσαν καὶ καρτίστοις ἐμάχοντο[Refs 8th c.BC+ [[prev. work] 267, compare 459, 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 22.475, 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Ajax” 1, “Tr.” 689, 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Medea” 125 (_anapaest meter_)]], etc.: rarely in Prose, τρία μὲν ἔτη ἀντεῖχον.., καὶ οὐ πρότερον ἐνέδοσαν [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 2.65 (uncertain).]]

__B
μέν before other Particles:

__B.I
where each Particle retains its force,

__B.I.1
μὲν ἄρα, in [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Homerus Epicus μέν ῥα, 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 2.1, 6.312, 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 1.127, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Phaedrus” 258d, “R.” 467d, etc.]]

__B.I.2
μὲν γάρ [Refs 8th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Tyrannus” 62, 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 1.142, etc.:— in 8th c.BC: Homerus Epicus]] there is frequently no second clause, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 1.173, 392, compare 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Tyrannus” 1062, etc.; μὲν γὰρ δή 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 11.825; μὲν γάρ τε 17.727.]]

__B.I.3
μέν γε, when a general statement is explained in detail, Κορινθίοις μέν γε ἔνσπονδοί ἐστε [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 1.40, compare 70, 6.86, 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 6.46, 5th c.BC: Antipho Orator 5.14, 5th c.BC: Lysias Orator 13.27, 4th c.BC: Isaeus Orator 4.8, 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Nubes” 1382, “V.” 564, 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Fragmenta” 909.4.]]

__B.I.4
μὲν δή [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 1.514, 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.32, etc.]]: frequently used to express positive certainty, ἀλλ᾽ οἶσθα μὲν δή [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Trachiniae” 627, compare “OT” 294; τὰ μὲν δὴ τόξ᾽ ἔχεις [prev. author] “Ph.” 1308]]; especially as a conclusion, τοῦτο μὲν δὴ.. ὁμολογεῖται [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Gorgias” 470b, compare 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 1.1.6, etc.]]: in closing a statement, τοιαῦτα μὲν δὴ ταῦτα [Refs 8th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Prometheus Vinctus” 500, etc.: used in answers to convey full assent, ἦ μὲν δή (compare supr. A) 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 9.348, 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 4.33; καὶ μὲν δή.. γε 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 409b]]; οὐ μὲν δή, to deny positively, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 8.238, 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 1.6.9, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Theaetetus” 148e, etc.; οὐ μὲν δή.. γε 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 2.2.3, 3.2.14]]; ἀλλ᾽ οὔ τι μὲν δή.. [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Theaetetus” 187a.]]

__B.I.5
μὲν οὖν, see below 11.2.

__B.II
where the Particles combine so as to form a new sense,

__B.II.1
μέν γε at all events, at any rate (not in Trag.), τοῦτο μέν γ᾽ ἤδη σαφές [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Acharnenses” 154, compare “Nu.” 1172, “Lys.” 1165, “Ra.” 80, 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 3.39; μέν γέ που 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 559b, “Tht.” 147a.]]

__B.II.2
μὲν οὖν is frequently used with a corresponding δέ, so that each Particle retains its force, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 4.780, 5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “O.” 1.111, 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Tyrannus” 244, 843; “Ph.” 359, 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 2.5, etc.]]: but frequently also absolutely, so then, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Antigone” 65; ταῦτα μὲν οὖν παραλείψω 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 2.3]]; especially in replies, sometimes in strong affirmation, παντάπασι μὲν οὖν [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Theaetetus” 158d; κομιδῇ μὲν οὖν [prev. work] 159e; πάνυ μὲν οὖν [prev. work] 159b; ἀνάγκη μὲν οὖν [prev. work] 189e]]; also to substitute a new statement so as to correct a preceding statement, nay rather, κακοδαίμω; Answ. βαρυδαίμων μὲν οὖν! [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Ecclesiazusae” 1102]]; μου πρὸς τὴν κεφαλὴν ἀποψῶ wipe your nose on my head: Answ. ἐμοῦ μὲν οὖν.. nay on mine, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. author] “Eq.” 911, compare 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Persae” 1032 (Lyric poetry), “Ag.” 1090 (Lyric poetry), 1396, 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Ajax” 1363, “El.” 1503, “OT” 705, 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Ranae” 241, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Crito” 44b, “Grg.” 466a, 470b, “Prt.” 309d, etc.; also μὲν οὖν δή 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Trachiniae” 153; καὶ δὴ μὲν οὖν [prev. author] “OC” 31]]; compare οὐμενοῦν: in  “NT” μενοῦν and μενοῦνγε", to begin a sentence, yea rather, [NT+5th c.BC+ [NT.Luke.11.28, NT.Rom.9.20, etc., compare 2nd c.AD: Phrynichus Atticista 322, 5th c.AD(?): Hesychius Legal icographus —In _Ionic dialect_, μέν νυν is used for μὲν οὖν, 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.18, 4.145, etc.]]

__B.II.3
by μέν τε, if δέ τε follows, the two clauses are more closely combined than by τε.., τε.., [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 5.139, +others; μέν τε is frequently answered by δέ alone, 16.28, +others]]; by ἀλλά, αὐτάρ,[Refs 8th c.BC+ [17.727, 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 1.215, +others]]; perhaps by ἠδέ, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 4.341:— 8th c.BC: Homerus Epicus also uses μέν τε]] absolutely, when τε loses its force, as after ἦ, τίς, etc., [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 2.145, +others]]

__B.II.4
μέν τοι in [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Homerus Epicus]] always occurs in speeches, where τοι can be regarded as the dative of the pronoun: later, μέντοι is written as a single word, and is used:

__B.II.4.a
with a conjunctive force, yet, nevertheless, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Prometheus Vinctus” 320, 1054 (_anapaest meter_), 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Trachiniae” 413, etc.]]; and sometimes stands for δέ, answering to μέν, see above [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus 11.6 a.]]

__B.II.4.b
as an  adverb, in strong protestations, οὐ μέντοι μὰ Δία[Refs 4th c.BC+ [.. 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 4.49]]; in eager or positive assent, of course, φαμέν τι εἶναι..; Answ. φαμὲν μέντοι νὴ Δία [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Phaedo” 65d, +others: with a _negative_ to give emphasis to a question, οὐ σὺ μέντοι..]]; why, are you not.. ? [Refs [[prev. author] “Prt.” 309a, compare “Phdr.” 229b, “R.” 339b, etc.: sometimes to express impatience, ὄμνυμι γάρ σοι—τίνα μέντοι, τίνα θεῶ; [prev. author] “Phdr.” 236d]]; τί μ. πρῶτον ἦν, τί πρῶτον ἦ; nay what was the first? [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Nubes” 787; οὗτος, σὲ λέγω μ. [prev. author] “Ra.” 171]]; σὺ μέντοι.. [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd c.AD: Lucianus Sophista “Alex.” 44: with _imperative_, to enforce the command, τουτὶ μ. σὺ φυλάττου]] only take heed.., [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Pax” 1100, compare “Av.” 661, 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 1.4.8: in answers, γελοῖον μέντἂν εἴη]] nay it would be absurd, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Theaetetus” 158e]]; summing up a long temporal clause, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Andocides Orator 1.130.]]

__B.II.4.c
μέντοι γε [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 5.5.24, etc.; οὐ μ. γε 5th c.BC: Diogenes Apolloniates Philosophus 5: in later Gr. μέντοιγε]] stands first in the sentence, μ. οὐ θέλω [Refs 1st c.AD+ [“PLond.” 3.897.13 (1st c.AD)]]; also γε μέντοι [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Agamemnon” 938, 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Tyrannus” 778, 1292, 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Hecuba” 600; ὅμως γε μ. 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Ranae” 61.]]

__B.II.4.d
καὶ μ. καί is used to add a point to be noted, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [1st c.AD(?): Heraclitus 28, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 331d]]; also καί.. μ., νῦν σοι καιρός ἐστιν ἐπιδείξασθαι τὴν παιδείαν, καὶ φυλάξασθαι μέντοι.. and of course to take care.., [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 4.6.15 (variant), compare 1.8.20, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Protagoras” 339c, “Tht.” 143a.]]

__B.II.4.e
ἀλλὰ μέντοι well, if it comes to that, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 4.6.16]]; well, of course, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 331e, etc.]]; compare μέντον.

__C
for μέν after other Particles, see each Particle.

__D
Position of μέν. Like δέ, it usually stands as the second word in a sentence. But when a sentence begins with words common to its subordinate clauses, μέν stands second in the first of these clauses, as ἥδε γὰρ γυνὴ δούλη μέν, εἴρηκεν δ᾽ ἐλεύθερον λόγον [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Trachiniae” 63]]; οἱ Ἀθηναῖοι ἐτάξαντο μέν.., ἡσύχαζον δέ.. [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 4.73, compare 113, etc. It also attaches itself to words which mark opposition, as πρῶτον μέν, τότε μέν, ἐγὼ μέν]], even when these do not stand first: sometimes however it precedes them, ὡς μὲν ἐγὼ οἶμαι [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Phaedrus” 228b; ὡς μέν τινες ἔφασαν 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 5.2.28]]. It generally stands between the Article and Noun, or the preposition and its Case: but if special stress is laid on the Noun, this is sometimes neglected, as οἱ Τεγεᾶται μὲν ἐπηυλίσαντο, Μαντινῆς δὲ ἀπεχώρησαν [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 4.134]]; ἀνὰ τὸ σκοτεινὸν μέν.. [Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. author] 3.22; also τῇ σῇ μὲν εὐδαιμονίῃ, τῇ ἐμεωυτοῦ δὲ κακοδαιμονίῃ 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.87]].

__D.II
μέν is frequently repeated:

__D.II.1
when, besides the opposition of two main clauses, a subordinate opposition is introduced into the first, ὁ μὲν ἀνὴρ τοιαῦτα μὲν πεποίηκε τοιαῦτα δὲ λέγει, ὑμῶν δέ.. [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 1.6.9, compare 5.8.24, 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 8.104, 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 18.214, 23.208.]]

__D.II.2
in apodosi with the demonstrative pronoun or adverb, τὸν μὲν καλέουσι θέρος, τοῦτον μὲν προσκυνέουσι, τὸν δὲ χειμῶνα[Refs 5th c.BC+ [.. 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 2.121; ὅσοι μὲν δὴ νομοῦ τοῦ Θηβαίου εἰσί, οὗτοι μέν [νυν].. αἶγας θύουσι· ὅσοι δὲ.. νομοῦ τοῦ Μενδησίου εἰσί, οὗτοι δὲ.. ὄϊς θύουσι [prev. work] 42, compare 3.108, +others]]; ὅτε μέν με οἱ ἄρχοντες ἔταττον.., τότε μὲν ἔμενον.., τοῦ δὲ θεοῦ τάττοντος,.. ἐνταῦθα δέ.. [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Apologia” 28e, compare “Grg.” 512a.]]

__D.II.3
μέν used absolutely is frequently followed by a correlative μέν, εἰ μὲν οὖν ἡμεῖς μὲν.. ποιοῦμεν [Refs [[prev. author] “R.” 421a.]]

__D.III
μέν is sometimes omitted (especially in Poetry) where it is implied in the following δέ, φεύγων, ὁ δ᾽ ὄπισθε διώκων [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 22.157; ἐλευθεροῦτε πατρίδ᾽, ἐλευθεροῦτε δὲ παῖδας 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Persae” 403; σφραγῖδε.. χρυσοῦν ἔχουσα τὸν δακτύλιον, ἡ δ᾽ ἑτέρα ἀργυροῦν “IG” 22.1388.45, compare 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Nubes” 396, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Sophista” 221e, 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Poetica” 1447b14, etc.]]

μένω,
[in LXX for קוּם ,עמד, etc. ;]
to stay, abide, remain.
__1. Intrans.;
__(i) of place: before ἐν, Luk.8:27, al.; παρά, with dative of person(s), Jhn.1:40, al; σύν, Luk.1:56; καθ᾽ ἑαυτόν, Act.28:16; with adv., ἐκεῖ, Mat.10:11; ὧδε, Mat.26:38; metaphorically, 1Jn.2:18; of the Holy Spirit, Jhn.1:32, 33 14:17; of Christ, Jhn.6:56 15:4, al.; ὁ θεός, 1Jn.4:15, conversely, of Christians, Jhn.6:56 15:4, 1Jn.4:15, al.; ὁ λόγος τ. θεοῦ, 1Jn.2:14; ἡ ἀλήθεια, II Jo 2, al.
__(ii) Of time;
__(a) of persons: Php.1:25; before εἰς τ. αἰῶνα, Jhn.12:34, Heb.7:24, 1Jn.2:17; ὀλίγον, Rev.17:10; ἕως ἔρχομαι, Jhn.21:22, 23;
__(b) of things, lasting or enduring: cities, Mat.11:23, Heb.13:14; λόγος θεοῦ, 1Pe.1:23; ἁμαρτία, Jhn.9:41.
__(iii) Of condition: with pred., μόνος, Jhn.12:24; ἄγαμος, 1Co.7:11; πιστός, 2Ti.2:13; ἱερεύς, Heb.7:3; with adv., οὕτως, 1Co.7:40; ὡς κἀγώ, ib. 8; before ἐν, ib. 20, 24.
__2. Trans. (Bl., §34, 1; Field, Notes, 132): with accusative of person(s), Act.20:5, 23 (cf. ἀνα-, δια-, ἐν-, ἐπι-, κατα-, παρα-, συν-παρα-, περι-, προσ-, ὑπο-μένω).

LSJ / STEPBible (TFLSJ)
μένω,
Epic dialect infinitive μενέμεν [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 5.486; 4th c.AD(?): Arcadius Grammaticus]] present participle μίνονσαι [Refs 4th c.BC+ [“Schwyzer” 657.49 (Tegea, 4th c.BC)]]; Epic dialect, Ionic dialect imperfect μένεσκον [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 19.42, 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 4.42]]: Epic dialect, Ionic dialect future μενέω [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 19.308, 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 4.119]]; Attic dialect μενῶ [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Acharnenses” 564, etc.]]: aorist ἔμεινα [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 15.656, etc.]]: perfect μεμένηκα [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 18.321]]; compare μίμνω:—stay, wait:

__I
stand fast, in battle, οὐδ᾽ ἴφθιμοι Λύκιοι μένον, ἀλλὰ φόβηθεν [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 16.659; μενέω καὶ τλήσομαι 11.317]]; φεύγειν μηδὲ μένειν Oracle texts cited in [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.55, compare 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 3.3.45, 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Tyrannus” 295; ἐμπέδως μ. 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Agamemnon” 854; ἀραρότως [prev. author] “Supp.” 945]]; μ. κατὰ χώραν, of soldiers, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 4.26.]]

__I.2
stay at home, stay where one is, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 16.838; ἔντοσθε μένοντες 8th-7th c.BC: Hesiodus Epicus “Theogonia” 598; μ. αὐτοῦ 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 8.62; οἴκοι 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Fragmenta - American Journal of Philology” 317; εἴσω δόμων [prev. author] “Th.” 232; κατ᾽ οἶκον 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Iphigenia Aulidensis” 656; ἐν δόμοις 5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “N.” 3.43, 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Ajax” 80; ἔνδον 4th c.BC: Amphis Comicus 1.3.]]

__I.2.b
lodge, stay, παρὰ ματρί [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “P.” 4.186; πρὸς τοὺς γονέας 5th c.BC: Hippocrates Medicus “ἐπιστολαί” 13; ἐκεῖ 2nd c.BC: Polybius Historicus 30.4.10 codices (perhaps οἴκοι),compare 4th c.AD: Alciphro Epistolographus 3.5.]]

__I.2.c
μ. ἀπὸ ἧς ἀλόχοιο stay away, be absent from.., [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 2.292; ἀπὸ πτολέμοιο 18.64]]: and so absolutely, to be a shirker, ἴση μοῖρα μένοντι καὶ εἰ μάλα τις πολεμίζοι [Refs [9.318.]]

__I.2.d
οἱ μένοντες, opposed to οἱ φεύγοντες (exiles), [Refs [“IG” 12.10.27.]]

__I.3
stay, tarry, ἐς ἠέλιον καταδύντα [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 17.570; μενέουσι, εἰς ὅ κέ περ Τροίην διαπέρσομεν 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 9.45]]; loiter, be idle,[Refs 5th c.BC+ [11.666, 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Persae” 796; οἱ μένοντες 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 4.4.19, etc.]]

__I.4
of things, to be lasting, remain, stand, στήλη μένει ἔμπεδον [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 17.434; ἀσφαλὲς αἰὲν.. μένει οὐρανός 5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “N.” 6.4; τάδ᾽ αἰανῶς μένοι 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Eumenides” 672; αἰῶνα δ᾽ ἐς τρίτον μένει [prev. author] “Th.” 744 (Lyric poetry)]]; opposed to φέρεσθαι, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Phaedrus” 261d]]; εἰ μηδὲν μένει if nothing is fixed, [Refs 1st c.BC+ [[prev. author] “Cra.” 440a; τὴν μεμενηκυῖαν κρίσιν 1st c.BC: Philodemus Philosophus “περὶ τῶν Στωικῶν” 339.15]]; οἱ μένοντες (i.e. ἀστέρες) having no proper motion, opposed to οἱ πλάνητες, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “de Caelo” 290a21; μένων κύκλος 4th c.BC: Autolycus Astronomus 12, +others, 1st c.BC: Ptolemaeus Epigrammaticus “Hyp.” 1.3]]; μένουσιν ἀριστοκρατίαι are stable, permanent, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Politica” 1308a3.]]

__I.4.b
μ. παρά τινι remain in one's possession, [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [“CPR” 18.37 (2nd c.AD), etc.]]

__I.5

of or at midnight, ἔκλειψις [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Meteorologica” 367b26; ὥρα 1st c.BC: Diodorus Siculus Historicus 19.31, compare “Anacreontea” 31.1: with a Verb, μεσονύκτιον δέξασθαί τινα 5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus]]l.7(6).5; μ. ὠλλύμαν [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Hecuba” 914 (Lyric poetry)]]: neuter as adverb, [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [3rd c.BC: Theocritus Poeta Bucolicus 13.69]]: as substantive μεσο-νύκτιον, τό, [NT+5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Hippocrates Medicus “περὶ νούσων” 2.48, LXX.Judg.16.3, 1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus “Caesar” 43, 2nd c.AD: Lucianus Sophista “Merc.Cond.” 26, Vett. Abbott-Smith / STEPBible (TBESG)
μέσος, -η, -ον
[in LXX chiefly for תָּוֶךְ ;]
middle, in the middle or midst;
__1. prop., as an adj.: Luk.23:45, Jhn.19:18, Act.1:18; with genitive pl., Luk.22:55, Jhn.1:26; genitive temp. (Bl., § 36, 13), μέσης νυκτός, Mat.25:6; μ. ἡμέρας, Act.26:13.
__2. In adverbial phrases, neut., μέσον, τὸ μ., as subst.: ἀνὰ μέσον, with genitive, between (cl.; in LXX: Gen.1:4, al.), elliptically (but see M, Pr., 99), 1Co.6:5; = ἐν μ., among, in the midst of (El., § 39, 2; 40, 8; cf. in LXX: Jos.19:1, Sir.27:2), Mat.13:25, Mrk.7:31, Rev.7:17; διὰ μέσου, with genitive, Luk.4:30; διὰ μέσον (Rec. -ου, see 81., § 42, 1), between, Luk.17:11 (ICC, in l); εἰς τὸ μ. (see: εἰς), Mrk.3:3, Luk.4:35 5:19 6:8, Jhn.20:19, 26; εἰς μ., Mrk.14:60; ἐν τῷ μ., Mat.14:6; ἐν μ., Jos.8:3, 9, Act.4:7; with, genitive loc., Mrk.6:47, Luk.21:21 22:55, Act.17:22, Heb.2:12" (LXX), Rev.4:6 5:6 22:2. with genitive pl., Mat.10:16 18:2, 20, Mrk.9:36, Luk.2:46 8:7 10:3 22:27 24:36, Act.1:15 2:22 27:21, 1Th.2:7, Rev.1:13 2:1 5:6 6:6; κατὰ μέσον τ. νυκτός, Act.27:27 (Bl., § 47, 6); ἐκ τοῦ μ. (Lft., in l; Deiss., BS, 252 f.), Col.2:14; ἐκ μ.., 2Th.2:7; ἐκ τοῦ μ., with genitive, Mat.13:49, Act.17:33 23:10, 1Co.5:2, 2Co.6:17.
__3. Neut., μέσον, adverbially, with genitive, in the midst of, Mat.14:24 (WH, txt., R, mg., aliter), Php.2:15 (διὰ μέσου­see supr.-also Jhn.8:50, R, mg.).†
(AS)

μέσος, η, ον,
also [Refs 4th c.AD+ [4th c.AD(?): Arcadius Grammaticus (see. ἰμέσος, μεσακόθεν)]]; Epic dialect μέσσος (also Aeolic dialect, [Refs 7th c.BC+ [7th-6th c.BC: Sappho Lyrica 1.12, “IG” 11(4).1064b32, and Lyric poetry, 5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “P.” 4.224, and sometimes in Trag., 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Hercules Furens” 403 (Lyric poetry), 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Coloneus” 1247 (Lyric poetry), “Tr.” 635 (Lyric poetry), “Ant.” 1223, 1236, “fragment” 255.5)]], Boeotian dialect, Cretan dialect μέττος, [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [“IG” 7.2420.20 (3rd c.BC), “GDI” 5000]] ii b 2 [Refs 5th c.BC+ [(5th c.BC)]]:—middle, in the middle,

__I
of Space, especially with Nouns, of the middle point or part, μ. σάκος [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 7.258; ἱστίον 1.481]]; οὐρανός zenith, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 4.400]]; μ. ἀπήνης from mid chariot, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Tyrannus” 812]]; ἐν αἰθέρι μ. in mid-air, [Refs [[prev. author] “Ant.” 416]]; μ. μετώπῳ in the middle of the forehead, [Refs 1st c.AD+ [“PRyl.” 128.30 (1st c.AD)]]: in Prose frequently preceding the Article, κατὰ μέσον τὸν σταθμόν [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 1.7.14; ἐν μ. τῇ χώρᾳ [prev. work] 2.1.11]]; ἐκ μ. τῆς νήσου, κατὰ μ. τὴν νῆσον, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Critias” 113d, 119d]]; ἐπὶ μέσου τοῦ τμάματος at the middle point of the segment, [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [3rd c.BC: Archimedes Geometra “περὶ ἰσορροπιῶν” 1.6; ἁ ἐπὶ μέσαν τὰν βάσιν ἀγομένα (i.e. εὐθεῖα) [prev. work] 12]]: sometimes following the Noun, ἐν τῇ ἀγορᾷ μέσῃ [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 29.12]]: less frequently midmost, central, of three or more objects, μ. ὁδός [Refs 6th c.BC+ [6th c.BC: Theognis Elegiacus 220, 331]]; ὁ μ. [δάκτυλος] [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 523c]]; τὸ μ. στῖφος the central division of the army, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 1.8.13]]; μέσον, τό, centre, ἡ ἐπὶ τὸ μ. φορά [Refs 4th c.AD+ [4th c.AD: Iamblichus Philosophus “Protrepticus” 21.]]

__I.b
with a Verb, ἔχεται μ. by the middle, by the waist, proverbial from the wrestling-ring, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Equites” 387 (Lyric poetry), compare “Ach.” 571 (Lyric poetry), “Nu.” 1047, “Ra.” 469; μέσην λαβόντα [prev. author] “Ach.” 274, compare 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 9.107, 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 53.17; ὁ πέπλος ἐρράγη μ. 4th-3rd c.BC: Philippides Comicus 25.5.]]

__I.c
with genitive, midway between, ἑνὸς καὶ πλήθους τὸ ὀλίγον μ. [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Politicus” 303a (also μ. ἐπ᾽ ἀμφότερα, [prev. passage]):— 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus has μέσος ἀπὸ [τοῦ κρατῆρος] τοῦ τε πέτρου “OC” 1595.]]

__I.2
of Time, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Homerus Epicus only in phrase μέσον ἦμαρ midday, 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 21.111, 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 7.288, 5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “P.” 9.113; μέσαι νύκτες 7th-6th c.BC: Sappho Lyrica 52, 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 4.181, 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 7.8.12, etc.; θέρευς ἔτι μέσσου ἐόντος 8th-7th c.BC: Hesiodus Epicus “Opera et Dies” 502; χειμῶνος μέσου 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Fragmenta” 569.1; μ. ἡμέρα 2nd c.AD: Herodianus Grammaticus 8.5.9]]; μ. ἡλικία middle age, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Epistulae” 316c: so μέσοι τὴν ἡλικίαν 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Epistulae - Epistolographi” 5]]; μέσος ἀκμῆς variant in [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [3rd c.BC: Theocritus Poeta Bucolicus 25.164.]]

__I.3
metaphorically, impartial, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 4.83, “PLond.” 1.113(1).27 (6th c.AD).]]

__I.3.b
inter-mediate, frequently with genitive, μ. τις γέγονα χρηματιστὴς τοῦ τε πάππου καὶ τοῦ πατρός [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 330b; ψιλὸν μὲν τὸ π ¯, δασὺ δὲ τὸ φ ¯, μέσον δὲ ἀμφοῖν τὸ β ¯ 1st c.BC: Dionysius Halicarnassensis “de Compositione Verborum” 14 (see. below d); ἡ τρίτη καὶ μ. τῶν εἰρημένων δυεῖν ἁρμονιῶν [prev. work] 24; ὁ μ. χαρακτήρ [prev. work] 21]]; indeterminate, [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd c.AD: Lucianus Sophista “Par.” 28]]; τὰ μ. things indifferent (neither good nor bad), [Refs [“Stoicorum Veterum Fragmenta” 3.135, +others]]; of words such as τύχη, [Refs [“Etymologicum Magnum” 626.38]]; ζῴδια (neither lucky nor unlucky) [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd c.AD: Vettius Valens Astrologus 93.9; μ. δίαιτα Diocl.fragment 141, compare 2nd c.AD: Soranus Medicus 1.46.]]

__I.3.c
Grammars, of Verbs, middle, [Refs [12th c.AD: Eustathius Episcopus Thessalonicensis 1846.30, etc.]]; μ. διάθεσις, σχήματα, [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd c.AD: Apollonius Dyscolus Grammaticus “de Syntaxi;” 226.10, 210.18]]; μ. ἐνεστώς present middle, [Refs [[prev. work] 278.25.]]

__I.3.d
Grammars, of consonants, Latin mediae, i. e. β ¯ γ ¯ δ ¯, [Refs 2nd c.BC+ [2nd c.BC: Dionysius Thrax Grammaticus 631.23]]: but also of semi-vowels, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Philebus” 18c: of accent, ὀξύτητι καὶ βαρύτητι καὶ τῷ μέσῳ]], i. e. the circumflex, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Poetica” 1456b33.]]

__II
middling, moderate,

__II.1
of size, μέσοι ὀφθαλμοί, ὦτα, γλῶττα, [Refs [[prev. author] “HA” 492a8, 33, b31]]; μ. μεγέθει[Refs 3rd c.BC+ [[prev. work] 496a21, “PPetr.” 1p.37 (3rd c.BC)]]; μ. alone, of middle height, [Refs 2nd c.BC+ [PGrenf. 2.23 (a) ii 3 (2nd c.BC), “POxy.” 73.13 (1st c.AD), etc.]]

__II.2
of class or quality, πάντων μέσ᾽ ἄριστα [Refs 6th c.BC+ [6th c.BC: Theognis Elegiacus 335; παντὶ μέσῳ τὸ κράτος θεὸς ὤπασεν 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Eumenides” 529 (Lyric poetry); μ. ἐν πόλει 6th c.BC: Phocylides Lyricus 12]]; μ. ἀνήρ a man of middle rank, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.107; μ. πολίτης 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 6.54; τὰ μ. τῶν πολιτῶν [prev. author] 3.82 (so τῶν ἀνὰ πόλιν τὰ μ. 5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “P.” 11.52)]]; οἱ μ., between οἱ εὔποροι and οἱ ἄποροι, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Politica” 1289b31, 1295b3; οἱ μ. πολῖται [prev. work] 1296a19; τὸ μ. [prev. work] 1295b37]]; μ. [πολιτεία[Refs 2nd c.AD+ [] [prev. work] 1296a7; ὁ μ. βίος 2nd c.AD: Lucianus Sophista “Luct.” 9]]; mediocre, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Protagoras” 346d; τῶν ἑταιρῶν αἱ μ. Theopomp. Comedy texts 21.]] adverb μέσως, ἱκανόν fairly adequate, [Refs 1st c.BC+ [1st c.BC: Philodemus Gadarensis Epigrammaticus “Rh.” 2.4S.]]

__III
μέσον, τό, midst, intervening space, mostly with Preps.,

__III.a
ἐν μέσσῳ, ={ἐν μεταιχμίῳ}, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 3.69, 90; ἐν τῷ μ.]]in the midst, [NT.Matt.14.6]; ἡ 'ν μέσῳ [μοῖρα] σῴζει πόλεις the middle class, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Supplices” 244: without ἐν, ἔμβαλε μέσσῳ 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 4.444; ἔνθορε μέσσῳ 21.233; μέσσῳ ἀμφοτέρων 3.416, 7.277; τῶνδέ τ᾽ ἐν μ. πεσεῖν 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Phoenissae” 583; ἐν μ. λόγους ἔχειν [prev. author] “Hel.” 630; μῆκος ἐν μ. χρόνου 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Supplices” 735; χρόνος οὑν μ. 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Phoenissae” 589 (troch.)]]; τὰ ἐν μ. what went between, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Coloneus” 583]]; οἱ ἐν μ. λόγοι the intervening words, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. author] “El.” 1364, 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Medea” 819; κλίνης ἐν μ. [prev. author] “Hec.” 1150]]; ἐν μ. ἡμῶν καὶ βασιλέως between us and him, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 2.2.3; σοφίας καὶ ἀμαθίας ἐν μ. 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Symposium” 203e]]; ἐν μ. νυκτῶν at midnight, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 5.3.52]]; ἆθλα κείμεν᾽ ἐν μέσῳ offered for competition (compare below b), [Refs 6th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 4.5, compare 6th c.BC: Theognis Elegiacus 994, 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 3.1.21]]; ἡ τιμὴ ἐν τῷ μέσῳ ἔστω deposited with the court, [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [3rd c.BC: Herodas Mimographus 2.90: without ἐν, καὶ μέσῳ πάντες καὶ χωρὶς ἕκαστος]] both collectively and severally, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [“IG” 12(5).872.27,31,38, +others (from Tenos): in _plural_, κεῖτο δ᾽ ἄρ᾽ ἐν μέσσοισι 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 18.507; ἐν μέσοισ᾽ 6th c.BC: Xenophanes Poeta Philosophus 1.7]]; ἐν μέσῳ εἶναι τοῦ συμμεῖξαι to stand in the way of.., [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 5.2.26]]; ἡ γὰρ θάλαττα ἐν τῷ μ. is an obstacle, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [[prev. author] “Ath.” 2.2; οὐδεὶς ἐν μέσσῳ γείτων πέλεν 3rd c.BC: Theocritus Poeta Bucolicus 21.17; οὐδὲν ἂν ἦν ἐν μ. πολεμεῖν ἡμᾶς 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 23.183]]; compare ἰμέσος.

__III.b
ἐς μέσον, ἐς μ. ἀμφοτέρων, frequently in [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Homerus Epicus for ἐς μεταίχμιον, 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 4.79, 6.120]]; ἀνδρὶ δὲ νικηθέντι γυναῖκ᾽ ἐς μέσσον ἔθηκε deposited her as a prize (compare above a),[Refs 5th c.BC+ [23.704; ἐς μ. δεικνύναι τινί τι 5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “Fragmenta.” 42.3]]; ἐς μ. ἵεσθαι, ἐλθεῖν, παρελθεῖν, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Trachiniae” 514 (Lyric poetry), 3rd c.BC: Theocritus Poeta Bucolicus 22.183, 1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus “Agis” 9; ἐς μέσον ἀμφοτέροισι.. δικάσσατε 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 23.574]]; ἐς τὸ μ. φέρειν bring forward publicly, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 4.97, 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 18.139; ἐς τὸ μ. λέγεσθαι 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 6.129]]; ἐς μ. Πέρσῃσι καταθεῖναι τὰ πρήγματα to give up the power in common to all, [Refs [[prev. author] 3.80; ἐς μ. τὴν ἀρχὴν τιθεὶς ἰσονομίην ὑμῖν προαγορεύω [prev. work] 142.]]

__III.c
ἐκ τοῦ μέσου away, ἐκ μ. ἀνελεῖν [NT+4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 10.36, 18.294; [χειρόγραφον] ἦρκεν ἐκ τοῦ μ. NT.Col.2.14, compare 2nd c.AD: Arrianus Historicus “Epicteti Dissertationes” 3.3.15]]; also ἐκ μ. a half, ἔτη ὀκτὼ καὶ ἔνατον ἐκ μ. [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 4.133]]; also ἐκ μ. κατῆστο remained in the middle, i. e. neutral [Refs 5th c.BC+ [compare (ἐκ 1.6 near the end), 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 3.83, compare 4.118, 8.22, 73.]]

__III.d
διὰ μέσου between, τὸ διὰ μ. ἔθνος [Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. author] 1.104; διὰ μ. ποιεῖσθαι 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 6.3.3]]; διὰ μ. γενέσθαι intervene, of an event, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 4.20: with _genitive_, διὰ μέσου τῆς πόλεως ῥεῖ ποταμός 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 1.2.23; διὰ μ. ῥεῖ τούτων ποταμός [prev. work] 1.4.4, etc.]]; τὸ τούτων διὰ μ. [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Leges” 805e]]; also οἱ διὰ μέσου the middle party, the moderates, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 8.75, 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Historia Graeca (Hellenica)” 5.4.25]]; τὸ διὰ μ. the middle class, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Politica” 1296a8]]; of Time, ὁ διὰ μ. χρόνος [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 9.112]]; ἡ διὰ μ. ξύμβασις an interim agreement, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 5.26]]; διὰ μέσου, as a figure of speech, use of parenthesis, [Refs [Herodianus Rhetor “de Figuris - Rhet.” p.95S.]]

__III.e
ἀν (ὀν) τὸ μ. in the midst, [Refs 7th c.BC+ [7th-6th c.BC: Alcaeus Lyricus 18.3, 6th c.BC: Xenophanes Poeta Philosophus 1.11, 6th c.BC: Theognis Elegiacus 839]]; ἀνὰ μέσον midway between, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Historia Animalium” 496a22, 4th c.BC: Antiphanes Comicus 13, 3rd c.BC: Theocritus Poeta Bucolicus 22.21, etc.; ἀνὰ μ. τοῦ ναοῦ καὶ τοῦ βωμοῦ “GDI” 2010 (Delph.), compare “PTeb.” 13.9 (2nd c.BC), +others]]; θρὶξ ἀνὰ μέσσον [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [3rd c.BC: Theocritus Poeta Bucolicus 14.9; ἀνὰ μέσσα 2nd c.BC: Nicander Epicus “Theriaca” 167]]; also ἀνὰ μέσον φέρε, ={μετρίως}, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-3rd c.BC: Menander Comicus 531.18.]]

__III.f
κατὰ μέσσον, = {ἐν μέσῳ}, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 5.8, 16.285, etc.: with _genitive_, κὰδ δὲ μέσον τάφρου καὶ τείχεος ἷζον]] between, [Refs [9.87.]]

__III.2
μέσον, τό, difference, τὸ μ. πρὸς τὰς μεγίστας καὶ ἐλαχίστας the average between.., [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 1.10]]; πολλὸν τὸ μ., πολὺ τὸ μ., the difference is great, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.126, 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Alcestis” 914 (_anapaest meter_)]]; τὸ μ. οὐδὲν τῆς ἔχθρης ἐστί there is no middle course for our enmity, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 7.11.]]

__III.3
middle state, mean, τὸ μ. καὶ τὸ εὖ [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Ethica Nicomachea” 1109b26]]; ποιήματα μέσα, opposed to ὀγκώδη, in the (correct) mean, [Refs 1st c.BC+ [1st c.BC: Philodemus Philosophus “περὶ ποιημάτων” 5.5]]. adverb -ως, ἀναστρέφεσθαι [Refs [[prev. author] “Rh.” 1.155S.]]

__III.4
in Logic, τὸ μ. the middle term of a syllogism, opposed to τὰ ἄκρα, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Analytica Priora” 66a30; also ὁ μ. (i.e. ὅρος) [prev. work] 25b33.]]

__III.5
in Mathematics texts, middle terms in a proportion, [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [3rd c.BC: Euclides Geometra 6.16]]; μέση, or μέση (μέσος) ἀνάλογον a mean proportional (straight line or number), [Refs [[prev. work] 13, 17, 8.11, 12, +others]]; μέσης εὕρεσις [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “de Anima” 413a19, “Metaphorical” 996b21]]; μέση medial, a specific kind of irrational (straight line), [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [3rd c.BC: Euclides Geometra 10.21, +others]]; μέσον ὀρθογώνιον (χωρίον) medial rectangle (area), [Refs [[prev. work] 24, +others]]

__III.6

deep_entry:

μετά (before vowel μετ᾽; on the neglect of elision in certain cases, V. WH, App., 146 b),
prep. with genitive, accusative (in poet, also with dative), [in LXX for אַחַד ,עִם ,אֵת, etc.].
__I. C. genitive,
__1. among, amid: Mrk.1:13, Luk.22:37 (LXX, ἐν) 24:5, Jhn.18:5, al.; διωγμῶν, Mrk.10:30.
__2. Of association and companionship, with (in which sense it gradually superseded σύν, than which it is much more frequently in NT; cf. Bl., §42, 3): with genitive of person(s), Mat.8:11 20:20 Mrk.1:29 3:7 Luk.5:30, Jhn.3:22, Gal.2:1, al. mult.; εἶναι μετά, Mat.5:25, Mrk.3:14, al.; metaphorically, of divine help and guidance, Jhn.3:2, Act.7:9, Php.4:9, al.; opposite to εἶναι κατά, Mat.12:30, Luk.11:23; in Hellenistic usage (but see M, Pr., 106, 246f.), πολεμεῖν μετά = cl. π., with dative, to wage war against (so LXX for נִלְחַם עִם, 1Ki.17:33), Rev.2:16, al.; with genitive of thing(s), χαρᾶς, Mat.13:20, Mrk.4:16, al.; ὀργῆς, Mrk.3:5, al.
__II. C. accusative,
__1. of place, behind, after: Heb.9:3.
__2. Of time, after: Mat.17:1, Mrk.14:1, Luk.1:24, Act.1:5, Gal.1:18, al.; μετὰ τοῦτο, Jhn.2:12, al.; ταῦτα, Mrk.16:[12], Luk.5:27, Jhn.3:22, al; with inf. artic. (BL, §71, 5; 72, 3), Mat.26:32, Mrk.1:14, al.
__III. In composition,
__1. of association or community: μεταδίδωμι, μετέχω, etc.
__2. Exchange or transference: μεταλλάσσω, μετοικίζω, etc.
__3. after: μεταμέλομαι.
(AS)

__A.III
later, in one's dealings with, ὅσα ἐποίησεν ὁ θεὸς μετ᾽ αὐτῶν [NT+2nd c.AD+ [NT.Act.14.27; ὁ ποιήσας τὸ ἔλεος μετ᾽ αὐτοῦ NT.Luke.10.36; τί ἡμῖν συνέβη μ. τῶν ἀρχόντων “PAmh.” 2.135.15 (2nd c.AD)]]: even of hostile action, σὺ ποιεῖς μετ᾽ ἐμοῦ πονηρίαν [LXX+NT+2nd c.AD+ [LXX.Judg.11.27, compare 15.3; πολεμῆσαι μ. τινός NT.Rev.12.7, compare 2nd c.AD: Apollodorus Damascenus Mechanicus “Abhandlungen der Göttinger Gesellschaft der Wissenschaften (Phil.-hist. Klasse)” 190.4 codices (but μ. may be a gloss), Wilcken “Chr.” 23.10 (5th c.AD), “OGI” 201.3 (Nubia, 6th c.AD)]]: to denote the union of persons with qualities or circumstances, and so to denote manner, τὸ ἄπραγμον.. μὴ μ. τοῦ δραστηρίου τεταγμένον [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 2.63, etc.; ἱκετεῦσαι μ. δακρύων 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Apologia” 34c; οἴκτου μέτα 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Coloneus” 1636; μετ᾽ ἀσφαλείας μὲν δοξάζομεν, μετὰ δέους δὲ.. ἐλλείπομεν 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 1.120, compare “IG” 22.791.12; μ. ῥυθμοῦ βαίνοντες 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 5.70; ὅσα μετ᾽ ἐλπίδων λυμαίνεται [prev. work] 103, etc.]]; ψυχὴν ὁσίως βεβιωκυῖαν καὶ μετ᾽ ἀληθείας [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Gorgias” 526c, compare “Phdr.” 249a, 253d]]; also, by means of, μετ᾽ ἀρετῆς πρωτεύειν [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Memorabilia” 3.5.8; γράφε μ. μέλανος “PMag.Lond.” 121.226.]]

__A.III.2
serving to join two predicates, γενόμενος μ. τοῦ δυνατοῦ καὶ ξυνετός, i.e. δυνατός τε καὶ ξυνετός, 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 2.15; ὅταν πλησιάζῃ μ. τοῦ ἅπτεσθαι 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Phaedrus” 255b.

__A.IV
rarely of Time, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [μ. τοῦ γυμνάζεσθαι ἠλείψαντο, for ἅμα, 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 1.6]]; μετ᾽ ἀνοκωχῆς during.., [Refs [[prev. author] 5.25.]]

__B
WITH DAT., only poetry, mostly Epic dialect:

__B.I
between, among others, but without the close union which belongs to the genitive, and so nearly ={ἐν}, which is sometimes exchanged with it, μ. πρώτοισι.. ἐν πυμάτοισι [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 11.64:]]

__B.I.1
of persons, among, in company with, μετ᾽ ἀθανάτοισι [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 1.525; μετ᾽ ἀνθρώποις 5th c.BC: Bacchylides Lyricus 5.30; μ. κόραισι Νηρῆος 5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “O.” 2.29]]; μ. τριτάτοισιν ἄνασσεν in the third generation (not μ. τριτάτων belonging to it), [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 1.252]]; of haranguing an assembly, μετ᾽ Ἀργείοις ἀγορεύεις [Refs [10.250, etc.]]; between, of two parties, φιλότητα μετ᾽ ἀμφοτέροισι βάλωμεν [Refs [4.16.]]

__B.I.2
of things, μ. νηυσίν, ἀστράσι, κύμασιν, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [13.668, 22.28, 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 3.91; δεινὸν δ᾽ ἐστὶ θανεῖν μ. κύμασιν 8th-7th c.BC: Hesiodus Epicus “Opera et Dies” 687; χαῖται δ᾽ ἐρρώοντο μ. πνοιῇς ἀνέμοιο 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 23.367; αἰετὼ.. ἐπέτοντο μ. π. ἀ. 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 2.148.]]

__B.I.3
of separate parts of persons, between, μ. χερσὶν ἔχειν to hold between, i.e. in, the hands, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 11.4, 184, 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Philoctetes” 1110 (Lyric poetry), etc.; τὸν μ. χ. ἐρύσατο 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 5.344]]; ὅς κεν.. πέσῃ μ. ποσσὶ γυναικός, of a child being born, 'to fall between her feet', [Refs [19.110; so μ. γένυσσιν, γαμφηλῇσιν, 11.416, 13.200; μ. φρεσί 4.245, etc.]]

__B.II
to complete a number, besides, over and above, αὐτὰρ ἐγὼ πέμπτος μ. τοῖσιν ἐλέγμην I reckoned myself to be with them a fifth, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 9.335, compare 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 3.188]]; Οὖτιν.. πύματον ἔδομαι μ. οἷς ἑτάροισι last to complete the number, i.e. after, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 9.369, compare 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Persae” 613, 3rd c.BC: Theocritus Poeta Bucolicus 1.39, 17.84.]]

__B.III
with dative singular, only of collective Nouns (or the equivalent of such, μεθ᾽ αἵματι καὶ κονίῃσιν [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 15.118), μ. στροφάλιγγι κονίης 21.503; στρατῷ 22.49; μ. πρώτῃ ἀγορῇ 19.50, etc.; μετ᾽ ἀνδρῶν.. ἀριθμῷ 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 11.449; μετ᾽ ἄλλῳ λαῷ 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Choephori” 365 (Lyric poetry).]]

__C
WITH ACCUSATIVE

__C.I
of motion, into the middle of, coming into or among, especially where a number of persons is implied, ἵκοντο μ. Τρῶας καὶ Ἀχαιούς [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 3.264; μ. φῦλα θεῶν 15.54, compare 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 3.366, +others; μ. μῶλον Ἄρηος 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 16.245; μ. λαὸν Ἀχαιών 5.573, +others; μ. στρατόν, μεθ᾽ ὅμιλον, μεθ᾽ ὁμήγυριν, 5.589, 14.21, 20.142: so of birds, ὥς τ᾽ αἰγυπιὸς μ. χῆνας (though this may be referred to signification 2), 17.460]]; of things, εἴ τινα φεύγοντα σαώσειαν μ. νῆας [Refs [12.123]]; με μ... ἔριδας καὶ νείκεα βάλλει plunges me into them, [Refs [2.376]]; of place, μ. τ᾽ ἤθεα καὶ νομὸν ἵππων [Refs [6.511]]; δράγματα μετ᾽ ὄγμον πῖπτον into the midst of the furrow, [Refs [18.552.]]

__C.I.2
in pursuit or quest of, of persons, sometimes in friendlysense, βῆ ῥ᾽ ἰέναι μ. Νέστορα went to seek [Refs 8th c.BC+ [3rd c.AD: Nestor Epigrammaticus, 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 10.73, compare 15.221: sometimes in hostile sense, βῆναι μ. τινά]] to go after, pursue him, [Refs [5.152, 6.21, +others]]; also of things, πλεῖν μ. χαλκόν to sail in quest of it, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 1.184]]; ἵκηαι μ. πατρὸς ἀκουήν in search of news of thy father, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [2.308, compare 13.415; οἴχονται μ. δεῖπνον 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 19.346]]; πόλεμον μέτα θωρήσσοντο they armed for the battle, [Refs [20.329]]; ὡπλίζοντο μεθ᾽ ὕλην prepared to seek after wood, [Refs [7.418, compare 420; μ. δούρατος ᾤχετ᾽ ἐρωήν 11.357; μ. γὰρ δόρυ ᾔει οἰσόμενος 13.247.]]

__C.II
of sequence or succession,

__C.II.1
of Place, after, behind, λαοὶ ἕπονθ᾽, ὡς εἴ τε μ. κτίλον ἕσπετο μῆλα like sheep after the bell-wether, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 13.492, compare 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 6.260, 21.190, “hymnus ad Venerem” 69; ἔσχατοι μ. Κύνητας οἰκέουσι 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 4.49]]; μ. τὴν θάλασσαν beyond, on the far side of the sea, [Refs [Theo Sm. p.122 H.]]

__C.II.2
of Time, after, next to, μ. δαῖτας [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 22.352]]; μεθ᾽ Ἕκτορα πότμος ἑτοῖμος after Hector thy death is at the door, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 18.96; μ. Πάτροκλόν γε θανόντα 24.575, compare 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.34; μετ᾽ εὐχάν 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Agamemnon” 231 (Lyric poetry), etc.; μ. ταῦτα]]thereupon, there-after, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [hymnus ad Mercurium 126, etc.; τὸ μ. ταῦτα 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Philebus” 34c; τὸ μ. τοῦτο [prev. author] “Criti.” 120a]]; μετ᾽ ὀλίγον ὕστερον shortly after, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [[prev. author] “Lg.” 646c; μ. μικρόν 2nd c.AD: Lucianus Sophista “Demon.” 8; μ. ἡμέρας τρεῖς μ. τὴν ἄφεδρον 1st c.AD: Dioscorides (Dioscurides) Medicus 2.19; μ. ἔτη δύο 1st c.AD: Josephus Historicus “Bellum Judaicum” 1.13.1; μ. τρίτον ἔτος 4th-3rd c.BC: Theophrastus Philosophus “Historia Plantarum” 4.2.8]]; μ. χρυσόθρονον ἠῶ after daybreak, [Refs [“hymnus ad Mercurium” 326: but μετ᾽ ἡμέρην]] by day, opposed to νυκτός, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 2.150, compare 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Phaedrus” 251e, etc.]]; μεθ᾽ ἡμέραν, opposed to νύκτωρ, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Bacchae” 485; μ. νύκτας 5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “N.” 6.6]]; μ. τὸν ἑξέτη καὶ τὴν ἑξέτιν after the boy or girl has attained the age of six years, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Leges” 794c.]]

__C.II.3
in order of Worth, Rank, etc., next after, following superlative, κάλλιστος ἀνὴρ.. τῶν ἄλλων Δαναῶν μετ᾽ ἀμύμονα Πηλεΐωνα [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 2.674, compare 7.228, 12.104, 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 2.350, 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 4.53, 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 7.2.11, etc.; κοῦροι οἳ.. ἀριστεύουσι μεθ᾽ ἡμέας 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 4.652, compare 5th-6th c.BC: Isocrates Orator 9.18]]: where superlative is implied, ὃς πᾶσι μετέπρεπε.. μ. Πηλεΐωνος ἑταῖρον [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 16.195, compare 17.280, 351]]; μ. μάκαρας next to the gods, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Septem contra Thebas” 1080 (_anapaest meter_)]]; also μάχεσθαι μ. πολλοὺς τῶν Ἑλλήνων to be inferior in fighting to many.., [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd-3rd c.AD: Philostratus Sophista “Heroicus” 6.]]

__C.III
after, according to, μ. σὸν καὶ ἐμὸν κῆρ as you and I wish, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 15.52; μετ᾽ ἀνέρος ἴχνι᾽ ἐρευνῶν 18.321; μετ᾽ ἴχνια βαῖνε 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 2.406.]]

__C.IV
generally, among, between, as with dative (B.I), μ. πάντας ὁμήλικας ἄριστος best among all, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 9.54, compare 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 16.419; μ. πληθύν 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 2.143]]; μ. τοὺς τετελευτηκότας including those who have died, [Refs 1st c.AD+ [“PLond.” 2.260.87 (1st c.AD)]]; μ. χεῖρας ἔχειν [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 7.16. β᾽, 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 1.138, “POxy.” 901.9 (4th c.AD),compare 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Agesilaus” 2.14, etc.]]

__D
μετά with all cases can be put after its substantive, and is then by anastrophe μέτα, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 13.301]], but not when the ultima  is elided, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [17.258, 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 15.147.]]

__E
absolutely as adverb., among them, with them, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 2.446, 477, etc.]]; with him, οὐκ οἶον, μ. καὶ Γανυμήδεα [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [3rd c.BC: Apollonius Rhodius Epicus 3.115.]]

__E.II
and then, next afterwards, opposed to πρόσθε, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 23.133.]]

__E.III
thereafter,[Refs 5th c.BC+ [15.67, 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.88, 128, 150, 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Agamemnon” 759 (Lyric poetry), etc.]]; μ. γάρ τε καὶ ἄλγεσι τέρπεται ἀνήρ one feels pleasure even in troubles, when past, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 15.400]]; μ. δέ, for ἔπειτα δέ, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.19, 2nd c.AD: Lucianus Sophista “DMort.” 9.2, etc.]]

__F
μέτα, -μέτεστι, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 21.93, 4th-5th c.BC: Parmenides Poeta Philosophus 9.4, 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.88, 171, 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Antigone” 48,etc.]]

__G
IN COMPOSITION (joined with other words),

__G.I
of community or participation, as in μεταδίδωμι, μετέχω, usually with genitive of things.

__G.I.2
of action in common with another, as in μεταδαίνυμαι, μεταμέλπομαι, etc., with dative person

__G.II
in the midst of, of space or time, as in μεταδήμιος, μεταδόρπιος 1; between, as in μεταίχμιον, μεταπύργιον.

__G.III
of succession of time, as in μεταδόρπιος 2, μετακλαίω, μεταυτίκα.

__G.IV
of pursuit, as in μεταδιώκω, μετέρχομαι.

__G.V
of letting go, as in μεθίημι, μεθήμων.

__G.VI
after, behind, as in μετάφρενον, opposed to πρόσθε.

__G.VII
reversely, as in μετατρέπω, μεταστρέφω.

__G.VIII
most frequently of change of place, condition, plan, etc., as in μεταβαίνω, μεταβάλλω, μεταβουλεύω, μεταγιγνώσκω, etc.

μετα-βαίνω
[in LXX: Wis.7:27 19:19, 2Ma.6:1 2Mac 6:9 2Mac 6:24 * ;]
to pass over from one place to another : Mat.17:20, Luk.10:7; with reference to the point of departure only, to withdraw, depart: Mat.8:34 11:1 12:9 15:29, Jhn.7:3, Act.18:7; of removal from this life, ἐκ τ. κότμου πρὸς τ. Πατέρα, Jhn.13:1; metaphorically, ἐκ τ. θανάτου εἰς τ. ζωήν, Jhn.5:24, 1Jn.3:14.†

LSJ / STEPBible (TFLSJ)
μεταβάλλω,
future - βᾰλῶ [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Aves” 1568:]]aorist μετέβᾰλον:—throw into a different position, turn quickly or suddenly, Hom.only once, in tmesi, μετὰ νῶτα βαλών [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 8.94; χαλεπῶς μ. δέμας 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Hippolytus” 204 (_anapaest meter_), compare 2nd c.AD: Galenus Medicus 15.556; μ. θοἰμάτιον ἐπιδεξιά 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus [same place]]]; μ. γῆν turn, i.e. plough, the earth, [LXX+5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Oeconomicus” 16.14; μετέβαλε Κύριος ἄνεμον ἐκ θαλάσσης LXX.Exo.10.19]]; μ. ποταμόν change the course of a river, [Refs 4th c.AD+ [4th c.AD: Julianus Imperator “Orationes” 3.126d.]]

__II
turn about, change, alter, τὸ οὔνομα [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.57; τὴν πολιτείαν 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Politica” 1292b21]]; [οἱ Βρίγες] τὸ οὔνομα μετέβαλον [ἐς Φρύγας] [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 7.73; τὰς φυλὰς μετέβαλε [ὁ Κλεισθένης] ἐς ἄλλα οὐνόματα [prev. author] 5.68; μ. μορφήν τινος εἰς ἀνδρὸς φύσιν 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Bacchae” 54; [τινὰ] ἐπὶ κακόν 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Thesmophoriazusae” 723; ἐπὶ τὸ βέλτιον 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 381b]]; μ. δίαιταν change one's way of life, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 2.16]]; μ. ὕδατα drink different water, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 8.117; ὀργὰς μ. 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Medea” 121 (_anapaest meter_); μ. τοὺς τρόπους 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Plutus” 36, 5th c.BC: Eupolis Comicus 357.7; μ. τὸ ἔθος 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 1.123]]; μ. εὔνοιαν lose it,[Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. work] 77; μ. χώραν ἐκ χώρας 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Theaetetus” 181c: frequently with _adjectives_, etc., implying change, μ. ἄλλους τρόπους]] change and adopt other ways, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Iphigenia Aulidensis” 343 (troch.); μ. ἄλλας γραφάς [prev. work] 363 (troch.)]]; εἶδος καινὸν μουσικῆς μ. [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 424c; πόλις ἄλλον ἐξ ἄλλου -βάλλουσα τύραννον 1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus “Timoleon” 1]]; μ. ἀντὶ τοῦ ὁμο- ἀ-” [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Cratylus” 405d; ἐμαυτὸν ἄνω κάτω μετέβαλλον [prev. author] “Phd.” 96b; ἄνω καὶ κάτω τὰς δόξας μ. [prev. author] “R.” 508d: with _accusative_ _cognate_, πολλὰς μεταβολὰς.. μ. ὑδάτων καὶ σίτων [prev. work] 404a.]]

__II.b
translate, νόμον εἰς τὴν Ἑλλάδα φωνήν [Refs 1st c.AD+ [1st c.AD: Josephus Historicus “AJProoem.” 3, compare 12.2.13 (_passive_).]]

__II.c
stir with a spoon, [Refs 1st c.AD+ [1st c.AD: Dioscorides (Dioscurides) Medicus 3.22 (_passive_).]]

__III
intransitive, undergo a change, μ. ἐς εὐνομίην [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.65, compare 5th c.BC: Antipho Orator 2.4.9; μ. εἰς ὀλιγαρχικὸν ἐκ τοῦ τιμοκρατικοῦ 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 553a, etc.; μ. ἐπὶ τοὐναντίον [prev. author] “Plt.” 270d; ὅταν εἰς ἑτέραν -βάλῃ πολιτείαν ἡ πόλις 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Politica” 1276b14, compare 1301a20: _impersonal_, μεταβάλλει διὰ πλειόνων ζῴων]] changes run through a series of creatures, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-3rd c.BC: Theophrastus Philosophus “Historia Plantarum” 2.4.4]]: with genitive of things, come in exchange for or instead of, καιναὶ καινῶν μεταβάλλουσαι.. συντυχίαι [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Troades” 1118.]]

__III.b
vary, μεταβάλλειν τὰς ἐπιστήμας τοῖς τόποις [Refs 5th c.BC+ [1st c.BC: Philodemus Gadarensis Epigrammaticus “Rh.” 2.115 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus]]

__III.2
change one's course, μεταβαλὼν πρὸς Ἀθηναίους turning to the Athenians, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 8.109:]]aorist participle μεταβαλών absolutely, instead, in turn, μεταβαλόντας ἀντὶ Κρητῶν γενέσθαι Ἰήπυγας [Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. author] 7.170, compare 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Ion” 1614, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Symposium” 204e, “Grg.” 480e]]: also present participle μεταβάλλων [Refs [[prev. author] “Tht.” 166d.]]

__B
middle, turn round, shift a load, μεταβαλλόμενος τἀνάφορον [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Ranae” 8; προβαλλομένους τὰ ὅπλα ἢ μεταβαλλομένους 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 6.5.16.]]

__B.2
cause to be removed, σῖτον [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [“PHib.” 1.45.6 (3rd c.BC), etc.]]

__B.2.b

any space measured or measurable, length, size, in plural, dimensions, μέτρα κελεύθου the length of the way, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 4.389; μέτρα θαλάσσης 8th-7th c.BC: Hesiodus Epicus “Opera et Dies” 648, Oracle texts cited in 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.47]]; μορφῆς μέτρα bodily dimensions, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Alcestis” 1063]]; τὰ μ. τοῦ λίθου its distances from a given point in given directions, its position, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 2.121.ά, compare 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Leges” 843e, 1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus “Solon” 23; ἄστρων μέτρα 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Fragmenta” 432.8; ἀπέχει.. θαλάσσης μέτρον ἑξήκοντα σταδίους 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 8.95]]; τῷ Ἴστρῳ ἐκ τῶν ἴσων μ. ὁρμᾶται [ὁ Νεῖλος] starts from the same distances as (i.e. the position corresponding to the source of) the [Refs 5th c.BC+ [3rd c.BC: Ister Historicus, 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 2.33; εἰδέναι τὴν ἑαυτοῦ χώραν μέτρῳ καὶ τόπῳ 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 8.5.3; ἐντὸς τῶν μ. τετμημένον μέταλλον 4th c.BC: Hyperides Orator “pro Euxenippo” 35]]; later of Time, duration, μέτρα βίοιο ἄρκια [Refs 1st c.AD+ [“APl.” 4.333 (1st c.AD: Antiphilus Epigrammaticus)]]; ἐτέων μέτρα, ὡράων μέτρον, [Refs [“Anthologia Graeca” 7.334,9.481]]; μέτρα ἐνιαυτῶν, νυκτός, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-3rd c.BC: Aratus Epicus 464.731; χρονικὰ μ. 6th c.AD: Simplicius Philosophus in “de An.” 299.37.]]

__3.b
limit, goal, ὅρμου μ. the goal which is the mooring-place, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 13.101]]; ἥβης μ. ἱκέσθαι the term which is puberty, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 11.225, 8th-7th c.BC: Hesiodus Epicus “Opera et Dies” 132]]; but, ἥβης μ. ἔχειν full measure of youthful vigour,[Refs 6th c.BC+ [[prev. work] 438, 6th c.BC: Theognis Elegiacus 1119; σοφίης, γνωμοσύνης μ. 6th c.BC: Solon Lyricus 13.52, 16.2.]]

__4
due measure or limit, proportion, μέτρα φυλάσσεσθαι [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th-7th c.BC: Hesiodus Epicus “Opera et Dies” 694; χρὴ κατ᾽ αὐτὸν παντὸς ὁρᾶν μέτρον 5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “P.” 2.34; μέτρα μὲν γνώμᾳ διώκων, μέτρα δὲ καὶ κατέχων [prev. author] “I.” 6(5).71; κατὰ μέτρον 8th-7th c.BC: Hesiodus Epicus “Opera et Dies” 720; πίνειν ὑπὲρ μέτρον 6th c.BC: Theognis Elegiacus 498; προστιθεὶς μ. 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Choephori” 797 (Lyric poetry)]]; τί μ. κακότατος ἔφ; [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Electra” 236 (Lyric poetry)]]; μ. ἔχει have a moderating power, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Leges” 836a; πλέον πίνειν τοῦ μέτρου [prev. author] “R.” 621a; μ. ἔχειν [prev. author] “Lg.” 957a]]; μέτρῳ, ={μετρίως},{καταβαίνειν} [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “P.” 8.78; οὐδεὶς τῷ μ. τὸ πίνειν ἔστεργε 4th c.AD: Alciphro Epistolographus 3.32.]]

__5
τίς ἱππείοις ἐν ἔντεσσιν μέτρα.. ἐπέθηκ᾽ checks, i.e. bits, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “O.” 13.20.]]

metre, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Nubes” 638, 641, etc.]]; opposed to μέλος (music) and ῥυθμός (time), [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Gorgias” 502c, etc.]]; λόγους ψιλοὺς εἰς μέτρα τιθέντες putting into verse, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. author] “Lg.” 669d; τὰ ἐν μέτρῳ πεποιημένα ἔπη 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Memorabilia” 1.2.21.]]

__II.2
plural, verses, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Lysis” 205a. (I.- 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus]] *métro-m from *métro-m 'measuring instrument', cf. Gothic mitan 'measure'.)

(bef. consonants, exc. Luk.16:16, μέχρι Ἰωάνου) and μέχρις (bef. vowels, Mk, Ga, ll. with, Heb.12:4; see Bl., § 5, 4)
__1. as prep., with genitive, as far as, even to, until;
__(a) of place: Rom.15:19;

μέχρῐ,
and μέχρῐς, adverb as far as, so used chiefly in Prose and before a preposition, μέχρι πρός.. [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Timaeus” 25b, “Criti.” 118a; μ. εἰς 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 6.4.26; ἐς γόνυ μ. χιτῶνα ζώννυσθαι 3rd c.BC: Callimachus Epicus “Hymnus in Dianam” 11: before Advs. of Place or Time, μ. ἐνταῦθα 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Sophista” 222a, +others; μ. δεῦρο τοῦ λόγου [prev. author] “Smp.” 217e]]; μ. ὅποι.. [Refs [[prev. author] “Grg.” 487c]]; μ. ὅπου.. [Refs 5th c.BC+ [3rd c.BC: Callimachus Epicus “Hymnus in Delum” 169; οὕτω μέχρι πόρρω 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 18.163; μ. τότε 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 8.24; μ. τὰ νῦν 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Leges” 686b]]; μ. νῦν (variant{τοῦ νῦν}) [Refs 1st c.BC+ [1st c.BC: Diodorus Siculus Historicus 17.110; μ. καὶ νῦν 1st c.BC-1st c.AD: Strabo Geographus 16.2.13]]; μέχρι πότε χηρεύομε; [Refs 3rd c.AD+ [3rd c.AD(?): Achilles Tatius Astronomus 4.1.]]

__II.1
of Place, μέχρι θαλάσσης [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 13.143; μ. τοῦ γούνατος 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 2.80; μ. τῆς πόλεως 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 6.96, compare 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 1.7.6, +others]]: rarely following its case, ὀμφαλοῦ μ. [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Leges” 925a, compare “Supp.epigram” 3.400.5 (Delph., 3rd c.BC).]]

of Time, τέο μέχρι; i.e. τίνος μέχρι χρόνο; how long? [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 24.128]]; μέχρις τε; [Refs 7th c.BC+ [7th c.BC: Callinus Epicus 1.1: in Prose, μέχρι τούτου 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.4]]; μέχρι οὗ, μέχρι ὅσου, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Menexenus” 245a, 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 8.3, +others]]; μ. τοσούτου, ἕως ἂν.. [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 1.90; μ. τούτου,.. μέχρις ἂν ῥηθῶσιν 4th-3rd c.BC: Dinarchus Orator 1.91, compare 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Phaedo” 81d: with the _Article_, τὸ μ. ἐμεῦ]] up to my time, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 3.10, 5.115]]; μ. τῆς ἐκείνου ζόης till the end of his life, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. author] 3.160; μ. ἡμερέων ἑπτά [prev. author] 6.12; μέχρι Πυθίων 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 5.1; μέχρι ἡλίου δύντος “IG” 12.188.4.]]

__II.3
of Measure or Degree, μ. τοῦ δικαίου so far as consists with right, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 3.82; μ. τοῦ δυνατοῦ 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 498e]]; μ. ὑγιείας, μ. ἡδονῆς,[[prev. work] 559a, “Grg.” 500b; μ. θανάτου NT.Phil.2.8.]

__II.4
with Numbers to express a round sum, up to, about, nearly, μ. δώδεκα [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Symposium” 2.8, etc.]]: sometimes without altering the case of the substantive, τοὺς μ. τριάκοντα ἔτη γεγονότας [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aeschines Orator 2.133; but πίνειν.. τοὺς μ. ἐτῶν τριάκοντα 4th-3rd c.BC: Apollodorus Carystius Comicus 5.19]]; μ. τινὸς πλήθους up to a certain number, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aeneas Tacticus 15.3]]: hence, just short of, μ. κόρου μετρεῖσθαι [Refs 1st c.AD+ [1st c.AD: Josephus Historicus “Bellum Judaicum” 2.8.5.]]

in [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus, μέχρι οὗ]] is sometimes used like the simple μέχρι, μέχρι οὗ ὀκτὼ πύργων [Refs [1.181; μέχρι οὗ τροπέων τῶν θερινέων 2.19; μ. ὅτεν πληθώρης ἀγορῆς [prev. work] 173.]]

__III
as a conjunction, until, with indicative, μέχρι.. ὁρμὴ ἐνέπεσε [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 4.4, compare 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Symposium” 220d; μ. σκότος ἐγένετο 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 4.2.4]]; μέχρι ἄν with subjunctive [Refs [, [prev. work] 1.4.13, 2.3.24; μέχρις ἂν ἥλιος δύῃ “IG” 12(5).647.17 (from Ceos)]]; μέχρις κε μένῃ [NT+5th c.BC+ [3rd c.BC: Callimachus Epicus “Sosibii Victoria” 5.4: rarely without ἄν, μ. τοῦτο ἴδωμεν 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 4.119; μ. πλοῦς γένηται 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 1.137; μ. οὗ τι δόξῃ [prev. author] 3.28; μέχρι τέκῃ 3rd c.BC: Callimachus Epicus “Sosibii Victoria” 5.5; μέχρις οὗ εἴπῃ 3rd c.BC: Herodas Mimographus 2.43; μ. καταντήσωμεν NT.Eph.4.13; μέχρις ἵνα ψαύσειε 3rd c.BC: Callimachus Epicus “Hymnus in Dianam” 28 (assuming variant)]]: with infinitive, μ. σβεσθῆναι τὸ πῦρ [Refs 1st c.AD+ [2nd c.AD: Appianus Historicus “Ἰβηρική” 75; μέχρις ἠῶ δῖαν ἱκέσθαι 4th c.AD(?): Quintus Smyrnaeus Epicus 1.830; also μέχρι ἂν ἕξιν λαβεῖν 1st c.AD: Cebes Philosophus 35.]]

as long as, whilst, with indicative, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 3.10, 98, 2nd c.BC: Polybius Historicus 1.62.4]]; μ. ἄν with subjunctive, μέχρις ἂν ζῶσιν πονεῖν [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-3rd c.BC: Menander Comicus 633; μέχρις ἂν ἐνδημῶσιν οἱ πρέσβεις 4th c.BC: Aeneas Tacticus 10.11, compare 1st-2nd c.AD: Epictetus Philosophus “Enchiridion” 11]]; Doric dialect μέχρι κα ζώη [Refs 2nd c.BC+ [“GDI” 1807.7 (2nd c.BC), +others]]—The μετώπο-ι is elided in [Refs [“IG” 12.115.15, “Supp.epigram” [same place]]] —Cf. ἄχρι throughout and entry near the end

deep_entry:
Abbott-Smith / STEPBible (TBESG)
μή,
subjective negative particle,
used where the negation depends on a condition or hypothesis, expressed or understood, as distinct from οὐ, which denies absolutely. μή is used where one thinks a thing is not, as distinct from an absolute negation. As a general rule, οὐ negatives the indic, μή the other moods, incl, ptcp. [In LXX for אֵין ,אַיִן ,אַל ]
__I. As a neg. adv., not;
__1. with ref. to thought or opinion: Jhn.3:18, Tit.1:11, 2Pe.1:9.
__2. In delib. questions, with subjc. (M, Pr., 185): Mrk.12:14, Rom.3:8.
__3. In conditional and final sentences, after εἰ, ἐάν, ἄν, ἵνα, ὅπως: Mat.10:14, Mrk.6:11 12:19, Luk.9:5, Jhn.6:50, Rom.11:25, al.
__4. C. inf. (see M, Pr., 234f., 239, 255),
__(a) after verbs of saying, etc.: Mat.2:12 5:34, Mrk.12:18, Act.15:38, Rom.2:21, al.;
__(b) with artic. inf.: after a prep., Mat.13:5, Mrk.4:5, Act.7:19, 1Co.10:6, al.; without a prep., Rom.14:13, 2Co.2:1, 13 1Th 4:6;
__(with) in sentences expressing consequence, after ὥστε: Mat.8:28, Mrk.3:20, 1Co.1:7, 2Co.3:7, al.
__5. C. ptcp. (see M, Pr., 231f., 239), in hypothetical references to persons of a certain character or description: Mat.10:28 12:30, Luk.6:49, Jhn.3:18, Rom.4:5, 1Co.7:38, 1Jn.3:10, al.; where the person or thing being definite, the denial is a matter of opinion: Jhn.6:64, 1Co.1:28 4:7, 18, 2Co.5:21, al.; where the ptcp. has a concessive, causal or conditional force, if, though, because not: Mat.18:25, Luk.2:45, Jhn.7:49, Act.9:26, Rom.2:14 5:13, 2Co.3:14, Gal.6:9, Ju 5; where the ptcp. has a descriptive force (being such as), not: Act.9:9, Rom.1:28, 1Co.10:33, Gal.4:8, Heb.12:27, al.
__6. μή prohibitive, in indep. sentences,
__(a) with subjc. praes., 1 of person(s) pl.: Gal.5:26 6:9, 1Th.5:6, 1Jn.3:18;
__(b) with imperat. praes., usually where one is bidden to desist from what has already begun (cf. M, Pr., 122ff.): Mat.7:1, Mrk.5:36, Luk.6:30, Jhn.2:16 5:45, Act.10:15, Rom.11:18, Jas.2:1, Rev.5:5, al.;
__(with) forbidding that which is still future: with imperat. aor., 3 of person(s), Mat.24:18, Mrk.13:15, Luk.17:31, al.; with subjc. aor., 2 of person(s), Mat.3:9 10:26, Mrk.5:7, Luk.6:29, Jhn.3:7, Rom.10:6, al.;
__(d) with optative, in wishes: 2Ti.4:16 (LXX); μὴ γένοιτο (see M, Pr., 194; Bl., §66, 1), Luk.20:16, Rom.3:3, al.; μή τις, Mrk.13:5, al.
__II. As a conj.,
__1. after verbs of fearing, caution, etc., that, lest, perhaps (M, Pr., 192f.): with subjc. praes., Heb.12:15; with subjc. aor., Mat.24:4, Mrk.13:5, Luk.21:8, Act.13:40, Gal.5:15, al.; ὅρα μή (see M, Pr., 124, 178), elliptically, Rev.19:10 22:9; with indic, fut. (M, Pr., l.with), Col.2:8.
__2. in order that not: with subjc. aor., Mrk.13:36, 2Co.8:20 12:6.
__III. Interrogative, in hesitant questions (M, Pr., 170), or where a negative answer is expected: Mat.7:9, 10, Mrk.2:19, Jhn.3:4, Rom.3:3 10:18, 19, 1Co.1:13, al.; μή τις, Luk.22:35, al.; before οὐ (Rom.10:17, al. in Pl.), expecting an affirm, ans.; οὐ μή, Luk.18:7, Jhn.18:11.
__IV. οὐ μή as emphatic negation (cf. M, Pr., 188, 190ff.; Bl. §64, 5), not at all, by no means: with indic, fut., Mat.16:22, Jhn.6:35, Heb.10:17, al.; with subjc. aor., Mat.24:2, Mrk.13:2, Luk.6:37, Jhn.13:8, 1Co.8:13, al.
(AS)

---

LSJ / STEPBible (TFLSJ)
μή,
Elean μά [ᾱ] [Refs 6th c.BC+ [“SIG” 9.5 (Olympia, 6th c.BC)]]. (Cf. Sanskrit mā´, Armenian mi [from I.-[Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus]] mē´], negative used in prohibitions):—not, the negative of the will and thought, as οὐ of fact and statement; μή rejects, οὐ denies; μή is relative, οὐ absolute; μή subjective, οὐ objective. (A few examples of μηδέ and μηδείς have been included.)

__A
in INDEPENDENT sentences, used in expressions of will or wish, command, entreaty, warning,

__A.1
with present imperative, 2 person, μή μ᾽ ἐρέθιζε [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 1.32, +others; 3 _person_, μή μευ πειράτω 9.345, etc.]]: rarely with aorist imperative, μὴ.. ἔνθεο τιμῇ [Refs 8th c.BC+ [4.410, compare 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 24.248]]; in Attic dialect, μὴ ψεῦσον, ὦ Ζεῦ, τῆς.. ἐλπίδος [Refs 8th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Thesmophoriazusae” 870; 3 _person_, μή τις ἀκουσάτω 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 16.301, compare 5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “O.” 8.55, “P.” 5.23, 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Septem contra Thebas” 1041, 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Ajax” 1180; μηδεὶς νομισάτω, προσδοκησάτω 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 7.5.73, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Apologia” 17c: with]]perfect imperative [Refs 8th c.BC+ [3 _person_, μή τις ὀπίσσω τετράφθω 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 12.272; or 2]] person when perfect = present, μὴ κεκράγετε [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Vespae” 415.]]

__A.2

__A.2.b
with present or aorist subjunctive in a warning or statement of fear, μὴ.. γένησθε take care you do not become, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 5.487]]; μὴ.. ὑφαίνῃσιν I fear.. may prove to be weaving, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 5.356; αἷμα μὴ σοῖς ἐξομόρξωμαι πέπλοις 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Hercules Furens” 1399]]: in Attic dialect Prose, to make a polite suggestion of apprehension or hesitation, perhaps, μὴ ἀγροικότερον ᾖ τὸ ἀληθὲς εἰπεῖν [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Gorgias” 462e, compare “Tht.” 188d, 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Politica” 1291a8, +others]]: in later Greek the indicative is found, μὴ ἡ ἔννοια ἡμῶν.. ἀντιλαμβάνεται [Refs 5th c.AD+ [5th-6th c.AD: Damascius Philosophus “de Principiis” 27.]]
