when the thing feared is future, mostly with subjunctive: with present subjunctive, δεινῶς ἀθυμῶ μὴ βλέπων ὁ μάντις ᾖ shall proveto be.., [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Tyrannus” 747, compare “Ant.” 1113; ὅρα μὴ κυβεύῃς 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Protagoras” 314a]]: more frequently with aorist, δείδοικα.. μή σε παρείπῃ [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 1.555, compare 9.244, 13.745]]: with perfect, shall prove to have been, δέδοικα μὴ περαιτέρω πεπραγμέν᾽ ᾖ μοι [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Trachiniae” 663, compare “Ph.” 494, 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 3.119, 4.140, etc.]]: less frequently with future indicative, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 2.3.6, 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Ecclesiazusae” 488, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Philebus” 13a]]: with optative according to the sequence of moods and tenses: present optative, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Trachiniae” 482, 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 1.10.9]]: aorist, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 11.634, etc.]]: perfect, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 1.3.10]]: with future optative in oratio obliqua, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. author] “HG” 6.4.27, “Mem.” 1.2.7, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Euthyphro” 15d: with _optative_ and ἄν, 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Trachiniae” 631, 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus]]vect.4.41.

__B.8.b
when the action is present or past, the indicative is used, εἰσόρα μὴ σκῆψιν οὐκ οὖσαν τίθης [Refs 8th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Electra” 584, compare 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Ion” 1523, 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Nubes” 493, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Laches” 196c; ὅρα μὴ παίζων ἔλεγεν [prev. author] “Tht.” 145b, compare 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Helena” 119; φοβούμεθα μὴ ἀμφοτέρων ἡμαρτήκαμεν 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 3.53, compare 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Orestes” 209, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Lysis” 218d; δείδω μὴ δὴ πάντα θεὰ νημερτέα εἶπεν 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 5.300.]]

__B.8.c
with indicative and subjunctive in consecutive clauses, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Phoenissae” 93.]]

__C
in QUESTIONS:

__C.I
direct questions,

__C.I.1
with indicative, where aneg. answer is anticipated (but more generally in [Refs 8th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Agamemnon” 683 (Lyric poetry), 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Coloneus” 1502, “Tr.” 316, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Gorgias” 488b), in 8th c.BC: Homerus Epicus only ἦ μή..; 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 6.200, 9.405]]; μή σοι δοκοῦμεν..; [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Persae” 344, compare “Pr.” 249, 959, etc.: in Trag. and _Attic dialect_ frequently ἆρα μ; [prev. author] “Th.” 208, 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Electra” 446, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 405a: for questions in which μή]] (μηδέ) follows οὐ, see at {οὐ μή}.

__C.I.1.b
in other questions, τί μὴ ποιήσ; what am I not to do? [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Electra” 1276 (Lyric poetry)]]; τί μ; why not? [Refs [[prev. author] “Aj.” 668 (assuming variant)]]; compare μήν

__C.I.2
with subjunctive, when the speaker deliberates about a negative action, μὴ οὕτω φῶμε; [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 335c, compare 337b, 417b]]; ὁ τοιοῦτος μὴ δῷ δίκη; [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 21.35]]; πῶς μὴ φῶμε; [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Theaetetus” 161e: with _optative_ and ἄν, πῶς ἄν τις μὴ θυμῷ λέγοι]]; how can a man help being excited when he speaks? [Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. author] “Lg.” 887c, compare “Grg.” 510d, 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Memorabilia” 3.1.10.]]

__C.II
indirect questions, frequently with Verbs implying fear and apprehension [Refs 8th c.BC+ [compare (5th c.BC: Bacchylides Lyricus 8), ὄφρα ἴδωμεν μὴ τοὶ κοιμήσωνται 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 10.98, compare 101, 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 21.395; περισκοπῶ μή πού τις.. ἐγχρίμπτει 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Electra” 898, compare 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 2.13, etc.]]; also σκοπεῖσθαι πῶς ἂν μή.. [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Isocrates Orator 5.8, compare 15.6]]; later in simple indirect questions, ἐπυνθάνετο μὴ ἔγνω [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd c.AD(?): Antoninus Liberalis Mythographus 23.5.]]

__C.II.2
in questions introduced by εἰ, ἤρετό με.. εἰ μὴ μέμνημαι [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aeschines Orator 2.36 (εἰ οὐκ in same sense, 1.84): in the second part of a disjunctive question, εἰ.. ἢ (or εἴτε) μή.., εἴτε.. εἴτε μή.., 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Eumenides” 468, 612, 5th-6th c.BC: Andocides Orator 1.7, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Apologia” 18a, “R.” 457d, 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 2.1.7]]; εἴτε.. εἴτε μή.., εἰ.. ἢ οὔ, εἰ.. ἢ μή without difference of meaning between μή and οὐ, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Isaeus Orator 8.9; so also, τοὺς νόμους καταμανθάνειν εἰ καλῶς κεῖνται ἢ μή,.. τοὺς λόγους, εἰ ὀρθῶς διδάσκουσι τὸ πρᾶγμα ἢ οὔ 5th c.BC: Antipho Orator 5.14.]]

__D
POSITION of μή. When the negative extends its power over the whole clause, μή properly precedes the Verb. When its force is limited to single words, it precedes those words. But Poets sometimes put μή after the Verb, ὄλοιο μή πω [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Philoctetes” 961]]; φράσῃς.. μὴ πέρα[Refs [[prev. work] 332, compare “OC” 1522.]]

__D.2
μή is sometimes repeated, μή, μή καλέσῃς [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Vespae” 1418, compare 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Ajax” 190, “OC” 210 (both Lyric poetry).]]

__E
PROSODY: in Trag. μή may be joined by synizesis with a following ει or ου, μὴ οὐ, μὴ εἰδέναι, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Tyrannus” 13, 221, “Tr.” 321, etc.]]: initial ε after μή is cut off by aphaeresis, μὴ 'πὁθουν [Refs [[prev. author] “Aj.” 962; μὴ 'μβαίνῃς [prev. author] “OC” 400; μὴ 'γώ [prev. author] “Ph.” 910: in Prose, μὴ 'κ “IG” 12.115.11: μή]] followed by α is sometimes written μἀ.. (see. μὴ ἀλλά, etc.); sometimes separately, μὴ ἀδικεῖν [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Eumenides” 85, etc.]]

__F
μή in COMPOSITION (joined with other words), as μὴ ἀλλά, μὴ γάρ, μὴ οὐ, μὴ ὅπως or ὅτι, μή ποτε, etc., will be found in alphabetical order.

elsewhere relative, in which place, where,[Refs 8th c.BC+ [2.558, 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 9.136, 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 2.133, 9.27, 54, 5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “O.” 1.95, 5th c.BC: Bacchylides Lyricus 10.79, 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Prometheus Vinctus” 21, +others, 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Electra” 22, 855, 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Ranae” 1231, etc.]]: rarely in Attic dialect Prose, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Lysias Orator 13.72 (see. below), 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Apologia” 17c, “Phlb.” 61b]]; ἵ. ἡ Νίκη (i.e. ἐστίν) [Refs 8th c.BC+ [“IG” 22.1407.13: rare in later Greek, 2nd c.AD: Arrianus Historicus “Anabasis” 1.3.2, 2nd c.AD: Lucianus Sophista “Cont.” 22, “Ind.” 3: with particles, ἵ. τε 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 20.478; ἵ. περ 24.382, 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 13.364, 5th c.BC: Lysias Orator]] [same place]; ἵν᾽ ἄν with subjunctive, wherever, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Coloneus” 405, 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Ion” 315]]; as indirect interrogative, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.179, 2.150, 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Hecuba” 1008.]]

special usages:

elliptical usages,

never, not ever, a double negative strengthening the denial; not at all, surely not

---

LSJ / STEPBible (TFLSJ)
οὐ μή,
in independent sentences, is used either in Denial or in Prohibition:

__I
in Denial,

__I.1
with subjunctive,

__I.1.a
chiefly of aorist, οὔ τι μὴ ληφθῶ δόλῳ [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Septem contra Thebas” 38, compare 199, 282, “Ch.” 895; οὔ τοί σ᾽ Ἀχαιῶν.. μή τις ὑβρίσῃ 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Ajax” 560, compare “El.” 42, 1029, “Ph.” 103, 381, “OT” 329, 771, “OC” 450, 1023 (see. below); οὔ τι μὴ φύγητε λαιψηρῷ ποδί 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Hecuba” 1039, compare “HF” 718; οὐ γὰρ μὴ ἀπώσηται 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.199, compare 7.53; οὐ μήποτε.. ἐσβάλωσιν 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 4.95, compare 5.69; οὐ μή ποθ᾽ ἁλῶ 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Acharnenses” 662, compare “V.” 394; οὐ μή ποτε δέξηται 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Phaedo” 105d, compare “Phdr.” 260e, “R.” 609b; οὐ μὴ κρατηθῶ 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 5.1.17, compare 3.2.8 (variant{δέξονται}), “An.” 4.8.13; so οὐδεὶς μή ποθ᾽ εὕρῃ κατ᾽ ἔμ᾽ οὐδὲν ἐλλειφθέν 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 18.246.]]

__I.1.b
rarely of present, mostly with Verbs expressing possibility or ability, οὐ μὴ δύνηται (variant{δυνήσεται}) [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 8.1.5, compare “An.” 2.2.12, “Hier.” 11.15; οὐ μὴ οἷός τ᾽ ᾖς 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 341b; οὐ γὰρ μὴ δυνατὸς ὦ [prev. author] “Phlb.” 48d: in 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Coloneus” 1023, for οὐ μή ποτε.. φυγόντες.. ἐπεύχωνται θεοῖς, two Mss. give ἐπεύξωνται]], and this has been adopted by most editions; and in [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Isaeus Orator 8.24, for οὐ μὴ εἰσίῃς Bekk. restored οὐ μὴ εἴσει εἰς..:—Note: οὐ μή]] with subjunctive probably arose from the ellipsis of a Verb or phrase expressing fear or apprehension; such words are sometimes expressed, οὐ γὰρ ἦν δεινὸν.. μὴ ἁλῷ κοτε [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.84, compare 7.235, 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Ecclesiazusae” 650, 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Memorabilia” 2.1.25, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Apologia” 28b, “Phd.” 84b, “Grg.” 520d, “R.” 465b.]]—Sts. there is no idea of fear, as in [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Philoctetes” 103, 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Iphigenia Taurica” 18]]; the construction is freely used after ὅτι, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 5.69, 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Historia Graeca (Hellenica)” 4.2.3, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 499b]]; after ὡς, since, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Aves” 461]]; after ὥστε, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Phaedrus” 227d.]]

__I.2
with future indicative, οὔ σοι μὴ μεθέψομαί ποτε [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Electra” 1052, compare “OC” 176 (Lyric poetry); οὐ μή σ᾽ ἐγὼ περιόψομαι 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Ranae” 508]]; οὐ μὴ δέξονται (variant{δέξωνται}) [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 3.2.8: the reading in [prev. author] “HG” 1.6.32 is doubtful: in indirect speech the _optative_ is used, ἐθέσπισεν ὡς οὐ μή ποτε πέρσοιεν 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Philoctetes” 611]]: or infinitive, εἶπεν.. οὐ μή ποτε.. εὖ πράξειν πόλιν [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Phoenissae” 1590.]]

__II
in Prohibition, οὐ μή is used interrogatively with future indicative (chiefly of the  2 _person_) so as to express a strong prohibition, οὐ μὴ 'ξεγερεῖς τὸν ὕπνῳ κάτοχο; ={μὴ ἐξέγειρε},[Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Trachiniae” 978 (_anapaest meter_)]]; οὐ μὴ προσοίσεις χεῖρα μηδ᾽ ἅψῃ πέπλων ; [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Hippolytus” 606, compare 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Nubes” 296, “Ra.” 298.—The prohibition is changed into a direct command by ἀλλά or δέ, οὐ μὴ λαλήσεις ἀλλ᾽ ἀκολουθήσεις ἐμο; [prev. author] “Nu.” 505, compare “Ra.” 202, 462, 524, 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Bacchae” 792]]; οὐ μὴ προσοίσεις χεῖρα βακχεύσεις δ᾽ ἰών;[Refs [[prev. work] 343, compare “Med.” 1151, “El.” 383.]]

__II.2
later οὐ μὴ ἐμπέσω let me not fall, [LXX.2Ki.24.14.]

__II.3
in questions, οὐ μή, = Latin nonne, ὁ θεὸς οὐ μὴ ποιήσῃ τὴν ἐκδίκησιν τῶν ἐκλεκτῶν αὐτοῦ ; [NT.Luke.18.7.]

__III
in [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Septem contra Thebas” 250, οὐ σῖγα μηδὲν τῶνδ᾽ ἐρεῖς κατὰ πτόλιν]]; seems to mean keep silent and say nothing.., σῖγα being short for σιγήσει and καὶ being omitted: similarly, οὐ σῖγ᾽ ἀνέξει, μηδὲ δειλίαν ἀρῇ; submit silently and do not play the coward, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Ajax” 75, compare “Tr.” 1183, “OT” 637, 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Hippolytus” 498, “Hel.” 437, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Symposium” 175a.]]

negative particle, related to οὐδέ as μή to οὐ,
__1. as conic., continuing a negation or prohibition, but not, and not, nor: preceded by μή, Mat.6:25 22:29, Mrk.12:24, Luk.14:12, al.; ἵνα μή, Jhn.4:15; ὅπως μή, Luk.16:26; μηδέ . . . μηδέ, neither . . . nor, Mat.10:10, 1Co.10:8-9.
__2. As adv., strengthening a negation, not even: Mrk.2:2, 1Co.5:11, al
(AS)

---

LSJ / STEPBible (TFLSJ)
μηδέ,
(μή, δέ) negative Particle (compare οὐδέ): as conjunction, and not (Epic dialect also, but not), nor, connecting two whole clauses, used with the same constructions as μή, μή τι σὺ ταῦτα.. διείρεο μηδὲ μετάλλα [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 1.550, etc.: without a _negative_ preceding, 4.302, etc.]]; τεκνοῦσθαι, μηδ᾽ ἄπαιδα θνῄσκειν [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Agamemnon” 754 (Lyric poetry), compare “Eu.” 714, “Supp.” 409; ὕδατος, μελίσσης, μηδὲ προσφέρειν μέθυ 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Coloneus” 481, compare 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 7.77.]]

__2
in μηδέ.. μηδέ.. the first μ. may belong to μηδέ A, e.g. [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 4.303f, or to μηδέ B, e.g. 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 391c; μήτε.. μηδέ 5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “I.” 2.45, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Protagoras” 327d]]; but μήτε cannot follow μηδέ:—for μηδέ after οὐδέ, see at {οὐ} [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus 11.3.]]

__B
as adverb, joined with a single word or phrase, not even, not either, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 21.375, 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 4.710, etc.]]; repeated emphatically, μηδ᾽ ὅντινα γαστέρι μήτηρ κοῦρον ἐόντα φέροι μηδ᾽ ὃς φύγοι let not the babe unborn —no let not even it escape, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 6.58; τὸ μήποτ᾽ αὖθις μηδ᾽ ἀναστῆναι 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Agamemnon” 569:]] —for μηδέ τι see at {μήτις}.

LSJ / STEPBible (TFLSJ)
μηδείς, μηδεμίᾰ, μηδέν
(i.e. μηδὲ εἷς, μηδὲ μία, μηδὲ ἕν): feminine μηδὲ ἴα or μηδεΐα (or -έϊα) [Refs [“IG” 12(2).6.12 (Mytil.)]]:— not one, not even one, nobody (in neuter nothing), once in [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Homerus Epicus (who elsewhere uses μή τις, see at {μήτις}), ἀναίνετο μηδὲν ἑλέσθαι 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 18.500; μή πως.. μηδὲν ἀνύσσῃς 8th-7th c.BC: Hesiodus Epicus “Opera et Dies” 395; μηδὲν ἄγαν 5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “Fragmenta.” 216, etc.: rare in _plural_ (μηδαμοί being used in _Ionic dialect_), μηδένες ἄλλοι 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Historia Graeca (Hellenica)” 5.4.20; μηδένας 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Euthydemus” 303c.]]

__2
μηδὲ εἷς (so written) is found in Attic dialect Inscrr., as [Refs [“IG” 12.114.41, 22.487.9 (μηδ᾽ hενί [prev. work]12.73.6), but is used especially in an emphatic sense,]]not even one, μηδὲ ἕν [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Plutus” 37]]: frequently with an intervening Particle or preposition, μηδ᾽ ἂν ἕνα [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Cratylus” 414d; μηδ᾽ ἐν ἑνὶ χρόνῳ [prev. author] “Prm.” 156c; μηδ᾽ ἐξ ἑνός [prev. author] “Phdr.” 245d; μηδ᾽ ἐφ᾽ ἑνί [prev. author] “R.” 553d; μηδὲ περὶ ἑνός [prev. author] “Tht.” 171c]]; μηδ᾽ ὑφ᾽ ἑνός, μηδ᾽ ὑπὸ μιᾶς, [Refs [[prev. author] “Smp.” 222d, Alcaeus1.122a; μηδὲ ὑφ᾽ ἑνός “IG” 12.32.8.]]

__II
nobody, naught, good for naught, κἄμ᾽ ἴσον τῷ μ. [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Coloneus” 918: _plural_, οὐ γὰρ ἠξίου τοὺς μηδένας [prev. author] “Aj.” 1114]]; μηδέν or τὸ μηδέν as substantive, naught, nothing, κεἰ τὸ μ. ἐξερῶ [Refs [[prev. author] “Ant.” 234]]; μ. λέγειν to say what is naught, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 8.3.20, etc.; ἡ ἡμετέρη εὐδαιμονίη.. ἀπέρριπται ἐς τὸ μ. 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.32; τοῦ μηδενὸς ἀξίη [prev. author] 6.137; ἐπὶ μηδὲν ἔρχεσθαι 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Electra” 1000; ἐς τὸ μ. ἥκειν 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Hecuba” 622]]; of persons, τὸ μ. a good-for-nothing, τὸ μ. εἶναι, of a eunuch, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 8.106; τοιγὰρ σὺ δέξαι μ᾽ ἐς τὸ σὸν στέγος, τὴν μηδὲν ἐς τὸ μ. 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Electra” 1166; κἂν τὸ μ. ὦ [prev. author] “Tr.” 1107; τὸ μ. ὄντας [prev. author] “Aj.” 1275; ὁ μ. ὤν [prev. work] 767; ὅτ᾽ οὐδὲν ὢν τοῦ μηδὲν ἀντέστης ὕπερ [prev. work] 1231, compare 1094, 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Hecuba” 843, etc.]]; ἧττον αὐτοῖς ἔνι ἢ τὸ μ., i.e. it is a mere impossibility, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Theaetetus” 180a]]; also μ. εἶναι without the Article, [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd c.AD: Lucianus Sophista “Rh.Pr.” 2.]]

__III
neuter μηδέν as adverb, not at all, by no means, μηδὲν ἐγκέλευ᾽ ἄγαν [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Prometheus Vinctus” 72, compare 344; μ. διαφέρειν πλὴν ὀνόματι 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Politicus” 280a, etc.]]: with an adverb, μ. αἰνικτηρίως [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Prometheus Vinctus” 949: frequently with _comparative_, μ. μᾶλλον, ἧσσον, etc., 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Ajax” 280, 1329, etc.]] — When other negatives, also derived from μή, are used with it, they do not destroy, but strengthen the negation, μηδέποτε μηδὲν αἰσχρὸν ποιήσας ἔλπιζε λήσειν never hope to escape, when you have done anything base. [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Isocrates Orator 1.16]]; compare μηθείς.

Doric dialect μᾶκος [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Archytas Tarentinus Philosophus 1]]: εος, τό:— length, of a club, τόσσον ἔην μῆκος, τόσσον πάχος so large was it in length, so large in thickness, [LXX+8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 9.324; φιλότης ἴση μ. τε πλάτος τε 5th c.BC: Empedocles Poeta Philosophus 17.20, compare 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.181, etc.; ἐς μῆκος [prev. author] 2.155; εἰς τὸ μῆκος LXX.Gen.12.6; ἐν μήκει καὶ πλάτει καὶ βάθει 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Sophista” 235d, compare 5th c.BC: Gorgias Rhetor et Sophista 3, 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Physica” 209a5]]; ἐπὶ μῆκος lengthwise, ἐπὶ μ. ἔκτασις [Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. author] “HA” 504a15, +others; κατὰ μῆκος [prev. author] “Mete.” 387a2; μ. ὁδοῦ 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Fragmenta - American Journal of Philology” 378, 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.72, etc.; πλοῦ 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 6.34]]; μᾶκος ἔδικε threw a long distance, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “O.” 10(11).72: _plural_, μήκη καὶ βάθη καὶ πλάτη 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Politicus” 284e, compare 4th c.AD: Iamblichus Philosophus “de communi mathematica scientia” 26]]; τὰ μεγάλα μ. great lengths, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Protagoras” 356d.]]

__b
height, of a wall, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Aves” 1130]]; of persons, stature, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 20.71]]; μῆκος in height,[Refs 5th c.BC+ [11.312; εἰς μ. αὐξάνεσθαι 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Respublica Lacedaemoniorum” 2.6.]]

__c
generally, μήκει in linear measurement, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Theaetetus” 147d, compare 148a]]; linearity, one-dimensional magnitude, opposed to ἐπίπεδον, βάθος, [Refs [[prev. author] “Lg.” 817e]]: in Arith., in the first power, [Refs [Theol.Ar. 3,4.]]

__2
of Time, μ. χρόνου [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Prometheus Vinctus” 1020; ἐν μ. χρόνου 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Trachiniae” 69; ἐν χρόνου τινὸς μήκεσιν ἀπλέτοις 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Leges” 683a]]; μ. λόγου, μ. τῶν λόγων, a long speech, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Eumenides” 201, 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Coloneus” 1139; ἐν μήκει λόγων διελθεῖν 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 4.62]]; μῆκος at length, εἰπέ μοι μὴ μ., ἀλλὰ σύντομα [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Antigone” 446.]]

__3
of Size or Degree, greatness, magnitude, ὄλβου [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Empedocles Poeta Philosophus 119]]; μῆκος in greatness, ἔοικεν ἄλλῃ μ. οὐδὲν ἡδονῇ [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Antigone” 393.]]

__4
longitude, [Refs 1st c.BC+ [1st c.BC-1st c.AD: Strabo Geographus 1.4.5, 2nd c.AD: Cleomedes Astronomus 2.1, 1st c.BC: Ptolemaeus Epigrammaticus “Alm.” 2.12, 2nd c.AD: Vettius Valens Astrologus 260.5, etc.]]

__5
in Prosody, length, opposed to βραχύτης, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Poetica” 1456b32, 1st c.BC: Dionysius Halicarnassensis “de Compositione Verborum” 15: _plural_, μήκη καὶ βραχύτητας προσῆπτε 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 400b.]]

__6
first line of phalanx, [Refs 1st c.BC+ [1st c.BC: Asclepiodotus Tacticus “Tact.” 2.5. (From same Root as μακρός. Hence μήκιστος, _superlative_ of μακρός.)]]

LSJ / STEPBible (TFLSJ)
μηκύν-ω,
Doric dialect μᾱκ- [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus (see. below)]]: future - ῠνῶ [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 4.17]], Ionic dialect -ῠνέω [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 2.35]]: aorist ἐμήκῡνα [Refs [[prev. author] 3.60:]] —middle, see below [Refs [7]]:—passive, perfect μεμήκυσμαι [Refs 1st c.BC+ [1st c.BC: Philodemus Gadarensis Epigrammaticus (see. below), Eust.ad 2nd c.AD: Dionysius Periegeta 64]]:— lengthen, prolong, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Hippocrates Medicus “ἀφορισμοί” 1.12; τὸ μέτωπον τῆς τάξεως 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “de Equitum magistro” 4.9; τὰς ὁδούς [prev. author] “Mem.” 3.13.5; μηκυνθέν τε καὶ σχὸν πλάτος 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Politicus” 282e]]; of Time, μ. χρόνον, βίον, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Hercules Furens” 87, 143]]:—passive, νοσεύματα μηκυνθέντα [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Hippocrates Medicus “Aër.” 7; ἐμηκύνετο ὁ πόλεμος 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 1.102.]]

__2
delay, put off, τέλος [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “P.” 4.286.]]

__3
μ. λόγον, λόγους, spin out a speech, speak at length, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 2.35, 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Electra” 1484; τέκν᾽ εἰ φανέντ᾽ ἄελπτα μηκύνω λόγον [prev. author] “OC” 1120; τὴν ἀπολογίαν 5th-6th c.BC: Isocrates Orator 11.44; λόγους μακροτέρους 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 4.17: without λόγον]], to be lengthy or tedious, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 3.60, 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Lysistrata” 1132, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 437a, 1st c.BC: Dionysius Halicarnassensis “de Compositione Verborum” 23]]; μ. περί τινος enlarge upon.., [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demetrius Phalereus Rhetor “Demetrius on Style” 71: _accusative_ objecti, μ. τὰ περὶ τῆς πόλεως, τὴν ὠφελίαν]], talk at length about, dwell upon.., [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 2.42, 43]]:—passive, to be expounded at length, αὖθις ταῦτα μηκυνθήσεται [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-3rd c.BC: Epicurus Philosophus “De rerum natura - Wien. Stud.” 14.5; μεμηκυσμένον σύγγραμμα 1st c.BC: Philodemus Philosophus “περὶ ποιημάτων” 5.26]]; to be continually repeated, [Refs 1st c.BC+ [1st c.BC: Dionysius Halicarnassensis “de Compositione Verborum” 12]]; to be dwelt upon, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demetrius Phalereus Rhetor “Demetrius on Style” 137.]]

__4
μ. βοήν raise a loud cry, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Coloneus” 489.]]

__5
Grammars, lengthen a syllable, [Refs 1st c.BC+ [1st c.BC-1st c.AD: Strabo Geographus 10.5.8]]:—passive, [Refs 1st c.BC+ [1st c.BC: Dionysius Halicarnassensis “de Compositione Verborum” 15, 1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus 2.275f, 2nd c.AD: Apollonius Dyscolus Grammaticus “de Adverbiis;” 146.18]]; φωνῆεν μηκυνόμενον a vowel capable of being scanned long, as αιυ, [Refs 7th c.AD+ [7th c.AD: Hephaestio Grammaticus 1.4.]]

__6
Arith., multiply by a fresh factor, [Refs [Theol.Ar. 24,48.]]

__7
middle, ἐμακύναντο κολοσσόν reared a tall statue, [Refs [“Anthologia Graeca” 6.171.]]

deep_entry:
Abbott-Smith / STEPBible (TBESG)
μήν
a particle of assurance, verily, truly; εἰ (εἶ) μ. (= cl., ἦ μ. in LXX and π.), now verily, full surely: Heb.6:14 (LXX).†
(AS)

---

LSJ / STEPBible (TFLSJ)
μήν,
Doric dialect [Refs 5th c.BC+ [(5th c.BC: Epicharmus Comicus 78, etc.)]], Aeolic dialect [Refs 7th c.BC+ [(7th-6th c.BC: Sappho Lyrica “Papyrus fragments” in E. Diehl, 23.5, etc.)]], and old Epic dialect μάν (in Hom.always followed by a vowel except [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 5.895, 765, whereas μήν]] is followed by a consonant except in [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 19.45]]; original μάν has probably been changed to μέν except when the metre prevented), a Particle used to strengthen asseverations, verily, truly; a synonym of μέν but stronger, and like it always following the word which begins the clause, ὧδε γὰρ ἐξερέω, καὶ μ. τετελεσμένον ἔσται and so verily.., [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 23.410]]; ἴστε μὰν.. ye know doubtless, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “I.” 4(3).35: frequently with _imperative_, ἄγε μ.]] on then, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 1.302; ἄγρει μάν 5.765; ἄναγε μάν 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Choephori” 963 (Lyric poetry); ἕπεο μάν 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Coloneus” 182 (Lyric poetry).]]

__II
after other Particles,

__II.1
ἦ μήν, now verily, full surely, ἦ μὴν καὶ πόνος ἐστίν [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 2.291, compare “hymnus ad Apollinem” 87, 8th-7th c.BC: Hesiodus Epicus “Scutum Herculis” 101; ἦ μάν 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 2.370, 13.354, Sapph.[same place], 5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “P.” 4.40, +others (εἶ μάν “IG” 5 (1).1390.27 (Andania, 1st c.BC))]]: strengthened, ἦ δὴ μάν [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 17.538]]: frequently later in strong protestations or oaths, with infinitive, ὄμνυσι δ᾽ ἦ μὴν λαπάξειν [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Septem contra Thebas” 531, compare 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Trachiniae” 1186, 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 2.3.26: in negation, ἦ μ. μή.. 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 8.81, etc. (but also ὀμνύω μὴ μὰν φρονησεῖν “SIG” 527.36 (Crete, 3rd c.BC))]]: in Prose also to begin an independent clause, ὀμνύω.., ἦ μ. ἐγὼ ἐθυόμην [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 6.1.31; καὶ νὴ τὸν κύνα,.. ἦ μ. ἐγὼ ἔπαθόν τι τοιοῦτον 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Apologia” 22a.]]

__II.2
καὶ μήν, sometimes simply to add an asseveration, see entry [near the start],[Refs 5th c.BC+ [compare 5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “N.” 2.13, etc.; καὶ δὴ μάν 3rd c.BC: Theocritus Poeta Bucolicus 7.120]]: frequently to introduce something new or deserving special attention, καὶ μὴν Τάνταλον εἰσεῖδον [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 11.582, compare 593, 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Prometheus Vinctus” 459, “Pers.” 406, etc.]]; especially in dramatic Poets to mark the entrance of a person on the stage, here comes.., [Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. author] “Th.” 372, 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Electra” 339; also ὅδε μ. Αἵμων 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Antigone” 626 (_anapaest meter_)]], etc.; of new facts, and besides, nay more, καὶ μήν.. γε [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Prometheus Vinctus” 982, compare 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Pax” 369, 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Symposium” 4.15, etc.]]; in Orators to introduce new arguments, καὶ μήν.. γε [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Theaetetus” 153b, 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 21.56]]; to introduce a counter-argument, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Nubes” 1185, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Gorgias” 452c; καὶ μὴν καί 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 27.30, etc.: also in answers, to denote approbation or assent, ἀλλ᾽ ἢν ἐφῇς μοι.. λέξαιμ᾽ ἂν ὀρθῶς. Answ. καὶ μ. ἐφίημι]] well, I allow it, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Electra” 556]]; μὴ νῦν διάτριβ᾽, ἀλλ᾽ ἄνυε πράττων.. Answ. καὶ μ. βαδίζω [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Plutus” 413 (variant), compare “Ra.” 895, 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Hecuba” 317; so καὶ μ... γε 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 426e, etc.]]

__II.3
ἀλλὰ μήν, yet truly, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. author] “Pers.” 233, etc.; ἀλλὰ μάν 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Acharnenses” 765; ἀλλὰ μήν.. γε [prev. author] “Ra.” 258]]; to allege something not disputed, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Theaetetus” 187a: rarely separated, ἀλλ᾽ ἐστὶ μ. οἰκητός 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Coloneus” 28]]; ἀλλ᾽ οὐδ᾽ ἐγὼ μ... [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Hecuba” 401: more strongly, ὅμως μ. 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Politicus” 297d.]]

__II.4
ναὶ μήν, above all, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Empedocles Poeta Philosophus 76.2.]]

__II.5
οὐ μήν, of a truth not, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 24.52, 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Agamemnon” 1068, etc.: elsewhere in 8th c.BC: Homerus Epicus οὐ μάν, 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 12.318, etc.]]; μὴ μάν (Attic dialect μὴ μήν) oh do not, [Refs [8.512, 15.476]], etc.; ἀλλ᾽ οὐ μάν [Refs 5th c.BC+ [17.41; ἀλλ᾽ οὐ μάν.. γε 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Coloneus” 153 (Lyric poetry); οὐδὲ μάν 5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “P.” 4.87.]]

__II.6
ὡς μήν, = {ἦ μήν}, ὀμμνύω Δία.. ὡς μ. κρινεῖν τὰ ἀντιλεγόμενα [Refs [“Delph.” 3(1).362 i 40.]]

__III
after interrogatives, τί μ.; well, what of it? [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Eumenides” 203, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Theaetetus” 145e, etc.]]; τί μ. οὔ well, why not? [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Rhesus” 706 (Lyric poetry)]]; τῶς μ.; well, but how.. ? [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 1.6.28; τίνος μ. ἕνεκ; [prev. passage]; ποῦ μ.]]; to express surprise, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Theaetetus” 142a]]; ἀλλὰ πότε μή; [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Symposium” 4.23.]]

__IV
with adversative force, especially after a negative, so that it is equivalent to μέντοι, νῦν ἐμὲ μὲν στυγέει.., ἔσται μὰν ὅτ᾽ ἄν.. [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 8.370 - 373; οὐ μὴν ἄτιμοι.. τεθνήξομεν 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Agamemnon” 1279]]; ἀνάγκη μὲν καὶ ταῦτ᾽ ἐπίστασθαι.., οὐδὲν μ. κωλύει κτλ. [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Phaedrus” 268e, compare “Grg.” 493c, “R.” 529e, etc.; χαλεπῶς ἔχει ὑπὸ τραυμάτων, μᾶλλον μ. αὐτὸν αἱρεῖ τὸ νόσημα [prev. author] “Tht.” 142b]]; expressed more strongly by γε μ., [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “P.” 7.18, 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Septem contra Thebas” 1067 (_anapaest meter_), 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Coloneus” 587, 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 6.1.7, etc.; also οὐ μ... γε 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Prometheus Vinctus” 270, “Th.” 538]]; οὐδὲ μ.[Refs [[prev. work] 809, “Ch.” 189]]; οὐ μ. οὐδέ nor yet indeed, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 1.3, 82, etc.; οὐ μὰν οὐδέ 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 4.512; ἀλλ᾽ οὐ μὰν οὐδέ 23.441:—on οὐ μὴν ἀλλά, see at {ἀλλά} II.5.]]

Included with:  μείς, μηνός, ὁ,
nominative singular μείς [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 19.117, 8th-7th c.BC: Hesiodus Epicus “Opera et Dies” 557, “hymnus ad Mercurium” 11, 6th c.BC: Anacreon Lyricus 6.1, 5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “N.” 5.44, 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 2.82, 5th c.BC: Hippocrates Medicus “περὶ ἑπταμήνου” 3 (variant), 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Cratylus” 409c, “Ti.” 39c, 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “de Generatione Animalium” 777b23, 4th-3rd c.BC: Theophrastus Philosophus “de Signis Tempestatum” 27, 3rd c.BC: Callimachus Epicus “Hecale” 1.1.12, “SIG” 1009. 27 (Chalcedon, 3rd-2nd c.BC), 1047.46 (Amorgos, 2nd-1st c.BC), “IG” 9(1).682 (Corc., 4th c.BC), 3rd c.BC: Chrysippus Stoicus 2.199, 4th c.BC: Eudoxus Astronomus “Ars Prooem.”, 13.1, 2nd c.BC: Ezekiel Poeta Judaeus “Exagoge - Mnemosyne” 153, 1st c.BC-1st c.AD: Strabo Geographus 13.1.64, “Sammelb.” 1191]]; Ind.” p.81 M.]]

with accusative et participle, πρὸς τὸν βασιλέα μ. τινὰ ἔχοντα show that he has, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 2.121. γ᾽; ἐξ ἐπιβουλῆς ἀποθανόντα τινὰ μ. 5th c.BC: Antipho Orator 2.1.5; γεγονὼς ἐμηνύθη πόλεμος 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Criti.” [same place]: the]]participle is sometimes omitted, τόδ᾽ ἔργον.. σε μηνύει κακόν (i.e. ὄντα) [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Hippolytus” 1077]]: with accusative et infinitive, [ποιηταὶ] ταῦτα οὕτως ἔχειν μ. deep_entry:
Abbott-Smith / STEPBible (TBESG)
μὴ οὐκ, see: μή, III.
μή,
subjective negative particle,
used where the negation depends on a condition or hypothesis, expressed or understood, as distinct from οὐ, which denies absolutely. μή is used where one thinks a thing is not, as distinct from an absolute negation. As a general rule, οὐ negatives the indic, μή the other moods, incl, ptcp. [In LXX for אֵין ,אַיִן ,אַל ]
__I. As a neg. adv., not;
__1. with ref. to thought or opinion: Jhn.3:18, Tit.1:11, 2Pe.1:9.
__2. In delib. questions, with subjc. (M, Pr., 185): Mrk.12:14, Rom.3:8.
__3. In conditional and final sentences, after εἰ, ἐάν, ἄν, ἵνα, ὅπως: Mat.10:14, Mrk.6:11 12:19, Luk.9:5, Jhn.6:50, Rom.11:25, al.
__4. C. inf. (see M, Pr., 234f., 239, 255),
__(a) after verbs of saying, etc.: Mat.2:12 5:34, Mrk.12:18, Act.15:38, Rom.2:21, al.;
__(b) with artic. inf.: after a prep., Mat.13:5, Mrk.4:5, Act.7:19, 1Co.10:6, al.; without a prep., Rom.14:13, 2Co.2:1, 13 1Th 4:6;
__(with) in sentences expressing consequence, after ὥστε: Mat.8:28, Mrk.3:20, 1Co.1:7, 2Co.3:7, al.
__5. C. ptcp. (see M, Pr., 231f., 239), in hypothetical references to persons of a certain character or description: Mat.10:28 12:30, Luk.6:49, Jhn.3:18, Rom.4:5, 1Co.7:38, 1Jn.3:10, al.; where the person or thing being definite, the denial is a matter of opinion: Jhn.6:64, 1Co.1:28 4:7, 18, 2Co.5:21, al.; where the ptcp. has a concessive, causal or conditional force, if, though, because not: Mat.18:25, Luk.2:45, Jhn.7:49, Act.9:26, Rom.2:14 5:13, 2Co.3:14, Gal.6:9, Ju 5; where the ptcp. has a descriptive force (being such as), not: Act.9:9, Rom.1:28, 1Co.10:33, Gal.4:8, Heb.12:27, al.
__6. μή prohibitive, in indep. sentences,
__(a) with subjc. praes., 1 of person(s) pl.: Gal.5:26 6:9, 1Th.5:6, 1Jn.3:18;
__(b) with imperat. praes., usually where one is bidden to desist from what has already begun (cf. M, Pr., 122ff.): Mat.7:1, Mrk.5:36, Luk.6:30, Jhn.2:16 5:45, Act.10:15, Rom.11:18, Jas.2:1, Rev.5:5, al.;
__(with) forbidding that which is still future: with imperat. aor., 3 of person(s), Mat.24:18, Mrk.13:15, Luk.17:31, al.; with subjc. aor., 2 of person(s), Mat.3:9 10:26, Mrk.5:7, Luk.6:29, Jhn.3:7, Rom.10:6, al.;
__(d) with optative, in wishes: 2Ti.4:16 (LXX); μὴ γένοιτο (see M, Pr., 194; Bl., §66, 1), Luk.20:16, Rom.3:3, al.; μή τις, Mrk.13:5, al.
__II. As a conj.,
__1. after verbs of fearing, caution, etc., that, lest, perhaps (M, Pr., 192f.): with subjc. praes., Heb.12:15; with subjc. aor., Mat.24:4, Mrk.13:5, Luk.21:8, Act.13:40, Gal.5:15, al.; ὅρα μή (see M, Pr., 124, 178), elliptically, Rev.19:10 22:9; with indic, fut. (M, Pr., l.with), Col.2:8.
__2. in order that not: with subjc. aor., Mrk.13:36, 2Co.8:20 12:6.
__III. Interrogative, in hesitant questions (M, Pr., 170), or where a negative answer is expected: Mat.7:9, 10, Mrk.2:19, Jhn.3:4, Rom.3:3 10:18, 19, 1Co.1:13, al.; μή τις, Luk.22:35, al.; before οὐ (Rom.10:17, al. in Pl.), expecting an affirm, ans.; οὐ μή, Luk.18:7, Jhn.18:11.
__IV. οὐ μή as emphatic negation (cf. M, Pr., 188, 190ff.; Bl. §64, 5), not at all, by no means: with indic, fut., Mat.16:22, Jhn.6:35, Heb.10:17, al.; with subjc. aor., Mat.24:2, Mrk.13:2, Luk.6:37, Jhn.13:8, 1Co.8:13, al.
(AS)

Included with:  μὴ οὐ  is used of an apprehended negative:

__I
with finite forms of the Verb, after Verbs expressing fear or apprehension [Refs 5th c.BC+ [compare (μή 5th c.BC: Bacchylides Lyricus 8):]]

__I.a
mostly with subjunctive, δείδω μὴ οὔ τίς τοι ὑπόσχηται τόδε ἔργον [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 10.39, compare 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 6.9, 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 3.53, 57, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Meno” 89d, etc.: after historical tenses, with _optative_, ἠθύμησάν τινες ἐννοούμενοι μὴ οὐκ ἔχοιεν ὁπόθεν λαμβάνοιεν 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 3.5.3, etc.]]: with future optative representing future indicative in indirect speech, μὴ οὐκ ὀρθῶς αὐτὸ ποιήσοις [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Euthyphro” 15d.]]

__I.b
with indicative, ὁρᾶτε μὴ οὐκ ἐμοὶ μάλιστα τῶν πολιτῶν προσήκει [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Andocides Orator 1.103, compare 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Laches” 196c, Alcaeus2.139d.]]

__I.2
without introductory Verb, with subjunctive, μή νύ τοι οὐ χραίσμῃ [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 1.28, compare 566, 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Troades” 982]]; also to suggest hesitation, perhaps [Refs 5th c.BC+ [compare (μή 5th c.BC: Bacchylides Lyricus 9), μὴ οὐ τοῦτο ᾖ τὸ χρηστήριον 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 5.79, compare 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Phaedo” 67b, “Smp.” 194c, 214c, etc.: also with _indicative_, μὴ τοῦτο οὐ καλῶς ὡμολογήσαμεν [prev. author] “Men.” 89c.]]

__I.3
μή is sometimes doubled, irregularly, for μὴ οὐ, ἐθαύμαζε δ᾽ εἴτις.. φοβοῖτο, μὴ ὁ γενόμενος καλὸς κἀγαθὸς.. μὴ τὴν μεγίστην χάριν ἔχοι [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Memorabilia” 1.2.7, compare 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 2.13.]]

__II
after a negative expressed or implied:

__II.1
with infinitive,

__II.1.a
after Verbs of hindering, denying, avoiding, needing, when these Verbs are themselves negatived or questioned, οὐκέτι ἀνεβάλλοντο μὴ οὐ τὸ πᾶν μηχανήσασθαι they no longer hesitated to try every expedient, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 6.88, compare 8.100, 119]]; τί δῆτα μέλλεις μὴ οὐ γεγωνίσκει; [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Prometheus Vinctus” 627, compare 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Ajax” 540, 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Acharnenses” 320, 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 1.4.2, 4.3.8, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Euthydemus” 304c, 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 24.24; οὐκ ἀνατίθεμαι μὴ οὐ καλῶς λέγεσθαι 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Meno” 89d, compare “Phd.” 87a; πολλοῦ δέω μὴ οὐ δύο γε φεύγειν [prev. author] “Euthd.” 297b]]; τίνος ἐνδέομεν μὴ οὐ πανσυδίᾳ χωρεῖ; [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Troades” 797 (_anapaest meter_)]]; after ὥστε, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 8.57]]: with the Article, οὐκ ἐναντιώσομαι τὸ μὴ οὐ γεγωνεῖν πᾶν [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Prometheus Vinctus” 787, compare 918, 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Tyrannus” 283, 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Phoenissae” 1176; αὐτὴν οὐ μισοῦντ᾽ ἐκείνην τὴν πόλιν τὸ μὴ οὐ μεγάλην εἶναι 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Aves” 37]]; τοῖς θεοῖς οὐδὲν ἂν ἔχοιμεν μέμψασθαι τὸ μὴ οὐχί.. [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 7.5.42, compare 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Philebus” 13a, etc.; compare μή 5th c.BC: Bacchylides Lyricus 5b.]]

__II.1.b
after Verbs and phrases signifying impossibility, impropriety, reluctance, when not negatived, ἄνδρα δ᾽ οὐκ ἔστι μὴ οὐ κακὸν ἔμμεναι [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Simonides Lyricus 5.10; δεινὸν ἐδόκεε εἶναι μὴ οὐ λαβεῖν 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.187; ἔστι οὐδεμία μηχανὴ μὴ οὐκ ἀπολωλέναι [prev. author] 2.181, compare 3.51, 7.5; οὐδεὶς ἂν τολμήσειεν μὴ οὐ χρῆσθαι τῷ νόμῳ 5th c.BC: Antipho Orator 5.87, compare 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 8.60; αἰσχύνη ἦν μὴ οὐ συσπουδάζειν 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 2.3.11; αἰσχρόν ἐστι μὴ οὐκ ἄλλας πληγὰς ἐμβάλλειν τῷ υἱεῖ [prev. author] “Lac.” 6.2]]; οὐδεὶς οἷός τ᾽ ἐστὶν ἄλλως λέγων μὴ οὐ (nemo potest non) καταγέλαστος εἶναι [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Gorgias” 509a]]: after an implied negative, μὴ οὐχὶ παντὶ τρόπῳ ἐλέγχειν μαλθακοῦ εἶναι ἀνδρός [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [[prev. author] “Phd.” 85c; μόνῃ τῇ μορφῇ μὴ οὐχὶ πρόβατα εἶναι διαφερόντων 2nd c.AD: Lucianus Sophista “Alex.” 15]]; after ὥστε, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Fragmenta” 1068, 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Respublica Atheniensium” 3.8]]; μή and μὴ οὐκ in consecutive clauses, [Refs [[prev. author] “Ap.” 34]]: with the Article, οὐκ ἀνέξομαι τὸ μὴ οὐ.. τιμᾶν [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Eumenides” 914]]; οὐδείς γέ μ᾽ ἂν πείσειεν.. τὸ μὴ οὐ.. [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Ranae” 68, compare 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Historia Graeca (Hellenica)” 5.2.36.]]

__II.2
less frequently with participle after a negative expressed or implied, οὔκων δίκαιον [ἀνδριάντα] ἱστάναι.. μὴ οὐκ ὑπερβαλλόμενον τοῖσι ἔργοισι [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 2.110, compare 6.9, 106; δυσάλγητος γὰρ ἂν εἴην τοιάνδε μὴ οὐ κατοικτείρων ἕδραν 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Tyrannus” 13, compare 221, “OC” 360, 5th-6th c.BC: Isocrates Orator 10.47 (uncertain reading), 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Lysis” 212d, 4th-3rd c.BC: Philemo Comicus 213.5: hence]]

__II.3
= {εἰ μή}, except, πόλεις.. χαλεπαὶ λαβεῖν, μὴ οὐ χρόνῳ καὶ πολιορκίᾳ [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 19.123.]]

__III
in questions expecting an affirmative answer, [LXX+NT+5th c.BC+ [LXX.Judg.14.3, NT.1Cor.9.4, 5th-4th c.BC: Aesopus Fabularum Scriptor 404.]]

Abbott-Smith / STEPBible (TBESG)
μήποτε
(= μή ποτε, and so written in WH, exc. Mat.25:9),
negative particle, related to οὔποτε as μή to οὐ.

μή-τι
interrog. particle, expecting a negative answer: Mat.7:16 26:22, 25, Mrk.4:21 14:19, Luk.6:39, Jhn.8:22 18:35, Act.10:47, 2Co.12:18, Jas.3:11; in hesitant questions (see M, Pr., 170.), μ οὗτός ἐστιν,
can this be, Mat.12:23, Jhn.4:29; μ. ἄρα, 2Co.1:17; On εἰ μήτι (Luk.9:13, cf. Bl., § 65, 6), see: εἰ.†
εἰ,
conjunctive particle, used in conditions and in indirect   questions.
__I. Conditional, if;
__1. with indic, expressing a general assumption;
__(a) pres.: before indic, pres., Mat.11:14, Rom.8:25, al.; before imperat., Mrk.4:23  9:22, Jhn.15:18, 1Co.7:9, al.; before fut. indic., Luk.16:31, Rom.8:11, al.; before pf. or aor., with negation in apodosis, Mat.12:26, Rom.4:14, al.; similarly, before impf., Luk.17:6, Jhn.8:39; before quæst., Mat.6:23, Jhn.5:47  7:23 8:46, 1Pe.2:20;
__(b) fut.: Mat.26:33, 1Pe.2:20;
__(with) pf.: Jhn.11:12, Rom.6:5, al.;
__(d) aor.: Luk.16:11  19:8, Jhn.13:32, 18:23, Rev.20:15, al.
__2. Where the assumption is certain = ἐπεί: Mat.12:28, Jhn.7:4, Rom.5:17, al.
__3. Of an unfulfilled condition, with indic, impf., aor. or plpf., before ἄν, with imp. or aor. (see: ἄν, I, i).
__4. C. indic., after verbs denoting wonder, etc., sometimes, but not always, coupled with an element of doubt: Mrk.15:44, 1Jn.3:13, al.
__5. C. indic., as in LXX (Num.14:3o, 1Ki.14:45, al. = Heb. אִם), in oaths, with the formula of imprecation understood in a suppressed apodosis (WM, 627; Burton, §272): Mrk.8:12, Heb.3:11" (LXX)  4:3 (LXX).
__6. Rarely (cl.) with optative, to express a merely possible condition: Act.24:19 27:39, 1Co.14:10 15:37, I Pe3:14, 17.
__II. Interrogative, if, whether.
__1. As in cl., in indir. questions after verbs of seeing, asking, knowing, saying, etc.: with indic. pres., Mat.26:63, Mrk.15:36, Act.19:2, 2Co.13:5, al.; fut., Mrk.3:2, Act.8:22, al.; aor., Mrk.15:44, 1Co.1:16, al.; with subjc. aor. (M, Pr., 194), Php.3:12.
__2. As in LXX (= Heb. אִם and interrog. הֲ, Gen.17:17, al.; see WM, 639f.; Viteau, i, 22), in direct questions: Mrk.8:23 (Tr., WH, txt.), Luk.13:23, 22:49, Act.19:2, al.
__III. With other particles.
__1. εἰ ἄρα, εἴγε, εἰ δὲ μήγε, see: ἄρα, γε.
__2. εἰ δὲ καί, but if also: Luk.11:18; but even if, 1Co.4:7, 2Co.4:3 11:16.
__3. εἰ δὲ μή, but if not, but if otherwise: Mrk.2:21, 22 Jhn.14:2, Rev.2:5, al.
__4. εἰ καί, if even, if also, although: Mrk.14:29, Luk.11:8, 1Co.7:21, 2Co.4:16, Php.2:17, al.
__5. καὶ εἰ, even if, see: καί
__6. εἰ μή, if not, unless, except, but only: Mat.24:22, Mrk.2:26 6:5, Jhn.9:33, 1Co.7:17 (only), Gal.1:19 (cf. ἐὰν μή, 2:16; see Hort., Ja., xvi); ἐκτὸς εἰ μή, pleonastic (Bl., §65, 6), 1Co.14:5 15:2, 1Ti.5:19.
__7. εἰ μήν = cl. ἦ μήν (M, Pr., 46), in oaths, surely (Eze.33:27, al.): Heb.6:14.
__8. εἴ πως, if haply: Act.27:12, Rom.1:10.
__9. εἴτε . . . εἴτε, whether . . . or; Rom.12:6-8, 1Co.3:22 13:8, al.

Abbott-Smith / STEPBible (TBESG)
μία, see: εἷς.
εἷς
ιά, ἕν, genitive ἑνός, μιᾶς, ἑνός,
cardinal numeral, one;
__1. one, as opposite to many: Mat.25:15, Rom.5:12, 1Co.10:8, al.; as subst., Rom.5:15, Eph.2:14; id. with genitive partit., Mat.5:19, al.; before ἐκ (ἐξ), Mrk.14:18, Jhn.6:8, al.; metaphorically, of union and concord, Jhn.10:30 17:11, Rom.12:4-5, Php.1:27; ἀπὸ μιᾶς (B1., § 44, 1), Luk.14:18; with neg., εἷς. . . οὐ (μή), more emphatic than οὐδείς, no one, none (cl.), Mat.5:18 10:29, Luk.11:46 12:6.
__2. Emphatically, to the exclusion of others;
__(a) a single (one): Mat.21:24, Mrk.8:14; absol., 1Co.9:24, al.; οὐδὲ εἷς, Mat.27:14, Jhn.1:3, Rom.3:10, al.;
__(b) one, alone: Mrk.2:7 10:18, Luk.18:19;
__(with) one and the same: Rom.3:30, 1Co.3:8 11:5 12:11, 1Jn.5:8.
__3. In late Gk., with weakened force, = τις or indef. art. (of. Heb. אֶחָד, Gen.22:13, al.; see B1., § 45, 2; M, Pr., 96 f.): Mat.8:19 19:6, Rev.8:13, al.; εἷς τις (Bl., l.with), Luk.22:50, Jhn.11:49
__4. Distributively: εἷς καστος (cl.), Luk.4:40, Act.2:6, al.; εἷς . . . καὶ εἷς (cl., εἷς μὲν . . . εἷς δέ), Mat.17:4, Mrk.9:5, Jhn.20:12, al. (cf. LXX and use of Heb. אֶחָד, Exo.17:12, al); ὁ εἷς . . . ὁ ἕτερος (ἄλλος) = cl. ὁ μὲν (ἕτερος) . . . ὁ δέ (ἕτερος), Mat.6:24, Luk.7:41, Rev.17:10; καθ᾽ εἷς, εἷς κ. είς (in which καθ᾽ is adverbial, or the expression formed from the analogy of ἕν καθ᾽ ἔν; M, Pr., 105), one by one, severally: Mrk.14:19, Rom.12:5, al.; εἷς τὸν ἕνα = ἀλλήλους (B1., 45, 2; M, Pr., 246), 1Th.5:11.
__5. As ordinal = πρῶτος (like Heb. אֶחָד; Bl., § 45, 1; M, Pr., 95 f.), first: Mat.28:1, Mrk.16:2, al
(AS)

Related to:  εἷς, μίᾰ, ἕν
(μίη only in late Ionic dialect Prose): genitive ἑνός, μιᾶς, ἑνός:—Epic dialect ἕεις [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th-7th c.BC: Hesiodus Epicus “Theogonia” 145, “Anthologia Graeca” 7.341 (5th c.AD: Proclus Philosophus), conjecture in 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 5.603]]:—Doric dialect ἧς [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [3rd c.BC: Rhinthon Comicus 12, “Tab.Heracl.” 1.136]]:—Epic dialect, Aeolic dialect, and Ionic dialect feminine ἴᾰ [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 13.354, probably in 5th c.BC: Hippocrates Medicus “περὶ νούσων” 4.37; _accusative_ ἴαν 7th-6th c.BC: Alcaeus Lyricus 33.6 (probably), 7th-6th c.BC: Sappho Lyrica 69.1 (compare μηδεΐα), 6th c.BC: Corinna Lyrica “Supp.” 2.56, “IG” 9(2).517.22(Thess.); _genitive_ ἰῆς 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 16.173, 24.496; _dative_ ἰῇ 9.319, 11.174, etc.]]: neuter dative (ἰῷ κίον ἤματι) [Refs 5th c.BC+ [6.422. (In Comedy texts οὐδὲ (μηδὲ) εἷς, οὐδὲ (μηδὲ) ἕν, occur, mostly at the end of an iambic trimeter, without elision, 5th c.BC: Cratinus Comicus 302, 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Ranae” 927, “Pl.” 37, 138, +others)]] (Orig. ἕνς, assim. ἔν (δ) probably in [Refs [“Leg.Gort.” 9.50, from *εμς,]] Indo-European sem-(compare ὁμός); μία from sm-ί; ἴα is not related to μία, but probably to pronominal stem i-(Latin is), compareἰός.)

__1
as a Numeral, εἷς κοίρανος ἔστω [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 2.204, etc.]]; strengthened, εἷς οἶος, μία οἴη, a single

__A
one, one alone,[Refs 8th c.BC+ [4.397, 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 7.65; μία μούνη 23.227; εἷς μοῦνος 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.119, 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Plutus” 1053, etc.; εἷς καὶ μόνος 1st c.BC: Dionysius Halicarnassensis 1.74; εἷς ὤν 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Tyrannus” 247, 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Phoenissae” 894, etc.; opposed to πολύς, μία τὰς πολλὰς ψυχὰς ὀλέσασα 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Agamemnon” 1456, compare 1465, “Ch.” 299, etc.]]

__b
emphatically with a superlative, εἷς οἰωνὸς ἄριστος [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 12.243, etc.: frequently in Trag., εἷς ἀνὴρ πλεῖστον..πόνον παρασχών 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Persae” 327; πλείστας ἀνὴρ εἷς.. ἔγημε 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Trachiniae” 460; κάλλιστ᾽ ἀνὴρ εἷς [prev. author] “OT” 1380; ἕνακριθέντ᾽ ἄριστον [prev. author] “Ph.” 1344]]; also in Prose, ἐπὶ πλεῖστον δὴ χλιδῆς εἷς ἀνὴρ ἀπίκετο [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 6.127, compare 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 8.68; Μυτιληναίους μάλιστα δὴ μίαν πόλιν [prev. author] 3.39; πάντων εἷς ἀνὴρ μεγίστων αἴτιος κακῶν 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 18.143]]: without a superlative, Ἐτεοκλέης ἂν εἷς πολὺς κατὰ πτόλιν ὑμνοῖθ᾽ [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Septem contra Thebas” 6.]]

__c
in oppos., made emphatic by the Article, ὁ εἷς, ἡ μία, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 20.272, 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 20.110, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Crito” 48a; τοῦ ἑνὸς οἱ δύο ἀγαθοὶ βελτίους 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Politica” 1287b13, compare 3rd c.BC: Theocritus Poeta Bucolicus 6.22.]]

__d
with a negative, εἷς οὐδείς no single man, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.32; ἓν οὐδὲ ἓν ἴαμα 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 2.51]]; οὐκ ἐν ἄλλῳ ἑνί γε χωρίῳ in no other single country, [Refs [[prev. author] 1.80]]; οὐχ εἷς, i.e. more than one, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Septem contra Thebas” 103, 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Andromache” 96]]; εἷς οὐ.., εἷς μή.., emphatic for οὐδείς, μηδείς, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Thesmophoriazusae” 549, 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 5.6.12]]; more emphatic, οὐδὲ εἷς, μηδὲ εἷς, see at {οὐδείς},{μηδείς}.

__e
εἷς ἕκαστος each one, each by himself, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.123, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Protagoras” 332c, etc.]]; αἴσθησις μία ἑνός (i.e. γένους) one of each, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Metaphysica” 1003b19: _plural_, ἑκάτεροι ἕνες “POxy.” 276.8 (1st c.AD).]]

__f
with κατά, καθ᾽ ἓν ἕκαστον each singly, piece by piece, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.9, etc.]]; καθ᾽ ἕν one by one, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Sophista” 217a, etc.]]; καθ᾽ ἕν, τό, list, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Elephantine Papyri 20.7 (3rd c.BC), etc.]]; καθ᾽ ἕν᾽ ἡμῶν ἕκαστον ἀποστερεῖν to deprive each of us singly, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 21.142, compare 4th-3rd c.BC: Menander Comicus “Ἐπιτρέποντες” 164, 186]]; εἷς κατὰ εἷς one by one, [NT.Mark.14.19]; but καθ᾽ ἓν γίγνεσθαι, εἶναι, to be united, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 8.46, 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Historia Graeca (Hellenica)” 5.2.16.]]

__g

Akad.” 70.5, etc.]]; infinitive μιχθήμεναι [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 11.438; but in 8th c.BC: Homerus Epicus and _Attic dialect_ more commonly]]aorist 2 ἐμίγην [ῐ]; Epic dialect μίγην [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 21.143]]; infinitive μιγήμεναι [Refs 4th c.BC+ [15.409, μιγῆν 4th-5th c.BC: Parmenides Poeta Philosophus 12.5; both forms in Trag., μιχθῆναι A.[same place], +others (see. below), μιγῆναι [prev. author] “Pr.” 738]]: Epic dialect aorist passive ἔμικτο [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 1.433, μίκτο 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 11.354, 16.813, 3rd c.BC: Apollonius Rhodius Epicus 3.1223]]; participle μίγμενος in transitive sense, [Refs 2nd c.BC+ [2nd c.BC: Nicander Epicus “Alexipharmaca” 574]]: aorist middle ἐμιξάμην [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-3rd c.BC: Theophrastus Philosophus “de Causis Plantarum” 3.22.3]]: perfect μέμιγμαι [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 10.424, etc.]]; 3rd.pers. plural ἀνα-μεμίχαται [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.146]]: pluperfect ἐμέμικτο [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 4.438.]]—For the present and imperfect [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Homerus Epicus and 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus always use μίσγω]], which occurs once in Trag., [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Fragmenta” 271 (_anapaest meter_)]], never in Comedy texts, sometimes in Attic dialect Prose, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 6.104 (προς-), 4th-3rd c.BC: Theophrastus Philosophus “de Sensu” 43]]; __II
generally, join, bring together, in various ways:

__II.1
in hostile sense, μῖξαι χεῖράς τε μένος τε join battle hand to hand, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 15.510; μίξαντες.. Ἄρευα 7th-6th c.BC: Alcaeus Lyricus 31; Κόλχοισι βίαν μ. 5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “P.” 4.213]]; χερσὶν ἐναντία χεῖρας ἔμιξεν [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [3rd c.BC: Apollonius Rhodius Epicus 2.78]]; Ἄρη μίξουσιν [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Coloneus” 1047 (Lyric poetry)]]:—passive, μιγνυμένου πολέμου [Refs 7th c.BC+ [7th c.BC: Callinus Epicus 1.11.]]

__II.1.b
in good sense, ἀλώπηξ καἰετὸς ξυνωνίην ἔμιξαν [Refs 7th c.BC+ [7th c.BC: Archilochus Lyricus 86.]]

__II.2
bring into connexion with, make acquainted with, ἄνδρας.. μισγέμεναι κακότητι καὶ ἄλγεσι [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 20.203]]; Καδμεῖοί νιν.. ἄνθεσι μίγνυον covered him with flowers, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “N.” 4.21]]; reversely, ᾧ πότμον.. Ἄρης ἔμιξεν upon whom [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus]] brought death, [Refs [[prev. author]]]l.7(6).25.

__B
passive, with future middle μείξομαι (see. entry [near the start]):—to be mixed up with, mingled among, προμάχοισιν ἐμίχθη [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 5.134, etc.; ἐνὶ προμάχοισι μιγέντα 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 18.379; [σῆμα] οὔ τι μεμιγμένον ἐστὶν ὁμίλῳ 8.196]]; ἐώλπει μίξεσθαι ξενίῃ hoped to hold intercourse in guest-friendship,[Refs 8th c.BC+ [24.314; Τρώεσσιν ἐν ἀγρομένοισιν ἔμιχθεν 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 3.209, compare 10.180]]; ἐν ταῖς κακαῖσιν ἁγαθαὶ μεμιγμέναι [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Ion” 399]]; hold intercourse with, live with, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 7.247, etc.; ἐμίσγετο δαίμονι δαίμων 5th c.BC: Empedocles Poeta Philosophus 59.1; αἷς οὐ μίγνυται θεῶν τις 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Eumenides” 69]]: absolutely, hold intercourse, θάμ᾽ ἐνθάδ᾽ ἐόντες ἐμισγόμεθ᾽ [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 4.178.]]

__B.b
to be mixed or compounded, μεμιγμένον μέλι σὺν γάλακτι [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “N.” 3.77; Κύπριδος ἐλπὶς.. μειγνυμένα Διονυσίοισι δώροις 5th c.BC: Bacchylides Lyricus “Scolia” 1361 “fragment” 1.9]]; σύλλογος νέων καὶ πρεσβυτέρων μεμιγμένος [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Leges” 951d, compare 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Fragmenta” 997; μεμιγμένην πολιτείαν ἐκ κακοῦ τε καὶ ἀγαθοῦ 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 548c; ἔκ τε ταὐτοῦ καὶ θατέρου καὶ τῆς οὐσίας μ. [prev. author] “Ti.” 35b.]]

__B.2
to be brought into contact with, κάρη κονίῃσιν ἐμίχθη his head wasrolled in the dust, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 10.457, 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 22.329; ὅτ᾽ ἐν κονίῃσι μιγείης 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 3.55]]; οὐδ᾽ ἔτ᾽ ἔασε [ἔγχος].. μιχθήμεναι ἔγκασι φωτός she let not the spear reach them,[Refs [11.438; κλισίῃσι μιγήμεναι 15.409]]; ἐς Ἀχαιοὺς μίσγετο went to join them, [Refs [18.216]]; ἔσω μίσγεσθαι to come among us in the house, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 18.49]]; μίσγεσθαι ὑπὲρ ποταμοῖο to join the rest across the river, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 23.73: frequently in 5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus in various senses, with _dative_ (with or without ἐν)]], come to, ἔν τ᾽ Ὠκεανοῦ πελάγεσσι μίγεν [Refs [“P.” 4.251; Λακεδαιμονίων μιχθέντες ἀνδρῶν ἤθεσιν [prev. work] 257]]; ἐν αἱμακουρίαις μέμικται is present at that feast, [Refs [“O.” 1.91]]; φύλλοις ἐλαιᾶν μιχθέντα, στεφάνοις ἔμιχθεν (3rd.pers. plural), come to, i.e. win, the crown of victory, [Refs [“N.” 1.18, 2.22; μ. εὐλογίαις “I.” 3.3; μ. ἐν τιμαῖς [prev. work] 2.29]]; μ. θάμβει to be affected by amazement, [Refs [“N.” 1.56]]; also βροτοὶ ξὺν κακοῖς μεμιγμένοι [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Electra” 1485.]]

__B.3
in hostile sense, mix in fight, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 4.456, compare 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 5.317]]; ἐν δαΐ, ἐν παλάμῃσι μ., [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 13.286, 21.469.]]

__B.4
in [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Homerus Epicus and 8th-7th c.BC: Hesiodus Epicus]] most frequently of the sexes, have intercourse with, both of the man and the woman, sometimes absolutely, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 9.275, etc.: more frequently μιγῆναί τινι, of the man, 21.143]], etc.; of the woman, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 1.73; ἄρσενι θῆλυ μιγῆν 4th-5th c.BC: Parmenides Poeta Philosophus 12.5, compare 5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “P.” 3.14, +others]]; but in Trag. only of the man, as μητρὶ μιχθῆναι, μιγῆναι, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Tyrannus” 791, 995]]; but in Comedy texts μιγνυμένας τοῖσιν ἀδελφοῖς [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Ranae” 1081 (_anapaest meter_): in Prose]]present μίσγεσθαι in this sense, of the man, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 2.64, etc.]]; of the woman, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [[prev. author] 1.5, 199, 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 22.445]]; in full, φιλότητί τινι μιγῆναι, of the man, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 6.165]]; of the woman,[Refs 8th c.BC+ [[prev. work] 161, 8th-7th c.BC: Hesiodus Epicus “Theogonia” 927, 970, etc.]]; ἐμισγέσθην φ., of the two, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 14.295]]; ἐν φιλότητι μίσγεσθαι (with or without τινι), of the man, [Refs [2.232, 24.131]]; of the woman, [Refs [“Hymni Homerici” 33.5]]; Διὸς φιλότητι μιγῆναι, Διὸς ἐν φ. μ., of the woman, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th-7th c.BC: Hesiodus Epicus “Theogonia” 920, “hymnus ad Mercurium” 4]]; σῇ φ. μ., of the man, [Refs [“hymnus ad Venerem” 150]]; εὐνῇ μ., of the man, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 1.433]]; φιλότητι καὶ εὐνῇ, of the man, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 3.445, compare 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 15.420]]; of the woman, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [5.126; but ἐν ἀγκοίνῃσι Διός 11.268: with _accusative_ _cognate_, φιλότης.., ἣν ἐμίγης 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 15.33.]]—The aorist I is not used in this sense by [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Homerus Epicus]], but occurs in the Hymns, [Refs [“hymnus ad Venerem” 46, +others]]; the aorist I is more frequently in [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th-7th c.BC: Hesiodus Epicus and 5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus]] (Cf. Latin misceo, Sanskrit meksáyati 'stir', miśrás 'mixed'.)

little, small, short, lesser
little, small, in size quantity, etc. Mt. 13:32; Lk. 12:32; Rev. 3:8; small, little in age, young, not adult, Mk. 15:40; little, short in time, Jn. 7:33; μικρόν, i.e. χρόνον, a little while, a short time, Jn. 13:33; μετὰ μικρόν, after a little while, a little while afterwards, Mt. 26:73; little in number, Lk. 12:32; small, little in dignity, low, humble, Mt. 10:42; 11:11; μικρόν, as an adverb, little, a little, Mt. 26:39

Included with:  μικρός
and σμῑκρός, ά, όν, Doric dialect, Ionic dialect μικκός (which see): σμικρός is corroborated by metre in [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 17.757, 8th-7th c.BC: Hesiodus Epicus “Opera et Dies” 361]], and might be restored in [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 5.801, 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 3.296 (μικρός codices)]]; it is probably the only form in [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus]] (μικρός [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 2.74 codices): frequently in Lyric poetry and probably always in Trag. (except where metre requires μικρός, as 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Ajax” 161 (_anapaest meter_, _comparative_))]]; most frequently in [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus; but in 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus, also 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus and other Comedy texts, μικρός prevails, σμικρός being found 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 4.13, 7.75, 8.81, 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Acharnenses” 523, “V.” 5]]; Attic dialect Inscrr. have σμικρός [Refs [“IG” 12.313.111, +others, μικρός [prev. work]369.10, +others]]:—small, little,

__1
in Size, μ. ἔην δέμας [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 5.801; μ. λίθος 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 3.296; κίρκον, ὅ τε σμικρῇσι φόνον φέρει ὀρνίθεσσιν 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 17.757; σμ. ἄστεα 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.5; μεγάθεϊ σμικροί [prev. author] 2.74: with Dims., μ. πολίχνιον, γῄδιον, παιδάρια, 5th-6th c.BC: Isocrates Orator 5.145, 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 8.3.38, “Ages.” 1.21]]: as a Comedy texts exaggeration, δικαστηρίδιον μ. πάνυ [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Vespae” 803; σκαλαθυρμάτι᾽ ἄττα μ. [prev. author] “Nu.” 630, etc.]]: with infinitive, μικροὶ δ᾽ ὁρᾶν [Refs [[prev. author] “Pax” 821]]: as a term of reproach, Κλειγενὴς ὁ μικρός [Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. author] “Ra.” 709, compare 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Protagoras” 323d, 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Ethica Nicomachea” 1123b7, 2nd c.AD: Alexander Rhetor 98.7; Ἀμύντας ὁ μ. 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Politica” 1311b3]]; οἱ ἐν μικρῷ μεγάλοι short but stoutly built, [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd-3rd c.AD: Philostratus Sophista “de gymnastica” 36; ὁ μ. δάκτυλος “SIG” 1172.4 (from Lebena).]]

__2

μιμνήσκω
(Bl., -ῄ-, § 3, 3), [in LXX chiefly for זָכַר ;]
to remind: mid, and pass.;
__(a) reflexive, to remind oneself of, hence, to remember: with genitive of thing(s), Mat.26:75, Luk.1:54, 72 24:8, Act.11:16, 2Pe.3:2, Ju 17; with neg., of sins, = to forgive, Heb.8:12 10:17" (LXX) ; with genitive of person(s), Luk.23:42; before ὅτι, Mat.5:23 27:63, Luk.16:25, Jhn.2:17, 22 12:16; ὡς, Luk.24:6; pf., μέμνημι, in Pres. sense (cl.), with genitive of person(s) (of thing(s)), 1Co.11:2, 2Ti.1:4; pres., μιμνήσκομαι (only in late writers), with genitive of person(s), in sense of caring for, Heb.2:6 (LXX) Heb.13:3;
__(b) in passive sense, to be remembered, aor., ἐμνήσθην : before ἐνώπιον, with genitive of person(s) (cf. Eze.18:22), Act.10:31, Rev.16:19 (cf. ἀνα-, ἐπ-ανα-, ὑπο- μιμνήσκω. The tenses of this verb are from the older μνάομαι).†

(Lyric poetry), [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Alcestis” 878: compounds with ἀνα- or ὑπο- were preferred in Prose.]]

[Refs 8th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Philebus” 31a: more frequently with _genitive_, φίλου μεμνήσομ᾽ ἑταίρου 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 22.390; τοῦ ποτε μεμνήσεσθαι ὀΐομαι 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 19.581; οὐδὲ παῖδος οὐδὲ φίλων τοκήων οὐδὲν ἐμνάσθη 7th-6th c.BC: Sappho Lyrica “Supp.” [same place], compare 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 8.62, 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Hippolytus” 1461, etc.; also μεμνημένος ἀμφ᾽ Ὀδυσῆϊ 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 4.151; ἀμφὶ Διώνυσον.. μνήσομαι “Hymni Homerici” 7.2; περὶ πομπῆς μνησόμεθα 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 7.192]]:—passive, to be remembered (not in early Prose), τὰ παραπτώματα οὐ μνησθήσεται [LXX+NT [LXX.Eze.18.22; αἱ ἐλεημοσύναι σου ἐμνήσθησαν NT.Act.10.31, cf. __B.3
after [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Homerus Epicus, with]]participle, θνατὰ μεμνάσθω περιστέλλων μέλη let him remember that he clothes, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “N.” 11.15]]; μέμνημαι κλύων I remember hearing, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Agamemnon” 830; μεμνήμεθα ἐλθόντες 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Hecuba” 244; μ. ἀκούσας 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 1.6.3, etc.]]: followed by a relative, μέμνησ᾽, ὅπως εὖ μοι στομώσεις αὐτόν [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Nubes” 1107.]]

short_definition: to me — ἐγώ, genitive, etc., ἐμοῦ, ἐμοί, ἐμέ (enclitic μου, μοι, με), pl. ἡμεῖς, -ῶν, -ῖν, -ᾶς,
deep_entry:
Abbott-Smith / STEPBible (TBESG)
ἐγώ, genitive, etc., ἐμοῦ, ἐμοί, ἐμέ (enclitic μου, μοι, με), pl. ἡμεῖς, -ῶν, -ῖν, -ᾶς,
of person(s) pron.
I.
__(a) The nom. is usually emphatic, when expressed as subjc, as in Mat.3:11, Mrk.1:8, Luk.3:16, al. But often there is no apparent emphasis, as Mat.10:16, Jhn.10:17; ἰδοὺ ἐ. (= Heb. הִנֵּנִי, cf. 1Ki.3:8), Act.9:10; ἐ. (like Heb. אֲנִי), I am, Jhn.1:23 (LXX), Act.7:32 (LXX).
__(b) The enclitic forms (see supr.) are used with nouns, adjectives, verbs, adverbs, where there is no emphasis: ἐν τ. πατρί μου, Jhn.14:20; μου τ. λόγους, Mat.7:24; ὀπίσω μου, Mat.3:11; ἰσχυρότερός μου, ib.; λέγει μοι, Rev.5:5; also with the prep. πρός, as Mrk.9:19, al. The full forms (ἐμοῦ, etc.) are used with the other prepositions, as δι᾽ ἐμοῦ, ἐν ἐμοί, εἰς ἐμέ, etc., also for emphasis, as Luk.10:16, Jhn.7:23, Mrk.14:7, al.
__(with) The genitive μου and ἡμῶν are often used for the poss. pronouns ἐμός, ἡμέτερος: τ. λαόν μου, Mat.2:6; μου τῂ ἀπιστιᾳ, Mrk.9:24.
__(d) τί ἐμοὶ καὶ σοί ( = Heb. מַה־לִי וָלָךְ, Jdg.11:12, al.), i.e. what have we in common: Mat.8:29, Mrk.1:24, 5:7, Luk.8:28, Jhn.2:4; τί γάρ μοι, 1Co.5:2.
__(e) The interchange of ἐγώ and ἡμεῖς, common in π., appears in Pauline Epp. (see M, Pr., 86f., M, Th., 131f.).
__(f) κἀγώ (= καὶ ἐγώ), and I, even I, I also: Mat.2:8, Luk.2:48, Jhn.6:56, Rom.3:7, 1Co.7:40, al.; κἀγώ . . . καί, both . . . and, Jhn.7:28.
(AS)

---

LSJ / STEPBible (TFLSJ)
ἐγώ,
I: pronoun of the first person:—Epic dialect mostly ἐγών before vowels (so in Doric dialect, before consonants, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Epicharmus Comicus 85, 5th c.BC: Sophron Comicus 81, 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Acharnenses” 748, 754), rarely in Trag., 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Persae” 932 (Lyric poetry)]]; Boeotian dialect ἱών [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd c.AD: Apollonius Dyscolus Grammaticus “de Pronominibus;” 51.4]]:— strengthened ἔγωγε, I at least, for my part, indeed, for myself (more frequently in Attic dialect than in [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Homerus Epicus)]]: Doric dialect ἐγώνγα [Refs 7th c.BC+ [7th c.BC: Alcman Lyricus 51, 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Acharnenses” 736, “Lys.” 986, _dative_ ἐμίνγα “IG” 22.1126.7 (Amphict. Delph.)]]: Boeotian dialect ἱώνγα [Refs 6th c.BC+ [6th c.BC: Corinna Lyrica 21]]; ἱώνει [Refs [Ead. 10]]; ἰώγα [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Acharnenses” 898]]: Laconian dialect and Tarentum dialect ἐγώνη, [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [5th c.AD(?): Hesychius Legal icographus, 2nd c.AD: Apollonius Dyscolus Grammaticus “de Conjunctionibus;” 255.29.]]

__II
oblique cases from a different root, genitive ἐμοῦ, enclitic μο; Ionic dialect and Epic dialect ἐμέο, ἐμεῦ, μευ, also ἐμέθεν [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 1.525, 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Helena” 177 (Lyric poetry)]]; Aeolic dialect ἔμεθεν [Refs 7th c.BC+ [7th-6th c.BC: Sappho Lyrica “Papyrus fragments” in E. Diehl, 23.7; ἐμεῖο “IG” 3.1337; μεθέν 5th c.BC: Sophron Comicus 20]]; Doric dialect ἐμέος, ἐμεῦς, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Epicharmus Comicus 144]]; Boeotian dialect ἐμοῦς [Refs 6th c.BC+ [6th c.BC: Corinna Lyrica 37; also ἐμῶς, ἐμίο, ἐμίω, ἐμίως 2nd c.AD: Apollonius Dyscolus Grammaticus “de Pronominibus;” 74.17:]] — _dative_ ἐμοί, enclitic μοι (which may be compared with Sanskrit genitive me in κλῦθί μοι [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 5.115, +others); ὅ μοι πόσις “Schwyzer” 683 (5th c.AD: Cypria)]]; Doric dialect ἐμίν [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Epicharmus Comicus 99, “AJA” 29.461 (Rhodian, 5th c.BC), 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Acharnenses” 733, 3rd c.BC: Theocritus Poeta Bucolicus 4.30]]; Tarentum dialect ἐμίνη [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [3rd c.BC: Rhinthon Comicus 13: _accusative_ ἐμέ]], enclitic μ; [Refs 5th c.AD+ [5th c.AD: Cypria μι “Inscription Cyprian dialect” 59,60 H.]]

__III
dual, nominative and accusative, νῶι, we two, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 5.34, etc.]]; accusative νῶιν Zenod.ad [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 8.377]]; Attic dialect νώ [Refs 8th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Phaedrus” 278b (also 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 5.219, 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 15.475); νῶε 5th-6th c.BC: Antimachus Colophonius Elegiacus et Epicus 39, 6th c.BC: Corinna Lyrica 5: _genitive_, _dative_ νῶι; νῷν 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Antigone” 3]]; νῶι dative, [Refs 5th c.AD+ [5th-6th c.AD: Orphica “Lithica” 773]]; νῶιν, ={ἡμῖν}, [Refs 4th c.AD+ [4th c.AD(?): Quintus Smyrnaeus Epicus 1.213, etc.]]

__IV
plural, nominative ἡμεῖς (ἡμέες falsa lectio in [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 2.6, +others, rejected by 2nd c.AD: Apollonius Dyscolus Grammaticus “de Pronominibus;” 93.1)]]; Aeolic dialect ἄμμες [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 9.303, 7th-6th c.BC: Alcaeus Lyricus 18.3, 5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “P.” 4.144]]; Doric dialect ἁμές [Refs 7th c.BC+ [7th c.BC: Alcman Lyricus 65, 5th c.BC: Epicharmus Comicus 42, 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Lysistrata” 168:— _genitive_ ἡμῶν (also ἥμων 2nd c.AD: Apollonius Dyscolus Grammaticus “de Syntaxi;” 130.23)]]; Ionic dialect ἡμέων [Refs 8th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.112, etc.; ἡμείων 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 24.170, 3rd c.BC: Herodas Mimographus 1.46]]; Aeolic dialect ἀμμέων [Refs 7th c.BC+ [7th-6th c.BC: Alcaeus Lyricus 88, “Milet.” 3 No.152.29]]; ἄμμων [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [[prev. work]74, 2nd c.AD: Apollonius Dyscolus Grammaticus “de Pronominibus;” 95.3]]; Doric dialect ἁμέων [Refs 7th c.BC+ [7th c.BC: Alcman Lyricus 66]]; ἁμῶν [[Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Epicharmus Comicus] 266, 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Lysistrata” 168, 3rd c.BC: Theocritus Poeta Bucolicus 2.158]]; Cretan dialect, Boeotian dialect ἁμίων [Refs 5th c.BC+ [“SIG” 528.5, 2nd c.AD: Apollonius Dyscolus Grammaticus “de Pronominibus;” 95.21:— _dative_ ἡμῖν, in 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus also ἡμίν]] (ῐ) (or ἧμιν Aristarch.ad [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 1.214, 2nd c.AD: Apollonius Dyscolus Grammaticus “de Pronominibus;” 95.3)]]; also rarely in Comedy texts, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Phrynichus Comicus 37, 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Aves” 386 (uncertain)]]; Aeolic dialect ἄμμῐν, ἄμμῐ, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 1.384, 7th-6th c.BC: Alcaeus Lyricus 80, +others, 5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “P.” 4.155, 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Septem contra Thebas” 156 (Lyric poetry), “Milet.” 3 No.152; ἄμμεσιν 7th-6th c.BC: Alcaeus Lyricus 100]]; Doric dialect also ἁμίν or ἇμιν, [Refs 7th c.BC+ [7th c.BC: Alcman Lyricus 77, 78, 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Eumenides” 347 (Lyric poetry), 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Lysistrata” 1081]]; with ῑ, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [[prev. author] “Ach.” 821, 3rd c.BC: Theocritus Poeta Bucolicus 7.145:— _accusative_ ἡμᾶς (also ἧμᾰς 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 16.372)]]; Ionic dialect ἡμέας [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 8.211, “SIG” 273.25 (Milet., 4th c.BC)]]; ἥμεας [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 4.294 (cf. Hdn.Gr. 2.140)]]; Aeolic dialect ἄμμε [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 1.59, 7th-6th c.BC: Sappho Lyrica 115]], Theocr.8.25; Doric dialect ἁμέ [Refs 6th c.BC+ [“SIG” 1 (Abu Simbel, 6th c.BC), 5th c.BC: Epicharmus Comicus 173, 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Acharnenses” 759 codices, “Lys.” 95.]]—On these dialectic varieties, [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [see 2nd c.AD: Apollonius Dyscolus Grammaticus “de Pronominibus;” 50]] ff. deep_entry:
Abbott-Smith / STEPBible (TBESG)
ἐγώ, genitive, etc., ἐμοῦ, ἐμοί, ἐμέ (enclitic μου, μοι, με), pl. ἡμεῖς, -ῶν, -ῖν, -ᾶς,
of person(s) pron.
I.
__(a) The nom. is usually emphatic, when expressed as subjc, as in Mat.3:11, Mrk.1:8, Luk.3:16, al. But often there is no apparent emphasis, as Mat.10:16, Jhn.10:17; ἰδοὺ ἐ. (= Heb. הִנֵּנִי, cf. 1Ki.3:8), Act.9:10; ἐ. (like Heb. אֲנִי), I am, Jhn.1:23 (LXX), Act.7:32 (LXX).
__(b) The enclitic forms (see supr.) are used with nouns, adjectives, verbs, adverbs, where there is no emphasis: ἐν τ. πατρί μου, Jhn.14:20; μου τ. λόγους, Mat.7:24; ὀπίσω μου, Mat.3:11; ἰσχυρότερός μου, ib.; λέγει μοι, Rev.5:5; also with the prep. πρός, as Mrk.9:19, al. The full forms (ἐμοῦ, etc.) are used with the other prepositions, as δι᾽ ἐμοῦ, ἐν ἐμοί, εἰς ἐμέ, etc., also for emphasis, as Luk.10:16, Jhn.7:23, Mrk.14:7, al.
__(with) The genitive μου and ἡμῶν are often used for the poss. pronouns ἐμός, ἡμέτερος: τ. λαόν μου, Mat.2:6; μου τῂ ἀπιστιᾳ, Mrk.9:24.
__(d) τί ἐμοὶ καὶ σοί ( = Heb. מַה־לִי וָלָךְ, Jdg.11:12, al.), i.e. what have we in common: Mat.8:29, Mrk.1:24, 5:7, Luk.8:28, Jhn.2:4; τί γάρ μοι, 1Co.5:2.
__(e) The interchange of ἐγώ and ἡμεῖς, common in π., appears in Pauline Epp. (see M, Pr., 86f., M, Th., 131f.).
__(f) κἀγώ (= καὶ ἐγώ), and I, even I, I also: Mat.2:8, Luk.2:48, Jhn.6:56, Rom.3:7, 1Co.7:40, al.; κἀγώ . . . καί, both . . . and, Jhn.7:28.
(AS)

---
