ἐγώ,
I: pronoun of the first person:—Epic dialect mostly ἐγών before vowels (so in Doric dialect, before consonants, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Epicharmus Comicus 85, 5th c.BC: Sophron Comicus 81, 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Acharnenses” 748, 754), rarely in Trag., 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Persae” 932 (Lyric poetry)]]; Boeotian dialect ἱών [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd c.AD: Apollonius Dyscolus Grammaticus “de Pronominibus;” 51.4]]:— strengthened ἔγωγε, I at least, for my part, indeed, for myself (more frequently in Attic dialect than in [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Homerus Epicus)]]: Doric dialect ἐγώνγα [Refs 7th c.BC+ [7th c.BC: Alcman Lyricus 51, 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Acharnenses” 736, “Lys.” 986, _dative_ ἐμίνγα “IG” 22.1126.7 (Amphict. Delph.)]]: Boeotian dialect ἱώνγα [Refs 6th c.BC+ [6th c.BC: Corinna Lyrica 21]]; ἱώνει [Refs [Ead. 10]]; ἰώγα [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Acharnenses” 898]]: Laconian dialect and Tarentum dialect ἐγώνη, [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [5th c.AD(?): Hesychius Legal icographus, 2nd c.AD: Apollonius Dyscolus Grammaticus “de Conjunctionibus;” 255.29.]]

__II
oblique cases from a different root, genitive ἐμοῦ, enclitic μο; Ionic dialect and Epic dialect ἐμέο, ἐμεῦ, μευ, also ἐμέθεν [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 1.525, 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Helena” 177 (Lyric poetry)]]; Aeolic dialect ἔμεθεν [Refs 7th c.BC+ [7th-6th c.BC: Sappho Lyrica “Papyrus fragments” in E. Diehl, 23.7; ἐμεῖο “IG” 3.1337; μεθέν 5th c.BC: Sophron Comicus 20]]; Doric dialect ἐμέος, ἐμεῦς, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Epicharmus Comicus 144]]; Boeotian dialect ἐμοῦς [Refs 6th c.BC+ [6th c.BC: Corinna Lyrica 37; also ἐμῶς, ἐμίο, ἐμίω, ἐμίως 2nd c.AD: Apollonius Dyscolus Grammaticus “de Pronominibus;” 74.17:]] — _dative_ ἐμοί, enclitic μοι (which may be compared with Sanskrit genitive me in κλῦθί μοι [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 5.115, +others); ὅ μοι πόσις “Schwyzer” 683 (5th c.AD: Cypria)]]; Doric dialect ἐμίν [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Epicharmus Comicus 99, “AJA” 29.461 (Rhodian, 5th c.BC), 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Acharnenses” 733, 3rd c.BC: Theocritus Poeta Bucolicus 4.30]]; Tarentum dialect ἐμίνη [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [3rd c.BC: Rhinthon Comicus 13: _accusative_ ἐμέ]], enclitic μ; [Refs 5th c.AD+ [5th c.AD: Cypria μι “Inscription Cyprian dialect” 59,60 H.]]

__III
dual, nominative and accusative, νῶι, we two, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 5.34, etc.]]; accusative νῶιν Zenod.ad [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 8.377]]; Attic dialect νώ [Refs 8th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Phaedrus” 278b (also 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 5.219, 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 15.475); νῶε 5th-6th c.BC: Antimachus Colophonius Elegiacus et Epicus 39, 6th c.BC: Corinna Lyrica 5: _genitive_, _dative_ νῶι; νῷν 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Antigone” 3]]; νῶι dative, [Refs 5th c.AD+ [5th-6th c.AD: Orphica “Lithica” 773]]; νῶιν, ={ἡμῖν}, [Refs 4th c.AD+ [4th c.AD(?): Quintus Smyrnaeus Epicus 1.213, etc.]]

__IV
plural, nominative ἡμεῖς (ἡμέες falsa lectio in [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 2.6, +others, rejected by 2nd c.AD: Apollonius Dyscolus Grammaticus “de Pronominibus;” 93.1)]]; Aeolic dialect ἄμμες [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 9.303, 7th-6th c.BC: Alcaeus Lyricus 18.3, 5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “P.” 4.144]]; Doric dialect ἁμές [Refs 7th c.BC+ [7th c.BC: Alcman Lyricus 65, 5th c.BC: Epicharmus Comicus 42, 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Lysistrata” 168:— _genitive_ ἡμῶν (also ἥμων 2nd c.AD: Apollonius Dyscolus Grammaticus “de Syntaxi;” 130.23)]]; Ionic dialect ἡμέων [Refs 8th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.112, etc.; ἡμείων 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 24.170, 3rd c.BC: Herodas Mimographus 1.46]]; Aeolic dialect ἀμμέων [Refs 7th c.BC+ [7th-6th c.BC: Alcaeus Lyricus 88, “Milet.” 3 No.152.29]]; ἄμμων [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [[prev. work]74, 2nd c.AD: Apollonius Dyscolus Grammaticus “de Pronominibus;” 95.3]]; Doric dialect ἁμέων [Refs 7th c.BC+ [7th c.BC: Alcman Lyricus 66]]; ἁμῶν [[Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Epicharmus Comicus] 266, 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Lysistrata” 168, 3rd c.BC: Theocritus Poeta Bucolicus 2.158]]; Cretan dialect, Boeotian dialect ἁμίων [Refs 5th c.BC+ [“SIG” 528.5, 2nd c.AD: Apollonius Dyscolus Grammaticus “de Pronominibus;” 95.21:— _dative_ ἡμῖν, in 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus also ἡμίν]] (ῐ) (or ἧμιν Aristarch.ad [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 1.214, 2nd c.AD: Apollonius Dyscolus Grammaticus “de Pronominibus;” 95.3)]]; also rarely in Comedy texts, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Phrynichus Comicus 37, 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Aves” 386 (uncertain)]]; Aeolic dialect ἄμμῐν, ἄμμῐ, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 1.384, 7th-6th c.BC: Alcaeus Lyricus 80, +others, 5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “P.” 4.155, 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Septem contra Thebas” 156 (Lyric poetry), “Milet.” 3 No.152; ἄμμεσιν 7th-6th c.BC: Alcaeus Lyricus 100]]; Doric dialect also ἁμίν or ἇμιν, [Refs 7th c.BC+ [7th c.BC: Alcman Lyricus 77, 78, 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Eumenides” 347 (Lyric poetry), 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Lysistrata” 1081]]; with ῑ, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [[prev. author] “Ach.” 821, 3rd c.BC: Theocritus Poeta Bucolicus 7.145:— _accusative_ ἡμᾶς (also ἧμᾰς 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 16.372)]]; Ionic dialect ἡμέας [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 8.211, “SIG” 273.25 (Milet., 4th c.BC)]]; ἥμεας [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 4.294 (cf. Hdn.Gr. 2.140)]]; Aeolic dialect ἄμμε [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 1.59, 7th-6th c.BC: Sappho Lyrica 115]], Theocr.8.25; Doric dialect ἁμέ [Refs 6th c.BC+ [“SIG” 1 (Abu Simbel, 6th c.BC), 5th c.BC: Epicharmus Comicus 173, 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Acharnenses” 759 codices, “Lys.” 95.]]—On these dialectic varieties, [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [see 2nd c.AD: Apollonius Dyscolus Grammaticus “de Pronominibus;” 50]] ff. (Cf. Sanskrit ahám (ἐγών), accusative plural asmā´n; for νώ cf. Sanskrit nau):—frequently in answers, as an affirmative, especially in form ἔγωγε, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Trachiniae” 1248, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Theaetetus” 149b, etc.]]; οὗτος ἐ. here am [Refs 5th c.BC+ [I, 5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “O.” 4.26; ὅδ᾽ ἐκεῖνος ἐ. 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Coloneus” 138 (Lyric poetry)]]; rarely with Article, τὸν ἐμέ myself, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Theaetetus” 166a, “Sph.” 239b (but ὁ ἐ.]] the Self, the Ego, [Refs 5th c.AD+ [5th-6th c.AD: Damascius Philosophus “de Principiis” 444)]]; τίς ὢν οὗτος ὁ ἐγὼ τυγχάν; [Refs 4th c.BC+ [1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus 2.1119a; τί ἐστι φίλο; ἄλλος ἐ. 4th-5th c.BC: Pythagoras Philosophus cited in 5th c.AD: Hermias Alexandrinus Philosophus “in Platonis Phaedrum scholia” p.166 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus]]; τί τοῦτ᾽ ἐμο; ἡμῖν τί τοῦτ᾽ ἔστ; Latin quid mea hoc refert ? __5
thing thought, unspoken word, purpose, design, 1.545 (plural); μύθων οὓς μνηστῆρες ἐνὶ φρεσὶ βυσσοδόμευον [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 4.676, compare 777; ἔχετ᾽ ἐν φρεσὶ μῦθον 15.445; ἔχε σιγῇ μ., ἐπίτρεψον δὲ θεοῖσι 19.502, compare 11.442]]; matter, θεοῖσι μῦθον ἐπιτρέψαι [Refs [22.289]]; μῦθον μυθείσθην, τοῦ εἵνεκα λαὸν ἄγειραν the reason why.., [Refs [3.140.]]

[Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Fragmenta” 484, compare 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Symposium” 177a, 3rd c.BC: Callimachus Epicus “Lavacrum Palladis” 56, 1st c.AD: Philo Judaeus 1.601, 1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus 2.661a]]; saw, proverb, τριγέρων μ. τάδε φωνεῖ [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Choephori” 314 (_anapaest meter_).]]

__7
talk of men, rumour, ἀγγελίαν.. τὰν ὁ μέγας μ. ἀέξει [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Ajax” 226 (Lyric poetry), compare 188 (Lyric poetry, _plural_), 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Iphigenia Aulidensis” 72]]; report, message, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Trachiniae” 67 (_plural_), 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Ion” 1340.]]

__II
tale, story, narrative, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 3.94, 4.324, 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Antigone” 11, etc.: in 8th c.BC: Homerus Epicus like the later λόγος, without distinction of true or false, μ. παιδός]] of or about him, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 11.492: so in Trag., ἀκούσει μῦθον ἐν βραχεῖ λόγῳ (χρόνῳ codex M.) 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Persae” 713; μύθων τῶν Λιβυστικῶν [prev. author] “fragment” 139.1: in Prose, τὸν εἰκότα μ.]] the like ly story, like lihood, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Timaeus” 29d: proverbial, μ. ἀπώλετο]], either of a story which never comes to an end, or of one told to those who do not listen, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Cratinus Comicus 59, 5th c.BC: Crates Comicus 21, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Theaetetus” 164d, compare “R.” 621b, “Lg.” 645b, “Phlb.” 14a]]; μ. ἐσώθη 'that's the end of the story', [Refs 9th c.AD+ [9th c.AD: Photius Legal icographus, etc.]]

fiction (opposed to λόγος, historic truth), [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “O.” 1.29 (_plural_), “N.” 7.23 (_plural_), 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Phaedo” 61b, “Prt.” 320c, 324d, etc.]]

__II.3
generally, fiction, μ. ἴδιοι [Refs 1st c.BC+ [1st c.BC: Philodemus Philosophus “περὶ ποιημάτων” 5.5]]; legend, myth, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 2.45, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 330d, “Lg.” 636c, etc.; ὁ περὶ θεῶν μ. 4th-3rd c.BC: Epicurus Philosophus “Epistulae” 3p.65U.; τοὺς μ. τοὺς ἐπιχωρίους γέγραφεν “SIG” 382.7 (Delos, 3rd c.BC).]]

__II.4
professed work of fiction, children's story, fable, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 377a]]; of Aesop's fables, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Meteorologica” 356b11.]]

plot of a comedy or tragedy, [Refs [[prev. author] “Po.” 1449b5, 1450a4, 1451a16.]]

={στάσις}, [Refs [Panyasis Epicus in “Coll.Alex.” p.249, variant in Batrachomyomachia 135]]; compare μυθιήτης.

as adjective νεκρός, ά, όν, dead, first in [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus, ν. ἵππος “fragment” 203]]; ν. σώματα Mitteis [Refs 5th c.BC+ [“Chr.” 31 ii 22 (2nd c.BC), 3rd c.AD(?): Achilles Tatius Astronomus 3.5, compare 1st c.BC: Nicolaus Damascenus Historicus 58 1st c.AD: Josephus Historicus, 1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus 2.685b, 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus Eph.5.1, “POxy.” 51.8 (2nd c.AD), “BGU” 1024vii26 (4th-5th c.AD)]] (but also τὰ τῶν ν. σώματα [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Leges” 959b; σῶμα.. νεκροῦ 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Hecuba” 679); ν. χελώνη 2nd c.AD: Lucianus Sophista “DDeor.” 7.4]]: comparative -ότερος[Refs 1st c.AD+ [“Anthologia Graeca” 11.135 (1st c.AD: Lucillius Epigrammaticus).]]

deep_entry:
Abbott-Smith / STEPBible (TBESG)
νέος, -α, -ον
[in LXX for נַעַר (Gen.37:2, Exo_33:11, al.), חָדָשׁ (Lev.23:16, Num.28:26, al.), etc.; compar. -ώτερος for קָטָן, צָעִיר, etc. ;]
__1. young, youthful: Tit.2:4.
__2. new (prop., in respect of time; see: καινός): οἶνος (cf. οἶ. καινός, Mat.26:20), Mat.9:17, Mrk.2:22, Luk.5:37-39; φύραμα (figuratively), 1Co.5:7; διαθήκη (cf. καινὴ δ., Heb.9:15), Heb.12:24; metaphorically, ἄνθρωπος (cf. καινὸς ἀ, Eph.2:15), Col.3:10.
__3. Compar., -ώτερος, -α, -ον, younger: Luk.15:12-13 22:26, Jhn.21:18; pl., οἱ ν., Act.5:6 (Rackham, in l), 1Ti.5:11, Tit.2:6; opposite to πρεσβύτεροι, 1Ti.5:1, 1Pe.5:5; αἱ ν., 1Ti.5:2 5:14.
__4. Νέα Πόλις, Neapolis: Act.16:11 (Rec., Νεάπολις, which see)
νεώτερος, see: νέος
SYN.: καινός, which see  (AS)

---

LSJ / STEPBible (TFLSJ)
νέος, νέα,
Ionic dialect νέη, νέον; Ionic dialect νεῖος (which see): [feminine νέας as monosyllable, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Septem contra Thebas” 327 (Lyric poetry)]]; contraction feminine νῆ [Refs 6th c.BC+ [6th c.BC: Xenophanes Poeta Philosophus 42 (= 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Fragmenta” 9), 5th c.BC: Eugaeon Historicus (?) 1]:]]

__1
young, youthful (of children, youths, and of men at least as old as [Refs 8th c.BC+ [30, see 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Memorabilia” 1.2.35), ν. πάϊς 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 4.665; κοῦροι ν. 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 13.95; ν. ἀνήρ 23.589: alone, νέοι]]youths, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [1.463, 8th-7th c.BC: Hesiodus Epicus “Scutum Herculis” 281, etc.]]: later mostly with Article, οἱ νέοι [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Nubes” 1059, etc.: proverbial, ὁ ν. ἔσται ν.]] 'boys will be boys', [Refs 4th c.AD+ [4th c.AD: Libanius Sophista “Epistulae” 910.3]]; οἱ ν., corporately organized, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [“SIG” 831.8 (Pergam., 2nd c.AD), etc.; opposed to ἔφηβοι, παῖδες, [prev. work]589.38 (Magn.Mae., 2nd c.BC): opposed to γέρων, ἠμὲν νέοι ἠδὲ γέροντες 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 2.789, etc.; ἢ ν. ἠὲ παλαιός 14.108, compare 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 1.395, etc.; opposed to γεραίτερος, 3.24; opposed to προγενέστερος, 2.29]]; opposed to γεραιός, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Respublica Lacedaemoniorum” 1.7]]; εὐθὺς ἐκ νέου ἐθίζειν from youth upwards, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Gorgias” 510d, etc.; ἐκ νέων παίδων [prev. author] “Lg.” 887d; ἐκ νέων ἐθίζεσθαι 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Ethica Nicomachea” 1103b24]]; ἐκ νέας (i.e. ψυχῆς) [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 409a]]; τὸ ν., ={νεότης}, youth (in the abstract), [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Coloneus” 1229 (Lyric poetry), 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Ion” 545: also in concrete sense, τὸ ν. ἅπαν]] all young creatures, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Leges” 653d; οὐ δύναται τὸ ν. ἡσυχάζειν 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Politica” 1340b29; σκιρτητικὸν τὸ ν. 1st c.AD: Cornutus Philosophus “de Natura Deorum” 20]]; also, of minors, νέου ὄντος ἔτι [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 1.107]]; compare νεώτερος.

__1.b
rarely of animals and plants, ὄρπηκες, ἔρνος, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 21.38, 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 6.163; οἱ ν. τῶν νεβρῶν 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Cynegeticus” 9.8.]]

__2
suited to a youth, youthful, ἄεθλοι [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “O.” 2.43; ν. θράσος 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Persae” 744 (troch.)]]; ν. φροντίς youthful spirits, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Medea” 48; νέαις ταῖς διανοίαις χρωμένους 5th c.BC: Lysias Orator 24.16]]; of persons, ἄφρων νέος τε [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Iphigenia Aulidensis” 489, compare 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 378a; ν. τε καὶ ὀξύς [prev. author] “Grg.” 463e (but διαφέρει οὐδὲν ν. τὴν ἡλικίαν ἢ τὸ ἦθος νεαρός 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Ethica Nicomachea” 1095a6).]]

__II
new, fresh, ν. θάλαμος [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 17.36; ν. ἄλγος 6.462; νέῳ.. κόλλοπι 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 21.407 (this sense elsewhere in 8th c.BC: Homerus Epicus only in _adverb_ νέον, see below)]]; λίνον [Refs 7th c.BC+ [7th-6th c.BC: Alcaeus Lyricus 15 (uncertain); πόνοι.. νέοι παλαιοῖσι συμμιγεῖς κακοῖς 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Septem contra Thebas” 740 (Lyric poetry), etc.; οἶνος ν. 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Pax” 916; ἐν τοῖς μουσικοῖς τὰ ν. [μέλη] εὐδοκιμεῖ 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 1.6.38]]; ἡ ν. (i.e. σελήνη) the new moon, especially in phrase ἕνη καὶ νέα, see at {ἕνος} [Refs [2]]; but μηνὸς τῇ ν. (i.e. ἡμέρᾳ) on the first day of the month, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Leges” 849b; ν. ἦμαρ 3rd c.BC: Apollonius Rhodius Epicus 4.1479]]: in this sense rarely of persons, ὁ ν. ταγὸς μακάρων [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Prometheus Vinctus” 96 (_anapaest meter_), compare 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Plutus” 960; οἱ ν. θεοί 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Eumenides” 721]]; compare νεώτερος.

__II.2
of events, etc., new, with collateral notion of unexpected, strange, untoward, evil, τί ν.; [Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. author] “Ag.” 85 (_anapaest meter_); προσδοκῶ τι γὰρ ν. 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Supplices” 99]]; μῶν τι βουλεύῃ ν.; [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Philoctetes” 1229, compare 554, 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Hippolytus” 794, “Ba.” 362. 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 5.50. etc.: ἀπροσδοκήτους καὶ ν. λόγους 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Supplices” 712; καινὰ ν. τ᾽ ἄχη [prev. author] “Pers.” 665 (Lyric poetry): this sense is more common in _comparative_, see at {νεώτερος}.]]

__III
neuter νέον as adverb of Time, lately, just now, opposed to both to distant past and present, παῖδα ν. γεγαῶτα [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 19.400, compare 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 3.394; ν. κρατεῖν 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Prometheus Vinctus” 35, 955, etc.: also used Adverbially with the _Article_, καὶ τὸ πάλαι (variant{παλαιόν}) καὶ τὸ ν. 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 9.26: in Prose νεωστί (which see): rarely _comparative_]] adverb νεωτέρως,[Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Leges” 907c]]: superlative νεώτατα most recently, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 1.7]]; also ἐκ νέας, Ionic dialect αὖτις ἐκ νέης, anew, afresh, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.60, 5.116.]]

__IV
. the degrees of comparative are νεώτερος, νεώτατος, see at {νεώτερος}: νεαίτερος is corrupt for νεαίρετος in [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Fragmenta - American Journal of Philology” 330. (νέϝος (in νεϝόστατος, which see)]], cf. Sanskrit návas, Latin novus, etc.)

[Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “I.” 8(7).50]]; νεῦσον, Κρονίων [Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. author] “P.” 1.71; νεῦσον, τέκνον, πείσθητι 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Philoctetes” 484, compare 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Pax” 883]]: with accusative et infinitive, grant, assure, promise that.., νεῦσε δέ οἱ λαὸν σόον ἔμμεναι [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 8.246]]: with infinitive future, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “O.” 7.67]]: with infinitive aorist, [Refs 1st c.BC+ [“Anthologia Graeca” 6.244 (1st c.BC-1st c.AD: Crinagoras Epigrammaticus)]]: with accusative of things, grant, promise, νεῦσε δέ οἱ κούρην [Refs 5th c.BC+ [“hymnus ad Cererem” 445, compare 463; νεύσατε τὰν ἀδόκητον χάριν 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Coloneus” 248 (Lyric poetry), compare 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Alcestis” 978 (Lyric poetry).]]

__3
generally, nod, bend forward, of warriors, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 13.133; νεῦον τὸ αἰδοῖον 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 2.48; λόφος καθύπερθεν ἔνευεν 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 3.337, compare 7th-6th c.BC: Alcaeus Lyricus 15.3, etc.; στάχυες νεύοιεν ἔραζε 8th-7th c.BC: Hesiodus Epicus “Opera et Dies” 473, etc.; ν. κάτω]]stoop, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Electra” 839; ν. ἐς τὴν γῆν 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Vespae” 1110, compare 3rd c.BC: Theocritus Poeta Bucolicus 22.90: with _accusative_, οὕτω νῦν μνηστῆρες.. νεύοιεν κεφαλὰς δεδμημένοι 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 18.237; ἐς πέδον κάρα νεῦσαι φόβῳ 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Antigone” 270, compare 441.]]

Ionic dialect νικέω [NT+4th c.BC+ [3rd c.AD: Democritus Epigrammaticus 249, 3rd c.BC: Herodas Mimographus 1.51, also “GDI” 1413.16 (Aetol.), “SIG” 265.4 (Delph., 4th c.BC), variant in NT.Rev.2.7]]; Aeolic dialect νίκημι [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [3rd c.BC: Theocritus Poeta Bucolicus 7.40, “Anthologia Graeca” 7.743 (Antip.)]]; also in imperfect νίκη conjecture in [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “N.” 5.5, compare 3rd c.BC: Theocritus Poeta Bucolicus 6.46]]: Epic dialect imperfect 1st pers. plural νικάσκομεν [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 11.512:]]future -ήσω, later -ήσομαι[Refs 4th c.AD+ [4th c.AD(?): Hierocles Facetiarum Scriptor “Facet.” 205]]; Doric dialect 2nd pers. singular νικαξῇ variant in [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [3rd c.BC: Theocritus Poeta Bucolicus 21.32:]]perfect νενίκηκα, etc.: (νίκη):

__I
absolutely, conquer, prevail in battle, in the games, or in any contest, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 3.439, etc.]]; ὁ νικήσας the conqueror,[Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. work] 138, 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Symposium” 5.9, etc.]]; ὁ νικηθείς the conquered, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 23.656, 663]]; ἐνίκησα καὶ δεύτερος καὶ τέταρτος ἐγενόμην I won the first prize [at Olympia], etc., [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 6.16, compare 5th-6th c.BC: Isocrates Orator 16.33]]: present frequently in sense, to be (or be proclaimed) conqueror, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “O.” 9.112, 13.30, compare 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 8.2.27, “An.” 2.1.1]]; νικᾶν πᾶσι τοῖς κριταῖς or ἑνὶ κριτῇ in their opinion, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Aves” 445, 447]]; πολὺ ν. win a decisive victory, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 7.34, etc.; τὰ πάντα ν. 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “An.” [same place]: frequently with _dative_ modi, πυγμῇ]] in boxing, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 23.669; ναυμαχίῃ 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 7.10.β᾽]]; ἵππῳ [Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. author] 6.122; μάχῃ 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Phoenissae” 1143, etc.; ἵππῳ ἢ συνωρίδι ἢ ζεύγει 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Apologia” 36d; λαμπάδι 5th-6th c.BC: Andocides Orator 4.42, etc.: with _accusative_ _cognate_ in same sense, πάντα ἐνίκα]] he won all the bouts, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 4.389, 5.807]]; τὰ κοῦφα, τὰ μείζοναν., [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Alcestis” 1029, 1031; τῶν παλαισμάτων ἓν ν. 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Phaedrus” 256b; ἅρμα ν. 5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “I.” 4(3).25; παγκράτιον 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 5.49]]; ναυμαχίαν, μάχας, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. author] 7.66, 5th-6th c.BC: Isocrates Orator 12.257, etc.: frequently ν. Ὀλύμπια]] to be conqueror in the Olympian games, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 1.126; τὠλύμπια 4th c.BC: Timocles Comicus 8.17; τὰ Παναθήναια 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Ion” 530b; ν. Ὀλυμπιάδα 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 9.33 (also ν. Ὀλυμπίασιν 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Apologia” 36d; ἐν Πυθίοισι 5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “N.” 2.9): with _dative_ et _accusative_, τὰ Πύθια τῷ τεθρίππῳ ν. 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 59.33]]; πολλοὺς ἀγῶνας οὐ παγκρατίῳ μόνον, κτλ., [Refs 1st c.AD+ [1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus 2.811d]]; Ὀλυμπίασι παῖδας στάδιον ν. conquer in the boys' race in the stadium at Olympia, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 58.66: with double _accusative_, Πύθια ν. ἄνδρας]] Diog.Cyn. cited in [Refs 3rd c.AD+ [3rd c.AD(?): Diogenes Laertius 6.33]]: also in Attic dialect Inscrr. with genitive, Λεωντὶς ἀνδρῶν ἐνίκα [Refs [“IG” 2.1291, +others: generally with _accusative_ _cognate_, νίκην ν.]] win a victory, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Supplices” 1060, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 465d, etc. (compare below 11)]]; also ν. τρίποδα win it, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Simonides Lyricus 147.]]

__I.2
prevail, be superior, μύθοισιν, ἔγχεϊ, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 18.252; δόλοισι 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 3.121]]; κάλλει ἐνίκα (i.e. κρητήρ) [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 23.742; πᾶσαν ἀρετὴν νενικηκώς 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Leges” 964c]]: with participle, εὐεργετῶν ν. [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Agesilaus” 9.7.]]

__I.3
of opinions, etc., βουλὴ κακὴ νίκησεν the evil counsel prevailed, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 10.46; τὰ χερείονα νικᾷ 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 1.576, 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 18.404; ἐνίκα ἡ γνώμη 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 5.36, compare 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 2.12, etc.; ἡ νικῶσα βουλή 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Medea” 912]]; ἐκ τῆς νικώσης [γνώμης] according to the prevailing opinion, vote of the majority, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 6.1.18, 6.2.12; ταῦτ᾽ ἐνίκα 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Antigone” 274; νικᾷ πάσαισι ταῖς ψήφοις ὁ νόμος]]is carried, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Leges” 801a; σὺν ψάφῳ τᾷ νικεούσᾳ “SIG” 265.4 (Delph., 4th c.BC)]]: frequently of orators, νικᾷ.. ὁ κακὸς ἐν πλήθει λέγων [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Orestes” 944; ν. γνώμῃσι 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 3.82 (so γνώμῃ, variant{γνώμην}, [prev. author] 1.61, compare 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Vespae” 594): frequently _impersonal_, ἐνίκα (i.e. ἡ γνώμη)]] it was resolved, with infinitive, ἐνίκα μὴ ἐκλιπεῖν τὴν πόλιν it was carried not.., [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 6.101; τέλος γε μέντοι δεῦρ᾽ ἐνίκησεν μολεῖν 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Antigone” 233, etc.]]; ἐνίκησε.. λοιμὸν εἰρῆσθαι it was the prevailing opinion that.., [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 2.54]]; ἐν δημοκρατίᾳ νικᾷ ζῆν it is preferable.., [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Politicus” 303b.]]

__I.4
with infinitive, succeed in.., ἐνίκησε σκορπίσαι [Refs [“Psalms of Solomon [1st c.BC]” 4.13.]]

__I.5
as law-term, ν. τὴν δίκην win one's cause, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Electra” 955, compare 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Vespae” 581; simply νικᾶν “GDI” 5011.11 (from Gortyn), 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Ἀθηναίων Πολιτεία” 42.1, “Rh.Al.” 1433a6, “PHal.” 1.58 (3rd c.BC), etc.]]; νικήσεις ἐν τῷ κρίνεσθαί σε [NT.Rom.3.4]:—passive, with genitive, αἴ κα νικαθῇ τῶν ἐνεχύρων [Refs 5th c.BC+ [“Schwyzer” 177.9 (Crete, 5th c.BC)]]; see below 11.

__II
with accusative, conquer, vanquish, Ἕκτορα [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 7.192, etc.: frequently with _dative_ modi, μάχῃ ν. Ἀχαιούς 16.79; ἀγορῇ ν. υἷας Ἀχαιῶν 2.370; πόδεσσι δὲ πάντας ἐνίκα 20.410; κάλλει ἐνίκων φῦλα γυναικῶν 9.130]]; πάντα ν. ἄνδρα.. κακοῖσιν surpass him in miseries, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Hecuba” 659; ν. τινὰ ἔν τινι 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Symposium” 213e, etc.]]; μὴ φῦναι τὸν ἅπαντα νικᾷ λόγον excels the whole account, [NT+5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Coloneus” 1224 (Lyric poetry); νίκα ἐν τῷ ἀγαθῷ τὸ κακόν NT.Rom.12.21: with _accusative_ _cognate_, μάχην ν. τινά 5th-6th c.BC: Isocrates Orator 8.58, 4th c.BC: Aeschines Orator 3.181, etc.]]:—passive, ἔστιν ἃ τῶν ἄθλων δὶς ἕκαστος ἐνικήθη [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Historia Graeca (Hellenica)” 4.5.2]]: with participle, ν. ἀλεξόμενός τινα [Refs [[prev. author] “An.” 1.9.11, etc.]]

__II.b
as law-term [Refs 8th c.BC+ [compare(1.5), νίκης τήν μιν ἐγὼ νίκησα 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 11.545]]:—passive, ἧ δέ κα νικαθῇ [Refs [“Leg.Gort.” 1.23, +others]]; also of objects in dispute, damages, etc., recover, [Refs [[prev. work]1.28, +others]]:—passive, to be assigned, adjudicated, [Refs [[prev. work]1.55.]]

__II.2
generally, overpower, especially of passions, etc., νόον νίκησε νεοίη [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 23.604; μὴ φόβος σὲ νικάτω φρένας 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Eumenides” 88, compare 133; [φύσις] νικᾷ τῷ ἥσσονι τὸ μεῖζον τῆς ἐλπίδος 3rd c.AD: Democritus Epigrammaticus 176]]; βαρεῖαν ἡδονὴν νικᾶτέ με grievous is the pleasure ye win prevailing over me, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Coloneus” 1204: with]]infinitive, μηδ᾽ ἡ βία σε.. νικησάτω τοσόνδε μισεῖν let not violence prevail on thee to.., [Refs [[prev. author] “Aj.” 1334: with _genitive_ of comparison, νικᾷ γὰρ ἁρετή με τῆς ἔχθρας πολύ]] weighs with me more than enmity, from the comparable force in νικᾷ, [Refs [[prev. work] 1357 codices]]

__II.3
passive, to be vanquished, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Homerus Epicus only in]]participle νικηθείς (see. above [Refs [1.1)]]; νικᾶσθαι ὕπνῳ, κέρδεσιν, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Agamemnon” 291, 342; ἡδονῇ 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Electra” 1272; συμφορᾷ 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Medea” 1195; also ὑπὸ τοῦ κακοῦ 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 2.51; πρὸς ἱμέρου 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Fragmenta” 932.4, etc.: sometimes with _genitive_, ἱμέρου νικώμενος 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Supplices” 1005; αὐτῆς [τε] τῆς δίκης.. αὐτοῦ τε τοῦ ἀληθοῦς νικᾶσθαι 5th c.BC: Antipho Orator 5.87: frequently of persons, νικᾶσθαί τινος,]] with genitive of comparison, to be inferior, yield to, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Ajax” 1353, 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Medea” 315, “Cyc.” 454]]; ξείνων νενίκανται θύραι the doors give way to the guests, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “N.” 9.2; ἢν τοῦτο νικηθῇς ἐμοῦ 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Nubes” 1087.]]

νοιεω νοέω, -ῶ
(νοῦς), [in LXX chiefly for בִּין, also for שָׂכַל hi., etc ;]
__1. to perceive with the mind, understand (for the phrase νοῶν κ. φρονῶν, in wills, see MM, xvii): absol., Mat.16:9, Mrk.8:17; with accusative, Eph.3:4, 1Ti.1:7; with dative instr., τ. καρδίᾳ, Jhn.12:40; pass., Rom.1:20; before ὅτι, Mat.15:17 16:11, Mrk.7:18; with accusative and inf., Heb.11:8.
__2. to think, consider: absol., Mat.24:15, Mrk.13:14, Eph.3:20; with accusative of thing(s), 2Ti.2:7
(cf. -εὐ, κατα-, μετα-, προ-, ὑπο-νοέω).†

νο-έω,
Aeolic dialect νόημι (which see): Epic dialect aorist 1 νόησα [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 8.91]]; Ionic dialect ἔνωσα (ἐν-) [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.86:]]perfect νενόηκα, Ionic dialect νένωκα (ἐν-) [Refs [[prev. author] 3.6]]; imperative νενόηθι Hilgard Excerpta e libris Herodiani [Refs [30]]:—middle, Epic dialect aorist νοήσατο [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 10.501]]; participle νοησάμενος [Refs 7th c.BC+ [7th-6th c.BC: Alcaeus Lyricus “Supp.” 7.6, νωσάμενος 6th c.BC: Theognis Elegiacus 1298, 3rd c.BC: Theocritus Poeta Bucolicus 25.263, 3rd c.BC: Callimachus Epicus “Fragmenta” 345, etc.:]] —passive (mostly in middle sense), future νοηθήσομαι [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd c.AD: Sextus Empiricus Philosophus “Πυρρώνειοι ὑποτυπώσεις” 2.175, 2nd c.AD: Galenus Medicus “de Usu Partium” 17.1]]: aorist ἐνοήθην [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Leges” 692c]]; also Ionic dialect (ἐπ-) [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 3.122, 6.115:]]perfect νενόημαι, Ionic dialect νένωμαι [Refs 6th c.BC+ [6th c.BC: Anacreon Lyricus 10, 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 9.53, 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Fragmenta” 182, Aëthlius 4: _3rd.pers._]]singular pluperfect ἐνένωτο (in middle sense) [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.77. Hdn.Gr. 2.253 cites νοῦνται from 3rd c.AD: Democritus Epigrammaticus (see. below)]] and perfect passive νένοται. —The compounds with ἀπό, διά, ἐν, ἐπί, μετά, πρό are used chiefly in middle:—perceive by the eyes, observe (οἱ ἀρχαῖοι τὸ ν. σωματικὸν.. ὑπολαμβάνουσιν [Refs 8th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “de Anima” 427a26), 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 3.396]]; ὀξὺ ν.[Refs 8th c.BC+ [[prev. work] 374, 8th-7th c.BC: Hesiodus Epicus “Theogonia” 838, etc.]]; ὀφθαλμοῖσιν, ἐν ὀφθαλμοῖσι ν., [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 15.422, 24.294.]]

__2
perceive by the mind, apprehend, τὸν δὲ ἰδὼν ἐνόησε [Refs 8th c.BC+ [11.599; οὐ.. ἴδον οὐδ᾽ ἐνόησα 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 13.318, compare 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 10.550, 24.337, etc.; ἡ δ᾽ οὔτ᾽ ἀθρῆσαι δύνατ᾽ ἀντίη οὔτε νοῆσαι 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 19.478]]; ἢ λάθετ᾽ ἢ οὐκ ἐνόησεν or did not take notice, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 9.537, compare 5.665]]; νοέεις δὲ καὶ αὐτός thou thyself art aware of it, [LXX+8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 21.257; θυμῷ νοέω καὶ οἶδα ἕκαστα 18.228; ν. τῇ καρδίᾳ LXX.Isa.44.18]]; πρὸ ὃ τοῦ ἐνόησεν one perceives before the other, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 10.224: _absolutely_, [θεὸς] οὖλος ὁρᾷ, οὖλος δὲ νοεῖ, οὖλος δὲ τ᾽ ἀκούει 6th c.BC: Xenophanes Poeta Philosophus 24; ταὐτὸν δ᾽ ἐστὶ νοεῖν τε καὶ οὕνεκέν ἐστι νόημα 4th-5th c.BC: Parmenides Poeta Philosophus 8.34]]: frequently in Philos., of thought, μάλιστα ἔοικεν ἴδιον [ψυχῆς] τὸ ν. [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “de Anima” 403a8; ἔοικε δὴ τὸ ζῆν εἶναι κυρίως τὸ αἰσθάνεσθαι ἢ ν. [prev. author] “EN” 1170a19, compare 1166a22; καλῶς ν. καὶ λέγειν καὶ πράττειν 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Cynegeticus” 1.18]]: also with participle added, ὡς ἐνόησεν ἔμ᾽ ἥμενον [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 10.375]]; of a future event, νοέω κακὸν ὔμμιν ἐρχόμενον [Refs [20.367]]: with infinitive, οὐκ ἐνόησα ἄψορρον καταβῆναι [NT+8th c.BC+ [11.62; πίστει νοοῦμεν κατηρτίσθαι τοὺς αἰῶνας NT.Heb.11.3: followed by ὡς.., 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 22.32, compare 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Epinomis” 977c; νόει θ᾽ ᾗ δῆλον ἕκαστον 5th c.BC: Empedocles Poeta Philosophus 4.13]]:—middle, νωσάμενος [Refs 6th c.BC+ [6th c.BC: Theognis Elegiacus 1298; νοούμενος 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Tyrannus” 1487]]:—passive, to be apprehended by thought, τὰς ἰδέας νοεῖσθαι μὲν ὁρᾶσθαι δ᾽ οὔ [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 507b]]; τὰ νοούμενα, opposed to τὰ αἰσθητά,[[prev. work] 508c; τὰ ἀόρατα τοῖς ποιήμασι νοούμενα NT.Rom.1.20.]

__3
think, consider, reflect, φρεσὶ ν. ἔνθ᾽ εἴην ἢ ἔνθα” [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 15.81; μετὰ φρεσὶ σῇσι νόησον Αἰνείαν, ἤ κέν μιν ἐρύσσεαι ἦ κεν ἐάσῃς 20.311; οὐδ᾽ ἐνόησε κατὰ φρένα καὶ κατὰ θυμὸν ὡς.. [prev. work] 264]]; ἐπ᾽ ἀμφότερα ν. look to both sides, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 8.22: with _accusative_ _cognate_, ἄλλα νοέειν]] to be other wise minded, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. author] 7.168; also εἰπὲ δ᾽ ᾗ νοεῖς 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Trachiniae” 1135, compare “El.” 1435]]: participle νοέων, έουσα, wary, discreet, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 1.577; τὴν μέν κεν ἐπαινέσσειε νοήσας 8th-7th c.BC: Hesiodus Epicus “Opera et Dies” 12, compare 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 15.170]]; τὰ νοέων λέγει what he says advisedly, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 8.102]]; νοῶν καὶ φρονῶν sane and in his right mind, in wills, [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [“Test.Epict.” 1.1, “PPetr.” 3p.4 (3rd c.BC)]], etc.:— in middle, φρενὶ θεῖα νοῦνται [Refs 6th c.BC+ [3rd c.AD: Democritus Epigrammaticus 129; ὑψηλὰ νενωμένος 6th c.BC: Anacreon Lyricus 10.]]

__4
consider, deem, presume to be so and so, ὡς μηκέτ᾽ ὄντα κεῖνον.. νόει [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Philoctetes” 415]]; τόδε γὰρ νοῶ κράτιστον[Refs 4th c.BC+ [[prev. work] 1176; δεῖ ν. συνεχῆ τὰ ἔνοπτρα 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Meteorologica” 373a19: with]]infinitive, δεῖ νοῆσαι τὸ μὲν ὑγρὸν εἶναι[Refs [[prev. work] 340b24, etc.]]; compare νοητέον.

__II
think out, devise, conceive τοῦτό γ᾽ ἐναίσιμον οὐκ ἐνόησε [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 2.122; ἔνθ᾽ αὖτ᾽ ἄλλ᾽ ἐνόησε θεά [prev. work] 382]]; ἄλλα μὲν αὐτὸς ἐνὶ φρεσὶ σῇσι νοήσεις, ἄλλα δὲ καὶ δαίμων ὑποθήσεται[Refs 8th c.BC+ [3.26; οὐ γάρ τις νόον ἄλλος ἀμείνονα τοῦδε νοήσει 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 9.104]]: frequently with neuter plural adjective, πεπνυμένα πάντα νοῆσαι [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 18.230]]; ἄνδρων πλεῖστα νοησάμενος most cunning of men, of Sisyphus, [Refs 7th c.BC+ [7th-6th c.BC: Alcaeus Lyricus “Supp.” 7.6; ὀρθὰ ν. 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 8.3]]:—passive, ἐνθύμημα νενοημένον οὐκ ἀτόπως [Refs 1st c.BC+ [1st c.BC: Dionysius Halicarnassensis “de Thucydide” 37.]]

__II.2
purpose, intend, ἐσθλά τινι [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th-7th c.BC: Hesiodus Epicus “Opera et Dies” 286; κακόν τινι 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 3.81, compare 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Hiero” 1.15.]]

__III
with infinitive, to be minded, intend, οὐδ᾽ ἐνόησε ἐξερύσαι δόρυ bethought himself, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 5.665]]; νοέω φρεσὶ τιμήςuσθαι[Refs [22.235; νοέω δὲ καὶ αὐτὸς Ἕκτορά τοι λῦσαι 24.560]]; ἦ γὰρ νοεῖς θάπτειν σφ; [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Antigone” 44, compare 770, “El.” 389, etc.]]:—middle, once in [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Homerus Epicus, μάστιγα.. νοήσατο χερσἰν ἑλέσθαι]] he thought with himself to take the scourge, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 10.501]]; ἐνέ- νωτο στρατεύειν he was minded to march, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.77, compare 7.206, 9.53.]]

__IV
of words, bear a certain sense, mean, πυθοίμεθ᾽ ἂν τὸν χρησμὸν ὅ τι νοεῖ [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Plutus” 55, compare “Nu.” 1186, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Cratylus” 407e]]; [εἰ] τοῦτο.. νοεῖ αὐτῷ if this means for him that.., [Refs [[prev. author] “R.” 335e; also ἐπιδεῖξαι ἐθέλω τὸ νυνί μοι συμβεβηκὸς τί ποτε νοεῖ [prev. author] “Ap.” 40a]]; τὸ νοούμενον the sense, meaning, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [1st c.BC: Philodemus Gadarensis Epigrammaticus “Po.Herc.” 991.4, +others—Not in 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus or Oratt.]]

__2
thought, purpose, idea, design, τοιοῦτον ἐνὶ στήθεσσι νόημα [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 13.330; Ζεὺς.. ἐνὶ φρεσὶν ὧδε νόημα ποίησ᾽ 14.273; νοήματα.. ἐκτελέει 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 10.104, compare 7th-6th c.BC: Alcaeus Lyricus 77, 5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “P.” 6.29; σοφώτατα νοήματα [prev. author] “O.” 7.72; οὐκ οἶδ᾽ ὄττι θέω· δίχα μοι τὰ ν. 7th-6th c.BC: Sappho Lyrica 36; ἐκτὸς τῶν ἐωθότων ν. στῆσαί τινα 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 3.80; τὸ μὲν ν. τῆς θεοῦ, τὸ δὲ κλέμμ᾽ ἐμόν 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Equites” 1203, compare “Nu.” 743.]]

__3
in Philos., thought, concept, opposed to sensation, sense-presentation, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Parmenides Poeta Philosophus 8.34, etc.; φύσει διῄρηται τά τε ν. καὶ τὰ αἰσθήματα 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Fragmenta” 87; σύνθεσίς τις νοημάτων [prev. author] “de An.” 430a28]]; discursive thinking, as the function of διάνοια, [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd-3rd c.AD: Hermes Trismegistus cited in 5th c.AD: Stobaeus, Joannes 2.8.31.]]

understanding, mind, παρέπλαγξεν δὲ νόημα [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 20.346, compare 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 19.218, 6th c.BC: Theognis Elegiacus 435, 5th c.BC: Empedocles Poeta Philosophus 110.10; αἷμα γὰρ ἀνθρώποις περικάρδιόν ἐστι ν. LSJ / STEPBible (TFLSJ)
νόθ-ος, η, ον,
also ος, ον [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [(3rd c.BC: Callimachus Epicus “Fragmenta” 279)]], bastard, baseborn, i.e. born of a slave or concubine, frequently in [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” (never in 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey”), ν. υἱός 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 2.727, etc.; παῖδες ν. 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 8.103, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Apologia” 27d]]; opposed to γνήσιος, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 11.102, 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Aves” 1650]]; ὅδ᾽, εἰ ν. τις, γνησίοις ἴσον σθένει [NT+8th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Fragmenta” 87; νόθοι καὶ οὐχ υἱοί ἐστε NT.Heb.12.8: _feminine_, κούρη νόθη 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 13.173.]]

__2
at Athens, child of a citizen father and an alien mother, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 23.213, etc.; νόθος πρὸς μητρός 1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus “Themistocles” 1.]]

__3
plural, in Egypt, a class of temple-attendants, Wilcken [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [“Chr.” 66 (3rd c.BC).]]

__4
of animals, cross-bred, πρόβατα [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [“PHib.” 1.32.15 (3rd c.BC).]]

__II
generally, spurious, counterfeit, supposititious, of persons and things, λογισμῷ τινι ν. νομή, -ῆς, ἡ
(νέμω, to pasture), [in LXX chiefly for מִרְעֶה, also for נָוֶה, etc. ;]
__1. a pasture, pasturage: figuratively, Jhn.10:9
__2. a grazing, feeding; metaphorically, of a spreading sore, 2Ti.2:17 (Polyb.).†
(AS)

---

LSJ / STEPBible (TFLSJ)
νομ-ή, ἡ,
(νέμω) pasturage, ἀμφίβιον.. ἔδωκε ν. βατράχοισι Κρονίων [Refs 5th c.BC+ [Batrachomyomachia 59; νομὰς νέμειν 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.110]]; νομὰς νέμεσθαι[Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. work] 78, compare 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Leges” 679a, 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Historia Animalium” 575b4, etc.; ποιμνίων νομαί 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Tyrannus” 761]]: in concrete sense, νομαὶ βοσκημάτων herds, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 3.5.2.]]

__2
food from pasturing, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Critias” 111 C, etc.; αἷμα, ν. σαρκῶν [prev. author] “Ti.” 80e; ἡ προσήκουσα ψυχῆς ν. [prev. author] “Phdr.” 248b; ν. τῶν μελιττῶν τὸ θύμον 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Historia Animalium” 626 b20, compare “PCair.Zen.” 520.10 (3rd c.BC).]]

__3
feeding, grazing, of herds, νομὴν ποιεῖσθαι, ={νέμεσθαι}, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Historia Animalium” 596a14.]]

__3.b
metaphorically, spreading, ν. πυρός [Refs 2nd c.BC+ [2nd c.BC: Polybius Historicus 1.48.5, 1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus “Alexander” 35]]; frequently of sores, etc., ν. ποιεῖσθαι spread, [NT+3rd c.BC+ [2nd c.BC: Polybius Historicus 1.81.6; ὡς γάγγραινα, ν. ἕξει NT.2Tim.2.17, compare 3rd c.BC: Asclepiades Epigrammaticus cited in 2nd c.AD: Galenus Medicus 12.995; ἵσταται ἡ ν., of baldness, [prev. author][prev. work]411; νομαί]]spreading ulcers, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Hippocrates Medicus “προρρητικόν” 2.13, compare 2nd c.AD: Galenus Medicus 13.860, +others; ν. σαρκὸς θηριώδεις 1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus 2.165e.]]

__II
division, distribution, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 2.52 (_plural_), 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Protagoras” 321c, +others]]; of an inheritance, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 36.12]]; ἡ πατρῴα (variant{πατρῴων}) ν. [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Politica” 1303b34]]; διεφθαρκὼς νομῇ χρημάτων τὸν δῆμον by largess of money, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aeschines Orator 2.76, compare “IG” 5(1).1346 (_Laconian dialect_)]]: in plural, = Latin donativa, [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd c.AD: Herodianus Grammaticus 3.8.9, 5.5.8, 6.8.8.]]

__II.2
paying out or distribution in bandaging, [Refs 1st c.AD+ [1st-2nd c.AD: Heliodorus Medicus cited in 4th c.AD: Oribasius Medicus 48.25.1, 2nd c.AD: Galenus Medicus 18 (2).741.]]

__III
in Law, = Latin possessio, Wilcken [Refs 3rd c.AD+ [“Chr.” 41 iii 20 (3rd c.AD)]]; μακρᾶς ν. παραγραφή, = longae posses- sionis praescriptio, Mitteis [Refs 3rd c.AD+ [“Chr.” 374 i 3 (3rd c.AD)]]; ν. ἄδικος, = injusta possessio, [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [PTeb. 286.7 (2nd c.AD)]]; ἐπὶ νομῆς πέμπειν, = in possessionem mittere, [Refs 6th c.AD+ [6th c.AD: Justinianus Imperator “Novellae” 53.4.1.]]

__IV
ἐν χειρῶν νομαῖς, ={ἐν χειρῶν νόμῳ} [Refs 2nd c.BC+ [compare (νόμος 1.1 e), “SIG” 700.29 (1st c.AD(?): Macedonius Epigrammaticus, 2nd c.BC).]]

Abbott-Smith / STEPBible (TBESG)
νομίζω
(νόμος), [in LXX: Wis.13:2 17:3, Sir.29:4, 1-28; 2Ma.4:1-50, 4Ma.8:1-29 * ;]
__1. to practise, hold by custom: Act.16:13 (Rec., but see infr.).
__2. to deem, consider, suppose: Mat.5:17 10:34 20:10, Luk.2:44 3:23, Act.7:25 8:20 14:19 16:13, 27 17:29 21:29, 1Co.7:26 7:36, 1Ti.6:5.†
SYN.: ἡγέομαι, q.v  (AS)

LSJ / STEPBible (TFLSJ)
νομ-ίζω,
future νομιῶ [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Aves” 571, 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 4.87, etc.]]; Ionic dialect 1st pers. plural νομιοῦμεν [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 2.17; later νομίσω 3rd c.AD(?): Longus Scriptor Eroticus 1.1 codices, 5th-6th c.AD: Procopius Gazaeus Rhetor “Epistulae - Epistolographi” 12:]]aorist ἐνόμισα, poetry νόμισα [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “I.” 5(4).2]]: perfect νενόμικα [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Axionicus Comicus 6.8]]:—passive, future νομισθήσομαι [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Sophista” 240e, etc.:]]future middle νομιοῦμαι in passive sense, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Hippocrates Medicus “περὶ ἱερῆς νούσου” 1]]: aorist ἐνομίσθην (see. below [Refs [1.1, 2)]]: perfect νενόμισμαι, 3rd.pers. plural νενομίδαται [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd-3rd c.AD: Dio Cassius Historicus 51.23]]; Doric dialect infinitive -ίχθαι[Refs 5th c.AD+ [Sthenidas Philosophus cited in 5th c.AD: Stobaeus, Joannes 4.7.63]]: pluperfect 3rd.pers. singular ἐνενόμιστο [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Nubes” 962]]: (νόμος):—use customarily, practise, ἓν τόδε ἴδιον νενομίκασι [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.173]]; ν. γλῶσσαν to have a language in common use,[Refs [[prev. work] 142; φωνήν [prev. author] 2.42; οὔτε ἀσπίδα οὔτε δόρυ [prev. author] 5.97]]; πανήγυριν, πληγὴν ἐν τῇ ὁρτῇ, [Refs [[prev. author] 2.63]]; ταῦτα.. Ἕλληνες ἀπ᾽ Αἰγυπτίων νενομίκασι have adopted these customs from the Egyptians, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. work] 51, compare 4.27; ἱπποτροφίας ἐν Πανελλάνων νόμῳ 5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “I.” 2.38; ἀργυροστερῆ βίον 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Choephori” 1003(989); ν. θειότατον νόμον 5th c.BC: Gorgias Rhetor et Sophista “fragment” 6D.]]; ν. ἐκκλησίαν have a regular popular assembly, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Politica” 1275b7]]; ἀγορᾶς κατασκευὴν ν. (conjecture for ὀνομάζουσιν)[Refs 2nd c.BC+ [[prev. work] 1331a32; δραχμὰς ἇν Τροζάνιοι νομίζοντι “IG” 42(1).77.16 (Epid., 2nd c.BC)]]:—frequently in passive, to be customary, οὔτω τοῦτο νομίσδεται [Refs 7th c.BC+ [7th-6th c.BC: Alcaeus Lyricus “Supp.” 24; ὅπου τὸ χαίρειν μηδαμοῦ νομίζεται 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Eumenides” 423; σωφροσύνη 'νενόμιστο]]was the fashion, [Refs 6th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Nubes” 962: _impersonal_, εἰκῇ νομίζεται 6th c.BC: Xenophanes Poeta Philosophus 2.13]]; ὡς νομίζεται as is the custom, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Eumenides” 32, 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Alcestis” 99 (Lyric poetry), etc.; οἷάπερ ν. 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Agamemnon” 1046; οἷα τοῖς κάτω νομίζεται 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Electra” 327, compare 691; ᾗ νομίζεται [prev. author] “OC” 1603:]]participle νομιζόμενος customary, γέρα τὰ ν. [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 1.25; εὐχαὶ αἱ ν. [prev. author] 6.32; εἰς τὸν ν. χρόνον “IG” 12.19.15; τὰ ν.]]customs, usages, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.35, 5.42, 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Plutus” 1185; τὰ ν. μυστήρια 1st c.AD(?): Heraclitus 14; τὰ ἱερὰ τὰ ν. 5th c.BC: Antipho Orator 5.82; συντελέσαι τὰ ν. τοῖς θεοῖς “IG” 12.22.4, compare 54.16; τὰ τοῖς θεοῖς ν. 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 4.5.14]]; frequently of funeral rites, τὰ ν. ποιεῖν [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aeschines Orator 1.13, compare 5th-6th c.BC: Isocrates Orator 19.33; ἐπειδὴ τὰ ν. αὐτῷ φέροιτο 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 18.243]]: also aorist participle, τό τοι νομισθὲν τῆς ἀληθείας κρατεῖ [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Fragmenta” 86; τὰ ν. 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Bacchae” 71 (Lyric poetry)]]: perfect participle, τὰ νενομισμένα τοῖς κατοιχομένοις [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [“PRyl.” 153.6 (2nd c.AD),compare “SIG” 1109.34 (2nd c.AD).]]

__2
of a legislator, enact, ἐνόμισεν ἑνὶ ἱματίῳ δι᾽ ἔτους προσεθίζεσθαι [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Respublica Lacedaemoniorum” 2.4, compare 12.3, “Cyr.” 8.5.3: with _accusative_, [prev. author] “Lac.” 1.7]]:—passive, [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd-3rd c.AD: Dio Cassius Historicus 37.20; τὰ νομισθέντα ὑπὸ Μάρκου [prev. author] 78.22; compare νομιστέος 1.]]

__3
with dative, make common use of, use, φωνῇ [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 4.117; ὑσί [prev. work] 63]]; νομίζουσι Αἰγύπτιοι οὐδ᾽ ἥρωσι οὐδέν, i.e. practise no such worship, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. author] 2.50; ἀγῶσι καὶ θυσίαις 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 2.38; εὐσεβείᾳ [prev. author] 3.82; οὔτε τούτοις χρῆται οὔθ᾽ οἷς ἡ ἄλλη Ἑλλὰς ν. [prev. author] 1.77]]; especially use as current coin, ἐν Βυζαντίοις, ὅπου σιδαρέοισι νομίσμασιν νομίζουσι [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Comicus 96 (uncertain reading); ἐν Λακεδαίμονι σιδηρῷ σταθμῷ νομίζουσι 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Eryxias” 400b]]:—hence in passive, to be struck, ἀργύριον νενομισμένον ἐς Τιβέριον, i.e. with the head of Tiberius, [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd-3rd c.AD: Philostratus Sophista “Vita Apollonii” 1.15.]]

__4
with infinitive, to be accustomed to do, νομίζουσι Διὶ θυσίας ἔρδειν [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.131, compare 133, 202, 3.15]], etc.:— passive, νενόμισται τὰ σχέτλια ἔργα Λήμνια καλέεσθαι [Refs [[prev. author] 6.138]]; γυμνοὺς εἰσιέναι νομίζεται it is customary for them.., [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Nubes” 498, compare 1420, 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 2.15, 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Historia Graeca (Hellenica)” 2.4.36.]]

__II
own, acknowledge, consider as, ὡς δούλους ν. τινάς [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 2.1; τὸν προέχοντα ἔτεσι ν. ὡς πατέρα 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Leges” 879c: ὡς]] is frequently omitted, ὄμμα γὰρ δόμων νομίζω δεσπότου παρουσίαν [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Persae” 169; τοὺς κακοὺς χρηστοὺς ν. 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Tyrannus” 610, compare “Ant.” 183, “El.” 1317; τοὺς αὐτοὺς φίλους νομιῶ καὶ ἐχθρούς “IG” 12.71.20; νομίσαι χρὴ ταῦτα μυστήρια 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Nubes” 143]]; θεὸν ν. τινά believe in one as a god, σὺ Ἔρωτα οὐ θεὸν νομίζεις [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Symposium” 202d; θεὰν οὐ τὴν Ἀναίδειαν, ἀλλὰ τὴν Αἰδῶ ν. 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Symposium” 8.35]]; ν. τούτους [θεούς] believe in these [as gods], [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 4.59; οὓς ἡ πόλις ν. θεοὺς οὐ νομίζων 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Memorabilia” 1.1.1, “Ap.” 10, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Apologia” 24b; τοὺς ἀρχαίους οὐ ν. [prev. author] “Euthphr.” 3b]]; but ν. θεοὺς εἶναι believe that there are gods, [Refs [[prev. author] “Ap.” 26c, “Lg.” 886a (compare below 4): without εἶναι, δίκην καὶ θεοὺς μόνον ν. [ἄνθρωπος] [prev. author] “Mx.” 237d]]; τὸ παράπαν θεοὺς οὐδαμῶς ν. to be an atheist, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [[prev. author] “Lg.” 885c, compare 908c, “Ap.” 18c, “Prt.” 322a; θεοὺς ν. οὐδαμοῦ 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Persae” 497]]:—passive, to be deemed, reputed, considered, οἷς τὸ πέλειν τε καὶ οὐκ εἶναι ταὐτὸν νενόμισται [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Parmenides Poeta Philosophus 6.8; Ἕλληνες ἤρξαντο νομισθῆναι 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 2.51]]; οἱ νομιζόμενοι μὲν υἱεῖς, μὴ ὄντες δέ.. [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 40.47]]; ἡ -ομένη (variant{ὀνομαζ-}) πολιτεία [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Politica” 1293b22.]]

__II.2
esteem, hold in honour, χρυσὸν.. περιώσιον ἄλλων [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “I.” 5(4).2; οὔτε θεοὺς οὔτε ἀνθρώπους ν. 5th c.BC: Lysias Orator 12.9]]:—passive, to be esteemed, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Gorgias” 466b.]]

__II.3
with accusative of things, hold, believe, ταὐτὰ περί τινος [Refs [[prev. author] “Phdr.” 258c, etc.; ἐποίει ἄλλα παρ᾽ ἃ ἐνόμισεν [prev. author] “Min.” 320b]]; ἀκοῇ ν., opposed to πείρᾳ αἰσθάνεσθαι, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 4.81.]]

__II.4
with accusative et infinitive, deem, hold, believe that.., πότερα νομίζεις δυστυχεῖν ἐμ; [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Coloneus” 800, compare “OT” 549, 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Historia Graeca (Hellenica)” 3.4.11; θεὸν νομίζουσι εἶναι τὸ πῦρ 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 3.16]]: with future infinitive, expect that.., [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Tyrannus” 551]]: aorist infinitive is sometimes found in codices referring to future, ἐνόμισαν ἐπιθέμενοι ῥᾳδίως κρατῆσαι [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 2.3 (κρατήσειν in same phrase, 4th c.BC: Aeneas Tacticus 2.3), compare 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 3.24, 5th c.BC: Lysias Orator 13.6; in 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Ajax” 1082 the]]aorist infinitive may be gnomic.

__II.5
with participle, νομίσωμεν ἐκγενησόμενον [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 7.68; νόμιζε.. ἄνδρα ἀγαθὸν ἀποκτείνων 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 6.6.24; νόμιζε ταῦτα δεδογμένα 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 450a, compare 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 14.9 (assuming variant).]]

__II.6
with ὡς, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 3.88.]]

__II.7
passive, with genitive of the person in possession, τοῦ θεῶν νομίζετα; whose sanctuary is it held to be? [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Coloneus” 38]]; οὐ τοῦ κρατοῦντος ἡ πόλις ν.; [Refs [[prev. author] “Ant.” 738.]]

__II.8
absolutely, νομίζοντα λέγειν to speak with full belief, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Phaedrus” 257d (nisi to be read ὀνειδίζοντα).]]

__II.9
frequent, μυχὸν ν. [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Choephori” 801 (Lyric poetry, uncertain reading).]]

Abbott-Smith / STEPBible (TBESG)
νομικός, -ή, -όν
(νόμος), [in LXX: 4Ma.5:4 * ;]
__1. relating to law: μάχαι, Tit.3:9.
__2. learned in the law; as subst., ὁ ν. (EV, lawyer): Mat.22:35, Luk.10:25, Tit.3:13; pl., Luk.7:30 11:45-46, 52 14:3 (cf. MM, xvii).†
SYN.: γραμματεύς, q.v  (AS)

---

LSJ / STEPBible (TFLSJ)
νομ-ικός, ή, όν,
relating to laws, αἴτια, title of work by Democritus; resting on law, ἤθη [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Leges” 625a]]; conventional, ν. δίκαιον, opposed to φυσικόν, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Ethica Nicomachea” 1134b20; ν. φιλία, opposed to ἠθική, [prev. work] 1162b23.]] adverb -κῶς after the manner of law, i.e. in a broad, general way, [Refs [[prev. author] “Pol.” 1341b31.]]

__2
forensic, μάχαι [NT.Tit.3.9]; ἀγῶνες, opposed to λογικοί, ἠθικοί, [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd-3rd c.AD: Philostratus Sophista “Vitae Sophistarum” 1.22.1]]; relating to points of law (opposed to matters of fact), στάσις, ζήτημα, [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd c.AD: Hermogenes Rhetor “περὶ τῶν στάσεων” 2, 3]]; ν. ὀνόματα law-terms, [Refs [[prev. author] “Meth.” 2; τὰ ν.]]law matters, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [1st c.BC: Philodemus Gadarensis Epigrammaticus “Rh.” 1.37 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus, 1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus “Cicero” 26]]. adverb -κῶς by legal process, [Refs [[prev. author] 2.533b.]]

__II
learned in the law, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [2nd c.AD: Alexander Rhetor 39, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Minos” 317e (_superlative_)]]; doctor of the Jewish law, [NT.Matt.22.35, +others]

__II.2

deep_entry:

νόμος, -ου, ὁ
(νέμω, to deal out, distribute), [in LXX chiefly for תּוֹרָה, also for חֻקָּה, etc. ;]
that which is assigned, hence, usage, custom, then law; in NT (only in Mt, Jo, Ja, and the Lucan and Pauline bks.);
__1. of law in general: Rom.3:27 5:13b; pl., of divine laws, Heb.8:10 10:16; ὁ ν. τ. Χριστοῦ, Gal.6:2; (τ.) ἐλευθερίας, Jas.1:25 2:12; βασιλικιός (Hort., in l.; Deiss., LAE, 267:3), Jas.2:8.
__2. Of a force or influence impelling to action: Rom.7:21, 23a, 25 8:2.
__3. Of the Mosaic law: Mat.5:18, Luk.2:27, Jhn.1:17, Act.6:13, Rom.2:15, 1Co.9:8, 1Ti.1:8, Heb.7:19; al.; Μωυσέως, Luk.2:22, Jhn.7:23, Act.15:5, al.; κυρίου, Luk.2:39; κατὰ τὸν ν., Act.22:12, Heb.7:5 9:22.
__4. As printed, Abbott-Smith mistakenly numbers this as 3.Anarthrous (Bl, §46, 8; ICC on Rom.2:12, 13), νόμος,
__(a) of law in general: Rom.2:12, 14b 3:20, 21 4:15, al.;
__(b) of the Mosaic law in its quality as law: Rom.2:14a 5:20 10:4, Gal.2:19, al.; οἱ ἐκ ν., Rom.4:14; ὑπὸ νόμον, 1Co.9:20, Gal.4:5; ν. πράσσειν (πληροῦν), Rom.2:25 13:8.
__5. Of Christian teaching: ν. πίστεως, Rom.3:27; τ. Χριστοῦ, Gal.6:2.
__6. By meton., of the  books which contain the law;
__(a) of the Pentateuch: Mat.12:5, Jhn.1:45, al.; ὁ ν. καὶ οἱ προφῆται, Mat.5:17, Luk.16:16, al.; ὁ ν. καὶ προφῆται κ. ψαλμοί, Luk.24:44.
__(b) of the OT Scriptures in general (as Heb. תּוֹרָה): Jhn.10:34 12:34 15:25, 1Co.14:21, al.
(AS)

---

νόμος, ὁ,
(νέμω) that which is in habitual practice, use or possession, not in [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Homerus Epicus (compare 1st c.AD: Josephus Historicus “contra Apionem” 2.15), though read by 4th-3rd c.BC: Zenodotus Grammaticus in 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 1.3.]]

__I
usage, custom, [Μοῦσαι] μέλπονται πάντων τε νόμους καὶ ἤθεα κεδνά [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th-7th c.BC: Hesiodus Epicus “Theogonia” 66; ν. ἀρχαῖος ἄριστος [prev. author] “fragment” 221]]; ἔνθα ν. (i.e. ἐστί) with infinitive, where it is the custom.., [Refs 7th c.BC+ [7th-6th c.BC: Alcaeus Lyricus “Supp.” 25.5]]; ν. πάντων βασιλεύς custom is lord of all, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “Fragmenta.” 169.1; ν. δεσπότης 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 7.104, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Leges” 715d; ν. τύραννος τῶν ἀνθρώπων [prev. author] “Prt.” 337d; ἴησις ὀθονίοισι κατὰ τὸν ν. τὸν ἀρθριτικόν 5th c.BC: Hippocrates Medicus “περὶ ἄρθρων ἐμβολῆς” 18; ὡς νόμος [prev. author] “Mochl.” 37]]: hence, law, ordinance, τόνδε.. ν. διέταξε Κρονίων.. θηρσὶ.. ἐσθέμεν ἀλλήλους [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th-7th c.BC: Hesiodus Epicus “Opera et Dies” 276; τρέφονται πάντες οἱ ἀνθρώπειοι ν. ὑπὸ τοῦ θείου 1st c.AD(?): Heraclitus 114; ἄφθογγον εἶναι τὸν παλαμναῖον ν. [ἐστί] 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Eumenides” 448; ν. κάλλιστον ἐξευρόντα, πειθαρχεῖν πατρί 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Trachiniae” 1177]]; ν. κοινός, ={ὀρθὸς λόγος}, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th-3rd c.BC: Zeno Citieus Stoicus 1.43: _plural_, ἔργων.. ὧν νόμοι πρόκεινται ὑψίποδες 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Tyrannus” 865 (Lyric poetry); νεοχμοῖς ν. Ζεὺς κρατύνει 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Prometheus Vinctus” 150 (Lyric poetry).]]

__I.b
in VT, of the law of God, ἐν τῷ νόμῳ Κυρίου τὸ θέλημα αὐτοῦ [LXX.Psa.1.2, +others, cf. LXX.Isa.2.3]; νόμον ὃν ἐνετείλατο ὑμῖν Μωϋσῆς[LXX.Deu.33.4]; so in NT, ὁ ν. Μωϋσέως [NT.Luke.2.22, etc.; but also ὁ ν. τοῦ Χριστοῦ NT.Gal.6.2]; ὁ ν. τοῦ Πνεύματος τῆς ζωῆς, opposed to ὁ ν. τῆς ἁμαρτίας καὶ τοῦ θανάτου, [NT.Rom.8.2; ν. τέλειος ὁ τῆς ἐλευθερίας NT.Jam.1.25.]

__I.c
with Preps., κατὰ νόμον according to custom or law, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th-7th c.BC: Hesiodus Epicus “Theogonia” 417, 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.61, etc.; κὰν νόμον 5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “O.” 8.78]]; οἱ κατὰ ν. ὄντες θεοί the established deities, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Leges” 904a; κατὰ νόμους 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Supplices” 241]]; παρὰ νόμον contrary to.., [Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. author] “Eu.” 171 (Lyric poetry); παρὰ τοὺς τῆς φύσεως ν. 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Timaeus” 83e; ἐν Πανελλάνων νόμῳ 5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “I.” 2.38]]; ἐν Ἀδραστείῳ νόμῳ by the law of Adrastus, i.e. at the Nemean games, [Refs [[prev. author] “N.” 10.28: especially in _dative_ νόμῳ]] by custom, conventionally, opposed to φύσει, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 4.39, 5th-6th c.BC: Philolaus Philosophus 9, 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Ethica Nicomachea” 1094b16, etc.]]; ν. γλυκύ, ν. πικρόν, [Refs 3rd c.AD+ [3rd c.AD: Democritus Epigrammaticus 9; εἰ μή τις λέγοι ν. ὁρᾶν καὶ τὰς λεγομένας ποιότητας μὴ ἐν τοῖς ὑποκειμένοις εἶναι 3rd c.AD: Plotinus Philosophus 4.4.29]]; ὅσον νόμου χάριν just for form's sake, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-3rd c.BC: Diphilus Comicus 43.14, 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Metaphysica” 1076a27.]]

__I.d
statute, ordinance made by authority, [Σόλων] νόμους ἔθηκεν ἄλλους, τοῖς δὲ Δράκοντος θεσμοῖς ἐπαύσαντο χρώμενοι πλὴν τῶν φονικῶν [Refs [[prev. author] “Ath.” 7.1 (but τὸν Δράκοντος ν. τὸν περὶ τοῦ φόνου “IG” 12.115.5), etc.]]; νόμον τιθέναι, τίθεσθαι, see at {τίθημ; βασιλικὸς ν}. [NT+2nd c.AD+ [“OGI” 483.1 (Pergam., 2nd c.AD), NT.Jam.2.8]]: frequently of general laws, opposed to ψηφίσματα (special decrees), [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Theaetetus” 173d, etc.; ὅταν τὰ ψηφίσματα κύρια ᾖ ἀλλὰ μὴ ὁ ν. 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Politica” 1292a7]]: generally, law, ἄνευ ὀρέξεως νοῦς ὁ ν. ἐστίν [Refs [[prev. work] 1287a32]]; ἄγραφος ν. Legal cited in [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Andocides Orator 1.85, etc.]]; opposed to γεγραμμένος, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Rhetorica” 1373b6; ν. ἴδιος, opposed to κοινός, [prev. work] 4]]; ὁ ν. frequently as subject, οἱ ν. διδόασι τιμωρίας [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 18.12; ὧν ὁ ν. ἀγορεύει “Inscription Magn.” 92b16 (2nd c.BC)]]; μὴ ὁ ν. κρίνει τὸν ἄνθρωπον ἐὰν μὴ ἀκούσῃ πρῶτο; [NT.John.7.51.]

__I.e

__I.3
with accusative, forsake, abandon, παῖδά τ᾽ ἐμὴν νοσφισσαμένην θάλαμόν τε πόσιν τε [Refs 8th c.BC+ [4.263; elsewhere in 8th c.BC: Homerus Epicus of places, Κρήτης ὄρεα νιφόεντα νοσφισάμην [prev. work] 19.339; νοσφισσαμένη τόδε δῶμα [prev. work] 579, 21.77, 104]]; νοσφισθεῖσα θεῶν ἀγορήν [Refs 7th c.BC+ [“hymnus ad Cererem” 92; ὅρκον ἐνοσφίσθης 7th c.BC: Archilochus Lyricus 96]]; εἴ σε νοσφίζομαι if I forsake thee, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Tyrannus” 693 (Lyric poetry).]]

__II
after [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Homerus Epicus (ἀπονοσφίσσειεν first in “hymnus ad Cererem” 158)]] in active, set apart, separate, remove, τινὰ ἐκ δόμων [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Helena” 641 (Lyric poetry); βρέφος ματέρος ἀποπρό [prev. author] “IA” 1286 (Lyric poetry); τινὰ ἀπό τινος 3rd c.BC: Lycophron Tragicus 1331]]; τινα [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [3rd c.BC: Apollonius Rhodius Epicus 2.793: _metaphorically_, ν. τινὰ βίου]] separate him from life, i. e. kill him, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Philoctetes” 1427]]; τῷ νύ μ᾽.. ἐκ βιότοιο νοσφίσατ᾽ (imperative) ἐσσυμένως [Refs 4th c.AD+ [4th c.AD(?): Quintus Smyrnaeus Epicus 13.282]]; ν. τινά alone, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Choephori” 438 (Lyric poetry), “Eu.” 211; ν. τινὰ ἐρωμανίης “Anthologia Graeca” 5.292 (Paul. Sil.).]]

νότος, -ου, ὁ
[in LXX chiefly for נֶגֶב, also for דָּרוֹם, תֵּימָן and קָדִים ;]
__1. prop., the south wind: Luk.12:55, Act.27:13 28:13
__2. South: Luk.13:29, Rev.21:13
__3. the South, as a region (cf. נֶגֶב): Mat.12:42, Luk.11:31.†
(AS)

---

LSJ / STEPBible (TFLSJ)
νότος, ὁ,
south wind (opposed to Βορέας, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Meteorologica” 363b15, compare 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 5.331), εὖτ᾽ ὄρεος κορυφῇσι Ν. κατέχευεν ὀμίχλην 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 3.10; ὅ τε ν. καὶ ὁ λίψ, ἀνέμων ὑετιώτατοι 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 2.25 (but ὁ ν. οὐκ ἀρχόμενος ἀλλὰ λήγων ὑέτιος 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Problemata” 942a29); ἐτέγχθη κρᾶτ᾽.. πληγῇσι νότου 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Philoctetes” 1457 (_anapaest meter_); χειμερίῳ νότῳ [prev. author] “Ant.” 335 (Lyric poetry); ὑγρὸς καὶ βαρύς 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Historia Animalium” 597b11; ὑδατωδέστερος [prev. author] “Pr.” 943a5]]; ὅταν μὲν ἐλάττων ᾖ, αἴθριός ἐστιν, ὅταν δὲ μέγας, νεφώδης[Refs [[prev. work] 942a34; καυματώδης [prev. author] “Mete.” 364b23: in _plural_, [prev. author] “HA” 612b6.]]

__2
N. personified as god of the South wind, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th-7th c.BC: Hesiodus Epicus “Theogonia” 380, 870.]]

__II
south or south-west quarter, πρὸς μεσαμβρίης τε καὶ νότου [NT+5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 2.8; πρὸς νότον κεῖται τῆς Λήμνου [prev. author] 6.139; τῆς δὲ γῆς τὸ πρὸς ν. 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Fragmenta” 24.6; τὸ πρὸς ν. τῆς πόλεως 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 3.6; βλέπειν πρὸς ν. “IG” 22.1227.18; ὁ τοῖχος ὁ πρὸς ν. [prev. work]12.372.51; πρὸς νότου ἀνέμου [prev. work]56; βασίλισσα νότου NT.Matt.12.42]]; ἀπὸ νότου with genitive, to the south of, [Refs 2nd c.BC+ [“PTeb.” 164.17 (2nd c.BC)]], etc.; later ἐκ νότου with genitive, [Refs 3rd c.AD+ [“PStrassb.” 29.8 (3rd c.AD)]], etc.: genitive νότου to the south, [Refs 2nd c.BC+ [PTeb. 105.13 (2nd c.BC), etc.]]

νουθετέω, -ῶ
(νοῦς, τίθημι, hence, put in mind), [in LXX: 1Ki.3:13 (כָּהָה pi.), Job.8:1-22 (יָסַר pi., בִּין), Wis.11:10 12:2, 26 * ;]
to admonish, exhort: with accusative of person(s), Act.20:31, Rom.15:14, 1Co.4:14, Col.1:28 3:16, 1Th.5:12 5:14, 2Th.3:15.†
(AS)

---

LSJ / STEPBible (TFLSJ)
νουθετ-έω,
(τίθημι) put in mind: hence, admonish, warn, re- buke, with accusative person, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 2.173; παραινεῖν ν. τε τὸν κακῶς πράσσοντα 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Prometheus Vinctus” 266; οὐδὲ νουθετεῖν ἔξεστί σε 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Electra” 595]]; κᾆτα νουθετεῖς ἐμέ [Refs [[prev. author] “Ph.” ; Ἔρωτα “Lyrica Alexandrina Adespota” 8]] (a): with accusative of things, ν. τάδε [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Electra” 1025, compare 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Vespae” 732 (Lyric poetry)]]; advise concerning, μηχανήματα [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Hercules Furens” 855 (troch.): with double _accusative_, τοιαῦτ᾽ ἄνολβον ἄνδρ᾽ ἐνουθέτει 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Ajax” 1156; ἅπερ με νουθετεῖς 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Supplices” 337, compare “Or.” 299; ν. τινὰ ὡς.. 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 8.2.15]]:—passive, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Coloneus” 1193, 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Medea” 29, etc.; πρὶν ὑπὸ σοῦ ταῦτα νουθετηθῆναι 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Hp.Ma.” 301c.]]

__2
metaphorically, chastise, ν. τινὰ κονδύλοις, πληγαῖς, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Vespae” 254, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Leges” 879d:]] —passive, coupled with κολάζεσθαι, [Refs [[prev. author] “Grg.” 478e.]]

deep_entry:
Abbott-Smith / STEPBible (TBESG)
νεομηνία (Att.. contr., νουμ-, Rec.), -ας, ἡ
(νέος, μήν), [in LXX chiefly for חֹדֶשׁ ;]
new moon: of the Jewish festival, Col.2:16.†
(AS)

---

LSJ / STEPBible (TFLSJ)
νουμην-ία, ἡ,
Attic dialect contraction for νεομηνία (which occurs in [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “N.” 4.35, 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 6.57 (_plural_), “PMag.Leid.W.” 1.28,9.43 (_plural_), 2nd c.AD: Galenus Medicus 14.298)]]:—also νευμηνία, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [“SIG” 1106.19 (Cos, 4th-3rd c.BC)]]; νεμονηΐα, [Refs [“GDI” 5015.28, +others (from Crete)]]; νομενία, [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [“PCair.Zen.” 167.5 (3rd c.BC)]]:— new moon: the first of the month, Pi.[same place], [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Antipho Orator “fragment” 58 (_plural_), 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Equites” 43, “Ach.” 999 (_plural_)]], etc.; ν. κατὰ σελήνην to denote the true or natural new moon, as opposed to to the νουμηνία of the calendars, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 2.28; also ἡ κατὰ θεὸν ν. “PMag.Par.” 1.787, 2389]]; ν. τοῦ ἔτους, of the spring equinox, [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd c.AD: Ptolemaeus Mathematicus “Tetrabiblos” 91.]]
source_notes: STEPBible TBESG (CC BY), STEPBible TFLSJ (CC BY)

deep_entry:
Abbott-Smith / STEPBible (TBESG)
νοῦς
(contr. from νόος), ὁ, genitive, dative, νοός, νοΐ (late forms, = cl., νοῦ, νῷ; Bl., § 9, 3), accusative, νοῦν, [in LXX chiefly for לֵב, לֵבָב ;]
__1. prop., of the ruling faculty, mind, understanding, reason (see Lft., Notes, 88 f.; Vaughan on Rom.7:23): Luk.24:45, Rom.1:28 7:23 12:2 14:5, Eph.4:17, 23 Php.4:7, 2Th.2:2, 1Ti.6:5, 2Ti.3:8, Tit.1:15, Rev.13:18 17:9; ν. τ. σαρκός (ICC, in l), Col.2:18; opposite to σάρξ, Rom.7:25; to πνεῦμα, 1Co.14:14-15; to γλῶσσα, 1Co.14:19
__2. By meton., of an act of mind, a mind, thought, purpose: Rom.11:34 = 1Co.2:16" (LXX), 1Co.1:10.†
νόος, see: νοῦς
SYN.: see: πνεῦμα  (AS)

---

LSJ / STEPBible (TFLSJ)
νόος, νόου, ὁ,
Attic dialect contraction νοῦς, genitive νοῦ: [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Homerus Epicus]] uses the contraction form once, in nominative, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 10.240, compare 8th-7th c.BC: Hesiodus Epicus “Fragmenta” 205 (5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus never)]]: Trag. use contraction form, except in [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Choephori” 742 (iambic), 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Philoctetes” 1209 (Lyric poetry)]]: Aeolic dialect genitive νῶ [Refs 7th c.BC+ [7th-6th c.BC: Alcaeus Lyricus “Supp.” 9.1; _accusative_ νῶν Sapph.[prev. work]25.2; νόον Ead.70 (assuming variant)]]: irregular forms are found in “NT” and later writers, genitive νοός [LXX+NT+1st c.AD+ [NT.Rom.7.23, LXX.4Mac.1.35; _dative_ νοΐ NT.1Cor.1.10, [2nd c.AD: Aristides Rhetor] “Or.” 35(9).26; _nominative_ _plural_ νόες 1st c.AD: Philo Judaeus 1.86, 3rd c.AD: Plotinus Philosophus 6.7.17, 5th-6th c.AD: Damascius Philosophus “de Principiis” 96; _accusative_ _plural_ νόας 1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus “Fragmenta - fragment uncertainFragmenta incerta” 7.27, 4th c.AD: Iamblichus Philosophus “de Mysteriis” 1.15, 5th c.AD: Ammonius Philosophus “in Aristotelis de Interpretatione commentarius - pars” 243.3 (variant), 5th-6th c.AD: Damascius Philosophus “de Principiis” 103: _Attic dialect_ _plural_ νοῖ, _accusative_ νοῦς, _genitive_ νόων [prev. work] 122, _dative_ νοῖς [prev. passage]]], is rare in early writers, as [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Fragmenta” 471, but frequently in later philosophy:]]

__1
mind, as employed in perceiving and thinking, sense, wit, οὐ λῆθε Διὸς πυκινὸν ν. [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 15.461; ν. πολυκερδέα 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 13.255; ν. ὁρῇ καὶ ν. ἀκούει, τἄλλα κωφὰ καὶ τυφλά 5th c.BC: Epicharmus Comicus 249, compare 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Tyrannus” 371]]; νόῳ prudently, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 6.320]]; παρὲκ νόον senselessly, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 20.133]]; σὺν νόῳ wisely, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 8.86, 138]]; ξὺν νῷ with play on ξυνῷ, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [1st c.AD(?): Heraclitus 114 (νόῳ codices 5th c.AD: Stobaeus, Joannes); ξὺν νῷ ἑλομένῳ 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 619b; οὐδενὶ ξὺν νῷ [prev. author] “Cri.” 48c; μηδενὶ ξὺν νῷ 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Nubes” 580; τοῦ νοῦ χωρίς 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Tyrannus” 550; τοῦ ν. κενός [prev. author] “OC” 931]]; νόῳ λαβεῖν τι to apprehend it, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 3.51]]; νόῳ σχεῖν, ἔχειν, recall, remember, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. author] 5.92.ή, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 490a; κοινὸς ν. 1st c.BC: Philodemus Gadarensis Epigrammaticus “Rh.” 1.37 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus, 2nd c.AD: Arrianus Historicus “Epicteti Dissertationes” 3.6.8]]; ἀγαθὸς ν., σπουδαῖος ν., [Refs 5th c.BC+ [1st c.BC: Philodemus Gadarensis Epigrammaticus “Rh.” 2.61, 1.252 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus]]

__2
νοῦν ἔχειν in two senses,

__2.a
to have sense, be sensible, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Trachiniae” 553, “El.” 1013, 1465, 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Ranae” 535, etc.; ὁ νοῦς ὅδ᾽ αὐτὸς ν. ἔχων οὐ τυγχάνει 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Iphigenia Aulidensis” 1139]]; so ν. ὀλίγον κεκτημένος [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Ecclesiazusae” 747; σμικρὸν νοῦ κεκτῆσθαι 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Leges” 887e; _impersonal_, τὸ γὰρ περισσὰ πράσσειν οὐκ ἔχει ν. οὐδένα 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Antigone” 68, compare 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Timaeus” 68b]]; compare νουνεχόντως.

__2.b
νοῦν or τὸν ν. ἔχειν to have one's mind directed to something, ἄλλοσ᾽ ὄμμα, θητέρᾳ δὲ ν. ἔχειν [Refs 7th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Trachiniae” 272, compare 7th-6th c.BC: Sappho Lyrica “Papyrus fragments” in E. Diehl, 25.2; τὸν ν. πρὸς αὑτὸν οὐκ ἔχων, ἐκεῖσε δέ 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Phoenissae” 1418; δεῦρο ν. ἔχε [prev. author] “Or.” 1181; οἴκοι τὸν ν. ἔχειν [prev. author] “Ion” 251]]; ποῦ τὸν ν. ἔχει; [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Ecclesiazusae” 156]]; τὸν ν. ἔχειν πρός τινα or τι (like προσέχειν τὸν ν.) [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 7.19, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Gorgias” 504d; πρός τινι [prev. author] “Prt.” 324a, etc.; περί τινος [prev. author] “R.” 534b; ἐν πέρδιξιν “Anthologia Graeca” 7.206 (6th c.AD: Damocharis Epigrammaticus): conversely, ἐπὶ νοῦν ἐλθεῖν τινι]] to occur to one, [Refs 1st c.BC+ [1st c.BC: Dionysius Halicarnassensis 3.15, 2nd c.AD: Arrianus Historicus “Anabasis” 7.24.3.]]

__3
mind, more widely, as employed in feeling, deciding, etc., heart, χαῖρε νόῳ [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 8.78; κεῦθε νόῳ 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 1.363; [χόλος] οἰδάνει νόον 9.554; ἐνὶ στήθεσσιν ἀτάρβητος ν. ἐστί 3.63]]; ν. ἔμπεδος, ἀκήλητος, ἀπηνής,[Refs 8th c.BC+ [11.813, 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 10.329, 18.381]]; ν. εὐμενής, ἄγναμπτος, etc., [Refs 8th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “P.” 8.18, 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Prometheus Vinctus” 164 (Lyric poetry), etc.; πολλῶν ἀνθρώπων νόον ἔγνω 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 1.3]]; ἐκ παντὸς νόου with all his heart and soul, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 8.97]]; τῷ νῷ.. κἀπὸ τῆς γλώσσης in heart as well as tongue, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Coloneus” 936: frequently in phrase κατὰ νόον]] according to one's mind, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.117, 7.104; εἰ τάδ᾽ ἔχει κατὰ νοῦν κείνῳ 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Coloneus” 1768 (_anapaest meter_); πράξειας κατὰ ν. τὸν ἐμόν [prev. author] “fragment” 469 (_anapaest meter_); κατὰ ν. πράξας 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Equites” 549; χωρεῖ κατὰ ν. [prev. author] “Pax” 940, compare 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Euthyphro” 3e.]]

__4
mind, resolve, purpose, ἀγαθῷ νόῳ, i.e. kindly, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.60]]; τί σοι ἐν νόῳ ἐστὶ ποιέει; what do you intend to do? [Refs [[prev. work] 109]]; ἡμῖν ἐν ν. ἐγένετο εἰπεῖν [Refs [[prev. author] 9.46]]; ἐν ν. ἔχειν with future infinitive, to intend.., [Refs [[prev. author] 1.10 (variant)]]: with present infinitive,[Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. work] 27, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 344d]]; ποιέειν τι ἐπὶ νόον τινί to put into his mind to do.., [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.27]]; ἐπὶ νόον τρέπειν τινί.. [Refs [[prev. author] 3.21; ταύτῃ [ὁ] ν. ἔφερε [prev. author] 9.120.]]

__5
reason, intellect, νόου φρενί [Refs 6th c.BC+ [6th c.BC: Xenophanes Poeta Philosophus 25, compare 4th-5th c.BC: Parmenides Poeta Philosophus 16.2, etc.; θεῖος ν. 3rd c.AD: Democritus Epigrammaticus 112, compare [prev. author] cited in 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “de Anima” 404a28]]; opposed to δόξα, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Timaeus” 51d, compare 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “de Anima” 428a5.]]

__5.b
“Mind” as the active principle of the Universe, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Anaxagoras Philosophus 12, etc.; Θαλῆς νοῦν τοῦ κόσμου τὸν θεόν “Placita Philosophorum” 1.7.11; ἡ τοῦ κόσμου γένεσις ἐξ ἀνάγκης καὶ νοῦ συστάσεως 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Timaeus” 48a, compare “Sph.” 249a, “Phlb.” 30c, 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Metaphysica” 1072b20, “de An.” 430a17, 4th-3rd c.BC: Zeno Citieus Stoicus 1.28, 3rd c.AD: Plotinus Philosophus 5.1.4.]]

__II
act of mind, thought, ἡμῖν δ᾽ οὔ τις τοῦδε νόος καὶ μῆτις ἀμείνων [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 15.509; οὐ γάρ τις νόον ἄλλος ἀμείνονα τοῦδε νοήσει 9.104; οὐ γὰρ δὴ τοῦτον μὲν ἐβούλευσας νόον αὐτή 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 5.23.]]

__II.2
purpose, design, νόον τελεῖν τινι [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 23.149; σάφα οἶσθ᾽ οἷος ν. Ἀτρεΐωνος 2.192.]]

__III
sense, meaning of a word, etc., οὗτος ὁ νόος τοῦ ῥήματος [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 7.162, compare 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Ranae” 1439, 2nd c.BC: Polybius Historicus 5.83.4, 1st c.BC: Philodemus Gadarensis Epigrammaticus “Rh.” 1.106 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus, etc.]]; ὁ νόος τῆς θυσίης conjecture for νόμος in [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.216]]; meaning of a work of art, [Refs 1st c.AD+ [2nd-3rd c.AD: Philostratus Sophista “Vita Apollonii” 4.28; πολὺς ν. ἐν ὀλίγῃ λέξει συνέσταλται 1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus 2.510e]]; πρὸς τὸν αὐτὸν νοῦν to the same effect, [Refs 1st c.BC+ [1st c.BC-1st c.AD: Strabo Geographus 15.3.7]]; πρὸς νοῦν οὐδὲν λέγοντες to the point, [Refs 1st c.BC+ [1st c.BC: Philodemus Gadarensis Epigrammaticus “Mus.” p.96K.; οὐδὲ νοῦν ἔχον]]senseless, [Refs [[prev. author] “Po.” 5.29.]]

__IV
[Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Pythagoras Philosophus name for μονάς, “Theologumena Arithmeticae” 6. (Etym. uncertain; the _proper name_ Πολυνόϝα “IG” 9(1).870 hardly proves νόϝος.)]]

short_definition: Nympha — Νυμφᾶς, -ᾶ, ὁ (WH, R, mg., Νύμφα, which see),
deep_entry:
Abbott-Smith / STEPBible (TBESG)
