[ἄνθρωποι] men of the present day, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.68; οἵ γε ν. 5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “O.” 1.105, 5th c.BC: Bacchylides Lyricus 5.4, compare 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Metaphysica” 1069a26]]; ὁ ν. τρόπος, τὸ ν. βαρβαρικόν, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 1.6]]; Βοιωτοὶ οἱ ν.[Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. work] 12; ὁ ν. παρὼν χρόνος 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Trachiniae” 174, +others, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Parmenides” 141e; ἡμέρα ἡ ν. 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Tyrannus” 351; νὺξ ἡ ν. [prev. author] “Ant.” 16; ἡ ν. ὁδός [prev. author] “El.” 1295; τὸ ν.]]the present, [LXX+5th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Physica” 218a6, +others; ἀπὸ τοῦ ν. 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Parmenides” 152c, LXX.Gen.46.30, etc.; ἀπὸ ν. “Anthologia Graeca” 5.40 (2nd-3rd c.AD: Rufinus Epigrammaticus); ἕως τοῦ ν. LXX.Gen.46.34]]; μέχρι ν. (variant{μ. τοῦ ν}.) [Refs 1st c.BC+ [1st c.BC: Diodorus Siculus Historicus 17.110]]; τὰ νῦν simply, ={ν}., [NT+5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 7.104, 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Heraclidae” 641, etc.; τό περ ν. 5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “N.” 7.101; τὰ δὲ ν. 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Coloneus” 133 (Lyric poetry); τὸ ν. εἶναι 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 506e, 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 5.3.42, 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Ἀθηναίων Πολιτεία” 31.2; τὸ ν. ἔχον NT.Act.24.25.]]

__2
of the immediate past, just now, but now, ν. Μενέλαος ἐνίκησεν [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 3.439, compare 13.772, 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 1.43, 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Coloneus” 84, 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 4.5.48; ν. γοῦν ἐπεχείρησας 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 341c; ἡλίκα ν. ἐτραγῴδει 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 18.13.]]

__3
of the future, presently, ν. αὖτ᾽ ἐγχείῃ πειρήσομαι [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 5.279, compare 20.307, 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 1.200; ν. φεύξομαι, τόθ᾽ ἁγνὸς ὤν 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Electra” 975]]; compare νῦν δή, νυνί.

__4
sometimes opposed to to what might have been under other circumstances, as it is (or was), as the case stands (or stood), as a matter offact, ν. δ᾽ ὁ μὲν ὣς ἀπόλωλε [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 1.166; εἰ μὲν ὑπώπτευον, οὐκ ἂν.. ἐποιούμην· ν. δὲ κτλ. 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 4.126, compare 1.122, 3.113, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Cratylus” 384b, 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 18.195, etc.]]; καὶ ν. even so, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 7.4.24, 7.7.17.]]

__5
coupled with other Particles, τὰ ν. γε [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Philoctetes” 245, etc.; ν. γε μάν 5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “P.” 1.50]]; ν. δή, see entry : with other expressions of Time, ν... σήμερον, ν. ἡμέρη ἥδε, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 7.29, 13.828]]; ν. ἤδη henceforth, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Antigone” 801]] (anapaest meter), etc.; ν... ἄρτι but now, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Cratylus” 396c.]]

__II
enclitic (but see below) νυν, νυ. [νυ only Epic dialect, Boeotian dialect, and [Refs 4th c.AD+ [5th c.AD: Cypria (also 4th c.AD(?): Arcadius Grammaticus in ὅνυ, which see)]]; νῠν twice in [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Homerus Epicus, 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 10.105, 23.485: ῡ?~X in Trag. (ῡ 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Septem contra Thebas” 242, 246, 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Antigone” 705, 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Orestes” 1678, etc.]]; ῠ [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Trachiniae” 92, 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Andromache” 91, etc.)]], ῡ in Comedy texts [Refs 5th c.BC+ [(5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Vespae” 1381, “Pl.” 975, +others), except 5th c.BC: Cratinus Comicus 144, 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Thesmophoriazusae” 105 (Lyric poetry, citing 5th c.BC: Agatho Tragicus), and perhaps “Nu.” 141]]; both quantities in τοίνυν, which see]

__II.1
rarely of Time, now, perhaps so used in [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 10.105, compare 4th-5th c.BC: Parmenides Poeta Philosophus 19.1, 5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “P.” 11.44, +others, 5th c.BC: Epicharmus Comicus 170.6.]]

__II.2
in Epic dialect mostly as a particle of emphasis, ἧκε δ᾽ ἐπ᾽ Ἀργείοισι κακὸν βέλος· οἱ δέ νυ λαοὶ θνῇσκον [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 1.382, etc.]]: frequently coupled with other Particles or Conjs., ἦ ῥά ν. [Refs [4.93; καί νύ κεν 3.373; οὔ ν., μή νύ τοι, 10.165, 1.28]]; ἐπεί νύ τοι[Refs [[prev. work] 416; ὥς νύ περ 2.258.]]

__II.3
in commands or entreaties, μή ν. μοι νεμεσήσετ᾽ [Refs [15.115: frequently with other _adverbs_, δεῦρό ν.]] come now ![Refs 5th c.BC+ [23.485; ἐνταῦθά ν. ὕβριζε 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Prometheus Vinctus” 82, compare 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Thesmophoriazusae” 1001, “V.” 149, “Pl.” 724; εἶά ν. [prev. author] “Pax” 467, “V.” 430, “Pl.” 316: frequently with _imperative_, φέρε ν. [prev. work] 789; ἄγε ν. [prev. author] “Pax” 1056, “V.” 381; σπεῦδέ ν. [prev. author] “Pl.” 414; σίγαν. 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Ajax” 87, Cratin. [prev. cited]; περίδου ν. 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Nubes” 644, compare 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 5.3.21, etc.; ὕφαινέ ν. 5th c.BC: Bacchylides Lyricus 18.8]]; so in Boeotian dialect, ν. ἔνθω [Refs 5th c.AD+ [“IG” 7.3172.88 (Orchom.); also in 5th c.AD: Cypria with _optative_ in commands, δυϝάνοι ν., δώκοι ν., “Inscription Cyprian dialect” 135.6,16 H. (from Idalion).]]

__II.4
in questions, τίς ν.; τί ν.; who, what, why now? [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 5.373, 1.414, 4.31]]; ἦ νυ..; [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 6.125. [In signf. I always _perispomenon_ In signf. II _perispomenon_ except when short, Hdn.Gr. 2.39, +others; _enclitic_ when short, sometimes in codices, as 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 23.485 (Papyrus in “AJP” 21.304, etc.]]; oxytone when ={δή}, Tyrannioap.Hdn.Gr.2.27; καθ᾽ ὁμαλισμόν or κατ᾽ ἔγκλισιν when=δή, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [Scholia 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Plutus” 414, Scholia 3rd c.BC: Apollonius Rhodius Epicus 1.664)]]. In codices usually perispomenon in both senses, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Prometheus Vinctus” 82, “Th.” 242, 246, 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Antigone” 705, “El.” 324, 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Plutus” 414, “V.” 758, 922, etc.]]; even νῠν is written νῦν in codices vett. [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus]] passim, also in [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Ajax” 87, “Tr.” 92, etc.]]; hence νυν may frequently be restored where the sense requires it. The accent of τοίνῡ?~Xν perhaps shows that both νῠν and νῡν could be enclitic.—Position: in signf. I νῦν can occupy any position; in signf. II it prefers (like other enclitics, but also like{ἄν, δέ, γάρ}, etc.) the second place in the sentence, e.g. πρός νύν σε πατρός [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Philoctetes” 468, compare “OC” 1333; ἀπό νύν με λείπετ᾽ ἤδη [prev. author] “Ph.” 1177 (Lyric poetry); μετά νυν δός 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Supplices” 56 (Lyric poetry)]]; νυ (always enclitic) precedes other enclitics and allows only δέ to precede.] (Cf. Sanskrit nú, n[umacracute], nūnám, O[Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus]] nū 'now', etc.)

[in LXX chiefly for לַיִל ;]

(of the time within which something  happens; M, Pr., 73; B1., § 36, 13), νυκτός, by night, Mat.2:14, Jhn.3:2, 1Th.5:7, al.; ν. κ. ἡμέρας, Mrk.5:5, 1Th.2:9, al.; ἡμέρας κ. ν., Luk.18:7, Rev.4:8, al.; μέσης ν., Mat.25:6; dative, νυκτί, in ans. to the question, "when?" LSJ / STEPBible (TFLSJ)
νύξ, νυκτός, ἡ,
night: either generally, mght-season (opposed to day), or a night, ν. ἀμβροσίη [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 24.363; ν. ἄμβροτος 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 11.330]]; but ν. ὀλοή[Refs 8th c.BC+ [[prev. work] 19, 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 16.567, compare below 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 3]], III; νυκτός by night, as adverb, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 13.278, etc.; οὔτε ν. οὔτ᾽ ἐξ ἡμέρας 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Electra” 780]]; νυκτὸς ἔτι while it was still night, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 9.10; also τῆς νυκτός 2nd c.AD: Alexander Rhetor 78.3, 148; ν. τῆσδε 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Ajax” 21]]; ἄκρας ν. at dead of night, [Refs [[prev. work] 285 (but ἄκρῃ νυκτί at]]night-fall, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-3rd c.BC: Aratus Epicus 775, ἀκρόθι νυκτός]] on the verge of dawn, [Refs [[prev. author] 308)]]; ἀωρὶ νυκτός, τῶν νυκτῶν, see at {ἀωρί}: in plural, τῶν νυκτῶν at nights, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Ecclesiazusae” 668: rarely, νυκτί 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 7.12; ν. τῇδε 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Electra” 644]]; νύκτα the night long, νύκτα φυλάσσειν to watch the night through, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 10.312, 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 5.466: _plural_, νύκτας ἰαύειν 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 9.325, 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 5.154, etc.; δύω νύκτας, τρεῖς ν., [prev. work] 388, 17.515]]: in Attic dialect, ὅλην τὴν ν. [Refs 8th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Pherecrates Comicus 177, 4th c.BC: Amphis Comicus 20.4; τὴν νύχθ᾽ ὅλην 4th c.BC: Eubulus Comicus 3; τὰς νύκτας 4th-3rd c.BC: Diphilus Comicus 32.14; ὅλας γε καὶ πάσας τὰς ν. 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Symposium” 4.54; νύκτας τε καὶ ἦμαρ 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 5.490; νύκτας τε καὶ ἡμέρας 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Theaetetus” 151a; οὔτε νύκτ᾽ οὔθ᾽ ἡμέραν 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Bacchae” 187; τὴν νύχθ᾽ ὅλην τήν θ᾽ ἡμέραν 4th c.BC: Eubulus Comicus 53.1]]; νύκτα ἡμέραν ποιούμενος ἀπόστειλον (κατάπεμψον), i. e. without delay, [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [“PCair.Zen.” 314.7, “PSI” 5.514.3 (both 3rd c.BC)]]; μέσαι νύκτες midnight, [Refs 7th c.BC+ [7th-6th c.BC: Sappho Lyrica 52, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 621b; περὶ μ. νύκτας 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 7.8.12; ἐν μέσῳ νυκτῶν [prev. author] “Cyr.” 5.3.52; πρωΐτερον μέσων νυκτῶν 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 8.101; ἔξω μέσων ν. 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 54.26.]]

__2
frequently with Preps., ἀνὰ νύκτα by night, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 14.80]]; ἀνὰ πᾶσαν ν. all night through, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [2nd c.AD: Pausanias Periegeta 1.32.4; διὰ νύκτα 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 19.66, etc.]]; εἰς νύκτα, εἰς τὴν ν., towards night, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Cynegeticus” 11.4, “HG” 4.6.7]]; ἐν νυττί (νυκτί), opposed to πεδ᾽ ἀμέραν, [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [“Leg.Gort.” 2.14, “SIG” 527.40 (Dreros, 3rd c.BC)]]; κατὰ νύκτα [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Fragmenta” 561 (Lyric poetry)]]; ὑπὸ νύκτα to wards nightfall, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 4.67, 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Agesilaus” 2.19]]; μετὰ νύκτας by night, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “N.” 6.6]]; μεθ᾽ ἡμέραν καὶ διὰ νυκτός all through the night, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Critias” 117e]]; ἐκ νυκτός after nightfall, [LXX+6th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 1.4.2, LXX.Isa.26.9, etc.; ἐκ πολλῆς ἔτι νυκτός 1st c.BC: Dionysius Halicarnassensis 6.67; ἐκ νυκτῶν 6th c.BC: Theognis Elegiacus 460, 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Choephori” 287, 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Rhesus” 13, 17 (both _anapaest meter_); ἐκ νυκτὸς εἰς νύκτα 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Axiochus” 368b]]; πόρρω τῶν νυκτῶν far into the night, [Refs [[prev. author] “Smp.” 217d, “Prt.” 310c]]; ἐπὶ νυκτί by night, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 8.529; ἐφ᾽ ἡμέρῃ αἱ δ᾽ ἐπὶ νυκτί 8th-7th c.BC: Hesiodus Epicus “Opera et Dies” 102; ἐν νυκτί 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Agamemnon” 653, 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Symposium” 1.9, etc.; ὀψίᾳ ἐν ν. 5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “I.” 4(3).36; ἐν ν. τῇ νῦν 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Antigone” 16; νύκτεσσιν ἔν θ᾽ ἁμέραις 5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “P.” 4.130.]]

__3
in plural, watches of the night, [Refs [[prev. work] 256]]; three such, παροίχωκεν δὲ πλέων νὺξ τῶν δύο μοιράων, τριτάτη δ᾽ ἔτι μοῖρα λέλειπται [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 10.252]]; τρίχα νυκτὸς ἔην, for τρίτον μέρος τῆς νυκτὸς ἦν, it was the third watch, i. e. next before morning, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 12.312.]]

__II
metaphorically of darkness, νυκτὶ καλύψαι [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 5.23, compare 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 20.351, etc.]]

__II.2
metaphorically of death, ἀμφὶ δὲ ὄσσε κελαινὴ ν. ἐκάλυψε [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 5.310, +others; ν. Ἅιδης τε 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Ajax” 660.]]

__II.3
in Comparisons, of anything dark and direful, νυκτὶ ἐοικώς like night, of Apollo in his wrath, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 1.47, compare 12.463, 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 11.606]]; τάδε νυκτὶ ἐΐσκει what is here he like ns to night, [Refs [20.362]]; ὀλεθρία ν., of a great calamity, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Coloneus” 1684 (Lyric poetry).]]

__III
Νύξ as proper name, the goddess of Night, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 14.259, 8th-7th c.BC: Hesiodus Epicus “Opera et Dies” 17, “Th.” 123, 211; N. ὀλοή [prev. work] 224.]]

__IV
the night- or evening-quarter of heaven, the West, πρὸς νυκτός [Refs [[prev. work] 275. (Cf. Latin]]nox, Lithuanian naktis, Gothic nahts, etc.)

Abbott-Smith / STEPBible (TBESG)
ξένος, -η, -ον
[in LXX chiefly for נׇכְרִי ;]
__(a) foreign, alien: δαιμόνια, Act.17:18; διδαχαί Heb.13:9;
__(b) with genitive of thing(s), strange to, estranged from, ignorant of: Eph.2:12;
__(with) strange, unusual: 1Pe.4:12.
As subst., ὁ ξ.,
__(a) a foreigner, stranger: Mat.25:35, 38 25:43-44 27:7, Act.17:21, 3Jn.5; ξέίνοι κ. τάροικοι (opposite to συμπολῖται, οίκεῖοι), Eph.2:19; ξ. καὶ παρεπίδημοι,  Heb.11:13;
__(b) one of the parties bound by ties of hospitality;
__α the guest;
__β the host (= ξενοδόκος, Hom., Ii, xv, 532) : Rom.16:23.†
(AS)

---

LSJ / STEPBible (TFLSJ)
ξένος, ὁ,
Epic dialect and Ionic dialect ξεῖνος (also frequently in [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus, “N.” 7.61, +others]], used by Trag. for the sake of meter even in trimeter, mostly in vocative, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Coloneus” 33, +others, 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Iphigenia Taurica” 798 codices, “El.” 247)]], Aeolic dialect ξέννος [Refs [Hdn.Gr. 2.302]]; scanned ¯ ?~X and written ξεῖνος in [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [3rd c.BC: Theocritus Poeta Bucolicus 28.6, 30.17: _Aeolic dialect_ _superlative_ ξεννότατος Scholia 12th c.AD: Tzetzes, Joannes Grammaticus in “An. Ox.” 3.356.18 (sed see near the end)]].

__I
guest-friend, applied to persons and states bound by a treaty or tie of hospitality, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 1.313, etc.; ξεῖνοι δὲ.. εὐχόμεθ᾽ εἶναι ἐκ πατέρων φιλότητος 15.196; ξ. πατρώϊός ἐσσι παλαιός 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 6.215; ξ. δ᾽ ἀλλήλων πατρώϊοι εὐχόμεθ᾽ εἶναι 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 1.187; φησὶ δ᾽ Ὀδυσσῆος ξεῖνος πατρώϊος εἶναι 17.522; later frequently coupled with φίλος, Πλούταρχος ὁ τούτου ξένος καὶ φίλος 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 21.110, compare 18.46, 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 2.1.5, 5th c.BC: Lysias Orator 19.19; βασιλέως πατρικὸς ξ. 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Meno” 78d.]]

__I.2
of parties giving or receiving hospitality, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 8.145, etc.]]; mostly of the guest, opposed to the host, ξεινοδόκοι καὶ ξεῖνος [Refs [[prev. work] 543]], etc.; ἁ ξείνα the visitor, [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [3rd c.BC: Theocritus Poeta Bucolicus 2.154]]; of guests at a club, opposed to σύνδειπνοι, [Refs 2nd c.BC+ [“PTeb.” 118.4 (2nd c.BC)]]: less frequently of the host, [NT+8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 15.532, 3rd c.BC: Apollonius Rhodius Epicus 1.208, NT.Rom.16.23, etc.: with _dative_, ξεῖνός τινι 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.20, 22, compare 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 2.13, 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 1.1.10, etc.; also ξ. τινός [prev. work] 2.4.15.]]

__II
stranger, especially wanderer, refugee (under the protection of Ζεὺς ξένιος), sometimes coupled with ἱκέτης, Ζεὺς ἐπιτιμήτωρ ἱκετάων τε ξείνων τε ξείνιος [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 9.270, compare 8.546; with πτωχός, πρὸς γὰρ Διός εἰσιν ἅπαντες ξεῖνοί τε πτωχοί τε 6.208.]]

__III
generally, stranger, foreigner, opposed to ἔνδημος, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th-7th c.BC: Hesiodus Epicus “Opera et Dies” 225]]; opposed to ἀστός, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “O.” 7.90, 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Coloneus” 13, 5th-6th c.BC: Andocides Orator 4.10, etc.; πολιατᾶν καὶ ξ. 5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “I.” 1.51, compare 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Septem contra Thebas” 924 (Lyric poetry), 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Gorgias” 473d, etc.]]; opposed to ἐπιχώριος, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. author] “Men.” 94d: coupled with μέτοικος, 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 4.90, compare “IG” 12.39.53]]; with ἔπηλυς, [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd c.AD: Lucianus Sophista “Herm.” 24]]; opposed to a member of the family, [Refs 6th c.AD+ [“PMasp.” 169.10 (6th c.AD), etc.]]

__III.b
as a term of address to any stranger, ὦ ξένε [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Ion” 247, 2nd c.BC: Moschus Bucolicus 1.5, etc.; ὦ ξένη 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Symposium” 204c.]]

__III.2
={βάρβαρος}, at Sparta, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 9.11, 55.]]

__IV
hireling, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 14.102]]; especially mercenary soldier, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [Inscriptiones Graecae 12.949.89, 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 1.1.10, 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 18.152, etc.; ξ. ναυβάται 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 1.121]]: rarely simply, ally, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Respublica Lacedaemoniorum” 12.3.]]

__B
as adjective ξένος, η, ον (also ος, ον [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Supplices” 94)]], Ionic dialect ξεῖνος, η, ον, foreign, not in [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Homerus Epicus (in the phrases ξεῖνε πάτερ 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 7.28, ἄνθρωποι ξεῖνοι 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 24.202, both words are _substantive_)]]; frequently in later writers, ξείνα γαῖα [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “P.” 4.118 codices; ξένης ἐπὶ χθονός 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Coloneus” 1256; γᾶς ἐπὶ ξένας [prev. work] 1705 (Lyric poetry, compare ξένη)]]; ἐν ξένῃσι χερσί by foreign hands, [Refs [[prev. author] “El.” 1141]]; ξ. δόμοι, πόλις, etc., [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Phoenissae” 339 (Lyric poetry), 369, etc.]]; of alien property, ξ. ἄρουραι [Refs 6th c.AD+ [“PMasp.” 295.22 (6th c.AD).]]

__B.II
with genitive of things, strange to a thing, unacquainted with, ignorant of it, ξ. τοῦ λόγου [NT+5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Tyrannus” 219, compare “Anthologia Graeca” 4.3a.37 (6th c.AD: Agathias Historicus et Epigrammaticus); ξ. τῶν διαθηκῶν τῆς ἐπαγγελίας NT.Eph.2.12, compare “BGU” 405.12 (4th c.AD).]] adverb ξένως, ἔχω τῆς ἐνθάδε λέξεως I am a stranger to the mode of speech, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Apologia” 17d; ἔχειν τῆς διαλέκτου 4th c.AD: Themistius Sophista “Orationes” 21.253c.]]

__B.III
strange, unusual, λόγοι [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Prometheus Vinctus” 688 (Lyric poetry); τιμωρίαι 5th-4th c.BC: Timaeus Locrus Philosophus 104d; ποιεῖν ξένην τὴν διάλεκτον 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Rhetorica” 1404b11, compare 1415a7; οὐδὲν ξ. ἐν τῷ παντὶ ἀποτελεῖται 4th-3rd c.BC: Epicurus Philosophus “Fragmenta” 266; τοῖς νέοις ποιεῖν ξένα τὰ φαῦλα 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Politica” 1336b34; ξένα ταῖς ὄψεσι 1st c.BC: Diodorus Siculus Historicus 3.15]]; ὡς ξένου συμβαίνοντος NT.1Pet.4.12 [; διδαχαὶ ποικίλαι καὶ ξ. NT.Heb.13.9; ξ. δαιμόνια NT.Act.17.18]: superlative, πράξεων ὡς -οτάτων [Refs 1st c.BC+ [1st c.BC: Philodemus Gadarensis Epigrammaticus “Herc.” 1251.5; ξ. αὐτῷ δοκεῖ τὸ πρᾶγμα 2nd c.AD: Lucianus Sophista “Cont.” 13, etc.]] adverb ξένως, λαλεῖν [Refs 1st c.BC+ [1st c.BC: Philodemus Gadarensis Epigrammaticus P 0.5.12.]]

__B.III.2
τοῦ πνεύματος.. ῥύσις ὡς -ωτάτη air as fresh as possible, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Hippocrates Medicus “περὶ φύσιος ἀνθρώπου” 9. (From ξένϝος,compare πρόξενϝος “IG” 9(1).867, Ξενϝάρης [prev. work]869, Ξενϝοκλῆς, Ξένϝων, [prev. work]4.315,348: hence it is improbable that the _Aeolic dialect_ form was ξέννος.)]]

Abbott-Smith / STEPBible (TBESG)
ὁ, ἡ, τό,
the prepositive article (ἄρθρον προτακτικόν), originally a demonstr. pron. (so usually in Hom.), in general corresponding to the Eng. definite article.
__I. As demonstr. pron.
__1. As frequently in Hom., absol., he (she, it), his (etc.): Act.17:28 (quoted from the poet Aratus).
__2. Distributive, ὁ μὲν . . . ὁ δέ, the one . . . the other: 1Co.7:7, Gal.4:22; pl., Act.14:4, 17:32, Php.1:16, al.; οἱ μὲν . . . ἄλλοι δέ, Mat.16:14, Jhn.7:12; οἱ μεν̀ . . . ὁδέ, Heb.7:21, 23.
__3. In narration (without ὁ μὲν preceding), ὁ δέ, but he: Mat.2:14, Mrk.1:45, Luk.8:21, Jhn.9:38, al. mult.
__II. As prepositive article, the, prefixed,
__1. to nouns unmodified: ὁ θεός, τὸ φῶς, etc.; to abstract nouns, ἡ σοφία, etc., to pl. nouns which indicate a class, οἱ ἀλώπεκες, foxes, Mat.8:20, al.; to an individual as representing a class, ὁ ἐργάτης, Luk.10:7; with nom. = voc. in addresses, Mat.11:26, Jhn.19:3, Jas.5:1, al.; to things which pertain to one, ἡ χεῖρ, his hand, Mrk.3:1; to names of persons well known or already mentioned; usually to names of countries (originally adjectives), ἡ Ἰουδαία, etc.
__2. To modified nouns: with of person(s) pron. genitive, μοῦ, σοῦ, etc.; with poss. pron., ἐμός, σός, etc.; with adj. between the art. and the noun, ὁ ἀγαθὸς ἄνθρωπος, Mat.12:35; the noun foll, by adj., both with art., ὁ ποιμὴν ὁ καλός, Jhn.10:11 (on ὁ ὄχλος πολύς, Jhn.12:9, see M, Pr., 84); before adjectival phrases, ἡ κατ᾽ ἐκλογὴν πρόθεσις, Rom.9:11.
__3. To Other parts of speech used as substantives;
__(a) neuter adjectives: τ. ἀγαθόν, etc.;
__(b) cardinal numerals: ὁ εἶς, οἷ δύο, etc.;
__(with) participles: ὁ βαπτίζων (= ὁ Βαπτιστής, Mat.14:2), Mrk.6:14; πᾶς ὁ, with ptcp., every one who, etc.;
__(d) adverbs: τὸ πέραν, τὰ νῦν, ὁ ἔσω ἄνθρωπος;
__(e) infinitives: nom., τὸ θέλειν, Rom.7:18, al.; genitive, τοῦ, after adjectives, ἄξιον τοῦ πορεύεσθαι, 1Co.16:4; verbs, ἐλαχεν τοῦ θυμιᾶσαι, Luk.1:9; and frequently in a final sense, ἐξῆλθεν ὁ σπείρειν, Mat.13:3 (on the artic. inf., see Bl., §71).
__4. In the neut. to sentences, phrases or single words treated as a quotation: τὸ Ἐι δύνῃ, Mrk.9:23; τὸ ἔτι ἅπαξ, Heb.12:27; τὸ ἀνέβη, Eph.4:9, al.
__5. To prepositional phrases: οἱ ἀπὸ Ἰταλίας, Heb.13:24; οἱ ἐκ νόμου, Rom.4:14; neut. accusative absol., in adverbial phrases, τὸ καθ᾽ ἡμέραν, daily, Luk.11:3; τὸ κατὰ σάρκα, as regards the flesh, Rom.9:5.
__6. To nouns in the genitive, denoting kinship, association, etc.: ὁ τοῦ, the son of (unless context indicates a different relationship), Mat.10:2, al.; τὰ τοῦ θεοῦ, the things that pertain to God, Mat.16:23; τὰ τῆς εἰρήνης, Rom.14:19 (cf. M, Pr., 81ff.; Bl, §§46, 47).

The _Attic dialect_]] Poets also used the Ionic dialect and _Epic dialect_ forms τοῖσι, ταῖσ; and in Trag. we find τοὶ μέν.., τοὶ δέ.., for οἱ μέν.., οἱ δέ.., not only in Lyric poetry, as [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Persae” 584, “Th.” 295, 298; οἱ μέν.. τοὶ δ᾽ 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Ajax” 1404 (_anapaest meter_)]]; but even in a trimeter, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Persae” 424. VIII. 5. (With ὁ, ἁ,]] cf. Sanskrit demonstrative pronoun sa, sā, Gothic sa, sō, ONorse sá, sú, Old Latin accusative sum, sam (Enn.): —with τό [from *τόδ] cf. Sanskrit tat (tad), Latin is-tud, Gothic pata: —with τοί cf. Sanskrit te, Lithuanian tĩe, O[Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus]] pá, etc.:—with τάων cf. Sanskrit tāsām, Latin is-tarum:— the origin of the relative ὅς, ἥ, ὅ (which see) is different.)

__A
ὁ, ἡ, τό, DEMONSTR. PRONOUN, that, the oldest and in [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Homerus Epicus]] the commonest sense: frequently also in [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus (1.86, 5.35, +others)]], and sometimes in Trag. (mostly in Lyric poetry, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Supplices” 1047, etc.; in trimeters, [prev. author] “Th.” 197, “Ag.” 7, “Eu.” 174]]; τῶν γάρ.., τῆς γάρ.., [Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. author] “Supp.” 358, 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Tyrannus” 1082]]; seldom in Attic dialect Prose, except in special phrases, see infr. VI, VII):

__A.I
joined with a substantive, to call attention to it, ὁ Τυδεΐδης he—Tydeus' famous son, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 11.660]]; τὸν Χρύσην that venerable man Chryses, I.II: and so with appellative, Νέστωρ ὁ γέρων N.—thataged man, [Refs [7.324]]; αἰετοῦ.. τοῦ θηρητῆρος the eagle, that which is called hunter, [Refs [21.252, +others]]; also to define and give emphasis, τιμῆς τῆς Πριάμου for honour, namely that of Priam, [Refs [20.181]]; οἴχετ᾽ ἀνὴρ ὤριστος a man is gone, and he the best, [Refs [11.288, compare 13.433, +others: sometimes with words between the _pronoun_ and Noun, αὐτὰρ ὁ αὖτε Πέλοψ 2.105; τὸν Ἕκτορι μῦθον ἐνίσπες 11.186, compare 703, +others]]:—different from this are cases [Refs 8th c.BC+ [like 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 1.409 αἴ κέν πως ἐθέλῃσιν ἐπὶ Τρώεσσιν ἀρῆξαι, τοὺς δὲ κατὰ πρύμνας τε καὶ ἀμφ᾽ ἅλα ἔλσαι Ἀχαιούς]] if he would help the Trojans, but drive those back to the ships—I mean the Achaeans, where Ἀχ. is only added to explain τούς, compare [Refs [1.472, 4.20, 329, +others]]

__A.II
frequently without a substantive, he, she, it, ὁ γὰρ ἦλθε [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 1.12, +others]]

__A.III
placed after its Noun, before the Relat. Prons., ἐφάμην σὲ περὶ φρένας ἔμμεναι ἄλλων, τῶν ὅσσοι Λυκίην ναιετάουσι far above the rest, above those to wit who, etc., [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 17.172]]; οἷ᾽ οὔ πώ τιν᾽ ἀκούομεν οὐδὲ παλαιῶν, τάων αἳ πάρος ἦσαν.. Ἀχαιαί such as we have not heard tell of yet even among the women of old, those women to wit who.., [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 2.119, compare 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 5.332; θάλαμον τὸν ἀφίκετο, τόν ποτε τέκτων ξέσσεν 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 21.43, compare 1.116, 10.74:]] —for the _Attic dialect_ usage see below

__A.IV
before a Possessive pronoun its demonstrative force is sometimes very manifest, φθίσει σε τὸ σὸν μένος that spirit of thine, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 6.407, compare 11.608; but in 15.58, 16.40, and elsewhere it is merely the _Article_]]

__A.V
for cases in which the Homeric usage approaches most nearly to the Attic, see below [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Bacchylides Lyricus [near the start]]]

__A.VI
ὁ μέν.., ὁ δέ.. without a substantive, in all cases, genders, and numbers, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Homerus Epicus, etc.: sometimes in Opposition, where ὁ μέν]] properly refers to the former, ὁ δέ to the latter; more rarely ὁ μέν the latter, ὁ δέ the former, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Protagoras” 359e, 5th-6th c.BC: Isocrates Orator 2.32,34]]: sometimes in Partition, the one.., the other.., etc.—The Noun with it is regularly in genitive plural, being divided by the ὁ μέν.., ὁ δέ.., into parts, ἠΐθεοι καὶ παρθένοι.., τῶν δ᾽ αἱ μὲν λεπτὰς ὀθόνας ἔχον, οἱ δὲ χιτῶνας εἵατο [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 18.595; τῶν πόλεων αἱ μὲν τυραννοῦνται, αἱ δὲ δημοκρατοῦνται, αἱ δὲ ἀριστοκρατοῦνται 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 338d, etc.]]: but frequently the Noun is in the same case, by a kind of apposition, ἴδον υἷε Δάρητος, τὸν μὲν ἀλευάμενον τὸν δὲ κτάμενον [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 5.28, compare 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 12.73, etc.]]: so in Trag. and Attic dialect, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Antigone” 22, etc.; πηγὴ ἡ μὲν εἰς αὐτὸν ἔδυ, ἡ δὲ ἔξω ἀπορρεῖ 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Phaedrus” 255c]]; if the Noun be collective, it is in the genitive singular, ὁ μὲν πεπραμένος ἦν τοῦ σίτου, ὁ δὲ ἔνδον ἀποκείμενος [Refs 8th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 42.6: sometimes a Noun is added in apposition with ὁ μέν or ὁ δέ, ὁ μὲν οὔτασ᾽ Ἀτύμνιον ὀξέϊ δουρὶ Ἀντίλοχος.., Μάρις δὲ.. 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 16.317 - 19, compare 116; τοὺς μὲν τὰ δίκαια ποιεῖν ἠνάγκασα, τοὺς πλουσίους, τοὺς δὲ πένητας κτλ. 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 18.102, compare 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Gorgias” 501a, etc.]]

__A.VI.2
when a negative accompanies ὁ δέ, it follows δέ, e.g. τὰς γοῦν Ἀθήνας οἶδα τὸν δὲ χῶρον οὔ [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Coloneus” 24; τὸν φιλόσοφον σοφίας ἐπιθυμητὴν εἶναι, οὐ τῆς μὲν τῆς δ᾽ οὔ, ἀλλὰ πάσης 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 475b; οὐ πάσας χρὴ τὰς δόξας τιμᾶν, ἀλλὰ τὰς μὲν τὰς δ᾽ οὔ· οὐδὲ πάντων, ἀλλὰ τῶν μὲν τῶν δ᾽ οὔ [prev. author] “Cri.” 47a, etc.]]

__A.VI.3
ὁ μέν τις.., ὁ δέ τις.. is used in Prose, when the Noun to which ὁ refers is left indefinite, ἔλεγον ὁ μέν τις τὴν σοφίαν, ὁ δὲ τὴν καρτερίαν.., ὁ δέ τις καὶ τὸ κάλλος [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 3.1.41; νόμους.. τοὺς μὲν ὀρθῶς τιθέασιν τοὺς δέ τινας οὐκ ὀρθῶς 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 339c, compare “Phlb.” 13c.]]

__A.VI.4
on τὸ μέν.., τὸ δέ.., or τὰ μέν.., τὰ δέ.., [Refs [see infr. VIII. 4.]]

__A.VI.5
ὁ μέν is frequently used without a corresponding ὁ δέ, οἱ μὲν ἄρ᾽ ἐσκίδναντο.., Μυρμιδόνας δ᾽ οὐκ εἴα ἀποσκίδνασθαι [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 23.3, compare 24.722, 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 8.12, etc.: also followed by ἀλλά, ἡ μὲν γάρ μ᾽ ἐκέλευε.., ἀλλ᾽ ἐγὼ οὐκ ἔθελον 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 7.304]]; by ἄλλος δέ, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 6.147, etc.; τὸν μὲν.., ἕτερον δέ 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Aves” 843, etc.; ὁ μέν.., ὃς δέ.. 6th c.BC: Theognis Elegiacus 205 (variant{οὐδέ}): less frequently ὁ δέ in the latter clause without ὁ μέν preceding, τῇ ῥα παραδραμέτην φεύγων, ὁ δ᾽ ὄπισθε διώκων (for ὁ μὲν φεύγων) 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 22.157; σφραγῖδε.. χρυσοῦν ἔχουσα τὸν δακτύλιον, ἡ δ᾽ ἑτέρα ἀργυροῦν “IG” 22.1388.45, compare μέν 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator III; γεωργὸς μὲν εἷς, ὁ δὲ οἰκοδόμος, ἄλλος δέ τις ὑφαντής 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 369d, compare “Tht.” 181d.]]

__A.VI.6
ὁ δέ following μέν sometimes refers to the subject of the preceding clause, τοῦ μὲν ἅμαρθ᾽, ὁ δὲ Λεῦκον.. βεβλήκει [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 4.491; τὴν μὲν γενομένην αὐτοῖσι αἰτίην οὐ μάλα ἐξέφαινε, ὁ δὲ ἔλεγέ σφι 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 6.3, compare 1.66, 6.9, 133, 7.6]]: rare in Attic dialect Prose, ἐπεψήφιζεν αὐτὸς ἔφορος ὤν· ὁ δὲ οὐκ ἔφη διαγιγνώσκειν τὴν βοήν [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 1.87; ἔμενον ὡς κατέχοντες τὸ ἄκρον· οἱ δ᾽ οὐ κατεῖχον 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 4.2.6: this is different from ὁ δέ in apodosi, see below 7; also from passages in which both clauses have a common verb, see at {ὅ γε} 11.]]

__A.VI.7
ὁ δέ is frequently used simply in continuing a narrative, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 1.43, etc.]]; also used by [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Homerus Epicus in apodosi after a _relative_, see at {ὅδε} III.3.]]

__A.VI.8
the opposition may be expressed otherwise than by μέν and δέ, οὔθ᾽ ὁ.. οὔθ᾽ ὁ [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 15.417; ἢ τοῖσιν ἢ τοῖς 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Supplices” 439; οὔτε τοῖς οὔτε τοῖς 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Leges” 701e.]]

__A.VII
the following usages prevailed in Attic dialect Prose,

__A.VII.1
in dialogue, after καί, it was usual to say in nominative singular masculine καὶ ὅ; in the other cases the usual forms of the Article were used (see. ὅς [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus]] II.I and cf. Sanskrit sas, alternatative form of sa); so, in accusative, καὶ τὸν εἰπεῖν [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Symposium” 174a, compare 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 1.3.9, etc.; also in 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus, καὶ τὴν φράσαι 6.61, +others]]

__A.VII.2
ὁ καὶ ὁ such and such, τῇ καὶ τῇ ἀτιμίᾳ [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Leges” 721b]]: but mostly in accusative, καί μοι κάλει τὸν καὶ τόν [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Lysias Orator 1.23, compare 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Leges” 784d; τὰ καὶ τὰ πεπονθώς 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 21.141, compare 9.68; τὸ καὶ τό [prev. author] 18.243]]; ἀνάγκη ἄρα τὸ καὶ τό it must then be so and so, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Rhetorica” 1401a4, compare 1413a22]]; but τὰ καὶ τά now one thing, now another, of good and bad, τὸν δ᾽ ἀγαθὸν τολμᾶν χρὴ τά τε καὶ τὰ φέρειν [Refs 6th c.BC+ [6th c.BC: Theognis Elegiacus 398, compare 5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “P.” 5.55, 7.20, +others; τῶν τε καὶ τῶν καιρόν [prev. author] “O.” 2.53]]; so πάντα τοῦ μετρίου μεταβαλλόμενα ἐπὶ τὰ καὶ ἐπὶ τά, of excess and defect, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Hippocrates Medicus “περὶ διαίτης ὀξέων” 46; compare 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus VI.8.]]

__A.VIII
absolutely usages of single cases,

__A.VIII.1
feminine dative τῇ, of Place, there, on that spot, here, this way, that way, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 5.752, 858, +others: followed by ᾗ, 13.52]], etc.: also in Prose, τὸ μὲν τῇ, τὸ δὲ τῇ [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Respublica Atheniensium” 2.12.]]

__A.VIII.1.b
with a notion of motion towards, that way, in that direction, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 10.531, 11.149, 12.124; τῇ ἴμεν ᾗ.. 15.46; δελφῖνες τῇ καὶ τῇ ἐθύνεον ἰχθυάοντες 8th-7th c.BC: Hesiodus Epicus “Scutum Herculis” 210:]] —only poetry

__A.VIII.1.c
of Manner, τῇ περ τελευτήσεσθαι ἔμελλεν in this way, thus, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 8.510.]]

__A.VIII.1.d
repeated, τῇ μέν.., τῇ δέ.., in one way.., in another.., or partly.., partly.., [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Orestes” 356, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Symposium” 211a, etc.: without μέν, τῇ μᾶλλον, τῇ δ᾽ ἧσσον 4th-5th c.BC: Parmenides Poeta Philosophus 8.48.]]

__A.VIII.1.e
relative, where, by which way, only Epic dialect, as [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 12.118, 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 4.229.]]

__A.VIII.2
neuter dative τῷ, therefore, on this account, frequently in [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Homerus Epicus, 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 1.418, 2.254, +others (see. below): also in Trag., 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Prometheus Vinctus” 239, 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Tyrannus” 510 (Lyric poetry); in Prose, τῷ τοι.. 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Theaetetus” 179d, “Sph.” 230b.]]

__A.VIII.2.b
thus, so, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 2.373, 13.57, etc.: it may also, especially when εἰ]] precedes, be translated, then, if this be so, on this condition, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 1.239, 3.224, 258, +others, 3rd c.BC: Theocritus Poeta Bucolicus 29.11.—In 8th c.BC: Homerus Epicus the true form is probably τῶ, as in codex A, or τώ,compare 2nd c.AD: Apollonius Dyscolus Grammaticus “de Adverbiis;” 199.2.]]

__A.VIII.3
neuter accusative τό, wherefore, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 3.176, 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 8.332, +others, 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Philoctetes” 142 (Lyric poetry)]]; also τὸ δέ absolutely, but the fact is.., [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Apologia” 23a, “Men.” 97c, “Phd.” 109d, “Tht.” 157b, “R.” 340d, “Lg.” 967a]]; even when the τό refers to what precedes, the contrast may lie not in the thing referred to, but in another part of the sentence (compare above[Refs 5th c.BC+ [VI. 6), τὸ δ᾽ ἐπὶ κακουργίᾳ.. ἐπετήδευσαν 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 1.37; τὸ δὲ.. ἡμῖν μᾶλλον περιέσται [prev. author] 2.89]]; φασὶ δέ τινες αὐτὸν καὶ τῶν ἑπτὰ σοφῶν γεγονέναι· τὸ δὲ οὐκ ἦν but he was not, [Refs 1st c.BC+ [1st c.BC: Nicolaus Damascenus Historicus 58J.]]

__A.VIII.4
τὸ μέν.., τὸ δέ.., partly.., partly.., or on the one hand.., on the other.., [Refs 8th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 7.36, etc., compare 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 2.46]]; more frequently τὰ μέν.., τὰ δέ.., [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.173, 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Trachiniae” 534, etc.; also τὰ μέν τι.., τὰ δέ τι.. 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 4.1.14; τὸ μέν τι.., τὸ δέ τι.. 2nd c.AD: Lucianus Sophista “Macr.” 14; τὰ μέν.., τὸ δὲ πλέον.. 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 1.90: sometimes without τὸ μέν..]] in the first clause, τὸ δέ τι [Refs [[prev. author] 1.107, 7.48: rarely of Time, τὰ μὲν πολλὰ.., τέλος δέ]] several times..  and finally, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 3.85.]]

__A.VIII.5
of Time, sometimes that time, sometimes this (present) time, συνμαχία κ᾽ ἔα ἑκατὸν ϝέτεα, ἄρχοι δέ κα τοΐ (where it is possible, but not necessary, to supply ϝέτος) [Refs 6th c.BC+ [“SIG” 9.3 (Olympia, 6th c.BC): so with Preps., ἐκ τοῦ, _Epic dialect_ τοῖο,]] from that time, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 1.493, 15.601.]]

__A.VIII.5.b
πρὸ τοῦ, sometimes written προτοῦ, before this, aforetime, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.103, 122, 5.55, 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Agamemnon” 1204, 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Nubes” 5, etc.; ἐν τῷ πρὸ τοῦ χρόνῳ 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 1.32, compare 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Eumenides” 462; τὸ πρὸ τοῦ 1st c.BC: Diodorus Siculus Historicus 20.59.]]

__A.VIII.5.c
in Thess. Prose, ὑππρὸ τᾶς yesterday, τὰ ψαφίσματα τό τε ὑππρὸ τᾶς γενόμενον καὶ τὸ τᾶμον the decree which was passed yesterday (literal before this [day]), and to-day's, [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [“IG” 9(2).517.43 (Larissa, 3rd c.BC).]]

__A.VIII.6
ἐν τοῖς is frequently used in Prose with Superlatives, ἐν τοῖσι θειότατον a most marvellous thing, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 7.137]]; ἐν τοῖς πρῶτοι the very first, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 1.6, etc.]]; ἐν τοῖσι πρῶτος (πρώτοις codices) [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Pherecrates Comicus 145.4]]; [Ζεὺς] Ἔρωτά τε καὶ Ἀνάγκην ἐν τοῖς πρῶτα ἐγέννησεν first of all, [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd c.AD: Aristides Rhetor “Orationes” 43(1).16, compare 37(2).2: when used with _feminine_ Nouns, ἐν τοῖς remained without change of gender, ἐν τοῖς πλεῖσται δὴ νῆες]] the greatest number of ships, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 3.17; ἐν τοῖς πρώτη ἐγένετο (i.e. ἡ στάσις) [prev. work] 82]]: also with adverbs, ἐν τοῖς μάλιστα [Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. author] 8.90, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Crito” 52a, 1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus 2.74e, 421d, 723e, “Brut.” 6, 11, +others, 2nd c.AD: Pausanias Periegeta 1.16.3, etc.; ἐν τοῖς χαλεπώτατα 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 7.71; τὴν Αἴγυπτον ἐν τοῖς μάλιστα μελάγγειον οὖσαν 1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus 2.364c]]: in late Prose, also with Positives, ἐν τοῖς παράδοξον [Refs 1st c.BC+ [2nd c.AD: Aristides Rhetor “Orationes” 48(24).47 codices; with πάνυ, ἐν τοῖς πάνυ 1st c.BC: Dionysius Halicarnassensis 1.19, compare 66 (ἐν ταῖς πάνυ _falsa lectio_ 4.14, 15).]]

__B
ὁ, ἡ, τό, THE DEFINITE ARTICLE, the, to specify individuals: rare in this signification in the earliest Gr., becoming commoner later. In [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Homerus Epicus]] the demonstrative force can generally be traced, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [see above 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus]] I, but the definite Article must be recognized in places [Refs 8th c.BC+ [like 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 1.167, 7.412, 9.309, 12.289, 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 19.372]]: also when joined to an adjective to make it a substantive, αἰὲν ἀποκτείνων τὸν ὀπίστατον the hindmost man, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 11.178; τὸν ἄριστον 17.80; τὸν δύστηνον 22.59; τὸν προὔχοντα 23.325; τῷ πρώτῳ.., τῷ δευτέρῳ.., etc., [prev. work] 265s q]].; also in τῶν ἄλλων [Refs [2.674, +others: with Advs., τὸ πρίν 24.543, +others; τὸ πάρος περ 17.720; τὸ πρόσθεν 23.583]]; also τὸ τρίτον[Refs [[prev. work] 733; τὰ πρῶτα 1.6, +others]]; τὸ μὲν ἄλλο for the rest,[Refs [23.454; ἀνδρῶν τῶν τότε 9.559.]]—The true Article, however, is first fully established in 5th C Attic dialect, whilst the demonstrative usage disappears, except in a few cases, V. [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus VI-VIII.]] —Chief usages, especially in _Attic dialect_

__B.I
not only with common Appellats., adjectives, and Parts., to specify them as present to sense or mind, but also frequently where we use the Possessive pronoun, τὸ κέαρ ηὐφράνθην [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Acharnenses” 5]]; τὴν κεφαλὴν κατεάγην my head was broken, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Andocides Orator 1.61, etc.]]; τοὺς φίλους ποιούμεθα we make our friends, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Antigone” 190]]; τὰς πόλεις ἔκτιζον they began founding their cities, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 1.12; οὐχ ὑπὲρ τὴν οὐσίαν ποιούμενοι τοὺς παῖδας 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 372b.]]

__B.I.b
omitted with proper nounsand frequently with Appellats. which require no specification, as θεός, βασιλεύς, see at {θεός} [Refs [I.1, βασιλεύς]] III; ἐμ πόλει in the Acropolis, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [“IG” 12.4.1, +others: but added to proper nouns, when attention is to be called to the previous mention of the person, as 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus (3.70) speaks first of Πειθίας and then refers to him repeatedly as ὁ Π.]]; compare Θράσυλος in [Refs [[prev. author] 8.104, with ὁ Θ. [prev. work] 105]]; or when the person spoken of is to be specially distinguished, Ζεύς, ὅστις ὁ Ζεύς whoever this Zeus is, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Fragmenta” 480]]; and therefore properly omitted when a special designation follows, as Σωκράτης ὁ φιλόσοφος: seldom in Trag. with proper nouns, save to give peculiar emphasis, like Latin ille, ὁ Λάϊος, ὁ Φοῖβος, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Tyrannus” 729, “El.” 35, etc.: later, however, the usage became very common (the Homeric usage of ὁ with a _proper name_ is different, see A.I).]]

__B.I.c
Aristotle says Σωκράτης meaning the historical Socrates, as in [Refs [“SE” 183b7, “PA” 642a28, +others, but ὁ Σωκράτης]] when he means the Platonic Socrates, as [Refs [“Pol.” 1261a6, +others: so with other proper nouns, “EN” 1145a21, 1146a21, +others]]

__B.I.d
for Σαῦλος ὁ καὶ Παῦλος, etc., see at {καί} [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Bacchylides Lyricus 2.]]

__B.I.2
in a generic sense, where the individual is treated as a type, οἷς ὁ γέρων μετέῃσιν.. λεύσσει [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 3.109; πονηρὸν ὁ συκοφάντης 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 18.242, etc.]]

__B.I.2.b
frequently with abstract Nouns, ἥ τε ἐλπὶς καὶ ὁ ἔρως [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 3.45, etc.]]

__B.I.3
of outstanding members of a class, ὁ γεωγράφος, ὁ κωμικός, ὁ ποιητής, ὁ τεχνικός, see at {γεωγράφος}, κωμικός, ποιητής, τεχνικός.

__B.I.4
with infinitives, which thereby become Substantives, τὸ εἴργειν prevention, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Gorgias” 505b]]; τὸ φρονεῖν good sense, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Antigone” 1348 (_anapaest meter_), etc.: when the subject is expressed it is put between the _Article_ and the]]infinitive, τὸ θεοὺς εἶναι the existence of gods, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Phaedo” 62b]]; τὸ μηδένα εἶναι ὄλβιον the fact or statement that no one is happy, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.86.]]

__B.I.5
in neuter before any word or expression which itself is made the object of thought, τὸ ἄνθρωπος the word or notion man; τὸ λέγω the word λέγ; τὸ μηδὲν ἄγαν the sentiment 'ne quid nimis', [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Hippolytus” 265 (Lyric poetry)]]; τὸ τῇ αὐτῇ the phrase τῇ αὐτῇ, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Meno” 72e: and so before whole clauses, ἡ δόξα.. περὶ τοῦ οὕστινας δεῖ ἄρχειν]] the opinion about the question 'who ought to rule', [Refs [[prev. author] “R.” 431e]]; τὸ ἐὰν μένητε παρ᾽ ἐμοί, ἀποδώσω the phrase 'I will give back, if.. ', [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 5.1.21, compare 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 327c, etc.; τοὺς τοῦ τί πρακτέον λογισμούς 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 23.148]]; τὸ ὀλίγοι the term few, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Politica” 1283b11.]]

__B.I.6
before relative clauses, when the Article serves to combine the whole relative clause into one notion, τῇ ᾗ φὴς σὺ σκληρότητι the harshness you speak of, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Cratylus” 435a]]; τὸν ἥμερον καρπόν.., καὶ τὸν ὅσος ξύλινος (i.e. καὶ τὸν καρπὸν ὅσος ἂν ᾖ ξύλινος) [Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. author] “Criti.” 115b; τῶν ὅσοι ἂν.. ἀγαθοὶ κριθῶσιν [prev. author] “R.” 469b; ἐκ γῆς καὶ πυρὸς μείξαντες καὶ τῶν ὅσα πυρὶ καὶ γῇ κεράννυται [prev. author] “Prt.” 320d, compare 4th c.BC: Hyperides Orator “pro Lycophrone” 2; ταύτην τε τὴν αἰτίαν καὶ τὴν ὅθεν ἡ κίνησις 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Metaphysica” 987a8; τὸν ὃς ἔφη 5th c.BC: Lysias Orator 23.8: hence the _relative_, by attraction, frequently follows the case of the _Article_, τοῖς οἵοις ἡμῖν τε καὶ ὑμῖν, i.e. τοῖς οὖσιν οἷοι ἡμεῖς καὶ ὑμεῖς, 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Historia Graeca (Hellenica)” 2.3.25, etc.]]

__B.I.7
before Prons.,

__B.I.7.a
before the person Prons., giving them greater emphasis, but only in accusative, τὸν ἐμέ [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Theaetetus” 166a, “Phlb.” 20b]]; τὸν.. σὲ καὶ ἐμέ[Refs [[prev. work] 59b; τὸν αὑτόν [prev. author] “Phdr.” 258a; on ὁ αὐτός, see at {αὐτός} 111.]]

__B.I.7.b
before the interrogative pronoun (both τίς and ποῖος), referring to something before, which needs to be more distinctly specified, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Prometheus Vinctus” 251, 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Pax” 696; also τὰ τ; because οἷα went before, [prev. work] 693. Of τίς only the _neuter_ is thus used (see.above): ποῖος is thus used not only in _neuter_ _plural_, τὰ ποῖ; 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Phoenissae” 707; but also in the other genders, ὁ ποῖο; [prev. work] 1704]]; τῆς ποίας μερίδο; [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 18.64]]; τοῖς ποίοις..; [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Physica” 227b1.]]

__B.I.7.c
with τοιοῦτος, τοιόσδε, τηλικοῦτος, etc., the Article either makes the pronoun into a substantive, ὁ τοιοῦτος that sort of person, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Memorabilia” 4.2.21, etc.]]; or subjoins it to a substantive which already has an Article, τὴν ἀπολογίαν τὴν τοιαύτην [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 41.13.]]

__B.I.8
before ἅπας, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “N.” 1.69, 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 3.64, 7.153 (assuming variant), 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Coloneus” 1224 (Lyric poetry), 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 18.231, etc.]]; also τὸν ἕνα, τὸν ἕνα τοῦτον, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Politica” 1287b8, 1288a19: on its usage with ἕκαστος,]] see entry; and on οἱ ἄλλοι, οἱ πολλοί, etc., see at {ἄλλος} [Refs [11.6, πολύς 11.3, etc.]]

__B.I.9
the Article with the comparative is rare, if ἤ follows, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Antigone” 313, “OC” 796.]]

__B.II
elliptic expressions:

__B.II.1
before the genitive of a proper name, to express descent, son or daughter, Θουκυδίδης ὁ Ὀλόρου (i.e. υἱός) [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 4.104]]; Ἑλένη ἡ τοῦ Διός (i.e. θυγάτηρ) [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Helena” 470]]: also to denote other relationships, e.g. brother, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Lysias Orator 32.24, 4th c.AD: Alciphro Epistolographus 2.2.10]]; ἡ Σμικυθίωνος Μελιστίχη M.the wife of [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus, 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Ecclesiazusae” 46]]; Κλέαρχος καὶ οἱ ἐκείνου Cl. and his men, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 1.2.15]]; ὁ τοῦ Ἀντιγένεος the slave of [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus, 5th c.BC: Hippocrates Medicus “περὶ χυμῶν” 20.]]

__B.II.2
generally, before a genitive it indicates a wider relation, as τὸ τῶν νεῶν, τὸ τῶν Ἑρμῶν, the matter of the ships, the affair of the Hermae, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 4.23, 6.60]]; τὰ τοῦ Ἀρριβαίου πράσσειν to promote the interests of Arrhibaeus, [Refs [[prev. author] 4.83, compare 6.89, etc.]]; τὸ τῆς τύχης,=ἡ τύχη, [Refs [[prev. author] 4.18]]; τὰ τῆς τύχης accidents, chance events, [Refs [[prev. work] 55]]; τὰ γὰρ φθιτῶν τοῖς ὁρῶσι κόσμος performance of the rites due to the dead befits the living, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Supplices” 78 (Lyric poetry)]]; τὰ τῶν θεῶν that which is destined by the gods, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Trachiniae” 498 (Lyric poetry): hence with _neuter_ of Possessive _pronoun_, τὸ ἐμόν, τὸ σόν,]] what regards me or thee, my or thy business or interests, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Ajax” 124, “El.” 251, etc.]]: and with genitive of [Refs 5th c.BC+ [3 _person_, τὸ τῆσδε 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Hippolytus” 48. But τό τινος]] is frequently also, a man's word or saying, as τὸ τοῦ Σόλωνος [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.86]]; τὸ τοῦ Ὁμήρου as Homer says, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Theaetetus” 183e]]; also τά τινος so-and-so's house, [NT+5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Vespae” 1432, 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 54.7, 3rd c.BC: Theocritus Poeta Bucolicus 2.76, 3rd c.BC: Herodas Mimographus 5.52, NT.Luke.2.49.]]

__B.II.3
very frequently with cases governed by Preps.. αἱ ἐκ τῆς Ζακύνθου νῆες the ships from Zacynthus, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 4.13; οἱ ἀμφί τινα, οἱ περί τινα, such an one and his followers, see at {ἀμφί} with 1.3, περί with 1.2]]; also τὰ ἐπὶ Θρᾴκης the Thrace-ward district, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 1.59, +others]]; τὰ ἀπὸ τοῦ καταστρώματος matters on deck, [Refs [[prev. author] 7.70]]; τὰ ἀπ᾽ Ἀλκιβιάδου the proposals of Alcibiades, [Refs [[prev. author] 8.48]]; τὰ ἀπὸ τῆς τύχης the incidents of fortune, [Refs [[prev. author] 2.87, etc.]]

__B.II.4
on μὰ τόν, μὰ τήν, etc., see at {μά} IV.

__B.II.5
in elliptical phrases, ἐπορευόμην τὴν ἔξω τείχους (i.e. ὁδόν) [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Lysis” 203a; ἡ ἐπὶ θανάτῳ (i.e. στολή, δέσις), see at {θάνατος}; κατὰ τὴν ἐμήν (i.e. γνώμην), see at {ἐμός} II.4]]; ἡ αὔριον (i.e. ἡμέρα), see at {αὔριον}; ἡ Λυδιστί (i.e. ἁρμονία) [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Politica” 1342b32, etc.: frequently with Advs., which thus take an adjective sense, as ὁ, ἡ, τὸ νῦν]]; ὁ οἴκαδε πλοῦς [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 1.52; οἱ τότε, οἱ ἔπειτα (i.e. ἄνθρωποι), [prev. work] 9, 10]], etc.; but τό stands absolutely with Advs. of time and place, when one cannot (as in the preceding instances) supply a substantive, as κἀκεῖσε καὶ τὸ δεῦρο [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Phoenissae” 266, compare [315] (Lyric poetry)]]; ὁ μὲν τὸ κεῖθεν, ὁ δὲ τὸ κεῖθεν [Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. author] “Or.” 1412 (Lyric poetry): rarely _absolutely_ in _genitive_, ἰέναι τοῦ πρόσω to go forward, 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 1.3.1; τοῦ προσωτάτω δραμεῖν 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Ajax” 731.]]

__C
as RELATIVE PRONOUN in many dialects; both in nominative singular masculine ὅ, as κλῦθί μοι, ὃ χθιζὸς θεὸς ἤλυθες [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 2.262, compare 1.300, +others; Ἔρως, ὃ κατ᾽ ὀμμάτων στάζεις πόθον 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Hippolytus” 526 (Lyric poetry); Ἄδωνις, ὃ κἠν Ἀχέροντι φιλεῖται 3rd c.BC: Theocritus Poeta Bucolicus 15.86]]; ὃ ἐξορύξη he who banishes him, [Refs [“Schwyzer” 679.12,25 (from Cyprus)]]; and in the forms beginning with τ, especially in [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Homerus Epicus (8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 4.160, +others), 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.7, +others]]: also in Ionic dialect Poets, ἐν τῷ κάθημαι [Refs 7th c.BC+ [7th c.BC: Archilochus Lyricus 87.3, compare 7th-6th c.BC(?): Semonides Iambographus 7.3, 6th c.BC: Anacreon Lyricus 86 (probably), 3rd c.BC: Herodas Mimographus 2.64, +others: frequently in Trag., τῆς 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Coloneus” 1258, “Tr.” 381, 728, 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Alcestis” 883 (_anapaest meter_); τῷ 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Philoctetes” 14; τήν [prev. author] “OC” 747, “Tr.” 47, “El.” 1144]]; τό [Refs [[prev. author] “OT” 1427]]; τῶν[Refs [[prev. work] 1379, “Ant.” 1086.]]—Never in Comedy texts or Attic dialect Prose:—Epic dialect genitive singular τεῦ [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 18.192 (assuming variant).]]

__D
CRASIS OF ARTICLE:

__D.a
Attic dialect ὁ, ἡ, τό, with ᾰ make ᾱ, as ἁνήρ, ἁλήθεια, τἀγαθόν, τᾄτιο; so οἱ, αἱ, τά, as ἅνδρες, τἀγαθ; also τοῦ, τῷ, as τἀγαθοῦ, τἀγαθῷ: ὁ, τό, οἱ, before e gives ου, οὑξ, οὑπί, οὑμός, τοὔργον, οὑπιχώριοι, etc.; also τοῦ, as τοὐμοῦ, τοὐπιόντο; but ἅτερος, θάτερον ([musical notation]), Ionic dialect οὕτερος, τοὔτερον (see. ἕτερος), Attic dialect feminine ἡτέρα, dative θητέρᾳ (see. ἕτερος); τῷ loses the iota, τὠμῷ, τὠπιόντι: ὁ, τό, before ο gives ου, as Οὁδυσσεύς, Οὑλύμπιος, τοὔνομα: ὁ, τό, etc., before αυ gives ᾱυ, αὑτός, ταὐτό, ταὐτῷ (frequently written ἁτός, etc. in Inscrr. and Papyrus); so τὰ αὐτά=ταὐτά, αἱ αὐταί=αὑταί: ἡ before εὐ gives ηὑ, as ηὑλάβεια: τῇ before ἡ gives θη, as θἠμέρᾳ: τὸ before ὑ gives θου, as θοὔδωρ for τὸ ὕδωρ.

__D.b
other dialects: in their treatment of crasis these follow the local laws of contraction, hence, e.g., Doric dialect ὡξ from ὁ ἐξ [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [3rd c.BC: Theocritus Poeta Bucolicus 1.65, ὥλαφος from ὁ ἔλαφος [prev. work] 135]]; Ionic dialect ᾡσυμνήτης from ὁ αἰς-[Refs 5th c.BC+ [“SIG” 57.45 (Milet., 5th c.BC)]]; ὡυτή from ἡ αὐτή [Refs 1st c.AD+ [1st c.AD(?): Heraclitus 60, etc.]]

ὄγκος, -ου, ὁ
bulk, mass; metaphorically, an encumbrance: Heb.12:1.†
SYN.: βάρος, a weight; φορτίον, a burden, that which is borne  (AS)

---

LSJ / STEPBible (TFLSJ)
ὄγκος, ὁ,

__B
bulk, size, mass of a body, μελέων ἀριδείκετον ὄ. [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Empedocles Poeta Philosophus 20.1; ἀέρος ὄ. [prev. author] 100.13; σφαίρης ἐναλίγκιον ὄγκῳ 4th-5th c.BC: Parmenides Poeta Philosophus 8.43: frequently in 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus, μήτε ὄγκῳ μήτε ἀριθμῷ “Tht.” 155a]]; τὸν.. ὄ. τοῦ ἀριθμοῦ their total number, [Refs [“Lg.” 737c; τὸν τῶν σαρκῶν ὄ. [prev. work] 959c]]; σμικρᾶς πόλεως ὄ. a city of small size, Plt.[Refs [259b]]; ἔχθρας ὄ. μέγαν [Refs [“Lg.” 843b]]; θαυμαστὸν ὄ. ἀράμενοι τοῦ μύθου taking on my shoulders a monstrous great story, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [“Plt.” 277b, etc.: frequently also in 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus]], the space filled by a body, opposed to τὸ κενόν, [Refs [“Ph.” 203b28, +others; ἴσος τὸν ὄ.]]in bulk, GC [Refs [326b20; ὄγκῳ μικρόν “EN” 1178a1, etc.]]

__B.b
flatulent distentions, [Refs [Diocl.fragment 43 (_plural_).]]

__B.2
bulk, mass, body, ὄ. φρυγάνων a heap of faggots, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 4.62]]; ὄ. μαλθακός mass or roll of something soft, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Hippocrates Medicus “περὶ ἄρθρων ἐμβολῆς” 26]]; σμικρὸς ὄ. ἐν σμικρῷ κύτει, of a dead man's ashes, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Electra” 1142]]; γαστρὸς ὄ., of a child in the womb, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Ion” 15; ὄ. πλήρης φλεβίων 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Historia Animalium” 515b1: _plural_, ὄγκοι]]bodies, material substances, [Refs [[prev. author] “Metaphorical” 1085a12, 1089b14]]; also ὁ ὄ. τῆς φωνῆς the volume of the note, [Refs [[prev. author] “Aud.” 804a15.]]

__B.3
a bushy top-knot, [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd c.AD(?): Pollianus Epigrammaticus 4.133.]]

__B.4
the human body, τῆς χολῆς ἀναχεομένης εἰς τὸν ὄ. [Refs 1st c.AD+ [2nd c.AD: Rufus Medicus “ἀνατομή” 30, compare 2nd c.AD: Soranus Medicus 1.26, 1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus 2.653f, 2nd c.AD: Galenus Medicus 1.272.]]

__B.II
metaphorically, bulk, weight, trouble, βραχεῖ σὺν ὄ. [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Coloneus” 1341.]]

__B.II.2
weight, dignity, pride, and in bad sense, self-importance, pretension, ὄ. ὀνόματος μητρῷος pride in the name of mother, [Refs [[prev. author] “Tr.” 817]]; ὄγκον αἴρειν exalt one's dignity, [Refs [[prev. author] “Aj.” 129; βραχὺν.. μῦθον οὐκ ὄγκου πλέων]]of pretension, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. author] “OC” 1162; μείζον᾽ ὄ. δορὸς ἤ φρενῶν 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Troades” 1158; ἔχει τιν᾽ ὄ. Ἄργος Ἑλλήνων πάρα [prev. author] “Ph.” 717; ἐς ὄ. βλέπειν τύχης [prev. author] “fragment” 81; τοῖς ζῶσι δ᾽ ὄγκος [prev. author] “Rh.” 760; ὁ τῶν ὑπεροπτικῶν ὄ. 5th-6th c.BC: Isocrates Orator 1.30; τῷ.. γένους ὄγκῳ 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus Alcaeus1.121b; πραγμάτων ὄ. 4th-3rd c.BC: Epicurus Philosophus “Fragmenta” 548; τῆς ἀρχῆς τὸ μέγεθος καὶ ὁ ὄ. 1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus “Fabius Maximus” 4; ὄγκον περιθεῖναί τινι [prev. author] “Per.” 4, etc.]]

[prev. author] “Po.” 1459b28, compare 4th c.BC: Demetrius Phalereus Rhetor “Demetrius on Style” 36, +others]]: in bad sense, bombast, ὁ Αἰσχύλου ὄ. deep_entry:
Abbott-Smith / STEPBible (TBESG)
ὅδε, ἥδε, τόδε
(the old demonstr. pron., ὁ + the enclitic δε), = Lat. hicce, this (here),
referring prop, to what is present, can be seen or pointed out: of a person just named, τῇδε (= ταύτῃ), Luk.10:39; neut. pl., τάδε (λέγει), referring to words which follow (so in Att.., and see MM, xvii) : Act.21:11, Rev.2:1, 8 2:12, 18 3:1, 7 3:14; εἰς τήνδε τ. πόλιν (= Att.. τῇ καὶ τῇ, Plat., Legg., iv, 721 B), such and such a city, Jas.4:13.†
(AS)

---

LSJ / STEPBible (TFLSJ)
ὅδε, ἥδε, τόδε,
demonstrative pronoun, this, formed by adding the enclitic -δε to the old demonstrative pronoun ὁ, ἡ, τό, and declined like it through all cases: Epic dialect dative plural τοῖσδεσσι, τοῖσδεσσιν, as well as τοῖσδε, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 10.462, 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 2.47, +others; and τοῖσδεσι 10.268, 21.93; τοῖσδεσιν 3rd c.AD: Democritus Epigrammaticus 175; τοισίδε 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.32, +others]]: Aeolic dialect genitive plural τῶνδεων [Refs 7th c.BC+ [7th-6th c.BC: Alcaeus Lyricus 126: argument _genitive_ _plural_ τωνδεωνήν (={τῶνδεων ἤν}) “Mnemos.” 57.208(6th c.BC): _nominative_ _plural_ _neuter_ ταδήν [prev. passage], “IG” 4.506.1]]; ταδή [Refs 5th c.BC+ [Scholia 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Acharnenses” 744:]] —ὅδε, like{οὗτος}, is opposed to ἐκεῖνος, to designate what is nearer as opposed to to what is more remote; but ὅδε refers more distinctly to what is present, to what can be seen or pointed out, though this distinction is sometimes not observed, e.g. ξύμπας Ἀχαιῶν λαός, ἐν δὲ τοῖσδ᾽ ἐγώ [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Philoctetes” 1243 (variant{τοῖς}),compare “Ant.” 449, and on the other hand, ἦ τόνδε φράζεις]];— τοῦτον, ὅνπερ εἰσορᾷς [Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. author] “OT” 1120: the forms ὁδί, ἡδί, etc. [ῑ], are frequently in Comedy texts and Oratt., but are not used in Trag.: the ῑ may be separated from the ὅδε by the adversative δέ, as τὸν μὲν.., τηνδεδί 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Aves” 18, compare “Ec.” 989.]]

__I
of Place, to point out what is present or before one, Ἕκτορος ἥδε γυνή this is, or here is, the wife of Hector, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 6.460: very frequently in Trag., ἀκτὴ μὲν ἥδε Λήμνου 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Ph.” I, compare 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Troades” 4, “Ion” 5, “Hel.” I, “HF” 4, “Ba.” 1]]; in Comedy texts, ἐγὼ σιωπῶ τῷδ; [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Ranae” 1134, etc.]]; and in Prose, ὧν Θεόδωρος εἷς ὅδε [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Theaetetus” 164e]]; of what belongs to this world, [Refs [[prev. author] “Phdr.” 250a, “Smp.” 211c.]]

__I.2
with Verbs of action, = here, ἀνδρί, ὅστις ὅδε κρατέει who holds sway here, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 5.175]]; ἔγχος μὲν τόδε κεῖται ἐπὶ χθονός here it lies, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [20.345, compare 21.533, 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 1.185, etc.]]; ἥδ᾽ ἡ κορώνη.. λέγει the crow here.., variant in [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Aves” 23: frequently in Trag., especially to indicate the entrance of a person on the stage, καὶ μὴν Ἐτεοκλῆς.. ὅδε χωρεῖ]] here comes.., [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Phoenissae” 443, compare 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Tyrannus” 297, 531, 632, “OC” 32, 549]]; falsa lectio in [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Heraclidae” 80.]]

__I.3
with a person pronoun, ὅδ᾽ ἐγὼ.. ἤλυθον here am I come, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 16.205]]; ἡμεῖς οἵδε περιφραζώμεθα let us here.., [Refs [1.76]]; δῶρα δ᾽ ἐγὼν ὅδε.. παρασχέμεν here am I [ready] to provide.., [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 19.140]]: with a proper name, ὅδ᾽ εἰμ᾽ Ὀρέστης [Refs 8th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Orestes” 380: with αὐτός, ὅδ᾽ αὐτὸς ἐγώ 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 21.207, 24.321.]]

__I.4
also with τίς and other interrogative words, τίς δ᾽ ὅδε Ναυσικάᾳ ἕπετα; who is this following her? [Refs [6.276, compare 1.225]]; τί κακὸν τόδε πάσχετ; what is this evil ye are suffering? [Refs [20.351]]; πρὸς ποῖον ἂν τόνδ᾽.. ἔπλε; [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Philoctetes” 572, compare 1204.]]

__I.5
in Trag. dialogue, ὅδε and ὅδ᾽ ἀνήρ, ={ἐγώ}, [Refs [[prev. author] “OT” 534, 815, etc.]]; γυναικὸς τῆσδε, for ἐμοῦ, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Agamemnon” 1438; τῆσδέ γε ζώσης ἔτι 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Trachiniae” 305]]; so ξὺν τῇδε χερί with this hand of mine, [Refs [[prev. author] “Ant.” 43, compare “OT” 811.]]

__I.6
in [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus, τοδί]] designates a particular thing, 'such and such', τοδὶ διὰ τοδὶ αἱρεῖται [Refs [“EN” 1151a35; τόδε μετὰ τόδε “GA” 734a28, compare b9; Καλλίᾳ κάμνοντι τηνδὶ τὴν νόσον τοδὶ συνήνεγκε “Metaphorical” 981a8; τόδε τὸ ἐν τῷ ἡμικυκλίῳ “APo.” 71a20]]; ἥδε ἡ ἰατρική, opposed to αὐτὴ ἡ ἰ., [Refs [“Metaphorical” 997b30]]; τόδε τι a this, i.e. a fully specified particular, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [“Cat.” 3b10, +others, compare 2nd c.AD: Galenus Medicus 6.113,171; τόδε τι καὶ οὐσία 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Metaphysica” 1060b1]]; πορευσόμεθα εἰς τήνδε τὴν πόλιν [NT.Jam.4.13.]

__II
of Time, to indicate the immediate present, ἥδ᾽ ἡμέρα [Refs 8th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Tyrannus” 438, etc.: more strongly, κατ᾽ ἦμαρ.. τὸ νῦν τόδε [prev. author] “Aj.” 753; τοῦδ᾽ αὐτοῦ λυκάβαντος 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 14.161]]; but νυκτὸς τῆσδε in the night just past, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Ajax” 21; νυκτὶ τῇδε [prev. author] “El.” 644]]; so τῆσδε τῆς ὁδοῦ on this present journey, [Refs [[prev. author] “OT” 1478, compare “Ant.” 878 (conjecture)]]; also ἀπόλλυμαι τάλας ἔτος τόδ᾽ ἤδη δέκατον now for these ten years, [Refs [[prev. author] “Ph.” 312]]; τῶνδε τῶν ἀσκητῶν athletes of the present day, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 403e.]]

__II.2
ἐς τόδε elliptic with genitive, ἐς τόδ᾽ ἡμέρας [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Phoenissae” 425; ἐς τόδε ἡλικίης 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 7.38]]; πῶς ἐς τόδ᾽ ἂν τόλμης ἔβ; [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Tyrannus” 125.]]

__III
in sentences beginning this is.., the Engl. this is frequently represented by nominative plural neuter τάδ; ἐπεὶ οὐκ ἔρανος τάδε γ᾽ ἐστίν this is not an ἔρανος, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 1.226]]; ἆρ᾽ οὐχ ὕβρις τάδ; is not this insolence? [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Coloneus” 883]]; of persons, Ἀπόλλων τάδ᾽ ἦν this was [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus, 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Tyrannus” 1329 (Lyric poetry); οὐ γὰρ ἔσθ᾽ Ἕκτωρ τάδε 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Andromache” 168; οὐκέτι Τροία τάδε [prev. author] “Tr.” 100 (_anapaest meter_); οὐ τάδε Βρόμιος [prev. author] “Cyc.” 63 (Lyric poetry); οὐκ Ἴωνες τάδε εἰσίν 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 6.77]]; τάδ᾽ οὐχὶ Πελοπόννησος, ἀλλ᾽ Ἰωνία Inscription cited in [Refs 1st c.BC+ [1st c.BC-1st c.AD: Strabo Geographus 9.1.6.]]

__III.2
to indicate something immediately to come, τόδε μοι κρήηνον ἐέλδωρ (which then follows) [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 1.41, 504, compare 455, +others; Ἀθηναίων οἵδε ἀπέθανον “IG” 12.943.2: hence, in historical writers, opposed to what goes before (compare οὗτος with 1.2), ταῦτα μὲν Λακεδαιμόνιοι λέγουσι.., τάδε δὲ ἐγὼ γράφω 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 6.53; ταῦτα μὲν δὴ σὺ λέγεις· παρ᾽ ἡμῶν δὲ ἀπάγγελλε τάδε 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 2.1.20, etc.]]; see at {οὗτος} [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Bacchylides Lyricus 1.2]]; opposed to ἐκεῖνος, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Electra” 784: rarely applied to different persons in the same sentence, νῦν ὅδε]] [La_us] πρὸς τῆς τύχης ὄλωλεν, οὐδὲ τοῦδ᾽ ὕπο [by Oedipus] [Refs [[prev. author] “OT” 948.]]

__III.3
as 'antecedent' to a defining Relat., ὃν πόλις στήσειε, τοῦδε χρὴ κλύειν [Refs 8th c.BC+ [[prev. author] “Ant.” 666, compare “Tr.” 23, “Ph.” 87, etc.: in 8th c.BC: Homerus Epicus, in such cases, the δέ]] is separate, as ὃς δέ κε μηρίνθοιο τύχῃ.., ὁ δ᾽ οἴσεται ἡμιπέλεκκα [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 23.858, compare 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 11.148, 149, +others (but ὅδε]] sometimes has its deictic force and the relative clause merely explains, as νήσου τῆσδ᾽ ἐφ᾽ ἧς ναίει [Refs 8th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Philoctetes” 613, compare 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 2.346, 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 7.3.47, etc.).]]

__IV
Adverbial usage of some cases:

__IV.1
τῇδε,

__IV.1.a
of Place, here, on the spot, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 12.345, 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 6.173, etc.; so τῶν τε ὑπὸ γῆς θεῶν καὶ τῶν τ. 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Leges” 958d.]]

__IV.1.b
of Manner, thus, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Eumenides” 45; ὅρα δὲ καὶ τ., ὅτι.. 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Phaedo” 79e, compare “R.” 433e, etc.]]

__IV.2
accusative neuter τόδε with ἱκάνω, etc., hither, to this spot, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 14.298, 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 1.409, +others; also δεῦρο τόδε 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 14.309, 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 17.444, 524.]]

__IV.2.b
therefore, on this account, τόδε χώεο [Refs [23.213]]: so also accusative plural neuter, τάδε γηθήσειε on this account, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 9.77.]]

__IV.3
dative plural neuter, τοισίδε in or with these words, τοισίδε ἀμείβεται [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.120]]; τοισίδε προέχει in these respects, [Refs [[prev. work] 32.]]

(obj.), ἐθνῶν, Mat.10:5; τ. ἁγίων (figuratively), Heb.9:8; accusative, ὁδόν, with force of prep. (like Heb. דֶּרֶךְ; Bl., §34, 8; 35, 5), ὁ. θαλάσσης, Mat.4:15 (LXX).
__2. A traveller's way, journey: ἐν τ. ὁ., Mat.5:25, Mrk.8:27, al.; ἐξ ὁ., Luk.11:6; εἰς ὁ., Mat.10:10; τ. ὁδὸν πορεύεσθαι, Act.8:39; ὁ. ἡμέρας, Luk.2:44; ὁδὸν ποιεῖν (= cl., ὁ. ποιεῖσθαι; V. Field, Notes, 25), to make one's way, i.e. proceed on one's journey, Mrk.2:23.

Βαλαάμ, 2Pe.2:15; εἰρήνης, Rom.3:17; ζωῆς, Act.2:28; ἡ ὁ. ἡ ἀπάγουσα εἰς τ. ζωήν (Dalman, Words, 160), Mat.7:14; τ. δικαιοσύνης, Mat.21:32; σωτηρίας, Act.16:17; αἱ ὁ. τ. θεοῦ (κυρίου), Act.13:10, Rom.11:33, Rev.15:3 (cf. 1. as Substantive Verb, to be, to exist , οὐκ ἔσθ᾽ οὗτος ἀνήρ, οὐδ᾽ ἔσσεται (Odyssey by Homer); τεθνηῶτος, μηδ᾽ ἔτ᾽ ἐόντος (Odyssey by Homer); οὐκέτ᾽ ἔστι he is no more , (Euripides); θεοὶ αἰὲν ἐόντες (Iliad by Homer); ἐσσόμενοι posterity, (Iliad by Homer); ζώντων καὶ ὄντων Ἀθηναίων (Demosthenes Orator):—;so of cities, etc., ὄλωλεν, οὐδ᾽ ἔτ᾽ ἔστι Τροία (compare Troja fuit) , (Euripides)
2. of things, to be, exist , εἰ ἔστιν ἀληθέως [ ἡ τράπεζα] (Herdotus Historicus); ἕως ἂν ὁ πόλεμος ἦι so long as it last , (Thucydides)
3. to be , opposite to appearing to be , as esse  to videri , τὸν ἐόντα λόγον the true  story, (Herdotus Historicus); τὰ ὄντα ἀπαγγέλλειν (Thucydides); τῶι ὄντι, Lat. revera, in reality, in fact, (Plato Philosophus)
4. followed by the Relative, οὐκ ἔστιν ὅς, no one , (Iliad by Homer), etc.; εἰσὶν οἵ, Lat. sunt qui, (Thucydides), etc.; ἐστὶν ἅ some things , (Thucydides); also ἔστιν οἵ, for εἰσὶν οἵ, (Herdotus Historicus), etc.:—;so withrelat. Particles, ἔστιν ἔνθα, Lat. est ubi, (Xenophon Historicus), etc.; ἔστιν ὅπη, ἔσθ᾽ ὅπου, somewhere , or somehow , (Plato Philosophus), etc.; ἔστιν ὅπως in some manner , (Herdotus Historicus), etc.; ἔστιν ὅτε, ἔσθ᾽ ὅτε, sometimes , (Sophocles Tragicus), etc.
5. ἔστι impersonal, with infinitive, like πάρεστι, it is possible , (Homer), attic
6. to be , Copula connecting predicate with subject, both being in the same case, (Homer), etc.
7. sometimes εἶναι with Part. represents finite Verb, ἦν τεθνηκώς, for ἐτεθνήκει, (Aeschulus Tragicus); πεφυκός ἐστι = πέφυκε, (Aristophanes Comicus)
8. the Inf. is redundant in some phrases, ἑκὼν εἶναι (see. ἑκών II); τὸ ἐπ᾽ ἐκείνοις εἶναι quantum in illis esset , (Thucydides); τὸ σύμπαν εἶναι (Herdotus Historicus); τὸ νῦν εἶναι (Plato Philosophus), etc. (ML)

__A
as the substantive Verb,

__A.I
of persons, exist, οὐκ ἔσθ᾽ οὗτος ἀνήρ, οὐδ᾽ ἔσσεται [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 16.437]]; ἔτ᾽ εἰσί they are still in being,[Refs 8th c.BC+ [15.433, compare 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Philoctetes” 445, etc.; τεθνηῶτος.. μηδ᾽ ἔτ᾽ ἐόντος 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 1.289]]; οὐκέτ᾽ ἐστί he is no more, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Hippolytus” 1162]]; οὐδὲ δὴν ἦν he was not long-lived, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 6.131]]; ὁ οὐκ ὤν, οἱ οὐκ ὄντες, of those who are no more, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 2.45, 44]]; οἱ ὄντες the living, [Refs 2nd c.BC+ [2nd c.BC: Polybius Historicus 9.29.2]]; ὁ ὤν the [LXX+8th c.BC+ [“Eternal”, LXX.Exo.3.14, +others, 1st c.AD: Philo Judaeus 1.289; θεοὶ αἰὲν ἐόντες 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 1.290]]; ἐσσόμενοι posterity,[Refs 5th c.BC+ [2.119; κἀγὼ γὰρ ἦ ποτ᾽, ἀλλὰ νῦν οὐκ εἴμ᾽ ἔτι 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Hecuba” 284]]; ὡς ἂν εἶεν ἅνθρωποι might continue in being, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Symposium” 190c; ζώντων καὶ ὄντων Ἀθηναίων 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 18.72, compare 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “de Generatione et Corruptione” 318b25]]; of things, εἰ ἔστι ἀληθέως [ἡ τράπεζα] [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 3.17, etc.]];
