__A.II
of the real world, be, opposed to become, γίγνεται πάντα ἃ δή φαμεν εἶναι [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Theaetetus” 152d, etc.]]; τὸ ὄν [Refs 5th c.BC+ [“Being”, 4th-5th c.BC: Parmenides Poeta Philosophus 8.35, 5th c.BC: Protagoras Philosophus 2, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Timaeus” 27d, etc.]]; opposed to τὸ μὴ ὄν, [LXX+5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Gorgias Rhetor et Sophista “fragment” 3 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator, etc.; οὐδὲν γίνεται ἐκ τοῦ μὴ ὄντος 4th-3rd c.BC: Epicurus Philosophus “Epistulae” 1p.5U.; ἐξ οὐκ ὄντων ἐποίησεν αὐτὰ ὁ θεός LXX.2Mac.7.28]]; τὰ ὄντα the world of things, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [1st c.AD(?): Heraclitus 7, 5th c.BC: Empedocles Poeta Philosophus 129.5, etc.]]; ὄνindeclinable, τῶν ὂν εἰδῶν species of Being, [Refs 3rd c.AD+ [3rd c.AD: Plotinus Philosophus 6.2.10.]]

__A.II.2
of circumstances, events, etc., to happen, τά τ᾽ ἐόντα, τά τ᾽ ἐσσόμενα, πρό τ᾽ ἐόντα [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 1.70; ἡ ἐσβολὴ ἔμελλεν ἔσεσθαι 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 2.13, etc.]]; τῆς προδοσίας οὔσης since treachery was there, [Refs [[prev. author] 4.103]]; ἕως ἂν ὁ πόλεμος ᾖ so long as it last, [Refs [[prev. author] 1.58; αἱ σπονδαὶ ἐνιαυτὸν ἔσονται [prev. author] 4.118]]; τί ἐστι; what is it? what's the matter? [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Thesmophoriazusae” 193]]; τί οὖν ἦν τοῦτ; how came it to pass? [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Phaedo” 58a: repeated with a _relative_ to avoid a positive assertion, ἔστι δ᾽ ὅπῃ νῦν ἔ.]] things are as they are, i.e. are ill, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Agamemnon” 67.]]

__A.III
be the fact or the case, διπλασίαν ἂν τὴν δύναμιν εἰκάζεσθαι ἤ ἐστιν twice as large as it really is, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 1.10]]; αὐτὸ ὅ ἐστι καλόν beauty in its essence, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Symposium” 211c, compare “Phd.” 74b]]; frequently in participle, τὸν ἐόντα λόγον λέγειν or φαίνειν the true story, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.95, 116]]; τῷ ἐόντι χρήσασθαι tell the truth,[Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. work] 30; τὰ ὄντα ἀπαγγέλλειν 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 7.8]]; σκῆψιν οὐκ οὖσαν, λόγον οὐκ ὄντα, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Electra” 584, 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Ranae” 1052]]; τῷ ὄντι in reality, in fact, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Protagoras” 328d, etc.]]; to apply a quotation to a case in point, τῷ ὄντι κλαυσίγελως real 'smiles through tears' (with allusion to [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 6.484), 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Historia Graeca (Hellenica)” 7.2.9, compare 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Laches” 196d]]; κατὰ τὸ ἐόν according to the fact, rightly, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.97]]; πᾶν τὸ ἐόν the whole truth, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. author] 9.11; τοῦ ἐόντος ἀποτεύξεται 5th c.BC: Hippocrates Medicus “περὶ ἀρχαίης ἰητρικῇς” 2.]]

__A.IV
followed by the relative, οὐκ ἔστιν ὅς or ὅστις no one, οὐκ ἔσθ᾽ ὃς.. ἀπαλάλκοι [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 22.348; οὐκ ἔ. οὐδεὶς ὅς 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Electra” 903]]; οὐκ ἔ. ὅτῳ, ={οὐδενί}, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Prometheus Vinctus” 293 (_anapaest meter_), compare 989: frequently in _plural_, εἰσὶν οἵ]], = Latin sunt qui, used exactly like{ἔνιοι}, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 6.88, 7.44, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Meno” 77d, “Grg.” 503a, etc. (εἰσί τινες οἵ.. 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 3.24)]]; ἐστὶν ἃ χωρία, πολίσματα, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. author] 1.12, 65; ἐστὶν ἃ εἰπεῖν [prev. author] 2.67; ἦσαν οἵ 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 5.2.14]]; the singular Verb is used even with masculine and feminine plural, ἐστὶν οἵ, αἵ, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Hippocrates Medicus “περὶ ἀγμῶν” 1, “VC” 4, 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 2.3.16]]; more frequently in oblique cases, ποταμῶν ἐστὶ ὧν [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 7.187; ἐστὶν ἀφ᾽ ὧν 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 8.65]]; ἐστὶ παρ᾽ οἷς, ἐστὶν ἐν οἷς, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. author] 1.23, 5.25: in questions ὅστις is used, ἔστιν ἥντινα δόξαν.. ἀπεκρίνατ; 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Meno” 85b: with _relative_ Particles, ἐστὶν ἔνθα]], = Latin est ubi, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 7.4.15, etc.]]; ἐ. ὅπῃ, ἔσθ᾽ ὅπου, somehow, somewhere, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Protagoras” 331d, 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Eumenides” 517, 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Tyrannus” 448, etc.]]; in questions expecting a negative answer, ἐ. ὁπόθεν, ὅπω; [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Philebus” 35a, “R.” 493e, etc.; οὐ γάρ ἐσθ᾽ ὅπως 5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “Fragmenta.” 61, compare 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 7.102, 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Agamemnon” 620]]; οὐκ ἔ. ὅπως οὐ in any case, necessarily, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Pax” 188; οὐκ ἔ. ὡς 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Meno” 76e, etc.]]; ἐ. ὅτε, ἔσθ᾽ ὅτε, sometimes, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “Fragmenta.” 180.2, 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Ajax” 56, 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 7.21, etc.]]

__A.V
ἦν is sometimes used with plural masculine and feminine, usually at the beginning of a sentence, there was, τῆς δ᾽ ἦν τρεῖς κεφαλαί [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th-7th c.BC: Hesiodus Epicus “Theogonia” 321; (but in ἦν δ᾽ ἐρῳδιοί τε πολλοί 5th c.BC: Epicharmus Comicus 46, compare 59, +others, it may be taken as _Doric dialect_ _3rd.pers._ _plural_)]]; ἦν δ᾽ ἀμφίπλεκτοι κλίμακες [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Trachiniae” 520 (Lyric poetry)]]; ἦν ἄρα κἀκεῖνοι ταλακάρδιοι epigram cited in [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aeschines Orator 3.184; less frequently ἔστι, ἔστι δὲ μεταξὺ.. ἑπτὰ στάδιοι 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.26, compare 7.34; ἔστι.. ἄρχοντές τε καὶ δῆμος 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 463a]]; before dual Nouns, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Vespae” 58, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Gorgias” 500d.]]

__A.VI
ἔστι impersonal, with infinitive, it is possible, ἔστι γὰρ ἀμφοτέροισιν ὀνείδεα μυθήσασθαι [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 20.246; ἔστι μὲν εὕδειν, ἔστι δὲ τερπομένοισιν ἀκούειν 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 15.392]]; εἴ τί πού ἐστι (i.e. πιθέσθαι)[Refs 5th c.BC+ [4.193; τοιάδε.. ἐστὶν ἀκοῦσαι 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Prometheus Vinctus” 1055 (_anapaest meter_); ἔστι τεκμήρια ὁρᾶν 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 3.2.13, compare 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Ranae” 1163, 4th c.BC: Aeschines Orator 3.105, 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 18.272, 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Ἀθηναίων Πολιτεία” 53.6, etc.]]; so in imperative, optative, and subjunctive, ἔστω ἀποφέρεσθαι τῷ βουλομένῳ [Refs 8th c.BC+ [“IG” 12.10.7; μυρία ἂν εἴη λέγειν 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Politicus” 271e; ὅπως ἂν ᾖ δρᾶν “IG” 2.1054.91: more frequently in _negative_ clauses, 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 6.267, etc.]]; followed by ὥστε with infinitive, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Philoctetes” 656]]: with accusative et infinitive, ἁδόντα δ᾽ εἴη με τοῖς ἀγαθοῖς ὁμιλεῖν [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “P.” 2.96; ἔστιν ἐκπεσεῖν ἀρχῆς Δία 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Prometheus Vinctus” 757]]: sometimes not impersonal in this sense, θάλασσα δ᾽ οὐκέτ᾽ ἦν ἰδεῖν [Refs [[prev. author] “Pers.” 419.]]

__A.VI.b
ἔστω in argument, let it be granted, ἔστω τοῦτο ἀληθὲς εἶναι [Refs 4th c.BC+ [1st c.BC: Dionysius Halicarnassensis “de Compositione Verborum” 25; ἔστω σοι τοῦθ᾽ οὕτως 1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus 2.987b; ἔστω εἶναί τινα τοιοῦτον 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator Chr.74.24.]]

__B
most frequently, to be, the Copula connecting the predicate with the Subject, both being in the same case: hence, signify, import, τὸ γὰρ εἴρειν λέγειν ἐστίν [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Cratylus” 398d]]; especially in the phrase τοῦτ᾽ ἔστι, hoc est; Σκαιόλαν, ὅπερ ἐστὶ Λαϊόν [Refs 1st c.AD+ [1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus “Publicola” 17: with numerals, τὰ δὶς πέντε δέκα ἐστίν]] twice five are ten, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Memorabilia” 4.4.7]]; εἶναί τις or τι, to be somebody, something, be of some consequence, see at {τι; οὐδὲν εἶναι} [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 562d, etc.]]

__B.2
periphrastic with the Participle to represent the finite Verb: with perfect participle once in [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Homerus Epicus, τετληότες εἰμέν, for τετλήκαμεν, 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 5.873]]; so in Trag. and Attic dialect, ἦν τεθνηκώς, for ἐτεθνήκει, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Agamemnon” 869]]; ἔσται δεδορκώς[Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. work] 1179; εἰμὶ γεγώς 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Ajax” 1299; πεφυκός ἐστι 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Aves” 1473; δεδρακότες εἰσίν 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 3.68; κατακεκονότες ἔσεσθε 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 7.6.36]]: with aorist participle, once in [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Homerus Epicus, βλήμενος ἦν 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 4.211]]; so προδείσας εἰμί, οὐ σιωπήσας ἔσε; [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Tyrannus” 90, 1146, compare 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Supplices” 460]]: with present participle, ἦν προκείμενον [Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. author] “Pers.” 371; φεύγων Ὀρέστης ἐστίν [prev. author] “Ch.” 136; εἴην οὐκ ἂν εὖ φρονῶν 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Ajax” 1330]]; τί δ᾽ ἐστί.. φέρο; [Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. author] “OT” 991, compare 274, 708; λέγων ἐστίν τις 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Hecuba” 1179; ἦν τίς σ᾽ ὑβρίζων [prev. author] “HF” 313; πόρρω ἤδη εἶ πορευόμενος 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Lysis” 204b; βαδίζων εἰμί 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Ranae” 36; frequently in 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus, ἦσαν ἱέντες 1.57, +others; even εἰσὶ διάφοροι ἐόντες 3.49 (assuming variant):]] — if the _Article_ is joined with the Part., the noun is made emphatic, Κᾶρές εἰσι οἱ καταδέξαντες the persons who showed her were Carians, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. author] 1.171; αὐτὸς ἦν ὁ μαρτυρῶν 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Eumenides” 798; δόλος ἦν ὁ φράσας 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Electra” 197 (_anapaest meter_).]]

__C
εἶναι is frequently modified in sense by the addition of adverbs, or the cases of Nouns without or with Preps.:

__C.I
εἶναι with adverbs, where the adverb often merely represents a Noun and stands as the predicate, ἅλις δέ οἱ ἦσαν ἄρουραι [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 14.122, etc.]]; ἀκέων, ἀκήν εἶναι, to be silent,[Refs 8th c.BC+ [4.22, 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 2.82; σῖγα πᾶς ἔστω λεώς 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Hecuba” 532; διαγνῶναι χαλεπῶς ἦν ἄνδρα ἕκαστον 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 7.424]]; ἀσφαλέως ἡ κομιδὴ ἔσται will go on safely, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 4.134]]; ἐγγύς, πόρρω εἶναι, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 6.88, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Protagoras” 356e: frequently _impersonal_ with words implying good or ill fortune, Κουρήτεσσι κακῶς ἦν]] it fared ill with them, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 9.551; εὖ γὰρ ἔσται 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Medea” 89, compare 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Plutus” 1188, etc.; ἡδέως ἂν αὐτοῖς εἴη 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 59.30.]]

__C.II
with genitive, to express descent or extraction, πατρὸς δ᾽ εἴμ᾽ ἀγαθοῖο [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 21.109; αἵματός εἰς ἀγαθοῖο 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 4.611, compare 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 3.71, 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 2.71, etc.; πόλεως μεγίστης εἶ 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 7.3.19.]]

__C.II.b
to express the material of which a thing is made, ἡ κρηπίς ἐστι λίθων μεγάλων consists of.., [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.93; τῆς πόλιος ἐούσης δύο φαρσέων [prev. work] 186]]; τοιούτων ἔργων ἐστὶ ἡ τυραννίς is made up of.., [Refs [[prev. author] 5.92]].ή, etc.

__C.II.c
to express the class to which a person or thing belongs, εἶ γὰρ τῶν φίλων you are one of them, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Plutus” 345; ἐτύγχανε βουλῆς ὤν 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 3.70; ὅσοι ἦσαν τῶν προτέρων στρατιωτῶν [prev. author] 7.44; Κριτίας τῶν τριάκοντα ὤν 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Memorabilia” 1.2.31]]; ἔστι τῶν αἰσχρῶν it is in the class of disgraceful things, i. e. it is disgraceful, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 2.2.]]

__C.II.d
to express that a thing belongs to another, Τροίαν Ἀχαιῶν οὖσαν [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Agamemnon” 269; τὸ πεδίον ἦν μέν κοτε Χορασμίων 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 3.117, etc.]]: hence, to be of the party of, ἦσαν.. τινὲς μὲν φιλίππου, τινὲς δὲ τοῦ βελτίστου [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 9.56, compare 37.53]]; to be de pendent upon, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Antigone” 737, etc.]]; to be at the mercy of, ἔστι τοῦ λέγοντος, ἢν φόβους λέγῃ [Refs [[prev. author] “OT” 917.]]

__C.II.e
to express one's duty, business, custom, nature, and the like, οὔτοι γυναικός ἐστι 'tis not a woman's part, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Agamemnon” 940; τὸ ἐπιτιμᾶν παντὸς εἶναι 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 1.16]]; τὸ δὲ ναυτικὸν τέχνης ἐστίν is matter of art, requires art, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 1.142, compare 83.]]

__C.II.f
in LXX, to be occupied about, ἦσαν τοῦ θύειν [LXX.2Ch.30.17]; ἔσεσθαι, with genitive, to be about to, ἐσόμεθα τοῦ σῶσαί σε [LXX.2Ki.10.11.]

__C.III
with the dative, ἐστί μοι I have, frequently in [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Homerus Epicus, etc.]]

__C.III.2
with two datives., σφίσι τε καὶ Ἀθηναίοισι εἶναι οὐδὲν πρῆγμα that they and the Athenians have nothing to do one with another, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 5.84; μηδὲν εἶναι σοὶ καὶ φιλίππῳ πρᾶγμα 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 18.283]]; more shortly, σοί τε καὶ τούτοισι πρήγμασι τί ἐστ; [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 5.33]]; τί τῷ νόμῳ καὶ τῇ βασάν; [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 29.36]]; τί ἐμοὶ καὶ σο; Latin quid tecum est mihi? [NT.Mark.5.7, etc.]; also ἐμοὶ οὐδὲν πρὸς τοὺς τοιούτους (i.e. ἐστίν) [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Isocrates Orator 4.12; ἐν οἷς πρὸς τοὺς ἐναντίους ἐστὶ τῷ δήμῳ 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 18.278]]; ἔσται αὐτῳ πρὸς τὸν θεόν, in tomb inscriptions, [Refs [“JHS” 18.113, etc.]]

__C.III.3
with ἄσμενος, βουλόμενος, etc., added, ἐμοὶ δέ κεν ἀσμένῳ εἴη 'twould be to my delight, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 14.108; οὐκ ἂν σφίσι βουλομένοις εἶναι 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 7.35; προσδεχομένῳ [prev. author] 6.46; θέλοντι 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Tyrannus” 1356 (Lyric poetry); ἡδομένοις 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Laches” 187c.]]

__C.IV
with Preps., εἶναι ἀπό τινος, ={εἶναί τινος}[Refs 5th c.BC+ [(above 11.a), 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Memorabilia” 1.6.9; εἰσὶν ἀπ᾽ ἐναντίων αὗται πραγμάτων 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Philebus” 12d]]; but εἶναι ἀπ᾽ οἴκου to be away from.., [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 1.99.]]

__C.IV.2
εἶναι ἔκ τινος to be sprung from, εἴμ᾽ ἐκ Παιονίης, Μυρμιδόνων ἔξ εἰμι, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 21.154, 24.397, etc.]]; ἔστιν ἐξ ἀνάγκης it is of necessity, i. e. necessary, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Sophista” 256d.]]

__C.IV.3
εἶναι ἐν.. to be in a certain state, ἐν εὐπαθείῃσι [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.22]]; ἐν ἀθυμία, etc., [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 6.46, etc.; ἐν ταραχαῖς 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 18.218]]; εἶναι ἐν ἀξιώματι to be in esteem, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 1.130]]; οἱ ἐν τέλεϊ ἐόντες those in office, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 3.18, etc.]]; but εἶναι ἐν τέχνῃ, ἐν φιλοσοφία to be engaged in.., [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Tyrannus” 562, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Phaedo” 59a.]]

__C.IV.3.b
ἐν σοί ἐστι it depends on thee, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 6.109, 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Philoctetes” 963; ἐν σοὶ γάρ ἐσμεν [prev. author] “OT” 314; so also ἐπί τινι [prev. author] “Ph.” 1003, 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 1.6.2, etc.]]

__C.IV.4
εἶναι διά.., much like{εἶναι ἐν}.., εἶναι διὰ φόβου, ={φοβεῖσθαι}, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 6.34]]; εἶναι δι᾽ ὄχλου, ={ὀχληρὸν εἶναι}, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. author] 1.73; εἶναι διὰ μόχθων 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 1.6.25]]; εἶναι δι᾽ αἰτίας, ={αἰτιᾶσθαι}, [Refs 1st c.BC+ [1st c.BC: Dionysius Halicarnassensis 1.70]]; Geometry texts, pass through, διὰ τᾶς ἑτέρας διαμέτρου ἐόντος τοῦ ἐπιπέδου [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [3rd c.BC: Archimedes Geometra “περὶ κωνοειδέων καὶ σφαιροειδέων” 20.]]

__C.IV.5
εἶναι ἐφ᾽ ἑαυτῆς to be by oneself, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 25.23]]; εἶναι ἐπὶ ὀνόματος to bear a name, [Refs [[prev. author] 39.21]]; εἶναι ἐπὶ τοῖς πράγμασιν to be engaged in.., [Refs [[prev. author] 2.12]]; εἶναι ἐπί τινα to be against him, [Refs [[prev. author] 6.33]]; εἶναι ἐφ᾽ ἑξήκοντα στάδια to reach sixty stadia, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 4.6.11]]; εἶναι ἐπὶ τὰς ἁφάς pass through the points of contact, [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd c.AD: Apollonius Biographus Perg. “Con.” 4.1]]; εἶναι ἐπί τινι, see above 3 b.

__C.IV.6
εἶναι πρός τινος to be in one's favour, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 4.10, 29, etc.]]; to suit, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 1.2.11, etc.]]; εἶναι πρός τινι engaged in, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Phaedo” 84c, 2nd-3rd c.AD: Philostratus Sophista “Vita Apollonii” 5.31]]; πρὸς τοῖς ἰδίοις mind one's own affairs, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Politica” 1309a6, “Ath.” 16.3; εἶναι πρὸς τὸ κωλύειν 2nd c.BC: Polybius Historicus 1.26.3]]; πρὸς τὸ πονεῖν[Refs 5th c.BC+ [Teles p.46 H.; εἶναι περί τι 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 3.5.7, etc.]]

__C.IV.7
εἶναι παρά τινι or τινα, = παρειναι, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. author] “Cyr.” 6.2.15, 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 8.140.ά]] (assuming variant).

__C.IV.8
εἶναι ὑπό τινα or τινι to be subject to.., [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Historia Graeca (Hellenica)” 5.2.17 (assuming variant), 6.2.4.]]

__C.IV.9
περὶ τούτων ἐστίν that is the question, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-3rd c.BC: Menander Comicus “Ἐπιτρέποντες” 30.]]

__C.IV.10
εἶναι ἀπό.., in Geometry texts, to be constructed upon, [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [3rd c.BC: Archimedes Geometra “περὶ σφαίρας καὶ κυλίνδρου” 2.9, “Con.Sph.” 7.]]

__D
ἐστί is very frequently omitted, mostly in the present indicative before certain predicates, as ἀνάγκη, ἄξιον, δυνατόν, εἰκός, ἕτοιμον, οἷόν τε, ῥᾴδιον, χρεών, etc., and after the neuter of Verbals in -τέος, and such forms as θαυμαστὸν ὅσον: less frequently with other persons and moods, εἰμί omitted, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Tyrannus” 92, “Aj.” 813]]; εἶ, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 4.206]]; ἐσμέν, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Antigone” 634]]; ἐστέ, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 10.463]]; εἰσί, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Tyrannus” 499 (Lyric poetry), “IG” 2.778 B]]; subjunctive ᾖ, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 14.376, 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Hippolytus” 659, 5th c.BC: Antipho Orator 5.32]]; optative εἴη, [Refs [“IG” 22.1183.12]]; imperfect ἦν, [Refs [[prev. work]2.778 B]]; future ἔσονται, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 14.394.]]

__E
the Inf. frequently seems redundant,

__E.1
in phrases implying power or will to do a thing, ἑκὼν εἶναι (see. ἑκών) κατὰ δύναμιν εἶναι [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Isaeus Orator 2.32; εἰς δύναμιν εἶναι 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Politicus” 300c]]; τὸ ἐπ᾽ ἐκείνοις εἶναι, quantum in illis esset, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 8.48, 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Historia Graeca (Hellenica)” 3.5.9, compare 5th c.BC: Lysias Orator 13.58; τὸ ἐπὶ σφᾶς εἶναι 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 4.28; τὸ κατὰ τοῦτον εἶναι 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 1.6.9; κατὰ τοῦτο εἶναι 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Protagoras” 317a]]; τὸ τήμερον, τὸ νῦν εἶναι, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [[prev. author] “Cra.” 396e, “La.” 201c, Theopomp. Comedy texts 98, Decrees cited in 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Ἀθηναίων Πολιτεία” 31.2, etc.]]

__E.2
after Verbs of naming or choosing, σοφιστὴν ὀνομάζουσι τὸν ἄνδρα εἶναι [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Protagoras” 311e; σύμμαχόν μιν εἵλοντο εἶναι 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 8.134]]; of giving, δῶκε ξεινήϊον εἶναι [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 11.20.]]

__F
imperfect ἦνissts. used where other languages take the present,

__F.1
after ἄρα, to express a fact which is and has always been the same, δέρμα δὲ ἀνθρώπου.. ἦν ἄρα σχεδὸν δερμάτων πάντων λαμπρότατον human skin then it appears is.., [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 4.64; Κύπρις οὐκ ἄρ᾽ ἦν θεός 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Hippolytus” 359]]; ὡς ἄρ᾽ ἦσθ᾽ ἐμὸς πατὴρ ὀρθῶς[Refs 3rd c.BC+ [[prev. work] 1169; ἦ πολύμοχθον ἄρ᾽ ἦν γένος.. ἁμερίων [prev. author] “IA” 1330; ἦ στωμύλος ἦσθα 3rd c.BC: Theocritus Poeta Bucolicus 5.79]]; so also when there is reference to a past thought, τουτὶ τί ἦ; what is this? [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Acharnenses” 157, compare 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Cratylus” 387c: so in the Aristotelian formula τὸ τί ἦν εἶναι (“APo.” 82b38, +others)]], used to express the essential nature of a thing, where τί ἦν (for ἐστί) takes the place of the dative in such phrases as τὸ ἀγαθῷ εἶναι, τὸ μεγέθει εἶναι, [Refs [“APr.” 67b12, “de An.” 429b10.]]

__G
ἐγώ εἰμι, in [LXX, pleonastic for ἐγώ, ἐγώ εἰμι οὐχ ἥμαρτον LXX.Judg.11.27, compare 6.18; also ἔσται πᾶς ἀποκτενεῖ με LXX.Gen.4.14.]

Abbott-Smith / STEPBible (TBESG)
ὄζω
[in LXX: Exo.8:14 (בָּאַשׁ)* ;]
to smell (i.e. emit a smell): Jhn.11:39.†
(AS)

---

LSJ / STEPBible (TFLSJ)
ὄζω,
Doric dialect ὄσδω [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [3rd c.BC: Theocritus Poeta Bucolicus 1.149 (compare also III below)]]: imperfect ὦζε [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Crates Comicus 2 (conjecture Pors. for ὦ Ζεῦ)]]: future ὀζήσω [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Vespae” 1059]]; Ionic dialect ὀζέσω [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Hippocrates Medicus “περὶ ἐπικυήσιος” 25, “Geoponica” 12.29.5, 12th c.AD: Eustathius Episcopus Thessalonicensis 1523.39, “Anecdota Graeca - MSS. Bibl. Oxon.” 2.396]]: aorist ὤζησα [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Fragmenta” 635]]; Ionic dialect ὤζεσα [LXX+5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Hippocrates Medicus “περὶ ἐπικυήσιος” 25, LXX.Exo.8.14(10)]]: perfect ὤζηκα [Refs 9th c.AD+ [9th c.AD: Photius Legal icographus, etc.]]; but perfect with present sense ὄδωδα [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [3rd c.BC: Phylarchus Historicus 10 1st c.AD: Josephus Historicus, “Anthologia Graeca” 7.30 (Antip. Sid.), 1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus 2.916d, 2nd c.AD: Aretaeus Medicus “περὶ αἰτιῶν καὶ σημείων ὀξέων παθῶν” 1.9]]: pluperfect as imperfect ὠδώδειν [Refs 1st c.AD+ [1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus “Alexander” 20]]; Epic dialect ὀδώδειν (see. below):—smell, whether smell sweet or stink, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Homerus Epicus]] only in 3rd.pers. singular pluperfect with sense of imperfect, ὀδμὴ κέδρου.. ἀνὰ νῆσον ὀδώδει [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 5.60; ὀδμὴ δ᾽ ἡδεῖα ἀπὸ κρητῆρος ὀδώδει, of wine, 9.210]]: later with genitive of things, frequently with neuter adjective or adverb added, smell of a thing, τόδ᾽ ὄζει θυμάτων [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Agamemnon” 1310; ὄζων τρυγός 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Nubes” 50; βύρσης κάκιστον ὄζων [prev. author] “Eq.” 892, compare “V.” 38; also ὠδώδει ὑπὸ μύρων ὁ οἶκος 1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus “Alexander” 20]]: metaphorically, smell or savour of a thing, Κρονίων ὄζων smelling of musty antiquity, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Nubes” 398, compare 1007, “Ach.” 192, “Lys.” 616; καλοκἀγαθίας 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Symposium” 2.4]]; that from which the smell comes is also in genitive, ὄζων κακὸν τῶν μασχαλῶν [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Acharnenses” 852; τοῦ στόματος 5th c.BC: Pherecrates Comicus 67: so with double _genitive_, τῆς κεφαλῆς ὄζω μύρου 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Ecclesiazusae” 524; see below 11.]]

__II
frequently impersonal, ὄζει ἀπ᾽ αὐτῆς ὡσεὶ ἴων there is a smell from it as of violets, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 3.23]]; ὄζει ἡδὺ τῆς χρόας there is a sweet smell from the skin, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Plutus” 1020; τῆς γῆς ὡς γλυκὺ ὄζει 4th c.BC: Cratinus Junior Comicus 1]]; ὄζειν ἐδόκει τοῦ ἄρτου καὶ τῆς μάζης κάκιστον there seemed to be a most foul smell from.., [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Lysias Orator 6.1]]; οὐκ ὄζει αὐτῶν (i.e. τῶν λαγῶν) no scent of the hares remains, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Cynegeticus” 5.1, compare 7: with double _genitive_, ἱματίων ὀζήσει δεξιότητος]] there will be an odour of cleverness from your clothes, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Vespae” 1059, compare “Pax” 529; ἀπὸ στόματος.. ὄζει ἴων, ὄζει δὲ ῥόδων, ὄζει δ᾽ ὑακίνθου 5th c.BC: Hermippus Comicus 82.8; ὄζει ἐκ τοῦ στόματος μελικήρας 5th c.BC: Pherecrates Comicus 25.]]

__III
middle, κακὸν ὀζόμενος, for ὄζων, [Refs 6th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Hippocrates Medicus “περὶ τόπων τῶν κατὰ ἄνθρωπον” 12; οἶνος.. ἄνθεος ὀσδόμενος 6th c.BC: Xenophanes Poeta Philosophus 1.6; δριμὺ ὀσδομένου τοῦ σώματος “PSI” 4.297.3 (ca. 5th c.AD)]]. (Cf. Latin odor, Lithuanian uodžiu 'I smell'.)

Abbott-Smith / STEPBible (TBESG)
ὅθεν
adv.,
whence;
__(a) of direction or source: Mat.12:44, Luk.11:24, Act.14:26 28:13; = ἐκεῖθεν ὅπου, Mat.25:24, 26 (cf. Thuc., i, 89, 3); ὅ. γινώσκομεν, 1Jn.2:18;
__(b) of cause, whence, wherefore: Mat.14:7, Act.26:19, Heb.2:17 3:1 7:25 8:3 9:18 11:19.†
(AS)

---

LSJ / STEPBible (TFLSJ)
ὅθεν,
relative adverb whence, ὑπὸ πλατανίστῳ, ὅ. ῥέεν ἀγλαὸν ὕδωρ [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 2.307]]; ἐξ Ἐνετῶν, ὅ. ἡμιόνων γένος[Refs [[prev. work] 852; γένος δέ μοι ἔνθεν, ὅ. σοί 4.58, etc.; πόλεως ὅθεν εἶ “IG” 12(5).310.2 (from Paros)]]; also, from whom or which, ὅθεν περ Ὁμηρίδαι ἄρχονται, Διὸς ἐκ προοιμίου [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “N.” 2.1; τὴν τεκοῦσαν.., ὅθεν περ αὐτὸς ἐσπάρη 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Tyrannus” 1498; Φοῖνιξ, ὅθεν περ τοὔνομ᾽ ἡ χώρα φέρει 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Fragmenta” 819.8: followed by Particles, ὅθεν περ (see. above)]]; ὅθεν δή [Refs 8th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Supplices” 15 (_anapaest meter_); ὅθεν τε 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 4.358.]]

__b
in Attic dialect Prose, ὅθεν δή from whatever source, in what manner soever, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Phaedrus” 267d; so ὁθενδήποτε Dosith. p.410 K.]]; also ἄλλοθεν ὁθενοῦν from any other place whatsoever, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Leges” 738c.]]

__2
for where or whither, by attraction, when the antecedent clause contains a notion of place whence, ἐκ δὲ γῆς, ὅ. προὔκειτ᾽ from the ground where it lay, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Trachiniae” 701]]; ὅ... ἀπέλιπες, ἀποκρίνου answer [from the point] where you left off, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Gorgias” 497c; διεκομίζοντο.. ὅ. ὑπεξέθεντο παῖδας καὶ γυναῖκας 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 1.89]]; ὅθεν, ={ἐκεῖσε ὅθεν}, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 1.3.17, 7.6.12, etc.]]; ὅθεν περ, ={ἐκεῖθεν ὅθεν περ}, [Refs [“IG” 12.78.9,88.23.]]

__II
whence, for which reason, σφυρῶν.. κέντρα διαπείρας μέσον, ὅ. νιν Ἑλλὰς ὠνόμαζεν Οἰδίπουν [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Phoenissae” 27, compare 5th c.BC: Antipho Sophista 54, 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Ἀθηναίων Πολιτεία” 3.2, “IG” 22.1011.42, +others; ὅ... ἱδρύσαθ᾽ ἱερόν 2nd c.AD: Alexander Rhetor 267.4]]; for what reason, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Protagoras” 319b; ὅ. ἠνάγκασμαι κατηγορεῖν αὐτῶν, περὶ τούτων πρῶτον εἰπεῖν βούλομαι 5th c.BC: Lysias Orator 22.1.]]

LSJ / STEPBible (TFLSJ)
οἰκεῖος, α, ον,
also ος, ον [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Heraclidae” 634]]; Ionic dialect οἰκήϊος, η, ον: in or of the house, once in [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th-7th c.BC: Hesiodus Epicus, δούρατ᾽ ἀμάξης οἰκήϊα θέσθαι “Op.” 457; λέβης 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Fragmenta - American Journal of Philology” 1; κῆρυξ 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Trachiniae” 757]]; of or for household affairs, domestic (for οἰκηΐη, see at {οἰκία} II), τὰ οἰ. household affairs, property, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 2.37, 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Antigone” 661; τὰ οἰ. ἀγαθά 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Oeconomicus” 9.18]]; τὰ οἰ. τὰ αὑτοῦ his household goods, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Lysias Orator 13.41]]; opposed to πολιτικά, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 2.40]]; opposed to τὰ τῆς πόλεως, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Apologia” 23b.]]

__2
Astrology texts, οἰ. ζῴδια domiciliary signs, [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd c.AD: Vettius Valens Astrologus 37.21, +others]]

__II
of persons, of the same household, family, or kin, related, ὥς οἱ ἐόντες οἰκήϊοι as being akin to him, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 4.65]]; οἰκεῖον οὕτως οὐδὲν.. ὡς ἀνήρ τε καὶ γυνή so closely akin, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-3rd c.BC: Menander Comicus 647]]; ἀνὴρ οἰ. kinsman, relative, near friend, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.108]]; οἱ οἰ. kinsmen, opposed to οἱ ἀλλότριοι, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Andocides Orator 4.15, compare 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 2.51]]; opposed to ὀθνεῖοι, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Protagoras” 316c]]; οἱ ἑωυτοῦ οἰκηϊότατοι his own nearest kinsmen, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 3.65, compare 5.5, 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 18.288]]; of the tie itself, κατὰ τὸ οἰ. Ἀτρεῖ because of his relationship to Atreus, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 1.9.]]

__II.2
friendly, εἴχομέν ποτε.. τὸν τόπον τοῦτον οἰ. [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 4.4; οὓς ἂν ἡγήσαιτο -οτάτους τε καὶ ἑταιροτάτους 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Phaedo” 89e.]]

__III
of things. belonging to one's house or family, one's own (defined as ὅταν ἐφ᾽ αὑτῷ ᾖ ἀπαλλοτριῶσαι [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Rhetorica” 1361a21), οἰ. ἄρουραι 5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “O.” 12.19; σταθμοῖς ἐν οἰκείοισι 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Prometheus Vinctus” 398]]; γῆ, χθών, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Ajax” 859, “Ant.” 1203]]; οἰκεῖον, ἢ 'ξ ἄλλου τινό; born in the house, or.. ? [Refs [[prev. author] “OT” 1162]]; αἱ οἰ. πόλεις their own cities, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Historia Graeca (Hellenica)” 3.5.2]]; ἡ οἰ. (i.e. γῆ), Ionic dialect ἡ οἰκηΐη [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.64]]; [ἀναθήματα] οἰκήϊα his own property, [Refs [[prev. work] 92]]; πόλεμοι οἰ. wars in one's own country, of the Helot war in Laconia, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 1.118, compare 4.64; σῖτος οἰ. καὶ οὐκ ἐπακτός]]homegrown, [Refs [[prev. author] 6.20.]]

__III.2
={ἴδιος}, one's own, personal, private, οἰκείων κερδέων εἵνεκα [Refs 6th c.BC+ [6th c.BC: Theognis Elegiacus 46; ἐὼν ἐν κακῷ οἰκηΐῳ 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.45, compare 153, 5th c.BC: Antipho Orator 1.13; αἱ χεῖρες -ότεραι τοῦ σιδήρου [prev. author] 4.3.3]]; μηδὲν -οτέρᾳ τῇ ἀπολαύσει with enjoyment not more our own, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 2.38, compare 7.70; ἀλλοτρίας γῆς πέρι οἰ. κίνδυνον ἔχειν [prev. author] 3.13]]; οἰ. ξύνεσις mother wit, [Refs [[prev. author] 1.138]]; πρὸς οἰκείας χερός by his own hand, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Antigone” 1176, etc.; for 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Agamemnon” 1220, see at {βορά}.]]

__III.2.b
in Stoic Philos., endeared by nature to all animals, including man, τὸ πρῶτον οἰ. what is earliest endeared, [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [3rd c.BC: Chrysippus Stoicus 3.43, 4th c.AD(?): Hierocles Facetiarum Scriptor p.7A.]]

__IV
proper to a thing, fitting, suitable, οὔτε.. καλὸν οὐδὲν [οὐδ᾽] οἰκήϊον [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 3.81, compare 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 18.59.]]

__IV.2
with dative of things, belonging to, conformable to the nature of a thing, προοίμιον οἰ. ἑκάστῳ [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Leges” 772e, compare “R.” 468d, +others, and frequently in 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus, as “EN” 1098a29: also with _genitive_, τὰ αὐτῶν οἰ. 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Phaedo” 96d; οἰ. τῆς διαλεκτικῆς 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Topica” 101b2, compare “EN” 1096b31, “Rh.” 1360a22; οἰ. πρός τι 2nd c.BC: Polybius Historicus 5.105.1.]]

__IV.2.b
of persons, with genitive, a student of.., σοφίας [Refs 1st c.BC+ [1st c.BC-1st c.AD: Strabo Geographus 17.1.5]]; addicted to, καινοτομίας [Refs 4th c.AD+ [4th c.AD: Iamblichus Philosophus “de vita Pythagorica” 30.176.]]

__IV.3
proper, fit, οἰ. κατάγελως fit subject for ridicule, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-3rd c.BC: Menander Comicus 160]]; οἰ. ὄνομα a word in its proper, literal sense, opposed to metaphor, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Rhetorica” 1404b35.]]

__B
adverb οἰκείως has the same senses as the adjective, οἰ φέρε bear it like your own affair, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Thesmophoriazusae” 197]]; διαλέγεσθαι οἰ. τινί converse familiarly with him, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 6.57; οἰ. χρῆσθαί τινι]]to be on familiar terms, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Historia Graeca (Hellenica)” 2.3.16; οἰ. διακεῖσθαί τινι [prev. author] “An.” 7.5.16; πρός τι 2nd c.BC: Polybius Historicus 13.1.2; οἰ. δέχεσθαί τινας 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 18.215; οἰ. ἔχειν τινί [prev. author] 4.4, etc.]]: comparative -ότερον[Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Isaeus Orator 1.49]]; -οτέρως [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Categoriae” 7a16]]: superlative -ότατα[Refs 2nd c.BC+ [2nd c.BC: Polybius Historicus 5.106.4.]]

__B.II
properly, naturally, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Lysistrata” 1118, 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Oeconomicus” 2.17]]; opposed to ἀλλοτρίως, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-3rd c.BC: Epicurus Philosophus “Epistulae” 1p.14U.]]

__B.II.2
affectionately, dutifully, ἔθαψε, περιέστειλεν οἰ. [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th-3rd c.BC: Menander Comicus 325.12, compare 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 2.60.]]

__B.II.3
literally, actually, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [2nd c.AD: Galenus Medicus “φιλόσοφος ἱστορία - Doxographi Graeci” 39 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator]]

__B.II.4
Astrology texts, οἰ. σχηματίζεσθαι, of a planet, to be in its domicile, [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd c.AD: Vettius Valens Astrologus 58.27, +others]]

οἰκέτ-ης, ου, ὁ,
(οἶκος) household slave, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Choephori” 737, 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 6.137, 7.170, 5th c.BC: Antipho Orator 1.30, 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 2.4; δημόσιος οἰ. τῆς πόλεως 4th c.BC: Aeschines Orator 1.54.]]

οἱ οἰκέται also, ={οἰκετεία}, household, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Agamemnon” 732 (Lyric poetry), 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 8.4, 106, 142, 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Trachiniae” 908, 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 4.2.2: hence opposed to δοῦλοι, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Leges” 763a, 777a, 853e; διαφέρειν φησὶ Χρύσιππος δοῦλον οἰκέτου, διὰ τὸ τοὺς ἀπελευθέρους μὲν δούλους ἔτι εἶναι, οἰκέτας δὲ τοὺς μὴ τῆς κτήσεως ἀφειμένους “Stoicorum Veterum Fragmenta” 3.86: but frequently synonymous with δοῦλος, 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Politica” 1252b12, +others, “PLille” 29.2 (3rd c.BC), “IG” 5(1).1390.77 (Andania, 1st c.BC)]]; δοῦλος μεῖζον οἰκέτου φρονῶν [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-3rd c.BC: Menander Comicus 796.]]

as epithet of Apollo, ἱερέως.. Καρνείου Βοικέτα [Β = ϝ] [Refs [“IG” 5(1).497, compare 589,608 (from Sparta). (Cf. οἰκότης.)]]

(οἶκος), [in LXX chiefly for יָשַׁב ;]

LSJ / STEPBible (TFLSJ)
οἰκέω,
Epic dialect οἰκείω [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th-7th c.BC: Hesiodus Epicus “Theogonia” 330]], Locrian dialect ϝοικέω [Refs [“IG” 9(1).334.29]]; Aeolic dialect present participle οἴκεις [Refs 7th c.BC+ [7th-6th c.BC: Alcaeus Lyricus 69]]; argument 3rd.pers. singular present optative οἰκείη [Refs [“BCH” 33.452]]: imperfect ᾤκεον [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 20.218, +others, _Attic dialect_ ᾤκουν,]] Ionic dialect οἴκεον [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.57]]: future οἰκήσω [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Iphigenia Aulidensis” 1508 (Lyric poetry)]]: aorist ᾤκησα [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.1]]: perfect ᾤκηκα [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Electra” 1101:]] — passive and middle, future οἰκήσομαι in middle sense,[Refs 5th c.BC+ [Men.Rh. p.363 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus]]; but in passive, see [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus 11]]: aorist ᾠκήθην [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 2.668, etc.; ᾠκησάμην 2nd c.AD: Aristides Rhetor 1.103 1st c.AD: Josephus Historicus:]]perfect ᾤκημαι as middle and passive, Ionic dialect 3rd.pers. plural οἰκέαται, see [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus 1.2]], 3: (οἶκος):

__A
transitive, inhabit, ὑπωρείας ᾤκεον πολυπίδακος Ἴδης [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 20.218 (elsewhere in 8th c.BC: Homerus Epicus always _intransitive_, see infr. B)]]; οἰ. τοῦτον τὸν χῶρον [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.1, compare 175, etc.; οἰ. δόμους 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Supplices” 961; ἄντρον [prev. author] “Eu.” 194: _metaphorically_, οἰ. αἰῶνα καὶ μοῖραν]] have, enjoy, E. [prev. cited]:—passive, to be inhabited, οἰκέοιτο πόλις Πριάμοιο [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 4.18; ἐς γῆν.. οἰκουμένην 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Philoctetes” 221]]; διὰ τῆς οἰκεομένης through the inhabited country, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 2.32; ὁδοιπόρεον ἐς τὴν οἰκεομένην [prev. author] 4.110]]; τὰς ἄλλας πόλιας οἰκεομένας μηδὲν ἧσσον although inhabited no less than before, [Refs [[prev. author] 1.170: for ἡ οἰκουμένη, see entry.]]

__2
colonize, settle in, τὰς πλείστας τῶν νήσων [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 1.8, compare 2.27]], etc.; πόλιν probably in [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Fragmenta” 360.11]]; νῆσον οἰκῆσαι, i.e. to be deported, [Refs 4th c.AD+ [“POxy.” 1101.24 (4th c.AD)]]: in perfect passive, to be settled in, occupy, τοῖσι τὰς νήσους οἰκημένοισι Ἴωσι [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.27; αἱ δύο [πόλιες] νήσους οἰκέαται [prev. work] 142 (compare below 3).]]

__3
in passive, to be settled, of men or tribes to whom new abodes are assigned, τριχθὰ ᾤκηθεν καταφυλαδόν [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 2.668: _Ionic dialect_]]perfect passive οἴκημαι, as present, οἱ ἐν τῇ ἠπείρῳ οἰκημένοι Ἕλληνες those who have been settled, i.e. those who dwell.., [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.27; οἱ ἐντὸς Ἅλυος ποταμοῦ οἰ. [prev. work] 28, compare 8.115]]; also of cities, to be situated, lie, παρ᾽ ὃν [ποταμὸν] Νίνος πόλις οἴκητο [Refs [[prev. author] 1.193.]]

__II
manage, direct a household or a state, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Coloneus” 1535 (uncertain meaning), 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Electra” 386, 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 3.37; οἴκει τὴν πόλιν ὁμοίως ὥσπερ τὸν πατρῷον οἶκον 5th-6th c.BC: Isocrates Orator 2.19: _metaphorically_, μὴ τὸν ἐμὸν οἴκει νοῦν]] don't manage.., [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Fragmenta” 144:]] — passive, εὖ οἰκούμεναι πόλεις well governed, [Refs [[prev. author] “Hipp.” 486]]; μετρίως, ὀρθῶς, ἄριστα οἰ., [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Leges” 936b, “R.” 371c, 520d, etc.; πατρίδος τετυχηκὼς ἣ νόμοις.. μάλιστα οἰκεῖσθαι δοκεῖ 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 21.150:]]future οἰκήσεται in passive sense, καθ᾽ ὅτι ἄριστα ἡ πόλις οἰκήσεται [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 8.67, compare 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Laches” 185a, 4th c.BC: Aeschines Orator 1.22, 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 58.62, 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Politica” 1284b38.]]

__B
intransitive, dwell, live, of persons, families, or tribes, have their abodes, settlements, in [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Homerus Epicus and 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus generally with ἐν.., ᾤκεον δ᾽ ἐν Πλευρῶνι 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 14.116, compare 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 9.200, 400; οἴκεε ἐν Πίνδῳ 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.56, compare 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Agamemnon” 1234, 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Aves” 967 (Oracle texts), 5th c.BC: Antipho Orator 5.78]]; especially of metics, ἐγ Κολλυτῷ οἰκοῦντι [Refs 8th c.BC+ [“IG” 12.373.60, +others; κατὰ στέγας 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Ion” 314; ὑπὸ χθονός [prev. author] “fragment” 450: after 8th c.BC: Homerus Epicus with _dative_ (_locative_) alone, Σαλαμῖνι “IG” 12.1.2 (6th c.BC)]]; οὐρανῷ [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “N.” 10.58; ναοῖσι 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Ion” 314; ἐλθόνθ᾽ ἁγνὸν ἐς Θήβης πέδον οἰ. 4th c.BC: Eubulus Comicus 10; παρὰ κρημνοῖσιν 5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “P.” 3.34; παρὰ ὄχθον 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Iphigenia Taurica” 1098 (Lyric poetry)]]; οἰ. μετά τινος, ={συνοικεῖν τινι}, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Tyrannus” 414, 990]]; κέρδη μὲν οἰκήσαντα.. having fixed my dwelling [there] with gain to my hosts, [Refs [[prev. author] “OC” 92]]; τὸ τὴν φροντίδ᾽ ἔξω τῶν κακῶν οἰκεῖν γλυκύ sweet it is for the mind to keep free from cares, [Refs [[prev. author] “OT” 1390]]; ἐπὶ προστάτου οἰ. (see. προστάτης) [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Lysias Orator 31.9.]]

__B.II
of cities, to be situated, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 2.166, 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Historia Graeca (Hellenica)” 7.1.3, 7.5 5]]; but τὴν πόλιν σποράδην καὶ κατὰ κώμας οἰκοῦσαν formed of detached villages, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Isocrates Orator 10.35, compare 4.39]] (so in passive, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 1.4.1).]]

__B.II.2
to be governed or administered, τίς τῶν πόλεων διὰ σὲ βέλτιον ᾤκησε; [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 599d, compare 462d, 472e, 473a, 543a, +others]]: frequently hardly distinguishable from the passive (above [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus II)]]; σωφρόνως γε οἰκοῦσα [πόλις] εὖ ἂν οἰκοῖτο a state administered by self-control would be well governed, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. author] “Chrm.” 162a; ἀρετῆς, ᾗ πόλεις τε καὶ οἶκοι εὖ οἰκοῦσι 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Memorabilia” 1.2.64]]; εἰς ὀλίγους, εἰς πλείους οἰκεῖν, to be governed in the interest of the few or the many, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 2.37.]]

deep_entry:
Abbott-Smith / STEPBible (TBESG)
οἰκία, -ας, ἡ
(οἶκος), [in LXX chiefly (very freq.) for בַּיִת ;]
a house, dwelling: Mat.2:11 7:24-27, Mrk.1:29, al.; ἐν οἰκίᾳ (= cl. κατ ̓ οἰκίαν), at home, Luk.8:27; εἰς οἰ., II Jn 10; οἰ, with genitive of person(s), usually has the art. (Mat.8:14, al., but cf. οἶκος and see Bl., § 46, 9); ἡ οἰ. τ. πατρός μου, Jhn.14:2.
Metaphorical,
__(a) of the body as the dwelling of the soul: 2Co.5:1;
__(b) of property (as בַּיִת, Gen.45:18, LXX, τ. υπάρχοντα; 3Ki.13:8, LXX, οἶκος) = οἶκος (which see): Mrk.12:40, Luk.20:47;
__(with) of the inmates of the dwelling, the household: Mat.12:25; with genitive of person(s), Jhn.4:53, 1Co.16:15
SYN.: οἶκος, which in Attic law denoted the whole estate, οἰκία, the dwelling only. In cl. poets οἶκος has also the latter sense, but not in prose, except in metaphorically usage, where it signifies both property and household. The foregoing distinction is not, however, consistently maintained in late Greek; cf. MM, ii, xvii, and see Thayer, see word οἰκία  (AS)

__2. By meton., a house, household, family: Luk.10:5, Act.7:10, 1Co.1:16, 1Ti.3:4, 5 al.; of the Church, ὁ οἶ. τ. θεοῦ, 1Ti.3:15, Heb.3:2, 1Pe.4:17; of descendants, οἶ Ἰσραήλ (Δαυείδ, Ἰακώβ; Bl, §47, 9), Mat.10:6, Luk.1:27, 33 al. (cf. Exo.6:14, 1Ki.2:30, al.).

LSJ / STEPBible (TFLSJ)
οἴομαι,
in [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Homerus Epicus]] always un contraction ὀΐομαι (except οἴομαι [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 10.193, οἴοιτο 17.580, 22.12)]], see below:—the shortened form οἶμαι is the one chiefly used in Trag., οἴομαι only in [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Choephori” 758, 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Coloneus” 28]]; but οἴομαι is frequently in [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus (“Eq.” 407, +others); 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus]] does not use either form; in Attic dialect Prose codices vary, but οἶμαι prevails, and was exclusively used in parenthesis (see. infr. IV): imperfect ᾠόμην [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Prometheus Vinctus” 270, 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Vespae” 791, etc.; also 1 _person_ ᾤμην [prev. author] “fragment” 636, etc.]]: future οἰήσομαι [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Lysias Orator 30.8, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 397a, etc., later οἰηθήσομαι 2nd c.AD: Galenus Medicus “περὶ τῆς ἀρίστης διδασκαλίας” 42]]:—Epic dialect aorist ὠϊσάμην (see. below): aorist ὠΐσθην [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 4.453, 16.475]]; participle ὀϊσθείς [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 9.453]]; Attic dialect and Ionic dialect aorist ᾠήθην [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Hippocrates Medicus “περὶ ἀρχαίης ἰητρικῇς” 14, 5th c.BC: Antipho Orator 1.8, 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 4.130, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Theaetetus” 178c, etc.]]; but rare in Comedy texts and Trag., οἰηθῇς [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Equites” 860, οἰηθείς, -εῖσα, 4th c.BC: Antiphanes Comicus 194.2, 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Iphigenia Aulidensis” 986]]; also aorist infinitive οἰήσασθαι [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-3rd c.BC: Aratus Epicus 896]]:—active, Epic dialect present ὀΐω and οἴω, but only in 1st pers. singular (see. below); Laconian dialect οἰῶ [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Lysistrata” 81, 156, 998, 5th-6th c.BC(?): Epilycus Comicus 3]]. [In the un contraction forms, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Homerus Epicus uses ῑ in ὀΐομαι 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 5.644, ὀΐεαι 1.561, 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 10.380, ὀΐεται 17.586, ὀϊόμεθ᾽ 21.322, 22.165, ὀϊόμενος 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 15.728, 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 2.351, +others (οἰόμενος 3rd c.BC: Callimachus Epicus “Epigrammata” 8.2), ὠΐετο 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 10.248, ὀΐσατο 1.323, 9.213, 19.390, ὀϊσάμενος 15.443 (but the variant{ὀϊσσατο},{ὀϊσσάμενος} in 8th c.BC: Homerus Epicus]] can be supported by ὀϊσσάμενος [Refs 4th c.BC+ [3rd c.BC: Apollonius Rhodius Epicus 2.1135, compare “Epica Alexandrina Adespota” 2.41, 4th-3rd c.BC: Aratus Epicus 1006, by ὑποίζεσθαι (: ὑπονοεῖν) 5th c.AD(?): Hesychius Legal icographus, and by ὠῐσάμην 3rd c.BC: Apollonius Rhodius Epicus 1.291, ὠΐσατο [ῐ] 2nd c.BC: Moschus Bucolicus 2.8, etc.)]]; active present ὀΐω has ῑ when it stands at the end of a line, also in [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 19.215 (in fourth foot), 18.259 (before caesura in third foot)]]; but ῐ in [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 1.558, 13.153, 23.467, etc.; οἴω as _disyllable_ is always at the end, except in 15.298, 21.533, 23.310]].]:—forebode, presage, with accusative, κῆρας ὀϊομένῳ [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 13.283; γόον δ᾽ ὠΐετο θυμός 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 10.248]]; expect, ἐελδομένοισι μάλ᾽ ἡμῖν, οὐδ᾽ ἔτ᾽ ὀϊομένοισι [Refs [24.401]]; suspect, ἤ τι ὀϊσάμενος, ἢ καὶ θεὸς ὣς ἐκέλευσεν [Refs [9.339; ἦ τινά που δόλον ἄλλον ὀΐεαι 10.380]]; fear, κατὰ θυμὸν ὀΐσατο, μή ἑ λαβοῦσα οὐλὴν ἀμφράσσαιτο [Refs [19.390; τῷ ἑπόμην.., ὀϊόμενός περ, ἀνάγκῃ 14.298: _absolutely_, αἰεὶ μὲν ὀΐεαι, οὐδέ σε λήθω]] thou art ever suspecting, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 1.561; πατὴρ δ᾽ ἐμὸς αὐτίκ᾽ ὀϊσθεὶς πολλὰ κατηρᾶτο 9.453, compare 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 15.443: followed by ὡς, καὐτὸς ὀΐεαι ὥς κεν ἐτύχθη]] you can guess how it would have happened, [Refs [3.255, compare 17.586: with _accusative_ et]]future infinitive, ὀΐομαι ἄνδρα χολωσέμεν [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 1.78; ἅ τιν᾽ οὐ πείσεσθαι ὀΐω [prev. work] 289, compare 5.252, 284, +others]]; τὸ καὶ τελέεσθαι ὀΐω [Refs [1.204; ἀλλ᾽ οὐ νῦν ἐρύεσθαι ὀΐομαι 20.195]]: with accusative et present infinitive, referring to present time, οὐδέ τι θυμῷ ὠΐσθη δόλον εἶναι [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 4.453, compare 10.232; ὀΐσατο γὰρ θεὸν εἶναι 1.323; τῶ δ᾽ ὀΐω κείνης τάδε πάσχειν ἐννεσίῃσιν 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 5.894]]: with accusative et aorist infinitive, referring to past time, τῇ δ᾽ ὀΐω κατανεῦσαι [Refs 8th c.BC+ [1.558, compare 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 3.27, +others: the]]subjunctive of the infinitive must frequently be supplied from the context, διωκέμεναι γὰρ ὀΐω I fear [they] are pursuing me, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [15.278, compare 1.201, 12.212, 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 12.66, +others: with]]infinitive alone, when both Verbs have the same subject, as κιχήσεσθαι δέ δ᾽ ὀΐω I think I shall catch you, [Refs [6.341]]; mean, intend, with future infinitive, οὐ γὰρ ἔγωγ᾽ ἔτι σοὶ πείσεσθαι ὀΐω [Refs 8th c.BC+ [1.296, compare 170, 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 19.215]]: with present infinitive, οὐ γὰρ ὀΐω ἀνδρῶν δυσμενέων ἑκὰς ἱστάμενος πολεμίζειν [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 13.262.]]

__II
impersonal, only [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 19.312, ἀλλά μοι ὧδ᾽ ἀνὰ θυμὸν ὀΐεται]] there comes a boding into my heart.

__III
think, suppose, believe, frequently in [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Homerus Epicus, as 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 1.59, 5.644, etc.; οἶμαι βοὴν ἄμικτον ἐν πόλει πρέπειν 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Agamemnon” 321]]; οἶμαι γάρ νιν ἱκετεύσειν (ἱκετεῦσαι codices) [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Iphigenia Aulidensis” 462]]; κτήσεσθαι (-σασθαι codices) [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Lysias Orator 12.19]]; διαπράξεσθαι (-ξασθαι codices) [Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. author] 13.53; ἤδη γὰρ αὐτοὺς οἴομαι δεδειπνάναι 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Fragmenta” 464]]; opposed to εἰδέναι, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 506c4; οἴονται, ἴσασι δ᾽ οὐδέν 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Rhetorica” 1389b17, compare “APo.” 75a15: followed by ὅτι.., 1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus 2.90b]]:—passive, μάρτυρας δύο παρεχέτω ὀμνύντας οἰόμενον that he is the putative father, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [Schwyzer 784a (Tenos, 4th c.BC).]]

__IV
parenthetically, mostly in first person, ἐν πρώτοισιν, ὀΐω, κείσεται among the first, I ween, will he be lying, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 8.536; ἔπειτά γ᾽, ὀΐω, γνώσεαι 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 16.309, compare 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 13.153, 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 2.255, etc.: in 8th c.BC: Homerus Epicus only in _active_ form ὀΐω, except ὀΐομαι 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 22.140, and perhaps 14.363, compare 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Choephori” 758]]; in Attic dialect this parenthetic use is probably confined to the shorter form οἶμαι, imperfect ᾤμη; rarely in other persons than the first, as οὐκ οἴει ἀναγκασθήσετα; [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 486c, compare “Tht.” 147b]]; πόσης οἴεσθε γέμει σωφροσύνη; [Refs [[prev. author] “Smp.” 216d.]]

__IV.2
expressive of modesty or courtesy, to avoid over-great bluntness of assertion, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. author] “Grg.” 483c, 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 1.3.11, etc.]]: even between a preposition and its case, ἐξ οἶμαι τῆς ἀκροτάτης ἐλευθερίας [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 564a; ἐν οἶμαι πολλοῖς 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 20.3]]; or between Article and substantive, οἱ γὰρ οἶμαι βέλτιστοι [Refs [[prev. author] 54.38.]]

__V
answering a question, I think so, I should think so, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Acharnenses” 919, etc.; νὴ τὸν Ἡρακλέα, οἶμαί γε [prev. author] “Th.” 27; οἶμαι ἔγωγε 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Crito” 47d, etc.]]; οἴεσθαί γε χρή one must think so, it would seem so, [Refs [[prev. author] “Prt.” 325c, “Cri.” 53d, “Phd.” 68b, “Grg.” 522a.]]

__VI
Attic dialect phrases:

__VI.1
πῶς οἴε; you can't think how, to add force, like{πῶς δοκεῖς}; πόθος τὴν καρδίαν ἐπάταξε πῶς οἴει σφόδρα [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Ranae” 54.]]

__VI.2
οἴομαι δεῖν I think it my duty, think fit, hence sometimes, intend, purpose, λέγειν οἴεται δεῖν ποιεῖν δεινούς his object is to train orators, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Meno” 95c, compare 86b, “Tht.” 207e; βδελυρὸς καὶ ὑβριστὴς ᾤετο δεῖν εἶναι 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 21.143; τοὺς ἐχθροὺς ἀμυνόμενοι τεθνάναι δεῖν ᾤοντο [prev. author] 60.31, compare 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Protagoras” 316c, 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 2.6.26, “Mem.” 4.6.3, 6]]; [ὁ ἀκόλαστος] οἰόμενος δεῖν [διώκει τὰ ἡδέα] intentionally, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Ethica Nicomachea” 1152a6, compare 1136b8, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Hipparchus” 225b]]; but οἴομαι δὲ δεῖν οὐδέν methinks there is no need, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Coloneus” 28; and in 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus Alcaeus2.144d ἆρ᾽ οὐκ ἀναγκαῖον.. οἰηθῆναι δεῖν.. ἡμᾶς εἰδέναι ἢ τῷ ὄντι εἰδέναι]]; must we not either think we know or really know? (δεῖν being superfluous).

__VI.3
οἴομαι without δεῖν I mean to, intend, οὐκ οἴει.. δοῦναι δίκη; [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Lysias Orator 12.26, compare 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Critias” 62d, “Ly.” 200b, “Ep.” 324b]]; οὐ βαλεῖν (variant{βάλλειν}).. ᾠήθη [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Ethica Nicomachea” 1135b14, compare 1172a7.]]

οἷος, οἵα,
Ionic dialect οἵη, οἷον, (ὅς) such as, of what sort, relative and indirect interrogative pronoun, correlative to direct interrogative ποῖος, indefinite ποιός, demonstrative τοῖος: ὅσσος ἔην οἷός τε [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 24.630; ὁσσάτιόν τε καὶ οἷον 5.758: with _accusative_, οἶδ᾽ ἀρετὴν οἷός ἐσσι]] what a man for valour, [Refs [13.275: frequently to be rendered by an]] adverb, οἷος πόλεμόνδε μέτεισι as he rushes into war, [Refs [[prev. work] 298, etc.:]] —Usage:

__I
οἷος in an independent sentence as an exclamation of astonishment, ὢ πόποι.., οἷον ἔειπες [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 7.455]]; οἷ. τὸ πῦρ what a fire is this ! [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Agamemnon” 1256, compare “Pers.” 733, +others; οἷ. εἰργάσασθε 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 450a; οἷ. ἄνδρα λέγεις ἐν κινδύνῳ εἶναι [prev. author] “Tht.” 142b; οἷα ποιεῖς [prev. author] “Euthphr.” 15e, etc.: so in _neuter_ as]] adverb, see below see [Refs [1.]]

__I.2
in indirect sentences, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Tyrannus” 624, 1402, 1488, etc.; ὁρᾶτε δὴ ἐν οἵῳ ἐστέ 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 3.2.12; ὁρῶν ἐν οἵοις ἐσμέν [prev. author] “An.” 3.1.15.]]

__II
more frequently as relative to a demonstrative τοῖος, τοιόσδε, τοιοῦτος, or to ὁ, ὅδε, as τῷ ἴκελον, οἷόν ποτε Δαίδαλος ἤσκησεν [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 18.591; θέαμα τοιοῦτον οἷ. καὶ στυγοῦντ᾽ ἐποικτίσαι 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Tyrannus” 1296]]: but the demonstrative pronoun is frequently omitted, οὐ γὰρ ἐμὴ ἲς ἔσθ᾽ οἵη πάρος ἔσκεν [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 11.669, etc.]]; οἷ. καὶ Πάρις.. ᾔσχυνε like as Paris also.., [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Agamemnon” 399 (Lyric poetry), compare “Pers.” 21, +others: with δή added, τοιόνδ᾽, οἷ. δὴ σύ]] such as you surely are, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 24.376, see below see 2]]: with περ added, οἵη περ φύλλων γενεή, τοίη δὲ καὶ ἀνδρῶν just such as.., [Refs 5th c.BC+ [6.146, compare 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Agamemnon” 607, 1046, 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 1.6.19]]: very frequently with τε added (this οἷός τε must be distinguished from οἷός τε with infinitive, see[Refs 8th c.BC+ [below 111.2), οἷός τε πελώριος ἔρχεται Ἄρης 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 7.208, compare 17.157, 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 7.106, etc.; οἷός που 20.35: οἷός τις, οἷόν τι]] generalizes a Comparison, the sort of person who.., thing which.., [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 5.638, 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 9.348]]; οἶσθα εἰς οἷόν τινα κίνδυνον ἔρχει..; [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Protagoras” 313a]]; with attraction of οἷος to the case of its antecedent (which may follow instead of preceding), οἵοις περ σὺ χρώμενοι συμβούλοις [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 24.185]]; and with further attraction of the subject of the relative clause, οὐ γάρ πω τοίους ἴδον ἀνέρας.., οἷον Πειρίθοον (for οἷος Πειρίθοος) [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 1.263; πρὸς ἄνδρας τολμηρούς, οἵους καὶ Ἀθηναίους 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 7.21, compare 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Memorabilia” 2.9.3; περὶ τοῦ τοιούτου.., οἵου τοῦ ἑνός 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Parmenides” 161b.]]

__II.2
οἷος, οἵα, οἷον frequently introduce an 'indirect exclamation', giving the reason for what precedes, ἄνακτα χόλος λάβεν, οἷον ἄκουσε because of what he heard, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 6.166, compare 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 17.479]]; ἐμακάριζον τὴν μητέρα οἵων τέκνων ἐκύρησε [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.31; ἀγανάκτησιν ἔχει ὑφ᾽ οἵων κακοπαθεῖ 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 2.41; τὴν ἐμαυτοῦ τύχην [ἀπέκλαον], οἵου ἀνδρὸς.. ἐστερημένος εἴην 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Phaedo” 117c, compare 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Tyrannus” 701.]]

__II.3
sometimes in [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Homerus Epicus οἷος]] introduces the reason for saying what is said, ὠκύμορος.. ἔσσεαι, οἷ᾽ ἀγορεύεις [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 18.95, compare 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 4.611; αἲ γάρ με θυμὸς ἀνείη ὤμ᾽ ἀποταμνόμενον κρέα ἔδμεναι, οἷα ἔοργας 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 22.347.]]

__II.4
οἷα δὴ εἴπας saying so and so, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.86 (compare ὅσος 111.2): later with other Particles, see infr. VI.]]

__II.5
οὐδὲν οἷον.. there's nothing like.., ἀλλ᾽ οὐδὲν οἷ. ἐστ᾽ ἀκοῦσαι τῶν ἐπῶν there's nothing like hearing the verses, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Aves” 966, compare “Lys.” 135; οὐδὲν γὰρ οἷ. ἀκούειν αὐτοῦ τοῦ νόμου 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 21.46, compare 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Gorgias” 447c, 481b, 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Oeconomicus” 3.14.]]

__II.6
never used like adverb οἷον (infr. V. I) with an adjective = how, for in [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 11.653, οἶσθα.. οἷ. ἐκεῖνος δεινὸς ἀνήρ]] = what manner of man, namely dread, compare [Refs 8th c.BC+ [15.94, 21.108, 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 19.493, etc.]]

__II.7
as indefinite, a sort or kind of.., ὁ δ᾽ ἕτερος οἷός ἐστιν οἰκουρὸς μόνον only a kind of watch-dog, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Vespae” 970]]; so with adjective, ἀφόρητος οἷος.. κρυμός of an intolerable kind, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 4.28]]; θαυμαστὸς οἷος of a wonderful nature, [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd c.AD: Lucianus Sophista “Zeux.” 6]]; οἷος ἔμπειρος πολέμου rather skilled in war, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 2.18]]; οἷον τετανότριχα rather straight-haired, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Euthyphro” 2b]]; frequently with superlative, χωρίον οἷον χαλεπώτατον country of a very difficult kind, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 4.8.2, compare 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Equites” 978, “Ach.” 384, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Apologia” 23a; ἀνὴρ οἷος κράτιστος 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Ethica Nicomachea” 1165b27; κόλπος οἷος βαθύτατος 2nd-3rd c.AD: Aelianus “De Natura Animalium - Ar.Byzantine Epit.” 14.26: in some of these passages with _superlative_ it is possible to take οἷος as _relative_, supplying δυνατόν,compare ξύμμαχος ἔσομαι οἷος ἂν δύνωμαι ἄριστος “IG” 12.39.28.]]

__III
οἷος with infinitive implies fitness or ability for a thing, οὐ γὰρ ἦν ὥρα οἵα τὸ πεδίον ἄρδειν fit for watering, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 2.3.13, compare 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Gorgias” 487d]]; οἷοι φιλεῖν, μισεῖν, etc., [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 25.2, etc.: frequently with τοιοῦτος]] expressed, τοιοῦτός τις οἷ. διαπονεῖσθαι [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Cratylus” 395a, compare “R.” 415e]]; τὸ πρᾶγμα μέγα.. καὶ μὴ οἷ. νεωτέρῳ βουλεύσασθαι not proper for a young man to advise upon, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 6.12]]: without infinitive, λόγους οἵους εἰς τὰ δικαστήρια [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Euthydemus” 272a.]]

__III.b
οἷός εἰμι I intend, ἐβιάζετο.. καὶ οἷος ἦν ἐξευρεῖν τὴν θύραν [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Lysias Orator “Fragmenta” 159 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus, compare 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 4.9, +others, 4th c.BC: Isaeus Orator 8.21]]; οἷος ἦν κατεσθίειν was on the point of eating, [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [3rd c.BC: Antigonus Carystius Paradoxographus Car. cited in 2nd c.AD: Athenaeus Epigrammaticus 7.345d.]]

__III.2
more frequently οἷός τε with infinitive, fit or able to do, λιποίμην οἷός τ᾽.. ἀέθλια κάλ᾽ ἀνελέσθαι [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 21.117 (preceded by τοῖον [prev. work] 173), 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.29, 67, 91; λέγειν οἷός τε κἀγώ 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Equites” 343, compare 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 3.16, 5th-6th c.BC: Isocrates Orator 8.69, etc.]]; inclined to.., [Refs 2nd c.BC+ [2nd c.BC: Polybius Historicus 3.90.5, 1st c.AD: Josephus Historicus “Antiquitates Judaicae” 4.6.3: most frequently in _neuter_ _sing._ and _plural_, οἷόν τε [ἐστί]]] it is possible to.., [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 1.80, etc.; οἷά τε [ἐστί] 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.194, etc.; a _dative_ is sometimes added, μὴ οἷόν τε εἶναι ἐμοὶ κωλῦσαι 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 7.14.]]

__III.3
without infinitive, πάνυ προθύμως ὡς οἷός τ᾽ ἦν ἐπήραξεν [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Protagoras” 314d: but mostly in _neuter_, οἷόν τε [ἐστίν]]] it is possible, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Isocrates Orator 9.9; οὐχ οἷόν τε ἐστίν 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Nubes” 198, etc.]]: with superlative, καλὸν ὡς οἷόν τε μάλιστα [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Protagoras” 349e; ὡς οἷόν τε σμικρότατα [prev. author] “Prm.” 144b; ὡς οἷόν τε διὰ βραχυτάτων [prev. author] “Grg.” 449d]]: without superlative, φρίττειν.. ποιεῖ ὡς οἷόν τε πάντας [Refs [[prev. author] “R.” 387c (uncertain reading)]]; ὡς οἷόν τε sometimes so far as possible, of what cannot be done completely, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 8.75, 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Politica” 1313a39, 2nd c.AD: Lucianus Sophista “Im.” 3.]]

__IV
sometimes twice in the same clause, οἷ᾽ ἔργα δράσας οἷα λαγχάνει κακά after what deeds what sufferings are his ! [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Electra” 751]]; ἱερῶν οἵαν οἵων χάριν ἠνύσω what thanks for what offerings ! [Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. author] “Tr.” 994, compare 1045, 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Alcestis” 144: so in Prose, 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 4.5.29, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Symposium” 195a.]]

__V
as adverb in neuter singular οἷον, in Poets and Ionic dialect Prose also plural οἷα, how, οἷον δή νυ θεοὺς βροτοὶ αἰτιόωνται [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 1.32, compare 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 5.601, 13.633, 15.287: also with _adjectives_, οἷον ἐερσήεις]] how fresh, [Refs [24.419]]; οἷον δὴ Μενέλαον ὑπέτρεσας seeing how thou didst shrink from M., [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 17.587, compare 21.57. (Regul. _adverb_ οἵως is rare, as in 5th c.BC: Hippocrates Medicus “ἐπιδημίαι” 6.7.2, _falsa lectio_ in 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Vespae” 1363]]; οἷος ὢν οἵ. ἔχεις in what a state art thou for such a man! [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Ajax” 923; οἵως τέ σφ᾽ ἐσάωσα 3rd c.BC: Apollonius Rhodius Epicus 4.786.)]]

__V.2
as, just as, οἷον ὅτε.. [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 14.295: also _neuter_ _plural_ οἷα, οἷά τις.. ἀηδών 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Agamemnon” 1142 (Lyric poetry), compare 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Trachiniae” 105 (Lyric poetry), etc.: so οἷά τε in 8th c.BC: Homerus Epicus, οἷά τε ληϊστῆρες 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 3.73, compare 9.128, 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 2.175: strengthened by Particles, οἷα δή 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 8.84, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Symposium” 219e, “R.” 467b; οἷα δή που 2nd-3rd c.AD: Aelianus “De Natura Animalium - Ar.Byzantine Epit.” 1.14]]: later a double form occurs, οἷον ὡς.. [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demetrius Phalereus Rhetor “Demetrius on Style” 94, Scholia 2nd c.BC: Dionysius Thrax Grammaticus p.113 H.; οἷον ὥσπερ.. 2nd c.AD: Phrynichus Atticista “Praeparatio Sophistica” p.80 5th c.BC: Bacchylides Lyricus, uncertain in 1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus 2.563f.]]

__V.2.b
as for instance, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Sophista” 218e, 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “de Generatione et Corruptione” 333a11, etc.]]; οἷον τί λέγει; as for example, what do you mean ? [Refs 8th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Theaetetus” 207a, compare 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 4.271, where οἷον is]] adjective

__V.2.c
in numerical estimates, about, οἷον δέκα σταδίους [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 4.90; μῆκος οἷον ἐπὶ δέκα δακτύλους “IG” 22.1457.17.]]

__V.2.d
οἷον parenthetically prefixed to any word or phrase, as it were, so to speak, οἷον υἱεῖς γνησίους [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Phaedrus” 278a, compare “Cra.” 396a, 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Historia Animalium” 532a6, “GA” 753a33; τῶν οἷον προγυμναζομένων 2nd c.AD: Marcus Antoninus Imperator 6.20; τοῦ οἷον δόγματος 3rd c.AD(?): Diogenes Laertius 9.69]]; τὴν.. οἷον φάτταν the ring-dove of my parable, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Theaetetus” 199b.]]

__V.2.e
οἷον explanatory, that is to say, τὸ νῦν ῥηθησόμενον, οἷον.. what I am about to mention, i.e. , [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “de Partibus Animalium” 639b6, compare “GC” 333a11, +others]]; κατὰ τὸ μέσον, οἷον κατὰ τὴν συμβολὴν τῶν ἐν αὐτοῖς διαγωνίων in the middle, i. e. at the intersection of their diagonals, [Refs 5th c.AD+ [5th c.AD: Proclus Philosophus “Hypotyposis astronomicarum positionum” 3.16, compare 22, 5th c.AD(?): Hesychius Legal icographus see at {οἰοφάγῳ}, +others]]

__V.3
like{ὡς, ἅτε}, with a participle, οἷα ἀπροσδοκήτου κακοῦ γενομένου [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 2.5, compare 8.95, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Symposium” 203b.]]

__V.4
οὐχ οἷον or μὴ οἷον, followed by ἀλλ᾽ οὐδέ or ἀλλὰ μηδέ, not only not.., but not even.., [Refs 5th c.BC+ [2nd c.BC: Polybius Historicus 1.20.12, 1st c.BC: Diodorus Siculus Historicus 3.18, 1st c.BC: Philodemus Gadarensis Epigrammaticus “Rh.” 2.249 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus, etc.]]

__VI
strengthened with various Particles, οἷος δή, see above 11.4: οἱοσδήποτε, οἱαδήποτε, οἱονδήποτε, of such and such a kind, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Ethica Nicomachea” 1114b17]]; οἱοσδηποτοῦν, of whatever kind, [Refs 2nd c.BC+ [2nd-1st c.BC(?): Hero Mechanicus “*Geometry texts” 12.30, +others, “BGU” 895.28 (2nd c.AD), 7th c.AD: Paulus Aegineta Medicus 6.88]]; οἱοσδήπως, [Refs 5th c.AD+ [“OGI” 521.4 (Abydos, 5th-6th c.AD)]]; οἱοσδητισοῦν, [Refs 3rd c.AD+ [[prev. work]515.16 (Mylasa, 3rd c.AD)]]; οἱοσοῦν, [Refs 6th c.AD+ [6th c.AD: Justinianus Imperator “Novellae” 30.7.1]]; οἱοσποτοῦν, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Topica” 146b26]]; οἱοστισοῦν, see reading in [Refs 8th c.BC+ [1st c.AD: Dioscorides (Dioscurides) Medicus 2.76.13. [οῐ is found in 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 13.275, 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 7.312; and sometimes in Trag., as 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Agamemnon” 1256]], especially in the form οἷός τε [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Tyrannus” 1415, “OC” 262, 803, +others]]]

Abbott-Smith / STEPBible (TBESG)
ὀκνέω, -ῶ
(ὄκνος, shrinking, hesitation), [in LXX: Num.22:16 (מָנַע ni.), Jdg.18:9 (אָצַל ni.), Tob.12:6, 13, Jdth.12:13, Sir.7:35, 4Ma.14:4 * ;]
to shrink from doing, hesitate to do (Hom., Thuc., al.); hence, to delay with inf., Act.9:38 (cf. Nu, l.with, and see MM, xviii).†
(AS)

---

LSJ / STEPBible (TFLSJ)
ὀκν-έω,
Epic dialect ὀκνείω [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 5.255]]: imperfect ὤκνεον [Refs [20.155]]: future -ήσω[Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Isocrates Orator 6.72]]: aorist ὤκνησα [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 18.103, etc.]]: (ὄκνος):—shrink from doing, scruple, hesitate to do a thing, with infinitive, ὀκνείω ἵππων ἐπιβαινέμεν [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 5.255; ἀρχέμεναι πολέμοιο ὤκνεον 20.155.]] —In _Attic dialect_ mostly with collateral sense of the feeling which causes the hesitation, and so,

__1
of shame or fear (in a moral sense), ὀκνῶ προδότης καλεῖσθαι I shrink from being called, fear to be called, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Philoctetes” 93, compare 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 5.61, 5th c.BC: Lysias Orator “Fragmenta” 23]]; οἷα ἐγὼ ὀκνῶ πρὸς ὑμᾶς ὀνομάσαι shrink from naming, hesitate to name, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 2.19, compare 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Gorgias” 462e; τοσαῦθ᾽ ὅσ᾽ ὀκνήσαιμ᾽ ἂν.. εἰπεῖν 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 18.103, compare 24.7, etc.]]

__2
of pity, σὰς ὀκνῶ θρᾶξαι φρένας [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Prometheus Vinctus” 628, compare 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Electra” 1271.]]

__3

ὀλίγος, -η, -ον
(on οὐχ ὁλ., see infr.), [in LXX chiefly for מָעַט ;]
of number, quantity, size, few, little, small, slight: Mat.9:37 15:34, Mrk.6:5 8:7, Luk.10:2 12:48 (sc. πληγάς, opposite to πολλάς), 1Ti.5:23, Heb.12:10, Rev.3:4 12:12; οὐκ ὀ. (in the best uncials written οὐκ ὁ.; see WH, App., 143; M, Pr., 44; Thackeray, Gr., 126 f.), Act.12:18 14:28 15:2 (with genitive part.) Act.17:4, 12 19:23-24 27:20; pl., absol., Mat.7:14 20:16 (WH, txt., RV, om.) Mat.22:14, Luk.13:23, 1Pe.3:20. Neut. sing (τὸ) ὀ.: Luk.7:47, 2Co.8:15; πρὸς ὀλίγον, 1Ti.4:8, Jas.4:14; ἐν ὀ., Act.26:28-29 (with little effort; see Page, in l); id., in brief, Eph.3:3; adverbially, ὀλίγον, of time, Mrk.6:31, 1Pe.1:6 5:10, Rev.17:10; of space, Mrk.1:19, Luk.5:3; pl., ὀλίγα, Luk.10:42, Rev.2:14; ἐπ᾽ ὀλίγα, Mat.25:21, 23; δι᾽ ὀλίγων, in few words, briefly, 1Pe.5:12 (cf. Plat., Legg., vi, 778 e).†
**ὀλίγως, adv.
(ὀλίγος), [in Aq.: Isa.10:7 * ;]
