LSJ / STEPBible (TFLSJ)
ὀλίγος [ῐ], η, ον,
later ὀλίος (which see), of Size, little, small, frequently in [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Homerus Epicus, rarer later, opposed to μέγας, σάκος 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 14.376; κῦμα 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 10.94, etc.]]; ὀλίγῃ ὀπί with small, low voice, [Refs [14.492]]; of stature,[Refs 3rd c.BC+ [9.515; ὀ. κῶρος 3rd c.BC: Theocritus Poeta Bucolicus 1.47; οὐκ ὀλίγης αἷμα βοὸς κέχυται Callias Epigrammaticus “Aet.Oxy.” 2080.85]]; of Space, ὀ. χῶρος [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 10.161, etc.]]; of Time, χρόνος [Refs 5th c.BC+ [19.157, 23.418, 5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “N.” 7.38, etc.; ἐν βραχεῖ κὠλίγῳ χρόνῳ 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Fragmenta” 646 (cf. IV. 3).]]

__2
sometimes in a sense between that of Size and Quantity, ὀ. δόσις [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 6.208; οὖρα ὀλίγα]]not copious, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Hippocrates Medicus “ἐπιδημίαι” 1.2]]; ὑποστάσιες ὀλίγαι slight sediments, [Refs [[prev. work] 17]]; ὀ. καὶ οὐδέν little or nothing, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Apologia” 23a; οὐδὲν ἢ ὀ. 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “de Partibus Animalium” 651b17.]]

__3
of Degree, ὀ. καὶ μέγας of low and high degree, [Refs 7th c.BC+ [7th c.BC: Callinus Epicus 1.17.]]

__4
weak, ἀθυμοτέρη καὶ ὀλιγωτέρη φύσις [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Hippocrates Medicus “περὶ παρθενίων” 1.]]

__II
of Number, few, or of Quantity, little, not in [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Homerus Epicus]], frequently in Attic dialect, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Aves” 1417, “Eq.” 717, etc.]], but rare in Trag., as ὀλίγα κακά [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Persae” 330.—The governing body in Oligarchies and the oligarchical party in Democracies was called οἱ ὀ., 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 6.38, 8.9, etc.]]; ἡ ὑπὸ τῶν ὀ. δυναστεία, αἱ διὰ τῶν ὀ. δυναστεῖαι, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Politicus” 291d, 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 60.25; ἑνὸς καὶ πλήθους τὸ ὀ. μέσον 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Politicus” 303a.]]

__II.2
with infinitive, ὀλίγους.. στρατιῇ τῇ Μήδων συμβαλεῖν too few to engage.., [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 6.109, compare 7.207; μὴ.. αἱ σφέτεραι δέκα νῆες ὀλίγαι ἀμύνειν ὦσιν 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 1.50.]]

__III
neuter ὀλίγον as adverb, a little, slightly, little, with Verbs, ὀ. παρακλίνας [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 23.424, compare 11.52, 12.452; φροντίσας 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Cyclops” 163; ὀ. τοῦ ποιήματος προελθών 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Protagoras” 339d: also _neuter_ _plural_, ἠκροβολίσαντο ὀλίγα 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 3.73.]]

__III.2
with comparative adjectives, ὀλίγον προγενέστερος [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 23.789; ὀ. ἧσσον 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 15.365; στιβαρώτερον οὐκ ὀ. περ 8.187; φέρτερος οὐκ ὀ. περ 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 19.217]]; ὀ. τι πρότερον, variant for{ὀλίγῳ}, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 4.79, 81, compare 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Politicus” 262b, etc.; ὀ. ὕστερον [prev. author] “Grg.” 454b, etc.]]; but ὀλίγῳ is more frequently in Prose, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus [same places] (with variant), 7.113, +others, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Gorgias” 460c, “R.” 327c, etc.]]

__IV
special Phrases:

__IV.1
ὀλίγου δεῖν almost (see. δεῖ II); ὀλίγου ἐδέησε καταλαβεῖν wanted but little of overtaking, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 7.10.γ᾽: hence ὀλίγου]] alone, within a little, allbut, almost, ὀλίγου σεκύνες διεδηλήσαντο [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 14.37, compare 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Acharnenses” 348, 381, “Nu.” 722, 5th c.BC: Lysias Orator 14.17, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Protagoras” 361b, 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 19.334, etc.; ὀ. ἅπαντες 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Apologia” 22b; ὀ. ἐς χιλίους]]close upon [Refs 5th c.BC+ [1, 000, 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 4.124]]; ὀ. ἦλθεν ἑλεῖν[Refs 2nd c.AD+ [(see. below 9) 2nd c.AD: Pausanias Periegeta 1.13.6.]]

__IV.2
δι᾽ ὀλίγου at a short distance, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Phoenissae” 1098, 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 2.89, 3.21, uncertain in 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Septem contra Thebas” 762 (Lyric poetry)]]; for (during) a short time, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 1.77, 2.85, 3.43]]; within or after a short time, [Refs [[prev. author] 6.11, 47, 7.39, etc.]]; but

__IV.2.b
δι᾽ ὀλίγων in few words, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Philebus” 31d, etc.; see infr. VI. 2.]]

__IV.3
ἐν ὀλίγῳ (χώρῳ is added in [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 9.70)]] in a small space, within small compass, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Supplices” 1126 (Lyric poetry); ἐν ὀ. στρατοπεδευομένοις 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 4.26]]; κυκλωθέντων ἐν ὀ.[Refs 4th c.BC+ [[prev. work] 96; εἰς ταὐτὸ πάντα.. ἁθροίσαντ᾽ ἐν ὀ. 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 3.18]]; also ἐν ὀ. (i.e. χρόνῳ) for a brief time, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “P.” 8.92]]; but also, in a short time, quickly, ἔγνων καὶ περὶ τῶν ποιητῶν ἐν ὀ. τοῦτο [NT+5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Apologia” 22b, compare 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 4.55, NT.Act.26.28.]]

__IV.3.b
ἐν ὀλίγοις one among few, i.e. exceedingly, remarkably, ποταμὸς ἐν ὀ. μέγας [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 4.52; ἐν ὀλίγοισι Περσέων.. ἀνὴρ δόκιμος [prev. author] 9.41]]: frequently in later writers, [Refs 1st c.AD+ [1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus “Pompeius” 10, 3rd c.AD: Heliodorus Scriptor Eroticus 3.1; so σὺν ὀλίγοις, see below 10.]]

__IV.4
ἐξ ὀλίγου at short notice, suddenly, ἐξ ὀ. καὶ δι᾽ ὀργῆς [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 2.11, compare 61, 4.108, etc.]]

__IV.5
ἐς ὀλίγον, like{παρ᾽ ὀλίγον}, within a little, ἐς ὀ. ἀφίκετο τὸ στράτευμα νικηθῆναι [Refs [[prev. work] 129.]]

__IV.6
ἐπ᾽ ὀλίγον for a short time, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Hippocrates Medicus “προρρητικόν” 1.26, 3rd c.AD: Plotinus Philosophus 4.4.29, “Geoponica” 7.12.22, 10.7.10, etc.]]; a little at a time, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Hippocrates Medicus “περὶ τῶν ἐν κεφαλη—ͅ τρωμάτων” 18; εἴρηται ἐν τῷ [βιβλίῳ] ἐπ᾽ ὀλίγον]]a little way on, near the beginning, [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd c.AD: Galenus Medicus 15.428.]]

__IV.7
κατ᾽ ὀλίγον by little and little, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 1.69, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Timaeus” 85d, 2nd c.AD: Lucianus Sophista “Nec.” 11, etc.; ἐκ τοῦ κατ᾽ ὀ. 1st c.BC: Diodorus Siculus Historicus 15.34, 1st c.AD: Athenaeus Medicus cited in 4th c.AD: Oribasius Medicus 1.2.6]]: but the adjective frequently takes the gender and number of its substantive, κατ᾽ ὀλίγους [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 2.93, 8.113]]; οὗτοι κατ᾽ ὀλίγους γινόμενοι ἐμάχοντο fought few at a time, in small parties, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. author] 9.102, compare 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Theaetetus” 197d]]; κατ᾽ ὀλίγον μαχεῖται (i.e. τὸ πλῆθος αὐτῶν) [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 4.10.]]

__IV.8
μετ᾽ ὀλίγον τούτων shortly after.., [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Historia Graeca (Hellenica)” 1.1.2.]]

__IV.9
παρ᾽ ὀλίγον with little to spare, only just, ἀπέφυγες [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Iphigenia Taurica” 870 (Lyric poetry)]]; to within a short distance of, παρ᾽ ὀ. ἦλθε.. ἐκπεσεῖν [Refs 2nd c.BC+ [2nd c.BC: Polybius Historicus 2.55.4, compare 18.46.12]]; but

__IV.9.b
παρ᾽ ὀ. ποιεῖσθαι hold of small account, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 6.6.11.]]

__IV.10
σὺν ὀλίγοις, ={ἐν ὀλίγοις, ἐπαινεθῆναι} [Refs 1st c.AD+ [1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus “Galba” 3; see supr. IV. 3b.]]

__V
regular adverb ὀλίγως is rare, [NT+2nd c.AD+ [NT.2Pet.2.18, 2nd c.AD: Aquila LXX.Isa.10.7; οὐκ ὀ. “Anthologia Graeca” 12.205 (2nd c.AD: Strato Epigrammaticus).]]

__VI

Aeolic dialect 3rd.pers. singular present ὀμίλλει [Refs 7th c.BC+ [7th-6th c.BC: Alcaeus Lyricus 61.29]] Lobel, to be in company with, consort with, μνηστῆρσιν [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 2.21, +others, compare 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Symposium” 2.10, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 500c, etc.: with Preps., ἠὲ μετὰ Τρώεσσιν ὁμιλέοι ἦ μετ᾽ Ἀχαιοῖς 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 5.86, compare 834; ἐνὶ πρώτοισιν ὁ. 18.194, compare 535]]; πὰρ παύροισι.. ὁμιλεῖς consortest with few, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 18.383.]]

__2
absolutely, μηδ᾽ ἄλλοθ᾽ ὁμιλήσαντες joining in company, [Refs [4.684]]; περὶ νεκρὸν ὁ. throng about the corpse, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 16.641, compare 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 24.19.]]

__II
in hostile sense, join battle with, ὁμιλέομεν Δαναοῖσιν [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 11.523, compare 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 1.265; μετὰ τοῖσιν 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 11.502; σὺν Λαπίθαισί σε Κενταύρων ὁμιλῆσαι δορί 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Andromache” 792 (Lyric poetry)]]: absolutely, join battle, εὖτ᾽ ἂν πρῶτον ὁμιλήσωσι φάλαγγες [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 19.158.]]

__III
of social intercourse, hold converse with, be acquainted with, associate with, τινι [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 3.130; κακοῖς ἀνδράσιν 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Persae” 753 (troch.)]]; ἀλλήλοις, μετ᾽ ἀλλήλων, πρὸς ἀλλήλους, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Symposium” 188d, “Plt.” 272c, “Lg.” 886c; τούτῳ τῷ τρόπῳ πρὸς τοὺς ἐρωμένους ὁ. [prev. author] “Phdr.” 252d]]; so of political intercourse, εἰθισμένος πρὸς ἡμᾶς ἀπὸ τοῦ ἴσου ὁ. [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 1.77; ἡμῖν ἀπὸ τοῦ ἴσου ὁ. [prev. author] 3.11]]; of scholars, ὁ. τινί frequent a teacher's lectures, be his pupil, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Memorabilia” 1.2.15, 39]]; ὁ. τῇ Ὁμήρου ποιήσει to be familiar with it, [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd c.AD: Lucianus Sophista “Pr.Im.” 26]]; compare ὁμιλητής.

__III.2
to be friends, οἱ μάλιστά τινι ὁμιλέοντες [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 3.99.]]

__III.3
speak to, address, harangue, with dative, [NT+2nd c.BC+ [2nd c.BC: Polybius Historicus 4.4.7: _absolutely_, ὑπερηφάνως ὁ. [prev. author] 16.34.6; πρὸς ἵππον 2nd c.AD: Babrius Fabularum Scriptor 15.2; πρὸς ἀλλήλους NT.Luke.24.14]]: generally, speak, converse, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [1st c.BC: Philodemus Gadarensis Epigrammaticus “Rh.” 1.116 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus; κατά τινα διάλεκτον 2nd c.AD: Sextus Empiricus Philosophus “adversus Mathematicos” 9.179; Ἑβραϊστί 1st c.AD: Josephus Historicus “Antiquitates Judaicae” 11.5.6]]; ὁ. τινὶ περί τινος talk to.., [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [“POxy.” 928.5 (2nd c.AD)]]:—passive, perfect participle ὡμιλημένος used in conversation, [Refs 1st c.BC+ [1st c.BC: Philodemus Gadarensis Epigrammaticus “Rh.” 2.27S.]]

__IV
of marriage or sexual intercourse, γυναιξὶ καὶ παρθένοις ὁ. [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 3.2.25; παιδικοῖς [prev. author] “Mem.” 2.1.24, etc.; σὺν τοῖς φιλτάτοις 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Tyrannus” 367, compare 1185; cf. Moer. p.276 P.]]

__V
of things or business which one has to do with, attend to, busy oneself with, ὁμιλεῖν ἀρχῇ, πολέμῳ, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 6.55, 70; καινοῖς πράγμασιν 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Nubes” 1399, compare ὁμιλία 1.4]]; φιλοσοφίᾳ, γυμναστικῇ, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 496b, 410c; παιδείᾳ “OGI” 505.7 (from Aezani)]]; ἐμ Μούσαις [Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. work]282.16 (5th c.BC: Magnes Comicus Mae., 3rd c.BC)]]; πονηροτάτοις σώμασιν ὁ., of a physician, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 408d]]; also like{χρῆσθαι}, meet with, enjoy, ὁ. τύχαις to be in good fortune, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “N.” 1.61; εὐτυχίᾳ ὁ. 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Orestes” 354 (Lyric poetry)]]; but also,

__V.2
of the things themselves, πλαγίαις φρένεσσιν ὄλβος οὐ πάντα χρόνον ὁ. does not consort with a crooked mind, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “I.” 3.6, compare “P.” 7.6]]; κυλίκων νεῖμεν ἐμοὶ τέρψιν ὁμιλεῖν gave me their delight to keep me company, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Ajax” 1201 (Lyric poetry); πλοῦτος καὶ δειλοῖσιν ἀνθρώπων ὁμιλεῖ 5th c.BC: Bacchylides Lyricus 1.51, compare 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Electra” 940: in physical sense, ὁ ὁ βραχίων τῷ κοίλῳ τῆς ὠμοπλάτης πλάγιος]] fils obliquely into.., [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Hippocrates Medicus “περὶ ἄρθρων ἐμβολῆς” 1]]; of a plaster, to be in contact, ὁ. τῷ νοσέοντι μέρει [Refs [[prev. author] “περὶ ἰητροῦ” 3.]]

__VI
deal with a man, bear oneself towards him, καλῶς ὁ. τινί [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Isocrates Orator “Epistulae” 4.9; πρός τινα [prev. author] 2.24; τῷ δήμῳ πρὸς χάριν 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Ἀθηναίων Πολιτεία” 35.3]] (so in passive, συνειθισμένοι ὑπὸ πάντων πρὸς χάριν ὁμιλεῖσθαι [Refs 1st c.BC+ [1st c.BC: Philodemus Philosophus “περὶ παρρησίας” p.62 O.)]]; ταῦτα ἡ ἐμὴ νεότης.. ἐς τὴν Πελοποννησίων δύναμιν.. ὡμίλησε these were the achievements of my youth in intercourse with their power, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 6.17.]]

__VII
of place, come into, enter, visit, with dative, διαβάντες τὸν Ἅλυν.. ὡμίλησαν τῇ Φρυγίῃ [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 7.26, compare 214, 5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “P.” 7.8]]; βαρεῖα χώρᾳ τῇδ᾽ ὁ. heavily will I visit this land, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Eumenides” 720; ὁ. παρ᾽ οἰκείαις ἀρούραις 5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “O.” 12.19; ὁ. τοιᾷδε πόλει 5th c.BC: Eupolis Comicus 292; poetry also ὁ. ἄνθεσιν 4th-5th c.BC: Simonides Lyricus 47]]:—passive, τὰ ὁμιλούμενα τῶν χωρίων most frequented, [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd-3rd c.AD: Philostratus Sophista “Vita Apollonii” 1.16.]]

__VIII
ἐκτὸς ὁμιλεῖ (i.e. τῶν ξυντρόφων ὀργῶν) he wanders from his senses, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Ajax” 640 (Lyric poetry).]]

[prev. author] “Pr.” 39, etc.]]; ὁ. τινός communion or intercourse with one, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 4.174; πρός τινα 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Philoctetes” 70, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Symposium” 203a, +others]]; τοὺς ἀξίους δὲ τῆς ἐμῆς ὁ. of my society, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Plutus” 776; ἡ σὴ ὁ. 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Hp.Ma.” 283d]]; ὁ. χθονός intercourse with a country, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Phoenissae” 1408]]; ἔχειν ἐν θεοῖς ὁ. live among them, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. author] “IA” [1622]; ἥκειν εἰς ὁ. τινί 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Tyrannus” 1489]]; ἡ καθ᾽ ὑμᾶς αὐτοὺς πολιτεία καὶ ὁ. public and private life, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 1.68]]; ἐξ ὁμιλίας by persuasion, opposed to βίᾳ, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator “Epistulae” 1.12]]: also in plural, ἀνθρώπων κακῶν-ίαι [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 7.16.α᾽,compare 1st-2nd c.AD: Epictetus Philosophus “Enchiridion” 33.14, etc.; φθείρουσιν ἤθη χρήσθ᾽ ὁ. κακαί 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Fragmenta” 1024 (= 4th-3rd c.BC: Menander Comicus 218)]]; Ἑλληνικαὶ ὁ. association with Greeks, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 4.77; ἐνδίκοις ὁ. 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Eumenides” 966 (Lyric poetry)]]; αἱ.. συγγενεῖς ὁ. intercourse with kinsfolk, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Troades” 51; ὁ. κακαῖς χρῆσθαι 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 550b; αἱ τῶν ἀνθρώπων ὁ. καὶ αἱ τῶν πραγμάτων 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Politica” 1336b32, etc.]]

__2

instruction, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Memorabilia” 1.2.6 and 15]]; lecture, [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd-3rd c.AD: Aelianus “Varia Historia” 3.19]]: in plural, title of work by [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Critias Philosophus, Tragicus, Elegiacus, 2nd c.AD: Galenus Medicus 18(2).656.]]

ὁμιλέειν ὁμιλίῃ to be versed in it by practice, opposed to λόγῳ εἰδέναι, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Hippocrates Medicus “περὶ ἄρθρων ἐμβολῆς” 10.]]

association, company, ἀνδρῶν τῶν ἀρίστων ἐπιλέξαντες ὁμιλίην [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 3.81, compare 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Eumenides” 57.]]

metaphorically, τὸ τῆς ψυχῆς ὄ. [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 533d, 4th c.AD: Iamblichus Philosophus “Protrepticus” 21.κδ᾽.]]

__II
the eye of heaven, i.e. the sun, ὄ. αἰθέρος [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Nubes” 285, compare 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Iphigenia Taurica” 194 (_anapaest meter_)]]; but ὄ. νυκτός is a periphrasis for night (see. below see), ἕως.. νυκτὸς ὄμμ᾽ ἀφείλετο (i.e. τὴν μάχην) [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Persae” 428]]; ὅταν δὲ νυκτὸς ὄ. λυγαίας μόλῃ the dark night, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Iphigenia Taurica” 110; νυκτὸς ὄ. τῆς μελαμπέπλου 2nd c.AD: Alexander Rhetor 89; compare ὀφθαλμός 111, βλέφαρον 11.]]

__III
generally, light: hence, metaphorically, that which brings light, ὄμμα ξείνοισι a light to strangers, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “P.” 5.56; ὄ. δόμων νομίζω δεσπότου παρουσίαν 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Persae” 169; ἄελπτον ὄμμ᾽ ἐμοὶ φήμης ἀνασχὸν τῆσδε 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Trachiniae” 203.]]

__III.2
metaphorically, anything dear or precious, as the apple of an eye, ὄ. γὰρ πάσης χθονὸς.. ἐξίκοιτ᾽ ἄν [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Eumenides” 1025.]]

__IV
face or human form, ὦ δυσθέατον ὄ. [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Ajax” 1004; ἐμπαίει τί μοι ψυχῇ ξύνηθες ὄ. [prev. author] “El.” 903; τὸ ἐρωτικὸν ὄ. 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Phaedrus” 253e: as periphrastic of the person, ὄ. πελείας, ={πελεία}, 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Ajax” 140 (_anapaest meter_)]]; ὄ. νύμφας, ={νύμφα}, [Refs [[prev. author] “Tr.” 527 (Lyric poetry)]]; ξύναιμον ὄ., ={ξυναίμων}, [Refs [[prev. author] “Aj.” 977]]; ὦ ταυρόμορφον ὄ. Κηφισοῦ, ={ὦ ταυρόμορφε Κηφισέ}, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Ion” 1261; see above 11 and compare ὄνομα IV.]]

__V
ὄ. τυκτόν eye-hole in a helmet, [Refs 4th c.AD+ [4th-5th c.AD(?): Nonnus Epicus “Dionysiaca” 22.62.]]

(El., § 39, 4), Mat.5:34, 36 23:16, 18 23:20-22 Rev.10:6 (Bl., § 70, 3).†

LSJ / STEPBible (TFLSJ)
ὄμνῡμι,
[Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “P.” 4.166, etc.]]; imperative ὄμνῠθι [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 23.585, ὄμνῡ 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Trachiniae” 1185, 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Medea” 746, cf. Oracle texts cited in 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 6.86. γ]]; 3rd.pers. singular ὀμνύτω [Refs [“IG” 12.134.5]]; 3rd.pers. plural ὀμνύντων. Foed. cited in [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 5.47, “IG” 12.87.24]]: imperfect ὤμνυν [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Aves” 520, “Ec.” 823, 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 17.10, etc.]]: also (from present ὀμνύω) 3rd.pers. singular imperative ὀμνῠέτω [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 19.175]]; participle ὀμνύουσα [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Hyperides Orator “adv. Athenogenem” 2]]: imperfect ὤμνῠον [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 14.278, Foed. cited in 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 5.19, 24, “IG” 22.236.14, etc.]] (for present indicative the Trag. and [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus use only ὄμνυμι, 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus and _Attic dialect_ Prose writers also ὀμνύω,]] which also occurs in Comedy texts, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Pherecrates Comicus 143.9, 4th c.BC: Amphis Comicus 42, 4th-3rd c.BC: Diphilus Comicus 101, 4th c.BC: Antiphanes Comicus 241.1, 2nd c.AD: Alexander Rhetor 160; in 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.153 ὀμνύντες is restored for the uncertain form ὀμοῦντες)]]: future ὀμοῦμαι, εῖ, εῖται, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 1.233, 9.274, 8th-7th c.BC: Hesiodus Epicus “Opera et Dies” 194, 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Nubes” 246, “Lys.” 193, 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Historia Graeca (Hellenica)” 1.3.11, etc.]]; Doric dialect 1st pers. plural ὀμιώμεθα [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Lysistrata” 183]]; later future ὀμόσω [Refs 1st c.AD+ [“Anthologia Graeca” 12.201 (2nd c.AD: Strato Epigrammaticus), 1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus “Cicero” 23, etc.]]: aorist ὤμοσα [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 4.253, etc.]]; Epic dialect ὤμοσσα [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 20.313; _Epic dialect_ also without augment ὄμοσα, -οσσα, 19.113, 10.328]]: perfect ὀμώμοκα [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Hippolytus” 612, 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Ranae” 1471, etc.]]: pluperfect ὠμωμόκειν [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Historia Graeca (Hellenica)” 5.1.35, 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 9.16, 19.318]]:—middle, [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd c.AD: Pausanias Periegeta 10.26.3]], aorist participle ὀμοσάμενος [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [“SIG” 531.28 (Dyme, 3rd c.BC), “IG” 5(2).357.11 (from Stymphalus), also in compounds ἀντ-, ἀπ-, δι-, ὑπ-]]:—passive, future ὀμοσθήσομαι [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Andocides Orator 3.34]]: aorist ὠμόσθην [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Historia Graeca (Hellenica)” 7.4.10, (ὑπ-) 4th c.BC: Hyperides Orator “Fragmenta” 202; but ὠμόθην 4th c.BC: Isaeus Orator 2.40, (ὑπ-) 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 48.25]]: perfect 3rd.pers. singular ὀμώμοται [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Agamemnon” 1284, ὀμώμοσται 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Rhesus” 816, 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Rhetorica” 1377a11]]; 3rd.pers. plural ὀμώμονται Legal cited in [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Andocides Orator 1.98]]; participle ὀμωμοσμένος [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 7.10, 22.4, 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Rhetorica” 1377b7 (ὠμοσμένος see reading in 2nd c.AD: Appianus Historicus “Αιβυκή” 83, etc.)]]:—swear, with accusative cognate, ὀμνυέτω δέ τοι ὅρκον [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 19.175, +others; ὅτις κ᾽ ἐπίορκον ὀμόσσῃ 3.279; ἑκὼν ἐπίορκον ὀμόσσας 8th-7th c.BC: Hesiodus Epicus “Opera et Dies” 282: with _dative_ _person_, νῦν μοι ὄμοσσον.. ὅρκον 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 19.108, +others; πρός τινα 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 14.331, 19.288]]:—passive, ὀμώμοται γὰρ ὅοκος ἐκ θεῶν [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Agamemnon” 1284; ὅρκων ὀμωμος μένων 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 7.10; εἰ ὀμώμοσται οὗτος [ὁ ὅρκος] 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Rhetorica” 1377a11, compare b7.]]

__II
swear to a thing, affirm or confirm by oath,

__II.1
followed by accusative, ταῦτα δ᾽ ἐγὼν ἐθέλω ὀμόσαι [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 19.187, compare 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Coloneus” 1145, 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Agesilaus” 1.11]]; ὄ. τὰς σπονδάς Foed. cited in [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 5.47; τὴν εἰρήνην 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 18.32, compare 9.16; θεῶν πίστεις τινί 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 5.30, etc.]]

__II.2
followed by future infinitive, swear that one will.., [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 21.373, etc., compare 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Philoctetes” 623, 941]] (present infinitive, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 21.188 codices): frequently with ἦ μέν, _Attic dialect_ ἦ μήν,]] preceding the infinitive, καί μοι ὄμοσσον ἦ μέν μοι.. ἀρήξειν [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 1.76, compare 10.321, 5th c.BC: Lysias Orator 31.1, 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Historia Graeca (Hellenica)” 5.3.26, etc.: also by]]aorist infinitive and ἄν, [Refs [[prev. author] “An.” 7.7.40]]: by present infinitive, swear that one does.., [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Philoctetes” 357]]: by perfect infinitive, swear that one has.., [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 21.119; ὤμνυς μὴ γεγονέναι 5th c.BC: Magnes Comicus 6]]: by aorist infinitive, swear that one did.., ὀμνύουσι μὴ 'κπιεῖν ἀλλ᾽ ἢ μίαν [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Pherecrates Comicus 143.9, compare 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 2.179]](aorist infinitive is perhaps used, without ἄν, in future sense, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 23.170 (assuming variant))]]: sometimes a clause follows in the indicative, ὀμνύω.., ἦ μὴν ἐγὼ ἐθυόμην [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 6.1.31; ὄμνυμί σοι.., οὐκ ἤθελον.. 3rd c.BC: Theocritus Poeta Bucolicus “Adon.” 22.]]

__II.3
absolutely, εἶπον ὀμόσας ἄν I would have given my word of honour, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Symposium” 215d.]]

__III
with accusative of the person or thing sworn by, swear by, νῦν μοι ὄμοσσον ἀάατον Στυγὸς ὕδωρ [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 14.271; γαιήοχον ἐννοσίγαιον ὄμνυθι 23.585, compare 15.40, 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 5.7, 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Septem contra Thebas” 529, 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Trachiniae” 1185, etc.; ὀμωμοκὼς τοὺς θεούς 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 18.217]]; ὄμνυμι θεοὺς καὶ θεάς followed by infinitive, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 6.6.17, compare 6.1.31: rarely with _dative_, τῷ γὰρ ὄμνυτ᾽]]; ἢ σιδαρέοισ; [NT+5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Nubes” 248: in Prose also with Preps., ὀ. καθ᾽ ἱερῶν τελείων Legal cited in 5th-6th c.BC: Andocides Orator 1.97, 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 5.47; κατ᾽ ἐξωλείας 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 21.119; κατὰ τῆς Πολιάδος 2nd c.AD: Lucianus Sophista “Symp.” 32; εἰς τὸν Οὐιτέλλιον 1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus “Otho” 18; ἐπὶ τῶν ἱερῶν 2nd c.BC: Polybius Historicus 38.20.5; ἐν Κυρίῳ LXX.Judg.21.7; ἐν τῷ ναῷ NT.Matt.23.16:—]]passive, ὀμώμοσται Ζεύς Zeus has been sworn by, adjured, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Rhesus” 816, compare 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Nubes” 1241.]]

Rev.1:15 2:18 4:6-7 9:7, 10 (B1., § 37, 62) Rev_9:19; Rev_11:1; Rev_13:2; Rev_13:11; ὁράσει, Rev_4:3; of nature, condition, ability, etc., Mat_22:39, Act_17:29, Gal_5:21, 1Jn_3:2, Rev_13:4; Rev_18:18; Rev_21:11; Rev_21:18; of comparison in parables, Mat_13:31 ff. LSJ / STEPBible (TFLSJ)
ὅμοιος
or (as in [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Homerus Epicus, _Ionic dialect_, and old _Attic dialect_)]] ὁμοῖος, α, ον (compare ἐρῆμος, ἑτοῖμος): later Epic dialect also ὁμοίιος (B, which see); Aeolic dialect ὔμοιος [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [3rd c.BC: Theocritus Poeta Bucolicus 29.20]] (adverb -ως[Refs 4th c.AD+ [“IG” 12(2).69a6); 4th c.AD(?): Arcadius Grammaticus]] ὑμοῖος [Refs 4th c.BC+ [“Schwyzer” 665 A 15 (Orchom., 4th c.BC)]]: (ὁμός):—like, resembling, ὡς αἰεὶ τὸν ὁ. ἄγει θεὸς ὡς τὸν ὁ. 'birds of a feather flock together', [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 17.218; ὁ ὅ. τῷ ὁ. 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Gorgias” 510b; ὁ ὅ. ὡς τὸν ὅ. 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Ethica Nicomachea” 1155a34; τὸ ὅ. τῷ ὁ. φίλον [prev. work] 1165b17, see below 6]]; ὡς ἐπὶ τῶν ὁ. as in similar cases (of persons), [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [“BGU” 79.18 (2nd c.AD)]], etc.: comparative -ότερος more like, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Phaedo” 79b]]: superlative -ότατος most like, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 2.92, 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Antigone” 833 (Lyric poetry), etc.]]

__2
the same, ἄμφω γὰρ πέπρωται ὁμοίην γαῖαν ἐρεῦσαι [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 18.329; χρὼς οὐκέθ᾽ ὁ. 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 16.182]]; hence (i.e. ἑαυτῷ), always the same, unchanging, αἰεὶ πόδας καὶ χεῖρας ὁμοῖοι [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th-7th c.BC: Hesiodus Epicus “Opera et Dies” 114; ὅ. τὴν γνώμην]]the same as ever, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Antipho Orator 5.76; γνῶμαι πρὸς τοὺς αὐτοὺς κινδύνους ὁμοῖαι 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 2.89; ἀεὶ ὅ. εἶ, ὦ Ἀπολλόδωρε 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Symposium” 173d]]; ἓν καὶ ὅ. one and the same, [Refs [[prev. author] “Phdr.” 271a.]]

__3
equal in force, a match for one, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 23.632, 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 9.96.]]

__4
of things, suiting, according with, πολλά τε καὶ ὅ. ἑαυταῖς [Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. author] “R.” 549e; ὅ. τῇ φύσει 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Thesmophoriazusae” 167.]]

__5
ὁμοῖον ἡμῖν ἔσται it will be all the same, all one to us, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 8.80; σὺ δ᾽ αἰνεῖν εἴτε με ψέγειν θέλεις, ὁμοῖον 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Agamemnon” 1404, compare 1239, 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Supplices” 1069; ἐν τῷ ὁ. καθειστήκει 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 2.49.]]

__6
τὸ ὅ. ἀνταποδιδόναι give 'tit for tat', [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.18]]; so τὴν ὁμοίην (i.e. δίκην, χάριν) ἀποδιδόναι τινί [Refs [[prev. author] 4.119, 6.21, 62]]; τὴν ὁ. φέρεσθαι παρά τινος to have a like return made one, [Refs [[prev. passage]; ἐπ᾽ ἴσῃ καὶ ὁμοίᾳ, see at {ἴσος} II.2.]]

__7
ἐν ὁμοίῳ ποιεῖσθαί τι hold a thing in like esteem, [Refs [[prev. author] 7.138, 8.109.]]

__8
to be uniform, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Physica” 261b25: proverbial, οὐδ᾽ ὅκου χώρης οἱ μῦς ὁ. τὸν σίδηρον τρώγουσιν]]like any other food, [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [3rd c.BC: Herodas Mimographus 3.76]] (but perhaps all alike,[Refs 5th c.BC+ [compare 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Equites” 1296 codex R, 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 5.15 (assuming variant), 1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus 2.763c)]]: comparative -ότερον[Refs 1st c.AD+ [“Anthologia Graeca” 11.233 (1st c.AD: Lucillius Epigrammaticus)]]: superlative -ότατα[Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Fragmenta” 281.]]

Included with:  ὅμοιος
or (as in [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Homerus Epicus, _Ionic dialect_, and old _Attic dialect_)]] ὁμοῖος, α, ον (compare ἐρῆμος, ἑτοῖμος): later Epic dialect also ὁμοίιος (B, which see); Aeolic dialect ὔμοιος [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [3rd c.BC: Theocritus Poeta Bucolicus 29.20]] (adverb -ως[Refs 4th c.AD+ [“IG” 12(2).69a6); 4th c.AD(?): Arcadius Grammaticus]] ὑμοῖος [Refs 4th c.BC+ [“Schwyzer” 665 A 15 (Orchom., 4th c.BC)]]: (ὁμός):—like, resembling, ὡς αἰεὶ τὸν ὁ. ἄγει θεὸς ὡς τὸν ὁ. 'birds of a feather flock together', [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 17.218; ὁ ὅ. τῷ ὁ. 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Gorgias” 510b; ὁ ὅ. ὡς τὸν ὅ. 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Ethica Nicomachea” 1155a34; τὸ ὅ. τῷ ὁ. φίλον [prev. work] 1165b17, see below 6]]; ὡς ἐπὶ τῶν ὁ. as in similar cases (of persons), [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [“BGU” 79.18 (2nd c.AD)]], etc.: comparative -ότερος more like, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Phaedo” 79b]]: superlative -ότατος most like, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 2.92, 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Antigone” 833 (Lyric poetry), etc.]]

__2
the same, ἄμφω γὰρ πέπρωται ὁμοίην γαῖαν ἐρεῦσαι [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 18.329; χρὼς οὐκέθ᾽ ὁ. 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 16.182]]; hence (i.e. ἑαυτῷ), always the same, unchanging, αἰεὶ πόδας καὶ χεῖρας ὁμοῖοι [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th-7th c.BC: Hesiodus Epicus “Opera et Dies” 114; ὅ. τὴν γνώμην]]the same as ever, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Antipho Orator 5.76; γνῶμαι πρὸς τοὺς αὐτοὺς κινδύνους ὁμοῖαι 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 2.89; ἀεὶ ὅ. εἶ, ὦ Ἀπολλόδωρε 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Symposium” 173d]]; ἓν καὶ ὅ. one and the same, [Refs [[prev. author] “Phdr.” 271a.]]

__3
equal in force, a match for one, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 23.632, 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 9.96.]]

__4
of things, suiting, according with, πολλά τε καὶ ὅ. ἑαυταῖς [Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. author] “R.” 549e; ὅ. τῇ φύσει 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Thesmophoriazusae” 167.]]

__5
ὁμοῖον ἡμῖν ἔσται it will be all the same, all one to us, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 8.80; σὺ δ᾽ αἰνεῖν εἴτε με ψέγειν θέλεις, ὁμοῖον 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Agamemnon” 1404, compare 1239, 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Supplices” 1069; ἐν τῷ ὁ. καθειστήκει 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 2.49.]]

__6
τὸ ὅ. ἀνταποδιδόναι give 'tit for tat', [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.18]]; so τὴν ὁμοίην (i.e. δίκην, χάριν) ἀποδιδόναι τινί [Refs [[prev. author] 4.119, 6.21, 62]]; τὴν ὁ. φέρεσθαι παρά τινος to have a like return made one, [Refs [[prev. passage]; ἐπ᾽ ἴσῃ καὶ ὁμοίᾳ, see at {ἴσος} II.2.]]

__7
ἐν ὁμοίῳ ποιεῖσθαί τι hold a thing in like esteem, [Refs [[prev. author] 7.138, 8.109.]]

__8
to be uniform, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Physica” 261b25: proverbial, οὐδ᾽ ὅκου χώρης οἱ μῦς ὁ. τὸν σίδηρον τρώγουσιν]]like any other food, [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [3rd c.BC: Herodas Mimographus 3.76]] (but perhaps all alike,[Refs 5th c.BC+ [compare 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Equites” 1296 codex R, 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 5.15 (assuming variant), 1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus 2.763c)]]: comparative -ότερον[Refs 1st c.AD+ [“Anthologia Graeca” 11.233 (1st c.AD: Lucillius Epigrammaticus)]]: superlative -ότατα[Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Fragmenta” 281.]]

future -ιῶ[Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Tyrannus” 1423, 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Troades” 430, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Apologia” 30a:]]aorist ὠνείδισα (Epic dialect ὀν-) [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 9.34, etc.]]: perfect ὠνείδικα [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Lysias Orator 16.15]]:—passive, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Troades” 936, etc.:]]future middle ὀνειδιεῖσθε (in passive sense) [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Tyrannus” 1500]]: aorist ὠνειδίσθην [Refs 2nd c.BC+ [2nd c.BC: Polybius Historicus 11.4.10:]]

__I
cast in one's teeth, make a reproach to one, usually with accusative of things et dative person, ἀλκὴν μέν μοι πρῶτον ὀνείδισας [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 9.34, compare 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 18.380, 8th-7th c.BC: Hesiodus Epicus “Opera et Dies” 718, 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.90, 8.106; αἰσχύνομαί σοι τοῦτ᾽ ὀνειδίσαι 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Choephori” 917; ἃ δ᾽ εἰς γάμους μοι βασιλικοὺς ὠνείδισας 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Medea” 547; ὀ. φόνον [τινί] 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 21.120; ὄνειδος ὀ. εἴς τινα 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Coloneus” 754, “Ph.” 523]]: with a relative clause instead of the accusative, Ἀγαμέμνονι.. ὀνειδίζων, ὅτι.. [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 2.255, compare 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Apologia” 30a, +others; ὀ. τινί, ὡς.. 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Memorabilia” 2.9.8, compare 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 1.211 (without _dative_); ὀ. εἰς ἀχαριστίαν τινί, διότι.. 2nd c.BC: Polybius Historicus 28.4.11]]: with infinitive, εἴ τίς τῳ ὀ. φιλοκερδεῖ εἶναι [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Hipparchus” 232c; ὀ. τινὶ τετρῆσθαι τὰ ὦτα 3rd c.AD(?): Diogenes Laertius 2.50: without _dative_ _person_, ὀνειδιῶν τι τῶν πάρος κακῶν]]make a reproach, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Tyrannus” 1423, compare 441, 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 8.143]]:—passive, to be made a reproach, καὶ σχεδὸν δὴ πάντα.. οὐκ ὀρθῶς ὀνειδίζεται [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Timaeus” 86d, compare 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 1.77.]]

__II
without accusative of things, reproach, upbraid,

__II.1
with dative person, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Lysias Orator 27.16, etc.; τισὶ περί τινος 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 4.79; [τινὶ] ἔς τι [prev. author] 8.92; without _dative_ _person_, 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 7.95.]]

__II.2
with accusative person, chide, reproach, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Apologia” 30e]]; τοιαῦτ᾽ ὀνειδίζεις με thus dost thou reproach me, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Coloneus” 1002]]; also ἐπειδὴ.. τυφλόν μ᾽ ὠνείδισας (i.e. ὄντα) didstreproach me with being blind, [Refs [[prev. author] “OT” 412]]:—passive, to be reproached, ἔκ τινων [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Troades” 936; εἰς δειλίαν 1st c.BC: Diodorus Siculus Historicus 20.62; τὴν μικροπολιτείαν]]with.., [Refs 5th c.AD+ [5th c.AD: Stobaeus, Joannes 3.39.29.]]

_imperative_ ὄνησο 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 19.68]]; participle ὀνήμενος [Refs [2.33]] (compare ἀπ-); also ὠνάμην, ὤνασθε [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Hercules Furens” 1368, ὤναο 3rd c.BC: Callimachus Epicus “Aetia” 3.1.6, and frequently later, 2nd c.AD: Lucianus Sophista “D Mort.” 12.2, etc.; ὤνατο “IG” 14.1389 ii 37, ὤναντο 1st c.BC: Dionysius Halicarnassensis 1.23]]; infinitive ὄνασθαι [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Hippolytus” 517, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 528a; _optative_ ὀναίμην, which is frequently (see. below 11.2)]], may belong to either form: in [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Homerus Epicus ὠνάμην is the]]aorist I of ὄνομαι:—passive ὀνέομαι occurs twice, ὀνεῖται [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [5th c.AD: Stobaeus, Joannes 4.22.62, ὀνούμενοι Ps.- 2nd c.AD: Lucianus Sophista “Philopatr.” 26]]: aorist infinitive ὀνηθῆναι [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 5.5.2]]; Doric dialect ὠνάθην [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [3rd c.BC: Theocritus Poeta Bucolicus 15.55:]]

__I
active, profit, benefit, help, and sometimes gratify, delight, absolutely, βουλὴν.. ὑποθησόμεθ᾽ ἥτις ὀνήσει [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 8.36, compare 8th-7th c.BC: Hesiodus Epicus “Theogonia” 429, 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Medea” 533, etc.]]: with neuter adjective or adverb, ὀ. παῦρα [Refs 8th c.BC+ [“hymnus ad Mercurium” 577; σμικρὰ ὀνήσει πόλιν 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Heraclidae” 705 (_anapaest meter_), compare 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Philebus” 58c; μᾶλλον 4th-5th c.BC: Simonides Lyricus 55, 2nd c.AD: Aretaeus Medicus “ὀξέων νούσων θεραπευτικόν” 1.4: c._accusative_ _person_, 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 5.205, 7.172, Oracle texts cited in 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 7.141, 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Hippolytus” 314, 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Lysistrata” 1033, etc.]]: with neuter adjective, ἄνδρας μέγα σίνεται ἠδ᾽ ὀνίνησι [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 24.45, compare 9.509, variant in 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 3.1.38, etc.; πολλὰ ὀ. τινά 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 14.67; τοσόνδε 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Troades” 933; εἴ ποτε δή τι 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 1.395: with _dative_ modi, εἴ ποτε δή σε ὄνησα ἢ ἔπει ἢ ἔργῳ [prev. work] 503: with]]participle, Ξενοφῶντα ὠνήσατε οὐχ ἑλόμενοι by not electing him, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 6.1.32, compare 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Symposium” 193d, “Hp.Ma.” 301c; ὡς ὤνησας ὅτι ἀπεκρίνω [prev. author] “Ap.” 27c: with double _accusative_, σὲ δὲ τοῦτό γε γῆρας ὀνήσει]] this benefit at least will thine old age bestow on thee, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 23.24]]; also οὐδεμίαν ὤνησε κάλλος εἰς πόσιν ξυνάορον helped her in her relations with.., [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Fragmenta” 909.1.]]

__II
middle, have profit or advantage, enjoy help or support, have enjoyment or delight, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 6.260, 7.173, 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 14.415, 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Hippolytus” 517, etc.]]: with participle, have benefit from being or doing so and so, [Refs 6th c.BC+ [6th c.BC: Theognis Elegiacus 1380, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Apologia” 30c, “R.” 380b, “Men.” 84c, etc.]]: but most frequently with genitive, have advantage from.., have delight or enjoyment of.., δαιτὸς ὄνησο [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 19.68; λέκτρων -ήσομαι 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Medea” 1348]]; πρὶν σφῷν ὄνασθαι[Refs [[prev. work] 1025, cf. Alcaeus335: frequently with _neuter_]] adjective added, τί σευ ἄλλος ὀνήσετα; what good will others have of thee, i. e. what good will you have done them? [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 16.31; τοσόνδ᾽ ὀνήσῃ τῶν ἐμῶν.. πορθμῶν 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Trachiniae” 570, etc.; so ὄνασθαί τι ἀπό τινος 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 528a; also ὀ. τοῦτο ὅτι.. 2nd c.AD: Lucianus Sophista “DMort.” 12.2: also with an ironical sense, ὄναιο μέντἄν, εἴ τις ἐκπλύνειέ σε]] you'd be the better of it, if one were to wash you clean, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Plutus” 1062]]; ἁλσὶν διασμηχθεὶς ὄναιτ᾽ ἂν οὑτοσί he'd be very nice if he were rubbed down with salt, [Refs [[prev. author] “Nu.” 1237]]; so ὠνάθην μεγάλως ὅτι.. lucky for me that.., [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [3rd c.BC: Theocritus Poeta Bucolicus 15.55; ὤνησο, διότι μὴ ὁ Ζεὺς ἐπήκουσέ σου 2nd c.AD: Lucianus Sophista “Prom.” 20.]]

__II.2
aorist optative ὀναίμην, αιο, αιτο, in protestations, wishes, etc., ὄναιο mayst thou have profit, i. e. bless thee.., [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Orestes” 1677, etc.: and with _genitive_, ὄναιο τῶν φρενῶν]] bless thee for.., [Refs [[prev. author] “IA” 1359; ὄναισθε μύθων [prev. author] “IT” 1078, compare “Hel.” 1418]]; οὕτως ὀναίμην τῶν τέκνων so may I have profit of them, in a parenthesis, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Thesmophoriazusae” 469; οὕτως ὄναισθε τούτων 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 28.20; ὄναιντο βίου 4th-5th c.BC: Simonides Lyricus 128]]; μή νυν ὀναίμην, ἀλλ᾽.. ὀλοίμην may I not see good, but die, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Tyrannus” 644]]; ὄναιο τοῦ γενναίου χάριν bless thee for thy noble spirit, [Refs [[prev. author] “OC” 1042.]]

__II.3
aorist participle ὀνήμενος, of those to whom (or of whom) one says ὄναιο (ὄναιτο), blessed, ἐσθλός μοι δοκεῖ εἶναι, ὀνήμενος [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 2.33: for this sense of a]]participle compare ἐπίτριπτος, οὐλόμενος.

Abbott-Smith / STEPBible (TBESG)
ὄνομα, -τος, τό,
[in LXX chiefly for שֵׁם ;]
__1. in general, the name by which a person or thing is called: Mat.10:2, Mrk.3:16, Luk.1:63, Jhn.18:10,  al.; ἄνθρωπος (etc.), ᾧ (οὗ) ὄ. (τ. ὄ), sc. ἦν or ἐστίν (BL, §30, 3), Mrk.14:32, Luk.1:26, 27; with same ellipsis, καὶ τ. ὄ. αὐτοῦ, Luk.1:5, Jhn.1:6, al.; ὀνόματι, before nom. prop., Mat.27:32, Mrk.5:22, Luk.1:5, Act.5:1, al.; accusative absol. (Bl., §34, 7), τοὔνομα (= τ. ὄνομα), Mat.27:57; ὄ. μοι (sc. ἐστίν; cf. Hom., Od., ix, 366), Mrk.5:9 (cf. Luk.8:30); ἔξειν ὄ., Rev.9:11; καλεῖν (ἐπιτιθέναι) ὄ. (Bl., §33, 1), Mat.1:21, Mrk.3:16; τ. ὄ. ἐν (τ.) βίβλῳ ζωῆς (cf. Deiss., LAE, 121), Php.4:3, Rev.13:8, cf. Luk.10:20 (ἐν τ. οὐρανοῖς); ὄ. βλασφημίας, Rev.13:1; the name as opposite to the reality, Rev.3:1 (cf. Hdt., vii, 138); as a title: Eph.1:21, Php.2:9, 10 (Lft., in l.).
__2. By a usage similar to that with ref. to Heb. שֵׁם (Lft., Notes, 106f.), but also common in Hellenistic (M, Pr., 100; Bl., §39, 4; Deiss, BS, 146f., 196f.; LAE, 123:4, of all that the name implies, of rank, authority, character, etc.: of acting on one's authority or in his behalf, ἐν (εἰς) ὄ., with genitive of person(s) (see reff. supr.), Mat.10:41 21:9 28:19, Mrk.11:9, Luk.13:35, Jhn.5:43, Act.8:16, 1Co.1:13; of the name Christian, 1Pe.4:16; esp. of the name of God as expressing the divine attributes: ἁγιάζειν (ἅγιον) τὸ ὄ. (τ. Πατρός, Κυρίου), Mat.6:9, Luk.1:49 11:2; ψάλλειν (ὁμολογεῖν) τῷ ὀ., Rom.15:9, Heb.13:15; δοξάζειν (φανεροῦν, φοβεῖσθαι) τὸ ὄ., Jhn.12:28 17:6, 26 Rev.11:18 15:4; βλασφημεῖν, Rom.2:24, 1Ti.6:1, Rev.13:6; similarly, of the name of Christ: τ. καλὂν ὄ. (Deiss., LAE, 276); πιστεύειν τῷ ὀ., 1Jn.3:23; π. εἰς τ. ὄ. (Bl., §39, 4), Jhn.1:12 2:23 3:18; ὀνομάζειν τὸ ὄ., 2Ti.2:19; κρατεῖν, Rev.2:13; οὐκ ἀρνεῖσθαι, Rev.3:8; ἐν τ. ὀ. (see reff. supr.), Mrk.9:38 16:[17], Luk.10:17, Jhn.14:13 16:23, 24 20:31, Act.3:6 4:12, Eph.5:20, 1Pe.4:14, al.; εἰς τ. ὄ. συνάγεσθαι, Mat.18:20; ἕνεκεν τοῦ ὀ., Mat.19:29; διὰ τὸ ὄ., Mat.10:22, Mrk.13:13, al.; διὰ τοῦ ὀ., 1Co.1:10; ὑπὲρ τοῦ ὀ., Act.9:16, Rom.1:5, al.; id. absol., Act.5:41, 3Jo.7; πρὸς τὸ ὄ., Act.26:9.
__3. cause, ground, reason (in cl., usually in bad sense, pretext): Mrk.9:41 (Swete, in l.; Dalman, Words, 305f.).
__4. In late Greek (Deiss., BS., 196f.), an individual, a person: Act.1:15, Rev.3:4 11:13.
(AS)

ὄνομα,
Aeolic dialect and Doric dialect ὄνῠμα [Refs [“IG” 12(2).68.8 (Lesb.), “GDI” 4992a iii 7 (from Crete), “SIG” 1122.8 (from Selinus), “Berl.Sitzb.” 1927.167 (from Cyrene)]]; Laconian dialect *ἔνυμα probably in proper nouns Ἐνυμακρατίδας [Refs [“IG” 5(1).213.45, Ἐνυμαντιάδας [prev. work] 97.20, 280.2]]; poetry also (for the sake of meter) οὔνομα (see.below), which appears regularly in codices of [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus (along with ὀνομάζω, as 2.50, 4.35, +others)]], and sometimes in other Ionic dialect prose authors (variant in [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Hippocrates Medicus “προγνωστικόν” 25, etc.)]], but is probably not Ionic; Ionic dialect Inscrr. have only ὄνομα, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [“IG” 7.235.39 (from Oropus), etc.: 8th c.BC: Homerus Epicus has οὔνομα 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 6.194, 9.355, 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 3.235, οὐνόματ᾽ (α) 17.260, ὄνομα 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 9.16, 364, 366, 19.183, ὄνομ᾽ (α) 4.710]] et saep.:—name of a person or thing, in [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Homerus Epicus]] always of a person, except ἐρέω δέ τοι οὔνομα λαῶν [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 6.194 and in 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 13.248 (see. infr. II); Οὖτις ἐμοί γ᾽ ὄ. 9.366, compare 18.5, 19.183, 247]]; Ἀρήτη δ᾽ ὄνομ᾽ ἐστὶν ἐπώνυμον [Refs 8th c.BC+ [7.54, compare 19.409, 8th-7th c.BC: Hesiodus Epicus “Theogonia” 144: in Prose ὄνομα]] is used absolutely, by name, πόλις ὄ. Καιναί [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 2.4.28, etc.: also _dative_, πόλις Θάψακος ὀνόματι [prev. work] 1.4.11 (variant)]]; ὀνόματι λέγειν by name, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Apologia” 21c; ἐπ᾽ ὀνόματος δηλοῦσθαι 2nd c.BC: Polybius Historicus 18.45.4, etc.]]; κατ᾽ ὄνομα by name, [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [3rd c.BC(?): Strato Comicus 1.14, “epigram Gr.” 983.4 (from Philae)]]; ἀσπάζου τοὺς φίλους κατ᾽ ὄ. each by his name, [NT.3John.14.]

__2
ὄ. τίθεσθαι or θέσθαι τινί give one a name, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 19.403, 406, 8.554, 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Fragmenta - American Journal of Philology” 6, 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Aves” 810:]] —passive, ὄ. κεῖταί τινι[Refs [[prev. work] 1291]]; ὄ. ἐστι or κεῖται ἐπί τινι, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Memorabilia” 3.14.2, “Cyr.” 2.2.12]]; so ὄ. φέρειν or ἐπιφέρειν ἐπί τι, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Ethica Nicomachea” 1119a33, “HA” 572a11.]]

__3
ὄνομα καλεῖν τινα call one by name, εἴπ᾽ ὄνομ᾽, ὅττι σε κεῖθι κάλεον [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 8.550; καλοῦσί με τοῦτο τὸ ὄ. 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Oeconomicus” 7.3, compare 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Ion” 259, 800, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Cratylus” 393e, etc.]]:—so in passive, ὄ. δ᾽ ὠνομάζετο Ἕλενος [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Philoctetes” 605, compare “El.” 694; ὄ. δημοκρατία κέκληται 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 2.37; τὸ ἐναντίον ὄ. ἀφροσύνη μετωνόμασται [prev. author] 1.122; ὄ. ἓν κεκλημένους Σικελιώτας [prev. author] 4.64; λεγόμενοι τοὔνομα γεωργικοί 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Leges” 842e; but also ὀνόματί τινα προσαγορεύειν 5th c.BC: Antipho Orator 6.40]]; reversely, ὄνομα καλεῖν τινι give a name to, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Politicus” 279e, “Cra.” 385d; ὄ. καλεῖν ἐπί τινι [prev. author] “Prm.” 147d; τύμβῳ δ᾽ ὄ. σῷ κεκλήσεται.. Κυνὸς σῆμα 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Hecuba” 1271; τοὔνομα προσηγορεύθη 4th c.BC: Anaxilas Comicus 21.3.]]

__II
name, fame, Ἰθάκης γε καὶ ἐς Τροίην ὄνομ᾽ ἵκει [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 13.248; οὐδὲ θανὼν ὄνομ᾽ ὤλεσας 24.93]]; ὄ. ἔχειν or σχεῖν ἀπό τινος, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.71, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Hp.Ma.” 282a; τὸ μεγα ὄ. τῶν Ἀθηνῶν 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 7.64; τῷ μέλλοντι χρόνῳ καταλιπεῖν ὄ. ὡς.. [prev. author] 5.16; τοὔνομά τινος μεῖζον ἀφικνεῖται εἰς τὴν πόλιν 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 6.1.20; ὧν ὀνόματα μεγάλα λέγεται ἐπὶ σοφίᾳ 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Hp.Ma.” 281c; ὄ. μέγιστον ἔχειν 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 2.64]]; ἐν ὀνόματι εἶναι to have a name, to be notable, [Refs 2nd c.BC+ [1st c.BC-1st c.AD: Strabo Geographus 9.1.23; οἱ ἐν πράγμασιν ἐπ᾽ ὀνόματος γεγονότες 2nd c.BC: Polybius Historicus 15.35.1; παράσιτοι δ᾽ ἐπ᾽ ὀνόματος ἐγένοντο]]notably, [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd c.AD: Athenaeus Epigrammaticus 6.240c; τῶν δι᾽ ὀνόματος παρασίτων [prev. work] 241a.]]

__III
a name and nothing else, opposed to the real person or thing, ἵνα μηδ᾽ ὄνομ᾽ αὐτοῦ ἐν ἀνθρώποισι λίπηται [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 4.710; βοᾶς δ᾽ ἔτι μηδ᾽ ὄνομ᾽ εἴη 3rd c.BC: Theocritus Poeta Bucolicus 16.97]]; opposed to ἔργον, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Orestes” 454, “Hipp.” 502; περὶ ὄ. μάχεσθαι 5th c.BC: Lysias Orator 33.3; ἐκ τῶν ὀ. μᾶλλον ἢ τῶν πραγμάτων σκέψασθαι 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 9.15]]; ὀνόματι διαφέρεσθαι dispute about a word, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Euthydemus” 285a, “Lg.” 644a.]]

__III.2
false name, pretence, pretext, ὀνόματι ἐννόμῳ ξυμμαχίας under the pretence.., [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 4.60; μετ᾽ ὀνομάτων καλῶν [prev. author] 5.89; χώρα καλῶν ὀ. καὶ προσχημάτων μεστή 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 495c, compare 2nd c.BC: Polybius Historicus 11.5.4.]]

__IV
in periphrastic phrases, ὄ. τῆς σωτηρίας, ={σωτηρία}, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Iphigenia Taurica” 905, compare ὄνομ᾽ ὁμιλίας ἐμῆς (variant for ὄμμ᾽) [prev. author] “Or.” 1082]]: with the names of persons, periphrastic for the person, ὦ φίλτατον ὄ. Πολυνείκους [Refs [[prev. author] “Ph.” 1702.]]

__IV.2
of persons, ὄχλος ὀνομάτων [NT.Act.1.15]; ἕτερα ὀ. ἀντ᾽ αὐτοῦ.. πέμψαι Wilcken [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [“Chr.” 28.19 (2nd c.AD)]]; in Accountancy, both of persons and things (cf. Latin nomen), [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Hyperides Orator “adv. Athenogenem” 6, 10 (both _plural_), “Jahresh.” 26 “Beibl.” 13 (Ephes., 2nd c.AD, _plural_)]]; βαρέσαι τὸ ἐμὸν ὄ. charge my account, [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [POxy. 126.8 (6th c.AD); τὸν τόκον τὸν ὀνόματί μου παραγραφέντα [prev. work]513.22 (2nd c.AD)]]; in registers of titledeeds, etc., οἰκίας οὐ κειμένης ἐν ὀνόματι τῆς ἀποδομένης not booked under the name of the seller, [Refs 3rd c.AD+ [“PLips.” 3 ii 25 (3rd c.AD)]]; ὀνόματι ἰδιωτικῆς under the head of private land, [Refs 4th c.AD+ [“PCair.Preis.” 47.10 (4th c.AD)]]; δικαιώματα.. ἑκάστῳ ὀνόματι παράκειται [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [“BGU” 113.11 (2nd c.AD)]]; in tax-receipts, ἔσχον ὀνόματος Σομτοῦς on account of [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus, “Ostr.Bodl.” ii 39 (2nd c.AD),compare “PFay.” 85.7 (3rd c.AD), etc.]]

__V
phrase, expression, especially of technical terms, ὀ. τὰ ἐν τῇ ναυτικῇ [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Respublica Atheniensium” 1.19: generally, 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 19.187.]]

__VI
Grammars, word, opposed to ῥῆμα (expression), [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Cratylus” 399b, compare “Ap.” 17c, “Smp.” 198b, 199b, 221e, 5th-6th c.BC: Isocrates Orator 9.9, 11, 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Rhetorica” 1404b5, 4th c.BC: Aeschines Orator 3.72, 2nd c.AD: Apollonius Dyscolus Grammaticus “de Syntaxi;” 12.25, +others, 4th c.BC: Demetrius Phalereus Rhetor “Demetrius on Style” 23, +others]]; τὸ ἰλλαίνειν ὄ. the word ἰλλαίνειν, [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd c.AD: Galenus Medicus 17(1).679.]]

__VI.2
noun, opposed to ῥῆμα (verb, predicate), [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Theaetetus” 168b, “Sph.” 262a, 262b, compare 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Poetica” 1457a10, “Int.” 16a19, +others]]; as one of five parts of speech, [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [3rd c.BC: Chrysippus Stoicus 2.45]]; ὄ. κύριον a proper name, opposed to προσηγορικόν, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [2nd c.BC: Dionysius Thrax Grammaticus 636.16, 2nd c.AD: Apollonius Dyscolus Grammaticus “de Pronominibus;” 26.12, +others (so ὄ. alone, 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Nubes” 681 ff., 2nd c.BC: Diogenes Babylonius Stoicus 3.213)]]; also of adjectives, [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd c.AD: Sextus Empiricus Philosophus “adversus Mathematicos” 1.222]]. (Cf. Gothic namo, genitive namins, Latin nōmen, Sanskrit nāma.)

deep_entry:
Abbott-Smith / STEPBible (TBESG)
ὀνομάζω
(ὄνομα), [in LXX for זָכַר, נָקַב, קָרָא ;]
__1. to name, mention, or address by name: Act.19:13; pass., Rom.15:20, Eph.1:21 5:3; of the use of the Divine name in praise and worship, 2Ti.2:19 (LXX, Num.16:26; cf. Isa.52:11, Amo.6:10).
__2. to name, call, give a name to: Mrk.3:14 (T, R, txt. om.), Luk.6:13-14; pass., 1Co.5:11; before ἐξ (cl.), Eph.3:15 (cf. ἐπ-ονομάζω).†
(AS)

---

LSJ / STEPBible (TFLSJ)
ὀνομάζω,
imperfect ὠνόμαζον [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Agamemnon” 682 (Lyric poetry)]], etc.; Epic dialect ὀν- [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 1.361, +others]]: future ὀνομάσω [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Cratylus” 423d]]: aorist ὠνόμασα [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 24.339, etc.]]: perfect ὠνόμακα [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Sophista” 219b]]:—passive, future -ασθήσομαι[Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd c.AD: Galenus Medicus “de Usu Partium” 6.16, +others:]]aorist ὠνομάσθην and perfect ὠνόμασμαι, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 1.96, 6.96, etc.]]; Epic dialect ὀνόμασται [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Parmenides Poeta Philosophus 9.1, etc.]]; 3rd.pers. plural ὠνομάδαται [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd-3rd c.AD: Dio Cassius Historicus 37.16]]:—middle, imperfect ὠνομάζετο [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Tyrannus” 1021.]] —Aeolic dialect or _Doric dialect_ future 3rd.pers. singular ὀνυμάξει (or -εῖ) [Refs [“Berl.Sitzb.” 1927.167 (from Cyrene)]]: aorist ὀνύμαξε [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “P.” 2.44]]; middle future ὀνυμάξομαι[Refs [[prev. work] 7.5]]: present ὀνυμάζεται[Refs 5th c.AD+ [Metop. cited in 5th c.AD: Stobaeus, Joannes 3.1.116]]: (ὄνομα):—speak of by name, call or address by name, of persons, πατρόθεν ἐκ γενεῆς ὀνομάζων ἄνδρα ἕκαστον [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 10.68, compare 22.415 and ὀνομακλήδην]]; Πυθοδώρου.., ὃν Ἀθηναῖοι οὐκ ὀνομάζουσιν [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Historia Graeca (Hellenica)” 2.3.1 (interpolated)]]; τοῖς προγόνοις -αζομένοις ἀπομνημονεύεται ὁπόστος ἀφ᾽ Ἡρακλέους ἐγένετο his descent.. is traced by naming his ancestors, [Refs [[prev. author] “Ages.” 1.2.]]

__2
of things, name, specify, περικλυτὰ δῶρ᾽ ὀνόμαζον [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 18.449]]; but also, name or promise, opposed to giving, εἰ μὲν.. μὴ δῶρα φέροι, τὰ δ᾽ ὄπισθ᾽ ὀνομάζοι [Refs [9.515]]; εἶναί τι ὀνομάζειν use the term 'being', [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Theaetetus” 160b, compare 166c, 201d]]; dedicate, τράπεζαν τῷ δαίμονι [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Theopompus Historicus 121]]:—passive, λόγοισι.. ὠνόμασται βραχέσι have been expressed, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Coloneus” 294.]]

__II
ὀ. τινά τι call one something, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “P.” 2.44, 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Agamemnon” 681 (Lyric poetry), 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 4.6, 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 1.3, 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Helena” 1193]]; ὄνομα τί σε.. ὠνόμαζεν λεώ; [Refs [[prev. author] “Heracl.” 87 (Lyric poetry):]] —rarely in middle, παῖδά μ᾽ ὠνομάζετο called me his son, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Tyrannus” 1021]]:—passive, ὄνομα δ᾽ ὠνομάζετο Ἕλενος [Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. author] “Ph.” 605; τὴν αὑτῆς ἐπωνυμίαν ὀνομαζόμενον 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Phaedrus” 238a; ἀντὶ γὰρ φίλων καὶ ξένων, ἃ τότ᾽ ὠνομάζοντο 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 18.46.]]

__II.b
nominate, ὀνομασθεὶς εἰς δεκαπρωτείαν [Refs 3rd c.AD+ [“POxy.” 1257.1, compare 1204.4 (3rd c.AD).]]

__II.2
εἶναι is frequently added pleonastic, τὰς ὀνομάζουσι εἶναι Ὑπερόχην καὶ.. whose names they say are Hyperoche and.., [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 4.33; σοφιστὴν ὀνομάζουσιν τὸν ἄνδρα εἶναι 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Protagoras” 311e, compare “R.” 428e (_passive_), 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Apologia Socratis” 13, etc.; compare καλέω 11.3 b.]]

__III
name or call with reference to, in accordance with, or after.., τινὰ or τι ἐπί τινι [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 493c]]:—passive, ἐπί τινος [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Isocrates Orator 12.183; ἔκ τινος 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Tyrannus” 1036, 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Memorabilia” 4.5.12; ὁ τῆς ἀρίστης μητρὸς ὠνομασμένος 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Trachiniae” 1105.]]

__IV
utter names or words, ἐς τρὶς ὀνομάσαι Σόλων [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.86; μάλα σεμνῶς ὀνομάζων 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 18.35, compare 122, 21.158:]] —passive, φύσις ἐπὶ τοῖς ὀνομάζεται ἀνθρώποισι the name φύσις is given by men to those things, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Empedocles Poeta Philosophus 8.4, compare 4th-5th c.BC: Parmenides Poeta Philosophus 9.1]]; παρανομίαν ἐπὶ τοῖς μὴ ἀνάγκῃ κακοῖς ὀνομασθῆναι the name of transgression is applied.., [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 4.98]]; ἀπὸ τούτου τοῦτο ὀνομάζεται (i.e. οὐ φροντὶς Ἱπποκλείδῃ) hence this saying is used, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 6.130.]]

__V
make famous, in passive, οἱ ὠνομασμένοι persons of renown, variant for{διωνομασμένοι} in [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Isocrates Orator 20.19.]] —Cf. ὀνομαίνω.

deep_entry:
Abbott-Smith / STEPBible (TBESG)
ὄνος, -ου, ὁ, ἡ
[in LXX chiefly for חֲמוֹר, also for אָתוֹן, etc. ;]
an ass: Mat.21:2, 5" (LXX), Luk.14:5, Jhn.12:15" (LXX) ; ὁ, Luk.13:15; ἡ, Mat.21:7 .†
(AS)

---

LSJ / STEPBible (TFLSJ)
ὄνος, ὁ
and ἡ, ass, once in [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Homerus Epicus, 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 11.558; then in “IG” 12.40.12, 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 4.135, etc., compare 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Historia Animalium” 580b3]]; ὄνοι οἱ τὰ κέρεα ἔχοντες, together with a number of fabulous animals, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 4.191, 192; ὄ. μονοκέρατος 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Historia Animalium” 499b19, “PA” 663a23, compare 2nd-3rd c.AD: Aelianus “De Natura Animalium - Ar.Byzantine Epit.” 3.41:]] —frequently in proverbs:

__1
ὄ. λύρας (i.e. ἀκούων), of one who can make nothing of music, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-3rd c.BC: Menander Comicus 527, [prev. author] “Mis.” 18, cf. Varroap. 2nd c.AD: Gellius, Aulus Grammaticus Latinus 3.16.13, 4th-5th c.AD: Diogenianus Paroemiographus 7.33; explained in 15th c.AD: Apostolius Paroemiographus 12.91a, ὄ. λύρας ἤκουε καὶ σάλπιγγος ὗς]]; ὄ. κάθηται, of one who sits down when caught in the game of ὀστρακίνδα, [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd c.AD(?): Pollianus Epigrammaticus 9.106, 112]]; the two proverbs combined by [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Cratinus Comicus 229 ὄνοι δ᾽ ἀπωτέρω κάθηνται τῆς λύρας, compare κιθαρίζω.]]

__2
περὶ ὄνου σκιᾶς for an ass's shadow, i.e. for a trifle, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Vespae” 191 (see. Scholia), 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Phaedrus” 260c; ταῦτα πάντ᾽ ὄνου σκιά 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Fragmenta” 331.]]

__3
ὄνου πόκαι or πόκες, see at {πόκος} [Refs [11]]; ὄνον κείρεις, of those who attempt the impossible, [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd c.AD: Zenobius Paroemiographus 5.38.]]

__4
ἀπ᾽ ὄνου καταπεσεῖν, of one who gets into a scrape by his own clumsiness. with a pun on ἀπὸ νοῦ πεσεῖν, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Nubes” 1273, compare 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Leges” 701d.]]

__5
ὄνος ὕεται an ass in the rain, of being unmoved by what is said or done, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Cratinus Comicus 52, compare 5th-6th c.BC: Cephisodorus Comicus 1; ὄνῳ τις ἔλεγε μῦθον, ὁ δὲ τὰ ὦτα ἐκίνει 4th-5th c.AD: Diogenianus Paroemiographus 7.30; ὄ. εἰς Ἀθήνας 15th c.AD: Macarius Paroemiographus “Prov.” 6.31.]]

__6
ὄ. ἄγω μυστήρια, i.e my part is to carry burdens, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Ranae” 159.]]

__7
ὄνων ὑβριστότερος, of wanton behaviour, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 5.8.3; κριθώσης ὄνου 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Fragmenta” 876.]]

__8
ὦτ᾽ ὄνου λαβεῖν, like Midas, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Plutus” 287.]]

__9
ὄ. εἰς ἄχυρα, of one who gets what he wants, [Refs 4th c.AD+ [4th-5th c.AD: Diogenianus Paroemiographus 6.91; ὄνου γνάθος, of a glutton, [prev. work] 100.]]

__10
ὄ. ἐν μελίσσαις, of one who has got into a scrape, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Crates Comicus 36]]; but ὄ. ἐν πιθήκοις, of extreme ugliness, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-3rd c.BC: Menander Comicus 402.8]]; ὄ. ἐν μύρῳ 'a clown at a feast', [Refs [10th c.AD: Suidas Legal icographus]]

__11
εἰς ὄνους ἀφ᾽ ἵππων, of one who has come down in the world, [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [4th c.AD: Libanius Sophista “Epistulae” 34.2, compare 2nd c.AD: Zenobius Paroemiographus 2.33, etc.]]

__II
a fish of the cod family, especially the hake, Merluccius vulgaris, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Epicharmus Comicus 67, 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Historia Animalium” 599b33, “fragment” 326, 4th c.AD: Heniochus Comicus 3.3, 2nd-3rd c.AD: Oppianus Anazarbensis Epicus “Halieutica - Poetae Bucolici et Didactici” 1.151, etc.]]

__III
wood-louse, κυλισθεὶς ὥς τις ὄ. ἰσόσπριος [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Fragmenta” 363, compare 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Historia Animalium” 557a23 (variant{ὀνίοις}), 4th-3rd c.BC: Theophrastus Philosophus “Historia Plantarum” 4.3.6]], [Refs 5th c.AD+ [5th c.AD(?): Hesychius Legal icographus see at {σηνίκη};compare ὀνίσκος 11, ἴουλος IV.]]

__IV
wingless locust, ={τρωξαλλίς}, [Refs 1st c.AD+ [1st c.AD: Dioscorides (Dioscurides) Medicus 2.52.]]

__V
ὄνων φάτνη a nebulous appearance between the ὄνοι (two stars in the breast of the Crab), [Refs 4th c.BC+ [3rd c.BC: Theocritus Poeta Bucolicus 22.21, compare 4th-3rd c.BC: Aratus Epicus 898, 4th-3rd c.BC: Theophrastus Philosophus “de Signis Tempestatum” 23 (ἡ τοῦ ὄνου φάτνη [prev. work] 43, 51), 2nd c.AD: Ptolemaeus Mathematicus “Tetrabiblos” 23.]]

__VI
ὄνου πετάλειον, ={φύλλον ὀνίτιδος}, [Refs 2nd c.BC+ [2nd c.BC: Nicander Epicus “Theriaca” 628.]]

__VII
from the ass as a beast of burden the name passed to:

__VII.1
windlass, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 7.36, 5th c.BC: Hippocrates Medicus “περὶ ἀγμῶν” 31, 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Mechanica” 853b12.]]

__VII.2
the upper millstone which turned round, ὄ. ἀλέτης [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 1.5.5; also ὄ. ἀλετών 2nd c.AD: Alexander Rhetor 13, 204, compare 5th c.AD(?): Hesychius Legal icographus]]see entry {μύλη}; perhaps simply, millstone, [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [3rd c.BC: Herodas Mimographus 6.83: 9th c.AD: Photius Legal icographus, etc.]] says that Aristotle also calls the fixed nether millstone ὄνος (but [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Problemata” 964b38 says, ὄνου λίθον ἀλοῦντος]] when the millstone is grinding stone, as it does when no grist is in the mill).

__VII.3
beaker, winecup, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Vespae” 616, 2nd-1st c.BC: Posidonius Historicus 2 1st c.AD: Josephus Historicus]]

__VII.4
spindle or distaff, [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd c.AD(?): Pollianus Epigrammaticus 7.32, 10.125, 5th c.AD(?): Hesychius Legal icographus]]

__VII.5
perhaps coping of a wall, [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [“Inscription Délos” 372 A 158 (3rd-2nd c.BC).]]

__VIII
ass's load, as a measure, πυροῦ ὄ. τρεῖς [Refs 1st c.AD+ [“PFay.” 67.2 (1st c.AD).]]

adverb participle of εἰμί (sum), really, actually, verily, with Verbs, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Hercules Furens” 610, “Ion” 223 (Lyric poetry), “IA” [1622], 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Nubes” 86, “Pl.” 286, 289, 3rd c.BC: Herodas Mimographus 4.65, etc.]]; ὄντως τε καὶ ἀληθῶς really and truly, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Sophista” 263d; ὄ. φιλοσοφεῖν 4th-3rd c.BC: Epicurus Philosophus “Fragmenta” 220]]; opposed to to ὡς ἔπος εἰπεῖν, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Leges” 656e]]; to εἰκότως, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Antipho Orator 2.2.10 and 4.10: in 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus with the]]participle ὤν, οὖσα, ὄν, to imply real existence, [Refs [“Phdr.” 247c, 247e, “R.” 597d]]: also with Nouns, τὰ ὄντως ἀγαθά [Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. author] “Phdr.” 260a; ὅ γε ὄντως φιλομαθής [prev. author] “R.” 490a; ὄντως ἑταίρας 4th c.BC: Antiphanes Comicus 212.6, compare 4th-3rd c.BC: Menander Comicus 367, etc.: not used by 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus or 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus, nor in _Ionic dialect_ (ἐόντως is not found)]]; more freq in the later dialogues of [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus than in the earlier.]]

opening, hole, ὀπὰς γὰρ εἶχεν οὐκ ὀλίγας [τὸ τριβώνιον] [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Plutus” 715]]; a mouse's hole, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sannyrio Comicus 8]]; of holes in the earth, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Historia Animalium” 559a4, +others]]; in a door, [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd c.AD: Lucianus Sophista “Asin.” 52]]; in a rock, [LXX.Exo.33.22]; of an orifice in the body, [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd c.AD(?): Pollianus Epigrammaticus 5.73; ἡ ὀπὴ τῶν ὤτων [prev. author] 2.84 (codex B).]]

behind, after: Mat.9:20, Mrk.5:27, Luk.8:44, Rev.4:6 5:1. As prep. with genitive: Mat.15:23, Luk.23:26, Rev.1:10 (WH, mg.).†

LSJ / STEPBible (TFLSJ)
ὄπισθεν,
in Ionic dialect [Refs 5th c.BC+ [(5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 4.72, +others, “SIG” 46.65 (Halic., 5th c.BC), etc.)]] and late Attic dialect [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [(2nd c.AD: Lucianus Sophista “Am.” 16, etc.)]] ὄπισθε before a consonant, as also in Poets, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Cyclops” 545, “IT” 1333]]: poetry also ὄπῐθεν [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 6.181, +others, 5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “O.” 10(11).35, 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Persae” 1001 (Lyric poetry)]]:— adverb:

__I
of Place, behind, at the back, opposed to πρόσθε, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 5.595; πρόσθε λέων ὄπιθεν δὲ δράκων μέσση δὲ χίμαιρα 6.181; ὄπισθεν καταλιπεῖν 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 10.209; μένειν 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 9.332, etc.; πέμψει οὖρον ὄ. 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 15.34]]; ὄπιθεν κομόωντες with long back-hair, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 2.542; ὄπιθεν κομόωσαι ἔθειραι “IG” 12(9).1179.9 (from Euboea)]]; ὄ. ἕπεσθαι, ἀκολουθεῖν, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus]] [same place], etc.; οἱ ὄπιθεν those who are left behind, e.g. at home, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 11.66]]; but also, those who are in the rear, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 2.2.8]]; εἰ τοὺς ὄ. ἐς τὸ πρόσθεν ἄξομεν shall bring the rear ranks to the front (metaphorically), [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Ajax” 1249]]; αἱ ὄ. ἁψῖδες the hinder fellies, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 4.72]]; τὰ ὄ. the hinder parts, rear, back, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 11.613; οἱ ὄ. ἁρμοί “IG” 12.372.117; εἰς τοὔπισθεν]]back, backwards, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Phoenissae” 1410, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Sophista” 261b, etc.]]; εἰς τ. τοξεύειν, i. e. 'versis sagittis', like the Parthians, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 3.3.10: opposed to ἐκ τοὔπισθεν 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Ecclesiazusae” 482, compare 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 7.79, 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 4.1.6; ἐν τῷ ὄ. 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 614c, 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Cynegeticus” 9.8, etc.]]; ὄ. ποιήσασθαι τὸν ποταμόν place the river in his rear, [Refs [[prev. author] “An.” 1.10.9.]]

__I.2
preposition with genitive, behind, στῆ δ᾽ ὄπιθεν δίφροιο [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 17.468; ὄπισθε μάχης 13.536; ὄπισθε τῆς θύρης 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.9; ἔμπροσθέ τε Θερμοπυλέων καὶ ὄ. [prev. author] 7.176; ὄ. ἐμοῦ.. εἰσῄει 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Symposium” 175a, etc.]]: sometimes after its case, δίφρου ὄπισθεν [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 24.15]]; ἴμεν φάμας ὄπισθεν follow the voice, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “O.” 6.63; γνώμης πατρῴας πάντ᾽ ὄ. ἑστάναι 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Antigone” 640; also τούτοισι δ᾽ ὄ. ἴτω 5th c.BC: Cratinus Comicus 30; πνοιαῖς ὄπιθεν Βορέα 5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “O.” 3.31 (assuming variant).]]

__II
of Time, after, in future, hereafter, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 4.362, 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 2.270, 18.168, etc.]]; either of a thing absolutely future, or of one which follows something else, opposed to αὐτίκα, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 9.519; ὄπιθεν οὐ πολλόν 5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “O.” 10(11).35; πολλοῖς μησὶν ὄ. 3rd c.BC: Theocritus Poeta Bucolicus “Epigrammata” 22.8; compare ὀπίσω 11.1.]]

__II.2
ἐν τοῖσι ὄ. λόγοισι in the books yet to come, in the following books, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 5.22, 7.213; compare ὀπίσω 11.2]]: but, in Grammars, of what has gone before, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [Scholia 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 3.366, 5th c.AD(?): Hesychius Legal icographus see {Ἴωνες}, Scholia 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Ranae” 1488]]; ὁ ὄπιθεν χρόνος the earlier time, [Refs 6th c.AD+ [“PMasp.” 158.22 (6th c.AD):]] —for _comparative_ ὀπίστερος, _superlative_ ὀπίστατος, (see entry). (Prob. from *ὄπις 'back', contained in ἀνόπιν, κατόπιν, μετόπιν, ὀπίσω.)

ὀπίσω
adv.
of place and time,
[in LXX chiefly for אַחַר and cogn. forms ;]
__1. prop., as in cl., adv.,
__(a) of time (not in NT);
__(b) of place, back, behind, after: Mat.24:18, Luk.7:38; τὰ ὀ., Php.3:13; εἰς τὰ ὀ., Mrk.13:16, Luk.9:62 17:31, Jhn.6:66 18:6 20:14.
__2. By a usage not found in cl., and in LXX representing the Heb. prep. אַחַר (Bl., § 40, 8; Thackeray, Gr., 46 f.), but also prob. general in vernacular (M, Pr., 99), as prep. with genitive;
__(a) of time, after: Mat.3:11, Mrk.1:7 Jhn.1:15, 27 1:30;
__(b) of place, behind, after: Mat.4:19 10:38 16:23-24, Mrk.1:17, 20 8:33-34, Luk.9:33 14:27 19:14 21:8, 2Pe 2;10, Ju 7, Rev.1:10 12:15; in constr. praegn. (see Swete on Re, l.with), Jhn.12:19, Act.5:17 20:30, 1Ti.5:15, Rev.13:3.†

LSJ / STEPBible (TFLSJ)
ὀπίσω [ῐ],
Epic dialect ὀπίσσω, the former rare in [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Homerus Epicus and only in signification 1]]; Aeolic dialect ὐπίσσω [Refs 7th c.BC+ [7th-6th c.BC: Sappho Lyrica “Papyrus fragments” in E. Diehl, 8.9]]:— adverb:

__I
of Place, backwards, opposed to to πρόσω, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 12.272]]; to προπρηνές,[Refs 8th c.BC+ [3.218; ἀνεχάζετο τυτθὸν ὀπίσσω 5.443; ἀ. πολλὸν ὀ. 16.710; πάλιν εἶσιν ὀπίσσω 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 11.149: in Prose also, τὸ ὀπίσω,]] contraction τοὐπίσω, τὸ ὀ. φεύγειν [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.207, compare 8.108; ἄναγε εἰς τοὐπίσω 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 528a, compare 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 4.4, 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Fragmenta” 106, etc.; [γνάμ]φθη δ᾽ ὀπίσσω [φάσγα]νον 5th c.BC: Bacchylides Lyricus 12.53]]; τὰ ὀ. the hinder parts, [LXX+1st c.BC+ [LXX.Joel.2.20; τοῦ προπύλου τὸ ὀ. μέρος “SIG” 756.17 (Athens, 1st c.BC); τὴν ὀ. τοῦ προπύλου στέγην [prev. work]12; ἐκ τοῦ ὀ.]] on the back (of the papyrus), [Refs 1st c.BC+ [“BGU” 1002.16 (1st c.BC)]]; τἀπίλοιπα ὀ. [Refs 2nd c.BC+ [“PTeb.” 58.37 (2nd c.BC).]]

__I.2
back, back again, of movement, ἀπήνυσαν οἴκαδ᾽ ὀπίσσω [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 7.326; ὀπίσω πάλιν οἴκαδε 5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “N.” 3.62; ἂψ ὀ. 3rd c.BC: Theocritus Poeta Bucolicus 25.74; ἀπίκοντο ὀ. 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.62; ὀ. πορευόμενοι [prev. work] 75; ὀ. ἀναπλῶσαι [prev. work] 78]]; ἐν τῇ ὀ. κομιδῇ on his way back, [Refs [[prev. author] 8.120, compare 1.111, etc.]]

__I.3
back again, again, of action that reverses an action or occurrence, ἀνακτᾶσθαι ὀ. τὴν τυραννίδα [Refs [[prev. work] 61, compare 68, 2.14; ἀποδόντες ὀ. [prev. author] 5.92.γ᾽]]; σφραγίζεις λύεις τ᾽ ὀπίσω [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Iphigenia Aulidensis” 38 (_anapaest meter_).]]

__I.4
with genitive, δεῦτε ὀ. μου come after me, follow me, [NT.Matt.4.19.]

__II
of Time, hereafter, since the future is unseen and was therefore regarded as behind us, whereas the past is known and therefore before our eyes, ἡμῖν τεκέεσσί τ᾽ ὀπίσσω πῆμα λίποιτο [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 3.160]]; Τρῳαὶ δέ μ᾽ ὀπίσσω πᾶσαι μωμήσονται[Refs 8th c.BC+ [[prev. work] 411, compare 8th-7th c.BC: Hesiodus Epicus “Opera et Dies” 741, “Th.” 488; ἔς περ ὀπίσσω 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 20.199 (εἰσοπίσω 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Philoctetes” 1104 (Lyric poetry)); opposed to to νῦν, τούτῳ δ᾽ οὔτ᾽ ἂρ νῦν φρένες ἔμπεδοι [εἰσίν], οὔτ᾽ ἄρ᾽ ὀπίσσω ἔσσονται 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 6.352; to προπάροιθε, σεῖο δ᾽, Ἀχιλλεῦ, οὔ τις ἀνὴρ προπάροιθε [ἦν] μακάρτατος, οὔτ᾽ ἄρ᾽ ὀπίσσω [ἔσσεται] 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 11.483]]; where ὀπίσσω and πρόσσω are opposed, πρόσσω must be the past and ὀπίσσω the future, οἶδε νοῆσαι ἅμα πρόσσω καὶ ὀπίσσω [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 1.343; ἅμα πρόσσω καὶ ὀ. λεύσσει 3.109; ὅρα πρόσσω καὶ ὀ. 18.250, 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 24.452; so ὅσα τ᾽ ἦν ὅσα τ᾽ ἔσθ᾽ ὅσα τ᾽ ἔσται ὀπίσσω 5th c.BC: Empedocles Poeta Philosophus 21.9 (cited in 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Metaphysica” 1000a30)]]; οὔτ᾽ ἐνθάδ᾽ ὁρῶν οὔτ᾽ ὀπίσω neither present nor future, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Tyrannus” 488 (Lyric poetry); τοὐπίσω σκοπεῖν 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Fragmenta” 49; θνητὸς πεφυκὼς τοὐπίσω πειρῶ βλέπειν Isidorus Tragicus 2; compare ὄπισθεν 11.1.]]

__II.2
ἐν τοῖσι ὀ. λόγοις in the books yet to come, in the following books, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.75; compare ὄπισθεν 11.2.]]

__2
of chariothorses, get ready, harness, equip, αὐτὰρ ὅ γ᾽ υἷας ἄμαξαν.. ὁπλίσαι ἠνώγει [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 24.190]] (so in middle, prepare or get ready for oneself, ἐΰτριχας ὡπλίσαθ᾽ ἵππους [Refs 5th c.BC+ [23.301); ὥπλιζον ἵππους προμετωτιδίοις 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 6.4.1]]:— passive, of ships, νῆες.. ὁπλίζονται [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 17.288]]; of any implements, λαμπὰς διὰ χερῶν ὡπλισμένη ready for use,[Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Septem contra Thebas” 433]]; θώρακα.. περιβόλοις ὡπλισμένον furnished with, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Ion” 993.]]
