LSJ / STEPBible (TFLSJ)
ὅπλον, τό,
tool, implement, mostly in plural, like{ἔντεα},{τεύχεα}: (probably from ἕπω A):

__I
a ship's tackle, tackling, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Homerus Epicus (only in 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey”), 2.390, +others, 8th-7th c.BC: Hesiodus Epicus “Opera et Dies” 627]]; especially ropes, halyards, etc., δησάμενοι δ᾽ ἄρα ὅπλα [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 2.430, etc.]]; in which sense [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Homerus Epicus]] twice uses the singular, rope, [Refs [14.346, 21.390: generally,]]any ropes, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 7.25, 9.115, 5th c.BC: Hippocrates Medicus “περὶ ἄρθρων ἐμβολῆς” 78.]]

__II
tools, strictly so called, in [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Homerus Epicus]] especially of smiths' tools, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 18.409, 412; in full, ὅπλα χαλκήϊα 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 3.433: in _sing._, ὅπλον ἀρούρης sickle, “Anthologia Graeca” 6.95 (from Antiphil)]]; ὅπλον γεροντικόν staff, [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [3rd c.BC: Callimachus Epicus “Epigrammata” 1.7]]; δείπνων ὅπλον ἑτοιμότατον, of the wine-flask, [Refs [“Anthologia Graeca” 6.248 (Marc. argument).]]

__III
in plural, also, implements of war, arms and armour, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Homerus Epicus (only in 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad”), αὐτὰρ ἐπεὶ πάνθ᾽ ὅπλα κάμε,]] of the arms of Achilles, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [18.614, compare 19.21; ὅπλοισιν ἔνι δεινοῖσιν ἐδύτην 10.254, 272; so in 5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “N.” 8.27, “IG” 12.1.9, 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Hecuba” 14, etc.]]: rarely in singular, weapon, οὐδέ τι ἀρήϊον ὅπλον ἐκτέαται [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 4.23, compare 174, 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Hercules Furens” 161, 570, 942, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 474a, 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 7.4.15]]; ποτὶ πονηρὸν οὐκ ἄχρηστον ὅπλον ἁ πονηρία [[Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Epicharmus Comicus] 275]]; piece of armour, [Refs 1st c.BC+ [1st c.BC: Diodorus Siculus Historicus 3.49.]]

__III.2
the large shield, from which the men-at-arms took their name of ὁπλῖται (εἰκόνα γραπτὴν ἐν ὅπλῳ [Refs 5th c.BC+ [“IG” 22.1012.18 (2nd c.BC),compare “IGRom.” 4.1302.35 (Cyme, 1st c.BC-1st c.AD), 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 7.75, 1st c.BC: Diodorus Siculus Historicus 15.44, 17.18); ὅπλον στύππινον “IG” 11(2).203 B 99 (Delos, 3rd c.BC)]]: metaphorically, τῆς πενίας ὅπλον ἡ παρρησία [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Nicostratus Comicus 29; ὅ. μέγιστον.. ἁρετὴ βροτοῖς 4th-3rd c.BC: Menander Comicus “Μονόστιχοι - Fragmenta Comicorum Graecorum” 433, compare 619.]]

__III.3
in plural, also, heavy arms, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 9.53]]; ὅπλων ἐπιστάτης, ={ὁπλίτης}, opposed to κώπης ἄναξ, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Persae” 379; ὁ πόλεμος οὐχ ὅπλων τὸ πλέον ἀλλὰ δαπάνης 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 1.83; ὅπλα παραδοῦναι [prev. author] 4.69; ὅπλα ἀποβάλλειν 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Vespae” 27, etc.]]

__III.4
ὅπλα, ={ὁπλῖται}, men-at-arms, πολλῶν μεθ᾽ ὅπλων [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Antigone” 115 (Lyric poetry): and frequently in Prose, ἐξέτασιν ὅπλων ποιεῖσθαι]] to have a muster of the men-at-arms, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 4.74, etc.]]; ὁ ἐπὶ τῶν ὅπλων στρατηγός, opposed to ὁ ἐπὶ τῆς διοικήσεως, Decrees cited in [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 18.38, Decrees [prev. work] 115; χειροτονηθεὶς ἐπὶ τὰ ὅ. πρῶτος.. στρατηγός “IG” 22.682.44 (3rd c.BC)]]; στρατηγεῖν ἐπὶ τὰ ὅ. [Refs 2nd c.BC+ [“SIG” 697 E (Delph., 2nd c.BC), etc.]]

__III.5
τὰ ὅ. the place of arms, camp, ἦλθεν εἰς τὰ ὅ. [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Lysias Orator 13.12, compare 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 7.2.5, etc.; ἐκ τῶν ὅ. προϊέναι 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 1.111, compare 3.1.]]

__III.6
Phrases: ἐνέδυνον (variant{ἐνέδυντο}) τὰ ὅ. [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 7.218, etc.]]; ἐν ὅπλοισι εἶναι or γενέσθαι to be in arms, under arms, [Refs 7th c.BC+ [[prev. author] 1.13, compare 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Bacchae” 303, 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 6.56; ἐν ὄπλοισι [ἰππομ]άχεντας 7th-6th c.BC: Sappho Lyrica “Papyrus fragments” in E. Diehl, 5.19; ἐν ὅπλοις μάχεσθαι 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Gorgias” 456d; ἡ ἐν τοῖς ὅπλοις μάχη [prev. author] “Lg.” 833e]]; ποιῆσαι ἐξέτασιν ἐν ὅπλοις Decrees cited in [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Ἀθηναίων Πολιτεία” 31.2; εἰς τὰ ὅ. παραγγέλλειν 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 1.5.13]]; ἐφ᾽ ὅπλοις or παρ᾽ ὅπλοις ἧσθαι, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Supplices” 674, 357; μένειν ἐπὶ τοῖς ὅπλοις 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 7.2.8]]; for ὅπλα ῥίπτειν, ἀφιέναι, κατατίθεσθαι, (see entry).; for ὅπλα τίθεσθαι, see at {τίθημι}.

__IV
of the arms possessed by animals for self-defence, [τὸν ἄνθρωπον] οὐκ ἔχοντα ὅπλον πρὸς τὴν ἀλκήν [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “de Partibus Animalium” 687a25, compare b4, +others]]

__V
membrum virile, [Refs 2nd c.BC+ [2nd c.BC: Nicander Epicus “fragment” 74.30, “APl.” 4.242 (1st c.BC: Erycius Epigrammaticus), 5th c.AD(?): Hesychius Legal icographus]]

__VI
a gymnastic exercise, the last which came on in the games, [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd c.AD: Artemidorus Daldianus Onirocriticus 1.63.]]

LSJ / STEPBible (TFLSJ)
ὁποῖος, α, ον,
Epic dialect ὁπποῖος, η, ον, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Homerus Epicus, but twice ὁποῖος, 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 17.421, 19.77]]; Ionic dialect ὁκοῖος, η, ον, [Refs 7th c.BC+ [7th c.BC: Archilochus Lyricus 70, 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 2.82, +others, “GDI” iv p.883 (Erythrae, 4th c.BC)]]; Cretan dialect ὀτεῖος (which see): correlated to ποῖος: replaced by οἷος in Attic dialect Inscrr. after [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC:]]

__1
as Relat., of what sort or quality, ὁπποῖόν κ᾽ εἴπῃσθα ἔπος, τοῖόν κ᾽ ἐπακούσαις as [is] the word thou hast spoken, such shalt thou hear again, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 20.250]]; τοίῳ ὁποῖος ἔοι such as he might be, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 17.421; οὔθ᾽ οἷ᾽ ἔπασχεν οὔθ᾽ ὁποῖ᾽ ἔδρα κακά 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Tyrannus” 1272.]]

__2
in indirect questions, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 1.171, etc.; εὑρεῖν ὁποίοις φαρμάκοις ἰάσιμος 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Prometheus Vinctus” 475]]: in direct questions only as [Refs 5th c.BC+ [_falsa lectio_ in 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Phoenissae” 878, “Ba.” 663: sometimes followed by ποῖος]] in the same clause, οὐ γὰρ αἰσθάνομαί σου ὁποῖον νόμιμον ἢ ποῖον δίκαιον λέγεις [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Memorabilia” 4.4.13; οὐκ οἶδα ὁποίᾳ τόλμῃ ἢ ποίοις λόγοις χρώμενος ἐρῶ 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 414d.]]

__II
with indefinite words added, ὁποῖός τις [Refs 8th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 7.38, 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 2.2.2; ὁκοῖόν τι 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.158; γιγνομένων ὁποῖοί τινες ἔτυχον 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Politica” 1286b24; so in 8th c.BC: Homerus Epicus, ὁπποῖ᾽ ἄσσα]] of what sort, for ὁποῖά τινα, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 19.218; ὁποῖ᾽ ἄττα 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Gorgias” 465a; ὁποιοσοῠν]]of what kind soever, [Refs [[prev. author] “Tht.” 152d, +others]]; ὁποῖος δή, δήποτε, δηποτοῦν, and οὖν δή, as ὁποία δὴ φλέψ [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Historia Graeca (Hellenica)” 5.4.58; τοὺς ὁποιουσδήποτε.. ἐξεπέμπετε στρατηγούς 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 18.146: _genitive_, ὁποίου τινὸς οὖν 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 2.4.10: _accusative_ _feminine_, ὁποιαντινοῦν 5th c.BC: Lysias Orator 13.11; ὁποῖόσπερ 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Choephori” 669; ὁποιοσποτοῦν 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Physica” 253b23; ὁποιοσδητισοῦν 4th c.AD: Iamblichus Philosophus cited in 6th c.AD: Simplicius Philosophus “in Aristotelis Physica commentaria - Comm. in Arist. Graeca” 639.30]]; πόλιν.. οὐδ᾽ ὁποίας ἥττω inferior to none, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [2nd c.BC: Polybius Historicus 4.65.3; οὔτ᾽ ἄλλους οὐδ᾽ ὁποίους 4th c.BC: Theopompus Historicus 217]] (c); μηδὲ καθ᾽ ὁποῖον τρόπον [Refs 2nd c.BC+ [“SIG” 672.14 (Delph., 2nd c.BC)]]; μηδ᾽ ὁτίη or μηδοτίη, see at {μηδοτίη}.

__III
neuter plural used as adverb, like as, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Tyrannus” 915, 1076, 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Hecuba” 398.]]

__IV
adverb ὁποίως, qualiter, [Refs [“Corpus Glossariorum Latinorum”]]

short_definition: when(-ever) — 1. of Time, correlated to πότε, much like ὅτε:
deep_entry:
Abbott-Smith / STEPBible (TBESG)
1. of Time, correlated to πότε, much like ὅτε:
2. with the indicative, when , Lat. quando, (Homer): —; εἰς ὁπότε, with future, when, by what time , λέγειν εἰς ὁπότ᾽ ἔσται (Aeschines Orator)
3. with the optative in reference to the past, whenever , to express an event that has often occurred, ὁπότε Κρήτηθεν ἵκοιτο (Iliad by Homer), etc.:—;also in oratio obliqua, (Sophocles Tragicus), etc.
4. in indirect phrases, ἴδμεν, ὁππότε Τηλέμαχος νεῖται when he is to return , (Odyssey by Homer); with optative, δέγμενος ὁππότε ναυσὶν ἐφορμηθεῖεν (Iliad by Homer)
5. in causal sense, for that, because, since , like Lat. quando for quoniam , (Theognis Elegiacus), etc.: so ὁπότε γε, Lat. quandoquidem, (Sophocles Tragicus) (ML)

---

LSJ / STEPBible (TFLSJ)
ὁπότε,
Epic dialect ὁππότε, both in [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Homerus Epicus]]; Ionic dialect ὁκότε; Cyrenaic ὁπόκᾰ [Refs [“Berl.Sitzb.” 1927.164]]; in Doric dialect Poets ὁππόκᾰ [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [3rd c.BC: Theocritus Poeta Bucolicus 5.98:]] adverb of Time, correlated to πότε, used much like{ὅτε}, except that the sense is less definite [Refs 5th c.BC+ [compare (5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 1.6.3), though the two were frequently used without distinction:]]

__I
Relat., with the indicative, mostly with reference to the past, when, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 1.399, 3.173, etc.; the _indicative_ ἦστε is omitted, 8.230: in Class. _Attic dialect_ Prose only ὅτε is so used, when referring to a particular time, but later ὁπότε returns, as ὁπότε περιῆν]] when she was alive, [Refs 1st c.AD+ [“POxy.” 243.10 (1st c.AD)]]: with the present in a simile, ὡς δ᾽ ὁπότε.. ποταμὸς πεδίονδε κάτεισι [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 11.492]]: with subjunctive, like{ὁπόταν}, with reference to an indefinite number of occasions in the present or to the future, ὁππότ᾽ Ἀχαιοὶ Τρώων ἐκπέρσωσ᾽ εὖ ναιόμενον πτολίεθρον [Refs 8th c.BC+ [1.163, compare 13.817, 21.112, 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 14.170, 8th-7th c.BC: Hesiodus Epicus “Theogonia” 782: sometimes in similes, ὡς ὁπότε νέφεα Ζέφυρος στυφελίξῃ 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 11.305, compare 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 4.335]]; but ὁπότ᾽ ἄν, Epic dialect ὁπότε or ὁππότε κεν, is more common with subjunctive, and in Attic dialect Prose ἄν must be used, see at {ὁπόταν}: Cyrenaic ὁπόκα κα δήληται [Refs [“Berl.Sitzb.” [prev. cited]]]

__I.2
with optative:

__I.2.a
to express an event that occurred often, ὁπότε Κρήτηθεν ἵκοιτο [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 3.233, compare 10.189, 15.284, 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 11.591, 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 1.99, 2.15, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Symposium” 220a, 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 3.4.28.]]

__I.2.b
after a verb of waiting, of a time future relatively to the past, ἷζε.. δέγμενος ὁππότε ναῦφιν ἀφορμηθεῖεν [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 2.794, compare 4.334, 7.415, 9.191, 18.524.]]

__I.2.c
in indirect speech, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Trachiniae” 824 (Lyric poetry), 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 4.6.20]]; in implied indirect speech, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 24.344 (of a past promise)]]; ἀποδοτέον.. ὁ. μανεὶς ἀπαιτοῖ we were not [as you remember] to.., [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 332a.]]

__I.2.d
where the principal clause has an optative, μηδ᾽ ἀντιάσειας ἐκείνῳ ὁππότε νοστήσειε [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 18.148, compare 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 396c, 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 1.6.3.]]

__II
in indirect questions, with indicative, ἦ ῥά τι ἴδμεν.. ὁππότε Τηλέμαχος νεῖτα; when he is to return, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 4.633; εἰς ὁ.]]by what time, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aeschines Orator 3.99: rarely after a past tense, προσεδέρκετο, δέγμενος αἰεί, ὁππότε δὴ.. ἐφήσει (for ἐφείη, see above 1.2 b) 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 20.386; εἰς σὲ βλέψαι καὶ τὸν ταμίαν ὁπότ᾽ ἄριστον παραθήσει 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Vespae” 613.]]

__III
ὁποτεοῦν at any time whatever, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Metaphysica” 1049a1.]]

__B
in causal sense, because, since, with indicative, [Refs 6th c.BC+ [6th c.BC: Theognis Elegiacus 749 (assuming variant), 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 2.125, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Leges” 895c, etc.; also ὁπότε γε 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Coloneus” 1699 (Lyric poetry), 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 8.3.7.]]

Abbott-Smith / STEPBible (TBESG)
ὅπου
adv.
of place, correlat. of ποῦ (which see), where.
__I. Prop., of place,
__1. where;
__(a) in relative sentences, with indic: Mat.25:24, 26, Mrk.2:4 4:5, 15 5:40 13:14, Jhn.3:8 6:62 7:34, 36 11:32 14:3 17:24 20:19, Rom.15:20, Rev.2:13; after nouns of place, for relat. prepositional phrase (ἐν ᾧ., etc.), Mat.6:19-20 13:5 26:57 28:6, Mrk.6:55 9:48 Luk.12:33, Jhn.1:28 4:20, 46 6:23 7:42 10:40 11:30 12:1 18:1, 20 19:18, 20 19:41 20:12, Act.17:1, Rev.2:13 11:8 20:10; before ἐκεῖ., Mat.6:21, Luk.12:34 17:37 Jhn.12:26; id. pleonast. (= Heb. שָׁם . . . אֲשֶׁר; Aram. תַּמָּן . . דּ; of. Gen.13:3), ὅ. . . . ἐκεῖ, Rev.12:6, 14; ὅ. . . . ἐπ᾽ αὐτῶν, Rev.17:9; ὅ. ἄν, wherever (M, Pr., 168), with imperfect indic., Mrk.6:56; with Pres. subjc., Mat.24:28; ὅ. ἐάν, Mat.26:13, Mrk.6:10 9:18 14:9, 14 a;
__(b) in quaest. indir., with aor. subjc.: Mrk.14:14 b, Luk.22:11.
__2. In late writers (sometimes also in cl.; Bl., § 25, 2), with verbs of motion, = ὅποι, whither: with indic., Jhn.8:21-22 13:33, 36 14:4 21:18, Heb.6:20, Jas.3:4; ὅ. ἄν, whithersoever, with present ind., Rev.14:4; subjc., Luk.9:57; ὅ. ἐάν, Mat.8:19.
__II. Without strict local sense,
__1. of time or condition: Col.3:11, Heb.9:16 10:18, Jas.3:16, 2Pe.2:11.
__2. Of cause or reason (AV, whereas): 1Co.3:3.†

LSJ / STEPBible (TFLSJ)
ὅπου,
Ionic dialect ὅκου, Relat., indirect interrogative, and indefinite adverb of Place, correlated to ποῦ:

__I
as a Relat., sometimes with genitive loci, τῆς πόλεως ὅπου κάλλιστον στρατοπεδεύσασθαι [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 415d, compare 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 2.172; ὅπου βούλοιτο τοῦ δρόμου 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Historia Graeca (Hellenica)” 2.4.27; ἔσθ᾽ ὅπου]]in some places, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Eumenides” 517 (Lyric poetry), “fragment” 302: standing for the Relat.]] adjective, μέλη, ὅπου (i. e. ἐν οἷς)[Refs 5th c.BC+ [χελιδὼν ἦν τις ἐμπεποιημένη 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Aves” 1301]]: with other Particles, ὅκου δή somewhere or other, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 3.129]]; ὅπου ἄν wherever, with subjunctive, [Refs [“IG” 12.76.11, etc.]]; in Trag. the ἄν may be omitted, as ὅπου δ᾽ Ἀπόλλων σκαιὸς ᾖ, τίνες σοφο; [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Electra” 972, etc. (never in _Attic dialect_ Prose)]]: with genitive, ὅπου ἂν τύχῃ τῶν λεγομένων [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Protagoras” 342e; ὁπουοῦν]]anywheresoever, [Refs [[prev. author] “Cra.” 403c]]; ὅπουπερ with optative, wherever, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 3.3.5; ὅπου ποτέ 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Coloneus” 12]]; ὁπουδάν, ={ὅπου δὲ ἄν}, anywhere, [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd-3rd c.AD: Dio Cassius Historicus “fragment” 109.21]]; ὁπουδήποτε, = ubicumque, Dosith.p.410 K.; ὁπουδηποτοῦν anywheresoever, [Refs 1st c.AD+ [1st c.AD: Josephus Historicus “contra Apionem” 2.15.]]

__I.2
in indirect questions, ὄφρα πύθηαι πατρός, ὅπου κύθε γαῖα [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 3.16, compare 16.306, 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Tyrannus” 924, etc.]]: with Verbs of motion in pregnant sense, ὅκου ἐτράπετο, οὐκέτι εἶχον εἰπεῖν [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 2.119; κεῖνος δ᾽ ὅπου βέβηκεν, οὐδεὶς οἶδε 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Trachiniae” 40, variant in 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 3.1.37, etc.: in many passages editors have in this sense restored ὅποι,]] mostly from codices; in repeating a question, ἡ Λακεδαίμων ποῦ 'στι; Answ. ὅπου 'στί; (do you ask) where it is? [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Nubes” 214: with _genitive_, εἰδότες ὅκου γῆς εἴη 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 4.150, compare 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 403e.]]

__II
the strict local sense occasionally passes into,

__II.1
a sense involving Time or Occasion, ὅ. τιν᾽ ἴδῃ [Refs 6th c.BC+ [6th c.BC: Theognis Elegiacus 922, compare 999, 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Historia Graeca (Hellenica)” 3.3.6; σιγᾶν θ᾽ ὅ. δεῖ καὶ λέγειν τὰ καίρια 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Choephori” 582, compare “Eu.” 277]]; οὐκ ἔσθ᾽ ὅ. there is no case in which, i.e. in no case. [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Tyrannus” 448, “Aj.” 1069, 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Hercules Furens” 186, 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 3.35]]; so ἔστιν ὅ.; as a question, [Refs [[prev. author] 18.22.]]

__II.2
of Cause, whereas, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.68, 4.195, 5th c.BC: Antipho Orator 1.7; ὅ. γὰρ ἐγὼ.. ὁμολογῶ 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 21.205]]; ὅκου γε, Latin quandoquidem or quippe, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 7.118; ὅπου γε 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 2.3.11, etc.]]

__B
later as a demonstrative adverb, only in the phrase ὅ. μέν.., ὅ. δέ.. here.., there.., [Refs 1st c.AD+ [1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus 2.427c, 2nd c.AD: Sextus Empiricus Philosophus “Πυρρώνειοι ὑποτυπώσεις” 1.53, etc.]]

__1. late summer, early autumn (the time between the risings of Sirius and Arcturus, i.e. late July, all August and early September).

ὀπώρ-α,
Ionic dialect ὀπώρ-η, ἡ: sometimes ὁπώρα, compare χεῖμα χὠπώραν, i.e. καὶ ὁπ-, [Refs 7th c.BC+ [7th c.BC: Alcman Lyricus 76 (χειμάχωι πάραν, etc. codices)]]; proper nouns Ὁπωρίς [Refs [“IG” 5(1).1497, “Hopora” “CIL” 6.21782]]; compare μεθόπωρον, μεθοπωρινός:—the part of the year between the rising of Sirius and of Arcturus (i.e. the last days of July, all Aug., and part of Sept.), the latter part of summer; [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Homerus Epicus names θέρος and ὀπώρη]] together, θέρος τεθαλυῖά τ᾽ ὀπώρη [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 11.192]]; Σείριος being the star of ὀπώρη, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 22.27]]; compare ὀπωρινός.—In later times it became the name of a definite season, autumn (see. ὥρα [Refs [1.1 c)]], but was still used sometimes to denote summer (autumn being distinguished as φθινόπωρον or μετόπωρον), ἀρξάμενος ἀπὸ τοῦ ἠρινοῦ χρόνου πρὸ ὀπώρας [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Historia Graeca (Hellenica)” 3.2.10, compare 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Aves” 709, 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Meteorologica” 348a1; ἐπ᾽ ὀκτὼ μῆνας Κυρηναίους ὀπώρη ἐπέχει 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 4.199; νέας δ᾽ ὀπώρας ἡνίκ᾽ ἂν ξανθῇ στάχυς 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Fragmenta - American Journal of Philology” 304.7.]]

__II
fruit, γλαυκῆς ὀπώρας.. ποτοῦ χυθέντος.. Βακχίας ἀπ᾽ ἀμπέλου [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Trachiniae” 703; τέμνεται βλαστουμένη καλῶς ὀ. [prev. author] “fragment” 255.8; σικυούς, βότρυς, ὀπώραν 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Fragmenta” 569.1: so in Prose, 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Historia Graeca (Hellenica)” 2.4.25, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Leges” 844d, 845c, 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Historia Animalium” 606b2, 629a2]]: in this sense also in plural, [Refs 7th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Isaeus Orator 11.43; 7th c.BC: Alcman Lyricus (75)]] even calls honey κηρίνα ὀπώρ; ἐαρινὴ ὀπώρα [Refs 4th c.AD+ [4th c.AD: Alciphro Epistolographus “fragment” 6.10.]]

metaphorically, life's summer, the time of youthful ripeness, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “I.” 2.5]]; τέρειναν ματέρ᾽ οἰνάνθας ὀπώραν (see. οἰνάνθη) [Refs [[prev. author] “N.” 5.6]]; ripe virginity, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Supplices” 998, 1015; ὀ. Κύπριδος 4th c.BC: Chaeremon Tragicus 12.]]

ὅπως
__I. Relat. adv. of manner, as, how: with indic., Luk.24:20.
__II. Conj., with subjc. (in cl. also with opt., indic.: so in Mat.26:59, LT, Tr.), in order that, to the end that, that;
__1. final, denoting purpose or design (in which the original idea of modality has been merged): after pres., Mat.6:2, al.; pf., Act.9:17, al.; impf., Act.9:24; aor., Act.9:2, al.; plpf., Jhn.11:57; fut., Mat.23:35; imperat., Mat.2:8, al.; ὅ. μή (M, Pr., 185), Mat.6:18, Luk.16:26, Act.20:16, 1Co.1:29; ὅ. πληρωθῇ, Mat.2:23 8:17 13:35; ὅ. ἄν (B1., § 65, 2; WM, § 42, 5), Luk.2:35, Act.3:19 15:17, Rom.3:4 (cf. Gen.12:13, Psa.59:7. 1Mac 1032, al.).
__2. After verbs of asking, exhorting, etc.: Mat.9:38, Luk.7:3, Jas.5:16, al. (in late writers its place is often taken by the correl. πῶς, which see)
(AS)

---

LSJ / STEPBible (TFLSJ)
ὅπως,
Epic dialect also and Aeolic dialect ὅππως, Ionic dialect ὅκως, Doric dialect ὁπῶς accusative to [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd c.AD: Apollonius Dyscolus Grammaticus “de Adverbiis;” 173.11: correlated to ὡς and πῶς.]] adverb of Manner, Relat. as, in such manner as, and with interrogative force how, in what manner, rarely indefinite, see below [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus V.]]

__B
FINAL CONJUNCTION, in such a manner that, in order that. adverb of Manner, how, as:

__B.I
Relat. to ὥς or οὕτως (like ὡς), in such manner as, as:

__B.I.1
with the ordinary Constr. of the Relat.:

__B.I.1.a
with indicative, ἦ τοι νόστον, ὅπως φρεσὶ σῇσι μενοινᾷς, ὥς τοι Ζεὺς τελέσειεν [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 15.111; οὕτως ὅ... 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Trachiniae” 330; ὧδ᾽ ὅ. [prev. author] “El.” 1301; οὕτως ὅ. δύνανται 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 7.67: sometimes an analogous word replaces the antecedent]] adverb, με τοῖον ἔθηκεν, ὅπως (for οἷον)[Refs 8th c.BC+ [ἐθέλει 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 16.208: frequently without any antecedent expressed, ἔλθοι ὅ... ἐθέλω (i.e. αὐτὸν ἐλθεῖν) 14.172; ἔρξον ὅ. ἐθέλεις 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 4.37, 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 13.145; χρῶ ὅ. βούλει 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 8.3.46; ποίει ὅ. ἄριστόν σοι δοκεῖ εἶναι [prev. work] 4.5.50]]; ὅ. ἔχω as I am, on the spot, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Philoctetes” 819.]]

__B.I.1.b
with future indicative, especially after Verbs of seeing, providing, taking care.., in the manner in which, how, that, οἱ Περσικοὶ νόμοι ἐπιμέλονται ὅπως μὴ τοιοῦτοι ἔσονται οἱ πολῖται [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 1.2.3; ποιέειν ὅκως μηκέτι κεῖνος ἐς Ἕλληνας ἀπίξεται 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 5.23; ἐφρόντιζον ὅκως μὴ λείψομαι τῶν πρότερον γενομένων [prev. author] 7.8.ά, compare 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Apologia” 29e; ἔπρασσον ὅπως τις βοήθεια ἥξει 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 3.4; τοῦτο μηχανᾶσθαι ὅπως ἀποφεύξεται πᾶν ποιῶν θάνατον 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Apologia” 39a; τούτου στοχαζόμενοι, ὅπως.. ἔσονται [prev. author] “Grg.” 502e (compare below 111.1 b, etc.)]]: this future indicative may become optative after a historical tense, ἐπεμελεῖτο ὅπως μήτε ἄσιτοι μήτε ἄποτοί ποτε ἔσοιντο [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 8.1.43, compare “HG” 7.5.3, “Cyr.” 8.1.10, “Oec.” 7.5, “Ages.” 2.8]]; and ὅπως is frequently used interchangeably with such forms as δι᾽ ὧν, ὅτῳ τρόπῳ, etc., εἰσηγοῦνται μὴ δι᾽ ὧν.. ἀσκήσουσιν, ἀλλ᾽ ὅπως.. δόξουσι [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Isocrates Orator 1.4, compare 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 6.11]]: this sense easily passes into a final sense, so that, τοῦτο ἀπόβαλε οὕτω ὅκως μηκέτι ἥξει [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 3.40]]; οὕτω δ᾽ (i.e. ποίει) ὅπως μήτηρ σε μὴ 'πιγνώσεται [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Electra” 1296, compare 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Ranae” 905, 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 4.5.25, “HG” 2.4.17]]; see below [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Bacchylides Lyricus]]

__B.I.2
with ἄν (Epic dialect κε) and subjunctive in indefinite sentences, in whatever way, just as, however, ὅππως κεν ἐθέλῃσιν [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 20.243 (but ὅπως ἐθέλῃσιν (without κε) 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 1.349, 6.189); οὕτως ὅκως ἂν καὶ δυνώμεθα 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 8.143; οὕτως ὅπως ἂν αὐτοὶ βούλωνται 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 1.1.2, compare “IG” 22.1.13 (5th c.BC), 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Phaedo” 116a, “Smp.” 174b, etc.]]

__B.I.2.b
with optative after historical tenses, οὕτως ὅ. τύχοιεν [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 8.95; ὅ. βούλοιντο 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Historia Graeca (Hellenica)” 2.3.13]]; in a gnomic statement, εἰκῇ κράτιστον ζῆν ὅ. δύναιτό τις [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Tyrannus” 979: when ἄν appears with the _optative_, it belongs to the Verb and not to ὅπως, ὅ. ἄν τις ὀνομάσαι τοῦτο]] however one might think fit to call it, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 13.4.]]

__B.I.3
a very common phrase is οὐκ ἔστιν ὅ. (οὐκ ἔσθ᾽ ὅπως) there is no way in which.., it cannot be that, οὐκ ἔστι ὅκως κοτὲ σοὺς δέξονται λόγους [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 7.102, compare 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Plutus” 18, 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 18.208, +others]]; so οὐκ ἔστιν ὅ. οὐ, fieri non potest quin, οὐκ ἔσθ᾽ ὅ. οὐ πιστὸν ἐξ ὑμῶν πτερὸν ἐξήγαγ᾽ [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Coloneus” 97, compare 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Acharnenses” 116, “Eq.” 426, “Th.” 882, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Apologia” 27e]]; οὐδαμῶς ὅ. οὐ, in answer, it must positively be so, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. author] “Tht.” 160d; so also οὐκ ἂν γένοιτο τοῦθ᾽ ὅ... οὐ φανῶ 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Tyrannus” 1058]]; οὐ γὰρ γένοιτ᾽ ἄν, ταῦθ᾽ ὅ. οὐχ ὧδ᾽ ἔχειν (anacoluthon for ἔχει or ἕξει) [Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. author] “Aj.” 378: so in questions, ἔσθ᾽ ὅ... ἔλθωμε; 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Vespae” 471 (variant{-οιμεν})]]; ἔστιν οὖν ὅ. ὁ τοιοῦτος φιλοσοφήσε; [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 495a, compare “Phdr.” 262b, “Tht.” 154c: so, besides _indicative_ of all tenses, οὐκ ἔσθ᾽ ὅ.]] may be followed by optative with ἄν, οὐ γάρ ἐσθ᾽ ὅπως μί᾽ ἡμέρα γένοιτ᾽ ἂν ἡμέραι δύο [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Nubes” 1181, compare “V.” 212, 5th-6th c.BC: Isocrates Orator 12.156, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Laches” 184c: by _indicative_ with ἄν, οὐκ ἔστιν ὅπως ἂν.. κατέστησαν 5th-6th c.BC: Isocrates Orator 15.206, compare 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 33.28: ἄν]] is omitted in οὐκ ἔσθ᾽ ὅπως λέξαιμι [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Agamemnon” 620, compare 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Alcestis” 52, 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Vespae” 471 (variant{ἔλθωμεν}).]]

__B.I.4

after historical tenses (see. ἵνα [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Bacchylides Lyricus 1.1b), when there is no]]perfect form, or when the aorist represents the perfect, ξυνελέγημεν ἐνθάδε, ὅ. προμελετήσωμεν we were convened, i. e. we have met in assembly, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Ecclesiazusae” 117; παρήλθομεν.., ὅπως μὴ χεῖρον βουλεύσησθε 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 1.73; also when the occurrence purposed is regarded from the point of view of the person purposing, ἦλθον πρεσβευσόμενοι, ὅπως μὴ σφίσι.. τὸ αὐτῶν [ναυτικὸν] ἐμπόδιον γένηται [prev. work] 31, compare 57, 65]], etc.: sometimes the optative and subjunctive appear in consecutive clauses, φρυκτοὺς παρεσκευασμένους ἐς αὐτὸ τοῦτο, ὅπως ἀσαφῆ τὰ σημεῖα.. ᾖ καὶ μὴ βοηθοῖεν [Refs [[prev. author] 3.22, compare 6.96, 7.17.]]

__B.3
with indicative,

__B.3.a
of historical tenses, where the principal clause expresses an action or obligation unfulfilled, εἴθ᾽ εἶχε φωνὴν ἔμφρον᾽ ἀγγέλου δίκην, ὅ. δίφροντις οὖσα μὴ 'κινυσσόμην [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Choephori” 196, compare 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Electra” 1134]]: rare in Prose, ἐδεξάμην ἃν.. φράσαι πρὸς ὑμᾶς.., ὅ... προῄδετε [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Andocides Orator 2.21]]; τίς οὐκ ἂν.. ταῦτα ἐδήλωσεν, ὅ... ταῦτα ἠλέγχθ; [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 36.20; οὐκοῦν ἐχρῆν σε Πηγάσου ζεῦξαι πτερόν, ὅ. ἐφαίνου τοῖς θεοῖς τραγικώτερος 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Pax” 135]]; τί.. οὐκ ἔρριψ᾽ ἐμαυτὴν.. ὅ. ἀπηλλάγη; [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Prometheus Vinctus” 749.]]

of future, θέλγει, ὅ. Ἰθάκης ἐπιλήσεται (= φραζομένη ὅπως ἐ.) [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 1.57, compare 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 1.136; [χρὴ] ἀναβιβάζειν ἐπὶ τὸν τροχὸν τοὺς ἀπογραφέντας, ὅ. μὴ πρότερον νὺξ ἔσται 5th-6th c.BC: Andocides Orator 1.43; ἐμισθώσατο τοῦτον.., ὅ. συνερεῖ 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 19.316]]: sometimes future indicative and aorist subjunctive are conjoined, σιγᾶθ᾽, ὅ. μὴ πεύσεταί τις, ὦ τέκνα, γλώσσης χάριν δὲ πάντ᾽ ἀπαγγείλῃ τάδε [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Choephori” 265.]]

ὁράω, -ῶ,
[in LXX chiefly for ראה, also for חזה, etc. ;] in "durative" sense (hence aor. act., εἶδον, pass., ὤφθην, fut., ὄψομαι, from different roots; see M, Pr., 110f.), to see (in colloq. even the present is rare, its place being generally taken by θεωρέω, see BL, §24).
__1. Of bodily vision, to see, perceive, behold: absol., Mrk.6:38, al.; ἔρχου καὶ ἴδε, Jhn.1:46, al.; before ὅτι, Mrk.2:16, al.; with accusative, Mat.2:2, Mrk.1:10 16:7, Gal.1:19, al.; θεόν, Jhn.1:18, 1Jn.4:20, al.
__2. to see with the mind, perceive, discern: absol, Rom.15:21; with accusative of thing(s), Mat.9:2 27:54, Act.8:23, Col.2:18, al.
__3. to see, take heed, beware: ὅρα μή, with aor. subjc., Mat.8:4 18:10, Mrk.1:44, 1Th.5:15; id., sc. μὴ ποήσῃς, Rev.19:10 22:9 (Bl., §81, 1); before imperat. Mat.9:30 16:6, Mrk.8:15
__4. to experience: τ. θάνατον, Luk.2:26, Heb.11:5; ζωήν, Jhn.3:36; τ. διαφθοράν, Act.2:27.
__5. to visit: with accusative of person(s), Luk.8:20, Jhn.12:21, Rom.1:11, al.; with accusative loc, Act.19:21.
__6. to see to, care for: Mat.27:4, Act.18:15 (cf. ἀφ-, καθ-, προ-, συν-οράω).
SYN.: see: βλέπω. (AS)

Senses:

__A0.I
absolutely, see, look, frequently in [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Homerus Epicus]]; εἴς τι or εἴς τινα to or at a thing or person, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 24.633, 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 20.373, +others, 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Fragmenta” 607; εἰς τὸν πράττοντα 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Poetica” 1460a14]]:—middle, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 5.439, 8th-7th c.BC: Hesiodus Epicus “Opera et Dies” 534, “fragment” 188]]; but ἔς τινα ὁρᾶν to be of so-and-so's party, [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd-3rd c.AD: Philostratus Sophista “Vitae Sophistarum” 1.18]]; εἰς τὴν Ἀττάλου καθαίρεσιν εἶδεν aimed at.., [Refs 8th c.BC+ [1st c.BC: Zosimus Epigrammaticus 6.12; for κατ᾽ αὐτοὺς αἰὲν ὅρα 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 16.646, Τροίην κατὰ πᾶσαν ὁρᾶται 24.291, compare καθοράω 11]]; ὁρόων ἐπ᾽ ἀπείρονα πόντον looking over the sea, [Refs [1.350]]; ὁρᾶν πρός τι look towards, ἀκρωτήριον τὸ πρὸς Μέγαρα ὁρῶν [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 2.93, compare “Anthologia Graeca” 7.496 (4th-5th c.BC: Simonides Lyricus, conjecture)]]; πρὸς πλοῦν ὁρᾷ looks to sail (i.e. is ready), [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Iphigenia Aulidensis” [1624]; ὁ. ἐπὶ τὴν προδοσίαν 1st c.BC: Diodorus Siculus Historicus 36.3; πρὸς σπονδάς [prev. author] 33.1.]]

__A0.I.2
have sight, opposed to μὴ ὁρᾶν, to be blind, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Ajax” 84]]; ὅσ᾽ ἂν λέγωμεν, πάνθ᾽ ὁρῶντα λέξομεν [though I am blind,] my words shall have eyes, i.e. shall be to the purpose, [Refs [[prev. author] “OC” 74]]; ἐν σκότῳ.. οὓς μὲν οὐκ ἔδει ὀψοίαθ᾽, i.e. should be blind, [Refs [[prev. author] “OT” 1274]]; ἀμβλύτερον ὁ., opposed to ὀξύτερον βλέπειν, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 596a]]; ἐπὶ σμικρὸν ὁ. to be short-sighted, [Refs [[prev. author] “Tht.” 174e; ὁ. βραχύ τι [prev. author] “R.” 488b.]]

__A0.I.3
see to, look to, i.e. take or give heed, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 10.239]]; ὁ. εἰς γλῶσσαν.. ἀνδρός look to, pay heed to, [Refs 6th c.BC+ [6th c.BC: Solon Lyricus 11.7, compare 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Supplices” 104 (Lyric poetry)]]: frequently in imperative, like{βλέπε}, followed by a dependent clause, ὅρα ὅπως.. [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Ecclesiazusae” 300, compare 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 5.27]]; ὅρα εἰ.. see whether.., [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Prometheus Vinctus” 997, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Phaedo” 118, etc.; also ὅρα μὴ.. 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Philoctetes” 30, 519, etc.]]; ὅρα τί ποιεῖς[Refs 4th c.BC+ [[prev. work] 589; πῶς.. ὑπερδικεῖς, ὅρα 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Eumenides” 652.]]

__A0.I.4
ὁρᾷ; ὁρᾶτ; see'st thou? d'ye see? parenthetically, especially in explanations, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Nubes” 355, “Th.” 490, etc.; ὡς ὁρᾷς 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Electra” 1114, “Tr.” 365]]; also ὁρᾷ; at the beginning of a sentence, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. author] “El.” 628, 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Andromache” 87]]; ἀλλ᾽—ὁρᾷ; but, do you see.. ?, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Protagoras” 336b; ὁρᾷς οὖν.. ὅτι [prev. author] “Grg.” 475e]]; οὐχ ὁρᾷ; ironically, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 18.232.]]

__A0.I.5
with accusative cognate, like{βλέπω} 11, look so and so, δεινὸν ὁρῶν ὄσσοισι [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th-7th c.BC: Hesiodus Epicus “Scutum Herculis” 426; ὁρᾶν ἀλκάν 5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “O.” 9.111; ἔαρ ὁρόωσα Νύχεια 3rd c.BC: Theocritus Poeta Bucolicus 13.45]]; also ἡδέως ὁρᾶν look pleasant, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Iphigenia Aulidensis” 1122: with _accusative_, κακῶς ὁρᾶν τινα 2nd-3rd c.AD: Philostratus Sophista “Vita Apollonii” 7.42.]]

__A0.II
transitive, see an object, behold, perceive, observe, with accusative, frequently in [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Homerus Epicus, etc.:]]perfect ὄπωπα exclusively in this sense, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 2.799, 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 21.94, etc.]]; ὀφθαλμοῖσιν or ἐν ὀφθαλμοῖσιν ὁρᾶν to see with or before the eyes, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 24.392, 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 8.459, etc.]]; αἰεὶ τέρμ᾽ ὁρόων always keeping it in sight, keeping his eye on it, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 23.323; φίλως χ᾽ ὁρόῳτε καὶ εἰ δέκα πύργοι Ἀχαιῶν.. μαχοίατο, i.e. δέκα πύργους, εἰ μαχοίατο, 4.347]]; ὁ. τινά look to (for aid), [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 45.64: in significations 1 and 11 combined, οὐχ ὁρᾷς ὁρῶν τάδ; 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Agamemnon” 1623, compare 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 25.89.]]

__A0.II.b
ζώει καὶ ὁρᾷ φάος ἠελίοιο, poetry for ζῆν, like{βλέπειν}, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 18.61, 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 4.833, etc.; so φῶς ὁρᾶν 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Tyrannus” 375, 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Orestes” 1523, Alcaeus691]]:— in middle, φέγγος ὁρᾶσθαι [Refs [[prev. author] “Andr.” 113 (eleg.)]]; so ὁρᾶν alone, τὰ γὰρ φθιτῶν τοῖς ὁρῶσι κόσμος [Refs [[prev. author] “Supp.” 78 (Lyric poetry).]]

__A0.II.c
followed by a clause, οὐχ ὁράᾳς οἷος..; [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 21.108]]; ὁρᾷς ἡμᾶς, ὅσοι ἐσμέ; [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 327c]]; οὐχ ὁρᾷς ὅτι ἥμαρτε; [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Prometheus Vinctus” 261, compare 325, 951; Διὸς.. οὐχ ὁρῶ μῆτιν ὅπᾳ φύγοιμ᾽ ἄν [prev. work] 906 (Lyric poetry); ἴδεσθέ μ᾽ οἷα.. πάσχω [prev. work] 92.]]

__A0.II.d
with participle, καπνὸν.. ὁρῶμεν ἀπὸ χθονὸς ἀΐσσοντα we see it rising, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 10.99]]; ὁρῶν ἐμαυτὸν ὧδε προυσελούμενον seeing myself thus insulted, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Prometheus Vinctus” 438, compare 70, 384, +others]]; ὁρῶ σε κρύπτοντα.. see you hiding.., [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Hecuba” 342]]; so ὁρῶ μ᾽ ἔργον ἐξειργασμένην I see that I have done, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Trachiniae” 706; compare below 4b]]; rarely in reference to the subject, ὁρῶ μὲν ἐξαμαρτάνων (= ὅτι ἐξαμαρτάνω) [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Medea” 350]]:—so in middle, ἄνδρα διωκόμενον.. ὁρῶμαι [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 22.169, compare 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Prometheus Vinctus” 896 (Lyric poetry)]]: also with infinitive, ἑώρων οὐκέτι οἷόν τε εἶναι.. [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 8.60.]]

__A0.II.e
rarely with genitive, οὐδεὶς Σωκράτους οὐδὲν ἀσεβὲς.. οὔτε πράττοντος εἶδεν οὔτε λέγοντος ἤκουσεν (where the Constr. is suggested by the use of ἤκουσεν) [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Memorabilia” 1.1.11; μέχρι βορῆος ἀπαστράψαντος ἴδηαι 4th-3rd c.BC: Aratus Epicus 430.]]

__A0.II.2
see to, ἴδε πῶμα [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 8.443]]; look out for, provide, τινί τι [LXX+5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Ajax” 1165 (_anapaest meter_), 3rd c.BC: Theocritus Poeta Bucolicus 15.2; πρόβατον εἰς ὁλοκάρπωσιν LXX.Gen.22.8.]]

__A0.II.3
the infinitive is used after an adjective, δεινὸς ἰδεῖν [Refs 6th c.BC+ [6th c.BC: Solon Lyricus 13.6; εὐφεγγὴς ἰδεῖν 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Persae” 387, compare 398, “Ch.” 174, 176, +others (compare Εἴδω 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus 1.1 a)]]; ἐχθίστου.. ὁρᾶν most hateful to behold, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Ajax” 818; ὦ πάτερ δύσμοιρ᾽ ὁρᾶν [prev. author] “OC” 327; ὁρᾶν στυγνὸς ἦν 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 2.6.9]]:—middle or passive, αἰσχρὸς ὁρᾶσθαι [Refs [[prev. author] “Cyn.” 3.3]]: with an adverb, μὴ διχορρόπως ἰδεῖν [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Agamemnon” 349]]: with a substantive, ἄνδρα τευχηστὴν ἰδεῖν [Refs [[prev. author] “Th.” 644]]: with a Verb, πρέπουσι.. ἰδεῖν [Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. author] “Supp.” 720, compare 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Tyrannus” 792.]]

__A0.II.4
middle is used by Poets like active, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 13.99, 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Persae” 179, “Ch.” 407 (Lyric poetry), 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Antigone” 594 (Lyric poetry), “Tr.” 306, 5th c.BC: Cratinus Comicus 138, etc., see above 11.1 b, c: but in Prose]]middle occurs only in compounds, as προ-ορῶμαι: for the imperative ἰδοῦ, ἰδού, see at {ἰδοῦ}.

__A0.II.4.b
no passive is used by [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Homerus Epicus]]; in Attic dialect the passive has the sense to be seen, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Prometheus Vinctus” 998, “Eu.” 411, etc.: with]]participle, ὤφθημεν ὄντες ἄθλιοι was seen in my wretchedness, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Iphigenia Taurica” 933; ὀφθήσεται διώκων]]he will prove to be.., [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Phaedrus” 239c, compare “Smp.” 178e]]; τὰ ὁρώμενα all that is seen, things visible, like{τὰ ὁρατά}, [Refs [[prev. author] “Prm.” 130a.]]

__A0.III
metaphorically, of mental sight, discern, perceive, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Electra” 945, etc.]]; so blind Oedipus says, φωνῇ γὰρ ὁρῶ, τὸ φατιζόμενον I see by sound, as the saying is, [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [[prev. author] “OC” 138 (_anapaest meter_); ἂν οἴνου.. ὀσμὴν ἴδωσιν 2nd c.AD: Alexander Rhetor 222.4; compare above 1.4, δέρκομαι 1.2.]]

__A0.IV
absolutely, see visions, ὁ ἀληθινῶς ὁρῶν [LXX.Num.24.3, 15]:—passive, appear in a vision, ὤφθη ἄγγελος πρὸς τὴν γυναῖκα[LXX.Judg.13.3.]

__A0.V
interview, ἐμνήσθης μοι ἰδεῖν τὸν κεραμέα περὶ τῶν κεραμίων you told me to see the potter about the jars, [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [“PCair.Zen.” 264 (3rd c.BC).]]

deep_entry:
Abbott-Smith / STEPBible (TBESG)
ὀργή, -ῆς, ἡ
[in LXX chiefly for אַף, also for חָרוֹן, חֵמָה, קָצַף, etc. ;]
__1 1, impulse, propensity, disposition.
__2. anger, wrath;
__(a) of men: Mrk.3:5, Eph.4:31, Col.3:8, 1Ti.2:8, Jas.1:19-20;
__(b) of God;
__α that reaction of the divine nature against sin which in anthropomorphic language is called anger: Rom.1:18 9:22 12:19, (ICC, in l), 1Th.1:10 2:16, Heb.3:11 4:3" (LXX) Rev.14:10 16:19 19:15;
__β of the effect of God's anger: Mat.3:7, Luk.3:7 21:23, Jhn.3:36, Rom.2:5, 8 3:5 4:15 5:9 13:4-5 Eph.5:6, Col.3:6, 1Th.5:9, Jas.1:20, Rev.6:16-17 11:18; σκεύη ὀργῆς, Rom.9:22; τέκνα ὀργῆς, Eph.2:3.†
SYN.: see: θυμός  (AS)

---

LSJ / STEPBible (TFLSJ)
ὀργή, ἡ,
natural impulse or propensity (see. ὀργάω II): hence, temperament, disposition, mood, κηφήνεσσι κοθούροις εἴκελος ὀργήν [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th-7th c.BC: Hesiodus Epicus “Opera et Dies” 304, compare 6th c.BC: Theognis Elegiacus 98, 214, 964, etc.; ὀργὴν ἄλλοτ᾽ ἀλλοίην ἔχει 7th-6th c.BC(?): Semonides Iambographus 7.11]]; so μείλιχος, γλυκεῖα ὀργά, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “P.” 9.43, “I.” 2.35; εὐανθεῖ ἐν ὀργᾷ παρμένων [prev. author] “P.” 1.89; ὀργῆς τραχύτης 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Prometheus Vinctus” 80]]; ὠμή, ἀτέραμνος ὀργή, [Refs [[prev. author] “Supp.” 187, “Pr.” 192, etc.]]; ὀργῆς νοσούσης εἰσὶν ἰατροὶ λόγοι of 'a mind diseased', [Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. work] 380: so in _plural_, “hymnus ad Cererem” 205, 5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “I.” 5(4).34; ὀργαῖς ἀλωπέκων ἴκελοι [prev. author] “P.” 2.77; κνωδάλων ἔχοντες ὀργάς 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Supplices” 763]]; ἀστυνόμοι ὀργαί social dispositions, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Antigone” 356 (Lyric poetry, compare σύντροφος 3); ὀργαὶ ἤπιοι 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Troades” 53]]: also in Prose, διεπειρᾶτο αὐτῶν τῆς τε ἀνδραγαθίης καὶ τῆς ὀργῆς [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 6.128; οὐ τῇ αὐτῇ ὀ. ἀναπειθομένους τε πολεμεῖν καὶ ἐν τῷ ἔργῳ πράσσοντας 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 1.140; τῇ ὀ... χαλεπῇ ἐχρῆτο [prev. work] 130]]; ἐπιφέρειν ὀργάς τινι suit one's moods to another, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. author] 8.83, compare 5th c.BC: Cratinus Comicus 230; ὁ πόλεμος πρὸς τὰ παρόντα τὰς ὀ. τῶν πολλῶν ὁμοιοῖ 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 3.82; τὴν τῶν πολλῶν.. συνιόντων ὀ... σοφίαν ἡγούμενος 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 493d.]]

__II
anger, wrath, ὀργῇ χρῆσθαι to be in a passion, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 6.85, 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Tyrannus” 1241; ὀργὴν ποιήσασθαι 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 3.25; ὀργὴν ποιεῖσθαι εἰ.. 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 4.122; ὀργῇ χάριν δοῦναι 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Coloneus” 855]]; ὀργῇ εἶξαι, χαρίζεσθαι, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Helena” 80, “fragment” 31; ὀργὴν ἔχειν τινί 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Pax” 659 (but ὀ. ἔχει]] involves anger, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 10.44); δι᾽ ὀργῆς ἔχειν τινά 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 5.46]]; ἐν ὀργῇ ἔχειν, ποιεῖσθαί τινα, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. author] 2.65, 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 1.16; οὐ τίθεται ταῦτα παρ᾽ ὑμῖν εἰς.. ἣν προσῆκεν ὀ. [prev. author] 18.138; εἰς ὀργὴν πεσεῖν 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Orestes” 696, etc.; ὀργῇ περιπεπτωκέναι 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator “Epistulae” 2.14]]; ἀνιέναι τῆς ὀργῆς, ὀργὴν χαλᾶν, remit one's anger, be pacified, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Ranae” 700, “V.” 727; ὀ. κατέχειν 4th-3rd c.BC: Philemo Comicus 185; ὀργῆς κρατεῖν 4th-3rd c.BC: Menander Comicus 574]]; ὀ. ἐμποιεῖν τινι make one angry, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Leges” 793e]]; ὀργῆς τυγχάνειν to be visited with anger, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 21.175, etc.]]; ὀργὴν ἄκρος quick to anger, passionate, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.73: in _plural_, ὀργὰς ἀφιέναι 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Prometheus Vinctus” 317; φαίνειν [prev. author] “Ch.” 326 (Lyric poetry), +others]]

__II.2
Adverbial usages, ὀργῇ in anger. in a passion, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.61, 114, 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Tyrannus” 405, etc.; ὀργᾷ περιόργῳ 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Agamemnon” 216 (Lyric poetry); δι᾽ ὀργῆς 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Tyrannus” 807, 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 2.11; δι᾽ ὀργάν 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Eumenides” 981 (Lyric poetry); ἐξ ὀργῆς 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Antigone” 766; κατ᾽ ὀργήν [prev. author] “Tr.” 933, etc.; μετ᾽ ὀργῆς 5th-6th c.BC: Isocrates Orator 2.23, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Apologia” 34d; μετὰ τῆς ὀ. 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 21.76; πρὸς ὀργήν 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Electra” 369, 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Ranae” 844, 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 2.65]]; ὀργῆς χάριν, ὀ. ὕπο, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Andromache” 688, “IA” 335.]]

__II.3
with genitive, Πανὸς ὀργαί visitations of Pan's wrath, [Refs [[prev. author] “Med.” 1172]]; but

__II.3.b
with genitive objecti, ὀργή τινος anger at or because of a thing, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Philoctetes” 1309 (conjecture), 5th c.BC: Lysias Orator 12.20; ὀ. τῆς προδοσίας εἶχε τοὺς Ἀθηναίους 1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus “Themistocles” 9; ἀπύρων ἱερῶν ὀργάς 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Agamemnon” 71 (_anapaest meter_).]]

__II.4
see at {ὀργάς} [Refs 8th c.BC+ [2.—Not in 8th c.BC: Homerus Epicus, who uses θυμός]] instead; once in [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th-7th c.BC: Hesiodus Epicus]]; frequently in Eleg. and Lyric poetry and in Ionic dialect and Attic dialect Prose.

Abbott-Smith / STEPBible (TBESG)
ὀργίζω
(ὀργή), [in LXX chiefly for חָרָה, also for קָצַף, etc. ;]
to make angry, provoke to anger; in cl. most frequently in pass., and so always in NT, to be provoked to anger, be angry: absol., Mat.18:34 22:7, Luk.14:21 15:28, Eph.4:26" (LXX), Rev.11:18; with dative, Mat.5:22; before ἐπί, with dative (3Ki.11:9, al.), Rev.12:17 (cf. παρ-ὀργίζω).†
(AS)

---

LSJ / STEPBible (TFLSJ)
ὀργ-ίζω,

ὄργυιᾰ,
Attic dialect ὄργυᾰ, ᾶς, [Refs [“IG” 22.1672.9]]; Ionic dialect ὄργυιᾰ, ῆς, ἡ (see. below): (ὀρέγω):— the length of the outstretched arms, about 6 feet or I fathom, ἕστηκε ξύλον.. ὅσον τ᾽ ὄργυι᾽ ὑπὲρ αἴης [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 23.327; τοῦ μὲν ὅσον τ᾽ ὄργυιαν ἐγὼν ἀπέκοψα 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 9.325, compare 10.167, 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Memorabilia” 2.3.19.]]

more precisely, αἱ ἑκατὸν ὀργυιαὶ δίκαιαί εἰσι στάδιον ἑξάπλεθρον, ἑξαπέδου τῆς ὀργυιῆς μετρεομένης καὶ τετραπήχεος [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 2.149, compare 4.41, 86, “PHal.” 1.98 (3rd c.BC), “POxy.” 669.39 (3rd c.AD).]]

(Proparox. in nominative and accusative singular, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Homerus Epicus [same places]; oxytone or _perispomenon_ in other cases, cf. Hdn.Gr. 2.613, +others]]; in Ionic dialect the nominative and accusative singular end in -ᾰ, -ᾰν, as in Attic dialect, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Homerus Epicus [same places], the _genitive_ and _dative_ _sing._ in -ῆς, -ῇ (_accusative_ ὀργυιήν]] before consonant in [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-3rd c.BC: Aratus Epicus 69, 196, is corrected to ὄργυιαν by Voss)]]; ὀργυιά, -άν in late Gr., [Refs 2nd c.BC+ [2nd-1st c.BC(?): Hero Mechanicus [same place], etc.)]]

LSJ / STEPBible (TFLSJ)
ὀρέγω,
[Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 17.366, 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Phoenissae” 1710 (Lyric poetry), etc.]]; Ionic dialect and later Prose, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 2.2, 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Historia Animalium” 497b27, etc.]]: imperfect ὤρεγον [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “P.” 4.240, 2nd c.AD: Appianus Historicus “Bella Civilia” 4.126]]: future ὀρέξω [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 13.327, 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Medea” 902]]: aorist ὤρεξα [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 23.406, Trag. (5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Coloneus” 846, etc.), and sometimes in Prose, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Phaedo” 117b, 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 7.3.29]]:—middle and passive, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 24.506, 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 2.65, etc.]]: future ὀρέξομαι [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Helena” 353, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 486a]] (ἐπ-): aorist ὠρεξάμην [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 23.99, 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Hercules Furens” 16, etc.: rare in Prose, 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Memorabilia” 1.2.15]]; also ὠρέχθην[Refs 8th c.BC+ [[prev. work] 16, “Ages.” 1.4, “Smp.” 8.35, 5th c.BC: Hippocrates Medicus “ἐπιστολαί” 17, 4th-3rd c.BC: Epicurus Philosophus “Sententiae” 7, “fragment” 187, as well as in 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus (“Hel.” 1238) (not in 8th c.BC: Homerus Epicus)]]: perfect ὤρεγμαι [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Hippocrates Medicus “περὶ ὀστέων φύσιος” 18]]; reduplicate 3rd.pers. plural ὀρωρέχαται, pluperfect -έχατο, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 16.834, 11.26.]] —Cf. ὀρέγνυμι, ὀριγνάομαι:—reach, stretch, stretch out, χεῖρ᾽ ὀρέγων [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 17.366; εἰς οὐρανόν 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 15.371, 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 9.527; χεῖρας ἐμοὶ ὀρέγοντας, in entreaty, 12.257, compare 1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus “Camillus” 36; μοι.. λεχέων ἐκ χεῖρας ὄρεξας 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 24.743; πρός τινα 5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “P.” 4.240, compare 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Coloneus” 846, etc.]]; Ὅμηρον.., ἐφ᾽ ὃν πᾶσαι χεῖρ᾽ ὀρέγουσι πόλεις, to claim him, [Refs [“APl.” 4.294.]]

__2
reach out, hold out, hand, give, κοτύλην καὶ πύρνον [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 15.312; δέπας 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 24.102; ὁπποτέροισι πατὴρ Ζεὺς κῦδος ὀρέξῃ 5.33, compare 17.453, 8th-7th c.BC: Hesiodus Epicus “Theogonia” 433; ἠέ τῳ εὖχος ὀρέξομεν, ἦέ τις ἡμῖν 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 12.328, compare 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Philoctetes” 1203 (Lyric poetry); ὀ. πλοῦτόν τινι 5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “P.” 3.110; τέλος ἔμπεδον [prev. author] “N.” 7.58; ὤρεξε τὴν κύλικα τῷ Σωκράτει 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Phaedo” 117b]]; later βοήθειαν ὀρέξαι τοῖς ἀδικουμένοις extend help, [Refs 5th c.AD+ [“POxy.” 902.11 (5th c.AD).]]

__II
middle and passive,

__II.1
absolutely, stretch oneself out, stretch forth one's hand, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 21.53; ἀνδρὸς.. ποτὶ στόμα χεῖρ᾽ ὀρέγεσθαι 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 24.506 (but χεῖρας ὀρεξαμένου]]having lent a helping hand, [Refs [epigram Gr. 448.4 (from Syria))]]; ὀρεξαμένη ἀπὸ δίφρου [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th-7th c.BC: Hesiodus Epicus “Scutum Herculis” 456]]; ὠρέξατο χερσὶ φίλῃσι, χειρὶ σκαιῇ, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 23.99, 8th-7th c.BC: Hesiodus Epicus “Theogonia” 178]]; ἔγχει ὀρεξάσθω let him lunge with the spear (from the chariot), [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 4.307; πρόσθεν Ἄρης ὠρέξαθ᾽ ὑπὲρ ζυγὸν.. ἔγχεϊ χαλκείῳ 5.851]]; ποσσὶν ὀρωρέχαται πολεμίζειν, of horses, they galloped to the fight, [Refs [16.834]]; ὀρέξατ᾽ ἰών he stretched himself as he went, i.e. made a stride, [Refs [13.20]]; ὀρωρέχατο προτὶ δειρήν were stretched out towards the neck, [Refs [11.26]]; of fish, rise at the bait, καί τις τῶν τραφερῶν ὠρέξατο [Refs 4th c.BC+ [3rd c.BC: Theocritus Poeta Bucolicus 21.44; for 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Agamemnon” 1111, see at {ὄρεγμα} I.1.]]

__II.2
with genitive, reach at or to a thing, grasp at, οὗ παιδὸς ὀρέξατο he reached out to his child, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 6.466, compare 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 11.392]]; in a hostile sense, aim at, assail, hit, τοῦ δ᾽ ἀντίθεος Θρασυμήδης ἔφθη ὀρεξάμενος.. ὦμον hit him first on the shoulder, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 16.322; [prev. work] 314, a _genitive_ _person_ must be supplied, ἔφθη ὀρεξάμενος πρυμνὸν σκέλο; so in 23.805 ὁππότερός κε φθῇσιν ὀρεξάμενος χρόα καλόν]]; δηΐων ὀρέγοιτ᾽ ἐγγύθεν ἱστάμενος [Refs 7th c.BC+ [7th c.BC: Tyrtaeus Elegiacus 12.12]]; also of a suppliant, τί χρῆμα θηρῶσ᾽ ἱκέτις ὠρέχθης ἐμο; [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Helena” 1238.]]

__II.2.b
metaphorically, reach after, grasp at, yearn for, γάμων [Refs 3rd c.AD+ [[prev. author] “Ion” 842; τῶν μεγίστων [prev. author] “fragment” 240; ἀπεόντων 3rd c.AD: Democritus Epigrammaticus 202; ζωῆς [prev. author] 205]]: frequently in Attic dialect Prose, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Antipho Orator 2.2.12, 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 3.42, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 439b, 485d, etc.; ὀ. τοῦ πρῶτος ἕκαστος γίγνεσθαι 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 2.65]]: so with infinitive, πόλιν ὠρέξατ᾽ οἰκεῖν [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Hercules Furens” 16; ὀ. τοιοῦτος γενέσθαι 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Protagoras” 326a; οὐδέποτε ὠρέχθην τοῖς πολλοῖς ἀρέσκειν 4th-3rd c.BC: Epicurus Philosophus “Fragmenta” 187]]: also, absolutely, yearn, desire, πάσῃσιν ὀρέξαιτο πραπίδεσσιν [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Empedocles Poeta Philosophus 129.4; θυμὸς ὀρέξατο γηθοσύνῃσιν 3rd c.BC: Apollonius Rhodius Epicus 2.878; ὀρεγόμεθα κατὰ τὴν βούλευσιν 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Ethica Nicomachea” 1113a12]]; compare ὀρεκτός, ὄρεξις.

__II.3
with accusative, σῖτόν τ᾽ ὄρεξαι take food, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Orestes” 303 (variant{σίτων})]]; αἰώρημα διὰ δέρης ὀρέξομαι I will put the noose on my neck, [Refs [[prev. author] “Hel.” 353 (Lyric poetry).]]

in height, upright, standing, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Homerus Epicus]], who commonly joins it with στῆναι, στῆ δ᾽ ὀρθός [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 23.271, +others, compare 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 5.111, 9.22 (where it is used of a horse rearing)]]; ὀρθαὶ τρίχες ἔσταν [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 24.359, compare 8th-7th c.BC: Hesiodus Epicus “Opera et Dies” 540; ὀρθῶν ἑσταότων ἀγορή 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 18.246; οἱ δ᾽ ἐν νηΐ μ᾽ ἔδησαν.. ὀρθὸν ἐν ἱστοπέδῃ 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 12.179, compare 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Ajax” 239 (_anapaest meter_); κυρβασίας.. ὀρθὰς εἶχον πεπηγυίας 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 7.64; ὀρθὸν αἴρεις κάρα 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Choephori” 496, etc.]]; ὀρθὸν οὖς ἵστησι pricks up his ear, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Electra” 27, etc.]]; applied to the erect posture of man, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “de Partibus Animalium” 653a31, +others]]; ὀ. θηρίον, of man, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-3rd c.BC: Philemo Comicus 3]]; of buildings, standing with their walls entire, [τὸ Πάνακτον] ὀρθὸν παραδοῦναι [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 5.42; ὀρθαὶ κίονες 5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “P.” 4.267, compare “PLond.” 3.755v. 2 (4th c.AD)]]; of a standing crop, [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [[prev. work] 1165.2 (2nd c.AD).]] adverb, ὀρθῶς ἑστῶτες [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “de Partibus Animalium” 689b19.]]

__I.b
Geometry texts, at right angles to.., εὐθεῖα πρὸς ἐπίπεδον ὀρθή ἐστιν ὅταν.. [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [3rd c.BC: Euclides Geometra 11 “Def.” 3.]]

__I.c
Astrology texts, ὀρθὰ ζῴδια signs which rise vertically, opposed to πλάγια, [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd c.AD: Dorotheus Astrologus in “Cat. Codex Astr.” 5 (1). 240.]]

__II
in line, straight (opposed to σκολιός crooked and πλάγιος aslant), ἀντ᾽ ἠελίου τετραμμένος ὀρθός straight, right opposite the sun, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th-7th c.BC: Hesiodus Epicus “Opera et Dies” 727; ὀρθὸν εὐθύνοι βέλος 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Fragmenta - American Journal of Philology” 200]]; ποιῶν ὀρθὰ πάντα πρὸς κανόνα [Refs 2nd c.BC+ [“IG” 7.3073.108 (Lebadea, 2nd c.BC)]]; ὀ. τρῶμα longitudinal to the muscle, opposed to ἐπικάρσιος, [Refs 6th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Hippocrates Medicus “προρρητικόν” 2.15; ὀρθὸς εἰς ὁδὸν πορεύεται 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Ajax” 1254; εἶμι.. ὀ. ὁδόν 6th c.BC: Theognis Elegiacus 945; ὀ. κέλευθον ἰών 5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “P.” 11.39]]; ὀρθὴν κελεύεις, i. e. ὀρθὴν ὁδόν με ἰέναι κ., [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Aves” 1]]; so ὀρθὴν ἄνω δίωκε (i.e. όδόν) [Refs 4th c.BC+ [[prev. author] “Th.” 1223 (but ὀρθήν, ={εὐθύς}, 4th c.BC: Hyperides Orator “Fragmenta” 257)]]; δι᾽ ὀρθῆς τήνδε ναυκληρεῖς πόλιν (i.e. ὁδοῦ) [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Antigone” 994; εἰς ὀρθὸν τρέχειν 4th-3rd c.BC: Diphilus Comicus 61.5]]; εἰς ὀρθὸν ἀποδοῦναι to face the front originally held, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [1st c.BC: Asclepiodotus Tacticus “Tact.” 10.1; κατ᾽ ὀρθὸν εὐδρομεῖν 4th-3rd c.BC: Menander Comicus 681]]; also ὀρθᾷ χερί straightway, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “O.” 10(11).4]]; ὀρθῷ ποδί[Refs [[prev. work] 13.72, “fragment” 167]]; but τιθέναι ὀρθὸν πόδα is probably to put the foot out, as in walking, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Eumenides” 294 (see. κατηρεφής 1), compare 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Medea” 1166.]]

__II.2
βλέπειν ὀρθά, opposed to being blind, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Tyrannus” 419; ὀρθὸν ἀνέβλεψε]]recovered his sight, [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [Inscriptiones Graecae 14.966 (Rome, 2nd c.AD)]]; ἐξ ὀμμάτων ὀ.. κἀξ ὀρθῆς φρενός [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Tyrannus” 528; ὀρθοῖς ὄμμασιν [prev. work] 1385; see at {ὄμμα} 1.]]

__III
metaphorically,

__III.1
right, safe, prosperous:

__III.1.a
partly from signification[Refs [1, τοὺς δὲ τομαῖς ἔστασεν ὀρθούς]]set them up, restored, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “P.” 3.53]]; so ὀρθὸν ἀστάσας (= ἀναστήσας) [Refs 4th c.BC+ [“IG” 42(1).122.52 (Epid., 4th c.BC)]]; ἐς ὀρθὸν ἱστάναι τινά [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Supplices” 1230; ὀρθὰν φυλάσσειν Τένεδον 5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “N.” 11.5; so στάντες τ᾽ ἐς ὀρθὸν καὶ πεσόντες ὕστερον 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Tyrannus” 50, compare 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Laches” 181b]]; ταύτης ἔπι (i.e. χθονός) πλέοντες ὀρθῆς (the state being represented as a ship) [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Antigone” 190; ἐν ὀρθῷ κεῖσθαι 2nd c.BC: Polybius Historicus 31.7.1.]]

__III.1.b
partly from signification [Refs 5th c.BC+ [11, κατ᾽ ὀρθὸν ἐξελθεῖν, of prophecies, 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Tyrannus” 88, compare “OC” 1424]]; κατ᾽ ὀρθὸν οὐρίσαι to speed in prosperous course, [Refs [[prev. author] “OT” 695 (Lyric poetry).]]

__III.2
right, true, correct, ἄγγελος, ἀγγελία, νόος, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “O.” 6.90, “P.” 4.279, 10.68; μάρτυρες 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Eumenides” 318 (_anapaest meter_), etc.; γλῶσσα 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Fragmenta” 351; ὀρθᾷ φρενί 5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “O.” 8.24]]; ὄρθ᾽ ἀκούειν to be rightly, truly called, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Tyrannus” 903 (Lyric poetry); κατὰ τὸ ὀ. δικάζειν 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.96; ὀ. λόγῳ]]strictly speaking, in very truth, [Refs [[prev. author] 2.17, 6.68, etc.]]: so in adverb, ὀρθῶς λέγειν [Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. author] 1.51; ὀ. ἔλεξας 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Philoctetes” 341; ὀ. φράσαι 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Choephori” 526; εἴρηκας ὀ. 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Electra” 1040; ὀ. φρονεῖν 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Prometheus Vinctus” 1000, 4th c.BC: Archytas Tarentinus Philosophus 1 (so εἰς ὀρθὸν φ. 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Fragmenta” 612); ὀ. γνῶναι 5th c.BC: Antipho Orator 2.2.8]]; ὀ. ἔχει it is right, with infinitive, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Euthyphro” 9a; ὀ. ἐνδίκως τ᾽ ἐπώνυμον 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Septem contra Thebas” 405, compare 829 (_anapaest meter_)]]: in answers, rightly, exactly, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Protagoras” 359e; ὀ. γε 4th-3rd c.BC: Diphilus Comicus 32.18]]: superlative, ὀρθότατα καλεόμενος [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 4.59; so τὸ ὀρθὸν ἐξείρηκα 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Trachiniae” 374]]; φωνεῖν δίκης ἐς ὀρθόν[Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. work] 347; κατ᾽ ὀρθόν 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Timaeus” 44b.]]

__III.3
true, real, genuine, ὀ. πολιτεῖαι, opposed to παρεκβάσεις, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Politica” 1279a18, etc.]]; ὀ. μανία real madness, [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [2nd-3rd c.AD: Aelianus “De Natura Animalium - Ar.Byzantine Epit.” 11.32, compare 3rd c.BC: Theocritus Poeta Bucolicus 11.11.]] adverb -θῶς really, truly, τοὺς ὀ. φιλομαθεῖς [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Phaedo” 67b; ὁ ὀ. κυβερνήτης [prev. author] “R.” 341c; τὸν ὀ. συγγενῆ 4th-3rd c.BC: Diphilus Comicus 102.]]

__III.4
upright, just, ἐμμένειν ὀ. νόμῳ [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Ajax” 350 (Lyric poetry); τὸ ὀ.]]uprightness, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 540d]]; ἐπιστήμη ἐνοῦσα καὶ ὀ. λόγος (see. λόγος IV. I) [Refs [[prev. author] “Phd.” 73a]]; ὁ ὀ. λόγος διὰ πάντων ἐρχόμενος (see. λόγος [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [111.7) 3rd c.BC: Chrysippus Stoicus 3.4]]; ὀ. λόγοι virtues on the intellectual side, [Refs 1st c.BC+ [1st c.BC: Philodemus Philosophus “de Pietate - Herkulanische Studien” 8]]. adverb ὀρθῶς rightly, justly, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 3.56; ὀ. καὶ δικαίως 5th c.BC: Antipho Orator 1.10, “IG” 22.228.14 (4th c.BC), “IPE” 12.32 B 73 (Olbia, 3rd c.BC), etc.]]; ὀ. καὶ νομίμως [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Isocrates Orator 7.28.]]

__III.5
of persons, 'straight', straightforward, σμικροὶ καὶ οὐκ ὀρθοὶ τὰς ψυχάς [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Theaetetus” 173a.]]

__III.6
on tiptoe, full of expectation, excited, ὀρθῆς τῆς πόλεως γενομένης διά τι [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Isocrates Orator 16.7; τὴν Ἑλλάδα ὀρθὴν οὖσαν ἐπί τινι [prev. author] 5.70; ὀ. ἦν ἡ πόλις ἐπὶ τοῖς συμβεβηκόσιν 4th c.BC: Lycurgus Orator 39, compare 4th c.BC: Hyperides Orator “Fragmenta” 39; ὀ. καὶ μετέωροι ταῖς διανοίαις 2nd c.BC: Polybius Historicus 28.17.11; ὀ. καὶ περίφοβος ἦν ἡ πόλις [prev. author] 3.112.6; ὀ. διὰ τὸν φόβον 1st c.BC: Diodorus Siculus Historicus 16.84; ὀ. καὶ δραστήριος διὰ τὸ θαρρεῖν 1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus “Philopoemen” 12.]]

__IV
ἡ ὀρθή,

__IV.1
(i.e. ὁδός) see above [Refs [11.1.]]

__IV.2
ὀ. γωνία right angle, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Timaeus” 55b]]; so ὀ. alone, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Ethica Nicomachea” 1098a30, +others; compare ὄρθιος see 1: τέμνειν πρὸς ὀρθάς]] to cut at right angles, [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [3rd c.BC: Euclides Geometra 3.3, +others]]; εἴ τις δείξειεν ὅτι αἱ ὀρθαὶ οὐ συμπίπτουσι.. that right angles do not meet (short for 'that two straight lines making, with a third, interior angles equal to two right angles, etc.'), [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Anthologia Graeca” 0.74a13]]; τὸ δυσὶν ὀρθαῖς the theorem that the angles of a triangle are together equal to two right angles, [Refs [[prev. work]85b5]]; ὀρθὸς κῶνος, κύλινδρος, a right cone, cylinder, [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [3rd c.BC: Archimedes Geometra “περὶ σφαίρας καὶ κυλίνδρου” 1.26, 1.11.]]

__IV.3
(with or without πτῶσις) nominative, Latin casus rectus, opposed to the oblique cases, [Refs 2nd c.BC+ [2nd c.BC: Dionysius Thrax Grammaticus 636.3, 1st c.BC-1st c.AD: Strabo Geographus 14.2.28, 2nd c.AD: Apollonius Dyscolus Grammaticus “de Pronominibus;” 39.10, +others, 2nd c.AD: Sextus Empiricus Philosophus “adversus Mathematicos” 1.177.]]

__V
ὀρθά active verbs, opposed to ὕπτια (passive) and οὐδέτερα (neuter), [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [3rd c.BC: Chrysippus Stoicus 2.59.]]

__VI
ὀ. τόνος real or unmodified (compare above [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [111.3) accent, opposed to ἐγκλινόμενος, 2nd c.AD: Apollonius Dyscolus Grammaticus “de Pronominibus;” 36.10, +others; so ὀρθὴ τάσις [prev. work] 54.8, +others (The gloss of 5th c.AD(?): Hesychius Legal icographus, βορθ-αγορίσκοι, ={ὀ}., and the dialect forms of Ὀρθεία (which see), suggest that the word originally had ϝ.)]]

straight,

__I
in height, upright, standing, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Homerus Epicus]], who commonly joins it with στῆναι, στῆ δ᾽ ὀρθός [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 23.271, +others, compare 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 5.111, 9.22 (where it is used of a horse rearing)]]; ὀρθαὶ τρίχες ἔσταν [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 24.359, compare 8th-7th c.BC: Hesiodus Epicus “Opera et Dies” 540; ὀρθῶν ἑσταότων ἀγορή 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 18.246; οἱ δ᾽ ἐν νηΐ μ᾽ ἔδησαν.. ὀρθὸν ἐν ἱστοπέδῃ 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 12.179, compare 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Ajax” 239 (_anapaest meter_); κυρβασίας.. ὀρθὰς εἶχον πεπηγυίας 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 7.64; ὀρθὸν αἴρεις κάρα 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Choephori” 496, etc.]]; ὀρθὸν οὖς ἵστησι pricks up his ear, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Electra” 27, etc.]]; applied to the erect posture of man, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “de Partibus Animalium” 653a31, +others]]; ὀ. θηρίον, of man, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-3rd c.BC: Philemo Comicus 3]]; of buildings, standing with their walls entire, [τὸ Πάνακτον] ὀρθὸν παραδοῦναι [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 5.42; ὀρθαὶ κίονες 5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “P.” 4.267, compare “PLond.” 3.755v. 2 (4th c.AD)]]; of a standing crop, [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [[prev. work] 1165.2 (2nd c.AD).]] adverb, ὀρθῶς ἑστῶτες [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “de Partibus Animalium” 689b19.]]

__I.b
Geometry texts, at right angles to.., εὐθεῖα πρὸς ἐπίπεδον ὀρθή ἐστιν ὅταν.. [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [3rd c.BC: Euclides Geometra 11 “Def.” 3.]]

__I.c
Astrology texts, ὀρθὰ ζῴδια signs which rise vertically, opposed to πλάγια, [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd c.AD: Dorotheus Astrologus in “Cat. Codex Astr.” 5 (1). 240.]]

__II
in line, straight (opposed to σκολιός crooked and πλάγιος aslant), ἀντ᾽ ἠελίου τετραμμένος ὀρθός straight, right opposite the sun, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th-7th c.BC: Hesiodus Epicus “Opera et Dies” 727; ὀρθὸν εὐθύνοι βέλος 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Fragmenta - American Journal of Philology” 200]]; ποιῶν ὀρθὰ πάντα πρὸς κανόνα [Refs 2nd c.BC+ [“IG” 7.3073.108 (Lebadea, 2nd c.BC)]]; ὀ. τρῶμα longitudinal to the muscle, opposed to ἐπικάρσιος, [Refs 6th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Hippocrates Medicus “προρρητικόν” 2.15; ὀρθὸς εἰς ὁδὸν πορεύεται 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Ajax” 1254; εἶμι.. ὀ. ὁδόν 6th c.BC: Theognis Elegiacus 945; ὀ. κέλευθον ἰών 5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “P.” 11.39]]; ὀρθὴν κελεύεις, i. e. ὀρθὴν ὁδόν με ἰέναι κ., [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Aves” 1]]; so ὀρθὴν ἄνω δίωκε (i.e. όδόν) [Refs 4th c.BC+ [[prev. author] “Th.” 1223 (but ὀρθήν, ={εὐθύς}, 4th c.BC: Hyperides Orator “Fragmenta” 257)]]; δι᾽ ὀρθῆς τήνδε ναυκληρεῖς πόλιν (i.e. ὁδοῦ) [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Antigone” 994; εἰς ὀρθὸν τρέχειν 4th-3rd c.BC: Diphilus Comicus 61.5]]; εἰς ὀρθὸν ἀποδοῦναι to face the front originally held, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [1st c.BC: Asclepiodotus Tacticus “Tact.” 10.1; κατ᾽ ὀρθὸν εὐδρομεῖν 4th-3rd c.BC: Menander Comicus 681]]; also ὀρθᾷ χερί straightway, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “O.” 10(11).4]]; ὀρθῷ ποδί[Refs [[prev. work] 13.72, “fragment” 167]]; but τιθέναι ὀρθὸν πόδα is probably to put the foot out, as in walking, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Eumenides” 294 (see. κατηρεφής 1), compare 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Medea” 1166.]]

__II.2
βλέπειν ὀρθά, opposed to being blind, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Tyrannus” 419; ὀρθὸν ἀνέβλεψε]]recovered his sight, [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [Inscriptiones Graecae 14.966 (Rome, 2nd c.AD)]]; ἐξ ὀμμάτων ὀ.. κἀξ ὀρθῆς φρενός [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Tyrannus” 528; ὀρθοῖς ὄμμασιν [prev. work] 1385; see at {ὄμμα} 1.]]

__III
metaphorically,

__III.1
right, safe, prosperous:

__III.1.a
partly from signification[Refs [1, τοὺς δὲ τομαῖς ἔστασεν ὀρθούς]]set them up, restored, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “P.” 3.53]]; so ὀρθὸν ἀστάσας (= ἀναστήσας) [Refs 4th c.BC+ [“IG” 42(1).122.52 (Epid., 4th c.BC)]]; ἐς ὀρθὸν ἱστάναι τινά [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Supplices” 1230; ὀρθὰν φυλάσσειν Τένεδον 5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “N.” 11.5; so στάντες τ᾽ ἐς ὀρθὸν καὶ πεσόντες ὕστερον 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Tyrannus” 50, compare 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Laches” 181b]]; ταύτης ἔπι (i.e. χθονός) πλέοντες ὀρθῆς (the state being represented as a ship) [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Antigone” 190; ἐν ὀρθῷ κεῖσθαι 2nd c.BC: Polybius Historicus 31.7.1.]]

__III.1.b
partly from signification [Refs 5th c.BC+ [11, κατ᾽ ὀρθὸν ἐξελθεῖν, of prophecies, 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Tyrannus” 88, compare “OC” 1424]]; κατ᾽ ὀρθὸν οὐρίσαι to speed in prosperous course, [Refs [[prev. author] “OT” 695 (Lyric poetry).]]

__III.2
right, true, correct, ἄγγελος, ἀγγελία, νόος, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “O.” 6.90, “P.” 4.279, 10.68; μάρτυρες 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Eumenides” 318 (_anapaest meter_), etc.; γλῶσσα 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Fragmenta” 351; ὀρθᾷ φρενί 5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “O.” 8.24]]; ὄρθ᾽ ἀκούειν to be rightly, truly called, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Tyrannus” 903 (Lyric poetry); κατὰ τὸ ὀ. δικάζειν 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.96; ὀ. λόγῳ]]strictly speaking, in very truth, [Refs [[prev. author] 2.17, 6.68, etc.]]: so in adverb, ὀρθῶς λέγειν [Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. author] 1.51; ὀ. ἔλεξας 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Philoctetes” 341; ὀ. φράσαι 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Choephori” 526; εἴρηκας ὀ. 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Electra” 1040; ὀ. φρονεῖν 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Prometheus Vinctus” 1000, 4th c.BC: Archytas Tarentinus Philosophus 1 (so εἰς ὀρθὸν φ. 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Fragmenta” 612); ὀ. γνῶναι 5th c.BC: Antipho Orator 2.2.8]]; ὀ. ἔχει it is right, with infinitive, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Euthyphro” 9a; ὀ. ἐνδίκως τ᾽ ἐπώνυμον 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Septem contra Thebas” 405, compare 829 (_anapaest meter_)]]: in answers, rightly, exactly, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Protagoras” 359e; ὀ. γε 4th-3rd c.BC: Diphilus Comicus 32.18]]: superlative, ὀρθότατα καλεόμενος [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 4.59; so τὸ ὀρθὸν ἐξείρηκα 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Trachiniae” 374]]; φωνεῖν δίκης ἐς ὀρθόν[Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. work] 347; κατ᾽ ὀρθόν 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Timaeus” 44b.]]

__III.3
true, real, genuine, ὀ. πολιτεῖαι, opposed to παρεκβάσεις, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Politica” 1279a18, etc.]]; ὀ. μανία real madness, [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [2nd-3rd c.AD: Aelianus “De Natura Animalium - Ar.Byzantine Epit.” 11.32, compare 3rd c.BC: Theocritus Poeta Bucolicus 11.11.]] adverb -θῶς really, truly, τοὺς ὀ. φιλομαθεῖς [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Phaedo” 67b; ὁ ὀ. κυβερνήτης [prev. author] “R.” 341c; τὸν ὀ. συγγενῆ 4th-3rd c.BC: Diphilus Comicus 102.]]

__III.4
upright, just, ἐμμένειν ὀ. νόμῳ [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Ajax” 350 (Lyric poetry); τὸ ὀ.]]uprightness, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 540d]]; ἐπιστήμη ἐνοῦσα καὶ ὀ. λόγος (see. λόγος IV. I) [Refs [[prev. author] “Phd.” 73a]]; ὁ ὀ. λόγος διὰ πάντων ἐρχόμενος (see. λόγος [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [111.7) 3rd c.BC: Chrysippus Stoicus 3.4]]; ὀ. λόγοι virtues on the intellectual side, [Refs 1st c.BC+ [1st c.BC: Philodemus Philosophus “de Pietate - Herkulanische Studien” 8]]. adverb ὀρθῶς rightly, justly, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 3.56; ὀ. καὶ δικαίως 5th c.BC: Antipho Orator 1.10, “IG” 22.228.14 (4th c.BC), “IPE” 12.32 B 73 (Olbia, 3rd c.BC), etc.]]; ὀ. καὶ νομίμως [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Isocrates Orator 7.28.]]

__III.5
of persons, 'straight', straightforward, σμικροὶ καὶ οὐκ ὀρθοὶ τὰς ψυχάς [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Theaetetus” 173a.]]

__III.6
on tiptoe, full of expectation, excited, ὀρθῆς τῆς πόλεως γενομένης διά τι [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Isocrates Orator 16.7; τὴν Ἑλλάδα ὀρθὴν οὖσαν ἐπί τινι [prev. author] 5.70; ὀ. ἦν ἡ πόλις ἐπὶ τοῖς συμβεβηκόσιν 4th c.BC: Lycurgus Orator 39, compare 4th c.BC: Hyperides Orator “Fragmenta” 39; ὀ. καὶ μετέωροι ταῖς διανοίαις 2nd c.BC: Polybius Historicus 28.17.11; ὀ. καὶ περίφοβος ἦν ἡ πόλις [prev. author] 3.112.6; ὀ. διὰ τὸν φόβον 1st c.BC: Diodorus Siculus Historicus 16.84; ὀ. καὶ δραστήριος διὰ τὸ θαρρεῖν 1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus “Philopoemen” 12.]]

__IV
ἡ ὀρθή,

__IV.1
(i.e. ὁδός) see above [Refs [11.1.]]

__IV.2
ὀ. γωνία right angle, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Timaeus” 55b]]; so ὀ. alone, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Ethica Nicomachea” 1098a30, +others; compare ὄρθιος see 1: τέμνειν πρὸς ὀρθάς]] to cut at right angles, [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [3rd c.BC: Euclides Geometra 3.3, +others]]; εἴ τις δείξειεν ὅτι αἱ ὀρθαὶ οὐ συμπίπτουσι.. that right angles do not meet (short for 'that two straight lines making, with a third, interior angles equal to two right angles, etc.'), [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Anthologia Graeca” 0.74a13]]; τὸ δυσὶν ὀρθαῖς the theorem that the angles of a triangle are together equal to two right angles, [Refs [[prev. work]85b5]]; ὀρθὸς κῶνος, κύλινδρος, a right cone, cylinder, [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [3rd c.BC: Archimedes Geometra “περὶ σφαίρας καὶ κυλίνδρου” 1.26, 1.11.]]

__IV.3
(with or without πτῶσις) nominative, Latin casus rectus, opposed to the oblique cases, [Refs 2nd c.BC+ [2nd c.BC: Dionysius Thrax Grammaticus 636.3, 1st c.BC-1st c.AD: Strabo Geographus 14.2.28, 2nd c.AD: Apollonius Dyscolus Grammaticus “de Pronominibus;” 39.10, +others, 2nd c.AD: Sextus Empiricus Philosophus “adversus Mathematicos” 1.177.]]

__V
ὀρθά active verbs, opposed to ὕπτια (passive) and οὐδέτερα (neuter), [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [3rd c.BC: Chrysippus Stoicus 2.59.]]

__VI
ὀ. τόνος real or unmodified (compare above [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [111.3) accent, opposed to ἐγκλινόμενος, 2nd c.AD: Apollonius Dyscolus Grammaticus “de Pronominibus;” 36.10, +others; so ὀρθὴ τάσις [prev. work] 54.8, +others (The gloss of 5th c.AD(?): Hesychius Legal icographus, βορθ-αγορίσκοι, ={ὀ}., and the dialect forms of Ὀρθεία (which see), suggest that the word originally had ϝ.)]]
