Abbott-Smith / STEPBible (TBESG)
ὁρίζω
(ὅρος, a boundary), [in LXX for אָסַר, גְּבוּל, etc. ;]
__1. to separate, mark off by boundaries (so Num.34:6, Jhn.13:27).
__2. to determine, appoint, designate: of time, with accusative, Act.17:26, Heb.4:7; with accusative of person(s), Act.17:31; with inf., Act.11:29; pass., Luk.22:22, Act.2:23 10:42, Rom.1:4 (cf. ὀφ-, ἀπο- δι-, τρο-ορίζω),†
(AS)

---

LSJ / STEPBible (TFLSJ)
ὁρίζω,
Ionic dialect οὐρ- [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus (see. below)]]: future ὁριῶ [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Categoriae” 5b5, (δι-) 5th-6th c.BC: Isocrates Orator 4.174]]: aorist ὥρισα [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Antigone” 452, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Leges” 864e]]; Ionic dialect οὔρισα [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 3.142]]: perfect ὥρικα [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 26.24, 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Meteorologica” 382a19]]:—middle, future -ιοῦμαι[Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Theaetetus” 190e, “Lg.” 737d]]: aorist ὡρισάμην [Refs 4th c.BC+ [[prev. author] “Tht.” 148a, 4th c.BC: Epicrates Comicus 11.18, etc.]]:—passive, future ὁρισθήσομαι [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Theaetetus” 158d]]: aorist ὡρίσθην [Refs [[prev. author] “Chrm.” 171a]]: perfect ὥρισμαι [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 1.71, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Symposium” 182a, etc.]]; but in middle sense, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Hecuba” 801, 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 31.5]]: (ὅρος):—divide or separate from, as a border or boundary, c.accusative et dative, ὁ Νεῖλος ὁ τὴν Ἀσίην οὐρίζων τῇ Λιβύῃ [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 2.16: with _accusative_ et _genitive_, 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Philoctetes” 636]]:—passive, θύρᾳ βαλανωτῇ ὡρισμένην ἀπὸ τῆς ἀνδρωνίτιδος [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Oeconomicus” 9.5]]; or

__b
with two accusatives joined by καί, separate, [λίμνη] οὐρίζει τήν τε Σκυθικὴν καὶ τὴν Νευρίδα γῆν [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 4.51, compare 56, 7.123, 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Historia Animalium” 501b16, “OGI” 335.112 (Pergam., 2nd c.BC), 3rd c.BC: Lycophron Tragicus 1289, etc.; ἐὰν.. κύκλος.. ὁρίζῃ τό τε ἀφανὲς καὶ τὸ φανερὸν ἡμισφαίριον 4th c.BC: Autolycus Astronomus “Sph.” 4: hence ὁρίζων κύκλος [prev. author] 1.1]]; see at {ὁρίζων}.

__c
delimit, χρὴ τὸν νόμον ὁρίζειν πειρᾶσθαι κατὰ μέρη [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Leges” 944a.]]

__2
bound, τὴν ἀρχὴν ὥριζεν αὐτῷ ἡ Ἐρυθρὰ θάλαττα [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 8.6.21; τὰ δὲ πρὸς Τριβαλλοὺς.. Τρῆρες ὥριζον 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 2.96]]; of a line (or surface) as limiting a surface (or solid), [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Metaphysica” 1017b17]]:—passive, Εὔβοια.. ὅροις ὑγροῖσιν ὡρισμένη [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Ion” 295: _metaphorically_, ὡρίσθω μέχρι τοῦδε]] so far let it go and no further, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 1.71.]]

__3
pass between or through, διδύμους πέτρας [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Medea” 433 (Lyric poetry).]]

__4
part, divide, χειμὼν ἄλλοσ᾽ ἄλλον ὥρισεν [Refs [[prev. author] “Hel.” 128]]; ὁ. τινὰ ἀπὸ.. banish one from.., [Refs [[prev. author] “Hec.” 941 (Lyric poetry):]] —passive, ματρὸς ἐκ χερῶν ὁ. depart from.., [Refs [[prev. author] “Ion” 1459 (Lyric poetry)]], but very uncertain in [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Ecclesiazusae” 202; compare ἐξορίζω (A) 11, 111.]]

__II
mark out by boundaries, mark out, βωμὸν ἱδρύσατο καὶ τέμενος περὶ αὐτὸν οὔρισε [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 3.142, compare 6.108, 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Trachiniae” 754, 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Helena” 1670, “IG” 12.76.54, 42(1).76.19 (_passive_, Epid., 2nd c.BC), etc.]]; see infr. IV. 1: metaphorically, ὁ. τι ἔς τι limit one thing according to another, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 3.82.]]

__II.2
trace out as a boundary, πόρον (of [Refs 4th c.BC+ [10 tracing out the Bosporus), 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Supplices” 546 (Lyric poetry).]]

__III
ordain, determine, lay down, αἶσα τόνδε σοὐρίζει (i.e. σοι ὁρίζει) μόρον [Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. author] “Ch.” 927 (σοι πορίζει M 1, σ᾽ ὁ. M 2); ἡμῖν ὥρισεν σωτηρίαν 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Iphigenia Taurica” 979; ἐς τήνδε παῖδα ψῆφον ὥρισαν φόνου [prev. author] “Hec.” 259; ἡ Δίκη.. ἐν ἀνθρώποισιν ὥρισεν νόμους 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Antigone” 452; [τὸν χρόνον] ὁ νόμος ὁ. 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Leges” 864e; ἀριθμὸς ὁ ὁρίζων τὸ πολὺ καὶ τὸ ὀλίγον 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 7.7.36; τὸ δοῦλον γένος πρὸς τὴν ἐλάσσω μοῖραν ὥρισεν θεός 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Fragmenta” 218; ὁρίσατέ μοι μέχρι πόσων ἐτῶν δεῖ νομίζειν νέους 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Memorabilia” 1.2.35]]: with infinitive, ἄνακτες ὥρισαν.. θανεῖν ἐμὴν δέσποιναν οὐ ψήφῳ μιᾷ [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Ion” 1222, compare 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Fragmenta” 24]]; ὁ. τινὰ θεόν determine one to be a god, deify, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [Anthologia Graeca 12.158.7 (1st c.BC: Meleager Epigrammaticus); ὁ. θάνατον εἶναι τὴν ζημίαν 4th c.BC: Lycurgus Orator 65, compare 4th-3rd c.BC: Dinarchus Orator 1.61 (_middle_)]]; θάνατον ὡρικέναι τὴν ζημίαν [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 26.24]]:—passive, ὧραι ἑκάστοις εἰσὶν ὡρισμέναι [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Historia Animalium” 542a19, etc.]]; ἐπί τισι ὡρισμένοις on certain definite terms (compare ῥητός), [Refs [[prev. author] “Pol.” 1285b22]]; ἀρχαὶ ἀριθμῷ ὡρισμέναι limited, definite, opposed to ἄπειροι, [Refs [[prev. author] “Metaphorical” 1002b18; τόποι ὡ. [prev. author] “Cael.” 273 a14; τὸ ὡρισμένον [prev. author] “Mete.” 369b29.]]

__III.2
define a thing, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Charmides” 171a (_passive_), 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Memorabilia” 4.6.4, +others: more frequently in]]middle than active,[Refs [see infr. IV.  3.]]

__IV

define a thing, τὴν ἡδονὴν ἀγαθὸν ὁ. [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 505c, compare “Sph.” 246b; ὁ. τὰς ἀρετὰς ἀπαθείας τινάς 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Ethica Nicomachea” 1104b24, +others; ἡδονῇ τε καὶ ἀγαθῷ ὁ. τὸ καλόν 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Gorgias” 475a; τὸ ζῆν ὁ. δυνάμει αἰσθήσεως 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Ethica Nicomachea” 1170a16, +others]]: with accusative et infinitive, ὁ. δικαίους εἶναι τοὺς εἰδότας κτλ. [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 2.378, etc.; ὅ. ἀπώμνυ [prev. work] 377, compare 10.381; ἐπὶ δ᾽ ὅρκον ὀμεῖται 8th-7th c.BC: Hesiodus Epicus “Opera et Dies” 194; κατομόσαι 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Iphigenia Taurica” 790]]; ὅ. ἐπιορκῆσαι take a false oath, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aeschines Orator 1.115, etc.]]; ὅρκου προστεθέντος when an oath is added, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Fragmenta” 472, compare “El.” 47]]; δαίμονι τῷ Πλεισθενιδῶν ὅρκους θεμένη having made a sworn compact with.., [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Agamemnon” 1570 (_anapaest meter_); ὅ. ἀλλήλοις ποιοῦνται οἱ μὲν ἔφοροι ὑπὲρ τῆς πόλεως, βασιλεὺς δ᾽ ὑπὲρ ἑαυτοῦ 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Respublica Lacedaemoniorum” 15.7; ὅρκους συνῆψαν 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Phoenissae” 1241, etc.]]; of the person demanding the oath, ὅ. ἑλέσθαι τινός or τινί take it of him, i.e. make him swear, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 4.746, 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 22.119]]; ὅρκους ἐπελάσαι and προσάγειν τινί lay oath upon a man, put him on his oath, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.146, 6.62, 74]]; τὸν ὅ... ἐπάγειν.. ὁρμάω,
future -ήσω[Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Leges” 875b]]: aorist ὥρμησα [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 6.338, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Ion” 534c]]; Laconian dialect imperative ὅρμᾱον, i.e. ὅρμαὁν, ={ὅρμησον}, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Lysistrata” 1247]]: perfect ὥρμηκα [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Politicus” 265a]]:—middle and passive, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “N.” 1.5, 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Prometheus Vinctus” 339, 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.17, etc.]]: Epic dialect imperfect ὡρμᾶτο [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 3.142]]: future ὁρμήσομαι [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 5.34, 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 7.1.9, ὁρμηθήσομαι 2nd c.AD: Galenus Medicus 5.85]]: aorist ὡρμησάμην [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 21.595, variant in 8th-7th c.BC: Hesiodus Epicus “Scutum Herculis” 127]] (ἐφ-), never in Prose, except ἐξ- [Refs 8th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Historia Graeca (Hellenica)” 6.5.20 codices: more frequently in _passive_ form ὡρμήθην 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 5.12, +others, 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 3.98, etc.]]: perfect ὥρμημαι [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Electra” 70, 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Electra” 340, 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 6.33, etc.: _Ionic dialect_ _3rd.pers._ _plural_]]perfect and pluperfect ὁρμέαται and -έατο (with variants ὡρμ-) [Refs 8th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 5.121, 8.35; in 8th c.BC: Homerus Epicus]] codices usually have the augment, but [Refs 8th c.BC+ [3rd-2nd c.BC: Aristarchus Grammaticus read ὁρμήθησαν in 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 10.359]]: (ὁρμή):

__A
active,

__I
causal, set in motion, urge on, cheer on, τινὰ εἰς πόλεμον [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 6.338, 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 1.127; τινὰ ποτὶ κλέος 5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “O.” 10(11).21; τὸ στράτευμα ὁ. ἐπὶ τὰς Ἀθήνας 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 8.106, compare 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Ajax” 174 (Lyric poetry), 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Orestes” 352 (_anapaest meter_); ἡ φύσις ὁρμήσει τινὰ ἐπὶ πλεονεξίαν 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Leges” 875b, compare “Ion” 534c; [τὰ] ὁρμῶντα [σώματα] 5th c.BC: Hippocrates Medicus “ἐπιδημίαι” 6.8.7; μέριμναν ὁρμήσασ᾽ ἐπ᾽ ἔργον 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Phoenissae” 1064 (Lyric poetry)]]; ὁ. τινὰ ἐκ χερός tear from one's arms, [Refs [[prev. author] “Hec.” 143 (_anapaest meter_):]] —passive, ὁρμηθεὶς θεοῦ ἄρχετο inspired by the god he began, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 8.499; πρὸς θεῶν ὡρμημένος 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Electra” 70; ὑπὸ ἔρωτος 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Symposium” 181d]]; ἵπποι.. ὁρμηθέντες ὑπὸ πληγῇσιν ἱμάσθλης urged on by.., [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 13.82.]]

__I.2
with a thing as the object, stir up, πόλεμον [Refs [18.376]]: with accusative et infinitive, τὰς διόδους τῶν πτερῶν.. ὥρμησε πτεροφυεῖν [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Phaedrus” 255d]]:—passive, ὡρμάθη πλαγά was sped, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Electra” 196 (Lyric poetry).]]

__II
more frequently intransitive, start,

__II.1
with infinitive, ἴρηξ ὃς ὁρμήσῃ διώκειν ὄρνεον ἄλλο starts in chase of.., [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 13.64]]; ὁσσάκι δ᾽ ὁρμήσειε πυλάων.. ἀντίον ἀΐξασθαι whenever he started to rush for the gates,[Refs [22.194; ὁσσάκι δ᾽ ὁρμήσειε.. στῆναι ἐναντίβιον 21.265]]; ἐξελαύνειν ὁρμῆσαι τὸν στρατόν began to lead out.., [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.76, compare 7.150; νίκην ὁρμῶντ᾽ ἀλαλάξαι]]eager to.., [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Antigone” 133 (Lyric poetry); ὥρμα ἀντιλαμβάνεσθαι τοῦ λόγου 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 336b.]]

__II.2
with genitive, rush headlong at one, Τρώων [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 4.335: more frequently with Preps., ὁ. ἐπί τινα 8th-7th c.BC: Hesiodus Epicus “Scutum Herculis” 403, 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.1, etc.; πύργωμα Καδμείων ἔπι 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Supplices” 1220; εἴς τινας 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 7.1.17; καθ᾽ αὑτούς [prev. author] “An.” 5.7.25]]; also ὁ. ἐς μάχην hasten to battle, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Persae” 394; εἰς ἀγῶνα 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Phoenissae” 259 (Lyric poetry); εἰς τὸ διώκειν 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 1.8.25; ἐπὶ ἁρπαγάς 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 391d; ἐπὶ τοὺς Ἀθηναίους 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 7.34]]; ὥρμασε (Doric dialect) ἐπὶ τὰ βασίλεια τῶν Σκυθᾶν [Refs 2nd c.BC+ [“SIG” 709.19 (Chersonesus, 2nd c.BC)]]: without any sense of hostility, rush, τᾶσδ᾽ ἀπὸ πέτρας πηδήσασα πυρὸς ἔσω [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Supplices” 1015 (Lyric poetry); ἐς πατρὸς δόμους [prev. author] “Med.” 1178]]; set out, ἀπὸ [τῆς Οἰνόης] [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 2.19; ἐς φυγήν 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 7.179, etc.; εἰς τὸ ἐπ᾽ ἐκεῖνα τῆς γῆς 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Phaedo” 112b; ἐπ᾽ ἄλλον λόγον 5th c.BC: Antipho Orator 3.4.5; ἐπὶ τὸ σκοπεῖν 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Memorabilia” 3.7.9]]; ἐπὶ τραγῳδίαν ὥρμηκε has turned to tragedy, [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd c.AD: Alexander Rhetor 135.14]]; δηλώσεις.. τὴν φύσιν ἐπὶ τί μάλισθ᾽ ὥρμηκε, i. e. what your natural bent is,[Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. work] 8; φυσικῶς ἐπὶ τὴν ὀργὴν ὁρμᾶν 1st c.BC: Philodemus Gadarensis Epigrammaticus “Ir.” 93 W.; πρὸς τὰς πράξεις [prev. author] “Mus.” p.71 K.; ἐπὶ φιλοσοφίαν [prev. author] “Acad.Ind.” p.64 M.; πρὸς τὰς ὀχείας 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Historia Animalium” 546a15: with _accusative_ _cognate_, ὁδόν 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 3.1.8; στρατείαν [prev. author] “Cyr.” 8.6.20.]]

__II.3
absolutely, start, begin, ὥσπερ ὡρμήσαμεν, ἴωμεν [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Protagoras” 314b, compare “R.” 425c]]; αἱ μάλιστα ὁρμήσασαι [νῆες] the ships that were hottest in pursuit, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 8.34.]]

__B
middle and passive, like the intransitive active, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus II:]]

__B.1
with infinitive, μὴ φεύγειν ὁρμήσωνται that they put not themselves in motion, set not themselves to flee, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 8.511; so διώκειν ὁρμήθησαν 10.359, compare 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 4.282]]; ὡρμήθη κόρυθα κρατὸς ἀφαρπάξαι he rushed to snatch.., [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 13.188, compare 182]]; ἦτορ ὡρμᾶτο πτολεμίζειν ἠδὲ μάχεσθαι was eager to.., [Refs [21.572]]; μᾶλλον ὅρμητο στρατεύεσθαι was eager to march, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 7.1, compare 19, +others, 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 3.45]]; ὅδε ὁ λόγος ὅρμηται λέγεσθαι this account has begun to be given, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 4.16, compare 6.86.δ᾽ (λέγεσθαι is restored for λέγεται in 3.56)]]; but λόγον, τὸν ὅρμητο λέγειν which he purposed to make, [Refs [[prev. author] 5.50.]]

__B.2
the object for or after which one goes is sometimes in genitive, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 14.488, 21.595]]: a case with a preposition, ὡρμήθησαν ἐπ᾽ ἀνδράσιν [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 10.214; ἐπί τινα 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Ajax” 47, etc.; εἴς τινα 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 7.1.9]]; μετά τινα after one, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 17.605; so ὁ. ἐπὶ τὸ ἱρόν 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 8.35; ἐς πύλας 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Septem contra Thebas” 31; πρὸς δόμους 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Hippolytus” 1152; ἐπ᾽ ἀλήθειαν 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Sophista” 228c; ἐς φυγήν 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 4.14; πρὸς τίσιν 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Coloneus” 1328; πρὸς τὸ κρατεῖν 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 581a; [ἡ ποίησις] πρὸς ἡδονὴν ὥρμηται [prev. author] “Grg.” 502c]]; οἱ περὶ λόγον ἢ παιδείαν ὁρμώμενοι persons keen about.., [Refs 5th c.BC+ [2nd c.AD: Vettius Valens Astrologus 199.5: rarely with _accusative_ loci, νερτέρας πλάκας 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Coloneus” 1576 (Lyric poetry).]]

__B.2.b
the starting-point is expressed by ἐκ, ὡρμᾶτ᾽ ἐκ θαλάμοιο [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 3.142, compare 9.178]], etc.; or ἀπό, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Trachiniae” 156, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Phaedo” 101d, etc.; ἀπὸ φιλοσοφίας 1st c.BC: Philodemus Gadarensis Epigrammaticus “Rh.” 1.357 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus]]; or by a form in -θεν, σέθεν.. ὕμνος ὁρμᾶται θέμεν αἶνον [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “N.” 1.5: in historical Prose, ὁρμᾶσθαι ἐκ..]] start from, begin from, especially of the place where one carries on any regular operations, ἐνθεῦτεν ὁρμώμενοι living there and going out from thence to do their daily work, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.17]]; of fishers, ἐκ πλοίων ὁρμώμενοι [Refs [[prev. author] 3.98]]; of a general, making that place his head-quarters or base of operations, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. author] 8.133, compare 5.125, +others, 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 1.64, 2.69, +others]]; ἀπ᾽ ἐλασσόνων ὁρμώμενος setting out, beginning with smaller means, [Refs [[prev. work] 65, compare 1.144]]; of rivers, ἐκ τῆς Ἴδης ὁ. rising.., [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Leges” 682b.]]

__B.3
absolutely, rush, dart, attack, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 5.12, 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 12.126, +others, 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Coloneus” 1068 (Lyric poetry)]]; also with ἔγχεϊ, ξιφέεσσι, etc., added, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 5.855, 17.530, 13.496, +others]]

__B.3.b
generally, hasten, be eager, ὁρμώμενον δὲ μηδαμῶς μ᾽ ἀντισπάσῃς [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Prometheus Vinctus” 339, compare 395; ἀλλ᾽ ἥδε.. ὁρμᾶται]]comes forth, [Refs [[prev. author] “Pers.” 151 (_anapaest meter_); τὸ φέγγος ὁρμάσθω πυρός [prev. author] “Eu.” 1029]]; ὕβρις ἀτάρβητα ὁρμᾶται insolence goes fearless forth, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Ajax” 197 (Lyric poetry).]]

LSJ / STEPBible (TFLSJ)
ὁρμ-ή, ἡ,
rapid motion forwards, onrush, onset, assault, μόγις δέ μευ ἔκφυγεν ὁρμήν [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 9.355]]; ἐκ τοῦ αὐτοῦ χωρίου ἡ ὁ. ἔσται the attack, invasion, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.11; ἡ ἐπὶ βασιλέα ὁ. 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 3.1.10]]; also of an impulse received from another, ἐμέ τ᾽ εἰσορόων καὶ ἐμὴν ποτιδέγμενος ὁ. [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 10.123, compare 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 2.403.]]

__2
more frequently of things, πυρὸς ὁ. the rage of fire, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 11.157]]; ὑπὸ κύματος ὁρμῆς by the shock of a wave, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 5.320; ἔγχεος ὁ. 8th-7th c.BC: Hesiodus Epicus “Scutum Herculis” 365]]; but ἐς ὁρμὴν ἔγχεος ἐλθεῖν within my spear's cast, within reach of my spear, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 5.118]]; ὁ. γονάτων spring of knee, i.e. power to spring or leap, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “N.” 5.20]]; ποδὸς ὁ. speed of foot, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Electra” 112 (Lyric poetry)]]: plural, of the tides, [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd c.AD: Ptolemaeus Mathematicus “Tetrabiblos” 3.]]

__II
impulse to do a thing, effort, μίνυνθα δέ οἱ γένεθ᾽ ὁρμή [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 4.466; μελέη δέ μοι ἔσσεται ὁ. 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 5.416; φιλότητος.. ἄμβροτος ὁ. 5th c.BC: Empedocles Poeta Philosophus 35.13; πίστιος ὁ. [prev. author] 114.3; ἐπεὶ δὲ δαιμονίη τις γίνεται ὁ. 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 7.18; μαινομένᾳ σὺν ὁρμᾷ 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Antigone” 135 (Lyric poetry), compare “Tr.” 720]]; τίς προσήγαγε χρεί; τίς ὁ.; [Refs [[prev. author] “Ph.” 237]]; οὕτω καθ᾽ ὁρμὴν δρῶσιν, i. e. with so much zeal,[Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. work] 566; εἰ.. ἄγοι αὐτὸν ὁ. θειοτέρα 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Phaedrus” 279a: joined with ἐπιθυμία, [prev. author] “Phlb.” 35d, 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 3.36]]; μιᾷ ὁ. with one impulse, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 3.2.9; ἀπὸ μιᾶς ὁ. 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 7.71; ὑπὸ μιᾷ τῇ ὁ. 2nd c.AD: Lucianus Sophista “Hist.Conscr.” 2]]: with genitive objecti, eager desire of or for a thing, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 7.43, etc.]]: so with a preposition, ἡ ὁρμή, ἣν ὁρμᾷς ἐπὶ τοὺς λόγους [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Parmenides” 135d, compare 130b; ἔχειν ὁρμὴν πρός τι 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Magna Moralia” 1185a31, +others]]; ὁ. ἐπέπεσέ τισι, with infinitive, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 4.4]]; ὁ. παραστῆσαί τισι εἴς τι or with infinitive, [Refs 2nd c.BC+ [2nd c.BC: Polybius Historicus 2.48.5, 1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus “Coriolanus” 33]]; ὁ. σχεῖν, with infinitive, [Refs [[prev. author] “Publ.” 19.]]

__II.2
in Stoic philosophy, appetition, including reasoned choice and irrational impulse, [Refs [“Stoicorum Veterum Fragmenta” 3.40, +others]]

__II.3
[Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Pythagoras Philosophus name for 2, Anatolius cited in “Theologumena Arithmeticae” 8.]]

__III
setting oneself in motion, start on a march, etc., ἐν ὁρμῇ εἶναι to be on the point of starting, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 2.1.3, compare 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Rhetorica” 1393a3]]; ἐπὶ παντὸς ὁρμῇ.. πράγματος at the start of every undertaking, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Timaeus” 27c]]; ἡ ὁ. [τούτων τῶν ἀνέμων] the point at which these winds start, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Meteorologica” 364b5, compare 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 511b (_plural_)]]. (Cf. Sanskrit s´rati 'flow'.)

LSJ / STEPBible (TFLSJ)
ὄρνις, ὁ,
also ἡ [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 9.323, 14.290, +others, frequently in _Attic dialect_, compare 111]]; genitive ὄρνῑθο; accusative singular ὄρνῑθα and ὄρνιν, neither in [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Homerus Epicus: _plural_, _nominative_ and _accusative_ ὄρνῑθες, -θας, but in _accusative_ also ὄρνεις or ὄρνῑς (5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Tyrannus” 966, 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Hippolytus” 1059, 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Aves” 717, 1250, 1610, 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 19.245, etc.)]]:—also ὄρνιξ, [NT+3rd c.BC+ [“PCair.Zen.” 375.1 (3rd c.BC), variant in NT.Luke.13.34]], called Ionic dialect and Doric dialect by [Refs 7th c.BC+ [9th c.AD: Photius Legal icographus, etc. (but ὄρνις _nominative_ in 7th c.BC: Alcman Lyricus 26.4)]]; accusative ὄρνῑχα [Refs 7th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “O.” 2.88; _genitive_ ὄρνῑχος [prev. author] “I.” 6(5).53: _nominative_ _plural_ ὄρνῑχες 5th c.BC: Bacchylides Lyricus 5.22, 3rd c.BC: Theocritus Poeta Bucolicus 7.47; _genitive_ _plural_ ὀρνίχων 7th c.BC: Alcman Lyricus 67, “Abh.Berl.Akad.” 1925(5).33 (Cyrene, 4th c.BC)]]; dative ὄρνιξι, ὀρνίχεσσι, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “P.” 5.112, 4.190 (ὄρνιξι also in “PLond.” 1.131r. 125, +others (1st c.AD))]]: on the gender and declension, see [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd c.AD: Athenaeus Epigrammaticus 9.373f (Cf. ὄρν-εον,]] Gothic ara, genitive arins 'eagle', etc.) [In the trisyllable cases ῑ always: [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Homerus Epicus has ὄρνῑς in 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 9.323, 12.218, but ὄρνῐς [prev. work] 24.219]]; and later Epic dialect use both ὄρνῑς and ὄρνῐς: in Trag. both quantities are found, ὄρνῐς in [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Fragmenta - American Journal of Philology” 304.3 (-ῐν), 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Antigone” 1021, “El.” 149 (Lyric poetry), “fragment” 654, 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Hercules Furens” 72, and so 4th-3rd c.BC: Philemo Comicus 79.10; but ὄρνῑς 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Bacchae” 1365, and always in 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus (“Av.” 103, +others), for inib. 168, the words τίς ὄρνῐς οὗτος]]; are borrowed from Sophocles; ὄρνῑς is said to be Attic dialect, [Refs [“Etymologicum Magnum” 632.8.]]]

__I
bird, including birds of prey and domestic fowls, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Homerus Epicus, etc.]]; applied to ostriches, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 1.2.7]]: frequently added to the specific names, ὄρνισιν ἐοικότες αἰγυπιοῖσιν [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 7.59; λάρῳ ὄρνιθι ἐοικώς 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 5.51]]; ὄ. ἀηδών, πέρδιξ, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Ajax” 629, “fragment” 323]]; ὄ. ἁλκυών, ὄ. κύκνος, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Iphigenia Taurica” 1089 (Lyric poetry), “Hel.” 19.]]

__II
like{οἰωνός}, bird of omen, from the flight or cries of which the augur divined, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th-7th c.BC: Hesiodus Epicus “Opera et Dies” 828]]; δεξιός, ἀριστερὸς ὄρνις, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 13.821, 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 20.242, +others; χρηστηρίους ὄρνιθας 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Septem contra Thebas” 26, compare “Ag.” 112, 157 (both Lyric poetry); ὄ. αἴσιος 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Tyrannus” 52, compare 1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus “Fabius Maximus” 19, 2nd c.AD: Galenus Medicus 12.314; ὀρνίθων οἰωνίσματα 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Phoenissae” 839.]]

__II.2
metaphorically, omen taken from the flight or cries of birds, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 10.277, +others]]: generally, omen, presage, without direct reference to birds,[Refs 5th c.BC+ [24.219, 5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “P.” 4.19; ὄρνιθα δ᾽ οὐ ποιῶ σε τῆς ἐμῆς ὁδοῦ 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Fragmenta - American Journal of Philology” 95, compare 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Iphigenia Aulidensis” 988, 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Plutus” 63, “Av.” 719 ff.]]; see at {ὅδιος}.

__III
in Attic dialect ὄρνις, ὁ, is mostly, cock, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Electra” 18; κοκκυβόας ὄ. [prev. author] “fragment” 791, compare 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Vespae” 815]]; ὄρνις, ἡ, hen, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-3rd c.BC: Menander Comicus 167, 168, “PCair.Zen.” 266 (3rd c.BC, _plural_)]]; ἀλέκτορα καὶ ὄρνιθα τελέαν cock and hen, [Refs [“TAM” 2(1).245.8 (from Lycia)]]; in full, ὄ. ἐνοίκιος [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Eumenides” 866; θήλεια ὄ. 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Fragmenta” 477]]; πότερον ὄ. ἢ ταὧ; [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Aves” 102 (with play on this signification and signf. I)]]; ὁ ὄρνιξ ὁ σιτευτός fatted fowl, [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [3rd c.BC: Zenon Papyri du Caire 375.1; ὀρνίθων φοινικολόφων 3rd c.BC: Theocritus Poeta Bucolicus 22.72, compare 24.64, 2nd c.BC: Moschus Bucolicus 3.49; ὄ. οἰκίης 2nd c.AD: Babrius Fabularum Scriptor 17.1]]; also, goose, [Refs [[prev. author] 123.1.]]

__IV
in plural sometimes, bird-market, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 19.245; compare ὄρνεον 11.]]

__V
Μοισᾶν ὄρνιχες song-birds, i.e. poets, [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [3rd c.BC: Theocritus Poeta Bucolicus 7.47.]]

__VI
Provs.: διώκει παῖς ποτανὸν ὄρνιν [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Agamemnon” 394 (Lyric poetry); ὄ. ὥς τις ἐκ χερῶν ἄφαντος 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Hippolytus” 828]]; ὀρνίθων γάλα 'pigeon's milk', i.e. any marvellous dainty or good fortune, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Vespae” 508, “Av.” 1673, 4th c.BC: Mnesimachus Comicus 9, 4th-3rd c.BC: Menander Comicus 936; but ὄρνιθος γάλα]]white of egg, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Anaxagoras Philosophus 22]]; also a plant, see at {ὀρνιθόγαλον}.

__VII
a constellation, later Cygnus, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Eudoxus Astronomus cited in 2nd c.BC: Hipparchus Astronomicus 1.2.16, 4th-3rd c.BC: Aratus Epicus 275, 2nd c.AD: Ptolemaeus Mathematicus “Tetrabiblos” 26.]]

deep_entry:
Abbott-Smith / STEPBible (TBESG)
ὄρος, -ους, τό
[in LXX chiefly, and very freq., for הַר ;]
a mountain: Mat.4:8 17:1, Mrk.9:2, Jhn.4:20, 2Pe.1:18, al.; opposite to βουνός, Luk.3:5 (LXX); ὄ. τ. ἐλαιῶν, Mat.21:1 24:3, al. (see: ἐ.); ὄ. Σιών (Σ., prob. in gem appos.), Heb.12:22, Rev.14:1; ὄ. Σινά, Act.7:30, 38 Gal.4:24-25; τὸ ὄ., of the hill district as distinct from the lowlands, esp. the hills above the Sea of Galilee, Mat.5:1 8:1, Mrk.3:13 6:46, al.; τὰ ὄ., Mat.18:12, Mrk.5:5, Heb.11:38, Rev.6:14, al.; proverbially (cf. Rabbinic, הדים עקר), of overcoming difficulties, accomplishing marvels, ὄρη μεθιστάνειν, 1Co.13:2, cf. Mat.17:20 21:21, Mrk.11:23
(AS)

---

LSJ / STEPBible (TFLSJ)
ὄρος, εος, τό:
genitive plural ὀρέων (the form proper to Ionic dialect and other dialects) is required by the metre in [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Bacchae” 719 (iambic) and frequently in Lyric poetry verse, as 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Tyrannus” 1106]], and is alone used in [LXX+2nd c.BC+ [LXX, LXX.Gen.8.5, +others, compare “IG” 7.2225.18 (2nd c.BC), NT.Rev.6.15]]; but ὀρῶν (the Attic dialect form) is required in [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Prometheus Vinctus” 719, 811, “fragment” 342, 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Bacchae” 791, and occurs in 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 3.24, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Critias” 111c, “SIG” 888.120 (Scaptopara, 3rd c.AD), etc.: the _Epic dialect_ and Lyric poetry forms οὔρεος, οὔρεϊ, οὔρεα, οὔρεσι probably have οὐρ- for the sake of meter for ὀρ- (so ὤρεα, ὤρεος]] for the sake of meter| in Doric dialect, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [3rd c.BC: Theocritus Poeta Bucolicus 1.77, 115, 4.35, “Hymnus ad Isim” 162): the _Ionic dialect_ form is ὀρ-, 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 9.21, +others, 6th c.BC: Anacreon Lyricus 2.5]], see at {ὄρειος} (οὔρεσιν is an Epicism in [Refs 7th c.BC+ [7th-6th c.BC(?): Semonides Iambographus 14.1, compare οὔρη]] at end of a hexameter, [Refs [“IG” 12(8).445.6 (from Thasos))]]; ὄρος is found in codices of [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.43, 2.8, 12, 7.176]] and should perhaps be restored elsewhere:—mountain, hill, ὄρεος κορυφῇσι [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 3.10, +others; οὔρεος ἐν βήσσῃσιν 11.87; ἐν ὄρεσσι 1.235, +others; ἐν οὔρεσιν 24.614, +others; τρέμε δ᾽ οὔρεα μακρά 13.18, etc.; Γαῖα.. γείνατο δ᾽ Οὔρεα μακρά, θεῶν χαρίεντας ἐναύλους 8th-7th c.BC: Hesiodus Epicus “Theogonia” 129.]]

__2
canton, parish, ὄ. Ἀργειατᾶν, ὄ. Ὀγχνιάἱον, etc., [Refs 4th c.BC+ [“Mnemos.” 42.332 (Argos, 4th c.BC).]]

__3
in Egypt, desert, [Refs 1st c.AD+ [PTeb. 383.61 (1st c.AD)]]; as place of burial, [Refs 1st c.AD+ [“POxy.” 274.27 (1st c.AD), “PRyl.” 153.5 (2nd c.AD), “PGrenf.” 2.77.22 (3rd-4th c.AD).]]

__4
part of the foot, ={τὸ ἄνω πρὸ τῶν δακτύλων}, [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd c.AD(?): Pollianus Epigrammaticus 2.197.]]

__5
={ἀμίς}, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [Scholia 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Acharnenses” 82.]]

to dig: with accusative, ληνόν, Mat.21:33; ὁπολήνιον, Mrk.12:1; γῆν, Mat.25:18 (cf. δι-, ἐξ-ορύσσω).†

LSJ / STEPBible (TFLSJ)
ὀρύσσω,
[Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 10.305]], Attic dialect ὀρύττω (late present imperative ὄρυγε [Refs [“IG” 12(5).519 (from Seriphos))]]: future ὀρύξω [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 7.341:]]aorist ὤρυξα, Epic dialect ὄρυξα as always in [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Homerus Epicus, 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 11.25, +others:]]perfect ὀρώρῠχα (κατ-) [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Pherecrates Comicus 145.19]]: pluperfect ὠρωρύχειν [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd c.AD: Appianus Historicus “Bella Civilia” 4.107]]:—middle, aorist ὠρυξάμην [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.186, 3rd c.BC: Apollonius Rhodius Epicus 3.1032, etc.:]] —passive, future ὀρυχθήσομαι (κατ-) [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Antipho Orator 3.2.10, also ὀρῠχήσομαι (κατ-) 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Aves” 394 (Elmsl.) and ὀρωρύξομαι 10th c.AD: Suidas Legal icographus see at {ὤρυσσον} (probably)]]: aorist ὠρύχθην [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.186, etc.]]: perfect ὀρώρυγμαι [Refs [[prev. author] 2.158, etc.]]; in compounds, ὤρυγμαι (κατ- [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Antipho Orator 3.3.12 codices, ὑποκατ- 5th c.BC: Sophron Comicus 3, δι- 2nd c.AD: Lucianus Sophista “Tim.” 53, etc.)]]: pluperfect ὀρωρύγμην [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.186, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Critias” 118c, also ὠρωρύγμην (δι-) 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 7.8.14.]] —An aorist 2 active ὤρῠγον occurs in [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd-3rd c.AD: Philostratus Sophista “Vita Apollonii” 1.25]]: passive ὠρύγην [Refs 1st c.AD+ [“OGI” 72.7,673.6 (Egypt, 1st c.AD), (δι-) 3rd c.AD: Heliodorus Scriptor Eroticus 9.7, “Geoponica” 4.3.2]], (κατ-) falsa lectio in [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 5.8.11]]:—dig, ὀρύξομεν ἐγγύθι τάφρον [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 7.341; βόθρον ὄρυξα 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 11.25; ἔλυτρον 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.186; ὀρύγματα [prev. author] 4.200; ταῖς ὁπλαῖς εὐνάς 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Equites” 605; ὑπόνομον ἐκ τῆς πόλεως 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 2.76: _absolutely_, ὤρυσσον ὑπὸ μαστίγων 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 7.22; ἐὰν ὀρύξῃ τις παρὰ τὴν θάλασσαν 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Problemata” 933b33]]:—middle, δεξαμενὰς ὀρύξασθαι [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 3.9:]] —passive, ὀρώρυκται (i.e. ἡ διῶρυξ) [Refs [[prev. author] 2.158]]; τὸ ὀρυχθέν, ={τὸ ὄρυγμα}, the trench, [Refs [[prev. author] 1.186.]]

__II
dig up, [μῶλυ] [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 10.305; κυκλάμινον 3rd c.BC: Theocritus Poeta Bucolicus 5.123:]]middle, λίθους ὠρύξατο had stones dug or quarried, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.186:]] —passive, ὁ ὀρυσσόμενος χοῦς the soil that was dug up,[Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. work] 185; ὑπὸ μεταλλείας ὀρύττεσθαι 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Critias” 114e.]]

__III
dig through, i. e. make a canal through (like διορύσσειν), τὸν ἰσθμὸν ὀ. Oracle texts cited in [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.174; τὸ χωρίον ὀρώρυκτο [prev. author] 1.186]]; of moles, burrow, either absolutely, as [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Historia Animalium” 606a2]]; or γῆν ὀ., [Refs [[prev. author] “Mir.” 842b4.]]

__IV
bury, ἔγχος.. γαίας ὀρύξας ἔνθα μήτις ὄψεται (where γαίας depends on ἔνθα) [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Ajax” 659, compare 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Oeconomicus” 19.2.]]

__V
of a wrestler, dig into, gouge a tender part, τὠφθαλμώ [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Aves” 442, compare “Pax” 899, 2nd-3rd c.AD: Philostratus Sophista “Vita Apollonii” 8.25]]; gouge out, ὀφθαλμὸν ὤρυττέν τις ὥσπερ ἰχθύος [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Antiphanes Comicus 119.]]

[in LXX for יָתוֹם ;]

LSJ / STEPBible (TFLSJ)
ὀρφᾰνός, ή, όν,
also ός, όν [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Hecuba” 149 (_anapaest meter_)]]:— orphan, without parents, fatherless, αἱ δ᾽ ἐλίποντο ὀρφαναί [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 20.68; ὀ. τέκνα 8th-7th c.BC: Hesiodus Epicus “Opera et Dies” 330; παῖδά τ᾽ ὀ. λιπεῖν 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Ajax” 653]]: as substantive, orphan, ἐπίκληροι καὶ ὀ. [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Lysias Orator 26.12; ὀρφανοῖς καὶ ὀρφαναῖς 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Leges” 926c; ὀρφανῶν κάκωσις 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Ath.” 56.6, compare “IG” 12.6.124: also in _neuter_, εἰς ὀρφανὰ καὶ ἔρημα ὑβρίζειν 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Leges” 927c]]; of animals, ὄρνις [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Aves” 1361]]; ὀ. οἶκος, δόμος, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Fragmenta” 943, 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Alcestis” 657]]: metaphorically, neglected, ἡ δέλτος ὀρφανὴ κεῖται [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [3rd c.BC: Herodas Mimographus 3.15]]; ὀρφανὰ κεῖται σκῦλα epigram cited in [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd c.AD: Pausanias Periegeta 1.13.3.]]

__II
with genitive, bereaved or bereft of,

__II.1
of children, ὀ. πατρός reft of father, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Electra” 914, 1010; τοῦ πατρὸς ὀ. 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 57.70; γονέων 1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus 2.293d, etc.]]

__II.2
of parents, πότμον ὀρφανὸν γενεᾶς childless, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “O.” 9.61]]; ὀ. παιδός, τέκνων, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Hecuba” 149 (_anapaest meter_), “fragment” 332.6; νεοσσῶν ὀρφανὸν λέχος 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Antigone” 425.]]

__II.3
generally, ὀ. ἑτάρων [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “I.” 7(6).10, compare 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Leges” 730d; νύμφας ἔθηκεν ὀρφανὰς ξυναόρων 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Orestes” 1136; ἐπιστήμης 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus Alcaeus2.147a; κρατός Sositheus Tragicus 2.20]]; ὀρφανοὶ ὕβριος free from insolence, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “I.” 4(3).8(26); ψόφον.. Κασταλίας ὀρφανὸν ἀνδρῶν χορεύσιος [prev. author] “Pae.” 6.9]]; ὀ. μαχᾶν, ={ἀπόμαχος}, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Timotheus Lyricus “Persae” 154]]; ὀρφανὴ βίου, i.e. poor, [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [3rd c.BC: Herodas Mimographus 3.39; ὀ. ἀγκίστρου κάλαμος “Anthologia Graeca” 12.42 (3rd c.BC: Dioscorides Epigrammaticus): Comedy texts _metaphorically_, ὀ. ταρίχιον]] salt-fish without sauce, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Pherecrates Comicus 22 (uncertain reading). (A shorter form ὀρφο- appears in ὀρφο-βότης (which see), ὀρφόω,]] cf. Latin orbus, Gothic arbi 'inheritance'.)

Euph. [prev. cited] (_passive_): also with _accusative_ _cognate_, Λακωνικὰ σχημάτια ὀρχεῖσθαι]] dance Laconian steps, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. author] 6.129; ὀ. τὸ Περσικόν 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 8.4.12; ὀ. πρὸς τὸν αὐλὸν σχήματα [prev. author] “Smp.” 7.5; ὀ. τὸν ὅρμον 2nd c.AD: Lucianus Sophista “Salt.” II]] {ὀρχηδόν}, etc.:—passive, τῶν ὕμνων οἳ μὲν ὠρχοῦντο οἳ δὲ οὐκ ὠρχοῦντο [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd c.AD: Athenaeus Epigrammaticus 14.631d.]]

__2
represent by dancing or pantomime, ὀρχεῖσθαι τὴν τοῦ Κρόνου τεκνοφαγίαν, ὀ. τὸν Αἴαντα, [Refs 1st c.AD+ [2nd c.AD: Lucianus Sophista “Salt.” 80, 83, compare “Anthologia Graeca” 9.248 (1st c.AD: Boethus Epigrammaticus), 11.254 (1st c.AD: Lucillius Epigrammaticus).]]

__II
metaphorically, leap, bound, ὀρχεῖται δὲ καρδία φόβῳ [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Choephori” 166, compare 4th c.BC: Anaxandrides Comicus 59]]; Θεσσαλίη ὠρχήσατο Thessaly shook, trembled, [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [3rd c.BC: Callimachus Epicus “Hymnus in Delum” 139.]]

__III
active ὀρχέω, make to dance (see. [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Cratylus” 407a)]], is used by Ion Trag.[Refs [50, ἐκ τῶν ἀέλπτων μᾶλλον ὤρχησεν φρένας]] made my heart leap (so codices [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd c.AD: Athenaeus Epigrammaticus, ὤρχησαι Nauck)]]; but ὀρκῆσι in [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Thesmophoriazusae” 1179 is a barbarism for ὀρχῆται.]]

Abbott-Smith / STEPBible (TBESG)
ὅς, ἥ, ὅ,
the postpositive article (ἄρθρον ὑποτακτικόν).
__I. As demonstr. pron. = οὗτος, ὅδε, this, that, also for αὐτός, chiefly in nom.: ὅς δέ, but he (cf. ἦ δὲ ὅς, frequently in Plat.), Mrk.15:23, Jhn.5:11; ὃς μὲν . . . ὃς δέ, the one . . . the other, Mat.21:35, 22:5, 25:15, Luk.23:33, Act.27:14, Rom.14:5, 1Co.11:21, 2Co.2:18, Ju 22; neut., ὃ μὲν . . . ὃ δέ, the one . . . the other, some . . . some, Mat.13:8, 23, Rom.9:21; ὃς (ὃ) μὲν . . . (ἄλλος (ἄλλο)) . . . ἕτερος, Mrk.4:4, Luk.8:5, 1Co.12:8-10; οὓς μέν, absol., 1Co.12:28; ὃς μὲν . . . ὁ δέ, Rom.14:2.
__II. As relat. pron., who, which, what, that;
__1. agreeing in gender with its antecedent, but differently governed as to case: Mat.2:9, Luk.9:9, Act.20:18, Rom.2:29, al. mult.
__2. In variation from the common construction;
__(a) in gender, agreeing with a noun in apposition to the antecedent: Mrk.15:16, Gal.3:16, Eph.6:17, al.; constr. ad sensum: Jhn.6:9, Col.2:19, 1Ti.3:16, Rev.13:14, al.;
__(b) in number, constr. ad sensum: Act.15:36, 2Pe.3:1;
__(with) in case, by attraction to the case of the antecedent (Bl., §50, 2): Jhn.4:18, Act.3:21, Rom.15:18, 1Co.6:19, Eph.1:8, al.
__3. The neut. ὅ with nouns of other gender and with phrases, which thing, which term: Mrk.3:17 12:42, Jhn.1:39, Col.3:14, al.; with a sentence, Act.2:32, Gal.2:10, 1Jn.2:8, al.
__4. With ellipse of a demonstrative (οὗτος or ἐκεῖνος), before or after: before, Mat.20:23, Luk.7:43, Rom.10:14, al.; after, Mat.10:38, Mrk.9:40, Jhn.19:22, Rom.2:1 al.
__5. Expressing purpose, end or cause: Mat.11:10 (who = that he may), Mrk.1:2, Heb.12:6 al.
__6. C. prep, as periphrasis for conjc.: ἀνθ᾽ ὧν ( = ἀντὶ τούτων ὧν), because, Luk.1:20, al.; wherefore, Luk.12:3; ἐξ οὗ, since, for that, Rom.5:12; ἀφ᾽ οὗ, since (temporal), Luk.13:25; ἐξ οὗ, whence, Php.3:20; etc.
__7. With particles: ὃς ἄν (ἐάν), see: ἄν, ἐάν; ὃς καί, Mrk.3:19, Jhn.21:20, Rom.5:2, al.; ὃς καὶ αὐτός, Mat.27:57.
__8. Gen., οὗ, absol., as adv. (see: οὗ).
(AS)

LSJ / STEPBible (TFLSJ)
ὅς, ἥ, ὅ,

genitive οὗ, ἧς, οὗ, etc.; dative plural οἷς, αἷς, οἷς, etc.: Epic dialect forms, genitive ὅου (probably replacing Οο) in the phrases ὅου κλέος οὔ ποτ᾽ ὀλεῖται [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 2.325, “hymnus ad Apollinem” 156; ὅου κράτος ἐστὶ μέγιστον 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 1.70 (elsewhere οὗ 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 7.325, +others, never οἷο)]]; feminine ἕης [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 16.208 (perhaps imitation of ὅου]]; elsewhere only ἧς [Refs [5.265, +others)]]; dative plural οἷς, οἷσι, ᾗς, ᾗσι (never αἷς or αἷσι in [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Homerus Epicus):]] — _pronoun_ used,

__A
as demonstrative by the side of οὗτος, ὅδε, and the Article ὁ, ἡ, τό: in post-Homeric Gr. this use survived only in a few special phrases.

__B
as a Relat. by the side of the Article ὅ, ἥ, τό (see. ὁ, ἡ, τό, c):—this demonstrative and Relat. pronoun must not be confounded with the Possess. ὅς, ἥ, ὅν. (With Gr. Relat. ὅς, ἥ, ὅ cf. Sanskrit Relat. yas, yā, yad, Lithuanian jis, ji (he, she), Oslav. i, ja, je (he, she, it).)

__A
DEMONSTR. PRON., ={οὗτος},{ὅδε}, this, that; also, he, she, it:

__A.I
Homeric usage: this form only occurs in the nominative masculine and neuter ὅς, ὅ, and perhaps nominative feminine ἥ and nominative plural οἵ, the other cases being supplied by ὁ, ἡ, τό (ὅ, ἡ, τό); most codices have ἥ in [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 17.551, 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 24.255, +others, and this (as also οἵ) can be referred equally to either (on the accent see ὁ, ἡ, τό): with γάρ or καί, ὃς γὰρ δεύτατος ἦλθεν 1.286; ἀλλὰ καὶ ὃς δείδοικε 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 21.198; ὃ γὰρ γέρας ἐστὶ θανόντων 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 24.190, 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 23.9, compare 12.344: frequently used emphatically in apodosi, mostly with οὐδέ or μηδέ]] before it, μηδ᾽ ὅν τινα γαστέρι μήτηρ κοῦρον ἐόντα φέροι, μηδ᾽ ὃς φύγοι [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 6.59, compare 7.160, 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 4.653: after a]]participle, εἰς ἕτερον γάρ τίς τε ἰδών.., ὃς σπεύδει (for ὅστις ἂν ἴδῃ, ὃς σπεύδει) [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th-7th c.BC: Hesiodus Epicus “Opera et Dies” 22.]]

__A.II
in later Gr. this usage remained in a few forms:

__A.II.1
at the beginning of a clause, καὶ ὅς and he, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 7.18, 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Symposium” 1.15, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Phaedo” 118, “Prt.” 310d]]; καὶ ἥ and she, καὶ οἵ and they, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 8.56, 87, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Symposium” 201e, 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 7.6.4.]]

__A.II.2
ὃς καὶ ὅς such and such a person, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 4.68:]] —here also the _Article_ supplied the oblative cases.

__A.II.3
ἦ δ᾽ ὅς, ἦ δ᾽ ἥ, said he, said she, see at {ἠμί}.

__A.II.4
in oppositions, where it sometimes answers to the Article, Λέριοι κακοί· οὐχ ὁ μέν, ὃς δ᾽ οὔ.. [Refs 6th c.BC+ [6th c.BC: Phocylides Lyricus 1; ὃς μὲν.., ὃ δὲ.. 2nd c.BC: Moschus Bucolicus 3.76; ὃ μὲν.., ὃς δὲ.., ὃ δὲ.., ὃς δὲ.. 2nd c.BC: Bion Bucolicus 1.81; so τῷ μὲν.., ᾧ δὲ.., ᾧ δὲ.. “Anthologia Graeca” 6.187 (1st c.AD: Alpheus Epigrammaticus)]]; ὃ μὲν.., ὃ δὲ.., ὃ δὲ.. (neuter) [NT+4th c.BC+ [NT.Matt.13.8; ἂ μὲν.., ἃ δὲ.. 1st c.AD(?): Heraclitus 102, 4th c.BC: Archytas Tarentinus Philosophus cited in 5th c.AD: Stobaeus, Joannes 3.1.110; ὧν μὲν.., ὧν δὲ.. 4th-3rd c.BC: Philemo Comicus 99; πόλεις ἃς μὲν.., ἃς δὲ.. 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 18.71 (as see l.)]]: so in Doric dialect dative feminine as adverb, ᾇ μὲν.., ᾇ δὲ.. [Refs 4th c.BC+ [“Tab.Heracl.” 1.81; ἐφ᾽ ὧν μὲν.., ἐφ᾽ ὧν δὲ.. 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Ethica Nicomachea” 1109a1]]: very frequently in late Prose, [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd c.AD: Arrianus Historicus “Epicteti Dissertationes” 3.25.1, etc.]]: also answering to other Prons., ἑτέρων.., ὧν δὲ.. [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-3rd c.BC: Philemo Comicus 31.6; ἐφ᾽ ᾧ μὲν.., ἐπὶ θατέρῳ δὲ.. 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Historia Animalium” 564a21, etc.]]

__B
RELAT. PRON., who, which.—By the side of the simple Relat., ὅς, ἥ, ὅ (in [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Homerus Epicus also ὁ, ἡ, τό), we find in common use the _compound_ forms ὅστε, ὅστις and ὅτις, ὅσπερ and ὅπερ, ὅς γε (which see).]]

__A0
USAGE of the Relat. pronoun (the following remarks apply to ὅς γε, ὅσπερ, ὅστε, ὅστις, as well as to ὅς, and to ὁ, ἡ, τό as relative):

__A0.I
in respect of CONCOR[Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator]] —Prop. it agrees in gender and number with the Noun or _pronoun_ in the antecedent clause.—But this rule admits of many exceptions:

__A0.I.1
the Relat. mayagree with the gender implied, not expressed, in the antecedent, φίλον θάλος, ὃν τέκον αὐτή [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 22.87; τέκνων, οὓς ἤγαγε 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Supplices” 12]]: so after collective Nouns, the Relat. is frequently put in plural in the gender implied in the Noun, λαόν.., οὕς.. [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 16.369]]; στρατιάν.. τοιαύτην.., οἵ τινες.., τὸ ναυτικόν, οἵ.., [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 6.91, 3.4; πλήθει, οἵπερ.. 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Phaedrus” 260a]]; especially after the names of countries or cities, Τηλέπυλον Λαιστρυγονίην ἀφίκανεν, οἳ.. (i. e. to Telepylos of the Laestrygonians, who.. ) [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 23.319; τὰς Ἀθήνας, οἵ γε.. 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 7.8. β; Μέγαρα.., οὓς.. 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 6.94: it also may agree with the Noun or _pronoun_ implied in an]] adjective, Θηβαίας ἐπισκοποῦντ᾽ ἀγυιάς, τάν.. the streets of Thebes, which.., [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Antigone” 1137 (Lyric poetry)]]; τοὺς Ἡρακλείους παῖδας, ὃς.. the children of Heracles, who.., [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Hercules Furens” 157; τῆς ἐμῆς ἐπεισόδου, ὅν..]]of me whom.., [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Coloneus” 731]]; τὸν ἥμισύν ἐστ᾽ ἀτελὴς τοῦ χρόνου· εἶθ᾽ ἧς πᾶσι μέτεστι.., where ἧς agrees with ἀτελείας implied in ἀτελής, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 20.8.]]

__A0.I.2
when the antec. Noun in singular implies a class, the Relat. is sometimes in plural, ἦ μάλα τις θεὸς ἔνδον, οἳ.. ἔχουσιν (for τις θεῶν, οἵ..) in some places, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Orestes” 638]]; οὗ μέν.., οὗ δέ.. in some places.., in others.., [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Oeconomica” 1345b34: with _genitive_, οὐκ εἶδεν οὗ γῆς εἰσέδυ]] in what part of the earth, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Iphigenia Aulidensis” [1583]; ἐννοεῖς οὗ ἐστὶ.. τοῦ ἀναμιμνήσκεσθαι 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Meno” 84a; συνιδὼν οὗ κακῶν ἦν 2nd c.AD: Lucianus Sophista “Tox.” 17.]]

__A0.I.2
in pregnant phrases, μικρὸν προϊόντες..,οὗ ἡ μάχη ἐγένετο (for ἐκεῖσε οὗ) [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 2.1.6; so οὗπερ προσβεβοηθήκει 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 2.86, compare 1.134]]; ἀπιὼν ἐκ τῆς πόλεως, οὗ κατέφυγε (for οἷ κατέφυγε καὶ οὗ ἦν) [NT+5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 5.4.14 (uncertain reading); ἐπειδὰν ἱζήσωμεν οὗ ἄγεις 2nd-3rd c.AD: Philostratus Sophista “Her.Prooem.” 13: in later Gr. οὗ was used simply for οἷ, οὗπερ ἂν ἔλθῃ Tim069,cf. NT.Luke.10.1, etc.]]: but in early writers this is falsa lectio, as in [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 21.74, etc.]]

__A0.II
dative feminine ᾗ, Doric dialect ᾇ, of Place, where, or Manner, as, see at {ᾗ}.

__A0.III
old locative οἷ, as adverb, see at {οἷ}.

__A0.III.2
old ablative (?) ὧ, in Doric dialect (compare ϝοίκω), τηνῶθε καθεῖλον, ὧ (whence) μ᾽ ἐκέλευ καθελεῖν τυ [Refs 5th c.BC+ [3rd c.BC: Theocritus Poeta Bucolicus 3.11; ἐν τᾷ πόλι, ὧ κ᾽ ᾖ, καρῡξαι ἐν τἀγορᾷ “IG” 9(1).334.21 (_Locrian dialect_, 5th c.BC).]]

__A0.IV
accusative singular neuter ὅ, very frequently ={ὅτι}, that, how that, λεύσσετε γὰρ τό γε πάντες ὅ μοι γέρας ἔρχεται ἄλλῃ [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 1.120, +others]]; and so also, because, ταρβήσας ὅ οἱ ἄγχι πάγη βέλος [Refs [20.283, +others]]

__A0.IV.2
in Attic dialect ὅ, for which reason, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Hecuba” 13, “Ph.” 155, 263, 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Ecclesiazusae” 338: also _accusative_ _neuter_ _plural_ ἅ in this sense, 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Trachiniae” 137 (Lyric poetry), 5th-6th c.BC: Isocrates Orator 8.122.]]

__A0.IV.3
whereas, [NT+5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 2.40, 3.12, NT.Rom.6.10, NT.Gal.2.20.]]

__A0.V
ἀφ᾽ οὗπερ from the time that.., [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Persae” 177.]]

__A0.VI
ἐφ᾽ ᾧ, see at {ἐπί} [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Bacchylides Lyricus 111.3.]]

LSJ / STEPBible (TFLSJ)
ὁσάκις [ᾰ],
Epic dialect ὁσσάκι, as always in [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Homerus Epicus]]; also ὁσσάκις, [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [“Tab.Heracl.” 1.132, 3rd c.BC: Callimachus Epicus “Epigrammata” 2.2]]: (ὅσος):— as many times as, as of ten as, Relat. to τοσσάκι, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 21.265, 22.194, 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 11.585]]; Attic dialect form in [NT+5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 7.18, 5th c.BC: Lysias Orator 25.9, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Theaetetus” 143a, 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Memorabilia” 3.4.3, NT.1Cor.11.25, etc.]]:—also ὁσᾰκισδήποτε, [Refs [Dosith. p.409]] K.; ὁσᾰκισοῦν, [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd c.AD: Nicomachus Gerasenus Mathematicus “Arithmetica Introductio” 2.17.]]

deep_entry:
Abbott-Smith / STEPBible (TBESG)
ὅσιος, -ον
(so sometimes in cl., but most frequently -α, -ον), [in LXX chiefly for חָסִיד, also for טָהוֹר, יָשָׁר, תָּמִים ;]
religiously right, right­eous, pious, Holy: of men, Tit.1:8. Heb.7:26; by meton., ὁ. χεῖρας, 1Ti.2:8 (cf. Deu.32:4); of God, Rev.15:4 16:5; as subst., ὁ ὅ., of the Messiah, Act.2:27 13:35" (LXX) ; τὰ ὅ. Δανεὶδ τ. πιστά (Field, Notes, 121), Act.13:34 (LXX).†
SYN.: see: ἅγιος (cf. also DB, ii, 399.b; iv, 352.b, and ref. see word -ίως)  (AS)

---

LSJ / STEPBible (TFLSJ)
ὅσι-ος, α, ον,
also ος, ον [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Leges” 831d, 1st c.BC: Dionysius Halicarnassensis 5.71]]:— hallowed, i. e. sanctioned or allowed by the law of God or of nature, δίκη [Refs 6th c.BC+ [6th c.BC: Theognis Elegiacus 132; θοῖναι 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Prometheus Vinctus” 529 (Lyric poetry); λουτρά 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Ajax” 1405 (_anapaest meter_); καθαρμοί 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Bacchae” 77 (Lyric poetry); μέλος 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Aves” 898]]; οὐχ ὅ. unhallowed, ὕβρις [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Bacchae” 374 (Lyric poetry); ἔρως [prev. author] “Hipp.” 764 (Lyric poetry); θυσίαι [prev. author] “IT” 465 (_anapaest meter_).]] —The sense of ὅσιος often depends on its relation on the one hand to δίκαιος (sanctioned by human law), on the other to ἱερός (sacred to the gods):

__1

ὀσμ-ή, ἡ,
Attic dialect form of the older ὀδμή (see. near the end), smell, odour, frequently of foul smells, δεινὴ δὲ θεείου γίγνεται ὀδμή [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 14.415]]; πικρὸν ἀποπνείουσαι ἁλὸς.. ὀδμήν, of seals, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 4.406; ὀδμὰ.. κατὰ χῶρον κίδναται 5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “Fragmenta.” 129.6; ὀσμὴ βροτείων αἱμάτων 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Eumenides” 253]]; ὀσμὴν ἀπ᾽ αὐτοῦ (i.e. τοῦ νεκροῦ).. πεφευγότες [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Antigone” 412; κακὴ ὀσμή [prev. author] “Ph.” 891: _plural_, βυρσῶν ὀσμὰς δεινάς 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Pax” 753; ὀσμαὶ οὐκ ἀνεκτοί 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 7.87, etc.]]; but also of fragrant odours, ὡς καλὴν ὀσμὴν ἔχει [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Cyclops” 153, compare 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Ecclesiazusae” 1124; οἴνου ὀ. 2nd c.AD: Alexander Rhetor 222.4, 4th-3rd c.BC: Philemo Comicus 98.4]]: hence, scent, perfume, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Hiero” 1.4, 3rd c.AD(?): Achilles Tatius Astronomus 2.38]]; on ὀ. as affecting the sense,[Refs 4th c.BC+ [compare 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “de Sensu” 440b28f, “de An.” 421a7f, 4th-3rd c.BC: Theophrastus Philosophus “de Causis Plantarum” 6.1.1f]]

__II
the sense of smell, ={ὄσφρησις}, [Refs 3rd c.AD+ [3rd c.AD: Democritus Epigrammaticus 11, 5th c.AD(?): Hesychius Legal icographus]] —The older form ὀδμή (compare ὄδωδα, ὄζ-ω, od-or) is alone used by [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Homerus Epicus, 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus, and 5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus]]; it occurs also in [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Prometheus Vinctus” 115 (Lyric poetry), 3rd c.AD: Democritus Epigrammaticus]] [same place], and in later Prose, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-3rd c.BC: Theophrastus Philosophus “de Causis Plantarum” 6.14.1, +others, 3rd c.BC: Phylarchus Historicus 63 1st c.AD: Josephus Historicus, Diocl.fragment 129, 1st c.AD: Anonymus Londinensis 34.38, etc.]]; but ὀσμή is Attic dialect accusative to [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd c.AD: Phrynichus Atticista 71]]; also Ionic dialect, [Refs [Hippon.in  “PSI” 9.1089.11.]]

ὅσον μή so far as not, save or except so far as, καλός τε κἀγαθὸς τὴν φύσιν, ὅσον μὴ ὑβριστής (sic to be read) [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Euthydemus” 273a]]; ὅσον γ᾽ ἂν αὐτὸς μὴ ποτιψαύων so far as I can without touching.., [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Trachiniae” 1214; ὅσον μὴ χερσὶ καίνων [prev. author] “OT” 347; ὅσα μή 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 1.111, 4.16]]: sometimes with a finite Verb, πείθεσθαι.., ὅσον ἂν μὴ ἀνάγκη ᾖ [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Oeconomicus” 21.4, compare 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Phaedo” 83a; compare ὅ τι 11.]]

__IV.6
ὁσονοῦν, Ionic dialect ὁσονῶν, ever so little, εἰ τοίνυν ἐχιόνιζε καὶ ὁσονῶν [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 2.22; so ἐφ᾽ ὁσονοῦν 4th-3rd c.BC: Theophrastus Philosophus “Historia Plantarum” 6.7.5, 4th c.AD: Iamblichus Philosophus “in Nicomachi arithmeticam introductionem” p.14 P.]]

__IV.7
ὅσα and ὅσαπερ, just like{ὡς, ὥσπερ}, as, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 1.5.12, 2nd c.AD: Lucianus Sophista “VH” 1.24, etc.]]

__V
ὅσῳ, ὅσῳπερ, by how much, frequently with comparative, ὅσῳ πλέον ἥμισυ παντός [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th-7th c.BC: Hesiodus Epicus “Opera et Dies” 40; ὅσῳ κρείττω 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Fragmenta” 488.3; ὅσῳ ἂν πλεονάκις εἰσίῃς 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 1.3.14]]: with superlative, διέδεξε, ὅσῳ ἐστὶ τοῦτο ἄριστον [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 3.82, compare 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Antigone” 59, 1050.]]

__V.2
ὅσῳ with comparative when followed by another comparative with τοσούτῳ, the more.., so much the more.., [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 7.5.80; ὅ. μᾶλλον πιστεύω, τοσούτῳ μᾶλλον ἀπορῶ 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 368b: with τοσούτῳ omitted, 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Nubes” 1419, 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Coloneus” 792]]: sometimes a superlative replaces the comparative, ὅσῳ μάλιστα ἐλεύθεροι.., τοσούτῳ καὶ θρασύτατα [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 8.84, compare 5th c.BC: Lysias Orator 7.39]]; ὅσῳ alone, ἑωυτοὺς δὲ γενέσθαι τοσούτῳ.., ἀμείνονας, ὅσῳ.. [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 6.137, compare 5.49, 8.13; νιν τῶνδε πλεῖστον ᾤκτισα.., ὅσῳπερ καὶ φρονεῖν οἶδεν μόνη 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Trachiniae” 313, compare “OC” 743.]]

__VI
ἐς ὅσον, ἐφ᾽ ὅσον, καθ᾽ ὅσον are frequently used much like{ὅσον, εἰς ὅσον σθένω} [Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. author] “Ph.” 1403 (troch.); ἐφ᾽ ὅσον ἐδύνατο 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 1.4; εἰς ὅσον δύνανται 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 607a; καθ᾽ ὅσον δυνατόν [prev. author] “Ti.” 51b]]; ἐφ᾽ ὅσον ἐστὶν δυνατός as far as he can, [Refs 2nd c.BC+ [“IG” 22.903.11 (2nd c.BC)]]; later of Time, ἐς ὅσον δύναμίς μοι ὑπῆρχεν as long as.. [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [POxy. 899.8 (2nd-3rd c.AD)]]; ἐφ᾽ ὅσον περιῆσαν as long as they lived, Mitteis [Refs 2nd c.BC+ [“Chr.” 31i23 (2nd c.BC).]]

__VI.2
ἐν ὅσῳ while, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Pax” 943 (Lyric poetry), 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 8.87.]]

__VII
no adverb ὅσως occurs.

deep_entry:
Abbott-Smith / STEPBible (TBESG)
ὅσπερ, see: ὅς.
ὅς, ἥ, ὅ,
the postpositive article (ἄρθρον ὑποτακτικόν).
__I. As demonstr. pron. = οὗτος, ὅδε, this, that, also for αὐτός, chiefly in nom.: ὅς δέ, but he (cf. ἦ δὲ ὅς, frequently in Plat.), Mrk.15:23, Jhn.5:11; ὃς μὲν . . . ὃς δέ, the one . . . the other, Mat.21:35, 22:5, 25:15, Luk.23:33, Act.27:14, Rom.14:5, 1Co.11:21, 2Co.2:18, Ju 22; neut., ὃ μὲν . . . ὃ δέ, the one . . . the other, some . . . some, Mat.13:8, 23, Rom.9:21; ὃς (ὃ) μὲν . . . (ἄλλος (ἄλλο)) . . . ἕτερος, Mrk.4:4, Luk.8:5, 1Co.12:8-10; οὓς μέν, absol., 1Co.12:28; ὃς μὲν . . . ὁ δέ, Rom.14:2.
__II. As relat. pron., who, which, what, that;
__1. agreeing in gender with its antecedent, but differently governed as to case: Mat.2:9, Luk.9:9, Act.20:18, Rom.2:29, al. mult.
__2. In variation from the common construction;
__(a) in gender, agreeing with a noun in apposition to the antecedent: Mrk.15:16, Gal.3:16, Eph.6:17, al.; constr. ad sensum: Jhn.6:9, Col.2:19, 1Ti.3:16, Rev.13:14, al.;
__(b) in number, constr. ad sensum: Act.15:36, 2Pe.3:1;
__(with) in case, by attraction to the case of the antecedent (Bl., §50, 2): Jhn.4:18, Act.3:21, Rom.15:18, 1Co.6:19, Eph.1:8, al.
__3. The neut. ὅ with nouns of other gender and with phrases, which thing, which term: Mrk.3:17 12:42, Jhn.1:39, Col.3:14, al.; with a sentence, Act.2:32, Gal.2:10, 1Jn.2:8, al.
__4. With ellipse of a demonstrative (οὗτος or ἐκεῖνος), before or after: before, Mat.20:23, Luk.7:43, Rom.10:14, al.; after, Mat.10:38, Mrk.9:40, Jhn.19:22, Rom.2:1 al.
__5. Expressing purpose, end or cause: Mat.11:10 (who = that he may), Mrk.1:2, Heb.12:6 al.
__6. C. prep, as periphrasis for conjc.: ἀνθ᾽ ὧν ( = ἀντὶ τούτων ὧν), because, Luk.1:20, al.; wherefore, Luk.12:3; ἐξ οὗ, since, for that, Rom.5:12; ἀφ᾽ οὗ, since (temporal), Luk.13:25; ἐξ οὗ, whence, Php.3:20; etc.
__7. With particles: ὃς ἄν (ἐάν), see: ἄν, ἐάν; ὃς καί, Mrk.3:19, Jhn.21:20, Rom.5:2, al.; ὃς καὶ αὐτός, Mat.27:57.
__8. Gen., οὗ, absol., as adv. (see: οὗ).
(AS)

LSJ / STEPBible (TFLSJ)
ὅσπερ, ἥπερ, ὅπερ
(Epic dialect ὅπερ as masculine, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 7.114, 21.107)]]; genitive οὗπερ, Epic dialect οἷόπερ [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [3rd c.BC: Apollonius Rhodius Epicus 1.1325]]; in Ionic dialect writers and in Poets the oblative cases are sometimes borrowed from the Article, τόπερ [Refs 8th c.BC+ [[prev. author] 3.1098; τοῦπερ 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Persae” 779; τῇπερ 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 24.603, 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.30; τοίπερ 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 13.130; τάπερ 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Choephori” 418 (Lyric poetry), 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 3.16; τῶνπερ 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 13.638, 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Agamemnon” 974]]; on concord and construction [Refs 5th c.BC+ [compare ὅς 5th c.BC: Bacchylides Lyricus 1.1,2,4, 11.1a]],3, IV. 4:—the very man who, the very thing which; frequently indistinguishable from simple ὅς,[Refs [compare ὅσος 111.4: with words intervening between ὅς]] and περ, ὅς ῥ᾽ ἔβαλέν περ [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 4.524, compare 13.101, etc.]]

__2
used after adjectives of resemblance, ὡυτὸς ὅσπερ [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 8.42; ἐκ τῶν ἴσων.., ὧνπερ αὐτὸς ἐξέφυ 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Tyrannus” 1499]]; ὅμοια ἔπραττον ἅπερ ἄν.. [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 5.4.34]]; ὅρκια τάπερ τε.. the same as.., [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.74.]]

__II
special uses of cases,

__II.1
ὅπερ, wherefore, [Refs 1st c.BC+ [1st c.BC: Diodorus Siculus Historicus 13.18 codices (assuming variant)]]; although, [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd c.AD: Apollonius Dyscolus Grammaticus “de Pronominibus;” 103.7.]]

__II.2
ἅπερ, as, like, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Choephori” 381 (Lyric poetry), “Eu.” 131, 660, 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Ajax” 168 (_anapaest meter_, as variant), “OT” 175 (Lyric poetry), 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Historia Graeca (Hellenica)” 5.1.18, etc.]]; compare καθάπερ.

__II.3
οὗπερ, see at {ὅς} A b. [Refs [1.]]

__II.4
ᾗπερ, Doric dialect ᾇπερ, which way, where, whither, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 6.41, 12.33, 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 6.5.10, etc.]]; Ionic dialect τῇπερ, ἔθαψαν.. τῇπερ ἔπεσε [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.30]]; also, as, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 7.286, 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Choephori” 440 (Lyric poetry), 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Acharnenses” 364; ᾗπερ δή 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 9.310; ᾗπερ καί 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Memorabilia” 3.8.2.]]

__II.5
in the Logic of Aristotle, ὅπερ ἐστί, or ὅπερ alone, has two senses:

__II.5.a
non-technical, and unemphatic, what (a thing) is, ἑκάστη οὐσία τοῦθ᾽ ὅ. ἐστίν, οὐ λέγεται μᾶλλον καὶ ἧττον each substance is called what it is without the difference of more or less, [Refs [“Cat.” 3b36]]; τὸ διπλάσιον τοῦθ᾽ ὅ. ἐστίν, ἑτέρου λέγεται the double is called what it is (i.e.  the double) of something, i.e. is relative, [Refs [[prev. work]6a39.]]

__II.5.b
expressing identity, οὔτε ἡ χιὼν ὅ. λευκόν snow is not what white is, i.e. is not identical with white, [Refs [“Top.” 120b23]]; ὁ λευκὸς ἄνθρωπος οὐκ ἔστιν ὅ. χρῶμα [Refs [[prev. work]116a27: hence, to indicate the]]precise or essential nature of a thing, οὐ γὰρ ἂν φαίη ὅ. κακόν τι εἶναι τὴν ἡδονήν he would not say that pleasure is essentially something bad, [Refs [“EN” 1153b6]]; τὰ μὲν οὐσίαν σημαίνοντα ὅ. ἐκεῖνό ἢ ὅ. ἐκεῖνό τι σημαίνει expressions which show the essence show precisely what the thing in question is or precisely of what kind it is (i.e. indicate either its species or its genus), [Refs [“APo.” 83a24]]; ὅ. [τόδε] τί ἐστι τὸ τί ἦν εἶναι the essence of a thing is precisely a 'this', i.e. a fully specified particular, [Refs [“Metaphorical” 1030a3]]; ἡ μὲν [ἐπιστήμη] ὅ. ἀνθρώπου ἐστίν knowledge (that man is an animal) is apprehension that 'animal' is an element in the essential nature of man, [Refs [“APo.” 89a35.]]

ὀστέον, τό,

_nominative_ ὀστέον “PLit.Lond.” 167.17 (2nd-3rd c.AD)]]; dative plural ὀστέοις [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd c.AD: Diogenes Oenoandensis Epicureus 39]]; Epic dialect genitive plural ὀστεόφιν (see. below):—bone, frequently in [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Homerus Epicus (8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 4.460, +others) and 5th c.BC: Hippocrates Medicus (“VC” 1, +others); 8th-7th c.BC: Hesiodus Epicus]] only in plural, [Refs [“Th.” 540, +others]]; λεύκ᾽ ὀστέα the bleached bones of the dead, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 1.161, etc.; σάρκας τε καὶ ὀστέα 9.293]]; πολὺς δ᾽ ἀμφ᾽ ὀστεόφιν θίς a huge heap of bones around,[Refs 5th c.BC+ [12.45; ῥινὸν ἀπ᾽ ὀστεόφιν ἐρύσαι 14.134; γυμνοῦσι τὰ ὀστέα τῶν κρεῶν 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 4.61]]; ὀστέων στέγαστρον, of the skin, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Fragmenta - American Journal of Philology” 367; ἀρχὴ τῶν ὀστῶν ἡ καλουμένη ῥάχις 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “de Partibus Animalium” 54b11]]; especially of the cranium, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Hippocrates Medicus “περὶ τῶν ἐν κεφαλη—ͅ τρωμάτων” 2, +others, compare 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 12.185.]]

metaphorically, γῆς ὀστέοισιν ἐγχριμφθεὶς πόδα, i.e. rocks, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Choerilus Tragicus 2 (ὀστοῖσιν Nauck).]]

stone of fruit, ὀστῶν περσεΐνων [Refs 8th c.BC+ [“PCair.Zen.” 176.168 (3rd c.BC),compare 1st c.AD: Dioscorides (Dioscurides) Medicus “Eup.” 1.66, “Geoponica” 10.13.3, +others, Scholia 2nd c.BC: Nicander Epicus “Alexipharmaca” 99. [Accent ὀστέον Hdn.Gr. 2.943, but ὄστεον Anonymus cited in Scholia 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 24.793]].] (Cf. Sanskrit ´sthi, genitive asthn´s 'bone', etc.)

deep_entry:
Abbott-Smith / STEPBible (TBESG)
ὅστις, ἥτις, ὅ τι (also written ὅ, τι and ὅτι; see LS, see word; WH, §411; Tdf., Pr., 111), in NT scarcely ever except in nom. (M, Pr., 91), the only instance of the oblique cases being found in ἕως ὅτου (see: ἕως), relative of indef. reference (related to simple ὅς as Lat. quisquis to qui),
whoever, anyone who;
__(a) of an indef. person or thing: in general statements, Mat.5:39, 41 13:12, and freq., Luk.14:27, Gal.5:4, al.; in relative sentences, Mat.7:26, Luk.15:7, Php.3:7, al.; πᾶς, with indic., Mat.7:24 10:32; ὅ ἄν (ἐάν), with subjc., Mat.12:50 13:12, Jhn.14:13, 1Co.16:2, Gal.5:10, al.;
__(b) of a definite person or thing, indicating quality, "either  generic, which, as other like things, or essential, which by its very nature" (Hort on 1Pe.2:11), who is such as: Mat.2:6 7:26, Luk.2:10 7:37, Jhn.8:53, Act.7:53, Rom.6:2, 1Co.3:17, Gal.4:24, Eph.1:23, al.;
__(with) where the relative sentence expresses a reason, consequence, etc. (M, Pr., 92), seeing that he (it, they), and he (it, they): Luk.8:3 10:42, Act.10:47 11:28, Php.4:3, al.;
__(d) as in Ionic and late Greek (Bl., §50, 1; M, Pr., l.with), differing but little from ὅς: Luk.2:4 9:30, Act.17:10, Rev.12:13.
(AS)

neuter ὅτινα [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 22.450; _genitive_ ὅτεων 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 10.39, 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 8.65]], Attic dialect ὅτων [Refs 8th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Tyrannus” 414, 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 7.6.24 (conjecture), “Oec.” 3.2 (conjecture) (also in 8th-7th c.BC: Hesiodus Epicus “Fragmenta” 238, 5th c.BC: Anaxagoras Philosophus 12, 5th c.BC: Hippocrates Medicus “Aër.” 21); _dative_ ὁτέοισι (ν) 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 15.491, 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 2.82]], Attic dialect ὅτοισι [Refs 8th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Antigone” 1335, 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Equites” 758, ὅτοις 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Trachiniae” 1119; _accusative_ ὅτινας 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 15.492]], Aeolic dialect ὄττινας [Refs 7th c.BC+ [7th-6th c.BC: Sappho Lyrica 12: in a few forms only the first part is inflected, Cretan dialect _genitive_ _sing._ ὦτι probably in “Leg.Gort.” 1.5, 2.50, 11.50, +others, “GDI” 4993 ii 10: _neuter_ _plural_ ἄτι “Leg.Gort.” 2.47, +others]]: of the forms with double inflexion [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Homerus Epicus has only ὅν τινα 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 2.188, +others, ἥν τινα 3.286, +others, οἵ τινες 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 4.94, +others, οὕς τινας 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 4.240, +others, ἅς τινας 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 8.573]]; ᾧτινι first in [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th-7th c.BC: Hesiodus Epicus “Opera et Dies” 31, ἧστινος 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Agamemnon” 1358, ᾗ τινι δή 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 8.87, οἷστισι 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Pax” 1279: _Attic dialect_ Inscrr. have ἧστινος ᾗτινι along with _masculine_ and _neuter_ ὅτου ὅτῳ, and this rule holds with few exceptions in Trag. and _Attic dialect_ Prose before 4th c.BC]]; ᾡτινιοῦν occurs in [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Lysias Orator 1.37, etc.: ὅτῳ]] rarely as feminine, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Iphigenia Taurica” 1071.]]—For the Ionic dialect and Epic dialect form ἅσσα, Attic dialect ἅττα, see at {ἅσσα}.—On the concord and construction[Refs 5th c.BC+ [compare ὅς 5th c.BC: Bacchylides Lyricus 1.1,3, 11.3]], 111.2a,b:—Radic. sense, any one who, anything which, whosoever, whichsoever; ὣς ἀπόλοιτο καὶ ἄλλος, ὅτις τοιαῦτά γε ῥέζοι [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 1.47; ἀθανάτων ὅς τίς σε φυλάσσει 15.35, etc.]]: frequently without express antecedent, χαίρει δέ μιν ὅς τις ἐθείρῃ [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 21.347; ἆσσον ἴτω ὅς τις δέπας οἴσεται 23.667]]: hence frequently in maxims or sentiments, οὐκ ἔστιν ὅ. πάντ᾽ ἀνὴρ εὐδαιμονεῖ [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Ranae” 1217; μακάριος ὅ. οὐσίαν καὶ νοῦν ἔχει 4th-3rd c.BC: Menander Comicus 114]]; οὗτος βέλτιστος ἂν εἴη, ὅ... [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Lysias Orator 3.4, etc.: frequently in such phrases as ὅστις εἶ, ὅστις ἐστί, see at {ὅς} 5th c.BC: Bacchylides Lyricus 111.2]]; ἔστιν ὅ., frequently with a negative, οὐ γὰρ ἔην ὅς τίς σφιν.. ἡγήσαιτο [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 2.687; οὐκ ἔστιν ὅτῳ μείζονα μοῖραν νείμαιμ᾽ ἢ σοί 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Prometheus Vinctus” 293 (_anapaest meter_), compare 989, 1070 (_anapaest meter_), etc.]]; εἰσὶν οἵτινες [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Fragmenta” 354.5]]; οὐδὲν ὅ τι οὐ.. everything, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 5.97, 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 7.87:—in these phrases the case of ὅστις commonly depends on that of οὐδεί; but sometimes the reverse, see at {οὐδείς} I.2: also joined with _superlative_, τρόπῳ ὅτῳ ἂν δύνωνται ἰσχυροτάτῳ Foed. cited in 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 5.23; ὅντινα ἀφανέστατον δύναιντο τρόπον 2nd c.AD: Pausanias Periegeta 10.1.5: in Trag. and _Attic dialect_ sometimes strengthened by an antecedent πᾶς]], but only in singular, ἅπας δὲ τραχὺς ὅ. ἂν νέον κρατῇ [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Prometheus Vinctus” 35, compare 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 8.90 (πάντες ὅσοι being commonly used in _plural_, not πάντες οἵτινες]]; but πᾶσιν.. ὅστις ἐρωτᾷ [Refs [“IG” 12.410).]]

__II
referring to a definite object, properly only when a general notion is implied, Πολυκράτεα.., δι᾽ ὅντινα κακῶς ἤκουσε, not the man through whom, but one through whom.., [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 3.120]]; τελευταῖόν σε προσβλέψαιμι νῦν, ὅστις πέφασμαι φύς τ᾽ ἀφ᾽ ὧν οὐ χρῆν may I see thee now for the last time, I who am one born from sinful parentage, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Tyrannus” 1184, compare 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Prometheus Vinctus” 38, “Ag.” 1065]]; but in quite definite sense, βωμόν, ὅστις νῦν ἔξω τῆς πόλεώς ἐστι [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 6.3: sometimes even with οὗτος or ὅδε as antecedent, 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.167, 2.99, 6.47, 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Hippolytus” 943, 3rd c.BC: Theocritus Poeta Bucolicus 8.87.]]

__II.2
ἐφ᾽ ὅτῳ, ={ἐφ᾽ ᾧτε}, [Refs 2nd c.BC+ [1st c.BC: Diodorus Siculus Historicus 16.4; so ἐφ᾽ ὅτῳ τε “Delph.” 3(2).236 (2nd c.BC).]]

__III
in indirect questions, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Homerus Epicus, etc., εἴπ᾽ ἄγε μοι καὶ τόνδε.., ὅς τις ὅδ᾽ ἐστί 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 3.192, compare 167, etc.]]; ἔσπετε νῦν μοι, Μοῦσαι, ὅς τις δὴ κτλ. who it was that..,[Refs 8th c.BC+ [14.509; ξεῖνος ὅδ᾽, οὐκ οἶδ᾽ ὅς τις 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 8.28: in dialogue, when the person questioned repeats the question asked by τίς, as οὗτος τί ποιεῖ;—ὅ τι ποι; 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Ranae” 198]]; ἀλλὰ τίς γὰρ ε;—ὅστις; πολίτης χρηστός [Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. author] “Ach.” 595, compare “Pl.” 462, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Euthyphro” 2c, etc.]]

__III.2
rare and late in direct questions, ὅ τι ἐστὶ τὸ ἐμποδίζον ; [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd c.AD: Apollonius Dyscolus Grammaticus “de Adverbiis;” 140.12]]; ἀνθ᾽ ὅτου.. ; = why? [Refs 4th c.AD+ [4th c.AD: Julianus Imperator “Epistulae” 82p.109B.]]-C.; compare ὅπως.

__IV
limited or made more indefinite by the addition of Particles:

__IV.1
ὅστις γε being one who (compare ὅσγε), [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Tyrannus” 1335, “OC” 810, 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Ranae” 1184.]]

__IV.2
ὅστις δή (see. δή IV. [Refs [1), frequently used without any distinct relative force, θεῶν ὅτεῳ δή]]to some one or other of the gods, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.86; ὅτευ δὴ χρήματος δεησόμενον [prev. author] 3.121; ᾗ τινι δὴ γνώμῃ 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 8.87, etc.; also ὅ τι δήκοτε πρήξοντα 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 6.134; ὅστις δήποτ᾽ ὤν 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Phaedrus” 273c; ὡς ἀπετύγχαν᾽ ὁτουδήποτε 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 19.167; ὁτῳδήτινι τρόπῳ “PFay.” 21.11 (2nd c.AD)]]; so

__IV.2.b
ὁστισοῦν, ὁτιοῦν anybody (anything) whatsoever, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 4.16, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Symposium” 198b, etc.; μετὰ ὁτουοῦν τρόπου 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 8.27; ὁτῳοῦν 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Theaetetus” 175a]]; εἷς ὁστισοῦν any one person, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Politica” 1286a31: frequently with _negative_, μηδ᾽ ἂν ὁστισοῦν τυγχάνῃ ὤν 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Euthyphro” 5e, compare “Phd.” 78d, etc.]]; οὐδ᾽ ὁτιοῦν not the least mite, nothing whatsoever, [Refs 6th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Nubes” 344, “Pl.” 385; μηδοτιοῦν 6th c.BC: Theognis Elegiacus 64]]: rarely, = whoever (whatever), as subject of a verb, ὁτιοῦν ἔτυχε τῶν ἐπὶ μέρους (variant{ὅτι ἄν}) [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “de Mundo” 391a22.]]

__IV.2.c
ὁστισδηποτοῦν [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 40.8, 4th c.BC: Aeschines Orator 1.164.]]

__IV.2.d
so also ὅστις alone, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Hp.Ma.” 282d, etc.: with _negative_, μηδὲ οἵτινες]] none at all, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Historia Graeca (Hellenica)” 1.5.9; οὐδ᾽ ἧστινος ἂν ἀσχολίας τὸ πρᾶγμα προσεδεῖτο 2nd c.BC: Polybius Historicus 9.14.6.]]

__IV.3
ὅστις ποτε whoever, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Agamemnon” 160 (Lyric poetry), compare 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 8.65.]]

__IV.4
ὅστις περ (compare ὅσπερ), mostly in neuter, ὅ τι πέρ ἐστ᾽ ὄφελος [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Ecclesiazusae” 53, compare 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 492e: in _masculine_, 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 21.225.]]

__IV.5
ὅστις τε, where τε is otiose as in ὅστε, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 23.43, +others]]

__V
neuter ὅ τι used absolutely as a conjunction, see at {ὅ τι}.

__VI
ἐξ ὅτου from which time, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Coloneus” 345, “Tr.” 326, 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Nubes” 528, 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 8.2.16, etc.; ἐξ ὅτου περ 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Acharnenses” 596]]; ἀπ᾽ ὅτευ since.., [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.7, compare “SIG” 45.18 (Halic., 5th c.BC)]]; so ἕως ὅτου until.., [NT.Luke.13.8.]

__VI.2
from what cause, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Trachiniae” 671, 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Cyclops” 639.]]
