[Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Supplices” 808 (Lyric poetry), compare 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Ranae” 781; ἵππον οὐράνια βρέμοντα 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Troades” 519 (Lyric poetry)]]: metaphorically, mountainous, colossal, οὐ. ἄχη [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Persae” 573 (Lyric poetry); ἡμάρτηκεν οὐράνιόν γ᾽ ὅσον 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Ranae” 1135.]]

sky-blue, λίθος κυανωτάτη καὶ -ία ἰδεῖν [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd-3rd c.AD: Philostratus Sophista “Vita Apollonii” 1.25.]]

οὐράνιον, τό, name of an eye-salve, [Refs 4th c.AD+ [4th c.AD: Oribasius Medicus cited in 6th c.AD: Aëtius Medicus 7.106.]]

deep_entry:
Abbott-Smith / STEPBible (TBESG)
οὐρανός, -οῦ, ὁ,
[in LXX chiefly for שָׁמַיִם (hence, often pl., οἱ οὐ., see infr.) ;]
heaven;
__1. of the vault or firmament of heaven, the sky and the aerial regions above the earth: opposite to ἡ γῆ, Heb.1:10, 2Pe.3:5, 10; ὁ οὐ. καὶ ἡ γῆ, i.e. the world, the universe, Mat.5:18, Mrk.13:31, Luk.10:21, Act.4:24, Rev.10:6, al.; ἀπ᾽ ἄκρων οὐ. ἕως ἄ. αὐτῶν (on the absence of art. aft. prep., see Bl, §46, 5), Mat.24:31; ὑπὸ τὸν οὐ., Act.2:5, Col.1:23; ὑψωθῆναι ἕως τοῦ οὐ., figuratively, Mat.11:23, Luk.10:15; σημεῖον ἐκ τοῦ οὐ., Mat.16:1, Mrk.8:11, al.; αἱ νεφέλαι, Mat.24:30, al.; τὰ πετεινὰ τοῦ οὐ., Mat.6:26, Mrk.4:32, al.; οἱ ἀστέρες τοῦ οὐ., Rev.6:13, al.; pl. (οἱ) οὐ. (Bl., §32, 5), Mat.3:16, Mrk.1:10, Jhn.1:32, 2Pe.3:7, 13 al.
__2. Of the abode of God and other blessed beings: of angels, Mat.24:36, Mrk.12:25, Gal.1:8, Rev.10:1, al.; of Christ glorified, Mrk.16:[19], Luk.24:51, Act.3:21, Rom.10:6, al.; of God, Mat.5:34, Rom.1:18, al.; ὁ Πατὴρ ὁ ἐν τοῖς οὐ. (Dalman, Words, 184ff.), Mat.5:16 6:1, al.; θησαυρὸς ἐν οὐ., Mat.6:20, Mrk.10:21, al.
__3. By meton.,
__(a) of the inhabitants of heaven: Rev.18:20 (cf. ib. 12:12, Job.15:15, Isa.44:23);
__(b) as an evasive  reference to God, characteristic of later Judaism (Dalman, Words, 204ff.): Mat.21:25, Mrk.11:30, Luk.15:18, Jhn.3:27, al.; ἡ βασιλεία τῶν οὐ. (= τοῦ Θεοῦ); see: βασιλεία).
βασιλεία, -ας, ἡ
(βασιλεύω), [in LXX chiefly for מַמְלָכָה ,מַלְכוּת ;]
__1. prop. abstract, sovereignty, royal power, dominion: Luk.1:33 22:29, Jhn.18:36, Act.1:6, Heb.1:8, 1Co.15:24; λαβεῖν β., Luk.19:12, 15 Rev.17:12; δοῦναι τὴν, ib. 17; ἔχειν β., ib. 18; ἔρχεσθαι ἐν τ. (εἰς τὴν) β., Mat.16:28, Luk.23:42; β. τ. θεοῦ, Rev.12:10.
__2. By meton., concrete (MM, Exp., x),
__(a) a kingdom, the territory or people over whom the king rules (Est.5:3, al.): Mat.4:8 12:25, 26 24:7, Mrk.3:24 6:23, Luk.4:5, Heb.11:33, al.;
__(b) the royal majesty (cf. our phrase His Majesty), the king himself (τ. σπέρμα τῆς β., 4Ki.11:1).
__3. In LXX (Wis.6:5, Tob.13:1, al.), Targ. and NT, of the Messianic rule and kingdom, ἡ β. τ. θεοῦ, τ. οὐρανῶν (Heb. מַלְכוּת שָׁמַיִם, Aram. מַלְכוּתָא דִשׁמַיָּא; see Dalman, Words, 91-147; Cremer, 132, 658), the kingdom of God (on the equivalence of the two phrases, see Dalman, op. cit., 93, 218f.); τ. θεοῦ, Mat.6:33 12:28, al.; τ. οὐρανῶν, Mat.3:2 4:17, al.; τ. Χριστοῦ (מַלִכוּת דִמְשִׁיחא, Targ. Jon. on Isa.53:10), Eph.5:5; τ. κυρίου, 2Pe.1:11, Rev.11:15; τ. Δαυείδ, Mrk.11:10; absol., ἡ β., Mat.4:23, Jas.2:5, al. The kingdom is regarded as present: Mat.11:12, Luk.17:21, Rom.14:17, al.; as that which is to be consummated in the future, Mat.6:10, Mrk.9:1, Jhn.3:5, 2Pe.1:11, al. Noteworthy phrases are: ζητεῖν τὴν β., Mat.6:33; δέχεσθαι, Mrk.10:15; κλρονομεῖν, Mat.25:34; διδόναι, Lk 12:32; παραλαμβάνειν, Heb.12:28; αὐτῶν (τοιούτων) εστὶν ἡ β., Mat.5:3, 10 19:14, Mrk.10:14, Luk.18:16; διὰ τὴν β., Mat.19:12; ἕνεκεν τῆς β., Luk.18:29; εὐαγγελίζεσθαι, κηρύσσειν, διαγγέλλειν τὴν β., Luk.4:43 9:2, 60; ἤγγικεν ἡ β., Mat.3:2, Mrk.1:15; κλεῖς τῆς β., Mat.16:10; κλείειν τὴν β., Mat.23:14; υἱοὶ τῆς β., Mat.8:12 13:38 (cf. Cremer, 132, 658).
\ (AS)

οὐρᾰνός, ὁ,
Doric dialect and Boeotian dialect ὠρανός [Refs 7th c.BC+ [7th c.BC: Alcman Lyricus 23.16, 3rd c.BC: Theocritus Poeta Bucolicus 2.147, 5.144, 6th c.BC: Corinna Lyrica “Supp.” 2.79, “Hymnus ad Isim” 19]]; Aeolic dialect ὄρανος (ὀράνω [Refs 7th c.BC+ [7th-6th c.BC: Sappho Lyrica 37, 64, 7th-6th c.BC: Alcaeus Lyricus 34, but ὠράνω 7th-6th c.BC: Sappho Lyrica 1.11 (assuming variant), 7th-6th c.BC: Alcaeus Lyricus 17 (assuming variant), and see at {Οὐρανία}): —never used in _plural_ by classical writers, see 1.4: (see. near the end):]]

__I
heaven: in [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Homerus Epicus and 8th-7th c.BC: Hesiodus Epicus,]]

__I.1
vault or firmament of heaven, sky, γαῖα.. ἐγείνατο ἶσον ἑαυτῇ οὐρανὸν ἀστερόεντα, ἵνα μιν περὶ πάντα καλύπτοι [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th-7th c.BC: Hesiodus Epicus “Theogonia” 127; ἔχει δέ τε κίονας αὐτὸς [Ἄτλας] μακράς, αἳ γαῖάν τε καὶ οὐρανὸν ἀμφὶς ἔχουσι 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 1.54, compare 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Prometheus Vinctus” 351; χάλκεος 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 17.425; πολύχαλκος 5.504, 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 3.2; σιδήρεος 15.329]]; wrapped in clouds, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 15.192, 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 5.303]]; above the aether, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 2.458, 17.425, 19.351, cf. Scholia 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 3.3; even 5th c.BC: Empedocles Poeta Philosophus]] continued to regard it as solid (στερέμνιον), [Refs [“Placita Philosophorum” 2.11.2 (“Vorsokr.” ip.209)]]; defined as αἰθέρος τὸ ἔσχατον by [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th-3rd c.BC: Zeno Citieus Stoicus 1.33, compare 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Nubes” 95 ff.]]; ἠέλιος δὲ οὐρανοῦ ἐξαπόλωλε, of an eclipse, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 20.357, compare 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Ajax” 845; ἐν δὲ τὰ τείρεα πάντα, τά τ᾽ οὐρανὸς ἐστεφάνωται 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 18.485; Ἕσπερος, ὃς κάλλιστος ἐν οὐρανῷ ἵσταται ἀστήρ 22.318; οὐρανὸς ἀστερόεις 6.108, +others]]

__I.2
heaven, as the seat of the gods, outside or above this skyey vault, the portion of Zeus (see. Ὄλυμπος),[Refs 8th c.BC+ [15.192, compare 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 1.67, etc.; οὐ. Οὔλυμπός τε 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 1.497, 8.394; Οὔλυμ πός τε καὶ οὐ. 19.128]]; πύλαι οὐρανοῦ [Refs [“Heaven” -gate, i. e. a thick cloud, which the Ὧραι lifted and put down like a trap-door, 5.749, 8.393]]; so, later, οἱ ἐξ οὐρανοῦ the gods of heaven, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Prometheus Vinctus” 897 (Lyric poetry)]]; οἱ ἐν οὐρανῷ θεοί (viz. Sun, etc.) [Refs 8th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 508a; εὔχετο, χεῖρ᾽ ὀρέγων εἰς οὐ. ἀστερόεντα 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 15.371, 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 9.527]]; νὴ τὸν οὐ. [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Plutus” 267, 366.]]

__I.3
in common language, sky, οὐδέ τις ἄλλη φαίνετο γαιάων, ἀλλ᾽ οὐ. ἠδὲ θάλασσα [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 14.302; σέλας δ᾽ εἰς οὐ. ἵκῃ 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 8.509]]; κλέος οὐρανὸν ἵκει, κλέος οὐ. εὐρὺν ἱκάνει, renown reaches to heaven,[Refs 8th c.BC+ [[prev. work] 192, 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 19.108]]; so ὀρυμαγδός, κνίση, σκόπελος οὐρανὸν ἷκεν or ἱκάνει, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 17.425, 1.317, 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 12.73 (compare οὐράνιος 11, οὐρανομήκης): _metaphorically_, ὕβρις τε βίη τε σιδήρεον οὐ. ἵκει]] deeds of violence 'cry to heaven', [Refs 5th c.BC+ [15.329, 17.565; γῇ τε κοὐρανῷ λέξαι.. τύχας 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Medea” 57, compare 4th-3rd c.BC: Philemo Comicus 79.1]]; πρὸς οὐρανὸν βιβάζειν τι to exalt to heaven, [Refs [S “OC” 381]]; πρὸς τὸν οὐ. ἥλλοντο leaped up on high, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 1.4.11; πρὸς τὸν οὐ. βλέπειν [prev. author] “Oec.” 19.9.]]

__I.4
in Philos., the heavens, universe, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Politicus” 269d, “Ti.” 32b, 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “de Caelo” 278b21, “Metaphorical” 990a20, +others: _plural_ in “VT”, οἱ οὐρανοί]] the heavens, [LXX.Psa.96(97).6, 148.4, +others]

__I.5
a region of heaven, climate, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.142.]]

__I.6
[Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Pythagoras Philosophus name of 10, “Theologumena Arithmeticae” 59.]]

__II
anything shaped like the vault of heaven, as,

__II.1
vaulted roof or ceiling, [Refs 5th c.AD+ [5th c.AD(?): Hesychius Legal icographus]]

__II.2
roof of the mouth, palate, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Historia Animalium” 492a20, “PA” 660a14, 2nd c.AD: Athenaeus Epigrammaticus 8.344b, “Anthologia Graeca” 5.104 (Marc. argument).]]

__II.3
lid, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Matro Parodius “Convivium - Corpusculum poesis epicae ludibundae” 12.]]

__II.4
tent, pavilion, [Refs 4th c.AD+ [4th c.AD: Themistius Sophista “Orationes” 13.166b.]]

__III
proper name, “Uranos”, son of Erebos and Gaia, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th-7th c.BC: Hesiodus Epicus “Theogonia” 127s q]].; but husband of Gaia, parent of Cronos and the Titans (compare Οὐρανίδης),[Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. work] 106, “Hymni Homerici” 30.17, compare 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Prometheus Vinctus” 207. (Acc. to 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “de Mundo” 400a7, from ὅρος and ἄνω,compare 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Cratylus” 396c. This must be wrong, but the true etymology is doubtful.)]]

οὖς
(nominative singular frequently in [Refs 8th c.BC+ [“IG” Il(2).161 B 126, +others (Delos, 3rd c.BC), see entry near the end), τό, _genitive_ ὠτός, _dative_ ὠτί: _plural_ _nominative_ ὦτα, _genitive_ ὤτων, _dative_ ὠσί (ὤτοις condemned by 2nd c.AD: Phrynichus Atticista 186):— 8th c.BC: Homerus Epicus has only _accusative_ _sing._ and _dative_ _plural_ (see. below)]]; the other cases he forms as if from οὖας (which is found in [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Simonides Lyricus 37.14), _genitive_ οὔατος, _plural_ _nominative_ and _accusative_ οὔατα (also in 5th c.BC: Epicharmus Comicus 21, 5th c.BC: Hippocrates Medicus “περὶ καρδίης” 8, +others, “SIG” 1025.62 (Cos, 4th-3rd c.BC))]], dative οὔασι [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 12.442 (ὠσίν 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 12.200)]]: Hellenistic nominative singular ὦς [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [“PPetr.” 3p.33 (3rd c.BC), “PGrenf.” 1.12.29, 2.15 ii I (2nd c.BC), “IG” 7.3498.19 (Oropus, 2nd c.BC), Roussel “Cultes Egyptiens” 217 (Delos, 2nd c.BC), “PStrassb.” 87.14 (2nd c.BC)]]: also Doric dialect ὦς [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [3rd c.BC: Theocritus Poeta Bucolicus 11.32]]; plural ὤϝαθ᾽ conjecture for ὦτά θ᾽ in [Refs 7th c.BC+ [7th c.BC: Alcman Lyricus 41]]:—ear, Ἄντιφον αὖ παρὰ οὖς ἔλασε ξίφει [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 11.109; [κηρὸν] ἐπ᾽ ὠσὶν ἄλειψ᾽ 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” [same place]]]; αἲ γὰρ δή μοι ἀπ᾽ οὔατος ὧδε γένοιτο oh may I never hear of such a thing! [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 18.272; αἲ γὰρ ἀπ᾽ οὔατος εἴη 22.454; ἀμφὶ κτύπος οὔατα βάλλει 10.535]]; ὀρθὰ ἱστάναι τὰ ὦτα, of horses, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 4.129, compare 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Electra” 27, etc.; ἐν τοῖσι ὠσὶ.. οἰκέει ὁ θυμός 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 7.39, compare 1.8]]; βοᾷ ἐν ὠσὶ κέλαδος rings in the ear, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Persae” 605; φθόγγος βάλλει δι᾽ ὤτων 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Antigone” 1188, compare 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Choephori” 56 (Lyric poetry); δι᾽ ὠτὸς παῦρα ἐννέπειν πρός τινα 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Electra” 1437 (Lyric poetry)]]; ὀξὺν δι᾽ ὤτων κέλαδον ἐνσείσας[Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. work] 737, compare “OT” 1387; δι᾽ ὤτων ἦν λόγος 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Medea” 1139, compare “Rh.” 294, 566; so ἁμῖν τοῦτο δι᾽ ὠτὸς ἔγεντο 3rd c.BC: Theocritus Poeta Bucolicus 14.27; λόγους ψιθύρους εἰς ὦτα φέρει 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Ajax” 149 (_anapaest meter_); εἰς οὖς ἑκάστῳ.. ηὔδα λόγους 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Andromache” 1091, compare “Hipp.” 932; προσκύψας μοι μικρὸν πρὸς τὸ οὖς 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Euthydemus” 275e]]; ἐπ᾽ (ἐς conjecture Dawes) οὔατα λάθριος εἶπεν [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [3rd c.BC: Callimachus Epicus “Hymnus in Apollinem” 105]]; reversely, παρέχειν τὰ ὦτα to lend the ears, i. e. to attend, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Cratylus” 396d, etc.; so ἐπισχέσθαι τὰ ὦτα [prev. author] “Smp.” 216a; παραβάλλειν [prev. author] “R.” 531a, cf. Callias Epigrammaticus “anonymous fragment” 375; τὰ ὦτα ἐξεπετάννυτο 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Equites” 1347; ὦτα χορηγεῖν 1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus 2.232f; ἀποκλείειν τὰ ὦτα [prev. work]143f; οἱ ὦτα ἔχοντες]] those who have ears to hear, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. work] 1113c: _metaphorically_, of spies in Persia, 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 8.2.10s q., 2nd c.AD: Lucianus Sophista “Ind.” 23, compare 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Politica” 1287b30; τὸ τῶν λεγομένων ὤτων καὶ προσαγωγέων γένος 1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus 2.522f]]; τὰ ὦτα ἐπὶ τῶν ὤμων ἔχοντες, of persons who slink away ashamed (hanging their ears like dogs), [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 613c]]: proverbial, see at {λύκο; τεθλασμένος οὔατα πυγμαῖς}, of a boxer, [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [3rd c.BC: Theocritus Poeta Bucolicus 22.45 (compare ὠτοκάταξις)]]; ἐπ᾽ ἀμφότερα τὰ ὦτα καθεύδειν sleep soundly, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aeschines Orator 5th-4th c.BC: Socratis et Socraticorum Epistulae 54 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator]]

__II
from resemblance to an ear,

__II.1
handle, especially of pitchers, cups, etc., οὔατα δ᾽ αὐτοῦ τέσσαρ᾽ ἔσαν [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 11.633, compare 18.378, 2nd c.BC: Bion Bucolicus cited in 1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus 2.536a, “IG” 11(2).161 B 126 (Delos, 3rd c.BC), 2nd-1st c.BC(?): Hero Mechanicus “(Spiritalia) Pneumatica” 2.23, 1st c.AD: Dioscorides (Dioscurides) Medicus 5.87; [ποτήριον] ὦτα συντεθλασμένον 2nd c.AD: Alexander Rhetor 270.3.]]

__II.2
in Architecture texts, ={παρωτίς}[Refs [4, “IG” 12.372.201, compare 319.6.]]

__II.3
οὖς Ἀφροδίτης, a kind of shell-fish, Antig.Car. cited in [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd c.AD: Athenaeus Epigrammaticus 3.88a]]; οὖς θαλάττιον, ={ἀγρία λεπάς}, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Historia Animalium” 529b16.]]

__II.4
τὰ ὦτα (οὔατα [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Hippocrates Medicus) τῆς καρδίας]] the auricles of the heart, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Hippocrates Medicus “περὶ καρδίης” 8, 2nd c.AD: Galenus Medicus “de Usu Partium” 6.15, compare 2.615K.]]

__II.5
name of part of a bandage, Heraclas cited in [Refs 4th c.AD+ [4th c.AD: Oribasius Medicus 48.15 at Title Page [Written ὀ̄ς in “IG” 12]]. [prev. cited]] (Cogn. with Latin auris, Lithuanian ausìs, O[Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus]] éar, etc.; details obscure; nominative singular οὖς perhaps from *ο(ϝ)ος (contained in ἀμφώης).)

LSJ / STEPBible (TFLSJ)
οὐσί-α,
Ionic dialect -ιη[Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.92, 6.86.ά, “SIG” 167.26 (Mylasa, 4th c.BC)]]; Doric dialect ἐσσία, ὠσία (which see): ἡ: (ὀντ-, participle of εἰμί sum):—that which is one's own, one's substance, property, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus [same places], 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Trachiniae” 911 (assuming variant), 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Hercules Furens” 337, “Hel.” 1253 (_plural_, “fragment” 354 (assuming variant)), 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Ecclesiazusae” 729, 5th c.BC: Lysias Orator 18.17, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 551b, “SIG”]][same place], etc.; opposed to τὰ σώματα (civil status), [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Andocides Orator 1.74; καλῶς.. ἐπεμελήθη τῶν οὐσιῶν ὑπὲρ τοῦ δημάρχου “BSA” 24.154 (Attica, 4th c.BC)]]; εἰ ἐκεκτήμην οὐ. if I had been a man of substance, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Lysias Orator 24.11; ὑπὲρ τὴν οὐ. δαπανᾶν 4th-3rd c.BC: Diphilus Comicus 32.7; πατρῴαν οὐ. κατεσθίειν 4th c.BC: Anaxippus Comicus 1.32, compare 5th c.BC: Critias Philosophus, Tragicus, Elegiacus 45 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator]]; φανερὰ οὐσία real property, immovables, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Andocides Orator 1.118]]; opposed to ἀφανής, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Lysias Orator 32.4]]; frequently of estates in Egypt, [Refs 2nd c.BC+ [“PTeb.” 6.23 (2nd c.BC, _plural_), “BGU” 650.3 (1st c.AD), “OGI” 665.30 (1st c.AD), etc.]]

__II
in Philos., like Ionic dialect φύσις (with which it is interchanged in various uses, e. g. [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Philolaus Philosophus 11, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 359a, 359b, 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “de Partibus Animalium” 646a25, 4th-3rd c.BC: Theophrastus Philosophus “Historia Plantarum” 6.1.1)]], stable being, immutable reality, opposed to γένεσις, ὅτιπερ πρὸς γένεσιν οὐσία, τοῦτο πρὸς πίστιν ἀλήθεια [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Timaeus” 29c, compare “Sph.” 232c; ὧν κίνησις γένεσιν παραλαβοῦσα ἀέναον οὐ. ἐπόρισεν [prev. author] “Lg.” 966e; γένεσις μὲν τὸ σπέρμα, οὐ. δὲ τὸ τέλος 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “de Partibus Animalium” 641b32, compare 640a18, etc.]]; ὁδὸς εἰς οὐσίαν [Refs [[prev. author] “Metaphorical” 1003b7]]: hence, being in the abstract, opposed to non-being (τὸ μὴ εἶναι), [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Theaetetus” 185c.]]

__II.2
substance, essence, opposed to πάθη ('modes'), [Refs 4th c.BC+ [[prev. author] “Euthphr.” 11a; πάθη οὐσίας 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Metaphysica” 1003b7]]; opposed to συμβεβηκότα ('accidents'), [Refs [[prev. author] “APo.” 83a24, “PA” 643a27; ἡ φύσις [τῆς ψυχῆς] καὶ ἡ οὐ., εἶθ᾽ ὅσα συμβέβηκε περὶ αὐτήν [prev. author] “de An.” 402a8.]]

__II.3
true nature of that which is a member of a kind, defined as ὃ τυγχάνει ἕκαστον ὄν [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Phaedo” 65d]]; as τὸ ὅ ἐστι[Refs 4th c.BC+ [[prev. work] 92d; as τὸ τί ἐστι 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Analytica Posteriora” 90b30]]; τὸ εἶναί τε καὶ τὴν οὐ. [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 509b]]; expressed in a formula or definition, ψυχῆς οὐ. τε καὶ λόγον [Refs 4th c.BC+ [[prev. author] “Phdr.” 245e; τὸ τί ἦν εἶναι οὗ ὁ λόγος ὁρισμός, καὶ τοῦτο οὐ. λέγεται 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Metaphysica” 1017b22; μόνης τῆς οὐ. ἐστὶν ὁ ὁρισμός [prev. work] 1031a1.]]

__II.4
the possession of such a nature, substantiality, ἔτι ἐπέκεινα τῆς οὐ. πρεσβείᾳ.. ὑπερέχοντος [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 509b.]]

__II.5
in the concrete, the primary real, the substratum underlying all change and process in nature, applied by [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus]] to the atoms of Democritus, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [“fragment” 208; to τὰ ἁπλᾶ σώματα [prev. author] “Cael.” 298a29, compare “Metaphorical” 1017b10; πᾶσαι αἱ φυσικαὶ οὐ. ἢ σώματα ἢ μετὰ σωμάτων γίγνονται [prev. author] “Cael.” 298b3, +others; ταὐτὸν σῶμα καὶ οὐσίαν ὁριζόμενοι 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Sophista” 246a; but also, νοητὰ ἄττα καὶ ἀσώματα εἴδη.. τὴν ἀληθινὴν οὐ. [prev. work]b.]]

__II.6
in Logic, substance as the leading category, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Categoriae” 1b26, “Metaphorical” 1045b29]]; αἱ πρῶται οὐ. (individuals), αἱ δεύτεραι οὐ. (species and genera), [Refs [[prev. author] “Cat.” 2b5, 2a15 (but ὁ ἄνθρωπος καὶ ὁ ἵππος.. οὐκ ἔστιν οὐ. ἀλλὰ σύνολόν τι [prev. author] “Metaphorical” 1035b29, compare σύνθετος or συνθέτη οὐ. [prev. work] 1043a30, “de An.” 412a16); ἡ μὲν ψυχὴ οὐ. ἡ πρώτη, τὸ δὲ σῶμα ὕλη [prev. author] “Metaphorical” 1037a5; ἡ ψυχὴ οὐ. ὡς εἶδος [prev. author] “de An.” 412a19]]; ἡ οὐ. ἐντελέχεια[Refs [[prev. work] 21; [ψυχὴ] οὐ. τοῦ ἐμψύχου [prev. author] “Metaphorical” 1035b15]]; of the abstract objects of mathematics, μονὰς οὐ. ἄθετος, στιγμὴ δὲ οὐ. θετός [Refs [[prev. author] “APo.” 87a36.]]

__II.7
after [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus and 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus in various uses, as ἡ ἄποιος οὐ., ={ἡ ὕλη}, 4th-3rd c.BC: Zeno Citieus Stoicus 1.24]]; κατὰ οὐσίαν, opposed to κατὰ δύναμιν ἢ ἐνέργειαν, Polystr.p.12 W.; πᾶς νοῦς ἀμέριστός ἐστιν οὐ. [Refs 3rd c.AD+ [5th c.AD: Proclus Philosophus “Inst.” 171, compare 3rd c.AD: Plotinus Philosophus 2.4.5, 2.6.1, 4.7.8, 6.1.2, +others]]

__II.8
[Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Pythagoras Philosophus name for I, “Theologumena Arithmeticae” 6.]]

__III
name of a plaster, [Refs 6th c.AD+ [6th c.AD: Aëtius Medicus 15.15,45.]]

__IV
αἱ οὐ. fireresisting substances, Zos.Alch.p.168 [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Bacchylides Lyricus]]; of the four σώματα (copper, tin, lead, iron), [Refs 5th c.BC+ [2nd c.AD: Pseudo-Democritus Alchemista cited in [same work] p.167 5th c.BC: Bacchylides Lyricus]]

__V
in Magic, a material thing by which a connexion is established between the person to be acted upon and the supernatural agent, e.g. a hair, λαβὼν βελόνην διείρων τὴν οὐ. εἰς αὐτήν [Refs [“PMag.Par.” 1.2949, compare “PMag.Osl.” 1.73; mould from a tomb, “PMag.Par.” 1.435; κυνοκεφάλου οὐ.,.. κυνὸς οὐ., ={κόπρος} (compare 2460), [prev. work]2687, etc.]]

οὔτε
negative particle, related to μήτε as οὐ to μή,
and not, neither, nor: οὐδεὶς . . . οὔτε, Rev.5:4; οὐδὲ . . . οὔτε, Gal.1:12; οὔτε . . . καί, Jhn.4:11; after a question with μή interrog., Jas.3:12; οὔτε . . . οὔτε, neither . . . nor, Mat.6:20, Mrk.12:25, Jhn.4:21, Act.15:10, Rom.8:38-39, Gal.5:6, al
(AS)

---

LSJ / STEPBible (TFLSJ)
οὔτε,
adverb, (οὐ, τε) joining negative clauses, as τε joins positive, but rare in the simple sense and not, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 22.265 (variant), 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 3.155 (variant)]]; οὔτε γὰρ ἐκείνους διδόναι, Latin neque enim, [Refs [[prev. author] 1.3 (probably _falsa lectio_ for{οὐδὲ})]]; and occasionally in later writers, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Physica” 208a8, 2nd c.AD: Lucianus Sophista “Par.” 27, 53, etc.]]

__II
mostly repeated, οὔτε.., οὔτε.. neither.., nor.., Latin neque.., neque.., [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Homerus Epicus, etc.— 8th c.BC: Homerus Epicus frequently joins another Particle with the first or second οὔτε]], as οὔτ᾽ ἂρ.., οὔτε..; οὔτ᾽ ἂρ.., οὔτ᾽ ἂρ..; οὔτ᾽ ἄρ τε.., οὔτ᾽ ἄρα.. [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 5.89; οὔτ᾽ οὖν, see at {οὖν} 1; οὔτε.. οὖν.., οὔτ᾽ ἄρα.. 20.7]]; οὔτ᾽ ἄρ.., οὔτε τι.., or οὔτε τι.., οὔτε..,[Refs 8th c.BC+ [1.115, 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 1.202]]; so too οὔτε.., οὔτε μὴν.. [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 4.3.12; οὔτε.., οὔτ᾽ αὖ.., see below 3.]]

__II.2
frequently used to divide up a general negation into two or more parts, ὡς δ᾽ ἐν ὀνείρῳ οὐ δύναται φεύγοντα διώκειν, οὔτ᾽ ἂρ ὁ τὸν δύναται ὑποφεύγειν οὔθ᾽ ὁ διώκειν [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 22.200; thrice repeated, οὔ μοι Τρώων.. μέλει ἄλγος.., οὔτ᾽ αὐτῆς Ἑκάβης οὔτε Πριάμοιο ἄνακτος οὔτε κασιγνήτων 6.450; οὐκ ἔπειθεν οὔτε τοὺς στρατηγοὺς οὔτε τοὺς στρατιώτας 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 4.4]]: without a negative preceding, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 1.490, 2.202, etc.]]

__II.3
within one of the two clauses distinguished by οὔτε a subordinate part may be introduced by οὐδέ, οὔτε γὰρ ἐκ σκίλλης ῥόδα φύεται οὐδ᾽ ὑάκινθος (οὐθ᾽ codices), οὐ δέ ποτ᾽ ἐκ δούλης τέκνον ἐλευθέριον [Refs 6th c.BC+ [6th c.BC: Theognis Elegiacus 537; οὔτε.. ἀπέφηνεν οὐδὲ παρέσχηται μάρτυρας, οὔτ᾽ αὖ τὸν ἀριθμὸν.. ἐπανέφερεν 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 27.49: sometimes after several clauses distinguished by οὔτε the last is introduced emphatic by οὐδέ, οὔτε φάρμακα οὔτε καύσεις οὔτε τομαὶ οὐδ᾽ αὖ ἐπῳδαί]] nor yet incantations, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 426b, compare 499b (so μηδέ]] after clauses with μήτε, μήτε παιδεία μήτε δικαστήρια μήτε νόμοι μηδὲ ἀνάγκη μηδεμία [Refs [[prev. author] “Prt.” 327d)]]; so οὐδέ (μηδέ) may sometimes follow a single οὔτε (μήτε), οὐδέ ποτέ σφιν οὔτε τι πημανθῆναι ἔπι δέος, οὐδ᾽ ἀπολέσθαι neither to suffer misery, nor yet to die, see reading in [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 8.563, compare 5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “P.” 8.83, “I.” 2.44, 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Coloneus” 1139, 1141 (assuming variant), 1297 (conjecture), 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Apologia” 19d: in many of these places, however, the readings vary, and editors have altered οὐδέ into οὔτε]]; but this cannot be done in some cases, as οὔτ᾽ ἂν ὑπό γε ἑνὸς.. πάθοι, ἴσως δ᾽ οὐδὲ ὑπὸ πλεόνων [Refs 8th c.BC+ [[prev. author] “La.” 182b: so when οὔτε is followed by οὐδὲ μέν, 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 13.207]]; by οὐδὲ μήν, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 4.5.27]]; οὐδ᾽ αὖ, see above—But οὔτε (μήτε) cannot be used simply answering to οὐδέ (μηδέ), see at {μηδέ} [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus 2.]]

__II.4
οὔτε may be followed by a Posit. clause with τε, οὔτ᾽ αὐτὸς κτενέει, ἀπό τ᾽ ἄλλους πάντας ἐρύξει he both will not kill and will defend, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 24.156, compare 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Prometheus Vinctus” 246, 262, 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 5.49, 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 7.7.48, etc.]]: sometimes the negative is added after the τε, οὔτ᾽ ὦν.. καρπὸν ἔδωκαν ἄρουραι, δένδρεά τ᾽ οὐκ ἐθέλει.. φέρειν [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “N.” 11.40, compare 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Antigone” 763, 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Hippolytus” 302; κυάμους δὲ οὔτε τι μάλα σπείρουσι, τούς τε γενομένους οὔτε τρώγουσι οὔτε ἕψοντες πατέονται 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 2.37: the combination οὔτε.., καί]].. is uncertain in [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Iphigenia Taurica” 591]], but is found in later writers, as [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd c.AD: Lucianus Sophista “DMeretr.” 2.4, Chor.in “Rev.Phil.” 1877.218.]]

__II.5
οὔτε is frequently, by anacoluthon, followed not by a second οὔτε, but by some other Particle, as by οὐδέ, see above 3; by δέ alone, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 24.368, 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.108, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 388e, 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 6.3.16.]]

__II.5.b
in Poets, οὐ sometimes follows without any conjunctive Particle, οὐκ ἦν ἀλέξημ᾽ οὐδὲν οὔτε βρώσιμον, οὐ χριστόν, οὔτε πιστόν [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Prometheus Vinctus” 479]]; οὔτε πλινθυφεῖς δόμους.. ᾖσαν, οὐ ξυλουργίαν[Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. work] 450, compare 3rd c.BC: Theocritus Poeta Bucolicus 15.139f; οὔτε βλάστας.. πατρός, οὐ μητρὸς εἶχον 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Coloneus” 972, compare “Ant.” 249, 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Orestes” 41]]: so also in the Prose of [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus, ἐς ποταμὸν οὔτε ἐνουρέουσι οὔτε ἐμπτύουσι, οὐ χεῖρας ἐναπονίζονται, οὐδέ.. 1.138.]]

__II.5.c
in Poets also οὔτε is sometimes replaced by οὐ, οὐ νιφετὸς οὔτ᾽ ἂρ χειμὼν πολὺς οὔτε ποτ᾽ ὄμβρος [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 4.566; οὐ γὰρ ἂν εἰδείης ἀνδρὸς νόον οὔτε γυναικός 6th c.BC: Theognis Elegiacus 125 (uncertain reading), compare 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 1.115, 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 9.136, 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Persae” 588 (Lyric poetry, assuming variant), etc.]]

__II.5.d
the former οὔτε is sometimes omitted, ναυσὶ δ᾽ οὔτε πεζὸς ἰών [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “P.” 10.29]]; νόσοι δ᾽ οὔτε γῆρας[Refs 4th c.BC+ [[prev. work] 41; Πάρις γὰρ οὔτε συντελὴς πόλις 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Agamemnon” 532, compare “Ch.” 294; and see at {μήτε} 2.]]

__II.6
when οὔτε and μήτε correspond, each retains its proper sense, ἀναιδὴς οὔτ᾽ εἰμὶ μήτε γενοίμην neither am I shameless, nor may I become so, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 8.68, compare 4th c.BC: Aeschines Orator 3.128.]]

short_definition: this/he/she/it — οὗτος, αὕτη, τοῦτο, genitive, τούτου, ταύτης, τούτου,
deep_entry:
Abbott-Smith / STEPBible (TBESG)
οὗτος, αὕτη, τοῦτο, genitive, τούτου, ταύτης, τούτου,
[in LXX chiefly for זֹאת ,זֶה ;]
demonstr. pron. (related to ἐκεῖνος as hic to ille),
this;
__1. as subst., this one, he;
__(a) absol.: Mat.3:17, Mrk.9:7, Luk.7:44, 45, Jhn.1:15, Act.2:15, al.; expressing contempt (cl.), Mat.13:55, 56, Mrk.6:2, 3, Jhn.6:42, al.; εἰς τοῦτο, Mrk.1:38, Rom.14:9; μετὰ τοῦτο (ταῦτα; V. Westc. on Jhn.5:1), Jhn.2:12 11:7, al.;
__(b) epanaleptic (referring to what precedes): Mat.5:19, Mrk.3:35, Luk.9:48, Jhn.6:46, Rom.7:10, al.;
__(with) proleptic (referring to what follows): before ἵνα (Bl., §69, 6), Luk.1:43, Jhn.3:19 (and freq.) 15:8, Rom.14:9, al.; before ὅτι, Luk.10:11, Jhn.9:3o, Act.24:14, Rom.2:3, al.; ὅπως, Rom.9:17; ἐάν, Jhn.13:35;
__(d) special idioms: τοῦτο μὲν . . . τ. δέ (cl), partly . . . partly. Heb.10:33; καὶ τοῦτο (τοῦτον, ταῦτα), and that (him) too, Rom.13:11, 1Co.2:2, Heb.11:12; τοῦτ᾽ ἐστιν, Mat.27:46.
__2. As adj., with subst.;
__(a) with art.
__(α) before the art.: Mat.12:32, Mrk.9:29, Luk.7:44, Jhn.4:15, Rom.11:24, Rev.19:9, al.;
__(β) after the noun: Mat.3:9, Mrk.12:16, Luk.11:31, Jhn.4:13, Act.6:13, Rom.15:28, 1Co.1:20, Rev.2:24, al.;
__(b) with subst. anarth. (with predicative force; Bl., §49, 4): Luk.1:36 2:2 24:21, Jhn.2:11 4:54 21:14, 2Co.13:1.
(AS)

LSJ / STEPBible (TFLSJ)
οὗτος, αὕτη, τοῦτο,
genitive τούτου, ταύτης, τούτου, etc.: the dual feminine never in Attic dialect, see ὁ, ἡ, τό, [near the start]:—demonstrative pronoun, this, common from [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Homerus Epicus downwards]]

__A
ORIGIN and FORMS: οὗτος, αὕτη, τοῦτο probably arose from a reduplication of the demonstrative ὁ, ἡ, τό with insertion of -υ- (= Sanskrit Particle u), e.g. ταῦτα from τα-υ-τα: Doric dialect genitive singular feminine τούτας [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Philolaus Philosophus 11; _nominative_ _plural_ τοῦτοι, ταῦται 2nd c.AD: Apollonius Dyscolus Grammaticus “de Syntaxi;” 111.23: the former occurs 5th c.BC: Sophron Comicus 24, “GDI” 3045 B 6 (from Selinus), “SIG” 339.16 (Rhodes, 3rd c.BC)]], etc., the latter is uncertain in [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophron Comicus 97, certain in “SIG” 241 B 117 (Delph., 4th c.BC): in _Boeotian dialect_ all forms begin with οὑτ-]], as genitive singular neuter οὕτω [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [“Supp.epigram” 3.359.11 (3rd c.BC)]]; accusative singular feminine οὕταν [Refs 6th c.BC+ [6th c.BC: Corinna Lyrica “Supp.” 2.80; _accusative_ _plural_ _neuter_ οὗτα “SIG” 1185.20 (Tanagra, 3rd c.BC), etc.: _genitive_ _plural_ _feminine_ _Attic dialect_ τούτων, Cretan dialect ταυτᾶν “Leg.Gort.” 5.19; _neuter_ ταύτων “Michel” 1334.10 (Elis, 4th c.BC).—In _Ionic dialect_ sometimes written ταότην, ταο̄τα, “SIG” 283.19 (Chios, 4th c.BC), 46.7 (Halic., 5th c.BC), +others]] —In _Attic dialect_ οὗτος was frequently strengthened by the _demonstrative_ -ί, οὑτοσί, αὑτηί, τουτί, _genitive_ τουτουί, _dative_ τουτῳί, _accusative_ τουτονί; plural nominative οὑτοιί, neuter ταυτί, etc., this man here: sometimes a Particle is inserted between the pronoun and -ί, as αὑτηγί for αὑτηί γε, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Acharnenses” 784]]; τουτογί for τουτί γε, [Refs [[prev. author] “V.” 781, “Av.” 894, +others]]; ταυταγί for ταυτί γε, [Refs [[prev. author] “Eq.” 492, “Pax” 1057, +others]]; τουτοδί for τουτὶ δέ, [Refs [[prev. author] “Pl.” 227]]; τουτουμενί for τουτουὶ μέν, [Refs [[prev. author] “Ra.” 965.]] —In codices the ν ἐφελκυστικόν is sometimes added in the forms οὑτοσίν, οὑτωσίν, and οὑτοσίν is said to be Attic dialect by [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd c.AD: Apollonius Dyscolus Grammaticus “de Pronominibus;” 59.24, 82.11]]. [This ι is always long, and a long vowel or diphthong before it becomes short, as αὑτη?~Xί, τουτω?~Xί, οὑτοῐί, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Nubes” 201, “Pl.” 44, “Ach.” 40, etc.]]]

__B
USAGE in regard to CONCOR[Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator οὗτος]] is frequently used as a pronoun substantive: hence neuter is followed by genitive, κατὰ τοῦτο τῆς ἀκροπόλιος [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.84; εἰς τοῦθ᾽ ὕβρεως ἐλήλυθεν 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 4.37; εἰς τοῦθ᾽ ἥκεις μανίας [prev. author] 36.48; ταῦτα τῶν μαθημάτων 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Euthydemus” 278b: but quite as frequently as]] adjective, in which case its substantive commonly takes the Article, οὗτος ὁ ἀνήρ or ὁ ἀνὴρ οὗτος.—But the Article is absent,

__B.1
always in Epic dialect Poets (except [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 18.114), οὗτος ἀνήρ 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 14.471, 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 1.406, etc.]]: sometimes also in Trag., [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Persae” 122 (Lyric poetry), 495, 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Philoctetes” 406, “OC” 471, 1177: once in an Inscription, τοπεῖα: τούτων τὰ ἡμίσεα τοπείων “IG” 22.1622.135 (4th c.BC).]]

__B.2
sometimes when the Noun is so specified that the Article is not needed, ἐς γῆν ταύτην.., ἥντινα νῦν Σκύθαι νέμονται [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 4.8; ταύτας ἃς οἱ πατέρες παρέδοσαν μελέτας 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 1.85, compare 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 449d, etc.; πατὴρ σὸς οὗτος, ὃν θρηνεῖς ἀεί 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Electra” 530.]]

__B.3
when οὗτος is used in local sense, here, see below with [Refs [1.5.]]

__B.4
when the Noun with which οὗτος agrees stands as its Predicate, αὕτη γὰρ ἦν σοι πρόφασις [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Philoctetes” 1034]]; δικαστοῦ αὕτη ἀρετή [ἐστι] [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Apologia” 18a: this exception extends to cases in which the Predicate is not so distinctly separated from the Subject, αἰτίαι μὲν αὗται προυγεγένηντο]] these were the grievances which already existed, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 1.66]]; ταύτην φήμην παρέδοσαν this was the report which.., [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Philebus” 16c: frequently with a _superlative_, κίνησις αὕτη μεγίστη δὴ.. ἐγένετο]] this was notably the greatest movement which.., [NT+5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 1.1, compare 3.113: with πρῶτος [prev. author] 1.55, 98, 6.31, NT.Luke.2.2.]]

__B.5
when 3rd pers. is used for 2nd pers. to express contempt, οὗτος ἀνήρ, οὑτοσὶ ἀνήρ, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Gorgias” 467b, 489b, etc.]]

__B.II
though οὗτος usually agrees with the Noun that serves as Predicate, it is not rare to find it in the neuter, μανία δὲ καὶ τοῦτ᾽ ἐστί [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Bacchae” 305; τοῦτο γάρ εἰσι.. εὔθυναι 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 19.82, etc.]]: and in plural, οὐκ ἔστι ταῦτα ἀρχή [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aeschines Orator 3.13; ταῦτ᾽ ἐστὶν ὁ προδότης [prev. author] 2.166]]: so with an explanatory clause added, τοῦτο γάρ ἐστιν ὁ συκοφάντης, αἰτιᾶσθαι μὲν πάντα ἐξελέγξαι δὲ μηδέν [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 57.34.]]

__B.II.2
so also with a Noun in apposition, τούτοισιν μὲν ταῦτα μέλει, κίθαρις καὶ ἀοιδή [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 1.159; τούτου τιμῶμαι, ἐν πρυτανείῳ σιτήσεως 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Apologia” 36e, compare 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Fragmenta” 323.3, etc.]]

__B.II.3
the neuter also may refer to a masculine or feminine Noun, καρπὸν φορέει κυάμῳ ἴσον: τοῦτο ἐπεὰν γένηται πέπον κτλ. [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 4.23, compare 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 1.5.10, etc.]]

__B.II.4
the neuter is also used of classes of persons, μελιτοπῶλαι καὶ τυροπῶλαι: τοῦτο δ᾽ εἰς ἕν ἐστι συγκεκυφός [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Equites” 854, compare 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Leges” 711a]]; or of an abstract fact, οὐκ Ἰοφῶν ζ;—τοῦτο γάρ τοι καὶ μόνον ἔτ᾽ ἐστὶ λοιπὸν ἀγαθόν [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Ranae” 73.]]

__B.III
with Prons.,

__B.III.1
personal, οὗτος σύ, in local sense, see below

__B.III.2
interrogative, τί τοῦτ᾽ ἔλεξα; what is this that.. ? [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Philoctetes” 1173 (Lyric poetry), compare “Ant.” 7]]; ποίοισι τούτοι; for ποῖά ἐστι ταῦτα οἷς [ἔχεις ἐλπίδα]; [Refs [[prev. author] “OC” 388, compare “Ant.” 1049]]; Νέστορ᾽ ἔρειο ὅν τινα τοῦτον ἄγει whom he brings here, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 11.612.]]

__B.III.3
with οἷος, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 20.377, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Phaedo” 61c.]]

__B.III.4
possessive, πατὴρ σὸς οὗτος this father of thine, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Electra” 530, compare 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 7.3.30.]]

__B.III.5
demonstrative, οὗτος ἐκεῖνος, τὸν σὺ ζητέεις, where ἐκεῖνος is the Predicate, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.32; τοῦτ᾽ ἔστ᾽ ἐκεῖνο 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Helena” 622, compare “Or.” 804; αὐτὸ τοῦτο, see at {αὐτός} I.7]]; τοῦτον τὸν αὐτὸν ἄνδρα this same man, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Philoctetes” 128.]]

__B.III.5.b
exceptionally, Διφίλου οὗτος ὅδ᾽ ἐστὶ τύπος [Refs [“IG” 12(5).300 (from Paros).]]

__B.III.6
ἄλλος τις οὗτος ἀνέστη another man here, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 20.380.]]

__B.IV
with Numerals, τέθνηκε ταῦτα τρία ἔτη these three years, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Lysias Orator 7.10 codices]]; [στρατείαν] ἑνδέκατον μῆνα τουτονὶ ποιεῖται for these eleven months, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 8.2, compare 3.4; τριακοστὴν ταύτην ἡμέραν 4th-3rd c.BC: Menander Comicus “Ἐπιτρέποντες” 27; ταύτας τριάκοντα μνᾶς 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 27.23, compare 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Gorgias” 463b, etc.]]

__C
SIGNIFICATION AND SPECIAL IDIOMS:

__C.I
this, to designate the nearer, opposed to ἐκεῖνος, that, the more remote, ταῦτα, like τὰ ἐνταῦθα, things round and about us, earthly things, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Phaedo” 75e (variant)]]; compare ὅδε [near the start]: but οὗτος sometimes indicates that which is not really nearest, but most important, δεῖ.. τὸ βέλτιστον ἀεί, μὴ τὸ ῥᾷστον λέγειν: ἐπὶ ἐκεῖνο μὲν γὰρ ἡ φύσις αὐτὴ βαδιεῖται, ἐπὶ τοῦτο δὲ κτλ. [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 8.72, compare 51.3 and 18.]]

__C.I.2
when, of two things, one precedes and the other follows, ὅδε properly refers to what follows, οὗτος to what precedes, οὐκ ἔστι σοι ταῦτ᾽, ἀλλά σοι τάδ᾽ ἔστι [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Coloneus” 787, compare ὅδε III. 2: frequently, however, where there are not two things, οὗτος]] refers to what follows, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 13.377, 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 2.306, etc.]]; οὔκουν.. τοῦτο γιγνώσκεις, ὅτι..; [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Prometheus Vinctus” 379, etc.]]

__C.I.3
οὗτος is used emphatic, generally in contempt, while ἐκεῖνος denotes praise, ὁ πάντ᾽ ἄναλκις οὗτος, i.e. Aegisthus, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Electra” 301; τούτους τοὺς συκοφάντας 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Crito” 45a; so 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator “de Coron.” uses οὗτος of Aeschines, ἐκεῖνος]] of Philip; but οὗτος is used of Philip, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 2.15, 4.3.]]

__C.I.3.b
of what is familiar, τούτους τοὺς πολυτελεῖς χιτῶνας, of the Persians, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 1.5.8; οἱ τὰς τελετὰς.. οὗτοι καταστήσαντες 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Phaedo” 69c, compare “Men.” 80a]]; τὸ θυλακῶδες τοῦτο the familiar bag-like thing, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-3rd c.BC: Theophrastus Philosophus “Historia Plantarum” 3.7.3, compare 3.18.11, 4.7.1; οἱ τὰς κόρας ταύτας ὠνούμενοι τοῖς παισίν 1st-2nd c.AD: Dio Chrysostomus Sophista 31.153.]]

__C.I.4
in Attic dialect law-language, οὗτος is commonly applied to the opponent, whether plaintiff (as in [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aeschines Orator 2.130)]] or defendant (as in [Refs [[prev. author] 1.1)]]; so, in the political speeches of [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator, οὗτοι]] are the opposite party, [Refs [4.1, 8.7]], etc.; but in the forensic speeches, οὗτοι frequently means the judges, the court, [Refs [21.134, 36.47.]]

__C.I.5
much like an adverb, in local sense (compare ὅδε [near the start]), τίς δ᾽ οὗτος κατὰ νῆας.. ἔρχεα; who art thou here that comest.. ? [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 10.82]]; frequently in Attic dialect, τίς οὑτοσ; who's this here? [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Acharnenses” 1048]]; πολλὰ ὁρῶ ταῦτα πρόβατα I see many sheep here, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 3.5.9 (as variant): with _pronoun_ of 2 _person_, οὗτος σύ]] ho you! you there! [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Tyrannus” 532, 1121, 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Hecuba” 1280, etc.: and then οὗτος alone like a _vocative_, οὗτος, τί ποιεῖ; 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Supplices” 911,compare 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Ajax” 71, 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Alcestis” 773, 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Equites” 240, “Nu.” 220, +others]]: with a proper name, ὦ οὗτος, Αἴας [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Ajax” 89; ὦ οὗτος οὗτος, Οἰδίπους [prev. author] “OC” 1627, compare 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Vespae” 1364: with _vocative_, βέντισθ᾽ οὗτος 3rd c.BC: Theocritus Poeta Bucolicus 5.76:—the _feminine_ is rarer, αὕτη 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Medea” 922; αὕτη σύ 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Thesmophoriazusae” 610.]] —This phrase mostly implies anger, impatience, or scorn.

__C.II
simply as antecedent to ὅς, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 2.40, 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Tyrannus” 1180, etc.: frequently following _relative_ clause, ἅ γ᾽ ἔλαβες,.. μεθεῖναι ταῦτα [prev. author] “Ph.” 1247, compare 1319, “Ant.” 183, 203, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Gorgias” 469c.]]

__C.III
= τοιοῦτος, οὗτος ἐγὼ ταχυτᾶτι [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “O.” 4.26; σὺ τοίνυν οὗτος εὑρέθης 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 18.282, compare 173.]]

__C.IV
after a parenthesis, the Subject, though already named, is frequently emphatic repeated by οὗτος, οὐδὲ γὰρ οὐδὲ Ἀριστέης.., οὐδὲ οὗτος προσωτέρω.. ἔφησε ἀπικέσθαι [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 4.16, compare 81 (assuming variant), 1.146, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Phaedo” 107d, etc.]]

__C.V
καὶ οὗτος is added to heighten the force of a previous word, ξυνεστῶτες.. ναυτικῷ ἀγῶνι, καὶ τούτῳ πρὸς Ἀθηναίους [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 4.55, compare 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.147, 6.11, etc.; so οὐδὲ τούτου 4th c.BC: Aeschines Orator 2.100]]; see infr. VIII.2.

__C.VI
repeated, where for the second we should merely say he or it, τοῖσιν τούτου τοῦτον μέλεσιν.. κελαδοῦντες [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Ranae” 1526, compare 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Laches” 200d.]]

__C.VII
ταῦτα is used in some special phrases,

__C.VII.1
ταῦτ᾽, ὦ δέσποτα yes Sir (i. e. ἔστι ταῦτα, ταῦτα δράσω, etc.), [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Vespae” 142, “Pax” 275, compare “Eq.” III; so ταῦτα δή [prev. author] “Ach.” 815; ταῦτά νυν [prev. author] “V.” 1008]]; so also ἦν ταῦτα even so, true, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Phoenissae” 417.]]

__C.VII.2
ταῦτα μὲν δὴ ὑπάρξει so it shall be, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Phaedo” 78a.]]

__C.VII.3
καὶ ταῦτα μὲν δὴ ταῦτα so much for that, frequently in Attic dialect, as [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Symposium” 220c.]]

__C.VII.4
ταῦτα at end of a formula in epitaphs, etc., probably short for ταῦτα οὕτως ἔχει or ὁ βίος ταῦτά ἐστιν, e.g. οὐδὶς (= -εὶς) ἀθάνατος: ταῦτα [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [“IG” 14.420; Προκόπι ταῦτα [prev. work]1824; χαίρεται (= -τε) ταῦτα [prev. work]1479, etc.: similarly perhaps in a letter, ἂμ μὴ πέμψῃς, οὐ μὴ φάγω, οὐ μὴ πείνω. ταῦτα “POxy.” 119.15 (2nd-3rd c.AD).]]

__C.VIII
Adverbial usages:

__C.VIII.1
ταῦταabsolutely, therefore, that is why.., [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 11.694; ταῦτ᾽ ἄρα 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Acharnenses” 90, “Nu.” 319, 335, 394, +others, 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Symposium” 4.55; ταῦτα δή 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Persae” 159, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Symposium” 174a; ταῦτ᾽ οὖν 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Trachiniae” 550, 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Vespae” 1358, etc.]]; αὐτὰ ταῦτα ἥκω, ἵνα.. [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Protagoras” 310e: τοῦτο]] is rare in this sense, τοῦτ᾽ ἀφικόμην, ὅπως.. εὖ πράξαιμί τι [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Tyrannus” 1005]]; αὐτὸ γὰρ τοῦτο just because of this, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Symposium” 204a.]]

__C.VIII.1.b
πρὸς ταῦτα so then, therefore, properly used in indignant defiance, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Prometheus Vinctus” 992, 1043, 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Ajax” 971, 1115, 1313, “OT” 426, “OC” 455, etc.]]

__C.VIII.2
καὶ ταῦτα, adding a circumstance heightening the force of what has been said, and that, ἄνδρα γενναῖον θανεῖν, καὶ ταῦτα πρὸς γυναικός [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Eumenides” 627]]: but mostly with a participle, ὅς γ᾽ ἐξέλυσας ἄστυ.., καὶ ταῦθ᾽ ὑφ᾽ ἡμῶν οὐδὲν ἐξειδὼς πλέον [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Tyrannus” 37, compare 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Ranae” 704, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Phaedrus” 241e, etc.]]; or with a participle omitted, ἥτις.. τὴν τεκοῦσαν ὕβρισεν, καὶ ταῦτα τηλικοῦτος (i.e. οὖσα) [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Electra” 614; so καὶ ταῦτα μέντοι 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Eryxias” 400b.]]

__C.VIII.2.b
καὶ ταῦτα anyhow, no matter what happens (or happened), ἐπεχείρησας, οὐδὲν ὢν καὶ ταῦτα you tried, but were no good anyhow, i.e. try as you might, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [[prev. author] “R.” 341c, compare 4th c.BC: Diodorus Comicus 3.5.]]

__C.VIII.3
τοῦτο μέν.., τοῦτο δέ.. on the one hand.., on the other.., partly.., partly.., very frequently in [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus, as 1.161, +others]]; τοῦτο μέν is sometimes answered by δέ only,[Refs 5th c.BC+ [4.76, 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Ajax” 670, “OC” 440]]; by δὲ αὖ, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 7.176]]; by ἔπειτα δέ, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Antigone” 61]]; by ἀλλά, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 22.13]]; by εἶτα, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Philoctetes” 1345]]; by τοῦτ᾽ αὖθις, [Refs [[prev. author] “Ant.” 165.]]

__C.VIII.4
dative feminine ταύτῃ,

__C.VIII.4.a
on this spot, here, ταύτῃ μὲν.., τῇδε δ᾽ αὖ.. [Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. author] “Ph.” 1331; ἀλλ᾽ ἐὰν ταύτῃ γε νικᾷ, ταυτῃὶ πεπλήξεται 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Equites” 271, compare “Th.” 1221.]]

__C.VIII.4.b
in this point, herein, μηδὲν ταύτῃ γε κομήσῃς [Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. author] “Pl.” 572, compare 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Hiero” 7.12, etc.]]

__C.VIII.4.c
in this way, thus, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Prometheus Vinctus” 191, 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Coloneus” 1300, etc.; οὐ.. ταῦτ᾽ ἐστί πω ταύτῃ 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Equites” 843; ἀλλ᾽ οὔτι ταύτῃ ταῦτα 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Medea” 365, compare 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Prometheus Vinctus” 511: antecedent to ὥσπερ, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 330c]]; to ὅπῃ, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 8.3.2; οὕτω τε καὶ ταύτῃ γίγνοιτο 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Leges” 681d; καὶ οὕτω καὶ ταύτῃ ἂν ἔχοι [prev. work] 714d]]; ταύτῃ καλεῖσθαι, etc., like οὕτω κ., [Refs 5th c.BC+ [Scholia 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Symposium” 215b.]]

__C.VIII.5
ἐκ τούτου or τούτων thereupon, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Historia Graeca (Hellenica)” 3.1.6, “Oec.” 2.1]]; therefore, [Refs [[prev. author] “An.” 3.3.5.]]

__C.VIII.6
ἐν τούτῳ in that case, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 440c.]]

__C.VIII.6.b
in the meantime, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.126, 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 3.72, 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Memorabilia” 2.1.27.]]

__C.VIII.7
πρὸς τούτοις (-οισι) besides, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 2.51, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Protagoras” 326a, 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Memorabilia” 2.4.4, 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Plutus” 540.]]

deep_entry:
Abbott-Smith / STEPBible (TBESG)
οὕτως, rarely (Bl., §5, 4; WH, App., 146f.) οὕτω, adv.
(οὗτος), [in LXX chiefly for כֵּן ;]
in this way, so, thus;
__1. referring to what precedes: Mat.5:16 6:30, Mrk.10:43 14:59, Luk.1:25 2:48 15:7, Jhn.3:8, Rom.1:15, 1Co.8:12, al.; οὕτως καί, Mat.17:12, Mrk.13:29, al.; pleonastically, resuming a ptcp. (cl.; see Bl., §74, 6), Act.20:11 27:17.
__2. Referring to what follows: Mat.1:18 6:9, Luk.19:31, Jhn.21:1, 1Pe.2:15; bef. quotations from OT, Mat.2:5, Act.7:6, 1Co.15:45, Heb.4:4.
__3. C. adj. (marking intensity): Heb.12:21, Rev.16:18; similarly with adv., Gal.1:6 (cl.).
__4. As a predicate (Bl., §76, 1): Mat.1:18 9:33, Mrk.2:1, 2 4:26, Rom.4:18 9:20, I Pe  2:15; οὕ ἔχειν (Lat. sic or ita se habere), Act.7:1, al.; ἐκαθέζετο (as he was, without delay or preparation), Jhn.4:6.
__5. In comparison, with correlative adv.: καθάπερ . . . οὕ., Rom.12:4, 5 al.; καθὼς . . . οὕ., Luk.11:30, al.; οὕ. . . . καθώς, Luk.24:24, al.; ὡς . . . οὕ., Rom.5:15, al.; οὕ . . . ὡς, Mrk.4:26, al; ὥσπερ . . . οὕ., Mat.12:40, al.; οὕ. . . . οὕ., 1Co.7:7.
(AS)

LSJ / STEPBible (TFLSJ)
οὕτως,
and before a consonant οὕτω (but sometimes οὕτως before a consonant, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Aves” 63, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Gorgias” 522c, 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 23.34, “PPetr.” 2p.20 (3rd c.BC), “PTeb.” 124.18 (2nd c.BC), etc.]], and οὕτω before a vowel is found in Epic dialect Poets and _Ionic dialect_ Prose, see near the end); in Attic dialect strengthened

__A
οὑτωσί [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Gorgias” 503d, etc.; οὑτωσίν Hdn.Gr. 1.509.2]]; see at {οὗτος Α}:— adverb of οὗτος, in this way or manner, so, thus: οὕτως is antecedent to ὡς, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 4.178, 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 4.148, etc.]]; in Attic dialect also οὕτως ὥσπερ [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Trachiniae” 475, etc.]]; ὥσπερ.., οὕτω καὶ.. [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 1.4.21]]; ὡσαύτως, ὥσπερ.., οὕτω καὶ.. [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Ion” 534a]]; also οὕτως, ὅπως.. [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Trachiniae” 330, 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 1.1.2]]; poetry also ὥστε.., οὕτω δὲ.. [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Trachiniae” 116 (Lyric poetry): οὕτως]] is frequently left out after ὡς, ὡς ἔδοξεν αὐτοῖς, καὶ ἐποίουν ταῦτα [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 8.1, compare 3rd c.BC: Theocritus Poeta Bucolicus 7.45f —In Prose, the _relative_ _pronoun_ frequently follows instead of ὥστε, see infr. III: when two modes are opposed, they are frequently expressed by οὕτω and ἐκείνως, τότε μὲν ἐκείνως, νῦν δ᾽ οὕτω 5th-6th c.BC: Isocrates Orator 12.172; οὕτω ῥᾷον ἢ 'κείνως 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 370a, etc.]] —Sts. οὕτω or -ως refers to what follows, thus, as follows, οὕτω χρὴ ποιεῖν: ἐὰν.. [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 2.2.2; οὑτωσὶ δὲ λογίζεσθε 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 18.244; οὕτω πως ὑπείληφα [prev. work]269; οὑτωσί πως]] followed by a quotation, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Apologia” 28c]]; καὶ οὕτως even so, even on this supposition, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 1.10; οὐδ᾽ οὕτως [prev. author] 2.76, 6.89, 5th c.BC: Lysias Orator 1.14, variant in 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 4.8.3: strengthened οὕτω δή 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 2.158; οὕτω γὰρ δή τοι 15.201]]; οὕτω δή τι, see infr. III; also οὕτω που so I ween,[Refs 8th c.BC+ [2.116, 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 9.262, etc.; οὕτω πῃ 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 24.373]]; ὣς ὁ μὲν οὕτως ἐστὶ σόος so in this way is he saved, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 19.300:]] —Phrases:

__A.1
οὕτω δὴ ἔσται so it shall be, ratifying what goes before,[Refs [11.348; ἔσσεται οὕτως 16.31, etc.: in Prose οὕτως]] alone in answers, even so, just so, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Oeconomicus” 1.9; so ἢ οὐχ οὕτω;—οὕτω μὲν οὖν 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 551b, etc.]]

__A.2
emphatic with the imperative, just, without more ado, ἔρρ᾽ οὕτως [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 22.498, compare 21.184, 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 6.218, 17.447]]; but, οὕτω νῦν ἀπόπεμπε as you say, [Refs [5.146.]]

__A.3
in wishes or prayers, so, i.e. if you grant my prayer, οὕτως ἔρως σοι.. τελεσφόρος γένοιτο [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Medea” 714; οὕτω τί σοι δοίησαν αἱ Μοῦσαι.. τοῦτον.. δεῖρον 3rd c.BC: Herodas Mimographus 3.1]]; also in protestations, so, i.e. only if what I say is true, οὕτως ὀναίμην τῶν τέκνων, μισῶ τὸν ἄνδρ᾽ (as in Engl., so help me God, so mote I thrive, etc.) [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Thesmophoriazusae” 469, compare 4th-3rd c.BC: Menander Comicus “Ἐπιτρέποντες” 530, 3rd c.BC: Herodas Mimographus 7. 25, 5th c.AD: Aristaenetus Rhetor 2.13]]; οὕτω.. νομιζοίμην σοφός, ὡς.. [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Nubes” 520.]]

__A.4
in colloquial phrase, beginning a story, οὕτω ποτ᾽ ἦν μῦς καὶ γαλῆ there were once on a time.., [Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. author] “V.” 1182; οὕτως ἦν νεανίσκος [prev. author] “Lys.” 785; ἦν οὕτω δὴ παῖς 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Phaedrus” 237b.]]

__A.5
οὕτω with genitive, τούτων μὲν οὕτω so much for this, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Agamemnon” 950]]; οὕτω καὶ τῶν οἰκονομικῶν (variant{τῷ -κῷ}) so also of.., [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Politica” 1253b27]]; ὥσπερ Χαλκὶς.. τῆς Εὐβοίας.. κεῖται, οὕτω Χερρονήσου.. ἡ Καρδιανῶν πόλις as Chalcis in respect of Euboea.., so Cardia in respect of the Chersonese, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 23.182]]; so οὕτως ἔχω τινός or περί τινος, see at {ἔχω} (A) [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Bacchylides Lyricus II. 2; also for εἰς τοῦτο, οὕτω δὲ τάρβους.. ἀφικόμην 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Phoenissae” 361 codices (uncertain reading).]]

__A.6
ὁ οὕτω καλούμενος, ὀνομαζόμενος, the so-called.., τῶν Ῥιπαίων οὕτω καλουμένων [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd-3rd c.AD: Aelianus “De Natura Animalium - Ar.Byzantine Epit.” 11.1; τοῦ καὶ ὀνομασθέντος οὕτω ῥήτορος 2nd c.AD: Hermogenes Rhetor “περὶ ἰδεῶν” 2.11]]; Ποταμὸς δῆμος οὕτω καλούμενος P., a deme of that name, [Refs 1st c.BC+ [1st c.BC-1st c.AD: Strabo Geographus 9.1.22.]]

__A.7
οὕτω, or οὕτω δή, frequently introduces the apodosis after a protasis, ἐπειδὴ περιελήλυθε ὁ πόλεμος.., οὕτω δὴ Γέλωνος μνῆστις γέγονε [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 7.158, compare 150, 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 1.131, 2.12, 19, etc.]]; especially after parts., ἐν κλιβάνῳ πνίξαντες, οὕτω τρώγουσι, i.e. ἐπειδὰν πνίξωσιν, οὕτω.., [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 2.92, compare 100; also οὕτω δή [prev. author] 7.174; τὰ ἄλλα καταστρεψάμενος, οὕτως.. στρατεῦσαι ὕστερον 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 3.96; εἰς τὰ σκληρότατα ἀποβλέποντες, οὕτως ἂν μᾶλλον συννοήσαιμεν 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Philebus” 44e, compare “Grg.” 457d, 507e, “Ap.” 29b; so ἔπειτα οὕτως 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 7.1.4]]: so also after the genitive absolutely, ὡς.. τῶν ἡγεμόνων ὑμῖν μὴ μεμπτῶν γεγενημένων, οὕτω τὴν γνώμην ἔχετε [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 7.15, compare 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 1.6.11, “An.” 1.3.6, etc.]]

__A.II
sometimes in a really inferential sense, as we say so for therefore, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Antigone” 677; οὕτω δή 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Phaedo” 61b, etc.]]

__A.III
to such an extent, so, so much, so very, so excessively, καλὸς οὕτω [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 3.169]]; πρυμνόθεν οὕτως so entirely, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Septem contra Thebas” 1061 (_anapaest meter_), compare 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 2.47, 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 1.3.8; οὕτως τι 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Aves” 63: frequently followed by ὡς or ὥστε, 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.32, 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 7.4.3, etc.: sometimes the _relative_ ὅς takes the place of ὥστε, κρήνη οὕτω δή τι ἐοῦσα πικρή, ἣ.. κιρνᾷ (i. e. ὥστε κιρνᾶν) 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 4.52; οὐκ ἔστιν οὕτω μῶρος ὃς θανεῖν ἐρᾷ 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Antigone” 220]]; τίς δ᾽ οὕτως ἄνους ὃς.. ; [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Acharnenses” 736, compare 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 8.44]]; also δυσχείμερος αὕτη ἡ.. χώρη οὕτω δή τί ἐστι, ἔνθα (i. e. ὥστε ἐνταῦθα) τοὺς μὲν ὀκτὼ τῶν μηνῶν ἀφόρητος οἷος γίνεται κρυμός [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 4.28: sometimes no connecting Particle is used, αἱ [κεφαλαὶ] οὕτω δή τι ἰσχυραί, μόγις ἂν λίθῳ παίσας διαρρήξειας]] so excessively hard, you could scarcely break them, [Refs [[prev. author] 3.12.]]

__A.III.2
with superlative adjective, τῆς οὕτω μεγίστης ἐγχειρήσεως ἀποσφαλείς [Refs 1st c.BC+ [1st c.BC: Zosimus Epigrammaticus 5.19.]]

__A.IV
sometimes, like{αὔτως}, with a diminishing power, so, merely so, simply, in [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Homerus Epicus always μὰψ οὕτω, 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 2.120 (for without μάψ he always uses αὔτως),compare 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.5; μὴ διὰ μέθης.. ἀλλ᾽ οὕτω πίνοντας πρὸς ἡδονήν 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Symposium” 176e, compare “Grg.” 494e, “Phdr.” 235c, “Tht.” 147c, 158b, 4th-3rd c.BC: Theophrastus Philosophus “de Odoribus” 67, etc.; ἐν συνουσίᾳ καὶ διατριβῇ οὕτως ἰδίᾳ 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 21.71, compare 1.20]]; τοὺς ὀδόντας.. οὕτως ἂν τοῖς δακτύλοις αὐτοῖς.. παρατρίβειν, i.e. without a dentifrice, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [Diocl. fragment 141; so οὕτω γε ἀπὸ στόματος 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Theaetetus” 142d; οὕτω ποτέ [prev. author] “Ly.” 216c; οὕτω πως 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 1.20]]; also, off-hand, at once, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Gorgias” 464b, etc.; ἁπλῶς οὕτως [prev. author] “Lg.” 633c]]; ἀλλ᾽ οὕτως ἄπει ; so, without a word more.. ? [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Philoctetes” 1067]]; ἢ στραφεὶς οὕτως ἴω ; [Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. author] “Ant.” 315, compare 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Heraclidae” 374 (Lyric poetry); ἐφεξῆς οὑτωσὶ καθεζόμενος 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 21.119]]; ὡς οὕτω γ᾽ ἀκοῦσαι at first hearing, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Euthyphro” 3b; so ὥς γε οὑτωσὶ ἀκοῦσαι [prev. author] “Ly.” 216a; ἀκούειν μὲν οὕτως ἁπλῶς [prev. author] “Phlb.” 12c]]; οὐ.. οὕτως ἄπει, = impune, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Alcestis” 680.]]

__A.V
as Hebraism, οὕτως, = such a person (thing), οὕτως οὐδέποτε εἴδαμεν [LXX+NT [NT.Mark.2.12, cf. LXX.Gen.29.26, NT.Matt.9.33, NT.Luke.2.48, +others]]

__B
Position of οὕτω or οὕτως, mostly before the word which it limits, but in Poets sometimes after, καλὸς οὕτω [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 3.169; οὐδέ τι λίην οὕτω νώνυμός ἐστιν 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 13.239]]; ἔρημος οὕτω, ἄγαν οὕτω, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Philoctetes” 487, 598]]: rarely at the end of a clause, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 18.255, 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 7.170 (uncertain reading)]]: sometimes separated from the word which it limits, οὕτως ἔχει τι δεινόν ; [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Philoctetes” 104; οὕτως ἐπὶ δεινὰς ἁρπαγάς 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 391d, compare 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 2.11]]; οὕτω δ᾽ ἦν ὁ Φίλιππος ἐν φόβῳ.., ὥστε.. [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 18.33.]]

__C
Prosody. The last syllable of οὕτω is short before a vowel in [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 3.169, 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 3.315]]. The ι of οὑτωσί is always long, see at {οὗτος} [near the start]

Abbott-Smith / STEPBible (TBESG)
οὐχί
strengthened form of οὐ,
not;
__(a) in neg. sentences, not, not at all: Luk.1:60 12:51, Jhn.13:10, al.;
__(b) more frequently in questions where an affirm. ans. is expected (Lat. nonne) : Mat.5:46-47, Luk.6:39, Jhn.11:9, al.

LSJ / STEPBible (TFLSJ)
Included with:  οὐ,
the negative of fact and statement, as μή of will and thought; οὐ denies, μή rejects; οὐ is absolute, μή relative; οὐ objective, μή subjective. —The same differences hold for all compounds of οὐ and μή, and some examples of οὐδέ and οὐδείς are included below.—As to the Form, see infr. G. USAG[Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus]]

__I
as the negative of single words,

__II
as the negative of the sentence.

__I
οὐ adhering to single words so as to form a quasi-compound with them:—with Verbs: οὐ δίδωμι withhold, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 24.296]]; οὐκ εἰῶ prevent, [Refs [2.132, 4.55, +others]]; οὐκ ἐθέλω refuse, [Refs [1.112, 3.289, +others]]; οὔ φημι deny, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [7.393, 23.668, +others (In most of these uses μή can replace οὐ when the _construction_ requires it, e.g. εἰ μή φησι ταῦτα ἀληθῆ εἶναι 4th c.BC: Lycurgus Orator 34]]; but sometimes οὐ is retained, εἰ δ᾽ ἂν.. οὐκ ἐθέλωσιν [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 3.289; εἰ δέ κ᾽.. ου᾽κ εἰῶσι 20.139; ἐὰν οὐ φάσκῃ 5th c.BC: Lysias Orator 13.76]]; ἐάντε.. οὐ (variant{μή}) φῆτε ἐάντε φῆτε [Refs 8th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Apologia” 25b):—with Participles: οὐκ ἐθέλων 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 4.224, 300, 6.165, etc.:— with Adjectives: οὐκ ἀέκοντε 5.366, 768, +others; οὐ πολλήν 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 6.7, etc.:— with Adverbs: οὐχ ἥκιστα [prev. author] 1.68, etc.: rarely with Verbal Nouns (see. below 11.10).]] —On the use of οὐ in contrasts, see below [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Bacchylides Lyricus]]

__II
as negativing the whole sentence,

__II.1
οὐ is frequently used alone, sometimes with the ellipsis of a definite Verb, οὔκ (i.e. ἀποκερῇ), ἄν γε ἐμοὶ πείθῃ [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Phaedo” 89b]]: sometimes as negativing the preceding sentence, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Pax” 850, 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Historia Graeca (Hellenica)” 1.7.19: as a Particle of solemn denial frequently with μά (which see)]] and the accusative; sometimes without μά, οὐ τὸν πάντων θεῶν θεὸν πρόμον Ἅλιον [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Tyrannus” 660 (Lyric poetry), compare 1088 (Lyric poetry), “El.” 1063 (Lyric poetry), “Ant.” 758.]]

__II.2
with indicative of statement, τὴν δ᾽ ἐγὼ οὐ λύσω [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 1.29, compare 114, 495]]; οὐ φθίνει Κροίσου φιλόφρων ἀρετά [Refs 8th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “P.” 1.94; ἔνθα κεν οὔ τιν᾽ ἀδάκρυτόν γ᾽ ἐνόησας Ἀργείων 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 24.61; οὔ κεν.. ἔπαξε 5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “N.” 7.25; οὐκ ἂν ὑπεξέφυγε 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 8.369.]]

__II.3
with subjunctive in future sense, only in Epic dialect, οὐ γάρ τίς με βίῃ γε ἑκὼν ἀέκοντα δίηται [Refs [7.197; οὐκ ἄν τοι χραίς μῃ κίθαρις 3.54, compare 11.387.]]

__II.4
with optative in potential sense (without ἄν or κεν), also Epic dialect, ὃ οὐ δύο γ᾽ ἄνδρε φέροιεν [Refs [5.303, 20.286.]]

__II.5
with optative and ἄν, κείνοισι δ᾽ ἂν οὔ τις.. μαχέοιτο [Refs 5th c.BC+ [1.271, compare 301, 2.250, 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 6.63, 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Prometheus Vinctus” 979, 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Ajax” 155 (_anapaest meter_), 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Iphigenia Aulidensis” 310, 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Acharnenses” 403, etc.]]

__II.6
in dependent clauses οὐ is used,

__II.6.a
with ὅτι or ὡς, after Verbs of saying, knowing, and showing, ἐκ μέν τοι ἐρέω.. ὡς ἐγὼ οὔ τι ἑκὼν κατερύκομαι [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 4.377, compare 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Electra” 561, 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 2.8, etc.]]: so with indicative or optative and ἄν, ἀπελογοῦντο ὡς οὐκ ἄν ποτε οὕτω μωροὶ ἦσαν [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Historia Graeca (Hellenica)” 5.4.22, compare 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 330a; ὡς δὲ οὐκ ἂν δικαίως αὐτοὺς δέχοισθε μαθεῖν χρή 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 1.40, compare 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 1.1.3, etc.: with _optative_ representing _indicative_ in indirect speech, ἔλεξε παιδὶ σῷ.. ὡς.. Ἕλληνες οὐ μενοῖεν 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Persae” 358, compare 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Philoctetes” 346, 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 1.38, 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Historia Graeca (Hellenica)” 6.1.1, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Apologia” 22b, etc.: for μή]] in such sentences, see at {μή} [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Bacchylides Lyricus 3.]]

__II.6.b
in all causal sentences, and in temporal and Relat. sentences unless there is conditional or final meaning, χωσαμένη, ὅ οἱ οὔ τι θαλύσια.. ῥέξε [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 9.534; ἄχθεται ὅτι οὐ κάρτα θεραπεύεται 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 3.80; διότι οὐκ ἦσαν δίκαι, οὐ δυνατοὶ ἦμεν παρ᾽ αὐτῶν ἃ ὤφειλον πράξασθαι 5th c.BC: Lysias Orator 17.3; μή με κτεῖν᾽, ἐπεὶ οὐχ ὁμογάστριος Ἕκτορός εἰμι 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 21.95, etc.; νῦν δὲ ἐπειδὴ οὐκ ἐθέλεις.., εἶμι 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Protagoras” 335c; ἐπειδὴ τὸ χωρίον οὐχ ἡλίσκετο 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 1.102; νηπιάχοις οἷς οὔ τι μέλει πολεμήϊα ἔργα 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 2.338, etc.]]: in causal relative sentences, οἵτινές σε οὐχὶ ἐσώσαμεν [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Crito” 46a]]; especially in the combinations, οὐκ ἔστιν ὅστις οὐ.., as οὐκ ἔστ᾽ ἐραστὴς ὅστις οὐκ ἀεὶ φιλεῖ [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Troades” 1051, compare “Hec.” 298; οὔτις ἔσθ᾽ ὃς οὔ 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Ajax” 725]]; οὐδείς ἐστιν ὅστις οὐ.. [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Isocrates Orator 15.180.]]

__II.6.c
after ὥστε with indicative or optative with ἄν, ὥστ᾽ οὐ δυνατόν σ᾽ εἵργειν ἔσται [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Vespae” 384, compare 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Ajax” 98, “OT” 411; οὕτως αὐτοὺς ἀγαπῶμεν.. ὥστε.. οὐκ ἂν ἐθελήσαιμεν 5th-6th c.BC: Isocrates Orator 8.45; οὐκ ἂν ὡρκίζομεν αὐτὸν ὥστε τῆς εἰρήνης ἂν διημαρτήκει καὶ οὐκ ἂν ἀμφότερ᾽ εἶχε 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 18.30: ὥστε οὐ with]]infinitive is almost invariably due to indirect speech, ὥστ᾽ οὐκ αἰσχύνεσθαι (for οὐκ αἰσχύνονται) [Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. author] 19.308, compare 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 5.40, 8.76, 5th c.BC: Lysias Orator 18.6, 4th c.BC: Isaeus Orator 11.27 (conjecture Reiske).]]—Rarely not in indirect speech, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Electra” 780, 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Phoenissae” 1358, “Hel.” 108, 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 53.2, 9.48.]]

__II.7
in a conditional clause μή is necessary, except,

__II.7.a
in [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Homerus Epicus, when the εἰ]] clause precedes the apodosis and the verb is indicative, εἰ δέ μοι οὐκ ἐπέεσσ᾽ ἐπιπείσεται [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 15.162, compare 178, 20.129, 24.296, 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 2.274, 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 4.160, 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 12.382, 13.144 (9.410 is an exception).]]

__II.7.b
when the εἰ clause is really causal, as after Verbs expressing surprise or emotion, μὴ θαυμάσῃς, εἰ πολλὰ τῶν εἰρημένων οὐ πρέπει σοι [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Isocrates Orator 1.44; κατοικτῖραι.., εἰ.. οὐδεὶς ἐς ἑκατοστὸν ἔτος περιέσται 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 7.46, compare 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Ajax” 1242; so also δεινὸν γὰρ ἂν εἴη πρῆγμα, εἰ Σάκας μὲν καταστρεψάμενοι δούλους ἔχομεν, Ἕλληνας δὲ οὐ τιμωρησόμεθα 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 7.9, compare 5th-6th c.BC: Andocides Orator 1.102, 5th c.BC: Lysias Orator 20.8 (probably), 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 8.55; οὐκ αἰσχρόν, εἰ τὸ μὲν Ἀργείων πλῆθος οὐκ ἐφοβήθη τὴν Λακεδαιμονίων ἀρχήν, ὑμεῖς δ᾽ ὄντες Ἀθηναῖοι βάρβαρον ἄνθρωπον.. φοβήσεσθ; [prev. author] 15.23, compare 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 5.97, 5th c.BC: Lysias Orator 22.13.]]

__II.7.c
when οὐ belongs closely to the next word (see. [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus I)]], or is quoted unchanged, εἰ, ὡς νῦν φήσει, οὐ παρεσκευάσατο [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 54.29 codices]]; εἰ δ᾽ οὐκέτ᾽ ἐστί (i.e. ὥσπερ λέγεις), τίνι τρόπῳ διεφθάρη ; [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Ion” 347.]]

__II.8
οὐ is used with infinitive in indirect speech, when it represents the indicative of orat. recta, φαμὲν δέ οἱ οὐ τελέεσθαι [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 4.664, compare 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 17.174, 21.316, 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Philoctetes” 1389, etc.; λέγοντες οὐκ εἶναι αὐτόνομοι 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 1.67, compare 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 348c, 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 1.6.18; οἶμαι.. οὐκ ὀλίγον ἔργον αὐτὸ εἶναι 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 369b, compare 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Tyrannus” 1051, 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 1.71, etc.; ἡγήσαντο ἡμᾶς οὐ περιόψεσθαι [prev. work] 39. (For the occasional use of μή, see at {μή} 5th c.BC: Bacchylides Lyricus 5c]]; sometimes we have οὐ and μή in consecutive clauses, οἶμαι σοῦ κάκιον οὐδὲν ἂν τούτων κρατύνειν μηδ᾽ ἐπιθύνειν χερί [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Philoctetes” 1058s q.; αὐτὸ ἡγοῦμαι οὐ διδακτὸν εἶναι μηδὲ.. παρασκευαστόν 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Protagoras” 319b.)]]

__II.9
οὐ is used with the participle, when it can be resolved into a finite sentence with οὐ, as after Verbs of knowing and showing, τὸν κατθανόνθ᾽ ὁρῶντες οὐ τιμώμενον [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Hecuba” 316; κατενόησαν οὐ πολλοὺς τοὺς Θηβαίους ὄντας 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 2. 3; ἔργῳ δηλώσω οὐ παραγενόμενος 5th c.BC: Antipho Orator 2.4.8, etc.]]; or into a causal sentence, τῶν βαρβάρων οἱ πολλοὶ ἐν τῇ θαλάσσῃ διεφθάρησαν νέειν οὐκ ἐπιστάμενοι [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 8.89; τὴν Μένδην πόλιν ἅτε οὐκ ἀπὸ ξυμβάσεως ἀνοιχθεῖσαν διήρπασαν 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 4.130]]; or into a concessive sentence, δόξω γυναῖκα καίπερ οὐκ ἔχων ἔχειν [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Alcestis” 352, compare 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Philoctetes” 377, etc.: regularly with ὡς]] and participle, ὡς οὐχὶ συνδράσουσα νουθετεῖς τάδε [Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. author] “El.” 1025, etc.; ἐθορυβεῖτε ὡς οὐ ποιήσοντες ταῦτα 5th c.BC: Lysias Orator 12.73, compare 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Philoctetes” 884, “Aj.” 682, 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 7.99, 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 1.2, 5, 28, 68, 90; ὥσπερ οὐ πάντας τούτῳ τῷ τεκμηρίῳ χρωμένους 4th c.BC: Lycurgus Orator 90, compare 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 8.1, 5th-6th c.BC: Isocrates Orator 4.11]]:—for exceptions, see at {μή} [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Bacchylides Lyricus 6.]]

__II.9.b
when the participle is used with the Article, μή is generally used, unless there is a distinct reference to a fact, when οὐ is occasionally found, ἡμεῖς δὲ ἀπὸ τῆς οὐκ οὔσης ἔτι [πόλεως] ὁρμώμενοι [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 1.74; τοὺς ἐν τῇ πόλει οὐδὲν εἰδότας [prev. author] 4.111; οἱ οὐκ ἐθέλοντες 5th c.BC: Antipho Orator 6.26; τῶν οὐ βουλομένων 5th-6th c.BC: Andocides Orator 1.9; τοὺς οὐδὲν ἀδικοῦντας ἀκρίτους ἀπέκτειναν 5th c.BC: Lysias Orator 12.82, compare τὸν οὐδὲ συμπενθῆσαι τὰς τῆς πατρίδος συμφορὰς τολμήσαντα (preceded by τὸν.. μήτε ὅπλα θέμενον ὑπὲρ τῆς πατρίδος μήτε τὸ σῶμα παρασχόντα κτλ.) 4th c.BC: Lycurgus Orator 43; τὸ οὐχ εὑρημένον 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 427e.]]

__II.10
Adjectives and abstract Substantives with the article commonly take μή (see. μή [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Bacchylides Lyricus 7) but οὐ]] is occasionally used, τὰς οὐκ ἀναγκαίας πόσεις [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Respublica Lacedaemoniorum” 5.4; τοὺς οὐδένας 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Iphigenia Aulidensis” 371; τὸν οὐδέν [prev. author] “Ph.” 598 (whereas ὁ μηδείς, τὸ μηδέν is the rule)]]; τὴν τῶν γεφυρῶν οὐ διάλυσιν the non- dissolution of the bridges, the fact of their notbeing broken up, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 1.137; ἡ οὐ περιτείχισις [prev. author] 3.95; ἡ τῶν χωρίων οὐκ ἀπόδοσις [prev. author] 5.35, compare 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Hippolytus” 196 (_anapaest meter_)]]; so without the article, ἐν οὐ καιπῷ [Refs [[prev. author] “Ba.” 1287; οὐ πάλης ὕπο [prev. work] 455.]]

__II.11
for οὐ μή, see entry

__II.12
in questions οὐ ordinarily expects a positive answer, οὔ νυ καὶ ἄλλοι ἔασι..; [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 10.165]]; οὐχ ὁράᾳς..; dost thou not see? [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 17.545; οὐκ.. ᾐσθόμη; 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Prometheus Vinctus” 956]]: so as a strong form of imperative,;[Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Agamemnon” 273, “fragment” 310; πῶς δ᾽ οὐχ; [prev. author] “Supp.” 918, 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Pax” 1027]]; ἐμὸς μὲν οὐχί [NT+5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Iphigenia Aulidensis” 859: also in Prose, 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 1.120, +others, NT.1Cor.5.12, etc.]]: the diphthong is genuine and always written ου (ουκ, ουδε, etc.) in early Inscrr., [Refs 4th c.BC+ [“IG” 12.10.22, etc.; in 4th c.BC rarely written οκ, [prev. work] 22.1635.112,116,121]]; οὐ abbreviated ο, Suid. see at {Φιλοξένου γραμμάτιον}.

__H
ACCENTUATION. οὐ is oxytone accusative to Hdn.Gr.1.494 (text doubtfulin 504): [Refs 8th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Sophistici Elenchi” 166b6, referring to 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 23.328 τὸ μὲν ου (i.e. οὐ ={οὒ}) καταπύθεται ὄμβρῳ, says λύουσι.. τῇ προσῳδίᾳ λέγοντες τὸ ου ὀξύτερον (i.e. οὗ), compare 178b3. In codices the word is written oxytone when followed by a pause (see. supr. B), and is usually written without any accent in other cases.]]

__H.I
οὐ in connexion with other Particles will be found in alphabetical order, οὐ γάρ, οὐ μή, etc.—The corresponding forms of μή should be compared.
