deep_entry:
Abbott-Smith / STEPBible (TBESG)
ὀφείλω
[in LXX: Deu.15:2, Isa.24:2 (נָשָׁה), Eze.18:7 (חוֹב), Wis.12:15, 20, al. ;]
to owe, be a debtor: with accusative of thing(s), Mat.18:28, Luk.7:41 16:7, Phm 18; id. with dative of person(s), Mat.18:28, Luk.16:5. Pass., to be owed, to be due: τ. ὀφειλόμενον, Mat.18:30, 34. Metaphorical: absol. (= Rabbinic חַיָּב; see McNeile, in l), Mat.23:16, 18; with accusative of thing(s) and dative of person(s), Rom.13:8; with inf., to be bound or obliged to do (of. Westc., Epp. Jo., 50), Luk.17:10, Jhn.13:14 19:7, Act.17:29, Rom.15:1, 27, 1Co.5:10 7:36 9:10 11:7 11:10, 2Co.12:14, Eph.5:28, 2Th.1:3 2:13, Heb.2:17 5:3, 12, 1Jn.2:6 Jn 3:16 Jn 4:11, 3Jn.8; ὤειλον συνίστασθαι, I ought to have been commended, 2Co.12:11. In peculiar Aram. sense of having wronged one (see: όφείλημα; but of. also Inscr. ἁμαρτίαν ὀφείίλω, Deiss., BS, 225), with dative of person(s), Luk.11:4 (cf. προσ-οφίελω).†
(AS)

---

LSJ / STEPBible (TFLSJ)
ὀφείλ-ω,
imperfect ὤφειλον; Epic dialect ὀφέλλω (also Aeolic dialect, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [“IG” 12(2).67.7 (Mytil.), and 4th c.AD(?): Arcadius Grammaticus, [prev. work] 5(2).343.27 (Orchom. 4th c.AD(?): Arcadius Grammaticus, 4th c.BC)),]]imperfect ὤφελλον or ὄφελλον, see infr. II. [Refs 8th c.BC+ [2, 3 (the _Attic dialect_ or _Ionic dialect_ ὀφείλετ᾽, ὄφειλον in 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 11.686, 688, 698, 8th-7th c.BC: Hesiodus Epicus “Opera et Dies” 174 is probably due to the Copyists)]]: future ὀφειλήσω [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 7.2.28, 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 30.7, also ὀφειλέσω “TAM” 2.431, +others]]: aorist 1 ὠφείλησα [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Aves” 115, 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 8.5]] (ἐπ-): perfect ὠφείληκα: pluperfect -ήκειν[Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 45. 33:]]aorist 2 ὤφελον (see. below [Refs [11.2, 3)]]:—passive, aorist participle ὀφειληθείς [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 3.63]]. (Cretan dialect ὀφήλω [Refs [“GDI” 5015.21]], written ὀπέλο [Refs 4th c.AD+ [“Leg.Gort.” 10.20, +others, 4th c.AD(?): Arcadius Grammaticus]] ὀφέλλω (see. above) and ὀφήλω [Refs 4th c.BC+ [“SIG” 306.40 (Tegea, 4th c.BC)]]: in early Attic dialect Inscrr. written both ὀφελ -IG 12.91.8[Refs [, +others, and ὀφειλ- [prev. work]109.9, +others)]]:—owe, have to pay or account for, τὸ καὶ μοιχάγρι᾽ ὀφέλλει [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 8.332]]; ὅτι μοι.. ζωάγρι᾽ ὀφέλλεις[Refs 8th c.BC+ [[prev. work] 462; χρεῖος, τό ῥά οἱ πᾶς δῆμος ὄφελλεν 21.17; πολέσιν γὰρ Ἐπειοὶ χρεῖος ὄφειλον 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 11.688; ζημίην ὀ. τῷ θεῷ 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 3.52, etc.: _metaphorically_, μητέρα μοι ζώουσαν ὀφέλλετε 3rd c.BC: Callimachus Epicus “Fragmenta” 126]]; τί ὀφείλω; what do I owe? [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Nubes” 21]]; ὀ. ἀργύριον, χρέα, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. author] “Av.” 115, “Nu.” 117; ὀ. ἢ θεῷ θυσίας ἢ ἀνθρώπῳ χρήματα 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 331b; ὀ. τινὶ δρᾶν τι [prev. work] 332a: with _dative_ only, ὀ. τινί]] to be debtor to another, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Nubes” 1135, “Lys.” 581, etc.; τρίτον δὲ χαίρειν, εἶτ᾽ ὀ. μηδενί 4th-3rd c.BC: Philemo Comicus 163]]: absolutely, to be in debt, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Nubes” 485, etc.]]; οἱ ὀφείλοντες debtors, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Ethica Nicomachea” 1167b21, 1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus 2.832a]]:—passive, to be due, ἔνθα χρεῖός μοι ὀφέλλεται (variant{ὀφείλεται}) [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 3.367; χρεῖος ὀφείλετο 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 11.686, 698; ἢν.. ὀφείληταί τί μοι 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Nubes” 484; μισθὸς τοῖς στρατιώταις ὠφείλετο 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 1.2.11, etc.]]; τὸ ὀφειλόμενον a debt,[Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. work] 7.7.34; -όμενα ἀποδιδόντες 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 5.99, compare 4th-5th c.BC: Simonides Lyricus cited in 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 331e.]]

__2
metaphorically, ὀ. μέλος τινί [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “O.” 10(11).3; πολλὰ δώμασιν καλά 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Hercules Furens” 287]]; ὀ. χάριν, see at {χάρις} [Refs 5th c.BC+ [1.2; Ἀπόλλωνι χαριστήρια 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 7.2.28; τὴν ψυχὴν πᾶσιν 2nd-3rd c.AD: Aelianus “Varia Historia” 10.5]]:—passive, ὀφείλεταί τινι ἐκ θεῶν κλέος [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Fragmenta - American Journal of Philology” 315; ὀ. τινὶ εὐεργεσία 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 1.137; ἀντὶ χαρίτων ἔχθραι ὀ. 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 4.5.32; τοῖς μὲν ἐχθροῖς βλάβην ὀ., τοῖς δὲ φίλοις ὠφελίαν 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 335e, compare 332b]]; τοὐφειλόμενον πράσσουσα Δίκη what is due, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Choephori” 310.]]

__3
as a legal term, to be bound to render, εὐθύνας ὤφειλον [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Andocides Orator 1.73 codices (_falsa lectio_ for{ὦφλον}): hence, like{ὀφλισκάνω}]], incur a penalty, ζημίαν [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Lysias Orator 9.10; διπλῆν τὴν βλάβην [prev. author] 1.32, compare 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Andromache” 360; τὴν τοιαύτην δίκην 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Leges” 909a, compare 774b, 774d, 844e, 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 21.77; ἁμαρτίαν ὀ. Μηνὶ Τυράννῳ “IG” 3.74.15 (2nd-3rd c.AD).]]

__4
in passive, of persons, to be due or liable to, θανάτῳ πάντες ὀφειλόμεθα [LXX+4th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Simonides Lyricus 122, cf. LXX.Wis.12.20, “IG” 3.1381; but τοιαύταις χερσὶν ὀφειλόμεθα]]our help is due, [Refs 1st c.BC+ [Anthologia Graeca 9.283 (1st c.BC-1st c.AD: Crinagoras Epigrammaticus).]]

__II
with infinitive, to be bound, to be obliged to do, ὀφέλλετε ταῦτα πένεσθαι ye are bound, ye ought to.., [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 19.200, compare 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.41, 42, +others, 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Alcestis” 682, 712, etc.]]; and of things, ought to be, ὁ λόγος οὐκ ἀκριβῶς ὀ. λέγεσθαι [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Ethica Nicomachea” 1104a2]]:—passive, δράσαντι γάρ τοι καὶ παθεῖν ὀφείλεται [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Fragmenta - American Journal of Philology” 456]]; σοὶ τοῦτ᾽ ὀφείλεται παθεῖν it is thy destiny to.., [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Philoctetes” 1421, compare “El.” 1173; ὡς πᾶσιν ἡμῖν κατθανεῖν ὀφείλεται 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Alcestis” 419, compare 782, “Or.” 1245, 5th c.BC: Lysias Orator 25.11; see above 1.4.]]

__II.2
in this signification Epic dialect imperfect ὤφελλον or ὄφελλον and aorist ὤφελον or ὄφελον are used of that which one has not, but ought to have, done (ought being the pret. of owe), ὤφελεν ἀθανάτοισιν εὔχεσθαι [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 23.546; νῦν ὄφελεν πονέεσθαι λισσόμενος 10.117, compare 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 4.472.]]

__II.3
these tenses are also used, followed by present or aorist infinitive, in wishes that something were or had been in present or past, ἀνδρὸς.. ὤφελλον ἀμείνονος εἶναι ἄκοιτις I ought to be.., would that I were.. ! [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 6.350]]; τὴν ὄφελ᾽ ἐν νήεσσι κατακτάμεν Ἄρτεμις would that Artemis had slain her !, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 19.59, compare 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 4.97; τιμήν πέρ μοι ὄφελλεν Ὀλύμπιος ἐγγυαλίξαι 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 1.353: frequently preceded by εἴθε (_Epic dialect_ αἴθε), ὡς, ὡς δή, which express the wish still more strongly, αἴθ᾽ ὄφελες ἄγονός τ᾽ ἔμεναι ἄγαμός τ᾽ ἀπολέσθαι]] O that thou hadst!, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 3.40, compare 1.415, etc.; αἴθ᾽ ὤφελλες.. σημαίνειν 14.84; αἴθ᾽ ὤφελλ᾽ ὁ ξεῖνος.. ὀλέσθαι 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 18.401; αἴθ᾽ ἅμα πάντες.. ὠφέλετε.. ἐπὶ νηυσὶ πεφάσθαι 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 24.254: with ὡς, ὡς ὄφελον.. ἑλέσθαι]] O that I had.. !,[Refs 8th c.BC+ [11.380; θανέειν 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 14.274; ὡς πρὶν ὤφελλον ὀλέσθαι 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 24.764, compare 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 14.68; ὡς ὤφελες αὐτόθ᾽ ὀλέσθαι 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 3.428; ὡς.. ὤφελες 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 2.184]]; ὡς ὄφελεν.. [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 3.173, etc.: strengthened, ὡς δὴ ἔγωγ᾽ ὄφελον.. 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 1.217: also with _negative_, μὴ ὄφελες λίσσεσθαι]].. would thou hadst never.. !, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 9.698; ἣ μὴ ὤφελλε γενέσθαι 17.686; τὼ μὴ γείνασθαι ὄφελλον 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 8.312; ὡς μὴ ὤφελλε τεκέσθαι 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 22.481; ὡς δὴ μὴ ὄφελον νικᾶν 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 11.548.—So in Trag. and _Attic dialect_, ὤφελον.. 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Tyrannus” 1157]]; ὤφελες.. [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Thesmophoriazusae” 865]]; ὤφελε.. [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Prometheus Vinctus” 48, 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 2.1.4, etc.: also, as in _Epic dialect_, εἴθ᾽ ὤφελες.. 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Electra” 1021]]; εἴθ᾽ ὤφελ᾽.. [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Nubes” 41, etc.]]; εἰ γὰρ ὤφελον.. [Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. author] “Ec.” 380, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 432c, “Cri.” 44d]]; ὡς ὤφελες.. [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Ranae” 955: with _negative_, μήποτ᾽ ὤφελον 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Philoctetes” 969, 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Alcestis” 880 (_anapaest meter_), 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 18.288]]; ὡς μήποτ᾽ ὤφελον.. [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Ion” 286; ὡς μηδὲ νῦν ὤφελον 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 21.78: without augment in 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus, εἶδον.. τὸ μὴ ἰδεῖν ὄφελον (variant{ὤ-}) 1.111, compare 3.65: sometimes in Trag. (Lyric poetry and _anapaest meter_), εἴθ᾽ ὄφελε.. 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Persae” 915]]; ὄφελε.. [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Ajax” 1192]]; μήποτ᾽ ὄφελον.. [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Medea” 1413. (In this signification ὤφειλον]] is used in late Epic dialect, ὡς μὴ ὤφειλες ἱκέσθαι [Refs 8th c.BC+ [4th c.AD(?): Quintus Smyrnaeus Epicus 5.194, but ὤφελλον should be read in 8th-7th c.BC: Hesiodus Epicus “Opera et Dies” 174 and ὤφελε in 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Iphigenia Aulidensis” 1291.)]]

__II.3.b
with indicative, ὤφελε μηδ᾽ ἐγένοντο θοαὶ νέες [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [3rd c.BC: Callimachus Epicus “Epigrammata” 19.1, compare 4th c.AD(?): Quintus Smyrnaeus Epicus 10.378, etc.]]

__II.3.c
ὄφελον (adverb accusative to [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd c.AD: Apollonius Dyscolus Grammaticus “de Adverbiis;” 142.9, “Etymologicum Magnum” 643.48)]] in this signification: with accusative et infinitive, ὤμοι ἐγών, ὄφελόν με.. ὀλέσθαι [NT+1st c.AD+ [5th-6th c.AD: Orphica “Argonautica” 1159: even with 2 _person_ of Verb, ὄφελον ἐβασιλεύσατε NT.1Cor.4.8, cf. NT.2Cor.11.1, NT.Gal.5.12, NT.Rev.3.15, LXX.Job.14.13, 2nd c.AD: Athenaeus Epigrammaticus 4.156a; ὄφελον δυνήσῃ 2nd c.AD: Lucianus Sophista “Sol.” 1 (as a solecism): with 3 _person_, 2nd c.AD: Arrianus Historicus “Epicteti Dissertationes” 2.18.15, 1st-2nd c.AD: Dio Chrysostomus Sophista 38.47: with 1 _person_ _plural_, ὄφελον ἀπεθάνομεν LXX.Exo.16.3]]; ὤφελον (sic) εἰ ἐδυνάμεθα πέτασθαι [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [“PGiss.” 17.10 (2nd c.AD): with]]infinitive, ὄφελομ μὲν ἡ θεὸς.. στερῆσαι.. [Refs 2nd c.BC+ [“OGI” 315.16 (Pessinus, 2nd c.BC).]]

__III
impersonal ὀφείλει, it behoves, with accusative et infinitive, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “N.” 2.6]]; ὄφελλέ με μήτε.. εἰσοράαν κτλ. [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [3rd c.BC: Apollonius Rhodius Epicus 3.678: so _person_ in]]participle, absolutely, αἱ ὀφείλουσαι ἱερουργίαι τῶν θεῶν the due services of the gods, [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [“PTeb.” 294.24 (2nd c.AD)]]; κατὰ τὸν ὀφείλοντα καιρόν [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd c.AD: Soranus Medicus 1.79]]. (ὦφλον, ὤφληκα, aorist and perfect of ὀφλισκάνω, were probably originally aorist and perfect of ὀφείλω: ὄφελον in signf. II. [Refs [3c]] may be originally neuter participle of ὤφελε (signification [Refs [111) with omission of ἐστί.)]]

deep_entry:
Abbott-Smith / STEPBible (TBESG)
ὄφελον  2 aorist of ὀφείλω, without the augment (see M, Pr., 201n), used to express a fruitless wish;
[in LXX (with aor. indic.): Exo.16:3 (נָתַן מִי), Num.14:2 Num.20:3 (לוּא), Psa.119:5 (אַחֲלַי), etc. ;]
in cl. with an infin. (chiefly poët.),
would that: with indic. aor., 1Co.4:8; impf., 2Co.11:1, Rev.3:15; fut., Gal.5:12 (a practicable wish, see 131., 206 f., 220. The construction with indic. is only found in late writers.)†
(AS)

---

LSJ / STEPBible (TFLSJ)
Included with:   ὀφείλ-ω,
imperfect ὤφειλον; Epic dialect ὀφέλλω (also Aeolic dialect, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [“IG” 12(2).67.7 (Mytil.), and 4th c.AD(?): Arcadius Grammaticus, [prev. work] 5(2).343.27 (Orchom. 4th c.AD(?): Arcadius Grammaticus, 4th c.BC)),]]imperfect ὤφελλον or ὄφελλον, see infr. II. [Refs 8th c.BC+ [2, 3 (the _Attic dialect_ or _Ionic dialect_ ὀφείλετ᾽, ὄφειλον in 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 11.686, 688, 698, 8th-7th c.BC: Hesiodus Epicus “Opera et Dies” 174 is probably due to the Copyists)]]: future ὀφειλήσω [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 7.2.28, 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 30.7, also ὀφειλέσω “TAM” 2.431, +others]]: aorist 1 ὠφείλησα [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Aves” 115, 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 8.5]] (ἐπ-): perfect ὠφείληκα: pluperfect -ήκειν[Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 45. 33:]]aorist 2 ὤφελον (see. below [Refs [11.2, 3)]]:—passive, aorist participle ὀφειληθείς [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 3.63]]. (Cretan dialect ὀφήλω [Refs [“GDI” 5015.21]], written ὀπέλο [Refs 4th c.AD+ [“Leg.Gort.” 10.20, +others, 4th c.AD(?): Arcadius Grammaticus]] ὀφέλλω (see. above) and ὀφήλω [Refs 4th c.BC+ [“SIG” 306.40 (Tegea, 4th c.BC)]]: in early Attic dialect Inscrr. written both ὀφελ -IG 12.91.8[Refs [, +others, and ὀφειλ- [prev. work]109.9, +others)]]:—owe, have to pay or account for, τὸ καὶ μοιχάγρι᾽ ὀφέλλει [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 8.332]]; ὅτι μοι.. ζωάγρι᾽ ὀφέλλεις[Refs 8th c.BC+ [[prev. work] 462; χρεῖος, τό ῥά οἱ πᾶς δῆμος ὄφελλεν 21.17; πολέσιν γὰρ Ἐπειοὶ χρεῖος ὄφειλον 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 11.688; ζημίην ὀ. τῷ θεῷ 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 3.52, etc.: _metaphorically_, μητέρα μοι ζώουσαν ὀφέλλετε 3rd c.BC: Callimachus Epicus “Fragmenta” 126]]; τί ὀφείλω; what do I owe? [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Nubes” 21]]; ὀ. ἀργύριον, χρέα, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. author] “Av.” 115, “Nu.” 117; ὀ. ἢ θεῷ θυσίας ἢ ἀνθρώπῳ χρήματα 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 331b; ὀ. τινὶ δρᾶν τι [prev. work] 332a: with _dative_ only, ὀ. τινί]] to be debtor to another, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Nubes” 1135, “Lys.” 581, etc.; τρίτον δὲ χαίρειν, εἶτ᾽ ὀ. μηδενί 4th-3rd c.BC: Philemo Comicus 163]]: absolutely, to be in debt, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Nubes” 485, etc.]]; οἱ ὀφείλοντες debtors, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Ethica Nicomachea” 1167b21, 1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus 2.832a]]:—passive, to be due, ἔνθα χρεῖός μοι ὀφέλλεται (variant{ὀφείλεται}) [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 3.367; χρεῖος ὀφείλετο 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 11.686, 698; ἢν.. ὀφείληταί τί μοι 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Nubes” 484; μισθὸς τοῖς στρατιώταις ὠφείλετο 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 1.2.11, etc.]]; τὸ ὀφειλόμενον a debt,[Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. work] 7.7.34; -όμενα ἀποδιδόντες 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 5.99, compare 4th-5th c.BC: Simonides Lyricus cited in 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 331e.]]

__2
metaphorically, ὀ. μέλος τινί [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “O.” 10(11).3; πολλὰ δώμασιν καλά 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Hercules Furens” 287]]; ὀ. χάριν, see at {χάρις} [Refs 5th c.BC+ [1.2; Ἀπόλλωνι χαριστήρια 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 7.2.28; τὴν ψυχὴν πᾶσιν 2nd-3rd c.AD: Aelianus “Varia Historia” 10.5]]:—passive, ὀφείλεταί τινι ἐκ θεῶν κλέος [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Fragmenta - American Journal of Philology” 315; ὀ. τινὶ εὐεργεσία 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 1.137; ἀντὶ χαρίτων ἔχθραι ὀ. 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 4.5.32; τοῖς μὲν ἐχθροῖς βλάβην ὀ., τοῖς δὲ φίλοις ὠφελίαν 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 335e, compare 332b]]; τοὐφειλόμενον πράσσουσα Δίκη what is due, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Choephori” 310.]]

__3
as a legal term, to be bound to render, εὐθύνας ὤφειλον [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Andocides Orator 1.73 codices (_falsa lectio_ for{ὦφλον}): hence, like{ὀφλισκάνω}]], incur a penalty, ζημίαν [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Lysias Orator 9.10; διπλῆν τὴν βλάβην [prev. author] 1.32, compare 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Andromache” 360; τὴν τοιαύτην δίκην 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Leges” 909a, compare 774b, 774d, 844e, 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 21.77; ἁμαρτίαν ὀ. Μηνὶ Τυράννῳ “IG” 3.74.15 (2nd-3rd c.AD).]]

__4
in passive, of persons, to be due or liable to, θανάτῳ πάντες ὀφειλόμεθα [LXX+4th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Simonides Lyricus 122, cf. LXX.Wis.12.20, “IG” 3.1381; but τοιαύταις χερσὶν ὀφειλόμεθα]]our help is due, [Refs 1st c.BC+ [Anthologia Graeca 9.283 (1st c.BC-1st c.AD: Crinagoras Epigrammaticus).]]

__II
with infinitive, to be bound, to be obliged to do, ὀφέλλετε ταῦτα πένεσθαι ye are bound, ye ought to.., [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 19.200, compare 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.41, 42, +others, 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Alcestis” 682, 712, etc.]]; and of things, ought to be, ὁ λόγος οὐκ ἀκριβῶς ὀ. λέγεσθαι [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Ethica Nicomachea” 1104a2]]:—passive, δράσαντι γάρ τοι καὶ παθεῖν ὀφείλεται [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Fragmenta - American Journal of Philology” 456]]; σοὶ τοῦτ᾽ ὀφείλεται παθεῖν it is thy destiny to.., [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Philoctetes” 1421, compare “El.” 1173; ὡς πᾶσιν ἡμῖν κατθανεῖν ὀφείλεται 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Alcestis” 419, compare 782, “Or.” 1245, 5th c.BC: Lysias Orator 25.11; see above 1.4.]]

__II.2
in this signification Epic dialect imperfect ὤφελλον or ὄφελλον and aorist ὤφελον or ὄφελον are used of that which one has not, but ought to have, done (ought being the pret. of owe), ὤφελεν ἀθανάτοισιν εὔχεσθαι [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 23.546; νῦν ὄφελεν πονέεσθαι λισσόμενος 10.117, compare 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 4.472.]]

__II.3
these tenses are also used, followed by present or aorist infinitive, in wishes that something were or had been in present or past, ἀνδρὸς.. ὤφελλον ἀμείνονος εἶναι ἄκοιτις I ought to be.., would that I were.. ! [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 6.350]]; τὴν ὄφελ᾽ ἐν νήεσσι κατακτάμεν Ἄρτεμις would that Artemis had slain her !, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 19.59, compare 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 4.97; τιμήν πέρ μοι ὄφελλεν Ὀλύμπιος ἐγγυαλίξαι 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 1.353: frequently preceded by εἴθε (_Epic dialect_ αἴθε), ὡς, ὡς δή, which express the wish still more strongly, αἴθ᾽ ὄφελες ἄγονός τ᾽ ἔμεναι ἄγαμός τ᾽ ἀπολέσθαι]] O that thou hadst!, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 3.40, compare 1.415, etc.; αἴθ᾽ ὤφελλες.. σημαίνειν 14.84; αἴθ᾽ ὤφελλ᾽ ὁ ξεῖνος.. ὀλέσθαι 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 18.401; αἴθ᾽ ἅμα πάντες.. ὠφέλετε.. ἐπὶ νηυσὶ πεφάσθαι 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 24.254: with ὡς, ὡς ὄφελον.. ἑλέσθαι]] O that I had.. !,[Refs 8th c.BC+ [11.380; θανέειν 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 14.274; ὡς πρὶν ὤφελλον ὀλέσθαι 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 24.764, compare 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 14.68; ὡς ὤφελες αὐτόθ᾽ ὀλέσθαι 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 3.428; ὡς.. ὤφελες 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 2.184]]; ὡς ὄφελεν.. [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 3.173, etc.: strengthened, ὡς δὴ ἔγωγ᾽ ὄφελον.. 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 1.217: also with _negative_, μὴ ὄφελες λίσσεσθαι]].. would thou hadst never.. !, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 9.698; ἣ μὴ ὤφελλε γενέσθαι 17.686; τὼ μὴ γείνασθαι ὄφελλον 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 8.312; ὡς μὴ ὤφελλε τεκέσθαι 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 22.481; ὡς δὴ μὴ ὄφελον νικᾶν 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 11.548.—So in Trag. and _Attic dialect_, ὤφελον.. 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Tyrannus” 1157]]; ὤφελες.. [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Thesmophoriazusae” 865]]; ὤφελε.. [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Prometheus Vinctus” 48, 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 2.1.4, etc.: also, as in _Epic dialect_, εἴθ᾽ ὤφελες.. 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Electra” 1021]]; εἴθ᾽ ὤφελ᾽.. [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Nubes” 41, etc.]]; εἰ γὰρ ὤφελον.. [Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. author] “Ec.” 380, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 432c, “Cri.” 44d]]; ὡς ὤφελες.. [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Ranae” 955: with _negative_, μήποτ᾽ ὤφελον 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Philoctetes” 969, 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Alcestis” 880 (_anapaest meter_), 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 18.288]]; ὡς μήποτ᾽ ὤφελον.. [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Ion” 286; ὡς μηδὲ νῦν ὤφελον 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 21.78: without augment in 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus, εἶδον.. τὸ μὴ ἰδεῖν ὄφελον (variant{ὤ-}) 1.111, compare 3.65: sometimes in Trag. (Lyric poetry and _anapaest meter_), εἴθ᾽ ὄφελε.. 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Persae” 915]]; ὄφελε.. [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Ajax” 1192]]; μήποτ᾽ ὄφελον.. [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Medea” 1413. (In this signification ὤφειλον]] is used in late Epic dialect, ὡς μὴ ὤφειλες ἱκέσθαι [Refs 8th c.BC+ [4th c.AD(?): Quintus Smyrnaeus Epicus 5.194, but ὤφελλον should be read in 8th-7th c.BC: Hesiodus Epicus “Opera et Dies” 174 and ὤφελε in 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Iphigenia Aulidensis” 1291.)]]

__II.3.b
with indicative, ὤφελε μηδ᾽ ἐγένοντο θοαὶ νέες [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [3rd c.BC: Callimachus Epicus “Epigrammata” 19.1, compare 4th c.AD(?): Quintus Smyrnaeus Epicus 10.378, etc.]]

__II.3.c
ὄφελον (adverb accusative to [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd c.AD: Apollonius Dyscolus Grammaticus “de Adverbiis;” 142.9, “Etymologicum Magnum” 643.48)]] in this signification: with accusative et infinitive, ὤμοι ἐγών, ὄφελόν με.. ὀλέσθαι [NT+1st c.AD+ [5th-6th c.AD: Orphica “Argonautica” 1159: even with 2 _person_ of Verb, ὄφελον ἐβασιλεύσατε NT.1Cor.4.8, cf. NT.2Cor.11.1, NT.Gal.5.12, NT.Rev.3.15, LXX.Job.14.13, 2nd c.AD: Athenaeus Epigrammaticus 4.156a; ὄφελον δυνήσῃ 2nd c.AD: Lucianus Sophista “Sol.” 1 (as a solecism): with 3 _person_, 2nd c.AD: Arrianus Historicus “Epicteti Dissertationes” 2.18.15, 1st-2nd c.AD: Dio Chrysostomus Sophista 38.47: with 1 _person_ _plural_, ὄφελον ἀπεθάνομεν LXX.Exo.16.3]]; ὤφελον (sic) εἰ ἐδυνάμεθα πέτασθαι [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [“PGiss.” 17.10 (2nd c.AD): with]]infinitive, ὄφελομ μὲν ἡ θεὸς.. στερῆσαι.. [Refs 2nd c.BC+ [“OGI” 315.16 (Pessinus, 2nd c.BC).]]

__III
impersonal ὀφείλει, it behoves, with accusative et infinitive, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “N.” 2.6]]; ὄφελλέ με μήτε.. εἰσοράαν κτλ. [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [3rd c.BC: Apollonius Rhodius Epicus 3.678: so _person_ in]]participle, absolutely, αἱ ὀφείλουσαι ἱερουργίαι τῶν θεῶν the due services of the gods, [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [“PTeb.” 294.24 (2nd c.AD)]]; κατὰ τὸν ὀφείλοντα καιρόν [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd c.AD: Soranus Medicus 1.79]]. (ὦφλον, ὤφληκα, aorist and perfect of ὀφλισκάνω, were probably originally aorist and perfect of ὀφείλω: ὄφελον in signf. II. [Refs [3c]] may be originally neuter participle of ὤφελε (signification [Refs [111) with omission of ἐστί.)]]

deep_entry:
Abbott-Smith / STEPBible (TBESG)
ὄφελος, -ονς, τό
(ὀφέλλω, to increase) [in LXX: Job.15:3 (יָעַל hi.)* ;]
advantage, help: 1Co.15:32, Jas.2:14, 16.†
(AS)

---

LSJ / STEPBible (TFLSJ)
ὄφελος, τό,
(ὀφέλλω B) only in nominative and accusative singular, furtherance, advantage, help, αἴ κ᾽ ὄφελός τι γενώμεθα in case we can be of any use, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 13.236]]; ὅς τοι πόλλ᾽ ὄ. γένετο who was a help to thee in many matters, [Refs [17.152]]; οὐδὲν σοί γ᾽ ὄ. not as any good to thee,; [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Gorgias” 504e, compare 513e]]; τί ζῆν ὄ. ᾧ μή 'στι τὸ ζῆν εἰδέναι ; [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-3rd c.BC: Philemo Comicus 104.]]

__2
with genitive, φυγᾶς ὄ. εἴ τί μοι [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Supplices” 737 (Lyric poetry); τῶν ὄ. ἐστι οὐδέν 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 8.68. ; οἷσι.. οὐδὲν ὄ. ἐστιν οὔτε χρημάτων οὔτε τῶν ἄλλων οὐδενὸς ἄτερ τῆς ὑγιείης 5th c.BC: Hippocrates Medicus “περὶ διαίτης” 3.69; τί τῆς εὐμορφίας ὄ.; 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Fragmenta” 548]]; ἐλευθερίας οὐδὲν ὄ. [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Andocides Orator 4.17; ἐάν τι ἡμῶν ὡς νομοθετῶν ὄ. ᾖ 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 530c; ἀνὴρ ὅτου τι καὶ σμικρὸν ὄ. ἐστιν [prev. author] “Ap.” 28b; γεωργοῦ ἀργοῦ οὐδὲν ὄφελος 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 1.6.18; μαγείρῳ μαχαίρας οὐδὲν ὄ. ἥτις μὴ τέμνει 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 25.46; τί δ᾽ ὄ. εὖ λαλοῦντος, ἂν κακῶς φρον; 4th-3rd c.BC: Menander Comicus 821.]]

__3
ὅ τι πέρ ἐστ᾽ ὄ. ἐν τῇ πόλει all that is best, all the best people, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Ecclesiazusae” 53, compare 2nd c.AD: Lucianus Sophista “Herod.” 8: with _genitive_, ὅ τι περ ὄ. τοῦ στρατεύματος]] the serviceable part (or perhaps the flower) of the army, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Historia Graeca (Hellenica)” 5.3.6, compare 3rd c.BC: Theocritus Poeta Bucolicus 13.18]]; ὅ τι περ.. ἀπληστίας ὄ. the flower (acme) of gluttony, [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd c.AD: Lucianus Sophista “Tim.” 55.]]

__4
with genitive objecti, help against a thing, [Refs 2nd c.BC+ [2nd c.BC: Nicander Epicus “Theriaca” 518.]]

deep_entry:
Abbott-Smith / STEPBible (TBESG)
ὀφθαλμός, -οῦ, ὁ,
[in LXX chiefly for עַיִן ;]
the eye (as in cl., chiefly pl.): Mat.5:38, Mrk.9:47, Luk.6:41, Jhn.9:6, al.; τοὺς ὀ. ἐξορύθσσειν (figuratively), Gal.4:15; ἐπᾶραι, Luk.6:20, Jhn.6:5; ἀνοῖξα, Act.9:40; id., of restoring sight, Mat.20:33, Jhn.9:10, al.; ἐν ῥιπῇ ὀφθαλμοῦ, 1Co.15:52; by anthropom., of  God, Heb.4:13, 1Pe.3:12; pleonastically (cf. Thackeray, Gr., 42f.), εἶδον οἱ ὀ. μοθ, Luk.2:30 (similarly, ib. 4:20 10:23, Jhn.12:40, 1Co.2:9, 1Jn.1:1, Rev.1:7). Metaphorical (as otherwise in cl.; see LS, see word);
__(a) of ethical qualities: ὀ. πονηρός (meton., for envy; cf. Heb. עַיִן רַע, Pro.28:22; cf. Sir.14:10 34:13), Mat.6:22, 23 Mrk.7:22, Luk.11:34; ἁπλοῦς, Mat.6:22, Luk.11:34; ἐπιθυμία (which see) ὀφθαλμῶν (cf. Ecc.4:8, Sir.14:9), 1Jn.2:16; ὀ. μεστοὶ μοιχαλἰδος, 2Pe.2:14;
__(b) of mental vision: Mat.13:15, Mrk.8:18, Luk.19:42, Jhn.12:40, Rom.11:8, Gal.3:1, Eph.1:18, al.; ἐν ὀφθαλμοῖς before genitive (on the absence of the art., seeBl, §46, 9.II; M, Pr., 81), Mat.21:42, Mrk.12:11.
(AS)

---

LSJ / STEPBible (TFLSJ)
ὀφθαλμός, ὁ,

__2
στέρησις ὀφθαλμῶν temporary loss of sight, [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd c.AD: Galenus Medicus 17(1).400.]]

__II
in singular, the eye of a master or ruler, πάντα ἰδὼν Διὸς ὀ. [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th-7th c.BC: Hesiodus Epicus “Opera et Dies” 267; Δίκης ὀ. ὃς τὰ πάνθ᾽ ὁρᾷ 4th-3rd c.BC: Menander Comicus “Μονόστιχοι - Fragmenta Comicorum Graecorum” 179; δεσπότου ὀ. 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Oeconomicus” 12.20]]; ἀκοίμητος ὀ., of God, [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd c.AD: Secundus Gnomologus “Sententiae - FPG” 3]]; so a king is called ὀ. οἴκων [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Choephori” 934 (so ὄμμα “Pers.” 169)]]; and in Persia ὀφθαλμὸς βασιλέως the king's eye was a confidential officer, through whom he beheld his kingdom and subjects, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Persae” 979 (Lyric poetry), 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.114, 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Acharnenses” 92, 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 8.2.10f, 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Politica” 1287b29, 1st c.AD: Philo Judaeus 1.642]]; compare οὖς.

__III

__IV
the dearest, best, as the eye is the most precious part of the body, hence of men, ὀ. Σικελίας, στρατιᾶς, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “O.” 2.10, 6.16]]; also, light, cheer, comfort, μέγας [γ᾽] ὀ. οἱ πατρὸς τάφοι [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Tyrannus” 987, compare 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Andromache” 406.]]

__V
eye or bud of a plant or tree, [Refs 7th c.BC+ [7th c.BC: Alcman Lyricus 43, Ion Eleg. 1.6, 5th c.BC: Hippocrates Medicus “περὶ φύσιος παιδίου” 26, 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Oeconomicus” 19.10, 4th-3rd c.BC: Theophrastus Philosophus “Historia Plantarum” 1.8.5, etc.]]

Architecture texts, in dual, the disks forming the centres of the volutes of an Ionic capital, [Refs [“IG” 12.374.291.]]

Abbott-Smith / STEPBible (TBESG)
1. as Substantive Verb, to be, to exist , οὐκ ἔσθ᾽ οὗτος ἀνήρ, οὐδ᾽ ἔσσεται (Odyssey by Homer); τεθνηῶτος, μηδ᾽ ἔτ᾽ ἐόντος (Odyssey by Homer); οὐκέτ᾽ ἔστι he is no more , (Euripides); θεοὶ αἰὲν ἐόντες (Iliad by Homer); ἐσσόμενοι posterity, (Iliad by Homer); ζώντων καὶ ὄντων Ἀθηναίων (Demosthenes Orator):—;so of cities, etc., ὄλωλεν, οὐδ᾽ ἔτ᾽ ἔστι Τροία (compare Troja fuit) , (Euripides)
2. of things, to be, exist , εἰ ἔστιν ἀληθέως [ ἡ τράπεζα] (Herdotus Historicus); ἕως ἂν ὁ πόλεμος ἦι so long as it last , (Thucydides)
3. to be , opposite to appearing to be , as esse  to videri , τὸν ἐόντα λόγον the true  story, (Herdotus Historicus); τὰ ὄντα ἀπαγγέλλειν (Thucydides); τῶι ὄντι, Lat. revera, in reality, in fact, (Plato Philosophus)
4. followed by the Relative, οὐκ ἔστιν ὅς, no one , (Iliad by Homer), etc.; εἰσὶν οἵ, Lat. sunt qui, (Thucydides), etc.; ἐστὶν ἅ some things , (Thucydides); also ἔστιν οἵ, for εἰσὶν οἵ, (Herdotus Historicus), etc.:—;so withrelat. Particles, ἔστιν ἔνθα, Lat. est ubi, (Xenophon Historicus), etc.; ἔστιν ὅπη, ἔσθ᾽ ὅπου, somewhere , or somehow , (Plato Philosophus), etc.; ἔστιν ὅπως in some manner , (Herdotus Historicus), etc.; ἔστιν ὅτε, ἔσθ᾽ ὅτε, sometimes , (Sophocles Tragicus), etc.
5. ἔστι impersonal, with infinitive, like πάρεστι, it is possible , (Homer), attic
6. to be , Copula connecting predicate with subject, both being in the same case, (Homer), etc.
7. sometimes εἶναι with Part. represents finite Verb, ἦν τεθνηκώς, for ἐτεθνήκει, (Aeschulus Tragicus); πεφυκός ἐστι = πέφυκε, (Aristophanes Comicus)
8. the Inf. is redundant in some phrases, ἑκὼν εἶναι (see. ἑκών II); τὸ ἐπ᾽ ἐκείνοις εἶναι quantum in illis esset , (Thucydides); τὸ σύμπαν εἶναι (Herdotus Historicus); τὸ νῦν εἶναι (Plato Philosophus), etc. (ML)

of cities, ὄλωλεν, οὐδ᾽ ἔτ᾽ ἐστὶ Τροία [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Troades” 1292, compare “Heracl.” 491]]; δοκεῖ μοι Καρχηδόνα μὴ εἶναι censeo Carthaginem esse delendam, [Refs 1st c.AD+ [1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus “Cat.Ma.” 27]]; ἂν ᾖ τὸ στράτευμα be in existence, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 8.17]]; of money, to be in hand, τῶν ὄντων χρημάτων καὶ τῶν προσιόντων [Refs [“IG” 12.91.25]]; τὰ ὄντα property, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Gorgias” 511a, 1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus “Antonius” 24, etc.]]; __A.II
of the real world, be, opposed to become, γίγνεται πάντα ἃ δή φαμεν εἶναι [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Theaetetus” 152d, etc.]]; τὸ ὄν [Refs 5th c.BC+ [“Being”, 4th-5th c.BC: Parmenides Poeta Philosophus 8.35, 5th c.BC: Protagoras Philosophus 2, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Timaeus” 27d, etc.]]; opposed to τὸ μὴ ὄν, [LXX+5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Gorgias Rhetor et Sophista “fragment” 3 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator, etc.; οὐδὲν γίνεται ἐκ τοῦ μὴ ὄντος 4th-3rd c.BC: Epicurus Philosophus “Epistulae” 1p.5U.; ἐξ οὐκ ὄντων ἐποίησεν αὐτὰ ὁ θεός LXX.2Mac.7.28]]; τὰ ὄντα the world of things, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [1st c.AD(?): Heraclitus 7, 5th c.BC: Empedocles Poeta Philosophus 129.5, etc.]]; ὄνindeclinable, τῶν ὂν εἰδῶν species of Being, [Refs 3rd c.AD+ [3rd c.AD: Plotinus Philosophus 6.2.10.]]

__A.II.2
of circumstances, events, etc., to happen, τά τ᾽ ἐόντα, τά τ᾽ ἐσσόμενα, πρό τ᾽ ἐόντα [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 1.70; ἡ ἐσβολὴ ἔμελλεν ἔσεσθαι 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 2.13, etc.]]; τῆς προδοσίας οὔσης since treachery was there, [Refs [[prev. author] 4.103]]; ἕως ἂν ὁ πόλεμος ᾖ so long as it last, [Refs [[prev. author] 1.58; αἱ σπονδαὶ ἐνιαυτὸν ἔσονται [prev. author] 4.118]]; τί ἐστι; what is it? what's the matter? [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Thesmophoriazusae” 193]]; τί οὖν ἦν τοῦτ; how came it to pass? [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Phaedo” 58a: repeated with a _relative_ to avoid a positive assertion, ἔστι δ᾽ ὅπῃ νῦν ἔ.]] things are as they are, i.e. are ill, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Agamemnon” 67.]]

__A.III
be the fact or the case, διπλασίαν ἂν τὴν δύναμιν εἰκάζεσθαι ἤ ἐστιν twice as large as it really is, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 1.10]]; αὐτὸ ὅ ἐστι καλόν beauty in its essence, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Symposium” 211c, compare “Phd.” 74b]]; frequently in participle, τὸν ἐόντα λόγον λέγειν or φαίνειν the true story, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.95, 116]]; τῷ ἐόντι χρήσασθαι tell the truth,[Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. work] 30; τὰ ὄντα ἀπαγγέλλειν 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 7.8]]; σκῆψιν οὐκ οὖσαν, λόγον οὐκ ὄντα, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Electra” 584, 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Ranae” 1052]]; τῷ ὄντι in reality, in fact, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Protagoras” 328d, etc.]]; to apply a quotation to a case in point, τῷ ὄντι κλαυσίγελως real 'smiles through tears' (with allusion to [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 6.484), 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Historia Graeca (Hellenica)” 7.2.9, compare 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Laches” 196d]]; κατὰ τὸ ἐόν according to the fact, rightly, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.97]]; πᾶν τὸ ἐόν the whole truth, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. author] 9.11; τοῦ ἐόντος ἀποτεύξεται 5th c.BC: Hippocrates Medicus “περὶ ἀρχαίης ἰητρικῇς” 2.]]

__A.IV
followed by the relative, οὐκ ἔστιν ὅς or ὅστις no one, οὐκ ἔσθ᾽ ὃς.. ἀπαλάλκοι [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 22.348; οὐκ ἔ. οὐδεὶς ὅς 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Electra” 903]]; οὐκ ἔ. ὅτῳ, ={οὐδενί}, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Prometheus Vinctus” 293 (_anapaest meter_), compare 989: frequently in _plural_, εἰσὶν οἵ]], = Latin sunt qui, used exactly like{ἔνιοι}, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 6.88, 7.44, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Meno” 77d, “Grg.” 503a, etc. (εἰσί τινες οἵ.. 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 3.24)]]; ἐστὶν ἃ χωρία, πολίσματα, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. author] 1.12, 65; ἐστὶν ἃ εἰπεῖν [prev. author] 2.67; ἦσαν οἵ 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 5.2.14]]; the singular Verb is used even with masculine and feminine plural, ἐστὶν οἵ, αἵ, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Hippocrates Medicus “περὶ ἀγμῶν” 1, “VC” 4, 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 2.3.16]]; more frequently in oblique cases, ποταμῶν ἐστὶ ὧν [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 7.187; ἐστὶν ἀφ᾽ ὧν 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 8.65]]; ἐστὶ παρ᾽ οἷς, ἐστὶν ἐν οἷς, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. author] 1.23, 5.25: in questions ὅστις is used, ἔστιν ἥντινα δόξαν.. ἀπεκρίνατ; 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Meno” 85b: with _relative_ Particles, ἐστὶν ἔνθα]], = Latin est ubi, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 7.4.15, etc.]]; ἐ. ὅπῃ, ἔσθ᾽ ὅπου, somehow, somewhere, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Protagoras” 331d, 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Eumenides” 517, 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Tyrannus” 448, etc.]]; in questions expecting a negative answer, ἐ. ὁπόθεν, ὅπω; [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Philebus” 35a, “R.” 493e, etc.; οὐ γάρ ἐσθ᾽ ὅπως 5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “Fragmenta.” 61, compare 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 7.102, 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Agamemnon” 620]]; οὐκ ἔ. ὅπως οὐ in any case, necessarily, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Pax” 188; οὐκ ἔ. ὡς 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Meno” 76e, etc.]]; ἐ. ὅτε, ἔσθ᾽ ὅτε, sometimes, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “Fragmenta.” 180.2, 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Ajax” 56, 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 7.21, etc.]]

__A.V
ἦν is sometimes used with plural masculine and feminine, usually at the beginning of a sentence, there was, τῆς δ᾽ ἦν τρεῖς κεφαλαί [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th-7th c.BC: Hesiodus Epicus “Theogonia” 321; (but in ἦν δ᾽ ἐρῳδιοί τε πολλοί 5th c.BC: Epicharmus Comicus 46, compare 59, +others, it may be taken as _Doric dialect_ _3rd.pers._ _plural_)]]; ἦν δ᾽ ἀμφίπλεκτοι κλίμακες [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Trachiniae” 520 (Lyric poetry)]]; ἦν ἄρα κἀκεῖνοι ταλακάρδιοι epigram cited in [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aeschines Orator 3.184; less frequently ἔστι, ἔστι δὲ μεταξὺ.. ἑπτὰ στάδιοι 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.26, compare 7.34; ἔστι.. ἄρχοντές τε καὶ δῆμος 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 463a]]; before dual Nouns, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Vespae” 58, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Gorgias” 500d.]]

__A.VI
ἔστι impersonal, with infinitive, it is possible, ἔστι γὰρ ἀμφοτέροισιν ὀνείδεα μυθήσασθαι [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 20.246; ἔστι μὲν εὕδειν, ἔστι δὲ τερπομένοισιν ἀκούειν 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 15.392]]; εἴ τί πού ἐστι (i.e. πιθέσθαι)[Refs 5th c.BC+ [4.193; τοιάδε.. ἐστὶν ἀκοῦσαι 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Prometheus Vinctus” 1055 (_anapaest meter_); ἔστι τεκμήρια ὁρᾶν 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 3.2.13, compare 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Ranae” 1163, 4th c.BC: Aeschines Orator 3.105, 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 18.272, 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Ἀθηναίων Πολιτεία” 53.6, etc.]]; so in imperative, optative, and subjunctive, ἔστω ἀποφέρεσθαι τῷ βουλομένῳ [Refs 8th c.BC+ [“IG” 12.10.7; μυρία ἂν εἴη λέγειν 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Politicus” 271e; ὅπως ἂν ᾖ δρᾶν “IG” 2.1054.91: more frequently in _negative_ clauses, 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 6.267, etc.]]; followed by ὥστε with infinitive, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Philoctetes” 656]]: with accusative et infinitive, ἁδόντα δ᾽ εἴη με τοῖς ἀγαθοῖς ὁμιλεῖν [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “P.” 2.96; ἔστιν ἐκπεσεῖν ἀρχῆς Δία 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Prometheus Vinctus” 757]]: sometimes not impersonal in this sense, θάλασσα δ᾽ οὐκέτ᾽ ἦν ἰδεῖν [Refs [[prev. author] “Pers.” 419.]]

__A.VI.b
ἔστω in argument, let it be granted, ἔστω τοῦτο ἀληθὲς εἶναι [Refs 4th c.BC+ [1st c.BC: Dionysius Halicarnassensis “de Compositione Verborum” 25; ἔστω σοι τοῦθ᾽ οὕτως 1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus 2.987b; ἔστω εἶναί τινα τοιοῦτον 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator Chr.74.24.]]

__B
most frequently, to be, the Copula connecting the predicate with the Subject, both being in the same case: hence, signify, import, τὸ γὰρ εἴρειν λέγειν ἐστίν [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Cratylus” 398d]]; especially in the phrase τοῦτ᾽ ἔστι, hoc est; Σκαιόλαν, ὅπερ ἐστὶ Λαϊόν [Refs 1st c.AD+ [1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus “Publicola” 17: with numerals, τὰ δὶς πέντε δέκα ἐστίν]] twice five are ten, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Memorabilia” 4.4.7]]; εἶναί τις or τι, to be somebody, something, be of some consequence, see at {τι; οὐδὲν εἶναι} [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 562d, etc.]]

__B.2
periphrastic with the Participle to represent the finite Verb: with perfect participle once in [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Homerus Epicus, τετληότες εἰμέν, for τετλήκαμεν, 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 5.873]]; so in Trag. and Attic dialect, ἦν τεθνηκώς, for ἐτεθνήκει, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Agamemnon” 869]]; ἔσται δεδορκώς[Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. work] 1179; εἰμὶ γεγώς 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Ajax” 1299; πεφυκός ἐστι 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Aves” 1473; δεδρακότες εἰσίν 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 3.68; κατακεκονότες ἔσεσθε 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 7.6.36]]: with aorist participle, once in [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Homerus Epicus, βλήμενος ἦν 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 4.211]]; so προδείσας εἰμί, οὐ σιωπήσας ἔσε; [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Tyrannus” 90, 1146, compare 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Supplices” 460]]: with present participle, ἦν προκείμενον [Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. author] “Pers.” 371; φεύγων Ὀρέστης ἐστίν [prev. author] “Ch.” 136; εἴην οὐκ ἂν εὖ φρονῶν 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Ajax” 1330]]; τί δ᾽ ἐστί.. φέρο; [Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. author] “OT” 991, compare 274, 708; λέγων ἐστίν τις 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Hecuba” 1179; ἦν τίς σ᾽ ὑβρίζων [prev. author] “HF” 313; πόρρω ἤδη εἶ πορευόμενος 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Lysis” 204b; βαδίζων εἰμί 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Ranae” 36; frequently in 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus, ἦσαν ἱέντες 1.57, +others; even εἰσὶ διάφοροι ἐόντες 3.49 (assuming variant):]] — if the _Article_ is joined with the Part., the noun is made emphatic, Κᾶρές εἰσι οἱ καταδέξαντες the persons who showed her were Carians, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. author] 1.171; αὐτὸς ἦν ὁ μαρτυρῶν 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Eumenides” 798; δόλος ἦν ὁ φράσας 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Electra” 197 (_anapaest meter_).]]

__C
εἶναι is frequently modified in sense by the addition of adverbs, or the cases of Nouns without or with Preps.:

__C.I
εἶναι with adverbs, where the adverb often merely represents a Noun and stands as the predicate, ἅλις δέ οἱ ἦσαν ἄρουραι [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 14.122, etc.]]; ἀκέων, ἀκήν εἶναι, to be silent,[Refs 8th c.BC+ [4.22, 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 2.82; σῖγα πᾶς ἔστω λεώς 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Hecuba” 532; διαγνῶναι χαλεπῶς ἦν ἄνδρα ἕκαστον 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 7.424]]; ἀσφαλέως ἡ κομιδὴ ἔσται will go on safely, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 4.134]]; ἐγγύς, πόρρω εἶναι, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 6.88, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Protagoras” 356e: frequently _impersonal_ with words implying good or ill fortune, Κουρήτεσσι κακῶς ἦν]] it fared ill with them, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 9.551; εὖ γὰρ ἔσται 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Medea” 89, compare 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Plutus” 1188, etc.; ἡδέως ἂν αὐτοῖς εἴη 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 59.30.]]

__C.II
with genitive, to express descent or extraction, πατρὸς δ᾽ εἴμ᾽ ἀγαθοῖο [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 21.109; αἵματός εἰς ἀγαθοῖο 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 4.611, compare 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 3.71, 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 2.71, etc.; πόλεως μεγίστης εἶ 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 7.3.19.]]

__C.II.b
to express the material of which a thing is made, ἡ κρηπίς ἐστι λίθων μεγάλων consists of.., [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.93; τῆς πόλιος ἐούσης δύο φαρσέων [prev. work] 186]]; τοιούτων ἔργων ἐστὶ ἡ τυραννίς is made up of.., [Refs [[prev. author] 5.92]].ή, etc.

__C.II.c
to express the class to which a person or thing belongs, εἶ γὰρ τῶν φίλων you are one of them, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Plutus” 345; ἐτύγχανε βουλῆς ὤν 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 3.70; ὅσοι ἦσαν τῶν προτέρων στρατιωτῶν [prev. author] 7.44; Κριτίας τῶν τριάκοντα ὤν 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Memorabilia” 1.2.31]]; ἔστι τῶν αἰσχρῶν it is in the class of disgraceful things, i. e. it is disgraceful, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 2.2.]]

__C.II.d
to express that a thing belongs to another, Τροίαν Ἀχαιῶν οὖσαν [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Agamemnon” 269; τὸ πεδίον ἦν μέν κοτε Χορασμίων 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 3.117, etc.]]: hence, to be of the party of, ἦσαν.. τινὲς μὲν φιλίππου, τινὲς δὲ τοῦ βελτίστου [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 9.56, compare 37.53]]; to be de pendent upon, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Antigone” 737, etc.]]; to be at the mercy of, ἔστι τοῦ λέγοντος, ἢν φόβους λέγῃ [Refs [[prev. author] “OT” 917.]]

__C.II.e
to express one's duty, business, custom, nature, and the like, οὔτοι γυναικός ἐστι 'tis not a woman's part, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Agamemnon” 940; τὸ ἐπιτιμᾶν παντὸς εἶναι 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 1.16]]; τὸ δὲ ναυτικὸν τέχνης ἐστίν is matter of art, requires art, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 1.142, compare 83.]]

__C.II.f
in LXX, to be occupied about, ἦσαν τοῦ θύειν [LXX.2Ch.30.17]; ἔσεσθαι, with genitive, to be about to, ἐσόμεθα τοῦ σῶσαί σε [LXX.2Ki.10.11.]

__C.III
with the dative, ἐστί μοι I have, frequently in [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Homerus Epicus, etc.]]

__C.III.2
with two datives., σφίσι τε καὶ Ἀθηναίοισι εἶναι οὐδὲν πρῆγμα that they and the Athenians have nothing to do one with another, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 5.84; μηδὲν εἶναι σοὶ καὶ φιλίππῳ πρᾶγμα 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 18.283]]; more shortly, σοί τε καὶ τούτοισι πρήγμασι τί ἐστ; [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 5.33]]; τί τῷ νόμῳ καὶ τῇ βασάν; [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 29.36]]; τί ἐμοὶ καὶ σο; Latin quid tecum est mihi? [NT.Mark.5.7, etc.]; also ἐμοὶ οὐδὲν πρὸς τοὺς τοιούτους (i.e. ἐστίν) [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Isocrates Orator 4.12; ἐν οἷς πρὸς τοὺς ἐναντίους ἐστὶ τῷ δήμῳ 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 18.278]]; ἔσται αὐτῳ πρὸς τὸν θεόν, in tomb inscriptions, [Refs [“JHS” 18.113, etc.]]

__C.III.3
with ἄσμενος, βουλόμενος, etc., added, ἐμοὶ δέ κεν ἀσμένῳ εἴη 'twould be to my delight, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 14.108; οὐκ ἂν σφίσι βουλομένοις εἶναι 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 7.35; προσδεχομένῳ [prev. author] 6.46; θέλοντι 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Tyrannus” 1356 (Lyric poetry); ἡδομένοις 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Laches” 187c.]]

__C.IV
with Preps., εἶναι ἀπό τινος, ={εἶναί τινος}[Refs 5th c.BC+ [(above 11.a), 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Memorabilia” 1.6.9; εἰσὶν ἀπ᾽ ἐναντίων αὗται πραγμάτων 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Philebus” 12d]]; but εἶναι ἀπ᾽ οἴκου to be away from.., [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 1.99.]]

__C.IV.2
εἶναι ἔκ τινος to be sprung from, εἴμ᾽ ἐκ Παιονίης, Μυρμιδόνων ἔξ εἰμι, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 21.154, 24.397, etc.]]; ἔστιν ἐξ ἀνάγκης it is of necessity, i. e. necessary, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Sophista” 256d.]]

__C.IV.3
εἶναι ἐν.. to be in a certain state, ἐν εὐπαθείῃσι [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.22]]; ἐν ἀθυμία, etc., [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 6.46, etc.; ἐν ταραχαῖς 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 18.218]]; εἶναι ἐν ἀξιώματι to be in esteem, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 1.130]]; οἱ ἐν τέλεϊ ἐόντες those in office, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 3.18, etc.]]; but εἶναι ἐν τέχνῃ, ἐν φιλοσοφία to be engaged in.., [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Tyrannus” 562, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Phaedo” 59a.]]

__C.IV.3.b
ἐν σοί ἐστι it depends on thee, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 6.109, 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Philoctetes” 963; ἐν σοὶ γάρ ἐσμεν [prev. author] “OT” 314; so also ἐπί τινι [prev. author] “Ph.” 1003, 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 1.6.2, etc.]]

__C.IV.4
εἶναι διά.., much like{εἶναι ἐν}.., εἶναι διὰ φόβου, ={φοβεῖσθαι}, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 6.34]]; εἶναι δι᾽ ὄχλου, ={ὀχληρὸν εἶναι}, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. author] 1.73; εἶναι διὰ μόχθων 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 1.6.25]]; εἶναι δι᾽ αἰτίας, ={αἰτιᾶσθαι}, [Refs 1st c.BC+ [1st c.BC: Dionysius Halicarnassensis 1.70]]; Geometry texts, pass through, διὰ τᾶς ἑτέρας διαμέτρου ἐόντος τοῦ ἐπιπέδου [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [3rd c.BC: Archimedes Geometra “περὶ κωνοειδέων καὶ σφαιροειδέων” 20.]]

__C.IV.5
εἶναι ἐφ᾽ ἑαυτῆς to be by oneself, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 25.23]]; εἶναι ἐπὶ ὀνόματος to bear a name, [Refs [[prev. author] 39.21]]; εἶναι ἐπὶ τοῖς πράγμασιν to be engaged in.., [Refs [[prev. author] 2.12]]; εἶναι ἐπί τινα to be against him, [Refs [[prev. author] 6.33]]; εἶναι ἐφ᾽ ἑξήκοντα στάδια to reach sixty stadia, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 4.6.11]]; εἶναι ἐπὶ τὰς ἁφάς pass through the points of contact, [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd c.AD: Apollonius Biographus Perg. “Con.” 4.1]]; εἶναι ἐπί τινι, see above 3 b.

__C.IV.6
εἶναι πρός τινος to be in one's favour, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 4.10, 29, etc.]]; to suit, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 1.2.11, etc.]]; εἶναι πρός τινι engaged in, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Phaedo” 84c, 2nd-3rd c.AD: Philostratus Sophista “Vita Apollonii” 5.31]]; πρὸς τοῖς ἰδίοις mind one's own affairs, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Politica” 1309a6, “Ath.” 16.3; εἶναι πρὸς τὸ κωλύειν 2nd c.BC: Polybius Historicus 1.26.3]]; πρὸς τὸ πονεῖν[Refs 5th c.BC+ [Teles p.46 H.; εἶναι περί τι 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 3.5.7, etc.]]

__C.IV.7
εἶναι παρά τινι or τινα, = παρειναι, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. author] “Cyr.” 6.2.15, 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 8.140.ά]] (assuming variant).

__C.IV.8
εἶναι ὑπό τινα or τινι to be subject to.., [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Historia Graeca (Hellenica)” 5.2.17 (assuming variant), 6.2.4.]]

__C.IV.9
περὶ τούτων ἐστίν that is the question, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-3rd c.BC: Menander Comicus “Ἐπιτρέποντες” 30.]]

__C.IV.10
εἶναι ἀπό.., in Geometry texts, to be constructed upon, [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [3rd c.BC: Archimedes Geometra “περὶ σφαίρας καὶ κυλίνδρου” 2.9, “Con.Sph.” 7.]]

__D
ἐστί is very frequently omitted, mostly in the present indicative before certain predicates, as ἀνάγκη, ἄξιον, δυνατόν, εἰκός, ἕτοιμον, οἷόν τε, ῥᾴδιον, χρεών, etc., and after the neuter of Verbals in -τέος, and such forms as θαυμαστὸν ὅσον: less frequently with other persons and moods, εἰμί omitted, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Tyrannus” 92, “Aj.” 813]]; εἶ, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 4.206]]; ἐσμέν, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Antigone” 634]]; ἐστέ, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 10.463]]; εἰσί, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Tyrannus” 499 (Lyric poetry), “IG” 2.778 B]]; subjunctive ᾖ, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 14.376, 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Hippolytus” 659, 5th c.BC: Antipho Orator 5.32]]; optative εἴη, [Refs [“IG” 22.1183.12]]; imperfect ἦν, [Refs [[prev. work]2.778 B]]; future ἔσονται, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 14.394.]]

__E
the Inf. frequently seems redundant,

__E.1
in phrases implying power or will to do a thing, ἑκὼν εἶναι (see. ἑκών) κατὰ δύναμιν εἶναι [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Isaeus Orator 2.32; εἰς δύναμιν εἶναι 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Politicus” 300c]]; τὸ ἐπ᾽ ἐκείνοις εἶναι, quantum in illis esset, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 8.48, 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Historia Graeca (Hellenica)” 3.5.9, compare 5th c.BC: Lysias Orator 13.58; τὸ ἐπὶ σφᾶς εἶναι 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 4.28; τὸ κατὰ τοῦτον εἶναι 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 1.6.9; κατὰ τοῦτο εἶναι 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Protagoras” 317a]]; τὸ τήμερον, τὸ νῦν εἶναι, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [[prev. author] “Cra.” 396e, “La.” 201c, Theopomp. Comedy texts 98, Decrees cited in 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Ἀθηναίων Πολιτεία” 31.2, etc.]]

__E.2
after Verbs of naming or choosing, σοφιστὴν ὀνομάζουσι τὸν ἄνδρα εἶναι [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Protagoras” 311e; σύμμαχόν μιν εἵλοντο εἶναι 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 8.134]]; of giving, δῶκε ξεινήϊον εἶναι [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 11.20.]]

__F
imperfect ἦνissts. used where other languages take the present,

__F.1
after ἄρα, to express a fact which is and has always been the same, δέρμα δὲ ἀνθρώπου.. ἦν ἄρα σχεδὸν δερμάτων πάντων λαμπρότατον human skin then it appears is.., [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 4.64; Κύπρις οὐκ ἄρ᾽ ἦν θεός 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Hippolytus” 359]]; ὡς ἄρ᾽ ἦσθ᾽ ἐμὸς πατὴρ ὀρθῶς[Refs 3rd c.BC+ [[prev. work] 1169; ἦ πολύμοχθον ἄρ᾽ ἦν γένος.. ἁμερίων [prev. author] “IA” 1330; ἦ στωμύλος ἦσθα 3rd c.BC: Theocritus Poeta Bucolicus 5.79]]; so also when there is reference to a past thought, τουτὶ τί ἦ; what is this? [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Acharnenses” 157, compare 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Cratylus” 387c: so in the Aristotelian formula τὸ τί ἦν εἶναι (“APo.” 82b38, +others)]], used to express the essential nature of a thing, where τί ἦν (for ἐστί) takes the place of the dative in such phrases as τὸ ἀγαθῷ εἶναι, τὸ μεγέθει εἶναι, [Refs [“APr.” 67b12, “de An.” 429b10.]]

__G
ἐγώ εἰμι, in [LXX, pleonastic for ἐγώ, ἐγώ εἰμι οὐχ ἥμαρτον LXX.Judg.11.27, compare 6.18; also ἔσται πᾶς ἀποκτενεῖ με LXX.Gen.4.14.]

πάθημα, -τος, τό
(πάσχω), like πάθος,
__1. that which befalls one, a suffering, affliction: pl., Rom.8:18, 2Co.1:6-7, Col.1:24, 2Ti.3:11, Heb.2:10 10:32, 1Pe.5:9; of Christ's sufferings: τὰ εἰς Χ., 1Pe.1:11; τ. Χριστσῦ, 1Pe.5:1; id. as shared by Christians, 2Co.1:5, Php.3:10, 1Pe.4:13.

πᾰθ-ημα, ατος, τό,
dative plural παθημάτοις [Refs [“Comica Adespota” 283 (Aetol. _accusative_ to 12th c.AD: Eustathius Episcopus Thessalonicensis 279.42, 1761.36)]]:—that which befalls one, suffering, misfortune, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Trachiniae” 142, 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 4.48, etc.]]; τὸ π. τοῦ Χριστοῦ the passion of Christ, [NT.2Cor.1.5]; of good fortune, χαῖρε παθὼν τὸ π. __II
emotion or condition, affection, π. τῆς ψυχῆς εἶναι τὴν σωφροσύνην, οὐ μάθημα [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 3.1.17, compare 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Phaedo” 79d]]; opposed to ποίημα, [Refs 3rd c.AD+ [[prev. author] “Sph.” 248b; τὸ τῆς ἑτέρας χειρὸς π. 3rd c.AD: Plotinus Philosophus 4.9.2]]; but in early writers mostly in plural, affections, feelings, opposed to ποιήματα, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 437b; τὰ περὶ τὸ σῶμα π. [prev. author] “Phlb.” 33d; ὅσα διὰ τοῦ σώματος π. ἐπὶ τὴν ψυχὴν τείνει [prev. author] “Tht.” 186c; π. ἐν τῇ ψυχῇ γιγνόμενα [prev. author] “R.” 511d]]; παθήμασιν ὑπηρετεῖν obey the feelings, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Politica” 1254b24]]; opposed to ἤθη, ἕξεις, [Refs [[prev. author] “Rh.” 1396b33, compare “Po.” 1449b28.]]

__II.2
in Medicine texts, plural, troubles, symptoms, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Hippocrates Medicus “περὶ ἀρχαίης ἰητρικῇς” 2, “Epid.” 2.2.24; π. καὶ νοσήματα 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 439d, compare 389c.]]

incidents or changes of material bodies, τὰ οὐράνια π. [Refs 4th c.BC+ [[prev. author] “Ion” 531c, compare “Phd.” 98a; τὰ τῆς σελήνης π. 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Metaphysica” 982b16, compare “Mete.” 363a24, 365a12.]]

__III.3
in Logic, incidents, properties, or accidents, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Phaedrus” 271b, “Prm.” 141d, 157b, 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Analytica Posteriora” 76b13, “Cael.” 310a20]]; τὰ π. τὰ αἰσθητά, of colour, etc., [Refs [[prev. author] “Sens.” 445b4.]]

πάθος, -ους, τό
(πάιτχω), [in LXX: Job.30:31 (אֵבֶל), Pro.25:20, and very frequently in (4Ma.1:1 n, al.)* ;]
like πάθημα;
__1. that which befalls one, that which one suffers

(paroxytone), τό, diminutive of παῖς (never in Trag.), little or young child (up to 7 years, accusative to [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Hippocrates Medicus cited in 1st c.AD: Philo Judaeus 1.26), 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.110, 2.119, 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Pax” 50; τὰ νεωστὶ γεγονότα π. 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Lysis” 212e]]; ἐκ παιδίου from a child, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Equites” 412, 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 1.6.20: proverbial, τοῦ πατρὸς τὸ π.]] 'chip of the old block', [Refs 1st c.BC+ [“Comica Adespota” 672, title of satire by Varro; so τῆς μητρὸς τὸ π. 1st c.BC-1st c.AD: Strabo Geographus 10.3.15 (with play on Μήτηρ).]]

young slave, male or female, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [“IG” 12.329.27, 22.1554.67, 1556.22, 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Ranae” 37, “Nu.” 132, “Av.” 1150 (assuming variant).]]

παίδι-ος, ὁ, barbarism for {παιδιόθεν}, [Refs 1st c.AD+ [1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus “Alexander” 27.]]

παίζω
(παῖς), [in LXX: Gen.21:9 26:8, Exo.32:6 (צָחַק pi.); and more frequently (Jdg.16:25, al.) for (שָׂחַק pi. ;]

παίζω,
Doric dialect παίσδω [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [3rd c.BC: Theocritus Poeta Bucolicus 15.42]]: Laconian dialect present participle genitive plural feminine παιδδωἇν [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Lysistrata” 1313 (Lyric poetry):]]future παιξοῦμαι Syrac. in [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Symposium” 9.2]], παίξομαι [LXX+3rd c.BC+ [LXX.2Ki.6.21, “Anthologia Graeca” 12.46 (3rd c.BC: Asclepiades Epigrammaticus), παίξω [prev. work] 211 (2nd c.AD: Strato Epigrammaticus), “Anacreontea” 41.8]]: aorist 1 ἔπαισα [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Homerus Epicus (see. below), 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Plutus” 1055, etc.]]: perfect πέπαικα [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-3rd c.BC: Menander Comicus 923.3]]: perfect passive πέπαισμαι [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 4.77 (variant{πέπλασται}), 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Thesmophoriazusae” 1227; _imperative_ πεπαίσθω 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Euthydemus” 278d]]: also aorist ἔπαιξα [LXX+5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Crates Comicus 23, 5th-6th c.BC: Ctesias Historicus “fragment” 29.59, LXX.Judg.16.25, 2nd c.AD: Lucianus Sophista “DDeor.” 6.4, etc.]]: perfect πέπαιχα [Refs 1st c.AD+ [1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus “Demosthenes” 9]]:—passive, aorist ἐπαίχθην [Refs 3rd c.AD+ [[prev. author] 2.123f, 3rd c.AD: Heliodorus Scriptor Eroticus 8.6]]: perfect πέπαιγμαι [Refs [“epigram Gr.” 979.3 (from Philae)]]; infinitive πεπαῖχθαι Timarch. cited in [Refs 8th c.BC+ [2nd c.AD: Athenaeus Epigrammaticus 11.501f; _imperative_ πεπαίχθω 1st c.BC: Philodemus Gadarensis Epigrammaticus “Mus.” p.106 K., Fronto “Epig.Gr.” 5.86: 8th c.BC: Homerus Epicus]] uses only present and imperfect, and (in [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 8.251)]]aorist imperative παίσατ; Trag. only present: (παῖς):—properly, play like a child, sport, τῇ δέ θ᾽ ἅμα Νύμφαι.. ἀγρονόμοι παίζουσι [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 6.106, compare 7.291 (never in 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad”), 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.114, etc.: _metaphorically_, αἰὼν παῖς ἐστὶ παίζων 1st c.AD(?): Heraclitus 52.]]

__2
especially dance, παίσατε [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 8.251; δῶμα περιστεναχίζετο ποσσὶν ἀνδρῶν παιζόντων 23.147, compare 8th-7th c.BC: Hesiodus Epicus “Scutum Herculis” 277; π. τε καὶ χορεύειν 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Ranae” 409, compare 390; ἐνόπλια χαλκωθεὶς ἔπαιζεν 5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “O.” 13.86:]] —passive, ἀλλὰ πέπαισται μετρίως ἡμῖν, of the chorus, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Thesmophoriazusae” 1227.]]

__3
play [a game], σφαίρῃ π. [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 6.100; κλεψύδρῃ 5th c.BC: Empedocles Poeta Philosophus 100.9]]; κύβοις ἐπὶ συνθήκαις π. Ctes.[same place]; ἀντ᾽ ἀστραγάλων κονδύλοισι π. [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Pherecrates Comicus 43, compare 4th c.BC: Antiphanes Comicus 92]]; π. διὰ γραμμῆς (see. γραμμή[Refs 5th c.BC+ [III. 2); π. πρὸς κότταβον 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Comicus 46.1]]; μετά τινων with others, [Refs 6th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.114: with _accusative_ _cognate_, κότταβον ἀγκύλῃ π. 6th c.BC: Anacreon Lyricus 53 (uncertain); σφαῖραν 1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus “Alexander” 73; π. παιδιὰν πρός τινα 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Plutus” 1055, compare 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus Alcaeus1.110b]]; κύνα καὶ πόλιν π., of a game similar to our draughts, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Cratinus Comicus 56: with _adverbs_, φαινίνδα π. 4th c.BC: Antiphanes Comicus 283, compare 5th c.BC: Crates Comicus [same place], etc.]]

__4
play on a musical instrument, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [“hymnus ad Apollinem” 206: with _accusative_, Πὰν ὁ καλαμόφθογγα παίζων 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Ranae” 230]]; dance and sing, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “O.” 1.16.]]

__5
play amorously, πρὸς ἀλλήλους [LXX+5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Symposium” 9.2; μετά τινος LXX.Gen.26.8]]; of mares, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Historia Animalium” 572a30.]]

__6
hunt, pursue game, π. κατ᾽ ἄλσος [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Electra” 567.]]

__II
jest, sport, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 2.28, 5.4, 9.11]]; opposed to σπουδάζω, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Memorabilia” 4.1.1]]; opposed to σπουδῇ λέγω, [Refs [[prev. author] “Cyr.” 8.3.47]]; παίζετε ταῦτα λέγοντες (opposed to σπουδάζετε) [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Euthydemus” 283b; π. καὶ χλευάζειν 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Ranae” 376; π. καὶ γελᾶν 4th c.BC: Antiphanes Comicus 218.4; πῖνε, παῖζε 4th c.BC: Amphis Comicus 8]]; π. πρός τινα make fun with a person, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Hercules Furens” 952, compare 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Meno” 79a, 4th-3rd c.BC: Menander Comicus “Περικειρομένη” 198]]; π. εἴς τι play with a thing, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Phaedo” 89b]]: with adjective neuter, τοιαῦτα ἔπαιζον σπουδῇ πρὸς ἀλλήλους [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 6.1.6:]]participle παίζων is frequently absolutely, jestingly, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Theaetetus” 145b, +others]]; opposed to σπουδάζων, [Refs [[prev. author] “Lg.” 636c, +others:]] —passive, ὁ λόγος πέπαισται has been made up as a jest (variant for{πέπλασται}), [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 4.77]]; ταῦτα πεπαίσθω ὑμῖν enough of jest, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Euthydemus” 278d, compare “Phdr.” 278b, 1st c.BC: Philodemus Gadarensis Epigrammaticus [same place]]]; πεπαῖχθαι τὴν λέξιν Timarch. [same place]; τοῦτο τὸ παιζόμενον 'as the joke is', [Refs 1st c.AD+ [1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus 2.1090f; τὸ Μενεδήμῳ πεπαιγμένον [prev. work]81e; but οἷα πέπαιγμαι, in _active_ sense, “epigram Gr.” 979.3 (from Philae).]]

__II.2
with accusative, play with, make sport of, [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd c.AD: Lucianus Sophista “Nigr.” 20, “Anthologia Graeca” 10.64 (6th c.AD: Agathias Historicus et Epigrammaticus).]]

__II.3
Grammars, of words played upon or coined for the joke's sake, οἱ κωμῳδοὶ παίζειν εἰώθασι τὰ τοιαῦτα [Refs 5th c.BC+ [Scholia 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Aves” 42, compare 68, etc.]]

deep_entry:
Abbott-Smith / STEPBible (TBESG)
παῖς, genitive, παιδός, ὁ, ἡ
[in LXX chiefly for עֶבֶד, also for נַעַר, נַעֲרָה, etc. ;]
__1. a child, boy, youth, maiden: ὁ π., Mat.17:18, Luk.2:43 9:42, Act.20:12; ἡ π. Luk.8:51, 54 (on the artic. fern, of address, see M, Pr., 70 f., 235; B1., § 33, 4); pl., Mat.2:16 21:15; of parentage, with genitive, Jhn.4:51
__2. Like Heb. עֶבֶד, Lat. Auer, Fr. garcon, Eng. boy (Æsch., Aristoph., Xen., al.), servant, slave, attendant: Mat.8:6, 8 8:13 Luk.7:7 12:45 15:26; in late writers (Diod., LXX: Gen.41:37, al.), of a king's attendant or minister : Mat.14:2; so (= Heb. יְהוָֹה עֶבֶד) π. τ. θεοῦ (Psa.69:18, Isa.41:8, Wis.2:13, al.), of Israel, Luk.1:54; of David, Luk.1:69, Act.4:25; of Jesus (but see Dalman, Words, 277 f.), Mat.12:18 (LXX), Act.3:13, 26 4:27, 30.†
SYN.:
__1. τέκνον, child, with emphasis on parentage and the consequent community of nature; υἱός, son, with emphasis on the privileged position of heirship; π. refers both to age and parentage, but with emphasis on the former. Cf. also (παιδάριον), (παιδίον), (παιδίσκη), and see Westc. on 1Jn.3:1.
__2. see: θεράπων, and cf. Thackeray, Gr., 7 f
(AS)

LSJ / STEPBible (TFLSJ)
παῖς,
also παῦς (which see), παιδός, ὁ, ἡ, genitive plural παίδων, Doric dialect παιδῶν[Refs 5th c.BC+ [Greg.Cor. p.317 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus]]; dative plural παισί, Epic dialect παίδεσσι [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 3.381, etc.]]; in early Epic dialect frequently disyllable in nominative πάϊς, e. g. when forming part of two different feet, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 2.609, 5.704, etc.]]; probably also in the fifth foot, [Refs [9.57, 11.389]]; and before bucolic diaeresis, [Refs [2.205, +others]]; also in Lyric poetry, [Refs 7th c.BC+ [7th-6th c.BC: Sappho Lyrica 38, 85]]; and in Boeotian dialect, [Refs [“IG” 7.690, +others (from Tanagra)]], compare πῆ; πάϊ [ᾰῑ] [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 24.192]] (παιδ- is never disyllable in oblique cases in [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Homerus Epicus); _accusative_ πάϊν 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus R.4.697, “Anthologia Graeca” 3.8 (Inscription Cyzic.), 9.125]]; genitive παϊδός epigram cited in [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd c.AD: Lucianus Sophista “Symp.” 41]]; dative παϊδί probably in [Refs 6th c.BC+ [6th c.BC: Anacreon Lyricus 17:]]

__I
in relation to Descent, child, whether son, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 2.205, 609, +others (with special reference to the father, opposed to τέκνον, which see): _plural_, 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 1.4, etc.]]; or daughter, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 1.20, 443, 3.175; παῖδες ἄρρενες καὶ θήλειαι 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Leges” 788a]]; παῖς, opposed to κόρα, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [“Berl.Sitzb.” 1927.7 (_Locrian dialect_, 5th c.BC)]]; of an adopted son, ἀλλά σε παῖδα ποιεύμην [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 9.494; παίδων παῖδες, τοί κεν μετόπισθε γένωνται 20.308, compare 5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “N.” 7.100, “Inscription Cyprian dialect” 135.11 H., etc.; Ἀγήνορος παῖδες ἐκ παίδων 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Phoenissae” 281]]; frequently in orators of legal issue, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Isocrates Orator 19.9, 4th c.BC: Isaeus Orator 7.31, etc.]]; of animals, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Agamemnon” 50 (_anapaest meter_).]]

__I.2
metaphorically, ἀμπέλου π., of wine, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “N.” 9.52; χορῶν ἐραστὴς κισσὸς ἐνιαυτοῦ δὲ παῖς 4th c.BC: Chaeremon Tragicus 5]]; ὀρείας πέτρας π., of Echo, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Hecuba” 1110]]; ὅρκου π. ἀνώνυμος, of the penalty of perjury, Oracle texts cited in [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 6.86]].; ἄναυδοι π. τᾶς ἀμιάντου, of fishes, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Persae” 578 (Lyric poetry).]]

__I.3
periphrastic, οἱ Λυδῶν παῖδες sons of the Lydians, i. e. the Lydians, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.27, compare 5.49; π. Ἑλλήνων 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Persae” 402]]; οἱ [Ἀσκληπιοῦ] π., i. e. physicians, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 407e]]; οἱ ζωγράφων π. painters, [Refs [[prev. author] “Lg.” 769b]]; παῖδες ῥητόρων orators, [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd c.AD: Lucianus Sophista “Anach.” 19]]; π. ἰατρῶν, π. πλαστῶν καὶ γραφέων, [Refs [[prev. author] “Dips.” 5, “Im.” 9; compare υἱός 2.]]

__II
in relation to Age, child, boy or girl, νέος π. [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 4.665; παῖδες νεαροί 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 2.289; σμίκρα π. 7th-6th c.BC: Sappho Lyrica 34: with another]] substantive, π. συφορβός boy-swineherd, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 21.282; παῖδα κόρην γαμεῖν 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Lysistrata” 595; ἐν παισὶ νέοισι π. 5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “N.” 3.72; π. ἔτ᾽ ὤν 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Choephori” 755, compare 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 11.710; ἔτι π. 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Protagoras” 310e; παιδὸς μηδὲν βελτίων [prev. work] 342e: distinguished from παιδίον, μειράκιον, 5th c.BC: Hippocrates Medicus “περὶ ἑβδομάδων - Die Hippokratische Schrift von der Siebenzahl” 5, compare 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Symposium” 4.17, “Cyr.” 8.7.6, 1.2.4]]; ἐκ παιδός from a child, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 374c; ἐκ παιδὸς εἰς γῆρας 4th c.BC: Aeschines Orator 1.180; ἐκ τῶν παίδων εὐθύς 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Leges” 694d, compare “R.” 386a; ἀκούων τῶν παίδων εὐθύς [prev. author] “Lg.” 642b; εὐθὺς ἐκ παίδων ἐξελθών 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 21.154]]; ἡλικίαν ἔχειν τὴν ἄρτι ἐκ π. to be just out of one's childhood, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Historia Graeca (Hellenica)” 5.4.25; ἐκ μικρῶν π. 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Politica” 1336a14; [Ἡρακλῆς] ἐν παισὶν ὄφεις ἀπέκτεινεν 2nd-3rd c.AD: Dio Cassius Historicus 56.36]]; ἐν παισὶ (variant{παιδὶ}) ποιμαίνων [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd c.AD: Herodianus Grammaticus 6.8.1]]; χορηγεῖν παισί [Refs 5th c.BC+ [compare (χορηγέω 11): proverbial, τοῦτο κἂν π. γνοίη 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Euthydemus” 279d; δῆλον τοῦτό γε ἤδη καὶ παιδί [prev. author] “Smp.” 204b; παῖδας [τοὺς πρὸ αὐτοῦ] ἀπέφηνε 2nd c.AD: Lucianus Sophista “Peregr.” 11, compare “Alex.” 4]]; ἔνι τις καὶ ἐν ἡμῖν π., of the superstitious fears of a child, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Phaedo” 77e, compare 3rd c.AD: Porphyrius Tyrius Philosophus “de Abstinentia - Porphyrii Opuscula” 1.41.]]

__III
in relation to Condition, slave, servant, man or maid (of all ages), παῖ, παῖ [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Choephori” 653, compare 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Acharnenses” 395, 4th c.BC: Epicrates Comicus 5.2, etc.; παῖ, παιδίον 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Nubes” 132]]: plural, of the crew of a ship, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 33.8. (From Παϝις, compare παῦρος]], Latin puer.)

(i.e. πληγάς) 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 5.8.12]]; τί μ᾽ οὐκ ἀνταίαν ἔπαισέν τις (i.e. πληγήν) ; [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Antigone” 1309 (Lyric poetry)]]; π. ἅλμην, of rowers, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Persae” 397, 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Iphigenia Taurica” 1391:]] —middle, ἐπαίσατο τὸν μηρόν he smote his thigh, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 7.3.6, compare 1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus “Pompeius” 24]]:—passive, παιομένους [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 4.47, compare 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Persae” 416, 5th c.BC: Antipho Orator 2.4.4, etc.]]; πὺξ παιόμενος, opposed to ἐγχειριδίῳ πληγείς, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Lysias Orator 4.6.]]

(πάλαι), [in LXX: Lev.25:22 26:10, Sng.7:13 (14) (יָשֵׁן), יָשֵׁן), Jos.9:4-5, Jer.38:11 (בָּלֶה), etc. ;]

πᾰλαιός, ά, όν,
Aeolic dialect πάλαος [Refs [12th c.AD: Eustathius Episcopus Thessalonicensis 28.33, “epigram Gr.” 992 (from Balbilla)]]; Boeotian dialect παληός [Refs [“Etymologicum Magnum” 32.6]]; Laconian dialect παλεός (see. below): regular comparative and superlative παλαιότερος [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “N.” 6.53, 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 1.1 codices, παλαιότατος 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Timaeus” 83a, etc.: more frequently παλαίτερος, παλαίτατος (from πάλαι), 5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “P.” 10.58, “N.” 7.44, 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 1.4, etc.]] [The penultimate is sometimes short in Poets, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Fragmenta” 956 (assuming variant), 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Electra” 497, 1st c.AD: Damocrates Poeta Medicus cited in 2nd c.AD: Galenus Medicus 13.1049; παλεός γα ναὶ τὸν Κάστορα ἄνθρωπος 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Lysistrata” 988]]; in these places παλεός (a form mentioned by Hdn.[Refs 5th c.BC+ [Gr. 2.909, compare 9th c.AD: Theognostus Grammaticus “Can.” 50.3, Scholia 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Lys.” [same place], 10th c.AD: Suidas Legal icographus, and corroborated by the Papyrus (4th c.BC) of Timotheus (see. παλεομίσημα, παλεονυμφάγονος)) may be retained or restored).]:]]

__I
old in years,

__I.1
mostly of persons, aged, ἢ νέος ἠὲ παλαιός [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 14.108; νέοι ἠδὲ παλαιοί 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 1.395, compare 4th-3rd c.BC: Epicurus Philosophus “Epistulae” 3p.59U.; παλαιῷ φωτὶ ἐοικώς 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 14.136]]; π. γέρων, π. γρηῦς, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 13.432, 19.346, compare 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Acharnenses” 676; χρόνῳ π. 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Coloneus” 112; ἐν παλαιτέροισι 5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “N.” 3.73; ἔνθα δὴ παλαίτατοι θάσσουσι 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Medea” 68]]: in bad sense, a dotard (μωρός [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.AD(?): Hesychius Legal icographus, but σκώπτης 10th c.AD: Suidas Legal icographus), 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Lysistrata” 988.]]

__I.2
of things, οἶνος [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 2.340]]; νῆες.. νέαι ἠδὲ π.[Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. work] 293; τρὺξ π. καὶ σαπρά 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Plutus” 1086; [τριήρεις] π. ἀντὶ καινῶν 5th c.BC: Lysias Orator 28.4; ὑποδήματα 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Meno” 91d; σπέρματα 4th-3rd c.BC: Theophrastus Philosophus “Historia Plantarum” 7.1.6.]]

__II
of old date, ancient,

__II.1
of persons, ξεῖνος π. an old guest-friend, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 6.215, compare 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Trachiniae” 263, 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Alcestis” 212; Ἴλου παλαιοῦ 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 11.166; κέρδεα.. οἷ᾽ οὔ πώ τιν᾽ ἀκούομεν οὐδὲ παλαιῶν 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 2.118; Μίνως παλαίτατος ὧν ἀκοῇ ἴς μεν 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 1.4; οἱ πάνυ π. ἄνθρωποι 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Cratylus” 411b]]; οἱ π. the ancients, [LXX+5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 1.3; π. ἡμερῶν LXX.Dan.7.9.]]

__II.2
of things, λέκτρον [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 23.296; παλαιά τε πολλά τε εἰδώς 7.157; καινὰ καὶ π. ἔργα 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 9.26; νόμοι 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Eumenides” 778 (Lyric poetry); κατὰ τὸ νόμιμον τὸ π. καὶ ἀρχαῖον 5th c.BC: Lysias Orator 6.51; κατὰ τὸν π. λόγον 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Gorgias” 499c; ἡ π. παροιμία [prev. author] “R.” 329a; παλαί᾽ ἂν [εἴη], ἐξ ὅτου 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Philoctetes” 493; παλαιᾷ σύντροφος ἁμερᾷ [prev. author] “Aj.” 622 (Lyric poetry)]]; of places, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Persae” 17 (_anapaest meter_), 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Electra” 4, etc.]]; καιροὶ π. ancient times, [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [“PPetr.” 2p.15 (3rd c.BC)]]; τὸ π. as adverb, anciently, formerly, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Persae” 102 (Lyric poetry), 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.171, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Cratylus” 401c, etc.]]; ἐκ παλαιοῦ from of old, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.157; ἐκ π. ἐχθρὸς ὢν αὐτοῦ 5th c.BC: Antipho Orator 2.1.5; ἐκ τῶν παλαιῶν 3rd c.BC: Herodas Mimographus 2.102]]; ἐκ παλαιτέρου from older time, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.60; ἐκ παλαιτάτου 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 1.18; also εὐθὺς ἀπὸ παλαιοῦ [prev. work] 2]]; ἀρχαῖα καὶ παλαιά joined, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 22.14, compare 5th c.BC: Lysias Orator (see. above); παλαιὸν δῶρον ἀρχαίου ποτὲ θηρός 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Trachiniae” 555.]]

__II.3
of things, also,

__II.3.a
in good sense, venerable, held in esteem, like Latin antiquus, ἅπερ μέγιστα καὶ παλαιότατα τοῖς ἀνθρώποις [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Antipho Orator 6.4.]]

__II.3.b
in bad sense, antiquated, obsolete, κωφὰ καὶ π. ἔπη [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Tyrannus” 290.]]

__II.3.c
π. δρᾶμα a drama which has been previously acted, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [“SIG” 1078 lxxxvii (Athens, 4th c.BC).]]

__III
adverb παλαιῶς in an old way, τὰ καινὰ π. διδάσκειν [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-4th c.BC: Socratis et Socraticorum Epistulae “Ep.” 30.9: _comparative_ παλαίτερον]] at an earlier time, [Refs 1st c.BC+ [1st c.BC: Dionysius Halicarnassensis 8.57, +others]]
