Abbott-Smith / STEPBible (TBESG)
παρά, prep. with genitive, dative, accusative,
with radical sense, beside.
__I. C. genitive of person(s), from the side of, from beside, from, indicating source or origin, [in LXX for מֵאֵצֶל ,מִיַד ,מִלִּפְנֵי ;] after verbs of motion, Mrk.14:43, Luk.8:49, Jhn.15:26, al.; after verbs of seeking, receiving, hearing, etc., Mrk.8:11 12:2, Jhn.4:9, 52 10:18, Php.4:18, 2Ti.1:18, Jas.1:7, al.; after passive verbs, of the agent (like ὑπό), Mat.21:42, Mrk.12:11, Luk.1:37; absol., οἱ παρ᾽ αὐτοῦ, his family, his kinsfolk, Mrk.3:21 (cf. M, Pr., 106f.; Field, Notes, 25f.; Swete, in l.); τὰ παρ᾽ αὐτῆς (αὐτῶν, ὑμῶν, one's means, wealth, Mrk.5:26, Luk.10:7, Php.4:18.

__II. C. dative of person(s) (exc. Jhn.19:25, π. τ. σταυρῷ), by the side of, beside, by, with, [in LXX for בְּעֵינֵי ,בְּיַד ,אֵצֶל ;] Luk.11:37 19:7, Jhn.1:40 4:40, Act.28:14, al.; παρ᾽ ἑαυτῷ, at home, 1Co.16:2; with dative pl., among, Mat.22:25, Col.4:16, al.; metaphorically, Mat.19:26, Mrk.10:27, Luk.1:30, Rom.2:13, Jas.1:27, al.

__III. C. accusative, of motion by or towards, [in LXX for בְּעֵבֶר ,עַל יַד ,אֵצֶל ;]
__1. of place, by the side of, beside, by, along: Act.10:32, Heb.11:12; after verbs of motion, Mat.4:18, Mrk.4:4, Luk.8:5, Act.4:35, al.; after verbs of rest, Mat.13:1, Mrk.5:21, Luk.8:35, al.
__2. beside, beyond, metaphorically;
__(a) beyond, against, contrary to: Act.18:13, Rom.1:26 4:18 11:24, al.; except, 2Co.11:24;
__(b) beyond, above, in comparison with: Luk.3:13, Rom.12:3 14:5, Heb.1:4, 9 3:3, al.;
__(with) on account of: 1Co.12:15, 16.
__IV. In composition: beside, to (παραλαμβάνω, παράγω), at hand (πάρειμι), from (παραρρέω), amiss (παρακούω), past (παρέρχομαι), compared with (παρομοιάζω), above measure (παροργίζω).
(AS)

πᾰρά [ρᾰ],
Epic dialect and Lyric poetry also παραί: shortened πάρ, in [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Homerus Epicus]], Lyric poetry (but rarely in Trag., in Lyric poetry passages, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Supplices” 553, 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Trachiniae” 636)]], and in all dial ects except Attic dialect, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [“GDI” 5434.8 (from Paros), “IG” 5(2).3.14 (Tegea, 4th c.BC), “Inscription Magn.” 26.28 (Thess.)]], etc.:—preposition with genitive, dative, and accusative, properly beside: hence,

__A
WITH GEN. properly denoting motion from the side of, from beside, from:

__A.I
of Place, πὰρ νηῶν ἔλθωμεν [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 13.744; παρὰ ναῦφιν ἐλευσόμεθ᾽ 12.225, etc.; παρ᾽ Ὠκεανοῖο ῥοάων.. ἐπερχομένη 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 22.197; πὰρ νηῶν ἀπώσεται 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 8.533, etc.; δῶρα π. νηὸς ἐνεικέμεν 19.194; φάσγανον ὀξὺ ἐρυσσάμενος π. μηροῦ 1.190, compare 21.173; σπασσάμενος.. ἄορ παχέος π. μηροῦ 16.473]]; πλευρὰ παρ᾽ ἀσπίδος ἐξεφαάνθη was exposed beside the shield,[Refs 4th c.BC+ [4.468, compare 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Septem contra Thebas” 624.]]

__A.II
commonly of Persons,

__A.II.1
with Verbs of going or coming, bringing, etc., ἦλθε.. πὰρ Διός [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 2.787; παρ᾽ Αἰήταο πλέουσα 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 12.70, etc.; ἀγγελίη ἥκει π. βασιλέος 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 8.140. ; αὐτομολήσαντες π. βασιλέως 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 1.7.13; ἐξεληλυθὼς παρ᾽ Ἀριστάρχου 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 21.117]]; ὁ π. τινὸς ἥκων his messenger, [NT+5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 4.5.53; so οἱ π. τινός 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 7.10, NT.Mark.3.21, etc.; ὅστις ἀφικνεῖτο τῶν π. βασιλέως πρὸς αὐτόν 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 1.1.5, etc.]]; τεύχεα καλὰ φέρουσα παρ᾽ Ἡφαίστοιο from his workshop, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 18.137, compare 617, etc.; ἀπαγγέλλειν τι π. τινός 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 2.1.20; σὺ δὲ οἰμώζειν αὐτοῖς παρ᾽ ἐμοῦ λέγε 2nd c.AD: Lucianus Sophista “DMort.” 1.2.]]

__A.II.2
issuing from a person, γίγνεσθαι π. τινός to be born from, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Symposium” 179b]]; λόγος (i.e. ἐστί) π. Ἀθηναίων with accusative et infinitive, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 8.55: frequently following a Noun, δόξα ἡ π. τῶν ἀνθρώπων]] glory from (given by) men, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Phaedrus” 232a]]; ἡ π. τινὸς εὔνοια the favour from, i. e. of, any one, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Memorabilia” 2.2.12]]; τὸ παρ᾽ ἐμοῦ ἀδίκημα done by me, [Refs [[prev. author] “Cyr.” 5.5.13]]; τὰ π. τινός all that issues from any one, as commands, commissions, [Refs [[prev. author] “An.” 2.3.4, etc.; or promises, gifts, presents, [prev. author] “Mem.” 3.11.13]]; τὰ παρ᾽ ἐμοῦ my opinions, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Symposium” 219a]]; παρ᾽ ἑωυτοῦ διδούς giving from oneself, i. e. from one's own means, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 2.129, 8.5; παρ᾽ ἑαυτοῦ προσετίθει 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Historia Graeca (Hellenica)” 6.1.3]]; νόμον θὲς παρ᾽ ἐμοῦ by my advice, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Protagoras” 322d]]; αὐτοὶ παρ᾽ αὑτῶν of themselves, [Refs [[prev. author] “Tht.” 150d, compare “Phdr.” 235c.]]

__A.II.3
with Verbs of receiving, obtaining, and the like, τυχεῖν τινος π. τινός [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 6.290, 15.158; πὰρ δ᾽ ἄρα μιν Ταφίων πρίατο 14.452; ἀρέομαι πὰρ μὲν Σαλαμῖνος Ἀθαναίων χάριν 5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “P.” 1.76; εὑρέσθαι τι π. τῶν θεῶν 5th-6th c.BC: Isocrates Orator 9.14, compare “IG” 12.40.10]]; δέχεσθαι, λαμβάνειν, ἁρπάζειν π. τινός, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 1.20, 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Oeconomicus” 9.11, 8th-7th c.BC: Hesiodus Epicus “Theogonia” 914]]; ἀντιάσαι, αἰτήσασθαι π. τινός, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Electra” 870 (Lyric poetry), 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Historia Graeca (Hellenica)” 3.1.4; ἀξιοῖ π. τοῦ ἰατροῦ φάρμακον πιὼν ἐξεμέσαι τὸ νόσημα 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 406d; κόσμος τοῖς πράξασι γίγνεται π. τῶν ἀκουσάντων [prev. author] “Mx.” 236e: without Verb, ὁ καρπὸς ὁ π. τῶν δημάρχων “IG” 12.76.27: with Verbs of learning, etc., μεμαθηκέναι π. τινῶν 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 2.104, etc.]]

__A.II.4
with passive Verbs, πὰρ Διὸς.. μῆνις ἐτύχθη [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 15.122; π. θεῶν ἡ τοιαύτη μανία δίδοται 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Phaedrus” 245c, etc.]]; τὰ π. τῶν θεῶν σημαινόμενα, συμβουλευόμενα, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 1.6.2; τὰ π. τινὸς λεγόμενα [prev. work] 6.1.42]]; τὰ π. τῆς τύχης δωρηθέντα the presents of.., [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Isocrates Orator 4.26; με π. σοῦ σοφίας πληρωθήσεσθαι 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Symposium” 175e.]]

__A.III
rarely for παρά with dative, by, near, πὰρ ποδός [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “P.” 10.62, 3.60]]; παρὰ δὲ κυανέων πελαγέων uncertain reading in [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Antigone” 966 (Lyric poetry); τὸν Ῥειτὸν τὸν παρὰ τοῦ ἄστεως “IG” 12.81.5]]; πολλοὶ παρ᾽ ἀμφοτέρων ἔπιπτον, ={ἀμφοτέρωθεν}, [Refs 1st c.BC+ [1st c.BC: Diodorus Siculus Historicus 19.42.]]

__A.IV
π. τῆς συγχωρήσεώς τινος without his consent, [Refs [“BCH” 46.337 (from Teos).]]

__B
WITH DAT. denoting rest by the side of any person or thing, answering the question where?

of Places, κατ᾽ ἂρ ἕζετ᾽.. πὰρ πυρί, ἔκειτο π. σηκῷ, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 7.154, 9.319; νέμονται π. πέτρῃ 13.408; ἑσταότες παρ ὄχεσφιν 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 8.565]]; πὰρ ποσὶ μαρναμένων ἐκυλίνδετο at their feet, [Refs [14.411]], etc.; π. θύρῃσι at the door,[Refs 8th c.BC+ [7.346; π. ῥηγμῖνι θαλάσσης 2.773; δεῖπνον.. εἵλοντο παρ᾽ ὄχθῃσιν ποταμοῖο 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 6.97, compare 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 4.475, 20.53, etc.; κεῖσθαι παρ᾽ Ἅιδῃ 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Tyrannus” 972]]; παρ᾽ οἴνῳ over wine, [Refs [[prev. work] 780, etc.]]

at one's house or place, with one, μένειν π. τισί [Refs 8th c.BC+ [9.427; θητευέμεν ἄλλῳ, ἀνδρὶ παρ᾽ ἀκλήρῳ 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 11.490; φιλέεσθαι π. τινί 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 13.627]]; παρ᾽ ἑωυτοῖσι at their own house, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.105, compare 86; παιδευθῆναι π. τινί 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 1.2.15; καταλύειν π. τινί 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 18.82 (but παρά τινα καταλῦσαι 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 1.136), etc.: hence οἱ παρ᾽ ἐμοί]] those of my household, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Memorabilia” 2.7.4, etc.]]; τὰ παρ᾽ ἐμοί life with me, [Refs [[prev. author] “An.” 1.7.4]]; οἱ παρ᾽ ἡμῖν ἄνθρωποι our people, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Phaedo” 64b]]; ἡ παρ᾽ ἡμῖν πολιτεία, ὁ παρ᾽ ὑμῖν δῆμος, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 15.19]]; ὁ παρ᾽ αὑτῷ βίοτος one's own life, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Tyrannus” 612; τὸ παρ᾽ ἡμῖν πῦρ 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Philebus” 29f; ὅσος παρ᾽ ὑμῖν ὁ φθόνος φυλάσσεται 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Tyrannus” 382; τὸ παρ᾽ ἡμῖν σῶμα 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Philebus” 29f]]; also, in one's hands, τὰ π. τοῖς Ἑλληνοταμίαις ὄντα [Refs 5th c.BC+ [“IG” 12.91.6; ἔχειν παρ᾽ ἑωυτῷ 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.130, etc.]]; οὔπω παρ᾽ ἐμοὶ τότ᾽ ἦν λέγειν I had no right to speak then, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-3rd c.BC: Menander Comicus “Ἐπιτρέποντες” 98.]]

π. τοσοῦτον ἦλθε κινδύνου, ={παρῆλθε τοσοῦτον κινδύνου}, passed over so much ground within the sphere of danger, i.e. incurred such imminent peril, [Refs [[prev. author] 3.49, compare 7.2]]; in such phrases the tmesis was forgotten, and the accusative came to be governed by παρά, which thus came to mean 'by such and such a margin', 'with so much to spare', ἐνίκησαν π. πολύ, ἡσσηθέντες π. πολύ, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. author] 1.29, 2.89, compare 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Apologia” 36a]]; παρὰ δ᾽ ὀλίγον ἀπέφυγες only just, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Iphigenia Taurica” 870 (Lyric poetry); παρ᾽ ὀλίγον ἢ διέφευγον ἢ ἀπώλλυντο 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 7.71]]; δεινότατον π. πολύ by far, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Plutus” 445]]; παρ᾽ ὅσον quatenus, [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd c.AD: Lucianus Sophista “Nec.” 17, etc.]]; π. δύο ψήφους ἀπέφυγε by two votes, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Hyperides Orator “pro Euxenippo” 28, compare 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 23.205; π. τέτταρας ψήφους μετέσχε τῆς πόλεως 4th c.BC: Isaeus Orator 3.37]]; π. τοσοῦτον ἐγένετο αὐτῷ μὴ περιπεσεῖν by so much (= little) he missed falling in with.., [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 8.33; π. πέντε ναῦς πλέον ἀνδρὶ ἑκάστῳ ἢ τρεῖς ὀβολοὶ ὡμολογήθησαν [prev. work] 29]]; οὐ π. μικρὸν ἐποίησαν they made no little difference, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Isocrates Orator 4.59.]]

__C.III.5.b
in phrases like{π. τοσοῦτον ἦλθε κινδύνου, τοσοῦτον} was sometimes understood of the interval from danger, etc., and παρά came to mean 'by so much short of' (τὸ π. μικρὸν ὥσπερ οὐδὲν ἀπέχειν δοκεῖ [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Physica” 197a29)]], within such and such a distance of, so near to, τὴν Ἠϊόνα π. νύκτα ἐγένετο (i.e. αὐτῷ) λαβεῖν he was within one night of taking [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus, 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 4.106]]; π. μικρὸν ἦλθον ἀποθανεῖν I came within a little of.., [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Isocrates Orator 19.22, compare 2nd c.BC: Polybius Historicus 1.43.7, 1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus “Caesar” 39]]; παρ᾽ ἐλάχιστον ἦλθε.. ἀφελέσθαι was within an ace of taking away, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 8.76]]; παρ᾽ οὐδὲν μὲν ἦλθον ἀποκτεῖναι (were within a mere nothing, within an ace of killing him), ἐξεκήρυξαν δ᾽ ἐκ πόλεως [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aeschines Orator 3.258, compare 1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus “Pyrrhus” 14, “Alex.” 62]]; π. τοσοῦτον ἦλθε διαφυγεῖν so near he came to escaping, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [2nd c.AD: Lucianus Sophista “Cat.” 4; παρὰ ἓν πάλαισμα ἔδραμε νικᾶν Ὀλυμπιάδα 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 9.33; παρ᾽ οὐδὲν ἐλθόντες τοῦ ἀποβαλεῖν 2nd c.BC: Polybius Historicus 1.45.14, compare 2.55.4, 1st c.BC: Diodorus Siculus Historicus 17.42: hence without ἐγένετο or ἐλθεῖν, π. μίαν μονάδα (less)]] by one, i.e. less one, [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd c.AD: Nicomachus Gerasenus Mathematicus “Arithmetica Introductio” 1.8]]; τεσσαράκοντα π. μίαν, =[39, NT.2Cor.11.24]; παρ᾽ ἕνα τοσοῦτοι the same number less one, [Refs 1st c.AD+ [1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus “Publicola” 9]]; σύ μοι παρ᾽ ἕνα ἥκεις ἄγων you have brought me one too few, [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd c.AD: Lucianus Sophista “Cat.” 4; δύναται π. δύο συλλαβὰς εἶναι τὸ καταληκτόν 7th c.AD: Hephaestio Grammaticus 4.2]]; τὰ ὁλοκόττινα ηὑρέθησαν π. ἑπτὰ κεράτια seven carats short, [Refs 6th c.AD+ [PMasp. 70.2 (6th c.AD)]]; πάντες παρ᾽ ἕνα, πάντες παρ᾽ ὀλίγους, all save one (a few), [Refs 1st c.AD+ [1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus “Cat.Mi.” 20, “Ant.” 5; ἔτη δύο π. ἡμέρας δύο “IG” 5(1).801 (from Laconia)]]; of one Μάρκος, θηρίον εἶ π. γράμμα you are a bear (ἄρκος) all but a letter, [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [“Anthologia Graeca” 11.231 (2nd c.AD: Ammianus Epigrammaticus)]]; ὡς π. τι καὶ τὰς ὄψεις ἀφανίσαι so that he all but (literal less something) lost his sight, [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd c.AD: Vettius Valens Astrologus 228.6]]; π. τι βυθίζεσθαι variant in [NT.Luke.5.7]; τὸ π. τοῦτο the figure less that, i.e. the remainder or difference, [Refs 2nd c.BC+ [PTeb. 99.10 (2nd c.BC),compare “POxy.” 264.4 (1st c.AD), “PAmh.” 2.148.5 (5th c.AD)]]; hence of any difference whether of excess or defect, οὐδὲν π. τοῦτο ποιούμενοι τοὺς.. Λευκανούς τε καὶ τοὺς.. Σαυνίτας making no difference between.., [Refs 1st c.BC+ [1st c.BC-1st c.AD: Strabo Geographus 6.1.3, compare 14.5.11, 1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus 2.24c.]]

__C.III.6
hence of the margin by which anything increases or decreases, and so of the cause according to which anything comes into existence or varies, τὸ εὖ π. μικρὸν διὰ πολλῶν ἀριθμῶν γίνεται [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Polyclitus Philosophus 2 (compare μικρός III. 5 c)]]; διαφέρει π. τὰς τῶν παθημάτων ἐναντιώσεις according to.., [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Historia Animalium” 486b5; μεταπίπτει π. τὰ κλίματα 1st c.BC: Geminus Astronomicus 5.29, compare 11.5, +others]]; π. τὰ πράγματα conjecture in [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-3rd c.BC: Apollodorus Carystius Comicus 11.]]

__C.III.7
more generally of the margin by which an event occurs, i.e. of the necessary and sufficient cause or motive (τὸ μὴ π. τοῦτο γίνεσθαι τότε λέγομεν, ὅταν ἀναιρεθέντος τούτου μηδὲν ἧττον περαίνηται ὁ συλλογισμός [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Analytica Priora” 65b6, compare 48a24, +others), κεινὰν π. δίαιταν]] just for the sake of unsatisfying food, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “O.” 2.65]]; ἕκαστος οὐ π. τὴν ἑαυτοῦ ἀμέλειαν οἴεται βλάψειν each thinks that his own negligence will not suffice to cause injury, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 1.141, compare 5th-6th c.BC: Isocrates Orator 3.48]]; π. τὴν αὑτοῦ ἁμαρτίαν all through his own fault, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Antipho Orator 3.4.5, compare 5th-6th c.BC: Isocrates Orator 6.52, 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 4.11, 18.232]]; πολλὰ.. ἐστιν αἴτια τούτων, καὶ οὐ παρ᾽ ἓν οὐδὲ δύ᾽ εἰς τοῦτο τὰ πράγματ᾽ ἀφῖκται not from one or two causes only, [Refs [[prev. author] 9.2]]; οὐ π. τοῦτο οὐκ ἔστι it does not follow that it is not.., [NT.1Cor.12.15]; π. τὸ τὴν ἀρίθμησιν ποιήσασθαι ἐξ ἑτοίμου τοὺς ἐργώνας οὐκ ὀλίγα χρήματα περιεποίησε τῇ πόλει by the simple fact of prompt payment, [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [“IPE” 12.32 B 35 (Olbia, 3rd c.BC)]]; οὐδὲν ἂν παρ᾽ ἕνα ἄνθρωπον ἐγένετο τούτων [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Lycurgus Orator 63, compare 2nd c.BC: Polybius Historicus 3.103.2, 18.28.6, +others]]; οὐδεὶς παρ᾽ ἑαυτόν ἐστι βασιλεύς thanks to himself alone,[Refs 5th c.BC+ [Aristeas 224; παρ᾽ αὑτὸν ἀτυχεῖ 2nd c.AD: Arrianus Historicus “Epicteti Dissertationes” 3.24.2, compare 1st c.BC: Philodemus Gadarensis Epigrammaticus “Rh.” 2.16 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus; παρ᾽ ἡμᾶς ἡ τῶν ἀγαθῶν ἀπόστασις 5th c.AD: Hierocles Platonicus Philosophus “in Carmen Aureum - FPG” 25p.477M.]]; εἶναι π. τοῦτο σωτηρίαν τε πόλει καὶ τοὐναντίον, i.e. on this depends.., [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Leges” 715d, compare 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “de Equitum magistro” 1.5, 2nd-3rd c.AD: Dio Cassius Historicus “fragment” 36.5; π. μίαν ἡμέραν καὶ ἓν πρᾶγμα καὶ ἀπόλλυται προκοπὴ καὶ σῴζεται 1st-2nd c.AD: Epictetus Philosophus “Enchiridion” 51.2]]; π. τὸ Ἕλληνά με εἶναι just because I am a Greek, [Refs 2nd c.BC+ [“UPZ” 7.13 (2nd c.BC)]]; π. τὸ ἀγαπᾶν αὐτὸν αὐτήν [LXX.Gen.29.20, cf. LXX.Exo.14.11]; later more loosely, because of.., [Refs 5th c.BC+ [1st c.BC: Philodemus Gadarensis Epigrammaticus “Rh.” 1.158 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus, 1st c.BC: Geminus Astronomicus 6.24, etc.]]; οὐδὲν π. σὲ γέγονε it is no fault of yours, [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [“PRyl.” 243.6 (2nd c.AD),compare “POxy.” 1420.7 (2nd c.AD).]]

__C.III.8
of a limit of possibility, εἴπερ ἐνεδέχετο π. τοὺς παρόντας καιρούς [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 18.239]]; πεῖσαι τό γε παρ᾽ αὑτόν to persuade (the judges) so far as in you lies, [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd c.AD: Arrianus Historicus “Epicteti Dissertationes” 2.2.20]]; οἴμωζε παρ᾽ ἐμέ as far as I am concerned, for all I care, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Aves” 846.]]

__D
POSITION: παρά may follow its substantive in all three cases, but then becomes by anastrophe πάρα: when the ultima  is elided, the practice varies, τῇσι παρ᾽ [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 18.400; but Ἡφαίστοιο πάρ᾽ [prev. work] 191.]]

__E
παρά absolutely, as adverb., near, together, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 1.611, +others, 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Iphigenia Aulidensis” 201 (Lyric poetry).]]

__F
πάρα (with anastrophe) stands for πάρεστι and πάρεισι, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 1.174, 8th-7th c.BC: Hesiodus Epicus “Opera et Dies” 454, 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Persae” 167, 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.42, +others, 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Electra” 285, 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Acharnenses” 862, etc.]]

__G
IN COMPOSITION (joined with other words),

__G.I
alongside of, beside, of rest, παράκειμαι, παράλληλοι, παρέζομαι, πάρειμι (εἰμί), παρίστημ; of motion, παραπλέω, πάρειμι (εἶμι).

__G.II
to the side of, to, παραδίδωμι, παρέχω.

__G.III
to one side of, by, past, παρέρχομαι, παροίχομαι, παραπέμπω, παρακμάζω, παρατρέχω.

__G.IV
metaphorically,

__G.IV.1
aside or beyond, i.e. amiss, wrong, παραβαίνω, παράγω, παροράω, παρορκέω, παρακούω, παραγιγνώσκω.

__G.IV.2
of comparison, as in παραβάλλω, παρατίθημι.

__G.IV.3
of alteration or change, as in παραλλάσσω, παραπείθω, παραπλάσσω, παρατεκταίνω, παραυδάω, παράφημι.

__G.IV.4
of a side-issue, παραπόλλυμι. (Cogn. with Gothic faúr 'along', Latin por-.)

παρα-βαίνω
[in LXX for סוּר, עָבַר, פָּרַר, שָׂטָה, etc. ;]
__1. in Hom. (twice), to go by the side of, stand beside.
__2. In Æsch., Herod., Thuc., al., to go past or pass over, chiefly metaphorically, to overstep, violate, transgress (Jos.7:11, Eze.16:59, Sir.40:14, al.) : τ. παράδοσιν, Mat.15:2; τ. ἐντολήν, Mat.15:3; before ἀπό (as מִן סוּר, Deu.17:20, al.), to turn aside, fall away (cf. π. τῆς ἀληθείας, Arist., Cael., i, 5, 2): Act.1:25.†
(AS)

---

LSJ / STEPBible (TFLSJ)
παραβαίνω,
Epic dialect imperfect παρέβασκε (see. below): accusative plural present participle παρβεῶντας [Refs [“Abh.Berl.Akad.” 1925(5).21 (from Cyrene) is probably from a byform Παραβάω:]]future -βήσομαι: perfect -βέβηκ; participle -βεβώς, Epic dialect -βεβᾰώς: perfect passive -βέβασμαι (see. below 11.1): aorist 2 παρέβην: aorist passive παρεβάθην [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 4.23]]:—go by the side of, and in perfect, stand beside, twice in [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Homerus Epicus]], with dative, of one standing beside the warrior in the chariot (compare παραβάτης), Ἕκτορι παρβεβαώς [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 11.522]]; of two warriors, παρβεβαῶτε.. ἀλλήλοιιν [Refs [13.708]]; also imperfect παρέβασκε, of the combatant in the chariot,[Refs 5th c.BC+ [11.104; but παρεβεβήκεέ οἱ ἡνίοχος 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 7.40.]]

__II
pass beside or beyond, mostly metaphorically (literal π. τὸν ὅρον [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [“PHal.” 1.87 (3rd c.BC)), in _transitive_ sense:]]

__II.1
overstep, transgress, τὰ νόμιμα [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.65; δίκην 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Agamemnon” 789 (_anapaest meter_); δίκην τὴν δεδικασμένην 5th c.BC: Antipho Orator 5.87; εἴ τι τούτων παραβαίνοιμι “IG” 12.15.42, compare 76.57; θεοῦ νόμον 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Ion” 230 (Lyric poetry); οὐ τοὺς νόμους μόνον, ἀλλὰ καὶ τὸν καιρὸν τῆς ἀναρρήσεως καὶ τὸν τόπον 4th c.BC: Aeschines Orator 3.204]]; θεσμούς, ὅρκους, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Aves” 331, 332 (both Lyric poetry), compare 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 1.78, 5th c.BC: Lysias Orator 9.15; τὰς σπονδάς 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Aves” 461: with _accusative_ _person_, π. τινὰ δαιμόνων]] sin against a god, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 6.12, compare 1st c.BC: Dionysius Halicarnassensis 1.23]]; οὓς παραβαίνειν αἰσχρόν disappoint,[Refs 5th c.BC+ [Chor. p.80 5th c.BC: Bacchylides Lyricus (compare see): _absolutely_, παραβάντες]] transgressors, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Agamemnon” 59 (_anapaest meter_); ὁ παραβαίνων 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Politica” 1325b5]]:—passive, to be transgressed or offended against, σπονδὰς.., ἅς γε ὁ θεὸς.. νομίζει παραβεβάσθαι [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 1.123; νόμῳ παραβαθέντι [prev. author] 3.67; ἐὰν καὶ ὁτιοῦν παραβαθῇ [prev. author] 4.23; παραβεβασμένοις ὅρκοις 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 17.12]]; παραβαινομένων absolutely, as offences were committed, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 3.45.]]

__II.1.b
with preposition, π. παρὰ τὴν συγγραφήν [Refs 4th c.BC+ [“AJA” 16.13 (Sardes, 4th-3rd c.BC).]]

__II.1.c
with genitive, go aside from, τῆς ἀληθείας [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “de Caelo” 271b8.]]

__II.2
pass over, omit, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Trachiniae” 499 (Lyric poetry), 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 18.211, Aristeas 297.]]

__II.3
let pass, καιρούς [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-3rd c.BC: Dinarchus Orator 1.36.]]

__II.4
οὔ με παρέβα φάσμα it escaped me not, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Hecuba” 704 (Lyric poetry).]]

__III
pass on, π. εἰς ἀπέχθειαν [Refs 2nd c.BC+ [2nd c.BC: Polybius Historicus 38.12.3 (sed to be read προβῆναι).]]

__IV
come forward, especially of the Comedy texts parabasis (see. παραβασις),π. πρὸς τὸ θέατρον step forward to address the spectators, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Acharnenses” 629, “Eq.” 508, “Pax” 735; also οὐκ ἂν παρέβην εἰς λέξιν τοιάνδ᾽ ἐπῶν 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Comicus 92.2: similarly, _metaphorically_, δοκεῖν παραβεβηκέναι τῇ πρώτῃ σκηνῇ 5th c.AD: Proclus Philosophus “in Platonis Parmenidem commentarii” p.523 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus]]

__V
in middle, with accusative person, commit an offence against, Chor.p.68 [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Bacchylides Lyricus]]

παρα-βάλλω
[in LXX: Pro.2:2 4:20 5:1, 13 22:17 (נָטָה hi.), Rut.2:16 (שָׁלַל), 2Ma.14:38 (elsewhere as seel.4)* ;]
__1. to throw to or beside, as fodder to horses (Hom., al.).
__2. to lay beside, compare (Hdt., Plat., al.): Mrk.4:30, Rec.
__3. Reflexive, to betake oneself, come near; of seamen, to cross over: εἰς Σάμον, Act.20:15.
__4. In mid. = παραβολεύομαι, which see†

LSJ / STEPBible (TFLSJ)
παραβάλλω,
future -βᾰλῶ: aorist 2 παρέβᾰλον: perfect -βέβληκα:— throw beside or by, throw to one, as fodder to horses, παρὰ δέ σφισι βάλλετ᾽ ἐδωδήν [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 8.504, compare 5.369; πὰρ δ᾽ ἔβαλον ζειάς 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 4.41; π. [τοῖς ἵπποις] ἀμβροσίαν 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Phaedrus” 247e; π. τοὺς ἀνθρώπους τοῖς ὄχλοις 2nd c.BC: Polybius Historicus 38.17.2]]; πυρὶ φρύγανα π. add fuel to the flame, [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd c.AD: Arrianus Historicus “Epicteti Dissertationes” 2.18.5, compare 2.18.12:]] — passive, παραβληθῆναι [τοῖς θηρίοις] [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd-3rd c.AD: Dio Cassius Historicus 59.10]]; τάριχος.. ἀπόνως παραβεβλημένον thrown carelessly before people, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Fragmenta” 333:]] —middle, μάζας ἐπὶ κάλαμον παραβαλλόμενοι ordering them to be served up, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 372b.]]

__b

παρα-γίνομαι
(Ion. and late for -γίγν-), [in LXX chiefly for בּוֹא ;]
__1. to be beside or at hand (Hom., Hdt., al.), hence, to stand by, sup­port (Æsch., Thuc., al.) : with dative of person(s), 2Ti.4:16.
__2. to come, come up, arrive (Hdt., Xen., al., and frequently in later writers; see MM, xviii; Thackeray, Gr., 267.2): absol., Luk.14:21 19:16, Jhn.3:23, Act.5:21-22, 25 9:39 10:32-33 11:23 14:27 17:10 18:27 21:18 23:16, 35 24:17, 24 25:7 28:21, 1Co.16:3; before εἰς, Jhn.8:2, Act.9:26 15:4; ἐπί, with accusative, Luk.22:52; πρός, with accusative, Luk.7:4, 20 8:19, Act.20:18; id. before ἐκ, Luk.11:6; παρά, with genitive, Mrk.14:43; ἀπὸ . . . εἰς, Mat.2:1, Act.13:14; ἀπὸ . . . ἐπὶ . . . πρός, Mat.3:13; of a teacher coming forward in public: Mat.3:1, Luk.12:51, Heb.9:11.†

παρ-άγω,
future παράξω [Refs 5th c.BC+ [1st c.BC: Philodemus Gadarensis Epigrammaticus “Rh.” 1.19 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus]]: perfect παραγέωχα [Refs 2nd c.BC+ [“PTeb.” 5.198 (2nd c.BC), παραγείοχα “Stud.Pal.” 22.3 (2nd c.AD)]]:—lead by or past a place, with accusative loci, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 4.158, compare 9.47]]; πάραγε πτέρυγας fly past, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Ion” 166 (Lyric poetry); π. θριάμβους 2nd c.AD: Appianus Historicus “Μιθριδάτειος” 117, compare “BC” 2.101]]; of a person, ἐν θριάμβῳ παράγεσθαι [Refs 1st c.AD+ [1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus “Caesar” 55.]]

__2
in Tactics, march the men up from the side, bring them from column into line, π. τοὺς ἐπὶ κέρως πορευομένους.. εἰς μέτωπον [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Historia Graeca (Hellenica)” 7.5.22, compare “Cyr.” 2.3.21, “An.” 4.6.6; τὰς [τάξεις] εἰς τὰ πλάγια [prev. work] 3.4.14; ἔξωθεν τῶν κεράτων [prev. work] 3.4.21.]]

__3
bring round or forward, ἀγκῶνα παρὰ τὸ στῆθος [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Hippocrates Medicus “περὶ ἄρθρων ἐμβολῆς” 2, compare 74]]; twist round or out of place, [Refs 3rd c.AD+ [3rd c.AD: Alexander Aphrodisiensis Philosophus “in librum de sensu commentarium - pars” 16.19.]]

__4
π. ὑπόχυμα couch a cataract, [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd c.AD: Galenus Medicus “Θρασύβουλος - Scripta Minora” 23.]]

__II
lead aside from the way, mislead, ἔννυχοι πάραγον κοῖται [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “P.” 11.25; σοφία παράγοισα μύθοις [prev. author] “N.” 7.23; π. τινὰεἰς ἀρκύστατα 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Persae” 99 codices (Lyric poetry); π. ψεύδεσι 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 383a; φενακίζειν καὶ π. 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 22.34, compare “PMagd.” 12.7 (3rd c.BC), “PCair.Zen.” 289.20 (3rd c.BC)]]:—passive, φόβῳ παρηγόμην [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Tyrannus” 974; λόγοις παράγεσθαι 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 1.91]]; ἀπάτῃ π. ὑπό τινων[Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. work] 34; νέοις παραχθείς 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Supplices” 232.]]

__II.2
divert from one's course, influence, Μοίρας [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.91]]: with accusative person et genitive of things, divert from, [τινὰ] τοῦ τῆς ῥητορικῆς τέλους Phld.[same place]; induce, lead to or into a thing, ἔς τι [Refs 7th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Iphigenia Taurica” 478: mostly in bad sense, π. ἐς ἀμπλακίην, ἐς ἀναιδείην, 6th c.BC: Theognis Elegiacus 404, 7th c.BC: Archilochus Lyricus 78]]:—passive, to be influenced, persuaded, οἷοι θυσίαις τε καὶ εὐχωλαῖς παράγεσθαι [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 365e, compare “Lg.” 885b, 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 2.64; λόγῳ παραχθέντες 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Memorabilia” 4.8.5]]: with infinitive, παρηγμένος μισθοῖς εἰργάσθαι τι [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Antigone” 294.]]

__II.3
of things, lead aside: hence, wrest, π. τοὺς νόμους ἐπί τι pervert the laws to this end, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 550d, compare 4th c.BC: Isaeus Orator 11.36; οἱ θεοὶ τῶν πονηρῶν ἀνθρώπων τὴν διάνοιαν π. 4th c.BC: Lycurgus Orator 92; π. τὴν ἀλήθειαν 2nd-3rd c.AD: Philostratus Sophista “Epistulae” 35:]] —passive, τὰ γράμματα παρῆκται, from age, [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd c.AD: Pausanias Periegeta 6.19.5.]]

__II.4
avert, πειθοῖ καὶ λόγῳ τὴν ἀνάγκην [Refs 1st c.AD+ [1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus “Phocion” 2.]]

__II.5
change slightly, of letters in the derivation of words, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Cratylus” 398c, 398d, 400c, 1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus 2.354c]]: frequently in Grammars  in passive, to be derived, ἀπό.. [Refs 2nd c.BC+ [2nd c.BC: Demetrius Lacon Philosophus “Herc.” 1014.58, 2nd c.BC: Dionysius Thrax Grammaticus 641.4, 2nd c.AD: Apollonius Dyscolus Grammaticus “de Pronominibus;” 34.25]]; ἐκ.. [Refs [[prev. author] “Synt.” 111.2]]; παρά with accusative, [Refs [[prev. author] “Adv.” 146.10: with _genitive_, τὸ μελιτηρὸν τοῦ τηρεῖν [παραχθέν] [prev. author] “Pron.” 30.17]]: generally, to be formed, διὰ τοῦ θεν [Refs [[prev. author] “Adv.” 184.12; τὴν κτητικὴν διὰ τῆς οι π. [prev. author] “Pron.” 109.6]]; to be inflected, ἀντωνυμίαι ὡς ὀνόματα εἰς τὰ γένη καὶ τὰς πτώσεις π.[Refs [[prev. work] 111.2, compare “Synt.” 110.8]]; ὁ ἀνδριὰς οὐ λέγεται ξύλον, ἀλλὰ παράγεται ξύλινος is called by a modification, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Metaphysica” 1033a17.]]

__III
bring and set beside others, bring forward, introduce, ἐς μέσον [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 3.129; εἰς τὸ μέσον 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Leges” 713b; εἰς ὑμᾶς 5th c.BC: Antipho Orator 4.1.5]]; π. εἰς τὸν δῆμον bring before the people, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Lysias Orator 13.32, compare 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 5.45]]; εἰς τὸ δικαστήριον before the court, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 26.17; παραχθῆναι τὴν γραφήν 5th c.BC: Antipho Orator 2.3.6]]; also, bring forward as a witness, etc., τὸν ἥκοντα παρήγαγον [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 18.170]]:—middle, μάρτυρα παραγόμενος [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Leges” 836c.]]

__III.b
introduce on the stage, bring in, [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd c.AD: Athenaeus Epigrammaticus 3.117d, 6.230b, +others, 3rd c.AD(?): Diogenes Laertius 2.28, probably in Anonymus]] de Comedy texts (CGF p.7); οἵους οἱ κωμῳδοδιδάσκαλοι π. ἀγροίκους [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Ethica Eudemia” 1230b19]]: hence, represent, portray, τοξότας αὐτοὺς παρήγαγον [Refs 1st c.AD+ [1st c.AD: Cornutus Philosophus “de Natura Deorum” 32, compare 14 (_passive_).]]

__III.c
produce, deliver, ἐπὶ τὰ χώματα καλαμείαν [Refs 2nd c.BC+ [“PTeb.” 5.198 (2nd c.BC), compare 92.8 (2nd c.BC, _passive_).]]

__III.2
bring in, with a notion of secrecy, ἄνδρας π. ἔσω [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 5.20]]:—passive, come in stealthily, slip in, π. γὰρ ἐνέρων δολιόπους ἀρωγὸς εἴσω στέγας [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Electra” 1391 (Lyric poetry)]]; of things, τὸ ὕδωρ ὀρύγμασι καὶ τάφροις εἰς τὸ πεδίον π. [Refs 1st c.AD+ [1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus “Camillus” 4.]]

carry on, protract, τὴν πρᾶξιν [Refs 1st c.BC+ [1st c.BC: Diodorus Siculus Historicus 18.65]]; π. τὸν χρόνον pass it, [Refs 1st c.AD+ [1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus “Agis” 13, etc.]]; see below [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Bacchylides Lyricus III.]]

__V

a ravenous sea-fish, [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd-3rd c.AD: Aelianus “De Natura Animalium - Ar.Byzantine Epit.” 9.49, 2nd-3rd c.AD: Oppianus Anazarbensis Epicus “Halieutica - Poetae Bucolici et Didactici” 1.368.]]

πάρ-ειμι
[in LXX for בּוֹא, etc. ;]
__1. to be by, at hand or present;
__(a) of persons: Rev.17:8; παρών (opposite to ἀπών), 1Co.5:3, 2Co.10:2 10:11 13:2 13:10; before ἐπί with genitive, Act.24:19; ἐνώπιον, Act.10:33; ἐνθάδε, Act.17:6; πρός, with accusative of person(s), Act.12:20, 2Co.11:8, Gal.4:18, 20;
__(b) of things : of time, ὁ καιρός, Jhn.7:6; τ. παρόν, Heb.12:11; ἡ ἀλήθεια, 2Pe.1:12; ταῦτα, 2Pe.1:9; τ. παρόντα, Heb.13:5.
__2. to have come or arrived (Hdt., Thuc., al.; see Field, Notes, 65) : Luk.13:1, Jhn.11:28, Act.10:21; before εἰς, Col.1:6; before ἐπί, with accusative of thing(s), Mat.26:50 (cf. συν-πάρειμι).†
(AS)

---

LSJ / STEPBible (TFLSJ)

(εἰμί sum), infinitive -εῖναι, Epic dialect 3rd.pers. plural παρέᾱσι [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 5.192, 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 13.247]]; Ionic dialect subjunctive παρέω [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 4.98]]; Epic dialect infinitive παρέμμεναι [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 4.640]], participle παρεών [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 24.475]]: Epic dialect imperfect παρέην [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 3.267 (tmesis)]]; 2nd pers. singular παρῆας variant in [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 4.497 (Scholia, “Legal icon Messanense”)]]; 3rd.pers. plural πάρεσαν [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 11.75]]; Attic dialect imperfect παρῆ [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Choephori” 523]]; in later Greek παρήμην [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd c.AD: Lucianus Sophista “VH” 2.25]]: Epic dialect future παρέσσομαι [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 13.393]]:—to be by or present, ὑμεῖς θεαί ἐστε πάρεστέ τε ἴστε τε πάντα [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 2.485, etc.: in tmesi, πὰρ δ᾽ ἄρ᾽ ἔην καὶ ἀοιδός 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 3.267]]; πάρα used for πάρεστι and πάρεισι, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 20.98, 23.479, etc.]]: frequently in participle, ποίπνυον παρεόντε [Refs [24.475; σημάντορος οὐ π. 15.325]], etc.; ἀπεόντα νόῳ παρεόντα [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Parmenides Poeta Philosophus 2.1, compare 1st c.AD(?): Heraclitus 34.]]

__2
to be by or near one, with dative, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 5.105; μήλοισι 4.640; π. τινὶ παροινοῦντι 5th c.BC: Antipho Orator 4.1.7; π. παρά τινι 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Philoctetes” 1056]]; π. τινί to be his guest, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Aves” 131.]]

__3
to be present in or at, μάχῃ [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 4.497; ἐν δαίτῃσι 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 10.217]]; δόμοις π. [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Hippolytus” 805; τοῖς πράγμασιν 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 1.2, etc.; ἐν λόγῳ 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Acharnenses” 513; ἐν ταῖς συνουσίαις 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Protagoras” 335b; ἐπὶ τοῖς ἀγῶσι 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 24.159.]]

__4
to be present so as to help, stand by, τινι [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 18.472, 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 13.393, 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Persae” 235; πλησίον παρῆσθα κινδύνων ἐμοί 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Orestes” 1159, etc.]]; especially of one accused, οἱ νῦν παρόντες αὐτῷ καὶ συνδικοῦντες [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 34.12, compare 24.159: in Medicine texts, of nurses, assistants, etc., 5th c.BC: Hippocrates Medicus “ἀφορισμοί” 1.1, 3rd c.BC: Herodas Mimographus]] middle cited in [Refs 4th c.AD+ [4th c.AD: Oribasius Medicus 10.37.11.]]

__6

[Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aeschines Orator 2.101; Θείβαθεν αὐληταὶ πάρα 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Acharnenses” 862.]]

__II
of things, to be by, i.e. ready or at hand, τά τε δμώεσσι πάρεστι [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 14.80, etc.; πάρα ἔργα βόεσσιν 8th-7th c.BC: Hesiodus Epicus “Opera et Dies” 454; οὐ γάρ οἱ πάρα νῆες 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 4.559]]; εἴ μοι δύναμίς γε παρείη if power were at my command,[Refs 4th c.BC+ [2.62; ὅση δύναμίς γε πάρεστι 23.128; ὅ τι πάρεστι 4th-3rd c.BC: Menander Comicus 62]]; τὰ παρεόντα what is ready, χαριζομένη παρεόντων [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 1.140; ἡ τοῦ πλέονος ἐπιθυμίη τὸ παρεὸν ἀπόλλυσι 3rd c.AD: Democritus Epigrammaticus 224, compare 191]]; ἐκ τῶν παρεουσέων αὐγέων the best light available, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Hippocrates Medicus “κατ᾽ ἰητρεῖον” 3; ἐκ τῶν παρεόντων τὸ εὔπορον εὑρίσκειν [prev. author] “Art.” 78; εἰ τὰ δεσμὰ μὴ παρείη [prev. passage];]] of feelings, conditions, etc., φόβος βαρβάροις παρῆν [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Persae” 391; θαῦμα παρῆν 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Antigone” 254; ἐν τοῖς τότε παρεοῦσι.. κακοῖσι 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 8.20, compare 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Prometheus Vinctus” 26; ὡς παρεσομένου σφι πολέμου 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 8.20: in Philos., of qualities or predicates, παρείη γ᾽ ἂν αὐταῖς (i.e. θριξίν) λευκότης 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Lysis” 217d, compare 3rd c.AD: Plotinus Philosophus 5.6.4]]; of Time, ὁ παρὼν νῦν χρόνος [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Electra” 1293, compare 4th c.BC: Aeschines Orator 1.93, 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Poetica” 1457a18; ἡ νῦν π. ἡμέρα 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Leges” 683c]]; ἡ ἱερὰ συμβουλὴ π. [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 5.6.4]]; τὰ παρόντα (Ionic dialect παρεόντα) the present state of affairs, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.113, etc.; τὰ π. πρήγματα [prev. author] 6.100]]; opposed to τὰ γεγονότα, τὰ μέλλοντα, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Theaetetus” 186b: _sing._, τὸ παρόν (_Ionic dialect_ παρεόν), πρὸς τὸ π. βουλεύειν, τὸ π. θεραπεύειν, 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.20, 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Philoctetes” 149 (Lyric poetry); πρὸς παρεόν 5th c.BC: Empedocles Poeta Philosophus 106: Adverbial phrases, τὸ παρόν]] just now, τὸ π. εἴπομεν [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Leges” 693b; τὰ παρόντα 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Electra” 215 (Lyric poetry): in Prose, ἐκ τῶν π]]. according to present circumstances, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 5.40, etc.; ἐν τῷ π., opposed to τὸ ἔπειτα, [prev. work] 63, etc.]]; ἐν τῷ νῦν π. καὶ ἐν τῷ ἔπειτα [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Phaedo” 67c]]; ἐν τῷ τότε π. [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 1.95; πρὸς τὸ παρόν 5th-6th c.BC: Isocrates Orator 15.94]]; ὡς πρὸς τὸ π. Abbott-Smith / STEPBible (TBESG)
παρ-έχω
[in LXX: Psa.30:7 (עָמַד hi.), etc. ;]
__I. Active voice.,
__1. to furnish, provide, supply; with ref. to incorporeal things, to afford, show, give, cause: with accusative, Act.22:2, 1Ti.1:4; with accusative and dative, Mat.26:10, Mrk.14:6, Luk.11:7 18:5, Act.16:16 17:31 28:2, Gal.6:17, 1Ti.6:17.
__2. to present, offer: with accusative and dative, Luk.6:29; with prop. reflex. and accusative pred., to show or present oneself (see infr., and cf. B1., § 55, 1).
__II. Middle voice.,
__1. to supply, furnish or display of one's own part: with accusative and dative, Luk.7:4, Act.19:24, Col.4:1.
__2. In late writers, with prop. reflex. and accusative pred. (= act. ut supr.), to show or present oneself (Xen., FlJ, al.; cf. M, Pr., 248; Deiss., BS, 254) : Tit.2:7.†
(AS)

[In 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 19.113, πᾱρέχη.]]]

__A

__2

__3
of incorporeal things, afford, cause, φιλότητα, ἀρετήν, γέλω τε καὶ εὐφροσύνην,[Refs 8th c.BC+ [3.354, 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 18.133, 20.8; ὀνίαις 7th-6th c.BC: Alcaeus Lyricus 88; π. εἰράναν τισί 5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “P.” 9.23; ὕμνον [prev. author] “N.” 6.33; αἶσαν [prev. author] “O.” 6.102; Σάρδεσιπένθος 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Persae” 322]]; τύχην, φρίκην, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Tyrannus” 53, 1306 (_anapaest meter_)]]; χάριν, εὔνοιαν, [Refs [[prev. author] “OC” 1498 (lvr.), “Tr.” 708]]; ὄχλον, πρήγματα π., [Refs 7th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.86, +others (see. πρᾶγμα); πόνον 7th-6th c.BC: Alcaeus Lyricus 19, 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.177; ἔργον 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Nubes” 523; π. εὔνοιαν εἴς τινα 5th c.BC: Antipho Orator 5.76]]; αἴσθησιν παρέχει τινός enables one to observe a thing, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 2.50]]; but αἴσθησιν π., absolutely, it causes remark, is perceived, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. author] 3.22, 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 4.6.13]]; πενία ἀνάγκῃ τὴν τόλμαν π. [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 3.45]]; ὑφειμένου δόξαν π., ={ὑφειμένῳ ἐοικέναι}, [Refs 1st c.AD+ [1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus 2.131a.]]

__II

__II.1
with infinitive, [ὄϊες] παρέχουσι.. γάλα θῆσθαι [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 4.89; π. τὸ σῶμα τύπτειν 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Nubes” 441; τὸ στράτευμα π. τισὶ διαφθεῖραι 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 8.50]](withoutinfinitive, πτήξας δέμας παρεῖχε [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Persae” 210): with _reflexive_ _pronoun_, ἐμαυτόν σοι ἐμμελετᾶν π]]. I give myself up to you to practise upon, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Phaedrus” 228e; π. ἐμαυτὸν ἐρωτᾶν [prev. author] “Ap.” 33b, compare “Prt.” 312c; π. ἑαυτοὺς τοῖς ἄρχουσι χρῆσθαι ἤν τι δέωνται 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 1.2.9]]: rarely with a participle, π. ἑαυτὸν δεδησόμενον [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd c.AD: Lucianus Sophista “Tox.” 35.]]

__II.2

[ἑωυτοὺς] διαφθαρῆναι [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 9.17]]; πατεῖν παρεῖχετῷ θέλοντι [ἑαυτόν] [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Ajax” 1146, compare 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Nubes” 422; τοῖς ἰατροῖς παρέχουσι.. ἀποτέμνειν καὶ ἀποκάειν 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Memorabilia” 1.2.54, compare 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Gorgias” 456b]]; τῷ λόγῳ ὥσπερ ἰατρῷ παρέχων ἀποκρίνου[Refs [[prev. work] 475d, compare “Tht.” 191a; ἕτοιμός εἰμί σοι παρέχειν ἀποκρινόμενος [prev. author] “Prt.” 348a]]; especially of a woman, obscene meaning, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Lysistrata” 162, 227, 2nd c.AD: Lucianus Sophista “DMeretr.” 5.4, etc. (in full, π. ἑαυτήν [prev. author] “DMar.” 13.1, 2nd c.AD: Artemidorus Daldianus Onirocriticus 1.78).]]

__II.3

__III
allow, grant, σιγὴν παρασχὼν κλῦθί μου [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Trachiniae” 1115: with]]infinitive, ἐπεὶ παρέσχες ἀντιφωνῆσαι did'st allow me to..,[Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. work] 1114; π. αὐτοὺς δικαστὰς.. γίγνεσθαι 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 1.37: _absolutely_ in imperative, πάρεχε]] make way, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Troades” 308, “Cyc.” 203, 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Vespae” 1326, “Av.” 1720 (all Lyric poetry); πάρεχ᾽ ἐκποδών [prev. author] “V.” 949.]]

__III.2
impersonal, παρέχει τινί with infinitive, it is allowed, in one's power to do so and so, παρεῖχε ἄν σφι εὐδαιμονέειν [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.170, compare 3.73, +others, 5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “I.” 8(7).76; ὑμῖν οὐ παρασχήσει ἀμύνασθαι 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 6.86; σωφρονεῖν παρεῖχέ σοι 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Electra” 1080: _neuter_]]participle used absolutely, παρέχον it being in one's power, since one can, like{ἐξόν, παρόν, παρέχον [ὑμῖν] ἄρχειν} [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 5.49]]; also εὖ, καλῶς παρασχόν, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 1.120, 5.14; κάλλιον π. [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Medea” 388, etc.]]

__B.2
of natural objects, furnish, present, exhibit, [ποταμὸς] κροκοδείλους π. [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 4.44; π. λίμνην ὁ Πόντος.. οὐ πολλῷ τεῳ ἐλάσσω ἑωυτοῦ [prev. work] 86, compare 46, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Phaedo” 81d.]]

παρίημι,
future παρήσω [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 7.161, 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Antigone” 1193]]: aorist 1 παρῆκα [Refs [[prev. author] “OC” 570]]: 3rd.pers. plural aorist 2 παρεῖσαν [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Antipho Orator 6.44]]; participle παρείς [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Electra” 732:]]perfect παρεῖκα (see. below); παρῆκα [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-3rd c.BC: Theophrastus Philosophus “Historia Plantarum” 5.3.6]]:—passive, aorist 1 παρείθην [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 23.868]]; infinitive παρεθῆναι [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 21.105]]: aorist 2 παρείμην [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Coloneus” 1666]]: perfect παρεῖμαι [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Phoenissae” 852]]:—let fall at the side, let fall, πὰρ δ᾽ ἴεισι τὰ πτέρα [Refs 7th c.BC+ [7th-6th c.BC: Sappho Lyrica 16; τὴν χεῖρα παρεικώς 4th-3rd c.BC: Clearchus Historicus 25; παρεῖσ᾽ ἐμαυτήν 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Electra” 819; π. ἀπ᾽ ὀμμάτων πέπλον 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Hercules Furens” 1203 (Lyric poetry); τὸ μάργον τῆς γνάθου [prev. author] “Cyc.” 310:]] —passive, ἡ δὲ παρείθη μήρινθος ποτὶ γαῖαν it hung down to earth, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 23.868.]]

__II
pass by, pass over, πᾶν ἔθνος καταστρεφόμενος καὶ οὐδὲν παριείς [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.177; π. κλύδων᾽ ἔφιππον 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Electra” 732, compare 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 18.263; π. τι ἄρρητον 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Leges” 754a]]:—passive, περὶ μὲν τούτου παρείσθω [Refs 2nd c.BC+ [2nd c.BC: Polybius Historicus 2.59.3.]]

__II.2
pass unnoticed, disregard, τι [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “P.” 1.86, 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.14, 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Agamemnon” 291, “Ch.” 925, 1032, 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Antigone” 1193, etc.; τὰ παθήματα.. παρεῖσ᾽ ἐάσω [prev. author] “OC” 363]]:—passive, παίδων πόθος παρεῖτο [Refs 4th c.BC+ [[prev. author] “El.” 545; μηδαμῇ παρεθῆναι 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 21.105]]: with infinitive, omit to do, παρέντα τοῦ μὲν τὸ φρόνιμον ἐγκωμιάζειν, τοῦ δὲ τὸ ἄφρον ψέγειν [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Phaedrus” 235e, compare “PCair.Zen.” 369.2 (3rd c.BC), 4th c.AD: Iamblichus Philosophus “de communi mathematica scientia” 1]]: with a negative repeated, μὴ παρῇς τὸ μὴ οὐ φράσαι [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Tyrannus” 283]]: with participle, οὐ παρίει σείων ὁ θεός [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd c.AD: Pausanias Periegeta 3.5.9: _absolutely_, αἰ δέ κα παρῇ “Berl.Sitzb.” 1927.169 (from Cyrene)]]:—middle, neglect, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Hercules Furens” 778 (Lyric poetry); τὸν δῆμον 2nd-3rd c.AD: Dio Cassius Historicus 51.5.]]

__II.3
of Time, let pass, τὸν χειμῶνα [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.77; ἕνδεκα ἡμέρας [prev. author] 7.183; νύκτα μέσην [prev. author] 8.9; τὸν καιρόν 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 4.27, etc.]]

__III
relax, τοὺς τερθρίους παρίει [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Equites” 440]]; οἶνος παρίησι weakens, [Refs 3rd c.AD+ [3rd c.AD(?): Diogenes Laertius 9.86]]; remit, γόον, πόθον, χόλον, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Supplices” 111, “Tr.” 650, “IA” [1609]]]; give up, μελέτας [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 1.85]]; τὸν φελλόν give up the use of.., Thphr. [prev. cited]:—passive, to be relaxed, weakened, κόπου δ᾽ ὕπο.. παρεῖται [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Bacchae” 635; κόπῳ παρεῖμαι [prev. author] “Ph.” 852; παρειμένος νόσῳ [prev. author] “Or.” 881; ὕπνῳ [prev. author] “Cyc.” 591; γήρᾳ 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Leges” 931d; σώμασι παρειμέναι 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Bacchae” 683; παρειμένα μέρη τοῦ σώματος 1st c.AD: Dioscorides (Dioscurides) Medicus 3.73, compare 2nd c.AD: Aretaeus Medicus “περὶ αἰτιῶν καὶ σημείων χρονίων παθῶν” 1.7, etc.; καὶ δὴ παρεῖται σῶμα 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Supplices” 1070; τῷ λίαν παρειμένῳ [prev. author] “Or.” 210; τὰ σώματα παρειμένοι 1st c.BC: Diodorus Siculus Historicus 14.105; ὥστε καὶ τοῦ σώ ματός τι παρεθῆναι 2nd-3rd c.AD: Dio Cassius Historicus 68.33.]]

τοῦ ποδὸς παρίει slack away the sheet, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Equites” 436: so perhaps _metaphorically_, τοῦ μετρίου παρείς]] letting go one's hold of moderation, i. e. giving it up, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Coloneus” 1212 (Lyric poetry).]]

__III.3
remit punishment, τιμωρίαν [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Lycurgus Orator 9 (_passive_)]]; pardon, τὴν συμφοράν [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Ranae” 699:]] —passive, ἐποίησεν παρεθῆμεν (Doric dialect for παρεθῆναι) secured our release from the obligation, [Refs 1st c.BC+ [“IG” 42(1).66.47 (Epid., 1st c.BC)]]: with genitive, παρεῖσθαι τὰς πόλεις τῶν τόκων [Refs 1st c.BC+ [“OGI” 444.15 (Ilium, 1st c.BC).]]

__IV
yield, give up, νίκην τινί [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 6.103, compare 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Agamemnon” 943; τυραννίδα τινί 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Phoenissae” 523; αὑτοὺς κυμάτων δρομήμασιν [prev. author] “Tr.” 693; π. τινὶ τὴν ἀρχήν 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 6.23, compare 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Politica” 1285b15; οὐδὲ δεῖν δυνάμενον ἄρχειν παριέναι τῷ πλησίον [prev. work] 1325a37]]; leave a thing to another, σοὶ παρεὶς τάδε [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Philoctetes” 132; Ζεὺς τὰ μικρὰ.. ἄλλοις δαίμοσιν παρεὶς ἐᾷ “Tragica Adespota” 353]]:—middle, give up, συμμαχίαν [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Rhetorica ad Alexandrum” 1446b28]]; resign, στρατηγίαν [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd-3rd c.AD: Dio Cassius Historicus 39.23, etc.:]] —passive, [γῆ] παρειμένη left in private ownership, [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [“PHib.” 1.53.5 (3rd c.BC).]]

__IV.2
permit, allow, with dative person et infinitive, ἄλλῳ δὲ παρήσομεν οὐδενὶ ναυαρχέειν [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 7.161, compare 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Electra” 1482, 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Equites” 341, 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Politica” 1336b29: with]]subjunctive, πάρες ὑπερβῶ suffer me to.., [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Fragmenta” 308 (_anapaest meter_): _absolutely_ (the _infinitive_ being understood), 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Coloneus” 591, 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Equites” 340, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Symposium” 199c, etc.]]; μὴ παρῇς σαυτοῦ βροτοῖς ὄνειδος do not allow them to have cause to reproach thee, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Philoctetes” 967]]; παρῆκεν, ὥστε βραχέα μοι δεῖσθαι φράσαι has allowed that there should be but little for me to say, [Refs [[prev. author] “OC” 570.]]

παρ-ίστημι
[in LXX for עָמַד, etc. ;]
__I. Transitive verb. in present tense., imperfect., future tense., 1 aorist.;
__1. to place beside, present, provide: with accusative, Act.9:41 23:24, 2Co.4:14, Col.1:28; with accusative and dative, Mat.26:53, Luk.2:22, Act.1:3 23:33, 1Co.8:8; before accusative pred., Rom.6:13, 16 (late pres., παριστάνετε), Rom.6:19 12:1, 2Co.11:2, Eph.5:27, Col.1:22, 2Ti.2:15.
__2. to present to the mind (cl.) : by argument, to prove (Xen., FlJ, al.), with accusative, Act.24:13.
__II. Intransitive. in  perfect., pluperfect., 2 aorist.;
__1. to stand by or beside one : with dative of person(s), Act.1:10 9:39 23:2 27:23; ptcp., Mrk.14:47, 69-70 15:35, 39 Jhn.18:22 19:26.
__2. to appear: with nom. pred., before ἐνώπιον, Act.4:10; with dative of person(s), Act.27:24; so fut. mid. (of. LS, see word, B, ii, 2), Rom.14:10.
__3. to be at hand, be present, have come: Act.4:26 (LXX); of servants in attendance, ἐνώπιον τ. θεοῦ, Luk.1:19; absol., οἱ παρεστῶτες, Luk.19:24; before αὐτῷ, Act.23:2, 4; of time, Mrk.4:29
__4. to stand by for help or defence (Hom., Dem., Xen., al.): with dative of person(s), Rom.16:2, 2Ti.4:17.†

furnish, supply, deliver, [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [3rd c.BC: Zenon Papyri du Caire 790.10 (3rd c.BC), “PTeb.” 5.196 (2nd c.BC), “Abh. Berl.Akad.” 1925(5).31 (from Cyrene).]]

__A.II.5
make good, prove, show, τι πολλοῖς τεκμηρίοις [NT+5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Lysias Orator 12.51, cf. NT.Act.24.13; καθάπερ προϊόντες -στήσομεν 1st c.BC: Philodemus Gadarensis Epigrammaticus “Ir.” p.85 W., compare “Mus.” p.37 K.]]

__A.II.6
with accusative person, present, offer, ἑαυτοὺς τῷ θεῷ, ἑαυτοὺς δούλους εἰς ὑπακοήν, [NT.Rom.6.13, 16.]

__A.II.6.b
commend, βρῶμα ἡμᾶς οὐ παραστήσει τῷ θεῷ [NT.1Cor.8.8.]

__A.II.7
render, [ἡ πίσσα] τὸν οἶνον ἔὔποτον παρίστησι ταχέως [Refs 1st c.AD+ [1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus 2.676c.]]

__A.II.8
in later Greek, as in middle (V. C. 1), produce in court, etc., [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [“BGU” 759.22 (2nd c.AD)]], etc.:—passive, [Refs 2nd c.BC+ [“Sammelb.” 4512.82 (2nd c.BC), etc.]]

__A.III
set side by side, compare, [πόλεις] μικρὰς μεγάλαις [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Isocrates Orator 12.40.]] — The use of these active tenses occurs in Pl.[same place], but first becomes common in Oratt.

__B
passive, with aorist 2, perfect and pluperfect active, intransitive:

__B.I
stand by, beside, or near, θέων δέ οἱ ἄγχι παρέστη [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 15.442, compare 483; ἀμφίπολος δ᾽ ἄρα οἱ κεδνὴ ἑκάτερθε παρέστη 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 1.335, compare 8.218, 18.183]]; ἑξείης πάντεσσι παρίστασαι, of a beggar,[Refs 8th c.BC+ [17.450; οὐδ᾽ ἄρα οἵ τις ἀνουτητί γε παρέστη 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 22.371]]; ζωγράφῳ παρεστηκυῖα, of a painter's model, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Memorabilia” 3.11.2: frequently in]]participle παραστάς with a Verb, εἶπε παραστάς [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 12.60; οὖτα π. 20.472]]; παρασταθείς, variant for{κατασταθείς}, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Orestes” 365.]]

__B.I.2
stand by, i.e. help, defend, τινι [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 10.279, etc.; Τρωσὶ παρεστάμεναι καὶ ἀμύνειν 21.231, compare 15.255; Ὀδυσῆϊ π. ἠδ᾽ ἐπαρήγει 23.783, compare 8th-7th c.BC: Hesiodus Epicus “Theogonia” 439, 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.87, etc.; π. τινὶ χερσί 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Ajax” 1384]]; βοηθοὶ π. [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 5.3.19; οὐ παρέστη οὐδ᾽ ἐβοήθησεν 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 45.64.]]

__B.II
more frequently in past tenses, to have come, δεῦρο παρέστης [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 3.405]]; to be at hand, νῆες δ᾽ ἐκ Λήμνοιο παρέστασαν [Refs [7.467, etc.]]

__B.II.2
of events, to be near, be at hand, ἀλλά τοι ἤδη ἄγχι παρέστηκεν θάνατος [Refs 8th c.BC+ [16.853; κακὴ Διὸς αἶσα παρέστη ἡμῖν 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 9.52, compare 16.280]]: in future middle, σοὶ..παραστήσεσθαι ἔμελλεν μοῖρ᾽ ὀλοή [Refs 4th c.BC+ [24.28; ἐάν του καιρὸς ἢ χρεία παραστῇ 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 21.101]], compare 73: frequently in perfect, παρέστηχ᾽ ὡς ἔοικ᾽ ἀγὼν μέγας [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Hecuba” 229, compare “Med.” 331]]; in participle, τὸ χρῶμα τὸ παρεστηκός [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Equites” 399; ὁ νῦν παρεστηκὼς ἡμῖν λόγος 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Leges” 962d]]: in Attic dialect form παρεστώς, ῶσα, ός, th=s parestw/shs no/sou [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Philoctetes” 734]]; τοῦ π. θέρους[Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. work] 1340; τὰς παρεστώσας τύχας 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Orestes” [1024]]]; τὰ παρεστῶτα present circumstances, τὰ λῷστα, κράτιστα τῶν π., [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Agamemnon” 1053, “Pr.” 218; πρὸς τὸ παρεστός 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Equites” 564; πρὸς τὸ παριστάμενον 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “de Equitum magistro” 9.1.]]

__B.III
come to the side of another, come over to his opinion, παραστῆναι ἐς τῶν Περσέων τὴν γνώμην [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 6.99]]: absolutely, come to terms, surrender, submit, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [[prev. author] 3.13, 5.65, 6.140; οἱ πολέμιοι παραστήσονται [prev. author] 3.155; τῷ πολέμῳ παραστῆναι 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 22.15, compare “Etymologicum Magnum” 653.2.]]

__B.IV
happen to one, τῷ δὴ λέγουσι.. θῶμα μέγιστον παραστῆναι [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.23; τὸ φρονεῖν ἀλλοῖα παρίσταται 5th c.BC: Empedocles Poeta Philosophus 108]]; especially come into one's head, occur to one, τὼς νόος ἀνθρώποισι παριστᾶται [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Parmenides Poeta Philosophus 16.2; δόξα μοι παρεστάθη ναοὺς ἱκέσθαι 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Tyrannus” 911]]; δόξα π. τινὶ ὥστε.. [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Phaedo” 66b]]; σοὶ τοῦτο παρέστηκεν, ὡς.. [Refs [[prev. author] “Phdr.” 233c]]; π. θαῦμα, γνώμη, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Andocides Orator 2.2, 24 (assuming variant); ἔκπληξις παρέστη 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 8.96: _impersonal_, παρίσταταί μοι]] it occurs to me; τῷ οὐ παραστήσεται.. τεθνάναι βούλεσθαι to whom it will not occur to wish for death, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 7.46: followed by ὡς, 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 4.61, 95, 5th c.BC: Lysias Orator 12.62, etc.]]: with infinitive, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [[prev. author] 7.17; οὐχὶ παρίσταταί μοι ταὐτὰ γιγνώσκειν 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 3.1]]: with accusative et infinitive, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Lysias Orator 21.12, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Phaedo” 58e]]; participle, τὸ παριστάμενον that which comes into one's head, a thought, [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd c.AD: Lucianus Sophista “Cont.” 13]]; ἐκ τοῦ π. λέγειν speak offhand, [Refs 1st c.AD+ [1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus “Demosthenes” 9, compare 2nd c.AD: Galenus Medicus 14.295.]]

__B.V
to be disposed, πρὸς τὰς πράξεις [Refs 1st c.BC+ [1st c.BC: Philodemus Gadarensis Epigrammaticus “Mus.” p.71 K.; εἰρηνικῶς παρεστώτων [prev. author] “Hom.” p.45 O.]]

__B.V.2
collect oneself, παραστῆναι πρὸς τὸν κίνδυνον [Refs 1st c.BC+ [1st c.BC: Diodorus Siculus Historicus 17.43]]; τῷ θυμῷ παραστάς[Refs 1st c.AD+ [[prev. work] 99; π. πρὸς τὴν ἀπολογίαν 1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus “Alcibiades” 19; παρεστηκότες ταῖς γνώμαις 2nd c.AD: Arrianus Historicus “Fragmenta Historica - FHG” 161 1st c.AD: Josephus Historicus]]

__B.V.3
metaphorically, οἶνος παρίσταται the wine improves, becomes fit for drinking, opposed to ἐξίσταται, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-3rd c.BC: Theophrastus Philosophus “de Causis Plantarum” 6.14.10, compare 1st c.AD: Dioscorides (Dioscurides) Medicus 5.8.]]

__B.V.3.b
of a crop, to be ripe, ὅταν ὁ πρώϊμος σπόρος παραστῇ [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [“OGI” 56.68 (Egypt, 3rd c.BC)]]; so probably ἡ γῆ παρέστηκεν [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [“PLille” 8.5 (3rd c.BC).]]

__B.VI
παρεστηκέναι φρενῶν to be beside oneself, lose one's wits, [Refs 2nd c.BC+ [2nd c.BC: Polybius Historicus 18.53.6; π. ταῖς διανοίαις [prev. author] 14.5.7, etc.]]; ἐπὶ τοσοῦτον π. [Refs [[prev. author] 22.8.13; compare παρεξίστημι 11.]]

__B.VI.2
to be passionately devoted to, ἵπποισι παρεστεῶτες [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Hippocrates Medicus “ἐπιστολαί” 17.]]

__B.VII
absolutely, παρεστηκός, ={παρόν}, since it was in their power, since the opportunity offered, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 4.133.]]

__C
Some tenses of middle, present and imperfect sometimes, future and aorist I almost always (for exceptions, see above [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Bacchylides Lyricus 11.2, III, iv), are used in causal sense:]]

__C.I
set by one's side, bring forward, produce, π. ἱερεῖα [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 6.1.22]]; especially in a court of justice, τοὺς παῖδας παραστησάμενοι [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Lysias Orator 20.35]]; παιδία παραστήσεται (of a culprit) [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 21.99; ταῦτα παραστησάμενος [prev. work]187; μάρτυρας παρίστανται 4th c.BC: Isaeus Orator 4.13, etc.]]; παραστήσασθαί τινα produce him as witness, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. author] 9.9, 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 34.28, etc.; π. τινὰ εἰς κρίσιν 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 555b.]]

__C.I.2
commend, τινί τινα [Refs 1st c.AD+ [1st c.AD: Josephus Historicus “Antiquitates Judaicae” 15.7.3.]]

__C.II
bring to one's side, bring over by force, bring to terms, ἀέκοντας παραστήσασθαι [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 8.80; π. βία 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Coloneus” 916; π. πολιορκίᾳ 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 1.98; πολιορκοῦντας π. ὁμολογίᾳ [prev. work] 29: _absolutely_, π. τινά, π. πόλιν, 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 3.45, 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 1.124, etc.; τοὺς οἰκοῦντας τὴν Ἀττικὴν π. εἰς φορὰν δασμοῦ 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Leges” 706b.]]

__C.II.2
generally, dispose for one's own views or purposes, τινὰ παραστήσασθαι οὕτως ὥστε.. so to dispose a person that.., [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 4.136; ἑαυτοὺς πρὸς τὴν μάχην 2nd c.BC: Polybius Historicus 3.109.9]]; dispose, induce a person, πρὸς τὸ κοινωνεῖν [Refs [[prev. author] 29.3.5]]: with accusative et infinitive, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Chio Epistolographus “Ep.” 3.]]

__B
way by or past, passage, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 3.21, 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “de Caelo” 294b26]]; π. καὶ τροπαὶ τῶν ἄστρων[Refs 6th c.AD+ [[prev. work] 296b4, compare 6th c.AD: Simplicius Philosophus “in Aristotelis de Caelo commentaria - Comm. in Arist. Graeca” 507.24]]; π. τοῦ χρόνου passage, lapse of time, [Refs 3rd c.AD+ [3rd c.AD: Porphyrius Tyrius Philosophus “Sententiae ad intelligibilia ducentes” 44.]]

narrow entrance or approach, mountain-pass, as Thermopylae, etc., [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Lysias Orator 2.30, 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 4.7.4, etc.]]; λαβεῖν τὰς π. take the pass, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 5.20, compare 9.32, 1st c.BC: Philodemus Gadarensis Epigrammaticus “Rh.” 1.334 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus]]; opposed to δίοδοι, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Cynegeticus” 6.6.]]

especially side-entrance on the stage, [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [Semus 20, 2nd c.AD(?): Pollianus Epigrammaticus 4.126.]]

gallery or passage-way surmounting fortifications, [Refs [“IG” 22.463.49,52,1672.110.]]

coming forward, appearance, especially before the assembly, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator “Epistulae” 3.29, 4th c.AD: Julianus Imperator “Orationes” 7.205b, etc.]]

use of stage for an artist's performance, ἡ π. εὗρεν δραχμήν [Refs [“Michel” 908, 909 (lasos).]]

public recitation, [Refs [Anthologia Graeca 11.422 (Antioch.).]]

[Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. author] “Ph.” 391; οὔσης παρρησίας 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Thesmophoriazusae” 541; διδόναι π. τισί 5th-6th c.BC: Isocrates Orator 2.28; ἐλευθερίας ἡ πόλις μεστὴ καὶ π. γίγνεται 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 557b; τἀληθῆ μετὰ παρρησίας ἐρῶ 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 6.31; τὴν ὑπὲρ τῶν δικαίων π. ἀποδόμενος 4th-3rd c.BC: Dinarchus Orator 2.1]]; δημοκρατίας οὔσης οὐκ ἔστι π. [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Isocrates Orator 8.14; π. καὶ ἰσηγορία καὶ δημοκρατία 2nd c.BC: Polybius Historicus 2.38.6]]; περὶ παρρησίας, title of work by Philodemus.

__2
in bad sense, licence of tongue, ἡ εἰς τοὺς θεοὺς π. [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Isocrates Orator 11.40, compare 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Phaedrus” 240e, 1st c.BC: Cicero, M. Tullius Orator et Philosophus “Epistulae ad Atticum” 1.16.8.]]

__3
freedom of action, [Refs 5th c.AD+ [5th c.AD: Aristaenetus Rhetor 2.7]]; π. ζωῆς καὶ θανάτου power of life and death, [Refs [Vett. Val. 6.3, +others]]; licence, permission, [Refs 6th c.AD+ [6th c.AD: Justinianus Imperator “Novellae” 1.1.1]]; παρρησίᾳ ἐκτέμνεται τὸ δέρμα without fear, [Refs 6th c.AD+ [6th c.AD: Aëtius Medicus 15.8]]; ἤγαγον ὑμᾶς μετὰ παρρησίας openly, [LXX.Lev.26.13.]

__4
liberality, lavishness, κεκόσμηκε τὸν αὑτοῦ βίον τῇ καλλίστῃ π. [Refs 2nd c.BC+ [“OGI” 323.10(Pergam., 2nd c.BC)]]; ἐπὶ τῇ.. τῶν καμάτων καὶ πάσης ἐπιμελείας παρρησίᾳ [Refs 3rd c.AD+ [“IG” 5(1).547 (Sparta, 3rd c.AD)]]; = copia, [Refs [“Corpus Glossariorum Latinorum”]]

deep_entry:
Abbott-Smith / STEPBible (TBESG)
πᾶς, πᾶσα, πᾶν, genitive, παντός, πάσης, παντός,
[in LXX chiefly for כֹּל ;]
all, every.
__I. As adj.,
__1. with subst. anarth., all, every, of every kind: Mat.3:10 4:23, Mrk.9:49, Luk.4:37, Jhn.2:1o, Act.27:20, Rom.7:8, Rev.18:17, al. mult.; pl., all, Act.22:15, Rom.5:12, Heb.1:6, al.; of the highest degree, π. ἐξουσία (προθυμία, χαρά), Mat.28:18, Act.17:11, Phi 2:29, al.; also the whole (though in this sense more frequently with art.), Mat.2:3, Act.2:36, Rom.11:26.
__2. C. art.  (before the art., after the noun, or, denoting totality, between the art. and noun), all, whole: Mat.8:32 13:2, Mrk.5:33, Luk.1:10, Act.7:14, Rom.3:19, Gal.5:14, Eph.4:16, al.; pl., Mat.2:4, Mrk.4:13, Rom.1:5, al.
__II. As pron.,
__1. masc. and fem., every one: Mrk.9:49, Luk.16:16, Heb.2:9; before rel. pron., Mat.7:24, Act.2:21, Gal.3:10, al.; with ptcp. (anarth.), Mat.13:19, Luk.11:4; with ptcp. (with art.), Mat.5:22, Mrk.7:8, Luk.6:47, Jhn.3:8, Rom.1:16, al.; pl., πάντες, absol., all, all men, Mat.10:22, Mrk.13:13, Luk.20:38, Jhn.1:7 3:26, 1Co.8:1, al.; οἱ π. (collectively, as a definite whole), Rom.11:32, 1Co.1:17, Eph.4:13, al.; π. οἱ (ὅσοι), Mat.4:24, Mrk.1:32, Luk.4:40, al.
__2. Neut.,
__(a) sing., πᾶν, everything, all: πᾶν τό, with ptcp., 1Co.10:25, 27, Eph.5:13, 1Jn.2:16 5:4 (sc. ὄν); πᾶν ὅ, Jhn.17:2, Rom.14:23; collectively, of persons (Westc., in l.), Jhn.6:37, 39; with prep., in adverbial phrases, διὰ παντός, always, Mat.18:10, al.; ἐν παντί, in everything, in every way, 2Co.4:8, Phi 4:6, al.;
__(b) pl., πάτνα, all things: absol., Jhn.1:3, 1Co.2:10, Heb.2:8, al.; of certain specified things, Mrk.4:34, Luk.1:3, Rom.8:28, 1Th.5:21, al.; accusative, πάντα, adverbially, wholly, in all things, in all respects, Act.20:35, 1Co.9:25, al.; with art., τὰ π., all things (a totality, as distinct from anarth. πάντα, all things severally; cf. Westc, Eph., 186f.), absol.: Rom.11:36, 1Co.8:6, Eph.3:9, Heb.1:3, al.; relatively, Mrk.4:11, Act.17:25, Rom.8:32, al.; πάντα, with ptcp., Mat.18:31, al.; πάντα ταῦτα (ταῦτα π.), Mat.6:32, 33, al.; πάντα, with prep, in adverbial phrases, πρὸ πάντων, above all things, Jas.5:12, 1Pe.4:8; ἐν π́, in all things, in all ways, 1Ti.3:11, 1Pe.4:11, al.; κατὰ πάντα, in all respects, Act.17:22, al.
__3. C. neg., πᾶς οὐ (μή) = οὐδείς, see: οὐ and μή, and cf. M, Pr., 245f.
(AS)
