LSJ / STEPBible (TFLSJ)
πᾶς, πᾶσα, πᾶν,

__A
Aeolic dialect παῖς, παῖσα [Refs 7th c.BC+ [7th-6th c.BC: Sappho Lyrica “Papyrus fragments” in E. Diehl, 13.8, 21.2, 20a. 14, 7th-6th c.BC: Alcaeus Lyricus “Supp.” 12.6, 25.8; Cretan dialect, Thess., 4th c.AD(?): Arcadius Grammaticus]] feminine πάνσα [Refs 8th c.BC+ [“GDI” 4976 (from Gortyn), “IG” 9(2).234.2 (Pharsalus, 3rd c.BC), 5(2).343.16 (Orchom. 4th c.AD(?): Arcadius Grammaticus, 4th c.BC): _genitive_ παντός, πάσης, παντός: _genitive_ _plural_ _masculine_ and _neuter_ πάντων, _feminine_ πᾱσῶν, _Epic dialect_ and _Ionic dialect_ πᾱσέων, _Epic dialect_ also πᾱσάων [σᾱ] 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 6.107: _dative_ _plural_ _masculine_ and _neuter_ πᾶσι]], Epic dialect and Delph. πάντεσσι [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 14.246, “IG” 22.1126.22,44]]; also Locrian dialect πάντεσιν [Refs 5th c.BC+ [“Berl.Sitzb.” 1927.8 (5th c.BC); Delph. πάντεσι “SIG” 452.5 (3rd c.BC)]]; πάντοις [Refs 2nd c.BC+ [“GDI” 2652 (Delph., 2nd c.BC), “Tab.Defix.Aud.” 75.8: πᾶν]] as accusative masculine in [LXX+7th c.BC+ [LXX, π. ἄνδρα, οἰκέτην, οἶκον, LXX.1Ki.11.8, LXX.Exo.12.44, LXX.Jer.13.11. [_Doric dialect_ and _Aeolic dialect_ πάν [ᾰ] Hdn.Gr. 2.12, 5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “O.” 2.85, 7th-6th c.BC: Sappho Lyrica “Papyrus fragments” in 1787 “fragment” 3 ii 5, +others, and _Attic dialect_ in compounds, as ἅπᾰν, πάμπᾰν]], etc. (but in compounds sometimes long in Attic dialect, [Refs [“Anecdota Graeca - Bekker” 416)]].]—Coll. pronoun, when used of a number, all; when of one only, the whole; of the several persons in a number, every.

__A.I
in plural, all, πάντες τε θεοὶ πᾶσαί τε θέαιναι [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 8.5, etc.]]; πάντες ὅσοι.. [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 1.11, etc.]]; πάντας ᾧ ἂνπεριτυγχάνῃ, for ὅσοις ἄν, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 566d]]: also with the Article, see.below [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Bacchylides Lyricus]]

__A.I.2
strengthened by adverbs, ἅμα πάντες all together, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 24.253, etc.; πάντες ἅμα 1.495 (in Prose commonly ἅπαντες]], but not always, see [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 9.23, 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 1.3.10, etc.)]]: with a collective noun, ἅμα πᾶς ὁ δῆμος [Refs 8th c.BC+ [1st c.BC: Dionysius Halicarnassensis 2.14; πάντες ὁμῶς 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 15.98; ὁμοῦ πάντες 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Electra” 715; πάντα μάλα 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 22.115, 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 5.216, etc.; πάντες ὁμοίως 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 20.85, etc.]]

__A.I.3
with superlative,πάντες ἄριστοι all the noblest, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 9.3, 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 4.272, etc.]]

__A.I.4
consisting or composed wholly of, i.e. nothing but, only, φρουρούμενος ὑπὸ πάντων πολεμίων [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 579b; ἐκ πασῶν δυνάμεων συνεστώς “Corpus Hermeticum” 13.2]]; see 11.2.

__A.II
singular, all, the whole, πᾶς δ᾽ ἄρα χαλκῷ λάμπε [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 11.65, compare 13.191]]; πᾶσα ὕλη all the wood, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th-7th c.BC: Hesiodus Epicus “Opera et Dies” 511, compare “Th.” 695, etc.]];πᾶσα ἀληθείη all the truth, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 24.407, 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 11.507]]; τὴν φάτνην ἐοῦσαν χαλκέην πᾶσαν all of bronze, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 9.70]]; ἦν ἡ μάχη καρτερὰ καὶ ἐν χερσὶ πᾶσα, ἦν γὰρ τὸ χωρίον πρόσαντες πᾶν, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 4.43, etc.]]; πᾶν κράτος the whole power, sovereign power, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Philoctetes” 142 (Lyric poetry); τὸ πᾶν κράτος 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 6.35; μετὰ πάσης ἀδείας 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 18.305; πᾶσα ἀνάγκη 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Phaedrus” 240a]]; πᾶσαι δ᾽ ὠΐγνυντο πύλαι, πᾶσαι γὰρ ἐπῴχατο [πύλαι], the whole gate was open (shut), i.e. the gate was wide open, quite shut, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 2.809, 12.340, as explained by 3rd-2nd c.BC: Aristarchus Grammaticus]]; see below [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Bacchylides Lyricus]]

__A.II.2
as in [Refs [1.4, with attraction, ὁ πάντ᾽ ἄναλκις οὗτος, ἡ πᾶσα βλάβη who is]]nought but mischief, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Electra” 301, compare “Ph.” 622, 927.]]

__A.III
every, οἱ δ᾽ ἄλκιμον ἦτορ ἔχοντες.. πᾶς πέτεται [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 16.265, compare 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 13.313, 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Electra” 972, 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Bacchae” 1131, 1135]]; ἄκουε πᾶς, ={ἀκούετε πάντες}, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Thesmophoriazusae” 372; πᾶς χώρει [prev. author] “Pax” 555: with _partitive_ _genitive_, παντὶ βροτῶν (variant{βροτῷ}) 5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “O.” 1.100; πᾶς τοῦτό γ᾽ Ἑλλήνων θροεῖ 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Coloneus” 597; τῶν ἀνθρώπων πᾶς 1st-2nd c.AD: Dio Chrysostomus Sophista 3.70; also πᾶς ἀνήρ 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Ajax” 1366, 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Ranae” 1125, etc.; πᾶσα ἀνθρώπου ψυχή 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Phaedrus” 249e]]: with the Article, see infr. B; πᾶς τις every single one, [Refs 6th c.BC+ [6th c.BC: Theognis Elegiacus 621, 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.50, 3.79, 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Ajax” 28, etc.; πᾶς τις βροτῶν [prev. author] “El.” 984, compare “OC” 25, etc.]]; πᾶς ὅστις.. [Refs [[prev. author] “Aj.” 1413]]; πᾶν ὅσον.. [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Prometheus Vinctus” 787, etc.]]

__A.III.2
less frequently, any one, τὸ μὲν ἐπιτιμᾶν.. φήσαιτις ἂν.. παντὸς εἶναι [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 1.16; παντὸς ἀνδρός [ἐστι] γνῶναι 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Ion” 532e; χαλεπόν τι καὶ οὐχὶ παντός [prev. author] Alcaeus1.129a]]; παντὸς ἀκούοντος.. when any one hears.., [NT.Matt.13.19]; ἀμήχανον δὲ παντὸς ἀνδρὸς ἐκμαθεῖν ψυχήν any man's soul, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Antigone” 175]]; πάντων ἀποστερεῖσθαι λυπηρόν to be deprived of anything, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 18.5; compare 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 111.2, VI.]]

__B
with the Article, in the sense of all, the whole, when the substantive is to be strongly specified, πᾶς being put either before the Article or after the substantive, πᾶσαν τὴν δύναμιν all his force, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.214; τὰ ἀγαθὰ πάντα 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 3.1.20 (assuming variant)]]: with abstract Nouns and others which require the Article, πάντα τὰ μέλλοντα [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Prometheus Vinctus” 101; πᾶσαν τὴν ἀλήθειαν 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 6.87]]; τὰ τῆς πόλεως π. all the affairs of state, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Lysias Orator 19.48, etc.: emphatically, τὰς νέας τὰς πάσας 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 7.59.]]

__B.II
πᾶς is put between the Article and substantive, to denote totality (V. [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus 11), ὁ πᾶς ἀριθμός 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Persae” 339; τὴν πᾶσαν ἵππον 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.80; τὸ πᾶν πλῆθος 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 8.93]]; οἱ πάντες ἄνθρωποι absolutely all.., [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 5.6.7, etc.]]; so πᾶν the neuter with the Article itself becomes a substantive, τὸ πᾶν the whole, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Prometheus Vinctus” 275, 456, etc., see below 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator IV]]; τὰ πάντα the whole, [Refs [[prev. author] “Eu.” 415]]; τοῖς πᾶσιν in all points, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 2.64, 5.28]]; οἱ πάντες all of them, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.80]]; but also, the community, opposed to οἱ ὀλίγοι, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 4.86]]; ἡ μὲν [τάξις] πάντα ἕν, ἡ δὲ πάντα ὅλον, ἡ δὲ πάντα πᾶν all things as a unity, as a totality, as an integral sum, [Refs 5th c.AD+ [5th-6th c.AD: Damascius Philosophus “de Principiis” 206.]]

__C
with Numerals to mark an exact number, ἐννέα πάντες full nine, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 8.258, compare 24.60; ἐννέα πάντ᾽ ἔτεα 8th-7th c.BC: Hesiodus Epicus “Theogonia” 803; δέκα πάντα τάλαντα 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 19.247, etc.; but κτήνεα τὰ θύσιμα πάντα τρισχίλιαἔθυσε 3, 000]] of all kinds, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.50]]; τὸν ἀρχιτέκτονα.. ἐδωρήσατο πᾶσι δέκα with ten presents of all kinds, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. author] 4.88; Παυσανίῃ πάντα δέκα ἐξαιρέθη [prev. author] 9.81; τὰ πάντα μυρία [prev. author] 3.74; πάντα θύειν ἑκατόν 5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “Fragmenta.” 170; πάντα χίλια ἔθυεν 3rd c.AD: Porphyrius Tyrius Philosophus “de Abstinentia - Porphyrii Opuscula” 2.60.]]

__C.II
with the Article, in all, οἱ πάντες.. εἷς καὶ ἐνενήκοντα [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 9.70, compare 1.214, 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 1.60, 3.85, etc.; τριήρεις.. τὰς πάσας ἐς διακοσίας [prev. author] 1.100, compare 7.1; ἐν εἴκοσι ταῖς πάσαις ἡμέραις 2nd c.AD: Arrianus Historicus “Anabasis” 1.11.5.]]

__D
Special Usages: in dative plural masculine πᾶσι, with or in the judgement of all, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 2.285, 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Coloneus” 1446; ὁ πᾶσι κλεινός [prev. author] “OT” 8; κράτιστον πᾶσιν Οἰδίπου κάρα [prev. work] 40.]]

__D.2
feminine plural, ἔδοξε πάσαις (i.e. ταῖς ψήφοις) carried unanimously, [Refs 2nd c.BC+ [Inscriptiones Graecae 12(3).168.14 (Astypalaea, 2nd-1st c.BC),compare 2nd c.AD: Lucianus Sophista “Bis Acc.” 18,22.]]

__D.II
neuter plural πάντα all kinds of things, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Homerus Epicus, frequently in phrase δαίδαλα πάντα, 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 5.60, +others; οἰωνοῖσι πᾶσι 1.5.]]

__D.II.2
πάντα γιγνόμενος becoming all things, i. e. assuming every shape, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 4.417.]]

__D.II.3
πάντα εἶναί τινι to be everything to one, ἦν οἱ.. τὰ πάντα ἡ Κυνώ [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.122]]; ἦσάν οἱ πάντα —ἅπαντα codices) αἱ Συρήκουσαι [Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. author] 7.156; Εὔβοια αὐτοῖς πάντα ἦν 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 8.95; πάντ᾽ ἐκεῖνος ἦν αὐτοῖς 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 18.43]]; π. ἦν Ἀλέξανδρος (i.e. ὑμῖν) [Refs [[prev. author] 23.120]]; π. εἶναι ἔν τισι to be all in all among them, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 3.157.]]

__D.II.4
πάντα as adverb for πάντως, in all points, entirely, wholly, π. νοήμονες [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 13.209; π. γὰρ οὐ κακός εἰμι 8.214; ὁ πάντ᾽ ἄναλκις 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Electra” 301; τῷ πάντ᾽ ἀγαθῷ [prev. author] “Aj.” 1415 (_anapaest meter_); τὸν πάντ᾽ ἄριστον [prev. author] “OC” 1458; πάντ᾽ ἐπιστήμης πλέων [prev. author] “Ant.” 721 (hence παντάγαθος, παντάριστος, etc. as _compound_ words)]]; τὰ πολλὰ π. almost throughout, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 5.67, compare 1.203, 2.35]]; but τὰ π. in every way, by all means, altogether, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. author] 5.97; οἰόμενοι τὰ π. νικᾶν 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 2.1.1; ὁ τὰ π. φιλαίτατος 3rd c.BC: Theocritus Poeta Bucolicus 7.98]]; also ἐς τὰ π. [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 4.81]]; κατὰ π. [Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. passage], 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Timaeus” 30d.]]

__D.III
neuter singular, τὸ πᾶν the whole (V. [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Bacchylides Lyricus 11), περὶ τοῦ π. δρόμον θέειν 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 8.74; πολλοῦ γε καὶ τοῦ π. ἐλλείπω 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Prometheus Vinctus” 961; τοῦ π. ἡμαρτηκέναι 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Phaedrus” 235e]]; ἄξιοι τοῦ π. [Refs [[prev. author] “Sph.” 216c]]; τὸ πᾶν as adverb, completely, altogether, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Supplices” 781 (Lyric poetry), 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Electra” 1009, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Leges” 959a, etc.]] (but, for all that, nevertheless, [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd c.AD: Apollonius Dyscolus Grammaticus “de Syntaxi;” 188.27)]]: with negative, at all, οὐκ ἠξίωσαν οὐδὲ προσβλέψαι τὸ πᾶν [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Prometheus Vinctus” 217, etc.]]; also πᾶν alone, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.32, etc.]]

__D.III.b
in Philos., τὸ πᾶν the universe, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Empedocles Poeta Philosophus 13, 4th-5th c.BC: Pythagoras Philosophus cited in 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “de Caelo” 268a11, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Timaeus” 28c, 30b, etc.]]; including τὸ κενόν (opposed to τὸ ὅλον), [Refs 4th c.BC+ [“Placita Philosophorum” 2.1.7; also, 4th-5th c.BC: Pythagoras Philosophus]] name for ten, [Refs 4th c.AD+ [4th c.AD: Iamblichus Philosophus “in Nicomachi arithmeticam introductionem” p.118P., “Theologumena Arithmeticae” 59.]]

__D.III.c
τῷ παντί in every point, altogether, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Historia Graeca (Hellenica)” 7.5.12, etc.]]

__D.III.d
τὸ π., ={μολυβδόχαλκος}, Ps.- [Refs 5th c.BC+ [3rd c.AD: Democritus Epigrammaticus Alch. p.56 5th c.BC: Bacchylides Lyricus, Maria cited in Zos.Alch.p.192 5th c.BC: Bacchylides Lyricus]]

__D.III.2
πᾶν anything, πᾶν μᾶλλον ἢ στρατιήν οἱ ἐδίδου [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 4.162]]; εἴη δ᾽ ἂν πᾶν anything is possible, [Refs [[prev. work] 195]]; πᾶν ποιῶν by any means whatever, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Apologia” 39a (also πᾶν ποιεῖν καὶ λέγειν [prev. passage]]]; πᾶν ποιεῖν ὥστε.. [Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. author] “Phd.” 114c), compare 5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “I.” 4(3).48; πᾶν ἂν ἔπραξαν 5th c.BC: Lysias Orator 9.16: more frequently in _plural_, πάντα ποιῶν [prev. author] 12.84, 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 21.2]]; π. ποιεῖν ὅπως.. [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Historia Graeca (Hellenica)” 7.4.21; πάντα τολμῶν 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Coloneus” 761; compare 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus 111.2.]]

__D.III.3
ἐπὶ πᾶν on the whole, in general, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Leges” 875d; ὡς ἐπὶ πᾶν εἰπεῖν [prev. author] “Euthd.” 279e, etc.; τὸ πρὸς ἅπαν ξυνετὸν ἐπὶ πᾶν ἀργόν 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 3.82.]]

__D.III.4
παντὸς μᾶλλον more than anything, i. e. above all, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Crito” 49b, “Prt.” 344b, “Grg.” 527b; π. μᾶλλον οὐ [prev. author] “Phdr.” 228d: in answers, π. γε μᾶλλον]] quite so, [Refs [[prev. author] “Phd.” 67b.]]

__D.IV
with Preps., εἰς πᾶν προελήλυθε μοχθηρίας [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 3.3]]; ἐς τὸ πᾶν altogether, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Agamemnon” 682 (Lyric poetry), “Eu.” 52, 83]]; ἐν παντὶ ἀθυμίας εἶναι to be in utter despair, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 7.55: more frequently ἐν παντὶ εἶναι, ἐν παντὶ κακοῦ εἶναι]], to be in great danger or fear, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Symposium” 194a, “R.” 579b; ἐν π. γενέσθαι [prev. author] “Euthd.” 301a; ἐμ παντὶ ἐοῦσα “IG” 42(1).122.27 (Epid., 4th c.BC)]]; ἐν παντὶ εἶναι μή.. to be in great fear lest.., [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Historia Graeca (Hellenica)” 5.4.29; ἐς πᾶν κακοῦ ἀπίκατο 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 7.118; ἐς πᾶν ἀφικέσθαι 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Historia Graeca (Hellenica)” 6.1.12; εἰς πᾶν ἐλθεῖν 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 54.13]]; ἐπὶ πᾶσιν in all things, καιρὸς δ᾽ ἐπὶ π. ἄριστος [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th-7th c.BC: Hesiodus Epicus “Opera et Dies” 694]]; but also, finally, [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd-3rd c.AD: Philostratus Sophista “Vitae Sophistarum” 2.11.1, +others]]; περὶ παντὸς ποιεῖσθαι esteem above all,[Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Historia Graeca (Hellenica)” 7.1.26, “An.” 1.9.16]]; πρὸ παντὸς εὔχεσθαι wish above all, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Phaedrus” 239e]]; διὰ παντός (i.e. χρόνου) for ever, continually, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Ajax” 705 (Lyric poetry), 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 1.38, etc.]]; also, altogether, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 407d; διὰ πάντων [prev. author] “Sph.” 254b]]; ὁ κατὰ πάντων λόγος the common formula, [Refs [“PMag.Par.” 1.2186]]; ἡ κ. π. τελετή [Refs [[prev. work]1596, “PMag.Lond.” 121.872]]; μέχρι παντός for ever, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [1st c.BC-1st c.AD: Strabo Geographus 8.6.18; εἰς τὸ πᾶν ἀεί 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Choephori” 684; ἐς τὸ πᾶν χρόνου [prev. author] “Eu.” 670.]]

__D.V
διὰ πασῶν (i.e. χορδῶν), see at {διαπασῶν}.

__D.VI
οὐ πᾶς not any, i.e. none, [LXX+NT [LXX.Psa.142(143).2, NT.Luke.1.37, NT.Gal.2.16, +others]]; ἄνευ πάσης ταραχῆς without any disturbance, [Refs 1st c.BC+ [1st c.BC: Diodorus Siculus Historicus 15.87.]]

deep_entry:
Abbott-Smith / STEPBible (TBESG)
πάσχα, τό indecl. (Aram. טַּסְחָא),
[in LXX for פֶּסַח ;]
__1. the festival of the Passover: Mat.26:2, Mrk.14:1, Luk.22:1, Jhn.2:13, 23 6:4 11:55 12:1 18:39 19:14, Act.12:4, Heb.11:28; .ἡ ἐορτὴ τοῦ π., Luk.2:41, Jhn.13:1.
__2. By meton.,
__(a) the paschal supper: ἑτοιμάζειν τὸ π., Mat.26:19, Mrk.14:16, Luk.22:8, 13; ποιεῖν τό π., Mat.26:18;
__(b) the pasohal lamb: θύειν τό π. (Exo.12:21), Mrk.14:12, Luk.22:7; of Christ, 1Co.5:7; φαγεῖν τὸ π. (lamb or supper), Mat.26:17, Mrk.14:12, 14, Luk.22:11, 15, Jhn.18:28 (cf. 2Ch.30:17).†
(AS)

deep_entry:
Abbott-Smith / STEPBible (TBESG)
πάσχω
[in LXX: Amo.6:6 (חָלָה ni.), Wis.12:27, Sir.38:16, al. ;]
to suffer, be acted on, as opposite to acting, often limited by a word expressive of good or evil;
__(a) of misfortunes (most frequently without any limiting word) : absol., Luk.22:15 24:46, Act.1:3 3:18 17:3, 1Co.12:26, Heb.2:18 9:26 13:12, 1Pe.2:19-20 2:23 3:17 4:15 4:19; before ὑπό, with genitive, Mat.17:12; ὑπέρ, Act.9:16, Php.1:20, 2Th.1:5, 1Pe.2:21; with dative ref., 1Pe.4:1; περί, with genitive (before ὑπέρ), 1Pe.3:18; διά, with accusative, 1Pe.3:14; ὀλίγον (a little while), 1Pe.5:10; with accusative, Mat.27:19, Mrk.9:12, Luk.13:2 24:26, Act.28:5, 2Ti.1:12, Heb.5:8, Rev.2:10; παθήματα, 2Co.1:6; ταῦτα, Gal.3:4 (EV; cf. Lft., in l, but see infr.); accusative before ἀπό, Mat.16:21, Luk.9:22 17:25; ὑπό, Mrk.5:26, 1Th.2:14;
__(b) of pleasant experiences (but always with qualifying word, εὖ or accusative of thing(s)) : Gal.3:4 (cf. Grimm-Thayer, see word; Interp. Corn., in l, but see supr.) (cf. προ-, συν-πάσχω).†
(AS)

LSJ / STEPBible (TFLSJ)
πάσχω,
[Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 20.297, etc.]]: imperfect ἔπασχον [Refs [17.375, etc.]]: future πείσομαι [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 2.134, etc.]]; Doric dialect 3rd.pers. singular παισεῖται [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [“Abh.Berl.Akad.” 1925(5).21 (Cyrene, 3rd c.BC)]]: aorist ἔπᾰθον [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 9.492, etc.]]: perfect πέπονθα [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 13.6, etc.:]]pluperfect ἐπεπόνθειν[Refs [[prev. work] 92, etc.]]; Attic dialect ἐπεπόνθη [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Symposium” 198c]] (all the above tenses in [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Homerus Epicus]], present and aorist only in [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th-7th c.BC: Hesiodus Epicus). —Rarer forms, _2nd pers._ _plural_]]perfect πέπασθε (so [Refs 8th c.BC+ [3rd-2nd c.BC: Aristarchus Grammaticus) 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 3.99, πέποσθε 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 23.53]]; feminine perfect participle πεπᾰθυῖα [Refs [17.555]]; Doric dialect perfect πέποσχα [Refs 7th c.BC+ [7th-6th c.BC: Stesichorus Lyricus 89, 5th c.BC: Epicharmus Comicus 11, “PCair.Zen.” 482.18 (3rd c.BC)]]:—have something done to one, suffer, opposed to do, ὅσσ᾽ ἔρξαν τ᾽ ἔπαθόν τε [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 8.490; ῥέζοντά τι καὶ παθεῖν ἔοικεν 5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “N.” 4.32]]; δρᾶν καὶ πάσχειν, see at {δρά; πολλὰ μὲν.. πείσεσθαι}, πολλὰ δὲ ποιήσειν [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 5.89, etc.: hence used as]]passive of ποιέω compare [Refs 4th c.BC+ [(4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Categoriae” 2a4, “Metaphorical” 1017a26, 3rd c.AD: Plotinus Philosophus 3.6.8, etc.), π. τι ὑπό τινος]] to be treated so and so by another, suffer it at his hands, ἃ πάσχοντες ὑφ᾽ ἑτέρων ὀργίζεσθε, ταῦτα τοὺς ἄλλους μὴ ποιεῖτε [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Isocrates Orator 3.61, compare 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.44, 124, +others; ἐξ ἐμοῦ μὲν ἔπαθες οἷα φῂς παθεῖν, δρᾷς δ᾽ οὐδὲν ἡμᾶς εὖ 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Hecuba” 252; οἷα πρὸς θεῶν πάσχω θεός 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Prometheus Vinctus” 92, compare 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.36.]]

__II
to have something happen to one, to be or come to be in a state or case, καί τι ἔφη γελοῖον παθεῖν [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Symposium” 174e; ὅπερ οἱ τὰς ἐγχέλεις θηρώμενοι πέπονθας 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Equites” 846, compare “V.” 946]]; ὁρᾶτε μὴ ταὐτὸ πάθητε τῷ ἵππῳ see that it be not with you as with the horse in the fable, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Rhetorica” 1393b20, compare 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 488a]]; παραπλήσιον π. ὥσπερ ἂν εἰ.. [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Isocrates Orator 1.27]]; ὁμοιότατον πεπονθέναι ὥσπερ ἂν εἴ τις.. [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Phaedo” 98c.]]

__II.2
of the influence of passion or feeling, to be affected in a certain way, be (or come to be) in a certain state of mind, οἱ Καμαριναῖοι ἐπεπόνθεσαν τοιόνδε [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 6.88, compare 1.80, 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 20.56; ὅ τι μὲν ὑμεῖς πεπόνθατε ὑπὸ τῶν ἐμῶν κατηγόρων οὐκ οἶδα 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Apologia” 17a, compare 21c, 22c, Alcaeus1.118b, “Smp.” 198c; π. τι πρός τινας 5th-6th c.BC: Isocrates Orator 2.42, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Gorgias” 485b, compare 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Symposium” 4.11, 8.15, etc.; τι ἔς τινας 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 6.11: sometimes with]] adjective, ὑϊκὸν πάσχει he is swinishly disposed, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Memorabilia” 1.2.30: _absolutely_, ὁ πάσχων]] the man of feeling or impulse, ὁ μὴ πάσχων the unimpassioned man, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Magna Moralia” 1203b21.]]

__II.3
of things, πεπόνθασι.. αἱ Ἰώνων ὁρταὶ τοῦτο this is the case with.., [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.148]]; πάσχει δὲ ταὐτὸ τοῦτο καὶ τὰ κάρδαμα this is just the way with.., [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Nubes” 234; οἷον τὰ γράμματα πεπονθότ᾽ ἂν εἴη 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Sophista” 253a]]; ὁμοίως π. τῷ Νείλῳ to be in the same case with.., [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 2.20.]]

__II.4
Grammars, of words, to be subject to certain changes, [Refs [EM 200.11, 491.2, etc.]]; τὸ πεπονθός a modified form, [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd c.AD: Apollonius Dyscolus Grammaticus “de Adverbiis;” 137.16.]]

__II.4.b
to be passive in meaning, [Refs [[prev. author] “Synt.” 244.6, +others]]

__III
frequently with adverbs, κακῶς πάσχειν or παθεῖν to be in evil plight, unlucky, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 16.275, 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 3.146, etc.]]; κακῶς π. ὑπό τινος to be ill used, ill treated by.., [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Prometheus Vinctus” 1041 (_anapaest meter_); ἐκ Διὸς π. κακῶς [prev. work] 759 (but also κακὸν π. ὑ. τ. 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 8.48): frequently with an]] adjective, κακά, αἰνά, λυγρὰ π[Refs 8th c.BC+ [., 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 3.99, 22.431, 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 9.37; ἀνάρσια πρός τινος [prev. author] 5.89: frequently in Trag., π. δύσοιστα, τάλανα, ἀμήχανα, οἰκτρά, σχέτλια, ἀνάξια, 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Eumenides” 789 (Lyric poetry), “Th.” 988 (uncertain), 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Hippolytus” 598, “Hec.” 321, “Andr.” 1180 (uncertain), “IA” 852: also in Prose, δεινά, βίαια π., 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 51.19, 21.1, etc.]]; πρέποντα πάσχειν[Refs 8th c.BC+ [Anti-pho 3.3.9: in 8th c.BC: Homerus Epicus also with]] substantive, ἄλγεα, κήδεα, πήματα, ἀεκήλια ἔργα[Refs 8th c.BC+ [, 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 20.297, 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 17.555, 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 5.886, 18.77]]: rarely in Attic dialect, πράγματ᾽ αἴσχιστ᾽ ἂν ἐπάθομεν [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 21.17.]]

__III.b
εὖ πάσχειν to be well off, in good case, with genitive, τῶν αὑτοῦ (to be read ὧν αὐτοῦ, compare ὅς Possess.) κτεάνων εὖ πασχέμεν to have the good of, enjoy one's own, like{ἀπολαύω}, γεύομαι, etc., [Refs 6th c.BC+ [6th c.BC: Theognis Elegiacus 1009, compare 5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “N.” 1.32]]; εὖ πάσχειν receive benefits, opposed to εὖ δρᾶν, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Eumenides” 868, 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 2.40, etc.; ἀνθ᾽ ὧν ἔπασχον εὖ.. χάριν δοῦναι 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Coloneus” 1489; τιμᾶσθαι.. ἐν τῇ μνήμῃ τῶν εὖ πεπονθότων 4th c.BC: Aeschines Orator 3.182; εὖ παθεῖν ὑπό τινων 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Gorgias” 519d, etc.]]: also with an adjective, π. ἀγαθά [Refs 7th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 2.37; τι ἐσλόν 5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “P.” 9.89, compare 7th-6th c.BC: Alcaeus Lyricus “Supp.” 22.5; τερπνόν τι 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Ajax” 521, compare 3rd c.BC: Theocritus Poeta Bucolicus 7.83]]; χαρτά, ὅσια, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Phoenissae” 618, “Hec.” 788]]; γλυκέα, χαρίεντα π., [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Pax” 591, “Ec.” 794; δίκαια 4th-3rd c.BC: Dinarchus Orator 1.10; φιλικὰ ὑπό τινος 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 4.6.6.]]

__III.2

Syngr. cited in 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 35.13.]]

in Law, suffer punishment, pay the penalty, [NT+5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Lysias Orator 20.30; π. ὡς ἱερόσυλος “SIG” 1016.7 (Iasos, 4th c.BC),cf. NT.1Pet.4.15]]; ὡς προδότης καὶ ἐπιβουλεύων τῷ δήμῳ πασχέτω τι Aen.[Refs 5th c.BC+ [Tact. 11.9; τιμᾶν ὅ τι χρὴ παθεῖν.. ἢ ἀποτεῖσαι 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Politicus” 299a (-τίνειν codices),compare “Ap.” 36b, 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Memorabilia” 2.9.5, “IG” 12.65.50, etc.]]

__III.3
τί πάθ; what is to become of me? ὤμοι ἐγώ, τί π.; [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 11.404, 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 5.465, 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Coloneus” 216 (Lyric poetry), 3rd c.BC: Theocritus Poeta Bucolicus 3.24]]; sometimes what (else) am I to do? [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Euthydemus” 302d, compare 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 4.118.]]

__III.4
in 2nd pers. singular, τί πάσχει; what's the matter with you? [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Nubes” 708, “Av.” 1044]]; τί χρῆμα πάσχει; [Refs [[prev. author] “Nu.” 816]]: so in aorist participle, τί παθώ; τί παθόντε λελάσμεθα θούριδος ἀλκῆ; what possesses us that we have forgotten.. ? [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 11.313]]; but τί παθόντες γαῖαν ἔδυτ; what befell you that you died ? [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 24.106]]; also οὐδὲν θαυμαστὸν ἔπαθεν.. πεισθείς no wonder that he was induced, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Antipho Orator 2.4.7.]]

to be ill, suffer, with accusative of the part affected, π. τοὺς πόδας, τὴν πλευράν, [Refs 3rd c.AD+ [“PSI” 4.293.23 (3rd c.AD), “PGen.” 56.27 (4th c.AD): _absolutely_ in]]participle, ὁ πάσχων, almost ={ὁ κάμνων}, the patient, PMag. __IV
in later Stoic Philos., πάσχειν is to be acted upon by outward objects, take impressions from, them, opposed to ἀποπάσχω, mostly followed by ὅτι, to be led to suppose that.., [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd c.AD: Arrianus Historicus “Epicteti Dissertationes” 1.2.3, 1.18.1, etc.]]: also with accusative, have experience of, ἀρετήν, λόγον, [Refs 1st c.AD+ [1st c.AD: Philo Judaeus 2.449, 1.121.]] (Πṇθσκω, future Πένθ-σομαι, compare πένθος.)

deep_entry:
Abbott-Smith / STEPBible (TBESG)
πατήρ, πατρός, -τρί, τέρα,  [in LXX chiefly and very frequently for אָב ;]
a father;
__1. prop.,
__(a) of the male parent: Mat.2:22, Luk.1:17, Jhn.4:53; anarth., Heb.12:7 (M, Pr., 82 f.); pl., of both parents (cl.), Heb.11:23; οἱ π. τ. σαρκός, Heb.12:9;
__(b) of a forefather or ancestor (in cl. usually in pl.; Hom., al.): Mat.3:9, Luk.1:73, Jhn.8:39, al.; pl., Mat.23:30, 32 Luk.6:23, 26 Jhn.4:20, 1Co.10:1, al.
__2. Metaphorical,
__(a) of an author, originator, or archetype (= αἴτιος, ἀρχηγός, etc.; Pind., Plat., al.): Jhn.8:41-44, Rom.4:11, 12 16.
__(b) as a title of respect or honour, used of seniors, teachers and others in a position of responsible authority (Jdg.17:10, 2Ki.2:12, Pro.1:8, al.): Mat.23:9 Act.7:2 22:1, 1Jn.2:13.
__3. Of God (as in cl. of Zeus) as Father;
__(a) of created things: τ. φώτων, Jas.1:17;
__(b) of all sentient beings: Eph.3:14, 15 Heb.12:9;
__(with) of men, esp. those in covenant relation with Him (freq in OT and later Jewish lit.; see Dalman, Words, 184ff.): Mat.6:4, Luk.6:36, Jhn.4:21, Jas.3:9, al.; ὁ π. ὁ ἐν (τ.) οὐρανοῖς, Mat.5:16, Mrk.11:25; ὁ π. ὁ οὐράνιος, Mat.6:14 15:13; esp. in the Epp., of Christians: Rom.8:15, 2Co.6:18, Gal.4:6, Eph.2:18 4:6, 1Jn.2:1; with genitive qual., τ. οἰκτιρμῶν, 2Co.1:3; τ. δοξῆς, Eph.1:17;
__(d) of Christ (Dalman, Words, 190 ff.);
__(α) by our Lord himself: ὁ π., Mat.11:25-27, Luk.10:2, 22 Jhn.5:20-23, al.; ὁ π. μου, Mat.11:27, al.; ὁ ἐν τ. οὐρανοῖς, Mat.7:11, al.; ὁ οὐράνιος, Mat.15:13; vocat., Jhn.11:41 12:27, 28 17:1, 5, 11, 20, 25 (cf. Abbott, JG., 96 f.);
__(β) by Apostles: Jhn.1:14 (anarth.; see M, Pr., l.with), Rom.15:6, 2Co.1:3 11:31, Eph.1:3, Col.1:3, Heb.1:5, 1Pe.1:3, Rev.1:6 (cf. Westc., Epp. Jo., 27-34).
(AS)

__II
especially as epithet of Zeus, πατὴρ Ζεύς, π. Κρονίδης, π. ἀνδρῶν τε θεῶν τε, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 4.235, 21.508, 1.544, +others]]; Ζεὺς π. [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Septem contra Thebas” 512, etc.; Ζεῦ πάτερ καὶ θεοί 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Acharnenses” 225]]; π. Οὐρανιδᾶν Ζ. __I

__I.1
with accusative only, bring to an end, check, sometimes of persons, ἵνα παύσομεν ἄγριον ἄνδρα [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 21.314, compare 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Antigone” 963 (Lyric poetry), 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Equites” 330]]; stop or silence by death, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 20.274, 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Tyrannus” 397]]:—passive and middle, take one's rest, ἐνὶ κλισίῃ [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 24.17, compare 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 9.52, etc.]]; cease, have done, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 8.295, 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 4.103, etc.]]; of one singing or speaking, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [17.359, 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 7.8.δ]]: generally, middle denotes willing, passive forced, cessation.

__I.1.b

[Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Isocrates Orator 4.91.]]

__3
of animals, land, opposed to birds and fishes, τὰ π. καὶ τὰ πτηνά beasts and birds, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Symposium” 207a, compare “Plt.” 264e]]; π. καὶ ἔνυδρον[Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. work] 288a, compare “Lg.” 823b, 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Topica” 143b1, etc.; ἡ π. θήρα 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Sophista” 222b, compare “Lg.” 824a.]]

__II
metaphorically [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [compare (αὐτὰρ ἐγὼ Μουσέων πεζὸς ἔπειμι νομόν 3rd c.BC: Callimachus Epicus “Aetia” 4.1.9)]], of language, prosaic, λόγοι π. prose[Refs 1st c.BC+ [(compare 111.3), 1st c.BC: Dionysius Halicarnassensis “de Compositione Verborum” 6, 2nd c.AD: Pausanias Periegeta 4.6.1]]; διὰ πεζῶν [λ.] [Refs 1st c.BC+ [1st c.BC: Philodemus Gadarensis Epigrammaticus “Mus.” p.87 K.; λόγος “POxy.” 724.10 (2nd c.AD)]]; ἡ π. διάλεκτος [Refs 1st c.BC+ [1st c.BC: Dionysius Halicarnassensis “de Compositione Verborum” 3; ἡ π. λέξις [prev. work] 1; opposed to ἡ ἔμμετρος, [prev. work] 4]]; ἡ π. alone, [Refs 1st c.BC+ [1st c.BC-1st c.AD: Strabo Geographus 1.2.6; τινὰ καὶ πεζὰ καὶ ἐν ἔπεσι ποιήματα 2nd-3rd c.AD: Dio Cassius Historicus 69.3]]; π. τις ποιητική, of bombastic prose, [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd c.AD: Lucianus Sophista “Hist.Conscr.” 8]]; κομιδῇ πεζὸν καὶ χαμαιπετές[Refs 4th c.BC+ [[prev. work] 16, compare 1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus 2.853c; τὰ ἄγαν π. καὶ κακόμετρα [ὀνόματα] [prev. work]747f; π. ὀνόματα, opposed to ποιητικά, 4th c.BC: Demetrius Phalereus Rhetor “Demetrius on Style” 167.]]

__II.2
of verse, unaccompanied by music, καὶ πεζὰ καὶ φορμικτά [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Fragmenta” 16]]; πεζῷ γόῳ· ἄνευ αὐλοῦ ἢ λύρας, [Refs 9th c.AD+ [9th c.AD: Photius Legal icographus, etc.; compare 111.2.]]

__II.3
common, ordinary, ἑταῖραι [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Theopompus Historicus 205; μόσχοι 5th c.BC: Eupolis Comicus 169; π. αὐλητρίς 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Comicus 155.]]

__III
dative feminine πεζῇ (i.e. ὁδῷ) as adverb,

__III.1
on foot, opposed to σὺν ἵππῳ, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Oeconomicus” 5.5.]]

__III.1.b
more commonly, by land, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 2.159, 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 2.94, etc.]]; π. ἕπεσθαι to follow by land, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 7.110, 115; στρατιὰν μέλλων π. πορεύσειν 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 4.132; π. πορεύεσθαι 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 5.6.1; οὔτε π. οὔτε κατὰ θάλατταν [prev. work] 5.6.10]]; καὶ π. καὶ ναυμαχοῦντες by land and by sea, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 3.24.]]

__III.2
without musical accompaniment[Refs 5th c.BC+ [(compare 11.2), παῦσαι μελῳδοῦσ᾽ ἀλλὰ π. μοι φράσον “Comica Adespota” 601, compare 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Sophista” 237a.]]

__III.3
regular adverb πεζῶς in prose, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [1st c.BC: Philodemus Gadarensis Epigrammaticus “Rh.” 1.165 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus, 10th c.AD: Suidas Legal icographus see at {ἱστορῆσαι}.]]

__IV
comparative πεζότερος more like a foot-journey, [Refs 1st c.AD+ [1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus 2.804d]]; more like prose, στίχοι π. τῇ συνθέσει [Refs 8th c.BC+ [Scholia 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 2.252, etc.: _superlative_ πεζότατος, τὸ π. μόριον τῆς ψυχή,compare 5th c.AD: Proclus Philosophus “in Platonis Timaeum commentarii” 3.317 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator]]

πείθω,
[in LXX chiefly for בָּטַח בֶּטַח, its parts and derivatives ;]
__(i) Active;
__1. trans., to apply persuasion ("conative" in pres.; see M, Pr., 147), to prevail upon or win over, persuade: absol., Mat.28:14,  Act.19:26; before περί, with genitive of thing(s), Act.19:8; with accusative of person(s), Act.12:20 14:19 18:4, 2Co.5:11, Gal.1:10; τ. καρδίας ἡμῶν, 1Jn.3:19; with accusative before περί, Act.28:23; with accusative and inf., Act.13:43 26:28 (see Field, Notes, 141 ff.); with accusative before ἵνα (Plut.), Mat.27:20.
__2. Intrans., 2 pf. πέποιθα with Pres. sense (see M, Pr., 147, 154; Bl., § 59, 2): to trust, be confident, have confidence: with accusative and inf., Rom.2:19; with accusative ref. (see Ellic., in l) : Php.1:6, 25; with dative, Php.1:14, Phm 21; ἑαυτῷ, with inf., 2Co.10:7; before ἐν, Php.3:3-4; ἐν κυρίῳ ὅτι, Php.2:24; ἐπί, with dative, Mat.27:43 (WH, mg.), Mrk.10:24 (T, WH, R, mg., om.), Luk.11:22 18:9, 2Co.1:9, Heb.2:13; ἐπί, with accusative, Mat.27:43 (with dative, WH, mg.); id. before ὅτι, 2Co.2:3, 2Th.3:4 (see Lft., Notes, 127); εἰς, with accusative of person(s) before ὅτι, Gal.5:10.
(ii) Pass. and mid.;
__1. to be persuaded, believe (see M, Pr., 158) : absol., Luk.16:31, Act.17:4 21:14, Heb.13:18; with dative, Act.28:24; with accusative and inf., Act.26:26; so also pf., πέπεισμαι, πεπεισμένος εἰμί: with accusative ref. before περί, Heb.6:9; with accusative and inf., Luk.20:6; ὅτι, Rom.8:38, 2Ti.1:5 1:12; id. with ἐν κυρίῳ, Rom.14:14; περί, with genitive before ὅτι, Rom.15:14.
__2. to listen to, obey: with dative of person(s), Act.5:36-37, 40 23:21 27:11, Rom.2:8, Gal.5:7, Heb.13:17, Jas.3:3 (cf. ἀνα-πείθω).†
Πειθώ, -οῦς, ἡ
__1. Peitho, Persuasion (as a goddess).
__2. per­suasion: ἐν πειθοῖ (so Orig., Eus. and some cursives in 1Co.2:4 for πειθός, which see).†

[NT+1st c.AD+ [NT.Matt.27.20, 1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus 2.181a]]; π. τινὰς ὡς χρὴ.., ὡς ἔστι.., [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 327c, 364b; π. τινὰ ἐς τὴν ὁμολογίαν 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 5.76; κοὐδείς γέ μ᾽ ἂν πείσειεν.. τὸ μὴ ἐλθεῖν 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Ranae” 68]]; πείθω ἐμαυτόν I persuade myself, am persuaded, believe, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 6.33, 5th-6th c.BC: Andocides Orator 1.70, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Gorgias” 453b, etc.; also π. τι ὠφέλιμον ὄν 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 4.17: frequently in]]participle, πείσας by persuasion, by fair means, opposed to ἐν δόλῳ, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Philoctetes” 102, compare 612]]; opposed to βίᾳ, [Refs [“Tragica Adespota” 402]]; πόλιν πείσας having obtained the city's consent, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Coloneus” 1298; δᾶμον πείσαις λόγῳ 5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “O.” 3.16]]; π. γυναῖκα, opposed to βιάζεσθαι, [Refs [[prev. author] “Cyr.” 6.1.34]]; πέπεικε, opposed to ἠνάγκακε, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Hipparchus” 232b (but π. ἀνάγκῃ 2nd-3rd c.AD: Dio Cassius Historicus 62.16, compare πειθανάγκη)]]: with neuter pronoun, persuade one to or of a thing, τοῦτό γε οὐκ ἔπειθε τοὺς Φωκαιέας [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.163, compare 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Prometheus Vinctus” 1064 (_anapaest meter_), 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 399b, etc.; ἔπειθον οὐδέν᾽ οὐδέν 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Agamemnon” 1212]]; μὴ πεῖθ᾽ ἃ μὴ δεῖ do not attempt to persuade me to.., [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Coloneus” 1442]]; also τοιάνδ᾽ ἔπειθε ῥῆσιν addressed them thus, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Supplices” 615.]]

__2
prevail on by entreaty, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 24.219, 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 14.363; τότε κέν μιν ἱλασσάμενοι πεπίθοιμεν 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 1.100; ὥς κέν μιν ἀρεσσάμενοι πεπίθωμεν 9.112, compare 181, 386, 8th-7th c.BC: Hesiodus Epicus “Scutum Herculis” 450; Ζηνὸς ἦτορ λιταῖς 5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “O.” 2.80, compare 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 366a, “Ap.” 37d: with double _accusative_, τὸν φόρον ὑποτελῶ Ἀθηναίοισιν, ὃν ἂν πείθω Ἀθηναίους “IG” 12.39.27.]]

__II
in bad sense, talk over, mislead, ἐπεὶ οὐ παρελεύσεαι οὐδέ με πείσεις [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 1.132, compare 6.360; ἔληθε δόλῳ καὶ ἔπειθεν Ἀχαιούς 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 2.106, compare 14.123; πεπιθοῦσα θυέλλας 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 15.26.]]

__II.2
π. τινὰ χρήμασι bribe, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 8.134, 5th c.BC: Lysias Orator 21.10]]; π. ἐπὶ μισθῷ μισθῷ, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 8.4, 9.33, 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 2.96, etc.]] (passive, χρήμασι πεισθείς [Refs 8th c.BC+ [[prev. author] 1.137): proverbial, δῶρα θεοὺς πείθει 8th-7th c.BC: Hesiodus Epicus “Fragmenta” 272]]; πείθειν τινά alone, [NT+5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Lysias Orator 7.21, 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 1.3.19, NT.Act.12.20.]]

__II.3
offood, tempt, [Refs 1st c.AD+ [1st c.AD: Xenocrates Medicus cited in 4th c.AD: Oribasius Medicus 2.58.84.]]

__B
passive and middle, to be prevailed on, won over, persuaded, absolutely, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 5.201, etc.]]; imperative frequently in Trag., πείθου be persuaded, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Coloneus” 520, “El.” 1015, 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Fragmenta” 440]]; but πιθοῦ comply, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Coloneus” 1181, “El.” 1207]]: with infinitive, to be persuaded to do, [Refs [[prev. author] “Ph.” 624]]; πείθεσθέ μοι πρύτανιν ἑλέσθαι [Refs [Pl. “Prt.” 338a]]; also πείθεσθαί τινι ὥστε.. [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 2.2]]; ὃ.. ὑμεῖς.. ἥκιστ᾽ ἂν ὀξέως πείθοισθε (i.e. πρᾶξαι) [Refs [[prev. author] 6.34]]; ἑκὼν καὶ πεπεισμένος of one's own free will, [Refs 4th c.AD+ [POxy. ivp 203 (4th c.AD)]], etc.; τὰ μὲν παρ᾽ ἡμῶν ἴσθι σοι πεπεισμένα we are won over to you, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Thesmophoriazusae” 1170.]]

__B.2
πείθεσθαί τινι listen to one, obey him, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 1.79, etc.]]; τοῖς ἐν τέλει βεβῶσι π. [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Antigone” 67]]; τοῖς ἄρχουσι, τῷ νόμῳ, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 1.2.8, “An.” 7.3.39; μᾶλλον τῷ θεῷ ἢ ὑμῖν 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Apologia” 29d: sometimes with double _dative_, ἔπεσι, μύθοισι π. τινί, 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 1.150, 23.157: without _dative_ _person_, ἐπείθετο μύθῳ 1.33, compare 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 17.177]]; γήραϊ πείθεσθαι yield, succumb to old age, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 23.645]]; στυγερῇ πειθώμεθα δαιτί let us comply with the custom of eating, sad though the meal be, [Refs [[prev. work] 48; νῦν μὲν πειθώμεθα νυκτὶ μελαίνῃ, of leaving off the labours of the day, 8.502]]; ἀδίκοις ἔργμασι π. [Refs 6th c.BC+ [6th c.BC: Solon Lyricus 4.11, 13.12.]]

__B.2.b
with adjective neuter, σημάντορι πάντα πιθέσθαι obey him in all things, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 17.21]]; ἅ τιν᾽ οὐ πείσεσθαι ὀΐω wherein I think some will not obey, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 1.289, compare 4.93, 7.48, 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 6.100, etc.; πάντ᾽ ἔγωγε πείσομαι 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Ajax” 529; πείσομαι δ᾽ ἃ σοὶ δοκεῖ [prev. author] “Tr.” 1180; οὐ.. πείθομαι τὸ δρᾶν [prev. author] “Ph.” 1252; μύθοις.. πεισθεὶς ἀφανῆ 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Hippolytus” 1288 (_anapaest meter_), compare 5th c.BC: Lysias Orator 22.3: rarely with Noun in _accusative_, χρήμασι πεισθῆναι [τὴν ἀναχώρησιν] 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 2.21 (assuming variant).]]

__B.3
with genitive, four times in [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus, πείθεσθαί τινος 1.126, 5.29, 33, 6.12, compare 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Iphigenia Aulidensis” 726, 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 7.73; πείσθητί μευ 3rd c.BC: Herodas Mimographus 1.66]]; κείνου.. πιθοίατο vulgar form in [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 10.57.]]

__B.II
πείθεσθαί τινι believe, trust in, πείθεθ᾽ ἑταίρῳ [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 20.45; οἰωνοῖσι 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 12.238; τεράεσσι θεῶν καὶ Ζηνὸς ἀρωγῇ 4.408; ἐνυπνίῳ 5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “O.” 13.79; λεγομένοισι 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 2.146, etc.]]: with accusative et infinitive, believe that.., οὐ γάρ πω ἐπείθετο ὃν πατέρ᾽ εἶναι [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 16.192, compare 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.8, etc.: with _dative_ _person_ et]]infinitive, π. τινὶ μὴ εἶναι χρήματα, ={ὅτι χρήματα οὐκ ἔχει}, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 7.8.3: with ὡς, οὐ πείσονται ὡς σὺ αὐτὸς οὐκ ἠθέλησας 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Crito” 44c, compare “R.” 391b: with _neuter_]] adjective or pronoun, τὰ περὶ Αἴγυπτον τοῖσι λέγουσι αὐτὰ π., οὐκ ἐπείθοντο τὰ ἐσαγγελθέντα[Refs 5th c.BC+ [, 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 2.12, 8.81; πείθεσθε τούτῳ ταῦτα 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Thesmophoriazusae” 592]]; ταῦτ᾽ ἐγώ σοι οὐ πείθομαι I do not take this on your word, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Apologia” 25e, compare “Phdr.” 235b: _absolutely_, ὡς ἐγὼ πείθομαι 1st c.BC: Philodemus Philosophus “περὶ ποιημάτων” 5.34.]]

__B.II.b
π. τινὰ ὅπως.. to believe of him, that.., [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Hippolytus” 1251.]]

__B.III
perfect [Refs [2 πέποιθα]]trust, rely on, with dative person vel of things, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 4.325, etc.]] (not frequently in early Prose, as αὑτῷ πεποιθέναι [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Menexenus” 248a)]]: with dative et infinitive, οὔ πω χερσὶ πέποιθα ἄνδρ᾽ ἀπαμύνασθαι [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 16.71, compare 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 13.96, etc.: with _dative_, οἷσι.. μαρναμένοισι πέποιθε 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 16.98: later with]]infinitive only, πέποιθα τοῦτ᾽ ἐπισπάσειν κλέος I trust to win this fame, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Ajax” 769]]; αἰχμήν.. μᾶλλον θεοῦ σέβειν πεποιθώς daring to.., [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Septem contra Thebas” 530: once in 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus, χρήμασι ἐπεποίθεσαν διώσεσθαι 9.88]]: rarely with accusative et infinitive, πέποιθα.. τὸν πυρφόρον ἥξειν κεραυνόν [NT+4th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Septem contra Thebas” 444; εἴ τις πέποιθεν ἑαυτῷ Χριστοῦ εἶναι NT.2Cor.10.7]]; π. εἴς τινας ὅτι.. [NT.Gal.5.10]; ἐπί τινας ὅτι.. [NT.2Cor.2.3; ἐπὶ χρήμασι NT.Mark.10.24: _absolutely_, ὄφρα πεποίθῃς] that you may feel confidence, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 1.524, 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 13.344]]; πεποιθώς in sure confidence, [LXX.Deu.33.28.]

__B.IV
post-[Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Homerus Epicus]]perfect passive πέπεισμαι believe, trust, with dative, νεκροῖσι [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Eumenides” 599; ὀνείροις 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Helena” 1190, etc.: with _accusative_ et]]infinitive, συνοίσειν ταῦτα πέπ. [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 4.51, compare 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 368a: _absolutely_, νῦν δὲ πέπεισμαι [prev. author] “Prt.” 328e]]; πεπεισμένος ἔκ τινων λογίων persuaded by.., [NT+1st c.AD+ [1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus “Romulus” 14; πεπείσμεθα περὶ ὑμῶν τὰ κρείττονα NT.Heb.6.9]]. (Cf. Latin fido, fides.)

forms in αε contraction into η not ᾱ (as in διψάω,[Refs 2nd c.AD+ [compare 2nd c.AD: Phrynichus Atticista 42)]], πεινῇς, -ῇ [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Equites” 1270]]; infinitive πεινῆν [Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. author] “Nu.” 441, “Pl.” 595, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Gorgias” 496c]]; Epic dialect πεινήμεναι [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 20.137 (only here in 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey”)]]: imperfect ἐπείνων [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Historia Graeca (Hellenica)” 6.2.15]]: future πεινήσω [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 2.13, 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Plutus” 539, 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Memorabilia” 2.1.17]]; later πεινάσω [ᾱ] [LXX+NT [LXX.Sir.24.21, +others, NT.Rev.7.16]]: aorist ἐπείνησα [LXX+5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 8.3.39, ἐπείνᾱσα LXX.Gen.41.55, 2nd c.AD: Lucianus Sophista “epigram” 50, 5th-4th c.BC: Aesopus Fabularum Scriptor 62, 3rd c.AD: Pseudo-Callisthenes Historicus 3.6]]: perfect πεπείνηκα [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 606a]]: later we find the contraction of αε into ᾱ, ἐπείνας, πεινᾷ, -ᾶν, [LXX+NT [LXX.Deu.25.18, NT.Rom.12.20, etc.]]: (πεῖνἀ):—to be hungry, πεινάων, of a lion, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 3.25; λέοντε.. ἄμφω πεινάοντε 16.758; λέοντα.. μέγα πεινάοντα 18.162]]; κακῶς π. to be starved, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 2.13, 14; π. βάδην 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Acharnenses” 535]]; thrice in Trag., πεινῶσα [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Fragmenta” 199; πεινῶντι 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Fragmenta” 895, 5th c.BC: Achaeus Tragicus 25; πεινᾶντι δὲ μηδὲ ποτένθῃς 3rd c.BC: Theocritus Poeta Bucolicus 15.148: _metaphorically_, πεινῆν φασι τὴν γῆν 4th-3rd c.BC: Theophrastus Philosophus “Historia Plantarum” 8.6.2.]]

__II
with genitive, hunger after, σίτου δ᾽ οὐκέτ᾽ ἔφη πεινήμεναι [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 20.137.]]

__II.2
metaphorically, hunger, crave after, χρημάτων [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 8.3.39, etc.; ἐπαίνου [prev. author] “Oec.” 13.9]]; simply, to be in want of, lack, πεινῶντες ἀγαθῶν [NT+5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 521a; μάλα π. συμμάχων 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 7.5.50, etc.: later with _accusative_, οἱ π. καὶ διψῶντες τὴν δικαιοσύνην NT.Matt.5.6]]. [ᾱ in un contraction forms in [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Homerus Epicus With this the _Doric dialect_ contractions δια-πεινᾶμες (see. διαπεινάω) and πεινᾶντι 3rd c.BC: Theocritus Poeta Bucolicus]] [same place], and the Attic dialect contractions (-η- from -ηε-) agree; but πεινῶντι Doric dialect 3rd.pers. plural present indicative in [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Historia Graeca (Hellenica)” 1.1.23]] codices points to -ᾰοντι.]

deep_entry:
Abbott-Smith / STEPBible (TBESG)
πειράζω  poët. and late prose form of πειράω, which see,
[in LXX for נָסָה pi. ;]
__1. to make proof of (Hom.).
__2. to try, attempt (Luc., Polyb., with inf. (see M, Pr., 205; B1., § 69, 4), Act.9:26 16:7 24:6.
__3. In LXX and NT, like Heb. נָסָה, with accusative of person(s), to test, try, prove;
__(a) in a good sense : Jhn.6:6, 2Co.13:5, Heb.11:17, Rev.2:2; esp. of trials and af6ictions sent or permitted by God (Gen.22:1, Exo.20:20, Wis.3:5, al.), 1Co.10:13, Heb.2:18 4:15 11:17, 37, Rev.3:10;
__(b) in a bad sense (Apoll. Rhod., 3, 10): of the attempts made to ensnare Jesus in his speech, Mat.16:1 19:3 22:18, 35 Mrk.8:11 10:2 12:15, Luk.11:16, Jhn.8:6; of temptation to sin, to tempt, Jas.1:13-14 (see Hort, in l), Gal.6:1, Rev.2:10; esp. of temptations of the devil, Mat.4:1, 3 Mrk.1:13, Luk.4:2, 1Co.7:5, 1Th.3:5; ὁ πειράζων, the tempter, Mat.4:3, 1Th.3:5;
__(with) in bad sense also (Exo.17:2, 7, Num.14:22, al.), of distrustful testing, trying or challenging of God: Act.15:10, 1Co.10:9 (WH, mg., ἐξεπείρασαν), Heb.3:9; τ. πνεῦμα Κυρίου, Act.5:9 (of. ἐκ-πειράζω).†
SYN.: δοκιμάζω, q.v  (AS)

deep_entry:
Abbott-Smith / STEPBible (TBESG)
πειρασμός, -οῦ, ὁ
(πειράζω), [in LXX for מַסָּה, עִנְיָן ;]
__1. = πεῖρα, an experiment Diosc.).
__2. a trial, of ethical purpose and effect, whether good or evil (see Hort on Jas.1:13)
__(a) in good or neutral sense: Gal.4:14, Jas.1:12, 1Pe.4:12; esp. of afflictions sent by God  (Deu.7:19, Sir.21:1-28, al.): 2Pe.2:9, Rev.3:10; pl., Luk.22:28, Act.20:19, Jas.1:2, 1Pe.1:6;
__(b) of trial regarded as leading to sin, temptation: Luk.8:13, 1Co.10:13, 1Ti.6:9; of the temptation of Jesus by the devil, Luk.4:13; εἰσφέρειν (ἔρχεσθαι, εἰσέρχ-) εἰς π., Mat.6:13 26:41, Mrk.14:38, Luk.11:4 22:40, 46;
__(with) of the testing or challenge of God by man (see: πειράζω, 3, with) : Heb.3:8 (LXX: Psa.95:9, where κατα τ. ἡμέραν πειρασμοῦ = מַסָּה the day of Massah).†
SYN.: δοκίμιον  (AS)

πείθω,
[in LXX chiefly for בָּטַח בֶּטַח, its parts and derivatives ;]
__(i) Active;
__1. trans., to apply persuasion ("conative" in pres.; see M, Pr., 147), to prevail upon or win over, persuade: absol., Mat.28:14,  Act.19:26; before περί, with genitive of thing(s), Act.19:8; with accusative of person(s), Act.12:20 14:19 18:4, 2Co.5:11, Gal.1:10; τ. καρδίας ἡμῶν, 1Jn.3:19; with accusative before περί, Act.28:23; with accusative and inf., Act.13:43 26:28 (see Field, Notes, 141 ff.); with accusative before ἵνα (Plut.), Mat.27:20.
__2. Intrans., 2 pf. πέποιθα with Pres. sense (see M, Pr., 147, 154; Bl., § 59, 2): to trust, be confident, have confidence: with accusative and inf., Rom.2:19; with accusative ref. (see Ellic., in l) : Php.1:6, 25; with dative, Php.1:14, Phm 21; ἑαυτῷ, with inf., 2Co.10:7; before ἐν, Php.3:3-4; ἐν κυρίῳ ὅτι, Php.2:24; ἐπί, with dative, Mat.27:43 (WH, mg.), Mrk.10:24 (T, WH, R, mg., om.), Luk.11:22 18:9, 2Co.1:9, Heb.2:13; ἐπί, with accusative, Mat.27:43 (with dative, WH, mg.); id. before ὅτι, 2Co.2:3, 2Th.3:4 (see Lft., Notes, 127); εἰς, with accusative of person(s) before ὅτι, Gal.5:10.
(ii) Pass. and mid.;
__1. to be persuaded, believe (see M, Pr., 158) : absol., Luk.16:31, Act.17:4 21:14, Heb.13:18; with dative, Act.28:24; with accusative and inf., Act.26:26; so also pf., πέπεισμαι, πεπεισμένος εἰμί: with accusative ref. before περί, Heb.6:9; with accusative and inf., Luk.20:6; ὅτι, Rom.8:38, 2Ti.1:5 1:12; id. with ἐν κυρίῳ, Rom.14:14; περί, with genitive before ὅτι, Rom.15:14.
__2. to listen to, obey: with dative of person(s), Act.5:36-37, 40 23:21 27:11, Rom.2:8, Gal.5:7, Heb.13:17, Jas.3:3 (cf. ἀνα-πείθω).†

πέρ
(akin to περί),
enclitic particle, adding force or positiveness to the word which precedes it: indeed, by far, etc. In the NT, it is always affixed to the word to which it relates, see: διόπερ, άἐνπερ, εἴπερ, ἐπείπερ, ἐπειδήπερ, ἤπερ, καθάπερ, καίπερ, ἅσπερ, ὥσπερ
ὥσ-περ

just as, even as: Mat.6:2 20:28, Act.3:17, 1Co.8:5, 1Th.5:3 al.; in protasis, with οὕτως (καί) in apodosis: Mat.12:40, Luk.17:24, Jhn.5:21, Rom.5:19, Gal.4:29, Jas.2:26, al
(AS)

LSJ / STEPBible (TFLSJ)
περ,
enclitic Particle, adding force to the word to which it is added, probably a shortened form of περί (which see) in the sense of

__A
very much, however much.—Chiefly Epic dialect and Lyric poetry; also in Trag. with relats. and parts.:

__1
in [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Homerus Epicus frequently with]] adjective and participle ὤν, ἐπεί μ᾽ ἔτεκές γε μινυνθάδιόν π. ἐόντα all shortlived as I am, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 1.352]]; φίλην π. ἐοῦσαν[Refs [[prev. work] 587; Ἰθάκης κραναῆς π. ἐούσης 3.201: mostly concessive like{καίπερ} (which see), ἀγαθός π. ἐών]] however brave thou art, [Refs [1.131, +others]]; κρατερός π. ἐών [Refs [15.164; κύνεός π. ἐών 9.373]]; δουρικτητήν π. ἐοῦσαν[Refs [[prev. work] 343; μέγαν π. ἐόντα 5.625]]: so in Trag., ἄελπτά π. ὄντα [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Supplices” 55 (Lyric poetry); γενναῖός π. ὤν 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Philoctetes” 1068]]: with a substantive, ἀλόχῳ π. ἐούσῃ [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 1.546; γυνή π. οὖσα 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Septem contra Thebas” 1043]]: with adjective and substantive, λιγύς π. ἐὼν ἀγορητής [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 2.246: with καί]] preceding, καὶ κρατερός π. ἐών [Refs [15.195, etc.: with the]]participle ὤν omitted, φράδμων π. ἀνήρ however shrewd,[Refs [16.638; κρατερός π. 21.63; χερείονά π. 17.539]]; καὶ θεός π. [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Agamemnon” 1203, compare 1084: with parts., ἱεμένων π]]. however eager, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 17.292]]; καὶ ἀχνύμενός π. ἑταίρου grieved though he was for.., [Refs [8.125.]]

__2
intensive, ἐλεεινότερός π. more pitiable by far, [Refs [24.504]]; μίνυνθά π. for a very little, [Refs [1.416, 13.573; ὀλίγον π. 11.391]]; πρῶτόν π. first of all, [Refs [14.295; ὑστάτιόν π. 8.353]]; ὀψέ π. [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “N.” 3.80: to strengthen a negation, οὐδὲ.. π]]. not even, not at all, οὐδ᾽ ὑμῖν ποταμός π. ἐΰρροος ἀρκέσει [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 21.130, compare 8.201, 11.841, 21.410, 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 1.59, 3.236; μή ποτε καὶ σὺ γυναικί π. ἤπιος εἶναι 11.441]]; ἢν μή π. [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 6.57.]]

__3
to give emphasis, ἀλλὰ καὶ αὐτοί π. πονεώμεθα [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 10.70; ἡμεῖς δ᾽ αὐτοί π. φραζώμεθα 17.712; σθένος ἀνέρος ἀμφότεροί π. σχῶμεν 21.308]]: especially at any rate, τιμήν π. μοι ὄφελλεν ἐλλυαλίξαι honour (whatever else) he owed me, [Refs [1.353, compare 2.236, 17.121, 239]]; τόδε π. μοι ἐπικρήηνον ἐέλδωρ [Refs [8.242: in _imperative_ clauses with the _person_ _pronoun_, ἀλλὰ σύ π. μιν τῖσον]] at all events, [Refs [1.508: in the apodosis of a conditional sentence, εἰ δέ τοι Ἀτρεΐδης μὲν ἀπήχθετο.., σὺ δ᾽ ἄλλους π... ἐλέαιρε 9.301, compare 11.796, 12.349.]]

__II
after Conjs. and relative words, with which it commonly coalesces:

__II.1
after hypothetical Conjs., see at {εἴπερ}.

__II.2
after temporal Conjs., ὅτε π. just when, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 4.259, 5.802, etc.; ἦμος.. π. 11.86]]; ὅταν π. [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Coloneus” 301, etc.]]; πρίν π. before even, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 15.588.]]

__II.3
after causal Conjs., see at {ἐπείπερ, ἐπειδήπε; δι᾽ ὅ τι π}. just because, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 4.186.]]

__II.4
after relats., see at {ὅσπερ, οἷός περ, ὅσοσπερ, ἔνθαπερ, ὅθιπερ, οὗπερ, ᾗπερ, ὥσπερ}.

__II.5
after the comparative particle, see at {ἤπερ, ἠέπερ}.

__II.6
after καί, see at {καίπερ}.

__B
περ (B), Aeolic dialect for περί.

Epic dialect πεῖραρ (which see), ᾰτος, τό, end, limit, boundary,

in local sense, ἐκ περάτων γᾶς [Refs 7th c.BC+ [7th-6th c.BC: Alcaeus Lyricus 33.1, compare 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 1.69; π... αὔλ[ε]ιος θύρα ἐλευθέρα γυναικὶ νενόμιστ᾽ οἰκίας 4th-3rd c.BC: Menander Comicus 546]]; τὸ π. tip, τοῦ αἰδοίου [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “de Generatione Animalium” 773a21]]; [τῆς ῥινός] [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd c.AD: Galenus Medicus 18(2).28]]; τισὶ τὰ π. ἀλγέει the extremities, [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd c.AD: Aretaeus Medicus “περὶ αἰτιῶν καὶ σημείων χρονίων παθῶν” 1.7.]]

__II
generally, limit, either opposed to ἀρχή, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Physica” 264b27]], or including it, τελευτή γε καὶ ἀρχὴ π. ἑκάστου [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Parmenides” 137d, compare 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “de Generatione Animalium” 777b29, “Metaphorical” 1022a4; οὐκ ἔχων π. κακῶν 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Andromache” 1216, compare “Or.” 511, 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Persae” 632, 5th c.BC: Lysias Orator 12.88, etc.; π. ἅπασιν ἀνθρώποις ἐστὶ τοῦ βίου θάνατος 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 18.97, compare 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Ethica Nicomachea” 1115a26; εἰ π. μηδὲν ἔσται σφίσι τοῦ ἀπαλλαγῆναι τοῦ κινδύνου 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 7.42]]; π. ἔχειν, ={περαίνεσθαι}, come to an end, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Isocrates Orator 4.5, 4th c.BC: Lycurgus Orator 60, etc.; π. λαμβάνειν 2nd c.BC: Polybius Historicus 5.31.2]]; ἐπιθεῖναι τῇ γενέσει π. [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “de Generatione Animalium” 776a4; ἐν π. εἶναι 4th-3rd c.BC: Theophrastus Philosophus “de Causis Plantarum” 5.18.2.]]

__II.2
perfection of a thing, τὸ π. τῆς μαγειρικῆς.. εὑρηκέναι [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [3rd c.BC: Hegesippus Comicus 1.4, compare 10, 3rd c.BC: Posidippus Comicus 26.17.]]

__II.2.b
Philos., τὸ τῶν ἀγαθῶν π., τὰ π. τῆς ἡδονῆς, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-3rd c.BC: Epicurus Philosophus “Epistulae” 3p.65U., “Sent.” 20; ἐν τῷ κατὰ φύσιν π. κατακέκλειται τἀγαθόν 4th c.AD: Metrodorus Epigrammaticus “Herc.” 831.8.]]

__II.3
end, object, εὐχῆς, ἐλπίδος, [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd c.AD: Lucianus Sophista “Harm.” 2f]]

__II.4
Philos., that which limits or has limits, opposed to τὸ ἄπειρον, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Pythagoras Philosophus cited in 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Metaphysica” 986a23, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Philebus” 30a, etc.; τὰ ἐλάχιστα καὶ ἀμιγῆ π. [τῆς ἀτόμου] 4th-3rd c.BC: Epicurus Philosophus “Epistulae” 1p.17U.: Comedy texts, of a person, τὸν καλούμενον Π. Philostephanus Comicus 1.3.]]

Abbott-Smith / STEPBible (TBESG)
περί,
prep. with genitive, accusative (in cl. also with dative; cf. M, Pr., 105f.),
with radical sense round about (as distinct from ἀμφί, on both sides).
__I. C. genitive,
__1. of place, about (poët.).
__2. Causal, about, on account of, concerning, in reference to: Mat.2:8, Mrk.1:44, Luk.4:38, Jhn.16:26, Act.28:21, al. mult.; τὰ περί, with genitive, the things concerning one, one's state or case: Mrk.5:27, Act.1:3 28:15, Eph.6:22, al.; at the beginning of a sentence, περί, regarding, as to, 1Co.7:1, al.; in the sense on account of (Mat.26:28, 1Co.1:13, al.), often with ὑπέρ as variant (cf. M, Pr., 105).
__II. C. accusative,
__1. of place, about, around: Mat.3:4, Mrk.1:6, Luk.13:8, Act.22:6, al.; οἱ περί, with accusative of person(s), of one's associates, friends, etc., Mrk.4:10, Luk.22:49, Jhn.11:19, Act.13:13; οἱ περὶ τ. τοιαῦτα ἐργάται, Act.19:25; metaphorically, about, as to, concerning: 1Ti.1:19 6:4 2Ti.2:18 3:8, Tit.2:7; τὰ περὶ ἐμέ, Php.2:23; αἱ περὶ τ. λοιπὰ ἐπιθυμίαι, Mrk.4:19.
__2. Of time, in a loose reckoning, about, near: Mat.20:3, 5 6, 9 27:46, Mrk.6:48, Act.10:3, 9 22:6.
__III. In composition: round about (περιβάλλω, περίκειμαι), beyond, over and above (περιποιέω, περιλείπω), to excess (περιεργάζομαι, περισσεύω).
(AS)

περί,
Thess., Delph. περ [Refs 5th c.BC+ [“IG” 9(2).517.17 (3rd c.BC), +others, “Schwyzer” 323 A 4 (5th-4th c.BC)]], also Aeolic dialect, see below [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus]] V; Elean παρ [Refs [[prev. work]413.4]]: preposition with genitive, dative, and accusative:—round about, all round (properly different from ἀμφί, on both sides). (Cogn. with Sanskrit pári 'round about'.)

__A
WITH GENITIVE,

__A.I
of Place, sometimes in Poets, round about, around, τετάνυστο π. σπείους ἡμερίς [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 5.68; τείχη π. Δαρδανίας 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Troades” 818 (Lyric poetry, assuming variant); εἴλυμα π. χροός 3rd c.BC: Apollonius Rhodius Epicus 2.1129: rarely, like{ἀμφί}]], on both sides, see at {περιβαίνω} [Refs [1 near the end]]

__A.I.2
about near, π. σοῦ πάντα γένοιτο ῥόδα [Refs [“IG” 14.2508 (from Nemausus).]]

__A.II
to denote the object about or for which one does something:

__A.II.1
with Verbs of fighting or contending, π. τινός for an object—from the notion of the thing's lying in the middle to be fought about, π. τῶνδε for these prizes, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 23.659; π. πτόλιος.. μαχήσεται 18.265; π. Πατρόκλοιο θανόντος [prev. work] 195, compare 17.120; π. σεῖο 3.137; π. νηὸς ἔχον πόνον 15.416; ἀμύνεσθαι π. πάτρης, π. νηῶν, π. τέκνων, 12.243, 142, 170, etc.]]; δόλους καὶ μῆτιν ὕφαινον, ὥς τε π. ψυχῆς since it was for my life, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 9.423; π. ψυχῆς θέον Ἕκτορος 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 22.161; π. ψυχέων ἐμάχοντο 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 22.245]]; in Prose, τρέχειν π. ἑωυτοῦ, π. τῆς ψυχῆς, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 7.57, 9.37; ἀγῶνας δραμέονται π. σφέων αὐτῶν [prev. author] 8.102; νεναυμάχηκε τὴν π. τῶν κρεῶν 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Ranae” 191; [τὸν] π. τοῦ παντὸς δρόμον θέοντες 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 8.74; κινδυνεύειν π. τινός [prev. passage], etc.; οὐ π. τῶν ἴσων ὁ κίνδυνός ἐστι 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Historia Graeca (Hellenica)” 7.1.7]]; and without a Verb, π. γῆς ὅρων διαφοραί [Refs 8th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 1.122; π. πάντων ἀγαθῶν ὁ ἀγών 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 3.3.44, compare 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Ajax” 936 (Lyric poetry), etc.; μάχη π. τινός 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Theaetetus” 179d; ἐπειγόμενοι π. νίκης 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 23.437, compare 639, 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 8.26; πεῖραν θανάτου π. καὶ ζωᾶς ἀναβάλλεσθαι 5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “N.” 9.29; π. θανάτου φεύγειν 5th c.BC: Antipho Orator 5.95]]; but ἐρίσσαι π. μύθων contend about speaking, i. e. who can speak best, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 15.284; καὶ ἀθανάτοισιν ἐρίζεσκον π. τόξων 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 8.225, compare 24.515.]]

__A.II.2
with words which denote care or anxiety, about, on account of, π. Τρώων.. μερμηρίζειν [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 20.17; ἄχος π. τινός 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 21.249; φόνου π. βουλεύειν 16.234; φροντίζειν π. τινός 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 8.36, etc.; κήδεσθαι π. τ. 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Philoctetes” 621; δεδιέναι π. τ. 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Protagoras” 320a, etc.; ἀπολογεῖσθαι π. τ. 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 2.2.13]]; κρίνειν, διαγιγνώσκειν π. τ., [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “N.” 5.40, 5th c.BC: Antipho Orator 5.96]]; π. τ. ψηφίζεσθαι, διαψηφίζεσθαι, ψῆφον φέρειν, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [“IG” 12.57.42, 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Historia Graeca (Hellenica)” 2.3.50, 4th c.BC: Lycurgus Orator 11; βουλεύεσθαι π. τῆς κοινῆς σωτηρίας 5th-6th c.BC: Isocrates Orator 5.69; π. Μεθωναίων “IG” 12.57.49]]; διανοεῖσθαι, σκοπεῖν π. τινός, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Phaedrus” 270d, “Phd.” 65e; μαντεύεσθαι π. τ. 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 8.36, compare 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Trachiniae” 77]]; π. πότου γοῦν ἐστί σο; so with you it is a question of drink? [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Equites” 87, compare 1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus 2.43b.]]

__A.II.3
with Verbs of hearing, knowing, speaking, etc., about, concerning, π. νόστου ἄκουσα [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 19.270; οἶδα γὰρ εὖ π. κείνου 17.563; π. πομπῆς μνησόμεθα 7.191; π. πατρὸς ἐρέσθαι 1.135, 3.77]]; π. τινὸς ἐρέειν, λέγειν, λόγον ποιήσασθαι, etc., [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.5, 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Tyrannus” 707, 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 1.6.13, etc.; λέγειν καὶ ἀκούειν π. ἑκάστου 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 4.22, etc.; λόγος π. τινός 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Protagoras” 347b, etc.; ἡ π. τινὸς φήμη 4th c.BC: Aeschines Orator 1.48]]; π. τινὸς ἀγγεῖλαι, κηρῦξαι, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Electra” 1111, “Ant.” 193]]; π. τινὸς διελθεῖν, διεξελθεῖν, διηγεῖσθαι, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Isocrates Orator 9.2, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Politicus” 274b, “Euthphr.” 6c, etc.; παίζειν π. τινός 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Memorabilia” 1.3.8; ἐμπειροτέρως ἔχειν π. τινός 4th c.BC: Aeschines Orator 1.82; νόμον γράψαι π. τινός 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Historia Graeca (Hellenica)” 2.3.52, etc.; νόμῳ χρῆσθαι π. τινός 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Antigone” 214.]]

__A.II.4
of impulse or motive rather than object, ἐμαρνάσθην ἔριδος πέρι fought for very enmity, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 7.301, compare 16.476, 20.253.]]

__A.II.5
about, in regard to, μεμηνυμένος π. τινός [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 6.53; οὕτως ἔσχε π. τοῦ πρήγματος τούτου 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.117; τὰ π. τῶν Πλαταιῶν γεγενημένα 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 2.6; τὸ π. τούτου γεγονός 2nd c.BC: Polybius Historicus 1.54.5]]: in Prose frequently without a Verb, ἡ π. τῶν Μαντινικῶν πρᾶξις [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 6.88]]; τὰ π. τινός the circumstances of.., [Refs [[prev. work] 32, 8.14, 26, etc. (compare infr. C. 1.5)]]; οὕτω δὴ καὶ π. τῶν ἀρετῶν (i.e. ἔχει) [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Meno” 72c, compare “R.” 534b, 551c, etc.]]; π. τοῦ καταλειφθῆναι τὸν σῖτον as for reserving the corn, [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [“PMich.Zen.” 28.5 (3rd c.BC): without the _Article_, ἀριθμοῦ πέρι]] as to number, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 7.102]]; χρηστηρίων δὲ πέρι.. [Refs [[prev. author] 2.54.]]

__A.III
before, above, beyond, of superiority, chiefly in Epic dialect, π. πάντων ἔμμεναι ἄλλων [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 1.287; π. δ᾽ ἄλλων φασὶ γενέσθαι 4.375; τετιμῆσθαι π. πάντων 9.38; ὃν π. πάσης τῖεν ὁμηλικίης 5.325; ὃν.. π. πάντων φίλατο παίδων 20.304; π. πάντων ἴδριες ἀνδρῶν 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 7.108; κρατερὸς π. πάντων 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 21.566, compare 1.417, 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 11.216: in this sense frequently divided from its _genitive_, π. φρένας ἔμμεναι ἄλλων]] in understanding to be beyond them, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 17.171, compare 1.258, 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 1.66; π. μὲν εἶδος, π. δ᾽ ἔργα τέτυκτο τῶν ἄλλων Δαναῶν 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 17.279; π. μὲν κρατέεις, π. δ᾽ αἴσυλα ῥέζεις ἀνδρῶν 21.214; π. δ᾽ ἔγχει Ἀχαιῶν φέρτατός ἐσσι 7.289, compare 5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “O.” 6.50, 3rd c.BC: Theocritus Poeta Bucolicus 25.119.]] —In this sense π. is sometimes adverbial, and the genitive is absent, see below [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus II.]]

__A.IV
in [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus and _Attic dialect_ Prose, to denote value, ἡμῖν π. πολλοῦ ἐστι]] it is of much consequence, worth much, to us, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1. 120, compare 5th c.BC: Antipho Orator 6.3]]; π. πολλοῦ ποιεῖσθαί τινας to reckon them for, i.e. worth, much, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.73, 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Memorabilia” 2.3.10, etc.]]; π. πλείονος, π. πλείστου ποιεῖσθαι, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. author] “An.” 7.7.44, “Cyr.” 7.5.60; π. πλείστου ἡγεῖσθαι 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 2.89; π. παντὸς ποιεῖσθαι 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 1.4.1]]; π. ἐλάττονος ἡγούμενοι, π. οὐδενὸς ἡγήσασθαι, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Lysias Orator 2.71, 31.31.]]

__A.V
Aeolic dialect περί and περ ={ὑπέρ, στροῦθοι περὶ γᾶς.. δίννεντες πτέρα} [Refs 7th c.BC+ [7th-6th c.BC: Sappho Lyrica 1.10]]; περ κεφάλας probably in [Refs 7th c.BC+ [7th-6th c.BC: Alcaeus Lyricus 93, compare 18; περρ ἁπαλῶ στύματός σε πεδέρχομαι 3rd c.BC: Theocritus Poeta Bucolicus 29.25]]; also Hellenistic, ὃ διέγραψε Προῖτος περί μου paid on my behalf, PCair. Zen.[Refs 3rd c.BC+ [790.23 (3rd c.BC),compare “UPZ” 57.12 (2nd c.BC).]]

__B
WITH DATIVE (in Attic dialect Prose mostly in signification [Refs 5th c.BC+ [11, especially in 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus),]]

__B.I
of Place, round about, around, of close-fitting dresses, armour, etc., ἔνδυνε π. στήθεσσι χιτῶνα [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 10.21; χιτῶνα π. χροῒ δῦνεν 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 15.60; δύσετο τεύχεα καλὰ π. χροΐ 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 13.241; ἕσσαντο π. χροῒ χαλκόν 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 24.467; κνημῖδας.. π. κνήμῃσιν ἔθηκε 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 11.17; βεβλήκει τελαμῶνα π. στήθεσσι 12.401: in Prose, π. τῇσι κεφαλῇσι εἶχον τιάρας 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 7.61; θώρακα π. τοῖς στέρνοις ἔχειν 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 1.2.13]]; οἱ στρεπτοὶ οἱ π. τῇ δέρῃ καὶ τὰ ψέλια π. ταῖς χερσί[Refs 8th c.BC+ [[prev. work] 1.3.2.; π. τῇ χειρὶ δακτύλιον ὄντα 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 359e, etc.; χαλκὸς ἔλαμπε π. στήθεσσι 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 13.245; χιτῶνα π. στήθεσσι δαΐξαι 2.416; πήληξ.. κονάβησε π. κροτάφοισι 15.648]]; in other relations, π. δ᾽ ἔγχεϊ χεῖρα καμεῖται will grow weary by grasping the spear,[Refs [2.389; δράκων ἑλισσόμενος π. χειῇ 22.95; κνίση ἑλισσομένη π. καπνῷ 1.317; π. σταχύεσσιν ἐέρση 23.598; μάρναντο π. Σκαιῇσι πύλῃσιν 18.453]]: rarely in Trag., π. βρέτει πλεχθείς [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Eumenides” 259 (Lyric poetry); κεῖται νεκρὸς π. νεκρῷ 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Antigone” 1240.]]

__B.I.2
in Poets, also, around a weapon, i. e. spitted upon it, transfixed by it, π. δουρὶ πεπαρμένη [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 21.577; ἐρεικόμενος π. δουρί 13.441; κυλινδόμενος π. χαλκῷ 8.86; π. δουρὶ ἤσπαιρε 13.570; πεπτῶτα π. ξίφει 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Ajax” 828; αἷμα ἐρωήσει π. δουρί 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 1.303.]]

Πατρόκλῳ.. βεβήκει [prev. work] 137, compare 355; π. σκύμνοισι βεβηκώς 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Equites” 1039.]]

__B.II
of an object for or about which one struggles (compare above [Refs 8th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus 11.1), π. οἷσι μαχειόμενος κτεάτεσσι 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 17.471; μαχήσασθαι π. δαιτί 2.245; π. παιδὶ μάχης πόνος 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 16.568; ἄνδρα π. ᾗ πατρίδι μαρνάμενον 7th c.BC: Tyrtaeus Elegiacus 10.2; π. τοῖς φιλτάτοις κυβεύειν 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Protagoras” 314a; π. τῇ Σικελίᾳ ἔσται ὁ ἀγών 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 6.34 codices; κινδυνεύειν π. αὑτῷ 5th c.BC: Antipho Orator 5.6.]]

__B.II.2
with Verbs denoting care, anxiety, or the opposite (compare above [Refs 8th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus 11.2), π. γὰρ δίε ποιμένι λαῶν, μή τι πάθοι 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 5.566; ἔδεισεν δὲ π. ξανθῷ Μενελάῳ 10.240, compare 11.557; δεδιότες π. τῷ χωρίῳ 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 1.60, compare 74, 119, 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Equites” 27; θαρρεῖν π. τῇ ἑαυτοῦ ψυχῇ 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Phaedo” 114d, compare “Tht.” 148c; π. πλέγματι γαθεῖ 3rd c.BC: Theocritus Poeta Bucolicus 1.54.]]

__B.II.3
generally, of the cause or occasion, on account of, by reason of, ἀτύζεσθαι π. καπνῷ, variant for{ὑπὸ καπνοῦ} in [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 8.183; μὴ π. __C
WITH ACCUSATIVE,

__C.I
of Place, properly of the object round about which motion takes place, π. βόθρον ἐφοίτων came flocking round the pit, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 11.42; π. νεκρὸν ἤλασαν ἵππους 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 23.13; π. τέρματα ἵπποι τρωχῶσι 22.162; ἄστυ πέρι.. διώκειν [prev. work] 173, 230]]; ἐρύσας π. σῆμα [Refs 8th c.BC+ [24.16, compare 51, etc.; π. φρένας ἤλυθ᾽ ἰωή 10.139; π. φρένας ἤλυθε οἶνος 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 9.362]]: also of extension round, ἑστάμεναι π. τοῖχον, π. βωμόν, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 18.374, 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 13.187, etc.; λέξασθαι π. ἄστυ 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 8.519; μάρνασθαι π. ἄ. 6.256, etc.; φυλάσσοντας π. μῆλα 12.303; οἳ π. Πηνειὸν.. ναίεσκον, π. Δωδώνην.. οἰκί᾽ ἔθεντο, 2.757, 750; σειρήν κεν π. ῥίον Οὐλύμποιο δησαίμην 8.25, compare 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 18.67: in Prose, ἰκριῶσαι π. τὼ ἀγάλματε “IG” 12.371.22; φυλακὰς δεῖ π. τὸ στρατόπεδον εἶναι 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 5.1.9]]; π. τὴν κρήνην εὕδειν somewhere near it, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Phaedrus” 259a, compare 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 1.2.9; εἶναι π. τὸν λαγώ [prev. author] “Cyn.” 4.4]]; π. λίθον πεσών upon it, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Acharnenses” 1180]]; π. αὑτὰ καταρρεῖν collapse upon themselves, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 2.10; ταραχθεῖσαι [αἱ νῆες] π. ἀλλήλας 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 7.23]]; πλεῦνες π. ἕνα many to one, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 7.103]]; π. τὸν ἄρξαντα.. τὸ ἀδίκημά ἐστι is imputable to him who.., [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Antipho Orator 4.4.2: frequently with a]] substantive only, ἡ π.
