__C.I.2
of persons who are about one, ἔχειν τινὰ π. αὑτόν [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Historia Graeca (Hellenica)” 5.3.22]]; especially οἱ π. τινά a person's attendants, connexions, associates, or colleagues, οἱ π. τὸν Πείσανδρον πρέσβεις [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 8.63]]; οἱ π. Ἡράκλειτον his school, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Cratylus” 440c, compare 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 1.5.8, etc.]]; οἱ π. Ἀρχίαν πολέμαρχοι Archias and his colleagues, [Refs [[prev. author] “HG” 5.4.2, compare “An.” 2.4.2, etc.]]; οἱ π. τινά so-and-so and his family, [Refs 2nd c.BC+ [PGrenf. 1.21.16 (2nd c.BC), etc.]]; later οἱ π. τινά, periphrastic for the person himself, οἱ π. Φαβρίκιον Fabricius, [Refs 1st c.AD+ [1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus “Pyrrhus” 20, compare “Tim.” 13, “IGRom.” 3.883.14 (Tarsus, 2nd-3rd c.AD)]]; compare ἀμφί C. 1.3.

__C.I.3
of the object about which one is occupied or concerned, π. δόρπα πονεῖσθαι, π. δεῖπνον πένεσθαι, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 24.444, 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 4.624 (but π. τεύχε᾽ ἕπουσι, tmesis for περιέπουσι, 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 15.555)]]; later mostly εἶναι π. τι, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 7.31, 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Historia Graeca (Hellenica)” 2.2.4; γενέσθαι 5th-6th c.BC: Isocrates Orator 3.12]]; π. γυναῖκας γενέσθαι Vett.[Refs 5th c.BC+ [Val. 17.20; ὄντων ἡμῶν π. ταύτην τὴν πραγματείαν 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 48.6; διατρῖψαι π. τὴν θήραν 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 1.2.11, etc.: less frequently ἔχειν π. τινάς [prev. author] “HG” 7.4.28, 2nd c.AD: Galenus Medicus 15.442]]; in periphrastic phrases, οἱ π. τὴν ποίησιν καὶ τοὺς λόγους ὄντες poets and orators, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Isocrates Orator 12.35; οἱ π. τὴν φιλοσοφίαν ὄντες [prev. author] 9.8; οἱ π. τὴν μουσικήν [prev. work]4; οἱ π. τὰς τελετάς]] ministers of the mysteries, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Phaedo” 69c]]; ὁ π. τὸν ἵππον the groom, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “de Equitandi ratione” 6.3; compare ἀμφί C. 1.6.]]

__C.I.4
round or about a place, and so in, π. νῆσον ἀλώμενοι [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 4.368, compare 90; ἐμέμηκον π. σηκούς 9.439]]; ἃν π. ψυχὰν γάθησεν in his heart, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “P.” 4.122; χρονίζειν π. Αἴγυπτον 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 3.61, compare 7.131; εὕροι ἄν τις [βασιλείας] π. τοὺς βαρβάρους 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 544d, etc.]]; οἱ π. Φωκίδα τόποι [Refs 2nd c.BC+ [2nd c.BC: Polybius Historicus 5.24.12, etc.]]

__C.I.5
about, in the case of, τὰ π. τὴν Αἴγυπτον γεγονότα, τὰ π. Μίλητον γενόμενα, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 3.13, 6.26; εὐσεβεῖν π. θεούς 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Symposium” 193a; ἀσεβεῖν π. ξένους 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 5.2.10; ἁμαρτάνειν π. τινάς [prev. author] “An.” 3.2.20; ἀνήρ ἐστιν ἀγαθὸς π. τὸν δῆμον τὸν Ἀθηναίων “IG” 12.59.10; ἄνδρ᾽ ἀγαθὸν ὄντα Μαραθῶνι π. τὴν πόλιν 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Acharnenses” 696; τοιαύτην γνώμην ἔχειν π. τὸν πατέρα 5th c.BC: Lysias Orator 10.21; οὐδεμία συμφορὴ.. ἔσται.. π. οἶκον τὸν σόν 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 8.102]]; ποιέειν or πράττειν τι π. τινά, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. author] 1.158, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Gorgias” 507a; τὰ π. Πρηξάσπεα πρηχθέντα 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 3.76; καινοτομεῖν π. τὰ θεῖα 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Euthyphro” 3b; π. θεοὺς μὴ σωφρονεῖν 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Memorabilia” 1.1.20]]; σπουδάζειν π. τινά promote his cause, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Isocrates Orator 1.10]]: without a Verb, αἱ π. τοὺς παῖδας συμφοραί [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 7.2.20; ἡ π. αὑτὸν ἐπιμέλεια 5th-6th c.BC: Isocrates Orator 9.2; ἡ π. ἡμᾶς ἡνιόχησις 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Phaedrus” 246b]]: generally, of all relations, about, concerning, in respect of, π. μὲν τοὺς ἰχθύας οὕτως ἔχει [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 2.93, compare 8.86; πονηρὸν π. τὸ σῶμα 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Protagoras” 313d; ἀκόλαστος π. ταῦτα 4th c.BC: Aeschines Orator 1.42; γελοῖος π. τὰς διατριβάς [prev. work]126; ξυνηνέχθη θόρυβος π. τὸν Ἀστύοχον 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 8.84]]; as to [Refs 5th c.BC+ [compare (4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus 11.5), π. τὸ παρὸν πάθος 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Theaetetus” 179c, compare “Phd.” 65a: frequently in place of an]] adjective, ὄργανα ὅσα π. γεωργίαν, i.e. γεωργικά[Refs [, [prev. author] “R.” 370d; οἱ νόμοι οἱ π. τοὺς γάμους [prev. author] “Cri.” 50d; αἱ π. τὰ μαθήματα ἡδοναί [prev. author] “Phlb.” 51e]]; also in place of a genitive, οἱ π. Αυσίαν λόγοι the speeches of L., [Refs [[prev. author] “Phdr.” 279a]]; ἡ π. Φίλιππον τυραννίς the despotism of P., [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Historia Graeca (Hellenica)” 5.4.2; ἀκρασίας τῆς π. τὸν θυμόν 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Ethica Nicomachea” 1149b19]]: in Prose, to denote circumstances connected with any person or thing, τὰ π. Κῦρον, τὰ π. Ἑλένην, τὰ π. Βάττον, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.95, 2.113, 4.154]]; τὰ π. τὸν Ἄθων the works at Mount Athos, [Refs [[prev. author] 7.37]]; τὰ π. τὰς ναῦς naval affairs, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 1.13]]; τὰ π. τὴν ναυμαχίαν (variant for{τῆς ναυμαχίας}) the events of.., [Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. author] 8.63; τὰ π. τὸν πόλεμον 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 468a; τὰ π. τὸ σῶμα [prev. author] “Phdr.” 246d; τὰ π. τοὺς θεούς 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 8.1.23, etc.; compare ἀμφί with 1.4.]]

__C.II
of Time, π. λύχνων ἁφάς about the time of lamp-lighting, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 7.215]]; π. μέσας νύκτας about midnight, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 1.7.1; π. πλήθουσαν ἀγοράν [prev. work] 2.1.7]]; π. ἡλίου δυσμάς[Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. work] 6.5.32; π. τούτους τοὺς χρόνους 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 3.89, etc.]]

__C.II.2
of round numbers, π. ἑβδομήκοντα about seventy, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. author] 1.54; π. ἑπτακοσίους 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Historia Graeca (Hellenica)” 2.4.5, etc.]]

__D
Position: π. may follow its substantive, when it suffers anastrophe, ἄστυ πέρι [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 22.173; ἔριδος πέρι 16.476: most frequently with _genitive_, τοῦδε πράγματος πέρι 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Eumenides” 630; τῶνδε βουλεύειν πέρι [prev. author] “Th.” 248, etc. (5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus]] only once uses it before its genitive, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [“Aj.” 150 (_anapaest meter_)): in Prose, σφέων αὐτῶν πέρι 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 8.36; σοφίας πέρι 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Philebus” 49a; δικαίων τε πέρι καὶ ἀδίκων [prev. author] “Grg.” 455a, etc.; γραμμάτων εἴπομεν ὡς οὐχ ἱκανῶς ἔχεις πέρι [prev. author] “Lg.” 809e, compare “Ap.” 19c.]]

__E
περί absolutely, as adverb., around, about, also, near, by, frequently in [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Homerus Epicus, γέλασσε δὲ πᾶσα π. χθών 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 19.362, +others: strengthened, περί τ᾽ ἀμφί τε κάλλος ἄητο]]round about, [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [Hymnus in Cererem 276, compare 3rd c.BC: Callimachus Epicus “Hecale” 1.1.13.]]

__E.II
before or above others [Refs 4th c.BC+ [compare (4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus 111)]], exceedingly, only Epic dialect, in which case it commonly suffers anastrophe, Τυδεΐδη, πέρι μέν σε τίον Δαναοί [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 8.161, compare 9.53]]; σε χρὴ πέρι μὲν φάσθαι ἔπος ἠδ᾽ ἐπακοῦσαι[Refs 8th c.BC+ [[prev. work] 100; τοι πέρι δῶκε θεὸς πολεμήϊα ἔργα 13.727; ἅ οἱ πέρι δῶκεν Ἀθήνη 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 2.116, compare 7.110; πέρι γάρ μιν ὀϊζυρὸν τέκε μήτηρ 3.95; πέρι κέρδεα οἶδεν 2.88; τὸν πέρι Μοῦσ᾽ ἐφίλησεν 8.63.]]

__E.II.2
π. does not suffer anastrophe in the Epic dialect phrase π. κῆρι right heartily, π. κῆρι φίλησε [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 13.430, etc. (κῆρι φιλεῖν alone, 9.117); ἀπέχθωνται π. κῆρι 4.53]]; π. κῆρι τιέσκετο[Refs 8th c.BC+ [[prev. work] 46, compare 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 5.36, 7.69; π. κῆρι.. ἐχολώθη 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 13.206; also π. φρεσὶν ἄσπετος ἀλκή 16.157; π. φρεσὶν αἴσιμα ᾔδη 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 14.433; ἀλύσσοντες π. θυμῷ 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 22.70, compare 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 14.146; π. σθένεϊ 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 17.22.]]

__E.II.3
for περὶ πρό, see at {περιπρό}.

__E.II.4
περὶ κάτω bottom upwards, δῖνος π. κάτω τετραμμένος [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Strattis Comicus 34, compare 9th c.AD: Photius Legal icographus, etc.; τὴν κόγχην στρέψας π. τὰ κάτω 2nd-3rd c.AD: Aelianus “De Natura Animalium - Ar.Byzantine Epit.” 9.34.]]

__F
IN COMPOSITION (joined with other words), all its chief senses recur, especially

__F.I
extension in all directions as from a centre, all round, as in περιβάλλω, περιβλέπω, περιέχω.

__F.II
completion of an orbit and return to the same point, about, as in περιάγω, περιβαίνω, περίειμι (εἶμι ibo), περιέρχομαι, περιστρέφω.

__F.III
a going over or beyond, above, before, as in περιβαίνω III, περιβάλλω see, περιγίγνομαι, περιεργάζομαι, περιτοξεύω.

__F.IV
generally, a strengthening of the simple notion, beyond measure, very, exceedingly, as in περικαλλής, περίκηλος, περιδείδω, like Latin per-.

__F.V
the notion of double-ness which belongs to ἀμφί is found in only one poetic compound, περιδέξιος (which see).

__G
PROSODY: περί never suffers elision in [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” or 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” (περ᾽ ἰγνύσι “hymnus ad Mercurium” 152); once in 8th-7th c.BC: Hesiodus Epicus, περίαχε “Th.” 678 (compare 4th c.AD(?): Quintus Smyrnaeus Epicus 3.601, 11.382), see.{ἰάχω}]] near the end; περ᾽ ἰγνύῃσι [Refs 5th c.BC+ [3rd c.BC: Theocritus Poeta Bucolicus 25.242; περ᾽ Ἠδάλιον “Inscription Cyprian dialect” 135.27 H.; also in 5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus, περάπτων “P.” 3.52; περόδοις “N.” 11.40; περιδαῖος “fragment” 154; περ᾽ αὐτᾶς “P.” 4.265; ταύτας περ᾽ ἀτλάτου πάθας “O.” 6.38: not in Trag. (περεβάλοντο, περεσκήνωσεν are ff. lines in 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Agamemnon” 1147, “Eu.” 634)]]; in Comedy texts and codices of Prose writers only in participle of περίειμι (εἶμι ibo) (which see):—π. stands before a word beginning with a vowel in Comedy texts, περὶ Ἀθηνῶν, περὶ ἐμοῦ, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Equites” 1005]] {περιαγαπάζομαι}:—Aeolic dialect περρ for the sake of meter, see [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus 5.]]

περιάγω [ᾰ],
future -άξω [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-3rd c.BC: Menander Comicus 532.13, etc.]]:— lead or draw round, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.30, +others; τὰ φορτία ἐν βάρισι περὶ τὸ Δέλτα [prev. author] 2.179; π. τινὰς ἐν ἁμάξῃσι κειμένους [prev. author] 4.73: with _accusative_ loci, περιάγουσι τὴν λίμνην κύκλῳ (i.e. τὴν παρθένον) [prev. work] 180 (assuming variant),compare 4th-3rd c.BC: Menander Comicus]] [same place]; carry about for sale, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Protagoras” 313d]]:—middle, lead round with one, ἐλέφαντα [Refs 2nd c.BC+ [2nd c.BC: Epinicus Comicus 2.4.]]

__b
cause to revolve, ψυχὴ π. πάντα [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Leges” 898d, compare 3rd c.AD: Plotinus Philosophus 5.1.2]]:—passive, rotate, οἷον τροχοῦ περιαγομένου [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Timaeus” 79b.]]

__2
lead about with one, have always by one, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 2.2.28, compare 1.3.3]]:—more frequently in middle, ἀκολούθους πολλοὺς περιάγεσθαι [Refs 4th c.BC+ [[prev. author] “Mem.” 1.7.2, compare 4th c.BC: Theopompus Historicus 89 (a), 2nd-1st c.BC: Posidonius Historicus 7 1st c.AD: Josephus Historicus, etc.]]

__2.b
metaphorically, lead round and round, perplex, τὼ θεώ με περιάγουσιν, ὥστε.. [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Andocides Orator 1.113 (assuming variant), compare 2nd c.AD: Lucianus Sophista “Nigr.” 8]]:—passive, περιαγόμενος τῷ λόγῳ [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Laches” 187e.]]

__3
turn round, turn about, τὴν κεφαλήν, τὸν τράχηλον, τὸν αὐχένα, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Pax” 682, “Av.” 176, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 515c, compare 5th c.BC: Hippocrates Medicus “περὶ ἄρθρων ἐμβολῆς” 18; τινὰ πρὸς τἀριστερά 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Cyclops” 686 (assuming variant); μύλην 2nd c.AD(?): Pollianus Epigrammaticus 7.180]]; π. τὴν σκυταλίδα twist it round in order to tighten a noose, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 4.60]]; τὼ χεῖρε περιαγαγὼν εἰς τοὔπισθεν καὶ δήσας twisting back the hands behind the back, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Lysias Orator 1.25; simply π. τὼ χεῖρε 1st c.BC: Dionysius Halicarnassensis 6.82]]:—passive, περιαχθεὶς τὼ χεῖρε [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd-3rd c.AD: Philostratus Sophista “Heroicus” 10.7]]; so probably περιαχθείς alone, π. κρεμήσεται [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [“PCair.Zen.” 202.9 (3rd c.BC).]]

__4
pass round, τὸ περιαγόμενον ποτήριον [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd c.AD: Athenaeus Epigrammaticus 10.420a, etc., compare 3rd c.AD: Heliodorus Scriptor Eroticus 3.11.]]

__5

__III.2
hold fast by, cling to, with genitive, γούνων περισχομένη [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [3rd c.BC: Apollonius Rhodius Epicus 4.82 (but with _accusative_, περίσχετο γούνατα χερσίν [prev. author] 3.706); περιίσχετο κούρης 2nd c.BC: Moschus Bucolicus 2.11]]: hence, cleave to, be fond of a person or thing, γενσάμενοι τῶν ἡμετέρων ἀγαθῶν περιέξονται [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.71, compare 3.53, 5.40, 7.39, 160, etc.]]; τὠυτοῦ περιεχόμεθα we are compassing, aiming at the same end, [Refs 1st c.AD+ [[prev. author] 3.72, compare 1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus “Themistocles” 9]]; κρίσιν.. ἧς μᾶλλον περιέχομαι on which I place more reliance, [Refs 4th c.AD+ [4th c.AD: Alciphro Epistolographus 2.4.]]

__III.3
rarely with infinitive, περιείχετο.. μένοντας μὴ ἐκλιπεῖν τὴν τάξιν clung to his resolution that they should stay and not leave their post, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 9.57.]]

__IV
Aeolic dialect περρέχω, ={ὑπερέχω}, ὁπόσον τῷ ποδὶ περρέχει τᾶς γᾶς, τοῦτο χάρις, i.e. every inch of his stature is grace, [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [3rd c.BC: Theocritus Poeta Bucolicus 30.3.]]

LSJ / STEPBible (TFLSJ)
περιίστημι,.
in the transitive tenses (with perfect περιέστᾰκα [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Axiochus” 370d)]], place round, π. τοὺς ἑαυτοῦ [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 8.108, etc.; π. στήλην τινί 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 3.24; π. κύτος τῷ ζῴῳ 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Timaeus” 78c; στράτευμα περὶ πόλιν 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 7.5.1: _metaphorically_, π. τινὶ ἔτι πλείω κακά 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 21.123; κινδύνους τοῖς Καρχηδονίοις 2nd c.BC: Polybius Historicus 12.15.7; π. ἀγῶνάς τισι 1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus “Comp. Ag.Gracch.” 5.]]

__2
bring round, ὁ δῆμος εἰς ἑαυτὸν περιέστησε τὴν πολιτείαν [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Politica” 1304a33; εἰς τοὐναντίον π. τινὰ τῷ λόγῳ 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Ax.” l]].with; εἰς τοσοῦτον π. τινά, ὥστε.. [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Heraclides Ponticus Historicus cited in 2nd c.AD: Athenaeus Epigrammaticus 12.537c]]; especially into a worse state, εἰς τοῦθ᾽ ἡ τύχη τὰ πράγματα αὐτῶν περιέστησεν ὥστε.. [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Isocrates Orator 6.47, compare 4th c.BC: Aeschines Orator 3.82; π. εἰς μοναρχίαν τὴν πολιτείαν 2nd c.BC: Polybius Historicus 3.8.2]]; οἴκους εἰς πενίαν π. [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd c.AD: Herodianus Grammaticus 7.3.5]]; convert, εἰς τὸ περιφερὲς [τὸν ἀέρα] [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-3rd c.BC: Epicurus Philosophus “Epistulae” 2p.51U.]]; transfer, π. τὰς ἑαυτοῦ συμφορὰς εἴς τινα [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 40.20; π. τὴν αἰτίαν εἴς τινα 1st c.BC: Dionysius Halicarnassensis 3.3.]]

__II
in aorist 1 middle, place round oneself, ξυστοφόρων κύκλον [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 7.5.41; φρουρὰν περὶ τὸ σῶμα 2nd c.AD: Appianus Historicus “Bella Civilia” 3.4.]]

__B
passive and middle, with aorist 2 (aorist 1, see.below [Refs [2),]]perfect, and pluperfect active:—stand round about, περίστησαν γὰρ ἑταῖροι [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 4.532]]; κῦμα περιστάθη a wave rose around (Epic dialect aorist passive), [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 11.243; περιστῆναι περί τι 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Timaeus” 84e; τοῦ περιεστῶτος ἔξωθεν πνεύματος [prev. work] 76b]]; οἱ περιεστῶτες the bystanders, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Antipho Orator 6.14; ὄχλου πολλοῦ περιστάντος “IG” 42(1).123.25 (Epid.).]]

__B.2
with accusative objecti, encircle, surround, χορὸν περιίσταθ᾽ ὅμιλος [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 18.603]]; βοῦν δὲ περιστήσαντο (perhaps περίστησάν τε)[Refs 8th c.BC+ [2.410, compare 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 12.356]]; μή πώς με περιστήωσ᾽ ἕνα πολλοί (Epic dialect 3rd.pers. plural subjunctive aorist 2 for -στῶσι) that their numbers surround me not, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 17.95, compare 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 20.50; so περιστάντες [τὸ θηρίον] κύκλῳ 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.43, compare 9.5, 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Fragmenta - American Journal of Philology” 379, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 432b; π. τὸν λόφον τῷ στρατεύματι 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 3.1.5: _metaphorically_, τὸ περιεστὸς ἡμᾶς δεινόν 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 4.10, compare 7.70; τοσούτου πολέμου τὴν Ἀσίαν περιστάντος 5th-6th c.BC: Isocrates Orator 4.162; χωρὶς τῆς περιστάσης ἂν ἡμᾶς αἰσχύνης 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 3.8; διὰ τὸν φόβον τὸν περιστάντα αὐτούς 4th c.BC: Aeschines Orator 3.137; φόβος π. τινά 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 3.54, compare 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 18.195.]]

__B.3
with dative, περιισταμένους τῇ κλίνῃ [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Leges” 947b]]: mostly metaphorically, come round to one, ἡμῖν.. ἀδοξία τὸ πλέον ἢ ἔπαινος περιέστη [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 1.76; τῇ [Ἑλλάδι] δουλεία περιέστηκε 5th c.BC: Lysias Orator 2.60; τοῦ πολέμου περιεστηκότος Θηβαίοις 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 16.28; πηλίκα τῇ πόλει περιέστηκε πράγματα [prev. author] 19.340]]; ἀνάγκη π. τινί, with infinitive, [Refs [[prev. work]212: _absolutely_, of]]circumstances, mostly bad, τὰ περιεστηκότα πράγματα [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Lysias Orator 2.32, compare 4th-3rd c.BC: Epicurus Philosophus “Sententiae” 38; οἱ περιεστῶτες καιροί 2nd c.BC: Polybius Historicus 3.86.7.]]

__B.II
come round, revolve, κύκλῳ [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Physica” 217a19]]; of winds, ἐκ τῶν ἀπαρκτίων εἰς θρασκίας [Refs [[prev. author] “Mete.” 365a6]]; of Time, περιισταμένης τῆς ὥρας [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th-3rd c.BC: Theophrastus Philosophus “de Causis Plantarum” 2.11.2, compare 5th c.BC: Hippocrates Medicus “περὶ φύσιος ἀνθρώπου” 7.]]

__B.II.2
come round to, devolve upon, περιειστήκει ὑποψία ἐς τὸν Ἀλκιβιάδην [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 6.61; νομίσαντες τὸ παρανόμημα ἐς τοὺς Αθηναίους τὸ αὐτὸ περιεστάναι [prev. author] 7.18]]; εἰς ὀλίγους ἡμᾶς περιέστη [ἡ στατίων] [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [“IG” 14.830.8 (Puteoli, 2nd c.AD).]]

__B.II.3
of events, come round, turn out, especially for the worse, ἐξ ἀρρωστίης π. τινὶ ἐς ὕδερον [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Hippocrates Medicus “Κωακαὶ προγνώσιες” 471 (but also of persons, ἐς ὕδρωπα περιίσταντο]] became dropsical, [Refs [[prev. author] “Epid.” 3.13)]]; ἐς τοῦτο περιέστη ἡ τύχη fortune was so completely reversed, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 4.12]]; τοὐναντίον περιέστη αὐτῷ it turned out quite contrary for him, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. author] 6.24, compare 5th c.BC: Lysias Orator 12.64, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Meno” 70c; ὁ τοῦ δικαίου λόγος εἰς τοὐναντίον περιειστήκει [prev. author] “R.” 343a]]; φιλεῖ ἐς τύχας τὰ πολλὰ περιίστασθαι come to be dependent on chances, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 1.78; εἰ τὰ μὲν πράγματ᾽ εἰς ὅπερ νυνὶ περιέστη 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 18.201, compare 3.9; τὸ πρᾶγμ᾽ εἰς ὑπέρδεινόν μοι περιέστη [prev. author] 21.111, compare 37.10]]; ἐνταῦθα τὰ πράγματα π. ὥστε.. [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Isocrates Orator 8.59, compare 5.55]]; περιέστηκεν εἰς τοῦτο ὥστε.. [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Lycurgus Orator 3]]: with infinitive, περιειστήκει τοῖς βοηθείας δεήσεσθαι δοκοῦσιν αὐτοὺς βοηθεῖν ἑτέροις [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 18.218, compare 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Menexenus” 244d]]: with participle, περιέστηκεν ἡ πρότερον σωφροσύνη νῦν ἀβουλία φαινομένη [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 1.32.]]

__B.III
later, go round so as to avoid, shun, τὰς ἁμαρτίας [Refs 5th c.BC+ [1st c.BC: Philodemus Gadarensis Epigrammaticus “Rh.” 1.384 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus; τὴν ὁμιλίαν 1st c.AD: Josephus Historicus “Antiquitates Judaicae” 1.1.4; κύνας 2nd c.AD: Lucianus Sophista “Herm.” 86]] (though he censures this usage, [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [“Sol.” 5), compare 2nd c.AD: Galenus Medicus “de Usu Partium” 10.14, 3rd c.AD: Porphyrius Tyrius Philosophus “de Abstinentia - Porphyrii Opuscula” 4.7, etc.; τὸν κίνδυνον 4th c.AD: Iamblichus Philosophus “de vita Pythagorica” 33.239]]; τὸ μοναρχικόν[NT+2nd c.AD+ [[prev. work] 31.189; τὴν ἀφροσύνην 2nd c.AD: Sextus Empiricus Philosophus “adversus Mathematicos” 11.93; κενοφωνίας NT.2Tim.2.16; τὸ εἰκῇ καὶ μάτην 2nd c.AD: Marcus Antoninus Imperator 3.4; τοὺς ἡγουμένους 2nd c.AD: Artemidorus Daldianus Onirocriticus 4.59]]; π. μὴ.. to be afraid lest.., [Refs 1st c.AD+ [1st c.AD: Josephus Historicus “Antiquitates Judaicae” 4.6.12]]; sneak round, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [1st c.BC: Philodemus Gadarensis Epigrammaticus “Rh.” 1.99 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus]]; circumvent, τοὺς λογιστάς Mitteis [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [“Chr.” 88iv 11 (2nd c.AD)]]:—so in passive, περιεσταμένης τῆς λογοθεσίας [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [“BGU” 1019.8 (2nd c.AD).]]

περισσεύω
(περισσός), [in LXX: 1Ki.2:33 (מַרְבִּית), 1Ki.2:36 Ecc.3:19 (יָתַר ni., יוׄתֵר), Tob.4:16, Sir.10:27 11:12 19:24, Sir 30:38 (Sir.33:29), 1Ma.3:30 * ;]
__I. Prop., intrans.,
__1. of things, to be over and above the number (Hes.), hence,
__(a) to be or remain over: Mat.14:20 15:37, Luk.9:17, Jhn.6:12-13;
__(b) to abound, be in abundance: Mrk.12:44, Luk.12:15 21:4, Act.16:5, Rom.3:7 5:15, 2Co.1:5 8:2 9:12, Php.1:26.
__2. Of persons,
__(a) to abound in, have in abundance: 1Co.14:12 15:58, Php.4:12, 18; with genitive, Luk.15:17 T;
__(b) to be superior or better, to excel: absol., 1Co.3:9 8:8; with dative ref., 2Co.3:9; before ἐν, Rom.15:13, 1Co.15:58, 2Co.3:9 8:7, Col.2:7; μᾶλλον, 1Th.4:1 4:10; μ καὶ μ., Php.1:9; πλεῖον, Mat.5:20.
__II. In late writers (Lft., Notes, 48 f.), trans.,
__(a) to make to abound: with accusative before εἰς, 2Co.4:15 9:8, Eph.1:8; pass., Mat.13:12 25:29; with genitive of thing(s), Luk.15:17, WH;
__(b) to make to excel: with accusative of person(s), dative of thing(s), 1Th.3:12 (cf. ὑπερ-περισσεύω).†
SYN.: πλεονάζω  (AS)

[ἀργύριον] [Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. author] “Vect.” 4.7; ἂν ᾖ τι.. περιττεῦον 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Leges” 855b; εἴ τι π. ἀπὸ τῶν τόκων “SIG” 672.19 (Delph., 2nd c.BC)]]; ἡ περιττεύουσα τροφή [NT+4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Historia Animalium” 619a20; τὸ π. τῶν κλασμάτων NT.Matt.14.20]]; τοσοῦτον τῷ Περικλεῖ ἐπερίσσευσε, κτλ. such abundance of reason had Pericles for his belief, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 2.65; τοσόνδ᾽ ἐπερίσσευσεν αὐτοῖς εὐνοίας 1st c.AD: Josephus Historicus “Antiquitates Judaicae” 19.1.18; τὸ ἀνδρεῖον ἐπερίττευεν αὐτῇ 1st c.BC: Dionysius Halicarnassensis 3.11.]]

to be superior, π. παρά τινα to be better than.., [LXX.Eccl.3.19]; ὑπέρ τινα[LXX.1Mac.3.30 (variant)]; be better, have the advantage, [NT.1Cor.14.12]; π. μᾶλλον abound more and more, i.e. in Christian graces, [NT.1Thes.4.1, 11:—]middle, περισσευόμεθα, opposed to ὑστερούμεθα, [NT.1Cor.8.8.]

Attic dialect περιττός, ή, όν, (from περί, as ἔπισσαι from ἐπί, μέτασσαι from μετά) beyond the regular number or size, prodigious, δῶρα [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th-7th c.BC: Hesiodus Epicus “Theogonia” 399 (never in 8th c.BC: Homerus Epicus); μος “Tragica Adespota” 458.3]]; στάθμα, uncertain meaning, see at {ἕλκω} [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Bacchylides Lyricus 3.]]

__2

[Refs 4th c.BC+ [[prev. author] 15.145; π. καὶ θαυμαστά 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Ethica Nicomachea” 1141b6]]; πρᾶξις π. [Refs [[prev. author] “Pol.” 1312a27; οὐθὲν δὴ λέγοντες π. φαίνονταί τι λέγειν [prev. author] “Metaphorical” 1053b3]]; τί π. ποιεῖτ; [NT+4th c.BC+ [NT.Matt.5.47; περιττοτάτη φύσις 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Historia Animalium” 531a9]]; συνανθρωπίζον.. πάντων περισσότατον, of the dog, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [2nd c.AD: Athenaeus Epigrammaticus 13.611c, compare 4th-3rd c.BC: Clearchus Historicus 24]]; in Literature, striking, τὸ περιττόν, as a quality of οἱ τοῦ Σωκράτους λόγοι, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Politica” 1265a11]]; τὰ σοφὰ καὶ τὰ π. refinements, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-3rd c.BC: Epicurus Philosophus “Fragmenta” 409]]; opposed to κοινὸς καὶ δημώδης, [Refs 3rd c.AD+ [3rd c.AD: Longinus Rhetor 40.2]] (but also, elaborate, π. καὶ πεποιημένος [Refs [[prev. author] 3.4]]; in bad sense, far-fetched, [Refs 1st c.BC+ [1st c.BC: Dionysius Halicarnassensis “Epistula ad Pompeium” 2, “Dem.” 56).]]

__3
of persons, extraordinary, remarkable, especially for great learning, π. ὢν ἀνήρ [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Hippolytus” 948; τοὺς.. π. καί τι πράσσοντας πλέον [prev. author] “fragment” 788]]; δυστυχεῖς εἶναι τοὺς π. [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Metaphysica” 983a2; π. γένος τῶν μελιττῶν [prev. author] “GA” 760a4]]: frequently with the manner added, π. κατὰ φιλοσοφίαν [Refs [[prev. author] “Pr.” 953a10]]; περὶ τὸν ἄλλον βίον περιττότερος somewhat extravagant or eccentric, [Refs [[prev. author] “Pol.” 1267 b24]]; τῇ φύσει π. [Refs 1st c.AD+ [[prev. author] “HA” 622b6; κάλλει 1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus “Demetrius” 2; ἐν ἅπασι [prev. author] “Dem.” 3; τὴν ὥραν 4th c.AD: Alciphro Epistolographus 1.12]]: with infinitive, [Refs 1st c.BC+ [1st c.BC: Dionysius Halicarnassensis “de Compositione Verborum” 18.]]

__4
with genitive, περισσὸς ἄλλων πρός τι beyond others in.., [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Electra” 155]]; θύσει τοῦδε περισσότερα greater things than this, [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [“Anthologia Graeca” 6.321 (Leon. 2nd c.AD: Alexander Rhetor); περιττότερος προφήτου]]one greater than.., [NT.Matt.11.9.]

__II
more than sufficient, superfluous, αἱ π. δαπάναι [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Memorabilia” 3.6.6]]; περιττὸν ἔχειν to have a surplus, [Refs [[prev. author] “An.” 7.6.31]]; οἱ μὲν.. περιττὰ ἔχουσιν, οἱ δὲ οὐδὲ τὰ ἀναγκαῖα.. [Refs [[prev. author] “Oec.” 20.1: with _genitive_, τῶν ἀρκούντων περιττά]] more than sufficient, [Refs [[prev. author] “Cyr.” 8.2.21; τὰ π. τῶν ἱκανῶν [prev. author] “Hier.” 1.19: frequently in military sense, οἱ π. ἱππεῖς]] the reserve horse, [Refs [[prev. author] “Eq.Mag.” 8.14; οἱ π. τῆς φυλακῆς [prev. work] 7.7]]; π. σκηναί spare tents, [Refs [[prev. author] “Cyr.” 4.6.12 (but τοῖς περιττοῖς χρήσεσθαι]] their superior numbers, [Refs [[prev. author] “An.” 4.8.11, compare “Cyr.” 6.3.20)]]; τὸ π. the surplus, residue, Inscription cited in [same work][Refs [“An.” 5.3.13 (but τὸ π. τοῦ Ἰουδαίου]] the advantage of the Jew, [NT.Rom.3.1)]; Ἁρπυιῶν τὰ π. their leavings, [Refs 1st c.AD+ [Anthologia Graeca 11.239 (1st c.AD: Lucillius Epigrammaticus)]]; τὸ π. τῆς ἡμέρας the remainder of the day, [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd c.AD(?): Xenophon Ephesius Scriptor Eroticus 1.3]]; π. γράμματα supplementary provisions in a will, [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [“BGU” 326ii9 (2nd c.AD).]]

__II.2
in bad sense, superfluous, useless, οὐδέ τι τοῦ παντὸς κενεὸν πέλει οὐδὲ π. [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Empedocles Poeta Philosophus 13]]; μόχθος π. [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Prometheus Vinctus” 385, compare 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Antigone” 780; π. κἀνόνητα σώματα [prev. author] “Aj.” 758; βάρος π. γῆς ἀναστρωφώμενοι [prev. author] “fragment” 945; ἄχθος [prev. author] “El.” 1241 (Lyric poetry); τὰ γὰρ π. πανταχοῦ λυπήρ᾽ ἔπη [prev. author] “fragment” 82; αὐδῶ σε μὴ περισσὰ κηρύσσειν 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Septem contra Thebas” 1048; π. πάντες οὑν μέσῳ λόγοι 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Medea” 819; π. φωνῶν [prev. author] “Supp.” 459.]]

__II.3
excessive, extravagant, μηχανᾶσθαι περισσά commit extravagances, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 2.32]]; περισσὰ δρᾶν, πράσσειν, to be over-busy, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Trachiniae” 617, “Ant.” 68]]; π. φρονεῖν to be over-wise, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Fragmenta” 924 (_anapaest meter_); ἡ π. αὕτη ἐπιμέλεια τοῦ σώματος 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 407b]]; μῆκος πολὺ λόγων π. [Refs [[prev. author] “Lg.” 645c]]; redundant, overdone, οἱ καρτεροὶ καὶ π. λόγοι [Refs [[prev. author] “Ax.” 365c, etc.]]; of dress, ἐσθὴς π. [NT+1st c.AD+ [1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus 2.615d; περισσοτέρα λύπη NT.2Cor.2.7]]; τοῦ τὰ δέοντ᾽ ἔχειν περιττὰ μισῶ I hate extravagance in comparison with moderation, [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd c.AD: Alexander Rhetor 254, etc.]]

__II.4
of persons, over-wise, over-curious, περισσὸς καὶ φρονῶν μέγα [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Hippolytus” 445, compare “Ba.” 429 (Lyric poetry)]]; ὁ πολυπράγμων καὶ π. [Refs 2nd c.BC+ [2nd c.BC: Polybius Historicus 9.1.4]]; τὴν περὶ τὸ σῶμα θεραπείαν ἀκριβὴς καὶ π. [Refs 1st c.AD+ [1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus “Cicero” 8]]; so, of speakers, π. ἐν τοῖς λόγοις Δημοσθένης [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aeschines Orator 1.119.]]

__II.5
as a term of praise, subtle, acute, ἀκριβὴς καὶ π. διάνοια [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Topica” 141b13.]]

__III
Arith., ἀριθμὸς π. an odd, uneven number, opposed to ἄρτιος, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Epicharmus Comicus 170.7, 5th-6th c.BC: Philolaus Philosophus 5, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Protagoras” 356e, etc.; π. ἡμέραι 5th c.BC: Hippocrates Medicus “ἀφορισμοί” 4.61]]; τὸ π. καὶ τὸ ἄρτιον the nature of odd and even, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Gorgias” 451c, etc.]]; π. χῶραι the odd places in a verse, [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [7th c.AD: Hephaestio Grammaticus 5.1; ἀρτιάκις π. ἀριθμός a number divisible by an odd number an even number of times, as 2, 6, 10, 3rd c.BC: Euclides Geometra 7 “Def.” 9.]]

__IV
περισσότεροι more in number, extra, Carnead. cited in [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd c.AD: Sextus Empiricus Philosophus “adversus Mathematicos” 9.140.]]

__V
περιττόν, τό, ={στρύχνος μανικός, θρύον}[Refs 4th c.BC+ [11, 4th-3rd c.BC: Theophrastus Philosophus “Historia Plantarum” 9.11.6; περισσόν 1st c.AD: Dioscorides (Dioscurides) Medicus 4.73; περίσκον 4th c.AD: Oribasius Medicus 12.8.56.]]

__B
adverb περισσῶς extraordinarily, exceedingly, θεοσεβέεες π. ἐόντες [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 2.37]]; ἐπαινέσεται π. [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Bacchae” 1197 (Lyric poetry)]]; π. παῖδας ἐκδιδάσκεσθαι to have them educated overmuch, [Refs [[prev. author] “Med.” 295]]; περιττοτέρως τῶν ἄλλων far above all others, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Isocrates Orator 3.44; περισσότερον τοῦ ἑνός 2nd c.AD: Lucianus Sophista “Pr.Im.” 14; also περισσά 5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “N.” 7.43, 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Hecuba” 579, etc.]]

__B.2
remarkably, περισσότερον τῶν ἄλλων θάψαι τινά more sumptuously, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 2.129; οἴκησις π. ἐσκευασμένη 2nd c.BC: Polybius Historicus 1.29.7]]; περιττότατα ἔχειν to be most remarkable, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Historia Animalium” 589a31; κοσμουμένη π. καὶ σεμνῶς 1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus 2.145e]]; περισσότατα ἀνθρώπων θρησκεύειν in the most singular way, [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd-3rd c.AD: Dio Cassius Historicus 37.17]]; ἡδέως καὶ π. in an uncommon manner, [Refs 1st c.BC+ [1st c.BC: Dionysius Halicarnassensis “de Compositione Verborum” 3]]; εἰπεῖν στρογγύλως καὶ π. [Refs [[prev. author] “Is.” 20]]; ἰδίως καὶ π. [Refs 1st c.AD+ [1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus “Theseus” 19]]; τὰ καινῶς ἱστορούμενα καὶ π. [Refs [[prev. author] 2.30d.]]

__B.3
abundantly, ἐχέτω π. τῆς κρόκης [Refs 4th c.AD+ [4th c.AD: Alciphro Epistolographus 3.41.]]

__B.4
with a negative, οὐδὲν περισσὸν τούτων nothing more than or beyond these, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Antipho Orator 3.4.6; οὐδὲν τῶν ἄλλων περιττότερον πραγματεύεσθαι 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Apologia” 20c]]; οὐδὲν π. ἢ εἰ.. no otherwise than if.., [Refs [[prev. author] “Smp.” 219c]]; περισσόν alone, furthermore, [LXX.Eccl.12.12, +others]

__B.5
τὰ περισσά in vain, [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [Anthologia Graeca 12.182 (2nd c.AD: Strato Epigrammaticus).]]

__B.II
ἐκ περιττοῦ superfluously, uselessly, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Protagoras” 338c, “Sph.” 265e]]; but ὑπερέχειν ἐκ π. to be far superior, [Refs [[prev. author] “Lg.” 734d, compare 802d]]; ἡ κάμινος ἐκαύθη ἐκ π. __2

__II
fount, source, τοῦ Νείλου [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 2.28, 4.53 (_plural_), “OGI” 168.9 (Syene, 2nd c.BC), 1st c.BC-1st c.AD: Strabo Geographus 17.1.52 (_plural_)]]; πηγαὶ ἡλίου the fount of light, i. e. the South, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Prometheus Vinctus” 809]]; πηγαὶ νυκτός the North, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Fragmenta” 956; παγὰ ἐπέων 5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “P.” 4.299]]; πυρὸς παγαί[Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. work] 1.22, compare 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Prometheus Vinctus” 110, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Timaeus” 79d]]; πηγὴ ἀργύρου, of the silver-mines at Laureion, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Persae” 238]]; τῆς ἀκουούσης π. δι᾽ ὤτων, i.e. the sense of hearing, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Tyrannus” 1387]]; ἀπὸ μιᾶς ἀρχῆς καὶ π. [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “de Partibus Animalium” 668a15, compare 1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus 2.856e.]]

__II.2
metaphorically, source, origin, mostly in singular, κακῶν π. [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Persae” 743]]; αἱ τέχναι, ἃς πηγάς φασι τῶν καλῶν εἶναι [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 7.2.13; π. καὶ ἀρχὴ κινήσεως 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Phaedrus” 245c]]; π. ἡδονῶν, τοῦ φρονεῖν, νοσημάτων, etc., [Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. author] “Phlb.” 62d, “Lg.” 808d, “Ti.” 85b, etc.; ἀρχαὶ καὶ π. τῶν στάσεων 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Politica” 1301b5, compare 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Leges” 690d; π. τῆς κακοπραγμοσύνης 2nd c.BC: Polybius Historicus 18.40.3]]; βέβηκα π. εἰς ἐμάς I have returned to the source of my existence, [Refs 5th c.AD+ [“epigram Gr.” 463 (from Crommyon), compare 5th-6th c.AD: Damascius Philosophus “de Principiis” 95, +others]]

__II.3

πήξομαι (as passive) [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Hippocrates Medicus “Aër.” 8:]]aorist 1 ἐπήχθην, Epic dialect 3rd.pers. plural πῆχθεν [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 8.298]], Doric dialect subjunctive παχθῇ [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [3rd c.BC: Theocritus Poeta Bucolicus 23.31]], participle πηχθείς [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Cyclops” 302: more frequently]]aorist 2 ἐπάγην [ᾰ], Epic dialect πάγην, Epic dialect 3rd.pers. plural πάγεν [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 11.572]]; participle παγείς [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Eumenides” 190, 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Iphigenia Aulidensis” 395:]]perfect πέπηγμαι (κατα-, συμ-) [Refs 1st c.BC+ [1st c.BC: Dionysius Halicarnassensis 5.46, 2nd c.AD: Arrianus Historicus “Anabasis” 2.21.1]]: pluperfect ἐπέπηκτο [Refs 4th c.AD+ [4th c.AD: Julianus Imperator “Orationes” 3.123b]]; _optative_ πεπαγοίην 5th c.BC: Eupolis Comicus 435]]: pluperfect ἐπεπήγειν [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 13.442, 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 3.23:]]

__I
stick or fix in, ἐν δὲ μετώπῳ πῆξε [τὴν αἰχμήν] [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 4.460, etc.; ἔνθα οἱ ἔγχος ἔπηξε 13.570; ἐν γαίῃ π. ἐρετμόν 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 23.276 (or γαίῃ 11.129); π. ἐπὶ τύμβῳ ἐρετμόν 11.77 (or τύμβῳ 12.15)]]; [γύην] ἐν ἐλύματι π. [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th-7th c.BC: Hesiodus Epicus “Opera et Dies” 430; ἔπαξε διὰ φρενῶν ξίφος 5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “N.” 7.26]]; fix in the earth, plant, σκῆπτρον [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Electra” 420, compare “Aj.” 821]]; σκηνήν, σκηνὰς π., pitch a tent, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Andocides Orator 4.30, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Leges” 817c (in _middle_, σκηνὰς πηξάμενοι]] pitching themselves tents, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 6.12)]]; σταύρωμα π. [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 6.66; τὰς σχαλίδας π. ὑπτίας 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Cynegeticus” 6.7]]; plant seeds or cuttings, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-3rd c.BC: Theophrastus Philosophus “Historia Plantarum” 6.6.9, 7.4.10: _intransitive_]]perfect and passive, δόρυ δ᾽ ἐν κραδίῃ ἐπεπήγει the spear stuck fast in his heart, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 13.442; [δοῦρα] ἐν χροῒ πήγνυτο 15.315; [ὀϊστοὶ] ἐν χροῒ πῆχθεν 8.298; δοῦρα ἐν σάκεϊ πάγεν 11.572; [ξίφος] πέπηγεν ἐν γῇ 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Ajax” 819; σκηνὴ ἔσκε πεπηγυῖα ἑτοίμη 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 7.119; κυρβασίας ὀρθὰς πεπηγυίας [prev. work] 64, compare 70:]] —middle, ἐν ἀλλήλοις χείλεα πηξάμενοι, of kissing, [Refs [“Anthologia Graeca” 5.254 (Paul. Sil.).]]

__I.2
stick or fix on, κεφαλὴν ἀνὰ σκολόπεσσι [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 18.177; σκόλοψι δέμας 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Iphigenia Taurica” 1430; κρᾶτα πήξασ᾽ ἐπ᾽ ἄκρον θύρσον [prev. author] “Ba.” 1141:]] —passive, ἀμφὶ βουπόροισι πηχθέντας μέλη ὀβελοῖσι having their limbs fixed on spits, [Refs [[prev. author] “Cyc.” 302]]; ὑπὸ ῥάχιν παγέντες impaled, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Eumenides” 190.]]

__I.3
fix upon an object, κατὰ χθονὸς ὄμματα π. [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 3.217]]: intransitive perfect, πρὸς ἀστρονομίαν ὄμματα πέπηγεν [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 53o d, compare 4th c.AD: Julianus Imperator [prev. cited] (_passive_)]]; πεπηγυῖα τὰς τῶν ὀμμάτων βολὰς ἐς τὰ τῆς ψυχῆς ἀπόρρητα [Refs 3rd c.AD+ [3rd c.AD: Philostratus Junior Sophista “Imagines” 11: with]]infinitive, ἡ σοφία ἀρέσκειν πέπηγε is bent upon pleasing, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 605a: _absolutely_, τὸ πεπηγὸς ὄμμα]] immovable eye, fixed gaze, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Hippocrates Medicus “προρρητικόν” 1.46, compare 2nd c.AD: Galenus Medicus 16.610.]]

__II
fasten [different parts] together, fit together, build, νῆας πῆξαι [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 2.664]]; ἴκρια π. [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 5.163:]] —middle, πήξασθαι ἄμαξαν build oneself a wagon, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th-7th c.BC: Hesiodus Epicus “Opera et Dies” 455; νέας πηξάμενοι 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 5.83]]:—passive, to be joined or put together, ψυχὴ καὶ σῶμα παγέν [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Phaedrus” 246c.]]

__III
make solid or stiff, especially of liquids, freeze, θεὸς.. πήγνυσι πᾶν ῥέεθρον [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Persae” 496]]; τοὺς ποταμοὺς ἔπηξε (i.e. ὁ θεός) [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Acharnenses” 139; βορρᾶς πηγνὺς τοὺς ἀνθρώπους 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 4.5.3]]; curdle, γάλα [Refs 1st c.AD+ [1st c.AD: Dioscorides (Dioscurides) Medicus 4.95:]] —middle, τυροὺς πήγνυσθαι to make oneself cheese (by curdling the milk), [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd c.AD: Lucianus Sophista “VH” 1.24]]:—passive and intransitive perfect, become solid, stiffen, γοῦνα πήγνυται [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 22.453; ἄρθρα πέπηγέ μου 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Hercules Furens” 1395]] (but also, become firm or set, of limbs, [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd-3rd c.AD: Aelianus “De Natura Animalium - Ar.Byzantine Epit.” 2.11; πεπηγυῖα ὑγιεινὴ κατάστασις 2nd c.AD: Galenus Medicus “Θρασύβουλος - Scripta Minora” 7)]]; of liquids, freeze, ἡ θάλασσα πήγνυται [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 4.28]]; ἅλες πήγνυνται salt crystallizes, [Refs 7th c.BC+ [[prev. work] 53, compare 6.119; φόνος πέπηγεν 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Choephori” 67 (Lyric poetry); πεπάγαισιν ὐδάτων ῤόαι 7th-6th c.BC: Alcaeus Lyricus 34, compare 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 7.4.3]]; κρύσταλλος ἐπεπήγει οὐ βέβαιος was not frozen so as to bear, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 3.23; ἁνίκα [χιὼν] παχθῇ 3rd c.BC: Theocritus Poeta Bucolicus 23.31]]; ὄστρακον [ᾠοῦ] π. [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “de Generatione Animalium” 752a35]]; γάλα π. drawing- or writing-tablet, ={δέλτος}, γράψας ἐν π. πτυκτῷ [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 6.169; πίναξιν.. ἐγγεγραμμένα 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Supplices” 946; πινάκων ξεστῶν δέλτοι 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Thesmophoriazusae” 778; ἐν χρυσῷ π. γράψαντες 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Critias” 120c, compare “R.” 501a]]; of a votive tablet hung on the image of a god, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Supplices” 463, compare 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Politica” 1341a36, “IG” 42(1).121.24(Epid., 4th c.BC, _plural_), 3rd c.BC: Herodas Mimographus 4.19, 1st c.BC-1st c.AD: Strabo Geographus 8.6.15 (_plural_), etc.]]; Πίνακες tables or catalogues of authors, name of a work by Callimachus, [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [3rd c.AD(?): Diogenes Laertius 8.86, compare 2nd c.AD: Athenaeus Epigrammaticus 6.244a, 13.585b, 10th c.AD: Suidas Legal icographus see {Καλλίμαχος}]]; lists of philosophers, [Refs 1st c.BC+ [1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus “Sulla” 26; αἵ τ᾽ ἀναγραφαὶ τῶν π. αἵ τε βυβλιοθῆκαι 1st c.BC: Philodemus Philosophus “περὶ τῶν Στωικῶν” 339.13.]]

__2
trencher, platter, κρειῶν πίνακας παρέθηκεν [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 1.141, compare 16.49]]; ἐπ᾽ ἀργυροῦ π. [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-3rd c.BC: Philippides Comicus 9.4; π. χαλκοῦς 2nd c.AD: Athenaeus Epigrammaticus 4.128d]]; salver, πίνακα.. μέγαν, ἔχοντα μικροὺς πέντε πινακίσκους [Refs [Lynceus Comicus 1.5, compare 17, 19]]; πίνακες ὑέλινοι [Refs 6th c.AD+ [6th c.AD: Aëtius Medicus 7.106.]]

__3
board for painting on, picture, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Simonides Lyricus 178, 4th c.BC: Anaxandrides Comicus 33.2; π. οἱ γραφόμενοι 4th-3rd c.BC: Theophrastus Philosophus “Historia Plantarum” 5.7.4, compare “IG” 11(2).161 A 75 (Delos, 3rd c.BC).]]

__4
generally, plate with anything drawn or engraved on it, χάλκεος π., of a map, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 5.49, compare 1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus “Theseus” 1]]; π. γεωγραφικός, first made by Anaximander, [Refs 1st c.BC+ [1st c.BC-1st c.AD: Strabo Geographus 1.1.11.]]

__5
board or tablet on which astronomical tables were drawn, ἡ περὶ πίνακα μέθοδος the art of casting nativities, [Refs 1st c.AD+ [1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus “Romulus” 12]]; ἀγυρτικοὶ π. [Refs [[prev. author] “Comp. Arist.Cat.” 3, compare πινάκιον 11.3.]]

__5.b
proverbial, ἐκ πίνακος καὶ πυλαίας, of a trivial fiction, [Refs [[prev. author] 2.386b.]]

__6

__7
strop, to sharpen knives on, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-3rd c.BC: Theophrastus Philosophus “Historia Plantarum” 5.5.1.]]

πίνω [ῑ],
Epic dialect infinitive πινέμεναι and -έμεν, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 4.346, 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 7.220]]: Ionic dialect imperfect πίνεσκον [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 16.226]]: future πίομαι [Refs 6th c.BC+ [13.493, 6th c.BC: Theognis Elegiacus 962, 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Choephori” 578, 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Coloneus” 622, 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Equites” 1289, 1401, “fragment” 311; later πῐοῦμαι 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Rhetorica” 1370b18, 2nd-3rd c.AD: Aelianus “Varia Historia” 12.49, etc.]]; also as falsa lectio in earlier authors, πιεῖσθαι [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Hippocrates Medicus “περὶ τῶν ἐντὸς παθῶν” 12, πιεῖσθε 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Symposium” 4.7, but rejected by 2nd c.AD: Phrynichus Atticista 23, 2nd c.AD: Athenaeus Epigrammaticus 10.446d]]; 2nd pers. singular πίεσαι [LXX+NT [LXX.Deu.28.39, NT.Luke.17.8:]]aorist ἔπῐον, Epic dialect πίον [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 22.2, etc.]]; 2nd pers. singular subjunctive πίῃσθα [Refs 8th c.BC+ [6.260; _imperative_ πίε 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 9.347, 4th-3rd c.BC: Menander Comicus 151, “Carmina Popularia” 33, (ἐκ-) 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Cyclops” 563, 5th-6th c.AD: Orphica “Fragmenta” 32 b iii; also πῖθι 5th c.BC: Cratinus Comicus 141, Ion Trag. 27, 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Vespae” 1489, 5th-6th c.BC: Amipsias Comicus 18, 4th c.BC: Antiphanes Comicus 163.1, etc., (ἔκ-) 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Cyclops” 570]]; πίει, πίεις, Kretschmer [Refs [“Griech. Vaseninschr.” p.195]]; infinitive πιεῖν [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 8.70, 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 4.172, etc.]]; later contraction πεῖν [Refs 1st c.AD+ [“Anthologia Graeca” 11.140 (1st c.AD: Lucillius Epigrammaticus), “Mim.Oxy.” 413.66, “PMag.Lond.” 121.738, “PFlor.” 101.8 (1st c.AD), etc.]]; Epic dialect πῐέμεν [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 15.378, πιέειν 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 4.263, πιέναι]] falsa lectio for{ὑπιέναι} in [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Hippocrates Medicus “ἐπιδημίαι” 5.18]]; participle πῐών, πῐοῦσα, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 24.102, etc., πῐέουσα 5th c.BC: Hippocrates Medicus “ἐπιδημίαι” 7.11]]:—middle, subjunctive πινώμεθα [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Hermippus Comicus 25; _imperative_ πίνεο 2nd c.BC: Nicander Epicus “Theriaca” 912]]: πίομαι [ῑ] as present middle, [Refs 6th c.BC+ [6th c.BC: Ibycus Lyricus 17 (assuming variant), 5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “O.” 6.86, and so ἐκπίομαι [ῑ] 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Acharnenses” 199, ἐμπίομαι [ῐ] 6th c.BC: Theognis Elegiacus 1129]] (passive in [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [“Anthologia Graeca” 5.43 (2nd-3rd c.AD: Rufinus Epigrammaticus))]]:—passive, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 20.312, 5th c.BC: Hippocrates Medicus “Aër.” 9, etc.: _Epic dialect_]]imperfect πίνετο [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 9.45.]] —Other tenses are from πω- or πο-, perfect πέπωκα [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Septem contra Thebas” 821, etc.:]] —passive, future ποθήσομαι (κατα-) [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Vespae” 1502, (ἐκ-) 1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus 2.240e:]]aorist ἐπόθην (ἐξ-) [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Choephori” 66, (κατ-) 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Critias” 111d]]: perfect infinitive πεπόσθαι [Refs 6th c.BC+ [6th c.BC: Theognis Elegiacus 477]]: Aeolic dialect present πώνω [Refs 7th c.BC+ [7th-6th c.BC: Alcaeus Lyricus 20, 52, “Supp.” 20.3:]]aorist imperative πῶθι, τῶ, [Refs [“Etymologicum Magnum” 698.52]]. [ῑ always in πίνω. πίνομα; ῐ always in aorist ἔπιον, hence πίε must be read for πῖνε in [Refs 8th c.BC+ [“Anthologia Graeca” 11.19 (2nd c.AD: Strato Epigrammaticus), and ἔπῑνον for ἔπιον in “Anacreontea” 5.5: 8th c.BC: Homerus Epicus has ἐθέλουσι δὲ πῑέμεν ἄμφω 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 16.825, compare 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 18.3; but καὶ φαγέμεν πῐέμεν τε 15.378]]; in imperative πῖθι, ῑ always.—In future πίομαι [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Homerus Epicus and Trag. use ῑ, 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 13.493, 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Choephori” 578, 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Coloneus” 622, compare 6th c.BC: Theognis Elegiacus 962, 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Equites” 1289, 1401, “fragment” 311; but ῐ in lon Lyric poetry 2.10 (nisi to be read πιέτω), (ἐκ-) 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Comicus 9, 5th-6th c.BC: Amipsias Comicus 22]]; also in later Poetry, [Refs 1st c.AD+ [“Anthologia Graeca” 11.8,25.5 (1st c.AD: Apollonides Epigrammaticus)]]; for present middle πίομαι, see above]: —drink, frequently from [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Homerus Epicus downwards, with _accusative_, π. οἶνον, ὐρόν, αἷμα, etc., 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 15.391, 17.225, 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Coloneus” 622, etc.]]; π. ὕδωρ Αἰσήποιο drink its water, i.e. live on its banks, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 2.825, compare 5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “O.” 6.86 (_middle_)]]: with genitive partitive, drink of a thing, π. οἴνοιο [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 22.11]]; εἰς οἶνον.., ἔνθεν ἔπινον whereof..,[Refs [4.220; αἵματος ὄφρα πίω 11.96, compare 15.373]]; also πίνειν κρητῆρας οῐνοιο to drink bowls of wine, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 8.232; κύπελλα ὄνου 4.346]]; π. ἀπὸ κρήνης drink of a spring, [Refs 6th c.BC+ [6th c.BC: Theognis Elegiacus 959 (but κρήνης 962)]]; π. ἀπ᾽ αὐτοῦ (i.e. δέπαος) αἴθοπα οἶνον from it, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 16.226; δέπα ἔνθεν ἔπινον 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 19.62; ἐκ κεράμων μέθυ πίνετο 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 9.469; ἐκ τῆς χειρὸς διδοῖ πιεῖν 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 4.172; ἐκ ταὐτοῦ.. ποτηρίου 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Equites” 1289; ἐξ ἀργύρου ἢ χρυσοῦ 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 417a; ἀπὸ τοῦ ποταμοῦ 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 4.5.4]]; σκύφος ᾧ περ ἔπινεν with which.., [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 14.112]]; π. κερατίνοις ποτηρίοις variant in [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 6.1.4]]; τὰ φάρμακα π. παρὰ τοῦ ἰατροῦ draughts sent by him, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Gorgias” 467c.]]

__2
absolutely, drink, ἐσθιέμεν καὶ πινέμεν [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 2.305; ὁ πῖνε καὶ ἦσθε 5.94, 6.249, compare 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 24.476, etc.]]; μῆλα πιόμεν᾽ ἐκ βοτάνης going to drink after pasture,[Refs 7th c.BC+ [13.493; πρὸς βίαν πώνην 7th-6th c.BC: Alcaeus Lyricus 20; πῖνε, πῖν᾽ ἐπὶ συμφοραῖς 4th-5th c.BC: Simonides Lyricus 14; π. πρὸς ἡδονήν 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Symposium” 176e; εἰς μέθην [prev. author] “Lg.” 775b; διδόναι πιεῖν 5th c.BC: Cratinus Comicus 124; πιεῖν αἰτεῖν 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 8.3.41]]; τινὶ πιεῖν ἐγχέας[Refs 4th c.BC+ [[prev. work] 1.3.9; πιεῖν τις ἡμῖν ἐγχεάτω 4th-3rd c.BC: Philemo Comicus 9: in]]perfect πέπωκα, to be drunk, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Cyclops” 536]]; πίνοντά τε καὶ πεπωκότα drinking and having finished drinking, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Phaedo” 117c.]]

__II
celebrate by a carouse, νίκην [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd-3rd c.AD: Philostratus Sophista “de gymnastica” 54.]]

__III
metaphorically, drink up, as the earth does rain, τὸ ὕδωρ, ὄμβρον, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 3.117, 4.198; πιοῦσα κόνις μέλαν αἷμα 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Eumenides” 979 (Lyric poetry), compare “Th.” 736 (Lyric poetry), 821, 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Tyrannus” 1401]]; of plants, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Symposium” 2.25]]; of a lamp, π. τοὔλαιον [Refs 5th c.BC+ [2nd c.AD: Lucianus Sophista “Cat.” 27; λύχνος.. πολλὰ πιὼν μέλη “Anthologia Graeca” 5.196 (1st c.BC: Meleager Epigrammaticus, uncertain reading). (I.- 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus]] pōy- and pī-, cf. Sanskrit pāy-áyati 'cause to drink', pīti- 'a drink', Latin pōtus, etc.)

participle περάσαντες [Refs [“hymnus ad Cererem” 132]]; aorist optative 3rd.pers. singular περάσειε [ᾰ] [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 14.297]]; aorist subjunctive 2nd pers. plural περάσητε [Refs [15.453, compare ἀποπέρνημι]]; Ionic dialect ἐπρήθην [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.156, “SIG” 229.5 (Erythrae, 4th c.BC), etc.: _Attic dialect_]]future πεπράσομαι [ᾱ] [LXX+5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Vespae” 179, 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 7.1.36, later πρᾱθήσομαι 4th c.BC: Sopater Comicus 6, LXX.Lev.25.23, etc., cf. Moer. p.294]] P.: Aeolic dialect present infinitive πόρναμεν [Refs 5th c.AD+ [5th c.AD(?): Hesychius Legal icographus]] (perhaps πορνάμεναι): present participle passive πορνάμεναι[Refs [[prev. author]]] —In Attic dialect the usual present in active sense is πωλέω, future ἀποδώσομαι, aorist ἀπεδόμην: from πέπρᾱμαι, ἐπράθην, etc. is formed the later present passive πιπράσκομαι, first found in [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Lysias Orator 18.20, interpolated in 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Phaedo” 69b, “Sph.” 224a]], and from this the present active πιπράσκω first found in [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd c.AD: Lucianus Sophista “Asin.” 32]]: imperfect ἐπίπρασκον [Refs 1st c.AD+ [1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus 2.178c, “Per.” 16]]; Ionic dialect πιπρήσκω [Refs 5th c.BC+ [3rd c.BC: Callimachus Epicus “Iambi” 1.93, variant in 5th c.BC: Hippocrates Medicus “ἐπιστολαί” 17]]:—export for sale, in Epic dialect usually of exporting captives to foreign parts for sale as slaves, πολλοὺς ζωοὺς ἑλον ἠδὲ πέρασσα [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 21.102, compare 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 14.297]]; π. τινὰ Αῆμνον sell one to Lemnos, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 21.40; ἐς Αῆμνον [prev. work] 58 (_passive_), 78; σέ γε.. νηυσὶν λάβον ἠδ᾽ ἐπέρασσαν τοῦδ᾽ ἀνδρὸς πρὸς δώμαθ᾽ 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 15.387]]; κατ᾽ ἀλλοθρόους ἀνθρώπους[Refs 8th c.BC+ [[prev. work] 453; δήσειν καὶ περάαν νήσων ἔπι τηλεδαπάων 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 21.454; κτείνων καὶ περνὰς ν. ἔ. τ. 22.45; πέρνασχ᾽ ὅν τιν᾽ ἕλεσκε πέρην ἁλὸς.. ἐς Σάμον 24.752; οὐδ᾽ ἡμᾶς περνᾶσι 6th c.BC: Theognis Elegiacus [same place], compare 6th c.BC: Hipponax Iambographus 46]]; later also of other merchandise, ὡς χαραδριὸν περνάς [Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. author] 52 (variant{μῶν.. περνᾷ;; τοῖς ξένοις τὰ χρήματα περνάντα σ᾽ εἶδον} 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Cyc.”]][same place]:—passive, κτήματα περνάμεν᾽ ἵκει [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 18.292, compare 5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “I.” 2.7; πάντα.. πέρναται 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Equites” 176.]]

__2
simply, sell (as always in the Attic dialect forms), τὰ κτήματα πέντε ταλάντων πεπρακότας [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Isaeus Orator]] [same place]:—passive, to be sold, especially for exportation, [Refs 6th c.BC+ [6th c.BC: Solon Lyricus [same place], 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.156, 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Choephori” 915, 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Ion” 310]]; ἐς Αιβύην, ἐς Θεσπρωτούς, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 2.54, 56; ἐπ᾽ ἐξαγωγῇ “SIG” 45.38 (Halic., 5th c.BC)]]; ὠνούμενά τε καὶ πιπρασκόμενα interpolated in [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Phaedo” 69b; τὸ ὠνηθὲν ἢ πραθέν [prev. author] “Lg.” 850a; πραθείσης ὀλίγου [τῆς πεντηκοστῆς] the tax of 2]] per century. having been sold or let for a small sum, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Andocides Orator 1.133.]]

__II
sell for a bribe, of political leaders, τοὺς πεπρακότας αὑτοὺς ἐκείνῳ [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 10.63, compare 17.13; τὰ ὅλα πεπρακέναι [prev. author] 18.28; τἆλλα πλὴν ἑαυτοὺς οἰομένοις πωλεῖν πρώτους ἑαυτοὺς πεπρακόσιν αἰσθέσθαι [prev. work]46; τὴν πατρῴαν γῆν πεπρακέναι 4th-3rd c.BC: Dinarchus Orator 1.71; πεπρακότες τὴν τοῦ βίου παρρησίαν 2nd c.AD: Alexander Rhetor 146.1: _metaphorically_ in]]passive, πέπραμαι I am bought and sold !, i. e. betrayed, ruined, πέπραμαι κἀπόλωλα [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Philoctetes” 978; εὐμορφίᾳ πραθεῖσα 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Troades” 936. (Cogn. with περάω (A), πέραν]], OIr. renaid 'he sells'.)

Abbott-Smith / STEPBible (TBESG)
πίπτω
[in LXX chiefly for נָפַל ;]
to fall;
__1. of descent, to fall, fall down or from: before ἐπί, with accusative loc., Mat.10:29, al.; εἰς, Mat.15:14, al.; ἐς μέσῳ, with genitive, Luk.8:7; παρὰ τ. ὁδόν, Mat.13:4, Mrk.4:4, Luk.8:5; before ἀπό, Mat.15:27, al.; ἐκ, Mrk.13:25, Luk.10:18, Rev.8:10 9:1. Metaphorical: ὁ ἥλιος, before ἐπί, Rev.7:16; ἀχλὺς κ. σκότος, Act.13:11; ὁ κλῆρος, Act.1:26; ὑπὸ κρίσιν, Jas.5:12.
__2. Of prostration,
__(a) of persons, to fall prostrate, prostrate oneself: χαμαί Jhn.18:6; before ἐπί, with accusative, Mat.17:6, Act.9:4; id. with genitive, Mrk.9:20; πρὸς τ. πόδας, Act.5:10, Rev.1:17; πεσὼν ἐξέψυξε, Act.5:5; of supplication, homage or worship: πρὸς (παρὰ, ἐπὶ) τ. πὸδας, Mrk.5:22, Luk.8:41, Act.10:25, al.; π. καὶ προσκυνεῖν, Rev.5:14 19:4; ptcp. with προσκυνεῖν, Mat.2:11, al.; ἐνώπιον, Rev.4:10 5:8; ἐπὶ πρόσωπον, Mat.26:39, al.;
__(b) of things, to fall, fall down: Mat.21:44, Luk.23:30; of falling to ruin and destruction, Mat.7:25, Act.15:16, Heb.11:30; ἔπεσε (timeless aorist; M, Pr.,134), Rev.18:2. Metaphorical: Rom.11:11; πόθεν πέπτωκας, Rev.2:5; opposite to ἑστόναι, 1Co.10:12; to στήκειν, Rom.14:4; of virtues, 1Co.13:8; of precepts, Luk.16:17.
(cf. ἀνα-, ἀντι-, ἀπο-, ἐκ-, ἐπι-, κατα-, παρα-, περι-, προσ-, συν-πίπτω.)
συν-πίπτω (Rec. συμπ-),
[in LXX for נָפַל, etc. ;]
to fall together, fall in, etc.: of a house (cf. MM, xxiv), Luk.6:49.†
(AS)

LSJ / STEPBible (TFLSJ)
πίπτω,
Aeolic dialect πίσσω, accusative to Grammars  in Hilgard Exc. ex libris Herodiani p.28 (cf. Hdn.Gr.2.377 note); poetry subjunctive πίπτῃσι [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Comicus 153.5]]: Epic dialect imperfect πῖπτον [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 8.67, etc.]] (for the quantity of ι[Refs 2nd c.AD+ [compare 2nd c.AD: Herodianus Grammaticus Gr. 2.10)]]; Ionic dialect πίπτεσκον (συμ-) [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Empedocles Poeta Philosophus 59.2]]: future πεσοῦμαι [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Choephori” 971 (Lyric poetry), etc.]]; Ionic dialect3rd.pers. plural πεσέονται [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 11.824]], 3rd.pers. singular πεσέεται [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 7.163, 168:]]aorist ἔπεσον, infinitive πεσεῖν, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 13.178, etc.]]; 2nd pers. singular optative πεσοίης [Refs 1st c.AD+ [1st-2nd c.AD: Polemo Sophista “Callimachus” 10.14]]; Aeolic dialect and Doric dialect ἔπετον [Refs 7th c.BC+ [7th-6th c.BC: Alcaeus Lyricus 60, 5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “O.” 7.69, “P.” 5.50, (κάπετον) “O.” 8.38, (ἐμ-) “P.” 8.81, compare 3rd c.BC: Isyllus Lyricus 8, “IG” 14.642 (from Thurii)]]; in later writers ἔπεσα, [LXX+5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.AD: Orphica “Argonautica” 521, LXX.Lev.9.24, +others, _falsa lectio_ in 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Troades” 291]] (προς-): perfect πέπτωκα [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Eumenides” 147, 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Ranae” 970, etc.]]; Epic dialect participle πεπτεώς, εῶτος (the εω forming one syllable by synizesis), [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 21.503, etc.]]; also πεπτηώς, ηυῖα, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 14.354, 4th-5th c.BC: Simonides Lyricus 183.7, 5th c.BC: Hippocrates Medicus “γυναικεῖα” 1.69, 3rd c.BC: Apollonius Rhodius Epicus 4.1298, “Anthologia Graeca” 7.427 (Antip. Sid.), compare πτήσσω]]; Trag. participle πεπτώς [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Ajax” 828, “Ant.” 697]]. (Redupl. from πετ-, which appears in Aeolic dialect and Doric dialect aorist ἔ-πετ-ον (see. above), and the poetry form πίτ-ν; cognate with πέτομαι, which see)

__A
Radical sense, fall down, and (when intentional) cast oneself down, πρηνέα πεσεῖν, ὕπτιος πέσεν, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 6.307, 15.435, etc.; νιφάδες.. π. θαμειαί 12.278; ὀπίσω πέσεν 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 12.410; etc.:—Constr., with Preps., in 8th c.BC: Homerus Epicus almost always ἐν.., ἐν κονίῃσι π]]. fall in the dust, i.e. to rise no more, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 11.425, compare 13.205; ἐν αἵματι καὶ κονίῃσι πεπτεῶτας 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 22.384]]; π. ἐν ἀγκοίνῃσί τινος fall into his arms, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th-7th c.BC: Hesiodus Epicus “Fragmenta” 142.5]]; ἐν χθονὶ πεπτηώς Simon. [prev. cited] (compare πτήσσω) π. ἐν δεμνίοις [Refs 8th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Orestes” 35, compare 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Persae” 125 (Lyric poetry) (see. below 5th c.BC: Bacchylides Lyricus 1): rare in Prose, π. ἐν ποταμῷ 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Agesilaus” 1.32: with _dative_ only, πεδίῳ πέσε 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 5.82]]; δεμνίοις π. [Refs 8th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Orestes” 88 (assuming variant); π. ἐπὶ χθονί 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 24.535; οὐδέ οἱ ὕπνος πῖπτεν ἐπὶ βλεφάροις 8th-7th c.BC: Hesiodus Epicus “Fragmenta” 188.4; ἐπὶ γᾷ 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Antigone” 134 (Lyric poetry); πρὸς πέδῳ 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Bacchae” 605; πρὸς ἀγκάλαις [prev. author] “Ion” 962; ἀμφὶ σώμασίν τινων 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Agamemnon” 326]]: with a preposition of motion first in [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th-7th c.BC: Hesiodus Epicus, Πληϊάδες π. ἐς πόντον “Op.” 620; [ποταμὸς] εἰς ἅλα “Th.” 791; εἰς ἄντλον 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Hecuba” 1025 (Lyric poetry); ἐπὶ γᾶν π. αἷμα 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Agamemnon” 1019 (Lyric poetry); ἐπὶ στόμα 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Cynegeticus” 10.13; πρὸς οὖδας 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Hecuba” 405.]]

__2
in [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Homerus Epicus with Advs. of motion as well as of rest, χαμάδις π. 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 7.16, 15.714, etc.; χαμαὶ π. 4.482, compare 14.418, etc.]]; π. ἔραζε [Refs 8th c.BC+ [12.156, compare 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 22.280.]]

__3
with Preps. denoting the point from which one falls, ἀπ᾽ ὤμων χαμαὶ πέσε [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 16.803; ἀπ᾽ οὐρανοῦ 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Fragmenta - American Journal of Philology” 44.3; ἀπό τινος ὄνου 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Leges” 701d; ἐκ χειρῶν π. ἡνία 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 5.583; π. ἐκ νηός 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 12.417; πεσὼν ἐκ νηὸς ἀποφθίμην ἐνὶ πόντῳ 10.51.]]

__4
Geometry texts, of perpendiculars or parts of applied figures, π. ἐπί τι fall upon, [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [3rd c.BC: Euclides Geometra 3.11, 3rd c.BC: Archimedes Geometra “περὶ τῶν ὀχουμένων” 2.8, +others, 3rd-2nd c.BC: Apollonius Pergaeus Geometra “Conica” 1.2]]; but π. ἐπί τι, ποτί τι, intersect, meet, [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [3rd c.BC: Archimedes Geometra “περὶ κωνοειδέων καὶ σφαιροειδέων” 16, “Spir.” 15]]; π. διά τινος pass through, [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [[prev. author] “Con.Sph.” 17; π. κατά τινος [prev. author] “Sph.Cyl.” 1 “Def.” 2; ἐπί τι κατά τινα 3rd-2nd c.BC: Apollonius Pergaeus Geometra “Conica” 1.2.]]

__B
Special usages:

__B.I
πίπτειν ἔν τισι fall violently upon, attack, ἐνὶ νήεσσι πέσωμεν [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 13.742 (but ἐν νήεσσι πεσόντες]] tumbling into the ships, [Refs [2.175)]]; ἐν βουσὶ π. [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Ajax” 375 (Lyric poetry)]]; Ἔρως, ὃς ἐν κτήμασι π. [Refs [[prev. author] “Ant.” 782 (Lyric poetry)]]; ἐπ᾽ ἀλλήλοισι, of combatants, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th-7th c.BC: Hesiodus Epicus “Scutum Herculis” 379, compare 375; πρὸς μῆλα καὶ ποίμνας 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Ajax” 1061; πρὸς πύλαις 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Septem contra Thebas” 462.]]

__B.I.2
throw oneself down, fall down, πρὸς βρέτη θεῶν[Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. work] 185; ἀμφὶ σὸν γόνυ 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Hecuba” 787]]; ἐς γόνατα on one's knees, of a wrestler, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Simonides Lyricus 156; ἐς τὸν ὦμον 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Equites” 571.]]

__B.II
fall in battle, πῖπτε δὲ λαός [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 8.67, etc.]]; οἱ πεπτωκότες the fallen, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 1.4.24; νέκυες πίπτοντες 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 10.200; νεκροὶ περὶ νεκροῖς πεπτωκότες 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Phoenissae” 881; πεσήματα.. πέπτωκε δοριπετῆ νεκρῶν [prev. author] “Andr.” 653; π. ὑπὸ Ἀθηναίων 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 9.67; ὡς.. θάμνοι πρόρριζοι πίπτουσι.., ὣς ἄρ᾽ ὑπ᾽ Ἀτρεΐδῃ πῖπτε κάρηνα Τρώων 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 11.157, compare 500, etc.; τὸ Περσῶν ἄνθος οἴχεται πεσόν 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Persae” 252.]]

__B.II.2
fall, be ruined, δόμον δοκοῦντα κάρτα νῦν πεπτωκέναι [Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. author] “Ch.” 263, compare 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Philebus” 22 e; πεσεῖν.. πτώματ᾽ οὐκ ἀνασχετά 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Prometheus Vinctus” 919, compare 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Laches” 181b; στάντες τ᾽ ἐς ὀρθὸν καὶ πεσόντες ὕστερον 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Tyrannus” 50]]; ἀβουλίᾳ, ἐξ ἀβουλίας π., [Refs [[prev. author] “El.” 429, 398; ἀπὸ σμικροῦ κακοῦ [prev. author] “Aj.” 1078]]; of an army, μεγάλα πεσόντα πρήγματα ὑπὸ ἡσσόνων [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 7.18, compare 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 2.89; ὁ Ξέρξεω στρατὸς αὐτὸς ὑπ᾽ ἑωυτοῦ ἔπιπτε 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 8.16]]; of a city, π. δορί [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Hecuba” 5.]]

__B.II.3
fall, sink, ἄνεμος πέσε the wind fell, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 19.202 (but in 8th-7th c.BC: Hesiodus Epicus “Opera et Dies” 547, Βορέαο πεσόντος is used for ἐμπεσόντος]], falling on, blowing on one): metaph, πέπτωκεν κομπάσματα [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Septem contra Thebas” 794, compare 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Antigone” 474: with _dative_, ταῖς ἐλπίσι πεσεῖν]] fail in one's hopes, [Refs 2nd c.BC+ [2nd c.BC: Polybius Historicus 1.87.1.]]

__B.II.4
fall short, fail, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Phaedo” 100e]]; of a playwright, fail, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Equites” 540.]]

__B.III
πίπτειν ἔκ τινος fall out of, lose a thing, unintentionally, σοι ἐκ θυμοῦ πεσέειν fall out of, lose thy favour, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 23.595]]; ἐξ ἐλπίδων π. [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Fragmenta” 420.5; τοὔμπαλιν π. φρενῶν [prev. author] “Hipp.” 390]]; also of set purpose, ἐξ ἀρκύων π. escape from.., [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Eumenides” 147; ἔξω τῶν κακῶν 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Ranae” 970.]]

__B.III.2
reversely, πολλὴν ἐς κακότητα π. [Refs 6th c.BC+ [6th c.BC: Theognis Elegiacus 42; εἰς ἄτην 6th c.BC: Solon Lyricus 13.68; εἰς δουλοσύνην [prev. author] 9.4; ἐς δάκρυα 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 6.21; ἐς νόσον 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Prometheus Vinctus” 478]]; εἰς ἔρον, ἔριν, ὀργήν, φόβον, ἀνάγκας, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Iphigenia Taurica” 1172, “fragment” 578.8, “Or.” 696, “Ph.” 69, 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 3.82]]; also ἐν γυιοπέδαις π. [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “P.” 2.41; ἐν μέσοις ἀρκυστάτοις 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Electra” 1476; ἐν φόβῳ 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Orestes” 1418 (Lyric poetry); ἐν σολοικισμῷ 2nd c.AD: Lucianus Sophista “Sol.” 3; πρὸς τόλμαν 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Ichn.” 11: with _dative_ only, π. δυσπραξίαις [prev. author] “Aj.” 759; αἰσχύνῃ [prev. author] “Tr.” 597, etc.]]; οὐκ ἔχω ποῖ γνώμης πέσω I know not which way to turn, [Refs [[prev. work] 705.]]

__B.III.3
εἰς ὕπνον π. fall asleep, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. author] “Ph.” 826; but ἐν ὕπνῳ 5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “I.” 4(3).23]]; simply ὕπνῳ, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Eumenides” 68.]]

__B.III.4
π. εἰς (ἰατρικὴν) χρῆσιν to be applied to (medicinal) use, [Refs 1st c.AD+ [1st c.AD: Dioscorides (Dioscurides) Medicus 5.19,151, +others]]

__B.III.5
π. ὑπ᾽ αἴσθησιν to be accessible to perception, [Refs 4th c.AD+ [4th c.AD: Iamblichus Philosophus “de communi mathematica scientia” 8, “in Nic.” p.7 P.]]

__B.IV
πίπτειν μετὰ ποσσὶ γυναικός to fall between her feet, i.e. to be born, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 19.110.]]

__B.V

__1. intrans., to have faith (in), to believe; in cl., with accusative, dative, in NT also with prep, (on the significance of the various constructions, see M, Pr., 67f.; Vau. on Rom.4:5; Ellic. on 1Ti.1:16; Abbott, JV, 19-80): absol., Mat.24:23, 26 Mrk.13:21, 1Co.11:18; with accusative of thing(s), Act.13:41, 1Co.13:7; with dative of person(s) (to believe what one says), Mrk.16:[13, 14], 1Jn.4:1; τ. ψεύδει, 2Th.2:11; περί . . . ὅτι, Jhn.9:18; esp. and most frequently with reference to religious belief: absol., Mat.8:13, Mrk.5:36, Luk.8:50, Jhn.11:40, al.; before ὅτι, Mat.9:28, al.; with dative (see supr., and cf. DB, i, 829a), Jhn.3:12 5:24 6:30 8:31, Act.16:34, Gal.3:6" (LXX), 2Ti.1:12, 1Jn.5:10, al.; with prep., (expressing personal trust and reliance  as distinct from mere credence or belief; see M, Pr., l.with; DB, i, 829b), to believe in or on: ἐν (Psa.77 (78):22, al.), Mrk.1:15 (see Swete, in l.); εἰς, Mat.18:6, Jhn.2:11 (see Westc., in l.), and freq., Act.10:43 19:4, Rom.10:14, Gal.2:16, Php.1:29, I Jhn.5:10, 1Pe.1:8; εἰς τ. ὄνομα, Jhn.1:12 2:23 3:18, 1Jn.5:13; ἐπί, with accusative, Mat.27:42, Act.9:42 11:17 16:31 22:19, Rom.4:5; ἐπί, with dative, Rom.9:33 (LXX) 10:11 (ib.), 1Ti.1:16, 1Pe.2:6" (LXX) ; ptcp. pres., οἱ π., as subst., Act.2:44, Rom.3:22, 1Co.1:21, al.; aor., Mrk.16:[16], Act.4:32; pf., Act.19:18 21:20 (on Johannine use of the tenses of π., see Westc, Epp. Jo., 120).
__2. Trans., to entrust: with accusative and dative, Luk.16:11, Jhn.2:24; pass., to be entrusted with: with accusative, Rom.3:2, 1Co.9:17, Gal.2:7, 1Th.2:4 (see Lft., Notes, 21f.), 1Ti.1:11, Tit.1:3.

πίστις, -εως, ἡ
(πείθω), [in LXX chiefly for אֱמוּנָה ;]
__1. in active sense, faith, belief, trust, confidence, in NT always of religious faith in God or Christ or spiritual things: Mat.8:10, Luk.5:20, Act.14:9, Rom.1:8, 1Co.2:5, 2Co.1:24, 1Ti.1:5, al.; with genitive obj., Mrk.11:22, Act.3:16, Rom.3:22, Gal.2:16, Eph.3:12, Jas.2:1, al.; with prep., ἐν, Rom.3:25, Gal.3:26, Eph.1:15, Col.1:24, 1Ti.1:14 3:13, 2Ti.1:13 3:15, 2Pe.1:1; εἰς, Act.20:21 24:24 26:18, Col.2:5, 1Pe.1:21; πρός, 1Th.1:8, Phm 5; ἐπί, with accusative Heb.6:1; ἐν τῇ π. στήκειν (εἶναι, μένειν), 1Co.16:13, 1Co.13:5, 1Ti.2:15; ὑπακοὴ τῆς π., Rom.1:5 16:26; ὁ ἐκ π., Rom.3:26 4:16, Gal.3:12; διὰ (τῆς) π., Rom.3:30, Gal.2:16, Php.3:9. By meton., objectively, that which is the object or content of belief, the faith: Act.6:7 14:22, Gal.1:23 3:23 6:10, Php.1:26, 27 Ju 3, 20, and perh. also Act.13:8 16:5, Rom.1:5 and 16:26 (see supr.), 1Co.16:13, Col.1:23, 2Th.3:2 (Lft., Notes, 125), 1Ti.1:19 3:9 4:1, 6 5:8 6:10, 12, 2Ti.3:8 4:7 Tit.1:4, 13 3:15, 1Pe.5:9.
__2. In passive sense,
__(a) fidelity, faithfulness: Mat.23:23, Gal.5:22; ἡ π. τοῦ θεοῦ, Rom.3:3;
__(b) objectively, plighted faith, a pledge of fidelity: 1Ti.5:12. (On the various shades of meaning in which the word is used in NT, see esp. ICC on Rom.1:17, pp. 31ff.; Lft., Ga., 154ff.; Stevens, Th. NT, 422, 515ff.; DB, i, 830ff.; Cremer, see word)

__I. Pass., to be trusted or believed;
__1. of persons, trusty, faithful : Mat.24:45 25:21, 23 Luk.12:42, Act.16:15, 1Co.4:2 4:17 7:25, Eph.1:1 6:21, Col.1:2, 7 4:7, 9, 1Ti.1:12, 2Ti.2:2, Heb.2:17 3:2, 5, 1Pe.5:12, Rev.2:13 19:11; of God, 1Co.1:9 10:13, 2Co.1:18, 1Th.5:24, 2Th.3:3, Heb.10:23 11:11, 2Ti.2:13, 1Jn.1:9, 1Pe.4:19; before ἐν, Luk.16:10-12 19:17, 1Ti.3:11; ἐπί, with accusative, Mat.25:23; ἄχρι θανάτου, Rev.2:10; ὁ μάρτυς ὁ π., Rev.1:5; id. καὶ ἀληθινός, Rev.3:14.

__2. As subst., pl. masc, πολλοί, many (persons): Mat.7:22, Mrk.2:2, al.; with genitive partit., Mat.3:7, Luk.1:16, al.; before ἐκ, Jhn.7:31, Act.17:12; with art., οἱ π., the many, Mat.24:12, Rom.12:5, 1Co.10:17, 33 2Co.2:17; opposite to ὁ εἶς (Lft., Notes, 291), Rom.5:15, 19; neut. pl., πολλά: Mat.13:3, Mrk.5:26, al.; accusative with adverbial force, Mrk.1:45, Rom.16:6 (Deiss., LAE, 317), 1Co.16:12, Jas.3:2, al.; neut. sing., πολύ: Luk.12:48; adverbially, Mrk.12:27, al.; πολλοῦ (genitive pret.), Mat.26:9; with compar. (Bl., §44, 5), π. σπουδαιότερον, 2Co.8:22; πολλῷ πλείους, Jhn.4:41.
Compar., πλείων
, neut., πλεῖον and πλέον (see WH, App., 151), pl., πλείονες, -ας, -α, contr., πλείους, -ω (cf. Mayser, 69), more, greater;
__1. as adj.: Jhn.15:2, Act.18:2o, Heb.3:3; before παρά, Heb.11:4 (cf. Westc, in l. Was ΠΛΙΟΝΑ here a primitive error for ΗΔΙΟΝΑ ?); pi., Act.13:31, al.; with genitive compar., Mat.21:36; with num. (ἤ of comp. omitted), Act.4:22 24:11, al.
__2. As subst., οἱ π., the greater number: Act.10:32 27:12, 1Co.10:5 15:6; also (Bl., §44, 3) others, more, the more: 2Co.2:6 4:15, Php.1:14; πλείονα, Luk.11:53; πλειον, πλέον, Mat.20:10, 2Ti.3:9; with genitive comp., Mk  12:43, Luk.21:3; π. Ἰωνᾶ ὧδε, Mat.12:41; adverbially, Act.4:17 20:9 24:4.
__3. As adv., πλεῖον: before ἤ, Luk.9:13; with genitive comp., Mat.5:20; πλείω: with num., Mat.26:53.
Superl., πλεῖστος, -η, -ον
, __(a) prop., most: Mat.11:20 21:8; adverbially, τὸ π., 1Co.14:27;
__(b) elative (M, Pr., 79), very great: ὄχλος π., Mrk.4:1.

Abbott-Smith / STEPBible (TBESG)
πλέον, see: πολύς.
πολύς, πολλή, πολύ,
[in LXX chiefly for רַב and cognate forms ;]
__1. as adj., much, many, great, of number, space, degree, value, time, etc.: ἀριθμός, Act.11:21; ὄχλος, Mrk.5:24; θερισμός, Mat.9:37; χόρτος, Jhn.6:10; χρόνος, Mat.25:19; γογγυσμός, Jhn.7:12; πόνος, Col.4:13; δόξα, Mat.24:30; σιγή, Act.21:40; pl., προφῆται, Mat.13:17; ὄχλοι, Mat.4:25; δαιμόνια, Mrk.1:34; δυνάμεις, Mat.7:22,
__2. As subst., pl. masc, πολλοί, many (persons): Mat.7:22, Mrk.2:2, al.; with genitive partit., Mat.3:7, Luk.1:16, al.; before ἐκ, Jhn.7:31, Act.17:12; with art., οἱ π., the many, Mat.24:12, Rom.12:5, 1Co.10:17, 33 2Co.2:17; opposite to ὁ εἶς (Lft., Notes, 291), Rom.5:15, 19; neut. pl., πολλά: Mat.13:3, Mrk.5:26, al.; accusative with adverbial force, Mrk.1:45, Rom.16:6 (Deiss., LAE, 317), 1Co.16:12, Jas.3:2, al.; neut. sing., πολύ: Luk.12:48; adverbially, Mrk.12:27, al.; πολλοῦ (genitive pret.), Mat.26:9; with compar. (Bl., §44, 5), π. σπουδαιότερον, 2Co.8:22; πολλῷ πλείους, Jhn.4:41.
Compar., πλείων
, neut., πλεῖον and πλέον (see WH, App., 151), pl., πλείονες, -ας, -α, contr., πλείους, -ω (cf. Mayser, 69), more, greater;
__1. as adj.: Jhn.15:2, Act.18:2o, Heb.3:3; before παρά, Heb.11:4 (cf. Westc, in l. Was ΠΛΙΟΝΑ here a primitive error for ΗΔΙΟΝΑ ?); pi., Act.13:31, al.; with genitive compar., Mat.21:36; with num. (ἤ of comp. omitted), Act.4:22 24:11, al.
__2. As subst., οἱ π., the greater number: Act.10:32 27:12, 1Co.10:5 15:6; also (Bl., §44, 3) others, more, the more: 2Co.2:6 4:15, Php.1:14; πλείονα, Luk.11:53; πλειον, πλέον, Mat.20:10, 2Ti.3:9; with genitive comp., Mk  12:43, Luk.21:3; π. Ἰωνᾶ ὧδε, Mat.12:41; adverbially, Act.4:17 20:9 24:4.
__3. As adv., πλεῖον: before ἤ, Luk.9:13; with genitive comp., Mat.5:20; πλείω: with num., Mat.26:53.
Superl., πλεῖστος, -η, -ον
, __(a) prop., most: Mat.11:20 21:8; adverbially, τὸ π., 1Co.14:27;
__(b) elative (M, Pr., 79), very great: ὄχλος π., Mrk.4:1.
(AS)
