πλείων,
πλέων, ὁ, ἡ, neuter πλεῖον, πλέον, πλεῖν, comparative of πολύς (on the forms see entry near the end), more, of number, size, extent, etc., οἱ δὲ μάχονται παυρότεροι πλεόνεσσι [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 13.739; πλείων μὲν πλεόνων μελέτη 8th-7th c.BC: Hesiodus Epicus “Opera et Dies” 380]]; ἐς πλείονας οἰκεῖν govern for the interest of the majority, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 2.37]]; πλέον᾽ ἔλπομαι λόγον Ὀδυσσέος ἢ πάθαν greater than.., [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “N.” 7.21]]; τὸν πλείω λόγον all further speech, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Trachiniae” 731; ὁ ὄχλος πλείων καὶ πλείων ἐπέρρει 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 7.5.39]]; πλείω τὸν πλοῦν.. ποιησάμενοι having made the voyage longer, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 8.39]]; ὁ π. βίος a longer life, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Timaeus” 75c; μακροτέρα καὶ π. ὁδός [prev. author] “R.” 435d, etc.]]; of Time, longer, π. χρόνος [Refs 8th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 9.111, 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Antigone” 74; πλέων νὺξ τῶν δύο μοιράων 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 10.252.]]

__2
with Article, οἱ πλέονες the greater number, the mass or crowd,[Refs 8th c.BC+ [5.673, 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 2.277; οἱ πλεῦνες 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.106, etc.: with _genitive_, τὰς πλεῦνας τῶν γυναικῶν [prev. work] 1]]; the people, opposed to the chief men, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. author] 7.149, 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 8.73, 89, etc.]]; euphemistic of the dead, ἀνεστηκυῖα παρὰ τῶν πλειόνων [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Ecclesiazusae” 1073; εὖτ᾽ ἂν ἵκηαι ἐς πλεόνων “Anthologia Graeca” 11.42 (1st c.BC-1st c.AD: Crinagoras Epigrammaticus)]]; ἐς πλεόνων μετοικεσίην[Refs 1st c.AD+ [[prev. work] 7.731 (1st c.AD: Leonidas Alexandrinus Epigrammaticus)]]; τὸ πλεῖον πολέμοιο the greater part of.., [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 1.165]]; ὅστις τοῦ πλέονος μέρους χρῄζει, opposed to τοῦ μετρίου, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Coloneus” 1211 (Lyric poetry); τοῦ πλέονος ἐλπίδι ὀρέγονται 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 4.17, compare 92.]]

__II
peculiar usages of neuter:

__II.1
as a Noun, more, πλεῦν ἔτι τούτου [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 2.19, etc.; εἴ τι ἐνορῶ πλέον [prev. author] 1.89]]; τὸ δὲ π. nay, what is more, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Supplices” 158 (Musgr. for τί δὲ..)]]; to a greater extent, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 1.90, 7.57, etc.]]; πλέον or τὸ πλέον τινός a higher degree of a thing, τίς πλέον τᾶς εὐδαιμονίας φέρε; [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Tyrannus” 1189 (Lyric poetry); τὸ π. τοῦ χρόνου 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 1.118, etc.]]; also τὸ π. ὃ ἀναφέρει the excess which he reports, [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [“PCair.Zen.” 661 (3rd c.BC)]]; ᾧ πλεῖον the excess, probably in [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [“PPetr.” 2p.42 (3rd c.BC),compare “PCair.Zen.” 742.26 (3rd c.BC)]]; πλέον ἔχειν to have the advantage, have the best of it, like{πλεονεκτέω}, with genitive, [Refs 6th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 9.70, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 343d, 349b, etc.; τὸ π. πάντων ἔχειν 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 1.3.18: more fully, μοίρης πλεῖον ἔχειν 6th c.BC: Theognis Elegiacus 606; π. τινὸς φέρεσθαι 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 8.29; π. φέρεσθαι τῶν ἄλλων 5th-6th c.BC: Andocides Orator 4.4, etc.]]; π. ποιεῖν do some good, be successful, βουλοίμην ἂν πλέον τί με ποιῆσαι ἀπολογούμενον [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Apologia” 19a]]; οὐδὲν π. ποιήσειν, -ῆσαι, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Andocides Orator 1.149, 4.7, compare 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Phaedo” 115c, etc.; παραινοῦσ᾽ οὐδὲν ἐς π. ποιῶ 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Tyrannus” 918; οὐδὲν π. ὀψοφαγῶν ποιήσεις 2nd c.AD: Athenaeus Epigrammaticus 8.344b; οὐδὲν εἴργασμαι π. 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Hippolytus” 284; οὐδὲν π. πρᾶξαι [prev. author] “IA” 1373, 5th-6th c.BC: Andocides Orator 4.20, etc.]]; οὐδὲν ἐπίσταμαι π. have no superior knowledge, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Theaetetus” 161b]]; τί πλέο; what more, i.e. what good or use is it? [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Antipho Orator 5.95, etc.; τί π. πλουτεῖν.. πάντων ἀποροῦντα; 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Plutus” 531; τί σοι π. λυπουμένῃ γένοιτ᾽ ἄ; 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Helena” 322; τί π. ἔστ᾽ εἰς τέκνα πονεῖ; “Supp.epigram” 1.567.1 (Karanis, 3rd c.BC),compare “Anthologia Graeca” 7.261.1 (3rd c.BC(?): Diotimus Epigrammaticus); also οὐδὲν ἦν π. τοῖς πεπονθόσιν 5th c.BC: Lysias Orator 19.4 (= 5th-6th c.BC: Andocides Orator 1.7), compare 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 35.31; ὧν οὐδέν μοι π. γέγονε 5th-6th c.BC: Isocrates Orator 15.28; οὐδέν γέ σοι π. ἔσται 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 341a; τί τὸ π.; “epigram Gr.” 306 a. 3]]; ἐπὶ πλέον as adverb, more, further, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 2.171, 5.51, 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 6.54, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Phaedrus” 261b, etc.]]: with genitive, beyond, ἐπὶ π. τῶν ἄλλων ἰσχύσας [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 1.9 (but, ἐπὶ τὸ π. ἵκεο μοίσας]]to surpassing height in.., [Refs 5th c.BC+ [3rd c.BC: Theocritus Poeta Bucolicus 1.20); also ὅταν τις ἐς π. πέσῃ τοῦ θέλοντος 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Coloneus” 1219 codices (Lyric poetry)]]; περὶ πλείονος ποιεῖσθαι, see at {περί} [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus IV.]]

__II.2
as adverb, more, rather, π. ἔφερέ οἱ ἡ γνώμη κατεργάσεσθαι τὴν Ἑλλάδα he inclined rather to the belief.., [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 8.100; οὐ τοῦτο δειμαίνεις π.; 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Prometheus Vinctus” 41; σέ.. τῶνδ᾽ ἐς πλέον σέβω 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Tyrannus” 700; ἢ π. ἢ ἔλαττον 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 18.125]]; π. ἔλαττον more or less, [Refs 6th c.AD+ [“BGU” 402.9 (6th c.AD), “IG” 14.177 (from Syracuse)]]; also τὸ π., Ionic dialect τὸ πλεῦν, for the most part, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 1.81, etc.]]; αὐτῆς τὸ π. μέτοχός εἰμι have the larger share, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 3.52]]; τὸ π., ={μᾶλλον, οὐ χάριτι τὸ π. ἢ φόβῳ} [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 1.9, compare 2.37]]; ἐστὶν ὁ πόλεμος οὐχ ὅπλων τὸ π., ἀλλὰ δαπάνης not so much.., as.., [Refs [[prev. author] 1.83.]]

__II.2.b
with Numerals, τοξότας π. ἢ εἴκοσι μυριάδας [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 2.1.6; οἶκος πλέον ἢ τεττάρων ταλάντων 4th c.BC: Isaeus Orator 10.23]]; ἐν πλέον ἢ διακοσίοις ἔτεσι variant in [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 24.141 (perhaps πλεῖν, see below)]]; π. ἢ ἐν διπλασίῳ χρόνῳ [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Oeconomicus” 21.3:—in this sense a short form πλεῖν is used by _Attic dialect_ writers (cf. Moer. p.294]] P., but the rule is not universal,[Refs 5th c.BC+ [compare “IG” 22.657.25 (3rd c.BC), etc.), πλεῖν ἢ τριάκονθ᾽ ἡμέρας 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Acharnenses” 858]]; πλεῖν ἢ χιλίας (i.e. δραχμάς) [Refs [[prev. author] “Eq.” 444; στάδια πλεῖν ἢ χίλια [prev. author] “Av.” 6, compare “Nu.” 1041, 1065, +others; πλεῖν ἤ γε διπλοῦν [prev. author] “Lys.” 589; πλεῖν ἢ 'νιαυτῷ πρεσβύτερος [prev. author] “Ra.” 18, compare 91]]; πλεῖν (πλεῖον codices) ἢ πέντε τάλαντα [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 21.173; πλεῖν ἢ δυοῖν ποδοῖν 4th c.BC: Eubulus Comicus 119.10]]; ἤ is frequently omitted, πλεῖν ἑξακοσίας [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Aves” 1251]]; ἔτη γεγονὼς πλείω ἑβδομήκοντα variant in [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Apologia” 17d]]; but δέκα πλείοσιν ἔτεσι for ten years more, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. author] “Lg.” 932c; τρεῖς μῆνας καὶ πλείω 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Historia Graeca (Hellenica)” 2.2.16; λίθους.. ὅσον μνααίους καὶ πλεῖον καὶ μεῖον [prev. author] “Eq.Mag.” 1.16]]: with number in genitive, κώμας.. οὐ πλεῖον εἴκοσι σταδίων ἀπεχούσας [Refs [[prev. author] “An.” 3.2.34, compare 7.3.12.]]

__II.2.c
Comedy texts, πλεῖν ἢ μαίνομαι more than to madness, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Ranae” 103, 751.]]

__II.2.d
plural πλείω used like{πλέον}, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 1.3, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 417b, 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 23.213, etc.; τὰ π. 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 1.81; πλέω 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Agamemnon” 868 codices]]

__II.2.e
regular adverb πλειόνως [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aeneas Tacticus 7.4, 1st c.AD: Josephus Historicus “Antiquitates Judaicae” 17.1.1.]]

__B
FORMS: Epic dialect use πλείων or πλέων as metre requires, also nominative and accusative plural πλέες, πλέᾰς, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 2.129, 11.395, Callias Epigrammaticus “Aet.Oxy.” 2080.85]] (so, with ι from ε, Cretan dialect πλίες, πλίας, [Refs [“Leg.Gort.” 7.18,24, “GDI” 5125 B 8, also πλίαδ (δὲ) “Leg.Gort.” 7.29, πλίανς [prev. work]5.54]]; πλέας also Aeolic dialect, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [“IG” 12(2).1.9 (Mytil., 4th c.BC))]]; dative plural πλεόνεσσι [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 13.739 (πλεόνεσιν]] is falsa lectio in [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 7.224); Cretan dialect also _accusative_ _sing._ _neuter_ πλίον “Leg.Gort.” 1.37, +others, _genitive_ πλίονος [prev. work]2.39, +others, _neuter_ _plural_ πλίονα [prev. work]4.51, πλία [prev. work]10.17]]; Aeolic dialect πλήων Hdn.Gr.2.431, also late Doric dialect, [Refs 1st c.AD+ [“IPE” 12.79.18 (Byzant., 1st c.AD)]]; Attic dialect Inscrr. have -ει- always before -ου- and -ω-, [Refs [“IG” 12.76.7, 22.657.25, 2498.22, etc., but -ε- and -ει- before -ο-, [prev. work]12.94.33,40.3,4, 22.2670.4 (but always πλέον).]]

__2

__II
metaphorically, devise, contrive, mostly of tortuous means, π. δόλον ἀμφί τινι [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Choephori” 220: proverbial, δεινοὶ πλέκειν τοι μηχανὰς Αἰγύπτιοι [prev. author] “fragment” 373; so π. πλοκάς 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Ion” 826]]; ἐκ τέχνης τέχνην[Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. work] 1280; παντοίας παλάμας 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Vespae” 644 (Lyric poetry)]]:—passive, μηχανὴ πεπλεγμένη [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Andromache” 995.]]

__II.2
of Poets, π. ὕμνον, ῥήματα, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “O.” 6.86, “N.” 4.94; ᾠδάς 5th c.BC: Critias Philosophus, Tragicus, Elegiacus “fragment” 1 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator; π. λόγους 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Rhesus” 834, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Hp.Mi.” 369b]]; form the plot of a tragedy, opposed to λύειν, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Poetica” 1456a9:]] —hence in passive, μῦθοι πεπλεγμένοι complex, opposed to ἁπλοῖ, [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [[prev. work] 1452a12, compare b32, 1459b9; συλλογισμὸς πεπλ. 2nd c.AD: Arrianus Historicus “Epicteti Dissertationes” 1.29.34; πέπλεκται [ἡ τῶν συμπάντων τῶν ὄντων νομοθεσία] ἐκ.. λόγων τε καὶ αἰτίων κτλ. 3rd c.AD: Plotinus Philosophus 4.3.15.]]

__2
with genitive, exceed, opposed to λείπω, [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd c.AD: Ptolemaeus Mathematicus “Geographia” 1.20.7: _absolutely_, τὸ -άζον ἔργον]] the extra work, [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [“PLille” 1v. 16 (3rd c.BC)]]; τοὺς -άζοντας τῶν ρκέ (i.e. ἐρίφους) the odd [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [25 out of 125, “PCair.Zen.” 422.7 (3rd c.BC).]]

__II
of persons, go beyond bounds, take or claim too much, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Isocrates Orator 2.33, 12.85, 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 9.24, 39.14]]: with dative, presume upon.., εὐτυχίᾳ [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 1.120; but π. κυνηγεσίαις]]go beyond bounds in.., [Refs 1st c.BC+ [1st c.BC-1st c.AD: Strabo Geographus 11.5.1]]; of a writer, τοῖς ὀνόμασι π. [Refs [[prev. author] 3.3.7]]: absolutely, to be lengthy, tedious, [LXX+1st c.BC+ [[prev. author] 9.1.16, 1st c.BC: Diodorus Siculus Historicus 1.90, LXX.2Mac.2.32]]; περί τινος Parmenisc. cited in [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd c.AD: Athenaeus Epigrammaticus 4.156d.]]

__II.2
π. τινός have an excess of, abound in a thing, opposed to ἐνδεὴς εἶναι, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Politica” 1257a33, compare 4th-3rd c.BC: Epicurus Philosophus “Sententiae” 4]]; but π. τοῦ καιροῦ exceed all bounds.., of a writer, [Refs 1st c.BC+ [1st c.BC: Dionysius Halicarnassensis “de Compositione Verborum” 22.]]

__III
with accusative, state at a higher figure, [Refs 1st c.BC+ [1st c.BC-1st c.AD: Strabo Geographus 6.3.10]]:—passive, to be magnified, exaggerated, [νομίσειεν ἂν] ἔστιν ἃ πλεονάζεσθαι [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 2.35, compare 1st c.BC-1st c.AD: Strabo Geographus 2.4.3]]; πεπλεόνασται has been overdone, opposed to ἐνδεὲς πεποίηται, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Hippocrates Medicus “περὶ ἀγμῶν” 7, compare “Art.” 47.]]

make to increase, τινὰς τῇ ἀγάπῃ [NT.1Thes.3.12.]

__III.3
eat in too great quantity, τι [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [3rd c.BC: Diphilus Siphnius Rerum Naturalium Scriptor cited in 2nd c.AD: Athenaeus Epigrammaticus 8.356d, 1st c.AD: Dioscorides (Dioscurides) Medicus 4.75, 82 (all _passive_).]]

__II.4
metaphorically, ταύτης ἔπι πλέοντες ὀρθῆς while [the ship of] our country bearing us is on an even keel, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Antigone” 190]]; οὐδ᾽ ὅπως ὀρθὴ πλεύσεται (i.e. ἡ πόλις) προείδετο [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 19.250; πάντα ἡμῖν κατ᾽ ὀρθὸν πλεῖ 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Leges” 813d; θεοῦ θέλοντος κἂν ἐπὶ ῥιπὸς πλέοις 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Fragmenta” 397; also κέρδους ἕκατι κἂν ἐπὶ ῥιπὸς πλέοι 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Pax” 699. τύπτει τὰς ἴσας πληγὰς ἐμοί 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Ranae” 636]]; τύπτεσθαι τῇ δημοσίᾳ μάστιγι ν πληγάς Legal cited in [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aeschines Orator 1.139; πολλὰς πληγὰς μαστιγούσθω 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Leges” 914b (but in such phrases πληγήν or πληγάς]] is frequently omitted, τρίτην ἐπενδίδωμι [NT+5th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Agamemnon” 1386; καιρίῃ (i.e. πληγῇ) τετύφθαι [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 3.64; πληγὰς ὑπομένειν 4th c.BC: Aristopho Comicus 4.6; εἰληφέναι καὶ δεδωκέναι πληγάς 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 54.14]]; πλῆθος, -ους, τό
[in LXX chiefly for רֹב, also for הָמוֹן, etc. ;]
__1. a great number, a multitude;
__(a) of things : ἰχθύων, Luk.5:6, Jhn.21:6; φρυγάνων, Act.28:3; ἁμαρτιίῶν, Jas.5:20, 1Pe.4:8; τ. πλήθει, in multitude, Heb.11:12;
__(b) of persons: Act.21:22 (WH, R, om.); with genitive, Luk.2:13, Jhn.5:3, Act.5:14; π. πολύ (πολὺ π.), Mrk.3:7-8; id. with genitive, Luk.6:17 23:27, Act.14:1 17:4
__2. πλῆθος, εος, τό,
Doric dialect and [Refs 4th c.AD+ [4th c.AD(?): Arcadius Grammaticus]] πλῆθος [Refs 5th c.BC+ [“Schwyzer” 84.8, +others (Argive, found in Crete, 5th c.BC), “IG” 5(2).6.20 (Tegea, 4th c.BC), etc.]]; Boeotian dialect πλεῖθος [Refs [[prev. work]7.3171.46 (Orchom. _Boeotian dialect_)]]; pseudo-Doric dialect and pseudo-Aeolic dialect πλᾶθος [Refs 1st c.BC+ [“GDI” 5176.21 (from Crete), “IGRom.” 4.1302.18 (Cyme, 1st c.BC/ 1st c.AD), Hippodamus Pythagoreus cited in 5th c.AD: Stobaeus, Joannes 4.1.93: (πλήθω,]] see at {πίμπλημι}):—great number, multitude, especially of people, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 17.330, 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 7.49, etc.]]; στρατοῦ π., periphrastic for στρατὸς πολύς, [Refs [[prev. author] 9.73]]; ὡς πλήθει for the mass of men, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 389d.]]

__2
τὸ π. the greater number, the mass, main body, τὸ π. τοῦ στρατοῦ [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.82, compare 5.92]]; τὸ π. τῆς ψυχῆς the largest part of.., [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Leges” 689a]]: as Noun of Multitude with plural Verb, Ἀθηναίων τὸ π. οἴονται [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 1.20]]; τὸ π. ἐψηφίσαντο πολεμεῖν the majority,[Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. work] 125, compare 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 2.4.20]]; τῷ π. by a majority, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [Berl.Sitzb. 1927.8 (_Locrian dialect_, 5th c.BC)]]: hence, people, population, σμικρὸν τὸ π. τῆσδε γῆς [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Phoenissae” 715.]]

__2.b
the commons, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 1.9, etc.; ἡ τοῦ π. ἀρχή, δημοκρατία τοὔνομα κληθεῖσα 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Politicus” 291d; ἐς τὸ π. φέρειν τὸ κράτος 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 3.81]]: frequently of the popular assembly, τὸ ὑμέτερον π., τὸ π. τὸ ὑμέτερον, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Lysias Orator 12.42, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Apologia” 31c]]; Ἐρυθραίων τῷ π., Ἀθηναίων τοῦ π., [Refs [“IG” 12.10.21, 22]]; = Latin plebs, [Refs 2nd c.BC+ [2nd c.BC: Polybius Historicus 6.15.11, 1st c.BC: Diodorus Siculus Historicus 12.25, 1st c.BC: Dionysius Halicarnassensis 4.71]]; also, association, corporation, or guild, τὸ π. τὸ Ἁλιαδᾶν [Refs [“IG” 12(1).155.6, 156.5 (from Rhodes)]]; τὸ τῶν Πανιαστῶν π. Ἡρακλῆο; 8th-7th c.BC: Hesiodus Epicus “Scutum Herculis” 74, compare 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Prometheus Vinctus” 914, “IG” 12.6.108, etc.: with γε, 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Electra” 909, etc.]]; ὑπεγγύους π. θανάτου liable to any punishment short of death, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 5.71]]; ἐπιτρέψαι περὶ σφῶν αὐτῶν π. θανάτου save in respect of death, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 4.54]]; σκυλεύειν τοὺς τελευτήσαντας π. ὅπλων of anything save their arms, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 469c]]; διαρπάσαι.. ἐπέτρεψε πλὴν ἀνδραπόδων to carry off all plunder save slaves, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 2.4.27.]]

__2
later, besides, in addition to, [LXX.Deu.18.8, 29.1.]

__B
conjunction:

__B.I
with single words and phrases, especially when a negative precedes, οὐκ ἆρ᾽ Ἀχαιοῖς ἄνδρες εἰσὶ π. ὅδ; [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Ajax” 1238; οὐκ οἶδα π. ἕν [prev. author] “OC” 1161, 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Electra” 752; οὐ κάτοιδα π. ἐπὶ σμικρὸν φράσαι 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Electra” 414, compare 4th c.BC: Amphis Comicus 13]]: after a question implying a negative, τί σοι πέπρακται π.τεύχειν κακ; [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Eumenides” 125, compare 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Antigone” 646: after πᾶς, etc., τὸ δ᾽ ἄρσεν αἰνῶ πάντα π. γάμου τυχεῖν 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Eumenides” 737; παντὶ δῆλον π. ἐμοί 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 529a, compare 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Philoctetes” 299, 5th-6th c.BC: Isocrates Orator 12.19, etc.; νικᾶν.. πανταχοῦ.. ἔφυν π. εἰς σέ 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Philoctetes” 1053 (πᾶς]] is sometimes omitted, θνῄσκουσι [πάντες] π. εἷς τις [Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. author] “OT” 118; ἀλλ᾽ ἔστι [πᾶσι] πλὴν σοί [prev. work] 370): frequently with ἄλλος (much like{ἤ}), τί οὖν μ᾽ ἄνωγας ἄλλο π. ψευδῆ λέγει; [prev. author] “Ph.” 100, compare “Aj.” 125, “Ant.” 236, 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Plutus” 106, 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 1.2.1, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Protagoras” 334b, etc.]]: after a comparative, ταῦτ᾽ ἐστὶ κρείσσω π. ὑπ᾽ Ἀργείοις πεσεῖν [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Heraclidae” 231, compare 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Minos” 318e, etc.; πάντα μᾶλλον π. αὐτὸς ἅψασθαι 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 21.179]]: after a superlative, τὸ μέγιστον εἴργται π. αἱ τάξεις τοῦ φόρου [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Respublica Atheniensium” 3.5.]]

__B.II
frequently joined with other Particles:

__B.II.1
π. εἰ, π. ἐάν, ὅταν,

__B.II.1.a
followed by a Verb, π. εἴ τις κωμῳδοποιὸς τυγχάνει ὤν [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Apologia” 18d, compare “Tht.” 177d, 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 3.18, 10.39, etc.; π. ὅταν 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Prometheus Vinctus” 260, 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Electra” 293, etc.; π. εἰ ἄρα μή 1st c.BC-1st c.AD: Strabo Geographus 7.3.8; π. ἐὰν μὴ ἐξέλθῃ 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Historia Animalium” 554b2.]]

__B.II.1.b
with Verb omitted, οὐδεὶς οἶδεν.., π. εἴ τις ἄρ᾽ ὄρνις [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Aves” 601, compare 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Historia Graeca (Hellenica)” 4.2.21, etc.]]; π. εἰ μή, after a negative, οὐδὲν προσδεησόμεθα, π. εἰ μὴ πάρεργόν τι [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Politicus” 286d (variant); οὐδὲν ἂν πάθοι.., π. εἰ μή που κατὰ συμβεβηκός 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “de Generatione et Corruptione” 323b26; οὐ δεῖ.. τοῦτο.. κινεῖσθαι, π. εἰ μὴ κατὰ σ. [prev. author] “de An.” 406b8, compare “APr.” 43a39, 4th-3rd c.BC: Theophrastus Philosophus “de Causis Plantarum” 1.10.6, 1st c.BC: Dionysius Halicarnassensis 4.74.—The pleonastic phrase π. εἰ μή is censured by 2nd c.AD: Lucianus Sophista “Sol.” 7.]]

__B.II.2
πλὴν ἤ (where ἤ adds nothing to the sense; πλὴν εἰ is a common variant), οὐκ ἄλλῳ π. ἢ Προδίκῳ [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Nubes” 361, compare 734; οὐδὲν κάκιον.., πλὴν ἄρ᾽ ἢ γυναῖκες [prev. author] “Th.” 532, compare 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 2.111, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Apologia” 42a (variant{π. εἰ})]]; also οὐ τὸν ἄνθρωπον ὑγιάζει π. ἀλλ᾽ ἢ.. [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Metaphysica” 981a18 (variant).]]

__B.II.3
π. οὐ only not, πάντες προσδέχονται, π. οὐχ οἱ τύραννοι [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Hiero” 1.18 (variant cited in 2nd c.AD: Athenaeus Epigrammaticus 4.144d), compare “Lac.” 15.6, 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 18.45, 56.23, “Berl.Sitzb.” [prev. cited]]]

__B.II.4
π. ὅτι except that.., save that.., καίτοι τί διαφέρουσιν ἡμῶν ἐκεῖνοι, π. ὅτι ψηφίσματ᾽ οὐ γράφουσι; [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Nubes” 1429; π. ἢ ὅτι 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 4.189]]; πλήν γε ὅτι, πλήν γε δὴ ὅτι, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Theaetetus” 183a, “Phd.” 57b]]; after ὁμοίως, τὰ αὐτά, [Refs 1st c.AD+ [1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus “Pelopidas” 4, 2nd c.AD: Artemidorus Daldianus Onirocriticus 1.56.]]

__B.II.5
π. ὅσον except or save so far as.., παρήκουσι παρὰ πᾶσαν [τὴν Λιβύην].., π. ὅσον Ἕλληνες.. ἔχουσι [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 2.32, compare 1st c.BC: Dionysius Halicarnassensis 1.23; π. ὅσα 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 456a; π. καθόσον 2nd-3rd c.AD: Dio Cassius Historicus 72.19; π. καθόσον εἰ 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 6.88 codices]]

__B.II.5.b
without a Verb, πάντων ἐρήμους, π. ὅσον τὸ σὸν μέρος save so far as thou art concerned, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Tyrannus” 1509]]; τοὺς πολλοὺς ἀπέκτειναν π. ὅσον ἐκ τριῶν νεῶν οὓς ἐζώγρησαν except only.., [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 7.23, compare 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Leges” 670a, 856d; ἀληθευτικός, π. ὅσα μὴ δι᾽ εἰρωνείαν 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Ethica Nicomachea” 1124b30.]]

__B.III
introducing a clause, mostly preceded by οὐδείς, πᾶς, ἄλλος, save that, νῦν δ᾽ οὐδεμία πάρεστιν.., π. ἥ γ᾽ ἐμὴ κωμῆτις ἥδ᾽ ἐξέρχεται [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Lysistrata” 5, compare 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Trachiniae” 41, 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 1.8.20, etc.; οὐκ ἀντεξῄεσαν π. ἕως ἀκροβολισμοῦ 2nd c.BC: Polybius Historicus 1.18.2]]: without any such word preceding, only, albeit, ἀπέπεμπε κήρυκας ἐς τὴν Ἑλλάδα, π. οὔτε ἐς Ἀθήνας οὔτε ἐς Λακεδαίμονα ἀπέπεμπε [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 7.32, compare 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Coloneus” 1643, 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 8.70, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Protagoras” 328e, etc.]]

__B.III.2
to break off and pass to another subject, only, however, π. γνώριζε ἄτοπος ὤν [NT+3rd c.BC+ [“PCair.Zen.” 454.10 (3rd c.BC),compare 2nd c.BC: Polybius Historicus 1.69.14, 2.17.1, NT.1Cor.11.11, 2nd c.AD: Diogenes Oenoandensis Epicureus 8, 1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus “Pericles” 34, etc.]]: in late Prose, π. ἀλλά [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [[prev. author] “Pyrrh.” 5, 2nd c.AD: Lucianus Sophista “Prom.” 20, “DMort.” 13.3, 20.4, etc.; π. ἀλλά γε [prev. author] “Rh.Pr.” 24.]]

__B.III.3
simply for δέ, but, πολλὴν στρατιὰν ἀθροίσας, π. ἄπειρον μάχης [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd c.AD: Herodianus Grammaticus 3.4.1; δυστυχῶν μέν, π. ἀλλ᾽ Ἑλλήνων 3rd c.AD: Heliodorus Scriptor Eroticus 6.7. (Cogn. with πλησίος, πελάζω, compare ἔμπλην.)]]

πλήσσω,
[Refs 8th c.BC+ [2nd c.BC: Nicander Epicus “Alexipharmaca” 456, present used by 8th c.BC: Homerus Epicus and _Attic dialect_ writers only in _compound_ ἐκπλ- (compare πλήγνυμι)]]; Attic dialect πλήττω [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Physica” 224a33]]: future πλήξω [Refs 8th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Fragmenta - American Journal of Philology” 275, and late Prose, 2nd-3rd c.AD: Philostratus Sophista “Vita Apollonii” 5.39, (ἐπι-) 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 23.580, (ἐκ-) 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 436e, (κατα-) 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Respublica Lacedaemoniorum” 8.3:]]aorist ἔπληξα, Epic dialect πλῆξα, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 2.266, 8th-7th c.BC: Hesiodus Epicus “Theogonia” 855, 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 3.64, and later Greek, 1st c.AD: Josephus Historicus “Antiquitates Judaicae” 4.8.33, 1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus 2.233f, “BGU” 759.14 (2nd c.AD), etc.]]; Doric dialect πλᾶξα [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “N.” 1.49]]; never in Attic dialect [Refs 5th c.BC+ [(5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Iphigenia Aulidensis” 1579 is spurious) except in compounds ἐκ-, κατα- (which see)]]; in the simple Verb the future and aorist of πατάσσω or παίω are used instead, as also in [Refs [LXX:]]perfect πέπληγα, subjunctive πεπλήγῃ [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Aves” 1350]], infinitive πεπληγέναι [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 6.1.5]] (uncertain, but read by [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd c.AD: Athenaeus Epigrammaticus 1.15e)]], participle πεπληγώς [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 5.763, +others]] (also in passive sense in late writers, [LXX+1st c.AD+ [LXX.2Ch.29.9, 1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus “Lucullus” 31, 2nd c.AD: Lucianus Sophista “Trag.” 115, 4th c.AD(?): Quintus Smyrnaeus Epicus 5.91, etc.)]]; later perfect πέπληχα [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-3rd c.BC: Menander Comicus “Ἐπιτρέποντες” 485, “Sam.” 86, 1st c.AD: Josephus Historicus “Antiquitates Judaicae” 4.8.33]]: Epic dialect reduplicate aorist 2 ἐπέπληγον [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 5.504, πέπληγον 23.363, 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 8.264]]; infinitive πεπληγέμεν [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 16.728, 23.660]]; but participle πεπλήγοντες in present sense, [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [3rd c.BC: Callimachus Epicus “Hymnus in Jovem” 53, 4th-5th c.AD(?): Nonnus Epicus “Dionysiaca” 28.327:]] —middle, future πλήξομαι (κατα-) [Refs 2nd c.BC+ [2nd c.BC: Polybius Historicus 4.80.2, 1st c.BC: Dionysius Halicarnassensis 6.10, etc.:]]aorist ἐπληξάμην, Epic dialect πληξάμην, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [“hymnus ad Cererem” 245, 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 3.14]], and in late Prose, [Refs 2nd c.BC+ [1st c.AD: Josephus Historicus “Antiquitates Judaicae” 16.10.7, (κατα-) 2nd c.BC: Polybius Historicus 2.52.1, etc.]]; participle πληξάμενος [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 16.125]]: Epic dialect aorist 2 πεπλήγετο [Refs 8th c.BC+ [12.162, 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 13.198, πεπλήγοντο 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 18.51]]:—passive, present πλήσσομαι [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd c.AD: Ptolemaeus Mathematicus “Harmonica - Opera Mathematica” 1.1]]: future πληγήσομαι [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 2.3.10, 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 18.263 (but in _composition_ ἐκ-πλᾰγήσομαι)]]; also πεπλήξομαι [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Hippolytus” 894, 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Equites” 271, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Theaetetus” 180a]]: aorist ἐπλήχθην [Refs 5th c.BC+ [1st c.AD: Philo Judaeus 1.39, 1st c.AD: Dioscorides (Dioscurides) Medicus 1.93, “Placita Philosophorum” 4.14.3, but mostly ἐπλήγην, 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 5.120, 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Coloneus” 605, etc.]] (the former nowhere in Trag., except ἐκ-πληχθείς [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Troades” 183 (Lyric poetry))]]; participle πληγείς [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 8.12, 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Septem contra Thebas” 608, “Frr.” 139, 180, 5th c.BC: Antipho Orator 4.4.3, etc.; _Doric dialect_ πλᾱγείς (see. below 1.1a ad near the end)]]; Aeolic dialect πλάγεις [ᾱ] [Refs 7th c.BC+ [7th-6th c.BC: Alcaeus Lyricus “Supp.” 26.3]]; (ἐπλάγην [ᾰ] only in compounds ἐξ-, κατ-, of persons struck with terror or amazement): perfect πέπληγμαι [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.41, etc.]]—in Attic dialect and Trag., also LXX, the simple Verb is scarcely found except in future 2 and 3, aorist 2, and perfect passive, but future active is used once by [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus]], perfect [Refs 5th c.BC+ [2 πέπληγα by 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus and 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus (see. above); 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus uses the _active_ (_aorist_) only in 3.64, 78.]] —The _present_ πλήσσω, πλήσσομαι are unknown to Attic dialect writers (also to [LXX, exc. LXX.4Mac.14.19), who use the]present active and passive of παίω, τύπτω instead (see. entry his vv.); whereas the aorist 2 passive ἐπλήγην is used instead of ἐπαίσθην, ἐπατάχθην, or ἐτύφθην (ἐτύπην): hence παίσαντές τε καὶ πληγέντες [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Antigone” 172; πότερον πρότερος ἐπλήγην ἢ ἐπάταξα 5th c.BC: Lysias Orator 4.15]]; πατάξας καταβάλλω, opposed to πληγεὶς κατέπεσεν, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [[prev. author] 1.25,27; ὁ πληγεὶς ἀεὶ τῆς πληγῆς ἔχεται, κἂν ἑτέρωσε πατάξῃ τις, ἐκεῖσ᾽ εἰσὶν αἱ χεῖρες 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 4.40; ὅταν ὁ μὲν πληγῇ, ὁ δὲ πατάξῃ 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Ethica Nicomachea” 1132a8; πατάξαι ἢ πληγῆναι [prev. author] “Rh.” 1377a21; so in 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 21.33,38 the]]active πατάξαι corresponds with the passive πληγῆναι[Refs [in [prev. work] 36,39]]:—strike, smite, frequently in [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Homerus Epicus, especially of a direct blow, opposed to βάλλειν (οὔτε πληγέντα.., οὔτε βληθέντα 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 6.117), πλῆξεν.. κόρυθος φάλον 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 3.362; σκήπτρῳ δὲ μετάφρενον ἠδὲ καὶ ὤμω πλῆξεν 2.266, compare 16.791]]; πλήξας ξίφει αὐχένα[Refs 8th c.BC+ [[prev. work] 332; μή τις.. ἐμὲ χειρὶ βαρείῃ πλήξῃ 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 18.57, etc.; ἱστὸς.. πλῆξε κυβερνήτεω κεφαλήν 12.412]]: with accusative double person et of things, strike one on.., τὸν δ᾽ ἄορι πλῆξ᾽ αὐχένα [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 11.240, etc.; πλῆξ᾽ αὐτοσχεδίην 12.192]]; πεπληγὼς ἀγορῆθεν ἀεικέσσι πληγῇσιν having driven him with blows, [Refs [2.264]]; κῦμα.. μιν.. πλῆξεν struck him, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 5.431; πλοῖον, τό,
(πλέω) properly floating vessel: hence, generally, ship, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Septem contra Thebas” 602, “Ag.” 625, 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.168, “IG” 12.128.5, etc.: more nearly defined, π. λεπτά]] small craft, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 7.36, 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 2.83]]; π. ἁλιευτικόν a fishing-boat, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 7.1.20]]; ἱππαγωγὰ π. transports for horses, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 6.48]]; π. μακρά ships of war, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. author] 5.30, 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 1.14]]; π. στρογγύλα or φορτηγικά ships of burden, merchantmen, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Historia Graeca (Hellenica)” 5.1.21; μεγάλα π. 1st c.BC: Diodorus Siculus Historicus 13.78; ἱερὸν π. τοῦ Ὀσείριος “OGI” 56.51 (Canopus, 3rd c.BC): when distinguished from ναῦς,]] without adjective, mostly merchant-ship or transport, as opposed to ship of war, τοῖς π. καὶ ταῖς ναυσί [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 4.116, compare 6.44]]; πλεῖν μὴ μακρᾷ νηΐ, ἄλλῳ δὲ κωπήρει πλοίῳ Foed.[Refs 5th c.BC+ [cited in [same work] 4.118; πλοῖά τε καὶ τριήρεις 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Hp.Ma.” 295d]]; πλοῖα alone, ={τριήρεις}, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Historia Graeca (Hellenica)” 1.2.1, Docum. cited in 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 18.106.]]

πλόος, ὁ,

τὸ ἑαυτοῦ ἱμάτιον 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Charmides” 161e; τὰς κοιλίας 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Equites” 160; ἄμμον 4th-3rd c.BC: Theophrastus Philosophus “de Lapidibus” 58; ἐάν τις ἢ λόηται ἢ πλύνει τι ἐν ταῖς κρήναις “IG” 12(5).569.5 (Ceos, 3rd c.BC)]]; στολήν [LXX.Gen.49.11]:—passive, σησάμου πεπλυμένου [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [“PCair.Zen.” 562.19 (3rd c.BC)]]; σκίλλης πλυθείσης Porph. [prev. cited]

__b
metaphorically, πέπλυται τὸ πρᾶγμα the thing is washed to pieces, i. e. worn out, [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [3rd c.BC(?): Sosipater Comicus 1.3: hence τὸ πεπατημένον καὶ πεπλυμένον]]threadbare, hackneyed, [Refs 3rd c.AD+ [3rd c.AD: Longinus Rhetor “Ars Rhetorica” p.190H.]]

as a slang term, πλύνειν τινά 'give him a dressing', abuse, κἀκυκλοβόρει κἄπλυνε [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Acharnenses” 381; ἀλλήλους πλυνοῦμεν 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 39.11; πλύνοντες αὑτοὺς τἀπόρρητα [prev. author] 58.40; τὸν πατέρα καὶ σὲ τούς τε σοὺς ἐγὼ πλυνῶ 4th-3rd c.BC: Menander Comicus 608; τοὺς κρείσσονας 2nd-3rd c.AD: Dio Cassius Historicus 46.4: with _dative_ modi, τὸν τάριχον τουτονὶ πλύνων ἅπασιν ὅσα σύνοιδ᾽ αὐτῷ κακά 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Fragmenta” 200: with double_accusative_, πλυνεῖ τε τὰ κακὰ τῶν κακῶν ὑμᾶς 5th c.BC: Diocles Comicus 2. (πλῠ-ν-yω _cognate_ with πλε (ϝ) -ω,]] also with Lithuanian pláuti 'bathe', OSlavonic pluti 'flow', 'sail'.)

deep_entry:
Abbott-Smith / STEPBible (TBESG)
πνεῦμα, -τος, τό,
[in LXX chiefly and very frequently for רוּחַ ;]
__1. of air in motion;
__(a) wind: Jhn.3:8; pl., Heb.1:7 (LXX);
__(b) breath: π. ζωῆς, Rev.11:11; π. τοῦ στόματος, figuratively, 2Th.2:8 (cf. Ps 32 (33)6).
__2. Of the vital principle, the spirit (Arist., Polyb., al.): Luk.8:55, Jhn.19:30, Act.7:59, al.; opposite to σάρξ, Mat.26:41, Mrk.14:38, 1Co.5:5, al.; to σῶμα, Rom.8:10, 1Co.6:17 7:34, 1Pe.4:6; to ψυχή, Php.1:27, Heb.4:12; τὸ π. καὶ ἡ ψ. καὶ τ. σῶμα, 1Th.5:23 (M, Th., in l.); dative, τῷ π., in spirit, Mrk.2:8 8:12, Jhn.11:33 13:21, Act.18:25, Rom.12:11, 1Co.7:34, 1Pe.3:18, al.; of the human spirit of Christ, Rom.1:4, 1Ti.3:16.
__3. spirit, i.e. frame of mind, disposition, influence: Luk.1:17, Rom.8:15, 1Co.4:21, Gal 6:1, Eph.2:2, 2Ti.1:7, 1Jn.4:6, al.
__4. An incorporeal being, a spirit: Luk.24:37, 39 Act.23:8; π. ὁ θεός, God is spirit, Jhn.4:24; πατὴρ τῶν π., Heb.12:9; of disembodied human beings, Heb.12:23, 1Pe.3:19 (ICC, in l.; DB, iii, 795); of angels. Heb.1:14; of demons or evil spirits, Mat.8:16, Mrk.9:20, Luk.9:39, al.; π. πύθυωνα, Act.16:16; πνεύματα δαιμονίων, Rev.16:14; π. δαιμονίου ἀκαθάρτου, Luk.4:33; π. ἀσθενείας (Bl., §35, 5), Luk.13:11; π. ἀκάθαρτον, Mat.10:1, Mrk.1:23, Luk.4:36, Act.5:16; π. ἄλαλον (καὶ κωφόν), Mrk.9:17, 25; πονηρόν, Luk.7:21, Act.19:12, al.
__5. Of the Holy Spirit, π. ἅγιον, τὸ ἅ. π., τὸ π. τὸ ἅ. τὸ π., π. (the article as a rule being used when the Spirit is regarded as a Person or a Divine Power, and omitted when the reference is to an operation, influence or gift of the Spirit; see WM, 151:5; Bl., §46, 7): anarth., Mat.1:18 3:11, 16 4:1, Mrk.1:8 (Swete, in l.), ib.10, Luk.1:15, Jhn.7:39, Act.19:2, Rom.5:5, 1Co.2:4, al.; with art., Mat.4:1 12:31, 32 Mrk.1:10 3:29, Luk.2:26, Jhn.7:36 14:26, Act.4:31 5:3, Rom.8:16, al.; (τὸ) π. (τοῦ) θεοῦ, Mat.3:16, Rom.8:9, Eph.3:16, 1Jn.4:2, al.; τὸ π. τ. πατρός, Mat.10:20; π. θεοῦ ζῶντος, 2Co.3:3; (τὸ) π. τοῦ κυρίου, Luk.4:18, Act.5:9 8:39; τὸ π. Ἰησοῦ, Act.16:7; Χριστοῦ, Rom.8:9; Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ, Php.1:19; τὸ π. τ. ἀληθείας, Jhn.15:26 16:13, 1Jn.4:6; λείγει (μαρτυρεῖ) τὸ π. (τὸ ἅγιον), Act.21:11 28:25, 1Ti.4:1, Heb.3:7 10:15, Rev.14:13; before τ. ἐκκλησίαις,  Rev.2:7, 11 17, 29, 3:6, 12, 22; ἐν τ. π., Luk.2:27; κατὰ πνεῦμα, Rom.8:4, 5; ἐξ ὕδατος καὶ π., Jhn.3:5, διὰ πνεύματος αἰωνίου, Heb.9:14; ἐν ἁγιασμῷ πνεύματος, 2Th.2:13, 1Pe.1:2; ἓν π., 1Co.12:13, Eph.2:18 4:4; ὁ δὲ κύριος τὸ π. ἐστιν, 2Co.3:17; of that which is effected or governed by the Spirit, opposite to γράμμα, Rom.2:29 7:6, 2Co.3:6.
SYN.: νοῦς, which in NT is contrasted with π. as "the action of the understanding in man with that of the spiritual or ecstatic impulse" (DB, iv, 612); ψυχή — the usual term in cl. psychology—in NT, "expresses man as apart from God, a separate individual, π. expresses man as drawing his life from God" (DB, 1-vol., 872). (AS)

LSJ / STEPBible (TFLSJ)
πνεῦμα, ατος, τό,
(πνέω) blast, wind, first in [Refs 6th c.BC+ [6th c.BC: Anaximenes Philosophus 2, ὅλον τὸν κόσμον π. καὶ ἀὴρ περιέχει]]: frequently in Trag., etc., ἀνέμων πνεύματα πάντων [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Prometheus Vinctus” 1086 (_anapaest meter_), compare 1047 (_anapaest meter_)]]; θαλάσσας.. πνεύματι λάβρῳ [Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. author] “Pers.” 110 (Lyric poetry); πνευμάτων ἐπομβρίᾳ [prev. author] “fragment” 300.3; τέως δὲ κούφοις πνεύμασιν βόσκου 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Ajax” 558; πνεύμασιν θαλασσίοις ἐξωσθέντες 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Cyclops” 278 (but πνοή]] is commoner in Poets; [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Homerus Epicus uses πνοιή); πνεύματα ἀνέμων 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 7.16. ; τὸ π. κατῄει 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 2.84]]; κατὰ πρύμναν ἵσταται τὸ π.[Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. work] 97; τὸ π. λεῖον καὶ καθεστηκὸς λαβεῖν 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Ranae” 1003; τὸ π. ἔλαττον γίγνεται [prev. author] “Eq.” 441; εἰ φορὸν π. εἴη 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Historia Graeca (Hellenica)” 6.2.27]]; κατὰ πνεῦμα στῆναι τοῦ ἄρρενος to leeward of him, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Historia Animalium” 560b14]]; but κατὰ π. προσιόντες down wind, [Refs [[prev. work] 535a19]]; πνεύματος ἀνείλησις, ἐκπύρωσις, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-3rd c.BC: Epicurus Philosophus “Epistulae” 2pp.44,45 U.]]; as an element, air, [Refs 3rd c.AD+ [Corp.Herm. 1.9, 16; τὸ π. τὸ περὶ τὴν ψυχήν 3rd c.AD: Plotinus Philosophus 2.2.2, compare 3rd c.AD: Porphyrius Tyrius Philosophus “Sententiae ad intelligibilia ducentes” 29.]]

__2
metaphorically, θαλερωτέρῳ π. with more genial breeze or influence, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Septem contra Thebas” 708 (Lyric poetry); λύσσης π. μάργῳ [prev. author] “Pr.” 884 (_anapaest meter_)]]; αἰδοίῳ π. χώρας with air or spirit of respect on the part of the country, [Refs [[prev. author] “Supp.” 29 (_anapaest meter_)]]; π. ταὐτὸν οὔποτ᾽.. ἐν ἀνδράσιν φίλοις βέβηκεν the wind is constantly changing even among friends, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Coloneus” 612; π. συμφορᾶς 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Iphigenia Taurica” 1317; ὅταν θεοῦ σοι π. μεταβαλὸν τύχῃ [prev. author] “HF” 216.]]

__II
breathed air, breath, σάλπιγξ βροτείου πνεύματος πληρουμένη [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Eumenides” 568]]; αὐλῶν, λωτοῦ π., [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Bacchae” 128 (Lyric poetry), “Ph.” 787 (Lyric poetry, _plural_)]]; π. ἀπέρρηξεν βίου the breath of life, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Persae” 507; π. ἀπώλεσεν [prev. author] “Th.” 984 (Lyric poetry)]]; π. ἄθροισον collect breath, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Phoenissae” 851]]; π. ἀφεῖναι, ἀνεῖναι, μεθεῖναι, to give up the ghost, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. author] “Hec.” 571, “Or.” 277, “Tr.” 785 (_anapaest meter_); π. δειμαίνων λιπεῖν [prev. author] “Supp.” 554; π... δυσῶδες ἠφίει 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 2.49]]; πνεύματος διαρροαί the wind-pipe, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Hecuba” 567; τὰς τοῦ π. διεξόδους ἀποφράττον 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Timaeus” 91c (see. πνεύμων); πνεύματος ῥώμη 1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus 2.804b: proverbial, ἄνθρωπός ἐστι π. καὶ σκιὰ μόνον 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Fragmenta” 13.]]

__II.2
breathing, respiration, frequently in [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Hippocrates Medicus, π. πυκνόν, ἀραιόν, ἐκτεῖνον, κατεπεῖγον, “Epid.” 2.3.7; π. πυκνότερον “Acut.” 16]]; π. προσκόπτον checked, difficult breathing, Aph.[Refs [4.68]]; π. ἄσημον indistinct, feeble breathing, Epid.[Refs [6.7.8]]; π. βηχῶδες [Refs [“Coac.” 622]]; π. μετέωρον shallow breathing, Epid.[Refs [2.3.1]]; τὸ π. ἔχειν ἄνω to be out of breath, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-3rd c.BC: Menander Comicus 23, cf. Sosicrates Comicus 1]]; τὸ π. ἀνήνεγκαν recovered their breath, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Hippocrates Medicus “προρρητικόν” 2.12 (so without τὸ π. “Aph.” 2.43)]]; but ἀναφέρουσιν.. κλαίοντά τε καὶ ἐς τὰς ῥῖνας ἀνέλκοντα τὸ π. they sob.., [Refs [[prev. author] “Hebd.” 51.]]

__II.2.b
plural, of the air imagined as filling the veins, πνευμάτων ἀπολήψιες ἀνὰ φλέβας [Refs [[prev. author]]]Acut.(Sp.)[Refs [7, +others]]

__II.3
flatulence, in plural, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Eubulus Comicus 107.9, 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Problemata” 948b25, 1st c.AD: Dioscorides (Dioscurides) Medicus 2.112, 3rd c.AD(?): Diogenes Laertius 6.94.]]

__II.4
breath of life, π. ζωῆς [LXX+1st c.AD+ [LXX.Gen.6.17, 7.15, compare 1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus “Pericles” 13,etc.]]; π. ἔχειν retain life, [Refs 2nd c.BC+ [2nd c.BC: Polybius Historicus 31.10.4]]; living being, ἐγὼ Νίνος πάλαι ποτ᾽ ἐγενόμην π. [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [3rd c.BC: Phoenix Iambographus 1.16]]; οὐ π. πάντα βρότεια σοὶ (i.e. Πλούτωνι) νέμετα; [Refs [“IG” 14.769 (from Naples).]]

__II.5
that which is breathed forth or exhaled, odour, ὦ θεῖον ὀδμῆς π. [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Hippolytus” 1391]]; π. βαρὺ ἀφιεῖσα, of a tree, [Refs 1st c.AD+ [1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus 2.647b.]]

__II.6
Grammars, breathing with which a vowel is pronounced, [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [[prev. work] 1009e (_plural_), 2nd c.AD: Apollonius Dyscolus Grammaticus “de Adverbiis;” 147.18]]; π. δασύ, ψιλόν, [Refs [[prev. author] “Pron.” 78.6, “Adv.” 148.9.]]

__III
divine inspiration, ἄγρια.. πνεύματα θευφορίης [Refs 5th c.BC+ [“Anthologia Graeca” 6.220.4 (3rd c.BC: Dioscorides Epigrammaticus); εἰ μή τι θεῖον.. ἐνῆν π. τῇ ψυχῇ 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Axiochus” 370c; τὸ ἱερὸν καὶ δαιμόνιον ἐν μούσαις π. 1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus 2.605a; καθαρὸν δίκαιον.. π. θεοῦ σωτῆρος “BMus.Inscription” 1062 (Cyrene, 2nd c.AD).]]

__IV
the spirit of God, π. θεοῦ [LXX.Gen.1.2, etc.]: frequently in NT, τὸ π. τὸ ἅγιον [NT.Mark.3.29, +others]

__IV.2
spirit of man, εἴτ᾽ ἐστὶ τοῦτο π. θεῖον εἴτε νοῦς [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-3rd c.BC: Menander Comicus 482.3]]: in NT, opposed to ψυχή, [NT.1Thes.5.23, cf. NT.Rom.8.2]; τῷ π., opposed to τῷ σώματι, [NT.1Cor.5.3]; also, opposed to γράμμα, [NT.Rom.2.29.]

__V
spiritual or immaterial being, angel, [NT.Heb.1.14, NT.Rev.1.4]; τὰ ἄχραντα π., τὰ κακὰ π., [Refs 4th c.AD+ [4th c.AD: Iamblichus Philosophus “de Mysteriis” 3.31]]; π. πονηρόν, ψευδές, [LXX+NT+3rd c.AD+ [LXX.Judg.9.23, LXX.1Ki.22.21, cf. NT.Act.19.12, 15, NT.Rev.16.14, 3rd c.AD: Porphyrius Tyrius Philosophus cited in 4th c.AD: Eusebius Caesariensis Scriptor Ecclesiasticus “Praeparatio Evangelica” 4.23, etc.]]; ἀλάλου καὶ κακοῦ π. οὖσα πλήρης (i.e. ἡ Πυθία) [Refs 1st c.AD+ [1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus 2.438b.]]

__VI
Rhet., sentence declaimed in one breath, [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd c.AD: Hermogenes Rhetor “περὶ εὑρέσεως” 3.10, 4.4, +others]]

Abbott-Smith / STEPBible (TBESG)
πνευματικός, -ή, -όν
(πνεῦμα),
__1. of or caused by the wind, air or breath (Arist., al.).
__2. spiritual (opposite to σωματικός, Plut.);
__(a) of created beings : τὰ π. (RV, the spiritual hosts), Eph.6:12; of that which is related to the human spirit, opposite to ψυχικός, 1Co.15:44 15:46;
__(b) of that which belongs to or is actuated by the Divine Spirit;
__α of persons : 1Co.2:15 3:1 14:37, Gal.6:1; οἶκος π., figuratively, 1Pe.2:5;
__β of things : Rom.1:11 7:14, 1Co.2:13 10:3-4 12:1 14:1, Eph.1:3 5:19, Col.1:9 3:16, 1Pe.2:5; opposite to τ. σαρκικά, Rom.15:27, 1Co.9:11.†
SYN.: ψυχικός, which see, and cf. DB, ii, 410, iv, 612  (AS)

---

πνευμᾰτ-ικός, ή, όν,
of wind or air, κινήσεις [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Problemata” 916b4; βία π. [prev. author] “HA” 586a17; φύσεις 4th-3rd c.BC: Epicurus Philosophus “Epistulae” 2p.39U.; ἀέρος ψυχρότης 4th-3rd c.BC: Theophrastus Philosophus “de Causis Plantarum” 4.12.5]]; π. [ὄργανον] a machine moved by wind, [Refs 1st c.BC+ [1st c.BC: Vitruvius Scriptor de Architectura Latinus 10.1.1; μηχάνημα 2nd c.AD: Galenus Medicus “περὶ ψυχῆς παθῶν κτλ. - Galeni Scripta Minora” 2.3.]]

__2
of the nature of wind or air, τὰ π. [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Meteorologica” 380a23]]; π. ξηρότης, i. e. a dry vapour, [Refs 1st c.AD+ [1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus “Alexander” 35.]]

__2.b
of subtle substance, τὸ π. [Refs 1st c.BC+ [1st c.BC-1st c.AD: Strabo Geographus 1.3.5]]; οὐσία, opposed to ὑγρά, [Refs 1st c.AD+ [1st c.AD: Philo Judaeus 1.15, compare 2nd c.AD: Cleomedes Astronomus 1.8, 2nd c.AD: Galenus Medicus 7.596.]]

__3
inflated, distended with air, ὑστέραι [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Historia Animalium” 584b22.]]

__4
active (= πνευματώδης [Refs [1.3)]], causing flatulence, οἶνος [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [[prev. author] “Pr.” 955a35; βρώματα 3rd c.BC: Nicomachus Comicus 1.31, compare 3rd c.BC: Diphilus Siphnius Rerum Naturalium Scriptor cited in 2nd c.AD: Athenaeus Epigrammaticus 3.73a (_superlative_), 1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus 2.286e, 2nd c.AD: Soranus Medicus 1.52]]. adverb -κῶς by flatulence, [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd c.AD: Archigenes Medicus cited in 2nd c.AD: Galenus Medicus 12.537.]]

__5
breathing, exhaling, εὐοσμία [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-3rd c.BC: Theophrastus Philosophus “de Causis Plantarum” 6.16.3.]]

__II
of the breath or breathing, τὸ π. μόριον, ὁ π. τόπος, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “de Generatione Animalium” 781a31, “Pr.” 962a11.]]

__III
of spirit, spiritual, interpolated in [Refs 1st c.AD+ [1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus 2.129c]]; opposed to σαρκικός, ψυχικός, [NT.Rom.15.27, NT.1Cor.2.13, etc.] adverb -κῶς[Refs [[prev. work] 14.]]

__IV
οἱ Π. a school of physicians who referred all questions of health to pneumatic agencies, [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd c.AD: Galenus Medicus 8.749, 15.111.]]

__V
conveying πνεῦμα, κοιλία, of the left ventricle of the heart (opposed to αἱματική), [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [3rd c.BC: Erasistratus Medicus cited in [same work] “UP” 6.12, compare “Placita Philosophorum” 4.5.7.]]

__VI
Rhet., adverb -κῶς in one breath (compare πνεῦμα VI), ἀποτείνεσθαι [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd c.AD: Hermogenes Rhetor “περὶ εὑρέσεως” 4.1.]]

πνέω,
poetry πνείω as always in [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Homerus Epicus except 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 5.469:]]future πνεύσομαι (ἐκ-) [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Hercules Furens” 886 (Lyric poetry), (ἐμ-) [prev. author] “Andr.” 555, (παρα-) 5th c.BC: Hippocrates Medicus “γυναικεῖα” 2.133]]; also πνευσοῦμαι [LXX+5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Ranae” 1221, 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Meteorologica” 367a13, 4th-3rd c.BC: Theophrastus Philosophus “de Signis Tempestatum” 34, 4th c.AD: Palaephatus Paradoxographus 17; πνεύσω 4th-3rd c.BC: Theophrastus Philosophus “de Signis Tempestatum” 32, LXX.Psa.147.7(18), LXX.Sir.43.20, “Geoponica” 1.12.34, “Anthologia Graeca” 9.112 (1st c.BC: Antipater Thessalonicensis Epigrammaticus), (ἀνα-) 4th c.AD(?): Quintus Smyrnaeus Epicus 13.516 (συμ-πνευσόντων]] is falsa lectio in [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 18.169)]]: aorist 1 ἔπνευσα [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th-7th c.BC: Hesiodus Epicus “Opera et Dies” 506, 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 2.20, etc., (ἐν-) 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 17.456, (ἀν-) 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Ajax” 274:]]perfect πέπνευκα (ἐπι-) [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Phaedrus” 262d, (ἐκ-) 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Problemata” 904a1:]] —passive, future πνευσθήσομαι (δια-) [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd c.AD: Aretaeus Medicus “ὀξέων νούσων θεραπευτικόν” 1.1:]]aorist ἐπνεύσθην (δι-) [Refs 8th c.BC+ [4th-3rd c.BC: Theophrastus Philosophus “Historia Plantarum” 5.5.6, etc.— 8th c.BC: Homerus Epicus and early Prose writers use the simple Verb only in]]present and imperfect, to which Trag. add future and aorist 1 active —For the form ἄμπνυε, see. {ἀναπνέω}; for ἀμπνύνθη, -πνυτο, see at {ἄμπνυτο}; and for perfect passive πέπνῡμαι, participle πεπνῡμένος, see at {πέπνυμαι}.—Like other disyllable Verbs in -έω, this Verb contracts only εε, εε; but ἐκπνέων is disyllable in [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Agamemnon” 1493, 1517 (both Lyric poetry)]]:—blow, of wind and air, οὐδέ ποτ᾽ οὖροι πνείοντες φαίνονθ᾽ [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 4.361; αὔρη δ᾽ ἐκ ποταμοῦ ψυχρὴ πνέει 5.469; ἐτησίαι.. οὐκ ἔπνευσαν 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 2.20, etc.]]; τῷ πνέοντι (i.e. ἀνέμῳ or πνεύματι) [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd c.AD: Lucianus Sophista “Cont.” 3]]; ἡ πνέουσα (i.e. αὔρα) [NT.Act.27.40]; also of a flute-player, μέγα πνέων [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd c.AD(?): Pollianus Epigrammaticus 4.72]]; and of the flutes themselves, αὐλοὺς ἡδὺ πνέοντας [Refs [“Anthologia Graeca” 6.254 (Myrinus Epigrammaticus)]]; πνεῖται flutes are sounding, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Mnesimachus Comicus 4.57 (_anapaest meter_).]]

__II
breathe, send forth an odour, ἀμβροσίη.. ἡδὺ πνείουσα [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 4.446]]; π. εὐῶδες, δυσῶδες, [Refs 1st c.AD+ [2nd c.AD(?): Pollianus Epigrammaticus 2.75, etc.: _absolutely_, 1st c.AD: Dioscorides (Dioscurides) Medicus 3.80.]]

__II.2
with accusative, breathe out, send forth, Ζεφύρου πνείοντος ἐέρσην [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [3rd c.BC: Callimachus Epicus “Hymnus in Apollinem” 82.]]

__II.3
with genitive, breathe or smell of a thing, οὐ μύρου πνέον [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Fragmenta” 565; τράγου π. “Anthologia Graeca” 11.240 (1st c.AD: Lucillius Epigrammaticus); μόγοιο 4th c.AD(?): Quintus Smyrnaeus Epicus 6.164; λύθρου καὶ αἵματος [prev. author] 5.120 (ἐπιπν- codices)]]: rarely with dative, μύροισι π. smell with.., [Refs [Anthologia Graeca 5.199]]: frequently metaphorically, breathe, be redolent of, Χαρίτων πνείοντα μέλη [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Simonides Lyricus 184.3; ὄμματα.. πόθου πνείοντα “Anthologia Graeca” 5.258 (Paul. Sil.)]]; φόνου π. conjecture in [Refs 1st c.BC+ [3rd-4th c.AD: Tryphiodorus Epicus 505; αὐθαδείας πολὺς ἔπνει 1st c.BC: Dionysius Halicarnassensis 7.51.]]

__III
of perceptible breathing, [ἵππω] πνείοντε κατ᾽ ὤμων [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 13.385; π. ὕπνῳ 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Choephori” 621 (Lyric poetry).]]

__IV
generally, draw breath, breathe: hence, live, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 17.447]]; οἱ πνέοντες, ={οἱ ζῶντες}, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Trachiniae” 1160; ὄλβος ἀεὶ πνεῖ 3rd c.BC: Simmias 25.12; ἥμισύ μευ ψυχῆς ἔτι τὸ πνέον 3rd c.BC: Callimachus Epicus “Epigrammata” 42.]]

__V
metaphorically, with accusative cognate, breathe forth, μένεα πνείοντες breathing spirit, epithet of warriors, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 2.536, 3.8, 11.508, etc.; so πῦρ π. 8th-7th c.BC: Hesiodus Epicus “Theogonia” 319, 5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “Fragmenta.” 146; φόνον δόμοι πνέουσιν 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Agamemnon” 1309; κότον πνέων [prev. author] “Ch.” 34 (Lyric poetry), compare 951 (Lyric poetry)]]; φρενὸς πνέων τροπαίαν [Refs [[prev. author] “Ag.” 219 (Lyric poetry); Ἄρη πνεόντων [prev. work] 376 (Lyric poetry)]]; πνέων χάριν τινί[Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. work] 1206; πῦρ πνειόντων.. ἄστρων 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Antigone” 1146 (Lyric poetry); πῦρ π. καὶ φόνον 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Iphigenia Taurica” 288; ὠδῖνας [prev. author] “HF” 862: _paratragoedia_ in Comedy texts, πνέοντας δόρυ καὶ λόγχας 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Ranae” 1016]]; τρέχει τις Ἀλφειὸν πνέων, of a swift runner, [Refs [[prev. author] “Av.” 1121, etc.]]; and in a rhetorical passage, οἱ πῦρ πνέοντες, οἱ νενικηκότες Λακεδαιμονίους [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Historia Graeca (Hellenica)” 7.5.12.]]

__V.2
with neuter adjectives or Prons., πνέοντες μεγάλα giving themselves airs, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Andromache” 189]]; τόσονδ᾽ ἔπνευσας[Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. work] 327; κενεὰ πνεύσαις 5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “O.” 10(11).93; χαμηλὰ πνέων [prev. author] “P.” 11.30: _absolutely_, ὑπὲρ σακέων πνείοντες]] breathing over their shields, i. e. unable to repress their rage for war, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th-7th c.BC: Hesiodus Epicus “Scutum Herculis” 24; θρασείᾳ πνέων καρδίᾳ 5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “P.” 10.44: with _nominative_, Ἄρης.. μέγας πνέων 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Rhesus” 323; πολὺς ἔπνει καὶ λαμπρός 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 25.57; οὗτος.. καικίας ἢ συκοφαντίας πνεῖ 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Equites” 437]]; ᾧ σὺ μὴ πνεύσῃς ἐνδέξιος on whom thou breathest not favourably, [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [3rd c.BC: Callimachus Epicus “Epigrammata” 10.3.]]

πνοή, ῆς, ἡ,
Epic dialect πνοιή, always in [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Homerus Epicus]]; Doric dialect πνοά (see. below); Lyric poetry πνοιά [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “O.” 3.31, 5th c.BC: Bacchylides Lyricus 5.28]]: (πνέω):— blowing, blast, πνοιαὶ παντοίων ἀνέμων [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 17.55, compare 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 4.839, 8th-7th c.BC: Hesiodus Epicus “Theogonia” 253, 268; πνοιὴ Βορέαο 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 5.697]]:absolutely, blast, breeze, [Refs [11.622, 13.590]], etc.; ὀλίγη π. a light breeze, [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd c.AD: Arrianus Historicus “Tactica” 34.4]]; π. βιαία a stiff breeze,[Refs 3rd c.AD+ [[prev. work] 35.4; οἷον π. εἰς ἄλλο 3rd c.AD: Plotinus Philosophus 6.3.23]]; especially to denote excessive swiftness, ἅμα πνοιῇς ἀνέμοιο along with, i.e.swift as, blasts of wind, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 24.342, etc.; ἅμα πνοιῇ Ζεφύροιο 19.415; ἐπέτοντο μετὰ πνοιῇς ἀνέμοιο 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 2.148; πέτετο πνοιῇς ἀνέμοιο 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 12.207; ἅμα πνοιῇσι πετέσθην 16.149; imitated by 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Aves” 1396 (Lyric poetry)]], ἅμ᾽ ἀνέμων πνοαῖσι βαίη; frequently in Trag., ταχύπτεροι πνοαί [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Prometheus Vinctus” 88; πνοαὶ δ᾽ ἀπὸ Στρυμόνος μολοῦσαι [prev. author] “Ag.” 192 (Lyric poetry), compare 654, 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Nubes” 161, 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “de Mundo” 392b11, etc.]]; blast of bellows, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 4.100.]]

breathing hard, panting, of horses, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 23.380, 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Electra” 719 (_plural_).]]

__II.2
generally, breath, ἔμπνους μέν εἰμι.. καὶ πνοὰς.. πνέω [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Hercules Furens” 1092; μητρὸς οἴχονται πνοαί [prev. author] “Or.” 421: _metaphorically_, πνοιὴ Ἡφαίστοιο]] the breath of Hephaestus, i.e. flame, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 21.355; πυρὸς πνοᾷ 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Troades” 815 (Lyric poetry); πρὶν καταιγίσαι πνοὰς Ἄρεως 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Septem contra Thebas” 63, compare 115 (Lyric poetry); θεοῦ πνοαῖσιν ἐμμανεῖς 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Bacchae” 1094; πνοαὶ Ἀφροδίτης [prev. author] “IA” 69; θυμοῦ πνοαί [prev. author] “Ph.” 454.]]

__III

breath of a wind-instrument, Αἰολῇσιν ἐν πνοαῖσιν αὐλῶν [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “N.” 3.79; αὐλῶν π. 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Ranae” 313; σύριγγος πνοά 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Orestes” 145 (Lyric poetry).—poetical (5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Cratylus” 419d is no exception), once in 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus and frequently in later Prose (see. above) for πνεῦμα.]]

ποιέω, -ῶ,
[in LXX for a great variety of words, but chiefly for עשׂה ;]
__1. to make, produce, create, cause: with accusative of thing(s), Mat.17:4, Mrk.9:5, Jhn.9:11, Act.9:39, Rom.9:20, al.; of God as Creator (with accusative of person(s) also), Mat.19:4, Mrk.10:6, Luk.11:40, Act.4:24, Heb.1:2, al.; like Heb. עשׂה, absol. = ἐργάζομαι, to work, Mat.20:12 (cf. Rut.2:19; so AV, but see infr.), Rev.13:5, R, mg. (but see infr.); σκάνδαλα, Rom.16:17; εἰρεήνην, Eph.2:15, Jas.3:18; ἐπίστασιν, Act.24:12; συστροφήν, Act.23:12; with accusative of thing(s) and dative of person(s), Luk.1:68, Act.15:3; with nouns expressing action or its accomplishment, forming a periphr. for the cogn. verb: ὁδόν π. (cl. ὁ ποιεῖσθαι), to go on, advance, Mrk.2:23; πόλεμον, Rev.11:7, al.; ἐκδίκησιν, Luk.18:7, 8; ἐνέδραν, Act.25:3; κρίσιν, Jhn.5:27, Ju 15; ἔργα, Jhn.5:36, al.; (σημεῖα), Jhn.2:23 and freq., Act.2:22, al.; so also mid. ποιεῖσθαι: μονήν, Jhn.14:23; πορείαν, Luk.13:22; κοινωνίαν, Rom.15:26; of food, to make ready, prepare: δεῖπνον, Mrk.6:21, al.; δοχήν, Luk.5:29 14:13; γάμους, Mat.22:2; of time, to spend (cl.): ὥραν, Mat.20:12, RV (but see supr. and cf. McN, in l.); μῆνας, Rev.13:5, R, txt. (cf. Swete, in l.; but see supr.); ἐνιαυτόν, Jas.4:13; with accusative before ἐκ, Jhn.2:15, al.; with accusative and accusative pred., Mat.3:3 12:16, Mrk.1:3 3:12, Jhn.5:11, al.; with adv., καλῶς, Mrk.7:37; ἑορτὴν π. (Dem., Exo.23:16, al.), Act.18:21, Rec.; πάσχα, Mat.26:18; to make or offer a sacrifice (Plat., Xen., al.; Job.42:8, 3Ki.11:33; so some understand τοῦτο ποιεῖτε, Luk.22:19, but see Abbott, Essays, 110ff.); before ἵνα (WM, 422f.; M, Pr., 228), Jhn.11:37, Col.4:16, Rev.3:9.
__2. to do, perform, carry out, execute: absol., with adv., καλῶς π., Mat.12:12, 1Co.7:37, 38 Jas.2:19; id. before ptcp. (cl.; see M, Pr., 228), Act.10:33, Php.4:14, 2Pe.1:19, 3Jo.6; οὕτως, Mat.24:46, Luk.9:15, al.; ὡς (καθώς), Mat.1:24 2:16, al.; ὁμοίως, Luk.3:11; ὡσαύτως, Mat.20:5; with ptcp., ἀγνοῶν ἐποίησα, 1Ti.1:13; with accusative of thing(s): τί interrog., Mat.12:3, Mrk.2:25, Luk.6:2, al.; τοῦτο, Mat.13:28, Mrk.5:32, Luk.22:19 (WH om.; see supr., ref. to Abbott, Essays), Rom.7:20, al.; with nouns expressing command or regulation: τ. νόμον (not as in cl., to make a law), Jhn.7:19, Gal.5:3 (cf. in LXX, Jos.22:5, 1Ch.22:12, al.); τ. ἐντολάς, Mat.5:19; similarly with other nouns expressing conduct: τ. δικαιοσύνην, Mat.6:1, al.; τ. ἀλήθειαν, Jhn.3:21, al., etc.; with dupl. accusative, Mat.27:22, Mrk.15:12; with accusative of thing(s) and dative of person(s) (commod., incomm.; rare in cl.), Mat.7:12, Mrk.5:19, 20 Luk.1:49, Jhn.9:26, al.
SYN.: πράσσω, which see The general distinction between the two words is that between particular action and its habitual performance (cf. Tr., Syn., §xcvi; Westc. on Jhn.3:21; ICC on Rom.1:32).  (AS)

ποιέω,
Doric dialect ποιϝέω [Refs [“IG” 4.800 (from Troezen)]], etc.: Epic dialect imperfect ποίεον [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 20.147]]; contraction ποίει [Refs [18.482]]; Ionic dialect ποιέεσκον [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.36, 4.78:]]future ποιήσω: aorist ἐποίησα, Epic dialect ποίησα [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 18.490:]]perfect πεποίηκα:—middle, Ionic dialect imperfect ποιεέσκετο [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 7.119]]: future ποιήσομαι [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 9.397: in _passive_ sense, 5th c.BC: Hippocrates Medicus “περὶ εὐσχημοσύνης” 11, 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Metaphysica” 1021a23:]]aorist ἐποιησάμην, Epic dialect ποι- [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 5.251, +others:]]perfect πεποίημαι in middle sense, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Andocides Orator 4.22, Decrees cited in 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 18.29:]] —passive, future ποιηθήσομαι (μετα-) [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 23.62]], see above; πεποιήσομαι [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Hippocrates Medicus “γυναικεῖα” 1.11, 37]]: aorist ἐποιήθην [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 2.159, etc. (used as _middle_ only in _compound_ προσ-)]]: perfect πεποίημαι [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 6.56, etc.]]:—Attic dialect ποῶ [Refs [(“Etymologicum Magnum” 679.24)]], etc., is guaranteed by metre in Trag. and Comedy texts, as ποῶ [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Tyrannus” 918, ποεῖν [prev. author] “Tr.” 385, ποεῖς 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Acharnenses” 410, etc.]], and found in codex Laur. of [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus, codex Rav. of 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus, also “IG” 12.39.6]] (ποήσω), 82.9 (ποεῖ), 154.7 (ἐποησάτην), etc.; but ποι- is always written before -οι, -ου, -ω in Inscrr.: πο- also in Aeolic dialect πόημι πόης πόει [Refs 7th c.BC+ [“PBouriant” 8.71, 75, 7th-6th c.BC: Sappho Lyrica “Papyrus fragments” in E. Diehl, 1.9, +others, and 4th c.AD(?): Arcadius Grammaticus ποέντω, ={ποιούντων}, “IG” 5(2).6.9 (Tegea, 4th c.BC)]]; compare ποιητής. Used in two general senses, make and do.

__A
make, produce, first of something material, as manufactures, works of art, etc. (opposed to πράττειν, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Charmides” 163b), in 8th c.BC: Homerus Epicus frequently of building, π. δῶμα, τύμβον, 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 1.608, 7.435; εἴδωλον 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 4.796]]; π. πύλας ἐν [πύργοις] [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 7.339]]; of smith's work, π. σάκος[Refs [[prev. work] 222; ἐν [σάκεϊ] ποίει δαίδαλα πολλά 18.482, compare 490, 573: frequently in Inscrr. on works of art, Πολυμήδης ἐποίϝη]]h' (= ἐποίησε) Ἀργεῖος [Refs 6th c.BC+ [“SIG” 5 (6th c.BC,compare “Class.Phil.” 20.139); Θεόπροπος ἐποίει Αἰγινάτας “SIG” 18 (6th-5th c.BC), etc.; ἐποίησε Τερψικλῆς [prev. work]3b(Milet., 6th c.BC), etc.]]; τίς.. τὴν λίθον ταύτην τέκτων ἐποίε; [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [3rd c.BC: Herodas Mimographus 4.22]]; εἵματα ἀπὸ ξύλων πεποιημένα made from trees, i.e. of cotton, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 7.65; ναὸν ἀπὸ τοῦ ἱεροῦ ἀργυρίου 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 5.3.9; πλοῖα ἐκ τῆς ἀκάνθης ποιεύμενα 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 2.96; καρβάτιναι πεποιημέναι ἐκ βοῶν 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 4.5.14: with _genitive_ materiae, πωρίνου λίθου π. τὸν νηόν 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 5.62; ἔρυμα λίθων λογάδην πεποιημένον 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 4.31; φοίνικος αἱ θύραι πεποιημέναι 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 7.5.22: rarely ποιεῖσθαί τινι]]to be made with.., [Refs 3rd c.AD+ [3rd c.AD(?): Longus Scriptor Eroticus 1.4]]; also τῶν τὰ κέρεα.. οἱ πήχεες ποιεῦνται the horns of which are made into the sides of the lyre, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 4.192]]; also δέρμα εἰς περικεφαλαίας πεποίηται [Refs [Scholia Patm.D.in “BCH” 1.144]]:—middle, make for oneself, as of bees, οἰκία ποιήσωνται build them houses, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 12.168, compare 5.735, 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 5.251, 259, 8th-7th c.BC: Hesiodus Epicus “Opera et Dies” 503]]; [ῥεῖθρον] π., of a river, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-3rd c.BC: Theophrastus Philosophus “Historia Plantarum” 3.1.5]]; also, have a thing made, get it made, ὀβελούς [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 2.135; στεφάνους οὓς ἐποιησάμην τῷ χορῷ 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 21.16, compare 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 5.3.5]]; τὸν Ἀπόλλω, i.e. a statue of [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Epistulae” 361a; αὑτοῦ εἰκόνας 1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus “Themistocles” 5, compare “Inscription Prien.” 25.9 (3rd c.BC?).]]

__A.2
create, bring into existence, γένος ἀνθρώπων χρύσεον [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th-7th c.BC: Hesiodus Epicus “Opera et Dies” 110, compare “Th.” 161, 579, etc.; ὁ ποιῶν]]the creator, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Timaeus” 76c; ἕτερον Φίλιππον ποιήσετε 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 4.11]]:—middle, beget, υἱόν [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Andocides Orator 1.124; ἔκ τινος [prev. author] 4.22]]; παῖδας ποιεῖσθαι, ={παιδοποιεῖσθαι}, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 5.3.19, 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 57.43]]; conceive, παιδίον π. ἔκ τινος [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Symposium” 203b]]:—active in this sense only in later Gr., [Refs 1st c.AD+ [1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus 2.312a]]; of the woman, παιδίον ποιῆσαι [Refs [[prev. work]145d.]]

__A.3
generally, produce, ὕδωρ π., of Zeus, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Vespae” 261: _impersonal_, ἐὰν πλείω ποιῇ ὕδατα, ={ἐὰν ὕη}, 4th-3rd c.BC: Theophrastus Philosophus “de Causis Plantarum” 1.19.3]]; π. γάλα, of certain kinds of food, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Historia Animalium” 522b32]]; ἄρρεν π., of an egg, [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd-3rd c.AD: Aelianus “Varia Historia” 1.15]]; μέλι ἄριστον π., of Hymettus, [Refs 1st c.BC+ [1st c.BC-1st c.AD: Strabo Geographus 9.1.23]]; π. καρπόν, of trees, [NT.Matt.3.10] (metaphorically in religious sense,[Refs [[prev. work] 8)]]; of men, κριθὰς π. grow barley, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Pax” 1322; π. σίτου μεδίμνους 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 42.20]]; π. πενίαν, πλοῦτον, of the stars, [Refs 3rd c.AD+ [3rd c.AD: Plotinus Philosophus 2.3.1.]]

__A.3.b
in Mathematics texts, make, produce, τομήν, σχῆμα, ὀρθὰς γωνίας, [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [3rd c.BC: Archimedes Geometra “περὶ σφαίρας καὶ κυλίνδρου” 1.16, 38, “Con.Sph.” 12; ὁ Α τὸν Γ πολλαπλασιάσας τὸν Η πεποίηκεν 3rd c.BC: Euclides Geometra 7.19:]] —passive, πεποιήσθω ὡς.. let it be contrived that.., [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [3rd c.BC: Archimedes Geometra “περὶ σφαίρας καὶ κυλίνδρου” 2.6.]]

__A.3.c
postulate, imply, ἡ προσθήκη ἀφαίρεσιν καὶ ἔλλειψιν ποιεῖ [Refs 3rd c.AD+ [3rd c.AD: Plotinus Philosophus 3.9.3.]]

__A.3.d
π. τὸ πρόβλημα effect a solution of the problem, [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [3rd-2nd c.BC: Apollonius Pergaeus Geometra “Conica” 2.49, 51]]; π. τὸ ἐπίταγμα fulfil, satisfy the required condition, [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [3rd c.BC: Archimedes Geometra “περὶ σφαίρας καὶ κυλίνδρου” 1.2, 3.]]

__A.4
after [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Homerus Epicus]], of Poets, compose, write, π. διθύραμβον, ἔπεα, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.23, 4.14; π. θεογονίην Ἕλλησι [prev. author] 2.53]]; π. Φαίδραν, Σατύρους, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Thesmophoriazusae” 153, 157]]; π. κωμῳδίαν, τραγῳδίαν, etc., [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Symposium” 223d; παλινῳδίαν 5th-6th c.BC: Isocrates Orator 10.64, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Phaedrus” 243b, etc.; ποιήματα [prev. author] “Phd.” 60d]]: absolutely, write poetry, write as a poet, ὀρθῶς π. [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 3.38; ἐν τοῖσι ἔπεσι π. [prev. author] 4.16, compare 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Ion” 534b]]: followed by a quotation, ἐπόησάς ποτε.. [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Thesmophoriazusae” 193; εἴς τινα 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Phaedo” 61b; περὶ θεῶν [prev. author] “R.” 383a, etc.]]

__A.4.b
represent in poetry, Ὅμηρον Ἀχιλλέα πεποιηκέναι ἀμείνω Ὀδυσσέως [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Hp.Mi.” 369c, compare 364c, “Smp.” 174b]]; ποιήσας τὸν Ἀχιλλέα λέγοντα having represented Achilles saying, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus 2.105b, compare 25d, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Gorgias” 525d, 525e, 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Poetica” 1453b29.]]

__A.4.c

with accusative cognate, πόλεμον π. [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 551d]], Arist.[same place], etc.:—passive, [πολέμους] τοὺς ἐπὶ Θησέως πολεμηθέντας [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Memorabilia” 3.5.10; κατὰ θάλατταν ὁ π. ἐπολεμεῖτο [prev. author] “HG” 5.1.1, compare 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 600a]]; ὅσα ἐπολεμήθη whatever hostilities took place, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 4.1.1; τὰ περὶ Πύλον κατὰ κράτος ἐπολεμεῖτο 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 4.23, compare 3.6.]] —The form used by Poets is πολεμίζω.

Abbott-Smith / STEPBible (TBESG)
πολύς, πολλή, πολύ,
[in LXX chiefly for רַב and cognate forms ;]
__1. as adj., much, many, great, of number, space, degree, value, time, etc.: ἀριθμός, Act.11:21; ὄχλος, Mrk.5:24; θερισμός, Mat.9:37; χόρτος, Jhn.6:10; χρόνος, Mat.25:19; γογγυσμός, Jhn.7:12; πόνος, Col.4:13; δόξα, Mat.24:30; σιγή, Act.21:40; pl., προφῆται, Mat.13:17; ὄχλοι, Mat.4:25; δαιμόνια, Mrk.1:34; δυνάμεις, Mat.7:22,
__2. As subst., pl. masc, πολλοί, many (persons): Mat.7:22, Mrk.2:2, al.; with genitive partit., Mat.3:7, Luk.1:16, al.; before ἐκ, Jhn.7:31, Act.17:12; with art., οἱ π., the many, Mat.24:12, Rom.12:5, 1Co.10:17, 33 2Co.2:17; opposite to ὁ εἶς (Lft., Notes, 291), Rom.5:15, 19; neut. pl., πολλά: Mat.13:3, Mrk.5:26, al.; accusative with adverbial force, Mrk.1:45, Rom.16:6 (Deiss., LAE, 317), 1Co.16:12, Jas.3:2, al.; neut. sing., πολύ: Luk.12:48; adverbially, Mrk.12:27, al.; πολλοῦ (genitive pret.), Mat.26:9; with compar. (Bl., §44, 5), π. σπουδαιότερον, 2Co.8:22; πολλῷ πλείους, Jhn.4:41.
Compar., πλείων
, neut., πλεῖον and πλέον (see WH, App., 151), pl., πλείονες, -ας, -α, contr., πλείους, -ω (cf. Mayser, 69), more, greater;
__1. as adj.: Jhn.15:2, Act.18:2o, Heb.3:3; before παρά, Heb.11:4 (cf. Westc, in l. Was ΠΛΙΟΝΑ here a primitive error for ΗΔΙΟΝΑ ?); pi., Act.13:31, al.; with genitive compar., Mat.21:36; with num. (ἤ of comp. omitted), Act.4:22 24:11, al.
__2. As subst., οἱ π., the greater number: Act.10:32 27:12, 1Co.10:5 15:6; also (Bl., §44, 3) others, more, the more: 2Co.2:6 4:15, Php.1:14; πλείονα, Luk.11:53; πλειον, πλέον, Mat.20:10, 2Ti.3:9; with genitive comp., Mk  12:43, Luk.21:3; π. Ἰωνᾶ ὧδε, Mat.12:41; adverbially, Act.4:17 20:9 24:4.
__3. As adv., πλεῖον: before ἤ, Luk.9:13; with genitive comp., Mat.5:20; πλείω: with num., Mat.26:53.
Superl., πλεῖστος, -η, -ον
, __(a) prop., most: Mat.11:20 21:8; adverbially, τὸ π., 1Co.14:27;
__(b) elative (M, Pr., 79), very great: ὄχλος π., Mrk.4:1.
(AS)

πολύς,
Attic dialect πολλή, πολ; genitive πολλοῦ, ῆς, ou=; dative πολλῷ, ῇ, ; accusative πολύν, πολλήν, πολύ:—Ionic dialect πολλός [Refs 6th c.BC+ [6th c.BC: Anacreon Lyricus 43.3]], πολλή, πολλόν [Refs 6th c.BC+ [6th c.BC: Xenophanes Poeta Philosophus 9, 3rd c.AD: Democritus Epigrammaticus 219, 5th c.BC: Hippocrates Medicus “περὶ ἀρχαίης ἰητρικῇς” 1, 3rd c.BC: Herodas Mimographus 3.19]]; also in Trag., [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Antigone” 86, “Tr.” 1196]]; accusative πολλόν, πολλήν, πολλόν: [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus]] uses the Ionic dialect forms, but codices have πολύν [Refs 1st c.AD+ [2.121.δ, 3.57, variant in 6.125, πολύ 2.106, 3.38, 6.72, 7.46, 160 (πολύ also in 1st c.AD(?): Heraclitus 114, 3rd c.AD: Democritus Epigrammaticus 244)]]:—both sets of forms are found in Epic dialect, also genitive singular πολέος [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 4.244, etc.: _nominative_ _plural_ πολέες 2.417, +others]], once contraction πολεῖς [Refs [11.708; _genitive_ πολέων (_trisyllable_) 5.691, (_disyllable_) 16.655]]; dative πολέσι [Refs 8th c.BC+ [10.262, +others; πολέσσι 13.452, +others; πολέεσσι 9.73, 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 5.54, 8th-7th c.BC: Hesiodus Epicus “Opera et Dies” 119, etc.]]; accusative πολέας (trisyllable) [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 3.126, etc., (_disyllable_) 1.559, 2.4, 8th-7th c.BC: Hesiodus Epicus “Opera et Dies” 580]] (frequently with variant{πολεῖς} [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 15.66, etc.)]]; in later Epic dialect πολέες is used as feminine, [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [3rd c.BC: Callimachus Epicus “Hymnus in Delum” 28, also πολέας [prev. author] “Dian.” 42, 3rd c.BC: Apollonius Rhodius Epicus 3.21; _neuter_ πολέα 4th c.AD(?): Quintus Smyrnaeus Epicus 1.74 (see. below)]]:—Epic dialect also have πουλύς (once in [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th-7th c.BC: Hesiodus Epicus, “Th.” 190, also 6th c.BC: Theognis Elegiacus 509, sometimes _feminine_ in 8th c.BC: Homerus Epicus, πουλὺν ἐφ᾽ ὑγρήν 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 10.27, ἠέρα πουλύν 5.776), _neuter_ πουλύ 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 19.387]]; these forms are found in codices of [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Hippocrates Medicus and 2nd c.AD: Aretaeus Medicus (who uses πολύ, πουλύ and πολλόν in _neuter_), but not in 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus:]] — Lyric poetry and Trag. (Lyric poetry) sometimes use Epic dialect forms, dative singular πολεῖ [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Supplices” 745; _nominative_ _plural_ πολέες 5th c.BC: Bacchylides Lyricus 10.17; _neuter_ πολέα 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Agamemnon” 723; πολέων 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Helena” 1332 (_feminine_, 5th c.BC: Bacchylides Lyricus 5.100); _dative_ _plural_ πολέσι 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Iphigenia Taurica” 1263. [ῠalways.]]]

__I
of Number, many, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 2.417, etc.]]; ἐκ πολλῶν, opposed to ἐξὀλίγων, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th-7th c.BC: Hesiodus Epicus “Theogonia” 447]]; τριηκόντων ἐτέων πόλλ᾽ ἀπολείπων wanting many of thirty years, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [[prev. author] “Op.” 696; παρῆσάν τινες, καὶ πολλοί γε 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Phaedo” 58d; οὐ πολλοί τινες 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Persae” 510: with Nouns of multitude, πουλὺς ὅμιλος 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 8.109; πλῆθος πολλόν 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.141; ἔθνος πολλόν [prev. author] 4.22]]; later πουλὺ.. ἐπ᾽ ἔτος many a year, [Refs 2nd c.BC+ [“Anthologia Graeca” 6.235 (Thall.); π. ἦν ὁ καταπλέων 2nd c.BC: Polybius Historicus 15.26.10]]; of anything often repeated, περὶ σέο λόγος ἀπῖκται π. [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.30; πολλὸν ἦν τοῦτο τὸ ἔπος [prev. author] 2.2, compare 3.137, etc.; πολὺ.. τὸ σὸν ὄνομα διήκει πάντας 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Coloneus” 305; τούτῳ πολλῷ χρήσεται τῷ λόγῳ]]often, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 21.29]]; τοῦτο ἐπιεικῶς πολὺ νῦν ἐστι is fairly frequent, [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd c.AD: Lucianus Sophista “Hist.Conscr.” 15.]]

__I.2
of Size, Degree, Intensity, much, mighty, ὄμβρος, νιφετός, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 10.6; π. ὕπνος 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 15.394; πῦρ.. π. 10.359]]; π. ὑμέναιος a loud song, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 18.493]]; π. ὀρυμαγδός, ῥοῖζος, etc.,[Refs 8th c.BC+ [2.810, 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 9.315, etc.]]; π. ἀνάγκη strong necessity, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Phoenissae” 1674]]; π. γέλως, βοή, much or great, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Ajax” 303, 1149; μωρία [prev. work] 745]]; ὄλβος, αἰδώς, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Persae” 251, “Ag.” 948; ἀσφάλεια 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 2.11]]; ἀλογία, εὐήθεια, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Phaedo” 67e, “Phdr.” 275c, etc.]]

__I.2.b
rarely of a single person, great, mighty, μέγας καὶ πολλὸς ἐγένεο [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 7.14, compare 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Hippolytus” 1]]; ὁ π. σοφιστής, στρατηγός,[Refs 5th c.BC+ [Chor. p.23 5th c.BC: Bacchylides Lyricus, [prev. author]in “Rev.Phil.” 1.68; ὁ πάντα π. [prev. author] p.27 5th c.BC: Bacchylides Lyricus]]; ὁ πολύς alone, of Hippocrates, [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd c.AD: Galenus Medicus 19.530]]; of Trajan, [Refs 1st c.BC+ [6th c.AD: Lydus, Joannes Laurentius Historicus “Mag.” 2.28; ῥώμην σώματος πολύς 1st c.BC: Dionysius Halicarnassensis 2.42.]]

__I.2.c
joined with a Verb, Κύπρις γὰρ οὐ φορητός, ἢν πολλὴ ῥυῇ if she flow with full stream, metaphorically from a river, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Hippolytus” 443; θρασυνομένῳ καὶ πολλῷ ῥέοντι 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 18.136]]; from the wind, ὡς π. ἔπνει καὶ λαμπρός was blowing strong and fresh, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. author] 25.57, compare 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Equites” 760, “Anthologia Graeca” 11.49 (5th c.BC: Evenus Elegiacus)]]: generally, with might or force, ὅταν ὁ θεὸς.. ἔλθῃ πολύς [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Bacchae” 300; ἢν π. παρῇ [prev. author] “Or.” 1200; π. καὶ τολμηρὸς ἅνθρωπος 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 40.53: with]]participle and εἰμί, πολλὸς ἦν λισσόμενος was all entreaties, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 9.91; ἦν πολλὸς ὑπὸ παντὸς ἀνδρὸς αἰνεόμενος [prev. author] 1.98; Ἐτεοκλέης ἂν εἷς π... ὑμνοῖθ᾽ 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Septem contra Thebas” 6; π. ἐνέκειτο λέγων 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 7.158; π. τοῖς συμβεβηκόσιν ἔγκειται 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 18.199; also π. ἦν ἐν τοῖσι λόγοισι 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 8.59; πρὸς ταῖς παρασκευαῖς 2nd c.BC: Polybius Historicus 5.49.7; ἐπὶ τῇ τιμωρίᾳ 1st c.BC: Diodorus Siculus Historicus 14.107]]: without a preposition, π. ἦν τοῖς ἐπαίνοις καὶ ἐπαχθής [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aeschines Orator 2.41]]; π. μὲν γὰρ ὁ Φίλιππος ἔσται will be often mentioned, [Refs [[prev. author] 1.166.]]

__I.3
of Value or Worth, πολέος δέ οἱ ἄξιος ἔσται [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 23.562, compare 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 8.405; πολλοῦ ἄξιος 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 4.1.28, etc.; πολλῶν ἄξιος 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Pax” 918]]; περὶ πολλοῦ ποιεῖσθαί τι, Latin magni facere,[Refs 4th c.BC+ [compare περί 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus IV]]; ἐπὶ πολλῷ at a high price, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 8.53; ἐπὶ π. ἐρραθυμηκότες [prev. author] 1.15]]; πολύ ἐστί τι it is worth much, of great conscquence, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Oeconomicus” 18.7.]]
