IV.]]

__I.5
of Time, long, χρόνος [Refs 8th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Ajax” 1402 (_anapaest meter_), etc.; πολὺν χρόνον 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 2.343, etc.; οὐ π. χρ. 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Philoctetes” 348, etc.; so πολλοῦ χρόνου 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Plutus” 98; χρόνῳ πολλῷ 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Trachiniae” 228]]; διὰ πολλοῦ (i.e. χρόνου) [Refs 5th c.BC+ [2nd c.AD: Lucianus Sophista “Nec.” 15; ἐκ πολλοῦ 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 1.58, 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 21.41]]; πρὸ πολλοῦ long before, [Refs 1st c.BC+ [1st c.BC: Diodorus Siculus Historicus 14.43; οὐ μετὰ πολύ 2nd c.AD: Lucianus Sophista “Tox.” 54]]; ἔτι πολλῆς νυκτός while still quite night, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 8.101]]; πολλῆς ὥρας late in the day, [NT+2nd c.BC+ [2nd c.BC: Polybius Historicus 5.8.3; ἤδη ὥρα πολλή NT.Mark.6.35; ἔτι ἔστιν ἡμέρα πολλή LXX.Gen.29.7.]]

__II
Special usages:

__II.1
with partitive genitive, e.g. πολλοὶ Τρώων, for πολλοὶ Τρῶες, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 18.271, etc.]]; neuter, πολλὸν σαρκός, for πολλὴ σάρξ, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 19.450]]: in Prose, the adjective generally takes the gender of the genitive, τὸν πολλὸν τοῦ χρόνου [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.24]]; τῆς γῆς οὐ πολλήν [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 6.7; τῆς ἀθάρης πολλήν 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Plutus” 694; πολλὴν τῆς χώρας 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 3.2.2; ὁ π. τοῦ λόγου 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 44.6]]; see below 3.

__II.2
joined with another adjective, πολλὰ δυστερπῆ κακά [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Choephori” 277, compare 585 (Lyric poetry), etc.: more frequently joined to another]] adjective by καί, πολέες τε καὶ ἐσθλοί many men and good, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 6.452, etc.; πολέες τε καὶ ἄλκιμοι 21.586; πολλὰ καὶ ἐσθλά 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 2.312]]; παλαιά τε πολλά τε[Refs 8th c.BC+ [[prev. work] 188; ἄκοσμά τε π. τε 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 2.213; πολλαί γε.. καὶ ἄλλαι 8th-7th c.BC: Hesiodus Epicus “Theogonia” 363; π. τε καὶ κακά 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 4.167, etc.; π. κἀγαθά 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Thesmophoriazusae” 351 (but π. ἀγαθά “IG” 12.76.45); π. καὶ ἀνόσια 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 416e; π. καὶ μακάρια [prev. author] “Plt.” 269d; π. καὶ πονηρά 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Memorabilia” 2.9.6; πολλά τε καὶ δεινά [prev. author] “An.” 5.5.8; μεγάλα καὶ π. 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 36.22]]; π. καὶ καλοὺς (assuming variant) κινδύνους, π. καὶ καλὰ παραδείγματα, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-3rd c.BC: Dinarchus Orator 1.109.]]

__II.3
with the Article (in [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Homerus Epicus]] without the Article, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 2.483, 5.334, 22.28), of persons or things well known, Ἑλένα μία τὰς πολλάς, τὰς πάνυ π. ψυχὰς ὀλέσασ᾽]] those many lives, [NT+5th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Agamemnon” 1456 (Lyric poetry), compare 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Tyrannus” 845, 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 3.87, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Phaedo” 88a, “Ti.” 54a, NT.Act.26.24]]: with abstract Nouns, τᾶς πολλᾶς ὑγιείας [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Agamemnon” 1001 (Lyric poetry, uncertain); τὸ πολλόν]]numbers, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.136.]]

__II.3.b
οἱ π. the many, i.e. the greater number, Ἀθηναῖοι.. ἀπῆλθον οἱ πολλοί [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 1.126, compare 3.32, etc. (so in _sing._, ὁ πολλὸς λόγος]] the prevailing report, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.75); τοῖς π. κριταῖς 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Ajax” 1243: with _genitive_, τοῖς π. βροτῶν [prev. work] 682; οἱ π. τῶν ἀνθρώπων 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 8.2.24; οἱ πολλοὶ ἅπαντες]]far the most, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Hippocrates Medicus “Aër.” 20 (variant{μάλιστα} for ἅπαντες); for τὰ πολλὰ πάντα, see below 111.1a: hence οἱ πολλοί]] the people, the commonalty, opposed to οἱ μείζω κεκτημένοι, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 1.6]]; opposed to οἱ κομψότεροι, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 505b]]; οἱ π., = Latin plebs, [Refs 1st c.BC+ [1st c.BC: Diodorus Siculus Historicus 20.36]]; τῶν πολλῶν εἷς one of the multitude, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 21.96; also ὁ π. λεώς 2nd c.AD: Lucianus Sophista “JTr.” 53, compare “Rh.Pr.” 17; ὁ π. ὅμιλος [prev. author] “Luct.” 2. 2nd c.AD: Herodianus Grammaticus 1.1.1, etc.; ὁ π. δῆμος 2nd c.AD: Lucianus Sophista “Apol.” 15; ὁ π. ὄχλος 1st c.AD: Philo Judaeus 2.4]]; ὁ π. alone, = vulgus, variant in [Refs 1st c.BC+ [1st c.BC: Diodorus Siculus Historicus 2.29]]; the ordinary man, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-3rd c.BC: Epicurus Philosophus “Fragmenta” 478, 1st c.BC: Philodemus Gadarensis Epigrammaticus “Rh.” 2.154S.; νίμμα ὁ π. λέγει, ἡμεῖς ἀπόνιπτρον λέγομεν 2nd c.AD: Phrynichus Atticista 170, compare369]]; ὁ ἐμπαθὴς καὶ π. ἄνθρωπος 'l'homme moyen sensuel', [Refs 5th c.AD+ [5th c.AD: Hermias Alexandrinus Philosophus “in Platonis Phaedrum scholia” p.146A.]]; ὁ π. ἄνθρωπος (with plural Verb) the average man, opposed to τὸ ἐξαίρετον, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.AD: Eunapius Historicus “Fragmenta Historica - HGM” p.216 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator]]

__II.3.c
τὸ πολύ, with genitive, τῆς στρατιῆς τὸ πολλόν [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 8.100; τὸ π. τοῦ χρόνου 5th c.BC: Hippocrates Medicus “Aër.” 20; τῶν λογάδων τὸ π. 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 5.73; τῶν ὅπλων τὸ π. 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Politicus” 288b; also ὁ στρατὸς ὁ πολλός 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.102; ἡ δύναμις ἡ π. 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 1.24]]; ὁ π. βίοτος the best part of life, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Electra” 185 (Lyric poetry).]]

__II.3.d
τὰ πολλά the most, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 22.273, and perhaps 2.58, 17.537 (elsewhere in 8th c.BC: Homerus Epicus πολλά,]] as substantive, means much riches, great possessions, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 11.684, 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 19.195); τὰ π. τοῦ πολέμου 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 2.13]]; πρὸς τὸ τῶν π. μέγεθος in regard to the size of the average, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Rhetorica” 1363b11.]]

__II.4
plural πολλά very much, too much, πολλὰ πράσσειν, ={πολυπραγμονεῖν}, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Supplices” 576, 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Ranae” 228; π. ἔπαθεν 5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “O.” 13.63, etc.]]; π. ἔρξαι τινά to do one much harm, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Septem contra Thebas” 923 (Lyric poetry).]]

__II.5
πολλάς with Verbs of beating (πληγάς being omitted), see at {πληγή} [Refs [1.]]

__II.6
πολύς repeated, ἦ πολλὰ πολλοῖς εἰμι διάφορος βροτῶν [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Medea” 579, compare 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Supplices” 451; τὰ μὲν οὖν πολλὰ πολλοῦ χρόνου διηγήσασθαι 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 615a, etc.; πολλοῦ πολύς, see below 111.1b: with _adverbs_ πολλάκις, πολλαχῇ, etc. (which see, compare 111.1 e).]]

__III
Adverbial usages:

__III.a
neuter πολύ (Ionic dialect πολλόν), πολλά, much, πόλλ᾽ ἀεκαζομένη [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 6.458, etc.; strengthened, μάλα πολλά 8.22, +others; πάνυ πολύ 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus Alcaeus1.119c; πολύ τι [prev. author] “R.” 484d]]; especially of repetition, often, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 2.798, 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 13.29, 8th-7th c.BC: Hesiodus Epicus “Opera et Dies” 322]]; so of earnest commands and entreaties, πολλὰ κελεύων, πόλλ᾽ ἐπέτελλον, πολλὰ λισσομένη, πολλὰ μάλ᾽ εὐχομένω, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 5.528, 11.782, 5.358, 9.183]]: with the Article, τὸ πολύ for the most part, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Protagoras” 315a, etc.]] (but with numerals, at most, Vett.[Refs 5th c.BC+ [Val. 9.5); ὡς τὸ π. 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Memorabilia” 1.1.10, etc.; τὰ πολλά 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 1.13, 2.11, 87, etc.; ὡς τὰ π. [prev. author] 5.65, etc.; τὰ π. πάντα 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.203, 2.35, 5.67.]]

__III.b
of Degree, far, very much, ἀπέφυγε πολλὸν τοὺς διώκοντας [Refs [[prev. author] 6.82: also _absolutely_ _genitive_ πολλοῦ]] very, θρασὺς εἶ πολλοῦ [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Nubes” 915, compare 5th c.BC: Eupolis Comicus 74; πολλοῦ δύνασθαι 4th c.AD: Alciphro Epistolographus 1.9 (assuming variant)]]; πολλοῦ πολύς, πολλὴ πολλοῦ, much too much, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Equites” 822, “Ra.” 1046.]]

__III.c
of Space, a great way, far, οὐ πολλόν [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.104; πολὺ οὐκ ἐξῄεσαν 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 1.15, etc.]]

__III.d
of Time, long, ὡς πολλὸν τοῦτο ἐγίνετο [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 4.126, compare 6.129.]]

__III.e
of Probability, ἐὰν πολλὰ πολλῶν τέκῃς, perhaps ={ἐὰν πολλάκις τέκῃς},[Refs 1st c.BC+ [“POxy.” 744.9 1st c.BC-1st c.AD]]; ἐάν τι πολλὰ πολλάκις πάθω [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Ecclesiazusae” 1105.]]

__III.2
πολύ is frequently joined with adjectives and adverbs,

__III.2.a
with a comparative to increase its comparative force, πολὺ μεῖζον, πολλὸν παυρότεροι, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 1.167, 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 14.17]]; πολὺ μᾶλλον much more, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 9.700]]; πολύ τι μᾶλλον falsa lectio in [Refs 1st c.BC+ [1st c.BC: Dionysius Halicarnassensis “de Compositione Verborum” 4 (p.22 U.-R.): with words, esp. Preps., between πολύ and its]] adjective, π. ἐν πλέονι, π. ἐπὶ δεινοτέρῳ,[Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 1.35, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 589e; πολὺ ἔτι ἐκ λαμπροτέρων [prev. author] “Phd.” 110c; π. σὺν φρονήματι μείζονι 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 3.1.22, compare 3.2.30, “Smp.” 1.4 (but the _preposition_ frequently comes first, ἐκ π. ἐλάττονος 5th-6th c.BC: Andocides Orator 1.109, etc.)]]; so πολλῷ is frequently used with the comparative, by far, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Prometheus Vinctus” 337, 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.134, etc.; π. μᾶλλον 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Tyrannus” 1159, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Phaedo” 80e]]; οὐ πολλῷ τεῳ ἀσθενέστερον not a great deal weaker, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.181, compare 2.48, 67, etc.: πολύ with all words implying comparison, πολὺ πρίν]] much sooner, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 9.250; π. πρό 4.373]]: with the comp. Verb φθάνω, ἦ κε πολὺ φθαίη [Refs 5th c.BC+ [13.815; so πολὺ προβέβηκας ἁπάντων, πολὺ προμάχεσθαι ἁπάντων, 6.125, 11.217; προὔλαβε πολλῷ 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 7.80: with βούλομαι,]] = prefer, ἡμῖν πολὺ βούλεται ἢ Δαναοῖσι νίκην [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 17.331, compare 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 17.404]]; πολύ γε in answers, after a comparative or superlative, ἀργὸς.. γενήσεται μᾶλλο; Answ. πολύ γε [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 421d, compare 387e, etc.]]

__III.2.b
with a superlative, πολὺ πρώτιστος, πολλὸν ἄριστος, far the first, etc., [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 2.702, 1.91, etc.; προθυμία π. τολμηροτάτη 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 1.74, etc.; πολλόν τι μάλιστα 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.56; π. δή, π. δὴ γυναῖκ᾽ ἀρίσταν 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Alcestis” 442 (Lyric poetry), compare 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Aves” 539, 4th c.BC: Archestratus Epicus “fragment” 34.9; also πολλῷ πλεῖστοι 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 5.92.έ, 8.42; π. μεγίστους [prev. author] 4.82.]]

__III.2.c
with a Positive, to add force to the adjective, ὦ πολλὰ μὲν τάλαινα, πολλὰ δ᾽ αὖ σοφή [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Agamemnon” 1295; also ἐς πόλλ᾽ ἀθλία πέφυκ᾽ ἐγώ 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Phoenissae” 619 (troch.); πολὺ ἀφόρητος 2nd c.AD: Lucianus Sophista “DMeretr.” 9.3]]; compare πλεῖστος.

__IV
with Preps.,

__IV.1
διὰ πολλοῦ at a great interval of Space or Time, see at {διά} [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus 1.5, 11.2.]]

__IV.2
εἰς πολύ for a long time, [Refs 3rd c.AD+ [3rd c.AD: Plotinus Philosophus 2.1.3.]]

__IV.3
ἐκ πολλοῦ from a great distance, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 4.32, etc.]]; for a long time, see at {ἐκ} [Refs [II.1.]]

__IV.4
ἐπὶ πολύ,

__IV.4.a
over a great space, far, οὐκ ἐπὶ πολλόν [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 2.32]]; ἐπὶ π. τῆς θαλάσσης, τῆς χώρας, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 1.50, 4.3, etc.]]; to a great extent, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. author] 1.6, 18, 3.83; compare ποιέω 5th c.BC: Bacchylides Lyricus 11.2.]]

__IV.4.b
for a long time, long, [Refs [[prev. author] 5.16; τῆς ἡμέρας ἐπὶ π. [prev. author] 7.38, compare 39.]]

__IV.4.c
ὡς ἐπὶ π. very generally,[Refs 4th c.BC+ [[prev. author] 1.12 (variant), 4th c.BC: Archytas Tarentinus Philosophus cited in 5th c.AD: Stobaeus, Joannes 3.1.195;]] ὡς ἐπὶ τὸ π. for the most part, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 2.13, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Politicus” 294e, etc.; μὴ καθ᾽ ἓν ἕκαστον, ἀλλ᾽ ὡς ἐπὶ τὸ π. 5th-6th c.BC: Isocrates Orator 4.154; τό γ᾽ ὡς ἐπὶ τὸ π. [prev. author] 8.35.]]

__IV.5
παρὰ πολύ by far, see at {παρά} C.111.5.

__IV.6
περὶ πολλοῦ, see above [Refs [1.3.]]

__IV.7
πρὸ πολλοῦ far before, τῆς πόλεως [Refs 1st c.BC+ [1st c.BC: Dionysius Halicarnassensis 9.35]]; also of Time, οὐ πρὸ π. not long before, [Refs [[prev. author] 5.62.]]

__IV.8
σὺν πολλῷ in no small degree, only too much or too well, [Refs 3rd c.AD+ [3rd c.AD: Heliodorus Scriptor Eroticus 2.8, 9.20, 10.9 (compare “CR” 41.53).]]

__V
for comparative πλείων, πλέων, superlative πλεῖστος, (see entry). (Cf. Sanskrit purú-, Gothic filu 'much'.)

πολυ-τελής, ές,
(τέλος) very expensive, costly, opposed to εὐτελής, οἰκίη [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 4.79; τράπεζα 3rd c.AD: Democritus Epigrammaticus 210; παρακομιδή 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 7.28; ζῶναι 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Hp.Mi.” 368c; παρασκευαί 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Hiero” 1.20 (_comparative_)]]; π. νεκρός honoured with a costly funeral, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-3rd c.BC: Menander Comicus “Per.fragment” 2]]; λίθοι, λιθεία, precious stones, [Refs 2nd c.BC+ [“OGI” 90.34 (Rosetta, 2nd c.BC), 132 (Egypt, 2nd c.BC)]]: generally, valuable, -εστάτην τὴν τοῦ ὁρᾶν.. δύναμιν ἐδημιούργησεν [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 507c]]; -έστατον ζῷον, variant for{πολυφρονέστατον}, [Refs 5th c.AD+ [Euryphamus Pythagoreus cited in 5th c.AD: Stobaeus, Joannes 4.39.27.]]

of persons, lavish, extravagant, coupled with ἄσωτος, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-3rd c.BC: Menander Comicus 615; γυνὴ π. ἐστ᾽ ὀχληρόν [prev. author] 325.7; ἑταίρα π. [prev. author] 824; π. τῷ βίῳ 4th c.BC: Antiphanes Comicus 80.5]]. adverb -λῶς[Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Eupolis Comicus 335, 5th c.BC: Lysias Orator 7.31, 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Memorabilia” 3.11.4]]: superlative, τὰ -λέστατα in the costliest manner, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 2.87.]]

Included with:  πολύ-τροπος, ον,
(τρέπω) much-turned, i.e. much-travelled, much-wandering, epithet of Odysseus, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 1.1, 10.330.]]

__II
turning many ways: metaphorically, shifty, versatile, wily, of Hermes, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [“hymnus ad Mercurium” 13, 439; τοῖς ἀσθενέσι καὶ π. θηρίοις 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Politicus” 291b]]; and in this sense Plato took the word as applied to Odysseus, [Refs [“Hp.Mi.” 364e (_superlative_), +others]]; τὸ π. τῆς γνώμης their versatility of mind, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 3.83]]; τὸ π., of Alcibiades, [Refs 1st c.AD+ [1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus “Alcibiades” 24.]]

__II.2

__A
absolutely:

__I
of Place, generally with a notion of motion, forwards, onwards, π. ἄγειν, φέρειν, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 18.388, 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 9.542, etc.; [δοῦρα] ὄρμενα πρόσσω 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 11.572]]; ἵπποι πρόσσω μεμαυῖαι[Refs [[prev. work] 615; πρόσω ἵεσθε 12.274, etc.; π. πᾶς πέτεται 16.265]]; π. κατέκυψε[Refs [[prev. work] 611; π. ἀΐξας 17.734]]; π. τετραμμένος αἰεί[Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. work] 598; νέμεσθαι π. 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 3.133]]; παραγγεῖλαι, πέμψαι π., [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Agamemnon” 294, 853]]; βῆναι, ἕρπειν π., [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Trachiniae” 195, 547]]; μὴ πόρσω φωνεῖν speak no further, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. author] “El.” 213 (Lyric poetry); μηκέτι πάπταινε πόρσιον 5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “O.” 1.114: with _Article_, πορεύεσθαι αἰεὶ τὸ πρόσω 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 7.30, compare 9.57]]; also ἰέναι τοῦ π. [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 1.3.1; ἤϊε αἰεὶ ἐς τὸ π. 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 3.25.]]

__II
of Distance, far off, παπταίνειν τὰ πόρσω [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “P.” 3.22; ἐγγὺς παρεστὼς καὶ πρόσω δ᾽ ἀποστατῶν 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Eumenides” 65; ὡς ἀπ᾽ ὀμμάτων, πρόσω 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Coloneus” 15]]; πρόσω λεύσσειν to see at a distance, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. author] “fragment” 858.3; πόρρω ποι ἀπεσκοποῦμεν 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 432e; ἐγγύς, οὐ πρόσω βεβηκώς 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Phoenissae” 596; ἡ δέ γ᾽ Εὔβοια.. παρατέταται μακρὰ πόρρω πάνυ 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Nubes” 212; εἴτ᾽ ἐγγύς, εἴτε πόρρω 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Protagoras” 356e; πόρρω που ἐκτὸς ὄντι [prev. author] “R.” 499c, etc.]]; πόρρω ποιεῖν τι leave at a distance, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Anaxilas Comicus 22.18, compare 3rd c.BC: Herodas Mimographus 6.90 (uncertain); πάνυ π. γενέσθαι 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 4.3.16]]; τὰ σκέλη κινεῖν ταχὺ καὶ π., of a runner, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Rhetorica” 1361b24; οἱ πόρρω βάρβαροι [prev. author] “EN” 1149a11.]]

__II.2

__III

__B
with genitive:

__B.I
of Place, further into, π. τοῦ ποταμοῦ προβαίνειν [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 4.3.28, compare 5th c.BC: Hippocrates Medicus “γυναικεῖα” 1.2: especially _metaphorically_, προβήσεσθαι πόρρω μοχθηρίας]] will go far in wickedness, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Apologia Socratis” 30]]; π. ἀρετῆς ἀνήκειν to have reached a high point of virtue, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 7.237; οὕτω πόρρω σοφίας ἥκεις 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Euthydemus” 294e; πόρρω σοφίας ἐλαύνειν [prev. author] “Euthphr.” 4b, compare “Grg.” 486a, “Cra.” 410e, “Ly.” 204b]]; π. τέχνης a past master, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Vespae” 192 (see. below 11); π. πάνυ ἐλάσαι τῆς πλεονεξίας 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 1.6.39]]: also with Article, προβήσομαι ἐς τὸ π. τοῦ λόγου [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.5; ἐς τὸ π. οὐδὲν προεκόπτετο τῶν πρηγμάτων [prev. author] 3.56]]; ἐς τὸ π. μεγάθεος τιμῶνται are honoured to a high point of greatness, i.e. very greatly, [Refs [[prev. work] 154.]]

__B.II
of Distance, far from, οὐ π. τοῦ Ἑλλησπόντου [Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. author] 5.13; οὐ π. Σπάρτης πόλις 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Andromache” 733; στάντες οὐ πόρρω τῶν βωμῶν 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Leges” 800d, compare 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 3.2.22, etc.: _metaphorically_, π. δικαίων 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Eumenides” 414]]; πόρρω τέχνης,= οὐκ ἀπὸ τέχνης, i. e. φύσει, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Vespae” 192 (_accusative_ to Scholia, sed see above 5th c.BC: Bacchylides Lyricus 1); π. τοῦ χειρίσματος 5th c.BC: Hippocrates Medicus “περὶ ἄρθρων ἐμβολῆς” 11; οὐκέτι πόρρω διθυράμβων φθέγγομαι 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Phaedrus” 238d]]; πόρρω που τῶν ἐμαυτῷ πεπολιτευμένων far below them, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 18.299; πόρρω εἶναι τοῦ οἴεσθαι 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Phaedo” 96e; πόρρω τῶν πραγμάτων 5th-6th c.BC: Isocrates Orator 4.16; πόρρω τοῦ διαφθείρειν [prev. author] 15.240; πόρρω λίαν τῆς ὑποθέσεως ἀποπλανηθῆναι [prev. author] 7.77]]; π. σαρκός very far (i. e. different) from, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Historia Animalium” 504b11, compare 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 581e: also followed by ἀπό, ἐξαναχωρέειν π. ἀπὸ τῶν φορτίων 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 4.196; πάνυ πόρρω ἀπὸ τῆς θαλάσσης 5th c.BC: Antipho Orator 5.27; ἀπὸ τοῦ τείχους 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 5.4.49]]; also οὕτω πόρρω εἶ περὶ τοῦ δικαίου so far out in your notions of right, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 343c.]]

πότερος, α, ον;
Ionic dialect κότερος, η, ον: whether of the two? both in direct and indirect questions; once in [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Homerus Epicus, οὐκ ἂν γνοίης ποτέροισι μετείη 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 5.85; κότερα τούτων αἱρετώτερά ἐστι..; 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 3.52, compare 1.126; πότερα τύχης καὶ πότερα γνώμης ἔργα κρίνει; 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Memorabilia” 1.4.4; σκόπει πρὸς ποτέρους διαλέγῃ 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 528a, etc.]]: sometimes the two objects referred to follow in apposition, ἐρωτώσης τῆς μητρός, π. καλλίων.. δοκεῖ εἶναι, ὁ πατὴρ ἢ οὗτος [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 1.3.2, compare “Mem.” 1.6.9; πότερος.., ὁ ἰατρὸς ἢ ὁ ὀψοποιό; 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Gorgias” 464d, compare 498a, etc.]]; modified by τις, [Refs [[prev. author] “Lg.” 715a, etc.]]; repeated in the same sentence, πότερος ποτερου φίλος γίγνετα; [Refs [[prev. author] “Ly.” 212a.]]

__II
neuter πότερον and πότερα (interchangeable, πότερον δέδρακεν ἢ οὔ, καὶ πότερ᾽ ἄκων ἢ ἑκώ; [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 23.79, compare 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Memorabilia” 3.6.16), as]] adverb at the beginning of an interrogative sentence containing two alternative propositions, the second being connected by ἤ.., whether.. or,

__II.a
in direct questions, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “P.” 11.22, “fragment” 213, 5th c.BC: Bacchylides Lyricus 17.33, 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.88, etc.; τίνες κατῆρξαν, πότερον Ἕλληνες ἢ παῖς ἐμό; 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Persae” 351, etc.; πότερα δικαστὴν ἢ δικηφόρον λέγει; [prev. author] “Ch.” 120, compare “Supp.” 336.]]

__II.b
in indirect questions, ἐπείρεσθαι κότερα τὴν ἑωυτοῦ ἢ τὴν Κύρου λέγοι ἀρχήν [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.91, compare 3.32, etc.: the Verb is sometimes repeated, π. οὐδενὶ δύναται ἀρέσαι, ἢ ἔστιν οἷς καὶ πάνυ ἀρέσκε; 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Memorabilia” 2.3.6: sometimes π.]] precedes the common Verb, π. βούλοιτο μένειν ἢ ἀπιένα; [Refs [[prev. author] “Cyr.” 1.3.15, compare “Oec.” 18.1.]]

__II.2
sometimes a third clause (with ἤ) is inaccurately added, κότερα παρὰ δήμου ἢ ὀλιγαρχίης ἢ μουνάρχο; [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 3.82, compare 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Supplices” 247, 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Tyrannus” 112]]; and a fourth, [Refs [[prev. author] “El.” 539.]]

__II.3
the second alternative is sometimes left to be supplied, πότερα δὴ κερτομῶν λέγεις τάδε (i.e. ἢ μή..); [Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. author] “Ph.” 1235, compare “OC” 333, 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Persae” 239, “Th.” 94 (Lyric poetry), “Ag.” 274, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Sophista” 228a, “R.” 501d, etc.]]

__II.4
πότερον is sometimes omitted in the first clause, ἐπισκέψασθαι.., ὀρθὴ ἢ ψευδής [Refs [[prev. author] “Tht.” 161d, compare “Lg.” 670b.]]

__II.5

Ionic dialect κου, Aeolic dialect ποι [Refs 7th c.BC+ [7th-6th c.BC: Sappho Lyrica “Papyrus fragments” in E. Diehl, 25.17, 5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “P.” 5.101, “BCH” 37.157 (Cyme, 3rd c.BC), probably in 7th-6th c.BC: Alcaeus Lyricus 9]]:—enclitic adverb anywhere, somewhere, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 16.514, etc.]]; frequently with other Advs. of Place, οὐχ ἑκάς π. somewhere not far off, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Philoctetes” 41; πέλας π. [prev. work] 163 (_anapaest meter_); μηδαμοῦ.. π. [prev. work] 256 (uncertain reading)]]; π. πέραν τοῦ ποταμοῦ [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 4.3.3; ἄλλοθί π. 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 4.41; τῇδέ π. 2nd c.BC: Polybius Historicus 3.108.3, etc.: with _genitive_, ἀλλά π. αὐτοῦ ἀγρῶν]] in some part there of the fields, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 4.639]]; ἐμβαλεῖν π. (perhaps ποι) τῆς χώρας some part of the country, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 6.1.42; εἴ π. τῆς χώρας ταὐτὸ τοῦτο πάθος συνέβη 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 18.195.]]

without reference to Place, in some degree, καί πού τι [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 2.87]]: frequently to qualify an expression, perhaps, I suppose, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Homerus Epicus, etc.]]; added to introductory Particles, οὕτω π... [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 2.116; Ζεὺς μέν π. τό γε οἶδε 3.308; ὡς ὅτε π. 11.292]]; ἤν π., εἰ μή π., [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Hiero” 3.2, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 372a: strengthened, τάχ᾽ ἄν π. 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Tyrannus” 1116; ἴσως π. 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Electra” 518]]: attached to single words to limit their significance, πάντως κ. [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 3.73]]; τί π. δράσει; what in the world? [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Prometheus Vinctus” 743; οὐδείς π. 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Philebus” 64d]]; with numerals, ἔτεα τρία καὶ δέκα κ. μάλιστα about thirteen years, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.119, compare 209, 7.22, etc.: οὔ τί που]] denies with indignation or wonder, surely it cannot be.., οὔ τί π. οὗτος Ἀπόλλων [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “P.” 4.87, compare 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Philoctetes” 1233, 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Nubes” 1260, “Pax” 1211, “Ra.” 522, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 362d, etc.]]; οὐ δήπου adds a shade of suspicion, οὐ δήπου Στράτω; [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Acharnenses” 122, compare “Av.” 269, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Symposium” 194b]]: for δήπου, ἦπου, (see entry).—In late writers [LXX+NT+2nd c.AD+ [(LXX.Josh.2.5, +others, NT.John.7.35, +others, 2nd c.AD: Arrianus Historicus “Epicteti Dissertationes” 1.27.9, 4.1.93, etc.) ποῦ, που]] take the place of ποῖ, ποι, with Verbs of motion, as in Engl. where for whither? π. θέειν, πηδᾶν, σκαίρειν, πλίσσεσθαι, [prev. work] 622, 21.269, 18.572, 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 6.318; ὀρχεῖσθαι 8th-7th c.BC: Hesiodus Epicus “Theogonia” 3; ἔρχεσθαι 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 6.39; πάρος ποσὶν οὖδας ἱκέσθαι 8.376; νέρθε δὲ ποσσὶν ἤϊε μακρὰ βιβάς 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 7.212]]; also emphatically with Verbs denoting to trample or tread upon, πόσσι καταστείβοισι [Refs 7th c.BC+ [7th-6th c.BC: Sappho Lyrica 94; ἐπεμβῆναι ποδί 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Electra” 456]]; πόδα βαίνειν, see at {βαίνω} [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus 11.4]]; πόδα τιθέναι to journey, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Thesmophoriazusae” 1100: _metaphorically_, νόστιμον ναῦς ἐκίνησεν πόδα]] started on its homeward way, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Hecuba” 940 (Lyric poetry); νεῶν λῦσαι ποθοῦσιν οἴκαδ᾽.. πόδα [prev. work] 1020]]; χειρῶν ἔκβαλλον ὀρείους πόδας ναός, i. e. oars, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Timotheus Lyricus “Persae” 102]]; φωνὴ τῶν π. τοῦ ὑετοῦ sound of the pattering of rain, [LXX.3Ki.18.41.]

__3
as a point of measurement, ἐς πόδας ἐκ κεφαλῆς from head to foot, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 18.353; ἐκ κεφαλῆς ἐς πόδας ἄκρους 16.640; and reversely, ἐκ ποδῶν δ᾽ ἄνω.. εἰς ἄκρον κάρα 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Fragmenta - American Journal of Philology” 169; ἐκ τῶν ποδῶν ἐς τὴν κεφαλήν σοι 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Plutus” 650; also ἐκ τριχὸς ἄχρι ποδῶν “Anthologia Graeca” 5.193 (3rd c.BC: Posidippus Comicus or 3rd c.BC: Asclepiades Epigrammaticus); ἐς κορυφὰν ἐκ ποδός [prev. work] 7.388 (from Bianor).]]

__4
πρόσθε ποδός or ποδῶν, προπάροιθε ποδῶν, just before one, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 23.877, 21.601, 13.205; τὸ πρὸ ποδὸς.. χρῆμα 5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “I.” 8(7).13; αὐτὰ τὰ πρὸ τῶν ποδῶν ὁρᾶν 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Respublica Lacedaemoniorum” 3.4, compare “An.” 4.6.12, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 432d.]]

__4.b
παρά or πὰρ ποδός off-hand, at once, ἀνελέσθαι πὰρ ποδός [Refs 6th c.BC+ [6th c.BC: Theognis Elegiacus 282; γνόντα τὸ πὰρ ποδός 5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “P.” 3.60, compare 10.62; πὰρ ποδί]]close at hand, [Refs [[prev. author] “O.” 1.74]]; but παραὶ ποσὶ κάππεσε θυμός sank to their feet, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 15.280; παρὰ πόδα]]in a moment, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Philoctetes” 838 (Lyric poetry), 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Sophista” 242a]]; close behind, Νέμεσις δέ γε πὰρ πόδας (to be read πόδα) βαίνει Prov. cited in [Refs [10th c.AD: Suidas Legal icographus]]; also παρὰ πόδας immediately afterwards [Refs 2nd c.BC+ [2nd c.BC: Polybius Historicus 1.35.3, 5.26.13, 2nd c.AD: Galenus Medicus 5.272; παρὰ π. οἱ ἔλεγχοι 2nd c.AD: Lucianus Sophista “Hist. Conscr.” 13, compare 2nd c.AD: Aristides Rhetor 2.115 1st c.AD: Josephus Historicus]]; τὰ ἔμπροσθεν αὐτοῦ καὶ παρὰ πόδας at his very feet, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Theaetetus” 174a; περὶ τῶν παρὰ πόδας καὶ τῶν ἐν ὀφθαλμοῖς [prev. work]c; τὸ πλησίον καὶ παρὰ π. 2nd c.AD: Lucianus Sophista “Cal.” 1.]]

__4.c
ἐν ποσί in one's way, close at hand, τὸν ἐν π. γινόμενον [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 3.79, compare 5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “P.” 8.32; τἀν ποσὶν κακά 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Antigone” 1327, compare 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Andromache” 397; τοὐν ποσὶν κακόν [prev. author] Alcaeus739; τὴν ἐν ποσὶ [κώμην] αἱρεῖν 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 3.97; τὰ ἐν ποσὶν ἀγνοεῖν]]everyday matters, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Theaetetus” 175b, compare 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Politica” 1263a18, etc.]]

__4.d
τὸ πρὸς ποσί, ={τὸ ἐν ποσί}, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Tyrannus” 130.]]

__4.e
all these phrases are opposed to ἐκ ποδῶν out of the way, far off, written ἐκποδών [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 6.35, etc.; also, βίαια πάντ᾽ ἐκ ποδὸς ἐρύσαις 5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “N.” 7.67.]]

__5
to denote close pursuit, ἐκ ποδὸς ἕπεσθαι follow in the track, i.e. close behind, [Refs 2nd c.BC+ [2nd c.BC: Polybius Historicus 3.68.1, compare 1st c.BC: Diodorus Siculus Historicus 20.57, 1st c.BC: Dionysius Halicarnassensis 2.33, etc.; ἐκ ποδῶν διώξαντες 1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus “Pelopidas” 11.]]

__5.b
in earlier writers κατὰ πόδας on the heels of a person, [LXX+5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 5.98, 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 3.98, 8.17, 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Historia Graeca (Hellenica)” 2.1.20, LXX.Gen.49.19 (also κατὰ πόδα ὑπολαβεῖν]]on the moment, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Sophista” 243d)]]; ἡ κατὰ πόδας ἡμέρα the very next day, [Refs 2nd c.BC+ [2nd c.BC: Polybius Historicus 1.12.1 (but κατὰ πόδας αἱρεῖν]] catch it running, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 1.6.40, compare “Mem.” 2.6.9): with _genitive_ _person_, κατὰ πόδας τινὸς ἐλαύνειν, ἰέναι,]] march, come close at his heels, on his track, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 9.89, 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 5.64]]; τῇ κατὰ π. ἡμέρᾳ τῆς ἐκκλησίας on the day immediately after it, [Refs 2nd c.BC+ [2nd c.BC: Polybius Historicus 3.45.5; κατὰ π. τῆς μάχης 2nd c.AD: Aristides Rhetor 1.157J., etc.]]

__6
various phrases:

__6.a
ἀνὰ πόδα backwards, [Refs 5th c.AD+ [5th c.AD(?): Hesychius Legal icographus]]

__6.b
ἐπὶ πόδα backwards facing the enemy, ἐπὶ π. ἀναχωρεῖν, ἀνάγειν, ἀναχάζεσθαι, to retire without turning to fly, leisurely, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 5.2.32, “Cyr.” 3.3.69, 7.1.34, etc.; also ἐπὶ πόδας 2nd c.AD: Lucianus Sophista “Pisc.” 12]]; but γίνεται ἡ ἔξοδος οἷον ἐπὶ πόδας the offspring is as it were born feetforemost, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “de Generatione Animalium” 752b14.]]

__6.c
περὶ πόδα, properly of a shoe, round the foot, i.e. fitting exactly, ὡς ἔστι μοι τὸ χρῆμα τοῦτο περὶ πόδα [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Comicus 197, compare 129: with _dative_, ὁρᾷς ὡς ἐμμελὴς ἡ ἀρχὴ καὶ περὶ πόδα τῇ ἱστορίᾳ 2nd c.AD: Lucianus Sophista “Hist.Conscr.” 14, compare “Ind.” 10, “Pseudol.” 23.]]

__6.d
ὡς ποδῶνἔχει as he is off for feet, i. e. as quick as he can, ὡς ποδῶν εἶχον [τάχιστα] ἐβοήθεον [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 6.116; ἐδίωκον ὡς ποδῶν ἕκαστος εἶχον [prev. author] 9.59; φευκτέον ὡς ἔχει ποδῶν ἕκαστος 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Gorgias” 507d; so, σοῦσθε.. ὅπως ποδῶν [ἔχετε] 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Supplices” 837 (Lyric poetry).]]

__6.e
ἔξω τινὸς πόδα ἔχειν keep one's foot out of a thing, i. e. be clear of it, ἔξω κομίζων πηλοῦ πόδα [Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. author] “Ch.” 697; πημάτων ἔξω πόδα ἔχει [prev. author] “Pr.” 265; ἐκτὸς κλαυμάτων 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Philoctetes” 1260; ἔξω πραγμάτων 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Heraclidae” 109: without a _genitive_, ἐκτὸς ἔχειν πόδα 5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “P.” 4.289: opposed to εἰς ἄντλον ἐμβήσῃ πόδα 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Heraclidae” 168; ἐν τούτῳ πεδίλῳ.. πόδ᾽ ἔχων 5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “O.” 6.8.]]

__6.f
ἀμφοῖν ποδοῖν, etc., to denote energetic action, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Aves” 35, compare 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 13.78; συνέχευε ποσὶν καὶ χερσὶν 15.364; χερσίν τε ποσίν τε καὶ σθένει 20.360; τιμωρήσειν χειρὶ καὶ ποδὶ καὶ πάσῃ δυνάμει 4th c.BC: Aeschines Orator 2.115, compare 3.109]]; τερπωλῆς ἐπέβημεν ὅλῳ ποδί with all the foot, i.e. entirely, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [3rd c.BC: Apollonius Rhodius Epicus 4.1166, compare 1st-2nd c.AD: Dio Chrysostomus Sophista 13.19 (probably); καταφεύγειν ἐπὶ τὴν πόλιν ὥσπερ ἐκ δυοῖν ποδοῖν 2nd c.AD: Aristides Rhetor 1.117J.; opposed to οὐκ ἂν προβαίην τὸν πόδα τὸν ἕτερον 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Ecclesiazusae” 161; οὐκ ἂν ἔφασκεν ἐξελθεῖν οὐδὲ τὸν ἕτερον πόδα 4th-3rd c.BC: Dinarchus Orator 1.82.]]

__6.g
τὴν ὑπὸ πόδα [κατάστασιν] just below them, [Refs 2nd c.BC+ [2nd c.BC: Polybius Historicus 2.68.9]]; ὑπὸ πόδας τίθεσθαι trample under foot, scorn, [Refs 1st c.AD+ [1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus 2.1097c]]; οἱ ὑπὸ πόδα those next below them (in rank), [Refs 1st c.AD+ [1st c.AD: Onosander (Onasander) Tacticus 25.2]]; ὑπὸ πόδα χωρεῖν recede, decline, of strength, [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd c.AD: Athenaeus Epigrammaticus]] middle cited in [Refs 4th c.AD+ [4th c.AD: Oribasius Medicus (?) 21.16.]]

__6.h
for ὀρθῷ ποδί, see at {ὀρθός} [Refs [II.1.]]

__6.k
ἁλιεῖς ἀπὸ ποδός probably fishermen who fish from the land, not from boats, [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [“BGU” 221.5 (2nd-3rd c.AD)]]; ποτίσαι ἀπὸ ποδός perhaps irrigate by the feet (of oxen turning the irrigation-wheel), [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [“PRyl.” 157.21 (2nd c.AD)]]; τόπον.. ἀπὸ ποδὸς ἐξηρτισμένον uncertain meaning in [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [“POsl.” 55.11 (2nd-3rd c.AD).]]

__1
ἀγγεῖον.. τρήματα ἐκ τῶν ὑπὸ ποδὸς ἔχον round the bottom, [Refs 1st c.AD+ [1st c.AD: Dioscorides (Dioscurides) Medicus 2.72.]]

__7
πούς τινος, as periphrastic for a person as coming, etc., σὺν πατρὸς μολὼν ποδί, i.e. σὺν πατρί, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Hippolytus” 661; παρθένου δέχου πόδα [prev. author] “Or.” 1217, compare “Hec.” 977, “HF” 336; χρόνου πόδα [prev. author] “Ba.” 889 (Lyric poetry), 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Ranae” 100]]; also ἐξ ἑνὸς ποδός, i.e. μόνος ὤν, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Philoctetes” 91]]; οἱ δ᾽ ἀφ᾽ ἡσύχου π., i.e. οἱ ἡσύχως ζῶντες, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Medea” 217.]]

__II
metaphorically, of things, foot, lowest part, especially foot of a hill, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 2.824, 20.59 (_plural_), 5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “P.” 11.36, etc.]]; of a table, couch, etc., [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Fragmenta” 530, 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 8.8.16, etc.]]; compare πέζ; of the side strokes at the foot of the letter Ω, Callias cited in [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd c.AD: Athenaeus Epigrammaticus 10.454a]]; ={ποδεών}[Refs 5th c.BC+ [11.1, ἀσκοῦ.. λῦσαι π. 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Medea” 679.]]

__II.2
in a ship, πόδες are the two lower corners of the sail, or the ropes fastened therelo, by which the sails are tightened or slackened, sheets [Refs 8th c.BC+ [compare (ποδεών 11.4), 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 5.260]]; χαλᾶν πόδα ease off the sheet, as is done when a squall is coming, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Orestes” 707]]; τοῦ ποδὸς παρίει let go hold of it, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Equites” 436; ἐκδοῦναι ὀλίγον τοῦ ποδός 2nd c.AD: Lucianus Sophista “Cont.” 3]]; ἐκπετάσουσι πόδα ναός (with reference to the sail), [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Iphigenia Taurica” 1135 (Lyric poetry): opposed to τεῖναι πόδα]] haul it tight, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Antigone” 715]]; ναῦς ἐνταθεῖσα ποδί a ship with her sheet close hauled, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Orestes” 706; κὰδ᾽ δ᾽.. λαῖφος ἐρυσσάμενοι τανύοντο ἐς πόδας ἀμφοτέρους 3rd c.BC: Apollonius Rhodius Epicus 2.932; ἱστία.. ἐτάνυσσαν ὑπ᾽ ἀμφοτέροισι πόδεσσι 4th c.AD(?): Quintus Smyrnaeus Epicus 9.438.]]

__II.2.b
perhaps of the rudder or steering-paddle, αἰεὶ γὰρ πόδα νηὸς ἐνώμων [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 10.32 (cf. Scholia (at [prev. work])); πὰρ ποδὶ ναός 5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “N.” 6.55.]]

__III
a foot, as a measure of length, = [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4 palms (παλασταί) or 6 fingers, 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 2.149, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Meno” 82c, etc.]]

__IV
foot in Prosody, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Ranae” 1323 (Lyric poetry), 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 400a, 4th c.BC: Aristoxenus Musicus “Harmonica” p.34 M., 7th c.AD: Hephaestio Grammaticus 3.1, etc.]]; so of a metrical phrase or passage, ἔκμετρα καὶ ὑπὲρ τὸν π. [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd c.AD: Lucianus Sophista “Pr.Im.” 18]]; of a long passage declaimed in one breath, κήρυκες ὅταν τὸν καλούμενον πόδα μέλλωσιν ἐρεῖν [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd c.AD: Galenus Medicus 4.459, compare 2nd c.AD: Lucianus Sophista “Demon.” 65, 2nd c.AD(?): Pollianus Epigrammaticus 4.91.]]

__V
boundary stone, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Isaeus Orator “fragment” 27]]. (Cf. Latin pes, Gothic fotus, etc. 'foot'; related to πέδον as noted by [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “de Incessu Animalium” 706a33.)]]

Abbott-Smith / STEPBible (TBESG)
πρᾶγμα, -τος, τύ
(πράσσω), [in LXX chiefly for דָּבָר ;]
__1. that which has been done, a deed, act: Luk.1:1, Act.5:4, 2Co.7:11, Heb.6:18.
__2. That which is being done (like Lat. res), hence, a thing, matter, affair: Mat.18:19, Rom.16:2, 1Th.4:6 (see M, Th., in l), Heb.10:1 11:1, Jas.3:16; in forensic sense (as frequently in π., see Deiss., BS, 233), a law-suit: 1Co.6:1.†
(AS)

---

LSJ / STEPBible (TFLSJ)
πρᾶγμα, ατος, τό,
Ionic dialect πρῆχμα [Refs 5th c.BC+ [“Schwyzer” 688 B 16, C 5 (Chios, 5th c.BC), “GDI” 5598.4 (from Ephesus)]]; also πρῆγμα [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 5.33, +others, but 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus]] perhaps wrote πρῆχμα, which is see[Refs 2nd c.AD+ [l. in 1.133 cited in 2nd c.AD: Athenaeus Epigrammaticus 4.144a (codex A), and in 3.49, 57 (“POxy.” 1619.326, 379)]]; compare πρήχματος οὐχ ὁσίου imitated from [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus in “epigram Gr.” 1092 (from Erechtheum)]]: (πράσσω):— deed, act, the concrete of πρᾶξις, but frequently approaching to the abstract sense, [Refs 6th c.BC+ [6th c.BC: Theognis Elegiacus 116, +others]]; opposed to λόγοι, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 2.12, etc.; πραγμάτων ὀρθὰν ὁδόν 5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “O.” 7.46]]; γυναίου π. ἐποίει did the act of a woman, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 25.57, compare 18.24, etc.]]

__II
occurrence, matter, affair, πᾶσαν τελευτὰν πράγματος [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “O.” 13.75, compare “P.” 4.278; τί τοῦδε σοὶ μέτεστι π. λέγε 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Eumenides” 575, compare 584; π. τοιόνδε συνηνείχθη γενέσθαι 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 5.33, compare 9.92, 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 2.64; ἐς μέσον σφι προετίθεε τὸ π. 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.206; τί δ᾽ εἰδὼς τοῦδε π. πέρ; 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Ajax” 747 codices; τὸ π. εἰς ὑπέρδεινόν μοι περιέστη 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 21.111]]; ὁρᾶτε τὸ π., οἷ προελήλυθε κτλ., [Refs [[prev. author] 4.9, compare 8.7.]]

__II.2
thing, concrete reality, ἆρ᾽ ἔστιν αὔλησίς τι π.; [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Epicharmus Comicus 171.1]]; opposed to ὄνομα, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Cratylus” 391b, 436a, 5th-6th c.BC: Andocides Orator 4.27; δύο π... τοιάδε, οἷον Κρατύλος καὶ Κρατύλου εἰκών 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Cratylus” 432b]]; ὡς ἀργαλέον π. ἐστίν with infinitive, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Plutus” 1; οὐδὲ π. οὐθέν ἐστι παρὰ τὰ μεγέθη.. τὰ αἰσθητὰ κεχωρισμένον 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “de Anima” 432a3, compare “Mete.” 379a32, “Ph.” 226b30, 227b28; διαμάχονται περὶ τοῦ λευκὸν ἢ μὴ λευκὸν εἶναι τὸ π. 1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus 2.1109d, compare 1112d; ἐξ ἀζωΐας καὶ ζωῆς συγκείμενον π. 3rd c.AD: Porphyrius Tyrius Philosophus “Sententiae ad intelligibilia ducentes” 21: _plural_, τῶν π. ἀΐδιος ἔσσα 5th-6th c.BC: Philolaus Philosophus 6, compare 3rd c.AD: Democritus Epigrammaticus 164, 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “de Xenophane” 974a25, “Pol.” 1252a24; τὰ μετέωρα π. 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Nubes” 228, compare 250, 741]]; opposed to ὀνόματα, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Cratylus” 39o e, 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 9.15.]]

__II.2.b
contemptuously, thing, creature, κακῷ πράγματι wretched creature, i.e.  the sophist, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Protagoras” 312c]]; τούτῳ τῷ π., i.e.  the demos, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [[prev. author] “Grg.” 520b; ὁ δῆμος ἀσταθμητότατον π. 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 19.136]]; ἄμαχον π., of a woman, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 6.1.36.]]

__II.3
like{πρᾶξις}[Refs 5th c.BC+ [1.2, ὄφελος 1, in 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus, πρῆγμά ἐστι or ἐστί μοι,]] with infinitive, it is advantageous for me, εὕρισκε π. οἱ εἶναι ἐλαύνειν [Refs [1.79, compare 4.11]]: with a negative, εὕρισκέ οἱ οὐ π. εἶναι στρατεύεσθαι [Refs [[prev. author] 7.12: also with _accusative_ et]]infinitive, οὐδὲν ἂν εἴη π. γνώμας ἐμὲ σοὶ ἀποφαίνεσθαι there will be no advantage or need, [Refs [[prev. author] 1.207]]; π. ἂν ἦν μοῦνον the only thing needful, [Refs [[prev. author] 7.130.]]

__II.4
thing of consequence or importance, π. ποιήσασθαι [τι[Refs [] [prev. work] 150; π. οὐδὲν ἐποιήσαντο [prev. author] 6.63]]; οὐδὲν π., ὦ Σώκρατες no matter, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Gorgias” 447b, compare 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Medea” 451; ὡς.. οὐδὲν ὂν π., εἰ καὶ ἀποθάνοι 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Euthyphro” 4d]]; δῆλον ἦν ὅτι π. τι εἴη that there was something the matter, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 4.1.17.]]

__II.4.b
π. ἐστί μοι it concerns me, σφίσι τε καὶ Ἀθηναίοισι εἶναι οὐδὲν π. they had nothing to do with the [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus, 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 5.84, compare 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 18.283]]; ᾧ μὴ π. μὴ εἰσίναι no admittance except on business, [Refs 1st c.BC+ [Sammelb. 6152.22 (1st c.BC):]] with genitive _of things_, οἷς μηδὲν ἦν π. τοῦ πολέμου who were not concerned in the war, [Refs 1st c.AD+ [1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus “Pompeius” 65]]; τὸ σὸν τί ἐστι π.; what is your pursuit or business, what are you about? [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Apologia” 20c, cf. Alcaeus1.104d.]]

__II.4.c
μέγα π. a man of consequence, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 35.15; τὸ μέγα π. ἐν τῇ πόλει 4th-3rd c.BC: Menander Comicus “Σαμία” 175]]; ἦν μέγιστον π. Δημοκήδης παρὰ βασιλέϊ he was made much of by the king, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 3.132]]; π. μέγα φρέατος a fine large tank, [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd c.AD: Alexander Rhetor 179.]]

__II.5
used of a battle, action, affair, ὡς οἱ σωθέντες ἐκ τοῦ π. ἀπέφυγον [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Historia Graeca (Hellenica)” 7.1.17.]]

__II.6
τὸ π. the love-affair of Harmodius and Aristogeiton, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aeschines Orator 1.132.]]

__II.7
fact, opposed to λόγος, ὄνομα, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Topica” 146a3, “SE” 175a8; πρὸς τὸ π. καὶ τὴν ἀλήθειαν [prev. author] “Ph.” 263a17: _plural_, οὐκ ἐχρῆν τῶν π. τὴν γλῶσσαν ἰσχύειν πλέον 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Hecuba” 1188.]]

__II.8
matter in hand, question, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Hippocrates Medicus “περὶ διαίτης ὀξέων” 39; πρὸς τὸ π. 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Meno” 87a, 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Analytica Priora” 70a32, 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 54.26; διαιρεῖν κατὰ τὸ π. 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Politica” 1299b18; ἔξω τοῦ π., see at {ἔξω} 1.2b.]]

__III
in plural, πράγματα,

__III.1
circumstances, affairs, τὰ ἀνθρωπήϊα π. [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.207; ἐν εἰρήνῃ καὶ ἀγαθοῖς π. 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 3.82, compare 1.89]]; τοῖς π. τέθνηκα τοῖς δ᾽ ἔργοισιν οὔ by circumstances, not by acts, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Helena” 286; ἐν τοιούτοις π. 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Memorabilia” 2.7.2, “An.” 2.1.16, etc.; δεινὸς πράγμασι χρῆσθαι 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 1.3, compare 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Historia Graeca (Hellenica)” 3.5.1; τύχη τὰ θνητῶν πράγματ᾽, οὐκ εὐβουλία 4th c.BC: Chaeremon Tragicus 2]]; ἀποτυγχάνειν τῶν π. fail to prosper, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Memorabilia” 4.2.28]]; the condition of a patient, τὰ τῶν νοσεύντων π. [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Hippocrates Medicus “προγνωστικόν” 1 (also in _sing._, ἐξαπίνης ὅλῳ τῷ π. μεταβάλλειν [prev. author] “Acut.” 35]]; so also poetry, ποῦ ποτ᾽ εἰμὶ πράγματο; [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Trachiniae” 375, compare “Aj.” 314).]]

__III.2
state-affairs, τὰ πολιτικὰ π. [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Apologia” 31d]]; ἔστ᾽ ἐν ἡμῖν τῆς πόλεως τὰ π. the fortunes of the state, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Lysistrata” 32]]; a state or empire, τὰ Περσικὰ π. the Persian power, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 3.137; τὰ Περσέων π. [prev. author] 7.50, etc.; διαπεπόρθηται τὰ Περσῶν π. 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Persae” 714; ἐν ταῖς ναυσὶ τῶν Ἑλλήνων τὰ π. ἐγένετο 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 1.74; μὴ ὥσπερ θεῷ νομίζετ᾽ ἐκείνῳ τὰ παρόντα πεπηγέναι π. ἀθάνατα 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 4.8, compare 44, etc.; παρασπάσασθαί τι τῶν ὅλων π. [prev. author] 1.3]]; of government, καταλαμβάνειν τὰ π. [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 6.39, compare 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 3.30 (_passive_); ἔχειν τὰ π. [prev. work] 62, 72,compare 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 6.83; κατέχειν τὰ π. 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 4.2; ἐς μέσον Πέρσῃσι καταθεῖναι τὰ π. 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 3.80]]; οἱ ἐν τοῖς π. those who are in power or office, [LXX+5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 3.28, 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 9.56, 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Politica” 1307b10; οἱ ἐπὶ τοῖς π. ὄντες 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 9.2; οἱ ἐπὶ τῶν π. [prev. author] 18.247, compare 2nd c.BC: Polybius Historicus 3.69.4, LXX.1Mac.3.32]]; ἐν τυραννίδι καὶ πλούτῳ καὶ πράγμασι [Refs 1st c.AD+ [1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus 2.150c]]; τριῶν ἀνδρῶν δημοσίων π. ἀποκαταστάσεως, = Latin triumvir reipublicae constituendae, [Refs 1st c.BC+ [Sammelb. 4224.2 (1st c.BC)]]; κοινωνοὶ τῶν π. [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Historia Graeca (Hellenica)” 2.3.17; νεώτερα π.]]innovations, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Lysias Orator 13.6, 5th-6th c.BC: Isocrates Orator 7.59, etc., compare 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 5.19]]; but εὐνούστατος τοῖς π. a friend to things as they are, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Lysias Orator 12.65.]]

__III.3
fortunes, cause, circumstances, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 7.236, 237; κοινὰ π. 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Iphigenia Taurica” 1062; τέρας γὰρ ὁ βίος καὶ τὰ π. ἐστί μου [prev. author] “Hel.” 260; ἔρρει τἀμὰ π. 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Symposium” 1.15, compare 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Alcestis” 280: τὰ π.]] alone, one's all, one's fortunes, ἐν ᾧπέρ ἐστι πάντα μοι τὰ π. [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Acharnenses” 474]]; ={κτήματα}, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Hippocrates Medicus (“Legal” 5 ?) cited in 1st c.AD: Erotianus Grammaticus: in _sing._, φαῦλον γὰρ ἂν εἴη τὸ ἐμὸν π. 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Hp.Ma.” 286e, compare “Cri.” 53d, “Ap.” 42a.]]

__III.4
business, especially lawbusiness, πρός τινα [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Antipho Orator 6.12, 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 1.128; οὔτε ἐμαυτοῦ οὔτε ἀλλότρια π. πράξας 5th c.BC: Lysias Orator 12.3; δικῶν γὰρ οὐ δέομ᾽ οὐδὲ πραγμάτων 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Vespae” 1426; πράγματα κἀντιγραφάς [prev. author] “Nu.” 471: _metaphorically_ in _sing._, πονηρὸν τὸ π. ἔχειν]] to have a bad case, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Rhetorica” 1415b22.]]

__III.5
in bad sense, trouble, annoyance, ἁπάντων αἰτίους τῶν π. [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Acharnenses” 310]]; πρήγματα ἔχειν, with participle, to have trouble about a thing, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 7.147, compare 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Theaetetus” 174b, etc.; π. ἔχειν ἐν τῷ δείπνῳ 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 1.3.4, etc.; π. λαμβάνειν [prev. author] “Lac.” 2.9]]; π. παρέχειν τινί to cause one trouble, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.155, 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Plutus” 20, +others]]: with infinitive, cause one the trouble of doing, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Phaedo” 115a, 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 4.5.46, 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Vespae” 313; πραγμάτων.. ἀπαλλαγείς [prev. author] “Ach.” 269 (Lyric poetry), compare 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Apologia” 41d, “R.” 406e]]; ἄνευ πραγμάτων, σὺν πράγμασι, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 1.20, 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 6.3.6: less frequently in _sing._, μηδὲν πρῆγμα παρέχειν 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 7.239.]]

deep_entry:
Abbott-Smith / STEPBible (TBESG)
πραγματία (Rec. -εία, as in cl.), -ας, ἡ
(πραγματεύομαι) [in LXX for חֲשַׁל, etc. ;]
__1. careful application, hard work.
__2. business, occupation: pl., 2Ti.2:4.†
(AS)

---

LSJ / STEPBible (TFLSJ)
πραγμᾰτ-εία,
Ionic dialectπρηγμᾰτίη, poetry πραγμᾰτίη [Refs 4th c.AD+ [4th c.AD(?): Manetho Astrologus 1.38]]: ἡ:— prosecution of business, diligent study, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Isocrates Orator 1.44, 5.7, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Cratylus” 408a, +others; πόνων πολλῶν καὶ πραγματείας εἶναι 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 8.48; πλείονος εἶναι πρηγματίης 5th c.BC: Hippocrates Medicus “περὶ ἀρχαίης ἰητρικῇς” 7]]; ἡ μάταιος π. [λογισμῶν] this idle attention to argumentations, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Memorabilia” 4.7.8]]; μετὰ πολλῆς π. with a great deal of trouble, [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [3rd c.BC: Zenon Papyri du Caire 19.4 (3rd c.BC).]]

__II
occupation, business, ἡ π. αὐτῆς (i.e. τῆς ῥητορικῆς) ἅπασα.. εἰς τοῦτο τελευτᾷ [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Gorgias” 453a]]; ἡ τοῦ διαλέγεσθαι π. the business of dialectic, [Refs [[prev. author] “Tht.” 161e]]; τοῦ πολιτικοῦ.. πᾶσα ἡ π. περὶ πόλιν [ἐστί] Arist [Refs [“Pol.” 1274b37, compare “EN” 1105a11]]; ἡ δημηγορικὴ π. the business of oratory, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [[prev. author] “Rh.” 1354b24; ἀπὸ τῆς ἀναισχύντου π. ἀποστῆναι 4th c.BC: Aeschines Orator 3.242]]; πραγματεῖαι official duties, opposed to ἀρχαί, [Refs 2nd c.BC+ [[prev. work]13,compare “PTeb.” 5.143, +others (2nd c.BC)]]; especially law-business, lawsuit, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Isocrates Orator 2.18, +others; ἡ περὶ τὰ δικαστήρια π. [prev. author] 15.31]]: plural, affairs in general, κάτω βλέπειν εἰς ἀνθρώπων πραγματείας [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 500c; μεθισταμένων πραγματειῶν 5th c.BC: Antipho Orator 2.4.9 (nisi to be read πραγμάτων)]]; troubles, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 61.37, 4th-3rd c.BC: Epicurus Philosophus “Epistulae” 1p.28U.]]; πρὸς ἔθνη τὴν π. ἔχειν to have dealings with.., [Refs 1st c.BC+ [1st c.BC-1st c.AD: Strabo Geographus 9.2.2.]]

__II.b
plural, works, of the buildings of Solomon, [LXX.3Ki.9.1.]

__III
treatment of a subject, εἰδέων [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Archytas Tarentinus Philosophus 4]]; ἡ τοῦ ἐπιπέδου π., as a definition of plane geometry, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 528d]]; ἡ Πλάτωνος π. Plato's system, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Metaphysica” 987a30, compare 986a8, 4th-3rd c.BC: Epicurus Philosophus “Epistulae” 1p.3U., 1st c.BC: Philodemus Gadarensis Epigrammaticus “D.” 1.17]]; manner of dealing with, ἡ περὶ τοὺς μάρτυρας π. [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Rhetorica” 1376b4.]]

__III.2
philosophical argument or treatise, [Refs [[prev. author] “Top.” 100a18, 101a26; τοῦ εἰδέναι χάριν ἡ π. [prev. author] “Ph.” 194b18; ἡ παροῦσα π. οὐ θεωρίας ἕνεκα [prev. author] “EN” 1103b26]]; the subject of such a treatise, τρεῖς αἱ π. [Refs 1st c.BC+ [[prev. author] “Ph.” 198a30, compare “SE” 183b4; ἡ περὶ τῶν ἀγαθῶν ἐκδοθεῖσα π. 1st c.BC-1st c.AD: Strabo Geographus 1.2.2, etc.]]

__III.3
systematic or scientific historical treatise, [Refs 2nd c.BC+ [2nd c.BC: Polybius Historicus 1.1.4, 1.3.1, 1st c.BC: Diodorus Siculus Historicus 1.1, 1st c.BC: Dionysius Halicarnassensis 1.74, 2nd c.AD: Lucianus Sophista “Hist.Conscr.” 13]]; Τρωϊκὴ π. the legends of the Trojan war, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Arg. Sophocles Tragicus]]Aj.; π. συνέταξεν ἐν δράματι τῶν Δαρδάνου πράξεων τὰς μνημοσύνας [Refs [“BMus.Inscription” 3.444.18 (from Iasus).]]

__III.4
magical operation, spell, ἡ Σολομῶνος π. [Refs [“PMag.Par.” 1.853, compare776.]]

deep_entry:
Abbott-Smith / STEPBible (TBESG)
πραγματεύομαι
(πρᾶγμα), [in LXX: 3Ki.10:22 B, 3Ki.9:19 A (חָשַׁק), Dan LXX 8:27 (מְלָאכָה ־אֵת עָשָׂה) * ;]
__1. to busy oneself.
__2. to be engaged in business, esp. to trade: Luk.19:13 (cf. δια-πραγματεύομαι).†
(AS)

---

LSJ / STEPBible (TFLSJ)
πραγμᾰτ-εύομαι,
Ionic dialect πρηγμ-, aorist ἐπραγματευσάμην, Ionic dialect ἐπρηγμ-, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Hippocrates Medicus “ἐπιδημίαι” 6.8.32, 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Oeconomicus” 10.9, etc.]]; also ἐπραγματεύθην, Ionic dialect ἐπρηγμ-, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 2.87, 5th-6th c.BC: Isocrates Orator 12.249]]: perfect πεπραγμάτευμαι [Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. author] 11.1, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Phaedo” 99d, 100b, +others]]; also in passive sense, see below:—busy oneself, take trouble, ἀπέδωκαν τὸν νεκρὸν οὐδὲν ἔτι πρηγματευθέντες Hdt.[same place],[Refs 5th c.BC+ [compare 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Cratylus” 437c; π. περὶ σωφροσύνης [prev. author] “R.” 430d, compare “Cra.” 425c; περὶ τὰ ὄντα [prev. author] “Tht.” 187a, compare 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Memorabilia” 4.2.7, 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Ethica Nicomachea” 1102a22, etc.]]; πολλὰ ἐπί τινι π. work at at thing, labour to bring it about, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Memorabilia” 1.3.15; πρός τι 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Eryxias” 398a]]; πραγματεύονται ὅπως ἄρξουσι exert themselves to.., [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Respublica Lacedaemoniorum” 14.5: _absolutely_, 4th-3rd c.BC: Theophrastus Philosophus “Historia Plantarum” 4.4.1]]; μηδὲν πραγματεύου do not worry, [Refs [[prev. author] “Char.” 18.9]]: c.infinitive, exert oneself to.., [Refs 1st c.AD+ [1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus “Themistocles” 19.]]

__2
to be engaged in business, spend one's time in business, ὅληντὴννύκτα all nightlong, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 2.4.26; π.καὶ κακοπαθεῖν τὸν βίον ἅπαντα 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Ethica Nicomachea” 1176b29, compare 1122a9]]; simply, conduct a business, [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [3rd c.BC: Zenon Papyri du Caire 199.11 (3rd c.BC)]]; transact business, of clerks, [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [[prev. work] 647.11 (3rd c.BC)]]; π. ἀπὸ ἐμπορίας καὶ δανεισμῶν make money by trade and loans, [Refs 1st c.AD+ [1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus “Cat.Mi.” 50, compare “Sull.” 17, etc.]]; οἱ πραγματευόμενοι, = Latin negotiatores, [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [“OGI” 532.6 (from Galatia), compare “SIG” 797.10 (Assus, 1st c.AD): with _accusative_, π. τὸ συνηγορικὸν καὶ (τὸ) ἐπιδέκατον, of a tax-farmer, “Ostr.” 1537 (2nd c.BC), “PLeid.F” in “Ostr.” i ; τὴν ὑϊκὴν π. “PSI” 4.384.2 (3rd c.BC)]]; generally, of officials, to be employed in public affairs, [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [PGnom. 174 (2nd c.AD), etc.]]

__II
with accusative of things, take in hand, treat laboriously, be engaged in, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Protagoras” 361d, “Hp.Ma.” 304c, 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 18.26, etc.]]; undertake, τὸν δεύτερον πλοῦν [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Phaedo” 99d.]]

__II.2
of authors, elaborate a work, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Nubes” 526]]; of a science, work out, ἃ θέλει [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Archytas Tarentinus Philosophus 4]]; treat of, περὶ φύσεως πάντα [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Metaphysica” 989b33, compare 4th-3rd c.BC: Epicurus Philosophus “De rerum natura - Wien. Stud.” 15.34; περί τινος 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Physica” 193b31; περί τι [prev. author] “Metaphorical” 1025b17, 1st c.BC: Philodemus Gadarensis Epigrammaticus “Mus.” p.96K., +others]]; τοιαύτην οὐκ ἐπραγματεύθησαν ἀκριβολογίαν περὶ τὰς φλέβας did not use such precision in treating of.., [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Historia Animalium” 513a9.]]

__II.3
of historians, treat systematically, τὰς πράξεις [Refs 2nd c.BC+ [2nd c.BC: Polybius Historicus 1.4.3: _absolutely_, οἱ πραγματευόμενοι]]systematic historians, [Refs [[prev. author] 5.33.5, etc.]]

Abbott-Smith / STEPBible (TBESG)
πράσσω
(Att.. -ττω, and so Act.17:7 Rec.; cf. M, Pr., 25, 45), [in LXX chiefly for עָשָׂה, פָּעַל ;]
= Lat agere, as ποιέω (which see) = facere,
__1. to do, practise, be engaged in: Act.19:19, 36, 1Co.9:17; τ. ἴδια π., to mind one's own business (τὰ ἑαυτοῦ, Soph., Plat.), 1Th.4:11; intrans., to act, Act.17:7.
__2. to achieve, effect, accomplish, perform: Act.26:20, 26 Rom.7:15 9:11, 2Co.5:10, Php.4:9; νόμον (ICC, in l), Rom.2:25; of unworthy acts (for WH. usually ποιέω in cl.), to commit, do: Luk.22:23 23:41, Jhn.3:20 5:29, Act.3:17 5:35 16:28 25:11, 25 26:9, 31, Rom.1:32 (ICC, in l), Rom.2:1-3 7:19 13:4, 1Co.5:2, 2Co.12:21, Gal.5:21.
__3. to transact, manage, hence, of payment, to exact (cl.): Luk.3:13 19:23.
__4. Reflexively, of state or condition, to do or fare Æsch., Hdt., al.): Eph.6:21; εὖ π. (see M, Pr., 228 f.), Act.15:29.†
SYN.: see: ποιέω  (AS)

πράσσω,
Epic dialect and Ionic dialect πρήσσω, Attic dialect πράττω (first in [Refs 5th c.BC+ [“IG” 12.7.11, +others, 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus and 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus)]], Cretan dialect πράδδω [Refs [“Leg.Gort.” 1.35]]: future πράξω, Ionic dialect πρήξω: aorist ἔπραξα, Ionic dialect ἔπρηξα: perfect πέπραχα, Ionic dialect πέπρηχα, (transitive) [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 5.106, 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Historia Graeca (Hellenica)” 5.2.32, “Cyr.” 3.1.15, 4th-3rd c.BC: Dinarchus Orator 3.21, 4th-3rd c.BC: Menander Comicus 619, “IG” 9(2).517.36 (Larissa, 3rd c.BC), “PHib.” 1.80.11 (3rd c.BC), (_intransitive_) 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Comicus 187 codices, 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Rhetorica ad Alexandrum” 1440a36]]: pluperfect ἐπεπράχει (ν) (transitive) [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus [same place], (_intransitive_) 2nd c.AD: Appianus Historicus “Bella Civilia” 5.83]]: perfect [Refs 5th c.BC+ [2 πέπρᾱγα, _Ionic dialect_ πέπρηγα, (_intransitive_) 5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “P.” 2.73, 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 2.172, 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Plutus” 629, “Ra.” 302, 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Historia Graeca (Hellenica)” 1.4.2, (_transitive_) 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Ethica Nicomachea” 1168b35, +others, “SIG” 364.70 (Ephesus, 3rd c.BC)]]: pluperfect ἐπεπράγεσαν (intransitive) [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 2.4, 7.24]]:— perfect πέπραγα Attic dialect, πέπραχα Hellenistic, accusative [Refs 5th c.BC+ [to Moer. p.293 P., 2nd c.AD: Phrynichus Atticista “Praeparatio Sophistica” p.103 5th c.BC: Bacchylides Lyricus]], but see above:—middle, future πράξομαι [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Antipho Orator “fragment” 67, 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Historia Graeca (Hellenica)” 6.2.36 (also in _passive_ sense, 5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “P.” 4.243 (probably), 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 452a)]]: aorist ἐπραξαμην [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Tyrannus” 287, 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 4.65, etc.:]] —passive, future (see.above), also πραχθήσομαι [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aeschines Orator 3.98, 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Rhetorica” 1359a11, etc.]]; future [Refs 5th c.BC+ [3 πεπράξομαι 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Coloneus” 861, 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Aves” 847, 5th c.BC: Eupolis Comicus 9.3 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator]]: aorist ἐπράχθην [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Trachiniae” 679, 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 4.54, etc.]]: perfect πέπραγμαι [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Prometheus Vinctus” 75, etc. (sometimes in middle sense, see below vi). [ᾱ by nature, as is shown by the _Ionic dialect_ form πρήσσω, and by the accent in πρᾶγμα, πρᾶξις, etc.]]]

__I
in Epic dialect only, pass through, pass over, δὶς τόσσον ἅλα πρήσσοντες ἀπῆμεν [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 9.491; ῥίμφα πρήσσοντε κέλευθον 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 14.282, 23.501; ῥίμφα πρήσσουσι κέλευθον 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 13.83; ὁδὸν πρήσσουσιν ὁδῖται “hymnus ad Mercurium” 203: with _genitive_, ἵνα πρήσσωμεν ὁδοῖο 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 24.264, 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 15.219]]; ὄφρα πρ. ὁδοῖο[Refs [[prev. work] 47; ἵνα πρήσσῃσιν ὁδοῖο 3.476]]: Grammars  note that this sense is found only in present, [Refs [“Anecdota Graeca - MSS. Bibl. Oxon.” 1.355, “Etymologicum Magnum” 688.1.]]

__II
experience certain for- tunes, fare well or ill, ὁ στόλος οὕτως ἔπρηξε [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 3.26, compare 4.77, 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 7.24; so ὡς ἔπρηξε 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 7.18; κατὰ νόον π. [prev. author] 4.97, compare 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Equites” 549; πράξασαν ὡς ἔπραξεν 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Agamemnon” 1288; εὖ πέπραγεν, ὅτι.. 5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “P.” 2.73, compare 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.24, 42, etc.; φλαύρως π. τῷ στόλῳ [prev. author] 6.94; π. καλῶς 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Prometheus Vinctus” 979; χαλεπώτατα π. 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 8.95; ταπεινῶς π. 5th-6th c.BC: Isocrates Orator 5.64; ὅστις καλῶς πράττει, οὐχὶ καὶ εὖ πράττε; 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus Alcaeus1.116b; π. εὐτυχῶς 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Antigone” 701; κάλλιστα 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Heraclidae” 794]]; μακαρίως, εὐδαιμόνως, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Plutus” 629, 802]]: frequently with neuter pronoun or adjective, εὖ π. τι [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Tyrannus” 1006, compare “OC” 391; μηδὲν εὖ π. 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Memorabilia” 1.6.8; χρηστόν τι π. 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Plutus” 341; καλά 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 6.16; χείρω [prev. author] 7.71; μεγάλα 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Iphigenia Aulidensis” 346; πάντ᾽ ἀγαθά 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Ranae” 302, compare “Eq.” 683 (Lyric poetry); εὐδαίμονα 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Electra” 1359 (_anapaest meter_); πολλὰ καὶ ἀγαθά 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 6.4.8; οἷον ἥθελεν 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Coloneus” 1704 (Lyric poetry); πράξας ἅπερ ηὔχου 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Orestes” 355 (_anapaest meter_), compare 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Memorabilia” 3.9.14.]]

__III
achieve, effect, accomplish, οὔ τι [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 1.562, 11.552, 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 2.191, etc.; οὐδέ τι ἔργον ἐνθάδ᾽ ἔτι πρήξει 19.324, compare 16.88; χρῆμα μὲν οὐ πρήξεις, σὺ δ᾽ ἐτώσια πόλλ᾽ ἀγορεύσεις 8th-7th c.BC: Hesiodus Epicus “Opera et Dies” 402]]; κλέος ἔπραξεν won it, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “I.” 5(4).8]]; ἔπραξε δεσμόν achieved bondage, i.e. brought it on himself, [Refs [[prev. author] “P.” 2.40; τινὰ Νηρεΐδων π. ἄκοιτιν [prev. author] “N.” 5.36]]; ὕμνον π. grant power of song, [Refs [[prev. work] 9.3]]; λεόντεσσι π. φόνον do slaughter upon them,[Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. work] 3.46; τὴν Κυπρίων ἀπόστασιν π. 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 5.113]]; π. εἰρήνην, φιλίαν, bring it about, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 3.7, 18.162]]; π. τι παρά τινος get something from.., ὧν δέονται πάντων πεπραγότες εἶεν παρὰ βασιλέως [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Historia Graeca (Hellenica)” 1.4.2; ἐλπὶς πράξειν τι παρὰ τῶν θεῶν ἀγαθόν 5th-6th c.BC: Isocrates Orator 2.20]]; also, attempt, plot, δήμου κατάλυσιν [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Andocides Orator 3.6: with _dative_ _person_, δαίμοσιν π. φίλα 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Prometheus Vinctus” 660; Αοξίᾳ χάριν 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Ion” 37, compare 896 (Lyric poetry), “El.” 1133, etc.; σὺ τοῦτο πράξεις ὥστε..; 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Eumenides” 896]]:—passive, πέπρακται τοὖργον [Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. author] “Pr.” 75; φεῦ φεῦ πέπρακται 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Hippolytus” 680; τὰ πεπραγμένα 5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “O.” 2.15, etc.; ἡ ἐπὶ τοῖς πεπρ. ἀδοξία 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 1.11; τὰ πεπρ. λῦσαι [prev. author] 24.76; τὰ πραχθέντα 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Prometheus Vinctus” 683, etc.]]; τὰ ἔργα τῶν πραχθέντων the facts of what took place, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 1.22; οὐ γὰρ ἂν τό γε πραχθὲν ἀγένητον θείη 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Protagoras” 324b.]]

__III.2
absolutely, effect an object, be successful, δὸς Τηλέμαχον πρήξαντα νέεσθαι [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 3.60; ἔπρηξας καὶ ἔπειτα 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 18.357.]]

__III.3
of sexual intercourse, ἐπράχθη τὰ μέγιστα [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [3rd c.BC: Theocritus Poeta Bucolicus 2.143.]]

__III.4
to be busy with, σὺ μὲν τὰ σαυτῆς πρᾶσσ᾽ mind your own business, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Electra” 678; πράττων ἔκαστος τὸ αὑτοῦ 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Phaedrus” 247a, compare “Plt.” 307e; τὰ αὑτοῦ π. καὶ μὴ πολυπραγμονεῖν [prev. author] “R.” 433a, compare 400e, etc. (whereas πολλὰ π. ={πολυπραγμονεῖν}, 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 5.33, 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Hercules Furens” 266, 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Ranae” 228, etc.); φιλοσόφου τὰ αὑτοῦ πράξαντος καὶ οὐ πολυπραγμονήσαντος 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Gorgias” 526c, compare “Ap.” 33a, etc.]]; οὐδ᾽ εὖ.. οἰκοῦνται αἱ πόλεις, ὅταν τὰ αὑτῶν ἕκαστοι πράττωσι (ironical) [Refs [[prev. author] Alcaeus1.127b]]; μὴ τὰ αὑτῶν π. not to act their part, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. author] “R.” 452c; π. τὰ δέοντα 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Memorabilia” 3.8.1.]]

__III.5
manage affairs, do business, act, εἰπεῖν τε καὶ πρᾶξαι [Refs [[prev. work] 2.9.4, compare 2.8.6]]; πράττειν τὰ πολιτικὰ πράγματα, τὰ τῆς πόλεως, manage state-affairs, take part in government, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Apologia” 31d, 5th c.BC: Lysias Orator 16.20; τὰ Ἀθηναίων 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Symposium” 216a; οἱ τὰ κοινὰ π. καὶ πολιτευόμενοι 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Politica” 1324b1: _absolutely_, without any addition, ἱκανωτάτω λέγειν τε καὶ πράττειν, of able statesmen, 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Memorabilia” 1.2.15, compare 4.2.1, 4; πολιτεύεσθαι καὶ π. 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 18.45, compare 59, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Protagoras” 317a.]]

__III.6
generally, transact, negotiate, manage, οἱ πράξαντες πρὸς αὐτὸν τὴν λῆψιν τῆς πόλεως [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 4.114]]; Θηβαίοις τὰ πράγματα π. manage matters for their interest, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 19.77:]] —so in passive, τῷ Ἱπποκράτει τὰ.. πράγματα ἀπό τινων ἀνδρῶν.. ἐπράσσετο matters were negotiated with him by.., [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 4.76]]: but frequently absolutely, treat, negotiate, manage, act, οἱ πράσσοντες αὐτῷ [Refs [[prev. work] 110, compare 5.76; π. πρός τινα [prev. author] 2.5, 4.73, etc.]]; ἐς (variant{πρὸς}) τοὺς βαρβάρους, ἐς τοὺς Εἵλωτας, [Refs [[prev. author] 1.131, 132]]:—passive, ἐπράττετο οὐ πρὸς τοὺς ἄλλους [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aeschines Orator 3.64; also π. τι ὑπὲρ τῶν κοινῶν 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 26.2; π. ὑπὲρ τῆς πόλεως τὰ πάτρια [prev. author] 59.73; π. περὶ εἰρήνης 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Historia Graeca (Hellenica)” 6.3.3; π. τῇ δύναιτο ἄριστα 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 5.30; π. ὡς ἄριστα καὶ πιστότατα 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 1.129; οἱ πράσσοντες]]the traitors, [Refs [[prev. author] 4.89, 113]]:—followed by dependent clauses, πρᾶσσε καὶ τὰ ἐμὰ καὶ τὰ σὰ ὅπῃ κάλλιστα ἕξει [Refs [[prev. author] 1.129; ἐς τὴν Πελοπόννησον ἔπρασσεν, ὅπῃ ὠφελία τις γενήσεται [prev. work] 65; π. ὅπως πόλεμος γένηται [prev. work] 57; π. ὅπως τιμωρήσονται [prev. work] 56, compare 3.4, 70]], etc.: with accusative et infinitive, μὴ δεῦρο πλεῖν τὴν ναῦν ἔπραττεν [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 32.22.]]

__III.6.b
especially of secret practices and intrigues, εἴ τι μὴ ξὺν ἀργύρῳ ἐπράσσετ᾽ ἐνθένδ᾽ unless some bribery was being practised, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Tyrannus” 125; καί τι αὐτῷ καὶ ἐπράσσετο ἐς τὰς πόλεις προδοσίας πέρι 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 4.121, compare 5.83; μετάστασις ἐπράττετο 5th c.BC: Lysias Orator 30.10; τούτοις ἔπρασσον τὴν πόλιν 2nd c.BC: Polybius Historicus 4.17.12]]; νῦν δ᾽ αὔτ᾽ Ἀτρεῖδαι φωτὶ παντουργῷ φρένας ἔπραξαν have jobbed them (the arms) away to a villain, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Ajax” 446.]]

__IV
practise, πόνῳ π. θεοδμάτους ἀρετάς [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “I.” 6(5).11; δίκαια ἢ ἄδικα 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Apologia” 28b, etc.; ταῦτ᾽ ἔπραξάν τε καὶ ἔλεξαν 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 5.1.1; ἃ καὶ λέγειν ὀκνοῦμεν οἱ πεπραχότες 4th-3rd c.BC: Menander Comicus 619]]: then absolutely, act, π. ἔργῳ μὲν σθένος βουλαῖσι δὲ φρήν [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “N.” 1.26]]; ὡς πράττοντες as doing, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 527a]]; μεθ᾽ ἡμῶν ἔπραττεν, i. e. he took our side, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Isaeus Orator 5.14.]]

__IV.2
study, δράματα [Refs [10th c.AD: Suidas Legal icographus]] see at {Ἀριστοφάνη; συλλογισμούς} [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd c.AD: Arrianus Historicus “Epicteti Dissertationes” 2.17.27]]; ἐν τοῖς πραττομένοις in the poems which are now studied, made the subject of commentaries, [Refs 2nd c.BC+ [Scholia 2nd c.BC: Nicander Epicus “Theriaca” 11.]]

__V
with double accusative person et of things, πράττειν τινά τι do something to one, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Helena” 1394, 5th-6th c.BC: Isocrates Orator 12.93; ἀγαθόν τι π. τὴν πόλιν 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Ecclesiazusae” 108.]]

__VI
exact payment from one, αὐτοὺς ἑκατὸν τάλαντα ἔπρηξαν [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 3.58]]; πράσσει με τόκον he makes me pay interest, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [Batrachomyomachia 185; π. τινὰ χρέος 5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “O.” 3.7, compare “P.” 9.104; ὅσοι πράξεις πεπράγασιν “SIG” 364.70 (Ephesus, 3rd c.BC)]]; τοὐφειλόμενον π. Δίκη [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Choephori” 311 (_anapaest meter_); ἀντίποινα [prev. author] “Pers.” 476]]: frequently of tax-gatherers or other collectors of public debt, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [“IG” 12.116.16, +others, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Leges” 774d; π. τὰς εἰσφοράς 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 22.77, etc.]]; φόρον ἔπρησσον παρ᾽ ἑκάστων obtained or demanded from.., [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.106]]: with accusative person, press for payment, μὴ π. τοὺς ὀφειλέτας [Refs 2nd c.BC+ [2nd c.BC: Polybius Historicus 38.11.10]]; π. τινά τι ὑπέρ τινος demand from one as the price for a thing, [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd c.AD: Lucianus Sophista “Vit.Auct.” 18: _metaphorically_, φόνον π.]] exact punishment or vengeance for a murder: hence, avenge, punish, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Eumenides” 624; τὰ περὶ τὸν φόνον ἀγριωτέρως π. 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Leges” 867d:]] —passive, ὑπὸ βασιλέως πεπραγμένος φόρους called on to pay up the tribute, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 8.5]]; πραχθεὶς ὑπὸτῶνδε [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Lysias Orator 9.21 codices, compare 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Leges” 921c]]:—middle, exact for oneself, πράξασθαί τινα μισθόν [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “O.” 10(11).30]]; ἀργύριον, χρήματα, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 2.126, 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 4.65, compare 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Ranae” 561, etc.; τὴν διπλασίαν π. τὸν ὑποφεύγοντα 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Leges” 762b, compare 2nd c.BC: Polybius Historicus 5.54.11; π. τοὺς ἐξάγοντας τριακοστήν 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 20.32; πράσσεσθαι χρέος 5th c.BC: Antipho Orator “fragment” 67]]; φόρους πράσσεσθαι ἀπό, ἐκ τῶν πόλεων, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 8.5, 37;
