(The ι subscr. is frequently written in codices, but Πρᾶος is written in [Refs 4th c.BC+ [“IG” 22.1928.20 (_proper name_, 4th c.BC), “IGRom.” 4.504 (Pergam.), compare 9th c.AD: Photius Legal icographus, etc., “Etymologicum Gudianum” 478.31]]; πραύτερος is found once in codices, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Ti.” [prev. cited] (proved wrong by πραΰς “Comica Adespota” in “Gött. Nachr.” 1922.31, πραέα (_neuter_ _plural_) in “PCair.Zen.” 33.12 (3rd c.BC), πραέως “UPZ” 144.6 (2nd c.BC), and by the absence of iota in _Ionic dialect_ πρηΰς))]]:—mild, soft, gentle (not in [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” or 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey”):]]

__1
of things, πρηῢ σέλας [Refs 5th c.BC+ [“H.Hom.” 8.10; πραῢς ὄαρος 5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “P.” 4.136]]; mild, πυρετοί Hp.[same place]; ἰητρείη πρηεῖα [Refs [[prev. author] “Art.” 69]]; of sound, soft, gentle, τὴν φωνὴν πραοτέραν ποιοῦνται [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Symposium” 1.10; ἀνέμων πρηΰτατε Ζέφυρε “Anthologia Graeca” 6.349 (1st c.BC: Philodemus Gadarensis Epigrammaticus)]]; ὠδῖνες[Refs 1st c.BC+ [[prev. work] 244 (1st c.BC-1st c.AD: Crinagoras Epigrammaticus); κέντρον [prev. work] 229 ([prev. author]).]]

__2
of persons, mild, gentle, meek, πραῢς ἀστοῖς [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “P.” 3.71; πᾶσιν ἵλεώς τε καὶ πρᾶος 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 566e]]; πρὸς τοὺς οἰκείους π.[Refs [[prev. work] 375c; π. τὸ ἦθος [prev. author] “Phdr.” 243c; π. ἐν τοῖς λόγοις [prev. author] “Euthd.” 303d]]; especially after having been angry, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 2.181 (_comparative_)]]; ὁ θὴρ ὅδ᾽ ἡμῖν π., of Dionysus, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Bacchae” 436]]; of a horse, gentle, ἀλλήλοις πραότεροι [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 2.1.29]]; of other animals, tame, ἰχθύων μεγάλων καὶ πραέων [Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. author] “An.” 1.4.9, compare 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Historia Animalium” 488b22; ζῷα.. πραέα πρὸς τοὺς ἀνθρώπους 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Oeconomicus” 15.4: proverbial, πραΰτερος μολόχας 5th c.BC: Epicharmus Comicus 153; also, τόπος ἡμερώτερος καὶ πραότερος 5th-6th c.BC: Isocrates Orator 9.67.]]

__3
of actions, feelings, etc., mild, τιμωρίαι πραότεραι [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Leges” 867b; πραότεραι ἡδοναί [prev. work] 815e; λόγοι, ἤθη, φύσις, [prev. work] 888a, 930a, “R.” 375c; ὄσσοισι πρηέσιν δέρκευ “BMus.Inscription” 921b8 (Branchidae, 1st-2nd c.AD)]]; τὰ πραέα caresses, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “de Equitandi ratione” 9.10]]; πραότερα πάσχειν [Refs [Pl  “Cri.” 49b.]]

__II
making mild, taming, φάρμακον πραῢ τείνων ἀμφὶ γένυι, of a bridle, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “O.” 13.85; προκινεῖν αὐτὸν [τὸν ἵππον] ὡς πραοτάτοις σημείοις 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “de Equitandi ratione” 9.3.]]

__III
adverb πράως, mildly, gently, πράως πείθειν τινά, φέρειν τι, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 589c, “Cri.” 43b; πράως ἔχειν πρός τι [prev. author] “Ly.” 211e]]; πράως λέγειν τὸ πάθος to speak lightly of it, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 1.5.14]]; πράως διακεῖσθαι, opposed to ὀργίζεσθαι, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 21.183; πράως, μὴ πικρῶς [prev. author] 18.265]]; in physical sense, gently, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th c.AD: Oribasius Medicus “fragment” 134: _comparative_, πραότερον προδιδάσκειν, κολάζειν, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Gorgias” 489d, “Phd.” 94d]]; πραοτέρως (variant{-υτέρως}) ἔχειν τινί [Refs 1st c.AD+ [1st c.AD: Josephus Historicus “Antiquitates Judaicae” 17.6.4]]: superlative, φέρειν.. ὡς πραότωτα [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 387e]]: later form πραέως (πράως [Ἀττικοί], οὐ πραέως [Refs 2nd c.BC+ [9th c.AD: Photius Legal icographus, etc.), “UPZ” 144.6 (2nd c.BC), 1st c.BC: Diodorus Siculus Historicus 1.36, 1st c.AD: Dioscorides (Dioscurides) Medicus 1.13, uncertain in “Comica Adespota” 336.5 (compare πρατίας)]], etc.: Ionic dialect πρηέως conjecture in [Refs 3rd c.AD+ [3rd c.AD: Democritus Epigrammaticus 46 (πράως and πραέως codices)]]. (Cogn. with Sanskrit prīṇā´ti 'love, give pleasure to', Gothic frijon 'love', frijonds 'friend'.)

πρέπ-ω,
imperfect ἔπρεπον, which were the tenses chiefly in use: future πρέψω [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Eumenides” 995 (_anapaest meter_), 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Politicus” 269c, 288c]]: aorist ἔπρεψα [Refs [[prev. author] “Chrm.” 158c:]] — properly of impressions on the senses,

__1
on the eye, to be clearly seen, to be conspicuous among a number, ὁ δ᾽ ἔπρεπε καὶ διὰ πάντων [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 12.104; μετὰ δὲ π. ἀγρομένοισιν 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 8.172, 8th-7th c.BC: Hesiodus Epicus “Theogonia” 92]]; to be distinguished in or by a thing, φάρεσιν μελαγχίμοις [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Choephori” 12, compare “Th.” 124 (Lyric poetry), 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Alcestis” 512, 1050; π. παρηῒς φοινίοις ἀμυγμοῖς 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Choephori” 24 (Lyric poetry)]]; shine forth, show itself, πειρῶντι χρυσὸς ἐν βασάνῳ π. [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “P.” 10.67; πανσέληνος ἐν σάκει π. 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Septem contra Thebas” 390, compare “Pers.” 239 (troch.), “Ag.” 389 (Lyric poetry); πρέπουσά θ᾽ ὡς ἐν γραφαῖς [prev. work] 242 (Lyric poetry)]]; ἐπί τοι πρέπει ὄμμασιν αἰδώς [Refs 5th c.BC+ [“hymnus ad Cererem” 214; Ζεὺς πρέπων δι᾽ αἰθέρος 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Helena” 216 (Lyric poetry)]]: sometimes with participle, to be clearly seen as doing or being, ὁ φρυκτὸς ἀγγέλλων πρέπει [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Agamemnon” 30]]; σπλάγχνα.. πρέπουσ᾽ ἔχοντες[Refs [[prev. work] 1222, compare “Eu.” 995 (_anapaest meter_).]]

__2
on the ear, βοὰ π. the cry sounds loud and clear, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “N.” 3.67, compare 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Agamemnon” 321.]]

__3
on the smell, to be strong or rank, ὅμοιος ἀτμὸς ὥσπερ ἐκ τάφου π. [Refs [[prev. work] 1311.]]

__II
to be conspicuously like, resemble, π. τινὶ εἶδος to be like one in form, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “P.” 2.38; πρέποντα.. ταύρῳ δέμας 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Supplices” 301; εἴ τι σῇ δοκεῖ πρέπειν γυναικί 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Alcestis” 1121; πρέπεις.. θυγατέρων μορφὴν μιᾷ [prev. author] “Ba.” 917: with]]infinitive, τοῦδε γὰρ δράμημα φωτὸς Περσικὸν πρέπει μαθεῖν his running is like Persian to behold, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Persae” 247, compare “Supp.” 719]]; more frequently with ὡς or ὥστε, πρέπει ὡς τύραννος εἰσορᾶν [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Electra” 664; ὡς πένθιμος πρέπεις ὁρᾶν 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Supplices” 1056; πρέπει γ᾽ ὥστε θὴρ ἄγραυλος φόβῃ [prev. author] “Ba.” 1188 (Lyric poetry).]]

__III
to be conspicuously fitting, beseem, with dative person, θνατὰ θνατοῖσι πρέπει [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “I.” 5(4).16; τοῖς ὀλβίοις γε καὶ τὸ νικᾶσθαι πρέπει 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Agamemnon” 941, compare 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Charmides” 158c, etc.; with Preps., ποῦ τάδ᾽ ἐν χρηστοῖς πρέπε; 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Heraclidae” 510; οἷα δὴ εἰς πλῆθος πρέπει 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 2.1.24]]: with participle, ὅ τι γιγνόμενον ἂν πρέποι [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Epinomis” 976c, compare “Plt.” 269c, 288c]]; πρέποι γὰρ ἂν (i.e. λεχθεῖσα) [Refs [[prev. author] “Sph.” 219c.]]

__III.2
frequently in participle, ὕμνοι πρέποντες γάμοις [Refs [[prev. author] “R.” 460a, etc.]]; especially in participle neuter, πρέπον τε εἶναι καὶ ἁρμόττειν [Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. author] “Grg.” 503e; ἤν τι ἄλλο π. δοκῇ εἶναι 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 6.25; τὸ π. τῇ γραφῇ 2nd c.BC: Polybius Historicus 2.40.3: rarely with _genitive_, π. ἦν δαίμονος τοὐμοῦ τόδε 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Ajax” 534, compare 1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus “Caesar” 14, Thom.Mag. p.306R.]]; τὸ π. that which is seemly, propriety, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Hp.Ma.” 294a; πρὸς τὸ μέτριον καὶ τὸ π. [prev. author] “Plt.” 284e, etc.: _plural_, πρέποντα πάσχειν 5th c.BC: Antipho Orator 3.3.9; πρέποντα τῇ συγγενείᾳ ποιοῦντες 5th-6th c.BC: Isocrates Orator 10.23.]]

__III.3
rarely with personal subject, πρέπων ἔφυς πρὸ τῶνδε φωνεῖν art the fit person to.., [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Tyrannus” 9]]; Πομπήϊος.. πάνυ τοῖς ἔπεσι πρέπων suiting them, [Refs 1st c.AD+ [1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus “Pompeius” 72, compare “Publ.” 17.]]

__III.4
mostly impersonal, πρέπει it is fitting, both of outward circumstances and moral fitness, with dative person et infinitive, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 9.79, etc.; οὐ πρέπει νῷν.. δάσασθαι 5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “P.” 4.147; πρέπει ἐσλοῖσιν ὑμνεῖσθαι [prev. author] “fragment” 121, compare 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Agamemnon” 483 (Lyric poetry), 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Hippolytus” 115, etc.: with]]infinitive unexpressed, πρέπει γοῦν σοι [ἀποκρίνεσθαι] [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Historia Graeca (Hellenica)” 4.1.37.]]

__III.4.b
with accusative person et infinitive, πρέπει τὸν Αἰνησιδάμου ἐγκωμίων τε μελέων λυρᾶν τε τυγχανέμεν [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “O.” 2.46, compare 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Supplices” 203, 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Trachiniae” 728, 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 1.86, etc.]]

__III.4.c
with infinitive only, πρέπει γαρυέμεν [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “N.” 7.82, compare “P.” 5.43, 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Septem contra Thebas” 656, “Ag.” 636, etc.]]

__III.4.d
with infinitive understood, an accusative may be subject, ἀπήλλαξαν οὕτω ὡς κείνους ἔπρεπε [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 8.68.α᾽,compare 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Supplices” 195, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Protagoras” 312b; or object, τείσασθαι οὕτως, ὡς κείνους [τείσασθαι] πρέπει 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 4.139]]; so with dative of indirect object, [Refs [[prev. author] 8.114.]]

__IV
transitive, liken, τινί τι [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Agamemnon” 1328 (cited in 9th c.AD: Photius Legal icographus, etc.).]]

πρᾱν-ής, ές,
Ionic dialect πρηνής (also in [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Meteorologica” 350a11, “Spir.” 484b29, “fragment” 106, 1st c.AD: Josephus Historicus “Antiquitates Judaicae” 18.3.1, 19.8.2, 1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus 2.680a, “Tim.” 11, 2nd c.AD: Galenus Medicus “de Usu Partium” 2.2, 7.22, “PMag.Par.” 1.194, etc.)]], genitive έος, Attic dialect contraction οῦς:—of posture, with the face downwards, lying on the front, falling forwards, opposed to ὕπτιος, πρηνεῖς τε καὶ ὕπτιοι ἔκπεσον ἵππων [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 11.179; ἐκ δίφροιο.. ἐξεκυλίσθη πρηνὴς ἐν κονίῃσιν ἐπὶ στόμα 6.43, compare 2.418, 4.544, 8th-7th c.BC: Hesiodus Epicus “Scutum Herculis” 365; πρηνὴς ἐπὶ γαίῃ κεῖτο ταθείς 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 21.118; mostly with Verbs of falling, πρηνὴς κάππεσε, ἤριπε, ἐλιάσθη, 16.413, 5.58, 15.543]]; πρηνέα.. τανύσσας [Ἕκτορα[Refs [] 23.25; κατὰ πρηνὲς βαλέειν Πριάμοιο μέλαθρον]]headlong down, [2.414; π. γενόμενος NT.Act.1.18] (perhaps ={πρησθείς} becoming distended); ἐπὶ τὸ πρηνὲς ῥέπειν incline towards pronation, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Hippocrates Medicus “περὶ ἀγμῶν” 1; ἐς τὸ π. [prev. author] “Mochl.” 8]]; of the arm and hand, with the palm downwards, variant in [Refs [“Fract.” 2]]; opposed to ὕπτιος, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Spir.” [same place], 1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus “Timoleon” 11]]; of ἀστράγαλοι, ὀρθοὶ πίπτοντες ἢ πρηνεῖς [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [[prev. author] 2.680a, compare 2nd c.AD(?): Pollianus Epigrammaticus 7.204]]; of seeds, hollow side downwards, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-3rd c.BC: Theophrastus Philosophus “Historia Plantarum” 2.6.1]]; of a ship, bottom upwards, implied in [Refs 1st c.AD+ [1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus “Tim.” [prev. cited]]]

__II
of parts of animals or man, that part which is uppermost and visible when the animal or man is in the πρανής position (the normal one for a quadruped), the back part, τὰ τετράποδα.. ἐν τοῖς ὑπτίοις οὐκ ἔ χει τὰς τρίχας, ἀλλ᾽ ἐν τοῖς πρανέσι μᾶλλον· οἱ δ᾽ ἄνθρωποι τοὐναντίον ἐν τοῖς ὑπτίοις μᾶλλον ἢ ἐν τοῖς πρανέσιν [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “de Partibus Animalium” 658a17, compare “HA” 498b20, 519a21, 540a2, “GA” 717b30.]]

__II.2
of leaves and of the hand, the back or 'wrong' side, τὰς ἶνας καὶ τὰς φλέβας ἐν τοῖς π. ἔχουσιν ὥσπερ ἡ χείρ [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-3rd c.BC: Theophrastus Philosophus “Historia Plantarum” 1.10.2]] (misunderstood as the opposite by [Refs 1st c.AD+ [1st c.AD: Plinius Rerum Naturalium Scriptor “Historia Naturalis” 16.88), compare 3.14.2.]]

__III
of the sides of hills, πρὸς ἄναντες καὶ κατὰ πρανοῦς καὶ πλάγια ἐλαύνειν down hill, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “de Equitandi ratione” 3.7, compare “An.” 1.5.8, 4.8.28, 1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus “Sulla” 18; κατὰ τὰ π. 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “de Equitandi ratione” 8.6]]; τὸ π., opposed to τὸ ὄρθιον, [Refs [[prev. passage],compare “Cyr.” 2.2.24.]]

__III.2
convex, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Meteorologica” 350a11.]]

πρίν,
adverb and conjunction, before, until. [πρῐν 19 [Refs 8th c.BC+ [times in 8th c.BC: Homerus Epicus, 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 2.344, +others]]; πρῑν in [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 6.81, 13.172, +others]]; once written πρείν, [Refs [“Leg.Gort.” 7.40]], but πρίν [Refs [“IG” 12.60.11, 94.9, 114.46, etc.]]; Trag. and Comedy texts always πρῐν (πρίν γ᾽ must be read in [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Acharnenses” 176).]]]

__A
adverb of Time, before, either in the sense of sooner or in that of formerly, erst (implying duration up to a certain time):

__I
of future time, with future Indic., πρίν μιν καὶ γῆρας ἔπεισιν [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 1.29, compare 18.283, 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 2.198, etc.]]: with Subj. = future, πρὶν καὶ κακὸν ἄλλο πάθῃσθα [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 24.551]]: with Opt. and κεν, πρίν κεν ἀνιηθεὶς σὴν πατρίδα γαῖαν ἵκοιο [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 3.117, compare 11.330, 14.155, 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Pax” 1076, 1112: with Opt., 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 24.800: with Imper., 9.250: with Inf. (expressing a wish), 2.413, (expressing an oath) 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 4.254.]]

__II
of past time,

__II.1
formerly, once, πρὶν μέν μοι ὑπέσχετο.., νῦν δὲ.. [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 2.112, variant in 9.19, compare 23.827; πρὶν μὲν πόσιν ἐσθλὸν ἀπώλεσα 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 4.724, compare 3.408.]]

__II.2
formerly (up to a certain point), before, in this sense frequently with Article, τὸ πρίν γ᾽ ἐκέκαστο [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 5.54; τὸ πρίν γε.., νῦν δὲ.. 13.105; νῦν δὲ.. τὸ πρίν γε 16.208, compare 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Prometheus Vinctus” 443, 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.129: without _Article_, τὰς ἐπιστήμας ἅς ποτε καὶ π. εἴχομεν 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Phaedo” 75e: with ellipsis of]]participle γενόμενος, τὰ π. πελώρια (i.e. γενόμενα) the giants of old, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Prometheus Vinctus” 151 (Lyric poetry)]]; τοῦ π. Αἰγέως Aegeus gone before, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Coloneus” 69; ἐν τῷ π. χρόνῳ [prev. author] “Ph.” 1224; ἐν τοῖς π. λόγοις 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 2.62]]: with participle expressed, τὸ π. γενόμενον τέρας [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 8.37; τοὺς πρὶν φυλαττομένους 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 547c, etc.]]

__II.3
hitherto, π. μέν.. [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Bacchylides Lyricus 12.114]]; until that time, and so meanwhile, [Refs [[prev. author] 15.13.]]

__II.4
sometimes followed by genitive, π. ὥρας [LXX+5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “P.” 4.43; π. ἀνηκέστου πάθους 1st c.AD: Josephus Historicus “Bellum Judaicum” 1.6.1; π. γενέσεως 2nd c.AD(?): Theodotion LXX “Su.” 42; π. τῆς συνόδου 2nd c.AD: Sextus Empiricus Philosophus “adversus Mathematicos” 9.371; π. φάους 2nd c.AD: Arrianus Historicus “Anabasis” 3.18.6]]; π. τοῦ βλέψαι, π. τοῦ ἀποθανεῖν, [LXX+2nd c.AD+ [2nd c.AD: Sextus Empiricus Philosophus “Πυρρώνειοι ὑποτυπώσεις” 7.162, variant in LXX.Tob.14.15]]; also πρὶν οὗ with infinitive, [Refs 2nd c.BC+ [“SIG” 953.16 (Calymna, 2nd c.BC)]]; with indicative, Test. cited in [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 46.21.]]

__B
conjunction before, ere: frequently following an antecedent clause with adverbial π. (chiefly in Epic dialect), or its equivalents πρότερον, πρόσθεν, πάρος (poetry), especially with negative, οὐδὲ π..., π... [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 1.98, 7.481, 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 19.475; μὴ π..., π... 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 2.355, 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Hercules Furens” 605; π..., π... 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 2.348, 8.453, 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 19.586; οὐ πρότερον.., π... 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Ecclesiazusae” 620, 5th-6th c.BC: Andocides Orator 4.17, 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 9.61; μὴ πρότερον.. π... 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Philoctetes” 199 (_anapaest meter_), 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Phaedo” 62c, 4th c.BC: Aeschines Orator 1.10; πρότερον.., π... 5th-6th c.BC: Andocides Orator 4.1, 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 5.2.9; οὐ πρόσθεν.., π... 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 17.9, 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 1.4.23; μὴ πρόσθεν.., π... [prev. author] “An.” 1.1.10; πρόσθε., π. τυχεῖν 5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “P.” 2.92; οὐ πάρος.., π... 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 2.128, 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 5.219]]; preceded by φθάνω,[Refs 8th c.BC+ [16.322, 5th c.BC: Antipho Orator 1.29, 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 4.79, 104, 6.97, 8.12, 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 4.1.21, “Cyr.” 2.4.25; sometimes followed by ἤ, οὐ.. πρίν γ᾽ ἀποπαύσεσθαι πρίν γ᾽ ἢ ἕτερόν γε πεσόντα αἵματος ἆσαι Ἄρηα 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 5.288, compare 22.266, 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.136, 165, +others]]; uncertain and perhaps always corrupt in Attic dialect and [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus, 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 5.61, 5th c.BC: Lysias Orator 6.11, 5th-6th c.BC: Isocrates Orator 4.19 (variant), 4th c.BC: Lycurgus Orator 128, 4th c.BC: Aeschines Orator 2.132 (variant), 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 1.4.23, “An.” 4.5.1]], but frequently in later Greek, [LXX.Gen.29.26, etc.]

__B.I
with infinitive, the prevailing construction in [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Homerus Epicus, after positive and negative clauses alike: in _Attic dialect_ mostly after positive clauses, and always used with them when the action does not or is not to take place: the tense is,]]

__B.I
regularly aorist,

__B.I.a
after a positive clause, ναῖε δὲ Πήδαιον, πρὶν ἐλθεῖν υἷας Ἀχαιῶν [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 13.172, compare 8.453, 16.322, 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 1.210; Ζεὺς ὀλέσειε βίην, πρὶν ἥβης μέτρον ἱκέσθαι 4.668, compare 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 6.465, 24.245, 5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “P.” 2.92.3.9, “N.” 8.19, 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 6.119, 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Persae” 712, “Ag.” 1539 (_anapaest meter_). 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Antigone” 120 (Lyric poetry), “Tr.” 396, 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Alcestis” 281, 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Equites” 258, +others, 5th c.BC: Antipho Orator 5.67, 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 1.125, 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 4.1.7, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Protagoras” 350b, +others]]; after negative questions which expect a positive answer, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Andromache” 1069, “Ion” 524, “Rh.” 684, 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Ranae” 481, etc.]]

__B.I.b
after a negative clause, οὐδ᾽ ὅ γε πρὶν Δαναοῖσιν ἀεικέα λοιγὸν ἀπώσει, πρίν γ᾽ ἀπὸ πατρὶ φίλῳ δόμεναι ἑλικώπιδα κούρην [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 1.98, compare 19.423, 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 2.128, 4.747: after 8th c.BC: Homerus Epicus a negative antecedent is commonly followed by πρίν with finite Verb (see. below 11)]]; but Inf. is found where π. precedes, π. ἰδεῖν δ᾽, οὐδεὶς μάντις [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Ajax” 1419 (_anapaest meter_); π. μὲν γὰρ κριθῆναι, οὐ ῥᾴδιον ἦν εἰδέναι τὰς αἰτίας 5th-6th c.BC: Andocides Orator 4.8; π. νικῆσαι.., οὐκ ἦν.. 5th c.BC: Lysias Orator 19.28; π. δὲ ταῦτα πρᾶξαι, μὴ σκοπεῖτε 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 3.12, compare 4th c.BC: Lycurgus Orator 135; also, οὔτε.. π. ἱδρῶσαι δεῖπνον ᾑρεῖτο 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 8.1.38]]; also after Verbs of fearing (the positive being the thing dreaded), ὅταν.. δεδίωσι μὴ πρότερόν τι μάθῃς, π. τέλος ἐπιθεῖναι τοῖς πραττομένοις [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Isocrates Orator 5.70, compare 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Fragmenta” 453.6, 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Trachiniae” 632]]; in unfulfilled conditions and wishes, οὔθ᾽ ὁ Πλούτωνος κύων οὔθ᾽ οὑπὶ κώπῃ ψυχοπομπὸς ἂν Χάρων ἔσχον π. εἰς φῶς σὸν καταστῆσαι βίον [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Alcestis” 362, compare “Rh.” 61]]; otherwise not common, ὤφθην οὐδεπώποτε π. ταύτην τὴν συμφορὰν γενέσθαι [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Lysias Orator 19.55; οὐδὲ παύσεται χόλου.., π. κατασκῆψαί τινα 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Medea” 94, compare “HF” 605; καί μοι μὴ θορυβήσῃ μηδεὶς π. ἀκοῦσαι 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 5.15, compare 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Oeconomicus” 4.24: after _negative_ _optative_ with ἄν, οὕτω γένοιτ᾽ ἂν οὐδ᾽ ἂν ἔκβασις στρατοῦ καλή, π. ὅρμῳ ναῦν θρασυνθῆναι a. “Supp.” 772, compare 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Leges” 769e: after a past tense (in indirect speech), ὤμοσαν μὴ π. ἐς Φώκαιαν ἥξειν, π. ἢ τὸν μύδρον τοῦτον ἀναφανῆναι 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.165, compare 4.9, 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 7.50, 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Historia Graeca (Hellenica)” 6.5.23, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Phaedo” 61a.]]

__B.I.2
also present, to convey a special sense of continuance, effort, or the like, 'before undertaking to', 'before proceeding to', π. ἐξοπλίζειν Ἄρη [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Supplices” 702 (Lyric poetry), compare “Ag.” 1067; π. νυν τὰ πλείον᾽ ἱστορεῖν.., ἔξελθε 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Coloneus” 36, compare “El.” 20; π. κλαίειν τινά 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Andromache” 577, compare “Or.” 1095; π. λέγειν 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Thesmophoriazusae” 380, compare “Ach.” 383, 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 8.3, 5th-6th c.BC: Andocides Orator 4.1, 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 3.24, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Leges” 666a, 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 2.4.25, “Mem.” 1.2.40, etc.]]

__B.I.3
also perfect, after a future, π. τόδ᾽ ἐξηντληκέναι [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Medea” 79]]; after present or imperfect, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. author] “El.” 1069, compare 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 3.25; π..., τί μέλλετ᾽..; 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Phoenissae” 1145; π. καὶ τεθύσθαι 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Aves” 1034, compare “V.” 1156, “Pax” 375, “Lys.” 322 (Lyric poetry), “Ra.” 1185, 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 4.1.21, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Theaetetus” 164c, “Prt.” 320a, etc.]]; with ἥκειν in perfect sense, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 6.116; οὐ βουλόμενος διαγωνίσασθαι π. οἱ τοὺς βοηθοὺς ἥκειν 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 5.10.]]

__B.II
with a finite Verb:

__B.II.1
with Ind., chiefly aorist: not in [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Homerus Epicus (first in “hymnus ad Apollinem” 357), who uses Ind. only with πρίν γ᾽ ὅτε, πρίν γ᾽ ὅτε δή,]] after both positive and negative clauses, ἠλώμην.., πρίν γ᾽ ὅτε.. ἤγαγες [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 13.322; πρίν γ᾽ ὅτε δή με.. κάλεσσεν 23.43, compare 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 12.437; οὐδέ κεν ἡμέας ἄλλο διέκρινεν.., πρίν γ᾽ ὅτε δὴ θανάτοιο.. νέφος ἀμφεκάλυψεν 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 4.180: rarely with]]imperfect, οὐδ᾽ ὧς τοῦ θυμὸν.. ἔπειθον, πρίν γ᾽ ὅτε δὴ θάλαμος πύκ᾽ ἐβάλλετο (began to be hit) [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 9.588: frequently after 8th c.BC: Homerus Epicus, with]]aorist,

__B.II.1.a
after negative clauses: of a fact in the past, οὐκ ἦν ἀλέξημ᾽ οὐδὲν.., πρίν γ᾽ ἐγώ σφισιν ἔδειξα [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Prometheus Vinctus” 481; οὐ πρότερον ἀπανέστη.. Μαρδόνιος, πρὶν ἤ σφεας ὑποχειρίους ἐποιήσατο 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 6.45]]; ἀλλ᾽ οὐδ᾽ ὣς.. ἠξίωσαν νεώτερόν τι ποιεῖν ἐς αὐτο᾽ν.., πρίν γε δὴ αὐτοῖς.. μηνυτὴς γίγνεται (historical present = aorist) [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 1.132, compare 3.101, 5.61, 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 6.79, 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Aves” 700, 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 1.4.23, 4.5.13 (historical _present_), “HG” 5.4.58, etc.; once in 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus, “Phdr.” 266a]]; as part of an unfulfilled condition, οὐκ ἂν κατέσχε δῆμον οὐδ᾽ ἐπαύσατο π. ἀνταράξας πῖαρ ἐξεῖλεν γάλα [Refs 6th c.BC+ [6th c.BC: Solon Lyricus cited in 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Ἀθηναίων Πολιτεία” 12.5; οὐκ ἂν ἐσκεψάμεθα πρότερον.., πρὶν ἐζητήσαμεν 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Meno” 86d, compare “Tht.” 165e; χρῆν τοίνυν Αεπτίνην μὴ πρότερον τιθέναι τὸν ἑαυτοῦ νόμον, πρὶν τοῦτον ἔλυσε γραψάμενος 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 20.96]]; after verbs implying a negative, ἀμφιγνοεῖν [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 2.5.33, θαυμάζειν 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 1.51, λανθάνειν [prev. author] 3.29]]; also with imperfect, οὔπω ᾔδει.. π. ἐν τῷ κακῷ ἦν [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Antipho Orator 1.19, compare 5th-6th c.BC: Andocides Orator 4.17, 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 9.61.]]

__B.II.1.b
after positive clauses (both combined, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Prometheus Vinctus” 481, 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 1.118)]], with the sense until, ἠγόμην δ᾽ ἀνὴρ ἀστῶν μέγιστος.., πρίν μοι τύχη τοιάδ᾽ ἐπέστη [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Tyrannus” 776]]; σπουδαὶ δὲ λόγων ἦσαν ἴσαι πως, πρὶν.. πείθει (historical present) [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Hecuba” 131 (_anapaest meter_); πρίν γ᾽ ὁρᾷ [prev. author] “Med.” 1173; frequently followed by δή, π. δή τις ἐφθέγξατο [prev. author] “Andr.” 1147]]; τὰ περὶ τοὺς ἀγῶνας κατελύθη (negative idea) ὑπὸ ξυμφορῶν, πρὶν δὴ οἱ Ἀθηναῖοι τότε τὸν ἀγῶνα ἐποίησαν [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 3.104, compare 7.39 (historical _present_), 71.]]

__B.II.2
with Subj. only after negatives or equivalent of negative, ={ἕως} or ἢν μή (in [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Isocrates Orator 4.173 ἢν μή and πρὶν ἄν are used almost as synonyms)]]; οὐ καταδυσόμεθ᾽, ἀχνύμενοί περ.., πρὶν μόρσιμον ἦμαρ ἐπέλθῃ [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 10.175; μή πω καταδύσεο.., πρίν γ᾽ ἐμὲ.. ἴδηαι 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 18.135, compare 190, 24.781; ἀλλ᾽ ὄμοσον μὴ μητρὶ φίλῃ τάδε μυθήσασθαι, πρίν γ᾽ ὅτ᾽ ἂν ἑνδεκάτη τε δυωδεκάτη τε γένηται 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 2.374, compare 4.477: in Prose usually πρὶν ἄν (πρίν κα “Berl.Sitzb.” 1927.161 (from Cyrene)), rarely π. alone, as also πρὶν ἤ:]]

__B.II.2.a
generally with aorist, to express an action preceding the action of the antecedent clause, the Verb in which is future (or some equivalent of the future) or imperative, οὐ γαμέεται παρθένος οὐδεμία, πρὶν ἂν τῶν πολεμίων ἄνδρα ἀποκτείνῃ [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 4.117, compare 1.82 (variant), 3.109 (variant)]]; νῦν δ᾽ οὐδέν ἐστι τέρμα μοι προκείμενον μόχθων (the sense here is future), πρὶν ἂν Ζεὺς ἐκπέσῃ τυραννίδος [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Prometheus Vinctus” 756, compare 166 (Lyric poetry), 177 (_anapaest meter_)]]; οὐ γάρ ποτ᾽ ἔξει τῆσδε τῆς χώρας, πρὶν ἂν.. στήσῃς ἄγων [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Coloneus” 909, compare 48, 1041, “OT” 1529, etc.; οὐκ ἂν ἐκμάθοις.., πρὶν ἂν θάνῃ τις [prev. author] “Tr.” 2; οὐκ ἄπειμι πρὸς δόμους πάλιν, πρὶν ἄν σε.. ἔξω βάλω 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Medea” 276, compare 680, Alcaeus1145, “IA” 324, “IT” 19, 1302; μὴ προκαταγίγνωσκε.., π. ἄν γ᾽ ἀκούσῃς ἀμφοτέρων 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Vespae” 920, compare “Ach.” 176, 230, 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Hiero” 6.13, “Cyr.” 1.2.8, “An.” 1. 1.10, 5.7.12, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Phaedrus” 228c, “La.” 187e (ἂν added in later codices), etc.]]; μηδέν᾽ ὀλβίζειν π. ἀ᾽ν τέρμα τοῦ βίου περάσῃ [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Tyrannus” 1529 (troch.); οὐχὶ μὴ παύσησθε, π. ἄν.. ὑμᾶς τις ἐκτραχηλίσῃ 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Lysistrata” 704: π. without ἄν, μὴ στέναζε, π. μάθῃς 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Philoctetes” 917, compare “Ant.” 619 (Lyric poetry), “Aj.” 742, 965, “Tr.” 608, 946; οὐκ ἔστιν ὅστις αὐτὸν ἐξαιρήσεται.., π. γυναῖκ᾽ ἐμοὶ μεθῇ 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Alcestis” 849, compare “Or.” 1218, 1357 (Lyric poetry); π. χαρίσωνται 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Ecclesiazusae” 629 (assuming variant); οὐ γὰρ δή σφεας ἀπίει τῆς ἀποικίης, πρὶν δὴ ἀπίκωνται 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 4.157; π. διαγνῶσι 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 6.29; π... βεβαιωσώμεθα [prev. work] 10 (uncertain reading)]]; πρὶν ἀνάγκην τινὰ θεὸς ἐπιπέμψῃ [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Phaedo” 62c codices; π. ἐξετάσωσιν 4th c.BC: Hyperides Orator “pro Euxenippo” 4: πρὶν ἤ (never with ἄν), π. ἢ ἀνορθώσωσι 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.19, compare 136, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Timaeus” 57b, etc.: with _negative_ implied, ὁ δὲ ἀδικέει ἀναπειθόμενος π. ἢ ἀτρεκέως ἐκμάθῃ 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 7.10. ; αἰσχρὸν ἡγοῦμαι πρότερον παύσασθαι, π. ἂν.. ψηφίσησθε 5th c.BC: Lysias Orator 22.4; ὅστις οὖν οἴεται τοὺς ἄλλους πράξειν τι.., π. ἂν.. διαλλάξῃ, λίαν ἁπλῶς ἔχει 5th-6th c.BC: Isocrates Orator 4.16 (where ὅστις οὖν οἴεται ={οὐ δεῖ οὔεσθαι}, as is shown by ἀλλὰ δεῖ]] in the next sentence,[Refs 4th c.BC+ [compare 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 38.24).]]

__B.II.2.b
less frequently (never in [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Homerus Epicus) with]]present subjunctive: μήπω π. ἂν τῶν ἡμετέρων ἀΐῃς (the Verb has no aorist) μύθων [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Philoctetes” 1409 (_anapaest meter_); ὁ νομοθέτης τὰ διδασκαλεῖα ἀνοίγειν ἀπαγορεύει μὴ πρότερον π. ἂν ὁ ἥλιος ἀνίσχῃ 4th c.BC: Aeschines Orator 1.10, compare 5th c.BC: Antipho Orator 1.29, 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 2.2.8, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Phaedrus” 271c.]]

__B.II.3
πρίν with Opt.:

__B.II.3.a
representing subjunctive after historical tenses, οὐκ ἔθελεν φεύγειν π. πειρήσαιτ᾽ Ἀχιλῆος [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 21.580]]; πρίν γ᾽ ὅτε, as with subjunctive,[Refs 5th c.BC+ [9.488; ἔδοξέ μοι μὴ σῖγα π. φράσαιμί σοι τὸν πλοῦν ποεῖσθαι 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Philoctetes” 551, compare 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 3.22, 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 1.4.14, “HG” 6.5.19 (compare 2.4.18), “An.” 1.2.2, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Apologia” 36c, etc.]]

__B.II.3.b
by assimilation, ὄλοιο μήπω π. μάθοιμι [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Philoctetes” 961, compare “Tr.” 657 (Lyric poetry)]]; οὐδὲ γὰρ εἰδείης (potential optative).. π. πειρηθείης [Refs 6th c.BC+ [6th c.BC: Theognis Elegiacus 126; after _optative_ with ἄν, οὐκ ἂν πρότερον ὁρμήσειε π. βεβαιώσαιτο 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Leges” 799d, compare 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Tyrannus” 505 (Lyric poetry).]]

__B.II.4
π. ἄν with optative is doubtful, and (if not corrupt) due to the change required by indirect speech, ἀπαγορευόντων τῶν φίλων τῶν ἐμῶν μὴ ἀποκτείνειν τὸν ἄνδρα, πρὶν ἄν ἐγὼ ἔλθοιμι [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Antipho Orator 5.34 (assuming variant), compare 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Historia Graeca (Hellenica)” 2.3.48, 2.4.18.]]

__B.II.5
without a Verb, πρὶν ὥρη (i.e. γένηται) [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 15.394.]]

πρό
prep. with genitive,  [in LXX chiefly for פָּנִים ;]
before;
__(a) of place: Act.12:6, 14 14:13, Jas.5:9; π. προσώπου (= Heb. פָּנִים, Deu.3:18, Mal.3:1, al.; Bl., § 40, 9), Mat.11:10, Mrk.1:2, Luk.1:76 7:27 9:52 10:1, Act.14:13;
__(b) of time: Mat.8:29 24:38, Luk.11:38 21:12, Jhn.11:55 13:1 17:24, Act.5:36 21:38, 1Co.2:7 4:5, Eph.1:4, Col.1:17, 2Ti.1:9 4:21, Tit.1:2, Heb.11:5, 1Pe.1:20, Ju 25; π. ἐτῶν δεκατεσσάρων, fourteen years ago, 2Co.12:2; π. προσώπου (see supr.), Act.13:24; with genitive of person(s), Mat.5:12, Jhn.5:7 10:8, Rom.16:7, Gal.1:17; with genitive art. inf. (= πρίν; M, Pr., 100; Bl., § 69, 7), Mat.6:8 Luk.2:21 22:15, Jhn.1:49 13:19 17:5, Act.23:15, Gal.2:12 3:23; as in late writers (resembling a Latin idiom but indepen­dent of it; B1., § 40, 5; M, Pr., 100 f.; of. Am 2Ma.15:36, and for other exx., Soph., Lex., see word), πρὸ ἓξ ἡμέρας τοῦ πάσχα, on the sixth day before the Passover, Jhn.12:1;
__(with) of preference: π. πάντων, Jas.5:12, 1Pe.4:8;
__(d) in compos.,
__α with subst., of position before: προαύλιον, πρόδρομος; priority of rank or order, προπάτωρ; anticipation, πρό γνωσις, πρό νοια;
__β with adj., intensity, πρόδηλος;
__γ with verb., of place, προάγω, προβαίνω; of preference, προαιρέομαι.†
(AS)

LSJ / STEPBible (TFLSJ)
πρό,
before, forth:

__A
PREP. WITH GENIT.:

__A.I
of Place, before, in front of, ἠγερέθοντο π. ἄστεος [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 24.468, compare 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 15.351, etc.; π. πτόλιος δεδαϊγμένον 19.292; κείνους κιχησόμεθα π. πυλάων 10.126, compare 6.80, etc.; φύλοπις αἰνὴ ἕστηκε π. νεῶν 18.172; πυρὰ φαίνετο Ἰλιόθι π. 8.561, compare 10.12, 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 8.581, etc.; κλαγγὴ γεράνων πέλει οὐρανόθι π. 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 3.3; π. τειχέων 5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “O.” 13.56]]; ἔμπροσθε π. (variant) τῆς ἀκροπόλιος, ὄπισθε δὲ τῶν πυλέων [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 8.53, compare 9.52]]; π. δόμων, π. δωμάτων, in front of, i.e. outside the house, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “P.” 2.18, 5.96, etc.; π. θυρῶν 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Electra” 109 (_anapaest meter_), etc.]]; τὴν π. τοῦ Ἡραίου νῆσον before or off the Heraeum, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 3.75, compare 7.22; π. ποδός, see at {πούς} 1.4a]]; π. χειρῶν at hand, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Antigone” 1279, 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Rhesus” 274, uncertain in “Tr.” 1207; π. τῶν ὀφθαλμῶν προφαίνεσθαι 4th c.BC: Aeschines Orator 2.148.]]

__A.I.2
with Vbs. of motion, π. δ᾽ ἄρ᾽ αὐτῶν κύνες ἤϊσαν [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 19.435, compare 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 23.115; π. Ἀχαιῶν ἄγγελος ᾔει 10.286, compare 13.693; π. ἕθεν κλονέοντα φάλαγγας 5.96.]]

__A.I.3
before, in front of, for the purpose of shielding or guarding, π. Τρώων ἑσταότ᾽ [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 24.215]]: hence, in defence of, μάχεσθαι.. π. τε παίδων καὶ π. γυναικῶν [Refs 5th c.BC+ [8.57, compare 4.156, 373, 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 8.74, etc.]]; ὀλέσθαι π. πόληος, Latin pro patria mori, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 22.110; π. τῆς Σπάρτης ἀποθνῄσκειν 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 7.134, compare 172, 9.72, 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Alcestis” 18, 645, etc.; π. τοῦ θανόντος.. ἔθεσθ᾽ ἐπιστροφήν 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Tyrannus” 134; διακινδυνεῦσαι π. βασιλέως 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 8.8.4; βουλεύεσθαι, πράττειν π. τινός, [prev. work] 1.6.42, 4.5.44, compare “Mem.” 2.4.7]]; π. τοξευμάτων as a defence against arrows, [Refs [[prev. author] “An.” 7.8.18]]: hence also, for, on behalf of, instead of, ἀγρυπνῆσαι π. τινῶν[Refs [[prev. work] 7.6.36, compare “Leg.Gort.” 1.43]]; of an advocate, π. τῶνδε φωνεῖν [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Tyrannus” 10, compare “OC” 811]]; ὄτι δέ κ᾽ αὐτὸς π. Ειαυτοῦ [ἀμάρτῃ] whatever offence he commits of his own volition, Kohler-Ziebarth Stadtrecht von Gortyn [Refs [p.34.]]

__A.I.4
π. ὁδοῦ ἐγένοντο further on the road, i.e. forwards, onward, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 4.382, compare 2nd-3rd c.AD: Aelianus “De Natura Animalium - Ar.Byzantine Epit.” 3.16, 7.29 (see. φροῦδος)]]: also to denote distance, π. πολλοῦ τῆς πόλεως [Refs 1st c.BC+ [1st c.BC: Dionysius Halicarnassensis 9.35; π. τριάκοντα σταδίων]]at a distance of [Refs 1st c.BC+ [30 stades, 1st c.BC-1st c.AD: Strabo Geographus 8.6.24.]]

__A.I.5
π. ἠοῦς, π. ἑσπέρης τοῦ βωμοῦ, eastwards, westwards of.., [Refs 4th c.BC+ [“IG” 7.235.45 (Orop., 4th c.BC).]]

__A.II
of Time, before, π. γάμοιο [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 15.524; ἠῶθι π. 5.469]]; π. ὃ τοῦ ἐνόησεν one before the other, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 10.224]]; more frequently in later writers, π. τῶν Τρωικῶν [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 1.3, compare 1.1; π. τοῦ θανεῖν 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Antigone” 883; π. τοῦ θανάτου 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Phaedo” 57a; π. τοῦ λοιμοῦ [prev. author] “Smp.” 201d; π. δείπνου 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 5.5.39; π. ἡμέρας [prev. work] 4.5.14]]; π. τοῦ χρῆσθαι before one uses it, [Refs [[prev. author] “Mem.” 2.6.6]]; π. μοίρας τῆς ἐμῆς before my doom, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Agamemnon” 1266; π. τῆς εἱμαρμένης 5th c.BC: Antipho Orator 1.21; π. τοῦ καθήκοντος χρόνου 4th c.BC: Aeschines Orator 3.126]], compare 124; π. πολλοῦ long before, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 7.130, etc.]]; π. μικροῦ, π. ὀλίγου, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus “Pompeius” 73, 2nd c.AD: Appianus Historicus “Bella Civilia” 2.116; ὀλίγον π. τούτων 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 2.8; τὸ π. τοῦ (variant{τούτου}) [prev. work] 15]]; π. τοῦ (sometimes written προτοῦ) [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Agamemnon” 1204, 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.122, 5.83, 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Thesmophoriazusae” 418, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Symposium” 173a; ὁ π. τοῦ χρόνος 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Eumenides” 462, 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 2.58, etc.]]; π. τοῦ ἤ, ={πρὶν ἤ}, [Refs [“IG” 7.2225.22 (from Thisbe)]]; οἱ π. ἡμῶν γενόμενοι [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Isocrates Orator 13.19; οἱ π. ἐμοῦ 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 1.97.]]

__A.II.2
in later writers frequently with Numerals, π. τριάκοντα ἡμερῶν thirty days before, [LXX+1st c.AD+ [2nd-3rd c.AD: Aelianus “De Natura Animalium - Ar.Byzantine Epit.” 5.52; π. μιᾶς ἡμέρας 1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus “Caesar” 63; π. ἐνιαυτοῦ [prev. author] 2.147e; π. δυεῖν ἡμερῶν ἢ ἐτελεύτα [prev. author] “Sull.” 37: frequently with double _genitive_, π. δύο ἐτῶν τοῦ σεισμοῦ, π. δύο ὡρῶν τῆς ἐπιβολῆς, LXX.Amos.1.1, 1st c.AD: Dioscorides (Dioscurides) Medicus 1.64]]; π. ἓξ ἡμερῶν τοῦ πάσχα, π. μιᾶς ἡμέρας τῶν γενεθλίων, [NT+1st c.AD+ [NT.John.12.1, 1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus 2.717d; π. πολλοῦ τῆς ἑορτῆς 2nd c.AD: Lucianus Sophista “Sat.” 14.]]

__A.II.2.b
in rendering Roman dates, τῇ π. μιᾶς Νωνῶν Ὀκτωβρίων, = pridie Non. Oct., [Refs 1st c.AD+ [1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus 2.203a, etc.]]

__A.III
in other relations:

__A.III.1
of Preference, before, rather than, κέρδος αἰνῆσαι π. δίκας to praise sleight before right, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “P.” 4.140, compare 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 361e]]; πᾶν δὴ βουλόμενοι σφίσι εἶναι π. τῆς παρεούσης λύπης anything before, rather than, their actual trouble, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 7.152]] (so, in order to avoid, π. τοῦ δεινοτάτου [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 54.19); πᾶν π. τοῦ δουλεῦσαι ἐπεξελθεῖν 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 5.100, compare 4.59]]; ἑλέσθαι, αἱρεῖσθαι, or κρῖναί τι π. τινός to choose one before another, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. author] 5.36, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 366b, “Phlb.” 57e]]; π. πολλοῦ ποιήσασθαι to esteem above much, i.e. very highly, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Isocrates Orator 5.138; π. πολλῶν χρημάτων τιμήσασθαί τι 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 1.33, compare 6.10]]; π. ἄλλων more than others, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Menexenus” 249e (variant), compare 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Septem contra Thebas” 1002; δυσδαίμων.. π. πασᾶν γυναικῶν [prev. work] 927 (codices, Lyric poetry)]]; π. πάντων θεῶν τῇ Ἑστίᾳ πρώτῃ προθύειν [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Cratylus” 401d]]: after a comparative it is redundant, ἡ τυραννὶς π. ἐλευθερίης ἀσπαστότερον [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.62, compare 6.12, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Apologia” 28d, “Cri.” 54b, “Phd.” 99a]]; for ἤ after ἄλλος, οὐδεὶς ἄλλος π. σεῦ [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 3.85, compare 7.3.]]

__A.III.2
of Cause or Motive, for, from, π. φόβοιο for fear, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 17.667]]; ἀθλεύων π. ἄνακτος toiling before the face of, i.e. in his service, [Refs [24.734]]; π. τῶνδε there fore, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Electra” 495 (Lyric poetry).]]

__B
POSITION: words may be put between π. and its case, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 23.115]]; but it does not follow its case, except after Epic dialect forms in -θι, Ἰλιόθι πρό, οὐρανόθι πρό, ἠῶθι πρό (see. above).

__C
πρό, absolutely as adverb.:

__C.I
of Place, before, opposed to ἐπί (after), [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 13.799, 800]]; before, in front, [Refs [15.360]]; forth, forward, ἐκ δ᾽ ἄγαγε π. φόωσδε [Refs [19.118]]; χωρεῖν π. δόμων to come forth from, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Trachiniae” 960 (Lyric poetry); ἄγειν τινὰ π. δόμων 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Hecuba” 59 (_anapaest meter_)]]; γῆν π. γῆς ἐλαύνομαι I am driven on from one land to another, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Prometheus Vinctus” 682; διώκειν γῆν π. γῆς 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Acharnenses” 235.]]

__C.II
of Time, before, πρό οἱ εἴπομεν [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 1.37]]; earlier, τά τ᾽ ἐσσόμενα π. τ᾽ ἐόντα [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th-7th c.BC: Hesiodus Epicus “Theogonia” 32, 38.]]

__C.III
when joined with other Preps., ἀποπρό, διαπρό, ἐπιπρό, περιπρό, προπρό, it strengthens the first preposition, or adds to it the notion of forward, forth.

__D
πρό IN COMPOSITION (joined with other words),

__D.I
with Substantives, to denote

__D.I.1
position before or in front, πρόδομος, προάστιον, πρόθυρον, προπύλαια, etc.

__D.I.2
priority of rank, πρόεδρος, προεδρία, etc.: also priority of order, προάγων, πρόλογος, προοίμιον, προπάτωρ, etc.

__D.I.3
standing in another's place, πρόμαντις, πρόξενος.

__D.II
with adjectives, to denote

__D.II.1
proximity, πρόχειρο; and readiness, πρόθυμος, πρόφρων.

__D.II.2
away (compare 111.3 below), προθέλυμνος, πρόρριζος.

__D.II.3
prematureness, πρόμοιρος, πρόωρος.

__D.II.4
intensity, πρόπας, πρόπαρ, προπάροιθ; so also πρόκακος, πρόπαλαι.

__D.III
with Verbs,

__D.III.1
of Place, before, forwards, προβαίνω, προβάλλω, προτίθημι, etc.: also, before, in defence, προκινδυνεύω, προμάχομαι, etc.

__D.III.2
forth, προέλκω, προφέρω.

__D.III.2.b
publicly, προγράφω, προειπεῖν, πρόκειμαι.

__D.III.3
away, προδίδωμι, προϊάλλω, προϊάπτω, προΐημι, προλείπω, προρέω, προτέμνω, προτρέπομαι, προφεύγω, προχέω.

__D.III.4
in preference, προαιροῦμαι, προτιμάω, etc.

__D.III.5
before, beforehand, προαισθάνομαι, προγίγνομαι, προκαταλαμβάνω, etc.; of foresight, προνοέω, προοράω.

__E
Etymology: cf. Latin προ?~X-, Slavonic pro-, Sanskrit pra-, etc., in compounds.

προ-άγω
[in LXX: 1Ki.17:16 (נָגַשׁ), Wis.19:11, al. ;]
__1. prop. trans., to lead on, lead forth or forward: with accusative of person(s), Act.16:30 17:5; of bringing forth to trial, Act.12:6 (WH, txt., προσάγ-); before ἐπί, with genitive of person(s), Act.25:26.
__2. Intrans. (Plat., Polyb., and later writers; see Bl., § 53, 1; MM, xxi);
__(a) to lead the way, 1Ti.1:18 (R, mg.), hence, to go before, precede: Luk.18:39; opposite to ἀκολουθέω, Mrk.11:9; before εἰς, Mat.14:22, Mrk.6:45, 1Ti.5:24, Heb.7:18; with accusative of person(s), Mat.2:9 21:9, Mrk.10:32; before εἰς, Mat.21:31 26:32 28:7, Mrk.14:28 16:7;
__(b) to go on, advance (Sir.20:27): 2Jn.9.†
(AS)

LSJ / STEPBible (TFLSJ)
προάγω [ᾰ],
future -άξω: perfect active προῆχα [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 19.18, 25.8, 2nd c.AD: Pausanias Periegeta 3.11.10:]] —middle, see below: perfect passive in middle sense, see below [Refs [1.7]]:—lead forward or onward, μιν ἐς τὰ οἰκία [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 3.148, etc.]]; escort on their way, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. author] 8.132; τοὺς πεζοὺς οὐ πολλὴν ὁδόν 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 3.3.23]]:—passive, to be led on, προαγομένης τῆς πόλεως ἐπὶ συμφοράς [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Andocides Orator 2.9.]]

__2
carry on, αἱμασιάν [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 55.27]]; produce, [Refs 3rd c.AD+ [3rd c.AD: Plotinus Philosophus 3.7.6:]] —passive, [τάξις] εἰς ὀξὺ προηγμένη brought to a point, [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd c.AD: Arrianus Historicus “Tactica” 16.8.]]

__2.b
bring on in age, etc., προῆγεν αὐτὸν ὁ χρόνος εἰς ὥραν [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 1.4.4:]] —passive, ἐπὶ πλείω προῆκται τῆς κατ᾽ ἰητρικὴν ἐπιμελείας belong to more advanced medical study, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Hippocrates Medicus “περὶ ἰητροῦ” 13.]]

__2.c
increase, raise a dose, ἐπὶ ἓξ κοτύλας [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd c.AD: Rufus Medicus “fragment” 68 (variant{προσ-}).]]

__3
bring forward, νεκρόν εἰς τὸ φανερόν, τι εἰς τὸ πρόσθεν, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Leges” 960a, “Plt.” 262c; τὴν φύσιν εἰς φῶς πᾶσιν [prev. author] “Ep.” 341d; βουλὴν ἀπόρρητον εἰς φῶς ἡλίου 1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus 2.552d]]; οἱ προαγαγόντες εἰς φῶς, ={οἱ γονεῖς}, [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd c.AD(?): Pollianus Epigrammaticus 3.8, compare 3rd c.AD: Heliodorus Scriptor Eroticus 7.23]]; call up an apparition, Thessal. in [Refs [“Catalogus Codicum Astrologorum” 8(3).137.]]

__3.b
bring before a tribunal, [Refs 2nd c.BC+ [“SIG” 826 G 22 (2nd c.BC, _passive_)]]; π. δάνειον [Refs 3rd c.AD+ [“POxy.” 1562.14 (3rd c.AD).]]

__4
lead on, induce, persuade, δόλῳτινὰς π. metaphorically of narrative, argument, action, events, μὴ πέρα προβῇς λόγου [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Cratinus Comicus 66; προβήσομαι ἐς τὸ πρόσω τοῦ λόγου 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.5]]; προβάς φησιν.. further on, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [2nd c.BC: Demetrius Lacon Philosophus “Herc.” 1012.12, compare 1st c.BC: Philodemus Gadarensis Epigrammaticus “Rh.” 1.87 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus]]; π. ἐκ τῶν κνημέων ἐς τοὺς μηρούς went on.., [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 6.75]]; προέβαινε τὸ ἔθνος ἄρχον καὶ ἐπιτροπεῦον the nation was organized in a series of overlordships and mandates, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. author] 1.134; προὔβης τῶνδε καὶ περαιτέρω 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Prometheus Vinctus” 249; π. ἐπ᾽ ἔσχατον θράσους 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Antigone” 853 (Lyric poetry); οἷ προβαίνει τὸ πρᾶγμα τοῦ βουλεύματος 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Acharnenses” 836; ποῖ προβήσεται λόγο; 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Hippolytus” 342; πέρας δὴ ποῖ κακῶν προβήσετα; [prev. author] “Or.” 511, compare 749; τὸ τῆς τύχης ἀφανὲς οἷ προβήσεται [prev. author] Alcaeus785; μὴ προβαίη μεῖζον ἢ τὸ νῦν κακόν [prev. author] “Med.” 907; τὸ ἔθος ἐπὶ πολὺ προβαίνει 4th c.BC: Aeschines Orator 1.179: _impersonal_, εἰς τοῦτο προβέβηκε ὥστε..]] it has gone so far that..,[Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Leges” 839c]]; π. πόρρω μοχθηρίας to be far gone in knavery, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Apologia Socratis” 30; π. εἰς τοῦτο ἔχθρας ὥστε.. 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 12.16; εἰς ἀταξίαν 4th c.BC: Aeschines Orator 3.38; μέχρι τίνος 2nd c.BC: Polybius Historicus 2.1.3; ἐπὶ τὸ χεῖρον π. τὰ πράγματα [prev. author] 5.30.6]]: in good sense, make progress, τοσοῦτον προβεβήκαμεν ὥστε.. [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Theaetetus” 187a]]; of an enterprise, prosper, succeed, [Refs 1st c.BC+ [“BGU” 1209.10 (1st c.BC), etc.]]

__II
go before, i.e. be superior to, another, πολὺ προβέβηκας ἁπάντων σῷ θάρσει [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 6.125; κράτεϊ 16.54, compare 23.890]]; δυνάμει τε καὶ αἰδοῖ Τρηχῖνος προβέβηκε by might and awe he is over, i.e. rules, Trachis, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th-7th c.BC: Hesiodus Epicus “Scutum Herculis” 355, compare 3rd c.BC: Callimachus Epicus “Epigrammata” 1.5.]]

__III
with accusative of things, overstep, τέρμα προβάς [Refs [Pi  “N.” 7.71.]]

__IV
with accusative of the instrum. of motion, πόδα π. [Refs 6th c.BC+ [6th c.BC: Theognis Elegiacus 283; οὐκ ἂν προβαίην τὸν πόδα τὸν ἕτερον 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Ecclesiazusae” 161, compare 2nd c.AD: Lucianus Sophista “Hist. Conscr.” 29; προβὰς δὲ κῶλον 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Phoenissae” 1412; ἀρβύλαν προβάς [prev. author] “Or.” 1470 (Lyric poetry)]]; προβεβήκασι τὰ ἀριστερά have their left legs foremost (variant{προβεβλήκασι}, see at {προβάλλω} [Refs 8th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 1), 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “de Incessu Animalium” 706a7; προβὰς τὸν πόδα τὸν ἀριστερὸν καὶ τὸν δεξιὸν ὑποβάς 2nd c.AD(?): Pollianus Epigrammaticus 5.23.]]

__V
Causal, in future active, move forward, advance, τίς τρόπος ἄνδρα προβάσει [ᾱ]; [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “O.” 8.63.]]

[prev. author] “Av.” 626; π. τινὰ ταῖς Νύμφαις 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Phaedrus” 241e]]; ἀνδρὶ δέμας, of a woman, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Cretan dialect” 6: without _dative_, π. ἀκήδευτα τὰ σώματα 1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus “Pericles” 28.]]

put forward, π. πρόβλημα [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Sophista” 261a]]; ἄμφω τὰ δεξιὰ προβεβληκώς, of a horse, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Poetica” 1460b19]] (also middle, τὰ ἀριστερὰ προβάλλονται [Refs 4th c.BC+ [[prev. author] “IA” 706a6); χλαμύδα ἀλώπεκι 2nd c.AD: Pausanias Periegeta 4.18.6; π. αὐτὸν ἐς τὸ μέσον 2nd c.AD: Lucianus Sophista “Cat.” 25: _metaphorically_, ἀγαθὴν ἐλπίδα π. σαυτῷ 4th-3rd c.BC: Menander Comicus 572]]:—passive, see below [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Bacchylides Lyricus 111.1.]]

__II.b
in obstetrics, present, active and passive, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Hippocrates Medicus “γυναικεῖα” 1.69, 2nd c.AD: Soranus Medicus 2.60, +others]]

__II.2
ἔριδα προβαλόντες putting forth strife, i.e. striving, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 11.529.]]

__II.3
put forward as an argument or plea, ἐπεί μοι τὴν θέμιν προὔβαλες [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Trachiniae” 810; Κύπριν 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Hecuba” 825; τοὔνομα τὸ τῆς εἰρήνης 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 9.8]]:—passive, τὸν ὑφ᾽ ἁπάντων προβαλλόμενον λόγον [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 6.92; ἐς ἐνθυμίαν αἰεὶ προβαλλόμενος [prev. author] 5.16.]]

__II.4
middle, put forward, propose for an office, λῃτουργεῖν π. γυμνασίαρχον [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Andocides Orator 1.132]]:—passive, see below [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Bacchylides Lyricus 1.4.]]

propound a question, task, problem, riddle (compare πρόβλημα IV), [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Nubes” 757, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 536d]]; αἴνιγμα, γρῖφον, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. author] “Chrm.” 162b, 4th c.BC: Antiphanes Comicus 74.5; χαλεπὴν π. ᾱἵρεσιν 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Sophista” 245b; εὔσκεπτον σκέψιν π. [prev. author] “Phlb.” 65d]]; ὰπορίαν [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Politica” 1283b35: later followed by _interrogative_ clause, πρόβαλε σαυτῷ τί ἂν ἐποίησεν ἐν τούτῳ Σωκράτης 1st-2nd c.AD: Epictetus Philosophus “Enchiridion” 33.12; θεοῦ προβαλόντος πότερον.. 2nd c.AD: Aristides Rhetor 1.41 1st c.AD: Josephus Historicus:]] —passive, προβάλλεται τάδε θεωρῆσαι, περὶ τοῦ κώνου προβεβλημένα ἐστὶ τάδε, [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [3rd c.BC: Archimedes Geometra “Con.Sph.Praef., Spir.Praef.”]]

put forth beyond, κάρα.. ὀχημάτων [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Electra” 740; τῶν ὀδόντων τὴν γλῶσσαν 2nd c.AD: Aretaeus Medicus “περὶ αἰτιῶν καὶ σημείων ὀξέων παθῶν” 1.7; φλέγμα καὶ ἀφρῶδες ἐκ τοῦ στόματος 3rd c.AD: Philumenus Medicus “de Venenatis Animalibus” 1.2.]]

__III
expose, give up, π. σφέας αὐτοὺς ὑπὸ τοῦ κακοῦ give themselves up for lost, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 7.141; ἐμαυτὸν εἰς ἀρὰς δεινάς 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Tyrannus” 745; ψυχὴν π. ἐν κύβοισι δαίμονος]]hazard, venture, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Rhesus” 183.]]

__IV
send forth, emit, τράγου ὀσμήν variant (for προσ-) in [Refs 1st c.BC+ [1st c.AD: Dioscorides (Dioscurides) Medicus 4.50; τὴν φωνὴν ὀξεῖαν π. 1st c.BC: Diodorus Siculus Historicus 3.8; ἦχον τραχύν [prev. author] 5.30, etc.]]; produce, καρπόν [Refs 1st c.AD+ [1st c.AD: Josephus Historicus “Antiquitates Judaicae” 4.8.19; ἄνθος 6th c.AD: Aëtius Medicus 12.1]]:—passive, with genitive, to be emitted from, αἱ τῶν θεῶν δυνάμεις προβεβλημέναι τῶν πρώτων [Refs 5th c.AD+ [5th c.AD: Proclus Philosophus “in Platonis Parmenidem commentarii” p.552S.]]

__V
intransitive, stick out, of the tongue, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “de Partibus Animalium” 660a24.]]

__V.2

__B

__B.2

__B.4
put forward, propose for election, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.98, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Leges” 755cf, 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 6.1.25, “IG” 22.1343.29, etc.; προβαλλόμενος ἑαυτόν 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 21.15]]:—passive, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus [same place], Pl.[same place], etc.; προβληθεὶς πυλάγορος οὗτος 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 18.149, compare285.]]

with dative et infinitive, challenge a person to..,π. μοι [ὀμόσαι] Mitteis [Refs 2nd c.BC+ [“Chr.” 32i14, compare ii 13(2nd c.BC)]]:—passive, of the oath, to be proposed as a challenge, [Refs 1st c.AD+ [[prev. work]ii 25, “Sammelb.” 5231.9 (1st c.AD).]]

hold before oneself so as to protect, λαιᾷ ἴτυν [Refs 7th c.BC+ [7th c.BC: Tyrtaeus Elegiacus 15.3; Πηλεΐδᾳ κατ᾽ ὄμμα πέλταν 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Rhesus” 370 (Lyric poetry); τὼ χεῖρε 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Ranae” 201]]; π. τὰ ὅπλα level arms, opposed to μεταβάλλεσθαι [Refs 5th c.BC+ [compare (προβολή 1), τὴν φάλαγγα ἐκέλευσε προβαλέσθαι τὰ ὅπλα καὶ ἐπιχωρῆσαι 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 1.2.17, compare 6.5.16, “Mem.” 3.8.4: in]]perfect passive, σάρισαν προβεβλημένος having his pike advanced, with levelled pike, [Refs 1st c.BC+ [1st c.BC: Diodorus Siculus Historicus 17.100; τοὺς θυρεοὺς πρὸ τῶν νώτων.. -βεβλημένοι 2nd c.AD: Arrianus Historicus “Tactica” 36.1; εἰκοσάπηχύν τινα προβεβλ. κοντόν 2nd c.AD: Lucianus Sophista “DMort.” 27.4]]; also προβεβλημένοι τοὺς θωρακοφόρους having them to cover one in front, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 6.3.24]]; π. τάφρον, ποταμόν, of a general, [Refs 2nd c.BC+ [2nd c.BC: Polybius Historicus 1.18.3, 2.5.5; π. τῆς.. στρατοπεδείας τεῖχος [prev. author] 1.48.10, etc.; πόλις -βεβλημένη ποταμόν 1st c.BC-1st c.AD: Strabo Geographus 11.2.17]]; π. τὰ θηρία πρὸ τῶν κεράτων, λογχοφόρους τῆς δυνάμεως, [Refs 2nd c.BC+ [2nd c.BC: Polybius Historicus 3.72.9, 3.113.6]]: absolutely, stand in front, πρὸ ἀμφοῖν προβεβλημένος standing so as to cover both, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 4.2.21, compare “Cyr.” 2.3.10: with _genitive_, τούτου προβέβληται Πολύευκτος 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 21.139; προβάλλεσθαι ἢ ἐναντίον βλέπειν οὔτ᾽ οἶδεν οὔτ᾽ ἐθέλει [prev. author] 4.40]]; προαίρεσις τῆς πολιτείας προβεβλημένη a guarded policy, [Refs [[prev. author] 19.27]]; πρὸς ἅπαντας -βεβλημένος on one's guard against, [Refs 1st c.AD+ [1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus “Dio” 9]]:—passive, ἱππῆς προβέβληνται πρὸ τοῦ δεξιοῦ κέρως [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd c.AD: Arrianus Historicus “Tactica” 36.2; κράνη πρὸ τῆς κεφαλῆς π. [prev. work] 34.3.]]

metaphorically, put forward, τὴν ἀγαθὴν προβαλλόμενος ἐλπίδα [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 18.97; ταύτην τὴν συμμαχίαν [prev. work]195; τὴν Εὔβοιαν προβαλέσθαι πρὸ τῆς Ἀττικῆς [prev. work]301, compare 300, 5th-6th c.BC: Isocrates Orator 5.122; τι πρὸ τῆς αἰσχύνης 4th c.BC: Aeschines Orator 3.11.]]

__B.III.2.b
bring forward, cite on one's own part, in defence, τὸν Ὅμηρον π. [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Laches” 201b; π. μάρτυρας 4th c.BC: Isaeus Orator 7.3, etc.]]; ὁ προβαλόμενος one who has brought evidence, Legal cited in [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 46.10]]; cite as an example, ἔθνος οὐδὲν ἔχομεν προβαλέσθαι σοφίης πέρι [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 4.46]]; use as an excuse or pretext, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 2.87, etc.; τὸ εὐπρεπὲς ἄσπονδον προβέβληνται [prev. author] 1.37]]; π. σκῆψιν, πρόφασιν, [Refs 2nd c.BC+ [2nd c.BC: Polybius Historicus 5.56.7, 15.20.3.]]

in Attic dialect law, accuse a person by προβολή (see. προβολή see), present him as guilty of the offence, προὐβαλόμην ἀδικεῖν τοῦτον περὶ τὴν ἑορτήν [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 21.1 (compare 1st-2nd c.AD: Harpocratio Grammaticus see at {προβαλλομένους}); π. τινά τι [prev. work] 28]]; τινα alone, [Refs [[prev. work] 175]]; ὁ προβαλλόμενος the prosecutor in a προβολή, [Refs [[prev. work] 179]]:—passive, to be accused or presented, προὐβλήθησαν [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Historia Graeca (Hellenica)” 1.7.35]]: generally, attack, censure, τὸ ἔθος [Refs 1st c.BC+ [1st c.BC: Dionysius Halicarnassensis 4.24, compare 1st c.AD: Philo Judaeus 2.137; τοὺς ψευδομένους 1st c.AD: Josephus Historicus “Bellum Judaicum” 2.8.7 (assuming variant), compare 1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus “C. πρόβατον, -ου, τό
(προβαίνω), [in LXX chiefly for צֹאן, also for שֶׂה, more rarely for כֶּבֶשׂ (כֶּשֶׂב), רָחֵל ;]
__1. in Hom., Hdt., cattle, esp. of small cattle, sheep and goats.
__2. In NT, as in Attic writers generally (cf. MM, xxi), a sheep: Mat.7:15, Mrk.6:34, al.; πρόβατα σφαγῆς, Rom.8:36 (LXX). Metaphorical (in cl. of timidity, stupidity or idleness), of the followers of a leader or master, esp. of those who are subject to the care of the Good Shepherd: Mat.10:6 15:24 26:31" (LXX) Mrk.14:27 (LXX), Jhn.10:7-8, 15-16 10:26-27 21:16-17 (WH txt., προβάτια), Heb.13:20; opposite to ἐρίφια, Mat.25:33.
προβάτιον, -ου, τό,
dimin. of πρόβατον (used as a term of endearment, see El., § 27, 4), a little sheep: Jhn.21:16-17 (πρόβατα, WH, mg.).†
(AS)

B), also in 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus and 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus:]]future προέξω: aorist προέσχον, middle προεσχόμην, προὐσχόμην, compare προΐσχω:— hold before, τὴν ἀσπίδα τῆς κωλῆς [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Nubes” 989]]; especially so as to protect another, τὼ χεῖρε π. metaphorically, put forward as an excuse or pretence, use as a screen, τί τάδε προὐστήσω λόγ; [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Cyclops” 319; τὰ τῶν Ἀμφικτυόνωνδόγματα προστήσασθαι 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 5.19, etc.: with _genitive_, [τὴν ἀτυχίαν] τῆς κακουργίας προϊστάμενος 5th c.BC: Antipho Orator 2.3.1; τοῦ ἀγῶνος τὴν πρὸς ἔμ᾽ ἔχθραν προΐσταται 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 18.15.]]

__II.4
προστησώμεθα Τύρταιον put him forward, cite him as an authority, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Leges” 629a.]]

__II.5
prefer, value above, ὦτα τοῦ νοῦ προστησάμενοι [Refs [[prev. author] “R.” 531b.]]

__II.6
establish a thing before another, τοὺς ἀριθμοὺς τῆς ὑποστάσεως αὐτῶν (i.e. τῶν ὄντων) [Refs 3rd c.AD+ [3rd c.AD: Plotinus Philosophus 6.6.15, compare 5th c.AD: Proclus Philosophus “Inst.” 133.]]

__II.7
manifest, [Refs [[prev. work] 195, +others]]

__B
passive, with aorist 2 active προὔστην: perfect προέστηκα, 2nd pers. plural προέστατε [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 5.49]]; infinitive προεστάναι, participle προεστώς (see. below): future perfect προεστήξομαι, see below [Refs [11.2]]:—aorist passive προεστάθην, see below[Refs [11.3]]:—come forward, variant for{προσ-} in [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 60.15.]]

__B.2
c.accusative, approach as a suppliant, ἥ σε.. λιπαρεῖ προὔστην χερί [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Electra” 1378]]; προστῆναι μέσην τράπεζαν uncertain in [Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. author] “fragment” 660.1 (perhaps προσβῆναι):—in 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.86, προσστῆναι is restored.]]

__B.3
with dative, stand so as to face another, σοὶ γὰρ αἴας πολέμιος προὔστη ποτέ [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Ajax” 1133:—in 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.129, προσστάς is restored.]]

__B.4
stand in public, be a prostitute, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aeschines Orator “Epistulae” 7.3, Vett. Val. 16.7.]]

__B.II
with genitive, to be set over, be at the head of, τῆς Ἑλλάδος [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.69, 5.49; τῶν Ἀρκάδων τοὺς προεστεῶτας [prev. author] 6.74]]; especially to be chief or leader of a party, τῶν παράλων, τῶν ἐκ τοῦ πεδίου, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. author] 1.59; τοῦ δήμου [prev. author] 3.82, 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 3.70, 5th c.BC: Lysias Orator 13.7; ἡμῶν 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Vespae” 419; τῆς πόλεως 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 2.65]]; π. αὐτῶν to be their ringleader, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 6.2.9]]; π. χοροῦ, στρατεύματος, [Refs [[prev. author] “Mem.” 3.4.3]]; π. τῶν πολιτειῶν head the respective parties in the state, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Lysias Orator 25.9, etc.:]] absolutely, οἱ προεστῶτες, _Ionic dialect_ -εῶτες, the leading men, τῶν σκυθέων [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 4.79, compare 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 3.11, etc.; οἱ προεστηκότες ἐν ταῖς πόλεσι 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Historia Graeca (Hellenica)” 3.5.1]]; οἱ ἐν ταῖς πόλεσι προστάντες [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 3.82; τῷ προεστῶτι καὶ ἄρχοντι 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 428e.]]

__B.II.2
in various relations, govern, direct, οὐκ ὀρθῶς σεωυτοῦ προέστηκας you do not manage yourself well, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 2.173; π. τῆς μεταβολῆς 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 8.75; τοῦ ἱεροῦ 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Historia Graeca (Hellenica)” 3.2.31; τοῦ ἑαυτοῦ βίου [prev. author] “Mem.” 3.2.2; τοῦ πράγματος 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 30.18; προεστήξομαι τῆς χωνεύσεως “PCair.Zen.” 481.9 (3rd c.BC)]]; ἐργασίας, τέχνης, [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus “Pericles” 24, 2nd c.AD: Athenaeus Epigrammaticus 13.612a; π. ἐνδόξου καὶ καλῆς αἱρέσεως “OGI” 219.3 (Ilium, 3rd c.BC).]]

__B.II.3
stand before so as to guard, οἱ δορυφόροι Μασίστεω προέστησαν [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 9.107, compare 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Heraclidae” 306, etc.]]: hence, support, succour, πρόστητ᾽ ἀναγκαίας τύχης [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Ajax” 803]]; ὁ προστὰς τῆς εἰρήνης the champion of peace, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aeschines Orator 2.161]]; πάντων προστᾶσα [δύναμις] [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Timaeus” 25b]]; π. τινός to be his protector, [Refs 2nd c.BC+ [“GDI” 1726.6 (Delph., 2nd c.BC), “PFay.” 13.5 (2nd c.BC)]]; τῆς ἐναντίας π. γνώμης [Refs 2nd c.BC+ [2nd c.BC: Polybius Historicus 5.5.8; τοῖσιν ἐχθροῖς προὐστήτην φόνου]]were the authors of.., [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Electra” 980]]; π. [νόσου] [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Andromache” 221: _absolutely_, βέλεα.. ἀρωγὰ προσταθέντα 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Tyrannus” 206 (Lyric poetry).]]

προ-καλέω, -ῶ
[in LXX: 2Ma.8:11 A * ;]
to call forth.
Most frequently in mid.,

LSJ / STEPBible (TFLSJ)
προκαλ-έω,
call forth, [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd-3rd c.AD: Dio Cassius Historicus 44.34]]:—passive, [Refs 2nd c.BC+ [2nd c.BC: Polybius Historicus 22.9.2]]; to be evoked, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-3rd c.BC: Epicurus Philosophus “Fragmenta” 411.]]

__B
mostly middle, call out to fight, challenge, Αἴας δὲ πρῶτος προκαλέσσατο [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 13.809, compare 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 8.142; ἴθι νῦν προκάλεσσαι.. Μενέλαον ἐξαῦτις μαχέσασθαι 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 3.432, compare 7.39; προκαλέσσατο χάρμῃ [prev. work] 218]]; so, later, π. εἰς ἀγῶνα [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Memorabilia” 2.3.17, compare 2nd c.AD: Lucianus Sophista “Symp.” 20; εἰς μονομαχίαν 2nd-3rd c.AD: Aelianus “Varia Historia” 1.24; μάχῃ “Anacreontea” 12.7]]; ταῦτα π. τοὺς συνόντας thus.., [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 1.4.4]]; challenge to drink, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Critias Philosophus, Tragicus, Elegiacus “fragment” 6.7 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator]]; π. τινὰ συμπαίζει; συγγυμνάζεσθαι, [Refs 6th c.BC+ [6th c.BC: Anacreon Lyricus 14.4, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Symposium” 217c: proverbial, ἱππέας εἰς πεδίον προκαλῇ, Σωκράτη εἰς λόγους προκαλούμενος,]] of one who challenges another in his own department, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [[prev. author] “Tht.” 183d, compare 4th-3rd c.BC: Menander Comicus 268.]]

__B.2
invite or summon, τινὰ ἐς λόγους [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 4.201, 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 3.34; ἐς σπονδὰς καὶ διάλυσιν πολέμου [prev. author] 4.19; ἐπὶ ξυμμαχίαν [prev. author] 5.43; ἐπὶ τιμωρίαν 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 21.226; πρὸς τὸ συνδειπνεῖν 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Symposium” 217c]]; [ἰχθῦς] πρὸς τὴν θήραν π. entice them out, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Historia Animalium” 534a17]]; πρὸς αὑτόν τινας endeavour to attach them to oneself, [Refs 2nd c.BC+ [2nd c.BC: Polybius Historicus 3.77.7.]]

__B.3
with accusative et infinitive, invite one to do.., [Refs 5th c.BC+ [“Tragica Adespota” 165 (= “Comica Adespota” 1295), etc.; π. τινὰ ἐς λόγον ἐλθεῖν 5th-6th c.BC: Isocrates Orator 5.91; εἰρήνην ποιεῖσθαι 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Historia Graeca (Hellenica)” 2.2.15, compare 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Euthydemus” 294b, etc.; προκαλούμεθα ὑμᾶς φίλοι εἶναι καὶ ἐκ τῆς γῆς ἡμῶν ἀναχωρῆσαι 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 5.112]]; of things, αὐτὰ (i.e. τὰ πράγματα) προκαλεῖται παρασκευάζειν τι invite, admonish, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Politica” 1331a22: also π. εἰ βούλοιντο..,]] with infinitive, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 4.30.]]

__B.4
absolutely, αὐτῶν προκαλεσαμένων at or after their invitation,[Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. work] 20, compare 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 451c]]; appeal, προκαλεῖσθαι περί τινος ἐπὶ Ῥωμαίους [Refs 2nd c.BC+ [2nd c.BC: Polybius Historicus 24.9.13.]]

__B.II
with accusative of things, offer, propose, δίκην [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 1.39, compare 2.72, 73, 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Acharnenses” 984, etc.; τὰ εἰρημένα 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 5.37; τὰς σπονδάς 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Equites” 796: with _accusative_ _person_ added, προκαλεῖσθαί τινας τὴν εἰρήνην]] offer them peace, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. author] “Ach.” 652, compare 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Euthyphro” 5a, “Chrm.” 169c.]]

__B.II.2
law-term, make an offer or challenge to the opponent for bringing about a decision, e.g. for submitting the case to arbitration, letting slaves be put to the torture, etc., προκαλοῦνται πρόκλησιν ἡμᾶς [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 37.12, compare 40.44, 5th c.BC: Antipho Orator 1.6]]: with accusative person, challenge him, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. author] 6.23; π. εἰς πάντα τινάς [prev. work]26; εἰς ἀντίδοσιν 5th c.BC: Lysias Orator 24.9; εἰς ὅρκον 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 52.17; εἰς ἐμφανῶν κατάστασιν 4th c.BC: Isaeus Orator 6.31 (to be read προσ-)]]; π. τινά τι make one an offer, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 48.4, compare 37.42: with _accusative_ et]]infinitive, π. τὴν μητέρα ὀμόσαι offer that she should take an oath, [Refs [[prev. author] 55.27]]: with infinitive only, π. ἐθέλειν ἐπιδεῖξαι [Refs [[prev. author] 27.50, compare 54.27; also π. κατά τινος εἰς μαρτυρίαν [prev. author] 29.20 (προσκ- codices):]] —passive, π. περὶ Ἐπιδάμνου ἐς κρίσιν Th.l.34.

__B.III
call up or forth, εὐγένειαν [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Hercules Furens” 308; τὸν Θησαυρὸν ἐς τουμφανές 2nd c.AD: Lucianus Sophista “Tim.” 41; τρίχας 1st c.AD: Dioscorides (Dioscurides) Medicus 2.151.]]

LSJ / STEPBible (TFLSJ)
πρόκειμαι,
used as passive of προτίθημι, to be set before one, ὀνείαθ᾽ ἑτοῖμα προκείμενα the meats laid ready, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 9.91, +others]]; π. δαίς, δεῖπνον, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.211, 5.105; τὰ π. ἀγαθά [prev. author] 9.82]]; ἄρτοι προκείμενοι shew-bread, [LXX.Exo.39.18 (36); τράπεζα π. [prev. work] 38.9 (37.10).]

__2
lie exposed, ὁρέω παιδίον προκείμενον [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.111]]; of a tuft of wool, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Trachiniae” 702]]; ἄτιμος ὧδε πρόκειμαι, says Ajax of himself, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. author] “Aj.” 427 (Lyric poetry), compare 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Troades” 1179; νομίζετε τὸν παῖδα τουτονὶ ἱκετηρίαν ὑμῖν προκεῖσθαι 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 43.83]]; especially lie dead, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Septem contra Thebas” 964 (Lyric poetry), 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Ajax” 1059]]; προκείμενον νέκυν laid out for burial, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Alcestis” 1012, compare 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Antigone” 1101, 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Ecclesiazusae” 537, “Av.” 474, 5th c.BC: Antipho Orator 6.34, 2nd c.AD: Lucianus Sophista “Luct.” 12]]; opposed to ἐξενεχθείς, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Lysias Orator “Fragmenta” 23]] (also, to be buried first, [Refs 3rd c.AD+ [Inscriptiones Graecae ad res Romanas pertinentes 4.735 (from Eumenia), “MAMA” 4.357 ([prev. passage], 3rd c.AD)): _metaphorically_, πρὸς ὕβριν π.]] to be exposed to.., [Refs 1st c.BC+ [1st c.BC: Diodorus Siculus Historicus 33.15 (uncertain reading).]]

__3
to be set before competitors, as the prize of a contest, τοῖσι.. προὔκειτο μέγας τρίπος [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th-7th c.BC: Hesiodus Epicus “Scutum Herculis” 312: hence,]]

__3.b
metaphorically, to be set before one, proposed, γνῶμαι τρεῖς προεκέατο three opinions were set forth, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 3.83, compare 7.16. α; τοσούτων πέρι σκέψις πρόκειτα 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 533e, compare “Phdr.” 237c]]; π. τῷ συμβουλεύοντι σκοπὸς τὸ συμφέρον is proposed as a mark, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Rhetorica” 1362a17]]; ἡ προκειμένη ξυμμαγία the alliance which naturally offers, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 1.35]]; frequently of contests, πόνος τε καὶ ἀγὼν ἔσχατος ψυχῇ π. [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Phaedrus” 247b, compare “La.” 182a; καταγέλαστον.., ὃ πάλαι πρόκειται, τοῦτο πάλιν προτιθέναι [prev. author] “Euthd.” 279d]]; to be extant, προοίμια π. [Refs [[prev. author] “Lg.” 722e]]; frequently in participle, ὁ προκείμενος ἄεθλος the task set, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.126, 4.10, compare 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Prometheus Vinctus” 259, 755; ἀγῶνος μεγίστου π. 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 9.60; ἆθλα π. 5th c.BC: Lysias Orator 1.47, 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 2.3.2, etc.; τὸν π. πόνον 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Alcestis” 1149; ἔχειν ἔργον π. 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 407a]]; τὰ προκείμενα, opposed to μέλλοντα, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Antigone” 1334, compare 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Rhesus” 984; so ξυμφορᾶς προκειμένης [prev. author] Alcaeus551]]; τὸ π. ἐν τῷ λόγῳ or τὸ π., the question under discussion, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Gorgias” 457d, “La.” 184c, etc.]]; τὸ π. πρῆγμα the matter in hand, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.207: _impersonal_, περὶ σωτηρίας προκειμένου]] when the question is concerning safety, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Ecclesiazusae” 401; πρόκειται ἡμῖν ζητεῖν 2nd c.AD: Lucianus Sophista “Par.” 54, compare 1st c.BC: Dionysius Halicarnassensis “Ars Rhetorica” 7.5.]]

__4
to be set forth, settled, prescribed, appointed, ἔργων ὧν νόμοι πρόκεινται [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Tyrannus” 865 (Lyric poetry); π. σημήϊα 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 2.38]]; αἱ προκείμεναι ἡμέραι the prescribed days,[Refs [[prev. work] 87; ὀγδώκοντα ἔτεα ξόης πλήρωμα ἀνδρὶ προκεῖσθαι [prev. author] 3.22; ἀναγκαίη π. [prev. author] 1.11]]; τὸ θανεῖν.. πᾶσι πρόκειται probably in [Refs [“IG” 12(1).146 (from Rhodes)]]; of laws, νόμους ὑπερβαίνουσα τοὺς π. [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Antigone” 481]]; of punishments, στέρεσθαι κρατὸς ἦν προκείμενον [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Persae” 371; φόνον π. δημόλευστον 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Antigone” 36; πολλῶν [ἁμαρτημάτων] θανάτου ζημίαι π. 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 3.45.]]

__5
to be first stated, οὐ πρόκειται τοῦ λόγου τὸ τί ἐστιν [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Topica” 142b24.]]

__II
lie before, lie in front of, with genitive, Αἴγυπτος προκειμένη τῆς ἐχομένης γῆς projecting further than, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 2.12, compare 4.99]]; ᾗ (ᾧ codices) προὔκειτο μαστῶν περονίς where was set a brooch before her breasts, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Trachiniae” 925; πρὸ τῶν ἀνθρώπων π. τὰ παραφράγματα 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 514b; Ἐφέσου τεὰ τόξα πρόκειται 3rd c.BC: Callimachus Epicus “Hymnus in Dianam” 258; οἱ προκείμενοι τῶν στοῶν πύργοι 2nd c.BC: Polybius Historicus 1.48.2]]: absolutely, of a cape, island, etc., ἐν τῇ θαλάττῃ π. χωρίον [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 6.4.3; τὰ προκείμενα τῆς χώρας ὄρη [prev. author] “Mem.” 3.5.27; παρὰ ἤπειρον νῆσος π. [prev. author] “Ath.” 2.13, etc.]]

__II.2

Abbott-Smith / STEPBible (TBESG)

[in LXX: Dan LXX 11:37 (בִּין), Wis.6:7, al. ;]
