LSJ / STEPBible (TFLSJ)
προνοέω,
perceive before, foresee, δόλον [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 18.526, compare 5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “P.” 10.63; προνοῆσαι βραδεῖς τὰ.. ἀποβησόμενα 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 3.38; τὸ μέλλον ἔσεσθαι 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “de Caelo” 291a24]]; προνοῶν ὅτι ἀνάγκη ἔσοιτο foreseeing that.., [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 8.1.13]]; of divine foreknowledge, θεῖος νοῦς νοεῖ μὲν ὡς νοῦς, προνοεῖ δὲ ὡς θεός [Refs 3rd c.AD+ [5th c.AD: Proclus Philosophus “Inst.” 134, compare 3rd c.AD: Plotinus Philosophus 4.8.2.]]

__b
preconceive, [Refs 3rd c.AD+ [3rd c.AD: Porphyrius Tyrius Philosophus “Sententiae ad intelligibilia ducentes” 26.]]

__II
think of or plan beforehand, provide, οὐ.. τι πάρα προνοῆσαι ἄμεινον [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 5.364]]; opposed to μετανοέω, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Epicharmus Comicus 280]]; π. τὸ παραγγελλόμενον attend to it, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 4.1.6]]: absolutely, to be on one's guard, take precautions, ὥρα προνοεῖν πρὶν πελάσαι στρατόν [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Heraclidae” 289; περαιτέρω π. 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 3.43; π. καὶ προβουλεύεσθαι 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Memorabilia” 2.10.3: followed by _relative_]] adverb, π. ὅπως.. provide, take care that.., [Refs [[prev. author] “Eq.Mag.” 4.1]]; π. μὴ.., or ὡς μὴ.., cavere ne.., [Refs [[prev. author] “Oec.” 9.11, “Cyr.” 1.6.24]]; π. ὅτι.. pay due regard to the fact that.., [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 3.58.]]

__II.2
with genitive, provide for, take thought for, τῶν παίδων [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 8.1.1, compare 8.7.15, etc.]]; θεὸς π. τῶν ὅλων [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [2nd c.AD: Arrianus Historicus “Epicteti Dissertationes” 2.14.11, 5th c.AD: Proclus Philosophus “Inst.” 120; μάλιστα δὲ προνόησον Ἀρσινόης “PHal.” 1.179 (3rd c.BC)]]; opposed to ὀλιγωρεῖν, [Refs 1st c.BC+ [1st c.BC-1st c.AD: Strabo Geographus 5.3.8]]:—passive, [Refs 5th c.AD+ [5th c.AD: Proclus Philosophus “Inst.” 122.]]

__II.3
passive, to be provided, τὰ-ούμενα, of a poet's equipment, [Refs 1st c.BC+ [1st c.BC: Philodemus Philosophus “περὶ ποιημάτων” 5.3]]; of a patient, to be treated, [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd c.AD: Galenus Medicus 2.632]]; receive consideration, [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [PGiss. 7.23 (2nd c.AD).]]

__III
={προνοητεύω}, [Refs [“CIG” “Corpus Inscriptionum Graecarum” “Corpus Inscriptionum Graecarum” 3408 (Magn.Sip.).]]

__B
Attic dialect writers (also Inscrr. and Papyrus, see below) prefer middle προνοοῦμαι, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 6.9, etc. (so also 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 7.7.33, “Mem.” 4.3.12)]]: future -ήσομαι[Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator “Prooemia” 43, “IG” 22.1035.18, 1st c.BC: Dionysius Halicarnassensis 8.90, etc.]]: aorist προὐνοησάμην [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Hippolytus” 399, 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Equites” 421, 5th c.BC: Antipho Orator 5.43]]; in Prose mostly προὐνοήθην, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Cratylus” 395c, 5th c.BC: Lysias Orator 3.29, 4th c.BC: Isaeus Orator 2.46, 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 44.64, “PSI” 3.166.34 (2nd c.BC)]] (used in passive sense by [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd c.AD: Sextus Empiricus Philosophus “adversus Mathematicos” 9.404, 2nd c.AD: Galenus Medicus 2.632)]]: perfect προνενόημαι [Refs 2nd c.BC+ [2nd c.BC: Polybius Historicus 6.48.2, 1st c.BC: Diodorus Siculus Historicus 12.69]] (but infinitive πεπρονοῆσθαι [Refs [17.23), etc.]]—The sense and construction are the same as in the active: provide, ταῦτα [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 4.61, compare 4th c.BC: Isaeus Orator [same place], 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 44.64, etc.]]; οὐδέν Pl.[same place]; οἰκίδιόν τινι [Refs 5th c.BC+ [3rd c.AD(?): Diogenes Laertius 6.23; τὰ συμφέροντα ὑπὲρ τῶν μελλόντων 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Mem.” [same place]: _absolutely_, 5th c.BC: Lysias Orator 3.29, etc.; π. περὶ τούτων [prev. work]37; ὑπὲρ ὑμῶν καὶ τῆς πόλεως [prev. author] 26.15, compare 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 14.4]]: with infinitive, take care to do, E.[same place], [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Antipho Orator [same place]]]; π. μή with infinitive, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 23.135]]; π. ὅπως.. [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Lysias Orator 3.41; ὅτι.. 2nd c.BC: Polybius Historicus 38.16.1; ἵνα.. “Inscription Prien.” 27.12 (2nd c.BC).]]

__B.2
with genitive, provide for, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 6.9, etc.; τοῦ μέλλοντος 5th-6th c.BC: Andocides Orator 4.12; τῆς χώρας 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 7.7.33]]; superintend, τῆς οἰκοδομίας Haussoullier [Refs [“Milet” p.252; τῆς ἀναστάσεως τοῦ ἀνδριάντος “CIG” “Corpus Inscriptionum Graecarum” “Corpus Inscriptionum Graecarum” 2930b10 (from Tralles).]]

πρόνοια,
Ionic dialect προν-οίη, ἡ, (πρόνοος) perceiving beforehand, foresight, foreknowledge, τοὖπος τὸ θεοπρόπον τᾶς παλαιφάτου π. [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Trachiniae” 823 (Lyric poetry); προνοίαισι τοῦ πεπρωμένου 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Agamemnon” 684 (Lyric poetry).]]

__2
={πρόγνωσις}[Refs 5th c.BC+ [11.b, 5th c.BC: Hippocrates Medicus cited in 2nd c.AD: Galenus Medicus 18 (2).8.]]

__II
foresight, forethought, ἐπῄνεσ᾽.. πρόνοιαν ἣν ἔθου [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Ajax” 536; π. δ᾽ ἐστὶν οὐδενὸς σαφής [prev. author] “OT” 978]]; προνοίας οὕνεκα so far as foresight, caution is required, [Refs [[prev. author] “Ph.” 774, compare “El.” 1015; ἐκ προνοίης]]with forethought, purposely, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.120, 159, etc.]]; opposed to κατὰ τύχην, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. author] 8.87, compare 5th c.BC: Antipho Orator 5.21, 5th c.BC: Lysias Orator 26.19, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Phaedrus” 241e]]; ἀπὸ προνοίας τινῶν by their precautions, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 8.95; τὴν π. τὴν ές ἡμέας ἔχουσαν 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 8.144]]; προνοίᾳ τῶν συγγενῶν, φίλων, τῆς πόλεως, by care for.., [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Andocides Orator 1.56]]; especially of crimes committed with design or malice prepense, ἐκ προνοίας τραῦμα, ἐκ π. φόνοι, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aeschines Orator 3.212, 4th-3rd c.BC: Dinarchus Orator 1.6, etc.; ἐκ π. ἀποθνῄσκειν 5th c.BC: Antipho Orator 1.22, compare 5th c.BC: Lysias Orator 3.28]]; τὰ ἐκ π., opposed to ἀκούσια, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Politica” 1300b26]]; so οὐδεμία π. ἐστι τραύματος no intention of wounding, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Lysias Orator 3.41]]; πρόνοιαν ἔχειν (or ἴσχειν) τινός to take thought for.., show care for.., [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Alcestis” 1061, 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 2.89, etc.; περί τινος 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Antigone” 283; ὑπέρ τινος 5th-6th c.BC: Isocrates Orator 16.9; ἡ τοῦ χόρτου π. “PFlor.” 131.7 (3rd c.AD), compare 148.2 (3rd c.AD): with]]infinitive, πολλὴν π. εἶχεν εὐσχήμως (perhaps εὐσχήμων) πεσεῖν [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Hecuba” 569]]; πολλὴν π. ἔχειν μέλλοντας.. to beware of doing a thing, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Antipho Orator 5.91; π. ποιεῖσθαί τινος 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 21.97, etc.: _plural_, 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Oeconomicus” 7.38.]]

__II.2
providence, τοῦ θείου ἡ π. [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 3.108; τοῦ θεοῦ 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Coloneus” 1180; θεία π. 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Phoenissae” 637 (troch.); πρόνοιαι θεῶν 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Timaeus” 44c]]: absolutely, divine providence, προνοίας ἔργῳ [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Memorabilia” 1.4.6, etc., compare 4th-3rd c.BC: Zeno Citieus Stoicus 1.44, Cleanth.[prev. work]121, Chrysipp. [prev. work]2.168, +others (περὶ προνοίας as title of one of his works, [prev. work]3.203).]]

__II.3
[Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Pythagoras Philosophus]] name for five, [Refs [Theol.Ar. 31.]]

__II.4
office of προνοητής, [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [“POxy.” 472.10 (2nd c.AD).]]

__III
Πρόνοια Ἀθηνᾶ Athena as goddess of Forethought, under which name she was worshipped at Delphi, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 25.34, 1st c.BC: Diodorus Siculus Historicus 11.14, 1st c.BC: Parthenius Mythographus 25, 2nd c.AD: Pausanias Periegeta 10.8.6, 1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus 2.825b, 4th c.AD: Julianus Imperator “Orationes” 4.149b, etc.; at Delos _accusative_ to 4th-5th c.AD: Macrobius Grammaticus “Sat.” 1.17.55, compare 2nd c.AD: Aristides Rhetor 1.97 1st c.AD: Josephus Historicus, “Or.” 37(2).26; also Ἰουλία θεὰ Σεβαστὴ Π. “IG” 3.461]]: this name of Athena, which is guaranteed by the context in [Refs 8th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator, 2nd c.AD: Aristides Rhetor, 4th c.AD: Julianus Imperator, 4th-5th c.AD: Macrobius Grammaticus 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” cc., seems to have been a distortion of the name Προναία or Προνᾴα (see. πρόναος 1), but πρόνοια is _falsa lectio_ for{Προναία} (or Προνᾴα) in 4th c.BC: Aeschines Orator (see. πρόναος 1), and 1st c.BC: Diodorus Siculus Historicus, 1st c.BC: Parthenius Mythographus, 2nd c.AD: Pausanias Periegeta, 1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” cc. should perhaps be corrected.]]

Abbott-Smith / STEPBible (TBESG)
πρός,
prep. with genitive, dative, accusative
__I. I. C. genitive, of motion from a place, from the side of, hence metaphorically, in the interests of, Act.27:34 (cf. Page, in l.).
__II. II. C. dative, of local proximity, hard by, near, at: Mrk.5:11, Luk.19:37, Jhn.18:16  20:11,  12 Rev.1:13.
__III. C. accusative, of motion or direction towards a place or object, to, towards.
__1. Of place,
__(a) after verbs of motion or of speaking and other words with the idea of direction: ἔρχομαι, ἀναβαίνω, πορεύομαι,  λέγω, ἐπιστολή, etc., Mat.3:14, Mrk.6:51, Luk.11:5, Jhn.2:3, Act.9:2, al. mult.; metaphorically, of mental direction, hostile or otherwise, Luk.23:12, Jhn.6:52, 2Co.7:4, Eph.6:12, Col.3:13, al.; of the issue or end, Luk.14:32, Jhn.11:4, al.; of purpose, Mat.26:12, Rom.3:26, 1Co.6:5, al.; πρὸς τό, with inf., denoting purpose (cf. M, Pr., 218, 220; Lft., Notes, 131), Mat.5:28, Mrk.13:22, Eph.6:11, 1Th.2:9, al.;
__(b) of close proximity, at, by, with: Mat.3:10, Mrk.11:4, Luk.4:11, Act.3:2, al.; after εἶναι, Mat.13:56, Mrk.6:3, Jhn.1:1, al.
__2. 2. Of time,
__(a) towards (Plat., Xen., LXX: Gen.8:11, al.): Luk.24:29;
__(b) for: πρὸς καιρόν, Luk.8:13, 1Co.7:5; πρὸς ὥραν, Jhn.5:35, al.; πρὸς ὀλίγον, Jas.4:14.
__3. Of relation
__(a) toward, with: Rom.5:1, 2Co.1:12, Col.4:5, 1Th.4:12, al.;
__(b) with regard to: Mat.19:8, Mrk.12:12, Rom.8:31, al.;
__(with) pertaining to, to: Mat.27:4, Jhn.21:22, Rom.15:17, Heb.2:17 5:1;
__(d) according to: Luk.12:47, 2Co.5:10, Gal.2:14, Eph.3:4 4:14;
__(e) in comparison with: Rom.8:18.
__IV. In composition: towards (προσέρχομαι), to (προσάγω), against (προσκόπτω), besides (προσδαπανάω) .
(AS)

Ὀλύνθου 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 1.62, etc.]]; φυλακαὶ π. Αἰθιόπων, π. Ἀραβίων, π. __E
IN COMPOSITION (joined with other words),

__E.I
motion towards, as προσάγω, προσέρχομαι, etc.

__E.II
addition, besides, as προσκτάομαι, προσδίδωμι, προστίθημι, etc.

__E.III
a being on, at, by, or beside: hence, a remaining beside, and metaphorically connexion and engagement with anything, as πρόσειμι, προσγίγνομαι, etc.

__II.1

Attic dialect προστάττω ; Doric dialect ποτιτάσσω [Refs [“IG” 12(1).155.91 (from Rhodes), Anonymus in “PSI” 9.1091.1,]] also ποιτάσσω [Refs [“IG” 42(1).122.39, +others (Epid.)]]: perfect προστέταχα [LXX.Dan.2.8]:—passive, [Refs [1]] aorist προσετάχθην (see. below), also [Refs [2]] aorist προσετάγην[LXX.Sir.3.22:]

__I
with accusative person,

__I.1
place or post at a place, χωρεῖτε οἷ προστάσσομεν (i.e. ὑμᾶς) [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Orestes” 1678]]: —passive, προσταχθέντα.. πύλαις [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Septem contra Thebas” 527, compare 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Antigone” 670; ᾗ ἄν τις προσταχθῇ 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 2.87, compare 7.70.]]

__I.2
attach to, πρὸς τοῖσι ἔθνεσι τοὺς πλησιοχώρους π. attaching to certain tribes their next neighbours, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 3.89]]; π. τινάς τινι assign them to his command, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 5.8, compare 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 7.1.20]]:—passive, Ἰνδοὶ προσετετάχατο.. Φαρναζάθρῃ [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 7.65; κατὰ τέλη στρατηγῷ τινι προστεταγμένοι 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 6.42.]]

__I.3
reversely, ἐπὶ μὲν τῇ [μοίρῃ] ἑωυτὸν π. appointed himself to the one part as their head, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.94]]; π. ἄρχοντά τισι appoint as commander over them, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 6.93: with _dative_ omitted, [prev. author] 3.16, 8.23:]] —passive [Refs [, [prev. work] 8.]]

__II
with accusative of things, command, prescribe, enjoin, περὶ βοηθείας ἢ ἄλλο τι προστάττοντες τῆσι πόλεσι [Refs [“IG” 12.57.43]]; ἑκάστῳ ἔργον π., αὑτῷ πόνον π., [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.114, 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Ion” 1176, compare 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 4.5.25; πολὺ ἔργον π. ὡς τηλικῷδε 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Parmenides” 136d, etc.; πολλὰς ἐπιμελείας 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Politica” 1299b8; π. μνᾶς ἕξ]]prescribe [Refs 4th c.BC+ [6 minae, [prev. author] “EN” 1106b2; τισὶ περί τινος π. 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 19.71:]] —passive, τοῖσι δὲ ἵππος προσετέτακτο to others orders had been given to supply cavalry, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 7.21, compare 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Eumenides” 208]]; τὰ προσταχθέντα orders given, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 2.121.δ,compare 5th-6th c.BC: Isocrates Orator 3.13; τὸ προστεταγμένον 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 9.104; τὸ προσταχθέν [prev. author] 1.114, 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Philoctetes” 1010; τὰ προσταχθησόμενα 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Memorabilia” 3.5.6: _absolutely_, προσταχθὲν αὐτῷ]] the order having been given him, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Lysias Orator 30.2, compare 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 50.12; πλείω τῶν ὑπὸ τῆς πόλεως προσταττομένων δαπανᾶσθαι 5th c.BC: Lysias Orator 25.13.]]

__II.2
with dative person et infinitive, command, order one to do, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 5.105, 9.99, 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Coloneus” 1018, 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 7.29, 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 8.6.3, “PEnteux.” 6.4 (3rd c.BC), etc.]]; the dative must be supplied in [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.80, 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Coloneus” 494, etc.]]:—passive, impersonal, ἐκέλευε τοῖσι προσετέτακτο ταῦτα πρήσσειν διαταμεῖν [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 7.39; ὁ βασιλεὺς.. ἢ ἄλλος τις οἷς προστέτακται περὶ τούτων “IG” 12.94.19.]]

__II.3
with accusative et infinitive, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Helena” 890]]; both usages in successive clauses, ὅσα οἱ νόμοι π. τοὺς προσήκοντας ποιεῖν, ἡμῖν π. καὶ ἀναγκάζουσι ποιεῖν [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 43.59]]:—passive, to be ordered to do, τέσσερες.. κῶμαι.. τοῖσι κυσὶ προσετετάχατο σιτία παρέχειν [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.192, etc.]]; ὥσπερ προσετάχθησαν (i.e. ἐξεργάσασθαι) [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 5.75.]]

__II.4
absolutely, command, order, opposed to ὑπηρετέω, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Topica” 129a12]]:—passive, receive orders,[Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. work] 14; οἱ προστεταγμένοι 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 1.136.]]

__III
Astrology texts, correlative of ἀκούω see, [Refs 2nd c.BC+ [2nd c.AD: Ptolemaeus Mathematicus “Tetrabiblos” 35, 7th c.AD: Hephaestio Grammaticus Astr. 1.9, 2nd-1st c.BC(?): Serapio Astrologus in “Catalogus Codicum Astrologorum” 8(4).226.]]

π. ὅτι.. 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 18.231]]; of entries in accounts, προσετέθη τὰ τέλη τῷ κυριακῷ λόγῳ [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [“PAmh.” 77.15 (2nd c.AD),compare “BGU” 620.15 (4th c.AD), etc.]]; π. τινὶ [ἀργύριον] pay, [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [3rd c.BC: Zenon Papyri Michegan 28.24 (3rd c.BC),compare “PCair.Zen.” 647.56 (3rd c.BC), “PRyl.” 153.27 (2nd c.AD)]]; πρόσθες εἰς ὄνομα Ἐπωνύχου credit to account of [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus, “Ostr.” 1159 (2nd-3rd c.AD)]]; pay in, deposit gold in a bank or mint, [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [“PCair.Zen.” 23.32 (3rd c.BC).]]

__III.2
with accusative person, τίνα τῇδε προστιθῶ στάσε; [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Choephori” 114]]; Ἀθηναίοις π. σφᾶς αὐτούς join their party, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 3.92]]; π. ἑαυτόν τινι ἐς πίστιν, ἐπὶ ἰδίοις κέρδεσι, [Refs [[prev. author] 8.46, 50.]]

__III.3
in Mathematics texts, add, πὸτ ἀριθμόν.. φᾶφον [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Epicharmus Comicus 170.8 (probably); [χωρίον] ἕτερον αὐτῷ τουτὶ ἴσον 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Meno” 84d]]; πρὸς πεπερασμένον ἀεὶ π. [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Physica” 266b2]]:—passive, εἴ κα.. ποτὶ τὸ ἕτερον τῶν βαρέων ποτιτεθῇ,.. ῥέπειν ἐπὶ τὸ βάρος ἐκεῖνο ᾧ ποτετέθη [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [3rd c.BC: Archimedes Geometra “περὶ ἰσορροπιῶν” 1 “Def.” 2, compare 3rd c.BC: Euclides Geometra 1 “Ax.” 2, etc.; κοινοῦ -τεθέντος 3rd c.AD(?): Pappus Mathematicus 742.15.]]

__III.4
in Logic, add some determining word, opposed to ἀφαιρεῖν, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Analytica Posteriora” 91b27, compare “EN” 1147b33.]]

__III.5
in LXX and NT, continue or repeat an action, with infinitive, προσέθηκεν ἔτι λαλῆσαι [LXX.Gen.18.29; οὐ προσθήσω ἔτι πατάξαι [prev. work] 8.21]; οὐ μὴ προσθῶ πεῖν I will not drink again, [NT.Mark.14.25 (variant)]; also προσθεὶς Ἰὼβ εἶπεν Job continued and said, [LXX+NT [LXX.Job.27.1; προσθεὶς εἶπε παραβολήν NT.Luke.19.11]]; προσθεῖσα ἔτεκεν υἱόν she bore another son, [LXX.Gen.38.5]:—also in middle, see below [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Bacchylides Lyricus 111.]]

__B
middle, side with one, οἷς ἂν σὺ προσθῇ [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Coloneus” 1332, compare 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 3.11, 8.48, 87, 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 6.12, 11.6, 52.25]]; τῷ ἀστῷ π. to be favourable, wellinclined to him, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 2.160, compare 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 43.34]]; τῇ ἡδονῇ side with pleasure, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Magna Moralia” 1201a2]]: absolutely, come in, submit, Epist.[Refs 4th c.BC+ [1st c.AD: Philippus Epigrammaticus cited in 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 18.39.]]

__B.2
assent, agree, οὔ οἱ ἔγωγε π. τῇ γνώμῃ [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.109, compare 3.83, 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 6.50, 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 1.6.10; τῷ λόγῳ τῷ λεχθέντι 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 2.120; τῷ Καρχηδονίων νόμῳ 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Leges” 674a]]: later with infinitive, consent, bring onself to, [Refs 1st c.AD+ [1st c.AD: Josephus Historicus “Antiquitates Judaicae” 19.1.8.]]

__B.3
φῆφον δ᾽ Ὀρέστῃ τήνδ᾽ ἐγὼ προσθήσομαι will deposit this vote in favour of Orestes, i.e. will vote in his favour, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Eumenides” 735; ἡμῖν ἂν προσθέμενοι τὴν φῆφον εὐορκοίητε 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 57.69]]; so μὴ μιᾷ φήφῳ π. (i.e. τὴν γνώμην), ἀλλὰ δυοῖν [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 1.20]]; φῆφον π. ἐναντίαν τινί[Refs 3rd c.BC+ [[prev. work] 40; φῆφον π. ὥστε ἀποκτεῖναι “OGI” 218.102 (Ilium, 3rd c.BC).]]

__B.4
in Mathematics texts, add, [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [Sammelb. 6951 ii 30, +others (2nd c.AD).]]

__B.II
with accusative person, associate with oneself, i.e. take to one as a friend, ally, or helper, win over, π. τὸν δῆμον πρὸς τὴν ἑωυτοῦ μοῖραν [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 5.69, compare 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 6.18; εἰ στρατὸν προσθέοιτο φίλον 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.53, compare 69, 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Coloneus” 404]]; ταύτην προσθοῦ δάμαρτα take her to wife, [Refs [[prev. author] “Tr.” 1224]]: also in bad sense, πολέμιον π. τινά [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 2.4.12.]]

__B.II.2
with accusative of things, apply to oneself, βάλανον [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Hippocrates Medicus “ἐπιδημίαι” 1.26.a', compare 4.30 (_absolutely_, [prev. work] 1.26.δ᾽); ὀξύβαφον προσθοῦ λαβών 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Aves” 361; πατρὸς στέρνα προσθέσθαι θέλω 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Hercules Furens” 1408]]: metaphorically, put on, τῇ ὄφει ἀχθηδόνας [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 2.37]]; add to oneself, gain, τί ἂν προσθείμην πλέο; what should I be profited? [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Antigone” 40]]; π. χάριν, ={ἐπιχαρίζεσθαι}, [Refs [[prev. author] “OC” 767]]; especially of evils, bring or take upon onself, πρὸς κακοῖσι κακόν [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Persae” 531; μέριμναν 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Tyrannus” 1460; κακά 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Heraclidae” 146; ἄχθος ἐπ᾽ ἄχθει π. διπλοῦν [prev. author] “Andr.” 396]]; οἰκεῖον πόνον, κινδύνους αὐθαιρέτους, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 1.78, 144]]; ἔχθρας ἑκουσίους πρὸς ταῖς ἀναγκαίαις π. [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Protagoras” 346b.]]

__B.II.2.b
bring upon others, οἱ.. πόλεμον προσεθήκαντο made war upon him, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 4.65]]; οὐκ ἄν σφι Σπαρτιήτας μῆνιν οὐδεμίαν προσθέσθαι vented any wrath upon.., [Refs [[prev. author] 7.229.]]

__B.III
in LXX and NT, continue or repeat an action (compare above [LXX+4th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus 111.5), οὐ προσθήσεσθε ἔτι ἰδεῖν αὐτούς LXX.Exo.14.13]]; προσέθετο πέμφαι ἕτερον [NT.Luke.20.11]; προσέθετο συλλαβεῖν καὶ Πέτρον he caused Peter also to be arrested, [LXX+NT [NT.Act.12.3; also Φαραὼ προσέθετο τοῦ ἁμαρτάνειν LXX.Exo.9.34]]; οὐ προσέθετο τοῦ ἐπιστρέψαι[LXX.Gen.8.12.]

future -δρᾰμοῦμαι[Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 21.224]]:—run to or towards, come to one, πρὸς τοὺς νεκρούς [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 440a]]; τινι [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Acharnenses” 1084, “Av.” 759, 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 4.3.10, etc.]]: absolutely, run up, [Refs [[prev. author] “HG” 3.1.18, “Cyr.” 7.1.15, D.[same place], etc.]]

__2
in hostile sense, make a sally, πρός τι [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 5.4.47.]]

__3
of things, happen to one, τινι [Refs 1st c.BC+ [1st c.BC: Diodorus Siculus Historicus 13.37 codices]]; προστρέχει πολλαχοῦ τὸ γίγνεται” occurs frequently, [Refs 5th c.AD+ [5th-6th c.AD: Damascius Philosophus “de Principiis” 401.]]

__II
metaphorically, join or side with, [τῇ συγκλήτῳ] [Refs 2nd c.BC+ [2nd c.BC: Polybius Historicus 24.10.4, etc.; πρὸς τὴν τῶν πολλῶν γνώμην [prev. author] 28.7.8; πρὸς τὴν ἀλήθειαν [prev. author] 18.15.2.]]

__II.2
approach, -τρέχων τῇ ἐννόμῳ ἡλικίᾳ, i.e. not quite of age, [Refs 1st c.AD+ [“POxy.” 247.12 (1st c.AD).]]

__II.3
resemble, with dative, [Refs 1st c.AD+ [1st c.AD: Cornutus Philosophus “de Natura Deorum” 32.]]

fresh, not decomposed, of a corpse miraculously preserved, νῦν δέ μοι ἑρσήεις καὶ π. ἐν μεγάροισιν κεῖσαι [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 24.757]]; νεκρὸς π. of events and actions, recent, δίκαι [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Choephori” 804 (Lyric poetry); ἐπιστολαί 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Fragmenta” 128; ὀργή 5th c.BC: Lysias Orator 18.19; ὀχεία 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Historia Animalium” 509b31; φόβος 4th c.BC: Aeneas Tacticus 3.1; φθόνος 1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus “Themistocles” 24; θεωρίαι καὶ μαθήσεις 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Ethica Eudemia” 1237a24; φαντασία [prev. author] “MM” 1203b4]]; λύπη defined as δόξα πρόσφατος κακοῦ παρουσίας [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-3rd c.BC: Zeno Citieus Stoicus 1.52; ἀτύχημα 2nd c.BC: Polybius Historicus 1.21.9; εὐεργεσίαι [prev. author] 2.46.1]]; [πράγματα] [Refs 1st c.AD+ [1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus 2.146b]]; ὄγκοι (={οἰδήματα}) [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd c.AD: Galenus Medicus 18(2).145]]; βήξ, i.e. not yet chronic, [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd c.AD: Soranus Medicus 1.123, compare 2.46]]; γάλα, i.e. lately begun to be secreted, [Refs [[prev. author] 1.89]]; of persons, recent in date, of Homer, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Meteorologica” 351b35]]; μάρτυρες.. οἱ μὲν παλαιοὶ οἱ δὲ π. __3
new, οὐκ ἔστι πᾶν π. ὑπὸ τὸν ἥλιον [LXX.Eccl.1.9]; οὐκ ἔσται ἐν σοὶ θεὸς π.[LXX+NT+4th c.AD+ [LXX.Psa.80(81).10; ὁδὸν π. καὶ ζῶσαν NT.Heb.10.20; ἀεὶ ἡδίων ἡ π. ἀφροδίτη 4th c.AD: Alciphro Epistolographus 1.39.]]

adverb -τως newly, lately, π. ἠγγελμένων [LXX+4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aeneas Tacticus 16.2, cf. LXX.Deu.24.5, “OGI” 315.23 (Pessinus, 2nd c.BC), 1st c.BC: Parthenius Mythographus 28.1, 1st c.BC: Diodorus Siculus Historicus 14.115, 1st c.AD: Josephus Historicus “Bellum Judaicum” 1.6.2, 2nd c.AD: Babrius Fabularum Scriptor 30.3, Anon.Hist. (Heb. (פָּנִים מִלִּפְּנֵי); see Dalman, Words, 29), from the presence of, Act.3:19 5:41 7:45, 2Th.1:9, Rev.12:14 20:11; πρὸ π. (Heb. hold out, offer, μεγάλα π. ἐπ᾽ οἷσι ὁμολογέειν ἐθέλουσι [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 8.140. ; κέρδος 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Prometheus Vinctus” 777; τελετάς 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Bacchae” 238; κάλλος [prev. author] “Hel.” 28; φάντασμα 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 382a; ἐλπίδα 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Fragmenta” 131; δραχμὰς εἴκοσιν 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Plutus” 1019; ἐλευθερίαν 5th c.BC: Antipho Orator 5.50; δέλεαρ π. τὴν ἡδονήν 1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus 2 13a; ἐμοὶ λόγους 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Phaedrus” 230d]]: with infinitive, π. τινὶ λαβεῖν ὅ τι χρῄζει [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Oeconomicus” 5.8]]:—middle, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 5.24, 7.161; ἔρωτα 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Phaedrus” 266b; φιλίαν προτενεῖται 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 14.5; τὴν ἀειλογίαν [prev. author] 19.2]]:—passive, δυοῖν προτεινομένοιν ἀγαθοῖν [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Isocrates Orator 6.37, compare 12.117.]]

__II.4
put forward, propose, π. ζητήματα, ἐρωτήματα, [Refs 1st c.AD+ [1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus 2.737d, 2nd c.AD: Arrianus Historicus “Epicteti Dissertationes” 3.8.1; αἴνιγμά τινι 3rd c.AD(?): Diogenes Laertius 2.70, etc.]]:—middle, offer or put forward as instances, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Gorgias” 518b]]:—passive, [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd c.AD: Soranus Medicus 2.1, 4th c.AD: Iamblichus Philosophus “de Mysteriis” 1.3.]]

Med.. μισθὸν προτείνασθαι stipulate for as a reward, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 9.34.]]

put forward as a proposition (πρότασις [Refs 4th c.BC+ [1.1), 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Analytica Priora” 47a15, “Top.” 104a5, +others:]] —middle [Refs [, [prev. work] 164b4]]:—passive [Refs [, [prev. work] 7.]]

LSJ / STEPBible (TFLSJ)
πρότερος
and πρῶτος, comparative and superlative formed from πρό, opposed to ὕστερος, ὕστατος. comparative πρότερος, α, ον,

__I
of Place, before, in front, π. πόδες the fore-feet, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 19.228]]; π. ἵπποι horses in front, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Bacchylides Lyricus 5.43:]] — but mostly,

__II
of Time, former, earlier, ἄνδρες [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 21.405; ἄνθρωποι 5.637, 23.332]]; οἱ π. men of former times, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [4.308 (rarely without _Article_, 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Agamemnon” 1338 (_anapaest meter_), etc.); οὗτος δὲ προτέρης γενεῆς π. τ᾽ ἀνθρώπων 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 23.790]]: also, older, opposed to ὁπλότερος, [Refs [2.707, etc.; γενεῇ π. 15.182]]; but παῖδες π. children by the first or a former marriage, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 15.22; παῖδες ἐκ τῆς π. γυναικός 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 7.2]]; τῇ προτέρῃ (i.e. ἡμέρᾳ) on the day before, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 16.50]]; ἠοῖ τῇ π. [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 13.794 (in Prose more frequently τῇ προτεραίᾳ, compare προτεραῖος)]]; τοῦ π. ἐνιαυτοῦ the year before, [Refs [Inscriptiones Graecae 12.352.11]]; τοῖς π. Παναθηναίοις the preceding P., [Refs [[prev. work]57.8]]; τὰ π. what has preceded, [Refs 3rd c.AD+ [3rd c.AD: Plotinus Philosophus 3.2.8]]:—frequently used predicatively, sometimes where we should expect the adverb (which is never used by [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Homerus Epicus), ὅ με π. κάκ᾽ ἔοργε 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 3.351, compare 16.569, 8th-7th c.BC: Hesiodus Epicus “Opera et Dies” 708, etc.; σπονδὰς οὐ λύσετε πρότεροι 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 1.123; οἱ π. ἐπιόντες [prev. passage]; τοῖς π. μετὰ Κύρου ἀναβᾶσι 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 1.4.12, compare “IG” 22.1.7; εἰ μὴ π. ἑωράκη αὐτὸν ἢ ἐκεῖνος ἐμέ 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 336d, compare 432c, etc.; ὅτι εἴη π. ὑπὸ ἐκείνων ἠδικημένος “PCair.Zēn.” 288.9 (3rd c.BC).]]

__II.2
as regular comparative, with genitive, ἐμέο πρότερος [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 10.124; π. τούτων 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.168, compare 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Phaedo” 86b, “Hp.Ma.” 282d; τὰς γυναῖκας μὴ ἀπιέναι προτέρας τῶν ἀνδρῶν “IG” 12(5).593.19 (Iulis, 5th c.BC)]]; τῇ π. ἡμέρᾳ τῆς τροπῆς the day before.. , [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Politica” 1316a16; προτέρᾳ εἰδυῶν Ὀκτωμβρίων “IG” 7.2225.14 (Thisbe, Senatus Consultum, 2nd c.BC); τῷ π. ἔτει Παναθηναίων τῶν μεγάλων [prev. work]22.212.27; τῷ π. ἔτει τῆς ἥττης 2nd c.BC: Polybius Historicus 2.43.6: followed by ἤ, τῷ προτέρῳ ἔτεϊ ἢ τὸν κρητῆρα [ἐληΐσαντο] 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 3.47.]]

__III
of Rank, Worth, and generally of Precedence, superior, τῷ γένει, τῇ δυνάμει, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Isaeus Orator 1.17, 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 3.15]]; π. τινὸς πρός τι superior to him in.., [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Laches” 183b]]; π. τι ἄγειν, π. ποιήσασθαι τὰ σὰ πράγματα, [Refs 4th c.AD+ [4th c.AD: Libanius Sophista “Orationes” 58.36, 52.1.]]

__IV
after [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Homerus Epicus, _neuter_ πρότερον]] frequently as adverb, before, earlier, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “O.” 13.31, 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 4.45, “IG” 12.374.265, etc.]]; ὀλίγον π. [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Protagoras” 317e: with _genitive_, π. φήμης 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Septem contra Thebas” 866 (_anapaest meter_); ὀλίγῳ τι π. τούτων 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 8.95]]; πολλοῖσι ἔτεσι π. τούτων[Refs 4th c.BC+ [[prev. work] 96; ἐνιαυτῷ π. τῆς ἁλώσεως 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 9.60]]; also πρὸ τῶν Περσικῶν δέκα ἔτεσι π. [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Leges” 642d, compare “Criti.” 112a]]; τούτου π. [Refs 5th c.BC+ [2nd c.AD: Pausanias Periegeta 1.1.2: most frequently followed by ἤ, π. ἢ κατὰ τὴν προσδοκίαν 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Sophista” 264b; also μὴ π. ἀπαναστῆναι ἢ ἐξέλωσι 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 9.87, compare 7.54, 5th c.BC: Antipho Orator 2.1.2, 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 7.63, etc.]]: with infinitive, π. ἢ βασιλεῦσαι [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 7.2, compare 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 1.69, etc.: followed by πρίν, 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.82; by πρὶν ἄν, [prev. work] 140]]; by πρὶν ἤ with verb in Indic., [Refs [[prev. author] 6.45, 8.8, or Subj., 7.8.β (variant{πρὶν ἂν ἢ}), 9.93]]; also οὐ π. εἰ μὴ.. [Refs 1st c.AD+ [1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus “Lysander” 10, etc.]]; οὐ π. ἕως.., or ἕως ἂν.., [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Lysias Orator 12.71, 2nd c.AD: Athenaeus Epigrammaticus 14.640c; μὴ π., ἀλλ᾽ ὅταν.. 2nd c.BC: Polybius Historicus 9.13.3: also used with the _Article_, τὸ π. 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 522a, 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 4.4.14, etc. (τὸ π]]., also, for the first time, Ep. Gal.[Refs 5th c.BC+ [4.13): with _genitive_, τὸ π. τῶν ἀνδρῶν τούτων 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 2.144]]: the adverb is frequently put between Article and substantive, ὁ π. βασιλεύς [Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. author] 1.84; τὰ π. ἀδικήματα [prev. author] 6.87; αἱ π. ἁμαρτίαι 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Equites” 1355, etc.]]

__B
superlative πρῶτος, η, ον, Doric dialect πρᾶτος (which see):

__B.I
as adjective,

__B.I.1
of Place, foremost, πρώτοισιν ἐνὶ προμάχοισι μιγέντα [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 18.379]]; ἐν πρώτοις, μετὰ πρώτοισι alone, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 19.424, 11.64; πρώτῃ ἐν ὑσμίνῃ, ἐνὶ πρώτῳ ὁμάδῳ, 15.340, 17.380]]; τῆς πρώτης τάττειν (i.e. τάξεως) [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Isocrates Orator 12.180, compare 5th c.BC: Lysias Orator 16.15, etc.]]; ἐν π. ῥυμῷ at the front or end of the pole, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 6.40, 16.371]]; πρώτῃσι θύρῃσιν at the outermost doors, [Refs [22.66]]; π. ξύλον the front bench, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Acharnenses” 25, 2nd c.AD(?): Pollianus Epigrammaticus 4.121, etc.]]; οἱ π. πόδες, like{πρόσθιοι}, [Refs [[prev. author] 1.193.]]

__B.I.2
of Time, στάντα πρὸς π. ἕω looking towards first dawn, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Coloneus” 477; περὶ π. νύκτα 2nd c.AD(?): Pollianus Epigrammaticus 1.70.]]

__B.I.3
of Order, serving as ordinal to εἷς, ἄεθλα θῆκε.. τῷ πρώτῳ· ἀτὰρ αὖ τῷ δευτέρῳ.., αὐτὰρ τῷ τριτάτῳ.., κτλ., [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 23.265, compare 6.179; opposed to ὕστατος, 2.281, 5.703, etc.]]; opposed to τελευταῖος, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Agamemnon” 314]]; opposed to τανύστατος, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 9.449; πρῶτοι πάντων ἀνθρώπων 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 2.2; τὰ π. τῶν ὀνομάτων 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Cratylus” 421d; τῇ π. τῶν ἡμερέων 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 7.168, etc.; π. ἄξων “IG” 12.115.10]]; ἐπὶ τοῦ π. [ἱερείου] first-offered, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 4.3.9]]; ἐν τοῖς π. λόγοις in the earlier books, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Physica” 263a11, +others]]; ἐν πρώτοις among the first, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Isaeus Orator 7.40]]; hence, above all, especially, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 8.69, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 522c]]; in Attic dialect, ἐν τοῖς πρῶτοι (see. ὁ, ἡ, τό [Refs 8th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus VIII. 6):—frequently used predicatively of being the first to do something, Νέστωρ πρῶτος κτύπον ἄϊε 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 10.532; πρῶτος ἀνατέλλει 3rd c.BC: Eratosthenes Epicus “Cal.” 42; εἴθε π. σοι ἐνέτυχον 2nd c.AD: Lucianus Sophista “Tyr.” 21.]]

__B.I.3.b
Philos., first in order of existence, primary, αἱ π. οὐσίαι [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Categoriae” 2b26, compare “Metaphorical” 1032b2; π. ὕλη, π. φιλοσοφία, [prev. work] 1015a7, 1061b19]]; primitive, simple, οἰκία π., ἡ π. πόλις, [Refs [[prev. author] “Pol.” 1252b10, 1291a17; ἡ π. κοινωνία [prev. work] 1257a19; ἡ π. ὀλιγαρχία [prev. work] 1293a14]]; ὁ π. συλλογισμός normal, typical, [Refs [[prev. author] “Rh.” 1357a17]]; τὰ π. σώματα, μόρια,= τὰ ὁμοιομερῆ, [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd c.AD: Galenus Medicus 5.673,674]]; πρῶτα κατὰ φύσιν, e.g. health, perception, [Refs [“Stoicorum Veterum Fragmenta” 3.34; τὰ π. πάθη [prev. work]92; αἱ π. ἀρεταί [prev. work]64.]]

__B.I.3.c
in Mathematics texts, πρῶτοι ἀριθμοί prime numbers, [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [3rd c.BC: Euclides Geometra 7 “Def.” 11,12]]; but also, first numbers (= 1 to 100,000,000) in the notation of [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [3rd c.BC: Archimedes Geometra, “Aren.” 3.2.]]

__B.I.3.d
πρῶτος is sometimes used where we should expect πρότερος, Αἰνείας δὲ πρῶτος ἀκόντισεν [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 13.502, compare 18.92]]: in late Greek followed by genitive, πρῶτός μου ἦν [NT+2nd c.AD+ [NT.John.1.15, 30, compare 15.18; οἱ πρῶτοί μου ταῦτα ἀνιχνεύσαντες 2nd-3rd c.AD: Aelianus “De Natura Animalium - Ar.Byzantine Epit.” 8.12; πρώτη εὕρηται ἡ περὶ τοὺς πόδας κίνησις τῆς διὰ τῶν χειρῶν 2nd c.AD: Athenaeus Epigrammaticus 14.630c; γεννήτορα πρῶτον μητέρος εἰς ἀΐδην πέμψει 4th c.AD(?): Manetho Astrologus 1.329, 4.404]]; ἀλόχου πρῶτος before his wife, [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [“IG” 12(5).590.5 (vi (?) 2nd c.AD: Apollonius Dyscolus Grammaticus).]]

__B.I.4
of Rank or Dignity, μετὰ πρώτοισιν among the first men of the state, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 6.60, etc.; νομίσαντες πρῶτοι ἂν εἶναι 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 6.28]]; διαβάλλειν τοὺς π. [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 2.6.26, compare 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Politica” 1266a18; αἱ π. πόλεις 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 2.8; ὁ π. ἄρχων “IG” 12(3).481.10 (from Thera), “CIG” “Corpus Inscriptionum Graecarum” “Corpus Inscriptionum Graecarum” 2837 (from Aphrodisias)]]; ὁ π. τῆς πόλεως, as a title, [Refs [“IG” 12(5).292.2 (from Paros)]]; ὁ π. τῆς νήσου [NT.Act.28.7]; τῶν π. φίλων, title at the Ptolemaic court, [Refs 2nd c.BC+ [“PTeb.” 31.15 (2nd c.BC), etc.]]; τῶν π., as military title, [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [“PHib.” 1.110.72 (3rd c.BC), “PPetr.” 3p.23 (3rd c.BC), “PTeb.” 815 “fragment” 4.23, +others(3rd c.BC)]]: with genitive, ἐν πρώτοισι Μυκηναίων [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 15.643; οἱ π. στρατοῦ 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Philoctetes” 1305, compare 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Hecuba” 304, etc.: with _dative_ modi, ἀρετῇ π., οἱ π. καὶ χρήμασι καὶ γένει, πλούτῳ π. τῶν Ἑλλήνων, etc., 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Philoctetes” 1425, 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 3.65, 5th-6th c.BC: Isocrates Orator 16.31, etc.; π. ἐν συμφοραῖς βίου 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Tyrannus” 33.]]

__B.I.5
of Degree, first, highest, μοῖρα [Refs [[prev. author] “OC” 145 (_anapaest meter_), etc.]]

__B.II
as substantive in neuter plural πρῶτα, τά,

__B.II.1
(i.e. ἆθλα), first prize, τὰ π. λαβών [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 23.275; τὰ π. δόρει κρατύνων 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Coloneus” 1313; ἔχειν πρῶτα κυναγεσίας “Anthologia Graeca” 6.118 (Antip.); τὰ π. φέρεσθαι 2nd-3rd c.AD: Dio Cassius Historicus 42.57, etc.]]

__B.II.2
first part, beginning, τῆς Ἰλιάδος τὰ π. [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 392e]]; ἐν τοῖς π. [Refs [[prev. author] “Smp.” 221d; τὸ π. τοῦ ᾄσματος [prev. author] “Prt.” 343c.]]

__B.II.3
first, highest, in degree, τὰ π. τᾶς λιμῶ (Doric dialect) the extremities of famine, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Acharnenses” 743 (nisi to be read ἄπρατα); ἐχέτωσαν τὰ π. τῆς εὐδαιμονίας 2nd c.AD: Lucianus Sophista “Cont.” 10; ἐς τὰ π. τιμᾶσθαι 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 3.39, compare 56]]; φρενῶν ἐς τὰ ἐμεωυτοῦ π. οὔκω ἀνήκω I have not yet come to the highest development of my judgment, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 7.13, compare 2nd-3rd c.AD: Dio Cassius Historicus 38.22]]; of persons, ἐὼν τῶν Ἐρετριέων τὰ π. [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 6.100]]; Λάμπων.. Αἰγινητέων [ἐὼν] τὰ π. [Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. author] 9.78, compare 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Medea” 917]]; ἐστὶν τὰ π. τῆς ἐκεῖ μοχθηρίας (of a person) [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Ranae” 421.]]

__B.II.4
Philos., primary things, elements, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Empedocles Poeta Philosophus 38.1, 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “de Generatione et Corruptione” 335a29; τὰ π. αἴτια [prev. author] “Mete.” 338a20; also τὸ π. ἐνυπάρχον ἑκάστῳ [prev. author] “Ph.” 193a10.]]

__B.II.5
in Logic, the first undemonstrable propositions, on which all future conclusions rest, [Refs [[prev. author] “Top.” 100b18; τὰ π. ἀναπόδεικτα [prev. author] “APo.” 71b26.]]

__B.III
in Adverbial phrases,

__B.III.1
τὴν πρώτην (i.e. ὥραν, ὁδόν) first, for the present, just now, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 3.134, 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Thesmophoriazusae” 662, 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 3.2, 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Metaphysica” 1038a35, etc.; τὴν πρώτην εἶναι 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.153.]]

__B.III.2
with Preps., ἀπὸ πρώτης (i.e. ἀρχῆς) [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Antipho Orator 5.56, 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 1.77; ἀπὸ τῆς π. εὐθύς 2nd c.AD: Lucianus Sophista “Hist.Conscr.” 1]]; ἐκ π. [Refs 5th c.BC+ [2nd c.AD: Babrius Fabularum Scriptor 45.14; κατὰ πρώτας 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Politicus” 292b, 2nd-3rd c.AD: Dio Cassius Historicus 52.19; κατὰ τὴν π. εὐθύς [prev. author] 62.3]]; παρὰ τὴν π. the first time, opposed to ἐπὶ τῆς δευτέρας, [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd-3rd c.AD: Philostratus Sophista “Vita Apollonii” 1.22.]]

__B.III.3
frequently as adverb in neuter singular and plural, πρῶτον, πρῶτα,

__B.III.3.a
first, in the first place, πρῶτόν τε καὶ ὕστατον (vulgar form ὕστερον) [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th-7th c.BC: Hesiodus Epicus “Theogonia” 34; π. μὲν.., δεύτερον αὖ.., τὸ τρίτον αὖ.. 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 6.179]]; τί π. τοι ἔπειτα, τί δ᾽ ὑστάτιον καταλέξ; [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 9.14; Κύπριδα μὲν πρῶτα.., αὐτὰρ ἔπειτ᾽.. 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 5.458; οὐρῆας μὲν π. ἐπῴχετο.., αὐτὰρ ἔπειτα.. 1.50; π. μὲν.., ἔπειτα δὲ.. 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Coloneus” 632, 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 2.1.2, 23, “An.” 5.6.7 - 8, “Hier.” 11.8, etc.; π. μὲν.., ἔπειτα.. 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Phaedo” 89a, etc.; π. μὲν.., ἔπειτα δεύτερον.., τρίτον δὲ.. 4th c.BC: Aeschines Orator 1.7; π. μὲν.., εἶτα.. 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Philebus” 15b; π. μὲν.., εἶτα δὲ.. 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 1.2.16; π. μὲν.., εἶτα.., ἔτι δὲ.. [prev. author] “Mem.” 1.2.1; π. μὲν..,.. δὲ αὖ.. 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Leges” 935a; π. μὲν.., ἔτι δὲ.. 5th c.BC: Lysias Orator 4.10, etc.; π. μὲν.., ἔτι τοίνυν.. 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 44.57]]; frequently answered only by δέ, [Refs [[prev. author] 9.48, etc.]]; sometimes the answering clause must be supplied, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Agamemnon” 810, 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 7.7, etc.: also πρῶτον μὲν.. δεύτερον μήν.. 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Philebus” 66a: also πρῶτα μὲν.., ἔπειτα.. 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Trachiniae” 616, 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Plutus” 728; πρῶτα μὲν.., ἔπειτα.., εἶτα.. 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Medea” 548; πρῶτα μὲν..,.. δὲ.. 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Prometheus Vinctus” 447]]; πρῶτα μὲν.., ἔπειτα δὲ.. X [Refs 5th c.BC+ [“HG” 7.1.7, compare 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Philoctetes” 919]]; ἐπεί σε πρῶτα κιχάνω since my first meeting is with you, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 13.228, compare 7.53, 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 8.274: also τὸ πρῶτον]], first, in the first place, at the beginning, ὡς τὸ π. ὑπέστην καὶ κατένευσα [Refs 8th c.BC+ [4.267; οὕνεκά σ᾽ οὐ τὸ π., ἐπεὶ ἴδον, ὧδ᾽ ἀγάπησα 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 23.214. compare 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 3.443, 6.345, 5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “P.” 9.41, “N.” 3.49]]; τὸ μὲν οὖν π. [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Protagoras” 333d, etc.]]; τὸ π..., μετὰ ταῦτα.. [Refs 8th c.BC+ [Dem. 1.12: also τὰ π., 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 1.6, 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 1.257, etc.; πόντῳ μὲν τὰ π..., αὐτὰρ ἔπειτα.. 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 4.424; τὰ π. μὲν.., ὡς δὲ.. 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Persae” 412; τὰ π..., τέλος δὲ.. 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Fragmenta” 149.5, compare 966.]]

__B.b
too early, before the time, ἦ τ᾽ ἄρα καὶ σοὶ πρῶτα (variant for{πρωΐ}) παραστήσεσθαι ἔμελλε Μοῖρ᾽ ὀλοή [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 24.28.]]

__B.c
={πρότερον}, before, ἢν.. πρῶτον ἀπόλωμαι κακῶς [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Ecclesiazusae” 1079; π. οὐδ᾽ ὑφ᾽ ἑνὸς.. κρατηθέντες 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Historia Graeca (Hellenica)” 5.4.1]]; θάλασσα π. ἦν ἢ γενέσθαι γῆν variant in [Refs 4th c.BC+ [1st c.AD(?): Heraclitus 31; λόγῳ π. ἢ τοῖς ἔργοις 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Rhetorica ad Alexandrum” 1420b28; οὐ π. αὐτὴν ἀπέκτειναν πρὶν ἢ ἀπεκύησεν 2nd-3rd c.AD: Aelianus “Varia Historia” 5.18; π. συμμελετᾶν ἢ μελετᾶν μαθέτω “Anthologia Graeca” 12.206 (2nd c.AD: Strato Epigrammaticus).]]

__B.d
first, for the first time, οὐ.. νῦν πρῶτα ποδώκεος ἄντ᾽ Ἀχιλῆος στήσομαι [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 20.89; οὐ νῦν πρῶτον, ἀλλὰ καὶ πάλαι 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Philoctetes” 966; ἐνταῦθα πρῶτον ἔφαγον 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 2.3.16.]]

__B.e
πρῶτον, πρῶτα are used after the relative pronoun and after relative adverbs, like Engl.once (= at all), οὐδ᾽ ἐνοσίχθων λήθετ᾽ ἀπειλάων, τὰς.. Ὀδυσῆϊ π. ἐπηπείλησε [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 13.127, compare 3.320, 10.328, 13.133, 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 1.319, 19.136]]; μοῖραν δ᾽ οὔ τινά φημι πεφυγμένον ἔμμεναι ἀνδρῶν.. ἐπὴν τὰ π. γένηται when once he is born,[Refs 8th c.BC+ [6.489, compare 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 3.183, 4.13, 414; οὔτε.. Λυκίους ἐδύναντο τείχεος ἂψ ὤσασθαι, ἐπεὶ τὰ π. πέλασθεν 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 12.420, compare 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 11.106, 221]]; also ἐπεὶ τὸ (or τὰ) π. now that.. , ἀλλ᾽ ἐπεὶ οὖν τὸ π. ἀνέκραγον, οὐκ ἐπικεύσω now that I have spoken up,[Refs 8th c.BC+ [14.467; τὸ μὲν οὔ ποτε φύλλα καὶ ὄζους φύσει, ἐπεὶ δὴ πρῶτα τομὴν ἐν ὄρεσσι λέλοιπε 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 1.235, compare 276, 19.9: with]]participle, τῷ ῥ᾽ Αἴας τὸ π. ἐφεζόμενος μέγ᾽ ἀάσθη (the rock) on which once seated Aeschylus blasphemed, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 4.509]]: the sense as soon as is never necessary in [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Homerus Epicus]], but is possible in [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 4.414, 19.355]]; δινέμεν εὖτ᾽ ἂν πρῶτα φανῇ σθένος Ὠαρίωνος when once (or perhaps, as soon as), [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th-7th c.BC: Hesiodus Epicus “Opera et Dies” 598]]; ὅπως τις πρῶτα γένοιτο πάντας ἀποκρύπτεσκε as soon as each was born, [Refs [[prev. author] “Th.” 156]]; ὡς τὸ π. [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 7.8.14; τότ᾽ εὐθὺς.., ὅτε πρῶτον εἶδον 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 18.141]]; αὖθίς με ἀνερέσθαι ὅταν ἐντύχῃς πρῶτον the first time you meet me, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Lysis” 211b; ἐὰν μάθω γε πρῶτον.. τί λέγεις [prev. author] “R.” 338c.]]

__B.IV
adverb πρώτως primarily, first in [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus, π. καὶ κυρίως “EN” 1157a30; opposed to δευτέρως, [prev. work] 1158b31]]; π. καθ᾽ αὑτό, opposed to κατὰ συμβεβηκός, [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [[prev. author] “Ph.” 192b22, compare 2nd c.AD: Galenus Medicus 1.692, +others, 4th c.AD: Julianus Imperator “Orationes” 5.168b.]]

__B.IV.2
ὅτε π. ἐπεδήμησεν.. when he first visited.., [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [“BSA” 27.228 (Sparta, 2nd c.AD).]] —(From πρῶτος was formed a new _superlative_ πρώτιστος, which see)

deep_entry:
Abbott-Smith / STEPBible (TBESG)
A. Compar., πρότερος, -α, -ον,
[in LXX for רִאשׁוֹן ,לִפָנִים, etc. ;]
before, of time, place, rank, etc.; in NT always of Time, before, former: Eph.4:22. Adverbially, πρότερον, before, aforetime, formerly: Jhn.7:50, 2Co.1:15, Heb.4:6; opposite to ἔπειτα, Heb.7:27; τὸ π., Jhn.6:62 9:8, Gal.4:13, 1Ti.1:13; αἱ π. ἡμέραι, Heb.10:32; αἱ π. ἐπιθυμίαι, 1Pe.1:14.†
(AS)

---

LSJ / STEPBible (TFLSJ)
πρότερος
and πρῶτος, comparative and superlative formed from πρό, opposed to ὕστερος, ὕστατος. comparative πρότερος, α, ον,

__I
of Place, before, in front, π. πόδες the fore-feet, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 19.228]]; π. ἵπποι horses in front, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Bacchylides Lyricus 5.43:]] — but mostly,

__II
of Time, former, earlier, ἄνδρες [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 21.405; ἄνθρωποι 5.637, 23.332]]; οἱ π. men of former times, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [4.308 (rarely without _Article_, 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Agamemnon” 1338 (_anapaest meter_), etc.); οὗτος δὲ προτέρης γενεῆς π. τ᾽ ἀνθρώπων 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 23.790]]: also, older, opposed to ὁπλότερος, [Refs [2.707, etc.; γενεῇ π. 15.182]]; but παῖδες π. children by the first or a former marriage, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 15.22; παῖδες ἐκ τῆς π. γυναικός 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 7.2]]; τῇ προτέρῃ (i.e. ἡμέρᾳ) on the day before, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 16.50]]; ἠοῖ τῇ π. [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 13.794 (in Prose more frequently τῇ προτεραίᾳ, compare προτεραῖος)]]; τοῦ π. ἐνιαυτοῦ the year before, [Refs [Inscriptiones Graecae 12.352.11]]; τοῖς π. Παναθηναίοις the preceding P., [Refs [[prev. work]57.8]]; τὰ π. what has preceded, [Refs 3rd c.AD+ [3rd c.AD: Plotinus Philosophus 3.2.8]]:—frequently used predicatively, sometimes where we should expect the adverb (which is never used by [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Homerus Epicus), ὅ με π. κάκ᾽ ἔοργε 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 3.351, compare 16.569, 8th-7th c.BC: Hesiodus Epicus “Opera et Dies” 708, etc.; σπονδὰς οὐ λύσετε πρότεροι 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 1.123; οἱ π. ἐπιόντες [prev. passage]; τοῖς π. μετὰ Κύρου ἀναβᾶσι 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 1.4.12, compare “IG” 22.1.7; εἰ μὴ π. ἑωράκη αὐτὸν ἢ ἐκεῖνος ἐμέ 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 336d, compare 432c, etc.; ὅτι εἴη π. ὑπὸ ἐκείνων ἠδικημένος “PCair.Zēn.” 288.9 (3rd c.BC).]]

__II.2
as regular comparative, with genitive, ἐμέο πρότερος [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 10.124; π. τούτων 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.168, compare 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Phaedo” 86b, “Hp.Ma.” 282d; τὰς γυναῖκας μὴ ἀπιέναι προτέρας τῶν ἀνδρῶν “IG” 12(5).593.19 (Iulis, 5th c.BC)]]; τῇ π. ἡμέρᾳ τῆς τροπῆς the day before.. , [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Politica” 1316a16; προτέρᾳ εἰδυῶν Ὀκτωμβρίων “IG” 7.2225.14 (Thisbe, Senatus Consultum, 2nd c.BC); τῷ π. ἔτει Παναθηναίων τῶν μεγάλων [prev. work]22.212.27; τῷ π. ἔτει τῆς ἥττης 2nd c.BC: Polybius Historicus 2.43.6: followed by ἤ, τῷ προτέρῳ ἔτεϊ ἢ τὸν κρητῆρα [ἐληΐσαντο] 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 3.47.]]

__III
of Rank, Worth, and generally of Precedence, superior, τῷ γένει, τῇ δυνάμει, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Isaeus Orator 1.17, 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 3.15]]; π. τινὸς πρός τι superior to him in.., [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Laches” 183b]]; π. τι ἄγειν, π. ποιήσασθαι τὰ σὰ πράγματα, [Refs 4th c.AD+ [4th c.AD: Libanius Sophista “Orationes” 58.36, 52.1.]]

__IV
after [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Homerus Epicus, _neuter_ πρότερον]] frequently as adverb, before, earlier, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “O.” 13.31, 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 4.45, “IG” 12.374.265, etc.]]; ὀλίγον π. [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Protagoras” 317e: with _genitive_, π. φήμης 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Septem contra Thebas” 866 (_anapaest meter_); ὀλίγῳ τι π. τούτων 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 8.95]]; πολλοῖσι ἔτεσι π. τούτων[Refs 4th c.BC+ [[prev. work] 96; ἐνιαυτῷ π. τῆς ἁλώσεως 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 9.60]]; also πρὸ τῶν Περσικῶν δέκα ἔτεσι π. [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Leges” 642d, compare “Criti.” 112a]]; τούτου π. [Refs 5th c.BC+ [2nd c.AD: Pausanias Periegeta 1.1.2: most frequently followed by ἤ, π. ἢ κατὰ τὴν προσδοκίαν 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Sophista” 264b; also μὴ π. ἀπαναστῆναι ἢ ἐξέλωσι 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 9.87, compare 7.54, 5th c.BC: Antipho Orator 2.1.2, 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 7.63, etc.]]: with infinitive, π. ἢ βασιλεῦσαι [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 7.2, compare 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 1.69, etc.: followed by πρίν, 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.82; by πρὶν ἄν, [prev. work] 140]]; by πρὶν ἤ with verb in Indic., [Refs [[prev. author] 6.45, 8.8, or Subj., 7.8.β (variant{πρὶν ἂν ἢ}), 9.93]]; also οὐ π. εἰ μὴ.. [Refs 1st c.AD+ [1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus “Lysander” 10, etc.]]; οὐ π. ἕως.., or ἕως ἂν.., [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Lysias Orator 12.71, 2nd c.AD: Athenaeus Epigrammaticus 14.640c; μὴ π., ἀλλ᾽ ὅταν.. 2nd c.BC: Polybius Historicus 9.13.3: also used with the _Article_, τὸ π. 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 522a, 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 4.4.14, etc. (τὸ π]]., also, for the first time, Ep. Gal.[Refs 5th c.BC+ [4.13): with _genitive_, τὸ π. τῶν ἀνδρῶν τούτων 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 2.144]]: the adverb is frequently put between Article and substantive, ὁ π. βασιλεύς [Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. author] 1.84; τὰ π. ἀδικήματα [prev. author] 6.87; αἱ π. ἁμαρτίαι 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Equites” 1355, etc.]]

__B
superlative πρῶτος, η, ον, Doric dialect πρᾶτος (which see):

__B.I
as adjective,

__B.I.1
of Place, foremost, πρώτοισιν ἐνὶ προμάχοισι μιγέντα [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 18.379]]; ἐν πρώτοις, μετὰ πρώτοισι alone, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 19.424, 11.64; πρώτῃ ἐν ὑσμίνῃ, ἐνὶ πρώτῳ ὁμάδῳ, 15.340, 17.380]]; τῆς πρώτης τάττειν (i.e. τάξεως) [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Isocrates Orator 12.180, compare 5th c.BC: Lysias Orator 16.15, etc.]]; ἐν π. ῥυμῷ at the front or end of the pole, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 6.40, 16.371]]; πρώτῃσι θύρῃσιν at the outermost doors, [Refs [22.66]]; π. ξύλον the front bench, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Acharnenses” 25, 2nd c.AD(?): Pollianus Epigrammaticus 4.121, etc.]]; οἱ π. πόδες, like{πρόσθιοι}, [Refs [[prev. author] 1.193.]]

__B.I.2
of Time, στάντα πρὸς π. ἕω looking towards first dawn, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Coloneus” 477; περὶ π. νύκτα 2nd c.AD(?): Pollianus Epigrammaticus 1.70.]]

__B.I.3
of Order, serving as ordinal to εἷς, ἄεθλα θῆκε.. τῷ πρώτῳ· ἀτὰρ αὖ τῷ δευτέρῳ.., αὐτὰρ τῷ τριτάτῳ.., κτλ., [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 23.265, compare 6.179; opposed to ὕστατος, 2.281, 5.703, etc.]]; opposed to τελευταῖος, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Agamemnon” 314]]; opposed to τανύστατος, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 9.449; πρῶτοι πάντων ἀνθρώπων 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 2.2; τὰ π. τῶν ὀνομάτων 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Cratylus” 421d; τῇ π. τῶν ἡμερέων 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 7.168, etc.; π. ἄξων “IG” 12.115.10]]; ἐπὶ τοῦ π. [ἱερείου] first-offered, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 4.3.9]]; ἐν τοῖς π. λόγοις in the earlier books, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Physica” 263a11, +others]]; ἐν πρώτοις among the first, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Isaeus Orator 7.40]]; hence, above all, especially, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 8.69, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 522c]]; in Attic dialect, ἐν τοῖς πρῶτοι (see. ὁ, ἡ, τό [Refs 8th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus VIII. 6):—frequently used predicatively of being the first to do something, Νέστωρ πρῶτος κτύπον ἄϊε 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 10.532; πρῶτος ἀνατέλλει 3rd c.BC: Eratosthenes Epicus “Cal.” 42; εἴθε π. σοι ἐνέτυχον 2nd c.AD: Lucianus Sophista “Tyr.” 21.]]

__B.I.3.b
Philos., first in order of existence, primary, αἱ π. οὐσίαι [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Categoriae” 2b26, compare “Metaphorical” 1032b2; π. ὕλη, π. φιλοσοφία, [prev. work] 1015a7, 1061b19]]; primitive, simple, οἰκία π., ἡ π. πόλις, [Refs [[prev. author] “Pol.” 1252b10, 1291a17; ἡ π. κοινωνία [prev. work] 1257a19; ἡ π. ὀλιγαρχία [prev. work] 1293a14]]; ὁ π. συλλογισμός normal, typical, [Refs [[prev. author] “Rh.” 1357a17]]; τὰ π. σώματα, μόρια,= τὰ ὁμοιομερῆ, [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd c.AD: Galenus Medicus 5.673,674]]; πρῶτα κατὰ φύσιν, e.g. health, perception, [Refs [“Stoicorum Veterum Fragmenta” 3.34; τὰ π. πάθη [prev. work]92; αἱ π. ἀρεταί [prev. work]64.]]

__B.I.3.c
in Mathematics texts, πρῶτοι ἀριθμοί prime numbers, [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [3rd c.BC: Euclides Geometra 7 “Def.” 11,12]]; but also, first numbers (= 1 to 100,000,000) in the notation of [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [3rd c.BC: Archimedes Geometra, “Aren.” 3.2.]]

__B.I.3.d
πρῶτος is sometimes used where we should expect πρότερος, Αἰνείας δὲ πρῶτος ἀκόντισεν [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 13.502, compare 18.92]]: in late Greek followed by genitive, πρῶτός μου ἦν [NT+2nd c.AD+ [NT.John.1.15, 30, compare 15.18; οἱ πρῶτοί μου ταῦτα ἀνιχνεύσαντες 2nd-3rd c.AD: Aelianus “De Natura Animalium - Ar.Byzantine Epit.” 8.12; πρώτη εὕρηται ἡ περὶ τοὺς πόδας κίνησις τῆς διὰ τῶν χειρῶν 2nd c.AD: Athenaeus Epigrammaticus 14.630c; γεννήτορα πρῶτον μητέρος εἰς ἀΐδην πέμψει 4th c.AD(?): Manetho Astrologus 1.329, 4.404]]; ἀλόχου πρῶτος before his wife, [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [“IG” 12(5).590.5 (vi (?) 2nd c.AD: Apollonius Dyscolus Grammaticus).]]

__B.I.4
of Rank or Dignity, μετὰ πρώτοισιν among the first men of the state, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 6.60, etc.; νομίσαντες πρῶτοι ἂν εἶναι 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 6.28]]; διαβάλλειν τοὺς π. [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 2.6.26, compare 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Politica” 1266a18; αἱ π. πόλεις 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 2.8; ὁ π. ἄρχων “IG” 12(3).481.10 (from Thera), “CIG” “Corpus Inscriptionum Graecarum” “Corpus Inscriptionum Graecarum” 2837 (from Aphrodisias)]]; ὁ π. τῆς πόλεως, as a title, [Refs [“IG” 12(5).292.2 (from Paros)]]; ὁ π. τῆς νήσου [NT.Act.28.7]; τῶν π. φίλων, title at the Ptolemaic court, [Refs 2nd c.BC+ [“PTeb.” 31.15 (2nd c.BC), etc.]]; τῶν π., as military title, [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [“PHib.” 1.110.72 (3rd c.BC), “PPetr.” 3p.23 (3rd c.BC), “PTeb.” 815 “fragment” 4.23, +others(3rd c.BC)]]: with genitive, ἐν πρώτοισι Μυκηναίων [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 15.643; οἱ π. στρατοῦ 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Philoctetes” 1305, compare 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Hecuba” 304, etc.: with _dative_ modi, ἀρετῇ π., οἱ π. καὶ χρήμασι καὶ γένει, πλούτῳ π. τῶν Ἑλλήνων, etc., 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Philoctetes” 1425, 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 3.65, 5th-6th c.BC: Isocrates Orator 16.31, etc.; π. ἐν συμφοραῖς βίου 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Tyrannus” 33.]]

__B.I.5
of Degree, first, highest, μοῖρα [Refs [[prev. author] “OC” 145 (_anapaest meter_), etc.]]

__B.II
as substantive in neuter plural πρῶτα, τά,

__B.II.1
(i.e. ἆθλα), first prize, τὰ π. λαβών [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 23.275; τὰ π. δόρει κρατύνων 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Coloneus” 1313; ἔχειν πρῶτα κυναγεσίας “Anthologia Graeca” 6.118 (Antip.); τὰ π. φέρεσθαι 2nd-3rd c.AD: Dio Cassius Historicus 42.57, etc.]]

__B.II.2
first part, beginning, τῆς Ἰλιάδος τὰ π. [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 392e]]; ἐν τοῖς π. [Refs [[prev. author] “Smp.” 221d; τὸ π. τοῦ ᾄσματος [prev. author] “Prt.” 343c.]]

__B.II.3
first, highest, in degree, τὰ π. τᾶς λιμῶ (Doric dialect) the extremities of famine, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Acharnenses” 743 (nisi to be read ἄπρατα); ἐχέτωσαν τὰ π. τῆς εὐδαιμονίας 2nd c.AD: Lucianus Sophista “Cont.” 10; ἐς τὰ π. τιμᾶσθαι 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 3.39, compare 56]]; φρενῶν ἐς τὰ ἐμεωυτοῦ π. οὔκω ἀνήκω I have not yet come to the highest development of my judgment, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 7.13, compare 2nd-3rd c.AD: Dio Cassius Historicus 38.22]]; of persons, ἐὼν τῶν Ἐρετριέων τὰ π. [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 6.100]]; Λάμπων.. Αἰγινητέων [ἐὼν] τὰ π. [Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. author] 9.78, compare 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Medea” 917]]; ἐστὶν τὰ π. τῆς ἐκεῖ μοχθηρίας (of a person) [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Ranae” 421.]]

__B.II.4
Philos., primary things, elements, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Empedocles Poeta Philosophus 38.1, 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “de Generatione et Corruptione” 335a29; τὰ π. αἴτια [prev. author] “Mete.” 338a20; also τὸ π. ἐνυπάρχον ἑκάστῳ [prev. author] “Ph.” 193a10.]]

__B.II.5
in Logic, the first undemonstrable propositions, on which all future conclusions rest, [Refs [[prev. author] “Top.” 100b18; τὰ π. ἀναπόδεικτα [prev. author] “APo.” 71b26.]]

__B.III
in Adverbial phrases,

__B.III.1
τὴν πρώτην (i.e. ὥραν, ὁδόν) first, for the present, just now, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 3.134, 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Thesmophoriazusae” 662, 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 3.2, 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Metaphysica” 1038a35, etc.; τὴν πρώτην εἶναι 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.153.]]

__B.III.2
with Preps., ἀπὸ πρώτης (i.e. ἀρχῆς) [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Antipho Orator 5.56, 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 1.77; ἀπὸ τῆς π. εὐθύς 2nd c.AD: Lucianus Sophista “Hist.Conscr.” 1]]; ἐκ π. [Refs 5th c.BC+ [2nd c.AD: Babrius Fabularum Scriptor 45.14; κατὰ πρώτας 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Politicus” 292b, 2nd-3rd c.AD: Dio Cassius Historicus 52.19; κατὰ τὴν π. εὐθύς [prev. author] 62.3]]; παρὰ τὴν π. the first time, opposed to ἐπὶ τῆς δευτέρας, [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd-3rd c.AD: Philostratus Sophista “Vita Apollonii” 1.22.]]

__B.III.3
frequently as adverb in neuter singular and plural, πρῶτον, πρῶτα,

__B.III.3.a
first, in the first place, πρῶτόν τε καὶ ὕστατον (vulgar form ὕστερον) [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th-7th c.BC: Hesiodus Epicus “Theogonia” 34; π. μὲν.., δεύτερον αὖ.., τὸ τρίτον αὖ.. 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 6.179]]; τί π. τοι ἔπειτα, τί δ᾽ ὑστάτιον καταλέξ; [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 9.14; Κύπριδα μὲν πρῶτα.., αὐτὰρ ἔπειτ᾽.. 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 5.458; οὐρῆας μὲν π. ἐπῴχετο.., αὐτὰρ ἔπειτα.. 1.50; π. μὲν.., ἔπειτα δὲ.. 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Coloneus” 632, 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 2.1.2, 23, “An.” 5.6.7 - 8, “Hier.” 11.8, etc.; π. μὲν.., ἔπειτα.. 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Phaedo” 89a, etc.; π. μὲν.., ἔπειτα δεύτερον.., τρίτον δὲ.. 4th c.BC: Aeschines Orator 1.7; π. μὲν.., εἶτα.. 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Philebus” 15b; π. μὲν.., εἶτα δὲ.. 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 1.2.16; π. μὲν.., εἶτα.., ἔτι δὲ.. [prev. author] “Mem.” 1.2.1; π. μὲν..,.. δὲ αὖ.. 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Leges” 935a; π. μὲν.., ἔτι δὲ.. 5th c.BC: Lysias Orator 4.10, etc.; π. μὲν.., ἔτι τοίνυν.. 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 44.57]]; frequently answered only by δέ, [Refs [[prev. author] 9.48, etc.]]; sometimes the answering clause must be supplied, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Agamemnon” 810, 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 7.7, etc.: also πρῶτον μὲν.. δεύτερον μήν.. 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Philebus” 66a: also πρῶτα μὲν.., ἔπειτα.. 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Trachiniae” 616, 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Plutus” 728; πρῶτα μὲν.., ἔπειτα.., εἶτα.. 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Medea” 548; πρῶτα μὲν..,.. δὲ.. 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Prometheus Vinctus” 447]]; πρῶτα μὲν.., ἔπειτα δὲ.. X [Refs 5th c.BC+ [“HG” 7.1.7, compare 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Philoctetes” 919]]; ἐπεί σε πρῶτα κιχάνω since my first meeting is with you, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 13.228, compare 7.53, 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 8.274: also τὸ πρῶτον]], first, in the first place, at the beginning, ὡς τὸ π. ὑπέστην καὶ κατένευσα [Refs 8th c.BC+ [4.267; οὕνεκά σ᾽ οὐ τὸ π., ἐπεὶ ἴδον, ὧδ᾽ ἀγάπησα 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 23.214. compare 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 3.443, 6.345, 5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “P.” 9.41, “N.” 3.49]]; τὸ μὲν οὖν π. [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Protagoras” 333d, etc.]]; τὸ π..., μετὰ ταῦτα.. [Refs 8th c.BC+ [Dem. 1.12: also τὰ π., 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 1.6, 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 1.257, etc.; πόντῳ μὲν τὰ π..., αὐτὰρ ἔπειτα.. 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 4.424; τὰ π. μὲν.., ὡς δὲ.. 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Persae” 412; τὰ π..., τέλος δὲ.. 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Fragmenta” 149.5, compare 966.]]

__B.b
too early, before the time, ἦ τ᾽ ἄρα καὶ σοὶ πρῶτα (variant for{πρωΐ}) παραστήσεσθαι ἔμελλε Μοῖρ᾽ ὀλοή [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 24.28.]]

__B.c
={πρότερον}, before, ἢν.. πρῶτον ἀπόλωμαι κακῶς [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Ecclesiazusae” 1079; π. οὐδ᾽ ὑφ᾽ ἑνὸς.. κρατηθέντες 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Historia Graeca (Hellenica)” 5.4.1]]; θάλασσα π. ἦν ἢ γενέσθαι γῆν variant in [Refs 4th c.BC+ [1st c.AD(?): Heraclitus 31; λόγῳ π. ἢ τοῖς ἔργοις 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Rhetorica ad Alexandrum” 1420b28; οὐ π. αὐτὴν ἀπέκτειναν πρὶν ἢ ἀπεκύησεν 2nd-3rd c.AD: Aelianus “Varia Historia” 5.18; π. συμμελετᾶν ἢ μελετᾶν μαθέτω “Anthologia Graeca” 12.206 (2nd c.AD: Strato Epigrammaticus).]]

__B.d
first, for the first time, οὐ.. νῦν πρῶτα ποδώκεος ἄντ᾽ Ἀχιλῆος στήσομαι [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 20.89; οὐ νῦν πρῶτον, ἀλλὰ καὶ πάλαι 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Philoctetes” 966; ἐνταῦθα πρῶτον ἔφαγον 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 2.3.16.]]

__B.e
πρῶτον, πρῶτα are used after the relative pronoun and after relative adverbs, like Engl.once (= at all), οὐδ᾽ ἐνοσίχθων λήθετ᾽ ἀπειλάων, τὰς.. Ὀδυσῆϊ π. ἐπηπείλησε [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 13.127, compare 3.320, 10.328, 13.133, 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 1.319, 19.136]]; μοῖραν δ᾽ οὔ τινά φημι πεφυγμένον ἔμμεναι ἀνδρῶν.. ἐπὴν τὰ π. γένηται when once he is born,[Refs 8th c.BC+ [6.489, compare 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 3.183, 4.13, 414; οὔτε.. Λυκίους ἐδύναντο τείχεος ἂψ ὤσασθαι, ἐπεὶ τὰ π. πέλασθεν 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 12.420, compare 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 11.106, 221]]; also ἐπεὶ τὸ (or τὰ) π. now that.. , ἀλλ᾽ ἐπεὶ οὖν τὸ π. ἀνέκραγον, οὐκ ἐπικεύσω now that I have spoken up,[Refs 8th c.BC+ [14.467; τὸ μὲν οὔ ποτε φύλλα καὶ ὄζους φύσει, ἐπεὶ δὴ πρῶτα τομὴν ἐν ὄρεσσι λέλοιπε 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 1.235, compare 276, 19.9: with]]participle, τῷ ῥ᾽ Αἴας τὸ π. ἐφεζόμενος μέγ᾽ ἀάσθη (the rock) on which once seated Aeschylus blasphemed, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 4.509]]: the sense as soon as is never necessary in [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Homerus Epicus]], but is possible in [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 4.414, 19.355]]; δινέμεν εὖτ᾽ ἂν πρῶτα φανῇ σθένος Ὠαρίωνος when once (or perhaps, as soon as), [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th-7th c.BC: Hesiodus Epicus “Opera et Dies” 598]]; ὅπως τις πρῶτα γένοιτο πάντας ἀποκρύπτεσκε as soon as each was born, [Refs [[prev. author] “Th.” 156]]; ὡς τὸ π. [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 7.8.14; τότ᾽ εὐθὺς.., ὅτε πρῶτον εἶδον 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 18.141]]; αὖθίς με ἀνερέσθαι ὅταν ἐντύχῃς πρῶτον the first time you meet me, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Lysis” 211b; ἐὰν μάθω γε πρῶτον.. τί λέγεις [prev. author] “R.” 338c.]]

__B.IV
adverb πρώτως primarily, first in [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus, π. καὶ κυρίως “EN” 1157a30; opposed to δευτέρως, [prev. work] 1158b31]]; π. καθ᾽ αὑτό, opposed to κατὰ συμβεβηκός, [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [[prev. author] “Ph.” 192b22, compare 2nd c.AD: Galenus Medicus 1.692, +others, 4th c.AD: Julianus Imperator “Orationes” 5.168b.]]

__B.IV.2
ὅτε π. ἐπεδήμησεν.. when he first visited.., [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [“BSA” 27.228 (Sparta, 2nd c.AD).]] —(From πρῶτος was formed a new _superlative_ πρώτιστος, which see)

[in LXX: Exo.40:4, 23, Lev.24:8 (עָרַךְ) Psa.54:3 (שׂוּם), etc. ;]

__b
π. τινὰ κυσίν throw him to the dogs, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 24.409]]; τινὰ θηρσὶν ἁρπαγὴν π. [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Electra” 896.]]

__c
hand over for burial, τινά τινι [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Electra” 1198, compare 1487.]]

__2
expose a child, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.112; π. τινὰ ἔρημον 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Philoctetes” 268]]:—passive, ὁ θανάτῳ προτεθείς [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Phoenissae” 803 (Lyric poetry).]]

__3
set up, institute, propose, especially of contests, ἅμιλλαν λόγων [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Medea” 546; λόγων τοὺς ἀγῶνας 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 3.67; εἰ πονηρίας ἀγὼν προτεθείη 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Phaedo” 90b]]; ἄπορον αἵρεσιν offer a choice, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. author] “Tht.” 196c (but also προτίθεσθαί τινι αἵρεσιν [prev. author] “Lg.” 858a); π. νόμον 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Hippolytus” 1046.]]

__3.b
set up as a mark or prize, στέφανόν τισι τῶν ἀγώνων [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 2.46; σκοπὸν κάλλιστον ἐν τῷ ζῆν 2nd c.BC: Polybius Historicus 7.8.9]]:—passive, προὐτέθην ἐγὼ ἆθλον.. δορός [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Helena” 42.]]

__3.c
set as a penalty, θάνατον ζημίαν π. [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 3.44]]; τιμωρίας ἔτι μείζους οὐ μέχρι τοῦ δικαίου[Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. work] 82; τῶν νόμων τὰ ἔσχατα ἐπιτίμια προτεθηκότων 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 34.37; τοῖσι ἐκείνου ἀπογόνοισι ἀέθλους τοιούσδε 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 7.197.]]

fix, set, ἐς ἑβδομήκοντα ἔτεα οὖρον τῆς ζόης ἀνθρώπῳ π. [Refs [[prev. author] 1.32:]] —middle; οὖρον π. ἐνιαυτόν[Refs [[prev. work] 74.]]

appoint as a task or duty, τινί τι [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Trachiniae” 1049; νεωτέρῳ τοῦτο βαστάζειν πρόθες [prev. author] “Ant.” 216]]; δμῳαῖς π. πένθος οἰκεῖον στένειν[Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. work] 1249, compare 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 9.94]]:—middle, propose to oneself as a task or object, ὅπερ προὐθέμεθα σκέψασθαι [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Phaedrus” 259e, “R.” 352d, compare “Sph.” 221a, “Tht.” 169c; π. ψέγειν αὐτὸ ἢ ἐπαινεῖν [prev. author] “Lg.” 638c, compare 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Ethica Nicomachea” 1142b19 (uncertain), 2nd c.BC: Hipparchus Astronomicus 1.1.6, 2nd c.AD: Lucianus Sophista “Nec.” 19.]]

middle, also, put forth on one's own part, display, show, εὐλάβειαν [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Electra” 1334; ἀνδραγαθίαν 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 3.64; ἔχθραν [prev. author] 8.85.]]

__7
middle, θνητοὺς ἐν οἴκτῳ προθέμενος setting before oneself in pity, feeling compassion for, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Prometheus Vinctus” 241.]]

__8
advance money, [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [“IPE” 12.32 B 30,63 (Olbia, 3rd c.BC)]]; τὸ διδόμενον ἆθλον ὑπὸ τοῦ δήμου αὐτὸς προέθηκεν ἐκ τοῦ ἰδίου [Refs 1st c.BC+ [“IG” 12(9).234.18 (Eretria, 1st c.BC)]]; τισὶν τῶν πολιτῶν εἰς λύτρα προτιθείς [Refs 2nd c.BC+ [“SIG” 708.15 (Istropolis, 2nd c.BC).]]

__II
π. νεκρόν lay out a dead body, let it lie in state, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 5.8]]:—middle, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Alcestis” 664, “Supp.” 53 (Lyric poetry), 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Lysistrata” 611, 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 2.34, 5th c.BC: Lysias Orator 12.18, etc.; ποτήρια χρύσεα προθεῖτο 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 3.148.]]

__II.2
set out wares for show or sale, [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd c.AD: Lucianus Sophista “Nigr.” 25, +others]]

__II.3
display a public notice, τὸ λεύκωμα πρὸ τοῦ ναοῦ [Refs 2nd c.BC+ [“IG” 9(2).1109.35 (Coropa, 2nd c.BC)]]; ἐπ᾽ αὐτῆς τῆς οἰκίας π. ἐν λευκώματι [Refs 2nd c.BC+ [“UPZ” 106.20 (2nd c.BC)]]; τὸ ὑπογεγραμμένον ἔκθεμα [Refs 1st c.AD+ [“OGI” 664.4 (Egypt, 1st c.AD),compare “POxy.” 2108.8 (_passive_, 3rd c.AD)]]; notify publicly, τοὺς [προέδρους] προτιθέναι περὶ ὧν δεῖ βουλεύεσθαι [Refs 4th c.BC+ [“IG” 42(1).68.80 (Epid., 4th c.BC)]]; περὶ ὧν.. οἱ ἄρχοντες προτίθεισι [Refs 4th c.BC+ [Ἀρχ.Δελτ.9 παρ.53 (from Eresus),compare “IG” 12(2).526a21 ([prev. passage], 4th c.BC), 645b35 (Nesus, 4th c.BC)]]; τὰς πράξεις (exactions).. τῶν προτιθεμένων (passive) κατὰ τὰς ἐγγραφάς [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Politica” 1321b42]]; call a case for trial by means of a public notice, τῶν κατ᾽ αὐτοὺς προτεθέντων [Refs 2nd c.BC+ [“UPZ” 118.18 (2nd c.BC)]]; οἱ προτεθέντες ἐπ᾽ ἐμὲ καὶ μὴ ὑπακούσαντες ἴστωσαν ὅτι.. [Refs 1st c.AD+ [“PHamb.” 29.6 (1st c.AD)]]; advertise for sale or other purpose, [Refs 2nd c.BC+ [“BGU” 992 i 7 (_passive_, 2nd c.BC), “PLips.” 64.44 (4th c.AD), etc.]]; τοῖς συλλημψομένοις ὑμῖν γέρα προτιθέντα advertising rewards to those of you who apprehend (robbers), [Refs 3rd c.AD+ [“POxy.” 1408.16 (3rd c.AD).]]

__II.4
propose, bring forward a thing to be examined and debated, also give an opportunity for debate, voting, ἐς μέσον σφι π. πρῆγμα [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.206; π. τὸν λόγον [prev. author] 8.59; γνώμας σφίσιν αὐτοῖς 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 1.139]]; π. λόγον (i.e. εἰς ἐκκλησίαν) [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aeschines Orator 2.65; λόγον περί τινος 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Memorabilia” 4.2.3]]; γνώμας π. αὖθις Ἀθηναίοις, of the Prytanes, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 6.14, compare 3.36]]; π. τὴν διαγνώμην αὖθις περὶ Μυτιληναίων[Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. work] 42, compare 5th-6th c.BC: Isocrates Orator 8.15]]; π. βουλὴν εἴτε.. εἴτε.. [Refs 5th c.BC+ [1st c.BC: Dionysius Halicarnassensis 6.15; τὸν ἐπιμήνιον, ἢν μὴ προθῇ, ἑκατὸν στατῆρας ὀφείλειν “SIG” 58.10 (Milet., 5th c.BC), compare 141.12 (Corc. Nigra, 4th c.BC), 167.13 (Mylasa, 4th c.BC), +others]]; προθεῖναι αὖθις περὶ Μυτιληναίων λέγειν propose a discussion about.., [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 3.38; τὸ συμφέρον ἡ πόλις προὐτίθει σκοπεῖν 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 18.273, etc.]]; π. αὐτοῖς κρίσιν appoint a trial for them, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Lysias Orator 27.8; π. αὐτοῖς ἀγορὰν δικῶν 2nd c.AD: Lucianus Sophista “Bis Acc.” 4; προέθηκε.. λέγειν τὰ ἑκατέροισι.. κατέργασται]] has proposed (or initiated) a recital of what each has done, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 9.27]]: with dative person et infinitive, [Refs [[prev. author] 3.38]]: with accusative et infinitive, π. γνώμην ἀποφαίνεσθαι τὸν βουλόμενον [Refs [[prev. author] 8.49]]:—middle, ἤν τις προθῆται ψῆφον, ὥστε μὴ εἶναι τὸν νόμον τοῦτον [Refs 5th c.BC+ [“SIG” 45.33 (Halic., 5th c.BC):]] —passive, οὐ προὐτέθη σφίσι λόγος speech was not allowed them, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Historia Graeca (Hellenica)” 1.7.5; ψῆφος περὶ ἡμῶν ὑπὲρ ἀνδραποδισμοῦ προτεθεῖσα 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 19.65.]]

__II.5
convene a meeting, προὔθεσαν οἱ πρυτάνεις ἐκκλησίαν [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd c.AD: Lucianus Sophista “Nec.” 19]]:—middle, σύγκλητον τήνδε γερόντων προὔθετο λέσχην [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Antigone” 161 (_anapaest meter_).]]

__III
put forward, as one foot before the other, βραδύπουν ἤλυσιν ἄρθρων [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Hecuba” 67 (_anapaest meter_).]]

__III.2
hold out as a pretext, αἰτίαν [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Ajax” 1051]]:—middle, τὴν συγγένειαν [Refs 2nd c.BC+ [2nd c.BC: Polybius Historicus 2.19.1, etc.]]

__IV
put before or first, προτιθέντι ἀνάγκη.. λέγειν, opposed to ἐπιλέγοντι, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Rhetorica” 1394a15, compare b28; π. τοῦ λόγου προοίμιον 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Leges” 723c]]; set down first in writing, προθεὶς ἄρχοντα Νικόμαχόν φησιν οὕτως· ἐπὶ τούτου κτλ.” [Refs 1st c.BC+ [1st c.BC: Didymus Grammaticus]] in D.[Refs 2nd c.AD+ [1.19, compare 8.17, +others, 2nd c.AD: Galenus Medicus 19.183]]:— middle, put in front, τοὺς γροσφομάχους [Refs 2nd c.BC+ [2nd c.BC: Polybius Historicus 1.33.9]]; premise, λόγον [Refs [[prev. author] 3.118.11; τὰς προειρημένας αἰτίας [prev. author] 4.25.6]]:—passive, τὸ μὴ καὶ τὸ οὒ προτιθέμενα τῶν ἐπιόντων ὀνομάτων [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Sophista” 257c: _metaphorically_, 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 2.42.]]

__IV.2
put before or over, πρόσθεν ὀμμάτων πέπλον π. [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Iphigenia Aulidensis” 1550]]:— middle, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Iphigenia Taurica” 1218, etc.]]

__IV.3
prefer one to another, τί τινος [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 3.53, 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Medea” 963; ἡδονὴν ἀντὶ τοῦ καλοῦ [prev. author] “Hipp.” 382]]:—middle, πάρος τοὐμοῦ πόθου προὔθεντο τὴν τυραννίδα [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Coloneus” 419.]]
