προτρέπω,
urge forwards; used by [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Homerus Epicus]] only intransitive in middle or passive, turn to flight, προτρέποντο μελαινάων ἐπὶ νηῶν [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 5.700]]; of the sun, ὅτ᾽ ἂν ἂψ ἐπὶ γαῖαν ἀπ᾽ οὐρανόθεν προτράπηται [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 11.18, compare 12.381: _metaphorically_, ἄχεϊ προτραπέσθαι]] give myself up to grief, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 6.336.]]

__II
later, in active, urge on, impel, τίς σ᾽ ἀνάγκῃ τῇδε προτρέπε; [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Electra” 1193; π. τινά 5th-6th c.BC: Isocrates Orator 5.123]]; opposed to κωλύω, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Ethica Nicomachea” 1113b26]]: with accusative person et infinitive, urge on, impel, persuade one to do a thing, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 9.90, 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Antigone” 270; π. τὰ δέοντα ποιεῖν ὑμᾶς 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 2.3, compare “BGU” 164.17 (2nd-3rd c.AD), etc.]]; π. τοὺς δικαστὰς ὀργίζεσθαι [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aeschines Orator 2.3; ὁ καλῶς προτρέπων ἐρᾶν 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Symposium” 181a]]; προτρέψαι (or -τρέψασθαι) τινὰ ὥστε πειρᾶσθαι [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 8.63: followed by a _preposition_, π. τινὰ εἰς or ἐπὶ φιλοσοφίαν, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Euthydemus” 275a, 307a; ἐπ᾽ ἐλευθερίαν τὰ πλήθη [prev. author] “Lg.” 699e; ἐπ᾽ ἀρετήν 5th-6th c.BC: Isocrates Orator 2.8, 4th c.BC: Lycurgus Orator 10, etc.; ἐπὶ τὰς ἀδικίας 5th-6th c.BC: Isocrates Orator 7.46; πρὸς τὸ παρέπεσθαι 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Phaedo” 89a, etc.; συμβουλεύει ἢ προτρέπων ἢ ἀποτρέπων 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Rhetorica” 1358b15]]:— middle, with accusative person et infinitive, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Prometheus Vinctus” 990, 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Tyrannus” 358, etc.]]; προτρέπεσθαι ἀνθρώπους ἐπ᾽ ἀρετήν, τοὺς συνόντας πρὸς ἐγκράτειαν, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Memorabilia” 1.4.1, 4.5.1; νόμοι πολίτας ἐς δικαιοσύνην π. [prev. author] “Cyr.” 2.2.14; προὐτράπετο εἰς τὸ διαλέγεσθαι 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Protagoras” 348c; πρὸς ἀρετῆς ἐπιτηδεύματα π. τοὺς πολίτας [prev. author] “Lg.” 711b]]; ὡς.. προετρέψατο ὁ Σόλων τὸν Κροῖσον εἴπας.., ἐπειρώτα.., as Solon's story led Croesus on, he asked, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.31]]; προτρέψομαι I will lay an injunction on thee, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Tyrannus” 1446 (variant)]]; prescribe, ἐν τῇ φαρμακείῃ [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Hippocrates Medicus “περὶ φύσιος ἀνθρώπου” 9, but compare 2nd c.AD: Galenus Medicus 15.122, 19.133]]:—passive, to be persuaded or influenced, ὑπὸ τῶν ὀρνίθων ἀποτρέπεσθαι καὶ π. [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Memorabilia” 1.1.4, compare 2nd c.AD: Lucianus Sophista “Icar.” 29]]: with infinitive, ὑπ᾽ ἐκείνων -τραπήσεσθαι ὅ τι ἂν κελεύωνται ποιεῖν [Refs 1st c.BC+ [1st c.BC: Philodemus Gadarensis Epigrammaticus “Mus.” p.87K.; ὑπὸ τῆς ἐλπίδος π. “SIG” 1073.37 (Olympia, 2nd c.AD)]]; προετράπη γράψαι [Refs 3rd c.AD+ [3rd c.AD(?): Achilles Tatius Astronomus “Vit.Arat.” p.77 Maass.]]

__III
promote, οὖρα, χυμόν, [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd c.AD: Galenus Medicus 11.32; γάλα, σπέρμα, [prev. work] 771:]] —passive, ἢν προτρέπηται ὁποῖα δεῖ if stimulated in the right way, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Hippocrates Medicus “περὶ διαίτης ὀξέων” 51.]]

__IV
in middle, outstrip, outdo, πάντας ἐν τῷ πίνειν [Refs 1st c.AD+ [1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus 2.624c.]]

__V
search out, discover, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Hippolytus” 715 (_accusative_ to Scholia; uncertain reading).]]

take the initiative in a thing, with genitive, ἀδικίας [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 3.40]]; τῶν εὐεργεσιῶν, τῆς ἔχθρας, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Isocrates Orator 5.36,125: with _dative_, π. τῷ ποιεῖν εὖ 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 20.46]]: with neuter adjective, π. τι ἔς τινα [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd-3rd c.AD: Dio Cassius Historicus 38.34:]] —passive, τὰ προϋπηργμένα εἰς αὑτόν benefits formerly received, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 49.25, compare “OGI” 244.8 (Daphne, 2nd c.BC), 5th c.AD: Hierocles Platonicus Philosophus “in Carmen Aureum - FPG” 7p.429M.; but also προϋπηργμένα ἀδικήματα 4th c.AD: Iamblichus Philosophus “de Mysteriis” 4.5.]]

__II
intransitive, exist before, be pre-existent, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 2.85, 4.126, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Protagoras” 317d, “PLille” 1v4 (3rd c.BC), etc.]]; οἱ νόμοι οἱ προϋπάρχοντες [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Politica” 1292b20, compare “SIG” 526.31 (Itanos, 3rd c.BC)]]; ἡ τῶν σωμάτων αὔξησις ἐκ προϋπαρχόντων ἐστίν from pre-existent materials, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Rhetorica” 1419b22; πᾶσα μάθησις ἐκ προϋπαρχούσης γίνεται γνώσεως [prev. author] “APo.” 0.71a1]]; προϋπάρξαντα things that happened before, past events, variant for{πρὶν ὑπ}. in [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 1.11]]; τὰ προϋπάρχοντα former possessions, [Refs 1st c.AD+ [1st c.AD: Cebes Philosophus 31, 2nd-3rd c.AD: Dio Cassius Historicus 38.38]]; οἱ π. ὕπατοι the previous consuls, [Refs 2nd c.BC+ [2nd c.BC: Polybius Historicus 3.106.2:]]perfect passive, τὰ προϋπηργμένα antecedents, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 18.262, 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Rhetorica” 1367b13]]; οἰκειότης, χάρις προϋπηργμένη, [Refs 1st c.AD+ [1st c.AD: Josephus Historicus “contra Apionem” 1.29, 2nd c.AD: Apollonius Dyscolus Grammaticus “Synt.” 132.21.]]

__II.2
with genitive, προϋπάρχειν δεῖ τὸ κινοῦν τοῦ κινουμένου must exist before.. , [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “de Motu Animalium” 700b1; π. ἑαυτοῦ 2nd c.AD: Sextus Empiricus Philosophus “adversus Mathematicos” 10.208]]; to be logically prior, μέθοδος πασῶν προϋπάρχουσα καὶ κυριωτέρα [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd c.AD: Nicomachus Gerasenus Mathematicus “Arithmetica Introductio” 1.4.]]

(φήμι), [in LXX: Psa.141:4 (עֲלִילָה), ??עֲלִילָה), ??Dan.6:4-5(5-6) (עִלָּה) Pro.18:1, Hos.10:4 * ;]

πρόφᾰσ-ις, εως, ἡ,
(προφαίνω) motive or cause alleged, whether truly or falsely: then, actual motive or cause, whether alleged or not:

__I
alleged motive, plea, without implication of truth or falsity, ἐπὶ σμικρῇ π. [Refs 6th c.BC+ [6th c.BC: Theognis Elegiacus 323; νόστου π. γλυκεροῦ κώλυεν μεῖναι 5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “P.” 4.32; κατὰ θεωρίης πρόφασιν ἐκπλώσας 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.29; π. ἔχων, ὡς.. [prev. author] 6.133]]; καὶ ἐπὶ μεγάλῃ καὶ ἐπὶ βραχείᾳ π. whether the plea put forward be a trifle or a weighty matter, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 1.141]]; τῆς αἰτίας τὴν π. the plea in the case, the basis of the charge, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Lysias Orator 9.7]]; τοιαύτας ἔχοντες π. καὶ αἰτίας pleas and motives, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 3.13]]; π. ἐπιεικής[Refs 4th c.BC+ [[prev. work] 9; ἀναγκαῖαι 4th c.BC: Isaeus Orator 4.20, 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 54.17]]; προφάσεις ἀληθεῖς λέγοντος pleading what was in fact true, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Andocides Orator 4.17.]]

__I.2
falsely alleged motive (or cause), pretext, pretence, excuse, π. ἰδίης ἀβουλίης an excuse for.., [Refs 5th c.BC+ [3rd c.AD: Democritus Epigrammaticus 119; οὔτε τιν᾽ ἔχων π. οὔτε λόγον εὐτράπελον 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Vespae” 468 (Lyric poetry); καλλίστην εἶναι π., τιμωρεῖσθαι μὲν δοκεῖν, ἔργῳ δὲ χρηματίζεσθαι 5th c.BC: Lysias Orator 12.6: _absolutely_ in _accusative_, πρόφασιν]] in pretence, ostensibly, στενάχοντο γυναῖκες Πάτροκλον π., σφῶν δ᾽ αὐτῶν κήδε᾽ ἑκάστη [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 19.302, compare 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 5.33, 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Iphigenia Aulidensis” 362 (troch.), 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Equites” 466, etc.]]; opposed to τὸ ἀληθές, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 6.33: in _dative_, προφάσει [prev. author] 3.86]]; προφάσει τῶν δημοσίων on the pretence that public debts are owing, [Refs 1st c.AD+ [“OGI” 669.15 (Egypt, 1st c.AD)]]; προφάσιος [εἵνεκεν], προφάσεως ἕνεκα, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 4.135, 5th c.BC: Antipho Orator 6.14; προφάσεως χάριν 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Politica” 1297a14]]; ἐκ μικρᾶς π. [Refs 5th c.BC+ [2nd c.BC: Polybius Historicus 2.17.3; ἐπὶ προφάσιος 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 7.150: followed by an]]infinitive, αὕτη γὰρ ἦν σοι π. ἐκβαλεῖν ἐμέ for casting me out, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Philoctetes” 1034; οὔτε.. ἔστιν οὐδεμία π. τοῦ μὴ δρᾶν 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Timaeus” 20c]]; π. τοῖς δειλοῖς ἔχει μὴ ἰέναι gives them an excuse or plea for not going, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. author] “R.” 469c; οὐδεμία σοι π. ἐστιν ὡς.. 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 2.2.15]]; εὑρὼν π. [Refs 4th c.AD+ [“BGU” 1024 vi 21 (4th c.AD).]]

__I.2.b
phrases, πρόφασιν διδόναι, ἐνδοῦναι, allow, afford an excuse, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 43.53, 18.158; οὐκ ἐνδώσομεν π. οὐδενὶ κακῷ γενέσθαι 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 2.87]]; π. μηδεμίαν θέμενος making no excuse, [Refs 6th c.BC+ [6th c.BC: Theognis Elegiacus 364]]; π. προτεῖναι put forward a pretext, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.156; π. τὴν Παυσανίεω ὕβριν προϊσχόμενοι [prev. author] 8.3; προφάσεις παρέχειν 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Aves” 581, compare 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 10.35, 18.156]]; προφάσιας εἷλκον kept making pretences, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 6.86; πάσας π. ἕλκουσιν 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Lysistrata” 726; π. δέχεσθαι 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Cratylus” 421d (compare ἀγών 111.5); π. εὑρίσκειν τοῦ ἀδικήματος 5th c.BC: Antipho Orator 5.65; π. καλῶς εὑρημένη 5th-6th c.BC: Archippus Comicus 36; ἔχθρας π. ζητήσουσιν 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Phaedrus” 234a, compare “PCair.Zen.” 270.9 (3rd c.BC)]]; π. τινὰ πρεσβείας πορισάμενοι [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Epistulae” 350a; π. κατασκευάσαι 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 2.4.17]]; ἔχει προφάσεις it is excusable,[Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. work] 3.1.27; πρόφασιν ταύτην τῆς διαφορᾶς ποιούμενος 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Epistulae” 349d; προφάσεις εὐλόγους εἰλήφεσαν 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 18.152; ἐχόμενος προφάσιος 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 6.94; ἐπιλαβέσθαι [prev. author] 3.36, 6.49; τὰς π. ἀφελεῖν 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 2.27; προφάσεως δεῖσθαι 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Rhetorica” 1373a3: personified, τὰν Ἐπιμαθέος ὀψινόου θυγατέρα Π. 5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “P.” 5.28.]]

__I.2.c
elliptically, μή μοι πρόφασιν no excuse, no shuffling, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Acharnenses” 345; μὴ προφάσεις ἐνταῦθά μοι 2nd c.AD: Alexander Rhetor 127.1.]]

__II
the actual motive, purpose, or cause, whether alleged or not, οὔτ᾽ εὐνῆς πρόφασιν κεχρημένος οὔτε τευ ἄλλου [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 19.262; ἐπ᾽ αὐτομολίας προφάσει ἀπέρχονται 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 7.13]]; τὸ ἐκ προφάσεως τῶν.. στρατιωτῶν δηληγατευθὲν μέτρον ἐλαίου for the purpose of.., [Refs 4th c.AD+ [“PLips.” 64.2, compare 8 (4th c.AD)]]; τὴν ἀληθεστάτην π., ἀφανεστάτην δὲ λόγῳ [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 1.23, compare 6.6, 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 18.156, “SIG” 888.138 (Scaptopara, 3rd c.AD, _plural_)]]: especially as a medical technical term, external exciting cause, ἐκ πάσης π. ἐκτιτρώσκουσι they miscarry on any provocation, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Hippocrates Medicus “ἀφορισμοί” 3.12, compare “Epid.” 3.3, 3.17.ιά, “Acut.(Sp.”) 6; τοὺς δ᾽ ἄλλους ἀπ᾽ οὐδεμιᾶς π... τῆς κεφαλῆς θέρμαι.. ἐλάμβανε 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 2.49: _plural_, 5th c.BC: Hippocrates Medicus “Aër.” 16, “Fract.” 15, +others]]: generally, cause, σμικρὰ π. ἔξωθεν [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 556e]]; βραχεῖα π. [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Hippocrates Medicus “Κωακαὶ προγνώσιες” 477; ἀπὸ μηδεμιᾶς π. ἔξωθεν ἀξιολόγου Diocl.fragment 82]]; φανερὴ π. [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Hippocrates Medicus “ἀφορισμοί” 2.41, compare 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Historia Graeca (Hellenica)” 6.4.33; ἐπεὶ δέ οἱ ἔδεε κακῶς γενέσθαι, ἐγένετο ἀπὸ προφάσιος τὴν ἐγὼ.. ἀπηγήσομαι 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 2.161, compare 4.145, 7.230; ἄνθρωπός εἰμι, τοῦτο δ᾽ αὐτὸ τῷ βίῳ π. μεγίστην εἰς τὸ λυπεῖσθαι φέρει 4th-3rd c.BC: Diphilus Comicus 106, compare 4th-3rd c.BC: Menander Comicus 230, 811, 4th-3rd c.BC: Philemo Comicus 194]]; βραχείας προφάσεως ἔδει μόνον ἐφ᾽ ᾗ.. δεξόμεθα.. it needed but a little to move us to.., [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Iphigenia Aulidensis” 1180.]]

__II.2
occasion, θοἰμάτιον δεικνὺς τοδὶ πρόφασιν ἔφασκον, ὦ γύναι, λίαν σπαθᾷς I said à propos,.. I took occasion to say.., [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Nubes” 55]]; ἐπὶ τῇ ἐμῇ π. à propos of me, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Lysias Orator 6.19]]; ἐπὶ τῇ π. τῆς ἐμαυτοῦ ἀρχῆς on the occasion of my accession, [Refs 3rd c.AD+ [“PFay.” 20.11 (3rd-4th c.AD).]]

__III
persuasion, suggestion, uncertain reading in [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Trachiniae” 662 (Lyric poetry).]]

__IV
preface, τὰς σημειώσεις ὑπὸ μίαν ἐκθησόμεθα π. [Refs 1st c.AD+ [1st c.AD: Dioscorides (Dioscurides) Medicus “Ther.” 3.]]

LSJ / STEPBible (TFLSJ)
προφέρω,
Epic dialect and Ionic dialect imperfect προφέρεσκον, [Refs 4th c.AD+ [4th c.AD(?): Quintus Smyrnaeus Epicus 4.275, “IG” 14.1747.6 (from Rome):]]future προοίσω: aorist 1 προήνεγκα: aorist 2 προήνεγκον [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 5.17]]: Hom.only present; 3rd.pers. singular present subjunctive προφέρῃσι [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 9.323]]:—bring before or to one, present, ὡς ὄρνις.. νεοσσοῖσι προφέρῃσι μάστακα [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” [same place]; νέκυν Ἀχιλλῆϊ 17.121; μάντεις σφάγια προὔφερον 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 6.69; προενέγκας τὴν ἐπιστολήν “BGU” 1141.11 (1st c.BC),compare “PTeb.” 291.43 (2nd c.AD), etc.]]

__2
of words, σφιν ὀνείδεα π. cast reproaches in their teeth, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 2.251]]; π. τινί throw in one's teeth, bring forward, allege, especially in the way of reproach or objection, μή μοι δῶρ᾽ ἐρατὰ πρόφερε χρυσέης Ἀφροδίτης [Refs 5th c.BC+ [3.64, compare 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.3, 8.61, 125, 5th-6th c.BC: Isocrates Orator 4.100; π. τοὔνομα τοῦθ᾽ ὡς ὄνειδος 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 21.190; δικαιώσεις ἀλλήλοις 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 5.17]]: absolutely, reproach (followed by words quoted), [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 3.120]]:—also in middle, τὴν ἐν Δωδώνῃ ἀσέβειαν [Refs 2nd c.BC+ [2nd c.BC: Polybius Historicus 5.11.2; εἶναι βασιλικὴν γῆν “PTeb.” 81.17 (2nd c.BC),compare “PAmh.” 2.30.7 (2nd c.BC), etc.]]

__3
utter, μῦθον [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Medea” 189 (_anapaest meter_)]]:—middle, ζῷα ἀνθρωπίνας π. φωνάς [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd c.AD: Sextus Empiricus Philosophus “Πυρρώνειοι ὑποτυπώσεις” 1.73, compare 15, 4th c.AD: Julianus Imperator “Orationes” 7.218c.]]

__3.b
π. Αἴγιναν πάτραν proclaim it as their country, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “I.” 5(4).43]]; π. εἰς μέσον or εἰς τὸ μ. publish, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Leges” 812c, 936a:]] —middle, ὁπόσσω κα προφέρηται for whatever sum [the priest] lays down, [Refs [Berl.Sitzb. 1927.169 (from Cyrene).]]

__4
bring forward, cite, μὴ π. τὴν τότε γενομένην ξυνωμοσίαν [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 3.64, compare 5.26 (_passive_), 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Sophista” 259d]]; προφέρων Ἄρτεμιν putting forward her authority, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Agamemnon” 201 (Lyric poetry)]]; π. τὰς ἐπονειδίστους τῶν ἡδονῶν citing by way of example, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Ethica Nicomachea” 1173b21, compare “Pol.” 1288a20]]:—also in middle, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Philebus” 57a, 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Oeconomicus” 14.6]]; ἀναμνήσεως χάριν π. [Refs 2nd c.BC+ [2nd c.BC: Polybius Historicus 4.66.10]]; αὐτοῦ -ομένου τὴν περὶ τὸ σῶμα γεγενημένην ἀσθένειαν pleading.., [Refs 2nd c.BC+ [“OGI” 244.10 (Daphne, 2nd c.BC)]]; cite, [Refs 1st c.AD+ [1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus “Lycurgus” 21]]; recite, ποιήματα [Refs 2nd c.BC+ [1st c.BC: Diodorus Siculus Historicus 14.109, compare 16.92; ἀριθμοὺς τῶν ἀρχαίων ποιητᾶν “SIG” 703.7, compare 660.3 (Delph., 2nd c.BC).]]

__5
of an oracle, propose as a task, τοῖσι Θηραίοισι προέφερε ἡ Πυθίη τὴν ἐς Λιβύην ἀποικίην [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 4.151; ἡ Πυθίη προφέρει σφι, τὰς Ἀθήνας ἐλευθεροῦν [prev. author] 5.63:]] —passive, δόμοισι προὐνεχθέντος ἐν χρηστηρίοις (genitive absolutely) it having been commanded to do so, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Agamemnon” 964.]]

__II
bring forward, display, π. κρατερὸν μένος [LXX+8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 10.479; σπουδήν LXX “Si.Prol.” 22]]; ἔριδα π. show, i.e. engage in, rivalry, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 6.92; ἀντιώσεσθαι πόλεμον προφέρων 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 7.9.γ:]] —middle, ξεινοδόκῳ ἔριδα προφέρεσθαι challenge one's host to rivalry, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 8.210, compare 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 3.7.]]

__II.2
bring out, ἐντεῦθεν ὥσπερ ἐκ ταμιείου π. [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Isocrates Orator 1.44]]; ἤνοιξα τὸν τόπον τῶν οἰναρίων καὶ προενήνεχα (sic) οἴνου κεράμια νά [Refs 4th c.AD+ [“POxy.” 1288.12 (4th c.AD)]]; ἠξίωσαν προενεχθῆναι αὐτὸν ἀπὸ τοῦ δεσμωτηρίου that he should be produced.., [Refs 4th c.AD+ [“BGU” 1024 vii 4 (4th c.AD).]]

__III
carry off, sweep away, of a storm, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 6.346, 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 20.64]]; of death, π. σώματα τέκνων [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Medea” 1111 (_anapaest meter_).]]

__IV
put or move forward, πόδα [Refs [[prev. author] “Tr.” 1332 (Lyric poetry)]]; carry forward, pass on, σκυταλίδα [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aeneas Tacticus 22.27]]: hence, promote, further, ἠώς τοι προφέρει μὲν ὁδοῦ, π. δὲ καὶ ἔργου furthers one on the road and in the work, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th-7th c.BC: Hesiodus Epicus “Opera et Dies” 579: without _genitive_, “Anthologia Graeca” 9.344 (1st c.AD: Leonidas Alexandrinus Epigrammaticus 2nd c.AD: Alexander Rhetor)]]; μέγα π. εἴς τι conduce, help to wards gaining an object, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 1.93]]; μεγάλη τύχη πρὸς πάντα π. [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd-3rd c.AD: Dio Cassius Historicus 78.38]]:—passive, move forward, προενεχθέντος τοῦ σώματος [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “de Incessu Animalium” 711a29.]]

__IV.2
intransitive, surpass, excel another, δόξας ἔργα πολὺ προφέρει [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Simonides Lyricus 161, compare 3rd c.BC: Theocritus Poeta Bucolicus 12.5:]] with dative _of things_, εἴρια καλλονῇ τε προφέροντα καὶ ἀρετῇ τῶν ἀπὸ τῶν ὀΐων (tree) wool surpassing sheep's wool in beauty and goodness, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 3.106; πλούτῳ καὶ εἴδεϊ προφέρων Ἀθηναίων [prev. author] 6.127]]; ἡ Νάξος εὐδαιμονίῃ τῶν νήσων π. one who acts as an interpreter or forth-teller of the Divine will (see Lft., Notes, 83f.; Tr., Syn., §vi), a prophet;

__(b) of prophets in general: Mat.10:41 13:57 21:46, Mrk.6:4, Luk.13:33, al.;

__(d) of Christ: Mat.21:11, Jhn.6:14, Act.3:22, 23 7:37" (LXX) ;
__(e) of Christian prophets in the apostolic age: Act.15:32, 1Co.12:28, Eph.2:20, al.;
__(f) by meton., of the writings of prophets: Luk.24:27, Act.8:28, al.;
__(g) of a poet: Tit.1:12 (on the use of the term in π. and Inscr., see Deiss., BS, 235f.; MM, xxii).

of a repeated action, frequent, numerous, πυκνοὺς θεοπρόπους ἴαλλε [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Prometheus Vinctus” 658; τῶν π. φιλημάτων [prev. author] “fragment” 135; ὀδύναι πυκνόταται 5th c.BC: Hippocrates Medicus “περὶ ἀρχαίης ἰητρικῇς” 22; πυκινῶν κρεγμῶν ἀκροαζομένα 5th c.BC: Epicharmus Comicus 109 (_anapaest meter_); π. ὁδοὺς ἐλθόντα 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Troades” 235]]; π. βαίνων ἤλυσιν, of a blind man, [Refs [[prev. author] “Ph.” 844]]; ἐν πυκνῷ θεοῦ τροχῷ κυκλεῖται on the oft-revolving wheel, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Fragmenta” 871.1; μεταβολαὶ πυκνόταται 5th c.BC: Hippocrates Medicus “Aër.” 13; πνεῦμα πυκνότερον]] quicker breathing, [Refs 1st c.AD+ [[prev. author] “Acut.” 16; π. σφυγμὸς ἢ μανός 1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus 2.136f]]; continuous, constant, φῶς [Refs 5th c.BC+ [“Corpus Hermeticum” 16.10; ἐρωτήμασι πυκνοῖς χρώμενοι 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 7.44; ἡ.. εἰωθυῖά μοι μαντικὴ.. πάνυ πυκνὴ ἦν 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Apologia” 40a; ἐπιθυμίαι π. τε καὶ σφοδραί [prev. author] “R.” 573e; τὰς ἐντεύξεις π. ποιεῖσθαι 5th-6th c.BC: Isocrates Orator 1.20: with]]infinitive, πυκνοτέραν εἰσαφικνεῖσθαι πᾶσιν ἀνθρώποις ποιεῖν τὴν πόλιν more frequently visited by.., [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “de Vectigalibus” 5.1 codices]]

__III
of artificial union, well put together, compact, strong, πυκινὸς δόμος, χηλός, θύραι, θάλαμος, κευθμῶνες (see. below [Refs 8th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Bacchylides Lyricus 111.1), 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 10.267, 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 13.68, 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 14.167, 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 23.229, 10.283; ἀσπὶς ῥινοῖσιν πυκινή 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 13.804; π. δῶμα 6th c.BC: Xenophanes Poeta Philosophus 17]]: hence, close, concealed, πυκινὸς δόλος [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 6.187; and so perhaps π. λόχος, see above 11.1.]]

__III.2
in Music, πυκνόν, τό, part of the tetrachord in which the intervals are small, defined as τὸ ἐκ δύο διαστημάτων συνεστηκὸς ἃ συντεθέντα ἔλαττον διάστημα περιέξει τοῦ λειπομένου διαστήματος ἐν τῷ διὰ τεσσάρων [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aristoxenus Musicus “Harmonica” p.24M., compare 1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus 2.1135b, etc.]]

__IV
generally, strong of its kind, sore, excessive, ἄτη [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 24.480; μελεδῶναι 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 19.516; ἄχος 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 16.599.]]

__V
metaphorically of the mind, shrewd, wise, πυκιναὶ φρένες [Refs 8th c.BC+ [14.294, compare 7th-6th c.BC: Alcaeus Lyricus “Supp.” 14.9, 5th c.BC: Bacchylides Lyricus [same place]; νόος 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 15.461; μήδεα 3.208; βουλή 2.55; ἐφετμή 18.216; μῦθοι 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 3.23; ἔπος 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 11.788]]; θυμός, βουλαί, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “P.” 4.73, “I.” 7(6).8; φρήν 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Iphigenia Aulidensis” 67]]; μήτιδι πυκνῇ Oracle texts cited in [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 7.141, compare “IG” 3.1320: in Prose, πυκνὴ διάνοια 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 568a]]; τὸ π. terseness of expression, [Refs 1st c.BC+ [1st c.BC: Dionysius Halicarnassensis “de Thucydide” 24.]]

__V.2
of persons, sagacious, shrewd, crafty, cunning, Σίσυφος πυκνότατος παλάμαις [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “O.” 13.52; κύων πυκινώτατον ἑρπετόν [prev. author] “fragment” 106]]; πυκινοί the wise, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Philoctetes” 854 (Lyric poetry); πυκνότατον κίναδος 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Aves” 430 (Lyric poetry); πυκνός τις καὶ σοφὸς γνώμην ἀνήρ 5th c.BC: Critias Philosophus, Tragicus, Elegiacus 25.12.]]

__B
adverb πυκινῶς, and after [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Homerus Epicus πυκνῶς, θύραι or σανίδες πυκινῶς ἀραρυῖαι]] close or fast shut, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 9.475, 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 2.344, etc.]]

__B.II.2
πυκινὰ φρονεῖν (see. supr. A.V) [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 9.445.]]

__B.III
poetry adverb πύκα [??], thickly, solidly, θαλάμου πύκα ποιητοῖο [Refs 8th c.BC+ [1.436; π. π. δόμοιο 22.455; σάκεος π. π. 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 18. 608; Λυκίων π. θωρηκτάων 12.317, compare 15.689, 739]]; πύλαι π. στιβαρῶς ἀραρυῖαι [Refs [12.454.]]

__B.III.2
θάλαμος πύκ᾽ ἐβάλλετο with thick-falling darts, [Refs [9.588.]]

wisely, π. φρονεῖν [Refs 4th c.AD+ [[prev. work] 554, 14.217, 4th c.AD(?): Quintus Smyrnaeus Epicus 1.449, +others]]; τρέφειν rear carefully, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 5.70.]]

π. τί τινος learn something from a person, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 17.408, 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 10.537, 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Agamemnon” 599, 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Ranae” 1417, etc.; also π. τι ἀπό τινος 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Choephori” 737; ἐξ ἄλλων 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Coloneus” 1266; ἐκ τοῦ παρατυχόντος 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 1.22]]; frequently παρά τινος, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 2.91, etc.]]; παρ᾽ ἄλλων (variant{ἄλλων}) [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 4.1.3.]]

__2
with accusative of things only, hear or learn a thing, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 2.411, 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Choephori” 765, 5th c.BC: Antipho Orator 5.25, etc.: _absolutely_, αἰσχρὸν τόδε γ᾽ ἐστὶ καὶ ἐσσομένοισι πυθέσθαι 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 2.119, compare 5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “P.” 7.7, etc.; ὡς ἐγὼ πυνθάνομαι 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.22, etc.]]

__3
with genitive objecti, hear or inquire concerning, πυθέσθαι πατρός, ἀγγελιάων, μάχης, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 1.281, 2.256, 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 15.224, compare 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Electra” 35, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Leges” 635b.]]

__4
π. τινά τινος inquire about one person of or from another, τὸν ἄνδρα τῶν ὁδοιπόρων [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Acharnenses” 204; so π. περί τινος 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 2.75; πᾶσαν πυθέσθαι τῶνδ᾽ ἀλήθειαν πέρι 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Trachiniae” 91]]: with accusative person only, inquire about a person, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Thesmophoriazusae” 619.]]

__5
with participle, πυθόμην ὁδὸν ὁρμαίνοντα that he was starting, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 4.732, compare 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 9.58, 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Ajax” 692; π. τὸ Πλημμύριον ἑαλωκός 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 7.31, compare 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 1.7.16, etc.]]; οὔ πω.. πεπύσθην Πατρόκλοιο θανόντος they had not yet heard of his being dead, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 17.377, compare 427, 19.322, 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Choephori” 763; ὡς ἐπύθοντο τῆς Πύλου κατειλημμένης 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 4.6: with _accusative_ _of things_ added, εἰ σφῶϊν τάδε πάντα πυθοίατο μαρναμένοιιν 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 1.257.]]

__6
with accusative et infinitive, hear or learn that.. , [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.62, 5.15, 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Trachiniae” 103 (Lyric poetry), 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 7.25, etc.]]

__7
followed by an interrogative clause, ὡς πυθώμεθα ὅπου ποτ᾽ ἐσμέν [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Coloneus” 11]]; αὐτοῦ π. τί ποτε νοεῖ inquire or learn from him what.., [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Laches” 196c, compare 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 6.3.25, 2nd c.BC: Polybius Historicus 3.107.6; π., ὅτεῳ.. συνοικέει 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 3.68]]; π. εἰ.. inquire whether.., [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Coloneus” 993, “IG” 42(1).121.18 (Epid., 4th c.BC)]]; τοῦ ξένου ἡδέως ἂν π., τί ταῦθ᾽ ἡγοῦντο [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Sophista” 216d]]; π. τινῶν, ὅτι.. [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 4.6.17]]; π., ὅπως ἂν κάλλιστα πορευθείη[Refs [[prev. work] 3.1.7, compare “Cyr.” 1.4.7.]]

active, aorist 1 participle feminine πεύσασα having learned, [Refs 6th c.AD+ [PMasp. 5.7 (6th c.AD).]]

[Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Timaeus” 22b, compare “Tht.” 146d, 208e, etc.]]

__3
with genitive modi, π. ἀγῶνος ἥκομε; how are we come off in it? [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Electra” 751; π. ἔχει πλήθους ἐπισκοπεῖ 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Gorgias” 451c.]]

__4
with Verbs of selling, how? at what price? π. ὁ σῖτος ὤνιο; [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Acharnenses” 758, compare “Eq.” 480]]; τὰ δ᾽ ἄλφιθ᾽ ὑμῖν π. ἐπώλου;—Answ. τεττάρων δραχμῶν.. τὸν κόφινον [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Strattis Comicus 13.]]

__II
with other Particles, π. ἂν..; π. κε (ν)..; how possibly..? π. ἂν ἔπειτ᾽ ἀπὸ σεῖο.. λιποίμην οἶο; [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 9.437, compare 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 1.65, etc.]]; π. ἂν γένοιτ᾽ ἂν.. ποδῶν ἔκμακτρο; [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Electra” 534]]: so with indicative, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 22.202, 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Alcestis” 96 (Lyric poetry), etc.]]

__II.b
in Trag., π. ἄν with optative is frequently used to express a wish, O how might it be? i.e. would that it might..! π. ἂν θάνοιμ; π. ἂν ὀλοίμη; etc., [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Ajax” 388 (Lyric poetry), 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Supplices” 796 (Lyric poetry), compare “Hipp.” 208 (_anapaest meter_), 345]]; rare in Comedy texts, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Thesmophoriazusae” 22]] (a trace of this usage appears in [LXX+8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Homerus Epicus, 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 15.195): in later Prose, π. ἂν γένοιτο ἑσπέρ; LXX.Deu.28.67]]; also with aorist subjunctive (without ἄν), π. κοιμηθ; [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd c.AD: Marcus Antoninus Imperator 9.40]]; π. μή μοι μέγας λέων ἐπιφαν; [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd c.AD: Arrianus Historicus “Epicteti Dissertationes” 4.10.10]]; with present, π. μὴ χρῄζ; M.Ant. [prev. cited]

__II.2
π. ἄρα..; in reply, how then? π. τ᾽ ἄρ᾽ ἴω..; [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 18.188, compare 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 3.22, “hymnus ad Apollinem” 19, 207.]]

__II.3
π. γὰρ..; also in reply, as if something had gone before, [that cannot be], for how can..? [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 1.123, 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 10.337, etc.]]; π. γὰρ κάτοιδ; [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Philoctetes” 250, compare 1383; see below 111.1.]]

__II.4
π. δὲ..; to introduce a strong objection, π. δὲ σὺ νῦν μέμονας, κύον ἀδδεές..; [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 21.481, compare 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 18.31]]; δόξει δὲ π.; [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Prometheus Vinctus” 261.]]

__II.5
π. δ; how in the world? π. δὴ φῂς πολέμοιο μεθιέμε; [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 4.351, compare 18.364, 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Agamemnon” 543, etc.]]; also π. γὰρ δή..; [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 16.70]]; π. δῆτα..; [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Agamemnon” 622, 1211, 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Nubes” 79, etc.]]

__II.6
π. καὶ..; just how..? [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Hecuba” 515, “Ph.” 1354, etc.]]; π. δὲ καὶ..; [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Persae” 721, see at {καί} 5th c.BC: Bacchylides Lyricus 6]]; but καὶ π...; to introduce an objection, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Phoenissae” 1348, see at {καί} 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus 11.2: hence καὶ π.]]; alone, but how? impossible! [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus Alcaeus1.134c, “Tht.” 163d, etc.]]

__II.7
π. οὐ..; how not so..? i.e. surely it is so.. , π. οὐ δεινὰ εἴργασθ; [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 3.66, compare 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Nubes” 398, 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 18.273.]]

__II.8
π. οὖν..; like{π. ἄρα.}.; [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Supplices” 297, 340, 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Tyrannus” 568, etc.]]; π. ἂν οὖν.. with optative, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Persae” 243, 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Iphigenia Taurica” 98.]]

__II.9
π. ποτε..; how ever..? [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Tyrannus” 1210 (Lyric poetry), “Ph.” 687 (Lyric poetry).]]

__III
πῶς followed by several of the abovenamed Particles is frequently used in elliptical sentences, as,

__III.1
π. γά; inserted parenthesis in a negative sentence, for how is it possible? how can or could it be? hence in emphatic denial, κἀγὼ μὲν οὐκ ἔδρασα, τοῦτ᾽ ἐπίσταμαι, οὐδ᾽ αὖ σύ· π. γά; [Refs [[prev. author] “El.” 911]]; οὐκ ἀπορῶν (π. γά;), ὅς γε.. [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 18.312, compare 21.217, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Sophista” 263c, etc.]]; οὐδ᾽ ἐπὶ τὴν ἑστίαν καταφυγών (π. γὰρ ἄ;), ὅστις.. [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Lysias Orator 1.27]]; π. γὰρ ο; how can it but be? i.e. it must be so, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Choephori” 754, 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Electra” 1307, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Theaetetus” 160c, +others]]; π. γά; (i.e. ἄλλως ἔχει) is so used in [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Ajax” 279.]]

__III.2
π. δ; how so? [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Eumenides” 601, 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Nubes” 664, 673, etc.]]; π. δῆτ; [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Gorgias” 469b]]; π. δα; [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Vespae” 1212.]]

__III.3
π. δ᾽ ο; like{π. γὰρ οὔ}; (see.[Refs 5th c.BC+ [above 1), 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Theaetetus” 153b, “R.” 457a]]; π. δ᾽ οὐχ; [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Tyrannus” 1015, 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Pax” 1027; parenthetically, 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “OT” 567]]; π. δ᾽ οὐκ ἄν..; [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Prometheus Vinctus” 759.]]

__III.4
π. οὖ; how then? how next? [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Medea” 1376, “Hipp.” 598, 1261, 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 19.124]]; π. οὖν ἄν..; [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Memorabilia” 1.2.64.]]

__III.5
π. δοκεῖ; parenthesis, in conversation, how think you? hence (losing all interrogative force),= λίαν, wonderfully, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Plutus” 742, “Nu.” 881, “Ach.” 24; also π. οἴει σφόδρα [prev. author] “Ra.” 54; compare δοκέω 1.2.]]

__IV
π. in indirect questions for ὅπως, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Eumenides” 677, 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Trachiniae” 991 (_anapaest meter_), 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Equites” 614, 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Memorabilia” 1.2.36, etc.; ἐθαύμαζον ἂν π... ἔδεισαν “IG” 12(3).174.28 (Cnidus, Epist.Aug.); ζητηθήσεται π. ὅτι καὶ τοῦτο ἀληθές ἐστι 2nd c.AD: Sextus Empiricus Philosophus “adversus Mathematicos” 8.16.]]

__V
in exclamations, ὦ π. πονηρόν ἐστιν ἀνθρώπου φύσις τὸ σύνολον [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-3rd c.BC: Philemo Comicus 2]]; π. παραχρῆμα ἐξηράνθη.. ! [NT.Matt.21.20]; π. δυσκόλως.. ! [NT.Mark.10.23.]

LSJ / STEPBible (TFLSJ)
ῥάβδος, ἡ,
rod, wand, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Homerus Epicus (see. below), etc.]]; lighter than the βακτηρία or walking-stick, [NT+5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “de Equitandi ratione” 11.4 (but ={βακτηρία}, NT.Matt.10.10, +others). —Special uses:]]

__1
magic wand, as that of Circe, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 10.238, 319, etc.]]; that with which Athena touched Odysseus, to restore his youthful appearance, χρυσείῃ ῥάβδῳ ἐπεμάσσατο [Refs [16.172]]; that with which Hermes overpowers the senses of man, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 24.343]]; that with which Hades rules the ghosts, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “O.” 9.33]]; divining-rod, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 4.67.]]

__2
fishing-rod, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 12.251.]]

__3
limed twig, for catching small birds, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Aves” 527.]]

__4
shaft of a hunting-spear, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Cynegeticus” 10.3, 16.]]

__5
staff of office, like the earlier σκῆπτρον, [LXX+5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Axiochus” 367a, LXX.Psa.44(45).7, 109(110).2]]; carried by a βραβευτής, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [1st c.BC: Philodemus Philosophus “περὶ κακιῶν ί” p.25J.:— uncertain in 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Supplices” 248 for ῥαβδοῦχος.]]

__6
wand borne by the ῥαψῳδός, τὸν ἐπὶ ῥάβδῳ μῦθον ὑφαινόμενον [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [3rd c.BC: Callimachus Epicus “Fragmenta” 138 (= “fragment” 3.10P.), compare 2nd c.AD: Pausanias Periegeta 9.30.3: hence κατὰ ῥάβδον ἐπέων]] according to the measure of his (Homer's) verses, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “I.” 4(3).38(56).]]

__7
rod for chastisement, ῥ. κοσμοῦσα [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Leges” 700c]]; μάστιξ ἢ ῥ. riding-switch, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “de Equitandi ratione” 8.4]]; ῥ. βοηλάτις ox-goad, [Refs 2nd c.BC+ [Anthologia Graeca Appx. 4.200 (2nd c.BC: Moschus Bucolicus); ξαίνεσθαι ῥάβδοις 1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus “Alexander” 51, compare “Anthologia Graeca” 11.153 (1st c.AD: Lucillius Epigrammaticus)]]: of the fasces of the Roman lictors, [Refs 2nd c.BC+ [2nd c.BC: Polybius Historicus 11.29.6, 1st c.BC: Dionysius Halicarnassensis 4.11, 1st c.BC-1st c.AD: Strabo Geographus 5.2.2, 1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus “Publicola” 10, “Luc.” 36]]; πρὸς πέντε ῥάβδους, = Latin at (i.e. ad) quinque fasces (CIL[Refs 2nd c.AD+ [8.7044 (from Numidia)), “OGI” 543.18 (Ancyra, 2nd c.AD), “IGRom.” 3.175 ([prev. passage], 2nd c.AD)]]; compare ῥαβδονόμος, ῥαβδοῦχος.

__8
shepherd's staff or crook, [LXX.Psa.22(23).4, LXX.Mic.7.14.]

__9
ῥ. κληρονομίας measuring-rod,[LXX.Psa.73(74).2.]

__10
stitch, ἔντοσθεν δὲ βοείας ῥάψε θαμειὰς χρυσείῃς ῥάβδοισι διηνεκέσιν περὶ κύκλον [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 12.297]] (unless it means rivets, studs).

__II
young shoot of some trees,[Refs 4th c.BC+ [Ion Trag. 40, 4th-3rd c.BC: Theophrastus Philosophus “Historia Plantarum” 2.1.2.]]

__III
streak or stripe on the skin of animals, διαποίκιλα ῥάβδοις [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Historia Animalium” 525a12]]; of fish, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-3rd c.BC: Clearchus Historicus 73]]; of clothes, [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd c.AD(?): Pollianus Epigrammaticus 7.53]]; fluting of a column, [Refs 2nd c.BC+ [“Supp.epigram” 4.448.7 (Didyma, 2nd c.BC, _plural_)]]; of minerals, vein, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-3rd c.BC: Theophrastus Philosophus “de Causis Plantarum” 4.12.6, 1st c.BC: Diodorus Siculus Historicus 5.37]]; streak or shaft of light, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Meteorologica” 377a30, “Mu.” 395a31, 4th-3rd c.BC: Theophrastus Philosophus “de Signis Tempestatum” 11.]]

__IV
in Grammars,

__IV.1
line, verse, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [Scholia 5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “I.” 4.63.]]

__IV.2
a critical mark, like{ὀβελός}, [Refs 5th c.AD+ [5th c.AD(?): Hesychius Legal icographus]]

__IV.3
stroke forming a letter, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Theodectes Tragicus 6.6.]]

[Refs 1st c.AD+ [1st c.AD(?): Pseudo-Phocylidea 193; πρὸς τὸν Ἀλκιβιάδην ὁ δῆμος ὅλος ἐρρύη 1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus “Alcibiades” 21.]]

__c
of a river, also ῥ. ἀπὸ τηκομένης χιόνος derive its stream from melted snow, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 2.22.]]

__d
proverbial, ἄνω ῥεῖν flow upwards, of inversion of the usual or right order, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Supplices” 520; ἄνω ποταμῶν ἐρρύησαν οἱ.. λόγοι 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 19.287]]; compare ἄνω (B)1.

__e
ταῦτα μὲν ῥείτω κατ᾽ οὖρον (see. οὖρος (A))[Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Trachiniae” 468.]]

__2
metaphorically of things, ἐκ χειρῶν βέλεα ῥέον from their hands rained darts, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 12.159; ῥεῖ μάλιστα ὁ ἀὴρ ῥέων ἐν τοῖς ὑψηλοῖς 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Meteorologica” 347a34, compare 349a34; φλὸξ ῥυεῖσα 1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus “Brutus” 31; so τὴν Αἴτνην ῥυῆναι 2nd-3rd c.AD: Aelianus “Fragmenta” 2]]; especially of a flow of words, ἀπὸ γλώσσης μέλιτος γλυκίων ῥέεν αὐδή [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 1.249, compare 8th-7th c.BC: Hesiodus Epicus “Theogonia” 39.97; ἔπε᾽ ἐκ στόματος ῥεῖ μείλιχα [prev. work] 84]]: absolutely, of the tongue, run glibly, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Septem contra Thebas” 557; so θρασυνομένῳ καὶ πολλῷ ῥέοντι καθ᾽ ὑμῶν 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 18.136]]: hence, of words or sentiments, to be current, κληδόνος καλῆς μάτην ῥεούσης [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Coloneus” 259.]]

__3
fall, drop off, e.g. of hair, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 10.393, 8th-7th c.BC: Hesiodus Epicus “Fragmenta” 29, 3rd c.BC: Theocritus Poeta Bucolicus 2.89, etc.]]; of ripe fruit, [Refs 2nd c.BC+ [2nd c.BC: Polybius Historicus 12.4.14, “Geoponica” 9.12]]; of over-ripe corn, ἤδη ῥέοντα τὸν στάχυν [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd c.AD: Babrius Fabularum Scriptor 88.14]]; wear out, εἰ ῥέοι τὸ σῶμα καὶ ἀπολλύοιτο [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Phaedo” 87d]]; of a house, to be in a tumble-down condition, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Gorgias Rhetor et Sophista cited in 5th c.AD: Stobaeus, Joannes 4.51.28, 3rd c.BC: Teles Philosophus p.27 H.]]; ῥέουσαν σύγκρισιν στῆσαι to stay a collapse of the system, [Refs 1st c.AD+ [1st c.AD: Herodotus Medicus cited in 4th c.AD: Oribasius Medicus 5.27.1.]]

__4
of molten objects, liquefy, run, ῥεῖ πᾶν ἄδηλον [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Trachiniae” 698; τήκεται ὁ λίθος.. ὥστε καὶ ῥεῖν 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Meteorologica” 383b6, compare 4th-3rd c.BC: Theophrastus Philosophus “de Lapidibus” 9.]]

__5
to be in perpetual flux and change, ἅπανθ᾽ ὁρῶ ἅμα τῇ τύχῃ ῥέοντα μεταπίπτοντά τε [Refs 5th c.BC+ [“Comica Adespota” 200; ὡς ἰόντων ἁπάντων ἀεὶ καὶ ῥεόντων 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Cratylus” 439c, compare 411c; κινεῖται καὶ ῥεῖ.. τὰ πάντα [prev. author] “Tht.” 182c: hence οἱ ῥέοντες, of the Heraclitean philosophers, opposed to οἱ τοῦ ὅλου στασιῶται, [prev. work] 181a.]]

__5.b
'run', of ink, etc., metaphorically, στιγμῆς ῥυείσης γραμμὴν φαντασιούμεθα.., γραμμῆς δὲ ῥυείσης πλάτος ἐποιήσαμεν [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd c.AD: Sextus Empiricus Philosophus “adversus Mathematicos” 7.99; compare ῥυίσκομαι 11.]]

__6
of persons, ῥ. ἐπί τι to be inclined, given to a thing, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Isocrates Orator 8.5; πρός τι 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 485d; οἱ ταύτῃ ῥυέντες [prev. work] 495b.]]

__7
leak, of a ship, opposed to στεγανὸν εἶναι, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Fragmenta” 554, compare 2nd c.AD: Pausanias Periegeta 8.50.7]]; λύχνοι ῥέοντες [Refs 2nd c.BC+ [probably in Roussel “Cultes Egyptiens” p.222 (Delos, 2nd c.BC)]]; of a roof, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-3rd c.BC: Menander Comicus “Σαμία” 248; [ἀγγεῖον] ῥέον 1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus 2.782e; οἰνοχόαι ῥέουσαι “Michel” 815.131 (Delos, 4th c.BC).]]

__8
to have a flux, τὰς κοιλίας τὰς ῥεούσας [Refs 1st c.BC+ [1st c.BC: Diodorus Siculus Historicus 5.41.]]

__9
impersonal, ἐκ ῥινῶν ἐρρύη [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Hippocrates Medicus “ἐπιδημίαι” 1.19.]]

__II
very rarely transitive, let flow, pour, ἔρρει χοάς [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Hecuba” 528 (as variant for{αἴρει}):]] —this differs from the usage

__II.2
with accusative cognate, ῥείτω γάλα, μέλι, let the land run milk, honey, [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [3rd c.BC: Theocritus Poeta Bucolicus 5.124, 126]]; αἷμα ῥυήσεται, of the Nile, [LXX+5th c.BC+ [2nd c.BC: Ezekiel Poeta Judaeus “Exagoge - Mnemosyne” 133; οἶνον ῥέων 2nd c.AD: Lucianus Sophista “VH” 1.7, cf. LXX.Joel.3(4).18, Scholia 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Plutus” 287:—in place of this _accusative_ the best writers commonly used the _dative_, see above 1.1.]]

__III
see at {ῥέον}. (Cf. ῥόϝος, Sanskrit sravati, Lithuanian sravēti 'flow': I.-[Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus]] srèw- alternating with sr[ocaron]w- and sr[ucaron]-.)

deep_entry:
Abbott-Smith / STEPBible (TBESG)
λέγω,
[in LXX very freq., chiefly for אמר; λέγει for נְאֻם, Gen.22:16, al. ;]
__1. in Hom., to pick out, gather, reckon, recount.
__2. In Hdt. and Att., to say, speak, affirm, declare: absol., Act.13:15, 24:10; before orat. dir., Mat.9:34, Mrk.3:11, Jhn.1:29, al.; before ὅτι recit., Mrk.3:21, Luk.1:24, Jhn.6:14, al.; accusative and inf., Luk.11:18, Jhn.12:29, al.; after another verb of speaking, προσφωνεῖν κ. λέγειν, Mat.11:17, al.; ἀπεκρίθη (ἐλάλησεν) λέγων (καὶ λέγει; Dalman, Words, 24 ff.), Mat.25:9, Mrk.3:33, 7:28, Luk.24:6, 7, al.; of unspoken thought, λ. ἐν ἑαυτῷ, Mat.3:9, Luk.3:8, al.; of writing, 2Co.8:8, Php.4:11, al.; λέγει ἡ γραφή, Rom.4:3, Jas.2:23, al.; with accusative of thing(s), Luk.8:8, 9:33, Jhn.5:34, al.; σὺ λέγεις (a non-committal phrase; Swete, Mk., 359, 369f.), Mat.27:11, Mrk.15:2, Luk.23:3, Jhn.18:37; with dative of person(s), before orat. dir., Mat.8:20, Mrk.2:17, al. mult.; id. before ὅτι, Mat.3:9, al.; with prep., πρός, μετά, περί, etc., Mrk.4:41, Jhn.11:56, Heb.9:5, al.; to mean (cl.), Mrk.14:71, Jhn.6:71, 1Co.10:29, al.; to call, name, Mrk.10:18; pass., Mat.9:9, Mrk.15:7, al (cf. ἀντι-, δια- (-μαι), προ-, συλ-λέγω).
SYN.: λαλέω, which refers to the utterance, as λέγω to the meaning of what is said, its correspondence with thought (Tr., Syn., Ixxvi; Thayer, see word λαλέω). (AS)

(ῥήγνυμι), [in LXX: 3Ki.11:30-31 12:24, 4Ki.2:12 (קֶרַע), Amo.6:12 (11) A (בְּקִיעַ) * ;]

LSJ / STEPBible (TFLSJ)
ῥῆγ-μα, ατος, τό,
(ῥήγνυμι) breakage, fracture, joined with σπάσμα, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Hippocrates Medicus “Aër.” 4,compare 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 18.198, 1st c.AD: Dioscorides (Dioscurides) Medicus 3.74]]; with στρέμμα (a strain), [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 2.21, 11.14.]]

__2
laceration, rupture, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [2nd c.AD: Galenus Medicus 10.160, 18(2).882, compare 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Historia Animalium” 635a4.]]

__3
rent, tear, in clothes, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Archippus Comicus 38.]]

__4
cleft, chasm, ῥ. τῆς γῆς [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Historia Animalium” 628b29]]; chink, ἐν τοίχοις [Refs 2nd c.BC+ [2nd c.BC: Polybius Historicus 13.6.8]]; breach in a dyke, [Refs 1st c.AD+ [“PLond.” 1.131r. 45, 60 (1st c.AD).]]

__II
lesion or rupture of tissue, ὅταν ὑπὸ βίης διαστέωσιν αἱ σάρκες ἀπ᾽ ἀλλήλων [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Hippocrates Medicus “περὶ φυσῶν” 11, compare 2nd c.AD: Galenus Medicus 1.238, 10.232; especially oflung, 5th c.BC: Hippocrates Medicus “περὶ τόπων τῶν κατὰ ἄνθρωπον” 14, “Morb.” 1.20]]:hence ῥηγμᾰτίας, ου, ὁ, one who has such a rupture, [Refs 1st c.AD+ [[prev. author] “Aër.” 4, 1st c.AD: Dioscorides (Dioscurides) Medicus 3.146, 4.10; τοὺς ἐκ βηχὸς ῥηγματίας “Hippiatrica” 22]]; but ῥηγματίας πλεύμονος perhaps = pleurisy, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Hippocrates Medicus “περὶ νούσων” 2.53]]; ῥηγμᾰτώδης, ες, [Refs [[prev. author] “Epid.” 7.26.]]

deep_entry:
Abbott-Smith / STEPBible (TBESG)
ῥήγνυμι and (Mrk.9:18) ῥήσσω,
[in LXX chiefly for בָּקַע, also for קָרַע, etc. ;]
__1. to rend, break asunder: Mat.7:6, Mrk.2:22, Luk.5:37; pass., Mat.9:17.
__2. Of the voice, with accusative, φωνήν, etc. (Hdt., al.), to break forth into speech: absol., Gal.4:27 (LXX).
__3. = ῥήσσω (Dem., al.), to throw or dash down: Mrk.9:18, Luk.9:42
(cf. δια-, περι-, προσ-ρήγνυμι).†

Abbott-Smith / STEPBible (TBESG)
ῥιπή, ῆς, ἡ
(ῥίπτω),
poët. in cl., any rapid movement such as the throw or flight of a javelin, the rush of wind or flame, the flapping of wings, the twinkling of lights; ῥ. ὀφθαλμοῦ, the twinkling of an eye: 1Co.15:52 (L, mg., ῥοπή, which see).†
(AS)

---

LSJ / STEPBible (TFLSJ)
ῥῑπ-ή, ἡ,
(ῥίπτω) poet. Noun, swing or force with which anything is thrown, ὅσση δ᾽ αἰγανέης ῥιπὴ.. τέτυκται as far as is the flight of a javelin, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 16.589; λᾶος ὑπὸ ῥιπῆς 12.462, 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 8.192]]; πέτριναι ῥ. [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Helena” 1123 (Lyric poetry)]]; βελέων ῥ. [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “N.” 1.68]]; ὑπὸ ῥιπῆς.. Βορέαο the sweep or rush of the N. wind, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 15.171, 19.358, compare 5th c.BC: Bacchylides Lyricus 5.46; κυμάτων ῥιπαὶ ἀνέμων τε 5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “P.” 4.195, compare “Parth.” 2.20, “fragment” 88.2; ῥ. ἀνέμων [prev. author] “P.” 9.48, 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Antigone” 137]] (Lyric poetry, here metaphorically of gusts of passion, compare [Refs [930)]]; ῥ. Διόθεν τεύχουσα φόβον storm, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Prometheus Vinctus” 1089 (_anapaest meter_), compare 3rd c.BC: Apollonius Rhodius Epicus 1.1016]]; ῥ. πυρός rush of fire, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 21.12; ἀνδρός 8.355; ἀθανάτων 8th-7th c.BC: Hesiodus Epicus “Theogonia” 681, 849]]; κεραυνῶν, χαλάζης, [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd-3rd c.AD: Oppianus Anazarbensis Epicus “Halieutica - Poetae Bucolici et Didactici” 3.21, 4th c.AD(?): Quintus Smyrnaeus Epicus 14.77]]; ὑπὸ ῥιπῇς Ἀφροδίτης, of love, [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd-3rd c.AD: Oppianus Anazarbensis Epicus “Halieutica - Poetae Bucolici et Didactici” 4.141]]; νυχιᾶν (ἐννυχιᾶν Lachm.) ἀπὸ ῥιπᾶν from the night storms, i.e. from the “North”, the land of darkness and storms, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Coloneus” 1248 (Lyric poetry, but Scholia understands Ῥιπᾶν, see at {Ῥῖπαι}).]]

__2
πτερύγων ῥιπαί flapping of wings, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Prometheus Vinctus” 126 (_anapaest meter_), compare 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Fragmenta” 594.4]]; buzz of a gnat's wing, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Agamemnon” 893]]; of the lyre's quivering notes, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “P.” 1.10.]]

__3
quivering, twinkling light, ῥιπαὶ ἄστρων [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Electra” 106 (_anapaest meter_).]]

__3.b
of any rapid movement, ῥ. ποδῶν [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Iphigenia Taurica” 885 (Lyric poetry)]]; ῥ. ὠκυάλῳ, of a dolphin, [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd-3rd c.AD: Oppianus Anazarbensis Epicus “Halieutica - Poetae Bucolici et Didactici” 2.535]]; of a bird's wing, οὐδὲ τινάσσει ῥιπήν [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [3rd c.BC: Apollonius Rhodius Epicus 2.935]]; ἐν ῥ. ὀφθαλμοῦ the twinkling of an eye, [NT.1Cor.]

__4
a strong smell, ῥ. οἴνου [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “Fragmenta.” 166.]]

ῥιπίζω
(ῥιπίς, a fan) [in LXX: Dan LXX 2:35 (נְשָׂא) * ;]
primarily, to fan a fire, hence generally, to make a breeze (Plut., al.). In pass. (cf. Philo, de inter. round., 24), to be tossed or blown by the wind: of waves, ἀνεμιζομένῳ καὶ ῥιπιζομένῳ, blown and raised with the wind (Hort, in l), Jas.1:6.†
(AS)

---

LSJ / STEPBible (TFLSJ)
ῥῑπ-ίζω,
(ῥιπίς) blow up or fan the flame, πολέμου ἔριν [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.AD: Cypria “fragment” 1; στάσιν ἀνεγείρει καὶ ῥιπίζει 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Ranae” 360; ῥ. πῦρ 1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus “Flamininus” 21; φλόγα “Anthologia Graeca” 5.121 (1st c.BC-1st c.AD: Diodorus Epigrammaticus):]] —passive, τεμάχη ῥιπίζεται the fish is fanned to boiling-point, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Ecclesiazusae” 842.]]

__2
fan a person, in middle, fan oneself, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Hippocrates Medicus “περὶ ἀρχαίης ἰητρικῇς” 16]]:—passive, ῥιπίζεσθαι ὑπὸ τῶν περιστερῶν [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Antiphanes Comicus 202.5]]; to be fanned or blown about, ὑπ᾽ ἀνέμου [NT+4th c.BC+ [“Comica Adespota” 1324, compare 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Problemata” 967a21; πρὸς ἀνέμων 1st c.AD: Philo Judaeus 2.511; κλύδων ἀνεμιζόμενος καὶ ῥιπιζόμενος NT.Jam.1.6; ῥιπιζομένη ἄχνη 2nd-3rd c.AD: Dio Cassius Historicus 70.4: _metaphorically_, ῥ. ταῖς ἐλπίσι 4th c.AD: Alciphro Epistolographus 3.47.]]

__3
hurl, [Refs 3rd c.AD+ [3rd c.AD: Heliodorus Scriptor Eroticus 10.32, compare 30 (_passive_).]]

deep_entry:
Abbott-Smith / STEPBible (TBESG)
ῥιπτέω, see: ῥίπτω.
ῥίπτω and (Act.22:23) ῥιπτέω (strengthened form; see Veitch, see word ῥίπτω, fin.),
[in LXX chiefly for שָׁלַךְ hi. ;]
__1. to throw, cast, hurl: with accusative of thing(s), Mat.27:5, Act.27:19, 29; with accusative of person(s), Mat.15:30, Luk.4:35; pass., Luk.17:2; ptcp., ἐριμμένοι, cast down, prostrate (Polyb., al.): Mat.9:36; of garments, to throw off (for flight, Eur., Xen., al.; ὅπλα, 1Ma.5:43; so EV in Act.22:23, but see infr.).
__2. = ῥιπτάζω, to shake, toss, throw about: τ. ἱμάτια, Act.22:23 (EGT, Page, Rackham, in l; Field, Notes, 136; but see supr.).†
(AS)

LSJ / STEPBible (TFLSJ)
ῥίπτ-ω,
also ῥιπτέω, and (in frequentative sense) ῥιπτάζω (which see): —Ionic dialect Iterat. ῥίπτασκον [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 15.23, 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 11.592]], -εσκον [Refs 2nd c.BC+ [2nd c.BC: Nicander Epicus “fragment” 26]]: future ῥίψω [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 8.13, etc.]]: aorist ἔρριψα [Refs 6th c.BC+ [23.842, etc. (ἔριψα 6th c.BC: Arion Lyricus 18, 2nd c.BC: Moschus Bucolicus 3.32, ἀπέριψα 5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “P.” 6.37)]], Epic dialect ῥῖψα [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 3.378]]; also 3rd.pers. singular aorist 2 ἔρρῐφε [Refs 3rd c.AD+ [3rd c.AD: Oppianus Apamensis Epicus “Cynegetica” 4.350]]: perfect ἔρριφα [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Lysias Orator 10.9]]:—middle, aorist ῥίψαντο [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [4th c.AD(?): Manetho Astrologus 6.10, ἀπο-ρίψασθαι 2nd c.AD: Galenus Medicus 16.146:]] —passive, future ῥιφθήσομαι (ἀπορ-) [LXX+5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Ajax” 1019; ῥῐφήσομαι LXX.Eze.7.19, 1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus “C. Gracchus” 3 (variant in S.[same place]); 3]] future ἐρρίψομαι [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd c.AD: Lucianus Sophista “Merc.Cond.” 17]]: aorist ἐρρίφθην [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Supplices” 484 (ἀπο-), 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Andromache” 10 (variant), 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Leges” 944d]]; also ἐρρίφην [ῐ] [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Hecuba” 335, “fragment” 489, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Leges” 944a, Sositheus Tragicus 3, etc.; poetry ἐρίφην “Anthologia Graeca” 12.234 (2nd c.AD: Strato Epigrammaticus):]]perfect ἔρριμμαι Oracle texts cited in [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.62, 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Medea” 1404 (_anapaest meter_), 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Ecclesiazusae” 850, etc.; poetry reduplicate ῥερίφθαι 5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “Fragmenta.” 318, compare “PMag.Par.” 1.194, 2039]] (ἀπο-): pluperfect ἔρριπτο [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd c.AD: Lucianus Sophista “Nec.” 17. [ῑ by nature, Hdn.Gr. 2.10]]; frequently written with ει in later Inscrr. (compare ῥιπτέω, καταρρίπτω) and Papyri, as [Refs 5th c.BC+ [1st c.BC: Philodemus Gadarensis Epigrammaticus “Ir.” p.38 W., (προσ-) “Rh.” 2.94 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus]]; the Epic dialect aorist 1 is ῥῖψα, not ῥίψα: ῐ in future 2 and aorist 2 passive]:—throw, cast, hurl, σόλον, σφαῖραν [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 23.842, 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 6.115; χερσί 5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “P.” 3.57; ῥ. ἀπὸ βηλοῦ 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 1.591, etc.; ἤ μιν ἑλὼν ῥίψω ἐς Τάρταρον 8.13, compare 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Prometheus Vinctus” 1051 (_anapaest meter_); ἐς τὸ δυστυχές [prev. author] “Ch.” 913; ἐς φλόγα 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Trachiniae” 695; ποτὶ νέφεα 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 11.592]]; χθονὶ ῥ. ἑαυτόν throw on the ground, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Trachiniae” 790, compare 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Iphigenia Aulidensis” 39 (_anapaest meter_); ἐς ὕδωρ ψυχρόν 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 2.49: _absolutely_, ἐρριμμένος]] prostrate, ἐρριμμένους καὶ μεθύοντας [Refs 2nd c.BC+ [2nd c.BC: Polybius Historicus 5.48.2]]; ἔτι τῶν νεκρῶν.. ἐρριμμένων ἐπὶ τῆς ἀγορᾶς lying, [Refs 1st c.AD+ [1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus “Galba” 28; κλῶνας ἔχουσα ἐπὶ γῆς ἐρριμμένους 1st c.AD: Dioscorides (Dioscurides) Medicus 1.29]], compare 4.169; ἔρριπται νεκροῖς ὅμοια, of hibernating animals, [Refs 6th c.AD+ [6th c.AD: Aëtius Medicus 16.67; τὰ μελίσσεια ἐν ἀγρῷ ἔριπται]]have been deposited, [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [3rd c.BC: Zenon Papyri du Caire 467.5 (3rd c.BC)]]; cast a net, ἔρριπται ὁ βόλος the cast have been made, Oracle texts cited in [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.62]]; αὐτοῦ χερμάδας.. ἔρριπτον threw stones at him, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Bacchae” 1097, compare “Cyc.” 51 (Lyric poetry)]]; ῥ. τινὰ πρὸς πέτραν throw him against a rock, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Trachiniae” 780]]; but κατὰ στύφλου πέτρας down from a rock, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Iphigenia Taurica” 1430, compare 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Prometheus Vinctus” 748]]; κατὰ κρημνῶν down a precipice, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 7.44, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Leges” 944a (_passive_)]]; ὠλένας πρὸς οὐρανόν [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Helena” 1096.]]

__II
like{ῥιπτάζω}, ῥ. ἑωυτήν toss oneself about, as in a fever, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Hippocrates Medicus “γυναικεῖα” 1.2; ἐπὶ λαιὰ καὶ ἐπὶ δεξιὰ σαυτόν “Anthologia Graeca” 5.118 (1st c.BC-1st c.AD: Crinagoras Epigrammaticus)]]: generally, throw about, πλοκάμους [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Iphigenia Aulidensis” 758, compare “Ba.” 150 (both Lyric poetry)]]; winnow, [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd c.AD: Galenus Medicus 6.541.]]

__III
cast out of house or land, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Tyrannus” 719, “Ph.” 265, etc.; μὴ ῥιφθῶ κυσὶν πρόβλητος [prev. author] “Aj.” 830.]]

__IV
throw off or away, of arms, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Electra” 820]]; of clothes, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 474a, 5th c.BC: Lysias Orator 3.12]]; so ἔρριψε Πάγασος δεσπόταν threw him, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “I.” 7(6).44]]; especially ῥ. ἀσπίδα (compare ῥίψασπις), [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Lysias Orator 10.9, etc.; βιβλίον “PUniv.Giss.” 20.12 (2nd c.AD).]]

__V
ῥ. λόγους cast them forth, hurl them, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Prometheus Vinctus” 314, 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Alcestis” 680; τὸ προειρημένον ἀναποδείκτως ἐρρίφθαι 1st c.BC: Philodemus Gadarensis Epigrammaticus “Rh.” 1.57 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus]]; also, throw them away, waste them, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Agamemnon” 1068, compare 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Medea” 1404 (_anapaest meter_, _passive_)]]; λόγοι μάτην ῥιφέντες [Refs [[prev. author] “Hec.” 335]]; so οἴχεται.. ταῦτ᾽ ἐρριμμένα set at naught, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Ajax” 1271.]]

__VI
ῥ. ἐπὶ πάντας τοὺς κλήρους, as in a scramble, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 617e; ῥ. πάντα κύβον κεφαλῆς ὕπερθεν ἐμῆς “Anthologia Graeca” 5.24 ([1st c.BC: Philodemus Gadarensis Epigrammaticus]): hence ῥ. κίνδυνον]] make a bold throw, run a risk, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Fragmenta” 402.7.]]

__VII
ῥ. ἑαυτόν throw or cast oneself down, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 3.1.25]]: absolutely, fling oneself, ἐς πόντον [Refs 6th c.BC+ [6th c.BC: Theognis Elegiacus 176; ἐς ἅλμην 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Cyclops” 166; τάφρον ἐς κοίλην [prev. author] Alcaeus 897 (_anapaest meter_); ῥ. ἐν πένθει κατὰ δρία [prev. author] “Hel.” 1325 (Lyric poetry), compare 4th-3rd c.BC: Menander Comicus 312, Vett. Val. 126.22; compare βάλλω 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus 111.]]

__VIII
uncertain reading in [Refs 5th c.AD+ [5th-6th c.AD: Orphica “Fragmenta” 264.]]

σαίνω,
[Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th-7th c.BC: Hesiodus Epicus “Theogonia” 771]]: Epic dialect imperfect σαῖνον [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 10.219]]: aorist ἔσηνα [Refs [17.302]]; Doric dialect ἔσᾱνα [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “O.” 4.6, “P.” 1.52]]:—passive, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Choephori” 194]]:—properly of dogs, wag the tail, fawn, ὅτ᾽ ἂν ἀμφὶ ἄνακτα κύνες.. σαίνωσι [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 10.217; νόησε δὲ δῖος Ὀδυσσεὺς σαίνοντάς τε κύνας 16.6; σαίνεις δάκνουσα καὶ κύων λαίθαργος εἶ 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Fragmenta” 885; ἡ κύων ἔσηνε καὶ προσῆλθ᾽ 2nd c.AD: Apollodorus Damascenus Mechanicus Comedy texts 14.5: with the _dative_ added, οὐρῇ μέν ῥ᾽ ὅ γ᾽ ἔσηνε]], of the dog Argus, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 17.302; σ. οὐρῇ τε καὶ οὔασι 8th-7th c.BC: Hesiodus Epicus [same place]; ἔσαινεν οὐρᾷ με 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Fragmenta” 687 (ἔσαινεν οὐράν]] wagged his tail, Hemsterhuis, compare [Refs 4th c.BC+ [Scholia recentia 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Septem contra Thebas” 704, Scholia recentia 3rd c.BC: Theocritus Poeta Bucolicus 2.109).]]

__II
metaphorically of persons, fawn, cringe, ὑδαρεῖ σ. φιλότητι [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Agamemnon” 798 (_anapaest meter_), compare “Pers.” 97 (Lyric poetry, assuming variant); also σ. ποτὶ πάντας 5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “P.” 2.82]]; σ. ποτὶ ἀγγελίαν greet it with joy, [Refs [[prev. author] “O.” 4.6.]]

__III
with accusative person, fawn upon, κέρκῳ τινά [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Equites” 1031, compare “Anthologia Graeca” 9.604 (3rd c.BC(?): Nossis Epigrammatica)]]; so of fishes, σαίνοντες οὐραίοισι τὴν κεκτημένην [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Fragmenta” 762.]]

__III.2
fawn on, pay court to, greet, τινα [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “P.” 1.52; ὅτ᾽ ἐλεύθερος ἀτμένα σαίνει 3rd c.BC: Callimachus Epicus “Aetia” 1.1.19]]; σ. μόρον cringe to it, seek to avert it, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Septem contra Thebas” 383, 704]]; παιδός με σαίνει φθόγγος greets me, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Antigone” 1214]]; φαιδρὰ γοῦν ἀπ᾽ ὀμμάτων σαίνει με greets me gladly from her eyes, [Refs [[prev. author] “OC” 320.]]

__III.3
gladden, especially with hope or conviction, ἐλπίδι κέαρ [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Bacchylides Lyricus 1.55; οὐ γάρ με σ. θέσφατα 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Ion” 685 (Lyric poetry); τὰ λεγόμενα.. σ. τὴν ψυχήν 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Metaphysica” 1090a37]]; so σ. τὴν ὑπόσχεσιν receive it with marks of gladness, [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd c.AD: Lucianus Sophista “Merc.Cond.” 20 (uncertain, σαίνει τῇ ὑποσχέσει is probably conjecture)]]:—passive, σαίνομαι δ᾽ ὑπ᾽ ἐλπίδος [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Choephori” 194.]]

__III.4
beguile, cozen, deceive, ἡ δ᾽ ἄρ᾽ ἐν σκότῳ λήθουσά με ἔσαιν᾽ Ἐρινύς [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Fragmenta” 577]]; σ. μ᾽ ἔννυχος φρυκτωρία seeks to deceive me, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Rhesus” 55 (or in signification 111.3).]]

__III.5
in [NT.1Thes.3.3, σαίνεσθαι ἐν ταῖς θλίψεσι] seems to mean to be shaken, disturbed; σαινόμενοι τοῖς λεγομένοις ἐδάκρυον [Refs 3rd c.AD+ [3rd c.AD(?): Diogenes Laertius 8.41 (or in signification 111.4)]]; σαίνεται· κινεῖται, σαλεύεται, ταράττεται, [Refs 5th c.AD+ [5th c.AD(?): Hesychius Legal icographus]]; but compare σιαίνω.

deep_entry:
Abbott-Smith / STEPBible (TBESG)
σάκκος  also written σάκος, -ου, ὁ
(cf. Heb. שַׂק, which it renders in LXX),
__1. a coarse cloth, sackcloth, usually made of hair: Rev.6:12.
__2. Anything made of sackcloth;
__(a) a sack (Gen.42:25, al.);
__(b) a garment of sackcloth, expressive of mourning or penitence: Mat.11:21, Luk.10:13, Rev.11:3.†
(AS)

---

LSJ / STEPBible (TFLSJ)
σάκκος
or σάκος, ὁ, see entry near the end:— coarse cloth of hair, especially of goats' hair, σάκκος τρίχινος [LXX+NT [NT.Rev.6.12, cf. LXX.Isa.50.3, LXX.Sir.25.17.]]

__II
anything made of this cloth:

__II.1
sack, bag, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 9.80, 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Acharnenses” 745, “Lys.” 1209, 2nd c.AD: Galenus Medicus 2.559,8.672:—as a measure, “Ostr.” 1096, +others]]

__II.2
sieve, strainer, especially for wine, [Refs 6th c.BC+ [6th c.BC: Hipponax Iambographus 57, 2nd c.AD(?): Pollianus Epigrammaticus 6.19; σ. τρίχινοι “PHamb.” 10.39 (2nd c.AD).]]

__II.3
coarse garment, sackcloth, worn as mourning by the Jews, [LXX+NT+1st c.AD+ [LXX.Gen.37.34, NT.Luke.10.13, 1st c.AD: Josephus Historicus “Bellum Judaicum” 2.12.5, compare 1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus 2.239c.]]

__III
coarse beard, like rough hair-cloth, σάκον πρὸς ταῖν γνάθοιν ἔχειν [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Ecclesiazusae” 502; compare σακεσφόρος 11.]] —The form σάκος is said to be Attic dialect, [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd c.AD: Aelius Dionysius Grammaticus “fragment” 296, 2nd c.AD: Phrynichus Atticista 229, 2nd c.AD: Moeris Grammaticus p.354 P., 13th-14th c.AD: Thomas Magister Grammaticus p.344]] R., etc.; while σάκκος is called Doric dialect by [Refs 6th c.BC+ [2nd c.AD: Phrynichus Atticista [same place], Hellenic by 2nd c.AD: Moeris Grammaticus and 13th-14th c.AD: Thomas Magister Grammaticus [same places], Comic by 2nd c.AD(?): Pollianus Epigrammaticus 7.191. In 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Acharnenses” 822, “Ec.” 502, σάκος is required by the metre, as is σάκκος in “Ach.” 745 (from Megarian), and in 6th c.BC: Hipponax Iambographus [same place]; codices of 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus give σάκκος]]. Inscrr. have σάκος [Refs [“IG” 22.1672.73,74, 108 and σάκκος [prev. work] 198]]: Papyri have σάκος [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [“PCair.Zen.” 753.27 (3rd c.BC), “UPZ” 84.52 (2nd c.BC)]], but oftener σάκκος [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [“PSI” 4.427.1, 14 (3rd c.BC), “PTeb.” 116.3 (2nd c.BC)]], etc. (Prob. the word, like the thing, was borrowed from Phoenicia, cf. Hebrew saq.)

deep_entry:
Abbott-Smith / STEPBible (TBESG)
σαλεύω
(σάλος), [in LXX for מוֹט, זוּעַ, etc. ;]
prop., of the action of wind, storm, etc., to agitate, shake: of a reed, Mat.11:7, Luk.7:24; a house, Luk.6:48, Act.4:31 16:26; the earth, Heb.12:26; the heavenly bodies, Mat.24:29, Mrk.13:25, Luk.21:26; of a vessel shaken in filling, Luk.6:38. Metaphorical,
__(a) to shake, i.e. to render insecure: τὰ σαλευόμενα, τὰ μὴ., Heb.12:27;
__(b) with accusative of person(s), to cast down from a sense of security and happiness:  Act.2:25 (LXX);
__(with) to unsettle or drive away: pass., before ἀπὸ τ. νοός, 2Th.2:2;
__(d) to stir up: τ. ὄχλους, Act.17:13.†
(AS)

---

LSJ / STEPBible (TFLSJ)
σαλ-εύω,
future σαλεύσω [LXX.Wis.4.19]: aorist ἐσάλευσα [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Isocrates Orator 8.95, “Anthologia Graeca” 11.83]]:— passive, future σαλευθήσομαι [LXX+NT [LXX.Sir.16.18, NT.Luke.21.26]]: aorist ἐσαλεύθην [LXX+NT+5th c.BC+ [LXX.1Mac.9.13, NT.Act.4.31, NT.2Thes.2.2, variant in 5th-6th c.BC: Isocrates Orator [same place]:]]perfect σεσάλευμαι (see. below): (σάλος):—cause to rock, make to vibrate or oscillate, with accusative, [τὰς ἀγκύρας] οὐδεὶς χειμὼν σαλεύει [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Pythagoras Philosophus cited in 5th c.AD: Stobaeus, Joannes 3.1.29]]; σ. τρικυμίᾳ πέδον, of the sea, [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [3rd c.BC: Lycophron Tragicus 475]]; of an earthquake, [LXX+1st c.AD+ [“Anthologia Graeca” 11.83 (1st c.AD: Lucillius Epigrammaticus), compare 259 ([prev. author]): _metaphorically_, δόξαν σ. 1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus 2.1123f, compare 2nd c.AD: Sextus Empiricus Philosophus “adversus Mathematicos” 8.56, 337, etc.; σ. τινὰ ἐκ θεμελίων LXX.Wis.4.19; ἐπιστολαὶ δυνάμεναι λίθον σαλεῦσαι]]heartrending, [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [POxy. 528.12 (2nd c.AD)]]; σ. τοὺς ὄχλους stir them up, [LXX+NT [NT.Acts.17.13, cf. LXX.Sir.28.14]]:—passive, to be shaken to and fro, waver, totter, reel, χθὼν σεσάλευται [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Prometheus Vinctus” 1081; κύκλος σαλευόμενος 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Timaeus” 79e, compare 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Mechanica” 857a7, 4th-3rd c.BC: Theophrastus Philosophus “de Lassitudine” 11]]; of teeth or nails, to be loosened, [Refs 1st c.AD+ [2nd c.AD: Galenus Medicus 12.871, 1st c.AD: Dioscorides (Dioscurides) Medicus 5.3]]; of persons, ἐκ Βρομίου γυῖα σαλευόμενον [Refs 6th c.AD+ [“Anthologia Graeca” 11.26 (6th c.AD: Marcus Argentarius Epigrammaticus), compare 12.31 (Phanias Epigrammaticus)]]; ὑφ᾽ ἡδονῆς σαλευομένη κορώνη [Refs 7th c.BC+ [Scholia 4th-3rd c.BC: Aratus Epicus 1009 (wrongly attributed to 7th c.BC: Archilochus Lyricus, “fragment” 102)]]; later simply, stir, move, κατεσχέθην νόσῳ.. ὡς μὴ δύνασθαι μηδὲ σαλεύεσθαι [Refs 3rd c.AD+ [“PSI” 4.299.4 (3rd c.AD).]]

__2
shake in measuring, so as to give good measure, μέτρον σεσαλευμένον [NT.Luke.6.38; compare σαλάσσω 11.]

__II
intransitive, move up and down, roll, toss, especially of ships in a stormy sea or persons in them, σ. ἐν πλοίοις [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Oeconomicus” 8.17, compare 3rd c.AD: Heliodorus Scriptor Eroticus 10.4, etc.]]: generally, put out to sea, [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd c.AD: Appianus Historicus “Μιθριδάτειος” 77]]: metaphorically, toss like a ship at sea, to be tempest-tossed, be in sore distress, πόλις γὰρ.. ἄγαν ἤδη σαλεύει [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Tyrannus” 23; πρόδοτος δὲ.. σ. Ἠλέκτρα [prev. author] “El.” 1074 (Lyric poetry); ὅταν.. σαλεύῃ πόλις 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Rhesus” 249 (Lyric poetry), compare “OGI” 515.47 (Mylasa, 3rd c.AD)]]; ἐν νόσοις ἢ γήρᾳ σ. [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Leges” 923b, compare 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Problemata” 883a34]]; ἐν κινδύνῳ σ. [Refs 1st c.BC+ [1st c.BC: Dionysius Halicarnassensis 10.11; σ. ὑπὲρ ἑαυτοῦ 2nd-3rd c.AD: Aelianus “Fragmenta” 48]]; to be unstable, [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd c.AD(?): Pollianus Epigrammaticus 6.121]]; flicker, of the eye-balls in nystagmus, [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd c.AD: Galenus Medicus 18(2).68]]; oscillate, of the λόγος ἐνδιάθετος, ἐν τούτοις [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd c.AD: Sextus Empiricus Philosophus “Πυρρώνειοι ὑποτυπώσεις” 1.65.]]

__II.2
of ships also, ἐπ᾽ ἀγκυρῶν ride at anchor, [Refs 1st c.AD+ [2nd c.AD: Polyaenus Historicus 2.2.7: _metaphorically_, ὡς ἐπ᾽ ἀγκύρας τῆς φύσεως σ. 1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus 2.493d; σ. ἐπὶ τῶν ἐλπίδων 3rd c.AD: Heliodorus Scriptor Eroticus 1.26]]; also ὁρῶν ἡμᾶς ἐπὶ τούτῳ μόνῳ (i.e. τῷ υἱῷ) σαλεύοντας [Refs 1st c.AD+ [1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus “Demetrius” 38]]; γραῦν ἐπὶ ἑνὶ γομφίῳ σ. [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [4th c.AD: Alciphro Epistolographus 3.28, compare “POxy.” 472.50 (2nd c.AD)]]; ἐπὶ τοιούτοις παραγγέλμασιν [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd c.AD: Sextus Empiricus Philosophus “adversus Mathematicos” 2.12 (hence later in a causal sense, σ. ἐπί τινι τὰς ἐλπίδας]] anchor them upon.., [Refs 3rd c.AD+ [3rd c.AD: Heliodorus Scriptor Eroticus 2.33).]]

__II.3
metaphorically, roll like a ship, roll in one's walk, of persons with the hip-joints far apart, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Hippocrates Medicus “περὶ ἄρθρων ἐμβολῆς” 56.]]

Lft., Notes, 88): opposite to πνεῦμα, 1Co.5:5, 2Co.7:1, Col.2:5, 1Pe.3:18, 4:6; to ψύχη, Act.2:31, Rec.; of the present life, ἐν (τῇ) σ., Rom.7:5, Gal.2:20, Php.1:22, 24 1Pe.4:2; of Christ's life on earth, αἱ ἡμέραι τ. σαρκὸς αὐτοῦ, Heb.5:7; of things pertaining to the body, ἐν (τῇ) σ., Gal.6:12, 13 Php.3:3, 4.
__2. As in Heb. idiom,
__(a) of a living creature: πᾶσα σ. (Heb. כָּל־בָּשָׂר; cf. Bl., §47, 9), Mat.24:22, Mrk.13:20, 1Pe.1:24; esp. of man and his mortality (Psa.55 (56):5, Sir.28:5, al.), Jhn.1:14; πᾶσα σ. (see supr.), Luk.3:6, Jhn.17:2, Act.2:17, ἐν σ., 1Jo.4:2, 1Ti.3:16;
__(b) of natural origin and relationship (Gen.2:24, Isa.58:7, al.): τέκνα τῆς σ., Rom.9:8; κατὰ σάρκα, ib. 3, 5, 1Co.10:18, Gal.4:23, 29; ἡ σ. μου, Rom.11:14 (cf. Jdg.9:2, 2Ki.5:1, al.).
__3. Of the physical nature as subject to sensation and desire (Plut.),
__(a) without any ethical disparagement: Rom.7:18 13:14; opposite to πνεῦμα, Mat.26:41, Mrk.14:38; τ. θέλημα τῆς σ., Jhn.1:13; ἡ ἐπιθυμία τῆς σ., 1Jn.2:16; pl., 2Pe.2:18; παθεῖν σαρκί, 1Pe.4:1;
__(b) in ethical sense, esp. in Pauline Epp., of the flesh as the seat and vehicle of sinful desires: opposite to νοῦς, Rom.7:25; to πνεῦμα, Rom.8:4-9, 12, 13, Gal.5:16, 17 19 6:8 (cf. DB, ii, 14f.; iv, 165f.; Cremer, 844ff.).

of liquids, run dry, γάλα [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Historia Animalium” 587b28; πηγαί “Anthologia Graeca” 9.128; αἷμα 1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus 2.49d]]; αἶγες σβεννύμεναι goats which are going off their milk, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th-7th c.BC: Hesiodus Epicus “Opera et Dies” 590.]]

__II.3
generally, to be quelled or lulled, of wind, οὐδέ ποτ᾽ ἔσβη οὖρος [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 3.182]]; of sound, σβέννυτο θωρήκων ἐνοπή [Refs 1st c.AD+ [3rd-4th c.AD: Tryphiodorus Epicus 10: _metaphorically_, τὸ μάχιμον σβεννύμενον ὑπὸ γήρως 1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus “Pompeius” 8]]; ἐσβέσθη Νίκανδρος his charm is quenched, [Refs [Anthologia Graeca 12.39]]; of an orator, [Refs 1st c.BC+ [1st c.BC: Dionysius Halicarnassensis “Epistula ad Pompeium” 4; ἐσβέσθη τὰ φίλτρα “Anthologia Graeca” 7.221, compare 2nd-3rd c.AD: Philostratus Sophista “Vita Apollonii” 1.33, 3rd c.AD: Longinus Rhetor 21.1]]; of legal proceedings, to be cancelled, διὰ τὸ ἐσβέσθαι πᾶν σπέρμα δίκης [Refs 5th c.BC+ [“PMonac.” 1.43 (6th c.AD). (I.- 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus]] zg[uglide]es-, compare ζείναμεν· σβέννυμεν, [Refs 5th c.AD+ [5th c.AD(?): Hesychius Legal icographus]], Lithuanian gèsti 'to be extinguished'.)

αὐτός, -ή, -ό,
determinative pron., in late Gk. much more frequently than in cl. (WM, 178f.; Jannaris, HGG, §1399).
__1. Emphatic (so always in nom. exc. when preceded by the art., see infr., iii);
__(1) self (ipse), expressing opposition, distinction, exclusion, etc., αὐ. ἐκχυθήσεται, Luk.5:37; αὐ. ἐγινώσκεν, Jhn.2:25; αὐ.ὑμεῖς, Jhn.3:28; καὶ αὐ. ἐγώ, Rom.15:14; αὐ. Ἰησοῦς, Jhn.2:24; αὐ. καὶ οἱ μετ᾽ αὐτοῦ, Mrk.2:25; ὑμεῖς αὐ., Mrk.6:31; esp. (as freq in cl.) αὐ. ὁ, Mat.3:4, Mrk.6:17, Jhn.16:27, 1Th.3:11, al.; in late Gk., sometimes weakened, ἐν αὐτῇ τ. ὥρᾳ, in that hour, Luk.10:21 (M, Pr., 91; MM, see word);
__(2) emphatic, he, she, it (M, Pr., 86; Bl., §48, 1, 2, 7), Mat.1:21, 12:50, Luk.6:35, al.; pointing to some one as master (cl.), Mat.8:24, Mrk.4:38, al.; αὐ., καὶ αὐ. = οὗτος, ὁ δε (BL, §48, 1), Mat.14:2, Mrk.14:15, 44, Luk.1:22, 2:28, al.
__2. In oblique cases (cl.), for the simple pron. of 3rd of person(s), he, she, it, Mat.7:9, 10:12, 26:44, al.; with ptcp. in genitive absol., Mat.9:18, Mrk.13:1, al. (for irreg. constructions, V. Bl., §74, 5); pleonastically after the relative (cf. Heb. אֲשֶׁר לוֹ; WM, 184ff.; Bl., §50, 4; MM, see word), Mrk.7:25, Rev.3:8, 7:2, al.; in constr. ad sensum, without proper subject expressly indicated, Mat.4:23, Act.8:5, 2Co.2:13, al.; genitive αὐτοῦ = ἐκείνου, Rom.11:11, 1Th.2:19, Tit.3:5, Heb.2:4.
__3. ὁ, ἡ, τὸ αὐ., the same: Heb.1:12, 13:8; τὸ αὐ., ποιεῖν, Mat.5:46, 47, al.; φρονεῖν, Rom.12:16, 15:5, Php.2:2, al.; τὰ αὐ., Act.15:27, Rom.2:1, al.; κατὰ τὸ (τὰ) αὐ. (MM, see word), Act.14:1, Luk.6:23, al.; ἐπὶ τὸ αὐ., together (MM, see word), Mat.22:34, Act.1:15, al.; ἓν κ. τὸ αὐ., 1Co.11:5, 12:11; with dative (cl.), 1Co.11:5; with a noun, λόγος, Mrk.14:39; μέτρος, Php.1:30; πνεῦμα, 1Co.12:4.
(AS)
