Diehl, 16.6, 21.9]]; Doric dialect τύ [ῠ] [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “O.” 1.85, 5th c.BC: Epicharmus Comicus 34, +others, 3rd c.BC: Theocritus Poeta Bucolicus 3.33, etc.]]; Boeotian dialect τού [short syllable] [Refs 6th c.BC+ [6th c.BC: Corinna Lyrica “Supp.” 2.83, 2nd c.AD: Apollonius Dyscolus Grammaticus “de Pronominibus;” 55.6]] (also τούν [Refs [[prev. work] 50.27, 55.6): Nom.]]σύ, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 18.31, 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Agamemnon” 1035, 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Nubes” 29, etc.; _vocative_, 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 21.193, 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Acharnenses” 165, “Pl.” 1069.]]—Gen. σοῦ, [Refs [“Hymni Homerici” 29.4]], elsewhere only Attic dialect, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Acharnenses” 302, etc.]]; enclitic σου, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Philoctetes” 761, “OT” 538, etc.; never in 8th c.BC: Homerus Epicus, who uses σεῦ, lines 3.206, +others, σέο [prev. work] 446, +others]] (also in Lyric poetry, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [7th c.BC: Archilochus Lyricus (?)in “PLit.Lond.” 54, 5th c.BC: Bacchylides Lyricus 3.65), σεῖο 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 3.137, +others; also σέθεν 1.180, +others]] (which also occurs in Lyric poetry, [Refs 7th c.BC+ [7th-6th c.BC: Sappho Lyrica 33, 5th c.BC: Bacchylides Lyricus 10.9, and Trag., 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Septem contra Thebas” 264, +others)]], and as enclitic σευ, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 5.811, +others, σεο 1.396: 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus has only σέο 1.124]], σεο (enclitic) [Refs [[prev. work] 9, σεῦ [prev. passage], 3.42, 85, 7.38,]] σευ (enclitic) [Refs [3.36, 134, 7.49]]:—Doric dialect τεῦ, τευ, [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [3rd c.BC: Theocritus Poeta Bucolicus 5.19, 10.36, etc.]]; rarely τέο, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [7th c.BC: Alcman Lyricus 17; lengthened τεοῦ 5th c.BC: Epicharmus Comicus 145, 5th c.BC: Sophron Comicus 84, and τεοῖο 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 8.37, 468]]; Boeotian dialect τεῦς [Refs 6th c.BC+ [6th c.BC: Corinna Lyrica 24]]; Doric dialect τεοῦς [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophron Comicus 59; also τιοῦς 2nd c.AD: Apollonius Dyscolus Grammaticus “de Pronominibus;” 74.27; τεῦς 3rd c.BC: Theocritus Poeta Bucolicus 2.126]]; τοι variant in [Refs [[prev. author] 7.25]]; enclitic τεος [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophron Comicus 83; Cretan dialect τέορ 5th c.AD(?): Hesychius Legal icographus]]; other Doric dialect forms are τίω, τίως, both [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [3rd c.BC: Rhinthon Comicus 13, τίος 2nd c.AD: Apollonius Dyscolus Grammaticus “de Pronominibus;” 75.24.]]—Dat. σοί, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 1.158, 167, 7th c.BC: Archilochus Lyricus 88, 6th c.BC: Mimnermus Lyricus 8, 7th-6th c.BC: Sappho Lyrica 7,99, 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Prometheus Vinctus” 3, 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 3.42, 6.86.ά, 7.52]], etc.; Doric dialect τοί [Refs 7th c.BC+ [7th c.BC: Alcman Lyricus 86 (oxytone)]]; Doric dialect, Lesb., and Ionic dialect enclitic τοι[Refs 8th c.BC+ [Alem. 33, 7th-6th c.BC: Sappho Lyrica “Frr.” 2.2,8, 7th c.BC: Archilochus Lyricus 79, 6th c.BC: Hipponax Iambographus 20, 6th c.BC: Anacreon Lyricus 44, 75.3, 5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “N.” 3.76, 5th c.BC: Bacchylides Lyricus 10.104, 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.115, 3.35, 63, 85; in 8th c.BC: Homerus Epicus]], Lesbian Lyric poetry, and Ionic dialect Lyric poetry and Prose τοι is always enclitic, σοί never enclitic (τοί and σοι are not found except σοι [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 3.359, 11.381, ς (οι) 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 1.170]], and in codices of [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “P.” 4.270, 9.55]]; rarer than τοι in [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus, 3.69, +others)]]; in Attic dialect both σοί and σοι (enclitic) are used (σοί [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Nubes” 361, etc., σοι [prev. work] 87, etc.)]], τοί and τοι are not used; σοι is never elided except in [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 1.170, τοι is elided in 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 1.60, 347, 7th-6th c.BC: Alcaeus Lyricus 55, [prev. author] “Oxy.” 1788 “fragment” 15 ii 9, 7th-6th c.BC: Sappho Lyrica 28.2]]; Epic dialect and Lyric poetry also τεΐν, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 11.201, 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 4.619, epigram cited in 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 5.60, 61, 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Aves” 930]]; also τίν [ῐ], [Refs 7th c.BC+ [7th c.BC: Alcman Lyricus 16, 5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “P.” 1.29, 8.68 (uncertain reading)]]; τίν [ῑ], [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [[prev. author] “I.” 6(5).4, 3rd c.BC: Theocritus Poeta Bucolicus 2.20 (τίν]] before a consonant, [Refs 7th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “O.” 10(11).93); also τεΐ 7th c.BC: Alcman Lyricus 53; τίνη 3rd c.BC: Rhinthon Comicus 13.]]—Acc. σέ, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 6.256, +others]]; enclitic σε,[Refs 7th c.BC+ [1.26, 7th-6th c.BC: Sappho Lyrica 1.2, “Supp.” 23.9, 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 3.42, etc.]]; in late Gr. σέν, [Refs [“Anatolian Studies” p.76]]; Doric dialect τέ [Refs 7th c.BC+ [7th c.BC: Alcman Lyricus 52, 5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “O.” 1.48, 3rd c.BC: Theocritus Poeta Bucolicus 1.5, 3rd c.BC: Callimachus Epicus “Fragmenta” 114]]; τ᾽ variant (codex R) in [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Acharnenses” 779 (on the accent see 2nd c.AD: Apollonius Dyscolus Grammaticus “de Pronominibus;” 54.14, 83.4)]]; τρέ (to be read τϝέ) [Refs 5th c.AD+ [5th c.AD(?): Hesychius Legal icographus]]; or (enclitic) τυ [Refs 6th c.BC+ [“IG” 42(1).121.69 (Epid., 4th c.BC), 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Equites” 1225, “Ach.” 730 (uncertain in “Ach.” 779), 3rd c.BC: Theocritus Poeta Bucolicus 1.56, 78, etc.:—also τίν 6th c.BC: Corinna Lyrica 4, 3rd c.BC: Cercidas Iambographus 7.6, 3rd c.BC: Theocritus Poeta Bucolicus 11.39, 55, 68.]]

__2
in combination with γε, σύ γε, σέ γε, etc. (compare ἔγωγε), thou at least, for thy part, frequently in [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Homerus Epicus]] and Attic dialect; Doric dialect τύγε [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Epicharmus Comicus [272], 5th c.BC: Timocreon Lyricus 1 (variant{τύ γα}); τύγᾰ 3rd c.BC: Theocritus Poeta Bucolicus 5.69, 71]]; Boeotian dialect τούγα [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd c.AD: Apollonius Dyscolus Grammaticus “de Pronominibus;” 55.6]]: dative σοί γε [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 1.557]]: accusative σέ γε [Refs [10.96]], etc.:—also σύ περ [Refs [24.398.]]

__3
σύ with infinitive (as imperative), [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 3.134, 4.163.]]

__II
Dual nominative and accusative σφῶϊ, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 1.336, 4.286, +others]], you two, both of you; σφώ (not σφῴ,[Refs 8th c.BC+ [compare 2nd c.AD: Apollonius Dyscolus Grammaticus “de Pronominibus;” 85.17), 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 1.574, 11.782, 13.47, 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Coloneus” 344, 1543, etc.]]—Gen. and Dat. σφῶϊν, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 4.341, +others]]; contraction σφῷν once in [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Homerus Epicus, 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 4.62, and always in _Attic dialect_ (Hdn.Gr. 1.475) and Trag., e.g. 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Prometheus Vinctus” 12, 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Coloneus” 342, “OT” 1495, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Leges” 892e (codices 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus have σφῶϊν in “Tht.” 193c, +others, σφῶν “Euthd.” 273e, +others)]]. None of these forms are enclitic, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [2nd c.AD: Apollonius Dyscolus Grammaticus “de Pronominibus;” 38.9, 85.12; codex A of 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Leges” 658c, 673e, 689a wrongly makes σφῳν]] enclitic; Ζεὺς σφὼ is prescribed in [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 15.146 by Hdn.Gr. 2.93.]] —σφῶϊ is never dative; in [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 4.286]] it is the accusative depending on κελεύ; σφῶϊν is never accusative; in [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 23.52 it is dative commodi.]]

__III
Plur. nominative ὑμεῖς, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 2.75, +others (before a vowel, 4.246, 7.194, +others), 6th c.BC: Pherecydes Syrius Philosophus 11, 3rd c.AD: Democritus Epigrammaticus 29a, 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 3.72, etc.]], ye, you; Aeolic dialect and Epic dialect ὔμμες [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 1.274, +others, 7th-6th c.BC: Sappho Lyrica 24, 25]]; Doric dialect ὑμές [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophron Comicus 60, 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Acharnenses” 760, 761, 862; ὑμέν “SIG” 685.118 (Crete, 2nd c.BC), “GDI” 5155.6 ([prev. passage], 2nd c.BC)]]; Boeotian dialect οὐμές [Refs 6th c.BC+ [6th c.BC: Corinna Lyrica 6]]; a resolved form ὑμέες, [Refs 1st c.BC+ [1st c.BC: Parthenius Mythographus “fragment” 14, is a poeticlicence (so 2nd c.AD: Apollonius Dyscolus Grammaticus “de Pronominibus;” 93.3)]] rather than genuine Ionic [Refs 5th c.BC+ [(variant in 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 8.22).]]— Gen. ὑμῶν, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Acharnenses” 143, etc.]]; ὑμέων (disyllable) [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 7.159, 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 13.7, +others, 7th c.BC: Archilochus Lyricus 74.6 (ὑμῶν codices), 6th c.BC: Solon Lyricus 11.5 (variant{ὑμῶν})]]; ὑμέων also [Refs 8th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 3.73, 6.130, +others; as _trisyllable_, 3rd c.BC: Herodas Mimographus 2.27; ὑμείων 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 4.348, 7.195, +others]]; Doric dialect ὑμέων [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophron Comicus 46]]; also ὑμῶν, [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd c.AD: Apollonius Dyscolus Grammaticus “de Pronominibus;” 95.23]]; Aeolic dialect ὑμμέων [Refs 7th c.BC+ [7th-6th c.BC: Alcaeus Lyricus 96]]; Boeotian dialect οὐμίων [Refs 6th c.BC+ [6th c.BC: Corinna Lyrica 22.]]—Dat. ὑμῖν, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 2.46, 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.126, etc.]]; Ionic dialect enclitic ὗμῐν [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd c.AD: Apollonius Dyscolus Grammaticus “de Pronominibus;” 97.28,]] also Doric dialect, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophron Comicus 91]]; Doric dialect (not enclitic) ὑμίν [ῐ] [Refs [[prev. author] 92]]; ὑμίν [ῐ] also in [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Ajax” 864, 1242, “OT” 991, 1402, “Ant.” 308, “El.” 804, +others (but ὗμιν]] should perhaps be restored where the sense needs an enclitic on the principle stated by [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd c.AD: Apollonius Dyscolus Grammaticus “de Pronominibus;” 35.6, 36.5, “Synt.” 130.23)]]; ὕμιν[Refs 8th c.BC+ [(as _enclitic_) is prescribed by Hdn.Gr. (2.124) in 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 24.33, by “Etymologicum Magnum” 432.34 in 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 1.376, 2.141, etc.:—_Aeolic dialect_ and _Epic dialect_ ὔμμῐ, ὔμμῐν, 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 2.316, 11.336, +others, 8th-7th c.BC: Hesiodus Epicus “Scutum Herculis” 328, 7th-6th c.BC: Sappho Lyrica 14, 7th-6th c.BC: Alcaeus Lyricus “Supp.” 26.9, 5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “O.” 11(10).17.]]—Acc. ὑμᾶς, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Acharnenses” 325]], etc. (-υ [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.AD: Orphica “Argonautica” 820, variant in 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Philoctetes” 222]]; ὗμας or (more probably) ὕμας is required by the metre in [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd c.AD: Babrius Fabularum Scriptor 9.9, 47.11)]]; Ionic dialect ὑμέας (disyllable) [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 21.198, +others]]; enclitic ὕμεας (disyllable) [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [3rd c.BC: Herodas Mimographus 2.60 (Papyrus)]]; ὑμέας also [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.126, +others]]; Aeolic dialect and Epic dialect ὔμμε [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 23.412, +others, 5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “I.” 6(5).19; also in 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Eumenides” 620 (trimeter), and 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Antigone” 846 (Lyric poetry)]]; Doric dialect ὑμέ [Refs 7th c.BC+ [7th c.BC: Alcman Lyricus 3, 5th c.BC: Sophron Comicus 52, 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Acharnenses” 737, “Lys.” 1076, “SIG” 528.3 (Cretan dialogue, 3rd c.BC), 622 B 8 (Cretan, 2nd c.BC).]]—The plural is sometimes used in addressing one person, when others are included in the speaker's thought, as [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 12.81, 7th c.BC: Archilochus Lyricus 89. (With σύ]] cf. Latin tu, Gothic pu; with τοι Sanskrit genitive and dative te; the origin of σφῶϊ is doubtful; with ὑμεῖς cf. Sanskrit accusative plural yusmān.)

of things divine, ὄργια σ. [Refs 6th c.BC+ [“hymnus ad Cererem” 478, 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Trachiniae” 765; θέμεθλα δίκης 6th c.BC: Solon Lyricus 4.14; ὑγίεια 4th-5th c.BC: Simonides Lyricus 70; θυσία 5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “O.” 7.42]]; σ. ἄντρον the cave of Cheiron, [Refs [[prev. author] “P.” 9.30, compare “O.” 5.18]]; σ. δόμος the temple of Apollo, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [[prev. author] “N.” 1.72; παιάν 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Persae” 393]]; σέλμα σ. ἡμένων, of the Olympian gods, [Refs [[prev. author] “Ag.” 183 (Lyric poetry)]]; σ. ἔργα, of the gods, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. author] “Supp.” 1037 (Lyric poetry); μυστήρια 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Fragmenta” 804, 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Hippolytus” 25; τέρμων οὐρανοῦ [prev. work] 746]]; σ. βίος devoted to the gods, [Refs [[prev. author] “Ion” 56]]; σεμνὰ φθέγγεσθαι, ={εὔφημα}, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Choephori” 109 (variant), compare 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Nubes” 315, 364]]; ἦ πού τι σ. ἔστιν ὃ ξυναμπέχει; [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Prometheus Vinctus” 521]]; τὸ σ. holiness, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 21.126.]]

σημαίνω,
[Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 10.58, etc.]]; σᾱμαίνω, [Refs [“Schwyzer” 686.23 (from Pamphylia)]]: Ionic dialect imperfect σημαίνεσκον [Refs 4th c.AD+ [4th c.AD(?): Quintus Smyrnaeus Epicus 4.193]]: future σημᾰνῶ [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Agamemnon” 497, 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 6.20]], Ionic dialect -ᾰνέω[Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 12.26, 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.75:]]aorist ἐσήμηνα[Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. work] 43, 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 5.71]], Epic dialect σήμηνα [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 23.358]]; but in codices of [NT+5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus (“HG” 1.1.2, +others) and later writers (1st c.BC-1st c.AD: Strabo Geographus 13.3.6, NT.Act.25.27, 2nd c.AD: Polyaenus Historicus 1.41.3, 2nd c.AD: Arrianus Historicus “Anabasis” 1.6.2) ἐσήμᾱνα, and so in Mitteis “Chr.” 29.8 (2nd c.BC)]]: perfect σεσήμαγκα [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aristobulus Historicus cited in 4th c.AD: Eusebius Caesariensis Scriptor Ecclesiasticus “Praeparatio Evangelica” 13.12, 2nd c.AD: Arrianus Historicus “Epicteti Dissertationes” 3.26.29:]] —middle, future σημᾰνοῦμαι, Ionic dialect -έομαι[Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Hippocrates Medicus “προγνωστικόν” 3, etc.]]: aorist ἐσημηνάμην [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 7.175, etc.]]:—passive, future σημανθήσομαι [Refs 5th c.BC+ [2nd c.AD: Sextus Empiricus Philosophus “adversus Mathematicos” 8.267, (ἐπι-) 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Ion” 1593]]: future middle in passive sense, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Hippocrates Medicus “περὶ τῶν ἐντὸς παθῶν” 44]]: aorist ἐσημάνθην [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 47.16]]: perfect σεσήμασμαι [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 2.39, 5th c.BC: Lysias Orator 32.7, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Leges” 954a, etc.]]; 3rd.pers. singular σεσήμανται [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 2.125]], infinitive σεσημάνθαι [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Lysistrata” 1196]]: (σῆμα):—show by a sign, indicate, point out, τέρματα [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 23.358; δείξω ὁδὸν ἠδὲ ἕκαστα σημανέω 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 12.26]]; τοῦτον σημήνας after indicating the person, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.5; τέκμαρ 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Choephori” 667; θησαύρισμα 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Philoctetes” 37; σ. τι περί τινος 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Leges” 682a; σ. ὅ τι χρὴ ποιεῖν 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Apologia Socratis” 12]]; σ. εὔδια πάντα (i.e. εἶναι) [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [3rd c.BC: Theocritus Poeta Bucolicus 22.22:]] —middle, πάντα σημαίνει you have all things shown you (?), [Refs [“epigram Gr.” 1039.11 (from Limyra).]]

__2
absolutely, give signs, φθόγγος, φῶς σ., [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Supplices” 245, “Ag.” 293; ὁ λόγος σημαινέτω 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Trachiniae” 345]]; σ. καπνῷ make signal, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Agamemnon” 497: frequently in 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus]] in future with αὐτός, πλοῦς αὐτὸς σημανεῖ [Refs [“Hel.” 151; τὸ δ᾽ ἔργον αὐτὸ σημανεῖ “Andr.” 265]]; αὐτὸ σημανεῖ (without substantive) [Refs [“Ph.” 623; τἄλλα δ᾽ αὐτὸ σημανεῖ “Ba.” 976.]]

__3
of the Delphic oracle, οὔτε λέγει οὔτε κρύπτει ἀλλὰ σημαίνει [Refs 1st c.AD+ [1st c.AD(?): Heraclitus 93]]; so of omens, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Memorabilia” 1.1.2, etc.; σ. ἐν τοῖς ἱεροῖς [prev. author] “An.” 6.1.31; περί τινος [prev. author] “Mem.” 1.1.19; ἐπὶ τοῖς μέλλουσι γενήσεσθαι 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 2.8; πρὸ τῶν μελλόντων 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Historia Graeca (Hellenica)” 5.4.17]]:—passive, σημαίνεσθαι διὰ τῶν ἐμπύρων [Refs 1st c.AD+ [1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus 2.222f, etc.]]

__4
in later Prose intransitive, appear, be manifest, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Historia Animalium” 533a11]] (but passive in same sense,[Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. work] 588b18); σ. ἐκ τῶν εἰρημένων 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Epinomis” 989a; compare δηλόω 11.]]

__4.b
σημαίνει impersonal, signs appear, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Problemata” 941b2, 944a4.]]

__II
give a sign or signal to do a thing, or bid one do it, with dative person et infinitive, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.116, 6.78, 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Agamemnon” 26, 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Ajax” 688, 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 6.1.24]]; give orders to, bear command over, with dative, πᾶσι δὲ σημαίνειν [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 1.289, compare 10.58, 17.250]]; with genitive, στρατοῦ [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 14.85; also σ. ἐπὶ δμῳῇσι γυναιξίν 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 22.427]]: absolutely, give orders, ὁ δὲ σημαίνων ἐπέτελλεν [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 21.445, compare 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 22.450: in]]participle, σημαίνων,= σημάντωρ, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Coloneus” 704 codices]]

__II.2
in war or battle, give the signal of attack, etc., [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 2.84, etc.; in full, σ. τῇ σάλπιγγι 5th-6th c.BC: Andocides Orator 1.45, 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 4.2.1, 5th c.BC: Achaeus Tragicus 37.3; σ. τῷ κέρατι ὡς ἀναπαύεσθαι 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 2.2.4: with _accusative_, σ. ἀναχώρησιν]] give a signal for retreat, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 5.10; ἐπειδὰν ὁ σαλπιγκτὴς σημήνῃ τὸ πολεμικόν 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 4.3.29, compare 4.3.32; τὸ ἀνακλητικόν 1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus 2.236e]]: with infinitive, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 1.4.18, etc.: _impersonal_ σημαίνει (i.e. ὁ σαλπιγκτής)]], signal is given, as τοῖσι Ἕλλησι ὡς ἐσήμηνε when signal was given for the Greeks to attack, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 8.11: with]]infinitive, ἐσήμαινε παραρτέεσθαι πάντα signal was given to make all ready, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. author] 9.42, compare 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Heraclidae” 830]]; also σ. ἐπὶ πλόον πῦρ gives the signal for sailing, [Refs 3rd c.AD+ [3rd-4th c.AD: Tryphiodorus Epicus 145.]]

__II.3
generally, σ. [τῷ ἵππῳ] τι, προχωρεῖν σ. τῷ ἵππῳ, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “de Equitandi ratione” 9.4, 7.10.]]

__II.4
make signals, εἰς τὴν πόλιν [Refs [[prev. author] “HG” 6.2.33; σ. ὡς πολεμίων ἐπιόντων [prev. work] 7.2.5:]] —passive, ἐσημάνθησαν προσπλέουσαι[Refs [[prev. work] 6.2.34: _absolutely_, σημανθέντων τῷ Ἀστυάγει ὅτι.. [prev. author] “Cyr.” 1.4.18.]]

__III
signify, indicate, declare, φόνον [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Hercules Furens” 1218; τινί τι 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 7.18, 9.49, 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Tyrannus” 226: followed by ὡς.., 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.34]]; by ὅτι.., [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Coloneus” 320, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Phaedo” 62c; σ. ὅστις 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Prometheus Vinctus” 618; σ. ὅ τι χρή σοι συμπράσσειν [prev. work] 297 (_anapaest meter_); σ. ὅπῃ γῆς πεπλάνημαι [prev. work] 564 (_anapaest meter_)]]; σ. ὅπου.. [NT+5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Electra” 1294; σ. ὅτου τ᾽ εἶ χὠπόθεν [prev. author] “fragment” 104; σ. εἴτε.. [prev. author] “Ph.” 22; σ. ποίῳ θανάτῳ.. NT.John.12.33, 21.19]]: with participle, signify that a thing is, φρυκτοῦ φῶς.. σημαίνει μολόν [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Agamemnon” 293; Κρέοντα προσστείχοντα σημαίνουσί μοι 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Tyrannus” 79, compare “OC” 1669; ταῦτα ὡς πολέμου ὄντος σημαίνει 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Leges” 626e, compare 722e:]] —passive, ὁ σημαινόμενος δοῦλος the abovementioned slave, [Refs 1st c.AD+ [“POxy.” 283.12 (1st c.AD): _absolutely_, σημανθέντος]]it having been reported, [Refs 2nd c.BC+ [PAmh. 2.31.8 (2nd c.BC), compare above 11.4.]]

__III.2
interpret, explain, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.108]]; tell, speak, [Refs [[prev. author] 3.106: _absolutely_, σήμαινε]] tell, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Coloneus” 51, compare “OT” 1050; οὐ στηλῶν μόνον σ. ἐπιγραφή 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 2.43.]]

__III.3
of a writer, signify, indicate, ὅτι.. [Refs 1st c.BC+ [1st c.BC-1st c.AD: Strabo Geographus 8.6.5]]; of words, sentences, etc., signify, mean, ταὐτὸν σημαίνει [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Cratylus” 393a, compare 437c, “Phdr.” 275d, 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Physica” 213b30, etc.]]; σημαίνοντα significant sounds, opposed to ἄσημα, [Refs [[prev. author] “Po.” 1457a32f:]] —passive, τὸ σημαινόμενον the sense, meaning of words, [Refs 1st c.BC+ [[prev. author] “Rh.” 1405b8, 1st c.BC: Dionysius Halicarnassensis “de Thucydide” 31, 2nd c.AD: Apollonius Dyscolus Grammaticus “de Pronominibus;” 12.27, +others]]; opposed to τὸ σημαῖνον, [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [3rd c.BC: Chrysippus Stoicus 2.38 (_plural_).]]

__B
middle σημαίνομαι, give oneself a token, i.e. conclude from signs, conjecture, τὰ μὲν σημαίνομαι, τὰ δ᾽ ἐκπέπληγμαι [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Ajax” 32]]; ἄστροις σ. [τὰς πόλεις], proverbial in [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd-3rd c.AD: Aelianus “De Natura Animalium - Ar.Byzantine Epit.” 7.48; σ. τι ἔκ τινος [prev. work] 2.7]]; of dogs hunting, μυξωτῆρσι σ. τι [Refs 3rd c.AD+ [3rd c.AD: Oppianus Apamensis Epicus “Cynegetica” 1.454.]]

__B.II
provide with a sign or mark, seal, σημαίνεσθαι βύβλῳ (i.e. βοῦν), i.e. by sealing a strip of byblus round his horn, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 2.38, compare 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Leges” 954c, 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 8.2.17, 4th c.BC: Isaeus Orator 7.1, 2, 4th c.BC: Hyperides Orator “adv. Athenogenem” 8:]] —passive, εὖ σεσημάνθαι to be well sealed up, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Lysistrata” 1196]]; τὰ σεσημασμένα, opposed to τὰ ἀσήμαντα, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Leges” 954a, compare 5th c.BC: Lysias Orator 32.7, 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 39.17, “Ath.Mitt.” 7.368.]]

__B.II.2
mark out, choose for oneself, τοὺς εὐρωστοτάτους [Refs 2nd c.BC+ [2nd c.BC: Polybius Historicus 3.71.7.]]

Abbott-Smith / STEPBible (TBESG)
σημεῖον, -ου, τό
[in LXX chiefly for אוֹת ;]
a sign, mark, token;
__(a) of that which distinguishes a person or thing from others: Mat.26:48 Luk.2:12, 2Th.3:17 (cf. Deiss., LAE, 153.2); before genitive epexeg., Rom.4:11; with genitive obj., Mat.24:8, 30, 2Co.12:12; with genitive subj., Mat.16:3;
__(b) a sign of warning or admonition: Mat.12:39 16:4, Luk.2:34 11:29-30, 1Co.14:22;
__(with) a sign portending future events (Soph., Plat. al.): Mrk.13:4, Luk.21:7, 11 21:25, Act.2:19, Rev.12:1, 3 15:1;
__(d) of miracles and wonders (MM, xxii), regarded as signs of a divine authority: Mat.12:38-39 16:1, 4 Mrk.8:11-12 Luk.11:16, 29 23:8, Jhn.2:11, 18 2:23 4:54 6:30 10:41 12:18, Act.4:16, 22; pl., Mrk.16:17, 20, Jhn.2:11, 23 3:2 6:2, 14 6:26 7:31 9:16 11:47 12:37 20:30, Act.8:6, 1Co.1:22 (Lft., Notes, 162); the same ascribed to false teachers and demons: Mat.24:24, Mrk.13:22, 2Th.2:9, Rev.13:13-14 16:14 19:20; σ. καὶ τέρατα (τ. καὶ σ.; cf. Tr., Syn., § xci), Mat.24:24, Mrk.13:22, Jhn.4:48, Act.2:19, 43 4:30 5:12 6:8 7:36 14:3 15:12, Rom.15:19, 2Th.2:9; id. before καὶ δυνάμεις, 2Co.12:12, Heb.2:4; σ. καὶ δυνάμεις, Act.8:13; δ. καὶ τ. καὶ σ., Act.2:22; σ. διδόναι, Mat.24:24, Mrk.13:22.†
(AS)

LSJ / STEPBible (TFLSJ)
σημεῖον, τό,
Ionic dialect σημήϊον, Doric dialect σᾱμήϊον [Refs 4th c.BC+ [“IG” 12(3).452 (Thera, 4th c.BC)]], σᾱμεῖον [Refs 2nd c.BC+ [“IPE” 12.352.25 (Chersonesus, 2nd c.BC), “IG” 5(1).1390.16 (Andania, 1st c.BC)]], σᾱμᾶον [Refs [“CIG” “Corpus Inscriptionum Graecarum” “Corpus Inscriptionum Graecarum” 5168 (from Cyrene):]] —= σῆμα in all senses, and more common in Prose, but never in [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Homerus Epicus or 8th-7th c.BC: Hesiodus Epicus]]: mark by which a thing is known, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 2.38; σημεῖα τῶν δεδικασμένων.., σημεῖα πάντων ὧν ἔπραξαν 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 614c]]; sign of the future, τυραννίδος σ. [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Agamemnon” 1355; σ. λαβεῖν ἔκ τινος 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Hippolytus” 514]]; trace, track, σημεῖα δ᾽ οὔτε θηρὸς οὔτε του κυνῶν.. ἐξεφαίνετο [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Antigone” 257, compare “El.” 886; τῆς καταβάσεως 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 6.2.2]]; of a cork on a buoy, [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd c.AD: Pausanias Periegeta 8.12.1.]]

__b
Doric dialect, tomb, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [Inscriptiones Graecae 12(3).452 (4th c.BC), “CIG” “Corpus Inscriptionum Graecarum” “Corpus Inscriptionum Graecarum” [prev. cited]]]

__2
sign from the gods, omen, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Coloneus” 94; τὰ ἀπὸ τῶν θεῶν σ. γενόμενα 5th c.BC: Antipho Orator 5.81, compare 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Phaedrus” 244c, “Ap.” 40b, 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 1.6.1]]; wonder, portent, [LXX+2nd c.BC+ [LXX.Exo.4.8, +others; σ. καὶ τέρατα 2nd c.BC: Polybius Historicus 3.112.8, NT.Matt.24.24, NT.John.4.48, compare “IPE” [same place], 1st c.BC: Diodorus Siculus Historicus 17.114; φόβηθρα καὶ σ. ἀπ᾽ οὐρανοῦ NT.Luke.21.11]]; especially of the constellations, regarded as signs, δύεται σημεῖα [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Rhesus” 529 (Lyric poetry), compare “Ion” 1157.]]

__3
sign or signal to do a thing, made by flags, ἀνέδεξε σημήϊον τοῖσι ἄλλοισι ἀνάγεσθαι he made signal for the rest to put to sea, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 7.128]]; signal for battle, τὰ σ. ἤρθη, κατεσπάσθη, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 1.49, 63, etc.]]; καθαιρεῖν τὸ σ. to take it down, strike the flag, as a sign of dissolving an assembly, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Andocides Orator 1.36]]; τὸ τῆς ἐκκλησίας σ. [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Thesmophoriazusae” 278]]; ὕστερος ἐλθεῖν τοῦ σ. [Refs [[prev. author] “V.” 690]]: generally, signal, σ. ὑποδηλῶσαί τινι ὅτι.. also τίν [ῐ], [Refs 7th c.BC+ [7th c.BC: Alcman Lyricus 16, 5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “P.” 1.29, 8.68 (uncertain reading)]]; τίν [ῑ], [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [[prev. author] “I.” 6(5).4, 3rd c.BC: Theocritus Poeta Bucolicus 2.20 (τίν]] before a consonant, [Refs 7th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “O.” 10(11).93); in late Gr. σέν, [Refs [“Anatolian Studies” p.76]]; Doric dialect τέ [Refs 7th c.BC+ [7th c.BC: Alcman Lyricus 52, 5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “O.” 1.48, 3rd c.BC: Theocritus Poeta Bucolicus 1.5, 3rd c.BC: Callimachus Epicus “Fragmenta” 114]]; τ᾽ variant (codex R) in [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Acharnenses” 779 (on the accent see 2nd c.AD: Apollonius Dyscolus Grammaticus “de Pronominibus;” 54.14, 83.4)]]; τρέ (to be read τϝέ) [Refs 5th c.AD+ [5th c.AD(?): Hesychius Legal icographus]]; or (enclitic) τυ [Refs 6th c.BC+ [“IG” 42(1).121.69 (Epid., 4th c.BC), 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Equites” 1225, “Ach.” 730 (uncertain in “Ach.” 779), 3rd c.BC: Theocritus Poeta Bucolicus 1.56, 78, etc.:—also τίν 6th c.BC: Corinna Lyrica 4, 3rd c.BC: Cercidas Iambographus 7.6, 3rd c.BC: Theocritus Poeta Bucolicus 11.39, 55, 68.]]

__2
in combination with γε, σύ γε, σέ γε, etc. (compare ἔγωγε), thou at least, for thy part, frequently in [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Homerus Epicus]] and Attic dialect; Doric dialect τύγε [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Epicharmus Comicus [272], 5th c.BC: Timocreon Lyricus 1 (variant{τύ γα}); τύγᾰ 3rd c.BC: Theocritus Poeta Bucolicus 5.69, 71]]; Boeotian dialect τούγα [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd c.AD: Apollonius Dyscolus Grammaticus “de Pronominibus;” 55.6]]: dative σοί γε [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 1.557]]: accusative σέ γε [Refs [10.96]], etc.:—also σύ περ [Refs [24.398.]]

__3
σύ with infinitive (as imperative), [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 3.134, 4.163.]]

__II
Dual nominative and accusative σφῶϊ, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 1.336, 4.286, +others]], you two, both of you; σφώ (not σφῴ,[Refs 8th c.BC+ [compare 2nd c.AD: Apollonius Dyscolus Grammaticus “de Pronominibus;” 85.17), 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 1.574, 11.782, 13.47, 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Coloneus” 344, 1543, etc.]]—Gen. and Dat. σφῶϊν, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 4.341, +others]]; contraction σφῷν once in [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Homerus Epicus, 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 4.62, and always in _Attic dialect_ (Hdn.Gr. 1.475) and Trag., e.g. 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Prometheus Vinctus” 12, 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Coloneus” 342, “OT” 1495, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Leges” 892e (codices 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus have σφῶϊν in “Tht.” 193c, +others, σφῶν “Euthd.” 273e, +others)]]. None of these forms are enclitic, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [2nd c.AD: Apollonius Dyscolus Grammaticus “de Pronominibus;” 38.9, 85.12; codex A of 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Leges” 658c, 673e, 689a wrongly makes σφῳν]] enclitic; Ζεὺς σφὼ is prescribed in [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 15.146 by Hdn.Gr. 2.93.]] —σφῶϊ is never dative; in [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 4.286]] it is the accusative depending on κελεύ; σφῶϊν is never accusative; in [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 23.52 it is dative commodi.]]

__III
Plur. nominative ὑμεῖς, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 2.75, +others (before a vowel, 4.246, 7.194, +others), 6th c.BC: Pherecydes Syrius Philosophus 11, 3rd c.AD: Democritus Epigrammaticus 29a, 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 3.72, etc.]], ye, you; Aeolic dialect and Epic dialect ὔμμες [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 1.274, +others, 7th-6th c.BC: Sappho Lyrica 24, 25]]; Doric dialect ὑμές [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophron Comicus 60, 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Acharnenses” 760, 761, 862; ὑμέν “SIG” 685.118 (Crete, 2nd c.BC), “GDI” 5155.6 ([prev. passage], 2nd c.BC)]]; Boeotian dialect οὐμές [Refs 6th c.BC+ [6th c.BC: Corinna Lyrica 6]]; a resolved form ὑμέες, [Refs 1st c.BC+ [1st c.BC: Parthenius Mythographus “fragment” 14, is a poeticlicence (so 2nd c.AD: Apollonius Dyscolus Grammaticus “de Pronominibus;” 93.3)]] rather than genuine Ionic [Refs 5th c.BC+ [(variant in 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 8.22).]]— Gen. ὑμῶν, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Acharnenses” 143, etc.]]; ὑμέων (disyllable) [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 7.159, 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 13.7, +others, 7th c.BC: Archilochus Lyricus 74.6 (ὑμῶν codices), 6th c.BC: Solon Lyricus 11.5 (variant{ὑμῶν})]]; ὑμέων also [Refs 8th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 3.73, 6.130, +others; as _trisyllable_, 3rd c.BC: Herodas Mimographus 2.27; ὑμείων 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 4.348, 7.195, +others]]; Doric dialect ὑμέων [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophron Comicus 46]]; also ὑμῶν, [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd c.AD: Apollonius Dyscolus Grammaticus “de Pronominibus;” 95.23]]; Aeolic dialect ὑμμέων [Refs 7th c.BC+ [7th-6th c.BC: Alcaeus Lyricus 96]]; Boeotian dialect οὐμίων [Refs 6th c.BC+ [6th c.BC: Corinna Lyrica 22.]]—Dat. ὑμῖν, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 2.46, 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.126, etc.]]; Ionic dialect enclitic ὗμῐν [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd c.AD: Apollonius Dyscolus Grammaticus “de Pronominibus;” 97.28,]] also Doric dialect, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophron Comicus 91]]; Doric dialect (not enclitic) ὑμίν [ῐ] [Refs [[prev. author] 92]]; ὑμίν [ῐ] also in [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Ajax” 864, 1242, “OT” 991, 1402, “Ant.” 308, “El.” 804, +others (but ὗμιν]] should perhaps be restored where the sense needs an enclitic on the principle stated by [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd c.AD: Apollonius Dyscolus Grammaticus “de Pronominibus;” 35.6, 36.5, “Synt.” 130.23)]]; ὕμιν[Refs 8th c.BC+ [(as _enclitic_) is prescribed by Hdn.Gr. (2.124) in 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 24.33, by “Etymologicum Magnum” 432.34 in 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 1.376, 2.141, etc.:—_Aeolic dialect_ and _Epic dialect_ ὔμμῐ, ὔμμῐν, 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 2.316, 11.336, +others, 8th-7th c.BC: Hesiodus Epicus “Scutum Herculis” 328, 7th-6th c.BC: Sappho Lyrica 14, 7th-6th c.BC: Alcaeus Lyricus “Supp.” 26.9, 5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “O.” 11(10).17.]]—Acc. ὑμᾶς, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Acharnenses” 325]], etc. (-υ [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.AD: Orphica “Argonautica” 820, variant in 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Philoctetes” 222]]; ὗμας or (more probably) ὕμας is required by the metre in [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd c.AD: Babrius Fabularum Scriptor 9.9, 47.11)]]; Ionic dialect ὑμέας (disyllable) [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 21.198, +others]]; enclitic ὕμεας (disyllable) [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [3rd c.BC: Herodas Mimographus 2.60 (Papyrus)]]; ὑμέας also [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.126, +others]]; Aeolic dialect and Epic dialect ὔμμε [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 23.412, +others, 5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “I.” 6(5).19; also in 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Eumenides” 620 (trimeter), and 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Antigone” 846 (Lyric poetry)]]; Doric dialect ὑμέ [Refs 7th c.BC+ [7th c.BC: Alcman Lyricus 3, 5th c.BC: Sophron Comicus 52, 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Acharnenses” 737, “Lys.” 1076, “SIG” 528.3 (Cretan dialogue, 3rd c.BC), 622 B 8 (Cretan, 2nd c.BC).]]—The plural is sometimes used in addressing one person, when others are included in the speaker's thought, as [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 12.81, 7th c.BC: Archilochus Lyricus 89. (With σύ]] cf. Latin tu, Gothic pu; with τοι Sanskrit genitive and dative te; the origin of σφῶϊ is doubtful; with ὑμεῖς cf. Sanskrit accusative plural yusmān.)

LSJ / STEPBible (TFLSJ)
σός, ή, όν,
possessive adjective of 2 person singular (σύ), the alternative Epic dialect and Doric dialect form being τεός (which see), thy, thine, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 8.420, etc.]]; Epic dialect genitive σοῖο [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 15.511]]; σ. δέμας, σ. ἔργον, λέχος σ., etc., [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Prometheus Vinctus” 146 (Lyric poetry), 635, 557 (Lyric poetry), etc.: σ. ἑταῖρος]] a friend of yours, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Lysis” 204a, etc.]]: with the Article, τὸ σὸν γέρας [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 1.185, compare 207, +others, and so frequently in _Attic dialect_, δέμ·ας τὸ σ., τὸ σ. κάρα, etc., 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Prometheus Vinctus” 1019, “Ag.” 1615, etc.]] (but never so when it serves as predicate, οὐ σ. τόδ᾽ ἐστὶ τοὔργον [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Electra” 296; πάτερ, σός εἰμι [prev. author] “Ant.” 635)]]; σ. ἔργον with infinitive, 'tis thy business to.., ἔργον ἤδη σ. τὰ λοίφ᾽ ὑπηρετεῖν [Refs [[prev. author] “Ph.” 15]]; σόν [ἐστι] alone, σ. δ᾽ αὖ τὸ σιγᾶν [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Septem contra Thebas” 232, compare 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Electra” 1470]]; σὴ μὲν ἐγώ, σὰ δὲ πάντα thine am I, thine are all things, [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [3rd c.BC: Callimachus Epicus “Hymnus in Delum” 219.]]

__2
without a substantive, thine, εἰ ἐτεόν γε σός εἰμι thy son, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 9.529, compare 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Helena” 226 (Lyric poetry)]]; σὺ μὲν ἀπάγου τὴν σ. [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 3.1.37]]; οἱ σ. thy kinsfolk, people, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Tyrannus” 1448, etc.]]: also singular, your agent or servant, [Refs 1st c.AD+ [PFay. 123.5 (1st-2nd c.AD): τὸ σ]]. what concerns thee, thy interest, advantage, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Electra” 251, “Aj.” 1313]]; thy words, thy purpose, [Refs [[prev. work] 99, 1401]], etc.; τὰ σ. thy property, ἐπὶ σοῖσι καθήμενος [NT+8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 2.369, compare 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Memorabilia” 2.3.12, NT.Luke.6.30]]; εὖ φρονῶ τὰ σ. thy interests, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Ajax” 491]]; καὶ σὲ καὶ τὰ σ. [Refs [[prev. author] “El.” 522, etc.]]

__3

__II

αὐτός, -ή, -ό,
determinative pron., in late Gk. much more frequently than in cl. (WM, 178f.; Jannaris, HGG, §1399).
__1. Emphatic (so always in nom. exc. when preceded by the art., see infr., iii);
__(1) self (ipse), expressing opposition, distinction, exclusion, etc., αὐ. ἐκχυθήσεται, Luk.5:37; αὐ. ἐγινώσκεν, Jhn.2:25; αὐ.ὑμεῖς, Jhn.3:28; καὶ αὐ. ἐγώ, Rom.15:14; αὐ. Ἰησοῦς, Jhn.2:24; αὐ. καὶ οἱ μετ᾽ αὐτοῦ, Mrk.2:25; ὑμεῖς αὐ., Mrk.6:31; esp. (as freq in cl.) αὐ. ὁ, Mat.3:4, Mrk.6:17, Jhn.16:27, 1Th.3:11, al.; in late Gk., sometimes weakened, ἐν αὐτῇ τ. ὥρᾳ, in that hour, Luk.10:21 (M, Pr., 91; MM, see word);
__(2) emphatic, he, she, it (M, Pr., 86; Bl., §48, 1, 2, 7), Mat.1:21, 12:50, Luk.6:35, al.; pointing to some one as master (cl.), Mat.8:24, Mrk.4:38, al.; αὐ., καὶ αὐ. = οὗτος, ὁ δε (BL, §48, 1), Mat.14:2, Mrk.14:15, 44, Luk.1:22, 2:28, al.
__2. In oblique cases (cl.), for the simple pron. of 3rd of person(s), he, she, it, Mat.7:9, 10:12, 26:44, al.; with ptcp. in genitive absol., Mat.9:18, Mrk.13:1, al. (for irreg. constructions, V. Bl., §74, 5); pleonastically after the relative (cf. Heb. אֲשֶׁר לוֹ; WM, 184ff.; Bl., §50, 4; MM, see word), Mrk.7:25, Rev.3:8, 7:2, al.; in constr. ad sensum, without proper subject expressly indicated, Mat.4:23, Act.8:5, 2Co.2:13, al.; genitive αὐτοῦ = ἐκείνου, Rom.11:11, 1Th.2:19, Tit.3:5, Heb.2:4.
__3. ὁ, ἡ, τὸ αὐ., the same: Heb.1:12, 13:8; τὸ αὐ., ποιεῖν, Mat.5:46, 47, al.; φρονεῖν, Rom.12:16, 15:5, Php.2:2, al.; τὰ αὐ., Act.15:27, Rom.2:1, al.; κατὰ τὸ (τὰ) αὐ. (MM, see word), Act.14:1, Luk.6:23, al.; ἐπὶ τὸ αὐ., together (MM, see word), Mat.22:34, Act.1:15, al.; ἓν κ. τὸ αὐ., 1Co.11:5, 12:11; with dative (cl.), 1Co.11:5; with a noun, λόγος, Mrk.14:39; μέτρος, Php.1:30; πνεῦμα, 1Co.12:4.
(AS)

τεῦς 3rd c.BC: Theocritus Poeta Bucolicus 2.126]]; τοι variant in [Refs [[prev. author] 7.25]]; enclitic τεος [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophron Comicus 83; Cretan dialect τέορ 5th c.AD(?): Hesychius Legal icographus]]; in 8th c.BC: Homerus Epicus]], Lesbian Lyric poetry, and Ionic dialect Lyric poetry and Prose τοι is always enclitic, σοί never enclitic (τοί and σοι are not found except σοι [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 3.359, 11.381, ς (οι) 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 1.170]], and in codices of [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “P.” 4.270, 9.55]]; rarer than τοι in [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus, 3.69, +others)]]; in Attic dialect both σοί and σοι (enclitic) are used (σοί [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Nubes” 361, etc., σοι [prev. work] 87, etc.)]], τοί and τοι are not used; in late Gr. σέν, [Refs [“Anatolian Studies” p.76]]; Doric dialect τέ [Refs 7th c.BC+ [7th c.BC: Alcman Lyricus 52, 5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “O.” 1.48, 3rd c.BC: Theocritus Poeta Bucolicus 1.5, 3rd c.BC: Callimachus Epicus “Fragmenta” 114]]; __2
in combination with γε, σύ γε, σέ γε, etc. (compare ἔγωγε), thou at least, for thy part, frequently in [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Homerus Epicus]] and Attic dialect; Doric dialect τύγε [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Epicharmus Comicus [272], 5th c.BC: Timocreon Lyricus 1 (variant{τύ γα}); τύγᾰ 3rd c.BC: Theocritus Poeta Bucolicus 5.69, 71]]; Boeotian dialect τούγα [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd c.AD: Apollonius Dyscolus Grammaticus “de Pronominibus;” 55.6]]: dative σοί γε [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 1.557]]: accusative σέ γε [Refs [10.96]], etc.:—also σύ περ [Refs [24.398.]]

__3
σύ with infinitive (as imperative), [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 3.134, 4.163.]]

__II
Dual nominative and accusative σφῶϊ, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 1.336, 4.286, +others]], you two, both of you; σφώ (not σφῴ,[Refs 8th c.BC+ [compare 2nd c.AD: Apollonius Dyscolus Grammaticus “de Pronominibus;” 85.17), 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 1.574, 11.782, 13.47, 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Coloneus” 344, 1543, etc.]]—Gen. and Dat. σφῶϊν, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 4.341, +others]]; contraction σφῷν once in [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Homerus Epicus, 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 4.62, and always in _Attic dialect_ (Hdn.Gr. 1.475) and Trag., e.g. 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Prometheus Vinctus” 12, 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Coloneus” 342, “OT” 1495, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Leges” 892e (codices 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus have σφῶϊν in “Tht.” 193c, +others, σφῶν “Euthd.” 273e, +others)]]. None of these forms are enclitic, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [2nd c.AD: Apollonius Dyscolus Grammaticus “de Pronominibus;” 38.9, 85.12; codex A of 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Leges” 658c, 673e, 689a wrongly makes σφῳν]] enclitic; Ζεὺς σφὼ is prescribed in [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 15.146 by Hdn.Gr. 2.93.]] —σφῶϊ is never dative; in [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 4.286]] it is the accusative depending on κελεύ; σφῶϊν is never accusative; in [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 23.52 it is dative commodi.]]

__III
Plur. nominative ὑμεῖς, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 2.75, +others (before a vowel, 4.246, 7.194, +others), 6th c.BC: Pherecydes Syrius Philosophus 11, 3rd c.AD: Democritus Epigrammaticus 29a, 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 3.72, etc.]], ye, you; Aeolic dialect and Epic dialect ὔμμες [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 1.274, +others, 7th-6th c.BC: Sappho Lyrica 24, 25]]; Doric dialect ὑμές [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophron Comicus 60, 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Acharnenses” 760, 761, 862; ὑμέν “SIG” 685.118 (Crete, 2nd c.BC), “GDI” 5155.6 ([prev. passage], 2nd c.BC)]]; Boeotian dialect οὐμές [Refs 6th c.BC+ [6th c.BC: Corinna Lyrica 6]]; a resolved form ὑμέες, [Refs 1st c.BC+ [1st c.BC: Parthenius Mythographus “fragment” 14, is a poeticlicence (so 2nd c.AD: Apollonius Dyscolus Grammaticus “de Pronominibus;” 93.3)]] rather than genuine Ionic [Refs 5th c.BC+ [(variant in 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 8.22).]]— Gen. ὑμῶν, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Acharnenses” 143, etc.]]; ὑμέων (disyllable) [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 7.159, 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 13.7, +others, 7th c.BC: Archilochus Lyricus 74.6 (ὑμῶν codices), 6th c.BC: Solon Lyricus 11.5 (variant{ὑμῶν})]]; ὑμέων also [Refs 8th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 3.73, 6.130, +others; as _trisyllable_, 3rd c.BC: Herodas Mimographus 2.27; ὑμείων 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 4.348, 7.195, +others]]; Doric dialect ὑμέων [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophron Comicus 46]]; also ὑμῶν, [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd c.AD: Apollonius Dyscolus Grammaticus “de Pronominibus;” 95.23]]; Aeolic dialect ὑμμέων [Refs 7th c.BC+ [7th-6th c.BC: Alcaeus Lyricus 96]]; Boeotian dialect οὐμίων [Refs 6th c.BC+ [6th c.BC: Corinna Lyrica 22.]]—Dat. ὑμῖν, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 2.46, 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.126, etc.]]; Ionic dialect enclitic ὗμῐν [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd c.AD: Apollonius Dyscolus Grammaticus “de Pronominibus;” 97.28,]] also Doric dialect, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophron Comicus 91]]; Doric dialect (not enclitic) ὑμίν [ῐ] [Refs [[prev. author] 92]]; ὑμίν [ῐ] also in [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Ajax” 864, 1242, “OT” 991, 1402, “Ant.” 308, “El.” 804, +others (but ὗμιν]] should perhaps be restored where the sense needs an enclitic on the principle stated by [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd c.AD: Apollonius Dyscolus Grammaticus “de Pronominibus;” 35.6, 36.5, “Synt.” 130.23)]]; ὕμιν[Refs 8th c.BC+ [(as _enclitic_) is prescribed by Hdn.Gr. (2.124) in 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 24.33, by “Etymologicum Magnum” 432.34 in 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 1.376, 2.141, etc.:—_Aeolic dialect_ and _Epic dialect_ ὔμμῐ, ὔμμῐν, 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 2.316, 11.336, +others, 8th-7th c.BC: Hesiodus Epicus “Scutum Herculis” 328, 7th-6th c.BC: Sappho Lyrica 14, 7th-6th c.BC: Alcaeus Lyricus “Supp.” 26.9, 5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “O.” 11(10).17.]]—Acc. ὑμᾶς, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Acharnenses” 325]], etc. (-υ [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.AD: Orphica “Argonautica” 820, variant in 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Philoctetes” 222]]; ὗμας or (more probably) ὕμας is required by the metre in [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd c.AD: Babrius Fabularum Scriptor 9.9, 47.11)]]; Ionic dialect ὑμέας (disyllable) [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 21.198, +others]]; enclitic ὕμεας (disyllable) [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [3rd c.BC: Herodas Mimographus 2.60 (Papyrus)]]; ὑμέας also [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.126, +others]]; Aeolic dialect and Epic dialect ὔμμε [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 23.412, +others, 5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “I.” 6(5).19; also in 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Eumenides” 620 (trimeter), and 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Antigone” 846 (Lyric poetry)]]; Doric dialect ὑμέ [Refs 7th c.BC+ [7th c.BC: Alcman Lyricus 3, 5th c.BC: Sophron Comicus 52, 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Acharnenses” 737, “Lys.” 1076, “SIG” 528.3 (Cretan dialogue, 3rd c.BC), 622 B 8 (Cretan, 2nd c.BC).]]—The plural is sometimes used in addressing one person, when others are included in the speaker's thought, as [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 12.81, 7th c.BC: Archilochus Lyricus 89. (With σύ]] cf. Latin tu, Gothic pu; with τοι Sanskrit genitive and dative te; the origin of σφῶϊ is doubtful; with ὑμεῖς cf. Sanskrit accusative plural yusmān.)

σοφία, -ας, ἡ
[in LXX chiefly for חׇכְמָה ;]
skill, intelligence, wisdom, ranging from knowledge of the arts and matters of daily life to mental excellence in its highest and fullest sense;
__(a) of human wisdom: 1Co.2:1 2:4-5, Jas.3:15, Rev.13:18 17:9; σ. Σολομῶνος, Mat.12:42, Luk.11:31; Αἰγυπτίων, Act.7:22; Ἕλληνες σ. ζητοῦσιν, 1Co.1:22; σ. λόγου, 1Co.1:17; τ. σοφῶν, 1Co.1:19 (LXX); τ. κόσμου, 1Co.1:20-21 3:19; ἀνθρωπίνη, 1Co.2:13; σαρκική, 2Co.1:12;
of wisdom in spiritual things: Luk.21:15, Act.6:3, 10 7:10, 1Co.2:6, Col.1:28 2:23 3:16 4:5, Jas.1:5 3:13, 17, 2Pe.3:15; λόγος σοφίας, 1Co.12:8; πνεῦμα σοφίας, Eph.1:17; σ. καὶ φρόνησις, Eph.1:8; σ. καὶ σύνεσις, Col.1:9;
__(b) of divine wisdom: of God, Rom.11:33, 1Co.1:21 1:24 2:7, Rev.7:12; πολυποίκιλος, Eph.3:10

σοφίζω
(σοφός), [in LXX chiefly for חָכָם ;]

σοφ-ίζω,
make wise, instruct, [LXX+NT [LXX.Psa.18(19).8; τινὰ εἰς σωτηρίαν NT.2Tim.3.15.]]

__2
passive, become or be clever or skilled in a thing, with genitive of things, ναυτιλίης σεσοφισμένος skilled in seamanship, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th-7th c.BC: Hesiodus Epicus “Opera et Dies” 649; Μοίσαι σεσοφισμέναι 6th c.BC: Ibycus Lyricus “POxy.” 1790.23]]; so ἐν τοῖς ὀνόμασι σ. [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Cynegeticus” 13.6]]: absolutely, to become or be wise, frequently in [LXX+1st c.AD+ [LXX, LXX.Eccl.7.24(23), +others; βέλτερος ἀλκήεντος ἔφυ σεσοφισμένος ἀνήρ 1st c.AD(?): Pseudo-Phocylidea 130.]]

__3
middle, teach oneself, learn, ἐσοφίσατο ὅτι.. he became aware that.., [LXX.1Ki.3.8.]

__II
middle σοφίζομαι, with aorist middle and perfect passive (see. below), practise an art, [Refs 6th c.BC+ [6th c.BC: Theognis Elegiacus 19, “IG” 12.678]]; play subtle tricks, deal subtly, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Iphigenia Aulidensis” 744, 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 18.227, etc.]]; οὐδὲν σοφιζόμεσθα τοῖσι δαίμοσι we use no subtleties in dealing with the gods, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Bacchae” 200]]; to be scientific, speculate, περὶ τὸ ὄνομα [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 509d, compare “Plt.” 299b, 1st c.AD: Musonius Philosophus “fragment” 3p.12H., etc.]]; σοφιζόμενος φάναι to say rationalistically, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Phaedrus” 229c]]; καίπερ οὕτω τούτου σεσοφισμένου though he has dealt thus craftily, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 29.28]]; σοφίσασθαι πρός τι to use fraud for an end, [Refs 2nd c.BC+ [2nd c.BC: Polybius Historicus 6.58.12]]; οἱ ἰητροὶ σοφιζόμενοι ἔστιν οἳ ἁμαρτάνουσι when they deal in subtleties, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Hippocrates Medicus “περὶ ἀγμῶν” 1]]; οἱ μυθικῶς σοφ. [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Metaphysica” 1000a18, compare “HA” 582a35, 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 35.56]]; σ. πρὸς τὸν νόμον evade it, [Refs 1st c.AD+ [1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus “Demosthenes” 27.]]

__II.2
with accusative of things, devise cleverly or skilfully, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 2.66, 8.27, compare 1.80; καινὰς ἰδέας σοφίζεσθαι 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Nubes” 547; χαρίεντα καὶ σοφά [prev. author] “Av.” 1401]]; ἀλλότρια σ. meddle with other men's craft, [Refs [[prev. author] “Eq.” 299]]; with internal accusative, ἀνόητα σ. exercise one's skill without νοῦς, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Hp.Ma.” 283a, compare 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Memorabilia” 1.2.46; ὅσα.. σοφίζονται πρὸς τὸν δῆμον 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Politica” 1297a14]]; ἀλλ᾽ αὐτὸ τοῦτο δεῖ σοφισθῆναι this is the very thing one must gain by craft, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Philoctetes” 77]]; οἶνον ἀπὸ τῶν φοινίκων σ. make spurious wine, [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd-3rd c.AD: Philostratus Sophista “Vita Apollonii” 2.6; πορφύραν παρὰ τῆς κόχλου [prev. author] “Her.” 19.15:]] —passive, σεσοφισμένοι μῦθοι craftily devised, [NT.2Pet.1.16.]

__II.2.b
σ. νόμον evade it, [Refs 1st c.BC+ [2nd-3rd c.AD: Philostratus Sophista “Vita Apollonii” 2.40, compare 2nd-3rd c.AD: Aelianus “Varia Historia” 2.41, 4th c.AD: Palaephatus Paradoxographus 50, “OGI” 383.208 (Commagene, 1st c.BC).]]

__II.3
with accusative person, deceive, τὸν Τίτον [Refs 1st c.AD+ [1st c.AD: Josephus Historicus “Bellum Judaicum” 4.2.3; μή με σοφίζου “Anthologia Graeca” 12.25 (Stat. Flacc.); τὸν δῆμον 2nd c.AD: Herodianus Grammaticus 7.10.7; also σ. τὴν αἴσθησιν 2nd c.AD: Aretaeus Medicus “περὶ αἰτιῶν καὶ σημείων χρονίων παθῶν” 1.15.]]

__II.4
'counter' by a device, σοφίζεται τὴν βίαν τοῦ μηχανήματος [Refs 1st c.AD+ [1st c.AD: Josephus Historicus “Bellum Judaicum” 3.7.20.]]

[Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Antigone” 1003, 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Pax” 498, etc.:]]future σπάσω [ᾰ] [Refs 5th c.BC+ [3rd c.BC: Lycophron Tragicus 484, (δια-) 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 7.236, (ἐπι-) 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Ajax” 769]]: aorist ἔσπᾰσα [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 13.178 (tmesis)]], Epic dialect σπάσα [Refs [5.859 (tmesis)]], etc.: perfect ἔσπᾰκα [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Problemata” 930a21, (ἀν-) 5th c.BC: Hippocrates Medicus “περὶ ἐπικυήσιος” 22, 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Acharnenses” 1069]]:—middle, future σπάσομαι [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Hippocrates Medicus “περὶ διαίτης” 2.38, etc.]]: aorist ἐσπᾰσάμην [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 19.387, 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 3.29, 2nd-3rd c.AD: Philostratus Sophista “Vita Apollonii” 7.42]], Epic dialect σπασάμην [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 10.166, _Epic dialect_ also σπάσσασθε, σπασσάμενος (see. below)]]:—passive, future σπασθήσομαι [Refs 5th c.BC+ [2nd c.AD: Galenus Medicus 16.760, (δια-) 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 4.8.10]]: aorist ἐσπάσθην [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 11.458, etc.]]: perfect ἔσπασμαι [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Hippocrates Medicus “περὶ νούσων” 1.20, (δι-) 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 6.98, etc.]]; also in middle sense, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 7.4.16, “Cyr.” 7.5.29. Mostly poetry (ἕλκω being preferred in Prose)]]:—draw, hence,

__I
of a sword, draw, mostly in middle, φάσγανά τε σπάσσασθε [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 22.74; σπασσάμενος.. ἄορ παχέος παρὰ μηροῦ 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 16.473; ἐκ δ᾽ ἄρα σύριγγος.. ἐσπάσατ᾽ ἔγχος 19.387; σπασαμένων τὰς μαχαίρας “PTeb.” 48.19 (2nd c.BC), compare 138 (2nd c.BC)]]: in active, ξίφος σπάσαντα [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Orestes” 1194; φάσγανον σπάσας χερί [prev. author] “IT” 322:]] —passive, ἐσπασμένοι τὰ ξίφη having their swords drawn, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 7.4.16; ἐσπασμένον ὃν εἶχεν ἀκινάκην [prev. author] “Cyr.” 7.5.29; ἐσπασμένοις τοῖς ξίφεσι 1st c.BC: Diodorus Siculus Historicus 4.52.]]

__I.2
of other things, ἐκ χειρὸς χεῖρα σπάσατο [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 2.321; σπασάμην ῥῶπάς τε λύγους τε 10.166]]; ὡς ἕκαστος ἔσπασεν τύχης πάλον drew the lot (out of the helmet), [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Agamemnon” 333:]] —passive, σπασθέντος (i.e. ἔγχεος ἔξω χροός) [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 11.458.]]

__I.3
absolutely, σπᾶτ᾽ ἀνδρείως pull, hoist away, like men, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Pax” 498.]]

__II
of violent actions, pluck off or out, κόμην [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Tyrannus” 1243; λάχνην [prev. author] “Tr.” 690]]; compare σπαστέος.

__II.2
tear, rend, especially of ravenous animals, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Antigone” 258, 1003]]; λαιμοτόμους κεφαλάς uncertain reading in [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Iphigenia Aulidensis” 776 (Lyric poetry)]]; σ. τοῖς ὄνυξιν [τοὺς νεοττούς], of the eagle, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Historia Animalium” 619b31:]] —passive, φλέβιον, σάρκα σπασθῆναι, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Hippocrates Medicus “περὶ νούσων” 1.17.]]

__II.3
wrench, sprain, τὸ σκέλος ἔσπασε [Refs 1st c.AD+ [1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus “Aratus” 33]]:—passive, τὸν μηρὸν σπασθῆναι [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 6.134; τοὺς πόδας 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Cyclops” 639.]]

__II.4
snatch, tear or drag away, πῶλον παρὰ συννόμων [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Leges” 666e; ὑπὸ πτερῶν 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Andromache” 441]]:—passive, ἔλαφον ἀπ᾽ ἐμῶν γονάτων σπασθεῖσαν [Refs [[prev. author] “Hec.” 92 (Lyric poetry); ἐκ βραχίονος σπασθείς [prev. work] 408.]]

__II.5
metaphorically, carry away, draw aside, ἀλλά σ᾽ ἔσπασεν πειθώ [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Electra” 561; τὰ πάθη οἷον νεῦρα σ. ἡμᾶς 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Leges” 644e.]]

__II.6
in Medicine texts, cause convulsion or spasm, variant in [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Hippocrates Medicus “περὶ ἄρθρων ἐμβολῆς” 67]]:—passive, to be convulsed, σπασθεὶς ἀποθνῄσκει [Refs 4th c.BC+ [[prev. author] “Aph.” 5.5, 4th-3rd c.BC: Theophrastus Philosophus “Historia Plantarum” 4.4.13, etc.]]; ἐσπᾶτο γὰρ πέδονδε καὶ μετάρσιος, of Heracles in his agony, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Trachiniae” 786, compare σπάσμα, σπασμός]]: metaphorically, to be harassed, anxious, [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd c.AD: Arrianus Historicus “Epicteti Dissertationes” 1.1.16.]]

__III
draw in, suck in, θρόμβον αἵματος [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Choephori” 533; ἔσπασεν ἄμυστιν ἑλκύσας 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Cyclops” 417]]; συνεκθανεῖν σπῶντα χρὴ τῷ πώματι[Refs 2nd c.AD+ [[prev. work] 571; μεστὴν ἀκράτου Θηρίκλειον ἔσπασεν 2nd c.AD: Alexander Rhetor 5, compare 285]]; opposed to λάπτω, κάπτω, [Refs 1st c.AD+ [1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus 2.699d, compare σπάσις 11]]; σ. τὸν μαστόν suck it, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Historia Animalium” 587a33; σ. ἀμυστί 2nd-3rd c.AD: Aelianus “De Natura Animalium - Ar.Byzantine Epit.” 6.51]]; and in middle, ταυρείου σπασάμενος αἵματος [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd c.AD: Apollodorus Damascenus Mechanicus 1.9.27]]:—passive, of the female, to be sucked, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Historia Animalium” 576b11 (τὸ ἄγαν σπᾶσθαι probable reading);compare ἕλκω 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus 11.4.]]

__III.2
σ. τὸ πνεῦμα draw breath, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [[prev. author] “Resp.” 473a2; τὸν ἀέρα τὸν κοινόν 4th-3rd c.BC: Menander Comicus 531.7]]; absorb, ἕκαστον τῶν τοῦ σώματος τὸ αὑτῷ οἰκεῖον ἐσπακέναι [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Problemata” 930a21.]]

__III.3
metaphorically, derive, τροφήν, of winds, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Hippocrates Medicus “περὶ διαίτης” 2.38; πειθώ τε καὶ εἵμερον ἔσπασε ἐκ..]]drew, derived.., [Refs [Inscriptiones Graecae 14.889 (from Sinuessa)]]; σ. ἔρωτα enjoy it, [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd-3rd c.AD: Oppianus Anazarbensis Epicus “Halieutica - Poetae Bucolici et Didactici” 4.270]]; ὀλίγον ὕπνου σ. snatch a little sleep, [Refs 3rd c.AD+ [3rd c.AD: Heliodorus Scriptor Eroticus 5.1]]:—middle, [Refs [[prev. author] 2.16.]]

__IV
draw tight, pull the reins, χαλινῷ τὸ στόμα τοῦ ἵππου [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “de Equitandi ratione” 9.7.1, compare 9.5; but τὸν χαλινὸν ἐκ τῶν ὀδόντων ἵππου 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Phaedrus” 254e.]]

of angling, ἡ μήρινθος οὐδὲν ἔσπασεν [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Thesmophoriazusae” 928: hence proverbial, οὐκ ἔσπασεν ταύτῃ γε]] 'he took nothing by his motion', [Refs [[prev. author] “V.” 175.]]

Aeolic dialect σπέρρω[Refs [Scholia 2nd c.BC: Dionysius Thrax Grammaticus p.117 H., “Etymologicum Magnum” 300.19]]: Ionic dialect imperfect σπείρεσκον [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 4.42]]: future σπερῶ [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Electra” 79, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Phaedrus” 276d]]; Aeolic dialect σπέρσω [Refs 5th c.BC+ [Scholia 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Hecuba” 202]]: aorist ἔσπειρα [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Septem contra Thebas” 754 (Lyric poetry), 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 7.107, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Timaeus” 41c]]: perfect ἔσπαρκα [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd c.AD: Polyaenus Historicus 2.1.1, etc.]]:—middle, aorist infinitive σπείρασθαι [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [3rd c.BC: Apollonius Rhodius Epicus 3.1028]]; aorist 2 σπαρέσθαι uncertain reading in [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd c.AD: Polyaenus Historicus 8.26]]:—passive, future σπᾰρήσομαι [LXX+1st c.BC+ [LXX.Nah.1.14, (δια-) 1st c.BC: Diodorus Siculus Historicus 17.69:]]aorist ἐσπάρην [ᾰ] [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Tyrannus” 1498, 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 2.27]]: perfect ἔσπαρμαι [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Hercules Furens” 1098, 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Ranae” 1206, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Leges” 693a, etc.]]:— sow,

__I
sow seed, with accusative, [κέγχρους] [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th-7th c.BC: Hesiodus Epicus “Scutum Herculis” 399; σῖτον 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 4.17; στάχυν 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Cyclops” 121]]; of Cadmus, σ. γηγενῆ στάχυν [Refs [[prev. author] “Ba.” 264]] (so in middle, σπείρασθαι ὀδόντας [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [3rd c.BC: Apollonius Rhodius Epicus 3.1028)]]: absolutely, sow, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th-7th c.BC: Hesiodus Epicus “Opera et Dies” 391]]; opposed to θερίζω, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Aves” 710, etc.: _metaphorically_, θερ. καὶ σ. ταῖς γλώσσαις, of corrupt orators, [prev. work] 1697 (Lyric poetry)]]; καρπὸν ὧν ἔσπειρε θερίζειν [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Phaedrus” 260d; αἰσχρῶς μὲν ἔσπειρας κακῶς δὲ ἐθέρισας 5th c.BC: Gorgias Rhetor et Sophista 16: proverbial, εἰς πέτρας τε καὶ λίθους σ. 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Leges” 838e]]; σ. κατὰ πετρῶν, i.e. εἰς πέλαγος [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [compare (σπέρμα 1.1), 2nd c.AD: Lucianus Sophista “Am.” 20.]]

__I.2
engender, beget offspring [Refs 5th c.BC+ [compare(11.2), 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Ajax” 1293, “Tr.” 33, 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Ion” 49, etc.]]; οἱ σπείραντες the parents, [Refs [Inscriptiones Graecae 3.1339, compare 14.1794 (from Rome)]]; ἄθυτα παλλακῶν σπέρματα σ. [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Leges” 841d]]:—passive, spring or be born, ὅθενπερ αὐτὸς ἐσπάρη [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Tyrannus” 1498, compare 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Ion” 554 (troch.), 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 460b]]; πρὸ τοῦ Ζήνωνα.. σπαρῆναι before Z. was begotten, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [1st c.BC: Philodemus Gadarensis Epigrammaticus “Rh.” 2.110 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus]]

__I.3
scatter like seed, strew, χρυσὸν καὶ ἄργυρον [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 7.107; σ. φλόγα “Tragica Adespota” 85]]; of liquids, scatter or sprinkle, ἐκ τευχέων σ. δρόσον [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Andromache” 167]]; spread abroad, extend, σ. ἀγλαΐαν νάς ῳ [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “N.” 1.13]]; spread rumour, σ. ματαίαν βάξιν [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Electra” 642]]; μὴ σπεῖρε πολλοῖς τὸν παρόντα δαίμονα do not speak of it indiscriminately, [Refs [[prev. author] “fragment” 653]]:—passive, to be scattered or dispersed, ἐσπαρμένος κατὰ.. πόλιν, of the ashes of Solon scattered over Salamis, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Cratinus Comicus 228; τόξα δ᾽ ἔσπαρται πέδῳ 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Hercules Furens” 1098]]; of persons, ἐσπάρησαν καθ᾽ Ἑλλάδα [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 2.27; ἐσπαρμένοι εἰς ἁρπαγήν 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Historia Graeca (Hellenica)” 3.4.22]]; κατὰ χώραν[Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. work] 6.2.17; ἔσπαρται λόγος 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Fragmenta” 846 cited in 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Ranae” 1206.]]

__II
sow a field, νειόν [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th-7th c.BC: Hesiodus Epicus “Opera et Dies” 463]]; γῆν, τέμενος, πεδιάδα, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 4.42, 9.116, 122; ἄρουραν 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Fragmenta - American Journal of Philology” 158]]; ἡ σπειρομένη Αἴγυπτος the arable part of Egypt, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 2.77; τυχεῖν μὲν ἤδη 'σπαρμένα 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Pax” 1140; ἀροῦται καὶ σπείρεται τὸ Θηβαίων ἄστυ 4th-3rd c.BC: Dinarchus Orator 1.24: proverbial, πόντον σπείρειν]], of lost labour, [Refs 6th c.BC+ [6th c.BC: Theognis Elegiacus 106, 107: _metaphorically_, καινοτάταις σ. διανοίαις 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Vespae” 1044; σ. εἰς ἀρετῆς ἔκφυσιν 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Leges” 777e; τοὺς ἐν γράμμασι κήπους [prev. author] “Phdr.” 276d.]]

__II.2
of procreation, ματρὸς.. σ. ἄρουραν [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Septem contra Thebas” 754; σ. τέκνων ἄλοκα 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Phoenissae” 18; σ. λέχη [prev. author] “Ion” 64]]; ἣν ἔσπειρε, i.e. his wife, [Refs 4th c.AD+ [4th c.AD: Libanius Sophista “Orationes” 37.9; see above 1.2.]]

to pour out as a drink-offering, make a libation; pass., figuratively, σπένδομαι, I am poured out or offered as a libation (in the shedding of my life-blood): Php.2:17 (see Lft., in l), 2Ti.4:6 (for exx. from π., see Milligan, Selections, 114 f.; MM, xxiii).†

LSJ / STEPBible (TFLSJ)
σπένδω,
[Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 11.775, etc.]]; Epic dialect subjunctive 2nd pers. singular σπένδῃσθα [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 4.591]]: Ionic dialect imperfect σπένδεσκον [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 16.227, 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 7.138]]: future σπείσω [LXX+5th c.BC+ [LXX.Num.28.7, (κατα-) 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 2.151, 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Orestes” 1187]]: aorist ἔσπεισα [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 13.55, 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Fragmenta” 42, etc.]]; Epic dialect σπεῖσα [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 9.177, σπείσασκε 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 8.89]]; Epic dialect subjunctive σπείσομεν, for -ωμεν, [Refs [7.165, 181]]: perfect ἔσπεικα [Refs 1st c.AD+ [(κατ-) 1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus “Sertorius” 14]]:—middle, aorist ἐσπεισάμην [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 3.144, etc.]]:—passive, aorist ἐσπείσθην [Refs 1st c.AD+ [1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus “Romulus” 19:]]perfect ἔσπεισμαι, see below [Refs [11]] near the end:—make a drink-offering (because before drinking wine a portion was poured on the table, hearth, or altar), σπεῖσάν τ᾽ ἔπιόν θ᾽ ὅσον ἤθελε θυμός [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 9.177; ἐπὴν σπείσῃς τε καὶ εὔξεαι 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 3.45, compare 6th c.BC: Xenophanes Poeta Philosophus 1.15, 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Philoctetes” 1033, 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Bacchae” 313, etc.]]: with dative of the god to whom the libation was made, σέπας ἑλὼν σπείσασκε θεοῖσιν [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 8.89; ὡς σπείσῃς Διὶ πατρὶ καὶ ἄλλοις ἀθανάτοισι 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 6.259, compare 16.227, 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 3.334, etc.]]; τὴν (i.e. κύλικα) δὲ θεοῖς σπένδεις [Refs 6th c.BC+ [6th c.BC: Theognis Elegiacus 490]]; κρητῆρας σπενδέτω probably let him dedicate them by pouring an offering from them, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [“SIG” 57.13 (Milet., 5th c.BC):]] —the liquid poured is mostly in _accusative_, σ. οἶνον pour wine, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 11.775, 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 18.151; λοιβάς 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Electra” 270]]; σπονδάς, χοάς, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Electra” 512, “Or.” 1322]]; elliptically, σ. ἀγαθοῦ δαίμονος (i.e. σπονδήν) [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Equites” 106]]; σ. οἴνου (partitive genitive) [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd c.AD: Herodianus Grammaticus 5.5.7:]] rarely with dative _of things_, ὕδατι σ. make a drink-offering with water, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 12.363]]; Ὀλυμπίῳ σ. ἀοιδαῖς make libations with songs to Zeus, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “I.” 6(5).9: also with _dative_ instrumenti, σ. δέπαϊ, δεπάεσσι, 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 23.196, 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 7.137; χρυσίδι 5th c.BC: Cratinus Comicus 124; χαλκέῃ φιάλῃ 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 2.147; ἐκ χρυσέης φιάλης [prev. author] 7.54: with _genitive_, σ. βαιᾶς κύλικος 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Fragmenta” 42]]:—passive, οὗτος θεοῖσι σπένδεται θεὸς γεγώς [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Bacchae” 284: so _metaphorically_ of a person, σπένδομαι ἐπὶ τῇ θυσίᾳ]] I am offered (as a drink-offering) upon it, [NT.Phil.2.17, cf. NT.2Tim.4.6.]

__2
rarely without the religious sense, simply pour, τράγου οὖρον, as remedy for convulsions, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 4.187: _metaphorically_, σ. δάκρυα “Anthologia Graeca” 7.555b (Joann.), “IG” 14.1957, +others]]; ξίφος αἷμα τυράννων ἔσπ. [Refs [“Anthologia Graeca” 9.184.]]

__II
middle, pour libations one with another, and, as this was the custom in making treaties or agreements, make a treaty, make peace, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 3.144, 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Acharnenses” 199, “Av.” 1534, 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 4.99, 119, 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 1.9.7, etc.; τὰ μὲν σπενδόμενοι τὰ δὲ πολεμοῦντες 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 1.18:]] — Constr., σπένδεσθαί τινι make peace with one, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Acharnenses” 225, 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 5.5, etc.; in full, σπένδεσθαί τινι σπονδάς [prev. work] 14 (but σ. τῇ πρεσβείᾳ]] give it pledges of safe conduct, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aeschines Orator 3.63, compare 2.109]]; so σ. τινί obtain a truce for one, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 2.3.7)]]; σ. πρός τινας, for τισι, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 5.17, 30, 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 3.5.16]]; of a person, σπείσασθαι cum Bruto et Cassio, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [1st c.BC: Cicero, M. Tullius Orator et Philosophus “Epistulae ad Atticum” 15.29.2: _metaphorically_, σ. συμφοραῖς καὶ θεσπίσμασιν 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Orestes” 1680 {σπέος}]]; σ. ἐπὶ τοῖσδε on these terms, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. author] “Ph.” 1240; ἐφ᾽ ᾧ.. 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 4.4.6; also σ. ὥστε μὴ ἀδικεῖν 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 6.7; σ. ἦ μὴν ἐμμενεῖν ἐν ταῖς σπονδαῖς [prev. author] 4.118]]: with infinitive alone, [Refs [[prev. author] 7.83: less frequently with _accusative_, εἰρήνην σπεισάμενοι Λακεδαιμονίοισι]] having concluded a peace with them, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 7.148]]; νεῖκος ἐσπεῖσθαι make up a quarrel, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Medea” 1140; πόλεμον 1st c.BC: Dionysius Halicarnassensis 9.36]]; σ. ἀναίρεσιν τοῖς νεκροῖς obtain a truce for taking up the dead, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 3.24; σ. σφίσιν ἡμέραν τοὺς νεκροὺς ἀνελέσθαι [prev. author] 4.114; σ. ἀναχώρησίν τινι [prev. author] 3.109; σ. περὶ τῶν τέκνων 1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus 2.494d:]] —perfect ἔσπεισμαι is used in middle sense in [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Med.” [same place]; τοῖς ἐχθροῖς ἐσπείσμην 2nd c.AD: Lucianus Sophista “Phal.” 1.3]]; but in passive sense, ἐσπεῖσθαι τὰς σπονδάς [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 4.16; οἷς ἔσπειστο [prev. author] 3.111]]: aorist, ἐσπείσθησαν ἀνοχαί [Refs 5th c.BC+ [1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus “Romulus” 19. (In 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 4.98, τοὺς νεκροὺς σπένδουσιν ἀναιρεῖσθαι]], emphasis is laid on the act of one of the parties, and in [Refs 1st c.AD+ [“Anthologia Graeca” 9.422 (1st c.AD: Apollonides Epigrammaticus), σπεῖσαι δεύτερα φίλτρα γάμου, Reiske conjecture σπεύσῃς.)]] (Cf. Hittite š (i) pand- 'pour a libation', Latin spondeo.)

(σπείρω) [in LXX chiefly for זֶרַע ;]

__(a) of plants: Mat.13:24, 27 13:37-38, 2Co.9:10; pl., Mat.13:32, Mrk.4:31, 1Co.15:33; metaphorically, of an escaping remnant (שָׂרִיד, Isa.1:9; cf. Wis.14:6; Plat., Tim., 23c; FlJ, Ant., xi, 5, 3), Rom.9:29;

(as frequently in poets), seed, offspring, posterity: Mat.22:24-25, Mrk.12:19-22, Luk.1:55 20:28" (LXX) Jhn.7:42 8:33, 37 Act.3:25 7:5-6 13:23, Rom.1:3 4:13, 18 9:7-8 11:1, 2Co.11:22, Gal.3:16, 19, 2Ti.2:8, Heb.2:16 11:18; pl. (FlJ, Ant., viii, 7, 6; Flat., Leg., ix, 853 with; 4Ma.18:1; in Ga, l.with, contrasted with sing., see Lft., in l; Milligan, NTD, 105 f.), Gal.3:16; of spiritual offspring, Rom.4:16, 18 9:8, Gal.3:29, Rev.12:17.†

LSJ / STEPBible (TFLSJ)
σπέρμ-α, ατος, τό,
(σπείρω) seed, only once in [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Homerus Epicus, in _metaphorically_ sense, see below 1.2:]]

__I
mostly, seed of plants, σ. ἀνιέναι, κρύπτειν, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [“hymnus ad Cererem” 307, compare 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 3.97: _plural_, 8th-7th c.BC: Hesiodus Epicus “Opera et Dies” 446]]; σ. τῇ γῇ διδόναι, ἐμβαλεῖν, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Oeconomicus” 17.8, 10: proverbial, εἰς πέλαγος σ. βαλεῖν “epigram Gr.” 1038.8 (from Pamphylia)]]; of fruit, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Antiphanes Comicus 58.4]]; τοῖς γαίης σπέρμασι with the products of earth, of corn-stalks, [Refs 1st c.AD+ [“Anthologia Graeca” 9.89 (1st c.AD: Philippus Epigrammaticus).]]

__I.2
metaphorically, germ, origin of anything, σ. πυρός [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 5.490; φλογός 5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “O.” 7.48, compare “P.” 3.37]]; σπέρματα, ={στοιχεῖα}, elements, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Anaxagoras Philosophus 4, compare 4th-3rd c.BC: Epicurus Philosophus]]Ep.2p.38 U., [Refs 4th c.BC+ [“fragment” 250; ὁ τὸ σπέρμα παρασχών, οὗτος τῶν φύντων αἴτιος 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 18.159; συκοφάντου σ. καὶ ῥίζαν οἴεται δεῖν ὑπάρχειν τῇ πόλει [prev. author] 25.48; σ. τῆς στάσεως 1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus “Marius” 10; τοῦ ὅρκου 3rd c.AD: Longinus Rhetor 16.3.]]

__I.3
seed-time, sowing, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th-7th c.BC: Hesiodus Epicus “Opera et Dies” 781.]]

__II
of animals, seed, semen, φέροισα σ. θεοῦ pregnant by the god, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “P.” 3.15]]; but σ. φέρειν Ἡρακλέους to be pregnant of Heracles, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. author] “N.” 10.17; μυελὸν.. εἰς σ. καὶ γόνον μερίζεσθαι 5th-4th c.BC: Timaeus Locrus Philosophus 100b, compare 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Timaeus” 86c; σ. παραλαβεῖν 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Orestes” 553; σπέρματος πλῆσαι 1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus “Lycurgus” 15: _plural_, κατ᾽ ἀμφότερα τὰ σ. θεῶν ἀπόγονος 5th c.BC: Hippocrates Medicus “ἐπιστολαί” 2.]]

__II.2
race, origin, descent, τοὐμὸν.. σπέρμ᾽ ἰδεῖν βουλήσομαι [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Tyrannus” 1077]]; τίνος εἶ σπέρματος πατρόθε; [Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. author] “OC” 214 (Lyric poetry); γένεθλον σπέρμα τ᾽ Ἀργεῖον 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Supplices” 290, compare “Ch.” 236; σ. ἄντασ᾽ Ἐρεχθειδᾶν 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Antigone” 981 (Lyric poetry), compare 5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “O.” 7.93, etc.]]

σπλάγχνον, τό,

__2
any part of the inwards, ὑπὸ σπλάγχνων ἐλθεῖν to come from the womb, of a babe, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “O.” 6.43, compare “N.” 1.35; τῶν σῶν.. ἐκ σπλάγχνων ἕνα 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Antigone” 1066; μητρὸς ἐν σπλάγχνοις “IG” 14.1977]]: so in singular, τὸ κοινὸν σ. οὗ πεφύκαμεν [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Septem contra Thebas” 1036]]; of the lungs, μόχθοις ἀνδροκμῆσι φυσιᾷ σ. [Refs [[prev. author] “Eu.” 249]]; τοῦ γείτονος αὐτῷ (i.e. τῷ ἥπατι) σπλάγχνου, of the spleen, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Timaeus” 72c.]]

__3
οἱ παῖδες (children) σπλάγχνα λέγονται [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd c.AD: Artemidorus Daldianus Onirocriticus 1.44, compare 5.57.]]

__II
metaphorically (like heart), the seat of the feelings, affections, especially of anger, σ. θερμῆναι κότῳ [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Ranae” 844]]; τὰ σ. ἀγανακτεῖ[Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. work] 1006; μομφὰς ὑπὸ σπλάγχνοις ἔχειν 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Alcestis” 1009: generally, of anxiety, 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Agamemnon” 995 (Lyric poetry); σπλάγχνα δέ μου κελαινοῦται [prev. author] “Ch.” 413 (Lyric poetry)]]; of love, ἐκύμηνε τὰ σ. ἔρωτι καρδίην ἀνοιστρηθείς [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [3rd c.BC: Herodas Mimographus 1.56; παιδὸς ὑπὸ σπλάγχνοισιν ἔχει πόθον 3rd c.BC: Theocritus Poeta Bucolicus 7.99, compare 1st c.BC: Dionysius Halicarnassensis 11.35, “Anthologia Graeca” 5.55 (3rd c.BC: Dioscorides Epigrammaticus)]], etc.; of pity, [LXX+NT [LXX.Pro.12.10, NT.Phil.1.8, 2.1, etc.]]; ὑπὲρ σπλάχνου 'for pity's sake', [Refs 1st c.BC+ [“BGU” 1139.17 (1st c.BC)]]; so [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Ajax” 995, 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Orestes” 1201, “Hipp.” 118]]; ἀνδρὸς σ. ἐκμαθεῖν to learn a man's 'heart', [Refs 4th c.BC+ [[prev. author] “Med.” 220; ἀνδρὸς πονηροῦ σ. οὐ μαλάσσεται 4th-3rd c.BC: Menander Comicus “Μονόστιχοι - Fragmenta Comicorum Graecorum” 31]]; σ. σιδηροῦν, of Epaminondas, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-3rd c.BC: Epicurus Philosophus “Fragmenta” 560.]]
