στέγω
(cf. Lat. tego), [in LXX: Sir.8:17 * ;]
__1. prop., to cover closely, to protect by covering, esp. to keep water in or out (Soph., Plat., al.).
__2. to cover, keep secret, conceal (Sir, l.with, Polyb., al.): 1Co.13:7, R, mg.
__3. By covering to ward of, bear up under, endure (for exx., see, Lft., Notes, 40; M, Th., 36): 1Co.9:12 13:7, 1Th.3:1 3:5.†
(AS)

---

LSJ / STEPBible (TFLSJ)
στέγω,
used by early writers mainly in present and imperfect: future στέξω uncertain conjecture in [Refs 1st c.BC+ [1st c.BC: Diodorus Siculus Historicus 11.29]]: aorist ἔστεξα [Refs 2nd c.BC+ [2nd c.BC: Polybius Historicus 8.12.5, 1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus “Alexander” 35, etc.:]] —middle, aorist ἐστέξατο conjecture for ἐδέξατο in [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [“Anthologia Graeca” 13.27 (3rd c.BC: Phalaecus Epigrammaticus)]]:— passive, aorist ἐστέχθην [Refs 4th c.BC+ [6th c.AD: Simplicius Philosophus “in Epictetum commentaria” p.117 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator]]:—cover closely, so as to keep a fluid either out or in, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Timaeus” 78a (of fire):]]

__A
keep out water, δόμος ἅλα στέγων a house that keeps out the sea, i.e. a good ship, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Supplices” 135 (Lyric poetry): _absolutely_, νῆες οὐδὲν στέγουσαι]] not water-tight, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 2.94; εὐνὰς τοιαύτας οἵας.. στέγειν.. ἱκανὰς εἶναι 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 415e, compare “Ti.” 45c, “Cra.” 412d]]; τῇ.. στεγούσῃ γῇ in the impervious earth, [Refs [[prev. author] “Criti.” 111d]]; συμμύει καὶ στέγει, of timber, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th-3rd c.BC: Theophrastus Philosophus “Historia Plantarum” 5.7.4, compare 5.4.5; οἰκία στέγουσα “IG” 22.2498.23, compare 12(5).568.12 (Ceos, 5th-4th c.BC):]] —so in middle, στέγετο.. ὄμβρους kept off the rain from himself, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “P.” 4.81]]; νεῦς οὐκ ἐστέξατο κῦμα [Refs [“Anthologia Graeca” [prev. cited] (see. above); ταῦτα δὲ παρέξοντι οἰκοδομημένα καὶ στεγόμενα καὶ τεθυρωμένα “Tab.Heracl.” 1.142.]]

__2
of other things, fend off, repel, οὔτε οἱ πῖλοι ἔστεγον τὰ τοξεύματα [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 4.34; δόρυ πολέμιον στέγειν 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Septem contra Thebas” 216]]; στέγων γὰρ ἐχθροὺς θάνατον εἵλετ᾽[Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. work] 1014; σ. τὰς πληγάς 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Vespae” 1295; στέγει ἡ σὰρξ τὸ προσπῖπτον θερμόν 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Problemata” 889a11.]]

__3

[NT.1Cor.13.7, compare 9.12]: absolutely, contain oneself, hold out, στέγειν, καρτερεῖν [NT+5th c.BC+ [“Lyrica Alexandrina Adespota” 1.30, cf. __B

__B.II
generally, contain, hold, ἄγγος σῶμα τοὐκείνου σ. [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Electra” 1118, compare 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Ion” 1412; ὄχλον σ. δῶμα [prev. author] “Hipp.” 843.]]

__B.III
shelter, protect, πύργοι πόλιν στέγουσιν [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Coloneus” 15 codices, compare 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Septem contra Thebas” 797: _metaphorically_, ὅρκος σ. τὴν ὁμόνοιαν αὐτῶν 1st c.BC: Diodorus Siculus Historicus 11.29 (conjecture)]]; τὸ ξύλον ἔστεξεν ἡ γῆ retained and cherished it, so that it struck root, [Refs 1st c.AD+ [1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus “Romulus” 20, compare “Alex.” 35.]]

__B.III.2
conceal, keep hidden, κακόν τι κεύθεις καὶ στέγεις ὑπὸ σκότῳ [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Phoenissae” 1214; ἥξει.., κἂν ἐγὼ σιγῇ στέγω 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Tyrannus” 341]]; τί χρὴ στέγειν ἢ τί λέγει; [Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. author] “Ph.” 136 (Lyric poetry); τὸ γὰρ γυναιξὶν αἰσχρὸν σὺν γυναῖκα χρὴ στέγειν [prev. author] “fragment” 679; σ. τἀμὰ καὶ σ᾽ ἔπη 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Electra” 273; στέξαι τὸ κριθέν 2nd c.BC: Polybius Historicus 4.8.2]]:—passive, to be kept secret, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 6.72]]; παρ᾽ ὑμῶν εὖ στεγοίμεθ᾽ let my counsel be kept secret by you, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Trachiniae” 596.]]

__B.IV

[Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Simonides Lyricus 98; σ. εὐκλείας μέγας 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Ajax” 465, compare 5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “P.” 1. 100, 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Supplices” 315; μέγας γάρ σοι ὁ σ. ἐστιν ὑπὸ πάντων εὐλογεῖσθαι “PSI” 4.405.4 (3rd c.BC)]]; σ. ζωῆς, δόξης, [NT.Jam.1.12, NT.1Pet.5.4]; ὁ τῆς δικαιοσύνης σ. [NT+8th c.BC+ [NT.2Tim.4.8. ἀνδρὸς στέφανος παῖδες 8th c.BC: Homerus Epicus “Epigrammata” 13, compare 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Iphigenia Aulidensis” 194 (Lyric poetry), NT.1Thes.2.19.]]

__II.4
crown as a badge of office, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 21.32; πέπαυνται ἄρχοντες καὶ τοὺς σ. περιῄρηνται [prev. author] 26.5; ὁ βασιλεὺς ὅταν δικάζῃ περιαιρεῖται τὸν σ. 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Ἀθηναίων Πολιτεία” 57.4]]; ὁ σ. οὗτος, of the office of ἀρχιερεὺς Ἀσίας, [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd-3rd c.AD: Philostratus Sophista “Vitae Sophistarum” 1.21.2, compare “OGI” 470.21 (Asia Minor), 4th c.AD: Libanius Sophista “Orationes” 53.4]]; ἔχειν τὸν σ. to be in office, [Refs 2nd c.BC+ [“SIG” 1007.22 (Pergam., 2nd c.BC); ἡ ἀπόθεσις τῶν σ. [prev. work]900.16 (Panamara, 4th c.AD)]]; ἀναδήσασθαι τὸν σ. τοῦτον [Refs 3rd c.AD+ [“POxy.” 1252v. 20 (3rd c.AD)]]: see at {στεφανηφόρος} [Refs [11, στεφανόω 11.5.]]

__II.5
in Egypt, money gift to the sovereign, levied by the state, [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [PTeb. 746.24 (3rd c.BC), “PSI” 4.388.5 (3rd c.BC), “PCair.Zen.” 36.27 (3rd c.BC), etc.]]; like wise in Syria, [LXX.1Mac.10.20]; also of similar gifts to a court favourite, [Refs 2nd c.BC+ [“PFay.” 14 (2nd c.BC),compare “Ostr.Bodl.” i202 (2nd c.BC).]]

τὰς εἰς τὸν σ. ἐπαγγελίας οὐκ ἔλαβον,= aurum coronarium non accepi, Mon.Anc.[Refs 3rd c.AD+ [11.22,compare “PFay.” 20.7 (3rd-4th c.AD).]]

donation, euphemism for a bribe, διεθέντος μου ὑπάρξει σοι εἰς σ. τάλαντα δεκαπέντε [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [“PGrenf.” 1.41.2 (2nd c.BC),compare “OGI” 221.6 (Ilium, 3rd c.BC), “PGoodsp.Cair.” 5.5 (2nd c.BC)]]; gratuity, bonus, [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [PFlor. 74.14 (2nd c.AD).]]

the constellation [Refs 6th c.BC+ [“Corona”, 6th c.BC: Epimenides Philosophus 25, 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Meteorologica” 362b10, 4th-3rd c.BC: Aratus Epicus 71, “PHib.” 1.27.58, 187 (3rd c.BC)]]; σ. τόν τε κλείουσ᾽ Ἀριάδνης [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [3rd c.BC: Apollonius Rhodius Epicus 3.1003.]]

LSJ / STEPBible (TFLSJ)
στεφᾰν-όω,
middle, Syracusan 2nd pers. singular imperative στεφάνουσο [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [Scholia 3rd c.BC: Theocritus Poeta Bucolicus 11.42]]:—passive, future -ώσομαι[Refs 1st c.AD+ [2nd c.AD: Aristides Rhetor 1.496 1st c.AD: Josephus Historicus]]; -ωθήσομαι [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aeschines Orator 3.20, +others, “PCair.Zen.” 60.7 (3rd c.BC):]]

__I
used by [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Homerus Epicus and 8th-7th c.BC: Hesiodus Epicus]] only in passive, to be put round in a circle or as a rim or border, and hence to be put round, ἣν περὶ μὲν πάντῃ Φόβος ἐστεφάνωται round about the aegis is Terror wreathed, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 5.739; τῇ δ᾽ ἐπὶ μὲν Γοργὼ ἐστεφάνωτο 11.36]]; ἀμφὶ δέ μιν θυόεν νέφος ἐστεφάνωτο all round about him was a cloud, [Refs [15.153]]; νῆσον, τὴν πέρι πόντος ἐστεφάνωται the sea lies round about the island, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 10.195: rarely with _accusative_, τείρεα, τά τ᾽ οὐρανὸς ἐστεφάνωται]] constellations which heaven has all round it, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 18.485, compare 8th-7th c.BC: Hesiodus Epicus “Theogonia” 382, “IG” 42(1).129.9 (Epid.)]]; of a crowd of spectators surrounding a dancing-floor, ἀμφὶ δ᾽ ὅμιλος ἀπείριτος ἐστεφάνωτο [Refs [“hymnus ad Venerem” 120]]; περὶ δ᾽ ὄλβος ἀπείριτος ἐστεφάνωτο around were.. riches in a circle placed, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th-7th c.BC: Hesiodus Epicus “Scutum Herculis” 204]]: so in later Epic dialect, [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [3rd c.BC: Apollonius Rhodius Epicus 3.1214, 4th c.AD(?): Quintus Smyrnaeus Epicus 5.99, 5th-6th c.AD: Orphica “Argonautica” 45, etc.: also in]]active, περίτροχον ἐστεφάνωσαν αἱμασιήν made a fence round, [Refs 3rd c.AD+ [3rd c.AD: Oppianus Apamensis Epicus “Cynegetica” 4.90.]]

__I.2
to be surrounded, ἐστεφανωμένος τιάραν μυρσίνῃ having his tiara wreathed with myrtle, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.132]]; πεδία ἐστεφάνωται ὄρεσιν are surrounded by.. , [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Hippocrates Medicus “Aër.” 19; ὅπλοισιν πόλις epigram cited in 2nd c.AD: Pausanias Periegeta 9.15.6; χθὼν ἅτε νῆσος -ωται 2nd c.AD: Dionysius Periegeta 4]]: so in active, [Βαβυλῶνα] τείχεσιν ἐστεφάνωσεν [Refs [[prev. author] 1006.]]

__II
after [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Homerus Epicus]] in active, crown, wreathe, χαίταν [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “O.” 14.24]]; Ὀρέστην σ. [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Orestes” 924; κρᾶτα κισσίνοις βλαστήμασιν [prev. author] “Ba.” 177; στεφάνοις [prev. work] 101 (Lyric poetry)]]; with genitive, πίτυος [Refs 5th c.BC+ [3rd c.AD(?): Longus Scriptor Eroticus 2.31; σ. τινὰ ὡς σωτῆρα 5th-6th c.BC: Andocides Orator 1.45; τὸν νικῶντα θαλλῷ 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Leges” 946b; νῖκαι σ. τινά 5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “N.” 11.21]]; of crowning a corpse, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Ecclesiazusae” 538; a tomb, “IG” 12.1037, “Sammelb.” 7457.10 (3rd-2nd c.BC), 2nd c.AD: Lucianus Sophista “Cont.” 22, “PLips.” 30.2 (3rd c.AD)]]; ships, [Refs 1st c.AD+ [1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus 2.981e]]; of the nuptial crown, [LXX.Cant.3.11]; κατηρῶντο τοῖς ἐστεφανωμένοις newly wedded couples, [Refs 4th c.AD+ [4th c.AD: Libanius Sophista “Orationes” 33.29]]; στεφανοῦν εὐαγγέλια crown one for good tidings, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Equites” 647]]; στεφανοῦσα, title of a statue by Praxiteles (see. στέφω [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [111), compare 2nd c.AD: Athenaeus Epigrammaticus 12.534d]]:—passive, to be crowned or rewarded with a crown, [NT+5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 7.55, 8.59, “PCair.Zen.” [same place], NT.2Tim.2.5; ἐλαίᾳ 5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “O.” 4.13; ποίᾳ [prev. author] “P.” 8.19; φυτὸν στεφανούμενος 3rd c.AD(?): Achilles Tatius Astronomus 1.5; σ. καὶ ἀνακηρύττεσθαι 5th-6th c.BC: Andocides Orator 2.18]]:—middle, crown oneself, στεφανωσαμένη δρυῒ καὶ.. σπείραισι δρακόντων [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Fragmenta” 535 (_anapaest meter_); στεφανοῦσθε κισσῷ 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Bacchae” 106 (Lyric poetry); στεφανωσάμενος καλάμῳ 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Nubes” 1006]]; στεφανωσάμενος αὐτόν (i.e. τὸν στέφανον) [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [3rd-2nd c.BC: Phalaris Epistolographus “Epistulae - Epistolographi” 40; στεφανοῦνται τῶν ἀνθέων 2nd-3rd c.AD: Philostratus Sophista “Heroicus” 12a. 2; τῆς πίτυος 1st-2nd c.AD: Dio Chrysostomus Sophista 9.10]]: also absolutely, of one going to sacrifice, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 4.80; τῷ θεῷ 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Historia Graeca (Hellenica)” 4.3.21]]; at a festival, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Acharnenses” 1145, 4th-3rd c.BC: Menander Comicus 518.15, etc.]]; win a crown, of the victor at the games, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “O.” 7.15, 81, 12.17, “N.” 6.19]]:—passive, with double accusative, ἐστεφανώθη Ἐλεύθερος.. Ἁδριάνεια πάλην [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [“IG” 22.2087.64 (2nd c.AD).]]

__II.2
crown as an honour or reward [Refs 4th c.BC+ [compare (στέφανος 11.2b), 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 19.193, 4th c.BC: Theopompus Historicus 239, 4th-3rd c.BC: Menander Comicus 84, “IG” 22.212.30 (4th c.BC), etc.]]; reward by a gift of money, etc. [Refs 4th c.BC+ [compare (στέφανος 11.5), Καλλισθένην ἑκατὸν μναῖς 4th c.BC: Lycurgus Orator “fragment” 19, compare 1st c.BC: Diodorus Siculus Historicus 14.53, 1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus “Timoleon” 16; σ. τινὰ πεντακοσίοις ἀργυρίου ταλάντοις, χιλίοις δὲ λιβανωτοῦ 2nd c.BC: Polybius Historicus 13.9.5: also ἐστεφανωκότος.. τὰς δυνάμεις χρυσῶν μυριάδων τριάκοντα]] Gauthier et Sottas Décret trilingue en l' honneur de Ptolémée IV [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [p.67 (3rd c.BC).]]

__II.3
metaphorically, confer glory upon, decorate, honour, τινὰ μολπᾷ [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “O.” 1.100; τοὺς πρεσβυτέρους ἤθεσι χρηστοῖς 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Nubes” 959]]; ἀπὸ τῶν ὑπαρχόντων τὴν πόλιν (by a victory in the games) [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Andocides Orator 4.26; Ἑλλάδα 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Troades” 1030, compare 5th c.BC: Critias Philosophus, Tragicus, Elegiacus 4 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator; ἔργοις γένος “TAM” 1.44 (from Xanthus)]]; [τὸ ῥόδον] ἐγκωμίῳ [Refs 1st c.BC+ [2nd-3rd c.AD: Philostratus Sophista “Epistulae” 51; ἀριστείοις 1st c.BC: Diodorus Siculus Historicus 4.32; πανοπλίᾳ [prev. author] 20.84]]:—passive, σοφίας ἀριστεῖα ἐστεφανοῦτο [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd-3rd c.AD: Philostratus Sophista “Heroicus” 10.4.]]

__II.4
crown or honour with libations, σ. τύμβον αἵματι [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Hecuba” 126 (_anapaest meter_).]]

__II.5
crown with the badge of office, especially of persons sacrificing, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Lysias Orator 26.8]]:—passive, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 7.1.40]]; of magistrates in office, ὁ ἐστεφανωμένος ἄρχων [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 21.17; βούλεται -ωθῆναι ἐξηγητείαν “PRyl.” 77.37 (2nd c.AD).]]

LSJ / STEPBible (TFLSJ)
στῆθος, εος, τό,
breast, of both sexes, being the front part of the θώραξ, divided into two μαστοί [Refs 8th c.BC+ [(4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Historia Animalium” 493a12, “PA” 688a13, +others), 8th c.BC: Homerus Epicus and later (compare στέρνον), especially in Prose, rare (and usually _metaphorically_)]] in post-Homeric verse; found once in [Refs 8th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus, twice in 5th c.BC: Bacchylides Lyricus, twice in 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus, never in 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus or 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus (see. below 1, 11); βάλε σ. παρὰ μαζόν 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 4.480; ἔβαλε σ. μεταμάζιον 5.19; κληῒς ἀποέργει αὐχένα τε στῆθός τε 8.326, compare 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Timaeus” 69e, 79c (_plural_), “Prt.” 352a (_plural_): in _plural_, διὰ στήθεσφιν (_Epic dialect_ _genitive_) ἔλασσε 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 5.41; στήθεά τ᾽ ἠδ᾽ ἁπαλὴν δειρήν (of Briseis) 19.285]]; of animals, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [11.282, 16.163, +others,compare 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Cynegeticus” 4.1, 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Historia Animalium” 496a9, 15, +others, “PCair.Zen.” 532.7, 18 (3rd c.BC), “BGU” 469.7 (2nd c.AD)]]; σ. φάσσης ἑψημένης [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd c.AD: Soranus Medicus 2.41, compare 1.51]]: as the seat of the voice and breath, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 3.221, 9.610, 5th c.BC: Bacchylides Lyricus 5.15, 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Septem contra Thebas” 563 (Lyric poetry), 865 (_anapaest meter_)]]; more frequently as the seat of the heart, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 1.189, 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 1.341, 7th-6th c.BC: Sappho Lyrica 2.6, etc.]]; chest, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Hippocrates Medicus “προρρητικόν” 1.70, 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Nubes” 1012, 1017 (both _anapaest meter_), 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 2.49 (_plural_), Diocl.fragment 142, “IG” 42(1).121.100 (_plural_, Epid., 4th c.BC), frequently in 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus (see. above), “PEnteux.” 79.7 (3rd c.BC), “PTeb.” 316.19 (1st c.AD), 2nd c.AD: Soranus Medicus 1.70b, +others]]; τὰ σ. breasts of a woman, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Hippocrates Medicus “γυναικεῖα” 2.133.]]

__II
metaphorically, the breast as the seat of feeling and thought, as we use heart, frequently in [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Homerus Epicus]], but always in plural, θυμὸν ἐνὶ στήθεσσιν ὄρινε [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 2.142, +others; θάρσος ἐνὶ σ. ἐνῆκεν 17.570]]; ἔχει κότον.. ἐν σ. ἑοῖσι[Refs 8th c.BC+ [1.83; ἐν γάρ τοι σ. μένος πατρώϊον ἧκα 5.125; νόον καὶ θυμὸν ἐνὶ σ. ἔχοντες 4.309; μῆτιν ἐνὶ σ. κέκευθε 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 3.18, compare 5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “Fragmenta.” 218, 5th c.BC: Bacchylides Lyricus 10.54: in Prose, εἰπεῖν ἃ ἔφησθα ἐν τῷ σ. ἔχειν 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Phaedrus” 236c; πλῆρες τὸ σ. ἔχειν [prev. work] 235c.]]

__III
={στέρνον} [Refs [111,]]breastbone, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Hippocrates Medicus “περὶ ἄρθρων ἐμβολῆς” 14.]]

__III.2
ball of the foot, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [[prev. work] 55, 58,compare “Epid.” 4.1, 2nd c.AD: Rufus Medicus “περὶ ὀνομασίας” 125; τὸ σαρκῶδες [τοῦ ποδὸς] κάτωθεν στῆθος 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Historia Animalium” 494a13]]; ball of the hand (below the thumb), [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd c.AD: Rufus Medicus “περὶ ὀνομασίας” 86; (below the fingers), 2nd c.AD: Galenus Medicus 14.704]]; palm, uncertain in [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Hippocrates Medicus “περὶ ὀστέων φύσιος” 9: compare προστηθίς.]]

__III.3
swelling, tumour, ἐν τῷ ἥπατι [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd c.AD: Aretaeus Medicus “ὀξέων νούσων θεραπευτικόν” 2.6 (_plural_).]]

__IV
breastshaped hill or bank, [Refs 2nd c.BC+ [2nd c.BC: Polybius Historicus 4.41.3, “PMasp.” 169b47 (6th c.AD),compare 5th c.AD(?): Hesychius Legal icographus (στῆθος]] has pan-Hellenic η, [Refs 7th c.BC+ [7th-6th c.BC: Sappho Lyrica, 5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus [same places], “IG” 42(1) [same place], 3rd c.BC: Callimachus Epicus “Lavacrum Palladis” 88, 3rd c.BC: Theocritus Poeta Bucolicus 2.79, 15.108, 135.)]]

στοιχεῖον, -ου, τό
[in LXX: Wis.7:17 19:18, 4Ma.12:13 * ;]
prop., one of a row (στοῖχος) or series, hence,
__1. the shadow-line of a dial (Aristoph.).
__2. an elementary sound or letter of the alphabet (Anth., Plut., π.).
__3. the elements or rudiments of knowledge (Arist., al.) Heb.5:12; πτωχὰ σ., Gal.4:9; σ. τοῦ κόσμου, Gal.4:3, Col.2:8, 20 (but see infr.).
__4. The material elements of the universe (Plat.; LXX, ll. with): 2Pe.3:10 3:12.
__5. The heavenly bodies (Ding. Laert.).
__6. The demons or tutelary spirits of nature (Enoch., Test., Sol., al.; for this sense in Ga, Col, ll. with, see ICC on Col.2:8; Enc. Bibl., see word " Elements ").†

στοιχεῖον, τό:

__I
in a form of sun-dial, the shadow of the gnomon, the length of which in feet indicated the time of day, ὅταν ᾖ δεκάπουν τὸ σ. when the shadow is ten feet long, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Ecclesiazusae” 652]], see [Refs 4th c.BC+ [Scholia; ὁπηνίκ᾽ ἂν εἴκοσι ποδῶν.. τὸ σ. ᾖ 4th c.BC: Eubulus Comicus 119.7, compare 4th-3rd c.BC: Philemo Comicus 83.]]

__II
element,

__II.1
a simple sound of speech, as the first component of the syllable, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Cratylus” 424d]]; τὸ ῥῶ τὸ σ[Refs 4th c.BC+ [. [prev. work] 426d; γραμμάτων σ. καὶ συλλαβάς [prev. author] “Tht.” 202e; σ. ἐστι φωνὴ ἀδιαίρετος 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Poetica” 1456b22; φωνῆς σ. καὶ ἀρχαὶ δοκοῦσιν εἶναι ταῦτ᾽ ἐξ ὧν σύγκεινται αἱ φωναὶ πρώτων [prev. author] “Metaphorical” 998a23, compare 2nd c.AD: Galenus Medicus 15.6:]] —στοιχεῖα therefore, strictly, were different from letters (γράμματα), [Refs 2nd c.BC+ [2nd c.BC: Diogenes Babylonius Stoicus 3.213, Scholia 2nd c.BC: Dionysius Thrax Grammaticus p.32, +others]], but are frequently not clearly distinguished from them, as by [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Tht.” [same place], “Cra.” 426d; τὰ σ. τῶν γραμμάτων τὰ τέτταρα καὶ εἴκοσι 4th c.BC: Aeneas Tacticus 31.21]]; σ. ε ¯ letter ε (in a filing-system), [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [“BGU” 959.2 (2nd c.AD)]]; ἀκουόμενα σ. letters which are pronounced, [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd c.AD: Apollonius Dyscolus Grammaticus “de Adverbiis;” 165.17]]; γράμματα and ς. are expressly identified by [Refs 2nd c.BC+ [2nd c.BC: Dionysius Thrax Grammaticus 630.32]]; the ς. and its name are confused by [Refs 2nd c.BC+ [2nd c.AD: Apollonius Dyscolus Grammaticus “de Syntaxi;” 29.1, but distinguished by Hdn.Gr. cited in 4th-5th c.AD: Choeroboscus Grammaticus “Scholia in Theodosii Canones” 1.340, Scholia 2nd c.BC: Dionysius Thrax Grammaticus [same place]:]] — κατὰ στοιχεῖον in the order of the letters, alphabetically, [Refs 1st c.AD+ [Anthologia Graeca 11.15 (2nd c.AD: Ammianus Epigrammaticus); uncertain meaning in 1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus 2.422e.]]

__II.2
in Physics, στοιχεῖα were the components into which matter is ultimately divisible, elements, reduced to four by Empedocles, who called them ῥιζὤματα, the word στοιχεῖα being first used (accusative to [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Eudemus Philosophus cited in 6th c.AD: Simplicius Philosophus “in Aristotelis Physica commentaria - Comm. in Arist. Graeca” 7.13) by 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus]], τὰ πρῶτα οἱονπερεὶ σ, ἐξ ὧν ἡμεῖς τε συγκείμεθα καὶ τἄλλα [Refs [“Tht.” 201e]]; τὰ τῶν πάντων σ. [Refs 4th c.BC+ [“Plt.” 278d; αὐτὰ τιθέμενοι σ. τοῦ παντός “Ti.” 48b, compare 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “de Generatione et Corruptione” 314a29, “Metaphorical” 998a28, 4th-3rd c.BC: Theophrastus Philosophus “de Sensu” 3, +others, 3rd c.AD(?): Diogenes Laertius 3.24; σ. σωματικά 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Meteorologica” 338a22, 4th-3rd c.BC: Theophrastus Philosophus “Fragmenta” 46]]; ἄτομα σ. [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-3rd c.BC: Epicurus Philosophus “Epistulae” 2p.36U.]]; equivalent to ἀρχαί, Thales cited in [Refs 6th c.BC+ [1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus 2.875c, 6th c.BC: Anaximander Philosophus cited in 3rd c.AD(?): Diogenes Laertius 2.1, Anonymus cited in 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Physica” 188b28, “Metaphorical” 1059b23, +others; but 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus]] also distinguishes ς. from ἀρχή as less comprehensive, [Refs [[prev. work]1070b23]]; τὰ σ. ὕλη τῆς οὐσίας [Refs [[prev. work]1088b27]]; τρία τὰ σ. [Refs [[prev. author] “Ph.” 189b16]]; distinguished from ἀρχή on other grounds by [Refs [“Stoicorum Veterum Fragmenta” 2.111]]; ς. used in three senses by Chrysipp., [Refs [[prev. work]136, cf. Zeno [prev. work]1.24, +others]]; in Medicine, [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd c.AD: Galenus Medicus 6.3, 420, +others, 15.7, +others; Αἰθέρ, κόσμου σ. ἄριστον 5th-6th c.AD: Orphica “Hymni” 5.4]]; ἀνηλεὲς σ., of the sea, [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd c.AD: Babrius Fabularum Scriptor 71.4]]; τὸ σ., of the sea, [Refs 1st c.AD+ [1st-2nd c.AD: Polemo Sophista “Cynegirus” 44]]; ἄμφω τὰ σ., i.e. land and sea,[Refs 2nd c.AD+ [[prev. work] 11, compare 2nd c.AD: Herodianus Grammaticus 3.1.5, 4th c.AD: Himerius Sophista “Eclogae” 2.18.]]

__II.3
the elements of proof, e.g. in general reasoning the πρῶτοι συλλογισμοί, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Metaphysica” 1014b1]]; in Geometry, the propositions whose proof is involved in the proof of other propositions,[Refs [[prev. work] 998a26, 1014a36]]; title of geometrical works by Hippocrates of Chios, Leon, Theudios, and Euclid, [Refs 5th c.AD+ [5th c.AD: Proclus Philosophus “in primum Euclidis librum commentarius” pp.66,67, 68F.]]: hence applied to whatever is one, small, and capable of many uses, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Metaphysica” 1014b3]]; to whatever is most universal, e.g. the unit and the point,[Refs [[prev. work] 6]]; the line and the circle, [Refs [[prev. author] “Top.” 158b35; the τόπος (argument applicable to a variety of subjects), [prev. work] 120b13, +others, “Rh.” 1358a35, +others; στοιχεῖα τὰ γένη λέγουσί τινες [prev. author] “Metaphorical” 1014b10]]; τὸ νόμισμα σ. καὶ πέρας τῆς ἀλλαγῆς coin is the unit.. of exchange, [Refs [[prev. author] “Pol.” 1257b23]]; in Grammar, σ. τῆς λέξεως parts of speech, [Refs 1st c.BC+ [1st c.BC: Dionysius Halicarnassensis “de Compositione Verborum” 2]]; but also, the letters composing a word, [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd c.AD: Apollonius Dyscolus Grammaticus “de Syntaxi;” 313.7]]; letters of the alphabet, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Diogenes Cynicus Philosophus Bab. “Stoicorum Veterum Fragmenta” 3.213]]; σ. τοῦ λόγου the elements of speech, i.e.  words, or the kinds of words, parts of speech, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-3rd c.BC: Theophrastus Philosophus cited in 6th c.AD: Simplicius Philosophus “in Aristotelis Categorias commentarium - Comm. in Arist. Graeca” 10.24, 3rd c.BC: Chrysippus Stoicus 2.45, 2nd c.AD: Apollonius Dyscolus Grammaticus “de Syntaxi;” 7.1, 313.6.]]

__II.4
generally, elementary or fundamental principle, ἀρξάμενοι ἀπὸ τῶν σ. [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Memorabilia” 2.1.1; σ. χρηστῆς πολιτείας 5th-6th c.BC: Isocrates Orator 2.16]]; τὸ πολλάκις εἰρημένον μέγιστον σ. [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Politica” 1309b16; σ. τῆς ὅλης τέχνης 4th c.BC(?): Nicolaus Comicus 1.30, compare 4th-3rd c.BC: Epicurus Philosophus “Epistulae” 1p.10U., “Ep.” 3p.59U., 1st c.BC: Philodemus Gadarensis Epigrammaticus “Rh.” 1.127S., 2nd c.AD: Galenus Medicus 6.306.]]

__II.5
ἄστρων στοιχεῖα the stars, [NT+4th c.AD+ [4th c.AD(?): Manetho Astrologus 4.624; σ. καυσούμενα λυθήσεται NT.2Pet.3.10, compare 12]]; especially planets, στοιχείῳ Διός [Refs 1st c.AD+ [“PLond.” 1.130.60 (1st-2nd c.AD)]]; so perhaps in [NT.Gal.4.3, NT.Col.2.8]; especially a sign of the Zodiac, [Refs 3rd c.AD+ [3rd c.AD(?): Diogenes Laertius 6.102]]; of the Great Bear, [Refs [“PMag.Par.” 1.1303.]]

__II.6
σ. ={ἀριθμός}, as etymology of Στοιχαδεύς, Scholia 2nd c.BC: Dionysius Thrax Grammaticus p.192 H.

[Refs 6th c.BC+ [6th c.BC: Solon Lyricus 25]]; of animals, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th-7th c.BC: Hesiodus Epicus “Scutum Herculis” 146, 389, 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Philoctetes” 1156 (Lyric poetry), etc.:]] —_plural_ is sometimes used for _sing._, ἀμφιπίπτων στόμασιν, of kissing, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. author] “Tr.” 938, compare 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Alcestis” 403 (Lyric poetry)]], and frequently in later Poets, [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [3rd c.BC: Apollonius Rhodius Epicus 4.1607, 2nd c.BC: Nicander Epicus “Alexipharmaca” 210, 240, etc.: _metaphorically_, πτολέμοιο, ὑσμίνης στόμα]], the very jaws of the battle, as of a devouring monster, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 10.8, 20.359 (but compare below 111.1).]]

__2
especially the mouth as the organ of speech, δέκα μὲν γλῶσσαι, δέκα δὲ στόματ᾽ [Refs 6th c.BC+ [2.489, compare 6th c.BC: Theognis Elegiacus 18; βραχύ μοι σ. πάντ᾽ ἀνᾱγήσασθαι 5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “N.” 10.19]]; frequently in Trag., σ. τὸ Δῖον the mouth of Zeus, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Prometheus Vinctus” 1032]]; τὸ Φοίβου θεῖον ἀψευδὲς σ. [Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. author] “fragment” 350.5, compare 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Coloneus” 603; τοῦ στόματος τὸ στρογγύλον 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Fragmenta” 471]]; Μοισᾶν καπυρὸν σ. their mouthpiece, organ, [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [3rd c.BC: Theocritus Poeta Bucolicus 7.37, compare 2nd c.BC: Moschus Bucolicus 3.72]]; Πιερίδων τὸ σοφὸν σ., of Homer, [Refs 1st c.BC+ [“Anthologia Graeca” 7.4 (Paul. Sil.), compare 7.6 (Antip. Sid.), 7.75 (Antip.), 9.184; τὸ μισόχρηστον σ. τῆς κωμῳδίας 1st c.BC: Philodemus Philosophus “de Pietate - Herkulanische Studien” p.93G.]]; speech, utterance, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Tyrannus” 426, 706, “OC” 132 (Lyric poetry), etc.; εἰς τόδ᾽ ἐξελθόντος ἀνόσιον σ. [prev. work] 981]]; κἂν καλὸν φορῇ σ. [[prev. author] “fragment” 930; τὸ σὸν.. σ. ἐλεινόν [prev. author] “OT” 671; διδόναι σ. καὶ σοφίαν NT.Luke.21.15]: in plural of a single speaker, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Tyrannus” 1220 (Lyric poetry):—special phrases: οἴγειν σ. 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Prometheus Vinctus” 611]]; τοὐμὸν οὐ λύω σ. [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Hippolytus” 1060, compare 5th-6th c.BC: Isocrates Orator 12.96]]; διᾶραι τὸ σ. [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 19.112]]; κοίμησον σ. keep silence, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Agamemnon” 1247]]; δάκνειν σ., i.e. to keep a stern silence (compare ὀδάξ), [Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. author] “fragment” 397; ἴσχε δακὼν σ. σόν 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Trachiniae” 977 (_anapaest meter_)]]; ὀδόντι πρῖε τὸ σ. [Refs [[prev. author] “fragment” 897]]; so κλῄσας σ. [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Phoenissae” 865]]; οὐκ ἐφέξετε σ.; [Refs [[prev. author] “Hec.” 1283]]; σῖγ᾽ ἕξομεν σ. [Refs [[prev. author] “Hipp.” 660]]; εὖ ἔχειν σ.,= εὐφημεῖν, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Eupolis Comicus 381]]; συγκλῄειν σ. [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Thesmophoriazusae” 40 (_anapaest meter_):—of style, τὸ Λυσιακὸν σ. 1st c.BC: Dionysius Halicarnassensis “de Lysia” 12.]]

__3
with Preps.,

__3.a
ἀνὰ στόμα ἔχειν have always in one's mouth, whether for good or ill, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Electra” 80; ἀνὰ σ. καὶ διὰ γλώσσης ἔχειν [prev. author] “Andr.” 95.]]

__3.b
ἀπὸ στόματος εἰπεῖν speak from memory (compare ἀπὸ γλώσσης), [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Theaetetus” 142d, 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Memorabilia” 3.6.9, 4th-3rd c.BC: Philemo Comicus 48, 1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus “Solon” 8, etc.]]

__3.c
διὰ στόμα λέγειν [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Septem contra Thebas” 579, compare 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Orestes” 103 (so κατὰ τὸ σ. ᾄδειν 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Nubes” 158); διὰ στόμα ἔχειν [prev. author] “Lys.” 855; οἶκτος οὔτις ἦν διὰ στόμα 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Septem contra Thebas” 51]]; πᾶσι διὰ στόματος 'tis the common talk, [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [3rd c.BC: Theocritus Poeta Bucolicus 12.21.]]

__3.d
ἐν στόμασι εἶχον [Refs 6th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 3.157, 6.136; πολλῶν κείμενος ἐν στόμασιν 6th c.BC: Theognis Elegiacus 240; ἐν τῷ σ. λέγειν 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Acharnenses” 198.]]

__3.e
ἐξ ἑνὸς σ. with one voice, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. author] “Eq.” 670. 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 364a, “PGiss.” 36.13 (2nd c.BC), 2nd c.AD: Galenus Medicus 15.763]]; so ὡς ἀφ᾽ ἑνὸς σ. [Refs 1st c.AD+ [“Anthologia Graeca” 11.159 (1st c.AD: Lucillius Epigrammaticus).]]

__3.f
ἐπὶ στόμα on one's face, face-foremost, ἐξεκυλίσθη πρηνὴς.. ἐπὶ σ. [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 6.43, compare 16.410; ὡς κύων ἐπὶ σ. κείμενος 7th c.BC: Archilochus Lyricus “Supp.” 2.9]]; ὗς ἔκειτ᾽ ἐπὶ σ. [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-3rd c.BC: Menander Comicus 21]]; ἐπὶ σ. κεῖται lies prone, of the right ventricle, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Hippocrates Medicus “περὶ καρδίης” 4]]; ἐπὶ σ.,= pronus, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [“Corpus Glossariorum Latinorum”; ἐπὶ σ. πεσόντα 1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus “Artoxerxes” 29; ἐπὶ σ. φερόμενον ἐν πᾶσι 4th-3rd c.BC: Timaeus Historicus cited in 2nd c.BC: Polybius Historicus 12.8.4]]; also ὅ τι νῦν ἦλθ᾽ ἐπὶ σ. whatever came uppermost, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Fragmenta - American Journal of Philology” 351]]; ἐπὶ στόματος Φαραώ by the command of P., [LXX.2Ki.23.35.]

__3.g
κατὰ στόμα face to face, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 8.11, 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Heraclidae” 801, “Rh.” 409, 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 5.2.26]]; οἱ κατὰ σ. θεοί (compare ἀντήλιοι) [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Fragmenta” 781.33]]; κατὰ σ. τινός confronted with him, [NT+5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Leges” 855d; στόμα κατὰ στόμα λαλήσω αὐτῷ LXX.Num.12.8; στόμα πρὸς στόμα NT.2John.12, NT.3John.14, “PMag.Berol.” 1.39.]]

__II
mouth of a river, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 12.24, 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 5.441, 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Prometheus Vinctus” 847, 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 2.17, etc.]]; so ἠϊόνος σ. μακρόν the wide mouth of the bay, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 14.36, compare 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 10.90; σ. τοῦ Πόντου 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 4.75]]; κόλπου[Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. work] 49; τὸ σ. τῆς ἐσβολῆς 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Ecclesiazusae” 1107]]; τὸ ἄνω σ. [τῆς διώρυχος] the width of the trench at top, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 7.23 (but τὰ σ. τ. δ]]. mouths, [Refs [[prev. work] 37).]]

__II.2
any outlet or entrance, ἀργαλέον σ. λαύρης [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 22.137; σ. τῆς ἀγυιᾶς 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 2.4.4; σ. φρέατος [prev. author] “An.” 4.5.25; καδίσκου 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Fragmenta” 581, compare “Anthologia Graeca” 6.251 (1st c.AD: Philippus Epigrammaticus)]]; χθόνιον Ἄιδα σ. [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “P.” 4.44]]; τὰ τῶν διεξόδων σ. [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Phaedrus” 251d]]; ἑπτάπυλον σ. the seven gates of Thebes, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Antigone” 119 (Lyric poetry): in Medicine texts, τῶν μητρέων, τῶν ὑστερέων]],= os uteri (not distinguished from the cervix), [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Hippocrates Medicus “γυναικεῖα” 1.36, “Aph.” 5.46; τῆς κοιλίας 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Analytica Posteriora” 94b15, 2nd c.AD: Soranus Medicus 1.50; γαστρός 2nd c.BC: Nicander Epicus “Alexipharmaca” 20, 2nd c.AD: Galenus Medicus 5.274]]; [ἕλκους] [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Problemata” 863a11.]]

__III
foremost part, face, front:

__III.1
of weapons, point, κατὰ στόμα εἱμένα χαλκῷ [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 15.389; [ὁ κριὸς] ἔχει σ. σιδηροῦν 2nd c.AD: Athenaeus Epigrammaticus Mech. 24.2; τὸ σ. τῆς αἰχμῆς 2nd-3rd c.AD: Philostratus Sophista “Heroicus” 19.4]]; edge of a sword, μαχαίρας [NT+5th c.BC+ [1st c.BC: Asclepiodotus Tacticus “Tact.” 3.5, NT.Luke.21.24, etc.: _metaphorically_, ἐθηλύνθην σ. 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Ajax” 651.]]

__III.1.b
the front ranks of the battle, the front, ἀπὸ στόματος (opposed to ἀπὸ τῆς οὐρᾶς) [Refs 8th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 3.4.42, compare “HG” 4.3.4; τὸ σ. τοῦ πλαισίου [prev. author] “An.” 3.4.43, compare 5.4.22, 2nd c.BC: Polybius Historicus 10.12.7 (so perhaps σ. πολέμοιο, ὑσμίνης in 8th c.BC: Homerus Epicus, see above 1.1).]]

__III.1.c
τὸ τῶν λοχαγῶν τάγμα σ. καλεῖται [Refs 1st c.BC+ [1st c.BC: Asclepiodotus Tacticus “Tact.” 2.5.]]

__III.2
ἄκρον σ. πύργων the edge or top of the towers, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Phoenissae” 1166]]; πρὸς τῷ σ. τοῦ βίου at the very verge of life, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Agesilaus” 11.15.]]

__III.3
={ὀμφαλός}[Refs 2nd c.AD+ [111.3, 2nd-3rd c.AD: Aelianus “Tactica - Griechische Kriegsschriftsteller” 7.3]]. (Cf. Avest. staman-, m. 'mouth (of dog)', Welsh safn 'mouth'.)

στόμᾰχ-ος, ὁ,
(στόμα) throat, gullet, ἀπὸ στομάχους ἀρνῶν τάμε νηλέϊ χαλκῷ [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 3.292, compare 19.266; κατὰ στομάχοιο θέμεθλα νύξε 17.47]]; ={οἰσοφάγος}, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Historia Animalium” 495b19f, 493a8, 2nd c.BC: Nicander Epicus “Alexipharmaca” 22.]]

neck of the bladder, τῆς κύστιος [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Hippocrates Medicus]] “Aër.” 9; or of the uterus, [Refs [[prev. author] “Mul.” 1.18, “Steril.” 217; τοῦ αἰδοίου [prev. author] “Mul.” 1.36.]]

[Refs [“PMag.Leid.W.” 18.36]]; cf. Latin stomachus.

anger, γέγονε σ. πρὸς δουλικὸν πρόσωπον [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd c.AD: Vettius Valens Astrologus 216.3; ἵνα μὴ ἔχωμεν στομάχους μηδὲ φθόνον “POxy.” 533.14 (2nd-3rd c.AD).]]

Abbott-Smith / STEPBible (TBESG)
στρατεία (on the orthogr., see Deiss., BS, 181 f.), -ας, ἡ
(οτρατεύω), [in LXX chiefly for צָבָא ;]
an expedition, a campaign, warfare: metaphorically, 2Co.10:4 (-τιά, T), 1Ti.1:18.†
(AS)

---

LSJ / STEPBible (TFLSJ)
στρᾰτεία,
Ionic dialect -ηΐη, ἡ, (στρατεύω) expedition, campaign, στρατηΐην ποιεῖσθαι ἐς.., ἐπὶ.., [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.71, 171, etc.; πολλὰς σ. ἐποιήσαντο 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 2.11; σ. ἐστράτευσ᾽ ὀλεθρίαν 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Supplices” 116; σ. ἡμῖν εἰς Ποτείδαιαν ἐγένετο 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Symposium” 219e, compare “IG” 12(2).645.15 (from Nesus), etc.]]; ἀπὸ στρατείας coming from war, after service done, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Agamemnon” 603, “Eu.” 631]]; κατὰ τὴν Σιτάλκου σ. about the time of his expedition, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 2.101; εἰς δὲ σ. πάντας Ἀργείους ἄγων 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Supplices” 229]]; ἐπὶ στρατείας εἶναι to be on foreign service, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Symposium” 220c (codices, στρατιᾶς Cobet, Burnet)]]; so ἐν στρατείᾳ ὄντας [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 5.2.19]]; ἐν τῇ σ. [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [“PEnteux.” 48.3 (3rd c.BC)]]; παραγγέλλειν τινὶ σ. κατὰ γῆν [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Historia Graeca (Hellenica)” 7.1.13; ἐκδήμους σ. οὐκ ἐξῇσαν 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 1.15]]; στρατείαν ξυνεξελθεῖν[Refs 4th c.BC+ [[prev. work] 3; σ. δ᾽ οὐ φέρει περιουσίαν 4th-3rd c.BC: Menander Comicus 382, compare “OGI” 5.44 (Scepsis, 4th c.BC)]]; τῆς σ. γιγνομένης ἐκ καταλόγου [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Ἀθηναίων Πολιτεία” 26.1]]; frequently in plural, military service, warfare, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 404a]]; πρὸς ταῖς αὑτοῦ σ. in addition to the campaigns which he is bound to serve, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [[prev. author] “Lg.” 878d; ἐν ταῖς σ. μισθοφορεῖν 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Ἀθηναίων Πολιτεία” 27.2; ἀπὸ σ. ἱππικῶν “IGRom.” 3.58 (from Bithynia)]]; στρατείας στρατεύεσθαι [Refs [“IG” 22.505.54]]; ἀφειμένος στρατείας, = Latin exauctoratus, [Refs 1st c.AD+ [1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus 2.274a.]]

__2
σ. ἐν τοῖς ἐπωνύμοις levy of those liable to serve in the year of such and such archons, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [1st-2nd c.AD: Harpocratio Grammaticus see entry , compare 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Ἀθηναίων Πολιτεία” 53.7.]]

__3
σ. ἡ ἐν τοῖς μέρεσιν expedition for special service, to train the young soldiers next after serving as περίπολοι, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aeschines Orator 2.168, compare 10th c.AD: Suidas Legal icographus see at {τερθρεία}.]]

__4
military discipline, ἡ ἀκριβὴς σ. [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd-3rd c.AD: Dio Cassius Historicus 78.36.]]

__5
military appointment, ἐπώλησε στρατείας [Refs [[prev. author] 72.12.]] —στρατιά is a constant variant, and is sometimes undoubtedly used= στρατεία (campaign), see at {στρατιά} [Refs 5th c.BC+ [11 and cf. Scholia 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Thesmophoriazusae” 835 (= 5th c.BC: Eupolis Comicus 369)]]; but στρατεία= army, expeditionary force is very rare, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Iphigenia Aulidensis” 495 (restored in “Rh.” 263 (Lyric poetry)): in Inscrr. στρατεία]] never = army, but both -εία [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [(“IG” 22.1132.14, “SIG” 398.2 (Cos, 3rd c.BC), +others) and -ιά (which see)]] = campaign.

to turn: with accusative of thing(s) dative of person(s), Mat.5:39; = ἀποσ-, to bring back, Mat.27:3 (cf. Isa.38:8); reflexively (WM, § 38, 1), to turn oneself, Act.7:42; with accusative before εἰς, = μετασ-, to change, Rev.11:6. στρέφω,
[Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 23.323, etc.]]; Doric dialect στράφω [ᾰ] [Refs [“IG” 12(3).92.6 (Nisyrus, uncertain)]]; Aeolic dialect στροφῶ (to be read στρόφω) [Refs [“Etymologicum Magnum” 728.44]]: Epic dialect imperfect

__A
στρέψασκον [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 18.546]]: future στρέψω [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Medea” 1152, etc.]]: aorist 1 ἔστρεψα [Refs [[prev. author] “Tr.” 1243, etc.]], Epic dialect στρέψα [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 4.520:]]perfect ἔστροφα (ἀν-) [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [3rd c.BC: Cercidas Iambographus 17.30, (ἀντ-, variant{ἀν-}) Theognetus Comicus 1.8, (ἐπ-) 2nd c.BC: Polybius Historicus 5.110.6, (μετ-) 2nd c.AD: Aristides Rhetor 1.435 1st c.AD: Josephus Historicus]]; also ἔστρᾰφα (κατ-) [Refs 2nd c.BC+ [2nd c.BC: Polybius Historicus 23.11.2]] codices:—middle, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 18.488, etc.]]: future στρέψομαι [Refs [6.516, etc.]]: aorist ἐστρεψάμην [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Coloneus” 1416, (κατ-) 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 1.94, etc.:]]perfect passive (in middle sense) ἔστραμμαι (κατ-) [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Isocrates Orator 5.21]]:—passive, future στρᾰφήσομαι [LXX+5th c.BC+ [LXX.1Ki.10.6, (ἀνα-) 5th-6th c.BC: Isocrates Orator 5.64, (δια-) 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Equites” 175, “Av.” 177, (μετα-) 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 518d]]; future middle (in passive sense) στρέψομαι (ἀπο-) [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 5.5.36:]]aorist 1 ἐστρέφθην frequently in [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Homerus Epicus, 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 5.40, +others]], rare in Attic dialect, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Thesmophoriazusae” 1128, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Politicus” 273e]]; Doric dialect ἐστράφθην [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophron Comicus 88, 3rd c.BC: Theocritus Poeta Bucolicus 7.132, also variant (for κατεστράφησαν) in 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.130 (but στραφῆναι [prev. author] 3.129):]]aorist 2 ἐστράφην [ᾰ] [Refs 6th c.BC+ [6th c.BC: Solon Lyricus 37.6, always in Trag., 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Antigone” 315, etc.]], frequently in Attic dialect, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Acharnenses” 537 (μετα-), 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 5.97 (κατα-), 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Timaeus” 77b]]: perfect ἔστραμμαι [Refs 5th c.BC+ [“hymnus ad Mercurium” 411, 5th c.BC: Hippocrates Medicus “Aër.” 5, 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 4.7.15, etc.; ἔστρεμμαι 4th c.BC: Eudoxus Astronomus “Ars astronomica” 12.10 (Papyrus), compare ἀποστρέφω, καταστρέφω]]:—turn about or aside, ἂψ δὲ θεοὶ οὖρον στρέψαν [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 4.520]]; ἵππους σ. turn horses, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 8.168, 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 15.205, etc.; σ. πηδάλιον 5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “Fragmenta.” 40; τὸν οἴακα 4th c.BC: Anaxandrides Comicus 4.5, compare 4th-3rd c.BC: Menander Comicus 482.4; σάκος 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Ajax” 575]]; of persons, ἡλίου πρὸς ἀντολὰς στρέψασα σαυτήν [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Prometheus Vinctus” 708; πρόσωπον πρὸς κασίγνητον στρέφε 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Phoenissae” 457, compare “Hec.” 344; πάλιν στρέψεις κάρα [prev. author] “Med.” 1152; ὄμμα πανταχῇ στρέφων [prev. author] “IT” 68; σ. ἀνταυγεῖς κόρας 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Thesmophoriazusae” 902; σεαυτὸν εἰς πονηρὰ πράγματα [prev. author] “Nu.” 1455; πόλιν πρὸς κέρδος ἴδιον 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Supplices” 413; στρατὸν πρὸς ἀλκήν [prev. author] “Andr.” 1149]]; wheel soldiers round, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Respublica Lacedaemoniorum” 11.9]]; see below [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator]]

__A.2
cause to rotate as on an axis, κεραμικὴν γαῖαν σ., i.e. on the potter's wheel, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sannyrio Comicus 4; τὸν ἄτρακτον 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 5.12; τὸν κόσμον μήτε αὐτὸν στρέφειν ἑαυτόν, μήτε.. ὑπὸ θεοῦ στρέφεσθαι διττὰς περιαγωγάς 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Politicus” 269e, compare “Epin.” 977b.]]

__A.II
πάντ᾽ ἄνω τε καὶ κάτω σ. turn upside down, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Eumenides” 651]]; κάτω σ. [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Antigone” 717, 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Ecclesiazusae” 733; σ. λόγους ἄνω καὶ κάτω 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Gorgias” 511a, compare “Euthd.” 276d]]; ἄνω κάτω τοὺς νόμους σ. [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 21.91; so δίκα καὶ πάντα πάλιν στρέφεται 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Medea” 411 (Lyric poetry)]]; στρέφειν alone, overturn, upset, [Refs [[prev. author] “IT” 1166, “fragment” 536 (troch.)]]; γῆν σ. turn it over by digging or ploughing, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Oeconomicus” 16.15: with _accusative_ _cognate_, πάσας σ. στροφάς 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Timaeus” 43e]]; γράμματα πανταχῇ σ. [Refs [[prev. author] “Cra.” 414c]]: with infinitive, change a thing so as to.. , εὔκλειαν ἔχειν βιοτὰν στρέψουσι φᾶμαι [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Medea” 416 (Lyric poetry).]]

__A.III
σ. σφυρόν sprain or dislocate it, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [1st-2nd c.AD: Epictetus Philosophus “Enchiridion” 29.2, 2nd c.AD: Arrianus Historicus “Epicteti Dissertationes” 3.15.4 (so στραφῆναι τὸν πόδα 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 3.129, compare 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Leges” 789e).]]

__A.III.2
metaphorically of pain, twist, torture, κακὸν στρέφει με περὶ τὴν γαστέρα [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Antiphanes Comicus 177, compare 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Plutus” 1131, “fragment” 462, 2nd-3rd c.AD: Aelianus “De Natura Animalium - Ar.Byzantine Epit.” 2.44 (_passive_), 2nd c.AD: Galenus Medicus 19.141; βρέμει ἡ κοιλίη καὶ στρέφει καὶ βορβορύζει 5th c.BC: Hippocrates Medicus “περὶ τῶν ἐντὸς παθῶν” 6: so σ. τὴν ψυχήν]] torment, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 330e.]]

__A.III.3
of corruptions in Music, κάμπτων καὶ στρέφων [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Pherecrates Comicus 145.15.]]

__A.IV
twist, plait, σπάρτα ἐστραμμένα [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 4.7.15; ἐμβολάδην ἐστραμμέναι ἀλλήλῃσι “hymnus ad Mercurium” 411]]; spin, ὑπὸ μακρῷ λίνῳ στρεφομένη [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd c.AD: Lucianus Sophista “JConf.” 7, compare 1; ἔστρεψεν Μοιρῶν μία νήματα “IG” 14.607i (from Caralis)]]; κρόκην σ. [Refs 1st c.AD+ [2nd c.AD: Lucianus Sophista “Fug.” 12: _metaphorically_, μεγάλας σ. περιόδους 1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus 2.235e.]]

__A.V
technical term of wrestlers, twist the adversary back, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [2nd c.AD(?): Pollianus Epigrammaticus 3.155: _metaphorically_, ἔριδα σ. 5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “N.” 4.93.]]

__A.VI
metaphorically, turn a thing over in one's mind, τί στρέφω τάδ; [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Hecuba” 750; πρὸς ἀλλήλους 2nd c.AD: Lucianus Sophista “Alex.” 8; βουλὴν ἐν ἑαυτῷ 2nd-3rd c.AD: Aelianus “De Natura Animalium - Ar.Byzantine Epit.” 10.48; τὸ πρᾶγμα πανταχῇ στρέφων ἀγαγεῖν ἐπ᾽ ἐμέ 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 21.116.]]

__A.VII
return, give back, ἀργύριά τισι [NT.Matt.27.3.]

__A.VIII
convert, τὴν πέτραν εἰς λίμνας ὑδάτων [LXX.Psa.113(114).8, compare 29(30).12, LXX.Exo.4.17]; στραφήσῃ εἰς ἄνδρα ἄλλον[LXX.1Ki.10.6]; transmute metals,[Refs 5th c.BC+ [Zos.Alch. p.195 5th c.BC: Bacchylides Lyricus]]

__A.IX
falsa lectio for{τρέπω} in [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Lysias Orator 32.20.]]

__B
passive and middle, twist or turn oneself, στρεφθείς having turned face upward, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 9.435]]; turn round or about, turn to and fro, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 5.40, 575, etc.; ἔν τε κύνεσσι κάπριος ἠὲ λέων στρέφεται 12.42]]; ἐστρέφετ᾽ ἔνθα καὶ ἔνθα, of one tossing in bed, [Refs [24.5]]; τί δυσκολαίνεις καὶ στρέφει τὴν νύχθ᾽ ὅλη; [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Nubes” 36, compare 4th c.BC: Amphis Comicus 20.4]]; of patients, [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd c.AD: Galenus Medicus 7.664.]]

__B.2
turn to or from an object, ἔμελλε στρέψεσθ᾽ ἐκ χώρης [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 6.516, compare 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 16.352]]; στρεφθεὶς μετόπισθεν turning back, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 15.645]]; return, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Coloneus” 1648, “Ant.” 315, etc.; στραφέντες ἔφευγον 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 3.3.63, “An.” 3.5.1]]; ποῖ στρέφε; whither away? [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Thesmophoriazusae” 230, 610.]]

__B.3
of the heavenly bodies, revolve, circle, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 5.274, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Timaeus” 40b]]; of the distaff, [Refs [[prev. author] “R.” 617a]]; of a joint, ἐν ἄρθροις σ. κοτυληδών [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Vespae” 1495.]]

__B.II
turn or twist about, like a wrestler trying to elude his adversary: hence, in argument, twist and turn, shuffle, τί ταῦτα στρέφε; [Refs [[prev. author] “Ach.” 385]]; τί δῆτα ἔχων στρέφε; [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Phaedrus” 236e, etc.]]; πάσας στροφὰς στρέφεσθαι twist every way, [Refs [[prev. author] “R.” 405c, compare “Euthd.” 302b.]]

__B.II.2
turn and change, κἂν σοῦ στραφείη θυμός [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Trachiniae” 1134]]; στρεφόμενα λέγων things that tell both ways, [Refs 1st c.BC+ [1st c.BC: Dionysius Halicarnassensis “Ars Rhetorica” 8.15: with _genitive_ causae, τοῦ δὲ σοῦ ψόφου οὐκ ἂν στραφείην]] I would not turn for any noise of thine, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Ajax” 1117.]]

__B.III
to be always engaged in or about, ἐν τούτοις στρέφεται καὶ ἑλίττεται ἡ δόξα [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Theaetetus” 194b; περὶ τὸ αὐτὸ γένος στρέφεται ἡ σοφιστική 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Metaphysica” 1004b22, compare 1st c.BC: Philodemus Gadarensis Epigrammaticus “Rh.” 2p.124S.]]

__B.III.2
generally, to be at large, go about, ἀνειμένη στρέφει [Refs 6th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Electra” 516; ἐν κυσὶν.. ἐστράφην λύκος 6th c.BC: Solon Lyricus 37.6; στρέφεσθαι περὶ τὰ δικαστήρια 1st c.BC: Philodemus Gadarensis Epigrammaticus “Rh.” 2.139 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus]]; of things, to be rife, ταῦτα μὲν ἐν δήμῳ στρέφεται κακά [Refs 6th c.BC+ [6th c.BC: Solon Lyricus 4.23.]]

__B.III.3
of places, τόποι ἐπὶ.. τὰς ἄρκτους ἐστραμμένοι turned, lying towards.., [Refs 2nd c.BC+ [2nd c.BC: Polybius Historicus 2.15.8, etc.]]

__C
in strict middle sense, turn about with oneself, take back, στράτευμ᾽ ἐς Ἄργος [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Coloneus” 1416.]]

__D
intransitive in active, like passive, turn about, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 18.544, 546, where, however, ζεύγεα may be supplied from 543, as may ὄϊς in 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 10.528, and ἵππους in 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “de Equitandi ratione” 7.18]]; of soldiers, wheel about, [Refs [[prev. author] “An.” 4.3.26 and 32; στρέψαντες ἀπεχώρουν [prev. author] “Ages.” 2.3]]; ποῖ στροφαὶ.. μανιῶν στρέφουσ; [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Ichn.” 224]]; τὸν στρέφοντα κύκλον ἡλίου revolving, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. author] “fragment” 738, compare 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Ion” 1154]]; στρέψαι δεῦρ᾽, of the Comic Chorus, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Comicus 92]]; στρέψον τι, δούλη withdraw a little, [NT+3rd c.BC+ [3rd c.BC: Herodas Mimographus 1.8; ἔστρεψεν ὁ θεός NT.Act.7.42.]]

in 8th c.BC: Homerus Epicus]], Lesbian Lyric poetry, and Ionic dialect Lyric poetry and Prose τοι is always enclitic, σοί never enclitic (τοί and σοι are not found except σοι [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 3.359, 11.381, ς (οι) 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 1.170]], and in codices of [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “P.” 4.270, 9.55]]; rarer than τοι in [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus, 3.69, +others)]]; in Attic dialect both σοί and σοι (enclitic) are used (σοί [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Nubes” 361, etc., σοι [prev. work] 87, etc.)]], τοί and τοι are not used; σοι is never elided except in [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 1.170, τοι is elided in 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 1.60, 347, 7th-6th c.BC: Alcaeus Lyricus 55, [prev. author] “Oxy.” 1788 “fragment” 15 ii 9, 7th-6th c.BC: Sappho Lyrica 28.2]]; Epic dialect and Lyric poetry also τεΐν, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 11.201, 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 4.619, epigram cited in 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 5.60, 61, 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Aves” 930]]; also τίν [ῐ], [Refs 7th c.BC+ [7th c.BC: Alcman Lyricus 16, 5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “P.” 1.29, 8.68 (uncertain reading)]]; τίν [ῑ], [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [[prev. author] “I.” 6(5).4, 3rd c.BC: Theocritus Poeta Bucolicus 2.20 (τίν]] before a consonant, [Refs 7th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “O.” 10(11).93); also τεΐ 7th c.BC: Alcman Lyricus 53; τίνη 3rd c.BC: Rhinthon Comicus 13.]]—Acc. σέ, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 6.256, +others]]; enclitic σε,[Refs 7th c.BC+ [1.26, 7th-6th c.BC: Sappho Lyrica 1.2, “Supp.” 23.9, 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 3.42, etc.]]; in late Gr. σέν, [Refs [“Anatolian Studies” p.76]]; Doric dialect τέ [Refs 7th c.BC+ [7th c.BC: Alcman Lyricus 52, 5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “O.” 1.48, 3rd c.BC: Theocritus Poeta Bucolicus 1.5, 3rd c.BC: Callimachus Epicus “Fragmenta” 114]]; τ᾽ variant (codex R) in [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Acharnenses” 779 (on the accent see 2nd c.AD: Apollonius Dyscolus Grammaticus “de Pronominibus;” 54.14, 83.4)]]; τρέ (to be read τϝέ) [Refs 5th c.AD+ [5th c.AD(?): Hesychius Legal icographus]]; or (enclitic) τυ [Refs 6th c.BC+ [“IG” 42(1).121.69 (Epid., 4th c.BC), 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Equites” 1225, “Ach.” 730 (uncertain in “Ach.” 779), 3rd c.BC: Theocritus Poeta Bucolicus 1.56, 78, etc.:—also τίν 6th c.BC: Corinna Lyrica 4, 3rd c.BC: Cercidas Iambographus 7.6, 3rd c.BC: Theocritus Poeta Bucolicus 11.39, 55, 68.]]

__2
in combination with γε, σύ γε, σέ γε, etc. (compare ἔγωγε), thou at least, for thy part, frequently in [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Homerus Epicus]] and Attic dialect; Doric dialect τύγε [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Epicharmus Comicus [272], 5th c.BC: Timocreon Lyricus 1 (variant{τύ γα}); τύγᾰ 3rd c.BC: Theocritus Poeta Bucolicus 5.69, 71]]; Boeotian dialect τούγα [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd c.AD: Apollonius Dyscolus Grammaticus “de Pronominibus;” 55.6]]: dative σοί γε [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 1.557]]: accusative σέ γε [Refs [10.96]], etc.:—also σύ περ [Refs [24.398.]]

__3
σύ with infinitive (as imperative), [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 3.134, 4.163.]]

__II
Dual nominative and accusative σφῶϊ, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 1.336, 4.286, +others]], you two, both of you; σφώ (not σφῴ,[Refs 8th c.BC+ [compare 2nd c.AD: Apollonius Dyscolus Grammaticus “de Pronominibus;” 85.17), 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 1.574, 11.782, 13.47, 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Coloneus” 344, 1543, etc.]]—Gen. and Dat. σφῶϊν, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 4.341, +others]]; contraction σφῷν once in [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Homerus Epicus, 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 4.62, and always in _Attic dialect_ (Hdn.Gr. 1.475) and Trag., e.g. 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Prometheus Vinctus” 12, 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Coloneus” 342, “OT” 1495, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Leges” 892e (codices 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus have σφῶϊν in “Tht.” 193c, +others, σφῶν “Euthd.” 273e, +others)]]. None of these forms are enclitic, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [2nd c.AD: Apollonius Dyscolus Grammaticus “de Pronominibus;” 38.9, 85.12; codex A of 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Leges” 658c, 673e, 689a wrongly makes σφῳν]] enclitic; Ζεὺς σφὼ is prescribed in [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 15.146 by Hdn.Gr. 2.93.]] —σφῶϊ is never dative; in [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 4.286]] it is the accusative depending on κελεύ; σφῶϊν is never accusative; in [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 23.52 it is dative commodi.]]

__III
Plur. nominative ὑμεῖς, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 2.75, +others (before a vowel, 4.246, 7.194, +others), 6th c.BC: Pherecydes Syrius Philosophus 11, 3rd c.AD: Democritus Epigrammaticus 29a, 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 3.72, etc.]], ye, you; Aeolic dialect and Epic dialect ὔμμες [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 1.274, +others, 7th-6th c.BC: Sappho Lyrica 24, 25]]; Doric dialect ὑμές [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophron Comicus 60, 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Acharnenses” 760, 761, 862; ὑμέν “SIG” 685.118 (Crete, 2nd c.BC), “GDI” 5155.6 ([prev. passage], 2nd c.BC)]]; Boeotian dialect οὐμές [Refs 6th c.BC+ [6th c.BC: Corinna Lyrica 6]]; a resolved form ὑμέες, [Refs 1st c.BC+ [1st c.BC: Parthenius Mythographus “fragment” 14, is a poeticlicence (so 2nd c.AD: Apollonius Dyscolus Grammaticus “de Pronominibus;” 93.3)]] rather than genuine Ionic [Refs 5th c.BC+ [(variant in 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 8.22).]]— Gen. ὑμῶν, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Acharnenses” 143, etc.]]; ὑμέων (disyllable) [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 7.159, 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 13.7, +others, 7th c.BC: Archilochus Lyricus 74.6 (ὑμῶν codices), 6th c.BC: Solon Lyricus 11.5 (variant{ὑμῶν})]]; ὑμέων also [Refs 8th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 3.73, 6.130, +others; as _trisyllable_, 3rd c.BC: Herodas Mimographus 2.27; ὑμείων 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 4.348, 7.195, +others]]; Doric dialect ὑμέων [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophron Comicus 46]]; also ὑμῶν, [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd c.AD: Apollonius Dyscolus Grammaticus “de Pronominibus;” 95.23]]; Aeolic dialect ὑμμέων [Refs 7th c.BC+ [7th-6th c.BC: Alcaeus Lyricus 96]]; Boeotian dialect οὐμίων [Refs 6th c.BC+ [6th c.BC: Corinna Lyrica 22.]]—Dat. ὑμῖν, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 2.46, 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.126, etc.]]; Ionic dialect enclitic ὗμῐν [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd c.AD: Apollonius Dyscolus Grammaticus “de Pronominibus;” 97.28,]] also Doric dialect, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophron Comicus 91]]; Doric dialect (not enclitic) ὑμίν [ῐ] [Refs [[prev. author] 92]]; ὑμίν [ῐ] also in [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Ajax” 864, 1242, “OT” 991, 1402, “Ant.” 308, “El.” 804, +others (but ὗμιν]] should perhaps be restored where the sense needs an enclitic on the principle stated by [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd c.AD: Apollonius Dyscolus Grammaticus “de Pronominibus;” 35.6, 36.5, “Synt.” 130.23)]]; ὕμιν[Refs 8th c.BC+ [(as _enclitic_) is prescribed by Hdn.Gr. (2.124) in 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 24.33, by “Etymologicum Magnum” 432.34 in 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 1.376, 2.141, etc.:—_Aeolic dialect_ and _Epic dialect_ ὔμμῐ, ὔμμῐν, 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 2.316, 11.336, +others, 8th-7th c.BC: Hesiodus Epicus “Scutum Herculis” 328, 7th-6th c.BC: Sappho Lyrica 14, 7th-6th c.BC: Alcaeus Lyricus “Supp.” 26.9, 5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “O.” 11(10).17.]]—Acc. ὑμᾶς, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Acharnenses” 325]], etc. (-υ [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.AD: Orphica “Argonautica” 820, variant in 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Philoctetes” 222]]; ὗμας or (more probably) ὕμας is required by the metre in [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd c.AD: Babrius Fabularum Scriptor 9.9, 47.11)]]; Ionic dialect ὑμέας (disyllable) [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 21.198, +others]]; enclitic ὕμεας (disyllable) [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [3rd c.BC: Herodas Mimographus 2.60 (Papyrus)]]; ὑμέας also [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.126, +others]]; Aeolic dialect and Epic dialect ὔμμε [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 23.412, +others, 5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “I.” 6(5).19; also in 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Eumenides” 620 (trimeter), and 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Antigone” 846 (Lyric poetry)]]; Doric dialect ὑμέ [Refs 7th c.BC+ [7th c.BC: Alcman Lyricus 3, 5th c.BC: Sophron Comicus 52, 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Acharnenses” 737, “Lys.” 1076, “SIG” 528.3 (Cretan dialogue, 3rd c.BC), 622 B 8 (Cretan, 2nd c.BC).]]—The plural is sometimes used in addressing one person, when others are included in the speaker's thought, as [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 12.81, 7th c.BC: Archilochus Lyricus 89. (With σύ]] cf. Latin tu, Gothic pu; with τοι Sanskrit genitive and dative te; the origin of σφῶϊ is doubtful; with ὑμεῖς cf. Sanskrit accusative plural yusmān.)

συγγένεια, -ας, ἡ
(συγγενής), [in LXX chiefly for מִשְׁפָּחָה ;]
__1. kinship.
__2. By meton., kinsfolk, kindred: Luk.1:61, Act.7:3, 14 †
(AS)

LSJ / STEPBible (TFLSJ)
συγγέν-εια, ἡ,
kinship, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Iphigenia Aulidensis” 492, 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 3.65, etc.; πρὸς συγγενείας καὶ κηδεστίας 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Historia Graeca (Hellenica)” 2.4.21]]; ἡ πρώτη σ. primary kinship, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-3rd c.BC: Epicurus Philosophus “Sent.V at.” 61]]: with genitive, kin, relationship, with or to another, ἡ τοῦ θεοῦ σ. [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Protagoras” 322a]]; διὰ τὴν τοῦ Ἡρακλέους σ. [Refs [[prev. author] “Ly.” 205c: with _dative_, κατὰ τὴν αὑτῶν ἑκατέροις σ]]. with either of them, [Refs [[prev. author] “Plt.” 307d; σ. ἔχειν τινί [prev. work] 257d]]; ἡ πρὸς τοὺς παῖδας σ. [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Isocrates Orator 6.18]]; ἡ πρὸς ἀλλήλους σ. [Refs [[prev. author] 4.43, etc.]]: not properly applied to the relation of parents and children (see. συγγενής [Refs 4th c.BC+ [11.1 b), γένος γάρ, ἀλλ᾽ οὐχὶ συγγένεια, τοῦτ᾽ ἔστιν 4th c.BC: Isaeus Orator 8.33 (but compare 1st c.BC: Diodorus Siculus Historicus 13.20).]]

__2
ties of kindred, family connexion, family influence, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 491c, “Smp.” 178c]]; of the relation between Athens and Thebes, Decrees cited in [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 18.186.]]

__3
metaphorically, κατὰ σ. τῆς μορφῆς [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Historia Animalium” 539a22]]; ἡ πρὸς τὸ.. ἱερὸν πῦρ σ. [παντὸς πυρός] [Refs 1st c.AD+ [1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus 2.702f; ὤτων καὶ γλώττης 2nd c.AD: Lucianus Sophista “Herc.” 5]]; of metals, [Refs 3rd c.AD+ [3rd-4th c.AD: Zosimus Alchemista p.197B.]]

__4
congenital character of disease, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Hippocrates Medicus “γυναικεῖα” 2.125.]]

__II
kinsfolk, family, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Orestes” 733 (troch.), 4th-3rd c.BC: Menander Comicus 923.1]]; of a single kinsman, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Orestes” 1233]]: collectively, kinsfolk, kinsmen, [Refs [[prev. author] “Tr.” 754]]; ἡ Περικλέους ὅλη οἰκία ἢ ἄλλη σ. [NT+5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Gorgias” 472b, compare “Lg.” 627c, NT.Luke.1.61]]: plural, families, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 25.87]]; ἡ σ. ἡ Ἀγανιτέων clan, [Refs [“BCH” 46.397 (from Mylasa), compare “Michel” 476.9 (from Olymus).]]

__II.2
of animals, kind, species, παρὰ τὰς σ. συνδυάζεσθαι [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Historia Animalium” 566a26]]: generally, kind, class, [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [[prev. author] “APo.” 76a9, 3rd c.BC: Chrysippus Stoicus 2.39.]]

Abbott-Smith / STEPBible (TBESG)
σνγγενής, -ές (dative pl., -εῦσιν, Mrk.6:4, Luk.2:44, as though from -εύς, see Swete, Mk., l.with; Bl., § 8, 6; cf. 1Ma.10:89 A א2 *;)
(σύν, γένος), [in LXX for דּוֹד, דּוֹדָה, מִשְׁפָּחָה ;]
__1. congenital, natural, innate.
__2. akin to; as subst., a kinsman: Mrk.6:4, Luk.1:58 2:44 14:12 21:16, Jhn.18:26, Act.10:24; of tribal kinship, Rom.9:3 16:7, 11 16:21.†
SYN.: ἴδιος, οἰκεῖος (which see) (AS)

LSJ / STEPBible (TFLSJ)
συγγεν-ής, ές,
congenital, inborn, ἦθος [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “O.” 13.13; εὐδοξία [prev. author] “N.” 3.40]]; σ. εἶδος,= φύσις, character, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Hippocrates Medicus “περὶ χυμῶν” 1; νόσημα σ. ἐστί τινι [prev. author] “Prorrh.” 2.2; φόβος 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Eumenides” 691]]; παύροις.. ἐστι συγγενὲς τόδε natural to them, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [[prev. author] “Ag.” 832; ἡ τύχη προσγίγνεθ᾽ ἡμῖν σ. τῷ σώματι 4th-3rd c.BC: Philemo Comicus 10]]; πότμος σ. [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “N.” 5.40]]; προϊδεῖν σ. οἷς ἕπεται who have the natural gift to foresee, [Refs [[prev. work] 1.28]]; συγγενεῖς μῆνες my connate months, the months of my natural life, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Tyrannus” 1082]]; σ. τρίχες the hair born with one, i.e. the hair of the head as opposed to to the beard, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Historia Animalium” 518a18, 584a24]]; σημεῖα σ. birth-marks, [Refs [[prev. work] 585b31]]; δυνάμεις αἱ σ., opposed to αἱ ἔθει and αἱ μαθήσει, [Refs [[prev. author] “Metaphorical” 1047b31]]; αὔξει τὸ σ. increases its natural force, [Refs [[prev. author] “EN” 1119b9.]] adverb, -νῶς δύστηνος miserable from his birth, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Hercules Furens” 1293]]; see at {σύμφυτος}.

__II
of the same kin, descent, or family, akin to, τινι [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.109, 3.2, 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Heraclidae” 229]]: absolutely, akin, cognate, θεός [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Prometheus Vinctus” 14; γυνή 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Andromache” 887; χείρ 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Coloneus” 1387]]; συγγενέστατον φύσει πάντων most nearly akin, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Isaeus Orator 11.17; σ. γάμος ἀνεψιῶν 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Prometheus Vinctus” 855]]; of animals, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Historia Animalium” 539a23, “GA” 747a31, +others: hence,]]

__II.b
substantive, kinsman, relative, οὖσα σ. ἐκείνου [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Pax” 618 (troch.)]]; τῆς ἐμῆς γυναικὸς ξυγγενεῖ (dual) [Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. author] “Av.” 368 (troch.); πρὸς σ. τε καὶ οἰκείους αὐτῶν 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 378c; ἔργον εὑρεῖν συγγενῆ πένητός ἐστιν 4th-3rd c.BC: Menander Comicus 4; γάμει τὴν συγγενῆ [prev. author] 929: frequently in _plural_, οἱ σ]]. kinsfolk, kinsmen, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “P.” 4.133, 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 2.91, etc.]]; not properly applied to children (ἔκγονοι) in relation to their parents, and so opposed to ἔκγονοι in [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Isaeus Orator 8.30, see at {συγγένεια} 1 (but compare 5th-6th c.BC: Andocides Orator 1.17); τοῖς συγγενέσι τὰ τοῦ συγγενοῦς ψηφίζεσθαι 4th c.BC: Isaeus Orator 4.23.]]

__II.c
τὸ σ.,= συγγένεια, kindred, relationship, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Prometheus Vinctus” 291 (_anapaest meter_), 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Electra” 1469, 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 3.82, etc.]]; also, the spirit of one's race, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “P.” 10.12, “N.” 6.8]]; εἰ τούτῳ προσήκει Λαΐῳ τι σ. if he had any connexion with him, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Tyrannus” 814]]; of tribes, κατὰ τὸ ξ. [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 1.95.]]

__II.2

LSJ / STEPBible (TFLSJ)
σῡλ-άω,
imperfect contraction in Epic dialect ἐσύλα, σύλα, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 6.28, 4.116]]; Ionic dialect Iterat. σύλασκε [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th-7th c.BC: Hesiodus Epicus “Scutum Herculis” 480]]:—passive, future συληθήσομαι [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Prometheus Vinctus” 761, συλήσομαι 2nd c.AD: Pausanias Periegeta 4.7.10]]:—strip off, especially strip off the arms of a slain enemy, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Homerus Epicus (only in 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad”), Lyric poetry, etc. Construction:]]

__1
in full, with accusative person et of things, strip off from another, strip him of his arms (compare σκυλεύω), μή μιν Ἀχαιοὶ τεύχεα συλήσωσι [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 15.428, compare 16.500]]; ἔπειτα δὲ καὶ τὰ (i.e. ἔναρα).. νεκροὺς ἂμ πεδίον συλήσετε [Refs 5th c.BC+ [6.71; με κασίγνητον συλᾷς 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Iphigenia Taurica” 157 (_anapaest meter_); τὴν θεὸν τοὺς στεφάνους σεσυλήκασιν 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 24.182]]:— passive, with accusative of things, to be stripped, robbed, deprived of a thing, σκῆπτρα συληθήσεται [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Prometheus Vinctus” 761]]; ταῦτ᾽ (i.e. τὰ τόξα) ἐσυλήθην ἐγώ [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Philoctetes” 413; λέκτρα συλᾶσθαι βίᾳ 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Iphigenia Aulidensis” 1275; συληθεὶς τὰς βοῦς 5th-6th c.BC: Isocrates Orator 6.19; σεσυλήμεθα τὰ ἡμέτερα ὑπὸ τούτων 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 35.26.]]

__2
with accusative, strip a person of his arms, ἦ τινα συλήσων νεκύων [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 10.343]]: generally, pillage, plunder, τὰ ἱρά, τοὺς θεούς, etc., [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 6.101, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Leges” 864d, etc.; τοὺς νεώς 5th-6th c.BC: Isocrates Orator 4.155; θεῶν βρέτη 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Persae” 810; νεκρόν 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 469d]]:—passive, βαρβάρων συλᾶσθ᾽ ὕπο [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Helena” 600.]]

__3
with accusative of things, strip off, ὄφρα τάχιστα τεύχεα συλήσειε [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 4.466, etc.; frequently with additions, ἀπ᾽ ὤμων τεύχε᾽ ἐσύλα 6.28, etc.; τὰ μὲν ἔντε᾽ ἀπὸ χροὸς.. συλήσας 13.641.]]

__3.b
take off or out, ἐσύλα τόξον took out the bow [from its case], [Refs [4.105]]; σύλα πῶμα φαρέτρης took the lid off the quiver, [Refs [[prev. work] 116]]; with a notion of violence or suddenness, κρᾶτα σ. Μεδοίσας [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “P.” 12.16.]]

__3.c
carry off, τοὺς πολεμίους οὐ συλήσειν αὐτά (i.e. τὰ χρήματα) will not seize them as booty, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 5.36, compare 9.116]]; θεῶν γέρα σ. [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Prometheus Vinctus” 83, compare 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Coloneus” 922, “Ph.” 1365; λόγοις τὰ τῶν προγόνων ἔργα συλήσας καὶ διασύρας 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 19.313; σ. κατὰ βραχὺ τὴν τῶν πυρετῶν διάθεσιν 7th c.AD: Stephanus Medicus “in Gal.” 1.295 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator]]:—passive, to be carried off as spoil, ἄγαλμα σεσυλημένον [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 6.118]]; to be taken away, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Hippolytus” 799: _metaphorically_, συλᾶται ὕπνος ἀπὸ γλεφάρων 5th c.BC: Bacchylides Lyricus “fragment” 3.10.]]

__3.d
exercise right of σῦλαι, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [“IG” 9(1).333.3 (_Locrian dialect_, 5th c.BC):]] —passive, πανταχοῦ συλωμένων ἡμῶν the right of reprisals was exercised against us everywhere, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Isocrates Orator 3.33.]]

__4
after [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Homerus Epicus,]] with accusative person et genitive _of things_, τίς σε δαίμων συλᾷ πάτρα; carries thee away from.. , [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Helena” 669:]] —passive, συλαθεὶς ἀγενείων stealing from among the boys, and enlisting among the men, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “O.” 9.89.]]

συλ-λαμβάνω
[in LXX for תָּפַשׂ, הָרָה, etc. ;]
__1. with accusative, to bring together, collect.
__2. to seize, take: with accusative of person(s), as a prisoner, Mat.26:55, Mrk.14:48, Luk.22:54, Jhn.18:12, Act.1:16 12:3; pass., Act.23:27; mid., in sense of act., Act.26:21; σ. ἄγραν ἰχθύων, Luk.5:9.
__3. C. dative of person(s), to take part with, assist, succour; mid., in same sense: Luk.5:7, Php.4:3.
__4. Of a woman, to conceive: absol., Luk.1:24; before ἐν γαστρί, Luk.1:31; with accusative, Luk.1:36; ib. before ἐν τ. κοιλίᾳ, Luk.2:21; metaphorically, of lust producing sin, Jas.1:15.†

LSJ / STEPBible (TFLSJ)
συλλαμβάνω,
future -λήψομαι: perfect -είληφα, passive -είλημμαι: aorist συνέλᾰβον, infinitive συλλᾰβεῖν:—middle, present in [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-3rd c.BC: Philemo Comicus 53.4]]: aorist συνελαβόμην [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 3.49, etc.]]:—passive (see. below; in [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 7.2.14 συλληφθήσεται has been restored for συλλήψεται)]]:—collect, gather together, especially rally scattered troops, τῆς στρατιῆς τοὺς περιγενομένους [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 5.46; τὸ στράτευμα 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 3.3.1; τὰς δυνάμεις 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Gorgias” 456a; σ. θοινάτορας 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Ion” 1217.]]

__2
take with one, carry off, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Trachiniae” 1153; ξυλλαβὼν κατέκλινεν αὐτὸν εἰς Ἀσκληπιοῦ 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Vespae” 122, compare “Anthologia Graeca” 5.52 (tmesis, 3rd c.BC: Dioscorides Epigrammaticus)]]; συλλαβὼν θεσπίσματα κεῖται παρ᾽ Ἅιδῃ with all his prophecies, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Tyrannus” 971; ἔρρε, τάσδε συλλαβὼν ἀράς [prev. author] “OC” 1384]]; ἔκπλει σεαυτὸν συλλαβὼν ἐκ τῆσδε γῆς pack yourself off, [Refs [[prev. author] “Ph.” 577.]]

__3
put together, close, τὸ στόμα καὶ τοὺς ὀφθαλμούς (of a corpse) [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Phaedo” 118a]]; ξ. αὐτοῦ τὸ στόμα shut his mouth, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Acharnenses” 926, compare 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Historia Animalium” 623b2]]; enclose, τῇ ἐπιδέσει συλλαμβάνοντα συνάγειν τοὺς μηρούς [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd c.AD: Soranus Medicus 2.86; ξ. καὶ τοὺς τένοντας τοῖσι ἐρίοισι 2nd c.AD: Aretaeus Medicus “ὀξέων νούσων θεραπευτικόν” 1.6.]]

__3.b
combine in pronunciation, λέγε δὴ μόλωμεν ξυνεχὲς ὡδὶ ξυλλαβών say αὐτὸ μόλωμεν as one word, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Equites” 21.]]

__4
in speaking, comprehend, comprise, ἑνὶ ἔπεϊ πάντα συλλαβόντα εἰπεῖν [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 3.82; πᾶν.. συλλαβὼν εἴρηκας [prev. author] 7.16]].; εἰς ἓν πάντα σ. [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Sophista” 234b, compare “Tht.” 147d; τὰ ἄλλα εἰς ταὐτό [prev. author] “Plt.” 263d]]:—passive, to be comprehended (logically), μετὰ τοῦ γένους αἱ συλλαμβανόμεναι διαφοραί [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Metaphysica” 1037b31, compare 998b28]]; σὺν τῇ ὕλῃ συνειλημμένος, i.e. concrete, opposed to abstract, [Refs [[prev. work] 1039b21, compare 1035a25, +others]]

__II
lay hands on, seize, ὁλκάδας [Refs 7th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 6.26; κόμην ἀπρὶξ ὄνυξι συλλαβὼν χερί 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Ajax” 310; τέττιγα τοῦ πτεροῦ 7th c.BC: Archilochus Lyricus 143 (loosely paraphrased, compare “Hermes” 23.279); τὰ ποτήμενα συλλαβῆν 3rd c.BC: Theocritus Poeta Bucolicus 29.30]]; ξ. τῶν σχοινίων lay hold of them, help to pull, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Pax” 437:]] —middle, τίς ξυλλάβοιτ᾽ ἂν τοῦ ξύλο; [Refs [[prev. author] “Lys.” 313, compare “Pax” 465 (Lyric poetry).]]

__II.b

__II.2
seize the person of.., apprehend, arrest, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [Inscriptiones Graecae 12.39.7, 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 2.121.έ, 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Acharnenses” 206, 5th c.BC: Antipho Orator 5.29, 5th-6th c.BC: Andocides Orator 1.45, “PCair.Zen.” 15v. 44, 202.2 (3rd c.BC); συνέλαβον αὐτὸν καὶ ἀπήχθη εἰς τὸ δεσμωτήριον [prev. work] 484.21 (3rd c.BC)]]; σ. ζῶντα, ὅμηρον, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Rhesus” 513, “Or.” 1189; τινὰ ἐπὶ θανάτῳ 5th-6th c.BC: Isocrates Orator 4.154]]; συλλαβόντας αὐτὸν ἴσχειν seize and hold him, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [“IG” 42(1).122.40 (Epid., 4th c.BC):]] — passive, πρὶν ξυλληφθῆναι before they were arrested, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 1.20, compare 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.80, +others, 5th-6th c.BC: Andocides Orator 1.101, “PCair.Zen.” 15v. 7 (3rd c.BC).]]

__II.3
of the mind, grasp the meaning of, comprehend, τὸ χρηστήριον, τὸ ῥηθέν, τὸν λόγον, τὴν φωνήν, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.63, 91, 2.49, 4.114; παρκείμενον συλλαβὼν τέρας 5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “O.” 13.73, compare 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Sophista” 218c, etc.]]

__III

__IV
of females, conceive, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Historia Animalium” 582a19, “GA” 727b8, 2nd c.AD: Soranus Medicus 1.28, etc.; ἐν γαστρί 5th c.BC: Hippocrates Medicus “ἀφορισμοί” 5.46; ξυλλαβοῦσα τὴν γονήν [prev. author] “Steril.” 220]]; of the womb, σ. τὸ σπέρμα [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Historia Animalium” 583b29, +others, compare 2nd c.AD: Lucianus Sophista “VH” 1.22: but συνειληφυῖα τοῦ τεκεῖν]] near to be delivered, [LXX.1Ki.4.19.]

__V
take with or besides, take as an assistant, τὴν δίκην σ. [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Fragmenta” 584; ἄτεγκτον σ. καρδίαν [prev. author] “HF” 833.]]

__VI
with dative person, take pert with another, assist him, οὐ τοῖς ἀθύμοις ἡ τύχη ξ. [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Fragmenta” 927, compare 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Medea” 813, 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 6.125, etc.]]; τὰ δυνατὰ τῇ πόλει ξ. [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Ecclesiazusae” 861]]; σ. τισί τι take part with or assist them in a thing, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. author] “Lys.” 540 (Lyric poetry), 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 7.5.49, etc.; σ. τινί τινος 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Medea” 946, 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Vespae” 734 (Lyric poetry); σ. τινί τινι 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 18.20: with a _preposition_, συνέλαβε γὰρ ἄλλα.. ἐς τὸ πείθεσθαι]] contributed towards persuading, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 7.6, compare 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Memorabilia” 2.6.28]]: absolutely, assist, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Choephori” 812 (Lyric poetry), 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Trachiniae” 1019 (Lyric poetry), 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Equites” 229, 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 1.118]]; δεῖ δὲ ξυλλαμβάνοντα τοὺς θεοὺς ἐπικαλέεσθαι while invoking the gods one must help oneself, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Hippocrates Medicus “Insomn.” 87.]]

middle, c.genitive of things, take part in, συνελάβοντο τοῦ στρατεύματος [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 3.49; ὅστις νόσου κάμνοντι συλλάβοιτο 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Philoctetes” 282]]; ξυνελάβοντο τοῦ τοιούτου οὐχ ἥκιστα, ὥστε.. especially contributed to this, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 4.47: with _dative_, καιρῷ χειμῶνος συλλαβέσθαι κυβερνητικήν]] intervene in a storm together with circumstance, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Leges” 709c: sometimes in tmesi, ξύμ μοι λάβεσθε τοῦ μύθου [prev. author] “Phdr.” 237a, compare “Anthologia Graeca” 9.559 (1st c.BC-1st c.AD: Crinagoras Epigrammaticus).]]

__2

__3

[Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “de Equitum magistro” 2.5; χρηστόν τι σ. παρὰ θεῶν 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 1.11; τοὐναντίον συμβαίνειν πέφυκε 2nd c.AD: Galenus Medicus 15.460: with _dative_, [prev. work]67, 16.724: also euphemistic, ἄν τι ξυμβῇ]] if anything happen (i.e. any evil), [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 21.112, compare “Riv.Fil.” 60.59 (2nd c.BC)]]: generally, occur, be found, exist, ἐν τῇ ἀρχαίᾳ ἡμετέρᾳ φωνῇ σ. τὸ ὄνομα [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Cratylus” 398b, compare 2nd c.AD: Apollonius Dyscolus Grammaticus “de Pronominibus;” 29.15: but,]]

τὸ συμβεβηκός chance event, contingency, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. author] “Prm.” 128c; τὰ συμβαίνοντα 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 1.6.43; τὰ συμβάντα [prev. author] “An.” 3.1.13; ἀπὸ τοῦ συμβαίνοντος ὁ τόπος εἴληφε τὴν προσηγορίαν 2nd c.BC: Polybius Historicus 10.28.7: hence κατὰ συμβεβηκός]] by accident, contingently (see. below iv.
