Alcaeus 1.130c, “Cra.” 398e; δοκεῖ τὸ μαντεῖον τοὐναντίον ξυμβῆναι ἢ.. 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 2.17; τοιούτου τούτου συμβάντος [prev. author] 1.74]]; συμβαίνει καὶ σοὶ (i.e. ἄριστον) [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Leges” 903d]]: absolutely, turn out well, ἢν ξυμβῇ ἡ πεῖρα [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 3.3; εἴ μοι σ. τοῦτο 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Leges” 744a.]]

__III.3
of consequences, come out, result, follow, δαπανῶντες ἐς τοιαῦτα ἀφ᾽ ὦν ἡ ἀσθένεια ξυμβαίνει [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 8.45; κάλλιστον δὴ ἔργων ὑμῖν ξυμβήσεται [prev. author] 6.33]]; τὰ συμβάντα, opposed to ἡ προαίρεσις, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 18.192; δηλοῦται ἐκ τοῦ συμβάντος 2nd c.AD: Galenus Medicus 16.583; ἐὰν μὴ ὅτι τάχος ἀποσταλῇ τὰ ὑποζύγια, συμβήσεται τὰ μελίσσεια ἀπολέσθαι “PCair.Zen.” 467.8, compare 481.2, +others (3rd c.BC).]]

__III.3.b
of logical conclusions, result, follow, frequently in [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus and 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Gorgias” 459b, etc.; σ. ἐκ τῶν κειμένων 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Topica” 156b38, +others, compare 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 25.73]]: impersonal, it follows, with infinitive, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Theaetetus” 170c, “Phd.” 74a, 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Ethica Nicomachea” 1152b25, +others; also σ. μήτε κουφότητ᾽ ἔχειν μήτε βάρος, ἔπειθ᾽ ὅτι ἀδύνατον κινηθῆναι 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “de Caelo” 270a5: also _person_, συμβαίνει εἶναι or γίγνεσθαι]] turns out to be, i.e. consequently or inevitably is or happens, κάθαρσις εἶναι τοῦτο σ. [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Phaedo” 67c, compare 80b, “Cra.” 396a, “Phlb.” 55a, 64e, “Prm.” 134b, “R.” 438e; ὅσα συμβαίνει γίγνεσθαι κακὰ καὶ ὅσα συμβήσεται [prev. author] “Plt.” 301e: hence συμβεβηκός (see. below iv. 2).]]

__IV
in Philos., τὸ συμβεβηκός has two senses:

__IV.1
a contingent attribute or 'accident' (in the modern sense), [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Analytica Posteriora” 73b4, “Top.” 102b4, +others]]; κατὰ συμβεβηκός 'accidentally', opposed to καθ᾽ αὑτό, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [[prev. author] “Ph.” 192b22, compare “Metaphorical” 1052a18, 4th-3rd c.BC: Theophrastus Philosophus “de Sensu” 22]]; opposed to ἁπλῶς, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Analytica Posteriora” 71b10, +others]]; opposed to φύσει, [Refs [[prev. author] “de An.” 406a14]]; opposed to κυρίως, πρώτως, [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd c.AD: Galenus Medicus 15.629, compare 16.575, +others]]; opposed to ἄντικρυς, [Refs [[prev. author] 18(2).180.]]

__IV.2
an attribute necessarily resulting from the notion of a thing, but not entering into the definition thereof, οἷον τῷ τριγώνῳ τὸ δύο ὀρθὰς ἔχειν [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Metaphysica” 1025a31]]; distinguished by the addition of καθ᾽ αὑτό, [Refs [[prev. author] “APo.” 83b19, +others]]; in Epicurus, essential attribute, property, opposed to σύμπτωμα 'accident', τὰ τούτων συμπτώματα ἢ σ. [Refs 1st c.BC+ [“Ep.” 1p.6U., compare “Nat.” 4 G., +others; σ. ἀνθρώπου τὸ θνητὸν εἶναι 1st c.BC: Philodemus Philosophus “περὶ σημείων καὶ σημειώσεων” 3, +others]]; in the Stoics, consequence, opposed to αἴτιον, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-3rd c.BC: Zeno Citieus Stoicus 1.25.]]

Abbott-Smith / STEPBible (TBESG)
συν-βάλλω
(Rec. συμ-), [in LXX: 2Ch.25:19 (גָּרָה hith.), Isa.46:6 (זוּל), Jer.43:3 (סוּת hi.), Wis.5:8, al. ;]
to throw together, hence,
__(a) of speech (before λόγους, Eur., al.), to discuss, confer (sc. λόγους): with dative of person(s), Luk.11:53, WH, mg., Act.17:18; before πρὸς ἀλλήλους, Act.4:15;
__(b) to reflect, consider, ponder: ἐν τ. καρδίᾳ, Luk.2:19;
__(with) to meet with, fall in with: Act.20:14; in hostile sense, εἰς πόλεμον, with dative (εἰς μάχην, Polyb.), Luk.14:31;
__(d) mid., to contribute (Polyb., al.; cf. MM, xxiv): Act.18:27.†
(AS)

LSJ / STEPBible (TFLSJ)
συμβάλλω,
future -βᾰλῶ: aorist -έβᾰλον, infinitive -βᾰλεῖν: perfect -βέβληκα: aorist 1 passive -εβλήθην:—of these tenses [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Homerus Epicus uses only]]present active, aorist active and middle, but most commonly Epic dialect intransitive aorist forms συμβλήτην, -βλήμεναι, middle σύμβλητο, -βληντο, -βλήμενος, subjunctive 2nd pers. singular -βλήεαι probably conjecture for -βλήσεαι in [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 20.335]], 3rd.pers. singular contraction -βληται[Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 7.204]]:—throw together, dash together, σύν ῥ᾽ ἔβαλον ῥινούς, of men in close combat, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 4.447, 8.61; ἀσπίδας 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Phoenissae” 1405, 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Pax” 1274 (hexameters), 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Historia Graeca (Hellenica)” 4.3.19, etc.]]; bring together, unite, e.g. of rivers that fall into one another, ἐς μισγάγκειαν συμβάλλετον ὄβριμον ὕδωρ [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 4.453; ῥοὰς Σιμόεις συμβάλλετον ἠδὲ Σκάμανδρος 5.774]]:— middle, πολλοὶ ποταμοὶ σ. τὸ σφέτερον ὕδωρ [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 4.50 (compare δάκρυα δάκρυσι σ. 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Orestes” 336 (Lyric poetry, _active_))]]; ὁ Ἀκεσίνης τῷ Ἰνδῷ τὸ ὕδωρ σ. [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd c.AD: Arrianus Historicus “Anabasis” 6.1.5]]; σ. τὰ ὦτα πρὸς τὴν γῆν have their ears reaching to.., [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Historia Animalium” 606a15:]] —passive, κατὰ τὰς ῥᾶγας συμβεβλημένων [τῶν δακτύλων] [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd c.AD: Soranus Medicus 2.60.]]

__2
collect, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 2.1.5]]; store up, accumulate, κριθὰς ἵπποις συμβεβλημένας πολλάς [Refs [[prev. author] “An.” 3.4.31.]]

__3
jumble up together, διαφέροντα σ. εἰς ταὐτόν [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Politicus” 285a.]]

__4
intransitive in active, fit [Refs 4th c.BC+ [compare (σύμβολον 1.1), 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Ethica Eudemia” 1239b14]]; to be suitable, τὰ χεδροπὰ σ. εἰς τὰς νέας [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-3rd c.BC: Theophrastus Philosophus “de Causis Plantarum” 3.20.7]] (unless = sow, set).

__4.b
to be profitable, σ. τῷ πολιτικῷ.. δικαίῳ εἶναι [Refs 5th c.BC+ [1st c.BC: Philodemus Gadarensis Epigrammaticus “Rh.” 2.285 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus; σ. ἀναμένειν ἡμέραν μίαν 2nd c.AD: Galenus Medicus 16.496.]]

__5
intransitive, come together, ἔνθα δίστομοι.. σ. ὁδοί where two roads join, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Coloneus” 901, compare 1st c.BC-1st c.AD: Strabo Geographus 6.3.7]]; τὰ συμβάλλοντα the watersmeet, [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [Inscriptiones Graecae 9(2) p.xi (Delph., 3rd-2nd c.BC)]]; [φλὲψ] σ. τῇ ἀποσχίσει [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Historia Animalium” 514a12]]; collide, τοὺς τύπους ἀνάγκη συμβάλλειν ἑαυτοῖς [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-3rd c.BC: Theophrastus Philosophus “de Sensu” 52]]: Geometry texts, meet, τὸ σημεῖον, καθ᾽ ὃ συμβάλλουσιν the point in which (the straight lines) meet, [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [3rd c.BC: Archimedes Geometra “περὶ σφαίρας καὶ κυλίνδρου” 1.23, etc.]]

__6
βλέφαρα σ. ὕπνῳ close the eyes in sleep, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Agamemnon” 15; σ. ὄμμα, in death, [prev. work] 1294 (but ποῖον ὄμμα συμβαλῶ]]; how shall I meet her eyes with mine? [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Iphigenia Aulidensis” 455).]]

__7
generally, join, unite, σ. σχοινία twist ropes (compare συμβολεύς), [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Pax” 37; so τοπεῖα “IG” 22.1672.311 (4th c.BC)]]; ὠμόλινον σ. πεντάπλουν [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Hippocrates Medicus “περὶ συρίγγων” 4; στέφανον 2nd-3rd c.AD: Philostratus Sophista “Her.Prooem.”; [αἱ φλέβες] σ. [τὸ σῶμα] εἰς ἕν 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “de Partibus Animalium” 668b24]]; fit together, ἁρμούς [Refs 4th c.BC+ [“IG” 7.4255.23 (Oropus, 4th c.BC); σ. καὶ κολλῆσαι [prev. work] 22.1668.73 (4th c.BC)]]; κεραῖαι συμβεβλημέναι [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [“PCair.Zen.” 566.10 (3rd c.BC)]]; δεξιὰς σ. ἀλλήλοισι join hands, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Iphigenia Aulidensis” 58.]]

__8
σ. συμβόλαιά τινι or πρός τινα make a contract with a person, especially lend him money on bond, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 34.1, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 425c, compare 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 5.77 (_middle_)]]; συμβόλαιον εἰς τἀνδράποδα συμβεβλημένον money lent on the security of the slaves, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 27.27]]: absolutely, in same sense, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Isocrates Orator 21.13]]; make a contract, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus Alcaeus1.125d, “OGI” 669.21 (Egypt, 1st c.AD), “Codex Justinianus [4th-6th c.AD]” 1.3.55.4]]; of a marriage contract, Mitteis [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [“Chr.” 372 vi 22, compare 8 (2nd c.AD)]]; advance, lend, πέρα μεδίμνου κριθῶν [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Isaeus Orator 10.10]]; ἱμάτια, χρυσία, etc., [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Ecclesiazusae” 446]]; ἐπί τισι on certain terms, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [1st c.BC: Dionysius Halicarnassensis 6.29; σ. δανεισμῷ 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Leges” 921d]]; ὁ συμβαλών the lender, creditor, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 56.2, compare 1st c.BC: Dionysius Halicarnassensis 5.63 (but οἱ συμβ]]. the borrowers, debtors, [Refs [[prev. author] 4.9)]]:— middle, with perfect passive, pay a share, contribute, ὁλκάδα οἱ συμβαλέεσθαι give him a merchant-vessel, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 3.135, compare 5th c.BC: Lysias Orator 32.24, 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Agesilaus” 2.27]]; σ. χρήματά τινι εἰς τροφὴν τῶν στρατιωτῶν advance it, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [[prev. author] “An.” 1.1.9, compare “IG” 7.2418 (Thebes, 4th c.BC)]]; τριήρεις εἰς κίνδυνον [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Isocrates Orator 4.98; ἐφόδιον “PSI” 4.407.12 (3rd c.BC).]]

__9
generally, contribute:— passive, συμβάλλεταί τις.. μερίς [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd c.AD: Alexander Rhetor 149.4:]] —in this sense mostly in middle, τέμενος συμβάλλεσθαι add thereto, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “I.” 1.59; ἡ τύχη οὐδὲν ἔλασσον ξυμβάλλεται ἐς τὸ ἐπαίρειν 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 3.45, compare 5th c.BC: Hippocrates Medicus “Aër.” 2, 3rd c.BC(?): Sosipater Comicus 1.37, 4th-3rd c.BC: Damoxenus Comicus 2.11]]; τὸ μὴ ἀγανακτεῖν.. ἄλλα τέ μοι πολλὰ συμβάλλεται, καὶ.. many circumstances contribute to my feeling no vexation, and especially.., [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Apologia” 36a; σ. βοήθειαν οὐ σμικρὰν πρός τι [prev. author] “Lg.” 836b]]; τιμὴν καὶ δόξαν τῇ πόλει σ. [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Isocrates Orator “Epistulae” 8.6; οὐ δεῖ λογίζεσθαι, πότερος πλείω συμβέβληται 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Oeconomicus” 7.13]]; frequently with μέρος as object, ἔργων οὐκ ἐλάχιστον μέρος σ. [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Andocides Orator 1.143; μέρος σ. πρὸς ἀρετήν 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Leges” 836d, compare “R.” 331b, 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 41.11; οὐκ ἐλάχιστον μέρος πρὸς εὐδαιμονίαν 5th-6th c.BC: Isocrates Orator 7.79; συμβαλλέσθω τὸ μέρος ἕκαστος εἰς τὸ ἀνάλωμα “PHal.” 1.108, compare 113 (3rd c.BC)]]; τὴν μεγίστην εἰς αὐτὰ μοῖραν [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Timaeus” 47c, compare 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 6.1.28: also _absolutely_, οὔτε ποταμὸς οὔτε κρήνη οὐδεμία ἐσδιδοῦσα ἐς πλῆθός οἱ συμβάλλεται]] contributes to its volume, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 4.50; σ. πρὸς τὸ λανθάνειν 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 2.4.21, compare 5th-6th c.BC: Isocrates Orator 7.21]]; συμβαλλόμενα contributory causes, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-3rd c.BC: Theophrastus Philosophus “de Sudore” 6]]: absolutely, to be helpful, πολλά ἐστι τὰ συμβαλλόμενα τοῖς βουλομένοις [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Antipho Orator 5.79, compare 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Leges” 905b, 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 21.133]]; φόνου κηκὶς ξ. contributes to the proof, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Choephori” 1012: rarely with _genitive_ _partitive_, ξυμβάλλεται πολλὰ τοῦδε δείματος]] many things contribute [their share] of this fear, i.e. join in causing it, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Medea” 284.]]

__10
συμβάλλεσθαι γνώμας contribute one's opinion to a discussion, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 8.61; περί τινος 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Politicus” 298c; συμβαλέσθαι περί τινος λόγους 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 2.2.21]]; λόγον σ. περὶ βίου contribute an opinion about life, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Leges” 905c]]; also συμβαλέσθαι τι to have something to say, [Refs [[prev. author] “Ion” 532c, compare 533a]]; ταῦτά σοι περὶ Ἔρωτος σ. [Refs [[prev. author] “Smp.” 185c]]; συμβαλοῦ γνώμην contribute your opinion, help in judging, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Coloneus” 1151]]; σ. τὴν γνώμην τῆς βουλῆς, with or without εἰς τὸν δῆμον, communicate it, [Refs [“IG” 22.79.6, 103.17, +others]]; cast votes, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [“Schwyzer” 84.15 (Tylisus, 5th c.BC).]]

__II
συμβάλλειν (i.e. λόγους) converse, σ. τινί or πρός τινα, [NT+1st c.AD+ [1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus 2.222c, NT.Act.4.15:—]]middle, ἀτὰρ τί ἐγὼ περὶ κλοπῆς σ.; [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 4.6.14.]]

__II
bring men together in hostile sense, pit them against each other, match them, ἀμφοτέρους θεοὶ σύμβαλον [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 20.55; ἐμὲ.. καὶ Μενέλαον συμβάλετε.. μάχεσθαι 3.70]]; σ. σκύμνον λέοντος σκύλακι κυνός set one to fight with the other, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 3.32]]; ἄνδρα ἀνδρὶ καὶ ἵππον ἵππῳ σ. [Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. author] 5.1; τοὺς ἡβῶντας σ. εἰς ἔριν περὶ ἀρχῆς 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Respublica Lacedaemoniorum” 4.2]]; ἀλεκτρυόνας σ. [Refs 4th c.BC+ [[prev. author] “Smp.” 4.9; ἄνδρας φίλους [prev. author] “Cyr.” 6.1.32; εἰς χεῖρα δοῦλον δεσπότῃ μὴ συμβάλῃς 4th-3rd c.BC: Philemo Comicus 206: _metaphorically_, ἀναισχυντίᾳ σ. τινὰ καὶ προσγυμνάζειν]] make him contend with.., [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Leges” 647c.]]

__II.b
middle, join in fight, σὺν δ᾽ ἐβάλοντο μάχεσθαι ἐναντίον [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 12.377.]]

__II.c
intransitive, come together, σύμβαλον μάχεσθαι [Refs [16.565]]; also ς. alone, come to blows, engage, πρίν γ᾽ ἠὲ ξυμβλήμεναι ἠὲ δαμῆναι [Refs 5th c.BC+ [21.578; frequently in 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus, either _absolutely_, as 1.77, 82, or with _dative_ _person_, [prev. work] 80, 104]]; Ἄρης Ἄρει δυμβαλεῖ, Δίκα Δίκᾳ [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Choephori” 461 (Lyric poetry)]]; Ἕλληνες Μήδοις σ. [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Simonides Lyricus 136; also σ. πρός τινα 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 7.1.20, 5th-6th c.BC: Isocrates Orator 4.69; εἰς μονομαχίαν πρός τινα 1st c.BC-1st c.AD: Strabo Geographus 14.5.16]]; συμβάλλων coming into collision, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Politicus” 273a, cf. Wilcken “Chr.” 16.6 (2nd c.AD).]]

__II.2
σ. πόλεμον καὶ δηϊοτῆτα engage in war, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 12.181 (probably interpolated)]]; so in Trag., σ. βάκχαις μάχην [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Bacchae” 837; ἔχθραν τινί [prev. author] “Med.” 44; ἔριν φίλοις [prev. work] 521: _metaphorically_, συμβαλεῖν ἔπη κακά]] bandy reproaches, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Ajax” 1323; αἰσχρὸν δέ μοι γυναιξὶ συμβάλλειν λόγους 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Iphigenia Aulidensis” 830.]]

__II.3
middle, fall in with one, meet him, with dative, frequently in [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Homerus Epicus, who uses _Epic dialect_]]aorist forms beginning ξυμβλη- or συμβλη- solely in this sense, Νέστορι δὲ ξύμβληντο [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 14.27, compare 39; εἰ δ᾽ ἄρα τις.. ξύμβληται ὁδίτης 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 7.204; ξυμβλήμενος ἄλλος ὁδίτης 11.127]]; ὅτε κεν συμβλήσεαι (to be read -βλήεαι) αὐτῷ [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 20.335; ξυμβλήτην ἀλλήλοιιν 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 21.15.]]

__II.4
so in active, συμβαλών having met, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Choephori” 677]]; οἱ συμβάλλοντες those who come in contact with one, [Refs 1st c.AD+ [1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus “Marcellus” 20]]; φιλοσόφῳ σ. συμφέρω,
future συνοίσω [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Septem contra Thebas” 510]]: aorist 1 συνήνεγκα [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Hercules Furens” 488]], Ionic dialect -ήνεικα[Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 7.152]]: aorist 2 συνήνεγκον [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 2.51]]: perfect συνενήνοχα [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 18.198.]]

__A
active

__I

[Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 1.99]]; especially of dead bodies, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 6.4.9, 4th c.BC: Lycurgus Orator 45 codices]]

__I.4

[Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 4.3.13]]; ἐγώ σοι ξυμφέρω (i.e. τὴν παμπησίαν) [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Ecclesiazusae” 869]]; bring with, λύχνον.. παῖς μοι συμφέρει [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Epicharmus Comicus 35.8]]; of sufferings, labours, and the like, bear jointly, help to bear, ξυνοίσω πᾶν ὅσονπερ ἂν σθένω [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Electra” 946; σ. κακά 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Hercules Furens” 1366; πένθος τινί [prev. author] Alcaeus370; τὰς τούτων ἁμαρτίας 5th c.BC: Antipho Orator]]

__I.3
[Refs [2.11: hence,]]suffer, bear with, indulge, ὀργὰς ξυνοίσω σοι [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Eumenides” 848.]]

__II
intransitive, confer a benefit, be useful or profitable, οὔ οἱ συνήνεικε τὸ ἔχθος did not do him any good, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 9.37; τὸ καὶ συνήνεικε ποιησάσῃ [prev. author] 8.87; καλῶς ἂν ἡμῖν ξυμφέροι ταῦτα 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Supplices” 753, compare 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Acharnenses” 252; τοῦτο σ. τῷ βίῳ [prev. author] “Pl.” 38]]; ἅπαντ᾽ ἐπὶ τὸ βέλτιον ξ. turn out for the best, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. author] “Ec.” 475; σῖτον.. καὶ οἶνον.. καὶ εἴ τι ἄλλο βρῶμα, οἷ᾽ ἂν ἐς πολιορκίαν ξυμφέρῃ 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 4.26; πάντα ὅσα ἂν οἴηται συνοίσειν αὐτοῖς πρὸς τὸν βίον 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Memorabilia” 2.2.5; ὃ σ. πρὸς τὴν πολιτείαν 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Politica” 1272a30, etc.]]

__II.3

__II.3.b

[Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aeschines Orator 3.80; τὸ σ. τινός 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 338c, 340c, +others; τὸ σ. τινί [prev. work] 341d, 342b, 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 18.139; πρὸς τὸ σ. αὑτῷ “PCair.Zen.” 451.15 (3rd c.BC): frequently also in _plural_, τὰ σ. 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Philoctetes” 131, etc.]]; τὰ μικρὰ σ., opposed to τὰ ὅλα, the petty interests, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 18.28; τὰ συμφέροντα ἀνθρώποις 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Leges” 875a, compare “IG” 42(1).68.84 (Epid., 4th c.BC)]]; but also τὰ τῆς πατρίδος σ. [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th-3rd c.BC: Dinarchus Orator 1.99, compare 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Politicus” 297a, 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 18.120, etc.]]; also in aorist participle, τό τῳ ξυνενεγκόν [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 2.51]]; συμφέρον ἐστί, = {συμφέρει}, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [1st c.AD(?): Heraclitus 8, 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Plutus” 49, 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 6.1.26, etc.]]; εἰ μὴ ξυμφέρον (i.e. ἐστί) [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 3.44.]]

__III
intransitive, also,

__III.1
work with, assist, σφῷν ὅπως ἄριστα συμφέροι θεός [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Philoctetes” 627; πάντα συμφέρουσ᾽ Ἰάσονι 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Medea” 13]]; συμφέροντι (or Συμφέροντι as proper name) Ἡρακλεῖ [Refs [“IG” 22.2114.]]

σύν (old Att. ξύν),
prep. with dative,
expressing association, fellowship and inclusion. It gradually gave way to μετά, with genitive (cf. LS, see word; Bl., §41, 3), and is therefore comparatively infrequent in NT, being rare in Mat.4, Mrk.6, Jhn.3, and elsewhere (exx. Jas.1:11, 2Pe.1:18) only in Lk (Gosp. and Ac) and Paul. With, together with: of companionship and association, Luk.2:13, Jhn.21:3, Act.10:23, al.; εἶναι σύν τινι, Luk.7:12, Act.4:13, Php.1:23, al.; of partisanship, Act.4:13; οἱ σύν τινι, of attendants, companions or colleagues, Mrk.2:26, Luk.5:9, Act.5:17, al.; of assistance, ἡ χάρις τ. θεοῦ σὺν ἐμοί, 1Co.15:10; of two or more things together, almost = καί, Luk.23:11, Act.3:4 10:2 14:5 23:25, Eph.3:18; σὺν Χριστῷ ζῆν, 2Co.13:4; besides (FlJ, LXX), σὺν πᾶσι τούτοις, Luk.24:21. In composition: with (συνχαίρω), together (συνωδίνω), altogether (συντελέω)

(or ξ.) τοῖς ὅπλοις [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 2.90, 4.14, “Hellenica Oxyrhynchia” 10.1, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Leges” 763a, 4th c.BC: Aeneas Tacticus 11.8; σ. ἐγχειριδίοις “Hellenica Oxyrhynchia” 10.2; ξ. ξιφιδίῳ καὶ θώρακι 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 3.22; ξ. ἑνὶ ἱματίῳ [prev. author] 2.70]]; in some such cases ς. is little more than expletive, as σ. τεύχεσι θωρηχθέντες lines[Refs 8th c.BC+ [8.530, etc.: with αὐτός compare (αὐτός 1.5), chiefly in 8th c.BC: Homerus Epicus, ἀνόρουσεν αὐτῇ σ. φόρμιγγι 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 9.194, compare 14.498; αὐτῷ σ. τε λίνῳ καὶ ῥήγεϊ 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 13.118.]]

__A.5
of things accompanying, or of concurrent circumstances, ἄνεμος σ. λαίλαπι [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 17.57, compare 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 12.408]]; of coincidence in time, ἄκρᾳ σ. ἑσπέρᾳ [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “P.” 11.10]]; καιρῷ σ. ἀτρεκεῖ[Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. work] 8.7; σ. τῷ Χρόνῳ προϊόντι 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 8.7.6]]; in the course of, κείνῳ σ. ἄματι [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Bacchylides Lyricus 10.23, compare 125, 5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “Fragmenta.” 123.]]

__A.6
of necessary connexion or consequence, σὺν μεγάλῳ ἀποτεῖσαι to pay with a great loss, i.e. suffer greatly, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 4.161]]; δημοσίῳ σ. κακῷ with loss to the public, [Refs 6th c.BC+ [6th c.BC: Theognis Elegiacus 50]]; σ. τῷ σῷ ἀγαθῷ to your advantage, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 3.1.15]]; ὤλοντο.. σὺν μιάς ματι with pollution, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Antigone” 172]]; to denote agreement, in accordance with, σ. τῷ δικαίῳ καὶ καλῷ [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 2.6.18; σ. δίκᾳ 5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “P.” 9.96; σ. κόσμῳ 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 8.86, 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “de Mundo” 398b23; σ. τάχει 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Electra” 872, etc.]]

__A.7
of the instrument or means, with the help of, by means of, σ. ἐλαίῳ φαρμακώσαισα [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “P.” 4.221; διήλλαχθε σ. σιδάρῳ 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Septem contra Thebas” 885 (Lyric poetry); πλοῦτον ἐκτήσω ξ. αἰχμῇ [prev. author] “Pers.” 755 (troch.); ἡ [τῶν φίλων] κτῆσίς ἐστιν οὐδαμῶς σ. τῇ βίᾳ 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 8.7.13; ξ. ἐπαίνῳ 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 1.84.]]

__A.8
including, κεφάλαιον σ. ἐπωνίοις [Refs 5th c.BC+ [“IG” 12.329.5, compare 22.1388.85, 1407.12, +others; τοῦ Πειραιῶς ξ. Μουνυχίᾳ 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 2.13, compare 4.124, 5.26, 74, 7.42, 8.90, 95]]; δισχίλιαι γάρ εἰσι (i.e. δραχμαὶ) σ. ταῖς Νικίου [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Fragmenta” 100; ἀνήλωσα σ. τῇ τῆς σκευῆς ἀναθέσει ἑκκαίδεκα μνᾶς 5th c.BC: Lysias Orator 21.4, compare 2; αἶγας ἀπέδοτο σ. τῷ αἰπόλῳ τριῶν καὶ δέκα μνῶν 4th c.BC: Isaeus Orator 6.33, compare 8.8, 35, 11.42, 46, 4th c.BC: Aeschines Orator 2.162, 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 19.155, 27.23, +others, 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Historia Animalium” 525b15, 17, “Ath.” 19.6, 2nd c.BC: Hipparchus Astronomicus 1.1.9, +others, “PSI” 10.1124.14 (2nd c.AD).]]

__A.9
excluding, apart from, plus, ἓξ ἐμοὶ σ. ἑβδόμῳ six with (but not including) me the seventh, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Septem contra Thebas” 283; αἱ γὰρ καμπαὶ τέτταρες, ἢ δύο σ. τοῖς πτερυγίοις 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Historia Animalium” 490a32; σ. τοῖς ἀρχαίοις τὸν οἶκον ἐκ τῶν προσόδων μείζω ποιῆσαι 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 27.61; τὴν ἐφαπτίδα σ. τῇ σακκοπήρᾳ ἐν ᾗ ἐνῆν]]together with.., [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [PEnteux. 32.7, compare 89.9 (3rd c.BC)]]; οἱ γραμματεῖς σ. τοῖς πρεσβυτέροις [NT.Luke.20.1, cf. NT.Gal.5.24.]

__B
POSITION:—σύν sometimes follows its case, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 10.19, 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 9.332, 15.410]]. It frequently stands between adjective and substantive, as [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 11.359, 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 9.194, etc.]]; more rarely between substantive and adjective, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 13.258, 5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “P.” 8.7.]]

__B.2
frequently in tmesis in [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Homerus Epicus, as 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 23.687, 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 14.296, etc.]]

__B.3
in late Gr. σὺν καὶ with dative, στεφανηφορήσας σ. καὶ Αὐρ. Ἰάσονι [Refs 1st c.AD+ [“IG” 12(7).259 (Amorgos, 3rd c.AD),compare “Supp.epigram” 4.535 (Ephesus, 2nd-3rd c.AD), “Rev.Phil.” 50.11 (Sardis, 1st-3rd c.AD), “CPR” 26.16 (2nd c.AD); compare below with 2.]]

__C
σύν AS adverb., together, at once, κενεὰς σ. Χεῖρας ἔχοντες [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 10.42]]; mostly followed by δέ or τε, σ. δὲ πτερὰ πυκνὰ λίασθεν [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 23.879; σ. τε δύ᾽ ἐρχομένω 10.224 (compare σύνδυο); ξ. τε διπλοῖ βασιλῆς 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Ajax” 960 (Lyric poetry)]]. It is sometimes hard to distinguish this from tmesis, e.g. in [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 23.879]]; so ξὺν κακῶς ποιεῖν is ={Ξυγκακοποιεῖν} in [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 3.13]]. In Old Testament Gr. it is sometimes used to translate the Hebrew 'ēth (particle prefixed to the definite accusative) through confusion with the preposition 'ēth 'with', ἐμίσησα σὺν τὴν ζωήν [LXX.Eccl.2.17]; οὐκ ἐμνήσθη σ. τοῦ ἀνδρός[LXX+2nd c.AD+ [[prev. work] 9.15; ἔκτισεν ὁ θεὸς σὺν τὸν οὐρανὸν καὶ σὺν τὴν γῆν 2nd c.AD: Aquila LXX.Gen.1.1, etc.]]

__C.2
besides, also, σ. δὲ πλουτίζειν ἐμέ [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Agamemnon” 586; σ. δ᾽ αὔτως ἐγώ 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Antigone” 85, etc.; σ. δ᾽ ἐγὼ παρών [prev. author] “Aj.” 1288, compare “El.” 299; Δίρκα τε.. σ. τ᾽ Ἀσωπιάδες κόραι 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Hercules Furens” 785 (Lyric poetry)]]; in later Poetry σ. καί [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [3rd c.BC: Apollonius Rhodius Epicus 1.74, 3rd c.BC: Herodas Mimographus 4.3, 2nd c.BC: Nicander Epicus “Theriaca” 8, 2nd c.AD: Dionysius Periegeta 843]] (also in late Prose, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [2nd c.AD: Athenaeus Epigrammaticus 2.49a; compare above 5th c.BC: Bacchylides Lyricus 3).]]

__D
IN COMPOSITION (joined with other words),

__D.I
with, along with, together, at the same time, hence of any kind of union, connexion, or participation in a thing, and metaphorically of agreement or unity. In Compos. with a transitive Verb σύν may refer to the Object as well as the Subject, as συγκατακτείνειν may mean kill one person as well as another, or, join with another in killing.

__D.I.2
of the completion of an action, altogether, completely, as in συνάγνυμι, συνασκέω 2, συνθρύπτω, συγκόπτω, συμπατέω, συμπληρόω, συντελέω, συντέμν; sometimes, therefore, it seems only to strengthen the force of the simple word.

__D.I.3
joined with numerals, σύνδυο two together, which sense often becomes distributive, by twos, two and two; so σύντρεις, σύμπεντε, etc., like Latin bini, terni, etc.

__D.II
σύν in Compos., before β μ π φ ψ, becomes συμ-; before γ κ ξ Χ, συγ-; before λ συλ-; before σ usually συσ-; but becomes συ- before σ followed by a consonant (e.g. συστῆναι), before ζ, and perhaps sometimes before ξ. In a poetry passage, cited in [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Phaedrus” 237a, we have ξύμ alone in tmesi, ξύμ μοι λάβεσθε for συλλάβεσθέ μο;compare ὅτε ξὺμ πρῶτ᾽ ἐφύοντο 5th c.BC: Empedocles Poeta Philosophus 95: in Inscrr. and Papyri these assimilations are frequently not found.]]

συν-άγω
[in LXX chiefly for אָסַף, also for קָבַץ, etc. (cf. Kennedy, Sources, 128) ;]
to gather or bring together: of things, Jhn.6:12-13; before εἰς, Mat.3:12, al.; ἐκεῖ, Luk.12:18; ποῦ, Luk.12:17; συναγαγὼν πάντα (sc. εἰς ἀργύριον; see Field, Notes, 68, MM, xxiv), having sold off all: Luk.15:13; of persons, Jhn.11:52; esp. of assemblies, Mat.2:4, Jhn.11:47, Act.14:27, al. Pass., to be gathered or come together: Mat.22:41, Mrk.2:2, Luk.22:66, al.; before ἐπί Mrk.5:21, Act.4:27; πρός, Mat.13:2, Mrk.4:1, al.; εἰς, Rev.19:17; ἐν, Act.11:26; μετά, Mat.28:12; οὗ, Mat.18:20; ὅπου, Mat.26:57; ἐκεῖ, Jhn.18:2, al.
In late writers (see Kennedy, Sources, 128; cf. Deu.22:2, al.), to receive hospitably, entertain: Mat.25:35, 38 25:43 (cf. ἐπι-συνάγω)

συνάγω [ᾰ],
imperfect συνῆγον, Doric dialect -ᾶγον[Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Septem contra Thebas” 756 (Lyric poetry), probably in 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Iphigenia Aulidensis” 290 (Lyric poetry)]], Epic dialect σύνᾰγον [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 14.448:]]future συνάξω: aorist 1 συνῆξα, Doric dialect -ᾶξα[Refs 2nd c.BC+ [“GDI” 1772,1791 (Delph., 2nd c.BC)]]; infinitive συνάξαι variant in [NT.Luke.3.17]; participle συνάξας falsa lectio for{συννάξας} in [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 7.60: but the regular]]aorist is συνήγαγον: Attic dialect perfect συνῆχα [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Memorabilia” 4.2.8; συναγήοχα 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Oeconomica” 1346a28 (variant{-γιοχ-, -γιωχ-, γειοχ-}), 1st c.AD: Dioscorides (Dioscurides) Medicus 1.68, 4th c.AD: Iamblichus Philosophus “de vita Pythagorica” 35.254, etc.]]; Doric dialect συναγάγοχα [Refs [“Test.Epict.” 3.12:]]perfect passive συνῆγμαι, Doric dialect -ᾶγμαι[Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-4th c.BC: Timaeus Locrus Philosophus 101b]].--Old Attic dialect ξυνάγω, which [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Homerus Epicus]] also uses for the sake of meter:—bring together, gather together:

__I
of persons, animals, etc., ἡ δὲ ξυνάγουσα γεραιὰς νηόν.. to the temple, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 6.87, compare 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 2.111, 3.150, etc.; ἐς ἕνα Χῶρον σ. μυριάδα ἀνθρώπων [prev. author] 7.60; ἔνθα ποτ᾽ Ὀρφεὺς σύναγεν δένδρεα μούσαις, σύναγεν θῆρας 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Bacchae” 563 (Lyric poetry)]]; ποίμνας Ὀλύμπου σ. [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Fragmenta” 522]]; Ἕλληνας εἰς ἓν καὶ Φρύγας σ. [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Orestes” 1640, compare 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Lysistrata” 585 (_anapaest meter_)]]; σ. ἐς ὀλίγον crowd them into a narrow compass, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 2.84; σ. εἰς ταὐτόν 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Phaedrus” 256c, compare “Tht.” 194b]]; εἰς ἕν, εἰς μίαν ἀρχήν, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Politica” 1280b13, 1299b13; much like{συνοικίζω}, [prev. work] 1285b7.]]

__I.2
bring together for deliberation or festivity, βουλήν [Refs 5th c.BC+ [Batrachomyomachia 134; δικαστήριον 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 6.85; τοὺς στρατηγούς [prev. author] 8.59; ἐκκλησίαν τινὸς ἕνεκα 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 2.60]]; ἔς τι, περί τινος, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. author] 1.120, 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Historia Graeca (Hellenica)” 7.1.27; οἱ νόμοι σ. ὑμᾶς, ἵνα.. 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 19.1; τὴν βουλὴν καὶ τὸν δῆμον 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Ἀθηναίων Πολιτεία” 43.3]]; σ. πανηγύρεις, ἑταιρείας, συσσίτια, etc., [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Isocrates Orator 4.1,79, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 365d, “Lg.” 625e, etc.; σ. ἔρανον Μηνὶ Τυράννῳ “IG” 3.74.21, compare “GDI” 1772, 1791 (Delph., 2nd c.BC)]]:—passive, πανήγυρις.. συναγομένη [Refs 3rd c.AD+ [“SIG” 888.129 (Scaptopara, 3rd c.AD)]]: absolutely, hold a club dinner or meeting, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-3rd c.BC: Theophrastus Philosophus “Characteres” 30.18, and so perhaps “OGI” 130.5 (Egypt, 2nd c.BC)]]; σ. ἀπὸ συμβολῶν [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-3rd c.BC: Diphilus Comicus 43.28; ἔλεγον συνάγειν τὸ μετ᾽ ἀλλήλων πίνειν 2nd c.AD: Athenaeus Epigrammaticus 8.365c, compare 4th c.BC(?): Sophilus Comicus 4.2, 4th-3rd c.BC: Menander Comicus 158, 5th c.AD(?): Hesychius Legal icographus]]; νυνὶ.. συνάγουσι they are at dinner, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-3rd c.BC: Menander Comicus “Ἐπιτρέποντες” 195.]]

__I.3
in hostile sense, ξ. Ἄρηα, ἔριδα Ἄρηος, ὑσμίνην, join battle, begin the battle-strife, etc., [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 2.381, 5.861, 14.448, +others]]; πόλεμον σ. [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Isocrates Orator 4.84.]]

[Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Helena” 644 (Lyric poetry), compare 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Acharnenses” 991 (Lyric poetry); ἀνθρώπους εἰς κηδείαν 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Memorabilia” 2.6.36]]; γυναῖκα καὶ ἄνδρα, of Isis, [Refs 3rd c.AD+ [“IG” 12(5).14.20 (Ios, 3rd c.AD): hence γάμους σ]]. contract marriages, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Symposium” 4.64.]]

__I.5
bring together, make friends of, reconcile, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Empedocles Poeta Philosophus cited in 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Metaphysica” 1000b11, 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 58.42, 59.45]]; bring persons together in works of fiction, Κρέοντα καὶ Τειρεσίαν [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Epistulae” 311b.]]

σ. ἑαυτόν collect oneself, [Refs 1st c.AD+ [1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus “Philopoemen” 20.]]

lead with one, receive, σ. εἰς τὸν οἶκον [LXX.2Ki.11.27, cf. LXX.Judg.19.15; ξένος ἤμην καὶ συνηγάγετέ με]gave hospitality to.., [NT.Matt.25.35]:—passive, [NT.Act.11.26.]

[Refs 3rd c.BC+ [“PRev.Laws” 24.14 (3rd c.BC)]]; τὴν μήκωνα σ. [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [“Sammelb.” 4305 (3rd c.BC)]]; σ. εἰς μίαν γωνίαν τὸ ἀποκτένισμα τοῦ στιππύου [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [“PCair.Zen.” 176.41 (3rd c.BC)]]; συναγαγεῖν καὶ συναθροῖσαι τὸ θερμόν [NT+5th c.BC+ [4th-3rd c.BC: Theophrastus Philosophus “de Igne” 17; εἰς ἀποθήκας NT.Matt.6.26; κοινὸν σ. τὸν βίον 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Politicus” 311c; σ. ἐκ δικαίων τὸν βίον 4th-3rd c.BC: Menander Comicus “Μονόστιχοι - Fragmenta Comicorum Graecorum” 196]]; of an artist, σ. τὰ κάλλιστα ἐκ πολλῶν [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Memorabilia” 3.10.2, compare 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 488a.]]

__2. The supreme ecclesiastical court of the Jews, the Sanhedrin (i.e. Talmudic סַנְהֵדְרִין = συνέδριον): Mat.5:22 26:59, Mrk.14:55 15:1, Luk.22:66, Act.5:21, 27 5:34, 41 6:12, 15 22:30 23:1, 6 23:15, 20 23:28 (WH, R, mg., om.) σύνοιδα,
perfect with present sense, 1st pers. plural σύνισμεν [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Sophista” 232c]], Ionic dialect συνοίδαμεν [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 9.60]], 3rd.pers. plural συνίσᾱσι [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Electra” 93 (_anapaest meter_), 5th-6th c.BC: Isocrates Orator 8.113, 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 3.1.9, etc. (rarely συνοίδασι 5th c.BC: Lysias Orator 11.1, 2nd c.BC: Polybius Historicus 27.9.11); _imperative_ σύνισθι 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Hecuba” 870]]; infinitive ξυνειδέναι [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Antigone” 266:]]pluperfect with imperfect sense, συνῄδειν, Attic dialect συνῄδη, dual συνῄστην, plural -ῇσμεν, -ῇστε, -ῇσαν, Ionic dialect2nd pers. plural συνῃδέᾰτε [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 9.58]]: future συν (ξυν-) είσομαι [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Ecclesiazusae” 17, “V.” 999, 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Historia Graeca (Hellenica)” 2.4.17 (rarely συνειδήσω 5th-6th c.BC: Isocrates Orator 1.16]], and aorist participle -ειδήσας[Refs 1st c.BC+ [1st c.BC: Philodemus Philosophus “περὶ παρρησίας” p.32 O.)]]:—know something about a person, especially as a potential witness for or against him, ἢ (i.e. Δίκη) σιγῶσα σύνοιδε τὰ γιγνόμενα πρό τ᾽ ἐόντα [Refs 6th c.BC+ [6th c.BC: Solon Lyricus 4.15]]; τά τοι ἐγὼ καὶ ἀμφότερα συνειδὼς ἔχω μαρτυρέειν to both of which I, knowing them true of you, can testify, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 5.24; εἰ τέοισί τι χρηστὸν συνῄδεε πεποιημένον [prev. author] 8.113; ἐπαινεόντων τούτους τοῖσί τι καὶ συνῃδέατε [prev. author] 9.58]]; τὰ Μηδικὰ καὶ ὅσα αὐτοὶ σύνιστε our other services to which you can testify, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 1.73; ἂ ξύνισμεν τοῖσιν ἵπποις βουλόμεσθ᾽ ἐπαινέσαι 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Equites” 595 (troch.); συνοίδαμεν ὑμῖν ὑπὸ τὸν παρεόντα τόνδε πόλεμον ἐοῦσι πολλὸν προθυμοτάτοισι 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 9.60]]; ὑπολαμβάνων παρ᾽ ὑμῶν ἑκάστῳ τὸ συνειδὸς ὑπάρχειν μοι believing that I can rely on your acknowledgement of my services, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 18.110]]; τί μοι σύνοισθα τοιοῦτον εἰργασμέν; [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Symposium” 4.62; σύνοιδα τῷ μειρακίῳ κοσμίῳ τὸν πρότερον ὄντι χρόνον ἀεί 4th-3rd c.BC: Menander Comicus “Σαμία” 57; πότερον οὐ συνοίδασιν αὐτῷ ποιοῦντι τὰ δίκαια 2nd c.BC: Polybius Historicus 27.9.11]]; ξυνειδὼς οὐ φράσει; [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Tyrannus” 330; ἵνα τούτῳ ταῦτα συνειδῶμεν 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Protagoras” 348b; ἐρῶ.. ἂ σύνοιδα αὐτῷ 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Memorabilia” 2.7.1]]; οὐκ αἰσχυνοῦμαι.. εἰπεῖν (variant) ἅπασιν ὅσα σύνοιδ᾽ αὐτῷ κακά [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Fragmenta” 200; ξύνοιδ᾽ ἄντροισιν αἰσχύνην τινά 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Ion” 288]]; θνῄσκοντι συνείσῃ (conjecture Reiske for συνοίσῃ) thou wilt witness my death, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Philoctetes” 1085 (Lyric poetry); διὰ δικαιοσύνην, τήν οἱ ἄλλην συνῄδεε ἐοῦσαν 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 7.164; τοιοῦτον αὐτοῖς Ἄρεος εὔβουλον πάγον ἐγὼ ξυνῄδη χθόνιον ὄνθ᾽ 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Coloneus” 948]]; δύ᾽ ἡμῶν ἢ τρία κακὰ ξυνειδὼς εἶπε δρώσας μυρία (i.e. Εὐριπίδης) [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Thesmophoriazusae” 475, compare 553; __II
share the knowledge of something with somebody, to be implicated in or privy to it, οὐδὲ ξυνῄδει σοί τις ἔκθεσιν τέκνο; [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Ion” 956; δουλοῖ γὰρ ἄνδρα,.. ὅταν ξυνειδῇ μητρὸς ἢ πατρὸς κακά [prev. author] “Hipp.” 425]]; ξύνοιδε δ᾽ οὔτις οἰκετῶν νόσον[Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. work] 40; συνίσασί σοι πάντα ὅσα ἔπραξας 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 3.1.9; ξυνίσασ᾽ εὐναὶ.. ὅσα θρηνῶ 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Electra” 93 (_anapaest meter_); πλῆθος ὃ ξυνῄδει 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 4.68; ξυνειδώς τις [prev. passage]; ὁ συνειδὼς καὶ μὴ φράζων 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Leges” 742b; οἱ ξυνειδότες σφίσι 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 1.20; οἱ συνειδότες πεποιηκότι τι δεινόν 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Rhetorica” 1382b6; σύνοισθά που καὶ αὐτὸς ὅτι.. 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Phaedrus” 257d; σύνισμεν ὡς.. __II.b

know well, αὐτὸς ξυνειδώς, ἢ μαθὼν ἄλλου πάρ; as from his own knowledge, or.. ? [in LXX for צָוָה pi., קָהַל ni., etc.; 1Ma.12:43, 2Ma.4:24, 3Ma.1:19 (and frequently in these books) ;]
__1. trans.,
__(a) to commend, recommend: with accusative of person(s), 2Co.3:1 6:4 10:12 10:18; id. with dative, Rom.16:1 (as frequently at the beginning of a letter; Deiss., LAE, 226), 2Co.5:12; before πρός, 2Co.4:2; pass., before ὑπό, 2Co.12:11;
__(b) to show, prove, establish: with accusative, Rom.3:5 5:8, 2Co.6:4; dupl. accusative, Gal.2:13; accusative and inf., 2Co.7:11
__2. Intrans., pf., συνέστηκα (as also 2 aor. and plpf.);
__(a) to stand with or near: Luk.9:32;
__(b) to be composed of, consist, cohere: Col.1:17 (see Lft., in l), 2Pe.3:5.†

συνίστημι,
also συνιστάνω [Refs 2nd c.BC+ [(2nd c.BC: Polybius Historicus 4.82.5, 1st c.AD: Josephus Historicus “BJ Prooem.” 5, 2nd c.AD: Soranus Medicus 1.126 (_passive_))]]; συνιστάω [NT+4th c.BC+ [(4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “de Generatione Animalium” 777a6, “Pr.” 928a9, 1st c.BC-1st c.AD: Conon Historicus 48, NT.2Cor.6.4]]; imperfect συνίστα [Refs 2nd c.BC+ [2nd c.BC: Polybius Historicus 3.43.11, uncertain in 1st c.BC: Dionysius Halicarnassensis 8.18):]]imperfect συνίστην, future συστήσω, aorist 1 συνέστησα: transitive perfect συνέστᾰκα, found only in later texts, [Refs 1st c.AD+ [“PSI” 9.1035.14 (2nd c.AD), 2nd c.AD: Sextus Empiricus Philosophus “adversus Mathematicos” 7.109, “Anthologia Graeca” 11.139 (1st c.AD: Lucillius Epigrammaticus), 4th c.AD: Iamblichus Philosophus “de vita Pythagorica” 35.261]]:—set together, combine, τὰς χορδὰς ἀλλήλαις [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 412a]]; τὰς ἄρκυς καὶ τὰ δίκτυα falsa lectio in [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Cynegeticus” 6.12.]]

__II
combine, associate, unite, σ. τοὺς Ἀρκάδας ἐπὶ τῇ Σπάρτῃ [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 6.74, compare 3.84; Πελοποννήσου τὰ δυνατώτατα 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 6.16]]; ταύτας (i.e. τὰς πόλεις) [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Isocrates Orator 5.30; πόλεις πρὸς ἀλλήλας 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Historia Graeca (Hellenica)” 3.5.2; τοὺς ἐπιτηδείους ἐς ξυνωμοσίαν 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 8.48; τὰ πάντα ἀριθμοῖς 2nd c.AD: Sextus Empiricus Philosophus “adversus Mathematicos” 7.109.]]

__II.b
σ. Ἀσίην ἑωυτῷ unite Asia in dependence on himself, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.103]]; μαντικὴν ἑωυτῷ συστῆσαι bring prophetic art into union with himself, i.e. win, acquire it, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. author] 2.49; σ. τινὰ ἀντίπαλον ἑαυτῷ 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 6.1.26; σ. τισὶν ἡγεμόνα 2nd c.BC: Polybius Historicus 2.24.6, compare 3.42.6, 15.5.5.]]

__III
put together, organize, frame, ζῷον ἔμψυχον [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Timaeus” 91a; τέχνην [prev. author] “Smp.” 186e]]; πρᾶγμα ὁτιοῦν ἐκ μοχθηρῶν καὶ χρηστῶν σ. [Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. author] “Plt.” 308c; σ. τὴν ὀλιγαρχίαν 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 8.48; ἐκ δημοκρατίας καὶ μοναρχίας τὴν πολιτείαν 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Politica” 1266a23, compare 1284b18]]; ἑταιρείαν Legal cited in [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 46.26:]] —middle, τοῖς ἑτέραν αἵρεσιν (school) συστησαμένοις [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd c.AD: Galenus Medicus 15.505; οἱ συνιστάμενοι τὰς τέχνας [prev. work]449; θεωρήματα συνίστασθαι [prev. author] 16.725.]]

__III.2

__III.3

[Refs 2nd c.BC+ [“PAmh.” 2.31.17 (2nd c.BC),compare “PRein.” 18.33 (2nd c.BC)]]; σ. ἀγῶνας [Refs 1st c.AD+ [1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus “Fabius Maximus” 19; ἑορτήν 2nd c.AD: Apollodorus Damascenus Mechanicus 3.14.6]]; ναυτικὰς δυνάμεις, μισθοφόρους, [Refs 2nd c.BC+ [2nd c.BC: Polybius Historicus 1.25.5, 4.60.5]]; also, arrange in order of battle, rally, [Refs 1st c.BC+ [[prev. author] 3.43.11, uncertain in 1st c.BC: Dionysius Halicarnassensis 8.18.]]

__III.4
in Mathematics texts, erect two straight lines from points on a given straight line so as to meet and form a triangle, in passive, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Meteorologica” 376a2, b2, compare 3rd c.BC: Euclides Geometra 1.7, 3rd c.AD(?): Pappus Mathematicus 106.12]]; of two arcs of great circles on a sphere, [Refs [[prev. author] 476.19, 22.]]

__III.5

__IV

__IV.b
recommend, secure approval of a course of action, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [“SIG” 679.90 (5th c.BC: Magnes Comicus Mae., 2nd c.BC)]]:— middle, recommend persons for appointment, [Refs 4th c.AD+ [“PLond.” 3.1249.7 (4th c.AD).]]

__IV.c

__IV.d

__IV.e

__IV.2

__V
make solid or firm, brace up, τὸ σῶμα [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Hippocrates Medicus “ἀφορισμοί” 3.17, compare 4th-3rd c.BC: Theophrastus Philosophus “de Causis Plantarum” 1.8.3]]; σ. [τὰ ἴχνη] sets them, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Cynegeticus” 5.3]]; ὑπὲρ τοῦ συνεστῶτος [τοῦ τείχους], i.e. the unbroken part, [Refs 4th c.AD+ [4th c.AD: Julianus Imperator “Orationes” 2.64c]]; contract, condense, opposed to διακρίνω or διαλύω, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “de Generatione et Corruptione” 336a4, “Cael.” 280a12]]; of liquids, make them congeal, curdle, γάλα [Refs 5th c.BC+ [2nd c.AD(?): Pollianus Epigrammaticus 1.251; φλέγμα 5th c.BC: Hippocrates Medicus “περὶ διαίτης” 2.54 (variant): _metaphorically_, συστήσας τὸ πρόσωπον]] with a frown, [Refs 1st c.AD+ [1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus 2.152b.]]

__B

__B.II

__B.II.2

__B.II.3
to be involved or implicated in a thing, λιμῷ, πόνῳ, λιμῷ καὶ καμάτῳ, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 7.170, 8.74, 9.89; ἀλγηδόνος ᾇ ξυνέστας 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Coloneus” 514 (Lyric poetry); συνεστῶτες ἀγῶνι ναυτικῷ 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 4.55; καρτερᾷ μάχῃ [prev. work] 96.]]

__B.III
of friends, form a league or union, band together, [Refs [[prev. author] 6.21, 33, etc.]]; κατὰ σφᾶς αὐτοὺς ξ. [Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. author] 2.88; ἀλλήλοις 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Historia Graeca (Hellenica)” 2.1.1]]; ξυνίστασθαι πρὸς ἑκατέρους league themselves with one side or the other, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 1.1, compare 15; μετά τινος 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 34.34, etc.]]; ἐπί τινας against them, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Lysias Orator 22.17, compare 30.10 (_absolutely_)]]; καί μ᾽ οὐ λέληθεν οὐδὲν ἐν τῇ πόλει ξυνιστάμενον no conspiracy, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Equites” 863, compare 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 1.1.2]]; οἱ συνιστάμενοι the conspirators, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Lysistrata” 577 (_anapaest meter_); τὸ ξυνεστηκός 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 8.66.]]

__B.III.2

Attic dialect συντάττω, put in order together, especially as a military term, draw up, put in array, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 7.78, 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 8.28, 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Historia Graeca (Hellenica)” 4.8.28, etc.]]; σ. πεζοὺς αὐτοῖς (i.e. τῷ ἱππικῷ) draw up the foot with the horse, [Refs [[prev. work] 7.5.24]]:—passive, to be drawn up in order of battle, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Hercules Furens” 191, 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 1.4.18, etc.]]; μάλιστα ξυντεταγμένοι παντὸς τοῦ στρατοῦ in the best order of all the army, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 3.108; μεθ᾽ ὅπλων συντεταγμένοι 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 21.223]]; τισι or μετά τινων with others, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Historia Graeca (Hellenica)” 1.2.15, “Vect.” 2.3, compare “Cyr.” 6.4.14, etc.]]:—middle, form in order of battle, ὁμόσε χωρῶμεν ξυνταξάμενοι [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Lysistrata” 452:]]middle also transitive, συνταξάμενος βαθεῖαν τὴν φάλαγγα having drawn up his phalanx in deep order, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Historia Graeca (Hellenica)” 2.4.34.]]

__b
place under command of, τινὶ τάξιν [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd c.AD: Arrianus Historicus “Anabasis” 4.24.10]]:— passive, metaphorically, τὰ πάθη τῇ τοῦ λογισμοῦ ἡγεμονίᾳ [Refs 5th c.AD+ [5th c.AD: Hierocles Platonicus Philosophus “in Carmen Aureum - FPG” 19p.461M.]]

__c
place in the same class, with dative, [Refs 3rd c.AD+ [3rd c.AD: Plotinus Philosophus 6.1.25, 5th-6th c.AD: Damascius Philosophus “de Principiis” 1, +others]]

__2
passive, of single persons, to be collected, resolute, συντεταγμένος στρατηγός [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Historia Graeca (Hellenica)” 4.8.22]]; περὶ παίδων ἀγωγὴν ἄκρως σ. [Refs 3rd c.AD+ [3rd c.AD(?): Diogenes Laertius 5.65]]; so of the mind, πρὶν ξυνταχθῆναι.. τὴν δόξαν before they have time to get their thoughts collected, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 5.9 (ξυνταθῆναι is probably conjecture)]]; ἡ ἐπὶ τοῦ συντετάχθαι.. φρόνησις οὖσα [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Amphis Comicus 33.4]]; ἔφοδος ἐνεργὸς καὶ σ. [Refs 2nd c.BC+ [2nd c.BC: Polybius Historicus 3.19.5.]]

__II
arrange, organize, τὸ σῶμα [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Gorgias” 504a; τὰ συσσίτια συντέταχεν ὁ νόμος [prev. author] “Lg.” 625c; ἐνιαυτούς τε καὶ ὥρας καὶ μῆνας [prev. author] “Phlb.” 30c; σύνοδον 1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus “Antonius” 71]]: in bad sense, concoct, ψευδῆ κατηγορίαν [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aeschines Orator 2.183:]] —passive, ψυχὴ συντεταγμένη σώματι organically united with, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Leges” 903d]]; ὀλιγαρχικῶς συντετ. [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Politica” 1317a6]]; σημεῖον πολιτείας συντεταγμένης of an organized state, [Refs [[prev. work] 1272b30]]; Τροιζήνιοι σ. εἰς τοὺς Ἀχαιούς joined the Achaean League, [Refs 1st c.AD+ [1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus “Aratus” 24]]; οἱ συντεταγμένοι the conspirators, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Historia Graeca (Hellenica)” 3.3.7]]:—middle, arrange for oneself, i.e. make one's own plans of life, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Hippocrates Medicus “περὶ ἀρχαίης ἰητρικῇς” 10]]: also, get matters organized or arranged, or simply ordain, settle, τὰ νόμιμα ἡμῖν συνετάξατο [ὁ νομοθέτης] [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Leges” 626a, compare 625e, 781b; τὴν περὶ τοὺς νέους ἐπιμέλειαν 4th c.BC: Lycurgus Orator 106]]; καταστήσαντες.. εἰς τὴν προγεγραμμένην κώμην Τεβτῦνειν οὗ ἐὰν Ἀρίστων συντάσσηται wherever [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus]] may arrange to accept delivery, [Refs 1st c.BC+ [“PSI” 10.1098.24 (1st c.BC).]]

__II.2
of taxation, assess, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [Inscriptiones Graecae 12.63.17; σύνταγμα συντάξας εἰς ἑκατὸν ταλάντων πρόσοδον 4th c.BC: Aeschines Orator 3.95]]:—passive, to be organized for paying contributions, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [[prev. work]97, 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 13.3,9]]; but τὸ συντεταγμένον the assessed sum, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Politica” 1330a7]]:—middle, agree to such assessment, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 27.7, compare 28.8]]; τι εἰς τροφὴν συνταξάμενος ἐδίδου gave an allowance for food, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aeschines Orator 1.102: compare σύνταξις 11.3.]]

__II.3
compose or compile a narrative or book, [Refs 2nd c.BC+ [2nd c.BC: Polybius Historicus 2.40.4, 1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus “Brutus” 4]]:—middle, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Phaedrus” 263e, 2nd c.BC: Polybius Historicus 1.3.8, 2nd c.AD: Galenus Medicus 19.221]]: absolutely, write a book, [Refs 2nd c.BC+ [2nd c.BC: Polybius Historicus 9.2.2; οἱ τὰ Ῥωμαϊκὰ συνταξάμενοι 1st c.BC: Dionysius Halicarnassensis 4.7]]; σ. ὑπόθεσιν treat of.. , [Refs [[prev. author] “Comp.” 4]]:—passive, προοίμιον συντεταγμένον εἴς τι [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Leges” 930e, compare 4th c.BC: Aeschines Orator 3.201.]]

__II.4
with infinitive, ordain, prescribe, order, δασμοὺς ἀποφέρειν τινάς [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 8.6.8, compare 4th c.BC: Aeschines Orator 2.22, “PEnteux.” 27.13, 84.10, 16 (3rd c.BC), “PCair.Zen.” 28.1, +others (3rd c.BC), 2nd c.BC: Polybius Historicus 3.50.9, “PStrassb.” 100.21 (2nd c.BC)]]: without infinitive, συντάξαντος ἡμῖν Ἀμύντου [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [“PCair.Zen.” 27.1 (3rd c.BC)]]; καθὼς συνέταξεν αὐτοῖς ὁ Ἰησοῦς see l. for προσέταξεν in [NT.Matt.21.6.]

__II.4.b
with accusative of things, prescribe, of a physician, θεραπείαν [Refs 1st c.BC+ [1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus “Pericles” 13, compare 1st c.BC: Diodorus Siculus Historicus 1.70, 2nd c.AD: Soranus Medicus 1.60; also σ. τί πρῶτον οἰστέον 2nd c.AD: Alexander Rhetor 186.3]]:—passive, τοιαύτης ἐπιμελείας συνταχθείσης [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd c.AD: Soranus Medicus 2.48]]: generally, to be prescribed or ordained, ταὐτὸν περὶ τὰς ἡδονὰς συντεταγμένον ἐν τοῖς νόμοις [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Leges” 634b, compare 817e]]; ταῦτα τῷ ναυάρχῳ συνετάχθη Epist. cited in [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 18.78; ἄν τις πόλις μὴ ἀποστείλῃ τὴν δύναμιν τὴν συντεταγμένην “IG” 42(1).68.95 (Epid., 4th c.BC).]]

__II.5
Grammars, combine in interpretation, τοῖς προειρημένοις συντάττουσι ταῦτα [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd c.AD: Galenus Medicus 15.897, compare 16.533 (_passive_)]]; construct or construe a word, τὰ ἀρρενικὰ τοῖς θηλυκοῖς [Refs 1st c.BC+ [1st c.BC: Dionysius Halicarnassensis “Amm.” 2.11, compare 2nd c.AD: Apollonius Dyscolus Grammaticus “de Conjunctionibus;” 218.10; τὴν ἐν πρόθεσιν μετὰ γενικῆς 12th c.AD: Gregorius Corinthius Grammaticus p.44S.]]:—passive, [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd c.AD: Apollonius Dyscolus Grammaticus “de Pronominibus;” 69.15, 3rd c.AD(?): Diogenes Laertius 7.64]]; συντάσσεται ἀπὸ γενικῆς εἰς αἰτιατικήν (e.g. ἀφαιρῶ σοῦ τόδε) Thom.[Refs [Mag. p.33R.; compare συντακτός, σύνταξις 1.4.]]

__II.5.b
passive, to be added to, with dative, [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd c.AD: Apollonius Dyscolus Grammaticus “de Pronominibus;” 38.1]]; of syllables, τὸ σκλα καὶ στρα συντετάξεται [Refs [[prev. author] “Synt.” 313.16.]]

__III
middle, agree together, πάντα συνταξάμενοι καὶ οὐδὲν ἀπὸ ταὐτομάτου τούτων ἔπραττον [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 24.27; συνταξάσθω πρὸς αὐτοὺς.. πόσον δεῖ ἔλαιον.. πωλεῖν “PRev.Laws” 47.13 (3rd c.BC)]]; σ. πρὸς ἀλλήλους [Refs 2nd c.BC+ [2nd c.BC: Polybius Historicus 3.67.1]]: with infinitive, συνετάττετο κοινῇ πρεσβεύειν [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 19.13:]] —passive, κατὰ τὸ συντεταγμένον in accordance with what had been arranged, [Refs 2nd c.BC+ [2nd c.BC: Polybius Historicus 3.42.9, 3.43.6; πραξάντων τὸ συνταχθέν [prev. author] 8.28.10]]; κελεῖσαι προελθόντα στῆναι πρὸ τῆς πόλεως ἐπὶ τὸν συνταχθέντα τάφον the pre-arranged tomb, [Refs [[prev. author] 9.17.2; compare σύνταξις 11.2.]]

__IV
middle, take leave of one, bid him farewell, τινι [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd c.AD(?): Charito Scriptor Eroticus 8.4, 3rd c.AD: Menander Rhetor p.430S., “Anthologia Graeca” 9.171 (6th c.AD: Palladas Epigrammaticus)]]; compare ἀποτάσσω IV.

συντέλεια, -ας, ἡ
(συντελέω), [in LXX chiefly for כָּלָה and (in Da) for קוּם ;]
__1. in cl., a joint payment or contribution for public service; hence, generally, joint action (Plat.).
__2. In late writers (Polyb., al.), consummation, completion: σ. τ. αἰῶνος, -ων (cf. Dan LXX TH Dan.12:13, al.), Mat.13:39-40, 49 24:3 28:20, Heb.9:26.†
(AS)

συντέλεια, ἡ,
(συντελέω [Refs [11)]] joint contribution for the public burdens, χρημάτων σ. ποιῆσαι [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 18.237; σ. φόρου 2nd-3rd c.AD: Dio Cassius Historicus 42.6]]; εἰς σ. ἄγειν τὰς χορηγίας, i.e. to leave the choregia to be defrayed by subscription, not by a single person, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 20.23; μικρᾶς σ. ἑκάστῳ γιγνομένης [prev. passage]; πρὸς σ. χρημάτων 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Rhetorica ad Alexandrum” 1423b1.]]

__2
metaphorically, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Leges” 905b]]; ἡ παρὰ τοῦ διδασκάλου σ., i.e. instruction, [Refs 1st c.AD+ [2nd c.AD: Aristides Rhetor 2.226 1st c.AD: Josephus Historicus]]

__3
= collatio, (compulsory) provision of recruits, εἰς τὴν τῶν τειρώνων σ. [Refs [KeilPremerstein “Dritter Bericht“ p.87 (uncertain _locative_)]]; συντελείας βουργαρίων.. ἄνεσιν probably in [Refs 3rd c.AD+ [“SIG” 880.52 (Pizus, 3rd c.AD,compare “JRS” 8.26ff).]]

__II
at Athens, a body of citizens who contributed jointly to bear public burdens [Refs 5th c.BC+ [compare (συντελής 1), 5th c.BC: Antipho Orator “fragment” 56]]; αἱ σ. τῶν τριηράρχων Decrees cited in [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 18.105, compare 106.]]

__II.2
generally, company, ὦ ξυντέλεια (i.e. θεῶν), of the gods, who separately were called τέλειοι, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Septem contra Thebas” 251, cf. Scholia (at [prev. work])]]

__II.3
union of communities grouped together or united to a larger state, [Refs 2nd c.BC+ [2nd c.BC: Polybius Historicus 5.94.1, 1st c.BC: Diodorus Siculus Historicus 5.80, 1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus “Comp. Phil.Flam.” 1, 2nd c.AD: Pausanias Periegeta 7.15.2, “OGI” 565.13 (from Oenoanda).]]

__III
the consummation of a scheme, opposed to ἐπιβολή, [Refs 2nd c.BC+ [2nd c.BC: Polybius Historicus 1.3.3, compare 3.1.5; σ. ἐπιτεθεικὼς τοῖς ἔργοις [prev. author] 11.33.7]]; σ. σχεῖν, λαμβάνειν, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. author] 1.4.3, 4.28.3, compare “SIG” 695.13 (5th c.BC: Magnes Comicus Mae., 2nd c.BC), 1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus “Pericles” 13; εἰς σ. ἐλθεῖν 2nd c.BC: Polybius Historicus 2.40.6; ἡ σ. τῆς ἐπιβολῆς [prev. author] 5.32.3; ἡ σ. τοῦ ἀγῶνος “IG” 7.2712.78, 82 (from Acraephia)]]; τοῦ πολέμου [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [“OGI” 327.6 (Pergam., 2nd c.BC), 2nd c.BC: Polybius Historicus 4.28.5; τῶν ἔργων “PPetr.” 3p.109 (3rd c.BC)]]; τὰν τῶν μυστηρίων καὶ τᾶν θυσιᾶν σ. [Refs 1st c.BC+ [“IG” 5(1).1390.184 (Andania, 1st c.BC)]]; καταθύμιος λογισμῶν συντέλεια [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd c.AD: Vettius Valens Astrologus 173.11]]; completion, end, τοῦ ἐνιαυτοῦ [LXX+2nd c.AD+ [LXX.Deu.11.12; τοῦ διεληλυθότος ἔτους “POxy.” 1270.42 (2nd c.AD)]]; αἰῶνος [NT.Matt.13.39]; ποιῆσαι εἰς σ. make an end of, [LXX.Eze.20.17]; ἀνέβη σ. τῆς πόλεως εἰς οὐρανόν[LXX.Judg.20.40]; full realization, τῶν τελῶν [Refs 5th c.BC+ [1st c.BC: Philodemus Gadarensis Epigrammaticus “Rh.” 2.86 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus]]

__IV
unjust gain, [LXX.1Ki.8.3]; ={κακία}, [Refs 5th c.AD+ [5th c.AD(?): Hesychius Legal icographus]]

__V
in Grammar, completed action, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demetrius Phalereus Rhetor “Demetrius on Style” 214, 2nd c.AD: Apollonius Dyscolus Grammaticus “de Syntaxi;” 205.14, “Etymologicum Magnum” 472.23.]]

__VI
={ἐντελέχεια}, reality, [Refs 1st c.BC+ [1st c.BC(?): Ocellus Lucanus Philosophus 2.3.]]

συντελ-έω,
future -έσω[Refs 4th c.BC+ [“SIG” 1044.27 (Halic.. 4th-3rd c.BC)]], Attic dialect συντελῶ [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [“BCH” 54.270 (Rhamnus, 3rd c.BC)]]:—bring to an end, complete, σ. τὴν δαπάνην make up the whole expense, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 14.20]]; σ. εἰς τὰ ἑκατὸν ἅρματα make up the number of the chariots to one hundred, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 6.1.50]]; of a workman, σ. γεῖσον finish it off, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Lysias Orator “Fragmenta” 185 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus (_passive_),compare “IG” 12.372 E 14]]; στέφανον Test. cited in [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 21.22; ναῦς 2nd c.BC: Polybius Historicus 1.21.3 (_passive_)]]; σ. ταχύ finish it in a hurry, [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd c.AD: Alexander Rhetor 149.12]]; σ. τὴν ἐπίνοιαν accomplish it, [LXX+2nd c.BC+ [2nd c.BC: Polybius Historicus 4.81.3; λόγον LXX.Isa.10.22, 2nd c.AD: Galenus Medicus 15.59]]:—middle. [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [2nd c.BC: Polybius Historicus 1.9.6, “PFay.” 12.8 (2nd c.BC), 1st c.BC: Diodorus Siculus Historicus 1.59; ἵνα περὶ ὧν καταπέπλευκας συντετελεσμένος.. ἀναπλεύσῃς “PSI” 6.614.9 (3rd c.BC),compare 2nd c.BC: Polybius Historicus 5.100.9]]:— passive, [NT+3rd c.BC+ [“Inscription Délos” 502 A 15 (3rd c.BC), “PCair.Zen.” 124.7 (3rd c.BC), 1st c.BC: Diodorus Siculus Historicus 12.26, NT.Mark.13.4, etc.; λιθάρια συντετελεσμένα “PHolm.” 5.4.]]

__b
active, with infinitive, σ. καταφαγεῖν finish eating, [LXX.Gen.43.2, cf. LXX.Sir.24.28]: with participle,[LXX.Num.4.15, LXX.3Ki.8.54.]

__c
perpetrate, βίαιόν τι [Refs 1st c.BC+ [“BGU” 1818.21 (1st c.BC)]]:—middle, περὶ ὧν συντετέλεσται, τυχεῖν αὐτὸν.. τιμωρίας [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [“PEnteux.” 50.7 (3rd c.BC),compare “Klio” 16.150 (Delph., 2nd c.BC)]]:— passive, [Refs 2nd c.BC+ [“SIG” 684.5 (Dyme, 2nd c.BC), “BGU” 1762.7, +others (1st c.BC).]]

__2
passive, to be caused, brought about, frequently in [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-3rd c.BC: Epicurus Philosophus, πλεοναχῶς σ]]., of a plurality of causes, [Refs [“Ep.” 2p.37U., compare p.50 U.]]; simply, occur, happen, τὰς συντελουμένας.. φάσεις [Refs 1st c.BC+ [1st c.BC: Ptolemaeus Epigrammaticus “Phas.” p.10 H.]]

__3
celebrate or hold sacred rites, ἁγιστείας [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Axiochus” 371d; θυσίας “SIG” 1044.27, +others, “Supp.epigram” 1.366.29 (Samos, 3rd c.BC)]]; τὴν ἡμέραν [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-3rd c.BC: Epicurus Philosophus “Fragmenta” 217]]; τὸν ἀγῶνα, τὴν πανήγυριν, [Refs 1st c.BC+ [1st c.BC: Diodorus Siculus Historicus 11.29, 17.16; τὰ Ἴσθμια 1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus “Agesilaus” 21; τοὺς κός μους παρὰ τῇ Μητρί “Michel” 537 (Cyzicus, 1st c.BC):]] —passive, θυσία τῷ Διὶ σ. [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Mirabilia” 844a35, compare “PEnteux.” 6.6 (3rd c.BC).]]

__4
make an end of, destroy, [LXX.2Ch.20.23.]

__II
pay towards common expenses, contribute, σ. ἑξήκοντα τάλαντα [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aeschines Orator 3.95]]; but mostly without the sum expressed, ἐν ταῖς εἰσφοραῖς σ. εἰς τὸν πόλεμον contribute by payment of the εἰσφοραί towards the war, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 20.28.]]

__II.2
generally, contribute, πρὸς or εἰς τὴν γένεσιν, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “de Generatione Animalium” 715a12, “HA” 509a29; πρὸς μίαν ἀρχήν [prev. author] “PA” 669b19]]; πρὸς ἓν ἅπαντα σ. [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [[prev. author] “EN” 1096b28; εἰς ἀνάδοσιν τροφῆς 2nd c.AD: Galenus Medicus 15.196]]: also with dative, to be of service, be profitable, help, τῷ βίῳ [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd c.AD: Alexander Rhetor 271; τῇ λεπτυνούσῃ διαίτῃ 2nd c.AD: Galenus Medicus “περὶ λεπτυνούσης διαίτης - CMG” 6; τινὶ πρός τι 2nd c.AD: Lucianus Sophista “Alex.” 36]]:—passive, to be contributed, εἴς τι [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “de Generatione Animalium” 725a5, +others]]

__II.3

twist up, roll up, of a whirlwind, μή σ᾽ ἀναρπάσῃ.. συστρέψας ἄφνω [NT+5th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Fragmenta - American Journal of Philology” 195, compare 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Lysistrata” 975, “Th.” 61; φρυγάνων πλῆθος NT.Act.28.3; ἔριον περὶ μηλωτρίδα “POxy.” 234 ii 12 (2nd-3rd c.AD)]]; of animals, gather themselves together, in preparing to spring, σ. ἑαυτὸν ὥσπερ θηρίον [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 336b]]; σ. τὸν αὐχένα, of one struggling to get loose, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Eupolis Comicus 339]]; τὰ ὄμματα διὰ κενῆς, ὡς εἴ τι βλέπων, ξυνέστρεφε screwed up his eyes, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Hippocrates Medicus “ἐπιδημίαι” 7.83]]; συστρέψαι ἑαυτούς, of dolphins, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Historia Animalium” 631a27; [τὸ χόριον] σ. περὶ αὑτὸ τὴν ὑστέραν 2nd c.AD: Soranus Medicus 1.71:]] — passive, εἰ τὸ χόριον εἰς αὑτὸ συνεστραμμένον εἴη[Refs [[prev. work] 73]]; συνεστραμμένη χείρ clenched fist, [Refs [[prev. work] 102]]; of a whirlwind, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-3rd c.BC: Menander Comicus 536.4]]; of the moon, uncertain meaning in Palchus in [Refs [“Catalogus Codicum Astrologorum” 8(1).250.]]

__II
of soldiers, σ. ἑωυτούς form in a compact body, for attack or defence, collect themselves, rally, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 9.18]]; σ. εἰς ταὐτό (i.e. τὰς ἵππους) [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Historia Animalium” 572b14: frequently in]]passive, συστραφέντες in a body, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 4.136, 6.6, compare 40; συστρεφόμενοι [prev. author] 9.62, 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 7.30; ξυνεστρέφοντο ἐν σφίσιν αὐτοῖς [prev. author] 2.4; ὅσον.. ἦν ξυνεστραμμένον [prev. passage]; ἐπὶ πεντήκοντα ἀσπίδων συνεστραμμένοι ἦσαν]]they were formed in a mass [Refs 5th c.BC+ [50 deep, 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Historia Graeca (Hellenica)” 6.4.12]]; so of bees, fishes, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Historia Animalium” 629a19, 621a16.]]

__II.2
of soldiers, also, συστρέφειν ἐπὶ δόρυ wheel them to the right, variant in [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Respublica Lacedaemoniorum” 13.6]]; so probably σ. τὸν ἵππον turn him sharply, [Refs 1st c.BC+ [1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus “Pyrrhus” 16; σ. τὴν ὄψιν 1st c.BC(?): Satyrus Epigrammaticus 3.]]

__III
form into an organized whole, unite, τὸ Μηδικὸν ἔθνος [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.101; τοὺς τὰς οὐσίας ἔχοντας 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Politica” 1304b23]]:—passive, club together, conspire, [LXX+5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 4.68, 8.54; ἐπ᾽ ἐμὲ συστραφέντες ἥκουσι 4th c.BC: Aeschines Orator 2.178, cf. LXX.2Ki.10.9]]:—in active,[LXX.1Ki.16.9.]

__IV
passive, collect, gather, σ. αἷμα ἐς.. [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Hippocrates Medicus “ἀφορισμοί” 5.40; νιφετοῦ συστραφέντος 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “de Mundo” 394b2]]; of humours, gather, come to a head, φύματος συστραφέντος [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Hippocrates Medicus “προγνωστικόν” 23]]; of gravel collecting in the bladder, [Refs [[prev. author]]]Aër.[Refs [9.]]

__V
make the hair curl, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Theodectes Tragicus 17.3:]] —passive, συνεστραμμένα ξύλα knotted, gnarled, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-3rd c.BC: Theophrastus Philosophus “Historia Plantarum” 3.11.2; σ. ῥίζα [prev. author] “CP” 1.3.3; κιττὸς συνεστραμμένος ταῖς ῥίζαις [prev. author] “HP” 3.18.9.]]

[Refs [[prev. author] “Mu.” 394a27]]; πῦρ σ. concentrated, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-3rd c.BC: Epicurus Philosophus “Epistulae” 1p.28U.]]; compact, σ. τὸ εὐπαγές [Refs 1st c.BC+ [1st c.BC: Philodemus Gadarensis Epigrammaticus “Po.Herc.” 994.34]]; σωμάτιον σ. [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd c.AD: Arrianus Historicus “Epicteti Dissertationes” 1.24.8]]; συστρέφεσθαι καὶ ἀπεψῦχθαι, of an infant, [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd c.AD: Soranus Medicus 1.108; γάλα μελιτοειδῶς συστραφέν [prev. work] 91.]]

__VII
of sentences, narratives, and the like, bring into a close form, compress, ἐὰν μὴ συστρέφῃ τὰ πράγματα [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Cratinus Comicus 85]]; ἐνθυμήματα σ. [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Rhetorica” 1419a19]]; σ. τὰ νοήματα, τὸν νοῦν ἐν ὀλίγοις ὀνόμασι, [Refs 1st c.BC+ [1st c.BC: Dionysius Halicarnassensis “de Isocrate” 11, “Pomp.” 2.5: _absolutely_, συστρέψας γράφει]] writes briefly, curtly, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aeschines Orator 3.100; σ. εἰπεῖν τὸ πρᾶγμα 1st c.BC: Dionysius Halicarnassensis “de Lysia” 24:]] —frequently in passive, ῥῆμα βραχὺ καὶ συνεστραμμένον a short and pithy saying, of the Spartans, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Protagoras” 342e]]; λέξις συνεστραμμένη, opposed to διῃρημένη, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [1st c.BC: Dionysius Halicarnassensis “Ars Rhetorica” 5.7; ἡ Ἀττικὴ γλῶσσα σ. τι ἔχει 4th c.BC: Demetrius Phalereus Rhetor “Demetrius on Style” 177; συνέστραπται τοῖς νοήμασι 1st c.BC: Dionysius Halicarnassensis “de Lysia” 5. compare “Dem.” 19.]]

__VII.b
also, speak or write in an involved style, twist one's words, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Antiphanes Comicus 52.17, 217.17.]]

short_definition: to save — σώζω (on the more accurate σῴζω, see WH, Intr., §410; Bl., §3, 1-3),
root_and_cognates: LSJ-hänvisningar: ἀνασῴζω, εἴη, σώζεις, σώζεται, ἀρτεμισία
deep_entry:
Abbott-Smith / STEPBible (TBESG)
σώζω (on the more accurate σῴζω, see WH, Intr., §410; Bl., §3, 1-3),
[in LXX chiefly for ישׁע hi., also for מלט ni., נצל ni., etc. ;]
to save from peril, injury or suffering: Mat.8:25, Mrk.13:20, Luk.23:35, al.; τ. ψυχήν, Mat.16:25, al.; before ἐκ, Jhn.12:27, Heb.5:7, Ju 5; of healing, restoring to health: Mat.9:22, Mrk.5:34, al. In NT, esp. of salvation from spiritual disease and death, in which sense it is "spoken of in Scripture as either (1) past, (2) present, or (3) future, according as redemption, grace, or glory is the point in view. Thus (1) Rom.8:24, Eph.2:5, 8 2Ti.1:9, Tit.3:5; (2) Act.2:47, 1Co.1:18, 15:2, 2Co.2:15; (3) Mat.10:22, Rom.13:11, Php.2:12, Heb.9:28" (Vau. on Rom.5:9). Seq. ἀπό, Mat.1:21, Act.2:40, Rom.5:9; ἐκ, Jas.5:20, Ju 23 (cf. Cremer, 532ff.).
(AS)
