σῴζω,
with ι wherever ζ follows ω, as σῴζω, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [“Etymologicum Magnum” 741.27, and so (written σωιζ-) in Inscrr. and Papyri down to 3rd c.BC, e.g. “IG” 12.625.4, 22.687.35, 1611.378, 3rd c.BC: Isyllus Lyricus 75 (lapis), “PCair.Zen.” 482.17, 532.23 (3rd c.BC), “Test.Epict.” 1.6 (3rd-2nd c.BC), (ἀνα-) “IG” 22.492.13, also in codex Laur. of 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Electra” 993, +others]], but otherwise without it, e.g. ἔσωσε [Refs 5th c.BC+ [“IG” 9(2).257.11 (Thess., 5th c.BC)]]; but Didym. (and many Hellenistic and later Inscrr. and Papyri) rejected the ι everywhere, see [Refs 5th c.BC+ [“Etymologicum Magnum” [same place], and on the other hand Inscrr. show σῳσ- (always written σωισ-) from 5th c.BC, ἔσῳσεν “IG” 12.1085.5, 22.1236.6, συνδιασῴσαντες “GDI” 1612.9 (Dyme, 3rd c.BC), σῴσαι (_3rd.pers._ _sing._ _optative_) “IG” 5(2).357.152 (Stymphalus, 3rd c.BC), διέσῳσαν “OGI” 56.18 (Canopus, 3rd c.BC),compare “PPetr.” 3p.72 (3rd c.BC)]]; σοζ[, i.e. σωζ[, occurs in [Refs [“IG” 12.590]]: future σώσω [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Philoctetes” 1391, 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 1.137, etc.]]; early Attic dialect σωῶ [Refs [“IG” 12.188.30:]]perfect σέσωκα, also σέσῳκα, see. {ἀνασῴζω}:— middle, future σώσομαι [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Bacchae” 793, (ἐκ-) 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Persae” 360, (δια-) 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 4.2.28]]: aorist ἐσωσάμην [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Ecclesiazusae” 402]]:—passive, future σωθήσομαι [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 5.111, 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Nubes” 77, 5th c.BC: Hippocrates Medicus “προγνωστικόν” 1, etc.]]: aorist ἐσώθην [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 1.110, +others, “SIG” 167.37 (Mylasa, 4th c.BC) (ἐσώσθην only in 5th c.AD(?): Hesychius Legal icographus)]]: perfect σέσωσμαι [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Th.” [821 (820)], σέσωσται 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Iphigenia Taurica” 607, 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 56.33, σεσώσμεθα 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Trachiniae” 83, etc.; but σέσωται 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Critias” 109d, compare 110a, σεσωμένος “PCair.Zen.” 331.8 (3rd c.BC)]]; said to be Attic dialect by [Refs 9th c.AD+ [9th c.AD: Photius Legal icographus, etc.]]; διασεσῳμένους is found in [Refs 4th c.BC+ [“IG” 22.435.11 (after 4th c.BC) and διασεσῳμένοι in “PCair.Zen.” 240.11 (3rd c.BC)]]; later σέσῳσται [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [“IG” 12(7).386.25 (Amorgos, 3rd c.BC)]].--The foll. forms are found in [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Homerus Epicus and dialects,]]

__1
present participle σώζων [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 5.490]]; 3rd.pers. singular indicative or optative σώζει (-οι) [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th-7th c.BC: Hesiodus Epicus “Opera et Dies” 376 (variant for{εἴη}):]]present participle passive σωζόμενοι (-ομένοισι) [Refs 6th c.BC+ [6th c.BC: Theognis Elegiacus 68, 235 (assuming variant).]]

__2
from σᾰόω, 3rd.pers. singular σαοῖ [Refs 6th c.BC+ [6th c.BC: Theognis Elegiacus 868, 3rd c.BC: Callimachus Epicus “Hymnus in Delum” 22, etc.]]; 3rd.pers. plural σαοῦσι [Refs 7th c.BC+ [7th c.BC: Tyrtaeus Elegiacus 11.13]]; 2nd pers. singular imperative σάου [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [“Hymni Homerici” 13.3, 3rd c.BC: Callimachus Epicus “Epigrammata” 35 (as variant)]], etc.: future σαώσω [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 10.44]]: aorist ἐσάωσα [Refs 5th c.BC+ [21.611, 5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “Fragmenta.” 231]]: aorist infinitive passive σαωθῆναι [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 15.503, 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 10.473; _imperative_ σαωθήτω 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 17.228]]; Epic dialect 3rd.pers. plural ἐσάωθεν [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 3.185]]: future middle σαώσομαι [Refs [21.309.]]

__3
from σάωμι, Aeolic dialect 2nd pers. singular σάως [Refs 7th c.BC+ [7th-6th c.BC: Alcaeus Lyricus 73 (perhaps σάῳς)]]; 2nd pers. singular imperative σάω [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 13.230, 17.595, Callias Epigrammaticus [same place], etc.: σάω]] as 3rd.pers. singular imperfect, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 16.363, 21.238.]]

__4
from σώω, participle σώοντες [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 9.430]]; Ionic dialect imperfect σώεσκον [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 8.363]]; σώετε, σώεσθαι, [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [3rd c.BC: Apollonius Rhodius Epicus 4.197, 2.610.]]

__5
from σόω, subjunctive σόῃς, -ῃ, -ωσι, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 9.681, 424, 393 vulgar form, where Tyrannio cited in Hdn.Gr. 2.66 reads σοῷς, σοῷ, σοῶσ; in 9.681 3rd-2nd c.BC: Aristarchus Grammaticus read both σαῷς and σοῷς]]; the forms σοῷς, σοῷ perhaps arise from σαόω, by contraction and 'distraction': but σόωσι from σώωσι accusative to Hdn.Gr.[same place]; [Refs 5th c.AD+ [5th c.AD(?): Hesychius Legal icographus cites also σόεις, σοῦται as ={σώζεις, σώζεται}.]]

__6
Laconian dialect σωάδδει· παρατηρεῖ, [Refs 5th c.AD+ [5th c.AD(?): Hesychius Legal icographus]]: but also σχολι-σοΐδδω, aorist ἀπέσοιξεν· ἀπέσωσεν, Λάκωνες, [Refs [[prev. author]]]

__7
σωννύω, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Dinolochus Comicus 5]]:—save, keep,

__1
of persons, save from death, keep alive, σώοντες ἑταίρους [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 9.430; ζωοὺς σάω 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 21.238; ὄτ᾽ ἄσφ᾽ ἀπολλυμένοις σάως 7th-6th c.BC: Alcaeus Lyricus 73, compare 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 1.91, 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 3.1.38; πόδες καὶ γοῦνα σ. τινά 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 21.611; νὺξ στρατὸν σ. 9.78]]; spare, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 22.357]]:—passive, to be saved, kept alive, preserved, opposed to ἀπολέσθαι, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 15.503, 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 3.185, etc.; ἀγαπητῶς σεσωσμένους 5th c.BC: Lysias Orator 16.16]]; keep a whole skin, escape destruction, οἱ σωθησόμενοι [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Theaetetus” 176d]]; so in present σωζόμενος, [Refs 6th c.BC+ [6th c.BC: Theognis Elegiacus 68, 235 (assuming variant)]]; to be healed, recover from sickness, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Hippocrates Medicus “Κωακαὶ προγνώσιες” 136, 4th c.BC: Isaeus Orator 1.10 (uncertain reading); ὑγιαίνοντες καὶ σωζόμενοι “IG” 22.1028.89 (1st c.BC)]]; σώζεο, as a wish, God bless you, farewell, [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [3rd c.BC: Callimachus Epicus “Hymnus in Delum” 150, “Anthologia Graeca” 5.240 (Paul. Sil.), 9.372]]; σώζοισθε [Refs 6th c.AD+ [[prev. work]171 (6th c.AD: Palladas Epigrammaticus)]]; also, save oneself, escape, σώθητι [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Crito” 44b]]; μόγις or μόλις σῴζεσθαι escape with difficulty, [Refs 1st c.BC+ [[prev. author] “Ep.” 332c, 1st c.BC: Diodorus Siculus Historicus 2.48, etc.]]; χαλεπῶς σ. [Refs 6th c.BC+ [6th c.BC: Theognis Elegiacus 675.]]

__1.b
especially in [“NT”, of God or Christ, NT.1Cor.1.21, etc.; σ. τὸ ἀπολωλός NT.Luke.19.10; σ. τὸν κόσμον NT.John.12.47]:—frequently in passive, to be saved or in a state of salvation, [NT.Matt.19.25, etc.; οἱ σῳζόμενοι NT.Luke.13.23, NT.Act.2.47.]

__2
of things, keep safe, preserve, rare in [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Homerus Epicus, σάω μὲν ταῦτα, σάω δ᾽ ἐμέ 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 13.230; σπέρμα πυρὸς σώζων 5.490]]; πόλιν καὶ ἄστυ σ. [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 17.144; σαώσει Ἀργείους καὶ νῆας 10.44, compare 9.230]]: frequently in Trag. and Attic dialect, σ. φάρμακον [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Trachiniae” 686; τὰ τόξα [prev. author] “Ph.” 766]]; τὰ σκεύη, παῖδας οἶκον χρήματα, καρπούς, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Pax” 730 (_anapaest meter_), “Av.” 380 (troch.), 1062 (Lyric poetry)]]; τὰ πατρῷα, τὰ ὑπάρχοντα, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. author] “Th.” 820 (Lyric poetry), 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 1.70]]; σ. πόλιν preserve the city or the state, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 8.34, 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Septem contra Thebas” 749 (Lyric poetry), 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Antigone” 1058, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 417a, compare “Grg.” 512b, etc.; τὰ πράγματα 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 1.74; τὴν Ἑλλάδα 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Lysistrata” 525 (Lyric poetry)]]; τὰς πολιτείας, τὴν δημοκρατίαν, etc., [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Politica” 1309b15, 36]]; τόνδε γὰρ [λόγον] σῴζων keeping it secret, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Prometheus Vinctus” 524, compare 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Coloneus” 1530]]; σ. καιρόν save or recover an opportunity, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 19.6, compare 23.4]]:—middle, keep or preserve for oneself, τὴν εὐλάβειαν [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Electra” 993, compare 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Alcestis” 146, etc.; αὐτὸς αὑτῷ σ. τι 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Ecclesiazusae” 402, compare “Eq.” 1017 (hexameters):]] —passive, τὸ ἄπραγμον οὐ σῴζεται is not secure, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 2.63]]; ἡ.. πόλις οὐκ ἂν ἐσῴζετ; [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Ecclesiazusae” 219]]; to be preserved or extant, of books, [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [3rd c.AD: Longinus Rhetor cited in 3rd c.AD: Porphyrius Tyrius Philosophus “Vita Plotini” 20, 2nd c.AD: Galenus Medicus 15.705, 2nd-3rd c.AD: Dio Cassius Historicus 70.2.]]

__3
keep, observe, maintain laws, etc., σ. ἐφετμάς [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Eumenides” 241; τὸν παρόντα νοῦν [prev. author] “Pr.” 394; τοὺς καθεστῶτας νόμους 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Antigone” 1114, compare 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “de Virtutibus et Vitiis” 1250b17; τοὺς σοὺς λόγους 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Helena” 1552]]; τὸ μόρσιμον[Refs 2nd c.AD+ [[prev. work] 613; τὰ πρὸς τοὺς κατοίκους δίκαια “BGU” 562.19 (2nd c.AD)]]; confirm, τὸ τοῦ ποιήσαντος [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “de Mundo” 400b24, compare 3rd c.BC: Antigonus Carystius Paradoxographus “Mirabilia” 45 (_passive_)]]; πρὸς τὸ τὰ φαινόμενα σῴζειν to retain the observed facts, [Refs 5th c.AD+ [5th c.AD: Proclus Philosophus “Hypotyposis astronomicarum positionum” 5.10]]; κατὰ ποσὸν σῴζει τὴν πρὸς τὸ μῶλυ ἐμφέρειαν retains, i.e. does not lack, a certain resemblance to.., [Refs 1st c.AD+ [1st c.AD: Dioscorides (Dioscurides) Medicus 3.46, compare 98, 2nd c.AD: Soranus Medicus “de fasciis - Opera Hippocratis et Galeni” 8]]:—passive, to be maintained, τοῦ μήκους σῳζομένου [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Meteorologica” 386a2; ἐφ᾽ ᾧ τοῖς θεοῖς τὰ ἱερὰ σωθήσεσθαι “PHib.” 1.77.7 (3rd c.BC).]]

__4
keep in mind, remember, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Helena” 266, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 486c]]: more frequently in middle, παρῆκα θεσμῶν οὐδέν, ἀλλ᾽ ἐσῳζόμην.. ὅπως δύσνιπτον ἐκ δέλτου γραφήν [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Trachiniae” 682, compare “El.” 1257; μηδ᾽ ἂ ἔμαθε σῴζοιτο 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 455b; in full, μνήμην σῴζομαι στρατεύματος 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Iphigenia Aulidensis” 302 (Lyric poetry), compare 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Gorgias” 501a, “Tht.” 163d.]]

__II
Constr.:

__II.1
simply with accusative, see above

__II.2
with a sense of motion to a place, bring one safe to, τὸν δ᾽ ἐσάωσεν ἐς ποταμοῦ προχοάς [NT+8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 5.452; ἐς ὅμιλον 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 19.401; πόλινδε 5.224, etc.; ἐς οἴκους 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Philoctetes” 311; εἰς τὴν βασιλείαν τὴν ἐπουράνιον NT.2Tim.4.18]]:—passive, come safe to a place, σωθέντος ἐμεῦ ὀπίσω ἐς οἶκον [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 4.97, compare 9.104; πρὸς ἤπειρον σεσῶσθαι 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Persae” 737; δεῦρο 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Phoenissae” 725; οἴκαδε 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Historia Graeca (Hellenica)” 1.6.7]]; σῴζεσθαι ἐπὶ τὴν ὑμετέρην [χώρην] [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 5.98; ἐς δόμους σωθέντ᾽ 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Trachiniae” 611; σωθῶμεν ἐπὶ θάλατταν 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 6.5.20: with _dative_ _person_, μόλις ὔμμιν ἐσώθην 3rd c.BC: Theocritus Poeta Bucolicus 15.4.]]

__II.3
σ. τινὰ ἐκ φλοίσβοιο, ἐκ πολέμου, carry off safe, rescue from.. , [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 5.469, 11.752; ἐκ ποταμοῖο 21.274; ἐκ θανάτοιο 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 4.753; ἐκ πολλῶν πόνων 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Electra” 1356; ἀπὸ στρατείας 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Agamemnon” 603; διὰ δεινῶν πραγμάτων σεσωσμένοι 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 5.5.8: with _genitive_, σώσας ἐχθρῶν χθόνα]] having rescued it from them, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Antigone” 1162; σῶσαί τινα κακοῦ [prev. author] “Ph.” 919; σεαυτὸν νούσου “Ath.Mitt.” 56.124 (from Smyrna)]]; σωθῆναι κακῶν [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Orestes” 779]].--Both constructions may be combined, σ. τινὰ ἐκ πολέμοιο νῆας ἔπι [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 17.452; ἐκ π. μετὰ νῆας 12.123; ἐξ Αἰγίνης δεῦρο 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Gorgias” 511d.]]

__II.4
with accusative et dative person, save for another, υἷά τινι [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 4.765; ἡμῖν τὸν βίον 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Protagoras” 356e, etc.]]:— passive, σῴζεταί τί τινι [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Pax” 1022, 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 7.7.56.]]

__II.5
with infinitive, [σπονδαὶ] αἵ σε σῴζουσιν θανεῖν which save thee from dying, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Phoenissae” 600 (troch.).]]

__II.6
with participle, σῴζεσθαι φεύγοντες by flight, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 3.3.51.]]

__II.7
absolutely, τὰ σώσοντα what is likely to save, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 6.5]]; ἡ σῴζουσα [ψῆφος] [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd c.AD: Lucianus Sophista “Harm.” 3.]]

__II.7.b
σώζων, ὁ, [Refs [“Saviour”, of a god, “JRS” 14.28 (from Iconium)]]; epithet of Apollo, [Refs [“CR” 19.368 (from Sizma).]]

__II.7.c
σῴζουσα, ἡ, ={ἀρτεμισία}, Ps.-[Refs 1st c.AD+ [1st c.AD: Dioscorides (Dioscurides) Medicus 3.113.]]

deep_entry:
Abbott-Smith / STEPBible (TBESG)
σῶμα, -τος, τό,
[in LXX for גְּוִיָּה ,בָּשָׂר, etc., and for Aram. נְבֵלָה ;]
a body.
__1. Prop., of the human body,
__(a) as always in Hom. (opposite to δέμας), of the dead body: Mat.27:58, 59 Mrk.15:43, al.;
__(b) of the living body: Luk.11:34, 1Co.6:13, al.; ἐν σ. εἶναι, Heb.13:3; as the instrument of the soul, τὰ διὰ τοῦ σ., 2Co.5:10; opposite to πνεῦμα, Rom.8:10, 1Co.5:3 7:4, Jas.2:26; to ψυχή, Mat.6:25 10:28, Luk.12:22 (cf. Wis.1:1, al.); to τὸ π. καὶ ἡ ψ., 1Th.5:23; σ. ψυχικόν, opposite to σ. πνευματικόν, 1Co.15:44; ὁ ναὸς τοῦ σ. αὐτοῦ (genitive epexeg.), Jhn.2:21; τὸ σ. τ. ταπεινώσεως (Hebraistic "genitive of definition"; M, Pr., 73f.; Bl., §35, 5), opposite to τὸ σ. τ. δοξῆς αὐτοῦ, Php.3:21; similarly, τὸ σ. τ. σαρκός, Col.1:22; σ. τοῦ θανάτου (subject to death), Rom.7:24; σ. τ. ἁμαρτίας, Rom.6:6;
__(with) periphr., ἀνθρώπου, then absol., σῶμα (Soph., Xen., al.), a person, and in later writers (Polyb., al.), a slave: Rev.18:13 (cf. MM, i, ii, xxiv; Deiss., BS, 160).
__2. Of the bodies of animals: living, Jas.3:3; dead, Heb.13:11 ( Exo.29:14, al.).
__3. Of inanimate objects (cf. Eng. "heavenly bodies"): 1Co.15:37, 38 40 (Diod., al.).
__4. Of any corporeal substance (Plat., al.): opposite to σκιά, Col.2:17. Metaphorical, of a number of persons united by a common bond; in NT, of the Church as the spiritual body of Christ: Rom.12:5, 1Co.10:16, 17 12:13, 27, Eph.1:23 2:16 4:4, 12, 16 5:23, 30, Col.1:18, 24 2:19 3:15; ἓν σ. κ. ἓν πνεῦμα, Eph.4:4.
(AS)

LSJ / STEPBible (TFLSJ)
σῶμα, ατος, τό
[Refs 4th c.AD+ [(4th c.AD(?): Arcadius Grammaticus]] dative plural σωμάτεσι [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [“IG” 5(2).357.156 (Stymphalus, 3rd c.BC))]], body of man or beast, but in [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Homerus Epicus, as 3rd-2nd c.BC: Aristarchus Grammaticus remarks (see. 2nd c.AD: Apollonius Biographus “Lex.”)]], always dead body, corpse (whereas the living body is δέμας), ὥς τε λέων ἐχάρη μεγάλῳ ἐπὶ σώματι κύρσας [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 3.23, compare 18.161]]; ς. δὲ οἴκαδ᾽ ἐμὸν δόμεναι πάλιν [Refs 8th c.BC+ [7.79; σ. κατελείπομεν ἄθαπτον 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 11.53; ὦν.. σώματ᾽ ἀκηδέα κεῖται 24.187]]; so also in [NT+8th c.BC+ [8th-7th c.BC: Hesiodus Epicus “Scutum Herculis” 426, 4th-5th c.BC: Simonides Lyricus 119, 5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “O.” 9.34, 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 7.167, 2nd-1st c.BC: Posidonius Historicus 14 1st c.AD: Josephus Historicus, NT.Mark.15.43, etc.; τὸ σ. τοῦ τεθνεῶτος 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 469d, compare “Grg.” 524c, 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 43.65; σ. νεκρόν “POxy.” 51.7 (2nd c.AD)]]; νεκρὸν σ. [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd c.AD: Galenus Medicus 18(2).93, compare νεκρός 11.1]]; μέγιστον σ... σποδου, ={σ. μέγιστον ὃ νῦν σποδός ἐστι}, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Electra” 758; also later, Wilcken “Chr.” 499 (2nd-3rd c.AD).]]

__2
the living body, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th-7th c.BC: Hesiodus Epicus “Opera et Dies” 540, Batrachomyomachia 44, 6th c.BC: Theognis Elegiacus 650, 5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “O.” 6.56, “P.” 8.82, 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.139, etc.; δόμοι καὶ σώματα 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Septem contra Thebas” 896 (Lyric poetry)]]; γενναῖος τῷ σ. [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Philoctetes” 51]]; εὔρωστος τὸ σ. [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Historia Graeca (Hellenica)” 6.1.6]]; τὸ σ. σῴζειν or -εσθαι save one's life, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 22.55, 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 1.136]]; διασῴζειν or -εσθαι[Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Isocrates Orator 6.46, 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 5.5.13; περὶ πολλῶν σ. καὶ χρημάτων βουλεύειν 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 1.85]]; περὶ τοῦ σ. ἀγωνίζεσθαι for one's life, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Lysias Orator 5.1]]; ἔχειν τὸ σ. κακῶς, ὡς βέλτιστα, etc., to be in a bad, a good state of bodily health, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Memorabilia” 3.12.1, 3.12.5.]]

__3
body, opposed to spirit (εἴδωλον), [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “Fragmenta.” 131]]; opposed to soul (ψυχή), [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Gorgias” 493a, “Phd.” 91d]]; τὰ τοῦ σ. ἔργα bodily labours, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Memorabilia” 2.8.2]]; αἱ τοῦ σ. ἡδοναί, αἱ κατὰ τὸ σ. ἡδ.,[Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. work] 1.5.6, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 328d]]; τὰ εἰς τὸ σ. τιμήματα bodily punishments, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aeschines Orator 2.139; τὰ εἰς τὸ σ. ἀδικήματα “PHal.” 1.193 (3rd c.BC).]]

__4
animal body, opposed to plants, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 564a (_plural_)]]; but of plants, [NT.1Cor.15.38.]

__5
civic rights (like Latin caput), [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Lysias Orator 23.12]]; ἄτιμοι τὰ σ. [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Andocides Orator 1.74]]; μέρος ἠτιμῶσθαι τοῦ σ. [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 51.12.]]

__6
in “NT”, of the sacramental body of Christ, τοῦτό ἐστι τὸ σ. μου [NT.Matt.26.26, cf. NT.1Cor.10.16.]

__6.b
of the body of Christ's church, οἱ πολλοὶ ἓν σ. ἐσμεν ἐν Χριστῷ [NT.Rom.12.5]; ἡ ἐκκλησία ἥτις ἐστὶ τὸ σ. [τοῦ Χριστοῦ] [NT.Eph.1.23.]

__II
periphrastic, ἀνθρώπου σ. ἓν οὐδέν, ={ἄνθρωπος οὐδὲ εἷς}, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.32]]; especially in Trag., σῶμα θηρός, ={θήρ}, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Coloneus” 1568 (Lyric poetry)]]; τεκέων σώματα, ={τέκνα}, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Troades” 201 (Lyric poetry)]]; τὸ σὸν σ., ={σύ}, [Refs [[prev. author] “Hec.” 301]]; rarely in singular of many persons, σῶμα τέκνων [Refs [[prev. author] “Med.” 1108 (_anapaest meter_).]]

__II.2
a person, human being, τὰ πολλὰ σ., ={οἱ πολλοί}, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Antigone” 676]]; λευκὰ γήρᾳ σ. [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Hercules Furens” 909 (Lyric poetry); σ. ἄδικα [prev. author] “Supp.” 223, compare 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Leges” 908a, “PSI” 4.359.9 366.7 (3rd c.BC), etc.]]; ἑκάστου τοῦ σώματος, [Refs [“IG” 12.22.14; κατὰ σῶμα]]per person, [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [PRev.Laws 50.9 (3rd c.BC)]]; καταστήσαντες τὸ σ. ἀφείσθωσαν τῆς ἐγγύης [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [“PMich.Zen.” 70.12 (3rd c.BC)]]; ἐργαζομένη αὑτῇ τῷ ἰδίῳ σ. working for herself, earning her own living, [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [“PEnteux.” 26.7 (3rd c.BC)]]; τὰ φίλτατα σ., of children, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aeschines Orator 3.78]]; frequently of slaves, αἰχμάλωτα σ. [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 20.77, “IG” 12(7).386.25 (Amorgos, 3rd c.BC), “SIG” 588.64 (Milet., 2nd c.BC), etc.]]; οἰκετικὰ σ. Legal cited in [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aeschines Orator 1.16, compare “SIG” 633.88 (Milet., 2nd c.BC)]]; δοῦλα [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd c.AD(?): Pollianus Epigrammaticus 3.78]]; ἐλεύθερα σ. [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Historia Graeca (Hellenica)” 2.1.19, 2nd c.BC: Polybius Historicus 2.6.6, etc.]]; later, σῶμα is used absolutely for a slave, [NT+3rd c.BC+ [PHib. 1.54.20 (3rd c.BC), 2nd c.BC: Polybius Historicus 12.16.5, NT.Rev.18.13, etc.; σ. γυναικεῖον, ᾇ ὄνομα.. “GDI” 2154.6 (Delph., 2nd c.BC)]]; a usage censured by Poll. [prev. cited] and [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd c.AD: Phrynichus Atticista 355]]; also of troops, τὴν τῶν σ. σύνταξιν [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aeneas Tacticus 1.1; μηχανήμασιν ἢ σώμασιν ἐναντιοῦσθαι ὧδε [prev. author] 32.1.]]

__III
generally, a body, i.e. any corporeal substance, δεῖ αὐτὸ (i.e. τὸ ὄν) σ. μὴ ἔχειν [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Melissus Philosophus 9; ἢ μέγεθός ἐστιν ἢ σ. ἐστιν 5th c.BC: Gorgias Rhetor et Sophista 3]]; σ. ἄψυχον, ἔμψυχον, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Phaedrus” 245e, compare “Plt.” 288e, 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Physica” 265b29, +others; ὁ λίθος σ. ἐστι 2nd c.AD: Lucianus Sophista “Vit.Auct.” 25; φασὶν οἱ μὲν σ. εἶναι τὸν χρόνον, οἱ δὲ ἀσώματον 2nd c.AD: Sextus Empiricus Philosophus “adversus Mathematicos” 10.215]]; κυκλικὸν σ., of one of the spheres, [Refs 4th c.AD+ [4th c.AD: Julianus Imperator “Orationes” 5.162b, +others]]; τὸ πέμπτον σ. the fifth element, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Philolaus Philosophus 12, “Placita Philosophorum” 1.3.22, 4th c.AD: Julianus Imperator “Orationes” 4.132c]]; metallic substance, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [6th c.AD: Olympiodorus Philosophus Alch.p.71 5th c.BC: Bacchylides Lyricus]]

__III.2
in Mathematics texts, figure of three dimensions, solid, opposed to a surface, etc., [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Topica” 142b24, “Metaphorical” 1020a14, +others]]

__IV
the body or whole of a thing, especially of complete parts of the body, τὸ σ. τῶν νεφρῶν [Refs [[prev. author] “HA” 497a9; τὰ σ. τῶν αἰσθητηρίων [prev. author] “GA” 744b24]]; τὸ σ. τῆς γαστρός, τῆς κοιλίας, [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd c.AD: Galenus Medicus 15.667,806; σ. παιδοποιόν 2nd-3rd c.AD: Aelianus “De Natura Animalium - Ar.Byzantine Epit.” 17.42]]: generally, the whole body or frame of a thing, ὑπὸ σώματι γᾶς [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Septem contra Thebas” 947 (Lyric poetry)]]; τὸ σ. τοῦ παντός, τοῦ κόσμου, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Timaeus” 31b. 32c]]; ὕδωρ, ποταμοῦ σ. [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Chaeremon Tragicus 17]]; τὸ σ. τῆς πίστεως the body of the proof, i.e. arguments, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Rhetorica” 1354a15; τῆς λέξεως 3rd c.AD: Longinus Rhetor “Ars Rhetorica” p.188]] H.; of a body of writings, [Refs 1st c.BC+ [1st c.BC: Cicero, M. Tullius Orator et Philosophus “Epistulae ad Atticum” 2.1.4]]; text of a document, opposed to ὑπογραφή, [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [“BGU” 187.12 (2nd c.AD),compare “PFay.” 34.20 (2nd c.AD)]]; of a will, [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [“POxy.” 494.30 (2nd c.AD).]]

__IV.2
ξύλα σώματα logs, opposed to κλάδοι, [Refs 3rd c.AD+ [“POxy.” 1738.3 (3rd c.AD)]]; σ. μέγα περσέας [Refs 3rd c.AD+ [“CPHerm.” 7 ii 27, compare iii 8 (3rd c.AD).]]

Abbott-Smith / STEPBible (TBESG)
σωματικός, -ή, -όν
(σῶμα), [in LXX: 4Ma.1:32 4Mac 3:1 * ;]
__(a) of or for the body, bodily: γυμνασία, 1Ti.4:8;
__(b) (opposite to ἀσώματος) bodily, corporeal: εἶδος, Luk.3:22.†

LSJ / STEPBible (TFLSJ)
σωμᾰτ-ικός, ή, όν,
of or for the body, bodily, opposed to ψυχικός, ἔργα [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Ethica Nicomachea” 1101b33; πάθη [prev. work] 1173b9; ἡδοναί [prev. work] 1104b5]]; τὰ σ. ἡδέα[Refs 2nd c.BC+ [[prev. work] 1152a5; πόνοι “SIG” 708.11 (Istropolis, 2nd c.BC)]]; ἐργασίαι [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [“PFay.” 21.10 (2nd c.AD)]]; ἀσθένεια [Refs 1st c.BC+ [“BGU” 1773.13 (1st c.BC), “PFlor.” 51.5 (2nd c.AD).]]

(τάσσω), [in LXX: Job.38:12 (מָקוֹם), Psa.110:4 (דִּבְרָה), 2Ma.9:18, al. ;]
__1. an arranging, hence, in military sense, disposition of an army, battle array (Thuc., al.).

τάξις, εως,
Ionic dialect ιος, ἡ, (τάσσω) arranging, arrangement:

__I

__I.1
drawing up in rank and file, order or disposition of an army, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 5.68 ([near the start]), 7.5, etc.]]; τὰ ἀμφὶ τάξεις rules for it, tactics, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 2.1.7; τ. καὶ ἀντίταξις 1st c.BC: Philodemus Philosophus “de Pietate - Herkulanische Studien” 12.]]

__I.2
battle array, order of battle, κατὰ τάξιν [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 8.86; ἐν τάξει 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 4.72, etc.]]; ἐς τάξιν καθίστασθαι, ἀνάγειν,[Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. work] 93, 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Aves” 400 (_anapaest meter_)]]; ἵνα μὴ διασπασθείη ἡ τ. [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 5.70]]; of ships, ἀποπλῶσαι ἐκ τῆς τάξιος [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 6.14.]]

__I.3
a single rank or line of soldiers, ἐπὶ τάξιας ὀλίγας γίγνεσθαι to be drawn up a few lines deep, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. work] 111, compare 9.31; ἐλύθησαν αἱ τ. τῶν Περσῶν 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Laches” 191c.]]

__I.4
body of soldiers, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Persae” 298, 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Coloneus” 1311]]; especially at Athens, the quota of infantry furnished by each φυλή [Refs 5th c.BC+ [compare (ταξίαρχος 11), 5th c.BC: Lysias Orator 16.16]]; but frequently of smaller bodies, company, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 1.2.16, 6.5.11, etc.; ἱππέων τ. [prev. work] 1.8.21]]; so of ships, squadron, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Persae” 380]]: generally, band, company, φιλία γὰρ ἥδε τ., of the chorus, [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [[prev. author] “Pr.” 128 (Lyric poetry); ἐμφανίσας μοι ἐν ᾗ ἔσομαι τάξει “PCair.Zen.” 409.6 (3rd c.BC).]]

__I.4.b
especially a contingent of [Refs [128]]men, [Refs 1st c.BC+ [1st c.BC: Asclepiodotus Tacticus “Tact.” 2.8, 2nd c.AD: Arrianus Historicus “Tactica” 10.2, 2nd-3rd c.AD: Aelianus “Tactica - Griechische Kriegsschriftsteller” 9.3.]]

__I.4.c
in late Gr., membership of the militia palatina (compare ταξεώτης), [Refs 4th c.AD+ [4th c.AD: Libanius Sophista “Orationes” 27.17.]]

__I.5
post or place in the line of battle, ἀξιεύμεθα ταύτης τῆς τ. [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 9.26, compare 27; ἐν τῇ τ. εἶχε ἑωυτόν [prev. author] 1.82]]; μένειν ἐν τῇ ἑωυτοῦ τ. [Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. author] 3.158; τ. φυλάξων 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Rhesus” 664; ἡ τ. φυλακτέα 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 5.3.43; ᾗ ἕκαστος τὴν τ. εἶχεν [prev. author] “An.” 4.3.29; τῆς πρώτης τ. τεταγμένος 5th c.BC: Lysias Orator 14.11, compare 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 5.68 (near the end)]]; ἐκλιπόντας τὴν τ. [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 5.75, compare 9.21]]; λείπειν τὴν τ. [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Andocides Orator 1.74, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Apologia” 29a, 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 13.34, 15.32, 4th c.BC: Aeschines Orator 3.159, etc.; παραχωρεῖν τῆς τάξεως 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 3.36, etc.]]; but ἡγεμὼν ἔξω τάξεων officer on the unattached list, [Refs [Arch.Papyrus 3.188, compare “Sammelb.” 599, “OGI” 69 (from Coptos)]]; so οἱ ἔξω τάξεως staff-officers, aides-de-camp, [Refs 1st c.BC+ [1st c.BC: Diodorus Siculus Historicus 19.22.]]

__II.2
order, regularity, εἰς τ. ἄγειν ἐκ τῆς ἀταξίας [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Timaeus” 30a; τ. καὶ κόσμος [prev. author] “Grg.” 504a]]; οὔτε νόμος οὔτε τ. [Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. author] “Lg.” 875c, compare “R.” 587a; τ. περιόδου 4th-3rd c.BC: Epicurus Philosophus “Epistulae” 2p.42U.; διὰ τάξεως γίγνεσθαι 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Leges” 780a]]; τάξιν ἔχειν to be regular, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-3rd c.BC: Theophrastus Philosophus “Historia Plantarum” 3.9.6]]; ἐν τάξει in an orderly manner, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Leges” 637e; so τάξει “SIG” 741.12 (Nysa, 1st c.BC]], rendering of Latin ordine).

__II.3
ordinance, κατὰ τὴν τ. τοῦ νόμου [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Leges” 925b]]; παρὰ τὴν τοῦ νομοθέτου τ. [Refs [[prev. author] “Plt.” 305c, etc.]]

ταπεινός, -ή, -όν
[in LXX for שָׁפָל, עָנִי, etc. ;]
low-lying; metaphorically,
__(a) lowly, of low degree, brought low: Jas.1:9, 2Co.7:6 (cf. Sir.25:23); οἱ τ., opposite to δυνάσται, Luk.1:52; τ. ταπεινοῖς (neut., R, txt.; masc., R, mg.; see ICC, in l), Rom.12:16;
__(b) lowly in spirit, humble, in cl. usually in a slighting sense (see Tr., Syn., § xlii; but see also Abbott, Essays, 81), in NT in an honourable sense: 2Co.10:1; before τ. καρδίᾳ, Mat.11:29 (cf. Psa.34:19); opposite to ὑπερήφανος, Jas.4:6, 1Pe.5:5" (LXX) .†
(AS)

[Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd c.AD: Galenus Medicus 15.87.]]

of persons, humbled, abased in power, pride, etc., [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 7.14]]; σὺ δ᾽ οὐδέπω τ. [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Prometheus Vinctus” 322, compare 908; τ. παρέχειν τινά 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 2.5.13; τά τοι μέγιστα πολλάκις θεὸς ταπείν᾽ ἔθηκε 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Fragmenta” 716, compare “Hec.” 245, “Andr.” 979]]; submissive, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Hiero” 5.4 (_comparative_), etc.]]; αἱ τ. τῶν πόλεων small, poor, weak, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Isocrates Orator 4.95, compare 7.7, 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 7.5.69 (_superlative_)]]; τ. δύναμις [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 4.23]]; of low intelligence, αἱ τῶν ἀσυνέτων καὶ τ. ἀνθρώπων ψυχαί [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd c.AD: Galenus Medicus 19.220; τὴν μικρὰν καὶ τ. [ἰατρικὴν θεωρίαν] ὁ Ἱπποκράτης ηὔξησεν [prev. author] 16.550.]] adverb, ταπεινῶς (or ταπεινὰ) πράττειν to be in low estate or obscurity, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Isocrates Orator 5.64, 1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus “Theseus” 6; -νῶς ζῆν 4th-3rd c.BC: Philemo Comicus 227; ὁμιλεῖν 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Politica” 1313b41.]]

__3

in moral sense, either bad, mean, base, abject, τ. καὶ ἀνελεύθερος [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Leges” 791d, compare 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Memorabilia” 3.10.5, 5th-6th c.BC: Isocrates Orator 2.34, etc.]]; or good, lowly, humble, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Leges” 716a, 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 5.1.5]], frequently in NT, [NT.Matt.11.29, NT.2Cor.7.6, +others]

τ. ποδός flat of the foot. the part between the toes and the heel, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 11.377, 388, cf. 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 9.37, 5th c.BC: Hippocrates Medicus “περὶ ἀγμῶν” 9, 5th c.BC: Diogenes Apolloniates Philosophus 6]] (but also, palm of the hand, [Refs 1st c.AD+ [[prev. passage]); οὐλὴ ταρσῷ ἀριστερῷ “PMich.Teb.” 121r111 i3 (1st c.AD)]]: generally, foot, [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [Anacreont. 35.4, 3rd c.AD: Oppianus Apamensis Epicus “Cynegetica” 3.470, “Anthologia Graeca” 5.26 (2nd-3rd c.AD: Rufinus Epigrammaticus), 9.653 (6th c.AD: Agathias Historicus et Epigrammaticus).]]

__II.1.b
palm of the hand, [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd c.AD: Rufus Medicus “περὶ ὀνομασίας” 81, 2nd c.AD: Soranus Medicus “de signis fracturarum - Physici et Medici Graeci Minores” 22; see supr. 11.1a.]]

__II.1.c
ankle, [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd c.AD: Galenus Medicus “de Usu Partium” 3.6]]; but distinguished from σφυρόν, [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd c.AD: Soranus Medicus 1.84.]]

__II.2
τοὺς τ. τῶν κωπέων the rows of oars on the sides of ships, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 8.12]]; so τοὺς τ. alone, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 7.40: _sing._, “IG” 22.1628.590, 2nd c.BC: Polybius Historicus 1.50.3; ὁ δεξιὸς τ. τῆς νεώς [prev. author] 16.3.12]]: sing., oar, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Iphigenia Taurica” 1346.]]

__II.3
τ. πτερύγων flat of the outstretched wing, [Refs 1st c.BC+ [“Anthologia Graeca” 12.144 (1st c.BC: Meleager Epigrammaticus), cf. 2nd c.AD: Babrius Fabularum Scriptor 72.9; ὁ τ. τῶν πτερῶν 2nd-3rd c.AD: Aelianus “De Natura Animalium - Ar.Byzantine Epit.” 2.1]]: absolutely, wing, [Refs 1st c.BC+ [Anacreont. 9, “Anthologia Graeca” 9.287 (1st c.AD: Apollonides Epigrammaticus), etc.; in Prose, 1st c.BC: Dionysius Halicarnassensis 4.63]]: of a peacock's tail, [Refs 2nd c.BC+ [2nd c.BC: Moschus Bucolicus 2.60]]; ταρσοί feathers, [Refs 1st c.BC+ [1st c.BC: Diodorus Siculus Historicus 2.50.]]

__II.4
τ. ὀδόντων the row of teeth in a saw, [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd-3rd c.AD: Oppianus Anazarbensis Epicus “Halieutica - Poetae Bucolici et Didactici” 5.202.]]

__II.5
Pan's pipe, ταρσῷ Πὰν ὁ μελιζόμενος [Refs [“epigram Gr.” 781.10 (from Cnidus).]]

__II.6
edge of the eyelid and its lashes, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Hippocrates Medicus “ἐπιστολαί” 23, 2nd c.AD(?): Pollianus Epigrammaticus 2.69, 2nd c.AD: Galenus Medicus “de Usu Partium” 10.7.]]

τάσσω
[in LXX chiefly for שׂוּם, also for צָוָה pi., נָתַן, etc. ;]
primarily, in military sense, then generally, to draw up in order, arrange in place, assign, appoint, order: with dative (accusative) and inf. (Bl., § 72, 5), Act.15:2 18:2 (διατ-, WH) Act.22:10; ἑαυτούς, 1Co.16:15; pass., Mat.8:9 (T [WH], R, txt., om.), Luk.7:8, Rom.13:1; ὅσοι ἦσαν τεταγμένοι εἰς ζωὴν αἰώνιον (perh. in mid. sense; see EGT and Page, in l), Act.13:48; mid., to appoint for oneself or by one's own authority, Mat.28:16, Act.28:23.†
(AS)

LSJ / STEPBible (TFLSJ)
τάσσω,
[Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Agamemnon” 332, etc.]]; Attic dialect τάττω [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Protagoras” 262e, etc.]]: future τάξω [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Septem contra Thebas” 285, etc.]]: aorist ἔταξα [Refs [[prev. author] “Supp.” 986, etc.]]: perfect τέτᾰχα [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Oeconomicus” 4.5, (συν-) 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Leges” 625c]]: pluperfect ἐτετάχει [Refs 2nd c.BC+ [2nd c.BC: Polybius Historicus 5.65.7:]] —middle, future τάξομαι[(in _passive_ sense) LXX.Exo.29.43]: aorist ἐταξάμην [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 3.13, 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 2.83, etc.]]:— passive, future ταχθήσομαι [Refs 5th c.BC+ [1st c.BC: Diodorus Siculus Historicus 11.41, (ἐπι-) 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 1.140, etc.]]; later τᾰγήσομαι (ἐν-) [NT+5th c.BC+ [4th c.AD: Oribasius Medicus 8.1, (ὑπο-) NT.1Cor.15.28; 3f ut. τετάξομαι 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Iphigenia Taurica” 1046, 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 5.71, 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Aves” 637]]: aorist ἐτάχθην [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Eumenides” 279, etc.]]; later ἐτάγην [ᾰ] [Refs 2nd c.BC+ [“SIG” 708.9 (Istropolis, 2nd c.BC), 1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus 2.965e, Perictione Philosophus cited in 5th c.AD: Stobaeus, Joannes 4.25.50, etc.]]: perfect τέταγμαι [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “O.” 2.30, etc.]]; 3rd.pers. plural τετάχαται [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 3.13, (ἀντι-) 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 4.8.5]]: 3rd.pers. plural pluperfect ἐτετάχατο [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 5.6, 7.4]]:—draw up in order of battle, form, array, marshal, both of troops and ships, τὴν στρατιήν [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.191; τοὺς ὁπλίτας 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 4.9; νεῶν στῖφος ἐν στίχοις τρισίν 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Persae” 366; πολεμίων στίχας 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Heraclidae” 676; τ. εἰς μάχην στρατιάν 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 1.6.43: _absolutely_, 5th-6th c.BC: Isocrates Orator 18.47]]:—passive, to be drawn up, ἐς μάχην [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.80; οὐδένα κόσμον ταχθέντες [prev. author] 9.69]]; ἐπὶ τεττάρων ταχθῆναι in four lines, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 1.2.15]]; ἐπὶ μιᾶς, of ships, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [[prev. author] “HG” 1.6.29; ἐπὶ κέρως 4th c.BC: Eubulus Comicus 67.4]]; κατὰ μίαν ναῦν τεταγμένοι in line, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 2.84]]; ἐπὶ ὀκτώ, of troops, [Refs [[prev. author] 6.67: _absolutely_, τεταγμένοι]] in rank and file, [Refs [[prev. author] 2.81 (so _metaphorically_, τὸ ἐν τῷ τεταγμένῳ ὄν]] the rank and file, opposed to Senators and Equites, [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd-3rd c.AD: Dio Cassius Historicus 49.12)]]; στράτευμα τεταγμένον, opposed to ἄτακτον, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Memorabilia” 3.1.7]]:—middle, fall in, form in order of battle, frequently in [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus, 1.48, 4.11, etc.; ὡς ἐς μάχην 2.20]]; ἐτάξαντο κύκλον τῶν νεῶν formed in a circle, [Refs [[prev. work] 83, compare 3.78; ἐτάξαντο οὐ πάντες ὁμοίως 5.68; εἴκοσι ναυσὶ ἐτάξαντο 3.77 (but in 2.90 _transitive_, ἐπὶ τεσσάρων ταξάμενοι τὰς ναῦς]] having drawn up their ships in four lines,[Refs 5th c.BC+ [compare 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Heraclidae” 664).]]

__2
post, station, τὰς καμήλους ἀντία τῆς ἵππου [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.80, compare 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Phoenissae” 749]]; τινὰς ἐπί τινας one group against another, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 2.1.9 (but τ. τινὰ ἐπὶ τοὺς ἱππέας]] set him over them, to command them, [Refs [[prev. author] “HG” 3.4.20)]]; ἑαυτὸν ὑμῖν τάξαι παρέσχεν for enrolment, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Lysias Orator 31.9, compare 4th c.BC: Lycurgus Orator 43]]:—passive, to be posted or stationed, τῇ οὐδεὶς ἐτέτακτο [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.84, compare 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Persae” 381; ἐς τὸ ὄρος 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 7.212; but ἐς τὸ πεζόν or ἐς π. τετάχθαι to serve among the infantry, [prev. work] 21, 81; ἐς τὸν ναυτικὸν στρατὸν -θέντες [prev. work] 203: with _genitive_, τῆς πρώτης τάξεως (or simply τῆς πρώτης) τεταγμένος 5th c.BC: Lysias Orator 14.11, 16.15: with _accusative_ _cognate_, τάξιν τινὰ ταχθῆναι 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Phaedrus” 247a, etc.; δεξιὸν τεταγμένους κέρας 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Supplices” 657: frequently followed by Preps. (compare below 11.1, etc.), ταχθῆναι or τετάχθαι ἐπί τινα]] or τινας against another, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 3.78, etc.]]; ἐπί τινι or τισι [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Septem contra Thebas” 448, 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 2.70, 3.13, etc.]]; also, to be posted at a place, ἐφ᾽ ἑπτὰ πύλαις ταχθέντες ἴσοι πρὸς ἴσους [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Antigone” 142 (_anapaest meter_)]]; ἐπ᾽ εὐωνύμῳ κέρατι on the left wing, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Oeconomicus” 4.19; ἐπὶ τοῦ λαιοῦ κέρως 2nd c.BC: Polybius Historicus 1.34.4]]; τ. κατά τινα over against.. , [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 8.85, 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 2.3.19]]; τ. μετά τινα behind him.., [Refs [[prev. author] “HG” 7.2.4 (so ἐπί τινι [prev. author] “Lac.” 13.7)]]; μετά τινος with him, by his side, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [2nd c.BC: Polybius Historicus 2.67.2, etc., compare 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 2.63; σύν τινι 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 3.2.17, etc.; παρὰ τὸν ποταμόν 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 9.15]]; περὶ τὸ Ἥραιον[Refs [[prev. work] 69; ἀμφὶ τὴν Κέον [prev. author] 8.76.]]

__II
appoint to any service, military or civil, the latter being metaphorically from the former, ἄρχοντας [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Historia Graeca (Hellenica)” 7.1.24]]; τινὰ ἐπί τινι [Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. author] “Cyr.” 8.6.17, 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 17.20, etc.; ἐπὶ τὰς πράξεις 5th-6th c.BC: Isocrates Orator 5.151, compare 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Lysis” 209b, etc.; ἀξιῶ σε τάξαι με ἐπί τινος “PCair.Zen.” 447.3 (3rd c.BC): also τ. ἑαυτὸν ἐπί τι]] undertake a task, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 371c, 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 8.71, etc.; πρός τι 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Memorabilia” 2.4.6]]:—passive, οἱ τεταγμένοι βραβῆς [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Electra” 709, compare 759; πρέσβεις ταχθέντες 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 19.69]]; τετάχθαι ἐπί τινι to be appointed to a service, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.191, 2.38, 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Persae” 298, 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Ion” 1040, 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 4.6.1; ἐπί τι 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Aves” 637, 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 1.4.24, etc.; also ἐπί τινος 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 5.109 (ἐπ᾽ οὗ, variant{ὅκου}), 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 10.46; τὸν ἐπὶ τῆς σφαγῆς τεταγμένον 1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus “Cleomenes” 38, compare 2nd c.BC: Polybius Historicus 3.12.5]]; ὁ πρὸς τοῖς γράμμασι τεταγμένος secretary, [Refs [[prev. author] 15.27.7]]; οἱ πρὸς ταῖς φυλακαῖς (tolls) τετ. [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [“PCair.Zen.” 31.15 (3rd c.BC).]]

__II.2
with accusative et infinitive, appoint or order one to do or be, τάττετ᾽ ἐμὲ ἡγεῖσθαι [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 3.1.25, compare “Cyr.” 7.3.1, 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 3.25, 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Coloneus” 639, 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Hecuba” 223, etc.]]:—passive, μοῖρα ἡ ταχθεῖσα.. φρουρέειν [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 4.133, compare 8.13, 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Eumenides” 279, 639, etc.; τασσόμενος πορεύεσθαι 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 4.5.11, etc.]]; τοῦτο τετάγμεθα (i.e. ποιεῖν) [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Alcestis” 49; also τεταγμένος κίοι 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Supplices” 504]]; ὁ ἐπ᾽ Αἴγυπτον ταχθείς (i.e. κῆρυξ) ordered to Egypt, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 3.62, compare 68, 6.48.]]

__II.3
also τ. τινί with infinitive, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. author] 2.124, 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 1.5.5, etc.: _impersonal_, ἴωμεν.., ἵν᾽ ἡμῖν τέτακται (i.e. ἰέναι) 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Philoctetes” 1181 (Lyric poetry); οἷς ἐτέτακτο παραβοηθεῖν 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 3.22; τοῖς δὲ ἕπεσθαι τέτακται 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Respublica Lacedaemoniorum” 11.6: also with]]infinitive omitted, κόσμον φυλάσσουσ᾽ ὅντιν᾽ ἂν τάξῃ πόλις (i.e. φυλάσσειν) [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Supplices” 245, compare 460, “Hel.” 1390, etc.]]

__II.4
assign to a duty or class of dutiful persons, ἐν πᾶσιν ἐμαυτὸν ἔταττον [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 18.221]]; εἰς ὑπηρετικὴν αὑτοὺς τ. [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Politicus” 289e; πρός τινας τάξαι αὑτόν 4th-3rd c.BC: Dinarchus Orator 3.18; σὺν ἐμοὶ τ. σεαυτήν 1st c.BC: Dionysius Halicarnassensis 8.47; τ. ἐμαυτὸν εἰς τάξιν τινά 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Memorabilia” 2.8; τινὰς εἰς τοὺς ἀρχικούς [prev. work] 7; εἰς τὴν δουλείαν ἐμαυτόν [prev. work] 11]]; τ. ἑαυτόν τινων εἶναι range oneself with.., [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 19.302:]] —passive, πρὸς τὴν ξυμμαχίαν ταχθῆναι to join it, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 3.86.]]

__III
with accusative of things, place in a certain order or relative position, χωρὶς ἑκάτερα τ. [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 7.36]]; τίνα μέσον τάξω λόγο; [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Electra” 908]]; πρῶτον καὶ τελευταῖον τὸ κάλλιστον τ. [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Memorabilia” 3.1.9; τὰ τυφλὰ τοῦ σώματος καὶ ἄοπλα ἐναντία τάττειν τοῖς πολεμίοις [prev. author] “Cyr.” 3.3.45; τοὺς πόδας [τοῦ ἐμβρύου] κατ᾽ εὐθὺ τοῦ στομίου τῆς ὑστέρας τάσσειν 2nd c.AD: Soranus Medicus 2.60; μὴ κατὰ ἄνεμον τῶν οἰκημάτων τάττειν τὴν ἅλω “Geoponica” 2.26.1; τάξας.. ἀπὸ μὲν δύσεως μίαν θυρίδα φωτὸς ἕνεκεν [prev. work]14.6.6; [κηρίας] τὴν μεσότητα τάσσειν ὑπὸ τὸ γένειον “PMed.Lond.” 155ii 29, compare 2nd c.AD: Soranus Medicus “de fasciis - Opera Hippocratis et Galeni” 25. +others; εἰς ταὐτὸ τ. τὴν εὐτυχίαν τῇ εὐδαιμονίᾳ 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Ethica Nicomachea” 1099b7]]; Λυδοὺς.. πρὸς ἅπαντας range over against, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Politicus” 262e; τὴν σοφιστικὴν περὶ τὸ μὴ ὂν ἔταξεν 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Metaphysica” 1026b15, compare “Top.” 125b21]]; with infinitive, [Ὅμηρον] ἐν τοῖς.. σοφωτάτοις εἶναι τάττομεν [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aeschines Orator 1.142; οὐκ εὐλόγως τὸ τοιοῦτον σημεῖον ἐν τοῖς φρενιτικοῖς τάττει 2nd c.AD: Galenus Medicus 16.521, compare 18(2).238]]; τ. τι ἐπί τινος apply a term to a certain sense, [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd c.AD: Athenaeus Epigrammaticus 1.21a]]:—passive, τετάχθαι κατά τινος [Refs 5th c.BC+ [1st c.BC: Dionysius Halicarnassensis 2.48; ἔμπροσθεν τ. τινός 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Leges” 631d, compare 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Memorabilia” 3.1.7, etc.]]

__III.b
with an infinitive and adjective, lay down, rule to be so and so, ἅπερ ἂν.. αἰσχρὰ εἶναι καὶ κακὰ τάττῃ [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Leges” 728a; τά τε δίκαια ταχθέντ᾽ εἶναι καὶ ἄδικα [prev. author] “Plt.” 305b.]]

__III.2
ordain, prescribe, τ. τὰ περὶ τὰ τέκνα [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Politica” 1262b6: _absolutely_, ὁ νόμος οὕτω τ. 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Laches” 199a; οὕτω τ. ὁ λόγος 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Ethica Nicomachea” 1119b17]]:—passive, τὸ ταττόμενον [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Ecclesiazusae” 766; τὸ ταχθὲν τελεῖν 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Ajax” 528; τὰ τεταγμένα 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 1.2.5, etc.]]; τὰ τετ. ἄγειν the things appointed to them for conveying,[Refs 4th c.BC+ [[prev. work] 8.5.4; τῆς τροφῆς ἡ βελτίστη τέτακται τοῖς ἐλευθέροις 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “de Generatione Animalium” 744b18]]; ἐν τῷ τεταγμένῳ εἶναι to be fulfilling one's obligations, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [Inscriptiones Graecae 12.57.47, 22.116.48, 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 6.2.37.]]

__III.3
of taxes or payments, assess, τὸν φόρον ταῖς πόλεσι [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Andocides Orator 4.11, compare 4th c.BC: Aeschines Orator 2.23, 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 23.209; ταῖσδε ἔταξαν οἱ τάκται “IG” 12.218.45; so τ. τῷ ναύτῃ δραχμήν 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Historia Graeca (Hellenica)” 1.5.4]]: with infinitive added, χρήματα τοῖς πᾶσι τάξαντες φέρειν [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 1.19, etc.]] (passive, φόρον ἐτάχθησαν φέρειν [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 3.97)]]; τάσσειν ἀργυρίου πολλοῦ fix a high price, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 4.26]]:—passive, τὸ ταχθὲν τίμημα [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 551b; εἰσφέρειν τὸ τεταγμένον 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Politica” 1272a14]]:—middle, take a payment on oneself, i.e. agree to pay it, φόρον τάξασθαι [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 3.13, 4.35; χρήματα ἀποδοῦναι ταξάμενοι 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 1.101]]; χρήματα ταξάμενοι κατὰ χρόνους ἀποδοῦναι agreeing to pay by instalments, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. work] 117, compare 3.70; πόλεις αὐταὶ ταξάμεναι “IG” 12.212.72, compare 211 vi 6; also τάξασθαι ἐς τὴν δωρεήν 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 3.97 (but also, much like _active_, ἐτάξατο φόρους οἱ προσιέναι [prev. work] 89).]]

__III.3.b
middle, generally, agree upon, settle, ταξαμένους.. δέχεσθαι μισθὸν τῆς φυλακῆς [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 416e; τὰς τιμάς [prev. author] “Lg.” 743e, compare 844b, 844c, +others]]; τέταγμαι ποιμέσιν, οἵ μοι δώσουσιν τιμήν [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [“PMich.Zen.” 56.19 (3rd c.BC)]]; votum explained as εὐχή, ὃ τάττεταί τις θεῷ, [Refs [“Corpus Glossariorum Latinorum”]]: with infinitive future, [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [“PEnteux.” 54.5 (3rd c.BC), 2nd c.BC: Polybius Historicus 18.7.7, +others]]

__III.3.c
middle, pay, τῆς δὲ τιμῆς τάξονται παραχρῆμα τὸ δ μέρος, τὸ δὲ λοιπὸν ἐν ἔτεσι γ [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [“PEleph.” 14.18 (3rd c.BC),compare “PEnteux.” 60.9, 89.7, “PMich.Zen.” 79.9, “PCair.Zen.” 649.16 (all 3rd c.BC), “PAmh.” 2.31.1, 52.1, “Ostr.Bodl.” i 46, 96, +others, “PLond.” 3.1201.1, 1202.1 (all 2nd c.BC).]]

__III.4
impose punishments, τ. δίκην [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Vespae” 1420, etc.]]; τ. ζημίας, τιμωρίας, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Leges” 876c, 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 20.143; τῷ κλέψαντι θάνατον 4th c.BC: Lycurgus Orator 65]]:— also in middle, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 2.65.]]

__III.4.b
impose laws, οὓς [νόμους] ἔταξε αὐτοῖς ὁ νομοθέτης [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Leges” 772c.]]

__III.5
in perfect participle passive, fixed, settled, prescribed, ὁ τεταγμένος χρόνος (like τακτός) [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 2.41, etc.; ὥρα 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Bacchae” 723; ἡμέρα 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 1.2.4; ἔτη 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Leges” 810b; ἡ τετ. χώρα 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 5.3.40]]; αἱ τετ. θυσίαι the regular offerings, [Refs [[prev. author] “HG” 3.3.4]]; οἱ ἐπὶ τούτῳ τετ. [νόμοι] [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Crito” 50d]]; ἡ τετ. δίαιτα prescribed, [Refs [[prev. author] “R.” 404a]]; τὰ τετ. ὀνόματα received, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Isocrates Orator 9.9]]; τετ. τέχνη regular, [Refs [[prev. author] 13.12]]; τεταγμένον, opposed to ἄτακτον, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “de Caelo” 280a8; νὺξ τὰ τεταγμέν᾽ ἀπέχει “Lyric poetry Alex. Adesp.” 37.6]]; of geometrical figures, regular, i.e. equilateral and equiangular, [Refs 3rd c.AD+ [3rd c.AD(?): Pappus Mathematicus 306.2, 8, +others--compare τεταγμένως.]]

deep_entry:
Abbott-Smith / STEPBible (TBESG)
οὗτος, αὕτη, τοῦτο, genitive, τούτου, ταύτης, τούτου,
[in LXX chiefly for זֹאת ,זֶה ;]
demonstr. pron. (related to ἐκεῖνος as hic to ille),
this;
__1. as subst., this one, he;
__(a) absol.: Mat.3:17, Mrk.9:7, Luk.7:44, 45, Jhn.1:15, Act.2:15, al.; expressing contempt (cl.), Mat.13:55, 56, Mrk.6:2, 3, Jhn.6:42, al.; εἰς τοῦτο, Mrk.1:38, Rom.14:9; μετὰ τοῦτο (ταῦτα; V. Westc. on Jhn.5:1), Jhn.2:12 11:7, al.;
__(b) epanaleptic (referring to what precedes): Mat.5:19, Mrk.3:35, Luk.9:48, Jhn.6:46, Rom.7:10, al.;
__(with) proleptic (referring to what follows): before ἵνα (Bl., §69, 6), Luk.1:43, Jhn.3:19 (and freq.) 15:8, Rom.14:9, al.; before ὅτι, Luk.10:11, Jhn.9:3o, Act.24:14, Rom.2:3, al.; ὅπως, Rom.9:17; ἐάν, Jhn.13:35;
__(d) special idioms: τοῦτο μὲν . . . τ. δέ (cl), partly . . . partly. Heb.10:33; καὶ τοῦτο (τοῦτον, ταῦτα), and that (him) too, Rom.13:11, 1Co.2:2, Heb.11:12; τοῦτ᾽ ἐστιν, Mat.27:46.
__2. As adj., with subst.;
__(a) with art.
__(α) before the art.: Mat.12:32, Mrk.9:29, Luk.7:44, Jhn.4:15, Rom.11:24, Rev.19:9, al.;
__(β) after the noun: Mat.3:9, Mrk.12:16, Luk.11:31, Jhn.4:13, Act.6:13, Rom.15:28, 1Co.1:20, Rev.2:24, al.;
__(b) with subst. anarth. (with predicative force; Bl., §49, 4): Luk.1:36 2:2 24:21, Jhn.2:11 4:54 21:14, 2Co.13:1.
(AS)

LSJ / STEPBible (TFLSJ)
οὗτος, αὕτη, τοῦτο,
genitive τούτου, ταύτης, τούτου, etc.: the dual feminine never in Attic dialect, see ὁ, ἡ, τό, [near the start]:—demonstrative pronoun, this, common from [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Homerus Epicus downwards]]

__A
ORIGIN and FORMS: οὗτος, αὕτη, τοῦτο probably arose from a reduplication of the demonstrative ὁ, ἡ, τό with insertion of -υ- (= Sanskrit Particle u), e.g. ταῦτα from τα-υ-τα: Doric dialect genitive singular feminine τούτας [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Philolaus Philosophus 11; _nominative_ _plural_ τοῦτοι, ταῦται 2nd c.AD: Apollonius Dyscolus Grammaticus “de Syntaxi;” 111.23: the former occurs 5th c.BC: Sophron Comicus 24, “GDI” 3045 B 6 (from Selinus), “SIG” 339.16 (Rhodes, 3rd c.BC)]], etc., the latter is uncertain in [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophron Comicus 97, certain in “SIG” 241 B 117 (Delph., 4th c.BC): in _Boeotian dialect_ all forms begin with οὑτ-]], as genitive singular neuter οὕτω [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [“Supp.epigram” 3.359.11 (3rd c.BC)]]; accusative singular feminine οὕταν [Refs 6th c.BC+ [6th c.BC: Corinna Lyrica “Supp.” 2.80; _accusative_ _plural_ _neuter_ οὗτα “SIG” 1185.20 (Tanagra, 3rd c.BC), etc.: _genitive_ _plural_ _feminine_ _Attic dialect_ τούτων, Cretan dialect ταυτᾶν “Leg.Gort.” 5.19; _neuter_ ταύτων “Michel” 1334.10 (Elis, 4th c.BC).—In _Ionic dialect_ sometimes written ταότην, ταο̄τα, “SIG” 283.19 (Chios, 4th c.BC), 46.7 (Halic., 5th c.BC), +others]] —In _Attic dialect_ οὗτος was frequently strengthened by the _demonstrative_ -ί, οὑτοσί, αὑτηί, τουτί, _genitive_ τουτουί, _dative_ τουτῳί, _accusative_ τουτονί; plural nominative οὑτοιί, neuter ταυτί, etc., this man here: sometimes a Particle is inserted between the pronoun and -ί, as αὑτηγί for αὑτηί γε, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Acharnenses” 784]]; τουτογί for τουτί γε, [Refs [[prev. author] “V.” 781, “Av.” 894, +others]]; ταυταγί for ταυτί γε, [Refs [[prev. author] “Eq.” 492, “Pax” 1057, +others]]; τουτοδί for τουτὶ δέ, [Refs [[prev. author] “Pl.” 227]]; τουτουμενί for τουτουὶ μέν, [Refs [[prev. author] “Ra.” 965.]] —In codices the ν ἐφελκυστικόν is sometimes added in the forms οὑτοσίν, οὑτωσίν, and οὑτοσίν is said to be Attic dialect by [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd c.AD: Apollonius Dyscolus Grammaticus “de Pronominibus;” 59.24, 82.11]]. [This ι is always long, and a long vowel or diphthong before it becomes short, as αὑτη?~Xί, τουτω?~Xί, οὑτοῐί, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Nubes” 201, “Pl.” 44, “Ach.” 40, etc.]]]

__B
USAGE in regard to CONCOR[Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator οὗτος]] is frequently used as a pronoun substantive: hence neuter is followed by genitive, κατὰ τοῦτο τῆς ἀκροπόλιος [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.84; εἰς τοῦθ᾽ ὕβρεως ἐλήλυθεν 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 4.37; εἰς τοῦθ᾽ ἥκεις μανίας [prev. author] 36.48; ταῦτα τῶν μαθημάτων 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Euthydemus” 278b: but quite as frequently as]] adjective, in which case its substantive commonly takes the Article, οὗτος ὁ ἀνήρ or ὁ ἀνὴρ οὗτος.—But the Article is absent,

__B.1
always in Epic dialect Poets (except [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 18.114), οὗτος ἀνήρ 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 14.471, 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 1.406, etc.]]: sometimes also in Trag., [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Persae” 122 (Lyric poetry), 495, 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Philoctetes” 406, “OC” 471, 1177: once in an Inscription, τοπεῖα: τούτων τὰ ἡμίσεα τοπείων “IG” 22.1622.135 (4th c.BC).]]

__B.2
sometimes when the Noun is so specified that the Article is not needed, ἐς γῆν ταύτην.., ἥντινα νῦν Σκύθαι νέμονται [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 4.8; ταύτας ἃς οἱ πατέρες παρέδοσαν μελέτας 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 1.85, compare 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 449d, etc.; πατὴρ σὸς οὗτος, ὃν θρηνεῖς ἀεί 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Electra” 530.]]

__B.3
when οὗτος is used in local sense, here, see below with [Refs [1.5.]]

__B.4
when the Noun with which οὗτος agrees stands as its Predicate, αὕτη γὰρ ἦν σοι πρόφασις [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Philoctetes” 1034]]; δικαστοῦ αὕτη ἀρετή [ἐστι] [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Apologia” 18a: this exception extends to cases in which the Predicate is not so distinctly separated from the Subject, αἰτίαι μὲν αὗται προυγεγένηντο]] these were the grievances which already existed, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 1.66]]; ταύτην φήμην παρέδοσαν this was the report which.., [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Philebus” 16c: frequently with a _superlative_, κίνησις αὕτη μεγίστη δὴ.. ἐγένετο]] this was notably the greatest movement which.., [NT+5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 1.1, compare 3.113: with πρῶτος [prev. author] 1.55, 98, 6.31, NT.Luke.2.2.]]

__B.5
when 3rd pers. is used for 2nd pers. to express contempt, οὗτος ἀνήρ, οὑτοσὶ ἀνήρ, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Gorgias” 467b, 489b, etc.]]

__B.II
though οὗτος usually agrees with the Noun that serves as Predicate, it is not rare to find it in the neuter, μανία δὲ καὶ τοῦτ᾽ ἐστί [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Bacchae” 305; τοῦτο γάρ εἰσι.. εὔθυναι 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 19.82, etc.]]: and in plural, οὐκ ἔστι ταῦτα ἀρχή [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aeschines Orator 3.13; ταῦτ᾽ ἐστὶν ὁ προδότης [prev. author] 2.166]]: so with an explanatory clause added, τοῦτο γάρ ἐστιν ὁ συκοφάντης, αἰτιᾶσθαι μὲν πάντα ἐξελέγξαι δὲ μηδέν [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 57.34.]]

__B.II.2
so also with a Noun in apposition, τούτοισιν μὲν ταῦτα μέλει, κίθαρις καὶ ἀοιδή [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 1.159; τούτου τιμῶμαι, ἐν πρυτανείῳ σιτήσεως 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Apologia” 36e, compare 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Fragmenta” 323.3, etc.]]

__B.II.3
the neuter also may refer to a masculine or feminine Noun, καρπὸν φορέει κυάμῳ ἴσον: τοῦτο ἐπεὰν γένηται πέπον κτλ. [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 4.23, compare 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 1.5.10, etc.]]

__B.II.4
the neuter is also used of classes of persons, μελιτοπῶλαι καὶ τυροπῶλαι: τοῦτο δ᾽ εἰς ἕν ἐστι συγκεκυφός [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Equites” 854, compare 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Leges” 711a]]; or of an abstract fact, οὐκ Ἰοφῶν ζ;—τοῦτο γάρ τοι καὶ μόνον ἔτ᾽ ἐστὶ λοιπὸν ἀγαθόν [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Ranae” 73.]]

__B.III
with Prons.,

__B.III.1
personal, οὗτος σύ, in local sense, see below

__B.III.2
interrogative, τί τοῦτ᾽ ἔλεξα; what is this that.. ? [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Philoctetes” 1173 (Lyric poetry), compare “Ant.” 7]]; ποίοισι τούτοι; for ποῖά ἐστι ταῦτα οἷς [ἔχεις ἐλπίδα]; [Refs [[prev. author] “OC” 388, compare “Ant.” 1049]]; Νέστορ᾽ ἔρειο ὅν τινα τοῦτον ἄγει whom he brings here, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 11.612.]]

__B.III.3
with οἷος, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 20.377, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Phaedo” 61c.]]

__B.III.4
possessive, πατὴρ σὸς οὗτος this father of thine, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Electra” 530, compare 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 7.3.30.]]

__B.III.5
demonstrative, οὗτος ἐκεῖνος, τὸν σὺ ζητέεις, where ἐκεῖνος is the Predicate, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.32; τοῦτ᾽ ἔστ᾽ ἐκεῖνο 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Helena” 622, compare “Or.” 804; αὐτὸ τοῦτο, see at {αὐτός} I.7]]; τοῦτον τὸν αὐτὸν ἄνδρα this same man, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Philoctetes” 128.]]

__B.III.5.b
exceptionally, Διφίλου οὗτος ὅδ᾽ ἐστὶ τύπος [Refs [“IG” 12(5).300 (from Paros).]]

__B.III.6
ἄλλος τις οὗτος ἀνέστη another man here, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 20.380.]]

__B.IV
with Numerals, τέθνηκε ταῦτα τρία ἔτη these three years, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Lysias Orator 7.10 codices]]; [στρατείαν] ἑνδέκατον μῆνα τουτονὶ ποιεῖται for these eleven months, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 8.2, compare 3.4; τριακοστὴν ταύτην ἡμέραν 4th-3rd c.BC: Menander Comicus “Ἐπιτρέποντες” 27; ταύτας τριάκοντα μνᾶς 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 27.23, compare 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Gorgias” 463b, etc.]]

__C
SIGNIFICATION AND SPECIAL IDIOMS:

__C.I
this, to designate the nearer, opposed to ἐκεῖνος, that, the more remote, ταῦτα, like τὰ ἐνταῦθα, things round and about us, earthly things, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Phaedo” 75e (variant)]]; compare ὅδε [near the start]: but οὗτος sometimes indicates that which is not really nearest, but most important, δεῖ.. τὸ βέλτιστον ἀεί, μὴ τὸ ῥᾷστον λέγειν: ἐπὶ ἐκεῖνο μὲν γὰρ ἡ φύσις αὐτὴ βαδιεῖται, ἐπὶ τοῦτο δὲ κτλ. [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 8.72, compare 51.3 and 18.]]

__C.I.2
when, of two things, one precedes and the other follows, ὅδε properly refers to what follows, οὗτος to what precedes, οὐκ ἔστι σοι ταῦτ᾽, ἀλλά σοι τάδ᾽ ἔστι [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Coloneus” 787, compare ὅδε III. 2: frequently, however, where there are not two things, οὗτος]] refers to what follows, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 13.377, 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 2.306, etc.]]; οὔκουν.. τοῦτο γιγνώσκεις, ὅτι..; [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Prometheus Vinctus” 379, etc.]]

__C.I.3
οὗτος is used emphatic, generally in contempt, while ἐκεῖνος denotes praise, ὁ πάντ᾽ ἄναλκις οὗτος, i.e. Aegisthus, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Electra” 301; τούτους τοὺς συκοφάντας 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Crito” 45a; so 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator “de Coron.” uses οὗτος of Aeschines, ἐκεῖνος]] of Philip; but οὗτος is used of Philip, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 2.15, 4.3.]]

__C.I.3.b
of what is familiar, τούτους τοὺς πολυτελεῖς χιτῶνας, of the Persians, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 1.5.8; οἱ τὰς τελετὰς.. οὗτοι καταστήσαντες 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Phaedo” 69c, compare “Men.” 80a]]; τὸ θυλακῶδες τοῦτο the familiar bag-like thing, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-3rd c.BC: Theophrastus Philosophus “Historia Plantarum” 3.7.3, compare 3.18.11, 4.7.1; οἱ τὰς κόρας ταύτας ὠνούμενοι τοῖς παισίν 1st-2nd c.AD: Dio Chrysostomus Sophista 31.153.]]

__C.I.4
in Attic dialect law-language, οὗτος is commonly applied to the opponent, whether plaintiff (as in [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aeschines Orator 2.130)]] or defendant (as in [Refs [[prev. author] 1.1)]]; so, in the political speeches of [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator, οὗτοι]] are the opposite party, [Refs [4.1, 8.7]], etc.; but in the forensic speeches, οὗτοι frequently means the judges, the court, [Refs [21.134, 36.47.]]

__C.I.5
much like an adverb, in local sense (compare ὅδε [near the start]), τίς δ᾽ οὗτος κατὰ νῆας.. ἔρχεα; who art thou here that comest.. ? [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 10.82]]; frequently in Attic dialect, τίς οὑτοσ; who's this here? [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Acharnenses” 1048]]; πολλὰ ὁρῶ ταῦτα πρόβατα I see many sheep here, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 3.5.9 (as variant): with _pronoun_ of 2 _person_, οὗτος σύ]] ho you! you there! [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Tyrannus” 532, 1121, 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Hecuba” 1280, etc.: and then οὗτος alone like a _vocative_, οὗτος, τί ποιεῖ; 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Supplices” 911,compare 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Ajax” 71, 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Alcestis” 773, 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Equites” 240, “Nu.” 220, +others]]: with a proper name, ὦ οὗτος, Αἴας [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Ajax” 89; ὦ οὗτος οὗτος, Οἰδίπους [prev. author] “OC” 1627, compare 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Vespae” 1364: with _vocative_, βέντισθ᾽ οὗτος 3rd c.BC: Theocritus Poeta Bucolicus 5.76:—the _feminine_ is rarer, αὕτη 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Medea” 922; αὕτη σύ 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Thesmophoriazusae” 610.]] —This phrase mostly implies anger, impatience, or scorn.

__C.II
simply as antecedent to ὅς, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 2.40, 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Tyrannus” 1180, etc.: frequently following _relative_ clause, ἅ γ᾽ ἔλαβες,.. μεθεῖναι ταῦτα [prev. author] “Ph.” 1247, compare 1319, “Ant.” 183, 203, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Gorgias” 469c.]]

__C.III
= τοιοῦτος, οὗτος ἐγὼ ταχυτᾶτι [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “O.” 4.26; σὺ τοίνυν οὗτος εὑρέθης 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 18.282, compare 173.]]

__C.IV
after a parenthesis, the Subject, though already named, is frequently emphatic repeated by οὗτος, οὐδὲ γὰρ οὐδὲ Ἀριστέης.., οὐδὲ οὗτος προσωτέρω.. ἔφησε ἀπικέσθαι [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 4.16, compare 81 (assuming variant), 1.146, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Phaedo” 107d, etc.]]

__C.V
καὶ οὗτος is added to heighten the force of a previous word, ξυνεστῶτες.. ναυτικῷ ἀγῶνι, καὶ τούτῳ πρὸς Ἀθηναίους [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 4.55, compare 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.147, 6.11, etc.; so οὐδὲ τούτου 4th c.BC: Aeschines Orator 2.100]]; see infr. VIII.2.

__C.VI
repeated, where for the second we should merely say he or it, τοῖσιν τούτου τοῦτον μέλεσιν.. κελαδοῦντες [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Ranae” 1526, compare 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Laches” 200d.]]

__C.VII
ταῦτα is used in some special phrases,

__C.VII.1
ταῦτ᾽, ὦ δέσποτα yes Sir (i. e. ἔστι ταῦτα, ταῦτα δράσω, etc.), [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Vespae” 142, “Pax” 275, compare “Eq.” III; so ταῦτα δή [prev. author] “Ach.” 815; ταῦτά νυν [prev. author] “V.” 1008]]; so also ἦν ταῦτα even so, true, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Phoenissae” 417.]]

__C.VII.2
ταῦτα μὲν δὴ ὑπάρξει so it shall be, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Phaedo” 78a.]]

__C.VII.3
καὶ ταῦτα μὲν δὴ ταῦτα so much for that, frequently in Attic dialect, as [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Symposium” 220c.]]

__C.VII.4
ταῦτα at end of a formula in epitaphs, etc., probably short for ταῦτα οὕτως ἔχει or ὁ βίος ταῦτά ἐστιν, e.g. οὐδὶς (= -εὶς) ἀθάνατος: ταῦτα [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [“IG” 14.420; Προκόπι ταῦτα [prev. work]1824; χαίρεται (= -τε) ταῦτα [prev. work]1479, etc.: similarly perhaps in a letter, ἂμ μὴ πέμψῃς, οὐ μὴ φάγω, οὐ μὴ πείνω. ταῦτα “POxy.” 119.15 (2nd-3rd c.AD).]]

__C.VIII
Adverbial usages:

__C.VIII.1
ταῦταabsolutely, therefore, that is why.., [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 11.694; ταῦτ᾽ ἄρα 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Acharnenses” 90, “Nu.” 319, 335, 394, +others, 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Symposium” 4.55; ταῦτα δή 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Persae” 159, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Symposium” 174a; ταῦτ᾽ οὖν 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Trachiniae” 550, 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Vespae” 1358, etc.]]; αὐτὰ ταῦτα ἥκω, ἵνα.. [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Protagoras” 310e: τοῦτο]] is rare in this sense, τοῦτ᾽ ἀφικόμην, ὅπως.. εὖ πράξαιμί τι [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Tyrannus” 1005]]; αὐτὸ γὰρ τοῦτο just because of this, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Symposium” 204a.]]

__C.VIII.1.b
πρὸς ταῦτα so then, therefore, properly used in indignant defiance, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Prometheus Vinctus” 992, 1043, 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Ajax” 971, 1115, 1313, “OT” 426, “OC” 455, etc.]]

__C.VIII.2
καὶ ταῦτα, adding a circumstance heightening the force of what has been said, and that, ἄνδρα γενναῖον θανεῖν, καὶ ταῦτα πρὸς γυναικός [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Eumenides” 627]]: but mostly with a participle, ὅς γ᾽ ἐξέλυσας ἄστυ.., καὶ ταῦθ᾽ ὑφ᾽ ἡμῶν οὐδὲν ἐξειδὼς πλέον [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Tyrannus” 37, compare 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Ranae” 704, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Phaedrus” 241e, etc.]]; or with a participle omitted, ἥτις.. τὴν τεκοῦσαν ὕβρισεν, καὶ ταῦτα τηλικοῦτος (i.e. οὖσα) [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Electra” 614; so καὶ ταῦτα μέντοι 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Eryxias” 400b.]]

__C.VIII.2.b
καὶ ταῦτα anyhow, no matter what happens (or happened), ἐπεχείρησας, οὐδὲν ὢν καὶ ταῦτα you tried, but were no good anyhow, i.e. try as you might, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [[prev. author] “R.” 341c, compare 4th c.BC: Diodorus Comicus 3.5.]]

__C.VIII.3
τοῦτο μέν.., τοῦτο δέ.. on the one hand.., on the other.., partly.., partly.., very frequently in [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus, as 1.161, +others]]; τοῦτο μέν is sometimes answered by δέ only,[Refs 5th c.BC+ [4.76, 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Ajax” 670, “OC” 440]]; by δὲ αὖ, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 7.176]]; by ἔπειτα δέ, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Antigone” 61]]; by ἀλλά, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 22.13]]; by εἶτα, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Philoctetes” 1345]]; by τοῦτ᾽ αὖθις, [Refs [[prev. author] “Ant.” 165.]]

__C.VIII.4
dative feminine ταύτῃ,

__C.VIII.4.a
on this spot, here, ταύτῃ μὲν.., τῇδε δ᾽ αὖ.. [Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. author] “Ph.” 1331; ἀλλ᾽ ἐὰν ταύτῃ γε νικᾷ, ταυτῃὶ πεπλήξεται 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Equites” 271, compare “Th.” 1221.]]

__C.VIII.4.b
in this point, herein, μηδὲν ταύτῃ γε κομήσῃς [Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. author] “Pl.” 572, compare 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Hiero” 7.12, etc.]]

__C.VIII.4.c
in this way, thus, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Prometheus Vinctus” 191, 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Coloneus” 1300, etc.; οὐ.. ταῦτ᾽ ἐστί πω ταύτῃ 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Equites” 843; ἀλλ᾽ οὔτι ταύτῃ ταῦτα 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Medea” 365, compare 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Prometheus Vinctus” 511: antecedent to ὥσπερ, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 330c]]; to ὅπῃ, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 8.3.2; οὕτω τε καὶ ταύτῃ γίγνοιτο 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Leges” 681d; καὶ οὕτω καὶ ταύτῃ ἂν ἔχοι [prev. work] 714d]]; ταύτῃ καλεῖσθαι, etc., like οὕτω κ., [Refs 5th c.BC+ [Scholia 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Symposium” 215b.]]

__C.VIII.5
ἐκ τούτου or τούτων thereupon, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Historia Graeca (Hellenica)” 3.1.6, “Oec.” 2.1]]; therefore, [Refs [[prev. author] “An.” 3.3.5.]]

__C.VIII.6
ἐν τούτῳ in that case, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 440c.]]

__C.VIII.6.b
in the meantime, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.126, 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 3.72, 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Memorabilia” 2.1.27.]]

__C.VIII.7
πρὸς τούτοις (-οισι) besides, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 2.51, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Protagoras” 326a, 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Memorabilia” 2.4.4, 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Plutus” 540.]]
