LSJ / STEPBible (TFLSJ)
τᾰχύς [ῠ], εῖα, ύ:

__I
of motion, swift, fleet, opposed to βραδύς,

__I.1
of persons and animals, either absolutely, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 18.69, etc.]]; or more fully, πόδας ταχύς [Refs [13.249, 482, 17.709, etc.]]; ταχὺς ἔσκε θέειν [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 17.308]]; θείειν τ. [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 16.186, 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 3.112]]; κύνες, ἔλαφος, πτώξ, ἵππος, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 3.26, 8.248, 17.676, 23.347, etc.; οἰωνόν, ταχὺν ἄγγελον 24.292, compare 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 15.526]]; τ. βαδιστής a quick walker, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Medea” 1182]]; σφοδροὶ καὶ τ. [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 2.1.31.]]

__I.2
of things, τ. πόδες [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 6.514, compare 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 13.261, etc.]]; τ. ἰός, ὀϊστοί, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 4.94, 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 22.3, etc.; πτερά 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Aves” 1453; -ύτατα ἅρματα 5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “O.” 1.77]]; νῆες, τριήρεις, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 8.23, 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 6.43, etc.; [ἴχνος] τὸ τοῦ ποδὸς μὲν βραδύ, τὸ τοῦ δὲ νοῦ ταχύ 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Ion” 742.]]

__II
of thought and purpose, quick, hasty, φρονεῖν γὰρ οἱ ταχεῖς οὐκ ἀσφαλεῖς [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Tyrannus” 617: with]]infinitive, βλάπτειν τ. [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Ranae” 1428; τ. βουλεῦσαί τι ἀνήκεστον 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 1.132, compare 118, 2nd c.AD: Lucianus Sophista “Dem.Enc.” 12; also τ. πρὸς ὀργήν 1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus “Cat.Mi.” 1]]; τὸ ταχύ speed, haste, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Phoenissae” 452, 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “de Equitandi ratione” 7.18, etc.]]

__II.2
of actions, events, etc., rapid, sudden, πήδημα [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Ajax” 833]]; ᾅδης, μόρος, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Hippolytus” 1047, 2nd c.BC: Moschus Bucolicus 3.26; πόλεμος 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 4.55, 6.45; φυγή [prev. author] 4.44; μεταβολή 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 553d]]; short, τ. ἐλπίδες fleeting hopes, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “P.” 1.83; ἐπαυρέσεις 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 2.53; ἀτραπός 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Ranae” 127; ταχεῖ σὺν χρόνῳ 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Coloneus” 1602]]; τ. διήγησις short, rapid, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Rhetorica” 1416b30.]]

__B
adverb,

__B.1
regular τᾰχέως, quickly, opposed to βραδέως, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 23.365, 8th-7th c.BC: Hesiodus Epicus “Theogonia” 103, etc.]]:—rarely in sense perhaps [Refs 2nd c.BC+ [compare (τάχα 11), 2nd c.BC: Polybius Historicus 16.25.8.]]

__B.2
the  adverb is also expressed by periphrastic, διὰ ταχέων in haste, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 1.80, 3.13, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Apologia” 32d, 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 1.5.9; ἐκ ταχείας 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Trachiniae” 395; compare τάχος 11.]]

__B.3
neuter ταχύ as adverb, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “P.” 10.51, “N.” 1.51, 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Philoctetes” 349, 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Hercules Furens” 885 (Lyric poetry), 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Equites” 109, 2nd c.AD: Galenus Medicus 16.665, etc.]]; ἤδη ἤδη τ. τ. [Refs 3rd c.AD+ [“Sammelb.” 4321.21, “BGU” 956.3 (both 3rd c.AD)]]; ἄρτι ἄρτι τ. τ. [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [“Arch.Papyrus” 5.393 (2nd c.AD)]]; also τάχα (which see).

__B.4
the adjective ταχύς is frequently construed with Verbs, where we should use the adverb, ταχέες δ᾽ ἱππῆες ἄγερθεν [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 23.287; ταχεῖά γ᾽ ἦλθε χρησμῶν πρᾶξις 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Persae” 739; ὁρμάσθω ταχύς 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Philoctetes” 526]]; δεῦρ᾽ ἀφίξεται τ. [Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. author] “OC” 307; τ. χάρις διαρρεῖ [prev. author] “Aj.” 1266, compare 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 2.75, 5.66.]]

__C
Degrees of Comparison:

__C.I
comparative:

__C.I.1
the form τᾰχύτερος, α, ον, is used by [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus, ἐποίησα ταχύτερα ἢ σοφώτερα 3.65, compare 7.194]]; also in [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “de Mundo” 394b3, 2nd c.AD: Arrianus Historicus “Indica” 9.6, 2nd c.AD: Aretaeus Medicus “περὶ αἰτιῶν καὶ σημείων χρονίων παθῶν” 1.16]], but not in good Attic dialect; ταχύτερον as adverb, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 4.127, 9.101, 5th c.BC: Hippocrates Medicus “προγνωστικόν” 17.]]

__C.I.2
the more usual form is θάσσων, neuter θᾶσσον, genitive ονος, Attic dialect θάττων, neuter θᾶττον, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 15.570, 13.819 (elsewhere only _neuter_ in 8th c.BC: Homerus Epicus)]], etc.:—neuter as adverb, frequently in [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Homerus Epicus, 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 2.307, +others]]; θᾶσσον ἂν.. κλύοιμι sooner, i.e. rather, would I hear, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Philoctetes” 631]]; θᾶσσον also often stands for the Positive, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 2.440, 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 15.201, 16.130, 5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “P.” 4.181, 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Nubes” 506, “V.” 187, “Ra.” 94]]; οὐ θᾶσσον οἴσει; i.e. make haste and bring, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Trachiniae” 1183, compare “OT” 430]]; θᾶττον νοήματος quicker than thought, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Memorabilia” 4.3.13, compare 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Vespae” 824, etc.]]; with a conjunction, ὅτι θᾶσσον, like{ὅτι τάχιστα}, [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [3rd c.BC: Theocritus Poeta Bucolicus 24.48]]; ἐπειδὴ θᾶττον συνεσκότασεν as soon as.. , [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 54.5; ἐπειδὰν θ. συνιῇ τις 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Protagoras” 325c; ὅταν θ. φθέγγηται ὁ κόκκυξ 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Historia Animalium” 563b17, compare 611a5]]; ἐὰν or ἢν θ. as soon as.. , [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 3.3.20, “An.” 6.5.20, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus Alcaeus1.105a]]; ἂν θ. [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-3rd c.BC: Menander Comicus “Περικειρομένη” 174]]; εἰ θ. [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Epistulae” 324b]]; ὡς θ. [Refs 2nd c.BC+ [2nd c.BC: Polybius Historicus 1.66.1, 3.82.1]]; θ. rarely = sooner than, before, ἐξήλαυνον μεσημβρίας οὐ πολλῷ τινι θ. [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd c.AD: Aristides Rhetor “Orationes” 51 (27). 13 (compare τάχιον below 3).]]

__C.I.3
the form ταχίων [ῑ], neuter ιον, is frequently in late Prose, as [LXX+5th c.BC+ [LXX.Wis.13.9, LXX.1Mac.2.40, 3rd-2nd c.BC: Philo Mechanicus “(Belopoeica) Excerpte aus Philons Mechanik - Ath. Berl. Akad.” 69.14, 17, 73.23, 1st c.BC: Geminus Astronomicus 1.20, 1st c.BC: Dionysius Halicarnassensis 6.42, 1st c.BC: Diodorus Siculus Historicus 20.6, 1st c.AD: Josephus Historicus (see. below), 1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus 2.240d, NT.John.20.4, 4th c.AD: Alciphro Epistolographus 3.4; also in 5th c.BC: Hippocrates Medicus “γυναικεῖα” 1.1, 4th-3rd c.BC: Menander Comicus 402.16]]; but condemned by [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd c.AD: Phrynichus Atticista 58, 2nd c.AD: Herodianus Grammaticus “Philet.” p.436 P.]]; τὴν ταχίονα τῆς τροφῆς παράθεσιν earlier, sooner, [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd c.AD: Galenus Medicus 19.206:]] — adverb τάχιον earlier, πλέεται.. περὶ τὸν Σεπτέμβριον μῆνα.., οὐδὲν δὲ κωλύει κἂν τ. [Refs [“Periplus Maris Rubri [1st c.AD]” 24]]; τ. τῆς ὑποσχέσεως sooner than they had promised, [Refs [“Rev.Ét.Gr.” 6.159 (from Iasus)]]; τ. τοῦ παραγγέλματος [Refs 1st c.AD+ [1st c.AD: Josephus Historicus “Bellum Judaicum” 4.4.2; εἰς μακρὸν αὐτῶν γῆρας καὶ βίου μῆκος ὅμοιον τοῖς τ. ἐπερχομένων [prev. author] “AJ” 1.3.7; ἀποπαύεται οὔτε τ. ἐτῶν τεσσαράκοντα οὔτε βράδιον ἐτῶν πεντήκοντα 2nd c.AD: Soranus Medicus 1.20, compare 48, +others]]; formerly, ἐπεσκεύασαν τὸ παρόχιον,.. τ. γενόμενον γυμνάσιον [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [“IGRom.” 3.639 (Lycia, 2nd c.AD), compare 4.1517 (from Sardis), 1632.14 (from Philadelphia), 1665.5 (from Tira), Keil-Premerstein “Dritter Bericht“ p.79  (3rd c.AD), “Hermes” 63.229 (from Callatis)]]; compare above 2 near the end

__C.II
superlative:

__C.II.1
the form ταχύτατος is rare, ταχύτατα ἅρματα [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “O.” 1.77]]; ταχύτατα as adverb, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Historia Graeca (Hellenica)” 5.1.27 codices, 4th c.BC: Antiphanes Comicus 87 codices]]; but both passages have been corrected.

__C.II.2
the usual form is τάχιστος, η, ον, used by [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Homerus Epicus only in _neuter_ _plural_ τάχιστα]] as adverb, most quickly, most speedily, ὅττι τάχιστα as soon as may be, as soon as possible, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 4.193, 9.659, +others; ὅτι τάχιστα 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Tyrannus” 1341 (Lyric poetry), 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 3.31, etc.]]; so ὅσον τ. [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Choephori” 772, 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Tyrannus” 1436, etc.]]; ᾳ (probably) τ. [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “O.” 13.79]]; ὅπως τ. [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Agamemnon” 605, 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Tyrannus” 1410, 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Vespae” 167]]; ὡς τ. [Refs 5th c.BC+ [“IG” 12.76.23, 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.210, 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 4.15, 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Rhesus” 147, 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 1.3.14]]: these are elliptically phrases, as may be seen from the following examples, ὡς δυνατόν ἐστι τάχιστα [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Leges” 710b, 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 5.4.3]]; ᾗ δυνατὸν τ. [Refs [[prev. author] “HG” 6.3.6]]; ὡς or ᾗ ἠδύνατο τ. [Refs [[prev. author] “Cyr.” 3.2.14, “An.” 1.2.4]]; ὡς δύναιτο τ. [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.79]]; ὡς or ᾗ ἂν δύνωμαι τ. [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Historia Graeca (Hellenica)” 4.1.38, “Cyr.” 7.1.9, compare “IG” 12.106.18.]]

__C.II.2.b
τάχιστα after Particles of Time, as soon as, ἐπεὶ (Ionic dialect ἐπεί τε) τάχιστα [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Prometheus Vinctus” 201, 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.27, 75, 7.163, 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 7.2.6, “PCair.Zen.” 34.12 (3rd c.BC)]]; ἐπειδὴ τ. [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Protagoras” 310d, 4th c.BC: Isaeus Orator 9.3, 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 27.16, etc.]]; ἐπεὰν τ. [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 4.134, 7.129, 8.144]]; ἐπὰν τ. [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 4.6.9]]; ἐπειδὰν τ. [Refs [[prev. author] “Cyr.” 1.3.14, “An.” 3.1.9]]; ὅταν τ. [Refs [[prev. author] “Cyr.” 4.5.33: also ὡς τ]]. separated by one or more words, ὡς ἡμέρη τ. ἐγεγόνεε [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.11, compare 19, 47, 65, +others, 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 1.3.2, “Mem.” 1.2.16, +others; ὡς δὲ τ. ἐξῆλθε.. κόρον ἔτεκε “IG” 42(1).121.4 (Epid., 4th c.BC)]]; ὡς γὰρ τ. εἰσῆλθον [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-3rd c.BC: Menander Comicus “Περικειρομένη” 287; ὡς ἂν τ. λάβῃς τὴν ἐπιστολήν “PCair.Zen.” 241.1 (3rd c.BC); but ὡς τ. γὰρ ἀπεδήμησας [prev. work] 472.7 (3rd c.BC)]]; ὅπως τ. [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Prometheus Vinctus” 230:]] —the same notion is sometimes expressed by the participle, ἀπαλλαγεὶς τάχιστα, ={ὡς ἀπηλλάγη τ}., [Refs 1st c.AD+ [1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus “Demosthenes” 8, compare 25.]]

__C.II.3

[in LXX chiefly for parts and derivatives of מָהַר ;]
swiftness, speed. Adverbially, ἐν τ. (ταχέως), quickly, speedily, soon: Luk.18:8, Act.12:7 22:18 25:4, Rom.16:20, 1Ti.3:14, Rev.1:1 22:6.†

τάχος [ᾰ], εος, τό,
(ταχύς) swiftness, speed, ἵπποισι.., οἷσιν Ἀθήνη νῦν ὤρεξε τ. [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 23.406, compare 515; τ. καὶ βραδυτής 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Theaetetus” 156c, 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Physica” 228b29, etc.]]: plural, velocities, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Timaeus” 39d, “Lg.” 893d.]]

__2
τ. φρενῶν quickness of temper, hastiness, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Bacchae” 670; ὁ χρόνος μάθησιν ἀντὶ τοῦ τάχους.. δίδωσι [prev. author] “Supp.” 419]]; falsa lectio in [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Leges” 944c]]; τ. τῆς ψυχῆς quickness of apprehension, [Refs [[prev. work] 689c.]]

__II
τάχος is frequently used in Adverbial phrases for ταχέως, absolutely in accusative, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Septem contra Thebas” 58, “Ag.” 945, “Eu.” 124, 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Rhesus” 986, “HF” 860 (troch.), etc.]]; also in dative, τάχει ὁμοίως with like velocities, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Timaeus” 36d: with Preps., διὰ τάχους 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Ajax” 822, 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 1.63, etc.; ἐν τάχει 5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “N.” 5.35, 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Prometheus Vinctus” 747, 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Coloneus” 500, 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 1.86, “PCair.Zen.” 62 (b). 10 (3rd c.BC), etc.]]; εἰς τάχος [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “de Equitandi ratione” 3.5, 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Acharnenses” 686, etc.; κατὰ τάχος 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.124, 152, 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 1.73]]; κατὰ τὸ τ. [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [“PCair.Zen.” 130.11 (3rd c.BC); τὸ τ. (without κατὰ) [prev. work] 158.2, 166.4, 428.15, “PHib.” 1.62.13 (all 3rd c.BC). etc.]]; μετὰ τάχους [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Protagoras” 332b]]; μετὰ παντὸς τ. with all speed, [Refs 3rd c.AD+ [POxy. 2107.4 (3rd c.AD)]]; σὺν τάχει [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Ajax” 853, “OC” 885 (Lyric poetry), 904: also with relatives, ὡς τάχος,]] ={ὡς τάχιστα}, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Agamemnon” 27, “Ch.” 889, 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 5.106, 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Lysistrata” 1187; so ὅ τι τάχος 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 9.7.β, 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 7.42, “PCair.Zen.” 60.8 (3rd c.BC)]]; ὅσον τάχος [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Electra” 1373, etc.]]; ᾗ (Doric dialect ᾇ) τάχος [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “O.” 6.23, 3rd c.BC: Theocritus Poeta Bucolicus 14.68: also ὡς τάχεος εἶχε ἕκαστος 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 8.107, compare 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 2.90; ὡς εἶχον τάχους [prev. author] 7.2; πῶς πρὸς ἄλληλα τάχους ἔχει 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Gorgias” 451c.]]

Abbott-Smith / STEPBible (TBESG)
ταχύ
(neut. of ταχύς),
adv., [in LXX chiefly for מָהַר pi. ;]
quickly, speedily, forthwith: Mat.5:25 28:7-8, Mrk.9:39, Luk.15:22, Jhn.11:29, Rev.2:16 3:11 11:14 22:7, 12 22:2 o. Compar., τάχειον (T, Rec. τάχιον), = cl. θᾶσσον, θᾶττον (Att..), (see Bl., § 44, 3): Jhn.13:27 20:4, 1Ti.3:14 (T, Rec.), Heb.13:19, 23 Superl., τάχιστα: ὡς τ., as quickly as possible (BL, § 11, 3), Act.17:15.†
(AS)

LSJ / STEPBible (TFLSJ)
Included with:  τᾰχύς [ῠ], εῖα, ύ:

__I
of motion, swift, fleet, opposed to βραδύς,

__I.1
of persons and animals, either absolutely, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 18.69, etc.]]; or more fully, πόδας ταχύς [Refs [13.249, 482, 17.709, etc.]]; ταχὺς ἔσκε θέειν [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 17.308]]; θείειν τ. [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 16.186, 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 3.112]]; κύνες, ἔλαφος, πτώξ, ἵππος, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 3.26, 8.248, 17.676, 23.347, etc.; οἰωνόν, ταχὺν ἄγγελον 24.292, compare 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 15.526]]; τ. βαδιστής a quick walker, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Medea” 1182]]; σφοδροὶ καὶ τ. [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 2.1.31.]]

__I.2
of things, τ. πόδες [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 6.514, compare 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 13.261, etc.]]; τ. ἰός, ὀϊστοί, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 4.94, 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 22.3, etc.; πτερά 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Aves” 1453; -ύτατα ἅρματα 5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “O.” 1.77]]; νῆες, τριήρεις, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 8.23, 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 6.43, etc.; [ἴχνος] τὸ τοῦ ποδὸς μὲν βραδύ, τὸ τοῦ δὲ νοῦ ταχύ 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Ion” 742.]]

__II
of thought and purpose, quick, hasty, φρονεῖν γὰρ οἱ ταχεῖς οὐκ ἀσφαλεῖς [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Tyrannus” 617: with]]infinitive, βλάπτειν τ. [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Ranae” 1428; τ. βουλεῦσαί τι ἀνήκεστον 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 1.132, compare 118, 2nd c.AD: Lucianus Sophista “Dem.Enc.” 12; also τ. πρὸς ὀργήν 1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus “Cat.Mi.” 1]]; τὸ ταχύ speed, haste, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Phoenissae” 452, 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “de Equitandi ratione” 7.18, etc.]]

__II.2
of actions, events, etc., rapid, sudden, πήδημα [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Ajax” 833]]; ᾅδης, μόρος, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Hippolytus” 1047, 2nd c.BC: Moschus Bucolicus 3.26; πόλεμος 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 4.55, 6.45; φυγή [prev. author] 4.44; μεταβολή 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 553d]]; short, τ. ἐλπίδες fleeting hopes, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “P.” 1.83; ἐπαυρέσεις 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 2.53; ἀτραπός 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Ranae” 127; ταχεῖ σὺν χρόνῳ 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Coloneus” 1602]]; τ. διήγησις short, rapid, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Rhetorica” 1416b30.]]

__B
adverb,

__B.1
regular τᾰχέως, quickly, opposed to βραδέως, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 23.365, 8th-7th c.BC: Hesiodus Epicus “Theogonia” 103, etc.]]:—rarely in sense perhaps [Refs 2nd c.BC+ [compare (τάχα 11), 2nd c.BC: Polybius Historicus 16.25.8.]]

__B.2
the  adverb is also expressed by periphrastic, διὰ ταχέων in haste, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 1.80, 3.13, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Apologia” 32d, 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 1.5.9; ἐκ ταχείας 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Trachiniae” 395; compare τάχος 11.]]

__B.3
neuter ταχύ as adverb, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “P.” 10.51, “N.” 1.51, 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Philoctetes” 349, 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Hercules Furens” 885 (Lyric poetry), 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Equites” 109, 2nd c.AD: Galenus Medicus 16.665, etc.]]; ἤδη ἤδη τ. τ. [Refs 3rd c.AD+ [“Sammelb.” 4321.21, “BGU” 956.3 (both 3rd c.AD)]]; ἄρτι ἄρτι τ. τ. [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [“Arch.Papyrus” 5.393 (2nd c.AD)]]; also τάχα (which see).

__B.4
the adjective ταχύς is frequently construed with Verbs, where we should use the adverb, ταχέες δ᾽ ἱππῆες ἄγερθεν [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 23.287; ταχεῖά γ᾽ ἦλθε χρησμῶν πρᾶξις 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Persae” 739; ὁρμάσθω ταχύς 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Philoctetes” 526]]; δεῦρ᾽ ἀφίξεται τ. [Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. author] “OC” 307; τ. χάρις διαρρεῖ [prev. author] “Aj.” 1266, compare 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 2.75, 5.66.]]

__C
Degrees of Comparison:

__C.I
comparative:

__C.I.1
the form τᾰχύτερος, α, ον, is used by [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus, ἐποίησα ταχύτερα ἢ σοφώτερα 3.65, compare 7.194]]; also in [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “de Mundo” 394b3, 2nd c.AD: Arrianus Historicus “Indica” 9.6, 2nd c.AD: Aretaeus Medicus “περὶ αἰτιῶν καὶ σημείων χρονίων παθῶν” 1.16]], but not in good Attic dialect; ταχύτερον as adverb, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 4.127, 9.101, 5th c.BC: Hippocrates Medicus “προγνωστικόν” 17.]]

__C.I.2
the more usual form is θάσσων, neuter θᾶσσον, genitive ονος, Attic dialect θάττων, neuter θᾶττον, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 15.570, 13.819 (elsewhere only _neuter_ in 8th c.BC: Homerus Epicus)]], etc.:—neuter as adverb, frequently in [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Homerus Epicus, 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 2.307, +others]]; θᾶσσον ἂν.. κλύοιμι sooner, i.e. rather, would I hear, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Philoctetes” 631]]; θᾶσσον also often stands for the Positive, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 2.440, 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 15.201, 16.130, 5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “P.” 4.181, 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Nubes” 506, “V.” 187, “Ra.” 94]]; οὐ θᾶσσον οἴσει; i.e. make haste and bring, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Trachiniae” 1183, compare “OT” 430]]; θᾶττον νοήματος quicker than thought, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Memorabilia” 4.3.13, compare 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Vespae” 824, etc.]]; with a conjunction, ὅτι θᾶσσον, like{ὅτι τάχιστα}, [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [3rd c.BC: Theocritus Poeta Bucolicus 24.48]]; ἐπειδὴ θᾶττον συνεσκότασεν as soon as.. , [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 54.5; ἐπειδὰν θ. συνιῇ τις 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Protagoras” 325c; ὅταν θ. φθέγγηται ὁ κόκκυξ 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Historia Animalium” 563b17, compare 611a5]]; ἐὰν or ἢν θ. as soon as.. , [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 3.3.20, “An.” 6.5.20, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus Alcaeus1.105a]]; ἂν θ. [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-3rd c.BC: Menander Comicus “Περικειρομένη” 174]]; εἰ θ. [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Epistulae” 324b]]; ὡς θ. [Refs 2nd c.BC+ [2nd c.BC: Polybius Historicus 1.66.1, 3.82.1]]; θ. rarely = sooner than, before, ἐξήλαυνον μεσημβρίας οὐ πολλῷ τινι θ. [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd c.AD: Aristides Rhetor “Orationes” 51 (27). 13 (compare τάχιον below 3).]]

__C.I.3
the form ταχίων [ῑ], neuter ιον, is frequently in late Prose, as [LXX+5th c.BC+ [LXX.Wis.13.9, LXX.1Mac.2.40, 3rd-2nd c.BC: Philo Mechanicus “(Belopoeica) Excerpte aus Philons Mechanik - Ath. Berl. Akad.” 69.14, 17, 73.23, 1st c.BC: Geminus Astronomicus 1.20, 1st c.BC: Dionysius Halicarnassensis 6.42, 1st c.BC: Diodorus Siculus Historicus 20.6, 1st c.AD: Josephus Historicus (see. below), 1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus 2.240d, NT.John.20.4, 4th c.AD: Alciphro Epistolographus 3.4; also in 5th c.BC: Hippocrates Medicus “γυναικεῖα” 1.1, 4th-3rd c.BC: Menander Comicus 402.16]]; but condemned by [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd c.AD: Phrynichus Atticista 58, 2nd c.AD: Herodianus Grammaticus “Philet.” p.436 P.]]; τὴν ταχίονα τῆς τροφῆς παράθεσιν earlier, sooner, [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd c.AD: Galenus Medicus 19.206:]] — adverb τάχιον earlier, πλέεται.. περὶ τὸν Σεπτέμβριον μῆνα.., οὐδὲν δὲ κωλύει κἂν τ. [Refs [“Periplus Maris Rubri [1st c.AD]” 24]]; τ. τῆς ὑποσχέσεως sooner than they had promised, [Refs [“Rev.Ét.Gr.” 6.159 (from Iasus)]]; τ. τοῦ παραγγέλματος [Refs 1st c.AD+ [1st c.AD: Josephus Historicus “Bellum Judaicum” 4.4.2; εἰς μακρὸν αὐτῶν γῆρας καὶ βίου μῆκος ὅμοιον τοῖς τ. ἐπερχομένων [prev. author] “AJ” 1.3.7; ἀποπαύεται οὔτε τ. ἐτῶν τεσσαράκοντα οὔτε βράδιον ἐτῶν πεντήκοντα 2nd c.AD: Soranus Medicus 1.20, compare 48, +others]]; formerly, ἐπεσκεύασαν τὸ παρόχιον,.. τ. γενόμενον γυμνάσιον [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [“IGRom.” 3.639 (Lycia, 2nd c.AD), compare 4.1517 (from Sardis), 1632.14 (from Philadelphia), 1665.5 (from Tira), Keil-Premerstein “Dritter Bericht“ p.79  (3rd c.AD), “Hermes” 63.229 (from Callatis)]]; compare above 2 near the end

__C.II
superlative:

__C.II.1
the form ταχύτατος is rare, ταχύτατα ἅρματα [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “O.” 1.77]]; ταχύτατα as adverb, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Historia Graeca (Hellenica)” 5.1.27 codices, 4th c.BC: Antiphanes Comicus 87 codices]]; but both passages have been corrected.

__C.II.2
the usual form is τάχιστος, η, ον, used by [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Homerus Epicus only in _neuter_ _plural_ τάχιστα]] as adverb, most quickly, most speedily, ὅττι τάχιστα as soon as may be, as soon as possible, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 4.193, 9.659, +others; ὅτι τάχιστα 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Tyrannus” 1341 (Lyric poetry), 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 3.31, etc.]]; so ὅσον τ. [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Choephori” 772, 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Tyrannus” 1436, etc.]]; ᾳ (probably) τ. [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “O.” 13.79]]; ὅπως τ. [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Agamemnon” 605, 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Tyrannus” 1410, 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Vespae” 167]]; ὡς τ. [Refs 5th c.BC+ [“IG” 12.76.23, 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.210, 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 4.15, 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Rhesus” 147, 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 1.3.14]]: these are elliptically phrases, as may be seen from the following examples, ὡς δυνατόν ἐστι τάχιστα [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Leges” 710b, 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 5.4.3]]; ᾗ δυνατὸν τ. [Refs [[prev. author] “HG” 6.3.6]]; ὡς or ᾗ ἠδύνατο τ. [Refs [[prev. author] “Cyr.” 3.2.14, “An.” 1.2.4]]; ὡς δύναιτο τ. [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.79]]; ὡς or ᾗ ἂν δύνωμαι τ. [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Historia Graeca (Hellenica)” 4.1.38, “Cyr.” 7.1.9, compare “IG” 12.106.18.]]

__C.II.2.b
τάχιστα after Particles of Time, as soon as, ἐπεὶ (Ionic dialect ἐπεί τε) τάχιστα [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Prometheus Vinctus” 201, 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.27, 75, 7.163, 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 7.2.6, “PCair.Zen.” 34.12 (3rd c.BC)]]; ἐπειδὴ τ. [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Protagoras” 310d, 4th c.BC: Isaeus Orator 9.3, 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 27.16, etc.]]; ἐπεὰν τ. [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 4.134, 7.129, 8.144]]; ἐπὰν τ. [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 4.6.9]]; ἐπειδὰν τ. [Refs [[prev. author] “Cyr.” 1.3.14, “An.” 3.1.9]]; ὅταν τ. [Refs [[prev. author] “Cyr.” 4.5.33: also ὡς τ]]. separated by one or more words, ὡς ἡμέρη τ. ἐγεγόνεε [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.11, compare 19, 47, 65, +others, 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 1.3.2, “Mem.” 1.2.16, +others; ὡς δὲ τ. ἐξῆλθε.. κόρον ἔτεκε “IG” 42(1).121.4 (Epid., 4th c.BC)]]; ὡς γὰρ τ. εἰσῆλθον [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-3rd c.BC: Menander Comicus “Περικειρομένη” 287; ὡς ἂν τ. λάβῃς τὴν ἐπιστολήν “PCair.Zen.” 241.1 (3rd c.BC); but ὡς τ. γὰρ ἀπεδήμησας [prev. work] 472.7 (3rd c.BC)]]; ὅπως τ. [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Prometheus Vinctus” 230:]] —the same notion is sometimes expressed by the participle, ἀπαλλαγεὶς τάχιστα, ={ὡς ἀπηλλάγη τ}., [Refs 1st c.AD+ [1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus “Demosthenes” 8, compare 25.]]

__C.II.3
frequently also in Prose, τὴν ταχίστην (in full, τὴν τ. ὁδόν [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 1.2.20, 2nd c.AD: Lucianus Sophista “Rh.Pr.” 4)]] as adverb, by the quickest way, i.e. most quickly, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.24, 73, 81, 86, 4th c.BC: Hyperides Orator “pro Euxenippo” 7, 4th-3rd c.BC: Menander Comicus “Περικειρομένη” 75, 2nd c.BC: Polybius Historicus 1.33.4, etc. (Cf. Lith. (dialogue)]] deñgti, Lett. diêgt, both = 'run quickly', Polish dążyć 'hurry'.)

__I.1
of persons and animals, either absolutely, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 18.69, etc.]]; or more fully, πόδας ταχύς [Refs [13.249, 482, 17.709, etc.]]; ταχὺς ἔσκε θέειν [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 17.308]]; θείειν τ. [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 16.186, 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 3.112]]; κύνες, ἔλαφος, πτώξ, ἵππος, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 3.26, 8.248, 17.676, 23.347, etc.; οἰωνόν, ταχὺν ἄγγελον 24.292, compare 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 15.526]]; τ. βαδιστής a quick walker, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Medea” 1182]]; σφοδροὶ καὶ τ. [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 2.1.31.]]

__I.2
of things, τ. πόδες [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 6.514, compare 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 13.261, etc.]]; τ. ἰός, ὀϊστοί, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 4.94, 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 22.3, etc.; πτερά 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Aves” 1453; -ύτατα ἅρματα 5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “O.” 1.77]]; νῆες, τριήρεις, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 8.23, 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 6.43, etc.; [ἴχνος] τὸ τοῦ ποδὸς μὲν βραδύ, τὸ τοῦ δὲ νοῦ ταχύ 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Ion” 742.]]

__II
of thought and purpose, quick, hasty, φρονεῖν γὰρ οἱ ταχεῖς οὐκ ἀσφαλεῖς [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Tyrannus” 617: with]]infinitive, βλάπτειν τ. [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Ranae” 1428; τ. βουλεῦσαί τι ἀνήκεστον 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 1.132, compare 118, 2nd c.AD: Lucianus Sophista “Dem.Enc.” 12; also τ. πρὸς ὀργήν 1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus “Cat.Mi.” 1]]; τὸ ταχύ speed, haste, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Phoenissae” 452, 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “de Equitandi ratione” 7.18, etc.]]

__II.2
of actions, events, etc., rapid, sudden, πήδημα [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Ajax” 833]]; ᾅδης, μόρος, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Hippolytus” 1047, 2nd c.BC: Moschus Bucolicus 3.26; πόλεμος 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 4.55, 6.45; φυγή [prev. author] 4.44; μεταβολή 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 553d]]; short, τ. ἐλπίδες fleeting hopes, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “P.” 1.83; ἐπαυρέσεις 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 2.53; ἀτραπός 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Ranae” 127; ταχεῖ σὺν χρόνῳ 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Coloneus” 1602]]; τ. διήγησις short, rapid, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Rhetorica” 1416b30.]]

__B
adverb,

__B.1
regular τᾰχέως, quickly, opposed to βραδέως, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 23.365, 8th-7th c.BC: Hesiodus Epicus “Theogonia” 103, etc.]]:—rarely in sense perhaps [Refs 2nd c.BC+ [compare (τάχα 11), 2nd c.BC: Polybius Historicus 16.25.8.]]

__B.2
the  adverb is also expressed by periphrastic, διὰ ταχέων in haste, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 1.80, 3.13, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Apologia” 32d, 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 1.5.9; ἐκ ταχείας 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Trachiniae” 395; compare τάχος 11.]]

__B.3
neuter ταχύ as adverb, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “P.” 10.51, “N.” 1.51, 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Philoctetes” 349, 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Hercules Furens” 885 (Lyric poetry), 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Equites” 109, 2nd c.AD: Galenus Medicus 16.665, etc.]]; ἤδη ἤδη τ. τ. [Refs 3rd c.AD+ [“Sammelb.” 4321.21, “BGU” 956.3 (both 3rd c.AD)]]; ἄρτι ἄρτι τ. τ. [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [“Arch.Papyrus” 5.393 (2nd c.AD)]]; also τάχα (which see).

__B.4
the adjective ταχύς is frequently construed with Verbs, where we should use the adverb, ταχέες δ᾽ ἱππῆες ἄγερθεν [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 23.287; ταχεῖά γ᾽ ἦλθε χρησμῶν πρᾶξις 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Persae” 739; ὁρμάσθω ταχύς 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Philoctetes” 526]]; δεῦρ᾽ ἀφίξεται τ. [Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. author] “OC” 307; τ. χάρις διαρρεῖ [prev. author] “Aj.” 1266, compare 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 2.75, 5.66.]]

__C
Degrees of Comparison:

__C.I
comparative:

__C.I.1
the form τᾰχύτερος, α, ον, is used by [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus, ἐποίησα ταχύτερα ἢ σοφώτερα 3.65, compare 7.194]]; also in [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “de Mundo” 394b3, 2nd c.AD: Arrianus Historicus “Indica” 9.6, 2nd c.AD: Aretaeus Medicus “περὶ αἰτιῶν καὶ σημείων χρονίων παθῶν” 1.16]], but not in good Attic dialect; ταχύτερον as adverb, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 4.127, 9.101, 5th c.BC: Hippocrates Medicus “προγνωστικόν” 17.]]

__C.I.2
the more usual form is θάσσων, neuter θᾶσσον, genitive ονος, Attic dialect θάττων, neuter θᾶττον, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 15.570, 13.819 (elsewhere only _neuter_ in 8th c.BC: Homerus Epicus)]], etc.:—neuter as adverb, frequently in [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Homerus Epicus, 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 2.307, +others]]; θᾶσσον ἂν.. κλύοιμι sooner, i.e. rather, would I hear, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Philoctetes” 631]]; θᾶσσον also often stands for the Positive, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 2.440, 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 15.201, 16.130, 5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “P.” 4.181, 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Nubes” 506, “V.” 187, “Ra.” 94]]; οὐ θᾶσσον οἴσει; i.e. make haste and bring, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Trachiniae” 1183, compare “OT” 430]]; θᾶττον νοήματος quicker than thought, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Memorabilia” 4.3.13, compare 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Vespae” 824, etc.]]; with a conjunction, ὅτι θᾶσσον, like{ὅτι τάχιστα}, [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [3rd c.BC: Theocritus Poeta Bucolicus 24.48]]; ἐπειδὴ θᾶττον συνεσκότασεν as soon as.. , [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 54.5; ἐπειδὰν θ. συνιῇ τις 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Protagoras” 325c; ὅταν θ. φθέγγηται ὁ κόκκυξ 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Historia Animalium” 563b17, compare 611a5]]; ἐὰν or ἢν θ. as soon as.. , [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 3.3.20, “An.” 6.5.20, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus Alcaeus1.105a]]; ἂν θ. [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-3rd c.BC: Menander Comicus “Περικειρομένη” 174]]; εἰ θ. [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Epistulae” 324b]]; ὡς θ. [Refs 2nd c.BC+ [2nd c.BC: Polybius Historicus 1.66.1, 3.82.1]]; θ. rarely = sooner than, before, ἐξήλαυνον μεσημβρίας οὐ πολλῷ τινι θ. [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd c.AD: Aristides Rhetor “Orationes” 51 (27). 13 (compare τάχιον below 3).]]

__C.I.3
the form ταχίων [ῑ], neuter ιον, is frequently in late Prose, as [LXX+5th c.BC+ [LXX.Wis.13.9, LXX.1Mac.2.40, 3rd-2nd c.BC: Philo Mechanicus “(Belopoeica) Excerpte aus Philons Mechanik - Ath. Berl. Akad.” 69.14, 17, 73.23, 1st c.BC: Geminus Astronomicus 1.20, 1st c.BC: Dionysius Halicarnassensis 6.42, 1st c.BC: Diodorus Siculus Historicus 20.6, 1st c.AD: Josephus Historicus (see. below), 1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus 2.240d, NT.John.20.4, 4th c.AD: Alciphro Epistolographus 3.4; also in 5th c.BC: Hippocrates Medicus “γυναικεῖα” 1.1, 4th-3rd c.BC: Menander Comicus 402.16]]; but condemned by [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd c.AD: Phrynichus Atticista 58, 2nd c.AD: Herodianus Grammaticus “Philet.” p.436 P.]]; τὴν ταχίονα τῆς τροφῆς παράθεσιν earlier, sooner, [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd c.AD: Galenus Medicus 19.206:]] — adverb τάχιον earlier, πλέεται.. περὶ τὸν Σεπτέμβριον μῆνα.., οὐδὲν δὲ κωλύει κἂν τ. [Refs [“Periplus Maris Rubri [1st c.AD]” 24]]; τ. τῆς ὑποσχέσεως sooner than they had promised, [Refs [“Rev.Ét.Gr.” 6.159 (from Iasus)]]; τ. τοῦ παραγγέλματος [Refs 1st c.AD+ [1st c.AD: Josephus Historicus “Bellum Judaicum” 4.4.2; εἰς μακρὸν αὐτῶν γῆρας καὶ βίου μῆκος ὅμοιον τοῖς τ. ἐπερχομένων [prev. author] “AJ” 1.3.7; ἀποπαύεται οὔτε τ. ἐτῶν τεσσαράκοντα οὔτε βράδιον ἐτῶν πεντήκοντα 2nd c.AD: Soranus Medicus 1.20, compare 48, +others]]; formerly, ἐπεσκεύασαν τὸ παρόχιον,.. τ. γενόμενον γυμνάσιον [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [“IGRom.” 3.639 (Lycia, 2nd c.AD), compare 4.1517 (from Sardis), 1632.14 (from Philadelphia), 1665.5 (from Tira), Keil-Premerstein “Dritter Bericht“ p.79  (3rd c.AD), “Hermes” 63.229 (from Callatis)]]; compare above 2 near the end

__C.II
superlative:

__C.II.1
the form ταχύτατος is rare, ταχύτατα ἅρματα [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “O.” 1.77]]; ταχύτατα as adverb, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Historia Graeca (Hellenica)” 5.1.27 codices, 4th c.BC: Antiphanes Comicus 87 codices]]; but both passages have been corrected.

__C.II.2
the usual form is τάχιστος, η, ον, used by [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Homerus Epicus only in _neuter_ _plural_ τάχιστα]] as adverb, most quickly, most speedily, ὅττι τάχιστα as soon as may be, as soon as possible, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 4.193, 9.659, +others; ὅτι τάχιστα 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Tyrannus” 1341 (Lyric poetry), 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 3.31, etc.]]; so ὅσον τ. [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Choephori” 772, 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Tyrannus” 1436, etc.]]; ᾳ (probably) τ. [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “O.” 13.79]]; ὅπως τ. [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Agamemnon” 605, 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Tyrannus” 1410, 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Vespae” 167]]; ὡς τ. [Refs 5th c.BC+ [“IG” 12.76.23, 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.210, 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 4.15, 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Rhesus” 147, 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 1.3.14]]: these are elliptically phrases, as may be seen from the following examples, ὡς δυνατόν ἐστι τάχιστα [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Leges” 710b, 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 5.4.3]]; ᾗ δυνατὸν τ. [Refs [[prev. author] “HG” 6.3.6]]; ὡς or ᾗ ἠδύνατο τ. [Refs [[prev. author] “Cyr.” 3.2.14, “An.” 1.2.4]]; ὡς δύναιτο τ. [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.79]]; ὡς or ᾗ ἂν δύνωμαι τ. [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Historia Graeca (Hellenica)” 4.1.38, “Cyr.” 7.1.9, compare “IG” 12.106.18.]]

__C.II.2.b
τάχιστα after Particles of Time, as soon as, ἐπεὶ (Ionic dialect ἐπεί τε) τάχιστα [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Prometheus Vinctus” 201, 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.27, 75, 7.163, 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 7.2.6, “PCair.Zen.” 34.12 (3rd c.BC)]]; ἐπειδὴ τ. [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Protagoras” 310d, 4th c.BC: Isaeus Orator 9.3, 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 27.16, etc.]]; ἐπεὰν τ. [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 4.134, 7.129, 8.144]]; ἐπὰν τ. [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 4.6.9]]; ἐπειδὰν τ. [Refs [[prev. author] “Cyr.” 1.3.14, “An.” 3.1.9]]; ὅταν τ. [Refs [[prev. author] “Cyr.” 4.5.33: also ὡς τ]]. separated by one or more words, ὡς ἡμέρη τ. ἐγεγόνεε [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.11, compare 19, 47, 65, +others, 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 1.3.2, “Mem.” 1.2.16, +others; ὡς δὲ τ. ἐξῆλθε.. κόρον ἔτεκε “IG” 42(1).121.4 (Epid., 4th c.BC)]]; ὡς γὰρ τ. εἰσῆλθον [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-3rd c.BC: Menander Comicus “Περικειρομένη” 287; ὡς ἂν τ. λάβῃς τὴν ἐπιστολήν “PCair.Zen.” 241.1 (3rd c.BC); but ὡς τ. γὰρ ἀπεδήμησας [prev. work] 472.7 (3rd c.BC)]]; ὅπως τ. [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Prometheus Vinctus” 230:]] —the same notion is sometimes expressed by the participle, ἀπαλλαγεὶς τάχιστα, ={ὡς ἀπηλλάγη τ}., [Refs 1st c.AD+ [1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus “Demosthenes” 8, compare 25.]]

__C.II.3
frequently also in Prose, τὴν ταχίστην (in full, τὴν τ. ὁδόν [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 1.2.20, 2nd c.AD: Lucianus Sophista “Rh.Pr.” 4)]] as adverb, by the quickest way, i.e. most quickly, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.24, 73, 81, 86, 4th c.BC: Hyperides Orator “pro Euxenippo” 7, 4th-3rd c.BC: Menander Comicus “Περικειρομένη” 75, 2nd c.BC: Polybius Historicus 1.33.4, etc. (Cf. Lith. (dialogue)]] deñgti, Lett. diêgt, both = 'run quickly', Polish dążyć 'hurry'.)

deep_entry:
Abbott-Smith / STEPBible (TBESG)
τέ,
enclitic copulative particle (= Lat. -que as καί = and, ac, atque, not very frequently in NT, more than two-thirds of the occurrences being in Ac.
__1. τέ solitarium, and, denoting a closer affinity than καί between words and sentences which it connects (BL, §77, 8): Mat.28:12, Jhn.4:42, Act.2:33, 37 40 10:22 11:21, al.
__2. Denoting a closer connection than simple καί, τὲ . . . καί, τὲ καί, τὲ . . . τέ (Act.26:16 Rom.14:8), as well . . . as also, both . . . and: Luk.12:45, Act.1:1 15:9, 21:30, al.; τὲ . . . δέ, and . . . and, Act.19:2; τὲ γάρ . . . ὁμοίως δὲ καί, Rom.1:26, 27.
(AS)

---

LSJ / STEPBible (TFLSJ)
τε,
enclitic Particle, with two main uses (see. infr. A, B).

__A
as a Conjunction,

__A.I
τε.. τε, both.. and, joining single words, phrases, clauses, or sentences, the first τε merely pointing forward to the second, ἀνδρῶν τε θεῶν τε [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 1.544; ἀγαθῶν τε κακῶν τε 8th-7th c.BC: Hesiodus Epicus “Opera et Dies” 669; δίψῃ τε λιμῷ τε 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Persae” 491, compare 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Ajax” 34, 35, 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Acharnenses” 370, 375; τήν τε νῆσον τήν τε ἤπειρον 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 4.8, compare 5th c.BC: Antipho Orator 2.3.3, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 373b; λυσόμενός τε θύγατρα, φέρων τ᾽ ἀπερείσι᾽ ἄποινα 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 1.13; παῖδά τε σοὶ ἀγέμεν Φοίβῳ θ᾽ ἱερὴν ἑκατόμβην ῥέξαι [prev. work] 443]]; the elements joined by τε.. τε are usually short in [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Homerus Epicus]], longer in later Gr., e.g. ἐπειδὴ πρόξενοί τέ εἰσιν Ἀθηναίων καὶ εὐεργέται.., ἔν τε τῇ στήλῃ γέγραπται [Refs 5th c.BC+ [“IG” 12.103.7; ἥ τε γὰρ γῆ.. εὔυδρός ἐστι, ποταμοί τε δι᾽ αὐτῆς ῥέουσι 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 4.47]]; χρὴ.. τούς τε πρεσβυτέρους ὁμοιωθῆναι τοῖς πρὶν ἔργοις, τούς τε νεωτέρους.. μὴ αἰσχῦναι κτλ. [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 4.92, compare 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 474c, 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 1.4.25, 4th c.BC: Isaeus Orator 1.50]]; τά τε γὰρ ληφθέντα πάντ᾽ ἂν σῴζοιτο οἵ τ᾽ ἀδικήσαντες κατ᾽ ἀξίαν λάβοιεν τὰ ἐπιτίμια Aen.[Refs 3rd c.BC+ [Tact. 16.8, compare “Geoponica” 2.49.1, 12.3.2-3; τούτου γὰρ γενομένου.. τά τε ἐχφόρια Χρυσέρμῳ δυνήσομαι ἀποδοῦναι, ἐγώ τε ἔσομαι παρὰ σοῦ φιλανθρωπίας τετευχώς “PEnteux.” 60.11 (3rd c.BC)]]; κλείειν τε τὰ βλέφαρα δεομένων ἐλπιζόντων τε κοιμηθήσεσθαι [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd c.AD: Galenus Medicus 16.494]], compare 495,501; this use is common at all times in οὔτε.. οὔτε, μήτε.. μήτε, εἴτε.. εἴτε (which see); τε may be used three or more times, ἔν τ᾽ ἄρα οἱ φῦ χειρί, ἔπος τ᾽ ἔφατ᾽ ἔκ τ᾽ ὀνόμαζεν [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 15.530, compare 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 1.177, 2.58, 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Prometheus Vinctus” 89s q., 5th c.BC: Bacchylides Lyricus 17.19s q., 5th c.BC: Lysias Orator 19.17, 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 3.3.36:]] —ἑνδεκάτη τε δυωδεκάτη τε probably means the eleventh or twelfth, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 2.374, 4.588:]] —sometimes τε.. τε couples alternatives, ἀπόρως εἶχε δοῦναί τε μὴ δοῦναί τε [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Iphigenia Aulidensis” 56, compare “Heracl.” 153, “El.” 391]]; hence we find τε.. ἢ.., [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Theaetetus” 143c, “Ion” 535d]]; on ἢ (or ἦ).. τε in [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 2.289 and 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Eumenides” 524 (Lyric poetry) see at {ἦ} I.3.]]

__A.I.2
the first clause may be negative, the second affirmative, as ἐκκλησίαν τε οὐκ ἐποίει.., τήν τε πόλιν ἐφύλασσε [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 2.22]]; but οὔτε.. τε is more frequently, as οὔτε ποσίν εἰμι ταχύς.., γιγνώσκω τε [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 2.3.6 (see. οὔτε 11.4)]]; we also find οὐ.. τε.., as οὐχ ἡσύχαζον.., παρεκάλουν τε τοὺς ξυμμάχους [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 1.67]]; and μὴ.. τε.., as ἵνα μή τι διαφύγῃ ἡμᾶς, εἴ τέ τι βούλει κτλ. [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Phaedo” 95e.]]

__A.I.3
τε (both) sometimes corresponds to a following δέ (and), or τε (and) to a preceding μέν, e.g.

__A.I.3.a
τε.. δὲ.., as κόμισαί τέ με, δὸς δέ μοι ἵππους [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 5.359, compare 7.418, 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Coloneus” 367, “Tr.” 285, 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Phoenissae” 1625; ἐσθὰς ἀμφότερόν νιν ἔχεν, ἅ τε.. ἐπιχώριος.., ἀμφὶ δὲ παρδαλέᾳ στέγετο 5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “P.” 4.80; διήκουέ τε.., ἔπειτα δὲ καὶ ἐπῄνεσε 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 4.4.3]]; so with ἅμα δὲ καὶ.., ὡσαύτως δὲ καὶ.., [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 1.25, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Symposium” 186e:—so τε.., ἀτὰρ οὖν καὶ.., [prev. author] “Hp.Ma.” 295e.]]

__A.I.3.b
μὲν.. τε.., ἄνδρα μὲν.., τρεῖς τε κασιγνήτους [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 19.291 - 3, compare 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 22.475 - 6, 5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “O.” 6.88, 7.88, 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Septem contra Thebas” 924, “Ch.” 585 (Lyric poetry), 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Antigone” 963 (Lyric poetry), 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Heraclidae” 337 codices, “Cyc.” 41 (Lyric poetry), 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Nubes” 563 (Lyric poetry), 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Phaedrus” 266c, “Lg.” 927b: see.{μέν} 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus 11.6c.]]

__A.I.4
a single τε (and) joins a word, phrase, or (especially later) clause or sentence to what precedes, τελευτὴν κεφαλήν τε [Refs 8th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Timaeus” 69a; θνητὰ ἀθάνατά τε [prev. work]c; Ζεῦ ἄλλοι τε θεοί 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 6.476; κύνεσσιν οἰωνοῖσί τε πᾶσι 1.5; ῥίγησέν τ᾽ ἂρ ἔπειτα ἄναξ ἀνδρῶν Ἀγαμέμνων variant for{δ᾽ ἂρ} in 11.254]]; ἕν τε οὐδὲν κατέστη ἴαμα.., σῶμά τε αὔταρκες ὂν οὐδὲν διεφάνη.., [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 2.51; τά τε ἱερὰ.. νεκρῶν πλέα ἦν.. [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [3rd c.BC: Archimedes Geometra “περὶ ἑλίκων” 11 “Def.” 7; πρός τε τούτοις φησὶν.. “PEnteux.” 63.18 (3rd c.BC)]]; χωρίς τε τούτων [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [2nd c.BC: Polybius Historicus 2.56.13, 61.1, 3.17.7; ταῦτά τ᾽ ἐγίνετο.. __A.II
τε.. καὶ.., or τε καὶ.., both.. and.., where τε points forward to καί, and usually need not be translated, e.g. Ἀτρείδης τε ἄναξ ἀνδρῶν καὶ δῖος Ἀχιλλεύς [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 1.7; εἰ δὴ ὁμοῦ πόλεμός τε δαμᾷ καὶ λοιμὸς Ἀχαιούς [prev. work] 61]]; δειλός τε καὶ οὐτιδανὸς καλεοίμην[Refs [[prev. work] 293; ζωόν τε καὶ ἀρτεμέα 7.308, compare 327, 338, +others]]; τῆς τε γῆς ἐούσης ἐπιτηδέης καὶ τῶν ποταμῶν ἐόντων σφι συμμάχων [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 4.47; βούλεταί τε καὶ ἐπίσταται 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 2.35; ὁ φύς τε καὶ τραφείς 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 396c; βάσιν τε γὰρ πάλιν τὴν αὐτὴν ἔχουσι τὴν ΖΒ καὶ.. 3rd c.BC: Euclides Geometra 1.47]]; sometimes the elements joined by τε.. καὶ.. are joined in order to be compared or contrasted rather than simply joined, κάκιστος νῦν τε καὶ πάλαι δοκεῖ [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Antigone” 181; μεσαμβρίη τέ ἐστι καὶ τὸ κάρτα γίνεται ψυχρόν 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 4.181; ἔτυχόν τε ὕσταται ἐξαναχθεῖσαι καί κως κατεῖδον [prev. author] 7.194]]; ἐπαύσατό τε ὁ ἄνεμος καὶ τὸ κῦμα ἔστρωτο[Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. work] 193; ταὐτὰ.. νῦν τε καὶ τότε 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Aves” 24; χωρὶς τό τ᾽ εἰπεῖν πολλὰ καὶ τὰ καίρια 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Coloneus” 808; ὅσον τό τ᾽ ἄρχειν καὶ τὸ δουλεύειν δίχα 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Prometheus Vinctus” 927]]; sometimes (like τε.. τε) even used of alternatives, διάνδιχα μερμήριξεν, ἵππους τε στρέψαι καὶ ἐναντίβιον μαχέσασθαι [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 8.168; ἐν δίκᾳ τε καὶ παρὰ δίκαν 5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “O.” 2.16; θεοῦ τε.. θέλοντος καὶ μὴ θέλοντος 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Septem contra Thebas” 427; πείσας τε.. καὶ μὴ τυχών 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 3.42:—on οἵ τε ἄλλοι καὶ.., e.g. τοῖς τε ἄλλοις ἅπασι καὶ Λακεδαιμονίοις 5th-6th c.BC: Isocrates Orator 12.249, and ἄλλως τε καὶ.., see.{ἄλλος} 11.6, ἄλλως 1.3.]]

__A.II.2
in this sense τ᾽ ἠδέ is only Epic dialect, σκῆπτρόν τ᾽ ἠδὲ θέμιστας [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 9.99, compare 1.400, +others]]; also τε.., ἰδέ, χαλκόν τε ἰδὲ λόφον [Refs [6.469, compare 8.162.]]

__A.II.3
καὶ.. τε, both.. and.. , is occasionally found, as καὶ μητέρα πατέρα τ᾽ [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Alcestis” 646.]]

__A.II.3.b
καὶ.. τε perhaps means and.. also in καὶ ναυτικῷ τε ἅμα [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 1.9; καὶ πρός τε τοὺς Ῥηγίνους [prev. author] 6.44; καὶ αὐτός τε [prev. author] 8.68; see below with 10.]]

__A.II.4
τε.. τε or τε.. καὶ.. sometimes join elements which are not syntactically parallel, especially a participle and a finite verb, ἰοῖσίν τε τιτυσκόμενοι λάεσσί τ᾽ ἔβαλλον (for βάλλοντες) [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 3.80; ἄλλα τε ἐπιφραζόμενος καὶ δὴ καὶ ἐπεπόμφεε 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.85; ἀλλῳ τε τρόπῳ πειράζοντες καὶ μηχανὴν προσήγαγον 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 4.100; τῆς τε ὥρας.. ταύτης οὔσης.., καὶ τὸ χωρίον.. χαλεπὸν ἦν [prev. author] 7.47, compare 4.85, 8.81, 95.]]

__A.II.5
the copulative τε[Refs [becomes rare in later Gr.; it is found about 340 times in LXX, mostly in the Pentateuch and 1- “4 Ma.”, only 3 times in “Ps.”; in the “NT”]] it is found about 150 times in [NT.Act., 20 times in NT.Heb., and very rarely in the other books.]

__B
In Epic dialect (more rarely in other dactylic verse, see below [Refs [11)]] τε stands in general or frequentative statements or in statements of what is well known; such statements are frequently made as justifications of a preceding particular statement or of a preceding exhortation to a particular person or persons; the sense of τε thus approaches that of τοι (compare τοι and τε in [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 2.276 - 7, and compare 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 13.115 with 15.203)]]; although associated with numerous particles and other words of particular types (see. below) its meaning remains independent of these and applies to the whole sentence in which it stands: αἶψά τε φυλόπιδος πέλεται κόρος ἀνθρώποισιν [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 19.221; __B.2
in exhortations addressed to an individual, a subsidiary sentence or relative clause in which he is reminded of his special or characteristic sphere of activity is marked by τε, e.g. Ἑρμεία, σοὶ γάρ τε μάλιστά γε φίλτατόν ἐστιν ἀνδρὶ ἑταιρίσσαι καί τ᾽ ἔκλυες ᾧ κ᾽ ἐθέλῃσθα, βάσκ᾽ ἴθι.. [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 24.334; Ἀτρεΐδη, σοὶ γάρ τε μάλιστά γε λαὸς Ἀχαιῶν πείσονται μύθοισι.., νῦν δ᾽ ἀπὸ πυρκαϊῆς σκέδασον.. 23.156; δεῦρο δὴ ὄρσο, γρηῢ.., ἥ τε γυναικῶν δμῳάων σκοπός ἐσσι.., ἔρχεο 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 22.395, compare 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 17.249.]]

__B.3
similarly in general and frequentative statements consisting of two clauses (one of which may be a relative clause, frequently containing the subjunctive or optative), in which the fulfilment of the condition stated in the subsidiary or subordinate clause is declared to be generally or always followed by the result stated in the principal clause, either or both clauses may contain τε:

__B.3.a
the principal clause alone contains τε, ὅς κε θεοῖς ἐπιπείθηται, μάλα τ᾽ ἔκλυον αὐτοῦ [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 1.218; ὃς δ᾽ ἂν ἀμύμων αὐτὸς ἔῃ καὶ ἀμύμονα εἰδῇ, τοῦ μέν τε κλέος εὐρὺ διὰ ξεῖνοι φορέουσι πάντας ἐπ᾽ ἀνθρώπους, πολλοί τέ μιν ἐσθλὸν ἔειπον 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 19.333; εἴ περ γὰρ θυμῷ γε μενοινάᾳ πολεμίζειν, ἀλλά τε λάθρῃ γυῖα βαρύνεται.., βλάβεται δέ τε γούνατ᾽ ἰόντι 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 19.165 - 6; ᾧ μέν κ᾽ ἀμμείξας δώῃ Ζεὺς τερπικέραυνος, ἄλλοτε μέν τε κακῷ ὅ γε κύρεται ἄλλοτε δ᾽ ἐσθλῷ 24.530.]]

__B.3.b
the subordinate clause alone contains τε, λάζετο δ᾽ ἔγχος.. τῷ δάμνησι στίχας ἀνδρῶν ἡρώων οἷσίν τε κοτέσσεται ὀβριμοπάτρη [Refs 8th c.BC+ [5.747; ῥεῖα δ᾽ ἀρίγνωτος γόνος ἀνέρος ᾧ τε Κρονίων ὄλβον ἐπικλώση 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 4.207; ἀντί νυ πολλῶν λαῶν ἐστιν ἀνὴρ ὅν τε Ζεὺς κῆρι φιλήσῃ 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 9.117, compare 7.298, 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 6.287, 7.74, 8.547, 18.276; with _optative_, ἀλλὰ πολὺ πρώτιστος.. ἕλεσκον ἀνδρῶν δυσμενέων ὅ τέ μοι εἴξειε πόδεσσι 14.221]]: it is probably that τε has been replaced by κε in the text of [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Homerus Epicus in 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 1.218, 9.510 (compare 508)]], and some other passages in which κε seems to be used, exceptionally, in general relative clauses.

__B.3.c
both clauses contain τε, ὃς μέν τ᾽ αἰδέσεται κούρας Διὸς ἆσσον ἰούσας, τὸν δὲ μέγ᾽ ὤνησαν καί τ᾽ ἔκλυον εὐχομένοιο [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 9.508 - 9; εἴ περ γάρ τε χόλον γε καὶ αὐτῆμαρ καταπέψῃ, ἀλλά τε καὶ μετόπισθεν ἔχει κότον 1.82 - 3.]]

__B.4
in the subordinate clause of a collective sentence, in which the principal clause states something to be true of all those (i.e. each individual) to whom the predicate of the subordinate clause applies, ὑπόσχωμαι.. κτήματα.. πάντα μάλ᾽ ὅσσα τ᾽ Ἀλέξανδρος.. ἠγάγετο Τροίηνδ᾽.. δωσέμεν [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 22.115; πάντων ὅσσα τε γαῖαν ἔπι πνείει τε καὶ ἕρπει 17.447, compare 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 18.131, 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 19.105; βάλλειν ἄγρια πάντα τά τε τρέφει οὔρεσιν ὕλη 5.52, compare 18.485.]]

__B.5
in relative clauses (and in parenthetic principal clauses) which indicate what is customary, ἐπεὶ οὐχ ἱερήϊον οὐδὲ βοείην ἀρνύσθην, ἅ τε ποσσὶν ἀέθλια γίγνεται ἀνδρῶν which are the usual prizes.., [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 22.160; ἔργ᾽ ἀνδρῶν τε θεῶν τε, τά τε κλείουσιν ἀοιδοί 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 1.338, compare 3.435, 4.85, 13.410, 14.226, 17.423, 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 5.332; κύματος ἐξαναδύς, τά τ᾽ ἐρεύγεται ἤπειρόνδε 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 5.438; μολπή τ᾽ ὀρχηστύς τε, τὰ γάρ τ᾽ ἀναθήματα δαιτός 1.152]]: similarly in clauses with οἷά τε (πολλά), κῆτος ἐπισσεύῃ μέγα δαίμων ἐξ ἁλός, οἷά τε πολλὰ τρέφει.. Ἀμφιτρίτη [Refs [5.422; οὐ γάρ σ᾽ οὐδέ.. δαήμονι φωτὶ ἐΐσκω ἄθλων, οἷά τε πολλὰ μετ᾽ ἀνθρώποισι πέλονται 8.160, compare 11.364, 14.63, 15.324, 379.]]

__B.6
in relative clauses indicating what is true of all persons or things denoted by the same word, οὐ γάρ τις νήσων ἱππήλατος οὐδ᾽ εὐλείμων αἵ θ᾽ ἁλὶ κεκλίαται no one of the islands which lie in the sea (as all islands do, i.e. no island at all), [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 4.608; ἡμίονον.. ἥ τ᾽ ἀλγίστη δαμάσασθαι 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 23.655; ἐσθλὸς ἐὼν γαμβρὸς ἢ πενθερός, οἵ τε μάλιστα κήδιστοι τελέθουσι 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 8.582; αἰετοῦ οἴματ᾽ ἔχων.. ὅς θ᾽ ἅμα κάρτιστός τε καὶ ὤκιστος πετεηνῶν 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 21.252, compare 24.294; οὐδέ μιν εἰσοιχνεῦσι κυνηγέται, οἵ τε καθ᾽ ὕλην ἄλγεα πάσχουσιν 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 9.120; δικασπόλοι, οἵ τε θέμιστας πρὸς Διὸς εἰρύαται 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 1.238, compare 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 5.67, 101, 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 1.279, 19.31, 24.415; οἶνός σε τρώει.., ὅς τε καὶ ἄλλους βλάπτει 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 21.293, compare 14.464; πάρφασις, ἥ τ᾽ ἔκλεψε νόον πύκα περ φρονεόντων 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 14.217; οἰκωφελίη, ἥ τε τρέφει ἀγλαὰ τέκνα 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 14.223.]]

__B.7
when the antecedent is a definite group of gods or men, the relative clause with τε indicates an essential characteristic of the antecedent, Ἐρινύες, αἵ θ᾽ ὑπὸ γαῖαν ἀνθρώπους τείνυνται [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 19.259; Σειρῆνας.., αἵ ῥά τε πάντας ἀνθρώπους θέλγουσιν 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 12.39; Φαίηκές μ᾽ ἄγαγον ναυσίκλυτοι, οἵ τε καὶ ἄλλους ἀνθρώπους πέμπουσιν 16.227, compare 20.187; νυμφάων αἵ τ᾽ ἄλσεα καλὰ νέμονται καὶ πηγὰς ποταμῶν 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 20.8; Λωτοφάγων, οἵ τ᾽ ἄνθινον εἶδαρ ἔδουσι 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 9.84: similarly when the antecedent is an individual person (including god)]] or thing, the relative clause with τε indicates one of his or its general or essential characteristics or aspects, οὐ μὰ Ζῆν᾽ ὅς τίς τε θεῶν ὕπατος καὶ ἄριστος [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 23.43, compare 2.669, 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 5.4; Ἑρμείαο ἕκητι διακτόρου, ὅς ῥά τε πάντων ἀνθρώπων ἔργοισι χάριν καὶ κῦδος ὀπάζει 15.319; Λάμπον καὶ Φαέθονθ᾽, οἵ τ᾽ Ἠῶ πῶλοι ἄγουσι 23.246; Τειρεσίαο μάντιος ἀλαοῦ, τοῦ τε φρένες ἔμπεδοί εἰσι 10.493; τεύχεα δύνεις ἀνδρὸς ἀριστῆος, τόν τε τρομέουσι καὶ ἄλλοι 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 17.203, compare 7.112]]; κεῖται ἀνὴρ ὅν τ᾽ (variant{ὃν}) ἶσον ἐτίομεν Ἕκτορι δίῳ, Αἰνείας [Refs [5.467]]; the relative clause sometimes indicates what is customary, οὐδέ σε λήθω τιμῆς ἧς τέ μ᾽ ἔοικε τετιμῆσθαι μετ᾽ Ἀχαιοῖς [Refs 8th c.BC+ [23.649; ἔνθα δ᾽ ἀνὴρ ἐνίαυε πελώριος, ὅς ῥά τε μῆλα οἶος ποιμαίνεσκε 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 9.187; τῶν πάντων οὐ τόσσον ὀδύρομαι.. ὡς ἑνός, ὅς τέ μοι ὕπνον ἀπεχθαίρει καὶ ἐδωδὴν μνωομένῳ 4.105; σῆς ἀλόχου.. ἥ τέ τοι αὔτως ἧσται ἐνὶ μεγάροισιν 13.336; καὶ κήρυκα Μέδοντα σαώσομεν, ὅς τέ μευ αἰεὶ.. κηδέσκετο 22.357, compare 346.]]

__B.8
τε is used in descriptions of particular places or things when attention is called to their peculiar or characteristic features, or their position, e.g. Λιβύην, ἵνα τ᾽ ἄρνες ἄφαρ κεραοὶ τελέθουσι [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 4.85; ἔνθα δέ τ᾽ ὄρνιθες τανυσίπτεροι εὐνάζοντο 5.65, compare 9.124, 13.99, 100, 107, 109, 244]]; ἓξ δέ τέ οἱ (i.e. Σκύλλῃ) δειραὶ περιμήκεες [Refs [12.90, compare 93, 99, 105]]; ἐν δέ τε Γοργείη κεφαλή (in Athena's αἰγίς) [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 5.741]]; χαλεπὸν δέ τ᾽ ὀρύσσειν ἀνδράσι γε θνητοῖσι (i.e. μῶλυ) [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 10.305; δοιαὶ γάρ τε πύλαι ἀμενηνῶν εἰσὶν ὀνείρων 19.562]]; sometimes τε draws attention to a well-known custom or permanent feature, ἀρξάμενοι τοῦ χώρου, ὅθεν τέ περ οἰνοχοεύει [Refs 8th c.BC+ [21.142; ἦ μένετε Τρῶας σχεδὸν ἐλθέμεν, ἔνθα τε νῆες εἰρύατ᾽ εὔπρυμνοι 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 4.247, compare 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 6.266; ἐν ποταμῷ, ὅθι τ᾽ ἀρδμὸς ἔην πάντεσσι βοτοῖσιν 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 18.521, compare 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 14.353.]]

__B.9
a part of the anatomy is defined by a clause (containing τε) which indicates a feature which universally belongs to it, κατ᾽ ἰσχίον, ἔνθα τε μηρὸς ἰσχίῳ ἐνστρέφεται [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 5.305, compare 8.83, 13.547, 16.481, 20.478]]; similarly a point of time is defined, ὥρῃ ἐν εἰαρινῇ, ὅτε τ᾽ ἤματα μακρὰ πέλονται [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 18.367.]]

__B.10
τε is used in relative clauses which define a measurement of a particular thing or action by reference to the measurement (in general) of some thing or action well known in daily life, γεφύρωσεν δὲ κέλευθον μακρὴν ἠδ᾽ εὐρεῖαν, ὅσον τ᾽ ἐπὶ δουρὸς ἐρωὴ γίγνεται [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 15.358; τοῦ δ᾽ ἤτοι κλέος ἔσται ὅσον τ᾽ ἐπικίδναται ἠώς 7.451; ὅτε τόσσον ἀπῆν ὅσσον τε γέγωνε βοήσας 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 9.473, compare 3.321, +others]]; more rarely the definition is by reference to the measurement of a particular thing or action, ἤσθιε.. ἕως ὅ τ᾽ ἀοιδὸς ἐνὶ μεγάροισιν ἄειδεν[Refs [(assuming variant) 17.358; ἥ τις δὴ τέτληκε τόσα φρεσίν, ὅσσα τ᾽ ἐγώ περ 19.347.]]

__B.11
the frequently use of τε B in similes is to be explained under one or other of the {ταώς} heads, e.g. when reference is made to generally known kinds of things or natural phenomena, to human experience in daily life, or to well-known phenomena of the animal world, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 2.456, 459, 463, 468, 470, 471, 474, 481, 3.23 - 5, 33, 11.415 - 7, +others; or when universal characteristics of gods, men, animals, etc., are indicated by relative clauses introduced by ὅς τε, ὅς ῥά τε, etc., 3.61, 151, 198, +others; or by ὥς τε, ἠΰτε, ὥς τίς τε, etc., e.g. 5.136, 17.133, 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 4.535, ὡς εἴ τε 9.314, 14.254, etc.]]

__B.II
in post-[Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Homerus Epicus]] Gr. this use of τε is more restricted; outside of Epic dialect and other early dactylic verse [Refs 8th c.BC+ [(8th-7th c.BC: Hesiodus Epicus “Opera et Dies” 30, 214, 233, +others, 6th c.BC: Xenophanes Poeta Philosophus 13.3, 6th c.BC: Theognis Elegiacus 148, 359, etc.) it is not found except with relatives, and with these it has scarcely any discernible sense, so that ὅς τε in Lyric poetry and Trag. is for the most part only ={ὅς}, e.g. (possibly generalizing) Μοῖρ᾽, ἅ τε πατρώϊον τῶνδ᾽ ἔχει τὸν εὔφρονα πότμον 5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “O.” 2.35, compare 14.2, 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Eumenides” 1024, 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Hecuba” 445 (Lyric poetry), etc. (see. ὅστε)]]; without generalizing force, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “N.” 9.9, 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Persae” 297, “Ch.” 615, etc.; 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus has τά πέρ τε 1.74, ὅκως τε 2.108 codices, ὅσον τε]] (without a verb, as in [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 9.325, +others) 1.126, 2.96, 3.5, +others, οἷά τε 1.93 codices (adverbially 2.175, 5.11): in _Attic dialect_ Prose and Comedy texts even these uses disappear and we find only a few phrases, as ἅτε, ὥστε, ἐφ᾽ ᾧτε, οἷός τε]]; in later Gr. we find exceptionally ἔνθεν τε [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Hippocrates Medicus “ἐπιστολαί” 17; ἀφ᾽ οὗ τε “UPZ” 62.8 (2nd c.BC)]]; ἀπ᾽ οὗ τε [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [“PCair.Zen.” 291.3 (3rd c.BC)]]; οἵ τε [Refs 2nd c.BC+ [“GDI” 215.23 (Erythrae, 2nd c.BC)]]; ἥ τ᾽ [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [“PMag.Par.” 1.2962; ὅσον τε ὀκτὼ στάδια 2nd c.AD: Pausanias Periegeta 6.26.1]]; καὶ ἔστιν ἔπη Μαντικὰ ὁπόσα τε (= which) ἐπελεξάμεθα καὶ ἡμεῖς [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [[prev. author] 9.31.5; οἷόν τε καὶ ἐπὶ τῆς κύων φωνῆς θεωροῦμεν 2nd c.AD: Sextus Empiricus Philosophus “adversus Mathematicos” 11.28.]]

__C
in [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Homerus Epicus]] τε is also (but less frequently) used in conjunction with other particles in contexts (mainly particular statements) such as the following:

__C.1
in assurances, statements on oath, and threats, σχέτλιος, ἦ τ᾽ ἐκέλευον ἀπωσάμενον δήϊον πῦρ ἂψ ἐπὶ νῆας ἴμεν [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 18.13; ἐξ αὖ νῦν ἔφυγες θάνατον, κύον· ἦ τέ τοι ἄγχι ἦλθε κακόν 11.362; ἦ τε is similarly used in 11.391, 17.171, 236, 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 24.28, 311, +others]]; ἦ τ᾽ ἄν in [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 12.69, +others]]; γάρ τε (assuming variant) in οὐ γάρ τ᾽ οἶδα [Refs 8th c.BC+ [6.367, compare 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 10.190; νύ τε in 1.60, 347]] (but τ᾽ more probably = τοι, see at {σύ}); δέ τε in ἀγορῇ δέ τ᾽ ἀμείνονές εἰσι καὶ ἄλλοι [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 18.106; σὲ δέ τ᾽ ἐνθάδε γῦπες ἔδονται 16.836]]; μέν τε in σφὼ μέν τε σαώσετε λαὸν Ἀχαιῶν [Refs [13.47, compare 4.341]]; εἴ πέρ τε in οὔ τοι ἔτι δηρόν γε φίλης ἀπὸ πατρίδος αἴης ἔσσεται, οὐδ᾽ εἴ πέρ τε σιδήρεα δέσματ᾽ ἔχῃσιν [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 1.204, compare 188, 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 12.223, 245.]]

__C.2
also in commands, warnings, and admonitions, σίγα, μή τίς τ᾽ ἄλλος Ἀχαιῶν τοῦτον ἀκούσῃ μῦθον [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 14.90, compare 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 19.486; ὣς ἄγαγ᾽ ὡς μήτ᾽ ἄρ τις ἴδῃ μήτ᾽ ἄρ τε νοήσῃ 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 24.337]]; τούσδε τ᾽ (variant δ᾽) ἐᾶν [Refs [16.96 (nisi to be read τούσδ᾽ ἔτ᾽); δὸς δέ τέ μ᾽ ἄνδρα ἑλεῖν 5.118; μηδέ τ᾽ ἐρώει (nisi to be read μηδ᾽ ἔτ᾽) 2.179, 22.185.]]

__C.3
also in passionate utterances, in clauses which indicate the cause of the speaker's passion or a circumstance which might have caused others to behave more considerately towards him, ὤ μοι ἐγὼ δειλή.. ἥ τ᾽.. τὸν μὲν.. θρέψασα.. ἐπιπροέηκα [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 18.55; σχέτλιοί ἐστε, θεοί, ζηλήμονες ἔξοχον ἄλλων, οἵ τε θεαῖς ἀγάασθε.. ἤν τίς τε.. 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 5.119, 120, compare 21.87, 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 15.468, 17.174]]; ἡμεῖς δ᾽ αὖ μαχόμεσθ᾽, οἵ πέρ τ᾽ ἐπίκουροι ἔνειμεν and we, who (mark you) are only allies (not γαμβροί and κασίγνητοι), are fighting, [Refs [5.477]]; τρεῖς γάρ τ᾽ ἐκ Κρόνου εἰμὲν ἀδελφεοί for we, let me tell you, are three brothers, sons of Cronos (and Zeus has no prior title to power),[Refs 8th c.BC+ [15.187; ποῖόν δε ἔπος φύγεν ἕρκος ὀδόντων δεινόν τ᾽ ἀργαλέον τε· νεμεσσῶμαι δέ τ᾽ ἀκούων 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 21.169; οὐ μήν οἱ τό γε κάλλιον οὐδέ τ᾽ ἄμεινον 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 24.52.]]

__C.4
in descriptions of particular events and things where there is no general reference, κνίση μὲν ἀνήνοθεν, ἐν δέ τε φόρμιγξ ἠπύει [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 17.270]]; ὥς (= so) τέ μοι ὑβρίζοντες ὑπερφιάλως δοκέουσιν δαίνυσθαι κατὰ δῶμα [Refs 8th c.BC+ [1.227; τοὺς μέν τ᾽ ἰητροὶ πολυφάρμακοι ἀμφιπένονται.. σὺ δ᾽ ἀμήχανος ἔπλευ, Ἀχιλλεῦ 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 16.28]]; πόλιν πέρι δινηθήτην καρπαλίμοισι πόδεσσι, θεοὶ δέ τε πάντες ὁρῶντο uncertain [Refs 8th c.BC+ [l. in 22.166; εὗρε δ᾽ ἐνὶ σπῆϊ γλαφυρῷ Θέτιν, ἀμφὶ δέ τ᾽ ἄλλαι εἵαθ᾽ ὁμηγερέες ἅλιαι θεαί 24.83 (assuming variant); ἐν δέ τε φάρμακον ἧκε 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 10.317; νῶϊ δέ τ᾽ ἄψορροι κίομεν 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 21.456; πολλὰς γὰρ δὴ νύκτας.. ἄεσα καί τ᾽ ἀνέμεινα.. Ἠῶ 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 19.342; δέελον δ᾽ ἐπὶ σῆμά τ᾽ ἔθηκε 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 10.466; ἐν δέ τε οἶνον κρητῆρσιν κερόωντο 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 20.252]]; so with οὐδέ τ᾽ (nisi to be read οὐδ᾽ ἔτ᾽), τὸν καὶ ὑπέδδεισαν μάκαρες θεοὶ οὐδέ τ᾽ ἔδησαν [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 1.406; οὐδέ τ᾽ ἔληγε μέγας θεός, ὦρτο δ᾽ ἐπ᾽ αὐτόν 21.248; οὐδέ τ᾽ ἄειρε 23.730; οὐδέ τ᾽ ἔασεν 11.437, 21.596, compare 15.709.]]

__C.5
ὅτε τε (when) frequently introduces a temporal clause defining a point of time in the past by means of a well-known event which occurred then, ἦ οὐ μέμνῃ ὅτε τ᾽ ἐκρέμω ὑψόθε; [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 15.18; ὅτε τε Κρόνον.. Ζεὺς γαίης νέρθε καθεῖσε 14.203; ἤματι τῷ ὅτε τ᾽ ἦλθον Ἀμαζόνες 3.189 (but ἤματι τῷ ὅτε τε is general in 13.335]]; so also ὅτε πέρ τε.. κέρωνται[Refs 8th c.BC+ [in 4.259); ὅτε τ᾽ ἤλυθε νόσφιν Ἀχαιῶν ἄγγελος ἐς Θήβας 5.803, compare 10.286, 22.102, 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 7.323, 18.257.]]

__C.6
in ὅ τε (that or because) the τε has no observable meaning, χωόμενος ὅ τ᾽ ἄριστον Ἀχαιῶν οὐδὲν ἔτισας [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 1.244, compare 412, 4.32, 6.126, 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 5.357, +others]]

__C.7
ἐπεί τε = {ἐπεί} (when) is rare in [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Homerus Epicus, ἐπεί τ᾽ ἐνόησε 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 12.393, compare ἐπείτε.]]

__C.8
where τ᾽ ἄρ occurs in questions, e.g. πῇ τ᾽ ἂρ μέμονας καταδῦναι ὅμιλο; [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 13.307, compare 1.8, 18.188, +others]], ταρ (which see) should probably be read, since ἄρ (α) usually precedes a τε which is not copulative; so perhaps ταρα should be read for τ᾽ ἄρα in [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 1.346.]]

__C.9
in ἣ θέμις ἐστὶν.. ἤ τ᾽ ἀνδρῶν ἤ τε γυναικῶν [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 9.276]], it is not clear whether τε is copulative (τε A) or generalizing (τε B) or neither (τε C); ἤ is probably ={ἦ} (accented as in ἤτοι (; ἤ τ᾽ ἀλκῆς ἤ τε φόβοιο is uncertain reading in [Refs [17.42]]; ἤ τ᾽ = or is found in [Refs [19.148, =]]than in [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 16.216.]]

__C.10
Rarer and later uses;

__C.10.a
also, especially with ἄλλος, Ἑρμεία, σὺ γὰρ αὖτε τά τ᾽ ἄλλα περ ἄγγελός ἐσσι [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 5.29, compare 17.273, 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 23.483; ἐπεὶ τά τε ἄλλα πράττουσιν καλῶς, ἀναθεῖναι αὐτοὺς καὶ στήλην “IG” 22.1298.9, compare 4th c.BC: Lycurgus Orator 100 (assuming variant); ἐκομισάμην τὸ παρὰ σοῦ ἐπιστόλιον, ἐν ᾧ ὑπέγραψάς μοι τήν τε παρὰ Ζήνωνος πρὸς Ἰεδδοῦν γεγραμμένην “PCair.Zen.” 18.1 (3rd c.BC)]]; εἰ οὖν περὶ τούτων ἐπιστροφὴν μὴ ποιήσει, οἵ τε λοιποί μοι τὰς χεῖρας προσοίσουσιν (-σωσιν Papyrus) [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [“PPetr.” 2p.10 (3rd c.BC)]]; τῶν δὲ παρὰ ταῦτα ποιησόντων τά τε κτήνη ὑπὸ στέρεσιν ἀχθήσεσθαι πρὸς τὰ ἐκφόρια [Refs 2nd c.BC+ [“PTeb.” 27.74 (2nd c.BC)]]; see above [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus 11.3b.]]

__C.10.b
with ὅδε, adding a slight emphasis to the preceding word, εἰ δὴ τήνδε τε γαῖαν ἀνείρεαι [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 13.238, compare 15.484.]]

__C.10.c
τε γάρ rarely ={καὶ γάρ} or γάρ, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Analytica Posteriora” 75b41, “de An.” 405a4, “PA” 661b28, “Pol.” 1318b33, 1333a2]]; ἐάν τε γάρ for even if, [NT.2Cor.10.8]; τήν τε γὰρ ἐπιθυμίαν οὐκ ᾔδειν for I had not known even lust. [NT.Rom.7.7.]

__D
Position of τε:

__D.1
in signf. A, as an enclitic, it stands second word in the sentence, clause, or phrase, regardless of the meaning: ἐγγύθι τε Πριάμοιο καὶ Ἕκτορος near both Priam and Hector, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 6.317; ἡμέτεραί τ᾽ ἄλοχοι καὶ νήπια τέκνα 2.136, compare 4.505, 7.295; αἰεί τε δὴ νηλὴς οὺ καὶ θράσους πλέως 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Prometheus Vinctus” 42 codices, compare 291 (_anapaest meter_); ἄνευ τε δόλου καὶ ἀπάτης 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.69; ὑπέρ τε σοῦ καὶ τῆς ἀδελφῆς “PEnteux.” 6.6 (3rd c.BC)]]; τοῖς τε πόνοις καὶ μαθήμασι [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 537a, compare “Ti.” 70b; hence in 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Orestes” 897 πόλεος must be taken with what precedes (Porson (at [prev. work]))]]: but article + noun, preposition + noun are frequently regarded as forming a unity indivisible by τε, τοῖς κτανοῦσί τε [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Choephori” 41 (Lyric poetry); πρὸς βίαν τε [prev. author] “Pr.” 210]]; also the order is frequently determined by the meaning, τε being placed immediately after the word (or first word of a phrase or clause) which it joins to what precedes or to what follows, πατὴρ ἀνδρῶν τε θεῶν τε [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 1.544; ἔξω δόμων τε καὶ πάτρας 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Prometheus Vinctus” 665]]; the copulative or preparatory τε precedes many other particles, e.g. τε γάρ, τ᾽ ἄρα, τέ τις.

__D.2
τε is enclitic in signfs. B, C also, and stands early in its sentence, clause, or phrase (see. above), but many particles which follow τε in signf. A precede it in signfs. B, C, e.g. in signfs. B, C we have δέ τε, μέν τε, γάρ τε, ἀλλά τε, δ᾽ ἄρα τε, ὅς ῥά τε, οὔτ᾽ ἄρ τε, καὶ γάρ τίς τε, ὅς τίς τε, καί τε.

__E
Etymology: signf. A is found also in Sanskrit ca, Latin -que; for signfs. B and c cf. Sanskrit ca in yá[hudot] káś ca 'whosoever (with following verb)', Latin -que in quisque, ubique, plerique, usque, neque, nec (= non in necopinans, etc.), Gothic ni-h 'not' (also 'and not'), Latin namque (= nam).

Abbott-Smith / STEPBible (TBESG)
τέλειος, -α, -ον
(τέλος), [in LXX chiefly for שָׁלֵם, תָּמִים and cogn. forms ;]
having reached its end, finished, mature, complete, perfect;
__1. of persons, primarily of physical development,
__(a) full-grown, mature: Heb.5:14; ethically: Php.3:15; opposite to νήπιος (-άζειν), 1Co.2:6 14:20, Eph.4:13; τ. καὶ πεπληροφορημένοι, Col.4:12; τ. ἐν Χριστῷ, Col.1:28;
__(b) complete, perfect (expressing the simple idea of complete goodness, without reference either to maturity or to the philosophical idea of a τέλος; see Hort on Jas.1:4): Mat.5:48 19:21, Jas.1:4 3:2; of God, Mat.5:48.
__2. Of things, complete, perfect: Rom.12:2; ἔργον, Jas.1:4; νόμος, Jas.1:25; δώρημα, Jas.1:17; ἀγάπη, 1Jn.4:18; τὸ τ., 1Co.13:10; compar., τελειοτέρα (σκηνή), Heb.9:11.
(There is probably no reference in St. Paul's usage to the use of this term in the ancient mysteries; cf. ICC on Col.1:28; but see also Lft., in l, and Notes, 173 f.) †
SYN.: see: ὁλόκληρος (and cf. Rendall, He., 158 ff.)  (AS)

τελει-όω
and τελεόω (the latter always in [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus, and the prevailing form in _Attic dialect_ Prose, see below, and compare τέλειος [near the start])]]:— make perfect, complete:

__I
of things, acts, works, time, make perfect, complete, accomplish, πάντα ἐτελέωσε ποιήσας [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.120]]; τελεώσαντες τὰς σπονδάς having completed the libations, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 6.32; τελειοῖ τὴν ἐνέργειαν ἡ ἡδονή 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Ethica Nicomachea” 1174b23]]; τ. βίου ἐνιαυτούς complete the tale of years, [Refs [“App.Anth.” 2.281 (from Philadelphia)]]; τὸ ἔργον [NT+2nd c.AD+ [NT.John.4.34; τὰς ἡμέρας NT.Luke.2.43; τὸν δρόμον NT.Act.20.24; τὸν περὶ παιδοτροφίας λόγον ἐνθάδε τελειοῦμεν 2nd c.AD: Soranus Medicus 1.126]]:—middle, [Refs 4th c.AD+ [4th c.AD: Iamblichus Philosophus “de vita Pythagorica” 29.158, “Protr.” 20]]:—passive, to be accomplished, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.160, 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Trachiniae” 1257; ἐπειδὴ χρόνος ἐτελεώθη 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Politicus” 272d]]; τελεωθέντων ἀμφοτέροισι when both men had their wishes accomplished, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 5.11.]]

__I.b
execute a legal instrument, make it valid by completing it, [Refs 1st c.AD+ [“PCair.Preis.” 43.10 (1st c.AD), “PAmh.” 2.111.16 (2nd c.AD), “BGU” 578.21 (2nd c.AD), 1657.6 (3rd c.AD).]]

__I.2
in Logic, τ. τὸ εἶδος complete, make perfect the form or species, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Ethica Nicomachea” 1174a16]]:—passive, of syllogisms, to be made perfect (by reduction to the 1st pers. figure, the other figures being ἀτελεῖς), [Refs [[prev. author] “APr.” 29a16, 30, +others]]

__I.3
passive, of prophecies, to be fulfilled, [NT.John.19.28.]

__II
bring to perfection or consummation, ἐπιγενόμενα δὲ ταῦτα τῷ Δαρείῳ ἐτελέωσέ μιν sealed his success, in his claim to the monarchy, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 3.86]]; τελειῶσαι λόχον make the ambush successful, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Coloneus” 1089 (Lyric poetry)]]:— passive, to be made perfect, attain perfection, [Refs [[prev. author] “El.” 1510 (_anapaest meter_)]]; especially by reaching maturity in point of age, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Symposium” 192a, “R.” 466e, 487a, 498b, etc.]]; so of the embryo, plants, come to maturity, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “de Generatione Animalium” 776a31, 4th-3rd c.BC: Theophrastus Philosophus “Historia Plantarum” 8.2.6, 2nd c.AD: Soranus Medicus 1.33, +others, 2nd c.AD: Galenus Medicus 6.531; τελειωθέντος [μειρακίου] κατὰ τὸ μέγεθος [prev. work]162.]]

__II.2
in passive also, τελειωθῆναι, ={γῆμαι}, [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd c.AD: Pausanias Grammaticus “fragment” 306, compare τέλειος 1.2b, τέλος 1.6.]]

__II.3
passive, to be made perfect, of true Christians, [NT.Heb.11.40, 12.23.]

__II.4
passive, die, [Refs [Inscriptiones Graecae 14.628 (from Rhegium).]]

__III
intransitive, bring fruit to maturity, come to maturity, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “de Generatione Animalium” 757b24.]]

__2
of animals, full-grown, τέλεον νεαροῖς ἐπιθύσας [Refs 8th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Agamemnon” 1504 (_anapaest meter_, and so perhaps αἶγες τ. in 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” [same places])]]; ἐπ᾽ οὗ θύεται τὰ τ. τῶν προβάτων, opposed to γαλαθηνά, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.183, compare “SIG” 1015.31 (Halic.), 5th c.BC: Pherecrates Comicus 44, “PCair.Zen.” 429.13, +others (3rd c.BC), “Sammelb.” 5277.5 (3rd c.AD), etc.]]; τ. ζῷον defined in [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd c.AD: Galenus Medicus 7.677]]; as substantive, τέλειον καὶ δέκα ἄρνες [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [“SIG” 1024.35 (Myconus, 3rd-2nd c.BC)]]; τ. ἵππος, opposed to πῶλος, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Leges” 834c]]; τ. ἅρμα a chariot drawn by horses, opposed to ἅρμα πωλικόν, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [“CIG” “Corpus Inscriptionum Graecarum” “Corpus Inscriptionum Graecarum” 2758 111.D2 (from Aphrodisias), “SIG” 840 (Olympia, 2nd c.AD), 2nd c.AD: Lucianus Sophista “Tim.” 50; τελέᾳ συνωρίδι “IG” 5(2).549.2, +others (4th c.AD(?): Arcadius Grammaticus, 4th c.BC); τελέῳ τεθρίππῳ [prev. work] 5; κέλητι τελέῳ [prev. work] 550.29; κέλητι τελείῳ [prev. work] 7.1772.14, compare 16]]; of trees, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-3rd c.BC: Theophrastus Philosophus “de Causis Plantarum” 3.7.5, “POxy.” 909.18 (3rd c.AD)]]; εἰκὼν τελεία life-sized, [Refs 2nd c.BC+ [“GDI” 4942b7 (Crete, 2nd c.BC)]]; of a torsionengine, full-sized, opposed to to the model of one, [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [3rd-2nd c.BC: Philo Mechanicus “(Belopoeica) Excerpte aus Philons Mechanik - Ath. comparative and superlative: [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Homerus Epicus uses only τελειότατος: in Prose τελεώτερος, -ώτατος]] prevail, though the other forms occur in [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Ethica Nicomachea” 1097a30, 1174b22]]. comparative adverb τελεώτερον [Refs 8th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 520b (τελειοτέρως Scholia 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 2.350, variant in 5th c.AD: Proclus Philosophus “Inst.” 18); τελεώτατα 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 351b.]]
