future -ήσω[Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Troades” 1029, etc.]]: perfect τετελεύτηκα [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Meno” 75e, +others:]] —passive, future middle τελευτήσομαι always in passive sense, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 13.100, 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 8.510, 9.511, 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Hippolytus” 370 (Lyric poetry)]]: aorist ἐτελευτήθην [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 15.74]]:—bring to pass, accomplish, ὄφρα.. τελευτήσω τάδε ἔργα [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 8.9; τ. ἃ μενοινᾷς 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 2.275; ἐπὴν ταῦτα τελευτήσῃς τε καὶ ἔρξῃς 1.293, compare 2.306; γάμον τ. 24.126]]; fulfil an oath or promise, wish or hope, τ. ἐέλδωρ [Refs 8th c.BC+ [21.200; τ. ὅσ᾽ ὑπέστης 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 13.375; οὐ Ζεὺς ἄνδρεσσι νοήματα πάντα τελευτᾷ 18.328, compare 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 3.56, 62; ὅρκια 3rd c.BC: Callimachus Epicus “Aetia” 3.1.29]]; τελευτᾶν τινι κακὸν ἦμαρ bring about an evil day for one, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 15.524; τ. πόνους Δαναοῖς 5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “P.” 1.54, compare 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Phoenissae” 1581 (Lyric poetry); οἷ τ. λόγον [prev. author] “Tr.” 1029]]; τὸ δ᾽ ἔνθεν ποῖ τελευτῆσαί με χρ; to what end must I bring it? [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Coloneus” 476; Ζεὺς ὅ τι νεύσῃ, τοῦτο τελευτᾷ 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Alcestis” 979 (Lyric poetry)]], etc.:—passive, to be fulfilled, come to pass, happen, [same places] entry [near the start]; πρίν γε τὸ Πηλεΐδαο τελευτηθῆναι ἐέλδωρ [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 15.74; πρὶν τελευτηθῇ φόνος 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Orestes” 1218.]]

__2

__3
especially τ. τὸν αἰῶνα finish life, i.e. die, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.32, 9.17, etc.; τ. βίον 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Agamemnon” 929, 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Fragmenta” 646 codices (sed to be read δρόμον), 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Hecuba” 419, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Protagoras” 351b]]; ὑπ᾽ ἄλλου τ. τὸν βίον, i.e. to be killed, [Refs [[prev. author] “Lg.” 870e: also (after the analogy of παύομαι) with _genitive_, τελευτᾶν τοῦ ἀνθρωπίνου βίου]] make an end of life, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 8.7.17]]; so λόγου τ. with words indicating the kind of end or outcome, ἢν ὁ πόλεμος κατὰ νόον τ. [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 9.45, compare 7.47]]; εὖ τ. [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Supplices” 211]]; πτωχοὶ τ. end by being beggars, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 552c]]; οὕτως τ. [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 1.110, 138]]; τ. ἔς τι come to a certain end, issue in, αἱ εὐτυχίαι ἐς τοῦτο ἐτελεύτησαν [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 3.125]]; τ. ἐς τὠυτὸ γράμμα end in the same letter, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. author] 1.139, compare 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 2.51, 4.48, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 618a]]; εἰς ἄνδρας ἐκ μειρακίων τ. [Refs [[prev. author] “Tht.” 173b]]; ποῖ (ἐς τί) τελευτᾶν (φασι); came to what end? [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Persae” 735 (troch.), compare “Ch.” 528, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Leges” 630b; also τ. ἐπί τι [prev. author] “R.” 510d, “Smp.” 211c.]]

__II.3
die, see above [Refs [1.3b.]]

__II.4

of local limits and the like, μέχρι Σολόεντος ἄκρης, ἣ τελευτᾷ τῆς Λιβύης [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 2.32; τελευτῶντος τοῦ Λαβυρίνθου ἔχεται πυραμίς [prev. work] 148]]; τῇ ἡ Κνιδίη χώρη ἐς τὴν ἤπειρον τ. (τέλος), [in LXX for כָּלָה, pi., etc. ;]
__1. to bring to an end, complete, finish: τ. δρόμον, 2Ti.4:7; τ. λόγους, Mat.7:28 19:1 26:1; τ. παραβολάς, Mat.13:53; τ. πόλεις, Mat.10:23; pass., Rev.15:8 20:3, 5 20:7; with ptcp., Mat.11:1.
__2. to execute, perform, complete, fulfil: Luk.2:39, Act.13:29, Rom.2:27, 2Co.12:9, Gal.5:16, Jas.2:8, Rev.11:7; pass., Luk.12:50 18:31 22:37, Jhn.19:28, 30, Rev.10:7 15:1 17:17.
__3. to pay (frequently in cl.): Mat.17:24, Rom.13:6
(cf. ἀπο-, δια-, ἐκ-, ἐπι-, συν-τελέω).†
(AS)

τελέω,
Epic dialect also τελείω, both in [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Homerus Epicus]] (τελέοντες [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 3.262, compare 4.776, +others, τελείει 6.234, 23.161)]]: Epic dialect imperfect τέλεον [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 23.373, 768; ἐτέλειον 9.456, 15.593]]; Ionic dialect τέλεσκον [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [3rd c.BC: Callimachus Epicus “Hymnus in Dianam” 123, “fragment” 434; τελέεσκον 4th c.AD(?): Quintus Smyrnaeus Epicus 8.213]]: future τελέσω [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “N.” 4.43, 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 8.6.3, (δια-) 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 425e codices, 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 21.66 codices (-τελῶ Cobet in both places), “PAvrom.” 2 A 9 (1st c.BC)]]; Epic dialect also τελέω, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 8.415, 12.59, 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 2.256, etc.]]; Attic dialect τελῶ [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Electra” 1435, 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Ranae” 173, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Protagoras” 311b]]: aorist (ἐ) τέλεσα [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 5.390]]; Epic dialect τέλεσσα and ἐτέλεσσα [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 246, 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 12.222, 23.543, 559, +others]] (infinitive τελέσσαι [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “P.” 3.9)]]; Attic dialect ἐτέλεσα [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 4.78, etc.]]: perfect τετέλεκα [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Apologia” 20a, (δια-) 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 18.203]]:—middle, future (see. below): aorist ἐτελεσάμην [Refs [[prev. author] 38.18, etc.]]; perfect τετέλεσμαι [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [“Inscription Prien.” 11.34 (3rd c.BC)]]:—passive, Epic dialect imperfect ἐτελείετο [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 1.5]]: future τελεσθήσομαι [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-3rd c.BC: Theophrastus Philosophus “Characteres” 16.12]]; future middle in this sense, τελεῖται [Refs 8th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Prometheus Vinctus” 929, “Ag.” 68 (_anapaest meter_), etc., τελέεσθαι 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 2.36, τελεῖσθαι 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 23.284]]; participle τελεόμενος [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.206, τελεύμενος [prev. author] 3.134]]: aorist ἐτελέσθην [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 4.663, etc.]]; Aeolic dialect infinitive τελέσθην [Refs 7th c.BC+ [7th-6th c.BC: Sappho Lyrica “Papyrus fragments” in E. Diehl, 1.4]]: perfect τετέλεσμαι [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 18.74, etc.]]: pluperfect τετέλεστο [Refs [19.242]]: Cretan dialect perfect participle τετελημένος [Refs [“GDI” 4963]]; Ionic dialect 3rd.pers. plural perfect τετέληνται uncertain in [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [“SIG” 1024.22 (Myconus, 3rd-2nd c.BC)]]: (τέλος):—fulfil, accomplish, execute, perform, frequently in Poets from [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Homerus Epicus downwards, less frequently in Prose (except in significations 11 and 111); τελέσαι ἔργον τε ἔπος τε 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 2.272, compare 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 1.108, 523, etc.; τ. φιλοτήσια ἔργα 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 11.246]]; μ᾽ ἔφαντο ἄξειν εἰς Ἰθάκην, οὐδ᾽ ἐτέλεσσαν but did it not,[Refs 8th c.BC+ [13.212; τ. ἀέθλους 3.262; πόνον 23.250; πύματον δρόμον 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 23.373; ὁδόν 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 2.256, 6th c.BC: Mimnermus Lyricus 11; sometimes without ὁδόν, ἄτερ καμάτοιο τέλεσσαν ἤματι τῷ αὐτῷ καὶ ἀπήνυσαν οἴκαδ᾽ ὀπίσσω 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 7.325; ὁδῷ δὲ τὰ ξυντομώτατα ἐξ Ἀβδήρων ἐς Ἴστρον ἀνὴρ εὔζωνος ἑνδεκαταῖος τελεῖ 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 2.97]]; ταύτῃ τῇ ἡμέρᾳ ἐς Φάρσαλον ἐτέλεσε [Refs [[prev. author] 4.78]]; κίνδυνον τελέσσαι perform a dangerous feat, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Epicharmus Comicus 99; ἔργον 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Electra” 1399; δίδυμα κακά 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Septem contra Thebas” 782 (Lyric poetry); προστάγματα 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Leges” 926a]], compare d:—passive, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.206]]; καὶ εἰ τετελεσμένον ἐστί, ={τελεῖσθαι δύναται}, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 5.90, 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 14.196; τετέλεστο δὲ ἔργον 7.465]]; αὐτίκ᾽ ἔπειθ᾽ ἅμα μῦθος ἔην, τετέλεστο δὲ ἔργον 'no sooner said than done',[Refs 5th c.BC+ [19.242; ἐάνπερ ἐπὶ λόγῳ ἔργα τελῆται 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 389d, compare “Plt.” 288c; γραφὴ τῶν τετελεσμένων ἔργων “PPetr.” 3p.340 (3rd c.BC)]]; τετέλεσται [NT.John.19.30 (compare 28).]

__2
fulfil one's word, τ. ἔπος, μῦθον, ὑπόσχεσιν, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 14.44, 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 4.776, 10.483; τελέω τὰ πάροιθεν ὑπέστην 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 23.20]]; τελέσαι κότον, χόλον, glut one's fury, wrath, [Refs [1.82, 4.178: also,]]grant one the fulfilment or accomplishment of anything, τ. νόον τινί fulfil his wish,[Refs 8th c.BC+ [23.149, compare 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 22.51; τ. ἐέλδωρ 8th-7th c.BC: Hesiodus Epicus “Scutum Herculis” 36; λιτάς 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Septem contra Thebas” 627 (Lyric poetry); κατάρας [prev. work] 724 (Lyric poetry)]]; rarely with infinitive, οὐδ᾽ ἐτέλεσσε φέρων δόμεναι he succeeded not in.., [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 12.222 (compare ἀνύω 1.6)]]:—passive, to be fulfilled, [Refs [2.36, 330, +others: especially]]perfect participle, [μῦθος] τετελεσμένος ἐστί [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 1.388, compare “hymnus ad Venerem” 26; elsewhere in 8th c.BC: Homerus Epicus only _neuter_, τὸ δὲ καὶ τετελεσμένον ἔσται 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 1.212, compare 8.286, +others:]] —middle, τελέσασθαι δίκην bring a suit to issue, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 38.18, compare 39.18 (_passive_).]]

__3
grant in full, work out, ἀγαθόν τινι, ὅ τι φρεσὶν ᾗσι μενοινᾷ [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 2.34; νόστον 15.112; μόγις δ᾽ ἐτέλεσσε Κρονίων 3.119; τ. λυγρά 18.134; γῆρας ἄρειον 23.286; κακὰ κήδεα τ. τινί 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 18.8, compare 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 4.699, 18.389, 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Antigone” 3]]; θεῶν τελεσάντων (i.e. αὐτό) [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “P.” 10.49; εὖ τελεῖ θεός 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Septem contra Thebas” 35.]]

__4
ὅρκια τελεῖν make an oath effective, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 7.69]]: later, execute a legal document, δημόσιος χρηματισμὸς τετελεσμένος δι᾽ ἐπιτηρητῶν ἀγορανομίας Mitteis [Refs 1st c.AD+ [“Chr.” 200.10 (3rd c.AD),compare “POxy.” 290.22 (1st c.AD), etc.]]

__5
bring to fulfilment or perfection, ἀρετὰν.. πεπρωμέναν τελέσει [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “N.” 4.43]]; τ. τινά bless him with perfect happiness, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [[prev. author] “I.” 6(5).46 (uncertain); so τετελεσμένον ἐσλόν [prev. author] “N.” 9.6; τελεσθεὶς ὄλβος 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Agamemnon” 751 (Lyric poetry)]]: also, bring a child to maturity, bring it to the birth, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Bacchae” 100 (Lyric poetry).]]

__5.b
with an  adjective added, ἅπαντας ἡ παίδευσις ἡμέρους τελεῖ makes perfectly gentle, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-3rd c.BC: Menander Comicus “Μονόστιχοι - Fragmenta Comicorum Graecorum” 41.]]

__6
bring to an end, finish, end, ἐξ ἀγαθοῦ γὰρ ἀρξάμενος τελέω τὸν λόγον εἰς ἀγαθόν [Refs [“Lyric poetry Alex. Adesp.” 21.2.]]

__7
of Time, ὅτε δὴ τρίτον ἦμαρ.. τέλεσ᾽ Ἠώς [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 5.390]]; βίον τ. [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Simonides Lyricus 36, 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Antigone” 1114]]; πολλοὺς τρόχους ἡλίου[Refs [[prev. work] 1065; τελευτὴν τοῦ βίου [prev. author] “Tr.” 79]]; also τ. νοῦσον come to the end of it, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th-7th c.BC: Hesiodus Epicus “Theogonia” 799]]:—passive, περὶ δ᾽ ἤματα μακρὰ τελέσθη [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 10.470, compare 8th-7th c.BC: Hesiodus Epicus “Theogonia” 59; τετελεσμένον εἰς ἐνιαυτόν [prev. work] 795]]; ἐν τοῖς ἔτεσι τοῖς δὶς ἑπτὰ τετελ. [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Historia Animalium” 581a14, compare “Metaphorical” 994a26]]; of men, come to one's end, οἴμοι.. δεσπότου τελουμένου [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Choephori” 875 (assuming variant).]]

__8
sometimes intransitive, like the passive, come to an end, be fulfilled, turn out, οὐ γὰρ οἶδ᾽ ὅπῃ τελεῖ[Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. work] 1021, compare “Pers.” 225 (troch.), 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Electra” 1417 (Lyric poetry)]]: later ={τελέθω}, to be, φύσει τελῶν μνησίκακος [Refs [12th c.AD: Tzetzes, Joannes Grammaticus “Historiarum variarum chiliades” 2.83, +others]]

__II
pay what one owes, what is due, λιπαρὰς τελέουσι θέμιστας [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 9.156, 298]] (unless this means 'will administer good laws'); νῆας.. αἵ κεν τελέοιεν ἕκαστα ἄστε᾽ ἐπ᾽ ἀνθρώπων ἱκνεύμεναι bring supplies of everything, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 9.127]]: generally, pay, present, δῶρα, δωτίνην, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 9.598, 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 11.352; μισθόν 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 21.457, 5th c.BC: Eupolis Comicus 4; ἀργύριον 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Lysis” 208b; ἀργύριον.. μισθόν [prev. author] “Prt.” 311d; δύο δραχμὰς μισθόν 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Ranae” 173: _metaphorically_, τ. ὕμνον 5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “P.” 1.79, 2.13]]; τ. ψυχὰν Ἀΐδᾳ, i.e. die, [Refs [[prev. author] “I.” 1.68.]]

__II.b
especially pay tax, duty, toll, φόρον [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus Alcaeus1.123a; τὰ τέλη 4th c.BC: Cratinus Junior Comicus 9.5, 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Ἀθηναίων Πολιτεία” 55.3, compare 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Leges” 847b]]; τ. μετοίκιον pay the tax of a μέτοικος,[Refs 4th c.BC+ [[prev. work] 850b; ἱππάδα 4th c.BC: Isaeus Orator 7.39; θητικόν 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Ἀθηναίων Πολιτεία” 7.4, Legal cited in 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 43.54; ξενικά 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 57.34; συντάξεις 4th c.BC: Aeschines Orator 3.91; frequently in Papyri, οἱ τελοῦντες τὰ καθήκοντα εἰς τὸ βασιλικόν “PTeb.” 5.174 (2nd c.BC), etc.]]; τ. σῖτον pay one's contribution of corn, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Historia Graeca (Hellenica)” 5.3.21]]: absolutely, pay tax, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [Inscriptiones Graecae 12.1.2,3, 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 2.109]]:—passive, of money, etc., to be paid, [Refs [[prev. author] 9.93]]; of persons, to be in receipt of rent, χώραν ἀτέλεστον ἔχουσιν αὐτοὶ τετελεσμένοι [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator “Prooemia” 55.]]

__II.2
lay out, spend, χρήματα μεγάλα [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 3.137, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Apologia” 20a, compare 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 8.1.13]]:—passive, to be spent or expended, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 2.125]]; ἐς τὸ δεῖπνον τετρακόσια τάλαντα τετελεσμένα laid out upon the dinner, [Refs [[prev. author] 7.118]]; ἕνδεκα μυριάδας μεδίμνων τελεομένας ἐπ᾽ ἡμέρῃ ἑκάστῃ[Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. work] 187, compare 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Leges” 955e.]]

__II.2.b
consume, eat [Refs 5th c.BC+ [compare (ἀναλίσκω 1.3), [σιτία] μέτρια τελεύμενα 5th c.BC: Hippocrates Medicus “περὶ παθῶν” 47, compare 26, 43, 44.]]

__II.3
since, in many Greek cities, the citizens were distributed into classes accusative to their taxable property, τ. εἴς τινας meant to belong to a class, to be reckoned among, τ. ἐς Ἕλληνας, ἐς Βοιωτούς, belong to the Greeks, the Boeotians, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 2.51, 6.108]]; εἰς ἀστοὺς τ. become a citizen, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Tyrannus” 222]]; εἰς ἄνδρας τ. come to man's estate, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Leges” 923e]]; εἰς γυναῖκας ἐξ ἀνδρὸς τ. become a woman instead of a man, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Bacchae” 822]]; ἕκαστος ἡμῶν ὑπό τινα τελεῖ δαίμονα ὃς πάσης ἡμῶν τῆς ζωῆς ἐπάρχει belongs.. , [Refs 4th c.BC+ [5th c.AD: Hermias Alexandrinus Philosophus “in Platonis Phaedrum scholia” p.93 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus]]

__II.4
from the last sense perhaps may be explained the phrase, κοῖός τις δοκέοι ἀνὴρ εἶναι πρὸς τὸν πατέρα τελέσαι to compare with his father, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 3.34 (τελέσαι omitting codex E, secl. Hude).]]

__III
initiate in the mysteries, τινα [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Euthydemus” 277d; τῇ μητρὶ τελούσῃ τὰς βίβλους ἀναγιγνώσκειν 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 18.259]]; τυμπανίζειν καὶ τ. [Refs 1st c.AD+ [1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus 2.60a; τ. τῷ Διονύσῳ “Milet.” 6.23]]:—passive, to have oneself initiated, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Nubes” 258; τετελεσμένος 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Phaedo” 69c, “Berl.Sitzb.” 1927.169 (from Cyrene), etc.]]; ἐτέλεις, ἐγὼ δ᾽ ἐτελούμην [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 18.265]]; Διονύσῳ τελεσθῆναι to be consecrated to Dionysus, initiated in his mysteries, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 4.79; ὀργίοισι 5th c.BC: Hippocrates Medicus “νόμος” 5, compare 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Symposium” 1.10: with _accusative_, Βακχεῖ᾽ ἐτελέσθη 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Ranae” 357 (_anapaest meter_); τελέους τελετὰς τελούμενος 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Phaedrus” 249c, compare 250b; also τ. μεγάλοισι τέλεσι [prev. author] “R.” 560e.]]

__III.b
in Magic, endow a thing with potency, consecrate it, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [“PMag.Par.” 1.1744, “PMag.Lond.” 46.242, 121.590, Scholia 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Plutus” 884.]]

__III.c
enchant, Παλλάδιον τετελεσμένον Eust.ad [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd c.AD: Dionysius Periegeta 620.]]

__III.2
metaphorically, τελεσθῆναι στρατηγός to be formally appointed general, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 13.19]]; τετελεσμένος σωφροσύνῃ a votary of temperance, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Oeconomicus” 21.12.]]

__III.3
also of sacred rites, perform, ἱερά [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Bacchae” 485, compare “IT” 464 (_anapaest meter_); θυσίαν τοῖς θεοῖς 1st c.BC: Diodorus Siculus Historicus 4.34, compare 1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus “Theseus” 16; ὄργια “IG” 14.1183 (from Rome), 2nd c.AD: Pausanias Periegeta 4.14.1]]; γάμον, γάμους, [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [3rd c.BC: Callimachus Epicus “Hymnus in Apollinem” 14, 3rd c.BC: Lycophron Tragicus 1387]]:— passive, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Leges” 775a.]]

__III.4
passive, of women, to be married, [Refs [“GDI” 3721.5,9 (from Cos).]]

Abbott-Smith / STEPBible (TBESG)
τέλος, -ους, τό
[in LXX for קֵץ, etc.; εἰς τὸ τ., chiefly for נֶצַח and cognate forms ;]
__1. end: most frequently of the termination or limit of an act or state (in NT also of the end of a period of time, cl. τελευτή), Luk.1:33, 1Co.10:11, 2Co.3:13, 1Pe.4:7; by meton., of one who makes an end, Rom.10:4; ἕως (ἄχρι, μέκρι) τέλους, 1Co.1:8, 2Co.1:13, Heb.3:14 6:11, Rev.2:26; εἰς τ., to or at the end, Mat.10:22, Mrk.13:13, Luk.18:5, Jhn.13:1 (or here, to the uttermost, see Westc., in l); τ. ἔχειν, Luk.22:37; adverbially, τὸ δὲ τέλος, finally, 1Pe.3:8; of the last in a series, Rev.21:6 22:13; of the issue, fate or destiny, Mat.26:58; with genitive of thing(s), Rom.6:21, al.; with genitive of person(s), 2Co.11:13, al.; of the aim or purpose, 1Ti.1:5.
__2. toll, custom, revenue: Rom.13:7; pl., as most usually, Mat.17:25
(AS)

a length of time (or space), term, course, ἀρετάς, αἷσι Κλεωνυμίδαι θάλλοντες αἰεὶ σὺν θεῷ θνατὸν διέρχονται βιότου τ. [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “I.” 4(3).5(23); so perhaps in 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Hippolytus” 87 (see. below 3), and in διὰ τέλους (see. below 2 c).]]

__II.2
state of completion or maturity, τ. λαβεῖν, ἔχειν, of plants or animals, to attain maturity, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Phaedrus” 276b, “Lg.” 834c, compare 899e]]: hence, completion, end, finish, τ. ἐπιθεῖναι τῷ λόγῳ complete it, [Refs [[prev. author] “Smp.” 186a, compare “Prt.” 348a]]; ὃ πᾶσι τοῖς προτέροις ἐπ έθηκε τ. as a finish to all his former acts, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 18.140; τὸ τ. τῆς σκηνῆς ἐποιήσαντο 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 2.3.24; ταύτης.. τῆς ἡμέρας τοῦτο τὸ τ. ἐγένετο [prev. author] “An.” 1.10.18]]; τ. λαβεῖν to be completed, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 501e, 5th-6th c.BC: Isocrates Orator 4.5; τ. ἔχειν 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Leges” 772c]]; οὐ τ. ἵκεο μύθων didst not reach the end of thy speech, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 9.56; ἐπὶ τέλους τοῦ δρόμου 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 613d; μέχρι τοῦ τὸ προκείμενον ἐπὶ τέλος ἀχθῆναι “PTeb.” 14.8 (2nd c.BC)]]; ἑκάστων πρὸς τέλος ἀχθέντων [Refs 2nd c.BC+ [“UPZ” 108.29 (2nd c.BC),compare “BGU” 1816.11 (1st c.BC)]]; ἡ εἰκοστὴ τοῦ νοσήματος ἡμέρα τ. μὲν τριῶν ἑβδομάδων, ἓξ δὲ τετράδων [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd c.AD: Galenus Medicus 18(2).234:]] —frequently in Adverbial phrases:

__II.2.a
τέλος at last, ὥστε τ. ἡσυχίαν ἦγον [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 2.100, compare 5.46]]; but most frequently at the beginning of the clause, μάχης δὲ καρτερῆς γενομένης, τέλος οὐδέτεροι νικήσαντες διέστησαν [Refs 6th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.76, compare 4.131, +others; τέλος δέ [prev. author] 1.36, 6th c.BC: Theognis Elegiacus 1294, etc.]]; ἀλλὰ τ. [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 6.137; τ. μέντοι [prev. author] 5.89, 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Historia Graeca (Hellenica)” 5.4.30; τ. γε μέντοι 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Antigone” 233]]; καὶ τ. [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 4.154, 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 1.109]]; τό γε τ. [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Leges” 740e.]]

__II.2.b
<ἐς τ. in the end, in the long run, πάντως ἐς τ. ἐξεφάνη [Refs 6th c.BC+ [6th c.BC: Solon Lyricus 13.28, compare 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 9.37]]; εἰς τ. [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Philoctetes” 409; θνητῶν δ᾽ εἰς τ. ὄλβιος οὐδείς 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Iphigenia Aulidensis” 161 (_anapaest meter_), compare 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 3.40]]; ὁρῶντες τὴν Λιβύην εἰς τ. ἀβλαβῆ διαμένουσαν altogether, completely, [Refs 2nd c.BC+ [2nd c.BC: Polybius Historicus 1.20.7, compare “PTeb.” 38.11 (2nd c.BC), “OGI” 90.12 (Rosetta, 2nd c.BC), “PSI” 10.1120.5 1st c.BC-1st c.AD]]; ἐς τ. ἄνυε μοίρας uncertain reading in [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [3rd c.BC: Theocritus Poeta Bucolicus 1.93.]]

__II.2.c
διὰ τέλους (originally perhaps from signification [Refs [1.1 or 5, or 11.1b, through the (whole)]] performance or time), through to the end, completely, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Prometheus Vinctus” 275, 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Ajax” 685, 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Supplices” 270, 5th-6th c.BC: Isocrates Orator 5.24, 8.17, 19.4]]; throughout, all the time, always, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Antipho Orator 5.42, 4th c.BC: Timocles Comicus 8.5, 3rd c.BC: Hegesippus Comicus 2.3; so διὰ τέλεος 5th c.BC: Hippocrates Medicus “περὶ διαίτης ὀξέων” 46 (= διὰ παντὸς καὶ ἀεί _accusative_ to 2nd c.AD: Galenus Medicus 15.618); διὰ τέλους ἀεί 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Philebus” 36e]]; permanently, for good, τοῦ ἀφεθῆναί σε διὰ τ. [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [“PPetr.” 2p.45 (3rd c.BC).]]

__II.2.d
ἐπὶ τέλος at the end, opposed to ἐν ἀρχῇ, [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd c.AD: Galenus Medicus 19.183.]]

__II.2.e
τέλει perhaps in the end, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Tyrannus” 198 (Lyric poetry).]]

__II.3
especially τ. ἔχειν βίου to have reached the end of life, to be dead, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Leges” 801e; ἐμοὶ μὲν τοῦ βίου τὸ τ. ἤδη πάρεστιν 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 8.7.6; πᾶσίν ἐστιν ἀνθρώποις τ. τοῦ βίου θάνατος 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 57.27; εἰς τ. τοῦ ζῆν ἀφικνεῖσθαι 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Coloneus” 1530]]: less frequently absolutely, death, ἐλπίς ἐστι νύκτερον τ. μολεῖν [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Septem contra Thebas” 367 (Lyric poetry); οἱ νεηνίαι οὐκέτι ἀνέστησαν ἀλλ᾽ ἐν τέλεϊ τούτῳ ἔσχοντο 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.31]]; ἔχει τὸ κάλλιστον τ. [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 7.3.11]]; ἔχει τ., ={τετελεύτηκε}, Laconian phrase accusative to [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.AD(?): Hesychius Legal icographus; τῶν ἤδη τ. ἐχόντων 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Leges” 717e, compare 772c, “BGU” 1857.7 (1st c.BC)]]; reversely, τ. ἔχει τινά [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Leges” 740c; οἷόν σε βίου τ. εἷλε 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Rhesus” 735 (_anapaest meter_):]] —but ὀλβίως ἔλυσεν τὸ τ. βίου has paid life's toll [Refs 5th c.BC+ [compare(above 1.8), 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Coloneus” 1720 (Lyric poetry)]]; τὸ τ. ὁ χρόνος ἀπαιτεῖ poetical in [Refs 5th c.BC+ [“Mus.Script.” p.452 von Jan; also τ. δὲ κάμψαιμ᾽ ὥσπερ ἠρξάμην βίου 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Hippolytus” 87 (compare above 11.1b)]]; πρὶν ἂν πέλας (variant{τέλος}) γραμμῆς ἵκηται καὶ τ. κάμψῃ βίου [Refs [[prev. author] “El.” 955 - 6.]]

__II.4
end, cessation, ὡς δὲ πρὸς τ. γόων ἀφίκοντ᾽ [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Coloneus” 1621]]; πῶς τροχηλάτου μανίας ἂν ἔλθοιμ᾽ ἐς τ. πόνων τ᾽ ἐμῶ; [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Iphigenia Taurica” 83]]; ὅταν δὴ πημάτων λάβῃ τ. [Refs 4th c.BC+ [[prev. author] “Hel.” 534; τ. δέχει δὴ τῶν ἐμῶν προσφθεγμά των [prev. author] “Hec.” 413; ἡ μὲν οὖν ἐπανάστασις.. τοῦτο τὸ τ. ἔσχεν “Hellenica Oxyrhynchia” 10.3; ἐπειδὴ οὐχ οἷόν τε εἰς ἄπειρον, τ. ἔσται πάσης φορᾶς 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Metaphorical” 1074a30.]]

__II.5
end of a word, [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd c.AD: Apollonius Dyscolus Grammaticus “de Pronominibus;” 12.25, +others]]; of a sentence, ἐπὶ τέλει πρόσκειται [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd c.AD: Soranus Medicus 1.43, compare 2nd c.AD: Galenus Medicus 15.20]]; of a chapter or book, ἐπὶ τέλει ἀναλυθήσεται [Refs 5th c.BC+ [3rd c.BC: Archimedes Geometra “περὶ σφαίρας καὶ κυλίνδρου” 2.4, compare 2nd c.AD: Galenus Medicus 15.10; πρὸς τῷ τ. ῥηθήσεται 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Leges” 957b; πρὸς τῷ τ. τοῦ ἐντέρου 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “de Partibus Animalium” 675a16]]; ἀπὸ τέλους τοῦ σταδίου, opposed to ἀπὸ μέσου, [Refs [[prev. author] “Ph.” 239b34 (compare below 111.2).]]

__III
achievement, attainment, τηλοῦ ἐμοὶ νόστοιο τ. γλυκεροῖο γενέσθαι [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 22.323, compare 5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “N.” 3.25; τ. δὲ τῆς ἀπαλλαγῆς τοῦ Αἰθίοπος ὧδε ἔλεγον γενέσθαι 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 2.139]]; πῶς ἂν καὶ τοῦτο τοῦ τ. τυγχάνοι, i.e. might be achieved, [Refs 1st c.BC+ [1st c.BC: Geminus Astronomicus 8.36.]]

__III.2
winning-post, goal in a race, πρὸς τ. ὀρνύμενον [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Bacchylides Lyricus 5.45]]; in a contest, ἔστιν δ᾽ ἀφάνεια τύχας καὶ μαρναμένων, πρὶν τ. ἄκρον ἱκέσθαι [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “I.” 4(3).32(50)]]; εἰς τ. ἐλθεῖν, of runners in a race, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 613c.]]

__III.2.b
prize, ἔφερε πυγμᾶς τ. [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “O.” 10(11).67]]; οὐ γὰρ ἦν πενταέθλιον ἀλλ᾽ ἐφ᾽ ἑκάστῳ ἔργματι κεῖτο τ. [Refs [[prev. author] “I.” 1.27; ποτὶ γραμμᾷ μὲν αὐτὰν στᾶσεκοσμήσαις, τ. ἔμμεν ἄκρον [prev. author] “P.” 9.118]] (perhaps 'to be the winning post and prize'); κρίνεις τ. ἀρετᾶς [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Bacchylides Lyricus 10.6: _metaphorically_, οὐκ ἔχω εἰπεῖν τίνι τοῦτο Μοῖρα τ. ἔμπεδον ὤρεξε 5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “N.” 7.57.]]

__III.3
Philos., full realization, highest point. ideal, ἅπτεσθαι τοῦ τ. [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Symposium” 211b]]; πρὸς τ. ἰὼν τῶν ἐρωτικῶν[Refs [[prev. work] 210e; πρὸς τ. ἀρετῆς ἐλθόντα [prev. author] “Clit.” 410e, compare “R.” 613c.]]

__III.3.b
the end or purpose of action, τ. εἶναι ἁπασῶν τῶν πράξεων τὸ ἀγαθόν [Refs 4th c.BC+ [[prev. author] “Grg.” 499e; frequently in 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus, “EN” 1094a18, +others]]: hence, the final cause, ={τὸ οὗ ἕνεκα}, [Refs [[prev. author] “Metaphorical” 994b9, 996a26, +others]]; hence simply ={τὸ ἀγαθόν}, the chief good, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [[prev. author] “EN” 1097a21, 4th-3rd c.BC: Zeno Citieus Stoicus 1.45, etc.]]

[in LXX for חׇכְמָה, מַעֲשֶׂה, עֲבֹדָה ;]

---

LSJ / STEPBible (TFLSJ)
τέχν-η, ἡ,
(τέκτων) art, skill, cunning of hand, especially in metalworking, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 3.433, 6.234, 11.614]]; also of a shipwright, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 3.61]]; of a soothsayer, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Agamemnon” 249 (_plural_, Lyric poetry), “Eu.” 17, 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Tyrannus” 389, etc.; τέχναι ἑτέρων ἕτεραι 5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “N.” 1.25; ὤπασε τ. πᾶσαν [prev. author] “O.” 7.50.]]

__2
craft, cunning, in bad sense, δολίη τ. [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 4.455, 8th-7th c.BC: Hesiodus Epicus “Theogonia” 160]]: plural, arts, wiles, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 8.327.332, 8th-7th c.BC: Hesiodus Epicus “Theogonia” 496, 929; δολίαις τέχναισι χρησάμενος 5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “N.” 4.58]]; τέχναις τινός by his arts (or simply by his agency), [Refs [[prev. author] “O.” 9.52, “P.” 3.11]]; τέχνην κακὴν ἔχει he has a bad trick, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th-7th c.BC: Hesiodus Epicus “Theogonia” 770, compare 5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “I.” 4(3).35(53), S “Ph.” 88, etc.]]

__3
way, manner, or means whereby a thing is gained, without any definite sense of art or craft, μηδεμιῇ τ. in no wise, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.112]]; ἰθέῃ τ. straightway, [Refs [[prev. author] 9.57]]; πάσῃ τ. by all means, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Nubes” 1323, “Th.” 65, “Ec.” 366]]; παντοίᾳ τ. [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Ajax” 752, etc.; οὐκ ἀποστήσομαι.. οὔτε τ. οὔτε μηχανῇ οὐδεμιᾷ “IG” 12.39.22; πάσῃ τ. καὶ μηχανῇ 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 4.5.16; μήτε τ. μήτε μηχανῇ μηδεμιᾷ 5th c.BC: Lysias Orator 13.95.]]

__II
an art, craft, πᾶσαι τέχναι βροτοῖσιν ἐκ Προμηθέως [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Prometheus Vinctus” 506, compare “IG” 12.678]]; τὴν τ. ἐπίστασθαι to know the craft, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 3.130; φλαύρως ἔχειν τὴν τ. [prev. passage]; τῆς τ. ἔμπειρος 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Ranae” 811]]; ταύτην τέχνην ἔχει he makes this his trade, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Lysias Orator 1.16, compare 6.7]]; ἐν τῇ τ. εἶναι practise it, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Tyrannus” 562, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Protagoras” 317c]]; ἐπὶ τέχνῃ μαθεῖν τι to learn a thing professionally, opposed to ἐπὶ παιδείᾳ, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. work] 312b, compare 315a; τέχναι καὶ ἐργασίαι 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Memorabilia” 3.10.1]]; τέχνην τὸ πρᾶγμα πεποιημένοι having made a trade of it, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 37.53]]; τέχνας ἀσκεῖν, μελετᾶν, ἐργάζεσθαι, to practise them,[Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 1.6.26, 41 (_passive_), “Oec.” 4.3; πατρῴαν τέχναν ἐργάζεσθαι ἁλιεύεσθαι Πρακτικὰ Ἀρχ. Ἑτ. 1932.52 (Dodona, 4th c.BC)]]; ἰατρὸς τὴν τ. [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [“POxy.” 40.5 (2nd c.AD)]]; τεθεραπευκὼς ἀνεγκλήτως τῇ τ., of a barber, [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [“PEnteux.” 47.3 (3rd c.BC)]]; παραμενῶ πρὸς ὑπηρεσίαν τῆς τ. (i.e.  weaving) [Refs 3rd c.AD+ [“Sammelb.” 7358.20 (3rd c.AD)]]; ἀπὸ τεχνῶν τρέφεσθαι live by them, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Respublica Lacedaemoniorum” 7.1.]]

__III
an art or craft, i.e. a set of rules, system or method of making or doing, whether of the useful arts, or of the fine arts, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Epicharmus Comicus 171.11, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Phaedrus” 245a, 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Rhetorica” 1354a11, “EN” 1140a8; ἡ ἐμπειρία τέχνην ἐποίησεν, ἡ δ᾽ ἀπειρία τύχην Polus cited in [same work] “Metaphorical” 981a4]]; ἡ περὶ τοὺς λόγους τ. the [Refs 5th c.BC+ [“Art” of Rhetoric, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Phaedo” 90b]]; οἱ τὰς τ. τῶν λόγων συντιθέντες systems of rhetoric, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Rhetorica” 1354a12, compare 5th-6th c.BC: Isocrates Orator 13.19, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Phaedrus” 271c, 1st c.BC: Philodemus Gadarensis Epigrammaticus “Rh.” 2.50 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus, +others]]; hence title of various treatises on Rhetoric (see. VI; but rather tricks of Rhetoric, in [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aeschines Orator 1.117)]]; τέχνῃ by rules of art, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Euthydemus” 282d; ἢ φύσει ἢ τέχνῃ [prev. author] “R.” 381b; τέχνῃ καὶ ἐπιστήμῃ [prev. author] “Ion” 532c]]; ἄνευ τέχνης, μετὰ τέχνης, [Refs [[prev. author] “Phd.” 89e]]: τ. defined as ἕξις ὁδοποιητική, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-3rd c.BC: Zeno Citieus Stoicus 1.20, cf. Cleanth. [prev. work]1.110.]]

__IV
={τέχνημα}, work of art, handiwork, κρατῆρες.., ἀνδρὸς εὔχειρος τέχνη [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Coloneus” 472; ὅπλοις.., Ἡφαίστου τέχνῃ [prev. author] “fragment” 156, compare 1st c.BC-1st c.AD: Strabo Geographus 14.1.14, “PLond.” 3.854.4 (2nd c.AD), 2nd c.AD: Pausanias Periegeta 6.25.1, +others]]

__V
={συντεχνία, ἡ τ. τῶν λιθουργῶν, τῶν σακκοφόρων}, Dumont-Homolle “Mélanges d' archéol. et d' épigr.” [Refs [p.378 No. 65, 66 (from Perinthus); τ. βυρσέων, συροποιῶν, “IGRom.” 1.717,1482 (both Philippopolis)]]; τοὺς καταλειπομένους ἀπὸ τῇς τ. [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [“BGU” 1572.12 (2nd c.AD)]]; ὁ χαλκεὺς ἀπὸ τῆς τ. [Refs [“SIG” 1140 (from Amphipolis).]]

__VI
treatise on Grammar, [Refs 2nd c.BC+ [2nd c.BC: Dionysius Thrax Grammaticus at Title Page, or on Rhetoric, Anaximenes Lampsacenus at Title Page]]

τεχνῑτ-ης, ου, ὁ,
artificer, craftsman, opposed to γεωργός, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Oeconomicus” 6.6, 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Politica” 1262b26, +others]]; opposed to ῥήτωρ, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Empedocles Poeta Philosophus cited in 4th-3rd c.BC: Theophrastus Philosophus “de Sensu” 11]]; of a potter, [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [“PCair.Zen.” 500.2, 3 (3rd c.BC)]]; τεχνῖται οἱ χρήσιμόν τι ποιεῖν ἐπιστάμενοι, opposed to οἱ ἐλευθερίως πεπαιδευμένοι, [NT+5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Memorabilia” 2.7.4, 5, cf. Delph., 3rd c.BC), “CIG” “Corpus Inscriptionum Graecarum” “Corpus Inscriptionum Graecarum” 2619, +others (from Cyprus), “OGI” 50 (Egypt, 3rd c.BC), 2nd c.BC: Polybius Historicus 16.21.8, 2nd-1st c.BC: Posidonius Historicus 36 1st c.AD: Josephus Historicus, etc.]]; so perhaps in οἷος τ. παραπόλλυμαι, = Latin qualis artifex pereo (Nero's last words), [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd-3rd c.AD: Dio Cassius Historicus 63.29.]]

LSJ / STEPBible (TFLSJ)
τήκω,
[Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Fragmenta - American Journal of Philology” 300.5, etc.]], Doric dialect τάκω [ᾱ] [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Electra” 123 (Lyric poetry), 3rd c.BC: Theocritus Poeta Bucolicus 2.28]]: future τήξω [Refs 5th c.BC+ [“Anthologia Graeca” 5.277 (6th c.AD: Agathias Historicus et Epigrammaticus), (συν-) 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Iphigenia Aulidensis” 398 (troch.)]]; Doric dialect 2nd pers. singular ταξεῖς (κατα-) [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [3rd c.BC: Theocritus Poeta Bucolicus “Epigrammata” 6.1]]: aorist ἔτηξα [Refs 8th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 3.96, (κατ-) 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 19.206, etc.:]]perfect τέτηκα, in intransitive sense, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 3.176, etc.]]; Doric dialect τέτᾱκα [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Supplices” 1141 (Lyric poetry), (προσ-) 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Trachiniae” 836 (Lyric poetry)]]: pluperfect ἐτετήκειν [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 4.5.15:]] — middle, future τήξομαι (but in passive sense) [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Hippocrates Medicus “περὶ φυσῶν” 12]]: aorist ἐτηξάμην [Refs 2nd c.BC+ [2nd c.BC: Nicander Epicus “Alexipharmaca” 63, 164, 350]]:—passive, future τᾰκήσομαι [LXX+1st c.AD+ [LXX.Lev.26.39, +others, “Anacreontea” 10.16, (συν-) 1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus 2.752e:]]aorist ἐτάκην [ᾰ] [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Helena” 3, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Phaedrus” 251b, “Ti.” 83a]]; frequently in compounds ἐξ-, ἐν-, συν-; rarely ἐτήχθην, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Hippocrates Medicus “περὶ νούσων” 4.57, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Timaeus” 61b]], once in Trag., συντηχθείς [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Supplices” 1029 (Lyric poetry)]]: perfect τέτηγμαι [Refs 1st c.AD+ [1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus 2.106d, “Anthologia Graeca” 5.272 (6th c.AD: Agathias Historicus et Epigrammaticus)]]; but in early Gr. the perfect and pluperfect passive are supplied by the intransitive active perfect and pluperfect τέτηκα, ἐτετήκειν (see. above).

__I

__I.2
metaphorically, dissolve, cause to waste or pine away, μὴ θυμὸν τῆκε let it not melt or pine away, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 19.264]]; τίν᾽ αεὶ τάκεις ὧδ᾽ ἀκόρετον οἰμωγὰν τὸν Ἀγαμέμνον; (i.e. τί ὧδε τήκει οἰμώζουσα τὸν Ἀγ.;) [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Electra” 123 (Lyric poetry); τ. βιοτάν 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Medea” 141 (_anapaest meter_); σῶμα 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 609c]]; τ. καὶ λείβει [τὸ θυμοειδές[Refs [] [prev. work] 411b; τ. ἧπαρ Callias Epigrammaticus “Aet.Oxy.” 2079.8]]; διαφορεῖν καὶ τ. [σάρκα] carry off and reduce superfluous flesh, [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd c.AD: Galenus Medicus 6.96, compare  Vict. _Attic dialect_ 1; ἡ ταχεῖα κίνησις τὴν θερμασίαν ἐπὶ πλέον αὐξάνουσα τήκει τὸ σῶμα [prev. author] 15.191; ἔρωτες τήξουσιν κραδίην “Anthologia Graeca” 5.277 (6th c.AD: Agathias Historicus et Epigrammaticus).]]

__II
passive, with intransitive perfect active τέτηκα, melt, be dissolved, melt away, of snow, thaw, χιὼν τηκομένη [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 19.207; ῥέειν ἀπὸ τηκομένης χιόνος 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 2.22; λευκῆς τακείσης χιόνος 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Helena” 3; ἡνίκ᾽ ἂν τακῇ χιών [prev. author] “fragment” 228.4; τὴν χιόνα τετηκέναι 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 4.5.15]]; of metals, ἐτήκετο κασσίτερος ὥς [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th-7th c.BC: Hesiodus Epicus “Theogonia” 862; σίδηρος.. πυρὶ κηλέῳ τήκεται [prev. work] 866]]; also τετηκότα (i.e. κρέα) sodden flesh, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Cyclops” 246]]; ἄλφιτα πυρὶ τ. is consumed, [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [3rd c.BC: Theocritus Poeta Bucolicus 2.18]]; τήκεται κοιλίη, merely, is relaxed, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Hippocrates Medicus]]“Aër.” 7; of putrefying flesh, fall away, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Timaeus” 82e]]; of a corpse, κατθανὼν ἐτήκετο [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Antigone” 906]]; κηκὶς μηρίων ἐτήκετο[Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. work] 1008; πυρὸς τετακότας σποδῷ 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Supplices” 1141 (Lyric poetry)]]; εἰς τοῦτο τετηκυῖα resolved into.., [NT+5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Timaeus” 85d; στοιχεῖα καυσούμενα τήκεται NT.2Pet.3.12]]; of fat, τακείσης πιμελῆς [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd c.AD: Galenus Medicus 6.192, compare 18(2)]].140; of food in the digestive organs, τήκεται μὲν ἡ πρότερον ῥηθεῖσα [πτισάνη], ἡ δ᾽ ἑτέρα δύστηκτός ἐστι [Refs [[prev. author] 6.784.]]

__II.2
metaphorically, melt or waste away, pine, κλαίουσα τέτηκα [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 3.176; τήκετο χρώς 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 19.204]]; τήκετο καλὰ παρήϊα δάκρυ χεούσης[Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. work] 208; ἐν νούσῳ.. δηρὸν τηκόμενος 5.396; τ. νούσῳ 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 3.99, compare 3rd c.BC: Theocritus Poeta Bucolicus 1.66, 82, etc.]]; Ὀδυσσεὺς τήκετο was moved to tears, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 8.522; κλαίω, τέτηκα 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Electra” 283; μὴ λίαν τάκου 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Medea” 159 (Lyric poetry); ψυχὴν ἐτήκου [prev. author] “Heracl.” 645, compare “El.” 208 (Lyric poetry); ἐτάκευ βασκαίνων 3rd c.BC: Theocritus Poeta Bucolicus 5.12; τὸ κάλλος ἐτάκετο [prev. author] 2.83]]; come to naught, δόξαι.. τακόμεναι κατὰ γᾶν μινύθουσιν [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Eumenides” 374 (Lyric poetry)]]; ἐπί τινι τακείς consumed for love of.., [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [“Anthologia Graeca” 7.31 (3rd c.BC: Dioscorides Epigrammaticus), compare 2nd c.AD: Lucianus Sophista “DMeretr.” 12.1]]; βλέμμα τηκόμενον a languishing look, [Refs 1st c.AD+ [1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus “Antonius” 53]]. (Cf. Latin τᾱβες, O[Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus]] pawian 'thaw', Slavonic tajati 'melt'.)

Included with:  τηλαυγ-ής, ές,

of distant objects, far-seen, conspicuous, σκοπιή [Refs 6th c.BC+ [6th c.BC: Theognis Elegiacus 550; κορυφά 5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “Pae.” 7.12; φᾶρος 5th c.BC: Bacchylides Lyricus 16.5; ὄχθος 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Trachiniae” 524 (Lyric poetry)]]; of leprosy, [LXX.Lev.13.4, +others]

deep_entry:
Abbott-Smith / STEPBible (TBESG)
τηλικοῦτος, -αύτη, -οῦτο
(altern. of τηλικόσδε, -ήδε, -όνδε, strength­ened form of τηλίκος), [in LXX: 2Ma.12:3, 3Ma.3:9, 4Ma.16:4 * ;]
__1. of persons,
__(a) of such an age, so old;
__(b) so young.
__2. Of things, so great: 2Co.1:10, Heb.2:3, Jas.3:4, Rev.16:18.†

LSJ / STEPBible (TFLSJ)
τηλῐκόσδε, ήδε, όνδε,
and τηλῐκοῦτος, αύτη, οῦτον (also τηλικοῦτος as feminine, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Coloneus” 751, “El.” 614]]; and -οῦτο in neuter, [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd c.AD: Alexander Rhetor 244)]], strengthened forms of τηλίκος (as ὅδε, οὗτος of ὁ, τημοῦτος of τῆμος,

__A
see at {οὗτος} A); the latter being more common in Prose:

__A.I
of persons, of such an age, usually meaning so old, with a participle, τηλικόσδ᾽ ὤν [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Alcestis” 643, compare 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Apologia” 34e, etc.; γεγῶσα τηλικήδ᾽ ὅμως 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Fragmenta” 533; τηλικοῦτος ὤν 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Equites” 881, 4th c.BC: Antiphanes Comicus 261, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Gorgias” 489b, etc.: without]]participle, τηλικόσδε, τηλικοῦτος, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Coloneus” 735, “El.” 614]]; νοῦς τηλικοῦτος the mind of one so old as he is, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. author] “Ant.” 767; τηλικῷδε ἀνθρώπῳ 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Apologia” 37d: pleonastic, τηλικοίδε γέροντες ἄνδρες [prev. author] “Cri.” 49a (assuming variant): with _Article_, διδάσκεσθαι βαρὺ τῷ τηλικούτῳ 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Agamemnon” 1620, see below 3.]]

__A.I.2
of degrees of youth, so young, τηλικάσδ᾽ ὁρῶν πάντων ἐρήμους girls of so tender age, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Tyrannus” 1508, compare “OC” 1116]]; ἀεί σε κηδεύουσα.. τηλικοῦτος[Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. work] 751; ὃν εἰ τηλικοῦτον ὄντα ἀπεκτείνατε.. 5th c.BC: Lysias Orator 14.16, compare 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 378d, “Prt.” 361e.]]

__A.I.3
repeated in opposed to senses, οἱ τηλικοίδε καὶ διδαξόμεσθα δὴ φρονεῖν ὑπ᾽ ἀνδρὸς τηλικοῦδε τὴν φύσι; shall we old as we are take lessons forsooth from one so young? [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Antigone” 726]]; σὺ ἐμοῦ σοφώτερος εἶ τηλικούτου ὄντος τηλικόσδε ὤν you though so young are wiser than I though so old, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Apologia” 25d.]]

__A.II
so great, so large, ={τόσος, τοσόσδε, ἐμὲ τηλικόνδε ὄντα} the size I am, [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [[prev. author] “Tht.” 155b; τ. κακά 3rd c.BC: Lycophron Tragicus 819, compare 2nd c.AD: Athenaeus Epigrammaticus 9.380d]]; τὰ τ. [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Axiochus” 370c: mostly in the stronger form, ἡ τηλικαύτη [πόλις] [prev. author] “R.” 423b]]; ἀνὴρ τ. ὤν being so great, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Historia Graeca (Hellenica)” 6.4.31]]; ἡ τ. ἀρχή, τ. ἔχθρα, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Leges” 755b, 928e]]; τ. κακά, τ. ἀγαθόν, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Memorabilia” 2.1.5, 4.4.8]]; τ. [ἀδικήματα] [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 18.13; τ. τιμωρίαι 4th c.BC: Aeschines Orator 1.173; πεπραγμένα τ. τὸ μέγεθος 5th-6th c.BC: Isocrates Orator 5.151, compare 98; τηλικαύτην βλάβην “PCair.Zen.” 378.11 (3rd c.BC):]] —τηλικοῦτος is frequently conjoined with τοιοῦτος and τοσοῦτος, νησύδρια τοιαῦτα καὶ τ. so small, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Isocrates Orator 12.70; τ. καὶ τοιοῦτον σύστημα 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Leges” 686b; τ. καὶ τοσοῦτος θεός [prev. author] “Smp.” 177a; τοσοῦτοι καὶ τ. θόρυβοι 4th c.BC: Aeschines Orator 1.174; τ. καὶ τοσαῦτ᾽ ἀγαθά 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 19.24; οἱ τ. καὶ τοιοῦτοι τῷ γένει 4th-3rd c.BC: Menander Comicus “Ἐπιτρέποντες” 120.]]

deep_entry:
Abbott-Smith / STEPBible (TBESG)
τηρέω, -ῶ
[in LXX for שָׁמַר, נָצַר, etc. ;]
__1. to watch over, guard, keep, preserve: Mat.27:36, Act.16:23, al.; ἑαυτόν, 2Co.11:9, 1Ti.5:22, Jas.1:27, Ju 21; before εἰς, Jhn.12:7, Act.25:21, 1Pe.1:4, 2Pe.2:4 2:9 3:7, Ju 6; ἐν, Jhn.17:11-12, Ju 21; ἐκ, Jhn.17:15, Rev.3:10; τ. πίστιν, 2Ti.4:7, Rev.14:12; τ. ἑνότητα τ. πνεύματος, Eph.4:3.
__2. to watch, give heed to, observe: τ. σάββατον, Jhn.9:16; τ. ἐντολήν (-άς), Mat.19:17, Jhn.14:15 15:10, 1Ti.6:14, 1Jn.2:3-4 Jn 3:22 Jn 3:24 Jn 5:3, Rev.12:17 14:12; τ. λόγον (-ους), Jhn.8:51-52, 55 14:23-24 15:20 17:6, 1Jn.2:5, Rev.3:8, 10 22:7, 9; τ. νόμον, Act.15:5, Jas.2:10; τ. παράδοσιν, Mrk.7:9; τ. ἔργα, Rev.2:26; τ. γεγραμμένα, Rev.1:3 (cf. δια-, παρα-, συν-τηρέω)
SYN.: φυλάσσω, implying custody and protection: τ. expresses the idea of watchful care and "may mark the result of which φ. is the means" (Thayer see word)  (AS)

---

LSJ / STEPBible (TFLSJ)
τηρ-έω
(τη- also in Doric dialect, [Refs 7th c.BC+ [7th c.BC: Alcman Lyricus 23.77, 5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “P.” 2.88, compare διατηρέω)]], perfect τετήρηκα [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-3rd c.BC: Epicurus Philosophus “Sententiae” 24, etc.]]:—watch over, take care of, guard, δώματα [Refs 5th c.BC+ [“hymnus ad Cererem” 142; πόλιν 5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus [same place], compare 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Vespae” 210; τὰς κύνας 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Cynegeticus” 6.1; τὴν ἀσφάλειαν τῆς ἐπιβουλῆς 5th c.BC: Antipho Orator 2.2.8]]; rarely of persons, δαιμόνων.., αἵτινες τηροῦμεν ὑμᾶς [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Nubes” 579 (troch.)]]; τ. τὴν ἀρχήν maintain it, [Refs 2nd c.BC+ [2nd c.BC: Polybius Historicus 21.32.2; τὸ τῆς πόλεως ἀξίωμα 1st c.BC: Diodorus Siculus Historicus 17.15:]] —passive, τὸ ἔξωθεν [τεῖχος] ἐτηρεῖτο was constantly guarded, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 2.13:]]future middle τηρήσομαι in passive sense, [Refs [[prev. author] 4.30.]]

__2
τ. ὅπως.. ἔσται take care that.. , [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Politica” 1309b16; ὅπως μηθὲν παρανομῶσι [prev. work] 1307b31]]; τ. μὴ.. cavere ne.. , [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Thesmophoriazusae” 580, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Theaetetus” 169c; τ. ἐμέ, ὅπως μὴ ἐξαπατήσω 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 18.276]]: also in middle, τηρώμεσθ᾽, ὅπως μὴ.. αἰσθήσεται [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Vespae” 372; τηροῦ μὴ λάβῃς ὑπώπια [prev. work] 1386.]]

__3
τηρεῖν ἀπὸ τοῦ πυρός protect them from the fire, i.e. cook them slowly, Bilabel Ὀψαρτ.[Refs [P.  10.]]

__II
give heed to, watch narrowly, observe, τηρῶ αὐτοὺς οὐδὲ δοκῶν ὁρᾶν κλέπτοντας [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Equites” 1145, compare “V.” 364; τὰς ἁμαρτίας 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 4.60; ἐκεῖνο τ. μὴ.. 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Pax” 146, compare 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 442a; τ. ὅ τι καὶ δράσει 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Ecclesiazusae” 946.]]

__II.2
watch for a person or thing, with a participle, παραστείχοντα τηρήσας [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Tyrannus” 808]]; ἔνδον ὄντα τηρήσαντες αὐτόν having watched for his being within, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 1.134]]; τ. τὸν πορθμὸν κατιόντος τοῦ ἀνέμου watching for a crossing with the wind blowing down, [Refs [[prev. author] 6.2]]; τ. τινὰ ἀνιόντα watch for one's coming up, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 53.17: with _accusative_ only, ἄνεμον τηρῆσαι 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 1.65; τ. νύκτα χειμέριον [prev. author] 3.22, compare 4.27]]; νύκτα καὶ ὕδωρ, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 59.103; τ. τοὺς ἀστέρας 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “de Caelo” 292a8]]; τὴν θήραν τ. [Refs [[prev. author] “HA” 623a13; τ. καιρόν [prev. author] “Rh.” 1382b10:]] —passive, ὁ καιρὸς ἐτηρήθη was watched for, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Lysias Orator 12.71.]]

__II.3
absolutely, watch, keep watch, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 7.80, 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Ethica Nicomachea” 1167b13]]: with infinitive, watch or look out, so as to.., ἐτήρουν ἀνέμῳ καταφέρεσθαι [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 4.26.]]

__II.4
observe, notice, [μετακόσμησιν σωμάτων] [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd c.AD: Soranus Medicus 1.41; τὸν χαρακτῆρα τῆς φράσεως [prev. author] “Vit. Hippocr.” 13; τὸ πολὺ μὲν οὕτως ἀποβαίνειν τετήρηται 2nd c.AD: Galenus Medicus 18(2).13.]]

__II.5
test by observation or trial, τετηρημένον βοήθημα an approved method of treatment, [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd c.AD: Antyllus Medicus cited in 4th c.AD: Oribasius Medicus 6.22.3; τετήρηνται χρησιμεύοντές τισι [prev. author][prev. work] 21.9]]; as Empiric term, τετηρημένης ἐπ᾽ αὐτοῖς τῆς θεραπείας, οὐκ ἐνδεικτικῶς εὑρισκομένης [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd c.AD: Galenus Medicus 6.361; Μηνόδοτος ὁ ἐμπειρικός, ἐπὶ μόνῃ τῇ πληθωρικῇ καλουμένῃ συνδρομῇ φάσκων τετηρῆσθαι φλεβοτομίαν [prev. author] 15.766.]]

__III
observe or keep an engagement, ὅρκους [NT+5th c.BC+ [3rd c.AD: Democritus Epigrammaticus 239; παρακαταθήκας 5th-6th c.BC: Isocrates Orator 1.22; ἀπόρρητα 5th c.BC: Lysias Orator 31.31; εἰρήνην 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 18.89; τὸ πρέπον 1st c.BC: Philodemus Philosophus “περὶ ποιημάτων” 5.35; τὴν πίστιν NT.2Tim.4.7.]]

preserve, retain, τὰς αἰσθήσεις uncertain in [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th-3rd c.BC: Epicurus Philosophus “Epistulae” 1p.5U., compare 2nd c.BC: Demetrius Lacon Philosophus “Herc.” 1055.9,10; ἰδιότητας 1st c.BC: Philodemus Gadarensis Epigrammaticus “Rh.” 1.154 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus; τὴν ποιότητα 2nd c.AD: Soranus Medicus 1.51; τὴν τροφὸν ἐπ᾽ ὀλιγοποσίας.. τ. Abbott-Smith / STEPBible (TBESG)
τίθημι,
[in LXX for שִׁית ,נתן ,שׂוּם, etc. ;]
__1. causative of κεῖμαι,
__(a) to place, lay, set: Luk.6:48, Rom.9:33, al.; of laying the dead to rest, Mrk.15:47, Luk.23:55, Jhn.11:34, Act.7:16, al.; before ἐπί, with genitive, Luk.8:16, Jhn.19:19, al.; id. with accusative, Mrk.4:21, 2Co.3:13, al.; ὑπό, Mat.5:15, al.; παρά, Act.4:35, 37. Mid., to have put or placed, to place for oneself: of putting in prison, Act.4:3, 5:18, 25, al.; of giving counsel, βουλήν, Act.27:12; of laying up in one's heart, Luk.1:66 21:14 ( 1Ki.21:12);
__(b) to put down, lay down: of bending the knees, τ. γόνατα, to kneel, Mrk.15:19, Act.7:60, al.; of putting off garments, Jhn.13:4; of laying down life, τ. ψυχήν, Jhn.10:11, 15 17, 18 13:37, 38 15:13, 1Jn.3:16; of laying by money, παρ ̓ ἑαυτῷ, 1Co.16:2; of setting on food, Jhn.2:10; metaphorically, of setting forth an idea in symbolism, Mrk.4:30.
__2. to set, fix, establish: ὑπόδειγμα, 2Pe.2:6.
__3. to make, appoint: Mat.22:44, Mrk.12:36, Luk.20:43, Act.2:35, Rom.4:17, al. Mid., to make, set or appoint for oneself: Act.20:28, 1Co.12:28, 1Th.5:9, 1Ti.1:12, al.; before ἵνα, Jhn.15:16 (cf . ἀνα-, προσ-ανα-, ἀπο-, δια-, ἀντι-δια-, ἐκ-, ἐπι-, συν-επι-, κατα-, συν-κατα-, μετα-, παρα-, περι-, προ-, προσ-, συν-, ὑπο-τίθημι).
(AS)

τὰ πάντα ὅπως ἂν αὐτῇ ἡδὺ ᾖ οὕτως τίθεσθαι 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Memorabilia” 1.4.17; εἰ μὴ θήσομαι τἄμ᾽ ὡς ἄριστα 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Andromache” 378; τὸ σαυτοῦ θέμενος εὖ [prev. author] “IT” 1003, compare “Ba.” 49, “HF” 605, 938, “Hipp.” 709, 5th c.BC: Dionysius Chalcus Elegiacus 1.5; τὰ πρὶν εὖ θέμενος 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Electra” 1434]]; συνετῶν ἀνδρῶν (i.e. εἶναι), πρὶν γενέσθαι τὰ δυσχερῆ, προνοῆσαι ὅπως μὴ γένηται· ἀνδρείων δέ, γενόμενα εὖ θέσθαι [Refs 6th c.BC+ [6th c.BC: Pittacus Lyricus cited in 3rd c.AD(?): Diogenes Laertius 1.78]]; τὸ κοινῶς φοβερὸν ἅπαντας εὖ θέσθαι that all should face the common danger, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 4.61]]; of wars, quarrels, etc., bring them to a successful issue, but sometimes put a good face on them, patch them up, ἕως ἂν τὸν πόλεμον εὖ θῶνται [Refs [[prev. author] 8.84; θήσονται τὸν πόλεμον ᾗ βούλονται [prev. author] 1.31]]; πόλεμον ἀραμένους οὐ ῥᾴδιον εὐπρεπῶς θέσθαι[Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. work] 82; ὅτῳ τρόπῳ.. τὸ σφέτερον ἀπρεπὲς εὖ θήσονται [prev. author] 6.11; μεθ᾽ ἧς τὸ νῦν παρεστὸς νεῖκος εὖ θέσθαι χρεών 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Tyrannus” 633; τὸν τρὸς τοὺς Ἐλευσῖνι πόλεμον ὡς μετρίως ἔθεντο 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Menexenus” 243e]]; ἄμεινον ἢ τότε ἐθέμεθα τὸν πόλεμον[Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. work] 245e; τὰς γενομένας συμφορὰς πρὸς ἀλλήλους θέσθαι καλῶς 5th-6th c.BC: Andocides Orator 1.140: _absolutely_, θέσθαι καλῶς 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Fragmenta” 350:—_passive_, εἰ τεθήσεται κατὰ νοῦν τὰ πράγματα 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 4.120.]]

__A.VII.2
in the game of πεττεία, κυβεία, Latin tesserae (compare [Refs [Ter. “Adelph.” 739)]], to place as skilfully as possible the pieces which have been assigned to one by the luck of the dice, πεττείᾳ τινὶ ἔοικεν ὁ βίος, καὶ δεῖ ὥσπερ ψῆφόν τινα τίθεσθαι τὸ συμβαῖνον [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-4th c.BC: Socratis et Socraticorum Epistulae cited in 5th c.AD: Stobaeus, Joannes 4.56.39; ὥσπερ ἐν πτώσει κύβων πρὸς τὰ πεπτωκότα τίθεσθαι τὰ αὑτοῦ πράγματα ὅπῃ ὁ λόγος αἱρεῖ βέλτιστ᾽ ἂν ἔχειν 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 604c, compare 1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus “Pyrrhus” 26; στέργειν δὲ τἀκπεσόντα καὶ θέσθαι πρέπει σοφὸν κυβευτήν 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Fragmenta” 947]]; τὰ δεσποτῶν γὰρ εὖ πεσόντα θήσομαι I will take advantage of my master's good luck, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Agamemnon” 32]]: many of the passages cited in [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus v11. I may be _metaphorically_ applications of this sense.]]

__B
put in a certain state or condition, much the same as ποιεῖν, ποιεῖσθαι, and so often to be rendered by our make:

__B.I
followed by an attributive substantive, make one something, with the predicate in apposition, θεῖναί τινα αἰχμητήν, ἱέρειαν, μάντιν, etc., [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 1.290, 6.300, 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 15.253, etc.; θ. τινὰ ἀρχέπολιν 5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “P.” 9.54]]; θεῖναί τινα ἄλοχόν τινος make her another's wife, of a third person who negotiates a marriage, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 19.298 (for _middle_, see below 3)]]; ἥτε με τοῖον ἔθηκεν ὅπως ἐθέλει who has made me such as she will, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 16.208]]; σῦς ἔθηκας ἑταίρους thou hast made my comrades swine,[LXX+8th c.BC+ [10.338; so [νῆα] λᾶαν ἔθηκε 13.163, compare 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 2.319, etc.; ἕως ἂν θῶ τοὺς ἐχθρούς σου ὑποπόδιον LXX.Psa.109(110).1]]; but γέλων ἔθηκε συνδείπνοις caused them laughter, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Ion” 1172]]; λόγους εἰς μέτρα τ. put them into verse, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Leges” 669d.]]

__B.I.2
with an  adjective for the attributive, θεῖναί τινα ἀθάνατον καὶ ἀγήρων make him undying and undecaying, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 5.136]]; πηρόν, τυφλόν, ἀφνειὸν τ. τινά, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 2.599, 6.139, 9.483; τὸν μὲν.. θῆκε μείζονά τ᾽ εἰσιδέειν καὶ πάσσονα 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 6.229, compare 18.195, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Protagoras” 344d.]]

__B.I.2.b
of things, ἅλιον πόνον, πόνον οὐκ ἀτέλεστον, πάντα μεταμώνια, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 4.26, 57, 363; ὄλεθρον ἀπευθέα θῆκε Κρονίων 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 3.88, compare 11.274; ἀποίητον θέμεν ἔργων τέλος 5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “O.” 2.17; ἀρὰν τ. ἀλαθῆ 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Septem contra Thebas” 944 (Lyric poetry)]]; ἀναστάτους οἴκους τ. [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Antigone” 674; τ. λεῖον τὸν τραχὺν ἐχῖνον 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Pax” 1086]]; τὸ πραχθὲν ἀγένητον τ. [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Protagoras” 324b.]]

__B.I.3
frequently in middle, γυναῖκα or ἄκοιτιν θέσθαι τινά make her one's wife, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 21.72, 316, 5th c.BC: Bacchylides Lyricus 5.169]]; παῖδα τὸν αὑτᾶς πόσιν θ. take her own son as husband, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Septem contra Thebas” 929 (Lyric poetry).]]

__B.I.3.b
υἱὸν θέσθαι τινά, like{ποιεῖσθαι}, make one's son, adopt, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Leges” 929c, etc.: _absolutely_, θέσθαι τινά]] adopt, [Refs 1st c.AD+ [1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus “Aemilius Paulus” 5.]]

__B.I.3.c
generally, προσφιλῆ θέσθαι τινά [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Philoctetes” 532]]; but φίλον ἐμαυτῷ θ. deem my friend, [Refs [[prev. author] “Ant.” 188]]; γέλωτα θέσθαι τινά make him one's butt, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 3.29, 7.209.]]

__B.I.4
with infinitive, make one do so and so, τιθέναι τινὰ νικᾶσαι make him conquer, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “N.” 10.48 (uncertain); μετατραπεῖν [prev. author] “fragment” 177; τὸν πάθει μάθος θέντα κυρίως ἔχειν 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Agamemnon” 178 (Lyric poetry), compare 1036, 1174 (Lyric poetry), 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Medea” 718, “Heracl.” 990, etc.]]

__B.II
in reference to mental action, when middle is more frequently than active, lay down. assume, hold, reckon or regard as.. , τί δ᾽ ἐλέγχεα ταῦτα τίθεσθ; [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 21.333; δαιμόνιον αὐτὸ τίθημ᾽ ἐγώ 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Electra” 1270 (Lyric poetry); τοιοῦτον θέντες τὸν δίκαιον 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 361b, compare 430b (_middle_)]]; θὲς δή μοι.. now suppose so and so, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. author] “Tht.” 191c; εὐεργέτημά τι θεῖναι 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 1.10; with ὡς, θέντες ὡς ὑπάρχον εἶναι ὃ βούλονται 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 458a, compare “Phd.” 100a; μὴ τοῦτο ὡς ἀδίκημα θῇς 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 18.193.]]

__B.II.2
followed by adverbs, ποῦ χρὴ τίθεσθαι ταῦτ; in what light must we regard these things? [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Philoctetes” 451]]; οὐδαμοῦ τιθέναι τι hold of no account, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Andromache” 210]]; πρόσθεν or ἐπίπροσθέν τινος τιθέναι τι, [Refs [[prev. author] “Hec.” 129 (_anapaest meter_), “Supp.” 515]]; πόρρω τίθεσθαί τί τινων set far below.., [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 18.299.]]

__B.II.3
followed by Preps., τ. τινὰ ἐν φιλοσόφοις [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 475d; ἐν τοῖς φίλοις 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Memorabilia” 2.4.4]]; also εἰς ὁποτέραν (of two classes) [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Sophista” 264c]]; εἰς τὸν δῆμον, εἰς τοὺς πλουσίους, [Refs 7th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Memorabilia” 4.2.39; also οὐκ ἐν λόγῳ τίθεσθαί τινα 7th c.BC: Tyrtaeus Elegiacus 12.1; ἐν τιμῇ τίθεσθαί τινα 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 3.3; ἐν αἰτίῃ τιθέναι τινά [prev. author] 8.99]]; ἐν οἰωνῷ τινι τοῦ μέλλοντος, ἐν ἐπαίνῳ, ἐν γέλωτι τίθεσθαι, [Refs 1st c.AD+ [1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus “Alexander” 31, “Cat.Ma.” 20, “TG” 17]]; θέσθαι παρ᾽ οὐδέν set at naught, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Agamemnon” 230 (Lyric poetry), 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Iphigenia Taurica” 732, compare 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Phaedrus” 252a (but ἐν οὐδενί “BGU” 1816.23 (1st c.BC), “Supp.epigram” 7.1.6 (Susa, 1st c.AD, Epist.Artabani))]]; ἐν παρέργῳ θοῦ με [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Philoctetes” 473]]; πάντα ταῦτ᾽ ἐν εὐχερεῖ ἔθου[Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. work] 876; ταῦτ᾽ ἐν αἰσχρῷ θέμενος 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Hecuba” 806; ἐν ἀδικήματι θέσθαι τι 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 1.35; ἐν ἀδικήματος μέρει τιθέναι τι 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 23.148]]; θέσθαι τὰ δίκαια ἔκ τινος estimate them by.., [Refs [[prev. author] 8.8.]]

__B.II.4
with partitive genitive, ἐμὲ θὲς τῶν πεπεισμένων put me down as one of the convinced, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 424c, compare 376e, 437b]]; τῆς ἡμετέρας ἀμελείας ἄν τις θείη might reckon it as due to our carelessness, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 1.10.]]

__B.II.5
with infinitive, οὐ τίθημ᾽ ἐγὼ ζῆν τοῦτον I hold not that he lives, count him not as living, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Antigone” 1166]]: so in middle, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Phaedo” 93c, 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 25.43,44: rarely with]]participle, θήσω ἀδικοῦντα [αὐτόν] [Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. author] 23.76, compare 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Protagoras” 343e, “Ap.” 27c.]]

__B.II.6
elliptically, lay down, assume, θῶμεν δύο εἴδη (i.e. εἶναι) [Refs [[prev. author] “Phd.” 79a, etc.]]; θήσω οὕτω (i.e. εἶναί τι) [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 23.85, compare 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Politica” 1290a30.]]

__B.II.7
affirm, opposed to αἴρω (deny), τὸ ἐπέκεινα ὄντος οὐ τόδε λέγει- οὐ γὰρ τίθησιν--the phrase 'beyond being' does not denote a 'this' (for it is not an affirmation), [Refs 3rd c.AD+ [3rd c.AD: Plotinus Philosophus 5.5.6.]]

__C
without any attributive word following, make, work, execute, of an artist, ἐν δ᾽ ἐτίθει νειόν [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 18.541, compare 550, 561, 607]]; [δόρπον] θησέμεναι [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 20.394.]]

__C.2
make, cause, bring to pass, ἔργα [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 3.321; τ. κέλαδον καὶ ἀϋτήν 9.547; ὀρυμαγδόν 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 9.235; ἔριν μετ᾽ ἀμφοτέροισιν 3.136]]; φιλότητα, ὅρκια μετ᾽ ἀμφ., [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 4.83, 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 24.546: with _dative_ _person_, σῆμα τιθεὶς Τρώεσσι 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 8.171; Ἀχαιοῖς ἄλγε᾽ ἔθηκεν 1.2, etc.; πᾶσι δ᾽ ἔθηκε πόνον 21.524, compare 15.721, 16.262; φόως ἑτάροισιν 6 6, etc.; χάρματ᾽ ἄλλοις ἔθηκεν 5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “O.” 2.99; πόλει κατασκαφὰς θέντες 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Septem contra Thebas” 47; εἰρήνην φίλοις [prev. author] “Pers.” 769; αἷμα θήσεις 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Bacchae” 837 (assuming variant).]]

__C.3
frequently in middle, make or prepare for oneself, θέσθαι κέλευθον make oneself a road, open a way, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 12.418; θέτο δῶμα 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 15.241]]; τίθεντο δὲ δαῖτα, δόρπα, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 7.475, 9.88 (but δαῖτα τίθενται]] are holding a feast, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 17.269)]]; μεγάλην ἐπιγουνίδα θέσθαι to make oneself, get a large thigh, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 17.225]]; θέσθαι μάχην engage in.. , [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 24.402; δυσμενέεσσι πόνον καὶ δῆριν ἔθεντο 17.158]]; ἱδρῶτα τίθεσθαι have an access of perspiration, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Hippocrates Medicus “περὶ εὐσχημοσύνης” 2]]; μαρτύρια θέσθαι produce as testimony, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 8.55]]; ἀνδρὸς αἰδοίου πρόσοψιν θηκάμενος putting on the aspect of a reverend man, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “P.” 4.29, compare 5th c.AD(?): Hesychius Legal icographus]] see at {θήκατ; πόνον πλέω τίθου} work thyself the more annoy, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Eumenides” 226; εὐκλεᾶ θέσθαι βίον 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Philoctetes” 1422, etc.]]

__C.4
periphrastic for a single Verb. μνηστήρων σκέδασιν θεῖναι make a scattering, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 1.116]]; θέμεν κρυφόν, νέμεσιν, αἶνον, for κρύπτειν, νεμεσῦν, αἰνεῖν, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “O.” 2.97, 8.86, “N.” 1.5; μὴ σχολὴν τίθει 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Agamemnon” 1059]]; ὑμῖν ἔθηκε σὺν θεοῖς σωτηρίαν (variant{προμηθίαν}) [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Medea” 915:]] — also in middle, θέσθαι μάχην, for μάχεσθαι, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 24.402]]; θέσθαι θυσίαν, γάμον, for θύειν, γαμεῖσθαι, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “O.” 7.42, 13.53]]; σπουδήν, πρόνοιαν θέσθαι, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Ajax” 13, 536, compare 5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “P.” 4.276; θ. ἐπιστροφὴν πρό τινος 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Tyrannus” 134; περὶ τούτων οἰκονομίας “PEnteux.” 22.6 (3rd c.BC)]]; and with genitive, θ. λησμοσύναν, συγγνωμοσύνην τινῶν, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Antigone” 151 (Lyric poetry), “Tr.” 1265 (_anapaest meter_)]]. (Cf. Lithuanian dēti 'lay (eggs, etc.)', Sanskrit dáti 'lay down, place', Latin -do in con-do, etc., Engl. do, doom.)

τίκτω
[in LXX chiefly for יָלַד ;]
prop., of parents,
to beget, bring forth, but esp. the latter, and so always in NT: absol., Luk.1:57 2:6, Jhn.16:21, Gal.4:27" (LXX) (see M, Pr., 127), Rev.12:2, 4; υἱόν, Mat.1:21, 23 1:25 Luk.1:31 2:7, Rev.12:5, 13; pass., Mat.2:2, Luk.2:11. Metaphorical, of the earth, βοτάνην, Heb.6:7 (Æsch., al.); of lust, ἁμαρτίαν, Jas.1:15.†
(AS)

LSJ / STEPBible (TFLSJ)
τίκ-τω,
[Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 4.86, etc.]]: future τέξω [Refs 8th c.BC+ [11.249, “hymnus ad Mercurium” 493, Oracle texts cited in 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 5.92.β, 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Prometheus Vinctus” 851, 869, 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Troades” 747, 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Equites” 1037 (Oracle texts), “Th.” 509; also τέξομαι 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 19.99, 8th-7th c.BC: Hesiodus Epicus “Theogonia” 469, 898, “hymnus ad Apollinem” 101, 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Prometheus Vinctus” 768, 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 7.49, 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Lysistrata” 744, etc.]]; poetry infinitive also τεκεῖσθαι [Refs 4th c.BC+ [“hymnus ad Venerem” 127; _plural_ τεξείεσθε 4th-3rd c.BC: Aratus Epicus 124]]: aorist ἔτεκον, Epic dialect τέκον, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 1.352, 5.875]], etc.: aorist 1 ἔτεξα only late, [Refs 5th c.AD+ [5th-6th c.AD: Orphica “Hymni” 41.8 codices (for ἐντήξῃ]] is probable reading in [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Lysistrata” 553)]]: perfect τέτοκα [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th-7th c.BC: Hesiodus Epicus “Opera et Dies” 591, 5th c.BC: Hippocrates Medicus “ἀφορισμοί” 5.39, 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Pax” 757, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Comicus 64.5, 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Cynegeticus” 5.13, compare ἐντίκτω]]:—middle, in same sense as active, only in Poets, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Choephori” 127, “fragment” 44]]: future (see. above): aorist ἐτεκόμην [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Aves” 1193 (Lyric poetry)]], Epic dialect τεκόμην [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 4.59, +others]]; subjunctive τέκηαι [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [3rd c.BC: Apollonius Rhodius Epicus 1.905]]:—passive, present indicative τίκτεται [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Septem contra Thebas” 437]]; infinitive τίκτεσθαι [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd c.AD: Soranus Medicus 2.53;]]participle τικτόμενος[Refs [[prev. work] 54]]: future τεχθήσομαι [Refs 1st c.AD+ [1st c.AD: Josephus Historicus “Antiquitates Judaicae” 2.9.2, “Geoponica” 17.6.1, etc.]]: aorist ἐτέχθην [LXX+5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Hippocrates Medicus “περὶ ἐπικυήσιος” 18, Ps.- 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Fragmenta” 1132.44, LXX.Num.26.60 (variant), +others, “Geoponica” 17.6.2, etc.:]]perfect τέτεγμαι, infinitive τετέχθαι, [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd-3rd c.AD: Aelianus “De Natura Animalium - Ar.Byzantine Epit.” 2.12, 2nd c.AD: Pausanias Periegeta 3.7.7, etc.]]--These passive tenses seem not to have been used in correct Attic dialect:—bring into the world, engender; of the father, beget, of the mother, bring forth.

__I
imperfect active τίκτε, ἔτικτε, in [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Homerus Epicus]] usually of the father, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 2.628, 6.155, 206, 11.224, compare 8th-7th c.BC: Hesiodus Epicus “Fragmenta” 44 (of the mother, 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 16.180, 22.428, 24.497, 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 23.325); in 8th-7th c.BC: Hesiodus Epicus (“Frr.” 17,142)]], Lyric poetry, and Trag. the present and imperfect are also used of the mother, ἃ Θήβαν ἔτικτεν [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “O.” 6.85, compare 5th c.BC: Bacchylides Lyricus 18.50; μᾶτερ, ἅ μ᾽ ἔτικτες 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Eumenides” 321 (Lyric poetry), compare “Ag.” 763 (Lyric poetry, of Υβρις), 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Electra” 533]]; δεινὸν τὸ τίκτειν[Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. work] 770, compare 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Theaetetus” 151a, etc.; τ. καὶ γεννᾷ [prev. author] “Smp.” 206d]]; of both parents. Στάσις δὲ καὶ Κρόνος.. τίκτετον τύραννον [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Cratinus Comicus 240.]]

__I.2
aorist active τέκε, ἔτεκε, mostly of the mother, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 1.36, 352, 2.513, etc.]] (also future middle τέξεσθαι [Refs 5th c.BC+ [19.99); τεκεῖν τινά τινι 2.658, 6.22, etc.; ὑπό τινι 2.714, 728, etc.; τ. ἔκ τινος 1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus “Theseus” 20; παρά τινος 2nd c.AD: Lucianus Sophista “Alex.” 42; παρά τινι 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Electra” 62: but τέκεν]] of the father, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 13.450, 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 3.489, +others, 8th-7th c.BC: Hesiodus Epicus “Theogonia” 208, “fragment” 99.2: _metaphorically_, τῷ τεκόντι ἀρετήν 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Symposium” 212a.]]

__I.3
the aorist middle τέκετο is commonly used of the father, as [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 2.741, 6.154, +others, 8th-7th c.BC: Hesiodus Epicus “Fragmenta” 19: but τέκετο]] of the mother, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 2.742, 15.187, 22.48, 8th-7th c.BC: Hesiodus Epicus “Fragmenta” 46]]; so τῶν τεκομένων of the mother, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Choephori” 419 (Lyric poetry).]]

__I.4
the two are conjoined, ὃν τέκετο θάνατος, ἔτεκε δ᾽ αἰόλος δράκων [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Trachiniae” 834 (codices, Lyric poetry).]]

__I.5
aorist active is used in plural of both parents, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 7.55, 8.554 (οὓς Ἑκάβη ἠδὲ Πρίαμος τέκε παῖδας 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 22.234)]]; aorist middle τεκόμεσθα, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 23.61, 24.293.]]

__I.5.b
οἱ τεκόντες the parents, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Septem contra Thebas” 49, 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Tyrannus” 999, etc.]]; the Article is rarely omitted, πατέρων τε καὶ τεκόντων [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Choephori” 329 (Lyric poetry): with _genitive_, κιόντων τοῖς τεκοῦσι [prev. author] “Pers.” 245 (troch.): ὁ τεκών]] the father, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. author] “Ch.” 690, 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Coloneus” 1108]]; ἁ τεκοῦσα the mother, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Septem contra Thebas” 926 (Lyric poetry), compare “Ch.” 133, etc. (rarely ἡ τίκτουσα, 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Tyrannus” 1247, “El.” 342); in Prose, 5th c.BC: Lysias Orator 10.8]]; ἡ τ. αὐτόν his mother, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.116; ὅ τ᾽ ἐκεῖνον τεκών 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Electra” 335.]]

__I.6
frequently in in Medicine texts and other Prose, of women, τίκτουσι ῥηϊδίως [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Hippocrates Medicus “Aër.” 5,compare 2nd c.AD: Soranus Medicus 2.54, +others, 2nd c.AD: Galenus Medicus 16.670; κόρον ἔτεκε “IG” 42(1).121.5, compare 21 (Epid., 4th c.BC).]]

__II
of female animals, bear young, breed, of mares, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 16.150, 20.225]]; of cows, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th-7th c.BC: Hesiodus Epicus “Opera et Dies” 591]]; of sheep, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 4.86, etc.; τὰς τετοκυίας τοκάδας “PCair.Zen.” 292.305, compare 710.4 (3rd c.BC); ἐὰν τέκῃ ἵππος [prev. work] 635.2 (3rd c.BC)]]; of the hare, τὰ μὲν τέτοκε, τὰ δὲ τίκτει, τὰ δὲ κύει [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Cynegeticus” 5.13]]; of birds, hatch, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 2.313]]; ᾠὰ τ. lay eggs, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 2.68, 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Fragmenta” 185, 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “de Generatione Animalium” 718b23, etc.]]; of fish, spawn, [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [[prev. author] “HA” 568a16, 2nd c.AD: Galenus Medicus 6.718, etc.]]

__III
of the earth, bear, produce, ἔμπεδα μῆλα (sheep) [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 19.113; ἡ γῆ.. τίκτουσα ποίαν 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Cyclops” 333]]:—middle, γαῖαν.., ἣ τὰ πάντα τίκτεται [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Choephori” 127, compare “fragment” 44.4]]:—passive, τίκτεσθαι δὲ φόρους γᾶς.. εὐχόμεθ᾽ ἀεί [Refs [[prev. author] “Supp.” 674 (Lyric poetry).]]

__IV
metaphorically, generate, engender, produce, λέγω τὴν χώρην λιμὸν τέξεσθαι [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 7.49; ἐπειχθῆναι πρῆγμα τίκτει σφάλματα [prev. work] 10.ζ]]; of impiety, τὸ γὰρ δυσσεβὲς ἔργον μετὰ μὲν πλείονα τίκτει [NT+4th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Agamemnon” 759 (Lyric poetry), compare 763 (Lyric poetry, compare above 1.1), “Ch.” 805 (Lyric poetry); ἡ ἐπιθυμία τ. ἁμαρτίαν NT.Jam.1.15; μὴ θράσος τέκῃ φόβον 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Supplices” 498]]; of Night as the mother of Day, τῆς.. τεκούσης φῶς τόδ᾽ εὐφρόνης [Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. author] “Ag.” 279; ὃν αἰόλα νὺξ.. τίκτει.., Ἅλιον αἰτῶ 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Trachiniae” 95 (Lyric poetry): generally, τ. [νόμους] [prev. author] “OT” 870 (Lyric poetry); χάρις χάριν γάρ ἐστιν ἡ τίκτουσ᾽ ἀεί [prev. author] “Aj.” 522; τ. ἀοιδάς 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Hercules Furens” 767 (Lyric poetry); ὕδωρ δὲ πίνων οὐδὲν ἂν τέκοι σοφόν 5th c.BC: Cratinus Comicus 199; τ. ῥήματα 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Ranae” 1059 (_anapaest meter_)]]; also in Prose, νουσήματα [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Hippocrates Medicus “περὶ χυμῶν” 12; ἃ ἀεὶ τίκτει πόλεμον καὶ ἔχθραν 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 547a; πολλοὺς καὶ καλοὺς λόγους [prev. author] “Smp.” 210d; [δὰς] πῦρ τέξεται 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 7.5.23, etc.:]] —passive, τῷδε κέρδει (sic codices) κέρδος ἄλλο τίκτεται [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Septem contra Thebas” 437. (τίκτω from τί-τκ-ω reduplicate from τεκ (τέκνον, etc.).)]]
