Abbott-Smith / STEPBible (TBESG)
τίλλω
[in LXX: Est.9:3, Isa.18:7, Dan LXX 7:4 (מָרַט) * ;]
to pluck, pluck off: στάχυας, Mat.12:1, Mrk.2:23, Luk.6:1.†
(AS)

---

LSJ / STEPBible (TFLSJ)
τίλλω,
[Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 22.78, etc.:]]future τῐλῶ (ἀπο-) [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Cratinus Comicus 123, (παρα-) 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Equites” 373]]: aorist ἔτῑλα [Refs 5th c.BC+ [3rd c.BC: Theocritus Poeta Bucolicus 3.21, (ἀπ-) 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Lysistrata” 578. “fragment” 686]]: perfect τέτιλκα [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [“PCair.Zen.” 782 (b.). 121 (3rd c.BC)]]:—middle, Epic dialect imperfect τιλλέσθην [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 24.711:]]future τῐλοῦμαι (παρα-) [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-3rd c.BC: Menander Comicus 363.5]]:—passive, aorist ἐτίλθην [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Nubes” 1083: 2]]aorist ἐτίλην [ῐ[] LXX.Dan.7.4]; 3rd.pers. singular imperative τιλήτωι [Refs 3rd c.AD+ [“PFay.” 131.18 (3rd-4th c.AD)]]; participle τειλείς (i.e. τιλ-) [Refs 3rd c.AD+ [“PFlor.” 322.36 (3rd c.AD)]]: perfect τέτιλμαι [LXX+6th c.BC+ [LXX.Isa.18.7, (ἐκ-) 6th c.BC: Anacreon Lyricus 21.10, (ἀπο-) 4th c.BC: Anaxilas Comicus 22.20, (παρα-) 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Ranae” 516]]:—pluck or pull outhair, etc., πολιὰς δ᾽ ἄρ᾽ ἀνὰ τρίχας ἕλκετο χερσί, τίλλων ἐκ κεφαλῆς [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 22.78]]; τίλλε κόμην[Refs 4th c.BC+ [[prev. work] 406; τρίχας 4th-3rd c.BC: Menander Comicus “Ἐπιτρέποντες” 271, “Her.” 5; ἐρέβινθον “PCair.Zen.” 719.6 (3rd c.BC)]]; τ. στάχυας καὶ ἐσθίειν [NT+3rd c.AD+ [NT.Matt.12.1; τ. χόρτον τοῖς κτῆσι “PFlor.” 321.47 (3rd c.AD):—]]middle, Χαίτας τίλλεσθαι pluck out one's hair, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 10.567.]]

__2
with accusative of that from which the hair or feathers are plucked, τίλλειν πέλειαν, of birds of prey,[Refs 5th c.BC+ [15.527, compare 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 3.76; κίρκον εἰσορῶ.. χηλαῖς κάρα τίλλοντα 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Persae” 209]]; τίλλουσι τὴν γλαῦκα, of small birds attacking the owl, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Historia Animalium” 609a15]]; so of the cuckoo,[Refs [[prev. work] 618a29 (_passive_)]]; as a description of an idle fellow, τίλλων ἑαυτόν [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Pax” 546, compare “Ra.” 428]]; of a cook, pluck a fowl, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Eubulus Comicus 150.5, compare 1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus 2.233a; also τ. λαγών 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Fragmenta” 212]]; τ. πλάτανον pluck its leaves off, [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus “Themistocles” 18; τὸν στέφανον τῖλαί με κατ᾽ αὐτίκα λεπτὰ ποησεῖς 3rd c.BC: Theocritus Poeta Bucolicus [same place]]]; κῴδια τ. [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [“PPetr.” 2p.108 = 3p.78 (3rd c.BC)]]; also, pluck live sheep, instead of shearing, τοῖς τίλλουσιν τὰ ὑποδίφθερα (i.e. πρόβατα) [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [“PCair.Zen.” 430.3 (3rd c.BC),compare 10th c.AD: Suidas Legal icographus]] see entry {πεκτῆρες}:—passive, have one's hair plucked out, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Thesmophoriazusae” 593]]; τέφρᾳ τιλθῆναι, as a punishment of adulterers, [Refs [[prev. author] “Nu.” 1083]]; see at {παρατίλλω, τέφρα}.

__3
with accusative cognate, τίλματα τ. [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus 2.48b, compare 3rd c.BC: Herodas Mimographus 2.70.]]

__4
τ. μέλη pluck the harp-strings, play harp-tunes, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Cratinus Comicus 256 (Lyric poetry).]]

__5
pick so as to extract fibre, τετίλκασι στιππύου δέσμας σ [Refs [“PCair.Zen.” [prev. cited]]]

__6
νεφέλιον παρατεταμένον καὶ τιλλόμενον cirrous, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-3rd c.BC: Theophrastus Philosophus “de Signis Tempestatum” 43.]]

__II
since tearing the hair was a usual expression of sorrow, τίλλεσθαί τινα tear one's hair in sorrow for any one, τόν γ᾽ ἄλοχός τε φίλη καὶ πότνια μήτηρ τιλλέσθην [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 24.711: without _accusative_, τιλλόμενοι καὶ κλαίοντες 1st c.BC: Philodemus Gadarensis Epigrammaticus “Ir.” p.36 W.]]

__III
metaphorically, pluck, vex, annoy, [Refs 6th c.BC+ [6th c.BC: Anacreon Lyricus 13 B]]; στέφανον τ., ={τοὺς νόμους λυμαίνεσθαι}, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Pythagoras Philosophus cited in 3rd c.AD: Porphyrius Tyrius Philosophus “Vita Pythagorae - Porphyrii Opuscula” 42:]] —passive, ὑπὸ συκοφαντῶν τίλλεσθαι, with allusion to a bird's feathers, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Aves” 285. (Not found in _Attic dialect_ Prose.)]]

τῑμάω,
[Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 23.788, etc.]]: future τιμήσω [Refs [9.155, etc.]], Doric dialect 3rd.pers. plural τιμᾱσεῦντι [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [3rd c.BC: Theocritus Poeta Bucolicus “Epigrammata” 7.4]]: aorist ἐτίμησα [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 8.124, etc.]], Epic dialect τίμησα [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th-7th c.BC: Hesiodus Epicus “Theogonia” 399, Lyric poetry τίμᾱσα 5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “N.” 6.41, 5th c.BC: Bacchylides Lyricus 12.194]]: perfect τετίμηκα [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Lysias Orator 26.17, etc.]], Doric dialect τετίμᾱκα [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “I.” 4(3).37(55):]] —middle, future τιμήσομαι always in passive sense, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [“hymnus ad Apollinem” 485, 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Agamemnon” 581, 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Antigone” 210, 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Fragmenta” 360.49, 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 2.87, 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 8.7.15 (reading δι᾽ ἄνδρα with codices DF), “Hier.” 9.9, except in 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Apologia” 37b]], where it is used in a technical sense (see. below [Refs [111.2):]]aorist ἐτιμησάμην in senses shared by active, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 19.280, 20.129, 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 22.235, 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 3.40; in sense 111.2, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Crito” 52c]]:—passive, future τιμηθήσομαι [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 6.80, 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 19.223, “IG” 22.1182.9, etc.; τετιμήσομαι 5th c.BC: Lysias Orator 31.24 codices (τιμήσεται Cobet)]]: aorist ἐτιμήθην [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 5.5, etc.]]; Lyric poetry 3rd.pers. plural τίμᾱθεν [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “Parth.” 2.41]]: perfect τετίμημαι [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 12.310, etc.; also]]middle in technical sense, see [Refs [111.2]]:—honour, revere, reverence (in this sense the middle is used only by [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Homerus Epicus)]]; of the honour rendered to superiors, as by men to gods, by men to their elders, rulers, or guests, περὶ κῆρι θεὸν ὣς τιμήσαντο [LXX+8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 19.280, etc.; τίμα τὸν πατέρα σου LXX.Exo.20.12, +others]]; conversely of the honour bestowed by gods upon a man, μερμήριζε (i.e. Ζεὺς).., ὡς Ἀχιλῆα τιμήσῃ [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 2.4, compare 15.612, 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 3.379]]; by a father on his son, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [14.203, 8th-7th c.BC: Hesiodus Epicus “Theogonia” 532]]; by an elder brother, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 22.235 (_middle_): also in 5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus, 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus]], and Attic dialect, ἐξόχως τίμας εν [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “O.” 9.69; δαιμόνων τιμᾶν γένος 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Septem contra Thebas” 236; θεοὺς τιμῶντες 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Coloneus” 277, compare 1071 (Lyric poetry), 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 2.29; σέβεσθαι καὶ τ. τοὺς θεούς 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Memorabilia” 4.3.13; ἱλασκομένοις καὶ τιμῶσιν.. Δία Πατρώϊον “SIG” 1044.6 (Halic., 4th-3rd c.BC)]]; τὸν φίλον τιμῶσιν ἐξ ἴσου πατρί [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Antigone” 644, compare 516, 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Medea” 660 (Lyric poetry), 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 7.107, etc.; θεοὶ δ᾽ ὅταν τιμῶσιν, οὐδὲν δεῖ φίλων 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Hercules Furens” 1338: _absolutely_, οἱ τύραννοι μάλιστα δύνανται τιμᾶν]] bestow honours, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 20.15 (τιμᾶν secl. Bake),compare 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Leges” 631e]]: hence simply, reward, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 3.3.6, 5th-6th c.BC: Isocrates Orator 9.42]] (so in passive, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 7.213, 5th c.BC: Lysias Orator 12.64, 19.18)]]; ἐπαινεῖν καὶ τ., τ. καὶ δωρεῖσθαι, δωρεῖσθαί τε καὶ τ., τ. καὶ χαρίζεσθαι, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 1.2.12, 3.2.28, 8.2.10, 2.4.9: with _dative_ modi, δωτίνῃσι θεὸν ὣς τιμήσουσι]] will honour him with gifts, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 9.155; ξεῖνον ἐτιμήσασθ᾽ ἐνὶ οἴκῳ εὐνῇ καὶ σίτῳ 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 20.129]]; τιμᾶν τινα τάφῳ, γόοις, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Septem contra Thebas” 1051, “Supp.” 116 (Lyric poetry); πόλιν τ. συμμάχῳ δορί [prev. author] “Eu.” 773; ἐσθήμασι 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 3.58; χοροῖς 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Bacchae” 220; δώροις 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 1.9.14, “HG” 6.1.6; στρεπτοῖς καὶ ψελίοις τ. καὶ κοσμεῖν τινα [prev. author] “Cyr.” 1.3.3:]] —passive, mostly in perfect τετίμημαι, which alone is passive in [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Homerus Epicus]], to be honoured, held in honour, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 9.608, 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 7.69; ἐτιμήθη παρὰ Ξέρξῃ 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 8.105; ὑπό τινος 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 426c, etc.; τετίμαται πρὸς ἀθανάτων 5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “I.” 4(3).59(77); σκήπτρῳ.. δῶκε τετιμῆσθαι περὶ πάντων 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 9.38, compare 12.310; τιμᾶσθαι προεδρίαις 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “de Vectigalibus” 3.4, compare “Cyr.” 8.4.2; ἐκ τοῦ πολεμεῖν 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 5.16]]: with accusative cognate attracted to genitive, ὥς μευ ἀεὶ μέμνησαι ἐνηέος, οὐδέ σε λήθω, τιμῆς ἧς τέ μ᾽ ἔοικε τετιμῆσθαι [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 23.649 (but with _genitive_, τετειμημένος ὑπὸ τῶν αὐτοκρατόρων τετάρτης στρατείας]] (= Latin quattuor militiis) [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [Supp.epigram 7.145 (Palmyra, 2nd c.AD))]]; οἱ τετιμηυένοι men of rank, men in office, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 8.3.9]]; οἱ τιμώμενοι[Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. work] 8.8.4, compare 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Orestes” [913]]]; τῆς πόλεως τὸ τιμώμενον ἀπὸ τοῦ ἄρχειν the honour enjoyed by the city, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 2.63.]]

__II
of things, hold in honour or esteem, value, prize, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [Hymni Homerici 25.6, 5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “O.” 6.72, etc.]]; τί τὴν τυραννίδα τιμᾷς ὑπέρφε; [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Phoenissae” 550]]; νόμους τ. [Refs [[prev. author] “Tr.” 1211]]; τὴν εὐσέβειαν, ἀγνωμοσύναν, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. author] “Ion” 1046, “Ba.” 885 (Lyric poetry); ἰσότητα [prev. author] “Ph.” 536, compare 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Theaetetus” 149c; τὸ σωφρονεῖν τ. τοῦ βίου πλέον 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Supplices” 1013.]]

__II.2
with genitive pretii, estimate or value at a certain price, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Leges” 917c, 921b, “PCair.Zen.” 269.13, 15 (3rd c.BC), “UPZ” 67.3 (2nd c.BC), etc.]]; πλοῖα τετιμημένα χρημάτων [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 4.26: _absolutely_, τετιμῆσθαι ἕκαστον τὴν οὐσίαν χρεών]] that each man should have his property valued (for assessment), [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Leges” 955d, etc.; οἱ ὑπὲρ τὰς μυρίας τιμώμενοι δραχμάς 2nd c.BC: Polybius Historicus 6.23.15]]; τὸ τιμηθέν the estimate, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Leges” 954b]]:—frequently in middle, διακοσίων ταλάντων ἐτιμήσατο  αὑτοῦ estimated his property at.. , [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Lysias Orator 19.48, compare “PPetr.” 2 _intransitive_ p.33 (3rd c.BC)]]; πρὸ παντὸς τιμᾶσθαί τι, like{περὶ παντὸς ποιεῖσθαι} (see. περί [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus IV), 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 3.40, compare 1.33]]; πλείονος, μείζονος τιμᾶσθαι, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Memorabilia” 3.10.10, “Cyr.” 2.1.13; τοσούτου τ. τὴν πολιτείαν 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 22.45]]; μίαν ἡδονὴν θανάτου τ. [Refs 4th c.BC+ [1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus 2.5b: also with Preps., ἀντὶ παντὸς ἂν τιμησαίμην εἰπεῖν τοῦ βίου 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 18.214]]: without a genitive, ἐτιμήσαντο τήν τε χώραν καὶ τὰς οἰκίας [Refs 2nd c.BC+ [2nd c.BC: Polybius Historicus 2.62.7]]: simply, value, estimate, ἐν προικί [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Isaeus Orator 3.35, compare 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 47.57 (_passive_), 53.1]]; τινα [LXX+NT [LXX.Lev.27.8, NT.Matt.27.9.]]

__II.3
rarely, award or give as an honour, Παιάν τέ σοι τιμᾷ φάος [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “P.” 4.270; ταὐτὰ τῇδέ μοι τάδε τιμᾶτε 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Ajax” 688; ἐκείνῳ δυσσεβῆ τιμᾷς χάριν [prev. author] “Ant.” 514; πατρῴαν τιμῶν χάριν 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Orestes” 829 (Lyric poetry): hence,]]

__III
as Attic dialect lawterm [Refs [compare (τίμημα 4):]]

__III.1
in active (later in middle, [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [“PHal.” 1.201 (3rd c.BC), 3rd c.AD(?): Diogenes Laertius 2.41, etc.)]], of the court, estimate the amount of punishment due to the criminal, award the penalty, τιμάτω τὸ δικαστήριον, ὅ τι ἂν δέῃ πάσχειν.. τὸν ἡττηθέντα [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Leges” 843b; τὴν ἀξίαν τῆς βλάβης [prev. work] 879b; τ. τὰς βλάβας [prev. work] 843d; τ. τὴν δίκην [prev. work] 880d (compare below 2c)]]; ἅπασι τ. τὴν μακράν (i.e. γραμμήν) award them the long line, i.e. sentence of death, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Vespae” 106, ubi see Scholia: _absolutely_, ὡς ἐγὼ τιμᾶν βλέπω]] I carry penalty in my eyes, am itching for pains and penalties, [Refs [[prev. work] 847: the sentence or judgement awarded is added in the _genitive_, τ. τινὶ θανάτου (i.e. δίκην)]]give sentence of death against a man, condemn him to death, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Lysias Orator 27.7 (compare 8), 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Gorgias” 516a, 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 24.103 (_passive_), 32.15]]; τ. τινὶ δέκα ταλάντων mulct him in ten talents, [Refs [[prev. author] 58.31]]; τίνος τιμήσειν αὐτῷ προσδοκᾷς τὸ δικαστήριο; at what do you expect the court to fix his penalty? [Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. author] 21.151, compare 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Apologia” 37c]]; ἡ ἡλιαία τιμάτω περὶ αὐτοῦ ὅτου ἂν δόξῃ ἄξιος εἶναι παθεῖν Legal cited in [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 21.47: with _accusative_ _person_, τιμάτωσαν αὐτὸν καθ᾽ ὅτι ἂν δοκῇ τῷ κοινῷ “IG” 22.1275.16:]] —passive, τιμᾶσθαι ἀργυρίου to be condemned to a fine, τινος for a thing, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Lysias Orator 6.22, Legal cited in 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 21.47]]; ἐὰν.. ᾖ τῳ θανάτου τετιμημένον if sentence of death has been passed upon one, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Leges” 946e, compare 5th c.BC: Antipho Orator 6.38.]]

__III.2
in middle, of the parties before the court,

__III.2.a
of the accuser, τιμᾶταί μοι ὁ ἀνὴρ θανάτου (i.e. τὴν δίκην) he estimates the penalty at death (genitive pretii) for me, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Apologia” 36b; εἰ βούλοιτο θανάτου σοι τιμᾶσθαι [prev. author] “Grg.” 486b, compare 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 25.74,83, etc.]]

__III.2.b
of the person accused (compare ἀντιτιμάω, ὑποτιμάω), τιμήσεσθαι τοιούτου τινὸς ἐμαυτῷ estimate the penalty for myself at so high a rate, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Apologia” 37b, compare 38b; ἐξῆν σοι φυγῆς τιμήσασθαι [prev. author] “Cri.” 52c; ἔδησεν ἑαυτὸν τιμησάμενος δεσμοῦ 5th c.BC: Lysias Orator 6.21]]: perfect passive, θανάτου τετιμημένος ἑαυτῷ [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-3rd c.BC: Dinarchus Orator 1.1:— 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Rhetorica” 1375a1 uses the]]active in this sense.

__III.2.c
the accusative of δίκη or of the offence is added, πέντε μυριάδων τιμησάμενος τὴν δίκην [Refs 1st c.AD+ [1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus “Cicero” 8, compare “Lys.” 13, 3rd c.AD(?): Diogenes Laertius 2.42; θανάτου τιμῶμαι τὰ πεπολιτευμένα ἐμαυτῷ 1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus “Phocion” 34.]]

τῑμ-ή, ἡ,
(τίω, see ad near the end).

__I
worship, esteem, honour, and in plural honours, such as are accorded to gods or to superiors, or bestowed (whether by gods or men) as a reward for services, τιμῆς ἔμμοροί εἰσι [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 8.480; ὄφρ᾽ ἂν Ἀχαιοὶ υἱὸν ἐμὸν τίσωσιν ὀφέλλωσίν τέ ἑ τιμῇ 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 1.510; ἐκ δὲ Διὸς τιμὴ καὶ κῦδος ὀπηδεῖ 17.251; ἐν δὲ ἰῇ τ. ἠμὲν κακὸς ἠδὲ καὶ ἐσθλός 9.319, compare 4.410; ἐν τ. σέβειν 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Persae” 166 (troch.); ἐν τ. ἄγεσθαί τινας 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.134]]; ἐν τ. τίθεσθαι or ἄγειν τινά, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. author] 3.3, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 538e; ἐν τιμαῖς ἔχειν 4th-3rd c.BC: Philemo Comicus 199; τιμαῖς αὐξήσας τινάς 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 8.8.24]]; τιμὴν νεῖμαι, ἀπονέμειν τινί, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Philoctetes” 1062, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Leges” 837c]]; τοῖς φίλοις τιμὰς νέμειν pay due regard, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Ajax” 1351]]; τιμὰς ὤπασας, πορών, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Prometheus Vinctus” 30, 946; διδόναι 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Hippolytus” 1424, etc.; ἀποδοῦναι 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 415c; τὸ πρᾶγμ᾽ ἐμοὶ τιμὴν φέρει 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Hippolytus” 329; τινὶ τιμὰς προσάπτειν 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Electra” 356; ἀφύων τιμὴν περιάψας 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Acharnenses” 640 (_anapaest meter_)]]; τ. εὑρίσκεσθαι, δέκεσθαι, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “P.” 1.48, 8.5; τιμὴν παρ᾽ ἀνθρώποις φέρεσθαι 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Aves” 1278; τιμὰς ἔχειν 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 2.46, etc.; πρός τινος [prev. author] 1.120; ἐν μεγάλῃτιμῇ εἶναι 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 2.5.38]]; τιμῆς λαχεῖν, τυχεῖν, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Antigone” 699, “El.” 364 (variant)]]; οἱ γεραίτεροι ταῖς τῶν νέων τιμαῖς ἀγάλλονται paid to them by the young, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Memorabilia” 2.1.33: with _genitive_, χωρὶς ἡ τ. θεῶν]] the honour due to them, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Agamemnon” 637, compare “Ch.” 200; τιμὰς τὰς θεῶν πατεῖν 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Antigone” 745; τιμαὶ δαιμόνων 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Hippolytus” 107: τιμῇ]] with honour, honourably, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Coloneus” 381 codices]]; τιμῆς ἕνεκα as a mark of honour, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 7.3.28; τιμῇ προέξουσ᾽ 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Antigone” 208.]]

__I.2
honour, dignity, lordship, as the attribute of gods or kings, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 1.278, 9.498, etc.; θεῶν ἒξ ἔμμορε τιμῆς 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 5.335; τ. βασιληΐς 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 6.193, compare 8th-7th c.BC: Hesiodus Epicus “Theogonia” 393, 5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “P.” 4.108, 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Eumenides” 228 (_plural_); Περσονόμος τ. μεγάλη [prev. author] “Pers.” 919 (_anapaest meter_)]]; δίθρονος.. καὶ δίσκηπτρος τ. [Refs [[prev. author] “Ag.” 44 (_anapaest meter_)]]: generally, like{γέρας}, prerogative or special attribute of a king, and in plural his prerogatives, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 1.117, 8th-7th c.BC: Hesiodus Epicus “Theogonia” 203, 6th c.BC: Theognis Elegiacus 374, 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Tyrannus” 909 (Lyric poetry), etc.]]; βασιλικαὶ τ. imperial prerogatives, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [2nd c.AD: Herodianus Grammaticus 7.10.5; σκῆπτρον τιμάς τ᾽ ἀποσυλᾶται 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Prometheus Vinctus” 172 (_anapaest meter_).]]

__I.3
a dignity, office, magistracy, and in plural, civic honours (τιμὰς λέγομεν εἶναι τὰς ἀρχάς [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Politica” 1281a31), 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.59, etc.]]; ἔν τε ταῖς ἀρχαῖς καὶ ταῖς ἄλλαις τ. [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Apologia” 35b, compare “Ti.” 20a, etc.; μὴ φεύγειν τοὺς πόνους, ἢ μηδὲ τὰς τ. διώκειν 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 2.63; τιμὴν ἔχειν 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 1.3.8, etc.; τὴν τιμὴν εἴληχε 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Philebus” 61c]]; οἱ ἐν τιμαῖς men in office, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Iphigenia Aulidensis” 19 (_anapaest meter_), compare 5th-6th c.BC: Isocrates Orator 9.81; ἐκβαλῶ σε ἐκ τῆς τιμῆς 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 1.3.9]]; τιμὰς ἴσχειν hold the office of τιμοῦχος (which see), [Refs 5th c.BC+ [“Jahresh.” 12.136 (Erythrae, 5th-4th c.BC)]]: generally, office, task, ἄχαρις τιμή [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 7.36:]] —also,

__I.3.b

τίνω,
[Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 3.289, +others, (ἀπο-) “IG” 5(1).1390.76 (Andania, 1st c.BC)]], etc.: Ionic dialect imperfect τίνεσκον [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [3rd c.BC: Apollonius Rhodius Epicus 2.475:]]future τείσω (ἐκ-) [Refs 4th c.BC+ [“IG” 22.412.6 (4th c.BC), (ἀπο-) “epigram Gr.” 1132 (_Attic dialect_ vase, 4th c.BC), “PPetr.” 3p.55 (3rd c.BC), “IG” 7.3073.1 (Lebad., 2nd c.BC), etc.; 5th c.AD: Cypria]] 3rd.pers. singular πείσει [Refs [“Inscription Cyprian dialect” 135.12 H.:]]aorist ἔτεισα (ἀπ-) [Refs 5th c.BC+ [“SIG” 47.15 (_Locrian dialect_, 5th c.BC), 663.25 (Delos, 3rd-2nd c.BC), “PPetr.” 3p.41 (3rd c.BC), etc.: frequently written τίσω ἔτισα]] in Hellenistic and later Inscrr. and Papyrus, and in codices of all authors (future, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 8.348, 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Choephori” 277, 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Ajax” 113, etc.]]; aorist, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 24.352, 5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “O.” 2.58, 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Tyrannus” 810, etc.): in 8th c.BC: Homerus Epicus confused (both in codices and printed texts) with τίσω ἔτισα]]future and aorist of τίω, and only to be distinguished by the sense: perfect τέτεικα (ἀπο-) [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [“SIG” 437.6 (Delph., 3rd c.BC)]]; participle τετεικώς [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [3rd c.BC: Lycophron Tragicus 765 (τετικώς, τεθεικώς codices) (see. ἐκτίνω)]]:—middle, present first in [Refs 8th c.BC+ [6th c.BC: Theognis Elegiacus 204 (only τίνυμαι in 8th c.BC: Homerus Epicus)]]: future τείσομαι [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 13.15, +others]]: aorist ἐτεισάμην [Refs [3.197, 15.236, +others (τισ- codices)]]:—passive, aorist ἐξ-ετείσθην [Refs 4th c.BC+ [“IG” 22.1613.198, 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 39.15, 59.7]]: perfect 3rd.pers. singular ἐκ-τέτεισται [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Phaedrus” 257a, 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 24.187. [τῑνω (from *τίνϝω)]] in Epic dialect, also [Refs 6th c.BC+ [6th c.BC: Theognis Elegiacus 204, 3rd c.BC: Herodas Mimographus 2.51, “Anthologia Graeca” 7.657 (1st c.AD: Leonidas Alexandrinus Epigrammaticus)]]; τῐνω in Trag., as [Refs 6th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Prometheus Vinctus” 112, 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Coloneus” 635, 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Orestes” 7; also in 5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “P.” 2.24 (_middle_) and 6th c.BC: Solon Lyricus 13.31]]; also in some Epigrammatists, as [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [3rd c.BC: Simmias 25.1, “Anthologia Graeca” 9.286 (Marc. argument).]]]

__I
active, pay a price by way of return or recompense, mostly in bad sense, pay a penalty, with accusative of the penalty, τ. θωήν [NT+8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 2.193; τιμήν τινι 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 3.289; ποινάς 5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “O.” 2.58, 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Prometheus Vinctus” 112, 4th c.BC: Theodectes Tragicus 8.9; δίκην 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Ajax” 113, “El.” 298, “fragment” 107.9, NT.2Thes.1.9, etc.]]; also τ. ἴσην (i.e. δίκην) [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Tyrannus” 810; διπλῆν 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Leges” 946e; τὸ ἥμισυ [prev. work] 767e (assuming variant); μείζονα τὴν ἔκτισίν τινι [prev. work] 933e]]; τὴν προσήκουσαν τιμωρίαν[Refs [[prev. work] 905a, compare “Tragica Adespota” 490:]] —but also

__I.b
in good sense, pay a debt, acquit oneself of an obligation, ζωάγρια τ. [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 18.407; τείσειν αἴσιμα πάντα 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 8.348; εὐαγγέλιον (reward for bringing good news) 14.166]]; τ. χάριν τινί render one thanks, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Prometheus Vinctus” 985; τ. γῇ δασμόν 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Coloneus” 635; ἰατροῖς μισθόν 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Memorabilia” 1.2.54:]] —also simply,

__I.c
repay, with accusative of things, τροφάς τινι [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Orestes” 109:]] —in various phrases, τ. ἀντιποίνους δύας repay equivalent sorrows, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Eumenides” 268 (Lyric poetry)]]; φόνον φόνου ῥύσιον τ. [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Philoctetes” 959]]; αἱμάτων παλαιτέρων τ. μύσος send one pollution in repayment for another, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Choephori” 650 (Lyric poetry, Lachm., for τείνει); ἀρᾶς τ. χρέος [prev. author] “Ag.” 457 (Lyric poetry).--Constr.:]]

__I.1
with accusative of the thing paid or of the thing repaid (see. above).

__I.2
less frequently with dative, κράατι τείσεις with thy head, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 22.218; ψυχῇ 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Choephori” 277.]]

__I.3
with dative of person to whom payment is made (see. above).

__I.4
with dative of the penalty, τ. θανάτῳ ἅπερ ἦρξεν [Refs [[prev. author] “Ag.” 1529 (_anapaest meter_); τύμμα τύμματι [prev. work] 1430 (Lyric poetry).]]

__I.5
with genitive of the thing for which one pays, τ. ἀμοιβὴν βοῶν τινι pay him compensation for the cows, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 12.382]]; τ. τινὶ ποινήν τινος pay one retribution for.. , [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 3.14, 7.134]]; τ. μητρὸς δίκας for thy mother, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Orestes” 531]]; ἀντὶ πληγῆς πληγὴν τ. [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Choephori” 313 (_anapaest meter_)]]: also with accusative of the thing for which one pays, the price being omitted, pay or atone for a thing, τείσειαν Δαναοὶ ἐμὰ δάκρυα σοῖσι βέλεσσι [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 1.42; τ. ὕβριν 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 24.352]]; τ. φόνον or λώβην τινός, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 21.134, 11.142; κακά 6th c.BC: Theognis Elegiacus 735; διπλᾶ δ᾽ ἔτεισαν Πριαμίδαι θἀμάρτια 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Agamemnon” 537: less frequently with _accusative_ _person_, τείσεις γνωτὸν τὸν ἔπεφνες]] thou shalt make atonement for the brother thou hast slain, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 17.34.]]

__I.6
absolutely, make return or requital, [Refs 6th c.BC+ [6th c.BC: Solon Lyricus 13.29; παθόντα οὐκ ἐπίστασθαι τίνειν 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Coloneus” 1203, compare 230 (Lyric poetry).]]

__II
middle, have a price paid one, make another pay for a thing, avenge oneself on him, punish him, frequently from [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Homerus Epicus downwards.--Constr.:]]

__II.1
with accusative person, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 2.743, 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 3.197, 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.10, 123, 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Coloneus” 996, etc.]]

__II.2
with genitive criminis, τείσασθαι Ἀλέξανδρον κακότητος punish him for his wickedness, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 3.366, compare 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 3.206, 6th c.BC: Theognis Elegiacus 204 (where ἀμπλακίης, variant{-ίας}), 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 4.118, etc.; τ. τινὰ ἐφ᾽ ἁμαρτωλῇ 6th c.BC: Theognis Elegiacus 1248; ὑπέρ τινος 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.27, 73.]]

__II.3
with accusative of things, take vengeance for a thing, τείσασθαι φόνον, βίην τινός, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 15.116, 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 23.31; λώβην 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 19.208, etc.]]

__II.4
with double accusative person et of things, ἐτείσατο ἔργον ἀεικὲς ἀντίθεον Νηλῆα he made Neleus pay for the misdeed, visited it on his head, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 15.236; Ζεῦ ἄνα, δὸς τείσασθαι, ὅ με πρότερος κάκ᾽ ἔοργε, δῖον Ἀλέξανδρον 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 3.351]]; τείσασθαί τινα δίκην exact retribution from a person, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Medea” 1316 (uncertain reading).]]

__II.5
with dative modi, τίνεσθαί τινα ἀγαναῖς ἀμοιβαῖς, φυγῇ, repay or requite with.., [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “P.” 2.24, 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Septem contra Thebas” 638.]]

__II.6
absolutely, repay oneself, indemnify oneself, ἡμεῖς δ᾽ αὖτε ἀγειρόμενοι κατὰ δῆμον τεισόμεθ᾽ [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 13.15]]. (Root q[uglide][icaron]- [alternating with q[uglide]ei- and q[uglide]oi-] 'pay': τῐ-νϝ-ω, τῐ-σις, τεί-σω [[Refs 5th c.AD+ [5th c.AD: Cypria πείσει], ἔ-τει-σα [compare ἀππεισάτου see at {ἀποτίνω], ποι-νή} (which see)]]: Sanskrit cáy-ate 'avenge, punish': ápa-ci-tis 'vengeance':—not related to τίω.)

τις, neut., τι, genitive, τινός,

__II. II. As adj.,
__1. a certain: Mat.18:12, Luk.1:5 8:27, Act.3:2, al.; with proper names, Mrk.15:21, Luk.23:26, al.; with genitive partit., Luk.7:19, al.
__2. some: Mrk.16:[8], Jhn.5:14, Act.17:21 24:24, Heb.11:40, al.

__A.II
special usages:

__A.II.1
some one (of many), i.e. many a one, ὧδε δέ τις εἴπεσκεν [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 7.201, etc.]]: sometimes with meiosis, implying all or men,[Refs 8th c.BC+ [13.638, 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 3.224]]; so in Prose, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 5.49 near the end, 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 2.37, etc.]]

__A.II.2
any one concerned, every one, εὖ μέν τις δόρυ θηξάσθω [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 2.382]]; ἀλλά τις αὐτὸς ἴτω let every man come himself,[Refs [17.254; ἵνα τις στυγέῃσι καὶ ἄλλος 8.515, compare 16.209, 17.227, +others]]; so in Trag. and Attic dialect, even with the imperative, τοῦτό τις.. ἴστω S [Refs 5th c.BC+ [“Aj.” 417 (Lyric poetry), compare 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Bacchae” 346, 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Aves” 1187; ἀγορεύω τινὶ ἐμὲ μὴ βασανίζειν [prev. author] “Ra.” 628]]; τοὺς ξυμμάχους αὐτόν τινα κολάζειν that every man should himself chastise his own allies, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 1.40, compare 6.77; ὅ τί τις ἐδύνατο [prev. author] 7.75]]; ἄμεινόν τινος better than any others, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 21.66, compare 19.35]]:—this is more fully expressed by adding other pronominal words, τις ἕκαστος [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 9.65, 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 6.31, etc.; πᾶς τις 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Agamemnon” 1205, 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 6.80, 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 8.94, etc.; ἅπας τις 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 3.113, etc.; οὐδέν τι μᾶλλον [prev. author] 4.118]]. In these senses, τις is frequently combined with plural words, οἱ κακοὶ.. οὐκ ἴσασι, πρίν τις ἐκβάλῃ, for πρὶν ἐκβάλωσι, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Ajax” 965]]; οἷς ἂν ἐπίω, ἧσσόν τις πρόσεισι, for ἧσσον προσίασι, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 4.85; ἐτόλμα τις.., ὁρῶντες [prev. author] 2.53, compare 7.75]]; especially after εἴ or ἤν τις, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Memorabilia” 1.2.62, +others]]

__A.II.3
in reference to a definite person, whom one wishes to avoid naming, οὐκ ἔφασαν ἰέναι, ἐὰν μή τις χρήματα διδῷ (i.e. Cyrus) [Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. author] “An.” 1.4.12, compare 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Ranae” 552, 3rd c.BC: Theocritus Poeta Bucolicus 5.122]]; so also euphemistic for something bad, ἤν τι ποιῶμεν [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 2.74; ἂν οὗτός τι πάθῃ 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 4.11]]: hence for the 1st pers. or 2nd pers. pronoun, ἅ τιν᾽ οὐ πείσεσθαι ὀΐω [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 1.289, compare 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Antigone” 751]]; ποῖ τις τρέψετα; for ποῖ τρέψομα; [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Thesmophoriazusae” 603, compare 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Ajax” 245 (Lyric poetry), 1138, 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 4.59, 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 3.4.40, 5.7.31, etc.]]

__A.II.4
indefinitely, where we say they, French on, sometimes with an ironical force, φοβεῖταί τις [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Choephori” 59 (Lyric poetry); μισεῖ τις ἐκεῖνον 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 4.8]]; as vocative, τὸν Πλοῦτον ἔξω τις κάλει call P. out, somebody, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Plutus” 1196.]]

__A.II.5
τις, τι may be opposed, expressly or by implication, to οὐδείς, οὐδέν, and mean somebody, something, by meiosis for some great one, some great thing, ηὔχεις τις εἶναι you boasted that you were somebody, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Electra” 939; εἰσὶν ὅμως τινὲς οἱ εὐδοκιμοῦντες 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Politica” 1293b13; τὸ δοκεῖν τιν᾽ εἶναι 4th-3rd c.BC: Menander Comicus 156; τὸ δοκεῖν τινὲς εἶναι 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 21.213; ὡς σὲ μὲν ἐν τῇ πόλει δεῖ τινὰ φαίνεσθαι, τὴν πόλιν δ᾽ ἐν τοῖς Ἕλλησι μηδενὸς ἀξίαν εἶναι [prev. author] 10.71]]; κἠγών τις φαίνομαι ἦμεν after all I too am somebody, [NT+3rd c.BC+ [3rd c.BC: Theocritus Poeta Bucolicus 11.79, cf. NT.Act.5.36]]; also in neuter, οἴονταί τι εἶναι ὄντες οὐδενὸς ἄξιοι [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Apologia” 41e, compare “Phd.” 63c, “Phdr.” 243a, “Euthd.” 303c, etc.:— so τι λέγειν to be near the mark, opposed to οὐδὲν λέγειν, [prev. author] “Prt.” 339c, “R.” 329e, “Phdr.” 260a, etc.; ἵνα καὶ εἰδῶμεν εἴ τι ὅδε λέγει [prev. author] “Cra.” 407e; οἴεσθέ τι ποιεῖν, οὐδὲν ποιοῦντες [prev. author] “Smp.” 173c.]]

__A.II.5.b
τις is sometimes opposed to to another word, ἀελλοπόδων μέν τιν᾽ εὐφραίνοισιν ἵππων τιμαί.., τέρπεται δὲ καί τις.. [LXX+5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “Fragmenta.” 221; τισὶ τῶν πολιτῶν ἀποροῦσι συνεξέδωκε θυγατέρας.., τοὺς δ᾽ ἐλύσατο ἐκ τῶν πολεμίων 5th c.BC: Lysias Orator 19.59; μέρος μέν τι σιδήρου, μέρος δέ τι ὀστράκινον LXX.Dan.2.33 (more frequently with the Article, see below 10 c)]]; ἔστιν οὖν οὐ πᾶν τὸ ταχύ, ἀλλά τι (sic codices BT) αὐτοῦ ἀγαστόν [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Cratylus” 412c; ἀναγκαῖον ἤτοι πᾶσι τοῖς πολίταις ἀποδίδοσθαι πάσας ταύτας τὰς κρίσεις ἢ τισὶ πάσας.. ἢ τινὰς μὲν αὐτῶν πᾶσι τινὰς δὲ τισίν 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Politica” 1298a9, compare 1277a23]]; τὸ μεῖζον τοῦθ᾽ ὅπερ ἐστὶν ἑτέρου λέγεται· τινὸς γὰρ λέγεται μεῖζον greater than something, [Refs [[prev. author] “Cat.” 6a38; τὸ πρώτως ὂν καὶ οὐ τὶ ὂν ἀλλ᾽ ὂν ἁπλῶς [prev. author] “Metaphorical” 1028a30]]; πότερον τῷ τυχόντι ἢ τισί; [Refs [[prev. author] “Pol.” 1269a26.]]

__A.II.6
with (Proper name)s τις commonly signifies one named so-and-so, ἦν δέ τις ἐν Τρώεσσι Δάρης [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 5.9, compare 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 3.1.4, etc.]]; with a sense of contempt, Θερσίτης τις ἦν there was one Thersites, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Philoctetes” 442.]]

__A.II.6.b
one of the same sort, converting the (Proper name) into an appellative, ἤ τις Ἀπόλλων ἢ Πάν an Apollo or a Pan, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Agamemnon” 55 (_anapaest meter_)]]; [πόλιες] ταὶ μέλονται πρός τινος ἢ Διὸς ἢ γλαυκᾶς Ἀθάνας Lyric poetry in [Refs 5th c.BC+ [“PVat.” 11v xi7; Σκύλλαν τινά 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Agamemnon” 1233, compare 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Vespae” 181, “Av.” 512, “Ra.” 912: so also ὥς τις ἥλιος 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Agamemnon” 288]]; ἰσθμόν τιν᾽ [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Thesmophoriazusae” 647.]]

__A.II.7
with adjectives τις combines to express the idea of a substantive used as predicate, ὥς τις θαρσαλέος καὶ ἀναιδής ἐσσι προΐκτης a bold and impudent beggar, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 17.449, compare 18.382, 20.140, 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 3.220]]; ἐγώ τις, ὡς ἔοικε, δυσμαθής a dullard, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 358a, compare “Prt.” 340e]]; φόβου πλέα τις εἶ a coward, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Prometheus Vinctus” 696, compare “Th.” 979 (Lyric poetry), “Ag.” 1140 (Lyric poetry)]]; ὡς ταχεῖά τις.. χάρις διαρρεῖ in what swift fashion (={ταχέως πως}), [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Ajax” 1266, compare “OT” 618, 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 4.198]]; δεινόν τι ποιεύμενος thinking it a terrible thing, [Refs [[prev. author] 3.155, 5.33.]]

__A.II.8
with numerals and adjectives expressing number, size, or the like, εἷς δέ τις ἀρχὸς ἀνὴρ.. ἔστω some one man, [NT+8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 1.144; ἕνα τιν᾽ ἂν καθεῖσεν 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Ranae” 911; δώσει δέ τι ἕν γε φέρεσθαι 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 15.83; τινὰ μίαν νύκτα 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 6.61; προσκαλεσάμενός τινας δύο τῶν ἑκατονταρχῶν NT.Act.23.23]]; sometimes the τις softens the definiteness of the numeral, ἑπτά τινες some seven, seven or so, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 7.34; ἐς διακοσίους τινάς [prev. author] 3.111, compare 7.87, 8.21]]; so without an actual numeral, ἡμέρας τινάς some days, i.e. several, [Refs [[prev. author] 3.52]]; στρατῷ τινι of a certain amount, considerable, [Refs [[prev. author] 8.3]]; ἐνιαυτόν τινα a year or so, [Refs [[prev. author] 3.68]]; so οὐ πολλοί τινες, τινὲς οὐ πολλοί, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Persae” 510, 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 6.94, etc.]]; ὀλίγοι τινές or τινὲς ὀλίγοι [Refs [[prev. author] 2.17, 3.7]]; οὔ τινα πολλὸν χρόνον no very long time, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 5.48; τις στρατιὰ οὐ πολλή 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 6.61]]; so also ὅσσος τις χρυσός what a store of gold, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 10.45, compare 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.193, 2.18, etc.; κόσοι τινές [prev. author] 7.234; πηλίκαι τινὲς τιμωρίαι 5th-6th c.BC: Isocrates Orator 20.3; πολλὸς γάρ τις ἔκειτο 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 7.156; ἐκ πολλοῦ τευ χρόνου 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 2.58.]]

__A.II.9
with Pronominal words, ἀλλά τί μοι τόδε θυμὸς.. μερμηρίζει something, namely this, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 20.38, compare 380]]; οἷός τις what sort of a man, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 5.638 (uncertain reading), compare 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 9.348, 20.377, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Protagoras” 313a, etc.; ποῖός τις 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Antigone” 42, “OC” 1163, 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 3.34, 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 7.6.24, etc.; ὁποῖός τις [prev. author] “Cyr.” 2.2.2, +others; εὐτυχίη τις τοιήδε 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 3.139, compare 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Memorabilia” 1.1.1, etc.; τοιοῦτός τις [prev. author] “An.” 5.8.7.]]

__A.II.10
with the Article,

__A.II.10.a
when a noun with the Article is in apposition with τις, as ὅταν δ᾽ ὁ κύριος παρῇ τις when the person in authority, whoever he be, is here, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Coloneus” 289]]; τοὺς αὐτοέντας.. τιμωρεῖν τινας (variant τινα) [Refs [[prev. author] “OT” 107.]]

__A.II.10.b
in Philosophic writers, τις is added to the Article to show that the Article is used to denote a particular individual who is not specified in the general formula, although he would be in the particular case, ὁ τὶς ἄνθρωπος the individual man (whoever he may be), this or that man, opposed to ἄνθρωπος (man in general), ὁ τὶς ἵππος, ἡ τὶς γραμματική, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Categoriae” 1b4, 8]]; τὸ τὶ μέγεθος, opposed to ὅλως τὸ μέγεθος, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. author] “Pol.” 1283a4, compare 2nd c.AD: Sextus Empiricus Philosophus “Πυρρώνειοι ὑποτυπώσεις” 2.223; but in ἑνὸς γὰρ τό γε τὶ φήσεις σημεῖον εἶναι 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Sophista” 237d]], the Article is used as in [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad”]] cc. (which see) ὁ, ἡ, τό [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Bacchylides Lyricus 1.5: later ὅ τις (or ὁ τὶς) much like{ὁ δεῖνα}]], δεῦρο ὅ τις θεός, ὄφθητί μοι in a general formula of invocation, [Refs [“PMag.Par.” 1.236; αἴρω σε, ἥ τις βοτάνη [prev. work]287; εἰς τήν τινα κρείαν (to be read χρείαν) [prev. work]289.]]

__A.II.10.c
frequently in opposed clauses, ὁ μέν τις.., ὁ δὲ.. [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Medea” 1141, “Hec.” 624, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Phaedo” 99b, etc.; ὁ μέν τις.., ἄλλος δὲ.. 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Iphigenia Taurica” 1407; ὁ μὲν.., ὁ δέ τις.. 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 1.4.15: _plural_, οἱ μέν τινες.., οἱ δὲ.. 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.127, compare 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 2.91; οἱ μέν τινες.., οἱ δὲ.., οἱ δέ τινες 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 3.2.10, etc.; οἱ μὲν.., οἱ δέ τινες.. [prev. work] 6.1.26]], etc.: also combined with other alternative words, ὁ μέν τις.., ὁ δέ τις.., ἕτερος δέ τις.. [Refs [[prev. author] “Smp.” 2.6]]; ὁ μὲν.., ἕτερος δέ τις.., ὁ δὲ.., etc., [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Plutus” 162f]]: also in neuter, τὸ μέν τι.., τὸ δέ τι.. [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Epistulae” 358a; τὸ μέν τι.., τὸ δὲ.. 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 3.40]]; in adverbial sense, τὸ μὲν.., τὸ δέ τι.. partly.., partly.. , [Refs 2nd c.BC+ [2nd c.BC: Polybius Historicus 1.73.4]]; and τι remains unaltered even when the Article is plural, τὰ μέν τι μαχόμενοι, τὰ δὲ καὶ ἀναπαυόμενοι [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 4.1.14, compare “HG” 7.1.46]]; also τὸ δέ τι.. but in some measure.., without τὸ μέν preceding, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 1.107, compare 118, 7.48.]]

__A.II.10.d
later τις is used as in b above but without the Article, γράψον.. ὅτι τι καί τι εἴληφας that you have received such and such things, [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [“POxy.” 937.22 (3rd c.AD); κληρονόμους καταλείπω τὴν θυγατέρα μού τινα καὶ τὸν σύντροφον αὐτῆς τινα καί τινα [prev. work] 1034.2 (2nd c.AD)]]; τίς τινι χαίρειν [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [A to B greeting (in a draft letter),[prev. work] (2nd c.AD).]]

__A.II
the neuter τι is used,

__A.II.a
collectively, ἦν τι καὶ ἐν ταῖς Συρακούσαις there was a party.. , [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 7.48]]; so perhaps τῶν ἄλλων οὔ πέρ τι πεφυγμένον ἐστ᾽ Ἀφροδίτην, οὔτε θεῶν, οὔτ᾽ ἀνθρώπων no class, [Refs [hymnus ad Venerem 34]] (but masculine τις in [Refs [“hymnus ad Mercurium” 143).]]

__A.II.b
euphemistic for something bad, see above [Refs [3.]]

__A.II.c
joined with Verbs, somewhat, in any degree, at all, ἦ ῥά τί μοι κεχολώσεαι [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 5.421; παρεθάρρυνέ τι αὐτούς 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Historia Graeca (Hellenica)” 6.4.7, etc.: with _adjectives_ or Adverbs, οὕτω δή τι ἰσχυραί, οὕτω δή τι πολύγονον, etc., 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 3.12, 108, compare 4.52; so also ὀλίγον τι ἧσσον 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 15.365; οὐδέ τι μᾶλλον 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 6.123, etc.; ἧσσόν τι 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 3.75, etc.]]; οὐ πάνυ τι, πολύ τι, σχεδόν τι, see at {πάνυ} [Refs [1.3, πολύς 111.1a, 2a, σχεδόν IV]]; also in conjunction with οὐδέν, μηδέν, οὐδέν τι πάντως [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 6.3]]; οὐδέν, μηδέν τι μᾶλλον, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Alcestis” 522, 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Ajax” 280; μηδέν τι λίαν 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Andromache” 1234:]] —also καί τι καὶ.. ὑποψίᾳ in part also from suspicion, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 1.107; καί πού τι καί 5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “O.” 1.28.]]

__A.II.12
τίς τε frequently in [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Homerus Epicus, ὡς ὅτε τίς τε 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 3.33, 4.141, see τε 5th c.BC: Bacchylides Lyricus]]

__A.II.13
ἤ τις ἢ οὐδείς few or none, next to none, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 3.140, 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 7.5.45, 2nd-3rd c.AD: Dio Cassius Historicus 47.5, 48.4]]; ἤ τι ἢ οὐδέν little or nothing, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Apologia” 17b; ἢ οὐδεὶς ἤ τις 2nd-3rd c.AD: Dio Cassius Historicus 41.62 (assuming variant).]]

__A.II.14
τις is pleonastic in such phrases as οὐδέν τι or μηδέν τι, see above [Refs [11c.]]

__A.II.14.b
repeated in successive clauses, ὅσα λέγει τις ἢ πράσσειτις ἢψέγειν ἔχει [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Antigone” 689; εἴ τις δύο ἢ καὶ πλέους τις ἡμέρας λογίζεται [prev. author] “Tr.” 944 (where however κἄτι πλείους is probably conjecture),compare 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Orestes” 1218]] (whereas τις is sometimes omitted in the first clause, οὔτε φωνὴν οὔτε του μορφὴν βροτῶν [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Prometheus Vinctus” 21, compare 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Trachiniae” 3): but in 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Andromache” 734, ἔστι γάρ τις οὐ πρόσω.. πόλις τις]], the repetition is pleonastic, as also in [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Supplices” 57f (Lyric poetry, assuming variant).]]

__A.II.15
τις is sometimes omitted, οὐδέ κεν ἔνθα τεόν γε μένος καὶ χεῖρας ὄνοιτο (i.e. τις) [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 13.287]]; ὡς δ᾽ ἐν ὀνείρῳ οὐ δύναται (i.e. τις) φεύγοντα διώκειν [Refs 5th c.BC+ [22.199, compare 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Coloneus” 1226 (Lyric poetry), “Leg.Gort.” 2.2, 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Symposium” 5.2, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Gorgias” 456d]]: τις must often be supplied from what goes before,[Refs [[prev. work] 478c, “Prt.” 319d.]]

__A.II.15.b
sometimes also τις is omitted before a genitive case which must depend upon it, as ἢ [τις] τᾶς ἀσώτου Σισυφιδᾶν γενεᾶς [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Ajax” 189 (Lyric poetry)]]; ἢν γαμῇ ποτ᾽ αὐτὸς ἢ [τις] τῶν ξυγγενῶν [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Nubes” 1128; ἐν τῶν πόλεων “IG” 12.56.14.--Cf. ὅστις, οὔτις, μήτις, ἄλλο τι.]]

__A.III
Accentuation and position of τις:

__A.III.1
accentuation: τις is normally enclitic, but in certain uses is orthotone, i.e. theoretically oxytone (τίς, τινά, τινές, τινῶν, etc.,[Refs 4th c.AD+ [compare 4th-5th c.AD: Choeroboscus Grammaticus “Scholia in Theodosii Canones” 1.373 H.) and barytone when followed by another word (τὶς]] or τις, τινὰ, τινὲς, τινῶν, etc.). According to [Refs [Scholia 2nd c.BC: Dionysius Thrax Grammaticus p.240 H. its orthotone accent is τίς (not τὶς), τίνα, τίνες, etc. The orthotone form is used in codices:]]

__A.III.1.a
at the beginning of a sentence, τίς ἔνδον..; is any one within? [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Choephori” 654 (τὶς conjecture Hermann)]]; τί φημ; ={λέγω τι}; am I saying anything? [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Trachiniae” 865, “OT” 1471]];  ἦλθέ τις has anybody come? [Refs 2nd c.BC+ [“Somebody” has come, Scholia 2nd c.BC: Dionysius Thrax Grammaticus [same place]]]; τὶς κάθηται, τὶς περιπατεῖ, so and so is sitting (walking), [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd c.AD: Sextus Empiricus Philosophus “adversus Mathematicos” 8.97]]; τὶς αἰπόλος καλούμενος Κομάτας [Refs 5th c.BC+ [Scholia 3rd c.BC: Theocritus Poeta Bucolicus 7.78; τίς ποτε οἰκοδεσπότης.. ἐκοπία 5th-4th c.BC: Aesopus Fabularum Scriptor in “Corpus Glossariorum Latinorum” iii ; or after a pause, πῶς γὰρ ἄν, ἔφην ἐγώ, ὦ βέλτιστε, τὶς ἀποκρίναιτο 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 337e]]; τι οὖν (τὶς ἂν εἴποι) ταῦτα λέγει; [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 1.14 (variant); ἔντοσθεν δὲ γυνά, τι θεῶν δαίδαλμα 3rd c.BC: Theocritus Poeta Bucolicus 1.32; οὐ γυμνὸν τὸ φίλαμα, τι δ᾽ ὦ ξένε καὶ πλέον ἑξεῖς 2nd c.BC: Moschus Bucolicus 1.5 (variant for{τὺ}).]]

__A.III.1.b
when τις is opposed to to another τις or to some other word, τισὶ μὲν συμφέρει, τισὶ δ᾽ οὐ συμφέρει [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Politica” 1284b40, compare 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 2.92, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Crito” 49a, 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 9.2; τινὲς μὲν οὖν.., ἡμεῖς δὲ.. 2nd c.AD: Soranus Medicus 1.1; τὸ τὶ μὲν ψεῦδος ἔχον, τὶ δὲ ἀληθές 2nd c.AD: Sextus Empiricus Philosophus “adversus Mathematicos” 8.127; ἀλλὰ τινὰ μὲν.., τινὰ δὲ.. 1st c.BC: Geminus Astronomicus 14.6; ποτὲ μὲν πρὸς πάντα, ποτὲ δὲ πρὸς τινά 2nd c.AD: Soranus Medicus 1.48: without such opposition, τοῦτ᾽ εἰς ἀνίαν τοὔπος ἔρχεται τινί]] for a certain person, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Ajax” 1138]]. Codices are not consistent; in signification[Refs [11.5a, 10c, 13]] they make it enclitic; in signification [Refs [11.5b sometimes enclitic, sometimes orthotone (see. above)]]; sometimes enclitic and orthotone in the same sentence, πάντα δὲ τὰ γιγνόμενα ὑπό τέ τινος γίγνεται καὶ ἔκ τινος καὶ τί [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Metaphysica” 1032a14, compare 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Charmides” 165c.]]

__A.III.2
position:

__A.III.2.a
τις is rarely first word in the sentence, and rarely follows a pause (see. above [Refs [111.1a, b)]]; it may stand second word, ἔσκε τις ἐνθάδε μάντις ἀνήρ [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 9.508, compare 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 8.515, 23.331]]; but in general its position is not far before or after the word to which it belongs in sense, ἀλλ᾽ ἄγε δή τινα μάντιν ἐρείομεν [Refs [1.62; φυλακὴ δέ τις ἔμπεδος ἔστω 8.521.]]

__A.III.2.b
in Ionic dialect Prose it sometimes stands between its genitive and the Article of that genitive, τῶν τις Περσέων [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.85; τῶν τις ἱρέων [prev. author] 2.38; τῶν τινες Φοινίκων [prev. author] 8.90; ἐς τῶν τι ἄλλο στομάτων τοῦ Νείλου [prev. author] 2.179]]; so also in late Prose, [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd c.AD: Athenaeus Epigrammaticus 3.108d, 12th c.AD: Eustathius Episcopus Thessalonicensis 1402.18, 1659.27, 1676.1.]]

__A.III.2.c
it stands between the Article and substantive in signification[Refs 5th c.BC+ [11.10b.]]

__A.III.2.d
τίς τι is the correct order, not τί τις, “IG” 12.110.46, 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 7.10, 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 4.1.14 (codices dett.), 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 22.22, etc.

__A.III.2.e
whereas in _Attic dialect_ the order ἐάν τις is compulsory, in _Doric dialect_ the usual order is αἴ τίς κα, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [“Leg.Gort.” 9.43, +others, “Tab.Heracl.” 1.105, +others (but αἴ κά τις 5th c.BC: Epicharmus Comicus 35, 159; αἰ δέ κα μή τις “Leg.Gort.” 5.13)]]: later Doric dialect εἴ τί κα [Refs [“GDI” 2101.3, +others]]; καἴ τι ἂν (={καὶ εἴ τι ἂν}) [Refs 1st c.BC+ [“IG” 5(1).1390.50 (Andania, 1st c.BC]], see below [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Bacchylides Lyricus 11.1b)]]:—this Doric dialect order influenced the Koine, as in the rare εἴ τις ἂν [Refs 1st c.AD+ [1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus “Tiberius Gracchus” 15.]]

deep_entry:
Abbott-Smith / STEPBible (TBESG)
τίς, neut., τί, genitive, τίνος, interrog. pron., [in LXX for מָה ,מִי ;] in masc. and fem.,
who, which, what?; in neut., which, what?, used both in direct and in indirect questions.
__I. I. As subst.,
__1. 1. masc., fem.: τίς; who, what?, Mat.3:7 26:68; Mrk.11:28, Luk.9:9, al. mult.; with genitive partit., Act.7:52, Heb.1:5, al; before ἐκ (= genitive partit.), Mat.6:27, Luk.14:28, Jhn.8:46; = ποῖος, Mrk.4:41 6:2, Luk.19:3, Act.17:19, al.; = πότερος (M, Pr., 77), Mat.21:31 27:17, Luk.22:27, al.; = ὅς or ὅστις (rare in cl.; cf. Bl., §50, 5; M, Pr., 93), Act.13:25.
__2. Neut.: τί; what?, Mat.5:47 11:7, Mrk.10:3, al.; χάριν τίνος, 1Jn.3:12; διὰ τί, Mat.9:11, al.; εἰς τί, Mat.14:31, al.; elliptically, ἵνα τί (sc. γένηται), why, Mat.9:5, al.; τί οὖν, Rom.3:9 6:1, 15 1Co.14:15, al.; τί γάρ, Rom.3:3, Phi 1:18; τί ἐμοὶ (ὑμῖν) καὶ σοί, see: ἔγω.
__II. As adj.: who? what? which?, Mat.5:46, Luk.14:31, Jhn.2:18, al.
__III. As adv.: = διὰ τι (τί ὅτι), why, Mat.6:28, Mrk.4:40, Luk.6:46, Jhn.18:23, al.; in rhet. questions, = a negation, Mat.27:4, Jhn.21:22, 23 1Co.5:12 7:16, al. in exclamations (like Heb. מָה), how (2Ki.6:20, Psa.3:2, al.), Luk.12:49.
(AS)

LSJ / STEPBible (TFLSJ)
τίς

__B
Interrog. pronoun τίς, Elean and Laconian dialect τίρ (which see), τί:—genitive Epic dialect and Ionic dialect τέο [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 2.225, 3rd c.BC: Herodas Mimographus 8.1, etc., or τεῦ 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 15.509, 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 5.106, etc.]]; Trag. and Attic dialect τοῦ [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Prometheus Vinctus” 614, 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Nubes” 1223, etc.]]; Ionic dialect, Trag., and Attic dialect τίνος [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Simonides Lyricus 154, 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 6.80, 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Prometheus Vinctus” 563 (_anapaest meter_), 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Ajax” 892, Ar “Ach.” 588, etc.]]; dative Ionic dialect τέῳ [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.11, +others (as _feminine_, 4.155)]]; no dative in [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Homerus Epicus or 8th-7th c.BC: Hesiodus Epicus]]; Trag. and Attic dialect τῷ [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Antigone” 401, 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 19.60, etc.]]; Aeolic dialect τίῳ [Refs 7th c.BC+ [7th-6th c.BC: Sappho Lyrica 104]]; τίνι first in [NT+8th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “N.” 7.57, 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Persae” 715 (troch.), 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Tyrannus” 10, 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Acharnenses” 919, 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 3.38, 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 1.80, 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 20.115, etc.; _accusative_ τίνα 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 5.703, etc.; _neuter_ τί 1.362, etc.: dual τίνε (elided) 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Aves” 107: _plural_. _nominative_ τίνες 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 1.172, etc.; _neuter_ τίνα 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Phaedo” 102a, 4th c.BC: Aeschines Orator 2.81, 2nd c.BC: Hipparchus Astronomicus 1.1.4, 1st c.BC: Geminus Astronomicus 17.12, NT.Heb.5.12]]; genitive Epic dialect τέων [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 24.387, 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 20.192]], and as monosyllable [Refs [6.119, 13.200]]; Trag. and Attic dialect τίνων [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Electra” 1476, “OC” 2, 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Nubes” 1089, etc.]]; dative τίσι first in [Refs 8th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Tyrannus” 1126, 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Ranae” 1455, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 332d, etc. (no _dative_ in 8th c.BC: Homerus Epicus or 8th-7th c.BC: Hesiodus Epicus); also τοῖσι 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Trachiniae” 984 (_anapaest meter_)]]; Ionic dialect τέοισι [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.37, compare 2.82 (variant{ὁτέοισι})]]; Aeolic dialect τίοισι [Refs 7th c.BC+ [7th-6th c.BC: Sappho Lyrica 168; _accusative_ τίνας 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Coloneus” 115, 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Aves” 370 (troch.); _neuter_ τίνα 2nd c.AD: Arrianus Historicus “Epicteti Dissertationes” 1.30.3]]; Boeotian dialect τά [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “O.” 1.82 (_adverb_)]]; Megarian dialect σά [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Acharnenses” 757, 784 (_adverb_)]]: of the plural [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Homerus Epicus uses only _nominative_ τίνες]] with genitive τέω; ποῖος (what? which?) is sometimes preferred (especially in neuter plural) to the adjective τίς, e.g. τὰ ποῖα ταῦτα χρήματ; [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Nubes” 1270, compare 1337, “Th.” 621, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Cratylus” 391e, 395d, 406d; see at {ποῖος} I.3 and IV:]]

__B.I
in direct questions, who? which? neuter what? which? ὦ ξεῖνοι, τίνες ἐστ; [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 9.252; τί νύ μοι μήκιστα γένητα; 5.299; τίς δαίμων τόδε πῆμα προσήγαγ; 17.446]]; τίς ἀχώ, τίς ὀδμὰ προσέπτα μ᾽ ἀφεγγή; [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Prometheus Vinctus” 115 (Lyric poetry), compare 561 (_anapaest meter_), etc.]]; properly at the beginning of the sentence; but this position may be varied,

__B.I.a
for grammatical reasons, as between the Article and participle or noun, τοὺς τί ποιοῦντας τὸ ὄνομα τοῦτο ἀποκαλοῦσι; [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Memorabilia” 2.2.1, compare 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Symposium” 206b]]; τῆς περὶ τί πειθοῦς ἡ ῥητορική ἐστιν τέχν; [Refs [[prev. author] “Grg.” 454a]]; ὁ σοφιστὴς τῶν τί σοφῶν ἐστι; [Refs [[prev. author] “Prt.” 312d.]]

__B.I.b
for emphasis, ἃ δ᾽ ἐννέπεις, κλύουσα τοῦ λέγει; [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Coloneus” 412, compare “El.” 1191]]; πόλις τε ἀφισταμένη τίς πω.. τούτῳ ἐπεχείρησ; [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 3.45]]; especially when the Verb begins the sentence, δράσεις δὲ δὴ τ; [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Hercules Furens” 1246]]; ἦλθες δὲ κατὰ τ; [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Nubes” 239]]; διαφέρει δὲ τ; [Refs 8th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 18.205.--The person frequently follows in _genitive_ _plural_, as τίς θεῶ; 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 18.182, etc.]]; and of things or conditions, τί is frequently with the genitive singular, of all genders, πρὸς τί χρεία; [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Tyrannus” 1174]]; ἐλπίδων ἐς τ; [Refs [[prev. author] “OC” 1749 codices (Lyric poetry); κἀνήρετ᾽ ἐν τῷ πράγματος κυροῖ ποτε [prev. author] “Aj.” 314, etc.]]

__B.I.2
sometimes as the predicate, τίς ὀνομάζετα; what is he named? [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Phoenissae” 123]]; so also may be explained the union of τίς with a demonstrative or possessive pronoun, or with a Noun preceded by the Article, τί τοῦτ᾽ ἔλεξα; [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Philoctetes” 1173 (Lyric poetry)]]; τί ἐστι τουτ; τίς ὁ τρόπος τοῦ τάγματο; [Refs [[prev. author] “Ichn.” 114]]; also with pronoun in plural, τί ταῦτ; [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Phoenissae” 382, “Andr.” 548, etc.]]; τί γὰρ τάδ᾽ ἐστί; [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Nubes” 200]]; τί ποτ᾽ ἐστίν, ἂ διανοούμεθ; [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Theaetetus” 154e]]; τί ποτ᾽ ἐστὶ ταῦτα[Refs [; [prev. work] 155c; σκεπτέον τί τὰ συμβαίνοντα [prev. author] “Grg.” 508b]]; so τί is used as predicate of a masculine or feminine subject, τί νιν προσείπ; [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Choephori” 983(997)]]; τί σοι φαίνεται ὁ νεανίσκο; [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Charmides” 154d:]] —also τίς δ᾽ ὅδε Ναυσικάᾳ ἕπεται; who is this that follows N.? [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 6.276]]; τίς δ᾽ οὗτος ἔρχεα; [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 10.82, compare 7th-6th c.BC: Alcaeus Lyricus 84.1, 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Electra” 328, 388, “Ant.” 7, 218, 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Hecuba” 501, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Crito” 43c]]; and in the reverse order, τήνδε τίνα λεύσσω..; who is this I see? [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Iphigenia Aulidensis” 821]]; τίνι οὖν τοιούτῳ φίλους ἂν θηρῴη; with what means of such kind.. ? [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Memorabilia” 3.11.9]]; τί τοσοῦτον νομίζοντες ἠδικῆσθα; [Refs [[prev. author] “Smp.” 4.53]]; τί με τὸ δεινὸν ἐργάσ; what is the dreadful thing which.. ? [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Bacchae” 492, compare 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Coloneus” 598, 1488, etc.]]; τίν᾽ ὄψιν σὴν προσδέρκομα; what face is this I see of thine? [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Helena” 557]]; παρὰ τίνας τοὺς ὑμᾶ; who are 'you' to whom [I am to come]? [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Lysis” 203b:]] —the _Article_ is exceptionally added to τίς, when it leads up to a word which requires the Article, ληφθήσει.. Πανήμου εἰκάδι· καὶ Λῴου τῇ--τίν; τῇ δεκάτῃ on the twentieth of the month Panemus and of Loüs on the --what day? the tenth, [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [3rd c.BC: Callimachus Epicus “Epigrammata” 46:]] —in Comedy texts also τὸ τί; what is that? [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Nubes” 775, “Pax” 696, “Av.” 1039, “Pl.” 902, etc.]]; τοῦ τίνος χάρι; [Refs 2nd c.BC+ [“UPZ” 6.29 (2nd c.BC)]]; and with plural Article, τὰ τ; [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Pax” 693.]]

__B.I.3
with properly names treated as appellatives (see. τις indefinite [Refs 5th c.BC+ [11.6b), τίς ἆρα Κύπρις ἢ τίς Ἵμερο; 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Fragmenta” 874]]; τίς σε Θηρικλῆς ποτε ἔτευξ; [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Eubulus Comicus 43]]; τίς.. Χίμαιρα πύρπνοο; [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Anaxilas Comicus 22.3.]]

__B.I.4
τίς ἂν θεῶν.. δοί; like{πῶς ἄν}, would that some one.. , [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Coloneus” 1100, compare 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Agamemnon” 1448 (Lyric poetry).]]

__B.I.5
a question with τίς often amounts to a strong negation, τῶν δ᾽ ἄλλων τίς κεν οὐνόματ᾽ εἴπο; [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 17.260]]; τίς ἂν ἐξεύροι ποτ᾽ ἄμεινο; [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Plutus” 498]]; τίνες ἂν δικαιότερον.. μισοῖντ; [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 3.64, etc.]]

__B.I.6
sometimes two questions are asked in one clause by different cases of τί; ἡ τίσιν τί ἀποδιδοῦσα τέχνη δικαιοσύνη ἂν καλοῖτ; [Refs 8th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 332d; τί λαβόντα τί δεῖ ποιεῖν 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 4.36:—a like doubling of the question lies in the union of τίς with other _interrogative_ words, τίς πόθεν εἰς (εἶς codices) ἀνδρῶ; 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 1.170, compare 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Trachiniae” 421.]]

__B.I.7
τίς with Particles:—τίς γά; why who? who possibly? τίς γάρ σε θεῶν.. ἧκε; [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 18.182; see below 8 f.]]

__B.I.7.b
τίς δ; ὦ κοῦραι, τίς δ᾽ ὔμμιν.. πωλεῖτα; [Refs [“hymnus ad Apollinem” 169.]]

__B.I.7.c
τίς δ; who then? τίς δή κεν βροτὸς.. ἅζοιτ᾽ ἀθανάτους [Refs 6th c.BC+ [6th c.BC: Theognis Elegiacus 747]]; τίς δῆτ; [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Ajax” 518.]]

__B.I.7.d
τίς ποτ; who in the world? who ever? τίς ποτ᾽ ὢν γενεὰν καὶ ποίαν τινὰ φύσιν ἔχω; [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 1.1.6, compare 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Electra” 975]]; τίς δήποτ; [Refs [[prev. author] “fragment” 106 (but τίς ἄν ποτε is probably conjecture).]]

__B.I.8
the usages of the neuter τ; are very various:

__B.I.8.a
τ; alone, as a simple question, what? τί γά; [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Septem contra Thebas” 336 (Lyric poetry)]]:—on ὅτι τ; ὅτι τί δ; ὅτι δὴ τ; see at {ὅτι} [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Bacchylides Lyricus 1b]]; on ὡς τ; see {ὡς} F.1.

__B.I.8.b
τί τοῦτ; τί ταῦτ; see above 2.

__B.I.8.c
τί μο; τί σο; what is it to me? to thee? [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Philoctetes” 753, etc.]]; with genitive, τί μοι ἔριδος καὶ ἀρωγῆ; what have I to do with.. ? [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 21.360]]; τί δέ σοι ταῦτ; [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Lysistrata” 514, compare “Ec.” 521]] (where the answerer repeats the question in indirect form, ὅ τί μοι τοῦτ᾽ ἔστι;); ἀλλὰ δὴ τί τοῦτ᾽ ἐμο; [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-3rd c.BC: Diphilus Comicus 32.18]]; τί ἐμοὶ καὶ σο; what have I to do with thee? [LXX+2nd c.AD+ [LXX.Judg.11.12, 2nd c.AD: Arrianus Historicus “Epicteti Dissertationes” 2.19.19, NT.John.2.4]]; τί σοὶ καὶ εἰρήν; [LXX.4Ki.9.18, cf. LXX.Hos.14.9]; τί πρὸσσ; [NT+2nd c.AD+ [2nd c.AD: Marcus Antoninus Imperator 8.44, cf. NT.Matt.27.4]]; σοὶ δὲ καὶ τούτοισι τοῖσι πρήγμασι τί ἐστ; what have you to do with these matters? [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 5.33]]; τί τῷ νόμῳ καὶ τῇ βασάν; [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 29.36:—followed by a clause, τί δὲ τίν, εἰ κωτίλαι εἰμέ; 3rd c.BC: Theocritus Poeta Bucolicus 15.89]]; or with infinitive, τί γάρ μοι τοὺς ἔξω κρίνει; [NT.1Cor.5.12:—see. εἰμί with 111.2.]

__B.I.8.d
τίμαθώ; τί παθώ; see at {μανθάνω} see, πάσχω [Refs [111.4.]]

__B.I.8.e
τ; also often stands absolutely as adverb how? why? wherefore? [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 1.362, etc.]]; so too in Attic dialect, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Crito” 43c, etc.]]; δόμων γὰρ ζῶσι τῶνδε δεσπόται. Answ. τί ζῶσι; how do you mean ζῶσι ζῶσι forsooth! [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Alcestis” 806]]; Κιθαιρὼν--Answ. τί Κιθαιρώ; what aboutK.? [Refs [[prev. author] “Ba.” 1177 codices, compare 1182 (both Lyric poetry)]]; compare τίη.

__B.I.8.f
τί with Particles: -τί γά; why not? how else? and so it came to mean of course, no doubt, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Agamemnon” 1239, “Ch.” 880, “Eu.” 678, etc.]]; used in affirmative answers, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Phaedrus” 258d, “Tht.” 209b, +others]]; to introduce an argument, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Politica” 1281a14; see at {γάρ} I.4:]] —τί δαί; see at {δαί}:—τί δ; serving to pass on quickly to a fresh point, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Hp.Ma.” 288c, +others]]; τί δέ, εἰ..; but what, if.. ? [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Helena” 1043]]; τί δ᾽ ἄν, εἰ..; [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Thesmophoriazusae” 773]]; τί δ᾽ ἢν..; [Refs [[prev. author] “Nu.” 1444]]; τί δέ, εἰ μὴ..; what else but.. ? [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Oeconomicus” 9.1, compare 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Tyrannus” 941, “Ph.” 421]]; so τί δὲ δ; τί δ; τί δή ποτ; why ever? why in the world? what do you mean? [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 470e, “Grg.” 469a, “Sph.” 241d, 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Electra” 1184:]] —so also τί δῆτα; how, pray? τί δῆτ᾽ ἄν, εἰ..; [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Nubes” 154:]] — (τί μή; falsa lectio in [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Ajax” 668):]] —τί μήν; i.e. yes certainly, much like{τί γάρ}; [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Theaetetus” 162e, etc., probably in 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Ajax” 668:]] —τί μὴν οὔ; in reply to a question, [Refs [[prev. author] “El.” 1280 (Lyric poetry):]] —τί νυ; why now? [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 1.414, etc.:]] —τί δ᾽ οὔ; parenthetic, why not? as an affirmative answer, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Antigone” 460]]; τί οὐ καλοῦμε; i.e. let us call, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Lysistrata” 1103]]; τί οὐ βαδίζομε; etc., [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Protagoras” 310e, etc.:]] —τί οὖν; how so? making an objection, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Septem contra Thebas” 208; but τί οὖν ἔτ᾽ ἂν σαίνοιμεν.. μόρο; [prev. work] 704]]; τί οὖν οὐκ ἐρωτᾷ; [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Lysis” 211d:]] —τί ποτε; see at {τίπτε};

__B.I.8.g
with Conjunctions following:—τί ὅτι..; why is it that.. ? [NT+5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Strattis Comicus 62 (_falsa lectio_), LXX.Gen.3.1, NT.Luke.2.49, etc.:—with Conjunctions preceding, ἵνα τί]]; see at {ἵνα} [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Bacchylides Lyricus 11.3 with]]

__B.I.8.h
with Preps.:—διὰ τ; wherefore? [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Plutus” 1111, etc.:]] —ἐκ τίνος; from what cause? [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 5.8.4:]] —ἐς τί; to what point? how long? [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 5.465]]; but also, to what end? [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Trachiniae” 403, compare “OC” 524 (Lyric poetry):]] —κατὰ τί; for what purpose? [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Nubes” 239:]] —πρὸς τί; wherefore? [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Tyrannus” 766, 1027, etc.]]

__B.II
τίς is sometimes used for ὅστις in indirect questions, εἰρώτα δὴ ἔπειτα τίς εἴη καὶ πόθεν ἔλθοι [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 15.423, compare 17.368; δεῖξον τίς ἔσται τῇ ταλαιπώρῳ χρόνος 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Prometheus Vinctus” 623; οὐδ᾽ ἔχω τίς ἂν γενοίμαν [prev. work] 905 (Lyric poetry)]]; οὐκ ἔχω τί φῶ [Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. author] “Ch.” 91, compare 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Coloneus” 48, etc.; ἐπισκεψώμεθα τίνες πέπανται σφενδόνας 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 3.3.18; εἰπὲ τίνα γνώμην ἔχεις [prev. work] 2.2.10]]; frequently in later Gr., where ὅστις is very rare, εἰς τὸ λογιστήριον γράφων.. τί ὀφείλεται [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [“PHib.” 1.29.42 (3rd c.BC),compare “PCair.Zen.” 21.40, +others (3rd c.BC)]]; οὐθεὶς ἐσήμηνεν παρὰ τί ἂν τοῖς προστεταγμένοις.. οὐ κατηκολούθησαν nobody indicated why they should not have obeyed orders, [Refs 2nd c.BC+ [“PTeb.” 72.160, compare 61 (b). 227 (2nd c.BC)]]; ὅστις and τίς are sometimes combined, ὡς πύθοιθ᾽ ὅ τι δρῶν ἢ τί φωνῶν ῥυσαίμην [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Tyrannus” 71, compare 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Prometheus Vinctus” 489f, 617, 623:]] —later with infinitive, τί πράττειν οὐκ ἔχω I do not know what to do, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-4th c.BC: Aesopus Fabularum Scriptor 67, cf. Ps.- 2nd c.AD: Lucianus Sophista “Philopatr.” 29.]]

__B.II.b
sometimes not in indirect questions, whoever, whatever, αἰτοῦ τί χρῄζεις ἕν [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Fragmenta” 773.2]]; ταῦτα οὐκ ἀπέστελλον πάντα, ἀλλ᾽ ἐκλεγόμενοι τίνων αἱ τιμαὶ ἐπετέταντο whatever things had risen in price, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 56.24]]; τίνα δ᾽ ἁ Κύπρις οὐκ ἐφίλησεν whomsoever K. has not loved, [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [“Anthologia Graeca” 5.169 (3rd c.BC(?): Nossis Epigrammatica)]]; τίνι ἡ τύχη δίδωσι, λαβέτω Antiochusap.[Refs 3rd c.BC+ [2nd c.BC: Ptolemaeus Euergetes II Historicus 3 1st c.AD: Josephus Historicus; λαμβανέτω τί θέλει “Anthologia Graeca” 12.219 (2nd c.AD: Strato Epigrammaticus); τὰν ὀνάλαν κίς κε γινύειτει “IG” 9(2).517.22 (Larissa, 3rd c.BC); καὶ τί ἂν εἶ (={ᾖ}) λοιπόν [prev. work]5(1).1390.50 (Andania, 1st c.BC, nisi to be read καἴ τι ἂν]], see above[Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus 111.2e); τίς ἂν δὲ χεῖρα προσαγάγῃ “epigram Gr.” 376a (from Aezani)]]; τίς σοφός, αὐτῷ προσκολλήθητι [LXX+NT [LXX.Sir.6.34; οὐ τί ἐγὼ θίλω, ἀλλὰ τί σύ NT.Mark.14.36]]; τίς σοφίῃ πάντων πρῶτος, τούτου τρίποδ᾽ αὐδῶ Oracle texts cited in [Refs 1st c.BC+ [1st c.BC: Diodorus Siculus Historicus 9.3 et cited in 3rd c.AD(?): Diogenes Laertius 1.28 codices (ὃς]] Cobet from [Refs 5th c.BC+ [Scholia 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Plutus” 9); χαῖρε καὶ σύ, τίς ποτ᾽ εἶ “IG” 9 (2).953 (from Larissa), compare “CIG” “Corpus Inscriptionum Graecarum” “Corpus Inscriptionum Graecarum” 1982 (from Thessalonica)]]; in other places, as [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Electra” 1176, “Tr.” 339, “OT” 1144, 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Ion” 324, this _construction_ cannot be admitted.]]

__B.II.c
τίς ={ὅστις} after a negative, μή τίς ἐστιν ἐν ὑμῖν ἀνὴρ ἢ γυνὴ.., τίνος ἡ διάνοια ἐξέκλινεν κτλ.; [LXX.Deu.29.18.]

__B.II.d
= {ὅς} or ὅσπερ, τέων.. Ζεὺς ἐπὶ σαλπίγγων ἱρὰ βοῇ δέχεται Κᾶρες ὁμοῦ Λελέγεσσι [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [3rd c.BC: Callimachus Epicus “Aetia” 3.1.60, compare “Del.” 185, “epigram” 30.2, 2nd c.BC: Nicander Epicus “Alexipharmaca” 2; Δωροθέαν, τίς τὸν ἐμὸν ἄνδρα εἶχε “Tab.Defix.Aud.” 10.4 (Cnidus, 2nd-1st c.BC)]], compare 5.2,8; τίνας ἱερεωσύνας εἶχον ἐπενεγύων [Refs 2nd c.BC+ [“SIG” 705.43, compare 56 (Senatus consultum, Delph., 2nd c.BC)]]; τίνα με ὑπονοεῖτε εἶναι, οὐκ εἰμὶ ἐγώ [NT.Act.13.25]; τίς ἔζησεν ἔτη β who lived.., [Refs [“IG” 14.1560 (from Rome), compare 1391 ([prev. passage])]]; εὗρον γεωργόν, τίς αὐτὰ ἑλκύσῃ [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [“BGU” 822.5 (2nd-3rd c.AD).]]

__B.II.2
τί; τ; in direct or indirect questions may be construed with a participle, σὺ δὲ τίς ὢν ταῦτα λέγει; being who, i.e. who are you that.. ? [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Gorgias” 452a; ἐπειρέσθαι.. τίνες ἐόντες ἄνθρωποι.. ταῦτα προαγορεύουσι 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.153]]; καταμεμάθηκας.. τοὺς τί ποιοῦντας τὸ ὄνομα τοῦτο ἀποκαλοῦσ; [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Memorabilia” 2.2.1; or in a subordinate clause, ἀλλ᾽ ὅταν τί ποιήσωσι, νομιεῖς αὐτοὺς σοῦ φροντίζει; [prev. work] 1.4.14]]; νῦν δ᾽ ἐπειδὴ τίνος τέχνης ἐπιστήμων ἐστί, τίνα ἂν καλοῦντες αὐτὸν ὀρθῶς καλοῖμε; [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Gorgias” 448c.]]

__B.III
= {πότερος}; [NT+5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 1.3.17, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Philebus” 52d, NT.Matt.27.21, NT.Luke.5.23.]]

__B.IV
τί as exclamatory adverb, how.. ! τί ὡραιώθησαν σιαγόνες σου ὡς τρυγόνες [LXX.Cant.1.10, compare 4.10]; τί θέλω how I wish! [NT.Luke.12.49]; τί στενή variant in [NT.Matt.7.14.]

__C
Prosody: τις and τίς keep ῐ in all cases (digamma operates in [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 6.462, etc.).]]

__C.II
τί was never elided; but hiatus is allowed after τί in Epic dialect τί ἢ (see. τίη), also in Comedy texts, as τί ο; [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Aves” 149]]; τί οὖ; [Refs [[prev. author] “Pl.” 94]]; τί ἔστ; [Refs [[prev. author] “Nu.” 82, “Av.” 1036]]; τί, ὦ πάτε; [Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. author] “Nu.” 80:—a licence which is rarer in Trag., τί ἔστι; 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Philoctetes” 733]]; τί οὖ; [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Septem contra Thebas” 208, 704, “Eu.” 902, 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Ajax” 873 (Lyric poetry), “Ph.” 100, etc.]]; τί εἶπα; [Refs [[prev. author] “Tr.” 1203, “Ph.” 917.]]

deep_entry:
Abbott-Smith / STEPBible (TBESG)
1. enclit. Particle, serving to express belief in an assertion, let me tell you, surely, verily , used to express an inference, then, consequently , (Homer); and in [variant datesTragica Adespota, to introduce a general sentiment.

in narrative, τοιαῦτα properly refers to what goes before, τοιαῦτα μὲν δὴ ταῦτα [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Prometheus Vinctus” 500; καὶ ταῦτα μὲν τ. 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Electra” 696, compare 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 2.5.12, etc.; compare τοιόσδε near the end]]

__4.b
after a question, τοιαῦτα affirms like{ταῦτα} (see. οὗτος with VII.1), just so, even so, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Hecuba” 776, “El.” 645.]]

__5
τοιαῦτα absolutely, τἂ πλοῖα, τὰ τοιαῦτα ships and suchlike, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 8.25.]]

__6
τοιαῦτα as adverb, in such wise, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Tyrannus” 1327: regular]] adverb τοιούτως only late, [Refs [“Etymologicum Magnum” 650.42.]] —Cf. τοσοῦτος. [τοῐ- frequently in Trag. and Comedy texts, e.g. [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Agamemnon” 593, “Eu.” 194, 197, 424, 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Tyrannus” 406, 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Ranae” 1399, etc.]]; compare τοιόσδε near the end]

deep_entry:
Abbott-Smith / STEPBible (TBESG)
τοῖχος, -ου, ὁ
[in LXX chiefly for קִיר ;]
a wall, esp. of a house: figuratively, Act.23:3 (cf. τεῖχος).†
(AS)

---

LSJ / STEPBible (TFLSJ)
τοῖχος, ὁ,
wall of a house or enclosure, absolutely, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 2.342, 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Vespae” 130, etc.]]; ἅπαντ᾽ ἐρευνῶν τ. uncertain in [Refs 8th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Hecuba” 1174; τ. δώματος 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 16.212; μεγάροιο 18.374, compare 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 19.37]]; τ. καὶ θριγκοί (of the αὐλή)[Refs 8th c.BC+ [17.267, compare 8th-7th c.BC: Hesiodus Epicus “Opera et Dies” 732; τὸν τῆς αὐλῆς τ. “PEnteux.” 12.3 (3rd c.BC)]]; wall of a temple, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [Inscriptiones Graecae 12.372.51, +others; οἰκίας 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 574d; ἐν τοῖσι τ. ἔγραφ᾽ Ἀθηναῖοι καλοί 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Acharnenses” 144, compare 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Leges” 859a; εἰς τὸν τ. ἀντεγγραψάτω “IG” 12.94.24]]; νόμους ἀναγράφειν εἰς τοῖχον Decrees cited in [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Andocides Orator 1.84]]; κοινοὶ τ. party-walls, [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [“OGI” 483.101, +others (Pergam., 2nd c.AD)]]; τοίχῳ προσιστάμενοι γυμνάζονται [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd c.AD: Galenus Medicus 6.144]]: of the side of a tent or hut, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 9.219, 24.598, 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Ion” 1158.]]

__b
metaphorically, τοῖχε κεκονιαμένε, as a term of abuse, [NT.Act.23.3.]

__2
plural, sides of a ship, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 12.420, 6th c.BC: Theognis Elegiacus 674, 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Helena” 1573, 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 7.36, 3rd c.BC: Theocritus Poeta Bucolicus 22.12; τοίχου ἄρχω τοῦ δεξιοῦ 2nd c.AD: Lucianus Sophista “DMeretr.” 14.3, compare “JTr.” 49.]]

__3
of other things, as the human body, εἰς ἀμφοτέρους τοίχους (by metaphorically from a ship) [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Troades” 118 (_anapaest meter_), compare 2nd c.AD: Lucianus Sophista “Asin.” 9]]; of a cup, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Pherecrates Comicus 143.2]]; of a vessel, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Meteorologica” 359a3]]; of a bath (πύελος), [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd c.AD: Galenus Medicus 15.709.]]

__4
proverbial, τοίχους τοὺς δύο ἐπαλείφειν 'to run with the hare and hunt with the hounds', [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd c.AD: Pausanias Periegeta 6.3.15, compare 10th c.AD: Suidas Legal icographus]] see at {δύο τοίχου; ὁ εὖ πράττων τ}. 'the snug side of the ship', 'the right side of the hedge', [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Ranae” 537 (Lyric poetry); ἐς το᾽ν εὐτυχῆ τ. χωρεῖν 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Fragmenta” 89. (Akin to τεῖχος,]] but used in a special sense; later ={τεῖχος}, [LXX.Isa.25.12, probably so in “JHS” 24.39 (from Cyzicus).)]
