deep_entry:
Abbott-Smith / STEPBible (TBESG)
τόκος, -ου, ὁ
(τίκτω), [in LXX for נֶשֶׁךְ, etc. ;]
__(a) a bringing forth, birth;
__(b) offspring. Metaphorical, of the produce of money lent out, interest, usury (cf. Merch. of Venice, I, iii, "a breed of barren metal "): Mat.25:27, Luk.19:23 (Soph., Plat., al.).†
(AS)

---

LSJ / STEPBible (TFLSJ)
τόκος, ὁ,
(τίκτω) childbirth, parturition, of women, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 19.119, “hymnus ad Cererem” 101, “IG” 42(1).121.15,17 (Epid., 4th c.BC), 3rd c.BC: Herophilus Medicus cited in 2nd c.AD: Soranus Medicus 2.53]]; of animals, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 17.5; πλὴν ὅταν τ. παρῇ 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Fragmenta” 477; ποιεῖσθαι τὸν τ. 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Historia Animalium” 542a25, etc.: _plural_, τόκοισί τε ἀγόνοις γυναικῶν 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Tyrannus” 26, compare 173 (Lyric poetry), 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Medea” 1031, etc.]]

__b
the time of parturition, ὁ τ. τῆς γυναικός [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.111]]; period of gestation, ἐνιαύσιος ὁ τ. [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “de Generatione Animalium” 777b13.]]

__c
ἡ φύσις τοῦ παιδίου τοῦ ἐν τόκῳ in the foetal stage, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Hippocrates Medicus “Nat.Puer.” at Title Page (as cited in “Mul.” 1.1).]]

__II
offspring, of men or animals, πάντων Ἀργείων ἐρέων γενεήν τε τόκον τε [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 7.128, compare 15.141]]; of an eagle, ἐλθὼν ἐξ ὄρεος, ὅθι οἱ γενεή τε τόκος τε [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 15.175; μήλων τ. 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Cyclops” 162]]; Οἰδίπον τ. his son, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Septem contra Thebas” 372, compare 407, etc.]] (but also, daughter, θεὰ γεγῶσα καὶ θεοῦ πατρὸς τ. [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Andromache” [1254])]]; fry of fish, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Historia Animalium” 543a4]]; litter of pigs, πασῶν τῶν συῶν ἀπὸ τόκου χοῖρον λαμβάνειν [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Respublica Lacedaemoniorum” 15.5.]]

__II.2
metaphorically, produce of money lent, hence interest [Refs 5th c.BC+ [compare (5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Fragmenta” 477 (punningly), 5th c.BC: Sophron Comicus 35, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 555e, 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Politica” 1258b5), 5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “O.” 10(11).9, etc.; τ. ἐπίτριτος, see entry .; τ. πεντώβολος interest at 5]] obols per month on the mina, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [“IG” 11(2).146 B 17 (Delos, 4th c.BC)]]; τ. πεντεκαιδέκατος, i. e. 100/15 = 6 2/3%, [Refs 2nd c.BC+ [“SIG” 672.23 (Delph., 2nd c.BC)]]; singular and plural, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [“IG” 12.324.5, 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Nubes” 18, 20, 34, etc.; τόκους ἀποδοῦναι [prev. work] 739, etc.]]; κομίζεσθαι [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus [same place], “PEnteux.” 32.13 (3rd c.BC)]]; λαμβάνειν ἀπό τινος [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Isaeus Orator 8.35; ἀπολαμβάνειν 5th c.BC: Lysias Orator 17.3; δανείζειν ἐπὶ τόκῳ 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Leges” 742c; ὀφείλειν ἐπὶ τόκῳ 5th-6th c.BC: Isocrates Orator 17.7; τόκοι τόκων]]compound interest, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Nubes” 1156; τόκος τόκου 4th-3rd c.BC: Theophrastus Philosophus “Characteres” 10.10; τῶν τόκων ἔχων τόκους 4th-3rd c.BC: Menander Comicus 870:— 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus]] plays on the double meaning of the word, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [“Th.” 843f; so also 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 507a, 1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus 2.433e.]]

__II.3
metaphorically, interest, [γῄδιον] ὅτι λάβοι σπέρμα.. δικαίως ἀπεδίδου αὐτό τε καὶ τόκον [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 8.3.38, compare 4th-3rd c.BC: Philemo Comicus 231, 88.10; οἱ δ᾽ εἰς τὸ γῆρας ἀναβολὰς ποιούμενοι, οὗτοι προσαποτίνουσι τοῦ χρόνου τόκους 4th-3rd c.BC: Menander Comicus 235.9]]; offspring, ἢ τίκτων λόγους ἢ τὸν ἑτέρων τόκον λαμβάνων [Refs 4th c.AD+ [4th c.AD: Libanius Sophista “Orationes” 12.94]]; bringing forth, [Refs [[prev. work] 17.38.]]

__II.4
oppression, as translation of Hebrew τōκη, [LXX.Psa.71(72).14, LXX.Jer.9.6.]

Abbott-Smith / STEPBible (TBESG)
τολμάω, -ῶ
[in LXX: Job.15:12 (לָקַח), Est.1:18 7:5 (לֵב מָלֵא) Jdth.14:13, 2Ma.4:2, 3Ma.3:21 R, 4Ma.8:18 * ;]
to have courage, to venture, dare, be bold: absol, 2Co.11:21; before ἐπί, 2Co.10:2; with inf.  (Bl., § 69, 4), Mat.22:46, Mrk.12:34, Luk.20:40, Jhn.21:12, Act.5:13 7:32, Rom.15:18, 1Co.6:1, 2Co.10:12, Php.1:14, Ju 9; to submit to (in cl. usually absol. in this sense), Rom.5:7 (see Field, Notes, 155); τολμήσας εἰσῆλθεν, took courage and went in (see Field, op. cit., 44), Mrk.15:43 (cf. ἀπο-τολμάω).†
(AS)

---

LSJ / STEPBible (TFLSJ)
τολμ-άω,
Ionic dialect τολμέω [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 8.77]]; Doric dialect 2nd pers. singular τολμῇς [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [3rd c.BC: Theocritus Poeta Bucolicus 5.35]]: future τολμήσω [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Electra” 471]], Doric dialect -ᾱσῶ[Refs 3rd c.BC+ [3rd c.BC: Theocritus Poeta Bucolicus 14.67]]: perfect τετόλμηκα [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Prometheus Vinctus” 333]], Doric dialect -ᾱκα[Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “P.” 5.117]]:—middle, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Lysias Orator “Oxy.” 1606.420 (“Bodl. Quarterly Record” 5 (1928).303)]]:—undertake, take heart either to do or bear anything terrible or difficult:

__1
mostly absolutely, dare, endure, submit (see. Τλάω), ἐνὶ φρεσὶ θυμὸς ἐτόλμα [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 10.232]]; σὺ δ᾽ (i.e. κραδίη) ἐτόλμας [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 20.20; οὐδέ οἱ ἵπποι τόλμων 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 12.51; ἐγὼ δ᾽ ἐτόλμησ᾽ 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Prometheus Vinctus” 237, etc.; αἱ συμφοραὶ τοὺς ἡσυχίους τολμᾶν βιάζονται 5th c.BC: Antipho Orator 3.2.1; τ. καὶ ἐκλογίζεσθαι 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 2.40]]; τολμῶντες ἄνδρες[Refs 6th c.BC+ [[prev. work] 43, compare 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Trachiniae” 583; χρὴ τολμᾶν.. ἐν ἄλγεσι κείμενον ἄνδρα 6th c.BC: Theognis Elegiacus 555; τόλμα κακοῖσιν [prev. author] 355, 1029; τόλμα 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Philoctetes” 82; τόλμησον [prev. work] 481: in]]participle, τολμήσας.. παρέστη he took courage and.., [NT+1st c.AD+ [1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus “Camillus” 22, cf. NT.Mark.15.43.]]

__2
with accusative of things, endure, undergo, τ. χρὴ τὰ διδοῦσι θεοί [Refs 6th c.BC+ [6th c.BC: Theognis Elegiacus 591, compare 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Hecuba” 333, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Leges” 872e.]]

__II
with infinitive, to have the courage, hardihood, effrontery, cruelty, or the grace, patience, to do a thing in spite of any natural feeling, dare, or bring oneself, to do, εἰ.. τολμήσεις Διὸς ἄντα.. ἔγχος ἀεῖραι [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 8.424, compare 13.395, 17.68, 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 9.332, 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Ajax” 528, 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Nubes” 550, 5th c.BC: Lysias Orator 32.2, etc.; τόλμησον ὀρθῶς φρονεῖν 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Prometheus Vinctus” 999, compare 6th c.BC: Theognis Elegiacus 81, 377, etc.]]; τ. κατακεῖσθαι submit to keep one's bed, [NT+5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Hippocrates Medicus “περὶ ἀγμῶν” 10; τ. ἀποθανεῖν NT.Rom.5.7; οὐδὲ ἀπαιτούμενοι τὸν λόγον ἐτόλμησαν ἡμῖν δοῦναι “PCair.Zen.” 330.5 (3rd c.BC).]]

__II.2
sometimes with participle, ἐτόλμα.. βαλλόμενος he submitted to be struck, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 24.162; τόλμα ἐρῶσα 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Hippolytus” 476, compare 6th c.BC: Theognis Elegiacus 442, 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Hercules Furens” 756.]]

__II.3
with accusative, πόλεμον τολμήσαντα undertaking, venturing on it, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 8.519; [ἐσόδους] τετόλμακε 5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “P.” 5.117]]; τ. πάντα, δεινά, ἔργον αἴσχιστον, etc., [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Coloneus” 761, 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Iphigenia Aulidensis” 133 (_anapaest meter_), “Med.” 695, etc.; ὦ πᾶν σὺ τολμήσασα καὶ πέρα 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Fragmenta” 189; also τ. τὰ βέλτιστα 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 3.56, 4.98; πικρὰν πεῖραν 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Electra” 471]]; see at {τόλμημα}:—hence in passive, ο ἐτολμήθη πατήρ such things as my father had dared (or done) against him, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Electra” 277]]; τοῦτο τετολμήσθω εἰπεῖν let us take courage to say this, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 503b; τὰ τολμηθέντα 1st c.AD: Josephus Historicus “Antiquitates Judaicae” 2.3.1; αἱ τετολμημέναι ἐπίνοιαι 1st c.AD: Philo Judaeus 1.674; τὰ τετ. εἰς ἐμέ “PGoodsp.Cair.” 15.3 (4th c.AD).]]

__II.4
so in active, τετολμηκυῖαι [λέξεις] daring expressions, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [1st c.BC: Philodemus Gadarensis Epigrammaticus “Rh.” 1.341 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus]]

deep_entry:
Abbott-Smith / STEPBible (TBESG)
τότε, demonstr. adv. of time, correlat. of ὅτε,
then, at that time;
__(a) of concurrent events: Mat.2:17 3:5 and freq., Rom.6:21; before ptcp., Mat.2:16, Gal.4:8; opposite to νῦν, Gal.4:29, Heb.12:26; ὁ τ. κόσμος, 2Pe.3:6;
__(b) of consequent events, then, thereupon: Mat.2:7 3:5 4:1 and freq., Luk.11:26; τ. οὖν, Jhn.11:14 19:1, 16 20:8; εὐθέως τ., Act.17:14; ὅτε . . . τ., Mat.13:26 21:1, Jhn.12:16; ἀπὸ τ., Mat.4:17 16:21 26:16, Luk.16:16;
__(with) of things future: Mat.24:28, 40 25:1, 31ff.; opposite to ἄρτι, 1Co.13:12; καὶ τ., Mat.7:23, Mrk.13:21, Luk.21:27, 1Co.4:5, al.; ὅταν . . . τ., Mat.9:15, Mrk.2:20, Luk.5:35, 1Th.5:3, al. (more frequently in Mt than in the rest of the NT).

Doric dialect τόκᾰ (which see) (both forms in [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus (τότε “P.” 2.89, τόκα “O.” 6.66) and 3rd c.BC: Theocritus Poeta Bucolicus (τότε 13.23, τόκα 7.154))]]; Aeolic dialect τότᾰ [Refs 7th c.BC+ [7th-6th c.BC: Alcaeus Lyricus “Oxy.” 1789 “fragment” 1i12 (τόκα]] accusative to codices of [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [3rd c.BC: Theocritus Poeta Bucolicus 29.39]], compare ποτα, ὄτα):— adverb at that time, then, corresponding to Relat. ὅτε or ὁπότε (below [Refs [1.5), and to _interrogative_ πότε]]; mostly of some point in past time, opposed to νῦν, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 15.724, etc.: with _genitive_, τ. τοῦ χειμῶνος 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 7.31]]: also of a future time, τότε κέν μιν.. πεπίθοιμεν [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 1.100, compare 4.182; λέξεις καὶ τότ᾽ εἴσομαι 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Tyrannus” 1517 (troch.)]] (or of imagined circumstances, in that case [Refs 5th c.BC+ [compare (νῦν 1.4), 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 334c)]]; sometimes, then, next, πρῶτον μὲν.., εἶτα.., καὶ τ... [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 24.48]]:—in Trag. and Attic dialect also in indefinite sense, formerly, καὶ νῦν θ᾽ ὁμοίως καὶ τότ᾽ ἐξεπίσταμαι [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Electra” 907, compare “Ant.” 391, “Aj.” 650, 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Plutus” 1117, “Lys.” 1023 (Lyric poetry); ὃ δὴ καὶ τότε ἐλέγομεν]]just now, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Theaetetus” 157a]]; τ. μὲν.., νῦν δὲ.. [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Agamemnon” 799 (_anapaest meter_), compare 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Alcestis” 915 (_anapaest meter_); νῦν.. τότ᾽ [prev. author] “Med.” 1402 (_anapaest meter_); ὁμοῖοι καὶ τ. καὶ νῦν 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 1.86, compare 3.40, 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 6.12; also τότ᾽ ἢ τόθ᾽, ὅτε τὸ κύριον μόλῃ]]at one time or other, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Agamemnon” 766 (Lyric poetry); συμφοραὶ.. βροτοῖσιν ἢ τότ᾽ ἦλθον ἢ τ. 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Andromache” 853.]]

LXX.Psa.92(93).2, NT.Matt.4.17.]]

in apodosi, answering to ὅτε, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Coloneus” 778, etc.]]; to ὅταν, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Agamemnon” 971, 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Aves” 1116 (troch.)]]; to ὁππότε, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 16.244, 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 23.257]]; to ὁππότε κεν or ὁπότ᾽ ἂν δή, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 9.702, 21.341; to ἀλλ᾽ ὅτε δή, [prev. work] 451; to εἰ, 4.36; to ἐπεί κε, 11.192]]; to ἡνίκα, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Ajax” 773: also after a]]participle, like {εἶτα}, πάντα ἐάσαντες καὶ μόνον οὐχὶ συγκατασκευάσαντες αὐτῷ τ... ζητήσομε; [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 3.17, compare 9.73 (interpolated), etc.: frequently joined with other Particles, δὴ τ.]] after η ος, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 1.476; after αὐτὰρ ἐπεί, 12.17]]; after ὁππότε κεν, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 10.294]]; also καὶ τ. δή after ἦμος, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 8.69, 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 9.59]]; after ἀλλ᾽ ὅτε δή, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 22.209, 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 4.461]]; δή ῥα τ. after εὖτ᾽ ἄν, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th-7th c.BC: Hesiodus Epicus “Opera et Dies” 565; τότ᾽ ἔπειτα after αὐτὰρ ἐπὴν δή, [prev. work] 616]]; καὶ τότ᾽ ἔπειτα after ἦμος, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 1.478.]]

LSJ / STEPBible (TFLSJ)
ὁ,
ἡ, τό, is, when thus written,

__A
demonstrative Pronoun.

__B
in Attic dialect, definite or prepositive Article.

__C
in Epic dialect, the so-called postpositive Article, = relative Pronoun, ὅς, ἥ, ὅ.—The nominative masculine and feminine singular and plural, ὁ, ἡ, οἱ, αἱ, have no accent in codices and most printed books, except when used as the relative; but ὁ, ἡ, οἱ, αἱ differ only in writing from ὃ, ἣ, οἳ, α; the nominative forms of the article are said by Hdn.Gr.1.474 to be oxytone, and by [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd c.AD: Apollonius Dyscolus Grammaticus “de Pronominibus;” 8.7 not to be enclitic. The forms τῶν, τοῖς, ταῖς were barytone (i. e. τὼν, τοὶς, ταὶς)]] in Aeolic dialect accusative to [Refs 8th c.BC+ [3rd-2nd c.BC: Aristarchus Grammaticus cited in 2nd c.AD: Apollonius Dyscolus Grammaticus “de Syntaxi;” 51.26. For οἱ, αἱ some dialects (not 5th c.AD: Cypria, compare “Inscription Cyprian dialect” 135.30H., nor Cretan dialect, compare “Leg.Gort.” 5.28, nor Lesbian, compare 7th-6th c.BC: Alcaeus Lyricus 81, 7th-6th c.BC: Sappho Lyrica “Papyrus fragments” in E. Diehl, 5.1) and 8th c.BC: Homerus Epicus have τοί, ταί (though οἱ, αἱ are also found in 8th c.BC: Homerus Epicus): other Homeric forms are _genitive_ _sing._ τοῖο,]] genitive and dative dual τοῖιν [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 18.34, +others: _genitive_ _plural_ _feminine_ τάων [ᾱ], _dative_ τοῖσι, τῇς and τῇσι, never ταῖσι or ταῖς in 8th c.BC: Homerus Epicus]]— In Doric dialect and all other dialects except Attic dialect and Ionic dialect the feminine forms preserve the old ᾱ instead of changing it to η, hence Doric dialect etc. ἁ, τάν, τᾶ; the genitive plural τάων contracts in many dialects to τᾶ; the genitive singular is in many places τῶ, accusative plural τώς, but Cretan dialect, etc., τόνς [Refs [(“Leg.Gort.” 7.7, +others) or τός ([prev. work]3.50, +others)]]; in Lesbian Aeolic dialect the accusative plural forms are τοὶς, ταὶς, [Refs [“IG” 12(2).645 A 13, B 62]]; dative plural τοῖς, ταῖς (or τοὶς, ταὶς, see above), [Refs [[prev. work]645 A 8, [prev. work]1.6]]; ταῖσι as demonstrative, [Refs 7th c.BC+ [7th-6th c.BC: Sappho Lyrica 16. The _Attic dialect_]] Poets also used the Ionic dialect and _Epic dialect_ forms τοῖσι, ταῖσ; and in Trag. we find τοὶ μέν.., τοὶ δέ.., for οἱ μέν.., οἱ δέ.., not only in Lyric poetry, as [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Persae” 584, “Th.” 295, 298; οἱ μέν.. τοὶ δ᾽ 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Ajax” 1404 (_anapaest meter_)]]; but even in a trimeter, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Persae” 424. __A
ὁ, ἡ, τό, DEMONSTR. PRONOUN, that, the oldest and in [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Homerus Epicus]] the commonest sense: frequently also in [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus (1.86, 5.35, +others)]], and sometimes in Trag. (mostly in Lyric poetry, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Supplices” 1047, etc.; in trimeters, [prev. author] “Th.” 197, “Ag.” 7, “Eu.” 174]]; τῶν γάρ.., τῆς γάρ.., [Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. author] “Supp.” 358, 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Tyrannus” 1082]]; seldom in Attic dialect Prose, except in special phrases, see infr. VI, VII):

__A.I
joined with a substantive, to call attention to it, ὁ Τυδεΐδης he—Tydeus' famous son, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 11.660]]; τὸν Χρύσην that venerable man Chryses, I.II: and so with appellative, Νέστωρ ὁ γέρων N.—thataged man, [Refs [7.324]]; αἰετοῦ.. τοῦ θηρητῆρος the eagle, that which is called hunter, [Refs [21.252, +others]]; also to define and give emphasis, τιμῆς τῆς Πριάμου for honour, namely that of Priam, [Refs [20.181]]; οἴχετ᾽ ἀνὴρ ὤριστος a man is gone, and he the best, [Refs [11.288, compare 13.433, +others: sometimes with words between the _pronoun_ and Noun, αὐτὰρ ὁ αὖτε Πέλοψ 2.105; τὸν Ἕκτορι μῦθον ἐνίσπες 11.186, compare 703, +others]]:—different from this are cases [Refs 8th c.BC+ [like 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 1.409 αἴ κέν πως ἐθέλῃσιν ἐπὶ Τρώεσσιν ἀρῆξαι, τοὺς δὲ κατὰ πρύμνας τε καὶ ἀμφ᾽ ἅλα ἔλσαι Ἀχαιούς]] if he would help the Trojans, but drive those back to the ships—I mean the Achaeans, where Ἀχ. is only added to explain τούς, compare [Refs [1.472, 4.20, 329, +others]]

__A.II
frequently without a substantive, he, she, it, ὁ γὰρ ἦλθε [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 1.12, +others]]

__A.III
placed after its Noun, before the Relat. Prons., ἐφάμην σὲ περὶ φρένας ἔμμεναι ἄλλων, τῶν ὅσσοι Λυκίην ναιετάουσι far above the rest, above those to wit who, etc., [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 17.172]]; οἷ᾽ οὔ πώ τιν᾽ ἀκούομεν οὐδὲ παλαιῶν, τάων αἳ πάρος ἦσαν.. Ἀχαιαί such as we have not heard tell of yet even among the women of old, those women to wit who.., [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 2.119, compare 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 5.332; θάλαμον τὸν ἀφίκετο, τόν ποτε τέκτων ξέσσεν 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 21.43, compare 1.116, 10.74:]] —for the _Attic dialect_ usage see below

__A.IV
before a Possessive pronoun its demonstrative force is sometimes very manifest, φθίσει σε τὸ σὸν μένος that spirit of thine, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 6.407, compare 11.608; but in 15.58, 16.40, and elsewhere it is merely the _Article_]]

__A.V
for cases in which the Homeric usage approaches most nearly to the Attic, see below [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Bacchylides Lyricus [near the start]]]

__A.VI
ὁ μέν.., ὁ δέ.. without a substantive, in all cases, genders, and numbers, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Homerus Epicus, etc.: sometimes in Opposition, where ὁ μέν]] properly refers to the former, ὁ δέ to the latter; more rarely ὁ μέν the latter, ὁ δέ the former, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Protagoras” 359e, 5th-6th c.BC: Isocrates Orator 2.32,34]]: sometimes in Partition, the one.., the other.., etc.—The Noun with it is regularly in genitive plural, being divided by the ὁ μέν.., ὁ δέ.., into parts, ἠΐθεοι καὶ παρθένοι.., τῶν δ᾽ αἱ μὲν λεπτὰς ὀθόνας ἔχον, οἱ δὲ χιτῶνας εἵατο [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 18.595; τῶν πόλεων αἱ μὲν τυραννοῦνται, αἱ δὲ δημοκρατοῦνται, αἱ δὲ ἀριστοκρατοῦνται 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 338d, etc.]]: but frequently the Noun is in the same case, by a kind of apposition, ἴδον υἷε Δάρητος, τὸν μὲν ἀλευάμενον τὸν δὲ κτάμενον [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 5.28, compare 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 12.73, etc.]]: so in Trag. and Attic dialect, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Antigone” 22, etc.; πηγὴ ἡ μὲν εἰς αὐτὸν ἔδυ, ἡ δὲ ἔξω ἀπορρεῖ 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Phaedrus” 255c]]; if the Noun be collective, it is in the genitive singular, ὁ μὲν πεπραμένος ἦν τοῦ σίτου, ὁ δὲ ἔνδον ἀποκείμενος [Refs 8th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 42.6: sometimes a Noun is added in apposition with ὁ μέν or ὁ δέ, ὁ μὲν οὔτασ᾽ Ἀτύμνιον ὀξέϊ δουρὶ Ἀντίλοχος.., Μάρις δὲ.. 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 16.317 - 19, compare 116; τοὺς μὲν τὰ δίκαια ποιεῖν ἠνάγκασα, τοὺς πλουσίους, τοὺς δὲ πένητας κτλ. 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 18.102, compare 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Gorgias” 501a, etc.]]

__A.VI.2
when a negative accompanies ὁ δέ, it follows δέ, e.g. τὰς γοῦν Ἀθήνας οἶδα τὸν δὲ χῶρον οὔ [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Coloneus” 24; τὸν φιλόσοφον σοφίας ἐπιθυμητὴν εἶναι, οὐ τῆς μὲν τῆς δ᾽ οὔ, ἀλλὰ πάσης 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 475b; οὐ πάσας χρὴ τὰς δόξας τιμᾶν, ἀλλὰ τὰς μὲν τὰς δ᾽ οὔ· οὐδὲ πάντων, ἀλλὰ τῶν μὲν τῶν δ᾽ οὔ [prev. author] “Cri.” 47a, etc.]]

__A.VI.3
ὁ μέν τις.., ὁ δέ τις.. is used in Prose, when the Noun to which ὁ refers is left indefinite, ἔλεγον ὁ μέν τις τὴν σοφίαν, ὁ δὲ τὴν καρτερίαν.., ὁ δέ τις καὶ τὸ κάλλος [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 3.1.41; νόμους.. τοὺς μὲν ὀρθῶς τιθέασιν τοὺς δέ τινας οὐκ ὀρθῶς 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 339c, compare “Phlb.” 13c.]]

__A.VI.4
on τὸ μέν.., τὸ δέ.., or τὰ μέν.., τὰ δέ.., [Refs [see infr. VIII. 4.]]

__A.VI.5
ὁ μέν is frequently used without a corresponding ὁ δέ, οἱ μὲν ἄρ᾽ ἐσκίδναντο.., Μυρμιδόνας δ᾽ οὐκ εἴα ἀποσκίδνασθαι [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 23.3, compare 24.722, 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 8.12, etc.: also followed by ἀλλά, ἡ μὲν γάρ μ᾽ ἐκέλευε.., ἀλλ᾽ ἐγὼ οὐκ ἔθελον 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 7.304]]; by ἄλλος δέ, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 6.147, etc.; τὸν μὲν.., ἕτερον δέ 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Aves” 843, etc.; ὁ μέν.., ὃς δέ.. 6th c.BC: Theognis Elegiacus 205 (variant{οὐδέ}): less frequently ὁ δέ in the latter clause without ὁ μέν preceding, τῇ ῥα παραδραμέτην φεύγων, ὁ δ᾽ ὄπισθε διώκων (for ὁ μὲν φεύγων) 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 22.157; σφραγῖδε.. χρυσοῦν ἔχουσα τὸν δακτύλιον, ἡ δ᾽ ἑτέρα ἀργυροῦν “IG” 22.1388.45, compare μέν 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator III; γεωργὸς μὲν εἷς, ὁ δὲ οἰκοδόμος, ἄλλος δέ τις ὑφαντής 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 369d, compare “Tht.” 181d.]]

__A.VI.6
ὁ δέ following μέν sometimes refers to the subject of the preceding clause, τοῦ μὲν ἅμαρθ᾽, ὁ δὲ Λεῦκον.. βεβλήκει [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 4.491; τὴν μὲν γενομένην αὐτοῖσι αἰτίην οὐ μάλα ἐξέφαινε, ὁ δὲ ἔλεγέ σφι 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 6.3, compare 1.66, 6.9, 133, 7.6]]: rare in Attic dialect Prose, ἐπεψήφιζεν αὐτὸς ἔφορος ὤν· ὁ δὲ οὐκ ἔφη διαγιγνώσκειν τὴν βοήν [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 1.87; ἔμενον ὡς κατέχοντες τὸ ἄκρον· οἱ δ᾽ οὐ κατεῖχον 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 4.2.6: this is different from ὁ δέ in apodosi, see below 7; also from passages in which both clauses have a common verb, see at {ὅ γε} 11.]]

__A.VI.7
ὁ δέ is frequently used simply in continuing a narrative, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 1.43, etc.]]; also used by [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Homerus Epicus in apodosi after a _relative_, see at {ὅδε} III.3.]]

__A.VI.8
the opposition may be expressed otherwise than by μέν and δέ, οὔθ᾽ ὁ.. οὔθ᾽ ὁ [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 15.417; ἢ τοῖσιν ἢ τοῖς 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Supplices” 439; οὔτε τοῖς οὔτε τοῖς 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Leges” 701e.]]

__A.VII
the following usages prevailed in Attic dialect Prose,

__A.VII.1
in dialogue, after καί, it was usual to say in nominative singular masculine καὶ ὅ; in the other cases the usual forms of the Article were used (see. ὅς [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus]] II.I and cf. Sanskrit sas, alternatative form of sa); so, in accusative, καὶ τὸν εἰπεῖν [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Symposium” 174a, compare 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 1.3.9, etc.; also in 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus, καὶ τὴν φράσαι 6.61, +others]]

__A.VII.2
ὁ καὶ ὁ such and such, τῇ καὶ τῇ ἀτιμίᾳ [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Leges” 721b]]: but mostly in accusative, καί μοι κάλει τὸν καὶ τόν [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Lysias Orator 1.23, compare 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Leges” 784d; τὰ καὶ τὰ πεπονθώς 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 21.141, compare 9.68; τὸ καὶ τό [prev. author] 18.243]]; ἀνάγκη ἄρα τὸ καὶ τό it must then be so and so, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Rhetorica” 1401a4, compare 1413a22]]; but τὰ καὶ τά now one thing, now another, of good and bad, τὸν δ᾽ ἀγαθὸν τολμᾶν χρὴ τά τε καὶ τὰ φέρειν [Refs 6th c.BC+ [6th c.BC: Theognis Elegiacus 398, compare 5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “P.” 5.55, 7.20, +others; τῶν τε καὶ τῶν καιρόν [prev. author] “O.” 2.53]]; so πάντα τοῦ μετρίου μεταβαλλόμενα ἐπὶ τὰ καὶ ἐπὶ τά, of excess and defect, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Hippocrates Medicus “περὶ διαίτης ὀξέων” 46; compare 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus VI.8.]]

__A.VIII
absolutely usages of single cases,

__A.VIII.1
feminine dative τῇ, of Place, there, on that spot, here, this way, that way, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 5.752, 858, +others: followed by ᾗ, 13.52]], etc.: also in Prose, τὸ μὲν τῇ, τὸ δὲ τῇ [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Respublica Atheniensium” 2.12.]]

__A.VIII.1.b
with a notion of motion towards, that way, in that direction, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 10.531, 11.149, 12.124; τῇ ἴμεν ᾗ.. 15.46; δελφῖνες τῇ καὶ τῇ ἐθύνεον ἰχθυάοντες 8th-7th c.BC: Hesiodus Epicus “Scutum Herculis” 210:]] —only poetry

__A.VIII.1.c
of Manner, τῇ περ τελευτήσεσθαι ἔμελλεν in this way, thus, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 8.510.]]

__A.VIII.1.d
repeated, τῇ μέν.., τῇ δέ.., in one way.., in another.., or partly.., partly.., [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Orestes” 356, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Symposium” 211a, etc.: without μέν, τῇ μᾶλλον, τῇ δ᾽ ἧσσον 4th-5th c.BC: Parmenides Poeta Philosophus 8.48.]]

relative, where, by which way, only Epic dialect, as [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 12.118, 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 4.229.]]

__A.VIII.2
neuter dative τῷ, therefore, on this account, frequently in [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Homerus Epicus, 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 1.418, 2.254, +others (see. below): also in Trag., 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Prometheus Vinctus” 239, 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Tyrannus” 510 (Lyric poetry); in Prose, τῷ τοι.. 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Theaetetus” 179d, “Sph.” 230b.]]

__A.VIII.2.b
thus, so, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 2.373, 13.57, etc.: it may also, especially when εἰ]] precedes, be translated, then, if this be so, on this condition, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 1.239, 3.224, 258, +others, 3rd c.BC: Theocritus Poeta Bucolicus 29.11.—In 8th c.BC: Homerus Epicus the true form is probably τῶ, as in codex A, or τώ,compare 2nd c.AD: Apollonius Dyscolus Grammaticus “de Adverbiis;” 199.2.]]

__A.VIII.3
neuter accusative τό, wherefore, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 3.176, 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 8.332, +others, 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Philoctetes” 142 (Lyric poetry)]]; also τὸ δέ absolutely, but the fact is.., [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Apologia” 23a, “Men.” 97c, “Phd.” 109d, “Tht.” 157b, “R.” 340d, “Lg.” 967a]]; even when the τό refers to what precedes, the contrast may lie not in the thing referred to, but in another part of the sentence (compare above[Refs 5th c.BC+ [VI. 6), τὸ δ᾽ ἐπὶ κακουργίᾳ.. ἐπετήδευσαν 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 1.37; τὸ δὲ.. ἡμῖν μᾶλλον περιέσται [prev. author] 2.89]]; φασὶ δέ τινες αὐτὸν καὶ τῶν ἑπτὰ σοφῶν γεγονέναι· τὸ δὲ οὐκ ἦν but he was not, [Refs 1st c.BC+ [1st c.BC: Nicolaus Damascenus Historicus 58J.]]

τὸ μέν.., τὸ δέ.., partly.., partly.., or on the one hand.., on the other.., [Refs 8th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 7.36, etc., compare 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 2.46]]; more frequently τὰ μέν.., τὰ δέ.., [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.173, 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Trachiniae” 534, etc.; also τὰ μέν τι.., τὰ δέ τι.. 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 4.1.14; τὸ μέν τι.., τὸ δέ τι.. 2nd c.AD: Lucianus Sophista “Macr.” 14; τὰ μέν.., τὸ δὲ πλέον.. 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 1.90: sometimes without τὸ μέν..]] in the first clause, τὸ δέ τι [Refs [[prev. author] 1.107, 7.48: rarely of Time, τὰ μὲν πολλὰ.., τέλος δέ]] several times..  and finally, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 3.85.]]

of Time, sometimes that time, sometimes this (present) time, συνμαχία κ᾽ ἔα ἑκατὸν ϝέτεα, ἄρχοι δέ κα τοΐ (where it is possible, but not necessary, to supply ϝέτος) [Refs 6th c.BC+ [“SIG” 9.3 (Olympia, 6th c.BC): so with Preps., ἐκ τοῦ, _Epic dialect_ τοῖο,]] from that time, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 1.493, 15.601.]]

πρὸ τοῦ, sometimes written προτοῦ, before this, aforetime, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.103, 122, 5.55, 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Agamemnon” 1204, 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Nubes” 5, etc.; ἐν τῷ πρὸ τοῦ χρόνῳ 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 1.32, compare 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Eumenides” 462; τὸ πρὸ τοῦ 1st c.BC: Diodorus Siculus Historicus 20.59.]]

__A.VIII.5.c
in Thess. Prose, ὑππρὸ τᾶς yesterday, τὰ ψαφίσματα τό τε ὑππρὸ τᾶς γενόμενον καὶ τὸ τᾶμον the decree which was passed yesterday (literal before this [day]), and to-day's, [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [“IG” 9(2).517.43 (Larissa, 3rd c.BC).]]

__A.VIII.6
ἐν τοῖς is frequently used in Prose with Superlatives, ἐν τοῖσι θειότατον a most marvellous thing, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 7.137]]; ἐν τοῖς πρῶτοι the very first, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 1.6, etc.]]; ἐν τοῖσι πρῶτος (πρώτοις codices) [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Pherecrates Comicus 145.4]]; [Ζεὺς] Ἔρωτά τε καὶ Ἀνάγκην ἐν τοῖς πρῶτα ἐγέννησεν first of all, [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd c.AD: Aristides Rhetor “Orationes” 43(1).16, compare 37(2).2: when used with _feminine_ Nouns, ἐν τοῖς remained without change of gender, ἐν τοῖς πλεῖσται δὴ νῆες]] the greatest number of ships, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 3.17; ἐν τοῖς πρώτη ἐγένετο (i.e. ἡ στάσις) [prev. work] 82]]: also with adverbs, ἐν τοῖς μάλιστα [Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. author] 8.90, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Crito” 52a, 1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus 2.74e, 421d, 723e, “Brut.” 6, 11, +others, 2nd c.AD: Pausanias Periegeta 1.16.3, etc.; ἐν τοῖς χαλεπώτατα 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 7.71; τὴν Αἴγυπτον ἐν τοῖς μάλιστα μελάγγειον οὖσαν 1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus 2.364c]]: in late Prose, also with Positives, ἐν τοῖς παράδοξον [Refs 1st c.BC+ [2nd c.AD: Aristides Rhetor “Orationes” 48(24).47 codices; with πάνυ, ἐν τοῖς πάνυ 1st c.BC: Dionysius Halicarnassensis 1.19, compare 66 (ἐν ταῖς πάνυ _falsa lectio_ 4.14, 15).]]

__B
ὁ, ἡ, τό, THE DEFINITE ARTICLE, the, to specify individuals: rare in this signification in the earliest Gr., becoming commoner later. In [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Homerus Epicus]] the demonstrative force can generally be traced, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [see above 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus]] I, but the definite Article must be recognized in places [Refs 8th c.BC+ [like 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 1.167, 7.412, 9.309, 12.289, 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 19.372]]: also when joined to an adjective to make it a substantive, αἰὲν ἀποκτείνων τὸν ὀπίστατον the hindmost man, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 11.178; τὸν ἄριστον 17.80; τὸν δύστηνον 22.59; τὸν προὔχοντα 23.325; τῷ πρώτῳ.., τῷ δευτέρῳ.., etc., [prev. work] 265s q]].; also in τῶν ἄλλων [Refs [2.674, +others: with Advs., τὸ πρίν 24.543, +others; τὸ πάρος περ 17.720; τὸ πρόσθεν 23.583]]; also τὸ τρίτον[Refs [[prev. work] 733; τὰ πρῶτα 1.6, +others]]; τὸ μὲν ἄλλο for the rest,[Refs [23.454; ἀνδρῶν τῶν τότε 9.559.]]—The true Article, however, is first fully established in fifth-century. Attic dialect, whilst the demonstrative usage disappears, except in a few cases, V. [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus VI-VIII.]] —Chief usages, especially in _Attic dialect_

__B.I
not only with common Appellats., adjectives, and Parts., to specify them as present to sense or mind, but also frequently where we use the Possessive pronoun, τὸ κέαρ ηὐφράνθην [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Acharnenses” 5]]; τὴν κεφαλὴν κατεάγην my head was broken, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Andocides Orator 1.61, etc.]]; τοὺς φίλους ποιούμεθα we make our friends, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Antigone” 190]]; τὰς πόλεις ἔκτιζον they began founding their cities, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 1.12; οὐχ ὑπὲρ τὴν οὐσίαν ποιούμενοι τοὺς παῖδας 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 372b.]]

__B.I.b
omitted with proper nounsand frequently with Appellats. which require no specification, as θεός, βασιλεύς, see at {θεός} [Refs [I.1, βασιλεύς]] III; ἐμ πόλει in the Acropolis, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [“IG” 12.4.1, +others: but added to proper nouns, when attention is to be called to the previous mention of the person, as 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus (3.70) speaks first of Πειθίας and then refers to him repeatedly as ὁ Π.]]; compare Θράσυλος in [Refs [[prev. author] 8.104, with ὁ Θ. [prev. work] 105]]; or when the person spoken of is to be specially distinguished, Ζεύς, ὅστις ὁ Ζεύς whoever this Zeus is, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Fragmenta” 480]]; and therefore properly omitted when a special designation follows, as Σωκράτης ὁ φιλόσοφος: seldom in Trag. with proper nouns, save to give peculiar emphasis, like Latin ille, ὁ Λάϊος, ὁ Φοῖβος, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Tyrannus” 729, “El.” 35, etc.: later, however, the usage became very common (the Homeric usage of ὁ with a _proper name_ is different, see A.I).]]

__B.I.c
Aristotle says Σωκράτης meaning the historical Socrates, as in [Refs [“SE” 183b7, “PA” 642a28, +others, but ὁ Σωκράτης]] when he means the Platonic Socrates, as [Refs [“Pol.” 1261a6, +others: so with other proper nouns, “EN” 1145a21, 1146a21, +others]]

__B.I.d
for Σαῦλος ὁ καὶ Παῦλος, etc., see at {καί} [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Bacchylides Lyricus 2.]]

__B.I.2
in a generic sense, where the individual is treated as a type, οἷς ὁ γέρων μετέῃσιν.. λεύσσει [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 3.109; πονηρὸν ὁ συκοφάντης 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 18.242, etc.]]

__B.I.2.b
frequently with abstract Nouns, ἥ τε ἐλπὶς καὶ ὁ ἔρως [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 3.45, etc.]]

__B.I.3
of outstanding members of a class, ὁ γεωγράφος, ὁ κωμικός, ὁ ποιητής, ὁ τεχνικός, see at {γεωγράφος}, κωμικός, ποιητής, τεχνικός.

__B.I.4
with infinitives, which thereby become Substantives, τὸ εἴργειν prevention, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Gorgias” 505b]]; τὸ φρονεῖν good sense, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Antigone” 1348 (_anapaest meter_), etc.: when the subject is expressed it is put between the _Article_ and the]]infinitive, τὸ θεοὺς εἶναι the existence of gods, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Phaedo” 62b]]; τὸ μηδένα εἶναι ὄλβιον the fact or statement that no one is happy, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.86.]]

__B.I.5
in neuter before any word or expression which itself is made the object of thought, τὸ ἄνθρωπος the word or notion man; τὸ λέγω the word λέγ; τὸ μηδὲν ἄγαν the sentiment 'ne quid nimis', [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Hippolytus” 265 (Lyric poetry)]]; τὸ τῇ αὐτῇ the phrase τῇ αὐτῇ, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Meno” 72e: and so before whole clauses, ἡ δόξα.. περὶ τοῦ οὕστινας δεῖ ἄρχειν]] the opinion about the question 'who ought to rule', [Refs [[prev. author] “R.” 431e]]; τὸ ἐὰν μένητε παρ᾽ ἐμοί, ἀποδώσω the phrase 'I will give back, if.. ', [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 5.1.21, compare 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 327c, etc.; τοὺς τοῦ τί πρακτέον λογισμούς 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 23.148]]; τὸ ὀλίγοι the term few, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Politica” 1283b11.]]

__B.I.6
before relative clauses, when the Article serves to combine the whole relative clause into one notion, τῇ ᾗ φὴς σὺ σκληρότητι the harshness you speak of, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Cratylus” 435a]]; τὸν ἥμερον καρπόν.., καὶ τὸν ὅσος ξύλινος (i.e. καὶ τὸν καρπὸν ὅσος ἂν ᾖ ξύλινος) [Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. author] “Criti.” 115b; τῶν ὅσοι ἂν.. ἀγαθοὶ κριθῶσιν [prev. author] “R.” 469b; ἐκ γῆς καὶ πυρὸς μείξαντες καὶ τῶν ὅσα πυρὶ καὶ γῇ κεράννυται [prev. author] “Prt.” 320d, compare 4th c.BC: Hyperides Orator “pro Lycophrone” 2; ταύτην τε τὴν αἰτίαν καὶ τὴν ὅθεν ἡ κίνησις 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Metaphysica” 987a8; τὸν ὃς ἔφη 5th c.BC: Lysias Orator 23.8: hence the _relative_, by attraction, frequently follows the case of the _Article_, τοῖς οἵοις ἡμῖν τε καὶ ὑμῖν, i.e. τοῖς οὖσιν οἷοι ἡμεῖς καὶ ὑμεῖς, 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Historia Graeca (Hellenica)” 2.3.25, etc.]]

__B.I.7
before Prons.,

__B.I.7.a
before the person Prons., giving them greater emphasis, but only in accusative, τὸν ἐμέ [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Theaetetus” 166a, “Phlb.” 20b]]; τὸν.. σὲ καὶ ἐμέ[Refs [[prev. work] 59b; τὸν αὑτόν [prev. author] “Phdr.” 258a; on ὁ αὐτός, see at {αὐτός} 111.]]

__B.I.7.b
before the interrogative pronoun (both τίς and ποῖος), referring to something before, which needs to be more distinctly specified, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Prometheus Vinctus” 251, 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Pax” 696; also τὰ τ; because οἷα went before, [prev. work] 693. Of τίς only the _neuter_ is thus used (see.above): ποῖος is thus used not only in _neuter_ _plural_, τὰ ποῖ; 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Phoenissae” 707; but also in the other genders, ὁ ποῖο; [prev. work] 1704]]; τῆς ποίας μερίδο; [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 18.64]]; τοῖς ποίοις..; [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Physica” 227b1.]]

__B.I.7.c
with τοιοῦτος, τοιόσδε, τηλικοῦτος, etc., the Article either makes the pronoun into a substantive, ὁ τοιοῦτος that sort of person, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Memorabilia” 4.2.21, etc.]]; or subjoins it to a substantive which already has an Article, τὴν ἀπολογίαν τὴν τοιαύτην [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 41.13.]]

__B.I.8
before ἅπας, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “N.” 1.69, 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 3.64, 7.153 (assuming variant), 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Coloneus” 1224 (Lyric poetry), 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 18.231, etc.]]; also τὸν ἕνα, τὸν ἕνα τοῦτον, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Politica” 1287b8, 1288a19: on its usage with ἕκαστος,]] see entry; and on οἱ ἄλλοι, οἱ πολλοί, etc., see at {ἄλλος} [Refs [11.6, πολύς 11.3, etc.]]

__B.I.9
the Article with the comparative is rare, if ἤ follows, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Antigone” 313, “OC” 796.]]

__B.II
elliptic expressions:

__B.II.1
before the genitive of a proper name, to express descent, son or daughter, Θουκυδίδης ὁ Ὀλόρου (i.e. υἱός) [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 4.104]]; Ἑλένη ἡ τοῦ Διός (i.e. θυγάτηρ) [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Helena” 470]]: also to denote other relationships, e.g. brother, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Lysias Orator 32.24, 4th c.AD: Alciphro Epistolographus 2.2.10]]; ἡ Σμικυθίωνος Μελιστίχη M.the wife of [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus, 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Ecclesiazusae” 46]]; Κλέαρχος καὶ οἱ ἐκείνου Cl. and his men, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 1.2.15]]; ὁ τοῦ Ἀντιγένεος the slave of [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus, 5th c.BC: Hippocrates Medicus “περὶ χυμῶν” 20.]]

__B.II.2
generally, before a genitive it indicates a wider relation, as τὸ τῶν νεῶν, τὸ τῶν Ἑρμῶν, the matter of the ships, the affair of the Hermae, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 4.23, 6.60]]; τὰ τοῦ Ἀρριβαίου πράσσειν to promote the interests of Arrhibaeus, [Refs [[prev. author] 4.83, compare 6.89, etc.]]; τὸ τῆς τύχης,=ἡ τύχη, [Refs [[prev. author] 4.18]]; τὰ τῆς τύχης accidents, chance events, [Refs [[prev. work] 55]]; τὰ γὰρ φθιτῶν τοῖς ὁρῶσι κόσμος performance of the rites due to the dead befits the living, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Supplices” 78 (Lyric poetry)]]; τὰ τῶν θεῶν that which is destined by the gods, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Trachiniae” 498 (Lyric poetry): hence with _neuter_ of Possessive _pronoun_, τὸ ἐμόν, τὸ σόν,]] what regards me or thee, my or thy business or interests, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Ajax” 124, “El.” 251, etc.]]: and with genitive of [Refs 5th c.BC+ [3 _person_, τὸ τῆσδε 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Hippolytus” 48. But τό τινος]] is frequently also, a man's word or saying, as τὸ τοῦ Σόλωνος [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.86]]; τὸ τοῦ Ὁμήρου as Homer says, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Theaetetus” 183e]]; also τά τινος so-and-so's house, [NT+5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Vespae” 1432, 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 54.7, 3rd c.BC: Theocritus Poeta Bucolicus 2.76, 3rd c.BC: Herodas Mimographus 5.52, NT.Luke.2.49.]]

__B.II.3
very frequently with cases governed by Preps.. αἱ ἐκ τῆς Ζακύνθου νῆες the ships from Zacynthus, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 4.13; οἱ ἀμφί τινα, οἱ περί τινα, such an one and his followers, see at {ἀμφί} with 1.3, περί with 1.2]]; also τὰ ἐπὶ Θρᾴκης the Thrace-ward district, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 1.59, +others]]; τὰ ἀπὸ τοῦ καταστρώματος matters on deck, [Refs [[prev. author] 7.70]]; τὰ ἀπ᾽ Ἀλκιβιάδου the proposals of Alcibiades, [Refs [[prev. author] 8.48]]; τὰ ἀπὸ τῆς τύχης the incidents of fortune, [Refs [[prev. author] 2.87, etc.]]

__B.II.4
on μὰ τόν, μὰ τήν, etc., see at {μά} IV.

__B.II.5
in elliptical phrases, ἐπορευόμην τὴν ἔξω τείχους (i.e. ὁδόν) [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Lysis” 203a; ἡ ἐπὶ θανάτῳ (i.e. στολή, δέσις), see at {θάνατος}; κατὰ τὴν ἐμήν (i.e. γνώμην), see at {ἐμός} II.4]]; ἡ αὔριον (i.e. ἡμέρα), see at {αὔριον}; ἡ Λυδιστί (i.e. ἁρμονία) [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Politica” 1342b32, etc.: frequently with Advs., which thus take an adjective sense, as ὁ, ἡ, τὸ νῦν]]; ὁ οἴκαδε πλοῦς [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 1.52; οἱ τότε, οἱ ἔπειτα (i.e. ἄνθρωποι), [prev. work] 9, 10]], etc.; but τό stands absolutely with Advs. of time and place, when one cannot (as in the preceding instances) supply a substantive, as κἀκεῖσε καὶ τὸ δεῦρο [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Phoenissae” 266, compare [315] (Lyric poetry)]]; ὁ μὲν τὸ κεῖθεν, ὁ δὲ τὸ κεῖθεν [Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. author] “Or.” 1412 (Lyric poetry): rarely _absolutely_ in _genitive_, ἰέναι τοῦ πρόσω to go forward, 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 1.3.1; τοῦ προσωτάτω δραμεῖν 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Ajax” 731.]]

__C
as RELATIVE PRONOUN in many dialects; both in nominative singular masculine ὅ, as κλῦθί μοι, ὃ χθιζὸς θεὸς ἤλυθες [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 2.262, compare 1.300, +others; Ἔρως, ὃ κατ᾽ ὀμμάτων στάζεις πόθον 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Hippolytus” 526 (Lyric poetry); Ἄδωνις, ὃ κἠν Ἀχέροντι φιλεῖται 3rd c.BC: Theocritus Poeta Bucolicus 15.86]]; ὃ ἐξορύξη he who banishes him, [Refs [“Schwyzer” 679.12,25 (from Cyprus)]]; and in the forms beginning with τ, especially in [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Homerus Epicus (8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 4.160, +others), 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.7, +others]]: also in Ionic dialect Poets, ἐν τῷ κάθημαι [Refs 7th c.BC+ [7th c.BC: Archilochus Lyricus 87.3, compare 7th-6th c.BC(?): Semonides Iambographus 7.3, 6th c.BC: Anacreon Lyricus 86 (probably), 3rd c.BC: Herodas Mimographus 2.64, +others: frequently in Trag., τῆς 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Coloneus” 1258, “Tr.” 381, 728, 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Alcestis” 883 (_anapaest meter_); τῷ 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Philoctetes” 14; τήν [prev. author] “OC” 747, “Tr.” 47, “El.” 1144]]; τό [Refs [[prev. author] “OT” 1427]]; τῶν[Refs [[prev. work] 1379, “Ant.” 1086.]]—Never in Comedy texts or Attic dialect Prose:—Epic dialect genitive singular τεῦ [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 18.192 (assuming variant).]]

__D
CRASIS OF ARTICLE:

__D.a
Attic dialect ὁ, ἡ, τό, with ᾰ make ᾱ, as ἁνήρ, ἁλήθεια, τἀγαθόν, τᾄτιο; so οἱ, αἱ, τά, as ἅνδρες, τἀγαθ; also τοῦ, τῷ, as τἀγαθοῦ, τἀγαθῷ: ὁ, τό, οἱ, before e gives ου, οὑξ, οὑπί, οὑμός, τοὔργον, οὑπιχώριοι, etc.; also τοῦ, as τοὐμοῦ, τοὐπιόντο; but ἅτερος, θάτερον ([musical notation]), Ionic dialect οὕτερος, τοὔτερον (see. ἕτερος), Attic dialect feminine ἡτέρα, dative θητέρᾳ (see. ἕτερος); τῷ loses the iota, τὠμῷ, τὠπιόντι: ὁ, τό, before ο gives ου, as Οὁδυσσεύς, Οὑλύμπιος, τοὔνομα: ὁ, τό, etc., before αυ gives ᾱυ, αὑτός, ταὐτό, ταὐτῷ (frequently written ἁτός, etc. in Inscrr. and Papyrus); so τὰ αὐτά=ταὐτά, αἱ αὐταί=αὑταί: ἡ before εὐ gives ηὑ, as ηὑλάβεια: τῇ before ἡ gives θη, as θἠμέρᾳ: τὸ before ὑ gives θου, as θοὔδωρ for τὸ ὕδωρ.

__D.b
other dialects: in their treatment of crasis these follow the local laws of contraction, hence, e.g., Doric dialect ὡξ from ὁ ἐξ [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [3rd c.BC: Theocritus Poeta Bucolicus 1.65, ὥλαφος from ὁ ἔλαφος [prev. work] 135]]; Ionic dialect ᾡσυμνήτης from ὁ αἰς-[Refs 5th c.BC+ [“SIG” 57.45 (Milet., 5th c.BC)]]; ὡυτή from ἡ αὐτή [Refs 1st c.AD+ [1st c.AD(?): Heraclitus 60, etc.]]

τοὐναντίον

(AS)

LSJ / STEPBible (TFLSJ)
Included with:  ἐναντίος, α, ον,
opposite, ={ἀντίος} (which is rare in Prose):

__1
of Place, on the opposite side, opposite, c.dative, ἀκταὶ ἐναντίαι ἀλλήλῃσιν [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 10.89; Πάτροκλος δέ οἱ.. ἐ. ἧστο 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 9.190, compare 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 23.89]]: hence, fronting, face to face, αὐτῳ οὔ πω φαίνετ᾽ ἐναντίη [Refs 7th c.BC+ [6.329; ὄττις ἐ. τοι ἰσδάνει 7th-6th c.BC: Sappho Lyrica 2.2]]; δεῖξον.. τὸ σὸν πρόσωπον δεῦρ᾽ ἐ. πατρί before him, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Hippolytus” 947]]; τὰναντία τινί things open to one's sight, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 3.3.345: _absolutely_, ἐ. στάνθ᾽ 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Hippolytus” 1078 (but ἐ. κεῖσθαι]] look opposite ways, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Symposium” 190a).]]

__1.b

genitive τούτου, ταύτης, τούτου, etc.: the dual feminine never in Attic dialect, see ὁ, ἡ, τό, [near the start]:—demonstrative pronoun, this, common from [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Homerus Epicus downwards]]

__A
ORIGIN and FORMS: οὗτος, αὕτη, τοῦτο probably arose from a reduplication of the demonstrative ὁ, ἡ, τό with insertion of -υ- (= Sanskrit Particle u), e.g. ταῦτα from τα-υ-τα: Doric dialect genitive singular feminine τούτας [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Philolaus Philosophus 11; _nominative_ _plural_ τοῦτοι, ταῦται 2nd c.AD: Apollonius Dyscolus Grammaticus “de Syntaxi;” 111.23: the former occurs 5th c.BC: Sophron Comicus 24, “GDI” 3045 B 6 (from Selinus), “SIG” 339.16 (Rhodes, 3rd c.BC)]], etc., the latter is uncertain in [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophron Comicus 97, certain in “SIG” 241 B 117 (Delph., 4th c.BC): in _Boeotian dialect_ all forms begin with οὑτ-]], as genitive singular neuter οὕτω [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [“Supp.epigram” 3.359.11 (3rd c.BC)]]; accusative singular feminine οὕταν [Refs 6th c.BC+ [6th c.BC: Corinna Lyrica “Supp.” 2.80; _accusative_ _plural_ _neuter_ οὗτα “SIG” 1185.20 (Tanagra, 3rd c.BC), etc.: _genitive_ _plural_ _feminine_ _Attic dialect_ τούτων, Cretan dialect ταυτᾶν “Leg.Gort.” 5.19; __B
USAGE in regard to CONCOR[Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator οὗτος]] is frequently used as a pronoun substantive: hence neuter is followed by genitive, κατὰ τοῦτο τῆς ἀκροπόλιος [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.84; εἰς τοῦθ᾽ ὕβρεως ἐλήλυθεν 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 4.37; εἰς τοῦθ᾽ ἥκεις μανίας [prev. author] 36.48; ταῦτα τῶν μαθημάτων 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Euthydemus” 278b: but quite as frequently as]] adjective, in which case its substantive commonly takes the Article, οὗτος ὁ ἀνήρ or ὁ ἀνὴρ οὗτος.—But the Article is absent,

__B.1
always in Epic dialect Poets (except [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 18.114), οὗτος ἀνήρ 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 14.471, 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 1.406, etc.]]: sometimes also in Trag., [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Persae” 122 (Lyric poetry), 495, 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Philoctetes” 406, “OC” 471, 1177: once in an Inscription, τοπεῖα: τούτων τὰ ἡμίσεα τοπείων “IG” 22.1622.135 (4th c.BC).]]

__B.2
sometimes when the Noun is so specified that the Article is not needed, ἐς γῆν ταύτην.., ἥντινα νῦν Σκύθαι νέμονται [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 4.8; ταύτας ἃς οἱ πατέρες παρέδοσαν μελέτας 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 1.85, compare 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 449d, etc.; πατὴρ σὸς οὗτος, ὃν θρηνεῖς ἀεί 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Electra” 530.]]

__B.3
when οὗτος is used in local sense, here, see below with [Refs [1.5.]]

__B.4
when the Noun with which οὗτος agrees stands as its Predicate, αὕτη γὰρ ἦν σοι πρόφασις [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Philoctetes” 1034]]; δικαστοῦ αὕτη ἀρετή [ἐστι] [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Apologia” 18a: this exception extends to cases in which the Predicate is not so distinctly separated from the Subject, αἰτίαι μὲν αὗται προυγεγένηντο]] these were the grievances which already existed, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 1.66]]; ταύτην φήμην παρέδοσαν this was the report which.., [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Philebus” 16c: frequently with a _superlative_, κίνησις αὕτη μεγίστη δὴ.. ἐγένετο]] this was notably the greatest movement which.., [NT+5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 1.1, compare 3.113: with πρῶτος [prev. author] 1.55, 98, 6.31, NT.Luke.2.2.]]

__B.5
when 3rd pers. is used for 2nd pers. to express contempt, οὗτος ἀνήρ, οὑτοσὶ ἀνήρ, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Gorgias” 467b, 489b, etc.]]

__B.II
though οὗτος usually agrees with the Noun that serves as Predicate, it is not rare to find it in the neuter, μανία δὲ καὶ τοῦτ᾽ ἐστί [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Bacchae” 305; τοῦτο γάρ εἰσι.. εὔθυναι 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 19.82, etc.]]: and in plural, οὐκ ἔστι ταῦτα ἀρχή [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aeschines Orator 3.13; ταῦτ᾽ ἐστὶν ὁ προδότης [prev. author] 2.166]]: so with an explanatory clause added, τοῦτο γάρ ἐστιν ὁ συκοφάντης, αἰτιᾶσθαι μὲν πάντα ἐξελέγξαι δὲ μηδέν [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 57.34.]]

__B.II.2
so also with a Noun in apposition, τούτοισιν μὲν ταῦτα μέλει, κίθαρις καὶ ἀοιδή [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 1.159; τούτου τιμῶμαι, ἐν πρυτανείῳ σιτήσεως 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Apologia” 36e, compare 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Fragmenta” 323.3, etc.]]

__B.II.3
the neuter also may refer to a masculine or feminine Noun, καρπὸν φορέει κυάμῳ ἴσον: τοῦτο ἐπεὰν γένηται πέπον κτλ. [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 4.23, compare 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 1.5.10, etc.]]

__B.II.4
the neuter is also used of classes of persons, μελιτοπῶλαι καὶ τυροπῶλαι: τοῦτο δ᾽ εἰς ἕν ἐστι συγκεκυφός [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Equites” 854, compare 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Leges” 711a]]; or of an abstract fact, οὐκ Ἰοφῶν ζ;—τοῦτο γάρ τοι καὶ μόνον ἔτ᾽ ἐστὶ λοιπὸν ἀγαθόν [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Ranae” 73.]]

__B.III
with Prons.,

__B.III.1
personal, οὗτος σύ, in local sense, see below

__B.III.2
interrogative, τί τοῦτ᾽ ἔλεξα; what is this that.. ? [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Philoctetes” 1173 (Lyric poetry), compare “Ant.” 7]]; ποίοισι τούτοι; for ποῖά ἐστι ταῦτα οἷς [ἔχεις ἐλπίδα]; [Refs [[prev. author] “OC” 388, compare “Ant.” 1049]]; Νέστορ᾽ ἔρειο ὅν τινα τοῦτον ἄγει whom he brings here, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 11.612.]]

__B.III.3
with οἷος, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 20.377, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Phaedo” 61c.]]

__B.III.4
possessive, πατὴρ σὸς οὗτος this father of thine, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Electra” 530, compare 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 7.3.30.]]

__B.III.5
demonstrative, οὗτος ἐκεῖνος, τὸν σὺ ζητέεις, where ἐκεῖνος is the Predicate, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.32; τοῦτ᾽ ἔστ᾽ ἐκεῖνο 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Helena” 622, compare “Or.” 804; αὐτὸ τοῦτο, see at {αὐτός} I.7]]; τοῦτον τὸν αὐτὸν ἄνδρα this same man, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Philoctetes” 128.]]

__B.III.5.b
exceptionally, Διφίλου οὗτος ὅδ᾽ ἐστὶ τύπος [Refs [“IG” 12(5).300 (from Paros).]]

__B.III.6
ἄλλος τις οὗτος ἀνέστη another man here, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 20.380.]]

__B.IV
with Numerals, τέθνηκε ταῦτα τρία ἔτη these three years, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Lysias Orator 7.10 codices]]; [στρατείαν] ἑνδέκατον μῆνα τουτονὶ ποιεῖται for these eleven months, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 8.2, compare 3.4; τριακοστὴν ταύτην ἡμέραν 4th-3rd c.BC: Menander Comicus “Ἐπιτρέποντες” 27; ταύτας τριάκοντα μνᾶς 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 27.23, compare 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Gorgias” 463b, etc.]]

__C
SIGNIFICATION AND SPECIAL IDIOMS:

__C.I
this, to designate the nearer, opposed to ἐκεῖνος, that, the more remote, ταῦτα, like τὰ ἐνταῦθα, things round and about us, earthly things, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Phaedo” 75e (variant)]]; compare ὅδε [near the start]: but οὗτος sometimes indicates that which is not really nearest, but most important, δεῖ.. τὸ βέλτιστον ἀεί, μὴ τὸ ῥᾷστον λέγειν: ἐπὶ ἐκεῖνο μὲν γὰρ ἡ φύσις αὐτὴ βαδιεῖται, ἐπὶ τοῦτο δὲ κτλ. [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 8.72, compare 51.3 and 18.]]

__C.I.2
when, of two things, one precedes and the other follows, ὅδε properly refers to what follows, οὗτος to what precedes, οὐκ ἔστι σοι ταῦτ᾽, ἀλλά σοι τάδ᾽ ἔστι [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Coloneus” 787, compare ὅδε III. 2: frequently, however, where there are not two things, οὗτος]] refers to what follows, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 13.377, 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 2.306, etc.]]; οὔκουν.. τοῦτο γιγνώσκεις, ὅτι..; [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Prometheus Vinctus” 379, etc.]]

__C.I.3
οὗτος is used emphatic, generally in contempt, while ἐκεῖνος denotes praise, ὁ πάντ᾽ ἄναλκις οὗτος, i.e. Aegisthus, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Electra” 301; τούτους τοὺς συκοφάντας 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Crito” 45a; so 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator “de Coron.” uses οὗτος of Aeschines, ἐκεῖνος]] of Philip; but οὗτος is used of Philip, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 2.15, 4.3.]]

__C.I.3.b
of what is familiar, τούτους τοὺς πολυτελεῖς χιτῶνας, of the Persians, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 1.5.8; οἱ τὰς τελετὰς.. οὗτοι καταστήσαντες 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Phaedo” 69c, compare “Men.” 80a]]; τὸ θυλακῶδες τοῦτο the familiar bag-like thing, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-3rd c.BC: Theophrastus Philosophus “Historia Plantarum” 3.7.3, compare 3.18.11, 4.7.1; οἱ τὰς κόρας ταύτας ὠνούμενοι τοῖς παισίν 1st-2nd c.AD: Dio Chrysostomus Sophista 31.153.]]

__C.I.4
in Attic dialect law-language, οὗτος is commonly applied to the opponent, whether plaintiff (as in [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aeschines Orator 2.130)]] or defendant (as in [Refs [[prev. author] 1.1)]]; so, in the political speeches of [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator, οὗτοι]] are the opposite party, [Refs [4.1, 8.7]], etc.; but in the forensic speeches, οὗτοι frequently means the judges, the court, [Refs [21.134, 36.47.]]

__C.I.5
much like an adverb, in local sense (compare ὅδε [near the start]), τίς δ᾽ οὗτος κατὰ νῆας.. ἔρχεα; who art thou here that comest.. ? [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 10.82]]; frequently in Attic dialect, τίς οὑτοσ; who's this here? [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Acharnenses” 1048]]; πολλὰ ὁρῶ ταῦτα πρόβατα I see many sheep here, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 3.5.9 (as variant): with _pronoun_ of 2 _person_, οὗτος σύ]] ho you! you there! [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Tyrannus” 532, 1121, 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Hecuba” 1280, etc.: and then οὗτος alone like a _vocative_, οὗτος, τί ποιεῖ; 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Supplices” 911,compare 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Ajax” 71, 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Alcestis” 773, 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Equites” 240, “Nu.” 220, +others]]: with a proper name, ὦ οὗτος, Αἴας [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Ajax” 89; ὦ οὗτος οὗτος, Οἰδίπους [prev. author] “OC” 1627, compare 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Vespae” 1364: with _vocative_, βέντισθ᾽ οὗτος 3rd c.BC: Theocritus Poeta Bucolicus 5.76:—the _feminine_ is rarer, αὕτη 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Medea” 922; αὕτη σύ 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Thesmophoriazusae” 610.]] —This phrase mostly implies anger, impatience, or scorn.

__C.II
simply as antecedent to ὅς, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 2.40, 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Tyrannus” 1180, etc.: frequently following _relative_ clause, ἅ γ᾽ ἔλαβες,.. μεθεῖναι ταῦτα [prev. author] “Ph.” 1247, compare 1319, “Ant.” 183, 203, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Gorgias” 469c.]]

__C.III
= τοιοῦτος, οὗτος ἐγὼ ταχυτᾶτι [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “O.” 4.26; σὺ τοίνυν οὗτος εὑρέθης 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 18.282, compare 173.]]

__C.IV
after a parenthesis, the Subject, though already named, is frequently emphatic repeated by οὗτος, οὐδὲ γὰρ οὐδὲ Ἀριστέης.., οὐδὲ οὗτος προσωτέρω.. ἔφησε ἀπικέσθαι [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 4.16, compare 81 (assuming variant), 1.146, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Phaedo” 107d, etc.]]

__C.V
καὶ οὗτος is added to heighten the force of a previous word, ξυνεστῶτες.. ναυτικῷ ἀγῶνι, καὶ τούτῳ πρὸς Ἀθηναίους [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 4.55, compare 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.147, 6.11, etc.; so οὐδὲ τούτου 4th c.BC: Aeschines Orator 2.100]]; see infr. VIII.2.

__C.VI
repeated, where for the second we should merely say he or it, τοῖσιν τούτου τοῦτον μέλεσιν.. κελαδοῦντες [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Ranae” 1526, compare 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Laches” 200d.]]

__C.VII
ταῦτα is used in some special phrases,

__C.VII.1
ταῦτ᾽, ὦ δέσποτα yes Sir (i. e. ἔστι ταῦτα, ταῦτα δράσω, etc.), [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Vespae” 142, “Pax” 275, compare “Eq.” III; so ταῦτα δή [prev. author] “Ach.” 815; ταῦτά νυν [prev. author] “V.” 1008]]; so also ἦν ταῦτα even so, true, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Phoenissae” 417.]]

__C.VII.2
ταῦτα μὲν δὴ ὑπάρξει so it shall be, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Phaedo” 78a.]]

__C.VII.3
καὶ ταῦτα μὲν δὴ ταῦτα so much for that, frequently in Attic dialect, as [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Symposium” 220c.]]

__C.VII.4
ταῦτα at end of a formula in epitaphs, etc., probably short for ταῦτα οὕτως ἔχει or ὁ βίος ταῦτά ἐστιν, e.g. οὐδὶς (= -εὶς) ἀθάνατος: ταῦτα [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [“IG” 14.420; Προκόπι ταῦτα [prev. work]1824; χαίρεται (= -τε) ταῦτα [prev. work]1479, etc.: similarly perhaps in a letter, ἂμ μὴ πέμψῃς, οὐ μὴ φάγω, οὐ μὴ πείνω. ταῦτα “POxy.” 119.15 (2nd-3rd c.AD).]]

__C.VIII
Adverbial usages:

__C.VIII.1
ταῦταabsolutely, therefore, that is why.., [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 11.694; ταῦτ᾽ ἄρα 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Acharnenses” 90, “Nu.” 319, 335, 394, +others, 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Symposium” 4.55; ταῦτα δή 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Persae” 159, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Symposium” 174a; ταῦτ᾽ οὖν 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Trachiniae” 550, 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Vespae” 1358, etc.]]; αὐτὰ ταῦτα ἥκω, ἵνα.. [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Protagoras” 310e: τοῦτο]] is rare in this sense, τοῦτ᾽ ἀφικόμην, ὅπως.. εὖ πράξαιμί τι [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Tyrannus” 1005]]; αὐτὸ γὰρ τοῦτο just because of this, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Symposium” 204a.]]

__C.VIII.1.b
πρὸς ταῦτα so then, therefore, properly used in indignant defiance, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Prometheus Vinctus” 992, 1043, 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Ajax” 971, 1115, 1313, “OT” 426, “OC” 455, etc.]]

__C.VIII.2
καὶ ταῦτα, adding a circumstance heightening the force of what has been said, and that, ἄνδρα γενναῖον θανεῖν, καὶ ταῦτα πρὸς γυναικός [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Eumenides” 627]]: but mostly with a participle, ὅς γ᾽ ἐξέλυσας ἄστυ.., καὶ ταῦθ᾽ ὑφ᾽ ἡμῶν οὐδὲν ἐξειδὼς πλέον [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Tyrannus” 37, compare 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Ranae” 704, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Phaedrus” 241e, etc.]]; or with a participle omitted, ἥτις.. τὴν τεκοῦσαν ὕβρισεν, καὶ ταῦτα τηλικοῦτος (i.e. οὖσα) [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Electra” 614; so καὶ ταῦτα μέντοι 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Eryxias” 400b.]]

__C.VIII.2.b
καὶ ταῦτα anyhow, no matter what happens (or happened), ἐπεχείρησας, οὐδὲν ὢν καὶ ταῦτα you tried, but were no good anyhow, i.e. try as you might, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [[prev. author] “R.” 341c, compare 4th c.BC: Diodorus Comicus 3.5.]]

__C.VIII.3
τοῦτο μέν.., τοῦτο δέ.. on the one hand.., on the other.., partly.., partly.., very frequently in [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus, as 1.161, +others]]; τοῦτο μέν is sometimes answered by δέ only,[Refs 5th c.BC+ [4.76, 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Ajax” 670, “OC” 440]]; by δὲ αὖ, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 7.176]]; by ἔπειτα δέ, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Antigone” 61]]; by ἀλλά, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 22.13]]; by εἶτα, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Philoctetes” 1345]]; by τοῦτ᾽ αὖθις, [Refs [[prev. author] “Ant.” 165.]]

__C.VIII.4
dative feminine ταύτῃ,

__C.VIII.4.a
on this spot, here, ταύτῃ μὲν.., τῇδε δ᾽ αὖ.. [Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. author] “Ph.” 1331; ἀλλ᾽ ἐὰν ταύτῃ γε νικᾷ, ταυτῃὶ πεπλήξεται 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Equites” 271, compare “Th.” 1221.]]

__C.VIII.4.b
in this point, herein, μηδὲν ταύτῃ γε κομήσῃς [Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. author] “Pl.” 572, compare 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Hiero” 7.12, etc.]]

__C.VIII.4.c
in this way, thus, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Prometheus Vinctus” 191, 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Coloneus” 1300, etc.; οὐ.. ταῦτ᾽ ἐστί πω ταύτῃ 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Equites” 843; ἀλλ᾽ οὔτι ταύτῃ ταῦτα 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Medea” 365, compare 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Prometheus Vinctus” 511: antecedent to ὥσπερ, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 330c]]; to ὅπῃ, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 8.3.2; οὕτω τε καὶ ταύτῃ γίγνοιτο 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Leges” 681d; καὶ οὕτω καὶ ταύτῃ ἂν ἔχοι [prev. work] 714d]]; ταύτῃ καλεῖσθαι, etc., like οὕτω κ., [Refs 5th c.BC+ [Scholia 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Symposium” 215b.]]

__C.VIII.5
ἐκ τούτου or τούτων thereupon, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Historia Graeca (Hellenica)” 3.1.6, “Oec.” 2.1]]; therefore, [Refs [[prev. author] “An.” 3.3.5.]]

__C.VIII.6
ἐν τούτῳ in that case, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 440c.]]

__C.VIII.6.b
in the meantime, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.126, 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 3.72, 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Memorabilia” 2.1.27.]]

__C.VIII.7
πρὸς τούτοις (-οισι) besides, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 2.51, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Protagoras” 326a, 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Memorabilia” 2.4.4, 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Plutus” 540.]]

deep_entry:
Abbott-Smith / STEPBible (TBESG)
οὗτος, αὕτη, τοῦτο, genitive, τούτου, ταύτης, τούτου,
[in LXX chiefly for זֹאת ,זֶה ;]
demonstr. pron. (related to ἐκεῖνος as hic to ille),
this;
__1. as subst., this one, he;
__(a) absol.: Mat.3:17, Mrk.9:7, Luk.7:44, 45, Jhn.1:15, Act.2:15, al.; expressing contempt (cl.), Mat.13:55, 56, Mrk.6:2, 3, Jhn.6:42, al.; εἰς τοῦτο, Mrk.1:38, Rom.14:9; μετὰ τοῦτο (ταῦτα; V. Westc. on Jhn.5:1), Jhn.2:12 11:7, al.;
__(b) epanaleptic (referring to what precedes): Mat.5:19, Mrk.3:35, Luk.9:48, Jhn.6:46, Rom.7:10, al.;
__(with) proleptic (referring to what follows): before ἵνα (Bl., §69, 6), Luk.1:43, Jhn.3:19 (and freq.) 15:8, Rom.14:9, al.; before ὅτι, Luk.10:11, Jhn.9:3o, Act.24:14, Rom.2:3, al.; ὅπως, Rom.9:17; ἐάν, Jhn.13:35;
__(d) special idioms: τοῦτο μὲν . . . τ. δέ (cl), partly . . . partly. Heb.10:33; καὶ τοῦτο (τοῦτον, ταῦτα), and that (him) too, Rom.13:11, 1Co.2:2, Heb.11:12; τοῦτ᾽ ἐστιν, Mat.27:46.
__2. As adj., with subst.;
__(a) with art.
__(α) before the art.: Mat.12:32, Mrk.9:29, Luk.7:44, Jhn.4:15, Rom.11:24, Rev.19:9, al.;
__(β) after the noun: Mat.3:9, Mrk.12:16, Luk.11:31, Jhn.4:13, Act.6:13, Rom.15:28, 1Co.1:20, Rev.2:24, al.;
__(b) with subst. anarth. (with predicative force; Bl., §49, 4): Luk.1:36 2:2 24:21, Jhn.2:11 4:54 21:14, 2Co.13:1.
(AS)
