LSJ / STEPBible (TFLSJ)
τρέφω,
[Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 5.52, etc.]]; Doric dialect τράφω (see. entry); 1st pers. singular optative τρέφοιν [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Fragmenta” 903]]: future θρέψω [Refs [“hymnus ad Venerem” 257, etc.:]]aorist 1 ἔθρεψα, Epic dialect θρέψα [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 2.548:]]aorist 2 ἔτρᾰφον (see. infr. B): perfect τέτροφα intransitive, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 23.237, (συν-) 5th c.BC: Hippocrates Medicus “περὶ ἱερῆς νούσου” 11; but _transitive_, 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Coloneus” 186 (Lyric poetry); also τέτρᾰφα 2nd c.BC: Polybius Historicus 12.25h. 5:]] —middle, future θρέψομαι in passive sense, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Hippocrates Medicus “Genit.” 9, “Nat.Puer.” 23, 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 7.49, etc.]]: aorist ἐθρεψάμην [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “O.” 6.46, 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Choephori” 928]], etc.:—passive, future τρᾰφήσομαι Ps.-[Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 60.32, 1st c.BC: Dionysius Halicarnassensis 8.41]], etc., but in early writers in middle form θρέψομαι (see. above): aorist 1 ἐθρέφθην, Epic dialect θρέφθη [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th-7th c.BC: Hesiodus Epicus “Theogonia” 198]], rare in Trag. and Attic dialect, [Refs 6th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Hecuba” 351, 600, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Politicus” 310a; ἐθράφθη “IG” 12(9).286 (Eretria, 6th c.BC):]]aorist 2 ἐτράφην [ᾰ] [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Homerus Epicus (sed see infr. B), 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Septem contra Thebas” 754 (Lyric poetry), 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Aves” 335 (Lyric poetry), etc.]]; Epic dialect 3rd.pers. plural ἔτραφεν, τράφεν, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 23.348, 1.251]]: perfect τέθραμμαι [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Hippocrates Medicus “περὶ φύσιος ἀνθρώπου” 5, 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Heraclidae” 578, etc.]]; 2nd pers. plural τέθραφθε [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Leges” 625a (but συντέτραφθε]] [assuming variant] in [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 6.4.14)]]; infinitive τεθράφθαι [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Gorgias” 525a, 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Historia Graeca (Hellenica)” 2.3.24 (in both with see l. τετρ-).]]

__I
thicken or congeal a liquid, γάλα θρέψαι curdle it, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 9.246]]; τρέφε (imperfect) πίονατυρόν [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [3rd c.BC: Theocritus Poeta Bucolicus 25.106:]] —passive, with perfect active τέτροφα, curdle, congeal, γάλα τρεφόμενον τυρὸν ἐργάζεσθαι [Refs 8th c.BC+ [2nd-3rd c.AD: Aelianus “De Natura Animalium - Ar.Byzantine Epit.” 16.32; περὶ χροΐ τέτροφεν ἅλμη 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 23.237.]]

__II
usually, cause to grow or increase, bring up, rear, especially of children bred and brought up in a house, ὅ σ᾽ ἔτρεφε τυτθὸν ἐόντα [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 8.283; ἥ μ᾽ ἔτεχ᾽, ἥ μ᾽ ἔθρεψε 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 2.131, compare 12.134; εὖ ἔτρεφεν ἠδ᾽ ἀτίταλλεν 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 16.191, compare 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 19.354; ἐγώ σ᾽ ἔθρεψα, σὺν δὲ γηράναι θέλω 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Choephori” 908, compare “Supp.” 894; μέχρι ἥβης τ. 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 2.46; γεννᾶν καὶ τ. 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Politicus” 274a; τ. τε καὶ αὔξειν μέγαν [prev. author] “R.” 565c: with _accusative_ _cognate_, τ. τινὰ τροφήν τινα]] bring up in a certain way, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 2.2; also τῶν πρώτων μαθημάτων, ἐν οἷς οἱ παλαιοὶ τοὺς παῖδας ἔτρεφον 2nd c.AD: Galenus Medicus 16.691]]:—middle, rear for oneself, θρέψαιό τε φαίδιμον υἱόν [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 19.368; αὐτὸν ἐθρέψαντο δράκοντες 5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “O.” 6.46; τεκοῦσα τόνδ᾽ ὄφιν ἐθρεψάμην 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Choephori” 928; οἱ γεννήσαντες καὶ θρεψάμενοι 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Leges” 717c; τεκὼν ἀρετὴν καὶ θ. [prev. author] “Smp.” 212a; ἔτεκον μὲν ὑμᾶς πολεμίοις δ᾽ ἐθρεψάμην ὕβρισμα 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Hercules Furens” 458]]:—passive, to be reared, grow up, ὅς μοι τηλύγετος τρέφεται θαλίῃ ἔνι πολλῇ [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 9.143; τῇ ὁμοῦ ἐτρεφόμην 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 15.365; ἅμα τράφεν ἠδ᾽ ἐγένοντο 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 1.251, etc.]]; κάρτιστοι τράφεν ἀνδρῶν grew up the strongest men, [Refs [[prev. work] 266]]:—properly a boy was called τρεφόμενος only so long as he remained in the charge of the women, i. e. till his fifth year, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.136]]; ἐξ ὅτου 'τράφην ἐγώ from the time when I left the nursery, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Aves” 322]]; but even of pre-natal growth, ἐν σκότοισινηδύος τεθραμμένη [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Eumenides” 665, compare “Th.” 754 (Lyric poetry):—generally, in Trag., τραφεὶς μητρὸς εὐγενοῦς ἄπο 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Ajax” 1229]]; ὅπως πατρὸς δείξεις οἷος ἐξ οἵου τράφης[Refs [[prev. work] 557; κρατίστου πατρὸς.. τραφείς [prev. author] “Ph.” 3: παῖδες μητέρων τεθραμμέναι]] true nurslings of your mothers, implying a reproach for unmanliness (assuming variant), [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Septem contra Thebas” 792]]; μιᾶς τρέφει πρὸς νυκτός art nursed by night alone, i. e. art blind, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Tyrannus” 374.]]

__II.2
of slaves, cattle, dogs and the like, rear and keep them, κύνας [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 22.69, 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 14.22, etc.; ἵππους 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 2.766]]; λέοντος ἶνιν (see. σίνις) [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Agamemnon” 717 (Lyric poetry); μῆλα [prev. author] “Eu.” 946 (Lyric poetry); ὄφιν 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Fragmenta” 226 (conjecture for στρέφουσι); ἰκτῖνα 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Fragmenta” 628; ὄρτυγας 5th c.BC: Eupolis Comicus 214; ὄρνιθας 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Theaetetus” 197c]]; οἱ τρέφοντες (i.e. τοὺς ἐλέφαντας) the keepers, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Historia Animalium” 571b33; τ. παιδαγωγούς 4th c.BC: Aeschines Orator 1.187; also τ. γυναῖκα 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Iphigenia Aulidensis” 749]]; τ. [ἑταίραν], [πόρνας], keep.., [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Antiphanes Comicus 2, 4th-3rd c.BC: Diphilus Comicus 87]]; ὁ τρέφων one's master, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC(?): Nicolaus Comicus 1.11, 36: _metaphorically_, αἰγιαλὸν ἔνδον τρέφει]] he keeps a sea-beach in the house, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Vespae” 110]]:—passive, to be bred, reared, δοῦλος οὐκ ὠνητός, ἀλλ᾽ οἴκοι τραφείς [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Tyrannus” 1123]]; ἐν τῇ σῇ οἰκίᾳ γέγονεν καὶ τέθραπται was born and bred, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Meno” 85e]]; Ἀγαθῖνον θρεμένον (i. e. τεθρεμμένον, ={θρεπτόν}, see at {θρεπτός} [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [1) ἑαυτῶν “MAMA” 4.275 B (Dionysopolis, 2nd c.AD)]]; Νείκην τὴν θρεμένην μου [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [[prev. work]276 A (Dionysopolis, 2nd c.AD).]]

__II.3
tend, cherish, τὸν μὲν ἐγὼ φίλεόν τε καὶ ἔτρεφον, of Calypso, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 5.135, compare 7.256]]; of plants, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 17.53; θρέψασα φυτὸν ὥς 18.57, compare 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 14.175.]]

__II.4
of parts of the body, let grow, cherish, foster, χαίτην.. Σπερχειῷ τρέφε [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 23.142; τῷ θεῷ [πλόκαμον] τ. 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Bacchae” 494; ὑπήνην ἄκουρον τ. 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Vespae” 476 (Lyric poetry)]]; τ. κόμην, ={κομᾶν}, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.82; [τρίχες] πολλῷ ἐλαίῳ τραφεῖσαι 2nd-1st c.BC(?): Hero Mechanicus “Belopoeica” 112: also τά θ᾽ ὕεσσι τρέφει ἀλοιφήν]] things which put fat on swine, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 13.410; τεθραμμένη εἰς πολυσαρκίαν 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Memorabilia” 2.1.22.]]

__II.5
in Poets, of earth and sea, breed, produce, teem with, οὐδὲν ἀκιδνότερον γαῖα τ. ἀνθρώποιο [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 18.130; ἄγρια, τά τε τρέφει οὔρεσιν ὕλη 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 5.52; φάρμακα, ὅσα τρέφει εὐρεῖα χθών 11.741; ὅσ᾽ ἤπειρος.. τρέφει ἠδὲ θάλασσα 8th-7th c.BC: Hesiodus Epicus “Theogonia” 582; πολλὰ γᾶ τρέφει δεινά 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Choephori” 585 (Lyric poetry), compare 128, 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Hecuba” 1181; θάλασσα.. τρέφουσα πορφύρας ἰσάργυρον κηκῖδα 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Agamemnon” 959]]; ὃν πόντος τ., i. e. the sailors, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “I.” 1.48]]: rare in Prose, ἀεί τι ἡ Αιβύη τρέφει καινόν [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “de Generatione Animalium” 746b8.]]

__II.6
in Poets also, simply, have within oneself, contain, ὅ τι καὶ πόλις τέτροφεν ἄφιλον [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Coloneus” 186 (Lyric poetry), compare “Tr.” 817]]; τρέφειν τὴν γλῶσσαν ἡσυχαιτέραν to keep his tongue more quiet, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. author] “Ant.” 1089; ἡ γλῶσσα τὸν θυμὸν δεινὸν τ. [prev. author] “Aj.” 1124; τἀληθὲς γὰρ ἰσχῦον τρέφω [prev. author] “OT” 356 (so in 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus, τ. ἰσχυρὸν τὸ ἐλεινόν “R.” 606b); τ. νόσον 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Philoctetes” 795; ἐκ φόβου φόβον τ. [prev. author] “Tr.” 28; ἄταν [prev. author] “Aj.” 644 (Lyric poetry)]]; οἵας λατρείας.. τρέφει what services.. she has as her lot, [Refs [[prev. work] 503]]; ἐν ἐλπίσιν τρέφω.. ἥξειν I cherish hopes that.., [Refs [[prev. author] “Ant.” 897]]; τὸν Καδμογενῆ τρέφει.. βιότου πολύπονον [πέλαγος] is his daily lot, [Refs [[prev. author] “Tr.” 117 (Lyric poetry, but Reiske's conjecture στρέφει is probably)]]; πόνοι τρέφοντες βροτούς [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Hippolytus” 367 (Lyric poetry).]]

__III
maintain, support, τ. ἀνδρὸς μόχθος ἡμένας ἔσω [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Choephori” 921, compare 5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “O.” 9.106; τοῦ τρέφοντος Ἡλίου χθονὸς φύσιν 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Agamemnon” 633; τ. τὸν πατέρα 4th c.BC: Aeschines Orator 1.13; τὴν οἰκίαν ὅλην 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 59.67; οὐ δίκαιον τρέφεσθαι ὑπὸ πατρὸς ὑὸν ἡβῶντα 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 568e; τὰ κτήνη χιλῷ ἐτρέφοντο 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 4.5.25]]; γάλακτι, τυρῷ, κρέασι τ., [Refs [[prev. author] “Mem.” 4.3.10]]; σίτῳ, ὄψῳ, [Refs [[prev. author] “Lac.” 1.3]]; feed a patient, [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd c.AD: Galenus Medicus 15.503, 19.185]]; provide the food for an employee, σοῦ τρέφοντος αὐτόν, ἐμοῦ δὲ ἱματίζοντος αὐτόν [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [“BGU” 1647.14 (2nd c.AD)]]; also τ. ἀπό τινος [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Protagoras” 313c, 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Historia Graeca (Hellenica)” 2.1.1; ἔκ τινος 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Agamemnon” 1479 (Lyric poetry), compare 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 372b.]]

__III.2

LSJ / STEPBible (TFLSJ)
τροπ-ή, ἡ,
(τρέπω) turn, turning:

__I
τροπαὶ ἠελίοιο:

__I.a
ὅθι τροπαὶ ἠελίοιο apparently denotes a point on the horizon, probably the West or place where the sum sets (so [Refs 8th c.BC+ [12th c.AD: Eustathius Episcopus Thessalonicensis 1787.20), 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 15.404.]]

__I.b
each of two fixed points in the solar year, the solstices, first in [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th-7th c.BC: Hesiodus Epicus, ἠελίοιο τροπῇς]]at the time of the (winter) solstice, [Refs 7th c.BC+ [“Op.” 479; μετὰ τροπὰς ἠελ. [prev. work]564,663 (with _Doric dialect_ _accusative_ _plural_ in -ᾰς); πεδὰ τὰς τροπάς 7th c.BC: Alcman Lyricus 33.5:—later the two solstices were distinguished as τροπαὶ θεριναί and χειμεριναί, 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 2.19, 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 7.16, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Leges” 767c, 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Historia Animalium” 542b4ff, 2nd c.AD: Galenus Medicus 6.405, etc. (rarely in _sing._, τροπὴ θερινή 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Meteorologica” 364b2, 1st c.BC: Geminus Astronomicus 1.13]]; τ. χειμερινή[Refs 4th c.BC+ [[prev. work] 15); τροπαὶ νότιοι 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Historia Animalium” 542b11]]; τ. βόρειοι, νότιοι, [Refs 1st c.AD+ [1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus 2.601a:]] —when τροπαί is used alone, it mostly refers to the winter solstice, but the sense is always determined by the context, see [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th-7th c.BC: Hesiodus Epicus]] [same places]; περὶ ἡλίου τροπάς (i.e. χειμερινάς) [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 8.39; εὐθὺς ἐκ τροπῶν 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Historia Animalium” 542b20]]:—sometimes also of other heavenly bodies, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Timaeus” 39d; περὶ Πλειάδος δύσιν καὶ τροπάς 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Historia Animalium” 542b23, etc.; ἄστρων ἐπιτολάς, δύσεις, τροπάς 2nd c.AD: Alexander Rhetor 30.5; τροπὰς τῶν ἐνδεδεμένων ἄστρων 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “de Caelo” 296b4; τροπαὶ ἡλίου καὶ σελήνης 4th-3rd c.BC: Epicurus Philosophus “Epistulae” 2p.40U.:—sometimes four in number (the two equinoxes and two solstices), 2nd c.AD: Sextus Empiricus Philosophus “adversus Mathematicos” 5.11, 2nd c.AD: Galenus Medicus 17(1).22; so (on a sun-dial) θερινὴ τ., ἰσημερινὴ τ., χειμερινὴ τ., Ἀρχ.Δελτ. 12.236 (from Samos).]]

__I.2
turn, change, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Politica” 1316a17; πλείους τραπόμενος τροπὰς τοῦ Εὐρίπου 4th c.BC: Aeschines Orator 3.90]]; τ. πρὸς τὸ βέλτιον turn for the better, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [1st c.BC: Philodemus Gadarensis Epigrammaticus “Rh.” 2.25S.; ὀξυτέρας τρεπόμενος τ. τοῦ χαμαιλέοντος 1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus “Alcibiades” 23; αἱ τοῦ κόλακος ὥσπερ πολύποδος τ. [prev. author] 2.52f; αἱ τῶ αἵματος τ. καὶ ἀλλοιώσιες 5th-4th c.BC: Timaeus Locrus Philosophus 102c]]; αἱ περὶ τὸν ἀέρα τ. changes in the air or weather, [Refs 1st c.AD+ [1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus 2.946f]]; of wine, a turning sour, [Refs [[prev. work]939f (compare τροπίας)]]; going bad, of food, τ. καὶ διαφθορὰ τῶν παρακειμένων [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd c.AD: Galenus Medicus 19.208]]; of phonetic change in language, [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd c.AD: Apollonius Dyscolus Grammaticus “de Adverbiis;” 210.4, Hdn.Gr. 2.932.]]

__I.3
τροπαὶ λέξεως a change of speech by figures or tropes (τρόποι), [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd c.AD: Lucianus Sophista “Dem.Enc.” 6, compare 2nd c.AD: Hermogenes Rhetor “περὶ εὑρέσεως” 4.10, +others]]

__I.4
αἱ τροπαί, ={αἱ τροπαῖαι}, alternating winds, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Problemata” 940b16, 21, 4th-3rd c.BC: Theophrastus Philosophus “de Causis Plantarum” 2.3.1, “Vent.” 26.]]

__II
the turning about of the enemy, putting to flight or routing him, τροπήν (or τροπάς) τινος ποιεῖν or ποιεῖσθαι put one to flight, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.30, 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Equites” 246 (troch.), 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 2.19, 6.69, etc.]]; οἵαν ἂν τροπὴν Εὐρυσθέως θείμην (θείην codices) [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Heraclidae” 743; τροπὴ γινομένη 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 7.167, compare 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 1.49, 50, etc.: poetry, ἐν μάχης τροπῇ 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Agamemnon” 1237]]; ἐν τροπῇ δορός in the rout caused by the spear, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Ajax” 1275, 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Rhesus” 82.]]

__III
used by [Refs 3rd c.AD+ [3rd c.AD: Democritus Epigrammaticus for θέσις,]] position, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Metaphysica” 985b17, 1042b14, compare 3rd c.AD: Plotinus Philosophus 4.5.2, 4.5.6.]]

__IV
a coin, [Refs 5th c.AD+ [5th c.AD(?): Hesychius Legal icographus]]; compare τροπαϊκόν.

[Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Acharnenses” 801, compare 806]]; of cattle, τὸν θαλλόν, κόμαρον τ., [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [3rd c.BC: Theocritus Poeta Bucolicus 4.45, 9.11]]; rarely of dogs, Εὐριπίδην ἔτρωγον [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [3rd c.BC: Sotades Lyricus 15.15]]; of human beings in disease, λίθους τε καὶ γῆν τρώγουσι [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Hippocrates Medicus “προρρητικόν” 2.31.]]

__II
of men, eat vegetables or fruit, τοὺς γενομένους [κυάμους] οὔτε τρώγουσι οὔτε ἕψοντες πατέονται [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 2.37]]; τὸ κάτω [τῆς βύβλου[Refs 5th c.BC+ [] [prev. work] 92; τὸν καρπὸν τοῦ λωτοῦ [prev. author] 4.177; τ. βότρυς 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Equites” 1077; βολβοὺς τρώγων, τυροὺς κάπτων 4th c.BC: Anaxilas Comicus 18.3 (_anapaest meter_)]]; of dessert, eat fruits, as figs, almonds, etc., [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.71, 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Pax” 1324, 5th c.BC: Pherecrates Comicus 159 (see. τρωγάλια)]]; ἴτρια, μελίπηκτα, [Refs 6th c.BC+ [6th c.BC: Solon Lyricus 38.1, 4th c.BC: Antiphanes Comicus 140.4]]; of small fish as hors-d'oeuvres, κἀν ποίᾳ πόλει τοσοῦτος [ὢν] τὸ μέγεθος ἰχθῦς τρώγετα; [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Eupolis Comicus 23 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator: _absolutely_, πίνειν καὶ τ.]] drink and eat dessert, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 19.197: Comedy texts _metaphorically_, γνώμας τ. Πανδελετείους 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Nubes” 924 (_anapaest meter_)]]:—passive, τρώγεται ἁπαλὰ ταῦτα καὶ αὖα [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 2.92.]]

__III
later, simply eat, serving as present to ἔφαγον instead of ἐσθίω, ὁ τρώγων μου τὴν σάρκα καὶ πίνων μου τὸ αἷμα [LXX+NT [NT.John.6.54 (compare _aorist_ φάγητε.. πίητε [prev. work] 53); τρώγοντες καὶ πίνοντες NT.Matt.24.38; never in LXX (ὁ ἐσθίων ἄρτους μου LXX.Psa.40(41).10 becomes ὁ τρώγων μου τὸν ἄρτον]] when cited in [NT.John.13.18)]; δύο τρώγομεν ἀδελφοί is uncertain reading in [Refs 2nd c.BC+ [2nd c.BC: Polybius Historicus 31.23.9; ἔδωκεν εὔζωμον νήστῃ τρώγειν “SIG” 1171.9 (Crete, perhaps 1st c.BC)]]; ἡ νὺξ τὴν ἡμέραν τ. (of a black man eating white bread) Diog.Cyn. cited in [Refs 4th c.AD+ [“Sammelb.” 5730 (4th-5th c.AD)]]; ψυχρὰ τρώγοντα κατακαίεσθαι [Refs [“PMag.Lond.” 121.177; ἔμοιγε, ὅσσα παρ᾽ ἀνθρώποις, τρώγειν ἔθος Batrachomyomachia 34]]; this usage is mentioned by [Refs 9th c.AD+ [“Anecdota Graeca - Bekker” 114, censured by 9th c.AD: Photius Legal icographus, etc.]]

deep_entry:
Abbott-Smith / STEPBible (TBESG)
τυγχάνω
[in LXX: Deu.19:5 (מָצָא), Job.3:21 7:2 17:1, Pro.30:23 (without definite Heb. equiv.), Wis.15:19, 1Ma.11:42, 3Ma.3:7, al. ;]
__I. Trans.
__1. to hit (opposite to ἁμαρτάνω, to miss the mark: Hom., Xen., al.).
__2. to hit upon, light upon;
__(a) of persons, to meet with, fall in with: absol., ptcp., ὁ τυχών, a chance person, anyone (Lat. quivis), οὐ τυχών, not common or ordinary, Act.19:11 28:2;
__(b) of things, to reach, get, obtain: with genitive of thing(s) Luk.20:35, Act.24:3 26:22 27:3, 2Ti.2:10 Heb.8:6 11:35.
__II. Intrans., to happen; of things, to happen, chance, befall: impers., εἰ τύχοι, it may be, perhaps, 1Co.14:10 15:37; so ptcp., τυχόν (old accusative absol.; see M, Pr., 74), 1Co.16:6
(cf. ἐν-, ὑπερ-εν-, ἐπι-, παρα-, συν-τυγχάνω).†
τυχόν, adv., see: τυγχάνω
(AS)

---

LSJ / STEPBible (TFLSJ)
τυγχάνω,
[Refs 6th c.BC+ [6th c.BC: Theognis Elegiacus 253, 5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “P.” 3.104, “O.” 2.47, etc.]]: Epic dialect imperfect τύγχανον [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 14.231]], (παρετ-) [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 11.74]]: future τεύξομαι [Refs 8th c.BC+ [16.609, 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 19.314, 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Equites” 112, 5th c.BC: Lysias Orator 18.23]] (also as future middle of τεύχω): aorist 2 ἔτῠχον, Epic dialect τύχον, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 5.287, 587]], etc.; Epic dialect subjunctive τύχωμι, -ῃσι, [Refs [7.243, 11.116]]; later also τετύχῃσι, [Refs 1st c.BC+ [1st c.BC(?): Maximus Astrologus 577]]; late Epic dialect optative τετύχοιμι [Refs 4th c.AD+ [4th c.AD(?): Manetho Astrologus 3.299]]: Epic dialect also aorist 1 ἐτύχησα [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 15.581, +others, 8th-7th c.BC: Hesiodus Epicus “Fragmenta” 15:]]perfect τετύχηκα (intransitive) [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 10.88 (_participle_ τετυχηκώς,]] variant{τετυχηώς}. [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 17.748), 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 1.32, (_transitive_) 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 4.1.2, 5th-6th c.BC: Isocrates Orator 3.59]]; later also τέτευχα, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 21.150 (codex S), 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Ethica Nicomachea” 1119a10, “PA” 647b15, frequently later, “PEnteux.” 6.7 (3rd c.BC), “UPZ” 123.30 (2nd c.BC), “PStrassb.” 98.10 (2nd c.BC), “Inscription Prien.” 108.287 (2nd c.BC), etc.]]; Doric dialect perfect infinitive τετεύχεν [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [“SIG” 398.5 (Cos, 3rd c.BC)]]; but Ionic dialect pluperfect ἐτετεύχεε [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 3.14]]; τέτυχα variant in [NT+1st c.AD+ [NT.Heb.8.6, variant in 1st c.AD: Josephus Historicus “Bellum Judaicum” 7.5.4]], (συν-) [Refs [Aristeas  180]], etc.; participle τετυχώς [Refs [“Jahresh.” 29 “Beibl.” 163 (Stara Zagora)]]:—middle, aorist 1 τεύξασθαι [LXX.2Mac.15.7]:— passive, imperfect ἐτυγχάνετο [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd c.AD(?): Antoninus Liberalis Mythographus 39.3 (uncertain): elsewhere in compds,]]aorist 1 ἐτεύχθην (ἐν-) [Refs 2nd c.BC+ [2nd c.BC: Polybius Historicus 35.6.1:]]perfect τέτευγμαι (ἐπι-) [Refs [[prev. author] 6.53.2.]]

__A
happen to be at a place, εἴ πέρ τε τύχῃσι μάλα σχεδόν even if she be quite near, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 11.116]]; μὴ σύ γε κεῖθι τύχοις may'st thou not be there, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 12.106; πέτρη τετύχηκε διαμπερὲς ἀμφοτέρωθεν 10.88; πεδίοιο διαπρύσιον τετυχηκώς 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 17.748]] (but in these last two places the meaning may be 'has been made' (though not by human agency), compare [γαῖα] οὐδ᾽ εὐρεῖα τέτυκται [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 13.243; γυναικὸς ἄρ᾽ ἀντὶ τέτυξο 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 8.163, etc.]]; see ad near the end).

__2
of events, and things generally, happen to one, befall one, come to one's lot, with dative person, οὔνεκά μοι τύχε πολλά because much fell to me, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 11.684; καί μοι μάλα τύγχανε πολλά 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 14.231; θέλοιμ᾽ ἂν ὡς πλείστοισι πημονὰς τυχεῖν 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Prometheus Vinctus” 348, compare “Pers.” 706 (troch.); οἷ᾽ αὐτοῖς τύχοι 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Philoctetes” 275; εἴ τι δεσπόταισι τυγχάνει 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Alcestis” 138: _absolutely_, εἰ δ᾽ αὖθ᾽, ὃ μὴ γένοιτο, συμφορὰ τύχοι 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Septem contra Thebas” 5, compare “Ag.” 347, etc.; ἄριστα πρὸς τὸ τυγχάνον 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Helena” 1290, compare “Ion” 1511.]]

__2.b
aorist participle ὁ τυχών, the first one meets, any chance person, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th-7th c.BC: Hesiodus Epicus “Theogonia” 973, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 539d, etc.; οἱ τ.]]everyday men, the vulgar, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Memorabilia” 3.9.10, etc.; εἷς ἦν τῶν τ. 5th-6th c.BC: Isocrates Orator 10.21]]; οὐχ ὁ τ. ἀνήρ, of [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd c.AD(?): Moses Alchemista, 3rd c.AD: Longinus Rhetor 9.9: so of things, τὸ τυχόν]] any chance result, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Timaeus” 46e; ὃν ἐξαλείφει πρόφασις ἡ τυχοῦσ᾽ ὅλον 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Fragmenta” 1041]]; οὐχ ὁ τ. λόγος no common discourse, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Leges” 723e; σύνεσιν οὐ τὰν τυχοῦσαν 3rd c.BC: Archimedes Geometra]]Spir.Praef.; οἱ τ. φόβοι trifling fears, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Lycurgus Orator 37]]; καίπερ τὸ τ. καταβαλοῦσιν though they may have paid a trifling sum, [Refs 1st c.BC+ [1st c.BC-1st c.AD: Strabo Geographus 5.2.7:]] —in Mathematics texts, τυχὸν σημεῖον any point (at random), [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [3rd c.BC: Euclides Geometra 1.5, compare 6.9]]; ἄλλα, ἃ ἔτυχεν, ἰσάκις πολλαπλάσια any other equimultiples taken at random, [Refs [[prev. author] 5.4.]]

__3
in 3rd.pers. singular aorist or imperfect, impersonal (sometimes also person) in relative clauses, as (when, where, etc.) it (he, she, etc.) happened (may happen, etc.), i. e. anyhow, at any time, place, etc., καὶ ἀρχομένοις καὶ μεσοῦσι καὶ ὅπως ἔτυχέ τῳ at the beginning, middle, or any other point, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 5.20]]; ὡς ἔτυχε ζημιοῦσθαι to be penalized just anyhow, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Memorabilia” 3.9.13]]; οὐχ ὡς ἔτυχεν in no ordinary manner, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-3rd c.BC: Menander Comicus “Σαμία” 79, “BMus.Inscription” 4.481*.340 (Ephesus, 2nd c.AD)]]; τὴν μὲν δικαίαν, τὴν δ᾽ ὅπως ἐτύγχανεν just anyhow, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Hippolytus” 929]]; ἀποτετμάσθω δύο τμάματα ὡς ἔτυχεν let two segments be cut off at random, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [3rd c.BC: Archimedes Geometra “περὶ κωνοειδέων καὶ σφαιροειδέων” 24; χώρᾳ γ᾽ ἐν ᾗ ἔτυχε 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Oeconomicus” 3.3; ὅπου ἔτυχεν [prev. author] “Cyr.” 8.4.3; ὅπου ἂν τύχῃ 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Protagoras” 242e]]; ὁπότε τύχοι sometimes, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Phaedo” 89b]]; ὅταν τύχῃ sometimes, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Electra” 1169 (Lyric poetry)]]; but, at any odd time, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 1.142; ἡνίκ᾽ ἂν τ. 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 1.3]]; ἂν τύχῃ, εἰ τύχοι, it may be, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Cratylus” 430e, “Hp.Mi.” 367a; τὸ δέ, εἰ ἔτυχεν, οὐχ οὕτως ἔχει [prev. author] “Cra.” 439c; εἰ οὕτως ἔτυχεν 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Categoriae” 8b12; τὸ ὅπῃ ἔτυχεν]]mere chance, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Philebus” 28d]]: with attraction of the relative pronoun, τὸ οἷς ἔτυχε προσκρούειν [Refs 2nd c.BC+ [1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus “Cicero” 27; ὡμίλει ᾧ τύχοι 2nd c.BC: Polybius Historicus 26.1.3; ὧν ἔτυχε πιμπλάμενος 2nd c.AD: Lucianus Sophista “Vit.Auct.” 9]]; οὐδὲ γὰρ ὧν ἔτυχ᾽ ἦν they were not just any acts, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 18.130.]]

__3.b
with accusative et infinitive, ἔτυχε ὄμβρον συνεργῆσαι [Refs 1st c.AD+ [1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus “Alcibiades” 28, compare 2nd-3rd c.AD: Aelianus “De Natura Animalium - Ar.Byzantine Epit.” 5.6]]; ἔτυχεν ὥστε.. [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd-3rd c.AD: Dio Cassius Historicus 39.12.]]

__4
sometimes the Verb agrees in person and number with the subject of the principal clause, perhaps by assimilation, ἀπαίροντες ἀπὸ τῆς Πελοποννήσου ὁπόθεν τύχοιεν, for ὁπόθεν τύχοι, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 4.26, compare 93, 5.56, 7.70, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Theaetetus” 179c]]; ὅ τι ἂν τύχωσι, τοῦτο λέγουσι they say just anything, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. author] “Prt.” 353a; ὅ τι ἂν τύχωσι, τοῦτο πράξουτιν [prev. author] “Cri.” 45d, compare “Grg.” 522c, “Smp.” 181b; ἀναφύονται ὁπόθεν ἂν τύχῃ ἕκαστος [prev. author] “Tht.” 180c; ὡς ἐτύγχανον ἕκαστοι, ηὐλίζοντο 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 2.2.17, compare 3.1.3; τάχ᾽ ἄν, εἰ τύχοιεν, σωφρονέστεροι γένοιντο 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 15.16; δουλεύειν μᾶλλον ἢ μεθ᾽ ὁποτέρου ἂν τύχωσι τούτων ἐλευθέρους εἶναι 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 8.48]]; πρὸς ὀργὴν ἥν τινα τύχητε ἔστιν ὅτε σφαλέντες τὴν τοῦ πείσαντος μίαν γνώμην ζημιοῦτε yielding to the impulse of the moment, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. author] 3.43; εἶτ᾽ οὐκ ἐλήρουν ὅ τι τύχοιμ᾽ 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Ra.” 945]]: with attraction of the relative pronoun, οὓς ἂν τύχῃς ἐπαινῶν [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Isocrates Orator 12.206.]]

__5
neuter participle τυχόν, used absolutely like{ἐξόν, παρόν}, etc., since it so befell, οὕτως τ. [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd c.AD: Lucianus Sophista “Symp.” 43.]]

__5.b
as adverb, perchance, perhaps, [NT+5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Isocrates Orator 4.171, 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 6.1.20, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus Alcaeus2.140a, 150c, 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 18.221, 21.41, 4th-3rd c.BC: Menander Comicus “Περικειρομένη” 184, NT.1Cor.16.6; τ. ἴσως 5th c.BC: Epicharmus Comicus 277, 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Fragmenta” 953.9, 4th-3rd c.BC: Menander Comicus “Ἐπιτρέποντες” 287, 2nd c.BC: Polybius Historicus 2.58.9]]; τυχὸν μὲν.., τυχὸν δὲ.. [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd c.AD: Arrianus Historicus “Anabasis” 1.10.6, etc.]]

__A.II
joined with the participle of another Verb to express a coincidence, τύχησε γὰρ ἐρχομένη νηῦς a ship happened to be, i. e. was just then, starting, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 14.334; ξεῖνος ἐὼν ἐτύχησε παρ᾽ ἱπποδάμοισι Γερηνοῖς 8th-7th c.BC: Hesiodus Epicus “Fragmenta” 15.3, compare 7th-6th c.BC(?): Semonides Iambographus 7.19, 5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “N.” 1.49; πρυτανεία ἣ ἂν τυγχάνῃ πρυτανεύουσα “IG” 12.63.27]], compare 52; τὰ νοέων τυγχάνω what I happen to have, i.e. have at this moment, in my mind, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.88, compare 8.65, 68. ; ἐτετεύχεε ἐπισπόμενος [prev. author] 3.14]]; ὃ τυγχάνω μαθών which I have just learnt, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Trachiniae” 370]]; παρὼν ἐτύγχανον I was by just then, [Refs [[prev. author] “Aj.” 748]]; τυγχάνει καθεύδων he is sleeping just now, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Vespae” 336 (troch.)]]; ἔτυχον στρατευόμενοι they were just then engaged in an expedition, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 1.104]]; ἔτυχε κατὰ τοῦτο καιροῦ ἐλθών he came just at this point of time, [Refs [[prev. author] 7.2]]; ἥτις δέ τοι μάλιστα σωφρονεῖν δοκεῖ, αὕτη μέγιστα τυγχάνει λωβωμένη she is just the one who.., [Refs 7th c.BC+ [7th-6th c.BC(?): Semonides Iambographus 7.109]]; but frequently τυγχάνω cannot be translated at all, especially in phrase τυγχάνω ὤν, which is simply ={εἰμί}, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Ajax” 88, 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Plutus” 35, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Protagoras” 313c, etc.]]

__II.2
the participle ὤν is sometimes omitted, ὁ γὰρ μέγιστος τυγχάνει δορυξένων [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Electra” 46; εἴ σοι χαρτὰ τυγχάνει τάδε [prev. work] 1457]]; νῦν δ᾽ ἀγροῖσι τυγχάνει[Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. work] 313; ἔνδον γὰρ ἄρτι τυγχάνει [prev. author] “Aj.” 9; εἴ τις εὔνους τυγχάνει 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Ecclesiazusae” 1141; εἰ σὺ τυγχάνεις ἐπιστήμων τούτων 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Protagoras” 313e, compare “Grg.” 502b, “R.” 369b, +others: sometimes τυγχάνειν]] is used much like{εἶναι, Σωτὴρ γένοιτ᾽ ἂν Ζεὺς ἐπ᾽ ἀσπίδος τυχών} [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Septem contra Thebas” 520]]; οὐκ ἀποδάμου τυχόντος not being absent, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “P.” 4.5 (compare τόσσαις); ποῦ χρὴ τηνικαῦτα τυγχάνει; 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Iphigenia Aulidensis” 730]]; τ. ἐν ἐμπύροις to be engaged in.., [Refs 4th c.BC+ [[prev. author] “Andr.” 1113; frequently in 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus, δύο μέρη τετύχηκεν ἐξ ὧν ἡ πόλις “Pol.” 1318a31, compare 1289b16, “Top.” 151b11]]; also in later Gr., τὰ ἑπτάμηνα γόνιμα τυγχάνειν [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd c.AD: Soranus Medicus 1.55, compare 69, +others; νέος πάνυ τυγχάνων “PLips.” 40 ii 7 (4th c.AD), etc.:— 2nd c.AD: Phrynichus Atticista 244 rejects this usage in 2nd c.AD: Atticus Philosophus]]

__II.2.b
τυγχάνον, ={τὸ ἐκτὸς ὑποκείμενον}, the external reality, e. g. αὐτὸς ὁ Δίων as distinguished both from the word (φωνή) Δίων and its meaning, [Refs [“Stoicorum Veterum Fragmenta” 2.48.]]

__II.2.c
τὰ πράγματα τυγχάνοντα καλοῦσι (i.e. οἱ Στωϊκοί), τέλος γὰρ τὸ τυχεῖν τούτων,[Refs [[prev. work]77.]]

__II.3
later with infinitive, τυγχάνομεν ἐπιδεδωκέναι we happen to have handed in.., we have just handed in.., [Refs 2nd c.BC+ [“PTeb.” 796.13 (2nd c.BC),compare “PSI” 10.1118.8 (1st c.AD), 1.39.4 (2nd c.AD), 1st-2nd c.AD: Heliodorus Medicus et 2nd c.AD: Antyllus Medicus cited in 4th c.AD: Oribasius Medicus 44.8.21, 25, 44.23.21, 2nd c.AD: Galenus Medicus 18(2).394.]]

__B
gain one's end or purpose, succeed, οὐκ ἐτύχησεν ἑλίξας [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 23.466; εἰ τύχῃ τις ἔρδων 5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “N.” 7.11, compare 55]]; τὸ τυχεῖν, ={νίκη}, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. author] “O.” 2.51; πείθειν.. τυγχάνειν θ᾽ ἅμα 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Hecuba” 819; εἰ τύχοιμεν 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 4.63]]; τυχόντες if successful, opposed to σφαλέντες, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. author] 3.39, compare 82, 5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “P.” 10.62; τυγχάνουσι καὶ ἀποτυγχάνουσι 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Poetica” 1450a3; ὀρθῶς πράττειν καὶ τ. 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Euthydemus” 280a]]; gain one's request, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.213 (so τυχόντα γνώμης in 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 3.42)]]; in speaking, to be right, τί νιν καλοῦσα.. τύχοιμ᾽ ἄ; [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Agamemnon” 1233, compare “Ch.” 14, 317 (Lyric poetry), 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Philoctetes” 223, “OC” 1580; Δίκαν νιν προσαγορεύομεν τυχόντες καλῶς 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Choephori” 950 (Lyric poetry):]] —passive, impersonal, αὐτῷ πρὸς τὸ ἔργον οὐδὲν ἐτυγχάνετο nothing went right, uncertain in [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd c.AD(?): Antoninus Liberalis Mythographus 39.3:]] —in participle τυχήσας or τυχών, combined with νύξε, βάλε, οὖτα, etc., pierce, wound, etc., successfully, so that the whole phrase means hit, ἔγχεϊ νύξε κατὰ κληῗδα τυχήσας [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 5.579, compare 858, 12.394]]; βάλε δουρὶ κατὰ ζωστῆρα τυχήσας[Refs 8th c.BC+ [[prev. work] 189; ὑπὸ στέρνοιο τυχήσας βεβλήκει 4.106, compare 5.98, 582, 13.371, 397, 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 19.452, +others; also conversely, θηρητὴρ ἐτύχησε βαλών 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 15.581; βαλὼν τύχω 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 3.35]]; also apart from such combinations, hit, with genitive, προβιβάντος [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 16.609; μηρίνθοιο 23.857; τ. τοῦ σκοποῦ 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Leges” 717b, compare “R.” 523b, 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 2.35, 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 3.2.19, “Ap.” 1: with double _genitive_, εἰ.. τοῦ παιδὸς.. τύχω μέσης τῆς καρδίης 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 3.35: _absolutely_, ἤμβροτες οὐδ᾽ ἔτυχες 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 5.287; αἰ κε τύχωμι 7.243, 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 22.7.]]

__B.II
hit upon, light upon:

__B.II.1
meet, fall in with persons, Αακεδαίμονι.. τυχήσας having met [him] in Lacedaemon, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 21.13: with _genitive_, θρηνητοῦ 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Agamemnon” 1075; τριακτῆρος [prev. work] 172 (Lyric poetry)]]; ἀγαθῶν ἀνδρῶν [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Lysias Orator 2.5; γυναικῶν 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Symposium” 9.7]]: with a predicate added, μή τευ μελαμπύγου τύχῃς [Refs 7th c.BC+ [7th c.BC: Archilochus Lyricus 110; προφρόνων Μοισᾶν τ. 5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “I.” 4(3).43(61); θεῶν ἀμεινόνων τ. 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Heraclidae” 351; ἐμοῦ.. οἰκητοῦ 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Tyrannus” 1450, compare 677; ἡμῶν τ. οἵων σε χρή 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Helena” 1300, compare 5th c.BC: Lysias Orator 18.23; ἐρωτᾶτε αὐτοὺς ὁποίων τινῶν ἡμῶν ἔτυχον 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 5.5.15; τοῦ δαίμονος.. κακοδαίμονος 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Equites” 112.]]

__B.II.2
light on a thing, τύχε γάρ ἀμάθοιο βαθείης [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 5.587]]; attain, obtain a thing, with genitive, πομπῆς καὶ νόστοιο [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 6.290; αἰδοῦς 6th c.BC: Theognis Elegiacus 253, compare 256]]; [οἴκτου] [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Prometheus Vinctus” 241; ξυγγνώμης 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 7.15; τῆς ἀξίας 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Aves” 1223]]; of meeting with misfortunes, βίης τυχεῖν meet with, suffer violence, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 9.108]]; τραυμάτων, κακῶν, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Agamemnon” 866, 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Hecuba” 1280]]; δίκης, κρίσεως, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Gorgias” 472d, “Phdr.” 249a, compare “Lg.” 869b]]: absolutely, have the lot or fate, ἄλλος μὲν ἀποφθίσθω ἄλλος δὲ βιώτω, ὅς κε τύχῃ [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 8.430; τὴν παρὰ Δαρείου αἰτήσας ἔτυχε μισθόν 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 5.23 (where τὴν is governed by αἰτήσας).]]

__B.II.2.b
after [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Homerus Epicus]] also with accusative of neuter adjective or pronoun, τὰ πρόσφορα [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Choephori” 711, compare “Eu.” 30, 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Coloneus” 1106, “Ph.” 509 (Lyric poetry), 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Medea” 758, “Hec.” 51]]: later the accusative is used more freely, τ. ἐπίστασιν [Refs 1st c.AD+ [“Sammelb.” 5235.15 (1st c.AD)]]; ὑπογραφήν [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [“BGU” 615.23 (2nd c.AD)]]; βοήθειαν [Refs 4th c.AD+ [“PGoodsp.Cair.” 15.14 (4th c.AD)]]; εὐκαιρίαν [Refs 4th c.AD+ [“PSI” 9.1082.5 (4th c.AD)]]; τὰ γυναίκια δεσμὸν οὐδένα βούλεται τυγχάνειν [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd c.AD: Soranus Medicus 1.70b.]]

__B.II.2.c
after either case a genitive person may be added, obtain a thing from a person, ὧν δέ σου τυχεῖν ἐφίεμαι [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Philoctetes” 1315; σου τοῦτο τ. [prev. author] “OC” 1168]]; or the person may be added with a preposition, τ. ἐπαίνου ἔκ τινος [Refs 8th c.BC+ [[prev. author] “Ant.” 665; παρὰ σεῖο τ. φιλότητος 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 15.158; τιμίαν ἕδραν παρ᾽ ἀνδρῶν 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Eumenides” 856 (uncertain); αἰδοῦς ὑπό τινος 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 1.6.10, compare “Mem.” 4.8.10, etc.: _absolutely_, χρὴ πρὸς μακάρων τυγχάνοντ᾽ εὖ πασχέμεν 5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “P.” 3.104.]]

__B.II.2.d
with infinitive, οἶμαί σου τεύξεσθαι μεθεῖναί με [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Philebus” 50d; ἐὰν ψαῦσαι τοῦ νεκροῦ τύχωμεν 1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus “Pelopidas” 33]]; οὐ τυχὼν ἐπιδείξειν (={ἐπιδεῖξαι}) not having succeeded in proving, [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [“PPetr.” 3p.153 (3rd c.BC). (Τυ-γ-χ-άνω, with ἐτύχησα, τετύχηκα, is formed from the]]aorist τυχ-εῖν, which was originally the aorist passive (with active form) of τεύχω 'make'; ἔτυχε = factum est, as ἔτραφον = I was nourished (see. τρέφω); senses [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus 1.1-3 are the oldest and are parallel to τεύχω 11 (especially _passive_)]]; many of the forms belong equally to both verbs; τιτύσκομαι like wise belongs to both verbs; τ(ε)υχ- from *θ(ε)υχ-, compare ἀποθύσκειν, ἐνθύσκει, συνθύξω, and perhaps [Refs 1st c.BC+ [\{1st c.BC-1st c.AD\}: Germanicus Caesar Epigrammaticus]] taugen 'to be capable, useful', Engl. dow, doughty.)

τυμπᾰν-ίζω,
beat a drum, as was done in the worship of Cybele, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Eupolis Comicus 77, 1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus 2.60a]]:—passive, τυμπανίζεσθαι κατὰ τὰς ἐξόδους march out to the sound of drums, [Refs 1st c.BC+ [1st c.BC-1st c.AD: Strabo Geographus 15.1.58.]]

τ. ἐπὶ ταῖς θύραις drum with the hand on them, [LXX.1Ki.21.13.]

__II
perhaps ={ἀποτυμπανίζω} (which is variant), [NT.Heb.11.35 (_passive_)]; coupled with ἀνασκολοπίζεσθαι in [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd c.AD: Lucianus Sophista “JTr.” 19; compare τύμπανον 11.]]

__III
of orators, 'beat the big drum', [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd-3rd c.AD: Philostratus Sophista “Vitae Sophistarum” 1.21.5.]]

deep_entry:
Abbott-Smith / STEPBible (TBESG)
τύπος, -ου, ὁ
(τύπτω), [in LXX: Exo.25:39 (40) (תַּבְנִית), Amo.5:26, 3Ma.3:30, 4Ma.6:19 * ;]
__1. the mark of a blow: τῶν ἥλων, Jhn.20:25.
__2. An impression, impress, the stamp made by a die; hence, a figure, image: Act.7:43 (LXX).
__3. form (Plat.): Rom.6:17; the sense or substance of a letter (3Mac, l.with), Act.23:25.
__4. an example, pattern: Act.7:44, Heb.8:6" (LXX) ; in ethical sense, Php.3:17, 1Th.1:7, 2Th.3:9, 1Ti.4:12, Tit.2:7, 1Pe.5:3; in doctrinal sense, type (see ICC, in l), Rom.5:14.†
τυπικῶς, adv.
(τύπος),
__(a) typically (Greg. Naz.)
__(b) by way of example: 1Co.10:11.†
SYN.: see: ὑποτύπωσις  (AS)

LSJ / STEPBible (TFLSJ)
τύπ-ος [ῠ], ὁ,
(τύπτω) blow, τ. ἀντίτυπος Oracle texts cited in [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.67]]; beat of horses' hoofs, variant for{κτὺπος} in [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “de Equitandi ratione” 11.12; αἰθερίου πατάγοιο τ. βρονταῖον ἀκούων 4th-5th c.AD(?): Nonnus Epicus “Dionysiaca” 20.351; so perhaps νάβλα τ. 4th c.BC: Sopater Comicus 16.]]

__II
the effect of a blow or of pressure:

__II.1
impression of a seal, τύποι σφενδόνης χρυσηλάτου [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Hippolytus” 862, compare 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Theaetetus” 192a, 194b, 3rd c.BC: Chrysippus Stoicus 2.23, 2nd c.AD: Lucianus Sophista “Alex.” 21; τ. ἐνσημήνασθαί τινι 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 377b]]; stamp on a coin, τὰ ἀκριβῆ τὸν τ. [Refs 2nd c.BC+ [2nd c.AD: Lucianus Sophista “Hist.Conscr.” 10, compare 2nd-1st c.BC(?): Hero Mechanicus]] “*Mens.” 60, [Refs 5th c.AD+ [5th c.AD(?): Hesychius Legal icographus]] see entry  {Κυζικηνοι στατῆρες}; on a branding-iron, ὄ τ. τοῦ καυτῆρος ἔστω ἀλώπηξ ἢ πίθηκος [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd c.AD: Lucianus Sophista “Pisc.” 46]]: generally, print, impression, χύτρας τύπον ἀρθείσης ἐν σποδῷ μὴ ἀπολιπεῖν, ἀλλὰ συγχεῖν [Refs 1st c.AD+ [1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus 2.727c, compare 982b, 4th c.AD: Iamblichus Philosophus “Protrepticus” 21. κθ᾽, “Geoponica” 2.20.1]]; στίβου γ᾽ οὐδεὶς τ. no footprint, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Philoctetes” 29 (variant{κτύπος})]]; ὡς ἡδὺς ἐν πόρπακι σὸς (i.e. τοῦ βραχίονος) κεῖται τύπος thy imprint, (O arm), [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Troades” 1196 (σῷ conjecture Dobree)]]; τ. ὀδόντων imprint of teeth, [Refs [“Anthologia Graeca” 6.57.5 (Paul. Sil.)]]; print, βάλω τὸν δάκτυλόν μου εἰς τὸν τ. τῶν ἥλων [NT+2nd c.AD+ [NT.John.20.25; οἱ τ. τῶν πληγῶν 2nd c.AD: Athenaeus Epigrammaticus 13.585c.]]

__II.1.b
impressions supposed by [Refs 4th c.BC+ [3rd c.AD: Democritus Epigrammaticus and 4th-3rd c.BC: Epicurus Philosophus]] to be made on the air by things seen, and to travel through space, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-3rd c.BC: Theophrastus Philosophus “de Sensu” 52, 4th-3rd c.BC: Epicurus Philosophus “Epistulae” 1p.9U., “Nat.” 2.6, +others; ὁ θεὸς.. πνεῦμα ἐνεκέρασεν [τοῖς ὀφθαλμοῖς] οὕτως ἰσχυρὸν καὶ φιλότεχνον ὥστε ἀναμάσσεσθαι τοὺς τ. τῶν ὁρωμένων 2nd c.AD: Arrianus Historicus “Epicteti Dissertationes” 2.23.3.]]

__II.2
hollow mould or matrix, καθάπερ ἐν τύπῳ τὰ σχήματα πλασθῆναι [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “de Partibus Animalium” 676b9, compare “Pr.” 892b2]]; used by κοροπλάθοι, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [1st-2nd c.AD: Dio Chrysostomus Sophista 60.9, 5th c.AD: Proclus Philosophus “in Platonis Timaeum commentarii” 1.335, 394 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator, compare 5th c.AD(?): Hesychius Legal icographus]] see at {χοάνη}; by fruit-growers, to shape the fruit while growing, [Refs [“Geoponica” 10.9.3]]; die used in striking coins, metaphorically, Κύπριος χαρακτήρ τ᾽ ἐν γυναικείοις τύποις εἰκὼς πέπληκται τεκτόνων πρὸς ἀρσένων [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Supplices” 282.]]

__II.3
engraved mark, engraving, δέλτον χαλκῆν τύπους ἔχουσαν ἀρχαίων γραμμάτων engravings of letters, i. e. engraved letters, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus “Alexander” 17, compare 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Phaedrus” 275a; τὰ γεγραμμένα τύποις [prev. author] “Ep.” 343a]]; τὸ μέτρον τοῦ ποδὸς ὑποτέτακται τούτοις τοῖς τ. the length of the foot is subjoined in this engraving, [Refs [Rev.Bibl. 35.285 (from Jerusalem).]]

__II.4
the depression between the underlip and chin, [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd c.AD(?): Pollianus Epigrammaticus 2.90.]]

__II.5
pip on dice, [Refs [[prev. author] 9.95.]]

__III
cast or replica made in a mould, τ. κατάμακτος [Refs [“IG” 22.1534.87; τ. ἔγμακτος [prev. work]64.]]

__IV
figure worked in relief, whether made by moulding, modelling, or sculpture, αἱμασιὴ ἐγγεγλυμμένη τύποισι [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 2.138, compare 106, 136, 148, 153; θεοῦ τ. μὴ ἐπίγλυφε δακτυλίῳ 4th c.AD: Iamblichus Philosophus “Protrepticus” 21.κγ]]; σιδηρονώτοις ἀσπίδος τύποις [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Phoenissae” 1130; χρυσοκόλλητοι τ. [prev. author] “Rh.” 305; τ. ἀργυροῦς “IG” 22.1533.30, 11(2).161 B 77, compare 115 (Delos, 3rd c.BC); τύπους ἐργάσασθαι καὶ παρέχειν [prev. work]42(1).102.36 (Epid., 4th c.BC)]]; tablet bearing a relief, καθελέσθαι τοὺς τ. καὶ εἴ τι ἄλλο ἐστὶν ἀργυροῦν ἢ χρυσοῦν [Refs [[prev. work] 22.839.30, compare 56, +others]]; τ. Ἔρωτα ἔχων ἐπειργασμένον [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd c.AD: Pausanias Periegeta 6.23.5; τῶν τ᾽ ἄλλων ὧν τύπος εἰκόν᾽ ἔχει “IG” 2.2378, compare 22.2021.8, 3.1330.5; ἐνταῦθά εἰσιν ἐπὶ τύπου γυναικῶν εἰκόνες 2nd c.AD: Pausanias Periegeta 9.11.3]]; πεποιημένα ἐν τύπῳ in relief, [Refs [[prev. author] 2.19.17]]; typos scalpsit, [Refs 1st c.AD+ [1st c.AD: Plinius Rerum Naturalium Scriptor “Historia Naturalis” 35.128]]; impressā argillā typum fecit, [Refs [[prev. work] 151]]; πρὸς Ναυσίαν περὶ τοῦ τ., title of speech by Lysias, [Refs [10th c.AD: Suidas Legal icographus]] see entry {λιθουργικ; Γάλλοι.. ἔχοντες προστηθίδια καὶ τύπους} [Refs 2nd c.BC+ [2nd c.BC: Polybius Historicus 21.37.6, compare 21.6.7.]]

__V

τύπτω
[in LXX chiefly for hi. ;]
to strike, smite, beat: with accusative, Mat.24:49, Mrk.15:19, Luk.12:45, Act.18:17 21:32 23:2-3; of mourners, τὰ στήθη, Luk.18:13 23:48; ἐπὶ τ. σιαγόνα, Luk.6:29; εἰς τ. κεφαλήν, Mat.27:30. Metaphorical, of God inflicting evil: Act.23:3 (cf. Exo.8:2, Eze.7:9, al.); of disquieting conscience, 1Co.8:12.†

short_definition: Tyrannus — 1. an absolute sovereign , unlimited by law or constitution, (Herdotus Historicus), etc.: not applied to old hereditary sovereignties βασιλεῖαι); such as those of (Homer) or of Spa
deep_entry:
Abbott-Smith / STEPBible (TBESG)
1. an absolute sovereign , unlimited by law or constitution, (Herdotus Historicus), etc.: not applied to old hereditary sovereignties  βασιλεῖαι); such as those of (Homer) or of Sparta; for the term rather regards the irregular way in which the power was gained , than the way in which it was exercised , being applied to the mild Pisistratus, but not to the despotic kings of Persia. However, the word soon came to imply reproach, like our tyrant , (Plato Philosophus), etc.
2. in a wider sense, the tyrant's son , or any member of his family , (Sophocles Tragicus):—;so, ἡ τύραννος was both the queen  herself or a princess , (Euripides)
3. τύραννος, ον, as adjective kingly, royal , [variant datesTragica Adespota
4. imperious, despotic , (Thucydides); τύραννα δρᾶν (Sophocles Tragicus)
τύραννος is probably from same Root as κύριος, κοίρανος. (ML)

---

[Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 18.381, etc.]], Doric dialect -ίσδω [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [3rd c.BC: Theocritus Poeta Bucolicus 14.9]]: future Attic dialect -ιῶ[Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 21.221]], (ἐν-) probably in [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Thesmophoriazusae” 720 (-ίσεις codex R)]]: aorist ὕβρισα [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 6.87, 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Ajax” 560, etc.]]: perfect ὕβρικα [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Lysistrata” 400, 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 21.128]]: pluperfect ὑβρίκειν [Refs [[prev. author] 3.14]]:—middle, future ὑβριοῦμαι [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Ecclesiazusae” 666 (_anapaest meter_)]]:—passive, future ὑβρισθήσομαι [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 21.222]]: aorist ὑβρίσθην [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Ajax” 367, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Leges” 885a]]: perfect ὕβρισμαι [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Cyclops” 665, etc.]]: (ὕβρις):—wax wanton, run riot, in the use of superior strength or power, or in sensual indulgence, ὑβρίζοντες ὑπερφιάλως δοκέουσι δαίνυσθαι κατὰ δῶμα [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 1.227; ὑβρίζοντες ἀτάσθαλα μηχανόωνται 3.207, 17.588; ἀλλὰ μάλ᾽ ὑβρίζεις 18.381; ὁππότ᾽ ἀνὴρ ἄδικος καὶ ἀτάσθαλος.. ὑβρίζῃ πλούτῳ κεκορημένος 6th c.BC: Theognis Elegiacus 751; ἐνταῦθα νῦν ὕβριζε 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Prometheus Vinctus” 82, compare 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Antigone” 480, etc.]]; especially of lust, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Memorabilia” 2.1.30]]; opposed to σωφρονεῖν, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. author] “Cyr.” 8.1.30, 5th c.BC: Antipho Orator 4.4.2.]]

ὑγιῆ σώματα ἀπεργάζεσθαι 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Leges” 684c]]; τὸ ὑ. τοῦ σώματος, opposed to τὸ νοσοῦν, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. author] “Smp.” 186b, compare 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Memorabilia” 1.3.13]]; πόλις (opposed to φλεγμαίνουσα) [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 372e: proverbial, ὑγιέστερος κολοκύντας or ὄμφακος]] 'sound as a bell', [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Epicharmus Comicus [same place], 9th c.AD: Photius Legal icographus, etc.]]; ὑγιέστερος κροτῶνος or Κρότωνος [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-3rd c.BC: Menander Comicus 318, compare 1st c.BC-1st c.AD: Strabo Geographus 6.1.12.]]

__2
of one's case or condition, σῶς καὶ ὑ. safe and sound, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 4.76, 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 3.34.]]

__3
of things, safe and sound, in good case, of the Hermae, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Lysias Orator 6.12]]; of ships, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 8.107; κόσμος 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Memorabilia” 4.3.13; τὸ ἔδαφος καὶ οἱ τοῖχοι 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Mirabilia” 842a33; σῶν καὶ ὑγιὲς μένειν 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Timaeus” 82b]]; in good condition, unbroken, πίθοι, κώθων, λίθος, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [“IG” 12.326.7, 42(1).121.85 (Epid., 4th c.BC), 7.3073.32 (Lebad., 2nd c.BC)]]; πίθοι ὑ., opposed to ἀγγεῖα τετρημένα καὶ σαθρά, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Gorgias” 493e, compare “Cra.” 440c, “Men.” 77a (see. below 111.1); ἱμάτια “POxy.” 530.20 (2nd c.AD); μύλος ὑ. καὶ ἀσινής [prev. work] 278.18 (1st c.AD).]]

__II
sound in mind, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Simonides Lyricus 5.4, etc.; φρένες ὑγιεῖς 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Bacchae” 948]]; virtuous, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Phaedo” 89d; ἦθος [prev. author] “R.” 409d, etc.; ὡς ὑγιεστάτη ψυχή [prev. author] “Grg.” 526d]]; as a complimentary epithet, ὑγιέστατον ἀνθύπατον [Refs 3rd c.AD+ [“OGI” 568.6 (Tlos, 3rd c.AD).]]

__II.2
of words, opinions, and the like, sound, wholesome, wise, μῦθος ὃς.. νῦν ὑγιής the word which is now fitting, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 8.524]] (the only place where any of this family of words occurs in [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Homerus Epicus); ὑ. δόξαι 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 584e; εἴ τι ὑ. διανοοῦνται 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 4.22, compare 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Theaetetus” 194b; χεῖρας καὶ γνώμην καθαροὶ καὶ ὑγιεῖς “IG” 12(1).789.5 (Lindus, 2nd c.AD).]]

__II.3
frequently with a negative, λόγος οὐκ ὑ. [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.8; οὐδὲν ὑ. βούλευμα [prev. author] 6.100]]; so in Trag. and Attic dialect, ὦ μηδὲν ὑ. μηδ᾽ ἐλεύθερον φρονῶν [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Philoctetes” 1006; ἑλικτὰ κοὐδὲν ὑ. 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Andromache” 448; οὐδὲν ὑ. διανοουμένων 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 3.75; μηδὲν ὑ. λέγειν 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Phoenissae” 201, compare 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Thesmophoriazusae” 636, “Pl.” 274, etc.]]; φέρειν, ἀσκεῖν, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. author] “Ach.” 956, “Pl.” 50; οὐδὲν ὑ. οὐδ᾽ ἀληθὲς ἔχειν 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Phaedo” 69b]]: also of persons, τὰς οὐδὲν ὑγιές [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Thesmophoriazusae” 394; πανοῦργον, ἄδικον, ὑγιὲς μηδὲ ἕν [prev. author] “Pl.” 37: with _genitive_, οὐδ᾽ ἦν ἄρ᾽ ὑ. οὐδὲν ἐμπύρου φλογός]] there is nothing sound or good in it, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Helena” 746; φεῦ· ὡς οὐδὲν ἀτεχνῶς ὑ. ἐστιν οὐδενός 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Plutus” 362, compare 870, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Phaedo” 90c, “Grg.” 524e, “R.” 584a, 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 18.23, etc.; οὐχ ὑ. οὐδὲν ἔτι λέγω τῶν ὀργίων 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Bacchae” 262, compare “Cyc.” 259; ἐπ᾽ οὐδενὶ ὑγιεῖ οὐδ᾽ ἀληθεῖ 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 603b, compare 5th c.BC: Lysias Orator 9.4.]]

__II.4
logically sound, τὸ ὑ. συνημμένον [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd c.AD: Sextus Empiricus Philosophus “adversus Mathematicos” 8.118; ὑ. ἀπόδειξις [prev. author] “P.” 1.116, compare 2nd c.AD: Arrianus Historicus “Epicteti Dissertationes” 2.1.4.]]

__III
neuter as adverb, ὑγιὲς φθέγγεσθαι ring sound and clear, opposed to σαθρόν, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Theaetetus” 179d]]: also in phrase ἐξ ὑγιοῦς, φροντίζειν ὅπως καὶ τἆλλα γένηται.. ἐξ ὑ. correctly, in order, [Refs 2nd c.BC+ [PTeb. 27.60 (2nd c.BC)]]; οὐκ ἐξ ὑ. τὰς κτήσεις ποιοῦσιν, i. e. dishonestly, [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd c.AD: Vettius Valens Astrologus 90.32.]]

__III.2
regular adverb ὑγιῶς, healthily, διάγειν [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd c.AD: Athenaeus Epigrammaticus 2.46f]]; soundly, κρίνειν, φιλοσοφεῖν, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 409a, 619d; ὑ. πεπολίτευμαι 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 18.298; ὑ. ἀπαγγεῖλαι 3rd c.AD: Plotinus Philosophus 4.4.19]]; ὑ. καὶ πιστῶς honourably and faithfully, frequently in Papyrus, [Refs 3rd c.AD+ [“POxy.” 1031.18 (3rd c.AD), etc. (Prob. from ὑ-,]] cf. Sanskrit su- 'well', and -γιη-, I.-[Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus γυιψē]] compare guiyō in βιῶναι.)

deep_entry:
Abbott-Smith / STEPBible (TBESG)
ὑγρός, -ά, -όν,
[in LXX: Jdg.16:7,8 (לַח), Job.8:16 (רָשׂב), Sir.39:13
wet, moist, opposite to ξηρός: of wood, sappy, green: Luk.23:31.†
(AS)

---

LSJ / STEPBible (TFLSJ)
ὑγρός, ά, όν:
comparative ὑγρότερος [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Theaetetus” 162b, etc.]]: superlative -ότατος[Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “de Equitandi ratione” 7.7, etc.]]:—wet, moist, fluid (opposed to ξηρός), ὑγρὸν ἔλαιον, i. e. olive-oil, opposed to fat or tallow, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 23.281, 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 6.79]]; ὑ. πίσσα, νᾶπυ, raw pitch, liquid mustard, [Refs 1st c.BC+ [“SIG” 1171.14 (Lebena, 1st c.BC), “IG” 42(1).126.22 (Epid., 2nd c.AD)]]; τὸ ὑ. ξύλον, opposed to τὸ ξηρόν, [NT+8th c.BC+ [NT.Luke.23.31; ὑγρὸν ὕδωρ 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 4.458]]; ἄνεμοι ὑγρὸν ἀέντες winds blowing moist or rainy, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [5.478, 19.440, 8th-7th c.BC: Hesiodus Epicus “Opera et Dies” 625, “Th.” 869]]; ὑ. ἅλς, πέλαγος, θάλασσα, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “O.” 7.69. “P.” 4.40, 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Supplices” 259]]; ὑγρὰ νύξ a wet night, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Critias” 112a]]; ἐφ᾽ ὑγροῖς ζωγραφεῖν paint on a wet ground, [Refs 1st c.AD+ [1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus 2.759c.]]

__2
ὑγρά, Ionic dialect ὑγρή, ἡ, the moist, i.e. the sea, ἐπὶ τραφερήν τε καὶ ὑγρήν [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 14.308; ἠμὲν ἐφ᾽ ὑγρὴν ἠδ᾽ ἐπ᾽ ἀπείρονα γαῖαν 24.341, 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 1.97; ἐφ᾽ ὑγρᾷ 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Vespae” 678; πουλὺν ἐφ᾽ ὑγρήν 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 10.27]]; so ὑγρὰ κέλευθα the watery ways, i. e. the sea,[Refs 8th c.BC+ [1.312, 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 3.71.]]

__3
τὸ ὑ. and τὰ ὑ. wet, moisture, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.142, 5th c.BC: Hippocrates Medicus “περὶ τόπων τῶν κατὰ ἄνθρωπον” 9, “Liqu.” at Title Page]]; Liquid, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 4.172; γῆ ὑγρῷ φυραθεῖσα 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Theaetetus” 147c]]; ἐξερρύα συχνὸν ὑγρόν a quantity of fluid, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [Inscriptiones Graecae 42(1).122.4 (Epid., 4th c.BC)]]; μετρεῖν τὰ ὑγρά liquids, [Refs [[prev. work]22.1013.10]]; ἐπὶ ὑγροῖς οὐκ ἐξὸν δανείζειν [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [“PGnom.” 232 (2nd c.AD).]]

__4
μέτρα ὑγρὰ καὶ ξηρά liquid and dry measure, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Leges” 746e.]]

__5
θῆρες ὑ. water-animals, opposed to πεζοί, [Refs 1st c.BC+ [“Anthologia Graeca” 9.18 (\{1st c.BC-1st c.AD\}: Germanicus Caesar Epigrammaticus); οἱ ὄρνιθες οἱ ὑ. 2nd-3rd c.AD: Philostratus Sophista “Philostrati majoris imagines” 1.9]]; ὑ. ἀοιδός, of a frog, [Refs [“Anthologia Graeca” 6.43 (from Plato).]]

__6
of the bowels or faeces, loose, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Hippocrates Medicus “ἀφορισμοί” 2.20, 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Historia Animalium” 617a1.]]

__7
ὑ. σφυγμός a damp pulse, defined by [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd c.AD: Galenus Medicus 19.405.]]

__II
soft, pliant, supple, of the eagle's back, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “P.” 1.9]]; of the limbs and body, ὑγραῖς ἐν ἀγκάλαις [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Fragmenta” 941, compare 2nd c.AD: Babrius Fabularum Scriptor 34.7]]; ὑγρὸς τὸ εἶδος, of Ἔρως, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Symposium” 196a]]; νεώτερος καὶ ὑγρότερος, opposed to σκληρός, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. author] “Tht.” 162b; χορῷ.. ἔτερπον κέαρ ὑγροῖσι ποσσί 5th c.BC: Bacchylides Lyricus 16.108; ὑ. ὀρχηστής 2nd c.AD(?): Pollianus Epigrammaticus 4.96, compare 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “de Partibus Animalium” 655a24 (_comparative_)]]; ὑγρὰ ἔχειν τὰ σκέλη, of a horse, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “de Equitandi ratione” 1.6]]; of a horse's neck, [Refs [[prev. author] “Cyn.” 4.1 (so in _adverb_ of colts, γόνατα ὑγρῶς κάμπτειν, ὑγρῶς τοῖς σκέλεσι χρῆσθαι, [prev. author] “Eq.” 1.6, 10.15)]]; of the hare, [Refs [[prev. author] “Cyn.” 5.31]]; of the jackal, ταχυτῆτι διαφέρει διὰ τὸ ὑγρὸς εἶναι καὶ πηδᾷ πόρρω [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Historia Animalium” 580a30]]; also of plants, ὑ. ἄκανθος [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [3rd c.BC: Theocritus Poeta Bucolicus 1.55; ὑ. χολάδες 2nd c.AD: Babrius Fabularum Scriptor 1.10]]; σῶμα ὑγρὸν κείμενον lying in an easy position, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Hippocrates Medicus “προγνωστικόν” 3; ὑγρὸν χύτλασον σεαυτόν 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Vespae” 1213]]; κέρας ὑ., of a bow, [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [3rd c.BC: Theocritus Poeta Bucolicus 25.206.]]

__II.2
languid, feeble, of one dying, ἐς ὑγρὸν ἀγκῶνα.. παρθένῳ προσπτύσσεται [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Antigone” 1236; κἀπιθεὶς ὑγρὰν χέρα 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Phoenissae” 1439.]]

__II.3
of substance, flaccid, flabby, σάρκες [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Historia Animalium” 598a9, 603b32, +others]]

__II.3.b
tender, νεοττοί [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd-3rd c.AD: Aelianus “De Natura Animalium - Ar.Byzantine Epit.” 7.9; βρέφος 4th-5th c.AD(?): Nonnus Epicus “Dionysiaca” 1.4.]]

__II.4
moist with wine, tipsy, ὑγρὴν τὴν ψυχὴν ἔχειν [Refs 1st c.AD+ [1st c.AD(?): Heraclitus 117; ἡ διάνοια ὑ. γεγενημένη 1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus 2.713a; οἰνοβαρὴς.. ὑγρὸν ἀείδων, οὐ μάλα νγφάλιον κλάζων μέλος 2nd-3rd c.AD: Oppianus Anazarbensis Epicus “Halieutica - Poetae Bucolici et Didactici” 2.412.]]

__II.5
of the eyes, melting, languishing, ὑ. βλέμμα [Refs 1st c.AD+ [“Anacreontea” 15.21; ὑγρὰ δερκομένοισιν ἐν ὄμμασιν “Anthologia Graeca” 7.27 (Antip. Sid.); ἐπ᾽ ὄμμασιν ὑγρὰ δεδορκώς “APl.” 4.306 (1st c.AD: Leonidas Alexandrinus Epigrammaticus); τῶν ὀφθαλμῶν τὸ ὑ. ἅμα τῷ φαιδρῷ 2nd c.AD: Lucianus Sophista “Im.” 6]]; also πόθος ὑ. a languishing, longing desire, [Refs [“hymnus ad Panem” 33]]. adverb, ὑγρῶς βλέπειν [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd-3rd c.AD: Philostratus Sophista “Epistulae” 33]]: superlative, ὑγρότατα καὶ πένθιμα μελῳδεῖν [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd c.AD: Appianus Historicus “Bella Civilia” 1.106.]]

__II.6
of language, smoothly flowing, [Refs 1st c.BC+ [1st c.BC: Dionysius Halicarnassensis “de Demosthene” 20.]]

__II.7
metaphorically of persons or their tempers, facile, pliant, easy, ὑγρός τις καὶ δημοτικός [Refs 1st c.AD+ [1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus “Marius” 28; κόλαξ ὑγρὸς ὢν μεταβάλλεσθαι [prev. author] 2.51c]]; τὸ Κίμωνος ὑ. his easy temper, [Refs [[prev. author] “Per.” 5]]; pleasure-loving, [Refs 5th c.AD+ [5th c.AD(?): Hesychius Legal icographus]]; ὑγρότατος ἐς ταῦτα prone to.., [Refs 1st c.AD+ [2nd c.AD: Appianus Historicus “Bella Civilia” 5.8; ὑ. τῷ γελοίῳ 1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus “Brutus” 29 (_comparative_).]]

__II.7.b
soft, dainty, luxurious, voluptuous, [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [[prev. author] 2.751a; ὑ. πρὸς τὴν δίαιταν [prev. author] “Sol.” 3; βίου.., ὃν πάντες εἰώθασιν ὀνομάζειν ὑγρόν 2nd c.AD: Alexander Rhetor 203; compare ὑγρότης 11.2.]]

__II.8
of the vowels α ι υ, sometimes long and sometimes short, [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd c.AD: Sextus Empiricus Philosophus “adversus Mathematicos” 1.100.]]

__II.8.b
of στοιχεῖα, liquid (i.e.  λ μ ν ρ), [Refs 2nd c.BC+ [2nd c.BC: Dionysius Thrax Grammaticus 632.9, 7th c.AD: Hephaestio Grammaticus 1.3, +others]]

__III
adverb ὑγρῶς, see above [Refs [11.1 and 5]]; also ὑγρότερον δαπανᾶν spend more freely, [Refs 1st c.BC+ [1st c.BC: Philodemus Philosophus “περὶ οἰκονομίας” p.73J.]]

LSJ / STEPBible (TFLSJ)
ὑδρ-ία, ἡ,
(ὕδωρ) water-pot, pitcher, [NT+5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Vespae” 926, “Ec.” 678 (_anapaest meter_), LXX.Eccl.12.6, “CIG” “Corpus Inscriptionum Graecarum” “Corpus Inscriptionum Graecarum” 2855.10 (from Branchidae), NT.John.2.6, etc.]]; ὑδρίης πέρι δῆρις (compare ἀμφορίτης) [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [3rd c.BC: Apollonius Rhodius Epicus 4.1767: proverbial, ἐπὶ θύραις τὴν ὑδρίαν]] to break the pitcher at the door, 'there's many a slip 'twixt cup and lip', [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Rhetorica” 1363a7.]]

__II
vessel of any kind, e. g. wine-pot, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Fragmenta” 136]]; a pot of money, [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [[prev. author] “Av.” 602 (_anapaest meter_) (ἐν ὑδρίαις γὰρ ἔκειντο οἱ θησαυροί Scholia (at [prev. work]) (603)),compare “IG” 11(2).161 B 100 (Delos, 3rd c.BC)]]; ὑ. χαλκῆ [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 47.52]]; ὑ. χρυσῆ, ἀργυρᾶ, [Refs [“IG” 22.204.35]]; ὑδρίαι ἄρτων πέντε bread-pans, [Refs 6th c.AD+ [POxy. 155.4 (6th c.AD).]]

__II.2
balloting urn, especially in lawcourts, etc., [Refs 5th c.BC+ [“IG” 9(1).334.45 (_Locrian dialect_, 5th c.BC), 5th-6th c.BC: Isocrates Orator 17.33, 1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus “Tiberius Gracchus” 11.]]

__II.3
cinerary urn, [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [[prev. author] “Phil.” 21, 2nd c.AD: Lucianus Sophista “Dem.Enc.” 29, etc.]]

__II.4
water-clock, [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [2nd c.AD: Sextus Empiricus Philosophus “adversus Mathematicos” 5.75, 4th c.AD: Julianus Imperator “Caesares” 325c. [ῑ in 3rd c.BC: Apollonius Rhodius Epicus [same place], where ὑδρείης is variant]]]

ὑδρο-ποτέω,

ὕδωρ
genitive,

deep_entry:

υἱός, -οῦ, ὁ, [in LXX very frequently and nearly always for בֵּן, Gen.4:17, al.; for בַּר, Dan LXX TH 7:13, al.; etc. ;],
a son;
__1. in the ordinary sense: Mat.10:37, Mrk.9:17, Luk.1:13, al. mult.; omitted with the art. of origin (WM, §30, 3; Bl., §35, 2), τὸν τοῦ Ἰεσσαί, Act.13:22 (LXX); also with genitive anarth. (cl.), Σώπατρος Πύρρου Βεροιαῖος, Act.20:4; with adj., προτότοκος, Luk.2:7; μονογένης, Luk.7:12; opposite to νόθος, Heb.12:8; in a wider sense, of posterity: ὁ υἱ. Δαυΐδ, of the Messiah (cf. Dalman, Words, 316ff.; DCG, ii, 653f.), Mat.22:42, 45 Mrk.12:35, 37 Luk.20:41, 44 al.; υἱοὶ  Ἰσραήλ, (cf. υἷες Ἀχαιῶν, Hom., Il., i, 162, al.), Mat.27:9, Act.9:15, al.
__2. Metaphorical;
__(a) as belonging to, being connected with or having the quality of that which follows (a usage mainly due to translation from a Semitic original; cf. Deiss., BS, 161ff.; Dalman, Words, 115f.; DCG, ii, 652f.): τ. πονεροῦ (διαβόλου), Mat.13:38, Act.13:10; τ. νυμφῶνος (see: νυμφών), Mat.9:15, Mrk.2:19, al.; τ. φωτός (Lft., Notes, 74), Luk.16:8, Jhn.12:36, 1Th.5:5; τ. εἰρεήμης, Luk.10:6; γεέννης, Mat.23:15; τ. ἀπωλείας, Jhn.17:12, 2Th.2:3; τ. αἰῶνος τούτου, Luk.16:8 20:34; τ. ἀπειθειάς, Eph.2:2 5:6; βροντῆς, Mrk.3:17; τ. ἀναστάσεως, Luk.20:36; παρακλήσεως, Act.4:36; τ. προφητῶν κ. τ. διαθήκης, Act.3:25;
__(b) υἱὸς τ. θεοῦ (cf. Dalman, Words, 268ff.; Deiss., BS, 166f.; DB, iv, 570 ff.; DCG, ii, 654ff.), of men, as partakers of the Divine nature and of the life to come: Mat.5:9, Luk.20:36, Rom.8:14 9:26, al.; υἱοὶ (κ. θυγατέρες) τ. ὑψίστου, Luk.6:35, 2Co.6:18; in an unique sense of Jesus, Mat.4:3 8:29 28:19, Mrk.3:4, Luk.4:41, Jhn.9:35 11:27, al.; ὁ Χριστὸς ὁ υἱ. τ. θεοῦ ζῶντος (τ. εὐλογητοῦ), Mat.16:16, Mrk.14:61;
__(with) (ὁ) υἱὸς τοῦ ἀνθρώπου (in LXX for Heb. בּן אדם, Aram, בּר אנשׁ; cf. Dalman, Words, 234ff.; DB, iv, 579ff.; DCG, ii, 659ff.; Westc., St. John, i, 74ff.; other reff. in Swete, Mk, 2:10), based on the Aram. of Dan.7:13, where the phrase, like the corresponding Heb. (as in Psa.8:5), means a man, one of the species, and indicates the human appearance of the person in question. It is used of the Messiah in Enoch, with 46, §1-4, also in II Est.13:3, 12, al. Our Lord first makes the phrase a title, using the def. art. It seems to combine the ideas of his true humanity and representative character. Exc. in Act.7:56 and (anarth.) Rev.1:13 14:14, it is used of Jesus only by himself: Mat.8:20, Mrk.2:10, Luk.5:24, Jhn.1:52, al.
(AS)

Sanskrit pitṛ[snull]u); ὑέεσσι [Refs [“IG” 14.10 (Syrac.)]]; υἷος in [Refs 5th c.BC+ [“SIG” 55 (Thessaly, 5th c.BC) is perhaps the _Aeolic dialect_ _genitive_ (ὑός]] is nominative rather than genitive in [Refs 2nd c.BC+ [“IG” 12.828); _accusative_ ὗα “Schwyzer” 625 (Mytil., 2nd-1st c.BC)]]; a nominative ὑϊς (scanned - ?~X) [Refs 6th c.BC+ [“IG” 12.472 (Boeotia, 6th c.BC),compare 4th-5th c.BC: Simonides Lyricus 249 (see. below); _nominative_ _plural_ ὗες “IG” 22.3632.24 (hexameters, Eleusis, 2nd c.AD). The initial syllable is both υἱ-and ὑ]]-in Attic dialect Inscrr. down to [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC (e. g. ὑεῖς “IG” 12.115.14, ὑέ[σιν] [prev. work]54.14, ὑόν see above), afterwards ὑ-, but υἱός]] reappears under the Empire; in Plato codex A usually has ὑιος, which is found also in T, codex B always has υἱός, editors restore ὑό; accusative υἱόν is recommended by [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd c.AD: Phrynichus Atticista]] [same place]; in Inscrr. of Pergamon, Magnesia, and Delphi, and in non-literary Papyri, ὑός is at all times less common than υἱός:—ὁ υεἱός [Refs [“CIG” “Corpus Inscriptionum Graecarum” “Corpus Inscriptionum Graecarum” (add.) 3857p; _dative_ υεἱῷ [prev. work]3846z82 (both Phrygia),compare “BCH” 11.471]]:—son, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 6.366, etc.]]; υἱὸν ποιεῖσθαί τινα to adopt as a son, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aeschines Orator 2.28]]; υἱεῖς ἄνδρες grown-up sons, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 25.88: _metaphorically_, Κόρον Ὕβριος υἱόν]] Oracle texts cited in [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 8.77]]: rarely of animals, [NT.Matt.21.5.]

__2
periphrastic, υἷες Ἀχαιῶν, for Ἀχαιοί, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 1.162, +others; compare παῖς 1.3.]]

generally, child, and so υἱ. ἄρρην male child, [NT+3rd c.AD+ [NT.Rev. 12.5, “PSI” 9.1039.36 (3rd c.AD).]]

__4
frequently in [Refs [LXX in periphrases (Hebraisms with various meanings), υἱὸς ἐτῶν ἑκατόν 100]] years old, [LXX.Gen.11.10, +others]; υἱοὶ ἀδικίας [Refs [“2 Ki.” 7.10; υἱοὶ θανατώσεως “1 Ki.” 26.16; υἱοὶ τῶν συμμίζεων]]hostages, [LXX+NT [LXX.2Ki.14.14; so υἱὸς εἰρήνης NT.Luke.10.6.]]

in some dialects, including the Ionic dialect Prose of [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus, υἱός is replaced by παῖς: υἱός]] is rare in Trag., [Refs 8th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Septem contra Thebas” 609, “fragment” 320, 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Orestes” 1689 (_anapaest meter_), +others, and 7 times in 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus: 8th c.BC: Homerus Epicus has both words in this sense.]]

as a general term of affection, [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [“PGiss.” 68.2 (2nd c.AD), “POxy.” 1219.2 (3rd c.AD)]]; υἱέ, an author's address to the reader, [LXX.Pro.1.8, +others]

δάμου υἱός, υἱὸς πόλεως, Ἑλλάδος, as titles of honour, [Refs 1st c.AD+ [“SIG” 804.10 (Cos, 1st c.AD), 813A,B (Delph., 1st c.AD), 854 (Eleusis, 1st c.AD).]]

υἱοὶ ἀνθρώπων sons of men, periphrastic for men (compare above 2,4), [LXX.Psa.89(90).3]; οἱ υἱοὶ τῶν ἀ.[LXX+NT [LXX.Gen.11.5, NT.Mark.3.28; υἱὸς ἀνθρώπου]]man, [LXX.Eze.2.1, 3, +others]; of the Messiah,[LXX+NT [LXX.Dan.7.13, NT.Rev.14.14]]; used by Jesus of himself, [NT.Matt.8.20, +others] (by Stephen recalling the words of Jesus, [NT.Act.7.56).]

__9
υἱοὶ Θεοῦ sons of God, implying inheritors of the nature of God [compare(above 4), NT.Matt.5.9, compare 45, NT.Luke.6.35]; implying participants in the glory of God, [Refs [[prev. work] 20.36.]]

__9.b

__9.c
Θεοῦ υἱός, = Latin [Refs [“Divi” (i.e. “Caesaris”)]] filius, patronymic of Augustus, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [“BGU” 543.3 (1st c.BC), “PTeb.” 382.21 (1st c.BC), “IG” 12(3).174.2 (Epist. ad Cnidios, 5 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator)]]. [Hom.sometimes has the first syllable short in nominative, vocative and accusative singular, οὐδὲ Δρύαντος υἱός [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 6.130; Ἀμφιτρύωνος υἱός 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 11.270; Ποδῆς υἱὸς Ἠετίωνος 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 17.575, compare 590; Ἀνθεμίωνος υἱόν 4.473; Σελάγου υἱόν 5.612; Ἕκτορ, υἱὲ Πριάμοιο 7.47; and Πηλῆος υἱός, Μηκιστῆος υἱός seem to be the better readings in 1.489, 2.566: in these places some other form ought perhaps to be restored, but none of the known forms has a short ῠ: ὑός has ῡ in “IG” 12.585 (6th c.BC), 828 (5th c.BC), 2.2338, 22.4319 (both 4th c.BC)]]; Simon. [prev. cited] seems to have used a monosyllable nominative υἷς, and Hdn.Gr. may have read it as ὕις (??), but this is uncertain, as in [Refs 8th c.BC+ [Scholia 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 5.266 he seems to say that ὕις (υἷις codex)]] does not occur.] (Prob. from *sū-yú-s, cf. Sanskrit sūte 'procreate', Tocharian (A-dialogue) se, (B-dialogue) soyä 'son'; different suffix in *sū-nu-s, Sanskrit sūnūs, etc., and in *s[ucaron]-nu-s, O[Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus]] sunu, etc. (all = son); *sūyú- perhaps became *s[ucaron]wyú-, then *suiwú-; υἱός and υἱόν perhaps by dissimilation from υἱύς υἱύν, since the o-stem forms appear first where υ-υ would otherwise be repeated; ὗϊς (ὑΐς) may be another dissimilation; the precise origin of υἷος υἷι υἷες etc. is uncertain.)

ὕλη [ῡ], ἡ,
forest, woodland, [NT+8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 11.155, 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 17.316, NT.Jam.3.5, etc.; γῆν.. δασέαν ὕλῃ παντοίῃ 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 4.21; ἀπ᾽ ὕλης ἀγρίης ζώειν [prev. author] 1.203]]; ὕλα ἀεργός virgin forest, [Refs [Berl.Sitzb. 1927.167 (from Cyrene)]]; τὰ δένδρα καὶ ὕλη fruit-trees and forest-trees, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 4.69 (compareδένδρον)]]; not only of forest-trees, but also of copse, brushwood, undergrowth (compare ὕλημα), directly opposed to to timber-trees, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 1.5.1, “Oec.” 16.13, 17.12, “PSI” 6.577.8 (3rd c.BC), 2nd c.AD: Soranus Medicus 1.40]]: also in plural, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [“hymnus ad Cererem” 386, 4th-5th c.BC: Hecataeus Milesius Historicus 291 1st c.AD: Josephus Historicus, 2nd c.BC: Moschus Bucolicus 3.88, 2nd c.BC: Polybius Historicus 5.7.10, 1st c.BC: Diodorus Siculus Historicus 3.48, 1st c.BC: Dionysius Halicarnassensis “de Thucydide” 6, 1st c.BC-1st c.AD: Strabo Geographus 5.1.12, 15.1.60, 1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus “Pyrrhus” 25, “Cat. Ma.” 21, “Comp. Cim.Luc.” 3, 2nd c.AD: Lucianus Sophista “Prom.” 12, “Sacr.” 10, “Am.” 12, 2nd c.AD: Babrius Fabularum Scriptor 12.2, +others, 4th-5th c.AD(?): Nonnus Epicus “Dionysiaca” 3.69, 252, 16.91, 36.70, etc.]]

__II
wood cut down, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 5.257 (cf. III)]]; firewood, fuel, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 7.418, 23.50, 111, +others, 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 9.234, 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 4.164, 6.80]]; brushwood, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. author] 7.36, 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 2.75, etc.]]; timber, ὕ. ναυπηγησίμη [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Leges” 705c; ναυπηγήσιμος καὶ οἰκοδομική 4th-3rd c.BC: Theophrastus Philosophus “Historia Plantarum” 5.7.1, compare “IG” 42(1).102.50 (Epid., 4th c.BC)]]; also, twigs for birds' nests, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Historia Animalium” 559a2.]]

__III
the stuff of which a thing is made, material, (perhaps so of wood), [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 5.257]]; rarely of other material, as metal, οἱ παρ᾽ ἄκμονι.. ὕλην ἄψυχον δημιουργοῦντες [Refs 5th c.BC+ [1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus 2.802b (compare 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Fragmenta” 844, but ὕλη is Plutarch's word)]]: generally, materials, [Refs 6th c.AD+ [PMasp. 151.91 (6th c.AD).]]

__III.2
in Philosophy, matter, first in [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus (5th-4th c.BC: Timaeus Locrus Philosophus 93b, +others is later)]]; defined as τὸ ὑποκείμενον γενέσεως καὶ φθορᾶς δεκτικόν, [Refs [“GC” 320a2]]; as τὸ ἐζ οὗ γίγνεται, [Refs [“Metaphorical” 1032a17; οὐσία ἥ τε ὕ. καὶ τὸ εἶδος καὶ τὸ ἐκ τούτων [prev. work]1035a2; opposed to as δυνάμει τόδε τι to τόδε τι ἐνεργεία, [prev. work] 1042a27; opposed to ἐντελέχεια, [prev. work]1038b6:]] in later philosophical writers, mostly opposed to to the intelligent and formative principle (νοῦς), [Refs 4th c.AD+ [5th c.AD: Proclus Philosophus “Inst.” 72, etc.; ὕ. τῶν ἀριθμῶν 4th c.AD: Iamblichus Philosophus “de communi mathematica scientia” 4.]]

ὕ. ἰατρική materia medica, Dsc.at Title Page; so ὕλη alone, materia medica, [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [[prev. author] 1 “Prooem.”, 2nd c.AD: Galenus Medicus 17(2).181]]; ὗλαι τῆς τέχνης [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [[prev. passage], compare 6.77, 2nd c.AD: Soranus Medicus 1.83, 110, 2.15, 28; ἡ ὕ. τῶν ὁπλομαχικῶν ἐνεργειῶν 2nd c.AD: Galenus Medicus 6.157.]]

__III.4.b
ἡ μέση ὕλη the middle range of diet, [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd c.AD: Soranus Medicus 1.46, 2.15; τροφιμωτέρα ὕλη [prev. author] 1.95, compare 36.]]

αὐτός, -ή, -ό,
determinative pron., in late Gk. much more frequently than in cl. (WM, 178f.; Jannaris, HGG, §1399).
__1. Emphatic (so always in nom. exc. when preceded by the art., see infr., iii);
__(1) self (ipse), expressing opposition, distinction, exclusion, etc., αὐ. ἐκχυθήσεται, Luk.5:37; αὐ. ἐγινώσκεν, Jhn.2:25; αὐ.ὑμεῖς, Jhn.3:28; καὶ αὐ. ἐγώ, Rom.15:14; αὐ. Ἰησοῦς, Jhn.2:24; αὐ. καὶ οἱ μετ᾽ αὐτοῦ, Mrk.2:25; ὑμεῖς αὐ., Mrk.6:31; esp. (as freq in cl.) αὐ. ὁ, Mat.3:4, Mrk.6:17, Jhn.16:27, 1Th.3:11, al.; in late Gk., sometimes weakened, ἐν αὐτῇ τ. ὥρᾳ, in that hour, Luk.10:21 (M, Pr., 91; MM, see word);
__(2) emphatic, he, she, it (M, Pr., 86; Bl., §48, 1, 2, 7), Mat.1:21, 12:50, Luk.6:35, al.; pointing to some one as master (cl.), Mat.8:24, Mrk.4:38, al.; αὐ., καὶ αὐ. = οὗτος, ὁ δε (BL, §48, 1), Mat.14:2, Mrk.14:15, 44, Luk.1:22, 2:28, al.
__2. In oblique cases (cl.), for the simple pron. of 3rd of person(s), he, she, it, Mat.7:9, 10:12, 26:44, al.; with ptcp. in genitive absol., Mat.9:18, Mrk.13:1, al. (for irreg. constructions, V. Bl., §74, 5); pleonastically after the relative (cf. Heb. אֲשֶׁר לוֹ; WM, 184ff.; Bl., §50, 4; MM, see word), Mrk.7:25, Rev.3:8, 7:2, al.; in constr. ad sensum, without proper subject expressly indicated, Mat.4:23, Act.8:5, 2Co.2:13, al.; genitive αὐτοῦ = ἐκείνου, Rom.11:11, 1Th.2:19, Tit.3:5, Heb.2:4.
__3. ὁ, ἡ, τὸ αὐ., the same: Heb.1:12, 13:8; τὸ αὐ., ποιεῖν, Mat.5:46, 47, al.; φρονεῖν, Rom.12:16, 15:5, Php.2:2, al.; τὰ αὐ., Act.15:27, Rom.2:1, al.; κατὰ τὸ (τὰ) αὐ. (MM, see word), Act.14:1, Luk.6:23, al.; ἐπὶ τὸ αὐ., together (MM, see word), Mat.22:34, Act.1:15, al.; ἓν κ. τὸ αὐ., 1Co.11:5, 12:11; with dative (cl.), 1Co.11:5; with a noun, λόγος, Mrk.14:39; μέτρος, Php.1:30; πνεῦμα, 1Co.12:4.

αὐτός, -ή, -ό,
determinative pron., in late Gk. much more frequently than in cl. (WM, 178f.; Jannaris, HGG, §1399).
__1. Emphatic (so always in nom. exc. when preceded by the art., see infr., iii);
__(1) self (ipse), expressing opposition, distinction, exclusion, etc., αὐ. ἐκχυθήσεται, Luk.5:37; αὐ. ἐγινώσκεν, Jhn.2:25; αὐ.ὑμεῖς, Jhn.3:28; καὶ αὐ. ἐγώ, Rom.15:14; αὐ. Ἰησοῦς, Jhn.2:24; αὐ. καὶ οἱ μετ᾽ αὐτοῦ, Mrk.2:25; ὑμεῖς αὐ., Mrk.6:31; esp. (as freq in cl.) αὐ. ὁ, Mat.3:4, Mrk.6:17, Jhn.16:27, 1Th.3:11, al.; in late Gk., sometimes weakened, ἐν αὐτῇ τ. ὥρᾳ, in that hour, Luk.10:21 (M, Pr., 91; MM, see word);
__(2) emphatic, he, she, it (M, Pr., 86; Bl., §48, 1, 2, 7), Mat.1:21, 12:50, Luk.6:35, al.; pointing to some one as master (cl.), Mat.8:24, Mrk.4:38, al.; αὐ., καὶ αὐ. = οὗτος, ὁ δε (BL, §48, 1), Mat.14:2, Mrk.14:15, 44, Luk.1:22, 2:28, al.
__2. In oblique cases (cl.), for the simple pron. of 3rd of person(s), he, she, it, Mat.7:9, 10:12, 26:44, al.; with ptcp. in genitive absol., Mat.9:18, Mrk.13:1, al. (for irreg. constructions, V. Bl., §74, 5); pleonastically after the relative (cf. Heb. אֲשֶׁר לוֹ; WM, 184ff.; Bl., §50, 4; MM, see word), Mrk.7:25, Rev.3:8, 7:2, al.; in constr. ad sensum, without proper subject expressly indicated, Mat.4:23, Act.8:5, 2Co.2:13, al.; genitive αὐτοῦ = ἐκείνου, Rom.11:11, 1Th.2:19, Tit.3:5, Heb.2:4.
__3. ὁ, ἡ, τὸ αὐ., the same: Heb.1:12, 13:8; τὸ αὐ., ποιεῖν, Mat.5:46, 47, al.; φρονεῖν, Rom.12:16, 15:5, Php.2:2, al.; τὰ αὐ., Act.15:27, Rom.2:1, al.; κατὰ τὸ (τὰ) αὐ. (MM, see word), Act.14:1, Luk.6:23, al.; ἐπὶ τὸ αὐ., together (MM, see word), Mat.22:34, Act.1:15, al.; ἓν κ. τὸ αὐ., 1Co.11:5, 12:11; with dative (cl.), 1Co.11:5; with a noun, λόγος, Mrk.14:39; μέτρος, Php.1:30; πνεῦμα, 1Co.12:4.

in combination with γε, σύ γε, σέ γε, etc. (compare ἔγωγε), thou at least, for thy part, frequently in [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Homerus Epicus]] and Attic dialect; Doric dialect τύγε [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Epicharmus Comicus [272], 5th c.BC: Timocreon Lyricus 1 (variant{τύ γα}); τύγᾰ 3rd c.BC: Theocritus Poeta Bucolicus 5.69, 71]]; Boeotian dialect τούγα [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd c.AD: Apollonius Dyscolus Grammaticus “de Pronominibus;” 55.6]]: dative σοί γε [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 1.557]]: accusative σέ γε [Refs [10.96]], etc.:—also σύ περ [Refs [24.398.]]
