ὑμέναι-ος [ῠ], ὁ,
(Ὑμήν) the wedding or bridal song, sung by the bride's attendants as they led her to the bridegroom's house, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 18.493, 8th-7th c.BC: Hesiodus Epicus “Scutum Herculis” 274, 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Agamemnon” 707 (Lyric poetry), 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Iphigenia Aulidensis” 1036 (Lyric poetry, assuming variant): _plural_, παμφώνων ἰαχὰ ὑμεναίων 5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “P.” 3.17, cf. 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Alcestis” 922 (_anapaest meter_)]], etc.: Aeolic dialect ὐμήνᾰος [Refs 7th c.BC+ [7th-6th c.BC: Sappho Lyrica 91, “epigram Gr.” 418.7 (from Cyrene)]]: a form ὑμήναιος in [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [3rd c.BC: Callimachus Epicus “Aetia” 3.1.43.]]

__2
wedding, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Tyrannus” 422, 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Ion” 1475 (Lyric poetry): _plural_, 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Antigone” 813 (Lyric poetry), 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Iphigenia Aulidensis” 123 (Lyric poetry), 1st c.BC: Philodemus Gadarensis Epigrammaticus “Mus.” p.68K.]]

__II
={Ὑμήν}, Hymen, the god of marriage, addressed in wedding-songs, frequently in Trag. and Comedy texts (Lyric poetry), Ὑμὴν ὦ Υμέναι᾽ ἄναζ [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Troades” 314]]; Ὑμὴν ὦ Ὑμέναι᾽ Ὑμήν[Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. work] 331; Ὑμὴν Ὑμέναι᾽ ὦ 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Pax” 1335; Ὑμὴν ὦ, Ὑμέναι᾽ ὦ [prev. author] “Av.” 1736, 1742]]; Doric dialect Ὑμὰν ὦ Ὑμέναιε [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [3rd c.BC: Theocritus Poeta Bucolicus 18.58]]; hence the two are used as one word, ὑμὴν ὑμέναιον ἀείδων [Refs 3rd c.AD+ [3rd c.AD: Oppianus Apamensis Epicus “Cynegetica” 1.341.]]

__1. Emphatic (so always in nom. exc. when preceded by the art., see infr., iii);
__(1) self (ipse), expressing opposition, distinction, exclusion, etc., αὐ. ἐκχυθήσεται, Luk.5:37; αὐ. ἐγινώσκεν, Jhn.2:25; αὐ.ὑμεῖς, Jhn.3:28; καὶ αὐ. ἐγώ, Rom.15:14; αὐ. Ἰησοῦς, Jhn.2:24; αὐ. καὶ οἱ μετ᾽ αὐτοῦ, Mrk.2:25; ὑμεῖς αὐ., Mrk.6:31; esp. (as freq in cl.) αὐ. ὁ, Mat.3:4, Mrk.6:17, Jhn.16:27, 1Th.3:11, al.; in late Gk., sometimes weakened, ἐν αὐτῇ τ. ὥρᾳ, in that hour, Luk.10:21 (M, Pr., 91; MM, see word);
__(2) emphatic, he, she, it (M, Pr., 86; Bl., §48, 1, 2, 7), Mat.1:21, 12:50, Luk.6:35, al.; pointing to some one as master (cl.), Mat.8:24, Mrk.4:38, al.; αὐ., καὶ αὐ. = οὗτος, ὁ δε (BL, §48, 1), Mat.14:2, Mrk.14:15, 44, Luk.1:22, 2:28, al.
__2. In oblique cases (cl.), for the simple pron. of 3rd of person(s), he, she, it, Mat.7:9, 10:12, 26:44, al.; with ptcp. in genitive absol., Mat.9:18, Mrk.13:1, al. (for irreg. constructions, V. Bl., §74, 5); pleonastically after the relative (cf. Heb. אֲשֶׁר לוֹ; WM, 184ff.; Bl., §50, 4; MM, see word), Mrk.7:25, Rev.3:8, 7:2, al.; in constr. ad sensum, without proper subject expressly indicated, Mat.4:23, Act.8:5, 2Co.2:13, al.; genitive αὐτοῦ = ἐκείνου, Rom.11:11, 1Th.2:19, Tit.3:5, Heb.2:4.
__3. ὁ, ἡ, τὸ αὐ., the same: Heb.1:12, 13:8; τὸ αὐ., ποιεῖν, Mat.5:46, 47, al.; φρονεῖν, Rom.12:16, 15:5, Php.2:2, al.; τὰ αὐ., Act.15:27, Rom.2:1, al.; κατὰ τὸ (τὰ) αὐ. (MM, see word), Act.14:1, Luk.6:23, al.; ἐπὶ τὸ αὐ., together (MM, see word), Mat.22:34, Act.1:15, al.; ἓν κ. τὸ αὐ., 1Co.11:5, 12:11; with dative (cl.), 1Co.11:5; with a noun, λόγος, Mrk.14:39; μέτρος, Php.1:30; πνεῦμα, 1Co.12:4.

in 8th c.BC: Homerus Epicus]], Lesbian Lyric poetry, and Ionic dialect Lyric poetry and Prose τοι is always enclitic, σοί never enclitic (τοί and σοι are not found except σοι [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 3.359, 11.381, ς (οι) 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 1.170]], and in codices of [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “P.” 4.270, 9.55]]; rarer than τοι in [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus, 3.69, +others)]]; in Attic dialect both σοί and σοι (enclitic) are used (σοί [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Nubes” 361, etc., σοι [prev. work] 87, etc.)]], τοί and τοι are not used; σοι is never elided except in [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 1.170, τοι is elided in 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 1.60, 347, 7th-6th c.BC: Alcaeus Lyricus 55, [prev. author] “Oxy.” 1788 “fragment” 15 ii 9, 7th-6th c.BC: Sappho Lyrica 28.2]]; Epic dialect and Lyric poetry also τεΐν, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 11.201, 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 4.619, epigram cited in 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 5.60, 61, 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Aves” 930]]; also τίν [ῐ], [Refs 7th c.BC+ [7th c.BC: Alcman Lyricus 16, 5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “P.” 1.29, 8.68 (uncertain reading)]]; τίν [ῑ], [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [[prev. author] “I.” 6(5).4, 3rd c.BC: Theocritus Poeta Bucolicus 2.20 (τίν]] before a consonant, [Refs 7th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “O.” 10(11).93); also τεΐ 7th c.BC: Alcman Lyricus 53; τίνη 3rd c.BC: Rhinthon Comicus 13.]]—Acc. σέ, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 6.256, +others]]; enclitic σε,[Refs 7th c.BC+ [1.26, 7th-6th c.BC: Sappho Lyrica 1.2, “Supp.” 23.9, 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 3.42, etc.]]; in late Gr. σέν, [Refs [“Anatolian Studies” p.76]]; Doric dialect τέ [Refs 7th c.BC+ [7th c.BC: Alcman Lyricus 52, 5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “O.” 1.48, 3rd c.BC: Theocritus Poeta Bucolicus 1.5, 3rd c.BC: Callimachus Epicus “Fragmenta” 114]]; τ᾽ variant (codex R) in [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Acharnenses” 779 (on the accent see 2nd c.AD: Apollonius Dyscolus Grammaticus “de Pronominibus;” 54.14, 83.4)]]; τρέ (to be read τϝέ) [Refs 5th c.AD+ [5th c.AD(?): Hesychius Legal icographus]]; or (enclitic) τυ [Refs 6th c.BC+ [“IG” 42(1).121.69 (Epid., 4th c.BC), 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Equites” 1225, “Ach.” 730 (uncertain in “Ach.” 779), 3rd c.BC: Theocritus Poeta Bucolicus 1.56, 78, etc.:—also τίν 6th c.BC: Corinna Lyrica 4, 3rd c.BC: Cercidas Iambographus 7.6, 3rd c.BC: Theocritus Poeta Bucolicus 11.39, 55, 68.]]

__2
in combination with γε, σύ γε, σέ γε, etc. (compare ἔγωγε), thou at least, for thy part, frequently in [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Homerus Epicus]] and Attic dialect; Doric dialect τύγε [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Epicharmus Comicus [272], 5th c.BC: Timocreon Lyricus 1 (variant{τύ γα}); τύγᾰ 3rd c.BC: Theocritus Poeta Bucolicus 5.69, 71]]; Boeotian dialect τούγα [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd c.AD: Apollonius Dyscolus Grammaticus “de Pronominibus;” 55.6]]: dative σοί γε [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 1.557]]: accusative σέ γε [Refs [10.96]], etc.:—also σύ περ [Refs [24.398.]]

__3
σύ with infinitive (as imperative), [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 3.134, 4.163.]]

__II
Dual nominative and accusative σφῶϊ, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 1.336, 4.286, +others]], you two, both of you; σφώ (not σφῴ,[Refs 8th c.BC+ [compare 2nd c.AD: Apollonius Dyscolus Grammaticus “de Pronominibus;” 85.17), 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 1.574, 11.782, 13.47, 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Coloneus” 344, 1543, etc.]]—Gen. and Dat. σφῶϊν, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 4.341, +others]]; contraction σφῷν once in [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Homerus Epicus, 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 4.62, and always in _Attic dialect_ (Hdn.Gr. 1.475) and Trag., e.g. 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Prometheus Vinctus” 12, 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Coloneus” 342, “OT” 1495, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Leges” 892e (codices 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus have σφῶϊν in “Tht.” 193c, +others, σφῶν “Euthd.” 273e, +others)]]. None of these forms are enclitic, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [2nd c.AD: Apollonius Dyscolus Grammaticus “de Pronominibus;” 38.9, 85.12; codex A of 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Leges” 658c, 673e, 689a wrongly makes σφῳν]] enclitic; Ζεὺς σφὼ is prescribed in [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 15.146 by Hdn.Gr. 2.93.]] —σφῶϊ is never dative; in [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 4.286]] it is the accusative depending on κελεύ; σφῶϊν is never accusative; in [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 23.52 it is dative commodi.]]

__III
Plur. nominative ὑμεῖς, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 2.75, +others (before a vowel, 4.246, 7.194, +others), 6th c.BC: Pherecydes Syrius Philosophus 11, 3rd c.AD: Democritus Epigrammaticus 29a, 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 3.72, etc.]], ye, you; Aeolic dialect and Epic dialect ὔμμες [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 1.274, +others, 7th-6th c.BC: Sappho Lyrica 24, 25]]; Doric dialect ὑμές [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophron Comicus 60, 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Acharnenses” 760, 761, 862; ὑμέν “SIG” 685.118 (Crete, 2nd c.BC), “GDI” 5155.6 ([prev. passage], 2nd c.BC)]]; Boeotian dialect οὐμές [Refs 6th c.BC+ [6th c.BC: Corinna Lyrica 6]]; a resolved form ὑμέες, [Refs 1st c.BC+ [1st c.BC: Parthenius Mythographus “fragment” 14, is a poeticlicence (so 2nd c.AD: Apollonius Dyscolus Grammaticus “de Pronominibus;” 93.3)]] rather than genuine Ionic [Refs 5th c.BC+ [(variant in 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 8.22).]]— Gen. ὑμῶν, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Acharnenses” 143, etc.]]; ὑμέων (disyllable) [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 7.159, 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 13.7, +others, 7th c.BC: Archilochus Lyricus 74.6 (ὑμῶν codices), 6th c.BC: Solon Lyricus 11.5 (variant{ὑμῶν})]]; ὑμέων also [Refs 8th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 3.73, 6.130, +others; as _trisyllable_, 3rd c.BC: Herodas Mimographus 2.27; ὑμείων 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 4.348, 7.195, +others]]; Doric dialect ὑμέων [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophron Comicus 46]]; also ὑμῶν, [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd c.AD: Apollonius Dyscolus Grammaticus “de Pronominibus;” 95.23]]; Aeolic dialect ὑμμέων [Refs 7th c.BC+ [7th-6th c.BC: Alcaeus Lyricus 96]]; Boeotian dialect οὐμίων [Refs 6th c.BC+ [6th c.BC: Corinna Lyrica 22.]]—Dat. ὑμῖν, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 2.46, 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.126, etc.]]; Ionic dialect enclitic ὗμῐν [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd c.AD: Apollonius Dyscolus Grammaticus “de Pronominibus;” 97.28,]] also Doric dialect, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophron Comicus 91]]; Doric dialect (not enclitic) ὑμίν [ῐ] [Refs [[prev. author] 92]]; ὑμίν [ῐ] also in [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Ajax” 864, 1242, “OT” 991, 1402, “Ant.” 308, “El.” 804, +others (but ὗμιν]] should perhaps be restored where the sense needs an enclitic on the principle stated by [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd c.AD: Apollonius Dyscolus Grammaticus “de Pronominibus;” 35.6, 36.5, “Synt.” 130.23)]]; ὕμιν[Refs 8th c.BC+ [(as _enclitic_) is prescribed by Hdn.Gr. (2.124) in 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 24.33, by “Etymologicum Magnum” 432.34 in 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 1.376, 2.141, etc.:—_Aeolic dialect_ and _Epic dialect_ ὔμμῐ, ὔμμῐν, 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 2.316, 11.336, +others, 8th-7th c.BC: Hesiodus Epicus “Scutum Herculis” 328, 7th-6th c.BC: Sappho Lyrica 14, 7th-6th c.BC: Alcaeus Lyricus “Supp.” 26.9, 5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “O.” 11(10).17.]]—Acc. ὑμᾶς, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Acharnenses” 325]], etc. (-υ [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.AD: Orphica “Argonautica” 820, variant in 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Philoctetes” 222]]; ὗμας or (more probably) ὕμας is required by the metre in [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd c.AD: Babrius Fabularum Scriptor 9.9, 47.11)]]; Ionic dialect ὑμέας (disyllable) [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 21.198, +others]]; enclitic ὕμεας (disyllable) [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [3rd c.BC: Herodas Mimographus 2.60 (Papyrus)]]; ὑμέας also [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.126, +others]]; Aeolic dialect and Epic dialect ὔμμε [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 23.412, +others, 5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “I.” 6(5).19; also in 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Eumenides” 620 (trimeter), and 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Antigone” 846 (Lyric poetry)]]; Doric dialect ὑμέ [Refs 7th c.BC+ [7th c.BC: Alcman Lyricus 3, 5th c.BC: Sophron Comicus 52, 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Acharnenses” 737, “Lys.” 1076, “SIG” 528.3 (Cretan dialogue, 3rd c.BC), 622 B 8 (Cretan, 2nd c.BC).]]—The plural is sometimes used in addressing one person, when others are included in the speaker's thought, as [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 12.81, 7th c.BC: Archilochus Lyricus 89. (With σύ]] cf. Latin tu, Gothic pu; with τοι Sanskrit genitive and dative te; the origin of σφῶϊ is doubtful; with ὑμεῖς cf. Sanskrit accusative plural yusmān.)

Abbott-Smith / STEPBible (TBESG)
ὑμνέω, -ῶ
(ὕμνος) [in LXX for הָלַל pi., שִׁיר, יָדָה hi., etc. ;]
__1. trans., with accusative of person(s) (in cl. also with accusative of thing(s)), to sing to, laud, sing to the praise of: Act.16:25, Heb.2:12.
__2. Intrans., to sing: in LXX and NT, of singing hymns and praises to God (Psa.65:13, al.), Mat.26:30, Mrk.14:26 (see Swete, in l).†
(AS)

---

LSJ / STEPBible (TFLSJ)
ὑμν-έω,
Epic dialect ὑμνείω [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th-7th c.BC: Hesiodus Epicus “Opera et Dies” 2]]; Epic dialect 3rd.pers. plural ὑμνεῦσιν [Refs [“hymnus ad Apollinem” 190]]; feminine participle ὑμνεῦσα [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th-7th c.BC: Hesiodus Epicus “Theogonia” 11]]; Aeolic dialect infinitive ὔμνην to be restored for ὑμνεῖν in [Refs 7th c.BC+ [7th-6th c.BC: Alcaeus Lyricus 5.2]]; Laconian dialect 1st pers. plural subjunctive ὑμνίωμες [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Lysistrata” 1305 (Lyric poetry)]]: Aeolic dialect 3rd.pers. plural imperfect ὔμνην [Refs 7th c.BC+ [7th-6th c.BC: Sappho Lyrica “Papyrus fragments” in E. Diehl, 20c. 6]]: future ὑμνήσω [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “Parth.” 2.11]]: (ὕμνος):

__I
with accusative of person or thing sung of, sing of, first in [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th-7th c.BC: Hesiodus Epicus “Theogonia” 11, 33]], frequently in Hymni Homerici (Hymnus ad Apollinem[Refs 7th c.BC+ [178, +others), Lyric poetry (7th-6th c.BC: Sappho Lyrica [same place], 7th-6th c.BC: Alcaeus Lyricus [same place], 5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “N.” 10.2, +others, 5th c.BC: Bacchylides Lyricus 10.13, +others), and Trag. (5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Iphigenia Taurica” 367, etc.; θρήνοις.. σ᾽ ὑμνήσομεν [prev. author] “Rh.” 976)]]: also in Prose, celebrate in a hymn, commemorate, Ὦπιν [NT+5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 4.35; τὰς τούτων ἀρετάς 5th c.BC: Lysias Orator 2.2, compare 5th c.BC: Bacchylides Lyricus 5.33; [Παλαμήδη] ὑμνοῦσιν ὡς.. ἀπόλλυται 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Memorabilia” 4.2.33, etc.; τὸν θεόν NT.Act.16.25]]; of the hymn itself, οὔτε.. μέ τις ὕμνος ὕμνησεν [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Antigone” 815 (Lyric poetry): with double _accusative_, ἃ τὴν πόλιν ὕμνησα]] the points wherein I praised our city, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 2.42]]:—passive, to be celebrated in hymns, of gods, [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [“OGI” 56.66 (Canopus, 3rd c.BC), 2nd c.AD: Pausanias Periegeta 9.23.3, etc.]]; also Ἀργεῖοι.. τὰ πολλὰ πάντα ὑμνέαται (Ionic dialect for -ηνται) are everywhere praised, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 5.67; ὑμνηθήσεται πόλις 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Ion” 1590; ἡ ὑμνουμένη χρυσῆ πλάτανος]]famous, [LXX+5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Historia Graeca (Hellenica)” 7.1.38; αἱ ὑμνούμεναι φιλίαι 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Ethica Nicomachea” 1171a15; σοφία ἐν ἐξόδοις ὑμνεῖται LXX.Pro.1.20: _impersonal_, ὑμνεῖτο δ᾽ αἰσχρῶς]] foul songs were sung, [Refs [Comica Adespota 1203.5.]]

__I.2
descant upon, in song or speech, ἐν κατηρεφεῖ στέγῃ.. ὑμνήσεις κακά [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Electra” 382]]; τὰν ἐμὰν ὑμνεῦσαι (Doric dialect for -οῦσαι) ἀπιστοσύναν ever singing of my want of faith, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Medea” 423 (Lyric poetry)]]:— passive, Ἐτεοκλέης ἂν.. ὑμνοῖτο.. φροιμίοις πολυρρόθοις [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Septem contra Thebas” 7.]]

__I.3
with accusative cognate, sing, ᾆσμα, ὕμνον, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [1st c.AD(?): Heraclitus 15, 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Agamemnon” 1191: with double _accusative_, παιᾶνα.. ὑμνοῦσι.. τὸν Αατοῦς γόνον 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Hercules Furens” 688 (Lyric poetry), compare “SIG” 711 L 12 (Delph., 2nd c.BC).]]

__II
tell over and over again, harp upon, repeat, recite, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Protagoras” 317a, “R.” 549e, “Tht.” 174e, etc.]]; ὡς.. [Refs [[prev. author] “R.” 364a; ὑμνοῦσι τὸ γῆρας ὅσων κακῶν αἴτιόν [ἐστι] [prev. work] 329b]]; τὸν νόμον ὑμνεῖν recite the form of the law, [Refs [[prev. author] “Lg.” 871a:]] —passive, ὁ δ᾽ εἶπε πρός με βαί᾽, ἀεὶ δ᾽ ὑμνούμενα ([Refs 5th c.BC+ [Scholia τὰ πολυθρύλητα) 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Ajax” 292.]]

__III
intransitive, sing, chant, ὡς ποιηταὶ ὑμνήκασι περὶ αὐτῶν [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 1.21]]; ὑμνῶν οὔποτ᾽ ἔληγεν ὡς.. [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Agesilaus” 11.2.]]

__III.2
in passive sense, φῆμαι.. ὑμνήσουσι περὶ τὰ ὦτα will ring in their ears, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 463d. [On the quantity, see at {ὕμνος}.]]]

Abbott-Smith / STEPBible (TBESG)
ὕμνος, -ου, ὁ
[in LXX for תְּהִלָּה, נְגִינָה, שִׁיר, etc. ;]
a hymn;
__(a) in cl. a festal song in praise of gods or heroes;
__(b) in LXX and NT a song of praise addressed to God: Eph.5:19, Col.3:16.†
SYN.: ψαλμός, that which is sung to a musical accompaniment; ᾠδή, the generic term for song (cf. Tr., Syn., § LXXviii, Lft. on Col.3:16)  (AS)

---

LSJ / STEPBible (TFLSJ)
ὕμνος, ὁ,
hymn, ode, in praise of gods or heroes (καί τι ἦν εἶδος ῳδῆς εὐχαὶ πρὸς θεούς, ὄνομα δὲ ὕμνοι ἐπεκαλοῦντο [Refs 8th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Leges” 700b; ὕμνους θεοῖς καὶ ἐγκώμια τοῖς ἀγαθοῖς [prev. author] “R.” 607a, compare 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Poetica” 1448b27), once in 8th c.BC: Homerus Epicus, ἀοιδῆς ὕμνος 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 8.429 (followed by Demodocus' song of the Wooden Horse, 499ff)]]; ὕμνῳ νικήσαντα φέρειν τρίποδ᾽ [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th-7th c.BC: Hesiodus Epicus “Opera et Dies” 657; ἀνδρῶν τε παλαιῶν ἠδὲ γυναικῶν ὕμνον ἀείδουσιν “hymnus ad Apollinem” 161; frequently in 5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus, ὕμνος πολύφατος, ἐπικώμιος, etc., “O.” 1.8, “N.” 8.50, +others; Θήρωνος Ὀλυμπιονίκαν ὕμνον “O.” 3.3; and in 5th c.BC: Bacchylides Lyricus, ὑφάνας ὕμνον 5.10, compare 6.11, +others]]; ὕμνοι θεῶν to or in honour of the gods, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Leges” 801d; τιμῶν θεὰν ὕμνοισιν 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Hippolytus” 56; τοὺς χοροὺς.. καὶ τοὺς ὕ. τῷ θεῷ ποιεῖτε 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 21.51, compare 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Symposium” 177a]]; ὕμνοι Δαυείδ psalms of [NT+6th c.AD+ [6th c.AD: David Philosophus, LXX.2Ch.7.6; ψαλμοὶ καὶ ὕ. καὶ ᾠδαί NT.Eph.5.19]]: in Trag. also of mournful songs, addressed to gods or heroes, τὸν δυσκέλαδον ὕ. Ἐρινύος [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Septem contra Thebas” 868 (Lyric poetry), compare “Pers.” 620, 625 (_anapaest meter_), “Ch.” 475 (Lyric poetry); ὕ. ἐξ Ἐρινύων, δέσμιος φρενῶν, ἀφόρμικτος [prev. author] “Eu.” 331 (Lyric poetry), compare 306; ἐν ἀλύροις κλέοντες ὕμνοις 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Alcestis” 447 (Lyric poetry)]]; ὕ. Ἅιδου, of one whose songs are death, [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd c.AD: Phrynichus Atticista Comedy texts 69 (Lyric poetry).]] —On ὕμνοι of various kinds see Men.Rh.p.333 [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus; ὁ κυρίως ὕ. πρὸς κιθάραν ᾔδετο ἑστώτων 5th c.AD: Proclus Philosophus “Chr.” cited in 9th c.AD: Photius Legal icographus, etc. “Bibliotheca - Patrologia Graeca” p.320 5th c.BC: Bacchylides Lyricus, compare 1st c.BC: Didymus Grammaticus cited in “Etymologicum Magnum” 777.9]]. ὑπ-άγω
[in LXX: Exo.14:21 (הָלַךְ hi.), elsewhere only as seel., Tob.8:21, al. ;]
a word of the vulgar language, in Pres. and imperfect only (Bl., § 53, 1).
__I. Trans.
__1. to lead or bring under, subdue (Hom., Hdt., al.; Ex, l.with).
__2. to lead on slowly (Hdt., Xen., al.).
__II. Intrans., to go slowly away, withdraw oneself, depart (so less frequently in cl.; Thuc., Eur., al.): absol., Mat.8:32 13:44, Mrk.6:33, Luk.8:42 17:14, Jhn.6:67 8:2 11:44 14:5, 28 18:8; οἱ ἐρχόμενοι κ. οἱ ὑπάγοντες, Mrk.6:31; ὑπῆγον κ. ἐπίστευον, Jhn.12:11; ἵνα ὑπαγῆτε κ. καρπὸν ψέρητε, Jhn.15:16; opposite to ἔρχεσθαι, Jhn.3:8 8:14; imperat., ὕπαγε, Mat.4:10 8:13 20:14, Mrk.2:9 T, Mrk.7:29 10:52; εἰς εἰρήνην (ἐν εἰ.), Mrk.5:34, Jas.2:16; id. prefixed to another imperat. (Bl., § 79, 4), Mat.5:34 8:4 18:15 19:21 21:28 27:65 28:10, Mrk.1:44 10:21 16:7, Jhn.4:16 9:7, Rev.10:8; with καί inserted, Rev.16:1; euphemistically, of death, Mat.26:24, Mrk.14:21; with adv.: ποῦ (which see), Jhn.12:35 14:5 16:5, 1Jn.2:11; ὅπου (which see), Jhn.8:21-22 13:33, 36 14:4 Rev.14:4; ἐκεῖ, Jhn.11:8; with prep.: πρός, Jhn.7:33 13:3 16:5, 10 16:17; εἰς, Mat.9:6 20:4, 7, Mrk.2:11 11:2 14:13, Luk.19:30, Jhn.6:21 7:3 9:11 11:31, Rev.13:10 17:8, 11; εἰς . . . πρός, Mat.26:18, Mrk.5:19; ἐπί, Luk.12:58; μετά, Mat.5:41; ὀπίσω, Mat.16:23, Mrk.8:33; with inf., Jhn.21:3.†

subject, τὴν ἀρχομένην [διάθεσιν] τοῖς βοηθήμασιν [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd c.AD: Soranus Medicus 2.38]]:—passive, τῶν -ομένων τῇ διαίτῃ παθῶν [Refs [[prev. author] 1.2.]]

__II
bring a person before the judgement-seat (the ὑπό refers to his being set under or below the judge), ὑ. τινὰ ὑπὸ δικαστήριον bring one before a court, i.e. accuse, impeach him, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 9.93, compare 6.72 (_passive_)]]; ὑ. τινὰ ὑπὸ τοὺς ἐφόρους[Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. work] 82; οἱ -όμενοι εἰς ὑμᾶς 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Historia Graeca (Hellenica)” 2.3.28; ὑ. τινὰ ἐς δίκην 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 3.70; simply, ὑ. τινὰ ὡς ἐπιβουλεύοντα 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Historia Graeca (Hellenica)” 2.3.33; ὑ. τινὰ θανάτου on a capital charge, [prev. work] 2.3.12, 5.4.24]]; θανάτου ὑπὸ τὸν δῆμον Μιλτιάδεα impeached him before the commons on a capital charge, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 6.136: with _dative_, ὑ. τινὰς δικαστηρίοις 2nd c.AD: Lucianus Sophista “Fug.” 11]]:—middle, τάνδ᾽ ὑπάγεται Δίκα [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Electra” 1155 (Lyric poetry, uncertain reading, δίκαν codices)]]:—passive, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [1st c.BC: Philodemus Gadarensis Epigrammaticus “Rh.” 2.140 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus: with _dative_, τοῖς τῆς.. πεπρωμένης.. νόμοις ὑπαχθέντα “IG” 12(7).240.24 (Amorgos, 3rd c.AD)]]; ὁ πένης ὑπάγεται τῷ νόμῳ [Refs 4th c.AD+ [4th c.AD: Libanius Sophista “Declamationes” 36 at Title Page]]

__III
lead on by degrees, τὰς κύνας [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Cynegeticus” 5.15, compare 10.4]]; draw or lead on by art or deceit, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 9.94; τινὰ ἐπὶ κῶμον 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Cyclops” 507 (Lyric poetry)]]; ὑ. τοὺς πολεμίους εἰς δυσχωρίαν draw them on by pretended flight, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 1.6.37]]; ὑ. τοὺς πολεμίους ὑποφεύγοντες[Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. work] 3.2.8; τὸν ἐρῶντα τῷ ἐρωμένῳ ἀκολουθεῖν.., ὅπῃ ἂν ἐκεῖνος ὑπάγῃ 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Euthyphro” 14c; τίν᾽ ὑπάγεις μ᾽ ἐς ἐλπίδ; 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Helena” 826; ὁ θεὸς ὑπῆγεν αὐτόν, ἵνα ἀφικόμενος.. δοίη δίκην 5th c.BC: Lysias Orator 6.19]]; ἡ πέρδιξ.. ἀπὸ τῶν ῳῶν ὑπάγει (i.e. ἄνθρωπον) [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Historia Animalium” 613b32: with]]infinitive, σ᾽ ὑπήγαγον εἰς χεῖρας ἐλθεῖν so as to come, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Andromache” 428]]:—middle, lead on for one's own advantage, but frequently much like the active, lead on, ἐλπίσιν ὑπαγαγέσθαι τινά [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Isocrates Orator 5.91, compare 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 2.4.3]]; ὑ. Θετταλοὺς εἰς δουλείαν reduce them, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 8.62]]; ὑ. τινὰς ἐς μάχην, ἐς φιλίαν, [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd-3rd c.AD: Dio Cassius Historicus 36.4, 42.39; ἐς φόρου συντέλειαν 2nd c.AD: Herodianus Grammaticus 6.2.1]]; give one a lead in speech, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Andromache” 906, compare 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 2.1.18]]:—passive, κατὰ μικρὸν ὑπαχθείς [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Isocrates Orator 5.1; [ἐλπίσικαὶ θενακισμοῖς] ὑπαχθέντες 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 5.10 (variant{ἐπ-}]] (; ὑπὸ τῆς ἀπάτης καὶ τῶν ἀλαζονευμάτων [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aeschines Orator 1.178, etc.; εἰς ἔχθραν ὑπηγμένος ὑπότινος 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 18.188; ἐκλοιδορίας εἰς πληγάς [prev. author] 54.19. (In this sense, ἐπάγω is frequently variant)]]

__IV
take away from beneath, withdraw, τινὰ ἐκ βελέων [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 11.163; ὕπαγε τὰς ἀκροβελίδας 5th-6th c.BC: Archippus Comicus 10]]:—passive, ὑπαγομένου κάτωθεν τοῦ χώματος [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 2.76.]]

__IV.2
draw off, τὸ στράτευμα [[prev. author] 4.127; ὑπήγαγεν Κύριος τὴν θάλατταν LXX.Exo.14.21.]

__IV.3
carry off below, ὑ. τὴν κοιλίην purge the bowels, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Hippocrates Medicus “περὶ νούσων” 3.17, 2nd c.AD: Aretaeus Medicus “ὀξέων νούσων θεραπευτικόν” 1.10; ὑ. τὴν γαστέρα 2nd c.AD: Phrynichus Atticista 279, 2nd c.AD: Galenus Medicus 6.353, +others]]; see below [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Bacchylides Lyricus 111.]]

__IV.4
bring down a bandage, [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd c.AD: Soranus Medicus “de fasciis - Opera Hippocratis et Galeni” 2]]: with dative, bring under, τῷ κοίλῳ τοῦ ποδός [Refs [[prev. work] 59.]]

__B
intransitive, go away, withdraw, retire, ὑπάγω φρένα τέρψας [Refs 6th c.BC+ [6th c.BC: Theognis Elegiacus 921, compare 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Aves” 1017, “Anthologia Graeca” 9.341 (Glaucus Atheniensis Epigrammaticus)]]; of an army, draw off or retire slowly, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 4.120, 122, 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 4.126]]; of the lion, ὑπάγει βάδην [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Historia Animalium” 629b17]]; ἂν φυτεύῃ καὶ ὑπάγῃ if he.. goes away, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [Inscriptiones Graecae 12(7).62.54 (Amorgos, 4th c.BC)]]; ὑπάγει αὔριον he is going (= leaving, setting out) to-morrow, [Refs 1st c.AD+ [“POxy.” 1291.11 (1st c.AD)]]; ὑπάγοντι εἰς Ἑρμοῦ πόλιν [Refs 1st c.AD+ [“PLond.” 1.131.155, 218, +others (1st c.AD).]]

__B.II
go forwards, draw on, ὕπαγ᾽ ὦ, ὕπαγ᾽ ὦ on with you! [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Cyclops” 52 (Lyric poetry); ὕπαγε, τί μέλλει; 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Nubes” 1298; ὑπάγεθ᾽ ὑμεῖς τῆς ὁδοῦ [prev. author] “Ra.” 174; ὑ. εἰς τοὔμπροσθεν 5th c.BC: Eupolis Comicus 79]]: also of an army, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 3.4.48, 4.2.16.]]

__B.II.2
later, in present, simply go, opposed to ἔρχομαι 'come', ὕπαγε Σατανᾶ [NT.Matt.4.10]; ὕπαγε, δεῖξον.. [NT.Mark.1.44]; ἦσαν οἱ ἐρχόμενοι καὶ οἱ ὑπάγοντες πολλοί[NT+3rd c.AD+ [[prev. work] 6.31; ποῦ ὑπάγει; NT.John.16.5; ἐν πλοίῳ ὑπάγοντι ἰς Ταπόσιριν “Sammelb.” 7357.8 (3rd c.AD); ὕπαγε ἰς πάντα τόπον [prev. work] 7452.7, 19 (3rd c.AD)]]; καθ᾽ ἡμέρα[ν] ὑπάγω παρὰ Σεραπιάδα [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [“BGU” 38.17 (2nd-3rd c.AD)]]: the aorist is ἀπῆλθον, ὕπαγε.. καὶ ἀπῆλθε [NT.Matt.9.6:—αὐτόματα ὑπάγοντα] automata which go (from place to place), opposed to στατά (those which perform actions while standing still), [LXX+2nd c.BC+ [2nd-1st c.BC(?): Hero Mechanicus “Automatopoetica” 1.2:—rare in LXX]] (and only in codex א), [LXX.Tob.8.21, +others, LXX.Jer.43(36).19.]

__B.III
in Medicine texts, of the bowels, to be open, κοιλίη ὑπάγουσα [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Hippocrates Medicus “Acut.(Sp.”) 2, 2nd c.AD: Galenus Medicus 15.756]]; see above [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus IV. 3.]]

__B.IV
sink down, squat, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Historia Animalium” 540a7; compare ὑπαγωγή 111.2.]]

[in LXX: chiefly for שָׁמַע ;]

LSJ / STEPBible (TFLSJ)
ὑπᾰκού-ω,
future -ακούσομαι[LXX.Gen.41.40 (see. entry near the end);] later -ακούσω [Refs [“Mim.Oxy.” 413.222:]]

__I
hearken, give ear, θεοὶ δ᾽ ὑπὸ πάντες ἄκουον [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 8.4; ὁ δ᾽ ἄρ᾽ ἐμμαπέως ὑπάκουσε 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 14.485, compare “hymnus ad Venerem” 180: with _genitive_, ὄττις.. πλάσιον ἆδυ φωνείσας ὐπακούει 7th-6th c.BC: Sappho Lyrica 2.4; ὑμῶν 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Vespae” 318 (Lyric poetry); τῆς κρίσεως 4th c.BC: Aeschines Orator 3.56 (assuming variant).]]

__I.2
answer (by voice or act) when called, ἢ ἐξελθέμεναι ἢ ἔνδοθεν αἶψ᾽ ὑπακοῦσαι [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 4.283, compare 10.83, 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Alcestis” 400 (Lyric poetry), 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Vespae” 273 (Lyric poetry), 3rd c.BC: Theocritus Poeta Bucolicus 13.59: in Prose, ὁ κῆρυξ ἐκήρυττε τίς τὴν ἱκετηρίαν καταθείη, καὶ οὐδεὶς ὑπήκουεν 5th-6th c.BC: Andocides Orator 1.112; τῷ παιδίῳ 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Lysistrata” 878, compare “Nu.” 360 (_anapaest meter_), 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Agesilaus” 3.4, 4th c.BC: Aeschines Orator 1.49, 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 19.266.]]

__I.2.b
in a dialogue, answer when questioned, σοι [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Sophista” 217d; τοῖς λόγοις [prev. author] “Lg.” 898c.]]

__I.3
listen to, heed, regard, with genitive of things, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. author] “Tht.” 162d, 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 8.1.20; ὑ. νόμων 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Leges” 708d]]; ὑ. διαίτῃ submit to a regimen, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [[prev. author] “R.” 459c; λόγῳ 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Politica” 1333a18]]; ὑ. τῷ ξυμφόρῳ τινός comply with his interest, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 5.98]]; δείπνῳ ὑ. accept an invitation to dinner, [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd c.AD: Athenaeus Epigrammaticus 6.247d]]: absolutely, give way, submit, comply, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 3.148, 4.119, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Protagoras” 325a, “PCair.Zen.” 367.15 (3rd c.BC): with a _neuter_ _pronoun_, μάλα γε τοῦτο ὑπήκουσεν]] in this matter he obeyed, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 2.2.3; οὐδὲν τούτων ὑπήκουον 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 1.29, compare 139, 140, etc.]]; ὑ. τινός τι or τινί τι, obey one in a thing,[Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. work] 26, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Leges” 774b.]]

__II
Special senses:

__II.1
of porters, answer a knock at the door, ὑ. τινί [NT+4th c.BC+ [[prev. author] “Cri.” 43a: _absolutely_, [prev. author] “Phd.” 59e, NT.Act.12.13; [παρὰ] τὴν θύραν 4th-3rd c.BC: Theophrastus Philosophus “Characteres” 4.9, 28.3]]; ὁ ὑπακούσας the porter, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Symposium” 1.11, compare 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 47.35.]]

__II.2
of a judge, listen to a complainant, τινι [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 8.1.18]]; also of the parties in legal proceedings, appear before the court, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Isaeus Orator 4.28, 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 19.257,290; ὑ. εἰς τὸ δικαστήριον 4th c.BC: Hyperides Orator “pro Euxenippo” 2, compare “PSI” 10.1100.10 (2nd c.AD), “Sammelb.” 7369.10 (2nd-3rd c.AD).]]

__II.3
of dependants, subjects, etc., obey, submit to, Δαρείου οὐδαμὰ ὑ. [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 3.101; Ἀθηναίων 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 4.56, compare 6.82; τοῖς πέλας [prev. author] 2.61.]]

__II.3.b
Astrology texts, to aspect from South to North, of the southernmost of two zodiacal signs equidistant from an equinoctial point, opposed to προστάσσειν, [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd c.AD: Ptolemaeus Mathematicus “Tetrabiblos” 35]]; ={ἀκούω} see, [Refs 4th c.AD+ [4th c.AD: Paulus Alexandrinus Astrologus “E.” 2.]]

__II.4
answer one's expectations, succeed, ὑπήκουέ μοι τὸ πρᾶγμα [Refs 1st c.BC+ [2nd c.AD: Lucianus Sophista “Icar.” 10; τῆς μεταλλείας ἀσθενῶς ὑπακουούσης 1st c.BC-1st c.AD: Strabo Geographus 9.1.23.]]

__II.5
ὑ. αὐγαῖς ἁλίου to be subject to the sun's rays, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “O.” 3.24; ταῖς ὥραις 4th-3rd c.BC: Theophrastus Philosophus “de Causis Plantarum” 1.15.1; τοῦ ψύχους [prev. work] 5.4.2]]; ὑπακούουσι τῶν τῆς ἀρχῆς παθημάτων οἱ κατὰ τοὺς ὀφθαλμοὺς μύες feel the effects of.., [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd c.AD: Galenus Medicus 18(2).68.]]

__II.6
of ailments, yield, give way to a remedy, τινι [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Hippocrates Medicus “ἐπιδημίαι” 3.8, 2nd c.AD: Galenus Medicus 6.354: _absolutely_, 5th c.BC: Hippocrates Medicus “προρρητικόν” 2.39, 2nd c.AD: Soranus Medicus 1.122, 2nd c.AD: Galenus Medicus 6.439: _metaphorically_, τὸ μυθῶδες ὑ. λόγῳ 1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus “Theseus” 1; τοῖς ἰσχυρῶς φερομένοις ὑ. ὁ ἀήρ 4th c.BC: Archytas Tarentinus Philosophus 1]]; πληγαῖς ὑ., of metal, [Refs 1st c.AD+ [1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus 2.802b; ὑποχόνδριον ὑπακοῦον]]yielding to pressure, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Hippocrates Medicus “ἐπιδημίαι” 4.45; μὴ εὐθέως ὑπακούοντος εἰς ἐξολκὴν τοῦ ἐμβρύου 2nd c.AD: Soranus Medicus 2.62, compare 86.]]

__II.7
concede a point in dispute, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Topica” 161b15.]]

__II.8
correspond, πᾶσα παραγωγὴ ἐπιρρηματικὴ.. μιᾷ ὑπακούει πτώσει κατὰ τὴν διάλυσιν every adverbial derivative corresponds to a case, e.g. οἴκοθι to ἐν οἴκῳ, [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd c.AD: Apollonius Dyscolus Grammaticus “de Adverbiis;” 206.21]]; conform to a theory, [Refs [[prev. author] “Synt.” 236.14.]]

__III
κοινὸν ὑ. understand under the term κοινόν.., [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Philebus” 31c, compare 1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus 2.23c:]] —passive, κοινῶς ὑ. to be understood in a general sense, [Refs 1st c.BC+ [1st c.BC: Philodemus Philosophus “περὶ ποιημάτων” 5.35.]]

__III.2
in Grammars, understand a word omitted, [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd c.AD: Apollonius Dyscolus Grammaticus “de Syntaxi;” 22.21 (_passive_): τὸ -όμενον]] what one has in mind, the subject, [Refs [[prev. author] “Pron.” 68.15, +others]]

__III.3
understand, with accusative et infinitive, [Refs 1st c.BC+ [1st c.BC: Philodemus Gadarensis Epigrammaticus “Mus.” p.72 K., “Po.” 5.9.]]

__IV
future ὑπακούσεται in [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 6.69]], if correct, must be passive, if their service shall be lighter; but Scholia gives ὑπακούσονται, whence ξυγκαταστρεψάμενοι (for -οις) is conjectured.

LSJ / STEPBible (TFLSJ)
Included with:  ὑπάρχω,
future

__A
-ξω[Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 6.109, 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Antigone” 932 (_anapaest meter_):]]aorist ὑπῆρξα (see. below [Refs [1)]]:—passive, future ὑπαρχθήσομαι [Refs 3rd c.AD+ [“PTeb.” 418.7 (3rd c.AD):]]perfect ὕπηργμαι, Ionic dialect -αργμαι[Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 7.11]]:—begin, take the initiative:—Constr.:

__A.1
absolutely, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 24.286, 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Phoenissae” 1223; ὑπάρχων ἠδίκεις αὐτούς 5th-6th c.BC: Isocrates Orator 16.44]]; ὁ ὑπάρξας the beginner (in a quarrel), [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 59.15, compare 1; ἀμύνεσθαι τοὺς ὑπάρξαντας 5th c.BC: Lysias Orator 24.18; ἀμυνομένους, μὴ ὑπάρχοντας 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Gorgias” 456e; ὡς οὐχ ὑπάρχων ἀλλὰ τιμωρούμενος 4th-3rd c.BC: Menander Comicus 358]]:—middle, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Timaeus” 41c, 2nd-3rd c.AD: Aelianus “De Natura Animalium - Ar.Byzantine Epit.” 12.41, etc.]]

__A.2
with genitive, take the initiative in, begin, ἀδίκων ἔργων, ἀδικίης, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.5, 4.1, compare 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 2.74, etc.; ὑ. τῆς ἐλευθερίας τῇ Ἑλλάδι 5th-6th c.BC: Andocides Orator 1.142, compare 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Menexenus” 237b.]]

__A.3
with participle, take the initiative in doing, ἐμὲ ὑπῆρξαν ἄδικα ποιεῦντες [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 7.8.β, compare 6.133, 9.78]]; ὑπάρχει εὖ (or κακῶς) ποιῶν τινα [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 2.3.23, 5.5.9]]; τοῖς αὐτοῖς ἀμύνεσθαι οἷσπερ καὶ οἱ Λκεδαιμόνιοι ὑπῆρξαν retaliating by the means which the L. had used first, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 2.67 (where οἷσπερ is explained by the following ἀποκτείναντες and ἐσβαλόντες).]]

__A.3.b
in middle with infinitive, [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd-3rd c.AD: Aelianus “De Natura Animalium - Ar.Byzantine Epit.” 14.11: with _genitive_, βαδίσεως -ονται [prev. work] 4.34; ἡλίου -ομένου τῆς ἀκμῆς [prev. work] 1.20.]]

__A.4
with accusative, ὑ. εὐεργεσίας εἴς τινα or τινι take the initiative in [doing] kindnesses to one, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 19.280, 4th c.BC: Aeschines Orator 2.26]]; ὑ. τοῦτο (i.e. τὸ εὐνοεῖν) [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-3rd c.BC: Menander Comicus 927]]:—passive, ὑπηρεσίαι ὑπηργμέναι εἰς Φίλιππον αὑτῷ [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aeschines Orator 2.109; τὰ παρὰ τῶν θεῶν ὑπηργμένα 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 1.10]]; τὰ ἔκ τινος ὑπαργμένα (Ionic dialect for ὑπηργ-) [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 7.11; ὑπηργμένων πολλῶν κἀγαθῶν 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Lysistrata” 1159; οὐδέν μοι ὑπῆρκτο εἰς αὐτόν 5th c.BC: Antipho Orator 5.58; ἀνάξια τῶν εἰς ὑμᾶς ὑπηργμένων 5th c.BC: Lysias Orator 21.25]]; ἄξιον τῶν ὑ. equivalent to what was done for him, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Ethica Nicomachea” 1163b21: _impersonal_, ὑπῆρκτο αὐτοῦ (i.e. τοῦ Πειραιέως)]] a beginning of it had been made, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 1.93.]]

__B
in active only, to be the begining, παιδοβόροι μὲν πρῶτον ὑπῆρξαν μόχθοι τάλανες [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Choephori” 1068 (_anapaest meter_)]]; πολλῶν κακῶν, μεγάλων ἀχέων, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Phoenissae” 1582 (variant), “Andr.” 274 (Lyric poetry), compare “HF” 1169.]]

__B.2
to be already in existence, πημονῆς δ᾽ ἅλις γ᾽ ὑπάρχει [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Agamemnon” 1656 (troch.); φοίνισσα δὲ Θρηϊκίων ἀγέλα ταύρων ὑπᾶρχεν]]was already there, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “P.” 4.205]]; αὗται αἱ νέες τοῖσι Ἀθηναίοισι ὑπῆρχον already existed, opposed to to those they were about to build, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 7.144]]; εἰ τοίνυν σφι χώρη γε μηδεμία ὑπῆρχε if they had no country originally existing, [Refs [[prev. author] 2.15]]; χωρὶς δὲ τούτων οἱ χίλιοι ὑπῆρχον the original thousand existed, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 1.5.5; ἔδει πρῶτον μὲν ὑπάρχειν πάντων ἰσηγορίαν 5th c.BC: Eupolis Comicus 291 (Lyric poetry); ὑπαρχούσης μὲν τιμῆς, παρούσης δὲ δυνάμεως 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Agesilaus” 8.1; τοῦτο δεῖ προσεῖναι, τὰ δ᾽ ἄλλ᾽ ὑπάρχει 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 3.15, compare 8.53; ταὐτὰ ὑ. αὐτῷ ἅπερ ἐμοί 5th c.BC: Antipho Orator 5.60, compare 5th c.BC: Lysias Orator 12.23]]; ὑμῖν.. ἐλευθερίαν τε ὑπάρχειν καὶ Λακεδαιμονίων ξυμμάχοις κεκλῆσθαι there is in store for you.., [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 5.9: with _genitive_, οἶκος δ᾽ ὑ. τῶνδε.. ἔχειν]] there is store of these things for us to have, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Agamemnon” 961 (assuming variant, οἴκοις Pors.): frequently in]]participle, ἡ ὑπάρχουσα οὐσία the existing property, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Isocrates Orator 1.28; τὰ ὑ. ἁμαρτήματα 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 2.92]]; τῆς ὑ. τιμῆς for the current price, Syngr. cited in [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 35.12]]; οἱ ὑ. πολῖται the existing citizens, [Refs [[prev. author] 18.295]]; τῆς φύσεως ὑ. nature being what it is, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 6.4.4]]; also κρησφύγετόν τι ὑπάρχον εἶναι that there should be a refuge ready prepared, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 5.124.]]

__B.3
exist really, opposed to φαίνομαι, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “de Caelo” 297b22, “Metaphorical” 1046b10; ἀθεώρητοι τῶν ὑπαρχόντων [prev. author] “GC” 316a9; καταληπτικὴ φαντασία ἡ ἀπὸ τοῦ ὑπάρχοντος “Stoicorum Veterum Fragmenta” 2.25.]]

__B.4
simply, be, τοῖσιν ἄγουσιν κλαύμαθ᾽ ὑπάρξει [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Antigone” 932 (_anapaest meter_); ὅθεν εὐμάρει᾽ ὑπάρχοι πόρου [prev. author] “Ph.” 704 (Lyric poetry)]]: and with a predicate, θησαυρὸς ἄν σοι παῖς ὑπῆρχ᾽ οὑμός [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Hecuba” 1229; τὸ χωρίον καρτερὸν ὑ. 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 4.4]]; φύσεως ἀγαθῆς ὑπάρξαι to be of a good natural disposition, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Oeconomicus” 21.11; κἂν σοφὸς ὑπάρχῃ 4th-3rd c.BC: Philemo Comicus 102]]; μέγα ὑ. τοῖς τοιούτοις λόγοις ις of great advantage to them, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 3.19]]; πολλῶν ὑπάρξει κῦρος ἡμέρα καλῶν, ={κυρώσει πολλὰ καλά}, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Electra” 919.]]

__B.4.b
τὰ ὑπάρχοντα, much like{τὰ ὑπηργμένα} [Refs 4th c.BC+ [(4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus 4 _passive_)]], a man's record, ἀνάξιον τῶν ὑ. τῇ πόλει καὶ πεπραγμένων τοῖς προγόνοις [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 8.49]]; τὰ κάλλιστα τῶν ὑ. your past record, [Refs [[prev. author] 18.95]]; ἡ ὑπάρχουσα αἰσχύνη the disgrace which has been incurred, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [[prev. author] 19.217; τὰ ὑπάρχοντα [αὑτῷ] ἐγκλήματα 4th c.BC: Aeschines Orator 1.179.]]

__B.5
sometimes with a participle, much like{τυγχάνω, τοιαῦτα [αὐτῷ] ὑπῆρχε ἐὀντα} [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.192; ἐχθρὸς ὑ. ὤν 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 21.38; ὑ. δύναμιν κεκτημένοι [prev. author] 3.7, compare 15.1.]]

__B.6
προγόνων ὑ. τῶν ἐξ Ἰλίου to be the descendant of.., [Refs 1st c.BC+ [1st c.BC: Dionysius Halicarnassensis 2.65.]]

__B.II
like{ὑπόκειμαι} [Refs [II.2,]]to be laid down, to be taken for granted, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Symposium” 198d]]; τούτου ὑπάρχοντος, τούτων ὑπαρχόντων, this being granted, [Refs [[prev. author] “Ti.” 30c, 29b; θέντες ὡς ὑπάρχον [prev. author] “R.” 458a.]]

__B.III
belong to, fall to one, accrue, ὑπάρξει τοι.. τὰ ἐναντία you will have, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 6.109, etc.; τὸ μισεῖσθαι πᾶσιν ὑ. 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 2.64]]; τὴν ὑπάρχουσαν ἀπ᾽ ἀλλήλων ἀμφοτέροις [σωτηρίαν] [Refs [[prev. author] 6.86]]; ἡ ὑπάρχουσα φύσις your proper nature, its normal condition, [Refs [[prev. author] 2.45]]; τῇ τέχνῃ ὑπάρχειν διδούς assigning as a property of art, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Philebus” 58c, compare “Tht.” 150b, 150c.]]

__B.III.2
of persons, ὑ. τινί to be devoted to one, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 1.1.4, “HG” 7.5.5, 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 19.54, etc.]]; καθ᾽ ὑμῶν ὑπάρξων ἐκείνῳ he will be on his side against you, [Refs [[prev. work]118, compare 2.14.]]

__B.III.2.b
ἐν παντὶ.. πᾶς χωρίῳ, καὶ ᾧ μὴ ὑπάρχομεν every one in every place, even outside our sphere of influence (literal to which we do not belong), [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 6.87.]]

__B.III.3
in the Logic of [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus ὑπάρχειν]] denotes the subsistence of qualities in a subject, [Refs [“Metaphorical” 1025a14]]; ὑ. τινί, ={κατηγορεῖσθαί τινος}, [Refs [“APr.” 25a13, +others]]; ὑ. κατά τινος[Refs [[prev. work] 24a27, “Int.” 16b13]]; ἐπί τινος[Refs [[prev. work] 16a32; ὑ. τινὶ ζῴῳ πεζῷ δίποδι εἶναι “Top.” 109a14]]; ὑπάρξει τι [τῷ πρώτῳ] it will have predicates, [Refs 3rd c.AD+ [3rd c.AD: Plotinus Philosophus 5.6.2; ἡ γένεσις τῷ χρόνῳ.. ὑπάρχει 5th-6th c.AD: Damascius Philosophus “de Principiis” 142.]]

__B.IV
frequently in neuter plural participle, τὰ ὑπάρχοντα,

__B.IV.1
in signification [Refs [1,]]existing circumstances, presentadvantages, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [3rd c.AD: Democritus Epigrammaticus 191, 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 2.2; ἀπὸ τῶν αἰεὶ ὑ. σφαλέντες 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 4.18, compare 6.33]]; πρὸς τὰ ὑ.[Refs [[prev. work] 31; ἐκ τῶν ὑ.]]under the circumstances, according to one's means, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 6.4.9, 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Politica” 1288b33; ὡς ἐκ τῶν ὑ. 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 7.76, 8.1.]]

__B.IV.2
in signification [Refs [111,]]possessions, resources, [Refs [[prev. author] 1.70, 144, etc.]]; τὰ ἑκατέροις ὑ.[Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. work] 141; κινδυνεύειν περὶ τῶν ὑ. 5th-6th c.BC: Isocrates Orator 3.57]]: as a substantive, τὰ ὑ. αὐτοῦ [LXX+NT [NT.Matt.24.47, cf. LXX.Gen.12.5]]; ὑποθέμενος τὰ ὑ. καὶ ὑπάρξοντα present and future resources, [Refs 6th c.AD+ [POxy. 125.22 (6th c.AD), etc.]]

__B.IV.3

ὑπάρχω
[in LXX for הָיָה, יֵשׁ, לוּן, etc.; τ. ὑπάρχοντα for מִקְנֶה, רְכוּשׁ, etc. ;]
__1. to begin, make a beginning (Hom., Hdt., al.).
__2. to be in existence, be ready, be at hand (Hdt., Thuc., al.): Act.19:40 27:12, 21; before ἐν, Act.28:18.
__3. to be, prop, expressing continuance of an antecedent state or condition (cf. Gifford, Incarnation, 11 ff.; MM, xxv): with, nom, pred., Luk.8:41 9:48, Act.4:34 7:55 8:16 16:3 19:36 21:20, 1Co.7:26 12:22, Jas.2:15, 2Pe.3:11; ptcp. with pred., Luk.16:14 23:50, Act.2:30, 32 17:24 22:3, Rom.4:19, 1Co.2:15, 2Co.8:17 12:16, Gal.1:14 2:14; pl., Luk.11:13, Act.16:20, 37 17:29, 2Pe.2:19; before ἐν, with dative of thing(s), Luk.7:25 16:23, Act.5:4 10:12, 1Co.11:18, Php.3:20; ἐν μορφῇ θεοῦ ὑπάρχων (R, mg., being originally), Php.2:6; ἐν, with dative of person(s), (among), 1Co.11:18; μακρὰν ἀπό, Act.17:27; πρὸς τ. σωτηρίας, Act.27:34.
__4. to belong to (Thuc., Xen., al.): with dative of person(s), Act.3:6 4:37 28:7, 2Pe.1:8; τὰ ὑπάρχοντα, one's belongings, possessions: with dative of person(s), Luk.8:3 12:15, Act.4:32; with genitive of person(s), Mat.19:21 24:47 25:14, Luk.11:21 12:33, 44 14:33 16:1 19:8, 1Co.13:3, Heb.10:34 (cf. προ-υπάρχω).†

LSJ / STEPBible (TFLSJ)
ὑπάρχω,
future

__A
-ξω[Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 6.109, 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Antigone” 932 (_anapaest meter_):]]aorist ὑπῆρξα (see. below [Refs [1)]]:—passive, future ὑπαρχθήσομαι [Refs 3rd c.AD+ [“PTeb.” 418.7 (3rd c.AD):]]perfect ὕπηργμαι, Ionic dialect -αργμαι[Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 7.11]]:—begin, take the initiative:—Constr.:

__A.1
absolutely, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 24.286, 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Phoenissae” 1223; ὑπάρχων ἠδίκεις αὐτούς 5th-6th c.BC: Isocrates Orator 16.44]]; ὁ ὑπάρξας the beginner (in a quarrel), [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 59.15, compare 1; ἀμύνεσθαι τοὺς ὑπάρξαντας 5th c.BC: Lysias Orator 24.18; ἀμυνομένους, μὴ ὑπάρχοντας 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Gorgias” 456e; ὡς οὐχ ὑπάρχων ἀλλὰ τιμωρούμενος 4th-3rd c.BC: Menander Comicus 358]]:—middle, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Timaeus” 41c, 2nd-3rd c.AD: Aelianus “De Natura Animalium - Ar.Byzantine Epit.” 12.41, etc.]]

__A.2
with genitive, take the initiative in, begin, ἀδίκων ἔργων, ἀδικίης, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.5, 4.1, compare 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 2.74, etc.; ὑ. τῆς ἐλευθερίας τῇ Ἑλλάδι 5th-6th c.BC: Andocides Orator 1.142, compare 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Menexenus” 237b.]]

__A.3
with participle, take the initiative in doing, ἐμὲ ὑπῆρξαν ἄδικα ποιεῦντες [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 7.8.β, compare 6.133, 9.78]]; ὑπάρχει εὖ (or κακῶς) ποιῶν τινα [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 2.3.23, 5.5.9]]; τοῖς αὐτοῖς ἀμύνεσθαι οἷσπερ καὶ οἱ Λκεδαιμόνιοι ὑπῆρξαν retaliating by the means which the L. had used first, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 2.67 (where οἷσπερ is explained by the following ἀποκτείναντες and ἐσβαλόντες).]]

__A.3.b
in middle with infinitive, [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd-3rd c.AD: Aelianus “De Natura Animalium - Ar.Byzantine Epit.” 14.11: with _genitive_, βαδίσεως -ονται [prev. work] 4.34; ἡλίου -ομένου τῆς ἀκμῆς [prev. work] 1.20.]]

__A.4
with accusative, ὑ. εὐεργεσίας εἴς τινα or τινι take the initiative in [doing] kindnesses to one, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 19.280, 4th c.BC: Aeschines Orator 2.26]]; ὑ. τοῦτο (i.e. τὸ εὐνοεῖν) [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-3rd c.BC: Menander Comicus 927]]:—passive, ὑπηρεσίαι ὑπηργμέναι εἰς Φίλιππον αὑτῷ [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aeschines Orator 2.109; τὰ παρὰ τῶν θεῶν ὑπηργμένα 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 1.10]]; τὰ ἔκ τινος ὑπαργμένα (Ionic dialect for ὑπηργ-) [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 7.11; ὑπηργμένων πολλῶν κἀγαθῶν 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Lysistrata” 1159; οὐδέν μοι ὑπῆρκτο εἰς αὐτόν 5th c.BC: Antipho Orator 5.58; ἀνάξια τῶν εἰς ὑμᾶς ὑπηργμένων 5th c.BC: Lysias Orator 21.25]]; ἄξιον τῶν ὑ. equivalent to what was done for him, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Ethica Nicomachea” 1163b21: _impersonal_, ὑπῆρκτο αὐτοῦ (i.e. τοῦ Πειραιέως)]] a beginning of it had been made, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 1.93.]]

__B
in active only, to be the begining, παιδοβόροι μὲν πρῶτον ὑπῆρξαν μόχθοι τάλανες [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Choephori” 1068 (_anapaest meter_)]]; πολλῶν κακῶν, μεγάλων ἀχέων, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Phoenissae” 1582 (variant), “Andr.” 274 (Lyric poetry), compare “HF” 1169.]]

__B.2
to be already in existence, πημονῆς δ᾽ ἅλις γ᾽ ὑπάρχει [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Agamemnon” 1656 (troch.); φοίνισσα δὲ Θρηϊκίων ἀγέλα ταύρων ὑπᾶρχεν]]was already there, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “P.” 4.205]]; αὗται αἱ νέες τοῖσι Ἀθηναίοισι ὑπῆρχον already existed, opposed to to those they were about to build, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 7.144]]; εἰ τοίνυν σφι χώρη γε μηδεμία ὑπῆρχε if they had no country originally existing, [Refs [[prev. author] 2.15]]; χωρὶς δὲ τούτων οἱ χίλιοι ὑπῆρχον the original thousand existed, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 1.5.5; ἔδει πρῶτον μὲν ὑπάρχειν πάντων ἰσηγορίαν 5th c.BC: Eupolis Comicus 291 (Lyric poetry); ὑπαρχούσης μὲν τιμῆς, παρούσης δὲ δυνάμεως 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Agesilaus” 8.1; τοῦτο δεῖ προσεῖναι, τὰ δ᾽ ἄλλ᾽ ὑπάρχει 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 3.15, compare 8.53; ταὐτὰ ὑ. αὐτῷ ἅπερ ἐμοί 5th c.BC: Antipho Orator 5.60, compare 5th c.BC: Lysias Orator 12.23]]; ὑμῖν.. ἐλευθερίαν τε ὑπάρχειν καὶ Λακεδαιμονίων ξυμμάχοις κεκλῆσθαι there is in store for you.., [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 5.9: with _genitive_, οἶκος δ᾽ ὑ. τῶνδε.. ἔχειν]] there is store of these things for us to have, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Agamemnon” 961 (assuming variant, οἴκοις Pors.): frequently in]]participle, ἡ ὑπάρχουσα οὐσία the existing property, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Isocrates Orator 1.28; τὰ ὑ. ἁμαρτήματα 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 2.92]]; τῆς ὑ. τιμῆς for the current price, Syngr. cited in [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 35.12]]; οἱ ὑ. πολῖται the existing citizens, [Refs [[prev. author] 18.295]]; τῆς φύσεως ὑ. nature being what it is, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 6.4.4]]; also κρησφύγετόν τι ὑπάρχον εἶναι that there should be a refuge ready prepared, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 5.124.]]

__B.3
exist really, opposed to φαίνομαι, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “de Caelo” 297b22, “Metaphorical” 1046b10; ἀθεώρητοι τῶν ὑπαρχόντων [prev. author] “GC” 316a9; καταληπτικὴ φαντασία ἡ ἀπὸ τοῦ ὑπάρχοντος “Stoicorum Veterum Fragmenta” 2.25.]]

__B.4
simply, be, τοῖσιν ἄγουσιν κλαύμαθ᾽ ὑπάρξει [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Antigone” 932 (_anapaest meter_); ὅθεν εὐμάρει᾽ ὑπάρχοι πόρου [prev. author] “Ph.” 704 (Lyric poetry)]]: and with a predicate, θησαυρὸς ἄν σοι παῖς ὑπῆρχ᾽ οὑμός [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Hecuba” 1229; τὸ χωρίον καρτερὸν ὑ. 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 4.4]]; φύσεως ἀγαθῆς ὑπάρξαι to be of a good natural disposition, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Oeconomicus” 21.11; κἂν σοφὸς ὑπάρχῃ 4th-3rd c.BC: Philemo Comicus 102]]; μέγα ὑ. τοῖς τοιούτοις λόγοις ις of great advantage to them, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 3.19]]; πολλῶν ὑπάρξει κῦρος ἡμέρα καλῶν, ={κυρώσει πολλὰ καλά}, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Electra” 919.]]

__B.5
sometimes with a participle, much like{τυγχάνω, τοιαῦτα [αὐτῷ] ὑπῆρχε ἐὀντα} [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.192; ἐχθρὸς ὑ. ὤν 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 21.38; ὑ. δύναμιν κεκτημένοι [prev. author] 3.7, compare 15.1.]]

__B.III.2
of persons, ὑ. τινί to be devoted to one, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 1.1.4, “HG” 7.5.5, 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 19.54, etc.]]; καθ᾽ ὑμῶν ὑπάρξων ἐκείνῳ he will be on his side against you, [Refs [[prev. work]118, compare 2.14.]]

__B.III.2.b
ἐν παντὶ.. πᾶς χωρίῳ, καὶ ᾧ μὴ ὑπάρχομεν every one in every place, even outside our sphere of influence (literal to which we do not belong), [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 6.87.]]

__B.III.3
in the Logic of [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus ὑπάρχειν]] denotes the subsistence of qualities in a subject, [Refs [“Metaphorical” 1025a14]]; ὑ. τινί, ={κατηγορεῖσθαί τινος}, [Refs [“APr.” 25a13, +others]]; ὑ. κατά τινος[Refs [[prev. work] 24a27, “Int.” 16b13]]; ἐπί τινος[Refs [[prev. work] 16a32; ὑ. τινὶ ζῴῳ πεζῷ δίποδι εἶναι “Top.” 109a14]]; ὑπάρξει τι [τῷ πρώτῳ] it will have predicates, [Refs 3rd c.AD+ [3rd c.AD: Plotinus Philosophus 5.6.2; ἡ γένεσις τῷ χρόνῳ.. ὑπάρχει 5th-6th c.AD: Damascius Philosophus “de Principiis” 142.]]

frequently in neuter plural participle, τὰ ὑπάρχοντα,

__B.IV.1
in signification [Refs [1,]]existing circumstances, presentadvantages, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [3rd c.AD: Democritus Epigrammaticus 191, 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 2.2; ἀπὸ τῶν αἰεὶ ὑ. σφαλέντες 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 4.18, compare 6.33]]; πρὸς τὰ ὑ.[Refs [[prev. work] 31; ἐκ τῶν ὑ.]]under the circumstances, according to one's means, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 6.4.9, 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Politica” 1288b33; ὡς ἐκ τῶν ὑ. 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 7.76, 8.1.]]

LXX.Gen.12.5]]; ὑποθέμενος τὰ ὑ. καὶ ὑπάρξοντα present and future resources, [Refs 6th c.AD+ [POxy. 125.22 (6th c.AD), etc.]]

__B.IV.3
in Mathematics texts, ὑπάρχοντα εἴδη positive terms, [Refs 3rd c.AD+ [3rd c.AD: Diophantus Mathematicus 1 “Def.” 10.]]

__B.V
impersonal, ὑπάρχει the fact is that.., with accusative et infinitive, ὑ. γάρ σε μὴ γνῶναί τινα [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Electra” 1340]]; ὡς ὑ. τοῦ ἔχειν.. as the case stands with regard to having, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Historia Animalium” 516b25; περὶ τοὺς μαστοὺς ὑπεναντίως ὑ. [prev. work] 500a14.]]

it is allowed, it is possible, with dative et infinitive, ὑ. ἡμῖν ἐπικρατεῖν [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 7.63, compare 5th-6th c.BC: Andocides Orator 2.19, etc.; ὑ. αὐτῇ εὐδαίμονι εἶναι 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Phaedo” 81a, compare “Prt.” 345a, “Phdr.” 240b, etc.]]: also without a dative, οὐχ ὑ. εἰδέναι [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 1.82; ὑ. τὴν αὐτὴν εἶναι μητέρα 4th c.BC: Isaeus Orator 7.25, etc.: _absolutely_, ὥσπερ ὑπῆρχε]] as well as was possible, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 3.109.]]

in neuter participle, ὑπάρχον ὑμῖν πολεμεῖν since it is allowed you to.., [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 1.124, compare 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Symposium” 217a.]]

to be ὕπαρχος or subordinate colleague, [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd-3rd c.AD: Dio Cassius Historicus 36.36; τῷ.. Ἀντωνίνῳ [prev. author] 71.34.]]

uncertain in the sense of ἄρχω, rule; for [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 6.87]], where the [Refs 5th c.BC+ [Scholia is in error, see above 5th c.BC: Bacchylides Lyricus 111.2b; in 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Politica” 1291b32 ὑπερέχειν is probable reading]]

Epic dialect ὑποείκω, with imperfect ὑπόεικον, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 16.305]]: future ὑπείξω [Refs 8th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Agamemnon” 1362, 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Tyrannus” 625, 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 15.24; ὑπείξομαι 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 1.294, 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 12.117]]; Epic dialect also ὑποείξομαι [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 23.602]]: aorist 1 ὑπεῖξα [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 7.7.31]]; Epic dialect ὑπόειξα [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 15.227: compare ὑπεικαθεῖν]]:—retire, withdraw, depart, with genitive loci, νεῶν from the ships, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 16.305]]; ὑ. τινὶ ἕδρης retire from one's seat for another, make room for him, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 16.42]]; ὑ. τοῦ ἀρχαίου λόγου draw back from.., [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 7.160]]; ὑ. τινὶ λόγων (conjecture Valck. for λόγῳ) give one the first word, allow him to speak first, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Memorabilia” 2.3.16; πολίταις ὁδῶν καὶ θάκων καὶ λόγων ὑπείκειν [prev. author] “Cyr.” 8.7.10.]]

__2
yield, give way, ὑ. τινί [Refs [[prev. author] “An.” 7.7.31]]: absolutely, of a seaman, ὅστις.. πόδα τείνας ὑπείκει μηδέν [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Antigone” 716]]; of things, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 20.266; ὅσα δένδρων ὑ. 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Antigone” 713; ὑ. ὑγρὰ οὖσα ἡ κνήμη 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “de Equitandi ratione” 7.6; ὑ. αἱ δάπιδες]]are soft and yielding, [Refs [[prev. author] “Cyr.” 8.8.16]]; ἐν ὑπείκοντι in a yielding substance, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “de Partibus Animalium” 694b15; πρὸς ἀντιπῖπτον.. καὶ οὐ πρὸς ὑπεῖκον [prev. author] “Pr.” 961b4; καθ᾽ ἅπερ ἂν ὑπείκῃ 2nd c.AD: Galenus Medicus 2.711]]; τὸ ὑπεῖκον, ={οἱ ὑπείκοντες}, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Iphigenia Taurica” 327.]]

__3
with accusative, πάροιθε νεμεσσηθεὶς ὑπόειξε χεῖρας ἐμάς he scaped my hands, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 15.227.]]

__II
metaphorically, yield, give way, comply,[Refs 8th c.BC+ [[prev. work] 211; θεοῖσιν ὑπείξεαι ἀθανάτοισι 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 12.117, compare 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 23.602; ἀλλ᾽ ἤτοι μὲν ταῦθ᾽ ὑποείξομεν ἀλλήλοισι 4.62]]; σοὶ πᾶν ἔργον ὑπείξομαι I will give way to thee in.., [Refs [1.294: in Trag., _Attic dialect_, etc., sometimes _absolutely_,]]yield, submit, [NT+5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Ajax” 371, “OT” 625, 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 1.127, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Apologia” 32a, NT.Heb.13.17, etc.]]: sometimes with dative, submit to, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Agamemnon” 1362; τιμαῖς 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Ajax” 670; γήρᾳ ὑ. 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Iphigenia Aulidensis” 140 (_anapaest meter_); ὑ. θυμουμένοις 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Leges” 717d, compare “R.” 336e, etc.; ἐπιθυμίαις 1st c.BC: Philodemus Gadarensis Epigrammaticus “D.” 1.25: with]]infinitive, νῷν ὕπεικε τὸν κασίγνητον μολεῖν concede to us that.., [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Coloneus” 1184]]; ὑ. δαμῆναι submit to be conquered, [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [3rd c.BC: Apollonius Rhodius Epicus 4.1676]]; but ὑ. μὴ πολεμίζειν yield, so as not to.., probable reading [Refs [[prev. work] 408 (ὑπείξομαι, -ωμαι codices).]]

ὑπεναντί-ος, α, ον
[Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Politica” 1327a17, 1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus “Agesilaus” 24]]; but ος, ον [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus Alcaeus2.139b]]:— set over against, meeting, ἵπποι ὑ. ἀλλήλοισιν [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th-7th c.BC: Hesiodus Epicus “Scutum Herculis” 347.]]

set against, opposite, of enemies in battle, τοὺς σφίσιν ὑ. [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 2.2]]; οἱ ὑ. the enemy, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 1.6.38, compare 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 18.148, etc.]]

of logical propositions, subcontrary, [Refs 7th c.AD+ [7th c.AD: Stephanus Philosophus “in librum Aristotelis de Interpretatione commentarium - pars” 30.38.]] adverb -ίως[Refs [[prev. work] 32.24.]]

in Mathematics texts, subcontrary, τομή [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [3rd-2nd c.BC: Apollonius Pergaeus Geometra 1.5]]; of a mean, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Archytas Tarentinus Philosophus 2, 3rd c.AD(?): Pappus Mathematicus 84.14, etc.]]

adverb -ίως in a manner contrary to, τοῖς νόμοις [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aeschines Orator 3.8]]; ὑ. ἔχειν to be opposed, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “de Generatione Animalium” 719a28]]; ὑ. κεῖσθαι[Refs 1st c.BC+ [[prev. work] 719b18; περί τινα ὑ. ὑπάρχει πρός τι [prev. author] “HA” 500a13, +others, compare 1st c.BC: Philodemus Philosophus “περὶ ποιημάτων” 5.19; ὑ. θεραπεύσεις 6th c.AD: Aëtius Medicus 16.52: also _neuter_ _plural_ ὑπεναντία]] as adverb, [Refs 2nd c.BC+ [“IG” 22.1258.8, 7.2225.36 (Thisbe, 2nd c.BC, senatus consultum).]]

short_definition: above/for — ὑπέρ (when following subst.—poët.—ὕπερ; so as adv., 2Co.11:23),
deep_entry:
Abbott-Smith / STEPBible (TBESG)
ὑπέρ (when following subst.—poët.—ὕπερ; so as adv., 2Co.11:23),
prep. with genitive, accusative
__I. C. genitive, primarily of place (rest or motion), over, above, across, beyond, hence, metaphorically,
__1. for, on behalf of: of prayer, Mat.5:44, Act.8:24, Rom.10:1, Jas.5:16, al.; of laying down life, Jhn.10:11, Rom.9:3, al.; esp. of Christ giving his life for man's redemption, Mrk.14:24, Jhn.10:15, Act.21:13, Rom.5:6-8, al.; opposite to κατά, Mrk.9:40, Luk.9:50, Rom.8:31.
__2. Causal, for, because of, for the sake of: with genitive of person(s), Act.5:41, Rom.1:5, Php.1:29, 2Co.12:10, al.; with genitive of thing(s), Jhn.11:4, Rom.15:8, 2Co.1:6, al.
__3. = ἀντί (see M, Pr., 105), for, instead of, in the name of: 1Co.15:29, 2Co.5:15, 21 Gal.3:13, Col.1:7, Phm 13 (cf. Field, Notes, 225).
__4. In more colourless sense, = περί (M, Pr., l.with), for, concerning, with regard to: Rom.9:27, 2Co.1:6 8:23 12:8, Php.1:7, 2Th.2:1, al.

__II. C. accusative, primarily of place, over, beyond, across, hence, metaphorically, of measure or degree in excess, above, beyond, over, more than: Mat.10:24, 37 Luk.6:40, Act.26:13, 1Co.10:13, 2Co.1:8, Eph.1:22 3:20, Phm 16, al.; after comparatives = than (Jdg.11:25, al.), Luk.16:8, Heb.4:12.

__III. As adv. (see supr. ad init.), more: ὕπερ ἐγώ, I more, 2Co.11:23; in compounds, see: ὑπεράνω, ὑπερλίαν, ὑπερπερισσῶς.

__IV. In composition: over (ὑπεραίρω), beyond (ὑπερβάλλω), more (ὐπερνικάω), on behalf of (ὐπερεντυγχάνω).
(AS)

LSJ / STEPBible (TFLSJ)
ὑπέρ [ῠ],
Epic dialect also ὑπείρ, used by [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Homerus Epicus (for the sake of meter) only in the phrase ὑπεὶρ ἅλα (see. ὑπείρ); 4th c.AD(?): Arcadius Grammaticus]] ὁπέρ (which see): in Aeolic dialect replaced by περί (see. περί [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus V): _preposition_ governing _genitive_ and _accusative_, in 4th c.AD(?): Arcadius Grammaticus]] also dative (Cf. Sanskrit upaári 'above', Gothic ufar, O[Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus]] ofer 'over':—from it are formed the comparative and superlative ὑπέρτερος, -τατος, also adverb ὕπερθεν, and Nouns ὑπέρα, ὕπερος.)

__A
WITH GENIT.,

__A.I
of Place, over;

__A.I.1
in a state of rest, over, above, frequently in [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Homerus Epicus, βάλε.. στέρνον ὑ. μαζοῖο 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 4.528]]; χιτωνίσκους ἐνεδεδύκεσαν ὑ. γονάτων not reaching to the knees, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 5.4.13; ἕστηκε.. ὅσον τ᾽ ὄργυι᾽ ὑ. αἴης 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 23.327; εἴθ᾽ ὑ. γῆς, εἴτ᾽ ἐπὶ γῆς, εἴθ᾽ ὑπὸ γῆς 4th-3rd c.BC: Theophrastus Philosophus “de Igne” 1]]; στῆ δ᾽ ἄρ᾽ ὑ. κεφαλῆς stood over his head as he lay asleep, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 2.20, 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 4.803, +others; πασάων ὕ. ἥ γε κάρη ἔχει 6.107; ὑ. πόλιος, ὅθι Ἕρμαιος λόφος ἐστίν, ἦα 16.471]]; ὑ. κεφαλῆς οἱ ἐγίνετο διεξελαύνοντι over head, i. e. over the gateway, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.187; ὑ. τῆς ὀροφῆς “IG” 12.373.246; ὑ. τοῦ ἀγάλματος [prev. work]264; ὄρος τὸ ὑ. Τεγέης 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 6.105]]; τὰ ὑ. κεφαλῆς the higher ground, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Agesilaus” 2.20]]; Ἰονίας ὑ. ἁλὸς οἰκέων on the Ionian sea, i.e. on its shores, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “N.” 7.65; λιμὴν καὶ πόλις ὑ. αὐτοῦ κεῖται 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 1.46, compare 6.4, 2nd-3rd c.AD: Dio Cassius Historicus 40.14]]: of relative geographical position, above, farther inland, οἰκέοντες ὑ. Ἁλικαρνησσοῦ μεσόγαιαν [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.175; ἐξ Αἰθιοπίας τῆς ὑ. Αἰγύπτου 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 2.48; τοῖς ὑ. Χερρονήσου Θρᾳξίν 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 2.6.2; ὑ. Μασσαλίας 2nd c.BC: Polybius Historicus 2.14.8, compare 5.73.3, +others]]: in Hellenistic Gr. the accusative is commoner in this sense, see below [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Bacchylides Lyricus I.]]

__A.I.1.b
of ships at sea, off a place, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 1.112, 8.95; ναυμαχίην τὴν ὑ. Μιλήτου γενομένην 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 6.25; ὑ. τούτου (i.e. Φαλήρου) ἀνακωχεύσαντες τὰς νέας [prev. work] 116.]]

__A.I.2
in a state of motion, over, across, κῦμα νηὸς ὑ. τοίχων καταβήσεται [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 15.382; τὸν δ᾽ ὑ. οὐδοῦ βάντα προσηύδα 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 17.575; πηδῶντος.. τάφρων ὕ. 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Ajax” 1279; ὑ. θαλάσσης καὶ χθονὸς ποτωμένοις 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Agamemnon” 576]]; ἐκκυβιστᾶν ὑ. [τῶν ξιφῶν] [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Symposium” 2.11.]]

__A.I.3
over, beyond, ἐν Κρήτῃ εὐρείῃ τηλοῦ ὑ. πόντου [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 13.257.]]

__A.II
metaphorically, in defence of, on behalf of, τεῖχος ἐτειχίσσαντο νεῶν ὕ. [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 7.449; ἑκατόμβην ῥέξαι ὑ. Δαναῶν 1.444]]: generally, for the prosperity or safety of, τὰ ἱερὰ ὑ. τῆς Εὐβοίας θῦσαι [Refs 5th c.BC+ [“IG” 12.39.65, compare 45.5; ἱερὰ θυόμενα ὑ. τῆς πόλεως 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Memorabilia” 2.2.13; ἐπιτελεῖν τὰς θυσίας ὑ. τε ὑμῶν καὶ τῶν τέκνων “UPZ” 14.27 (2nd c.BC)]]; in dedications (always with reference to living persons), Σμικύθη μ᾽ ἀνέθηκεν.. εὐξαμένη.. ὑ. παίδων καὶ ἑαυτῆς [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [“IG” 12.524, compare 22.4403, 42(1).569 (Epid.); Ἀρτέμιδι Σωτείρᾳ ὑ. βασιλέως Πτολεμαίου Ἐπικράτης Ἀθηναῖος “OGI” 18 (Egypt, 3rd c.BC), compare 365 (Amasia, 2nd c.BC), +others; ὑ. τῆς εἰς αἰῶνα διαμονῆς Ἀντωνείνου Καίσαρος [prev. work]702.3 (Egypt, 2nd c.AD); ὑ. τῆς τύχης.. Ἀντωνείνου Σεβαστοῦ Εὐσεβοῦς [prev. work]703.2 (Ptolemais, 2nd c.AD); ὑ. σωτηρίας τοῦ κυρίου ἡμῶν.. Ἀντωνείνου [prev. work]706 (Egypt, 2nd-3rd c.AD)]]; εὑδόντων ὕ. φρούρημα [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Eumenides” 705]]; ὑ. τινὸς κινδυνεύειν, μάχεσθαι, βοηθεῖν, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 2.20, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Leges” 642c, 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 3.5.6; ἧς ἔθνῃσχ᾽ ὕ. 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Trachiniae” 708; ὑ. γῆς τῆς Ἀθηναίων ναυμαχέειν 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 8.70; ὑ. τῆς Ἑλλάδος ἀμῦναι 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Leges” 692d]]; ἀμυνῶ ὑ. ἱερῶν καὶ ὁσίων Jusj. cited in [Refs 5th c.BC+ [2nd c.AD(?): Pollianus Epigrammaticus 8.105; νῦν ὑ. πάντων ἀγών 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Persae” 405; ὑ. δόξης τελευτήσαντες 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 23.210, compare 5th-6th c.BC: Isocrates Orator 6.93]]; πάνθ᾽ ὑ. ὑμῶν φανήσεται πράξας Χαβρίας, καὶ τὴν τελευτὴν αὐτὴν τοῦ βίου πεποιημένος οὐχ ὑ. ἄλλου τινός in your interests, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 20.80, compare 83; ὑ. τῆς Ἀσίας στρατηγήσας 5th-6th c.BC: Isocrates Orator 4.154]]; of things sought, ὑ. τοῦ νεκροῦ ὠθισμὸς ἐγένετο πολύς [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 7.225]]; ἀφίκετο ὑ. γενεᾶς, ὑ. φωνᾶς, ὑ. τοῦ θησαυροῦ, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [“IG” 42 (1).121.10,42, 123.11 (Epid., 4th c.BC)]]; γίνωσκέ με πεπορεῦσθαι εἰς Ἡρακλέους πόλιν ὑ. τῆς οἰκίας [Refs 2nd c.BC+ [“UPZ” 68.3 (2nd c.BC)]]; sometimes even of the thing to be averted, ἱκέσιον λόχον δουλοσύνας ὕ. about slavery, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Septem contra Thebas” 111 (Lyric poetry), compare 4th c.BC: Aeschines Orator 3.10.]]

__A.II.2
for, instead of, in the name of, ὑ. ἑαυτοῦ τι προϊδεῖν on his own behalf, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 1.141; ὑ. τινὸς ἀποκρίνεσθαι 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 590a; προλέγειν 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 7.7.3; ἐπεὶ οὖν σὺ σιωπᾷς, ἐγὼ λέξω καὶ ὑ. σοῦ καὶ ὑ. ἡμῶν [prev. author] “Cyr.” 3.3.14, compare 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Electra” 554]]; ὑ. Ζήνωνος πράσσων as Zeno's representative, [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [“PSI” 4.389.8 (3rd c.BC)]]; ἔγραψεν ὑ. αὐτῶν διὰ τὸ φάσκειν αὐτοὺς μὴ εἰδέναι γράμματα [Refs 2nd c.BC+ [“PGrenf.” 2.17.9 (2nd c.BC)]]; θεάσασθε ὃν τρόπον ὑμεῖς ἐστρατηγηκότες πάντ᾽ ἔσεσθ᾽ ὑ. Φιλίππου as though by commission from P., [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 3.6]]; so in other dialects with accusative, see below [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Bacchylides Lyricus see]]

__A.II.3
in adjurations, with verbs of entreaty, entreat one as representative of another, τῶν ὕ. ἐνθάδ᾽ ἐγὼ γουνάζομαι οὐ παρεόντων, i. e. I entreat you as they would if they were here, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 15.665, compare 660]]; then more metaphorically, by, λίσσομ᾽ ὑ. ψυχῆς (as you value your life) καὶ γούνων σῶν τε τοκήων [Refs 8th c.BC+ [22.338, compare 24.466; λίσσομ᾽ ὑ. θυέων καὶ δαίμονος.. σῆς τ᾽ αὐτοῦ κεφαλῆς καὶ ἑταίρων 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 15.261; λίσσου᾽ ὑ. μακάρων σέο τ᾽ αὐτῆς ἠδὲ τοκήων 3rd c.BC: Apollonius Rhodius Epicus 3.701]]; ὑ. ξενίου λίσσεται ὔμμε Διός in the name of Zeus, [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [“Anthologia Graeca” 7.499.2 (3rd c.BC: Theaetetus Epigrammaticus)]]; so Aeolic dialect περ (see. περί [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus V).]]

__A.II.4
of the cause or motive, for, because of, by reason of, ἀλγέων ὕ. [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Supplices” 1125 (Lyric poetry); ὑ. παθέων [prev. author] “Hipp.” 159 (Lyric poetry); ἔριδος ὕ. [prev. author] “Andr.” 490 (Lyric poetry)]]; of punishment or reward, for, on account of, τοῖσιν ἄγουσιν κλαύμαθ᾽ ὑπάρξει βραδυτῆτος ὕ. [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Lysias Orator 24.4, compare 21, 16.20; ὑ. οὗ.. ὁμολογῶ.. διαφέρεσθαι τούτοις 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 18.31]]; βουλευομένων ὑ. τοῦ ποίαν τινὰ [εἰρήνην ποιητέον] [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [[prev. author] 19.94; ἔγραψάς μοι ὑ. τῶν καμίνων “PCair.Zen.” 273.2 (3rd c.BC)]]; ἐνεκάλουν ὑ. σύκων [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [“PSI” 6.554.24 (3rd c.BC)]]; ἐπεδώκαμέν σοι ὑπόμνημα ὑ. τοῦ μὴ εἰληφέναι τὴν.. ὄλυραν [Refs 2nd c.BC+ [“UPZ” 46.4 (2nd c.BC)]]; συλλαλήσαντες ὑ. τοῦ τὴν πόλιν ἐνδοῦναι τοῖς Ῥωμαίοις [Refs 2nd c.BC+ [2nd c.BC: Polybius Historicus 1.43.1]]; θροῦς ὑ. τοῦ τὸν Λυκοῦργον ἐκπέμπειν talk of sending L., [Refs [[prev. author] 5.18.5, compare 6]]; γνώμην ὑ. τῆς κοινῆς [δόξης] [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Isocrates Orator 6.93; ὑ. τῶν τούτου λῃτουργιῶν.. ὡδὶ γιγνώσκω 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 21.152; ἐκ τῶν ἐμφανῶν ὑ. τῶν ἀφανῶν πιστεύειν 4th c.AD: Julianus Imperator “Orationes” 4.138b; with verbs expressing emotion, ποίας.. γυναικὸς ἐκφοβεῖσθ᾽ ὕ.; 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Tyrannus” 989; εἰ τὰ παρὰ σοὶ καλῶς ἔχει, θάρρει ὑ. ἐκείνων 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 7.1.17; οὐδεὶς ὑ. μου δαιμόνων μηνίεται κατασφαγείσης 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Eumenides” 101 (approaching sense 11.1).]]

__B
WITH ACCUSATIVE

__B.I
of Place in reference to motion, over, beyond, frequently in [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Homerus Epicus, e.g. ὑ. ὦμον ἤλυθ᾽ ἀκωκή 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 5.16, compare 851; ἀλάλησθε.. ὑπεἰρ ἅλα 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 3.73, compare 7.135, +others, 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Eumenides” 250, 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Antigone” 1145 (Lyric poetry); ὑ. τὸν δρύφακτον ὑπερτιθέμενοι 2nd c.BC: Polybius Historicus 1.22.10]]: without such reference, ὑ. Ἡρακλείας στήλας ἔξω κατοικοῦσι [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Critias” 108e, compare 4th c.AD: Julianus Imperator “Orationes” 1.6d; τὰς κεφαλὰς ὑ. τὸ ὑγρὸν ὑπερίσχον 2nd c.BC: Polybius Historicus 3.84.9; τῶν ὑ. τὸ Σαρδῷον πέλαγος τόπων [prev. author] 2.14.6; ὑ. Μασσαλίαν [prev. author] 2.16.1; λόφον κείμενον ὑ. τὴν ὁδόν [prev. author] 2.27.5, compare 3.47.2, +others; τῶν συριῶν ὑ. τὴν σκηνὴν οὐσῶν “PHib.” 1.38.7 (3rd c.BC)]]; οὐλὴ.. ὑ. ὀφρὺν δεξιάν [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [“PCair.Zen.” 76.13 (3rd c.BC)]]; τὸ ὑ. τὸν ἔσχατον.. σπόνδυλον [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd c.AD: Soranus Medicus 1.102; ὑ. τὸν οὐρανόν 4th c.AD: Julianus Imperator “Orationes” 4.135a.]]

__B.II
of Measure, above, exceeding, beyond, ὑ. τὸν ἀλαθῆ λόγον [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “O.” 1.28; ὑ. τὸ βέλτιστον 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Agamemnon” 378 (Lyric poetry); ὑ. ἐλπίδα 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Antigone” 366 (Lyric poetry); ὑ. δύναμιν 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 6.16; μεγέθει ὑ. τοὺς ἐν τῇ νηΐ 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 488b; ὑ. ἄνθρωπον εἶναι [prev. author] “Lg.” 839d, 2nd c.AD: Lucianus Sophista “Vit.Auct.” 2]]; ὑ. ἡμᾶς beyond our powers, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Parmenides” 128b; ὑ. τὴν ἀξίαν 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Hercules Furens” 146; ὑ. τὴν οὐσίαν 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 372b]]; ὑ. τὸ ὕδωρ [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [compare (ὕδωρ 1.4) 2nd c.AD: Lucianus Sophista “Pr.Im.” 29.]]

__B.II.b
after comparative, than, δυνατώτεροι ὑ... [LXX.Judg.18.26: so after Posit., τοῖς ἀγαθοῖς ὑ. αὐτόν] better than he,[LXX.3Ki.2.32.]

__B.II.2
of transgression, in violation of, ὑ. αἶσαν, opposed to κατ᾽ αἶσαν, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 3.59, +others; ὑ. Διὸς αἶσαν 17.321; ὑ. μοῖραν 20.336]]; ὑ. μόρον (or ὑπέρμορον)[Refs [[prev. work] 30; ὑ. θεόν 17.327; ὑ. ὅρκια 3.299, +others]]

__B.III
of Number, above, upwards of, τὰ ὑ. δέκα μνᾶς [ξυμβόλαια] [Refs 5th c.BC+ [“IG” 12.41.23, compare 22.48, +others; ὑ. τεσσεράκοντα ἄνδρας 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 5.64]]; ὑ. τετταράκοντα (i.e. ἔτη) [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Historia Graeca (Hellenica)” 5.4.13; ὑ. τὰ στρατεύσιμα ἔτη γεγονόσι [prev. author] “Cyr.” 1.2.4]]; ὑ. ἥμισυ more than half, [Refs [[prev. work] 3.3.47.]]

__B.IV
of Time, beyond, i.e. before, earlier than, ὁ ὑ. τὰ Μηδικὰ πόλεμος [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 1.41; ὑ. τὴν φθοράν 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Timaeus” 23c.]]

__B.V
in some dialects, in sense [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus 11.1,2]], on behalf of, ὑ. τὰν πόλιν [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [“SIG” 437 (Delph., 3rd c.BC), +others,compare “IG” 42(1).109iv113 (Epid., 3rd c.BC), 5(2).438-40,442 (Megalopolis, 2nd c.BC), 42(1).380,665 (Epid., 1st c.AD), “IPE” 4.71.10 (Cherson., 2nd c.AD)]]; in sense [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus 111]], concerning, ἐπικράνθη μοι ὑ. ὑμᾶς [LXX.Ruth.1.13.]

__C
WITH DAT., only [Refs 4th c.AD+ [4th c.AD(?): Arcadius Grammaticus, μαχόμενοι ὑ. τᾷ τᾶς πόλιος ἐλευθερίᾳ]] fighting for.., [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [Inscriptiones Graecae 5(2).16 (Tegea, 3rd c.BC).]]

__D
POSITION: ὑπέρ may follow its substantive, but then by anastrophe becomes ὕπερ, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 5.339, 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 19.450, +others, 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Tyrannus” 1444, etc.]]

__E
AS adverb., over-much, above measure, ὑπὲρ μὲν ἄγαν [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Medea” 627 (Lyric poetry)]]; also written ὑπεράγαν, [Refs 1st c.BC+ [1st c.BC-1st c.AD: Strabo Geographus 3.2.9, 2nd-3rd c.AD: Aelianus “De Natura Animalium - Ar.Byzantine Epit.” 3.38, etc.]]; compare ὑπέρφευ: as a predicate, διάκονοι Χριστοῦ εἰσ; ὑπὲρ ἐγώ I am more [than they], [NT.2Cor.11.23.]

__F
IN COMPOSITION (joined with other words), signifies over, above, in all relations, e. g.,

__F.1
of Place, over, beyond, as in ὑπεράνω, ὑπέργειος, ὑπερβαίνω, ὑπερπόντιος.

__F.2
of doing a thing for or in defence of, as in ὑπερμαχέω, ὑπερασπίζω, ὑπεραλγέω.

__F.3
above measure, as in ὑπερήφανος, ὑπερφίαλος.
