[τὸ πέλαγος] εἰς.. [Refs 1st c.BC+ [[prev. author] 1.25.8; also τὸν Καταράκτην “OGI” 654.6 (Egypt, 1st c.BC)]]: absolutely, cross the sea, [Refs 2nd c.BC+ [2nd c.BC: Polybius Historicus 1.47.2]]: as naval and military term, outflank, τὸ λαιὸν τῶν πολεμίων [Refs 2nd c.BC+ [2nd c.BC: Polybius Historicus 1.50.6, compare 3.73.7]], etc.: without a sense of motion, rise above, τὸ ὕδωρ [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-3rd c.BC: Theophrastus Philosophus “Historia Plantarum” 4.8.10; τὸ μέγεθος τοῦ δένδρου [prev. author] “CP” 5.14.9.]]

__II.2
excel, τινι in a thing, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 18.220]]: with accusative, excel, [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [[prev. author] 60.21, Aristeas 16, 2nd-3rd c.AD: Philostratus Sophista “Heroicus” 2.19; τοὺς πρὸ ἑαυτοῦ ἡγεμονεύσαντας “SIG” 877 A 5 (Delph., 2nd-3rd c.AD)]]; νοῦν ὑπεραίρει [Refs 3rd c.AD+ [3rd c.AD: Plotinus Philosophus 6.7.22.]]

__II.3
overshoot, go beyond, μήθ᾽ ὑπεράρας μήθ᾽ ὑποκάμψας καιρόν [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Agamemnon” 786 (_anapaest meter_); ὑ. τὸν ὡρισμένον καιρόν 2nd c.BC: Polybius Historicus 9.14.11; τὴν συνήθειαν [prev. author] 28.14.2]]; exceed, ὑ. τῆς οὐσίας τὸ μέγεθος ὁ τῶν τέκνων ἀριθμός [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Politica” 1266b11; οὗ ἡ πρόνοια τὰς πάντων εὐχὰς οὐκ ἐπλήρωσε μόνον ἀλλὰ καὶ ὑπερῆρε “BMus.Inscription” 894.8 (Halic., 1st c.AD)]]; πυγωνιαῖον ἢ μικρὸν ὑπεραῖρον a little more, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-3rd c.BC: Theophrastus Philosophus “Historia Plantarum” 4.6.8]]; τῶν ὑπεραιρόντων ἱερέων the priests in excess (of a certain number), [Refs 3rd c.AD+ [“BGU” 1.16 (3rd c.AD)]]; τῶν ὑπεραιρούντων (sic) τὸν ἀριθμὸν τῶν ἱερέων [Refs 3rd c.AD+ [“PLond.” 2.347.6 (3rd c.AD)]]; τὸ ὑπεραῖρον ἀργύριον the money (received) in excess, [Refs 2nd c.BC+ [“SIG” 976.27 (Samos, 2nd c.BC)]]; τοσοῦτον ἐν [τοῖς δαπανηθεῖσιν] ὑπερῆρεν [αὐτόν] he so far exceeded him in his expenditure, [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd-3rd c.AD: Dio Cassius Historicus 37.8]]; λόγος ὑπεραίρων τοῖς ὀνόμασι καὶ ταῖς γνώμαις overdone, [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd-3rd c.AD: Philostratus Sophista “Vita Apollonii” 8.6]]; τὸ ὑπεραῖρον exaggeration, [Refs 2nd c.BC+ [2nd c.BC: Polybius Historicus 16.12.9.]]

__III
with genitive, pass beyond, double a cape, τοῦ ἀκρωτηρίου [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd-3rd c.AD: Philostratus Sophista “Vita Apollonii” 3.24]]; rise above, τῆς γῆς [Refs [[prev. author] “Her.” 19.16.]]

__III.2
transcend, exceed, μήθ᾽ ὑπεραίροντα τῶν εἰθισμένων ὄγκων (τὸν εἰθ. ὄγκον [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.AD: Stobaeus, Joannes) μήτ᾽ ἐλλείποντα 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Leges” 717d, compare 2nd-3rd c.AD: Dio Cassius Historicus 75.13 (with _genitive_), etc.; ὑ. τῷ μεγέθει τινῶν 1st c.BC: Diodorus Siculus Historicus 20.91, etc.]]; overcome, τέχνῃ τοῦ ῥοθίου [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd-3rd c.AD: Philostratus Sophista “Vita Apollonii” 7.26.]]

__III.3
with genitive, despise,[Refs 3rd c.AD+ [[prev. work] 1.2, 3rd c.AD: Philostratus Junior Sophista “Imagines” 7.]]

__IV
overflow, τὰ ἀγγεῖα [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Mirabilia” 835a32]]: absolutely, of a stream, ὑ. εἰς τὰ χωρία [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 55.10.]]

__IV.2
ὑ. ὑπέρ τι project beyond.., [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd c.AD: Arrianus Historicus “Tactica” 12.9]]; οἱ ἐν τῷ τρίτῳ ζυγῷ ὑ. τοὺς πρωτοστάτας πήχεις σ, i.e. their σάρισαι project beyond.., [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd-3rd c.AD: Aelianus “Tactica - Griechische Kriegsschriftsteller” 14.4]]; ὑπεραίρειν ἔξω τὰ βλέφαρα project beyond the eyelids, of a tumour, [Refs 6th c.AD+ [6th c.AD: Aëtius Medicus 7.36]], compare 15; overlap, [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [3rd c.BC: Aristarchus Samius Astronomus 8.]]

__V
Ὑπεραίρων, οντος, ὁ, Most Excellent, = Latin Exsuperatorius, name given to December by Commodus, [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd-3rd c.AD: Dio Cassius Historicus 72.15.]]

ὑπερβαίνω,
future -βήσομαι[Refs 1st c.AD+ [1st c.AD(?): Heraclitus 94:]]aorist 2 ὑπερέβην, Epic dialect 3rd.pers. plural ὑπέρβᾰσαν [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 12.469]]:—step over, mount, scale, with accusative, τεῖχος [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” [same place]; οὐδόν 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 8.80; τείχη 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Bacchae” 654, 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 3.20; γεῖσα τειχέων 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Phoenissae” 1180; τάφρους [prev. author] “Rh.” 111]]; ὑ. τοὺς οὔρους cross the boundaries, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 6.108]]; τὰ ὄρεα, Αἷμον, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. author] 4.25, 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 2.96]]; δόμους step over the threshold of the house, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Medea” 382 codices; δῶμα [prev. author] “Ion” 514 (troch., assuming variant); ὑ. τέγος ὡς τοὺς γείτονας 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 22.53]]; ὑ. τὴν οἰκίαν τινός, of burglars, [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [“PTeb.” 796.2 (2nd c.BC); but more usually ὑ. εἰς τὴν οἰκίαν [prev. work] 793vi21 (2nd c.BC),compare “BGU” 1007.10 (3rd c.BC), “PSI” 4.396.4 (3rd c.BC)]] (the usage with genitive is more than uncertain; in [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 3.54 the best codices have ἐπέβησαν]]; in [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Supplices” 1049 Kirchhoff restored ὑπεκβᾶσ᾽]]; in [Refs 5th c.BC+ [“Ion” 220 2nd-3rd c.AD: Hermes Trismegistus supplied βᾱλόν): _absolutely_, ὑ. εἰς τὴν τῶν Θηβαίων 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Historia Graeca (Hellenica)” 5.4.59; τῶν [ἡδονῶν] εἰς τὸ ἐπέκεινα ὑ. 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 587c]]; of rivers, overflow, ἐς τὴν χώρην, ἐς τὰς ἀρούρας, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 2.13, 14; εἰ ἐθελήσει ὑπερβῆναι ὁ ποταμὸς ταύτῃ [prev. work] 99.]]

__2
overstep, transgress, μέτρα [Refs 5th c.BC+ [1st c.AD(?): Heraclitus [same place]; οὐ θέμιν οὐδὲ δίκαν 5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “Fragmenta.” 1.5; νόμους τοὺς Περσέων 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 3.83, compare 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Antigone” 449, +others; τοὺς ὅρκους 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 11.2; τὸν τῶν ἀναγκαίων ὅρον 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 373d; τῆς εἱμαρμένης ὅρον “IG” 12(7).53.32 (Amorgos, 3rd c.AD)]]; τἀληθές exceed the truth, [Refs 1st c.BC+ [1st c.BC: Philodemus Philosophus “περὶ ποιημάτων” 5.24]]: absolutely, transgress, trespass, sin, ὅτε κέν τις ὑπερβήῃ (Epic dialect aorist subjunctive) καὶ ἁμάρτῃ [NT+8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 9.501; ὑ. καὶ ἁμαρτάνοντες 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 366a, cf. NT.1Thes.4.6.]]

__3
pass or go beyond, τοὺς προσεχέας [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 3.89]]; leave out, omit, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 528d, +others, 4th-3rd c.BC: Epicurus Philosophus “Epistulae” 3p.63U., 2nd c.AD: Galenus Medicus 15.592, etc.; ὑ. τι τῷ λόγῳ 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 4.38; ὑ. τὸ σαφὲς εἰπεῖν [prev. author] 60.31]]; pass over, i. e. leave unmolested, the next heir, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Isaeus Orator 3.57]]; ὑ. τῆς οὐσίας omit part of it, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Analytica Posteriora” 91b27.]]

__4
jump across an intervening space, [Refs 1st c.BC+ [1st c.BC: Philodemus Gadarensis Epigrammaticus “D.” 3.9.]]

__5
of Time, pass by, elapse, ὑπερβάντων τῶν τῆς συμπαθείας χρόνων [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd c.AD: Soranus Medicus 2.41.]]

__II
go beyond, ὑπερβὰς ἑβδομήκοντα [ἔτη] after passing the age of seventy, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Leges” 755b]]; ὑ. τοῦτο go beyond this, in their demands, [Refs 2nd c.BC+ [2nd c.BC: Polybius Historicus 2.15.6]]; transcend, τὸν νοῦν [Refs 3rd c.AD+ [3rd c.AD: Plotinus Philosophus 6.7.39]]: absolutely, dies ὑπερβαίνοντες supernumerary days in the calendar, [Refs 4th c.AD+ [4th-5th c.AD: Macrobius Grammaticus “Sat.” 1.13.10.]]

__II.2
surpass, outdo, πάσῃ παρὰ πάντας ἀνθρώπους ὑ. ἀρετῇ [Refs 6th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Timaeus” 24d; ὑ. ἢ γνῶσιν σαφηνείᾳ ἢ ἄγνοιαν ἀσαφείᾳ [prev. author] “R.” 478c: _absolutely_, uncertain reading in 6th c.BC: Theognis Elegiacus 1015.]]

__III
stand over. shield, protect, with dative, [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd-3rd c.AD: Oppianus Anazarbensis Epicus “Halieutica - Poetae Bucolici et Didactici” 1.710.]]

__IV
in perfect, to be higher than, δύο [ἐσχάρας] ὑπερβεβηκυίας τὴν ἐν τῷ μεταφρένῳ ἐσχάραν [Refs 7th c.AD+ [7th c.AD: Paulus Aegineta Medicus 6.44.]]

__B
Causal in aorist 1, put over, ὑπερβησάτω ἐπὶ τὰς δεξιὰς πλευρὰς τὴν κνήμην, as a direction to one mounting a horse, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “de Equitandi ratione” 7.2.]]

ὑπερβάλλω,
future -βαλῶ, Epic dialect -βαλέω[Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 11.597]]: Epic dialect aorist 2 ὑπειρέβαλον [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 23.637]]:—throw over or beyond a mark, overshoot, ὑπέρβαλε σήματα πάντων [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 23.843; τόσσον παντὸς ἀγῶνος (i.e. σήματα) ὑπέρβαλε [prev. work] 847]]; δουρὶ ὑ. Φυλῆα beat him in throwing with it, [Refs [[prev. work] 637.]]

__2
ὅτε μέλλοι ἄκρον [λόφον] ὑπερβαλέειν force the stone over the top, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” [prev. cited]]]

__3
intransitive, run beyond, overrun the scent, of hounds, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Cynegeticus” 6.20.]]

__4
outstrip or pass, in racing, τινας [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Electra” 716.]]

__5
middle, throw a stone over one's head, [Refs [“SIG” 1071 (from Olympia).]]

__II
in various metaphorically senses:

__II.1
outdo, excel, surpass, overpower, δέδοικα μὴ πρὶν πόνοις ὑπερβάλῃ με γῆρας [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Fragmenta” 453.5 (Lyric poetry): with _genitive_, 5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “Fragmenta.” 33; βροντῆς ὑπερβάλλοντα κτύπον 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Prometheus Vinctus” 923.]]

__II.2
go beyond, exceed, μήτ᾽ ἄρ᾽ ὑπερβάλλων βοὸς ὁπλὴν μήτ᾽ ἀπολείπων [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th-7th c.BC: Hesiodus Epicus “Opera et Dies” 489; ὑ. πόσιος μέτρον 6th c.BC: Theognis Elegiacus 479; τὴν τοῦ μετρίου φύσιν 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Politicus” 283e; ὑ. τὰ ἱκανά 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Hiero” 4.8: of Time, ὑ. ἑκατὸν ἔτεα]]exceed [Refs 5th c.BC+ [100 years, in age, 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 3.23]]; ὑ. τὰς τρεῖς ἡμέρας delay longer than.., [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Hippocrates Medicus “περὶ τῶν ἐν κεφαλη—ͅ τρωμάτων” 14]]; ὑ. τὸν χρόνον exceed the time, i. e. be too late, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Historia Graeca (Hellenica)” 5.3.21]]; ὑ. τὸν καιρόν exceed reasonable bounds, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [3rd c.AD: Democritus Epigrammaticus 235, 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 23.122: in number, intensity, etc., ἡδοναὶ ὑ. λύπας 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Leges” 734b, compare “Prt.” 356b (_passive_)]]: with dative modi, exceed one in.., πάντας ἀνθρώπους τόλμῃ καὶ μιαρίᾳ [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Historia Graeca (Hellenica)” 7.3.6; ἅπαντας ἀνθρώπους ὠμότητι 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 18.275: _absolutely_, ὑ. πρὸς ἀρετήν 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Leges” 945c.]]

__II.2.b
with genitive pro accusative, ἆρα λύπῃ ὑ. τὸ ἀδικεῖν τοῦ ἀδικεῖσθα; [Refs 4th c.BC+ [[prev. author] “Grg.” 475c, compare “Lg.” 734a; ὑ. τῆς συμμετρίας 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Politica” 1284b8, compare “HA” 503b22.]]

__II.3
absolutely, exceed, αἱ μέσαι ἕξεις πρὸς μὲν τὰς ἐλλείψεις ὑπερβάλλουσι compared with their defects are in excess, [Refs [[prev. author] “EN” 1108b17]]; exceed all bounds, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Persae” 291, 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Bacchae” 785, 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 7.67, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Theaetetus” 180a]]; οὐχ ὑπερβαλών keeping within bounds, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “N.” 7.66; μή νυν ὑπέρβαλλ᾽, ἀλλ᾽ ἐναισίμως φέρε 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Alcestis” 1077: with _dative_ modi, ὑ. τῇ μοχθηρίᾳ 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Plutus” 109; ἀδυναμίᾳ τοῦ δοξάσαι 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Theaetetus” 192c, compare 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Memorabilia” 4.3.7; ἀνοίᾳ 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 8.16.]]

__II.3.b
frequently in participle ὑπερβάλλων, ουσα, ον, exceeding, excessive, ὑ. δαπάνη [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Hiero” 11.2]]; ἡδονή, ἔπαινοι, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 402e, “Phdr.” 240e; θεάματα ταῖς δαπάναις ὑ. 5th-6th c.BC: Isocrates Orator 4.45, compare 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Leges” 899a]]; οἱ ὑπερβάλλοντες, opposed to οἱ καταδεέστεροι, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Isocrates Orator 9.13]]; τὰ ὑ. an over-high estate, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Medea” 127]] (anapaest meter); φεύγειν τὰ ὑ. ἑκατέρωσε extremes, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 619a]]; τὸ ὑ. αὐτῶν such part of them as goes beyond that, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 2.35]]; οἱ ὑ. [λόγοι], [Refs [title of work by Thrasymachus (“fragment” 7)]], perhaps overpowering arguments.

__II.4
overbid or outbid at auction, ἀλλήλους [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Lysias Orator 22.8, “POxy.” 1633.5 (3rd c.AD)]]; τὸ ὑπερβάλλον the overbid, [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [PPetr. 3p.195 (3rd c.BC)]]: absolutely, go on further and further, in making offers, προέβαινε τοῖσι χρήμασι ὑπερβάλλων he went on bidding more and more, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 5.51; ᾔτει τοσαῦτα ὑπερβάλλων 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 8.56, compare 5th-6th c.BC: Andocides Orator 1.133]]:— passive, ἕνεκα τοῦ-βεβλῆσθαι τὴν οἰκίαν [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [“POxy.” 513.25 (2nd c.AD)]]; see below [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Bacchylides Lyricus 1.3.]]

__II.5
adverb ὑπερβαλλόντως exceedingly, [NT+5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 492b, 4th-3rd c.BC: Epicurus Philosophus “De rerum natura - Wien. Stud.” 2.2, “SIG” 685.36 (Crete, 2nd c.BC), 1st c.BC: Philodemus Philosophus “περὶ παρρησίας” p.7O., NT.2Cor.11.23]]; written ὑπερβαλόντως in [Refs [“IG” 12(7).410.12 (from Amorgos)]]; opposed to μετρίως, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Isocrates Orator 1.28.]]

__III
pass over, cross mountains, rivers, and the like, πρῶνα [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Agamemnon” 307; κορυφάς [prev. author] “Pr.” 722; γῆς ὅρους 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Orestes” 443; τὰς Ἄλπεις εἰς τὴν Ἰταλίαν 1st c.BC-1st c.AD: Strabo Geographus 7.2.3: with _genitive_, θριγκοῦ τοῦδ᾽ ὑ. ποδί 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Ion” 1321 (where Dobree suggested θριγκοὺς τούσδ᾽)]]: metaphorically, surmount, τάσδ᾽ ὑ. τύχας [Refs [[prev. author] Alcaeus795.]]

__III.b
of ships, double a headland, ὑ. Μαλέην [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 7.168; τὴν ἄκραν 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 8.104.]]

__III.c
absolutely, cross over, ἐς τὴν ἄνω Μακεδονίην [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 8.137, compare 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 4.6.10; πρὸς τοὺς Θρᾷκας [prev. work] 7.5.1; κατὰ λόφους τινάς [prev. work] 6.5.7.]]

__III.2
of water, run over, beat over, with genitive, ὑπερβάλλει δὲ θάλασσα ἀμφοτέρων τοίχων [Refs 6th c.BC+ [6th c.BC: Theognis Elegiacus 673]]; of rivers, overflow, τὰς ἀρούρας [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 2.111]]: absolutely, of a kettle, boil over, [Refs [[prev. author] 1.59]]; of the sea, ἢν δ᾽ ὑπερβάλῃ.. πόντος [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Troades” 691.]]

__III.3
of the sun, to be very hot, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 4.184.]]

__III.4
exceed, i. e. overlap, a base, [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [3rd c.BC: Euclides Geometra 6.29; compare ὑπερβολή IV.—Note, the case that follows is almost always the _accusative_; the _genitive_ occurs in a few exceptional instances, see above 11.2 b, 111.1 and 2.]]

__B
middle, with perfect passive, = [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus 11]], outdo, overcome, conquer, τινα [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 5.124, 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Equites” 758 (Lyric poetry), “Nu.” 1035; τὴν βασιλέος δύναμιν 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 8.24; μάχῃ ὑ. τινά 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Orestes” 691; φίλτροις ὑ. τινά 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Trachiniae” 584, compare 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Equites” 413]]: absolutely, to be conqueror, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 6.9, 7.168.]]

__B.2
exceed, surpass, τινα [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 19.342, etc.; τοὺς ἀπ᾽ αἰῶνος “OGI” 542.11 (Ancyra, 2nd c.AD)]]; πάντας τῷ ὕψεϊ καὶ τῷ μεγάθεϊ [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 2.175, compare 110; τινὰ ἀναιδείᾳ 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Equites” 409]]; θωπείαις[Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. work] 890; εἴς τι 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Critias” 115d; ἔν τινι 1st c.BC-1st c.AD: Strabo Geographus 1.1.2.]]

__B.2.b
δόσι χρημάτων ὑ. surpass all, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.61; ἀρετῇ [prev. author] 9.71]]; ὑπερβαλλόμενος πλήθεϊ with overpowering numbers, [Refs [[prev. author] 3.21:]]perfect participle passive, ὑπερβεβλημένη γυνή an excellent, surpassing woman, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Alcestis” 153; φύσις ὑπερβεβλ. 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 558b; ταφῆς τῆς μὲν ὑπερβεβλ., τῆς δὲ ἐλλειπούσης [prev. author] “Lg.” 719d: with _genitive_, γόγγροι τῶν παρ᾽ ἡμῖν ὑπερβεβλ. κατὰ τὸ μέγεθος 1st c.BC-1st c.AD: Strabo Geographus 3.2.7.]]

__B.3
overbid, outbid (see. above [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus 11.4), τινὰ χρήμασιν 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Phaedrus” 232c, compare 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 5.3.32.]]

__B.4
outflank, τὸ κέρας τῶν πολεμίων [Refs 1st c.BC+ [1st c.BC: Asclepiodotus Tacticus “Tact.” 10.2, compare18.]]

__B.II
put off, postpone, τὴν ἀπόδοσιν [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 4.9; τὴν συμβολήν [prev. author] 9.45; εἰς ἄλλον καιρόν 1st c.BC: Philodemus Gadarensis Epigrammaticus “Rh.” 1.223S.]]; but ἢν ὑπερβάλωνται ἐκείνην τὴν ἡμέραν.. συμβολὴν μὴ ποιεύμενοι if they let that day pass without fighting, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 9.51]]: absolutely, delay, linger, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. author] 3.71, 76, 7.206; εἰς αὖθις ὑπερβαλέσθαι 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Phaedrus” 254d, compare 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Rhetorica ad Alexandrum” 1420a8, 1438b6.]]

Abbott-Smith / STEPBible (TBESG)
ὑπερ-βάλλω
[in LXX: Job.15:11 A (†), Sir.5:7 25:11, al. ;]
__1. trans., to throw over or beyond.
__2. Intrans., to run beyond. In both senses, metaphorically, to exceed, surpass, transcend: 2Co.3:10 9:14, Eph.1:19 2:7; with genitive obj., Eph.3:19.†
(AS)

---

LSJ / STEPBible (TFLSJ)
ὑπερβάλλω,
future -βαλῶ, Epic dialect -βαλέω[Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 11.597]]: Epic dialect aorist 2 ὑπειρέβαλον [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 23.637]]:—throw over or beyond a mark, overshoot, ὑπέρβαλε σήματα πάντων [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 23.843; τόσσον παντὸς ἀγῶνος (i.e. σήματα) ὑπέρβαλε [prev. work] 847]]; δουρὶ ὑ. Φυλῆα beat him in throwing with it, [Refs [[prev. work] 637.]]

__2
ὅτε μέλλοι ἄκρον [λόφον] ὑπερβαλέειν force the stone over the top, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” [prev. cited]]]

__3
intransitive, run beyond, overrun the scent, of hounds, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Cynegeticus” 6.20.]]

__4
outstrip or pass, in racing, τινας [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Electra” 716.]]

__5
middle, throw a stone over one's head, [Refs [“SIG” 1071 (from Olympia).]]

__II
in various metaphorically senses:

__II.1
outdo, excel, surpass, overpower, δέδοικα μὴ πρὶν πόνοις ὑπερβάλῃ με γῆρας [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Fragmenta” 453.5 (Lyric poetry): with _genitive_, 5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “Fragmenta.” 33; βροντῆς ὑπερβάλλοντα κτύπον 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Prometheus Vinctus” 923.]]

__II.2
go beyond, exceed, μήτ᾽ ἄρ᾽ ὑπερβάλλων βοὸς ὁπλὴν μήτ᾽ ἀπολείπων [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th-7th c.BC: Hesiodus Epicus “Opera et Dies” 489; ὑ. πόσιος μέτρον 6th c.BC: Theognis Elegiacus 479; τὴν τοῦ μετρίου φύσιν 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Politicus” 283e; ὑ. τὰ ἱκανά 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Hiero” 4.8: of Time, ὑ. ἑκατὸν ἔτεα]]exceed [Refs 5th c.BC+ [100 years, in age, 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 3.23]]; ὑ. τὰς τρεῖς ἡμέρας delay longer than.., [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Hippocrates Medicus “περὶ τῶν ἐν κεφαλη—ͅ τρωμάτων” 14]]; ὑ. τὸν χρόνον exceed the time, i. e. be too late, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Historia Graeca (Hellenica)” 5.3.21]]; ὑ. τὸν καιρόν exceed reasonable bounds, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [3rd c.AD: Democritus Epigrammaticus 235, 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 23.122: in number, intensity, etc., ἡδοναὶ ὑ. λύπας 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Leges” 734b, compare “Prt.” 356b (_passive_)]]: with dative modi, exceed one in.., πάντας ἀνθρώπους τόλμῃ καὶ μιαρίᾳ [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Historia Graeca (Hellenica)” 7.3.6; ἅπαντας ἀνθρώπους ὠμότητι 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 18.275: _absolutely_, ὑ. πρὸς ἀρετήν 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Leges” 945c.]]

__II.2.b
with genitive pro accusative, ἆρα λύπῃ ὑ. τὸ ἀδικεῖν τοῦ ἀδικεῖσθα; [Refs 4th c.BC+ [[prev. author] “Grg.” 475c, compare “Lg.” 734a; ὑ. τῆς συμμετρίας 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Politica” 1284b8, compare “HA” 503b22.]]

__II.3
absolutely, exceed, αἱ μέσαι ἕξεις πρὸς μὲν τὰς ἐλλείψεις ὑπερβάλλουσι compared with their defects are in excess, [Refs [[prev. author] “EN” 1108b17]]; exceed all bounds, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Persae” 291, 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Bacchae” 785, 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 7.67, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Theaetetus” 180a]]; οὐχ ὑπερβαλών keeping within bounds, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “N.” 7.66; μή νυν ὑπέρβαλλ᾽, ἀλλ᾽ ἐναισίμως φέρε 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Alcestis” 1077: with _dative_ modi, ὑ. τῇ μοχθηρίᾳ 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Plutus” 109; ἀδυναμίᾳ τοῦ δοξάσαι 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Theaetetus” 192c, compare 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Memorabilia” 4.3.7; ἀνοίᾳ 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 8.16.]]

__II.3.b
frequently in participle ὑπερβάλλων, ουσα, ον, exceeding, excessive, ὑ. δαπάνη [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Hiero” 11.2]]; ἡδονή, ἔπαινοι, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 402e, “Phdr.” 240e; θεάματα ταῖς δαπάναις ὑ. 5th-6th c.BC: Isocrates Orator 4.45, compare 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Leges” 899a]]; οἱ ὑπερβάλλοντες, opposed to οἱ καταδεέστεροι, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Isocrates Orator 9.13]]; τὰ ὑ. an over-high estate, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Medea” 127]] (anapaest meter); φεύγειν τὰ ὑ. ἑκατέρωσε extremes, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 619a]]; τὸ ὑ. αὐτῶν such part of them as goes beyond that, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 2.35]]; οἱ ὑ. [λόγοι], [Refs [title of work by Thrasymachus (“fragment” 7)]], perhaps overpowering arguments.

__II.4
overbid or outbid at auction, ἀλλήλους [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Lysias Orator 22.8, “POxy.” 1633.5 (3rd c.AD)]]; τὸ ὑπερβάλλον the overbid, [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [PPetr. 3p.195 (3rd c.BC)]]: absolutely, go on further and further, in making offers, προέβαινε τοῖσι χρήμασι ὑπερβάλλων he went on bidding more and more, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 5.51; ᾔτει τοσαῦτα ὑπερβάλλων 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 8.56, compare 5th-6th c.BC: Andocides Orator 1.133]]:— passive, ἕνεκα τοῦ-βεβλῆσθαι τὴν οἰκίαν [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [“POxy.” 513.25 (2nd c.AD)]]; see below [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Bacchylides Lyricus 1.3.]]

__II.5
adverb ὑπερβαλλόντως exceedingly, [NT+5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 492b, 4th-3rd c.BC: Epicurus Philosophus “De rerum natura - Wien. Stud.” 2.2, “SIG” 685.36 (Crete, 2nd c.BC), 1st c.BC: Philodemus Philosophus “περὶ παρρησίας” p.7O., NT.2Cor.11.23]]; written ὑπερβαλόντως in [Refs [“IG” 12(7).410.12 (from Amorgos)]]; opposed to μετρίως, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Isocrates Orator 1.28.]]

__III
pass over, cross mountains, rivers, and the like, πρῶνα [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Agamemnon” 307; κορυφάς [prev. author] “Pr.” 722; γῆς ὅρους 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Orestes” 443; τὰς Ἄλπεις εἰς τὴν Ἰταλίαν 1st c.BC-1st c.AD: Strabo Geographus 7.2.3: with _genitive_, θριγκοῦ τοῦδ᾽ ὑ. ποδί 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Ion” 1321 (where Dobree suggested θριγκοὺς τούσδ᾽)]]: metaphorically, surmount, τάσδ᾽ ὑ. τύχας [Refs [[prev. author] Alcaeus795.]]

__III.b
of ships, double a headland, ὑ. Μαλέην [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 7.168; τὴν ἄκραν 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 8.104.]]

__III.c
absolutely, cross over, ἐς τὴν ἄνω Μακεδονίην [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 8.137, compare 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 4.6.10; πρὸς τοὺς Θρᾷκας [prev. work] 7.5.1; κατὰ λόφους τινάς [prev. work] 6.5.7.]]

__III.2
of water, run over, beat over, with genitive, ὑπερβάλλει δὲ θάλασσα ἀμφοτέρων τοίχων [Refs 6th c.BC+ [6th c.BC: Theognis Elegiacus 673]]; of rivers, overflow, τὰς ἀρούρας [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 2.111]]: absolutely, of a kettle, boil over, [Refs [[prev. author] 1.59]]; of the sea, ἢν δ᾽ ὑπερβάλῃ.. πόντος [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Troades” 691.]]

__III.3
of the sun, to be very hot, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 4.184.]]

__III.4
exceed, i. e. overlap, a base, [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [3rd c.BC: Euclides Geometra 6.29; compare ὑπερβολή IV.—Note, the case that follows is almost always the _accusative_; the _genitive_ occurs in a few exceptional instances, see above 11.2 b, 111.1 and 2.]]

__B
middle, with perfect passive, = [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus 11]], outdo, overcome, conquer, τινα [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 5.124, 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Equites” 758 (Lyric poetry), “Nu.” 1035; τὴν βασιλέος δύναμιν 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 8.24; μάχῃ ὑ. τινά 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Orestes” 691; φίλτροις ὑ. τινά 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Trachiniae” 584, compare 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Equites” 413]]: absolutely, to be conqueror, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 6.9, 7.168.]]

__B.2
exceed, surpass, τινα [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 19.342, etc.; τοὺς ἀπ᾽ αἰῶνος “OGI” 542.11 (Ancyra, 2nd c.AD)]]; πάντας τῷ ὕψεϊ καὶ τῷ μεγάθεϊ [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 2.175, compare 110; τινὰ ἀναιδείᾳ 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Equites” 409]]; θωπείαις[Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. work] 890; εἴς τι 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Critias” 115d; ἔν τινι 1st c.BC-1st c.AD: Strabo Geographus 1.1.2.]]

__B.2.b
δόσι χρημάτων ὑ. surpass all, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.61; ἀρετῇ [prev. author] 9.71]]; ὑπερβαλλόμενος πλήθεϊ with overpowering numbers, [Refs [[prev. author] 3.21:]]perfect participle passive, ὑπερβεβλημένη γυνή an excellent, surpassing woman, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Alcestis” 153; φύσις ὑπερβεβλ. 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 558b; ταφῆς τῆς μὲν ὑπερβεβλ., τῆς δὲ ἐλλειπούσης [prev. author] “Lg.” 719d: with _genitive_, γόγγροι τῶν παρ᾽ ἡμῖν ὑπερβεβλ. κατὰ τὸ μέγεθος 1st c.BC-1st c.AD: Strabo Geographus 3.2.7.]]

__B.3
overbid, outbid (see. above [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus 11.4), τινὰ χρήμασιν 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Phaedrus” 232c, compare 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 5.3.32.]]

__B.4
outflank, τὸ κέρας τῶν πολεμίων [Refs 1st c.BC+ [1st c.BC: Asclepiodotus Tacticus “Tact.” 10.2, compare18.]]

__B.II
put off, postpone, τὴν ἀπόδοσιν [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 4.9; τὴν συμβολήν [prev. author] 9.45; εἰς ἄλλον καιρόν 1st c.BC: Philodemus Gadarensis Epigrammaticus “Rh.” 1.223S.]]; but ἢν ὑπερβάλωνται ἐκείνην τὴν ἡμέραν.. συμβολὴν μὴ ποιεύμενοι if they let that day pass without fighting, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 9.51]]: absolutely, delay, linger, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. author] 3.71, 76, 7.206; εἰς αὖθις ὑπερβαλέσθαι 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Phaedrus” 254d, compare 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Rhetorica ad Alexandrum” 1420a8, 1438b6.]]

Abbott-Smith / STEPBible (TBESG)
ὑπερ-βολή, -ῆς, ἡ
(ὑπερβάλλω), [in LXX: καθ᾽ ὑ., 4Ma.3:18 * ;]
a throwing beyond. Metaphorical, excess, superiority, excellence: 2Co.4:7 12:7; καθ᾽ ὑπερβολήν, beyond measure, exceedingly, Rom.7:13, 1Co.12:31, 2Co.1:8, Gal.1:13; κ. ὑ. εἰς ὑ., beyond all measure, 2Co.4:17.†
(AS)

---

LSJ / STEPBible (TFLSJ)
ὑπερβολ-ή, ἡ,
(ὑπερβάλλω) a throwing beyond others, δίσκων ὑπερβολαῖς [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd-3rd c.AD: Philostratus Sophista “Philostrati majoris imagines” 2.19]]: in intransitive sense, altitude of a star, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Meteorologica” 342b32.]]

__2
overshooting, superiority, χερῶν ὑπερβολαῖς [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Fragmenta” 434; στρατιᾶς 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 6.31.]]

__3
excess, τοῦ μεγέθεος [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Archytas Tarentinus Philosophus 1]]; opposed to ἔλλειψις or ἔνδεια, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Protagoras” 356a, 357a, 357b; θερμασίης 5th c.BC: Hippocrates Medicus “περὶ διαίτης” 2.65; ὑ. δισσὴ.., τῷ ποσῷ καὶ τῷ ποιῷ 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “de Partibus Animalium” 668b14]]; ὑπερβολὴν τῆς ἐπιθυμίας ἔχειν with accusative et infinitive, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Andocides Orator 3.33, etc.: hence in various phrases, χρημάτων ὑπερβολῇ.. πρίασθαι]] at an extravagant price, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Medea” 232]]; ἐπέφερον τὴν ὑ. τοῦ καινοῦσθαι pushed on their extravagance in revolutionizing, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 3.82]]; οὐκ ἔχον ἐστὶν ὑπερβολήν it can go no further, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 21.119, compare 25.54; ἃ μηδὲ πιθανὰς τὰς ὑ. ἔχει 4th-3rd c.BC: Menander Comicus “Ἥρως” 62]]; so οὐδεμίαν or μηδεμίαν ὑ. λείπειν, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Isocrates Orator 4.5,110, compare 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 3.25; οὐδεμίαν ὑ. καταλείπων φιλοτιμίας “SIG” 545.13 (Delph., 3rd c.BC)]]; εἴ τις ὑ. τούτου if there is aught beyond (worse than) this, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 19.66, compare 5th-6th c.BC: Isocrates Orator 5.42]]; ταῦτ᾽ οὐχ ὑ.; is not this the extreme, the last degree? [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 27.38]]; ὑπερβολὴν ποιήσομαι I will put an extreme case, [Refs [[prev. author] 19.332]]; τοσαύτην ὑ. ποιεῖσθαι ὥστε.. to go so far that.., [Refs [[prev. author] 18.190: followed by a _genitive_, ὑ. ποιεῖσθαι ἐκείνων τῆς αὑτοῦ βδελυρίας]] to carry his own rascality beyond theirs, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. author] 22.52, compare 23.201, 5th-6th c.BC: Andocides Orator 4.22, 5th c.BC: Lysias Orator 14.38]]; ὑ. ποιεῖν τῆς τιμῆς to raise the price, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Politica” 1259a26; εἰς ὑ. εὐδαιμονίας ἥκειν 5th-6th c.BC: Isocrates Orator 11.14; τοσαύτας ὑ. δωρειῶν παρές χηται 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 20.141]]; ὑ. ἀνοίας ἔχειν Polystr.p.27 W.

__4
with preposition in Adverbial phrases, ={ὑπερβαλλόντως}, εἰς ὑπερβολήν in excess, exceedingly; εἰς ὑ. ἄμεινον [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Fragmenta” 494; ἀγαθὸς εἰς ὑ. 4th c.BC: Antiphanes Comicus 80.11; ἐς ὑ. ἐκθερμαίνεσθαι 5th c.BC: Hippocrates Medicus “περὶ διαίτης” 2.65: with _genitive_, κτήσαιτ᾽ ἂν ὄλβον εἰς ὑ. πατρός 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Fragmenta” 282.6 (variant{εἰς ὑπεκτροφὴν πάτρας})]]; far beyond, τοῦ πρόσθεν εἰς ὑ. πανοῦργος, i. e. far more wicked, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. author] “Hipp.” 939, compare 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 61.33; ἀναλίσκειν πάντα εἰς ὑπερβολάς 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Epistulae” 326d:— ἐξ ὑπερβολῆς 2nd c.BC: Polybius Historicus 8.15.8:]] —καθ᾽ ὑπερβολὰν τοξεύσας with surpassing aim, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Tyrannus” 1196 (Lyric poetry); καθ᾽ ὑ. ἐπαινεῖν]]extravagantly, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Isocrates Orator 5.11]]; οἱ καθ᾽ ὑ. ἐν ἐνδείᾳ ὄντες in extremity of need, [NT+4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Politica” 1295b18; αἱ καθ᾽ ὑ. ἡδοναί [prev. author] “EN” 1151a12; τὸ καθ᾽ ὑ. τραχύ 1st c.BC: Philodemus Gadarensis Epigrammaticus “Po.Herc.” 994.35; καθ᾽ ὑ. ἁμαρτωλός NT.Rom.7.13: with _genitive_, καθ᾽ ὑ. φιλοδοξίας “OGI” 472.9 (Didyma, 1st c.AD)]]:—so in dative, εὐτελὴς ὑπερβολῇ [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-3rd c.BC: Menander Comicus 615; παχεῖ᾽ ὑ. 4th-3rd c.BC: Philemo Comicus 41; ὑ. ἀγαθός 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Historia Animalium” 625a29, etc.]]

__5
preeminence, perfection, without any notion of excess, δι᾽ ἀρετῆς ὑπερβολήν [Refs [[prev. author] “EN” 1145a24, compare “Rh.” 1367b1, “Pol.” 1284a4]]; ἡ ὑ. τῆς φιλίας the best and noblest kind of friendship, [Refs [[prev. author] “EN” 1166b1]]; but ἡ καθ᾽ ὑ. φιλία, ={ἡ καθ᾽ ὑπεροχήν}, [Refs [[prev. author] “EE” 1238b18.]]

__6
overstrained phrase, hyperbole, ὑπερβολὰς εἰπεῖν [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Isocrates Orator 4.88; οἱ πρὸς ὑπερβολὴν πεπονημένοι λόγοι [prev. work]11; ὑπερβολὰς εἰπεῖν]] make strong statements, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [[prev. author] 3.35, 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 27.64]]; as a figure of speech, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Rhetorica” 1413a29, 4th c.BC: Demetrius Phalereus Rhetor “Demetrius on Style” 52, 1st c.BC-1st c.AD: Strabo Geographus 3.2.9; πρὸς -ὴν εἰρημένος [prev. author] 1.2.33.]]

__7
τὸ καθ᾽ ὑπερβολήν the superlative degree, in Adjectives, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Topica” 134b24]]; τιθέναι ὑπερβολῇ[Refs [[prev. work] 139a9; καθ᾽ ὑ. εἰπεῖν [prev. author] “Cael.” 281a16.]]

__8
overbid at auction, [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [“PPetr.” 2p.44 (3rd c.BC).]]

__II
crossing over, passage of mountains, etc., [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 1.2.25, 2nd c.BC: Polybius Historicus 3.34.6, etc.]]

__II.2

deep_entry:
Abbott-Smith / STEPBible (TBESG)
ὑπερ-έχω
[in LXX: Gen.25:23 (אָמַץ), Exo.26:13 (עֲדַף), Sir.36:7, al. ;]
__1. trans., to hold over or above.
__2. Intrans. (when a noun follows, the case is governed by the prep.; see Bl., § 34, 1; 36, 8), to rise above, overtop; metaphorically,
__(a) to be superior in rank, etc.: Rom.13:1, 1Pe.2:13 (cf. Wis.6:6);
__(b) to be superior, excel, surpass: with genitive (cl.; see supr.), Php.2:3; with accusative (cl.; see supr.), Php.4:7; as subst., τ. ὑπερέχον, the excel­lency, the surpassing worth, Php.3:8.†
(AS)

---

LSJ / STEPBible (TFLSJ)
ὑπερέχω,
Epic dialect ὑπειρ- [Refs 6th c.BC+ [6th c.BC: Theognis Elegiacus (see. below 1.2)]]: Epic dialect imperfect ὑπείρεχον [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 2.426:]]aorist ὑπερέσχον, and in poetry form -έσχεθον, [Refs [11.735, 24.374]]: future -έξω[Refs 3rd c.BC+ [“PCair.Zen.” 60.6 (3rd c.BC), 5th c.AD(?): Hesychius Legal icographus]]:—hold over, σπλάγχνα.. ὑπείρεχον Ἡφαίστοιο held them over the fire, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 2.426; μου τὸ σκιάδειον ὑπέρεχε 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Aves” 1508; ἡμῶν ὑπερεῖχε τὴν χύτραν [prev. author] “Eq.” 1176]]; ὑπερέχοντα τὸν αὐλὸν τῆς θαλάσσης holding it up out of the sea, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Historia Animalium” 537b1.]]

__2
ὑ. χεῖρά (χεῖράς) τινος hold one's hand over him, so as to protect, μάλα γάρ ἑθεν εὐρύοπα Ζεὺς χεῖρα ἑὴν ὑπερέσχε [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 9.420, 687; τις.. ἐμεῖο θεῶν ὑπερέσχεθε χεῖρα 24.374; Ζεὺς τῆσδε πόληος ὑπειρέχοι.. χεῖρα 6th c.BC: Theognis Elegiacus 757; so πόλεως ἵν᾽ ὑπερέχοιεν ἀλκάν 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Septem contra Thebas” 215 (Lyric poetry), compare “fragment” 199.7: with _dative_ _person_, οἱ.. ὑπείρεχε χεῖρας Ἀπόλλων 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 5.433; αἴ κ᾽ ὔμμιν ὑπέρσχῃ χεῖρα Κρονίων 4.249, compare 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 14.184.]]

__3
hold above, ὑ. τὸ ῥύγχος, ὅπως ἀναπνέῃ, of the dolphin, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Historia Animalium” 589b11, compare 566b15, 599b27, +others; ὑ. ὀφρύν]]elevate, [Refs 6th c.AD+ [Anthologia Graeca 5.298 (6th c.AD: Agathias Historicus et Epigrammaticus).]]

__II
intransitive, to be above, rise above the horizon, εὖτ᾽ ἀστὴρ ὑπερέσχε φαάντατος [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 13.93]]; αὐτῆς [Αἰγύπτου] εἶναι οὐδὲν ὑπερέχον no part of it was above water, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 2.4]]; ὕδωρ,.. ὃ μόλις ὑπερέχοντες ἐπεραιώθησαν which they crossed, with their heads only just above it, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 3.23]]; ἕψεται ἄχρι ἂν ὑπερέχῃ τὸ ὕδωρ till it sticks out above the water, [Refs 1st c.AD+ [1st c.AD: Dioscorides (Dioscurides) Medicus 3.7]]; but ἐπιχέας ὕδωρ ὥστε ὑπερέχειν till it covers (i.e. the contents of the vessel), [Refs [[prev. author] 5.87; τὸ κέρας τὸ ἕτερον ἢ καὶ ἀμφότερα ὑπερέχοντα]]projecting above the ground, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 2.41]]; γεῖσον.. ὑπερέχον τρία ἡμιπόδια projecting a foot and a half, [Refs 2nd c.BC+ [“IG” 22.1668.34, compare 7.3073.71 (Lebad., 2nd c.BC): with _genitive_, ὑπερέσχεθε γαίης]] rose above, overlooked the earth, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 11.735; ὄμμ᾽ ὑπερσχὸν ἴτυος 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Phoenissae” 1384; [σταυροὺς] οὐχ ὑπερέχοντας τῆς θαλάσσης 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 7.25; σκεύη ὑπερέχοντα τοῦ τειχίου 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 514c, compare 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 3.5.7; ὤφθη.. ὁ δεξιὸς ὀφθαλμὸς ὑπερέχειν θατέρου παμπόλλῳ δή τινι 2nd c.AD: Galenus Medicus 18(2).301.]]

__II.2
overtop, be prominent above, στάντων μὲν Μενέλαος ὑπείρεχεν εὐρέας ὤμους, i. e. stood (head and) shoulders above them, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 3.210; ὅκως τινὰ ἴδοι τῶν ἀσταχύων ὑπερέχοντα 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 5.92.ζ,compare 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Politica” 1284a37; φιλέει ὁ θεὸς τὰ ὑπερέχοντα πάντα κολούειν 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 7.10.έ,compare 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 6.2.17]]; [ᾡ] ὁ πρῶτος ὅρος ὑ. τοῦ δευτέρου.. μέρει by the fraction by which the first term exceeds the second, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Archytas Tarentinus Philosophus 2: τὸ ὑπερέχον]] the excess, [Refs 3rd c.AD+ [3rd c.AD: Diophantus Mathematicus 1.6.]]

__II.3
in military phrase, outflank, τῶν πολεμίων ὑ. τῷ κέρατι [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Historia Graeca (Hellenica)” 4.2.18, compare 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 3.107.]]

__II.4
metaphorically, with accusative, overtop, excel, outdo, βροτῶν πάντων ὑπερσχὼν ὄλβον [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Persae” 709 (troch.); σωφροσύνῃ πάντας ὑ. 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Hippolytus” 1365 (_anapaest meter_); πελταστικῷ εἰκὸς ὑ. τὴν ἡμετέραν δύναμιν 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Historia Graeca (Hellenica)” 6.1.9.]]

__II.4.b
with genitive, πάντων ὑ. μεγέθει καὶ ἀρετῇ [NT+5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Timaeus” 24e, compare “Prm.” 150e, “Grg.” 475c; ὑ. τῶν πολλῶν 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 23.206, cf. NT.Phil.2.3; ἁπάντων ὑπερέχουσι τῶν κακῶν 4th c.BC: Anaxilas Comicus 22.7 (troch.).]]

__II.4.c
absolutely, prevail, θεῶν ὑπερέσχε νόος [Refs 6th c.BC+ [6th c.BC: Theognis Elegiacus 202]]; οἱ ὑπερσχόντες the more powerful, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Prometheus Vinctus” 215; τῶν πόλεων αἱ ὑπερέχουσαι 5th-6th c.BC: Isocrates Orator 4.95]]; οἱ ὑπερέχοντες those in authority, [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [3rd c.AD(?): Diogenes Laertius 6.78, compare 2nd c.AD: Vettius Valens Astrologus 61.30, +others;]] ἐπειδὰν ἡ θάλαττα ὑπέρσχῃ has prevailed, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 9.69]]; ἐν τοῖς πολεμίοις ὑ. excel in.., [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-3rd c.BC: Menander Comicus 642]]; ἐνδέχεται.. μὴ τοσοῦτον ὑ. τῷ ποσῷ, ὅσον λείπεσθαι τῷ ποιῷ exceed so much.., [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Politica” 1296b23]]; ὑπὲρ ὧν πλειονάκι ἐντετευχυιῶν ὑπερέχων ἡμᾶς ἀπράκτους καθίστησι being too strong for us, [Refs 2nd c.BC+ [“Sammelb.” 4638.18 (2nd c.BC)]]; πᾶν κρύφιον οὐχ ὑπερεῖχε σέ was beyond thee (i. e. thy comprehension), [LXX+2nd c.AD+ [2nd c.AD(?): Theodotion LXX.Eze.28.3.]]

__II.4.d
passive, to be outdone, ὑπό τινος [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Phaedo” 102c, 102d; τὴν δύναμιν τοῦ ὑπερέχειν καὶ ὑπερέχεσθαι [prev. author] “Prm.” 150d; κατὰ πλοῦτον ὑπερέχειν κατ᾽ ἀρετὴν δ᾽ ὑπερέχεσθαι 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Politica” 1281a7, compare 2nd c.AD: Galenus Medicus 15.805.]]

__II.5
in Logic, have a wider extension, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Analytica Posteriora” 99a24, compare “Rh.” 1363b8 (_active_ and _passive_).]]

__II.6
ἐπὶ τοῖς ὑπερέχουσι δανεῖσαι to lend on the security of excess value, of a second mortgage, [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [“SIG” 364.33 (Ephesus, 3rd c.BC).]]

__III
with genitive of things, rise above, be able to bear, τῆς ἀντλίας [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Pax” 17; τῶν ἀναλωμάτων 1st c.BC: Diodorus Siculus Historicus 4.80 (variant for{ὑπερεῖδον}).]]

__IV
have over, ὑπερέχει he has in hand, [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [3rd c.BC: Zenon Papyri du Caire 292.498, compare 790.25 (3rd c.BC); ὑπερέξομεν πρὸς τὸ διὰ χερός [prev. work]355.93 (3rd c.BC).]] —Cf. ὑπερίσχω.

LSJ / STEPBible (TFLSJ)
ὑπηρετ-έω,
future -ήσω[Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd c.AD: Alexander Rhetor (see. below)]], etc.: pluperfect ὑπηρετήκειν [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Historia Graeca (Hellenica)” 3.3.9]]:—properly do service on board ship, as a rower (compare ὑπηρέτης, ὑπηρεσία), [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [“SIG” 524.33,47 (Praesus, 3rd c.BC)]]:—passive, πλοῖον ὑπὸ δύο ἀνθρώπων ὑπηρετεῖσθαι δυνάμενον [Refs 1st c.BC+ [1st c.BC: Diodorus Siculus Historicus 2.55.]]

__II
to be a servant, do service, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Electra” 996, “Ph.” 990]]; opposed to ἄρχω, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Vespae” 518 (troch.); τοὺς διὰ φόβον ὑ. 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Hiero” 1.38.]]

__II.2
with dative, minister to, serve, τῷ παρόντι δαίμονι [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Electra” 1306, compare 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Phoenissae” 1708, 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 4.108, etc.]]; ὑ. τῷ χρηστηρίῳ submit to its ruling, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 8.41, compare 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Leges” 914a; ἔργοις ἀνοσίοις ὑ. 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Coloneus” 283]]; [νόμῳ, λόγῳ], [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Lysias Orator 2.19]]; ὑ. τοῖς τρόποις humour his ways, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Ranae” 1432]]; τῷδ᾽ ὑ. λόγῳ second, support it, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Medea” 588; ὢν ἄνθρωπος ἀνθρώπου τύχαις ὑπηρετήσω 2nd c.AD: Alexander Rhetor 150.]]

__II.3
ὑ. τινὶ εἴς or πρός τι, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.109, 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “de Equitandi ratione” 8.7, etc.]]; also ὑ. τινί τι serve one in a thing, οἷς σὺ ταῦθ᾽ ὑπηρετεῖς [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Philoctetes” 1024, compare 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Plutus” 979, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Symposium” 196c, 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 5.1.20, 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 18.138, 59.35.]]

__II.3.b
in financial sense, τὸν δὲ ταμίαν εἰς τὸ ἀνάλωμα ὑπηρετῆσαι [Refs 4th c.BC+ [“Supp.epigram” 1.351.30 (Samos, 4th c.BC), compare 363.43 ([prev. passage], 3rd c.BC), “Inscription Prien.” 3 (4th c.BC), 18 (3rd c.BC), +others]]

__II.3.c
at Athens, serve as ὑπηρέτης of the Council, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 19.70.]]

__II.3.d
in the Mithraic cult, to be a ὑπηρέτης or servitor, [Refs [Rev.Hist.Rel. 109.63 (from Rome).]]

__II.3.e
render military service, [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [“BGU” 180.14, 613.23 (both 2nd c.AD).]]

__II.4
absolutely, serve, be subordinate, opposed to προστάττω, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Topica” 129a13; ἡ ὑπηρετοῦσα ἐπιστήμη [prev. author] “Metaphorical” 982b5: with _neuter_ _plural_ of]] adjective, etc., τὰ λοίφ᾽ ὑ. help in what remains to be done, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Philoctetes” 15; ὑ. τὰ περὶ τὸν πόλεμον 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 467a]]; and with cognate accusative, ὑ. τὰς διακονικὰς πράξεις [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Politica” 1277a36]]:—passive, to be done as service, τὰ ἀπ᾽ ἡμέων ἐς ὑμέας ὑπηρετέεται [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 4.139]]; χρὴ σὴ τό γε ἐμὸν ὑπηρετέεσθαι that my service should be rendered, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. author] 1.108; ἢν τὰ παρ᾽ ὑμῶν ὑπηρετῆται 5th-6th c.BC: Isocrates Orator 3.63; τὸ πρᾶγμα τὸ ὑπηρετηθέν 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Ethica Eudemia” 1243a16, compare 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Historia Graeca (Hellenica)” 5.2.34.]]—The middle occurs in late texts, as [Refs 1st c.AD+ [3rd c.AD: Heliodorus Scriptor Eroticus 7.19, +others, and 4th c.AD: Alciphro Epistolographus 1.11, uncertain in “Supp.epigram” 1.327.19 (Callatis, 1st c.AD)]]; τὸ -ούμενον the retinue, [Refs 1st c.AD+ [1st c.AD: Memnon Historicus 2.4]]; future -ήσομαι[Refs 3rd c.AD+ [“POxy.” 58.24 (3rd c.AD)]]; but in [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Electra” 1306, ὑπηρετοίην was rightly restored by Musgrave and Elmsl. for -οίμην.]]

LSJ / STEPBible (TFLSJ)
ὑπηρέτ-ης, ου, ὁ,
(ἐρέτης) Doric dialect ὑπηρέτας [Refs 4th c.BC+ [“IG” 42(1).122.40,112 (Epid., 4th c.BC), “SIG” 1000.31 (Cos, 1st c.BC)]]:— rower, τοὶ ὑ. τᾶν μακρᾶν ναῶν [Refs [“SIG” [prev. cited] (uncertain meaning).]]

__II
underling, servant, attendant, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 3.63, 5.111; δοῦλοι καὶ πάντες ὑ. 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Politicus” 289c]]; ὑ. [τῆς πόλεως], opposed to ἄρχων, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [[prev. author] “R.” 552b; ἡ πόλις εἰς ὑπηρέτου σχῆμα.. προελήλυθεν 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 23.210]]; τῶν ἰατρῶν, τῶν δικαστῶν ὑ., [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Leges” 720a, 873b]]; used in Trag. and Attic dialect to express all kinds of subordinate relations, as Hermes is ὑ. θεῶν, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Prometheus Vinctus” 954, compare 983]]; the Delphians are Φοίβου ὑπηρέται, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Tyrannus” 712]]; Neoptolemus is ὑ. to Odysseus, [Refs [[prev. author] “Ph.” 53; the αὐλός is ὑ. to the Chorus, Pratin.Lyric poetry 1.7]]: sometimes with dative, τῷ θεῷ ὑ. [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Leges” 773e]]; τοῖς νόμοις[Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. work] 715c, 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Politica” 1287a21; also οἱ περὶ τυράννους καὶ πόλεις ὑ. 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Troades” 426]]; opposed to οἰκέτης, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Memorabilia” 2.10.3: with _genitive_ objecti, ὑ. παντὸς ἔργου]] a helper in every work, [Refs [[prev. author] “An.” 1.9.18.]]

__II.2
at Athens,

__II.2.a
the servant who attended each man-at-arms (ὁπλίτης) to carry his baggage, rations, and shield, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 3.17]]; sometimes light-armed as slingers or bowmen, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Aves” 1186.]]

__II.2.b
ὁ τῶν ἕνδεκα ὑ. the assistant of the Eleven, employed in executions of state-criminals, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Phaedo” 116b, compare 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Historia Graeca (Hellenica)” 2.3.54, 2.4.8.]]

__II.2.c
a petty officer of the Council, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [“IG” 12.879 (_plural_), “Hesperia” 3.63 (4th c.BC).]]

__II.3
plural, staff-officers in immediate attendance on the general, aides-de-camp, adjutants, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 2.4.4, 6.2.13, etc.: _sing._, 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 50.31]]; also, officer attached to τάξις, σύνταγμα, or ἑκατονταρχία, [Refs 1st c.BC+ [1st c.BC: Asclepiodotus Tacticus “Tact.” 2.9, 6.3, 2nd-3rd c.AD: Aelianus “Tactica - Griechische Kriegsschriftsteller” 9.4, 16.2, 2nd c.AD: Arrianus Historicus “Tactica” 10.4, 14.4.]]

__II.4
servitor in the cult of Mithras, [Refs [“Rev.Hist.Rel.” 109.64 (from Rome).]]

ὕπνος, ὁ,
sleep, slumber, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 11.245, +others (see. below)]]; of the sleep of death, κοιμήσατο χάλκεον ὕ. [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 11.241; Κάλχανθ᾽ ὕ. θανάτοιο κάλυψεν 8th-7th c.BC: Hesiodus Epicus “Fragmenta” 160 codices 1st c.BC-1st c.AD: Strabo Geographus; ὕπνῳ καὶ καμάτῳ ἀρημένος 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 6.2, compare 12.281; τάπητες μαλακώτεροι ὕπνω 3rd c.BC: Theocritus Poeta Bucolicus 15.125, compare 5.51.]] — Special phrases:

__I
of going to sleep, μιν ἐπήλυθε.. ὕ. [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 4.793; ἐπὶ.. ὕ. ὄρουσεν 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 23.232; ἱκάνει 1.610; ἔχει 10.4, etc.; τὸν ὕ. ἔμαρπτε 23.62, +others; ᾕρει 24.4, +others; λαμβάνει 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Philoctetes” 767; opposed to ὕπνος ἀνῆκέ τινα 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 2.71, 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 19.551, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Protagoras” 310d: of persons, ὕπνον ἀωτεῖν 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 10.159, etc.; ὕπνου δῶρον ἕλοντο 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 16.481, etc.; λαβεῖν 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Symposium” 223b; κοιμᾶσθαι 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Hiero” 6.7; ἡδὺν ὕπνον καθεύδειν 4th-3rd c.BC: Menander Comicus “Kith.fragment” 1.5; ὕπνου τυχεῖν 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Acharnenses” 713; μικρὸν ὕπνου λαχών 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 3.1.11; ὕπνου λαχεῖν μέρος 5th c.BC: Cratinus Comicus 218]]; ἐν ὕπνῳ or ὕπνῳ πεσεῖν to fall a-sleep, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “I.” 4(3).23(41), 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Eumenides” 68; εἰς ὕπνον πεσεῖν 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Philoctetes” 826]]; οὐχ ὕπνῳ γ᾽ ἐνδόντα (so Badham for εὕδοντά) μ᾽ ἐξεγείρετε [Refs [[prev. author] “OT” 65]]; also ὕπνῳ δεδμημένος, δαμείς, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 10.2, 14.353, etc.]]; νικώμενος, κρατηθεῖσ᾽, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Agamemnon” 290, “Eu.” 148 (Lyric poetry); κάτοχος 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Trachiniae” 978 (Lyric poetry); σκεδάσαι.. ἀπὸ βλεφάρων ὕπνον [prev. work] 991 (Lyric poetry).]]

__I.2
of waking from sleep, ἐγεῖραί τινα ἐξ ὕπνου [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 15.44, etc.]]: of the sleeper, ἀνόρουσε, ἔγρετο, ἐξ ὕ. [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 10.162, 2.41; ἐξ ὕ. στῆναι 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Philoctetes” 277; ἀπολακτίσασ᾽ ὕπνον 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Eumenides” 141; ἀποσείσασθαι 2nd c.AD: Lucianus Sophista “Tim.” 6.]]

__I.3
with Preps., when the plural also is not uncommon, ἐν ὕπνῳ in sleep, in a dream, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Iphigenia Taurica” 44, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 476c]]; ἐν τοῖς ὕ.[Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. work] 572b, “Sph.” 266b, 5th-6th c.BC: Isocrates Orator 9.21, “PCair.Zen.” 34.5 (3rd c.BC)]]; καθ᾽ ὕπνον ὄντα [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Trachiniae” 970 (Lyric poetry), compare 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Leges” 800a]]; καθ᾽ ὕπνον, κατὰ τοὺς ὕπνους, [Refs 1st c.AD+ [1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus 2.717e,555b, “Alex.” 50]]; περὶ πρῶτον ὕ. about one's first sleep, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Vespae” 31, 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 2.2; περὶ πρώτους ὕ. 4th c.BC: Eubulus Comicus 13; ἀπὸ πρώτου ὕ. 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 7.43; διὰ μέσων τῶν ὕ. 1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus “Themistocles” 28; ἐκ τῶν ὕ. ἐγείρεσθαι 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 330e]]: plural, dreams, ὕ. ἀγένητοι [Refs 1st c.BC+ [1st c.BC: Philodemus Gadarensis Epigrammaticus “D.” 1.22.]]

__II
Sleep, as a god, twinbrother of Death, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 14.231, 16.672, 682; _accusative_ to 8th-7th c.BC: Hesiodus Epicus “Theogonia” 212]], son of Night without father. Abbott-Smith / STEPBible (TBESG)
ὑπό (before smooth breathing ὑπ᾽, Mat.8:9b, Luk.7:8b; before rough breathing ὑφ᾽, Rom.3:9; on the neglect of elision in Mt, Lk, ll. witha, Gal.3:22, see WH, App., 146; Tdf., Pr., iv),
prep. with genitive, dative (not in NT), accusative
__I. C. genitive, primarily of place, under, hence, metaphorically, of the efficient cause, by: after passive verbs, with genitive of person(s), Mat.1:22, Mrk.1:5, Luk.2:18, Jhn.14:21, Act.4:11, 1Co.1:11, Heb.3:4, al.; with genitive of thing(s), Mat.8:24, Luk.7:24, Rom.3:21, al.; with neut. verbs and verbs with pass, meaning, Mat.17:12, Mrk.5:26, 1Co.10:9, 10 1Th.2:14, al.
__II. C. accusative, under;
__1. of motion: Mat.5:15 8:8, Mrk.4:21, Luk.13:34; hence, metaphorically, of subjection, Rom.7:14, 1Co.15:27, Gal.3:22, 1Pe.5:6, al.
__2. Of position: Jhn.1:49, Act.4:12, Rom.3:13, 1Co.10:1, al.; hence, metaphorically, under, subject to, Mat.8:9, Rom.3:9, 1Co.9:20, Gal.4:5, al.
__3. Of time, about: Act.5:21.
__III. In composition: under (ὑποδέω), hence, of subjection (ὑποτάσσω), compliance (ὑπακούω), secrecy (ὑποβάλλω), diminution (ὑποπνέω).

ὑπό [ῠ],
preposition with genitive, dative, and accusative: Aeolic dialect ὐπά [Refs 7th c.BC+ [7th-6th c.BC: Alcaeus Lyricus 39]]; Boeotian dialect ὑπά Ἀρχ.Δελτ. [Refs 5th c.BC+ [14 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus ii 19 (Thespiae, 3rd c.BC)]]; Ionic dialect ηυπύ only in [Refs 5th c.BC+ [“IG” 14.871 (Cumae, 5th c.BC); 4th c.AD(?): Arcadius Grammaticus]] ὁπύ [Refs 4th c.BC+ [“Schwyzer” 664.15,21 (Orchom. 4th c.AD(?): Arcadius Grammaticus, 4th c.BC)]]; in Epic dialect ὑπαί (also [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Bacchylides Lyricus 12.139)]]: this is found in [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Homerus Epicus]] only six times as a well-attested reading (ὑ. πόδα [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 2.824, ὑ. δέ 3.217, 11.417, 12.149, ὑ. δείους 10.376, 15.4)]]; elsewhere (before λ ν ρ ϝ) it is weakly attested as see l. for ὑπὸ (?~X ¯), e.g. ποσσὶ δ᾽ ὑπὸ (variant{ὑπαὶ}) λιπαροῖσι [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 2.44, +others]]; but ὑπαὶ νεφέων is given by most codices in [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 15.625, 16.375 (see. Allen ed. maj.), and ὑπαὶ νεφέεσσι Anonymus cited in 1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus 2.38e; also in compounds, ὑπαιδείδοικα “hymnus ad Mercurium” 165, ὑπαιφοινίσσω (which see)]]; it is not frequently in Trag. Poets, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Agamemnon” 892, 944, 1164 (Lyric poetry), “Eu.” 417, 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Electra” 711, 1418 (Lyric poetry), “Inach.” in “PTeb.” 692 ii5 (Lyric poetry), 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Electra” 1188 (Lyric poetry), 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Acharnenses” 970 (_paratragoedia_). (With ὑπό]] (ὕπο) cf. Sanskrit úpa 'towards, near to, etc.', Gothic uf 'under'.)

__A
WITH GENITIVE,

__A.I
of Place, with Verbs of motion, from under, αὖτις ἀναστήσονται ὑ. ζόφου they will rise again from under the gloom, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 21.56; ὑ. χθονὸς ἧκε φόωσδε 8th-7th c.BC: Hesiodus Epicus “Theogonia” 669; ῥέει κρήνη ὑ. σπείους 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 9.141, compare 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Phaedrus” 230b; ὄσσε δεινὸν ὑ. βλεφάρων ἐξεφάανθεν 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 19.17]]; ἐσιδόντες ὑπαὶ χειμῶνος αἴγλαν from under the storm-cloud, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Bacchylides Lyricus 12.139]]; especially of rescuing from under another's power, after the Verbs ἐρύεσθαι, ἁρπάζειν, ῥύεσθαι, ἐρύειν, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 9.248, 13.198, 17.224, 235; ἤγαγεν ὑμέτερόνδ᾽ ἀνδροκτασίης ὕ. λυγρῆς]]from the consequences of, [Refs [23.86]]; also ἵππους μὲν λῦσαν ὑ. ζυγοῦ from under the yoke,[Refs 8th c.BC+ [8.543, 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 4.39]]; ὑπ᾽ ἀρνειοῦ λυόμην I loosed myself from under the ram, [Refs [9.463]]; σπλάγχνων ὕπο ματέρος μόλεν, i.e. was born, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “N.” 1.35, compare “O.” 6.43]]; rarely in Trag., ὑ. πτερῶν σπάσας [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Andromache” 441; περᾷ γὰρ ἥδ᾽ ὑ. σκηνῆς πόδα [prev. author] “Hec.” 53; once in 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus, τὰς δέ οἱ ἵππους ὑ. τοῦ ἅρματος νεμομένας ἀφανισθῆναι 4.8; αἴ τις ὑ. τῶν νομίων τῶν ἐπιϝοικων ἀνχωρέῃ “SIG” 47.27 (Locris, 5th c.BC)]]; compare ὑπέκ.

ὑ. παροξυσμόν 2nd c.AD: Galenus Medicus 19.215]]; παραδόντω τοῖς αἱρεθεῖσι εἰς τὸν ὑπ᾽ αὐτὰ (or ὕπαυτα as adverb ={ἑξῆς}) ἐνιαυτόν [Refs 2nd c.BC+ [“IG” 9(1).694.60 (Corc., 2nd-1st c.BC)]]; ὑ. κύνα [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Historia Animalium” 547a14, 4th-3rd c.BC: Theophrastus Philosophus “de Causis Plantarum” 1.13.3, 1st c.BC: Diodorus Siculus Historicus 19.109; ὑ. τὰς θερινὰς [τροπὰς] καὶ τοῦ κυνὸς τὴν ἐπιτολήν “Geoponica” 2.6.17.]]

__C.IV
of accompaniment, ὑπὸ ὄρχησίν τε καὶ ᾠδήν [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Leges” 670a; ὑ. αὐλὸν διαλέγεσθαι 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Symposium” 6.3 codices (ὑ. τοῦ αὐλοῦ Cobet)]]; ὑ. κήρυκα (see. κῆρυξ [Refs 5th c.BC+ [1.3).—Compare 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus 11.5, 5th c.BC: Bacchylides Lyricus 11.4.]]

__C.IV.2
ὄνον ἕνα ὑ. λαχανόσπερμον laden with.., Meyer [Refs 1st c.AD+ [“Ostr.” 81.2 (1st c.AD),compare “PFay.” p.324 (1st c.AD)]]; ὄνοι ὑ. δένδρα [Refs 3rd c.AD+ [“BGU” 362i6, +others (3rd c.AD)]]; compare above [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus 11.8.]]

__D
POSITION: ὑ. can follow its substantive, becoming by anastrophe ὕπο. It is frequently separated from the substantive by intervening words, as in [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 2.465, 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 5.320, 7.130:]] —ὑπαί is placed after its case in [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Eumenides” 417, 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Electra” 1418, “Inach.” [same place], although _accusative_ to Hdn.Gr. 1.480 it cannot suffer anastrophe.]]

__E
AS adverb., under, below, beneath, frequently in [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Homerus Epicus]]; especially of young animals, under the mother, i.e. at the breast, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 4.636, 21.23.]]

__E.2
behind, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 7.61: cf. C. 1.]]

__E.II
ὑπ᾽ ἐκ or ὑπέκ, see at {ὑπέκ}.—In [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Homerus Epicus]] the separation of the preposition from its Verb by tmesis is very frequently, and sometimes it follows, in which case it suffers anastrophe, φυγὼν ὕπο νηλεὲς ἦμαρ [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 9.17.]]

__F
IN COMPOSITION (joined with other words),:

__F.I
under, as well of rest as of motion, as in ὕπειμι, ὑποβαίνω, etc.

__F.I.2
of the casing or covering of one thing with another, as ὑπάργυρος, ὑπόχρυσος.

__F.I.3
of the agency or influence under which a thing is done, to express subjection or subordination, ὑποδαμνάω, ὑποδμώς, ὑφηνίοχος, compare ἐπί [Refs [G.  111.]]

__F.II
denoting what is in small degree or gradual, somewhat, a little, as in ὑποκινέω, ὑποδεής, ὑπόλευκος (so in tmesi, ὑ. τι ἀσεβῆ [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Phaedrus” 242d, compare “Grg.” 493c; ὑ. τι μικρὸν ἐπιθήκισα 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Vespae” 1290 (Lyric poetry)).]]

__F.III
underhand, secretly, as in ὑποθέω, ὑποθωπεύω, ὑποκορίζομαι, ὑπόρνυμι.

suborn, [NT.Acts.6.11]:—passive, of an informer, [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd c.AD: Appianus Historicus “Bella Civilia” 1.74.]]

__III
suggest, whisper, as a prompter does, ἑσταότος μὲν καλὸν ἀκούειν, οὐδὲ ἔοικεν ὑββάλλειν [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 19.80]] (where Scholia B explanation it to interrupt); ὑποβαλεῖν δυνήσεσθε, ἤν τι ἐπιλανθάνωνται [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 3.3.55, compare 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Gorgias” 491a, 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 21.204, 4th c.BC: Aeschines Orator 3.48; ὑ. ὁ νόμος ἃ χρὴ γράφειν [prev. work]22; ἐγώ σοι λόγον ὑποβαλῶ καλόν [prev. author] 1.121; ὑ. παιδὶ λόγον]]dictate, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Isocrates Orator 12.231, compare 5.149]]; ὑ. ὀνόματα, of an informer, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Lysias Orator 13.25; τὸν -οντα τῇ Πυθίᾳ τοὺς χρησμούς 1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus 2.404b; τὰς ἀνειμένας [ἁρμονίας] ἡ φύσις ὑ. τοῖς τοιούτοις 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Politica” 1342b22; ταῦτα ἡ αἴσθησις ὑ. 4th-3rd c.BC: Epicurus Philosophus “Epistulae” 2p.39U.]]; so, provoke, produce, [Refs [[prev. work] 1p.29U., etc.:compare ὑποβλήδην 1.1, ὑποβολή 1.3.]]

χαῖρε δ᾽ Ὀδυσσεὺς ὅττι μιν ὣς ὑπέδεκτο 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 14.52; τὸν δ᾽ οὐχ ὑποδέξομαι αὖτις 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 18.59, 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 19.257; ξεῖνον.. ὑποδέξομαι οἴκῳ 16.70; Θέτις δ᾽ ὑπεδέξατο κόλπῳ 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 6.136, compare 18.398; Διὸς πλαστὴν ὑπέδεκτο γυναῖκα 8th-7th c.BC: Hesiodus Epicus [same place]; οἰκίοισι ὑ. τινά 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.41]]; ὑπέδεκτο ξεῖνον ὀχέων received the stranger [as he lighted] from his chariot, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus]] [same place]; ὁ ὑποδεξάμενος the man who had received him, [NT+5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Isocrates Orator 9.20; ἱκέτας ὑ. 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Heraclidae” 757 (Lyric poetry), compare “Berl.Sitzb.” 1927.167 (from Cyrene), NT.Jam.2.25; φυγάδας 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 5.83, compare “PRev.Laws” 44.14 (3rd c.BC)]]; harbour a runaway slave, [Refs 3rd c.AD+ [“POxy.” 1643.12 (3rd c.AD)]]; [ξένον] ἀγοραῖς καὶ λιμέσι καὶ δημοσίοις οἰκοδομήμασιν ἔξω τῆς πόλεως [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Leges” 952e, compare 953b, 953d, “OGI” 49.5 (Ptolemais, 3rd c.BC)]]; ὑ. φρουράν admit an enemy's garrison, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 58.38, compare 67, “IG” 12.87.10, 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Politica” 1303a36]]; λῃστάς, πειρατάς, harbour brigands, pirates, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [“SIG” 38 B 21 (Teos, 5th c.BC), “Supp.epigram” 3.378 B 11 (Delph., 2nd-1st c.BC),compare “POxy.” 1408.23 (3rd c.AD)]]; γυναῖκάς τινι εἰς τὸ αὐτὸ φοιτώσας ὑποδέχεσθαι [Refs 1st c.AD+ [1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus “Pericles” 32]]; αἱ Θίβρωνα ὑποδεξάμεναι πόλεις those who admitted him as a friend, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Historia Graeca (Hellenica)” 4.8.21, compare 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 3.111, 6.34: with a thing as subject, γαῖα.. ὑπέδεκτο μάντιν Οἰκλείδαν]] the earth opened up to receive the seer O., [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “N.” 10.8]]; αἰθὴρ μὲν ψυχὰς ὑπεδέξατο σώμ [ατα δὲ χθών] [Refs [“IG” 12.945.6]]; τῆς τεκούσης καὶ θρεψάσης καὶ ὑποδεξαμένης [χώρας] [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Menexenus” 237c.]]

__2
entertain to a meal, θύων Διὶ Κτησίῳ κἀκεῖνον ὑποδεχόμενος [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Antipho Orator 1.18, compare “IG” 4.679.15 (Hermione, 3rd-2nd c.BC)]]; ἵνα ἔχῃ ἡ στρατιὰ τὰ ἐπιτήδεια (πολλὴ γὰρ οὖσα οὐ πάσης ἔσται πόλεως ὑποδέξασθαι) [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 6.22]]; ὁ ὑποδεχόμενος the host (at a dinner party), [Refs 1st c.BC+ [1st-2nd c.AD: Epictetus Philosophus “Fragmenta” 17; τὸ πλῆθος λαμπρῶς ὑπεδέξατο 1st c.BC: Diodorus Siculus Historicus 17.115, compare 1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus “Alexander” 23.]]

__3
give ear to, hearken to, εὐχάς [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th-7th c.BC: Hesiodus Epicus “Theogonia” 419; τοὺς λόγους 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 8.106]]; ὑ. διαβολάς give ear to accusations, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Lysias Orator 25.11 codices (to be read ἀπο-).]]

__4
admit, allow a thing with which one is taxed, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 4.167; οὐκ ὑ.]]refuse to admit, deny, [Refs [[prev. author] 3.130, 6.69.]]

__II
take up a burden, ἡ γυνὴ ὑποδεξαμένη φέρει τὸ φορτίον τοῦτο [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Memorabilia” 2.2.5]]; of ships, take on board, τὰ εἴδη [Refs 3rd c.AD+ [“POxy.” 1412.10 (3rd c.AD)]]; of dolphins, [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd c.AD: Lucianus Sophista “DMar.” 8.1.]]

__II.2
bear patiently, βίας ὑποδέγμενος ἀνδρῶν [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 13.310, 16.189]]; submit to, τὰς κατὰ νόμους παραγγελίας [Refs 4th c.AD+ [“POxy.” 67.11 (4th c.AD)]]; μέτρον, i. e. accept it as correct, [Refs 6th c.AD+ [[prev. work] 157.5 (6th c.AD)]]; τροφὴ θλίβουσα πᾶν τὸ δοκοῦν αὐτὴν ὑποδέχεσθαι [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd c.AD: Soranus Medicus 1.115.]]

__III
undertake, promise, αἴδεσθεν μὲν ἀνήνασθαι, δεῖσαν δ᾽ ὑποδέχθαι [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 7.93, compare 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 9.21, 22]]; ὁ δέ οἱ πρόφρων ὑπέδεκτο (i.e. δώσειν) [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 2.387]]; ὑποδέκομαι (i.e. ἐνιαυτοῦ ἀποθυσεῖν τὰ ἴατρα) [Refs 4th c.BC+ [“IG” 42(1).121.46 (Epid., 4th c.BC)]]; with infinitive future, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [“hymnus ad Cererem” 443, 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 3.69, 4.119, 133, 6.11, 7.158, 8.29, 102, 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 2.29]] (infinitive aorist is variant for future in [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.24, 6.2)]]; with infinitive present, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Antipho Orator 3.3.6 (assuming variant)]]; ὑ. τινὶ ἦ μὴν.. with infinitive future, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 8.81]]; Κορίνθιοι ὑπεδέξαντο τὴν τιμωρίαν undertook to champion their cause, [Refs [[prev. author] 1.25; ὥσπερ ὑπεδέξασθε, βοηθήσατε [prev. work] 71]]; ὑ. μεγάλα τινί make him great promises, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 2.121. ; τὴν ἀτραπὸν ἐθελονταὶ Φωκέες ὑποδεξάμενοι Λεωνίδῃ ἐφύλασσον [prev. author] 7.217; ἃ ὑπεδέξατο οὐκ ἐπετέλει 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 2.95]]; undertake to contribute, ὅσον ἂν ἕκαστος θέλῃ [Refs 4th c.BC+ [“AJP” 56.362 (Colophon, 4th c.BC); _absolutely_, [prev. passage]; ὑπεδέξαντο εἰς τὰ τείχη [prev. work]363; also τὰ ἐκφόρια ἅπερ ὑπεδέξω]] the rents which you undertook to collect, [Refs 5th c.AD+ [POxy. 1134.7 (5th c.AD).]]

__III.2
accept as a responsibility, take in charge, as a nurse, [Refs [“hymnus ad Cererem” 226]]; of officials, shippers, farm bailiffs, etc., take over, receive as agent (compare ὑποδέκτης), τοὺς νεολέκτους.. ὑποδεξάμενοι κατὰ διαδοχὴν.. παραπέμψατε Wilcken [Refs 4th c.AD+ [“Chr.” 469.5 (4th c.AD)]]; καταπιστεῦσαι Αὐρηλίῳ Πέτρῳ.. σιτομέτρῃ.. ὑποδέξασθαι τὸν δημόσιον σῖτον [Refs 5th c.AD+ [“Sammelb.” 5273.4 (5th c.AD)]], cf. Wilcken [Refs 4th c.AD+ [“Chr.” 434.12 (4th c.AD), “PLips.” 34v. 7, 58.9, +others (4th c.AD), “POxy.” 1899.16, 1982.17 (5th c.AD), “Codex Justinianus [4th-6th c.AD]” 1.5.18.11; τὴν ὑποδοχὴν πᾶσαν τοῦ μακαρίου Ἰούστου αὐτὸς ὑπόδεξαι “POxy.” 1838.1 (6th c.AD)]]; accept (as a liability) a dowry or donatio ante nuptias, [Refs 6th c.AD+ [“Codex Justinianus [4th-6th c.AD]” 5.17.12, 6th c.AD: Justinianus Imperator “Novellae” 22.19.]]

__IV
receive in succession, take up, μέλος [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Supplices” 1022 (Lyric poetry); περαιωθέντας.. λειμὼν ὑποδέχεται 2nd c.AD: Lucianus Sophista “Luct.” 5, compare “VH” 2.44; τὴν εἰς τὸ στόμα φορὰν τῶν περιττωμάτων ὑποδέχεται στόμαχος 2nd c.AD: Galenus Medicus 6.421, compare 432, 18(2).163,176,218]]; ὁ ὑποδεξάμενος the receiver of stolen goods, [Refs [“Catalogus Codicum Astrologorum” 1.96.]]

__IV.2
intransitive, of a place, come next, τὸ πρὸς τὴν ἠῶ θάλασσα ὑποδέκεται καὶ τενάγεα [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 7.176]]; of rank, come next in order, ὅταν πλείονες συνδειπνῶσι,.. μέσος ὁ κράτιστος (i.e. κάθηται), ὁ δ᾽ ὑποδεχόμενος παρ᾽ αὐτόν [Refs 2nd c.BC+ [2nd-1st c.BC: Posidonius Historicus 15J.]]

__IV.3
intercept, ὁ μὲν.. ἐπόρουσεν, ὁ δ᾽ ἐμμαπέως ὑπέδεκτο [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th-7th c.BC: Hesiodus Epicus “Scutum Herculis” 442; ἐν δυσχωρίᾳ [τοὺς πολεμίους] 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 1.6.35]]; of hunters, intercept beaten-up game, [Refs [[prev. work] 2.4.20]]; catch, τὸ πήδημα τῆς σφαίρας [Refs 5th c.BC+ [2nd c.AD(?): Pollianus Epigrammaticus 9.105; ὑπτίαις ταῖς χερσὶ [τὸ μῆλον] 2nd-3rd c.AD: Philostratus Sophista “Philostrati majoris imagines” 1.6; τὸ ἐνθεῦτέν μιν οἱ ἐχθροὶ ὑποδεξάμενοι καὶ ὑπὸ δικαστήριον ἀγαγόντες 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 6.104]]; catch as in a trap, στυγερὸς δ᾽ ὑπεδέξατο κοῖτος a hateful resting-place receives (entraps) them, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 22.470]]; ἔτιγάρ νύ με πῆμ᾽ ὑπέδεκτο still more sorrow was in store for me,[Refs [14.275; ἀκλεής νιν δόξα πρὸς ἀνθρώπων ὑποδέξεται]]will be her lot, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Heraclidae” 624 (Lyric poetry)]]; ὑποδεξαμένης αὐτοὺς πολλῆς ῥύσεως ὕδατος when a rush of water takes them by surprise, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Leges” 944b.]]

__IV.4
catch, collect a liquid, παιδίον θεασάμενος, ἐπειδὴ κατέαξε τὸ σκεῦος, τῷ κοίλῳ τοῦ ψωμίου τὴν φακῆν ὑποδεχόμενον [Refs 3rd c.AD+ [3rd c.AD(?): Diogenes Laertius 6.37]]; of channels, receive, τὸ στόμα τῶν μητρέων οὐχ ὑποδέχεται τὸν γόνον [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Hippocrates Medicus “Aër.” 31; τὴν ἐσομένην τῶν ὑδάτων εἴσροιαν “POxy.” 1409.19 (3rd c.AD)]]; κατεφίλει καὶ ὑπεδέχετο τὰ δάκρυα [Refs 2nd c.BC+ [2nd c.AD(?): Xenophon Ephesius Scriptor Eroticus 1.9; ποταμὸς πάσας ὑποδεχόμενος τὰς ἀνθρωπείας λύμας 2nd c.BC: Polybius Historicus 5.59.11, compare “Geoponica” 12.2.4, +others]]; ἀγγεῖον τὸ μέλλον ὑποδέξεσθαι τὸ ὕδωρ see reading in [Refs 2nd c.BC+ [2nd-1st c.BC(?): Hero Mechanicus “(Spiritalia) Pneumatica” 1.24, compare 30.]]

ὑπο-δέω
[in LXX: 2Ch.28:15, Eze.16:10 (נָעַל) * ;]
to blind under, esp. of foot gear. Most frequently in mid, and pass. with accusative;
__(a) of the foot, ὑποδησάμενοι τ. πόδας, your feet shod: Eph.6:15;
__(b) of that which is put on, σανδάλια: Mrk.6:9, Act.12:8.†

LSJ / STEPBible (TFLSJ)
ὑποδέω,
late Gr. ὑποδέννω [Refs [“Corpus Glossariorum Latinorum”, Dosith.]] K.:— bind or fasten under, ἁμαξίδας ὑ. τῇσι οὐρῇσι, of long-tailed sheep, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 3.113.]]

__II
especially underbind the feet, i. e. shoe, because the ancient sandals or shoes were bound on with straps, [καμήλους] ὑ. καρβατίναις [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Historia Animalium” 499a29, compare 1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus “Pompeius” 24, 2nd c.AD: Pausanias Periegeta 10.25.4]]; so Cobet restores ὑποδῶν τὰ μὲν ὁπλαῖς, for ὑπὸ ποδῶν, in [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Protagoras” 321b]]:—mostly in middle, bind under one's feet, put on shoes, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Aves” 492 (_anapaest meter_), 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Symposium” 220b; ὑποδουμένη]]as I was putting on my shoes, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Ecclesiazusae” 36, compare 4th-3rd c.BC: Theophrastus Philosophus “Characteres” 10.14]]; ὑποδεῖται, for the purpose of going away, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Pherecrates Comicus 153.4 (hexameters)]]; οἱ ἔμπαλιν ὑποδούμενοι (see. ἔμπαλιν [Refs 5th c.BC+ [11.1) 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Theaetetus” 193c; ὑποδούμενος τὸν ἱμάντα.. τῆς ἐμβάδος ἀπέρρηξα 4th-3rd c.BC: Menander Comicus 109.]]

__III
in middle and passive, also, with accusative,

__III.1
of that which one puts on, κοθόρνους ὑποδέεσθαι [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.155, compare 6.125]]; ὑπόδημα[Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. work] 1; τὰς Λακωνικάς 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Ecclesiazusae” 269]]; Σκυθίκαις (Aeolic dialect accusative) [NT+7th c.BC+ [7th-6th c.BC: Alcaeus Lyricus 103; τὰς ἐμβάδας 4th c.BC: Eubulus Comicus 30, compare 5th c.BC: Theopompus Comicus 52; τὰ σανδάλια NT.Act.12.8; compare ὑποδύω 11.1 b:—so in]]perfect passive, ὑποδήματα, βλαύτας ὑποδεδεμένος, with shoes, slippers on one's feet, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Gorgias” 490e, “Smp.” 174a; ἁπλᾶς ὑποδέδενται 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 54.34: _absolutely_, ὑποδεδεμένοι ἐκοιμῶντο]]with their shoes on, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 4.5.14; ὥσπερ ὑποδεδ. 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “de Partibus Animalium” 687a28.]]

__III.2
of the foot, ὑποδεδεμένοι τὸν ἀριστερὸν πόδα with the left foot shod, [NT+5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 3.22, compare 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Fragmenta” 74; θάτερον [πόδα] σανδάλῳ ὑποδεδ. 2nd c.AD: Lucianus Sophista “Hist.Conscr.” 22, compare 2nd-3rd c.AD: Aelianus “Varia Historia” 1.18; ὑποδησάμενοι τοὺς πόδας ἐν ἑτοιμασίᾳ τοῦ εὐαγγελίου NT.Eph.6.15.]]

__IV
ὑποδῆσαι· ἐνεχυρασθῆναι, Ἰταλιῶται, [Refs 5th c.AD+ [5th c.AD(?): Hesychius Legal icographus]]

ὑπόδημ-α, ατος, τό,
(ὑποδέω) sole bound under the foot with straps, sandal, ποσὶν.. ὑποδήματα δοῦσα [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 15.369; ποσὶν.. ὑποδήματα δοίην 18.361, compare 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.195, etc.; ποδὸς ὑ. 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus Alcaeus1.128a, etc.]]; whereas ὑπόδημα κοῖλον is a shoe or half-boot, which covered the whole foot (see. κοῖλος 1.1); ὑπόδημα is sometimes used alone in this sense,[Refs 5th c.BC+ [compare 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Plutus” 983 (and Scholia (at [prev. work])), 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Rhetorica” 1392a32]]; εἰς ὑποδήματα γράφειν put down as paid for shoes, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Lysias Orator 32.20 (_passive_)]]; δεξιὸν εἰς ὑ., ἀριστερὸν εἰς ποδάνιπτρα, of one who is ready for anything, perhaps alluding to Theramenes (see. κόθορνος 3)[Refs 5th c.BC+ [, 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Fragmenta” 914 (perhaps 3rd-2nd c.BC: Aristophanes Byzantinus Philosophus, compare 1st c.BC: Didymus Grammaticus and 2nd c.BC: Polemo Historicus (“fragment” 101 M.) cited in 2nd c.AD(?): Helladius Epigrammaticus cited in 9th c.AD: Photius Legal icographus, etc. “Bibliotheca - Patrologia Graeca” p.533 5th c.BC: Bacchylides Lyricus)]]; similar words are ascribed to [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Pythagoras Philosophus by 4th c.AD: Iamblichus Philosophus “Protrepticus” 21]].ιά (where ὑπόδησις is used); τὸ ὑ. ἔρραψας μὲν σύ, ὑπεδήσατο δὲ Ἀρισταγόρης [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 6.1, compare 4th c.AD: Libanius Sophista “Epistulae” 52; ὁ σπάρτος, ἐξ οὗ πλέκουσιν ὑποδήματα τοῖς ὑποζυγίοις 2nd c.AD: Galenus Medicus 6.502.]]

__B.2
expound, interpret, explain, ὄνειρον [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 19.535, 555; ὀνείρατα 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Vespae” 53, compare 2nd-3rd c.AD: Philostratus Sophista “Vita Apollonii” 2.37, 5th c.BC: Hippocrates Medicus “ἐπιστολαί” 15]]; ὑ. ὅπως.. [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [3rd c.BC: Theocritus Poeta Bucolicus 24.67.]]

Tat., and 4th c.AD: Iamblichus Philosophus, 9th c.AD: Photius Legal icographus, etc. “Bibliotheca - Patrologia Graeca” p.73 5th c.BC: Bacchylides Lyricus]]; ape, mimic, τὸ τῶν Ἰνδῶν ἔργον [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd-3rd c.AD: Philostratus Sophista “Vita Apollonii” 3.4]]; represent in art, Philostr Jun.[Refs 4th c.AD+ [“Im.Prooem.”, compare 4th c.AD: Callistratus Sophista “Statuarum descriptiones” 7.]]

take up a notion, assume, suppose, frequently of an ill-grounded opinion, ὑ. θεῖον εἶναι τὸ ἐπαγγελλόμενον [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 2.55; οὐκ ἂν ὑπέλαβον τοῦτον ἀντειπεῖν 5th c.BC: Antipho Orator 3.3.2, compare 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Phaedo” 86b, “Prt.” 343d; ἐὰν ὑπολάβῃ.. Ἀθήνῃσιν εἶναι, ὢν ἐν Λιβύῃ 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Metaphysica” 1010b10]]: an adverb is frequently added to give the word a good sense, ὀρθῶς ὑ. [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Gorgias” 458e, 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Ethica Nicomachea” 1145b21, καλῶς [prev. author] “Rh.” 1404a1, etc.; βέλτιον ὑπελάβομεν εἶναι πάλιν γράψαι “PCair.Zen.” 36.15 (3rd c.BC): with εἶναι]] omitted, assume or understand a thing to be so and so, τὰ φύματα τεχνικώτατον ὑπειληφέναι (i.e. εἶναι) δεῖ δύνασθαι διαλύειν [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Hippocrates Medicus “περὶ ἰητροῦ” 10]]; τὸ χαλεπὸν κακὸν (i.e. εἶναι) ὑ. [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Protagoras” 341b; ὑ. τὸν Ἔρωτα ἕν τι τῶν ὄντων [prev. author] “Phdr.” 263d]]; ὑ. τι ὡς ὂν.. [Refs [[prev. author] “Prm.” 134c]]; τὸν αἰθέρα τῇδέ πῃ ὑ. conceive of the word αἰθήρ somewhat in this way, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. author] “Cra.” 410b; οὕτως ὑ. περί τινος 5th-6th c.BC: Isocrates Orator 3.26, compare 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 18.269: simply with _accusative_, καίπερ ὑπειληφὼς ταῦτα]] though I assume this to be so, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [[prev. author] 19.3, compare 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Metaphysica” 1005b26; τίς σε ἀναγκάσαι δύναται ὑπολαβεῖν τι ὧν οὐ θέλει; 2nd c.AD: Arrianus Historicus “Epicteti Dissertationes” 2.6.21]]; ὃ βούλει, ὑπολάμβανε[Refs 4th c.BC+ [[prev. work] 1.10.4; ὑ. πλῆθος ὡρισμένον 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Metaphysica” 1073b13]]; ὑ. ὅτι.. [Refs [[prev. author] “Pol.” 1301a25]]:—passive, τοιοῦτος ὑπολαμβάνομαι [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Isocrates Orator 12.5, compare 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Rhetorica” 1366a26; ὑ. μειζόνως ἢ κατὰ τὴν ἀξίαν 5th-6th c.BC: Isocrates Orator 11.24, compare 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 23.6; ἡ ὑπειλημμένη ἀρετή [prev. author] 14.1]]; ὅπως ποθ᾽ ὑπείλημμαι περὶ τούτων ἀρκεῖ μοι I am content with whatever opinion of me has been formed in these matters, [Refs [[prev. author] 18.269]]: with infinitive, τῇ φιλανθρωπίᾳ ἢν ἔχειν ὑπείληψαι παρὰ τοῖς ἀνθρώποις [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Isocrates Orator “Epistulae” 4.9, compare 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Rhetorica” 1383b8]]; ὑπολαμβάνεται δεδωκέναι is understood to have granted, [Refs [[prev. author] “SE” 178a20: τὸ ὑποληφθὲν πᾶν,]] ={πᾶσα ὑπόληψις}[Refs 4th c.BC+ [(11), 4th-3rd c.BC: Menander Comicus 249.7.]]

__III.2
suspect, disbelieve, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Agesilaus” 5.6, unless ὅ τι ὑπολαμβάνουσί τινες ταῦτα οὐκ ἀγνοῶ]] means 'I know how some people regard it'.

__IV
draw away, seduce, ὑ. μισθῷ μείζονι τοὺς ναυβάτας [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 1.121, compare 143; Κέρκυραν [prev. work] 68.]]

__IV.2
take away, remove, seize, τοῖς ἐπικούροις φράσας τὰ ὅπλα ὑπολαβεῖν ordering his bodyguard to remove the arms (of the citizens), [Refs [[prev. author] 6.58.]]

__IV.3
receive, ἀποτίσει.. ὃ ὑπείληφεν.. ἀργυρικὸν κεφάλαιον Mitteis [Refs 1st c.AD+ [“Chr.” 220.21 (1st c.AD),compare “BGU” 709.19 (2nd c.AD).]]

__V
ὑ. ἵππον, as a term of horsemanship, hold up the horse, check him in his course, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “de Equitandi ratione” 7.15, 9.5.]]

ὑπο-λείπω
[in LXX chiefly (pass.) for יָתַר ni., שָׁאַר ni. ;]
to leave remaining (Hom., Thuc., al.): pass., of survivors, Rom.11:3.†
