of sound, make it clear to the ear, make it ring clear, ἀοιδὴν φαίνειν [Refs 4th c.BC+ [8.499; σάλπιγξ.. ὑπέρτονον γήρυμα φαινέτω στρατῷ 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Eumenides” 569.]]

__3
show forth, display in action, ἀρετήν [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 8.237; ἀεικείας 20.309; βίην 8th-7th c.BC: Hesiodus Epicus “Theogonia” 689; εὐμαχανίαν 5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “I.” 4(3).2; εὔνοιαν 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 3.36]]; ὕβριν[Refs 4th c.BC+ [[prev. work] 127; ὀργάς 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Choephori” 326 (Lyric poetry).]]

__3.b
set forth, expound, νοήματα [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 18.295; λόγον 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.116; τριφασίας λόγων ὁδούς [prev. author] 1.95]]; but τὰ λαμπρὰ.. φ. ἔπη make them good, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Coloneus” 721.]]

__4
inform against one, denounce, φανῶ σε (σε φανῶ codices) τοῖς πρυτάνεσι [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Equites” 300 (Lyric poetry), compare “Ach.” 824, 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Antigone” 325]]: denounce a thing as contraband, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Acharnenses” 542, 819, +others; φαίνειν πλοῖον 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 58.9]]; τὰ φανθέντα articles denounced as contraband, [Refs [[prev. work] 13: _absolutely_,]]give information, ὁ φήνας ἢ ὁ γραψάμενος [Refs 5th c.BC+ [“IG” 12.45.3, compare 4.24, 5th-6th c.BC: Isocrates Orator 18.20, 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 1.2.14, 1st c.BC: Philodemus Gadarensis Epigrammaticus “Rh.” 2.207 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus, etc.]]

__5
φαίνειν φρουράν, call up a levy, at Sparta, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Historia Graeca (Hellenica)” 3.2.23, +others]]; also φ. θυσίαν proclaim, order a sacrifice, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Philodamus Scarpheus Lyricus 112:]] —passive, πέφαται θνατοῖσι νίκας ὕστερον εὐφροσύνα has been ordained, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Bacchylides Lyricus 9.52.]]

__II
absolutely, give light, shine, φαίνοντες νύκτας.. δαιτυμόνεσσι [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 7.102, compare 19.25]]; of the sun, moon, etc., φ. τινί [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Nubes” 586 (troch.); εἰς ἅπαντα φ. τὸν οὐρανόν 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Timaeus” 39b; ἀλλά, σελάνα, φαῖνε καλόν 3rd c.BC: Theocritus Poeta Bucolicus 2.11; οἱ λύχνοι φ. ἧττον 4th-3rd c.BC: Theophrastus Philosophus “de Igne” 11]]; compare φάω: so ἦρι μὲν φαίνοντι in spring when it shines forth, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Fragmenta - American Journal of Philology” 304.4 codices (to be read φανέντι)]]; of the Dioscuri shining in mid-air, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Electra” 1234 (_anapaest meter_): _metaphorically_, ἀγανὴ φαίνουσ᾽ ἐλπίς]] soft shining hope, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Agamemnon” 101 (_anapaest meter_, uncertain).]]

__II.b
Φαίνων, οντος, ὁ, the planet Saturn, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “de Mundo” 392a23, 1st c.BC: Cicero, M. Tullius Orator et Philosophus “de Natura Deorum” 2.20.52, etc.; Φ. ὁ τοῦ Ἡλίου 4th c.BC: Eudoxus Astronomus “Ars astronomica” 5.19]]; accusative -ωνα [Refs [“Placita Philosophorum” 2.15.4.]]

__III
Epic dialect iterative φάνεσκε appeared, μετὰ πρώτοισι φάνεσκε [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 11.64; ὑπένερθε δὲ γαῖα φάνεσκε 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 12.242, compare 11.587, 8th-7th c.BC: Hesiodus Epicus “Fragmenta” 14.3.]]

__III.2
perfect [Refs 5th c.BC+ [2 πέφηνα is also used _intransitive_, 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Coloneus” 328, etc.; less frequently in Prose, 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 9.120, 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 3.22, 2nd c.BC: Polybius Historicus 9.13.8.]]

__B
passive, come to light, appear, φάνεν δέ οἱ εὐρέες ὦμοι, being stripped bare, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 18.68, compare 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 22.324, 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 19.39]]: frequently of fire, shine brightly, πυρὰ φαίνετο Ἰλιόθι πρό [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 8.561; ἕκαθεν δέ τε φαίνεται αὐγή 2.456; δεινὼ δέ οἱ ὄσσε φάανθεν]]shone like fire, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 1.200]]: frequently of the rising of heavenly bodies, ἄστρα φαεινὴν ἀμφὶ σελήνην φαίνετ᾽ ἀριπρεπέα [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8.556, compare 8th-7th c.BC: Hesiodus Epicus “Opera et Dies” 598]]; of the first gleam of daybreak, ἦμος δ᾽ ἠριγένεια φάνη ῥοδοδάκτυλος Ἠώς [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 1.477, 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 2.1, +others]]; ἅμ᾽ ἠοῖ φαινομένηφι at break of day, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 9.618, compare 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 4.407, +others; ἀκτὶς ἀελίου, τὸκάλλιστον.. φανὲν.. τῶν προτέρων φάος, ἐφάνθης ποτ᾽ 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Antigone” 100 (Lyric poetry)]]: of a rising wind, οὐδέ ποτ᾽ οὖροι πνείοντες φαίνονθ᾽ ἁλιαέες [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 4.361]]; of a vapour, ἐκ νεφέων ἐρεβεννὴ φ. ἀήρ [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 5.864.]]

__B.2
of persons, οἴῳ φαινομένη appearing to him alone, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 1.198, compare 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 15.517, etc.; ἐφάνη λὶς εἰς ὁδόν 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 15.275]]; οὗπερ κἀφάνης where thou didst first appear, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Coloneus” 77; χρόνιος φανείς [prev. author] “Ph.” 1446 (_anapaest meter_)]]; ὁδόν φανῆναι a pregnant expression for ἐλθεῖν ὁδὸν ὥστε φανῆναι, [Refs [[prev. author] “El.” 1274 (Lyric poetry); κέλευθον φανείς “Aj.” 878 (Lyric poetry)]]; πόθεν φαίν; whence come you? [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Protagoras” 309a, 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Memorabilia” 2.8.1]]; οὐδαμοῦ φ. is nowhere to be seen, [Refs [[prev. author] “An.” 1.10.16.]]

__B.2.b
come into being, φανεὶς δύστηνος born to misery, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Coloneus” 974, compare 1225 (Lyric poetry)]]; become, ἐκ βασιλέως ἰδιώτην φανῆναι [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 7.7.28; δυοῖν ἐφάνη τριήραρχος 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 18.104]]; to be made out, δοῦλος λόγοισιν.. φανείς [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Ajax” 1020, compare 1241.]]

__B.3
of events, come about, τέλος οὔ πώ τι πέφανται [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 2.122; φάνη βιότοιο τελευτή 7.104]]; ἔργον, ἄεθλον, etc.,[Refs 8th c.BC+ [16.207, 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 21.106, etc.; τὸ φανθέν 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Trachiniae” 743]]; of sayings, to be set forth, λόγος ἀρχαῖος φανείς[Refs [[prev. work] 1, compare “OT” 474 (Lyric poetry), 848.]]

__B.II
appear to be so and so, with infinitive, δμῳάων ἥ τίς τοι ἀρίστη φαίνεται εἶναι [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 15.25, compare 11.336; οὐ γάρ σφιν ἐφαίνετο κέρδιον εἶναι 14.355; τοῦτό μοι θειότατον φαίνεται γενέσθαι 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 7.137; εὖ σὺ λέγειν φαίνει 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Nubes” 403 (_anapaest meter_), compare 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Prometheus Vinctus” 319, etc.]]: frequently with infinitive omitted, οὗ καὶ πρόσθεν ἀρίστη φαίνετο βουλή [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 9.94, compare 2.5; ὅς τις φαίνηται ἄριστος 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 14.106; σμερδαλέος αὐτῇσι φάνη 6.137; ἕρμαιον ἂν ἐφάνη 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 368d, etc.: but in 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus, etc.,]] also with participle, to be manifest: thus, ἐμοὶ σὺ πλουτέειν μέγα φαίνεαι you appear to me to be very rich, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.32]]; but εὔνοος ἐφαίνετο ἐών he was manifestly well-inclined, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. author] 7.173, compare 175, 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 1.2]]; οὐκ ἄκαιρα φαίνεται λέγειν he appears to be speaking.., [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Prometheus Vinctus” 1036]]; but φανέονται λέγοντες οὐδέν it will be manifest that they talk nonsense, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 3.35; φαίνομαι δύο καθορᾶν εἴδη 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Sophista” 235d; but οὐκ ἂν φανεῖμεν πήματ᾽ ἔρξαντες 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Persae” 786; πλαγκτὸς οὖσ᾽ ἐφαινόμην [prev. author] “Ag.” 593, compare 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 9.89, 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Andromache” 343; ἐφάνησαν πεπονθότες 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Apologia” 22c: with]]participle omitted, πέφανται ἁρματηλάτας σοφός (i.e. ὤν) [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “P.” 5.115, compare “N.” 6.14; κρατηθεὶς ἡμερώτερος φανεῖ 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Agamemnon” 1632]]; Κᾶρες ἐφάνησαν (i.e. ὄντες) they were seen to be Carians, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 1.8]]; τί φαίνομαι (i.e. ὤν) δῆτ; what do I look like? [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Bacchae” 925; ὡς ἀγαθοὶ.. ἐφάνησαν 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 408a: hence φαίνεσθαι, opposed to εἶναι, εἶναι μὲν ὅσπερ εἰμί, φαίνεσθαι δὲ μή 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Fragmenta” 698 (cited in 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Acharnenses” 441); στρατηγὸς ἀγαθὸς μὴ ὢν φαίνεσθαι 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Memorabilia” 1.7.3; ὀλίγοι καὶ ὄντες καὶ φαινόμενοι [prev. author] “HG” 6.5.28.]]

__B.II.2
in Philosophy, φαίνομαι (absolutely) is sometimes used of what appears to the senses, φαίνεται δ᾽ οὐδὲν is observed, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Physica” 204b35, compare “Cael.” 312b30; φ. κατὰ τὴν αἴσθησιν [prev. author] “GA” 716a31]]: sometimes of what is mentally manifest, [Refs [[prev. author] “EN” 1175a29]]; to be evident, [Refs [[prev. author] “APr.” 24b24]]: especially appear to the imagination [Refs 5th c.BC+ [compare (φαντασία 2), 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Sophista” 264b; φ. καὶ μύουσιν ὁράματα 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “de Anima” 428a16; φ. δέ τι.. οἷον τὰ ἐν τοῖς ὕπνοις [prev. work] a7: distinguished from αἰσθάνεσθαι and δοξάζειν, [prev. work] b1]]: especially in participle φαινόμενος, η, ον:

__B.II.2.a
appearing in sense experience, τὰ φ. κατὰ τὴν αἴσθησιν [Refs [[prev. author] “Cael.” 303a22, +others; εἴτε τὰ δοκοῦντα πάντα ἐστὶν ἀληθῆ καὶ τὰ φ. [prev. author] “Metaphorical” 1009a8, compare “de An.” 404a29 (_sing._); τὰ φ.]]sense-data, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [[prev. author] “PA” 639b8, 4th-3rd c.BC: Epicurus Philosophus “Epistulae” 1pp.9,10 U., +others: Astron., τὰ φ.]] = celestial phenomena, title of a work by Eudoxus, versified by Aratus, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [2nd c.BC: Hipparchus Astronomicus 1.1.8, compare 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “de Caelo” 293b27; πρός τινας δόξας αὑτῶν τὰ φ. προσέλκοντες [prev. work] 293a26]]: generally, τὸ μὴ ἐκ φαινομένων τὸ βλεπόμενον γεγονέναι [NT.Heb.11.3.]

__B.II.2.b
mentally apparent, opposed to ὄντα τῇ ἀληθείᾳ, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 596e, compare 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Topica” 100b24, “EN” 1113a24; τὰ οὖν ἐμοὶ φαινόμενα οὕτω φαίνεται 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 517b; [νοῦς] τῶν φ. θειότατον 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Metaphysica” 1074b16]]; τὸ φ. εἰπεῖν to express one's opinion, [Refs 1st c.AD+ [1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus 2.158c]]: hence, specious, fallacious, φ. ἐνθυμήματα, opposed to ὄντα, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Rhetorica” 1402a28.]]

__B.II.2.c
τὰ φ. what is to be seen, show, [Refs 4th c.AD+ [4th c.AD: Libanius Sophista “Orationes” 30.28.]]

__B.II.3
frequently in answers in Plato's dialogue, φαίνεται, yes, Prt.[Refs [332e, “R.” 333c, +others; ὥς γέ μοι φ. “Prt.” 324d, compare “R.” 383a, +others]]: [τοῦτο] φῂς εἶνα; Answ. φαίνομαι (i.e. λέγειν) [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Memorabilia” 4.2.20.]]

__B.II.3.b
later impersonal with dative person et infinitive, it seems good, ἐάν σοι φαίνηται Wilcken [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [“Chr.” 304.11 (3rd c.BC),compare “PCair.Zen.” 44.7, 16 (3rd c.BC)]], etc.; ὁπότε αὐτῷ φανείη στρατιὰν ἐξάγειν [Refs 1st c.BC+ [1st c.BC: Dionysius Halicarnassensis 2.14, compare 4.85.]]

__B.II.4
joined with δοκέω, εἰ δὴ κακός τε φ. δοκῶ τέ σοι [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Hippolytus” 1071; δοκοῖμεν ἂν.. χείρους φαίνεσθαι 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 1.122, compare 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Phaedrus” 269d, “Erx.” 399c, 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Memorabilia” 2.1.22.]]

__B.II.5
οὐδαμοῦ φαίνεσθαι 'to be nowhere', metaphorically from racing, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Phaedo” 72c, compare “Grg.” 456b, 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 18.310.]]

__B.III
τὰ φανθέντα, see above [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus 1.4.]]

φανερός, -ά, -όν
(φαίνομαι) [in LXX: Deu.29:29 (28) (גָּלָה ni.), Pro.14:4, Sir.6:22, al. ;]
open to sight, visible, manifest: Gal.5:19; before ἐν, Rom.1:19, 1Jn.3:10; with dative of person(s), Act.4:16 7:13, 1Ti.4:15; φ. γίνεσθαι (in LXX for בָּחַן ni., Gen.42:16), Mrk.6:14, Luk.8:17, 1Co.3:13 14:25; id. before ἐν, 1Co.11:19, Php.1:13; φ. ποιεῖν, Mat.12:16, Mrk.3:12; εἰς φ. ἐλθεῖν (cf. Bl., § 47, 2), Mrk.4:22, Luk.8:17; ἐν τῷ φ. (opposite to ἐν τ. κρυπτῷ), Rom.2:28.†
SYN.: see: δῆλος  (AS)

LSJ / STEPBible (TFLSJ)
φᾰνερός, ά, όν,
but ός, όν, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Bacchae” 991 (Lyric poetry)]]: (φαίνω):— visible, manifest, ἡ στήλη ἔχει πάντα φ., i.e. all that is in it can be plainly seen, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 3.24; φ. ὄμμασιν ἐμοῖς 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Bacchae” 501; φ. τι δεῖξαι 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Trachiniae” 608 (variant); θήσω φανέρ᾽ ἀθρό᾽ 5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “O.” 13.98; φ. ποιῆσαι 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Leges” 630b, etc.; ἐς φ. ὄψιν βαίνειν 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Electra” 1236 (_anapaest meter_); τοὔργον παρέσται φ. 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Philoctetes” 1291; φ. χαρακτὴρ ἀρετᾶς 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Hercules Furens” 658 (Lyric poetry); φ. πηγαί 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 2.15; ἐσβολαὶ ἐς Αἴγυπτον 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 3.5; φ. ἔχθραν κτήσασθαι 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 1.42; διαφορὰ φ. ἐγένετο [prev. work] 102]]; φ. θάνατος, ὄλεθρος, opposed to ἀφανής, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Antipho Orator 3.3.7, 5th-6th c.BC: Andocides Orator 1.53; φ. ὑποψία εἰς ἐμὲ ἰοῦσα 5th c.BC: Antipho Orator 2.2.6; φ. γενόμενος]]if detected, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Lysias Orator 7.12:]] — Constr.: φανερός εἰμι with participle, ἀπικόμενοι φανεροί εἰσι they are known to have come, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 3.26; ἐπισπεύδων φανερὸς ἦν [prev. author] 7.18; ὁ μέν ἐστι φ. ἐκβὰς ἐκ τοῦ πλοίου καὶ οὐκ εἰσβὰς πάλιν 5th c.BC: Antipho Orator 5.23: followed by _conjunction_, φανεροὶ γιγνόμενοι ὅτι ποιοῦσιν 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 2.2.12; φ. ἦν ὅπως ἐγίγνωσκεν [prev. author] “Mem.” 1.1.17: _impersonal_, φανερόν [ἐστιν] ὅτι.. [prev. work] 3.9.2]]; εἰ φανερὸν γίγνοιτο ὅτι.. [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Phaedo” 70d.]]

__2
shining, illustrious, προεδρίη [Refs 6th c.BC+ [6th c.BC: Xenophanes Poeta Philosophus 2.7; ὁδός 5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “O.” 6.73]]; conspicuous, remarkable, φ. μηδὲν κατεργάζεσθαι [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 1.17.]]

__3
φ. οὐσία real property, opposed to personalty (ἀφανής), [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Lysias Orator 32.4, “fragment” 79, 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 50.8.]]

__3.b

LSJ / STEPBible (TFLSJ)
φάσκω,
used by Epic dialect only in imperfect ἔφασκον [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 13.100]]; Epic dialect φάσκον [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 24.75, 8th-7th c.BC: Hesiodus Epicus “Theogonia” 209: frequently in Trag. and Comedy texts (but perhaps never in _present_ _indicative_, see below)]]: as imperfect of φημί [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Tyrannus” 110, etc., also 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Ranae” 742; also _imperative_ φάσκε 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Helena” 1077, 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Rhetorica ad Alexandrum” 1429a6]]; subjunctive φάσκω [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Choephori” 93, 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Vespae” 561 (_anapaest meter_), 5th c.BC: Antipho Orator 3.4.3, 5th c.BC: Lysias Orator 25.11, 4th c.BC: Isaeus Orator 10.11, “PHal.” 1.134 (3rd c.BC)]]; optative φάσκοιμι [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Ajax” 1037, 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 30.27]]; infinitive φάσκειν [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Electra” 9, “OT” 462, “Ph.” 1411 (_anapaest meter_), 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Ranae” 695 (troch.), 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Memorabilia” 1.2.52, +others, 5th-6th c.BC: Isocrates Orator 8.1]]; participle φάσκων [Refs 5th c.BC+ [“IG” 12.66.6, 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Hercules Furens” 1382]] (the only part of the Verb used in [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus (3.70) and 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus (“R.” 337e, +others), except ἔφασκεν [prev. author] “Lg.” 901a)]]:—passive is not found, ἐφάσκετ᾽ is for ἐφάσκετε [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Philoctetes” 114]]. Rare in present indicative [Refs 4th c.BC+ [before 3rd c.BC: φάσκει 4th c.BC: Isaeus Orator 6.16 (φάσκοι Reiske, Wyse), “PMich.Zen.” 82.6 (3rd c.BC), “PSI” 8.921.7 (2nd c.AD), uncertain in 2nd c.AD: Sextus Empiricus Philosophus “Πυρρώνειοι ὑποτυπώσεις” 1.17 (variant{φάσκοι}), 2nd c.AD: Galenus Medicus 15.35, “Geoponica” 9.14.2, 5th c.AD(?): Hesychius Legal icographus; φάσκεις “PSI” 9.1011.10 (3rd c.BC)]]; φάσκουσι (ν) [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aeschines Orator “Epistulae” 11.11, “PCair.Zen.” 21.25, 244.5, +others (3rd c.BC), 1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus “Antonius” 86, 2nd c.AD: Athenaeus Epigrammaticus 10.429b, “Geoponica” 5.2.9, etc.]]; φάσκομεν is uncertain conjecture (for πάσχομεν) in [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd c.AD: Alexander Rhetor 146.4]]:—say, affirm, assert, with accusative et infinitive, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 4.191, 8.565, +others]]; φάσκειν as imperative, in this construction, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Tyrannus” 462, “Ph.” 1411 (_anapaest meter_)]]; οὐ φασκόντων χρήσειν saying they would not.., [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 3.58; οὐ φάσκων ἀνεκτὸν εἶναι 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 8.52]]; the infinitive is frequently to be supplied, ἐν τῇδ᾽ ἔφασκε γῇ (i.e. εὑρεθήσεσθαι) [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Tyrannus” 110]]; φησίν γε· φάσκων δ᾽ (i.e. ἥξειν) [Refs [[prev. author] “El.” 319]]; τῶν φασκόντων γονέων (i.e. εἶναι) [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 538a, etc.]]; rarely φ. ὡς.., ὅτι.., [Refs 5th c.BC+ [2nd c.BC: Moschus Bucolicus 2.12, 1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus 2.215f: with _accusative_, τοῦτο φ. τοὔπος 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Choephori” 93, compare 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Hercules Furens” 1382, etc.: _absolutely_, ὡς ἔφασκεν 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Tyrannus” 114; φάσκουσα καὶ οὐ φάσκουσα 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Theaetetus” 190a.]]

__2
think, deem, expect, ὃ οὔ ποτ᾽ ἔγωγε τελευτήσεσθαι ἔφασκον [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 13.100; οὔ μ᾽ ἐφάσκεθ᾽.. οἴκαδ᾽ ἱκέσθαι 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 22.35]]; φάσκειν.. ὁρᾶν believe that you see, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Electra” 9.]]

__3
say, promise, with infinitive future, με.. ἔφασκε θήσειν ἀθάνατον [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 7.256; φάσκων προσποιήσειν αὐτήν 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 2.85, compare 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Ion” 541e.]]

φάτν-η, ἡ,
manger, crib, [ἵππους] ἀτίταλλ᾽ ἐπὶ φάτνῃ [NT+8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 5.271; ἵππος ἀκοστήσας ἐπὶ φ. 6.506; ἵππους μὲν κατέδησαν.. φάτνῃ ἐφ᾽ ἱππείῃ 10.568; ἐϋξέστῃ ἐπὶ φ. 24.280; ἡ φ. τῶν ἵππων 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 9.70, compare 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Bacchae” 510 (_plural_), 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 3.3.27 (_plural_), NT.Luke.2.7, +others]]; φάτναι Ζηνὸς, of the manger of Pegasus, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “O.” 13.92]]: also of oxen, ὥς τίς τε κατέκτανε βοῦν ἐπὶ φ. [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 4.535, 11.411.]]

__2
βοῦς ἐπὶ φ., proverbial of ease and comfort, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [2nd-3rd c.AD: Philostratus Sophista “Philostrati majoris imagines” 2.10; also πλουσίαν ἔχειν φ. 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Fragmenta” 378; φάτναις ἀργυραῖς χρῆσθαι 1st c.BC-1st c.AD: Strabo Geographus 3.2.14]]; ἡ ἐν τῇ φ. κύων 'the dog in the manger', [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd c.AD: Lucianus Sophista “Tim.” 14, compare “Anthologia Graeca” 12.236 (2nd c.AD: Strato Epigrammaticus)]]; θεραπεύειν τὴν φ. τινός to court one who feeds you, [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd-3rd c.AD: Aelianus “Fragmenta” 107; τοὺς ἐκ τῆς αὐτῆς οἱονεὶ φ. ἐδηδοκότας [prev. work] 39: τὴν αὐτὴν φ. ζητεῖν]] to return to their old haunts, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Eubulus Comicus 129.]]

__II
={φάτνωμα}[Refs 3rd c.BC+ [1, “IG” 11(2).161 A 46 (Delos, 3rd c.BC): _plural_, [prev. work]42(1).109 iii 85, +others (Epid., 3rd c.BC), 1st c.BC: Diodorus Siculus Historicus 1.66.]]

socket of tooth, [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd c.AD(?): Pollianus Epigrammaticus 2.93.]]

Abbott-Smith / STEPBible (TBESG)
φαῦλος, -η, -ον
[in LXX: Pro.22:8 (עֶוֶל) Pro.29:9 (אֱוִיל), etc. ;]
slight, worthless, of no account, both of persons and things in various shades of meaning (see LS, see word), in NT, as frequently in cl., always with distinct moral reference (see Ellic., Past. Epp., 203; Hort, Ja., 85; Tr., Syn., LXXxiv), worthless, bad: Jhn.3:20, Tit.2:8, Jas.3:16; opposite to ἀγαθός (which see), Jhn.5:29, Rom.9:11, 2Co.5:10.†
SYN.: see: ἄθεσμος  (AS)

---

LSJ / STEPBible (TFLSJ)
φαῦλος, η, ον,
also ος, ον [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Hippolytus” 435, “fragment” 1083.9, 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 6.21: (compare φλαῦρος)]]:— cheap, easy, slight, paltry, first found commonly in [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus, twicein 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.26, 126 (_comparative_, elsewhereφλαῦρος), six times in 3rd c.AD: Democritus Epigrammaticus, “fragment” 87, +others, twice in 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus, “Frr.” 41,771:]] adverb φαύλως[Refs 4th c.BC+ [once in 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus: 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Persae” 520.]]

__I
of things, easy, slight, φ. ἀθλήσας πόνον [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Supplices” 317]]; φαυλότατον ἔργον ''tis as easy as lying', [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Equites” 213; φ. πρᾶγμα [prev. author] “Lys.” 14; τὸ ζήτημα οὐ φ. 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 368c; φ. ἐρώτημα [prev. author] “Phlb.” 19a; φαῦλον αὐτοῖς προστάξομεν [prev. author] “R.” 423c: frequently with negative, οὐ φ., ἀλλὰ χαλεπὸν πιστεῦσαι [prev. work] 527d; μάχη οὐ φ. [prev. author] “Tht.” 179d; οὐ φ. τέχνη [prev. author] “Sph.” 223c]]; οὔτοι βασιλέα φαῦλόν [ἐστι] κτανεῖν 'tis no slight matter to kill a king, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Electra” 760]]; νυκτὸς γὰρ οὔτι φ. ἐμβαλεῖν στρατόν no easy matter, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [[prev. author] “Rh.” 285; οὐ φ. πληγαί 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 54.13; φιλοῦσιν ἰατροὶ λέγειν τὰ φαῦλα μείζω 4th-3rd c.BC: Menander Comicus 497]]; φαῦλα ἐπιφέρειν bring paltry charges, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.26]]; τὰ φ. νικήσας ἔχω have gained petty victories, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Fragmenta” 41 (wrongly glossed by μέγα in 9th c.AD: Photius Legal icographus, etc., 10th c.AD: Suidas Legal icographus, and “Etymologicum Magnum” 789.43, cf. Hsch)]]; σύμμαχον Τροίᾳ μολόντα Ῥῆσον οὐ φαύλῳ τρόπῳ, i. e. with no trivial force, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Rhesus” 599; παρὰ φαῦλον ποιεῖσθαί τι 1st c.BC: Dionysius Halicarnassensis “Ars Rhetorica” 4.2, compare 4th c.AD: Libanius Sophista “Orationes” 14.26.]] adverb -λως εὑρεῖν, τυχεῖν,[Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Equites” 404 (troch.), 509 (_anapaest meter_); φ. πάνυ [prev. author] “Lys.” 566 (_anapaest meter_)]]; φ. ἐκφυγεῖν to get off easily, [Refs [[prev. author] “Ach.” 215 (Lyric poetry); φ. ἀποδράς [prev. author] “Th.” 711 (Lyric poetry); φαυλότατα καὶ ῥᾷστα [prev. author] “Nu.” 778]]; οὔτι φαύλως ἦλθε with no trivial force, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Phoenissae” 112; φ. βοηθήσειν 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 15.13; φαύλως καὶ γλίσχρως παρείχοντο χρήματα “Hellenica Oxyrhynchia” 14.2]]; τὰς ἐλπίδας φ. ἔχειν to be slight, [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd c.AD: Herodianus Grammaticus 1.3.1.]]

__I.2
simple, ordinary, δίαιτα [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Hippocrates Medicus “περὶ ἀγμῶν” 36, “Art.” 49, Eur. “fragment” 213.4; σῖτα καὶ ποτὰ φαυλότατα 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Memorabilia” 1.6.2, compare 5th c.BC: Hippocrates Medicus “περὶ διαίτης” 3.68 (_comparative_)]]; but frequently with sense poor, indifferent, στρατιά [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 6.21]]; ἀσπίδες, τείχισμα, παρασκευή, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. author] 4.9.115, 6.31; ἱμάτιον 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus [prev. cited]]] adverb -λως, διατρίβειν ἐν φιλοσοφίᾳ [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Theaetetus” 173c; μὴ φ. μηδὲ ἰδιωτικῶς [prev. author] “Lg.” 966e.]]

__I.3
mean, bad, πρῆξις [NT+5th c.BC+ [3rd c.AD: Democritus Epigrammaticus 177; λόγοι 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Andromache” 870, ψόγος [prev. author] “Ph.” 94 (perhaps both in signification 1.1 and in 1.3); οὐ φ. ὄψις 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 519a; φ. δόξα 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 24.205; τὰ πράγματ᾽ ἐστὶ φ. [prev. author] 19.30; φαῦλα διαπεπραγμένος 4th-3rd c.BC: Philemo Comicus 229; ὁ φαῦλα πράττων NT.John.3.20; μηδὲ πραξάντων τι ἀγαθὸν ἢ φ. NT.Rom.9.11; τὸ φ.]]evil, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Iphigenia Taurica” 390]]; τὰ φ., opposed to τὰ ἀγαθά, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Symposium” 4.47]]; τύχη φ., opposed to ἀγαθή, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Physica” 197a26, compare “Metaphorical” 1065a35; τὴν πόλιν μηθὲμ φ. παθεῖν “OGI” 765.35 (from Priene)]]; κομίσασθαι.. εἴτε ἀγαθὸν εἴτε φ., of rewards and punishments, [NT+2nd c.AD+ [NT.2Cor.5.10; φ. μαίωσις 2nd c.AD: Soranus Medicus 2.17, compare 1.91, +others]]

__II
of persons, low in rank, mean, common, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Fragmenta” 688]]; οἱ φαυλότατοι the commonest sort (of soldiers), [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 7.77]]; [γάμος] ὁ ἐκ τῶν φαυλοτέρων, opposed to ἐκ μειζόνων, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Hiero” 1.27, compare 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 475b]]; of outward looks, αἱ φαυλότεραι the plainer ones, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Ecclesiazusae” 617, compare 626 (_comparative_, both _anapaest meter_).]]

__II.2
inefficient, bad, διδάσκαλος [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Fragmenta” 771.3]]; τὸ φ. καὶ τὸ μέσον καὶ τὸ πάνυ ἀκριβές the inefficient, the middling, and the perfect, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 6.18]]; φ. αὐλητής, opposed to ἀγαθός, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Protagoras” 327c; τοξότης [prev. author] “Tht.” 194a; οὐ δὲ φαύλων ἀνδρῶν οὐδὲ τῶν ἐπιτυχόντων [prev. author] “Cra.” 390d]]; opposed to σπουδαῖος, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Isocrates Orator 1.1, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Leges” 757a, etc.]]; especially in point of education and accomplishments, opposed to σοφός, οἱ γὰρ ἐν σοφοῖς φαῦλοι παρ᾽ ὄχλῳ μουσικώτεροι λέγειν [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Hippolytus” 989, compare “Ph.” 496, “Ion” 834, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Symposium” 174c, Alcaeus1.129a; τὸ πλῆθος τὸ -ότερον 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Bacchae” 431 (Lyric poetry)]]; οἱ -ότεροι, opposed to to οἱ ξυνετώτεροι, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 3.37]]; οἱ φαυλότεροι γνώμην[Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. work] 83; τὰ γράμματα φαῦλοι 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Phaedrus” 242c]] (so in adverb, φαυλοτέρως πεπαιδευμένοι [Refs [[prev. author] “Lg.” 876d)]]; generally, inferior, [Refs [[prev. author] “Grg.” 483c]]: with infinitive, φαῦλοι μάχεσθαι [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Iphigenia Taurica” 305]]; φ. λέγειν, φ. διαλεχθῆναι, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Theaetetus” 181b, “Prt.” 336c: of animals, φ. κύων 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 26.22; φαυλότατοι ἵπποι 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Memorabilia” 4.1.3.]]

__II.3
careless, thoughtless, indifferent, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Medea” 807:]] —especially in  adverb, φαύλως ἐκρίνατε judged lightly, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Persae” 520; φ. εὕδειν 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Rhesus” 769; οὐχ ὧδε φ. [prev. author] “Ion” 1546]]; φ. παραινεῖν off-hand, [Refs [[prev. author] “HF” 89]]; λόγισαι φαύλως μὴ ψήφοις ἀλλ᾽ ἀπὸ χειρός off-hand, roughly, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Vespae” 656]] (anapaest meter); φ. εἰπεῖν casually, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 449c]]; φ. φέρειν to bear lightly, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Iphigenia Aulidensis” 850, 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Aves” 961.]]

__II.4
in good sense, simple, unaffected, φαῦλον, ἄκομψον, τὰ μέγιστ᾽ ἀγαθόν [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Fragmenta” 473 (_anapaest meter_), compare 3rd c.AD(?): Diogenes Laertius 3.63]]. adverb -λως, παιδεύειν τινά by a very simple method, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Oeconomicus” 13.4; φ. καὶ βραχέως ἀποκρίνασθαι 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Theaetetus” 147c.]]

__II.5

φέγγος, -ους, τό

LSJ / STEPBible (TFLSJ)
φέγγος, εος, τό,
light, splendour, lustre, τῆλε δὲ φ. ἀπὸ χροὸς ἀθανάτοιο λάμπε θεᾶς [LXX+4th c.BC+ [“hymnus ad Cererem” 278; τὸ φ. τῆς χρόας 4th-3rd c.BC: Duris Epigrammaticus 14 1st c.AD: Josephus Historicus; τὸ φ. τῆς δόξης Κυρίου LXX.Eze.10.4]]; φ. ἀστραπῆς ὅπλων[LXX.Hab.3.11]: frequently like{φάος}, of daylight, either absolutely or with some word added, φ. ἡλίου [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Persae” 377, 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Trachiniae” 606, etc.; τὸ φ. τοῦ θεοῦ 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Alcestis” 722]]; without the Article, φ. εἰσορᾶν θεοῦ [Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. author] “Or.” 1025, compare 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Ajax” 673]]; ὦ φέγγος[Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. work] 859, 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Electra” 866; ὦ φ. ἡμέρας 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Agamemnon” 1577; δεκάτῳ φέγγει ἔτους in the tenth year, [prev. work] 504.]]

__b
moonlight, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Cynegeticus” 5.4]]; νυκτερινὰ φέγγη, opposed to ἡμερινὸν φῶς, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 508c; ἐὰν τὸ φ. ἐκλείψῃ “Catalogus Codicum Astrologorum” 4.172, compare 4th-5th c.AD(?): Nonnus Epicus “Dionysiaca” 38.255; φῶς ἡμέρας, φέγγος σελήνης 5th c.AD(?): Hesychius Legal icographus]] see at {φέγγο; τὸ φ. [τοῦ γάλακτος}], of the milky way, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Meteorologica” 346a26.]]

__c
of men, φ. ἰδεῖν, προσιδεῖν, to see the light, come into the world, ἐπεὶ πάμπρωτον εἶδον φ. [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “P.” 4.111; ἀελίου προσιδεῖν φ. 5th c.BC: Bacchylides Lyricus 5.162; λιπεῖν φ. 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Orestes” 954; ὄλωλα, φ. οὐκέτ᾽ ἔστι μοι 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Trachiniae” 1144.]]

__d
day, τριταῖον ἤδη φ. [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Hecuba” 32, compare 2nd c.BC: Sosiphanes Tragicus 3.1]]; μοιρίδιον φ. ={μ. ἦμαρ}, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Eleg.” 2.]]

__2
the light of torches or fire, φ. λαμπάδων [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Eumenides” 1022]]; πυρός[Refs [[prev. work] 1029, “Ch.” 1037]]: a light, torch, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Ranae” 448, 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Symposium” 1.9]]; plural φέγγη torches or watch-fires, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aeneas Tacticus 10.26 (conjecture), 1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus “Camillus” 25, etc.]]

__3
the light of the eyes, φ. ὀμμάτων [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Hecuba” 368, 1035; ὄσσων 3rd c.BC: Theocritus Poeta Bucolicus 24.75]]; τυφλὸν φ, i.e. blindness, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Hecuba” 1068 (Lyric poetry).]]

__II
light, as a metaphorically for delight, glory, pride, joy, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “P.” 8.97, “N.” 3.64, 4.13; τί γὰρ γυναικὶ τούτου φ. ἥδιον δρακεῖν, ἀπὸ στρατείας ἀνδρὶ σώσαντος θεοῦ πύλας ἀνοῖξα; 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Agamemnon” 602]]; of persons, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “N.” 9.42; μέγα βροτοῖσι φ. Ἀσκληπιόν 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Plutus” 640 (Lyric poetry); Μουσέων φ. Ὅμηρον “Anthologia Graeca” 7.6 (Antip. Sid.); ὦ ταῖς ἱεραῖς φ. Ἀθήναις 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Equites” 1319 (_anapaest meter_); πλοῦτος.. ἀνδρὶ φ. 5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “O.” 2.56]]; φ. ὀπώρας, of wine, [Refs [[prev. author] “fragment” 153.]]

__II.2
lustre, δικαιοσύνης καὶ σωφροσύνης [LXX+5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Phaedrus” 250b; φ. ἐλέους LXX.3Mac.6.4; τῆς ψυχῆς τὸ γάνωμα καὶ τὸ φ. 1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus 2.792a, etc.]]

Abbott-Smith / STEPBible (TBESG)
φείδομαι
[in LXX for חָמַל, חוּס, חָשַׂךְ, etc. ;]
to spare: 2Co.13:2; with genitive of person(s), Act.20:29, Rom.8:32 11:21, 1Co.7:28, 2Co.1:23, 2Pe.2:4-5; with inf., to forbear, 2Co.12:6.†

LSJ / STEPBible (TFLSJ)
φείδομαι,
[Refs 6th c.BC+ [6th c.BC: Anacreon Lyricus 101, etc.:]]imperfect φείδοντο (without augment) even in [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Electra” 716]] after a diphthong at the end of the preceding line: future φείσομαι [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Acharnenses” 312 (troch.), 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Apologia” 31a, etc.]], Epic dialect πεφῐδήσομαι [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 15.215]], later future passive in middle sense φ[ε]ισθήσομαι [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [“PUniv.Giss.” 21.6 (2nd c.AD)]]: aorist 1 ἐφεισάμην [Refs 6th c.BC+ [6th c.BC: Solon Lyricus 32.1, 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Septem contra Thebas” 412, 5th-6th c.BC: Andocides Orator 2.11, etc.]], Epic dialect 3rd.pers. singular φείσατο [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 24.236: _Epic dialect_ reduplicate]]aorist 2 πεφῐδόμην, used by [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Homerus Epicus in _optative_ πεφῐδοίμην, πεφίδοιτο, 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 9.277, 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 20.464]], infinitive πεφιδέσθαι [Refs [21.101]]: perfect participle πεφεισμένος [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd c.AD: Lucianus Sophista “Hist.Conscr.” 59 (in middle sense, 2nd-3rd c.AD: Dio Cassius Historicus 50.20)]]; Epic dialect imperative πεφίδησο [Refs [“IG” 14.1363.16]]; participle πεφιδημένος [Refs 4th c.AD+ [4th-5th c.AD(?): Nonnus Epicus “Dionysiaca” 12.392]]:—spare:

__I
spare persons and things, e.g. in war, i.e. not destroy them, with genitive, Τρώων [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 21.101; ἀνδρός 24.158, compare 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 9.277, 22.54, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Apologia” 31a; Ἰλίου 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 15.215; Ἄρης οὐκ ἀγαθῶν φ. 6th c.BC: Anacreon Lyricus [same place]; ἀπ᾽ ἀνδρῶν ὧν Ἄρης ἐφείσατο 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Septem contra Thebas” 412; γῆς πατρίδος 6th c.BC: Solon Lyricus]] [same place]; μὴ φείσῃ βίου spare not my life, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Philoctetes” 749; μὴ φείδεσθε.. στρατοῦ [prev. author] “Aj.” 844; φ. μήτε ἰδίου μήτε δημοσίου οἰκοδομήματος 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 1.90, compare 3.74]]: absolutely, spare, be merciful, [Refs [[prev. work] 59.]]

__II
spare persons and things in using them, use sparingly, ἵππων φειδόμενος, i. e. taking care of them, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 5.202; πίθου μεσσόθι φ. 8th-7th c.BC: Hesiodus Epicus “Opera et Dies” 369]]; φ. ὃν εἶχε βίον (βίον by attraction to the relative) [Refs 6th c.BC+ [6th c.BC: Theognis Elegiacus 908; ἰδίᾳ μὲν τῶν [ὄντων] φείδομαι δημοσίᾳ δὲ λῃτουργῶν ἥδομαι 5th c.BC: Lysias Orator 21.16; φείδεσθε τοὐλαίου σφόδρα 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus Comedy texts 190: in this sense, most frequently with a negative, οὐ φ.]] not to spare, i. e. to use or give freely, οὐδέ νυ τοῦ περ [δέπαος] φείσατο [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 24.236; μὴ φείδεο σίτου 8th-7th c.BC: Hesiodus Epicus “Opera et Dies” 604; θνῄσκωμεν ψυχέων μηκέτι φειδόμενοι 7th c.BC: Tyrtaeus Elegiacus 10.14; τᾶς ζωᾶς [prev. author] 15.5; σφετέρας οὐ φείσατο νευρᾶς 5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “I.” 6(5).33; φείδεο τῶν νεῶν, μηδὲ ναυμαχίην ποιέο 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 8.68. ; τούτων φ. μηδενός [prev. author] 9.41, compare 39; φείδοντο κέντρων οὐδέν 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Electra” 716; οὐδὲν φ. αὐτῶν οὔτ᾽ ἐν πόνοις κτλ. 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 4.2.1, compare 7.1.29; οὔτε τοῦ σώματος οὔτε τῶν ὄντων 5th-6th c.BC: Andocides Orator 2.11; οὐδενὸς ἂν ἐφείσατο τῶν ἑαυτοῦ 5th c.BC: Lysias Orator 19.24; οὔθ᾽ ἱερῶν κτεάνων οὔτε τι δημοσίων φ. 6th c.BC: Solon Lyricus 4.13; μήτε χρημάτων μήτε πόνων 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Phaedo” 78a: later also with _accusative_, τῶν συμμάχων and τὰ τῶν συμμάχων both in 2nd-3rd c.AD: Dio Cassius Historicus 50.20.]]

__II.2
absolutely, to be sparing, live thriftily, φείδεσθαι μὲν ἄμεινον [Refs 6th c.BC+ [6th c.BC: Theognis Elegiacus 931; τοὺς φειδομένους καὶ τοὺς ἀκριβῶς διαιτῶντας 5th-6th c.BC: Andocides Orator 4.32; οἱ γεωργοῦντες καὶ φ. 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 24.172, compare 5th c.BC: Antipho Sophista 53]]; frequently in participle φειδόμενος, η, ον, thrifty, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Plutus” 247, 553 (_anapaest meter_)]], etc.; ὄμμασι φειδομένοις with shrinking, shy eyes, [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [“Anthologia Graeca” 12.21 (2nd c.AD: Strato Epigrammaticus), compare 5.215 (6th c.AD: Agathias Historicus et Epigrammaticus), 268 ([prev. author])]]; αἱ μὴ φ. (i.e. μέλισσαι) the unthrifty ones, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Historia Animalium” 627a20: also ἔπαινοι πάνυ πεφεισμένοι 2nd c.AD: Lucianus Sophista “Hist.Conscr.” 59; πεφιδημένα δάκτυλα 4th-5th c.AD(?): Nonnus Epicus “Dionysiaca” 12.392]]; compare πεφεισμένως, φειδομένως.

__III
have consideration for, τῆς τοῦ λόγου συμμετρίας [Refs 1st c.AD+ [1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus 2.114b]]: with negative, pay no heed to, οὔτ᾽ ἀνθρώπων φείδεται οὔτε θεῶν [Refs 4th c.BC+ [“Anthologia Graeca” 5.278 (6th c.AD: Paulus Silentiarius Epigrammaticus), compare 7.706 (4th c.BC: Diogenes Cynicus Philosophus).]]

__IV
draw back from, refrain from, θαλάσσας [Refs 7th c.BC+ [7th-6th c.BC: Alcaeus Lyricus “Supp.” 4.13 (probably); κελεύθου 5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “N.” 9.20; κινδύνου 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 5.5.18; τᾶς θήρας 2nd c.BC: Bion Bucolicus “fragment” 10.12]]; τοῦ λέγειν, τοῦ ἀκολουθεῖν, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 1.6.19 (variant), “HG” 7.1.24; φείδου μηδὲν ὧνπερ ἐννοεῖς 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Ajax” 115, compare 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Medea” 401, etc.; οὐδενὸς φεισάμενος οὔτε τῶν πρὸς τοὺς θεοὺς οὔτε τῶν πρὸς τοὺς πολίτας δικαίων “SIG” 708.36 (Istropolis, 2nd c.BC): (_absolutely_, μὴ φείδεσθε 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Troades” 1285; φείδου μηδέν [prev. author] “Hec.” 1044; μὴ φείδου, εἴ τι ἔχεις διδάσκειν 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 1.6.35)]]: with infinitive, spare to do, forbear from doing, uncertain in [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Orestes” 393 (perhaps _absolutely_, post φείδου δ᾽ distinguendum)]]; also φ. μή τι δρᾶσαι τῶν τυραννικῶν [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 574b; τί φειδόμεσθα τῶν λίθων.. μὴ οὐ καταξαίνειν τὸν ἄνδρ; 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Acharnenses” 319 (troch.).]]

__V
in [Refs [LXX, with Preps., φ. ἐπί τινι]]have mercy upon.., [LXX.Jer.15.5, 21.7; ἐπί τινα [prev. author] 28(51).3]; φ. περί τινος to keep one's hands off.., [LXX.2Ki.12.6 (but φ. περὶ κακώσεως] spare to hurt, [LXX.Sir.13.12); φ. ὑπὲρ τῆς κολοκύνθης LXX.Jonah.4.10; ἀπό τινος LXX.1Ki.15.3, LXX.Eze.24.21]; φ. τι ἀπό τινος keep it off, Jb.[Refs [30.10]]; φ. τῆς ψυχῆς ἀπὸ θανάτου[[prev. work] 33.18, cf. LXX.Psa.18(19).14]; φειδεύμενοι (from contraction φειδέομαι) is conjecture for φιλεύμεναι in [Refs 4th c.AD+ [4th c.AD: Eusebius Myndius Philosophus 17.]]

[in LXX chiefly for בּוֹא. hi., also for נָשָׂא, etc. ;]
to bear;
__1. to bear, carry: with accusative, Luk.23:26 24:1, Jhn.19:39, Heb.1:3 (see Westc., in l); pass., Act.2:2 27:15, 17 Heb.6:1, 2Pe.1:17-18; of the mind, 2Pe.1:21.

__3. to bring, bring forward: with accusative of person(s), Act.5:16; id. before πρός, Mrk.1:32 2:3 9:17, 19-20; ἐπί, Luk.5:18; with dative, Mrk.7:32 8:22; with accusative of thing(s), Mrk.6:27 11:2 12:15, Luk.15:23, Act.4:34, 37 5:2, 2Ti.4:13; id. before πρός, Mrk.11:7; εἰς, Rev.21:24, 26; ἐπί, Mat.14:11, Mrk.6:28; ἀπό, Jhn.21:10; with dative, Mrk.12:15, Jhn.2:8; id. before ὧδε, Mat.14:18 17:17; before φαγεῖν (sc. τι), Jhn.4:33; τ. δάκτυλον (χεῖρα), Jhn.20:27; pass., ἡ χάρις, 1Pe.1:13; διδαχήν, II Jn 10; θάνατον (cf. Field, Notes, 230), Heb.9:16; κρίσιν, 2Pe.2:11; κατηγορίαν, Jhn.18:29; αἰτίαν, Act.25:18; αἰτιώματα, Act.25:7, Rec.
__4. to bear, produce, bring forth: καρπόν, Mat.7:18, Mrk.4:8, Jhn.12:24 15:2, 4-5 15:8, 16.
__5. to bring, lead: Mrk.15:22, Jhn.21:18, Act.14:13; metaphorically, of a gate (ὁδός, cl.), Seq. εἰς, Act.12:10
(cf. ἀνα-, ἀπο-, δια-, εἰσ-, παρ-εισ-, ἐκ-, ἐπι-, κατα-, -παρα-, περι-, προ-, προσ-, συν-, ὑπο-φέρω).†

μέγα φέρεται πὰρ σέθεν, of a word uttered, comes with weight, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “P.” 1.87; βίᾳ φέρεται 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Phaedrus” 254a; πνεῦμα φερόμενον [prev. author] “R.” 496d; simply, move, go, ποῖ γᾶς φέρομα; [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Tyrannus” 1309 (_anapaest meter_); οὐκ οἶσθ᾽ ὅποι γῆς οὐδ᾽ ὅποι γνώμης φέρῃ [prev. author] “El.” 922, compare 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Hecuba” 1076 (_anapaest meter_)]], etc.; of the excreta, τὰ φερόμενα.. εἰ μὲν αὐτομάτως φέροιτο [Refs 5th c.BC+ [3rd c.AD: Philumenus Medicus cited in 6th c.AD: Aëtius Medicus 9.12; πρὸς κοιλίαν φερομένην 6th c.AD: Aëtius Medicus 4.19: _metaphorically_, εἰς τὸ λοιδορεῖν φέρῃ 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Andromache” 729; πρὸς τὴν τοῦ κάλλους φύσιν 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Phaedrus” 254b, compare 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Memorabilia” 2.1.4]]; ἐπὶ ταὐτὸ φέρονται have the same tendency, [Refs 1st c.BC+ [1st c.BC: Philodemus Philosophus “περὶ κακιῶν ί” p.42 1st c.AD: Josephus Historicus; ἀπὸ δογμάτων καὶ ἀπὸ θεωρημάτων φ. 2nd c.AD: Vettius Valens Astrologus 238.30]]; of veins, to be conveyed, [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd c.AD: Galenus Medicus 15.531]]; also ἡ φερομένη οὐσία (the doctrine of) universal motion, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Theaetetus” 177c]]; οἱ φερόμενοι θεοί the moving gods, i. e. the stars and planets, [Refs 3rd c.AD+ [3rd c.AD: Plotinus Philosophus 2.3.9.]]

__B.I.2
frequently in participle with another Verb of motion, φερόμενοι ἐσέπιπτον ἐς τοὺς Αἰγινήτας they fell into their hands with a rush, at full speed, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 8.91; ἀπὸ.. ἐλπίδος ᾠχόμην φερόμενος 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Phaedo” 98b; ἧκε φερόμενος εἰς τὴν ἑαυτοῦ φύσιν 4th c.BC: Aeschines Orator 3.89.]]

__B.I.3
of voluntary and impulsive motion, ἰθὺς φέρεται μένει [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 20.172]]; ὁμόσε τινὶ φέρεσθαι come to blows with him, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Cynegeticus” 10.21; δρόμῳ φ. πρός τινα [prev. author] “HG” 4.8.37; φυγῇ εἰς ἑαυτοὺς φ. [prev. author] “Cyr.” 1.4.23; ἥξει ἐπ᾽ ἐκεῖνον τὸν λόγον φερόμενος 4th c.BC: Lycurgus Orator 59; φερόμενος ὑπ᾽ ὀργῆς 1st c.BC: Dionysius Halicarnassensis “de Compositione Verborum” 18.]]

__B.II
metaphorically, καλῶς, κακῶς φέρεσθαι, of things, schemes, etc., turn out, prosper well or ill, succeed or fail, οὔτ᾽ ἂν.. νόμοι καλῶς φέροιντ᾽ ἄν [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Ajax” 1074; κακῶς φ. τὰ ἑαυτοῦ 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Historia Graeca (Hellenica)” 3.4.25; εὖ φέρεται ἡ γεωργία [prev. author] “Oec.” 5.17]]; ὀλιγώρως ἔχειν καὶ ἐᾶν ταῦτα φέρεσθαι to neglect things and let them take their course, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 8.67]]; less frequently of persons, fare well or ill, εὖ φερόμενος ἐν στρατηγίαις being generally successful.., [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 5.16, compare 15; καλῶς φερόμενος τὸ καθ᾽ ἑαυτόν [prev. author] 2.60; φ. ἐν προτιμήσει παρά τινι 1st c.BC: Diodorus Siculus Historicus 33.5; χεῖρον φερομένη παρὰ τἀδελφῷ 1st c.AD: Josephus Historicus “Antiquitates Judaicae” 16.7.6]]; of euphonious writing, σύνθεσις καλῶς φερομένη [Refs 1st c.BC+ [1st c.BC: Philodemus Philosophus “περὶ ποιημάτων” 5.26.]]

__B.II.2
behave, ὑποκριτικῶς, ἀστάτως, etc., [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd c.AD: Vettius Valens Astrologus 38.20, 197.8, +others]]

__B.II.3
have an opinion, ὅπως ἠνέχθη περὶ τοῦ σφυγμοῦ what his opinion was about.., [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd c.AD(?): Marcellinus Medicus “de Pulsibus - Festschrift zur 49. Versammlung deutscher Philologen und Schulmänner” 233.]]

__C
middle: for its chief usages, see above [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus VI. 3.]]

Abbott-Smith / STEPBible (TBESG)
φεύγω
[in LXX chiefly for נוּס, also for בָּרַח, etc. ;]
to flee from or away, take flight: absol., Mat.8:33 26:56, Mrk.5:14 14:50, Luk.8:34, Jhn.10:12, Act.7:29; before εἰς, Mat.2:13 10:23 24:16 (WH, txt.), Mrk.13:14, Luk.21:21, Rev.12:6; ἐπί, with accusative loc., Mat.24:16 (WH, mg.); ἐκ, Act.27:30; ἀπό, with genitive loc. (cl.), Mrk.16:8; id. with genitive of person(s) (as in Heb.), Jhn.10:5, Jas.4:7. Metaphorical: absol., Rev.16:20; with accusative of thing(s), 1Co.6:18, Heb.11:34 (see M, Fr., 116); opposite to διώκειν, 1Ti.6:11, 2Ti.2:22; before άπό, with genitive of person(s), Rev.9:6; άπὸ τ. προσώπου, Rev.20:11; with genitive of thing(s), Mat.3:7 (M, Pr., l.with) Mat.23:33, Luk.3:7, 1Co.10:14 (cf. ἀπο-, δια-, ἐκ-, κατα-φεύγω).†
(AS)

LSJ / STEPBible (TFLSJ)
φεύγω,
[Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 21.472, etc.: _Epic dialect_]]infinitive φευγέμεν, φευγέμεναι, [Refs [10.147, 21.13]]; imperfect ἔφευγον [Refs 8th c.BC+ [22.158, etc., poetical φεῦγον 9.478, 7th c.BC: Tyrtaeus Elegiacus 5.8, 5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “N.” 9.13: iterative φεύγεσκον 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 17.461, 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 4.43]]: future φεύξομαι [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 18.307, etc.]]; also φευξοῦμαι in [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus and Comedy texts, 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Medea” 341, 346, “Hel.” 500, 1041, “Ba.” 659, 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Acharnenses” 203 (codex R), 1129, “Pl.” 447, “Av.” 932 (ἀπο-), 4th-3rd c.BC: Menander Comicus 283]] (but uncertain where found in Attic dialect Prose, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Leges” 635c, +others, 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 38.19]]; φευξεῖται is uncertain reading in [Refs 4th c.BC+ [“IPE” 12.24.11 (Olbia, 4th c.BC)]]; future active ἐκ-φεύξω only late, variant in [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-4th c.BC: Aesopus Fabularum Scriptor 349b, cf. Chambry ii p.479):]]aorist ἔφῠγον, Ionic dialect φύγεσκον [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 17.316]]: perfect πέφευγα [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 7.154 codices (see. below 11.1a)]]; optative πεφεύγοι [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 21.609 (ἐκ-πεφευγοίην 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Tyrannus” 840)]], participle πεφευγότες [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 1.12]]; participle perfect passive πεφυγμένος in active sense, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 6.488, 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 1.18, etc. (in _passive_ sense, 4th-3rd c.BC: Epicurus Philosophus “Fragmenta” 423)]]; Epic dialect πεφυζότες (compare φύζα) [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 21.6, 528, 532, 22.1, later _sing._ πεφυζώς 2nd c.BC: Nicander Epicus “Theriaca” 128]]; Aeolic dialect πεφύγγων, see at {φυγγάνω}:—middle, μὴ φεύγησθε Anon.Hist. in [Refs [“PLit.Lond.” 115:]]aorist 1 δια-φεύξασθαι Decrees [Refs 5th c.BC+ [2nd c.AD: Athenaeus Epigrammaticus in 5th c.BC: Hippocrates Medicus “ἐπιστολαί” 25.]]

__I
absolutely, flee, take flight, opposed to διώκω, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 22.157, etc.; βῆ φεύγων ἐπὶ πόντον 2.665; πῇ φεύγει; 8.94; πόσε φεύγετ; 16.422; ποῖ φύγωμεν.. χθονό; 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Supplices” 777 (Lyric poetry); ποῖ τις οὖν φύγ; 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Ajax” 403 (Lyric poetry); ἐνθένδε ἐκεῖσε φ. 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Theaetetus” 176b: with Preps., φ. ἀπό τινος 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 12.120; φεύξονται ἀφ᾽ ἑαυτῶν εἰς φιλοσοφίαν 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Theaetetus” 168a, etc.]]; ἐκ πολέμοιο, ἐκ θανάτοιο, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 7.118, 20.350; ἐκ κακῶν πεφευγέναι 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Antigone” 437, compare 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.65; ὑπὲκ κακοῦ 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 15.700, compare 17.461 (rarely with _genitive_ only, πεφυγμένος ἦεν ἀέθλων (see. below 11) 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 1.18; τῆς νόσου πεφευγέναι 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Philoctetes” 1044); φ. ἐς πατρίδα γαῖαν 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 2.140, 159, +others]]; ἐπὶ Σάρδεων, ἐπὶ τὸν Ἑλικῶνα, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 7.2.1, “Ages.” 2.11; πρὸς τὸ ὄρος [prev. author] “HG” 3.5.19; ὑπὸ γᾶν 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Eumenides” 175 (Lyric poetry); ὑπὸ δελφῖνος ἰχθύες φ. 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 21.23, compare 554 (compare below 111.2): with _accusative_ _cognate_, φύγε λαιψηρὸν δρόμον]] ran the course full swiftly, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “P.” 9.121; τίνα φυγὴν φευξούμεθ; 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Helena” 1041]]; φ. τὴν παρὰ θάλασσαν (i.e. ὁδόν) flee by the shore route, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 4.12; compare below 111]]; for φυγῇ φεύγειν, see[Refs [below 11.1, φυγή 1.1.]]

__I.2
present and imperfect tenses properly express only the purpose or endeavour to get away: hence participle φεύγων is added to the compound Verbs καταφεύγω, ἐκφεύγω, προφεύγω, to distinguish the attempt from the accomplishment, βέλτερον, ὃς φεύγων προφύγῃ κακὸν ἠὲ ἁλώῃ it is better that one should flee and escape than stay and be caught, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 14.81; φεύγων ἐκφεύγει 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 5.95, compare 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Acharnenses” 177; φ. καταφυγεῖν 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 4.23.]]

__I.3
φ. εἰς.. have recourse to.. take refuge in.., ἐς τοὺς ἀφώνους μάρτυρας [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Hippolytus” 1076.]]

__I.4
with infinitive, shun or shrink from doing, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 4.76, 5th c.BC: Antipho Orator 1.13, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Apologia” 26a]]; with infinitive omitted, φεύγουσι γάρ τοι χοἱ θρασεῖς shrink back, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Antigone” 580.]]

__II
with accusative, flee, avoid, escape, Ἕκτορα [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 11.327, etc.; φ. τινὰ ἐκ μάχης 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 7.104; φ. ἐς τὴν Ἀσίην τοὺς Σκύθας [prev. author] 4.12; φ. θάνατον 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 1.60; ἔνθ᾽ ἄλλοι μὲν πάντες, ὅσοι φύγον αἰπὺν ὄλεθρον, οἴκοι ἔσαν πόλεμόν τε πεφευγότες ἠδὲ θάλασσαν 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 1.11]]; ἔφυγον κακόν, εὗρον ἄμεινον, formula used by μύσται, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 18.259]]; with modal dative, φ. ὄνειδος λόγοις, ἀμαχανίαν ἔργῳ, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “O.” 6.90, “P.” 9.92]]; avoid, shun, χρὴ.. φεύγειν τὰ παχύνοντα [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd c.AD: Galenus Medicus “περὶ λεπτυνούσης διαίτης - CMG” 12; τὴν ἀργίαν καὶ τὴν ἀκινησίαν τοῦ σώματος 2nd c.AD: Soranus Medicus 1.93, compare 46, +others]]; φόνον φ. flee the consequences of the murder, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Medea” 796; αἷμα συγγενὲς φ. χθονός [prev. author] “Supp.” 148; τὰν Διὸς μῆτιν φ. 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Prometheus Vinctus” 906 (Lyric poetry); ὀσμὴν.., μὴ βάλῃ, πεφευγότες 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Antigone” 412; φεύγων φυγῇ τὸ γῆρας 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Symposium” 195b; ἐς πόντον.. φύγε πέτρας νηῦς 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 10.131]]; οὐδεμία [πόλις] πέφευγε (sed perhaps to be read ἀπέφυγε) δουλοσύνην πρὸς Ἱπποκράτεος at the hands of.., [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 7.154]]: participle perfect passive also retains the accusative in [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Homerus Epicus]] in periphrastic phrases, μοῖραν δ᾽ οὔ τινά φημι πεφυγμένον ἔμμεναι ἀνδρῶν [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 6.488; πεφυγμένον ἔμμεν ὄλεθρον 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 9.455; οὔ οἱ νῦν ἔτι γ᾽ ἔστι πεφυγμένον ἄμμε γενέσθαι 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 22.219, compare “hymnus ad Venerem” 34:]] — but in passive sense, τὸ πάραυτα πεφυγμένον κακόν Epicur. [prev. cited]

__II.b
seek to avoid, shirk, στρατείαν [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 21.162; εἰ τοῦτο φεύξονται καὶ μὴ 'θελήσουσι ποιεῖν [prev. author] 20.138]]; so in aorist, ἢν φύγῃ τις, ζημιοῦν [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Acharnenses” 717.]]

__II.2
of things, ἡνίοχον φύγον ἡνία escaped, slipped from his hands, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 23.465; Νέστορα δ᾽ ἐκ χειρῶν φύγον ἡνία 8.137, compare 11.128]]; τὸ φεῦγον the part which slips, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “de Equitandi ratione” 10.9, compare 5th c.BC: Hippocrates Medicus “κατ᾽ ἰητρεῖον” 9, 2nd c.AD: Galenus Medicus 18(2).735: with double _accusative_, ποῖόν σε ἔπος φύγεν ἕρκος ὀδόντων 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 4.350, 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 1.64, etc.]]

__II.2.b
of wine, 'go off', turn sour, [Refs [Gp. 7.7.8.]]

__III
flee one's country, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 9.478, 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 13.259]]; οἱ φεύγοντες the exiles, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 1.24, 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Agesilaus” 7.6; πατρίδα φ. 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 15.228, 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 3.1.24; τὴν αὑτοῦ 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 5.26; ἅπασαν τὴν Ἀθηναίων ξυμμαχίδα “IG” 12.10.30; φ. ἐξ Ἄργεος 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 15.224, compare 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 8.85]]; ἐξ Ἀθηνέων, ἐκ τῆς πατρίδος, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 6.103, 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 1.3.3.]]

__III.2
φ. ὑπὸ Σκυθέων to be expelled, driven out by.. [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 4.125]]: but especially to be exiled, φ. ὑπὸ τοῦ δήμου [Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. author] 5.30, 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Historia Graeca (Hellenica)” 1.1.27]]; φ. ἐξ Ἀρείου πάγου by their sentence, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th-3rd c.BC: Dinarchus Orator 1.44: also with _accusative_, φ. Πεισιστρατίδας 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 5.62.]]

__III.3
absolutely, go into exile, live in banishment, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Agamemnon” 1668 (troch.), 5th c.BC: Antipho Orator 2.2.9, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Menexenus” 242b; δύο ἔτη φευγέτω [prev. author] “Lg.” 867c]]; φ. ἀειφυγίαν to be banished for life, [Refs [[prev. work] 871d, +others]]; φεόγειν Ἀμφίπολιν ἀειφυγίην [Refs 4th c.BC+ [“SIG” 194.3, compare 24 (Amphipolis, 4th c.BC)]]; but also ἐν ἀειφυγίᾳ [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Leges” 877e; φεύγων ἀπ᾽ οἴκων ἃς ἐγὼ φεύγω φυγάς 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Andromache” 976]]; φεύγοντες being in exile, opposed to φυγόντες having gone into exile, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Lysias Orator 14.33]]; with play on words, “μέχρι τίνος φεύξῃ, Ἀρκαδίω; καὶ ὅς, ἔς τ᾽ ἂν τοὺς ἀφίκωμαι οἳ οὐκ ἴσασι Φίλιππον” [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-3rd c.BC: Duris Epigrammaticus 3 1st c.AD: Josephus Historicus]]

__IV
as law-term (mostly in present and imperfect, but[Refs 5th c.BC+ [compare 5th c.BC: Lysias Orator 12.4 (see. below))]], to be accused or prosecuted at law: ὁ φεύγων the accused, defendant, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Vespae” 893, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 405b, etc.; opposed to διώκω, οὔτε φεύγων ἁλοὺς οὔτε διώκων ἡττηθείς 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 23.66]]; with accusative, φ. γραφάς, δίκην, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Equites” 442 (Lyric poetry), “Nu.” 167; ὑπό τινος δίκας φ. 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Apologia” 19c, compare 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 49.1; οὐδενὶ πώποτε οὔτε ἡμεῖς οὔτε ἐκεῖνος δίκην οὔτε ἐδικασάμεθα οὔτε ἐφύγομεν 5th c.BC: Lysias Orator [same place]; φ. ἀπολογίας 4th c.BC: Aeschines Orator 3.201]]; the crime being added in genitive, φόνου δίκην φ. [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Antipho Orator 5.9; γραφὰς φ. παρανόμων 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 18.235]]; more frequently with genitive only, φ. φόνου to be charged with murder, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Lysias Orator 10.31, 4th c.BC: Lycurgus Orator 133, etc.; φ. δειλίας 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Acharnenses” 1129; ξενίας [prev. author] “V.” 718 (_anapaest meter_)]]; with genitive of the penalty, ἐὰν.. φεύγῃ δεσμῶν [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [“OGI” 218.92 (Ilium, 3rd c.BC)]]; also περὶ θανάτου φ. [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Antipho Orator 5.95; φ. ἐπὶ μηνύσει τινός 5th-6th c.BC: Andocides Orator 1.18]]; ἀσεβείας φ. ὑπό τινος is accused of impiety by.., [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Apologia” 35d]]; rarely of things, τὸ φεῦγον ψήφισμα the decree that is on its defence, the decree in question, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 23.58:—in 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 7.214 αἰτίην φ.]] has the older sense, flee from a charge, quit one's country on account of a charge.

__IV.2
plead in defence, δεῖ τοί σε φεύγειν.. ὡς οὐκ ἔχουσι κῦρος [οἱ νόμοι] [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Supplices” 390]]; ἔφευγε μὴ εἰδέναι pleaded ignorance, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Antigone” 263]], (Cf. Latin fugio, Gothic biugan 'bend', etc.)

LSJ / STEPBible (TFLSJ)
φήμη, ἡ,
Aeolic dialect and Doric dialect φάμα, [Refs 7th c.BC+ [7th-6th c.BC: Sappho Lyrica “Papyrus fragments” in E. Diehl, 20 a. 12, 5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “O.” 7.10]]; pseudo-Doric dialect φήμα [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Bacchylides Lyricus 5.194, +others, 3rd c.BC: Isyllus Lyricus 80]]: (φημί).

__I
utterance prompted by the gods, significant or prophetic saying, χαῖρε δὲ φήμῃ Ὀδυσσῆος φίλος υἱός [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 2.35]], ubi see [Refs 8th c.BC+ [Scholia; in the prayer of Odysseus to Zeus, φήμην τίς μοι φάσθω 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 20.100; followed by φήμην δ᾽ ἐξ οἴκοιο γυνὴ προέηκεν ἀλετρίς [prev. work] 105]]; φ. and κλεηδών are interchanged, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 5.72, compare 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Electra” 1109]] {φημί}; φ. about a τέρας, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 3.153; εἴτε του θεῶν φήμην ἀκούσας εἴτ᾽ ἀπ᾽ ἀνδρὸς οἶσθα 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Tyrannus” 43, compare 86, 475 (Lyric poetry)]]; τοῦ ὀνείρου ἡ φ. the message of the dream, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.43; φ. μαντικαί 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Tyrannus” 723; φ. θεσφάτων [prev. author] “Tr.” 1150; μάντεων φῆμαι 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Hippolytus” 1056. compare “Ion” 180 (Lyric poetry); φήμη τις οἴκων ἐν μυχοῖς ἱδρυμένη [prev. author] “Hel.” 820; φήμας τε καὶ μαντείας 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Phaedo” 111b, compare 5th-6th c.BC: Isocrates Orator 9.21; φήμας καὶ ἐνύπνια καὶ οἰωνούς 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Symposium” 4.48, compare “Cyr.” 8.7.3, etc.; φήμης ἕνεκα]]ominis causa, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Leges” 878a, compare 908a]]; τῇ πόλει (i.e. Aquileia) ἀετὸς οἴκιζομένῃ τὴν αὑτοῦ φ. χαρίζεται [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th c.AD: Julianus Imperator “Orationes” 2.72a; hence, comically, φήμη γ᾽ ὑμῖν ὄρνις ἐστί 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Aves” 720]]; φ. ἀγαθὴν λέξομεν ={εὐφημίαν παρέξομεν}, [Refs [[prev. author] “V.” 865 (_anapaest meter_).]]

__I.2
report, rumour, usually of uncertain and mysterious origin, φήμη οὔ τις πάμπαν ἀπόλλυται, ἥν τινα πολλοὶ λαοὶ φημίξωσι· θεός νύ τίς ἐστι καὶ αὐτή [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th-7th c.BC: Hesiodus Epicus “Opera et Dies” 763, compare 4th c.BC: Aeschines Orator 1.128 (citing φήμη δ᾽ ἐς στρατὸν ἦλθε as from 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad”)]]; Φήμης βωμός Scholia (at [prev. work]), [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd c.AD: Pausanias Periegeta 1.17.1]]; common report, opposed to συκοφαντία, [Refs 7th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aeschines Orator 2.145; φάμα δ᾽ ἦλθε κατὰ πτόλιν 7th-6th c.BC: Sappho Lyrica [same place]; ἄμβροτε Φ. 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Tyrannus” 158 (Lyric poetry); φ. ἐσέπτατο ἐς τὸ στρατόπεδον 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 9.100; φ. δημόθρους 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Agamemnon” 938; τίν᾽ ἔχων φ. ἀγαθὴν ἥκει; 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Equites” 1320 (_anapaest meter_); φ. ὑπορρεῖ 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Leges” 672b; φήμην κατασκεδάσαι [prev. author] “Ap.” 18c.]]

__I.3
report of a man's character, repute, δεινὴν δὲ βροτῶν ὑπαλεύεο φήμην· φ. γάρ τε κακὴ πέλεται, κούφη μὲν ἀεῖραι—ῥεῖα μάλ᾽, ἀργαλέη δὲ φέρειν, χαλεπὴ δ᾽ ἀποθέσθαι [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th-7th c.BC: Hesiodus Epicus “Opera et Dies” 760; ὑποδεέστερα τῆς φ. 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 1.11; περὶ τὸν τῶν ἀνθρώπων βίον.. καὶ πράξεις ἀψευδής τις πλανᾶται φ. 4th c.BC: Aeschines Orator 1.127; τοιαύτην φ. σαυτῇ περιφυομένην 5th-6th c.BC: Isocrates Orator 5.78: _plural_, ἐπιφέρειν γυναικείους ἑαυτοῖς φήμας 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Leges” 935a; ἐπώνυμος ἐν φήμαις βροτῶν 4th c.BC: Antiphanes Comicus 105]]:—especially of good report, fame, περιχαρὴς τῇ φ. [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.31; κατὰ τὴν εὐλογίαν καὶ τοὺς ἐπαίνους καὶ τὴν φ. 5th-6th c.BC: Isocrates Orator 5.134, compare 4.186; ὁ δ᾽ ὄλβιος ὃν φᾶμαι κατέχοντ᾽ ἀγαθαί 5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “O.” 7.10: but also φ. πονηραί 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Choephori” 1045]]; αἰσχρὰ φ., opposed to καλὴ δόξα, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Isocrates Orator 1.43; ψευδῆ φ. ὑμνεῖν κατὰ θεῶν 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Leges” 822c, compare “R.” 463d.]]

__I.4
φᾶμαι songs of praise, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “P.” 2.16; φάμα φιλοφόρμιγξ 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Supplices” 697 (Lyric poetry), compare “Th.” 866 (_anapaest meter_).]]

__II
any voice or words, speech, saying, λόγων φ. poetry periphrastic for λόγοι, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Philoctetes” 846 (Lyric poetry)]]; especially common report, tradition, legend, ἀλλ᾽ ἔστι φήμη.. [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Supplices” 760; πολιαὶ φῆμαι 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Electra” 701 (Lyric poetry), compare 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Philebus” 16c, “Lg.” 713c; αἱ ἀρχαῖαι φ. 2nd c.BC: Polybius Historicus 12.3.2]]; μνήμην παρὰ τῆς φήμης λαβών [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Lysias Orator 2.3.]]

__II.b
common report or parlance, [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [3rd c.BC: Chrysippus Stoicus 2.242]]; ὅσους ἡ κοινὴ φ. παραδέδωκεν [θεούς] [Refs 1st c.BC+ [1st c.BC: Philodemus Philosophus “de Pietate - Herkulanische Studien” 17.]]

__II.2
message, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Choephori” 741, 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Electra” 1155, 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Hippolytus” 158 (Lyric poetry).]]

infinitive φάναι, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.27, etc., poetry φάμεν 5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “N.” 8.19]]; participle φάς [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 9.35, 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.63, 141, “SIG” 279.18 (Zeleia, 4th c.BC), φᾶσα 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 6.135, _plural_ φάντες 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 3.44, 14.126, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus Alcaeus2.139b:]]future φήσω, Doric dialect φασῶ [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Acharnenses” 739, etc.]]; Doric dialect 3rd.pers. singular φᾶσε [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “N.” 1.66]]; 2nd pers. singular subjunctive (Doric dialect) φάσῃς [ᾱ] [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Simonides Lyricus 32 (φήσῃς etc. codices 5th c.AD: Stobaeus, Joannes, corr. Bgk.); _optative_ φήσειε 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 6.69, 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Prometheus Vinctus” 503]], participle φήσας [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Memorabilia” 3.11.1, 5th-6th c.BC: Isocrates Orator 12.239]], infinitive φῆσαι [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-3rd c.BC: Theophrastus Philosophus “Characteres” 2.7:]] —middle (chiefly poetry in early writers), imperfect and aorist 2 ἐφάμην, ἔφατο (also [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [“SIG” 437.6 (Delph., 3rd c.BC), “PCair.Zen.” 343.8 (3rd c.BC), “PSI” 4.437.8 (3rd c.BC), 1st c.BC: Parthenius Mythographus 4.5, etc.)]], Epic dialect φάτο [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 20.262, φάσθε 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 6.200, 10.562, ἔφαντο,]] Epic dialect φάντο [Refs [24.460; _imperative_ φάο 16.168, 18.171]], φάσθω, φάσθ; infinitive φάσθα; participle φάμενος (also [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [3rd c.BC: Archimedes Geometra “Spir. Prooem., Eratosth.Prooem.”, “SIG” 364.83 (Ephesus, 3rd c.BC), “PCair.Zen.” 236.4 (3rd c.BC), “PHamb.” 4.14 (1st c.AD), 1st c.AD: Josephus Historicus “Antiquitates Judaicae” 17.12.2, 2nd c.AD: Galenus Medicus 6.228, etc.): _Doric dialect_]]future φάσομαι [ᾱ] [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “N.” 9.43]]:—passive, perfect 3rd.pers. singular πέφαται [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [3rd c.BC: Apollonius Rhodius Epicus 2.500]]; 3rd.pers. singular imperative πεφάσθω [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Timaeus” 72d]]; but participle πεφασμένος [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 14.127, 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Prometheus Vinctus” 843 should be referred to φαίνω:]]aorist ἐφάθην [Refs 4th c.BC+ [(ἀπ-, κατ-) 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “de Interpretatione” 18b39. The]]present indicative φημί is enclitic, except in 2nd pers. singular present φῄς: φαμέν is 1st pers. plural present, φάμεν poetry infinitive: φαντί is 3rd.pers. plural, φάντι participle

__II
φάσκω supplied all moods of present except the indicative, also imperfect ἔφασκο; compare ἠμί. [ᾰ, except in φᾱσι, and in masculine and feminine participle φάς, φᾶσα: in infinitive φάναι ᾰ always; φᾶναι is corrupt in [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Eubulus Comicus 119.11 codices 2nd c.AD: Athenaeus Epigrammaticus]]]:—say, affirm, assert, either absolutely, or followed by infinitive, e. g. Λυσίθευς Μικίωνα φιλῖν (={-εῖν}) φησι [Refs [“IG” 12.924]], compare 57.48, or accusative et infinitive; the infinitive is frequently omitted, σὲ κακὸν καὶ ἀνάλκιδα φήσει (i.e. εἶναι) [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 8.153]]; also Κορινθίους τί φῶμε; what shall we say of them? [NT+8th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Historia Graeca (Hellenica)” 3.5.12; φ. πρός τινα, πρὸς ξεῖνον φάσθαι ἔπος ἠδ᾽ ἐπακοῦσαι 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 17.584: less frequently with _dative_, αὐτοῖς NT.Matt.13.28]]; κατά τινος φ. to speak against him, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Apologia Socratis” 25: sometimes followed by ὡς, 5th c.BC: Lysias Orator 7.19, variant in 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Historia Graeca (Hellenica)” 6.3.7]]; by ὅτι, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Gorgias” 487d, 1st c.AD: Cornutus Philosophus “de Natura Deorum” 30]]; by an interrogative clause, μή ποτε φάσῃς ὅ τι γίνεται αὔριον [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Simonides Lyricus]] [same place]; by participle, uncertain in [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Gorgias” 481c (perhaps to be read θῶμεν)]]; also parenthetic, τίνες, φῄς, ἦσαν οἱ λόγο; [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Phaedo” 59c.]]

__II.b
since what one says commonly expresses a belief or opinion, think, deem, suppose, φῆ γὰρ ὅ γ᾽ αἱρήσειν Πριάμου πόλιν [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 2.37]]; φαίης κε ζάκοτόν τέ τιν᾽ ἔμμεναι ἄφρονά τε you would say, would think, he was.., [Refs [3.220]]; ἶσον ἐμοὶ φάσθαι to say he is (i. e. fancy himself) equal to me, [Refs [1.187, 15.167]]; μὴ.. φαθὶ λεύσσειν think not that you see, [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [3rd c.BC: Theocritus Poeta Bucolicus 22.56]]; τί φῄ; what say you? i.e. what think you? (see.[Refs 5th c.BC+ [below 11.5); λέγ᾽ ἀνύσας ὅ τι φῄς 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Plutus” 349:]] —so φ. δεῖν, φ. χρῆναι, deem it right, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Andocides Orator 3.34, 5th-6th c.BC: Isocrates Orator 3.48.]]

__II.c
say, i.e. write, of an author, ὡς ἔφημεν [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd c.AD: Galenus Medicus 1.158, etc.]] —The middle has all these senses as well as the active

__II
Special Phrases:

__II.1
φασί, they say, it is said, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 5.638, 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 6.42, etc.; parenthetically, 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Ethica Nicomachea” 1109a35, 4th-3rd c.BC: Menander Comicus “Ἐπιτρέποντες” 223, etc.: Prose writers use φησί when quoting, 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 23.89, etc.]]; φησίν saith He, [NT.1Cor.6.16]; especially of an opponent's objection, [Refs 1st c.AD+ [1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus 2.112c; even after a plural, ὅ τοίνυν μέγιστον ἔχειν οἴονται.. καὶ αὐτός, φησί, τῶν εἰσιόντων ἦσθα 4th c.AD: Libanius Sophista “Orationes” 52.39]]; “τὸν δὲ μετ᾽ εἰσενόησα, ἔφη Ὅμηρος as H. said, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Protagoras” 315b.]]

__II.2
joined with a synonymous Verb, ἔφη λέγων, ἔφησε λέγων, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 3.156, 6.137, etc.; ἔλεγε φάς [prev. author] 1.122]]; λέγει οὐδέν, φαμένη.. [Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. author] 2.22; τί ἐροῦμεν ἢ τί φήσομε; 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 8.37, compare 25.100; τί φ; τί λέξ; 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Helena” 483.]]

__II.3
in repeating dialogues the Verb commonly goes before its subject, ἔφην ἐγώ, ἔφη ὁ Σωκράτης, said I, said [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus, but the order is sometimes inverted, ἐγὼ ἔφην, ὁ Σωκράτης ἔφη,]] I said, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus]] said.

__II.4
inserted parenthetically, though the sentence has been introduced by λέγει, εἶπεν, etc., ὁ Ἰσχόμαχος.. εἶπεν· ἀλλὰ παίζεις μὲν σύ γε, ἔφη [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Oeconomicus” 17.10, compare 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Charmides” 164e; ἡ κρίσις.. διαρρήδην λέγει διότι, φησίν, ἔδοξε τἀληθῆ εἰσαγγεῖλαι 5th c.BC: Lysias Orator 13.50.]]

__II.5
τί φημ; [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Tyrannus” 1471, and τί φῄ; “Ph.” 804, 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Helena” 706 (uncertain), are used extra metrum, as exclamations.]]

__II.6
κυριώτατα φάναι, in parenthesis, strictly speaking, [Refs 1st c.AD+ [1st c.AD: Philo Judaeus 2.374]]; ὡς οὕτω φάναι, ={ὡς εἰπεῖν, ἅπασαι ὡς οὕτω φάναι} practically all, [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd c.AD: Galenus Medicus “περὶ λεπτυνούσης διαίτης - CMG” 9]]; συνελόντα (variant{-όντι}) φάναι, ={συνελόντι εἰπεῖν}, [Refs [[prev. author] 16.502.]]

__II.7
Οἰδίπουν.. ἂν μόνον φῶ if I only mention Oedipus, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Antiphanes Comicus 191.6, compare 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Cratylus” 411a, 435a.]]

__III
like{κατάφημι}, say yes, affirm, assert, καὶ τοὺς φάναι and they said yes, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 8.88; καί φημι κἀπόφημι 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Coloneus” 317; ἔγωγέ φημι 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Gorgias” 526c; φάναι τε καὶ ἀπαρνεῖσθαι [prev. author] “Tht.” 165a]]: with infinitive, φῂς ἢ καταρνεῖ μὴ δεδρακέναι τάδ; [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Antigone” 442]]; but οὔ φημι means say no, deny, refuse, with infinitive, ἡ Πυθίη οὐκ ἔφη χρήσειν said she would not.., [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.19, compare 8.2; οὐκ ἔφασαν ἐπιτρέψαι 5th c.BC: Lysias Orator 13.15, 47 (to be read -τρέψειν)]]: with accusative et infinitive, οὔ φημ᾽ Ὀρέστην σ᾽ ἐνδίκως ἀνδρηλατεῖν [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Eumenides” 221, compare 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 2.63: _absolutely_, κἂν μὲν μὴ φῇ]] if he says no, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Aves” 555 (_anapaest meter_)]]; ἢ φάθι ἢ μὴ ἃ ἐρωτῶ answer me yes or no, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Gorgias” 475e]]; so in answers, φημί or οὕτως φημί yes, [Refs [[prev. author] “Phdr.” 270c, +others, “Grg.” 500e]]; οὐκ ἔφη he said no, [Refs [[prev. author] “Phd.” 118a.]] — In this sense _Attic dialect_ writers, besides present, mostly use future φήσω and aorist ἔφησα, but in imperfect, infinitive, and participle present, to avoid ambiguity, they prefer ἔφασκον, φάσκειν, φάσκων (see. φάσκω): φάναι is distinguished from φάσκειν, e.g. ἔφη σπουδάζειν he said he was in haste, ἔφασκε σπουδάζειν he alleged he was in haste; but ἔφησθα is found in this sense, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 1.6.7.]]

__IV
command, order, ἔφην τῷ Ὀρθοβούλῳ ἐξαλεῖψαί με [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Lysias Orator 16.13 (so ἔφασαν, see l. for ἔφρασαν in 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 4.6.11).]]
