φθάνω
[in LXX for נָגַע hi., מְטָא, etc. ;]
__1. to come before another, anticipate (cl.): with accusative of person(s), 1Th.4:15.
__2. In late writers and MGr. (see Kennedy, Sources, 156; Lft., Notes, 35), to come, arrive: Rom.9:31; before εἰς, Php.3:16; ἄχρι, 2Co.10:14; ἐπί (cf. Da TH Dan.4:21, and see Dalman, Words, 107), Mat.12:28, Luk.11:20, 1Th.2:16 (cf. προ-φθάνω).†
(AS)

---

LSJ / STEPBible (TFLSJ)
φθάνω,
[Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 9.506]], imperfect ἔφθανον [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Historia Graeca (Hellenica)” 6.2.30, “Anthologia Graeca” 9.272 (from Bianor)]]: future φθήσομαι [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 23.444, 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 5.10, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 375c, etc.]]; but φθάσω [ᾰ] [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Hippocrates Medicus “περὶ νούσων” 3.13 (assuming variant), 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 5.4.38]]: aorist ἔφθᾰσα [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 7.161, 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Persae” 752 (troch.), 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 3.49, 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 7.1.19, etc.; _imperative_ φθάσον 1st c.AD: Josephus Historicus “Antiquitates Judaicae” 6.11.7]]; optative 3rd.pers. singular φθάσειε [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Isocrates Orator 8.120, _plural_ φθάσειαν 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Historia Graeca (Hellenica)” 7.2.14]] (this tense prevails in later Gk., [Refs 2nd c.BC+ [2nd c.BC: Polybius Historicus 3.66.1, etc.)]]; Doric dialect ἔφθασσα [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [3rd c.BC: Theocritus Poeta Bucolicus 2.115: but the only _Epic dialect_]]aorist is ἔφθην,[Refs 5th c.BC+ [not found in 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus or 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus]], but the more usual form in [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus and 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus, less frequently in 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus, 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus, 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator]]; plural ἔφθημεν, -ητε, -ησαν, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Phoenissae” 1468, 5th-6th c.BC: Isocrates Orator 5.7, 5th c.BC: Antipho Orator 2.2.5]], Epic dialect plural 3 φθάν [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 11.51;]]subjunctive φθῶ, Epic dialect 3rd.pers. singular φθήῃ, φθῇσιν, [Refs [16.861, 23.805]]; Epic dialect 1st pers. plural φθέωμεν [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 16.383]]; 3rd.pers. plural φθέωσι [Refs [24.437]]; optative φθαίην, Epic dialect 3rd.pers. singular φθαίησι (παρα-) [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 10.346]]; infinitive φθῆναι [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 6.115, 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 4.4]]; participle φθάς [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 3.71]]; Epic dialect participle middle φθάμενος [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 5.119, +others, 8th-7th c.BC: Hesiodus Epicus “Opera et Dies” 554:]]perfect ἔφθᾰκα[LXX+4th c.BC+ [Philipp. cited in 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 18.39, LXX.2Ch.28.9, “IG” 12 9).906.26 (Chalcis, 3rd c.AD)]]; πέφθακα [Refs 3rd c.AD+ [3rd c.AD: Pseudo-Callisthenes Historicus 2.10 (see. l)]]: pluperfect ἐφθάκει [Refs 1st c.AD+ [1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus “Galba” 17, 2nd c.AD: Lucianus Sophista “Philops.” 6]]:—passive, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “de Mundo” 395a18]]: imperfect ἐφθάνετο [Refs [“Anthologia Graeca” 9.278 (from Bianor)]]; ἐφθάνοντο [Refs 1st c.AD+ [1st c.AD: Josephus Historicus “Bellum Judaicum” 5.2.4 (variant{ἐφονεύοντο})]]: aorist ἐφθάσθην [Refs 1st c.BC+ [1st c.BC: Dionysius Halicarnassensis 6.25, “epigram Gr.” 315 (from Smyrna), “IPE” 2.197 (Panticapaeum, 2nd c.AD), 1st c.AD: Josephus Historicus “Antiquitates Judaicae” 8.12.4. 2nd c.AD: Galenus Medicus 4.560]]. [φθᾰνω always in Attic dialect (so also in [Refs [“Anthologia Graeca” 9.272 (from Bianor), “APl.” 4.382, 384)]]; φθᾱνω in [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 9.506, 21.262 (where 4th-3rd c.BC: Zenodotus Grammaticus read φθανέει for φθάνει)]]]:—come or do first or before others:

__I
with accusative person, to be beforehand with, overtake, outstrip, in running or otherwise, φθάνει δέ τε καὶ τὸν ἄγοντα [NT+8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 21.262; φθῆ σε τελος θανάτοιο 11.451, compare 8th-7th c.BC: Hesiodus Epicus “Opera et Dies” 554, 570, 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 7.161, 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Heraclidae” 120, “IT” 669, 5th-6th c.BC: Isocrates Orator 9.42, etc.; οὐ μὴ φθάσωμεν τοὺς κοιμηθέντας NT.1Thes.4.15]]; so ἔφθησαν τὸν χειμῶνα they anticipated the storm, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 7.188; φθάσας τὸν λογισμόν 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 21.38]]:—passive, to be overtaken, ὑπό τινος [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “de Mundo” 395a18, “Anthologia Graeca” 9.278 (from Bianor)]]; ἐφθάσθην (see. above).

__II
absolutely, come or act first, opposed to ὑστερέω or ὑστερίζω, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Phoenissae” 975, 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 6.1.18, compare 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 4.121]]; τοῦ φθάσαντος ἁρπαγή the prey of the first comer, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Persae” 752 (troch.), compare “fragment” 23 (Lyric poetry); πρὶν ἐλθεῖν αὐτοὺς φθάσαι βουλόμενοι 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 7.36; μὴ φθάσῃ ἐς τὸν Ἑλλήσποντον ἐσπλεύσας [prev. author] 8, 100; φθάσαι πρὶν ἀδικηθῆναι 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Politica” 1302b23, compare “Rh.” 1373a23]]; in later writers, τὰ φθάσαντα the things before mentioned, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [2nd-3rd c.AD: Aelianus “Varia Historia” 1.34, 4th c.BC: Arg. Demosthenes Orator 46]]; participle φθάνων, φθάσας previous, τῶν φθασάντων δυεῖν βιβλίων [Refs 3rd c.AD+ [3rd c.AD: Porphyrius Tyrius Philosophus “de Abstinentia - Porphyrii Opuscula” 3.1]]; ἐν τοῖς φθάνουσιν ἔργοις Dex.Hist.[Refs 1st c.AD+ [“fragment” 26 1st c.AD: Josephus Historicus; τοῖς φθάνουσι κατορθώμασι [prev. author] “fragment” 6 1st c.AD: Josephus Historicus; οἱ φθάσαντες πόνοι 6th c.AD: Agathias Historicus et Epigrammaticus 5.16; τὸ φθάνον]]previous time, [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd-3rd c.AD: Aelianus “Varia Historia” 14.6]]; τὸ φθάσαν, τὰ φθάσαντα, the past, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [6th c.AD: Agathias Historicus et Epigrammaticus 3.2, +others, 5th-6th c.AD: Procopius Gazaeus Rhetor “Epistulae - Epistolographi” 32; ὁ φθάσας χρόνος 4th-3rd c.BC: Menander Comicus Prot. p.127 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator]]

__II.2
with Preps., come or arrive first, ἕως τῶν οὐρανῶν [LXX+NT [LXX.2Ch.28.9; ἔφθασεν ἐφ᾽ ὑμᾶς NT.Matt.12.28, NT.Luke.11.20, cf. NT.1Thes.2.16: φ. εἰς]].., simply, arriveat, attain to, [NT+1st c.AD+ [NT.Rom.9.31, NT.Phil.3.16, 1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus 2.338a; φθάσομεν εἰς Πηλούσι[ον] “PPar.” 18.14 (2nd c.AD)]]: absolutely, of Time, arrive, καιρὸς τῆς τομῆς ἔφθακε (variant{ἔφθασεν}) [LXX.Cant.2.12]; ἔφθασεν ὁ μὴν ὁ ἕβδομος[LXX.2Esd.3.1.]

__II.2.b
extend, μέχρι γῆς [Refs 3rd c.AD+ [3rd c.AD: Plotinus Philosophus 3.27; εἰς βορρᾶν “PFlor.” 50.87 (3rd c.AD).]]

__II.2.c
reach, αἰθέρα [Refs [“APl.” 4.384.]]

__II.2.d
Grammars, to be applied or applicable, ἐπ᾽ ἀμφοτέρας τὰς διαθέσεις [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd c.AD: Apollonius Dyscolus Grammaticus “de Syntaxi;” 211.22, compare 217.23, +others]]

__III
the action in which one is beforehand is expressed by the participle agreeing with the subject, [Ἄτη] πολλὸν ὑπεκπροθέει, φθάνει δέ τε πᾶσαν ἐπ᾽ αἶαν βλάπτουσ᾽ ἀνθρώπους and is beforehand in doing men mischief, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 9.506]]; ἀλλ᾽ ἄρα μιν φθῆ Τηλέμαχος κατόπισθε βαλών Telemachus was beforehand with him in striking, i.e. struck first, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 22.91, compare 16.383, 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 10.368; ἔφθασέν με προαπελθὼν Χάρμος “PCair.Zen.” 16.3 (3rd c.BC)]]; ἔφθησαν ἀπικόμενοι arrived first, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 4.136, compare 6.115]]; so φ. εὐεργετῶν to be the first to show a kindness, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Memorabilia” 2.3.14; ὅπως φθάσειαν βοηθήσαντες [prev. author] “HG” 7.2.14; ἔφθασαν προκαταλαβόντες 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 3.112; φθάνουσιν αὐτοὺς προκαταφυγοῦσαι [prev. author] 2.91; ἢν φθάσωσιν πρότερον διαφθείραντες τὸ στράτευμα [prev. author] 7.25; φ. γόνασι προσπεσὼν πατρός 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Hercules Furens” 986, etc:]]participle passive is also used, ἦ κε πολὺ φθαίη πόλις ἁλοῦσα, i.e. it would be taken first, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 13.815]]; εἴ κε φθήῃ τυπείς shall be wounded first, [Refs [16.861]]; φθαίητε γὰρ ἂν.. ἐξανδραποδισθέντες ἣ.. [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 6.108; μὴ φθάσωσι προεπιβουλευόμενοι 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 3.83; ἔφθη κατακωλυθείς 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Historia Graeca (Hellenica)” 1.6.17]]; φθάνειν δεῖ πεφραγμένους τοὶς πόρους they must first be blocked up, [Refs [[prev. author] “Cyr.” 2.4.25: these clauses, being comparable in sense, are followed by a _genitive_, φθὰν δὲ μέγ᾽ ἱππήων.. κοσμηθέντες]] were drawn up before the drivers, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 11.51]]; more frequently by πρὶν.. or ἢ.., ἔφθη ὀρεξάμενος, πρὶν οὐτάσαι [Refs 8th c.BC+ [16.322, compare 5th c.BC: Antipho Orator 1.29, 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 3.2.4; φθήσονται τούτοισι πόδες καὶ γοῦνα καμόντα ἢ ὑμῖν 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 23.444; ἔφθης πεζὸς ἰὼν ἢ ἐγὼ σὺν νηΐ 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 11.58]]; ἔφθησαν ἀναβάντες πρὶν ἢ.. [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 9.70]]; ἔφθησαν ἐκπεσόντες πρότερον ἢ.. [Refs [[prev. author] 6.91.]]

__III.b
in later Gr., with participle to express previous action or happening, φθάνω ὑμῖν πρότερον γεγραφηκώς I have already written to you, [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [“POxy.” 1666.3 (3rd c.AD), compare 237 vi30 (2nd c.AD)]], etc.; ἔφθασα εἰρηκώς [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd c.AD: Lucianus Sophista “Pisc.” 29; ὡς ἔφθην εἰπών [prev. author] “Par.” 3; compare 111.2b.]]

__III.2
in the same sense, participle φθάς or φθάσας, Epic dialect φθάμενος, is used like an adverb with a principal Verb, ὅς μ᾽ ἔβαλε φθάμενος, for ὅς μ᾽ ἔφθη βαλών, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 5.119, compare 13.387, 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 19.449]]; οὐκ ἄλλος φθὰς ἐμεῦ κατήγορος ἔσται no other shall be an accuser before me, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 3.71]]; ἀνέῳξάς με φθάσας you opened the door before me, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Plutus” 1102; φθάσας προσπεσοῦμαι 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 5.9, compare 2.91, 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 1.5.3, etc.]]; even with a participle, φθάσας.. ἁρπάσας [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 6.65]]; rarely participle present, φθάνοντες δῃοῦμεν [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 3.3.18.]]

__III.2.b
in signification [Refs [111.1b, φθάσαντες ἐπληρώσαμεν αὐτούς we had]]already paid them, [Refs 4th c.AD+ [“POxy.” 1103.6 (4th c.AD)]]; but ὡσεὶ καὶ ὁμογενῆ φθάσας εἶπον as if I had said (not had already said) ὁ., [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd c.AD: Galenus Medicus 16.502.]]

__III.3
rarely with infinitive, ὁ φθάσας θαρσῆσαι he that first gains confidence, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 3.82]]; σπεύδειν ὅπως.. φθαίης ἔτ᾽ εἰς ἐκκλησίαν ἐλθεῖν (variant{ἐλθών}) hurry to be in time to get to.., [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Equites” 935 (Lyric poetry), compare “Nu.” 1384 (see. infr. IV. 1)]]; μόλις φθάνει θρόνοισιν ἐμπεσοῦσα μὴ χαμαὶ πεσεῖν hardly manages by falling first on the seat not to fall on the ground, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Medea” 1169]]; more frequently in later writers, of actions which one manages to do, does before or has done first or already, [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [3rd c.BC: Apollonius Rhodius Epicus 1.1189, 1st c.BC: Dionysius Halicarnassensis 4.59, 61, 2nd c.AD: Soranus Medicus 1.111, 2nd c.AD: Galenus Medicus 15.2,93, 2nd c.AD: Lucianus Sophista “DMort.” 13.2, “Harm.” 2; ἐὰν φθάσω πρὸ τῆς τρύγης ἀνελθεῖν “PSI” 8.971.10 (3rd-4th c.AD)]]; ἐὰν ὁ ἰατρὸς αὐτὸ φθάσῃ κενῶσαι [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd c.AD: Galenus Medicus 16.499]]; φθάνοντος ἤδη πυρέττειν ἐκ τεττάρων ἡμερῶν τοῦ νοσοῦντος having already begun, [Refs [[prev. work]498]]; μὴ φθάνων προσηκόντως τρέφεσθαι if he is not first suitably nourished, [Refs [[prev. author] 18(2).36, compare 84,103]]; συμβαίνει φθάνειν ἀποθνῄσκειν τοὺς νεωτέρους the young die first, [Refs [[prev. work]222]]; εἰ φθάσαιμεν παλαιοὺς πίθους ἔχειν μεγάλους if we already have.., [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [“Geoponica” 6.3.11, compare 10.22.2, +others, 2nd c.AD: Apollonius Dyscolus Grammaticus “de Pronominibus;” 90.1; ἔφθακεν οὖν ταῦτα ἐψηφίσθαι καὶ τῇ βουλῇ “IG” 12(9).906.26 (Chalcis, 3rd c.AD).]]

__IV
with negatives,

__IV.1
with οὐ and participle (infinitive is see reading in [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Nubes” 1384), followed by καί or καὶ εὐθύς, of two actions following close on each other, οὐ φθάνειν χρὴ συσκιάζοντας γένυν καὶ.. ὁρμᾶν]] you must no sooner get your beard than you march, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Supplices” 1219]]; οὐ φθάνει ἐξαγόμενος καὶ εὐθὺς ὅμοιός ἐστι τοῖς ἀκαθάρτοις no sooner is he brought out than he becomes unclean, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “de Equitandi ratione” 5.10, compare 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Nubes” 1384]]; οὐκ ἔφθημεν εἰς Τροιζῆν᾽ ἐλθόντες καὶ τοιαύταις νόσοις ἐλήφθημεν ἐξ ὧν.. no sooner had we come to Troezen than.., [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Isocrates Orator 19.22, compare 5.53, 8.98, 9.53]]; οὐκ ἔφθη μοι συμβᾶσα ἡ ἀτυχία καὶ εὐθὺς ἐπεχείρησαν διαφορῆσαι τἄνδοθεν scarcely or no sooner had misfortune befallen me when.., [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 57.65, compare 43.69, 5th-6th c.BC: Isocrates Orator 4.86.]]

__IV.2
οὐκ ἂν φθάνοις, οὐκ ἂν φθάνοιτε, with participle present, express a strong exhortation or urgent command, οὐκ ἂν φθάνοιτε τὴν ταχίστην ὀπίσω ἀπαλλασσόμενοι you could not be too quick in departing, i.e. make haste and be off, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 7.162]]; οὐ φθάνοιτ᾽ ἔτ᾽ ἄν θνῄσκοντες make haste and die, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Orestes” 936, compare 941, Alcaeus 662, “Heracl.” 721, “Tr.” 456 (troch.), “IT” 245; οὐκ ἂν φθάνοιτον τοῦτο πράττοντε 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Plutus” 485; ἀποτρέχων οὐκ ἂν φθάνοις [prev. work] 1133]]; εἰς ἀγορὰν ἰὼν ταχέως οὐκ ἂν φθάνοις[Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. work] 874, compare “Ec.” 118; οὐκ ἂν φθάνοις λέγων 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Symposium” 185e, 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Memorabilia” 2.3.11]]; these phrases are not to be treated as questions, compare οὐκ ἂν φθάνοιμι (i.e. λέγων) [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Symposium” 214e, compare “Phd.” 100c, 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 25.40, 2nd c.AD: Lucianus Sophista “Fug.” 26, “Symp.” 2, “Anach.” 14]]: with participle aorist, once in [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd c.AD: Lucianus Sophista, “Vit.Auct.” 26.]]

__IV.2.b
in [Refs [1, 2, or 3 _person_, to express immediate futurity, οὐκ ἂν φθάνοις ἀκούων you]]shall hear in a moment, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Euthydemus” 272d]]; οὐκ ἂν φθάνοι τὸ πλῆθος τούτοις τοῖς θηρίοις δουλεῦον will soon (or inevitably) be enslaved to.., [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 24.143]]; also to express what is logically inevitable, οὐκ ἂν φθάνοιεν αὐτοὺς προσκυνοῦντες they will soon be (or cannot logically help) worshipping them, Aristeas 137; τοῦτο μὲν οὐκ ἂν φθάνοις καὶ Ἐμπεδοκλεῖ πρὸ αὐτοῦ ἐγκαλῶν [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd c.AD: Lucianus Sophista “Fug.” 2; οὐκ ἂν φθάνοι κἀμὲ μάντιν λέγων [prev. author] “Hes.” 8; οὐκ ἂν φθάνοι τις ἁπάσας ἀναιρῶν τὰς τοιαύτας προστασίας [prev. author] “Apol.” 11]]: with participle aorist, [Refs [[prev. author] “Tox.” 2.]]

φθέγγομαι
[in LXX for עָנָה, נָבַע hi., etc. ;]
of men or animals, to utter a sound or voice: absol., Act.4:18; before ἐν φωνῇ, 2Pe.2:16; with accusative, ὑπέρογκα, 2Pe.2:18.†
(AS)

---

LSJ / STEPBible (TFLSJ)
φθέγγομαι,
[Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 10.228, etc.]]: future φθέγξομαι [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 21.341:]]aorist ἐφθεγξάμην, Epic dialect and poetry φθεγξάμην [Refs 5th c.BC+ [18.218, 5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “O.” 6.14:]]perfect ἔφθεγμαι, 2nd pers. singular ἔφθεγξαι [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Leges” 830c]], 3rd.pers. singular ἔφθεγκται (transitive) [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Analytica Posteriora” 77a2, (_passive_) [prev. author] “Cael.” 279a23]]: —utter a sound or voice, especially speak loud and clear, frequently in [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Homerus Epicus, φθεγξάμενος παρὰ νηός 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 11.603, compare 10.67, +others, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 336b]] (properly of all animals that have lungs, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Historia Animalium” 535a30):]]

__I
of the human voice, ἀνθρωπηΐῃ φωνῇ φ. [Refs 8th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 2.57; ἀπὸ γλώσσας 5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus [same place]; διὰ τοῦ στόματος 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Sophista” 238b; [ψυχῆς] φθεγξαμένης ἀΐων 6th c.BC: Xenophanes Poeta Philosophus 7.5; φθεγξαμένου τευ ἢ αὐδήσαντος 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 9.497]]; with a participle expressing the kind of cry, φθέγξομ᾽ ἐγὼν ἰάχουσα [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 21.341; τοὶ δ᾽ ἐφθέγγοντο καλεῦντες 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 10.229, compare 12.249; so σφοδρῷ τῷ πνεύματι φ. 4th c.BC: Archytas Tarentinus Philosophus 1; φ. μετὰ βοῆς 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Leges” 791e, etc.; μέγιστον ἁπάντων 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 19.206; καλὸν καὶ μέγα [prev. work]216, compare 337; ἐλεύθερον καὶ μέγα 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Gorgias” 485e]]; also of weak, small voice, φθεγξάμενος ὀλίγῃ ὀπί [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 14.492; τυτθὸν φθεγξαμένη 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 24.170]]; of the battle-cry, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 1.8.18]]; of the recitative of the chorus, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. author] “Oec.” 8.3; οὐκέτι πόρρω διθυράμβων φ. 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Phaedrus” 238d]]; οὐδ᾽ ἂν φθέγξασθαι δυνηθείη would not be able to utter a syllable, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Isocrates Orator 15.192, compare 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 368c; opposed to silence, 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Memorabilia” 4.2.6]]; εἶτα σὺ φθέγγει..; open your mouth.. ? [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 18.283]]; of children just born, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Historia Animalium” 587a27]]:—Constr.:—with accusative cognate, utter, ἔπος [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 5.106; ἀγέλαστα 1st c.AD(?): Heraclitus 92; ὀδυρμοὺς καὶ γόους ἀνωφελεῖς 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Prometheus Vinctus” 34; καίρια 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Philoctetes” 862 (Lyric poetry)]]; ἀράς, λόγους, βλασφημίαν, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Phoenissae” 475, “Med.” 1307, “Ion” 1189; ῥῆμα μοχθηρόν “SIG” 1175.19 (Piraeus, Tab. Defix., 4th-3rd c.BC)]]; τἀληθῆ [NT+5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Philebus” 49b; ὑπέρογκα ματαιότητος φ. NT.2Pet.2.18]]: the person addressed added with a preposition, φ. εἰς ἡμᾶς [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Ph.” [same place]; πρός τινα 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Ion” 534d]]; later τισί, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus “Crassus” 27; φ. τι περί τινος 5th-6th c.BC: Isocrates Orator 10.13]]; τὸ φθεγγόμενον, absolutely, that which uttered the sound, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 8.65.]]

__I.2
of animals, as a horse, neigh, whinny, [Refs [[prev. author] 3.84, 85]]; of an eagle, scream, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 6.1.23]]; of a raven, croak, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-3rd c.BC: Theophrastus Philosophus “de Signis Tempestatum” 16]]; of a fawn, cry, [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [3rd c.BC: Theocritus Poeta Bucolicus 13.62]]; of birds, opposed to ἄφωνοί εἰσι, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Historia Animalium” 618a5; ἐν τῷ θέρει ᾄδει [κόττυφος], τοῦ χειμῶνος.. φ. θορυβῶδες [prev. work] 632b17]]; of worms, φ. οἷον τριγμόν [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-3rd c.BC: Theophrastus Philosophus “de Causis Plantarum” 5.10.5]]; of certain fish, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Fragmenta” 300, 2nd-3rd c.AD: Oppianus Anazarbensis Epicus “Halieutica - Poetae Bucolici et Didactici” 1.135.]]

__I.3
of inanimate things, of a door, creak, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Plutus” 1099]]; of thunder, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 7.1.3]]; of trumpets, [Refs [[prev. author] “An.” 4.2.7, 5.2.14]]; of the flute, [Refs 6th c.BC+ [[prev. author] “Smp.” 6.3, 6th c.BC: Theognis Elegiacus 532]]; of the lyre, φόρμιγξ φ. ἱρὸν μέλος [Refs 4th c.BC+ [[prev. author] 761, compare 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Metaphysica” 1019b15]]; of an earthen pot, εἴτε ὑγιὲς εἴτε σαθρὸν φ. whether it rings sound or cracked, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Theaetetus” 179d]]; φ. παλάμῃσι to clap with the hands, [Refs 4th c.AD+ [4th-5th c.AD(?): Nonnus Epicus “Dionysiaca” 5.106, compare “Anthologia Graeca” 9.505.17 (uncertain).]]

__II
={ὀνομάζω}, to name, call by name, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 527a, “Phlb.” 25c, 34a]]; τῷ πλέγματι τούτῳ τὸ ὄνομα ἐφθεγξάμεθα λόγον gave it the name of λόγος, [Refs [[prev. author] “Sph.” 262d; φ. εἴδωλον ἐπὶ πᾶσιν ὡς ἓν ὄν [prev. work] 240a]]; φ. γιγνόμενα speak of things as coming into existence, [Refs [[prev. author] “Tht.” 157b]]; καὶ τὸν κύλλαστιν φθέγγου use the word κ., [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Fragmenta” 257]]; also τῇ δυνάμει ταὐτὸν φ. have the same meaning, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Cratylus” 394c.]]

__III
with accusative person, sing, or celebrate one aloud, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “O.” 1.36]]; also, tell of, recount, θεῶν ἔργα [Refs 6th c.BC+ [6th c.BC: Xenophanes Poeta Philosophus 12.1.]]

poetry 3rd.pers. plural ἔφθαρεν [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “P.” 3.36]]: also participle κατα-φθερείς [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Epicharmus Comicus 35.13]]: perfect ἔφθαρμαι [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Electra” 765]], 3rd.pers. plural ἐφθάραται [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 3.13]]; infinitive ἐφθάρθαι [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Metaphysica” 1021b27, (δι-) 4th c.BC: Isaeus Orator 9.37]], Aeolic dialect ἔφθορθαι [Refs [12th c.AD: Eustathius Episcopus Thessalonicensis 790.8]]: pluperfect 3rd.pers. plural ἐφθάρατο [Refs 5th c.BC+ [2nd c.AD: Appianus Historicus “Bella Civilia” 3.15, (δι-) 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 8.90. The _compound_ διαφθείρω]] is much more frequently than the simple Verb:—destroy things, μῆλα κακοὶ φθείρουσι νομῆες [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 17.246]]; φ. τῶν Συρίων τοὺς κλήρους waste them, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.76, compare 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Historia Graeca (Hellenica)” 7.2.11, “An.” 4.7.20; τοὺς θεῶν νόμους 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Ajax” 1344]]; τὰς ναῦς see reading in [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 2.91; τὴν πόλιν καὶ νόμους 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Leges” 958c, compare 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Memorabilia” 1.5.3; εὐδαιμονίαν 4th-3rd c.BC: Dinarchus Orator [same place]; ἔμβρυα 1st c.AD: Dioscorides (Dioscurides) Medicus 2.163; τὸ συλληφθέν 2nd c.AD: Soranus Medicus 1.60]] (also absolutely, miscarry, [Refs [[prev. work] 59)]]; τὸν κοινὸν οἶκον Mitteis [Refs 2nd c.BC+ [“Chr.” 284.11 (2nd c.BC)]]: —passive, to be destroyed, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Ajax” 25, etc.; ἐκ τῶν αὐτῶν καὶ διὰ τῶν αὐτῶν καὶ γίνεται πᾶσα ἀρετὴ καὶ φθείρεται 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Ethica Nicomachea” 1103b8; εἰς τὸ μὴ ὂν φ.]]pass away, cease to be, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-3rd c.BC: Epicurus Philosophus “Epistulae” 1p.5U.; δυὰς προσθέσει μονάδος εἰς τριάδα φθείρεται μηκέτι μένουσα δυάς 1st c.AD: Philo Judaeus 2.509]]; of animals, perish, [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [PStrassb. 24.15 (2nd c.AD).]]

__2
of persons, μαψαῦραι... ναύτας φ. destroy them, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th-7th c.BC: Hesiodus Epicus “Theogonia” 876]] (but perhaps only active of signification[Refs 4th c.BC+ [11.4); στρατόν 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Persae” 244 (troch.), “Ag.” 652]]:—passive, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. author] “Pers.” 272, 283 (Lyric poetry); γειτόνων πολλοὶ ἁμᾷ.. ἔφθαρεν 5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “P.” 3.36; νόσῳ ἐφθάραται Ἀθηναῖοι 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 3.13, compare 7.48; πρόρριζον ἔφθαρται γένος 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Electra” 765]]; ἔφθαρμαι I am undone! [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-3rd c.BC: Menander Comicus “Ἥρως” 13; μὴφθαρῶσιν “PMich.Zen.” 80.4 (3rd c.BC).]]

__3
corrupt, bribe, τινα [Refs 1st c.BC+ [1st c.BC: Diodorus Siculus Historicus 4.73]]; lure, entice, trap, κημοῖσι πλεκτοῖς πορφύρας φθείρει γένος [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Fragmenta” 504 (assuming variant); φθείρει γὰρ ἡ πρόνοια τὴν ἀβουλίαν]]entices to its ruin, entraps, [Refs [Trag.Adesp. 484 (assuming variant)]]; pervert, φθείρουσιν ἤθη χρήσθ᾽ ὁμιλίαι κακαί [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Fragmenta” 1024:]] —passive, see below [Refs [11.3.]]

__3.b
seduce a woman, ὑπὸ τῆς θυγατρὸς ἀδικούμενον καὶ Διονυσίου τοῦ φθείραντος αὐτὴν κιναίδου [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [“PEnteux.” 26.11 (3rd c.BC)]]:—passive, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Fragmenta” 485, 1st-2nd c.AD: Dio Chrysostomus Sophista 11.153]] (but not Attic dialect accusative to [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd c.AD: Phrynichus Atticista 53, Moer.p.103 P.), 2nd c.AD: Artemidorus Daldianus Onirocriticus 5.17.]]

__4
ruin, spoil, ποσὶν φθείροντα πλοῦτον ἀργυρωνήτους θ᾽ ὑφάς, of one who treads on rich carpets, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Agamemnon” 949]]; βαφὰς φθείρουσα τοῦ ποικίλματος, of blood, [Refs [[prev. author] “Ch.” 1013]]; of a poison, ὧνπερ ἂν θίγῃ, φθείρει τὰ πάντα [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Trachiniae” 716; φαρμάκων φθείρειν πεφυκότων τὰ σώματα 2nd c.AD: Galenus Medicus 15.541]]; δούλην (wet-nurse) μὴ φθείρουσαν τὸ γάλα [Refs 1st c.BC+ [“BGU” 1058.29 (1st c.BC),compare 2nd c.AD: Soranus Medicus 1.88; τοῦ σώματος (i.e. τῶν νοσούντων) φθείροντος τὸ θρέψαι δυνάμενον [prev. work] 90, compare 63, +others]]

__5
τὰ μιγνύμενα τῶν χρωμάτων οἱ βαφεῖς φθείρεσθαι καὶ φθοράν τὴν μῖξιν ὀνομάζουσιν [Refs 1st c.AD+ [1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus 2.393c (where μιαίνω 1 is compared).]]

__II
passive (compare above 1.1, 2),

__II.1
φθείρεσθε (as a curse) may you perish! ruin take you! [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 21.128, 5th c.BC: Sannyrio Comicus 10]]; φθείρου as an imprecation, go to the devil! be off! [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Acharnenses” 460, “Pl.” 598, 610 (_anapaest meter_), 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Fragmenta” 610; ἐκποδὼν ἡμῖν φθείρεσθε 3rd c.BC: Herodas Mimographus 6.16:with _genitive_, φθείρεσθε τῆσδε]] off from her! unhand her, let her go, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Andromache” 715 (so in _future_ _indicative_, εἰ μὴ φθερῇ τῆσδ᾽ ὡς τάχιστ᾽ ἀπὸ στέγης]] if thou dost not depart... [Refs [[prev. work] 708).]]

__II.1.b
with a preposition, φθείρεσθαι πρὸς τοὺς πλουσίους, of hangers-on and flatterers, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 21.139, compare 1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus “Phocion” 21, “Eum.” 14, “Ant.” 24; εἰς ἡδονὰς ἀπὸ.. πόνων Anonymus cited in 5th c.AD: Stobaeus, Joannes 4.31.84; ἀκούω σε λυρῳδοῦ γυναικὸς ἐρᾶν καὶ εἰς ἐκείνης φθειρόμενον πᾶσαν τὴν ἐφήμερον ἄγραν κατατίθεσθαι 4th c.AD: Alciphro Epistolographus 1.18.]]

__II.2
in Medicine texts, ἡ κοιλίη φθαρήσεται will be deranged, disordered, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Hippocrates Medicus “περὶ ἀρχαίης ἰητρικῇς” 13.]]

__II.3
to be morally corrupted, ἐφθάρη ἡ γῆ ἐναντίον τοῦ θεοῦ [LXX+3rd c.BC+ [LXX.Gen.6.11, cf. LXX.Hos.9.9, +others; ἔστι ἐν Ἀλεξανδρείᾳ σκηνῶν ἐν τοῖς Ἀριστοβούλου φθειρόμενος “PCair.Zen.” 37.7 (3rd c.BC); φθαρεὶς Εὔτυχος ὑπὸ τῆς Ἀρσινόης [prev. work] 620.7 (3rd c.BC)]]; but ἐν Σικυωνίαι ἐφθαρμένους is falsa lectio for{ἐν Σικυῶνι διεφθ}. (conjecture Sintenis) in [Refs 1st c.AD+ [1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus “Aratus” 40.]]

__II.4
of seafarers, wander, drift [Refs 5th c.BC+ [compare(above 1.2, πολύφθορος 11.2, φθορά 8), πόσον χρόνον πόντου 'πὶ νώτοις ἅλιον ἐφθείρου πλάνο; 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Helena” 774]]; ναυτίλους ἐφθαρμένους sailors driven out of their course, [Refs [[prev. author] “IT” 276; ἱκέτας δέχεσθαι ποντίους ἐφθαρμένους [prev. author] “Cyc.” 300]]; of shipwrecked persons, νεῶν (ἐκ νεῶν Elmsl.) φθαρέντες [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Persae” 451]]; also of travellers or wanderers by land, οὐχ ἕνα νομίζων φθείρεται πόλεως νόμον (variant{τόπον}) [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Electra” 234; ὁ Μενέλαος χρόνον πολὺν ἐφθείρετο πανταχόσε τῆς Ἐλλάδος 1st-2nd c.AD: Dio Chrysostomus Sophista 7.95]]; οὐδὲν δεῖ φθείρεσθαι περιόντα (={περιιόντα}) τὴν ἀρχὴν ἅπασαν [Refs 1st c.AD+ [2nd c.AD: Aristides Rhetor “Orationes” 26(14).33; ἄνω κάτω διαθέοντας τὴν Ἑλλάδα καὶ φθειρομένους [prev. author] 1.420 1st c.AD: Josephus Historicus; τῶν μετοίκων τῶν ἐξ Ἑρμιόνης οὐκ οἶδ᾽ ὅπως εἰς Πειραιᾶ φθαρέντων 4th c.AD: Alciphro Epistolographus 1.13]]; μὴ περιΐδῃς ἀγαθοὺς γείτονας εἰς στενὸν τοῦ καιροῦ φθειρομένους[Refs 2nd c.AD+ [[prev. work] 24; [Ἀλέξανδρον] ὑπὲρ τὸν Ἰνδὸν κτλ. φθειρόμενον 2nd c.AD: Arrianus Historicus “Anabasis” 7.4.2]]; φθαρῆναι εἰς βάρβαρα ἔθνη (ἐν βαρβάροις ἔθνεσι or ἔθεσι codices) [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [3rd-2nd c.BC: Phalaris Epistolographus “Epistulae - Epistolographi” 49]]; φθαρέντων ἐς ἀλλήλους falling foul of one another, [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd c.AD: Appianus Historicus “Praefatio” 10 (assuming variant).]]

__II.5
of women, χέρσους φθαρῆναι pine away in barrenness, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Tyrannus” 1502, compare “El.” 1181]] (unless wander, compare above [Refs [11.4). (Cf. Sanskrit]]ksárati 'flow', later 'wane, perish', Avest. γζ?~Xαρ- and ζ?~Xγαρ- 'flow'.)

φθόγγος, -ου, ὁ
(φθέγγομαι), [in LXX: Psa.19:4 (קַו), Wis.19:18 * ;]
a sound: Rom.10:18 (LXX) 1Co.14:7.†
(AS)

LSJ / STEPBible (TFLSJ)
φθόγγ-ος, ὁ
(both poetical and Prose), any clear, distinct sound, especially voice of men, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 5.234, etc.]]; of the Sirens, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 12.41, 159; φθόγγῳ ἐπερχόμεναι 18.199; φ. ἀραῖον οἴκοις 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Agamemnon” 237 (Lyric poetry); γόων οὐκ ἀσήμονες φ. 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Coloneus” 1669]]; φ. οἰκείου κακοῦ voice, telling of.., [Refs [[prev. author] “Ant.” 1187; τὸν Αἵμονος φ. [prev. work] 1218, compare 1214]]; of birds, ἀλεκτρυόνων φ. [Refs 6th c.BC+ [6th c.BC: Theognis Elegiacus 864; ἀγνῶτα.. φ. ὀρνίθων 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Antigone” 1001, compare 424; φθόγγος οὔτ᾽ ὀρνίθων οὔτε θαλάσσης 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Iphigenia Aulidensis” 9 (_anapaest meter_); κυνῶν καὶ προβάτων καὶ ὀρνέων 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 397a.]]

__2
speech, Ἑλλάδος φθόγγον χέουσαν [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Septem contra Thebas” 73]]; φ. ἔμμετρος, opposed to πεζά, poetical speech, [Refs 1st c.BC+ [1st c.BC: Philodemus Gadarensis Epigrammaticus “D.” 3.13]]; utterance, saying, [Refs [Trag.Adesp. 417.]]

__II
generally, sound, ἀνέμων [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Simonides Lyricus 37.11; δαίμονος πεδαρσίου.. πτερωτὸς φ. 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Aves” 1198 (= “Tragica Adespota” 47)]]; φωνῆς μὲν οὔ, φθόγγου δὲ μετέχοντά τινος, of semi-vowels, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Philebus” 18c, compare 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “de Audibilibus” 801b2, 804b9; ἄνευ φθόγγου καὶ ἠχῆς 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Timaeus” 37b, compare 4th-3rd c.BC: Epicurus Philosophus “Epistulae” 1p.32U.; εἰς τοὺς φ. καὶ τὰς συλλαβάς 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Cratylus” 389d, compare 1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus “Alexander” 27, 2nd c.AD: Galenus Medicus 15.6.]]

__II.2
of musical sounds, λωτὸς φθόγγον κελάδει [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Electra” 716 (Lyric poetry); λύρας 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Leges” 812d, etc., compare φθόγγους ἀλύρους θρηνοῦμεν 2nd c.AD: Alexander Rhetor 162.6 (_anapaest meter_).]]

__II.2.b
plural, notes on a musical instrument; strings of lyre, [Refs 1st c.AD+ [1st-2nd c.AD: Dio Chrysostomus Sophista 10.19]]; stops of flute, [Refs 1st c.AD+ [2nd-3rd c.AD: Philostratus Sophista “Vita Apollonii” 5.21; compare 1st c.AD: Cornutus Philosophus “de Natura Deorum” 14.]]

φθονέω, -ῶ
(φθόνος), [in LXX: Tob.4:7, 16 AB * ;]
to envy: with dative (L, txt., Tr., mg., WH, mg., accusative), as in cl., Gal.5:26.†
(AS)

---

LSJ / STEPBible (TFLSJ)
φθον-έω,
aorist ἐφθόνησα, later ἐφθόνεσα [LXX+3rd c.AD+ [LXX.Tob.4.7, “JHS” 46.45 (Athens, 3rd-4th c.AD), “Anthologia Graeca” 5.303, 7.607 (6th c.AD: Palladas Epigrammaticus), 4th-5th c.AD(?): Nonnus Epicus “Dionysiaca” 3.159]]:—middle, future in passive sense φθονήσομαι [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 47.70]]:—passive, fut φθονηθήσομαι [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Hiero” 11.15]]: aorist ἐφθονήθην [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Electra” 30, 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Memorabilia” 4.2.33, etc.]]: perfect participle ἐφθονημένος [Refs 1st c.AD+ [1st c.AD: Josephus Historicus “Antiquitates Judaicae” 6.11.10, 2nd c.AD: Vettius Valens Astrologus 330.2]]: (φθόνος):—bear ill-will or malice, grudge, be envious or jealous,

__I
absolutely, εἴ περ γὰρ φθονέω τε καὶ οὐκ εἰῶ διαπέρσαι, οὐκ ἀνύω φθονέουσα [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 4.55, 56]]; κρείττων δόξα τῶν φθονούντων too high for envy, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 3.24]]; εἰ πέφυκε φθονεῖν τὸ θεῖον [Refs 4th c.BC+ [compare (φθονερός 1.2) 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Metaphysica” 982b32: with _accusative_ et]]infinitive, οὔτε τινὰ φθονέω δόμεναι I do not grudge that any should give thee, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 18.16; οὐ φθονῶ σ᾽ ὑπεκφυγεῖν 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Antigone” 553; τὸ μὲν σὸν οὐ φθονῶ καλῶς ἔχειν 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Medea” 312; ἐφθόνησαν [οἱ θεοὶ] ἄνδρα ἕνα βασιλεῦσαι 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 8.109]]; ἔφη (i.e. ὁ Σωκράτης) φθονεῖν τοῦς ἐπὶ ταῖς φίλων εὐπραξίαις ἀνιωμένους [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Memorabilia” 3.9.8; ὁ φθονῶν ἐπὶ κακοῖς τοῖς τῶν πέλας ἡδόμενος 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Philebus” 48b.]]

__I.2
with dative person, πτωχὸς πτωχῷ φθονέει καὶ ἀοιδὸς ἀοιδῷ [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th-7th c.BC: Hesiodus Epicus “Opera et Dies” 26; οὐ φ. ἀγαθοῖς 5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “P.” 3.71; φ. φασὶ μητρυιὰς τέκνοις 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Ion” 1025; τισὶ φ. καὶ δυσμενῶς ἔχειν 5th-6th c.BC: Isocrates Orator 12.241, compare 8.13]]; frequently with participle added, φ. τινὶ εὖ πρήσσοντι to envy him for his good fortune, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 7.236, 237; παιδικοῖς φ. οὐσίαν κεκτημένοις 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Phaedrus” 240a, compare 5th c.BC: Lysias Orator 27.11]]; without a Noun expressed, καλῶς πράττουσι, πλουτοῦντι φ., [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Isocrates Orator 1.26, 5th c.BC: Lysias Orator 21.15, etc.: with _dative_ _of things_, φ. τοῖς ἀγαθοῖς τινος 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 2.4.10 (variant{ἐπὶ τοῖς ἀγ}.,compare 5th-6th c.BC: Isocrates Orator 1.26; ἐφ᾽ οἷς ἕτεροι ποιήσαντες ἐτιμήθησαν φ. 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 20.151): with _genitive_ _of things_, τοῦ εὐτυχέειν φθονέουσι καὶ τὸ κρέσσον στυγέουσι 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 7.236]]; οὐδέ τί σε χρὴ ἀλλοτρίων φθονέειν to be envious because of other men's goods [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 18.18]]: with dative person et genitive of things, bear a grudge against a person on account of a thing, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Hercules Furens” 1309.]]

__I.3
resent, with genitive, τῆς δοκήσεως τῶν κερδῶν [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 3.43]]: with dative of things, feel righteous indignation at, ταῖς εὐπραγίαις τινῶν [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Isocrates Orator 8.124; also with _dative_ _person_, [prev. author] 4.184, 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 28.18.]]

__I.3.b
φ. τινὶ followed by ει.., or ἐάν.. take it ill or amiss that.., [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 3.146, 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Historia Graeca (Hellenica)” 2.4.29]]; μή μοι φθονήσητ᾽, ει.. [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Acharnenses” 496: _absolutely_, φ. ἐάν τις.. 5th c.BC: Lysias Orator 3.9]]; φθονεῖς ἄπαις οὖσ᾽, εἰ.. [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Ion” 1302]]; also φ. τινὶ ὅτι.., [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 3.1.39]]; φ. ὅτι.. [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Lysias Orator 24.3, uncertain reading in 18.16.]]

__II

φιλανθρωπία, -ας, ἡ
(φιλάνθρωπος, humane), [in LXX: Est.8:13, 2Ma.6:22 2Mac 14:9, 3Ma.3:15 3Mac 3:18 * ;]
humanity, kindness (see Field, Notes, 147 f.): Act.28:2, Tit.3:4 (cf. also DCG, ii, 356 ff.).†
(AS)

---

LSJ / STEPBible (TFLSJ)
φῐλανθρωπ-ία, ἡ,
humanity, benevolence, kind-heartedness, humane feeling, or, in a weaker sense, kindliness, courtesy,

__I
of men, [NT+5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Hippocrates Medicus “παραγγελίαι” 6, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Euthyphro” 3d, 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 1.4.1, NT.Act.28.2, etc.]]; opposed to σεμνότης, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Isocrates Orator 15.133]]; opposed to φθόνος, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 20.165; opposed to ὠμότης, [prev. work]109; joined with εὔνοια, 5th-6th c.BC: Isocrates Orator 5.114, 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 18.5]]; with πραότης, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Isocrates Orator 5.116]]; with χρηστότης, [Refs 4th c.AD+ [4th c.AD: Iamblichus Philosophus cited in 5th c.AD: Stobaeus, Joannes 4.5.76; φ. λόγων]]courtesy, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 18.298; τῆς παρὰ τουτωνὶ τιμῆς καὶ φ. [prev. work]209; φ. διὰ τῶν λόγων 2nd c.BC: Polybius Historicus 28.17.11; φ. προσάγειν τινί [prev. author] 1.81.8; φ. εἰς or πρὸς τοὺς αἰχμαλώτους, [prev. work] 79.8, 11]]; ὑπὸ φιλανθρωπίας Pl.[same place]; μετὰ φ. [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Isocrates Orator 15]] [same place]; clemency, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 7.5.73; so φιλανθρωπίᾳ [prev. author] “Ages.” 1.22]]; the intercourse of lovers, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aeschines Orator 1.171]]: plural, acts of kindness, courtesies, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 8.70, 25.86, 2nd c.BC: Polybius Historicus 36.17.13, 1st c.BC: Philodemus Gadarensis Epigrammaticus “Rh.” 2.160 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus, etc.]]

__I.b
ἡ σὴ φ. as a form of address, your Clemency, [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [PRyl. 296 (2nd c.AD), etc.]]

__I.2
of God, love to man, [NT.Tit.3.4, +others]

__II
of things, ἡ τοῦ ὀνόματος (i. e. νόμος) φ. its mildness, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 24.156]]; ἡ φ. τῆς τέχνης, of agriculture, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Oeconomicus” 15.4, compare 4th c.BC: Aeschines Orator 2.15]]; χώρα πάσης φ. ἐστερημένη, of a desert country, [Refs 1st c.BC+ [1st c.BC: Diodorus Siculus Historicus 17.50]]; in disease, mild symptoms, [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd c.AD: Galenus Medicus 19.219.]]

__III
concession, privilege, [Refs 2nd c.BC+ [“UPZ” 162 vii 21 (2nd c.BC), “OGI” 139.20 (Egypt, 2nd c.BC), “Rev.Phil.” 10 (1936).253 (from Ilium)]]; θεία φ. imperial grant, [Refs 3rd c.AD+ [“SIG” 888.102 (Scaptopara, 3rd c.AD).]]

LSJ / STEPBible (TFLSJ)
Included with:  φῐλάνθρωπ-ος, ον,
loving mankind, humane, benevolent, tender-hearted, and, in weaker sense, kind, courteous, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Epicharmus Comicus [274]; φ. καὶ φιλαθήναιος καὶ φιλόσοφος 5th-6th c.BC: Isocrates Orator “Epistulae” 5.2; φ. καὶ φιλόπολις [prev. author] 2.15; δημοτικὸς καὶ φ. 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Memorabilia” 1.2.60; ψυχὴν φιλανθρωπότατος [prev. author] “Cyr.” 1.2.1]]; φ. δὲ παύεσθαι τρόπου, of Prometheus, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Prometheus Vinctus” 11, compare 28]]; of animals that attach themselves to men, as of dogs, gentle, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Cynegeticus” 6.25]]; of horses, [Refs [[prev. author] “Eq.” 2.3]]; τὸ φιλάνθρωπον, ={φιλανθρωπία}, [Refs 1st c.BC+ [1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus “Cat.Ma.” 3, etc.; τὸ φ. καὶ μεταδοτικόν 1st c.BC: Philodemus Philosophus “περὶ οἰκονομίας” p.54J.]]; τὰ φιλάνθρωπα humane treatment, τῶν φ. τυχεῖν [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [“PCair.Zen.” 638.13 (3rd c.BC)]]; kindnesses, [Refs 2nd c.BC+ [2nd c.BC: Polybius Historicus 10.38.3, 12.5.3, etc.]]

__2
of the gods, loving men, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Symposium” 189c (_superlative_), “Lg.” 713d, 1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus “Numa” 4.]]

__II
of things, humane, humanizing, χάρις δικαία καὶ φ. [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Fragmenta” 953.41; γεωργία 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Oeconomicus” 19.17; ψηφίσματα [prev. author] “Vect.” 3.6; λόγοι 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 45.4]]; τρόπος, in Music, [Refs 1st c.AD+ [1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus 2.1135c, etc.]]; of wines, generous, [Refs [[prev. author] “Cleom.” 13 (_comparative_), compare 2.680b.]]

__II.2
appealing to human feeling, of situations, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Poetica” 1452b38, +others]] (less probably, satisfying the sense of poetic justice).

__II.3
in Medicine texts, of diet, generous, τροφὴ -οτέρα, opposed to ὀλίγη, [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd c.AD: Galenus Medicus 1.211]]; but of a medical treatise, popular, [Refs [[prev. author] 15.551 (_comparative_).]]

__III
φιλάνθρωπα, τά, concessions, grants, privileges, immunities, [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [“OGI” 221.14 (Ilium, 3rd c.BC), “PCair.Zen.” 37.11 (3rd c.BC), “SIG” 548.3 (Delph., 3rd c.BC), 2nd c.BC: Polybius Historicus 4.26.8, “UPZ” 162v 22, +others (2nd c.BC), “OGI” 331.42 (Pergam., 2nd c.BC)]], Epist.Jul.Caes. cited in [Refs 1st c.BC+ [1st c.AD: Josephus Historicus “Antiquitates Judaicae” 14.10.2, 1st c.BC: Diodorus Siculus Historicus 32.4, etc.]]; Thess. φιλάνθρουπα [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [“IG” 9(2).517.16 (Larissa, 3rd c.BC).]]

__III.b
singular, benefaction, endowment, gratuity, [Refs 1st c.BC+ [“BGU” 1202.10 (1st c.BC), “Mon.Anc.Gr.” 9.10, etc.]]

__III.c
singular, letter expressing friendly feelings, [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [“PSI” 4.439.32, “PCair.Zen.” 56.10 (both 3rd c.BC).]]

__IV
adverb, -ως τινὶ κεχρῆσθαι [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 19.225; φ. διακεῖσθαι πρός τινα 2nd c.BC: Polybius Historicus 1.68.13; φ. καὶ δημοτικῶς 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 24.24; θεοφιλῶς καὶ φ. 5th-6th c.BC: Isocrates Orator 9.43, compare 15.132, 1st c.BC: Philodemus Gadarensis Epigrammaticus “Herc.” 1251.14, etc.]]: superlative -ότατα[Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 24.191, 2nd-3rd c.AD: Dio Cassius Historicus 69.2.]]

__V
φῐλάνθρωπ-ον, τό, ={ἀπαρίνη}, [Refs 1st c.AD+ [1st c.AD: Dioscorides (Dioscurides) Medicus 3.90, 1st c.AD: Plinius Rerum Naturalium Scriptor “Historia Naturalis” 24.176]]; φιλανθρώπειος βοτάνη in [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd c.AD: Archigenes Medicus cited in 2nd c.AD: Galenus Medicus 12.574.]]

φῐλέω,
Aeolic dialect φίλημμι [Refs 7th c.BC+ [7th-6th c.BC: Sappho Lyrica 79, cf. Ead. “Oxy.” 1787 “fragment” 1 + 2.24]]; 2nd pers. singular φίλησθα Ead.22; late 3rd.pers. plural φίλεισι [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [“epigram Gr.” 990.12 (2nd c.AD: Balbilla Lyrica)]]: Boeotian dialect φίλειμι Hdn.Gr.[Refs [2.930: _Epic dialect_]]infinitive φιλήμεναι [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 22.265]]: Ionic dialect and Epic dialect imperfect φιλέεσκε [Refs [3.388, +others:]]future φιλήσω, Epic dialect infinitive φιλησέμεν [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 4.171]]: aorist 1 ἐφίλησα [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “P.” 2.16]], etc.: perfect πεφίληκα[Refs [[prev. work] 1.13]]:—middle, poetical [Refs [1]] aorist ἐφῑλάμη; 3rd.pers. singular ἐφίλατο, φίλατο, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 5.61, 20.304, Callias Epigrammaticus “Aet.Oxy.” 2080.55]]; 3rd.pers. plural φίλαντο [Refs 8th c.BC+ [3rd c.BC: Lycophron Tragicus 274; _imperative_ φῖλαι 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 5.117, 10.280]]; subjunctive φίλωνται [Refs 8th c.BC+ [“hymnus ad Cererem” 117, 8th-7th c.BC: Hesiodus Epicus “Theogonia” 97]]; but φίλατο as passive, [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [3rd c.BC: Apollonius Rhodius Epicus 3.66]]; also participle φιλάμενος [Refs [“IG” 14.1549 (from Rome):]] —passive, future middle φιλήσομαι in passive sense, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 1.123, 15.281, 5th c.BC: Antipho Orator 1.19]]: future 3 πεφιλήσομαι [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [3rd c.BC: Callimachus Epicus “Hymnus in Delum” 270]]: aorist ἐφιλήθην [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Hecuba” 1000, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Phaedrus” 253c]]: Epic dialect 3rd.pers. plural ἐφίληθεν [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 2.668]]: perfect πεφίλημαι [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “N.” 4.45, 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 1.9.28]]; Doric dialect participle πεφιλᾱμένος [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [3rd c.BC: Theocritus Poeta Bucolicus 3.3]]. [ῐ exceptin the forms ἐφίλατο, φῑλατο, etc.]: (φίλος):— love, regard with affection, opposed to μισεῖν, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 334c, 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Rhetorica” 1380b34; φιλήσω τὸν δῆμον τὸν Ἀθηναίων “IG” 12.15.36]]; (on its relation to sexual love see below 3); of the love of gods for men, φ. δέ ἑ μητίετα Ζεύς [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 2.197]]; πέρι γάρ μ᾽ ἐφίλει (of the love of the master for his swineherd) [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 14.146; (also ὃν περὶ κῆρι φ. Ζεὺς.. παντοίην φιλότητα 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 15.245, compare 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 9.117); μάλα τούς γε φ. ἑκάεργος Ἀπόλλων 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 16.94; εἰ.. Ἕκτορά περ φιλέεις καὶ κήδεαι αὐτοῦ 7.204, etc.]]; of love for a child reared, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 15.370; αἰ δὲ μὴ φίλει, ταχέως φιλήσει κωὐκὶ θέλοισα 7th-6th c.BC: Sappho Lyrica 1.23; λόγοις φιλοῦσαν οὐ στέργω φίλην 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Antigone” 543; φιλέων φιλέοντα 5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “P.” 10.66; ὃν δ᾽ ἐχρῆν φιλεῖν στυγεῖς 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Choephori” 907; μάλιστά σ᾽.. ἤχθηρα κἀφίλησ᾽ ἐν ἡμέρᾳ μιᾷ 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Electra” 1363; ὃν οἱ θεοὶ φιλοῦσιν ἀποθνῄσκει νέος 4th-3rd c.BC: Menander Comicus 125]]; ὅσα θεοὶ ἀνθρώποις οὓς φιλοῦσιν [διδόασιν] [Refs 1st c.BC+ [“SIG” 985.48 (Philadelphia, 1st c.BC)]]; οἱ φιλοῦντές τινα his friends, frequently in messages and letters, [NT+1st c.BC+ [“OGI” 184.10 (Philae, 1st c.BC), NT.Tit.3.15, “PSI” 8.971.30 (3rd-4th c.AD)]], etc.; φιλεῖν ἐμαυτήν, αὑτόν, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Helena” 999, “Med.” 86, etc.]]:—passive, to be beloved by one, ἐκ Διός [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 2.668; παρ᾽ αὐτῇ 13.627, etc.]]; τινι [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Hecuba” 1000.]]

__2
treat affectionately or kindly, especially welcome, entertain a guest, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 4.29, 5.135, 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 3.207, etc.; φίλος δ᾽ ἦν ἀνθρώποισιν, πάντας γὰρ φιλέεσκεν ὁδῷ ἔπι οἰκία ναίων 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 6.15; ξεῖνον ἐνὶ μεγάροισι φ. 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 8.42; ξεῖνον ἄγων ἐν δώμασι.. φιλέειν καὶ τιέμεν 15.543, compare 14.322]]; θεὸς (i. e. [Refs [8.208]]; etc.:—passive, παρ᾽ ἄμμι φιλήσεαι welcome shalt thou be in our house, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 1.123, compare 15.281.]]

__3
opposed to ἐρᾶν, τούτους μάλιστά φασι φιλεῖν ὧν ἂν ἐρῶσι regard with affection those for whom they have a passion, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Phaedrus” 231c; ὥστε οὐ μόνον φιλοῖο ἄν, ἀλλὰ καὶ ἐρῷο ὑπ᾽ ἀνθρώπων 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Hiero” 11.11, compare “Smp.” 8.21]]; εἰκὸς τὸ φιλεῖν τοὺς ἐρωμένους [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Analytica Priora” 70a6]]; but φ. is used of lovers, ἥ γ᾽ Εὐρυμάχῳ μισγέσκετο καὶ φιλέεσκεν [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 18.325; Λυσίθεος Μικίωνα φιλῖν φησι μάλισστα τῶν ἐν τῇ πόλει “IG” 12.924; οὐκ ἔστ᾽ ἐραστὴς ὅστις οὐκ ἀεὶ φιλεῖ 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Troades” 1051, compare 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 4.176 (_passive_), 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Lysistrata” 905]]; of the love of man for wife, ὅς τις ἀνὴρ ἀγαθὸς.. τὴν αὐτοῦ φιλέει (cherishes her) καὶ κήδεται ὡς καὶ ἐγὼ τὴν ἐκ θυμοῦ φίλεον [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 9.343, compare 486]]; τὴν αὐτὸς φιλέεσκεν loved and cherished as his wife, [Refs [[prev. work] 450]]; but ἐμὲ.. ἀτιμάζει, φιλέει δ᾽ ἀΐδηλον Ἄρηα (Hephaestus speaks of Aphrodite) [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 8.309: Comedy texts, ὦ Δῆμ᾽, ἐραστής εἰμι σὸς φιλῶ τέ σε καὶ κήδομαί σου 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Equites” 1341.]]

__3.b
of sexual intercourse, [Refs 5th c.AD+ [5th c.AD(?): Hesychius Legal icographus see at {βαίνειν}.]]

__4
show outward signs of love, especially kiss (not in [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Homerus Epicus), φ. τοῖσι στόμασι]] kiss on the mouth, opposed to τὰς παρειὰς φιλέονται, [NT+5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.134, compare 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 1.4.27, “Smp.” 9.5; κατὰ τὸ στόμα “Anthologia Graeca” 5.284 (6th c.AD: Agathias Historicus et Epigrammaticus); φιλήσω.. τὸ σὸν κάρα 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Coloneus” 1131; πατέρα.. περὶ χεῖρε βαλοῦσα φιλήσει 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Agamemnon” 1559 (_anapaest meter_), compare 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Aves” 671, 674, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Phaedrus” 255e, NT.Mark.14.44, etc.: with double _accusative_, τὸ φίλαμα, τὸ.. τὸν Ἄδωνιν.. ἀποθνάσκοντα φίλασεν]] the kiss wherewith she kissed him, [Refs 2nd c.BC+ [2nd c.BC: Moschus Bucolicus 3.69:]] —middle, τὰς παρειάς kiss each other's cheeks, Hdt. Alcaeus1.122c; ἐκ μέθης καὶ φιλονικίας 5th c.BC: Lysias Orator 3.43; διὰ στάσιν καὶ τὴν πρὸς ἀλλήλους φ. [prev. author] 33.4; εἰς πόλεμον καταστᾶσαι πρὸς ἀλλήλας καὶ φ. 5th-6th c.BC: Isocrates Orator 12.158; ἡ πρὸς ἀλλήλους ἔρις καὶ φ. 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 9.14, compare 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Timaeus” 88a; ἀλλά τίς με φ. εἴληφεν πρὸς τὰ εἰρημένα [prev. author] “La.” 194a; ὑπὸ τῆς πρὸς τἀμὰ ἔργα φ. 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 8.7.12; οὐ φιλονικίᾳ γε ἐρωτῶ 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Gorgias” 515b; ἐάν τις φιλονικίᾳ κριθῇ.. δρᾶν, τεθνάτω [prev. author] “Lg.” 938c]]; εἰς τοσοῦτον φιλονικίας ἐλθεῖν πρὸς τὴν πόλιν, ὥστε.. [NT+5th c.BC+ [[prev. author] “Mx.” 243b; ἐγένετο φ. ἐν αὐτοῖς τὸ τίς αὐτῶν δοκεῖ εἶναι μείζων NT.Luke.22.24: _plural_, φ. καὶ φιλοτιμίαι 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 548c, compare “Ti.” 90b, 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 18.246; περὶ ὁπόσων ἂν ἐγγένωνται ἀνθρώποις φ. 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 2.1.22; αἱ περὶ τὰς χορηγίας φ. 5th-6th c.BC: Isocrates Orator 7.53; φ. καὶ στάσεις 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Politica” 1308a31.]]

__2
in good sense, competition, emulation, emulous eagerness, ἔστω τούτων.. κατὰ νόμον ἅμιλλά τε καὶ φ. [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Leges” 834c; φ. αὐτοῖς ἔμβαλλε 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 7.1.18]]; φιλονικίας ἐμποιεῖν περὶ τῶν καλῶν ἔργων[Refs [[prev. work] 8.2.26; φ. ἐνέβαλε πρὸς ἀλλήλους τισί [prev. author] “Ages.” 2.8]]; especially in the games, πολλὴ φ. ἐγίγνετο [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 4.8.27, compare “Lac.” 4.2; διὰ φιλονικίαν [prev. author] “Hier.” 9.6; τῶν ἐργατῶν φ. πρὸς ἀλλήλους καὶ φιλοτιμία [prev. author] “Oec.” 21.10, compare “SIG” 685.12,36 (5th c.BC: Magnes Comicus Mae., 2nd c.BC, found in Crete).]] —On the form φιλονεικία, see at {φιλόνικος} near the end

deep_entry:

φιλό-νεικος, -ον
(νεῖκος, strife) [in LXX: Eze.3:7 (חָזָק ־מֵצַח)* ;]

LSJ / STEPBible (TFLSJ)
φῐλόνῑκ-ος, ον,
fond of victory, contentious.

__1
in bad sense, οὔτε δύσηρις ἐὼν οὔτ᾽ ὦν φ. ἄγαν [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “O.” 6.19 (-νεικ- codices vett.)]]; φ. ἐστι πρὸς ὃ ἂν ὁρμήσῃ [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Protagoras” 336e]]; coupled with φιλότιμος, [Refs [[prev. author] “R.” 545a, 582e (variant{-νεικ-}), compare 550b]]; ἐπίπονον καὶ φ. καὶ φιλότιμον.. καταστήσας τὸν βίον [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Lysias Orator 2.16.]]

__2
in good sense, of spirited horses, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “de Equitandi ratione” 9.8 (_superlative_)]]: of persons, φ. πρὸς τὸ μὴ ἐλλείπεσθαι [Refs 1st c.AD+ [[prev. author] “Mem.” 2.6.5, compare 1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus “Agesilaus” 2 (_superlative_)]]; τὸ φ., ={φιλονικία, ἔσῳζον τὸ φ. ἐν ταῖς ψυχαῖς} [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 7.5.64.]] adverb -κως in eager rivalry, παραθεῖν [Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. author] “Cyn.” 6.16; φ. ἔχειν πρὸς ἀλλήλους [prev. author] “Cyr.” 3.3.57, 8.4.4; φ. ἔχειν πρὸς τὸ εἰδέναι 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Gorgias” 505e]]; opposed to ἀνθρωπίνως, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator “Epistulae” 3.41. (In codices the forms φιλόνικος, -νικέω, -νικία and φιλόνεικος, -νεικέω, -νεικία]] occur, without any distinction of meaning, e.g. in [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Isocrates Orator we find περὶ τῶν καλλίστων ἐφιλονίκησαν 4.85, but τὰς θεὰς περὶ τοῦ κάλλους φιλονεικούσας 10.48; μὴ δύσερις ὢν.., μηδὲ πρὸς πάντας φιλόνικος 1.31; τῆς πρὸς ἡμᾶς φιλονικίας 4.19, but φιλονεικία in the same sense, 12.158]]; φιλόνῑκος is implied by [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Rhetorica” 1389a12 (where -νεικ-, though found in good codices, as also in 1363b1, 1368b21, 1370b33, “Phgn.” 809b35, must be _falsa lectio_), καὶ φιλότιμοι μέν εἰσι [οἱ νέοι], μᾶλλον δὲ φιλόνικοι· ὑπεροχῆς γὰρ ἐπιθυμεῖ ἡ νεότης· ἡ δὲ νίκη ὑπεροχή τις,compare 2nd c.AD(?): Pollianus Epigrammaticus 1.178, “Anecdota Graeca - Bekker” 315]]; the compound of φιλο- and νεῖκος would be Φιλονεική; the sense

__A
contentious arises naturally from fond of victory; in [Refs 8th c.BC+ [“SIG” 685 (see. φιλονικία entry near the end) we have φιλονικίαν 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 12, 36, and φιλονικίᾳ in “OGI” 335.7 (Pergam., decree of Pitane, 2nd c.BC)]]; -νῑκ- is also found in late documents, as [Refs 6th c.AD+ [“POxy.” 157.1 (6th c.AD).)]]

deep_entry:
Abbott-Smith / STEPBible (TBESG)
φίλος, -η, -ον
[in LXX chiefly for רֵעַ, אָהַב ;]
__1. pass., beloved, dear (Hom., Eur., al.).
__2. Act., loving, friendly (in cl. less frequently and only in poets): Act.19:31. As subst., a friend;
__(a) masc., ὁ φ.: Luk.7:6 11:5 14:10 15:6 16:9 21:16 23:12, Act.27:3, 3Jn.14; opposite to δοῦλος, Jhn.15:15; φ. ἀναγκαῖοι, Act.10:24; with genitive subj., Mat.11:19, Luk.7:34 11:6, 8 12:4 14:12 15:29, Jhn.11:11 15:13-14; ὁ φ. τοῦ νυμφίου, Jhn.3:29; τ. Καίσαρος (see Deiss., BS 167; LAE, 382 f.), Jhn.19:12; θεοῦ (see Hort, in l), Jas.2:23; with genitive of thing(s), τ, κόσμου, Jas.4:4;
__(b) fem., ἡ φ., Luk.15:9,†
(AS)

---

LSJ / STEPBible (TFLSJ)
φίλος, η, ον,
also ος, ον [Refs 8th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “O.” 2.93: [ῐ: but 8th c.BC: Homerus Epicus uses the _vocative_ φίλε]] with ῑ at the beginning of a verse, see below].

__I
passive, beloved, dear, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 1.20, etc.; παῖδε φίλω 7.279]]; frequently with dative, dear to one, μάλα οἱ φ. ἦεν [Refs [1.381; φ. ἀθανάτοισι θεοῖσι 20.347, etc.: _vocative_, φίλε κασίγνητε (at the beginning of the line) 4.155, 5.359]]; with neuter nouns, φίλε τέκνον [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 2.363, 3.184, etc.; but φίλον τέκος 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 3.162]]; also φίλος for φίλε (Attic dialect, accusative to [Refs 8th c.BC+ [2nd c.AD: Apollonius Dyscolus Grammaticus “de Syntaxi;” 213.28), φίλος ὦ Μενέλαε 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 4.189, compare 9.601, 21.106, +others, 5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “N.” 3.76, 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Prometheus Vinctus” 545 (Lyric poetry), 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Supplices” 277 (Lyric poetry), 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Nubes” 1168 (Lyric poetry)]]: genitive added to the vocative, φίλ᾽ ἀνδρῶν [Refs 5th c.BC+ [3rd c.BC: Theocritus Poeta Bucolicus 15.74, 24.40; ὦ φίλα γυναικῶν 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Alcestis” 460 (Lyric poetry): as]] substantive:

__I.a
φίλος, ὁ, friend, κουρίδιος φίλος, i.e. husband, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 15.22]]; φίλοι friends, kith and kin, νόσφιφίλων [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 14.256; τῆλεφίλων 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 2.333, compare 6.287]]; φ. μέγιστος my greatest friend, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Ajax” 1331]]; φίλοι οἱ ἐγγυτάτω, οἱ ἔγγιστα, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Lysias Orator 1.41 codices, 2nd c.BC: Polybius Historicus 9.24.2; after 8th c.BC: Homerus Epicus]] frequently with a genitive, ὁ Διὸς φίλος [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Prometheus Vinctus” 306]]; τοὺς ἐμαυτοῦ φ., τοὺς τούτων φ., [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aeschines Orator 1.47; φ. ἐμός 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Philoctetes” 421]]; τῶν ἐμε̄ν φ.[Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. work] 509; τοὺς σφετέρους φ. 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Historia Graeca (Hellenica)” 4.8.25: proverbial, ἔστιν ὁ φ. ἄλλος αὐτός]] a friend is another self, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Ethica Nicomachea” 1166a31; κοινὰ τὰ τῶν φ. 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Phaedrus” 279c, compare 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Ethica Nicomachea” 1159b31; οὐθεὶς φ. ᾧ πολλοὶ φ. [prev. author] “EE” 1245b20]]; also of friends or allies, opposed to πολέμιοι, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Historia Graeca (Hellenica)” 6.5.48; φ. καὶ σύμμαχος 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 9.12, etc.]]; of a lover, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Memorabilia” 3.11.4 (in bad sense, “Lac.” 2.13)]]; φίλε my friend, as a form of courteous address, [NT.Luke.14.10, etc.]; in relation to things, οἱ μουσικῆς φ. [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Fragmenta” 580.3; ἀληθείας 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 487a; τῶν εἰδῶν [prev. author] “Sph.” 248a; Χίους φ. ποιῆσαι 5th c.BC: Lysias Orator 14.36, etc.; ποιεῖσθαι 2nd c.AD: Lucianus Sophista “Pisc.” 38; κτᾶσθαι 5th-6th c.BC: Isocrates Orator 2.27, compare 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 2.40; φίλους τιθέντες τούς γε πολεμιωτάτους 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Hecuba” 848; φίλῳ χρῆσθαί τινι 5th c.BC: Antipho Orator 5.63; ἡμᾶς ἔχειν φίλους 5th-6th c.BC: Andocides Orator 1.40; for 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 3.49, see at {φίλιος}.]]

__I.b
φίλη, ἡ, dear one, friend, κλῦτε, φίλαι [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 4.722; λόγοις ἐγὼ φιλοῦσαν οὐ στέργω φίλην 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Antigone” 543]]; of a wife, φίλην τινὰ ἄγεσθαι take as one's wife, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 9.146, 288]]; ἡ Ξέρξου φ., of his mother, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Persae” 832]]; of a mistress, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Memorabilia” 2.1.23, 3.11.16; φίλην ποιήσασθαί τινα 5th c.BC: Antipho Orator 1.14.]]

__I.c
φίλον, τό, an object of love, τὸ φ. σέβεσθαι to reverence what the city loves, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Coloneus” 187 (Lyric poetry)]]: addressed to persons, darling, φ. ἐμόν [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Ecclesiazusae” 952 (Lyric poetry); so φίλτατον [prev. work] 970]]; τὰ φίλτατα one's nearest and dearest, dear ones, such as wife and children, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Persae” 851, “Eu.” 216, 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Tyrannus” 366, “OC” 1110, 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Medea” 16]]: see at {φίλτατο; τἀμὰ φίλα, τὰ σὰ φ}., [Refs [[prev. author] “Ion” 523 (troch.), 613.]]

__I.d
οἱ πρῶτοι φίλοι, a title at the Ptolemaic court, [Refs 2nd c.BC+ [“OGI” 99.3, “PTeb.” 11.4 (2nd c.BC)]], etc.; or simply οἱ φ. τοῦ βασιλέως [Refs [“OGI” 100.1; or οἱ φ. alone, [prev. work] 115.4; τῶν φ. και διοικητοῦ]] one of the king's friends and dioecetes, [Refs 2nd c.BC+ [“PTeb.” 79.56 (2nd c.BC).]]

__I.2
of things, pleasant, welcome, δόσις ὀλίγη τε φ. τε [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 6.208, compare 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 1.167: with _dative_ _person_, αἰεὶ γάρ τοι ἔρις τε φίλη 5.891, compare 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 8.248, 13.295; οὐ φίλα τοι ἐρέω 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 7.104]]; δαίμοσιν πράσσειν φίλα their pleasure, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Prometheus Vinctus” 660, compare below 11.]]

__I.2.b
frequently as predicate, φίλον ἐστί or γίγνεταί μοι pleases me, it is after my own heart, εἴ πού τοι φίλον ἐστί [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 7.320]]; μὴ φ. Διὶ πατρὶ γένοιτο[Refs 8th c.BC+ [[prev. work] 316, compare 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 7.387; εἰ τόδε πᾶσι φ. καὶ ἡδὺ γένοιτο 4.17; καί τοι φ. ἔπλετο θυμῷ 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 13.145, etc.; τοῦτο μὲν ἴτω ὅπῃ τῷ θεῷ φίλον 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Apologia” 19a]]: less frequently with infinitive, οὐ μὲν Τυδέϊ γ᾽ ὧδε φίλον πτωσκαζέμεν [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 4.372; πεφιδέσθαι ἐνὶ φρεσὶ φίλτερον ἦεν Τρώων 21.101, compare 24.334, 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 14.378; so ταῦτα δαίμονί κοω φίλον ἦν οὕτω γενέσθαι 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.87, compare 108, 4.97: rarely with]]participle, εἰ τόδ᾽ αὐτῷ φιλον κεκλημένῳ if it please him to be so called, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Agamemnon” 161 (Lyric poetry)]]: agreeing with plural, αἰεί τοι τὰ κάκ᾽ ἐστὶ φίλα φρεσὶ μαντεύεσθαι [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 1.107, compare 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 17.15; ἔνθα φίλ᾽ ὀπταλέα κρέα ἔδμεναι 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 4.345; σοὶ δ᾽ ἔργα φίλ᾽ ἔστω μέτρια κοσμεῖν 8th-7th c.BC: Hesiodus Epicus “Opera et Dies” 306.]]

__I.2.c
in [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Homerus Epicus]] and early Poets, one's own; frequently of limbs, life, etc., φίλον δ᾽ ἐξαίνυτο θυμόν he took away dear life, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 5.155, compare 22.58; κατεπλήγη φίλον ἦτορ 3.31; εἰς ὅ κε.. μοι φίλα γούνατ᾽ ὀρώρῃ 9.610; φίλον κατὰ λαιμόν 19.209]]; especially of one's nearest kin, πατὴρ φ. [Refs 8th c.BC+ [22.408, 7th-6th c.BC: Sappho Lyrica “Papyrus fragments” in E. Diehl, 20 a. 11; ἄλοχος φ. 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 5.480: compare φίλτατος: as a standing epithet when no affection is implied, μητρὶ φίλῃ Ἀλθαίῃ χωόμενος κῆρ]] angry with his own mother, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 9.555]]: simply to denote possession, φίλα εἵματα [Refs [2.261]]; φ. πόνος their wonted labour, [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [3rd c.BC: Theocritus Poeta Bucolicus 21.20.]]

__I.2.d
applied to the numbers [Refs 4th c.AD+ [284 and 220, 4th c.AD: Iamblichus Philosophus “in Nicomachi arithmeticam introductionem” p.35P.]]

__II

φοῖνιξ, ῑκος, ὁ, ἡ,
Phoenician, Φοῖνιξ ἀνὴρ ἀπατήλια εἰδώς [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 14.288, compare 13.272, 15.415; ὡς Φ. ἀνήρ, Σιδώνιος κάπηλος 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Fragmenta” 909.]]

__2
feminine, γυνή Φοίνισσα [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 15.417]]; Φοίνισσαι, name of plays by Euripides, Phrynichus, etc.; also Φ. ἐμπολά [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “P.” 2.67]]; χθών, νᾶσος, etc., [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Phoenissae” 6, 204 (Lyric poetry), etc.; Φ. βοά [prev. work] 301 (Lyric poetry)]]; κώπη [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [[prev. author] “Hel.” 1272; Φ. ἄμπεχος “PCair.Zen.” 33.14 (3rd c.BC).]]

__II
Carthaginian, ἀλαλατός [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “P.” 1.72; also _feminine_, Φοίνισσαι νῆες 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 1.116, 1st c.BC: Diodorus Siculus Historicus 13.80.]]

__B
φοῖνιξ, ῑκος, ὁ, purple or crimson, because the discovery and earliest use of this colour was ascribed to the Phoenicians, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 4.141, 6.219, 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 23.201, etc.:]] —hence,

__B.2
as adjective (feminine φοίνισσα [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus (see. below)]]; φοῖνιξ as feminine, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Troades” 815)]], blood-bay, of a horse, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 23.454]]; of red cattle, φοίνισσα ἀγέλα [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “P.” 4.205, compare 3rd c.BC: Theocritus Poeta Bucolicus 25.128]]: of the colour of fire, φοίνισσα φλόξ [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “P.” 1.24]]; πυρὸς φ. πνοά E.[same place]; also φ. ἱμάντες [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Simonides Lyricus 17; πέπλοι 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Helena” 181 (Lyric poetry), etc.]]

__B.II
date-palm, Phoenix dactylifera, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 6.163, “hymnus ad Apollinem” 117, 5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “Fragmenta.” 75 14 (uncertain), 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Hecuba” 458 (Lyric poetry), 1st c.BC: Diodorus Siculus Historicus 2.53; τόξα ἐκ φοίνικος σπάθης πεποιημένα 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 7.69, etc.]]: the male and female distinguished by [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus as [ὁ φ.] ἔρσην and [ἡ φ.] βαλανηφόρος, 1.193 (but the latter is _masculine_, [prev. passage] and in 4.172, 182); φοινίκων.. τῶν καρπίμων οἱ μὲν ἄρρενες αἱ δὲ θήλειαι 4th-3rd c.BC: Theophrastus Philosophus “Historia Plantarum” 2.6.6, but αἱ ἀπὸ τῶν ἀρρένων πρὸς τοὺς θήλεις [βοήθειαι] [prev. work] 2.8.4.]]

__B.II.2
palm-frond, as a badge of victory, Arist [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [“MM” 1196a36, 1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus 2.723b, etc.; τὸν φ. τινὶ ἀποδοῦναι 3rd c.BC: Chrysippus Stoicus 3.175.]]

__B.II.3
date, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Hellanicus Historicus 56J., 5th c.BC: Epicharmus Comicus 18, 4th c.BC: Antiphanes Comicus 65, 4th c.BC: Ephippus Comicus 24; more correctly, τοῦφοίνικος ὁ καρπός 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.193; καρπὸς φοίνικος 5th c.BC: Hermippus Comicus 63.22 (hexameters)]]; compare φοινικοβάλανος.

__B.III
ὁ χαμαιρριφής dwarf-palm, Chamaerops humilis, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-3rd c.BC: Theophrastus Philosophus “Historia Plantarum” 2.6.11.]]

__B.III.2
a Bactrian tree, Mazri palm, Nannorhops ritchieana, [Refs [[prev. work] 4.4.8.]]

__B.III.3
a sea-plant, Callophyllis laciniata, [Refs [[prev. work] 4.6.2, 10.]]

__B.III.4
rye-grass, Lolium perenne, [Refs 1st c.AD+ [1st c.AD: Dioscorides (Dioscurides) Medicus 4.43.]]

__B.IV
a musical instrument, like a guitar, invented by the Phoenicians, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 4.192, 4th c.BC: Ephorus Historicus 4 1st c.AD: Josephus Historicus, Phillis 2 (_plural_), Scamon 3]]; but so called because made from the Delian palm, accusative to [Refs [Semus 1.]]

__B.V
the fabulous bird phoenix, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th-7th c.BC: Hesiodus Epicus “Fragmenta” 171.4, 4th c.BC: Antiphanes Comicus 175; from Arabia _accusative_ to 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 2.73]]; but from India, [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd-3rd c.AD: Philostratus Sophista “Vita Apollonii” 3.49: proverbial, φοίνικος ἔτη βιοῦν 2nd c.AD: Lucianus Sophista “Herm.” 53.]]

__B.VI
an ornament, [LXX.Eze.41.25.]

__B.VII
perfume prepared from the fronds of the date-palm, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-3rd c.BC: Theophrastus Philosophus “de Odoribus” 28.]]

__B.VIII
a fish, [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd-3rd c.AD: Aelianus “De Natura Animalium - Ar.Byzantine Epit.” 12.24.]]

__B.IX
a bandage, [Refs 1st c.AD+ [1st-2nd c.AD: Heliodorus Medicus cited in 4th c.AD: Oribasius Medicus 49.11.2.]]

__B.X
={εὐρύνοτος}, [Refs [Agathemerus Geographus 2.7.]]

__B.XI
φ. ἐν ὁπλῇ, a disease of the hoof, [Refs [“Hippiatrica” 10.]]

__B.XII
an eye-salve, [Refs 4th c.AD+ [6th c.AD: Aëtius Medicus 7.116. [In all senses of the word ῑ in _genitive_, but _nominative_ φοῖνιξ, not φοίνιξ, Hdn.Gr. cited in 4th-5th c.AD: Choeroboscus Grammaticus “in Thd.” 1.292.]]]

LSJ / STEPBible (TFLSJ)
φρήν, ἡ,
genitive φρενός, plural φρένες, genitive φρενῶν, dative φρεσί: older dative plural φρασί (ν) [Refs 6th c.BC+ [“IG” 12.971 (6th c.BC), 5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “N.” 3.62, “BMus.Inscription” 909 (Halic., 1st c.BC): (see. entry near the end)]]:

__I
midriff, κραδία φρένα λακτίζει [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Prometheus Vinctus” 881 (_anapaest meter_)]]; elsewhere always in plural, ἔνθα φρένες ἔρχαται ἀμφ᾽ ἁδινὸν κῆρ [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 16.481, compare 5th c.BC: Hippocrates Medicus “περὶ ἀρχαίης ἰητρικῇς” 22, “Art.” 41]]; τὰς φρένας διάφραγμα εἰς τὸ μέσον αὐτῶν (i.e. τοῦ θώρακος καὶ τοῦ κύτους) τιθέντες [Refs 8th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Timaeus” 70a; τοῦτο δὲ τὸ διάζωμα καλοῦσί τινες φρένας, ὃ διορίζει τόν τε πλεύμονα καὶ τὴν καρδίαν 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “de Partibus Animalium” 672b11, compare “HA” 496b11, 506a6; also, in 8th c.BC: Homerus Epicus, more vaguely, πρὸς στῆθος ὅθι φρένες ἧπαρ ἔχουσι 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 9.301; μένεος φρένες ἀμφὶ μέλαιναι πίμπλαντ᾽ 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 1.103, +others; φρένας.. εἰς αὐτὰς τυπείς 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Prometheus Vinctus” 363, compare “Eu.” 159 (Lyric poetry).]]

__I.2
heart, as seat of the passions, e.g. of fear, τρομέοντο δέ οἱ φρένες ἐντός [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 10.10]]; of joy and grief, φρένα τέρπεσθαι φόρμιγγι [Refs [9.186; γάνυται φρένα ποιμήν 13.493; τί σε φρένας ἵκετοπένθο; 1.362; ἄχος πύκασε φρένας 8.124; ἔρως φρένας ἀμφεκάλυψε 3.442]]; of anger, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 6.147]]; of courage, ἕνα φρεσὶ θυμὸν ἔχοντες [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 13.487; ἐς φρένα θυμὸς ἀγέρθη 22.475, compare 8.202]], etc.; of bodily appetites, such as hunger, etc., [Refs [11.89]]: the shades of the dead are without it, ψυχὴ καὶ εἴδωλον, ἀτὰρ φρένες οὐκ ἔνι πάμπαν [Refs [23.104]] (except the shade of Teiresias, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 10.493)]]: so generally in Poets, φρενὸς ἔνδοθεν ἄλγεα κεῖται [Refs 6th c.BC+ [6th c.BC: Solon Lyricus cited in 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Ἀθηναίων Πολιτεία” 5.2; κῆλα δαιμόνων θέλγει φρένας 5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “P.” 1.12; φόβος μ᾽ ἔχει φρένας 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Supplices” 379; μαινομένα φρενί [prev. author] “Th.” 484 (Lyric poetry); στυγεῖν μιᾷ φρενί [prev. author] “Eu.” 986 (Lyric poetry); Διὸς γὰρ δυσπαραίτητοι φ. [prev. author] “Pr.” 34]]; ἐκ φρενός from one's very heart, ὁ ἐκ φρενὸς λόγος a sincere speech, [Refs [[prev. author] “Ch.” 107; ἐτύμως δακρυχέων ἐκ φρενός [prev. author] “Th.” 919 (Lyric poetry)]]; οὐκ ἀπ᾽ ἄκρας φρενός not superficially and carelessly, [Refs [[prev. author] “Ag.” 805 (_anapaest meter_); φρενὸς ἐκ φιλίας [prev. work] 1515 (_anapaest meter_), compare 546]]; φῦσαι φρένας to produce a haughty spirit, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Electra” 1463.]]

__I.3
mind, as seat of the mental faculties, perception, thought, ἔγνω ᾗσιν ἐνὶ φ. [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 22.296; μή μοι ταῦτα νόει φρεσί 9.600]]; μετὰ φρεσὶ μερμηρίξαι, βάλλεσθαι, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 10.438, 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 9.434; ἴδμεν ἐνὶ φρεσίν 2.301]]; τῷ γὰρ ἐπὶ φρεσί θῆκε put in his mind, suggested it,[Refs [1.55; σφῶϊν δ᾽ ὧδε θεῶν τις ἐνὶ φρεσὶ ποιήσειεν 13.55; ἐν φρεσὶ θέσθε ἕκαστος [prev. work] 121, compare 1.297, etc.; φρένας παραπεῖσαι, πείθειν, 7.120, 16.842]]; ἐπιγνάμπτει φρένας (variant for{νόον}) ἐσθλῶν [Refs [9.514; Διὸς ἐτράπετο φρήν 10.45]]; ἀνὴρ φρένας ἀφνειός rich (only) in his imagination, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th-7th c.BC: Hesiodus Epicus “Opera et Dies” 455]]; ὀρθᾷ, ἐλευθέρᾳ φρενί, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “O.” 8.24, “P.” 2.57; φρένες γὰρ αὐτοῦ θυμὸν ᾠακοστρόφουν 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Persae” 767; ἡ γλῶσσ᾽ ὀμώμοχ᾽, ἡ δὲ φ. ἀνώμοτος 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Hippolytus” 612; κατὰ φρένα καὶ κατὰ θυμόν 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 1.193, +others]]: plural, wits, Κύκλωπα περὶ φρένας ἤλυθε οἶνος [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 9.362, compare 454, 18.331; πλήγη φρένας ἂς πάρος εἶχεν 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 13.394; ἐκ γὰρ πλήγη φρένας 16.403; βλάπτε φρένας Ζεὺς ἡμετέρας 15.724; ἐξ... τοι θεοὶ φρένας ὤλεσαν 7.360; φρένας ἄφρων, φρένας ἠλέ or ἠλεέ, 4.104, 15.128, 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 2.243]]: of losing one's wits, φρενῶν ἀφεστάναι, ἐκστῆναι, μεθεστάναι, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Philoctetes” 865, 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Orestes” 1021, “Ba.” 944; τὰς φ. ἐκβάλλειν 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Antigone” 648; ἔξω φρενῶν 5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “O.” 7.47; φρενῶν οὐκ ἔνδον ὤν 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Heraclidae” 709; φρενῶν κεκομμένος 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Agamemnon” 479 (Lyric poetry); κενός 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Antigone” 754; τητώμενοι [prev. author] “El.” 1326]]; ἔξεδροι, παράκοποι, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Hippolytus” 935, “Ba.” 33; ποῦ ποτ᾽ εἶ φρενῶ; 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Electra” 390; φρένες διάστροφοι 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Prometheus Vinctus” 673, 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Ajax” 447; μαργότης φρενῶν [prev. author] “fragment” 846; ἀνακίνησις φρενῶν [prev. author] “OT” 727, etc.]]; of persons in their senses, ἐπήβολος φρενῶν [Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. author] “Ant.” 492; ἀνδρὸς νοῦν ἔχοντος καὶ φρένας 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Ranae” 535 (Lyric poetry)]] (so in later Prose, οἱ φρένας ἔχοντες [Refs 5th c.BC+ [1st c.BC: Philodemus Philosophus “περὶ ποιημάτων” 5.19, “Rh.” 1.240S.; οἱ τῶν σοφιστῶν τὰς κοινὰς φ. ἔχοντες [prev. work]202S.); also ἔσω φρενῶν λέγειν 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Agamemnon” 1052; γράφου φρενῶν ἔσω 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Philoctetes” 1325; τῆς λεπτότητος τῶν φ. 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Nubes” 153]]; φρένες, opposed to σῶμα, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 3.134; so αἱ σάρκες αἱ κεναὶ φρενῶν 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Electra” 387]]; attributed to animals, μετὰ φρεσὶ γίγνεται ἀλκή [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 4.245, compare 16.157, etc.]]—The word is not common in early Prose, τίς αὐτῶν νόος ἢ φρή; [Refs 1st c.AD+ [1st c.AD(?): Heraclitus 104]]; συμφορὰ τῶν φ., i.e. madness, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Andocides Orator 2.7; παραλλάττει τῶν φ. 5th c.BC: Lysias Orator “Fragmenta” 90; καρποῦ μὲν ἀφθονία φρενῶν δὲ ἀφορία 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Symposium” 4.55; νοῦς καὶ φρένες 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 18.324, compare 25.33.]]

__I.4
will, purpose, οὔ τι Διὸς βέομαι φρεσίν [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 15.194; σῆς ἀπεστάτουν φ. 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Antigone” 993, compare “OC” 1182]].—In usage there is little or no distinction observable between singular and plural, but the singular is not found in Prose (except [Refs 5th c.BC+ [1st c.AD(?): Heraclitus [same place]) or Comedy texts (except in _paratragoedia_, 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Ranae” 886).]]
