φρίσσω,
Attic dialect φρίττω [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 387c]]: future φρίξω [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd c.AD: Galenus Medicus 13.365]]: aorist ἔφριξα [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 13.339, etc.]]: perfect πέφρῑκα [Refs [11.383, etc.]]; poetry participle πεφρίκοντες [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “P.” 4.183]]: pluperfect ἐπεφρίκει [Refs 1st c.AD+ [1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus 2.781e, 4th c.AD: Alciphro Epistolographus 1.1:]] —middle, aorist 1 ἐφριξάμην falsa lectio in [Refs 8th c.BC+ [2nd c.AD: Polyaenus Historicus 4.6.7. [ῑ by nature, hence to be accented φρῖσσον in 8th-7th c.BC: Hesiodus Epicus “Scutum Herculis” 171, φρῖξαι 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Electra” 1408 (Lyric poetry)]]]:—to be rough or uneven on the surface, bristle, φρίσσουσιν ἄρουραι (i.e. σταχύεσσι) [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 23.599; φρίξας κάρπιμος στάχυς 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Supplices” 31]]; of a line of battle, ἔφριξεν μάχη ἐγχείῃσιν [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 13.339; φάλαγγες σάκεσίν τε καὶ ἔγχεσι πεφρικυῖαι 4.282, compare 7.62]]; φρίξας εὐλόφῳ σφηκώματι, of the crest of a helmet, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Fragmenta” 341]]; of a tree, φρίσσουσα ζεφύροις [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Eleg.” 25; φιάλα χρυσῷ πεφρικυῖα 5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “I.” 6(5).40]]; χερσὶ δεξιωνύμοις ἔφριξεν αἰθήρ, of a crowd holding up their hands to vote, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Supplices” 608]]; of hair, mane, or bristles, bristle up, stand on end, μηδ᾽ ὀρθαὶ φρίσσωσιν [τρίχες] [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th-7th c.BC: Hesiodus Epicus “Opera et Dies” 540, compare 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Historia Animalium” 560b8, “Pr.” 888a38; ἔφριξαν ἔθειραι 3rd c.BC: Theocritus Poeta Bucolicus 25.244]]; of foliage, φύλλα πεφρικότα, opposed to κεκλιμένα, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-3rd c.BC: Theophrastus Philosophus “Historia Plantarum” 3.9.4: with _accusative_ of respect, φρίξας εὖ λοφιήν]] having set up his bristly mane, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 19.446; φ. τρίχας 8th-7th c.BC: Hesiodus Epicus “Scutum Herculis” 391]]; φ. νῶτον, αὐχένας, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 13.473, 8th-7th c.BC: Hesiodus Epicus “Scutum Herculis” 171; χαίταν 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Ranae” 822 (Lyric poetry)]]; also πτεροῖσι νῶτα πεφρίκοντες bristling on their backs with feathers, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “P.” 4.183; λέοντος δέρος χαίτῃ πεφρικός 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Phoenissae” 1121.]]

__2
ἄσθματι φρίσσων πνοάς ruckling in his throat, of one just dying, uncertain reading in [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “N.” 10.74.]]

__3
of the rippling surface of smooth water [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [compare (φρίξ 1), φ. θάλασσαι.. πνοιῇσι 2nd c.AD: Dionysius Periegeta 112, compare 4th c.AD: Alciphro Epistolographus 1.1]]; of breakers, ῥηγμῖνες φ. [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [3rd c.BC: Apollonius Rhodius Epicus 4.1575, compare 2nd-3rd c.AD: Aelianus “De Natura Animalium - Ar.Byzantine Epit.” 7.33]]; also of rain, φρίσσοντες ὄμβροι [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “P.” 4.81, explained by Scholia as φρίσσειν ποιοῦντες,compare ὁπόταν.. φρίσσων Βορέας ἐπισπέρχῃ [prev. author] “Parth.” 2.18.]]

__II
frequently of a feeling of chill, shiver, shudder:

__II.1
of the effect of cold, shiver, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th-7th c.BC: Hesiodus Epicus “Opera et Dies” 512, 5th c.BC: Hippocrates Medicus “περὶ παθῶν” 11, 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Problemata” 963a33, 965a33]]; χωρὶς τοῦ φρῖξαι unless he catch a chill, [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd c.AD: Galenus Medicus 10.803]]; of the teeth, chatter, [Refs 1st c.BC+ [1st c.BC: Dionysius Halicarnassensis “Ars Rhetorica” 10.9.]]

__II.2
of the effect of fear, shudder, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Electra” 1408 (Lyric poetry), “Tr.” 1044; πέφρικ᾽ ἐγὼ μέν, αὖός εἰμι τῷ δέει 4th-3rd c.BC: Menander Comicus “Ἐπιτρέποντες” 480; φ. γαῖα πόντος τε “Hymni Homerici” 27.8]]; ἅλω δὲ πολλὴν.. ἔφριζα δινήσαντος I shuddered when he swung the vast shield round, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Septem contra Thebas” 490]]; οὐ φρίττουσιν (i.e. animals) ὡς φρίττουσιν οἱ ἄνθρωποι [Refs 1st c.BC+ [1st c.BC: Philodemus Gadarensis Epigrammaticus “D.” 1.12]]: with accusative, shudder at one, οἵ τέ σε πεφρίκασι [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 11.383; πάντες δέ με πεφρίκασιν 24.775, compare 5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “O.” 7.38, 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Antigone” 997, 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Nubes” 1133; τῶν δημοτέων φ. τὸν ἥκιστον 3rd c.BC: Herodas Mimographus 2.30; τοὺς τελώνας πᾶσα νῦν θύρη φρίσσει [prev. author] 6.64; πεφρικέναι τὸν θάνατον 1st c.BC: Philodemus Philosophus “de Morte - Papiri Ercolanesi” 39; φρίττουσι τὴν σύντροφόν τε καὶ φίλην οἱ ἰχθύες θάλατταν 2nd-3rd c.AD: Aelianus “De Natura Animalium - Ar.Byzantine Epit.” 9.57: with _accusative_ et]]infinitive, πέφρικα.. Ἐρινὺν τελέσαι I tremble at the thought of her accomplishing.., [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Septem contra Thebas” 720 (Lyric poetry) (but not with _dative_, for ἐρετμοῖσι φρίξουσι]] they shall shudder at the oars is falsa lectio for{φρύξουσι} in Oracle texts cited in [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 8.96): with]]participle, πέφρικα λεύσσων I shudder at seeing, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Supplices” 346; φ. σε δερκομένα [prev. author] “Pr.” 540 (Lyric poetry), compare 695 (Lyric poetry)]]: with infinitive, fear to do, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 21.135: with _preposition_, φ. πρὸς τοὺς πόνους 1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus 2.8f; φ. πρὸς τὴν ἀκοὴν τῆς Ῥωμαίων τέχνης 4th c.AD: Libanius Sophista “Orationes” 24.16; φ. ὑπὲρ ὧν προσήκει παθεῖν 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 51.9.]]

__II.3
feel a holy thrill or awe at, ἐν ἱερῷ φ. ἅπαντα καὶ προσκυνεῖν [Refs 1st c.AD+ [1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus 2.26b; τοὺς θεοὺς πέφρικα 4th c.AD: Julianus Imperator “Orationes” 7.212b, +others]]

__II.4
thrill with passionate joy, ἔφριξ᾽ ἔρωτι [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Ajax” 693, 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Fragmenta - American Journal of Philology” 387]].—Rare in early Prose, except in the sense of shuddering, fearing, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 387c, “Phdr.” 251a, D.[same places]]]

Abbott-Smith / STEPBible (TBESG)
φρονέω, -ῶ
(φρήν), [in LXX: Deu.32:29, Zec.9:2 (חָכָם), Psa.94:8 (שָׂכַל hi.), Isa.44:18 (בִּין) Isa.44:28, Est.8:13, Wis.1:1 14:30, 1Ma.10:20, 2Ma.9:12;  2Ma.14:8 2Mac 14:26 * ;]
__1. to have understanding (Hon., al.).
__2. to think, to be minded in a certain way: ὡς νήπιος, 1Co.13:11; with accusative (usually neut., adj., or pron., as frequently in cl.), ὃ δεῖ, Rom.12:3; ἃ, Act.28:22; τοῦτο, Php.3:15; τι ἑτέρως, ib.; οὐδὲν ἄλλο, Gal.5:10; τ. αὐτὸ φ. (Deiss., BS, 256), to be of the same mind, 2Co.13:11, Php.2:2 4:2; id. before εἰς (ἐν) ἀλλήλους(οις), Rom.12:16 15:5; τ. ἓν φ., Php.2:2 (Lft., in l); before ὑπέρ, Php.1:7.
__3. to have in mind, be mindful of, think of (Hdt., Xen., al.; Es, 1Mac, ll. with): τὰ τ. θεοῦ, opposite to τ. τ. ἀνθρώπων, Mat.16:23, Mrk.8:33; τὰ τ. σαρκός, opposite to τ. τ. πνεύρατος, Rom.8:5; τ. ἐπίγεια, Php.3:19; τὰ ἄνω, opposite to τ. ἐπὶ τ. γῆς, Col.3:2; τοῦτο φρονεῖτε (RV, have this mind in you), Php.2:5; ὑψηλά, Rom.12:16; φ. ἡμέραν (to observe a day), Rom.14:6; before ὑπέρ, Php.4:10 (cf. κατα-, παρα-, περι-, ὑπερ-φρσνέω).†

LSJ / STEPBible (TFLSJ)
φρον-έω,
Epic dialect subjunctive φρονέῃσι [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 7.75]]: Epic dialect imperfect φρόνεον [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 17.286, φρονέεσκον 3rd c.BC: Apollonius Rhodius Epicus 4.1164]]: future -ήσω[Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Ecclesiazusae” 630 (_anapaest meter_)]], etc.: aorist ἐφρόνησα [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.60, 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Eumenides” 115, etc.]]: perfect πεφρόνηκα [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Empedocles Poeta Philosophus 103.1, 5th-6th c.BC: Isocrates Orator 5.124, 1st c.BC: Diodorus Siculus Historicus 18.66]]:—passive, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “de Xenophane” 980a9]]; imperative φρονείσθω variant for{φρονεῖτε} in [NT.Phil.2.5]:—to be minded, either of reflection or of purpose: hence,

__I
have understanding, be wise, prudent, rare in [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Homerus Epicus, ἄριστοι.. μάχεσθαί τε φρονέειν τε]] best both in battle and counsel, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 6.79]]: but frequently in Trag. and Attic dialect, [Ζῆνα] τὸν φρονεῖν βροτοὺς ὁδώσαντα [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Agamemnon” 176 (Lyric poetry); φρονούντως πρὸς φρονοῦντας ἐννέπεις [prev. author] “Supp.” 204, compare 176; φρονεῖν γὰρ οἱ ταχεῖς οὐκ ἀσφαλεῖς 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Tyrannus” 617; φρονεῖν οἶδεν μόνη [prev. author] “Tr.” 313]]; λίαν φ. to be over-wise, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Iphigenia Aulidensis” 924; φ. πλέον 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Hp.Mi.” 371a; τὸ φρονεῖν]]understanding, prudence, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Antigone” 1347 (_anapaest meter_), 1353 (_anapaest meter_)]]; κράτιστοι φρονεῖν [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Antipho Orator 2.1.1; καὶ φ. καὶ συμπράττειν 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 5.5.44; εἰδέναι καὶ φ. 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus Alcaeus1.133c; τὸ φ. καὶ τὸ νοεῖν [prev. author] “Phlb.” 11b; λέγειν τε καὶ φ. [prev. author] “Phdr.” 266b, compare 5th-6th c.BC: Isocrates Orator 4.50; τῷ φρονεῖν τε καὶ σωφρονεῖν 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Leges” 712a]]; τὸ μὴ φρονοῦν, of an infant, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Choephori” 753; ἐπειδὴ τάχιστα ἤρχετο φ. 4th c.BC: Isaeus Orator 9.20; ἡ φρονοῦσα ἡλικία 4th c.BC: Aeschines Orator 1.139: Comedy texts of fish, ἰχθῦς φρονοῦντας]]full-grown, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Ephippus Comicus 21.3; ζῷον λογικὸν καὶ φρονοῦν 1st c.BC: Philodemus Philosophus “de Pietate - Herkulanische Studien” 15: with _accusative_, φρονῆσαι τὰ κυριώτατα]] to be wise in respect of the most important matters, [Refs [[prev. author] “Rh.” 2.35S.]]

__I.2
with adverbs, εὖ φρονεῖν think rightly, περί τινος [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 2.16]]; to be sane (compare infr. IV), [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Bacchae” 851, 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Nubes” 817, 5th c.BC: Lysias Orator 19.41, etc.; κέρδιστον εὖ φρονοῦντα μὴ φρονεῖν δοκεῖν 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Prometheus Vinctus” 387; οἱ φρονοῦντες εὖ κρατοῦσι πανταχοῦ 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Ajax” 1252, compare “El.” 394, 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Orestes” 99, +others (but εὖ φρ.,]] also, to be well disposed, see below [Refs [11.2)]]; κακῶς, καλῶς φ., [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 18.168, 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Tyrannus” 600, “Ant.” 557; ὀρθῶς φ. 5th-6th c.BC: Andocides Orator 2.23; ὀρθῶς φ. πρός τι 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Prometheus Vinctus” 1000]]; μῶρα, πλάγια φ., [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Ajax” 594, 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Iphigenia Aulidensis” 332 (troch.).]]

__I.3
think, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [1st c.AD(?): Heraclitus 113, 4th-5th c.BC: Parmenides Poeta Philosophus 16.3, 5th c.BC: Empedocles Poeta Philosophus 108.2, compare 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus]]de.An.427a19; ὡς.., ὅτι.., [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Antigone” 49, “OC” 872; φρόνει νιν ὡς ἥξοντα [prev. author] “Tr.” 289]]; mean, ἄλλα φ. καὶ ἄλλα λέγειν [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 9.54; ἕτερα μὲν λέγων, ἕτερα δὲ φρονῶν 4th-3rd c.BC: Dinarchus Orator 1.47; ὁ μὴ λέγων ἃ φρονεῖ 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 18.282, compare 19.224.]]

__I.4
feel by experience, know full well, σοὶ μὲν δοκεῖν ταῦτ᾽ ἔστ᾽, ἐμοὶ δ᾽ ἄγαν φρονεῖν [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Ajax” 942, compare “OC” 1741 (Lyric poetry)]]; πειρώμενος ὅ τι φρονέοιεν [τὰ μαντήϊα] to test the knowledge of the oracles, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.46.]]

__II
to be fain that.., with accusative et infinitive, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 3.98]]: with infinitive, to be minded to do, [Refs [9.608, 17.286]]; without infinitive, οἱ δ᾽ ἰθὺς φρόνεον [ἰέναι] were minded to go right on ward, [Refs [13.135, compare 12.124]]; ᾗπερ δὴ φρονέω [τελέσαι[Refs [] 9.310; φρονῶν ἔπρασσον]]of set purpose, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Coloneus” 271]]: in Prose, mean, intend, τοῦτο φρονεῖ ἡμῶν ἡ.. ἀγωγή this is what your bringing us here means, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 5.85.]]

__II.2
frequently with neuter adjective,

__II.2.a
φ. τινί τινα to have certain thoughts for or towards any one, to be so and so minded towards him, πατρὶ φίλα φρονέων kindly minded towards him, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 4.219, compare 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 6.313, etc.; κακὰ φρονέουσι.. ἀλλήλοισιν 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 22.264; τῷ ὀλοὰ φρονέων 16.701; μαλακὰ φ. ἐσλοῖς 5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “N.” 4.95; πιστά τινι [prev. author] “O.” 3.17; φρονοῦντας ἄριστα αὐτοῖς 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Plutus” 577 (_anapaest meter_): with _adverbs_, εὖ φρονεῖν τισι (compare above 1.2) 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 7.74, compare 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Agamemnon” 1436, etc.]]; φρονεῖς εὖ τοῖς ἠγγελμένοις you rejoice at them, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. author] “Ch.” 774; also εἰς ὑμᾶς εὖ φ. 5th-6th c.BC: Andocides Orator 2.4; τισὶ καλῶς φ. “SIG” 527.38 (Crete, 3rd c.BC)]]; τοιαῦτα περί τινος φ. [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Isocrates Orator 3.60]]: to be minded so and so, think or purpose such and such things, ἀγαθὰ φ. [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 6.162, 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 1.43]]; φίλα φ.[Refs 8th c.BC+ [[prev. work] 307; κακά 17.596; τὰ φρονέεις ἅ τ᾽ ἐγώ περ 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 4.361]]; κρυπτάδια φ. to have secret purposes, [Refs [1.542]]; ἀταλὰ φ. to be gaily disposed,[Refs 8th c.BC+ [18.567, 8th-7th c.BC: Hesiodus Epicus “Theogonia” 989]]; πυκινὰ φ. have wise thoughts, be cunningly minded, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 9.445]]; ἐφημέρια φ. think only of the passing day,[Refs 8th c.BC+ [21.85; θεοῖσιν ἶσα φ. 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 5.441; θνητὰ φ. 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Fragmenta” 590 (_anapaest meter_), 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Alcestis” 799; ἀθάνατα 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Timaeus” 90c; οὐ κατ᾽ ἄνθρωπον φ. 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Septem contra Thebas” 425, 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Ajax” 777; ἐπὶ ταῖς εὐτυχίαις ὑπὲρ ἄνθρωπον φ. 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 8.7.3; μηδὲν ὑπὲρ τὴν πήραν φ. 2nd c.AD: Lucianus Sophista “Tim.” 57: also καίρια φ. 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Electra” 228 (Lyric poetry); σώφρονα [prev. author] “fragment” 64; οὐ τὰ ἄριστα φ. 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 2.22; ἡ πόλις χεῖρον φ. 5th-6th c.BC: Isocrates Orator 8.126]]; τυραννικὰ φ. to have tyranny in mind, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Vespae” 507 (troch.)]]; ἀρχαιϊκὰ φ. to have old-fashioned notions, [Refs [[prev. author] “Nu.” 821]]; τὰ τοῦ θεοῦ, τὰ τῆς σαρκὸς φ., [NT.Matt.16.23, NT.Rom.8.5]; also οὐ παρδάλιος τόσσον μένος ὅσσον Πάνθου υἷες φρονέουσιν the panther's courage is not so great as is the spirit of the sons of Panthus, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 17.23.]]

__II.2.b
especially frequently in the phrase μέγα φρονεῖν to be high-minded, have high thoughts, to be high-spirited, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 11.296, 13.156]]; of lions and boars, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [16.758, 11.325, compare 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 7.5.62; φρονεῖ γὰρ ὡς γυνὴ μέγα 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Tyrannus” 1078, compare 5th c.BC: Lysias Orator 2.48, 5th-6th c.BC: Isocrates Orator 4.132]]; in Attic dialect, frequently in bad sense, to be presumptuous, ἐφ᾽ ἑαυτῷ, ἑαυτοῖς μέγα φ., [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 6.16, 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Historia Graeca (Hellenica)” 7.1.27 (also μεγάλα φ. 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Acharnenses” 988]]; φ. ἐφ᾽ αὑτῷ τηλικοῦτον ἡλίκον εἰκός.. of birds as giving omens, τοὺς ἄνωθεν φρονιμωτάτους οἰωνούς [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Electra” 1058 (Lyric poetry).]]

__III.3.b
sagacious, of animals, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Politicus” 263d, 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Historia Animalium” 488b15, “PA” 648a8 (_comparative_), 687a8 (_superlative_), “GA” 753a11 (_comparative_), +others]]

__III.4
τὸ φ. practical wisdom, prudence, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Fragmenta” 52.9 (Lyric poetry), 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 586d, +others]]; opposed to τὸ ἄφρον, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. author] “Phdr.” 235e; ἰέναι ἐπὶ τὸ φρονιμώτερον 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Symposium” 8.14: _plural_, ἄπορος ἐπὶ φρόνιμα]] helpless in point of wisdom, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Tyrannus” 692 (Lyric poetry); τὰ -ώτερα ποιεῖν 5th-6th c.BC: Isocrates Orator 15.211.]]

adverb -μως[Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Equites” 1364, “Av.” 1333 (Lyric poetry), 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Laches” 192e, etc.]]; opposed to ἀλόγως, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Isocrates Orator 3.9; φ. ἔχειν 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 3.3.57; διακεῖσθαι 5th-6th c.BC: Isocrates Orator 8.114]]: comparative φρονιμώτερον, διακεῖσθαι τῶν ἄλλων [Refs [[prev. author] 2.10]]; -ωτέρως [Refs [[prev. author] 13.15]]: superlative -ώτατα, λέγειν [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Apologia Socratis” 20.]]

deep_entry:
Abbott-Smith / STEPBible (TBESG)
φροντίζω
(φροντίς, thought), [in LXX: 1Ki.9:5 (דָּאַג), Psa.40:17 (חָשַׁב), al. ;]
to give heed, take thought (in cl. usually absol., with accusative, with genitive), with inf., Tit.3:8 (see Bl., § 69, 4; M, Pr., 206 f.).†
(AS)

---

LSJ / STEPBible (TFLSJ)
φροντ-ίζω,
future Attic dialect ιῶ [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Troades” 1234, 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Nubes” 125, 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Memorabilia” 2.1.24, etc.]]: aorist ἐφρόντισα [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Persae” 245 (troch.)]], etc.: perfect πεφρόντικα [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Alcestis” 773, 5th c.BC: Eupolis Comicus 352, 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Ecclesiazusae” 263, etc.:]] —middle, future φροντιοῦμαι, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Iphigenia Taurica” 343 (assuming variant)]]:— passive, see infr. IV: (φροντίς):

__I
absolutely, consider, reflect, take thought, φροντίζων εὑρίσκω [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 5.24, compare 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Prometheus Vinctus” 1034, “Supp.” 418 (Lyric poetry), 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Nubes” 75, +others; ζητεῖν καὶ φ. καὶ βουλεύεσθαι 5th-6th c.BC: Isocrates Orator 9.41]]; give heed, pay attention, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 558a.]]

__I.2
to be thoughtful or anxious, πεφροντικὸς βλέπεις you look careworn, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Alcestis” 773; τίς δ᾽ ἔστιν ὁ.. φροντίζω; 2nd c.AD: Phrynichus Atticista]] Comedy texts 21; τὸ πεφροντικός, as substantive, care, thought, [Refs 1st c.AD+ [1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus 2.983b.]]

__II
with an object,

__II.1
with accusative of things, consider, ponder, ἔχθος ἐμόν [Refs 6th c.BC+ [6th c.BC: Theognis Elegiacus 1247; Σωκράτης.. -ίζων τι ἕστηκε 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Symposium” 220c; δεινά.. τοῖς τεκοῦσι φροντίσαι 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Persae” 245 (troch.)]]; [ὀνείρατα] [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 7.16]].; devise, μηχανήν [Refs [[prev. author] 5.67; τοῦτο φ. ὅκως μὴ λείψομαι [prev. author] 7.8.ά]] (nisi to be read τοῦτον); ἐκεῖνο δ᾽ οὐ πεφροντίκαμεν, ὅτῳ τρόπῳ.. μνημονεύσομεν [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Ecclesiazusae” 263]]; also directly followed by a relative clause, φ. ἥντιν᾽ [ὁδὸν] ἴω προτέρην [Refs 6th c.BC+ [6th c.BC: Theognis Elegiacus 912; φ. πρὸς ἑωυτὸν ὡς δώσει 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 8.100; ἐφρόντισ᾽ ᾗ διέφθαρται βίος 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Hippolytus” 376; φ. ὅ τι βούλεται ἑαυτὸν καλεῖν 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 39.2, compare 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Memorabilia” 3.7.6]]; φ. τί ποτε τοῦτ᾽ ἔστι [Refs [[prev. author] “Cyr.” 3.3.32]]; take thought that.., see to it that, ὅπως.. [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Apologia” 29e, 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 2.6.8, “PHib.” 1.82.10 (3rd c.BC); later ἵνα.. [prev. work] 43.7 (3rd c.BC), 2nd c.BC: Polybius Historicus 2.8.8]]; ὡς.. [Refs 2nd c.BC+ [“PTeb.” 10.6, +others (2nd c.BC)]]: with infinitive, [NT+3rd c.AD+ [NT.Tit.3.8, “BGU” 8 ii 4 (3rd c.AD), etc.: followed by μή]] with subjunctive, φ. μὴ ἄριστον ᾖ [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.155, compare 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Memorabilia” 4.2.39, compare below 111]]; οὐδὲν φ. εἰ.. [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Gorgias” 503a]]; φ. εἴτε.., εἴτε.. [Refs [[prev. author] “R.” 344e]]: with infinitive, [Refs 1st c.AD+ [1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus “Fabius Maximus” 12]]: with participle, φροντίζεθ᾽ ὡς μαχούμενοι [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Electra” 1370.]]

__II.2
with genitive, take thought for, give heed to a thing, regard it, mostly with a negative expressed or implied, σοὶ δ᾽ ἔμεθεν μὲν ἀπήχθετο φροντίσδην [Refs 7th c.BC+ [7th-6th c.BC: Sappho Lyrica 41 (assuming variant); Περσέων οὐδὲν φ. 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 3.97, compare 100, 151, 4.167; γῆ αὐχμοῦ φροντίζουσα οὐδέν [prev. author] 4.198; Πενθέως οὐ φροντίσας 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Bacchae” 637 (troch.); μηδὲν ὅρκου φροντίσῃς 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Lysistrata” 915; τῶν οἰκετῶν.. μηδὲν φ. 5th c.BC: Lysias Orator 7.17]]; μησενὸς ἄλλου φ., πλὴν ὅπως.. [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Isocrates Orator 15.305; οὐδὲ τῶν νόμων φροντίζουσι 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 563d; τὸ παράπαν θεῶν μὴ φ. [prev. author] “Lg.” 701c]]; conversely, τοὺς θεοὺς φ. οὐδὲν τῶν ἀνθρωπίνων[Refs 4th c.BC+ [[prev. work] 888c, compare 4th-3rd c.BC: Menander Comicus “Ἐπιτρέποντες” 552]]: so with adverbs implying a negative, σμικρὰ φ. ὄχλου [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Orestes” 801 (troch.); ὀλίγον φ. δεσποτῶν [prev. author] “Cyc.” 163; σμικρὸν φ. Σωκράτους 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Phaedo” 91c]]; also without negative, οὗπερ δεῖ μάλιστα φ. [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Heraclidae” 242; τοῦ μὲν ὀνόματος φ., τοῦ δὲ πράγματος ἀμελεῖν 5th-6th c.BC: Andocides Orator 4.27; σφόδρα σοῦ φ. 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Memorabilia” 3.11.10; εἰ σοφὸς ἀνὴρ ταφῆς φροντιεῖ 2nd c.BC: Demetrius Lacon Philosophus “Herc.” 1012.26]]; later, to be steward or bailiff, τῶν ὑπαρχόντων τινός [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [“BGU” 300.4 (2nd c.AD): so with Preps., φ. περί τινος]] to be concerned or anxious about, σφέων αὐτῶν πέρι [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 8.36, compare 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Memorabilia” 1.1.12, 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Hippolytus” 709; ὑπέρ τινος 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Euthyphro” 4d; ὑπὲρ σωτηρίας 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 1.2; less frequently in this sense with _accusative_ only, [Σωκράτης] τἄλλα μὲν πεφρόντικεν 5th c.BC: Eupolis Comicus 352; ἄλλο οὐδὲν φροντίζειν 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Gorgias” 501e; ἀλλ᾽ οὐ τὰ βίου.. δεῖ φροντίσαι 4th-3rd c.BC: Menander Comicus 330; ἡ δ᾽ ἐφρόντισ᾽ οὐδὲ ἕν 5th c.BC: Cratinus Comicus 302 (troch.).]]

__II.2.b
later, see to, provide for, furnish, σιτάριον, χρήσιμα, [Refs 2nd c.BC+ [“ZUP” 73.5, 69.2 (both 2nd c.BC)]]; τὰ ἐπιβάλλοντα τῇ ἑορτῇ [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [“BGU” 845.18 (2nd c.AD)]]; μηδὲν φροντίσας [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Pherecrates Comicus 80.]]

__II.2.c
with accusative et participle, οὐ φροντίζει σκληρῶς σε καθήμενον [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Equites” 783 (_anapaest meter_).]]

__II.3
the object is frequently unexpressed, ἐφρόντιζε ἱστορέων, i. e. inquired carefully, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.56]]; οἲ τοὺς φίλους βλάπτοντες οὐ φροντίζετε who though ye do mischief to your friends reck not of it, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Hecuba” 256]]; μὴ φροντίσῃς heed it not [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Vespae” 228; οὐ, μὰ Δἴ, οὐδ᾽ ἐφρόντισα [prev. author] “Ra.” 493, compare 650, “Pl.” 215, 704]]; with participle, τοιαῦτα.. γιγνόμενα.. ὁρῶντες οὐδὲν φροντίζετε [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Andocides Orator 4.23.]]

__III
middle in signification [Refs 5th c.BC+ [11.1, φροντιζόμενον μή.. 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Hiero” 7.10: with _accusative_, 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Iphigenia Taurica” 343 (assuming variant).]]

__IV
later in passive, to be an object of thought or care, πεφροντισμένος carefully thought out; λόγος [Refs 1st c.BC+ [1st c.BC: Diodorus Siculus Historicus 15.78, 16.32; λόγοι πεφρ. εὖ 2nd-3rd c.AD: Philostratus Sophista “Vitae Sophistarum” 1.11; τρέφονται τροφῇ πεφροντισμένῃ 2nd-3rd c.AD: Aelianus “De Natura Animalium - Ar.Byzantine Epit.” 7.9]]; of a ward, ἡ-ομένη ὑπ᾽ ἐμοῦ θυγατριδῆ [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [“BGU” 300.16 (2nd c.AD).]]

φρουρέω, -ῶ
(φρουρός, a guard), [in LXX: I Est.4:56, Jdth.3:6, Wis.17:16, 1Ma.11:3 * ;]
to guard, keep under guard, protect or keep by guarding: 2Co.11:32; metaphorically, Gal.3:23, Php.4:7, 1Pe.1:5.†

LSJ / STEPBible (TFLSJ)
φρουρ-έω,
poetical imperfect φρούρουν [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Trachiniae” 915]]: future -ήσω[Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Prometheus Vinctus” 31, etc.]]: aorist ἐφρούρησα [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 2.30, etc.:]] —middle, future -ήσομαι in passive sense, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Ion” 603:]] —passive, aorist ἐφρουρήθην[Refs [[prev. work] 1390]]: perfect πεφρούρημαι [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Hippocrates Medicus “ἐπιστολαί” 23 (2nd c.AD: Pseudo-Democritus Alchemista), (δια-) 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Fragmenta - American Journal of Philology” 265]]: (φρουρός):—keep watch or guard, ἐν Ἐλεφαντίνῃ [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus [same place], compare 9.106, “IG” 12.99.21, “OGI” 38.1 (3rd c.BC)]], etc.; of ships, φ. περὶ Ναύπακτον or ἐν Ναυπάκτῳ, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 2.80, 83]]; φ. ἐπί τινι to keep watch over.., [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Alcestis” 35 (_anapaest meter_)]]; οἱ φρουροῦντες the guardians, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Leges” 763d; συνάπτειν.. φρουροῦντας.. φρουροῦσι [prev. work] 758b]]; proverbial, ἐν παντὶ.. σκορπίος φ. λίθῳ [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Fragmenta” 37]]; generally, 'keep a sharp look-out', [Refs [[prev. author] “Tr.” 915.]]

__II
transitive, watch, guard, τὴν χώρην [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 3.90; τὴν γέφυραν [prev. author] 4.133; τὴν ἀτραπόν [prev. author] 7.217; βρέτας 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Eumenides” 1024; σὲ δαίμων.. φρουρήσας τύχοι 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Tyrannus” 1479]]; τὴν Ποτείδαιαν φ. garrison it, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 3. [17], compare 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 6.1.17, etc.]]; φυλακαῖσι φ. σῶμ᾽ Ὀδυσσέως set a watch over.. [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Cyclops” 690: _metaphorically_, φ. πέτραν]] keep watch over it, of Prometheus, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Prometheus Vinctus” 31]]; στόμα εὔφημον φρουρεῖν ἀγαθόν keep silence, [NT+5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Ion” 98 (_anapaest meter_); ἡ εἰρήνη τοῦ θεοῦ.. φρουρήσει τὰς καρδίας ὑμῶν NT.Phil.4.7]]:—passive, to be watched or guarded, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 7.203, 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Eumenides” 218, 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Coloneus” 1013, 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Hecuba” 995, etc.]]: of the watch kept by besiegers, κύκλῳ φρουρούμενος ὑπὸ πάντων πολεμίων [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 579b.]]

__II.b
hold in subjection, opposed to παραφυλάττειν, [Refs 2nd c.BC+ [2nd c.BC: Polybius Historicus 18.4.6.]]

__II.c
Astrology texts, occupy, in passive, [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd c.AD: Vettius Valens Astrologus 106.18.]]

__II.d
bind, ἁλύσεσι πεφρουρημένος [Refs [“PMag.Par.” 1.3093.]]

__II.2
watch for, observe, φρουρῶν τόδ᾽ ἦμαρ [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Alcestis” 27; φ. ὄμμα ἐπὶ σῷ.. καιρῷ 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Philoctetes” 151 (Lyric poetry)]]; φ. χρέος to be observant of one's duty, [Refs [[prev. author] “El.” 74.]]

__III
middle, to be on one's guard against, beware of, with accusative, φρουρούμενος βέλεμνα [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Andromache” 1135]]:—active also in the same sense, ἐφρούρει μηδὲν ἐξαμαρτάνειν [Refs [[prev. author] “Supp.” 900]]; φ. ὅπως or ὅπως ἂν.., with subjunctive, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Electra” 1402, 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Helena” 742]]; φ. μή.., with subjunctive, [Refs [[prev. author] “El.” 1139.]]

φρυ-άσσομαι,
Attic dialect φρυάττομαι, properly of spirited, high-fed horses, neigh, whinny and prance, [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [3rd c.BC: Callimachus Epicus “Lavacrum Palladis” 2, “Anthologia Graeca” 5.201 (3rd c.BC: Asclepiades Epigrammaticus or 3rd c.BC: Posidippus Comicus), compare 6th c.AD: Thomas Epigrammaticus Mag. p.381R.]]; φ. πρὸς τοὺς ἀγῶνας neigh eagerly for the race, [Refs 1st c.AD+ [1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus “Lycurgus” 22]]; also of a cock, [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd-3rd c.AD: Aelianus “De Natura Animalium - Ar.Byzantine Epit.” 7.7, compare below 11.]]

deep_entry:
Abbott-Smith / STEPBible (TBESG)
φυλακή, -ῆς, ἡ
(φυλάσσω) [in LXX chiefly for מִשְׁמֶרֶת and  cogn. forms, also for כֶּלֶא etc. ;]
__(a) actively, a guarding, guard, watch (Hom., Plat., Xen., al.): cogn. accusative, φυλάσσειν φυλακάς, to keep watch, Luk.2:8;
__(b) of those who keep watch (as also Lat. custodia), a guard; pl., sentinels, a guard (Hom., al.): Act.12:10;
__(with) of the place where persons are kept under guard, a prison (Hdt., Thuc., al.): Mat.14:10, Mrk.6:17, Luk.3:20, Act.5:19, 2Co.6:5, 1Pe.3:19, Rev.18:2, al.;
__(d) of the time during which guard was kept by night (Lest. vigilia; Anthol.), a watch: Mat.14:25 24:43, Mrk.6:48, Luk.12:38
(AS)

---

LSJ / STEPBible (TFLSJ)
φῠλᾰκ-ή, ἡ,
(φύλαξ) watching or guarding, especially by night, φυλακῆς μνήσασθε [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 7.371]]; φυλακὰς ἔχειν keep watch and ward, [Refs [9.1, 471]]; φ. κατέχειν [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Troades” 194 (Lyric poetry)]]; φυλακὴ ἔχει αὐτόν watching engages him, variant in [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th-7th c.BC: Hesiodus Epicus “Fragmenta” 188.4; φ. νυκτερινή 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Vespae” 2: proverbial, γυμνῷ φυλακὴν ἐπιτάττειν]] tell an unarmed man to stand on the defensive, i.e. to give commands that cannot be obeyed, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Pherecrates Comicus 144, compare 4th-3rd c.BC: Philemo Comicus 12; περὶ φυλακῆς Εὐβοίας.. ἐπιμέλεσθαι “IG” 12.39.76]]; ὅπως ἀφανὴς εἴη ἡ φ. that there might be nothing visible to watch, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 4.67; φυλακὴν [τῶν τειχῶν] ἔρημον καταλιπεῖν 4th c.BC: Lycurgus Orator 17]]; φυλακὰς φυλάξειν keep watch and ward, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 2.6.10, compare 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Leges” 758d; τὴν ἐν θαλάττῃ φ. φυλάττειν 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 7.14; φ. ποιῆσαι 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 5.7.31; τὴν φ. ποιεῖσθαι 5th c.BC: Lysias Orator 12.16; φυλακὰς ποιήσασθαι 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 6.3.21; ἰσχυρὰς φ. ποιεῖσθαι [prev. author] “Cyr.” 1.6.37]]; φυλακὰς καταστήσασθαι, κατασκευάσασθαι, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Aves” 841, 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Historia Graeca (Hellenica)” 7.2.23.]]

__2
watch or guard, of persons, [NT+5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Protagoras” 321d (_plural_), NT.Act.12.10, etc.; φ. ἑωυτοῦ ποιεύμενός [τινας] 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 2.154]]; φ. τοῦ σώματος a body guard, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 23.3; τῶν σωμάτων 4th-3rd c.BC: Dinarchus Orator 1.9; φ. περὶ τὸ σῶμα 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 7.5.58, compare “PHib.” 1.59.5 (3rd c.BC)]], etc.; garrison of a place or fortress, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 2.30]]; ἡ ἐν τῇ Ναυπάκτῳ φ., of a squadron of ships, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 7.17, compare 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Historia Graeca (Hellenica)” 1.1.22.]]

__2.b
the rank of φύλακες, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 415c.]]

__3
station, post, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 10.408 (_plural_), 416 (_plural_), 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Historia Graeca (Hellenica)” 5.4.49; φυλακὰς προλιπών 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Rhesus” 18 (_anapaest meter_)]]; Διὸς φ., [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Pythagoras Philosophus]] name for the centre of the universe, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “de Caelo” 293b3.]]

__4
of time, a watch of the night, ἐπεὰν τῆς νυκτὸς ἦ δευτέρη φ. [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 9.51]]; πρώτης φ. ἀρχομένης Wilcken [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [“Chr.” 1 ii 18 (3rd c.BC)]]; φυλακαῖσι νυκτέροισιν [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Rhesus” 765; φ. νυκτερινὰς καὶ ἡμερινὰς καθιστάναι 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 1.6.43]]: of these there were three, accusative to [Refs 5th c.BC+ [Scholia 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Rhesus” 5]]; but five are mentioned in [Refs 7th c.BC+ [7th-6th c.BC: Stesichorus Lyricus 55, 4th-5th c.BC: Simonides Lyricus 219 A, 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Rhesus” 543 (Lyric poetry)]]; and the Roman division was four, [NT.Matt.14.25, 10th c.AD: Suidas Legal icographus]

__5
place for keeping others in, ward, prison, δημοσία φ. [NT+1st c.BC+ [1st c.BC: Diodorus Siculus Historicus 10.30; εἰς φυλακὴν βληθείς “Anthologia Graeca” 11.276 (1st c.AD: Lucillius Epigrammaticus); βαλεῖν τινὰ εἰς φ. NT.Matt.18.30, compare 2nd c.AD: Arrianus Historicus “Epicteti Dissertationes” 1.1.24; θέσθαι τινὰ ἐν φυλακῇ LXX.Gen.40.3, cf. NT.Matt.14.3]]; πολιτικὴ φ. the town-prison, [Refs 1st c.AD+ [POxy. 259.8 (1st c.AD).]]

__6
Astrology texts ={ταπείνωμα}, [Refs [“PMich.” in “Class.Phil.” 22.22 (_plural_).]]

__II
guarding, keeping, preserving, whether for security or custody, ἐν φυλακῇ ἔχειν τινά [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.24; ἐν φ. ἀδέσμῳ ἔχειν τινά 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 3.34; ἐν φυλακῇσι μεγάλῃσι ἔχεσθαι 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 2.99]]; τὸν Ἰσθμὸν ἔχειν ἐν φ. to keep the Isthmus guarded or occupied, [Refs [[prev. author] 7.207, compare 8.40]]; τὸν ἠνείκαντο γλώσσης χαρακτῆρα τοῦτον ἔχειν ἐν φ. to preserve the same character of language, [Refs 6th c.BC+ [[prev. author] 1.57; ἔχειν νόον ἐν φ. 6th c.BC: Theognis Elegiacus 439; τὰ παρὰ πᾶσιν ἐν πλείστῃ φ., παῖδας καὶ γυναῖκας 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 18.215; τὰ κατὰ τὸ στρατόπεδον διὰ φυλακῆς ἔχων 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 7.8; τὸν πλοῦν διὰ φ. ποιησάμενοι [prev. author] 8.39]]; στόματος φυλακᾷ κατασχεῖν φθόγγον probably in [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Agamemnon” 236 (Lyric poetry)]]; ἐν φ. σχεθέμεν μεγάλᾳ be very ware of, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “P.” 4.75]]; φυλακὴν ἔχειν, ={φυλάττεσθαι}, keep guard, be on the watch, περί τινα [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.39; φ. ἔχων εἴ κως δυναίμην.. [prev. work] 38]]; φ. ἔχειν μή.. [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 2.69]]; φ. λαμβάνειν μή.. [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-3rd c.BC: Menander Comicus “Περικειρομένη” 20]]; δεινῶς ἦσαν ἐν φυλακῇσι were straitly on their guard, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 3.152, compare 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Persae” 592 (Lyric poetry).]]

__II.2
custody of property, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Politica” 1309b6, “EN” 1120a9.]]

__II.3
safeguard, τὴν μεγίστην φ. ἀνῄρηκε τῆς πόλεως its chief safeguard, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Andocides Orator 4.19; φ. παρέχειν 5th-6th c.BC: Isocrates Orator 11.13]]; δημοκρατίας, μοναρχίας φ., [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Lysias Orator 25.28, 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Politica” 1315a8.]]

__III
(from middle) precaution, πολλῆς φ. ἔργον [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 537d; φ. θαυμαστῆς δεομένη [prev. author] “Lg.” 906a, +others, compare 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 5.99.]]

with genitive, precaution against, εὐλάβεια φ. κακοῦ [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Definitiones” 413d; ὑποψίας φυλακὴν ποιήσασθαι 5th c.BC: Antipho Orator 2.1.2; φ. τῶν πάντα μολυνόντων 4th-3rd c.BC: Epicurus Philosophus “Gnomologium Vaticanum - Kleine Schriften” 80, compare 73.]]

deep_entry:
Abbott-Smith / STEPBible (TBESG)
φυλάσσω
[in LXX chiefly and very frequently for שָׁמַר, also for נָצַר, etc. ;]
to guard, watch;
__(a) to guard or watch: with cogn. accusative, φυλακάς, Luk.2:8; with accusative of person(s), Act.12:4 28:16; pass., Luk.8:29, Act.23:35; with accusative of thing(s), Act.22:20;
__(b) to guard or protect: with accusative, Luk.11:21, Jhn.12:25 17:12, 2Th.3:3, 1Ti.6:20, 2Ti.1:12 1:14, 2Pe.2:5; ἑαυτὸν ἀπό, 1Jn.5:21 (Westc., in l); metaphorically of law, precept, etc., to keep, preserve, observe: Mat.19:20, Luk.11:28 18:21, Jhn.12:47, Act.7:53 16:4 21:24, Rom.2:26, Gal.6:13, 1Ti.5:21. Mid., to be on one's guard (against), keep oneself from, beware of: with accusative, Act.21:25, 2Ti.4:15; before ἀπό., Luk.12:15; ἵνα μή, 2Pe.3:17; as in LXX (Exo.12:17, Lev.18:4, al.), of laws, etc., to keep, observe: ταῦτα πάντα, Mrk.10:20 (cf. δια-φυάσσω).†
SYN.: τηρέω, q.v  (AS)

---

φῡλή, ἡ,
(φύω) properly, like{φῦλον}, a race, tribe; but accusative to [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Dicaearchus Historicus 9]] a union formed in an organized community (whether πόλις or ἔθνος): hence, tribe, i.e.

__I
a body of men united

__I.1
by supposed ties of blood and descent, clan, such as the three Dorian tribes, Rhetra cited in [Refs 5th c.BC+ [1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus “Lycurgus” 6, 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 5.68, 5th c.AD(?): Stephanus Byzantius s. vv. Ὑλλεῖς, Δυμᾶνες, “IG” 4.596 (from Argos)]]; of the four Ionic tribes, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 5.69, 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Ἀθηναίων Πολιτεία” 8.3, 1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus “Solon” 19, etc.]]; of the Laconian, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 4.145]]; of the old Roman, [Refs 1st c.BC+ [1st c.BC: Dionysius Halicarnassensis 2.7, etc.]]; of the Persian, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 1.2.5 and 12]]; of the Jewish, [LXX.Num.1.4, +others] (but also of subdivisions of the tribe (σκῆπτρον),[LXX+NT [LXX.1Ki.10.20.21), NT.Matt.19.28, etc.]]

__I.2
by local habitation, such as the ten local tribes at Athens formed by Cleisthenes, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 5.69, 6.131, “IG” 12.10.44, +others]]; or those formed by Servius at Rome, φ. τοπικαί, opposed to γενικαί, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [1st c.BC: Dionysius Halicarnassensis 4.14, compare 1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus “Romulus” 20; in Roman Egypt, “BGU” 1113.3 (1st c.BC), “PFlor.” 39.4 (4th c.AD), etc., compare (in general) 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Politica” 1264a8, 1300a25, 1309a12, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Leges” 753c, etc.]]

__I.3
subdivision of the priests in each Egyptian temple, [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [“OGI” 56.24 (Canopus, 3rd c.BC), “PAmh.” 2.112.7 (2nd c.AD), etc.]]

__II
military contingent furnished by a tribe, among the Athenians, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 6.111, “IG” 12.1085; ὁπλιτῶν 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 6.98, compare 3.90, 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Historia Graeca (Hellenica)” 4.2.19, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Leges” 755c, 755d; ταξίαρχος εἰς τὴν φυλὴν κατατάξας 5th c.BC: Lysias Orator 13.79.]]

__II.2
representatives of a tribe, on political bodies, φυλῆς πρυτανευούσης, προεδρευούσης, [Refs 2nd c.BC+ [“IG” 1.26a16, “SIG” 589.2 (Magn.Mae., 2nd c.BC), etc.]]

__III
of things, ={γένος}, kind, species, κατὰ φυλὰς διεκρίνομεν τὰ ἔπιπλα [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Oeconomicus” 9.6.]]

adverb -κῶς according to the laws of nature, [Refs [[prev. author] “Ph.” 198a23; opposed to λογικῶς, [prev. work] 204b10]]: comparative -ώτερον εἰπεῖν [Refs [[prev. author] “GC” 335b25.]]

LSJ / STEPBible (TFLSJ)
φύσις [ῠ], ἡ,
genitive φύσεως, poetry φύσεος probably (for the sake of meter) in [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Troades” 886, compare 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Vespae” 1282 (Lyric poetry), 1458 (Lyric poetry), _Ionic dialect_ φύσιος: dual φύσει]] (variant{φύση}) [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 410e]], (φύω):

__I
origin, φ. οὐδενός ἐστιν ἁπάντων θνητῶν οὐδὲ.. τελευτή [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Empedocles Poeta Philosophus 8.1 (compare 1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus 2.1112a); φ. βούλονται λέγειν γένεσιν τὴν περὶ τὰ πρῶτα 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Leges” 892c; ἡ φ. ἡ λεγομένη ὡς γένεσις ὁδός ἐστιν εἰς φύσιν 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Physica” 193b12; φ. λέγεται ἡ τῶν φυομένων γένεσις [prev. author] “Metaphorical” 1014b16]]; frequently of persons, birth, φύσει νεώτερος [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Coloneus” 1295, compare “Aj.” 1301, etc.; φύσι γεγονότες εὖ 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 7.134]]; φύσει, opposed to θέσει (by adoption), [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [3rd c.AD(?): Diogenes Laertius 9.25; φύσει Ἀμβρακιώτης, δημοποίητος δὲ Σικυώνιος 2nd c.AD: Athenaeus Epigrammaticus 4.183d]]; so ὁ κατὰ φύσιν πατήρ, υἱός, ἀδελφός, [Refs 2nd c.BC+ [2nd c.BC: Polybius Historicus 3.9.6, 3.12.3, 11.2.2]]; also in accusative, ἐκ πατρὸς ταὐτοῦ φύσιν [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Electra” 325]]; ἢ φίλων τις ἢ πρὸς αἵματος φύσιν[Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. work] 1125, compare 5th-6th c.BC: Isocrates Orator 3.42.]]

__I.2
growth, τριχῶν, παιδίου, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Hippocrates Medicus “περὶ φύσιος παιδίου” 20, 29, compare 27: _plural_, γενειάσεις καὶ φύσεις κεράτων 3rd c.AD: Plotinus Philosophus 4.3.13.]]

__II
the natural form or constitution of a person or thing as the result of growth (οἷον ἕκαστόν ἐστι τῆς γενέσεως τελεσθείσης, ταύτην φαμὲν τὴν φ. εἶναι ἑκάστου [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Politica” 1252b33): hence,]]

__II.1
nature, constitution, once in [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Homerus Epicus, καί μοι φύσιν αὐτοῦ (i.e. τοῦ φαρμάκου) ἔδειξε 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 10.303; φ. τῆς χώρης 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 2.5; τῆς Ἀττικῆς 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “de Vectigalibus” 1.2, compare “Oec.” 16.2, 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 18.146, etc.; τῆς τριχός 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “de Equitandi ratione” 5.5]]; αἵματος, ἀέρος, etc., [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “de Partibus Animalium” 648a21, “Mete.” 340a36, etc.: _plural_, φύσεις ἐγγιγνομένας καρπῶν καὶ δένδρων 5th-6th c.BC: Isocrates Orator 7.74; αἱ φ. καὶ δυνάμεις τῶν πολιτειῶν [prev. author] 12.134; ἡ τῶν ἀριθμῶν φ. 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 525c; ἡ τῶν πάντων φ. 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Memorabilia” 1.1.11, etc.; ἡ ἰδία τοῦ πράγματος φ. “IG” 22.1099.28 (Epist.Plotinae).]]

__II.2
outward form, appearance, μέζονας ἢ κατ᾽ ἀνθρώπων φύσιν [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 8.38]]; ἢ νόον ἤτοι φύσιν either in mind or outward form, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “N.” 6.5; οὐ γὰρ φ. Ὠαριωνείαν ἔλαχεν [prev. author] “I.” 4(3).49 (67); μορφῆς δ᾽ οὐχ ὁμόστολος φ. 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Supplices” 496; τὸν δὲ Λάϊον φύσιν τίν᾽ εἶχε φράζε 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Tyrannus” 740 (read εἷρπε, taking φ. with ἔχων),compare “Tr.” 379]]; δρακαίνης φ. ἔχουσαν ἀγρίαν probably in [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Bacchae” 1358; τὴν ἐμὴν ἰδὼν φ. 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Vespae” 1071 (troch.), compare “Nu.” 503; τὴν τοῦ σώματος φ. 5th-6th c.BC: Isocrates Orator 9.75.]]

__III
the regular order of nature, τύχη.. ἀβέβαιος, φ. δὲ αὐτάρκης [Refs 5th c.BC+ [3rd c.AD: Democritus Epigrammaticus 176; κατὰ φύσιν 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 444d, etc.]]; τρίχες κατὰ φύσιν πεφυκυῖαι growing naturally, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 2.38, compare 2nd c.AD: Alexander Rhetor 156.7 (troch.); κατὰ φύσιν νόμος ὁ πάντων βασιλεύς 5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “Fragmenta.” 169 (compare 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Gorgias” 488b); κατὰ φ. ποιεῖν 1st c.AD(?): Heraclitus 112]]; opposed to παρὰ φύσιν, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Phoenissae” 395, 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 6.17, etc.; παρὰ τὴν φ. 4th c.BC: Anaxippus Comicus 1.18]]; προδότης ἐκ φύσεως a traitor by nature, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aeschines Orator 2.165]]; πρὸ τῆς φ. ἥκειν εἰς θάνατον before the natural term, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus “Comp. Dem.Cic.” 5: frequently in _dative_ φύσει (ἐν φ. 5th c.BC: Hippocrates Medicus “Aër.” 14)]] by nature, naturally, opposed to τύχῃ, τέχνῃ, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Leges” 889b, compare “R.” 381b; φύσει τοιοῦτος 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Plutus” 275, compare 279, +others; ὁ ἄνθρωπος φ. πολιτικὸν ζῷόν ἐστι 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Politica” 1253a3]]; ὁ μὴ αὑτοῦ φ. ἀλλ᾽ ἄλλου ἄνθρωπος ὤν, οὗτος φ. δοῦλός ἐστιν[Refs 4th c.BC+ [[prev. work] 1254a15; φ. γὰρ οὐδεὶς δοῦλος ἐγενήθη ποτέ 4th-3rd c.BC: Philemo Comicus 95.2]]; opposed to νόμῳ (by convention), [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Philolaus Philosophus 9, Archelaus cited in 3rd c.AD(?): Diogenes Laertius 2.16, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Gorgias” 482e, compare “Prt.” 337d, etc.; τὰ μὲν τῶν νόμων ὁμολογηθέντα, οὐ φύντ᾽ ἐστίν, τὰ δὲ τῆς φύσεως φύντα, οὐχ ὁμολογηθέντα 5th c.BC: Antipho Sophista 44 “Ai” 32 (“Vorsokr.” 5); ἅπας ὁ τῶν ἀνθρώπων βίος φύσει καὶ νόμοις διοικεῖται 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 25.15; τοὺς τῆς φ. οὐκ ἔστι λανθάνειν νόμους 4th-3rd c.BC: Menander Comicus “Μονόστιχοι - Fragmenta Comicorum Graecorum” 492; οὐ σοφίᾳ, ἀλλὰ φύσει τινί 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Apologia” 22c; φ. μὴ πεφυκότα τοιαῦτα φωνεῖν 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Philoctetes” 79, compare 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Philebus” 14c, etc.; φύσει πάντα πάντες ὁμοίως πεφύκαμεν καὶ βάρβαροι καὶ Ἕλληνες εἶναι 5th c.BC: Antipho Sophista 44 “Bii” 10 (“Vorsokr.” 5)]]; φύσιν ἔχει with infinitive, it is natural, κῶς φύσιν ἔχει πολλὰς μυριάδας φονεῦσαι (i.e. τὸν Ἡρακλέα); [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 2.45, compare 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 473a]]; οὐκ ἔχει φύσιν it is contrary to nature,[Refs 4th c.BC+ [[prev. work] 489b; οὔτ᾽ εὔλογον οὔτ᾽ ἔχον ἐστὶ φύσιν 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 2.26; τὸ τόλμημα φύσιν οὐκ ἔχει 1st-2nd c.AD: Polemo Sophista “Callimachus” 36.]]

__IV
in Philosophy:

__IV.1

__IV.2

__IV.4
[Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Pythagoras Philosophus]] name for two, [Refs [Theol.Ar. 12.]]

__V.b
of plants or material substances, φ. εὐώδεις καρποφοροῦσαι [Refs 1st c.BC+ [1st c.BC: Diodorus Siculus Historicus 2.49; ὑγράν τινα φ. καπνὸν ἀποδιδοῦσαν “Corpus Hermeticum” 1.4.]]

LSJ / STEPBible (TFLSJ)
φῠτ-εύω,
[Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 5.340, etc.]], Epic dialect infinitive φυτευέμεν [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th-7th c.BC: Hesiodus Epicus “Opera et Dies” 812]]; future εύσω [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Oeconomicus” 19.13]]; aorist ἐφύτευσα [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 6.419, etc.:]]perfect πεφύτευκα, 3rd.pers. plural πεφύτευκαν [LXX.Eze.19.13]:—middle, future -εύσομαι[Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “P.” 4.15]]: aorist -ευσάμην[Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Memorabilia” 1.1.8]]:—passive, future -ευθήσομαι[Refs [“Geoponica” 5.19.1]]: aorist ἐφυτεύθην [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 5.3.12]], poetry3rd.pers. plural φύτευθεν [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “P.” 4.69]]: perfect πεφύτευμαι [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 2.138, etc.]]: (φυτόν).

__I
with accusative of the thing planted, plant trees, especially fruit-trees, οὔτε φυτεύουσιν χερσὶν φυτὸν οὔτ᾽ ἀρόωσιν [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 9.108; δένδρεα φ. 18.359, compare 7th-6th c.BC: Alcaeus Lyricus 44, etc.; ἄλσος πεφυτευμένον 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus [same place]; συκᾶς 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Fragmenta” 108 (troch.)]]; ὄρχους, ἀμπέλους, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Oeconomicus” 20.3, 4]]; joined with σπείρω,[NT+8th c.BC+ [[prev. work] 11.16, “Mem.” 2.1.13, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Phaedrus” 276e; φυτείαν NT.Matt.15.13; ἀρώμεναι ἠδὲ φ. 8th-7th c.BC: Hesiodus Epicus “Opera et Dies” 22; φ. ἐν γῇ 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Oeconomicus” 19.2]]; ἐν ἀφόρῳ[Refs 1st c.AD+ [[prev. work] 20.3; εἰς γῆν 1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus 2.986f; φ. ἀπὸ κορύνης “Geoponica” 10.8.1]]:—middle, plant for oneself, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “P.” 4.15, 2nd c.AD: Lucianus Sophista “Cat.” 20:]] — passive, δένδρα πεφυτευμένα, opposed to to those of spontaneous growth, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 55.13.]]

__I.2
metaphorically, beget, engender, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th-7th c.BC: Hesiodus Epicus “Opera et Dies” 812, “Sc.” 29, 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 4.145, 5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “N.” 7.84, etc.; φυτεύων παῖδας 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Alcestis” 662, compare “Or.” 11, 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Vespae” 1133, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Crito” 50d; ὁ φυτεύσας πατήρ 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Tyrannus” 793, 1514, 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Iphigenia Aulidensis” 1177 (assuming variant)]]; ὁ φυτεύσας alone, the father, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Philoctetes” 904, “Tr.” 1244; ὁ φ. αὐτόν 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Andromache” 49, etc.: opposed to ἡ τεκοῦσα, 5th c.BC: Lysias Orator 11.4]] (rarely of the mother, σὲ.. φύτευσεν Αἴθρα Ποσειδᾶνι [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Bacchylides Lyricus 16.59)]]; οἱ φυτεύσαντες the parents, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Tyrannus” 1007, “OC” 1377; τοὺς τεκόντας καὶ φυτ. [prev. author] “fragment” 64, compare 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Supplices” 1092: _metaphorically_, ὕβρις φυτεύει τύραννον 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Tyrannus” 873 (Lyric poetry); Μούσας λέγουσι Ἁρμονίαν φυτεῦσαι 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Medea” 832 (Lyric poetry)]]:—passive, to be begotten, spring from parents, κείνων [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “P.” 4.144; ἐκ Κρόνου [prev. author] “N.” 5.7; τοῦ κακοῦ πότμου φυτευθείς 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Coloneus” 1324.]]

__I.3
generally, produce, bring about, cause, mostly of evils, ὅτι τοι κακὰ πολλὰ φυτεύει [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 5.340; πρὶν ἡμῖν πῆμα φυτεῦσαι 4.668 (variant); φόνον καὶ κῆρα φ. 2.165, 17.82; once in 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad”, κακὸν μέγα πᾶσι φ. 15.134; φύτευέ οἱ θάνατον 5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “N.” 4.59; φ. πῆμα 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Ajax” 953]]; also in good sense, φ. γάμον, δόξαν, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “P.” 9.111, “I.” 6 (5). 12; Μίνωϊ τιμάν 5th c.BC: Bacchylides Lyricus 16.68; καδέων ἀνάπαυσιν [prev. author] 18.35]]:—passive, σὺν θεῷ φυτευθείς ὄλβος [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “N.” 8.17.]]

__I.4
implant in, τοῦθ᾽ ἡμῖν [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Timaeus” 80e; τι εἴς τι [prev. author] “Phdr.” 248d.]]

__I.5
set up, ἄγαλμα ἐν τῷ οἴκῳ [Refs 4th c.AD+ [4th c.AD: Iamblichus Philosophus “de vita Pythagorica” 18.84.]]

__II
less frequently with accusative of the ground planted, plant with fruit-trees, φ. γῆν [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 1.2; χωρίον φ. καὶ γεωργεῖν 4th c.BC: Isaeus Orator 9.28: _absolutely_, 5th c.BC: Eupolis Comicus 13, 4th-3rd c.BC: Philemo Comicus 116]]:—middle, ἀγρόν φ. [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Memorabilia” 1.1.8]]:—passive, γῆ πεφυτευμένη [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 4.127, compare 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Historia Graeca (Hellenica)” 3.2.10]]; opposed to ψιλή, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Eupolis Comicus 230, 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 20.115; τὰ πεφυτευμένα “PHal.” 1.102 (3rd c.BC)]], etc.; γεωργία καὶ ψιλὴ καὶ πεφ. [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Politica” 1259a2.]]

Abbott-Smith / STEPBible (TBESG)
φύω
[in LXX: Pro.26:9, Eze.37:8 (עָלָה), etc. ;]
__1. trans., to bring forth, produce (of men, to beget); pass., to spring up, grow: Luk.8:6, 8.
__2. Intrans., in 2 aor., pf., plpf., and rarely in present (see LS, see word, A, II.), to spring up: Heb.12:15.†
(AS)

LSJ / STEPBible (TFLSJ)
φύω,
[Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 6.148, etc.]]; Aeolic dialect φυίω perhaps to be read in [Refs 7th c.BC+ [7th-6th c.BC: Alcaeus Lyricus 97:]]imperfect ἔφυον, Epic dialect 3rd.pers. singular φύεν [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 14.347:]]future φύσω [ῡ[Refs 5th c.BC+ [] 1.235, 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Tyrannus” 438]]: aorist ἔφῡσα [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 10.393, etc.]]:—passive and middle,[Refs 5th c.BC+ [9.109, 5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “O.” 4.28, etc.]]: future φύσομαι [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Prometheus Vinctus” 871, 5th c.BC: Hippocrates Medicus “Mochl.” 42, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Leges” 831a, etc.]]: similar in sense are the intransitive tenses, perfect πέφῡκα [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 7.114, etc.]], Epic dialect 3rd.pers. plural πεφύᾱσι [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 4.484, 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 7.128]]; 3rd.pers. singular subjunctive πεφύῃ (ἐμ-) [Refs 6th c.BC+ [6th c.BC: Theognis Elegiacus 396]]; Epic dialect participle feminine πεφυυῖα (ἐμ-) [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 1.513, _accusative_ _plural_ πεφυῶτας 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 5.477]]; Doric dialect infinitive πεφύκειν [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Epicharmus Comicus 173.3]]: pluperfect ἐπεφύκειν [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 5.1.9, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Timaeus” 69e]]; Epic dialect πεφύκειν [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 4.109]]; Epic dialect 3rd.pers. plural ἐπέφῡκον [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th-7th c.BC: Hesiodus Epicus “Theogonia” 152, “Op.” 149:]]aorist 2 ἔφῡν (as if from φῦμι) [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 10.397, etc.]]: Epic dialect 3rd.pers. singular φῦ [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 6.253, etc., _3rd.pers._ _plural_ ἔφυν (for ἔφῡσαν, which is also _3rd.pers._ _plural_ of _aorist_ 1) 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 5.481, etc.]]; subjunctive φύω or φυῶ [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Fragmenta” 377.2, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 415c, 597c, 5th c.BC: Hippocrates Medicus “περὶ σαρκῶν” 12]]; 3rd.pers. singular optative φύη [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [3rd c.BC: Theocritus Poeta Bucolicus 15.94, (συμ-) 2nd c.AD: Soranus Medicus 2.89]]; infinitive φῦναι, Epic dialect φύμεναι [Refs 4th c.BC+ [3rd c.BC: Theocritus Poeta Bucolicus 25.39, φῦν 4th-5th c.BC: Parmenides Poeta Philosophus 8.10]]; participle φύς [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 18.410, etc.]], Boeotian dialect feminine φοῦσα [Refs 6th c.BC+ [6th c.BC: Corinna Lyrica 21: ἔφυσεν, ={ἔφυ}, uncertain in “IG” 14.2126.5 (from Rome)]]; conversely ἔφυ, ={ἔφυσεν}, [Refs [[prev. work]3.1350, “Sammelb.” 5883 (from Cyrene)]]: later, future φυήσω [LXX.Isa.37.31], passive φυήσομαι [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [“Geoponica” 2.37.1, 4th c.AD: Themistius Sophista “Orationes” 21.248c (in 2nd c.AD: Lucianus Sophista “JTr.” 19 ἀναφύσεσθαι is restored)]]: aorist 2 passive ἐφύην [Refs 4th c.BC+ [1st c.AD: Josephus Historicus “Antiquitates Judaicae” 18.1.1, probably in “BSA” 28.124 (from Didyma), (ἀν-) 4th-3rd c.BC: Theophrastus Philosophus “Historia Plantarum” 4.16.2]]; infinitive φυῆναι [Refs 1st c.BC+ [1st c.AD: Dioscorides (Dioscurides) Medicus 2.6, (ἀνα-) 1st c.BC: Diodorus Siculus Historicus 1.7]]; participle φῠείς [NT+5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Hippocrates Medicus “περὶ φύσιος παιδίου” 22, “Tragica Adespota” 529, “PTeb.” 787.30 (2nd c.BC), NT.Luke.8.6]]: aorist 1 passive συμ-φυθείς [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd c.AD: Galenus Medicus 7.725]]. [Generally ῠ before a vowel, Epic dialect, Trag. [Refs 5th c.BC+ [(4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Septem contra Thebas” 535, 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Fragmenta” 910.2)]], etc., ῡ before a consonant; but φῡει [Refs 5th c.BC+ [“Tragica Adespota” 454.2, φῡεται 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Fragmenta” 88.4, “Tragica Adespota” 543 (= 4th-3rd c.BC: Menander Comicus 565); φῡομεν 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Aves” 106]]; ἐφῡετο probably in [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Fragmenta” 680, compare 2nd c.BC: Nicander Epicus “Alexipharmaca” 14, 2nd c.AD: Dionysius Periegeta 941, 1013]]; even in thesi, προσφῡονται [Refs 2nd c.BC+ [2nd c.BC: Nicander Epicus “Alexipharmaca” 506, φῡουσιν 2nd c.AD: Dionysius Periegeta 1031]]; also in compounds]

__A
transitive, in present, future, and aorist 1 active:—bring forth, produce, put forth, φύλλα.. ὕλη τηλεθόωσα φύει [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 6.148; τοῖσι δ᾽ ὑπὸ χθὼν δῖα φύεν νεοθηλέα ποίην 14.347, compare 1.235, 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 7.119, etc.; ἄμπελον φύει βροτοῖς 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Bacchae” 651]]; so τρίχες.., ἃς πρὶν ἔφυσεν φάρμακον made the hair grow, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 10.393, compare 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Septem contra Thebas” 535; φ. χεῖρε, πόδε, ὀφθαλμὰ ἀνθρώποις 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Memorabilia” 2.3.19]]; of a country, καρπόν τε θωμαστὸν φύειν καὶ ἄνδρας ἀγαθούς [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 9.122; ὅσα γῆ φύει 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 621a, compare 5th c.BC: Anaxagoras Philosophus 4.]]

__2
beget, engender, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Phoenissae” 869, etc.; Ἄτλας.. θεῶν μιᾶς ἔφυσε Μαῖαν 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Ion” 3, compare “Tragica Adespota” 454.2]]; so of God creating man, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Antipho Orator 4.1.2, compare 1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus 2.1065c]]; ὁ φύσας the begetter, father (opposed to ὁ φύς the son, see below [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Bacchylides Lyricus 1.2), 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Tyrannus” 1019, 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Vespae” 1472 (Lyric poetry); ὁ φ. πατήρ 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Helena” 87; ὁ φ. χἠ τεκοῦσα [prev. author] Alcaeus290; τὴν τεκοῦσαν ἢ τὸν φύσαντα 5th c.BC: Lysias Orator 10.8]]; of both parents, γονεῦσι οἵ σ᾽ ἔφυσαν [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Tyrannus” 436; οἱ φύσαντες 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Phoenissae” 34, compare “fragment” 403.2; φ. τε καὶ γεννᾶν 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Politicus” 274a; ὦ γάμοι γάμοι, ἐφύσαθ᾽ ἡμᾶς 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Tyrannus” 1404]]; ἥδ᾽ ἡμέρα φύσει σε will bring to light thy birth,[Refs [[prev. work] 438; χρόνος φύει τ᾽ ἄδηλα καὶ φανέντα κρύπτεται [prev. author] “Aj.” 647.]]

__3
of individuals in reference to the growth of parts of themselves, φ. πώγωνα, γλῶσσαν, κέρεα, grow or get a beard, etc., [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 8.104, 2.68, 4.29; φ. πτερά 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Aves” 106, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Phaedrus” 251c; σάρκα [prev. author] “Ti.” 74e]]; φ. τρίχας, πόδας καὶ πτερά, etc., [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Historia Animalium” 518a33, 554a29, etc.: for the joke in φύειν φράτερας, see at {φράτηρ}.]]

__4
metaphorically, φρένας φῦσαι get understanding, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Coloneus” 804, “El.” 1463 (but also θεοὶ φύουσιν ἀνθρώποις φρένας [prev. author] “Ant.” 683): proverbial, ἁλιεὺς πληγεὶς νοῦν φύσει]] 'once bit, twice shy', [Refs 5th c.BC+ [Scholia 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Symposium” 222b; γέροντα τὸν νοῦν σάρκα δ᾽ ἡβῶσαν φύει 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Septem contra Thebas” 622]]; δόξαν φῦσαι get glory or to form a high opinion of oneself, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 5.91; θεὸς.. αἰτίαν φύει βροτοῖς 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Niob.” in “PSI” 11.1208.15; αὑτῷ πόνους φῦσαι 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Antigone” 647.]]

__II
in present seemingly intransitive, put forth shoots, εἰς ἔτος ἄλλο φύοντι [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [2nd c.BC: Moschus Bucolicus 3.101; δρύες.. φύοντι 3rd c.BC: Theocritus Poeta Bucolicus 7.75, compare 4.24: so ἀνδρῶν γενεὴ ἡ μὲν φύει ἡ δ᾽ ἀπολήγει]] one generation is putting forth scions, the other is ceasing to do so, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 6.149]]; ἐν στήθεσι φύει (perhaps φυίει) grows up, appears, [LXX+7th c.BC+ [7th-6th c.BC: Alcaeus Lyricus 97; ῥίζα ἄνω φύουσα ἐν χολῇ LXX.Deu.29.18.]]

__B
passive, with intransitive tenses of active, aorist 2, perfect and pluperfect, grow, wax, spring up or forth, especially of the vegetable world, θάμνος ἔφυ ἐλαίης [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 23.190, compare 5.481; πρασιαὶ παντοῖαι πεφύασιν 7.128; τά γ᾽ ἄσπαρτα φύονται 9.109, compare 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 4.483, 14.288, 21.352; φύεται αὐτόματα ῥόδα 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 8.138, compare 1.193; ὑπὸ φηγῷ πεφυκυίῃ]]growing there, [Refs [[prev. author] 2.56]]; πεφυκότα δένδρα trees growing there, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 4.3.5; τὰ φυόμενα καὶ τὰ γιγνόμενα 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Cratylus” 410d, compare “Phd.” 110d, “Plt.” 272a]]; τοῦ κέρα ἐκ κεφαλῆς ἑκκαιδεκάδωρα πεφύκει from his head grew horns sixteen palms long, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 4.109, compare 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.108, 3.133; φύονται πολιαί 5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “O.” 4.28]]; κεφαλαὶ πεφυκυῖαι θριξί grown with hair, [Refs 1st c.BC+ [1st c.BC: Diodorus Siculus Historicus 2.50 (assuming variant); πέφυκε λίθος ἐν αὐτῇ]]is produced, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “de Vectigalibus” 1.4: _metaphorically_, νόσημα ἐν ὀλιγαρχίᾳ φυόμενον, φυομένη πόλις, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 564b, “Lg.” 757d]]; ὁ σπέρμα παρασχών, οὗτος τῶν φύντων αἴτιος [κακῶν] of the things produced, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 18.159]]; also κατὰ πάντων ἐφύετο waxed great by or upon their depression, [Refs [[prev. work] 19.]]—In this sense aorist 2 is rare (see. above), except in phrases such as ἔν τ᾽ ἄρα οἱ φῦ χειρί (see. ἐμφύω), [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 2.302.]]

__B.2
of persons, to be begotten or born, most frequently in aorist 2 and perfect, ὁ λωφήσων οὐ πέφυκέ πω [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Prometheus Vinctus” 27; τίς ἂν εὔξαιτο βροτὸς ὢν ἀσινεῖ δαίμονι φῦνα; [prev. author] “Ag.” 1342 (_anapaest meter_)]]; μὴ φῦναι τὸν ἅπαντα νικᾷ λόγον not to be born is best, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Coloneus” 1224 (Lyric poetry)]]; γονῇ πεφυκὼς.. γεραιτέρᾳ[Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. work] 1294; οὐχ ὑπὸ θυσιῶν οὐδ᾽ ὑπὸ εὐχῶν φύς 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 461a]]; φύς τε καὶ τραφείς[Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. work] 396c; μήπω φῦναι μηδὲ γενέσθαι 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 5.1.7, compare 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Symposium” 197a: construed with _genitive_, πεφμκέναι or φῦναί τινος]] to be born or descended from any one, τὸ κοινὸν σπλάγχνον οὗ πεφύκαμεν [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Septem contra Thebas” 1036, compare 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Coloneus” 1379, etc.; θνατᾶς ἀπὸ ματρὸς ἔφυ 5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “Fragmenta.” 61, compare 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Tyrannus” 1359 (Lyric poetry), “Ant.” 562; ἀπ᾽ εὐγενοῦς ῥίζης 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Iphigenia Taurica” 610; ἀπὸ δρυός 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Apologia” 34d, etc.; φ. ἔκ τινος 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Tyrannus” 458, 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Heraclidae” 325, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 415c, etc.; ἐκ χώρας τινός 5th-6th c.BC: Isocrates Orator 4.24, etc.]]; οἱ μετ᾽ ἐκείνου φύντες, opposed to οἱ ἐξ ἐκείνου γεγονότες, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Isaeus Orator 8.30; ἐκ θεῶν γεγονότι.. διὰ βασιλέων πεφυκότι 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 7.2.24.]]

__B.II
in present, become, οὐδεὶς ἐχθρὸς οὔτε φύεται πρὸς χρήμαθ᾽ οἵ τε φύντες.. [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Fragmenta” 88.4; πιστοὺς φύσει φύεσθαι 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 8.7.13]]; the perfect and aorist 2 take a present sense, to be so and so by nature, κακός, σοφός πέφυκα (-κώς), etc., [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Philoctetes” 558, 1244, etc.; φωνέω, -ῶ
(φωνή), [in LXX for קָרָא (Jer.17:11, al.), etc. ;]
__I. Intrans.
__1. Of persons, to call out, cry out, speak aloud: Luk.8:8; φωνῇ μεγάλῃ, Mrk.1:26, Act.16:28; ἐφώνησε (φωνῇ μεγάλῇ) λέγων, Luk.8:54, Rev.14:18; φωνήσαντες ἐπύθοντο, Act.10:18.
__2. Of the cries of animals (rarely in cl.; Isa.38:14, Je, l.with): of a cock, to crow, Mat.26:34, Mrk.14:30, Luk.22:3, Jhn.13:38 18:27.
__II. Trans. (in cl. chiefly poët.), with accusative of person(s), to call, summon, invite: Mat.20:32 27:47, Mrk.9:35 10:49 15:35, Luk.14:12 16:2 19:15, Jhn.1:49 2:9 4:16 10:3 11:28 12:17 18:33, Act.9:41 10:7; to address, call by name (Soph.), Jhn.13:13 (cf. ἀνα-, ἐπι-, προσ-, συν-φωνέω).†
(AS)

φων-έω,
(φωνή) produce a sound or tone:

__I
properly of men, speak loud or clearly, or simply, speak, give utterance, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Homerus Epicus only in]]aorist (present and imperfect only in compounds); ὣς ἄρα φωνήσας ἀπέβη [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 6.116, compare 11.531, +others; ἔπος φάτο φώνησέν τε 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 4.370; φωνήσας προσέφη 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 14.41]]; καί μιν φωνήσας ἔπεα πτερόεντα προσηύδα addressed him with a loud voice in winged words, [Refs [1.201, compare 4.284, +others]]; φωνοῦντος ἢ ἠχοῦντος ἢ ψοφοῦντος [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-3rd c.BC: Epicurus Philosophus “Epistulae” 1p.13U.]]; followed by the words spoken, φώνησε (φώνασε codices) δ᾽, εὕδεις, βασιλεῦ [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “O.” 13.67; χρυσοῖς δὲ φωνεῖ γράμμασιν, πρήσω πόλιν 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Septem contra Thebas” 434, compare “Ag.” 1334 (_anapaest meter_)]]; οἱ βουλευταὶ ἐφώνησαν.. the Senators exclaimed.., [Refs 4th c.AD+ [POxy. 2110.6 (4th c.AD)]]; “βέκος φ. utter the word βέκος, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 2.2: with _accusative_ _cognate_, ὄπα φωνησάσης]] having made her voice sound, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 24.535; φ. φάτιν 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Electra” 329: with _neuter_]] adjective, φ. μέγιστον ἀνθρώπων to have the loudest voice, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 4.141, 7.117; ὄρθιον φ. 5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “N.” 10.76; ἄλλο τι φ. 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Prometheus Vinctus” 1063 (_anapaest meter_); τάδε φ. [prev. author] “Ch.” 314 (_anapaest meter_); μέγα φ. [prev. author] “Eu.” 936 (_anapaest meter_), 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Philoctetes” 574; ἄπυστα φ. [prev. author] “OC” 489; ὅσια φ. [prev. author] “Ph.” 662]]; δεινὸν φ.[Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. work] 1225; εὔφημα [prev. author] “Aj.” 362, 591, 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Iphigenia Taurica” 687, etc.; μηδεὶς ἔπος φωνείτω “IG” 22.1368.108; τὸν ῥηϊδίως φωνεῦντα πᾶν ἔπος 4th c.BC: Anaxarchus Philosophus 1]]: absolutely, cry aloud, as in joy, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Trachiniae” 202]]; of a singer, ἀοιδὸς.. αἰόλα φωνέων [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [3rd c.BC: Theocritus Poeta Bucolicus 16.44:]] —passive, τὰ φωνηθέντα sounds or words uttered, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Sophista” 262c, “Ti.” 72a, compare 3rd c.AD: Longinus Rhetor 39.4.]]

__I.2
of animals, utter their cries, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Historia Animalium” 578a32]]; of birds,[Refs [[prev. work] 593a14]]; [τὰ σελάχη] φωνεῖν οὐκ ὀρθῶς ἔχει φάναι, ψοφεῖν δέ[[prev. work] 535b25; ἐφώνησε πέρδιξ LXX.Jer.17.11]; of the cock, crow, [NT.Matt.26.34, +others]

__I.3
as law-term, affirm, testify in court, [Refs [“Leg.Gort.” 1.18, +others (written πωνίω).]]

__I.4
of a musical instrument, sound, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Orestes” 146 (Lyric poetry)]]; of sounds, ἡδὺ φωνεῖν sound sweetly, [Refs 1st c.AD+ [1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus 2.1021b]]; but βροντὴ φ. it has a voice, is significant, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Apologia Socratis” 12.]]

φ. τινα with infinitive, command, σὲ φωνῶ νεκρὸν.. μὴ συγκομίζειν [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Ajax” 1047.]]

__II.3
invite, τοὺς φίλους [NT.Luke.14.12.]

__II.4
with dative person, call to, cry to, Ζεῦ ἄνα, σοὶ φωνῶ [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Coloneus” 1485 (Lyric poetry), compare “OT” 1121; ἕρποντι φωνεῖς [prev. author] “Aj.” 543.]]

with accusative of things, speak or tell of, προσβολὰς Ἐρινύων [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Choephori” 283]]; ὁδοῦ τέλος.. οἷον οὐδὲ φωνῆσαί τινι ἔξεσθ᾽ tell to any one, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Coloneus” 1402]]; φ. τὸ Ἐπιχάρμειον recite it, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Axiochus” 366c.]]
