participle κεχαρμένος [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Orestes” 1122, “Tr.” 529 (Lyric poetry), “Cyc.” 367 (Lyric poetry):]]pluperfect 3rd.pers. singular and plural κεχάρητο, -ηντο, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th-7th c.BC: Hesiodus Epicus “Scutum Herculis” 65, “hymnus ad Cererem” 458]]:—rejoice, be glad, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 3.111, 21.347, etc.; γραῦς ἥδε οἰνοφόρος κεχαρημένη ὧδε κάθηται “IG” 12(8).679 (Scyros, 2nd c.BC): χ. θυμῷ 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 7.191, +others; ἐν θυμῷ 24.491, 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 22.411; φρεσὶν ᾗσι 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 13.609; φρένα 6.481]]; χ. νόῳ to rejoice in wardly, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 8.78; χαίρει δέ μοι ἦτορ 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 23.647; αὐτὰρ ἐμὸν κῆρ χ. 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 4.260; χ. καὶ γελᾶν 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Electra” 1300; ἥδομαι καὶ χαίρομαι κεὐφραίνομαι 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Pax” 291]]; opposed to λυπεῖσθαι, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Fragmenta - American Journal of Philology” 266.3, 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Ajax” 555, etc.]]; opposed to ἀλγεῖν, [Refs [[prev. author] “Tr.” 1119.]] —Constr.,

__1
with dative of things, rejoice at, take pleasure in a thing, νίκῃ [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 7.312; φήμῃ 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 2.35; δώρῳ 8th-7th c.BC: Hesiodus Epicus “Opera et Dies” 358; μόλπᾳ 7th-6th c.BC: Sappho Lyrica “Papyrus fragments” in E. Diehl, 25.5, compare 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Tyrannus” 1070, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Menexenus” 238d, etc.: with _dative_ _person_, χαῖρε.. ἀνδρὶ δικαίῳ 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 3.52]]; with a participle added, χάρη δ᾽ ἄρα οἱ προσιόντι [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 5.682, compare 24.706, 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 19.463: with Preps., χαίρειν ἐπί τινι 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Fragmenta” 926, 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Memorabilia” 2.6.35, “Cyr.” 8.4.12, 5th-6th c.BC: Isocrates Orator 2.30, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Leges” 739d, etc.; πρὸς τοῖς παιδικοῖς 5th c.BC: Eupolis Comicus 327]]; with a participle added, ἐπ᾽ ἐξεργασμένοις κακοῖσι χ. [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Bacchae” 1040, compare 1033: rarely ἔν τινι 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Eumenides” 996 (Lyric poetry), 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Trachiniae” 1119: also with _dative_ modi, χ. γέλωτι]] express one's joy by laughter, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 8.1.33.]]

__1.b
of a plant, χαίρει ὑφάμμοις χωρίοις [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-3rd c.BC: Theophrastus Philosophus “Historia Plantarum” 6.5.2; also ἡ κύστις χ. τῇ χολῇ 2nd c.AD: Galenus Medicus 19.646.]]

__2
rarely with accusative, with a participle added, χαίρω δέ σ᾽ εὐτυχοῦντα [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Rhesus” 390; τοὺς γὰρ εὐσεβεῖς θεοὶ θνῄσκοντας οὐ χ. [prev. author] “Hipp.” 1340]]; χαίρω σ᾽ [ἐλθόντα] [Refs [[prev. author] “fragment” 673]] (this usage is said to be Oropian, [Refs [“Etymologicum Magnum” 808.4).]]

__2.b
with a neuter adjective, ταὐτὰ λυπεῖσθαι καὶ ταὐτὰ χαίρειν τοῖς πολλοῖς [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 18.292: with _accusative_ _cognate_, ἁπλῆν χαίρειν ἡδονήν 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Ethica Nicomachea” 1154b26; χ. ἀνδραπόδων τινὰ χαράν 1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus 2.1091e.]]

__3
with participle, χαίρω.. τὸν μῦθον ἀκούσας I rejoice at having heard, am glad to hear, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 19.185, compare 7.54, 11.73; χαίρουσιν βίοτον νήποινον ἔδοντες 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 14.377, compare 12.380, 8th-7th c.BC: Hesiodus Epicus “Opera et Dies” 55; χαίρω.. κόμπον ἱείς 5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “N.” 8.49; χαίρεις ὁρῶν φῶς, πατέρα δ᾽ οὐ χαίρειν δοκεῖ; 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Alcestis” 691; χαίρω φειδόμενος 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Plutus” 247; θωπευόμενος χαίρεις [prev. author] “Eq.” 1116 (Lyric poetry), compare 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Symposium” 191e, etc.]]

__3.b
with participle present, delight in doing, to be wont to do, χρεώμενοι χαίρουσι [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 7.236, compare 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Philoctetes” 449, 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Vespae” 764, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Protagoras” 318d, 346c, 358a.]]

__4
χαίρειν ὅττι or ὅτι.., [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 14.51, 526, 5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “N.” 5.46]]; ἐχάρην καὶ ἐθρασυνάμην ὅτι ἔμαθον.. [Refs 4th c.AD+ [4th c.AD: Metrodorus Epigrammaticus “fragment” 42]]; χ. οὕνεκα.. [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 8.200.]]

__II
with negative, especially with future, οὐ χαιρήσεις thou wilt or shalt not rejoice, i.e. thou shalt not go unpunished, shalt repent it, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Plutus” 64; οὐ χαιρήσετον [prev. author] “Eq.” 235; so οὐδέ τιν᾽ οἴω Τρώων χαιρήσειν 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 20.363, compare 15.98, 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 2.249, 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Vespae” 186]]; ἀλλ᾽ οὐδ᾽ ὣς Κῦρός γε χαιρήσει [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.128]]; with an interrogative, σὺ.. χαιρήσειν νομίζει; [Refs 1st c.AD+ [1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus “Alexander” 51]]: rarely with other tenses, ὅπως ἂν μὴ χαίρωσιν. [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 19.299; οὐκ ἐχαίρησεν 1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus “Lucullus” 25: for a similar use of the]]participle, see below [Refs [IV.  2.]]

__III
frequently in imperative χαῖρε, dual χαίρετον, plural χαίρετε, as a form of greeting,

__III.1
at meeting, hail, welcome (especially in the morning, accusative to [Refs 8th c.BC+ [2nd-3rd c.AD: Dio Cassius Historicus 69.18, compare 2nd c.AD: Lucianus Sophista “Laps.”), 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 9.197, 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 13.229, etc.; χαῖρε, ξεῖνε, παρ᾽ ἄμμι φιλήσεαι 1.123; strengthened, οὖλέ τε, καὶ μάλα χαῖρε, θεοὶ δέ τοι ὄλβια δοῖεν 24.402; χαῖρέ μοι 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 23.19, compare 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Coloneus” 1137; repeated, 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Eumenides” 996, 1014 (both Lyric poetry), 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Ajax” 91, etc.; χαῖρ᾽ ὡς μέγιστα, χαῖρε [prev. author] “Ph.” 462]]; in greeting one's native land, the sun, etc., [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Agamemnon” 508, 22, 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Philoctetes” 1453 (_anapaest meter_).]]

__III.1.b
sometimes implied in the use of χαίρω, κῆρυξ Ἀχαιῶν, χαῖρε.. Answ. χαίρω I accept the greeting, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Agamemnon” 538]]; νῦν πᾶσι χαίρω, νῦν με πᾶς ἀσπάζεται I hear the word χαῖρε from all, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Tyrannus” 596: so in]]infinitive, τὸ χαίρειν uncertain reading in [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Charmides” 164e]]; χαίρειν δὲ τὸν κήρυκα προὐννέπω I bid him welcome, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Trachiniae” 227; προσειπών τινα χ. οὐκ ἀντιπροσερρήθη 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Memorabilia” 3.13.1]]; but χαίρειν τἄλλ᾽ ἐγώ σ᾽ ἐφίεμαι I bid thee have thy pleasure, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Ajax” 112.]]

__III.1.c
infinitive alone at the beginning of letters, Κῦρος Κυαζάρῃ χαίρειν (i.e. λέγει) [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 4.5.27, compare 3rd c.BC: Theocritus Poeta Bucolicus 14.1]]; used by Alexander the Great to Phocion as a mark of respect, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-3rd c.BC: Duris Epigrammaticus 51J.]]

__III.2
at leavetaking, fare-thee-well, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 5.205, 13.59, 15.151; χαῖρε πόλλ᾽ ὦδελφέ 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Ranae” 164; _plural_, χαίρετε πολλάκι 3rd c.BC: Theocritus Poeta Bucolicus 1.144]]; frequently put into the mouth of the dying, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Ajax” 863, “Tr.” 921, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Phaedo” 116d, etc.]]: hence in sepulchral inscriptions, [Refs [“IG” 7.203, etc.]]

__III.2.b
hence, imperative χαιρέτω, χαιρόντων, have done with.., away with.., εἴτ᾽ ἐγένετο ἄνθρωπος εἴτ᾽ ἐστὶ δαίμων, χαιρέτω [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 4.96; χαιρέτω βουλεύματα τὰ πρόσθεν 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Medea” 1044, χαιρόντων πόνοι [prev. author] “HF” 575; compare 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Symposium” 199a, “Lg.” 636d, 886d.]]

__III.2.c
ἐᾶν χαίρειν τινά or τι dismiss from one's mind, put away, renounce, [Refs 7th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 6.23, 9.41, 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Plutus” 1187, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Phaedo” 63e, “Prt.” 348a, 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 7.3.23, etc.; συχνὰ χ. ἐᾶν τινα 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Philebus” 59b; ἐλευθερίαν μακρὰ χ. ἐᾶν 2nd c.AD: Lucianus Sophista “Apol.” 3; μακρὰ χ. εἰποῦσα 2nd-3rd c.AD: Aelianus “Varia Historia” 12.1; πόλλα μοι τὰν Πωλυανάκτιδα παῖδα χαίρην 7th-6th c.BC: Sappho Lyrica 86; τὴν Κύπριν πόλλ᾽ ἐγὼ χαίρειν λέγω 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Hippolytus” 113, compare 1059, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Theaetetus” 188a; χ. κελεύων πολλὰ τοὺς Ἀχαρνέας 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Acharnenses” 200; εἰπεῖν χαίρειν τινά “Ath.Mitt.” 56.131 (Milet., Hellenistic), compare 2nd c.AD: Lucianus Sophista “Dem.Enc.” 50; χαίρειν προσαγορεύειν 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Plutus” 322 (_metaphorically_ in 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Leges” 771a); χαίρειν προσειπεῖν 5th c.BC: Eupolis Comicus 308: less frequently with _dative_ _person_ (never with ἐᾶν χ.), πολλὰ χαίρειν ξυμφοραῖς καταξιῶ 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Agamemnon” 572 (nisi to be read ξυμφοράς); φράσαι.. χαίρειν Ἀθηναίοισι 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Nubes” 609 (troch.); πολλὰ εἰπόντα χ. τῷ ἀληθεῖ 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Phaedrus” 272e, compare “Phd.” 64c, “R.” 406d, 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Historia Graeca (Hellenica)” 4.1.31 (codices, perhaps ἀλλήλους), 4th c.AD: Julianus Imperator]]ad Them.255a.

__III.3
on other occasions, as in comforting, be of good cheer, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 8.408; at meals, 4.60, 18.122]]; χαῖρε, γύναι, φιλότητι good luck be on our union,[Refs [11.248; εὐχωλῇς χαίρετε 13.358: χαῖρε ἀοιδῇ “Hymni Homerici” 9.7.]]

__IV
participle χαίρων glad, joyful, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 1.446, etc.; χαίροντα φίλην ἐς πατρίδ᾽ ἔπεμπον εἰς Ἰθάκην 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 19.461; χαίροντι φέρειν.. χαίρων 17.83]]; λυπούμενοι καὶ χαίροντες in sorrow and in joy, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Rhetorica” 1356a16]]: also perfect participle κεχαρηκώς [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 3.27, 42, etc.]]

__IV.2
joined with another Verb, safe and sound, with impunity, χαίροντα ἀπαλλάσσειν [Refs 4th c.BC+ [[prev. work] 69, compare 9.106, 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 24.153]]; more frequently with a negative, οὐ χαίρων to one's cost, οὐ χαίροντες γέλωτα ἐμὲ θήσεσθε [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 3.29; οὔ τι χαίρων.. ἐρεῖς 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Tyrannus” 363, compare “Ant.” 759, “Ph.” 1299, 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Medea” 398, 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Acharnenses” 563, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Gorgias” 510d; οὐ γὰπ.. χαίρων τις.. τοὐμὸν ἀλγυνεῖ κέαρ 5th c.BC: Eupolis Comicus 90; οὔτε χαίροντες ἂν ἀπαλλάζαιτε 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 5.6.32; also οὔτι χαιρήσων γε σύ 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Vespae” 186; compare above 11.]]

__IV.3
in the same sense as imperative (above [Refs [111), σὺ δέ μοι χαίρων ἀφίκοιο]]fare-thee-well, and may'st thou arrive, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 15.128, compare 3rd c.BC: Theocritus Poeta Bucolicus 2.163]]; χαίροισ᾽ ἔρχεο go thy way rejoicing, [Refs 7th c.BC+ [7th-6th c.BC: Sappho Lyrica “Papyrus fragments” in E. Diehl, 23.7]]; ἀλλ᾽ ἑρπέτω χαίρουσα let her go with a benison, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Trachiniae” 819]]; χαίρων ἴθι fare-thee-well, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Alcestis” 813, “Ph.” 921; χαίρουσα.. στεῖχε [prev. author] “Hipp.” 1440.]]

__IV.4
τὸ χαῖρον τῆς ψυχῆς [Refs 1st c.AD+ [1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus 2.136c, 1089e.]]

__V
Astrology texts, of a planet, occupy the position appropriate to another of its own αἵρεσις, [Refs 2nd c.BC+ [2nd-1st c.BC(?): Serapio Astrologus in “Catalogus Codicum Astrologorum” 8(4).230, 2nd c.AD: Ptolemaeus Mathematicus “Tetrabiblos” 51, 2nd c.AD: Vettius Valens Astrologus 63.6, 4th c.AD(?): Manetho Astrologus 2.348]]. (Cf. Sanskrit háryati 'take pleasure in', Umbr. heriest 'will wish', Latin horior.)

LSJ / STEPBible (TFLSJ)
χάλαζ-α [χᾰ], ης, ἡ,
hail [NT+8th c.BC+ [compare (5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Timaeus” 59e, 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “de Mundo” 394b1), ὄμβρον.. ἠὲ χάλαζαν ἢ νιφετόν 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 10.6, compare 15.170, NT.Rev.8.7, etc.: _plural_, 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Oeconomicus” 5.18, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Symposium” 188b, “R.” 397a; χ. στρογγύλαι]]hailstones, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Nubes” 1127 (troch.); ἀπὸ τῶν χαλαζῶν.. ἄπαγε σεαυτόν [prev. author] “Ra.” 852]]: metaphorically, any pelting shower, ὀμβρία χ. [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Coloneus” 1503; χ. αἵματος 5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “I.” 7(6).27.]]

__II
any small knot like a hailstone,

__II.1
pimple or tubercle in the flesh of swine, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Historia Animalium” 603b18, “Pr.” 963b34, Androsth. cited in 2nd c.AD: Athenaeus Epigrammaticus 3.93c.]]

__II.2
small cyst, such as grows on the eyelid, [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd c.AD: Galenus Medicus 19.437, 2nd c.AD(?): Pollianus Epigrammaticus 4.198, etc.]]

__II.3
a knot or hard lump; in an egg, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Historia Animalium” 560a28; in coal, 4th-3rd c.BC: Theophrastus Philosophus “de Signis Tempestatum” 25; in ivory, 2nd-3rd c.AD: Philostratus Sophista “Vita Apollonii” 2.13; λίθοι χαλάζης]]crystals, [Refs [1 “Enoch” 14.9,10]]. (Cf. Sloven. žled, Little Russian oželeda 'sleet, ice'.)

LSJ / STEPBible (TFLSJ)
χᾰλάω,
[Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Eumenides” 219, etc.]], Epic dialect 3rd.pers. plural χαλόωσιν [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd-3rd c.AD: Oppianus Anazarbensis Epicus “Halieutica - Poetae Bucolici et Didactici” 2.451]]; Aeolic dialect 3rd.pers. plural χόλαισι [Refs 7th c.BC+ [7th-6th c.BC: Alcaeus Lyricus 18.9 codices 1st c.AD(?): Heraclitus:]]future χᾰλάσω [λᾰ] [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Hippocrates Medicus “Aër.” 8, “Epid.” 7.80]]: aorist ἐχάλᾰσα [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Prometheus Vinctus” 177 (_anapaest meter_), 5th c.BC: Hippocrates Medicus “ἐπιδημίαι” 7.23, etc.]]; Epic dialect χάλασσα [Refs [“hymnus ad Apollinem” 6]], plural subjunctive χαλάσσομεν [Refs 7th c.BC+ [7th-6th c.BC: Alcaeus Lyricus “Supp.” 23.10]]; Doric dialect participle χᾰλάξαις [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “P.” 1.6]]; 3rd.pers. singular future or aorist subjunctive χαλάξει (uncertain meaning) [Refs [“Berl.Sitzb.” 1927.164 (from Cyrene)]]:—middle, Epic dialect aorist χαλάσαντο [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [3rd c.BC: Apollonius Rhodius Epicus 2.1264:]] —passive, aorist ἐχαλάσθην, subjunctive χᾰλασθῇ [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Prometheus Vinctus” 991, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Phaedo” 86c]]: perfect κεχάλασμαι [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [“Anthologia Graeca” 9.297 (Antip.), 2nd c.AD: Appianus Historicus “Μιθριδάτειος” 74, 3rd c.AD: Plotinus Philosophus 4.3.16]]: pluperfect ἐκεχάλαστο [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd c.AD: Aristides Rhetor 1.315J.]]

__I
transitive, slacken, loosen, χ. βιόν, τόξα, unstring the bow, [Refs [“hymnus ad Apollinem” 6, “Hymni Homerici” 27.12]]; χ. τὰ νεῦρα, opposed to συντείνειν, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Phaedo” 98d; χ. τὸν πόδα, of a ship, see at {πούς} II.2: _metaphorically_, τὰ τῆς πολιτείας χ., opposed to ἐπιτείνειν, 1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus 2.827b:]] —passive, opposed to ἐπιτείνεσθαι, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Phaedo” 86c, 94c; χαλᾶσθαι καὶ διαφθείρεσθαι [prev. author] “Lg.” 653c; χαλᾶσθαι ὑπὸ τῆς ἡδονῆς 3rd c.AD: Porphyrius Tyrius Philosophus “ad Marcellam - Porphyrii Opuscula” 7.]]

__I.2
let down, let fall, πτέρυγα χαλάξαις Pi.[same place]; χαλάσας ὀλίγον τὸ μέτωπον having unbent the brow, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Vespae” 655 (_anapaest meter_)]]; μαστοὺς χάλασον, says the Cyclops to his ewe, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Cyclops” 55 (Lyric poetry)]]; κράββατον, δίκτυα χ., [NT.Mark.2.4, NT.Luke.5.5; τὴν ἱερὰν ἄγκυραν 10th c.AD: Suidas Legal icographus]; dip in a liquid, εἰς αἷμα [Refs [“PMag.Par.” 1.2886]]; soak, [Refs [PHolm. 14.33:]] —middle, ἱστὸν χαλάσαντο lowered it, [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [3rd c.BC: Apollonius Rhodius Epicus 2.1264.]]

__I.3
let loose, release, τινὰ ἐκ δεσμῶν [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Prometheus Vinctus” 177 (_anapaest meter_)]]; absolutely, let go, slacken one's hold, μηδαμῇ χάλα [Refs [[prev. work] 58.]]

__I.4
ἡνίας χ. slacken the reins, especially in metaphorically sense, χ. τὰς ἡνίας τοῖς λόγοις [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Protagoras” 338a, compare 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Fragmenta” 409.]]

__I.5
κλῇθρα χ. loose the bars or bolts, i.e. undo or open the door, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Antigone” 1187, 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Hippolytus” 808; κλῇδας [prev. author] “Med.” 1314; χ. τοὺς μοχλούς 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Lysistrata” 310; but also πύλας μοχλοῖς χαλᾶτε 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Choephori” 879.]]

__I.6
loosen or undo things drawn tightly together, χ. κρεμαστὴν ἀρτάνην [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Tyrannus” 1266; χ. πᾶν κάλυμμ᾽ ἀπ᾽ ὀφθαλμῶν [prev. author] “El.” 1468; χ. δεσμά 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Andromache” 577; ἀσκόν [prev. author] “Cyc.” 161; τὸ στόμα 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “de Equitandi ratione” 6.8]]:—passive, τὰ χαλώμενα ὅπλα [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Hippocrates Medicus “περὶ ἄρθρων ἐμβολῆς” 43; πρὶν ἂν χαλασθῇ δεσμά 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Prometheus Vinctus” 991.]]

__I.7
of the bowels, etc., ὑγρὰ χ. [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Hippocrates Medicus “προρρητικόν” 1.99, compare “Coac.” 20; ἢν αἱ μῆτραι μὴ χαλάσωσι τὰ ἐπιμήνια [prev. author] “Mul.” 1.61.]]

__I.8
metaphorically, τὴν ὀργήν χ. let it go, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Vespae” 727 (_anapaest meter_); χ. [τὸν νόον] ἐς ὄψιν τινός 5th-4th c.BC: Timaeus Locrus Philosophus 104c; χ. ἐπιθυμίαν 1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus 2.133a; τὸ βαρὺ καὶ ἀμειδές 4th c.AD: Alciphro Epistolographus 3.3]]; remit, μήτε τῆς προνοίας χαλώσης τὴν.. ὑπεροχήν [Refs 5th c.AD+ [5th c.AD: Proclus Philosophus “Inst.” 122]]; τὸ ἀεὶ ταῦτα οὕτως ἔχειν ἐχάλασαν relaxed the strict principle that.. [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Sophista” 242e]]:—passive, to be softened, λίθος εἰς ὑγρότητα κεχαλασμένος [Refs 4th c.AD+ [4th c.AD: Callistratus Sophista “Statuarum descriptiones” 5]]; also κεχαλάσθαι εἰς τὸ αὐτεξούσιον to have free play, opposed to συντετάχθαι, [Refs 3rd c.AD+ [3rd c.AD: Plotinus Philosophus 4.3.16.]]

__II
intransitive, become slack or loose, opposed to συντείνω, [Refs 7th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Phaedo” 98d; χόλαισιν ἄγκυρραι 7th-6th c.BC: Alcaeus Lyricus 18.9 (assuming variant); ζῶναι χαλῶσι 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Bacchae” 935]]; πύλαι χαλῷσαι open gates, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 7.5.29]]: metaphorically with genitive, have a remission of, χαλάσσομεν τὰς θυμοβόρω λύας [Refs 7th c.BC+ [7th-6th c.BC: Alcaeus Lyricus “Supp.” 23.10; τί χαλᾷ μανιῶ; 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Prometheus Vinctus” 1057 (_anapaest meter_); (also _absolutely_, 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Coloneus” 203 (Lyric poetry), 840)]]; relax, φρονήματος χ. [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Fragmenta” 716; τῆς ὀργῆς 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Aves” 383 (troch.); [τὸ ὂν] χαλάσαν τῆς τοῦ ἑνὸς ἁπλότητος 5th-6th c.AD: Damascius Philosophus “de Principiis” 13.]]

__II.2
with dative person, χ. τινι give way or yield to any one, be indulgent to him, εἰ τοῖσιν.. κτείνουσιν ἀλλήλους χαλᾷς [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Eumenides” 219; χάλα τοκεῦσιν 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Hecuba” 403; with _genitive_ add., μοι τῆς ἀρχῆς χάλασον 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Meno” 86e, compare 1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus “Lycurgus” 7]]: absolutely, give way, εἴκειν ὁδοῦ χαλῶντα τοῖς κακίοσιν [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Ion” 637.]]

__II.3
absolutely, grow slack or weak, ἐπειδὰν αἱ ἐπιθυμίαι παύσωνται κατατείνουσαι καὶ χαλάσωσι [Refs [[prev. author] “R.” 329c]]; abate, χαλάσει ὁ παγετός [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Hippocrates Medicus “Aër.” 8; ὀδύνη [prev. author] “Acut.” 16.]]

LSJ-hänvisningar: Χαλδαϊκοῖς • Kopplad hebreisk kod: H3778
deep_entry:
Abbott-Smith / STEPBible (TBESG)
Χαλδαῖος, -ου, ὁ
a Chaldæan: γῆ Χαλδαίων, Act.7:4.†
(AS)

---

LSJ / STEPBible (TFLSJ)
χαλδ-αῖος, ὁ,
Chaldaean, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 3.155, 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Fragmenta” 638, etc.]]

__II
astrologer, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Fragmenta” 35, 1st c.BC: Cicero, M. Tullius Orator et Philosophus “Div.” 1.1.2, 1st c.BC: Philodemus Gadarensis Epigrammaticus “Rh.” 1.42S., 1st c.BC: Geminus Astronomicus 2.5]] (since the Chaldaeans were given to astrology,[Refs 5th c.BC+ [compare 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.181, 2nd c.AD: Arrianus Historicus “Anabasis” 7.17.1, etc.)]]:—Χαλδαία (i.e. γῆ), ἡ, Chaldaea, [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [5th c.AD(?): Stephanus Byzantius, 2nd c.AD: Ptolemaeus Mathematicus “Geographia” 5.19]]:— Χαλδαϊκός, ή, όν, Chaldaean, γράμματα [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd c.AD: Athenaeus Epigrammaticus 12.529f]]; ἱστορίαι, title of work by Berosus, [Refs 1st c.AD+ [1st c.AD: Josephus Historicus “Antiquitates Judaicae” 10.11.1, compare “Ap.” 1.20]]; μέθοδος, i.e. astrology, [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd c.AD: Sextus Empiricus Philosophus “adversus Mathematicos” 5.43 (so -κή alone, [prev. work] 45); ἐπιτηδεύματα 5th-6th c.AD: Damascius Philosophus cited in 10th c.AD: Suidas Legal icographus]] see entry {Χαλδαϊκοῖς}: comparative -ώτερος[Refs [[prev. author] “Pr.” 206.]] adverb -κῶς[Refs [[prev. work] 183]]— Χαλδαϊστί, adverb in the Chaldaean language, [LXX+1st c.AD+ [LXX.Dan.2.26, 1st c.AD: Philo Judaeus 2.546.]]

deep_entry:
Abbott-Smith / STEPBible (TBESG)
χαλεπός, -ή, -όν
[in LXX: Isa.18:2 (יָרֵא), Wis.3:19, Sir.3:21, al. ;]
hard;
__(a) hard to do or deal with, difficult;
__(b) hard to bear, painful, grievous: καιροί, 2Ti.3:1;
__(with) of persons, hard to deal with, harsh, fierce, savage: Mat.8:28.†
(AS)

---

LSJ / STEPBible (TFLSJ)
χαλεπ-ός, ή, όν,
difficult (ὃ ἂν μὴ ῥᾴδιον ᾖ ἀλλὰ διὰ πολλῶν πραγμάτων γίγνηται [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Protagoras” 341d: opposed to ῥᾴδιος, 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Rhetorica” 1363a24, in various relations):]]

__I
in reference to the feelings, hard to bear, painful, grievous (so frequently in [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Homerus Epicus), κεραυνός 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 14.417; θύελλα 21.335; ἄνεμοι 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 12.286; πόνος 23.250; ἄλγος, πένθος, 2.193, 6.169; γῆρας 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 8.103; ἄλη 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 10.464; χαλεπώτερος ἄεθλος 8th-7th c.BC: Hesiodus Epicus “Theogonia” 800]]; ἄλλα τῶν κατεχόντων πρηγμάτων - ώτερα [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 6.40; χ. πνεῦμα 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Supplices” 166 (Lyric poetry); δύα [prev. author] “Th.” 228 (Lyric poetry)]]; χαλεπώτατα [πράγματα] [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Trachiniae” 1273 (_anapaest meter_); συμφορά 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Hippolytus” 768 (Lyric poetry)]]; νόσος, πλάνη, etc., [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Symposium” 4.37, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Sophista” 245e (_comparative_), etc.]]; ἡ ἐσβολὴ αὕτη -ωτάτη τοῖς Ἀθηναίοις ἐγένετο [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 3.26]]; [θώρακες] δύσφοροι καὶ χ., of ill-fitting cuirasses, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Memorabilia” 3.10.13: τὸ χ. τοῦ πνεύματος]] the severity of the wind, [Refs [[prev. author] “An.” 4.5.4]]; τὰ χ. hardships, opposed to τὰ τερπνά, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. author] “Mem.” 2.1.23, etc.; τερπνῶν χαλεπῶν τε κρίσις 5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “Fragmenta.” 131, compare 3rd c.AD: Plotinus Philosophus 5.9.14]]: comparative, more unpleasant, [Refs 4th c.AD+ [4th c.AD: Julianus Imperator “Orationes” 6.202c.]]

__I.2
hard to do or deal with, difficult, irksome, -ώτατον ἔργον ἁπάντων [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Equites” 516 (_anapaest meter_); compare 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 3.59 (_superlative_), etc.]]; χαλεπὰ τὰ καλά proverbial cited in [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Hp.Ma.” 304e, +others]], attributed to Solon by Scholia (at [prev. work]); χαλεπὸν ὁ βίος [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Memorabilia” 2.9.1, compare 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Politicus” 299e: with]]infinitive active or middle, χαλεπή τοι ἐγὼ μένος ἀντιφέρεσθαι, = {χαλεπόν ἐστί μοι ἀντιφέρεσθαί σοι}, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 21.482; χαλεποὶ δὲ θεοὶ φαίνεσθαι ἐναργεῖς 20.131]]; χαλεπὸν δέ τ᾽ ὀρύσσειν [τὸ μῶλυ] [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 10.305; χ. προϊδέσθαι καπρός 8th-7th c.BC: Hesiodus Epicus “Scutum Herculis” 386; χ. ἔρις ἀνθρώποις ὁμιλεῖν κρεσσόνων 5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “N.” 10.72; χ. προσπολεμεῖν 5th-6th c.BC: Isocrates Orator 4.138, compare 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 7.51 (_comparative_)]]; χ. συγγενέσθαι, εὑρεῖν, γενέσθαι, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 330c, 412b, 502c; χ. πάσχειν [prev. author] “Cri.” 49b (_comparative_)]]: also with infinitive passive, χαλεπὸς διαγνωσθῆναι καὶ δειχθῆναι [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Antipho Orator 2.1.1, compare 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 3.94, etc.; χαλεπὸν ληφθῆναι ὁ τόπος 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Physica” 212a8]]; χαλεπόν [ἐστι] with infinitive, 'tis hard, difficult to do, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 4.651]]; with accusative et infinitive, 'tis difficult for one to do.., [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 16.620, 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 20.313]]: with dative et infinitive, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 21.184, 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 11.156.]]

__I.3
dangerous, λιμένες [Refs 5th c.BC+ [19.189; θάλασσα 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 4.24; χ. τὰ παρόντα 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 3.2.2.]]

__I.4
of ground, difficult, rugged, χωρία χ. καὶ πετρώδη [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 4.9; ὁδός [prev. author] 5.58, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 328e; χ... καὶ προσάντης.. ὁδός ἐστιν 4th c.BC: Anaxandrides Comicus 56; πρόσοδοι 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 5.2.3; πορεία [prev. work] 5.6.10; σταθμός [prev. work] 4.5.3]]; χωρίον -ώτατον a place most difficult to take, [Refs [[prev. work] 4.8.2.]]

__II
of persons, hard to deal with, cruel, harsh, stern (opposed to πρᾷος, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 493b (_superlative_), 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Ethica Nicomachea” 1126a26), βασιλεύς, δαίμων, 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 2.232, 19.201; χαλεποί τε καὶ ἄγριοι 8.575]]; -ώτερος a more bitter enemy, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 3.40]]; -ώτατοι most difficult to deal with, most dangerous or troublesome, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [[prev. work] 42, compare 7.21; -ώτεροι πάροικοι [prev. author] 3.113; χαλεπόν γε θυγάτηρ κτῆμα 4th-3rd c.BC: Menander Comicus 18]]: with dative person, cruel or harsh towards one, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 17.388; τοῖς ξυμπροθυμηθεῖσι τὸν ἔκπλουν 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 8.1, etc.]]; πρὸς τοὺς πολεμίους, τοὺς ἀγνῶτας, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 375c, 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Politica” 1328a8 (also πρὸς τοὺς δρόμους 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Cynegeticus” 5.17); ἐπὶ νύμφαις ἀλλοτρίαις 3rd c.BC: Theocritus Poeta Bucolicus 22.145.]]

__II.b
of words, χαλεπῷ ἠνίπαπε μύθῳ [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 2.245, etc.; ἐρεθιζέμεν αἰεὶ μύθοισιν χ. 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 17.395]]; χ. ὀνείδεα, ὁμοκλαί, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 3.438, 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 17.189; φῆμις 14.239; μῆνις 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 5.178.]]

__II.c
especially of judges, ἦν τὸ δίκαιον φυλάσσων χ. [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.100, compare 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Critias” 107d, 5th-6th c.BC: Andocides Orator 4.36; also χ. ἀρχή 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 1.77; τιμωρία 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Apologia” 39c (_comparative_)]]; νόμοι [Refs 4th c.BC+ [[prev. author] “Hp.Mi.” 372a (_comparative_), 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 21.44, 35.50.]]

__II.d
savage, fierce, κύνες [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 5.8.24, “Cyn.” 10.23]]; of bees, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Historia Animalium” 624b30 (_comparative_)]]; [θηρία] χ. τὰς φύσεις [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Politicus” 274b.]]

__II.2
ill-tempered, testy, χ. ὢν καὶ δύσκολος [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Vespae” 942, compare 5th-6th c.BC: Isocrates Orator 19.26; ὀργὴν χ. 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 3.131]]; χαλεπῇ τῇ χειρί with a rough hand, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Lysistrata” 1116.]]

__II.3
of plants, hurtful to the soil, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-3rd c.BC: Theophrastus Philosophus “Historia Plantarum” 8.9.3 (_superlative_).]]

__B
adverb -πῶς hardly, with difficulty, διαγνῶναι χ. ἦν ἄνδρα ἕκαστον [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 7.424; χ. δέ σ᾽ ἔολπα τὸ ῥέξειν 20.186; χ. κε φύγοις κακόν 8th-7th c.BC: Hesiodus Epicus “Opera et Dies” 684; χ. ὀργὰς μεταβάλλουσιν 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Medea” 121 (_anapaest meter_); χ. γνῶναι 5th c.BC: Antipho Orator 3.2.1; τὰ τοῖς ἄλλοις χ. εὑρημένα ῥᾳδίως μανθάνειν 5th-6th c.BC: Isocrates Orator 1.18, compare 44]] οὐ or μὴ χ. without much ado, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 1.2, 7.81, etc.]]

__B.2
hardly, scarcely, δοκέω.. χ. ἂν Ἕλληνας Πέρσῃσι μάχεσθαι [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 7.103; χ. παρὰ τοῖς ἐχθροῖς εὑρεθήσεται 5th c.BC: Lysias Orator 29.2; χ. ἂν πείσαιμι 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Phaedo” 84d.]]

__B.3
χ. ἔχει, ={χαλεπόν ἐστι}, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 3.53]]: with accusative et infinitive, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Historia Graeca (Hellenica)” 7.4.6.]]

__B.4
painfully, miserably, -ώτερον ζῆν [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 579d; ἐν τοῖς -ώτατα διῆγον 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 7.71.]]

__B.II
of persons, angrily, cruelly, harshly, χ. τιμωρεῖσθαι [Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. author] 3.46; ἀποκρίνασθαι [prev. author] 5.42, compare 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Hippolytus” 203 (_anapaest meter_), 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Plutus” 60, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Phaedrus” 269b]]; χ. φέρειν τι take it ill, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 2.16, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 330a, etc.]]; also χ. ἔφερον τῷ πολέμῳ, τοῖς πράγμασιν, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Historia Graeca (Hellenica)” 5.1.29, “An.” 1.3.3; ἐπὶ τῇ πολιορκίᾳ [prev. author] “HG” 7.4.21, compare 1st c.BC: Dionysius Halicarnassensis 3.50; also χ. φέρειν τινός 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 2.62; also χ. λαμβάνεσθαι τοῦ παιδός 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 2.121. ; χ. λαμβάνειν περί τινος 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 6.61]]; of the laws [Refs 5th c.BC+ [compare(above 11.1c), χ. προστάττειν 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Leges” 925d.]]

__B.II.2
frequently in the phrase χ. ἔχειν to be angry, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 6.4.16, etc.]]; τινι with one, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. author] “HG” 1.5.16; πρὸς τοὺς λόγους 5th-6th c.BC: Isocrates Orator 3.3, compare 51]] χ. ἔχειν τισὶν ἐπί τινι with persons for a thing, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 20.135, compare 1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus “Cicero” 43; χ. διακεῖσθαι πρὸς ἅπαντας 5th-6th c.BC: Isocrates Orator “Epistulae” 7.5; χ. πρὸς φιλοσοφίαν διακεῖσθαι 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 500b; χ. πρὸς ἡμᾶς διετέθησαν 5th-6th c.BC: Isocrates Orator 8.79; ἐπί τινι χ. διατεθείς 1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus “Pericles” 36.]]

__B.II.2.b
χ. ἔχειν, also, to be in a bad way, χ. ἔχω ὑπὸ τοῦ πότου [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Symposium” 176a, compare “Tht.” 142b.]]— Beside the regular comparative χαλεπώτερον [Refs 5th c.BC+ [(5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 1.77, 7.50, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Phaedo” 94d, etc.)]] we have -ωτέρως[Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 2.50, 8.40, 4th-3rd c.BC: Theophrastus Philosophus “Historia Plantarum” 6.7.1]]: superlative -ώτατα[Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 7.71, 8.95, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 579d, etc.]]

LSJ / STEPBible (TFLSJ)
χᾰλῑνός
(Aeolic dialect χάλιννος probably in [Refs [“Etymologicum Gudianum” 561.5)]], ὁ, irregular plural χαλινά [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [3rd c.BC: Apollonius Rhodius Epicus 4.1607, 2nd-3rd c.AD: Oppianus Anazarbensis Epicus “Halieutica - Poetae Bucolici et Didactici” 1.191, 1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus 2.613c, 2nd c.AD: Soranus Medicus 1.100, etc.]]:—bit, once in [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Homerus Epicus, ἐν δὲ χαλινοὺς γαμφηλῇς ἔβαλον 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 19.393; χαλινὸν ἐμβαλεῖν γνάθοις 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Alcestis” 492; χ. ἐξαιρεῖται 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “de Equitandi ratione” 3.2]]; of the horse, χ. οὐκ ἐπίσταται φέρειν (metaphorically of Cassandra) [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Agamemnon” 1066]]; χ. δέχεσθαι, λαμβάνειν, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “de Equitandi ratione” 3.2, 6.10]]; λαβεῖν, ἔχειν, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Rhetorica” 1393b16, 21]]; τὸν χ. ἐνδακεῖν champ the bit, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Phaedrus” 254d]]; of the rider, δοτέον τὸν χ. one must give a horse the rein, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “de Equitandi ratione” 10.12]]; ὀπίσω σπάσαι, ξυνέχειν ἀνάγκῃ, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Phaedrus” 254e, 2nd c.AD: Lucianus Sophista “DDeor.” 25.1; [χ.] εἰς ἄκρον τὸ στόμα καθιέμενος 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “de Equitandi ratione” 6.9.]]—Expld. of the bit, opposed to reins (ἡνίαι), by [Refs 5th c.BC+ [2nd c.AD(?): Pollianus Epigrammaticus 1.148; so ἡνίας τε.. καὶ χ. 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 601c; χ. τινα χαλκεῖ ἐκδιδόντα σκευάσαι [prev. author] “Prm.” 127a; κατὰ [τὸν κυνόδοντα] ἐμβάλλεται ὁ χ. 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Historia Animalium” 576b18, compare 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Septem contra Thebas” 123 (Lyric poetry), 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Coloneus” 1067 (Lyric poetry)]]; but distinguished from στόμιον by [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.215, compare 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Septem contra Thebas” 207 (Lyric poetry), 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “de Equitandi ratione” 6.9, 10.9, etc.]]; and may be used generally for bit and bridle, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 3.118, 4.64, “IG” 12.374.176, “PCair.Zen.” 659.11 (3rd c.BC).]]

__2
metaphorically, of anything which curbs, restrains, or compels, Ἀργοῦς χ., of an anchor, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “P.” 4.25]]; χ. λινόδετοι, ={χαλινωτήρια}, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Iphigenia Taurica” 1043]]; παρθενίας χ. λύειν, of the virgin zone, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “I.” 8(7).48]]; χαλινοῖς ἐν πετρίνοισιν, of Prometheus' bonds, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Prometheus Vinctus” 562 (_anapaest meter_); Διὸς χ., of the will of Zeus, [prev. work] 672]]; χαλινῶν ἀναύδῳ μένει, of forcible constraint, [Refs [[prev. author] “Ag.” 238 (Lyric poetry)]]; πολλῶν χαλινῶν ἔργον οἰάκων θ᾽ ἅμα, i.e. it requires much skill and force to guide, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Fragmenta” 869]]; τῷ δήμῳ χ. ἐμβαλεῖν ὕβρεως a bridle to curb their violence, [Refs 1st c.AD+ [1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus “Comp. Per.Fab.” 1, compare 2nd c.AD: Lucianus Sophista “Herm.” 82; τῆς γλώττης τὰ χ. 1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus 2.613c; ἐπέστω τῷ στόματι χ. 4th c.AD: Libanius Sophista “Epistulae” 315.4; χ. οὐδεὶς ὀμμάτων 2nd-3rd c.AD: Philostratus Sophista “Vita Apollonii” 6.11.]]

__II
generally, strap, thong, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Cyclops” 461 (dual).]]

__III
part of the tackle of a ship, [Refs [Inscriptiones Graecae 22.1610.11,14.]]

__IV
corner of the horse's mouth, where the bit rests, [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd c.AD(?): Pollianus Epigrammaticus 2.90 (_plural_)]]; of the human mouth, [Refs 2nd c.BC+ [2nd c.BC: Nicander Epicus “Alexipharmaca” 117, 223, “PUniv.Giss.” 44.7, (2nd-1st c.BC), 1st-2nd c.AD: Heliodorus Medicus cited in Orib 48.31.4, 2nd c.AD: Soranus Medicus 1.100, “PSI” 9.1016.25 (2nd c.BC), 2nd c.AD: Aretaeus Medicus “περὶ αἰτιῶν καὶ σημείων ὀξέων παθῶν” 1.9, 5th c.AD: Caelius Aurelianus Medicus “TP” 1.4, 6th c.AD: Aëtius Medicus 8.27]]; but, ={ἡ σύνδεσις τῶν γνάθων}, [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd c.AD: Rufus Medicus “περὶ ὀνομασίας” 53, compare 6th c.AD: Aëtius Medicus 8.40.]]

__IV.2
fangs of serpents, from their shape and position in the mouth, [Refs 2nd c.BC+ [2nd c.BC: Nicander Epicus “Theriaca” 234.]]

χάλκεος, έα,
Ionic dialect -έη [Refs 8th c.BC+ [(8th c.BC: Homerus Epicus always -είη (see. χάλκειος))]], εον (also εος, εον [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 18.222 (ὄπα χάλκεον Αἰακίδαο, where 4th-3rd c.BC: Zenodotus Grammaticus χαλκέην as _disyllable_), 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus (see. below): rarely in Trag., 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Choephori” 686, 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Fragmenta” 534.3, 7 (_anapaest meter_), 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Ion” 1]]; Aeolic dialect, Doric dialect χάλκιος [Refs 7th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Epicharmus Comicus 79, 7th-6th c.BC: Alcaeus Lyricus 15.3, “SIG” 945.6 (Assos, 4th c.BC), “IGRom.” 4.1302.35 (Cyme, 1st c.BC-1st c.AD)]], also Boeotian dialect, compare χαλκοῦ; Attic dialect χαλκοῦς, ῆ, οῦν [Refs [(“IG” 12.313.55, etc.]], but χαλκέων δέλτων [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Axiochus” 371a codices)]]; Epic dialect also χάλκειος, see at {χάλκειος}: (χαλκός):—of copper or bronze, brazen, οὐδός, δόμος, τεῖχος, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 8.15, 18.371, 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 10.4]]; ἄξων, κύκλα, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 13.30, 5.723; χ. Ἀράων θάλαμοι 5th-6th c.BC: Antimachus Colophonius Elegiacus et Epicus in “PMilan.” 17.48; χ. καὶ ἀδαμαντίνοις τείχεσι 4th c.BC: Aeschines Orator 3.84; ὀδός 4th c.BC: Astydamas Tragicus 9, 3rd c.BC: Ister Historicus 30]]; especially of arms and armour, ἔγχος, ξίφος, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 3.317, 335; σάκος 7.220; θώρηξ, χιτών, 13.398, 440]]; ἔντεα [Refs 5th c.BC+ [18.131, etc.; χαλκέοις ὅπλοις 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Phoenissae” 1359; also λέβητος χαλκέου 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Choephori” 686, compare 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Cyclops” 392]]; χαλκέοισικάδοις, χαλκέοις δρεπάνοις, S.[same place]; in Trag. mostly contraction, χαλκοῖς βάθροισι [Refs [[prev. author] “OC” 1591; χαλκῆς ὑπαὶ σάλπιγγος [prev. author] “El.” 711; χαλκῆς ἐκ δέλτου [prev. author] “Tr.” 683.]]

__b
of statues, χ. Ζεύς, χ. Ποσειδέων, a bronze statue of.., [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 9.81; χ. ταῦρος 5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “P.” 1.95; ἡ χαλκῆ Ἀθηνᾶ 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 19.272; ἱστάναι τινὰ χαλκοῦν [prev. author] 13.21; ἄξιος σταθῆναι χαλκοῦς 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Rhetorica” 1410a33; στήλη ἐφ᾽ ᾗ ὁ στρατηγός ἐστιν ὁ χαλκοῦς 5th-6th c.BC: Andocides Orator 1.38]]; compare χαλκῆ.

__c
χ. ἀγών a contest for a shield of brass, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “N.” 10.22.]]

__2
metaphorically, brazen, i. e. hard, stout, strong, χάλκεος Ἄρης [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 5.704, etc.]] (unless wearing brazen armour, compare χάλκεοι ἄνδρες Oracle texts cited in [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 2.152)]]; Χαλκοῦς, nickname of Aristomedes, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-3rd c.BC: Dinarchus Orator cited in 1st c.BC: Didymus Grammaticus]]in D.[Refs 5th c.BC+ [9.57, 4th-3rd c.BC: Philemo Comicus 1.2 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator, 1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus “Demosthenes” 11; χ. στονόεντ᾽ ὅμαδον 5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “I.” 8(7).27; χ. αὐδά [prev. author] “Pae.” 2.100]]; χάλκεον ἦτορ a heart of brass, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 2.490; ὄπα χ. 18.222; χ. ὕπνος, i. e. the sleep of death, 11.241]]; χαλκέοισι νώτοις, of Atlas, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Ion” 1.]]

as substantive, see at {χαλκοῦς. [χάλκεοι} is disyllable in [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th-7th c.BC: Hesiodus Epicus “Opera et Dies” 150.]]]

__II
in Poets frequently for anything made of metal, especially of arms (hence [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus calls it πολιός,]] the proper epithet of iron, [Refs [“P.” 3.48)]]; of offensive arms, ὀξέϊ χαλκῷ, νηλέϊ χ., of a spear, a sword, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 4.540, 3.292, +others]]; of a knife, [Refs [1.236, +others]]; of an axe, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [13.180, 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 5.244, +others]]; of a fish-hook, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 16.408]]; of defensive arms, as the plates laid on a shield, [Refs [20.275]]; χαλκὸν ζώννυσθαι, of a warrior girding on his armour,[Refs [23.130; κεκορυθμένος, αἴθοπι χ. 4.495; ἐδύσετο νώροπα χ. 2.578]]; of both combined, πλάγχθη δ᾽ ἀπὸ χαλκόφι χαλκός the spear of bronze glanced off the helm of bronze, [Refs [11.351.]]

__II.2
of vessels, copper, cauldron, urn,[Refs 8th c.BC+ [18.349, 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 8.426]]; of a cinerary urn, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Electra” 758]]; collectively of bronze plate, χ. μυρίος, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “N.” 10.45; θάλαμον.., ὅθι νητὸς χρυσὸς καὶ χ. ἔκειτο 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 2.338, compare 13.19, 21.10, 62, 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 2.226]]; used in payment of ransom, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [22.50, compare 340, 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 5.38.]]

__II.3
of a bronze mirror, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Fragmenta - American Journal of Philology” 393, 3rd c.BC: Callimachus Epicus “Lavacrum Palladis” 21, “Ap” 6.210 (4th-3rd c.BC: Philetas)]]; used as a burning-glass, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-3rd c.BC: Theophrastus Philosophus “de Igne” 73.]]

collectively, copper money, [NT+4th c.BC+ [“IPE” 12.24.15 (Olbia, 4th c.BC), NT.Matt.10.9, NT.Mark.12.41, compare ἰσόνομος 11]]; generally, money, opposed to κύαμοι, [Refs 3rd c.AD+ [“IG” 14.423 ii 21 (from Tauromenium), compare “BGU” 822.12 (3rd c.AD), etc.]]; χαλκοῦ σπάνις Men[Refs [“Mon.” 156; χαλκὸν ἔχων πῶς οὐδὲν ἔχεις μάθε “Anthologia Graeca” 11.167 (Pollian.).]]

__II.5
={χάλκωμα}, bronze plate or tablet, τὰν προξενίαν γράψαντας εἰς χαλκὸν ἀνθέμεν [Refs 4th c.BC+ [“IG” 9(1).682 (Corcyra, 4th c.BC)]]; οὐετρανοὶ οἱ χωρὶς χαλκῶν, who have not received bronze copies of the privileges granted on discharge, [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [“BGU” 113.5 (2nd c.AD), etc.]]

χαλκοῦ λεπίς, small pieces that scale off under the hammer, [Refs [[prev. work]78. (Perh. cf. Lith.]]geležìs 'iron'.)

Greek idiom, [Refs 1st c.BC+ [1st c.BC: Dionysius Halicarnassensis “Epistula ad Pompeium” 3]]: frequently of persons, feature, ὁ χ. τοῦ προσώπου [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.116; εἰληφέναι χαρακτῆρα ἑκατέρου τοῦ εἴδους 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Phaedrus” 263b; οἱ τῆς ὄψεως χ. 1st c.BC: Diodorus Siculus Historicus 1.91; ἀνδρῶν οὐδεὶς χ. ἐμπέφυκε σώματι 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Medea” 519; δεινὸς χ. κἀπίσημος.. ἐσθλῶν γενέσθαι [prev. author] “Hec.” 379; φανερὸς χ. ἀρετᾶς [prev. author] “HF” 659 (Lyric poetry)]]; ἠθικοὶ χ., title of work by [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-3rd c.BC: Theophrastus Philosophus: _plural_, οἱ χ.]] the features of the face, [Refs 1st c.BC+ [1st c.AD: Josephus Historicus “Antiquitates Judaicae” 13.12.1, compare “OGI” 508.13 (Ephesus, 2nd c.AD); χ. μορφῆς ἐμῆς [prev. work]383.60 (Nemrud Dagh, 1st c.BC, _sing._)]]; [τοῦ ἐμβρύου] [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd c.AD: Soranus Medicus 1.33 (_plural_): hence,]]

__II.4
type or character (regarded as shared with others) of a thing or person, rarely of an individual nature, ἀνδρὸς χ. ἐκ λόγου γνωρίζεται [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th-3rd c.BC: Menander Comicus 72; χ. μοχθηρότατον παραπλάττεσθαι 1st c.BC: Philodemus Gadarensis Epigrammaticus “Rh.” 1.6 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus; τὸν χ. τὸν Διογένους 2nd c.AD: Arrianus Historicus “Epicteti Dissertationes” 3.22.80; τίνα ἔχει χ. τὰ δόγματ; [prev. work] 4.5.17]]; of nations, [Refs 2nd c.BC+ [2nd c.BC: Polybius Historicus 18.34.7.]]

__II.5
style, frequently in Rhet., ὁ Δημοσθένους χ. [Refs 1st c.BC+ [1st c.BC: Dionysius Halicarnassensis “de Demosthene” 9, compare “Pomp.” 1, 1st c.BC: Cicero, M. Tullius Orator et Philosophus “Epistulae ad Quintum Fratrem” 2.15(16).5; χ. δικανικός 1st c.BC: Philodemus Gadarensis Epigrammaticus “Rh.” 2.137S.]]; χ. optimi the ideal type, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [1st c.BC: Cicero, M. Tullius Orator et Philosophus “Oralor” 11.36, compare 39.134; χ. ἰσχνός, μεγαλοπρεπής, γλαφυρός, δεινός 4th c.BC: Demetrius Phalereus Rhetor “Demetrius on Style” 36, compare 1st c.BC: Dionysius Halicarnassensis “de Demosthene” 33; χ. λέξεως [prev. author] “Lys.” 11; χ. Ἀσιανός 1st c.BC-1st c.AD: Strabo Geographus 13.1.66.]]

__II.6
impress, image, τῆς ὑποστάσεως [τοῦ θεοῦ] [NT.Heb.1.3]; πάθους, ἀρετῆς, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [3rd c.AD: Longinus Rhetor 22.1, 4th-5th c.AD: Eunapius Historicus “Fragmenta Historica - HGM” p.243 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator: _absolutely_, οἱ Σεβάστειοι χ.]] the imperial seal, i.e. the emperor himself, [Refs 1st c.BC+ [“IG” 5(2).268.24 (Mantinea, 1st c.BC).]]

__II.7
Grammars, typical form, [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd c.AD: Apollonius Dyscolus Grammaticus “de Syntaxi;” 20.10, 103.23.]]

χάραξ, -ακος, ὁ
(χαράσσω), [in LXX for סֹלְלָה, מָצוֹר, etc. ;]

LSJ / STEPBible (TFLSJ)
χάραξ [χᾰ], ᾰκος, ὁ,
also ἡ, (χαράσσω) pointed stake: especially,

__I
vine-prop, pole, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Acharnenses” 986, “V.” 1201, “Pax” 1263, 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 3.70, “BGU” 1122.17 (1st c.BC): proverbial ἐξηπάτησεν ἡ χ. τὴν ἄμπελον,]] of those who trust in a 'broken reed', [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Vespae” 1291.]]

__II
pale, used in fortifying the entrenchments of a camp, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [[prev. author] “Ach.” 1178, 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 21.167]]; = Latin vallus, [Refs 2nd c.BC+ [2nd c.BC: Polybius Historicus 1.29.3, 18.18.1:]]

__II.2
collectively, ={χαράκωμα}, palisaded camp, Theophil.[Refs 4th c.BC+ [Comedy texts 9, “SIG” 363.1 (Ephesus, 3rd c.BC), 4th-3rd c.BC: Menander Comicus 77, 1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus “Caesar” 17 (_plural_), 4th c.AD: Julianus Imperator “Orationes” 2.60b; τὰν ἐκτὸς τοῦ χ. χώραν “IG” 42(1).76.21 (Epid., 2nd c.BC)]]; palisade, χάρακα βαλέσθαι πρὸς τῇ πόλει (variant{χαράκωμα}) [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 18.87]]; = Latin vallum, [NT+2nd c.BC+ [2nd c.BC: Polybius Historicus 1.80.11, 3.45.5, +others, NT.Luke.19.43]]; χάρακα τίθεσθαι form an entrenched camp, [Refs 1st c.BC+ [1st c.BC: Dionysius Halicarnassensis 6.29; χ. βαλέσθαι 1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus “Aemilius Paulus” 17, compare “Marc.” 18, etc.; βάλλειν [prev. author] “Sull.” 28]]; ἀποταφρεύειν, περιταφρεύειν,[Refs 4th c.BC+ [[prev. work] 21, “Luc.” 31; διασπᾶν [prev. author] “Ant.” 18; χ. σεσιδηρωμένος καὶ ἁλύσεσι δεδεμένος 1st c.BC: Diodorus Siculus Historicus 19.83; χ. κύκλῳ τῆς νεώς 4th c.BC: Moschio Tragicus cited in 2nd c.AD: Athenaeus Epigrammaticus 5.208d.]]

__III
cutting, slip, especially of an olive, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-3rd c.BC: Theophrastus Philosophus “Historia Plantarum” 2.1.2, “CP” 5.1. [4], “Geoponica” 9.11.5]]; of other plants, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-3rd c.BC: Theophrastus Philosophus “de Causis Plantarum” 1.12.9.]]

__III.2
collectively, ={ἀκανθώδη φυτά}, [Refs 5th c.AD+ [5th c.AD(?): Hesychius Legal icographus]]

__IV
a seafish, one of the breams, Sargus, [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [3rd c.BC: Diphilus Siphnius Rerum Naturalium Scriptor cited in Ath 8.355e, 2nd-3rd c.AD: Oppianus Anazarbensis Epicus “Halieutica - Poetae Bucolici et Didactici” 1.173]]; also a fish of the Red Sea, [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd-3rd c.AD: Aelianus “De Natura Animalium - Ar.Byzantine Epit.” 12.25.]]

__V
name of a bandage, [Refs 1st c.AD+ [1st-2nd c.AD: Heliodorus Medicus cited in 4th c.AD: Oribasius Medicus 48.31 at Title Page, 2nd c.AD: Soranus Medicus “de fasciis - Opera Hippocratis et Galeni” 17, 2nd c.AD: Galenus Medicus 18 (1).777. (2nd c.AD: Phrynichus Atticista 43 gives ἡ χ.]] in signification 1, and in [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [“PS” p.125B. gives ὁ χ. in signification 11, compare 2nd c.AD(?): Pollianus Epigrammaticus 1.162; but this distinction is not observed by later writers.)]]

χαρίζομαι
(χάρις), [in LXX: Est.8:7 (נָתַן), Sng.1:4 א, Sir.12:3, 2 -4Ma.9:1-32 * ;]
__1. to show favour or kindness: with dative of person(s), Gal.3:18.
__2. to give freely, bestow: with accusative and dative, Luk.7:21, Act.3:14 25:11, 16 27:24, Rom.8:32, 1Co.2:12, Php.1:29 2:9, Phm 22.
__3. In late Gk. (= Lat. condonare), to grant forgiveness, forgive freely: of debt, Luk.7:42-43 (EGT, in l); of sin, 2Co.2:7 2:10 12:13, Eph.4:32, Col.2:13 3:13 (cf. DB, ii, 57a).†
(AS)

LSJ / STEPBible (TFLSJ)
χᾰρίζω,
future χαριῶ [Refs 5th c.BC+ [1st c.BC: Philodemus Gadarensis Epigrammaticus “Rh.” 1.381 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus, “Corpus Glossariorum Latinorum”]]: aorist imperative χάρισον [Refs [“PMag.Lond.” 122.17]]:—usually middle χαρίζομαι, future -ιοῦμαι[Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 3.40, 8.65]]; χαριῇ (variant{-εῖ}) also in [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.90; Cretan dialect χαριξίομαι “GDI” 5176.16 (found at Teos); also χαρίξομαι [prev. work]5178.17 ([prev. passage]); χαρίηνται]] is a false Aeolic dialect form in [NT+2nd c.AD+ [“Milet.” 3 No.152.56; later χαρίσομαι NT.Rom.8.32, 2nd c.AD: Lucianus Sophista “DDeor.” 22.4]]: aorist ἐχαρισάμην [Refs 8th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.91, etc.; _optative_ χαρίσαιτο 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 6.49]]; Aeolic dialect imperative χάρισσαι [Refs 7th c.BC+ [7th-6th c.BC: Sappho Lyrica “Papyrus fragments” in E. Diehl, 16.4]]; Cretan dialect infinitive χαρίξασθαι [Refs [“GDI” 5163b8 (from Mylasa):]] —passive forms, future χαρισθήσομαι in passive sense, [NT.Philm.22:]aorist ἐχαρίσθην in passive sense, [NT.Act.3.14, NT.1Cor.2.12:]perfect κεχάρισμαι in active sense, κεχάρισαι [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Ecclesiazusae” 1045]], -ισται [Refs [[prev. author] “Eq.” 54]]; also in passive sense, imperative -ίσθω[Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Phaedrus” 250c]]: pluperfect ἐκεχάριστο [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 8.5]], Epic dialect κεχάριστο [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 6.23]]:—say or do something agreeable to a person, show him favour or kindness, oblige, gratify, with dative person, frequently in participle, χαριζομένη πόσεϊ ᾧ [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 5.71, compare 11.23, 15.449, 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 8.538, 13.265; once in 8th-7th c.BC: Hesiodus Epicus, ποίησε.. χαριζόμενος Διί “Th.” 580; πᾶσι χαριζοίμην ἄν 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 6.130, compare 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 3.40; τοῖς θεοῖς 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Memorabilia” 4.3.16]]; Καλλίᾳ χαριζόμενος to oblige, humour him, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Protagoras” 362a, compare “Men.” 75b, 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Equites” 1368]]; of a judge, give a partial verdict, χ. οἷς ἂν δοκῇ αὐτῷ [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Apologia” 35c; also χ. τῷ ἵππῳ 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “de Equitandi ratione” 10.12]]: absolutely, make oneself agreeable, comply, opposed to ἀντία φάσθαι, once in [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus, “Pers.” 700 (Lyric poetry); οἱ ὑπὲρ καιρὸν χαριζόμενοι 5th-6th c.BC: Andocides Orator 4.7: with _accusative_ _cognate_, χάριτας χ. 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Fragmenta” 360.1, 5th-6th c.BC: Isocrates Orator 1.31, 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 18.239; χ. τι καὶ αὐτός 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 3.42]]; with participle added, χαρίζετο ἱερὰ ῥέζων [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 1.61, compare 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.90, 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Ecclesiazusae” 1045, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 338a, 426c, etc.: more frequently with _dative_ modi, μήτε τί μοι ψεύδεσσι χαρίζεο]] do not court favour by lies, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 14.387; χαριζόμενος φιλότητι 10.43, etc.; λόγῳ θωπεῦσαι καὶ ἔργῳ χ. 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Theaetetus” 173a codices]]; opposed to τὰ βέλτιστα λέγειν, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 9.2, compare 1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus 2.66a.]]

__2
gratify or indulge a humour or passion, once in [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus, θυμῷ χαρίζεσθαι κενά “El.” 331, compare 5th c.BC: Antipho Orator 4.3.2, 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 7.1.25; ὀργῇ 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Fragmenta” 31; γλώσσῃ [prev. author] “Or.” 1514 (troch.); ἔρωτι 5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “Fragmenta.” 127; τῇ ἐπιθυμίᾳ 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 561c: τῷ σώματι 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Memorabilia” 1.2.23]]; τῇ γαστρί[Refs [[prev. work] 2.1.2, “Cyr.” 4.2.39; τῇ ἡδονῇ [prev. work] 4.3.2.]]

__3
in erotic sense, grant favours to a man, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Ecclesiazusae” 629 (_anapaest meter_), 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Symposium” 182a, “Phdr.” 231c, 256a, 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Memorabilia” 3.11.12, etc.]]: hence of Comedy, ὀλίγοις χαρίσασθαι [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Equites” 517 (_anapaest meter_): with _accusative_ _cognate_, χ. θήλειαν ἀπόλαυσιν 2nd c.AD: Lucianus Sophista “Am.” 27.]]

__II
with accusative of things, give graciously or cheerfully, δῶρα [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 24.283; ἄποινα 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 6.49, 10.380; χαρίζεσθαί τινί τι 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.91, 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Acharnenses” 437, “Eq.” 54, 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 1.4.9, etc.; πωλεῖν καὶ χ. καὶ τέκνοις μεταδιδόναι “PGrenf.” 1.60.45 (6th c.AD)]]; so with accusative person, χαρίζομαί σε τοῖς ὄχλοις [Refs 1st c.AD+ [“PFlor.” 61.61 (1st c.AD)]]: with a strong oxymoron, ξείνια δυσμενέσιν λυγρὰ χ. [Refs 7th c.BC+ [7th c.BC: Archilochus Lyricus 7]]: with infinitive with Article, χ. τὸ ποθεῖν [LXX+1st c.AD+ [1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus 2.609a; τὸ ζῆν LXX.2Mac.3.33]]; without the Article, πολλοῖς ἐχαρίσατο βλέπειν (variant{τὸ β}.) [NT.Luke.7.21]; χάρισαι [αὐτοῖς] μένειν allow them to remain, [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd c.AD: Lucianus Sophista “Am.” 19, compare “Anthologia Graeca” 5.236 (6th c.AD: Agathias Historicus et Epigrammaticus)]]; so ἆρ᾽ ἄν τί μοι χαρίσαιο τοιόνδε—μή μου καταγελᾶ; [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Hp.Mi.” 364c.]]

__II.b
χ. τὴν δέησιν grant the request, [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd c.AD: Lucianus Sophista “Bis Acc.” 14.]]

__II.c
passive, with accusative, to be favoured with, ἀνάγκᾳ πνεῦμα χαριζόμενος [Refs [“epigram Gr.” 204.18 (from Cnidus).]]

__II.2
with genitive partitive, give freely of a thing, ἀλλοτρίων χ. [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 17.452]]; ταμίη.. χαριζομένη παρεόντων giving freely of such things as were ready, [Refs [1.140]], etc.; παντοίων ἀγαθῶν γαστρὶ χαριζόμενοι [Refs 6th c.BC+ [6th c.BC: Theognis Elegiacus 1000; γλώσσης μαφιδίοιο χ. παρεοῦσι 3rd c.BC: Theocritus Poeta Bucolicus 25.188]]; προικὸς χαρίζεσθαι, of his bounty, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 13.15.]]

__II.3
with accusative person, give up as a favour, τῇ μητρὶ χ. Ὀκτάβιον, by dropping a law aimed at him, [Refs 1st c.AD+ [1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus “C. Gracchus” 4]]; but also, by unjust condemnation, [NT.Act.25.11, 16]; also τῷ θεῷ με ἐχαρίσω, of a dedication ceremony, [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [“PBremen” 49.14 (2nd c.AD).]]

__II.4
forgive, τὴν ἀδικίαν τινί [NT.2Cor.12.13, cf. NT.Col.2.13: _absolutely_, NT.2Cor.2.7, etc.]

__III
passive, especially in perfect and pluperfect, κεχάριστο θυμῷ was dear to her heart, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 6.23]]; τοῖσι Εὐβοεῦσι ἐκεχάριστο the pleasure of the Euboeans was done, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 8.5]]; ταῦτα μὲν οὖν μνήμῃ κεχαρίσθω let a tribute be paid.. [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Phaedrus” 250c; compare χάρις 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus V.]]

__III.2
mostly participle perfect κεχαρισμένος, η, ον, as adjective, acceptable, welcome, ἐμῷ κεχαρισμένε θυμῷ [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 5.243, 826, etc.]]; κεχαρισμένα δῶρα θεοῖσι δίδωσι,[Refs 8th c.BC+ [20.298, compare 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 16.184, 19.397]]; κεχαρισμένα θεῖναί τινι to do things pleasing to one, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 24.661; ἀνὴρ κεχαρισμένα εἰδώς 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 8.584; θεοις κεχαρισμένα ποιεῖν 5th c.BC: Lysias Orator 6.33]]; κεχ. τοῖς θεοῖς λέγειν τε καὶ πράττειν, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Euthyphro” 14b, compare “Phdr.” 273e; δοίη ᾧ κ᾽ ἐθέλοι καί οἱ κεχαρισμένος ἔλθοι 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 2.54, compare 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.87, 3.119, 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Memorabilia” 1.2.10, etc.; κεχαρισμένα θύρσῳ 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Hercules Furens” 892 (Lyric poetry); κεχαρ. χοιρίδιον 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Pax” 386 (Lyric poetry); πᾶσιν κεχαρισμένος 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Sophista” 218a; λόγος κεχ. 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 14.1; σιτίον ἢ ποτόν 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Memorabilia” 2.1.24; ἐν τοῖς μὴ κεχαρισμένοις.. πρὸς τὴν αἴσθησιν 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “de Partibus Animalium” 645a7]]; compare κεχαρισμένως.

__III.3
later, comparative κεχαρισμενώτερος [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd-3rd c.AD: Aelianus “De Natura Animalium - Ar.Byzantine Epit.” 12.7]]; superlative -ώτατος[Refs 4th c.AD+ [4th c.AD: Alciphro Epistolographus 3.65.]] —Rare in Trag., but frequently in _Attic dialect_ Prose.

LSJ / STEPBible (TFLSJ)
Included with:  χάρις [ᾰ], ἡ,

__VI.2.b
πράσσειν τί τινι πρὸς χάριν [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Coloneus” 1776 (_anapaest meter_); δρᾶσαι 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Helena” 1281; τοῖσι πολλοῖς πρὸς χάριν λέγειν τι [prev. author] “Hec.” 257, compare 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Memorabilia” 4.4.4, “HG” 6.3.7, 5th-6th c.BC: Isocrates Orator 2.18, 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 8.1 (but πρὸς χ. βορᾶς]] for the sake of it, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Antigone” 30)]]; πρὸς χ., opposed to κλαίων, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. author] “OT” 1152:—but πρὸς χ. εὐσεβίας, just like{χάριν}, 5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “O.” 8.8; τίνος νόμου ταῦτα πρὸς χ. λέγ; 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Antigone” 908; πρὸς ἰσχύος χ. 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Medea” 538]]; πρὸς χ. alone, as a favour, freely, πρὸς χ. τε κοὐ βίᾳ [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Fragmenta” 28]]; but κορέσαι στόμα πρὸς χ. to their heart's content, [Refs [[prev. author] “Ph.” 1156 (Lyric poetry).]]

__VI.2.c
ἐν χάριτι κρίνειν τινά to decide from partiality to one, [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [3rd c.BC: Theocritus Poeta Bucolicus 5.69]]; but also, for one's gratification, pleasure, ἐν χάριτι διδόναι or ποιεῖν τινί τι, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Oeconomicus” 8.10, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Phaedo” 115b: παραλαμβάνειν ἐν χάρισιν]]gratefully, [Refs [[prev. author] “Lg.” 796b.]]

__VI.2.d
διὰ χαρίτων εἶναι or γίγνεσθαί [τινι] to be pleasing to one, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Hiero” 9.1, 2.]]

__VI.2.e
ἐθελοντὶ καὶ μετὰ χάριτος of pure good will, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [2nd c.BC: Polybius Historicus 2.22.5, etc.; ἐθελούσιοι καὶ χάριτος ἕνεκα ἐξιόντες 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 4.2.11.]]

__VII
metaphorically of the cypress, [Refs [Gp. 11.4.1]]; of some kind of myrtle, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [Scholia 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 17.51]]; of salt, ὅτι τὸ ἀναγκαῖον ἡδὺ ποιοῦσιν (i.e. ἅλες) [Refs 1st c.AD+ [1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus 2.685a.]]

__B
Χάρις, ἡ, as a mythological proper name declined like{χάρις}, save that the accusative is generally Χάριτα (except [Refs 8th c.BC+ [“Anthologia Graeca” 5.148 (1st c.BC: Meleager Epigrammaticus), 2nd c.AD: Lucianus Sophista “DDeor.” 15.1, 2nd c.AD: Pausanias Periegeta 9.35.4): poetry _dative_ _plural_ Χαρίτεσσι 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 17.51, 5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “N.” 9.54; Χάρισσιν [prev. work] 5.54]]:—Charis, wife of Hephaestus, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 18.382]]; mostly in plural Χάριτες, αἱ, the Graces, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [14.267, 275, 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 6.18, 5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “O.” 2.50, etc.]]; three in number, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th-7th c.BC: Hesiodus Epicus “Theogonia” 907, etc. (τέσσαρες αἱ 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus]], as a compliment, [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [3rd c.BC: Callimachus Epicus “Epigrammata” 52.1)]]; attendants of Aphrodite, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 5.338, 8th-7th c.BC: Hesiodus Epicus “Opera et Dies” 73, “hymnus ad Venerem” 61, 2nd c.AD: Pausanias Periegeta 6.24.7]]; coupled with Μοῦσαι, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th-7th c.BC: Hesiodus Epicus “Theogonia” 64]]; κόμαι Χαρίτεσσιν ὁμοῖαι, i.e. like that of the Graces, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 17.51]]; worshipped at Orchomenus in Boeotia, Ἐτεόκλειοι Χάριτες θεαί [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [3rd c.BC: Theocritus Poeta Bucolicus 16.104, cf. Scholia (at [prev. work]), 1st c.BC-1st c.AD: Strabo Geographus 9.2.40, 2nd c.AD: Pausanias Periegeta 9.35.3, 9.38.1]]: but at Lacedaemon and Athens only two were originally worshipped, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. author] 3.18.6, 9.35.2; Χαρίτων ἱερὸν ἐμποδὼν ποιοῦνται 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Ethica Nicomachea” 1133a3; θύειν ταῖς 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus 1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus 2.141f; in adjurations, πρὸς τῶν Χαρίτων 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Theaetetus” 152c; νὴ τὰς 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus 2nd c.AD: Lucianus Sophista “Hist.Conscr.” 26; ὦ φίλαι 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus 1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus 2.710d.— Rarely in _sing._, 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus ζωθάλμιος 5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “O.” 7.11; Χάριτος ἡδίστης θεῶν 4th c.BC: Antiphanes Comicus 228.4.]]

short_definition: grace — χάρις, -ιτος, ἡ Abbott-Smith does not include the article here., accusative, χάριν (χάριτα in Act.24:27, Ju 4; see WH, App., 157),
deep_entry:
Abbott-Smith / STEPBible (TBESG)
χάρις, -ιτος, ἡ Abbott-Smith does not include the article here., accusative, χάριν (χάριτα in Act.24:27, Ju 4; see WH, App., 157),
[in LXX chiefly for חֵן ;]
__1. objectively, that which causes favourable regard, gracefulness, grace, loveliness of form, graciousness of speech (cl.; Ecc.10:12, Sir.21:16, al.): Col.4:6; λόγοι τ. χάριτος (genitive qual.), Luk.4:22.
__2. Subjectively,
__(a) on the part of the giver, grace, graciousness, kindness, goodwill, favour: Luk.2:52, Act.7:10, al.; esp. in NT of the divine favour, grace, with emphasis on its freeness and universality: Luk.1:30, Act.14:26, Rom.1:7, 1Co.1:3, al.; opposite to ὀφείλημα, Rom.4:4, 16; to ἔργα, Rom.11:6;
__(b) on the part of the receiver, a sense of favour received, thanks, gratitude: Rom.6:17 7:25, al.; χ. ἔχειν, to be thankful, Luk.17:9, 1Ti.1:12, al.
__3. Objectively, of the effect of grace,
__(a) a state of grace: Rom.5:2, 2Ti.2:1, 1Pe.5:12, 2Pe.3:18;
__(b) a proof or gift of grace (cl., a favour): Jhn.1:16, Act.6:8, Rom.1:5, 1Co.3:10, 2Co.9:8, Gal.2:9, Eph.3:2, 1Pe.5:5, 10 al. (For fuller treatment of the NT usage, see AR, Eph., 221ff.; DB, ii, 254ff.; DCG, i, 686ff.; Cremer, see word).
(AS)
