LSJ / STEPBible (TFLSJ)
χάρις [ᾰ], ἡ,
genitive χάρῐτος: accusative χάριν [ῑ in arsi, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 5.874]]], etc.; also χάριτα [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 6.41, 9.107, 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Electra” 61, “Hel.” 1378, 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Historia Graeca (Hellenica)” 3.5.16, 3rd c.BC: Phylarchus Historicus 24 1st c.AD: Josephus Historicus, “PGen.” 47.17 (4th c.AD), etc. (un-Attic, _accusative_ to Moer.p.414P.): χάριταν “Corpus Glossariorum Latinorum”: _plural_ χάριτες]]; dative χάρισι, χαρίτεσσι, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 6.237, 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 17.51, 5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “O.” 7.93]]: (χαίρω):—grace:

__I
in objective sense, outward grace or fauour, beauty, properly of persons or their portraits, θεσπεσίην δ᾽ ἄρα τῷ γε χάριν κατεχεύατ᾽ Ἀθήνη [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 2.12, etc.; χάριν ἀμφιχέαι κεφαλῇ 8th-7th c.BC: Hesiodus Epicus “Opera et Dies” 65; εὐμόρφων δὲ κολοσσῶν ἔχθεται χ. ἀνδρί 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Agamemnon” 417 (Lyric poetry)]]: plural, graces, κάλλεϊ καὶ χάρισι στίλβων [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 6.237; ὄσσοις χάριτας Ἀφροδίτης ἔχων 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Bacchae” 236; μετὰ χαρίτων]]gracefully, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 2.41: less frequently of things, χ. δ᾽ ἀπελάμπετο πολλή,]] of ear-rings, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 14.183]]; of works, ἔργοισι χάριν καὶ κῦδος ὀπάζει [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 15.320]]; of words, οὔ οἱ χ. ἀμφιπεριστέφεται ἐπέεσσιν [Refs [8.175]]; πλείστη δὲ χ. κατὰ μέτρον ἰούσης [γλώσσης] [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th-7th c.BC: Hesiodus Epicus “Opera et Dies” 720; ταὶ Διωνύσου σὺν βοηλάτα χάριτες διθυράμβῳ 5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “O.” 13.19; ἡ τῶν λόγων χ. 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 4.38, compare 1st c.BC: Dionysius Halicarnassensis “de Compositione Verborum” 23; μῦθοι πληθόμενοι χαρίτων “Anthologia Graeca” 9.186 (1st c.BC: Antipater Thessalonicensis Epigrammaticus).]]

__I.2
glory, Φερενίκου χ. [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “O.” 1.18, compare 8.57, 80.]]

__II
in subjective sense, grace or favour felt, whether on the part of the doer or the receiver (both senses appear in such phrases as ὅτ᾽.. ἡ χάρις χάριν φέροι [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Coloneus” 779; χάρις χάριν γάρ ἐστιν ἡ τίκτουσ᾽ ἀεί [prev. author] “Aj.” 522, compare 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Helena” 1234, 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Rhetorica” 1385a16):]]

__II.1
on the part of the doer, grace, kindness, goodwill, τινος for or towards one, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th-7th c.BC: Hesiodus Epicus “Opera et Dies” 190; τῶν Μεσσηνίων χάριτι πεισθείς 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 3.95]]; οὐ χάριτι τῇ ἐμῇ not for any kind feeling towards me, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Antipho Orator 5.41: _absolutely_, εἰ δέ τις μείζων χ. 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Supplices” 960; τῆς παλαιᾶς χ. ἐκβεβλημένη 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Ajax” 808]]; ἦ μεγάλα χ. δώρῳ σύν ὀλίγῳ [LXX+3rd c.BC+ [3rd c.BC: Theocritus Poeta Bucolicus 28.24; χ. εὑρεῖν ἐναντίον τοῦ θεοῦ LXX.Gen.6.8, +others; χάριν ἔχειν πρὸς τὸν δῆμον 1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus “Demosthenes” 7]]; partiality, favour, μήτε ἔλεον μήτε συγγνώμην μήτε χ. μηδεμίαν περὶ πλείονος ποιήσασθαι τῶν νόμων [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Lysias Orator 14.40; οὐ συμφωνοῦσιν ὀργαὶ καὶ χάριτες μακαριότητι 4th-3rd c.BC: Epicurus Philosophus “Ep.” i p.28 U., compare 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Leges” 740c.]]

__II.2
more frequently on the part of the receiver, sense of favour received, thankfulness, gratitude, χάριν καὶ κῦδος ἄροιο [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 4.95; ἀρέομαι πὰρ Σαλαμῖνος Ἀθαναίων χ. 5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “P.” 1.76]]; τινος for a thing, οὐδέ τίς ἐστι χάρις μετόπισθ᾽ εὐεργέων [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 4.695, compare 22.319; ἀντὶ πόνων χ. 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 4.86: less frequently with]]infinitive, οὐκ ἄρα τις χάρις ἦεν μάρνασθαι one has, it seems, no thanks for fighting, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 9.316, 17.147; οἵ οἱ ἀπεμνήσαντο χ. εὐεργεσιάων 8th-7th c.BC: Hesiodus Epicus “Theogonia” 503, compare 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 1.137; χάριν φέρειν τινί 5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “O.” 10(11).17; χ. τροφεῦσιν ἀμείβων 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Agamemnon” 728 (Lyric poetry); φιλότητος ἀμειβόμεναι χ. 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Electra” 134 (Lyric poetry)]]; χάριν εἰδέναι τινί to acknowledge a sense of favour, feel grateful, once in [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Homerus Epicus, ἐγὼ δέ κέ τοι ἰδέω χ. ἤματα πάντα 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 14.235; frequently in Prose, 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 3.21, 5th c.BC: Lysias Orator 2.23, 5th-6th c.BC: Isocrates Orator 4.175, etc.]]; τούτων for a thing, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 1.6.11, etc.; τοῖς διαπεπραγμένοις 1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus “Alexander” 62; μοι χ. οἶδεν ἐπὶ τούτοις 2nd c.AD: Lucianus Sophista “Bis Acc.” 17; χ. προσειδέναι 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Apologia” 20a; ἀποδιδόναι [prev. author] “R.” 338a; τινὰ ἀποστερῆσαι χάριτος [prev. author] “Hp.Mi.” 372c; later χ. γνῶναι 2nd-3rd c.AD: Philostratus Sophista “Vita Apollonii” 2.17; πολλὴν γνοῦσα χ. 2nd c.AD(?): Xenophon Ephesius Scriptor Eroticus 3.5; χ. ἐπίσταμαι πᾶσι 2nd c.AD(?): Charito Scriptor Eroticus 3.4, compare 8.5, 2nd c.AD(?): Pollianus Epigrammaticus 5.142, 4th c.AD: Julianus Imperator “Orationes” 8.246c; also τῶν παροιχομένων ἔχειν σφι μεγάλην χ. 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 7.120, compare 1.71, 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Heraclidae” 767 (Lyric poetry), “IT” 847 (Lyric poetry), 5th c.BC: Lysias Orator 16.1, 4th c.BC: Hyperides Orator “adv. Athenogenem” 5]]: with participle, χ. ἔχειν σωθέντες [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 2.5.14]]; also χάριτας ἔχων πατρός owing him a debt of gratitude, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Orestes” 244: but ἀσπασμάτων χάριν τίν᾽ ἕξει]]; what thanks will she have for.. ? [Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. author] “Hec.” 830; χ. ἂν ἐν τούτῳ μείζω ἔτι ἔσχεν 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 8.87]]; χ. ὀφείλειν to owe gratitude, be beholden, τοῖς θεοῖς [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Antigone” 331, compare 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 3.2.30; προσοφείλειν 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 3.31; χ. οὐδεμία ἐφαίνετο πρὸς Ἀθηναίων 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 5.90]]; χάριν ἀθάνατον καταθέσθαι to lay up a store of undying gratitude, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. author] 7.178, compare 6.41; τῇ πόλει χ. καταθέσθαι 5th c.BC: Antipho Orator 5.61, compare 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 1.33]]; χάριν λαβεῖν τινος receive thanks from one, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Tyrannus” 1004, etc.; ἀπολαβεῖν παρά τινων 5th c.BC: Lysias Orator 20.31]]; τινος for a thing, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Memorabilia” 2.2.5, 4th c.BC: Aeschines Orator 2.4; διπλῆν ἐξ ἐμοῦ κτήσει χάριν 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Philoctetes” 1370; κἀπ᾽ ἐμοῦ κτήσει χ. [prev. author] “Tr.” 471; κομίσασθαι χ. 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 3.58; χάριτος τυχεῖν 4th c.BC: Lycurgus Orator 135; ἀπέχειν χάριτας 3rd c.BC: Callimachus Epicus “Epigrammata” 51.4, etc.]]; τοῖς θεοῖς χάρις (i.e. ἐστί) ὅτι.., thank the gods that.., [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 3.3.14, “Cyr.” 7.5.72; χ. τινί τινος 2nd c.AD: Lucianus Sophista “Tim.” 36; τινὶ ὑπέρ τινος 1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus 2.1122a.]]

__II.3
favour, influence, opposed to force, χάριτι τὸ πλέον ἢ φόβῳ [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 1.9]]; χ. καὶ δεήσει, opposed to ἀπειλῇ, [Refs 1st c.AD+ [1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus “Sulla” 38.]]

__II.4
love-charm, philtre, [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd c.AD: Lucianus Sophista “Alex.” 5, “Merc.Cond.” 40.]]

__III
in concrete sense, a favour done or returned, boon, χάριν φέρειν τινί confer a favour on one, do a thing to oblige him, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 5.211, 874, 9.613, 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 5.307, 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Iphigenia Taurica” 14, “Or.” 239, 5th-6th c.BC: Andocides Orator 2.24]] (so in middle, of the recipient,[Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. work] 9); ἄλλοις χ. φέροντες 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 3.54]]; χάριν θέσθαι or τίθεσθαί τινι, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 9.60, 107, 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Prometheus Vinctus” 782, 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Hecuba” 1211, etc.; προσθέσθαι 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Coloneus” 767; χ. ὑπουργῆσαί τινι 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Prometheus Vinctus” 635; παρασχεῖν 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Coloneus” 1183; πράσσειν 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Ion” 36, 896 (Lyric poetry); δράσας 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 2.40]]; ἀνύσαι probably in [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Trachiniae” 995 (_anapaest meter_); νέμειν [prev. author] “Aj.” 1371; χ. δοῦναί τινι 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Prometheus Vinctus” 821, 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Coloneus” 1489 (but χ. δοῦναι, ={χαρίζεσθαι} (1.2)]], indulge, humour, ὀργῇ[Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. work] 855; γαστρί 5th c.BC: Cratinus Comicus 317); χ. χαρίζεσθαι, see at {χαρίζομαι} I.1: χ. ἀνθυπουργεῖν]] return a favour, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Fragmenta” 339; τίνειν 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Prometheus Vinctus” 985, “Ag.” 821; χάριτας πατρῴας ἐκτίνων 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Orestes” 453, compare 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Menexenus” 242c, etc.; χ. ἀποδιδόναι τινί 5th c.BC: Lysias Orator 12.60, 28.17; ἀντί τινος 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Agesilaus” 2.29; ὑπέρ τινος 5th-6th c.BC: Isocrates Orator 4.56; τῶν ἔργων τὰς χάριτας ἀποδ. τινί 5th c.BC: Lysias Orator 31.24; χάριτας ἀντιδιδόναι 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 3.63]]; opposed to χάριν ἀπαιτεῖν to ask the repayment of a boon, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Hecuba” 276, compare 5th c.BC: Lysias Orator 18.23, 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 20.156; χάριτας ἀπ. 4th c.BC: Lycurgus Orator 139; χάριν ἐξαιτεῖσθαι 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Coloneus” 586]]; χ. ἀποστερεῖν withhold a return for what one has received, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Gorgias” 520c]]; τὰς αὑτοῦ εἰς τοὺς φίλους χ. the favours one has done them, [Refs [[prev. author] “Lg.” 729d]]; χ. ἄχαρις α thankless favour, one which receives, or deserves, no thanks, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Prometheus Vinctus” 545 (Lyric poetry); χ. ἀχάριτος [prev. author] “Ch.” 42 (Lyric poetry), 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Phoenissae” 1757 (Lyric poetry).]]

__III.b
grant made in legal form, [Refs 1st c.AD+ [“POxy.” 273.14 (1st c.AD), “PGrenf.” 2.70.5 (3rd c.AD), etc.]]; αἱ τῶν Σεβαστῶν χ. imperial grants, [Refs 1st c.AD+ [“OGI” 669.44 (Egypt, 1st c.AD).]]

__III.2
especially in erotic sense, of favours granted (see. χαρίζομαι 1.3), ἀλόχου χάριν ἰδεῖν [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 11.243, compare 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Agamemnon” 1206: more frequently in _plural_, 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Hiero” 1.34, 7.6, etc.]]; βίᾳ δ᾽ ἔπραξας χάριτας ἢ πείσας κόρη; [Refs 5th c.BC+ [“Tragica Adespota” 402; in full, χάριτες ἀφροδισίων ἐρώτων 5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “Fragmenta.” 128, compare 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Phaedrus” 254a, +others]]

__IV
gratification, delight, τινος in or from a thing, συμποσίου [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “O.” 7.5; νίκας [prev. author] “O.” 10(11).78; ὕπνου χ. 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Orestes” 159 (Lyric poetry); even χ. γόων [prev. author] “Supp.” 79 (Lyric poetry)]]; also concrete, of things, a delight, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “I.” 2.19 (_plural_); τὰν βοτρυώδη Διονύσου χ. οἴνας 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Bacchae” 535 (Lyric poetry), compare 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Nubes” 311 (Lyric poetry), 4th c.AD: Julianus Imperator “Orationes” 3.125b; ἔνοπτρα, παρθένων χάριτας 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Troades” 1108 (Lyric poetry): _absolutely_, Ἔρως.. εἰσάγων γλυκεῖαν χ. [prev. author] “Hipp.” 527 (Lyric poetry)]]; opposed to λύπη, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Electra” 821, 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Helena” 655 (Lyric poetry)]]; opposed to πόνος, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Coloneus” 232 (Lyric poetry); θανεῖν πολλὴ χάρις 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Agamemnon” 550, compare 1304; βίου χ. μεθεῖσα 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Medea” 227; οὐδεμίαν ἔχω τῷ βίῳ χάριν 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Lysistrata” 865; τοῖς δὲ σιτίοις χ. οὐδεμίαν οἶδ᾽ ἐσθίων [prev. work] 869]]; less frequently in Prose, χ. καὶ ἡδονή [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Gorgias” 462c, compare 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 20.26; τοσαύτην ἔχει χ. 5th-6th c.BC: Isocrates Orator 9.10.]]

__V
δαιμόνων χάρις homage due to them, their worship, majesty, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Agamemnon” 182 (Lyric poetry); ἀθίκτων χ. [prev. work] 371 (Lyric poetry)]]; ὅρκων [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Medea” 439 (Lyric poetry).]]

__V.2
thank-offering, εὐκταία χ. τινός, opposed to a common gift, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Agamemnon” 1387, compare 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Hiero” 8.4; ἔπεμψε χαίτην κουρίμην χ. πατρός 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Choephori” 180, compare 517; τιμὴ καὶ γέρα καὶ χ. 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Euthyphro” 15a, compare “La.” 187a.]]

__VI
Special usages:

__VI.1
accusative singular as adverb, χ. τινός in any one's favour, for his pleasure, for his sake, χ. Ἕκτορος [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 15.744]]; ψεύδεσθαι γλώσσης χ. for one's tongue's pleasure, i.e. for talking's sake, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th-7th c.BC: Hesiodus Epicus “Opera et Dies” 709, compare 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Choephori” 266]]; rarely with Article, τὴν Ἀθηναίων χάριν ἐστρατεύοντο [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 5.99.]]

__VI.1.b
as preposition, sometimes before its case (once in [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus, “P.” 2.70; χάριν πλησμονῆς 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Phaedrus” 241c; χ. φιλίας 4th-3rd c.BC: Epicurus Philosophus “Gnomologium Vaticanum - Kleine Schriften” 28]]; χ. τίνο; [LXX+1st c.BC+ [LXX.2Ch.7.21, compare “POxy.” 743.29 (1st c.BC), etc.)]], but mostly after, for the sake of, on behalf of, on account of, κακά νιν ἕλοιτο μοῖρα δυσπότμου χάριν χλιδᾶς [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Tyrannus” 888 (Lyric poetry)]]; τοῦ χάρι; for what reason? [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Plutus” 53; συγχωρῶ τοῦ λόγου χ. 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 475a]]; so ἐμὴν χάριν, χάριν σήν, for my, thy pleasure or sake, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Persae” 1046 (Lyric poetry), 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Hercules Furens” 1238, etc.; κείνου τε καὶ σὴν ἐξ ἴσου κοινὴν χ. 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Trachiniae” 485]]: less frequently with the Article, τὴν σὴν δ᾽ ἥκω χ. [Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. author] “Ph.” 1413 (_anapaest meter_); σοῦ τε τήν τ᾽ ἐμὴν χ. 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Phoenissae” 762:—pleonastic, τίνος χάριν ἕνεκ; 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Leges” 701d]]; also χάριν τινός as far as regards.., as to.., ἔπους σμικροῦ χ. [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Coloneus” 443]]; δακρύων χάριν if tears would serve, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [[prev. author] “fragment” 557.6; χ. θανάτου πόλιν ἀτείχιστον οἰκοῦμεν 4th-3rd c.BC: Epicurus Philosophus “Gnomologium Vaticanum - Kleine Schriften” 31]]; also, about, ἔπεμφεν ἐπὶ τὴν πενθεράν σου χ. τοῦ κτήματος about the farm, [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [“PFay.” 126.5 (2nd-3rd c.AD).]]—Orig. an accusative in apposition with the sentence, as in [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 15.744, etc.]], being a favour, since it is (was) a favour, as is evident in κακῆς γυναικὸς χάριν ἄχαριν ἀπώλετο [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Iphigenia Taurica” 566; τινὸς νίκας ἀκάρπωτον χ. 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Ajax” 176 (Lyric poetry).]]

__VI.2
with Preps.:

__VI.2.a
εἰς χάριν to do a pleasure, οὐδὲν ἐς χ. πράσσων [Refs 1st c.AD+ [[prev. author] “OT” 1353 (Lyric poetry); ἐς χ. τίθεσθαί τι 1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus “Marius” 46; μηδὲ κρίσιν εἰς χ. ἕλκε 1st c.AD(?): Pseudo-Phocylidea 9 (but ἐς τὴν τῶν ξυμμάχων χ.]] in such a way as to earn thanks.. [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 3.37); also κατὰ χάριν 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Leges” 740c; χάριτος ἕνεκα [prev. work] 771d.]]

__VI.2.b
πράσσειν τί τινι πρὸς χάριν [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Coloneus” 1776 (_anapaest meter_); δρᾶσαι 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Helena” 1281; τοῖσι πολλοῖς πρὸς χάριν λέγειν τι [prev. author] “Hec.” 257, compare 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Memorabilia” 4.4.4, “HG” 6.3.7, 5th-6th c.BC: Isocrates Orator 2.18, 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 8.1 (but πρὸς χ. βορᾶς]] for the sake of it, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Antigone” 30)]]; πρὸς χ., opposed to κλαίων, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. author] “OT” 1152:—but πρὸς χ. εὐσεβίας, just like{χάριν}, 5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “O.” 8.8; τίνος νόμου ταῦτα πρὸς χ. λέγ; 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Antigone” 908; πρὸς ἰσχύος χ. 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Medea” 538]]; πρὸς χ. alone, as a favour, freely, πρὸς χ. τε κοὐ βίᾳ [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Fragmenta” 28]]; but κορέσαι στόμα πρὸς χ. to their heart's content, [Refs [[prev. author] “Ph.” 1156 (Lyric poetry).]]

__VI.2.c
ἐν χάριτι κρίνειν τινά to decide from partiality to one, [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [3rd c.BC: Theocritus Poeta Bucolicus 5.69]]; but also, for one's gratification, pleasure, ἐν χάριτι διδόναι or ποιεῖν τινί τι, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Oeconomicus” 8.10, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Phaedo” 115b: παραλαμβάνειν ἐν χάρισιν]]gratefully, [Refs [[prev. author] “Lg.” 796b.]]

__VI.2.d
διὰ χαρίτων εἶναι or γίγνεσθαί [τινι] to be pleasing to one, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Hiero” 9.1, 2.]]

__VI.2.e
ἐθελοντὶ καὶ μετὰ χάριτος of pure good will, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [2nd c.BC: Polybius Historicus 2.22.5, etc.; ἐθελούσιοι καὶ χάριτος ἕνεκα ἐξιόντες 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 4.2.11.]]

__VII
metaphorically of the cypress, [Refs [Gp. 11.4.1]]; of some kind of myrtle, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [Scholia 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 17.51]]; of salt, ὅτι τὸ ἀναγκαῖον ἡδὺ ποιοῦσιν (i.e. ἅλες) [Refs 1st c.AD+ [1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus 2.685a.]]

__B
Χάρις, ἡ, as a mythological proper name declined like{χάρις}, save that the accusative is generally Χάριτα (except [Refs 8th c.BC+ [“Anthologia Graeca” 5.148 (1st c.BC: Meleager Epigrammaticus), 2nd c.AD: Lucianus Sophista “DDeor.” 15.1, 2nd c.AD: Pausanias Periegeta 9.35.4): poetry _dative_ _plural_ Χαρίτεσσι 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 17.51, 5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “N.” 9.54; Χάρισσιν [prev. work] 5.54]]:—Charis, wife of Hephaestus, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 18.382]]; mostly in plural Χάριτες, αἱ, the Graces, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [14.267, 275, 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 6.18, 5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “O.” 2.50, etc.]]; three in number, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th-7th c.BC: Hesiodus Epicus “Theogonia” 907, etc. (τέσσαρες αἱ 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus]], as a compliment, [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [3rd c.BC: Callimachus Epicus “Epigrammata” 52.1)]]; attendants of Aphrodite, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 5.338, 8th-7th c.BC: Hesiodus Epicus “Opera et Dies” 73, “hymnus ad Venerem” 61, 2nd c.AD: Pausanias Periegeta 6.24.7]]; coupled with Μοῦσαι, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th-7th c.BC: Hesiodus Epicus “Theogonia” 64]]; κόμαι Χαρίτεσσιν ὁμοῖαι, i.e. like that of the Graces, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 17.51]]; worshipped at Orchomenus in Boeotia, Ἐτεόκλειοι Χάριτες θεαί [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [3rd c.BC: Theocritus Poeta Bucolicus 16.104, cf. Scholia (at [prev. work]), 1st c.BC-1st c.AD: Strabo Geographus 9.2.40, 2nd c.AD: Pausanias Periegeta 9.35.3, 9.38.1]]: but at Lacedaemon and Athens only two were originally worshipped, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. author] 3.18.6, 9.35.2; Χαρίτων ἱερὸν ἐμποδὼν ποιοῦνται 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Ethica Nicomachea” 1133a3; θύειν ταῖς 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus 1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus 2.141f; in adjurations, πρὸς τῶν Χαρίτων 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Theaetetus” 152c; νὴ τὰς 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus 2nd c.AD: Lucianus Sophista “Hist.Conscr.” 26; ὦ φίλαι 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus 1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus 2.710d.— Rarely in _sing._, 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus ζωθάλμιος 5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “O.” 7.11; Χάριτος ἡδίστης θεῶν 4th c.BC: Antiphanes Comicus 228.4.]]

χειμάζω
(χεῖμα, winter cold) [in LXX: Pro.26:10 (†) * ;]

LSJ / STEPBible (TFLSJ)
χειμ-άζω
(future -άσω[Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-3rd c.BC: Theophrastus Philosophus “de Signis Tempestatum” 38)]]:—transitive, expose to the winter cold: found only in passive, to be exposed thereto, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Hippocrates Medicus “περὶ διαίτης” 3.68]]; pass the winter, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Fragmenta” 503; ὅπως χειμασθῇ καὶ ἡλιωθῇ ἡ γῆ 4th-3rd c.BC: Theophrastus Philosophus “de Causis Plantarum” 3.20.7]]; of trees, live through the winter, χειμασθέντα [δένδρα] [Refs [[prev. author] “HP” 4.14.1; χειμασθῆναι χειμῶσι ὡραίοις καὶ καλοῖς [prev. author] “CP” 2.1.2.]]

__2
intransitive, pass the winter, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Aves” 1097 (Lyric poetry), 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Oeconomicus” 5.9, 5th-6th c.BC: Isocrates Orator 7.54, etc.]]: of armies, go into winter quarters, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 8.133, 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Historia Graeca (Hellenica)” 1.2.15, 3.2.1, 2nd c.BC: Polybius Historicus 27.18.1, etc.]]

__II
raise a storm or tempest, θεοῦ τοιαῦτα χειμάζοντος [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Coloneus” 1504; ὅταν χειμάζῃ ὁ θεὸς ἐν τῇ θαλάττῃ 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Oeconomicus” 8.16, compare “IG” 7.4255.5 (Orop.); χειμάσει [ἡ νεφέλη] ἐφ᾽ ἡμᾶς 1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus 2.195d]]: impersonal, ἐχείμαζε ἡμέρας τρεῖς the storm continued, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 7.191]]; χειμάσει there will be stormy weather, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-3rd c.BC: Theophrastus Philosophus “Sign.” [prev. cited]]]

__III
with accusative, drive forth or away, of a storm, ἔξω χ. [τοὺς μύας] [Refs [[prev. author] “fragment” 174.7]]:—passive, to be driven by a storm, overtaken by it, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 2.25, 3.69, +others; χειμασθεὶς ἀνέμῳ [prev. author] 8.99; ἐν θαλάττῃ χειμαζομένου πλοίου 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Ion” 540b, etc.]]

__III.2
metaphorically, toss like a storm, distress, τόδ᾽ αἷμα χ. πόλιν [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Tyrannus” 101; τὴν σάρκα τὸ παρὸν μόνον χειμάζειν 4th-3rd c.BC: Epicurus Philosophus “Fragmenta” 452]]: also, annoy, vex, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Ichn.” 331, 4th-3rd c.BC: Menander Comicus 208, 1st c.BC: Philodemus Philosophus “περὶ παρρησίας” p.61 O., “POsl.” 48.8 (1st c.AD)]]; σφὴξ τοῖς κέντροις πλήσσων ἐχείμαζε [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-4th c.BC: Aesopus Fabularum Scriptor 393]]:—passive, to be tempest-tossed, distressed, especially of the state considered as a ship, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Supplices” 269, 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Ranae” 361; δόμων ὄλβος χειμάζεται 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Ion” 966]]; also of single persons, κατὰ θάλασσαν χειμασθεῖσαι (as example of a ψυχικὸν πάθος) [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd c.AD: Soranus Medicus 3.84]]; suffer grievously, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Prometheus Vinctus” 563 (_anapaest meter_), 838, 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Philoctetes” 1460 (_anapaest meter_), 5th c.BC: Gorgias Rhetor et Sophista “Pal.” 11, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Politicus” 273d; ἰσχὺς ἐν νόσῳ χειμάζεται 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Ichn.” 267; ταῖς σαῖς ἀπειλαῖς αἷς ἐχειμάσθην [prev. author] “Ant.” 391; ἄλλῃ δ᾽ ἐν τύχῃ χ. 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Hippolytus” 315; χειμαζόμεθα.. ὑπ᾽ ἀπορίας ἐν τοῖς νῦν λόγοις 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Philebus” 29b, compare “La.” 194c; ὑπό τινων “PSI” 4.349.4 (3rd c.BC)]]; ἐν στρατείαις ἢ νόσοις ἢ ἐν θαλάττῃ χ. [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Theaetetus” 170a]]; of feverish patients, χειμάζονται μάλιστα πεμπταῖοι [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Hippocrates Medicus “προγνωστικόν” 24.]]

joined with ποταμός, ὅν τε [the stone] ποταμὸς χειμάρροος ὤσῃ [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 13.138; ὡς δ᾽ ὁπότε πλήθων ποταμὸς πεδίονδε κάτεισιν χειμάρρους κατ᾽ ὄρεσφιν 11.493]]: frequently in contracted forms, ποταμῷ πλήθοντι ἐοικὼς χειμάρρῳ [Refs 6th c.BC+ [5.88; ὡς δ᾽ ὅτε χείμαρροι ποταμοὶ κατ᾽ ὄρεσφι ῥέοντες 4.452; χειμάρρῳ ποταμῷ ἴκελος 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 3.81, compare 6th c.BC: Theognis Elegiacus 348; παρὰ ῥείθροισι χειμάρροις 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Antigone” 712; φάραγγες ὕδατι χειμάρρῳ ῥέουσαι 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Troades” 449 (troch.); διὰ χειμάρρου νάπης [prev. author] “Ba.” 1093; χαράδρα χ. 2nd c.BC: Polybius Historicus 10.30.2.]]

__II
Special usages:

__II.1

[Refs 8th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Cyclops” 681; ἐπὶ δεξιὰ χειρός 5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “P.” 6.19; ἐπ᾽ ἀριστερὰ χειρός 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 5.277; χειρὸς εἰς τὰ δεξιά 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Fragmenta” 598; λαιᾶς χειρός 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Prometheus Vinctus” 714 (but χείρ is often omitted with δεξιά, ἀριστερά,]] as we say the right, the left).

__II.2
frequently in dative of all numbers with Verbs which imply the use of hands, λάβε χειρί, χερσὶν ἑλέσθαι, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 5.302, 10.501; χερσὶν ἀσπάζεσθαι 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 3.35; προκαλίζεσθαι 18.20]]; χειρί, χεροῖν ψαῦσαι, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Tyrannus” 1510, 1466]]: sometimes this dative is added pleonastic by way of emphasis, ὄνυξι συλλαβὼν χερί [Refs [[prev. author] “Aj.” 310.]]

__II.3
genitive, by the hand, χειρὸς ἔχειν τινά [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 4.154; χειρὸς ἑλών 1.323, etc.]]; γέροντα δὲ χειρὸς ἀνίστη he raised him by the hand,[Refs 8th c.BC+ [24.515, compare 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 14.319; χερὶ χειρὸς ἑλών 5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “P.” 9.122; τινὰ χειρός ἑλκειν [prev. author] “N.” 11.32; ἀνέλκειν τινὰ τῆς χ. 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Vespae” 569 (_anapaest meter_).]]

__II.4

ἐν χειρί τινος by the hand of.., [LXX+NT [LXX.Josh.21.2, +others; ἐν χ. ἀγγέλου NT.Act.7.35 (variant).]]

__II.6.g
ἐπὶ χειρὸς ἔχειν on or in one's hand, [Refs 6th c.BC+ [6th c.BC: Theognis Elegiacus 490]]; ἐπὶ χεῖράς τινων ἐκφέρουσι put into their hands, [Refs 1st c.AD+ [1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus 2.815b]]; also ἐπὶ χεῖρά τινος next to, [LXX.Neh.3.4.]

__II.6.h
κατὰ χειρός, of washing the hands before meals, ὕδωρ κατὰ χειρός (i.e. φερέτω τις), [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Vespae” 1216, compare “Av.” 464 (_anapaest meter_), “fragment” 502 (Lyric poetry), 3rd c.BC: Philoxenus Epigrammaticus 1, 2nd c.AD: Athenaeus Epigrammaticus 9.408e]]; (without ὕδωρ) κατὰ χ. ἐδόθη [Refs 4th c.BC+ [2nd c.AD: Alexander Rhetor 261.2, compare 4th-3rd c.BC: Archedicus Comicus 2.3]]: proverbial of that which is easily come by, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Teleclides Comicus 1.2 (_anapaest meter_); πάντα μοι κατὰ χ. ἦν τὰ πράγματα]]at hand, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Pherecrates Comicus 146.5]]; also κατὰ χειρῶν δοῦναι, χέειν, λαβεῖν, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Philyllius Comicus 3, 4th c.BC: Antiphanes Comicus 287 (variant), 4th-3rd c.BC: Menander Comicus 470 (troch.), cf. Phot. see at {κατὰ χειρὸς ὕδωρ}: κατὰ χεῖρα]] in deed or act, κατὰ χ. γενναιότατοι [Refs 1st c.BC+ [1st c.BC: Dionysius Halicarnassensis 7.6]]; opposed to συνέσει, [Refs 1st c.AD+ [1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus “Philopoemen” 7]]; κατὰ χεῖρά σου according to thy will, [LXX.Sir.25.26: but κατὰ χεῖρας [τῆς σοφίας]] by her side, [Refs [[prev. work] 14.25.]]

__i
μετὰ χερσὶν ἔχειν between, i.e. in, the hands, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 11.4, 15.717; [ἄλεισον] μετὰ χ. ἐνώμα 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 22.10: μετὰ χεῖρας ἔχειν]] to have in hand, be engaged in, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 7.16.β, 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 1.138.]]

__k
λάβε παρὰ χεῖρα take in hand, [LXX.Tob.11.4]; but τὸ πὰρ χειρός the work in hand, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Bacchylides Lyricus 13.10.]]

__l
πρὸ χειρῶν close before one, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Antigone” 1279, 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Troades” 1207 (assuming variant), “Rh.” 274]]; πρὸ χειρὸς εἶναι conjecture in [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Comicus 69.5.]]

__m
πρὸς χειρός τινος by his hand, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Supplices” 66 (Lyric poetry), etc.]]; πρὸς ἐμὴν χεῖρα at the signs given by my hand, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Philoctetes” 148 (_anapaest meter_)]]; πρὸς χεῖρα ὑποβορβορύζοντες on pressure, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Hippocrates Medicus “ἐπιδημίαι” 4.7.]]

__n
ὑπὸ χερσὶ ἁλοῦσα under, i.e. by, another's hands, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 2.374, etc.]]; ὑπὸ χεῖρα ποιεῖσθαι to bring under one's power, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Agesilaus” 1.22]]; οἱ ὑπὸ χ. persons in one's power, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 6.34]]; ὑπὸ τὴν χ. ἐλθεῖν to come into one's hand, [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd c.AD: Lucianus Sophista “Herm.” 57, etc.]]; ὑπὸ χ. in hand, i.e. in stock, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Meteorologica” 369b33]]; but also, at hand, i.e. at once, [Refs 1st c.AD+ [1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus 2.548e]]; τὰ ὑπὸ χ. [Refs 1st c.AD+ [[prev. work]56b, 1st c.AD: Dioscorides (Dioscurides) Medicus 1.35]]; ὁ ὑπὸ χ. the attendant, [Refs 1st c.AD+ [1st c.AD: Dioscorides (Dioscurides) Medicus 5.75; παρέργως καὶ ὑπὸ χ.]]extempore, [Refs 1st c.AD+ [1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus “Aratus” 3, etc.]]; also καθύπο χεῖρα κινῶν [τὰς οὐσίας], in Alchemy, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [2nd c.AD: Pseudo-Democritus Alchemista p.51 5th c.BC: Bacchylides Lyricus]]

__III
the hand often receives the attributes of the person using it, χ. μεγάλη, of Zeus, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 15.695 (χ. παγκρατής, of God, 2nd c.AD: Secundus Gnomologus “Sententiae - FPG” 3]]; χ. ὑπερμήκης, of the 'long arm' of the king, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 8.140.β᾽)]]; θοὴ χ., of one throwing, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 12.306; ἀφνειά 5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “O.” 7.1, compare 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Electra” 458]]; εὐσεβεστέρα, εὐφιλής, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Choephori” 141, “Ag.” 34]]; κάρβανος[Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. work] 1061; γεραιά 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Hecuba” 143 (_anapaest meter_); πονηρά [prev. author] “Ion” 1316, etc.]]: to denote wealth or poverty, πλειοτέρῃ σὺν χ. [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 11.359; κενεὰς σὺν χ. ἔχοντες 10.42, compare 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Helena” 1280, etc.]]

__III.2
it is represented as acting of itself, χεῖρες μαιμῶσιν [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 13.77, compare 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Ajax” 50; χεὶρ ὁρᾷ τὸ δράσιμον 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Septem contra Thebas” 554; δήμου κρατοῦσα χ. [prev. author] “Supp.” 604 (uncertain reading): proverbial, ἁ δὲ χ. τὰν χ. νίζει 5th c.BC: Epicharmus Comicus 273; or simply, ἁ χ. τὰν χ. “Anthologia Graeca” 5.207 (1st c.BC: Meleager Epigrammaticus).]]

__III.3
plural, in theurgy, name for spiritual powers, αἱ δημιουργικαὶ [τοῦ Ἀπόλλωνος] δυνάμεις ἃς θεουργῶν παῖδες χεῖρας ἀποκαλοῦσιν [Refs 5th c.AD+ [5th c.AD: Proclus Philosophus “in Platonis Cratylum commentaria” p.101]] P., compare [same work] in R.[Refs [2.252K.]]

__IV
to denote act or deed, opposed to mere words, in plural, ἔπεσιν καὶ χερσὶν ἀρήξειν [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 1.77]]; μνῆμ᾽ Ἑλένης χειρῶν of her handiwork, her art, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 15.126 (so in _sing._, δώρημ᾽ ἐκείνῳ τἀνδρὶ τῆς ἐμῆς χ. 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Trachiniae” 603); χερσὶν ἢ λόγῳ [prev. author] “OT” 883 (Lyric poetry), compare “OC” 1297, etc.]]; τῇ χειρὶ χρᾶσθαι to use one's hands, i.with be active, stirring, opposed to ἀργὸς ἐπεστάναι, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 3.78, compare 9.72]]; τὰς χ. προσφέρειν to apply force, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Memorabilia” 2.6.31: _sing._, βούλευμα μὲν τὸ Δῖον, Ἡφαίστου δὲ χείρ 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Prometheus Vinctus” 619]]; μιᾷ χειρί single-handed, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 21.219; χειρὶ καὶ ποδὶ καὶ πάσῃ δυνάμει 4th c.BC: Aeschines Orator 3.109, compare 2.115; χερσίν τε ποσίν τε 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 20.360, compare 5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “O.” 10(11).62]], especially of using the hands in a fight, compare above [Refs [11.6d]], e, f; of deeds of violence, πρὶν χειρῶν γεύσασθαι before we try force, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 20.181]]; ἀδίκων χ. ἄρχειν to give the first blow, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 1.5.13, 5th c.BC: Antipho Orator 4.2.1, 5th c.BC: Lysias Orator 4.11, etc.; ἀμυνόμενος ἄρχοντα χειρῶν 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Leges” 869d: generally, χεῖρες]] violent measures, force, ἐπίσχετε θυμὸν ἐνιπῆς καὶ χειρῶν [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 20.267; ὑπόδικος χερῶν 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Eumenides” 260 (Lyric poetry); χερσὶ πεποιθώς 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 16.624, etc.; ἐν χειρῶν νόμῳ see above 11.6d]]; ὅπως θανάτοιο βαρείας χ. ἀλάλκοι, variant for{κῆρας}, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 21.548.]]

__V
a number, band, body of men, especially of soldiers, χεὶρ μεγάλη [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 7.157; in _dative_, οὐ σὺν μεγάλῃ χ. [prev. author] 5.72; πολλῇ χ. 1.174, 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 3.96, 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Heraclidae” 337; pleonastic, χ. μεγάλῃ πλήθεος 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 7.20; δεδωμάτωμαι δ᾽ οὐδ᾽ ἐγὼ σμικρᾷ χερί 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Supplices” 958]]; οἰκεία χείρ, for χεὶρ οἰκετῶν, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Electra” 629; σὺν πλήθει χερῶν 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Tyrannus” 123.]]

__VI
handwriting, τὴν ἑαυτοῦ χεῖρα ἀρνήσασθαι [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Hyperides Orator “Lyc.fragment” 5, compare “IG” 9(1).189 (from Phocis)]]; τῇ ἐμῇ χ. Παύλου [NT.1Cor.16.21, NT.Col.4.18]: copy, counterpart of a document, [Refs 2nd c.BC+ [“SIG” 712.31 (Crete, 2nd c.BC)]]; deed, instrument, ἡ χ. ἥδε κυρία ἔστω [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [“PRein.” 28.18 (2nd c.BC),compare “PCair.Zen.” 477 (3rd c.BC), etc.]]

__VI.b
handiwork of an artist or workman, γλαφυρὰ χ. [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [3rd c.BC: Theocritus Poeta Bucolicus “epigram” 8.5, etc.; αἱ Ἐφεσίου χεῖρες 3rd c.BC: Herodas Mimographus 4.72, compare 6.66; σοφαὶ χέρες “APl.” 4.262; τὰς Φειδίου χ. 4th c.AD: Libanius Sophista “Orationes” 30.22.]]

__VII
of any implement resembling a hand:

__VII.1
a kind of gauntlet, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “de Equitandi ratione” 12.5, 2nd c.AD(?): Pollianus Epigrammaticus 1.135 (_plural_).]]

__VII.2
χ. σιδηρᾶ grappling-iron, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 4.25, 7.62]]; also of an anchor, [Refs 1st c.AD+ [Anthologia Graeca 6.38 (1st c.AD: Philippus Epigrammaticus).]]

__VII.3
axle-tree, [LXX.3Ki.7.18(32).]

__VII.4
in LXX, pillar or cairn, as it were a finger pointing to heaven, χεὶρ Ἀβεσσαλώμ [LXX.2Ki.18.18]; also ἀνέστακεν αὐτῷ χεῖρα, i.e. trophy,[LXX.1Ki.15.12.]

__VII.5
χεῖρες ἐλάτιναι, of oars, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Timotheus Lyricus “Persae” 7.]]

__VII.6
catch of a trigger, [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [2nd-1st c.BC(?): Hero Mechanicus “Automatopoetica” 13.9; χ. κατάγουσα τὴν τοξῖτιν 3rd-2nd c.BC: Philo Mechanicus “(Belopoeica) Excerpte aus Philons Mechanik - Ath. Berl. Akad.” 68.4, compare 2nd-1st c.BC(?): Hero Mechanicus “Belopoeica” 78.2.]]

__VII.7
instrument of torture, [LXX.4Mac.8.13.]

__VIII
handful, κορώνῃ χεῖρα πρόσδοτε κριθέων [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [3rd c.BC: Phoenix Iambographus 2.1.]]

__IX
ointment containing five ingredients, [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [4th c.AD: Oribasius Medicus “fragment” 89, 2nd c.AD: Alexander Rhetor Trall. 7.1]]. (Cf. Armenian jein (dzern), [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd c.AD: Albinus Philosophus]] dore, Tocharian (A-dialect) tsar, (B-dialect) sar, all = hand.)

__II
with accusative person, elect, properly by show of hands, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Acharnenses” 598, “Av.” 1571, etc.; εἰς τὴν ἀγορὰν χ. τοὺς ταξιάρχους.., οὐκ ἐπὶ τὸν πόλεμον 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 4.26; with double _accusative_, στρατηγὸν χ. τινά 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Historia Graeca (Hellenica)” 6.2.11, compare 5th-6th c.BC: Isocrates Orator 8.50]]:—passive, to be elected, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Acharnenses” 607]]; ἐπὶ τοῦτ᾽ ἐχειροτονήθησαν, ἵνα.. [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Lysias Orator 28.14; χ. ἔκ τινων 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Leges” 763e]]; χ. ἐπὶ τῆς διοικήσεως Decrees cited in [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 18.115: with _accusative_ _cognate_, χ. τὴν ἀρχὴν τὴν ἐπὶ τῷ θεωρικῷ 4th c.BC: Aeschines Orator 3.24, compare 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Ecclesiazusae” 517 (_anapaest meter_); χειροτονηθεὶς ἢ λαχών 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Politicus” 300a, compare 4th c.BC: Aeschines Orator 1.106.]]

__II.b
later, generally, appoint, [Refs 1st c.AD+ [1st c.AD: Philo Judaeus 2.112]]; of the Jewish High Priest, [Refs 1st c.AD+ [1st c.AD: Josephus Historicus “Antiquitates Judaicae” 13.2.2; τὸν ὑπὸ τοῦ θεοῦ κεχειροτονημένον βασιλέα [prev. work] 6.13.9, compare 7.9.3]]; appoint to an office in the Church, πρεσβυτέρους [NT.Act.14.23, cf. NT.2Cor.8.19 (_passive_).]

__II.2
with accusative of things, vote for a thing, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Ecclesiazusae” 297 (Lyric poetry), 797, Isocrates  7.84; γνώμας 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 18.248: with]]infinitive, ὁ δῆμος ἐχειροτόνησεν ἐξεῖναι.. πέμπειν voted to send, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aeschines Orator 2.13, compare “IG” 12.57.29, 63.4:]] —passive, κεχειροτόνηται ὕβρις τὸ πρᾶγυ᾽ εἶναι it is voted, ruled to be.., [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 21.216.]]

span with the hand, τὸ αἰδοῖον [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd c.AD: Artemidorus Daldianus Onirocriticus 1.78 (cited in 10th c.AD: Suidas Legal icographus]]; χειροκοπεῖν codices).

short_definition: worse than — χείρων, -ον, compar. of κακός
deep_entry:
Abbott-Smith / STEPBible (TBESG)
χείρων, -ον, compar. of κακός
[in LXX: 1Ki.17:43 B, Wis.15:18 17:6, 3Ma.5:20 * ;]
worse: Mat.9:16 12:45 27:64, Mrk.2:21, Luk.11:26, Jhn.5:14, 1Ti.5:8, Heb.10:29, 2Pe.2:20; εἰς (ἐπὶ) τὸ χεῖρον, Mrk.5:26, 2Ti.3:13.†
(AS)

---

LSJ / STEPBible (TFLSJ)
χείρων, ὁ, ἡ,
neuter χεῖρον, genitive -ονος, accusative -ονα: nominative and accusative plural χείρονες, -ας, χείρονα, contraction in Attic dialect Prose χείρους, χείρ; dative χείροσι, poetry χειρόνεσσι [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “N.” 8.22]]:—(for Epic dialect form χερείων, poetry χειρότερος, χερειότερος, (see entry).):—irregular comparative of κακός: (χείρων from *χερ-yων, compare χερείων):

__I
of persons, mcaner, inferior, either in bodily strength and bravery, or in rank, opposed to ἀρείων, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 10.238, 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 20.133; σὺ μὲν ἐσθλὸς ἐγὼ δὲ σέθεν πολὺ χείρων 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 20.434; τοῦ γένετ᾽ ἐκ πατρὸς πολὺ χείρονος υἱὸς ἀμείνων 15.641, compare 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 20.82; ἦ πολὺ χείρονες ἄνδρες ἀμύμονος ἀνδρὸς ἄκοιτιν μνῶνται 21.325]]; opposed to κρείσσων, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “I.” 4(3).34(52); τὸν ὄλβιον τόν τε χ. 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Bacchae” 422 (Lyric poetry); τὰ χείρονα 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Fragmenta” 192, 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Supplices” 196.]]

__I.2
later in moral sense, worse than others, sometimes almost like a positive, knave, opposed to ἀγαθός, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Philoctetes” 456, compare 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 3.9, 5th c.BC: Lysias Orator 16.3; οἱ πένητες καὶ οἱ δημόται καὶ οἱ χ. 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Respublica Atheniensium” 1.4, compare 3.10]]; οἱ χ., opposed to οἱ ἀγαθοί, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 460c, etc.]]

__I.2.b
χ. βίος, opposed to ἀμείνων,[Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. work] 618d; γνώμη 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 8.8.7.]]

__I.3
worse in quality, inferior, of horses, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 23.572]]: inferior, less skilful, ἰητροί [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Hippocrates Medicus “περὶ διαίτης ὀξέων” 6]]; ζωγράφοι, δημιουργοί, etc., [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Cratylus” 429a, “R.” 421e, etc.: χ. εἰς σοφίαν, εἰς τὴν ἀρετήν, [prev. author] “Tht.” 162c, “R.” 335b; πρὸς ἀλήθειαν 2nd c.AD: Lucianus Sophista “JTr.” 48; with _accusative_, χ. τὰ πολεμικά 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 8.8.20]]; χ. τὴν ψυχήν, τὴν διάνοιαν, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aeschines Orator 3.46. 5th-6th c.BC: Isocrates Orator 11.43; τὰ ἄλλα μηδὲν χ. [prev. author] 4.105]]; with infinitive, χ. ἡμῶν ταῦτα ποιεῖν [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 2.1.16]]; οὐδὲν χείρους ἔσεσθε.. ἀκηκοότες you will be none the worse for having heard.., [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 24.139]]; less kind, μὴ χ. περὶ ἡμᾶς αὐτοὺς εἶναι.. τῶν ὑπαρχόντων [Refs [[prev. author] 2.2.]]

__II
of things, inferior in quality, ἄεθλον [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 23.413; ὑποδήματα 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Oeconomicus” 13.10; ὄνομα 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Cratylus” 429b.]]

__II.2
worse, harder, more severe, νόσος [NT+5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Andromache” 220; μοῖρα 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Phaedrus” 248e; τιμωρία NT.Heb.10.29.]]

__III
neuter,

__III.1
as a substantive, τὸ χ. inferiority, [Refs 1st c.AD+ [1st-2nd c.AD: Polemo Sophista “Callimachus” 27]]; but mostly in phrases with Preps., ἐπὶ τὸ χ. τρέπεσθαι, κλῖναι, fall off, get worse, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 8.8.2, “Mem.” 3.5.13; ἐπὶ τὸ χ. μεταβάλλει ἑαυτόν 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 381b]]; ἀλλοιοῦσθαι ἐπὶ τὸ χ., opposed to ἐπὶ τὸ βέλτιον, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-3rd c.BC: Theophrastus Philosophus “de Causis Plantarum” 6.3.3]]; also πάντα ὑποπτεύοντες ἐπὶ τὸ χ. putting the worst construction on.. [Refs 5th c.BC+ [1st c.BC: Dionysius Halicarnassensis 6.85; λαμβάνειν τι ἐπὶ τὸ χ. 1st c.AD: Josephus Historicus “Antiquitates Judaicae” 16.7.4; also πρὸς τὸ χ. μεταβάλλειν 1st c.BC: Diodorus Siculus Historicus 20.57; κατὰ τὸ χ. 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Leges” 720e]]; in the lower sense, opposed to κατὰ τὸ κρεῖττον, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.AD: Damascius Philosophus “de Principiis” 7: less frequently in _plural_, ἐπὶ τὰ χείρω ἰέναι 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Memorabilia” 3.9.9; τὰ χ. προαιρεῖσθαι 5th-6th c.BC: Isocrates Orator 8.110.]]

__III.2
as a predicate, ἀλλὰ σοὶ αὐτῷ χ. (i.e. ἐστί or ἔσται) [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 15.515, compare 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 7.6.4]]; with a negative, οὐ χ. [ἐστι] with infinitive, we may as well, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Phaedo” 105a, 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Ethica Nicomachea” 1127a14]]; simply οὐ χεῖρον, in an answer, it is as well, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Equites” 37; λάβ᾽, ὦγάθ᾽· οὐδὲν χ. 4th c.BC: Clearchus Comicus 4.]]

__III.3
as adverb, worse, χ. βουλεύσασθαι [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 3.46, compare 6.89; χ. πρᾶξαι [prev. author] 7.67]]; βιῶναι, ζῆν, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 344e, 519d.]]

__III.3.b
in inferior degree, less, ἀγαπᾶν [Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. author] “Lg.” 928a; φυλακὰς χ. φυλαττομένας 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Historia Graeca (Hellenica)” 6.2.17, etc.]]

__B
superlative χείριστος, η, ον, worst, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Politicus” 303a, etc.]]; ὁ χ., opposed to ὁ βέλτιστος, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Lysias Orator 1.2; especially οἱ χ.]]men of lowest degrce, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Memorabilia” 1.2.32]]. adverb χείριστα [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “de Partibus Animalium” 687a24, “Metaphorical” 1083b2 (uncertain 1.);]] also -τως [LXX.2Mac.7.39.]

[Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Isocrates Orator 4.87, 93, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Critias” 119b: but χ. καὶ πεντακόσιοι 4th c.BC: Aeschines Orator 2.77]]; later καί is frequently omitted, [NT+5th c.BC+ [2nd c.BC: Polybius Historicus 3.33.10, LXX.Dan.12.11, NT.Rev.11.3; with Preps. χ. ἐπὶ μυρίοις 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Leges” 895a; τέτταρας πρὸς τοῖς χ. 2nd c.AD: Lucianus Sophista “Cat.” 4]]; οἱ χ. λογάδες (at Argos) the Thousand, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 5.67, compare 1st c.BC: Diodorus Siculus Historicus 12.80.]]

singular with collective nouns, χιλίη ἵππος a thousand horse, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 5.63, 7.41; τὴν ἵππον τὴν χιλίην [prev. author] 8.113; so ἵππον ἔχω εἰς χιλίαν 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 4.6.2]]; also χιλία ὁλοκαύτωσις burnt-offering of 1000 cattle, [LXX.3Ki.3.4.]

__3
χίλιαι (i.e. δραχμαί) as substantive, a thousand drachmae, περὶ χιλιῶν κινδυνεύειν [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 22.21; ἐν χιλίαις ὁ κίνδυνος [prev. work]26 (χ. δραχμαί in full, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Apologia” 36b)]]. in Ionic dialectProse κῐθών, ῶνος, ὁ (also probably in [Refs [“Sammelb.” 4291)]], Doric dialect κῐτών (which see):— garment worn next the skin, tunic.

__I
in early times, only of a man's tunic (the woman's being πέπλος, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [Scholia BT 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 2.42), χιτῶνα περὶ χροΐ δῦνεν 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 15.60; κιθῶνας ὑποδύνειν τοῖσι εἵμασι 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.155]]: sometimes with a girdle, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 14.72; τερμιόεις 19.242, 8th-7th c.BC: Hesiodus Epicus “Opera et Dies” 537]]; μαλακός, ἐΰννητος, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 1.437, 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 24.580; [χ.] λαμπρός.. ἠέλιος ὥς 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 19.234; χλαῖνάν τε χιτῶνά τε 14.132, 154; οἱ δ᾽ ἀροτῆρες ἤρεικον χθόνα δῖαν ἐπιστολάδην δὲ χιτῶνας ἐστάλατ᾽ 8th-7th c.BC: Hesiodus Epicus “Scutum Herculis” 287.]]

__I.2
later worn also by women, ἅμα κιθῶνι ἐκδυομένῳ συνεκδύεται καὶ τὴν αἰδῶ γυνή [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.8; σύροισα χιτῶνα 3rd c.BC: Theocritus Poeta Bucolicus 2.73]]; the Ionian sleeved χ. was distinguished fr the Dorian, fastened with περόναι, μετέβαλον [αἱ τῶν Ἀθηναίων γυναῖκες] ἐς τὸν λίνεον κ. ἵνα δὴ περόνῃσι μὴ χρέωνται [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 5.87; οἱ πρεσβύτεροι [τῶν Ἀθηναίων] οὐ πολὺς χρόνος ἐπειδὴ χιτῶνας λινοῦς ἐπαύσαντο φοροῦντες 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 1.6, compare 12th c.AD: Eustathius Episcopus Thessalonicensis 954.50]]; χ. ποδήρης, ὀρθοστάδιος, στατός (see entry); κιθὼν ποδηνεκής, worn by Babylonians, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.195]]; κιθῶνες λίνεοι περὶ τὰ σκέλεα θυσανωτοί, worn by Egyptians, [Refs [[prev. author] 2.81]]; κιθῶνες εἰρίνεοι, worn by Cilicians, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. author] 7.91; uncertain in 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Iphigenia Taurica” 288 (_plural_).]]

__II
coat of mail, probably of leather covered with scales or rings, στρεπτὸς χ. [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 5.113; χ. χάλκεος 13.439]]; κιθῶνες χειριδωτοὶ λεπίδος σιδηρέης coats of iron scales with sleeves, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 7.61 (assuming variant): but distinguished from θώρηξ [prev. author] 9.22, compare 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 6.4.1.]]

__III
part of a shoe that coats the foot, upper, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [[prev. work] 8.2.5 (_plural_), 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Rhetorica” 1392a31.]]

__IV
metaphorically, any coat, case, or covering, λάϊνος χιτών (see. λάϊνος) τειχέων κιθῶνες, i. e. walls, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 7.139]]; in Anatomy, coat, membrane, τὸν ἀμφὶ τὴν ὄψιν χ. [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Hippocrates Medicus “περὶ ἀρχαίης ἰητρικῇς” 19, compare “Aph.” 7.45, 4th-3rd c.BC: Epicurus Philosophus “De rerum natura - Wien. Stud.” 2.993.1; ὁ.. χ. τῆς καρδίας 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “de Respiratione” 480a4]]; χ. ὑμενώδης, ἀραχνιώδης, [Refs [[prev. author] “PA” 679a1, “HA” 557b16; τοῦ ᾠοῦ οἱ χ. οἱ περιέχοντες [prev. work] 561a14]]; of foetal membranes, [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd c.AD: Soranus Medicus 1.7, 58, +others]]; τριγλοφόροι χιτῶνες, of fishing-nets, [Refs 1st c.BC+ [“Anthologia Graeca” 6.11 (1st c.BC(?): Satyrus Epigrammaticus)]]; χιτῶνες ἀραχνίων spiders' webs, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Hippocrates Medicus “περὶ τῶν ἐντὸς παθῶν” 3]]: plural, pods or coats of seeds, bulbous roots, etc., [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-3rd c.BC: Theophrastus Philosophus “Historia Plantarum” 1.12.3, 8.4.1, “CP” 1.4.1, +others]]

__IV.2
vesture, [φύσις] σαρκῶν ἀλλογνῶτι περιστέλλουσα (i.e. ψυχάς) χιτῶνι [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Empedocles Poeta Philosophus 126; σῶμα χ. ψυχῆς “IG” 14.2241: _plural_, προσθέσει χιτώνων ἐνυλοτέρων,]] of the soul, [Refs 5th c.AD+ [5th c.AD: Proclus Philosophus “Inst.” 209]]. (Accad. kitinnu 'linen garment', Hebrew kètōnet 'tunic'; χεθὼν γὰρ τὸ λίνον ἡμεῖς καλοῦμεν [Refs 1st c.AD+ [1st c.AD: Josephus Historicus “Antiquitates Judaicae” 3.7.2.)]]

gall, bile, [Refs 7th c.BC+ [7th c.BC: Archilochus Lyricus 131, 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Choephori” 184, 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Fragmenta” 682, 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 2.49, etc.]]; χ. μέλαινα black, i. e. diseased, bile, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Hippocrates Medicus “ἀφορισμοί” 4.23, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Timaeus” 83c]] (but, ={μελαγχολία}, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th-3rd c.BC: Menander Comicus “Ἐπιτρέποντες” 459); ξανθὴ χ. 5th c.BC: Hippocrates Medicus “περὶ ἀρχαίης ἰητρικῇς” 19; πυρρά 2nd c.AD: Galenus Medicus 15.658]]; χολὴν ἐμεῖν, βῆξαι, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Nicopho Comicus 12, 3rd c.BC: Herodas Mimographus 3.70 (probable reading): proverbial, πικρῷ πικρὰν κλύζουσι φαρμάκῳ χολήν 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Fragmenta” 854; πικρότερ᾽ αὐτῆς τῆς χ. 2nd c.AD: Alexander Rhetor 16.12]]; χολῇ ἀλείφειν, proverbial of giving one a disgust for a thing, from the custom of mothers putting gall to the nipple when the child was to be weaned, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-3rd c.BC: Diphilus Comicus 74.]]

__2
plural χολαί, gall-bladder, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Antigone” 1010]]; called δοχαὶ χολῆς, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Electra” 828]]; also in singular, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Prometheus Vinctus” 495; χολὴν τῶν ζῴων τὰ μὲν ἔχει τὰ δ᾽ οὐκ ἔχει 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Historia Animalium” 506a20, compare “PA” 677b11.]]

__3
metaphorically (mostly in Poets) like{χόλος} (which see), bile, gall, i. e. bitter anger, wrath, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Pax” 66; ἢ γυναιξὶν οὐκ οἴει χολὴν ἐνεῖνα; [prev. author] “Lys.” 465; οὐδεὶς χολὴν οὐδ᾽ ὀργὴν ἔχων φανήσεται 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 25.27]]; πάνυ ἐστ᾽ ἤδη χ. stirs my bile, makes me sick, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Ranae” 4]]; ἐπιζεῖ χ. the bile boils over, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. author] “Th.” 468; χολὴν κινεῖν [prev. author] “V.” 403, compare 5th c.BC: Pherecrates Comicus 69.]]

__II
ink of the cuttle-fish, [Refs 2nd c.BC+ [2nd c.BC: Nicander Epicus “Alexipharmaca” 473, “Th.” 561.]]

in LXX = Hebrew rôsh, a poisonous plant, variously called hemlock or poppy, [LXX.Psa.68(69).22, LXX.Jer. 8.14.]

__IV
serpent's venom, χ. ἀσπίδος[LXX.Job.20.14]; of the hydra's venom, [Refs 1st c.BC+ [2nd c.AD: Apollodorus Damascenus Mechanicus 2.5.2, 1st c.BC: Diodorus Siculus Historicus 4.11.]]

middle, of the person to whom the response is given, consult a god or oracle, with dative, ψυχῇ χρησόμενος Θηβαίου Τειρεσίαο [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 10.492, 565]]; χ. θεῷ, χρηστηρίοισι, μαντηΐῳ, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.47, 53, 157; τῷ θεῷ 4th c.BC: Aeschines Orator 3.124; χ. μάντεσι Μούσαις 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Aves” 724 (_anapaest meter_), compare 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Leges” 686a; ὅσοι μαντικὴν νομίζοντες οἰωνοῖς χρῶνται 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Memorabilia” 1.1.3]]; χ. χρηστηρίῳ εἰ.. inquire at the oracle whether.., [Refs 8th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 3.57: _absolutely_, ὑπέρβη λάϊνον οὐδὸν χρησόμενος 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 8.81, compare “hymnus ad Apollinem” 252, 292; ἀπέστειλε ἄλλους χρησομένους 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.46]]; οἱ χρώμενοι the consulters, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Phoenissae” 957; χρωμένῳ ἐν Δελφοῖς 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 1.126; also χ. περὶ τοῦ πολέμου 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 7.220, compare 1.85, 4.150, 155, etc.]]; κεχρημένος having inquired of an oracle, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Rhetorica” 1398b33: with]]infinitive, σωφρονεῖν κεχρημένον being divinely warned to be temperate, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Persae” 829, compare 4th c.AD(?): Marcellinus Biographus “Vita Thucydidis” 6]]: later simply, receive a divine revelation, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [3rd c.AD: Plotinus Philosophus 5.3.14.— 8th c.BC: Homerus Epicus]] has the word in this sense only in [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey”: the]]active only in present participle χρείων (future χρήσω [Refs [“hymnus ad Apollinem” 132): the]]middle only in participle future χρησόμενος.

furnish with a thing, in which sense the present was κίχρημι, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 53.12, 1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus “Pompeius” 29]]; Cretan dialect 3rd.pers. singular κίγχρητι [Refs 2nd c.BC+ [“Inscription Cretan dialect” 1 xxiii 3 (Phaestus, 2nd c.BC)]]; Delph. 3rd.pers. singular present subjunctive κιχρῇ [Refs 4th c.BC+ [“Schwyzer” 324.17 (4th c.BC):]]aorist χρέη[Refs [[prev. work]13]]; present participle κιχρέντε [Refs [[prev. work]adn. __III.1
as a property, use, advantage, service, χρείης εἵνεκα μηδεμιῆς [Refs 6th c.BC+ [6th c.BC: Theognis Elegiacus 62; τῆς χ. τοῦ παιδὸς ἀποστερηθῆναι 5th c.BC: Antipho Orator 3.3.4; ἡ χ. τῆς ῥητορικῆς 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Gorgias” 480a; πωλοῦντες τὴν τῆς ἰσχύος χ. [prev. author] “R.” 371e]]; χρείαν ἔχειν τοῖς ἀνθρώποις to be of service to mankind, [Refs [[prev. author] “Smp.” 204c]]; τὰ οὐδὲν εἰς χρείαν things of no use or service, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator “Prooemia” 56.3]]; χρείαν ἔχει εἴς τι is of service towards.., [Refs 5th c.BC+ [3rd c.BC(?): Sosipater Comicus 1.41; for 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Tyrannus” 725, see at {ἐρευνάω} 1: _plural_, χρεῖαι.. φίλων ἀνδρῶν]] services rendered by them, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “N.” 8.42]]; χρείας παρέχεσθαι render services, Decrees cited in [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 18.84, “IG” 22.654.15, compare 2nd c.BC: Polybius Historicus 1.16.8 (_sing._)]]; ἵνα σοι τὰς χ. παρέσχωμαι (sic) [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [“PCair.Zen.” 498 (3rd c.BC)]]; μεγάλην παρεῖχε χ. τοῖς κοινοῖς πράγμασιν [Refs 2nd c.BC+ [2nd c.BC: Polybius Historicus 3.97.4]]; παρέχειν χ. to be serviceable, useful, [Refs 1st c.AD+ [Aristo Stoic. 1.79; ἑξήκοντα καὶ τριακόσια χρειῶν γένη παρέχον δένδρον 1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus 2.724e; χ. ναυτικαί]]equipments, [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd-3rd c.AD: Aelianus “Varia Historia” 2.10.]]

__III.2
as an action, using, use, κτῆσις καὶ χ. [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Memorabilia” 2.4.1, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 451c]]; ἐν χρείᾳ εἶναι in use, [Refs [[prev. author] “Phd.” 87c]]; κατὰ τὴν χ. for use, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. author] “R.” 330c; πρὸς τὴν ἀνθρωπίνην χ. 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Memorabilia” 4.2.25]]; ἡ χ. τῶν λόγων the employment of words, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Sophista” 239d, compare “Plt.” 272d: _plural_, λάμπει γὰρ ἐν χρείαισιν ὥσπερ.. χαλκός]] is made bright by constant use, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Fragmenta” 864.]]

__IV
of persons, familiarity, intimacy, τινος with one, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Antipho Orator 5.63]]: generally, any relation of business or intercourse, ἐν χρείᾳ τινὶ τῇ πρὸς ἀλλήλους [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 372a; ἡ πρὸς ἀλλήλους χ. 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Rhetorica” 1376b13; [Νικόμαχος] συνεβίω Ἀμυντᾳ.. ἰατροῦ καὶ φίλου χρείᾳ]]in the relationship, capacity, [Refs 3rd c.AD+ [3rd c.AD(?): Diogenes Laertius 5.1.]]

__V
Rhet., pregnant sentence, maxim, frequently illustrated by an anecdote, Sen.[Refs 1st c.AD+ [“Ep.” 33.7, 2nd c.AD: Hermogenes Rhetor “προγυμνάσματα” 3, Aphthon, “Prog.” 3, 1st-2nd c.AD(?): Theon Rhetor “Progymnasmata - Rhet.” 5, etc.]]: plural, title of works by Zeno [Refs 5th c.BC+ [(3rd c.AD(?): Diogenes Laertius 6.91), 5th-6th c.BC: Aristippus Philosophus, etc.; by 3rd c.BC: Macho Comicus]], a collection of sayings of courtesans, [Refs 1st c.AD+ [2nd c.AD: Athenaeus Epigrammaticus 13.577d; ἡ τοῦ Κλεομένους χ. 1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus 2.218a; χρεῖαι καὶ ἱστορίαι [prev. work]78f.]]

deep_entry:

LSJ / STEPBible (TFLSJ)
χρή,
impersonal, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 1.216, etc.]]; Aeolic dialect χρῆ [Refs 7th c.BC+ [7th-6th c.BC: Alcaeus Lyricus 20, 35, 46]]; other forms are contractions (crases) of χρή (probably originally a neuter substantive) with forms of εἰμί (sum): future χρἤσται [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Coloneus” 504, “fragment” 599, 5th c.BC: Pherecrates Comicus 103, 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Fragmenta” 362, 5th c.BC: Phrynichus Comicus 34 (on this form, for which codices generally have χρῆσται or χρῆσθαι, see Scholia 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “OC” [same place])]]: subjunctive χρῇ [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Philoctetes” 999, 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Alcestis” 49, 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Lysistrata” 133; _optative_ χρείη 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Prometheus Vinctus” 215, 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Trachiniae” 162, 5th c.BC: Lysias Orator 12.44, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Euthyphro” 4c]]; infinitive χρῆναι [Refs 5th c.BC+ [3rd c.AD: Democritus Epigrammaticus 276, 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Ecclesiazusae” 210, 5th c.BC: Antipho Orator 5.84, etc.]]; also χρῆν (see. below 111); participle neuter plural χρηεόντα (or χρὴ ἐόντα) [Refs 3rd c.AD+ [3rd c.AD: Democritus Epigrammaticus 174]]: imperfect ἐχρῆν [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “N.” 7.44, 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Choephori” 907, 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Fragmenta” 107.6 (only here in 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus, χρῆν l. 5), 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Ranae” 152, +others, 5th c.BC: Antipho Orator 1.1, 5th-6th c.BC: Andocides Orator 1.114, 5th c.BC: Lysias Orator 3.22, +others, 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 6.57, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Protagoras” 335c, 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 4.3, +others, etc.]]: frequently also without the augment, χρῆν [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “Fragmenta.” 123.1, 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Electra” 529, 579, “Tr.” 1133, 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Equites” 535 (_anapaest meter_), +others, 5th c.BC: Lysias Orator 8.6, +others, 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 3.63, 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 15.33, +others, etc.]]; both forms in [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Acharnenses” 540, ἐρεῖ τις, οὐ χρῆν· ἀλλὰ τί ἐχρῆν εἴπατε]]: future χρήδει [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 7.8]]: —it is necessary: with infinitive praes. aut aorist, it must needs, one must or ought to do (like δεῖ, which is only once used in [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Homerus Epicus), νῦν δὲ χ. τετλάμεν ἔμπης 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 3.209; τὸν νῦν χ. κομέειν 6.207, compare 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 1.216, 4.57, etc.; σήμαιν᾽ ὅ τι χ. σοι συμπράσσειν 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Prometheus Vinctus” 297 (_anapaest meter_)]]; ὅτι χ. πάσχειν ἐθέλω[Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. work] 1067; ὅ τι χρείη ποιεῖν 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Euthyphro” 4c, compare 9a; τούτου θανειν χρῆν αὐτὸν οὕνεκ᾽ ἐκ σέθε; 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Electra” 579; χρὴ τὸ λέγειν 4th-5th c.BC: Parmenides Poeta Philosophus 6.1]]: more frequently with accusative person et infinitive, one must, ἐμὲ δὲ χ. γήραϊ πείθεσθαι [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 23.644; τῷ σε χ. πόλεμον.. παῦσαι 7.331]]; οὐδέ τί σε χ. νηλεὲς ἦτορ ἔχειν [Refs 5th c.BC+ [9.496; τί χ. με.. στέγειν ἢ τί λέγει; 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Philoctetes” 135 (Lyric poetry): χρῆν γὰρ Κανδαύλῃ γενέσθαι κακῶς (where γενέσθαι is _infinitive_ of an _impersonal_ verb) 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.8.]]—Sts. the infinitive must be supplied from the context, especially in [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Homerus Epicus in phrases like{τίπτε μάχης. ἀποπαύεα; οὐδέ τί σε χρή}]] (i.e. ἀποπαύεσθαι) [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 16.721, compare 19.420]]; ὅθι χ. πεζὸν ἐόντα (i.e. μάρνασθαι) [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 9.50]]; so in Trag. and Attic dialect, πορθεῖν ἃ μὴ χ. (i.e. πορθεῖν) [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Agamemnon” 342]]; φύς τ᾽ ἀφ᾽ ὧν οὐ χρῆν (i.e. φῦναι), ξὺν οἷς τ᾽ οὐ χρῆν (i.e. ὁμιλεῖν) ὁμιλῶν [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Tyrannus” 1184]]; ἔκανες ὃν οὐ χρῆν (i.e. κτεῖναι) [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Choephori” 930]]; ἐπιπλεύσειέ τις ὡς χ. (i.e. ἐπιπλεῦσαι) [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 2.89]]; θύσαντες οἷς χ. (i.e. θῦσαι) [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 415e; ἀκαιρότερον ὄντα ἢ χ. [prev. author] “Plt.” 307e; λαλεῖν μετὰ ἀφελείας ἔνθα χ. 3rd c.AD: Longinus Rhetor 34.2.; so ὡς χ. 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Agamemnon” 1556 (_anapaest meter_), etc.]] —The imperfect frequently expresses something that ought to have been, but is not, ἐνθάδ᾽ οὐ παραστατεῖ, ὡς χρῆν, Ὀρέστης[Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. work] 879, compare 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Trachiniae” 1133; and sometimes stands for χρή, χρῆν τι λέγειν ὑμᾶς σοφὸν ῳ νικήσετε 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Plutus” 487 (_anapaest meter_), compare 432: _absolutely_, ἐρεῖτις, οὐ χρῆν· ἀλλὰτί ἐχρῆν εἴπατε [prev. author] “Ach.” 540.]]

__2
in [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Homerus Epicus without]]infinitive, with accusative person et genitive of things, οὐδέ τί σε χρὴ ἀφρποσύνης thou hast no need of imprudence, i. e. it does not befit thee, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 7.109; οὐ μέν σε χ. ἔτ᾽ αἰδοῦς 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 3.14; τί με χ. μητέρος αἴνο; 21.110]]; μυθήσεαι ὅττεό (i.e. ὅτου) σε χ. [Refs [1.124; τέο σε χ.; 4.463: τί χρὴ φίλων]] is found in most codices of [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Orestes” 667 (δεῖ codex V).]]

__3
with dative person pro accusative is not found; in [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 5.490, 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Prometheus Vinctus” 3]], the dative belongs to the infinitive μέλει; in [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Antigone” 736]] Dobree restored με for γ; in [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Medea” 886 ᾗ]] depends on μετεῖνα; in [Refs 5th c.BC+ [“Ion” 1316 Dobree read τοὺς δέ γ᾽ ἐνδίκους, and in 5th c.BC: Lysias Orator 28.10 δικαίους.. ὑφελομένους was restored by Cobet.]]

__II
sometimes in a less strong sense, πῶς τοῦτο περᾶσαι χρ; how is one to get through this? [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [3rd c.BC: Theocritus Poeta Bucolicus 15.45]]; τί ἐχρῆν με ποιεῖ; what was I to do? [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 18.28]]; ἓν οὐδὲν κατέστη ἴαμα ὅτι χρῆν προσφερόντας ὠφελεῖν there was no one remedy by the application of which one could (or was bound to) help them, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 2.51, compare 1.91.]]

__III
τὸ χρῆν (infinitive) fate, destiny, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Hecuba” 260 (assuming variant, τὸ χρὴ Nauck)]]; τὸ χρή [Refs [[prev. author] “HF” 828]]; conjecture for τὸ χρεών (monosyllable) in [Refs [[prev. author] “fragment” 733.3, “IT” 1486.]]

χρῄζω
(χρή) [in LXX Jdg.11:7, 1Ki.17:18 A * ;]

LSJ / STEPBible (TFLSJ)
χρῄζω,
[Refs 6th c.BC+ [6th c.BC: Theognis Elegiacus 958, 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Prometheus Vinctus” 376, 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Nubes” 891 (_anapaest meter_), 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 3.109, etc.; in _Attic dialect_ hardly found except in]]present and imperfect (but see below [Refs [11)]]: Epic dialect and Ionic dialect χρηΐζω, as always in [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Homerus Epicus, and 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.41, 5.19, 30, 9.87]]; written χρηιίζω, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [“SIG” 57.41 (Milet., 5th c.BC)]]; also χρεΐζω, [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [3rd c.BC: Herodas Mimographus 7.64]]; Doric dialect χρῄζω [Refs 5th c.BC+ [“SIG” 56.23 (Argos, 5th c.BC)]]; also χρήζω [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [[prev. work]1006.3 (Cos, 3rd c.BC)]]; χρείζω [Refs 2nd c.BC+ [[prev. work]953.27 (Calymna, 2nd c.BC)]]: sicil. Doric dialect χρῄσδω [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [3rd c.BC: Theocritus Poeta Bucolicus 8.11]]; Megarian dialect Doric dialect χρῄδδω [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Acharnenses” 734]]: future χρῄσω [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-4th c.BC: Timaeus Locrus Philosophus 99a]], Ionic dialect χρηΐσω [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 7.38]]: aorist Ionic dialect χρηΐσαι probably [Refs [[prev. author] 5.65]]; participle χρηΐσας[Refs [[prev. work] 20, 7.38]]: (χρή):—want, lack, have need of, with genitive, χρηΐζοντα.. ἰητῆρος [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 11.835; εἴρετο.. ὅττευ χρηΐζων ἱκόμην 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 17.121, compare 558; οὐδ᾽ ἐμοῦ διδασκάλου χρῄζεις 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Prometheus Vinctus” 376]]; δύο χρῄσει [μεσοτάτων] [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-4th c.BC: Timaeus Locrus Philosophus]] [same place]: absolutely in participle χρηΐζων needy, poor, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 11.340, 8th-7th c.BC: Hesiodus Epicus “Opera et Dies” 351.]]

__2
desire, long for, crave, χρηΐζειν ἀπεόντος[Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. work] 367; τοῦτον ὦν δοκέω.. ποιήσειν ὧν ἂν χρηΐζωμεν 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 5.30; χρημάτων χ. [prev. author] 9.87; βορᾶς 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Choephori” 530]]; τοῦ μακροῦ χ. βίου Soph.[Refs 5th c.BC+ [“Aj.” 473: rarely with _accusative_, πᾶν μᾶλλον δοκέων μιν χρηΐσειν ἢ τὸ ἐδεήθη 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 7.38; ὥστ᾽ ἄλλα χρῄζειν 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Tyrannus” 595, compare 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Supplices” 123]]; an infinitive may frequently be supplied, φράζε.. ὅ τι χρῄζεις (i.e. φράζειν) [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Nubes” 359, compare 453 (both _anapaest meter_); ἴθ᾽ ὅποι χρῄζεις (i.e. ἰέναι) [prev. work] 891 (_anapaest meter_),compare “Th.” 751, 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Prometheus Vinctus” 928, 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Tyrannus” 365]]; τί δῆτα χρῄζει;[Refs [[prev. work] 622, “OC” 643.]]

__2.b
with accusative person et infinitive, ask or desire that one should do a thing, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.41, 112, 152, +others]]; so with genitive person et infinitive, desire of one to do, [Refs [[prev. author] 5.19, 65, 9.55]]; in Trag., with infinitive only, desire to do a thing, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Prometheus Vinctus” 235, 285, +others, 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Tyrannus” 91, 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Hecuba” 347, etc.: rare in Prose, 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 3.109, 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 1.6.15.]]

__2.c
with double genitive person et of things, τῶνδε ἐγὼ ὑμέων χρηΐζων συνέλεξα hdt.[Refs [7.53.]]

__2.d
χρῄζειν παρά τινος with infinitive, Ps.-[Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus “Vitae Homeri” 17.]]

__3
participle χρῄζων is used absolutely for εἰ χρῄζει, if one will, if one chooses, [Refs 6th c.BC+ [6th c.BC: Theognis Elegiacus 958, 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Choephori” 340 (_anapaest meter_)]]; ἄλλα φανεῖ χρῄζων (i.e. Ἑρμῆς) if propitious, [Refs [[prev. work] [815] (Lyric poetry)]]; ἢν τὸν θεὸν χρῄζοντ᾽ ἔχῃ [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Supplices” 597]]; ποταγγελλέτω ὁ χρῄζων, ={ὁ βουλόμενος}, [Refs [“IG” 12(1).677.34 (from Ialysus)]]; also τὸ χρῇζον your solicitation, E.IA 1017.

__II
passive, χρησθείς is falsa lectio in [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Antigone” 24.]]

χρῆμα, ατος, τό:
(χράομαι):— need, in the phrase παρὰ χ. or παραχρῆμα (which see); a thing that one needs or uses,[Refs 5th c.BC+ [compare 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Oeconomicus” 1.9f (_plural_)]]: hence in plural, goods, property (χρήματα λέγομεν πάντα ὅσων ἡ ἀξία νομίσματι μετρεῖται [Refs 8th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Ethica Nicomachea” 1119b26), 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 2.78, 203, +others (never in 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad”), 8th-7th c.BC: Hesiodus Epicus “Opera et Dies” 320, 407, etc.]]; of temple-treasures, heirlooms, etc., [Refs 6th c.BC+ [“Mnemos.” 57.208 (Argos, 6th c.BC)]]; τὰ ἱρὰ χ. τῆς Ἀθηναίης [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 2.28, compare 9.81; θησαυρούς.. ἄλλα τε χρύσεα ἄφατα χ. [prev. author] 7.190; πολλῶν χ. ἐξαίρετον ἄνθος 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Agamemnon” 954; πειρῶ τὸν πλοῦτον χρήματακαὶ κτήματα κατασκευάζειν· ἔστι δὲ χ. μὲν τοῖς ἀπολαύειν ἐπισταμένοις, κ. δὲ τοῖς κτᾶσθαι δυναμένοις 5th-6th c.BC: Isocrates Orator 1.28; τοῖς σκεύεσι καὶ τοῖς χρήμασιν ἀποθήκη 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 6.97]]; πρόβατα καὶ ἄλλα χ. [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 5.2.4; τὰ ἀνδράποδα.. καὶ χρήματα τὰ πλεῖστα ἀπέδρα αὐτούς [prev. work] 7.8.12: proverbial, χρήματα ψυχὴ πέλεται.. βροτοῖσι]] a man's money is his life, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th-7th c.BC: Hesiodus Epicus “Opera et Dies” 686]]; χρήματ᾽ ἄνηρ 'money makes the man', [Refs 7th c.BC+ [7th-6th c.BC: Alcaeus Lyricus 49, 5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “I.” 2.11; ἐν χρήμασιν οἰκεῖ πατρώοις 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Eumenides” 757, compare “Ch.” 135; also χρημάτων πένητες 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Electra” 37; τὰ χρήματ᾽ ἐνεχυράζομαι 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Nubes” 241; χρήματα πορίζειν [prev. author] “Ec.” 236; ἄτιμοι ἦσαν τὰ σώματα, τὰ δὲ χ. εἶχον 5th-6th c.BC: Andocides Orator 1.74; χρημάτων ἥσσων 3rd c.AD: Democritus Epigrammaticus 50; χρημάτων κρείσσων 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 2.60; χρήμασι νικώμενος [prev. passage]; χρημάτων ἀδωρότατος [prev. work] 65; ἐλπίδα χρήμασιν ὠνητήν [prev. author] 3.40; μήτε χρημάτων φειδομένους μήτε πόνων 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Phaedo” 78a; ζημιοῦσθαι χρήμασιν [prev. author] “Lg.” 721b]]; even of debts, διαλῦσαι τὰ χ. [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 20.12; δεθέντ᾽ ἐπὶ χρήμασιν ἐν τῷ δεσμωτηρίῳ [prev. author] 24.168.—Acc. to 2nd c.AD(?): Pollianus Epigrammaticus 9.87 the _Ionic dialect_ used also the _sing._ in this sense, and so we find, ἐπὶ κόσῳ ἂν χρήματι..]]; for how much money.. ? Answ. ἐπ᾽ οὐδενί, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 3.38; ταύτην (i.e. τὴν χλανίδα) πωλέω μὲν οὐδενὸς χ. δίδωμι δὲ ἄλλως [prev. work] 139]]; also in [Refs 6th c.BC+ [6th c.BC: Theognis Elegiacus 197]], χ. δ᾽ ὃ μὲν Διόθεν καὶ σὺν δίκῃ ἀνδρὶ γένητα; in Attic dialect, οὐδενὸς ἂν χ. δεξάμενοι at no price, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Andocides Orator 2.4]]; and in later Prose, fund, sum of money, Arch. f. Religionswiss.[Refs 2nd c.BC+ [10.211 (Cos, 2nd c.BC)]]; τὸ πλῆθος τοῦ χ. [NT+1st c.BC+ [1st c.BC: Diodorus Siculus Historicus 13.106, cf. NT.Act.4.37, 2nd c.AD: Lucianus Sophista “VH” 1.20; χρήματα]]merchandise, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [1st c.AD(?): Heraclitus 90, 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Historia Graeca (Hellenica)” 1.6.37, 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 3.74]]; property, substance, [Refs [Berl.Sitzb. 1927.161 (from Cyrene).]]

__II
generally, thing, matter, affair, especially in Epic dialect and Ionic dialect, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [“hymnus ad Mercurium” 332, 8th-7th c.BC: Hesiodus Epicus “Opera et Dies” 344, 402; χρημάτων ἄελπτον οὐδέν 7th c.BC: Archilochus Lyricus 74; πάντων χ. δικαιότατον 6th c.BC: Mimnermus Lyricus 8; πρῶτον χρημάτων πάντων 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 7.145]]; ἀντὶ πάντων χ. on every account, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Andocides Orator 2.21; δεινότατον ἁπάντων χρημάτων [prev. work] 1]]; πᾶν χ. ἐκίνεε 'left no stone unturned', [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 5.96]]; τεκμαίρει χρῆμ᾽ ἕκαστον 'deeds show the man', [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “O.” 6.74; πάντων χ. μέτρον ἄνθρωπος 5th c.BC: Protagoras Philosophus 1]]; περαίνεται τὸ χ. the issue is being decided, [Refs 1st c.AD+ [1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus “Caesar” 47]]: plural, simply, things, ὁμοῦ πάντα χ. ἦν [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Anaxagoras Philosophus 1, compare 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Cratylus” 440a, “Euthd.” 294d, 3rd c.AD: Plotinus Philosophus 4.2.1.]]

__II.2
χρῆμα is frequently expressed where it might be omitted, δεινὸν χ. ἐποιεῦντο [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 8.16; οἷόν τι χ. ποιήσειε [prev. work] 138]]; ἐς ἀφανὲς χ. ἀποστέλλειν ἀποικίην to send out a colony without any certain destination, [Refs [[prev. author] 4.150]]; frequently in Trag., τί χρῆμ; ={τί}; what? τί χ. λεύσσ; [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Prometheus Vinctus” 300, “Ch.” 10]]; or why? [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Alcestis” 512]]; so in genitive, τοῦ χ. (i.e. ἕνεκα); [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Nubes” 1223; τί χ. δρᾷ; 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Ajax” 288, compare “Ph.” 1231; τί χ. πάσχε; 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Hippolytus” 909]]; τί δ᾽ ἐστὶ χρῆμ; what is the matter? [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Choephori” 885; πικρόν τί μοι δοκεῖ χ. εἶναι 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Gorgias” 485b; ἡδύ [prev. author] “Tht.” 209e, +others]]; μάλιστα χρημάτων most of anything, i. e. certainly, [Refs 3rd c.AD+ [Anonymus “Oxy.” 1611.68 (3rd c.AD);compare χρέος 11.2.]]

__II.3
used in periphrases to express something strange or extraordinary of its kind, ὑὸς χ. μέγα a huge monster of a boar, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.36; ἦν τοῦ χειμῶνος χ. ἀφόρητον [prev. author] 7.188]]; τὸ χ. τῶν νυκτῶν ὅσον what a business the nights are! [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Nubes” 2]]; λιπαρὸν τὸ χ. τῆς πόλεως what a grand city! [Refs [[prev. author] “Av.” 826, compare “Lys.” 83]]; κλέπτον τὸ χ. τἀνδρός a thievish sort of fellow, [Refs [[prev. author] “V.” 933; τὸ χ. τοῦ νοσήματος [prev. author] “Lys.” 1085]]; μακάριον.. λέγεις τυράννου χ. your tyrant-creature, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 567e; χ. θαυμαστὸν γυναικός 1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus “Antonius” 31]]: without a genitive, ἔλαφον, καλόν τι χ. καὶ μέγα [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 1.4.8]]; σοφόν τοι χρῆμ᾽ ἄνθρωπος truly a clever creature is he! [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [3rd c.BC: Theocritus Poeta Bucolicus 15.83]]; κοῦφον χ. ποιητής ἐστιν καὶ πτηνὸν καὶ ἱερόν, of the poet, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Ion” 534b]]; χ. καλόν τι such a fine thing! [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [3rd c.BC: Theocritus Poeta Bucolicus 15.23]]; also in a periphrastic use, οὐδὲν χ. τοῦ ἀγκῶνος κάμψαι δύνανται cannot bend the elbow at all, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Hippocrates Medicus “περὶ ἀγμῶν” 42.]]

__II.3.b
so, to express a great number or mass, as we say, a deal, a heap of.., πολλόν τι χ. τῶν τέκνων, χ. πολλὸν ἀρδίων, νεῶν, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 3.109, 4.81, 6.43; χ. πολλόν τι χρυσοῦ [prev. author] 3.130; σμικρὸν τὸ χ. τοῦ βίου 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Supplices” 953]]; ὅσον τὸ χ. παρνόπων what a lot of locusts! [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Acharnenses” 150; ὅσον τὸ χ. τοῦ πλακοῦντος [prev. author] “Eq.” 1219; πολὺ χ. τεμαχῶν [prev. author] “Pl.” 894]]; τὸ χ. τῶν κόπων ὅσον what a lot of them! [Refs [[prev. author] “Ra.” 1278; τῶν λαμπάδων ὅσον τὸ χ. [prev. author] “Th.” 281]]; also of persons, χ. θηλειῶν womankind, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Phoenissae” 198; σφενδονητῶν πάμπολύ τι χ. 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 2.1.5; μέγα χ. Λακαινᾶν 3rd c.BC: Theocritus Poeta Bucolicus 18.4: without a _genitive_, ὅσον τὸ χ. ἐπὶ δεῖπνον ἦλθε]] what a crowd.. ! [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Pax” 1192.]]

__III
(χράω (B) A) oracle, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Empedocles Poeta Philosophus 115.1.]]

Abbott-Smith / STEPBible (TBESG)
χρηματίζω
(χρῆμα), [in LXX: Jer.26:2 29:23 30:2 36:2, 4 A (דָבַר pi.), Jer.25:30) (שָׁאַג), 3Ki.18:27, Job.40:8 * ;]
__1. to transact business, hence, to consult, deliberate (Thuc., Dem., al.); hence in later writers,
__2. to make answer (esp. of offcial pronounce­ments by magistrates, etc.; in π. of the royal reply to an ἔντευξις, which see; cf. Deiss., BS, 122); of an answer by an oracle (Died., Plut., al.); in FlJ, LXX and NT, of divine communications, to instruct, admonish,  warn: pass. (Bl., § 54, 3), Mat.2:22, Heb.8:5 11:7 12:25; with inf. (Bl., § 69,4; 70, 3; 72, 5), Mat.2:12, Luk.2:26, Act.10:22
__3. to assume a name (as in business), be called (Polyb., al.): Act.11:26, Rom.7:3 (gnomic fut.; cf. Burton, § 69).†
(AS)
