LSJ / STEPBible (TFLSJ)
ὠδίνω [ῑ],
used by early writers only in present: future ὠδῑνήσω [LXX.Hab.3.10]: aorist ὤδῑνα [LXX+3rd c.AD+ [“Anthologia Graeca” 7.561 (Jul.Aeg.), 3rd c.AD: Oppianus Apamensis Epicus “Cynegetica” 1.5, 4th c.AD: Julianus Imperator “Orationes” 2.56d; ὠδίνησα LXX.Psa.7.15:—so]]aorist middle and passive, ὠδινησάμην, -ήθην, [LXX+2nd c.AD+ [2nd c.AD: Aquila LXX.Psa.113(114).7, LXX.Pro.8.25]]:—to have the pains of childbirth, be in travail, ὡς δ᾽ ὅταν ὠδίνουσαν ἔχῃ βέλος ὀξὺ γυναῖκα [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 11.269; ὠδίνειν τρομέω· χαλεπὸν βέλος Εἰλειθυίας 3rd c.BC: Theocritus Poeta Bucolicus 27.29, compare 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Thesmophoriazusae” 502, “Ec.” 529, 5th c.BC: Hippocrates Medicus “ἐπιδημίαι” 5.25, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 395e, etc.]]

__2
with accusative, to be in travail of a child, bring forth, [LXX+5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Iphigenia Aulidensis” 1234, LXX.Cant.8.5: of animals, ὠ. νεοττούς 2nd-3rd c.AD: Aelianus “De Natura Animalium - Ar.Byzantine Epit.” 2.46: proverbial, ὤδινεν ὄρος 2nd c.AD: Lucianus Sophista “Hist.Conscr.” 23.]]

__II
metaphorically of any great pain, to be in travail or anguish, of the Cyclops, στενάχων τε καὶ ὠδίνων ὀδύνῃσι [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 9.415; Κύπριδι “Anthologia Graeca” 7.30 (2nd c.BC: Antipater Sidonius Epigrammaticus)]]; labour painfully, ὠδίνουσι μέλισσαι [Refs 1st c.BC+ [[prev. work] 9.363.22 (1st c.BC: Meleager Epigrammaticus (?))]]; of the mind, to be in the throes or agonies of thought, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Theaetetus” 148e, +others]]; κυοῦμέν τε καὶ ὠ. περὶ ἐπιστήμης [Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. work] 210b; ὑπὲρ δισσῶν μίαν ὠδίνειν ψυχήν 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Hippolytus” 258 (_anapaest meter_)]]; ὥστε μ᾽ ὠδίνειν τί φῄς what you mean, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Ajax” 794, compare 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Heraclidae” 644]]; ὠδίνειν εἴς τι to long painfully for a thing, [Refs 3rd c.AD+ [3rd c.AD: Heliodorus Scriptor Eroticus 5.32]]: with infinitive, [Refs 3rd c.AD+ [[prev. author] 2.21, 4th c.AD: Himerius Sophista “Eclogae” 13.38, “Or.” 4.1: with _accusative_, 3rd c.AD: Heliodorus Scriptor Eroticus 10.31; ἔξοδον 6th c.AD: Choricius Rhetor 42.20 p.517 F.-R.]]

__II.b
worry, fuss, ὠδίνοντα μήποτε λήγειν περὶ τοῦ σώματος [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 407c.]]

__II.2
with accusative, to be in travail with, συμφορᾶς βάρος [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Trachiniae” 325; τὴν καύχησιν τὴν σοφιστικήν 4th-3rd c.BC: Epicurus Philosophus “Fragmenta” 93, compare “Anthologia Graeca” 9.578 (5th c.AD: Leo Philosophus Epigrammaticus) (where ὧν is in the case of the antecedent by attraction).]]

__II.3
Causal, cause to quiver, as in travail, φωνὴ βροντῆς ὠδίνησε γῆν [LXX+2nd c.AD+ [LXX.Sir.43.17(18) codex 2nd c.AD: Alexander Rhetor]]

(see. entry near the end):— the shoulder with the upper arm (ὠλένη being the lower), ξίφεϊ κληῗδα παρ᾽ ὦμον πλῆξ᾽, ἀπὸ δ᾽ αὐχένος ὦμον ἐέργαθεν ἠδ᾽ ἀπὸ νώτου [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 5.146, compare 8.325, 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 4.62; μεταφρένῳ ἐν δόρυ πῆξεν ὤμων μεσσηγύς 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 5.41; τεύχε᾽ ἀπ᾽ ὤμων συλήσειν 15.544; ὦμος στιβαρός, ὦμοι ἴφθιμοι, 5.400, 18.204; εὐρέες 3.210; κυρτώ 2.217; ἀμφ᾽ ὤμοισιν ἔχει σάκος 11.527, compare 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Fragmenta” 453; ἐπ᾽ ὤμου.. φέρειν 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 10.170, compare 5th-6th c.BC: Isocrates Orator 19.39; ἀρεῖτ᾽ ἐπ᾽ ὤμου 3rd c.BC: Herodas Mimographus 3.61]]; κατ᾽ ὤμου δεῖρον [Refs 8th c.BC+ [[prev. work] 3; ἐπ᾽ ὤμων πατέρ᾽ ἔχων 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Fragmenta” 373; τὰ ὦτα ἐπὶ τῶν ὤμων ἔχειν 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 613c; ὤμοισι φόρησεν 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 19.11; ἑλὼν.. σάκος ὤμῳ 15.474; ὤμῳ or ὤμοισιν ἔχειν, 14.376, 1.45, +others]]; ὤμοις or ἐπ᾽ ὤμοις φέρειν, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Fragmenta” 454, “Tr” 564; ἔχειν ἀνὰ φαιδίμῳ ὤμῳ 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 11.128, 23.275; λαβὼν.. ὦμον εἰς ἀριστερόν 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Iphigenia Taurica” 1381; ἐπ᾽ ὤμοις θεῖναι [prev. author] “Ba.” 755; κίον᾽ οὐρανοῦ.. ὤμοις ἐρείδων 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Prometheus Vinctus” 350]]; ὤμοισι τοῖσι ἐμοῖσι 'by the strength of mine arms', [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 2.106]]; ἀποστρέψαι τὸν ὦ. to dislocate it, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Equites” 263 (troch.); ὁ δ᾽ ὦμος.. πιέζεται [prev. author] “Ra.” 30; τὸν ὦμον θλίβομαι [prev. author] “fragment” 323: _plural_ for _sing._, ὤμοις ἀριστεροῖσιν ἀνακλάσας δέρην 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Orestes” 1471.]]

__b
the shoulder is sometimes more exactly specified as πρυμνότατος or πρυμνὸς ὦμος, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 17.462, 504; νείατος ὦ. 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 15.341, 17.310]]; sometimes opposed to χείρ (the arm), χεῖρες ὤμων.. ἐπαΐσσονται [Refs 8th c.BC+ [23.628; τῶν ἑκατὸν μὲν χεῖρες ἀπ᾽ μων ἀΐσσοντο 8th-7th c.BC: Hesiodus Epicus “Theogonia” 150]]; τοὺς ὤμους ἀποταμόντες σὺν τῇσι χερσί (arms) [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 4.62; ἀποταμόντα ἐν τῷ ὤμῳ τὴν χεῖρα [prev. author] 2.121.έ,compare 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Bacchae” 1127, 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Historia Animalium” 493b26.]]

__2
also of animals. as of a horse, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 6.510, 15.267, 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “de Equitandi ratione” 8.6]]; of a lion, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th-7th c.BC: Hesiodus Epicus “Scutum Herculis” 430]]; of a dog, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Cynegeticus” 4.1]]; of crabs, [Refs [Batrachomyomachia 296]]; of birds, [Refs 1st c.AD+ [1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus 2.983b]]; of ants, [Refs [“Geoponica” 13.10.14.]]

__3
the shoulder, in a dress, ἐπὶ τῶν ὤμων τῆς ἐπωμίδος [LXX+4th c.BC+ [LXX.Exo.28.12, compare 25(29); ἐπὶ τῷ ὤμῳ τοῦ χιτῶνος ὑποθέντες 4th c.BC: Aeneas Tacticus 31.23 codices (ἐπὶ τῇ ᾤᾳ conjecture Haupt).]]

__II
metaphorically of the parts below the top or head of any thing, especially of the fork of a vine (compare ὠμοχάραξ), [Refs [“Geoponica” 4.12.4]]; of the womb, Heroph. cited in [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd c.AD: Galenus Medicus 4.596, compare 2nd c.AD: Rufus Medicus “περὶ ὀνομασίας” 195]]. (Cf. Latin umerus (from *omesos), Gothic ams (stem amsa-), Sanskrit áṃsas, also Aeolic dialect ἐπ-ομμάδιος, and (non-Greek) ἀμέσω [Refs 5th c.AD+ [5th c.AD(?): Hesychius Legal icographus)]]

Abbott-Smith / STEPBible (TBESG)
εἰμί,
with various uses and significations, like the English verb to be.
__I. As substantive verb.
__1. Of persons and things, to be, exist: Act.17:28, Jhn.1:1, 8:58, 17:5, al; ὁ ὢν καὶ ὁ ἦν (for past ptcp.), Rev.1:4, 8, 4:8, 11:17, 16:5 (see Swete, Ap., 5; M, Pr., 228); τὰ (μὴ) ὄντα, Rom.4:17, 1Co.1:28.
__2. Of times, events, etc., to be, happen, take place: Mat.24:3, Mrk.14:2, 15:42, Luk.21:23, Jhn.4:6, 23, 5:10, al.
__3. to be present, be in a place, have come: Mat.2:13, 15, Mrk.1:45, 5:21, 15:40, Luk.1:80, 5:29, Jhn.7:30, al.; before εἰς, Mrk.2:1; before  ἐκ, (ἐξ), Mat.1:20, 21:25, Mrk.11:30, Jhn.3:31, al.
__4. Impers.,  ἔστι, ἦν, etc.;
__(a) there is (Fr. il y a), was, etc.: Mat.16:28, Luk.16:19, Jhn.3:1, 5:2, Rom.3:10, al.; with dative (of the possessor; Bl., §37, 3), Mat.16:22, Luk.1:7, Jhn.18.10, Rom.9:2, al.;  ἔστιν ὅς, ὅστις (chiefly in pl), Mat.16:28, 19:2, Mrk.9:1, al.;
__(b) with inf., = ἔξεστιν (which see), it is possible: Heb.9:5, 1Co.11:20, RV (but see ICC, in l.).
__II. As copula uniting subject and predicate.
__1. Expressing simply identity or equivalence: Mat.5:13, 14:15, Luk.1:18, 19, Jhn.1:1, 4:19, Rev.3:9, al. mult.
__2. Explicative, as in parable, figure, type, etc.: Mat.13:19, 1Co.9:2, 10:4, 11:25, Gal.4:24, Rev.17:15, al.; ταῦτ᾽ ἔστιν, Mat.27:46, Mrk.7:2, Rom.7:18 al.; ὅ ἐστιν, Mrk.3:17, Col.1:24, Heb.7:2, al.; akin to this is the sacramental usage: Mat.26:26-28, Mrk.14:22, 24, Luk.22:19, 1Co.11:24 (see ICC on Mk, I Co, ll. with; DB, iii, 148 f.).
__3. C. genitive: qual., etc., Mrk.5:42, Luk.3:23, 1Co.14:33, Heb.12:11, al.; part., 1Ti.1:20, 2Ti.1:15; poss., Mat.5:3, 10, Mrk.12:7, Luk.4:7; of service or partisanship, Rom.8:9, 1Co.1:12, 2Co.10:7, 2Ti.2:19.
__4. C. dative (BL, §37, 3): Act.1:8, 9:15, Rom.4:12, 1Co.1:18, 2:14, Rev.21:7, al.
__5. C. ptcp., as a periphrasis for the simple verb (Bl., §62, 1, 2; M, Pr., 225 ff.);
__(a) with ptcp. pf. (cl.): Mat.10:30, Luk.9:32, Jhn.3:24, Act.21:35, 1Co.15:19, al;
__(b) with ptcp. pr. (esp. in impf., as in Heb. and Aram.; Dalman, Words, 35 f.), Mat.7:29, Mrk.1:22, Luk.4:31, 14:1, Act.1:10, al. mult., id. for imper. (M, Pr., 180f., 182f.), with ellipsis of εἰμί, Rom.12:9, 10, Heb.13:5, al.;
__(with) with ptcp. aor. (cl), Luk.23:9.
__6. Seq. εἰς (cf. Heb. הָיָה לְ), a vernac. usage (M, Pr., 71): Mat.19:5, Mrk.10:8, Heb.8:10, al.
__7. C. adv.: Mat.19:20, Mrk.4:26, Luk.18:11, al.
__8. Ellipses;
__(a) of the copula (Bl., §30, 3): Mat.8:29, 24:32, Jhn.21:22, 23, Heb.6:4, al.;
__(b) of the predicate: ἐγώ εἰμί, Mat.14:27, Mrk.6:50, al.; absol. (cf. Deu.32:39; אֲנִי הוּא), Mrk.13:6, Jhn.4:26, al. (cf. ἄπ-, ἔν-, πάρ-, συμ-πάρ-, σύν-ειμι).
(AS)

__A
as the substantive Verb,

__A.I

__A.II
of the real world, be, opposed to become, γίγνεται πάντα ἃ δή φαμεν εἶναι [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Theaetetus” 152d, etc.]]; τὸ ὄν [Refs 5th c.BC+ [“Being”, 4th-5th c.BC: Parmenides Poeta Philosophus 8.35, 5th c.BC: Protagoras Philosophus 2, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Timaeus” 27d, etc.]]; opposed to τὸ μὴ ὄν, [LXX+5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Gorgias Rhetor et Sophista “fragment” 3 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator, etc.; οὐδὲν γίνεται ἐκ τοῦ μὴ ὄντος 4th-3rd c.BC: Epicurus Philosophus “Epistulae” 1p.5U.; ἐξ οὐκ ὄντων ἐποίησεν αὐτὰ ὁ θεός LXX.2Mac.7.28]]; τὰ ὄντα the world of things, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [1st c.AD(?): Heraclitus 7, 5th c.BC: Empedocles Poeta Philosophus 129.5, etc.]]; ὄνindeclinable, τῶν ὂν εἰδῶν species of Being, [Refs 3rd c.AD+ [3rd c.AD: Plotinus Philosophus 6.2.10.]]

__A.II.2
of circumstances, events, etc., to happen, τά τ᾽ ἐόντα, τά τ᾽ ἐσσόμενα, πρό τ᾽ ἐόντα [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 1.70; ἡ ἐσβολὴ ἔμελλεν ἔσεσθαι 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 2.13, etc.]]; τῆς προδοσίας οὔσης since treachery was there, [Refs [[prev. author] 4.103]]; ἕως ἂν ὁ πόλεμος ᾖ so long as it last, [Refs [[prev. author] 1.58; αἱ σπονδαὶ ἐνιαυτὸν ἔσονται [prev. author] 4.118]]; τί ἐστι; what is it? what's the matter? [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Thesmophoriazusae” 193]]; τί οὖν ἦν τοῦτ; how came it to pass? [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Phaedo” 58a: repeated with a _relative_ to avoid a positive assertion, ἔστι δ᾽ ὅπῃ νῦν ἔ.]] things are as they are, i.e. are ill, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Agamemnon” 67.]]

__A.III
be the fact or the case, διπλασίαν ἂν τὴν δύναμιν εἰκάζεσθαι ἤ ἐστιν twice as large as it really is, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 1.10]]; αὐτὸ ὅ ἐστι καλόν beauty in its essence, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Symposium” 211c, compare “Phd.” 74b]]; frequently in participle, τὸν ἐόντα λόγον λέγειν or φαίνειν the true story, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.95, 116]]; τῷ ἐόντι χρήσασθαι tell the truth,[Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. work] 30; τὰ ὄντα ἀπαγγέλλειν 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 7.8]]; σκῆψιν οὐκ οὖσαν, λόγον οὐκ ὄντα, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Electra” 584, 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Ranae” 1052]]; τῷ ὄντι in reality, in fact, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Protagoras” 328d, etc.]]; to apply a quotation to a case in point, τῷ ὄντι κλαυσίγελως real 'smiles through tears' (with allusion to [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 6.484), 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Historia Graeca (Hellenica)” 7.2.9, compare 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Laches” 196d]]; κατὰ τὸ ἐόν according to the fact, rightly, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.97]]; πᾶν τὸ ἐόν the whole truth, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. author] 9.11; τοῦ ἐόντος ἀποτεύξεται 5th c.BC: Hippocrates Medicus “περὶ ἀρχαίης ἰητρικῇς” 2.]]

__A.IV
followed by the relative, οὐκ ἔστιν ὅς or ὅστις no one, οὐκ ἔσθ᾽ ὃς.. ἀπαλάλκοι [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 22.348; οὐκ ἔ. οὐδεὶς ὅς 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Electra” 903]]; οὐκ ἔ. ὅτῳ, ={οὐδενί}, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Prometheus Vinctus” 293 (_anapaest meter_), compare 989: frequently in _plural_, εἰσὶν οἵ]], = Latin sunt qui, used exactly like{ἔνιοι}, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 6.88, 7.44, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Meno” 77d, “Grg.” 503a, etc. (εἰσί τινες οἵ.. 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 3.24)]]; __A.V
ἦν is sometimes used with plural masculine and feminine, usually at the beginning of a sentence, there was, τῆς δ᾽ ἦν τρεῖς κεφαλαί [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th-7th c.BC: Hesiodus Epicus “Theogonia” 321; (but in ἦν δ᾽ ἐρῳδιοί τε πολλοί 5th c.BC: Epicharmus Comicus 46, compare 59, +others, it may be taken as _Doric dialect_ _3rd.pers._ _plural_)]]; ἦν δ᾽ ἀμφίπλεκτοι κλίμακες [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Trachiniae” 520 (Lyric poetry)]]; ἦν ἄρα κἀκεῖνοι ταλακάρδιοι epigram cited in [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aeschines Orator 3.184; less frequently ἔστι, ἔστι δὲ μεταξὺ.. ἑπτὰ στάδιοι 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.26, compare 7.34; ἔστι.. ἄρχοντές τε καὶ δῆμος 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 463a]]; before dual Nouns, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Vespae” 58, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Gorgias” 500d.]]

__A.VI
ἔστι impersonal, with infinitive, it is possible, ἔστι γὰρ ἀμφοτέροισιν ὀνείδεα μυθήσασθαι [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 20.246; ἔστι μὲν εὕδειν, ἔστι δὲ τερπομένοισιν ἀκούειν 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 15.392]]; εἴ τί πού ἐστι (i.e. πιθέσθαι)[Refs 5th c.BC+ [4.193; τοιάδε.. ἐστὶν ἀκοῦσαι 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Prometheus Vinctus” 1055 (_anapaest meter_); ἔστι τεκμήρια ὁρᾶν 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 3.2.13, compare 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Ranae” 1163, 4th c.BC: Aeschines Orator 3.105, 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 18.272, 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Ἀθηναίων Πολιτεία” 53.6, etc.]]; so in imperative, optative, and subjunctive, ἔστω ἀποφέρεσθαι τῷ βουλομένῳ [Refs 8th c.BC+ [“IG” 12.10.7; μυρία ἂν εἴη λέγειν 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Politicus” 271e; ὅπως ἂν ᾖ δρᾶν “IG” 2.1054.91: more frequently in _negative_ clauses, 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 6.267, etc.]]; followed by ὥστε with infinitive, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Philoctetes” 656]]: with accusative et infinitive, ἁδόντα δ᾽ εἴη με τοῖς ἀγαθοῖς ὁμιλεῖν [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “P.” 2.96; ἔστιν ἐκπεσεῖν ἀρχῆς Δία 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Prometheus Vinctus” 757]]: sometimes not impersonal in this sense, θάλασσα δ᾽ οὐκέτ᾽ ἦν ἰδεῖν [Refs [[prev. author] “Pers.” 419.]]

__A.VI.b
ἔστω in argument, let it be granted, ἔστω τοῦτο ἀληθὲς εἶναι [Refs 4th c.BC+ [1st c.BC: Dionysius Halicarnassensis “de Compositione Verborum” 25; ἔστω σοι τοῦθ᾽ οὕτως 1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus 2.987b; ἔστω εἶναί τινα τοιοῦτον 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator Chr.74.24.]]

__B
most frequently, to be, the Copula connecting the predicate with the Subject, both being in the same case: hence, signify, import, τὸ γὰρ εἴρειν λέγειν ἐστίν [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Cratylus” 398d]]; especially in the phrase τοῦτ᾽ ἔστι, hoc est; Σκαιόλαν, ὅπερ ἐστὶ Λαϊόν [Refs 1st c.AD+ [1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus “Publicola” 17: with numerals, τὰ δὶς πέντε δέκα ἐστίν]] twice five are ten, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Memorabilia” 4.4.7]]; εἶναί τις or τι, to be somebody, something, be of some consequence, see at {τι; οὐδὲν εἶναι} [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 562d, etc.]]

__B.2
periphrastic with the Participle to represent the finite Verb: with perfect participle once in [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Homerus Epicus, τετληότες εἰμέν, for τετλήκαμεν, 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 5.873]]; so in Trag. and Attic dialect, ἦν τεθνηκώς, for ἐτεθνήκει, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Agamemnon” 869]]; ἔσται δεδορκώς[Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. work] 1179; εἰμὶ γεγώς 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Ajax” 1299; πεφυκός ἐστι 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Aves” 1473; δεδρακότες εἰσίν 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 3.68; κατακεκονότες ἔσεσθε 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 7.6.36]]: with aorist participle, once in [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Homerus Epicus, βλήμενος ἦν 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 4.211]]; so προδείσας εἰμί, οὐ σιωπήσας ἔσε; [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Tyrannus” 90, 1146, compare 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Supplices” 460]]: with present participle, ἦν προκείμενον [Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. author] “Pers.” 371; φεύγων Ὀρέστης ἐστίν [prev. author] “Ch.” 136; εἴην οὐκ ἂν εὖ φρονῶν 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Ajax” 1330]]; τί δ᾽ ἐστί.. φέρο; [Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. author] “OT” 991, compare 274, 708; λέγων ἐστίν τις 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Hecuba” 1179; ἦν τίς σ᾽ ὑβρίζων [prev. author] “HF” 313; πόρρω ἤδη εἶ πορευόμενος 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Lysis” 204b; βαδίζων εἰμί 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Ranae” 36; frequently in 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus, ἦσαν ἱέντες 1.57, +others; even εἰσὶ διάφοροι ἐόντες 3.49 (assuming variant):]] — if the _Article_ is joined with the Part., the noun is made emphatic, Κᾶρές εἰσι οἱ καταδέξαντες the persons who showed her were Carians, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. author] 1.171; αὐτὸς ἦν ὁ μαρτυρῶν 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Eumenides” 798; δόλος ἦν ὁ φράσας 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Electra” 197 (_anapaest meter_).]]

__C
εἶναι is frequently modified in sense by the addition of adverbs, or the cases of Nouns without or with Preps.:

__C.I
εἶναι with adverbs, where the adverb often merely represents a Noun and stands as the predicate, ἅλις δέ οἱ ἦσαν ἄρουραι [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 14.122, etc.]]; ἀκέων, ἀκήν εἶναι, to be silent,[Refs 8th c.BC+ [4.22, 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 2.82; σῖγα πᾶς ἔστω λεώς 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Hecuba” 532; διαγνῶναι χαλεπῶς ἦν ἄνδρα ἕκαστον 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 7.424]]; ἀσφαλέως ἡ κομιδὴ ἔσται will go on safely, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 4.134]]; ἐγγύς, πόρρω εἶναι, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 6.88, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Protagoras” 356e: frequently _impersonal_ with words implying good or ill fortune, Κουρήτεσσι κακῶς ἦν]] it fared ill with them, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 9.551; εὖ γὰρ ἔσται 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Medea” 89, compare 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Plutus” 1188, etc.; ἡδέως ἂν αὐτοῖς εἴη 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 59.30.]]

__C.II
with genitive, to express descent or extraction, πατρὸς δ᾽ εἴμ᾽ ἀγαθοῖο [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 21.109; αἵματός εἰς ἀγαθοῖο 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 4.611, compare 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 3.71, 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 2.71, etc.; πόλεως μεγίστης εἶ 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 7.3.19.]]

__C.II.b
to express the material of which a thing is made, ἡ κρηπίς ἐστι λίθων μεγάλων consists of.., [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.93; τῆς πόλιος ἐούσης δύο φαρσέων [prev. work] 186]]; τοιούτων ἔργων ἐστὶ ἡ τυραννίς is made up of.., [Refs [[prev. author] 5.92]].ή, etc.

__C.II.c
to express the class to which a person or thing belongs, εἶ γὰρ τῶν φίλων you are one of them, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Plutus” 345; ἐτύγχανε βουλῆς ὤν 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 3.70; ὅσοι ἦσαν τῶν προτέρων στρατιωτῶν [prev. author] 7.44; Κριτίας τῶν τριάκοντα ὤν 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Memorabilia” 1.2.31]]; ἔστι τῶν αἰσχρῶν it is in the class of disgraceful things, i. e. it is disgraceful, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 2.2.]]

__C.II.d
to express that a thing belongs to another, Τροίαν Ἀχαιῶν οὖσαν [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Agamemnon” 269; τὸ πεδίον ἦν μέν κοτε Χορασμίων 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 3.117, etc.]]: hence, to be of the party of, ἦσαν.. τινὲς μὲν φιλίππου, τινὲς δὲ τοῦ βελτίστου [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 9.56, compare 37.53]]; to be de pendent upon, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Antigone” 737, etc.]]; to be at the mercy of, ἔστι τοῦ λέγοντος, ἢν φόβους λέγῃ [Refs [[prev. author] “OT” 917.]]

__C.II.e
to express one's duty, business, custom, nature, and the like, οὔτοι γυναικός ἐστι 'tis not a woman's part, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Agamemnon” 940; τὸ ἐπιτιμᾶν παντὸς εἶναι 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 1.16]]; τὸ δὲ ναυτικὸν τέχνης ἐστίν is matter of art, requires art, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 1.142, compare 83.]]

__C.II.f
in LXX, to be occupied about, ἦσαν τοῦ θύειν [LXX.2Ch.30.17]; ἔσεσθαι, with genitive, to be about to, ἐσόμεθα τοῦ σῶσαί σε [LXX.2Ki.10.11.]

__C.III
with the dative, ἐστί μοι I have, frequently in [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Homerus Epicus, etc.]]

__C.III.2
with two datives., σφίσι τε καὶ Ἀθηναίοισι εἶναι οὐδὲν πρῆγμα that they and the Athenians have nothing to do one with another, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 5.84; μηδὲν εἶναι σοὶ καὶ φιλίππῳ πρᾶγμα 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 18.283]]; more shortly, σοί τε καὶ τούτοισι πρήγμασι τί ἐστ; [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 5.33]]; τί τῷ νόμῳ καὶ τῇ βασάν; [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 29.36]]; τί ἐμοὶ καὶ σο; Latin quid tecum est mihi? [NT.Mark.5.7, etc.]; also ἐμοὶ οὐδὲν πρὸς τοὺς τοιούτους (i.e. ἐστίν) [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Isocrates Orator 4.12; ἐν οἷς πρὸς τοὺς ἐναντίους ἐστὶ τῷ δήμῳ 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 18.278]]; ἔσται αὐτῳ πρὸς τὸν θεόν, in tomb inscriptions, [Refs [“JHS” 18.113, etc.]]

__C.III.3
with ἄσμενος, βουλόμενος, etc., added, ἐμοὶ δέ κεν ἀσμένῳ εἴη 'twould be to my delight, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 14.108; οὐκ ἂν σφίσι βουλομένοις εἶναι 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 7.35; προσδεχομένῳ [prev. author] 6.46; θέλοντι 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Tyrannus” 1356 (Lyric poetry); ἡδομένοις 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Laches” 187c.]]

__C.IV
with Preps., εἶναι ἀπό τινος, ={εἶναί τινος}[Refs 5th c.BC+ [(above 11.a), 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Memorabilia” 1.6.9; εἰσὶν ἀπ᾽ ἐναντίων αὗται πραγμάτων 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Philebus” 12d]]; but εἶναι ἀπ᾽ οἴκου to be away from.., [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 1.99.]]

__C.IV.2
εἶναι ἔκ τινος to be sprung from, εἴμ᾽ ἐκ Παιονίης, Μυρμιδόνων ἔξ εἰμι, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 21.154, 24.397, etc.]]; ἔστιν ἐξ ἀνάγκης it is of necessity, i. e. necessary, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Sophista” 256d.]]

__C.IV.3
εἶναι ἐν.. to be in a certain state, ἐν εὐπαθείῃσι [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.22]]; ἐν ἀθυμία, etc., [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 6.46, etc.; ἐν ταραχαῖς 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 18.218]]; εἶναι ἐν ἀξιώματι to be in esteem, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 1.130]]; οἱ ἐν τέλεϊ ἐόντες those in office, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 3.18, etc.]]; but εἶναι ἐν τέχνῃ, ἐν φιλοσοφία to be engaged in.., [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Tyrannus” 562, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Phaedo” 59a.]]

__C.IV.3.b
ἐν σοί ἐστι it depends on thee, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 6.109, 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Philoctetes” 963; ἐν σοὶ γάρ ἐσμεν [prev. author] “OT” 314; so also ἐπί τινι [prev. author] “Ph.” 1003, 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 1.6.2, etc.]]

__C.IV.4
εἶναι διά.., much like{εἶναι ἐν}.., εἶναι διὰ φόβου, ={φοβεῖσθαι}, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 6.34]]; εἶναι δι᾽ ὄχλου, ={ὀχληρὸν εἶναι}, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. author] 1.73; εἶναι διὰ μόχθων 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 1.6.25]]; εἶναι δι᾽ αἰτίας, ={αἰτιᾶσθαι}, [Refs 1st c.BC+ [1st c.BC: Dionysius Halicarnassensis 1.70]]; Geometry texts, pass through, διὰ τᾶς ἑτέρας διαμέτρου ἐόντος τοῦ ἐπιπέδου [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [3rd c.BC: Archimedes Geometra “περὶ κωνοειδέων καὶ σφαιροειδέων” 20.]]

__C.IV.5
εἶναι ἐφ᾽ ἑαυτῆς to be by oneself, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 25.23]]; εἶναι ἐπὶ ὀνόματος to bear a name, [Refs [[prev. author] 39.21]]; εἶναι ἐπὶ τοῖς πράγμασιν to be engaged in.., [Refs [[prev. author] 2.12]]; εἶναι ἐπί τινα to be against him, [Refs [[prev. author] 6.33]]; εἶναι ἐφ᾽ ἑξήκοντα στάδια to reach sixty stadia, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 4.6.11]]; εἶναι ἐπὶ τὰς ἁφάς pass through the points of contact, [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd c.AD: Apollonius Biographus Perg. “Con.” 4.1]]; εἶναι ἐπί τινι, see above 3 b.

__C.IV.6
εἶναι πρός τινος to be in one's favour, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 4.10, 29, etc.]]; to suit, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 1.2.11, etc.]]; εἶναι πρός τινι engaged in, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Phaedo” 84c, 2nd-3rd c.AD: Philostratus Sophista “Vita Apollonii” 5.31]]; πρὸς τοῖς ἰδίοις mind one's own affairs, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Politica” 1309a6, “Ath.” 16.3; εἶναι πρὸς τὸ κωλύειν 2nd c.BC: Polybius Historicus 1.26.3]]; πρὸς τὸ πονεῖν[Refs 5th c.BC+ [Teles p.46 H.; εἶναι περί τι 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 3.5.7, etc.]]

__C.IV.7
εἶναι παρά τινι or τινα, = παρειναι, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. author] “Cyr.” 6.2.15, 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 8.140.ά]] (assuming variant).

__C.IV.8
εἶναι ὑπό τινα or τινι to be subject to.., [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Historia Graeca (Hellenica)” 5.2.17 (assuming variant), 6.2.4.]]

__C.IV.9
περὶ τούτων ἐστίν that is the question, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-3rd c.BC: Menander Comicus “Ἐπιτρέποντες” 30.]]

__C.IV.10
εἶναι ἀπό.., in Geometry texts, to be constructed upon, [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [3rd c.BC: Archimedes Geometra “περὶ σφαίρας καὶ κυλίνδρου” 2.9, “Con.Sph.” 7.]]

__D
ἐστί is very frequently omitted, mostly in the present indicative before certain predicates, as ἀνάγκη, ἄξιον, δυνατόν, εἰκός, ἕτοιμον, οἷόν τε, ῥᾴδιον, χρεών, etc., and after the neuter of Verbals in -τέος, and such forms as θαυμαστὸν ὅσον: less frequently with other persons and moods, εἰμί omitted, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Tyrannus” 92, “Aj.” 813]]; εἶ, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 4.206]]; ἐσμέν, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Antigone” 634]]; ἐστέ, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 10.463]]; εἰσί, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Tyrannus” 499 (Lyric poetry), “IG” 2.778 B]]; subjunctive ᾖ, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 14.376, 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Hippolytus” 659, 5th c.BC: Antipho Orator 5.32]]; optative εἴη, [Refs [“IG” 22.1183.12]]; imperfect ἦν, [Refs [[prev. work]2.778 B]]; future ἔσονται, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 14.394.]]

__E
the Inf. frequently seems redundant,

__E.1
in phrases implying power or will to do a thing, ἑκὼν εἶναι (see. ἑκών) κατὰ δύναμιν εἶναι [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Isaeus Orator 2.32; εἰς δύναμιν εἶναι 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Politicus” 300c]]; τὸ ἐπ᾽ ἐκείνοις εἶναι, quantum in illis esset, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 8.48, 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Historia Graeca (Hellenica)” 3.5.9, compare 5th c.BC: Lysias Orator 13.58; τὸ ἐπὶ σφᾶς εἶναι 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 4.28; τὸ κατὰ τοῦτον εἶναι 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 1.6.9; κατὰ τοῦτο εἶναι 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Protagoras” 317a]]; τὸ τήμερον, τὸ νῦν εἶναι, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [[prev. author] “Cra.” 396e, “La.” 201c, Theopomp. Comedy texts 98, Decrees cited in 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Ἀθηναίων Πολιτεία” 31.2, etc.]]

__E.2
after Verbs of naming or choosing, σοφιστὴν ὀνομάζουσι τὸν ἄνδρα εἶναι [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Protagoras” 311e; σύμμαχόν μιν εἵλοντο εἶναι 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 8.134]]; of giving, δῶκε ξεινήϊον εἶναι [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 11.20.]]

__F
imperfect ἦνissts. used where other languages take the present,

__F.1
after ἄρα, to express a fact which is and has always been the same, δέρμα δὲ ἀνθρώπου.. ἦν ἄρα σχεδὸν δερμάτων πάντων λαμπρότατον human skin then it appears is.., [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 4.64; Κύπρις οὐκ ἄρ᾽ ἦν θεός 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Hippolytus” 359]]; ὡς ἄρ᾽ ἦσθ᾽ ἐμὸς πατὴρ ὀρθῶς[Refs 3rd c.BC+ [[prev. work] 1169; ἦ πολύμοχθον ἄρ᾽ ἦν γένος.. ἁμερίων [prev. author] “IA” 1330; ἦ στωμύλος ἦσθα 3rd c.BC: Theocritus Poeta Bucolicus 5.79]]; so also when there is reference to a past thought, τουτὶ τί ἦ; what is this? [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Acharnenses” 157, compare 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Cratylus” 387c: so in the Aristotelian formula τὸ τί ἦν εἶναι (“APo.” 82b38, +others)]], used to express the essential nature of a thing, where τί ἦν (for ἐστί) takes the place of the dative in such phrases as τὸ ἀγαθῷ εἶναι, τὸ μεγέθει εἶναι, [Refs [“APr.” 67b12, “de An.” 429b10.]]

__G
ἐγώ εἰμι, in [LXX, pleonastic for ἐγώ, ἐγώ εἰμι οὐχ ἥμαρτον LXX.Judg.11.27, compare 6.18; also ἔσται πᾶς ἀποκτενεῖ με LXX.Gen.4.14.]

Abbott-Smith / STEPBible (TBESG)
ὠνέομαι, -οῦραι
to buy: ὠνήσατο (= cl. ἐπρίατο; see Rutherford, NPhr., 210 ff.; Veitch, see word), with genitive pret., Act.7:16.†
(AS)

---

LSJ / STEPBible (TFLSJ)
ὠνέομαι,
[Refs [8th-7th c.BC: Hesiodus Epicus “Opera et Dies” 341, etc.]]: future -ήσομαι [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Hecuba” 360, 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Acharnenses” 815, “Pax” 1261, 5th c.BC: Lysias Orator 22.22, _Doric dialect_ ὠνασοῦμαι (see. below)]]:—in Attic dialect usually with the syllabic augment, ἐωνούμην [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Eupolis Comicus 184, 5th-6th c.BC: Andocides Orator 1.134, ἀντ-εωνεῖτο 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Oeconomicus” 20.26, etc.: but ὠνέετο 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 3.139, ὠνέοντο [prev. author] 1.69, ὠνούμην 5th c.BC: Lysias Orator 7.4 codices, ἀντ-ωνεῖτο 5th-6th c.BC: Andocides Orator 1.134, ἐξ-ωνεῖτο 4th c.BC: Aeschines Orator 3.91]]: aorist 1 ἐωνησάμην [Refs 5th c.BC+ [1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus “Cicero” 3; ὠνησάμην 5th c.BC: Hippocrates Medicus “ἐπιστολαί” 17, 1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus “Nicias” 10, 2nd c.AD: Lucianus Sophista “Herm.” 81]]; participle ὠνησάμενος [Refs 2nd c.BC+ [2nd c.BC: Polybius Historicus 4.50.3, 1st c.BC: Dionysius Halicarnassensis 7.20: ὠνήσασθαι]] not in Attic inscriptions earlier than [Refs 1st c.BC+ [“IG” 22.1035.8 (1st c.BC), ἐπριάμην]] being used in Attic dialect; ὠνησάμην in the proverbial Χῖος δεσπότην ὠνήσατο [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Eupolis Comicus 269:]]perfect ἐώνημαι in active sense, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Plutus” 7, 5th c.BC: Lysias Orator 7.2]] (so pluperfect ἐώνητο [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 37.5)]]; also as passive (see. below 11): aorist in passive sense (see. below 11) ἐωνήθη; future in passive sense ἀπ-ωνηθήσεται [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Theopompus Comicus 84: this verb is usually replaced in later Gr. by ἀγοράζω]]:—buy, purchase, opposed to πωλέω, πιπράσκ; πῶ τις ὦν ὄνον ὠνασεῖτα; [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophron Comicus 125]]; but in present and imperfect (which are the tenses most in use), offer to buy, bargain or bid for a thing, ὄφρ᾽ ἄλλων ὠνῇ κλῆρον [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th-7th c.BC: Hesiodus Epicus “Opera et Dies” 341]]; ὠνέεσθαι τῶν φορτίων wished to buy some of their wares, began to bargain for them, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.1]]; Κροῖσός σφι ὠνεομένοισι ἔδωκε gave it them when they offered to buy, [Refs [[prev. work] 69; τὰς νήσους οὐκ ἐβούλοντο ὠνευμένοισι πωλέειν [prev. work] 165, compare 3.139, 6.121]]; ὀκτὼ λάβοις ἄν (i.e. ὀβολούς); Answ. εἴπερ ὠνεῖ τὸν ἕτερον if you are willing to buy the other fish, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [2nd c.AD: Alexander Rhetor 16.10, compare 78.7; ὠνεῖσθαι καὶ πωλεῖν πρὸς ἀλλήλους 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Leges” 741b; ὠ. τὰς γυναῖκας παρὰ τῶν γονέων 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 5.6, compare 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Protagoras” 313d, 313e, 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 9.48; ἀπό τινος 3rd c.AD(?): Achilles Tatius Astronomus 5.17]]: with dative person, buy from.., [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Acharnenses” 815, “Pax” 1261]]; also ὠ. ἐκ Κορίνθου buy goods from Corinth, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Historia Graeca (Hellenica)” 7.2.17: ὠ. ἐξ ἀγορᾶς [prev. author] “An.” 3.2.21]]; metaphorically, καιρόν, σπονδάς ὠ., [Refs 4th c.BC+ [1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus “Sertorius” 6, 2nd c.AD: Herodianus Grammaticus 6.7.9; ὠ. μὴ ἀδικεῖσθαι τοὺς ἐμπόρους 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 8.25]]; with genitive pretii, buy for so much, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 5.6, compare 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Hecuba” 360, 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 7.6.24]]; ψυχῆς at the price of life, [Refs 1st c.AD+ [1st c.AD(?): Heraclitus 85]]: also with dative, buy with.., τἄχθιστα τοῖσι φιλτάτοις ὠνούμεθα [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Iphigenia Aulidensis” 1170: _absolutely_, 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Memorabilia” 2.10.4, “Ages.” 1.18: especially in participle, ὠνουμένους ἕξειν τὰ ἐπιτήδεια]]by purchase, [Refs [[prev. author] “An.” 2.3.27, compare 5.5.14, etc.]]; also ὁ ὠνούμενος the buyer, purchaser, ὁρῶντος τοῦ ὠνουμένου [Refs 1st c.AD+ [[prev. author] “Eq.” 3.2, compare 1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus “Cat.Mi.” 36]]; ὁ ἐωνημένος the owner by purchase (of a slave), [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Plutus” 7; ὁ ὠνησάμενος 1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus 2.242d]]; ὁ ὠνησόμενος the intending purchaser, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th-3rd c.BC: Dinarchus Orator 3.10: _metaphorically_, χάριτας πονηρὰς ὠ. 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Helena” 902; ὅσα ἄνθρωποι ἄθλων ὠνοῦνται 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Hiero” 9.11; εὔνοιαν παρά τινος 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 12.20; ὠ. τὰς αὑτῶν ψυχὰς παρὰ τῶν ἐχθρῶν 5th c.BC: Lysias Orator 28.9:—in 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Supplices” 337 Robortello restored ὄνοιτο.]]

__2
bid for, purchase the farming of public taxes or properties, λ ταλάντων [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Andocides Orator 1.134, 5th c.BC: Lysias Orator 7.2 (in _participle_ _perfect_ _passive_ with _transitive_ sense)]]; τέλη παρὰ τῆς πόλεως [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “de Vectigalibus” 4.19, etc.; ὠ. μέταλλα 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 19.293; τὸν ἐωνημένον τὴν ἰλὺν ἐκκομίσασθαι “IG” 12.94.20, compare ὠνή 11.]]

__3
buy off, avert by giving hush-money, ὠ. τὸν κίνδυνον [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 38.20]]; τὰ ἐγκλήματα [Refs [[prev. work]8]]; ταλάντου τὸ πλημμέλημα (i.e. its penalty) παρά τινος [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd c.AD: Lucianus Sophista “Herm.” 81.]]

__4
ὠ. τινα to buy a person, of one who bribes, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 18.247; ὠνεῖται καὶ διαφθείρει τινάς [prev. author] 9.45, compare 1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus “Philopoemen” 15.]]

__II
sometimes used as passive, uncertain in present since [ὠνούμενά τε καὶ πιπρασκόμενα] is interpolated in [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Phaedo” 69b]]; occasionally in perfect, participle ἐωνημένος [Refs 4th c.BC+ [[prev. author] “R.” 563b, 4th c.BC: Isaeus Orator 11.42, 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 19.209]] (but indicative ἐώνηνται [Refs 4th c.BC+ [Anonymus cited in 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Rhetorica” 1410a19 is _active_ in sense)]]: pluperfect ἐώνητο [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Pax” 1182 (troch.)]]; also in aorist ἐωνήθην [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Memorabilia” 2.7.12, ὠνηθῇ [prev. author] “Vect.” 4.19]]; participle ὠνηθείς [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Isaeus Orator 6.19, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Sophista” 224a, “Lg.” 850a.]]

__III
active perfect participle ἐωνηκώς, ={ἐωνημένος}, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Lysias Orator “Fragmenta” 135S.:]]aorist ὠνῆσαι· ἀγοράσαι, [Refs [12th c.AD: Zonaras Legal icographus:]]present ὠνεῖν· πωλεῖν, ἀπολαύειν, [Refs 5th c.AD+ [5th c.AD(?): Hesychius Legal icographus: the sense πωλεῖν is Cretan, ὠνῆν τὰ χρήματα]] they shall sell the property, [Refs [“Leg.Gort.” 5.47]]; αἰ δέ τις.. τὸ νόμισμα μὴ λείοι δέκετθαι ἢ καρπῶ ὠνίοι if any one refuses the currency or sells for produce, [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [“SIG” 525.8 (Crete, 3rd c.BC).]]

(Rec. ὠόν), -οῦ, τό [in LXX for בֵּיצָה ;]
an egg: Luk.11:12.†

LSJ / STEPBible (TFLSJ)
ᾠόν, τό,
old poetry forms ὤεον, ὤιον, see entry near the end:— egg, τίκτει ᾠὰ ἐν γῇ καὶ ἐκλέπει [ὁ κροκόδειλος] [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 2.68; ᾠὰ χήνεια 4th c.BC: Eriphus Comicus 7]]; of all birds, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Historia Animalium” 559a15]]; but mostly of hens' eggs, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Lysistrata” 856, “fragment” 185, etc.]]; [ᾠοῦ] τὸ λευκόν, τὸ ὠχρόν, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Historia Animalium” 559a18]]; τὸ πυρρόν, τὸ χρυσοῦν, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Hippocrates Medicus “γυναικεῖα” 2.171, 2nd c.AD: Athenaeus Epigrammaticus 9.376d]]; ᾠὰ ἡμιπαγέα half-boiled eggs, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Hippocrates Medicus “Acut.” (“Sp.”)]]; ἑφθά, ὠμά, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-3rd c.BC: Theophrastus Philosophus “de Vertigine” 2; ᾠὸν ῥοφεῖν 3rd c.BC: Nicomachus Comicus 3; καταπίνειν 4th c.BC: Antiphanes Comicus 140.5; ᾠὰ κολάπτειν 4th c.BC: Anaxilas Comicus 18.4 (_anapaest meter_)]]; ᾠὰ γόνιμα fertile eggs, opposed to ὑπηνέμια, ἄγονα, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “de Generatione Animalium” 730a6, 20; also ᾠὰ πλήρη [prev. author] “Mete.” 359a14]]; ᾠὸν τέλειον, opposed to ἀτελές, [Refs [[prev. author] “GA” 718b23, 24]]; ᾠὸν ἀνεμιαῖον, ζεφύριον, wind-egg, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Araros Comicus 6, 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Historia Animalium” 560a6]]; σμύρνης ᾠ. lump, [Refs 6th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 2.73; ὁ Χρόνος ἐγέννησεν ᾠόν 5th-6th c.AD: Orphica “Fragmenta” 54, +others, compare 6th c.BC: Epimenides Philosophus 5: _metaphorically_, ᾠὸν ἅπας γέγονεν]] he has become bald as an egg, [Refs [Anthologia Graeca 11.398 (from Nicias).]]

__2
of the eggs or spawn of fish, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 2.93; τὰ ᾠὰ ἀφιᾶσι 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Historia Animalium” 567b22, compare 525a7]]; of serpents, [Refs [[prev. work] 558a26]]; of tortoises, [Refs [[prev. work] 558a4.]]

__3
of plants, seed, [Refs [[prev. author] “GA” 731a6; compare ᾠοτοκέω 2.]]

__4
cupping-glass, τὰ ἰατρικὰ ᾠὰ ὑέλινα ὄντακαὶ σύστομα [Refs 2nd c.BC+ [2nd-1st c.BC(?): Hero Mechanicus “(Spiritalia) Pneumatica” 1]]Prooem.: egg-shaped cup, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Dinon Historicus 14]]. The word has the following forms: Attic dialect ᾠόν (- ?~X), confirmed by Inscrr. ὠιῶν [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [“IG” 11(2).224 A 11,12 (Delos, 3rd c.BC)]], Papyri (ὠιὰ χήνεα [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [“PCair.Zen.” 130.26 (3rd c.BC))]], and later Mss.; Aeolic dialect ὤιον, genitive ὠίω (¯ ?~X ?~X ¯), [Refs 7th c.BC+ [7th-6th c.BC: Sappho Lyrica 56, 112]]; ὤεον lbyc.16, [Refs 7th c.BC+ [7th-6th c.BC(?): Semonides Iambographus 11, 3rd c.BC: Callimachus Epicus “Epigrammata” 6.10, 2nd c.BC: Nicander Epicus “Theriaca” 192, 4th-3rd c.BC: Aratus Epicus 956]]; ὤβεον is Argive accusative to [Refs 5th c.AD+ [5th c.AD(?): Hesychius Legal icographus (i.e. ὤϝεον)]]; ᾠόν oxytone accusative to [Refs 9th c.AD+ [9th c.AD: Theognostus Grammaticus “Can.” 130; ὤεον _proparoxytone_, [prev. work]121. The form ὠόν,]] which Latin ovum would lead us to expect, is found only in late texts [LXX+NT [(LXX.Deu.22.6, NT.Luke.11.12, etc.)]] and is due to loss of the ι in [Refs 2nd c.BC+ [2nd c.BC]]; cognate with Latin ovum, OHGei, ONorse egg (prim. Germanic aiia -), whence Engl. examples

deep_entry:
Abbott-Smith / STEPBible (TBESG)
ὥρα, -ας, ἡ,
[in LXX chiefly for עֵת and in Da for שָׁעָה ;]
__1. any time or period fixed by nature, esp. a season (Hom., Hdt., Plat., al.).
__2. A part of the day, and esp. a twelfth part of day or night, an hour: Mat.24:36, Mrk.13:32, Act.10:3, al.; accus. in ans. to "when"? (M, Pr., 63, 215; Bl., §34, 8), Jhn.4:52, Act.10:3, 30 1Co.15:30, Rev.3:3; accusative of duration, Mat.20:12 26, Mrk.14:37; inexactly, πρὸς ὥραν, for a season, for a time, Jhn.5:35, 2Co.7:8, Gal.2:5; πρὸς καιρὸν ὥρας, for a short season (ICC, in l.), 1Th.2:17.
__3. A definite point of time, time, hour: Mat.26:45; with genitive of thing(s), Luk.1:10 14:17, Rev.3:10, al.; with genitive of person(s), Luk.22:53, Jhn.2:4 7:30, al.; ἡ ἄρτι ὥρα, 1Co.4:11; ἐσχάτη ὥ., 1Jn.2:18; before ὅτε, Jhn.4:21, 23 5:25 16:25; ἵνα, Jhn.12:23, al.; with accusative and inf., Rom.13:11 (cf. DB, ext., 475b 476b).
(AS)

---

LSJ / STEPBible (TFLSJ)
ὥρα,

__C
Ionic dialect ὥρη, ἡ: Epic dialect genitive plural ὡράων, Ionic dialect ὡρέων: locative plural ὥρασι, (which see) any period, fixed by natural laws and revolutions, whether of the year, month, or day (the sense 'day' is implied in the compound ἑπτάωρος, which see), νυκτός τε ὥραν καὶ μηνὸς καὶ ἐνιαυτοῦ [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Memorabilia” 4.7.4, compare 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Alcestis” 449 (Lyric poetry), 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 527d; τοῦ γνώμονος ἡ σκιὰ ἐπιοῦσα ἐπὶ τὰς γραμμὰς σημαίνει τὰς ὥρας τοῦ ἐνιαυτοῦ καὶ τῆς ἡμέρας “IG” 12(8).240 (from Samothrace): but specially,]]

__C.I
in [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Homerus Epicus]], part of the year, season; mostly in plural, the seasons, ὅτε τέτρατον ἦλθεν ἔτος καὶ ἐπήλυθον ὧραι [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 2.107, 19.152; ἀλλ᾽ ὅτε δὴ μῆνές τε καὶ ἡμέραι ἐξετελεῦντο, ἂψ περιτελλομένου ἔτεος, καὶ ἐπήλυθον ὧραι 11.295, 14.294; ἀλλ᾽ ὅτε δή ῥ᾽ ἐνιαυτὸς ἔην, περὶ δ᾽ ἔτραπον ὧραι 10.469, compare 8th-7th c.BC: Hesiodus Epicus “Theogonia” 58; Διὸς ὧραι 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 24.344, compare 5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “O.” 4.2; ὁ κύκλος τῶν ὡρέων ἐς τὠυτὸ περιιών 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 2.4, compare 1.32; δυώδεκα μέρεα δασαμένους τῶν ὡρέων ἐς [τὸν ἐνιαυτόν] [prev. author] 2.4]]; οὐ μεταλλάσσουσι αἱ ὧραι [Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. work] 77; περιτελλομέναις ὥραις 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Tyrannus” 156 (Lyric poetry)]]; πάσαις ὥραις at all seasons, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. author] “fragment” 592.6 (Lyric poetry), 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Aves” 696 (_anapaest meter_); ὧραι ἐτῶν καὶ ἐνιαυτῶν 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Leges” 906c, compare “Smp.” 188a, etc.; τῆς.. ὥρας τοῦ ἐνιαυτοῦ ταύτης οὔσης, ἐν ᾗ ἀσθενοῦσιν ἄνθρωποι μάλιστα 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 7.47]]; χαλεπὴ ὥ. a bad season, [Refs 7th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Protagoras” 344d; ἀ δ᾽ ὤρα χαλέπα 7th-6th c.BC: Alcaeus Lyricus 39]]; ἡ ὥ. αὕτη this season, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Cynegeticus” 7.1, compare 5.6]]; κατὰ τὰς ὥρας according to the seasons, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “de Generatione Animalium” 786a31; οἱ περὶ τὴν ὥραν χρόνοι [prev. author] “Pol.” 1335a37.— 8th c.BC: Homerus Epicus and 8th-7th c.BC: Hesiodus Epicus distinguish three seasons, and express each by the _sing._ ὥρη, with a word added to specify each:]]

__C.I.a
spring, ἔαρος.. ὥρη [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 6.148; ὥρη εἰαρινή 2.471, 16.643, 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 18.367, etc.]]; so in Trag. and Attic dialect, ἦρος ὥρα or ὧραι, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Nubes” 1008 (_anapaest meter_), 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Cyclops” 508 (Lyric poetry); ὥρα νέα 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Equites” 419; νεᾶνις 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Phoenissae” 786 (Lyric poetry); see below 2.]]

__C.I.b
summer, θέρεος ὥρη [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th-7th c.BC: Hesiodus Epicus “Opera et Dies” 584, 664; ὥρα θερινή 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Cynegeticus” 9.20, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Epinomis” 987a, etc.]]

__C.I.c
winter, χείματος ὥρη [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th-7th c.BC: Hesiodus Epicus “Opera et Dies” 450; ὥρῃ χειμερίῃ 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 5.485, 8th-7th c.BC: Hesiodus Epicus “Opera et Dies” 494]]; χειμῶνος ὥρᾳ in winter, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Andocides Orator 1.137; χιονοβόλος 1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus 2.182e.— 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus]] also names three seasons, [Refs [“Pr.” 454s q.]]; an Egyptian division of the year, accusative to [Refs 1st c.BC+ [1st c.BC: Diodorus Siculus Historicus 1.26.]]—A fourth first appears in [Refs 7th c.BC+ [7th c.BC: Alcman Lyricus 76]], θέρος καὶ χεῖμα κὠπώραν τρίταν καὶ τέτρατον τὸ ϝῆ; and in [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Hippocrates Medicus “περὶ διαίτης” 3.68, χειμών, ἦρ, θέρος, φθινόπωρο; ὥρας φαίνομεν ἡμεῖς ἦρος χειμῶνος ὀπώρας 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Aves” 709 (_anapaest meter_)]]; τετράμορφοι ὧραι E(?).[Refs [“fragment” 943 (hexameters)]]: later, seven seasons are named, ἔαρ, θέρος, ὀπώρα, φθινόπωρον, σπορητός, χειμών, φυταλιά [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd c.AD: Galenus Medicus 17(1).17.]]

__C.I.2
especially prime of the year, springtime, ὅσα φύλλα καὶ ἄνθεα γίγνεται ὥρῃ [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 9.51, compare 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 2.468; παρὰ τὴν καθεστηκυῖαν ὥραν 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 4.6.]]

__C.I.2.b
in historians, the campaigning season, τὸν τῆς ὥρας εἰς τὸν περίπλουν χρόνον [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Historia Graeca (Hellenica)” 6.2.13]]; especially in the phrase ὥρα ἔτους, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 2.52, 6.70, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Phaedrus” 229a, “Lg.” 952e, 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 50.23, 4th-3rd c.BC: Theophrastus Philosophus “de Causis Plantarum” 3.23.2]]; εἰς ἔτους ὥραν next season, [Refs 1st c.AD+ [1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus “Pericles” 10.]]

__C.I.3
the year generally, τῆς ὥρης μέσον θέρος [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 8.12]]; ἐν τῇ πέρυσιν ὥρᾳ last year, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 56.3]]; εἰς ὥρας next year, [LXX+5th c.BC+ [4th-3rd c.BC: Philemo Comicus 116, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Epistulae” 346c, LXX.Gen.18.10, “Anthologia Graeca” 11.17 (1st c.AD: Nicarchus Epigrammaticus), compare 1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus “Agesilaus” 22; also εἰς ἄλλας ὥρας]]hereafter, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Iphigenia Aulidensis” 122 (Lyric poetry); ἐς τὰς ὥρας τὰς ἑτέρας 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Nubes” 562 (Lyric poetry); ἐκ τῶν ὡρῶν εἰς τὰς ὥρας [prev. author] “Th.” 950 (_anapaest meter_)]]; κἠς ὥρας κἤπειτα next year and for ever, [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [3rd c.BC: Theocritus Poeta Bucolicus 15.74; also ὥραις ἐξ ὡρᾶν 3rd c.BC: Isyllus Lyricus 25]]; compare ὥρασιν.

__C.I.4
in plural, of the climate of a country, as determined by its seasons, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.142, compare 149, 4.199]] (here perhaps three harvest seasons); τὰς ὥ. κάλλιστα κεκρημένας [Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. author] 3.106; compare 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Critias” 111e, “Phd.” 111b]]; climatic conditions, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 2.26.]]

__C.II
time of day, νυκτὸς ἐν ὥρῃ [Refs [“hymnus ad Mercurium” 67, 155, 400]]; αἱ ὧ. τῆς ἡμέρας the times of day, i.e. morning, noon, evening, and night, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Memorabilia” 4.3.4]]; δι᾽ ὥραν ἡμέρας by the time of day (fixed for meetings), [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator “Prooemia” 49, etc.; πᾶσαν ὥ. τῆς ἡμέρας 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Meteorologica” 371b31; μεσονυκτίοις ποθ᾽ ὥραις “Anacreontea” 31.1: without ἡμέρας]] or νυκτός, ἑκάστης ἡμέρας μέχρι τρίτου μέρους ὥρας [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Leges” 784a; τῆς ὥρας μικρὸν πρὸ δύντος ἡλίου 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Historia Graeca (Hellenica)” 7.2.22]]; ψευσθεὶς τῆς ὥ. having mistaken the hour, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Andocides Orator 1.38]]; ἐποίησαν ἔξω μέσων νυκτῶν τὴν ὥραν, i.e. they prolonged the day beyond midnight, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 54.26; τῆς ὥρας ἐγίγνετ᾽ ὀψέ [prev. author] 21.84; ὀψίτερον τῆς ὥ. “PTeb.” 793 xi 12 (2nd c.BC)]]; πολλῆς ὥρας it being late, [NT+2nd c.BC+ [2nd c.BC: Polybius Historicus 5.8.3; ἤδη ὥρα πολλή NT.Mark.6.35]]; ἄχρι πολλῆς ὥρας till late in the day, [Refs 1st c.BC+ [1st c.BC: Dionysius Halicarnassensis 2.54.]]

__C.II.b
duration, interval or lapse of time, μετὰ ἱκανὴν ὥραν τοῦ κατενεχθῆναι τὸν πέλεκυν ἐξακούεται ἡ τῆς πληγῆς φωνή [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd c.AD: Sextus Empiricus Philosophus “adversus Mathematicos” 5.69]]; length of time, term, Ἄρτεμις ἐννέ᾽ ἐτῶν δεκάδας βίον Ἀρτεμιδώρῳ ἔκχρησεν, τρεῖς δ᾽ ὥραι(date.) ἔτι προσέθηκε Προνοίη [Refs 2nd c.BC+ [“IG” 12(3).1350.3 (Thera, 2nd c.BC)]]; ἐπὶ πολλὴν ὥ. for a long time, [Refs 1st c.AD+ [1st c.AD: Josephus Historicus “Antiquitates Judaicae” 8.4.4.]]

__C.II.2
the νυχθήμερον was probably first divided into twenty-four hours by [Refs 2nd c.BC+ [2nd c.BC: Hipparchus Astronomicus, ἐν πόσαις ὥραις ἰσημεριναῖς]] (equinoctial hours) ἕκαστον τῶν ἄστρων ἢ δύνει ἢ ἀνατέλλει [Refs 1st c.BC+ [2.4.5, compare 1st c.BC: Ptolemaeus Epigrammaticus “Alm.” 3.9, 4.9, +others]]

__C.II.2.b
in ordinary life the day from sunrise to sunset was divided into twelve equal parts called ὧραι (ὧραι καιρικαί when it was necessary to distinguish them from the ὧραι ἰσημεριναί, see at {καιρικός} 2 c), ἡμέρα ἡ.. δωδεκάωρος, τουτέστιν ἡ ἀπὸ ἀνατολῆς μέχρι δύσεως [NT+2nd c.AD+ [2nd c.AD: Sextus Empiricus Philosophus “adversus Mathematicos” 10.182; οὐχὶ δώδεκά εἰσιν ὧραι τῆς ἡμέρα; NT.John.11.9; ὡράων ἀμφὶ δυωδεκάδι “Anthologia Graeca” 9.782 (6th c.AD: Paulus Silentiarius Epigrammaticus)]]; the time of day was commonly given without the Article, ὥρᾳ ᾱ [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [“PHamb.” 1.96.3 (2nd c.AD)]], τρίτης ὥρας [Refs 1st c.AD+ [1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus “Romulus” 12]]; ὀγδόης, ἐνάτης, δεκάτης ὥ., [Refs [[prev. author] “Alex.” 60, “Aem.” 22, “Ant.” 68, etc.]]; but we have περὶ τὴν τρίτην ὥραν, περὶ τὴν ἑνδεκάτην, [NT+1st c.BC+ [NT.Matt.20.3, 6, beside περὶ ἕκτην καὶ ἐννάτην ὥ. [prev. work] 5; χθὲς ὥραν ἑβδόμην NT.John.4.52, compare “IG” 5(1).1390.109 (Andania, 1st c.BC), etc.]]; ἐρωτᾷ σε Χαιρήμων δειπνῆσαι.. αὔριον, ἥτις ἐστὶν ιε, ἀπὸ ὥρας θ ¯ -to-morrow the 15th at 9 o'clock, [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [POxy. 110 (2nd c.AD): proverbial, δωδεκάτης ὥ.,]] as we say 'at the eleventh hour', [Refs 1st c.AD+ [1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus “Crassus” 17.]]

__C.II.2.c
τὰ δυώδεκα μέρεα τῆς ἡμέρης παρὰ Βαβυλωνίων ἔμαθον οἱ Ἕλληνες [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 2.109; here ἡμέρη means the νυχθήμερον, and the μέρεα were each = 2]] ὧραι ἰσημερινα; these double hours (Assyr. kaš-bu) are called ὧραι by [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Eudoxus Astronomus, ἥμισυ ζῳδίου.., ὅ ἐστιν ὥρας ἥμισυ “Ars” 14.11, compare 16.2; compare δωδεκάωρος 11.]]

__C.III
Astrology texts, degree of the zodiac rising at the nativity compare (ὡρονόμος [Refs 4th c.AD+ [11, ὡροσκόπος 11), ὥ. μεροποσπόρος, τεκνοσπόρος, 4th c.AD(?): Manetho Astrologus 4.577, 597]]; ἐξ ὥρης ἐσορῶν Ζεὺς Ἑρμείην Jupiter in the ascendant in aspect with Mercury, [Refs [[prev. author] 3.186, compare 32, +others]]

__B
the fitting time or season for a thing (mostly without Article, even in Attic dialect), frequently in [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Homerus Epicus (see. below); ὥρα συνάπτει 5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “P.” 4.247; ὧραι ἐπειγόμεναι [prev. author] “N.” 4.34; ὅταν ὥ. ἥκῃ 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Memorabilia” 2.1.2]]; but with Article, τῆς ὥ. ἐνθυμεῖσθαι [Refs [[prev. author] “Cyn.” 8.6]]: frequently in later writers, τῆς ὥρας ἐπιγενομένης [Refs 2nd c.BC+ [2nd c.BC: Polybius Historicus 2.34.3, etc.]]

__B.2
with genitive of things, ὥρη κοίτοιο, μύθων, ὕπνου, the time for bed, tale-telling, or sleep, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 3.334, 11.379, compare 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.10; ὥρη δόρποιο 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 14.407; περὶ ἀρίστου ὥραν 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 7.81, 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Historia Graeca (Hellenica)” 1.1.13; πολυηράτου ἐς γάμου ὥρην 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 15.126; ἐς γάμου ὥρην ἀπικέσθαι 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 6.61; γάμων ἔχειν ὥραν 1st c.BC: Dionysius Halicarnassensis 5.32]]; so εἰς ἀνδρὸς ὥραν ἥκουσα time for a husband, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Critias” 113d]]; ὥρη ἀρότου, ἀμήτου, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th-7th c.BC: Hesiodus Epicus “Opera et Dies” 460, 575; μέχρι ἀρότου ὥρης “IG” 7.235.3 (Oropus, 4th c.BC)]]; καρπῶν ὧραι [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Ranae” 1034 (_anapaest meter_); ἡ ὥρα τῆς ὀχείας 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Historia Animalium” 509b20; τοῦ φωλεύειν [prev. work] 579a26, etc.]]; also ὥραν εἶχον παιδεύεσθαι I was of age to.. [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Isaeus Orator 9.28.]]

__B.3
ὥρα [ἐστίν] with infinitive, it is time to do a thing, ἀλλὰ καὶ ὥρη εὕδειν [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 11.330, compare 373]]; so also in Trag. and Attic dialect, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Phoenissae” 1584, “Heracl.” 288 (_anapaest meter_), 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Ecclesiazusae” 30, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Protagoras” 361e, 362a; so δοκεῖ οὐχ ὥρα εἶναι καθεύδειν 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 1.3.11, compare “HG” 7.2.13 (uncertain reading)]]: with accusative et infinitive, ὥρα δ᾽ ἐμπόρους καθιέναι ἄγκυραν [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Choephori” 661, compare 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Tyrannus” 466 (Lyric poetry)]]: with dative et infinitive, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 4.5.1, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Theaetetus” 145b]]: in these phrases the infinitive present is almost universal; the aorist, however, occurs in [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 21.428, 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Ajax” 245 (Lyric poetry), 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Acharnenses” 393 (where also ἐστί is added to ὥρα, as in 5th c.BC: Philyllius Comicus 3, ἀφαιρεῖν ὥρα 'στὶν ἤδη τὰς τραπέζας)]]; and the perfect in ὥρα πεπαῦσθαι [Refs 1st c.AD+ [1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus 2.728d]]: sometimes the infinitive must be supplied, οὐδέ τί σε χρή, πρὶν ὥρη, καταλέχθαι [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 15.394, compare 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Electra” 112 (Lyric poetry), 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Ecclesiazusae” 877]]; ὥρα κἠς οἶκον (i. e. ἰέναι εἰς οἶκον) [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [3rd c.BC: Theocritus Poeta Bucolicus 15.147.]]

__B.4
in various adverbial usages, τὴν ὥρην at the right time, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 2.2, 8.19, 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Oeconomicus” 20.16: but τὴν ὥ.]] at that hour, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th-7th c.BC: Hesiodus Epicus “Scutum Herculis” 401]]; ταύτην τὴν ὥραν at this season, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Cynegeticus” 9.1; [ἡ ἶρις] πᾶσαν ὥραν γίγνεται τῆς ἡμέρας 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Meteorologica” 371b31; δείελον ὥρην παύομαι ἀμήτοιο 3rd c.BC: Apollonius Rhodius Epicus 3.417]]; ὥραν οὐδενὸς κοινὴν θεῶν at an hour.., [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Eumenides” 109, compare 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Bacchae” 724, 4th c.BC: Aeschines Orator 1.9]]; αὐτῆς ὥρας immediately, [Refs 3rd c.AD+ [“PMich.” in “Class.Phil.” 22.255(3rd c.AD)]]; ἐν ὥρῃ in due season, in good time, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 17.176, 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.31, compare 5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “O.” 6.28, 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Vespae” 242, etc.]]; also αἰεὶ εἰς ὥρας in successive seasons, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 9.135]]; ἐς τὰς ὥρας for all time, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Ranae” 382 (Lyric poetry compare above 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus 1.3) (hence in an acclamation [ε] ἰς ὥρας πᾶσι τοῖς τὴν πόλιν φιλοῦσιν]] hurrah for.., [Refs 3rd c.AD+ [“POxy.” 41.29 (3rd-4th c.AD))]]; οἱ ὧδε χέζοντες εἰς ὥ. μὴ ἔλθοιεν [Refs 5th c.BC+ [“Milet.” 2(3) No.406, compare ὥρασ; καθ᾽ ὥραν 3rd c.BC: Theocritus Poeta Bucolicus 18.12, 2nd c.BC: Polybius Historicus 1.45.4, compare 3.93.6, etc.; opposed to παρ᾽ ὥρην “Anthologia Graeca” 7.534 (3rd c.BC: Alexander Aetolus Elegiacus or 1st c.AD: Automedon Epigrammaticus), compare 1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus 2.784b, etc.:— πρὸ τῆς ὥρας 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Oeconomicus” 20.16; πρὸ ὥρας 2nd c.AD: Lucianus Sophista “Luct.” 13; πρὸ ὥρας τελευτῆσαι “IG” 42(1).84.26 (Epid., 1st c.AD)]]; πρὶν ὥρας [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “P.” 4.43 (compare πρίν 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus 11.4).]]

__B.II
metaphorically, the spring-time of life, the bloom of youth, [Refs 6th c.BC+ [6th c.BC: Mimnermus Lyricus 3.1; ὥραν ἐχούσας 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Supplices” 997, compare “Th.” 13, 535; παῖδας πρὸς τέρμασιν ὥρας 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Aves” 705 (_anapaest meter_); πάντες οἱ ἐν ὥρᾳ 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 474d]]; οὐκ ἐνὥ., ={πρεσβύτερος}, [Refs [[prev. author] “Phdr.” 240d; ἐὰν ἐπὶ ὥρᾳ ᾖ [prev. author] “R.” 474e; ἕως ἂν ἐν ὥρᾳ ὦσι [prev. author] “Men.” 76b]]; παυσαμένου τῆς ὥ. probably in [Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. author] “Phdr.” 234a; ἀνθεῖν ἐν ὥ. [prev. author] “R.” 475a; τὴν ὥ. διαφυλάξαι ἄβατον τοῖς πονηροῖς 5th-6th c.BC: Isocrates Orator 10.58]]; λήγειν ὥρας, opposed to ἀνθεῖν, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus Alcaeus1.131e; ἑς ἐπιγινόμενόν τι τέλος, οἷον τοῖς ἀκμαίοις ἡ ὥρα 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Ethica Nicomachea” 1174b33, compare 1157a8.]]

__B.II.2
frequently involving an idea of beauty, φεῦ φεῦ τῆς ὥρας τοῦ κάλλους [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Aves” 1724 (Lyric poetry); ὥρᾳ.. ἡλικίας λαμπρός 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 6.54; κάλλει καὶ ὥρᾳ διενεγκόντες 4th c.BC: Aeschines Orator 1.134, compare [prev. work]158; καλὸς ὥρᾳ τε κεκραμένος 5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “O.” 10(11).104, compare 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Memorabilia” 2.1.22, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Leges” 837b]]; ἀφ᾽ ὥρας ἐργάζεσθαι quaestum corpore facere, [Refs 1st c.AD+ [1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus]]“Tim..” 14,compare [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus]]“Mem..” 1.6.13, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [“Smp.” 8.21; τὴν ὥ. πεπωληκότες 1st c.BC: Philodemus Gadarensis Epigrammaticus “Rh.” 1.344 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus:]] —then,

__B.II.2.b
generally, beauty, grace, elegance of style, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [1st c.BC: Dionysius Halicarnassensis “Epistula ad Pompeium” 2, 1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus 2.874b, etc.; γλυκύτης καὶ ὥ. 2nd c.AD: Hermogenes Rhetor “περὶ ἰδεῶν” 2.3, compare 4th-3rd c.BC: Menander Comicus “Rh.” p.335 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus, 4th c.AD: Himerius Sophista “Orationes” 1.2]]; of beauty in general, χάρις καὶ ὥρα [Refs 1st c.AD+ [1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus 2.128d.]]

__B.II.3
Ὥρα personified, like{Ἥβη}, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “N.” 8.1.]]

__B.III
={τὰ ὡραῖα}, the produce of the season, fruits of the year, ἀπὸ τῆς ὥρας ἐτρέφοντο [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Historia Graeca (Hellenica)” 2.1.1.]]

__C
personified, αἱὯραι, the Hours, keepers of heaven's cloudgate, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 5.749, 8.393]]; and ministers of the gods,[Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. work] 433; Ζεῦ, τεαὶ.. Ὧραι 5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “O.” 4.2]]; especially of Aphrodite, [Refs [“Hymni Homerici” 6.5,12]]; also Ὧ. Διονυσιάδες, Καρνειάδες, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Simonides Lyricus 148, 3rd c.BC: Callimachus Epicus “Hymnus in Apollinem” 87]]; three in number, Eunomia, Dike, Eirene, daughters of Zeus and Themis, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th-7th c.BC: Hesiodus Epicus “Theogonia” 901; Ωραι πολυάνθεμοι 5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “O.” 13.17, compare 2nd c.AD: Alexander Rhetor 261.6, 3rd c.BC: Theocritus Poeta Bucolicus 1.150, etc.: frequently joined with the Χάριτες, “hymnus ad Apollinem” 194, 8th-7th c.BC: Hesiodus Epicus “Opera et Dies” 75]]; worshipped at Athens, [Refs 1st c.BC+ [2nd c.AD: Pausanias Periegeta 9.35.1; at Argos, [prev. author] 2.20.5; at Attaleia, “BMus.Inscription” 1044 (1st c.BC).]]

ὡραῖος, -α, -ον
(ὥρα), [in LXX for נָאָה, טוֹב, יָפָה, etc. ;]
seasonable, timely, esp. of ripe fruits; hence, blooming, beautiful (both of things and persons): Mat.23:27, Act.3:2, 10, Rom.10:15 (LXX, ὥρα).†
(AS)

---

LSJ / STEPBible (TFLSJ)
ὡραῖος, α, ον,
produced at the right season (ὥρα), seasonable, timely: especially of the fruits of the earth, βίος or βίοτος ὡ. store of fruits gathered in due season, [Refs [8th-7th c.BC: Hesiodus Epicus “Opera et Dies” 32, 307]]; ὡ. καρποί the fruits of the season, καρποὺς.. κατατίθεσθαι ὡραίους to store them up in season, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.202: frequently in _neuter_, ὡραῖα, τά, 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 1.120, 3.58, 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 5.3.9, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Leges” 845e; ἑραίως τὰ ὡραῖα ἀποδιδόναι 5th c.BC: Hippocrates Medicus “ἀφορισμοί” 3.8]]; ὡραῖα.. ἀποτελεῖν ἱερά to render fruits of the season as sacred offerings, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Critias” 116c, cf. Oracle texts cited in 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 21.52; τρωκτὰ ὡ. 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 5.3.12; ἄνθεα “Anthologia Graeca” 9.564 (from Nicias)]]; σῦκα [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd c.AD: Aretaeus Medicus “χρονίων νούσων θεραπευτικόν” 1.3]]; also of animals, ὡ. ἄρνες yearling, [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [Anthologia Graeca 6.157 (3rd c.BC: Theodoridas Epigrammaticus)]]; of tunnies at a year old (from six months to one year they were called πηλαμύδες), πηλαμὺς.. ὡραία θέρους τῷ Βοσπορίτῃ [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Fragmenta” 503]]; ὡ. θύννοι Ps.-[Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th-7th c.BC: Hesiodus Epicus cited in 2nd c.AD: Athenaeus Epigrammaticus 3.116b, cf. Hices.[prev. work] 116e, 4th c.BC: Archestratus Epicus “fragment” 38.9, 3rd-2nd c.BC: Plautus Comicus Latinus “Capt.” 851]]; τάριχος ὡ. fish salted or pickled in the season, [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd c.AD: Alexander Rhetor 186.5; ἰχθύες ἐς τάγηνον ὡ. 2nd c.AD: Babrius Fabularum Scriptor 6.4]]; σαργάναι ὡ. pickling-tubs, [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd c.AD(?): Pollianus Epigrammaticus 7.27]]: hence generally, agricultural produce, εἶναι ἐνεχυρασίαν Αἰξωνεῦσιν ἐκ τῶν ὡ. τῶν ἐκ τοῦ χωρίου [Refs 4th c.BC+ [“IG” 22.2492.8 (4th c.BC).]]

__2
τὰ ὡραῖα, ={τὰ καταμήνια}, especially at their first appearance, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Hippocrates Medicus “περὶ ἐπικυήσιος” 34.]]

__3
substantive ἡ ὡραία (in full, ὥρη ἡ ὡραίη [Refs 5th c.BC+ [2nd c.AD: Aretaeus Medicus “περὶ αἰτιῶν καὶ σημείων χρονίων παθῶν” 1.4, 2nd c.AD: Phrynichus Atticista “Praeparatio Sophistica” p.128 5th c.BC: Bacchylides Lyricus, etc.)]], harvest-time, especially the twenty days before and twenty days after the rising of the dog-star, μίμνει ἐς ὡραίην till harvest-time, [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [3rd c.BC: Apollonius Rhodius Epicus 3.1390.]]

__3.b
the campaigning-season, during which the troops kept the field, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 9.48, 56.30, 2nd c.BC: Polybius Historicus 3.16.7.]]

__3.c
τὴν μὲν ὡραίην οὐκ ὕει it does not rain in the season (i.e. of rain), [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 4.28.]]

__II
happening or done in due season, seasonable, ἄροτος, ἔργον, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th-7th c.BC: Hesiodus Epicus “Opera et Dies” 617.642]]; πλόος [Refs 4th c.BC+ [[prev. work] 630; χειμῶνες 4th-3rd c.BC: Theophrastus Philosophus “Historia Plantarum” 4.14.1; ὕδατα [prev. author] “CP” 2.2.1]]; σκαπάνη [Refs [[prev. work] 3.16.1; τομὴ [καλάμου] [prev. author] “HP” 4.11.4]]; ὅτε ὡραῖον εἴη when the weather permitted, [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd c.AD: Appianus Historicus “Αιβυκή” 120.]]

__II.2
metaphorically, (ὥρα (C) B) seasonable, due, proper, ὡραίων τυχεῖν, ={νομίμων τυχεῖν} (compare ὥριος (A). [Refs 5th c.BC+ [111.2), 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Supplices” 175: ἐν ὡραί[ᾳ ἐκκλησίᾳ]]] uncertain in [Refs 4th c.BC+ [“SIG” 668.4 (Delphi, 2nd c.BC); ἐνιαύτια ὡ. [prev. work] 1025.37 (Cos, 4th-3rd c.BC),compare 5th c.AD(?): Hesychius Legal icographus]]

__III
of persons, seasonable or ripe for a thing, c.genitive, ἀνδρὸς ὡραίη [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.107, compare 5th c.BC: Lysias Orator “Fragmenta” 4]]; γάμων or γάμου ὡραῖαι, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.196, 6.122, compare 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 4.6.9; ἐς ἥβην ὡραίαν γάμων 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Helena” 12 (ὡραίων codices)]]; ὅστις οὐκέθ᾽ ὡραῖος γαμεῖ [Refs [[prev. author] “fragment” 804]]; ὡ. γάμος seasonable marriage, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Fragmenta - American Journal of Philology” 55]]; also of old persons, ripe or ready for death, πατήρ γε μὴν ὡ. [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Alcestis” 516; αὐτὸς δ᾽, ἐν ὠ. γὰρ ἕσταμεν βίῳ, θνῄσκειν ἕτοιμος [prev. author] “Ph.” 968; θάνατος ὡ. 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Agesilaus” 10.3; σορός 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Vespae” 1365; ὡραῖος ἀποτέθνηκεν 1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus 2.178e; so ὕλη ὡ. τέμνεσθαι 4th-3rd c.BC: Theophrastus Philosophus “Historia Plantarum” 5.1.1.]]

__III.2
in reference to age, in the prime of life, youthful, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th-7th c.BC: Hesiodus Epicus “Opera et Dies” 695]]: hence in the bloom of youth, opposed to ἄωρος, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Symposium” 8.21, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 574c; ὡ. ἐὼν καὶ καλός 5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “O.” 9.94; παιδίσκη ὡραιοτάτη 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Acharnenses” 1148 (_anapaest meter_), compare “Ra.” 291, 514; παῖς ὡραῖος [prev. author] “Av.” 138]]: but not necessarily implying beauty, τοῖς τῶν ὡραίων προσώποις, καλῶν δὲ μή [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 601b; ἄνευ κάλλους ὡραῖοι 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Rhetorica” 1406b37]]; compare ὥρα (C) [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Bacchylides Lyricus 11.]]

__III.3
generally, of things, beautiful, graceful, [LXX+NT [LXX.Gen.3.6, LXX.2Ch.36.19, NT.Matt.23.27; ἡ ὡ. πύλη τοῦ ἱεροῦ NT.Act.3.10, compare 3.2.]]

__IV
irregular superlative ὡραιέστατος [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Epicharmus Comicus 186d.]]

__V
adverb ὡραίως [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Hippocrates Medicus “ἀφορισμοί” 3.8.]]

Abbott-Smith / STEPBible (TBESG)
ὠρύομαι  depon.,
[in LXX for שָׁאַג ;]
of animals (also of men, Hdt., al.), to roar, howl: λέων, 1Pe.5:8.†
(AS)

---

LSJ / STEPBible (TFLSJ)
ὠρύομαι [ῡ],
future -ύσομαι[LXX.Hos.11.10]: aorist ὠρῡσάμην [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “O.” 9.109]]:—Ionic dialect and poet. Verb, very rarely used in Attic dialect (see. below), howl, properly of wolves and dogs, [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [3rd c.BC: Callimachus Epicus “Fragmenta” 423, 3rd c.BC: Theocritus Poeta Bucolicus 2.35, 5th-6th c.AD: Coluthus Epicus 116, 1st c.BC: Diodorus Siculus Historicus 1.87]]; of lions, roar, [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [3rd c.BC: Apollonius Rhodius Epicus 4.1339]]; of animals generally, [LXX+1st c.AD+ [1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus 2.973a, LXX.Wis.17.19]]; ὄρθιον ὤρυσαι Pi.[same place],[cf. LXX.Psa.37(38).9]; of primitive folk, either in mourning, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 3.117]], or in joy, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. author] 4.75; ὥσπερ ἀπόπληκτοι.. ὠρύονται 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Comicus 130]]; of the sea, [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd c.AD: Dionysius Periegeta 83.]]

__II
transitive, howl over, τῆνον μὰν θῶες, τῆνον λύκοι ὠ. [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [3rd c.BC: Theocritus Poeta Bucolicus 1.71; ὠ. ἐπί τινι 2nd c.AD: Lucianus Sophista “DMort.” 10.13.]]—The active [Refs [only in “Anthologia Graeca” 11.31 (Antip., uncertain reading), 10th c.AD: Suidas Legal icographus]] (Sanskrit rauti (plural ruvanti), ruváti 'bellow', Latin ru-mor, Slavonic rev-ą, raju-ti.)

deep_entry:
Abbott-Smith / STEPBible (TBESG)
ὡς, adverbial form of the relative pron. ὅς, ἥ, ὅ.
__I. As relat. adv. of manner, as, like as, just as, even as;
__1. with a demonstrative, like οὕτως, expressed or understood: οὕτως . . . ὡς, Mrk.4:26, 1Co.3:15, Eph.5:28, Jas.2:12, al.; ὡς . . . οὕτως, Act.8:32, 1Co.7:17, al.; elliptically (sc. οὕτως, οὕτω), with nom., Mat.6:29, al.; with accusative, Mat.19:19, Mrk.12:31, al.; with prep., Mat.26:55, Mrk.14:48, Luk.22:52, Jhn.7:10, al.; with verb., Jhn.15:6, 2Co.3:1, Eph.2:3, 1Th.5:6, al.; with ptcp. (the ptcp. however not having the special force wh. it has in cl.; see Bl., §73, 5; 74, 6), Mat.7:29, Mrk.1:22, Heb.13:17, al.; freq implying opinion or belief, Rom.9:32;  so esp, with genitive absol., 1Co.4:18, 2Co.5:20, 1Pe.4:12, 2Pe.1:3.
__2. Before numerals, about, nearly: Mrk.5:13, Jhn.1:40, Act.5:7, al.
__3. Before adjectives and adverbs, how: Rom.10:15 11:33, 1Th.2:10; with superl., ὡς τάχιστα, as quickly as possible, Act.17:15.

__II. As conjunction;
__1. temporal,
__(a) as, when, since: Mrk.9:21 14:72, Luk.1:23, Jhn.2:9, al.;
__(b) while, when, as long as: Luk.12:58, Jhn.12:36, Gal.6:10 (Field, Notes, 191); ὡς ἄν (M, Pr., 167, and see: ἄν), Rom.15:24, 1Co.11:34, Php.2:23.
__2. Final, in order that; with inf., in order to (M, Pr., 204n), Luk.9:52, Act.20:24, Heb.7:9.
(AS)
