LSJ / STEPBible (TFLSJ)
ὡς:—
Summary:

__A
as adverb of Manner.

__A.Aa
ὧς and ὥς (with accent), so, thus.

__A.Ab
ὡς (without accent) of the Relat. pronoun ὅς, as.

__A.Ac
ὡς Relat. and Interrog., how.

__A.Ad
ὡς temporal, when.

__A.Ae
ὡς Local, where,

__B
ὡς, as CONJUNCTION.

__C,D
various usages. adverb of Manner:

__A.Aa
ὥς, Demonstr., ={οὕτως}, so, thus, frequently in [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Homerus Epicus, 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 1.33, +others; ὢς εἶπ᾽ 7th-6th c.BC: Sappho Lyrica “Papyrus fragments” in E. Diehl, 20 a. 11 (Epic style)]]; in Ionic dialect Prose, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 3.13, +others; rare in _Attic dialect_, and almost confined to certain phrases, see below 2, 3]]; ὥς simply ={οὕτως}, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Agamemnon” 930, 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 3.37, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Protagoras” 338a; ἀλλ᾽ ὣς γενέσθω 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Hecuba” 888, +others]]

__A.2
καὶ ὧς even so, nevertheless, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 1.116, +others]]; οὐδ᾽ ὧς not even so, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [7.263, 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 1.6, +others, 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 6.76; οὐδέ κεν ὧς 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 9.386: the phrases καὶ ὧς, οὐδ᾽ ὧς, μηδ᾽ ὧς,]] are used in Trag. and Attic dialect, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Antigone” 1042, 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 1.74, 7.74; also later, “PCair.Zen.” 19.10 (3rd c.BC, unaccented), “UPZ” 146.40 (2nd c.BC), “GDI” 1832.11 (Delph., 2nd c.BC), “IG” 22.850.17 (3rd c.BC)]]; κἂν ὧς, εἴπερ μέλει σοι, ἀπόστειλόν μοί τινα [Refs 4th c.AD+ [“POxy.” 120.11 (4th c.AD)]]; δουλεύων καθὼς καὶ ὧς [Refs 2nd c.BC+ [“GDI” 2160 (Delph., 2nd c.BC)]]; Thess. καὶ οὗς [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [“IG” 9(2).234.1 (3rd c.BC)]]; for this phrase the accentuation ὧς[Refs 2nd c.AD+ [is prescribed by Hdn.Gr.2.932, +others,compare 2nd c.AD: Apollonius Dyscolus Grammaticus “de Syntaxi”; 307.16, and is found in good Mss. of Homer; for the remaining uses under this head (Aa. 1, 3, 4) the accentuation ὥς is prescribed by the same grammarians.]]

__A.3
in Comparisons, ὥς.., ὡς.., so.. as.., etc.; and reversely ὡς.., ὣς.., as.. so, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 1.512, 14.265, etc.]]; in Attic dialect, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 530d]]; also ὥς τε.. ὣς.., as.. thus.., [Refs 5th c.BC+ [“hymnus ad Cererem” 174 - 6, 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Bacchae” 1066 - 8; οἷα.. ὥς [prev. author] “El.” 151 - 5]]; ὥσπερ.., ὣς δὲ.. (in apodosi) [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Protagoras” 326d.]]

__A.4
thus, for instance, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 5.129, “hymnus ad Venerem” 218]]; ὥς should be accented in [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 5.121, 125.]]

__A.4.Ab
ὡς, Relat., as, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Homerus Epicus, etc.]]; properly relative to a demonstrative adverb, which is frequently omitted, κινήθη δ᾽ ἀγορὴ ὡς κύματα μακρὰ θαλάσσης, i. e. οὕτως, ὡς.., [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 2.144 (φὴ 4th-3rd c.BC: Zenodotus Grammaticus): it is _relative_ not only to the regular _demonstrative_ Advs. ὥς (ὧς), τώς, ὧδε, οὕτως, αὕτως, but also to ταύτῃ, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 365d, etc. We find a collateral _Doric dialect_ form ὥ (which see)]]; compare ὥτε. Usage:

__A.I
in similes, frequently in [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Homerus Epicus, 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 5.161, +others]]; longer similes are commonly introduced by ὡς ὅτε, ὡς δ᾽ ὅτε, ἤριπε δ᾽, ὡς ὅτε πύργος [ἤριπε] [Refs [4.462: ἤριπε δ᾽, ὡς ὅτε τις δρῦς ἤριπε 13.389, compare 2.394]]; so later, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Empedocles Poeta Philosophus 84.1, etc.; ὡς ὅτε θαητὸν μέγαρον, πάξομεν 5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “O.” 6.2: ὡς ὅτε]] is rare in short similes, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 11.368: ὡς]] is followed by indicative present, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 9.4, 16.364: also by]]aorist, [Refs [3.33f, 4.275, 16.823, +others]]; also by subjunctive present or aorist, [Refs [5.161, 10.183, 485, 13.334]] (sometimes ὡς δ᾽ ὅτ᾽ ἄν, [Refs [11.269, 17.520)]]; compare ὥστε A:—the Verb is sometimes omitted with ὡς, but may be supplied from the context, ἐνδούπησε πεσοῦσ᾽, ὡς εἰναλίη κήξ (i.e. πίπτει) [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 15.479, compare 6.20; θεὸς δ᾽ ὣς τίετο δήμῳ 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 5.78; οἱ δὲ φέβοντο.., βόες ὣς ἀγελαῖαι 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 22.299: where ὡς]] follows the noun to which it refers, it takes the accent; so in Comedy texts, Ἀριστόδημος ὥς [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Cratinus Comicus 151, compare 4th c.BC: Eubulus Comicus 75.6]]; see infr. H.

__A.I.2
like as, just as, ὡς οὗτος κατὰ τέκν᾽ ἔφαγε.., ὣς ἡμεῖς κτλ. [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 2.326, see supr. Aa. 3.]]

__A.I.3
sometimes in the sense as much as or according as, ἑλὼν κρέας ὥς (i. e. ὅσον) οἱ χεῖρες ἐχάνδανον [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 17.344]]; ὦκα δὲ μητρὶ ἔννεπον ὡς (i. e. ὅσα) εἶδόν τε καὶ ἔκλυον [Refs 8th c.BC+ [“hymnus ad Cererem” 172; τῶν πάντων οὐ τόσσον ὀδύρομαι.. ὡς ἑνός 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 4.105; τόσον.. ὡς 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 4.130]]; so in Trag., σοὶ θεοὶ πόροιεν ὡς ἐγὼ θέλω [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Coloneus” 1124; ὡς ἐγὼ οὐκ ἔστιν ὑμῶν ὅστις ἐξ ἴσου νοσεῖ [prev. author] “OT” 60]]; in Prose, ὡς δύναται as much as he can, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [3rd c.AD: Democritus Epigrammaticus 278; τὸ ῥῆμα μέμνημαι ὡς εἶπε 4th c.BC: Aeschines Orator 3.72]]; ὡς μή ={ὅσον μή, νέμεν ὅτι ἃν} (={ἂν}) βόλητοι ὡς μὴ ἰν τοῖ περιχώροι [Refs 4th c.BC+ [“IG” 5(2).3.9 (Tegea, 4th c.BC)]]; cf. Ab. 11.2 below

__A.I.4
sometimes after comparative, compared with, hence than, μᾶλλον πρέπει οὕτως ὡς.. [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Apologia” 36d; ἅ γε μείζω πόνον παρέχει.. οὐκ ἂν ῥᾳδίως οὐδὲ πολλὰ ἂν εὕροις ὡς τοῦτο [prev. author] “R.” 526c]]; οὐδενὸς μᾶλλον φροντίζειν ὡς.. [Refs 2nd c.BC+ [2nd c.BC: Polybius Historicus 3.12.5, compare 7.4.5, 11.2.9, 1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus “Coriolanus” 36: μᾶσσον ὡς]] is uncertain in [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Prometheus Vinctus” 629]], and [ἢ] should perhaps be inserted in [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Lysias Orator 7.12,31]]; compare ὥσπερ IV.

__A.II
with Adverbial clauses:

__A.II.1
parenthetically, in qualifying clauses, ὡς ἔοικε, etc., [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Symposium” 176c, etc.]]: in these cases γε or γοῦν is frequently added, ὡς γοῦν ὁ λόγος σημαίνει as at any rate the argument shows, [Refs [[prev. author] “R.” 334a]]; in some phrases with infinitive, see below [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Bacchylides Lyricus 11.3. An anacoluthon sometimes occurs by the Verb of the principal clause being made dependent on the parenthetic Verb, ὡς δὲ Σκύθαι λέγουσι, νεώτατον ἁπάντων ἐθνέων εἶναι (for ἦν)]] τὸ σφέτερον [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 4.5, compare 1.65; ὡς ἐγὼ ἤκουσα, εἶναι αὐτόν [prev. author] 4.76]]; ὡς γὰρ.. ἤκουσά τινος, ὅτι.. [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 6.4.18 codices]]; ἁνὴρ ὅδ᾽ ὡς ἔοικεν οὐ νεμεῖν (for οὐ νεμεῖ, ὡς ἔοικε), [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Trachiniae” 1238.]]

__A.II.2
in elliptical phrases, so far as.. (compare supr. Ab.[Refs 5th c.BC+ [1.3) ὡς ἐμοί [prev. author] “Aj.” 395 (Lyric poetry); so ὥς γε ἐμοὶ κριτῇ 2nd-3rd c.AD: Aelianus “Varia Historia” 2.41 and ὥς γ᾽ ἐμοὶ χρῆσθαι κριτῇ 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Alcestis” 801; ὡς ἐμῇ δόξῃ 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “de Vectigalibus” 5.2]]; ὡς ἀπ᾽ ὀμμάτων (i.e. εἰκάσαι) to judge by eyesight, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Coloneus” 15]]: especially in such phrases as οὐκέτι πολλὸν χωρίον, ὡς εἶναι Αἰγύπτου [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 2.8]]; οὐδὲ ἀδύνατος, ὡς Αακεδαιμόνιος for a Lacedaemonian, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 4.84, compare 1st c.BC: Dionysius Halicarnassensis 10.31; ὡς ἀνθρώποις 5th c.BC: Alcmaeon Philosophus 1]]; φρονεῖ.. ὡς γυνὴ μέγα for a woman, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Tyrannus” 1078]]; πιστός, ὡς νομεύς, ἀνήρ [Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. work] 1118; μακρὰν ὡς γέροντι.. ὁδόν [prev. author] “OC” 20, compare 385, “Ant.” 62, etc.; ὡπλισμένοι ὡς ἐν τοῖς ὄρεσιν ἱκανῶς 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 4.3.31; also with ἄν, μεγάλα ἐκτήσατο χρήματα, ὡς ἂν εἶναι Ῥοδῶπιν 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 2.135 codices (ἂν secl. Krüger, Ῥοδώπιος conjecture Valck.)]]:—for ὡς εἰπεῖν and the like, see below [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Bacchylides Lyricus 11.3.]]

__A.II.3
ὡς attached to the object of the Verb, as, ἑωυτὸν ὡς ἐχθρὸν λυπέει [Refs 5th c.BC+ [3rd c.AD: Democritus Epigrammaticus 88; ἔλαβεν ἀμφοτέρους ὡς φίλους ἤδη 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 3.2.25; ἐν οἰκήματι ᾧ ὡς ταμιείῳ ἐχρῆτο 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Protagoras” 315d]].— For the similar usage of ὡς with Participles and Prepositions, see below with

__A.III
with Adverbs:

__A.III.a
with the Posit., ὡς ἀληθῶς truly, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Phaedrus” 234e (compare ἀληθής 111.1b: as if _adverb_ of τὸ ἀληθές)]]; ὡς ἑτέρως in the other way, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [[prev. work] 276c, 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 18.212]] (adverb of ὁ ἕτερο; see at {ἕτερος} see 2) (see. below [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 1.1)]]; ὡς ἠπίως, ὡς ἐτητύμως, [LXX+5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Electra” 1438 (Lyric poetry), 1452; ὡς ὁμοίως “SIG” 708.34 (Istropolis, 2nd c.BC), LXX.4Mac.5.21, 1 “Enoch” 5.3, “IG” 7.2725.16 (Acraeph., 2nd c.AD)]]; ὡς ἐναλλάξ [Refs 4th c.BC+ [2nd c.AD: Vettius Valens Astrologus 215.9, 340.2; ὡς παντελῶς [prev. author] 184.26; ὡς ἄλλως 4th c.BC: Isaeus Orator 7.27, 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 6.32; ὡς ἐνδεχομένως “PPetr.” 2p.53 (3rd c.BC)]]; in ὣς αὔτως (see. ὡσαύτως) we have the adverb of ὁ αὐτός, but the ὥς retains its demonstrative force, as does ὁ in Homer; ὡς ἀληθῶς, ὡς ὁμοίως, and ὡς παντελῶς may be modelled on ὣς αὔτως, with which they are nearly synonymous; so also ὡς ἑτέρως and ὡς ἐναλλάξ, which are contrasted with it.

__A.III.b
with adverbs expressing anything extraordinary, θαυμαστῶς or θαυμασίως ὡς, ὑπερφυῶς ὡς, (see entry).; ὡς is sometimes separated by several words from its adverb, as θαυμαστῶς μοι εἶπες ὡς παρα᾽ δόξαν [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Phaedo” 95a; ὑπερφυῶς δὴ τὸ χρῆμα ὡς δύσγνωστον φαίνεται [prev. author] Alcaeus2.147c, compare “Phd.” 99d.]]

__A.III.c
with the superlative, as much as can be, ὡς μάλιστα [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 1.141, etc.: ὡς ῥᾷστα]] as easily as possible, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Prometheus Vinctus” 104; ὡς πλεῖστα 3rd c.AD: Democritus Epigrammaticus 189]]; ὠς τάχιστα as quickly as possible, [Refs 7th c.BC+ [7th-6th c.BC: Alcaeus Lyricus “Supp.” 4.15, etc.; more fully expressed, ὡς δυνατὸν ἄριστα 5th-6th c.BC: Isocrates Orator 12.153; ὡς ἐδύναντο ἀδηλότατα 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 7.50; μαχομένους ὡς ἂν δυνώμεθα κράτιστα 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 3.2.6; ὡς οἷόν τε βελτιστον 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 403d]]; ὡς ἀνυστὸν κάλλιστα Diog.[Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd c.AD: Apollonius Biographus 3: ὡς and ὅτι]] are sometimes found together, where one is superfluous, ὡς ὅτι μάλιστα [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Leges” 908a; βοῦν ὡς ὅτι κάλλιστον “IG” 22.1028.17 (2nd-1st c.BC)]]; see infr. G.

__A.III.d
with comparative, ὡς θᾶσσον [Refs 2nd c.BC+ [2nd c.BC: Polybius Historicus 1.66.1, 3.82.1.]]

__A.III.e
in the phrases ὡς τὸ πολύ, ὡς ἐπὶ τὸ πολύ, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 330c, 377b]]; ὡς ἐπὶ τὸ πλεῖον for the more part, commonly, ὡς ἐπὶ πλεῖστον [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 2.34]]; ὡς ἐπὶ τὸ πλῆθος, ὡς πλήθει, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 364a, 389d; ὡς τὸ ἐπίπαν 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 7.50, etc.; ὡς τὰ πολλά 2nd-3rd c.AD: Aelianus “De Natura Animalium - Ar.Byzantine Epit.” 12.17.]]

__A.III.2
with adjectives,

__A.III.2.a
Posit., ὑπερφυεῖ τινι.. ὡς μεγάλῃ βλάβῃ [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Gorgias” 477d.]]

__A.III.2.b
with superlative, ὡς ἄριστοι τὰς φύσεις [Refs [[prev. author] “Ti.” 18d; ὅπως ὡς βέλτισται ἔσονται [prev. author] “Grg.” 503a; ὡς ὅτι βέλτιστον [prev. author] “Smp.” 218d.]]

__A.III.2.c
separated from the adjective by a preposition, ὡς ἐς ἐλάχιστον [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 1.63, compare 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 18.246; ὡς ἐν βραχυτάτοις 5th c.BC: Antipho Orator 1.18; ὡς ἐν ἐχυρωτάτῳ ποιεῖσθαι 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 1.6.26, etc.]]

__A.III.2.Ac
Relat. and Interrog., how, μερμήριζε.. ὡς Ἀχιλῆα τιμήσειε [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 2.3, compare 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 365a; ἐβουλεύοντο ὡς.. στήσονται 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 3.84, etc.; οἷα δεῖ λέγειν καὶ ὥς 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Ethica Nicomachea” 1128a1]]; ὡς πέπραται how, i. e. at what price the goods have been sold, [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [“PCair.Zen.” 149 (3rd c.BC)]]; so οὐκ ἔσθ᾽ ὡς.. (for the more usually ὅπως) nowise can it be that.., [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Antigone” 750]]; οὐκ ἔσθ᾽ ὡς οὐ.., [Refs [[prev. author] “Ph.” 196 (_anapaest meter_, Porson for οὐκ ἔστιν ὅπως ου)]]; οἶσθ᾽ ὡς πόησο; by a mixture of constructions for ὡς χρὴ ποιῆσαι or ὡς ποιήσεις, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. author] “OT” 543, compare 5th c.BC: Hermippus Comicus 43, 4th-3rd c.BC: Menander Comicus 916]]; οἶσθ᾽ ὡς μετεύξει is falsa lectio in [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Medea” 600 (μέτευξαι Elmsley)]]; similarly, οἶσθα.. ὡς νῦν μὴ σφαλῇς [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Coloneus” 75.]]

__A.III.2
ὡς ἂν ποήσῃς however (in whatever way) thou mayest act, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. author] “Aj.” 1369, compare 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Symposium” 181a; αὐτῷ ὥς κεν ἅδῃ, τὼς ἔσσεται 3rd c.BC: Apollonius Rhodius Epicus 3.350.]]

__A.III.2.Ad

__B
ὡς as CONJUNCTION:

__B.I
with Substantive clauses, to express a fact, ={ὅτι}, that.

__B.II
with Final clauses, to express an end or purpose, ={ἵνα, ὅπως}, so that, in order that.

__B.III
Consecutive, ={ὥστε}, so that.

__B.IV
Causal, since, because.

__B.I
with Substantive Clauses, with verbs of learning, saying, etc., that, expressing a fact, γνωτὸν.., ὡς ἤδη Τρώεσσιν ὀλέθρου πείρατ᾽ ἐφῆπται [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 7.402, compare 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 3.194, etc.: in commands, προεῖπεν ὡς μηδεὶς κινήσοιτο 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Historia Graeca (Hellenica)” 2.1.22]]: with Verbs of fear or anxiety, with future indicative, μηκέτ᾽ ἐκφοβοῦ, μητρῷον ὥς σε λῆμ᾽ ἀτιμάσει ποτέ [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Electra” 1427, compare 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 6.2.30]]; μὴ φοβοῦ ὡς ἀπορήσεις [Refs 4th c.BC+ [[prev. work] 5.2.12, compare 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 10.36]]; a sentence beginning with ὡς is sometimes, when interrupted, resumed by ὅτι, and vice versa, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 5.3.30, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 470d, “Hp.Ma.” 281c]]; so ὡς with a finite Verb passes into the accusative and infinitive, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.70, 8.118: both constructions mixed in the same clause, ἐλογίζετο ὡς.. ἧττον ἂν αὐτοὺς ἐθέλειν.. 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 8.1.25, compare “HG” 3.4.27: after primary tenses (including historic _present_) ὡς]] is followed by indicative, after historic tenses by optative (sometimes by indicative, both constructions in ὑπίσχοντο.. ἀμυνέειν, φράζοντες ὡς οὔ σφι περιοπτέη ἐστὶ ἡ Ἑλλὰς ἀπολλυμένη.. ἀλλὰ τιμωρητέον εἴη [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 7.168)]]: sometimes with optative after a primary tense, κατάπτονται.. λέγοντες ὡς Ἀρίστων.. οὐ φήσειε [Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. author] 6.69, compare 1.70, 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 1.38, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Charmides” 156b.]]

__B.I.2
with Verbs of feeling, χαίρει δέ μοι ἦτορ, ὥς μευ ἀεὶ μέμνησαι [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 23.648; ἄχος ἔλλαβ᾽ Ἀχαιοὺς ὡς ἔπεσ᾽ 16.600.]]

__B.II
with Final Clauses, that, in order that; in this sense ὡς and ὡς ἄν, Epic dialect ὥς κεν, are used with the subjunctive after primary tenses of the indicative, and with the optative after the past tenses, βουλὴν ὑποθησόμεθ᾽.., ὡς μὴ πάντες ὄλωνται [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 8.37; τύμβον χεύαμεν.., ὥς κεν τηλεφανὴς.. εἴη 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 24.83; ἡμεῖς δ᾽ ἴωμεν ὡς, ὁπηνίκ᾽ ἂν θεὸς πλοῦν ἡμὶν εἴκῃ, τηνικαυθ᾽ ὁρμώμεθα 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Philoctetes” 464; [νέας] διηκοσίας περιέπεμπον.. ὡς ἂν μὴ ὀφθείησαν 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 8.7. b. rarely with]]future indicative, ὡς μὴ ὦν αὐτοὶ τε ἀπολέεσθε (conjecture Cobet for ἀπόλεσθε) κἀμὲ τρώσετε, ἐς ἄλλον τινὰ δῆμον ἀποίχεσθε [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Hecataeus Milesius Historicus 30J.]]

__B.II.2
ὡς is also used with past tenses of the indicative to express a purpose which has not been or cannot be fulfilled, τί μ᾽ οὐκ ἔκτεινας, ὡς ἔδειξα μήποτε..; so that I never should.., [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Tyrannus” 1392; ἔδει τὰ ἐνέχυρα λαβεῖν, ὡς μηδ᾽ εἰ ἐβούλετο ἐδύνατο ἐξαπατᾶν 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 7.6.23; compare ἵνα 5th c.BC: Bacchylides Lyricus 1.3, ὅπως 5th c.BC: Bacchylides Lyricus 1.3.]]

__B.II.3
ὡς with infinitive, to limit an assertion, ὡς μὲν ἐμοὶ δοκέειν [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 6.95, compare 2.124; ὡς εἰπεῖν λόγῳ [prev. work] 53]]; or ὡς ἔπος εἰπεῖν,compare ἔπος [Refs [11.4]]; ὡς συντόμως, or ὡς συνελόντι εἰπεῖν to speak shortly, to be brief, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Oeconomicus” 12.19, “Mem.” 3.8.10]]; ὡς εἰκάσαι to make a guess, i.e. probably, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.34, etc.; ὡς μικρὸν μεγάλῳ εἰκάσαι 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 4.36 (so without ὡς, οὐ πολλῷ λόγῳ εἰπεῖν 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.61), see supr. Ab. 11.1, 2.]]

__B.III
to express Consequence, like{ὥστε}, so that, frequently in [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus, εὖρος ὡς δύο τριήρεας πλέειν ὁμοῦ]] in breadth such that two triremes could sail abreast, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 7.24; ὑψηλὸν οὕτω.., ὡς τὰς κορυφὰς αὐτοῦ οὐκ οἷά τε εἶναι ἰδέσθαι 4.184]]; so in Trag. and Prose, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Persae” 437, +others, 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Tyrannus” 84, 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 3.5.7, etc.; ἀπέχοντας ἀπ᾽ ἀλλάλων ὡς ἦμεν Ϝικατίπεδον ἄντομον “Tab.Heracl.” 1.75; οὕτως.. ὡς ὁμολογεῖν 4th c.AD: Julianus Imperator “Orationes” 5.164d; ὡς καὶ τοὺς τεχνίτας λανθάνειν “PHolm.” 9.13]]; also, like{ὥστε}, with Indic., οὕτω κλεινὴ ἐγένετο, ὡς.. ἐξέμαθον [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 2.135, compare 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Trachiniae” 590, 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Historia Graeca (Hellenica)” 4.1.33.]]

__B.III.2
ἢ ὡς after a comparative, μάσσον᾽ ἢ ὡς ἰδέμεν [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “O.” 13.113; μαλακώτεροι.. ἢ ὡς κάλλιον αὐτοῖς 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 410d; compare ὥστε 5th c.BC: Bacchylides Lyricus 1.2: with words implying comparison, ὀλίγοι ἐσμὲν ὡς ἐγκρατεῖς εἶναι αὐτῶν]] too few to.., [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 4.5.15, γραῦς εἶ, ὦ Ἐλπινίκη, ὡς τηλικαῦτα διαπράττεσθαι πράγματα]] too old to.. [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Stesimbrotus Historicus 5J.]]

__B.III.3
ὡς is sometimes omitted where the antecedent demonstrative is expressed, οὕτω ἰσχυραί, μόγις ἂν διαρρήξειας so strong, you could hardly break them, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 3.12; ῥώμη σώματος τοιήδε, ἀεθλοφόροι τε ἀμφότεροι ἦσαν [prev. author] 1.31.]]

__B.IV
Causal, inasmuch as, since, τί ποτε λέγεις, ὦ τέκνο; ὡς οὐ μανθάνω [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Philoctetes” 914, compare 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Phoenissae” 843, 1077, 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Ranae” 278: with _optative_, μὴ καὶ λάθῃ με προσπεσών· ὡς μᾶλλον ἂν ἕλοιτο μ᾽ ἢ τοὺς πάντας Ἀργείους λαβεῖν 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Philoctetes” 46.]]

__B.IV.2
on the ground that.., with future indicative, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Lysias Orator 30.27.]]

with Participles in oblique cases, λέγουσιν ἡμᾶς ὡς ὀλωλότας they speak of us as dead, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Agamemnon” 672; ὡς μηδὲν εἰδότ᾽ ἴσθι μ᾽ ὧν ἀνιστορεῖς 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Philoctetes” 253; τὸν ἐκβαίνοντα κολάζουσιν ὡς παρανομοῦντα 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 338e; ἵνα μὴ ἀγανακτῇ ὑπὲρ ἐμοῦ ὡς δεινὰ πάσχοντος [prev. author] “Phd.” 115e, compare 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 5.85, 9.54; νῦν δέ σου τὰ ἔργα φανερὰ γεγένηται οὐχ ὡς ἀνιωμένου ἀλλ᾽ ὡς ἡδομένου τοῖς γιγνομένοις 5th c.BC: Lysias Orator 12.32; κτύπος φωτὸς ὡς τειρομένου [του] 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Philoctetes” 202 (Lyric poetry)]]; ἐν ὀλιγωρίᾳ ἐποιοῦντο, ὡς, ὅταν ἐξέλθωσιν, ἢ οὐχ ὑπομενοῦντας σφᾶς ἢ ῥᾳδίως ληψόμενοι βίᾳ made light of the matter, in the belief that.., [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 4.5.]]—Both constructions in one sentence, τοὺς κόσμους εἴασε χαίρειν ὡς ἀλλοτρίους τε ὄντας καὶ πλέον θάτερον ἡγησάμενος ἀπεργάζεσθαι [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Phaedo” 114e, compare 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 1.5.9.]]

ὡς before Preps., ἀνήγοντο ὡς ἐπὶ ναυμαχίαν (variant{-ίᾳ}) [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 1.48, compare 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Historia Graeca (Hellenica)” 2.1.22; φρύγανα συλλέγοντες ὡς ἐπὶ πῦρ [prev. author] “An.” 4.3.11]]; κατέλαβε τὴν ἀκρόπολιν ὡς ἐπὶ τυραννίδι, expressing the purpose, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 1.126; ἀπέπλεον.. ὡς ἐς τὰς Ἀθήνας [prev. author] 6.61; πλεῖς ὡς πρὸς οἶκον 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Philoctetes” 58; τὸ βούλευμ᾽ ὡς ἐπ᾽ Ἀργείοις τόδ᾽ ἦν [prev. author] “Aj.” 44: in these passages ὡς]] marks an intention; not so in the following: ἀπαγγέλλετε τῇ μητρὶ [χαίρειν] ὡς παρ᾽ ἐμοῦ [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 8.7.28; also ὡς ἀπὸ τῆς πομπῆς 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 327c; ὡς ἐκ κακῶν ἐχάρη 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 8.101.]]

__D

__D.I
as an exclamation, how, mostly with adverbs and adjectives, ὡς ἄνοον κραδίην ἔχες how silly a heart hadst thou! [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 21.441]]; ὡς ἀγαθὸν καὶ παῖδα λιπέσθαι how good is it.., [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 3.196, compare 24.194; φρονεῖν ὡς δεινόν 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Tyrannus” 316]]; ὡς ἀστεῖος ὁ ἄνθρωπος how charming he is! [LXX+5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Phaedo” 116d; ὡς ἐμεγαλύνθη τὰ ἔργα σου, Κύριε LXX.Psa.91(92).6, 103(104).24]]; in indirect clauses, ἐθαύμασα τοῦτο, ὡς ἡδέως.. ἀπεδέξατο marvelled at seeing how.., [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Phaedo” 89a.]]

__D.I.2
with Verbs, ὥς μοι δέχεται κακὸν ἐκ κακοῦ αἰεί how constantly.., [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 19.290, compare 21.273]]; ὡς οὐκ ἔστι χάρις μετόπισθ᾽ εὐεργέων how little thanks remain! [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 22.319]]; ὡς ὄχλος νιν.. ἀμφέπει see how.., [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Phoenissae” 148]]; ὡς ὑπερδέδοικά σου how greatly.., [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Antigone” 82; so perhaps ὡς οἰμώξεται 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Ranae” 279; ὡς ἅπανθ᾽ ὑμῖν τυραννίς ἐστι [prev. author] “V.” 488 (troch.).]]

__D.II
to mark a wish, oh that! with optative alone, ὡς ἔρις.. ἀπόλοιτο [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 18.107; ὡς ἀπόλοιτο καὶ ἄλλος 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 1.47, compare 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Electra” 126 (Lyric poetry)]]; also ὡς ἄν or κε with optative, ὡς ἂν ἔπειτ᾽ ἀπὸ σεῖο οὐκ ἐθέλοιμι λείπεσθαι [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 9.444; ὥς κέ οἱ αὖθι γαῖα χάνοι 6.281.]]

__D.II.2
joined with other words of wishing, ὡς ὤφελες αὐτόθ᾽ ὀλέσθαι [Refs 8th c.BC+ [3.428; ὡς δὴ μὴ ὄφελον νικᾶν 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 11.548.]]

__E
ὡς with numerals marks that they are to be taken only as a round number, as it were, about, nearly, σὺν ἀνθρώποις ὡς εἴκοσι [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 3.3.5]]; also ὡς πέντε μάλιστά κῃ about five (see. μάλα [Refs 5th c.BC+ [111.5), 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 7.30]]:—also with words compounded with numerals, δέπας.. ὡς τριλάγυνον [Refs 7th c.BC+ [7th-6th c.BC: Stesichorus Lyricus 7]]; παῖς ὡς ἑπτέτης of some seven years, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Gorgias” 471c; δρέπανα ὡς διπήχη 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 6.1.30, compare “An.” 5.4.12; compare ὡσεί 111.]]

__F
ὡς in some elliptical (or apparently elliptical) phrases:

__F.1
ὡς τί δὴ τόδε (i.e. γένηται); to what end? [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Orestes” 796 (troch.); compare ἵνα 5th c.BC: Bacchylides Lyricus 11.3c.]]

__F.2
know that (i.e. ἴσθι), ὡς ἔστιν ἀνδρὸς τοῦδε τἄργα ταῦτά σοι [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Ajax” 39; ὡς τοῦτό γ᾽ ἔρξας δύο φέρει δωρήματα [prev. author] “Ph.” 117; ὡς τῆσδ᾽ ἑκοῦσα παιδὸς οὐ μεθήσομαι 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Hecuba” 400, compare “Med.” 609, “Ph.” 720; ὡς τάχ᾽ οὐκέθ᾽ αἱματηρὸν.. ἀργήσει ξίφος [prev. work] 625 (troch.)]]; so in Comedy texts, ὡς ἔστ᾽ ἐν ἡμῖν τῆς πόλεως τὰ πράγματα [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Lysistrata” 32, compare 499 (_anapaest meter_), “Ach.” 333 (troch.), “Nu.” 209; also ἀλλ᾽ ὡς ἀπὸ τοῦ τείχους πάρεστιν ἄγγελος οὐδείς [prev. author] “Av.” 1119.]]

__F.3
ὡς ἕκαστος, ἕκαστοι, each severally (whether in respect of time, place, or other difference), ξυνελέγοντο.. Κορίνθιοι δισχίιοι ὁπλῖται, οἱ δ᾽ ἄλλοι ὡς ἕκαστοι, Φλειάσιοι δὲ πανστρατιᾷ [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 5.57, compare 1.107, 113]]; πρώτη τε αὕτη πόλις ξυμμαχὶς παρὰ τὸ καθεστηκὸς ἐδουλώθη, ἔπειτα δὲ καὶ τῶν ἄλλων ὡς ἑκάστη [ξυνέβη] (ξ. secl. Krüger: ἀπὸ κοινοῦ ἐδουλώθη [Refs [Scholia [same place]) [prev. author] 1.98; ἄλλοι τε παριόντες ἐγκλήματα ἐποιοῦντο ὡς ἕκαστοι [prev. work] 67, compare 7.65]]; χρησμολόγοι τε ᾖδον χρησμοὺς παντοίους, ὧν ἀκροᾶσθαι ὡς ἕκαστος ὥρμητο, i. e. different persons ran to listen to different prophecies, [Refs [[prev. author] 2.21]]; τὰς ἄλλας ὡς ἑκάστην ποι ἐκπεπτωκυῖαν ἀναδησάμενοι ἐκόμιζον ἐς τὴν πόλιν they made fast to the rest wherever each (ship) had been run ashore, [Refs [[prev. author] 7.74]]; οἱ δ᾽ οὖν ὡς ἕκαστοι Ἕλληνες κατὰ πόλεις τε ὅσοι ἀλλήλων ξυνίεσαν καὶ ξύμπαντες ὕστερον κληθέντες οὐδὲν πρὸ τῶν Τρωικῶν.. ἁθρόοι ἔπραξαν the various peoples that were later called by the common name of Greeks, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. author] 1.3; ὡς ἑκάστῳ ἔργον προστάσσων 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.114]]; ὡς ἑκάστην (one by one) αἱρέοντες (i.e. τὰς νήσους) οἱ βάρβαροι ἐσαγήνευον τοὺς ἀνθρώπους [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [[prev. author] 6.31, compare 79; ὡς ἑκασταχόσε 2nd-3rd c.AD: Dio Cassius Historicus 41.9, +others]]; rarely with a Verb, ὡς ἕκαστος ἀπικνέοιτο [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.29, compare 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 6.2: later ὡς]] follows ἕκαστος, ἑκάστῳ ὡς ὁ Θεὸς ἐμέρισεν μέτρον πίστεως [NT.Rom.12.3]:—for the etymology see infr. H; also ὡς ἑκάτεροι [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 3.74 (see. infr. H).]]

__G
ὡς pleonastic in ὡς ὅτι [NT+8th c.BC+ [1st c.BC: Dionysius Halicarnassensis 9.14, NT.2Cor.11.21, Scholia A 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 1.264, 129, 396, 3.280, “Anthologia Graeca” 9.530, uncertain reading in 1st c.BC-1st c.AD: Strabo Geographus 15.1.57.]]

__H
Etymology: this word is in origin five distinct words: [Refs [(1) ὡς ']]as' is the adverb from the Relat. ὅς (I.-[Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus]] stem yo-); with ὡς βέλτιστος cf. Sanskrit yācchrē[snull][tnull]á[hudot] 'the best possible': (2) ὧς 'thus' is the adverb of a Demonstr. stem so- found in Sanskrit sa, Gr. ὁ, Latin sō-c ([Refs [“Corpus Glossariorum Latinorum”]]; = ita, cf. Umbr. esoc); (3) ὡς postpositive (ὄρνιθες ὥς, etc.) constantly makes a preceding short closed syllable long in [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Homerus Epicus]], and must therefore have been ϝω; it may perhaps be related to Sanskrit vā, a form of va, iva (= [Refs [(1) or (2)]]like), Latin ve, Gr. ἦ[ϝ] ; [Refs [(4) ὡς preposition ']]to' is of doubtful origin (perhaps from *ὠς, cognate with Latin ōs 'face', Sanskrit ās: ὤς τινα ἐλθεῖν like{τί δέ δε φρένας ἵκετο πένθος};); (5) ὡς F. 3 is probably ϝως, adverb of ϝός the reflexive adjective, and means literal in his (their) own way (or place); it is idiomatically placed before ἕκαστος (ἑκάτερος),compare ϝὸν ϝεκάτερος [Refs [“Leg.Gort.” 1.18.]]

adverb of ὁ αὐτός, in like manner, just so, used by [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Homerus Epicus only at the beginning of clauses with δέ inserted, ὣς δ᾽ αὔτως.. 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 3.339, 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 9.31, +others; also in 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.215, +others, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Phaedo” 102e, 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Rhetorica” 1386b30, +others; after 8th c.BC: Homerus Epicus, in one word, ὡσαύτως καὶ]].. in like manner as.. [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 7.86, etc.; with _dative_, ὣς δ᾽ αὔτως τῇσι κυσὶ οἱ ἰχνευταὶ θάπτονται [prev. author] 2.67; πολλοὶ συνεξήκουον ὡ. ἐμοί 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Trachiniae” 372; ὥσπερ γὰρ.., ὡ. δὲ σύ [prev. author] “El.” 27]]; opposed to ὡς ἑτέρως, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Sophistici Elenchi” 169a31.]]

__2
further strengthened, ὡ. οὕτως so in like manner, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Gorgias” 460d; ὡ. κατὰ ταὐτά [prev. author] “Phd.” 78d.]]

ὡσεί
adv.,
__(a) as if, .as it were, like as, like: Mat.3:16 9:36, Act.2:3 6:15, Rom.6:13, Heb.1:12; γίνεσθαι (φαίνεσθαι) ὡσεί, Mrk.9:26, Luk.22:44 ([WH] R, mg., om.), Luk.24:11;

LSJ / STEPBible (TFLSJ)
ὡσεί
or ὡς εἰ, adverb as if, as though; with various moods:

__I
with optative, ἴσαν, ὡς εἴ τε πυρὶ χθὼν πᾶσα νέμοιτο [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 2.780, compare 11.389, 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 9.314, etc.]]

__I.2
ὡσεί τε with subjunctive, ἐρίλησ᾽ ὡς εἴ τε πατὴρ ὃν παῖδα φιλήσῃ [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 9.481.]]

__I.3
ὡς εἰ or ὡς εἴ τε, with indicative, ἕπονθ᾽ ὡς εἴ τε μετὰ κτίλον ἕσπετο μῆλα [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 13.492; φιάλαν ὡς εἴ τις.. δωρήσεται 5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “O.” 7.1.]]

__II
in comparisons, like, just as, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 16.59, 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 7.36, 8th-7th c.BC: Hesiodus Epicus “Scutum Herculis” 290, 5th c.BC: Bacchylides Lyricus 11.1, 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Antigone” 653, “El.” 234 (Lyric poetry)]], etc.: with participle, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 5.374, 8th-7th c.BC: Hesiodus Epicus “Scutum Herculis” 194; ὡς εἴ τε 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 11.474]]; with verb supplied, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 14.254, 5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “P.” 4.112]]; ὡσεί περ with participle, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th-7th c.BC: Hesiodus Epicus “Scutum Herculis” 189, compare 3rd c.BC: Theocritus Poeta Bucolicus 25.163 (nisi to be read εἰ περὶ σεῦ)]]; ὡς εἴ πέρ τε with a noun, [Refs [“hymnus ad Cererem” 215.]]

__II.2
ὡς εἴτε as it were, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “P.” 1.44.]]

__III
with Numerals, or measures of time and space, about, ὡσεὶ τριήκοντα σταδίων μάλιστά κῃ [NT+5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 7.109, compare 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Historia Graeca (Hellenica)” 1.2.9, LXX.Gen.24.55, +others, NT.Matt.14.21, +others]]

Abbott-Smith / STEPBible (TBESG)
ὥσ-περ
adv.,
just as, even as: Mat.6:2 20:28, Act.3:17, 1Co.8:5, 1Th.5:3 al.; in protasis, with οὕτως (καί) in apodosis: Mat.12:40, Luk.17:24, Jhn.5:21, Rom.5:19, Gal.4:29, Jas.2:26, al
(AS)

---

LSJ / STEPBible (TFLSJ)
ὥσπερ,
or ὥς περ, adverb of Manner, like as, even as, ζῆν ὥ. ἤδη ζῇς 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Philoctetes” 1396; ἐσῴζετ᾽ ἂν.., ὥ. οὐχὶ σῴζεται [Refs [[prev. author] “El.” 994]]; but the Verb is more often left to be supplied, οὔ τι κατακρύπτουσιν.., ὥ. Κύκλωπες [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 7.206, compare 2.333, 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 4.263, 14.50]]; ἔξεστί θ᾽, ὥ. Ἡγέλοχος, ἡμῖν λέγειν.. [Refs 8th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Ranae” 303; τεταγμένοι ὥ. ἔμελλον 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 4.93; τοῖς ἠτυχηκόσιν ὥ. ἐγώ 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 45.1; 8th c.BC: Homerus Epicus frequently puts a word between ὡς]] and περ, e.g. ὡς σύ περ αὐτή, ὡς τὸ πάρος περ, ὡς ἔσεταί περ [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 19.385, 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 5.806, 1.211]]; as for instance, ὅταν χορὸς.. γίγνηται, ὥ. [ὁ] εἰς Ηλον πεμπόμενος [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Memorabilia” 3.3.12]]; ὥσπερ differs from ὡς in [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Homerus Epicus]], in that it seldom has an antecedent expressed, as in [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 24.487]], τηλίκου ὥ. ἐγώ; also in [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th-7th c.BC: Hesiodus Epicus “Theogonia” 402]], ὣς δ᾽ αὔτως.., ὥ. ὑπέστ; but in Trag. and Attic dialect ὥ. is very frequently after demonstrative words; before οὕτως, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Melissus Philosophus 3, 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Aves” 188; after it, 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Trachiniae” 475, etc.]]; ὥ. καὶ.., οὕτω καὶ.. [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 7.5.75, compare 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 354b]]; ὥ.., ὧδε.. [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Tyrannus” 276; τοιοῦτος ὥ. 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Protagoras” 327d]]; αὐτοῦ ὥ. εἶχον just as they were, then and there, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 2.121.δ,compare 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Antigone” 1235; εὐθὺς ὥ. εἶχεν 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 4.1.19; εὐθὺς ὥ. ἔτυχε [prev. author] “HG” 3.1.19; τὰν τράπεζαν κάτθετε ὥ. ἔχει 5th c.BC: Sophron Comicus in “PSI” 11.1214a2]]; καὶ τὸν δαελὸν σβῆτε ὥ. ἔχει on the spot, [Refs [[prev. work] 14: with _genitive_,]] ὥ. ἔχει δόξης [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 612d: strengthened, ὥ. γε]]just exactly as, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Nubes” 673]]; ὥ. καί even as, ὡς καὶ ἐγώ περ [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 6.477; ὥ. καὶ ἄλλο τι 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 1.142, etc.: ὥ. also follows ἴσος, in 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 20.282, μοῖραν.. ἴσην, ὡς αὐτοί περ ἐλάγχανον,compare 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Electra” 533]]; so after ὁ αὐτός, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Phaedo” 86a, 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 9.33; after ὅμοιος, ὅμοιος ἀτμὸς ὥ. ἐκ τάφου πρέπει 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Agamemnon” 1311, compare 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 4.34.]]

__2
ὥσπερ ἄν with subjunctive, see below[Refs [111]]; with optative, ὥσπερ ἄν τις.. λέγοι [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Phaedo” 87b, compare 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Historia Graeca (Hellenica)” 3.1.14; compare ὡσπερεί 11.]]

__II
to limit or modify an assertion or apologize for a metaphor, as it were, so to speak, ὥ. ἀκονιτί [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 4.73; τὸν ἐγκέφαλον ὥ. σεσεῖσθαί μοι δοκεῖς 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Nubes” 1276, compare “Pax” 234; ἅμα μὲν.. ὥ. ὑπεφθόνει 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 4.1.13, compare 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Phaedrus” 270d, “Cra.” 384c]]; in later Gk. sometimes after the word to which it refers, ἐσφιγμένον ὥ. [Refs 3rd c.AD+ [3rd c.AD: Porphyrius Tyrius Philosophus “adversus Christianos - Abh. Berl. Akad.” 26]]; βάθρον ὥ. [Refs 5th c.BC+ [Scholia 5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “O.” 8.33; στέφανος ὥ. τῶν πόλεων τὰ τείχη [prev. work] 42]]: frequently with parts., ὥ. ἐγγελῶσα [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Electra” 277; ὥ. ἐντεταμένου τοῦ σώματος 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Phaedo” 86b]]; ὥ. τι τῶν ἄλλων εὐλόγως πεποιηκότες as if they had done, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Lysias Orator 12.7]]; ὥ. ἐξόν as if it were in our power, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 3.1.14; σιωπῇ ἐδείπνουν, ὥ. τοῦτο ἐπιτεταγμένον αὐτοῖς [prev. author] “Smp.” 1.11, compare “Mem.” 2.3.3]]; with a change of construction, ὥ. τὸν ἀριθμὸν τοῦτον ἔχοντα ἀνάγκην.., καὶ οὔτε.. οἷόν τε εἴη γενέσθαι [Refs [[prev. author] “HG” 2.3.19]]; τὴν ὥ. ἐπὶ τοῦ δίφρου ἕδραν a seat like that used in the chariot, [Refs [[prev. author] “Eq.” 7.5.]]

__III
rarely of Time,

__III.1
ὥσπερ ἄν ={ἕως ἄν}, so long as, or however long (compare ὡς Ad. [Refs 5th c.BC+ [2), ὥσπερ ἂν ζῶ 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Coloneus” 1361 (sed to be read ἕωσπερ).]]

__III.2
as soon as, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Pax” 24.]]

__IV
after a comparative (compare ὡς Ab. [Refs 6th c.BC+ [1.4); οὐ μείους ὥ. χίλιοι 6th c.BC: Xenophanes Poeta Philosophus 3.4; ἧττον.. ὥ. 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Historia Graeca (Hellenica)” 2.3.16]].—Cf. ὡσπερεί, ὥσπερ οὖν.

or ὥσπερ εἰ, adverb just as if, with indicative, ὥσπερ εἰ παρεστάτεις [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Agamemnon” 1201; with _optative_, ὥσπερ τις εἴ σοι.. μηδὲν διδοίη 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Coloneus” 776]]; τὸ ὡσπερεὶ φάναι to say 'as it were', [Refs 3rd c.AD+ [3rd c.AD: Longinus Rhetor 32.3]]; ὅμοια ὥ. εἰ.. [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Symposium” 4.37]]: with Nouns or parts., as it were, ὡ. ψῆτταν [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Lysistrata” 115; ὡ. προκείμενον [prev. author] “Ec.” 537; ἃ ὡ. στοιχεῖα τῶν ἄλλων ἐστί 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Cratylus” 422a.]]

__II
ὥσπερ ἂν εἰ or ὡσπερανεί (properly elliptical for ὥσπερ ἂν ἦν, εἰ.., or the like), [Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. author] “Grg.” 479a, “Prt.” 311b, 5th-6th c.BC: Isocrates Orator 4.148, 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 1.3.2]]; Doric dialect ὥσπερ αἰκ ἐξ ἑνὸς κελεύματος κεχάναντι they gape as it were 'by numbers' [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophron Comicus 25]]; ὥσπερ οὖν ἂν εἰ with imperfect, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 420c: compare ὥσπερ 1.2.]]

LSJ / STEPBible (TFLSJ)
ὥστε,
as adverb, bearing the same relation to ὡς as ὅστε to ὅς, and used by [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Homerus Epicus]] more frequently than ὡς in similes, when it is commonly written divisim, and is relative to a demonstrative ὥς: sometimes with present Indic., [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 2.459f, 12.421, 13.703]]: sometimes with aorist, ὥς τε λέων ἐχάρη [Refs [3.23: sometimes with]]subjunctive present or aorist, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [2.474f, 11.67, 16.428, 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 22.302]]: all three usages combined in one simile, with varied construction, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 5.136 - 9]]:—the verb is sometimes omitted, λάμφ᾽ ὥς τε στεροπή [Refs [10.154: this usage of ὥστε]] is chiefly Epic dialect [Refs 5th c.BC+ [(5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus uses ὧτε, which see)]], but it occurs in [Refs 7th c.BC+ [7th-6th c.BC: Alcaeus Lyricus (?) 27 (probably), 5th c.BC: Bacchylides Lyricus 12.124 and sometimes in Trag., κατώρυχες δ᾽ ἔναιον ὥστ᾽ ἀήσυροι μύρμηκες 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Prometheus Vinctus” 452, compare “Th.” 62, “Pers.” 424, “Ch.” 421 (Lyric poetry), 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Coloneus” 343, “Ant.” 1033, “Tr.” 112 (Lyric poetry).]]

__II
to mark the power or virtue by which one does a thing, as being, inasmuch as, like{ἅτε}, τὸν δ᾽ ἐξήρπαξ᾽ Ἀφροδίτη ῥεῖα μάλ᾽, ὥ. θεός [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 3.381, compare 18.518]]; ὥ. περὶ ψυχῆς since it was for life, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 9.423; ὥ. ταῦτα νομίζων 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.8, compare 5.83, 101, 6.94.]]

__B
as conjunction to express the actual or intended result of the action in the principal clause:

__B.I
mostly with infinitive, so as or for to do a thing, twice in [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Homerus Epicus, εἰ δέ σοι θυμὸς ἐπέσσυται, ὥ. νέεσθαι]] if thy heart is eager to return, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 9.42]]; οὐ τηλίκος.., ὥ. σημάντορι πάντα πιθέσθαι not of such age as to obey a master in all things, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 17.21; ῥηϊδίως κεν ἐργάσσαιο, ὥ. σε κεἰς ἐνιαυτὸν ἔχειν 8th-7th c.BC: Hesiodus Epicus “Opera et Dies” 44]]; ὥ. ἀποπλησθῆναι (ἀποπλῆσαι codices) τὸν χρησμόν [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 8.96: frequently in 5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus, “O.” 9.74, “N.” 5.1, 35, +others]]; also in Trag. and Attic dialect after demonstratives, οὔπω τοσοῦτον ἠπατημένος κυρῶ ὥστ᾽ ἄλλα χρῄζειν [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Tyrannus” 595, etc.]]; this construction is found in cases where (as in [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 9.42 above quoted) ὥστε]] seems superfluous; so after ἐθέλειν, Κύπρις.. ἤθελ᾽ ὥ. γίγνεσθαι τόδε [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Hippolytus” 1327]]; after ἔστι, for ἔξεστι, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Philoctetes” 656]]; after ψηφίζεσθαι, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 5.17]]; after ἐπαίρειν, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Supplices” 581; ἐπαγγελλόμενοι ὥ. βοηθεῖν 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 8.86]]; after words implying request, δεηθέντες.. ὥ. ψηφίσασθαι [Refs [[prev. author] 1.119; πεῖσαι ὥ. συγχωρῆσαι [prev. author] 8.45.]]

__B.I.2
after Comparatives with ἤ, when the possibility of the consequence is denied compare (ὡς [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Bacchylides Lyricus 111.2), μέζω κακὰ ἢ ὥστε ἀνακλαίειν]] woes too great for tears, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 3.14; μεῖζον ἢ ὥστε φέρειν δύνασθαι κακόν 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Memorabilia” 3.5.17: but in Poetry ὥστε]] is sometimes left out, νόσημα μεῖζον ἢ φέρειν [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Tyrannus” 1293; κρείσσον᾽ ἢ φέρειν κακά 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Hecuba” 1107 (rarely in Prose, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Theaetetus” 149c)]]; similarly with the Posit., ψυχρὸν ὥ. λούσασθαι too cold to bathe in, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Memorabilia” 3.13.3]]; ἡμεῖς ἔτι νέοι ὥ. διελέσθαι too young to.., [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Protagoras” 314b; γέρων ἐκεῖνος ὥ. δ᾽ ὠφελεῖν παρών 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Andromache” 80: this ὥστε is sometimes omitted after words implying comparison, ὀλίγους εἶναι στρατιῇ τῇ Μήδων συμβαλέειν]] too few.. [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 6.109; ταπεινὴ ἡ διάνοια ἐγκαρτερεῖν 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 2.61, etc.]]

__B.I.3
ὥστε.. ἄν is used with infinitive, of contingencies more or less improbable, οὕτως ἐκάετο ὥστε μήτε.. ἄλλο τι ἢ γυμνοὶ ἀνέχεσθαι, ἥδιστά τε ἂν ἐς ὕσωρ ψυχρὸν σφᾶς αὐτοὺς ῥίπτειν [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 2.49, compare 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Tyrannus” 374, “El.” 1316, 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 8.35.]]

__B.I.4
sometimes implying on condition that.., like{ἐφ᾽ ᾧτε}, παραδοῦναι σφᾶς αὐτοὺς Ἀθηναίοις, ὥστε βουλεῦσαι ὅ τι ἂν ἐκείνοις δοκῇ [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 4.37, compare 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 5.6.26.]]

__B.II
with Indic., to express the actual or possible result with emphasis, οὐκ οὕτω φρενοβλαβὴς ὁ Πρίαμος οὐδὲ οἱ ἄλλοι.., ὥ. κινδυνεύειν ἐβούλοντο [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 2.120 (perhaps delendum ἐβούλοντο)]]; ἀσθενέες οὕτω, ὥ... διατετρανέεις [Refs [[prev. author] 3.12]]; οὕτως ἀγνωμόνως ἔχετε, ὥ. ἐλπίζετε..; are you so foolish that you expect.. ? [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 2.26, βέβηκεν, ὥ. πᾶν ἐν ἡσύχῳ ἔξεστι φωνεῖν 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Coloneus” 82, compare “OT” 533: frequently in 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus, “Mem.” 2.2.3, +others]]; with ἄν and the imperfect or aorist implying a supposed case, ὥστ᾽, εἰ φρονῶν ἔπρασσον, οὐδ᾽ ἂν ὧδ᾽ ἐγιγνόμην κακός [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Coloneus” 271]]; ὥστε οὐκ ἂν ἔλαθεν αὐτόθεν ὁρμώμενος [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 5.6: ὥστε τὴν πόλιν ἂν ἡγήσω πολέμου ἐργαστήριον εἶναι 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Agesilaus” 1.26.]]

__B.II.2
at the beginning of a sentence, to mark a strong conclusion, and so, therefore, ὥστ᾽.. ὄλωλα καί σε προσδιαφθερῶ [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Philoctetes” 75; ὥστ᾽ οὐχ ὕπνῳ γ᾽ εὕδοντά μ᾽ ἐξεγείρετε [prev. author] “OT” 65; ὥ. καὶ ταῦτα λεχθήσεται 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Metaphysica” 1004a22: with _imperative_, θνητὸς δ᾽ Ὀρέστης, ὥ. μὴ λίαν στένε 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Electra” 1172; ὥ. θάρρει 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 1.3.18, compare 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Protagoras” 311a; ὥ. ἂν βούλησθε χειροτονήσατε 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 9.70 codex A (-ήσετε cett.)]]; before a question, ὥ. τίς ἂν ἀπετόλμησε..; [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Lysias Orator 7.28.]]

__B.II.3
with optative, with ἄν, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 2.16; βρέφος γὰρ ἦν τότ᾽.., ὥστ᾽ οὐκ ἂν αὐτὸν γνωρίσαιμ᾽ 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Orestes” 379, compare 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Tyrannus” 857, 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Acharnenses” 943 (Lyric poetry). b. with _optative_ in indirect speech, 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Historia Graeca (Hellenica)” 3.5.23]]; after optative in principal clause, [Refs [[prev. author] “Oec.” 1.13.]]

__B.II.4
with subjunctive, in order that, in Thessalian dialect, τὸς ταμίας φροντίσαι οὕστε.. γενειθεῖ τᾶ πόλι ἁ δόσις [Refs [“BCH” 59.38 (from Crannon); ἀντιλλαβέσθαι τᾶς πόλλιος (sic) οὕστε.. ἐς πάντουν ἐγλυθεῖ τοῦν δανείουν [prev. work]p.37.]]

__B.III
with participle, instead of infinitive, after a participle in the principal clause, τοσοῦτον ἁπάντων διενεγκόντες, ὥσθ᾽ ὑπὲρ Ἀργείων δυστυχησάντων Θηβαίοις.. ἐπιτάττοντες κτλ. [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Isocrates Orator 4.64 (assuming variant)]]; οὕτω σφόδρα μισοῦντα τοῦτον, ὥστε πολὺ δὴ (ἂν Dobree) θᾶττον διαθέμενον κτλ. [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Isaeus Orator 9.16; ὥστε.. δέον 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 3.1.]]

__B.IV
πόλεμος σκληρὸς ὥστε λίαν extremely, [LXX.2Ki.2.17.]

__B.V
in later Greek, followed by Preps., Παρμένοντι κλειδὸς ὥ. ἐπὶ τὸ Διοσκούριον [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [“Inscription Délos” 316.83 (3rd c.BC)]]; ξύλον ὥ. ἐπὶ τὴν ἅμαξαν [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [“IG” 11(2) 287 A 52 (3rd c.BC)]]; μόλυβδος ὥ. εἰς τὸ Κύνθιον [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [[prev. work]203 A 52 (3rd c.BC)]]; κριθῶν ὥ. εἰς τὰ κτήνη barley for the animals, [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [“PCair.Zen.” 251.5 (3rd c.BC)]]; ὥ. εἰς ξένια φοίνικας [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [“PHal.” 1.7.4 (3rd c.BC).]]

__B.V.b
with dative, for, χρεία αὐτοῦ ἐστὶν ὥ. Πισικλεῖ it is needed for P., [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [“PCair.Zen.” 241 (3rd c.BC)]]; ὥ. τοῖς χησίν [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [“IG” 11(2).287 A 45 (3rd c.BC).]]

Abbott-Smith / STEPBible (TBESG)
ὠφέλεια (WH, -λία), -ας, ἡ
[in LXX for יָעַל hi., בֶּצַע, etc. ;]
__1. assistance, help (Thuc., Plat., al.).
__2. profit, advantage, benefit (Hdt., Plat., al.): Rom.3:1, Ju 16.†

---

LSJ / STEPBible (TFLSJ)
ὠφέλ-εια, ἡ,
required by the metre (in iambics), [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Electra” 944, 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Thesmophoriazusae” 183]]; whereas ὠφελία is required in [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Andromache” 539 (_anapaest meter_), “fragment” 78 (Lyric poetry), 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Ecclesiazusae” 576 (Lyric poetry)]]: the best codices of [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus have ὠφελία more frequently than ὠφέλεια (although B always has ὠφέλεια in “Phdr.”), and ὠφελία]] is found in [Refs 5th c.BC+ [“IG” 12.69.24 (5th c.BC, Prose), 4th c.BC: Hyperides Orator “pro Euxenippo” 9, and frequently in 1st c.BC: Philodemus Gadarensis Epigrammaticus, as “Mus.” p.54 K., +others]]: Ionic dialect ὠφελίη [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 5.98, +others, “Anthologia Graeca” 6.187 (1st c.AD: Alpheus Epigrammaticus)]]:— help, aid, succour, especially in war, ἔπεμπον ἐς τὴν Ἐπίδαμνον.. τὴν ὠ. [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 1.26, compare 39; τὴν ὠ. παρέχειν τινί [prev. author] 3.13, compare 5th-6th c.BC: Andocides Orator 3.31; ὠ. ἀνδρὶ φέρειν 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Fragmenta” 78 (Lyric poetry); ὠ. προσλήψεσθαι 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 2.7; ἀπό τινων εὑρίσκεσθαι [prev. author] 1.31; τῆς ὠ. μεταλαμβάνειν [prev. author] 1.39; τυγχάνειν [prev. author] 6.17]]; ἐπάγεσθαί τινας ἐπ᾽ ὠφελίᾳ for aid, [Refs [[prev. author] 1.3, compare 5.38]]; ἀποχρήσασθαι τῇ ἑκατέρου ἡμῶν ὠ. to make full use of the assistance or services we both can give, [Refs 1st c.BC+ [[prev. author] 6.17; μετὰ τῶν κειμένων νόμων ὠφελίας [prev. author] 3.82, compare 1st c.BC: Dionysius Halicarnassensis “de Thucydide” 31]]; οὐδὲν ἰατρικῆς δεῖται οὐδ᾽ ὠφελίας or any other aid, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Lysis” 217a, compare “R.” 559b]]; καὶ τοῖσιν ἑλκωθεῖσιν ὠφελίαν (ὠφέλειαν codices, unmetrically) ἔχει [Refs [“Comica Adespota” 106.8.]]

__II
profit, advantage, βούλευμα ἀπ᾽ οὗ.. οὐδεμία ἔμελλε ὠφελίη ἔσεσθαι [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus [same place]; εἴ τις ὠφέλειά γε 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Electra” 944]]; τὴν κοινὴν ὠ. φυλάξαι the common interest of all, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 6.80; τίς ἂν εἴη ἡμῖν ὠ. εἰδόσιν αὐτ; 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Charmides” 167b]]; opposed to βλάβη, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 6.2.13, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus (see. below2), etc.]]; opposed to ζημία, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Memorabilia” 2.3.6; ἐπ᾽ ὠφελείᾳ ἐστί τι [prev. work] 1.4.4: with _genitive_ subjecti, τὴν ὠ. τὴν τῶν τειχέων]] their utility, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 7.139: with _genitive_ objecti, ἐπ᾽ ὠφελίᾳ τῶν φίλων]] for their benefit, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 334b]]; ὠφελίας ἕνεκα [Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. work] 398b; ἐναντία τῇ ἑαυτῶν ὠ. 5th-6th c.BC: Andocides Orator 2.2]]; ἐν ὠ. ἐστί 'tis of use, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “de Vectigalibus” 4.35]]; after ὠφελεῖν,compare ὠφελέω [Refs [1.5.]]

__II.2
source of gain or profit, service, frequently in plural, τὰς ὠ. τὰς ἐκ τῆς στρατείας.. ἐσομένας [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Isocrates Orator 4.15; αἱ κοιναὶ ὠ. 5th c.BC: Lysias Orator 19.62; αἱ ἀπὸ τινος γιγνόμεναι ὠ. 5th-6th c.BC: Isocrates Orator 4.29; ὠφελίας τε καὶ βλάβας ἀποδιδοῦσα [prev. author] “R.” 332d; αἱ παρὰ τῶν μισθοδοτούντων αὐτοὺς ὠ. 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 15.32.]]

__II.3
especially gain made in war, spoil, booty, [LXX+2nd c.BC+ [2nd c.BC: Polybius Historicus 2.3.8, 3.82.8, “Rev.Arch.” 6(1935).31 (_plural_, Amphipolis), LXX.2Mac.8.20]]; ὠ. μεγάλαι καὶ λάφυρα [Refs 2nd c.BC+ [1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus 2.255b; ὠφελείας ἀθροῖσαι [prev. author] “Cleom.” 12; πολλῆς ὠ. κυριεῦσαι 1st c.BC: Diodorus Siculus Historicus 15.36; τὴν χώραν γέμειν ὠφελείας 2nd c.BC: Polybius Historicus 3.80.3]]; τίθεσθαι τὰ χρήματα δι᾽ ὠφελείας to regard as booty, [Refs 1st c.BC+ [1st c.BC: Dionysius Halicarnassensis 7.37]]; so in the chase, game, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Cynegeticus” 6.4]]; so of a thief, ὠ. ἑτοίμην καὶ κατειργασμένην ἀφῆκεν [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Antipho Orator 2.1.4. (Prob. abstracted from οἰκ-ωφελία, which comes from οἶκον ὀφέλλειν]] 'to increase the οἶκος᾽; compare ὄφελος.)

LSJ / STEPBible (TFLSJ)
ὠφελ-έω,
future -ήσω [Refs [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Aves” 358, etc.]]: aorist ὠφέλησα [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 3.127, etc.]]: perfect -ηκα [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Hippocrates Medicus “περὶ διαίτης ὀξέων” 44, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Gorgias” 511e, etc.]]: pluperfect ὠφελήκη [Refs [[prev. author] “Ap.” 31d]]:—passive, future ὠφεληθήσομαι [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Andocides Orator 2.22, 4th c.BC: Isaeus Orator 10.16, 5th c.BC: Hippocrates Medicus “περὶ τῶν ἐντὸς παθῶν” 35, 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 3.2.20]]; more frequently future middle in passive sense, ὠφελήσομαι [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 6.18, 7.67, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 343c, 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Memorabilia” 1.6.14, variant in 5th c.BC: Lysias Orator 19.61]]: aorist ὠφελήθην [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 2.39, 5.90, etc.]]: perfect ὠφέλημαι [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Prometheus Vinctus” 222, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Gorgias” 512a, etc.]]: pluperfect ὠφέλητο [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 6.60]]: (ὄφελος):—help, aid, succour, first in [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus (see. below)]]; opposed to βλάπτω, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 6.14, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Phaedo” 107d]]; opposed to ζημιόω, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Isocrates Orator 6.5.]] —Construction:

__I
absolutely, to be of use or service, τὰ μηδὲν ὠφελοῦντα [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Prometheus Vinctus” 44, compare 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Fragmenta” 196, 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Iphigenia Aulidensis” 348 (troch.), 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Oeconomicus” 1.9; οὐδὲν ὠφελεῖ 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 2.87; τὸ πολλάκις ὠφελοῦν 5th-6th c.BC: Isocrates Orator 8.35.]]

__I.2
with accusative person, to be of service to, benefit, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 2.95, 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Prometheus Vinctus” 507; τὰς ψυχὰς ὠ. διδάσκοντες 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 2.3.23]]; ὠ. τινα ἔς τι to be of use to one towards a thing, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 4.75]]; τί δέ μ᾽ ὠφελήσουσ᾽ οἱ ῥυθμοὶ πρὸς τἄλφιτ; how will rhythms help me to earn my bread? [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Nubes” 648: _absolutely_, ἐπὶ τοῖς δεινοῖσιν 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Fragmenta” 84; διὰ τῶν ὤτων 1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus 2.38c]], compare 145b: with participle, αὐτοὺς ὠφελεῖ προσκείμενον [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Hippolytus” 970.]]

__I.2.b
especially of a general, enrich his soldiers by booty, [Refs 1st c.AD+ [1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus “Aemilius Paulus” 29; τοὺς στρατιώτας ὠφεληκὼς ἀπὸ τῶν στρατειῶν [prev. author] “Caes.” 12; compare ὠφέλεια 11.3.]]

__I.3
in Poets also (see. Thom.Mag.[Refs 5th c.BC+ [p.408R.) with _dative_ _person_, 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Prometheus Vinctus” 342, “Pers.” 842, 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Antigone” 560, 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Orestes” 666, 681, “Heracl.” 681, 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Aves” 421 (Lyric poetry); also in 5th c.BC: Antipho Orator 6.38, and variant in 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 5.23]]; the compounds προσωφελέω, ἐπωφελέω, συνωφελέω also take both constructions.

__I.4
with genitive, uncertain in οὐδεὶς ἔρωτος τοῦδ᾽ ἐφαίνετ᾽ ὠφελῶν [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Coloneus” 436 (perhaps to be read ἔρωτ᾽ ἐς τόνδ᾽).]]

__I.5
with accusative cognate, ὠφελίαν ὠ. τινα to render him a service, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 519e, compare “Euthd.” 275e; ὠφελίαν κοινῇ -οῦνται πάντες οἱ δημιουργοί [prev. author] “R.” 346c: with a _neuter_]] adjective, οὐδέν τινα ὠ. to do one no service, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 3.126, 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Alcestis” 875 (Lyric poetry)]]; πολλά, πλέον, πλεῖστον, ὡς πλεῖστα ὠ. τινα, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Isocrates Orator 3.30, 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Andromache” 679, 681, 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 6.14.]]

__II
passive, receive help or succour, derive profit or advantage, πρός τινος from a person or thing, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 2.68; ἔκ τινος 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Prometheus Vinctus” 222, 5th c.BC: Antipho Orator 3.2.3; ἀπό τινος 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 3.64, 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Oeconomicus” 1.15, compare 5th c.BC: Gorgias Rhetor et Sophista “Pal.” 10]]; ὑπό or παρά τινος, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Gorgias” 512a, “Amat.” 132d]]; ὠ. τοῦ νόμου to derive benefit from.., [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Antipho Orator 5.17 (uncertain reading)]]; τινι by a thing, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 3.67; διά τι [prev. work] 13]]; παρ᾽ ἐμοῦ ὠφελεῖσθαι to make something out of me, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Antipho Orator 2.2.13]]; ἐκ τῶν ὑμετέρων help the mselves, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Lysias Orator 27.7]]: especially of troops, acquire booty, πολλὰ παρὰ τὴν στρατείαν ὠ. [Refs 1st c.AD+ [1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus “Cat.Ma.” 10; ὠ. δι᾽ ἁρπαγῆς [prev. author] “Marc.” 19]]; ὠφελεῖσθαι πρός τι acquire advantage towards a thing, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Cynegeticus” 5.27: with]]participle, ὠφελεῖσθαι ἰδών to be profited by the sight of a thing, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 2.39: with adjective _neuter_, οὐδὲν ὠφελουμένη 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Antigone” 550: πολλὰ ὠφελεῖσθαι οὐδὲν πονοῦντες 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 3.2.20.]]

ἀγγέλλω,
(ἄγγελος): imperfect ἀγγέλλεσκον[Refs 5th c.AD+ [5th c.AD(?): Hesychius Legal icographus]]: Epic dialect and Ionic dialect future ἀγγελέω[Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 9.617, 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus, _Attic dialect_ ἀγγελῶ, _Doric dialect_ -ίω]] (ἀν-) [Refs [“Tab.Heracl.” 1.118]]: aorist 1 ἤγγειλα[Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Homerus Epicus]], Attic dialect: perfect ἤγγελκα[Refs 2nd c.BC+ [2nd c.BC: Polybius Historicus 35.4.2]], (κατ-) [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Lysias Orator 25.30]], (εἰσ-) [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Lycurgus Orator 1]], (περι-) [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 21.4:]] —middle (see. below): aorist ἠγγείλαμην (ἐπ-) [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 6.35, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Gorgias” 458d:]] —passive, future ἀγγελθήσομαι (ἀπ-) [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 19.324, later ἀγγελήσομαι]] (ἀν-) [LXX.Psa.21(22).30]: aorist ἠγγέλθην[Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus]], Attic dialect: perfect ἤγγελμαι[Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Choephori” 774, 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 8.97:]]pluperfect ἄγγελτο variant in [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 7.37:]] —aorist 2 passive ἠγγέλην is found [Refs [“IG” 1.27b]] (ἐπ-), [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Iphigenia Taurica” 932]], and became usual in Hellenistic Gk.,[cf. LXX.Josh.2.2] (ἀπ-), [Refs 1st c.AD+ [1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus “Antonius” 68, 2nd c.AD: Herodianus Grammaticus 3.7.1, etc.:]]aorist 2 active ἤγγελον is rare even in late writers, as (παρ-) [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd c.AD: Appianus Historicus “Bella Civilia” 1.121]] without imperfect as see l., though in [Refs 6th c.AD+ [“Anthologia Graeca” 7.614 (6th c.AD: Agathias Historicus et Epigrammaticus) ἀγγελέτην]] is required by the metre:—bear a message, ὦρτο δὲἾρις.. ἀγγελέουσα[Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 8.409; τινί 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 4.24, 15.458: with]]infinitive, οἵ κε.. κείνοις ἀγγείλωσι.. οἶκόνδε νέεσθαι may bring them word to return home,[Refs [16.350, compare “Etymologicum Magnum” 6.52]]: with accusative infinitive, κήρυκες δ᾽.. ἀγγελλόντων.. γέροντας λέξασθαι[Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 8.517.]]

__2
with accusative of things, announce, report, ἐσθλά[Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 10.448; φάος ἠοῦς 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 13.94; Ποσειδάωνι πάντα τάδε 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 15.159:—in Prose, μή τι νεώτερον ἀγγέλλει; 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Protagoras” 31c b]]; proverbial, οὐ πόλεμον ἀγγέλλεις 'that's good news', [Refs [[prev. author] “Phdr.” 242b]]; ἀγγέλλωμεν ἐς πόλιν τάδε ; [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Orestes” 1539]]; πρὸς τίν᾽ ἀγγεῖλαί με χρὴ λόγους ; [Refs [[prev. author] “Supp.” 399.]]

__3
with accusative person, bring news of.., εἴ κέ μιν ἀγγείλαιμι[Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 14.120; later, ἀ. περί τινος 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Electra” 1111]]:—dependent clauses are added with a conjunction, ἤγγειλ᾽ ὅττι ῥά οἱ πόσις ἔκτοθι μίμνε[Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 22.439]]; ἀ. ὡς.. [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Iphigenia Taurica” 704, 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 18.169]]; ὁθούνεκα.. [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Electra” 47:]] —also in participle, ἦ καὶ θανόντ᾽ ἤγγειλαν;[Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. work] 1452; Κῦρον ἐπιστρατεύοντα.. ἤγγειλεν 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 2.3.19, compare “Cyr.” 6.2.15; with ὡς, πατέρα τὸν σὸν ἀγγελῶν ὡς οὐκέτ᾽ ὄντα 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Tyrannus” 955; ἤγγειλας ὡς τεθνηκότα [prev. author] “El.” 1341.]]

__II
middle, only present, Τεύκρῳ ἀγγέλλομαι εἶναι φίλος I announce myself to him as a friend, [Refs [[prev. author] “Aj.” 1376.]]

__III
passive, to be reported of, ἐπὶ τὸ πλεῖον[Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 6.34]]: with participle, ζῶν ἢ θανὼν ἀγγέλλεται[Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Trachiniae” 73, compare 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Hecuba” 591, 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 3.16, 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Historia Graeca (Hellenica)” 4.3.13]]: with infinitive, ἤγγελται ἡ μάχη ἰσχυρὰ γεγονέναι[Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Charmides” 153b, compare 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 5.3.30:—ἠγγέλθη τοῖς στρατηγοῖς, ὅτι φεύγοιεν that.., [prev. author] “HG” 1.1.27:— ἐπὶ τοῖς ἠγγελμένοις 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 8.97. (ἀπ-αγγέλλω is more common in Oratt.)]]

1. to know , εὖ οἶδα I know  well; εὖ ἴσθι be assured : often with accusative rei, νοήματα οἶδε, μήδεα οἶδε he is versed in  counsels, (Homer); with neut. Adjs., πεπνυμένα, φίλα, ἀθεμίστια εἰδώς (Homer); also with genitive, τόξων εὖ εἰδώς cunning in the use of  the bow; οἰωνῶν σάφα εἰδώς (Odyssey by Homer): —; χάριν εἰδέναι τινί to acknowledge a debt to another, thank him , (Iliad by Homer), etc.:—;the Imperat. in protestations, ἴστω Ζεὺς αὐτός be  Zeus my witness , (Iliad by Homer); doric ἴττω Ζεύς, ἴττω (Aristophanes Comicus): —; εἰδώς absolute one who knows , εἰδυίηι πάντ᾽ ἀγορεύω (Iliad by Homer); ἰδυίηισι πραπίδεσσι with knowing  mind, (Iliad by Homer)
2. with infinitive to know how  to do, (Iliad by Homer), attic
3. with the participle to know that  so and so is the case, ἴσθι μοι δώσων know that  thou wilt give, (Aeschulus Tragicus); τὸν Μῆδον ἴσμεν ἐλθόντα (Thucydides)
4. οὐκ οἶδα εἰ, I know  not whether, expresses disbelief, like Lat. nescio an non, οὐκ οἶδ᾽ ἂν εἰ πείσαιμι (Euripides)
5. οἶδα or ἴσθι are often parenthetic, οἶδ᾽ ἐγώ (Euripides); οἶδ᾽ ὅτι, οἶσθ᾽ ὅτι, ἴσθ᾽ ὅτι, πάρειμι (Sophocles Tragicus); so, εὖ οἶδ᾽ ὅτι (Demosthenes Orator): —;in [variant datesTragica Adespota also, οἶσθ᾽ ὃ δρᾶσο; equivalent to δρᾶσον —; οἶσθ᾽ ; do —; know'st thou what? i. e. make haste and do; οἶσθ᾽ ὡς ποίησον, etc. (ML)

πρῶτος ὧν ἡμεῖς ἴδμεν the first we know of, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.6, etc.; παλαίτατος ὧν ἀκοῇ ἴσμεν 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 1.4: strengthened by εὖ or σάφα, εὖ τόδ᾽ ἴσθι]] know well, be assured of this, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Medea” 593; σάφ᾽ οἶδ᾽ ἐγώ 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Supplices” 740, etc.: frequently in 8th c.BC: Homerus Epicus with _neuter_]] adjective, to express character or disposition, ἄγρια οἶδε has fierceness in his heart, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 24.41]]; ἀθεμίστια ᾔδη had law lessness in his heart, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 9.189; αἴσιμα, ἄρτια ᾔδη, 14.433, 19.248]]; εἴ μοι ἤπια εἰδείη if he were kindly disposed towards me, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 16.73; φίλα εἰδότες ἀλλήλοισιν 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 3.277; κεχαρισμένα, πεπνυμένα εἰδώς, 8.584, 24.442]]: with genitive, ὃς σάφα θυμῷ εἰδείη τεράων [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 12.229; ὃς πάσης εἰδῇ σοφίης 15.412]]; τόξων ἐῢ εἰδώς cunning with the bow,[Refs 8th c.BC+ [2.718; αἰχμῆς ἐῢ εἰ. 15.525; οἰωνῶν σάφα εἰδώς 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 1.202; ἐῢ εἰδὼς τεκτοσυνάων 5.250; μάχης ἐῢ εἰδότε πάσης 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 2.823; κύνε εἰδότε θήρης 10.360; παῖδ᾽ ἔτ᾽ ἐόντ᾽ οὔ πω μάλα εἰδότε θούριδος ἀλκῆς 11.710; εἰδὼς πυγμαχίης 23.665; θεοπροπίων ἐῢ εἰδώς 6.438]]; χάριν εἰδέναι τινί acknowledge a debt to another, thank him,[Refs 5th c.BC+ [14.235, 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 3.21, etc.: _imperative_, frequently in protestations, ἴστω νῦν Ζεὺς αὐτός]] be Zeus my witness, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 10.329; ἴστω νῦν τόδε Γαῖα 15.36, etc.]]; Boeotian dialect ἴττω Ἡρακλῆς etc., [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Acharnenses” 860, etc.:]]participle εἰδώς, absolutely, one who knows, one acquainted with the fact, ἰδυίῃ πάντ᾽ ἀγορεύω [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 1.365; μετ᾽ εἰδόσιν ἀγορεύειν 10.250; μακρηγορεῖν ἐν εἰδόσιν 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 2.36, compare 3.53; μαθεῖν παρὰ τοῦ εἰδότος 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 337d, etc.]]; also ἰδυίῃσι πραπίδεσσι with knowing mind, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 1.608, +others]]

__2
with infinitive, know how to do, οἶδ᾽ ἐπὶ δεξιά, οἶδ᾽ ἐπ᾽ ἀριστερὰ νωμῆσαι βῶν [Refs 5th c.BC+ [7.238, compare 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Philoctetes” 1010, 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Vespae” 376]]; also, to be in a condition, be able, have the power, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Medea” 664, 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 4.40]]; of drugs, ὅσα λεπτύνειν οἶδε [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd c.AD: Alexander Rhetor Trall. “Febr.” 6]]; of a festival, οἶδε ἐκπέμπουσα δάκνειν Chor.p.124 [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Bacchylides Lyricus]]; learn, ἵν᾽ εἰδῇ μὴ 'πὶ τοῖς ἐμοῖς κακοῖς ὑψηλὸς εἶναι [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Hippolytus” 729.]]

__3
with participle, to know that such and such is the fact, the participle being in nominative when it is a predicate of the Subject of the Verb, ἴσθι μοι δώσων know that thou wilt give, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Agamemnon” 1670; ἴστω ὑπὸ τοῦ ἀδελφεοῦ ἀποθανών 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 4.76; οὐ γὰρ οἶδα δεσπότας κεκτημένος 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Hecuba” 397]]: in accusative when it is predicate of the Object, τοὺς φιλτάτους γὰρ οἶδα νῷν ὄντας πικρούς [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Choephori” 234; τὸν Μῆδον ἴσμεν ἐκ περάτων γῆς ἐλθόντα 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 1.69: with]]participle omitted, γῆν αὐτὰ οἶδεν ἀμφότερα (i.e. ὄντα) [Refs 4th c.AD+ [4th c.AD: Julianus Imperator “Orationes” 7.226a.]]

__4
less frequently c.accusative et infinitive, πλήθους.. ἂν σάφ᾽ ἴσθ᾽ ἕκατι βάρβαρον ναυσὶν κρατῆσαι [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Persae” 337, compare 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Philoctetes” 1329; εὖ ἴσθι τοῦτον.. ἰσχυρῶς ἀνιᾶσθαι 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 8.3.44; also εὖ τόδ᾽ ἴσθι, μηδάμ᾽ ἡμέρᾳ μιᾷ πλῆθος τοσουτάριθμον ἀνθρώπων θανεῖν 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Persae” 431; ἕν γ᾽ ἀκούσασ᾽ ἴσθι, μὴ ψευδῶς μ᾽ ἐρεῖν 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Iphigenia Aulidensis” 1005.]]

__5
with accusative followed by ὡς, ὅτι, etc., οἶδα κἀμαυτὴν ὅτι ἀλγῶ [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Electra” 332; ἐάν τινα εἰδῶσιν ὅτι ἄδικός ἐστι 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Protagoras” 323b, etc.]]

__6
οὐκ οἶδ᾽ εἰ.. I know not whether, to express disbelief or doubt, sometimes with ἄν transposed, οὐκ οἶδ᾽ ἂν εἰ πείσαιμί σε [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Alcestis” 48, compare 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 45.7: with Verb omitted after εἰ, as οὐκ οἶδ᾽ εἴ τις ἄλλος]] perhaps no other, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Isocrates Orator 6.1, 12.10.]]

__7
in similar ellipses with other Conjunctions, οὐκ οἶδ᾽ ὅπως I know not how, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 40c b; οὐκ οἶδ᾽ ὁπόθεν [prev. author] “Cra.” 396d.]]

__8
οἶδα, ἴσθι are frequently parenthetic, οἶδ᾽ ἐγώ [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Medea” 948; σάφ᾽ οἶδα [prev. work] 94, 963]]; also οἶδ᾽ ὅτι, οἶσθ᾽ ὅτι, ἴσθ᾽ ὅτι, πάρειμι δ᾽ ἄκων οὐχ ἑκοῦσιν, οἶδ᾽ ὅτι (i.e. πάρειμι) I know it well, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Antigone” 276]]; οἶδ᾽ ὅτι, frequently in [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator, as 9.1, +others; σάφ᾽ ἴσθ᾽ ὅτι 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Plutus” 889:]] —οἶσθ᾽ ὅ, οἶσθ᾽ ὡς, with _imperative_, are common in Trag. and Comedy texts, οἶσθ᾽ οὖν ὃ δρᾶσον; do—thou know'st what, i.e. make haste and do, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Equites” 1158, compare “Pax” 1051, etc.]]; οἶσθ᾽ ὡς πόησο; [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Tyrannus” 543]]; also οἶσθ᾽.. ὡς νῦν μὴ σφαλῇ; [Refs [[prev. author] “OC” 75]]; οἶσθα νῦν ἅ μοι γενέσθ; [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Iphigenia Taurica” 1203: rarely with the]]future, οἶσθ᾽ οὖν ὃ δράσεις (nisileg. δρᾶσον); [Refs [[prev. author] “Cyc.” 131, compare “Med.” 600 codices]]

deep_entry:
Abbott-Smith / STEPBible (TBESG)
scarcely, barely
Some manuscripts list ὀλίγος (G3641) in place of G6067 at 2Pe.2.18

---

LSJ / STEPBible (TFLSJ)
Included with:  ὀλίγος [ῐ], η, ον,
later ὀλίος (which see), of Size, little, small, frequently in [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Homerus Epicus, rarer later, opposed to μέγας, σάκος 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 14.376; κῦμα 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 10.94, etc.]]; ὀλίγῃ ὀπί with small, low voice, [Refs [14.492]]; of stature,[Refs 3rd c.BC+ [9.515; ὀ. κῶρος 3rd c.BC: Theocritus Poeta Bucolicus 1.47; οὐκ ὀλίγης αἷμα βοὸς κέχυται Callias Epigrammaticus “Aet.Oxy.” 2080.85]]; of Space, ὀ. χῶρος [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 10.161, etc.]]; of Time, χρόνος [Refs 5th c.BC+ [19.157, 23.418, 5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “N.” 7.38, etc.; ἐν βραχεῖ κὠλίγῳ χρόνῳ 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Fragmenta” 646 (cf. IV. 3).]]

__2
sometimes in a sense between that of Size and Quantity, ὀ. δόσις [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 6.208; οὖρα ὀλίγα]]not copious, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Hippocrates Medicus “ἐπιδημίαι” 1.2]]; ὑποστάσιες ὀλίγαι slight sediments, [Refs [[prev. work] 17]]; ὀ. καὶ οὐδέν little or nothing, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Apologia” 23a; οὐδὲν ἢ ὀ. 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “de Partibus Animalium” 651b17.]]

__3
of Degree, ὀ. καὶ μέγας of low and high degree, [Refs 7th c.BC+ [7th c.BC: Callinus Epicus 1.17.]]

__4
weak, ἀθυμοτέρη καὶ ὀλιγωτέρη φύσις [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Hippocrates Medicus “περὶ παρθενίων” 1.]]

__II
of Number, few, or of Quantity, little, not in [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Homerus Epicus]], frequently in Attic dialect, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Aves” 1417, “Eq.” 717, etc.]], but rare in Trag., as ὀλίγα κακά [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Persae” 330.—The governing body in Oligarchies and the oligarchical party in Democracies was called οἱ ὀ., 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 6.38, 8.9, etc.]]; ἡ ὑπὸ τῶν ὀ. δυναστεία, αἱ διὰ τῶν ὀ. δυναστεῖαι, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Politicus” 291d, 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 60.25; ἑνὸς καὶ πλήθους τὸ ὀ. μέσον 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Politicus” 303a.]]

__II.2
with infinitive, ὀλίγους.. στρατιῇ τῇ Μήδων συμβαλεῖν too few to engage.., [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 6.109, compare 7.207; μὴ.. αἱ σφέτεραι δέκα νῆες ὀλίγαι ἀμύνειν ὦσιν 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 1.50.]]

__III
neuter ὀλίγον as adverb, a little, slightly, little, with Verbs, ὀ. παρακλίνας [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 23.424, compare 11.52, 12.452; φροντίσας 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Cyclops” 163; ὀ. τοῦ ποιήματος προελθών 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Protagoras” 339d: also _neuter_ _plural_, ἠκροβολίσαντο ὀλίγα 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 3.73.]]

__III.2
with comparative adjectives, ὀλίγον προγενέστερος [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 23.789; ὀ. ἧσσον 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 15.365; στιβαρώτερον οὐκ ὀ. περ 8.187; φέρτερος οὐκ ὀ. περ 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 19.217]]; ὀ. τι πρότερον, variant for{ὀλίγῳ}, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 4.79, 81, compare 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Politicus” 262b, etc.; ὀ. ὕστερον [prev. author] “Grg.” 454b, etc.]]; but ὀλίγῳ is more frequently in Prose, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus [same places] (with variant), 7.113, +others, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Gorgias” 460c, “R.” 327c, etc.]]

__IV
special Phrases:

__IV.1
ὀλίγου δεῖν almost (see. δεῖ II); ὀλίγου ἐδέησε καταλαβεῖν wanted but little of overtaking, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 7.10.γ᾽: hence ὀλίγου]] alone, within a little, allbut, almost, ὀλίγου σεκύνες διεδηλήσαντο [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 14.37, compare 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Acharnenses” 348, 381, “Nu.” 722, 5th c.BC: Lysias Orator 14.17, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Protagoras” 361b, 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 19.334, etc.; ὀ. ἅπαντες 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Apologia” 22b; ὀ. ἐς χιλίους]]close upon [Refs 5th c.BC+ [1, 000, 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 4.124]]; ὀ. ἦλθεν ἑλεῖν[Refs 2nd c.AD+ [(see. below 9) 2nd c.AD: Pausanias Periegeta 1.13.6.]]

__IV.2
δι᾽ ὀλίγου at a short distance, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Phoenissae” 1098, 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 2.89, 3.21, uncertain in 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Septem contra Thebas” 762 (Lyric poetry)]]; for (during) a short time, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 1.77, 2.85, 3.43]]; within or after a short time, [Refs [[prev. author] 6.11, 47, 7.39, etc.]]; but

__IV.2.b
δι᾽ ὀλίγων in few words, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Philebus” 31d, etc.; see infr. VI. 2.]]

__IV.3
ἐν ὀλίγῳ (χώρῳ is added in [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 9.70)]] in a small space, within small compass, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Supplices” 1126 (Lyric poetry); ἐν ὀ. στρατοπεδευομένοις 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 4.26]]; κυκλωθέντων ἐν ὀ.[Refs 4th c.BC+ [[prev. work] 96; εἰς ταὐτὸ πάντα.. ἁθροίσαντ᾽ ἐν ὀ. 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 3.18]]; also ἐν ὀ. (i.e. χρόνῳ) for a brief time, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “P.” 8.92]]; but also, in a short time, quickly, ἔγνων καὶ περὶ τῶν ποιητῶν ἐν ὀ. τοῦτο [NT+5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Apologia” 22b, compare 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 4.55, NT.Act.26.28.]]

__IV.3.b
ἐν ὀλίγοις one among few, i.e. exceedingly, remarkably, ποταμὸς ἐν ὀ. μέγας [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 4.52; ἐν ὀλίγοισι Περσέων.. ἀνὴρ δόκιμος [prev. author] 9.41]]: frequently in later writers, [Refs 1st c.AD+ [1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus “Pompeius” 10, 3rd c.AD: Heliodorus Scriptor Eroticus 3.1; so σὺν ὀλίγοις, see below 10.]]

__IV.4
ἐξ ὀλίγου at short notice, suddenly, ἐξ ὀ. καὶ δι᾽ ὀργῆς [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 2.11, compare 61, 4.108, etc.]]

__IV.5
ἐς ὀλίγον, like{παρ᾽ ὀλίγον}, within a little, ἐς ὀ. ἀφίκετο τὸ στράτευμα νικηθῆναι [Refs [[prev. work] 129.]]

__IV.6
ἐπ᾽ ὀλίγον for a short time, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Hippocrates Medicus “προρρητικόν” 1.26, 3rd c.AD: Plotinus Philosophus 4.4.29, “Geoponica” 7.12.22, 10.7.10, etc.]]; a little at a time, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Hippocrates Medicus “περὶ τῶν ἐν κεφαλη—ͅ τρωμάτων” 18; εἴρηται ἐν τῷ [βιβλίῳ] ἐπ᾽ ὀλίγον]]a little way on, near the beginning, [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd c.AD: Galenus Medicus 15.428.]]

__IV.7
κατ᾽ ὀλίγον by little and little, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 1.69, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Timaeus” 85d, 2nd c.AD: Lucianus Sophista “Nec.” 11, etc.; ἐκ τοῦ κατ᾽ ὀ. 1st c.BC: Diodorus Siculus Historicus 15.34, 1st c.AD: Athenaeus Medicus cited in 4th c.AD: Oribasius Medicus 1.2.6]]: but the adjective frequently takes the gender and number of its substantive, κατ᾽ ὀλίγους [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 2.93, 8.113]]; οὗτοι κατ᾽ ὀλίγους γινόμενοι ἐμάχοντο fought few at a time, in small parties, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. author] 9.102, compare 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Theaetetus” 197d]]; κατ᾽ ὀλίγον μαχεῖται (i.e. τὸ πλῆθος αὐτῶν) [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 4.10.]]

__IV.8
μετ᾽ ὀλίγον τούτων shortly after.., [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Historia Graeca (Hellenica)” 1.1.2.]]

__IV.9
