LSJ / STEPBible (TFLSJ)
σῑτ-ίον, τό,
mostly in plural σιτία (singular in [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Hippocrates Medicus “Acut.” (“Sp.”) , “de Arte” 10, “VM” 6, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 338d, “Phdr.” 241c]], and later Prose, as [Refs 1st c.AD+ [2nd c.AD: Archigenes Medicus cited in 4th c.AD: Oribasius Medicus 8.1.15, Pythagorei cited in 1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus 2.12f, 3rd c.AD: Porphyrius Tyrius Philosophus “de Abstinentia - Porphyrii Opuscula” 1.27)]]; only used in Prose and Comedy:

__I
grain, corn, ἤλουν ὄρθριαι τὰ σ. [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Pherecrates Comicus 10.]]

__II
food made from grain, bread, τούτοισι δὲ (i.e. ὀσπρίοισι) μὴ χρῆσθαι εἰ μὴ μετὰ σιτίων [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Hippocrates Medicus “Acut.” (“Sp.”)]]; ἀπὸ ὀλυρέων ποιεῦνται σιτία make bread from spelt, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 2.36; σ. σφί ἐστι ἱρὰ πεσσόμενα [prev. work] 37.]]

__II.2
generally, victuals, provisions for men, opposed to χόρτος (fodder for cattle), [Refs [[prev. author] 1.94, 188, etc.]]; σιτί᾽ ἡμερῶν τριῶν three days' provision, of soldiers, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Acharnenses” 197, “Pax” 312, compare 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 1.48, 3.1]]; σ. καὶ ποτά food and drink, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Gorgias” 490b]]: so in singular, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 1.10.18, etc.; ἐν τοῖς σ. τε καὶ ὄψοις 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Protagoras” 334c]]; opposed to ῥύφημα, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Hippocrates Medicus “περὶ διαίτης ὀξέων” 13.]]

__II.3
τἀν Πρυτανείῳ σ. public maintenance in the Prytaneum, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Equites” 709.]]

__II.4
rarely, food for dogs, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Cynegeticus” 7.11.]]

__III
faces, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Ecclesiazusae” 355.]]

Related to:  συγγεν-ής, ές,
congenital, inborn, ἦθος [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “O.” 13.13; εὐδοξία [prev. author] “N.” 3.40]]; σ. εἶδος,= φύσις, character, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Hippocrates Medicus “περὶ χυμῶν” 1; νόσημα σ. ἐστί τινι [prev. author] “Prorrh.” 2.2; φόβος 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Eumenides” 691]]; παύροις.. ἐστι συγγενὲς τόδε natural to them, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [[prev. author] “Ag.” 832; ἡ τύχη προσγίγνεθ᾽ ἡμῖν σ. τῷ σώματι 4th-3rd c.BC: Philemo Comicus 10]]; πότμος σ. [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “N.” 5.40]]; προϊδεῖν σ. οἷς ἕπεται who have the natural gift to foresee, [Refs [[prev. work] 1.28]]; συγγενεῖς μῆνες my connate months, the months of my natural life, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Tyrannus” 1082]]; σ. τρίχες the hair born with one, i.e. the hair of the head as opposed to to the beard, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Historia Animalium” 518a18, 584a24]]; σημεῖα σ. birth-marks, [Refs [[prev. work] 585b31]]; δυνάμεις αἱ σ., opposed to αἱ ἔθει and αἱ μαθήσει, [Refs [[prev. author] “Metaphorical” 1047b31]]; αὔξει τὸ σ. increases its natural force, [Refs [[prev. author] “EN” 1119b9.]] adverb, -νῶς δύστηνος miserable from his birth, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Hercules Furens” 1293]]; see at {σύμφυτος}.

__II
of the same kin, descent, or family, akin to, τινι [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.109, 3.2, 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Heraclidae” 229]]: absolutely, akin, cognate, θεός [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Prometheus Vinctus” 14; γυνή 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Andromache” 887; χείρ 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Coloneus” 1387]]; συγγενέστατον φύσει πάντων most nearly akin, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Isaeus Orator 11.17; σ. γάμος ἀνεψιῶν 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Prometheus Vinctus” 855]]; of animals, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Historia Animalium” 539a23, “GA” 747a31, +others: hence,]]

__II.b
substantive, kinsman, relative, οὖσα σ. ἐκείνου [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Pax” 618 (troch.)]]; τῆς ἐμῆς γυναικὸς ξυγγενεῖ (dual) [Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. author] “Av.” 368 (troch.); πρὸς σ. τε καὶ οἰκείους αὐτῶν 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 378c; ἔργον εὑρεῖν συγγενῆ πένητός ἐστιν 4th-3rd c.BC: Menander Comicus 4; γάμει τὴν συγγενῆ [prev. author] 929: frequently in _plural_, οἱ σ]]. kinsfolk, kinsmen, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “P.” 4.133, 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 2.91, etc.]]; not properly applied to children (ἔκγονοι) in relation to their parents, and so opposed to ἔκγονοι in [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Isaeus Orator 8.30, see at {συγγένεια} 1 (but compare 5th-6th c.BC: Andocides Orator 1.17); τοῖς συγγενέσι τὰ τοῦ συγγενοῦς ψηφίζεσθαι 4th c.BC: Isaeus Orator 4.23.]]

__II.c
τὸ σ.,= συγγένεια, kindred, relationship, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Prometheus Vinctus” 291 (_anapaest meter_), 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Electra” 1469, 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 3.82, etc.]]; also, the spirit of one's race, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “P.” 10.12, “N.” 6.8]]; εἰ τούτῳ προσήκει Λαΐῳ τι σ. if he had any connexion with him, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Tyrannus” 814]]; of tribes, κατὰ τὸ ξ. [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 1.95.]]

__II.2
metaphorically, akin, cognate, of like kind, τοὺς τρόπους οὐ συγγενής [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Equites” 1280 (troch.), compare “Th.” 574]]; ξυγγενὴς ὁ κύσθος αὐτῆς θητέρᾳ (for τῷ τῆς ἑτέρας) [Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. author] “Ach.” 789; frequently in 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus, [ἡ ψυχὴ] σ. οὖσα τῷ θείῳ “R.” 611e; τῇ πολεμικῇ σ. ἡ πάλη “Lg.” 814d; τοῖς.. λόγοις τὴν αἰτίαν συγγενῆ δεῖ νομίζειν 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “de Generatione Animalium” 788b9, compare “Rh.” 1398a21 (_comparative_): rarely with _genitive_, νοῦς αἰτίας σ. 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Philebus” 31a, compare “Phd.” 79d, “R.” 403a, 487a: _absolutely_, σ. τιμωρίαι]] fitting, proper punishments, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Lycurgus Orator 122 (but probably _falsa lectio_ for{εὐγ-})]]; συγγενῆ things of the same kind, homogeneous, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Analytica Posteriora” 76a1; τὰ σ. καὶ τὰ ὁμοειδῆ [prev. author] “Rh.” 1405a35; σ. τέχναι “Stoicorum Veterum Fragmenta” 2.30]]; ἐν γαίῃ μὲν σῶμα τὸ σ. its congener, [Refs [Inscriptiones Graecae 9(1).882.7]] (Corcyra). adverb, συγγενῶς ἔρχεσθαι [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Leges” 897c; σ. τρέχων Πλάτωνι 2nd c.AD: Alexander Rhetor 1 (codices 3rd c.AD(?): Diogenes Laertius)]]; τὰ σ. εἰρημένα to similar effect, [Refs 1st c.BC+ [1st c.BC: Philodemus Gadarensis Epigrammaticus “Mus.” p.92K.]]

__III
συγγενής represented a title bestowed at the Persian court by the king as a mark of honour, 'cousin', [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 1.4.27, 2.2.31, 1st c.BC: Diodorus Siculus Historicus 16.50]]; also at the Ptolemaic and Seleucid courts, [LXX+2nd c.BC+ [“OGI” 104.2 (Delos, 2nd c.BC), +others, “BGU” 1741.12 (1st c.BC), LXX.1Mac.10.89]]; οἱ σ. τῶν κατοίκων ἱππέων probably a category of nobles among the κάτοικοι, [Refs 2nd c.BC+ [“PTeb.” 61 (b). 79 (2nd c.BC)]]; συγγενεῖς κάτοικοι [Refs 2nd c.BC+ [“UPZ” 14.8 (2nd c.BC).]]

short_definition: be downcast — 1. to fall together, meet in battle, come to blows , Lat. concurrere, (Homer): ς. ἐς νείκεα (Herdotus Historicus): to encounter , κλύδωνι (Euripides); νηί (Thucydides)
deep_entry:
Abbott-Smith / STEPBible (TBESG)
1. to fall together, meet in battle, come to blows , Lat. concurrere, (Homer): ς. ἐς νείκεα (Herdotus Historicus): to encounter , κλύδωνι (Euripides); νηί (Thucydides)
2. generally, to fall in with, meet with  accidents, misfortunes, with dative, (Herdotus Historicus)
3. of ailments, events, to fall upon, happen to , with dative pers., (Aeschulus Tragicus); also ἔς τινα (Herdotus Historicus)
4. absolute to happen  or fall out at the same time, concur , (Herdotus Historicus)
5. with part, like τυγχάνω, τόδε συνέπεσε γενόμενον (Herdotus Historicus)
6. impersonal, συνέπεσε, it happened, fell out, came to pass , with infinitive, (Herdotus Historicus); ξυνέπεσεν εἰς τοῦτο ἀνάγκης ὥστε . . matters came to such a pass that . ., (Thucydides); or with accusative et infinitive, (Thucydides)
7. to coincide, agree  or be in accordance with , τινί (Herdotus Historicus): absolute to agree exactly , (Herdotus Historicus); ἐμοὶ σὺ συμπέπτωκας ἐς ταὐτὸν λόγου have come to exactly  the same point with me, (Euripides)
8. to fall together , i. e. fall in, collapse , of a house, Lat. concidere, (Euripides); σῶμα συμπεσόν a frame having collapsed  from disease, (Plato Philosophus)
9. συμπίτνω poetry for συμπίπτω, when the penultimate is to be short
10. to fall  or dash together , of waves, (Aeschulus Tragicus)
11. to concur , (Aeschulus Tragicus); with dative, (Euripides) (ML)

Isocrates  2.35; πρὸς τὸ συμπῖπτον ἀεὶ διατάττων 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 8.5.16]]; τὸ συμπεσόν the incident, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Politica” 1284a32; καθάπερ ἐν κατάρροις ἐνίοτε συμπίπτει 2nd c.AD: Galenus Medicus 16.527, compare 18(2).185, +others]]

coincide, agree or be in accordance with, σ. τούτοισι τόνδε τὸν λόγον [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 7.151]]; ὥστε σ. τὸ πάθος τῷ χρηστηρίῳ turned out in accordance with it, [Refs [[prev. author] 6.18]]: absolutely, agree by chance, [Refs [[prev. author] 2.49]]; εἰς ταὐτὸν σ. agree in one, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Theaetetus” 160d, “R.” 473d, etc.]]; ἐμοὶ σὺ συμπέπτωκας ἐς ταὐτὸν λόγου have come to exactly the same point with me, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Troades” 1036.]]

__IV
fall together, i.e. fall in, especially of a house, συμπίπτει στέγη [Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. author] “HF” 905; πόλις ὑπὸ σεισμοῦ ξυμπεπτωκυῖα 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 8.41; οἰκία σ. 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 5.2.24]]; φοβουμένη μὴ συμπέσῃ [τὸ ἰσιεῖον] [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [“PEnteux.” 6.3 (3rd c.BC)]]; especially of the vessels of the body, fall in, collapse, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Hippocrates Medicus “κατ᾽ ἰητρεῖον” 13, 2nd c.AD: Soranus Medicus 1.16, +others; οἱ κρόταφοι συμπίπτουσι 2nd c.AD: Galenus Medicus 18(2).29]]; μυκτῆρες συμπεπτωκότες, opposed to ἀναπεπταμένοι, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “de Equitandi ratione” 1.10]]; σῶμα συμπεσόν a frame fallen in or emaciated, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Phaedo” 80c]]; ὀφθαλμοὶ σ. [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Historia Animalium” 561a21; αἱ κοιλίαι σ. τοῦ νέφους [prev. author] “Pr.” 940b31, +others]]; of plant-structures, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-3rd c.BC: Theophrastus Philosophus “de Causis Plantarum” 1.4.4]]; collapse, of animals, [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [“PSI” 6.584.25 (3rd c.BC)]]; of the heart, contract, [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd c.AD: Rufus Medicus “synopsis de pulsibus” 3.6]]; συνέπεσε τῷ προσώπῳ his face fell, [LXX.Gen.4.5]; τὸ πρόσωπον συνέπεσεν[LXX.1Ki.1.18]; -πέπτωκα τῇ καρδίᾳ ἀπὸ μερίμνης[LXX.1Mac.6.10.]

__IV.2
σταφυλὴ λευκὴ συμπεπτωκυῖα dried grapes, [Refs 6th c.AD+ [6th c.AD: Aëtius Medicus 9.30]]; πάντα δεδομένα κρέα συμπεπτωκότα ἔστω μέχρι δυοῖν ἡμερῶν hung, [Refs [[prev. passage]]]

__V
fall together, fall into the same line, σ. ἐπ᾽ ἀλλήλων ὑπὸ στενοχωρίας impinge one on another, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Theaetetus” 195a]]; converge, meet, τὸ τὰς παραλλήλους σ. οἴεσθαι [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Analytica Posteriora” 77b23, compare 3rd c.BC: Euclides Geometra 1 “Def.” 23, 3rd c.BC: Archimedes Geometra “περὶ ἑλίκων” 20, +others]]; οἱ πόροι παρ᾽ ἀλλήλους εἰσὶ καὶ οὐ σ. [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Historia Animalium” 495a15]]; of the sides of a triangle, [Refs 2nd c.BC+ [2nd c.BC: Polybius Historicus 2.14.5]]; of a river, σ. τῷ Κηφισῷ [Refs 1st c.AD+ [1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus “Sulla” 16.]]

short_definition: be conscious of — ύν-οιδα , pf. with Pres. meaning (see: οἶδα),
deep_entry:
Abbott-Smith / STEPBible (TBESG)
ύν-οιδα , pf. with Pres. meaning (see: οἶδα),
[in LXX: Lev.5:1 (יָדַע), Job.27:6; ptcp., 1Ma.4:21 A, 2Ma.4:41 A, 3Ma.2:8 R * ;]
__1. to share the knowledge of, be privy to (Hdt., Thuc., al.): ptcp., Act.5:2.
__2. C. prop. reflex., to be conscious of (Eur., Plat., al.), esp. of guilty consciousness: οὐδὲν γὰρ ἐμαυτῷ σ., for I know nothing against myself, 1Co.4:4.†
(AS)

---

LSJ / STEPBible (TFLSJ)
σύνοιδα,
perfect with present sense, 1st pers. plural σύνισμεν [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Sophista” 232c]], Ionic dialect συνοίδαμεν [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 9.60]], 3rd.pers. plural συνίσᾱσι [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Electra” 93 (_anapaest meter_), 5th-6th c.BC: Isocrates Orator 8.113, 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 3.1.9, etc. (rarely συνοίδασι 5th c.BC: Lysias Orator 11.1, 2nd c.BC: Polybius Historicus 27.9.11); _imperative_ σύνισθι 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Hecuba” 870]]; infinitive ξυνειδέναι [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Antigone” 266:]]pluperfect with imperfect sense, συνῄδειν, Attic dialect συνῄδη, dual συνῄστην, plural -ῇσμεν, -ῇστε, -ῇσαν, Ionic dialect2nd pers. plural συνῃδέᾰτε [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 9.58]]: future συν (ξυν-) είσομαι [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Ecclesiazusae” 17, “V.” 999, 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Historia Graeca (Hellenica)” 2.4.17 (rarely συνειδήσω 5th-6th c.BC: Isocrates Orator 1.16]], and aorist participle -ειδήσας[Refs 1st c.BC+ [1st c.BC: Philodemus Philosophus “περὶ παρρησίας” p.32 O.)]]:—know something about a person, especially as a potential witness for or against him, ἢ (i.e. Δίκη) σιγῶσα σύνοιδε τὰ γιγνόμενα πρό τ᾽ ἐόντα [Refs 6th c.BC+ [6th c.BC: Solon Lyricus 4.15]]; τά τοι ἐγὼ καὶ ἀμφότερα συνειδὼς ἔχω μαρτυρέειν to both of which I, knowing them true of you, can testify, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 5.24; εἰ τέοισί τι χρηστὸν συνῄδεε πεποιημένον [prev. author] 8.113; ἐπαινεόντων τούτους τοῖσί τι καὶ συνῃδέατε [prev. author] 9.58]]; τὰ Μηδικὰ καὶ ὅσα αὐτοὶ σύνιστε our other services to which you can testify, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 1.73; ἂ ξύνισμεν τοῖσιν ἵπποις βουλόμεσθ᾽ ἐπαινέσαι 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Equites” 595 (troch.); συνοίδαμεν ὑμῖν ὑπὸ τὸν παρεόντα τόνδε πόλεμον ἐοῦσι πολλὸν προθυμοτάτοισι 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 9.60]]; ὑπολαμβάνων παρ᾽ ὑμῶν ἑκάστῳ τὸ συνειδὸς ὑπάρχειν μοι believing that I can rely on your acknowledgement of my services, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 18.110]]; τί μοι σύνοισθα τοιοῦτον εἰργασμέν; [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Symposium” 4.62; σύνοιδα τῷ μειρακίῳ κοσμίῳ τὸν πρότερον ὄντι χρόνον ἀεί 4th-3rd c.BC: Menander Comicus “Σαμία” 57; πότερον οὐ συνοίδασιν αὐτῷ ποιοῦντι τὰ δίκαια 2nd c.BC: Polybius Historicus 27.9.11]]; ξυνειδὼς οὐ φράσει; [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Tyrannus” 330; ἵνα τούτῳ ταῦτα συνειδῶμεν 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Protagoras” 348b; ἐρῶ.. ἂ σύνοιδα αὐτῷ 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Memorabilia” 2.7.1]]; οὐκ αἰσχυνοῦμαι.. εἰπεῖν (variant) ἅπασιν ὅσα σύνοιδ᾽ αὐτῷ κακά [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Fragmenta” 200; ξύνοιδ᾽ ἄντροισιν αἰσχύνην τινά 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Ion” 288]]; θνῄσκοντι συνείσῃ (conjecture Reiske for συνοίσῃ) thou wilt witness my death, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Philoctetes” 1085 (Lyric poetry); διὰ δικαιοσύνην, τήν οἱ ἄλλην συνῄδεε ἐοῦσαν 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 7.164; τοιοῦτον αὐτοῖς Ἄρεος εὔβουλον πάγον ἐγὼ ξυνῄδη χθόνιον ὄνθ᾽ 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Coloneus” 948]]; δύ᾽ ἡμῶν ἢ τρία κακὰ ξυνειδὼς εἶπε δρώσας μυρία (i.e. Εὐριπίδης) [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Thesmophoriazusae” 475, compare 553; ἀφανίζει τὸν παῖδα, ὃς συνῄδει περὶ τῶν χρημάτων 5th-6th c.BC: Isocrates Orator 17.11, compare 4th-3rd c.BC: Menander Comicus “Ἐπιτρέποντες” 210; τῆς ἁρπαγῆς τοῦ παιδὸς εἰ ξύνοισθά τι, ταχέως λέγειν χρή 4th c.BC: Antiphanes Comicus 74.3]]; καὶ τίνα σύνοισθά μοι καλουμένῃ βροτῶ; [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Choephori” 216; σύνοιδ᾽ Ὀρέστην πολλά σ᾽ ἐκπαγλουμένην [prev. work] 217]]; σύνοιδα τοῖς πλείστοις αὐτῶν ἥκιστα χαίρουσι I can bear witness that most of them are far from pleased.., [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Isocrates Orator 7.50]]; with a mixture of dative and accusative construction, συνίσασι γὰρ αὐτῷ.. καθιστάμενον, ἐκ δὲ τούτων.. δυνάμενον [Refs 7th c.BC+ [[prev. author] 15.120; ἐγώ σοι σ... ἀνιστάμενον καὶ.. βαδίζοντα καὶ ἀναπείθοντα 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Oeconomicus” 3.7; frequently with _reflexive_ _pronoun_ in _dative_, ἔμ᾽ αὔτᾳ τοῦτο σύνοιδα 7th-6th c.BC: Sappho Lyrica 15]]; ἐξ ὧν αὐτὸς σύνοισθα σαυτῷ ἐν τῇ τῶν γραμμάτων μαθήσει from your experience of yourself.., [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Theaetetus” 206a]]; σύνοιδ᾽ ἐμαυτῇ πολλὰ (δείν᾽) [NT+5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Thesmophoriazusae” 477, compare 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Memorabilia” 2.9.6, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 331a; ξυνειδέναι τί μοι δοκεῖς σαυτῷ καλόν 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Equites” 184; πολλὴν ἑαυτοῖς συνειδέναι ἀσέβειαν 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Apologia Socratis” 24; συνειδὼς ἐμαυτῷ ἀμαθίαν 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Phaedrus” 235c; τὴν πατρίδα, εἰς ἢν τοσαύτην εὔνοιαν ἐμαυτῷ σύνοιδα 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator “Epistulae” 2.20; σ. ἑαυτοῖς ἄγνοιαν 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Ethica Nicomachea” 1095a25; σ. αὑτῷ τὴν δειλίαν [prev. author] “HA” 618a26; μηδὲν ἑαυτοῖς ἄτοπον συνειδέναι 5th-4th c.BC: Socratis et Socraticorum Epistulae cited in 5th c.AD: Stobaeus, Joannes 3.24.13, compare 5th-6th c.BC: Isocrates Orator 3.59, LXX.Job.27.6, NT.1Cor.4.4]]; συνειδότες αὑτοῖς with full consciousness, [Refs [Polystr. p.15]] W.:—with participle

__a
in nominative, πῶς οὖν ἐμαυτῷ τοῦτ᾽ ἐγὼ ξυνείσομαι, φεύγοντ᾽ ἀπολύσας ἄνδρ; [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Vespae” 999; ἡνίκ᾽ ἄν τις ἐσθλὸς ὢν αὑτῷ συνειδῇ 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Fragmenta” 931; ὅστις τούτων σύνοιδεν αὑτῷ παρημεληκώς 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 2.5.7; σύνισμεν ἡμῖν αὐτοῖς ἀπὸ παίδων ἀρξάμενοι ἀσκηταὶ ὄντες τῶν καλῶν κἀγαθῶν ἔργων [prev. author] “Cyr.” 1.5.11; συνειδέναι σαυτῷ δοκεῖς οὐπώποτ᾽ ἀμελήσας αὐτῶν [prev. work] 1.6.4, compare 3.3.38, “HG” 2.3.12; οὔτε μέγα οὔτε σμικρὸν σύνοιδα ἐμαυτῷ σοφὸς ὤν 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Apologia” 21b; ὅταν καὶ μηδὲν σαυτῷ συνειδῇς ἐξαμαρτάνων 5th-6th c.BC: Isocrates Orator 5.79.]]

__b
in dative, σύνοιδα ἐμαυτῷ ἀντιλέγειν οὐ δυναμένῳ [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Symposium” 216b; σύνισμεν ἡμῖν αὐτοῖς κηλουμένοις ὑπ᾽ αὐτῆς [prev. author] “R.” 607c; τὸ συνειδέναι πεπρακόσιν αὑτοῖς τὰ πράγματα 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 19.208; συνειδόθ᾽ αὑτῷ φαῦλα διαπεπραγμένῳ 4th-3rd c.BC: Philemo Comicus 229.]]

__2
with dative of things, know something about a thing, τοῖς διὰ τῶν εἰκότων τὰς ἀποδείξεις ποιουμένοις λόγοις σύνοιδα οὖσιν ἀλαζόσιν [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Phaedo” 92d; διὰ τὸ συνειδέναι τοῖς σφετέροις πράγμασι τετρυ[μ]μένοις καὶ κάμνουσιν ἤδη τῷ πολέμῳ 2nd c.BC: Polybius Historicus 1.62.7; σε.. συνειδότα τοῖς πρὸς ἐμὲ σοὶ πεπολιτευμένοις 3rd-2nd c.BC: Phalaris Epistolographus “Epistulae - Epistolographi” 109]]; καιρὸς.. σὲ εἰπεῖν ἃ σύνοισθα τῷ βίῳ ἑκάστῳ what you know about each life, [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd c.AD: Lucianus Sophista “Gall.” 15.]]

__II
share the knowledge of something with somebody, to be implicated in or privy to it, οὐδὲ ξυνῄδει σοί τις ἔκθεσιν τέκνο; [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Ion” 956; δουλοῖ γὰρ ἄνδρα,.. ὅταν ξυνειδῇ μητρὸς ἢ πατρὸς κακά [prev. author] “Hipp.” 425]]; ξύνοιδε δ᾽ οὔτις οἰκετῶν νόσον[Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. work] 40; συνίσασί σοι πάντα ὅσα ἔπραξας 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 3.1.9; ξυνίσασ᾽ εὐναὶ.. ὅσα θρηνῶ 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Electra” 93 (_anapaest meter_); πλῆθος ὃ ξυνῄδει 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 4.68; ξυνειδώς τις [prev. passage]; ὁ συνειδὼς καὶ μὴ φράζων 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Leges” 742b; οἱ ξυνειδότες σφίσι 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 1.20; οἱ συνειδότες πεποιηκότι τι δεινόν 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Rhetorica” 1382b6; σύνοισθά που καὶ αὐτὸς ὅτι.. 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Phaedrus” 257d; σύνισμεν ὡς.. [prev. author] “Sph.” 232c; σύνοιδέ μοι εἰ ἐπιορκῶ 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 7.6.18]]; συνειδέναι δὲ (i.e. τὰς μαντηΐας) καὶ τοὺς Πυθίους [NT+5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 6.57; συνειδυίας καὶ τῆς γυναικός NT.Act.5.2:— with]]participle

__II.a
in dative, μήτε τῳ ξυνειδέναι τὸ πρᾶγμα βουλεύσαντι [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Antigone” 266; εἰ μὴ συνῄδη Σωκράτει τε καὶ Ἀγάθωνι δεινοῖς οὖσι περὶ τὰ ἐρωτικά 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Symposium” 193e.]]

__II.b
in accusative, ἀνδράποδα, ἂ συνῄδει τὴν γυναῖκα.. θάνατον μηχανωμένην [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Antipho Orator 1.9, compare 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Leges” 773b, 870d, 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 49.58, 59.67, 61.23.]]

__III
know well, αὐτὸς ξυνειδώς, ἢ μαθὼν ἄλλου πάρ; as from his own knowledge, or.. ? [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Tyrannus” 704]]; so also (unless there is ellipse of reflexive pronoun) σύνοιδα δείν᾽ εἰργασμένος [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Orestes” 396; σύνοισθά γ᾽ εἰς ἔμ᾽ οὐκ εὔορκος ὤν [prev. author] “Med.” 495.]]

__IV
with dative of things. to be privy to, [Refs 1st c.BC+ [“BGU” 1141.50 (1st c.BC)]]; τῷ φόνῳ [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [Scholia 2nd c.AD: Hermogenes Rhetor in Rhetores Graeci 4.355 W.]]

__V
τὸ συνειδός complicity, τὸ σ. τοῦ πράγματος [Refs 1st c.AD+ [1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus “Publicola” 4]]; consciousness, τοῦ ἐνδεοῦς [Refs [[prev. author] 2.84d.]]

__V.2
conscience, ὑπὸ συνειδότος ἐπαρρησιάζετο ἀγαθοῦ [Refs 5th c.BC+ [2nd c.AD: Pausanias Periegeta 7.10.10, compare 3rd c.AD: Heliodorus Scriptor Eroticus 6.7, 4th c.AD: Alciphro Epistolographus 1.10.5, Chor. p.38 5th c.BC: Bacchylides Lyricus]]

__VI
ὡς ἂν συνειδῇς as you may think proper, [Refs 6th c.AD+ [6th c.AD: Aëtius Medicus 13.2.]]

good, in moral sense, first in [Refs 6th c.BC+ [6th c.BC: Theognis Elegiacus 438, compare 1st c.AD(?): Heraclitus 104, 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Electra” 1082, 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Memorabilia” 1.7.1, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Apologia” 41d, etc.; ψυχῆς ἀγαθῆς πατρὶς ὁ ξύμπας κόσμος 3rd c.AD: Democritus Epigrammaticus 247]]: frequently with other adjectives, ὁ πιστὸς κἀ.[Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Trachiniae” 541; δικαίων κἀ. [prev. work] 1050]]:—ironical, τὸν ἀ. Κρέοντα[Refs [[prev. author] “Ant.” 31.]]

__I.5
ὦ ἀγαθέ, my good friend, as a term of gentle remonstrance, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Protagoras” 311a, etc.]]

__I.6
ἀ. δαίμων, see entry δαίμω; ἀ. τύχη, see entry τύχ; ἀ. θεός = Latin bona dea, [Refs 1st c.AD+ [1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus “Caesar” 9, “Cic.” 19.]]

__II
of things,

__II.1
good, serviceable, Ἰθάκη.. ἀ. κουροτρόφος[Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 9.27, etc.; ἀ. τοῖς τοκεῦσι, τῇ πόλει 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Cynegeticus” 13.17: with _genitive_, εἴ τι οἶδα πυρετοῦ ἀ.]] good for it, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [[prev. author] “Mem.” 3.8.3; ἑλκῶν 4th-3rd c.BC: Theophrastus Philosophus “Historia Plantarum” 9.11.1.]]

__II.2
of outward circumstances, αἰδὼς οὐκ ἀ. κεχρημένῳ ἀνδρὶ παρεῖναι[Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 17.347]]; εἰπεῖν εἰς ἀγαθόν to good purpose, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 9.102]]; ὁ δὲ πείσεται εἰς ἀ. περ for his own good end, [Refs [11.789; οὐκ ἀγαθὸν πολυκοιρανίη 2.204:]] —ἀγαθόν [ἐστι], with infinitive, it is good to do so and so, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 7.282, 24.130, 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 3.196, etc.]]

__II.3
morally good, πρῆξις[NT+5th c.BC+ [3rd c.AD: Democritus Epigrammaticus 177; ἔργα 5th c.BC: Empedocles Poeta Philosophus 112.2, cf. NT.Rom.2.7, etc.]]

__II.4
ἀγαθόν, τό, good, blessing, benefit, of persons or things, ὦ μέγα ἀ. σὺ τοῖς φίλοις[Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 5.3.20; φίλον, ὃ μέγιστον ἀ. εἶναί φασι [prev. author] “Mem.” 2.4.2, compare 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Ranae” 74, etc;]] as term of endearment for a baby, blessing!, treasure!, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-3rd c.BC: Menander Comicus “Σαμία” 28:]] — ἀγαθόν τινα δεδρακέναι, πεποιηκέναι confer a benefit on.., [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 3.68, 5th c.BC: Lysias Orator 13.92]]; ἐπ᾽ ἀγαθῷ τινος for one's good, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 5.27, 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 7.4.3; ἐπ᾽ ἀ. τοῖς πολίταις 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Ranae” 1487; οὐκ ἐπ᾽ ἀ.]]for no good end, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 1.131; ἐπ᾽ οὐδενὶ ἀ. τῆς Ἑλλάδος 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Historia Graeca (Hellenica)” 5.2.35:—in _plural_, ἡ ἐπ᾽ ἀγαθοῖς γεναμένη (sic) κατασπορά “PFlor.” 21.10 (3rd c.AD):]] —τὸ ἀ. or τἀ., the good, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Epicharmus Comicus 171.5, compare 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 506b, 508e, 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Metaphysica” 1091a31, etc.:]] —in _plural_, ἀγαθά, τά, goods of fortune, treasures, wealth, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 2.172, 5th c.BC: Lysias Orator 13.91, 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Memorabilia” 1.2.63, etc.; ἀγαθὰ πράττειν]]fare well, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Aves” 1706]]; also, good things, dainties, [Refs 6th c.BC+ [6th c.BC: Theognis Elegiacus 1000, 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Acharnenses” 873, etc.]]: good qualities, τοῖς ἀ., οἷς ἔχομεν ἐν τῇ ψυχῇ[Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Isocrates Orator 8.32, compare 3rd c.AD: Democritus Epigrammaticus 37]]; good points, of a horse, εἰ τἄλλα πάντα ἀ. ἔχοι, κακόπους δ᾽ εἴη[Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “de Equitandi ratione” 1.2.]]

__III
comparative and superlative are usually supplied from other stems, i.e.  comparative ἀμείνων, ἀρείων, βελτίων, κρείσσων (κάρρων), λωΐων (λὥων), Epic dialect βέλτερος, λωΐτερος, φέρτερος:—superlative ἄριστος, βέλτιστος, κράτιστος, λώϊστος (λῷστος), Epic dialect βέλτατος, κάρτιστος, φέρτατος, φέριστος:— later, regular comparative ἀγαθώτερος[LXX+1st c.BC+ [LXX.Judg.11.25, 15.2, 1st c.BC: Diodorus Siculus Historicus 8 “fragment” 12, 3rd c.AD: Plotinus Philosophus 5.5.9, Diod.Rh. p.53.9H.]]: superlative ἀγαθώτατος[Refs 1st c.BC+ [1st c.BC: Diodorus Siculus Historicus 16.85, 3rd c.AD: Heliodorus Scriptor Eroticus 5.15,]] etc. (-ότατος [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [“POxy.” 1757.26 (2nd c.AD)).]]

__IV
adverb usually εὖ, which see: ἀγαθῶς[LXX+5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Hippocrates Medicus “κατ᾽ ἰητρεῖον” 9, 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Rhetorica” 1388b6, LXX.1Ki.20.7. (Etym. uncertain (ὅτι ἄγει ἡμᾶς ἐπὶ τὸν ὀρθὸν βίον “Stoicorum Veterum Fragmenta” 3.49)]]; perhaps cognate with ἄγαμαι, hence admirable.)

Ἀΐδα, of a tombstone, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “N.” 10.67.]]

__3
statue in honour of a god, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.131, 2.42, 46, 5th c.BC: Lysias Orator 6.15 (_plural_):—τὸ τοῦ Διὸς ἄ., opposed to εἰκόνες of men, 5th-6th c.BC: Isocrates Orator 9.57, compare “Michel” 545 (Phrygia, 2nd c.BC), etc.]]; as an object of worship, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Septem contra Thebas” 258, “Eu.” 55, 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Tyrannus” 1379, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Phaedrus” 251a]]:—sculpture, μήτε ἄ. μήτε γραφή[Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Politica” 1336b15.]]

__4
statue (more general than ἀνδριάς, which see), [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Meno” 97d, etc.]]:—also, portrait, picture, ἐξαλειφθεῖσ᾽ ὡς ἄ.[Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Helena” 262.]]

generally, image, τῶν ἀιδίων θεῶν[Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Timaeus” 37c; νεφέλης 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Helena” 705; μητρός “Tragica Adespota” 126]]; Ἄρεως Polemo [Refs 5th c.BC+ [“Call.” 52:—expressed by painting or words, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Symposium” 216e, compare “R.” 517d]]; hieroglyphic sign, [Refs 3rd c.AD+ [3rd c.AD: Plotinus Philosophus 5.8.6.]]

deep_entry:

1. to charge, accuse, censure, blame , with accusative pers., τάχα κεν καὶ ἀναίτιον αἰτιόωιτο (Iliad by Homer); αἰτ. τινά τινος to accuse  of a thing, (Herdotus Historicus), etc.;—;with infinitive, αἰτ. τινα ποιεῖν τι to accuse  one of doing, (Herdotus Historicus):—;in this signification, certain tenses are used in passive sense, to be accused , aor1 ἠιτιάθην (Thucydides); perfect ἠιτίαμαι (Thucydides)
2. with accusative rei, to lay to  one's charge, impute , τοῦτο αἰτ. (Xenophon Historicus); ταῦτα (Demosthenes Orator); with double accusative, τί ταῦτα τοὺς Λάκωνας αἰτιώμεθαa (Aristophanes Comicus)
3. to allege as the cause , αἰτ. τινα αἴτιον (Plato Philosophus); φωνάς τε καὶ ἄλλα μυρία αἰτ. (Plato Philosophus); τῆς ἱερᾶς χώρας ἠιτιᾶτο εἶναι he alleged  that it was part of the sacred territory, (Demosthenes Orator) (ML)

3. like καιρός, the best, most fitting time , [variant datesTragica Adespota; ἔργων, λόγων ἀκμή the time  for doing, speaking, (Sophocles Tragicus); ἀκμή ἐστι, with infinitive, 'tis high time  to do, (Aeschulus Tragicus); ἐπ᾽ ἀκμῆς εἶναι, with infinitive, to be on the point  of doing, (Euripides); ἐπ᾽ αὐτὴν ἥκει τὴν ἀκμήν 'tis come to the critical time , (Demosthenes Orator)

deep_entry:
Abbott-Smith / STEPBible (TBESG)
1. at the furthest point , and so either topmost  = Lat. summus, or outermost  = Lat. extremus:
2. highest, topmost , ἐν ἄκρηι πόλει = ἐν ἀκροπόλει, (Iliad by Homer); μέλαν ὕδωρ ἄκρον at its surface , (Iliad by Homer), etc.
3. outermost , ἄκρη χείρ, ἄκροι πόδες, ἄκρος ὦμος the end  of the hand, ends  of the feet, tip  of the shoulder, (Iliad by Homer); ἐπ᾽ ἄκρων [ δακτύλων] on tiptoe , (Sophocles Tragicus); ἄκροισι λαίφους κρασπέδοις with the outermost  edges of the sail, i. e. under close-reefed  sails, (Euripides)
4. of Time, it denotes completeness , ἄκραι σὺν ἑσπέραι when eve was fully come , (Pindar); ἄκρας νυκτός at dead  of night, (Sophocles Tragicus)
5. of Degree, the highest  in its kind, exceeding good, consummate, excellent : of persons, (Herdotus Historicus), etc.; ἄκρος μάντις (Sophocles Tragicus):—;often with an accusative modi added, ψυχὴν οὐκ ἄκρος not strong  in mind, (Herdotus Historicus); ἄκροι τὰ πολέμια, skilful  in war, (Herdotus Historicus), etc.; also with genitive modi, οἱ ἄκροι τῆς ποιήσεως (Plato Philosophus); also, ἄκρος εἰς or περί τι (Plato Philosophus)
6. as Substantive, see. ἄκρα, ἄκρον.
7. neuter as adverb on the top  or surface , just , ἄκρον ἐπὶ ῥηγμῖνος on the very  edge of the surf, il.
8. exceedingly , (Theocritus Poeta Bucolicus)
9. utterly, completely , (Plato Philosophus) (ML)

2. intransitive to walk, step , properly of motion on foot , ποσσὶ or ποσὶ βαίνειν (Homer), etc.; with infinitive in (Homer), βῆ ἰέναι, βῆ ἰέμεν set out  to go, went  his way, (Iliad by Homer); βῆ θέειν started  to run, (Iliad by Homer); βῆ δ᾽ ἐλάαν, (Iliad by Homer), etc.:—;with accusative loci, (Sophocles Tragicus); and with all Preps. implying motion, as, ἐπὶ νηὸς ἔβαινεν was going on  board ship, (Odyssey by Homer); ἐφ᾽ ἵππων βάντες having mounted  the chariot, (Odyssey by Homer); βαίνειν δι᾽ αἵματος to wade  through blood, (Euripides), etc.
3. in perfect to stand  or be  in a place, χῶρος ἐν ὧι βεβήκαμεν (Sophocles Tragicus); often almost= εἰμί (sum) , εὖ βεβηκώς on a  good footing , well established, prosperous , (Herdotus Historicus), etc.; so, οἱ ἐν τέλει βεβῶτες they who are  in office, (Herdotus Historicus); compare ξυρόν.
4. to go, go away, depart , (Iliad by Homer); βέβηκα euphamistic for τέθνηκα, (Aeschulus Tragicus):—;of things, ἐννέα ἐνιαυτοὶ βεβάασι nine years have come and gone , (Iliad by Homer)
5. to come , τίπτε βέβηκα; (Iliad by Homer): to arrive , (Sophocles Tragicus)
6. to go on, advance , ἐς τόδε τόλμης, ἐς τοσοῦτον ἐλπίδων (Sophocles Tragicus)
7. with accusative to mount , (Homer) only in aor1 middle, βήσασθαι δίφρον:—; Pass., ἵπποι βαινόμεναι brood  mares, (Herdotus Historicus)
8. χρέος ἔβα με debts came on  me, (Aristophanes Comicus)
9. in Poets, with accusative of the instrument of motion, which is simply pleonastic, βαίνειν πόδα to advance  the foot, step on , (Euripides), etc.
10. Causal, in future βήσω, aor1 ἔβησα:—; to make to go , βῆσεν ἀφ᾽ ἵππον, ἐξ ἵππων βῆσε brought  them down  from the chariot, (Iliad by Homer) The present in this sense is βιβάζω. (ML)

Abbott-Smith / STEPBible (TBESG)
1. fearful, terrible, dread, dire , (Homer), etc.; δεινὸν ἀϋτεῖν, βροντᾶν to shout, thunder terribly , (Iliad by Homer); δεινὸν δέρκεσθαι, παπταίνειν, ἰδεῖν to look terrible , (Homer); but, δεινὸς ἰδέσθαι fearful  to behold, (Odyssey by Homer); δεινὸς μὲν ὁρᾶν, δεινὸς δὲ κλύειν (Sophocles Tragicus):—; τὸ δεινόν danger, suffering, awe, terror , (Herdotus Historicus), etc.; so, τὰ δεινά (Sophocles Tragicus), etc.:—; οὐδὲν δεινοί, μὴ ἀποστέωσιν no fear  of their revolting, (Herdotus Historicus):—; δεινὸν ποιεῖσθαι to take ill, complain of, be indignant at  a thing, Lat. aegre ferre, (Herdotus Historicus), etc.; δεινὰ παθεῖν to suffer dreadful, illegal, arbitrary  treatment, attic; so in adverb, δεινῶς φέρειν (Herdotus Historicus); δ. ἔχειν to be in straits , (Xenophon Historicus)
2. with a notion of Force or Power, mighty, powerful , δεινὸν σάκος the mighty  shield, (Iliad by Homer)
3. simply, wondrous, marvellous, strange , τὸ συγγενές τοι δεινόν kin has a strange power , (Aeschulus Tragicus); δ. ἵμερος, ἔρως, δέος (Herdotus Historicus); δεινὸν ἂν εἴη, εἰ . ., it were strange  that . ., (Euripides):—;adverb -νῶς, marvellously, exceedingly , δ. μέλας, ἄνυδρος (Herdotus Historicus)
4. the sense of powerful, wondrous  passed into that of able, clever, skilful , (Herdotus Historicus), attic; especially of practical ability , opposite to σοφός, (Plato Philosophus): with infinitive, δεινὸς εὑρεῖν clever  at inventing, (Aeschulus Tragicus); δεινὸς λέγειν (Sophocles Tragicus); δεινὸς πράγμασι χρῆσθαι (Demosthenes Orator): also with accusative, δεινὸς τὴν τέχνην (Plato Philosophus); δ. περί τι or τινος (Plato Philosophus) (ML)

Related to:  εἰ,
Attic dialect-Ionic dialect and [Refs 4th c.AD+ [4th c.AD(?): Arcadius Grammaticus (for εἰκ, see below 11 ad [near the start]), = _Doric dialect_ and _Aeolic dialect_ αἰ, αἰκ (which see), 5th c.AD: Cypria]] ἤ [Refs [“Inscription Cyprian dialect” 135.10 H., both εἰ and αἰ]] in Epic dialect:— Particle used interjectionally with imperative and to express a wish, but usually either in conditions, if, or in indirect questions, whether. In the former use its regular negative is μ; in the latter, οὐ.

__A
INTERJECTIONALLY, in [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Homerus Epicus]], come now! with imperative, εἰ δὲ.. ἄκουσον [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 9.262; εἰ δὲ καὶ αὐτοὶ φευγόντων [prev. work] 46; most frequently with ἄγε (which see), 1.302, +others]]

__A.2
in wishes, with optative, ἀλλ᾽ εἴ τις.. καλέσειεν [Refs [10.111, compare 24.74]]; so later, εἴ μοι ξυνείη μοῖρα [Refs 8th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Tyrannus” 863 (Lyric poetry); εἴ μοι γένοιτο φθόγγος ἐν βραχίοσιν 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Hecuba” 836: more frequently followed by γάρ, αἲ γὰρ δὴ οὕτως εἴη 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 4.189, +others; εἰ γὰρ γενοίμην ἀντὶ σοῦ νεκρός 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Hippolytus” 1410; εἰ γὰρ γένοιτο 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 6.1.38; εἰ γὰρ ἐν τούτῳ εἴη 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Protagoras” 310d]]; of unattained wishes, in [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Homerus Epicus only with _optative_, εἰ γὰρ ἐγὼν.. Διὸς πάϊς αἰγιόχοιο εἴην 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 13.825; Ζεῦ πάτερ, αἰ γὰρ ἐμὸς πόσις εἴη 7th c.BC: Alcman Lyricus 29]]; later with past tenses of indicative, εἰ γάρ μ᾽ ὑπὸ γῆν.. ἧκεν [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Prometheus Vinctus” 152 (_anapaest meter_)]]; εἰ γὰρ τοσαύτην δύναμιν εἶχον ὥστε.. [Refs 8th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Alcestis” 1072: twice in 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” with]]infinitive (compare the use of infinitive in commands), αἰ γὰρ τοῖος ἐὼν.. ἐμὸς γαμβρὸς καλέεσθαι [Refs [7.311, compare 24.376.]]

__A.2.b
εἴθε, Epic dialect αἴθε, is frequently used in wishes in the above constructions, εἴθε οἱ αὐτῷ Ζεὺς ἀγαθὸν τελέσειεν [Refs 8th c.BC+ [2.33; εἴθ᾽ ὣς ἡβώοιμι 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 7.157; ἰὼ γᾶ, εἴθ᾽ ἔμ᾽ ἐδέξω 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Agamemnon” 1537 (Lyric poetry); εἴθε σοι, ὦ Περίκλεις, τότε συνεγενόμην 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Memorabilia” 1.2.46]]: later with infinitive, γαίης χθαμαλωτέρη εἴθε.. κεῖσθαι [Refs 1st c.BC+ [“Anthologia Graeca” 9.284 (1st c.BC-1st c.AD: Crinagoras Epigrammaticus).]]

__A.2.c
εἰ γάρ, εἴθε are also used with ὤφελον (Epic dialect ὤφελλον), of past unattained wishes, αἴθ᾽ ὤφελλες στρατοῦ ἄλλου σημαίνειν [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 14.84]]; εἰ γὰρ ὤφελον [κατιδεῖν] [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 432c.]]

__A.2.d
followed by a clause expressing a consequence of the fulfilment of the wish, αἰ γὰρ τοῦτο.. ἔπος τετελεσμένον εἴη· τῷ κε τάχα γνοίης.. [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 15.536, compare 17.496, +others]]; sometimes hard to distinguish from εἰ in conditions (which may be derived from this use), εἴ μοί τι πίθοιο, τό κεν πολὺ κέρδιον εἴη [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 7.28.]]

__B
IN CONDITIONS, if:

__B.I
with INDIC.,

__B.I.1
with all tenses (for future, see below [Refs [2), to state a condition, with nothing implied as to its fulfilment, εἰ δ᾽ οὕτω τοῦτ᾽ ἐστίν, ἐμοὶ μέλλει φίλον εἶναι but]]if this is so, it will be.., [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 1.564]]: any form of the Verb may stand in apodosi, εἰ θεοί τι δρῶσιν αἰσχρόν, οὐκ εἰσὶν θεοί [Refs 8th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Fragmenta” 292.7; εἰ δοκεῖ, πλέωμεν 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Philoctetes” 526; εἰ Φαῖδρον ἀγνοῶ, καὶ ἐμαυτοῦ ἐπιλέλησμαι 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Phaedrus” 228a; κάκιστ᾽ ἀπολοίμην, Ξανθίαν εἰ μὴ φιλῶ 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Ranae” 579, compare 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 17.475; εἰ θεοῦ ἦν, οὐκ ἦν αἰσχροκερδής· εἰ δ᾽ αἰσχροκερδής, οὐκ ἦν θεοῦ 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 408c; εἰ ταῦτα λέγων διαφθείρω τοὺς νέους, ταῦτ᾽ ἂν εἴη βλαβερά [prev. author] “Ap.” 30b, compare 25b]]; εἰ οὗτοι ὀρθῶς ἀπέστησαν, ὑμεῖς ἂν οὐ χρεὼν ἄρχοιτε if these were right in their revolt, (it would follow that) you rule when you have no right, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 3.40.]]

__B.I.1.b
to express a general condition, if ever, whenever, sometimes with present, εἴ τις δύο ἢ καὶ πλείους τις ἡμέρας λογίζεται, μάταιός ἐστιν [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Trachiniae” 943]]: with imperfect, εἴ τίς τι ἠρώτα ἀπεκρίνοντο [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 7.10]]: rarely with aorist, [Refs 1st c.BC+ [1st c.BC: Diodorus Siculus Historicus 31.26.1, 2nd c.AD: Sextus Empiricus Philosophus “Πυρρώνειοι ὑποτυπώσεις” 1.84; compare 111.2.]]

__B.I.2
with future (much less frequently than ἐάν with subjunctive), either to express a future supposition emphatically, εἰ φθάσομεν τοὺς πολεμίους κατακαίνοντες οὐδεὶς ἡμῶν ἀποθανεῖται [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 7.1.19; εἰ μὴ βοηθήσετε οὐ περιέσται τἀκεῖ 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 6.91; εἰ αὕτη ἡ πόλις ληφθήσεται, ἔχεται ἡ πᾶσα Σικελία [prev. passage];]] in threats or warnings, εἰ μὴ καθέξεις γλῶσσαν ἔσται σοι κακά [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Fragmenta” 5; εἰ τιμωρήσεις Πατρόκλῳ, αὐτὸς ἀποθανῇ 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Apologia” 28c, compare 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 28.21: or,]]

__B.I.2.b
to express a present intention or expectation, αἶρε πλῆκτρον εἰ μαχεῖ if you mean to fight, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Aves” 759; ἐγὼ μὲν οὐκ ἀνήρ.. εἰ ταῦτ᾽ ἀνατεὶ τῇδε κείσεται κράτη 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Antigone” 485, compare 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 1.61, 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Hecuba” 863.]]

__B.I.3
with historical tenses, implying that the condition is or was unfulfilled.

__B.I.3.a
with imperfect, referring to present time or to continued or repeated action in past time (in [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Homerus Epicus always the latter, 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 24.715, +others): ταῦτα οὐκ ἂν ἐδύναντο ποιεῖν, εἰ μὴ διαίτῃ μετρίᾳ ἐχρῶντο they would not be able to do this (as they do)]], if they did not live an abstemious life, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 1.2.16, compare 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 489b; οὐκ ἂν νήσων ἐκράτει, εἰ μή τι καὶ ναυτικὸν εἶχεν he (from Agamemnon)]] would not have been master of islands, if he had not had also some naval force, [Refs 7th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 1.9; αἰ δ᾽ ἦχες ἔσλων ἴμερον ἢ κάλων.. αἴδως κεν.. ἦχεν 7th-6th c.BC: Sappho Lyrica 28]]; εἰ ἦσαν ἄνδρες ἀγαθοὶ.. οὐκ ἄν ποτε ταῦτα ἔπασχον if they had been good men, they would never have suffered as they did, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Gorgias” 516e, compare 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Memorabilia” 1.1.5]]; εἰ γὰρ ἐγὼ τάδε ᾔδἐ.. οὐκ ἂν ὑπεξέφυγε if I had known this.., [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 8.366.]]

__B.I.3.b
with aorist referring to past time, εἰ μὴ ἔφυσε θεὸς μέλι.. ἔφασκον γλύσσονα σῦκα πέλεσθαι [Refs 6th c.BC+ [6th c.BC: Xenophanes Poeta Philosophus 38]]; εἰ μὴ ὑμεῖς ἤλθετε, ἐπορευόμεθα ἂν ἐπὶ βασιλέα had you not come, we should be on our way.., [Refs 8th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 2.1.4; καὶ ἴσως ἂν ἀπέθανον, εἰ μὴ ἡ ἀρχὴ διὰ ταχέων κατελύθη 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Apologia” 32d, compare 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 5.680, 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 4.364, 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 4.5, 27.63]]: with pluperfect in apodosi, εἰ τριάκοντα μόναι μετέπεσον τῶν ψήφων, ἀπεπεφεύγη ἄν [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Apologia” 36a.]]

__B.I.3.c
rarely with pluperfect referring to action finished in past or present time, λοιπὸν δ᾽ ἂν ἦν ἡμῖν ἔτι περὶ τῆς πόλεως διαλεχθῆναι, εἰ μὴ προτέρα τῶν ἄλλων τὴν εἰρήνην ἐπεποίητο if she had not (as she has done) made peace before the rest, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Isocrates Orator 5.56, compare 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Timaeus” 21c.]]

__B.II
with SUB[Refs 1st c.AD+ [1st c.AD: Josephus Historicus, εἰ is regularly joined with ἄν]] (Epic dialect κε, κεν), compare ἐάν: [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.AD(?): Arcadius Grammaticus εἰκαν in Tegean Inscrr. of 4th c.BC (“IG” 5(2).3.16, 31, 6.2, “SIG” 306.34) should be understood as εἰκ ἄν (εἰ: εἰκ ={οὐ}: οὐκ), since εἰ δ᾽ ἄν is also found in “IG” 5(2).3.2, 6.45, and εἰκ alone, [prev. work]3.21]]; but ἄν (κε, κεν) are frequently absent in [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Homerus Epicus as 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 5.221, 14.373 (and compare below 2), and Lyric poetry, 5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus (who never uses εἰ with ἄν or κε (ν)) “P.” 4.266, +others; in dialects, αἰ δείλητ᾽ ἀγχωρεῖν “IG” 9(1).334.6 (_Locrian dialect_, 5th c.BC)]], cf. Foed.Doric dialect cited in [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 5.79; rarely in 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus, εἰ μὴ ἀναβῇ 2.13]]; occasionally in Trag., [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Eumenides” 234, 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Tyrannus” 198 (Lyric poetry), etc.]]; very rarely in Attic dialect Prose, εἰ ξυστῶσιν αἱ πόλεις [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 6.21; εἴ τι που ἄλσος ἢ τέμενος ἀφειμένον ᾖ 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Leges” 761c]]: in later Prose, εἴ τις θελήσῃ [NT+3rd c.AD+ [NT.Rev.11.5; εἰ φονεύῃ 3rd c.AD: Plotinus Philosophus 2.9.9, compare 5th c.AD: Proclus Philosophus “Inst.” 26.]]

__B.II.1
when the apodosis is future, to express a future condition more distinctly and vividly than εἰ with optative, but less so than εἰ with future indicative (above [Refs [1.2a)]]; εἰ δέ κεν ὣς ἕρξῃς καί τοι πείθωνται Ἀχαιοί, γνώσῃ ἔπειθ᾽.. if thou do thus.., thou shalt know, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 2.364, compare 1.128, 3.281, 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 17.549; ἂν δέ τις ἀνθιστῆται, σὺν ὑμῖν πειρασόμεθα χειροῦσθαι 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 7.3.11]]; ἂν μὴ νῦν ἐθέλωμεν ἐκεῖ πολεμεῖν αὐτῷ, ἐνθάδ᾽ ἴσως ἀναγκασθησόμεθα τοῦτο ποιεῖν if we be not now willing, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 4.50, compare 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 5.3.27: followed by _imperative_, ἢν εἰρήνης δοκῆτε δεῖσθαι, ἄνευ ὅπλων ἥκετε [prev. work] 3.2.13, compare 5.4.30.]]

__B.II.2
when the apodosis is present, denoting customary or repeated action, to express a general condition, if ever, ἤν ποτε δασμὸς ἵκηται, σοὶ τὸ γέρας πολὺ μεῖζον (i.e. ἐστί) whenever a division comes, your prize is (always) greater, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 1.166]]; ἢν ἐγγὺς ἔλθῃ θάνατος, οὐδεὶς βούλεται θνῄσκειν if death come near, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Alcestis” 671]]; with ἄν omitted, εἴ περ γάρ τε χόλον.. καταπέψῃ ἀλλά.. ἔχει κότον [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 1.81.]]

__B.II.2.b
with Rhet. present in apodosis, ἐὰν μὴ οἱ φιλόσοφοι βασιλεύσωσιν, οὐκ ἔστι κακῶν παῦλα there is (i.e. can be, will be) no rest.., [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 473d.]]

__B.III
with OPTATIVE (never with ἄν in early Gr., later ἐάν with optative, [Refs 5th c.AD+ [5th-6th c.AD: Damascius Philosophus “de Principiis” 114, +others),]]

__B.III.1
to express a future condition less definitely than ἐάν with subjunctive, usually with optative with ἄν in apodosis, ἦ κεν γηθήσαι Πρίαμος Πριάμοιό τε παῖδες.. εἰ σφῶιν τάδε πάντα πυθοίατο μαρναμένοιιν surely they would exult, if they should hear.., [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 1.255, compare 7.28, 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 3.223; εἴης φορητὸς οὐκ ἄν, εἰ πράσσοις καλῶς 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Prometheus Vinctus” 979; οὐδὲ γὰρ ἄν με ἐπαινοίη, εἰ ἐξελαύνοιμι τοὺς εὐεργέτας 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 7.7.11; οἶκος δ᾽ αὐτός, εἰ φθογγὴν λάβοι, σαφέστατ᾽ ἂν λέξειεν 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Agamemnon” 37, etc.]]: future optative is falsa lectio in [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Theaetetus” 164a]]: with present indicative in apodosis, [Refs 6th c.BC+ [6th c.BC: Xenophanes Poeta Philosophus 34.3, 3rd c.AD: Democritus Epigrammaticus 253]]: with future indicative, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Melissus Philosophus 5.]]

__B.III.1.b
in Hom.sometimes with present optative, to express an unfulfilled present condition, εἰ μὲν νῦν ἐπὶ ἄλλῳ ἀεθλεύοιμεν, ἦ τ᾽ ἂν ἐγὼ τὰ πρῶτα φεροίμην if we were now contending, etc., [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 23.274: rarely in Trag., εἰ μὴ κνίζοι (={εἰ μὴ ἔκνιζε}) 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Medea” 568; also εἰ ἀναγκαῖον εἴη ἀδικεῖν ἢ ἀδικεῖσθαι, ἑλοίμην ἂν μᾶλλον ἀδικεῖσθαι 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Gorgias” 469c.]]

__B.III.2
when the apodosis is past, denoting customary or repeated action, to express a general condition in past time (corresponding to use of subjunctive in present time, above [Refs [11.2)]]; once in [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Homerus Epicus, εἴ τίς με.. ἐνίπτοι, ἀλλὰ σὺ τόν γ᾽.. κατέρυκες 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 24.768]]; εἰ δέ τινας θορυβουμένους αἴσθοιτο.., κατασβεννύναι τὴν ταραχὴν ἐπειρᾶτο if he should see (whenever he saw) any troops in confusion, he (always) tried, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 5.3.55, compare “An.” 4.5.13, “Mem.” 4.2.40]]; εἴ τις ἀντείποι, εὐθὺς ἐτεθνήκει if any one made objection, he was a dead man at once, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 8.66; ἀλλ᾽ εἴ τι μὴ φέροιμεν, ὤτρυνεν φέρειν 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Alcestis” 755. For εἰ with _indicative_ in this sense see above 1.1]]: indicative and optative are found in same sentence, ἐμίσει, οὐκ εἴ τις κακῶς πάσχων ἠμύνετο, ἀλλ᾽ εἴ τις εὐεργετούμενος ἀχάριστος φαίνοιτο [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Agesilaus” 11.3.]]

__B.III.3
in oratio obliqua after past tenses, representing ἐάν with subjunctive or εἰ with a primary (never an historical) tense of the indicative in oratio recta, ἐλογίζοντο ὡς, εἰ μὴ μάχοιντο, ἀποστήσοιντο αἱ πόλεις (representing ἐὰν μὴ μαχώμεθα, ἀποστήσονται) [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Historia Graeca (Hellenica)” 6.4.6, compare 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 21.104, 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Historia Graeca (Hellenica)” 5.2.2]]; ἔλεγεν ὅτι, εἰ βλαβερὰ πεπραχὼς εἴη, δίκαιος εἴη ζημιοῦσθαι (representing εἰ βλαβερὰ πέπραχε, δίκαιός ἐστι)[Refs [[prev. work] 32, compare “An.” 6.6.25]]; εἰ δέ τινα φεύγοντα λήψοιτο, προηγόρευεν ὅτι ὡς πολεμίῳ χρήσοιτο (representing εἴ τινα λήψομαι, χρήσομαι) [Refs [[prev. author] “Cyr.” 3.1.3]]; also, where oratio obliqua is implied in the leading clause, οὐκ ἦν τοῦ πολέμου πέρας Φιλίππῳ, εἰ μὴ Θηβαίους.. ἐχθροὺς ποιήσειε τῇ πόλει, i.e. Philip thought there would be no end to the war, unless he should make.. (his thought having been ἐὰν μὴ ποιήσω), [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 18.145; ἐβούλοντο γὰρ σφίσιν, εἴ τινα λάβοιεν, ὑπάρχειν ἀντὶ τῶν ἔνδον, ἢν ἄρα τύχωσί τινες ἐζωγρημένοι 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 2.5.]]

__B.III.4
with optative with ἄν, only when the clause serves as apodosis as well as protasis,[Refs 5th c.BC+ [compare 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Protagoras” 329b, 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 4.18, 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Memorabilia” 1.5.3 (see. ἄν 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus 111. d).]]

__B.IV
with infinitive, in oratio obliqua, only in [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus, εἰ γὰρ δὴ δεῖν πάντως περιθεῖναι ἄλλῳ τέῳ τὴν βασιληΐην, [ἔφη] δικαιότερον εἶναι κτλ. 1.129; εἰ εἶναι τοῦτο μὴ φίλον 2.64, compare 172, 3.105, 108.]]

__B.V
after Verbs denoting wonder, delight, indignation, disappointment, contentment, and similar emotions, εἰ with indicative is used instead of ὅτι, to express the object of the feeling in a hypothetical form, θαυμάζω εἰ μηδεὶς ὑμῶν μήτ᾽ ἐνθυμεῖται μήτ᾽ ὀργίζεται, ὁρῶν.. I wonder that no one of you is either concerned or angry when he sees.., [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 4.43; οὐκ ἀγαπᾷ εἰ μὴ δίκην δέδωκεν, ἀλλ᾽ εἰ μὴ καὶ χρυσῷ στεφάνῳ στεφανωθήσεται ἀγανακτεῖ 4th c.BC: Aeschines Orator 3.147]]: after past tenses, ἐθαύμασε δ᾽ εἰ μὴ φανερόν ἐστιν [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Memorabilia” 1.1.13; δεινὸν εἰσῄει, εἰ μὴ.. δόξει 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 19.33; ἐθαύμαζον εἴ τι ἕξει τις χρήσασθαι τῷ λόγῳ 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Phaedo” 95a; οὐδὲ ᾐσχύνθη εἰ.. ἐπάγει 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 21.105: in oratio obliqua (expressed or implied) with _optative_, ἐπεῖπεν ὡς δεινὸν (i.e. εἴη) εἰ.. μεγαλόψυχος γένοιτο 4th c.BC: Aeschines Orator 2.157; ᾤκτιρον εἰ ἁλώσοιντο 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 1.4.7]]; ἐθαύμαζε δ᾽ εἴ τις ἀρετὴν ἐπαγγελλόμενος ἀργύριον πράττοιτο he wondered that any one should demand money, [Refs [[prev. author] “Mem.” 1.2.7]]; ἔχαιρον ἀγαπῶν εἴ τις ἐάσοι I rejoiced, being content if any one should let it pass, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 450a:]] —in this use the _negative_ οὐ is also found, ἀγανακτῶ εἰ ὁ Φίλιππος ἁρπάζων οὐ λυπεῖ [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 8.55; δεινὸν ἂν εἴη εἰ οἱ ἐκείνων ξύμμαχοι οὐκ ἀπεροῦσιν 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 1.121; τέρας λέγεις, εἰ οὐκ ἂν δύναιντο λαθεῖν 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Meno” 91d, etc.]]

__B.VI
in citing a fact as a ground of argument or appeal, as surely as, since, εἴ ποτ᾽ ἔην γε if there was [as there was], i.e. as sure as there was such an one, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 3.180, +others; εἰ τότε κοῦρος ἔα, νῦν αὖτέ με γῆρας ὀπάζει 4.321]]; πολλοὺς γὰρ οἶκε εἶναι εὐπετέστερον διαβάλλειν ἢ ἕνα, εἰ Κλεομένεα μὲν μοῦνον οὐκ οἷός τε ἐγένετο διαβαλεῖν, τρεῖς δὲ μυριάδας Ἀθηναίων ἐποίησε τοῦτο it seems easier to deceive many than one, if (as was the fact, i.e. since) he was not able.., [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 5.97, compare 1.60, +others]]

__B.VII
ELLIPTICAL CONSTRUCTIONS:

__B.VII.1
with apodosis implied in the context, εἰ having the force of in case, supposing that, πρὸς τὴν πόλιν, εἰ ἐπιβοηθοῖεν, ἐχώρουν they marched towards the city [so as to meet the citizens], in case they should rush out, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 6.100]]; ἱκέται πρὸς σὲ δεῦρ᾽ ἀφίγμεθα, εἴ τινα πόλιν φράσειας ἡμῖν εὔερον we have come hither to you, in case you should tell us of some fleecy city (i.e. that we might hear of it), [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Aves” 120]]; παρέζεο καὶ λαβὲ γούνων, αἴ κέν πως ἐθέλῃσιν ἐπὶ Τρώεσσιν ἀρῆξαι sit by him and grasp his knees [so as to persuade him], in case he be willing to help the Trojans, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 1.408, compare 66, 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 1.94, 3.92]]; ἄκουσον καὶ ἐμοῦ, ἐάν σοι ἔτι ταὐτὰ δοκῇ hear me also [that you may assent], in case the same opinion please you, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 358b]]; ἰδὲ δή, ἐάν σοι ὅπερ ἐμοὶ συνδοκῇ look now, in case you approve what I do, [Refs [[prev. work] 434a.]]

__B.VII.2
with apodosis suppressed for rhetorical reasons, εἴ περ γάρ κ᾽ ἐθέλῃσιν Ὀλύμπιος.. στυφελίξαι if he wish to thrust him away, [he will do so], [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 1.580]]; εἰ μὲν δώσουσι γέρας—· εἰ δέ κε μὴ δώωσιν, ἐγὼ δέ κεν αὐτὸς ἕλωμαι if they shall give me a prize, [well and good]; but if they give not, then I will take one for myself, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [1.135, compare 6.150, 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Plutus” 468]]; καὶ ἢν μὲν ξυμβῇ ἡ πεῖρα—· εἰ δὲ μή.. and if the attempt succeed, [well]; otherwise.., [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 3.3, compare 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Protagoras” 325d.]]

__B.VII.3
with the Verb of the protasis omitted, chiefly in the following expressions:

__B.VII.3.a
εἰ μή except, οὐδὲν ἄλλο σιτέονται, εἰ μὴ ἰχθῦς μοῦνον [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.200]]; μὰ τὼ θεώ, εἰ μὴ Κρίτυλλά γ᾽ [εἰμί]—nay, if I'm not Critylla! i.e. I am, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Thesmophoriazusae” 898]]; εἰ μὴ ὅσον except only, ἐγὼ μέν μιν οὐκ εἶδον, εἰ μὴ ὅσον γραφῇ [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 2.73, compare 1.45, 2.20; εἰ μὴ εἰ 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 1.17, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Gorgias” 480b, etc.]]; εἰ μή τι οὖν, ἀλλὰ σμικρόν γέ μοι τῆς ἀρχῆς χάλασον if nothing else, yet.., [Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. author] “Men.” 86e; ironical, εἰ μὴ ἄρα ἡ τῆς ἀρετῆς ἐπιμέλεια διαφθορά ἐστιν 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Memorabilia” 1.2.8; εἰ μή πέρ γε τὸν ὑοσκύαμον χρήματα εἶναι φήσομεν [prev. author] “Oec.” 1.13.]]

__B.VII.3.b
εἰ δὲ μή but if not, i.e. otherwise, προηγόρευε τοῖς Λαμψακηνοῖσι μετιέναι Μιλτιάδεα, εἰ δὲ μή, σφέας πίτυος τρόπον ἀπείλεε ἐκτρίψειν [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 6.37, compare 56]]; after μάλιστα μέν, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 1.32, 35, etc.:]] —after a preceding _negative_, μὴ τύπτ᾽· εἰ δὲ μή, σαυτόν ποτ᾽ αἰτιάσει don't beat me; otherwise, you will have yourself to blame, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Nubes” 1433; ὦ Κῦρε, μὴ οὕτω λέγε· εἰ δὲ μή, οὐ θαρροῦντά με ἕξεις 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 3.1.35; οὔτ᾽ ἐν τῷ ὕδατι τὰ ὅπλα ἦν ἔχειν· εἰ δὲ μή [prev. author] “An.” 4.3.6, compare 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 1.28, 131, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Phaedo” 91c.]]

__B.VII.3.c
εἰ δέ sometimes stands for εἰ δὲ μή, εἰ μὲν βούλεται, ἑψέτω· εἰ δ᾽, ὅτι βούλεται, τοῦτο ποιείτω [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Euthydemus” 285c, compare “Smp.” 212c; εἰ δ᾽ οὖν 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Antigone” 722; εἰ δ᾽ οὕτως 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Ethica Nicomachea” 1094a24]]; εἰ δὲ τοῦτο and if so, [Refs 1st c.BC+ [1st c.BC-1st c.AD: Strabo Geographus 2.1.29.]]

__B.VII.3.d
εἰ γάρ for if so, [Refs [[prev. author] 7.3.6.]]

__B.VII.3.e
εἴ τις if any, i. e. as much as or more than any, τῶν γε νῦν αἴ τις ἐπιχθονίων, ὀρθῶς [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Bacchylides Lyricus 5.5; ὄτλον ἄλγιστον ἔσχον, εἴ τις Αἰτωλὶς γυνή 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Trachiniae” 8, compare “OC” 734]]; εἴ τις ἄλλος, siquis alius, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Andromache” 6, etc.; εἴ τινες καὶ ἄλλοι 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 3.2, etc.; εἴπερ τις ἄλλος 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 501d]]; also κατ᾽ εἰ δέ τινα τρόπον in any way, [Refs [“IG” 5(2).6.27 (from Tegea).]]

__B.VII.3.f
εἴ ποτε or εἴπερ ποτέ now if ever, ἡμῖν δὲ καλῶς, εἴπερ ποτέ, ἔχει.. ἡ ξυναλλαγή [Refs 7th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 4.20, compare 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Equites” 594; αἴ ποτα κἄλλοτα 7th-6th c.BC: Alcaeus Lyricus “Supp.” 7.11, compare 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 6.4.12, etc.]]; but in prayers, εἴ ποτέ τοι ἐπὶ νηὸν ἔρεψα.. τόδε μοι κρήηνον ἐέλδωρ [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 1.39.]]

__B.VII.3.g
εἴ ποθεν (i.e. δυνατόν ἐστι) if from any quarter, i.e. from some quarter or other, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Philoctetes” 1204 (Lyric poetry)]]; so εἴ ποθι somewhere, anywhere, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [[prev. author] “Aj.” 885 (Lyric poetry); εἴ που 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 4.193.]]

__B.VII.3.h
εἴ πως[Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. work] 388, 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 2.3.11]]: in an elliptical sentence (cf. VII. [Refs 5th c.BC+ [1), πρέσβεις πέμψαντες, εἴ πως πείσειαν 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 1.58.]]

with other PARTICLES:

__B.VIII.1

for ὡς εἰ, ὡς εἴ τε, ὥσπερ εἰ, etc., see at {ὡς} and ὥσπερ.

__B.VIII.3
for εἰ ἄρα, see at {ἄρα}; for εἰ δή, εἴπερ, see at {εἰ δή, εἴπερ}; for εἴ γε, see at {γέ}.

__C
IN INDIRECT QUESTIONS, whether, followed by the indicative, subjunctive, or optative, according to the principles of oratio obliqua:

__C.1
with IN[Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator after primary tenses, representing the same tense in the direct question, σάφα δ᾽ οὐκ οἶδ᾽ εἰ θεός ἐστιν]] whether he is a god, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 5.183; εἰ ξυμπονήσεις.. σκόπει 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Antigone” 41.]]

__C.2
with SUB[Refs 1st c.AD+ [1st c.AD: Josephus Historicus after primary tenses, representing a dubitative]]subjunctive in the direct question, τὰ ἐκπώματα οὐκ οἶδ᾽ εἰ Χρυσάντᾳ τουτῳῒ δῶ whether I should give them, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 8.4.16: sometimes elliptical, ἐς τὰ χρηστήρια ἔπεμπε, εἰ στρατεύηται ἐπὶ τοὺς Πέρσας 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.75.]]

__C.3
OPT. after past tenses, representing either of the two previous constructions in the direct question, ἤρετο εἴ τις ἐμοῦ εἴη σοφώτερος he asked whether any one was wiser than I (direct ἔστι τις σοφώτερο;), [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Apologia” 21a; ἐπεκηρυκεύετο Πεισιστράτῳ, εἰ βούλοιτό οἱ τὴν θυγατέρα ἔχειν γυναῖκα 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.60: rarely]]aorist optative for the aorist indicative, ἠρώτων αὐτὸν εἰ ἀναπλεύσειεν I asked him whether he had set sail (direct ἀνέπλευσα;), [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 50.55: but]]aorist optative usually represents aorist subjunctive, τὸν θεὸν ἐπήροντο εἰ παραδοῖεν Κορινθίοις τὴν πόλιν.. καὶ τιμωρίαν τινὰ πειρῷντ᾽ ἀπ᾽ αὐτῶν ποιεῖσθαι they asked whether they should deliver their city to the Corinthians, and should try.., [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 1.25:]] —in both constructions the _indicative_ or subjunctive may be retained, ψῆφον ἐβούλοντο ἐπαγαγεῖν εἰ χρὴ πολεμεῖν[Refs [[prev. work] 119]]; ἐβουλεύοντο εἴτε κατακαύσωσιν.. εἴτε τι ἄλλο χρήσωνται whether they should burn them or should dispose of them in some other way, [Refs [[prev. author] 2.4]]; ἀνακοινοῦσθαι αὐτὸν αὑτῷ εἰ δῷ ἐπιψηφίσαι τοῖς προέδροις [he said that] he consulted him whether he should give.., [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aeschines Orator 2.68.]]

__C.4
with OPT. and ἄν when this was the form of the direct question, ἠρώτων εἰ δοῖεν ἂν τούτων τὰ πιστά they asked whether they would give (direct δοιήτε ἄ;), [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 4.8.7.]]

__C.5
the NEG. used with εἰ in indirect questions is οὐ, when οὐ would be used in the direct question, ἐνετέλλετο.. εἰρωτᾶν εἰ οὔ τι ἐπαισχύνεται whether he is not ashamed, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.90, etc.]]; but if μή would be required in the direct form, it is retained in the indirect, οὐ τοῦτο ἐρωτῶ, ἀλλ᾽ εἰ τοῦ μὲν δικαίου μὴ ἀξιοῖ πλέον ἔχειν μηδὲ βούλεται ὁ δίκαιος, τοῦ δὲ ἀδίκου (the direct question would be μὴ ἀξιοῖ μηδὲ βούλετα; he does not see fit nor wish, does he?) [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 349b]]:—in double indirect questions, εἴτε.. εἴτε..; εἰ.. εἴτε..; εἴτε.. ἢ.., either οὐ or μή can be used in the second clause, ὅπως ἴδῃς εἴτ᾽ ἔνδον εἴτ᾽ οὐκ ἔνδον [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Ajax” 7; σκοπῶμεν εἰ ἡμῖν πρέπει ἢ οὔ 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 451d]]; εἰ ἀληθὲς ἢ μή, πειράσομαι μαθεῖν[Refs 4th c.BC+ [[prev. work] 339a; πολλὰ ἂν περιεσκέψω, εἴτε ἐπιτρεπτέον εἴτε οὔ·.. οὐδένα λόγον οὐδὲ συμβουλὴν ποιῇ, εἴτε χρὴ ἐπιτρέπειν σαυτὸν αὐτῷ εἴτε μή [prev. author] “Prt.” 313a, 313b; ἀνάγκη τὴν ἐμὴν μητέρα, εἴτε θυγάτηρ ἦν Κίρωνος εἴτε μή, καὶ εἰ παρ᾽ ἐκείνῳ διῃτᾶτο ἢ οὔ, καὶ γάμους εἰ διττοὺς ὑπὲρ ταύτης εἱστίασεν ἢ μὴ.. πάντα ταῦτα εἰδέναι τοὺς οἰκέτας 4th c.BC: Isaeus Orator 8.9]]; τοὺς νόμους καταμανθάνειν εἰ καλῶς κεῖνται ἢ μή.. τοὺς λόγους εἰ ὀρθῶς ὑμᾶς διδάσκουσιν ἢ οὔ [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Antipho Orator 5.14.]]
