deep_entry:
Abbott-Smith / STEPBible (TBESG)
1. to send before, send on  or forward , (Homer): also, to send  something to  another, ἀγγελίας, φήμην (Odyssey by Homer):—; (Homer) often with an infinitive added; αἰετὼ προέηκα πέτεσθαι, οὖρον προέηκεν ἀῆναι (Odyssey by Homer)
2. to send away, dismiss, let go , (Iliad by Homer); τήνδε θεῷ πρόες let  her go  to the god, i. e. in reverence to him, (Iliad by Homer)
3. to let loose, let fall , especially thoughtlessly, ἔπος προέηκε let drop  a word, (Odyssey by Homer); πηδάλιον ἐκ χειρῶν προέηκε he let  the helm slip  from his hands, (Odyssey by Homer); δάκρυα προῆκεν (Euripides)
4. of missiles, to send forth, shoot  or dart forth , (Homer)
5. of a river, ὕδωρ προί̈ει ἐς Πηνειόν it pours  its water into the Peneius, (Iliad by Homer)
6. πρ. τινί ποιεῖν τι to allow  one to do, (Pindar)
7. to give up, deliver over, betray  one to his enemy, (Herdotus Historicus): —;Pass. to be given  or thrown away , εἰ προεῖτο ταῦτα (Demosthenes Orator)

deep_entry:
Abbott-Smith / STEPBible (TBESG)
1. to be placed  or laid by  or upon, to lie by  or upon , οὔατα προσέκειτο handles were upon  it, (Iliad by Homer); τῇ θύρᾳ προσκεῖσθαι to keep close to  the door, (Aristophanes Comicus); δοκοὶ τῷ τείχει προσκείμεναι lying near  the wall, (Thucydides):—; ὁ προσκείμενος ἵππος the inside  horse (turning a corner), (Sophocles Tragicus)
2. to lie beside, cling to , (Sophocles Tragicus): of a woman, to be given to wife , τινί (Herdotus Historicus)
3. generally, to be involved in  or bound up with  good or evil, with dative, (Sophocles Tragicus)
4. to be attached  or devoted to , τινί (Herdotus Historicus), etc.; πρ. τῷ λεγομένῳ to put faith in  a story, (Herdotus Historicus); πρ. οἴνῳ to be addicted to  wine, (Herdotus Historicus); ἄγραις hunting, (Sophocles Tragicus), etc.
5. to press upon, be urgent with  a person, with dative, (Herdotus Historicus); προσκείμενος with zeal , (Thucydides)
6. in military sense, to press close  or hard, pursue closely , τινί (Thucydides); absolute to follow close , (Aristophanes Comicus); τὸ προσκείμενον the enemy , (Herdotus Historicus)
7. with a thing for the subject, to fall to, belong to , τοῖσι θεῶν τιμὴ αὕτη προσκέαται (Herdotus Historicus); πρ. τινι δοῦλος (Euripides):—; to be laid upon  as a charge, to do something, with infinitive, (Herdotus Historicus)
8. to be added  or attached to , (Sophocles Tragicus):—;absolute, ἡ χάρις προσκείσεται (Sophocles Tragicus) (ML)

σίγμα or σῖγμα (both accents are found in codices), τό, twentyfirst letter of the Etruscan abecedaria, [Refs [“IG” 14.2420]], and probably of the oldest Gr. alphabets (corresponding to the twenty-first Hebrew letter shin ??, Phoenician Ω, [Refs [“Syria” 6.103), but eighteenth of the _Ionic dialect_ alphabet: as numeral σ = 200, but σ᾽]] = 200,000: a semi-vowel, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Poetica” 1456b28, compare 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Theaetetus” 203b.]]

__A
the oldest forms expressing this sound were Μ (which is however the old eighteenth letter, which see), also Σ and ς; compared to a twisted curl, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Fragmenta” 382.7, 4th c.BC: Theodectes Tragicus 6]]; to a Scythian bow, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Agatho Tragicus 4]]; after this, but yet early, it took the shape of a semicircle ??, whence [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aeschrio Lyricus (“fragment” 1) calls the new moon τὸ καλὸν οὐρανοῦ νέον σῖγμα: hence the orchestra is called τὸ τοῦ θεάτρου σῖγμα, 9th c.AD: Photius Legal icographus, etc., “Anecdota Graeca - Bekker” 286]]: and Latin writers used sigma of a semicircular couch, [Refs 1st c.AD+ [1st c.AD: Martialis Epigrammaticus Latinus 10.48.6, etc.]]; compare σιγμοειδής. The rare form ?? is used in the numbering of building-stones in [Refs [“Berl.Sitzb.” 1888.1234, 1242 (Pergam.)]]. From final ς must be disting uished the character ς = 6, see ϝ ϝ (sixth letter).

__B
the name σίγμα (σῖγμα) was usually indeclinable, τοῦ σῖγμα [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus [same place], “Cra.” 402e, 427a, 2nd c.AD: Athenaeus Epigrammaticus 10.455c, 6th c.AD: Lydus, Joannes Laurentius Historicus “de Mensibus” 1.21 (variant{σίγματος}); τῷ σῖγμα 2nd c.AD: Galenus Medicus “de Usu Partium” 2.14, +others; τῶν σῖγμα 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Comicus 30; τὰ σίγμα τὰ ἐπὶ τῶν ἀσπίδων 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Historia Graeca (Hellenica)” 4.4.10, compare 2nd c.AD(?): Helladius Epigrammaticus cited in 9th c.AD: Photius Legal icographus, etc. “Bibliotheca - Patrologia Graeca” p.532 5th c.BC: Bacchylides Lyricus; later declined, τοῦ σίγματος 12th c.AD: Eustathius Episcopus Thessalonicensis 1389.15; σίγμασιν [prev. author] 905.7.]]

__B.2
we also hear of another name σάν [ᾰ], τό, τὰ οὐνόματά σφι (i.e. τοῖσι Πέρσῃσι) τελευτῶσι πάντα ἐς τὠυτὸ γράμμα, τὸ Δωριέες μὲν σὰν καλέουσι, Ἴωνες δὲ σίγμα [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.139, compare 5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “Dithyrambi - POxy.” 1604 “fragment” 1 ii 3, 2nd c.AD: Athenaeus Epigrammaticus 11.467a]]; as name of the fourth and tenth letters in Θρασύμαχος, and of the sixth in Διονύσο (υ), epigram cited in [Refs 5th c.BC+ [2nd c.AD: Athenaeus Epigrammaticus 10.454f, 5th c.BC: Achaeus Tragicus 33.4]]; compare the compound σαμ-φόρας: σάν and σίγμα were evidently pronounced alike; it is conjectured that σάν is originally the name of the old eighteenth letter.

Abbott-Smith / STEPBible (TBESG)
1. a sign  or token by which one infers  a thing, [variant datesTragica Adespota; λαμπάδος τὸ σύμβολον the token  of the beacon-fire, (Aeschulus Tragicus):—;often in plural, of marks  on the body, (Euripides); of omens , (Aeschulus Tragicus)
2. a pledge  or pawn , on which money was advanced, (Lysias Orator)
3. in plural tallies , Lat. tesserae hospitales, i.e. the halves  of a bone or coin, which two persons broke between them, each keeping one piece, (Herdotus Historicus), etc.
4. at Athens, a ticket, counter , Lat. tessera, such as were given to the dicasts, on presenting which they received their fee, (Demosthenes Orator)
5. a permit  or licence to reside, given to aliens , (Aristophanes Comicus); a ticket  given by each person who joined in a picnic, to be presented for payment at the end (compare συμβολή IV), (Aristophanes Comicus)
6. in Eccl. the distinctive mark  of Christians, a confession of faith, a creed , Lat. symbolum.
7. in legal phrase, σύμβολα were covenants between two states for protection of commerce , (Demosthenes Orator), etc.; σύμβολα ποιεῖσθαι πρὸς πόλιν to make a commercial treaty  with a state, τὰ ς. συγχέειν to violate such treaty , (Demosthenes Orator) (ML)

deep_entry:
Abbott-Smith / STEPBible (TBESG)
1. to stretch  by main force, to stretch to the uttermost , τόξον ἔτεινεν stretched  it to its full , (Iliad by Homer); ἐξ ἄντυγος ἡνία τείνας having tied  the reins tight  to the chariot-rail, (Iliad by Homer):—;Pass., [ ἱμὰς] τέτατο the strap was made tight , (Iliad by Homer); ἱστία τέτατο the sails were stretched , (Odyssey by Homer):—;absolute, μὴ τείνειν ἄγαν not to strain the cord  too tight, (Sophocles Tragicus)
2. metaphorically, ἶσον τείνειν πολέμου τέλος to strain  the even tug of war, (Iliad by Homer):—;Pass., ἐπὶ ἶσα μάχη τέτατο (Iliad by Homer); ἵπποισι τάθη δρόμος their pace was strained to the utmost , (Iliad by Homer): also, to exert oneself, be anxious , (Pindar)
3. to stretch out, spread , Ζεὺς λαίλαπα τείνει (Iliad by Homer); νὺξ τέταται βροτοῖσιν night is spread  over mankind, (Odyssey by Homer); so, of light, τέτατο φάος (Sophocles Tragicus); of sound, ἀμφὶ νῶτ᾽ ἐτάθη πάταγος (Sophocles Tragicus)
4. to aim at, direct towards  a point, properly from the bow, τείνειν βέλη (Sophocles Tragicus): then, metaphorically, τ. φόνον εἴς τινα to aim  death to one, design  it for him, (Euripides); τ. λόγον εἴς τινα (Plato Philosophus)
5. to stretch out in length , (Herdotus Historicus):—;Pass. to lie out at length, lie stretched , ταθεὶς ἐπὶ γαίηι (Iliad by Homer); ταθεὶς ἐνὶ δεσμῶι lying stretched  in chains, (Odyssey by Homer)
6. to stretch  or hold out, present , τινὰ ἐπὶ σφαγάν (Euripides):—;Mid., τείνεσθαι χέρε to stretch out one's  hands, etc., (Theocritus Poeta Bucolicus)
7. to extend, lengthen , of Time, (Aeschulus Tragicus); τείνειν λόγον (Aeschulus Tragicus)
8. intransitive, of geographical position, to stretch out  or extend , (Herdotus Historicus):—;of Time, τείνοντα χρόνον lengthening  time, (Aeschulus Tragicus)
9. to exert oneself, struggle , ἐναντία τινί (Plato Philosophus): to hurry on, hasten , (Euripides)
10. to extend to, reach , Lat. pertinere, ἐπὶ τὴν ψυχήν (Plato Philosophus)
11. to tend, refer, belong to , Lat. spectare ad, τείνει ἐς σέ it refers to, concerns  you, (Herdotus Historicus), etc.; ποῖ τείνε; to what tends  it? (Plato Philosophus); ἐγγύς τι τείνειν τοῦ θανάτου (Plato Philosophus) (ML)

13. to cut  or hew into shape , δούρατα (Odyssey by Homer), etc.
14. to cut lengthwise, to plough , Solon.

1. to satisfy, delight, gladden, cheer , (Homer), attic:—;absolute to give delight , (Odyssey by Homer); τὰ τέρποντα delights , (Sophocles Tragicus)

4. to enjoy oneself, make merry , with dative modi, φόρμιγγι, μύθοισι, etc., (Homer), etc.; so, τ. ἐν θαλίῃς (Odyssey by Homer), etc.:—; also with participle, τέρψει κλύων (Sophocles Tragicus); τέρπεται τιμώμενος (Euripides):—;absolute, πῖνε καὶ τέρπου drink and be merry , (Herdotus Historicus)

τέρπω,
[Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 1.347, etc.]]; Epic dialect subjunctive τέρπῃσι [Refs [17.385]]: Ionic dialect imperfect τέρπεσκον [Refs 4th c.AD+ [4th c.AD(?): Quintus Smyrnaeus Epicus 7.378, “Anthologia Graeca” 9.136 (from Cyrus)]]: future τέρψω [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Trachiniae” 1246, etc.]]: aorist ἔτερψα [Refs 5th c.BC+ [“hymnus ad Panem” 47, 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Heraclidae” 433, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Leges” 658b:]] —the passive and middle have a fivefold aorist,

__1
ἐτέρφθην [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 5.74, 8.131, 17.174, 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Coloneus” 1140, 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Ion” 541 (troch.)]]; rare in Prose, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Memorabilia” 2.1.24.]]

__2
_Epic dialect_ ἐτάρφθην, τάρφθην, 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 6.99, 19.213, 251, 21.57.

__3
_Epic dialect_ ἐτάρπην, τάρπην, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [23.300, 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 11.780, +others]]; infinitive ταρπῆναι [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 23.212, and ταρπήμεναι [prev. work] 346, 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 24.3;]]subjunctive τρᾰπείω, Epic dialect 1st pers. plural τρᾰπείομεν (see. below [Refs [11.2).]]

__4
Epic dialect also ἐταρπόμην, only in 1st pers. plural subjunctive ταρπώμεθα [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 4.295, +others]]; also reduplicate through all moods, τετάρπετο [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 19.19, 24.513; τεταρπώμεσθα 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 11.212, 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 23.10, 98; τεταρπόμενος 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 1.310, +others]]

__5
aorist 1 ἐτερψάμην, in Epic dialect subjunctive τέρψομαι [Refs [16.26 (but τέρψομαι]] is future middle in [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 20.23, 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Fragmenta” 677); _optative_ τέρψαιτο “hymnus ad Apollinem” 153]]; participle τερψάμενος [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 12.188]]:—delight, gladden, cheer, ὅ κεν τέρπῃσιν ἀείδων [Refs 8th c.BC+ [17.385; τῇ [φόρμιγγι] ὅ γε θυμὸν ἔτερπεν 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 9.189, +others; πεσσοῖσι.. θυμὸν ἔτερπον 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 1.107; καὶ τὸν ἔτερπε λόγοις 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 15.393; τοὐμὸν.. τ. κέαρ 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Trachiniae” 1246]]; θοίνῃ σε τ. [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Achaeus Tragicus 17]]; ἡ ἀγγελίη.. ἔτερψε [αὐτούς] [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 8.99]]; sometimes in Attic dialect Prose, ἔπεσι.. τὸ αὐτίκα τέρψει will give momentary pleasure, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 2.41, compare 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Leges” 658b, 658e, etc.]]; τ. τὴν ἀκοήν, τὰς ἀκοάς, [Refs 1st c.BC+ [1st c.BC: Philodemus Philosophus “περὶ ποιημάτων” 5.26, 28]]; ἧλιξ τέρπει τὸν ἥλικα, proverbial in [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Phaedrus” 240c, etc.]]: absolutely, give delight, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 1.347, 8.45, 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Ajax” 475]]; τὰ τέρποντα delights, [Refs [[prev. author] “OC” 1217 (Lyric poetry)]]; ῥήματα τέρψαντά τι[Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. work] 1281; οἱ τέρποντες λόγῳ ῥήτορες 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 3.40; τὰ τέρψοντα 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Agesilaus” 9.4.]]

__II
more frequently in passive and middle,

__II.1
in Epic dialect the aorist passive is used, with genitive of things, have full enjoyment of, enjoy to one's heart's content, ἐπεὶ τάρπημεν ἐδητύος ἠδὲ ποτῆτος [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 11.780; ἐπεὶ τάρπησαν ἐδωδῆς 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 3.70; σίτου τάρφθεν 6.99; τεταρπόμενοι φίλον ἦτορ σίτου καὶ οἴνοιο 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 9.705]]; ὕπνου, εὐνῆς ταρπήμεναι,[Refs 8th c.BC+ [24.3, 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 23.346; φιλότητος ἐταρπήτην [prev. work] 300; ἥβης ταρπῆναι [prev. work] 212]]: metaphorically, take one's fill of lamentation, τεταρπώμεσθα γόοιο [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 23.10, 98, 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 11.212, compare 19.213, 21.57.]]

__II.2
enjoy or delight oneself, with dative instrumental, φρένα τ. φόρμιγγι [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 9.186; μύθοισι 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 23.301; δαιτί 1.26; γόῳ φρένα 4.102; δίσκοισιν 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 2.774; ἐν θαλίῃς 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 11.603, 8th-7th c.BC: Hesiodus Epicus “Opera et Dies” 115]]; φιλότητι (or ἐν φ.) τραπείομεν εὐνηθέντε [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 3.441, 14.314 (whereas in the phrase λέκτρονδε τραπείομεν εὐνηθέντες (variant{-θέντε}), 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 8.292, the form τραπείομεν seems to be taken by the poet as belonging to τρέπω, though others retain the usually sense by connecting λέκτρονδε with εὐνηθέντες or by punctuating after λέκτρονδε)]]; so in Trag., λαμπάδι τερπόμεναι [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Eumenides” 1042 (Lyric poetry), compare 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Coloneus” 1140, etc.]]; delight in, τῇ τῶν πυραμίδων μεγαλειότητι [Refs 1st c.AD+ [“OGI” 666.26 (Egypt, 1st c.AD)]]; τοῖς εὐώδεσι [Refs 5th c.BC+ [2nd c.AD: Soranus Medicus 2.29; ἐπί τισι 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Rhesus” 194]]: with participle, λόγοις.. οἷς σὺ μὴ τέρψῃ κλύων [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Antigone” 691; τέρπεται τιμώμενος 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Bacchae” 321]]; τί ἂν.. ἀκούσας τερφθείη; [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Memorabilia” 2.1.24: _absolutely_, πῖνε καὶ τέρπευ]] drink and be merry, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 2.78.]]

__II.3
with internal accusative, οἴην μοῖραν δέκα μοιρέων τέρπεται ἀνήρ has only one tenth part of the enjoyment, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th-7th c.BC: Hesiodus Epicus “Fragmenta” 162; κενὴν ἐτερπόμην.. τέρψιν 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Fragmenta” 577; τέρπου κενὴν ὄνησιν 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Orestes” 1043.]]

__II.4
frequently with words which limit its sense, θυμῷ [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 19.313, 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 16.26; θυμόν 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 21.45; κατὰ θυμόν 8th-7th c.BC: Hesiodus Epicus “Opera et Dies” 58, 358; φρένα 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 1.474, 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 4.102, etc.; φρεσὶν ᾗσι τετάρπετο 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 19.19, compare 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 5.74; ἐνὶ φρεσίν 8.368; τεταρπόμενος φίλον κῆρ 1.310; ἀπάταισι θυμὸν τέρπεται 5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “P.” 2.74]]. Abbott-Smith / STEPBible (TBESG)
the Titans , a race of gods placed beneath Tartarus, (Iliad by Homer) (where two are named—;Iapetus and Cronus), accusative to (Hesiod), six sons and six daughters of Uranus and Gaia; hurled from Olympus into nether darkness, (Hesiod): other names are given by later Poets, as Atlas, (Aeschulus Tragicus); Prometheus, (Sophocles Tragicus); Θέμις (Aeschulus Tragicus); and in Lat. Poets Titan  is the Sun-god.

deep_entry:

4. Pass. and Mid., of places, to be turned  or look  in a certain direction, πρὸς ζόφον (Odyssey by Homer); πρὸς ἄρκτον, πρὸς νότον (Herdotus Historicus), etc.

7. to turn another way, to alter, change , νόον, φρένας (Homer), etc.; ἐς γέλων τρ. τὸ πρᾶγμα (Aristophanes Comicus):—;Pass. to be changed, change , (Homer), etc.; with accusative cognate, τρεπόμενος τροπάς undergoing  changes, (Aeschines Orator)

__2

__3

__II

deep_entry:

4. to wear out by rubbing : Pass., of a road, to wear  or tread it smooth , ἀτραπὸς τετριμμένη (Aristophanes Comicus)
5. of Time, to wear away, spend , Lat. terere vitam, (Sophocles Tragicus):—; absolute to waste time, tarry , (Aeschulus Tragicus)

7. metaphorically,

deep_entry:
Abbott-Smith / STEPBible (TBESG)
1. to lie under  or beneath , (Iliad by Homer); with dative, (Plato Philosophus)
2. in various metaphorically senses,
3. to be put under  the eyes or mind, i. e. to be submitted  or proposed to one , (Pindar); αἱ ὑποκείμεναι ἐλπίδες one's present  hopes, (Demosthenes Orator); ὑπόκειταί μοι ὅτι . . I have laid down the rule , that . ., (Herdotus Historicus)
4. to be laid down  or assumed as an hypothesis , (Plato Philosophus), etc.; τούτων ὑποκειμένων = Lat. his positis, (Plato Philosophus); impersonal, ὑπόκειται a rule is laid down , (Demosthenes Orator); ὑποκείσθω ὅτι . . let it be granted  that . ., (Aristotle Philosopher)
5. to be suggested , (Herdotus Historicus)
6. to be left at bottom, left remaining , (Thucydides)
7. to be subject to, submit to , τινι (Plato Philosophus): absolute to be submissive , (Plato Philosophus)
8. to be left behind in pledge, to be pledged  or mortgaged , τινος for  a certain sum, (Demosthenes Orator), etc.; ὑποκείμενοι, of persons, bound for payment  of a sum of money, (Demosthenes Orator)
9. to underlie , as a substratum, (Plato Philosophus), etc.
10. to be subordinate , (Plato Philosophus) (ML)

ὑπόκειμαι,
used as passive of ὑποτίθημι, future ὑποκείσομαι Pi.O.1.85, etc., but aorist ὑπετέθην:— lie under, ὑπὸ δὲ ξύλα κεῖται [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 21.364; θεμέλιοι ὑ. 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 1.93; τὸν μηρὸν ὑποκείμενον ἔχειν 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “de Incessu Animalium” 712b32, compare “PA” 686a13, 689b18: with _dative_, τοιαύτης τῆς κρηπῖδος ὑποκειμένης ταῖς πολιτείαις 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Politicus” 301e: τὰ ὑποκείμενα, opposed to τὰ ὑπερκείμενα, 2nd c.AD: Soranus Medicus 1.8.]]

__2
of places, lie close to, ὑποκειμένης τῆς Εὐβοίας ὑπὸ τὴν Ἀττικήν [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Isocrates Orator 4.108; ὑ. τὸ πεδίον τῷ ἱερῷ 4th c.BC: Aeschines Orator 3.118; λόφος ὑποκείμενος τοῖς Σιννάκοις 1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus “Crassus” 29; τὸ τὴν οἰκουμένην ὑποκεῖσθαι πρὸς τοῦτον τὸν τόπον 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Meteorologica” 364a7, compare “Pr.” 941b39; [τὰ] πρὸς βορρᾶν καὶ ἄρκτον ὑποκείμενα μέρη τῶν ὀρέων “Geoponica” 2.5.1]]; τὰ ὑποκείμενα ἐδάφη the adjacent soil, [Refs 1st c.BC+ [1st c.BC: Diodorus Siculus Historicus 3.50]]; ἡ-κειμένη χώρα the adjacent country, [Refs [[prev. passage] (but, the]]adjacent low lands, [Refs 2nd c.BC+ [[prev. author] 2.37, 1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus “Sertorius” 17); ὄρος ὑπόκειται 2nd c.BC: Polybius Historicus 5.59.4 codices (ἐπίκ- Schweigh.)]]; ὁ ὑποκείμενος ποταμός [Refs [[prev. author] 3.74.2]]; ὑποκεῖσθαι πρὸς τὴν ο?~Xψιν to be presented to the sight, [Refs 2nd c.BC+ [2nd c.BC: Demetrius Lacon Philosophus “Herc.” 1013.17.]]

__3
to be given below in the text, κατὰ τὴν.. συγγραφήν, ἧς τὸ ἀντίγραφον ὑπόκειται [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [“PCair.Zen.” 355.122 (3rd c.BC)]]; γράψον.. τοὺς χαρακτῆρας ὡς ὑπόκειται as below, [Refs [PMag.Par. 1.408; λέγε τὸν λόγον τὸν ὑποκείμενον [prev. work]230; ὡς ὑπόκειται]] as below, [Refs 1st c.AD+ [Sammelb. 5231.11 (1st c.AD), etc.]]; also, as set forth, [Refs 5th c.AD+ [PKlein.Form. 78 (5th-6th c.AD).]]

__II
in various metaphorically senses,

__II.1
to be established, set before one (by oneself or another) as an aim or principle, ἐμοὶ μὲν οὗτος ἄεθλος ὑποκείσεται shall be my appointed task, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus]] [same place]; δυοῖν ὑποκειμένοιν ὀνομάτοιν two phrases being prescribed, having legal sanction, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 23.36]]; ὑπόκειται πρῶτον μὲν διωμοσία, δεύτερον δὲ λόγος the prescribed course is.., [Refs [[prev. work]71]]; μένειν ἐπὶ τῶν ὑποκειμένων to abide by one's resolves, [Refs 2nd c.BC+ [2nd c.BC: Polybius Historicus 1.19.6, 2.51.1; μένειν ἐπὶ τῆς ὑ. γνώμης [prev. author] 1.40.5]]; ἐμοὶ ὑπόκειται ὅτι.. for me it is a fixed principle that.., [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 2.123, compare 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Oeconomica” 1343b9; νομίζω συμφέρειν.. τοῦθ᾽ ὑποκεῖσθαι 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 14.3]]; τῶν πραγμάτων ἐν οἷς τὰ ὑποκείμενα διαφέρει τῷ εἴδει things of which the principles differ in kind, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Politica” 1275a35]]; τὰς ὑποκειμένας μοίρας τξ the conventional[Refs 1st c.BC+ [3600, 1st c.BC: Ptolemaeus Epigrammaticus “Alm.” 5.1.]]

__II.2
to be assumed as a hypothesis [Refs 5th c.BC+ [compare (ὑπόθεσις 111), 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Cratylus” 436d, +others]]; ὑπέκειτο μὴ οἷόν τε εἶναι.. [Refs [[prev. author] “Erx.” 404b; τούτων ὑποκειμένων [prev. author] “Prt.” 359a, “R.” 478e]]; τὴν ἐκ τῶν -κειμένων ἀρίστην [πολιτείαν] the best (possible) in the circumstances, opposed to to τὴν κρατίστην ἁπλῶς and to τὴν ἐξ ὑποθέσεως, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Politica” 1288b26; ὑποκείσθω τι]]let it be taken for granted, [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [[prev. author] “EN” 1103b32, compare 1129a11, +others, 2nd c.AD: Galenus Medicus 15.175]]; ὑποκείσθω ὅτι.. let it be taken for granted that.., [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Politica” 1323b40; ὑ. εἶναι τὴν ἡδονὴν κίνησιν [prev. author] “Rh.” 1369b33: so with a _nominative_, ὑ. ἡ ἀρετὴ εἶναι.. [prev. author] “EN” 1104b27, compare “Rh.” 1357a11]]: with participle, τοιόνδε ζῷον ὑ. ὄν [Refs [[prev. author] “GA” 778b17: without any Verb, ἡ τοῦ δέρματος φύσις ὑ. γεώδης (i.e. εἶναι or οὖσα) [prev. work] 782a29, etc.: compare ὑποτίθημι IV. 1.]]

__II.3
to be suggested, τρόπῳ τῷ ἐξ ἐμεῦ -κειμένῳ [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 3.40.]]

__II.4
to be in prospect, ἐλπὶς ὑπόκειται σφαλεῖσι κἂν αὐτοὺς διασῴζεσθαι [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 3.84; αἱ ὑποκείμεναι προσδοκίαι καὶ αἱ ἐλπίδες 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 19.24]]; παρ᾽ ὑμῖν ὀργὴ μεγάλη καὶ τιμωρία ὑπόκειται τοῖς τὰ ψευδῆ μαρτυροῦσι is reserved for them, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [[prev. author] 34.19, compare 4th c.BC: Lycurgus Orator 130; δυοῖν κινδύνοιν -κειμένοιν [prev. passage]; ὁρᾶν τὸν θάνατον ὑποκείμενον “PPetr.” 3p.73 (3rd c.BC)]]; φόβου ὑποκειμένου ὅτι οἴσει τι βέβαιον παρὰ σοῦ [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [“PSI” 4.380.3 (3rd c.BC)]]; τοῦτο καὶ τοῖς μηθὲν ἀσεβὲς ἐπιτελεσαμένοις κατὰ τοὺς τοῦ πολέμου νόμους ὑπόκειται παθεῖν [Refs 2nd c.BC+ [2nd c.BC: Polybius Historicus 2.58.10.]]

__II.5
to be subject to, submit to, τῷ ἄρχοντι [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Gorgias” 510c; βασιλεῖ 2nd-3rd c.AD: Philostratus Sophista “Vita Apollonii” 3.20; πατράσιν “POxy.” 237 vii 16 (2nd c.AD)]]; ἐξετάσεσιν [Refs 4th c.AD+ [“PFlor.” 33.14 (4th c.AD)]]; βασάνοις [Refs 3rd c.AD+ [“POxy.” 58.25 (3rd c.AD)]]: absolutely, pay court to one, ὑποκείσονται δεόμενοι καὶ τιμῶντες [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 494c]]; τῷ λόγῳ to be captivated by the story, [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd-3rd c.AD: Philostratus Sophista “Vita Apollonii” 6.14; θρῆνοι -κείμενοι]]subdued, [Refs [[prev. author] “VS” 2.4.2.]]

__II.6
to be subject to, liable to a penalty, [Refs 6th c.AD+ [“Supp.epigram” 6.424, compare 415,421, +others (from Iconium), “PLond.” 1.77.53 (6th c.AD)]]: also with accusative, ὑποκείσεται τῷ φίσκῳ δηνάρια πεντακόσια [Refs [“Rev.Phil.” 36.61 (from Iconium).]]

__II.7
to be pledged or mortgaged, with genitive, for a certain sum, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Isaeus Orator 6.33, 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 49.11,35; ναῦς ὑποκειμένη ἡμῖν [prev. author] 56.4]]; τὰ ὑποκείμενα the articles pledged, Syngr. cited in [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 35.12]]; the mortgaged property, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [“SIG” 1044.28 (Halic., 4th-3rd c.BC)]]; ἐνέχυρα-κείμενα[Refs [“IG” 12(7).58 (from Amorgos)]]; ὑποκείμενοι, of slaves pledged for a sum of money, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 27.9.]]

__II.7.b
of payments, to have been granted or allocated, ἀποφαίνουσιν ὑποκεῖσθαι ἐν τῇ γραφῇ τῶν εἰς τὰ ἱερὰ (i.e. ὑποκειμένων) δίδοσθαι κτλ. [Refs 2nd c.BC+ [“UPZ” 21.4 (2nd c.BC), compare 23.21 (2nd c.BC), “BGU” 1197.4, 1200.28 (both 1st c.BC):]] substantive ὑποκείμενα, τά, ={φιλάνθρωπα}, salary (ear-marked proceeds of taxes), τὰ ἐπιβάλλοντά μοι ἐκ τοῦ ἱεροῦ ὑ. [Refs 1st c.AD+ [“PLond.” 2.357.9, compare 5 (1st c.AD)]]; ὑ. αἰτεῖ ἀπὸ τῶν κωμῶν [Refs 1st c.AD+ [“BGU” 23.12 (2nd-3rd c.AD),compare “OGI” 665.19,26 (Egypt, 1st c.AD)]]: with dative, as part of name of specific taxes, ὑ. βασιλικῇ γραμματείᾳ ear-marked for the benefit of.., [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [PPar. 17.22 (2nd c.AD)]]; ὑ. τοπογραμματείᾳ [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [“PSI” 1.101.18 (2nd c.AD),compare “POxy.” 1436.23 (2nd c.AD)]], etc.: also in singular, ὑποκείμενον ἐπιστρατηγία [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [“BGU” 199.14 (2nd c.AD),compare “PFlor.” 375.22 (2nd c.AD)]], etc.: also with genitive, ὑ. ἐννομίου [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [“PRyl.” 213.72, +others (2nd c.AD); τοπαρχίας [prev. work] 73, etc.]]

__II.8
in Philosophy, to underlie, as the foundation in which something else inheres, to be implied or presupposed by something else, ἑκάστῳ τῶν ὀνομάτων.. ὑ. τις ἴδιος οὐσία [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Protagoras” 349b, compare “Cra.” 422d, “R.” 581c, 5th-4th c.BC: Timaeus Locrus Philosophus 97e: τὸ ὑποκείμενον has three main applications: (1) to the matter which underlies the form, opposed to εἶδος, ἐντελέχεια, 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Metaphysica” 983a30; (2) to the substance (matter + form) which underlies the accidents, opposed to πάθη, συμβεβηκότα, [prev. author] “Cat.” 1a20, 27, “Metaphorical” 1037b16, 983b16; (3) to the logical subject to which attributes are ascribed, opposed to τὸ κατηγορούμενον, [prev. author] “Cat.” 1b10, 21, “Ph.” 189a31: applications (1) and (2)]] are distinguished in [Refs [[prev. author] “Metaphorical” 1038b5, 1029a1 - 5, 1042a26 - 31: τὸ ὑ.]] is occasionally used of what underlies or is presupposed in some other way, e. g. of the positive termini presupposed by change, [Refs [[prev. author] “Ph.” 225a3 - 7.]]

__II.8.b
exist, τὸ ἐκτὸς ὑποκείμενον the external reality, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [Stoic. 2.48, compare 4th-3rd c.BC: Epicurus Philosophus “Epistulae” 1pp.12,24 U.; φῶς εἶναι τὸ χρῶμα τοῖς ὑ. ἐπιπῖπτον 3rd-2nd c.BC: Aristarchus Grammaticus Sam. cited in “Placita Philosophorum” 1.15.5; τὸ κρῖνον τί τε φαίνεται μόνον καὶ τί σὺν τῷ φαίνεσθαι ἔτι καὶ κατ᾽ ἀλήθειαν ὑπόκειται 2nd c.AD: Sextus Empiricus Philosophus “adversus Mathematicos” 7.143, compare 83, 90, 91, 10.240]]; ={ὑπάρχω, τὰ ὑποκείμενα πράγματα} the existing state of affairs, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [2nd c.BC: Polybius Historicus 11.28.2, compare 11.29.1, 15.8.11, 13, 3.31.6, 4th-5th c.AD: Eunapius Historicus “Vitae Sophistarum” p.474 5th c.BC: Bacchylides Lyricus; Τίτος ἐξ ὑποκειμένων ἐνίκα, χρώμενος ὁπλις μοῖς καὶ τάξεσιν αἷς παρέλαβε 1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus “Comp. Phil.Flam.” 2; τῆς αὐτῆς δυνάμεως ὑποκειμένης [prev. author] 2.336b; ἐχομένου τοῦ προσιόντος λόγου ὡς πρὸς τὸν ὑποκείμενον 2nd c.AD: Apollonius Dyscolus Grammaticus “de Syntaxi;” 122.17.]]

short_definition: to stand — 1. in these tenses Causal, to place or set under , τί τινι (Herdotus Historicus); τρεῖς σταυροὺς ὑπίστησι plants three piles in the lake to support a house, (Herdotus Historicus):—
deep_entry:
Abbott-Smith / STEPBible (TBESG)
1. in these tenses Causal, to place  or set under , τί τινι (Herdotus Historicus); τρεῖς σταυροὺς ὑπίστησι plants  three piles in the lake to support  a house, (Herdotus Historicus):—;metaphorically, γνώμας ὑποστήσας σοφάς having laid  them as a foundation , (Sophocles Tragicus)
2. to post secretly  or in ambush , (Herdotus Historicus)
3. Causal also in future and aor1 middle to substitute , τί τινι one thing for  another, (Xenophon Historicus)
4. Pass., with aorist2  active ὑπ-έστην, perfect ὑφ-έστηκα, ionic participle ὑπ-εστεώς:—; to stand under as a support , with dative, (Herdotus Historicus)
5. to sink to the bottom, settle , τὸ ὑφιστάμενον the milk, opposite to τὸ ἐφιστάμενον (the cream), (Herdotus Historicus)
6. to place oneself under an engagement, engage  or promise  to do, with infinitive future, ὅσς᾽ Ἀχιλῆι ὑπέστημεν δώσειν (Iliad by Homer), etc.; with infinitive aorist, οὔ τίς με ὑπέστη σαῶσαι (Iliad by Homer); with infinitive present, (Herdotus Historicus):—;absolute, after promise given , (Odyssey by Homer); ὥσπερ ὑπέστη as he promised , (Thucydides):—;when followed by accusative, an infinitive may be supplied, τρίποδας οὕς οἱ ὑπέστη (i.e. δώσειν); (Iliad by Homer); ἐκτελέουσιν ὑπόσχεσιν ἥνπερ ὑπέσταν (Iliad by Homer)
7. to submit  to any one, τινι (Iliad by Homer)
8. with accusative rei, to submit to, consent to , ὁ τὸ ἐλάχιστον ὑπιστάμενος who offers to take  the least, (Herdotus Historicus); ὑφ. τὸν πλοῦν to undertake  it unwillingly , (Thucydides); so, ὑφ. τὸν κίνδυνον (Thucydides): —;rarely with dative, ὑφ. ξυμφοραῖς ταῖς μεγίσταις (Thucydides)
9. to undertake  an office, (Xenophon Historicus)
10. to lie concealed  or in ambush , (Herdotus Historicus), etc.
11. to support an attack, to resist, withstand , with dative, (Aeschulus Tragicus); with accusative, (Euripides):—;absolute to stand one's ground, face the enemy , Lat. subsistere, (Euripides) (ML)

short_definition: to pour — 1. Radic. sense, to pour :
deep_entry:
Abbott-Smith / STEPBible (TBESG)
1. Radic. sense, to pour :
2. properly of liquids, to pour out, pour , (Homer), etc.; Zeus χέει ὕδωρ, i. e. he makes it rain, (Iliad by Homer); χέει χιόνα βορέας (Euripides); absolute, χέει it snows , (Iliad by Homer):—;Mid. to pour for oneself , especially of drink-offerings, χοὰς χεόμην νεκύεσσι (Odyssey by Homer), etc.:—;Pass., χέονται κρῆναι they gush forth , (Euripides); χυθέντος ποτοῦ ἐς γῆν (Sophocles Tragicus)
3. χ. δάκρυα to shed  tears, (Iliad by Homer):—;Pass., of tears, to pour  or gush forth , (Homer); so of blood, to be shed , (Aeschulus Tragicus)
4. in Pass. to become liquid, melt, thaw , (Xenophon Historicus)
5. of solids, to shed, scatter , φύλλα (Iliad by Homer); πτερά (Odyssey by Homer); χ. κόνιν κὰκ κεφαλῆς (Homer); χ. καλάμην χθονί, of a mower or reaper (see. καλάμη), (Iliad by Homer)
6. like χώννυμι, to throw out  earth, so as to form a mound, σῆμα, τύμβον χ. (Homer)
7. χ. δοῦρα to pour  or shower  spears, (Iliad by Homer); Mid., βέλεα χέοντο they showered their  arrows, (Iliad by Homer)
8. to let fall  or drop , ἡνία (Iliad by Homer); so, χέειν κρόκου βαφὰς (see. βαφή II) (Aeschulus Tragicus); but, καρπὸν χ., of trees, to produce  fruit abundantly , (Odyssey by Homer)
9. in Pass. to be thrown  or heaped up together , (Homer)
10. in Pass. also of living beings, to pour  or stream in a dense mass  or throng , (Homer)
11. metaphorically of sounds, to pour forth , φωνήν, αὐδήν (Odyssey by Homer); φθόγγον (Aeschulus Tragicus)
12. of things that obscure the sight, κατ᾽ ὀφθαλμῶν χέεν ἀχλύν shed  a dark cloud over the eyes, (Iliad by Homer); πολλὴν ἠέρα χεῦε shed  a mist abroad, (Odyssey by Homer):—;Pass., ἀμφὶ δέ οἱ θάνατος χύτο was shed  around him, (Iliad by Homer); νόσος κέχυται (Sophocles Tragicus); φρὶξ ἐπὶ πόντον ἐχεύατο (Mid. in passive sense), (Iliad by Homer)
13. of persons, ἀμφ᾽ αὐτῶι χυμένη throwing herself  around him, (Homer): so in Mid., ἀμφὶ υἱὸν ἐχεύατο πήχεε (Iliad by Homer)
14. perfect passive κέχυμαι, to be wholly engaged in , Δᾶλος, ἐν ἇι κέχυμαι (Pindar) (ML)

Epic dialect ἔχευα [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 3.270, 4.269, χεῦα 14.436, 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 4.584, etc.]]; Epic dialect aorist 1 subjunctive χεύομεν [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 7.336 (late ἔχευσα “Anthologia Graeca” 14.124 (4th c.AD: Metrodorus Epigrammaticus)):]]perfect κέχῠκα, (ἐκ-) [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-3rd c.BC: Menander Comicus 915, “APl.” 4.242 (1st c.BC: Erycius Epigrammaticus)]]:—middle, future Attic dialect χεόμενος [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Isaeus Orator 6.51]]: aorist ἐχεάμην [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 7.43, 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Persae” 220 (troch.), 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Coloneus” 477, 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Vespae” 1020 (_anapaest meter_)]]; Epic dialect ἐχευάμην, χευάμην, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 5.314, 18.24, etc.]]; Epic dialect subjunctive χεύεται (περι-) [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 6.232 (perhaps _indicative_):]] —passive, future χῠθήσομαι (συγ-) [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 23.62, compare 1st c.AD: Josephus Historicus “Antiquitates Judaicae” 8.8.5: later χεθήσομαι, (ἐκ-) 2nd c.AD: Arrianus Historicus “Epicteti Dissertationes” 4.10.26:]] —aorist 1 ἐχύθην [ῠ] [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 19.590, etc.: later ἐχέθην,]] not in Inscrr. or Papyrus, falsa lectio in [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [1st c.AD: Philo Judaeus 1.455, 3rd c.BC: Euclides Geometra “Catoptr.Prooem.” (vii p.286 H., ἐγ-, ἐκ-), etc.: also _Epic dialect_]]aorist χύτο [ῠ] [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 23.385, 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 7.143; ἐξ-έχῠτο 19.470]]; ἔχυντο, χύντο,[Refs 8th c.BC+ [10.415, 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 4.526]]; participle χύμενος, η, ον, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [19.284, 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 8.527, and Trag. in Lyric poetry, 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Choephori” 401, “Eu.” 263, 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Heraclidae” 76]]: perfect κέχῠμαι [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 5.141, 7th-6th c.BC: Sappho Lyrica “Papyrus fragments” in E. Diehl, 25.12, 5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “I.” 1.4, etc.]]: pluperfect Epic dialect κέχῠτο [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 5.696, etc.]]—Epic dialect present χείω, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th-7th c.BC: Hesiodus Epicus “Theogonia” 83]]; later Epic dialect present χεύω both in the simple Verb and compounds, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [2nd c.BC: Nicander Epicus “Alexipharmaca” 381, “Lyrica Alexandrina Adespota” 35.19 (perhaps 2nd c.AD: Mesomedes Lyricus), 4th-5th c.AD(?): Nonnus Epicus 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 18.344, 3rd c.AD: Oppianus Apamensis Epicus “Cynegetica” 2.127]]:—middle, χεύομαι [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [3rd c.BC: Apollonius Rhodius Epicus 2.926]]: in later Prose present χύνω (which see); χῦσαι is falsa lectio for{λῦσαι} in codices dett. of [Refs 3rd c.AD+ [3rd-4th c.AD: Tryphiodorus Epicus 205.]] —Rare in Prose, except in compounds and in middle

__B
Radic. sense, pour:

__B.I
properly of liquids, pour out, let flow, κρήνη κατ᾽ αἰγίλιπος πέτρης χέει ὕδωρ [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 9.15; βασιλεῦσιν ὕδωρ ἐπὶ χεῖρας ἔχευαν 3.270, compare 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 1.146, etc.; οἶνον χαμάδις χέε 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 23.220; κατὰ στόματος νέκταρ 3rd c.BC: Theocritus Poeta Bucolicus 7.82: χέει ὕδωρ,]] of Zeus, i.e. makes it rain, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 16.385; ὅταν βορέας χιόνα.. χέῃ 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Cyclops” 328: _absolutely_, χέει]] it snows, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 12.281 (νειφέμεν is in l. 280)]]: frequently of drink-offerings, χέουσα χοάς [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Choephori” 87]]:—middle, χοὴν χεῖσθαι νεκύεσσι [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 10.518; χοὴν χεόμην νεκύεσσι 11.26; χοὰς χέασθαι 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 7.43, etc.: _absolutely_, 4th c.BC: Isaeus Orator 6.51, 65]]:—passive, κέχυται [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 12.284]]; κρῆναι χέονται they gush forth, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Hippolytus” 748 (Lyric poetry); ποτοῦ χυθέντος ἐς γῆν 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Trachiniae” 704]]; χέεσθαι βουτύρῳ, γάλακτι to flow with.., [LXX.Job.29.6.]

__B.I.2
χ. δάκρυα shed tears, δάκρυα θερμὰ χέοντες [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 7.426, compare 16.3, 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Troades” 38; ἀπ᾽ ὀφθαλμῶν [prev. author] “Cyc.” 405]]:—middle, ὅσα σώματα χεῖται [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Timaeus” 83e]]:—passive, of tears, flow, δάκρυα θερμὰ χέοντο [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 4.523; ἀπ᾽ ὀφθαλμῶν χύτο δάκρυα 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 23.385]]; of blood, to be shed, drip, φονίας σταγόνας χυμένας ἐς πέδον [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Choephori” 401 (_anapaest meter_), compare “Eu.” 263 (Lyric poetry).]]

__B.I.3
smelt metal, [LXX.Mal.3.3.]

__B.I.3.b
cast, of bronze statues, [Refs 6th c.BC+ [“SIG” 3g (Susa, from Didyma, 6th c.BC(?)).]]

__B.I.4
passive, become liquid, melt, dissolve, τὰ κεχυμένα, opposed to τὰ συνεστῶτα, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Timaeus” 66c]]; of the ground in spring, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Oeconomicus” 16.12, 4th-3rd c.BC: Theophrastus Philosophus “de Causis Plantarum” 3.4.4]]; κεχυμένοι ὀφθαλμοί perhaps moist, languishing eyes, [Refs 4th c.AD+ [4th c.AD: Hephaestio Astrologus 1.1.]]

__B.II
of solids, shed, scatter, φύλλα ἄνεμος χαμάδις χέει [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 6.147; κῦμα φῦκος ἔχευεν 9.7; πτερὰ ἔραζε 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 15.527]]; ἐν.. ἄλφιτα χ. δοροῖσιν pour into..,[Refs 8th c.BC+ [2.354; [κρέα] εἰν ἐλεοῖσιν 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 9.215; κόνιν κὰκ κεφαλῆς 18.24, 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 24.317]]; καλάμην χθονί, of a mower or reaper, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 19.222]]:—passive, ἐν νάσῳ κέχυται σπέρμα [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “P.” 4.42]]; πάγου χυθέντος when the frost was on the ground, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Philoctetes” 293]]; κέχυται νόσος has spread through his frame, [Refs [[prev. author] “Tr.” 853 (Lyric poetry).]]

__B.II.2
throw up earth, so as to form a mound, σῆμ᾽ ἔχεαν [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 24.799]]; χεύαντες δὲ τὸ σῆμα[Refs 8th c.BC+ [[prev. work] 801, compare 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 1.291; τύμβον χ. 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 7.336, etc.; θανόντι χυτὴν ἐπὶ γαῖαν ἔχευαν 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 3.258, compare 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 23.256.]]

__B.II.3
χ. δούρατα shower spears, [Refs [5.618]]:—middle, βέλεα χέοντο they showered their darts, [Refs [8.159.]]

__B.II.4
let fall, drop, κατὰ δ᾽ ἡνία χεῦεν ἔραζε [Refs 8th c.BC+ [17.619; εἴδατα ἔραζε 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 22.20]]; ἀπὸ κρατὸς χέε (variant for{βάλε}) δέσματα [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 22.468; κρόκου βαφὰς ἐς πέδον χέουσα 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Agamemnon” 239 (Lyric poetry) (but καρπὸν χ.,]] of trees, not to shed their fruit, but to let it hang down in profusion, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 11.588)]]:—passive, πλόκαμος γένυν παρ᾽ αὐτὴν κεχυμένος streaming down, falling, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Bacchae” 456.]]

__B.II.5
in passive, to be heaped up, massed together, [ἰχθύες] ἐπὶ ψαμάθοισι κέχυνται [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 22.387, compare 389]]; of dead geese, [Refs [19.539]]; of dung,[Refs 8th c.BC+ [17.298, 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 23.775; also σωρὸν σίτου κεχυμένον 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.22.]]

__B.II.6
passive, of living beings, stream in a dense throng, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 16.267, etc.; δακρυόεντες ἔχυντο 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 10.415, etc.: of sheep, 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 5.141.]]

__B.II.7
of persons, ἀμφ᾽ αὐτῷ χυμένη throwing herself around him,[Refs 8th c.BC+ [19.284, 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 8.527]]:—middle, ἀμφὶ φίλον υἱὸν ἐχεύατο πήχεε [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 5.314]]:—passive, of things, ἀμφὶ δὲ δεσμοὶ τεχνήεντες ἔχυντο [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 8.297.]]

__B.II.8
perfect passive κέχυμαι, to be wholly engaged or absorbed in, Δᾶλος, ἐν ᾇ κέχυμαι [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “I.” 1.4]]; κεχυμένος ἐς τἀφροδίσια, Latin effusus in Venerem, [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd c.AD: Lucianus Sophista “Sacr.” 5; πρὸς ἡδονήν 4th c.AD: Alciphro Epistolographus 1.6.]]

__B.III
of impalpable things:

__B.III.1
of the voice, φωνήν, αὐδὴν χ., [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 19.521, 8th-7th c.BC: Hesiodus Epicus “Scutum Herculis” 396, compare “Th.” 83; ἐπὶ θρῆνον ἔχεαν 5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “I.” 8(7).64; Ἑλλάδος φθόγγον χέουσα 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Septem contra Thebas” 73, compare “Supp.” 632 (Lyric poetry), “fragment” 36 (Lyric poetry)]]; of wind instruments, πνεῦμα χέων ἐν αὐλοῖς [Refs 7th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Simonides Lyricus 148.8, compare “APl.” 4.226 (7th-6th c.BC: Alcaeus Lyricus)]]:—middle, κωμῳδικὰ πολλὰ χέασθαι [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Vespae” 1020 (_anapaest meter_):]] —but in passive, κεχυμένα ᾄσματα non-rhythmical melodies, [Refs 3rd c.AD+ [3rd c.AD(?): Aristides Quintilianus Musicus 1.13.]]

__B.III.1.b
κὰκ κεφαλῆς χεῦεν πολὺ κάλλος [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 23.156; δόλον περὶ δέμνια χεῦεν 8.282.]]

__B.III.2
of things that obscure the sight, κατ᾽ ὀφθαλμῶν χέεν ἀχλύν shed a dark cloud over the eyes, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 20.321]]; πολλὴν ἠέρα χεῦε shed a mist abroad, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 7.15, etc. (so εὔκρατος ἀὴρ χεῖται 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Axiochus” 371d); τῷ δ᾽ ὕπνον ἀπήμονά τε λιαρόν τε χεύῃ ἐπὶ βλεφάροισιν 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 14.165, compare 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 2.395, etc.:]] — passive, ἀμφὶ δέ οἱ θάνατος χύτο was shed around him, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 13.544; κατ᾽ ὀφθαλμῶν κέχυτ᾽ ἀχλύς 5.696; νύξ 8th-7th c.BC: Hesiodus Epicus “Theogonia” 727 (but πάλιν χύτο ἀήρ]] the mist dissolved or vanished, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 7.143); οὔ κέ μοι ὕπνος ἐπὶ βλεφάροισι χυθείη 19.590]]; ἐχεύατο πόντον ἔπι φρίξ (middle in passive sense) [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 7.63.]]

__B.III.3
aorist passive, ἐχύθη οἱ θυμός his mind overflowed with joy, [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [3rd c.BC: Apollonius Rhodius Epicus 3.1009.]]

__B.III.4
passive, to be dissipated, diffused, [Refs 3rd c.AD+ [3rd c.AD: Plotinus Philosophus 1.4.10; οὐδὲν τοῦ χεῖσθαι δεηθέν [prev. author] 6.5.3]]; to be rarefied, opposed to πιλεῖσθαι, [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd c.AD: Galenus Medicus 15.28]]. (Cf. Sanskrit juhóti 'pour (sacrificial offerings)', participle hutás (= χυτός), Latin fundo, Gothic giutan 'pour'.)

short_definition: a claw — 1. a horse's hoof , (Hesiod):—;also, a cloven hoof , (Euripides)

deep_entry:
Abbott-Smith / STEPBible (TBESG)
1. a horse's hoof , (Hesiod):—;also, a cloven hoof , (Euripides)
2. in plural, of the talons  of a bird, [variant datesTragica Adespota; of a wolf's claws , (Theocritus Poeta Bucolicus)
3. a sea-bank, breakwater , formed of stones laid at the base of a sea-wall, to break the force of the waves (so called because it projected like a hoof) , Lat. crepido, (Thucydides)
4. the spur of a mountain  or ridge of rocks  answering a like purpose, (Thucydides)
5. a cloven implement , such as a netting-needle;—;  compare χηλεύω. (ML)

LSJ / STEPBible (TFLSJ)
χηλ-ή,
Doric dialect χᾱλά, ἡ, horse's hoof, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th-7th c.BC: Hesiodus Epicus “Scutum Herculis” 62, 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Phoenissae” 42, “Ion” 1242 (Lyric poetry), compare χηλαργός.]]

__2
of oxen and the like, cloven hoof, χηλαὶ ποδῶν [Refs 4th c.BC+ [[prev. author] “Ba.” 619 (troch.), compare 3rd c.BC: Apollonius Rhodius Epicus 2.667; τὰ δὲ δισχιδῆ καὶ ἀντὶ τῶν ὀνύχων χηλὰς ἔχει 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Historia Animalium” 499b9, compare “PA” 655b4, 663a29]]; of Chimaera, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Electra” 474 (Lyric poetry).]]

__3
crab's claw, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Historia Animalium” 527b5, “PA” 684a27; ὅ τι ἂν λάβῃ, προσάγεται πρὸς τὸ στόμα τῇ δικρόᾳ χηλῇ καθάπερ οἱ καρκίνοι [prev. author] “HA” 590b25: hence,]]

__3.b
Astron., Χηλαί, αἱ, the claws of the Scorpion, i.e. the constellation Libra, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-3rd c.BC: Aratus Epicus 89, 232, +others, 2nd c.AD: Ptolemaeus Mathematicus “Tetrabiblos” 24, etc.]]

__4
poetry plural, talons of a bird, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Persae” 208, 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Antigone” 1003, 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Ion” 1208]]; of the Sphinx, [Refs [[prev. author] “Ph.” 808 (Lyric poetry), 1025 (Lyric poetry)]]; of a wolf's claws, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [3rd c.BC: Theocritus Poeta Bucolicus “Epigrammata” 6.4, compare 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Hecuba” 90 (Lyric poetry, explained by 5th c.AD(?): Hesychius Legal icographus ={γνάθος}).]]

__II
breakwater, formed of stones laid at the base of a sea-wall, mostly in plural, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 1.63 (ubi see Scholia), 7.53, 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 7.1.17; αἱ χ. τοῦ λιμένος 1st c.BC: Diodorus Siculus Historicus 13.78, compare 2nd-3rd c.AD: Dio Cassius Historicus 74.10; _sing._, 1st c.BC: Diodorus Siculus Historicus 3.44; ἐπαιγιαλῖτις χ. “Anthologia Graeca” 10.8 (1st c.BC: Archias).]]

__II.2
spur of a mountain or ridge of rocks answering a like purpose, χ. γὰρ τοῦ Πειραιῶς ἡ Ἠετιωνεια [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 8.90, compare 1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus “Solon” 9, Anonymus cited in 10th c.AD: Suidas Legal icographus see at {χ. ὄρους}.]]

__III
of various cloven or hooked implements:

__III.1
in surgery, forked probe, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Hippocrates Medicus “περὶ νούσων” 2.33.]]

__III.2
notch of an arrow, [Refs 2nd c.BC+ [2nd-1st c.BC(?): Hero Mechanicus “Belopoeica” 111.1, 5th c.AD(?): Hesychius Legal icographus]] see at {γλυφίδες}; but also (plural) the claws composing the hook (χείρ), [Refs 2nd c.BC+ [2nd-1st c.BC(?): Hero Mechanicus [prev. work]2]]; also the claws or arms of the σκορπίος see, [Refs 1st c.BC+ [1st c.BC: Vitruvius Scriptor de Architectura Latinus 10.10.4, 10.11.7.]]

__III.3
rims of the eyelids, [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd c.AD: Rufus Medicus “περὶ ὀνομασίας” 20.]]

__III.4
crack in the heels or other parts, [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd c.AD(?): Pollianus Epigrammaticus 4.198.]]

__III.5
net, plait, [Refs 5th c.AD+ [5th c.AD(?): Hesychius Legal icographus see at {χηλευτὰ κράνη}.]]

Lat. laena, a large square upper-garment, a cloak, mantle, (Homer); it was made of wool, and worn over the χιτών, thrown over the shoulders, fastened with a pin or brooch  περόνη). It is also called φᾶρος by (Homer), and in later Greek ἱμάτιον, Latin pallium.

LSJ / STEPBible (TFLSJ)
χνόος, ὁ
(ἡ [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Fragmenta” 1106)]], Attic dialect contraction χνοῦς, genitive χνοῦ: irregular genitive χνοός [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.AD: Choeroboscus Grammaticus “Scholia in Theodosii Canones” 1.234H.; _dative_ χνοΐ 4th-3rd c.BC: Theophrastus Philosophus “de Causis Plantarum” 6.10.7, 2nd c.AD: Galenus Medicus 13.850:]] —ἁλὸς χ. incrustation from salt water, ἔκ κεφαλῆς ἔσμηχεν ἁλὸς χνόον, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 6.226]]; wool pulled for stuffing cushions, flock, falsa lectio for{μνοῦς} in [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Hippocrates Medicus “γυναικεῖα” 1.61]]; used in applying a powder, [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd c.AD: Galenus Medicus [same place]]]; chaff, [LXX.Psa.1.4]: powder, proverbial, [ὄνος] εἰς ἄχυρα καὶ χνοῦν [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Fragmenta” 76]]; dust of the earth, [LXX.2Ki.22.43, LXX.2Ch.1.9]; ὡς δοκεῖν τοῦ καλουμένου χνοῦ μεστοὺς εἶναι (i.e. τοὺς ὀφθαλμούς) [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd c.AD: Galenus Medicus 16.552.]]

__II
fine down on a flower or in the seed-vessel, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-3rd c.BC: Theophrastus Philosophus “Historia Plantarum” 2.8.4, 1st c.BC: Diodorus Siculus Historicus 2.59]]:bloom on fruit, ἐν Καρίᾳ φασὶν ἄπιόν τιν᾽ ἔχειν χνοῦν ἁλμώδη [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-3rd c.BC: Theophrastus Philosophus “de Causis Plantarum” 6.10.7; μάλων χνοῦς ἐπικαρπίδιος “Anthologia Graeca” 9.226 (1st c.BC-1st c.AD: Zonas Epigrammaticus)]]; the first down on the chin or cheeks, χνοῦς ὥσπερ μήλοισιν ἐπήνθει [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Nubes” 978 (_anapaest meter_); κοῦρος ἔτ᾽ ἀρτιγένειον ἔχων χνόον “Anthologia Graeca” 9.219 (1st c.BC-1st c.AD: Diodorus Epigrammaticus); θηλείαις οὐδ᾽ ὅσσον ἐπὶ χνόος ἦλθε παρειαῖς 3rd c.BC: Callimachus Epicus “Hymnus in Apollinem” 37; ἐντίκτει τι χνοῦ ἀνάπλεων 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Historia Animalium” 605b15: _plural_, 1st c.BC: Dionysius Halicarnassensis “de Demosthene” 51.]]

__II.2
metaphorically, bloom or film of archaism in writing, ὅ τε πίνος αὐτῇ (i.e. in Plato's style) [καὶ χ.] ὁ τῆς ἀρχαιότητος.. ἐπιτρέχει interpolated in [Refs 1st c.BC+ [1st c.BC: Dionysius Halicarnassensis “de Demosthene” 5]]; ἐπανθεῖ τις.. χνοῦς ἀρχαιοπινής[Refs 1st c.AD+ [[prev. work] 38, compare 1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus 2.79d]]; οἱονεὶ τῆς γονίμου φύσεως χ., of χλόη, [Refs 3rd c.AD+ [3rd c.AD: Porphyrius Tyrius Philosophus “de Abstinentia - Porphyrii Opuscula” 2.5. (Cf. χνιαρωτέρα, χνίει.)]]

short_definition: to join in a dance — 1. to dance a round or choral dance , (Sophocles Tragicus), etc.; especially of the Bacchic chorus, (Euripides):—; to take part in the chorus , regarded as a matter of religion, (S
deep_entry:
Abbott-Smith / STEPBible (TBESG)
1. to dance a round  or choral dance , (Sophocles Tragicus), etc.; especially of the Bacchic chorus, (Euripides):—; to take part in the chorus , regarded as a matter of religion, (Sophocles Tragicus): to be one of a chorus , (Aristophanes Comicus): —;with dative pers. to dance to  him, in  his honour , (Euripides)
2. generally, to dance , especially from joy, (Sophocles Tragicus)
3. metaphorically to practise  a thing, be versed  in it, (Plato Philosophus)
4. with accusative cognate, φροίμιον χορεύσομαι I will dance  a prelude (to festivities), (Aeschulus Tragicus); χ. γάμους to celebrate  them, (Euripides); ὄργια Μουσῶν (Aristophanes Comicus):—;Mid., χορεύεσθαι δίνας to ply the  eddying dance , (Euripides):—;Pass., κεχόρευται ἡμῖν (sings the Chorus) our part is played , (Aristophanes Comicus)
5. transitive to celebrate in choral dance , Ἴακχον (Sophocles Tragicus):—;Pass. to be celebrated in choral dance , (Aristophanes Comicus)
6. Causal, to set  one a dancing, to rouse, wake to the dance , τινά (Euripides); so, πόδα χορεύειν [variant datesAnthology Palantina (ML)

---

1. that which one needs must pay, an obligation, debt , (Odyssey by Homer); a debt for stolen cattle , (Iliad by Homer); χρεῖος ἀποστήσασθαι to pay a debt  in full, (Iliad by Homer); ἀρᾶς τίνει χρ. pays the debt demanded by  the curse, (Aeschulus Tragicus); χρέος πόλει προσάπτειν to attach a further debt , i.e. guilt  to the city, (Sophocles Tragicus); χρέος ἀποδιδόναι to repay a debt , (Herdotus Historicus):—;in plural debts , χρειῶν λύσις (Hesiod); τὴν οὐσίαν ἅπασαν χρέα κατέλιπε left all the property in outstanding debts , (Demosthenes Orator)
2. a needful business, an affair, matter , ἑὸν αὐτοῦ χρεῖος (Odyssey by Homer): a requirement, a purpose , (Sophocles Tragicus): with genitive, like χάριν, for the sake of , σὸν οὐκ ἔλασσον ἢ κείνης χρέος (Euripides)
3. like χρῆμα, a thing , τί χρέο; = τί χρῆμ; wherefore?  (Aeschulus Tragicus); ἐφ᾽ ὅ τι χρ. ἐμόλετ; (Euripides)
4. in (Odyssey by Homer), ἦλθον Τειρεσίαο κατὰ χρέος seems to be = Τειρεσίᾳ χρησόμενος, I came to consult  him:—;but, κατὰ χρέος according to what is due , as is meet , (Homeric Hymns)
5. a duty, task, charge, office , (Pindar) (ML)

LSJ / STEPBible (TFLSJ)
χρέος, τό
Epic dialect χρεῖος [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Homerus Epicus (who also uses χρέος, but only in 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey”, see below 1.1)]]: Attic dialect χρέως [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd c.AD: Phrynichus Atticista 370, Moeris p.403 P., 4th-5th c.AD: Choeroboscus Grammaticus “Scholia in Theodosii Canones” 1.360H.]] (and this form appears in codices of [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 25.69, 33.24, 38.14, 40.37, 42.5]]; but χρέος in [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Politicus” 267a, “Lg.” 958b)]]: genitive χρείους [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Iphigenia Aulidensis” 373 (troch., assuming variant), χρέους 5th c.BC: Lysias Orator 17.5 codices, χρέως 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 49.18 (and so Choerob.[same place])]]; no dative occurs in Epic dialect forms:—plural, nominative and accusative χρέᾰ [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th-7th c.BC: Hesiodus Epicus “Opera et Dies” 647, χρέᾱ 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Nubes” 39, 443 (_anapaest meter_), compare 5th-6th c.BC: Isocrates Orator 21.13, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Leges” 684e, etc.; 4th c.AD(?): Arcadius Grammaticus χρήατα (but “Schwyzer” [665] χρῆα τά) “IG” 5(2).343.20, 27 (Orchom., 4th c.BC)]]; genitive χρεῶν [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Nubes” 13, 117, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 566a, etc.]]; Epic dialect χρειῶν [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th-7th c.BC: Hesiodus Epicus “Opera et Dies” 404 (χρεέων conjecture Rzach)]]; Epic dialect dative χρέεσι [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [4th c.AD(?): Manetho Astrologus 4.135; χρήεσσι 3rd c.BC: Apollonius Rhodius Epicus 3.1198]]: (χράομαι, χρή):

__I
that which one needs must pay, obligation, debt, Ἄρης.. χρέος καὶ δεσμὸν ἀλύξας [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 8.353, compare 355]]; χρεῖος ἀποστήσασθαι, i.e. pay it in full, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 13.746]]: especially of the obligation to restore or pay for 'lified' cattle and plunder, so the heralds of the Pylians summoned to share in booty all οἷσι χρεῖος ὀφείλετ᾽·.. πολέσιν γὰρ Ἐπειοὶ χρεῖος ὄφειλον (where [Refs 8th c.BC+ [Scholia A, τὰ περιελασθέντα ἐκ τῆς Πύλου ὑπὸ τῶν Ἐπειῶν θρέμματα χρέως καλεῖ) 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 11.686, compare 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 3.367, 21.17]]; later simply, debt, αὐτὸς ἔτεισε.. χρέος [Refs 6th c.BC+ [6th c.BC: Theognis Elegiacus 205]]; ἀρᾶς τίνει χ. pays the debt demanded by the curse, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Agamemnon” 457 (Lyric poetry)]]; μή τι πέρα χρέος.. πόλει προσάψῃς debt, i. e. guilt, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Coloneus” 235 (Lyric poetry)]]; χ. πράσσειν τινά exact payment of a debt from one, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “O.” 3.7]]; ἐμὸν καταίσχυνε χ. dishonoured my debt, i.e. dishonoured me for not paying my debt, for not keeping my promise, [Refs [[prev. work] 10(11).8]]; τεὸν χ. the debt due to thee, [Refs [[prev. author] “P.” 8.33: in Comedy texts and Prose, χ. ἀποδιδόναι]] repay a debt, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 2.136 (where also we have χ. διδόναι]] to give a loan, and χ. λαμβάνειν to receive a loan),[Refs 5th c.BC+ [compare 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Nubes” 117, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Politicus” 267a]]; ἔχω χ. ὡς εἰπεῖν οὐδὲν ἀνδρὸς Ἕλληνος I know of nothing that 1 owe to any man of Greece, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 3.140; χ. ἀπαιτεῖν 1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus “Otho” 2; τὰ ὑπάρχοντα τῶν χ. ἀνεῖσθαι [prev. author] “Sol.” 15]]; τὸ ἐπὶ τὴν τράπεζαν χρέως (i.e. ὀφειλόμενον) [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 33.24]]; ὢ καλὸν εἰς ἄλοχον θέμενος χ., like{χάριν θέσθαι} (see. τίθημι [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus 11.7 near the end), epigram in “Arch.Papyrus” 1.220 (from Ptolemaic)]]; ἔχειν εἴς τι χ. [Refs 1st c.AD+ [1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus “Caesar” 48]]: plural, debts, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th-7th c.BC: Hesiodus Epicus “Opera et Dies” 647, 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Nubes” 13, etc.; χρειῶν λύσις 8th-7th c.BC: Hesiodus Epicus “Opera et Dies” 404; χρέα ἀπολαβεῖν 5th-6th c.BC: Andocides Orator 3.15; χρέα ἐπὶ τόκοις ὀφειλόμενα 4th c.BC: Isaeus Orator 11.42]]; τὴν οὐσίαν ἅπασαν χρέα κατέλιπον left all the property in outstanding debts, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 38.7; εἰσπραχθέντα χρέα [prev. passage]; ἐκπληρῶσαι τὸ χ. ἅπαν]] pay it, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Leges” 958b; τὸ χ. διαλυέτω “SIG” 306.46 (Tegea, 4th c.BC),compare 1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus “Lucullus” 20 (_passive_)]]; πρὸς τὰ χ. ἀπάγεσθαι [Refs 2nd c.BC+ [2nd c.BC: Polybius Historicus 38.11.10, 1st c.BC: Dionysius Halicarnassensis 4.9:]] —compare ἀποκοπή.

__I.2
metaphorically, the debt that all must pay, fate, death, οὐκ ἔστι τὸ χ. φυγεῖν [LXX+5th c.BC+ [4th c.AD: Alciphro Epistolographus 1.25; τὸ τῆς ψυχῆς ἀπαιτηθεὶς χ. LXX.Wis.15.8; also ἂν μή τις θᾶττον ὡς χ. ἀποδιδῷ τὸ ζην 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Axiochus” 367b]]; ὁπότε εἰς τὸν ἀέρα ἀναδράμῃ τὸ χ. (i.e. ἡ ψυχή, regarded as lent to the body) [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd c.AD: Vettius Valens Astrologus 330.33.]]

__II
in Poets, business, affair, matter, ἑὸν αὐτοῦ χρεῖος ἐελδόμενος [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 1.409, compare 2.45]]; χρέος πᾶν ἐπικραίνεις, of Pelasgos, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Supplices” 374 (Lyric poetry)]]; purpose, object, εἰ μὲν γὰρ ὑμῖν μὴ τόδ᾽ ἐκπράξω χρέος[Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. work] 472, compare 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Tyrannus” 156 (Lyric poetry); πᾶν ὃ θέλεις.. χ. ἐκτετέλεσται 3rd c.BC: Theocritus Poeta Bucolicus 25.53: with _genitive_, σὸν οὐκ ἔλασσον ἢ κείνης χ.]] your affair, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Hecuba” 892.]]

__II.2
almost ={χρῆμα}, thing, τί χρέο; ={τί χρῆμα}; [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Agamemnon” 85 (_anapaest meter_), 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Heraclidae” 95 (Lyric poetry), compare 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Coloneus” 251 (Lyric poetry); ἐφ᾽ ὅ τι χ. ἐμόλετε 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Orestes” 150 (lyr); τί χ. ἔβα δωμ; [prev. author] “fragment” 1011 (Lyric poetry); τί καινὸν ἦλθε δώμασιν χ.; [prev. author] “HF” 530, compare 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Nubes” 30]] (with play on signification[Refs 3rd c.BC+ [1), 3rd c.BC: Theocritus Poeta Bucolicus 24.66.]]

__II.3
ἐλάφους, μέγα τι χ. [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [compare (χρῆμα 11.3) 3rd c.BC: Callimachus Epicus “Hymnus in Dianam” 100.]]

__III
in [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 11.479, ἦλθον Τειρεσίαο κατὰ χρέος seems to be ={Τειρεσίᾳ χρησόμενος} (10.492)]] to consult him.

__III.2
elsewhere κατὰ χρέος means according to what is needful, in due fashion, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [“hymnus ad Mercurium” 138, 3rd c.BC: Apollonius Rhodius Epicus 3.189, 4th-3rd c.BC: Aratus Epicus 343.]]

__IV
duty, task, charge, office, ἦλθε τωὔτ᾽ ἐπὶ χρέος [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “O.” 1.45, compare 7.40; οἷς τόδ᾽ ἦν χρέος 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Persae” 777, compare “Th.” 20; τὸ σὸν μελέσθω.. φρουρῆσαι χρέος 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Electra” 74, compare 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Orestes” 1253 (Lyric poetry), “IT” 883 (Lyric poetry).]]

__V
τὸ συνδρῶν χ. the circumstance of being an accomplice, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Andromache” 337.]]

__VI
anything useful or serviceable, χρεῶν χρηΐζοντι μετάδοσιν ποιήσασθαι [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Hippocrates Medicus]]Jusj.; δέκα στατῆρανς καταστασεῖ, τῶ δὲ χρήϊος (={χρέους}) διπλεῖ ὄτι κ᾽ ὀ δικαστὰς ὀμόσει συνεσσάκσαι [Refs [“Leg.Gort.” 3.14, compare 11, “GDI” 5100.11 (from Malla).]]

__VI.2
value, validity, υηδὲν ἐς χρῆος (or χρέος) ἤμην τὰν δόσιν the gift shall be of no value, i. e. invalid, [Refs [“Leg.Gort.” 10.24, compare 31.]]

__VII
παρὰ χρέος, ={παραχρῆμα}, [Refs 2nd c.BC+ [Callias Epigrammaticus “Aet.Oxy.” 2080.14 (παραχρῆμ᾽ cited in 5th c.AD: Stobaeus, Joannes), 2nd c.BC: Nicander Epicus “Alexipharmaca” 614 (probably originally = signf. VIII).]]

__VIII
={χρεία, χρεώ}, need, τί δ᾽, ὦ τάλας, σε τοῦδ᾽ ἔχει πλέκους χρέο; Answ. χ. μὲν οὐδέν, βούλομαι δ᾽ ὅμως λαβεῖν [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Acharnenses” 454, compare 2nd c.BC: Bion Bucolicus “fragment” 2.2.]]

LSJ / STEPBible (TFLSJ)
χροιά,
Epic dialect and Ionic dialect χροιή, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 14.164, 6th c.BC: Theognis Elegiacus 1017 (in Callias Epigrammaticus “Lav. Pall.” 28 χροϊά (χροίην codices))]], Attic dialect χροιά and χρόα, the latter always in [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus (see. below), also in 1st c.BC: Philodemus Gadarensis Epigrammaticus “D.” 3.9, _sign._ 5, +others (see. χρώς)]]:—skin, especially of the human body, hence the body itself, παραδραθέειν φιλότητι ᾑ χροιῇ [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” [same place]; κατὰ χροιὴν ῥέει ἱδρώς 6th c.BC: Theognis Elegiacus [same place]; ὄζειν.. τῆς χρόας ἔφασκεν ἡδύ μου 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Plutus” 1020]]; τὰ ἐξανθεῦντα ἐς τὴν χροιὴν (skin, surface) ἢ χροιῇ (colour,[Refs 5th c.BC+ [signification 11) ἢ οἰδήμασι 5th c.BC: Hippocrates Medicus “περὶ τέχνης” 9: compare χρώς.]]

__2
metaphorically, 'skin', i.e. surface, Pythagorean term, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “de Sensu” 439a31, “Placita Philosophorum” 1.15.2, “Theologumena Arithmeticae” 18(_plural_); χ. ἐπίπεδος [prev. work]10; so perhaps in 4th-3rd c.BC: Epicurus Philosophus “Fragmenta” 81, 1st c.BC: Philodemus Philosophus “περὶ σημείων καὶ σημειώσεων” 5, +others]]

__3
appearance to the eye, of heavenly bodies, [Refs [[prev. author] “D.” 3.9.]]

__II
superficial appearance of a thing, its colour, [Refs 7th c.BC+ [6th c.BC: Theognis Elegiacus 451, 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Prometheus Vinctus” 493, 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Cyclops” 517 (Lyric poetry); παντοδάπαισι μεμειχμένα χροίαισιν 7th-6th c.BC: Sappho Lyrica 20, compare 2nd c.AD: Numenius Apamensis Platonicus cited in 2nd c.AD: Athenaeus Epigrammaticus 7.282a]]; τοιοῦτον (i.e. ἐρυθρόν) εἶναι τῇ χροιᾷ τὸ μέλι [Refs 5th c.BC+ [3rd c.AD: Porphyrius Tyrius Philosophus “de Antro Nympharum - Porphyrii Opuscula” 16; ἔστιν.. χρόα ἀπορροὴ σχημάτων ὄψει σύμμετρος καὶ αἰσθητός 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Meno” 76d; νόμῳ χροιή.. ἐτεῇ δ᾽ ἄτομα καὶ κενόν 3rd c.AD: Democritus Epigrammaticus 125, compare 5th c.BC: Anaxagoras Philosophus 4, 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “de Sensu” 440a8; ἐκ τριῶν τὰς χρόας ἅπασας μεμεγμένας, τοῦ φωτός, καὶ δι᾽ ὧν φαίνεται τὸ φῶς, καὶ τῶν ὑποκειμένων χρωμάτων [prev. author] “Col.” 793b33.]]

__II.2
especially colour of the skin, complexion, χροιῆς ἄνθος ἀμειβομένης [Refs 6th c.BC+ [6th c.BC: Solon Lyricus 27.6; χροιᾶς ἀμείψεις ἄνθος 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Prometheus Vinctus” 23; χροιὰν ἀλλάξασα 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Medea” 1168; λευκὴν χ. ἐκ παρασκευῆς ἔχεις [prev. author] “Ba.” 457, compare 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Nubes” 1012 (_anapaest meter_)]]; χρόᾳ ἀδήλῳ τῶν δεδραμένων πέρι with colour that gives no hint of what has passed, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Orestes” 1318]]; χρόαν.. τὴν σὴν ἥλιος.. αἰγυπτιώσει[Refs 5th c.BC+ [Pl.Com(?). p.615K. (post “fragment” 55); χρόας κάλλος 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Symposium” 196a; ἐρίζοι καὶ γάλακι χροιήν 3rd c.BC: Callimachus Epicus “Hecale” 1.4.3.]]

__III
in Music, nuance of a scale, [Refs 1st c.AD+ [1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus 2.1143e.—On the accent, see Hdn.Gr.1.301, +others]]

4. generally, bare, uncovered , ψιλὸν ὡς ὁρᾷ νέκυν (Sophocles Tragicus):—;with genitive bare of, separated from , ψιλὴ σώματος οὖσα [ ἡ ψυχή] (Plato Philosophus) b. bare, stript of appendages , ψιλὴ τρόπις the bare  keel with the planks torn from it, (Odyssey by Homer); ψ. θρίδαξ a lettuce with the side-leaves pulled off , (Herdotus Historicus); ψ. μάχαιραι swords without other arms , (Xenophon Historicus)
5. οἱ ψιλοί (i.e. τῶν ὅπλων); soldiers without heavy armour, light troops , such as archers and slingers, opposite to ὁπλῖται, (Herdotus Historicus), etc.; τὸ ψιλόν, opposite to τὸ ὁπλιτικόν, (Xenophon Historicus); ψ. ἔχων τὴν κεφαλήν bare-headed, without helmet , (Xenophon Historicus)
6. ψιλὸς λόγος bare  language, i. e. prose , as opposite to poetry which is clothed in metre, (Plato Philosophus); also, ψ. λόγος is a mere  speech, a speech unsupported by evidence , (Demosthenes Orator)
7. ψιλὴ ποίησις mere  poetry, without music , i. e. epic  poetry, as opposite to lyric , (Plato Philosophus):—;but, ψιλὴ μουσική instrumental  music unaccompanied by the voice , (Aristotle Philosopher)
8. Oedipus seems to call Antigone his ψιλὸν ὄμμα, as being the one poor  eye left him, (Sophocles Tragicus)
9. adverb ψιλῶς, merely, only , (Plutarch) (ML)

1. to thrust, push, shove, force onwards  or away , λᾶαν ἄνω ὤθεσκε he kept pushing  it upwards, (Odyssey by Homer); ἀπ᾽ ὀφθαλμῶν νέφος ὦσεν Ἀθήνη (Iliad by Homer); ἐκ μηροῦ δόρυ ὦσε he forced  the spear from the thigh, (Iliad by Homer); ὦσαί τινα ἀφ᾽ ἵππων (Iliad by Homer); ὦσαι ἑαυτὸν ἐς τὸ πῦρ to rush  into the fire, (Herdotus Historicus); so, ὠθ. τινὰ ἐπὶ κεφαλήν to throw  him headlong down, (Plato Philosophus); κατὰ πετρῶν (Euripides); ὦσαι τὴν θύραν to force  the door, (Aristophanes Comicus)
2. to push  or force back  in battle, (Iliad by Homer)
3. to thrust out, banish , [variant datesTragica Adespota; ὦσαί τινα φυγάδα (Plato Philosophus); ὠθ. τινα ἄθαπτον (Sophocles Tragicus)
4. metaphorically, ὠθ. τὰ πρήγματα to push  matters on, hurry  them, (Herdotus Historicus)
5. absolute, ὦσα παρέξ pushed off  from land, (Odyssey by Homer); ὤθει βιαίως (Euripides)
6. Mid., mostly in aor1, to thrust  or push from oneself, push  or force back, repulse , especially in battle, τείχεος ἂψ ὤσασθαι (Iliad by Homer); ὤσασθαι προτὶ Ἴλιον, προτὶ ἄστυ (Iliad by Homer); ὤσασθαι τὴν ἵππον (Herdotus Historicus); ὠσαμένων τὸ κέρας (Thucydides)
7. Pass. to be thrust on, to fall violently , ἐπὶ κεφαλήν (Herdotus Historicus); πρὸς βίαν (Euripides)
8. to force one's way , (Xenophon Historicus): to crowd on, throng , like ὠστίζομαι, (Xenophon Historicus) (ML)

LSJ / STEPBible (TFLSJ)
ὠθ-έω,
Attic dialect imperfect ἐώθουν [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Pax” 637 (troch.), 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 9.65, (ἐξ-) 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 7.52, etc., and ἐώθει even in “hymnus ad Mercurium” 305]]; Ionic dialect and Epic dialect 3rd.pers. singular ὤθει [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 21.241]]; Ionic dialect ὤθεσκε [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 11.596: but ὤθει 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Iphigenia Taurica” 1395 is _falsa lectio_ for{ὠθεῖ} (from Kirchhoff)]]: future ὠθήσω [Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. author] “Cyc.” 592, 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Ecclesiazusae” 300 (Lyric poetry), (ἐξ-) 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Ajax” 1248; but ὤσω 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Medea” 379, “Andr.” 344]], and always in Prose; ἀπ-ώσω [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 15.280]], Epic dialect infinitive ἀπ-ωσέμεν [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 13.367]]: Attic dialect aorist ἔωσα [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Timaeus” 60c, etc., (ἐξ-) 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Coloneus” 1296, 1330, etc.]]; Ionic dialect and Epic dialect ὦσα [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 1.220, 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 7.167]], Epic dialect ὤσασκε [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 11.599; but ἔωσα 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 16.410, (ἀπ-) 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 9.81; later ὤθησα 2nd-3rd c.AD: Aelianus “De Natura Animalium - Ar.Byzantine Epit.” 13.17, etc.:]]perfect ἔωκα (ἐξ-) [Refs 1st c.AD+ [1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus 2.48c:]]pluperfect ἐώκει (ἐξ-) [Refs [[prev. author] “Brut.” 42]]:—middle, future ὤσομαι (ἀπ-) [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Electra” 944, etc., (δι-) 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Fragmenta - American Journal of Philology” 199.9, etc.]]:—Attic dialect aorist ἐωσάυην [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 4.43, 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Vespae” 1085 (troch., with variants)]]; Ionic dialect and Epic dialect ὠσάμην [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 16.592, 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 9.25, variant in 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “V.”]][same place]:—passive, future ὠσθήσομαι [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Medea” 335 (variant{ὠθήσομαι}), (ἐξ-) 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 24.61: _Attic dialect_]]aorist ἐώσθην (ἐξ-) [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Historia Graeca (Hellenica)” 2.4.34, etc.]]; later ὤσθην (ἐξ-) [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd c.AD: Arrianus Historicus “Anabasis” 4.25.3, 3rd c.AD: Plotinus Philosophus 4.4.45]]: Attic dialect perfect ἔωσμαι [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 7.1.36]], (ἀπ-, περι-) [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 2.39, 3.57]]; Ionic dialect participle ἀπωσμένος [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 5.69]]:— thrust, push,

__I
mostly of human force, as of Sisyphus, σκηριπτόμενος χερσίν τε ποσίν τε λᾶαν ἄνω ὤθεσκε ποτὶ λόφον he kept pushing it.., [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 11.596, compare 599; ἀπὸ εἷο τράπεζαν ὦσε ποδὶ πλήξας 22.20]]; [ἔγχος] ὑπὲκ δίφροιο pushed it away from.., [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 5.854; ἂψ ἐς κουλεὸν ὦσε ξίφος 1.220; τοῖσι δ᾽ ἀπ᾽ ὀφθαλμῶν νέφος ἀχλύος ὦσεν Ἀθήνη 15.668; τὸν δε᾽ Ζεὺς ὦσεν ὄπισθε χειρί [prev. work] 694, compare 13.193; ὦσαί [τινα] ἀφ᾽ ἵππων 5.19; ἀφ᾽ ἵππων χαμᾶζε [prev. work] 835, etc.]]; so ὦσαι ἑωυτὸν ἐς τὸ πῦρ rush into the fire, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 7.167]]; ὠ. τινα ἐπὶ κεφαλήν throw him headlong down, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 553b]] (passive, ὠθέεσθαι ἐπὶ κ. [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 7.136); ὠ. τινα ἐπὶ τράχηλον 2nd c.AD: Lucianus Sophista “DMort.” 27.1; πετρῶν ὦσαι κάτω 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Cyclops” 448, compare 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Phaedrus” 229c; εἰς λιθοτομίας 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 53.17: frequently of weapons, ὠ. ξίφος δἰ ἀμφοτέρων]] thrust it through both, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 3.78; τεκούσης ἐς σφαγὰς ὦσαι ξίφος 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Orestes” 291; διὰ μέσου αὐχένος ὠθεῖ σίδηρον [prev. author] “Ph.” 1458; φάσγανον δἰ ἥπατος [prev. author] “Med.” 379; ξίφος πρὸς ἧπαρ [prev. author] “Hel.” 983; δαλοῦ κώπην ἔσω βλεφάρων [prev. author] “Cyc.” 485 (_anapaest meter_), compare 636]]; ἐκ μηροῦ δόρυ ὦσε θύραζε forced it out from the thigh, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 5.694]]; τὸ ἱμάτιον ὦσαι εἰς τὸ στόμα stuff it into his mouth, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-3rd c.BC: Theophrastus Philosophus “Characteres” 2.4: τὴν θύραν ὠθεῖ]] forces the door, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Vespae” 152, compare 5th c.BC: Lysias Orator 1.24; πύλας 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Orestes” 1562]]: sometimes of other than human force, as of a stream, ὦσε δὲ νεκρούς [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 21.235, compare 241]]; of the wind, Νότος μέγα κῡμα ποτὶ.. ῥίον ὠθεῖ [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 3.295]]; [ὁ ποταμὸς] ὠθεῖ κῦμα Metagen.[Refs 7th c.BC+ [6.3; ὠ. κολόκυμα 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Equites” 692: _metaphorically_, ἀ δ᾽ ἀτέρα τὰν ἀτέραν κύλιξ ὠθήτω 7th-6th c.BC: Alcaeus Lyricus 41.]]

__I.2
force back in battle, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 8.336, 13.193, etc.; ἄνδρας προτὶ ἄστυ 16.45; see below 11.]]

__I.3
thrust out, banish, ὠ. ἅπαντας τὸν ἀσεβῆ [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Tyrannus” 1382; ἔξω δόμων τε καὶ πάτρας ὠθεῖν τινα 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Prometheus Vinctus” 665; ἀπ᾽ οἴκων 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Tyrannus” 241; ἐκ δόμων 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Andromache” 344; ἔξω τινὰ φυγάδα 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 560d]]; σπονδῶν ἄπο, ἀπὸ τῶν ἱερῶν, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Bacchae” 46, 4th c.BC: Aeschines Orator 2.86; ὠ. τινας ἀθάπτους 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Ajax” 1307]]:—passive, ὠθούμεθ᾽ ἔξω [Refs [[prev. author] “fragment” 583.7.]]

__I.4
metaphorically, ὠ. τὰ πρήγματα push matters on, hurry them, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 3.81; ἐπιθυμία ὠθεῖ ἐπὶ τὰς ἀπολαύσεις 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “de Virtutibus et Vitiis” 1250a24.]]

__I.5
absolutely, ὦσα παρέξ pushed off from land, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 9.488; ὤθει βιαίως 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Troades” 356, compare 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Historia Graeca (Hellenica)” 7.4.31]]; τὸ ὠθοῦν the motive power, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Cratylus” 401d.]]

__II
middle, mostly in aorist, thrust or push away from oneself, force back, especially in battle, frequently in [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad”, ὄφρα τάχιστα ὤσαιτ᾽ Ἀργείους 5.691; τείχεος ἂψ ὤσασθαι 12.420; ὤσασθαι προτὶ Ἴλιον, προτὶ ἄστυ, 8.295, 16.655; τὴν ἵππον ὤσαντο 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 9.25, compare 3.72, 6.37; ὤσασθαί τινας κατὰ βραχύ 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 4.96; ὠσαμένων τὸ εὐώνυμον κέρας [prev. author] 6.70, etc.]]; once in Trag., [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Iphigenia Taurica” 326]]: of a horse, throw its rider, [Refs 6th c.BC+ [6th c.BC: Theognis Elegiacus 260 (assuming variant).]]

__II.2
intransitive, push, press forward, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 4.11, 35, 1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus “Agesilaus” 32; ὠθεῖσθαι εἰς τὸ πρόσθεν 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Historia Graeca (Hellenica)” 7.1.31; πρὸς τὴν πληγὴν ὁμόσε ὠθεῖσθαι 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Euthydemus” 294d; εἰς χεῖρας ὠθεῖσθαι τοῖς ἐναντίοις 1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus “Theseus” 5.]]

__III
passive, to be thrust, pushed, or forced, rush or fall violently, ἐπὶ κεφαλήν [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus (see. above 1.1); πρὸς βίαν 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Hecuba” 406; βιᾳ [prev. author] “Med.” 335, etc.; ἱδρῶτες ταχέως ὠθούμενοι 5th c.BC: Hippocrates Medicus “ἀφορισμοί” 7.85.]]

__III.2
middle, crowd, throng, jostle, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 3.3.64; ὠ. ὥσπερ ὕες 3rd c.BC: Theocritus Poeta Bucolicus 15.73, compare 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Historia Animalium” 572b25: _impersonal_ in]]passive, ἐπὶ μέζον ὠθεῖται the crush gets worse, [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [3rd c.BC: Herodas Mimographus 4.54.]]
