LSJ / STEPBible (TFLSJ)
ὠμός, ή, όν:
(see. entry near the end):— raw, crude compare ([Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Meteorologica” 380b5):]]

__I
properly of flesh, raw, uncooked, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 22.347, +others]]; opposed to ὀπταλέος, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 12.396]]; ὠμὸν καταφαγεῖν τινα or ὠμοῦ ἐσθίειν τινός to eat one raw, proverbial of savage cruelty, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 4.8.14, “HG” 3.3.6; so ὠμὸν βεβρώθοις Πρίαμον 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 4.35, compare 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 18.87, etc.]]

__I.2
of eggs, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-3rd c.BC: Theophrastus Philosophus “de Vertigine” 2]]; of vegetables, μύκητας ὠμοὺς.. φαγεῖν [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Antiphanes Comicus 188; κριθαί 2nd c.AD: Lucianus Sophista “Asin.” 17]]; compare ὠμήλυσις.

__I.3
of water, crude, opposed to ἄπεφθος, [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd c.AD: Alexander Rhetor 198]]; also of milk, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Meteorologica” 380b8.]]

__I.4
of fruit, uncooked by the sun, unripe, opposed to πέπων, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Equites” 260 (troch.), compare 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Oeconomicus” 19.19 (_comparative_), 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Meteorologica” 380b7.]]

__I.5
of pitch, opposed to ἑφθή, [Refs 2nd c.BC+ [“Geoponica” 6.5.5, compare 2nd c.BC: Polybius Historicus 5.89.6]]; of pottery, unbaked, χύτραι [Refs 4th c.BC+ [1st c.AD: Dioscorides (Dioscurides) Medicus 1.68, “Geoponica” 10.21.1; κέραμος ὠμός 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Meteorologica” 380b8, compare “GA” 743a9]]: even of soil which needs to be exposed to the sun, ὡς ἡ ὠμὴ αὐτῆς ὀπτῷτο [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Oeconomicus” 16.15.]]

__I.6
of food, undigested, [Refs 1st c.AD+ [1st c.AD: Anonymus Londinensis 25.7, +others, 1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus 2.131c, 133d]]; of a person, suffering from indigestion, [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd-3rd c.AD: Philostratus Sophista “de gymnastica” 54]]; also οὖρα, ὑποχωρήσεις, κατάρροι, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Meteorologica” 380b5.]]

__II
metaphorically, savage, fierce, cruel, [δεσπόται] ὠμοί τε δούλοις [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Agamemnon” 1045; ὠ. φρόνημα [prev. author] “Th.” 536; ὠμῇ ξὺν ὀργῇ [prev. author] “Supp.” 187; δαίμων 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Tyrannus” 828; τὰ.. Ἀγαμέμνονος κλύεις ὠμὰ καὶ πάντολμ᾽ 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Iphigenia Aulidensis” 913 (troch.); ὠμὸς ἔς τινα [prev. author] “Hipp.” 1264]]; and so in Prose, ὠμὸν τὸ βούλευμα.. ἐγνῶσθαι [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 3.36]]; οὕτως ὠμὴ [ἡ] στάσις προὐχώρησε [Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. work] 82; θηρευταὶ ὠμοὶ καὶ ἄνομοι 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Leges” 823e]]; ὠμὴ ψυχή [Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. work] 718d; χαλεπὸς καὶ ὠ. 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 2.6.12; τὸν οὕτως ὠμόν, τὸν οὕτως ἀγνώμονα 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 21.97]]; ὠμοὶ χρόνοι hard times, [Refs [“IG” 3.1372 (metrically)]]. adverb, ὠμῶς καὶ ἀπαραιτήτως [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 3. [84], compare 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “de Vectigalibus” 5.6; ὠ. καὶ σχετλίως ἔχειν 5th-6th c.BC: Isocrates Orator 19.31; ὠ. καὶ πικρῶς 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 29.2; ὠ. ἀποκτείνειν 5th c.BC: Lysias Orator 13.63 codices ὁμοίως Lipsius)]]: superlative, ὠμότατα διακεῖσθαι πρός τινα [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Isocrates Orator 9.49.]]

__II.2
harsh, rough, cruel, νόμοι [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Ajax” 548; δηλοῖ τὸ γέννημ᾽ ὠμὸν ἐξ ὠμοῦ πατρός [prev. author] “Ant.” 471]]; πῶς ἂν ὠμότερος συκοφάντης γενοιτ; a more coarse, more unmitigated sycophant, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 18.212.]] adverb ὠμῶς rudely, coarsely, παρελθεῖν ὠ. καὶ ἀναιδῶς [Refs [[prev. work] 285.]]

__II.3
(from [Refs [1.4) ὠμὸν γῆρας an]]unripe, premature old age, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 15.357, 8th-7th c.BC: Hesiodus Epicus “Opera et Dies” 705 (but ὠμότατον καὶ ἀγριώτατον γῆρας]] in signification [Refs 1st c.AD+ [11.1, 1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus “Marius” 2), compare ὠμογέρων: ὠμὸς τόκος]] an untimely birth, [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd-3rd c.AD: Philostratus Sophista “Vitae Sophistarum” 2.1.8]]. (Cf. Sanskrit āmás 'raw, uncooked'.)

Summary:

__A
as adverb of Manner.

__A.Aa
ὧς and ὥς (with accent), so, thus.

__A.Ab
ὡς (without accent) of the Relat. pronoun ὅς, as.

__A.Ac
ὡς Relat. and Interrog., how.

__A.Ad
ὡς temporal, when.

__A.Ae
ὡς Local, where,

__B
ὡς, as CONJUNCTION.

__C,D
various usages. adverb of Manner:

__A.Aa
ὥς, Demonstr., ={οὕτως}, so, thus, frequently in [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Homerus Epicus, 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 1.33, +others; ὢς εἶπ᾽ 7th-6th c.BC: Sappho Lyrica “Papyrus fragments” in E. Diehl, 20 a. 11 (Epic style)]]; in Ionic dialect Prose, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 3.13, +others; rare in _Attic dialect_, and almost confined to certain phrases, see below 2, 3]]; ὥς simply ={οὕτως}, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Agamemnon” 930, 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 3.37, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Protagoras” 338a; ἀλλ᾽ ὣς γενέσθω 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Hecuba” 888, +others]]

__A.2
καὶ ὧς even so, nevertheless, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 1.116, +others]]; οὐδ᾽ ὧς not even so, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [7.263, 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 1.6, +others, 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 6.76; οὐδέ κεν ὧς 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 9.386: the phrases καὶ ὧς, οὐδ᾽ ὧς, μηδ᾽ ὧς,]] are used in Trag. and Attic dialect, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Antigone” 1042, 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 1.74, 7.74; also later, “PCair.Zen.” 19.10 (3rd c.BC, unaccented), “UPZ” 146.40 (2nd c.BC), “GDI” 1832.11 (Delph., 2nd c.BC), “IG” 22.850.17 (3rd c.BC)]]; κἂν ὧς, εἴπερ μέλει σοι, ἀπόστειλόν μοί τινα [Refs 4th c.AD+ [“POxy.” 120.11 (4th c.AD)]]; δουλεύων καθὼς καὶ ὧς [Refs 2nd c.BC+ [“GDI” 2160 (Delph., 2nd c.BC)]]; Thess. καὶ οὗς [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [“IG” 9(2).234.1 (3rd c.BC)]]; for this phrase the accentuation ὧς[Refs 2nd c.AD+ [is prescribed by Hdn.Gr.2.932, +others,compare 2nd c.AD: Apollonius Dyscolus Grammaticus “de Syntaxi”; 307.16, and is found in good Mss. of Homer; for the remaining uses under this head (Aa. 1, 3, 4) the accentuation ὥς is prescribed by the same grammarians.]]

__A.3
in Comparisons, ὥς.., ὡς.., so.. as.., etc.; and reversely ὡς.., ὣς.., as.. so, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 1.512, 14.265, etc.]]; in Attic dialect, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 530d]]; also ὥς τε.. ὣς.., as.. thus.., [Refs 5th c.BC+ [“hymnus ad Cererem” 174 - 6, 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Bacchae” 1066 - 8; οἷα.. ὥς [prev. author] “El.” 151 - 5]]; ὥσπερ.., ὣς δὲ.. (in apodosi) [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Protagoras” 326d.]]

__A.4
thus, for instance, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 5.129, “hymnus ad Venerem” 218]]; ὥς should be accented in [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 5.121, 125.]]

__A.4.Ab
ὡς, Relat., as, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Homerus Epicus, etc.]]; properly relative to a demonstrative adverb, which is frequently omitted, κινήθη δ᾽ ἀγορὴ ὡς κύματα μακρὰ θαλάσσης, i. e. οὕτως, ὡς.., [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 2.144 (φὴ 4th-3rd c.BC: Zenodotus Grammaticus): it is _relative_ not only to the regular _demonstrative_ Advs. ὥς (ὧς), τώς, ὧδε, οὕτως, αὕτως, but also to ταύτῃ, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 365d, etc. We find a collateral _Doric dialect_ form ὥ (which see)]]; compare ὥτε. Usage:

__A.I
in similes, frequently in [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Homerus Epicus, 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 5.161, +others]]; longer similes are commonly introduced by ὡς ὅτε, ὡς δ᾽ ὅτε, ἤριπε δ᾽, ὡς ὅτε πύργος [ἤριπε] [Refs [4.462: ἤριπε δ᾽, ὡς ὅτε τις δρῦς ἤριπε 13.389, compare 2.394]]; so later, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Empedocles Poeta Philosophus 84.1, etc.; ὡς ὅτε θαητὸν μέγαρον, πάξομεν 5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “O.” 6.2: ὡς ὅτε]] is rare in short similes, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 11.368: ὡς]] is followed by indicative present, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 9.4, 16.364: also by]]aorist, [Refs [3.33f, 4.275, 16.823, +others]]; also by subjunctive present or aorist, [Refs [5.161, 10.183, 485, 13.334]] (sometimes ὡς δ᾽ ὅτ᾽ ἄν, [Refs [11.269, 17.520)]]; compare ὥστε A:—the Verb is sometimes omitted with ὡς, but may be supplied from the context, ἐνδούπησε πεσοῦσ᾽, ὡς εἰναλίη κήξ (i.e. πίπτει) [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 15.479, compare 6.20; θεὸς δ᾽ ὣς τίετο δήμῳ 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 5.78; οἱ δὲ φέβοντο.., βόες ὣς ἀγελαῖαι 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 22.299: where ὡς]] follows the noun to which it refers, it takes the accent; so in Comedy texts, Ἀριστόδημος ὥς [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Cratinus Comicus 151, compare 4th c.BC: Eubulus Comicus 75.6]]; see infr. H.

__A.I.2
like as, just as, ὡς οὗτος κατὰ τέκν᾽ ἔφαγε.., ὣς ἡμεῖς κτλ. [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 2.326, see supr. Aa. 3.]]

__A.I.3
sometimes in the sense as much as or according as, ἑλὼν κρέας ὥς (i. e. ὅσον) οἱ χεῖρες ἐχάνδανον [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 17.344]]; ὦκα δὲ μητρὶ ἔννεπον ὡς (i. e. ὅσα) εἶδόν τε καὶ ἔκλυον [Refs 8th c.BC+ [“hymnus ad Cererem” 172; τῶν πάντων οὐ τόσσον ὀδύρομαι.. ὡς ἑνός 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 4.105; τόσον.. ὡς 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 4.130]]; so in Trag., σοὶ θεοὶ πόροιεν ὡς ἐγὼ θέλω [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Coloneus” 1124; ὡς ἐγὼ οὐκ ἔστιν ὑμῶν ὅστις ἐξ ἴσου νοσεῖ [prev. author] “OT” 60]]; in Prose, ὡς δύναται as much as he can, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [3rd c.AD: Democritus Epigrammaticus 278; τὸ ῥῆμα μέμνημαι ὡς εἶπε 4th c.BC: Aeschines Orator 3.72]]; ὡς μή ={ὅσον μή, νέμεν ὅτι ἃν} (={ἂν}) βόλητοι ὡς μὴ ἰν τοῖ περιχώροι [Refs 4th c.BC+ [“IG” 5(2).3.9 (Tegea, 4th c.BC)]]; cf. Ab. 11.2 below

__A.I.4
sometimes after comparative, compared with, hence than, μᾶλλον πρέπει οὕτως ὡς.. [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Apologia” 36d; ἅ γε μείζω πόνον παρέχει.. οὐκ ἂν ῥᾳδίως οὐδὲ πολλὰ ἂν εὕροις ὡς τοῦτο [prev. author] “R.” 526c]]; οὐδενὸς μᾶλλον φροντίζειν ὡς.. [Refs 2nd c.BC+ [2nd c.BC: Polybius Historicus 3.12.5, compare 7.4.5, 11.2.9, 1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus “Coriolanus” 36: μᾶσσον ὡς]] is uncertain in [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Prometheus Vinctus” 629]], and [ἢ] should perhaps be inserted in [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Lysias Orator 7.12,31]]; compare ὥσπερ IV.

__A.II
with Adverbial clauses:

__A.II.1
parenthetically, in qualifying clauses, ὡς ἔοικε, etc., [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Symposium” 176c, etc.]]: in these cases γε or γοῦν is frequently added, ὡς γοῦν ὁ λόγος σημαίνει as at any rate the argument shows, [Refs [[prev. author] “R.” 334a]]; in some phrases with infinitive, see below [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Bacchylides Lyricus 11.3. An anacoluthon sometimes occurs by the Verb of the principal clause being made dependent on the parenthetic Verb, ὡς δὲ Σκύθαι λέγουσι, νεώτατον ἁπάντων ἐθνέων εἶναι (for ἦν)]] τὸ σφέτερον [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 4.5, compare 1.65; ὡς ἐγὼ ἤκουσα, εἶναι αὐτόν [prev. author] 4.76]]; ὡς γὰρ.. ἤκουσά τινος, ὅτι.. [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 6.4.18 codices]]; ἁνὴρ ὅδ᾽ ὡς ἔοικεν οὐ νεμεῖν (for οὐ νεμεῖ, ὡς ἔοικε), [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Trachiniae” 1238.]]

__A.II.2
in elliptical phrases, so far as.. (compare supr. Ab.[Refs 5th c.BC+ [1.3) ὡς ἐμοί [prev. author] “Aj.” 395 (Lyric poetry); so ὥς γε ἐμοὶ κριτῇ 2nd-3rd c.AD: Aelianus “Varia Historia” 2.41 and ὥς γ᾽ ἐμοὶ χρῆσθαι κριτῇ 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Alcestis” 801; ὡς ἐμῇ δόξῃ 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “de Vectigalibus” 5.2]]; ὡς ἀπ᾽ ὀμμάτων (i.e. εἰκάσαι) to judge by eyesight, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Coloneus” 15]]: especially in such phrases as οὐκέτι πολλὸν χωρίον, ὡς εἶναι Αἰγύπτου [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 2.8]]; οὐδὲ ἀδύνατος, ὡς Αακεδαιμόνιος for a Lacedaemonian, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 4.84, compare 1st c.BC: Dionysius Halicarnassensis 10.31; ὡς ἀνθρώποις 5th c.BC: Alcmaeon Philosophus 1]]; φρονεῖ.. ὡς γυνὴ μέγα for a woman, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Tyrannus” 1078]]; πιστός, ὡς νομεύς, ἀνήρ [Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. work] 1118; μακρὰν ὡς γέροντι.. ὁδόν [prev. author] “OC” 20, compare 385, “Ant.” 62, etc.; ὡπλισμένοι ὡς ἐν τοῖς ὄρεσιν ἱκανῶς 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 4.3.31; also with ἄν μεγάλα ἐκτήσατο χρήματα, ὡς ἂν εἶναι Ῥοδῶπιν 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 2.135 codices (ἂν secl. Krüger, Ῥοδώπιος conjecture Valck.)]]:—for ὡς εἰπεῖν and the like, see below [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Bacchylides Lyricus 11.3.]]

__A.II.3
ὡς attached to the object of the Verb, as, ἑωυτὸν ὡς ἐχθρὸν λυπέει [Refs 5th c.BC+ [3rd c.AD: Democritus Epigrammaticus 88; ἔλαβεν ἀμφοτέρους ὡς φίλους ἤδη 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 3.2.25; ἐν οἰκήματι ᾧ ὡς ταμιείῳ ἐχρῆτο 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Protagoras” 315d]].— For the similar usage of ὡς with Participles and Prepositions, see below with

__A.III
with Adverbs:

__A.III.a
with the Posit., ὡς ἀληθῶς truly, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Phaedrus” 234e (compare ἀληθής 111.1b: as if _adverb_ of τὸ ἀληθές)]]; ὡς ἑτέρως in the other way, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [[prev. work] 276c, 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 18.212]] (adverb of ὁ ἕτερο; see at {ἕτερος} see 2) (see. below [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 1.1)]]; ὡς ἠπίως, ὡς ἐτητύμως, [LXX+5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Electra” 1438 (Lyric poetry), 1452; ὡς ὁμοίως “SIG” 708.34 (Istropolis, 2nd c.BC), LXX.4Mac.5.21, 1 “Enoch” 5.3, “IG” 7.2725.16 (Acraeph., 2nd c.AD)]]; ὡς ἐναλλάξ [Refs 4th c.BC+ [2nd c.AD: Vettius Valens Astrologus 215.9, 340.2; ὡς παντελῶς [prev. author] 184.26; ὡς ἄλλως 4th c.BC: Isaeus Orator 7.27, 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 6.32; ὡς ἐνδεχομένως “PPetr.” 2p.53 (3rd c.BC)]]; in ὣς αὔτως (see. ὡσαύτως) we have the adverb of ὁ αὐτός, but the ὥς retains its demonstrative force, as does ὁ in Homer; ὡς ἀληθῶς, ὡς ὁμοίως, and ὡς παντελῶς may be modelled on ὣς αὔτως, with which they are nearly synonymous; so also ὡς ἑτέρως and ὡς ἐναλλάξ, which are contrasted with it.

__A.III.b
with adverbs expressing anything extraordinary, θαυμαστῶς or θαυμασίως ὡς, ὑπερφυῶς ὡς, (see entry); ὡς is sometimes separated by several words from its adverb, as θαυμαστῶς μοι εἶπες ὡς παρα᾽ δόξαν [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Phaedo” 95a; ὑπερφυῶς δὴ τὸ χρῆμα ὡς δύσγνωστον φαίνεται [prev. author] Alcaeus2.147c, compare “Phd.” 99d.]]

__A.III.c
with the superlative, as much as can be, ὡς μάλιστα [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 1.141, etc.: ὡς ῥᾷστα]] as easily as possible, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Prometheus Vinctus” 104; ὡς πλεῖστα 3rd c.AD: Democritus Epigrammaticus 189]]; ὠς τάχιστα as quickly as possible, [Refs 7th c.BC+ [7th-6th c.BC: Alcaeus Lyricus “Supp.” 4.15, etc.; more fully expressed, ὡς δυνατὸν ἄριστα 5th-6th c.BC: Isocrates Orator 12.153; ὡς ἐδύναντο ἀδηλότατα 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 7.50; μαχομένους ὡς ἂν δυνώμεθα κράτιστα 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 3.2.6; ὡς οἷόν τε βελτιστον 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 403d]]; ὡς ἀνυστὸν κάλλιστα Diog.[Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd c.AD: Apollonius Biographus 3: ὡς and ὅτι]] are sometimes found together, where one is superfluous, ὡς ὅτι μάλιστα [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Leges” 908a; βοῦν ὡς ὅτι κάλλιστον “IG” 22.1028.17 (2nd-1st c.BC)]]; see infr. G.

__A.III.d
with comparative, ὡς θᾶσσον [Refs 2nd c.BC+ [2nd c.BC: Polybius Historicus 1.66.1, 3.82.1.]]

__A.III.e
in the phrases ὡς τὸ πολύ, ὡς ἐπὶ τὸ πολύ, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 330c, 377b]]; ὡς ἐπὶ τὸ πλεῖον for the more part, commonly, ὡς ἐπὶ πλεῖστον [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 2.34]]; ὡς ἐπὶ τὸ πλῆθος, ὡς πλήθει, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 364a, 389d; ὡς τὸ ἐπίπαν 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 7.50, etc.; ὡς τὰ πολλά 2nd-3rd c.AD: Aelianus “De Natura Animalium - Ar.Byzantine Epit.” 12.17.]]

__A.III.2
with adjectives,

__A.III.2.a
Posit., ὑπερφυεῖ τινι.. ὡς μεγάλῃ βλάβῃ [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Gorgias” 477d.]]

__A.III.2.b
with superlative, ὡς ἄριστοι τὰς φύσεις [Refs [[prev. author] “Ti.” 18d; ὅπως ὡς βέλτισται ἔσονται [prev. author] “Grg.” 503a; ὡς ὅτι βέλτιστον [prev. author] “Smp.” 218d.]]

__A.III.2.c
separated from the adjective by a preposition, ὡς ἐς ἐλάχιστον [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 1.63, compare 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 18.246; ὡς ἐν βραχυτάτοις 5th c.BC: Antipho Orator 1.18; ὡς ἐν ἐχυρωτάτῳ ποιεῖσθαι 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 1.6.26, etc.]]

__A.III.2.Ac
Relat. and Interrog., how, μερμήριζε.. ὡς Ἀχιλῆα τιμήσειε [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 2.3, compare 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 365a; ἐβουλεύοντο ὡς.. στήσονται 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 3.84, etc.; οἷα δεῖ λέγειν καὶ ὥς 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Ethica Nicomachea” 1128a1]]; ὡς πέπραται how, i. e. at what price the goods have been sold, [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [“PCair.Zen.” 149 (3rd c.BC)]]; so οὐκ ἔσθ᾽ ὡς.. (for the more usually ὅπως) nowise can it be that.., [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Antigone” 750]]; οὐκ ἔσθ᾽ ὡς οὐ.., [Refs [[prev. author] “Ph.” 196 (_anapaest meter_, Porson for οὐκ ἔστιν ὅπως ου)]]; οἶσθ᾽ ὡς πόησο; by a mixture of constructions for ὡς χρὴ ποιῆσαι or ὡς ποιήσεις, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. author] “OT” 543, compare 5th c.BC: Hermippus Comicus 43, 4th-3rd c.BC: Menander Comicus 916]]; οἶσθ᾽ ὡς μετεύξει is falsa lectio in [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Medea” 600 (μέτευξαι Elmsley)]]; similarly, οἶσθα.. ὡς νῦν μὴ σφαλῇς [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Coloneus” 75.]]

__A.III.2
ὡς ἂν ποήσῃς however (in whatever way) thou mayest act, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. author] “Aj.” 1369, compare 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Symposium” 181a; αὐτῷ ὥς κεν ἅδῃ, τὼς ἔσσεται 3rd c.BC: Apollonius Rhodius Epicus 3.350.]]

__A.III.2.Ad

__B
ὡς as CONJUNCTION:

__B.I
with Substantive clauses, to express a fact, ={ὅτι}, that.

__B.II
with Final clauses, to express an end or purpose, ={ἵνα, ὅπως}, so that, in order that.

__B.III
Consecutive, ={ὥστε}, so that.

__B.IV
Causal, since, because.

__B.I
with Substantive Clauses, with verbs of learning, saying, etc., that, expressing a fact, γνωτὸν.., ὡς ἤδη Τρώεσσιν ὀλέθρου πείρατ᾽ ἐφῆπται [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 7.402, compare 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 3.194, etc.: in commands, προεῖπεν ὡς μηδεὶς κινήσοιτο 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Historia Graeca (Hellenica)” 2.1.22]]: with Verbs of fear or anxiety, with future indicative, μηκέτ᾽ ἐκφοβοῦ, μητρῷον ὥς σε λῆμ᾽ ἀτιμάσει ποτέ [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Electra” 1427, compare 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 6.2.30]]; μὴ φοβοῦ ὡς ἀπορήσεις [Refs 4th c.BC+ [[prev. work] 5.2.12, compare 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 10.36]]; a sentence beginning with ὡς is sometimes, when interrupted, resumed by ὅτι, and vice versa, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 5.3.30, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 470d, “Hp.Ma.” 281c]]; so ὡς with a finite Verb passes into the accusative and infinitive, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.70, 8.118: both constructions mixed in the same clause, ἐλογίζετο ὡς.. ἧττον ἂν αὐτοὺς ἐθέλειν.. 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 8.1.25, compare “HG” 3.4.27: after primary tenses (including historic _present_) ὡς]] is followed by indicative, after historic tenses by optative (sometimes by indicative, both constructions in ὑπίσχοντο.. ἀμυνέειν, φράζοντες ὡς οὔ σφι περιοπτέη ἐστὶ ἡ Ἑλλὰς ἀπολλυμένη.. ἀλλὰ τιμωρητέον εἴη [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 7.168)]]: sometimes with optative after a primary tense, κατάπτονται.. λέγοντες ὡς Ἀρίστων.. οὐ φήσειε [Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. author] 6.69, compare 1.70, 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 1.38, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Charmides” 156b.]]

__B.I.2
with Verbs of feeling, χαίρει δέ μοι ἦτορ, ὥς μευ ἀεὶ μέμνησαι [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 23.648; ἄχος ἔλλαβ᾽ Ἀχαιοὺς ὡς ἔπεσ᾽ 16.600.]]

__B.II
with Final Clauses, that, in order that; in this sense ὡς and ὡς ἄν, Epic dialect ὥς κεν, are used with the subjunctive after primary tenses of the indicative, and with the optative after the past tenses, βουλὴν ὑποθησόμεθ᾽.., ὡς μὴ πάντες ὄλωνται [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 8.37; τύμβον χεύαμεν.., ὥς κεν τηλεφανὴς.. εἴη 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 24.83; ἡμεῖς δ᾽ ἴωμεν ὡς, ὁπηνίκ᾽ ἂν θεὸς πλοῦν ἡμὶν εἴκῃ, τηνικαυθ᾽ ὁρμώμεθα 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Philoctetes” 464; [νέας] διηκοσίας περιέπεμπον.. ὡς ἂν μὴ ὀφθείησαν 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 8.7. b. rarely with]]future indicative, ὡς μὴ ὦν αὐτοὶ τε ἀπολέεσθε (conjecture Cobet for ἀπόλεσθε) κἀμὲ τρώσετε, ἐς ἄλλον τινὰ δῆμον ἀποίχεσθε [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Hecataeus Milesius Historicus 30J.]]

__B.II.2
ὡς is also used with past tenses of the indicative to express a purpose which has not been or cannot be fulfilled, τί μ᾽ οὐκ ἔκτεινας, ὡς ἔδειξα μήποτε..; so that I never should.., [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Tyrannus” 1392; ἔδει τὰ ἐνέχυρα λαβεῖν, ὡς μηδ᾽ εἰ ἐβούλετο ἐδύνατο ἐξαπατᾶν 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 7.6.23; compare ἵνα 5th c.BC: Bacchylides Lyricus 1.3, ὅπως 5th c.BC: Bacchylides Lyricus 1.3.]]

__B.II.3
ὡς with infinitive, to limit an assertion, ὡς μὲν ἐμοὶ δοκέειν [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 6.95, compare 2.124; ὡς εἰπεῖν λόγῳ [prev. work] 53]]; or ὡς ἔπος εἰπεῖν,compare ἔπος [Refs [11.4]]; ὡς συντόμως, or ὡς συνελόντι εἰπεῖν to speak shortly, to be brief, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Oeconomicus” 12.19, “Mem.” 3.8.10]]; ὡς εἰκάσαι to make a guess, i.e. probably, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.34, etc.; ὡς μικρὸν μεγάλῳ εἰκάσαι 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 4.36 (so without ὡς, οὐ πολλῷ λόγῳ εἰπεῖν 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.61), see supr. Ab. 11.1, 2.]]

__B.III
to express Consequence, like{ὥστε}, so that, frequently in [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus, εὖρος ὡς δύο τριήρεας πλέειν ὁμοῦ]] in breadth such that two triremes could sail abreast, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 7.24; ὑψηλὸν οὕτω.., ὡς τὰς κορυφὰς αὐτοῦ οὐκ οἷά τε εἶναι ἰδέσθαι 4.184]]; so in Trag. and Prose, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Persae” 437, +others, 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Tyrannus” 84, 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 3.5.7, etc.; ἀπέχοντας ἀπ᾽ ἀλλάλων ὡς ἦμεν Ϝικατίπεδον ἄντομον “Tab.Heracl.” 1.75; οὕτως.. ὡς ὁμολογεῖν 4th c.AD: Julianus Imperator “Orationes” 5.164d; ὡς καὶ τοὺς τεχνίτας λανθάνειν “PHolm.” 9.13]]; also, like{ὥστε}, with Indic., οὕτω κλεινὴ ἐγένετο, ὡς.. ἐξέμαθον [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 2.135, compare 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Trachiniae” 590, 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Historia Graeca (Hellenica)” 4.1.33.]]

__B.III.2
ἢ ὡς after a comparative, μάσσον᾽ ἢ ὡς ἰδέμεν [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “O.” 13.113; μαλακώτεροι.. ἢ ὡς κάλλιον αὐτοῖς 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 410d; compare ὥστε 5th c.BC: Bacchylides Lyricus 1.2: with words implying comparison, ὀλίγοι ἐσμὲν ὡς ἐγκρατεῖς εἶναι αὐτῶν]] too few to.., [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 4.5.15, γραῦς εἶ, ὦ Ἐλπινίκη, ὡς τηλικαῦτα διαπράττεσθαι πράγματα]] too old to.. [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Stesimbrotus Historicus 5J.]]

__B.III.3
ὡς is sometimes omitted where the antecedent demonstrative is expressed, οὕτω ἰσχυραί, μόγις ἂν διαρρήξειας so strong, you could hardly break them, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 3.12; ῥώμη σώματος τοιήδε, ἀεθλοφόροι τε ἀμφότεροι ἦσαν [prev. author] 1.31.]]

__B.IV
Causal, inasmuch as, since, τί ποτε λέγεις, ὦ τέκνο; ὡς οὐ μανθάνω [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Philoctetes” 914, compare 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Phoenissae” 843, 1077, 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Ranae” 278: with _optative_, μὴ καὶ λάθῃ με προσπεσών· ὡς μᾶλλον ἂν ἕλοιτο μ᾽ ἢ τοὺς πάντας Ἀργείους λαβεῖν 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Philoctetes” 46.]]

__B.IV.2
on the ground that.., with future indicative, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Lysias Orator 30.27.]]

with Participles in oblique cases, λέγουσιν ἡμᾶς ὡς ὀλωλότας they speak of us as dead, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Agamemnon” 672; ὡς μηδὲν εἰδότ᾽ ἴσθι μ᾽ ὧν ἀνιστορεῖς 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Philoctetes” 253; τὸν ἐκβαίνοντα κολάζουσιν ὡς παρανομοῦντα 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 338e; ἵνα μὴ ἀγανακτῇ ὑπὲρ ἐμοῦ ὡς δεινὰ πάσχοντος [prev. author] “Phd.” 115e, compare 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 5.85, 9.54; νῦν δέ σου τὰ ἔργα φανερὰ γεγένηται οὐχ ὡς ἀνιωμένου ἀλλ᾽ ὡς ἡδομένου τοῖς γιγνομένοις 5th c.BC: Lysias Orator 12.32; κτύπος φωτὸς ὡς τειρομένου [του] 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Philoctetes” 202 (Lyric poetry)]]; ἐν ὀλιγωρίᾳ ἐποιοῦντο, ὡς, ὅταν ἐξέλθωσιν, ἢ οὐχ ὑπομενοῦντας σφᾶς ἢ ῥᾳδίως ληψόμενοι βίᾳ made light of the matter, in the belief that.., [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 4.5.]]—Both constructions in one sentence, τοὺς κόσμους εἴασε χαίρειν ὡς ἀλλοτρίους τε ὄντας καὶ πλέον θάτερον ἡγησάμενος ἀπεργάζεσθαι [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Phaedo” 114e, compare 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 1.5.9.]]

ὡς before Preps., ἀνήγοντο ὡς ἐπὶ ναυμαχίαν (variant{-ίᾳ}) [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 1.48, compare 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Historia Graeca (Hellenica)” 2.1.22; φρύγανα συλλέγοντες ὡς ἐπὶ πῦρ [prev. author] “An.” 4.3.11]]; κατέλαβε τὴν ἀκρόπολιν ὡς ἐπὶ τυραννίδι, expressing the purpose, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 1.126; ἀπέπλεον.. ὡς ἐς τὰς Ἀθήνας [prev. author] 6.61; πλεῖς ὡς πρὸς οἶκον 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Philoctetes” 58; τὸ βούλευμ᾽ ὡς ἐπ᾽ Ἀργείοις τόδ᾽ ἦν [prev. author] “Aj.” 44: in these passages ὡς]] marks an intention; not so in the following: ἀπαγγέλλετε τῇ μητρὶ [χαίρειν] ὡς παρ᾽ ἐμοῦ [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 8.7.28; also ὡς ἀπὸ τῆς πομπῆς 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 327c; ὡς ἐκ κακῶν ἐχάρη 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 8.101.]]

__D

__D.I
as an exclamation, how, mostly with adverbs and adjectives, ὡς ἄνοον κραδίην ἔχες how silly a heart hadst thou! [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 21.441]]; ὡς ἀγαθὸν καὶ παῖδα λιπέσθαι how good is it.., [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 3.196, compare 24.194; φρονεῖν ὡς δεινόν 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Tyrannus” 316]]; ὡς ἀστεῖος ὁ ἄνθρωπος how charming he is! [LXX+5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Phaedo” 116d; ὡς ἐμεγαλύνθη τὰ ἔργα σου, Κύριε LXX.Psa.91(92).6, 103(104).24]]; in indirect clauses, ἐθαύμασα τοῦτο, ὡς ἡδέως.. ἀπεδέξατο marvelled at seeing how.., [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Phaedo” 89a.]]

__D.I.2
with Verbs, ὥς μοι δέχεται κακὸν ἐκ κακοῦ αἰεί how constantly.., [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 19.290, compare 21.273]]; ὡς οὐκ ἔστι χάρις μετόπισθ᾽ εὐεργέων how little thanks remain! [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 22.319]]; ὡς ὄχλος νιν.. ἀμφέπει see how.., [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Phoenissae” 148]]; ὡς ὑπερδέδοικά σου how greatly.., [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Antigone” 82; so perhaps ὡς οἰμώξεται 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Ranae” 279; ὡς ἅπανθ᾽ ὑμῖν τυραννίς ἐστι [prev. author] “V.” 488 (troch.).]]

__D.II
to mark a wish, oh that! with optative alone, ὡς ἔρις.. ἀπόλοιτο [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 18.107; ὡς ἀπόλοιτο καὶ ἄλλος 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 1.47, compare 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Electra” 126 (Lyric poetry)]]; also ὡς ἄν or κε with optative, ὡς ἂν ἔπειτ᾽ ἀπὸ σεῖο οὐκ ἐθέλοιμι λείπεσθαι [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 9.444; ὥς κέ οἱ αὖθι γαῖα χάνοι 6.281.]]

__D.II.2
joined with other words of wishing, ὡς ὤφελες αὐτόθ᾽ ὀλέσθαι [Refs 8th c.BC+ [3.428; ὡς δὴ μὴ ὄφελον νικᾶν 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 11.548.]]

__E
ὡς with numerals marks that they are to be taken only as a round number, as it were, about, nearly, σὺν ἀνθρώποις ὡς εἴκοσι [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 3.3.5]]; also ὡς πέντε μάλιστά κῃ about five (see. μάλα [Refs 5th c.BC+ [111.5), 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 7.30]]:—also with words compounded with numerals, δέπας.. ὡς τριλάγυνον [Refs 7th c.BC+ [7th-6th c.BC: Stesichorus Lyricus 7]]; παῖς ὡς ἑπτέτης of some seven years, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Gorgias” 471c; δρέπανα ὡς διπήχη 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 6.1.30, compare “An.” 5.4.12; compare ὡσεί 111.]]

__F
ὡς in some elliptical (or apparently elliptical) phrases:

__F.1
ὡς τί δὴ τόδε (i.e. γένηται); to what end? [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Orestes” 796 (troch.); compare ἵνα 5th c.BC: Bacchylides Lyricus 11.3c.]]

__F.2
know that (i.e. ἴσθι), ὡς ἔστιν ἀνδρὸς τοῦδε τἄργα ταῦτά σοι [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Ajax” 39; ὡς τοῦτό γ᾽ ἔρξας δύο φέρει δωρήματα [prev. author] “Ph.” 117; ὡς τῆσδ᾽ ἑκοῦσα παιδὸς οὐ μεθήσομαι 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Hecuba” 400, compare “Med.” 609, “Ph.” 720; ὡς τάχ᾽ οὐκέθ᾽ αἱματηρὸν.. ἀργήσει ξίφος [prev. work] 625 (troch.)]]; so in Comedy texts, ὡς ἔστ᾽ ἐν ἡμῖν τῆς πόλεως τὰ πράγματα [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Lysistrata” 32, compare 499 (_anapaest meter_), “Ach.” 333 (troch.), “Nu.” 209; also ἀλλ᾽ ὡς ἀπὸ τοῦ τείχους πάρεστιν ἄγγελος οὐδείς [prev. author] “Av.” 1119.]]

__F.3
ὡς ἕκαστος, ἕκαστοι, each severally (whether in respect of time, place, or other difference), ξυνελέγοντο.. Κορίνθιοι δισχίιοι ὁπλῖται, οἱ δ᾽ ἄλλοι ὡς ἕκαστοι, Φλειάσιοι δὲ πανστρατιᾷ [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 5.57, compare 1.107, 113]]; πρώτη τε αὕτη πόλις ξυμμαχὶς παρὰ τὸ καθεστηκὸς ἐδουλώθη, ἔπειτα δὲ καὶ τῶν ἄλλων ὡς ἑκάστη [ξυνέβη] (ξ. secl. Krüger: ἀπὸ κοινοῦ ἐδουλώθη [Refs [Scholia [same place]) [prev. author] 1.98; ἄλλοι τε παριόντες ἐγκλήματα ἐποιοῦντο ὡς ἕκαστοι [prev. work] 67, compare 7.65]]; χρησμολόγοι τε ᾖδον χρησμοὺς παντοίους, ὧν ἀκροᾶσθαι ὡς ἕκαστος ὥρμητο, i. e. different persons ran to listen to different prophecies, [Refs [[prev. author] 2.21]]; τὰς ἄλλας ὡς ἑκάστην ποι ἐκπεπτωκυῖαν ἀναδησάμενοι ἐκόμιζον ἐς τὴν πόλιν they made fast to the rest wherever each (ship) had been run ashore, [Refs [[prev. author] 7.74]]; οἱ δ᾽ οὖν ὡς ἕκαστοι Ἕλληνες κατὰ πόλεις τε ὅσοι ἀλλήλων ξυνίεσαν καὶ ξύμπαντες ὕστερον κληθέντες οὐδὲν πρὸ τῶν Τρωικῶν.. ἁθρόοι ἔπραξαν the various peoples that were later called by the common name of Greeks, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. author] 1.3; ὡς ἑκάστῳ ἔργον προστάσσων 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.114]]; ὡς ἑκάστην (one by one) αἱρέοντες (i.e. τὰς νήσους) οἱ βάρβαροι ἐσαγήνευον τοὺς ἀνθρώπους [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [[prev. author] 6.31, compare 79; ὡς ἑκασταχόσε 2nd-3rd c.AD: Dio Cassius Historicus 41.9, +others]]; rarely with a Verb, ὡς ἕκαστος ἀπικνέοιτο [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.29, compare 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 6.2: later ὡς]] follows ἕκαστος, ἑκάστῳ ὡς ὁ Θεὸς ἐμέρισεν μέτρον πίστεως [NT.Rom.12.3]:—for the etymology see infr. H; also ὡς ἑκάτεροι [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 3.74 (see. infr. H).]]

__G
ὡς pleonastic in ὡς ὅτι [NT+8th c.BC+ [1st c.BC: Dionysius Halicarnassensis 9.14, NT.2Cor.11.21, Scholia A 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 1.264, 129, 396, 3.280, “Anthologia Graeca” 9.530, uncertain reading in 1st c.BC-1st c.AD: Strabo Geographus 15.1.57.]]

__H
Etymology: this word is in origin five distinct words: [Refs [(1) ὡς ']]as' is the adverb from the Relat. ὅς (I.-[Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus]] stem yo-); with ὡς βέλτιστος cf. Sanskrit yācchrē[snull][tnull]á[hudot] 'the best possible': (2) ὧς 'thus' is the adverb of a Demonstr. stem so- found in Sanskrit sa, Gr. ὁ, Latin sō-c ([Refs [“Corpus Glossariorum Latinorum”]]; = ita, cf. Umbr. esoc); (3) ὡς postpositive (ὄρνιθες ὥς, etc.) constantly makes a preceding short closed syllable long in [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Homerus Epicus]], and must therefore have been ϝω; it may perhaps be related to Sanskrit vā, a form of va, iva (= [Refs [(1) or (2)]]like), Latin ve, Gr. ἦ[ϝ] ; [Refs [(4) ὡς preposition ']]to' is of doubtful origin (perhaps from *ὠς, cognate with Latin ōs 'face', Sanskrit ās: ὤς τινα ἐλθεῖν like{τί δέ δε φρένας ἵκετο πένθος};); (5) ὡς F. 3 is probably ϝως, adverb of ϝός the reflexive adjective, and means literal in his (their) own way (or place); it is idiomatically placed before ἕκαστος (ἑκάτερος),compare ϝὸν ϝεκάτερος [Refs [“Leg.Gort.” 1.18.]]

Abbott-Smith / STEPBible (TBESG)
γίγνομαι, see: γίνομαι.
γίνομαι, Ion. and κοινή for Att. γίγν- (M. Pr., 47; Bl., §6, 8 Mayser, 166 f.),
[in LXX chiefly for היה ;]
__1. of persons, things occurrences, to come into being, be born, arise, come on: Jhn.1:15 8:58, 1Co.15:37; a first appearance in public, Mrk.1:4, Jhn.1:6, al.; before ἐκ (of birth), Rom.1:3, Gal.4:4; διά, Jhn.1:3; βροντή, Jhn.12:29; σεισμός, Rev.6:12; γογγυσμός, Act.6:1; χαρά, Act.8:8, many other similar exx.; ἡμέρα, Luk.22:66, al.; ὀψέ, Mrk.11:19; πρωΐα, Mat.27:1; νύξ, Act.27:27.
__2. Of events, to come to pass, take place, happen: Mat.5:18, Mrk.5:14, Luk.1:20 2:15, Act.4:21, 2Ti.2:18, al.; μὴ γένοιτο [LXX for חָלִילָה, Jhn.22:29, al.], far be it, God forbid: Rom.3:4 (ICC, in l.), 1Co.6:15 and frequently in Pl.; καὶ ἐγένετο, ἐγένετο δέ ([in LXX for וַיְהִי ;] see Burton, 142 f.; M, Pr., 16f.; Dalman, Words, 32 f.; Robertson, Gr., 1042 f.), with indic, Mat.7:28, Luk.1:8, al.; before καί and indic., Luk.8:1, Act.5:7, al.; with accusative and inf., Mrk.2:23, Luk.3:21, al.; ὡς δὲ ἐγένετο, before τοῦ with inf., Act.10:25; with dative of person(s), to befall one: with inf., Act.20:16; with accusative and inf., Act.22:6; with adv., εὖ, Eph.6:3; τ́ ἐγένετο αὐτῷ (Field, Notes, 115), Act.7:40 (LXX); before εἰς, Act.28:6.
__3. to be made, done, performed, observed, enacted, ordained, etc.: Mat.6:10 19:8, Mrk.2:27 11:23, Act.19:26, al.; before διά with genitive, Mrk.6:2, Act.2:43; ὑπό, Luk.13:17; ἐκ, Luk.4:23; ἐν, 1Co.9:15; ἀπογραφή, Luk.2:2; ἀνάκρισις Act.25:26; ἄφεσις, Heb.9:22; ὁ νόμος, Gal.3:17; τὸ πάσχα, Mat.26:2.
__4. to become, be made, come to be: with pred., Mat.4:3, Luk.4:3, Jhn.2:9, 1Co.13:11, al.; before ὡς, ὡσεί, Mat.10:25, Mrk.9:26; εἰς (M, Pr., 71f.), Mrk.12:1o, al.; with genitive Rev.11:15; id., of age, Luk.2:42; with dative, γ. ἀνδρί ([LXX for הָיָה לְאִישׁ, Rut.1:12, al. ;] see Field, Notes, 156), Rom.7:3, 4; before ἐν, Act.22:17, Rev.1:10, al.; ἐπάνω, Luk.19:19; μετά, with genitive, Mrk.16:[10], Act.9:19; before εἰς, ἐπί (Field, Notes, 135), κατά (ib., 62), with accusative of place, Act.20:16 21:35 27:7, al.; before ἐκ, Mrk.9:7, Luk.3:22, 2Th.2:7, al. Aoristic pf. γέγονα (M, Pr., 52, 145f.; Field, Notes, 1f.), Mat.25:6, Luk.10:36, al. Aor. ἐγενήθη (for ἐγένετο, M, Pr., 139f.; Mayser, 379), Mat.11:23, al. (Cf. απο-, δια-, επι-, παρα-, συμ-, παρα-, προ-.)
(AS)

deep_entry:
Abbott-Smith / STEPBible (TBESG)
ἐθέλω, see: θέλω.
θέλω (the strengthened form ἐθέλω is found in Hom., and is the more frequently in Attic; see Rutherford, NPhr., 415f.),
[in LXX for חפץ ,אבה; with neg., מאן pi., etc. ;]
to will, be willing, wish, desire (more frequently than βούλομαι, which see, in vernac. and late Gk., also in MGr.; for various views as to its relation to β., see Thayer, 286; but see also BL, §24, see word): absol., Rom.9:16, 1Co.4:19 12:18, Jas.4:15; τ. θεοῦ θέλοντος, Act.18:21; with accusative of thing(s), Mat.20:21, Mrk.14:36, Jhn.15:7, Rom.7:15, 16 1Co.4:21 7:36, Gal.5:17; with inf., Mat.5:40, Mrk.10:43, Jhn.6:21, 67 Rom.7:21, Gal.4:9; with accusative and inf., Mrk.7:24, Luk.1:62, Jhn.21:22, 23 Rom.16:19, 1Co.14:5, Gal.6:13; οὐ θέλω, Mat.18:30, al.; id. with inf., Mat.2:18, Mrk.6:26, Jhn.5:40, 1Co.16:7; before ἵνα, Mat.7:12, Mrk.6:25, Jhn.17:24; opposite to ποιέω, πράσσω, ἐνεργέω, Rom.7:15, 19 2Co.8:10, 11 Php.2:13; before ἤ (ICG, in l.; Deiss., LAE, 179:24), 1Co.14:19; θέλων ἐν ταπεινοφροσυνῄ (of his own mere will, by humility, R, mg), Col.2:18; in OT quotations, for Heb. חפץ, with accusative of person(s), Mat.27:43; with accusative of thing(s), Mat.9:13 12:7, Heb.10:5, 8; with inf., 1Pe.3:10; for אמר, with inf., Act.7:28 (see Cremer, 726ff.).
(AS)

or θέλω (see. below), Epic dialect subjunctive ἐθέλωμι [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 1.549, 9.397]]: imperfect ἤθελον [Refs [14.120, etc.]]; Epic dialect and Lyric poetry ἔθελον [Refs 6th c.BC+ [6.336, 6th c.BC: Theognis Elegiacus 606, 5th c.BC: Bacchylides Lyricus 10.73]]; Ionic dialect ἐθέλεσκον [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 13.106, 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 6.12]]: future ἐθελήσω [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 18.262, etc.; θελήσω 5th c.BC: Antipho Orator 5.99]]: aorist 1 ἠθέλησα [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 2.2, etc.]]; Epic dialect ἐθέλησα [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 18.396; _imperative_ θέλησον 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Prometheus Vinctus” 783]]; subjunctive θελήσῃ[Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. work] 1028, 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 2.4.19, etc.; _optative_ θελήσαιμι 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Coloneus” 1133]]; participle θελήσας [Refs [[prev. author] “OT” 649 (Lyric poetry)]]: perfect ἠθέληκα [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 5.2.9, 4th c.BC: Aeschines Orator 2.139, 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 47.5]]; τεθέληκα (Alexandrian accusative to [LXX+5th c.BC+ [2nd c.AD: Phrynichus Atticista 307) LXX.Psa.40(41).12, 1st c.BC: Philodemus Gadarensis Epigrammaticus “Rh.” 2.76 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus, 2nd c.AD: Sextus Empiricus Philosophus “adversus Mathematicos” 2.37]]: pluperfect ἠθελήκει [Refs 8th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Historia Graeca (Hellenica)” 6.5.21; ἐτεθελήκεσαν 2nd-3rd c.AD: Dio Cassius Historicus 44.26 codices (elsewhere ἠθελήκεσαν as 46.47):—θέλω is never found in 8th c.BC: Homerus Epicus or 8th-7th c.BC: Hesiodus Epicus except 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 1.277 (uncertain), ὅττι θέλοιεν 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 15.317 as variant (ἅσσ᾽ ἐθέλοιεν 3rd-2nd c.BC: Aristarchus Grammaticus)]], nor in Aeolic dialect; rarely in early Epic dialect and Eleg., θέλοι [Refs 6th c.BC+ [“hymnus ad Apollinem” 46, θέλει 6th c.BC: Solon Lyricus 27.12]]; but is found in Ionic dialect Inscrr., [Refs 7th c.BC+ [“SIG” 45.16 (Halic., 5th c.BC), 1037.7 (Milet., 4th c.BC), and in 7th-6th c.BC(?): Semonides Iambographus 7.13, 6th c.BC: Hipponax Iambographus 22 B, 6th c.BC: Anacreon Lyricus 92]]:— both forms in codices of [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus and 5th c.BC: Hippocrates Medicus and in 1st c.AD(?): Heraclitus and 3rd c.AD: Democritus Epigrammaticus, also in 5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus and 5th c.BC: Bacchylides Lyricus: Trag. never use ἐθέλω except in augmented forms, ἤθελον, -ησα: Comedy texts never use θέλω except in phrases such as ἢν θεὸς θέλῃ, εἰ θεὸς θέλοι, 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Plutus” 347, “Ra.” 533]], or parodies of Trag.: early Attic dialect Inscrr, have ἐθέλω [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [“IG” 12.6.41, etc., till 3rd c.BC, when θέλω becomes common: _Attic dialect_ Prose writers rarely use θέλω]] except in phrases such as ἂν θεὸς θέλῃ [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-3rd c.BC: Dinarchus Orator 2.3]] or after a long vowel, e.g. μὴ θελῆσαι [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 5.72, μὴ θελήσας 4th c.BC: Isaeus Orator 8.11, μὴ θέλοντας 5th-6th c.BC: Andocides Orator 1.22, τῷ θέλοντι [prev. author] 4.7, etc.; but θέλω 5th c.BC: Antipho Orator 3.4.3, θελήσουσιν [prev. author] 5.99: in later Gr. θέλω]] is regular except in the augmented forms; ἐθέλω is not found in LXX or NT:—to be willing (of consent rather than desire, see at {βούλομαι} 1), but also generally, wish, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 3.324:]] —Constr.: _absolutely_, especially in participle, ἐθέλων ἐθέλουσαν ἀνήγαγεν[Refs 8th c.BC+ [[prev. work] 272; εἰ σύ γε σῷ θυμῷ ἐθέλοις 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 23.894; ἀλλά μοι ἤθελε θυμός 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 11.566]]: frequently followed by infinitive present or aorist, wish to.., [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 7.364, etc.: with]]infinitive supplied, εἰ δ᾽ ἐθέλεις πεζός (i.e. ἰέναι) [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 3.324]]: with accusative et infinitive, wish that.., [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 19.274, 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.3]]; rarely followed by ὥστε, [NT+5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Hippolytus” 1327: later with ἵνα, NT.Matt.7.12, etc.: not used with _accusative_ only, except when an]]infinitive is easily supplied, εὔκηλος τὰ φράζεαι ἅσσ᾽ ἐθέλῃσθα (i.e. φράζεσθαι) [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 1.554, compare 9.397, 7.182, 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 14.172]]; σιτέονται δὲ οὐκ ὅσα ἐθέλουσι (i.e. σιτέεσθαι) [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.71, compare 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 5.50]]; εἰ καὶ τῆς ἀξίας ἔλαττον ἐθελήσειέ τις (i.e. φράσαι) [Refs 4th c.AD+ [4th c.AD: Julianus Imperator “Orationes” 1.132a: also with _neuter_ _pronoun_ or]] adjective, τί δὴ θέλω; with what intent? [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Prometheus Vinctus” 118.]]

__2
with negative, almost, ={δύναμαι}, as μίμνειν οὐκ ἐθέλεσκον ἐναντίον they cared not to make a stand, i.e. they were unable, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 13.106; οὐδ᾽.. ἤθελε θυμὸς τειρομένοις ἑτάροισιν ἀμυνέμεν 17.702: _metaphorically_ of things, of a stream, οὐδ᾽ ἔθελε προρέειν ἀλλ᾽ ἴσχετο]] would not run on, but stopped,[Refs 8th c.BC+ [21.366, compare 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 8.223, 316, “hymnus ad Cererem” 45]]; αὔλειοι δ᾽ ἔτ᾽ ἔχειν οὐκ ἐθέλουσι θύραι [Refs 6th c.BC+ [6th c.BC: Solon Lyricus 4.28; τὰ δένδρα οὐδέν μ᾽ ἐθέλει διδάσκειν 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Phaedrus” 230d, compare “R.” 370b]] (said to be an Attic dialect use,[Refs 5th c.BC+ [Greg.Cor. p.135 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus).]]

__3
participle, ἐθέλων or θέλων willingly, gladly, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 3.272, etc. (also πιθοῦ θελήσας 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Tyrannus” 649 (Lyric poetry))]]; οὐκ ἐθέλων, ={ἀεκών}, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 4.300]]; with Article like{ὁ βουλόμενος}, whoever will, i.e. any one, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Philoctetes” 619, “Aj.” 1146, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Gorgias” 508c, etc.]]

__4
θέλεις οὐ θέλεις nolens volens, [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd c.AD: Arrianus Historicus “Epicteti Dissertationes” 3.9.16]]; θέλει οὐ θέλει[Refs 2nd c.AD+ [[prev. work] 3.3, 2nd c.AD: Marcus Antoninus Imperator 11.15.]]

__5
μὴ ἔθελε, with infinitive, do not, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 1.277, 2.247, 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Fragmenta” 174.]]

__6
εἰ θέλεις if you please, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Tyrannus” 343.]]

__7
followed by subjunctive, τί σοι θέλεις δῆτ᾽ εἰκάθ; in what wilt thou that I give way to thee? [Refs [[prev. work] 651 (Lyric poetry)]]; θέλεις μείνωμεν αὐτο; [Refs [[prev. author] “El.” 80.]]

__8
maintain, hold, with accusative et infinitive, [Refs 1st c.AD+ [1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus 2.883e, 2nd c.AD: Pausanias Periegeta 1.4.6.]]

__9
delight in, love, ἔν τινι [LXX.1Ki.18.22]; τινά[LXX.Psa.17(18).20]; but οἱ κακῶς τινὰς θέλοντες their ill-wishers, [Refs [Cat.Codex Astr. 7.234.]]

__10
ordain, decree, ἠθέλησεν [ὁ ἡγεμὼν] τὸν κίνδυνον τῆς προβολῆς εἶναι πρός τινας [Refs 3rd c.AD+ [“CPR” 20.17 (3rd c.AD), etc.]]

__II
of inanimate things (compare above [Refs [1.2),]]

__II.1
to express a future event, like our will or shall, εἰ ἐθελήσει ἀναβῆναι ἡ τυραννίς [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.109; εἰ ἐθελήσει ἐκτρέψαι τὸ ῥέεθρον ὁ Νεῖλος [prev. author] 2.11; εἰ θέλει τοι μηδὲν ἀντίξοον καταστῆναι [prev. author] 7.49, compare 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 370b, etc.:—in this sense, very rarely of living things, οὐ δοῦναι θέλοι, ={οὐκ ἂν δοίη}, 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Eumenides” 429; εἴπερ.. οὗτός [σ᾽] ἐθέλει κρατῆσαι 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Vespae” 536, compare 5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “N.” 7.90, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 375a.]]

__II.2
to be naturally disposed, to be wont or accustomed, with infinitive, συμβάσιες ἰσχυραὶ οὐκ ἐ. συμμένειν [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.74; μεγάλα πρήγματα μεγάλοισι κινδύνοισι ἐ. καταιρέεσθαι [prev. author] 7.50; αἱ πλευραὶ οὐκ ἐθέλουσιν ἐς τὸ εὐρὺ αὔξεσθαι 5th c.BC: Hippocrates Medicus “περὶ ἄρθρων ἐμβολῆς” 41; οὐκ ἐ. αἱ γνῶμαι.. ὁμοῖαι εἶναι 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 2.89; τοῦτ᾽ ἐνδελεχὲς ἐ. γίγνεσθαι 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Meteorologica” 347a5, compare “Metaphorical” 1013b27, +others]]; οὐ θέλει ζῆν, of premature births, [Refs [[prev. author] “HA” 575a28.]]

__II.3
in phrases expressive of meaning, τὸ θέλει σημαίνειν τὸ τέρας [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.78; τὸ θέλει τὸ ἔπος εἶπαι [prev. author] 6.37; τὸ θέλει τὰ δῶρα λέγειν [prev. author] 4.131]]; τὸ ἔπος τοῦτο ἐθέλει λέγειν ὡς.. [Refs [[prev. author] 2.13.]]

__II.4
τοῦ θέλοντος, ={τοῦ θελήματος}, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Coloneus” 1220 (Lyric poetry, assuming variant).]]

deep_entry:
Abbott-Smith / STEPBible (TBESG)
1. to roll up, pack  close, Lat. conglobare, κατὰ τείχεα λαὸν ἐέλσαι to roll up  the host and force  it back to  the walls, (Iliad by Homer); Ἀχαιοὺς ἐπὶ πρύμνηισιν ἐείλεον (Iliad by Homer); εἰλεῖν ἐν μέσσοισι to coop up  or hem in  on all sides, (Iliad by Homer); θῆρας ὁμοῦ εἰλεῖν to drive  game together, (Odyssey by Homer):—;Pass. to be cooped  or huddled up , εἰς ἄστυ ἄλεν (for ἄλησαν) (Odyssey by Homer); νηυσὶν ἐπὶ γλαφυρῆισιν ἐελμένοι (Odyssey by Homer):—;metaphorically, Διὸς βουλῆισιν ἐελμένος straitened, held in check  by the counsels of Zeus, (Odyssey by Homer)
2. to smite , νῆα κεραυνῶι Ζεὺς ἔλσας having smitten  the ship with lightning, (Odyssey by Homer)
3. to collect : Pass., ἀλὲν ὕδωρ water collected, ponded , (Iliad by Homer)
4. Pass., also, to draw oneself up, shrink up , ἀλῆναι ὑπ᾽ ἀσπίδι (Iliad by Homer); Ἀχιλῆα ἀλεὶς μένεν collecting himself  he waited the attack of Achilles, (Iliad by Homer)
5. Pass. also, to go to and fro , like Lat. versari, (Herdotus Historicus)
6. to wind, turn round :—; Pass. to turn round, revolve , ἰλλομένων ἀρότρων moving to and fro , (Sophocles Tragicus); ἕλιξ εἰλεῖται is twined round , (Theocritus Poeta Bucolicus) (ML)

---

LSJ / STEPBible (TFLSJ)
εἴλω
(also εἰλέω, εἱλέω, εἴλλω, εἵλλω, ἴλλω; εἱλῶνται is falsa lectio in [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd c.AD: Aretaeus Medicus “περὶ αἰτιῶν καὶ σημείων χρονίων παθῶν” 1.2)]], a word whose meanings are traceable to various roots of similar form, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [see below 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator]] —From εἴλω (present in [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Homerus Epicus only]]passive participle εἰλόμενος (see. below)), we have Epic dialect aorist ἔλσα [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 11.413]], infinitive ἐέλσαι [Refs [21.295]], Doric dialect participle ἔλσαις [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “O.” 10(11).43]]:—middle, aorist ἠλσάμην [Refs 7th c.BC+ [7th-6th c.BC(?): Semonides Iambographus 17]]:—passive, aorist 2 ἐάλην [ᾰ] [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 13.408]]; infinitive ἀλῆναι, ἀλήμεναι, [Refs [16.714, 18.76]]; participle ἀλείς, εῖσα, έν [Refs [22.308:]]perfect ἔελμαι, participle - μένος [Refs [13.524:]] —for ἐόλει, ἐόλητο, see.{ἐόλει}.—From εἰλέω [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 2.294]]: imperfect εἴλεον [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 22.460]]; contraction εἴλει [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 8.215, 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 12.210; ἐείλεον 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 18.447]]: future εἰλήσω [LXX+2nd c.AD+ [LXX.Job.40.21(26), “Anthologia Graeca” 12.208 (2nd c.AD: Strato Epigrammaticus)]]: aorist εἴλησα [LXX+1st c.AD+ [LXX.4Ki.2.8, 1st c.AD: Dioscorides (Dioscurides) Medicus 5.87 (ἐν-)]]:—middle, imperfect εἰλεῦντο [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 21.8]]; participle εἰλεύμενος [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 2.76]]:—passive, aorist εἰλήθην [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Hippocrates Medicus “περὶ νούσων” 4.52]]: perfect εἴλημαι [LXX+3rd c.BC+ [LXX.1Ki.21.9(10) and LXX.Isa.11.5 (assuming variant), 3rd c.BC: Lycophron Tragicus 1202]]: pluperfect εἴληντο [Refs 1st c.AD+ [1st c.AD: Josephus Historicus “Antiquitates Judaicae” 12.1.9.]]

__A
shut in (less frequently shut out, εἰλέσθων τοῦ ἱαροῦ let them be shut out from the temple, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [“IG” 22.1126.48 (4th c.BC))]]; [Ὀδυσῆα] ἔλσαν ἐν μέσσοισι μετὰ σφίσι, πῆμα δὲ ἔλσαν [Refs 8th c.BC+ [(4th-3rd c.BC: Zenodotus Grammaticus, variant{πῆμα τιθέντες}) 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 11.413; ὅτε Κύκλωψ εἴλει ἐνὶ σπῆϊ 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 12.210, compare 22.460; ἔνθα δυώδεκα μὲν μένον ἤματα δῖοι Ἀχαιοί· εἴλει γὰρ Βορέης ἄνεμος μέγας οὐδ᾽ ἐπὶ γαίῃ εἴα ἵστασθαι 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 19.200; ὅν περ ἄελλαι χειμέριαι εἰλέωσιν 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 2.294; εἱλεῖσθαι ἐν τῷ τόπῳ, μὴ δυνάμενον ἐκπλεῦσαι 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Mirabilia” 840a33, compare “Etymologicum Magnum” 298.29]]; εἰς ἄστυ ἄλεν (for ἄλησαν) [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 22.12; κατὰ ἄστυ ἐέλμεθα 24.662; ἐελμένοι ἔνδοθι πύργων 18.287; νηυσὶν ἔπι γλαφυρῇσιν ἐελμένοι 12.38]]; χειμέριον ἀλὲν ὕδωρ ponded water, prevented from flowing away, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 23.420]]; ὅσοι πικροὶ.. χυμοὶ κατὰ τὸ σῶμα πλανηθέντες ἔξω μὲν μὴ λάβωσιν ἀναπνοήν, ἐντὸς δὲ εἱλλόμενοι (variant{εἰλόμενοι}) τὴν ἀφ᾽ αὑτῶν ἀτμίδα τῇ τῆς ψυχῆς φορᾷ συμμείξαντες ἀνακερασθῶσι, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Timaeus” 86e.]]

__A.2
hinder, hold in check, prevent, ἧστο Διὸς βουλῇσιν ἐελμένος [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 13.524, compare 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Fragmenta - American Journal of Philology” 25: ἔλλοψ (as though ἴλλοψ) is derived from ἴλλεσθαι ={εἴργεσθαι} and ὄψ ={φωνή} by 2nd c.AD: Athenaeus Epigrammaticus 7.308c.]]

__A.3
enclose, cover, protect, ὑπ᾽ ἀσπίδος ἄλκιμον ἦτορ ἔλσας [Refs 7th c.BC+ [7th c.BC: Callinus Epicus 1.11]]; τῇ ὕπο (i.e. τῇ ἀσπίδι) πᾶς ἐάλη he was entirely covered, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 13.408.]]

__B
press, as olives and grapes, [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd c.AD: Pausanias Grammaticus “fragment” 155]]; ἀμφὶ βίην Διομήδεος.. εἰλόμενοι huddling around him, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 5.782]]; ἵππων φειδόμενος, μή μοι δευοίατο φορβῆς ἀνδρῶν, εἰλομένων, εἰωθότες ἔδμεναι ἄδην here where men throng,[Refs [[prev. work] 203; πλῆθεν.. ἵππων τε καὶ ἀνδρῶν εἰλομένων· εἴλει δὲ.. Ἕκτωρ 8.215, compare 1.409, 18.447, 21.295; πόλις δ᾽ ἔμπλητο ἀλέντων [prev. work] 607]]; ἐς ποταμὸν εἰλεῦντο they were forced into the river, [Refs [[prev. work] 8]]; εἱλουμένης τῆς τροφῆς the nourishment being concentrated, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [4th-3rd c.BC: Theophrastus Philosophus “de Causis Plantarum” 6.11.8; θῆρας ὁμοῦ εἰλεῦντα 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 11.573]]; [λέων] ἰλλόμενός περ ὁμίλῳ hard-pressed, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [3rd c.BC: Apollonius Rhodius Epicus 2.27; ἀπωθούμενον ὑπὸ τοῦ περιεστῶτος ἔξωθεν πνεύματος πάλιν ἐντὸς ὑπὸ τὸ δέρμα εἱλλόμενον κατερριζοῦτο 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Timaeus” 76b]]:—passive, of crowds, swarm, jostle one another, ἐν ὀλίγῳ εἰλουμένους [Refs 1st c.AD+ [1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus “Crassus” 25]]; of ants, [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd c.AD: Lucianus Sophista “Icar.” 19.]]

__B.2
in aorist passive, of a man or animal, contract his body, draw himself together, Αἰνείας δ᾽ ἐάλη καὶ ἀπὸ ἕθεν ἀσπίδ᾽ ἀνέσχεν [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 20.278]]; ἐνὶ δίφρῳ ἧστο ἀλείς (huddled up), ἐκ γὰρ πλήγη φρένας [Refs [16.403]]; of a lion when struck, ἐάλη τε χανών [Refs [20.168]]; of a warrior, Ἀχιλῆα ἀλεὶς μένεν [Refs 8th c.BC+ [21.571; οἴμησεν δὲ ἀλεὶς ὥς τ᾽ αἰετὸς ὑψιπετήεις 22.308, 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 24.538.]]

__B.II
without the idea of pressure, collect, ἐν Πίσᾳ ἔλσαις στρατὸν λείαν τε πᾶσαν [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “O.” 10(11).43:]] —passive, Ἀργείους ἐκέλευσα ἀλήμεναι ἐνθάδε πάντας to assemble, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 5.823.]]

__C
(found only in the forms εἰλέω (εἱλ-), ἴλλω) wind, turn round, σκολιήν τε καὶ οὐ μίαν ἀτραπὸν ἴλλων [Refs 2nd c.BC+ [2nd c.BC: Nicander Epicus “Theriaca” 478]]; ἀπὸ δὲ τῶ[ν πετρῶν] ἴλλει ἡ στεφάνη ἐπὶ τὸν λόφον [Refs 4th c.BC+ [“GDI” iv (4th c.BC)]]; νῆα δ᾽ ἔπειτα πέριξ εἴλει ῥόος [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [3rd c.BC: Apollonius Rhodius Epicus 2.571]]; roll, γλῶσσαν uncertain in [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [3rd c.BC: Callimachus Epicus “Iambi” 1.144]]:— passive, revolve, move to and fro, ἰλλομένων ἀρότρων [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Antigone” 340 (Lyric poetry); οἱ ἀστέρες ἐν τῷ οὐρανῷ εἰλέονται 2nd c.AD: Lucianus Sophista “Astr.” 29]]; περὶ τὴν γῆν ἀεὶ εἱλεῖν ἰών, as etymology of ἥλιος (ἀέλιος), [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Cratylus” 409a]]; εἰλέονται ἐπὶ τὸ ὑγιὲς σκέλος they pivot or swing round on the sound leg, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Hippocrates Medicus “περὶ ἄρθρων ἐμβολῆς” 52, compare “Mochl.” 20]]; of a flame, περὶ δ᾽ αὐτὸν εἰλεῖτο φλόξ [Refs 2nd c.BC+ [2nd c.BC: Moschus Bucolicus 4.104]]; κατ᾽ αὐτὸν (i.e. τὸν κισσὸν) ἕλιξ εἰλεῖται is twined round, [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [3rd c.BC: Theocritus Poeta Bucolicus 1.31; δαίμων ἐν μέσῳ τοῦ παντὸς εἱλουμένη 2nd-3rd c.AD: Hermes Trismegistus cited in 5th c.AD: Stobaeus, Joannes 1.3.52]]; also of hair on the crown, to be whorled, [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd c.AD: Rufus Medicus “περὶ ὀνομασίας” 13.]]

__C.II
roll up tight, [κῶας] εἴλει ἀφασσόμενος [LXX+3rd c.BC+ [3rd c.BC: Apollonius Rhodius Epicus 4.181; τὴν μηλωτὴν εἱλήσας LXX.4Ki.2.8:—]]passive, ἰλλομένοις ἐπὶ λαίφεσι furled, [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [3rd c.BC: Apollonius Rhodius Epicus 1.329.]]

deep_entry:
Abbott-Smith / STEPBible (TBESG)
1. a ring, circle, round , (Homer); ἀσπίδος κύκλος the round  shield, (Aeschulus Tragicus)
2. Adverbial usages, κύκλῳ in a circle  or ring, round about , (Odyssey by Homer), attic; with genitive, κ. τοῦ στρατοπέδου (Xenophon Historicus), etc.
3. any circular body :
4. a wheel , (Iliad by Homer)
5. a place of assembly , the ἀγορά, (Iliad by Homer), attic:—;then, like Lat. corona, a ring or circle of people , (Sophocles Tragicus)
6. the vault  of the sky, (Herdotus Historicus), etc.
7. the orb  or disk  of the sun and moon, (Herdotus Historicus), etc.
9. a round shield , see. above 1.
10. in plural the eye-balls, eyes , (Sophocles Tragicus):—;rarely in singular, the eye , (Sophocles Tragicus)
11. any circular motion, an orbit  of the heavenly bodies, revolution  of the seasons, cycle  of events, (Herdotus Historicus)
12. a circular dance , (Aristophanes Comicus) (ML)

---

LSJ / STEPBible (TFLSJ)
κύκλος, ὁ
(Doric dialect ἁ, see below 11.11), also with irregular plural κύκλα [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad”, etc., see below 11.1, 3, 9, 111.1]]:—ring, circle, ὅπποτέ μιν δόλιον περὶ κύκλον ἄγωσιν, of the circle which hunters draw round their game, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 4.792]]; κ. δέκα χάλκεοι (concentric) circles of brass on a round shield, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 11.33, compare 20.280]]; but ἀσπίδος κύκλον λέγω the round shield itself, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Septem contra Thebas” 489, compare 496, 591.]]

__2
Adverbial usages, κύκλῳ in a circle or ring, round about, κ. ἁπάντῃ [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 8.278; κ. πάντῃ 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 3.1.2; πανταχῇ 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 4.9; τὸ κ. πέδον 5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “O.” 10(11).46; κ. περιάγειν 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 4.180; λίμνη.. ἐργασμένη εὖ κ. [prev. author] 2.170; τρέχειν κ. 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Thesmophoriazusae” 662; περιέπλεον αὐτοὺς κ. 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 2.84; οἱ κ. βασιλεῖς 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 7.2.23]]; ἡ κ. περιφορά, κίνησις, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Leges” 747a, 2nd c.AD: Alexander Rhetor Aphr. “in Top.” 218.3: frequently with περί]] or words compounded there with, round about, κ. πέριξ [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Persae” 368, 418; περιστῆναι κ. 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.43; βωμὸν κ. περιστῆναι 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Fragmenta - American Journal of Philology” 379; ἀμφιχανὼν κ. 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Antigone” 118 (Lyric poetry); περιστεφῆ κ. [prev. author] “El.” 895; περισταδὸν κ. 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Andromache” 1137; κ. περιϊέναι 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Phaedo” 72b, etc.; τοῦ φλοιοῦ περιαιρεθέντος κ. 4th-3rd c.BC: Theophrastus Philosophus “Historia Plantarum” 4.15.1]]; so κ. περὶ αὐτήν round about it, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.185; περὶ τὰ δώματα κ. [prev. author] 2.62]]; also κύκλῳ with accusative, without περί, ἐπιστήσαντες κ. σῆμα [Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. author] 4.72; πάντα τὸν τόπον τοῦτον κ. 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 4.4: with _genitive_, κ. τοῦ στρατοπέδου 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 4.5.5; τὰ κ. τῆς Ἀττικῆς 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 18.96, compare “PFay.” 110.7 (1st c.AD)]], etc.: metaphorically, around or from all sides, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Antigone” 241, etc.]]; κεντουμένη κύκλῳ ἡ ψυχή all over, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Phaedrus” 251d]]; τὰ κ. the circumstances, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Rhetorica” 1367b29, “EN” 1117b2]]; ἡ κ. ἀπόδειξις, of arguing in a circle, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. author] “APo.” 72b17, compare “APr.” 57b18: with Preps., ἐν κ. 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Ajax” 723, “Ph.” 356, 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Bacchae” 653, 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Vespae” 432, etc.; ἅπαντες ἐν κ. [prev. author] “Eq.” 170, “Pl.” 679: with _genitive_, 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Hercules Furens” 926, 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 3.74; κατὰ κύκλον 5th c.BC: Empedocles Poeta Philosophus 17.13.]]

__II
any circular body:

__II.1
wheel, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 23.340; in which sense the irregular _plural_ κύκλα is mostly used, 5.722, 18.375]]; τοὺς λίθους ἀνατιθεῖσι ἐπὶ τὰ κύκλα on the janker, [Refs [Inscriptiones Graecae 12.350.47.]]

__II.2
trencher, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [“SIG” 57.32 (Milet., 5th c.BC), “Abh.Berl.Akad.” 1928(6).29 (from Cos), 2nd c.AD(?): Pollianus Epigrammaticus 6.84.]]

__II.3
place of assembly, of the ἀγορά, ἱερὸς κ. [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 18.504; ὁ κ. τοῦ Ζηνὸς τὠγοραίου “Schwyzer” 701 B 6 (Erythrae, 5th c.BC)]]; ἀγορᾶς κ. (compare κυκλόεις) [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Orestes” 919]]; of the amphitheatre, [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd-3rd c.AD: Dio Cassius Historicus 72.19.]]

__II.3.b
crowd of people standing round, ring or circle of people, κ. τυραννικός [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Ajax” 749]]; κύκλα χαλκέων ὅπλων, i.e. of armed men, uncertain in [Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. author] “fragment” 210.9, compare 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 7.5.41: _absolutely_, 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Andromache” 1089, 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 5.7.2 (both _plural_), 4th-3rd c.BC: Diphilus Comicus 55.3.]]

__II.3.c
place in the ἀγορά where domestic utensils were sold, [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd c.AD: Alexander Rhetor 99.]]

__II.4
vault of the sky, ὁ κ. τοῦ οὐρανοῦ [LXX+5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.131, LXX.1Esd.4.34; πυραυγέα κ. αἰθέρος “Hymni Homerici” 8.6, compare 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Ion” 1147; ὁ ἄνω κ. 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Philoctetes” 815; ἐς βάθος κύκλου 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Aves” 1715; νυκτὸς αἰανὴς κ. 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Ajax” 672]]; γαλαξίας κ. the milky way, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [“Placita Philosophorum” 2.7.1, +others, 2nd c.AD(?): Pollianus Epigrammaticus 4.159; also ὁ τοῦ γάλακτος κ. 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Meteorologica” 345a25; πολιοῖο γάλακτος κ. 4th-3rd c.BC: Aratus Epicus 511.]]

__II.4.b
μέγιστος κ. great circle, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Autolycus Astronomus “Sph.” 2, +others; μ. κ. τῶν ἐν τῇ σφαίρᾳ 3rd c.BC: Archimedes Geometra “περὶ σφαίρας καὶ κυλίνδρου” 1.30, compare 1st c.BC: Geminus Astronomicus 5.70]]; κ. ἰσημερινός, θερινός, etc., [Refs 1st c.BC+ [1st c.AD: Philo Judaeus 1.27; χειμερινός 1st c.BC: Geminus Astronomicus 5.7, 2nd c.AD: Cleomedes Astronomus 1.2]]; ἀρκτικός, ἀνταρκτικός, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [1st c.BC: Geminus Astronomicus 5.2, 9; ὁ κ. ὁ τῶν ζῳδίων 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Meteorologica” 343a24]]; ὁ ὁρίζων κ. the horizon, [Refs [[prev. author] “Cael.” 297b34]]; παράλληλοι κ., of parallels of latitude, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Autolycus Astronomus “Sph.” 1]]: in plural, the zones, [Refs [Stoic. 2.196.]]

__II.5
orb, disk of the sun and moon, ἡλίου κ. [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Prometheus Vinctus” 91, “Pers.” 504, 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Antigone” 416; πανσέληνος κ. 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Ion” 1155]]; μὴ οὐ πλήρεος ἐόντος τοῦ κύκλου (i.e. τῆς σελήνης) [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 6.106]]: in plural, the heavenly bodies, [Refs 1st c.BC+ [Inscriptiones Graecae 14.2012 A 9 (Sulp. 1st c.BC(?): Maximus Astrologus).]]

__II.6
circle or wall round a city, especially round Athens, ὁ Ἀθηνέων κ. [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.98, compare 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 2.13, etc.; οὐχὶ τὸν κ. τοῦ Πειραιῶς, οὐδὲ τοῦ ἄστεως 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 18.300.]]

__II.6.b
circular fort, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 6.99, +others]]

__II.7
round shield, see entry [near the start]

__II.8
in plural, eye-balls, eyes, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Tyrannus” 1270, “Ph.” 1354; ὀμμάτων κ. [prev. author] “Ant.” 974 (Lyric poetry)]]: rarely in singular, eye, ὁ αἰὲν ὁρῶν κ. Διός [Refs [[prev. author] “OC” 704 (Lyric poetry).]]

__II.9
οἱ κ. τοῦ προσώπου cheeks, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Hippocrates Medicus “περὶ νούσων” 2.50; κύκλα παρειῆς 4th-5th c.AD(?): Nonnus Epicus “Dionysiaca” 33.190, 37.412]]; but κύκλος μαζοῦ, poetry for μαζός, is falsa lectio in [Refs 3rd c.AD+ [3rd-4th c.AD: Tryphiodorus Epicus 34.]]

__II.10
κ. ἐλαίης an olive wreath, [Refs 5th c.AD+ [5th-6th c.AD: Orphica “Argonautica” 325 (_plural_).]]

__II.11
cycle or collection of legends or poems, κύκλον ἱστορημέναν ὑπὲρ Κρήτας [Refs [“GDI” 5187.9 (from Crete)]]; especially of the Epic cycle, ὁ ἐπικὸς κ. [Refs 5th c.BC+ [2nd c.AD: Athenaeus Epigrammaticus 7.277e, 5th c.AD: Proclus Philosophus cited in 9th c.AD: Photius Legal icographus, etc. “Bibliotheca - Patrologia Graeca” p.319 5th c.BC: Bacchylides Lyricus, compare 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Rhetorica” 1417a15]]; of the corpus of legends compiled by Dionysius Scytobrachion, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [2nd c.AD: Athenaeus Epigrammaticus 11.481e, cf. Scholia 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 2.120]]; κ. ἐπιγραμμάτων Suid. see at {Ἀγαθίας};[Refs [compare κυκλικός 11.]]

__III
circular motion, orbit of the heavenly bodies, κύκλον ἰέναι [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Timaeus” 38d; οὐρανὸς.. μιᾷ περιαγωγῇ καὶ κύκλῳ συναναχορεύει τούτοις 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “de Mundo” 391b18]]; revolution of the seasons, ἐνιαυτοῦ κ. [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Orestes” 1645, “Ph.” 477]]; τὸν ἐνιαύσιον κ. the yearly cycle,[Refs [[prev. work] 544; ἑπτὰ.. ἐτῶν κ. __A
ὦ μεγάλε Ζεῦ [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Septem contra Thebas” 822 (_anapaest meter_).]]

__A.I

__A.I.b
full-grown, of age as shown by stature, νῦν δ᾽ ὅτε δὴ μ. εἰμί [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 2.314; μήτε μέγαν μήτ᾽ οὖν νεαρῶν τινα 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Agamemnon” 358 (_anapaest meter_)]]; later, elder of two persons of the same name, Wilcken [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [“Chr.” 305 (3rd c.BC)]]; Σκιπίων ὁ μ. [Refs 2nd c.BC+ [2nd c.BC: Polybius Historicus 18.35.9.]]

__A.I.c
of animals, μ. ἵπποι, βοῦς, σῦς, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 2.839, 18.559, 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 19.439; αἰετός 5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “I.” 6(5).50.]]

__A.I.2
generally, vast, high, οὐρανός, ὄρος, πύργος, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 1.497, 16.297, 6.386]]; wide, πέλαγος, λαῖτμα θαλάσσης, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 3.179, 5.174]]; long, ἠϊών, αἰγιαλός, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 12.31, 2.210: sometimes opposed to ὀλίγος, κῦμα οὔτε μέγ᾽ οὔτ᾽ ὀ. 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 10.94]]; but usually opposed to μικρός or σμικρός, πρὸς ἑαυτὸ ἕκαστον καὶ μ. καὶ σμικρόν [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Anaxagoras Philosophus 3; τὸ ἄπειρον ἐκ μεγάλου καὶ μικροῦ 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Metaphysica” 987b26, etc.]]

__A.II
of quality or degree, great, mighty, frequently epithet of gods, ὁ μ. Ζεύς [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Supplices” 1052 (Lyric poetry), etc.]]; μεγάλα θεά, of Demeter and Persephone, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Coloneus” 683 (Lyric poetry)]]; θεοὶ μεγάλοι, of the Cabiri, [Refs [“IG” 12(8).71 (from Imbros), etc.]]; Μήτηρ μ., of Cybele, [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [“SIG” 1014.83 (Erythrae, 3rd c.BC), 1138.3 (Delos, 2nd c.BC)]]; Μήτηρ θεῶν μ. [Refs [“OGI” 540.6 (from Pessinus), etc.]]; Ἴσιδος μ. μητρὸς θεῶν [Refs 2nd c.BC+ [“PStrassb.” 81.14 (2nd c.BC)]]; μ. ἡ Ἄρτεμις Ἐφεσίων [NT.Act.19.28]; τίς θεὸς μ. ὡς ὁ θεὸς ἡμῶ; [LXX+NT [LXX.Psa.76(77).13; ὁ μ. θεός NT.Tit.2.13]]; of men, μ. ἠδὲ κραταιός [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 18.382; ὀλίγος καὶ μ. 7th c.BC: Callinus Epicus 1.17, etc.]]; μέγας ηὐξήθη rose to greatness, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 2.5; ἤρθη μ. [prev. work]8; βασιλεὺς ὁ μ.]], i. e. the King of Persia, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.188, etc. (θεῶν β. ὁ μ., of Zeus, 5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “O.” 7.34); βασιλεὺς μ. 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Persae” 24 (_anapaest meter_)]]; as a title of special monarchs, Ἀρδιαῖος ὁ μ. [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 615c; ὁ μ. [prev. author] “Tr.” 674; ἐπὶ μέγα ἦλθεν ἰσχύος 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 2.97.]]

__A.II.2
strong, of the elements, etc., ἄνεμος, λαῖλαψ, Ζέφυρος, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 19.200, 12.408, 14.458]]; of properties, passions, qualities, feelings, etc., of men, θάρσος, πένθος, ποθή, etc.,[NT+8th c.BC+ [9.381, 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 1.254, 11.471, etc.; ἀρετή 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 24.193, 5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “O.” 8.5; θυμός 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 9.496, 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Orestes” 702; κλέος 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 6.446; ἄχος 9.9; πυρετός NT.Luke.4.38 (incorrect _accusative_ to 2nd c.AD: Galenus Medicus 7.275)]]; ἡ μ. νοῦσος epilepsy, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Hippocrates Medicus “ἐπιδημίαι” 6.6.5, compare 2nd c.AD: Galenus Medicus 17(2).341.]]

__A.II.3
of sounds, great, loud, ἀλαλητός, ἰαχή, πάταγος, ὀρυμαγδός, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 12.138, 15.384, 21.9, 256]]; θόρυβοι, κωκυτός, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Ajax” 142 (_anapaest meter_), 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Medea” 1176; οὐκ ἔστι ὅκως τι νεῖκος ἔσται ἢ μέγα ἢ σμικρόν 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 3.62; μὴ φώνει μέγα 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Philoctetes” 574.]]

__A.II.4
generally, great, mighty, ὅρκος [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 19.113]]; ὄλβος, τιμά, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “O.” 1.56, “P.” 4.148]]; μ. λόγος, μῦθος, a great story, rumour, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Prometheus Vinctus” 732, 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Ajax” 226 (Lyric poetry)]]; ἐρώτημα a big, i. e. difficult, question, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Euthydemus” 275d, “Hp.Ma.” 287b]]; weighty, important, τόδε μεῖζον [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 16.291]]; μέγα ποιέεσθαί τι to esteem of great importance, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 3.42, compare 9.111; μέγα γενέσθαι εἴς τι 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Historia Graeca (Hellenica)” 7.5.6; μ. ὑπάρχειν πρός τι [prev. author] “Mem.” 2.3.4; μέγα διαφέρειν εἴς τι 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Leges” 78o c]]; οὐκ ἂν εἴη παρὰ μέγα τὸ δικολογεῖν not of great importance, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [1st c.BC: Philodemus Gadarensis Epigrammaticus “Rh.” 2.85 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus]]; τὸ δὲ μέγιστον and what is most important, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 4.70, compare 1.142]]; οἱ μέγιστοι καιροί the most pressing emergencies, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 20.44]]; μ. ὠνησάμενοι χρημάτων for large sums, [Refs 2nd c.BC+ [2nd c.BC: Polybius Historicus 4.50.3, etc.]]

__A.II.5
with a bad sense, over-great, μέγα εἰπεῖν to speak big, and so provoke divine wrath, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 22.288; λίην μέγα εἶπες 3.227, 16.243; μέγα ἔργον 3.261, 5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “N.” 10.64; ἔργων μ. 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Agamemnon” 1546 (_anapaest meter_); ὠμὸν τὸ βούλευμα καὶ μ. 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 3.36]]; ἔπος μ., μ. λόγοι, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Ajax” 423 (Lyric poetry), “Ant.” 1350 (_anapaest meter_); μ. γλῶσσα [prev. work] 127 (_anapaest meter_)]]; μηδὲν μέγ᾽ εἴπῃς [Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. author] “Aj.” 386; μὴ μέγα λέγε 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Phaedo” 95b; μὴ μεγάλα λίαν λέγε 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Ranae” 835; μέγα φρονεῖν 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Tyrannus” 1078, 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Hippolytus” 6; μεγάλα φρονεῖν 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Acharnenses” 988]]; μεγάλα, μεῖζον ἢ δικαίως πνεῖν, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Andromache” 189, 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Agamemnon” 376 (Lyric poetry); μέγα τι παθεῖν 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 5.8.17; μὴ μέγα λέγων μεῖζον πάθῃς 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Hercules Furens” 1244.]]

__A.II.6
of style. impressive, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demetrius Phalereus Rhetor “Demetrius on Style” 278]]; μεῖζον more striking, [Refs [[prev. work] 103.]]

__A.II.7
of days, long, [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd c.AD: Galenus Medicus 12.714.]]

__B
adverb μεγάλως [ᾰ] greatly, mightily, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 16.432, 8th-7th c.BC: Hesiodus Epicus “Theogonia” 429, 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.16, 30, +others, 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 8.2.10, 1st c.BC: Parthenius Mythographus 28.1, etc.; strengthened, μάλα μ. 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 17.723; δμαθέντες μ. 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Persae” 907 (Lyric poetry); with _adjectives_, 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.4, 7.190.]]

__B.II
more frequently neuter singular μέγα as adverb, very much, exceedingly, μ. χαῖρε all hail!, see l. for μάλα in [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 24.402]]; especially with Verbs expressing strong feeling, μ. κεν κεχαροίατο [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 1.256; μ. κήδεται 2.27, etc.: with Verbs expressing power, might, μ. πάντων.. κρατέει 1.78; ὃς μ. πάντων.. ἤνασσε 10.32; πατρὸς μ. δυναμένοιο 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 1.276, compare 8th c.BC: Homerus Epicus “Epigrammata” 15.1, 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Eumenides” 950 (_anapaest meter_), 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Helena” 1358 (Lyric poetry), 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Ranae” 141, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 366a; μ. δύνασθαι παρά τινι 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 2.29; πλουτέειν μ. 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.32]]; or those expressing sound, loudly, μ. ἰάχειν, ἀῧσαι, βοῆσαι, εὔξασθαι, ἀμβῶσαι, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 2.333, 14.147, 17.334, 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 17.239, 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.8 (also _plural_, μεγάλ᾽ εὔχετο 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 1.450]]; μ. αὐδήσαντος, μ. ἤπυεν, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 4.505, 9.399): strengthened, μάλα μ. 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 15.321; μ. δ᾽ ἔβραχε φήγινος ἄξων 5.838, etc.: so in Trag. with all kinds of Verbs, μ. στένειν, σθένειν, χλίειν, 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Agamemnon” 711 (Lyric poetry), 938, “Ch.” 137]]: also in plural, μεγάλα.. δυστυχεῖς [Refs [[prev. author] “Eu.” 791 (Lyric poetry).]]

__B.II.2
of Space, far, μέγα προθορών [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 14.363]]; ἄνευθε μέγα far away,[Refs 5th c.BC+ [22.88; οὐκ ἂν μέγα τι τῆς ἀληθείας παρεξέλθοις 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Philebus” 66b.]]

__B.II.3
with adjectives, as μέγ᾽ ἔξοχος, μέγα νήπιος, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 2.480, 16.46]]; μ. νήπιε Oracle texts cited in [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.85; μ. πλούσιος [prev. author] 1.32, 7.190; ὦ μέγ᾽ εὔδαιμον κόρη 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Prometheus Vinctus” 647]]: with comparative and superlative, by far, μέγ᾽ ἀμείνονες, ἄριστος, φέρτατος, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 4.405, 2.82, 16.21.]]

__C.1

Diehl, 7.6, 1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus “Lycurgus” 19]]: compare μέττον· μεῖζον, [NT+5th c.AD+ [5th c.AD(?): Hesychius Legal icographus (uncertain); later μειζότερος NT.3JOhn.4]] (used as title, elder, [Refs 6th c.AD+ [POxy. 943.3 (6th c.AD), etc.)]]; μειζονώτερος [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Fragmenta - American Journal of Philology” 434]]:—greater, longer, taller, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 3.168, 9.202, etc.]]; frequently also, too great, γέρας [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Sophista” 231a]]; Μηνόφιλος μείζων M. the elder, [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [Ostr.Bodl. see C 2 (2nd c.AD)]]; as title, μειζων κώμης headman of a village, [Refs 4th c.AD+ [“POxy.” 1626.5 (4th c.AD)]], etc.: generally, the higher authority, [Refs 3rd c.AD+ [PLond. 2.214.22 (3rd c.AD), “POxy.” 1204.17 (_plural_, 3rd c.AD)]]; οὔτε μεῖζον οὔτε ἔλαττον, a strong form of denial, nothing whatever, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [1st c.BC: Dionysius Halicarnassensis “de Compositione Verborum” 4; οὐδαμὰ προὔφηνεν οὔτε μείζον᾽ οὔτ᾽ ἐλάττονα 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Trachiniae” 324]]. adverb μειζόνως [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Hecuba” 1121, 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 1.130, 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Cynegeticus” 13.3, 5th-6th c.BC: Isocrates Orator 9.21, etc.]]; Ionic dialect μεζόνως [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 3.128, 3rd c.BC: Herodas Mimographus 4.80, etc.]]: neuter as adverb, μεῖζον σθένειν [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Philoctetes” 456, 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Supplices” 216; μ. ἰσχύειν 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator “Epistulae” 3.28; ἐπὶ μ. ἔρχεται 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Philoctetes” 259.]]

__C.2

[prev. author] “OC” 700 (Lyric poetry); τὰ μέγιστ᾽ ἐτιμάθης [prev. author] “OT” 1203 (Lyric poetry)]]; ἐς μέγιστον[Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. work] 521; ἐς τὰ μ. 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 8.111]]:—late superlative μεγιστότατος [Refs 1st c.AD+ [“PLond.” 1.130.49 (1st-2nd c.AD)]].
