short_definition: isn't it? — 1. after Verbs expressing fear or apprehension, = Lat. vereor ut, δέδοικα μὴ οὐ γένηταί τι I fear it will not be; whereas δέδοικα μὴ γένηται mean, I fear it will be. Here, μή and ο
deep_entry:
Abbott-Smith / STEPBible (TBESG)
1. after Verbs expressing fear  or apprehension, =  Lat. vereor ut, δέδοικα μὴ οὐ γένηταί τι I fear it will not  be; whereas δέδοικα μὴ γένηται mean, I fear it will be.  Here, μή and οὐ each retain their proper force.
2. with Inf.,
3. after Verbs of hindering, denying, avoiding, needing , when μὴ οὐ resembles Lat. quin or quominus , οὐδὲν κωλύει μὴ οὐκ ἀληθὲς εἶναι τοῦτο nihil impedit quin hoc verum sit;  or with the Art., οὐδὲν ἐλλείψω τὸ μὴ οὐ πυθέσθαι nihil praetermittam quominus reperiam , (Sophocles Tragicus)
4. after Verbs signifying impossibility, impropriety, reluctance , μὴ οὐ has a negative translation, δεινὸν ἐδόκεε εἶναι μὴ οὐ λαβεῖν (Herdotus Historicus); αἰσχύνη ἦν μὴ οὐ δυσπουδάζειν (Xenophon Historicus)
5. μὴ οὐ with the Partic., only after a negative, expressed or implied, δυσάλγητος γὰρ ἂν εἤν μὴ οὐ κατοικτείρων I should be hard-hearted if  I did not  pity, (Sophocles Tragicus)
6. = εἰ μή, except  πόλεις χαλεπαὶ λαβεῖν, μὴ οὐ πολιορκία (Demosthenes Orator) (ML)

---

LSJ / STEPBible (TFLSJ)
μὴ οὐ
is used of an apprehended negative:

__I
with finite forms of the Verb, after Verbs expressing fear or apprehension [Refs 5th c.BC+ [compare (μή 5th c.BC: Bacchylides Lyricus 8):]]

__I.a
mostly with subjunctive, δείδω μὴ οὔ τίς τοι ὑπόσχηται τόδε ἔργον [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 10.39, compare 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 6.9, 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 3.53, 57, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Meno” 89d, etc.: after historical tenses, with _optative_, ἠθύμησάν τινες ἐννοούμενοι μὴ οὐκ ἔχοιεν ὁπόθεν λαμβάνοιεν 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 3.5.3, etc.]]: with future optative representing future indicative in indirect speech, μὴ οὐκ ὀρθῶς αὐτὸ ποιήσοις [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Euthyphro” 15d.]]

__I.b
with indicative, ὁρᾶτε μὴ οὐκ ἐμοὶ μάλιστα τῶν πολιτῶν προσήκει [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Andocides Orator 1.103, compare 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Laches” 196c, Alcaeus2.139d.]]

__I.2
without introductory Verb, with subjunctive, μή νύ τοι οὐ χραίσμῃ [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 1.28, compare 566, 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Troades” 982]]; also to suggest hesitation, perhaps [Refs 5th c.BC+ [compare (μή 5th c.BC: Bacchylides Lyricus 9), μὴ οὐ τοῦτο ᾖ τὸ χρηστήριον 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 5.79, compare 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Phaedo” 67b, “Smp.” 194c, 214c, etc.: also with _indicative_, μὴ τοῦτο οὐ καλῶς ὡμολογήσαμεν [prev. author] “Men.” 89c.]]

__I.3
μή is sometimes doubled, irregularly, for μὴ οὐ, ἐθαύμαζε δ᾽ εἴτις.. φοβοῖτο, μὴ ὁ γενόμενος καλὸς κἀγαθὸς.. μὴ τὴν μεγίστην χάριν ἔχοι [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Memorabilia” 1.2.7, compare 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 2.13.]]

__II
after a negative expressed or implied:

__II.1
with infinitive,

__II.1.a
after Verbs of hindering, denying, avoiding, needing, when these Verbs are themselves negatived or questioned, οὐκέτι ἀνεβάλλοντο μὴ οὐ τὸ πᾶν μηχανήσασθαι they no longer hesitated to try every expedient, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 6.88, compare 8.100, 119]]; τί δῆτα μέλλεις μὴ οὐ γεγωνίσκει; [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Prometheus Vinctus” 627, compare 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Ajax” 540, 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Acharnenses” 320, 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 1.4.2, 4.3.8, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Euthydemus” 304c, 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 24.24; οὐκ ἀνατίθεμαι μὴ οὐ καλῶς λέγεσθαι 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Meno” 89d, compare “Phd.” 87a; πολλοῦ δέω μὴ οὐ δύο γε φεύγειν [prev. author] “Euthd.” 297b]]; τίνος ἐνδέομεν μὴ οὐ πανσυδίᾳ χωρεῖ; [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Troades” 797 (_anapaest meter_)]]; after ὥστε, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 8.57]]: with the Article, οὐκ ἐναντιώσομαι τὸ μὴ οὐ γεγωνεῖν πᾶν [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Prometheus Vinctus” 787, compare 918, 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Tyrannus” 283, 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Phoenissae” 1176; αὐτὴν οὐ μισοῦντ᾽ ἐκείνην τὴν πόλιν τὸ μὴ οὐ μεγάλην εἶναι 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Aves” 37]]; τοῖς θεοῖς οὐδὲν ἂν ἔχοιμεν μέμψασθαι τὸ μὴ οὐχί.. [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 7.5.42, compare 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Philebus” 13a, etc.; compare μή 5th c.BC: Bacchylides Lyricus 5b.]]

__II.1.b
after Verbs and phrases signifying impossibility, impropriety, reluctance, when not negatived, ἄνδρα δ᾽ οὐκ ἔστι μὴ οὐ κακὸν ἔμμεναι [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Simonides Lyricus 5.10; δεινὸν ἐδόκεε εἶναι μὴ οὐ λαβεῖν 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.187; ἔστι οὐδεμία μηχανὴ μὴ οὐκ ἀπολωλέναι [prev. author] 2.181, compare 3.51, 7.5; οὐδεὶς ἂν τολμήσειεν μὴ οὐ χρῆσθαι τῷ νόμῳ 5th c.BC: Antipho Orator 5.87, compare 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 8.60; αἰσχύνη ἦν μὴ οὐ συσπουδάζειν 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 2.3.11; αἰσχρόν ἐστι μὴ οὐκ ἄλλας πληγὰς ἐμβάλλειν τῷ υἱεῖ [prev. author] “Lac.” 6.2]]; οὐδεὶς οἷός τ᾽ ἐστὶν ἄλλως λέγων μὴ οὐ (nemo potest non) καταγέλαστος εἶναι [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Gorgias” 509a]]: after an implied negative, μὴ οὐχὶ παντὶ τρόπῳ ἐλέγχειν μαλθακοῦ εἶναι ἀνδρός [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [[prev. author] “Phd.” 85c; μόνῃ τῇ μορφῇ μὴ οὐχὶ πρόβατα εἶναι διαφερόντων 2nd c.AD: Lucianus Sophista “Alex.” 15]]; after ὥστε, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Fragmenta” 1068, 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Respublica Atheniensium” 3.8]]; μή and μὴ οὐκ in consecutive clauses, [Refs [[prev. author] “Ap.” 34]]: with the Article, οὐκ ἀνέξομαι τὸ μὴ οὐ.. τιμᾶν [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Eumenides” 914]]; οὐδείς γέ μ᾽ ἂν πείσειεν.. τὸ μὴ οὐ.. [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Ranae” 68, compare 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Historia Graeca (Hellenica)” 5.2.36.]]

__II.2
less frequently with participle after a negative expressed or implied, οὔκων δίκαιον [ἀνδριάντα] ἱστάναι.. μὴ οὐκ ὑπερβαλλόμενον τοῖσι ἔργοισι [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 2.110, compare 6.9, 106; δυσάλγητος γὰρ ἂν εἴην τοιάνδε μὴ οὐ κατοικτείρων ἕδραν 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Tyrannus” 13, compare 221, “OC” 360, 5th-6th c.BC: Isocrates Orator 10.47 (uncertain reading), 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Lysis” 212d, 4th-3rd c.BC: Philemo Comicus 213.5: hence]]

__II.3
= {εἰ μή}, except, πόλεις.. χαλεπαὶ λαβεῖν, μὴ οὐ χρόνῳ καὶ πολιορκίᾳ [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 19.123.]]

__III
in questions expecting an affirmative answer, [LXX+NT+5th c.BC+ [LXX.Judg.14.3, NT.1Cor.9.4, 5th-4th c.BC: Aesopus Fabularum Scriptor 404.]]

3. to have sense , be sensible , (Sophocles Tragicus), etc.; περισσὰ πράσσειν οὐκ ἔχει νοῦν οὐδένα to aim too high has no sense , (Sophocles Tragicus)

Attic dialect contraction νοῦς, genitive νοῦ: [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Homerus Epicus]] uses the contraction form once, in nominative, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 10.240, compare 8th-7th c.BC: Hesiodus Epicus “Fragmenta” 205 (5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus never)]]: Trag. use contraction form, except in [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Choephori” 742 (iambic), 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Philoctetes” 1209 (Lyric poetry)]]: Aeolic dialect genitive νῶ [Refs 7th c.BC+ [7th-6th c.BC: Alcaeus Lyricus “Supp.” 9.1; _accusative_ νῶν Sapph.[prev. work]25.2; νόον Ead.70 (assuming variant)]]: irregular forms are found in “NT” and later writers, genitive νοός [LXX+NT+1st c.AD+ [NT.Rom.7.23, LXX.4Mac.1.35; _dative_ νοΐ NT.1Cor.1.10, [2nd c.AD: Aristides Rhetor] “Or.” 35(9).26; _nominative_ _plural_ νόες 1st c.AD: Philo Judaeus 1.86, 3rd c.AD: Plotinus Philosophus 6.7.17, 5th-6th c.AD: Damascius Philosophus “de Principiis” 96; _accusative_ _plural_ νόας 1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus “Fragmenta - fragment uncertainFragmenta incerta” 7.27, 4th c.AD: Iamblichus Philosophus “de Mysteriis” 1.15, 5th c.AD: Ammonius Philosophus “in Aristotelis de Interpretatione commentarius - pars” 243.3 (variant), 5th-6th c.AD: Damascius Philosophus “de Principiis” 103: _Attic dialect_ _plural_ νοῖ, _accusative_ νοῦς, _genitive_ νόων [prev. work] 122, _dative_ νοῖς [prev. passage]]], is rare in early writers, as [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Fragmenta” 471, but frequently in later philosophy:]]

__1

[Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 15.461; ν. πολυκερδέα 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 13.255; ν. ὁρῇ καὶ ν. ἀκούει, τἄλλα κωφὰ καὶ τυφλά 5th c.BC: Epicharmus Comicus 249, compare 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Tyrannus” 371]]; νόῳ prudently, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 6.320]]; παρὲκ νόον senselessly, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 20.133]]; σὺν νόῳ wisely, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 8.86, 138]]; ξὺν νῷ with play on ξυνῷ, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [1st c.AD(?): Heraclitus 114 (νόῳ codices 5th c.AD: Stobaeus, Joannes); ξὺν νῷ ἑλομένῳ 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 619b; οὐδενὶ ξὺν νῷ [prev. author] “Cri.” 48c; μηδενὶ ξὺν νῷ 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Nubes” 580; τοῦ νοῦ χωρίς 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Tyrannus” 550; τοῦ ν. κενός [prev. author] “OC” 931]]; νόῳ λαβεῖν τι to apprehend it, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 3.51]]; νόῳ σχεῖν, ἔχειν, recall, remember, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. author] 5.92.ή, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 490a; κοινὸς ν. 1st c.BC: Philodemus Gadarensis Epigrammaticus “Rh.” 1.37 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus, 2nd c.AD: Arrianus Historicus “Epicteti Dissertationes” 3.6.8]]; ἀγαθὸς ν., σπουδαῖος ν., [Refs 5th c.BC+ [1st c.BC: Philodemus Gadarensis Epigrammaticus “Rh.” 2.61, 1.252 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus]]

LSJ / STEPBible (TFLSJ)
οὐ μή,
in independent sentences, is used either in Denial or in Prohibition:

__I
in Denial,

__I.1
with subjunctive,

__I.1.a
chiefly of aorist, οὔ τι μὴ ληφθῶ δόλῳ [Refs 5th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Septem contra Thebas” 38, compare 199, 282, “Ch.” 895; οὔ τοί σ᾽ Ἀχαιῶν.. μή τις ὑβρίσῃ 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Ajax” 560, compare “El.” 42, 1029, “Ph.” 103, 381, “OT” 329, 771, “OC” 450, 1023 (see. below); οὔ τι μὴ φύγητε λαιψηρῷ ποδί 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Hecuba” 1039, compare “HF” 718; οὐ γὰρ μὴ ἀπώσηται 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.199, compare 7.53; οὐ μήποτε.. ἐσβάλωσιν 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 4.95, compare 5.69; οὐ μή ποθ᾽ ἁλῶ 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Acharnenses” 662, compare “V.” 394; οὐ μή ποτε δέξηται 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Phaedo” 105d, compare “Phdr.” 260e, “R.” 609b; οὐ μὴ κρατηθῶ 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 5.1.17, compare 3.2.8 (variant{δέξονται}), “An.” 4.8.13; so οὐδεὶς μή ποθ᾽ εὕρῃ κατ᾽ ἔμ᾽ οὐδὲν ἐλλειφθέν 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 18.246.]]

__I.1.b
rarely of present, mostly with Verbs expressing possibility or ability, οὐ μὴ δύνηται (variant{δυνήσεται}) [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 8.1.5, compare “An.” 2.2.12, “Hier.” 11.15; οὐ μὴ οἷός τ᾽ ᾖς 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 341b; οὐ γὰρ μὴ δυνατὸς ὦ [prev. author] “Phlb.” 48d: in 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Coloneus” 1023, for οὐ μή ποτε.. φυγόντες.. ἐπεύχωνται θεοῖς, two Mss. give ἐπεύξωνται]], and this has been adopted by most editions; and in [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Isaeus Orator 8.24, for οὐ μὴ εἰσίῃς Bekk. restored οὐ μὴ εἴσει εἰς..:—Note: οὐ μή]] with subjunctive probably arose from the ellipsis of a Verb or phrase expressing fear or apprehension; such words are sometimes expressed, οὐ γὰρ ἦν δεινὸν.. μὴ ἁλῷ κοτε [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.84, compare 7.235, 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Ecclesiazusae” 650, 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Memorabilia” 2.1.25, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Apologia” 28b, “Phd.” 84b, “Grg.” 520d, “R.” 465b.]]—Sts. there is no idea of fear, as in [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Philoctetes” 103, 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Iphigenia Taurica” 18]]; the construction is freely used after ὅτι, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 5.69, 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Historia Graeca (Hellenica)” 4.2.3, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 499b]]; after ὡς, since, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Aves” 461]]; after ὥστε, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Phaedrus” 227d.]]

__I.2
with future indicative, οὔ σοι μὴ μεθέψομαί ποτε [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Electra” 1052, compare “OC” 176 (Lyric poetry); οὐ μή σ᾽ ἐγὼ περιόψομαι 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Ranae” 508]]; οὐ μὴ δέξονται (variant{δέξωνται}) [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 3.2.8: the reading in [prev. author] “HG” 1.6.32 is doubtful: in indirect speech the _optative_ is used, ἐθέσπισεν ὡς οὐ μή ποτε πέρσοιεν 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Philoctetes” 611]]: or infinitive, εἶπεν.. οὐ μή ποτε.. εὖ πράξειν πόλιν [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Phoenissae” 1590.]]

__II
in Prohibition, οὐ μή is used interrogatively with future indicative (chiefly of the 2 _person_) so as to express a strong prohibition, οὐ μὴ 'ξεγερεῖς τὸν ὕπνῳ κάτοχο; ={μὴ ἐξέγειρε};_ [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Trachiniae” 978 (_anapaest meter_)]]; οὐ μὴ προσοίσεις χεῖρα μηδ᾽ ἅψῃ πέπλων ; [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Hippolytus” 606, compare 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Nubes” 296, “Ra.” 298.—The prohibition is changed into a direct command by ἀλλά or δέ, οὐ μὴ λαλήσεις ἀλλ᾽ ἀκολουθήσεις ἐμο; [prev. author] “Nu.” 505, compare “Ra.” 202, 462, 524, 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Bacchae” 792]]; οὐ μὴ προσοίσεις χεῖρα βακχεύσεις δ᾽ ἰών;[Refs [[prev. work] 343, compare “Med.” 1151, “El.” 383.]]

__II.2
later οὐ μὴ ἐμπέσω let me not fall, [LXX.2Ki.24.14.]

__II.3
in questions, οὐ μή, = Latin nonne, ὁ θεὸς οὐ μὴ ποιήσῃ τὴν ἐκδίκησιν τῶν ἐκλεκτῶν αὐτοῦ ; [NT.Luke.18.7.]

__III
in [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Septem contra Thebas” 250, οὐ σῖγα μηδὲν τῶνδ᾽ ἐρεῖς κατὰ πτόλιν]]; seems to mean keep silent and say nothing.., σῖγα being short for σιγήσει and καὶ being omitted: similarly, οὐ σῖγ᾽ ἀνέξει, μηδὲ δειλίαν ἀρῇ; submit silently and do not play the coward, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Ajax” 75, compare “Tr.” 1183, “OT” 637, 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Hippolytus” 498, “Hel.” 437, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Symposium” 175a.]]

later form for οὐδείς, οὐδέν, found in Attic dialect Inscrr. from 4th c.BC onwards along with οὐδείς, which it supersedes entirely from about 4th c.BC to 2nd c.BC (forty examples of θ, none of δ); οὐθείς is in a majority in Ptolemaic papyri up to about 2nd c.BC, after which οὐδείς begins to be common, but does not prevail until 1st c.AD; the evidence of non-Attic dialect Inscrr. is in general agreement with the {οὐθατόεις}; codices of [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus, 5th c.BC: Antipho Orator, 5th-6th c.BC: Andocides Orator, 5th c.BC: Lysias Orator, and 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus never have οὐθείς]], but the θ forms are frequently in those of [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus, 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus, 5th-6th c.BC: Isocrates Orator, 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator, 4th c.BC: Hyperides Orator, 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus, and 4th-3rd c.BC: Theophrastus Philosophus]], frequently as variants for the δ forms; also in Hellenistic writers, [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [3rd c.BC: Teles Philosophus, 2nd c.BC: Polybius Historicus, etc.]]; the frequency of θ forms in the uncials of [Refs [LXX varies roughly according to the date (known or probable)]] of the translation of the book in question (though the δ forms are in a large majority in the [Refs [LXX as a whole)]]; the θ forms are rare in codices of [Refs 1st c.BC+ [1st c.BC-1st c.AD: Strabo Geographus]] and later writers.

2. at Athens, a Prytanis  or President : the πρυτάνεις were a committee of 50, chosen by lot from each of the 10 φυλαί, so that each set formed 1/10 part of the βουλή or Council of 500; out of these 50 πρυτάνεις one was chosen by lot as chief-president  ἐπιστάτης);  he chose 9 πρόεδρο; and the real business was in the hands of this smaller body, with a secretary  γραμματεύς); added.—;The φυλή which first entered office every year was determined by lot; and their term of office  πρυτανεία); was about five weeks. LSJ / STEPBible (TFLSJ)
τεῦχος, εος, τό,
(τεύχω) properly tool, implement:—but mostly in plural τεύχεα,

__I
implements of war, armour, arms, frequently in Epic dialect; more precisely, ἀρήϊα τεύχεα, πολεμήϊα τ., [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 14.381, 7.193; χρύσεια, χαλκήρεα, 10.439, 15.544; ποικίλα, αἰόλα παμφανόωντα, μαρμαίροντα, 3.327, 5.295, 18.617]]; always of a warrior's whole armour, harness, ἀρήϊα τεύχεα δύω [Refs 8th c.BC+ [6.340, compare 7.193, +others; ἐς τεύχε᾽ ἔδυνον 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 24.498; κατὰ τεύχε᾽ ἔδυν 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 4.222, compare 6.504, +others; Πάτροκλον περὶ τεύχεα ἕσσε 18.451; ἀπέδυσε, ἐξεδύοντο, 4.532, 3.114, compare 13.182, +others]]; also χαλκήρεα τεύχε᾽ ἀπ᾽ ὤμων συλήσειν [Refs 5th c.BC+ [15.544; Ἕκτορι δ᾽ ἥρμοσε τεύχε᾽ ἐπὶ χροΐ 17.210: Trag. τεύχη 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Myrm.” in “PSI” 11.1211.17, 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Ajax” 572, 577, 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Andromache” 617, etc.]]; un contraction τεύχεα [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Philoctetes” 398 (Lyric poetry).]]

__I.2
plural also, the gear of a ship, oars and the like, ἐγκοσμεῖτε τὰ τ. νηΐ μελαίνῃ [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 15.218; τ. δέ σφ᾽ ἀπένεικαν 16.326.]]

__II
in Trag. (rarely in Prose, see below) a vessel of any kind, e.g. bathing-tub, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Agamemnon” 1128 (Lyric poetry, Blomf. κύτει, for the sake of meter)]]; cinerary urn, τεύχη καὶ σποδός [Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. work] 435 (Lyric poetry),compare 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Electra” 1114, 1120, “Riv.Fil.” 57.379 (from Crete)]]; balloting-urn, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Agamemnon” 815, “Eu.” 742]]; vase for libations, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [[prev. author] “Ch.” 99, 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Iphigenia Taurica” 168 (Lyric poetry)]]; vase or ewer for water, [Refs [[prev. author] “Hec.” 609, “Andr.” 167, Diocl.fragment 129]]; cup, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Ion” 1184]]; amphora, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Fragmenta - American Journal of Philology” 108]]; scent-pot, [Refs [[prev. work] 180.5 (_plural_)]]; matula, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Fragmenta” 565]]; pot or jar, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 5.4.28]]; ξύλινα τ. chests, [Refs [[prev. work] 7.5.14]]; ἀλφίτων τ. a meal-barrel, [Refs [[prev. author] “HG” 1.7.11]]; bee-hive, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Historia Animalium” 625a26]]; capsule of a poppy, [Refs 2nd c.BC+ [2nd c.BC: Nicander Epicus “fragment” 74.52.]]

__III
in Medicine texts, of the vessels of the body, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Hippocrates Medicus “περὶ τόπων τῶν κατὰ ἄνθρωπον” 1, 24]]; also, the human frame, body, as holding the intestines, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [[prev. author] “Epid.” 6.2.1, 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Physiognomonica” 810b19]]; τεῦχος νεοσσῶν λευκόν an egg, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Helena” 258.]]

__IV
case for holding papyrus rolls, ά τεύχους, ά τόμου, κολλήματος ρδ᾽ [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [“PRyl.” 220.78 (2nd c.AD)]]; roll of writing-material, πεποίηται διπλῆν τὴν.. ἀναγραφὴν ἐν βυβλίνοις καὶ δερματίνοις τεύχεσιν [Refs 1st c.BC+ [“Inscription Prien.” 114.30, compare 11 (1st c.BC)]]; κελεύσας εἰς τάξιν ἀποδοῦναι τὰ τ. Aristeas 179; καθὼς ἀνεγνώσθη τὰ τ. [LXX+1st c.BC+ [[prev. author] 310, compare 2nd-3rd c.AD: Symmachus LXX.Isa.8.1 (where LXX has τόμος); βίβλων.. ἐν τεύχεϊ τῷδε πεντάς “Anthologia Graeca” 9.239 (1st c.BC-1st c.AD: Crinagoras Epigrammaticus); τ. βιβλειδίων “BGU” 970.4 (2nd c.AD)]]; τ. συγκολλησίμων βιβλειδίων [Refs 3rd c.AD+ [“POxy.” 2131.4 (3rd c.AD)]]; τ. = volumen, [Refs [“Corpus Glossariorum Latinorum”: hence πεντάτευχος, ὀκτάτευχος.]]

__V
masonry, fabric, ἀνεκτίσθη τὸ τ. τοῦτο [Refs 6th c.AD+ [“Sammelb.” 7439.7 (6th c.AD).]]

__II.2

__II.3
subject of a poem or treatise, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-3rd c.BC: Zeno Citieus Stoicus 1.23, 2nd c.BC: Polybius Historicus 1.2.1, 1st c.BC: Dionysius Halicarnassensis “Epistula ad Pompeium” 3, 3rd c.AD: Longinus Rhetor 38.2, 1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus “Pompeius” 42, 2nd c.AD: Lucianus Sophista “Charid.” 14, “Pseudol.” 5, +others]]; of a picture, [Refs [[prev. author] “Zeux.” 5, 7]]; of an impromptu declamation, ἐπειδὰν οἱ παρόντες ὑποβάλωσί τινας ὑ. καὶ ἀφορμὰς λόγου [Refs [[prev. author] “Rh.Pr.” 18]]; plot, story, μῦθοι καὶ ὑποθέσεις [Refs 5th c.BC+ [1st c.BC: Philodemus Philosophus “περὶ ποιημάτων” 2.62, compare 5.5, +others, argument 4th-3rd c.BC: Menander Comicus “Oxy.” 1235.113 (2nd c.AD), 4th c.BC: Dicaearchus Geographus cited in 2nd c.AD: Sextus Empiricus Philosophus “adversus Mathematicos” 3.3, 2nd c.AD: Artemidorus Daldianus Onirocriticus 4.59, Scholia 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Aj.Prooem.”, argument 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Ach.” at Title Page, etc.]]

__II.4
speech, αἱ δικανικαὶ καὶ δημηγορικαὶ ὑ. [LXX+1st c.AD+ [1st-2nd c.AD(?): Theon Rhetor “Progymnasmata - Rhet.” 1; ={ἐπίδειξις} I.3, ἀρξαμένων (variant{-ῳ}) τῆς ὑ. LXX.4Mac.1.12]]; ἀνδρὸς ἀρετὰς ὅλην πληρούσας ὑ. providing matter for a whole speech, [Refs [Chor. p.34B.]]

__II.4.b
speech or subject of a speech in which the person, occasion, etc. are particularized, opposed to θέσις see[Refs 1st c.AD+ [2, 4th-5th c.AD: Aphthonius Rhetor “Προγυμνάσματα - Rhet.” 13, compare 1st c.AD: Quintilianus Rhetor Latinus “Inst.” 3.5.7.]]

__II.5
a kind of play or pantomime, μῖμοί τινές εἰσιν ὧν τοὺς μὲν ὑποθέσεις τοὺς δὲ παίγνια καλοῦσιν [Refs 1st c.AD+ [1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus 2.712e]]; μιμολωγοι η υποθησις εικυρα (i. e. μιμολόγοι· ἡ ὑπόθεσις Ἑκυρά), i. e. 'theatrical performance: play, the Hecyra', [Refs 3rd c.BC+ [“Ath.Mitt.” 26.4 (inscription on lamp, 3rd c.BC)]]; κλάειν ἤρξαντο πάντες καὶ μετέβαλε τὸ συμπόσιον εἰς σκυθρωπὴν ὑ. into a tragedy, [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd c.AD(?): Charito Scriptor Eroticus 4.3; so perhaps in 2nd c.AD: Lucianus Sophista “Nigr.” 8]]; of Aesop's fables, χρῆται [τῇ ἀλώπεκι] ὁ Αἴσωπος διακόνῳ τῶν πλείστων ὑ. [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd-3rd c.AD: Philostratus Sophista “Philostrati majoris imagines” 1.3.]]

__III
supposition, ἢ βούλεσθε.. ἀπ᾽ ἐμαυτοῦ ἄρξωμαι καὶ τῆς ἐμαυτοῦ ὑ., περὶ τοῦ ἑνὸς αὐτοῦ ὑποθέμενος, εἴτε ἕν ἐστιν εἴτε μὴ ἕν, τί χρὴ συμβαίνει; [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Parmenides” 137b; αὕτη ἡ ὑ., εἰ ἓν μὴ ἔστιν [prev. work] 160b; χρὴ.. μὴ μόνον εἰ ἔστιν ἕκαστον ὑποτιθέμενον σκοπεῖν τὰ συμβαίνοντα ἐκ τῆς ὑ., ἀλλὰ καὶ εἰ μὴ ἔστι τὸ αὐτὸ τοῦτο ὑποτίθεσθαι [prev. work] 135e, compare 136a]]; [σκοπεῖν] τί ἐφ᾽ ἑκατέρας τῆς ὑ. συμβήσεται[Refs 4th c.BC+ [[prev. work] 136b; εἰ ὀρθὴ ἡ ὑ. ἦν, τὸ ψυχὴν ἁρμονίαν εἶναι [prev. author] “Phd.” 94b, compare 92d, “Sph.” 244c; πρὸς μὲν τὴν ὑ. ὀρθῶς λέγουσιν, ὅλως δ᾽ οὐκ ὀρθῶς 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Metaphysica” 1082b32]]; ἐξ ὑποθέσεως σκοπεῖσθαι examine by starting from an assumption, of reasoning by analysis in geometry, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Meno” 86e]]; τῶν τὴν τέχνην ζητεύντων ἐξ ὑποθέσιος λόγων arguments seeking to derive the (medical) art from an assumption, [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th c.BC: Hippocrates Medicus “περὶ ἀρχαίης ἰητρικῇς” 13; ὑ. αὐτοὶ αὑτοῖς ὑποθέμενοι τῷ λόγῳ [prev. work] 1]]; ἄγοντες ἐπὶ ὑπόθεσιν τὴν τέχνην[Refs 4th c.BC+ [[prev. work] 15; χρῆσιν ἀρετῆς τελείαν, καὶ ταύτην οὐκ ἐξ ὑ. ἀλλ᾽ ἁπλῶς· λέγω δ᾽ ἐξ ὑ. τἀναγκαῖα, οἷον.. τιμωρίαι καὶ κολάσεις.. τὸ καλῶς ἀναγκαίως ἔχουσι 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Politica” 1332810]]; ἡ πολιτεία ἡ ἐξ ὑ. (={ἡ δοθεῖσα}) the constitution based on a presupposition, [Refs [[prev. work] 1288b28]]; of currency, ἓν δή τι δεῖ εἶναι, τοῦτο δ᾽ ἐξ ὑ.· διὸ νόμισμα καλεῖται according to a presupposed convention, [Refs [[prev. author] “EN” 1133b21 (compare a29 - 31, “APr.” 41a40)]]; of reductio ad impossibile, ἢ δεικτικῶς ἢ ἐξ ὑ. τοῦ δ᾽ ἐξ ὑ. μέρος τὸ διὰ τοῦ ἀδυνάτου [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [[prev. author] “APr.” 40b25 - 6, compare 41a25; δυνατοῦ δεξάμενον ὑπόθεσιν ἐπ᾽ ἀδύνατον ἀπαχθῆναι 2nd c.AD: Arrianus Historicus “Epicteti Dissertationes” 1.7.25, compare 5th c.AD: Proclus Philosophus “in primum Euclidis librum commentarius” pp.76,252 F.]]; καθ᾽ ὑπόθεσιν by way of supposition, 'let us suppose', [Refs 5th c.BC+ [1st c.BC: Philodemus Gadarensis Epigrammaticus “Rh.” 1.95 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus, “Sign.” 12, 2nd c.AD: Cleomedes Astronomus 1.7.]]

__IV
={τὸ ὑποκείμενον} [Refs [compare (ὑπόκειμαι 11.8)]], the presupposition of an action, that which has been settled before it begins, περὶ τοῦ τέλους οὐθεὶς βουλεύεται, ἀλλὰ τοῦτ᾽ ἐστὶν ἀρχὴ καὶ ὑ. [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Ethica Eudemia” 1227a8, compare b30; τῶν πράξεων τὰς ἀρχὰς καὶ τὰς ὑ. ἀληθεῖς καὶ δικαίας εἶναι προσήκει 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 2.10]]; of a thing, that without which it cannot exist or be what it is, its essence, αὕτη (i.e. τὸ στέλεχος) οἷον ὑ. καὶ φύσις δένδρων [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th-3rd c.BC: Theophrastus Philosophus “Historia Plantarum” 4.13.4 (compare οὐσία καὶ φύσις τοῦ δένδρου [prev. passage])]]; ἐπὶ τοῖς χυμοῖς μόνοις σηπομένοις ἔχοντος τὴν ὑ. ὅλου τοῦ νοσήματος, ὅπερ ἐστὶ πυρετώδους ὄντος [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd c.AD: Galenus Medicus 18(2).299.]]

__IV.2
in the syllogism, the preliminary statements of fact (whether proved or not) from which inference starts, i. e. the premisses (προτάσεις), τῶν ἀποδείξεων αἱ ὑ., equivalent to ἀρχαί, [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Metaphysica” 1013a16; αἱ ἀρχαὶ καὶ αἱ λεγόμεναι ὑ. [prev. work]17; ὑπόθεσιν, αἴτησιν οὖσαν πράγματος εἰς κατασκευήν τινος 2nd c.AD: Sextus Empiricus Philosophus “adversus Mathematicos” 3.4; λαμβάνειν ἀναποδείκτους ὑ. 1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus 2.720f, compare 721d; ἀναγκαῖον ἢ τὰς ὑ. εἶναι τὰς πρώτας ψευδεῖς, ἢ τὰς ὑπὲρ τῶν συμβαινόντων ἀποφάς εις 2nd c.BC: Polybius Historicus 1.15.9, compare 11.]]

__IV.2.b
assumption of existence of any one of the fundamental objects of a particular science, ὁ ὁρισμὸς θέσις μέν ἐστι.. ὑ. δ᾽ οὐκ ἔστι· τὸ γὰρ τί ἐστι μονὰς καὶ τὸ εἶναι μονάδα οὐ ταὐτόν [Refs 4th c.BC+ [4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Analytica Posteriora” 72a23; ἐν ταῖς πράξεσι τὸ οὗ ἕνεκα ἀρχή, ὥσπερ ἐν τοῖς μαθηματικοῖς αἱ ὑ. [prev. author] “EN” 1151a17.]]

__IV.3
starting-point, ἐκ ταύτης τῆς ὑ. λαβεῖν τὸν λόγον τὴν εἰς ἑκάτερον μέρος ὁρμήν [Refs 4th c.AD+ [4th c.AD: Iamblichus Philosophus “de vita Pythagorica” 27.130]]; beginning, τὰς μὲν ἐλπίδας οὐ τελειοῖ (i.e. ὁ ὄνειρος), τὰς δὲ ὑ. τῶν πραγμάτων ταῖς περιοχαῖς ὁμοίας ποιεῖ (referring to a birth of twins which died), [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd c.AD: Artemidorus Daldianus Onirocriticus 4.47.]]

__IV.4
raw material, τὴν δοθεῖσαν ὑ. εὐφυᾶ πρὸς ὑποδοχὴν γυμναστικῆς.. ἀμείνω ἀποφαίνειν [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd c.AD: Lucianus Sophista “Hist. Conscr.” 35; οἵαν ὕλην καὶ ὑ. φεύγεις·.. μένε οὖν μέχρι ἐξοικειώσῃς σαυτῷ καὶ ταῦτα 2nd c.AD: Marcus Antoninus Imperator 10.31.]]

__V

__VI

__VI.2
thing placed under, base, τὰς ὑ.[Refs 5th c.BC+ [(signification 111) ποιούμενος οὐκ ἀρχὰς ἀλλὰ τῷ ὄντι ὑ., οἷον ἐπιβάσεις τε καὶ ὁρμάς 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 511b, compare 2nd c.AD: Arrianus Historicus “Epicteti Dissertationes” 1.7.22; in 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 2.10 (see. supr. in early Prose writers only used in such phrases as τοῖος ἢ τοῖος [Refs 5th c.BC+ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 429b, 437e; τοῖα καὶ τοῖα [prev. author] “Phdr.” 271d, cf. 3rd c.AD: Longinus Rhetor 27.1; οἱ μὲν τ. οἱ δὲ τ. 4th-3rd c.BC: Epicurus Philosophus “Epistulae” 1p.14U., cf. 2nd c.AD: Arrianus Historicus “Epicteti Dissertationes” 3.16.11; οὐ μᾶλλον τοῖον ἢ τοῖον εἶναι 1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus 2.1108f, +others]]: in late Prose used alone, [Refs 2nd c.AD+ [2nd c.AD: Sextus Empiricus Philosophus “Πυρρώνειοι ὑποτυπώσεις” 1.228, “M.” 7.197, 2nd-3rd c.AD: Aelianus “De Natura Animalium - Ar.Byzantine Epit.” 1.41, “POxy.” 903.14 (4th c.AD).]]

__II
τοῖος with infinitive, such as to do, i. e. fit or able to do, τοῖοι ἀμυνέμεν [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 2.60: cf. οἷος 111.]]

__III
with an adjective of the same gender and case, it emphasizes the sense of the adjective, so very, just.., ἐπιεικέα τοῖον just of moderate size, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 23.246]]; πέλαγος μέγα τοῖον a sea so large, [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 3.321]]; κερδαλέον δὴ τ. so very knowing, [Refs [15.451]]; still stronger, ἀβληχρὸς μάλα τ. so exceeding gentle, [Refs [11.135, 23.282; μείδησε.. σαρδάνιον μάλα τ. 20.302: rarely with _superlative_, τ. μέγιστος δοῦπος]] variant in [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th-7th c.BC: Hesiodus Epicus “Theogonia” 703.]]

__IV
in late Epic dialect, = {οἷος}, [Refs 2nd c.BC+ [2nd c.BC: Nicander Epicus “Theriaca” 762, “Al.” 232, 293.]]

__V
neuter τοῖον as adverb, thus, so much, τοῖον γὰρ ὑποτρομέουσι [Refs 8th c.BC+ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 22.241, cf. 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 3.496]]; θάμα τ. ever so often,[Refs 3rd c.BC+ [1.209; ἀλλ᾽ ἴθι σιγῇ τ. 7.30, cf. 4.776: in later _Epic dialect_ τοίως, 3rd c.BC: Theocritus Poeta Bucolicus 24.72 codices, 3rd c.BC: Apollonius Rhodius Epicus 3.1399.]]

__VI
[Refs 8th c.BC+ [Scholia 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 7.231 (v. supr. 1.1) has οἱ γλωσσογράφοι τὸ τοῖοι ἀντὶ τοῦ ἀγαθοί· ὅθεν καὶ Καλλίμαχος τῷ τοίων δεῖ κέχρηται.]]

§ Darius = "lord"
1) Darius the Mede, the son of Ahasuerus, king of the Chaldeans, who succeeded to the Babylonian kingdom on the death of Belshazzar; probably the same as "Astyages" the last king of the Medes (538 BC)

deep_entry:
STEPBible TBESH (Hebreiska)
A man of the tribe of Levi  living at the time of Exile and Return, first mentioned at 1Ch.9.21;
son of: Meshelemiah (H4920);
brother of: Jediael (H3043J), Zebadiah (H2069J), Jathniel (H3496), Elam (H5867H), Jehohanan (H3076I) and Eliehoenai (H0454A)
§ Zechariah = "Jehovah remembers"
1) king of Israel, son of Jeroboam II
2) son of Meshelemiah of Shelemiah, a Korhite, and keeper of the north gate of the tabernacle of the congregation
3) one of the sons of Jehiel
4) a Levite of the second order in the temple band in the time of David
5) one of the princes of Judah in the reign of Jehoshaphat
6) son of the high priest Jehoiada, in the reign of Joash king of Judah, who was stoned in the court of the temple
7) a Kohathite Levite in the reign of Josiah
8) the leader of the sons of Pharosh who returned with Ezra
9) son of Bebai
10) one of the chiefs of the people whom Ezra summoned in council at the river Ahava; stood at Ezra's left hand when Ezra expounded the law to the people
11) one of the family of Elam who had married a foreign wife after the captivity
12) ancestor of Athaiah or Uthai
13) a Shilonite, descendant of Perez, grandfather of Athaiah
14) a priest, son of Pashur
15) the representative of the priestly family of Iddo in the days of Joiakim the son of Jeshua; possibly the same as 1 above
16) one of the priests, son of Jonathan, who blew with the trumpets at the dedication of the city wall by Ezra and Nehemiah
17) a chief of the Reubenites at the time of the captivity by Tiglath-pileser
18) one of the priests who accompanied the ark from the house of Obed-edom
19) son of Isshiah of Jesiah, a Kohathite Levite descended from Uzziel
20) 4th son of Hosah, of the children of Merari
21) a Manassite, father of Iddo
22) father of Jahaziel. He prophesied in the spirit
23) one of the sons of Jehoshaphat
24) a prophet in the reign of Uzziah, who appears to have acted as the king's counsellor, but of whom nothing is known
25) father of Abijah or Abi, Hezekiah's mother
26) one of the family of Asaph in the reign of Hezekiah
27) one of the rulers of the temple in the reign of Josiah
28) son of Jeberechiah who was taken by the prophet Isaiah as one of the 'faithful witnesses to record' when he wrote concerning Maher-shalal-hash-baz

§ Zerah or Zarah = "rising"
1) a son of Reuel and grandson of Esau, one of the dukes of the Edomites
2) twin brother of Pharez, sons of Judah and Tamar; descendants are called Zarhites, Ezrahites, and Izrahites
3) son of Simeon; also called 'Zohar'
4) a Gershonite Levite, son of Iddo of Adaiah
5) the Ethiopian or Cushite, invader of Judah in the reign of Asa who defeated the invaders; probably the same as the Egyptian king Usarken I, second king of the Egyptian 22nd dynasty or perhaps more probably Usarken II, his 2nd successor
6) another Edomite leader; possibly same as 1

deep_entry:
STEPBible TBESH (Hebreiska)
A man living at the time of Divided Monarchy, first mentioned at Jer.28.1;
son of: Azzur (H5809H)
§ Hananiah = "God has favoured"
1) the godly friend of Daniel whom Nebuchadnezzar renamed Shadrach; one of the three friends who with Daniel refused to make themselves unclean by eating food from the king's table which went against the dietary laws which God had given the Jews; also one of the three who were thrown into the fiery furnace for refusing to bow down to a graven image of Nebuchadnezzar and who were saved by the angel of the Lord. See also, 'Shadrach' (H07714 or H07715)
2) one of the 14 sons of Heman and chief of the 16th course
3) a general in the army of King Uzziah
4) father of Zedekiah in the time of Jehoiakim
5) son of Azur, a Benjamite of Gibeon and a false prophet in the reign of Zedekiah king of Judah
6) grandfather of Irijah, the captain of the ward at the gate of Benjamin who arrested Jeremiah on the charge of deserting to the Chaldeans
7) a head of a Benjamite house
8) son of Zerubbabel from whom Christ derived His descent also called 'Joanna' by Luke
9) one of the sons of Bebai who returned with Ezra from Babylon
10) a priest, one of the makers of the sacred ointments and incense, who built a portion of the wall of Jerusalem in the days of Nehemiah
11) head of the priestly course of Jeremiah in the days of Joiakim
12) ruler of the palace at Jerusalem under Nehemiah and also, along with Hanani, the Tirshatha's brother, entrusted with the arrangements of guarding the gates of Jerusalem
13) Two post exilic Israelites

§ Jehoram or Joram = "Jehovah is exalted"

2) son of king Ahab of the northern kingdom of Israel and king of Israel himself for 12 years; he was murdered by Jehu on the plot of land for which his father had murdered Naboth thus fulfilling the prophecy of Elijah to the very letter
3) a priest in the reign of Jehoshaphat

A man of the tribe of Reuben  living at the time of Divided Monarchy, only mentioned at 1Ch.5.7
§ Jeiel or Jehiel = "God sweeps away"
1) one of the sons of Adonikam who returned from exile with Ezra
2) a chief Reubenite of the house of Joel
3) a Merarite Levite and a gatekeeper to the tabernacle who also played the harp and psaltery in the service before the ark
4) one of the chiefs of the Levites in the time of king Josiah
5) one of the sons of Nebo who took a foreign wife in the time of Ezra
6) a man of Gibeon and ancestor of king Saul
7) one of the sons of Hotham the Aroerite and one of David's mighty warriors
8) the scribe of king Uzziah who kept the account of the king's irregular predatory warriors
9) a Gershonite Levite of the sons of Elizaphan
10) a Gershonite Levite of the sons of Asaph and forefather of Jahaziel in the time of king Jehoshaphat

§ Micah or Micaiah or Michah = "who is like God"
1) the 6th in order of the minor prophets; a native of Moresheth, he prophesied during the reigns of Jotham, Ahaz, and Hezekiah of Judah, and was contemporary with the prophets Hosea, Amos, and Isaiah
2) an Ephraimite during the period of the judges
3) a descendant of Joel the Reubenite
4) son of Meribbaal and grandson of Jonathan
5) a Kohathite Levite, the eldest son of Uzziel the brother of Amram
6) father of Abdon, a man of high station in the reign of Josiah
7) son of Imlah and a prophet of Samaria who predicted the defeat and death of king Ahab of Israel

STEPBible TBESH (Hebreiska)
A man of the tribe of Levi living at the time of Divided Monarchy, only mentioned at 1Ch.6.40;
son of: Jeatherai (H2979);
father of: Baaseiah (H1202)
§ Malchijah or Malchiah or Melchiah = "my king is Jehovah"
1) the father of Pashur in the time of Jeremiah
2) the son of Hammelech into whose dungeon Jeremiah was cast
3) the head of the 5th course of priests in the time of David
4) one of the priests who was at the reading of the law by Ezra, sealed the covenant with Nehemiah, and was at the dedication of the wall with Nehemiah
5) a Levite ancestor of Asaph and descendant of Levi through Gershon
6) son of Parosh who put away a foreign wife in the time of Ezra
7) son of Harim who put away a foreign wife and helped repair the wall and the Tower of Ovens in the time of Ezra and Nehemiah
8) son of Rechab, leader of the district of Beth Haccerem, who helped repair the Refuse Gate in the time of Nehemiah
9) a goldsmith who helped repair the wall in the time of Nehemiah

deep_entry:
STEPBible TBESH (Hebreiska)
A man living at the time of Divided Monarchy, first mentioned at 1Ch.15.18
§ Maaseiah = "work of Jehovah"
1) a descendant of Jeshua who had taken a foreign wife in the time of Ezra
2) a priest of the sons of Harim who had taken a foreign wife in the time of Ezra
3) a priest of the sons of Pashur who had taken a foreign wife in the time of Ezra
4) a descendant of Pahath-moab who had taken a foreign wife in the time of Ezra
5) father of Azariah
6) one who stood on the right hand of Ezra when he read the law to the people
7) a Levite who assisted when Ezra read the law to the people
8) one of the heads of the people whose descendants signed the covenant with Nehemiah
9) a Benjamite ancestor of Sallu
10) a priest who took part in the musical service at the dedication of the wall of Jerusalem under Ezra
11) another priest who took part in the musical service at the dedication of the wall of Jerusalem under Ezra
12) father of Zephaniah the prophet in the reign of Zedekiah
13) father of Zedekiah the false prophet in the time of Jeremiah
14) a Levite of the 2nd rank who David appointed to sound with psalteries on Alamoth
15) son of Adaiah and one of the captains of hundreds in the reign of king Joash of Judah
16) an officer of high rank in the reign of king Uzziah
17) son of king Ahaz of Judah who was killed by Zichri in the invasion of Judah by king Pekah of Israel
18) governor of Jerusalem in the reign of Josiah
19) son of Shallum and a Levite of high rand in the reign of king Jehoiakim of Judah
20) ancestor of Baruch and Seraiah and a priest

STEPBible TBESH (Hebreiska)
A man living at the time of Divided Monarchy, only mentioned at 2Ki.22.3;
father of: Azaliah (H0683)
§ Meshullam = "friend"
1) grandfather of Shaphan, the scribe
2) son of Zerubbabel
3) a Benjamite of the sons of Elpaal
4) a Benjamite, father of Sallu
5) a Benjamite who lived at Jerusalem after the captivity
6) a Benjamite
6a) perhaps the same as 3 or 4
7) a Gadite in the reign of king Jotham of Judah
8) son of Berechiah who assisted in rebuilding the wall of Jerusalem
9) son of Besodeiah who assisted Jehoiada the son of Paseah in restoring the old gate of Jerusalem
10) a chief of the people who sealed the covenant with Nehemiah
11) father of Hilkiah and high priest probably in the reign of king Amon of Judah
11a) perhaps the same as 'Shallum'
12) a priest, son of Meshillemith or Meshillemoth, son of Immer, and ancestor of Maasiai or Amashai
13) a priest or family of priests who sealed the covenant with Nehemiah
14) a priest, head of the family of Ginnethon and representative of the house of Ezra in the days of Joiakim, the son of Jeshua
15) a priest, one of the princes of Judah at the dedication of the wall of Jerusalem
16) a Kohathite or family of Kohathite Levites in the reign of Josiah
17) a Levite, one of the heads sent to Iddo to gather the Levites to join the caravan about to return to Jerusalem; a chief man who assisted Ezra in abolishing the marriages which some of the people had made with foreign wives
18) ancestor of a family of porters or Levites in days of Nehemiah
19) a descendant of Bani who had a foreign wife and put her away
20) one of the men who stood at the left hand of Ezra when he read the law to the people
20a) maybe the same as 17

STEPBible TBESH (Hebreiska)
A man of the tribe of Judah living at the time of United Monarchy, first mentioned at 2Sa.5.14;
son of: David (H1732) and Bathsheba (H1339);
brother of: Shammua (H8051H), Shobab (H7727) and Solomon (H8010);
half-brother of: Amnon (H0550), Chileab (H3609), Absalom (H0053), Adonijah (H0138), Shephatiah (H8203), Ithream (H3507), Ibhar (H2984), Elishua (H0474), Nepheg (H5298H), Japhia (H3309I), Elishama (H0476H), Eliada (H0450), Eliphelet (H0467), Tamar (H8559H), Elpelet (H0467I), Nogah (H5052) and Jerimoth (H3406N);
father of: Mattatha (G3160)
Also named: Nathan (Ναθάν "Nathan" G3481)
§ Nathan = "giver"
1) a son of David by Bathsheba
2) the eminent prophet in the time of David and Solomon
3) a man of Zobah, father of one of David's mighty warriors
4) father of Azariah who was over the officers of Solomon
5) son of Attai and father of Zabad of the tribe of Judah
6) brother of Joel of the tribe of Judah
7) one of the head men who returned from Babylon with Ezra
8) a man with a foreign wife in the time of Ezra
9) head of a family of Israel who shall mourn when they look on Him whom they pierced

§ Obadiah = "servant of Jehovah"
1) the 4th of the 12 minor prophets; nothing personal is known of him but it is probable that he was contemporary with Jeremiah, Ezekiel, and Daniel
1a) the prophetic book by him; prophesies against Edom
2) father of Ishmaiah, one of the chiefs of Zebulun in the time of David
3) a Merarite Levite overseer of the work of restoring the temple in the time of king Josiah of Judah
4) chief of the household of king Ahab of Israel; an devout worshipper of Jehovah who at risk to his own life hid over 100 prophets during the persecution of Jezebel
5) a descendant of David
6) a chief of the tribe of Issachar
7) a Benjamite, one of the 6 sons of Azel and a descendant of king Saul
8) a Levite, son of Shemaiah and a descendant of Jeduthun
9) a Gadite chief, the 2nd of the lion-faced Gadites who joined David at Ziklag
10) a prince of Judah in the time of king Jehoshaphat of Judah
11) a priest, son of Jehiel of the sons of Joab who returned from exile with Ezra
12) a gatekeeper in the time of Nehemiah
13) one of the men who sealed the covenant with Nehemiah
13a) perhaps the same as 12

deep_entry:
STEPBible TBESH (Hebreiska)
A man of the tribe of Levi living at the time of United Monarchy, first mentioned at 1Ki.4.2;
son of: Ahimaaz (H0290H);
father of: Johanan (H3110J)
§ Azariah = "Jehovah has helped"
1) son of king Amaziah of Judah and king of Judah himself for 52 years; also 'Uzziah'
2) the godly friend of Daniel who Nebuchadnezzar renamed Abednego; one of the three friends who with Daniel refused to make themselves unclean by eating food from the king's table which went against the dietary laws which God had given the Jews; also one of the three who were thrown into the fiery furnace for refusing to bow down to a graven image of Nebuchadnezzar and who were saved by the angel of the Lord
2a) also, 'Abednego' (H5664 or H5665)
3) son of Nathan and an officer of Solomon; perhaps David's grandson and Solomon's nephew
4) a prophet in the days of king Asa of Judah
5) son of king Jehoshaphat of Judah and brother to 5
6) another son of king Jehoshaphat of Judah and brother to 4
7) a priest, son of Ahimaaz, grandson of Zadok and high priest in the reign of king Solomon
8) the high priest in the reign of king Uzziah of Judah
9) a priest who sealed the covenant with Nehemiah; probably same as 18
10) a Kohathite Levite, father of Joel in the reign of king Hezekiah of Judah
11) a Merarite Levite, son of Jehalelel in the reign of king Hezekiah of Judah
12) a Kohathite Levite, son of Zephaniah and ancestor of Samuel the prophet
13) a Levite who helped Ezra in instructing the people in the law
14) son of Jeroham and one of the temple captains of Judah in the time of queen Athaliah; probably the same as 21
15) son of Maaseiah who repaired part of the wall of Jerusalem in the time of Nehemiah
16) one of the leaders who returned from Babylon with Zerubbabel
17) a man who assisted in the dedication of the wall of Jerusalem in the time of Nehemiah; probably the same as 10
18) son of Johanan, one of the captains of Ephraim in the reign of king Ahaz of Judah
19) a Judaite, son of Ethan of the sons of Zerah
20) a Judaite, son of Jehu of the family of the Jerahmeelites and descended from Jarha the Egyptian slave of Sheshan; probably one of the captains of the time of queen Athaliah and the same as 15
21) a priest, son of Hilkiah
22) a priest, son of Johanan
23) son of king Jehoram of Judah; probably clerical error for 'Ahaziah'
24) son of Meraioth
25) son of Hoshaiah and one of the proud men who confronted Jeremiah

deep_entry:
STEPBible TBESH (Hebreiska)
A man living at the time of Exile and Return, first mentioned at Dan.1.6; also called Shadrach at Dan.1.7; 2.49; 3.12,13,14,16,19,20,22,23,26,28,29,30;
Another name of cha.nan.yah (חֲנַנְיָ֫הוּ "Hananiah" H2608T)
§ Shadrach = "royal" or "the great scribe"
1) the godly friend of Daniel whom Nebuchadnezzar renamed Shadrach; one of the three friends who with Daniel refused to make themselves unclean by eating food from the king's table which went against the dietary laws which God had given the Jews; also one of the three who were thrown into the fiery furnace for refusing to bow down to a graven image of Nebuchadnezzar and who were saved by the angel of the Lord
1a) also, 'Hananiah' (H2608L)
source_notes: STEPBible TBESH (CC BY)

deep_entry:
STEPBible TBESH (Hebreiska)
A king of the Kingdom of Israel, living at the time of Divided Monarchy, first mentioned at 2Ki.15.10;
son of: Jabesh (H3003H)
§ Shallum = "retribution"
1) son of Jabesh, conspirator and slayer of king Zachariah of the northern kingdom of Israel ending the dynasty of Jehu; assumed the throne and became the 15th king of the northern kingdom; reigned for one month and was killed by Menahem
2) the 3rd son of king Josiah of Judah and subsequent king of Judah; reigned for 3 months before he was taken captive to Egypt where he was placed in chains and later died
2a) also 'Jehoahaz'
3) husband of Huldah the prophetess in the reign of king Josiah of Judah. Maybe the same as 4
4) uncle of Jeremiah the prophet. Maybe the same as 3
5) a Simeonite, son of Shaul and grandson of Simeon
6) a Judaite, son of Sisamai and father of Jekamiah in the family of Jerahmeel
7) an Ephraimite, father of Jehizkiah
8) a son of Naphtali
9) a Korahite Levite, chief of a family of gatekeepers for the east gate of the temple
9a) maybe same as 13
10) son of Halohesh and ruler of a district of Jerusalem; also repairer of the wall of Jerusalem in the time of Nehemiah
11) a priest, of the family of Eleazar, son of Zadok and father of Hilkiah in the family line of Ezra
12) a Korahite Levite, son of Kore, father of Maaseiah, and in charge of the work of the service. Maybe same as 9
13) a Levite gatekeeper who had a foreign wife in the time of Ezra
14) a Levite and descendant of Bani who had a foreign wife in the time of Ezra

A prophet living at the time of United Monarchy, first mentioned at 1Ki.12.22
§ Shemaiah = "heard by Jehovah"
1) a prophet of the Lord in the reign of king Rehoboam of Judah
2) the Nehelamite, a false prophet in the time of the prophet Jeremiah
3) father of Delaiah, one of the princes of Judah in the time of the prophet Jeremiah
4) an inhabitant of Kirjathjearim and father of Urijah, a prophet of the Lord in the time of the prophet Jeremiah
5) a Judaite, son of Shechaniah, father of Hattush, and descendant of Zerubbabel
6) a Simeonite, father of Shimri
7) a Reubenite, son of Joel and father of Gog
8) a Merarite Levite, son of Hasshub in the time of Nehemiah

13) a Levite, descendant of Jeduthun the singer in the time of king Hezekiah of Judah
14) a Levite, one of the messengers of Ezra to Iddo
15) a Levite in the time of king Jehoshaphat of Judah
16) a Levite, one of several in charge of distributing the free will offerings brought to God to their Levite brethren in the time of king Hezekiah of Judah
17) a Levite in the time of king Josiah of Judah
18) head of a family of exiles who returned with Ezra
19) a priest, of the sons of Harim who had a foreign wife in the time of Ezra
20) an Israelite of the sons of Harim who had a foreign wife in the time of Ezra
21) son of Delaiah, grandson of Mehetabeel, and a false prophet hired by Tobiah and Sanballat to give false guidance to Nehemiah

deep_entry:

A man living at the time of United Monarchy, first mentioned at 2Sa.8.17;
father of: Elihoreph (H0456) and Ahijah (H0281); also called Shavsha at 1Ch.18.16;  Sheva(Ketiv: Sheya) at 2Sa.20.25; Shisha at 1Ki.4.3;
§ Seraiah = "Jehovah is ruler"
1) the scribe or secretary of David
2) son of Azariah, father of Jehozadak, and the chief priest in the reign of king Zedekiah of Judah and at the time of the capture of Jerusalem
3) son of Tanhumeth the Netophathite and one of the men who went to Gedaliah, the governor over Judah appointed by Nebuchadnezzar, and gave their oath to serve the king of Babylon
4) a Judaite, son of Kenaz, brother of Othniel, and father of Joab
5) a Simeonite, father of Josibiah and grandfather of Jehu
6) a people of the province who returned from exile with Zerubbabel
6a) maybe the same as 10
7) son of Azariah and father of Ezra the priest and scribe
8) a priest who sealed the covenant with Nehemiah
9) a priest, son of Hilkiah in the time of Nehemiah
10) a priest or Levite who returned from exile with Zerubbabel
10a) probably a priest and the head of a family of priests after the exile. Maybe same as 6
11) son of Meraiah and messenger sent by the prophet Jeremiah to Babylon with a book of his writings
12) son of Azriel and one of the 3 men commanded by king Jehoiakim of Judah to seize Jeremiah and Baruch

STEPBible TBESH (Hebreiska)
A man of the tribe of Benjamin living at the time of Divided Monarchy, only mentioned at 1Ch.7.10;
son of: Bilhan (H1092H);
brother of: Jeush (H3266H), Benjamin (H1144H), Ehud (H0164H), Chenaanah (H3668H), Zethan (H2133) and Ahishahar (H0300)
§ Tarshish or Tharshish = "yellow jasper"
1) son of Javan

3) one of the wise men close to king Ahasuerus of Persia
4) a city of the Phoenicians in a distant part of the Mediterranean Sea to which the prophet Jonah was trying to flee
1a) perhaps in Cyprus or Spain
5) a city somewhere near and accessible to the Red Sea to which ships constructed at Ezion-geber on the Elanitic Gulf on the Red Sea were to sail
